_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If you are a Tsubasa anime fan and want to play for the story, I recommend buying for around ~20$, otherwise stay away from this.-- EDIT: Patch 1.10 --A new patch was released a few days ago with 3 new DLC characters and a new story route (3 months after the games release), which are always welcome additions. But it also included a brand new feature not written in the games patch notes: MICROTRANSACTIONS!That's right! Microtransactions on top of a 60€ incomplete game filled with bugs, softlocks and hackers!No, but seriously, go f*ck yourself Tamsoft & Bandai.-- END EDIT --Please take this review with a pinch of salt, it is more of a vent than a review but it still holds truth and represents my experience with this game. This game is a very mixed bag for me. I am in a love-hate relationship with it. : The story mode is great. There are 2 modes for the story, one where you play as the young Tsubasa and his team for the national junior championship. And the "New Hero" mode where you create your own character and play for Japan for the World Cup.As a nostalgic Tsubasa fan, this game truly shines in Story mode. The in-game animations are fun to watch and faithful to the manga/anime. The story plays itself in a nice 3D visual novel style with some dialogue choices for the player. In the "New Hero" mode, you play with your custom player. The better your performance is, during the game, the better stats the custom player receives. You can select original players (Tsubasa, Hyugga, etc...)  to make friendships with and learn their moves/skills. This makes for some really cool movesets combos and allows for your creativity to flow into the game.It's a really fun mode to make new character builds and do some re-runs to see new events/story development with players or learn new hidden moves. This is the mode where I spent most of my time playing this game. : Play Point(PP) shop. There is a in-game currency in Captain Tsubasa called PP. You gain these points by completing overall challenges, doing story challenges and increasing Friendships. With PP, you can unlock new cosmetic items for your player and buy card packs. The cosmetic item shop is fine but the card packs are terrible. The card packs include player cards, that increase the level at which you gain Friendship with that player, and consumable  items that increase the stat growth of your custom player during "New Hero". I have a real problem with this because there is a real discrepancy between the amount of PP you get for each run and the amount of items you use in that run. Once your overall challenges are done, there is a real lack of gain for PP points without any place to really grind/play for it.And i hate the fact that you share the same currency between cosmetic items and packs. After 100 hours, I barely have any cosmetics for my custom players. That's because if I want to grow the best stats for my character, I have to spend everything in card packs just to get a few decent items. I think cosmetic items should be unlocked on challenges or friendship goals, so you can use all your PP in card packs freely. : The online. It's unplayable. I don't even know where to start with this one. You spend 15-30 minutes searching for a match so it can be ruined by terrible latency, lack of any collision register, miracle goals or straight-out softlocks. For brevity sakes, I'm just gonna give some examples that happened to me: - There is a very good chance for the ball to jump randomly in the air into oblivion, during any long pass or corner kick. - The game can freeze during a goal celebration and either player must leave to end the game. Whoever leaves, loses the game and receives penalties for quitting mid-game. - Miracle Goals. Some shots have a slight chance to be instant goals, bypassing the goalkeeper and defenders health. So no matter how much character stats or how well you play, there is a chance of you drawing or losing the game. - Once, the ball got stuck under the ground and neither team could reach it, making that half-time unplayable. - Sometimes, the game makes it impossible for you to select your own players, making it impossible to make them move or pass. The game comes to a dead-end because the goalkeeper cannot pass without him selected.  - The run animations can straight out crash making it impossible to steal the ball from that player. - It is impossible to pause mid-game, making substitutions only possible in half-time. - It is possible to greatly stall for time after your first goal without any consequence or punishment.  It is no wonder most people never play again after their first match.: Predatory gameplay incentives and marketing schemes. This last patch introduced the CC shop. A new currency that allows to buy better items than the PP shop. This currency can only be gained with the new dailes/ weeklies mechanics. And this is where I draw the line with this game. Why is there a second in-game currency in the game? If you want to make items rarer, you could just increase their price or lower their drop chance in the card packs. There is no need for another currency (Although I have my theories on why they put it).This game never needed dailies or weeklies. Not only is it mostly an offline game but people won't spend 15-30 minutes waiting to play a mode which is riddled with bugs and crashes so they can do their daily for some few useless virtual points. If you want people to play the online mode, you have fix the mess that are the online games and smooth the matchmaking/gameplay. None of these issues were addressed in this patch.One month after its release, the game goes to 40% which is a spit in their supporter's faces. They still haven't addressed any issues that shouldn't even be in the release of this game. Their priority is to implement some shady currency (which would probably be monetized if there were any online players yet) with dailies/weeklies in hopes that their players will stick a bit longer. After one month, they haven't released any character from the DLC pass, which, at this point, I probably think they aren't even coded yet. This game was released incomplete and unpolished. What it should be a fun/casual football anime game was ruined by rushed releases, weird game mechanics, predatory rewards systems and greed. I was hopeful for many things to be fixed in this patch (1.07), but now I have no doubts that this game was a shamless attempt to install a 60$ predatory micro-transaction online system inside the Captain Tsubasa fandom.The offline story is still pretty great though. So if you are a Tsubasa fan, I still recommend buying this game when it goes to 20€, which shouldn't take too long considering its current development.Thank you for reading my review. I would appreciate any criticism you have for it.Regards, ThunderEye

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: I'm still loving the game, I spent so much time creating new characters and trying different builds and team comps, if you are fan of Captain Tsubasa and Soccer anime I can't recommend this enough, the only problem I have with the game is just online PvP is either not stable or people are abusing broken mechanics that will be fixed soon for sure, but this game is going strong and I really appreciate Bandai Namco for making this realI was waiting for this game to be released since it was announced, and oh boy tbh this game exceeded my expectation in many ways and was underwhelming in some others, so I will try to keep this simplePROS:- Story mode is amazing, you get cut scenes and special events from the manga if you were able to perform specific tasks during the match, and oooh boy how satisfying it is and how beautiful they look- Graphics of the game pretty nice and the background is colorful and full, no empty spaces- Voice actors nailed it- Music is perfect- You are rewarded the more you play the game, not just you get better since getting the timing is important to build that muscle memory, also tons of collectible items and characters- Characters actually feel different from each other so building teams is a lot of fun- minimum RNG next nothing- no micro-transactions - online PvP is stable without any lags or delays even though I'm in USA and I played vs someone in JP- supports all controllers - the game is deeper than it looks but it's not complicated CONS:- Some game technical issues like it crashed on me twice but I think it was because I switched window mid a loading screen- Some visual bugs in the match like GK stuck mid air after a Save- The referee doesn't do much since you can't make a foul, but I guess this eliminates the RNG factor- After you become good at the game story mode becomes SOOOO easy, I wish there was a way to increase the difficulty - Subtitle is funny sometimesThis game is not perfect by any means, but as a first attempt to make a modern Anime soccer game this is an 8/10 attempt, I suggest (if you want to see more of this) to buy this game, you can even wait when it is on sale to buy, but I think this could be a great start for a new generation of Anime Soccer games that will make us happy for a long time

_childDocuments_.review: A quick summary from someone who's waited for this game for months since it was announced:pros:                            - great cutscenes both on pitch and in dialogue sequences                    - good voice acting                    - good attention to detail in character design and information                    - character editor                    - tactics!!!CONS:                              - lots of bugs, some buttons aren't registering (in the story mode, not in custom                        offline matches for me) even after resetting them customly, players run towards                        opposite directions to the input sometimes and the CPU randomly runs back in                        forth for no reason in random situations, in addition my game was plagued by                        frequent crashes no matter how many times i've changed the graphic settings                        (it most certainly wasn't a fps problem)Without considering the bugs the gameplay lacks the depth it tries to portray in the tutorials. The controls are marketed as a system for an own individual action for each button and each combination between them, yet multiple buttons fulfill the same purpose of an action with the only contrast being a 1 on 1 'Attack and Counter' battle (Defense: press "xy" button combination to block "xy" button combination of opponent, Attack: press "xy" button combination to faint "xy" button combination of opponent). It's basically a rock-paper-scissors method which seemed a bit random as I could press random buttons, as a defender, to block a move that I was told couldn't get blocked by using the button combination I pressed (idk if that is also a bug). Other than that the interactions in cutscenes or special moves are pretty much nonexistent. Goalies are simply a wall that only can get beaten if they are low on stamina, it's just a battle of stats and ressources that involves no skill. The lack of interaction could easily get fixed with a button interaction that boosts stats if pressed in the right moment (similar to the old PS2 version of the franchise). I think I've made my standings clear about why I see a problem in playing the game in the long run, even without the bugs now, but here follows a short list of what also could be a problem for players who seek long playing times with this game:                     - no goalkeeper interaction in cutscenes                     - massive RNG in penalties with very basic animations, basically "pick the right                        corner" system, yet ball can get in if correct corner was picked                     - (online matches have bad connection i was told, haven't tried cause i can't                         even really play the game with the control bugs)                     - only 3 CPU difficulties                     - only 3 camera angles, too close to player for my taste                     - random button mashing system in some occasions                     - very bad scripting of 'through ball' pass                        For a Triple-A title these are way too many problems as of now. I've tried                         reinstalling the game and switching                         controllers and nothing has helped with fixing the obvious flaws.         08.09.2020 issues still not fixed

_childDocuments_.review: The 'not recommended' is for surviving the bad phase of early game with constant crash and no online play. After it was fixed, online play was also terrible. Previously this review was about tips how to overcome crash. Since most of the crash are gone, I will relate my experience with the game.The Story/ Hero mode is both fun, but the content is lacking and can be done in total 6hours for both mode.This is a soccer game, with long matches, overtime and penalty. If you are buying for online experience. There is just 60min match, each half 30min, no overtime or penalty. You either Win/Lose/Draw which affect your points. PP is a currency which is from online play, it helps you buy cosmetics and stats boost items in Hero Mode to build your custom hero. How your custom hero plays affects his final stats after you finish hero mode. This hero will be saved and registered for online use. I spent 60hours making a few heroes to use online but you can also use story characters whichever do not exceed your team point limit which is a restriction online based on how many strong players you can have in a team. That was where most of the fun in this game was at... customising.Currently, you can make custom character with Hero Mode but the PVP meta is centred toward scoring the 1st goal with Skylab Aerial shots (Tachibana bros + Jito).It doesn't matter how much block, defence you have. I blocked using Tachibana, did a second block with a custom defender, and Muller (GK) still had the ball sneak past the goal at full spirit. I am not sure how this happens but if many people are using this as meta, there is no point in Hero Mode to make anything unrelated to this kind of build.Lastly, you will likely be watching a 30min passing game known as birdcage which online players like to abuse to stall time and prevent you from reaching the ball to even do anything once they have upperhand. There is an option to place 2 DF at each corner of the field to pass to 2 MF to stall time. So DF to GK to DF. If you go close, they pass from DF to MF to DF. Get the idea? Below video do not belong to me, it is use for illustration purpose, channel also analysed most flaws in online play.       While you can only control one character at a time, AI characters which you don't control will never ever attempt to steal or tackle these 2DF or MF.) Running depletes spirit, if you intend to intercept their pass. Normal pass don't use spirit.Unless you have a way to break these 2 formation, I would not recommend buying it for online experience. You could simply use the same strategy but it depends which player start the game ultimately. Perhaps you think I don't have skill to play a soccer game and give an honest review. _childDocuments_.review: I kinda wish Steam had a "mixed" review opinion, but when I remember why I decided to write this review in the first place anyway, the thumbs down is kinda deserved. Don't get me wrong, the game isn't bad, in fact, it has so much potential, but sadly the potential it has is kinda limited by really bad design decisions. Normally, this review was more informative about Captain Tsubasa series, but I hit the character limit so kiss bye bye to those.I won't really go on on positives and negatives (actually, I will rant about the bad game design after this paragraph), but I will just tell why and when you should buy this game. The game's an action-sports game, and like I mentioned before, it plays according to its own mechanics, and it's nothing unlike FIFA or PES. Now the mechanics are pretty straightforward, and truth be told, they are fun to pull off as you dribble through the entire opponent team and pull a flashy shot. However, it does get kinda old by time and there are not that many teams or even story modes, so you have been warned. I also think the game is a bit pricey, especially if you are in a 3rd world country, but hey, I mean... it could be a Paradox game with 500$ worth of DLCs. At the end of the day, I'd strongly recommend to buy this only and only if you are a Captain Tsubasa fan, and when it's on a sale. If you're not a Capt Tsuba fan, I'd suggest you first watch a few gameplay vids and decide for yourself. And finally, I recommend the game for the single player fun or maybe a few friendly multiplayer matches with your friends, but I strongly recommend you to stay away the broken circus that is multiplayer... barring the one with your friends of course.Now that I've put away with my recommendation, this will be the paragraph where I will write about the "inconsistency of game mechanics" and "bad design decisions", if you haven't played the game, just skip to the end, as you wouldn't get what I am talking about anyway.The game mechanics are straightforward and understandable, and not hard to pull off, right. L1 dribble beats L2 tackle, and L1 tackle beats L1 dribble, nothing wrong with that. But sometimes, it's not simple as that and game really does murder its own rules, sometimes highly in favour of the AI. Now, I will list my grievances about the game mechanics:- If you lose the ball around the defense area, you know, if one of the AI players tackle you and get the ball, whenever I press with another player of mine, he just... runs to the dude, halts and looks at him like "O SHID LOOK AT HIM GO :DDDDD". Same situation almost never happens whenever I get the ball on AI's side. I dunno if it's just me but this is an obvious handicap for the AI as I can't stop them by "abiding to game mechanics". Or heck, if there is something as such, the game should just outright tell me.- Some dribbles are super derpy and handicapped as their anims take too long, and you know what the AI can do? The AI can control 10 of its outfield players at the same time. Take for example, Carlos Turn. Anim of Carlos Turn easily takes 2-3 secs in which the AI, son of a mastermind at controlling players, just barges in with another player to where your anim would end and takes the ball away. Now, I'm not saying all dribbles should be perfect, but the way AI is handicapped to tackling you after a move is just too dirty. - The camera. THE CAMERA.  It's especially really criminal when you enter the Zone with a dribble and you know what the camera does? It shows your dribble in dazzling fashion. Okay, that's great. But it also  before zooming out. And there is literally no telling what kind of tackle the opponent team will pull next as it's off camera and you can't see it, I mean this for both AI and other players. The sideline cam is also criminal at times as your player is just a smidge off from the right-left corner of the viewing area, and if a fast player barges in with a tackle, say goodbye to your ball possession.- Many of the older reviews voiced the lag and ping problems in Multiplayer, I'll be also quickly mentioning it.- This is my biggest problem with this game. That is, . In SP, you can Dribble Move a Tackle Move if the tackling player is almost in a position where he could almost Dash Tackle you. This is great, because there is no telling if a guy's dashing at you and if he will pull a Dash Tackle or Tackle Move at the last second.  hit the Dribble Move button literally when the guy's almost about to hug you and you lose the ball to a Tackle Move. Why? Because AI literally hits Tackle Move button whenever you push the Dribble Move. That's okay though, the real problem here is that . In SP, you would actually dribble the guy, but in Multiplayer, the mechanics are  so that Dribble Move, even if the Tackle Move is about to end, - The AI is too much of a gremlin at times. Play against Netherlands in SP and you'll get what I mean. Since it can control 10 outfield players at the same time, it just sends 5 players against your one. You dribbled someone? Nice, now dribble 3 more. You dribbled one of them? Oh look out, he catched up to you once again! He is tackling! Oh no, you've lost the ball! This is especially also annoying.- Switching between players is also really poor, most of the time I can't choose the player I actually want to choose.- AI for players you don't control is also pretty poor, many times they will just hurr durr into an opponent player and you'll give out a free dribble. Passing AI is also poor at times, as it passes to the farthest possible player with a short pass.- This one's not really important, but they still haven't fixed the keybinds for Custom Player celebrations on keyboards.To conclude, I both recommend and don't recommend this game. I kinda have fun playing it, despite it driving me really mad at times with bad design decisions. If Tamsoft somehow reads my review and tries to improve on the negatives I've mentioned, then I'd be happy to turn my review from negative to positive. The reason why I'm giving a thumbs down is to make them improve anyway. This review would have been longer, but Steam is threatening me with drinking from my skull if it gets any longer. So yeah, Paitone out.Much later edit: And now they've released a new "game mode" along with some DLCs that feel like your average Paradox DLC and even disabled editing of character skills on original players... without addressing any of the existing issues. It's kinda incredible that they have caused further issues with this decision they've taken. Do yourself a favour, be prepared to not put any faith in devs fixing problematic gameplay mechanics if you buy this game and be ready to be completely disappointed with them.

_childDocuments_.review: Super smash bros + FIFA + Gacha. Captain Tsubasa RoNC is fun but a bit shallow. The mechanics in place dont do enough to reward players that are "trying" to use some kind of real world/sports world logic in them. You could play this game like real soccer, but then the elephant in the room speaks, the rpg mechanics/numbers that dictate everything. You would never expect someone to dribble through literally every person on your team then, send the goalie into the net with the ball, but with the rights skills and high enough stats, thats exactly what youll get, on either side of the ball. What does that mean? You have to recognize and respect "star" players, on teams because theyll walk all over your teammates without your interference. When the AI gives the ball to a player with vastly superior stats, it B lines where it wants, through whoever it thinks it can beat on your team, and its usually correct. After completing the CaC story 20 something times, the last majority of my attention while playing is on the friendship/card levels and how many broken skills I can incorporate into a build, not on the soccer im playing or fundamentally how im playing it. Im hoping for a deeper sequel or spiritual successor but I wont hold my breath.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start by saying that I was very, very excited for this game. I have been waiting ever since the first announcement, and have pre-ordered the game as soon as the option became available (something which, frankly, I regret).The game's not your regular football game: it's arcade-ish and fast-paced. The controls are tricky at first, but they don't take too long to get used to. The graphics are quite gorgeous and the animations are faithful to the manga, very smooth, and satisfying to watch.The singleplayer story is well-made and the voice acting is on point.All in all, you would say that Captain Tsubasa: Rise of New Champions is a solid, fun game, right? Well... There's a catch.It  be if Namco hadn't released a game which, in its current state, can only be described as an early access title. Never in my life have I witnessed so many glaring bugs and glitches in a mere two hours of gameplay. Let me list  of the ones I have encountered:• • • Again, when not windowed, the game will sometimes and run at double the speed, inevitably crashing after a few minutes• The game will sometimes crash in certain portions of the story• Sometimes, goalkeepers will fly away from the goal when trying to save a shot, conceding a free goal• Players can get stuck in a dribbling/tackling animation and literally glide across the entire pitch as if they were riding an invisible hoverboard• • The netcode makes it absolutely impossible to play online. Nothing makes sense. Players flying, drowning inside the map, balls disappearing, keepers magically becoming weak.On top of all this, the developer seems to communicate very rarely with the community, leaving players wondering if those issues have even been acknowledged.In conclusion, this is  a finished game. If you're a fan of the manga like me, then be my guest, but if you're looking for a new experience, don't disturb your wallet (or credit card) just yet. Hopefully, at some point, these terrible issues will be ironed out, the game will finally be what it's meant to be, and this review will turn into a positive one.EDIT: Some of the issues have been fixed, but the game still needs to be polished more.After playing the game for more time, I don't think this review will ever change. It's kinda painful for a game I was so hyped for, but, eh.EDIT 2: I've been trying to appreciate the game more. The online is definitely better. Only needs some tweaks to be a great game, now.

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with Captain Tsubasa was an interesting one, never did i think that i could find a game so in depth and just pure genius. The football is fluent, fast paced and above all its anime. Now I'm not a weeb but the thought of a Japanese school boy running around the pitch with the ball at his feet at the speed of light is what grips you to this game. You take control of the legendary Tsubasa and his team to take on this tournament and prove that Tsubasa is the best.However this doesnt even come close to when Tsubasa and his friends take it to the world stage, against some of the worlds best from across the globe, and this time you get to create your own avatar in the Tsubasa world. when i found out that this was possible my jaw hit the floor. the character customisation is deep and diverse, plentiful options to choose from to make your character stand out and really resemble yourself or your dream character that you want to tear it up on the pitch.Finalising this review i must say to anyone reading this, you need to purchase this game. it is a masterpiece in a genre where it is difficult to have a wow factor this is not your normal sports anime game, this is my personal game of the year. i cannot recommend this game enough to anyone, all ages of people will favour this game as one of their best ever experiences on a video game title, since the likes of skyrim or the witcher 310/10

_childDocuments_.review: [NOTE: for all you busy lads and lass' out there with a life and stuff -> scroll to the end for a summary]Let it be known to all that I am as biased as one can be. I grew up with the sport football and naturally watched Captain Tsubasa anime since I was able to look at the TV. Furthermore, I always dreamed of being in the same team as Tusbasa and always wanted an own football team in that universe.Let me continue with the fact that this game heavily delivers to ALL you fans. I will get as to why in a bit.Secondly, I shall be comparing this game with another game i like quite a lot: FIFA 08 for the DS. Because both games share a whole lot of similarities and both games are equally fun in SOLO mode as with FRIENDS.Now, I have been reading on other reviews and I would like to warn all who are friendless (or have anime-allergic friends) that this game is a bit OFF-PUTTING in online mode. Here is why: any game that benefits the lagger more than the skilled player, is a bad multiplayer gaming experience. This applies to this game as well. Tho, I haven't tried the online feature yet, due to the fact that I simply COULD NOT be asked to. I never cared for multiplayer in FIFA games and same goes to this one. For the aforementioned reason. Yet, the rule of thumb still applies: if lag benefits the player more than skill, then you might as well not bother with the online experience and play it with your friends on steam (less lag). Worked for FIFA 08 DS and it works with this game.So, with the multiplayer out of the way let's get into the real MEAT and POTATOES of this game: the single player. Truth be told, it is just the TOPS. There are some little ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but then again where is there a game where there aren't any? So, in short here are some bullet points:-Story: 2 modes -> Fanservice (non-ecchi kind) and the main story of Tsubasa.-Customization is the anime version as with FIFA 08 DS: own team creation; logo; jerseys; own character creation, but with more shirts styles and glasses (for some weird reason).About that HERO mode, because it is where this game truly shines. It is the all 10 school extravaganza story line with your very own character to cream yourself about. If you loved the anime, then this gamemode has its red dot sighted scope aimed right at your Thalamus (brain for all my younger peers). Because it allows you to view each school's struggles and character development in the football fields as well as in the outside life (a bit). HOWEVER, it is needless to say that after 10 runs it might get a bit samey, but nonetheless this is where the game truly shines and where most of the budget has gone into. And it shows!Now, another good thing about this game is the stat system. In HERO mode, you create and level your own character which then becomes playable OUTSIDE the story line. Which is a bit of a time sink, BUT here is where they nail it: YOUR skills determine YOUR future costum team! So, in other football games you would normally just slap a bunch of 99+ stats on all the bloody skills and call it a day. Become the most OP footballer in the world. But here is the true question: WHERE IS THE BLOODY POINT OR FUN IN THAT? In those games, you would get bored after your Saitama-like power play. THIS GAME - however - allows you to grow each time in a different area and to generate 11 (max 20) playable pawns for your team (or any team if you just switch them beforehand) you desire!This is good due to the variety of gamestyles you can pick, which is a BREATH OF FRESH air compared to most (repetitive) FIFA games. Whereas in those games you would just slap a 99+ stat on speed and you would be settled, this game requires you to be more strategical about your point distribution in your stats. This can be overwhelming, but do not worry there are plenty of guides online.For the last part come the last few ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and info bits:1-The stamina based gameplay is the tops, but there is no use for switching out players unlike in other football games. Plus, there are no Yellow or Red cards.  2- AI being a load of nonsense in this game[1]:The stamina or "spirit" - very clever - depletes but restores during the matches. So, once you have your 11 ALL-STARS on the field and remembering that there are no yellow or red cards, which means you can kick somebody in the toochy for that ball to be yours and the referee will think it is legit... What is the bloody point? They might as well dress up with a cheerleading tutu skirt and some bloody POM POMS for all the help they are for the team :I. This and the fact that the referee only gives penalties for off-side is a bit of what I like to call a "culture-shock". Since it goes against all my football knowledge of the real world. BUT, this does mean more action in the field, which is a bonus. Plus, you can name your character into somebody you dislike and kick him in his toochy for the ball and laugh at him (in call or on the couch) if that person is sitting next to you."10/10; would kick in the toochy again" - Santa 2021.[2]: The AI is a load of nonsense. It has 2 modes: busting my bladder hard mode or "don't know how to hold a controller"- mode.The first one is anything above the 2* rating of difficulty. The AI just KNOWS when you press to dribble/tackle button and will instantly counter that with the respective move. So, you might as well just sprint away and dodge; pass the ball a couple of times. Because it is just far easier to avoid the AI taking the ball away from you after you have had it for 0.02 seconds. And the AI cheats by taking over multiple oppenents and having them coming towards you. Very much like the anime, yes. But I am trying to score and this is my third attempt at this match and I would just like to not be part of your S&M club, thank you very much. Speaking of S&M group meet-ups outside of quarantine, these also can happen to your own team members. Maybe they just forgot to wish each other good luck and are doing that group YELL thingy, but not during my third-attempt-at-this-rubbish-matches, okey game?ALL-IN-ALL:-Buy this game during the sales (summer is best for your free time). It is absolutely worth 25€. The story hooks you in like a powerbait on a fishing hook. You git gut along the story and you get to know the less known struggles of the side characters of the anime.-Multiplayer: do not bother, unless it is with your friends on the couch or via steam remoteplay.-Singleplayer: plays like a fighting game but in the football world. Timing; football strats and stat point placement are the key to win this game. Not like most FIFA games where you just pick the "Ultimate XI" or that years most BS team and get the easiest games of your life. Nah, this game is more fair than other football games.This game has 2 story modes and your usual football game "mini-games".-Gameplay: again, plays like a action packed football match. With only off-sides as an offence and the referee barely plays a role in this match. Coming to think of it, I haven't seen one at all, so maybe that is why these teenagers are allowed to kick each other in the toochy for that lovely round football.Stamina/spirit matters only during the match (you can see it as action points for all your moves) and not during half-time break. No reason to switch unless you have evenly good players with different movesets. If that is the case, then it is a good reason. Otherwise do not bother.Timing, strats and stats are the surname of this game for anybody that bothers "Gitting Gut" at this.Thank you for those who have read it all :)Have fun and take care!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a dream come true (for Captain Tsubasa fans).Before I had started to play this game, I wasn't sure about gameplay mechanics even I have seen lots of gameplays from different players. As soon as I begin to play, I can say this is far beyond what I expected. Very fast and enjoyable gameplay that makes you concentrate in every second. Challenging at first, but quickly you get used to it. Buttons are very close to generic football games.I have really enjoyed story so far. It is a bit short but exactly what I have expected as a Captain Tsubasa fan.For the dream edit mode, this is where the real fun begins. Because you need to create a team from scratch and face against other players in ranked league. There is a limit for players you can put into your team. And this limit increases as you succeed better divisions. This makes you try different team combinations in every match.For custom players those you can create, this is grinding part of the game. But it is an enjoyable way to do it. You can create 20 different custom players. You are getting player cards and training cards from the packs those can be bought with game points (you gain these points as you play game, No microtransactions). These player cards makes your friendship increased faster with the player on the card in New Hero (custom player) Story Mode. You need to play story and increase your friendship with other players for what kind of character you want to create. And you can use these custom players on your ultimate team if you want (max 8 custom players in a team). This grinding may sound boring but the game at least have 3 times replayability thanks to its 3 different story routes. I have really enjoyed what I have seen in this game. I strongly recommend it to every Captain Tsubasa fan. For others who likes to play a football game, this is clearly no fifa or pes. 10/10 for Captain Tsubasa fans 7/10 for othersPS: I haven't experienced any performance issues so far. I have played it both in 144hz monitor and Led tv via steam link. It works smooth for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely a must-get for anybody who's a big fan of Captain Tsubasa as a whole. The graphics are definitely stunning, many fan favorites are in the game as well as new characters exclusive to the game, and the story brings a fun new twist on things as you play through as your own custom character. Online mode works well and is a blast to play, though you will bump into some problems with lag depending on your connection to the other players, including but not limited to REALLY weird rubberbanding. There are some bugs still present, like the occasional crash or ball-related oddity (such as the AI kicking the ball way off-field with a special shot, somehow). All characters are unlockable for free excluding future DLCs -- the card packs are NOT for unlocking characters, and are also completely free and gotten using in-game currency which is NOT sold for Steam funds but rather earned through gameplay. There is no pay-to-win aspect, and it all boils down to who plays better and sets up a stronger team.The gameplay itself is exciting, fast-paced, and action-packed, and it really feels like you have to strategize somewhat and put in that extra 10% to win out against strong opponents. Cinematic special shots, dribbles, and saves are gorgeous to look at, and you unlock more as you play the game and complete challenges, both for your custom character and existing characters in the story (for use outside of the story, as well).Overall, I'd say it'd be good to wait for a sale or wait for the price to drop a little bit, unless you're a big fan of Captain Tsubasa already. If you love Captain Tsubasa, you will love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to write a review just because of the amount of negative reviews that came in when this game launched.For those that tldr; THIS GAME IS A MASSIVE LOVE LETTER TO CAPTAIN TSUBASA FANS.Now onto the actual details of my experience (wow I played this game a lot):PROS:- Excellent story and RPG system, New Hero Chapters are superbly well-done and it really makes you feel like you are part of the team- Excellent character writing, they took away all the boring stuff from Captain Tsubasa's manga/anime and condensed it into a pure love story about soccer.- Very excellent animation and gorgeous graphics- The music is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing???? Like why is it so good???????? It is one of the best OST I've listened to and it works so well with the epicness of the story.CONS:- Unfortunately quite buggy: controls are quite buggy and as people mentioned, the FPS takes a dive from time to time which can make gameplay sometimes frustrating since you can easily lose a ball since you can't hit the dribble or your shot button not registeringMY THOUGHTS:As mentioned, I loved this game. In terms of pure story elements and gameplay, this is THE BEST Captain Tsubasa game I've ever played. And I've played a lot of them -- from the SNES ones to Dream Team and now this.Whoever wrote the story for this game should get a rounding applause, they took existing elements from the previous story and gave it a good polish. It packs more of an emotional punch and really pays respect to -every single character- that appears in this game. Characters that I hated in previous games/anime/manga became my favorites here and they each have their time to shine in your journey with them.The story mode is also mindblowingly good. It can be quite a shock because Episode Tsubasa is so short and you don't quite realize it's actually just an introduction to the main story that is Episode New Hero. It took me by surprise because I've seen how sports games treat these "RPG story modes". Usually it is very crap but this isn't the case here. This game treats their story mode with a massive respect and love towards the Captain Tsubasa franchise. The friendship system, the move learning system, the dialogue choices, and the different extra events that can occur depending on how you decide to play YOUR hero is crazy and what I would expect from a genuine RPG. Easy to say, this mode is the best mode of the game. The game is worth every single penny because of this mode and Tamsoft's execution of it.All I can say is... with all the teasing at the end -- they better as hell make an expansion story!When it comes to the actual gameplay, I was a bit worried when I first watched the trailer because the gameplay looked downright clunky and not smooth. However, playing the game is a completely different experience. The transition between your special moves and controlling your characters on the field is seamless and extremely fun... WHEN it is working the way it should.Many of the previous reviews before me has already mentioned, but this game is unfortunately a bit buggy. While nothing game breaking, but when you are hyped from the story and feeling that momentum, this is very frustrating. There's been a good handful of times I have lost a ball due to the game not registering my dribble and shoot buttons suddenly. My characters would sometimes run off the field too as a result. On top of that, the newest patch refused to work with my XBOX controller, so I had to switch to emulator controls. Having said that, it seems like Tamsoft and Bandai are aware and are working hard to fixing those issues. So my hopes are that they fix this in the very near future.The game is almost there really. I hope people will play it once the bugs are fixed, just because if they can get that final layer of polish on and go on to keep making these games, we'd have something amazing to keep playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this review by saying that I don't like football.That being said, when I saw Captain Chewbacca on sale for 40% off and it looked like a colourful, ridiculously over-the-top anime sports game, I felt that this could change my mind.I booted up the game and was immediately entranced by the aesthetics, the soundtrack and the feel-good vibes. Kicking off the story mode and ten seconds later I'd triggered a cutscene in which Captain Kielbasa dramatically smashed a ball straight through the keeper's hands and into the back of the net."YES!" I thought.Oh, how I miss those naive moments when all was good.It was shortly after that during the tutorial section when things turned sour. The game crashed to the desktop. "Fine," I thought - I'd seen the reviews and I knew that this game was new and I was expecting some teething problems, but I figured I could live with it...The opening match of the campaign is the characters training to defeat their first opponents - you see, in the cutscene prior to this, one of the opposing team kicks the ball and it TURNS INTO A GLOWING EAGLE, so Captain Susie Bassa and his crew of Football Chums need to train extra hard to defeat EAGLE BALL MAN* - and is scripted with on-screen prompts to help you get the basic flow of the match. Pass, tackle, shoot, score, win! Unfortunately, this is when the game went totally weird. Players were running at high speeds in tiny circles unless they had the ball, in which case they moved slower than a snail crawling through molasses underwater. When Captain Drum and Bass Set gets the ball, the game yells at me, RUN TO THE GOAL, SHOOT! So I try. He runs so slowly, but I inch my way up the field. Holding down 'X' to power my shot, I quickly notice that the power bar is climbing at a snail's pace. I stop running and keep 'X' held down.Standing a few feet away from the goal and holding 'X' down for a full 2 minutes - I took a few sips of coffee and checked my phone while i waited - none of the other players attempted to tackle me, everyone waited patiently for me to charge the shot.When it was fully charged, I released my finger from the 'X' button and stared in shock and awe as... the game crashed to the desktop.Great.Repeating this mission with all of the above bugs, I managed to pass it - I read many guides in the discussion forum about combating the bugs, so thanks everyone who posts there! - and was on to the first match. Thankfully the game seemed to be playing normally and it was a lot of fun. The action is fast and frantic. Every player is constantly yelling in Japanese about what they are doing, scoring goals feels EPIC and the cutscenes interspersed with the gameplay really made it feel like I was taking part in some wider story. i was really impressed. Finally, a Football game I could get behind!Sadly, my joy was once again, short-lived. The game repeatedly crashed and I looked around for reasons why. It turns out that in the first match, if Captain Titular Character gets the ball for more than a few seconds, or tackles another player the game immediately crashes. The match descends into this weird life-or-death game of avoiding the main character at all costs, trying to win the match. I am yet to complete it without accidentally tackling someone with Captain Gundam Unicorn and triggering a crash...It's amazing then, that the developers are currently focusing on building on the multiplayer mode of the game and expanding on the micro-transactions within the game when the campaign is so fundamentally broken.I bought this game for an escape from 2020's challenges - for those reading in the apocalyptic future, a killer virus wiped out all of humanity while we stayed inside playing anime football games and built a stock market out of virtual turnips - by playing a colourful, exciting game about victory through conquering adversity. Instead, I look in awe as characters run the opposite direction that I am trying to move them, the game crashes at seemingly random intervals, characters weirdly jerk around in cutscenes and I struggle in vain with my computer's settings to try to make the game feel stable. All while avoiding making a pass to the main character of the game.Despite all this, I have hope. That's what the game is about after all: It's about doing your best and winning despite the odds. Training really hard and overcoming your challenges to grasp victory from the jaws of defeat. I have faith that PC players will not be ignored and that the developers can turn this broken mess into a tremendously fun arcade football game that can compete with "real" football games.Captain Caveman - Rise of New Champions is not a game I would recommend you purchase at the current time, but if you're looking for a different sort of football game - a break from the FIFAs and the PES' of the world - then keep an eye on it. If the bugs get ironed out, this will be a must-buy for sports fans and anime fans alike.

_childDocuments_.review: : I wrote this review after I beat The Journey Episode Tsubasa and based on my experience from the game so far.Captain Tsubasa: Rise of New Champions is a new anime based game from BANDAI NAMCO, based on the manga  created by Yōichi Takahashi in 1981. The game is suprisingly good. The cutscenes, gameplay, and story were great. In fact, I had never had so much fun playing football game as I had playing this game today. This game is a breath of fresh air for the sports gaming industry and reminds me of FIFA Street and Mario Strikers. But, like any other game, it's still has it flaws.I've seen so many complaints about bugs and glitches from the community. But even after I finished one of the story mode (The Journey Episode Tsubasa), I didn't find anything. No bugs or glitches; just pure fun. The only thing I agree with is bad PvP mode. If you want to have fun with your friends then I can't recommend this game for you, unless you play locally, which fortunately is an option in this game., especially if you are a fan of Captain Tsubasa manga or anime. But, before the developers fix the Online Multiplayer mode and polish the game (especially the janky player movements), I suggest you only buy this game on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: “The boy was raised with a soccer ball never far from his feet. At eleven, his move to the city of Nankatsu would be the catalyst for two fateful encounters. One with the star of Brazilian soccer, Roberto Hongo... and the other with the goalkeeping prodigy, Genzo Wakabayashi. The good fortune of meeting these two became the robust roots of his passionate life of soccer. Fighting alongside teammates and rivals alike, forging bonds while severing others... Every experience became his strength. It’s been four years since those two fruitful encounters. He has faced down countless trials. And now... he finds himself ready to spread his wings and greet the wide world. His name is Tsubasa Ozora.” After agreeing to Bandai Namco Privacy Policy, you find yourself in the tunnel waiting to head out onto the field for the finals of the first “Jr. Youths World Challenge” which is being held in America. The finals are between japan and Germany! The winner will have bragging rights and be able to call themselves World Champions. This isn’t a full match however but a small tutorial of a few basics, Dribbling, Shooting, Tackling etcetera. To finish this tutorial, you must follow and complete certain moves in order to progress. After completing this small tutorial and following movie clip you’ll find yourself at the main menu screen.   On the main menu you will find, The Journey, here are two single player story campaigns “Episode Tsubasa” and “Episode New Hero”. Versus, Offline matches which supports up to four players. Online Versus, here you can face off against the world’s best online players. Practice, here you can undergo training and learn new skills. Ultimate Edit, you can make changes to players and teams you have created. Collection, here you can enjoy special videos and music. And finally, Options so you can configure your systems settings.   In the Episode Tsubasa you’ll follow Tsubasa through the thrilling competition of the middle school Nationals. Episode New Hero allows you to train your own hero in the original story. Match settings are optimised to fit the both stories, so you’re unable to change any game settings. Episode Tsubasa campaign is recommended for new players to familiarise themselves with the game. While Episode New Hero is for those players with more experience under their belts.  As I’m a bit rusty at the old football (that’s right it’s FOOTBALL!!! Not Soccer!) I went and played the Tsubasa campaign. Tsubasa plays for Nankatsu MS and have won the Nationals for the last two years running. Although this year Tsubasa and team mates will be going up against some of Tsubasa’s old teammates like Kojiro Hyuga, Captain of Toho MS and Shun Nitta of Otomo. Both teams express their desires of beating Nankutsu and becoming champions. After some boasting and chat, you’ll have the option to learn some more basics and skills or start your next match. You don’t actually play all games in the Nationals to reach the final, this is played on in the story. It will have Nankatsu MS and Otomo MS reach the National finals. This means you’ll be up against Nitta who is desperate to beat Tsubasa and prove that he’s the best. This will be your first full game you’ll play through, the winner of which will be crown National Champions. It’s not going to be easy the Otomo team play defensive and haven’t dropped a point throughout the tournament. Each player has Five Stats, Offence, Defence, Power, Speed and Technique. These will determine their General Offence and Defence, Shot Power, Movement Speed and Kick Gauge Fill Speed. Performing a Critical Defence allows you to successfully tackle a player who is filing their Kick Gauge. The longer you hold down the shoot button the more powerful your shot will be.  You can activate Shooting Moves by filling the Kick Gauge and while the Spirit Gauge is above a certain amount. Shooting Moves vary depending on the player. However, all Shooting Moves will weaken the opponent's goalkeepers Spirit. You will have better chance of scoring a goal the lower a goalkeepers Spirit is. Successful Tackling, Dibbling or Dueling will fill your V-Zone Gauge. Activating V-Zone Gauge when it’s full and on the offensive will allow your teammates Spirit and Kick Gauge to refill faster. It will also have other effects depending on your team captain.  In the Manage Team Menu you can select up to Four Tactics which you can swap on the fly any time within a match. There are Fifteen tactics you can choose from ranging from Offensive and Defensive Formations, Left-Side and Right-Side Focus. So, you should be able to find the right tactics to help you beat your opponents. At the end of a match you will be shown detail of the match, Score, Ball Possession, Shots, Successful Moves, Corner Kicks, Offside Penalties and V-Zones Activated.  In the settings there’s options for Graphic Settings (Anti-Aliasing, Texture Quality, Shadow Quality, Depth of Field and Bloom). Window Settings (Display Mode, Resolution, Framerate Limit and V-Sync). Audio Settings (Music, Movie, Menu SFX, Story Voice, Match SFX, Match Cheering, Match Play-by-Play Voice, Match Player Voice). Match Settings (Match Time (Half), Overtime, Penalty Kick off, Number of Substitutions, Stadium/Field, Time, Ball Type and Camera Type). Language (Subtitles and Languages English, Brazilian Portuguese, Latin American Spanish, French, Italian, German, Spanish, Arabic and Traditional Chinese). Key Config (Button Layout 1 to 8). Other Settings (Skip Story and Skip Bonding Events).  I have enjoyed playing Captain Tsubasa – Rise of New Champions so far. The graphics are good, the ambience and music are good. However, it did get very frustrating with the game crashing all the time. Sometimes I’d be five minutes into a match the next time it would three quarters way through the match. I tried everything I could think of to stop the game from crashing, made sure drivers all up to date, tried to run the game without the anti-cheat, turned off Steam overlay etcetera but no joy.  I searched the internet and found a couple options to try, one of which was to restart a new game, which I didn’t fancy doing but after trying all sorts I had no other choice but try. However, there’s a second part to starting a new game and that is not to do the tutorials which show up before matches. It seems that if you do the tutorials then it corrupts your game save and will then crash when in a match. I wouldn’t mind but I haven’t learnt everything and the tutorials would have been nice to have had a butchers at. I haven’t had a problem since I restarted the game and not doing the tutorial but it shouldn’t be like this so it really needs sorting out. I haven’t tried any of the other game modes other than the Tsubasa story campaign mode thus far.Positives + Two story modes + Offline and online versus modes + Customisable characters and teams + Good graphics + Has achievements + Remote Play Together Negatives - Kept crashing and silly fix - It’s called “Football not Soccer” - No cards currently Take to the field with your dream team or lead Captain Tsubasa to victory in the arcade football game, Captain Tsubasa: Rise of New Champions 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Edited: Finished the CampaignA treat for all Tsubasa fans! The game plays smoothly and the controls are simple to learn, but hard to master.I've finished the game, and there's still so much field to run across!The game is a treat from an action point of view. If you go into it expecting your traditional football game, you're going to struggle. Your first instinct is going to be to pass a lot, to run away from contests, forget all of that!The game takes after the anime, and favours 1-on-1s, aggressive tackling and shooting, and overall it's a blast.The story modes are split into two groups. The Tsubasa chapter is your tutorial and it gives you an abridged peek into the middle school arc of the series. New Hero allows you to create your own player by picking one of 3 positions (FW, MF, DF) and one of three schools (Furano, Musashi, Toho). You can develop your player by performing accordingly to your position, as well as by using training items. You can also learn special moves and skills by befriending the multiple special characters by drawing their player cards in a gacha-style draw, lvling up their characters and completing special missions during matches.You can also create your own dream teams and go online, although the PC version is still a little glitchy as of the writing of this review, but that should be fixed before long.Overall, the game offers great replayability through the New Hero chapter and through its online mode. You can create multiple custom teams to have fun with your friends, and if you're into flashy, over-the-top moves, this game has got you covered.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. Why don't I recommend it?TL;DR:It's an anime soccer game without fouls / yellow / red cards.I think it's a shadow of a game it could be.like other reviews, if you're thinking this is a soccer game, it's half that. What I mean is this.At offensive, you'll never score a goal unless you get the keeper's stamina down to red. You reduce the keeper's stamina by shooting at him and will cost his stamina more with super shots. Once his stamina is red, any super shot will basically go in.So it isn't a shooting game where you decide where to shoot, just gotta keep shooting.At defensive, it's less of a tactics than rock paper scissors where you almost lose every chance you try to steal the enemy's ball.- at offense you can short dash to instantly pass a defender. but if their tackle hits you, 100% stolen ball. no foul nor yellow / red card so its all fair game here. Slide tackle away.- at defense, your slide tackle will almost never work to steal their ball. almost being the key word. the game chooses randomly when your tackle succeeds.But. if there's a specific event that needs to happen in the main story, then the math will work against you (and once or twice for you) to set up that scene. Should a scene need to happen where the enemy shoots at your goal, then their dribble will be godlike 100% cannot be stolen.Despite saying all that, the animation work as usual is superb. just like the shippuden series. I wish they'd give more freedom at the actual game though and not take control / result away from the player as much.

Often times a pass overshoots.- AI is not helpful at all, when a ball is near them, if they were not the target of the pass, they simply run past the ball, despite being the closest.- scoring against a goalie is just a matter of draining their stamina/resistance bar. Once it's depleted, it's easier to score, especially with charged shots. There's no real aiming your shot manually, you just try to deplete the goalie's defense as fast as possible.The game overall is very shallow and at least on PC, released in a very glitchy state. The game boils down to being a tug of war with cutscenes instead of a reall soccer/football game. Yes, it's not supposed to be a simulation sports game, but even for an arcade sports title, the game is incredibley shallow. The price simply does not reflect that.

_childDocuments_.review: PSA: If the game is crashing over and over again, make sure that you are not pressing ALT because this will pause the game, and it will seem like the game has crashed. If this happens to you, you can press ALT again to unpause.Review Update Part II: Now that I have completed one route in story mode, I can tell you that what people have said about the content and mechanics being shallow simply is not true. First, there are multiple routes to play through the game depending on the MS you choose when you start New Hero mode. When you beat the national tournament in that mode,  and  The dialogue is also relatively dynamic based on how you play and who you are playing against, which is neat.Secondly, there is a fair amount of depth to the gameplay. Your plays can become more elaborate if you are willing to learn how to string together combo passes and shots. Each character in the game has a wide range of skills that are thematically appropriate, which your custom character can learn through choosing to train with them in between matches. Those skills are active, passive, and conditional. Active skills replace pretty much every maneuver in the game (passing, supers, tackles, etc.), while passive and conditional skills give you statistical bonuses. You can also unlock skills for other characters by meeting certain conditions/making certain plays in a match. With each match win you can increase your stats with bonus points awarded for meeting goals you set and winning matches on your first try. And each time you win the game you can save your custom character to use online. On top of that there is a great deal of cosmetic customization. Which means that (assuming you do well) you can create a roster of 20 (the limit for custom chars ATM) optimized and unique characters.Review Update: Servers have been working for me since a few hours ago. The Tsubasa story mode was incredibly short, but it looks like there are campaigns for three additional schools where you can create and train up a highly customizable character. Only just started playing, but being able to train particular stats and learn moves from other characters in the game seems pretty neat so far. On the more negative side of things, the resolution issues remain, and I had to skip the intro cutscene to the semi-finals because the game crashed.Original Review: Kinda wish I was playing Inazuma Eleven, but this is a better game than what is reflected in the reviews. The mechanics are relatively tight even though this is a fairly casual soccer game. The thematic elements of the show and each match play out nicely, which encourages you to adopt strategies suitable to defeating your opponents as they are portrayed in the show, which is neat. It is kind of frustrating that online is currently unavailable because these sorts of casual games are really fun when you can actually play with your friends.I think the main reason why this game is getting brutally downgraded (beyond no MP) are the bugs and the lack of support for certain resolutions. I have played for longer than many of the people that have been bashing the game, and I have only once encountered a bug where a character model in a cutscene stuttered. The stuttering lasted about 5 seconds. The game also displays text incorrectly if you attempt to force an unsupported resolution.I am fairly certain these bugs/issues will be ironed-out pretty soon. If the game looks fun to you and you don't mind playing the (two) single-player campaigns, I recommend picking it up. If it looks fun, but you want to play with some of your friends, wait for a server fix announcement. I say that because I think that the trailers offer a really honest depiction of the game play. If there are aspects of the game that you would not play at all, it might be a good idea to wait for a sale.

The gameplay is a bit too biased on RNG and the rock-scissors-paper mechanics.  It would work well as an alternative football game (vs FIFA / PES) but this doesn't work for Captain Tsubasa IMO.  Tsubasa is supposed to be nearly impossible to dispossess and his passing is near perfect.  I thought the RNG/RSP mechanics should be shelved during story mode to match the same level of invincibility Tsubasa had as a manga protaganist.Apart from that, the rest of the game felt neither here nor there.  Its not a SRPG like the NES/SNES version, nor is it a nice realistic match up against FIFA/PES.Even as a fan of the franchise this felt like a miss to me.  I am encouraged by the attempt though, and I hope the next try will be on mark!

_childDocuments_.review: I went into the Game with a clear state of mind - this is not a football game, it is a beat em up. The Gameplay is fairly easy and it is a even fun at times.Sadly the game is cleary only designed around the online multiplayer in mind which is kind of sad for someone not intending to play it.The Story mode of the Game is a complete Joke. The difficulty is not a smoth curve - every game pre international is a complete joke and starting with the international the enemy Forwards escalate where the only consistent way to win is not letting them shoot.The biggest Problem I have with the Story Mode is the fact that it ruins the Characters from the Manga/Anime. To make the game feel challenging, they are using drastically lowered stats for your goal keeper, while keeping the actual stats for the enemy goalie - which basically means that Wakabayashi - the SGGK that never lets anything but Schneiders Fire Shot past him if shot from outside the Penalty Area gets his ass whopped by any super shot fired from his side off the field. I have played the Story for about 10h (skipping most dialoges after the first playtrough to have more gameplay time) and I have yet to see him catch any serious shot even from the middle of the field.Characters like Hyuga on the otherhand manage to fail to score a goal sometimes even from inside the Penalty Area even with a fully charged Neo Tiger Shot. At somepoint I just wish the Shots where rarer or harder to do but just feel more .... meaningful?So, here a quick TL:DR:Is the Game fun? YesShould you buy it? SureIs Multiplayer Versus fun? Hell yes!Is it true to the Lore of the Manga? ♥♥♥♥ no... 0/10, would not reccomand to any fans of the series - great for over the top Football action though

_childDocuments_.review: To start off with, ive noticed quite a few negative reviews because of the servers and other technical issues with launch, and to sum it all up we all knew that the first couple of days were going to be rocky, but after a few patches the game will be fully stable so just wait for those before you start crying about it.Also people complaining about pack openings and the fact you 'get players' from packs with in game currency need to shut up and actually take a look at the game and how it works. There are challenges in game that allow you to acquire points that then allow you to open packs to get player cards that help level them up and unlock different moves to use in the game. There is not a single ounce of pay to win or unfairness here whatsoever, everybody has the same chance to get the same rewards you just have to play and see what you get, so again stop complaining. As for the gameplay and story, im working my way through the 'my player' story mode as i write this and so far ive been very surprised with the level of customisation and how good the gameplay actually is. Anybody that enjoys FIFA or PES and also enjoys anime will enjoy the game, theres plenty of inspiration from those games here that people will definitely love. All in all if youre looking for a fun game with some good mechanics with a lot of multiplayer/Esports potential then definitely consider this game.

Yeah they come from the same idea, but this is more like an anime RPG.Captain Tsubasa, Oliver y Benji or Supercampeones is a saga that has been very faithful to the series, repeating over and over again the premise of a Japanese boy with his friends looking for the soccer world title, therefore it repeats the same story but not the beginnings, only the arc of the V3 championship and the international youth tournament.I'm going to give you a series of problems that I have been collecting from users and those I found for myself:- An user named b4NG! mentions the interface is not very intuitive and always loads and connects to the server. It is extremely annoying but tolerable once you get used.- At first, the comments and dialogues were interesting, however this is because I have been following the series since my dad taught it to me, it is a game that is made for and only for fans. Whoever dont know the lore maybe dont be hooked, Likewise the game has some videos explaining the background of some characters like Genzo or Kojiro.- The online mode is a ♥♥♥♥. I only play with my friend, [EDIT: The online match-up it is an exploiters circus bacause they made their own characters who can shot and goal a lot of time, unstoppable. The road to Gold 1 (an elo) is annoying for exploiters, bots and players with a poor internet (or maybe the server is just a ♥♥♥♥)], Bandai no longer seems to support their server so it crashes or comes to load in the middle of matches just when you are playing against a player (because the ranked is dominated by players teams controlled by bots). The online match becomes technical and millimetric, you have to have the server on your side to at least pass some since it seems that the catenaccio (the v-zone ability always wins in the opponent's defence field) is passive for all players in this game mode.- The gameplay is technical and tedious, you must have control over the millimetre what you must do, the problem lies in the monotony that the game always is what shot will beat the goalkeeper, because in this game if your shot doesnt have a critical rate, then the gk always catch the ball and depends on your shot strength to beat him. Another problem that I see, the animations are bored after the 4-5 game that you play against normal character (offline mode/online too) and this show how quickly they wanted to launch the game because of the income it would generate. It is noticeable because in the DLCs of the players (character pass) they could have brought you the equipment and even introduced them as a cameo to the story (bandai made their own history) but they only designed to include the players and that's it.- The customization is very wasted since they could easily give you more than just 5 teams to fill, instead of having to do it player by player (yes, there is a story mode to create your OC) you could play it 1-2-3 times to unlock skills and a section to create players (which seems to only have 18-20 slots) BUT NO, they force you to replay many times and with luck you make your team to have a good time for 3 hours and just close the game. A lot of investment time for just empty minutes of play.I know I said a lot of bad things but there are truly good things and many others that are there for fans of the saga who would hug the game as if it were a newborn puppy and if I could tell easy and economical ways to improve the game I would do them. I hope to bandai make it a moddable game because despite of bad things, it is a good game.At least i recommend and play it, make your teams and lets play with me if you wantMy discord is Matutuh

No lag at all for me.Cons:- Gotta play this on 1920 x 1080 and cannot be played properly on 2560 x 1440 or higher resolution.- Game speed bugs out if you play on a monitor above 60 HZ. Just change your monitor's refresh rate to 60 HZ at 1920 x 1080 and the game should run fine.- I think the game is incomplete, seems like I could only play through Tsubasa's storyline for one season. Finished Story mode in like 5 hours. I hope there is more content coming up.- Through Pass can be buggy at times. Feels like a direct pass instead.Do not wait for a sale! Even if you do manage to pull off that feat you have to wear down their goalie with multiple shots, against near perfect AI, to achieve a goal. Even if you do manage to keep them from getting the ball past midfield, two cutscenes will trigger giving them 2 effortless goals. The first, with the Twin Goal kick, happened when I was in possession about to score - CUTSCENE - they magically obtain a point. The second is at the start of the second half where as soon as they get possession a cutscene triggers and they score again.There are reports of people having to do this 4-5 times to succeed. I've done my five, and done. This isn't fun. It is rank bull manure that just isn't fun and I question how this made it past any form of QA without it being flagged as rank bull manure that will turn people off.If you are holding off on purchasing, continue to do so until they patch this asinine rank bull manure. Apparently, that patch won't arrive until Mid-October 2020, and by then there are some amazing games that will be out that will probably make you forget about this asinine cheap rank bull manure.It just isn't fun not being able to skip insta-point cutscenes and facing an unfair uphill battle where your time is cut short by instapoint cutscenes. That is just asinine. Game was fun, but challenging right up until it went full rank bull manure.F this game.## UPDATE ## Apparently you can disable these cutscenes, but that sucks the fun and point of going through the single player story, which is meant to be an introduction to gameplay mechanics and characters before going into create-a-character mode. The sudden difficulty spike after barely 2 hours of gameplay presents a ridiculous roadblock that sours the experience of this game. Hopefully with the 2.0 patch this will be fixed. If it is addressed, I'll reassess my review.

_childDocuments_.review: Never heard of it, but looked like a cool game with that anime art style.  So I picked it up.  I kinda expected a lackluster port at best, because it's Bandai (life pro tip, if you see a fringe anime game, it's probably a Bandai Port, and if it is, it's likely to be very flawed).  Booted it via remote play from my steam deck (to not install it on my steam deck to save space) and the game won't accept control inputs (Xinput commands) from remote play via steam input.  Now I could probably just edit those controls to key presses to work, but I didn't.  Why?  Because upon tinkering with it, I found that if you select to change an input in the joystick mapper in game, the game will only respond to a joystick input.  There's no way to close it, there is no timeout timer.  You are left to only plug in a controller and press a button to assign it, or close the game with alt tab.  This is flat out poor design.  I refuse to go any further.  Maybe one day I'll pick this game up, but for now, I've lost any interest I've had to play it.  I can't recommend you buy it, as someone who buys everything, and will usually find a positive even with bad ports, I am saying, flat out DON'T BUY THIS GAME.  If you like anime, there are plenty of hentai games or something on Steam.  If you like soccer, play Fifa.  If you think you want this Anime Soccer game, you don't.  I could jump through hoops to fix the game and make it playable for me.  But why?  It was on sale and an interesting looking game.  I've lost that intrigue.  This is why ports need to be better.  Because you loose potential customers that will expand your brand.  People who pass by and say "hey, the marketing on this looks neat" will leave if the game is inconvenient to play.  That is what has happened here.  Again, do NOT buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: To those of you who have rescue animals, interacting with this game´s Ai director is sort of like trying to befriend and eventually rescue a stray, feral cat.At best, you can sort of predict what it wants from you, and by working with it and recognizing it´s behaviors and what it reacts positively to, you can have a wholesome time and enjoy it´s quirky personality.However, you have to always keep in mind that this creature is easily startled and that any time, it can turn tight controls and ace players into unresponsive passes straight to the enemy players and defenders that run away from the ball, apparently in a hurry to sign autographs in the stands, allowing the CPU to score.Overall, the experience is worth it, and if you are a fan of Captain Tsubasa you are going to love it, however, make sure you adapt to it´s needs and behaviour, and do understand it may sometimes scratch you.When it happens, however, do try to remember that deep down it appreciates you being there and that if you let it,  with experience (and patches) you can end up making a lifelong friend.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very fun to play. The goalkeeper is the final boss every match lol. If you are a Captain Tsubasa fan, you will like this game.  Although not deep, the game has certain degree of strategy and some system that make the experience more dynamic.Again, if you are a fan, this game can be extremely fun and enjoyable.The game has a lot of technical issues that I cannot believe were not tested before release plus it uses the same crappy anti-cheat engine Alicization Lycoris does. I might stop buying Bandai Namco games if they continue with this practice.These issues are being resolved slowly. As for this moment Namco Bandai has released two patches, mostly addressing the constant crashes.1) When going into full screen mode the icons and text get messed up. I don't know how to explain it, I've never seen this happen. There are two solutions: playing in windowed mode (issue happens in borderless window mode too) or using external software Borderless Gaming. Anyways, this is unacceptable specially for the price they are charging.[2) Random crashes. These can happen on loading screens, during matches, in the main menus, etc. The game just freezes and becomes unresponsive. I'm going to try disabling the cheat engine. From experience with Lycoris the anti-cheat engine might be the cause of this.[After deleting some files and checking the cashes integrity, which made Steam re-obtain the files, this issues has not happened in over 3 hours of gameplay in between Tsubasa mode and New Hero Mode.3) Can't get rid of  mouse pointer. Even if using a gamepad, the mouse pointer does not go away. It is quite distracting even if I move it to the corners of the screen.4) Low or unsteady framerate. Personally I haven't experienced this (the game runs fine with or without Vertical Sync for me) but some people are reporting that game runs at a very low framerate when V-Sync is enabled and the game running at "double the speed" when V-Sync is off.4) Where are the pre-order and deluxe edition contents?At this time, even with with some of the issues remaining, I'm having a blast with this game. After I finished Tsubasa mode I was a bit disappointed, but then I went to Hew Hero mode and realized that Tsubasa was barely an introduction to what this game has to offer. I can see myself, easily, spending 20+ hours won single player mode alone. I will now recommend this this, but be aware: there are still technical issues that remain but Bandai Namco has already patched the day twice in less than  a week so we can expect these issues to be solved.
