_childDocuments_.review: I've always wanted to play a successor to the Tecmo Cup NES game and I was on the fence for quite some time on this one, especially given the mixed reviews and tecnichal limitations.I've been playing the game on Deck after having read there's a few tricks that can be done in order to bypass the error that prevents it from launching successfully. Just search for Tsubasa RONC Deck and you'll find a helpful thread on the Steam forums. The game runs great on Deck, just apply all bells and whistles and limit the game to 45 Hz / 45 FPS for a smooth, silent and stable, well-performing game.As for the game itself: It's a lot of fun with the rock-paper-scissors method of dribble moves, knowing when to launch shots and tackles, and seeing over the top animations. The in-game tutorials are quick and not very good at explaining on how to really create a strong customer character though. Also, the two main menus are confusing.The biggest downside is that there's a huge shop for ingame items, which can be bought with real money. However, the two main campaigns do not rely on this and you're perfectly able to recreate the Tops team with Robin, Kevin, Brett and Brooke if you'd want so. With each match being limited to just a few reallife minutes, the rush is always on and even at the lowest difficulty level, it's a challenge. The campaigns scale automatically, in a rather fair yet unnoticable manner. There's a huge amount of story dialogue, too much, but it can be switched off once you've seen it all.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bit of a very soft recommendation because this game ultimately disappointed me. The core gameplay is fun, the style is exactly what you'd expect and hope for, and it generally delivers what it promised. Almost.I expected a fast-paced, action-focused football/soccer game that captured the essence of the Captain Tsubasa show/manga (which, while it never was a huge part of my childhood, I remember fondly) and had some story to it.I kinda got that, but I also got a hundred loot drops I had to click through when opening the game, being forced into the multiplayer menu before the game even told me there were single player modes (of course, I knew they were there, I was just momentarily confused) and a game that, while not a mobile game, seems to occasionally glance in the direction of mobile titles and contort its eyebrows really hard trying to get you to look over there. So yeah, the core game does deliver, and it's a refreshingly different experience from FIFA (more akin to old International Superstar Soccer on the N64), but the fact that it's pushing its multiplayer component way too desperately rubs me the wrong way - especially given the other reviews here that point at that function being utterly broken anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi there! I'm here to give you some insight from someone who wasn't a Tsubasa fan when the game came out and someone who isn't a fan of football. If you're interested, feel free to read this review!So... what did I think?I'm a fan now! I've revived my appreciation for football (I tried watching a match but I find it slow and boring, so I'll limit my excitement for cartoons.) I get these memories from back in the day when I loved to watch football shows with my brother. This game made me love the series like the Naruto and Dragon Ball games did more than a decade ago. I'm overjoyed!Why did I buy the game?Well... the fact there was a Dutch team piqued my interest, and I'm glad it did! Love me some Dutch representation in my animoes. Remember this Dutch samurai guy from this anime I don't know? Super fun! He speaks perfect Dutch and everything! Also props to the localizers for adding "leuk" in Kluivoort's dialogue, I noticed and I love it!Now the game itself.I think the matches are super fun! Not as chaotic like the Mario Strikers games (please Nintendo, make a new one) but it's filled with over the top shots, dribbles and passes. I took time to learn the controls and while there is enough jank to frustrate some of you, I still have a blast! There are enough bugs to be found in this game that makes me kinda frustrated and other times it makes me laugh. All in all it's not perfect, far from it, but for their first time this is a fantastic game!Online?Ech, not an online guy. I just love to create characters, play matches with my favorite players, get pumped every time I watch Tsubasa's Miracle Drive Shot and mock England's team for being... just there. I've heard that the meta isn't great and that people can abuse their custom characters to make the matches unfair so I'm in support for making online better but I'm probably never partaking in it. Good luck on the battlefield, voetbal kamaraden!The PC port...Oh no... It's pretty mediocre, bad even. From day one the game was riddled with issues I've never seen before. Text scaling was so bizarre, the speed of the game being sped up if you own a high refresh rate monitor. I had to play my first few hours in windowed mode on my TV. You can unlock the framerate but the V-sync doesn't really work so... and the game breaks in half if there isn't a 60 or 30fps lock enabled. Poor Pierre... his super shot just doesn't work when shot outside the penalty area... The devs are putting in effort to fix this though! Patch 1.07While the scaling issues was resolved a while ago, I got around the speed bug by leaving and entering fullscreen with alt+enter. The game ran perfectly at 4K60 for me with only the Fire Shot (ironic) effecting my performance somewhat. But since patch 1.07 the devs decided to take one step back for our g-sync warriors and ruin the fps anyway. G-sync doesn't work anymore and the game is locked at 33fps (22 at 30fps lock.) Unlocking it breaks the game in half, that isn't fixed yet but oh boy... I got around it with a fix in the command center but it's a big bummer... I have faith in you, devs. Please fix this! And the new CC shop? Outside extra waiting times to enter the customization shop (can be fixed by fixing the servers, again) I'm not personally bother by it. I get people's concerns and if the devs and Bandai Namco decide to enter Activision territory by adding microtransactions... yeah that's a big no no. I leave my review on positive, despite all the problems. I hope the devs put their all into fixing it! But if we ever get a sequel... it's gonna be an absolute BANGER.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun for a bit.. not worth the hefty price tag at all though. Pros1. That strong dose of nostalgia when you see your childhood characters play out the shaolin-soccer'esque match you always wanted to control. 2. New Hero mode - Especially with Musashi FC, makes you feel like you are part of the story.  This mode is where I spent most of my time. Once you're at the International stage though it just feels like you're an extra in a movie. Cons1. PvP is a pain - network stability is the worst ever with players skipping all over the place.PvE is .. well they want you to believe that the dribble/slide is a rock-paper-scissor mechanism; but when the CPU decides it, its rock-paper-shotgun.One of the worst ways to cheese cpu-difficulty. 2. The camera is a disaster, especially with the dialogue boxes that come up on the sides and obscure what little view you have of the field ahead even more.3. The AI is a disaster, you will see them trail a loose ball all the way to the sidelines without making an effort to retrieve it - this will happen more often than you would want it to. Even if the opponent's shot rebounds, defenders just casually run back to their 'designated positions' on the field with no worry about the opposing FW running to collect the loose ball.  If not for the mask of a beloved franchise, this game would just be average at best on its own. more or less 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: This review is referring to the SINGLE PLAYER offline aspect of the game. The ONLINE aspect deserves a ZERO. It is simply not functional, so if you are interested in online games, stay away as this is almost a scam. If you are into single player, read on!This game is GREAT!First things first: bugs and online disservice. Terrible, unforgivable and Namco should be ashamed. But I do not review games for their bugs, I care about gameplay and content.And this game is AMAZING. Sure, you have to be a fan of anime and in particular of Captain Tsubasa (Holly & Benji), which means you were probably born in the 70s, but if that is the case then you probably also miss soccer games of that era, definitely arcade and not bothering too much with realism and more with fun.Well, this game is just that great. It captures the spirit of some of the best of that era, like the legendary Kick and Run, and sprinkles some Pro Evolution Soccer/Winning Eleven on top of it, while maintaining its anime spirit with some of the most clean, sharp and pleasant to watch anime visuals and animations I've ever seen in a videogame. In short Captain Tsubasa is FUN to play, both versus the AI and other human players. It helps that the game perfectly supports Steam Remote Play Together, which means you can seamlessly invite your friends from Steam to play with you even if they don't own the game and they don't even have to install anything! It's like playing on the couch together, like in the 80s, except they are social distanced by default.Now, if you add on top of all that a LOT of story content, which I was absolutely not expecting, then you have a great game that is gonna keep you for a long time no matter the price. You have the short "Original" story, and then you have the Create your own Character story which takes place at an international tournament where you get to befriend all the characters from the show in what ends up being like a huge visual/kinetic novel about soccer, Captain Tsubasa, and you. And it's super long and it's like watching a new anime, but you are in it and you have to win the actual matches yourself!This is a bit of a dream come true. I was hyped about this game but was expecting a huge disappointment. It turned out to be fun to play and with tons of story to unravel in a very high quality visual format for the genre. I couldn't be happier. If you are a fun of Captain Tsubasa this is a MUST-HAVE as it's better than you'd dream.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is actually great. The main bulk of the gameplay is (unexpectedly) not the super shots, but rather the battle for ball possession. _childDocuments_.review: After a 14 years break from Home consoles, and 10 absent from handheld ones Tsubasa franchise finally makes it back to our screens. The game is best described as an arcade anime game crossed with a visual novel.The game focuses on Tsubasa and his team on their third try at nationals, or if you created your own character, any one of the Nankatsu, Toho or Musashi middle schools. As weird as that sounds the FIFA inspired soccer gameplay isn't the game's main draw - it's the cleverly setup interruptions to it. The story mode triggers some of the more important scenes from the anime while you struggle with the enemy team, making it feel like an episode from one of the excellent Tsubasa shows - in that way, the main draw isn't the gameplay offered at all, but reminding you of Tsubasa's heartwarming story of stoicism and fairplay.The release was a bit rocky, but I didn't have any gameplay problems aside from the first tutorial match having bugged spirit bars if you don't shoot with tsubasa during the L1 buff, and the online capabilities were restored with a patch shortly after release.You can take a more in depth look with

_childDocuments_.review: As you can tell by my played time on record, I've invested a lot into this game since release, however I can't give it a positive review because there's too much bad compared to the good it has, the animations are good and the graphics are accurate enough, unfortunately that's about where the good things stop, the gameplay is generally speaking ok, but this isn't a football game, it's an anime fighting game masquerading as a football one (which is really what the anime and manga were).All this time after release, the game is still not optimized, some stadiums and settings will cause any amount of issues from FPS drops to visual glitches to outright crashes to desktop, this happens a lot specially online, since the stadium/setting you get there is random, and speaking of online, the servers are terrible, you get either huge lag or DCs fairly often, resulting in a loss, dropping sportsmanship points (which can get your account temporarily suspended), sometimes characters get stuck halfway into an animation, you will often also get a massive black box in the middle of your screen warning that you're commiting a violation for not pressing any buttons, even if you're holding down the key/button for pressing/chasing the opponent carrying the ball.The new hero mode where you make your custom characters also has its issues, the most eggregious one for me being when I'm locked out of specific routes because the game decided to skip the required cutscenes despite me having all the requirements up to that point, and the online-based roster which is used to save the characters you make is also bugged, in order to "unlock more online-based roster character slots" you're required to spend the premium online currency, of which you get a tiny amount per week or you can spend real money on, I wasted around 6k of these to increase the amount of characters I could save there, only to find out literally none of the characters I had saved were actually there, it's been bugged since they released this feature many months ago, and I doubt they plan to fix it.Overall if you liked the franchise from the manga/anime and would like to play something related to it, go ahead, but the game isn't good, so be aware of what you're getting into, buy it on sale if you must, it's not worth paying full price for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright take this review from someone who has played 15 hours so far.What I am going to say is this, is the price worth the game? It depends. Are you a captain tsubasa fan? You've been waiting for this game yes. Otherwise it depends on your experience with the game hands on. play almost 2 hours of it, and the answer will be clear. if you don't like it, refund.Pros:-Online mode doesn't use micro-transactions for upgrading your team. Actually, there are no microtransactions at all besides the dlc one time purchase.-Story mode pulls you in if your a fan or even a new player.-there's a whole separate story mode for your own personal character.-character creation is in depth and very well made.-if you like anime over the top fun then this game has that for sure.-fun characters and awesome character designs.-this game has heart and clearly has hard work shown in its design and gameplay.-Music is awesome and puts you in the mood to play over the top.-When playing, you need to be smart about how you play each character and passing is important.-You can choose to dribble past five people as if your the mc as long as you play the game correctly.-V Zone is an awesome idea.-Creators of the game are trying to fix the problems with the game, so at least they aren't ignoring them and are actually trying.Cons:-Game has some bugs regarding crashing, though i myself only crashed twice on day one and never again since.-Bugs regarding moments when playing. (Such as character freezes and sliding across map).-Story mode cutscenes are meh, I wish they animated them more rather than a visual novel with 3d moving models talking.-Bug: Day 1-2 i crashed after winning a match and cutscenes sometimes in story mode.-Bug: Tsubasa sometimes freezes and stops moving or doing anything.-Bug: Online mode has problems in regards to bots, during the rookie league you will run into many bots. you may or may not be stuck facing bots grinding free wins.-Bug: Character models may lose their face when a defensive player blocks a shot at the goalie.-This game has lots of bugs, but to be fair, its been out for three days. _childDocuments_.review: Well, after completing both story modes and currently having over 26 hours (yes I played this for 2 whole days), I feel like I can finally review this game.Story mode: There are 2 story modes, one takes about 4 hours to complete while the other takes around 10. Both stories are extremely well developed from voice acting to actual gameplay. Depending on how you play you will trigger different events mid-game that will either just showoff some cool animation or result on an actual goal, however all this events are avoidable depending on how you play them. In the first story mode you pretty much play the entire nationals arch from the anime while on the other one you create your own character and compete against other national teams.Online: Unlike what other people are saying, it isn't broken, it literally says "Season: none" in other words the ranked season hasn't started yet however it allows u to earn online rewards by playing against bots which is a little odd but alright. It also allows you to create private lobbies and play with and or against friends.Gameplay: The game is actually extremely well balanced and the overall controls feel pretty smooth. It's not easy to score goals in general and you'll most likely need around 3 shots to the goal until you get one. The animations are very well connected to your actions and everything just feels really nice.As someone who has been playing Fifa since Fifa 2011 I can assure that this game is very similar quality wise to it plus it offers a really good connection the anime style. I would highly recommend this game and it honestly kinda hurts to see so many bad reviews, a lot of them being completely wrong.Extra: There are packs of players that can only be used in story mode, this does NOT affect multiplayer so don't let yourself get tricked by reviews that say so.Rating: 9/10

name: When The Past Was Around
detailed_description: From Brigitta Rena, the creator of A Raven Monologue and She & The Light Bearer . When the Past was Around is an adventure point-and-click puzzle game about love, moving on, letting go, and the joy and pain of everything in between. This is the story of Eda, a girl in her early 20s. Like anyone in her age, she’s lost. She lost her way in the journey to achieve her dreams. She lost her way in the journey to find love. That until she met The Owl. The man that would help her burn her passion, the man that would help her find the spark in a relationship, and also the man that would teach her about heartbreak. The game tells a bittersweet tale between a girl and her lover in a surreal world consisting of disjointed rooms from memories and time. With each gathered clue, solved puzzles, and unlocked door, the girl will find her way, unraveling the secrets between her and her lover, the secrets which she used to know. Features: A picture speaks a thousand words. Experience the game’s story not through words nor dialogues but beautifully hand-drawn art created by famous Indonesian artist, Brigitta Rena. A short, sweet and whimsical journey. Explore a bittersweet tale between a girl and her lover in a surreal world consisting of disjointed rooms of memories and time. Personal and ubiquitous. a game about overcoming the past and finding the self. Solve brain-teasing puzzles. Various intriguing puzzles to solve and stories to uncover. Let the music guide you. Atmospheric violin music will accompany you from the peaceful days to the angstiest moments When The Past Was Around is a short silent narrative experience that can be finished in less than 2 hours. Even though it is a short game, we’ve put all our hearts into delivering a deep and meaningful experience for you. We hope that the brief moment you spend with Eda and Owl would be priceless and unforgettable.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game, and I instantly bought it. Now, I don't normally play point and click adventures, and I'm not the greatest at puzzles. I am a huge sucker for lore and delicate details. I have a long, inside joke with my boyfriend. A lot of the times we will joke about him being an owl. To add onto that, funnily enough, I look like Eda. I read the bio of the game and I knew I had to at least try it.I'm not gonna air out my dirty laundry, but just as everyone else in the world, I've had my conflicts- especially relationship conflicts. I have felt everything Eda has felt, from warm love to the cold, slow aching in your chest that forces you to curl up in a ball.  Playing through this game felt as if I was watching a short film of the loveliest moments I've collected over time with my significant other, along with the difficulties that came with it. I know my particular connection with this game is extremely niche and unique, but I encourage others to play it. If you enjoy having your heartstrings pulled a few times, or are looking for something quaint and small to try, I urge you to give it a chance. The puzzles were great! It made me use my brain (which I don't do most of the time, so the smoke from my head and tears in my eyes made it hard to think). The quiet, cute music made it feel like something cozy you could curl up to with a cup of hot coco and take a nice nap after. When The Past Was Around is on the shorter end, but the story's emotional impression reminds us we're human (and it sticks).I finished the game and laid in the living room face down on the floor until my owl noticed. I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: Looking for an emotional rollercoaster and do not want to read lots of text? Then  – it masterfully presents its message through just pictures and music while touching your very soul with its wordless beauty. If anybody ever tells you that games are not work of art, show them this title. To begin with, I cannot but complement the developers that created this little gem. It is just SO beautiful in every aspect! The artwork is magnificent, and it was obvious just from the screenshots. In the game itself, all pictures look even better. I love this kind of art style – with lots of neat details, calm colors and a bit fairy-tale-like. Music is also enchanting, and all UI features have their own violin sounds. As I have already mentioned above, there is one tune that is the main connecting point for all parts of the story, and trust me, it will touch your heart the very moment you hear it.What else…ah, right! The point-and-click parts. It is definitely not a hidden-objects game, even though yes, you will need to search for some items. And yes, you do have an inventory. But still, there are no outlines of the objects that you need to find, nor any words that tell you what you need. So, compared to classical examples of the genre – such as many games by bigfish or Artifex Mundi, - I would say that Then When The Past Was Around is definitely a point-and-click title. This part aside, there are enough interactive features to keep you entertained through the whole story.Speaking of the puzzles, all of them are really interesting, even though several still confused me. My main advice here is to look for clues. Some are well-hidden and require major brain work, while others are in the open sight or will come in later. So try to be as be attentive as possible, it is worth it.Oh, by the way, as a good example of why rushing through this game is a bad idea, let me tell you the epic tale of my grandiose stupidity. There was a puzzle with numbers that you need to find somewhere. I immediately noticed several leads and started cracking them. Combination after combination, I began doubting both myself and the game: is it broken? Is there some kind of glitch? Why is not it working?! An hour later, I gave up and brought my mother into the fight. We both searched for clues, tried mixing numbers and just everything possible, but once again nothing worked. ‘OK’, I said and started bugging two of my close friends. They also decided to join my epic battle with the puzzle and offered their own suggestions. An hour and a half have passed…I was almost ready to just close the game and leave it before I decided to throw my laptop out of the window. And then, finally, it hit me! The solution was in front of me the whole damn time – and I just decided to overlook it. It was so simple, and yet I spent 90 minutes chasing an absolutely different thing. Well, my friends and mum definitely had a good laugh at my expense when I told them what I was doing wrong. And so did I, to be honest, because my mistake was hilarious. So, boys, girls and young individuals, do not repeat my mistake! In the end, the only thing I can say is do not think twice: buy this masterpiece right away. And then spend a bit more money and purchase the artbook and the soundtrack too.  is worth every coin and minute you spend on it, and its touching story will leave you craving for more. The best part is that it is both inspiring and mysterious until the very end - it leaves some unanswered questions, but does not feel unfinished; instead, this game lets your imagination run free. And it is amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: We often hear motivational things as children like "Follow your dreams." or "You can be anything you want to be."  But eventually we learn that sometimes all we can dream about is someone who is gone, and all we want to be is near them again.When time starts skipping like a needle across an old record, and your brain just can't handle the blank space that suddenly appeared.  As you go on with life but any little thing can suddenly send your mind rushing back.  It could be a ringing phone, a glimpse of someone from the corner of your eye, a book on the table, or maybe just a few notes of a song, and that someone is real again, for a second.  Like waves pushing you back.  Unsteady on your feet for a moment, then you move on.This game is about someone navigating that bittersweet space between the joy of being with someone you love, and learning to live without it.  A story about being in the present, but struggling with another time. A time When The Past Was Around.

_childDocuments_.review: is a short adventure game and is one of the best examples of wordless storytelling out there. For people who are on the fence about this game, there's the prologue (Chapter 0) that is available on a separate store page. This game is short and took me less than 2 hours to get through its 5 additional chapters aside from the prologue. But it's an absolute gem in its presentation, with the wonderful art and appropriate (lovely and jarring) sounds. I have to say after playing through the prologue almost a year ago, the wait was worth the experience. A lot of times demos show you the best parts of a game and the rest may be a downward trend in quality, this game only builds on that zeroth chapter and fulfills the set expectations. The story builds on the memories of the protagonist Eda through metaphors of her relationship with Owl. Really, play the prologue if you are curious how it starts.Several chapters, each with a few connected rooms with some puzzles within. The puzzles are fairly straight forward for the most part, only a couple gave me a bit of trouble but I eventually realized that I was staring at the answers the entire time, and just couldn't put two and two together. Made for a couple of good chuckles from me in just how hidden things may be, in plain sight. I think some of the puzzle designs are really good, and I was pleased by the quality of them.You only need a mouse, as long as it's connected and moves the cursor around on your computer and can click.The artwork is wonderful. You only need to look at the screenshots on the store page to see.Lovely music and really very fitting sounds. There are 18 tracks in the OST for a game that takes less than 2 hours to complete. So you know for a fact that the music plays a significant part of the game's overall experience.People who want to be emotionally involved in a wordless story would love this game. You can also dive in to enjoy the wonderful sights and sounds. Enjoy the well-designed and fun puzzles, though there are not many in numbers. Does this sound like you? If so, what are you waiting for?Some people are going to be caught up by the $7.99 USD price tag, because it's so short. For me, it's half the price of a movie ticket, and takes about the same amount of time. And I certainly enjoyed my time with this game more than many movies. is an indie gem that should be recognized for its quality. You can tell just how much love and care went into the game playing through it. I only wish it were longer. But that's okay, it just leaves me to look forward to the next title by this awesome team.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

Or - at the MINIMUM - set up a photosensitivity warning on the store page.

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous and meaningful hand drawn, click and point game. The puzzles to get through were quite interesting and I appreciate that they weren't *too* easy. I love games with no dialogue as you can experience the story in your own way. For me I viewed this as a story about relationships, grief and love, that no matter how much time has passed you will always have warm memories of someone. The grief aspect showed me that it's hard to accept when someone is gone too. I really enjoyed playing through this, I'm usually a crier in these types of games but I didn't get emotional with it - though the story and art style nonetheless was very expressive and just lovely.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautiful, both in art style and in soundtrack. However, the game is way too short to fulfil what it proposes to do. The game states it's about love, moving on, letting go and the joy and pain in between, however, it unfortunately failed to make me feel any of this - mostly because it did not develop any of this. You have a scene where the couple first meets, then some time they spend together, then the sickness and death of The Owl, and then the process of grievance and moving on through music. Each of this is given only one small and quick scene, way too short and shallow.On the very same thematic, being a puzzle game with no speech, The Last Day of June delivers a way better experience, in my opinion, and I would recommend that over this any day.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game in a Valentine's Humble Bundle, saw it had good ratings and went in blind, assuming it'd be a dating sim like the others in the bundle. Boy was I wrong. This is a story about loss and all the fun that entails: grief, supressing memories, blocking emotions, and so on. I was not expecting it at all, and the thing is, last summer I lost my dear life companion and I'm so, so, sooo far from done grieving. It caught me by surprise, had me in tears all throughout once I realised what was going on, especially **SOFT SPOILER ALERT** . It really hit too close to home.Anyway, it's a beautiful -albeit short- story. I finished the game in like 2 hours (although I did leave it running between breaks, and thus the 6 hour record). Cool Japanese vibes too... reminded me of 'The Girl from the Other Side' manga, for some reason. I highly recommend playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: is a simple hidden object puzzle game. The game may only take about 2 hours to complete, but it’s touching and endearing. Without using any words, the game tells a story of love, loss and grief that will likely tug at your heartstrings. Complemented by charming drawings, and a lovely soundtrack that features a beautiful eight-note motif, you’re more likely to remember  for its story than its gameplay. However, that’s fine with me because this is one of those games that you slip in between long, intense game sessions. It reminds us that there are some really great small indie titles out there for us to discover, and sometimes a short game can be more impactful because of its brevity.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bittersweet tale of losing someone so special that you can't let go, yet the journey from grief to healing, familiar to so many of us, is all here in a beautiful packaged experience.  There's no words to tell the story -- just the atmospheric soundtrack, the whimsical art, and the small puzzles to push the tale forward.And it works.  You interact with everything and try to figure out how to "escape" each room, a rather light point and click adventure system that is there to set the mood of each scene while not being the focus of the experience per se.It gets to the point that, as the story advances, the solutions to the puzzles become harder to find, involving frantically looking for anything that could be a clue in the past and present, breaking furniture, scribbling notes on paper, and only then allowing the protagonist to move forward with her grief.  It's a nice touch.That sense of unease, the emotional connection, the joy and sorrow, learning to use the past as a stepping stone... all in all, a short experience but one I'm glad to have enjoyed.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: Eda used to be a passionate girl being emotionally attached to music played by her own and her beloved Owl. The sound of music accompanied her everyday’s calm and cozy routine… such a peaceful lifestyle we often take as granted while being accustomed to our environment formed by brief moments of peace and the presence of our beloved ones.But what happens, if one day your cherished one won’t be there granting their presence anymore?The outcome will most likely result the same as the story of Eda who is stuck with her past memories, grieving and not willing to let go. She is lost once again, but a sweet and nostalgic melody opens up a path towards reviving the precious memories, and, finally… a bittersweet smile takes form on her face.This is a ~2h long point & click game which you get to experience on emotional level – instead of reading through the story or hearing dialogues you will have an illustrated adventure accompanied by relaxing music and characterized by soft color palettes. While the main trait of the game is that it is presented as surreal and very cozy and calming, the touched themes are not easy-going; quite the opposite in fact.The game is formed by the prologue followed by 5 chapters that recount the various stages of Eda’s relationship with Owl.You will have to solve puzzles and interact with the objects in order to progress with the story and discover the couple’s past.I was really looking forward to trying out this title and after completing it, I can confirm it is a wholesome little game that makes you think after reaching the ending.While the topic may be hard to swallow this game is recommended to those seeking for peace, a meaning of life and, maybe a push towards appreciating the little things we have.Suggested to public enjoying beautifully portrayed story rich games with a message to convey.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: When the Past Was Around is a very warm, atmospheric, and gentle game about love and how it doesn’t fade even after years, rather the memories remain with us, transforming as we grow with them. It is a bittersweet story at its core, highlighting the journey of moving on and letting go.It resembles Florence, so if you liked that, it can be a good choice. It is a point-and-click journey with puzzles (there are some harder ones, but most of them are quite easy), and I really appreciated the fact that the game is without narration, so it’s all on you how you imagine the story between Eda and Owl.The visuals, artwork, and music of this game are super cute. I liked the art style so much that I bought the separate Artwork, and I honestly recommend it as it displays how the characters were born and made to interact with each other. <3
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art and story, it's quite simple yet entertaining.A very simplistic point and click, a short game no longer than 2 and a half hours, three at most but with a very cute story about grief and the process of mourning, treasuring good old memories while learning to let go. There is not much to be said, if you enjoy short point & Click games with good art and a great story, this is for you!

The message is nice, but the game failed to make me feel things as I thought it would, and the puzzles were annoying sometimes. It felt a bit like a school project when two people work separately then copy paste everything on word.I'm still giving it a thumbs up because of the amazing art and the fact that the game deals with grief, which is not something you find everyday, but I really wish it had captivated me more.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very quiet story, despite the large amount of beautiful music. Memories of the love of the girl Eda and the Owl are slowly spreading warm paint over the canvas of the story. Memory can heal or it can hurt, burdening a bleeding heart with constant reminders of a heavy loss. That is why the fragile girl Eda travels through the labyrinths of her memory, trying to let go of what must be released. The plot, albeit not very long, but worked out by the authors from the first to the last word. They manage to avoid the falsehood that such stories about love and death are so dangerous with, by maximizing the emotional connection between the player and the main character. The game throbs like a living heart, sensitively capturing the slightest changes in the mood of the plot. The gameplay is in quite popular genre "Escape room", where we need to find and use objects, as well as solve puzzles, which will allow us to progress through the plot. The difficulty is varied, but most of it can be dealt without a lot of sweat on the back. The game looks and sounds just amazing, in everything here you can feel the soulfulness that its creators put into the game. This is a truly emotional and incredibly intense adventure that cannot leave indifferent a person who knows how to feel. Great job.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: As someone going through the stages of loss myself, this delightful game created a positive shift in my own life and outlook.  I cannot thank the developers enough for that gift.The concept of Owl is brilliant.  Without a human face, his meaning is not dictated and he is a bold, constant reminder of the treasure the gamer lost in real life "staring you in the face".  It is really amazing how this game does not shrink away from indescribable loss, but accesses the gamer's emotions flawlessly to promote positive change. The game structure is also conducive to psychological healing, allowing you to revisit chapters and identify your phases of pain, loss, and acceptance.  Some of the puzzles needed more refinement before release, but none of them are so difficult that they cannot be cracked without guidance.Highly recommended to those living with painful losses that they never publicly discuss.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: PROS* Art style / direction is good.* Puzzles are of two types, common point & click and the better ones, similar to IQ tests, as in they are abstract but once it clicks it makes sense.* The IQ tests are clever.* There can be noise to make the puzzles harder.* Silent. Uses symbolism for what it tries to tell.CONS* A few puzzles are not complex enough, they can be brute forced.* A bit short, take it as an "experimental" art project than a lengthy game. It feels at least 3 scenes were cut from the pictures owl keeps.Recommend to solve the puzzles on your own, the game is not long, so its only those few roadblocks before the end. If you find them hard, look back and try to come up with the logic that makes them not "random", there is such thing.The game is about loss, so it could put you in the blues if you lost something and haven't truly got over it yet.

_childDocuments_.review: When The Past Was Around is a beautiful and heart-wrenching tale of love and loss.When a game can tell you a story without a single dialogue line and pulls at your heart strings while you simply solve puzzles and observe the environment, you know it's a game done right. The music and art compliment the story perfectly; while relaxing, it's also very sad, yet absolutely beautiful at the same time. Your heart will undoubtedly break while experiencing this story.Overall, if you enjoy puzzles and point-and-click games but also want to experience an emotional story, I highly recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: Words are the principle way in which humans communicate. We loved them so much, we gather them into languages with grammars and syntax so we can put them together to express the all but simple thoughts in our minds. We can not imagine a world without words, and yet how often do they fail us. "It's something I just can't put into words." Sometimes words are not enough to say what we want to say. Sometimes you need to communicate without them.This is the form of communication that When The Past Was Around chooses to utilize. It tells a story without words. Music, images, actions and reactions. Anything that can perk your senses and move your attention, but isn't a word, is utilized by the game to slowly unravel a mysterious and emotional plot. Along the way there will be puzzles to solve and things to remember, and even a few fun secrets. When you finish the game, not a single word will have been spoken, and yet you'll feel like so much was said. You'll feel emotions in your heart that were placed their directly by the creators, but that you didn't actually interpret through language.It's an amazing sensation and will hopefully open your mind to a bigger world as we continue to explore the very limits of the medium of interactive entertainment. Because of this I highly recommend you go in as blind as possible and try to solve every puzzle without looking them up. It will be quite difficult at first, perhaps even frustrating. The very tool we use everyday in our speech is being robbed from us and taken away, of course it's going to feel foreign. But there will be a moment it begins to click, and suddenly your conscious mind will begin to fade and you'll start thinking in concepts rather than vocabulary. You'll see what's going on and understand it, but not need to say it.The story will end. You'll cry. And then you'll say, with words once again, "Wow, that was a good point-n-click game."
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: When The Past Was Around is a short and bittersweet narrative point-and-click puzzle game about newfound love, heartbreak and learning to move on and let go. The story is beautiful and sad, told without words, just pictures, scenes and music. It made me very emotional and got me bawling my eyes out at the end.The soundtrack is perfect, even though a little repetitive, but it gets better near the end. I am also in love with violins and this game just made me love them even more!I also like to point out that the other main character is an owl man, a very beautiful owl man who looks like the perfect boyfriend, which further confirms my suspicions of being a furry all along. The puzzles were relatively easy to do, so there was nothing difficult about the game.I would 100% recommend this game to people who like emotional stories.

_childDocuments_.review: A stunning visual novel (with some game mechanics) about overcoming grief and longing by traversing through memories. There is so much symbolism in this game that is difficult to understand until you reach the end. I had some issues with some of the puzzles since they aren't the most straightforward but other than that, I completely loved it. It also has some similarities to Florence by Annapurna Interactive which I loved as well (in case you wanted a similar recommendation). This game made me worried in some of the chapters, and I ended up really emotional at the end. If you're looking to cry, this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Visual art is certainly the strong point of the game, and every bit of the game is filled with the original line art, even some scenes that show up for only 1-2 seconds use a complex line art, setting up a really high standard even among similar art-based games. It is definitely an enjoyable experience to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: True love feels elusive to those who want it and fleeting to those who have it. Everyone can agree that true love is rare and is something to be treasured. The Indonesian studio Mojiken has partnered with Toge Productions to release When The Past Was Around. You might remember them for A Raven Monologue or She & The Light Bearer. If you’ve ever played one of Mojiken’s games. You will be familiar with their astonishing artwork. When the Past Was Around is a superb point & click with a touching narrative about love, pain, and letting go of the past.The game is about a young woman in her 20s named Eda. She’s just starting out in life. Like many others in the same situation, she’s a bit lost and looking for something to give her life meaning. That is until she met Owl, a musician, who like Eda also plays the violin. From the moment they meet, they know that they are made for each other and belong together. When the Past Was Around is all about the story, so I don’t want to give away too much. After their budding romance we are shown their life together, however a tragic situation unfolds. Unfortunately their romance wasn’t meant to be, so Eda has to live with this new reality. She’s forced to live with the pain, and learns to let go of the past without forgetting her most cherished memories.The artwork is simply stunning. The graphics are made using a series of hand-drawn images. These drawings are exceptional, and the artist is obviously very talented. For that alone When The Past Was Around is worth playing. I love the overall style, and how well each image convey the story. They are colorful, but still soft with their pastel colors, and represent the narrative so well. There are also several darker scenes representing Eda’s pain, and emotional turmoil. It takes a certain talent for a developer to communicate their story through visuals alone. Despite having no spoken or written narrative, When the Past Was Around still manages to convey its story, and evokes a huge emotional range. The soundtrack, like the artwork, is exceptional. The music is powerful, and portrays the emotional narrative superbly. One detail that really sets it apart is the section of the soundtrack played by a real violinist. What a thoughtful and amazing detail to add to an already very complete game. It gives more credibility to the story since When the Past Was Around is all about pleasing the senses. Furthermore it adds a tremendous amount of personality.The game is quite short, and can be finished in two to three hours if you like to take your time. However after finishing the game, I was satisfied and not left wanting. It is divided into five chapters plus a prologue.  Each chapter deals with a certain phase in Eda’s life, and is composed of many different locations. Every one of these locations is set up like of those ‘Escape Room’ type of puzzles. Each room/location has several puzzles that need to be completed before moving on. When the Past Was Around is for the most part linear. However in some puzzles, you might need to backtrack a bit. The puzzles are interesting and the majority of them fit rather well into the storyline. It’s not the kind of game where you’ll be perplexed by a puzzle. They are always logical and easily solved by reasoning alone. Most of them involve finding a specific object or deciphering a code. The puzzles are all on the easy side, but it actually works to the game advantage. The flow is never broken by getting stuck on an overly difficult puzzle. On the other hand, the puzzles being easier means that there’s not much incentive to do a second playthrough. I though that every puzzle added value to the game and enhanced the narrative. They are beautifully crafted and perfect in their simplicity.When The Past Was Around is a timeless and universal story that will reach everyone regardless of their ages. The artwork is simply breathtaking. It was a treat to play and one of the best point & click games that I’ve experienced this year. The superb aesthetics, the hauntingly beautiful music and the simplicity of its puzzles work in complete unison and perfectly complement the amazing story.  Whether you’re a fan of point & click or new to the genre, this game is for everyone and a perfect introduction to the genre. The replayability value is low unless you want to relive the story, but don’t let that stop you. It is a real hidden gem. Once in awhile you come across a game that stays with you long after you have finished playing it. When The Past Was Around is a must have whether you a fan of point & click or just appreciative of gorgeous artwork!With its stunning artwork, its beautiful soundtrack, and an emotionally charged narrative, When the Past Was Around is an absolute feast for all of your senses!

_childDocuments_.review: I was originally drawn to this game due to its hand-drawn graphics. My expectations of this game was rather sub-par due to the average game play length being a mere 2 hours or lesser. Nonetheless, the storyline for this game has exceeded my expectations although the soundtrack was repetitive and lacking after hearing it mainly throughout the game, despite all that, the soundtrack was still really good and relaxing to hear. Overall I did not regret my decision buying this game.A short storyline with no words needed about all the stages of love including every up and down you'd feel. From witnessing the mystery of a blooming love, to the happiness of the early stages of love and to the  Although I feel that this game deserves a longer storyline to capture the audiences heart, I personally believe that a 2 hour or lesser gameplay doesn't do it justice especially when it's exploring the joys of love. The predictability of the storyline is given away towards the first chapter and the viewers will already be aware of whats coming towards the ending chapters. Despite knowing the ending from the beginning, I still felt the sadness towards the end especially when I believed there was a plot twist during the after credits only to be taken back.This game utilizes the point and click as it's main style for it's puzzles. The puzzles itself are not that difficult in the beginning unlike other point and click based puzzle storyline games, the only challenging parts are mediocre at best as this game serves to be relaxing suggested from its game speed pace. The only problem is how there's a lightbulb at the top right corner of the screen which supposedly serves as a helping hand for players, except that it shows only the things that you're able to click on and not actually giving you directions or advice to help you clear the puzzles. This might be troublesome for certain younger players who might be slow in puzzles and would have to rely on outside resources for help instead. The bad point is that when you're finished with the first run through and for people who are beginning their achievement hunting run through, clicking on the wrong chapter and trying to return to the front page after going through all the cutscenes might take awhile due to it's long pace in panning out.The graphics are hand drawn and animated exceptionally well in a simplistic way whereby it's not overbearing to the eyes. The colours used throughout the game is well expressed which falls along nicely with the emotions of the characters and readers that they're trying to bring out throughout the storyline. The graphics are dark when it's meant to be mysterious or grim, light and purple when it's meant to make you feel at awe, it's just amazing in a simplistic way overall.The main soundtrack felt very lighthearted and serves as the main focal point of this game as it's the way of how it all begins. Likewise with the graphics, the soundtrack has different tunes meant to let readers know when it's expected to be sad, the tone of the soundtrack when it's far away and what not. The sound effects itself is rather done well and pleasing to hear with a pinch of reality in the objects and animal interactions used. Despite all this, the main background soundtrack may still be rather repetitive with the occasional different tunes here and there.Simple PuzzlesAdorable graphicsLovely soundtrackRelaxing gameplayGreat deal for moneyRealistic bittersweet storylineNo help hints givenRepetitive soundtrackStoryline felt too shortI extremely love the way the characters and storyline was portrayed which coincidentally felt like going through the  before learning to love yourself independently again. I just wish that they expanded more on the middle chapters but with the way it is right now, it's still a great playthrough. I'd recommend anyone that would love to relax to try out this short game of no words to just enjoy the storyline and graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this was a game that has no dialogue and relies on both graphics and the player to make connections and inferences to understand the story. For a pretty heavy topic (, it does a good job with balancing emotions. The story revolves around the character going through all stages of grief, which I think the game portrays pretty well. But, since the game does rely on graphics and being able to make those connections, it might not be as impactful for those that haven't experienced the same/similar kind of event in real life. The art was done very well, and I really liked the idea of the lover being an "owl", which just adds on to the whole surrealism of the game. The music was also really nice and very fitting for the graphics. There are some puzzles within the game, most are pretty easy. I only got stuck on two of them, one being the red box thing in the café and the other was the clock lock puzzle. It took me too long to figure out what I needed to do for the red box, but was at least able to figure it out and it did make sense to me. The clock lock puzzle, I was just completely lost. I ended up just moving the clock hands randomly until it clicked. I had no issues with any other puzzles. The biggest issue I had with the game was mainly just the moving border was a tad bit too much for me. It was a little too fast and a bit distracting. I really only felt a bit off during the prologue with the items (like the chair and desk) not lining up with the room's angle. I just had to focus on not looking at the border and it wasn't as bad in the later chapters. It might honestly just be me, but it would be nice to get an option to either slow that border down or turn its movement off. Overall, I had fun playing this game. I did end up feeling a little sad after playing the game but that is, of course, due to the game's topic. So, if you are easily affected by sad or emotional topics, just be aware. It doesn't go too in-depth with the topic, but it does have the player make inferences and connections. It is short, and I was able to beat it under 3 hours. I definitely would recommend this game, especially for fans of the shorter point and click games.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements. Minor spoilers ahead. When The Past Was Around is a fantasy and romance point and click/hidden object game with logic puzzles. It is targeted mostly at a female audience but can be enjoyed by everyone.The story is focused on the two main characters and what they experienced together and the later memories of those events. The events are sometimes retold with some surreal or fantasy twists and symbolism. Music and the violin in particular also have an important role in the story.The illustrations are beautifully hand drawn with lots of details, using a consistent color scheme that makes every chapter work well together and the transitions between them seem seamless. The character animations are too simple, fade out and fade in, but the art makes up for it.All the music and background sounds are very well done but the main theme in particular, played several times in the story, is very catchy, and blends well a mix of sadness and optimism.The puzzles are logical and easy to figure out most of the time. There’s a button to reveal points of interest to make sure you didn’t miss any, but there are no specific hints to solve the puzzles. Finding and reading the clues is very important, but a few of the puzzles rely on counting elements in the background that don’t seem obvious or connected to the object itself. I had to check the guide on a few of them.  20 Achievements. Around 2 hours. Easy, most puzzles are easy to figure out. Easy, most are story related, but check a guide for the missable ones like SPOILERS  When The Past Was Around is a great fantasy and romance point and click/hidden object game with logic puzzles. The illustrations are beautiful and hand drawn and the story is touching and well written.

'When The Past Was Around' is definitely a valuable addition to the the library of anyone who likes narrative adventure titles.

_childDocuments_.review: A short simple game about love & loss. When the Past was Around is a point-and-click storytelling adventure. We follow the story of Eda, a young woman dealing with the pain of losing her lover. We guide Eda through her past memories by solving various puzzles, revealing the blossoming relationship between her and her lover and the pain she experiences losing him. Admittedly, interpretive games as well as point-and-click games are very much a hit or miss for me. When I read a story, I want to know the whole story. I don’t want the writing to be ambiguous or have an ending that is left to the imagination. I simply struggle when it comes to artistic metaphorical games. Fortunately, When the Past was Around was pretty easy to follow. There were still some things that flew over my head, like the artistic choice to make her lover have an owl as his head. I looked it up, and then it made a lot more sense, but that had never been made clear throughout the story (at least not to me). I also actually enjoyed the point-and-click puzzle solving gameplay. Now, the puzzles are not very challenging, but if you get a little lost, clicking around usually does the trick. The art style is absolutely beautiful and despite a couple of critiques, it’s a great game to sit down and enjoy a cozy cup of coffee with. I completed the game, as well as unlocked all of the achievements, in a little over 2 hours. So if you’re looking for a bittersweet story to enjoy for a short period of time, I would recommend picking this one up!

_childDocuments_.review: this game has destroyed me. i have never experienced the loss of a partner, but this game fully put me in mourning for someone that doesn't exist.the puzzles are really well done, i like the secret achievements that will just randomly pop up, and i felt genuinely challenged with a lot of the puzzles. the challenge of finding the right combination for a lock was a shocking contrast to the challenge of trying not to cry throughout this whole game. there were a couple parts of the game i felt warranted a warning at the main menu, specifically for flashing lights and high pitched noises which caught me by surprise.like i said at the beginning, i have never lost a partner, but this felt like a well made game about the grieving process and how every little thing reminds you of them; the realistic portrayal of anger towards typical comforts/hobbies and the act of chasing anything that could possibly bring them back is.... it freakin hurts, man. and then the ending comes in, and you're like "oh!! it's an ambiguous ending so we can feel better!" and then the rug gets pulled out from under you and you weep on your desk.the game is beautiful in terms of graphics, storytelling, and music. again, the puzzles are pretty good and surprisingly challenging in some parts. it's a relatively quick game, but a good play nonetheless.i am sobbing and punching the wall. well done.

_childDocuments_.review: I love short, atmospheric, and melancholy games. This fell flat. _childDocuments_.review: has been one of my most-anticipated titles over the past year. Ever since Mojiken published the game's prologue/demo for the first(?) Steam Game Festival, I've wanted to see, play, hear and learn more about it.When it finally released, I jumped at it, and beat it in one sitting. It's a short game, but one that delivers enough artistry and emotional impact to prove worth the price of admission. Every scene is well-crafted, stunningly drawn and heartfelt. The soundtrack perfectly accompanies the wordless narrative, be it through moments of intense grief, whimsical dates or hopeful melancholy.While I am certain that the game and what it offers will hardly be for everyone, I firmly believe that it presents a labor of love of a timeless quality that is well-worth experiencing for anyone with a taste for bittersweet stories, or struggling with the loss of a loved one. It may just help them starting to heal.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: This game may be short in length but so big in heart. It is such a beautiful story told through wonderful artwork and music. _childDocuments_.review: Too many write-down-the-code-on-the-last-screen then fill-in-the-code-on-the-next-screen puzzles for me. That does not match what is supposedly two people's home...do they live in an escape room? I'd guess about 70% of the puzzles are code-solving variations. Who has so many indoor locks with a puzzle code? This isn't a mysterious mansion, just their home and a story of their love. The other puzzle / more truly point-click type puzzles are fun because they stand out.Beyond that gameplay gripe, two cons and two pros:-Pro, the art style is delightful. Makes me want to read a graphic novel of this (or see a short animation) instead of play a game...-Pro, the actual music is lovely (soundtrack in background, snippets at key moments, credits)-Con, the sound design (I mean the noises you trigger when you interact with the world) otherwise is a mismatch - loud, sudden, clunky. Does not fit for an art style that is pretty much artsy realism and a romantic story.  Maybe this is a stylistic thing I don't know about from this genre (not point and click in general, though). I don't like it.-Con, this is supposedly about a musician (partner...who is an owl? not sure why?) and music.  But somehow different *length* notes are different *tones*. This doesn't happen once but in basically every chapter, often multiple times. It's just kind of silly for anyone who can read written music notation, and anyway it's inaccurate. There are other visual ways they could have represented this that would seem less silly. Only a gripe because the game is so focused on the partner being a musician (who writes sheet music, during the plot)...many musicians who read sheet music would find this design choice weird :)

_childDocuments_.review: I play a ton of adventure games. I's probably my favorite genre of game, so when I saw When The Past Was Around, a very highly recommended adventure game, touted for its originality and story telling, which also happens to have a beautiful art style, somewhat reminiscent of Gorogoa, I figured I would share the love that so many other people seem to have towards the game. Unfortunately, it's not really my thing. Let me just say that I don't think there's anything wrong with When The Past Was Around necessarily, I would say my issues with it are highly subjective and mainly a factor of aesthetic tastes, but maybe you can use this review to gauge if When The Past Was Around would align with your tastes.Firstly, I found the main song that plays throughout the game to be fairly annoying. You know, normally music not aligning with your tastes wouldn't be a crazy huge issue for a game, but with When The Past Was Around, the music is so intertwined with the actual story that removing this element essentially eliminates the possibility of you enjoying the game. It's a love story about musicians who are literally making the song that's playing in the background the entire time, and also a large number of the interaction in the game are directly related to the musical notes in the song. It's kind of hard to get around. I actually muted the music about halfway through, because the highly repetitive song was giving me a headache. I beat this game in just over an hour and a half by the way, so that's not a long time for something to do that to you.**I highly recommend you listen to the music in the second trailer on the store page before buying the game for this reason**So I muted the game's music, and it was actually an interesting study in the reliance of music in storytelling. Personally I found without music to pull on your violin's heart strings, When The Past Was Around lacks any emotional response whatsoever. I found the story pretty hamfisted, and honestly kind of forced. I'm not going to go into to many details, because it's a very short game, but it's basically a series of memories of a couple, you can kind of use your imagination as to where it goes. It's not really trying to hide anything, and is pretty upfront about the premise. I can see how if you've been through something like what happens in this game, how you could be more moved than I was, but I don't believe empathy of a specific hardship should be a requirement to enjoy a game; so because of this, I can't recommend When The Past Was Around. The story and slightly generic aesthetics just didn't do it for me, and the puzzles are in no way good enough to make When The Past Was Around stand on it's own. 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10. Amazing art, good storytelling, cute character and environmental design!! I can't look away from any of the frames drawn and it's definitely worth to play if you're a big fan of point & click games. Although I think the Owl is too talented because he can play the violin both right-handed and left-handed lol (see if you'd notice in some of the cut-scenes)!Regardless, I enjoyed the game!! I bought it on sale which I think is fitting with the short game-play duration. If you're looking for a cute game, this is it fellas!

_childDocuments_.review: When the Past Was Around is a point-and-click puzzle game, where we follow the story of Eda.Musician who meets Owl and her life changes forever. Gameplay is like in your typical point-and-click game, you can interact with objects, pick them up, use them, open locks and move between locations.As i said previously, this game is really short, but thats not necessarily a bad thing. Actually thanks to that story fragments are coming up more fluidly, and there is less delay between them. Graphics are gorgeous, the artists did an incredible job with design and implementation. Everything looks really cute and expressful.The title is really important, "When the Past Was Around" i dont want to spoil the story so i wont go that deep into it, but it truly is a line that describes a tragic tale. A line that tells that someone is missing old times, and a line that manifests a true enemy of mankind - the Passage of Time.This game really feels like it was inspired by Rusty Lakes and Cube Paradoxes, although the themes and stories are vastly different, its still feels like there is a piece of those games in this. Which especially for me, is a really good thing.Do you like games, that make you expand your playlist with game soundtracks, by just having to add another amazing songs? Then this game is for you my friend. Main theme is short and simple but very memorable and catchy, it may trigger some people because its repeated a couple of times throughout the game, but its never fully the same song. Even the background tracks that play when you are solving the puzzles are quite good and noteworthy.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game ... it feels very relaxed and slow but also deals with super heavy themes of loss and death. _childDocuments_.review: A short story on the journey of losing on someone you love dearly.The game while short details the 5 stages of grief really nicely and without being overtly showy.For a game without texts and voice at all, I really like how it plays together without ever feeling like anything was missing to the experience of the game. The UI is clean and minimalist which is how I like things are, personally.I can't really help but emphasize that the artwork is astoundingly beautiful. I love every aspect of it, from the pretty background to mesmerizing details of the 2 main characters, and the background was so so adorable. The artists that worked on really gave their everything and spared nothing behind pouring everything in.Music in this game was what made me like the game to absolutely loving it, just by removing a few instruments here and there it really helps changes the entire setting and mood of the place. As there's no texts or voices in this game the game truly shines because of the music.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cute story game with some mild puzzle solving, took me less than two hours while I took breaks to explain things to my six year old who kept asking questions.Art? it's beautiful! Music? perfectStory? It is a story of loss and acceptance told visually in an engaging way.Gameplay? You click around and find things you need to advance.  Usually in the same room, but you need to backtrack a couple of times.  There is a hint system to highlight what you can click on.  I think there were one or two puzzles where the right answer didn't immediately work the first time.If you like story games, it's a good story that may stick with you for a bit.  if you like achievements, make sure to check them ahead of time because some are pretty arbitrary and easily missed.  The one glaring flaw to the game is that I have been unable to muster the desire to go back and get the achievments I missed.

_childDocuments_.review: Ummm this one was a hard one. I would give it a 4-6/10... The story was meh to me, I loved the actual point and click and drag gameplay, the puzzles were cute and just enough to keep me intrigued without being impossible. I didn't need a guide or walkthrough to solve anything. My biggest complaint, even though it's story driven, the cutscenes are just.... too slow and too much and too long. There's no way to skip them and they become really repetitive really fast. Especially when there's like 30 seconds of gameplay and then another slow cutscene of clicking music notes. I never got pulled into the story enough for those cutscenes to be something I cared about, and I just found myself wishing more and more I could skip them as the game went on and the actual gameplay got shorter just to encounter another cutscene of slowly clicking music notes. So... 4/10. Gameplay and artstyle, hidden achievements-- loved it. The rest, meh.

_childDocuments_.review: The strong points are obviously the art and music, but the interactive puzzles and non-puzzle interactions are woven in well, all towards understanding, progressing, and resolving the narrative. Well worth the cost of admission.Tonally, it's reminiscent of films like  (2011), which explore loss with a sense of warmth, and my 100m playtime went by like a satisfying film. While I can't say the game taught me anything new about life, this fundamentally speech-less and text-less journey gives you plenty of space to meditate on its very worthy topics and themes at your own pace, without any dialogue or narration intruding.Will definitely be following Mojiken closely.Wonderful seeing touches like Eda wearing kebaya and other familiar little Indonesian/SEA details, while at the same time the story feels fully universal, using minimal language dependence to tell its tale.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely recommend this game. It's short, it's cheap, it has a great story telling. First of all, artstyle is really appealing, it's simple but pretty. _childDocuments_.review: I was only of the lucky people who was able to beta test this masterpiece. The player is guided through Eda and Owl's life together and experiencing their emotions together whilst solving some puzzles. What you need to know is that the visuals and audio are breath-taking, and after playing the game you will find yourself humming its tunes.Thank you Mojiken for this heartfelt experience.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game about love and loss told without any words.The art style and music in this game are absolutely gorgeous. Which is important, as there's not a single bit of dialogue about humming. While this does mean that the story isn't told directly and obviously, I actually really enjoy that certain aspects can be interpreted differently by different people. I won't spoil the story, but I did really enjoy it. For the puzzles, they are overall very simple with only a little bit of thinking needed for the most part. I had one that confused me and I needed to look up, but overall, very manageable. I personally didn't find them boring, however, as it felt more like a relaxing time than a difficult challenge. Most of the achievements I got through a basic playthrough, and only needed to go back to do a few - made easier with the chapter select, though you still may need to replay a good little bit to get to certain parts. As the game is overall short, this is no big deal, however. All parts of this game felt important to the story. The puzzles didn't feel like they were there just to add gameplay, they all felt significant in Eda and Owl's lives. Every item had a bit of back story and seemed to play a part in their lives, together. It was beautifully told, something that can easily be failed at when attempting a game without dialogue. I really loved this game. it was a nice, short little adventure that, despite being sad, left me overall feeling happy.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: When The Past Was Around is a simple point and click puzzle game. Tells the story of the struggle of a girl named Eda who wants to let go of her past. This game carries the theme of separation which is packaged nicely through the story in the game.The gameplay in this game is mostly about solving  puzzles so that Eda's story can develop. You will encounter many puzzles that are sometimes confusing and require more attention. Sometimes thinking for a moment and observing all the available clues will help you solve all the puzzles in this game.The story mode in this game is quite short. There are only 5 chapters that you can watch and each chapter contains the journey of Eda and Owl's relationship. Even so, the art style used is so beautiful that you will enjoy their story even though it is short. Coupled with a calming soundtrack so you can feel all the emotions in each chapter.Because this is a narrative game, of course the core of this game is the story. Unfortunately, the 5 chapters presented are not very impressive. Eda and Owl lack of character because there is no dialogue in this game. Of course you will understand how the story goes even without dialogue. However, for me personally, Eda and Owl's characters were less connected and caused me to lack empathy.Even so, each chapter has good progress, describes how their relationship is, how they solve problems and ends with a beautiful ending. This game is suitable for people who want to enjoy a good short story and it will only take less than 2 hours to complete depending on how quickly they solve the puzzles. If you like Florence, you will also love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I started my journey of learning the piano when I was very young.A few years ago, I hit my bottleneck stage.When I first came into contact with the piano, I was only a four-year-old child. My motivation to learn the piano was out of a pure love for the piano.But as time goes by, I gradually grow up. The understanding of this world is no longer full of naive and lovely ideas like a four-year-old child.Although I have to admit that this is the reality - everything has changed. But my heart is still unwilling to accept this reality, I just want to stay in my good memories of my childhood.So the speed at which my piano playing skills are improving seems to be suspended.The original beautiful rhythm suddenly turned into mourning for the deceased.But this attitude of not accepting reality will not be tolerated by the God of Time.I am still growing up, and the people around me are also getting older. Many things and people that accompanied me growing up have also disappeared.I realized that if I kept living with the memories of the past, it would only make my life a complete tragedy.Although those sad notes and melodies are beautiful, they should never be the main theme of my life that just started.Good childhood memories are definitely not heavy things that people can't let go of for a long time.Her best destination should be to leave a piece of pure land in her heart. Taking care of her as the Garden of Eden, maybe one day, through my own efforts, I can create the real Garden of Eden instead of letting her linger in pain forever in my memory.At least for the rest of my life I don't have to worry about where my next meal is, and at least I still have a piano to play different rhythms—whether those rhythms are true or not in my inner world."Please continue to play that old piano and use it to play a new rhythm" - I said to myself.This game resonated with me a lot.
