_childDocuments_.review: is about grieving as much as it is about moving on while still respecting the life you lost. I got to experience as much as Eda’s anger and sadness as I did her love and inquisitiveness. Finding a new love and slowly losing them within the game was done all without dialogue.The back and forth movement through memories and areas filled with Eda and the Owl’s life were the most pivotal parts of the game for me. Going through Eda’s beautiful home before and after painful memories, only to ransack her home, felt good and felt bad. It was immersive. Looking for a key, or the handle for a music box, meant throwing books on the floor, flipping up a rug, knocking plants over. It felt like a catharsis as much as it felt like a temper tantrum that comes when you can’t or don’t want to acknowledge what’s truly wrong. Losing a loved one is impossible to imagine, and the game never took advantage of that grief. It was one of those few instances where experiencing grief in a game felt necessary, and I think that was the point. That accepting sadness and beginning to move on while still understanding that life has changed is a part of the process. It showed that you are able to continue living without feeling as though you’re forgetting about or disrespecting the life and death of a loved one.Overall, this game is a true gem that offer self-reflection of life and death, respecting the memories and experiences we have been through. Moving on does not imply that we have forgotten our loves one but in fact, it is an act of respect and appreciation where we are moving forward and continuously share the proof of our life experiences and stories we had with our loves one to the others who we love as well. By sharing these moments, we have keep the memories alive - within ourselves and those who we love that surrounding us.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a trip down memory lane and now holds a special place in my heart. When The Past Was Around is a beautiful masterpiece with beautiful illustrations, soundtrack and amazing storytelling which taught the meaning of loss, grief and acceptance. Artistically, the amount of details in this game is beyond words, from the album of photos to the details of the feathers down to their favourite cup of tea/coffee, the artists had done a remarkable job in allowing the players to fully immerse themselves into the game by showing each of the character's personalities. The puzzles were creatively placed and they were never repetitive. And what amazed me was the fact that the puzzles didn't feel forced or felt out of place but was beautifully molded together with the story and characteristics of the MC and her lover. This game brought me to tears countless times. Especially the scene where you were finally able to "touch" and be in the embrace of your loved one. All in all, I would highly recommend playing this game and purchasing their art book!

_childDocuments_.review: The game tells the tale of Edna, the female protagonist who seems to have lost her way until she meets The Owl (who really is an owl because I questioned this on stream and wondered whether he was a metaphor for something else, turns out not). Since it’s something to be experienced rather than be talked about, just like love and relationships and life in general, I’m just going to skip the plot details and talk about the features that made the game noteworthy for me.The story is cleverly disguised as a point-and-click visual novel with puzzles that you work on in order to progress through the game. It plays out in the form of unlocking memories and unhiding secrets in the form of clues. Most of the puzzles are quite straightforward and work in a linear fashion though there were a couple that left me doing the ol’ trial-and-error approach.There is no real-spoken dialogue and the game isn’t text-driven either. However, it does use a beautiful, unique art-style and music to convey certain life lessons, like heartbreak with a delicate sensibility. It is a short and bittersweet experience, but one that I would recommend. Obviously this won’t be a game for everyone, as some will lament the game’s length and replay value but oftentimes I just want to feel something when I play a story-based game and When The Past Was Around certainly delivers.

The Steam summary is a good enough (adventure point-and-click puzzle game about love, moving on, letting go, and the joy and pain of everything in between) but if you want a more spoilery description: You can't think too deeply about it because, like a dream, some things don't really make sense under closer inspection. However, (as long as you don't get stuck and refuse to use a guide) levels are pretty short so you move on to new content quickly which helps.It probably took me about an hour total to complete the game blind (using a guide when stuck), go back and get all missing achievements, and write this review.Other thoughts:

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has been through something very similar to this story, all I can say is that this game did a very good job of portraying 1% of the pain that you actually feel when you lose someone who was once a lover, a best friend, and a companion. That being said, that 1% that it managed to capture left me sobbing and an emotional wreck. Living with the other 99% is the struggle. However, time dulls that and eventually you see the beauty and the hope in the little things. I too miss when the past was around, but at the same time, I also feel the same sense of dread as the main heroine did. On one hand, you want the past to stay and linger. On the other hand, you also want it to go. You hope that time will heal the wounds and that you'll be better off someday. I am married now, happy, and am thriving. But will those wounds that I felt once still always be there? Oh yeah, of course. They have turned into scars. Did I see myself in the female protagonist? Oh yeah, big time. Did it hurt? Yes. Would I play this game again to feel the bittersweet cathartic emotions again? Absolutely.

_childDocuments_.review: When The Past Was Around is one of those games that sat on my wish-list for long enough I forgot what it was about until someone gifted it to me. The gorgeous art style and charming atmosphere adds to the puzzles that follow a logical train of thought and can be completed rather quickly if you're one that likes to click everything. All the same, the game punished my procrastination on the purchase by making me cry. Three separate times. In the span of two hours I fell in love with the relationship of the two characters you will follow, felt for them during both health and strife, and refused to grapple with grief that I knew was approaching from the get-go. Although this is a puzzle game, and it's a very good one, it's a game you play for the story above anything else. I recommend this to anyone and everyone! So go out there, break some pots, and try to pretend your heart isn't being chiseled away at while you play one of the most beautiful games of 2020.

_childDocuments_.review: I have found these "short story" types of games quite recently, and this game is a rather good example of the genre. The game itself is short (it took me about two hours to complete) and the game mechanics and puzzles are rather simple - but none of this is necessarily a bad thing. Both of these things let the game focus on the story that the devs want to tell, and if the story takes a couple of hours - well, so be it. A thing about the story though: as with quite a few of these games, When the Past was around wants to go straight to the feels and if it misses, there's not that much that the game can do for you. I felt quite unmoved for the majority of the game, but it still crept up on me a bit in the end. I wouldn't call it a masterpiece of storytelling by any means, but I still enjoyed it.The music and graphics are very cute and minimalistic, which goes quite well with the overall aesthetic and the pace of the game, which is quite slow. For me it was a bit of a double-edged sword, as a long time gamer I found the unskippable cutscenes to be a tiny bit annoying and the music started to repeat itself after a while. Even so, one can find the pacing to be contemplative and peaceful instead of just boring, and the music to be cute and "indie-like" (hey, it's quite a lot to ask to put two hours of music into a two-hour-long game).If you're looking for a challenging puzzle game with a surefire gripping story, then this is not for you. If you want to enjoy a warm-hearted tale on a human scale (which is enjoyable if not overtly happy), then by all means go and grab this game.

_childDocuments_.review: There is no point in playing this game. It has nothing to offer and no story to convey. Depression Quest gives it a run for its money.Being point-and-click means that your gameplay will be minimal, however "When The Past Was Around" really makes even the little game it has painful and tedious. It is brutally linear and some of the puzzles are straight up asinine. You only click to progress through the "puzzles". There is no world building; you cannot click on something in the world to look at it closer. If it does not progress you through the level it is not interactable.There is no character building either. You are supposed to feel bad only because the girl is drawn to be pretty and she is sad(?); that is literally the entirety of the story. To call the two characters one-dimensional would be an insult to pulp fiction. Even the little story it has completely perverts the Myth.This is 1.5 hours of manual labor yak shaving to view 60 seconds of slideshow cutscenes. This is the same sort of content farm shovelware people moan about but presented in pretty colors. There is so little to the game that it's hard to even say anything about it, it really feels like a generated "reading reddit stories" video. It's like "Eat Pray Love" watered down to the blandest possible while still being recognizable. To compare this with any other game would be an insult to whatever you were comparing it with.I would never want this to be associated with my name. This is a bad game full of missed opportunities and I would feel bad if I helped bring this to the world.

_childDocuments_.review: and now onto the short review//intro//Hey what is up my name is MF Kraven and I'm here to bring you another less than 10 mins review, today I will be looking at When the Past Was Around. WtPWA is a point & click adventure puzzle game with a haunting yet beautiful theme of grief. It's about remembering, forgetting, love, sorrow and everything that may lie in it. Is When the Past Around the next worthy tearjerker or should you forget about the game completely?Lets find out!//Graphics, Sound & Artstyle//I wanna start off by saying that everything that the artists and composers put forth on When the Past Was Around are absolute geniuses. All emotions evoked from me as I experienced the game. The artstyle paints a picture more beautiful than Studio Ghibli films, the score elevates the art to a level of serenity & sorrow. //Gameplay//Like any other point & click puzzle game, the actual gameplay doesn't stand out. Many have compared the prologue to a Rusty Lake-esque game, to a degree I agree. However the stylized simplistic way of where everything is positioned wont have rookies of the genre looking up what to do next rather, everything makes sense with the exception of one or two puzzles. I really appreciate having on the top right corner a button to press to highlight what may or may not be an interactable item or action.//Price//7.99 USD//How many hours estimated//I was stuck in two puzzles that really didn't make a lot of sense to me, with that & grabbing some popcorn, it took me about almost 3 hours to beat the game.//Final Thoughts//When the Past Was Around is a gorgeous game with an eclectic artstyle. I evoked emotions in me and had me on the verge of tears in some scenes. I had fallen ill a few years ago & some of the imagery took me back to a battle I couldve easily lost to my illness. Without spoiling anything..... the ending was initially inconclusive to me, but that is only due to the fact that the game is not voice acted; this is where my first negative note comes from. The game would serve better as a film rather than a game, don't get me wrong, I really liked the experience however- with half of an understanding at what's happening, a little dialouge would go a long way. Only other complaint I have is two of the puzzles in the game had me scratching my head wondering what I was supposed to do. Having 90% of the achievements, I obviously passed the game but it was through deductive reasoning but I just know there was a method to this madness, I would just like to understand HOW. In spite of everything just mentioned though, the game remains a treasure. The story is one that almost hit too close to home. It's art, only through interpretation can it be genuinely enjoyed. Is it perfect? No. Will you feel a lump in your throat as you see Eda cling to the very existence of her beloved Owl? In my experience, yes. It's an experience for connoisseurs of romance novels to embrace, a tale for the widows of the world to live through. Have I made my point? For the asking price of 7.99; I find that it's more than reasonable for the experience you are getting.

_childDocuments_.review: Find keys and other missing pieces in gameplay comparable to a story book or hidden object game with intuitive interactions.Relive memories of love, sickness, loss and death. Find the feather. Make a mess sometimes. Throw plants on floor or break tombstones. Other times tidy up. Make tea. It may sound inconsistent but it goes through the character's emotions at different stages of their relationship and the events that followed Owl's death, and it all makes sense.Hints are all there, they only require keen observation to details, occasionally remembering patterns or taking notes. It is quite a perfect blend of narrative and relatively simple puzzles.Nicely drawn scenes in earthy tones. Simple navigation typically involve only a few rooms at a time.In some scenes it was not clear if the order of picked notes made a difference when the sequence would repeat a few times, but in the end it did not seem to matter. Overall it took me 1h30 in a single session, without needing hints, leading to a pleasant and relaxing evening.Owl is strangely the only character with an animal head (everyone else is human), which may feel a bit weird to some. There is no direct explanation for his appearance, he even has a human silhouette at times, but feathers do play an important part throughout the short story.

_childDocuments_.review: When The Past Was Around is a point-and-click adventure game developed by Mojiken Studio and published by Toge Productions. This beautifully crafted game invites players into a poignant narrative of love, loss, and self-discovery. With its unique art style, evocative music, and emotionally resonant storytelling, When The Past Was Around stands out as a memorable experience that lingers long after the credits roll.Visual and Artistic AppealThe first thing that captures the player’s attention is the game’s exquisite hand-drawn art. The visual style is whimsical yet deeply expressive, perfectly complementing the game’s emotional tone. Each scene is meticulously detailed, and the use of color enhances the atmosphere, conveying both the joy and sorrow of the protagonist’s journey. The character designs, particularly that of the Owl, are distinctive and imbued with a subtle charm that makes the narrative even more engaging.Story and Emotional DepthThe narrative follows Eda, a young woman navigating the bittersweet memories of her past relationship with a mysterious figure known as the Owl. The story is told without dialogue, relying on visual storytelling and subtle interactions to convey the depth of their relationship. This approach allows for a universal emotional resonance, making the themes of love and loss accessible to a wide audience. The game’s pacing is deliberate, encouraging players to reflect on their own experiences as they unravel Eda’s story.Gameplay and MechanicsWhile the gameplay mechanics of When The Past Was Around are relatively simple, they are effective in driving the narrative forward. Players interact with objects and solve puzzles to unlock new memories and progress through the story. The puzzles are thoughtfully designed, striking a balance between challenge and accessibility. They serve to immerse the player deeper into the narrative, rather than detracting from it.Sound and MusicOne of the standout features of the game is its hauntingly beautiful soundtrack composed by Masdito "Ittou" Bachtiar. The music is integral to the game’s emotional impact, with each piece perfectly capturing the mood of the scenes it accompanies. The sound design, from the gentle strumming of a guitar to the ambient sounds of everyday life, adds an additional layer of immersion and helps to ground the fantastical elements of the story in a relatable reality.Overall ExperienceWhen The Past Was Around is more than just a game; it is an emotional journey that explores the complexities of love and the pain of letting go. Its compelling visual style, evocative music, and heartfelt storytelling make it a standout title in the indie game scene. The game’s ability to convey deep emotions through simple yet effective gameplay mechanics is a testament to the talent and vision of Mojiken Studio.In conclusion, When The Past Was Around is a must-play for anyone seeking a narrative-driven experience that resonates on a personal level. It is a reminder of the power of video games as a medium for storytelling and emotional expression. Whether you’re a fan of adventure games or simply looking for a beautifully crafted story, this game is sure to leave a lasting impression.Rating: 9/10Pros:Exquisite hand-drawn artEmotionally resonant storytellingBeautifully composed soundtrackThoughtful and immersive puzzlesCons:Relatively short playtimeLimited replayabilityWhen The Past Was Around is a shining example of how video games can touch our hearts and remind us of the universal experiences that bind us all.

_childDocuments_.review: When The Past Was Around is game of pure art through its well crafted story, gorgeous artstyle and calm music. The game puts its focus on learning to cope with loss and grief. You play as Eda, a woman in her 20s. Throughout the game you are faced with different puzzles in which you need to complete in order to unlock different memories from Eda's life. Every single puzzle is created in a way which puts you in Eda's shoes. You have to think like her in order to progress and heal her traumas. I can strongly recommend this game to anyone who has or currently is going through the grief of losing someone close to them. Letting go of someone close to you is never an easy thing. This game will accompany you on that journey and it will make you reflect in new ways in which you haven't done before. If you ever happen to feel down and have two hours to spare on a rainy day; get this game, go treat yourself with some healthy snacks, sit down in a comfortable chair and take the time to appreciate every single thing that this game has to offer. It is a perfect bitter sweet game and I cannot stress enough how much I enjoyed playing it!

_childDocuments_.review: I've never reviewed a game before so this may be a bit rough, BUTI downloaded this purely because it was listed as cozy and had an obvious tie to music. The story pretty immediately broke my heart (I should've known with the description mentioning loss and letting go) but was beautiful all the same. Owl and Eda's story is wonderful and I wish I could witness it for the first time all over again.The artwork is stunning, and the melody laced through out the game is very catchy and I've found myself humming it periodically throughout the past couple of days.There were just a few puzzles that made me have to use my brain more than I was up for in the moment, but that's probably because I have been very emotionally drained for the past couple of weeks. All in all it was lovely, beautiful, pulled at my heart strings, and will live on as one of my favorites for a very long time. My only complaint is how short lived the experience felt. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely Point-N-Click game. It follows Eda, the female, and Owl, her partner. Throughout the game, there is a melody that repeats and consists of notes that later become a very significant part of some of the gameplay and puzzles. This is a beautiful game about what it is to love someone, lose that loved one, move on, and find closure in memories from the coast of that said loved one. At the same time, playing this game you as the player will relive Eda's and Owl's relationship through the good and bad. You will learn with Eda how to move beyond grief and find closure while keeping the loved one close even in spirit.

_childDocuments_.review: For such a low production game, this game hits the right spot for its intended genre, and does it flawlessly. _childDocuments_.review: This game presents one of the toughest challenges for a review. It's not a definitive thumbs-down; it's a visually stunning game that exudes the care and passion poured into its creation. The artwork is breathtaking, and the music evokes genuine emotion. You can feel the creators' hearts woven into this gaming experience.However, the narrative leaves much to be desired. The loss of someone close is an incredibly profound human experience, yet the game barely delves beneath the surface of Eda's grief. It feels like a missed opportunity; the developers could have added at least three more chapters to truly explore the story's depth. It seems they played it safe, missing the chance to showcase Eda's journey in pursuing her dreams and the hurdles she encountered along the way.Yet, this game isn't deserving of overwhelmingly negative criticism. A definite thumbs-down would be too harsh. I urge you to experience the game firsthand, revel in the stunning animations, and immerse yourself in the enchanting music. Just temper your expectations before diving in.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a (very, very short) visual novel with a huge focus on visual art and music. The story is good, though I expected it to be more about rekindling your passions after challenging periods, it was more focused on the grief of losing someone close to you. I would say this is pretty accessible as a game, there are a few animations that might be bothersome to some but not a lot, and the hint button (in case you get stuck, can't see the next objective, etc) works out well. Game is playable with or without audio but the audio does enhance the game. The chapter select was nice, I only had to go back to the start for one achievement missed but it should be quick to figure out if you miss any.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: This game managed to bring me on the tearful yet peaceful in the end roller coaster that is the grieving process without using words. The entire time there is no dialogue , only music (the same tune connects all the memories beautifully) and a few times humming are used. The illustration in the game is very well done. The puzzles involved are not too difficult but not overly simplified so you are kept engaged. I am not ashamed to say there was one point in which I found myself crying along with the character. I recommend staying until the very end credits, not just to pop all the musical note bubbles they play but to get the full emotional wrap up as the main character has accepted the memories of her love as comfort and no longer tearful pain. The achievements available are a nice bonus and may have you playing through more than one to get however when that was the case for me I found myself enjoying playing the second time as much as the first. I highly recommend this emotional game and find myself yearning for more games that evoke such an emotional journey that leaves me on a comfortable everything is alright note. My hat is off to all the people who worked on this.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very short game but it was a fairly good game over all with cute graphic art style and good puzzles. The story was a sad one but told in a beautiful way. _childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game, even for people who are horrible at puzzels, it's pretty simple, so don't be afraid of getting stuck. This game excels not only at art, but on music and story telling. I got really attached to these characters. You might think the ending won't surprise you, especially already knowing the game is about grief, but if you got attached as I did, you will be. These characters are lovely, sweet, caring, and the moments they share are heartwarming and wholesome. If you love emotional stories, and listen to sad songs cause it feels good to be sad sometimes and cry it out, this game is for you. If you love owls, even more so, because this game has very cute owls, and very cute moments that make me wish I could experience such things, even for the short time they were.Mind you, it's short, so you could finish it in one sitting. But all short things just mean there was plenty of love made in it.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: When the Past was Around is an incredibly moving and immersive experience, masterfully weaving together stunning artwork and beautiful violin music to tell a touching story. The main character, Eda, solves puzzles throughout the game that help her progress through her memories, many of which are focused on her and her partner creating a song together. The recurring four chords of the song serve as a powerful anchor throughout the game, while its changing tones effectively convey a range of emotions, all without any dialogue. While exploring themes of loss, the game ultimately delivers a message of hope and healing. Its well-crafted narrative makes it a captivating and fulfilling experience to enjoy in one sitting, and it comes highly recommended to anyone looking for an emotional and memorable gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very beautifully-illustrated game as you can clearly see! The main aim for each level is to find the feather to give to your deceased love named Owl. Throughout the game, you'll relive what I think are memories of what you two shared together; it's bittersweet in a way. A few of the puzzles took a while for me to figure out, but other than that, the whole set of puzzles are pretty clever, plus you've got nice music to accompany you. The only downside for me is that this game is short, but I suppose it's nice to keep things short and sweet sometimes. However, if you like graphics/puzzles games like these, with a non-spoken dialogue, I think you'd want the game to be longer. I definitely got mentally-immersed in it!
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful game. Not only is it a puzzle game, but it is a thought provoking and open story about love and loss. _childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: I write this 5 minutes after sobbing like a little baby because stories related to grief always hit me hard but the melancholy somewhat bittersweet endings would leave anyone satisfied in some way even if they never engaged with the story as much as I did. But be warned, the game is not for everybody as it is a puzzle game but is a story game first in my opinion. The puzzles and environments never overstayed their welcome and any frustration I felt was immediately washed away at the adorable charm of the art and music which can seem repetitive but as it goes on, the different adaptations of the same melody keep it from going stale. Despite the short runtime of the game, I wholeheartedly believe that it is worth any price, full or discounted and if you want a nice little game to play really quick or something to help you get a quick cry, then please buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Made the mistake of playing this game after experiencing a loss of my own. Beautiful visuals and music. Many of the puzzles were super quick and intuitive, but a couple of the more obscure puzzles admittedly had me surfing though the community guide. Was left with wanting to know more about  Was confused by Aside from the couple of questions I was left with, I finished the game wiping tears from my face (and I'm sure a game about memories is supposed to feel a little vague)! In any case, the art and music are tremendously beautiful, and the way they are used to tell this story is truly captivating. It doesn't take much to get invested. _childDocuments_.review: When The Past Was Around has been on my list for some time, with me going back and forth on whether or not to play it. The art style fascinated me, and I generally like point and clicks, but I was uncertain if the silent aspect would ruin the storytelling for me.I am here to tell you that it does not. Instead, the player is treated to an absolutely beautiful soundtrack throughout the entire game, with neat sound effects here and there that definitely makes the world feel more real. As the player follows the protagonist on her journey of grief, the title melody (a beautiful lullaby-esque tune) changes slightly to reflect the current tone or emotion of the story. Much like Spiritfarer, the game does not need much for words to encompass the overall feeling and the end is just as touching. The only drawback to this game would be the short length. In total, I played 109 minutes and unlocked every achievement, struggling with only a few puzzles in the different chapters. Personally, I would have loved to have more moments between the couple, though the chapters we did get are wonderful by themselves. However, if this is not an issue for you, I believe you will still enjoy the experience. I purchased this game for under $10 and at that price point'--I believe it is worthwhile. Hope this helps if you are on the fence about it.

_childDocuments_.review: this is a game that is ideal for a cozy afternoon, perhaps a rainy day, or perhaps you're stuck at home in quarantine (which was why i decided to buy and play the game). you could finish the game pretty quickly, i didn't take the full 7 hours, and it's a journey through the female protagonist's grief, memory and loss of a beloved partner. what i love: the visual, the hand-drawn "sketch" feeling of it, the calming music, the "asmr" or rawness of the main character's emotions when we hear her humming along to the music, solving little puzzles what i especially love/find meaning in: in the later chapters, to solve the puzzles we have to go back and forth through different rooms (spoiler? not really) and that gave me the feeling of revisiting the same old memories again and again in our minds. the game's mood is bittersweet (escalating towards the end), and oscillates between nostalgia, grief and love. it is a journey towards peace.i also especially enjoyed the shattering of the tombs, plants, and other objects in the game, and wish there is more "frustration" or destruction caused by the frustration. for example, like amping up the "messiness" of losing a loved one. what i didn't really like: some parts feel sliightly redundant in terms of enjoyment level, like the part where we have to click the musical notes in bubbles. however, i enjoyed that they play the notes of the tune. i found myself actually humming to the tune after playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun short game, only took me a couple hours to finish. The art is very pretty and so is the music. It's a game about grief and the process of grieving a loss. I think the controls are a little clunky, and the point and click function can be a little too subtle at times (having to click things multiple times for it to open/move). Some of the puzzles are fun and interesting, but some of them are simply a process of elimination or clicking until you get something correct. Sometimes you would find numbers or arrows that could conceivably hint towards a puzzle solution, but they really didn't. I prefer puzzles you can complete with you brain or logic, not just through process of elimination/luck. Overall, it's a sweet game, very chill, but I'm not sure that this would be my first recommendation for someone interested in cozy puzzle games, maybe if it was on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful story about love, loss, and moving on, all told through a short game. When The Past Was Around is a beautiful discovery of the story between Eda and The Owl which you unlock by clicking through the chapters/pages of their relationship. What transpires in the game is not necessarily how everything happened but includes how Eda visualised and interpreted her love and her grief in the loss of that loved one. What adds to the game is the beautiful music interwoven into the story--be warned, it will make crying that much easier to do.The foundation of the gameplay is the puzzlework. Each chapter and each page includes a couple of puzzles which you will need to complete to get to the next page. It's a fun processes that doesn't require a lot of thinking or one-click solving, and a lot of the enjoyment comes from figuring out which actions match with what outcomes. You can easily repeat chapters without going through the whole story, though you will need to re-do entire chapters if you miss the lucky egg bonuses which award you with an achievement at the end of the game.Easily a fun 2-3 hour game you will become emotionally invested in the further along you play.

_childDocuments_.review: "When the Past Was Around" is one of the most beautiful games I've ever played. I've played it through completely twice so far, and it made me feel so much both times. The puzzles are super enjoyable, the art is stunning, the music is incredible. However, the story is what really hooked me most of all - it's told so beautifully and convincingly! Eda and Owl feel so real and fleshed out that it's impossible not to be touched by everything they go through, the bitter and the sweet. Spending time in their world is therapeutic and cathartic, and it's the perfect blend of absolute joy and crushing sorrow. Honestly, this is one of the best pieces of art I know that successfully tackle the themes of love and loss while leaving a lasting impression.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: A girl is trapped in her memories of bittersweet romance between her and the person that captured her, heart and soul. In the game When the Past was Around, you will play as the girl who is trapped in different memories in time. You will have to find clues and items to help advance the game and find a way to unlock the door to allow for you to move on to the next memory.This is one of the few games that had an emotional effect on me and there was never a word spoken during the entire game. The soft melody that repeats in the background coupled with the distress that you can see the girl going through just grabs ahold of you. There is also the romantic story that is played out before you through different scenes. The art style has this delicateness to it that really pairs well with the music. I think that’s the real reason this game was able to yank on my emotions throughout my playthrough. This is definitely not a game for everyone, but I have to admit that I was hooked once I got a full look at the story. Most of the game is centered around scouring the scenes to find things to pick up or interact with, and for the most part all of it is straightforward, there were a couple of head scratching sessions where I wasn’t sure what I was supposed to do, but those were few and far between. This game lasted about 90 minutes, so I went through all of my emotions in one sitting, which might have helped me feel the emotions as strongly as I did.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: This is a charming, warm, beautiful, and sad story wrapped together.  Everything thing is told through the pictures that are gorgeously hand drawn. The music score goes along with the story because music is part of it. It shows the thrill of finding love and the heartbreak that goes with it when someone you love becomes ill. It shows how how memories are there after the heartbreak and how in the end they are still beautiful because the person never left us. A beautiful point and click story with puzzles that aren't that difficult.  Easy to get the achievements because they are pretty much accomplished by doing the game.  There were a couple I had to just go back to the chapter and do because they were not that obvious until reading what was needed to get them.I recommend this game. It's just point and click.  Just be ready for lots of emotion!

But the game's theme is a common one that almost everyone can relate to. Would recommend if you're an emotional person and are looking for a little stir in your heart. A++ for the art and the music.

_childDocuments_.review: Breathtakingly beautiful.  The music becomes a character all in its own and the artwork adds a delightful cheery touch.  What I like most about the game is the lack of dialogue - the story and meaning becomes something different depending on who is playing the game.  For me, the game was about struggling with our own health and mortality, and the friendships we find along the way.  If you have a disability or are struggling with your body, it can be difficult some days to accept our limitations.  This game's message is about doing our best, whatever that looks like - and the power of celebrating the happy moments when we are able.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: As for point and click puzzle games go, this is not one of the more challenging ones, and is actually quite easy, but it is still a great game. The storyline explores the subject of grief in an incredibly touching way, and leaves you with an ultimately hopeful feeling. The storytelling is only made better by the gorgeous visuals and the warm, light soundtrack that plays throughout. If this game was more expensive I would be hesitant to recommend it, but given its fair price, I absolutely recommend you give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so sweet and definitely pulls at the heartstrings. The puzzles were pretty easy (although they do get moderately more challenging as the story progresses); it's clear that the point of this game is to consume the story, which is fine by me as the story is beautiful. _childDocuments_.review: I don't actually remember how I found this game but I'm pretty sure that it caught my eye because one of my steam friends owned it. I got it because I wanted another game to be able to play on my laptop, since it can't run much. I got it and 100 percented the game in less then 2 and a half hours. Let me go over the aspects of the game and rate them:Puzzles: 8/10- It was fun to find out the puzzle solutions and then go "Ohhhhh" as I solved them. There is a decent amount of puzzles, most of which were fun, although I looked up some of the codes for certain ones as I didn't know what to do. It is possible to do this with no guide though, the solutions are never far off. Vibe: 9/10- The game was really calming and fun to play, and it always felt wholesome. But when it needed to get dark for story purposes, like the scene where you (SPOILER): have to find the medicine, it worked well. Also, the music is amazing and one of my favorite game soundtracks, along with ones like resident evil 7 and Hitman Contracts/Blood Money. Story: 7.5/10- The reason this has less then an 8 is because certain points were slightly hard to understand. For example, (SPOILERS): Did the owl man actually die, and was the ending a vision? But other then that, its a gut-wrenching and beautifully told story of loss, remembrance, and recovery.Artstyle: 8/10: I love and appreciate the simple but eye-catching artstyle. I love the design of the boyfriend(Owl Man) as well. Bonus: I liked that I was easily able to get all of the steam achievements.Overall Rating: 8.5 out of 10. It may seem a bit high for a game I only have 2.3 hours on, but this game utterly charms me and woos me with its music, puzzles, and environment. Even for the price of 8 dollars, I would highly recommend this if you are into puzzle and point & click games. If you aren't sure about buying the game, just play the demo first.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this game is probably one of the best I've played in a long time, if you have depression or grief you might enjoy being able to relate to the concept of loss within this game. The game starts off with a funeral and slowly builds into the past of their relationship until everything comes crashing down, the whole story is reliving her memories and frankly they did a damn good job at it.As a person who struggles with depression I was able to find some comfort within the game, particularly the soundtrack which fails to disappoint. I love this game personally because they were able to show love in a way of showing that it never truly dies. Your loved ones may leave but the love is never going anywhere. For anyone who's reading this comment going through a form of loss or depression or anxiety  I just want to let you know you're not alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes visual novel games fall a bit flat. Either they're too much story, or too much game, not striking the balance that makes the best of the genre work. When the Past Was Around does both well and provides some evocative music besides. Evocative? Yes, this is an emotional game, for those who think and feel. Shallow people and human robots, this is not the puzzlefest you are looking for. Now, for specifics. The artwork is top-notch, manga-like without being excessively 2-D. The graphics effectively communicate the character's emotions without being over-the-top. There is an aching gentleness that suffuses the game, from its artwork, to its story, to its music. And the music? Not the most diverse of soundtracks, but it will stay with you. But back to the feel for a moment. The feel can be heavy at times (not for me but for some) -- think emotional intensity, not horror. As for story, the game is paced well and brings it all to a satisfying close without being cheesy or predictable. The characters are relatable. Although the two main characters' relationship isn't specified exactly (I don't recall rings), that is the only possible downer. Now for the puzzles. The puzzles are occasionally too difficult (think: the tic-tac-toe problem -- argh), but by the end you will probably be in tune with the developers and they will become easier. They're not too numerous and they're not cruel. Overall, you get a memorable experience that is both story and puzzle that's not too short nor too long, and it's something that you want to remember. Charming and timeless -- When the Past Was Around is a solid 8.5.
_childDocuments_.name: When The Past Was Around

_childDocuments_.review: When the past was around is a game about love, finding your soul mate and showing the happy memories you two can share together,  But the game is also about loss and in the end healing.  Losing a loved one is the greatest pain life has to offer but its important also to also not loss our selves to when the time comes.  Gameplay wise When the past was around is a cute point and click adventure that stole my heart.  I have very rarely loved a game as much as i have this one.  With out a doubt i could see myself in the characters and fall for them to and on my first play through mourn them only in my next play through celebrate their lives and the happyness they shared.  When the past was around is truly a piece of art capturing the emotions so perfectly.  To dexcribe the game simply id use the ost as a guide for the song never changes only our meaning of it does.

_childDocuments_.review: A short, but lovely game. The art is fantastic and expressive even with its simplicity. The music accompanies the scenes wonderfully, although it can get repetitive with the use of the main song. The puzzles aren't very difficult and consist mainly of grabbing items and placing them where they need to go, although there are a couple that make you think a bit. Their main function is to move everything forward.The main draw of this, for me, is the story. Told through the art, and without a bit of dialogue, the visuals move things along and convey the emotions between the two characters. The story focuses on working through grief and states that even though a person is gone, the memories built with them help to keep them alive. Bittersweet, yet it elegantly states a sad fact of life.I actually did tear up on this one towards the end.Definitely recommended. Just be aware it can be a bit of an emotional gut punch.

If there was a hint button, I didn't use it so can't speak to how that feature worked (assuming their was one).Not 100% sure I get the whole "story."  I know the girl is lost.  I know she runs into a strange man.  He changes her perspective.  Annnnd that's about it.  No idea why he's an owl.  No idea how long they've known each other (did this happen over the course of a year, a week, 7 years...) and I feel like that takes away from the emotions some?  No idea if some of the later stuff if her dreaming vs actually breaking into a crypt.Did I like it, yes.  Was it work $6 for two hours of game play, eh.  Did it make me cry or feel any emotional attachment to the characters, nope.  Did my viewers enjoy working on the puzzles with me, yes. _childDocuments_.review: So, I initially played through the 'Prologue' version of this game, and immediately went and bought the fully released version. The art style and game play is just my cup of tea, the kind of game I really enjoy and get into and cant stop playing. Its short, really, but that didn't detract from my enjoyment.The art style is beautiful, and I love the musical element to it as well which acts as a theme running through the somewhat sad story-line. It's a pretty common one, a girl trying to work through her emotions of loss and grief. I was a little baffled by the 'owl man', her lover, and his frequent disappearances though in the scenes. Often leaving the protagonist looking startled, scared, confused, somewhat abandoned...I found that a little odd.The puzzles were in no way difficult. I've gotten used to (what I would call) VERY hard puzzles in games from Rusty Lake and the Room series, and found that the puzzles in 'When the Past Was Around' were on a pleasant difficulty level. Enough to keep me brain working, but not enough that I was stuck for any real amount of time and getting frustrated. Overall a really nice simple little game, if a bit on the melancholy side. Nice to jump into for a light hour or two of puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: Life is but a flash of light in the eyes of the world, but love is eternal, it makes us fly, it makes us strong and unstoppable to the threats of the world and nothing is greater than the feeling of true love. When we suffer the loss of that who we love the mos, the feeling of dread, loss, confusion, the pain and grief of losing our biggest strength and our biggest weakness makes the world go black and white, dull, without taste and unbearable.This is the (short) story of how love, through music and the little things, can live on and be there in the worst of our times, even after loss and unending grief. It's a tale of cherishing love, sounds and moments of silence, the smell and touch of those we love. It's a tale of grief, of learning to let go, of forgiving but never forgetting, move on from the pains and suffering that tie us down and keeps us from moving forward.

_childDocuments_.review: No words were spoken and yet the story was told in a very unique way that's guaranteed to touch your soul and break your heart.Soundtrack? Definitely amazing 20/10. Made my hair stand on end (in a very good way).It's the kind of soundtrack that will make you close your eyes and take that bow and play the violin, put your fingers on the piano keys. Just listening to the song made me remember the scenes in the story. It's ingrained into me by now.Even though it is a point and click game, it was not dull or tedious  at all. For the puzzles, some of them, I had to spend a considerable amount of time as I have go to back to certain scenes as I didn't expect the way I have to solve them, but it was not too difficult, not too easy. Would I play it again? Yes! The puzzles may be repetitive in a sense but I would definitely play it again (actually did already).Go buy the game. I thank the gods for sending it my way.Worth it. Truly. Undeniably. And when you do buy the game, don't rush. Savor the moments.

_childDocuments_.review: I cried at the end of this game. Once the credits scrolled past. Once I was on the title screen once more I just started weeping. _childDocuments_.review: When the Past Was Around is a masterpiece of storytelling that weaves together beautiful visuals, enchanting music, and clever puzzles to create an unforgettable experience. It's a heartfelt exploration of love, loss, and the memories that shape us, leaving a lasting impression on your heart and soul. The presentation and use of music in this game is phenomenal and creative, elevating the emotional impact of the story to new heights.[✔️] **Poignant Storytelling:** The game's narrative is a masterclass in emotional storytelling, capturing the bittersweet essence of love and loss with incredible depth and nuance.[✔️] **Stunning Visuals:** The hand-drawn art style is simply breathtaking, with each scene a work of art that evokes a sense of warmth and nostalgia.[✔️] **Phenomenal Music:** The melancholic yet beautiful soundtrack is nothing short of phenomenal, perfectly complementing the game's emotional tone and further immersing you in the world of Eda and the Owl. The creative use of music, with melodies and motifs that evolve as the story progresses, is a testament to the developers' artistry and attention to detail.[✔️] **Clever Puzzles:** The puzzles are thoughtfully designed and seamlessly integrated into the narrative, offering a satisfying challenge without ever feeling frustrating.[✔️] **Heartfelt Characters:** Eda and the Owl are both beautifully realized characters, their relationship a testament to the power of love and the pain of loss.[❌] **Short Length:** The game can be completed in a few hours, leaving you yearning for more time with these beloved characters.When the Past Was Around is a rare gem of a game that will stay with you long after the credits roll. It's a poignant and bittersweet journey that explores the depths of human emotion with grace and tenderness. It made me cry, it made me laugh, and it made me reflect on my own experiences of love and loss.The game's beauty lies in its simplicity. There are no epic battles or grand quests, just a quiet exploration of two souls intertwined by love. Through its evocative visuals, phenomenal and creative use of music, and heartfelt narrative, When the Past Was Around paints a vivid picture of a relationship that is both joyful and painful, beautiful and fleeting.It's a game that celebrates the little moments, the shared memories, and the unspoken words that connect two hearts. It reminds us that love is a precious gift, and that even when it ends, the memories we cherish can continue to bring us comfort and joy.If you're looking for a game that will touch your heart, stir your soul, and leave you with a renewed appreciation for the beauty of life, then When the Past Was Around is a must-play. It's a masterpiece of storytelling that will linger in your thoughts long after you've finished playing, a testament to the power of video games to evoke genuine emotions and create truly meaningful experiences.So, dim the lights, put on your headphones, and let yourself be transported to the world of Eda and the Owl. Prepare to laugh, cry, and feel every emotion in between as you embark on a journey that will touch your heart and stay with you forever.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is spectacular.  I can think of nothing wrong to talk about this game besides a little bit of anxiety during a section where the screen flashed quite violently (it isn’t long but be careful if you are affected by such things.)  The game beautifully handles grief and the stages of grief.  The imagery is very well designed to express the emotions present in the story and to express the struggle of losing a loved one.  I would say that this game is on par with Gris but more specifically designed towards death and loss.  If you have played the demo, the prologue of the game is the demo.  I was concerned when I started to play that I had already completed a significant portion.  I was very wrong, there is a lot more to this game.  If you enjoyed the demo, I can guarantee you will enjoy the rest of the game, even if it means replaying a section.   No cats present in this game but there were many small birds.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game about love, loss, grief and remembrance, told without words. The music is the star here, which paired with the art really helped the emotional beats of the story hit home. The artwork is warm and lovely, with a strong musical motif (as well as flower and feather for Eda and the Owl, respectively), and the expressions of the characters are cute and at times heartbreaking. The puzzles and interactivity hit just the right amount of difficulty without significantly delaying progression, although in at least two instances I was forced to check a guide (missed a butterfly). One can obviously tell that much care was taken when making this game, and the experience was unequivocally an enjoyable one.(Edit 11/25/20: I nominated this game on Steam Awards for its Outstanding Visual Style. I don't know if it'll win, since there are a lot of contenders, but I think it is deserving of it.)

name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish
detailed_description: 'The Last Show of Mr. Chardish' is a journey through the variety of worlds created by the ingenious mind of the successful Director, Robert Chardish. Take the role of Ella, the Actress and through exploring an old theatre try to unveil secrets hidden in the extraordinary, magical plays created in the imagination of Mr. Chardish. When they were young, the Actress and the Director were full of dreams and ambitions. Decades later, the Actress returns to the theatre, to once more become the performer, the audience and the muse. The performances, the letters and the radio interviews - they are all meaningful, but will the Actress find what she's looking for? Attend the last show of a famous artist reflecting on his defining moments and your role in his life. With each play you will explore a new, incredible scenography, fully painted in VR. Each performance tells the story of different characters, with individual gameplay mechanics and a unique closure. Be a robot escaping a factory or a little, boastful musketeer - every role you take is a medium for emotional experiences of the Director. To separate the performances from the real world and put the stress on their artistic nature, we decided to reach for new, creative methods of graphic design. The plays’ segments of the game are painted using virtual reality technology. Exchanging traditional 3D modeling for painterly strokes and splatters granted us more expressive freedom in shaping the artistic vision of the Director. In The Last Show of Mr. Chardish you will experience: A rich, engaging story about the relationship of two artists, who founded a theatre in a British countryside. Multiple chapters with different gameplay mechanics, telling individual stories tied to the main plot. A unique art style created with VR painting technology.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you looking for an emotional game with an interesting story, incredible soundtracks and decent voice acting while experiencing a game with artistic and sometimes surrealistic visual graphics? Then The Last Show of Mr. Chardish is for you.Not all games about battle royales/PVP, having impossible challenges during platforming/parkour games, etc. Story oriented games could be called a niche genre, mainly created to adults because of their deep thoughts. These games offer much lower playtime than other games while the asking price is still 15-20$+. Considering a purchase is still a valid option if you like to support quality games with a deep meaning instead of buying the 500th reskin of a boring shooter.Interesting gameplay still required to sell a story. Usually, these kinds of games end up as walking simulators with puzzles. The Last Show of Mr. Chardish successfully tried to be different. Each act offers a different gaming experience. You can still find your puzzles, but then you can also expect sword fighting, platforming, a bird simulator and coloring a gray world to bring life and love to it.The acts you experience as Ella, the protagonist of the game, feels like remembering old theatre plays she participated in, but I believe that these acts represent the missed opportunities in life, wrong decisions, heartbreaking missed chances with someone you love while that feeling is mutual. The ending is like a dream, about a world and feelings Mr. Chardish could have been experienced, but decisions can’t be changed… Yes, The Last Show of Mr. Chardish will break your heart.A story oriented game and for those 3 things required to make it sellable and entertaining: A good story, decent voice acting and incredible soundtracks. The Last show of Mr. Chardish successfully mixed these into one game. Very interesting, sometimes heartbreaking story. I liked it, my opinion is very subjective but I think it is very good. Story rich game, it has nothing to offer on the second playthrough, unless you play it again after a few years and you have a bad memory. Good story, decent voice acting, awesome soundtracks….. Yes, you can forget about the world while playing this game. Looks nice, sometimes surreal. It is colorful and cute. Not realistic graphics, it provides a more artistic visual experience.. Art games come with decent music. This game is not an exception. Emotional and not challenging game. The puzzles, the “combat” isn’t hard at all.Perfection time: 4-6h. 1 playthrough enough, but there are many missable achievements and the total amount of collectibles HUGE. A whole playthrough could be done in 3h at first time without guides and chapter select available, so perfection is far from hard. I made a written+screenshoot collectible+achievement guide which include a walkthrough video if you get stuck on any part of the game:

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Show of Mr Chardish is an excellent narrative style game with delightful hand painted watercolour graphics.  It tells the story of Robert Chardish and the female protagonist Ella who co-founded a theatre in the British countryside.  Their relationship and successes and failures are revealed as Ella wanders through the now abandoned theatre.  The obsessive ambition of Robert and the blurring of real life and make believe comes under scrutiny.  The narrative is dictated as Ella walks around picking up notes and highlighted objects in the theatre.  Picking up a mask activates a chapter about one of their plays. The game is very emotional....full of regret, lost chances, dashed hopes and dreams, joy and love, anger and disappointment.  Each chapter contains collectables which activate a voice recording about a memory or conversation.The game play in each chapter is different as you take on a variety of characters.  You are an active member in a play and the role play can be charming and exciting.  It will thrill the actor in many people!  No time to get bored as there is plenty to do.  The story is really poignant and moving and draws you in with its emotion and charm.  I found the narrative voices good and clear.  Music was subtle and never drowned out the narrative.  Game play was clunky at times, especially with the flying sequence, but still doable on keyboard.There are two endings to this game.  There is the ability to replay each level to chase down the missing achievements which is what I did....hence my long play time!  There are many checkpoints in each chapter which is a swirling circle telling you that you've reached it.I found this game an enriching experience and I'm sure many of you will be able to relate to it in some way.  8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish is a story with multiple layers and is made up of a central framework with 5 very distinct 'mini-adventures.'  The sound track is enjoyable and the voice acting well done.The primary story is played from a first person perspective and is much like a walking simulator, exploring an old theater. You are Ella, an actress returning to your history at the request of Mr. Chardish (a person you worked closely with in your past). You walk through the ruins of the theater, listening to a taped interview with Chardish. You examine items lying about (collectibles) and listen to snippets of remembered conversations.  You find several masks in the theater and putting on each submerges you in an adventure based on a play by Chardish. These vary in artistic style and objectives. The mechanics of each are very different, as well. Within each of 5 segments, there are collectibles that contain more recordings of conversations to build out the history of your own past with the man and the theater. The segments have different styles of puzzles with a common theme of using the environment to build your path through a surreal landscape.The game saves at 'checkpoints' so if you exit between save points, you will lose some progress. There is an indicator that tells you when the game is saving so this is manageable.Most of the game uses the WASD keys and the mouse to move in the standard manner for a game built with the Unreal Engine. There is some minor platforming and the biggest hazard is falling from an edge or missing a jump which restarts the game from the last checkpoint.  There are some sections that differ a bit in terms of controls. The 'Anger' play involves minor swordplay (against pinata-like forms) that requires pointing and clicking in the proper direction. There is no penalty for failure and nothing is fighting back so this was easy for me. The 'Day Dreaming' play requires a good bit of clicking as you add color to your world and the 'Synchronicity' play involves clicking to clear obstacles from your path (since you are on wheels and cannot jump over things).In the 'Ascension' section, about half the chapter  is played as a bird. I personally found this impossible with a keyboard and mouse. I switched to a controller, slowed down the control responsiveness and inverted the horizontal. I was able to get through the chapter but really struggled. Flight sims have never been my strong suit. To make matters worse, the boundaries of the game are 'soft' so I continued to fly into spaces outside of the game world which resulted in a 'stuttering' and stuck bird and required a restart from the last checkpoint.Overall, I enjoyed the game and the discovery process as notes/letters are found and conversations/memories are heard. Without getting into spoiler territory, you have a choice to make at the end of the game. Your response changes one minor detail before the credits immediately begin to roll. Thus, this felt very anticlimactic and added little to the game itself.I recommend this to those who enjoy variety in their game-play, don't mind a brief incarnation as a bird, and take pleasure in having a story unfold through narrative bits found along the way.ONE ADDED NOTE: When circling back through specific chapters to pick up missed achievements, be prepared for some frustration. If you miss anything or fail at a task, you are likely to have to replay the chapter from the beginning to try again (backtracking is blocked or game progresses to next savepoint).
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: I am changing my review to recommended since I was able to figure out how to finish Chapter 4 from another reviewer’s tips.  So, let’s start over.This game has absolutely beautiful graphics and music and the voice acting was very well done.  The story was moving and kept my interest as it was conveyed through notes and recordings and as the characters’ thoughts as you move through the game.  The gameplay changes with the different theater plays you explore in each chapter.  Almost all of it was very doable with some parts being very easy to some challenges.  There are no combat or action elements other than hitting pinata like things that fly by you. Very easy.  The closest to a timed event is rolling onto a very slow moving crate or platform as it passes by a couple times to advance.  That said, Chapter 4 contains a bird flight simulation section that was so difficult for me I almost quit. I followed some advice to invert the horizontal axis and lower the sensitivity to almost nothing and I was able to make it through.  Even with that fix I struggled and missed picking up all the optional recordings for that section of the chapter.  I don’t play flight sims so that section was frustrating.  Once past it though, the game reverted to its slow paced beautiful self and I was very glad I got a chance to finish it.  On the whole this is a lovely game that keeps your interest with a touching story and variety in gameplay and scenes in each chapter that makes it worth it to play and enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish is a narrative-driven walking simulator with simple puzzle elements. And it was such a delight to play! We play as Ella, an aging actress who returns to an abandoned theater where she used to work with Robert Chardish, "a brilliant playright, actor and theater director". As we explore the place, we discover all kind of documents and objects that tell us more about the life at the theater and the different people who worked there. During our exploration we also find some masks, each one transporting us into fairytale worlds inspired by 5 different Mr. Chardish plays.The gameplay alternates between 1st person as Ella in the real world and 3rd person as one of the play characters in the fairytale worlds, both worlds types having two very distinct painting art styles. Puzzles mechanics are relatively simple and straighforward but of a good variety, some being quite fun to dabble with.The least we can say is that the game is utterly beautiful. The art style really made me feel like I was inside a painting. And as I played, I just kept being amazed by all the stunning sceneries.I was absolutely enchanted by this game visuals, and I can only recommend it to anyone who enjoys beautiful walking sims.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: It's...decent. But what 'The Last Show of Mr. Chardish' aspires to be is *poignant*, like 'What Remains of Edith Finch'. It doesn't get there, or anywhere close, but it is a decent story of a flawed man told through decently clever metaphorical plays, with actually really good art direction and not-bad (but not great) voice acting.For the genre of story-focused walking simulators, it's above average but not a standout. Get it on sale if you're curious.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty easy recommendation for those who enjoyed narrative games like Gone Home or What Remains of Edith Finch. The framing of the game is you, playing the actress Ella as she wanders through a dilapidated theater, reading notes, listening to audio logs and soaking up the atmosphere as you learn about the titular playwright. This is interrupted by third person adventure segments representing Chardish's plays. None of it is complicated, but the use of video game mechanics effectively communicates the themes and moods of the game, and it all comes together very well at the end. This is not a game about the story, the beats are pretty clear within the first few minutes, rather it is an exploration of the complicated emotional connection between two creative people, how they converged and how they came apart, and how even after parting that connection lingers.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: I can seriously recommend this indie game for everyone, who loves to see a wholesome beautiful piece of art!As you make your way through the theatric pieces of the game, you encounter different settings, with slightly different designs and mechanics. Each of them looking beautiful and interesting, the graphic design well done, the story well written, the music very fitting and soothing and everything overall just very captivating.I really enjoyed the characters and their voice acting as well.Experienced no bugs, just a bit of clipping here and there.Overall I was def blown away by the creative process that went into this. Well done!Ps.: Loved the lotr easter egg.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to neg on a game too hard when it's apparent a small team put a lot of time and effort into it, but I found The Last Show of Mr. Chardish incredbily dull and lifeless. The primary thing to making a decent walking sim is that the walking part of the game is at least interesting. Some of the first person environments were pretty nice looking, but 75% of this game are the play "vignettes" which I honestly found tedious. With the exception of robot puzzle, most of this game feels like playing a platformer with no platforming. Just running from point A to point B. Then running from A to B while adding color to the path. Then flying from A to B, The third vignette, Anger, is literally just running from A to B while punching 100 pinatas along the way. The cherry on top is the stroy just doesn't support the dull gameplay. You're supposed to believe you're witnessing the last remaining art of a talented artist, but it's hard to imagine even the most tripped out acid heads in the 70s enjoying the actual plays of these boring vignettes. Sorry to hate. Appreciate the work people put into small games, but I wholly did not enjoy this experience no matter how short it was.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into story-driven games that are short but sweet and if you're a bit of an art lover, I can highly recommend this game.- Wonderful soundtrack- A quality story told through different levels/theatre plays you go through- Gameplay that isn't just walking around like similar 'walking simulator' games have: keeps you engaged in the story
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: Very Edith Finch-inspired walking sim set around an old theater after the death of its featured playwright; as you explore, you'll find various masks, each of which sends you into a fantasy world inspired by one of the plays, with each world having its own distinct gameplay mechanics. Not nearly as good as Edith Finch, unsurprisingly (the "plays" feel very little like anything that could have been performed on a stage, and their central mechanics are nicely distinct from one another but don't tie into the story nearly as well), but it's still an admirably ambitious walking sim for a project that I imagine was developed on much less resources than Edith Finch, and manages to be polished enough to warrant a one-sitting play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the idea, but the excecution is very flat. This game has a bit of an identity crisis. It wants to present a metaphorical, artistic narrative but then gets lost in incredibly basic and repetitive non puzzle-platforming. It's not gameplay focused, but still tries to have some gameplay, then doesn't deliver on the strong aesthetic presentation something like this would need to work. There is this neat brushstroke texture design style, but it starts and ends there. Evoking emotion with art doesn't require looking painted, it requires composition, color, lighting, and especially the lighting is so flat and uninspired - even in a level that has light as a mechanic - it's truly tragic.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short walking sim (2 hours) that tells a story of a provincial theater director who... well, I won't spoil anything but let me just say it's a very good story that really engaged me from start to finish and left me in a very different mood than I started with. Highly recommended.The only problem for me was a strange bug: the items you interact with and interface elements didn't disappear when I put the item away, so after reading each note I had to bring up the menu -- that would remove the note from screen but the menu would stay until the next item.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: A little game with an interesting way of telling way of telling a story which does tug at the heart strings a little!A waking sim type game split up with some clever puzzles and a number of beautiful interactive scenarios as you move along the story.The music is lovely and voice acting also decent. I had a few bugs right at the start when playing on release day but they didn’t ruin the experience and didn’t occur again.I’d recommend to anyone wanting to dive into a short, beautiful, chill game with lovely music and not too much brain power required :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: Who should play "The Last Show of Mr Chardish"? Well, anyone who likes first-person exploration, a beautiful art style, a heartwarming narrative and a wonderful score. What sets this experience apart is its dreamlike quality and the well-designed puzzles in between. If you are a theatre or drama enthusiast, this could be an additional reason to take a closer look at this game. It is rather short, that's true, but it is well worth the entrance fee and the atmosphere and mood will stay with you for a while after playing through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: Simply said, this is a beautiful game.  Really enjoyed it.  Experience a complex relationship in the context of 5 "plays" (mini-levels), each with different mechanics and message.  It's all revealed and conveyed very well and fits together nicely.    If you like "touching" and "heartfelt" vibes similar to "To the Moon", then you'll probably like this also.  I'd never heard of the game, and just bought it based on the description, but very glad I did.  Give this a shot if you're even somewhat interested.  It's good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Show of Mr. Charlish is a ~2hr long walking simulator telling the story of actors Robert (the eponymous Charlish) and  Ella, decades since she left the Linfield theatre where they had both performed. In the modern day you guide Ella around the now abandoned theatre viewing old notes and relics of stage shows long since over. but through a series of masks you see (and play out) these past performances as they tell, in their own way, the story of Ella and RobertThese plays are each different small games with different characters and mechanics, though all adopt the same painted visual style. Play #2 in particular, though somewhat out of tone with everything else, I thought could have been an excellent ~10 minute game in its own right - though the 3rd I was happy to see end.Mechanically the game isn't perfect, the camera in both the real world and the plays can be a little jittery when changing elevation and some of the movement mechanics (in particular jumping, though it is infrequently necessary) lack a bit of smoothnessThe game is not as mysterious as the Steam tags may suggest, and it is more of an emotional and character driven story (in case that is important for you to know)It has it's clunkiness in the gameplay, and even as a purely narrative walking sim I wasn't always blown away - but i was charmed by this creative and unique game
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving it a thumbs up only cause i guess a lot of effort went to this game, and also can't give it neutral. I was expecting more, it's cute yes and the story is interesting, but i was expecting much more out of it. the ending doesn't give much either. I can't even say that if you like puzzle it's the game for you, because only one chapter offers it, that one kept me awake , the other ones are just going from a to b. I'm glad i got it on sale, maybe i'll go through it again to 100% the achievements , maybe ...
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: Punk Notion created some art with this game. The enviroments are beautiful. The puzzles levels are in diffirent styles, so it is not repetitive and you play with diffirent characters.I really got sucked into the sturoy so much that I just kept playing. There is nothing bad to say about The Last Show of Mr. Chardish. It is a good puzzle game with a story for a good price.Here is my first hour of gameplay:
