_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this one, though I got it on sale and would only recommend this to someone who really would be impressed by the art style alone and is easily impressed by a shallow sentimental story.  It does deliver the kind of magical atmosphere that is promised.  It is a walking simulator with the usual picking up notes and recordings as you move through these environments.  Mini games are scattered about, which add the second perspective of the romantic partner and I guess add more variety.  To me the mini games were a bit janky, and it was more like, "oh another mini-game" than something I looked forward to.  The addition of mainly parcour puzzles or primitive action elements rarely seemed that relaxing.  Some were a bit annoying, though not hard.  One of the flying sequences was supposed to convey a feeling of liberation, but the controls were so wonky that there was more likelihood of crashing into things such that, once I got the hang of it, it was easier to just stay the course rather than make any unnecessary moves.  Mostly I just found the narrative to be a dry, predictable, fairy tale love story with the odd regret.  At no point did it surprise me.  Most of the notes were brief and trivial rather than anything deep or revealing.  It came across to me like "old people reminiscing", and I am relatively old for a gamer.  I was done with it in over three hours, which isn't much considering I take my time with these games, and to be fair some of that time was chewed up when I would walk away to get something to eat or use the bathroom.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a thumbs up because it was quite different than other "walking simulator" type games I have played.Navigating through each of the plays was clever and the colorful visuals are appealing. The story is interesting... about relationships and how they change. There are some minor bugs, I hit a graphics glitch when flying too high once and I also fell through the world once jumping around in the final act, but I am willing to forgive those because the overall experience is enjoyable.Completed w/ all achievements in 2.5 hrs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: This was an interesting and quirky experience. I liked the combination of two extremely different art styles and from first to third person gameplay. The art style for the third person part of the game is an acquired taste that I'm not a fan of but it can be overlooked. The story is creative and oddly poetic, but you only begin to understand the latter when you've come relatively far into the game. All in all, it was a decently fun experience. However, the controls for the bird are ridiculously bad; it constantly went off course and got stuck under the path, as in I could see the set build, so I had to reload the latest save twice. I don't think everyone will experience that issue but it still needs to be said. My conclusion is that if you want to try something new and kind of weird then feel free to play this game but skip it if you're looking for something other than that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: Its kind of a mixed bag; the art-style was hit or miss, some of it was really nice and other scenes a bit too messy for my taste. Its a bit too abstract and I would have liked more narrative. That being said the game-play what little there was, was enjoyable enough.Overall I would recommend it but just about. Its super short though so wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: This game truly is a masterpiece. The way the plays are told in hand painted ways really hit harder then I thought. I was so pleasantly surprised by the adventure I was brought on.Pros:- Nice simple peaceful game- The story is very good and told quite well and creatively- The play sections are both unique in art and game playCons:- Not a ton of challenge- It is a bit short- Without going for the extra content you will lose some impact-full story piecesI must say that sometimes it felt a bit jagged in some sections but over all the art style really overcomes that and it kinda adds to the charm. I started out kinda meh about it and was truly in love by the end. I give it 4/5 stage plays.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish is a story about the relationship of two artists, who founded a theatre in a British countryside.You start the game in first person view, playing as Ella, set in the 1970s, Ella decides to travel to an old theatre that she used to perform at, as she explores she is able to access memories, and as she does you are transported into the mind of Mr Chardish, and you then see the world as he did, and this is where Act 1 Starts, and this is the first of the different "play styles" that exist within the world. Solitude, Anger, Symmetry, Ascension, and Daydream. Each play style is very different, and basically different games in their own sense.I will keep this review to just the Solitude and Symmetry levels, as they are what I have played and completed so far.As you play you will find letters to be read, records to be listened to and so on, they all make up what is a lovely story, which is very engaging.Solitude is pretty standard game play, easy to figure out in the 3rd person view, you explore the area, and have to solve puzzles so you can progress to the next area, for example you may need to move a stage light so that it shines on an area which in turn may make some steps appear, or more the light away and a door may become unlocked. Once you figure out how to do this, you can pretty much work your way through the level, all the while enjoying what are some amazing hand drawn graphics, now you do need a decent graphics card to get the best out of this game graphics wise, so do be warned.Symmetry, you play as a robot on wheels, you meet a companion and together you will try to pass obstacles and area, you may need to control a lift by mirroring yourself with the lift, or open and close gates, all in all this is a completely different experience to that of Solitude, and I found it much harder too. But once I got the hang of it, and with a bit of trial and error I found myself confident in what I was doing and so passed through the level.The GoodA fascinating idea for a game, with glorious graphics (if your PC can handle them), and a lovely engaging story.The BadOnce you figure out the basic idea for one of the 5 play styles, you will quickly complete it, so the game in that sense is quite short.And unless you have a powerful PC you may not be able to truly enjoy the incredible graphics.OverallAlthough the game is short, it is enjoyable, and best of all you can play the Solitude level for free as part of a Prologue release on Steam.An enjoyable game that I score 7/10Originally Published on
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

_childDocuments_.review: Decades have passed and the Actress, Ella, returns to the abandoned theatre to uncover a preserved collection of extraordinary performances. Explore a variety of magical, hand-painted worlds as you collect the lost pieces of the past.
_childDocuments_.name: The Last Show of Mr. Chardish

name: Trepang2
detailed_description: BE THE ULTIMATE BADASS You play as an escaped soldier, who has no memories of their past life, but is infused with supernatural abilities. Revenge is on your mind, and you’ll stop at nothing to get what you want. Deliver devastating punches, sneak around in the shadows, wield explosive weapons, and give the bad guys a taste of their own medicine. FEATURES: EXPLOSIVE SINGLE-PLAYER STORY CAMPAIGN A mysterious group breaks you out from a heavily guarded blacksite. Your memories are gone but your combat abilities are enhanced far beyond human limits. Fight back, find the truth and face a threat even deadlier than yourself. NEXT LEVEL SUPER-POWERS Master your superhuman strength and speed to knock waves of heavily armed mercenaries into next week. Slow down time to dodge rapid-fire bullets and use cloaking to become invisible and snap your enemies' necks when they least expect it. BRUTAL MELEE COMBAT Square up to your enemies in close quarters melee combat and go full throttle in rapid fire gunfights. Punch, kick, slide and deliver hardcore combos that reduce your foes to dust. END NOTE Follow, join the community and chat with the devs. Look in the external links to join our Twitter, Youtube and Discord. We're always listening!

_childDocuments_.review: the combat is satisfying in a way that makes the game addicting. The sounds and user feedback are so good its like eating authentic italian pizza but for your ears mhmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm this game makes you feel like john wick with superpowers. Wiping out squads on higher difficulties is especially satisfying. Story is pretty good (nun too crazy). The graphics and UI all feel like a AAA game and I cant wait for the story DLC
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, but can you add an option to disable the jump scares and other creepy parts of the game, I paused the game to go afk during the site 83 hallway area just right before the black cloud jump scared me, and when i came back and unpaused the game I nearly punched my monitor like that one maze dude, needless to say I chickened out and haven't returned to beat that level and move on with the game since then, so it would be much appreciated if there was an option to disable the jump scares when playing. Other than that the game is pretty fun. Have a good day!
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: [Over 100+ Hours in Horde Mode]This is THE action FPS of 2023. A perfect symphony of frantic fast paced dismembering action game goodness, Trepang² delivers hours of kinetic action well past the admittedly short campaign. There are many things this game falls short on but the core root of any problem from the campaign stems from the game not delivering EVEN HARDER on the set pieces and the bosses suffering from repetitive mechanics that don't compliment the beautiful sandbox that has been created by this gifted team of 4 dudes. With that in mind i'm not claiming hyperbole when I say this is THE best FPS to come out this year so far. The TRUE skill ceiling for this game is only known by the most dedicated and hardcore but in time the rest of the FPS audience will hopefully catch on to the BRILLIANT action game mechanics that this game offers. Fan of Doom Eternal and Devil May Cry? THIS IS THE GAME FOR YOU. Hint: Hold shift while air kicking to drop kick. That is this games enemy step. I'll leave the real ones to lab the rest in horde...
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: Overpriced and janky. Physics feel floaty and weightless, enemy AI is mindless murder-fodder.In general this feels like a hobby project. You can buy the entire FEAR franchise for under $10, just replay those games - and save your time & money!UPDATE: I gave it some more consideration, and this game is even worse than i thought. Don't fall for the hype! Bad physics, wonky blood effects. If you like good games, you should skip this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: one of those games that just has a wicked strong understanding of what makes a game fun. sliding, dual wielding, throwing people, and jump kicks are all super sick, so why not just throw them all in? the result is an endlessly cathartic shooter that can be enjoyed on any level between simple decompression and sweatily torturing yourself. even after finishing the wicked short campaign, i often find myself returning to the game's horde mode without even thinking and ripping through enemies like im playing with a stress ball. that's not to say im an expert by any means - i die all the time - but the gameplay is so smooth and satisfying that i dont mind mashing "restart" to get back into the action every time.sound design is an extremely vital aspect of any shooter, and this game knocks it out of the park with its wicked punchy gunshots, solid, meaty thwacks, and the perfect level of splatter and scrunch to punctuate it all. i'd say the only actual issues i take with this game are that the story is a total snoozefest (although that may be solely due to my total disinterest in call-of-duty-esque stories packed with generic soldiers, codenames, and secret organizations that i could never be bothered to memorize), and that the semi-frequent attempts at horror fall flat on their face and did nothing but make me tap my foot impatiently waiting for another wave of dudes to shoot. its honestly a baffling decision to try n put slow burn horror segments into a power fantasy type game where the entire point is that you play as an overpowered super soldier. also the final boss sucks butt. but, barring those nitpicks, i absolutely recommend trepang2 to anyone who's into the fps subgenre of "you get to do a bunch of hogwild bullsh/it" like me.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: One hell of a game!  For an indie team, Trepang2 is one of the most satisfying FPS games I experienced in 2023. Everything from the F.E.A.R-like gameplay to the banger OST. It's been one of the highlights of the year for me.Positives:Everything about the gunplay. Everything about it feels so brutal like every bullet is tearing through something whether it's a person or a wall. Every gun is useful in their own respective roles and can all be customized like a shotgun with fire rounds or a mini-gun with a bayonet. It all feels good especially the shotgun which has to be ranked as one of the top shotguns in FPS history. It's that good. The movement is also good too fitting in well with the over the top nature of the game. Visuals and Optimization are also top-notch as the game ran great on my RX 6600 on high settings with some hiccups here and there. The game can look and feel like peak UE4 with the over the top effects but it works with Trepang2 because the whole game is over the top especially when you can launch someone 40 feet in the air by sliding into them. OST: It blends in real well with all of the carnage in combat. It's pretty damn good.Negatives:It's really short taking me about 5 and a half hours to complete all of the main and side missions meaning there's isn't too meat on the bones here although there are cheats and a horde mode available for replay value. Variety in missions is also lacking as well as the side missions do end up repeating the same old kill waves of enemies until you're all done and main missions have the same kill everything that moves with some outliers here and there. It's great because it's more of Trepang2's combat but it's disappointing when a mission starts out somewhat promising but devolves into the same structure as the rest.The story is definitely a story. I will say that.Overall, I think Trepang2 is a great package and is one of the highlights of the year for everything it gets right about the FPS genre but I would say that you're in for a great ride, just not for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game but it just feels really unpolished and that kinda killed it for me. For starters there doesn't seem to be any way to aim down sights with any gun that doesn't have a scope, which makes pretty much every gun close-mid range only. For guns that do have a scope there's no ADS sensitivity setting so when aiming your mouse/controller sensitivity is the same as normal, which makes it basically impossible to aim while zoomed in on a controller.There also doesn't seem to be a way to tell how much focus or cloak power you have without trying to use them. For cloak power specifically if you cancel it after activating you lose the entire charge. If you hear some enemies around a corner and you want to cloak and peek then find out there's no enemies and cancel cloak you lose the whole charge which is just dumb. I basically never used it because I ended up wasting it every time I tried to peek and cancel.The default setting for sprint on a controller is left thumb stick but you have to hold it to sprint, there's no way to tab to engage and keep sprinting as long as you're moving like most other games do. The movement in general is clunky and just feels a little weird. These might seem like nit picks but the game is all about combat and yet every aspect of the combat is just clunky which makes the whole thing feel meh.

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang2, A True Spiritual Successor To F.E.A.R.Game straight slaps. A very high octane and very violent fps that is carried by its meaty gunplay, well crafted combat arenas and abilities that serve chaotic fun above all else. The story is a little on the lighter side and the game length is only roughly 8-10 hours, but garners more than enough intrigue to keep you blasting onward. There's quite a decent amount of spookage and things I won't spoil here too, which I honestly really dug. The atmosphere is intoxicating.*Dual wielding*Bullet Time*Sliding into foes to send their ragdolls flying*Kicking blokes in the head mid air to send you flying back in the air*Grabbing enemies and launching em (nade pin optional)*SPAS-12 TURNING ELITE SOLDIERS INTO PASTEThis game hits all of those F.E.A.R combat notes perfectly, and then some. Accompanied by a pretty breakneck score and intense enemy comms/screaming, you've got a solid but inspired fps recipe.That being said, this gory, fast paced n fluid, gorgeous to look at, VERY fun fps does stand on its own two legs as a great shooter, even if those legs are planted on the shoulders of F.E.A.R.10/10 Would Visit The Backrooms Again.

_childDocuments_.review: It's times like these where I really wish Steam had a "Mixed" option for reviews...Look, I like Trepang2, but I really feel like it could have been way better if it didn't try to be so many different games and then not even getting right what those other games did.The gunplay and movement is great, as long as you keep it to close quarter areas that is, I didn't even mind the harder difficulties, however when the game is designed to work in close quarters WHY are there so many levels with huge open areas?? The accuracy of the weapons can barely hit an enemy 10m away let alone 100.Why are the horror segments of this game so tedious and bland?You're gonna give me a chase sequence after getting jumpscared where I can barely run and take away all that momentum for what reason?The story isn't very good either, but I can't fault it for that too much since not many FPS games need a story to be good, but Trepang2 TRIES to make the story work and it just all feels so rushed and inconsistent.What was the point of the home base? Just for a small little twist at the end? There is nothing a level selector wouldn't have done better.Trepang2 EXCELS at CQB and that's it, it's a great game if you play it on the smaller maps, but not too small apparently because some of the "horde" maps are awfully small!! There is barely any cover in some of them and literally no variety in the enemy waves across all!There are a few songs I quite liked and even some of the side missions where you have to protect the computers, while some may find bland, I liked those, because the levels feel like they were actually designed with the gameplay in mind.I wish this game would've been so much better, I really think it could have been, I enjoyed it, and those who are looking for cool gun fu CQB will too, but it's hard to overlook the flaws...

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR, 8.5/10, good recall to FEAR, DOOM, and Timesplitters with a sprinkle of SCP, Creepypasta references, and good ol fashioned mayhem.  This game caught me by surprise in every chapter, starting from the first mission to every story mission afterwards.  Though the fighting got tedious at some points, the parts where it was you and the environment, that was when your senses peaked the fear and terror began to set it.  Great replayability, good gun play, good story that kept you guessing, and the atmosphere pulls you in and keeps you.  All in all, a solid indie approach to the old school idea of FEAR with a really solid landing and execution.If you ever liked FEAR or its counterparts, you wont be disappointed with Trepang, it may be on the shorter side if you go fast, but it will keep you hooked till its over.Grab it by itself, or on sale, and take the 7[ish] hours to do the main story on Normal/Hard.  Up the difficulty for a serious challenge, unlock all the cheats, play the sandbox, and look for everything the levels have to offer, this is just the tip of iceberg, and its worth the dive.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite funny with the title when it's nothing about sea cucumber xdTrepang 2 is instantly one of my favorite FPS, as it is what FEAR should had and has been, go between tactical shooters to horror survival, the game constantly puts you on edge and stress, as that's the point, because a cornered dog is dangerous.Play as a special human with invisibility, bullet time and super strength that can throw enemies flying and get them knocked on the ground.Your enemies, from human enemies to monsters, they are relentless, merciless, and will make you question your prowess about FPS. Playing on higher difficulty essentially makes you fight against pro players from every FPS competitive scene, you will die a lot. But guess what? So do they!Execute your enemies with styles! Slide over and knock them on the ground, shoot head. Go invisible, go behind them, grab them, snap their necks. Or go bullet time, shoot right into their heads. Run towards them and kick them in the heads. The choices are all yours.There are no bullet sponges, it's all about observation and how you execute your enemies, one bullet to the head will guarantee their death, especially against human bosses, save for the super natural creatures.There's no ADS and is all about hip fire, this really gives me good Half Life and Counter Strike nolstagia as both are still my most favorite series even to this day, just go and trigger happy until everyone but you is dead, and be sure to spare your friendly AIs of course, and no, you cannot swap their guns like in Halo. If you want their guns, you'll have to pry it off from their cold dead hands.Weapon and outfit customization, you can collect weapon parts in missions and further customize your guns to your heart desire, and it does not overly bloated with attachments like Call of Duty, and better than that, your outfits can be fully customized from hands to toes. Unlock more camoflauge patterns by playing on harder difficulty, and wear them with pride as you rightfully earned them!Collect anything you see! Pick up any intel you can to know more about your character, the organization you work with and against. Learn more about backgrounds and piece the puzzle together to formulate your own conspiracy theory.Cheat menus to have fun, each are unlocked by difficulty as well, either giving yourself infinite ammo to enemies with infinite grenades! Watch them slide all over the place by touching them is funny as heck xdAnd this is a game where it's done right, gameplay, loading screen, menu screen, even option screen are cool to browse through. Essentially don't want players get bored and keep them hyped for upcoming fights.Absolutely recommend for anyone who are eager for blood sheds and challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 is the shooter that I have been missing all my life since playing F.E.A.R back on the Xbox 360 console. While not a total recreation of part of its previous generation, it does mix in its own pace of combat that blends both the best of modern gun-ho shooter-ups like DOOM 2016, and the visual flair of the original F.E.A.R into something much more tantalizing to the present time. Not many FPS games take on this style of insane gun play quite like Trepang2 does, and it pulls no punches in its crisp game play and visceral dismemberment of foes. The story is not something special but it does enable the player to ease into the horror themes and action-adventure setting, as you play as a super soldier of sorts. Take revenge against a megacorporation, as you fight the usual cast of crass if competent PMCs along with eldritch, otherworldy creatures in a span of five story missions, along with a few other side missions that expand on the intrigue and gameplay loops. More lore on the universe can be found via intel documents scattered across all missions, as they do provide more context to the factions and paranormal. Overall, the story just provides a suitable backdrop for the enemies and locales you will be fighting in, and it does its job well.Highly recommend it to people who love F.E.A.R but also to fans of the contemporary FPS games like Black Mesa and the DOOM remakes.

Hard is the most fair difficultly. The rest are pain factories, especially extreme and rage mode. The story is decent, although not directly explained, it can be found through the many intel documents you find throughout. It does leave questions to be answered, what are the 106 subjects, why were they created. Who is the Syndicate? How did Anton create Horizon and why? And they could've fleshed out the Director of Task Force 27 a bit more as well. But still incorporate mystery in the story to keep the audience hooked. But this is less of a book and more of a adrenaline rush of violence and gore. Also, the soundtrack is killer.

_childDocuments_.review: Immensely fun gameplay, constantly challenging, and a lot of excellent mechanics. The story is an interesting one, and, without spoilers, ends on a low note for the protagonist. I now really want to go back through and find every single collectible, no game has ever made me want to do that this badly. Each mission is something different, even some of the side missions are really unique and interesting, and the enemy banter is great. Oh, you stumbled upon your dead friend with his head gone? You won't simply say "Hey, dead body here", no, you'll probably yell out in fear that the guy you were talking to just a minute ago is now missing his head. The enemies feel like real people, they have real reactions, they talk to each other and communicate. I've done so much on the higher difficulties because it feels like they use actual tactics to lock down your position. Unfortuneately for them, invisibility and time slowing easily beat out most tactics. The final boss fights are truly difficult, though the very last one is easy as long as you can recognize the attack patterns.

_childDocuments_.review: Intensely frustrating fun, but I do lean more towards 'recommend' than 'don't recommend.'  Still wish Steam had a middle-ground option that was more clear on how exactly people felt about the game.Apart from the usual-these-days complaints of shooters having enemies that turn on a dime with no momentum, bog-standard shot-spread problems that make snipers/DMRs impossible to use if you don't glue your eye to a scope, shotguns turn to confetti after 3 feet, and the ever-annoying omniscient AI problem, I do have one hyper-specific complaint, though, and it largely has to do with the gunplay.Why did Titanfall set the coolest-ever precedent that nobody thereafter followed?  The amount of time you have to spend in this game interrupting your own reload animation for various reasons, only to eject the 38th magazine from your pistol that only holds one, does get downright silly.  This game in particular, being so high-action high-octane and demanding so much from the player, would benefit TREMENDOUSLY from a  like the aforementioned Titanfall accomplished.In a game where you have to be highly mobile, switch weapons frequently due to ammo shortages, slide and hop around like a ♥♥♥♥♥-up rabbit with a shotgun, and have to make frequent use of grabbing enemies/melee as part of your arsenal, a system like that would be an incredible help to already pretty nice game.Also, please communicate better to the player that there's no fall damage.  I genuinely got stuck on the castle level because I didn't know you're intended to fall 2 stories straight down and expect to be perfectly fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 is a Visceral Ballet of Bullets and Blood.Thank You, Trepang Studios.I love your game.I feel blessed to not only have the opportunity to follow the development of this game for so long, but also be involved in creating content to market and advertise it.The game play is over the top.Non stop carnage and violence, the level of detail in not only the visual side, but sound design is just spot on.At the time of writing this I have 130 hours in the full game.I often find myself replaying a save point to just enjoy a firefight again and again and again.If your after a fast paced, very gory & violent game with in your face combat then Trepang2 will do it for you.Then there is the Soundtrack, the music in this game goes harder than your Nanna at Church on a Sunday!Brandon McKagan has an amazing talent for music.I started following the development of this game back in 2018, I was blown away with how the game play felt.I had not come cross any game that just scratched the itch the F.E.A.R. from 2005 have left me with.Yet their little demo on IndieDB certainly did it for me.Close quarters, fast paced melee combat that just flowed smoothly.I made a short video in 2018 and a little while later Wilson contacted me and ask if he could use the video and that cemented my love affair with this game and developer.Since 2018 the developer would send me builds of how the game was progressing.In 2019 I was slipped a few more test builds and the direction and design had come so far from the 2018 build.Then late in 2019 the first demo landed on Steam and their Fan Base began to grow.In Feb 2022 I was gifted the full game and have watched the ongoing development of this game to where it is now.For a small Indie Development Team, this game makes most AAA titles look weak.If I didn't own this game, I would buy buy it!Here's a short video covering 2017 to 2019 of the game development.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been following this game since the first public demo and im happy to see that the finished game exceeded my expectations.The story has a simple premise: "stop le evil corporation", you are rescued from a research facility and become part of a task force that goes on missions to "clean up" after said evil corporation in the most violent way possible. This sets up really good events like going in a cultist base and a haunted soviet underground facility. The soviet underground base was definitely the highlight of the game for me, there are really well done horror segments with gunfights inbetween. All missions are really well paced and i was never bored while playing. The lore is delivered mostly through the environment with intel messages that are written in a concise and compelling way: some intel is just employees talking crap and other is scientist or guard logs detailing how everything is going downhill.The combat hasn't changed much since the demo and that's fine because it was very fun and solid to begin with. The shooting alone feels really good: enemies have very detailed responses like active ragdolls, a solid gore system and incredible voice acting. Different enemy types and groups (like spec ops squads and cultists) have a different voice actor and they do an incredible job at conveying all the different emotions one can feel from being attacked by a lightning fast, dual wielding supersoldier.In combat you can go invisible, enable bullet time, slide really fast, kick, take hostages and throw said hostages with a live grenade. The game allows you to kill enemies stealthily by giving you ability to go invisible, suppressors, really quick stealth takedowns (no stupid choking out, you instantly snap their necks or punch them in the face) and overall really well designed enemy AI. Enemies constantly talk with each other, they peek around corners and wait next to doorways for ambushes. The fights are often incredibly fun, because you can do ridiculous combos like throwing a grenade hostage in a crowd, jump kicking one of the remaining enemies and getting launched in the air for a sick slow motion headshot and landing on a different guy with a dropkick. You can throw your own grenades, but hostages are free and they make a funny noise.The difficulty is very well thoght out: higher difficulties do not increase enemy health, but they react faster and you can't tank as many shots. The game has given you slow motion, invisibility and sliding and with all that you can definitely beat the game on Rage difficulty and still have an amount of fun (dual incendiary shotguns make it so much more tolerable).Overall i highly recommend the game to anyone who played the original F.E.A.R. and just about anyone else who likes shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever been more frustrated with a game I truly love before. This game is so damn close to being a straight up 10/10, but some baffling choices prevent it from attaining that honor in my eyes, and it would be so easy to fix.This is going to be a lot more of a critique of some things I hate about the game than a review. If you like FPS games buy it. If you liked Fear, Crysis, or any of the other 2000's supersoldier games, buy this right now. Absolutely worth 30$. It's so self evidently fantastic that it's easier for you to just play it and understand than it is for me to explain.This is going to sound strange, but the biggest flaw of this game is in it's weapons. They feel amazing, they're all mostly useful, but oh my God, why are they like this??? There are 9 weapons. 3 of them are power weapons very really carried by enemies, so it's really only 6. Not good variety. Each weapon has low ammo reserves, holding usually 3-4 reserve mags. This is obviously meant to make you switch weapons a lot, which is completely fine. There's also an attachment system! Hell yeah! I loved this is Crysis. However, and this pisses me off to no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ end, each gun only has like 4-6 attachments that are all the most basic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ muzzle laser and sight schlock you've ever seen. WHY????? You unlock them by playing through the game and picking up these collectible parts. Awesome. Exactly how it should be, and it provides gameplay progression that is desperately needed imo. But again, only 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ attachments per weapon, with only only 6 conventional guns? This is a game with supernatural elements, why are you limiting yourself to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ silencers and 2x scopes? We literally fight zombies and a mutated bat, I think we could suspend our disbelief for the sake of cool attachments. You would not believe how noticable this is as you continue to play. It gets even worse with the horde mode. Developer, if you're reading this, please for the love of God overhaul the weapons. I want to replay your game to get all the cool skins so bad. I want to complete the horde and survival modes over and over again. I want to master this kickass combat! But the gameplay just doesn't have enough variety to make it fun for me to do so. The game plays absolutely phenomenally, one of the best ever. You have the content, you have the enemies and levels, but the lack of meaningful weapon variety kills the replayability so hard. Please, take advantage of the awesome attachment system and go wild! There are literally more specials than there are guns. This is NOT the time for "less is more". For an example on how to pull off less weapons more choices, let's take a look at a game that pulls this system off perfectly. Nioh 2. In that game, there are also 9 weapons. However, you have three different movesets for each weapon, and about 15-20 unique skills that you can equip to use in various situations. I have 500 hours in Nioh 2, because the combat has such immense depth and variety that I just don't want to stop playing. Trepang2 could be this type of game. It's so close to being that game. Whenever I get bored, Trepang2 always sounds good in my head. But the lacking variety saps the replayability so hard, man. Horde mode becomes an absolute slog as you just dual wield shotguns the entire time and periodically use the SMG and Pistol for 20 entire waves. There are even attachments that change how a weapon functions in the game already! They're awesome! Please for the love of God, make more of them. Please, for the love of Buddha, add more weapons too. I can't even fathom how fun it would be to fan fire a revolver, do the one hand spin while dual wielding lever actions, disintegrate a cultist with a double barrel, laugh in awe as Subject 106 manages to dual wield bolt action rifles by pulling the bolt with his teeth, and so much more. Dev, you seem like a genuinely cool dude, you have the best base elements of an FPS game I have ever seen. Please, expand not add. This game doesn't need more grenades, it needs more sick ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ weapons, meaningful attachments, and greater combat variety. Skins are only as good of a reward as the weapon they're on. Don't be afraid to change the game for the better! Look at Dying Light 2, that game literally changed the entire base mechanics of it's combat system to be more like Dying Light 1, and everyone loved it. You don't even need to do that! All you have to do is add more of what you already have.

Exploration is rewarded, most of the time I was finding weapon parts and items politely put around for just keeping my eyes open.Voice acting is top notch and genuinely made me laugh multiple times, the dialogue is pretty funny in my opinion, you can tell the devs had fun making this. _childDocuments_.review: F.E.A.R was a game that absolutely amazed me in the early 2000s. The atmosphere, the aesthetic, the distinct look and feel of it all. Trepang2 is pretty much that. The first F.E.A.R game but updated to an extreme. This game has some insanely good gunplay and the weapon sound design is loud, booming and best of all, powerful. Even the starter pistol sounds like it will rip through super soldiers like tissue. If done right, it for damn sure can too. The graphics and presentation are stunning at times. So many modern games look lovely though a lot seems to blend together with very similar art styles. This game is one of very few where I stop and look at a scene just to admire the impressive lighting and heavy atmosphere. Some environments are just pure dark art. Where this kinda falls apart is the story. It has twists and turns but overall, it sometimes feels out of place. You go from hunting a cryptid among poison zombies to... a castle full of fanatical cultists who hilariously scream "MY HOLY WEAPON IS EMPTY" or something along those lines. It's very odd to have such strikingly different environments with a loose story and little explained. The rest of the lore is pretty much in collectibles. As far as the horror, it has so much potential and some scenes are genuinely cool. I LOVE horror aesthetics and this game has a lot of it. However, it's not consistent. The only consistent enemy type the entire game are soldiers, heavy armor soldiers and hard to spot spec ops soldiers. Monsters don't have a huge part in this. The one part that got me laughing was the very sudden inclusion of the Backrooms. Yyyyyeah. Despite those odd negatives, This game is a full recommend from me. The gunplay carries this game. Look you can strap bayonets to a minigun and turn the end of your barrel into a blender while you reload. That alone is worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: It's weird, it's unpolished, it's poorly paced, it's slightly overpriced, it's janky, it's got that cheap "asset store" look.It's also the most earnest, least pretentious game to release this year. It's an unabashedly indie production punching way above its weight, cobbled together by a skeleton crew of modders-turned-developers. Trepang2 is the power fantasy that you daydreamed of in high school and it isn't trying to be anything else. Glorious, exuberant powerviolence. When you truly get into that eardrum-shattering, hostage-killing, bombastic, ecstatic zone, everything else melts away into a red mist.Watch these developers' careers with great interest.

_childDocuments_.review: Doom ETERNAL. Now when I have your attention, yes, somehow when you play this game you will get feeling like you play Doom Eternal, but not fully Doom Eternal, but some wierd mesh of Brutal Doom and Doom Eternal, do you ask why? _childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 was one of those games that I had played the demo for about a year before it's release, and I got very hyped to be able to play the finished product. I enjoyed playing through Trepang2 immensely, and after going for the 100% achievements I feel obligated to write a review for what I believe to be one of the best FPS games I've ever played.• The gameplay loop  The gunplay and movement both feel amazing in Trepang2. They're very fast by nature but not too fast to understand what's happening. There are also several other combat mechanics such as being able to use human shields or slow down time that all pair well with each other and none of them feel particularly useless or shoehorned in.• The AIThe AI is very dynamic and is programmed well. Enemy guards will form into small squads and will also comment on a surprising amount of different situations, such as battle buddies disappearing or being the last soldier standing against the player. Maybe not to the same level as FEAR (not that I would know personally though), but about on par with the Hgrunts from Half-Life.• The weaponsThe weapons feel impactful and satisfying to use. Most of them have their place as part of the player's arsenal and their usability is bolstered by the ability to mod each one to better suit a specific playstyle or purpose.• The graphicsTrepang2 is visually stunning. I don't think I've ever been able to run anything that looks quite as good as Trepang2, which speaks volumes about it's optimization. Despite this, it loads faster than a majority of other games I've ever played, with load times only ever being a few seconds.• The soundtrackThe OST of Trepang2 is among my personal best. Compliments the gameplay well and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rocks. Shard and Server Technician in particular are my favorite.• The story   The plot feels it was written retroactively after all the main and side levels were finished as a means of "justifying" your rampage through each, as opposed to each level feeling like the next step in accomplishing a goal. It's also easy to miss a lot of important context or plot details if you don't find every intel document in each level, which is a dedicated effort since some levels have close to 30 collectible docs hidden in them.• The ending [SPOILERS]

_childDocuments_.review: really nutty and cool game, awesome combat and gunplay, although having a fairly lackluster narrative which is only really expanded upon through intel documents you find throughout the game. rather cool voice acting too and set-pieces, although sometimes the difficulty spiking at the very tail-end of the game is questionable, but still doable.you play as Subject 106, a super soldier, recently unshackled from their captor, Horizon Corporation. coupled with the ability to react with insane precision (bullet time/slow-mo), and absorbing all light around him to virtually cloak himself to stealth around and reposition when necessary, you're now on a path to retribution against Horizon and all of its questionable business practices.guns feel like they all definitely serve a purpose throughout the game. whether you want to get up-close and blow some guy's schnoz off with a shotgun, pick them out from afar with a DMR, blowing stuff up with a grenade launcher with reckless abandon, or guns blazing with a heavy machine gun. the biggest meat and potatoes of this game, is likely the side missions and combat simulations alongside the main course of the campaign. i have yet to play the survival mode DLC, but from what it seems like, it gives you objectives to complete in a specific horde map, and transitions you across multiple with different objectives every time. much more varied than the horde mode or simply endless, but there is a lot of fun to be had in the combat simulations. the Bladekisser DLC drops a week from now as a write this, and with it, 2-3 new weapons (a revolver, LMG and a funking SWORD), 2 new side missions, and 9 more combat sim maps, it seems like it'll add just a bit more onto this game.buy this game if you like F.E.A.R, or any general fact-paced FPS that allows you to do slow-mo and mercilessly decimate your enemies, there's tons of good fun to be had here.

_childDocuments_.review: My family was being torn apart. My wife and I kept getting into fights no matter how hard we tried to get along and my son stopped smiling at us or for pictures. My Brother In Law lost his job at the Whole Foods and had become depressed. Everything was spiraling out of control. Then I saw this masterpiece, a work of art made by Gods. I thought to myself that this game might be able to help me get away from it all, have piece for just one minute.    I got the game and booted it up. The first thing I noticed was the loading screen, a nuclear explosion. Then I loaded in and heard a killer soundtrack, I loved the game already. I created a new save and went into the first level, a prison complex. The gib physics were wonderful and the graphics were stunning. I loved being able to take out all my stress and anger on these little, insignificant, prison guards. I showed this game to my B.I.L. and his face lit up when he saw the spas-12 in his hand. He told me later that Trepang2 cured his depression, and it was his motivation to get a job as a litigation lawyer, making much more money than before. How he got a law degree to become a litigation lawyer? Hell if I know. I then showed my wife the game, I was a little worried at first that she would find the game to graphic or difficult but she was a natural. She used her abilities at exactly the right time and got only head shots. She was scary good at the game and was really happy when playing it. Gradually after several months of me, my wife, and my BIL playing Trepang2 my wife and I stopped getting into fights and my BIL stopped being as depressed.

_childDocuments_.review: A firm, hearty foundation settling a crude structure dressed in boards and gypsum.Despite my strong anticipation for its release, it's quite difficult to reminisce  after finishing its short campaign's chapters. It would have been slightly remiss to have expected the moon and the stars from it, considering it's allusions to FPS titles from the early Xbox 360 era: , , and , described in its gameplay quirks and from commentary indie journalists and content creators brought forth covering the game's demo back in 2019.However, 's ultimate goal is to be what its blurb states, only referencing those titles with its game mechanics and settings. It successfully marries the gameplay styles of  and , attributing player mechanics from either game (e.g. bullet time from , cloaking from ) without overpowering the player; it portrays a gameplay balancing act that at times resembles that of , with a similar amount of viscera to boot. Selective aim-down sights may seem odd to modern-FPS enthusiasts, but this is compensated with many levels in  being linear and compact, with the odd arena section to test your capability of bringing yourself closer to enemies using avenues in the environment or crudely exploiting the cloak and slide mechanics. Sadly, the A.I. doesn't live up to  's, rather it resembling 's, right down to the grenade/flare spamming and predictable enemy placements. There's nothing to analyze regarding narrative in ; it's basic, it's bare, it's there to scene the gameplay, which is sound for a game focusing on such. The environments, as dense as they were, didn't draw much from me as without any lingering threats to dread beyond heavily geared grunts in balaclavas, horror immersion fell flat for me.Despite its flaws and as someone who enjoys ,  appeals to me both as a belated oasis from 's lesser sequels, and as a proof of concept for an incredibly strong gameplay foundation that could elaborate into a passionately crafted series or developer motif with a unique identity set apart from its obvious inspirations.

_childDocuments_.review: If this game was supposed to be a FEAR successor, then the develops failed to realize what made FEAR so great almost 20 years ago.First the weapons are horrible, they have heavy recoil and are very inaccurate. They give you no ammo for the weapons you want to use. The attachment system makes no sense. you have to find weapon parts to permently unlock them and the game decides what to unlock, you cant choose what part you want to unlock. I don't understand why you cants switch weapon parts out anytime you want like crysis, you have to find weapon box to modify them. If you have a weapon with all your favorite attachments and you run out ammo you are forced to drop that weapon for another inferior weapon. its just dumb.The enemies are bullet sponges and move around so fast ,its so difficult to shoot a moving enemy. The AI still cant hold up to FEAR. The base where you choose a mission is just useless and a waste of time. I dont know why they even included it. The way you are dropped into a mission is weird. _childDocuments_.review: i don't usually buy games for for 30 euros but this game is well worth this amount. from an arena FPS perspective, the gameplay loop is literally perfect and the game is completely fair even on the highest difficulties (i finished it on extreme). i never got mad at it because when you ♥♥♥♥ up, it makes it obvious that it was your fault. everything that happens is clearly telegraphed so you always know where the enemies are and what they are doing. besides the gameplay, trepang2 has a great narrative. it's full of show-don't-tell, and, certainly, that doesn't make it good in itself, but how these spectacles are connected. you can easily make out the background of the game world if you spend enough time pondering it, and it all just makes sense. it's not something i can put into words, because i don't have the knowledge to critically analyze it, but it just works.this game is also amazing from a technical perspective. the graphics are very complex and detailed, yet it manages to run perfectly on my laptop with specs under the minimum requirements, and i don't even have to turn the settings that far down. i have not encountered a single bug playing this game. *and* the install size is under 40 GB. plus, even if this game is windows exclusive, it runs perfectly on linux systems through proton. it's absolutely amazing how well made this game is - i'd say it has AAA quality, but nowadays, no triple-a developer releases stable, optimized and well-designed games. 12/10 game of the year

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a FEAR Successor.This is kinda what I wanted with FEAR, an military group that is up against another group but also have to deal with supernatural things on the side. In the first FEAR, you are part of FEAR which handles supernatural things which was the biggest drawing point, an action shooter with some spooks on the side and you were special "His reflexes are off the charts." until Perseus Mandate where you play as someone else and he just happens to be special like you, FEAR 2 and 3 steered away at the concept of a military group called FEAR and made it all about Armachem and all the horrid things they have done and you end up playing as some rando that ends up being special because Alma had a huge crush on him. FEAR 3 was... yeah, full of inconsistencies from the previous games and it felt like they didn't know what direction they wanted to do with FEAR and therefore killing the franchise on a sour note.Back to Trepang2This game has done everything right for their first game as a FEAR successor.1. Action: Extremely heavy and intense.2. Music: Freaking bangers3. Voice Acting: So believable, you can hear how much emotion the Agents have in their sitreps, how stressed they are, how much they hate 106 and sometimes how scared they are.The ability to stealth for a little while is a nice addition to get you out of fire and take some time to reload all your guns and sneak around while the enemies shoot and throw all their grenades to the last place they saw you.The only thing that I wished for was for a little bit more destructive environments like FEAR 1 and how enemies respond like in FEAR 1. I know they do respond in ways depending on how many of them are left. like: "Okay you bastard, it's just you and me now!" or "Squad? Aw ♥♥♥♥! My Squad is down!" but it would be great that they acted more like a team and like take cover and give orders to other squad mates on where you are and then tell them to go flank while they suppress you. Hopefully if they make another addition to the game but that is just wishful thinking, Overall this game is amazing and brought back my love for High action FPS games with FEAR gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great game, would definitely recommend to any FPS fans looking for something new. However it is very niche, check out the demo. The way I like to describe it is the enemies are playing a tactical shooter, but the player is playing Doom.I think a lot of the appeal of this game comes from the atmosphere. The game acknowledges you as a super soldier multiple times. There's a lot of radio chatter from the soldiers, who are all faceless and have various operator designs. The game itself is very high paced, the combat has you either constantly on the move, or closing the distance in between bursts of cloak. By design the weapons are all hip fire and inaccurate at long distances. I would have liked just a bit more precision since without cloak enemies will pick you apart before you can close in. Enemies usually drop armor on death, so you're encouraged to fight in CQC so you can constantly replenish your armor as you take them down.A few things I would have liked to see is more weapon variety and levels. The SMG and rifle both feel samey due to the design making both imprecise. I completed the campaign in about 8 hours, and while there are still side missions and horde mode, I was craving more. I also think darkness could have been more impactful on enemies. Even when shooting out the lights, it only takes enemies an extra couple seconds to see you, and unfortunately they're usually paired with night vision enemies later on which means everyone will be aware of you anyway.  These are pretty minor nitpicks though, and the game overall is still solidly a 9/10 for me. Can't wait to see some follow up on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's idea is good, but the execution is not so good. It's fun, but it is not nearly as refined as FEAR was. This game lacks the atmosphere of FEAR entirely, which was one of the reasons why firefights were so good. You'd have those quiet, but tense moments that would suddenly erupt into intense firefights. Also, the firefights felt intense without there being all that many enemies in the field. This game has sort of nailed FEAR's gunplay and effects, but it feels like it's overdoing everything a lot. It has effects similar to FEAR, but unlike FEAR, which did also have the sparks, debris, smoke and dust filling the air in combat, this game simply overdoes all those effects while completely missing the point of many of those effects in FEAR. In FEAR, the effects were not so intense that they would completely blind and disorient you. In this game, there are so many sparks and stuff flying in the air that you literally cannot even see the game from all the effects and dust and smoke effects are not utilized in anyway really whereas in FEAR, they'd play a part in obstructing your vision during combat. You'd have smoke lingering around when you hit things and it would even remain after the firefight was over and the dust would settle on the floor as the player winded down from the adrenaline-packed action. This game also cheapens the a combat a lot by simply having too many enemies. In FEAR, every enemy encounter felt impactful and meaningful on top of being fun, but in this game the combat is just "okay fun" and that's that. Graphically this game looks like it could have come out back when FEAR 2 was released. Even the ragdolls are like in very old games. Over all this game is fun and I can recommend it, but it does feel like a bootleg FEAR that was made 10 years ago and misses the point of why FEAR's firefights were impressive besides the gunplay. It's still fun though.

_childDocuments_.review: I think, in part or in whole, I very much agree with the comparisons to F.E.A.R., but I'd argue this especially applies to the Expansion-packs of F.E.A.R. much more than people realize. I think, in particular, the Perseus Mandate (EXP-2) expansion to F.E.A.R., more or less for the survival/horde-mode and the concept of a boss that has phases (and isn't a "look at me absorbing all your bullets like a bullet-sponge!" boss-mechanic). I liked Perseus Mandate, and I liked it way more after near-100%'ing Trepang2 (I'm too scared and still too tired to play all the levels on the super-duper hard difficulty: lol). To bring this back to Trepang2, I gotta say I really do believe this game to be a spiritual-successor (and!... it has a story: I mean c'mon it's not like you're reading the Ancient Tomes of Alexandria to understand what's being told explicitly and implicitly in the intel and the environment and character-lines).Whether on sale or at its current price, it's worth the buy, yet if it is on sale, then it is a must-buy no matter what! I'd was able to play it on my five-year old PC, but I do recommend upgrading it (if you haven't this past half-decade) if you want to see the graphical-fidelity alongside the massacre of the mall-cops. The story is light enough (you get fed bits and pieces through the environment and in-game dialogue) and flows rather well with the entire gameplay; I happily can say that you are not even forced to read the intel to understand "WHY ARE WE HERE... JUST TO SUFFER?!" (totally not a MGS:V reference) as it is entirely up to you if you care about "learning more" (which anyways will enhance your utter massacre of everything and everyone that dares lay a finger on you). If you ever played F.E.A.R. (or thought of playing it), then I'd definitely suggest playing this as you will feel a great many similarities (but don't let these similarities blind you from the uniqueness of Trepang2's take on F.E.A.R.'s gameplay-mechanics). All in all, it's definitely worth your time and attention at the very least.

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 is a great example of a game that can make you feel like a total badass. but to better clarify I'll go through the aspects of the game individually.Gameplay: the game takes heavy inspiration of F.E.A.R with it's Gun-kata playstyle, using a mix of Focus and Cloak is key to winning fights, the shooting is done perfectly, however melee is a bit of a toss, you have to be looking directly at the enemy to actually hit them with melee, if this was changed for a 180 degree cone in front of the player I think melee would be far more enjoyable, there is a sword  coming to the new DLC so this is subject to change.Music: Aside from the game play this amazing soundtrack is one of the Best, huge respect to Brandon McKagan. its mix of techno, heavy metal guitar riffs and bass elevate the gameplay so much. plus, when horror is needed the music fits those tones as well. amazing work.Story: the story is interesting however major gripes I have are the inclusion of the "Backrooms" in the main plot, it would be fine if this was more of Easter Egg, but the fact there are in game written documents calling it the backrooms killed the vibes for me, it went from areas with good horror build up to complete disappointment all because they forced the Backrooms into the plot. other elements however do not even get touched on more like the Parasitic bio-mass in Pandora institute, the UFO on Oil Rig and so on. its a case where so much info is hidden behind intel, and then there is rarely explanation for the interesting plot points. again, this could be improved with future DLC, so I can't make final judgment on this yet.Difficulty and the AI: The difficulty of the game does not lie to you. I have so far completed the games story on Extreme and am now working on Rage Mode, The AI improvements are brutal the higher it goes, detection becomes faster, they are more accurate and they punish your mistakes. I recommend playing the game on Hard or Very hard for a first playthrough to get you in a habit of using your cloak and Focus wisely, then move to Extreme when you're ready. Rage Mode is not a joke, enemies will kill you without hesitation and with precision. excellent challenge and the AI is smart enough to try to counter you.Overall: The game offers gamepley first mentality, the story is serviceable but you'll be replaying purely for the combat of the game, and that's perfectly fine, not every game needs to be about a deep narrative, sometimes, you just need a game about killing things with style. easy 8/10 Needs better melee, and backrooms story bit knocked out points sadly.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very confused. My major gripes with this are the stealth mechanics, some writing, and the game's identity. For one, don't listen to people saying this is like fear. This is only fear in mechanics alone, and stealth may as well not exist. You can take out those lights, and hide in the shadows, but 99% of the time you'll be detected somehow and die trying to be sneaky. Cloaking is ridiculously short too, and frustrating, since your meter is instantly depleted at any point you deactivate it. Both cool features just seem wasted. Gamplay aside, the writing is pretty bad. The f*ck word does not make your characters sound cool or threatening when its used 5000 times in a 30 second dialogue exchange between two characters. Almost every character sounds like how I would've thought soldiers talked when I was playing with legos as a kid. Last thing is the game's identity. It's inconsistent. It felt as if the devs liked a bunch of different "things" and mushed them together. Going from something like dead space, to blood, felt like whiplash. The most blatant example of this was the use of "the backrooms" for a horror segment. It really cheapened the experience, and makes it feel like a tech-demo.Besides those issues I had, I'm giving it a thumbs up. The FPS gameplay was enjoyable, and other things like (stealthless) enemy interactions felt good (same can also be said for the grunts dialog interactions). For the whole game, you feel in control of any situation you're put in; you can take on anything. So if you're looking for a FPS with satisfying combat, this will probably do you well; If you're looking for a FPS with something deeper, (story, characters, situational approaches in gameplay) I would say look somewhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fun time waster for like an hour but gets super boring and repetitive after that. This game is kinda like if Fear, Max Payne, and Crysis had a baby. Also feels almost like a mobile game ad had a desktop port made for it (lots of stock props and crappy cut and paste map drops.. especially in the helicopter cut scenes where you're entering the city for missions). Super generic story that you can basically see the twist coming from the first mission (Extremely nonsensical/unexplained plot armor is also included if you're into that). One of my biggest problems with this game is how you can't find NVG's in the game (or at least I couldn't) and the game is ludicrously dark in TONS of places (you have a flashlight but its basically as useful as a phone flashlight). Oh and ADS for non-scoped weapons is a "cheat" option in this game and having it enabled treats all missions (regardless of difficulty completed) as only being completed on easy. There is a redeeming grace however, and it comes in the form of dual wielding two incendiary shell shotguns so even if you have trouble aiming (as long as you don't use the choke attachment) you can just mow down entire groups with a couple blasts and also destroy over 80% of your FPS in the process.Maybe worth 10 bucks... super derivative and ultimately lackluster.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is equal parts F.E.A.R and Crysis. It outright rips mechanics from both, flaws and and all.You have a cloak like Crysis, And my main two complaints from that game were that it didn't last long enough and depleted completely when you turned it off instead of conserving the energy. So of course they implemented that. It also lasts like 5 seconds so it's mainly used to break line of sight rather then stalk around. You can manipulate time like F.E.A.R. I find myself using this just so I can get accurate head shots in the fray and chaos that is every engagement. Enemies speeding around in almost pitch black atmospheres while explosions and derbies fly around everywhere make anything other then a purposeful head shot worth your time. All while I'm simultaneously trying to power slide out of danger and micro manage my cloak and time powers. The side missions are just arenas. From a downed plane to a haunted underground radio shack "I think" all the side missions are small and uninteresting with obvious boundaries and high value targets that don't feel any harder then basic enemies. If they didn't highlight them I'd never know the difference.     The whole base aspect of the game feels weird and tacked on. The base is empty say for me, the quartermaster, my pilot some disembodied voices on the radio and a group of cos players who show up in mission to die when S#!t gets real. I can customize my cloths, Why? I haven't beaten the game yet, so the camera may yet pull back to reveal I've been wearing a white T-shirt and jeans the whole time. But until this point I barley look at my feet and there's no mirror in my empty base. This game is fairly disappointing. It has allot of cool ideas that it fails to execute in an enjoyable way.

_childDocuments_.review: Reading all the negative reviews about this game not being as good as fear or not living up to what fear did or just not being a great "spiritual successor" has really pissed me off and I just want to be here to set the record straight. This game was not meant to be a spiritual successor. Nor was it ever aiming to be a fear "sequel" or copy. You can ask the developers themselves. Yes it took inspiration from fear with the slow motion, smart ai, super natural themes, etc. But it is its own thing entirely. If you're coming into this game expecting a fear follow up, please either go somewhere else or just realize this isn't what you're looking for. Is the story a masterpiece? No its not. But it has some really interesting lore and some pretty cool rabbit holes that are fun to dive into and talk/theorize about. The level design can get a little annoying sometimes. It feels like there can be times where its just constant repeat of the same objectives or goals. But thats where the gameplay comes in to save it from that tedium. By now I'm sure you've seen all the praise regarding the gameplay. Because its f**king amazing. And in order to keep it fresh you have to experiment with the different mechanics, or try out new weapon attachments, or limit yourself to only using certain guns or equipment, or trying to do melee only. Theres just so much you can do with the gameplay. And you can tell by my playtime I thoroughly enjoy this game. It became my most played on steam within 2 weeks of its release.I absolutely love this game.And even if it seems like theres minimal content, theres so many ways to further extend its enjoyment. If you collect all the intel for example you have tons of backstory and logs to go through to learn more about the games story and the characters. Theres also a lot of collectibles and things to unlock. Doing all the combat sims on very hard will get you most of the cosmetics (2 need to be on extreme). And while I get not everyone wants to 100% the game. I think its absolutely worth it. And it never really makes sense to me when people complain about there not being enough content when they chose not to even see all of what is being offered. Theres new areas in the combat sims, and even some old versions of areas that are used in the main game. Which is always fun to see because you can see how far they came with the environment building. And how drastically things changed sometimes. Theres even enemies that are exclusively found in those combat sims. Some being old demo npcs or just flat out unused. I think $30 is an absolute fair price for what the game has. Yes it doesn't seem like a lot at first glance. But theres just countless ways to enjoy the game and really extend its enjoyment so it feels you get your moneys worth. The developers are still planning on adding more in the future too. So its not like this is it forever. But what they delivered is outstanding. The team consists of 4 people. And the amount of detail some parts of this game go into is crazy for such a small team. This game is such a crazy achievement for a team thats last project was just a 2d scroller about shooting organs at enemies as a sea cucumber. Please just give it a try. Its not going to be for everyone. But coming into it with the wrong expectations won't do anything but sour your experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Very much enjoying this game - the demo was superb so I decided to buy the full thing and so far its really good.Probably spoilers but to be honest I could do without the monsters / experiments gone wrong stuff as they just tend to run at you and smack you down, whereas fighting the human enemies is really good fun as the AI seems pretty good and they scream and yell stuff thats very amusing as you blow them into pieces. I think I'd rather have a more down-to-earth plot with increasingly tricky human enemies armed with more dangerous stuff than the monsters.But when you get into a slow-mo fight and headshot a load of the soldiers while diving sideways through a window it really is just beyond anything I've experienced in a game so far, its just so much fun.The weapons are superb and have that same feeling of power and noise that you got during the heist in "Heat", letting rip and using up a huge amount of ammo amid massive amounts of stuff breaking and enemies getting blown-away is extremely satisfying, much more so than any other game I've ever player. Every other FPS game should take a good look at this one to see just how you make guns feel powerful and dangerous. Often I'll use the pistol in preference to the more powerful guns as picking out precise shots with the SFX and VFX is so good.I even enjoyed the round-based combat simulations, which is a great way to just let rip against a whole load of the soldiers without worrying about plots or progression, just a huge amount of ammo and some unbelievably great gameplay moments.No other game has had quite so many "Holy ****** ***" moments for me in the past few years as this one, you feel like a combination of Neo and Max Payne taking part in the best 80s action movie you can imagine.One thing I'd love to see though if you make Trepang Cubed is for the enemies to have more limb-specific damage, so I could disarm one with a single shot to the hand or remove a foot with the shotgun so they fall over, stuff like that that gives more slow-mo options beyond a lot of headshots.

_childDocuments_.review: Having sunk more hours into the game then my original review I felt it proper to revise it to more accurately reflect my experience at this point .So what has been my experience up until now? Great! The combat once you get used to the mechanics and their flow is very satisfying, and you can pull off all sorts of crazy stuff . For example, want to grab an enemy, pull the pin on 1 of his grenades, toss him at a group of his mates nearby and shoot him while he's still flying through the air so he blows before they can scramble to cover? You can do that. Want to slide into a group of enemies sending them ragdolling all over the place, grab 1 mid slide, toss him 20ft into the air, slo-mo and take out 5 others with headshots, then stand and catch the guy you tossed when he comes back down and snap his neck? You can do that. That goodness aside the decal life span of stuff like bullet holes, bodies and shell casings is insanely long and makes a mockery of the short time spans that games with twice this ones budget have. For example I was doing a wave clearing side mission and I found a nice cheese spot, 40 minutes later the floor was littered with shotgun shells, blood splatter, bodies/body parts, bloody boot prints from stepping on the splatter and weapons of the fallen. All that stuff just was there for over an hour with no signs of going anywhere (this particular mission lets you hang around and keep doing waves if you want long after you complete your objective and can leave). I should add that despite all this build up of things the game still ran silky smooth and I don't think it was my custom rig making all that happen I think game is just that well put together as it should be.However weapon selections are limited, though you can find attachments or grab more decked out versions from enemies you kill. While this can be a downer for some FPS lovers, I do think given your enemies are primarily security forces that it wouldn't make sense for them to have a rogues gallery line up of weapons but rather all be fitted with  select few for their various roles.Last but not least a thing I think more FPS games need to do and which this one does so well it keeps surprising me with just how much effort got put into it. Enemy NPC dialog and reactions to what is currently happening around them. You can scare them, they'll panic, start firing wildly in the areas they think you are in, they'll yell at each other for doing so and wasting ammo, they'll give each other ♥♥♥♥ if one gets knocked over by a blast, they'll get upset if they witness you brutally kill one of their own maybe they were good pals with, they'll express dismay when they realize their the last living member in their squad and its just them alone with you a super soldier who can cloak and move so fast time slows. All this means combat is chaotic, visceral and intense as it should be, when you're tearing apart an enemy squad it shouldn't just be a gun fire and silence (a sad norm for most AAA FPS games these days), it should be a chaotic symphony of deafening gunfire, explosions, call outs, screams of pain, yells of frustration, panicked mumblings, desperate pleas, you know the sound of an actual battle. The shear amount of line variety (they also have some voice variations too for various enemy types) caught me off guard, just when I think I've hear everything the enemies could say they drop a new one on me and I'm more then pleased that its still got more surprises to throw at me.Lastly the game does something that once wasn't uncommon but these days is rather rare. It rewards you for completing missions on higher difficulties, it has all sorts of cheats, some that offer you advantages while others that make the game even harder (eg: one that makes it so that only headshots kill enemies). The game is smart enough to make it so that you can't use exploits offered by some cheats to unlock others, so if you want to unlock any you gotta do honest hard work to get them which I think is fair.So with all that being said I personally have to say this game is hidden gem and I am glad I stumbled upon it. It does so much right that AAA FPS games manage to fail to do despite having so much more money poured into them that my expectations of AAA FPS games have only been raised further as if this indie game can achieve such things at a fraction of the budget they've got no decent excuse not to step up as well.I recommend this game if you're looking for an escape from the stale FPS norms of today and don't expect the game to offer you a profoundly deep plot though to be fair while cliche the game's plot writing is once again better then some stuff pushed out veteran writers with bigger budgets so in that sense I guess this game's writing is good for what you pay for.
