_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal. There are a few reasons one would by this game. A few being the atmosphere and level design, and the music. But I know most are here for the gunplay and violence. But here is why EVERYTHING about this game begs you to buy it, and sink your free time into it.Starting off, the atmosphere of the game shifts and twists with each level, and offers so many different tastes of genre pies that you feel like you are at a banquet. Without spoiling the games story or too many of the levels. The vibes I got from this game crossed from the chilling Resident Evil esq dark corporate secrets. Into the seamless hyper-power fantasy of Crysis and Crysis 2. To the insane and reckless cultist vibes of games like Dusk. Yet what surprised me the most of all the atmospheric changes was just how well they captured the horror aesthetic. There were scenes that pulled me back to my time on the Ishimura, hallways splayed with viscera and gore, and lightless misty tunnels beckoning whispers into your mind as you crawl through them. This game bleeds F.E.A.R. from every vein. Hell they even make references to the surrealism of liminal spaces!? There  something for everyone!It was nothing short of seriously entrancing the way each mission brings you into an entirely new environment, a full cut above from the last. And it just. Keeps. DOING IT. The game makes you feel like a god, a slayer, a punished martyr, and the weakest individual in the planet all in one campaign. It is epic, thrilling, chilling, exciting, and best of all. The sound design is also absolutely stellar. From the first time I shot just the basic pistol you start out with, I knew I was in love. It is hard to find a game that makes a pistol sound so heavy, so powerful, accurate and deadly. But not so much as to feel like your first weapon will be the only one you use. This is by design! Your starting weapons  feel weak, so that when you get a new toy to play with, you feel like you are gaining strength, the player is meant to be empowered. Trepang2 does that, yet all the while making the pistol one of the most satisfying weapons in the game. (Don't even get me started on the Spas. We will be here all day.)The music is just as immaculately tailored to the games levels, quiet and stinging in all the right places when the combat is low, or the horrific darkened atmospheres really seep in. But rippling at the seams, bursting with energy when you are in non-stop wave based action, or fighting off the games various bosses.  Brandon Mckagen absolutely knocked it out of the park with this. I don't buy stuff on bandcamp often, yet this is something I say with my whole chest; You may not think this is an important note, for a game where you basically shoot the hell out of anything and everything that moves (including your allies if you really want to lol) but the voice acting is very good! No- not the voice acting of the bricked up military dudes who accompany you on your mirthless slaughter, I mean the screams.Enemies scream at EVERYTHING. When you shoot, when you alert them, when you ragdoll them, if they get shot, if they shoot, if they see a frag, if they throw a frag, if they eat a frag, when you take a hostage, when they reload, when you reload, when they are having a chill coffee in the break room. Every single NPC in the game screams, with the exception of literally one. This game is made of screams. Over half of the gameplay, cutscenes, and dialogue are just screams. Like twenty something VA's are accredited to this game, and I swear every single one was hired to just bark commands, and hurl their voices out the window with death shrieks. Hell is full, and screams are fuel in this damn game.Last and definitely not least, the gunplay. I really don't want to spoil anyone for what weapons lurk in the later chapters of the game, or the upgrades for said guns. So I will talk about them vaguely. This game makes every weapon sound like they are supposed to. The shotguns blast enemies asunder, and sound like cracks of thunder. The pistols can be silent and precise, or spammed full auto in both hands, you become a storm of hot lead. The machine guns and rapid fire bullet spitting machines make you feel like every bullet matters. You HEAR the impacts, you FEEL the impression a shot leaves in your target. Its so incredible. Oh and the grenades, you ever stuck a rat to a frag and listened to a bakers dozen of armed to the teeth black ops members ♥♥♥♥ their pants before they audibly explode in a wet and churning blast? Yeah, this game lets you do that and I love it more than I should.This game is made of screams, and it will make you scream in more ways that one.Final note: This game also got away with literally only modelling one human face. The rest are just various forms of tactical, utilitarian, and special operative military helmets lmfao. You only see one dudes face the entire game and I find that funny.

_childDocuments_.review: The game primarily focuses on intense combat and excels in delivering an exhilarating, brutal, and stylish gaming experience. It immerses players in action-packed moments that make them feel like formidable, unstoppable warriors. You are 106, a special force agent that possesses unique abilities like sliding, temporary invisibility, and time manipulation, allowing for fast-paced takedowns of enemies. Dual wielding adds to the combat excitement, while the unexpected ability to leap long distances with stamina enhances the character's versatility.The game's structure allows players to choose and tackle missions, starting with a linear main campaign and unlocking side quests in different areas. Completing these missions not only advances the narrative but also provides opportunities to hone combat skills and learn more about the game world and its lore.Though the main campaign is relatively short with just five missions, the game's high difficulty levels can make it a challenging and rewarding experience. Players may find themselves retrying missions multiple times, especially during the demanding end boss fight, which requires strategic learning to conquer. The game's combat is very fun and despite not having the most impactful story or in-depth horror theme, the gameplay is the real star here. It's always fun to slow down time and confuse the enemy.   Despite being developed by a small team with a limited budget, I believe this game has a visually appealing quality. The explosions and slow-motion elements add excitement, regardless of player skill. However, there are issues with visibility in some areas, even with a flashlight, some sections of the main missions are hard to distinguish and confusion and desperation is something you'll most likely experience.In terms of cinematics, they are infrequent and somewhat lacking in depth, but the game still offers an enjoyable experience for those not seeking a narrative-driven game.   In terms of sound, including sound design, music, and voice acting, the game performs quite well. The music adds intensity to battles, although at times, it can linger longer than necessary after clearing enemies. Voice acting is well-executed, particularly the communication between characters through comms, adding a cool dynamic to teamwork.Sound effects, such as weapon sounds and explosions, feel impactful and immersive. However, the horror elements in the game leave room for improvement. While the music and atmosphere build tension, the enemy variety and thrill fall short compared to titles like FEAR. Overall, the game's sound and atmosphere are present, but they don't effectively deliver scares or tension.  The main story feels somewhat nostalgic, with elements that for some reason remind me of other games that came two decades ago. The silent protagonist might be as well the factor behind it, but there’s something about this game that talked to me this way that I can’t really express. Early moments in the game I felt a sense of loneliness and interest that personally worked well for me. I found the game’s story pretty interesting. While I do think it’s truly not the best action first-person shooter story out there, it’s definitely an interesting and decent one.   Despite being a short game, I find that the difficulty spike can get off the chart in Very Hard towards Rage Mode. It's incredibly difficult and only checkpoints and retrying over and over again is what can save you. You also have to carefully learn the patters of enemies in a way, listen to their communication, and use your abilities wisely. All in all, I think Trepang2 is a fun and exciting spiritual successor to the FEAR franchise, with cool and enjoyable bullet time moments that are worth checking out. The AI might not be as well-renowned as in FEAR games, but it does a good job of making each moment feel realistic through its communication with each other and with you, keeping you on your toes. If you're looking for a good time, this game is worth checking out. Don't let the short campaign deter you from trying this game, and if your budget is tight, consider wishlisting it for now and purchasing it at a discount. Overall, you'll spend a substantial amount of time in this game, enough to justify the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 is an addictive and refreshing FPS with a great deal of replay-value due its fast paced, well crafted combat and high difficulty selection. Best way to describe it in terms of other common household titles would be if Fear & Doom had a kid. This game really brought me back to why I picked up FPS games in the first place: Having a well made experience that feels great to play and keeps you hooked from start to finish.From polished combat to an immersive, driving yet also foreboding story. This game has clearly had A LOT of heart and soul poured into it, truly never has a dull moment and will completely shatter your expectations going in, in the best way possible. Beat the campaign, side missions included on very hard (the 4th hardest out of 6 total difficulties). Definitely will be returning to try to beat it again on the next difficulty up and maybe even the hardest if possible.The only complaint I have is that I wish the game was a longer. While each mission is just as action packed and lengthy as the last, there are only 5 campaign missions and 6 side missions which was undeniably a little disappointing, I was definitely expecting a little longer runtime for the listed $40 price tag.In short I think Trepang2 is an outstanding game for what it is for all the reasons listed above and more, It like many other Arena style shooters before it does a fantastic job of making the player feel completely badass. If you don't mind the shorter runtime compared to other titles this genre and just want a super fast, absolute fps slaughter-fest of a game, this game is for you.

Even still, they let you replay levels, play side missions, customize your guns and uniform, and just go on a rampage in a combat sim.  The feedback on sound and feel is astounding and that is the case going up against soldiers and more supernatural enemies.Time dilation and drop-kicking enemies into the sky like FEAR are also included, as well as an active camo cloak to add more to the gameplay.  The weapon selection is very "one of each kind of gun" like FEAR is and generally all feel good to use, though IMO I think the assault rifle feels the weakest I think?  That's nitpicking, though.Soundtrack is great and fitting, story is intriguing but not the most groundbreaking (though it is very short), and overall was one of the most fun games I've recently purchased.  Solid 9/10 at least as the price is not terrible for the cost to benefit ratio for what this game gives you but still $30 seems much for about 10 missions and good horde modes.

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 is a game steeped in referential humour. The core loop is very FEAR-esque, and the aesthetic design is phenomenal. Slick, intense gameplay forces you to play on the knife's edge of your optical camo and your bullet time bars - rewarding tactical movement and effective aggression. There is no worthwhile cover mechanics to speak of, and the vibe is very STALKER-analogous. There is no impactful progression or cosmetics - it's all quite tacked on. The voice-acting is quite hammy, but it's immersive enough when you're experiencing it for the first time. For what amounts to an on-rails-arena-shooter-haunted-house-war-crime-simulator, it's competent and fun. It's a little lacking in content, but it makes up for it with difficulty options that ramp all the way up to all but removing the TTK, but not really changing AI behaviour or adding any new spawns or giving you an uppercut to match the left and right hook of lower difficulties, so to speak. It's the same stuff down to the letter, but with no margin for error. Overall, Trepang2 is a beautiful game which doesn't really live up to its narrative or gameplay loop oriented potential. Don't bother with the DLC (more of the same), and buy only on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: As I have expected, it's an amazing game and already one of my all time favorites. However there is a reason why I tend to avoid getting games on release, there are some issues in the game that will probably be addressed post launch.The gameplay is a pretty simple and polished to a shine loop, short atmospheric walks as a little break in between absolute insanity of hectic combat. Shooting feels awesome, and I'm not sure what I could compare it too, you can try the demo and see why the power behind each weapon is conveyed so well. You will rarely ever use a scope in the game, and by default there is no ADS mechanic, as it would've been a waste of time with how fast you're zooming around the maps, instead you will find yourself unloading ridiculous amount of lead at short range, and throw grenades to flush out enemies that are hiding further down corridors. Besides guns your choices are slow-mo, invisibility cloak and enemy grabs like in crysis, and some absolutely ridiculous melee moves, like dropkicks, sliding that launches enemies, or punching/ripping head off of a grabbed baddie. It's all happening in matters of seconds, to the point where doom 2016 looks sluggish. Speed is closer to something like ultrakill than anything else I can think of.You have a selection of main and side missions after the prologue, that you can freely replay after unlocking and completing them once. For progression you have weapon attachment unlocks, increased weapon/tool choices for mission start loadout, fun and overpowered dual wield, colors for your outfit, and new stages for a separate wave mode. Other than that there are also collectibles, lore texts and "high value targets", kinda minibosses that appear on certain missions, sometimes only on specific difficulties.All in all, there is good amount of stuff to do, and while campaign is short, you should be able to squeeze out good fun for a bit under 10 hours at least.There are some questionable decisions in the design unfortunately, one is the slowly becoming infamous "house mission", which involves some pretty dull long range combat (I was hoping there would be some AI override that makes them always storm the house after a period of time), and very questionable and out of place "backrooms" sequence. I know the game is over the top already, but I don't know why you'd include a fad like that, which not only has an expiry date as a meme, it is actually already kinda old at the time of release.As of now (23.06.23) the game is unfortunately prone to crashing every few hours, and has pretty intense audio problems, some sounds seem unaffected by volume sliders, often music and sound completely cuts off, and every now and then there is a physics glitch "a la gmod" with rapid thud sounds, though the last is minor issue.The music (though sometimes its volume is uneven) absolutely slaps, I loved listening to it even before the game was released, and I will continue to have it on my regular playlists for a long time, now with full album out. The sounds and especially over the top VA is great, if the issues are sorted out, then there is a lot to appreciate, even if it might be a bit overwhelming for the senses, in the heat of battle.The visuals are very nice too, for a 5-15 people team it is very impressive with some of the views that can be achieved, the visual effects and lighting are king in building the atmosphere, and good portion of the props and wall surfaces are destructible and have physics, similar situation with enemy gibs. Though I noticed that if you slow down to look around (which the collectibles encourage on replays), you will notice a lot of weird parts of map design. There are valve catwalks that make even less sense, there was a pool ladder clipping through glass, background buildings that you sometimes see in cutscene intros look horrendous, often submerged in terain, all kind of clipping issues can be found with geometry all throughout the game, and that's a sign of a small team, that I can't really blame them for. Especially since so much of it is phenomenal for this small of an indie project.Story is there, it is predictable, but pushes itself forward, and has some nice humor to it too. Dialogues and monologues of the troops are also humorous in their writing. It is not the focus of the game's design and I never really wanted it to be.I bought the thing full price, and that is rare that I don't regret such a purchase, I can't recommend it enough, especially if it gets patched, and maybe even gets some post launch content or DLC/expansions. I love it, and will not complain at all if I get to play more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: This was pretty disappointing.I don't think I'm to be blamed here though. The demo, which I actually have more time in than the entire campaign in the full release, is so deliberately trying to be F.E.A.R. that it sort of makes me wonder when something is or isn't eligible for a lawsuit. That demo, which is the first level in the game, is sadly some of the best content this game has to offer.Everything in that first level really nails what I think most people wanted out of a new F.E.A.R. game: the slowmo, the over the top violence, enemies that make call outs and die terrible deaths. You know what I'm talking about. But after that first level, a lot of little things start to pop up. Little things that when isolated, and viewed in a vacuum, aren't so bad. It's like looking at one single dime sized dent in a car and thinking it's no big deal, but then zooming out to see there's another 10,000 dime sized dents.What this game desperately needed was a story that would have allowed for seamless transitions between levels. Something that would have created a sense of momentum that pushed the player forward.But instead, this game offers a totally inconsequential story as a weak framing device to have a few short campaign levels of varying quality. The real meat of the game is the side missions and the combat simulator. Those two things could be rolled into one thing called...the combat simulator. It's separated as a way to suggest there's more "types" of content in the game than there really is.One level has acid spitting muck monsters and a moth man that chases you. One level has some Resident Evil looking thing that dies almost right away. One level has Serious Sam suicide guys that run up to you and explode. The game has a sort of...goofiness to it that kind of killed the vibe for me. I kept thinking, "really? You're doing this?..."One level is completely barren and in lieu of combat encounters, you have to avoid the black smoke monster from Lost or else a scary face pops up on the screen! Spooky! Oh man, the backrooms? I remember that from memes! Who needs combat driven levels when instead you can have walking driven levels? That's what I want from a first person shooter.I can excuse a bad level or two, but not when a level or two is a large chunk of the game's campaign.Wait, did an enemy just call out that he's reloading his clip?...uh, these guys are soldiers, right? Hey! I just saw an enemy throw a grenade into the wall right in front of him, and then him and his buddies didn't move, and they all died in the explosion...I guess that answers the inevitable questions about the AI.The base is totally empty except one NPC that does nothing. The audio mixing is all over the place. The flashlight in this game is useless. The levels typically have really big, wide open areas which don't really play well to the strengths of the combat. When you breach a door, it literally just swings open with no damage done. But hey, at least you can change the color of your clothes, I guess.The combat feedback can be really good in some situations, though, and that's ultimately the selling point of the entire game. It's not like it's some terrible game but I can't help but feel like I've been duped. If you're wanting a bunch of wave based challenge maps to slide around in, dual wielding shotguns and slowmo kick jumping dudes, then this game is for you. If you're wanting a proper F.E.A.R. successor, then all I can say is: yeah, me too.

(probably a bug)- You never see anyone's face, EVER.I figured i would write the cons because there are simply too many obvious pros to go over, from all the aspects of the gun-play to the F.E.A.R. -esque vibes, all the way down to the BADA'SS soundtrack. 30 dollars is a more then reasonable asking price for this top notch shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: The debut title from the aptly named Trepang Studios, Trepang2 (Squared, not two!) is the spiritual successor to the missing-in-action FEAR series, mixing high-octane FPS combat with bullet-time mechanics, incredibly smart AI, and elements of psychological horror. While I haven’t played Trepang2’s inspirational series enough to compare the two, I can say that this game is a great effort from the primarily four-man development team. It may not be the most coherent package and doesn’t quite set out to execute everything it aimed to do, but if you were interested to play this game simply because it looked incredibly satisfying to control, then Trepang2 almost certainly will not disappoint you.You play as the silent protagonist superhuman named Subject 106. After escaping an experimental test site prison with help from a seemingly friendly task squad called The Syndicate, you’re recruited and sent on a globetrotting adventure to seek revenge on the Horizon Corporation who have a history of playing God in the name of military advancement. While there is a deeper mystery under the surface that’s slowly revealed as you progress the campaign, the dialogue is largely throwaway as it assumes you haven’t figured out its very predictable reveals by the second hour you play. The narrative is ultimately a backdrop to move you to the campaign’s set pieces, and this is even more evident with the game’s side missions, whose impact on the main narrative feels completely inconsequential.In terms of combat, the kit provided allows you to pull off a series of ridiculous kills, whilst also making the game’s skill ceiling surprisingly high. In terms of guns, all of your classic weapon archetypes are here, from pistols to grenade launchers to one of the most satisfying shotguns I’ve ever had the pleasure of using. Aside from the SMG, they are all consistently viable in most situations, and sound incredible to boot. All weapons can be augmented with collectable attachments, and many of these drastically change how they function. Scopes are not provided on most weapons by default, so unlocking this allows you to engage your enemies from a further distance. The shotgun can utilize incendiary ammo or attach a barrel for a tighter vertical spread. Many weapons can also be fitted with a silencer, though I found that this was unneeded since stealth wasn’t a viable option on the harder difficulties. You’ve also got a surprisingly varied series of throwables on offer; grenades and flashbangs are here, but there’s also more tactical choices like mines, or even rats strapped to a proximity bomb! Ultimately, there are very few weaponry choices that won’t feel satisfying to execute your foes with.You also have numerous abilities up your sleeve to even the odds against larger hordes of foes. Entering bullet time is exactly as satisfying as you would expect, though you have to use it carefully as it can only be recharged by hitting foes while this ability is turned off. You can also cloak which is instead a timed recharge, providing you with a bit of necessary breathing room, or alternatively take one of your foes hostage. You could then execute the guy right there, but why not pull one of their grenades and throw him back instead? During the third main mission, you will unlock the dual-wield serum which is a game-changing tactical option for all further combat encounters, though this does end up trivializing most of the game’s bosses. Finally, you have sprinting and sliding for movement options, though I found it odd that this incredibly powerful soldier was unable to sprint more than twenty metres before he runs out of breath. Despite these numerous powerful options, the game’s smart AI and well-balanced difficulty will decimate your dreams of effortless carnage, at least on the higher difficulties. I began the game on Hard, but found this to be too forgiving, so my first playthrough was largely completed on Very Hard, a difficulty balanced to perfection. The AI will not let up if you back off, yet they don’t have perfect aim when you pop your head out. Furthermore, aside from the juggernauts which require a bit too many bullets to dispatch, the enemies are quick to eliminate, but they can kill you nearly as quickly. If you die, it is entirely your fault for not taking effective positioning, using your abilities smartly, or saving your more powerful weapons for when they are most needed. If you are tired of the boring ‘higher numbers equals more challenge’ approach to modern difficulty, I would strongly recommend giving Very Hard a go.While the combat itself is consistently phenomenal, the same cannot be said for the levels within which the fighting takes place. Their layouts are quite good, with many spots to take cover and areas forcing you into different ranges of engagement. However, their visual design is largely quite bland; I distinctly remember the kills I pulled off while playing, but not so much the locations that they took place within. This can again be attributed to the campaign’s disjointed nature, alongside much of the levels taking place within SCP-like labs which do little to differentiate themselves from existing designs. As such, the game fails to carve out a distinct visual identity, and I think when looking at pictures of its level designs, people will struggle to identify they are from Trepang2.Separately, the attempts at horror made within these levels were underwhelming. There’s a couple of weak jumpscares, and a few decent attempts at creating a tense environment, but they were largely ineffective at producing any response of fear intended by the developers. I think this can be attributed to the game’s lighting; I rarely felt the need to use my flashlight throughout my time playing, as few areas were so dark that they required it to be turned on, to the point where I forgot the game provided you with one. What I haven’t forgotten, however, is the game’s incredible Doom 2016 esque soundtrack, boasting roaring guitars and heavy drums which elevate every combat encounter.The mileage you’ll get out of Trepang2 largely depends on the difficulty you select. Completing the 5  main missions and the equally stellar side missions took me about 8 hours on Very Hard difficulty. Had I played on Hard, this time would be cut in half. Because the gameplay is exceptional, I began a second playthrough on the game’s hardest difficulty, which essentially allows the AI to go nuts with reaction times and damage output. There’s also an abundance of intel collectables to flesh out the narrative, but this functions as textbook busywork since the world is not interesting enough to learn more about. Finally, there’s the combat simulator, a straightforward horde mode that rewards you with additional character customization options for completing each map. The mileage you’ll get out of Trepang2 ultimately depends on the extent you want to engage with horde mode and achievement hunting.After many years of waiting, Trepang2 does not disappoint. Almost everything about how the combat functions, and the design of critical aspects supporting it is absolutely brilliant. I just wish its levels were more visually interesting, and the campaign’s structure had greater coherency. Ultimately, Trepang2 delivers exactly what you were hoping it to, and I hope this team continues to build off of the great foundation they’ve established here for future updates. Or hey, maybe they have enough crazy ideas in store for a Trepang Cubed?  Click  for my review scores!

_childDocuments_.review: A simply sublime shooter. Trepang2 is the perfect fusion of the DOOM reboots and the original F.E.A.R. Combat is endlessly stylish, challenging, and fluid. Charge in, activate slow mo, kick a guy in the face, leapfrog off his head, blow his squad away with incendiary buckshot, land on the last survivor tomahawk-first! Slide around like you're coated in teflon, sending everyone in your path flying! Turn on your cloaking device, outflank your opponents, and shoot them in the back while they're still staring slack-jawed at the spot where you vanished! It's ridiculously fun from start to finish.The story is a mishmash of cliches and utter nonsense tossed into a bucket, sloshed around a little, and served as-is. But that's fine. You aren't here to witness a narrative for the ages. You're here to roleplay as a one-man Geneva Convention violation.Trepang2 is a good-looking game, but what's more, it's scarily well-optimized. My rig still has an HDD; 2-second loading times on high graphics settings feels like witchcraft. Zero frame drops in 8 hours of gameplay, even while the screen was nothing but splattering gore, fire, particle effects, and dynamic lighting. Your potato can run this, and it might even run it *well.*Trepang2 is one of the best shooters I have ever played. It's on the shorter side by modern standards, but there are plenty of side missions and combat arenas available if you want to stretch out your playtime a little. And you will, because the core gameplay loop is stupidly addictive. 10/10, would dual-wield incendiary shotguns again. And again. And again!

_childDocuments_.review: The long awaited sequel to Trepang1! Trepang2 is a FPS game with a focus on movement and slow motion powers. Greatly inspired by the FEAR games, most likely the first one, you follow Super Soldier 106 as he does what you would expect. Blasting his way through waves of Soldiers, Cults, and other things as he fights to defeat a corrupt company. Trepang2 excels at having some insanely fun and satisfying shooting but also manages to also lands points of frustration at times. However, it simply makes up for this because of how solid the base gameplay loop is. Gameplay of Trepang2 is essentially rooted in movement shooting. You got mantling, sliding, and sprinting, along with opportunities for enemy takedowns. The way Trepang2 makes it stand out is by injecting it with FEAR and a insane amount of shlock. Sure sliding is pretty fun, but sliding into a enemy sending them flying, picking them up mid-air, and then throwing them into a group of foes with a grenade attached is something of legends. 106 also has access to bullet-time which not only manages to make fire fights even more awesome, but also provides a breather for the player during combat. Likewise he also has a cloak for stealth opportunities, usually during combat. Now for one of the notable parts of the game, the guns. Trepang2's firearms aren't super luscious compared to something you'd see in a Boom Shoot. But it manages to make these ordinary guns simply amazing to use. Obviously you got your standard pistols, and smgs, which thanks to the sound design feels great to use. But then you get the SPAS-12 shotgun and everything is right. Simply a perfect weapon that still manages to be balanced cause it still acts like the typical modern FPS shotgun. The awe you get from hitting someone point blank with this thing in slow motion is incredible. Likewise you're also given a few novelty weapons like a minigun or a grenade launcher, which are also superb. As well as mods to adjust a handful of things on your weapon of choice. Story wise, and just general level progression. Trepang2's story is kinda straight forward. Stop the evil company from doing evil things, as well as stomp out a evil cult as well. While I haven't played FEAR yet at the time of this review, I do know that game has a much more involved story when compared to 106's adventure. But it's pretty much a non-issue since I highly bet that most people getting this game are getting more for the shooting blokes in the face with shotgun pellets than worrying about the game having a involving plot. Which leads me to pointing out that Trepang2 does have a low level count, which I should point out IS NOT a bad thing. but it does lead to the game rising up and just ending a bit too quickly, but it is nice that because of that. There isn't any filler in the campaign by technicality. Plus with the game's success there's DLC missions on the way so soon this point will hopefully be a nothing agreement. Now Style Wise, Trepang2 is a really good looking game and one that runs surprisingly well. As during fire fight it's very common, no, A GUARANTEE that props and particles will go flying during combat. While it's not as in depth as FEAR's level of detail, it's a amazing sight to see how much carnage you're causing while you're still fighting. Likewise the game runs on Unreal Engine 4, and is thankfully one of the games that knows how to make good visuals with said engine. It really helps to give some pretty good realism in the game where you can fight cryptids as a super soldier sliding around with two shotguns like a maniac. Really the one thing I don't think it exactly lands is the horror, as it mainly boggles down to either just moody atmosphere or underwhelming jumpscares. Which is a shame since a lot of those moody hallways between fights are pretty great, just not elaborated at all. Overall, Trepang2 does a great job at being a tribute to FEAR without it being FEAR exactly. It's gun combat is superb and with the modern technology of Unreal 4, they're able to make it feel a lot more realish while keeping that over the top shooting. Really it's only notable issue is just how short it is, which is only because the game is so good that you'd just want to play more. While there combat simulator mode and a survival mode DLC, I think the upcoming story mode DLC level will be something to keep tabs on. In all, Trepang3 won't be happening anytime soon, 2 still has some ground to cover in enemy matter.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely incredible. The art direction is beautiful. The music is bumping. The story is interesting. _childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 is a gripping first-person shooter that seamlessly blends the nail-biting atmosphere of F.E.A.R. with the chilling allure of the SCP Universe. As a fan of both these franchises, I was thrilled to discover this game on Steam.Trepang2 has exceptional gameplay mechanics. The ability to unleash slow-motion chaos and create a blood-soaked mess is undeniably satisfying. However, it would be a grave mistake to overlook the game's intriguing storyline. While it may not be spoon-fed to you, the narrative is incredibly captivating.Despite the game's emphasis on gameplay, the storyline, while not handed to you on a platter, is engaging and rich. Trepang2 leaves breadcrumbs throughout the game, allowing players to piece together the mystery surrounding the narrative at their own pace. It rewards those who take the time to explore and uncover the hidden depths of its world.

_childDocuments_.review: I heard of this game about a year ago and forgot all about it. Then I saw it was on the specials page and immediately bought it. I played through the whole game in one day and then continued playing it the next to start unlocking the higher difficulty and challenge rewards. If you like movement shooters or FPS games in general do yourself a favor and buy this game. It combines the atmosphere and general gameplay of the FEAR franchise and mixes it with Killing Floor music and the campy story and wackiness of an SCP article. If I can only give one tip to new players it is to experiment with the movement, I've seen people play it like COD and plink from cover. This is wrong for this game (unless you're stealthing), slide everywhere and jump and dropkick to your hearts content. Never stop moving, try to move like you're playing Ultrakill without the verticality, trust me you'll thank me if you try to play extreme difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun combat!Had a ton of fun and have not played a combat oriented fps like this in a long time. However the game is lacking in some other departments, which I am really hopeful they develop further/address going forward in the studio's next games. Considering they done a really amazing job with the core gameplay, the rest of my criticisms should be easy improvements which would make their next games bangers! I really enjoyed the balance of the slow motion/invisibility abilities and how their regeneration was tied to kills; helping you stay aggressive. Also helps that armored enemies drop bits of armor on being killed :P. Sliding into enemies and taking them hostage were also fun mechanics that make you feel like a badass. I played on hard which was a great balance for a first time playthrough. A bit forgiving at the start, but from there on I had to be on my toes as the player character can die easily. However that is simply your own fault given how well the game gears you with all it's mechanics. Personally, quite enjoyed double wielding incendiary round shotties myself :P.The missions were fun as well, quite a bit of a shooting gallery early on but mixed well with some later missions that were more atmospheric/paced a bit slower. I enjoyed the side missions quite a bit as well, they were fun and generally varied encounters. The boss fights were fun too, although I think the castle mission boss was definitely the best. I only wish some of the rare enemy varieties encountered early on made more appearances later on, even if only in minor capacities to add to the challenge.The levels could use more visual details but for a studio's first game, I am willing to look past it. The focus is on the combat anyways and that it does well!Criticisms would be to do with the story. While the set up of the story with our character 106 and Horizon/Syndicate is quite good; I just would have liked a bit more consistency in developing the lore and it being reflected in enemy variety across the game's missions. For example you would fight some peculiar enemies in some missions which never return again. That's all I ask going forward, a more considered progression with lore/plot and it being reflected in the gameplay missions as you go through the game.Visually the game looks fine. Could use more detail, but it's fine as it is. The visual clarity is good and keeps you focused on the enemies themselves. Would like to see more improvements with lightning going forward, as it can be inconsistent with the dark areas. Lens flares on lights can be toned down as well. Sound design is good and I especially liked the soundtrack which fits perfectly with a fast paced fps :P.Should be noted that I did not do the combat simulator or mess with the large variety of cheats that would make a replay fun.Overall, I would recommend this game to any FPS fan.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game. It's double the fun of Doom Eternal at half the price. The game has occasional rough edges, like an HVT not showing up consistently, and some audio mixing issues. But considering this team was largely four programmers, a screenful of artists and another screenful of voice actors, this is something I'm more than willing to turn a blind eye to. The best way to describe this, is that it's a spiritual successor to the old Soldier of Fortune games, with some inspiration taken from F.E.A.R, I'd say they took the good parts of both, and the game is really fun. You have bullet time, dual wielding, a cloak and some stealth mechanics, which are fleshed out to a surprising extent, difficulty that I can only describe as fair, and fun both going lower than I usually do, and higher. This game is also technically an aim trainer. If you like point and click adventures in first person, with shooty-shooty bits, you should feel right at home.  The mobility of your character feels amazing, especially given the positive feedback loop of shoot-enemy, get focus, get armour, get stamina, you feel powerful, even though technically, subject 106 is quite vulnerable. The game is clever with its use of mechanics, and good at both knowing when to give you more power, and when to take some away. The story is surprisingly satisfying. I won't go into too much detail, but I'd say that even in the Carmack sense, this thing is fun (notice I'm using this word a whole lot) and interesting, without much cringe. There are some no-strings-attached "side missions", some sandbox style gameplay some horde mode, and some more goodies that allow you to explore the CQC system, which is both in-depth and minimal. But there is a plot. It's surprisingly well-done and I found that most of it makes quite a bit of sense when you think about it. Sadly, the devs needed to spoonfeed the solution to some players, so there wasn't much of an "aha" moment... but I liked it quite a bit, nonetheless. The combat is where the main attraction is. Here's how it works. You want to shoot your enemies, and don't get hit. While the devs could give you a cover/lean mechanic and some ADS to boot, (which I'm not gonna lie, would have fit in quite well, and added to the immersion/coll factor), but instead you have the plain old crosshair, and bullets go there. The way accuracy works, is such that you really have to get close to your enemies, (unless you have a scope, which happens rarely, and is not too useful). If you kill an enemy that gives you focus, their weapon, and some armour. Focus gives you improved accuracy, allows you to move faster, and converts the (usually hitscan) bullets into projectiles. So how do you avoid damage? You can hide, you can cover, or you could take an enemy as a human shield. That enemy probably had a grenade, and you can definitely pull the pin on that, and throw the enemy too.  You can melee, you can kick, and you can dual wield. So how about the weapons? They're all really good. The pistol is something you'd think you'd throw away mid-game, but you don't really. It's pin-point accurate especially when you're moving. It can't kill most things with body shots, so you aim for the head. Headshots give you more focus, so using a pistol actually makes more sense than a rifle at times. The SMG is a bullet hose, that is not too accurate without focus. Plenty of ammo for it, though and quite powerful in a dual wield. The rifle is a bit too much recoil when dual wielded, but it's your workhorse for tanky enemies. Beyond that you get some guns which are useful to take with you and *some* enemies occasionally drop them, but in truth, you're not going to see many DMRs, Grenade launchers and miniguns, unless you took one before a mission. Overall, I'm quite happy with the end result, and I wish Trepang studios good luck.

_childDocuments_.review: AbsoLUTELY lives up to its goal to not only emulate but outright surpass FEAR. The gunplay is smooth, the atmosphere is on point, the movement is streamlined and sliding into someone in order to grab them and either use them as a human shield or toss their sticky-grenaded ass into a group of others, knocking them down before the explosion, is some of the most fun I've had in an FPS in a while. The deliberate lack of ADS and leaning forces you headfirst into the violence, rewarded with every kill increasing your stamina beyond its normal cap and allowing you to sprint and slide more, letting you build up the momentum for some truly amazing carnage. The shotgun is probably one of the most satisfying shotguns I've ever used in a video game, an increasing rarity in the current age. The only real gripe I have with the game is how dark some environments get, making it a bit hard to actually see your enemies and forcing you to rely on the relatively underpowered flashlight. It does fit with the overall aesthetic, I suppose, but it harms the gameplay readability a bit. That being said, I overall believe that it is indeed a worthy successor to FEAR, and look forward to its continued development! Something like Workshop support for custom maps would be great!

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang is a decent shooter with good gunplay but it's sadly lacking in almost all other areas. It never escaped that tech demo feel for me. It never established it's own identify, it felt like a mesh of ideas just thrown together. It lacks the atmosphere and immersion of F.E.A.R the game it's inspired by. It doesn't have a tone or vibe of any kind. I didn't like the levels themselves, they all just had a cheap feeling to them. That thought was in the back of my head throughout the whole game. I don't get that feeling with most indie games i play and it felt very prominent here. The side missions were also all pretty much just horde mode waves in one small area which i rarely like in any game. The story is also very throwaway and generic. Even though the shooting itself feels good, I never had intense and thrilling gunfights at any point because the enemies themselves are just cannon fodder. I've never once felt to need to take cover and just pause for a second (hard difficulty). Complete opposite feeling in F.E.A.R where i was leaning around corners to get a good shot on the smart enemies that were trying to flank me while waiting for my slow mo to recharge. They also throw monsters for you to fight which was just ridiculous and dumb. I think you get the whole gist of what this game is by playing the demo, i don't think it's worth buying the game itself.5/10 (Average)

Side-missions are often boring wave defense or pressing buttons while ghosts are ramming you. I couldn't push myself to finish the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought as part of a humble bundle. It's a pretty short campaign, so not recommended at the full $30 price, but every moment was enjoyable. The action is fast and the guns are punchy. The story feels heavily inspired by SCP lore in a very good way. I do have some issues with the audio design. Maybe I had some settings messed up, but explosions and gunshots were much louder than everything else, except when another character was talking. It would deafen all the action so you could hear the voice then ramp the sounds back up when the line was finished. This was especially noticeable in the helicopter. The other negative I have is the enemy variety. There are several factions, but they mostly feel the same. There are a couple of unique enemies like the kamikaze cultist or the shield soldier, but everything else feels like the same enemy with a different gun or different amount of health. The bosses have some cool designs, but sometimes they can feel bullet spongey. In summary, the vibes of the game are immaculate, story is fantastic, and its a blast overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: It's frantic, it's clever, it's just plain fun. Better than FEAR. Better than most Call of Duty campaigns. It's basically FEAR with better guns, better AI, and more-varied supernatural plots. I wish there was more of this game, as you could finish it in a weekend. However, from such a small dev team, it's an incredible amount of content. These people clearly thought about how they could streamline production while sacrificing as little quality as possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun fast-pace shooter- Campaign is fairly short and unless you read all the logs a bit confusing IMO- Only 7 weapons (excluding the dev-pistol and physics-gun)- No Mellee-Weapons (truly a shame)- Doesnt register M1-inputs at times- I recommend turning Effects down to low, as otherwise you get a lot of flashing particles blocking your view- IMO limited enemy types (either unarmored, medium armored or heavily armored enemies with different skins apart from the two or three unique enemy types and bosses)- Very fluid, fast paced combat- guns feel very satisfying to use- runs extremely well (best graphics and I easily get stable 144FPS without stutters)- Almost no loading times (takes 2-5sec to load a new mission/anything on an SSD)- the game comes with CHEATS! In 2023! A game that lets you mess around with cheats is a rarity nowadays!- fairly decent replayability- side missions and a wave-based fighting arena- decent AI (remembers where they last saw/heard you and push in on that location)- The voiceacting is amazing. The enemies are screaming at the top of their lungs at eachother/you- the sounddesign is very decent- very decent graphics for this price? A definate recommend if youre looking for a fast-pace singleplayer shooter and a nice fresh breeze in the stale high priced gaming market.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game a lot more since the combat is fantastic and it is a wild ride most of the way. But the lack of polish really sticks out. This is a game where you dual wield anything, with invisibility and slow mo, and it does those 3 things really well. However the bosses have very poor damage feed back, instant attack wind ups and broken amounts of damage (looking at you mothman and 107). The fact that they have limited stamina in a movement shooter is a brain dead choice and frustrating to a painful point. The fact that the checkpoints are blisteringly lacking, you need to kill to get slow mo making it useless with bosses and the jank sticks with you. Whilst I liked this game 80-90% of the time the lack of forethought and effort to either play test or iron out certain features makes this something I can only recommend to certain people. Those willing to "git gud", stick through frustration and maybe look up a play though or 2 when stuck to get to a grand spectacle of blood and action, if you are one of those this game will pay you back in kind.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow - unlike anything I have played for many, many years. Some elements of Doom, in the fast movement and jumps. This is a proper traditional FPS with elements of horror. Very well executed. Enjoy the game designs too and boss battles. I can see other influences too - some Dead Space with the winged Mothmen, some Serious Sam with the way kamikaze cultists with grenades run at you. The weapons are all awesome. The two superhuman capabilities - focus and cloak - come in handy a lot. I am trying to improve the way I melee enemies using the slide and the melee button as this a very powerful action. Yep, I'm enjoying this one!

While the current AI is good enough, I've encountered plenty of times where the enemies will just shoot blankly into the corner of wall. One thing Trepang nails is the AI comms. The small talk and sitreps feel organic and fit right in.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the main campaign though there's still plenty of side content + the DLC to do but from what I've played this is easily one of the best FPS games I've played to date. Worth the 18 year wait to have a proper spiritual successor to F.E.A.R. There are a lot of difficulty options but honestly I feel the harder you go the more you're going to get out of the game, unfortunately the difficulty options don't scale the bosses at all and so they remain rather easy throughout the game with even the final boss being pretty lacklustre. The bosses aren't "bad" they're just not good, 1-2 more attacks being added to each then speed everything up? then yeah they'd be a lot better. My only real complaint (and it's a minor one) is the physics engine can freak out semi frequently, I had a pretty tense horror section ruined for me because a bucket started to freak out and slam into everything making GMOD collision sounds constantly.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty great. It looks great, sounds great and plays great. The music sounds a bit generic in my opinion, but it's still good and compliments the action well. Every level has it's own gimmick to it. This makes the game feel a little all over the place, but it does prevent the game from becoming too repetitive. The main gameplay is clearly inspired by F.E.A.R. but it's absolutely not the same and it feels very much like it's own thing. It is similar how the AI behaves (again, it's not the same) and the general feel of the guns is very similar. Unlike F.E.A.R. though this game has limited weapon customization. You can choose a few skins if you're into that kind of thing, but more important is that you can choose a few attachments that in some cases wildly change how a gun operates. For example the explosive or penetrating bolts on the bolt launcher dramatically change how this weapon functions. Then there are the more standard attachments like scopes and suppressors that can also be useful in some situations. The incendiary attachment for the shotgun is super fun even though it's not very effective. Obviously the slomo thing is also similar to the slomo in F.E.A.R. but this time the slomo doesn't recharge over time. Instead it recharges by killing enemies. Besides the slomo you also have a cloak ability (which is not lifted from F.E.A.R. in case you're wondering) that makes you near invisible for a limited amount of time. This recharges very quickly, but also runs out quickly and cancelling it drains the whole cloak meter. Firing guns or throwing grenades cancels the cloak. Other than that you have the melee attacks that you can perform that is also very similar to how it works in F.E.A.R. Also similar to F.E.A.R. is how little I actually used it. The last cool ability you have is grabbing an enemy and using them as a living shield. This was obviously not lifted from F.E.A.R. It is really fun and also very useful as they can sometimes soak up a pretty good amount of fire before finally dying at which point you'll automatically drop them.The only thing I really dislike is the game's final boss. It's all fine until you get to the last room. It can take you a while to figure out an effective strategy to beat the boss and in my case it didn't feel satisfying at all to beat him. Unfortunately that's a pitfall of many games. Great overall game. The buildup towards the end, from the start right up to the very last level, just keeps getting better and better and better only for it end with a wet fart of a boss fight and overall weak ending. There is a "secret" ending that will only trigger when you have interacted with every drone in every level. I don't know how many there are exactly, but I honestly can't be bothered to go back and look for them just for that one last extra cutscene. Might as well check it out on Youtube. It's a pretty cool little scene and great sequel bait.I would love to see more of this. The team at Trepang Studios did an amazing job. It took me approximately 10 hours to beat the game on normal difficulty. Someone with more skill can probably beat it much quicker.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of fast paced FPS's this year (I've heard them referred to as movement shooters, which feels appropriate), and Trepang2 is definitely one of them.That might sound dismissive, but I did love this game. Much ado has been made how it is a spiritual successor to FEAR from back in the day, and this is true in many ways, the most obvious of which is the ability to slow time down.  Its general aesthetics of hunting down heavily armed dudes in dimly lit environments also owes quite a lot to FEAR, as do some of the more overt horror sequences that pop up in the middle of the campaign. It tells its own story though, one of private militaries and bad science gone wrong. You play as "Subject 106" who must break out of imprisonment in the beginning before being recruited by a company known only as The Syndicate to take on Horizon, a corrupt corporation conducting weird experiments in the guise of end of life care facilities. The story is further fleshed out via the copious amounts of notes scattered around. It's interesting enough, but hardly the main draw of the game. That would be the fantastic combat. While this isn't quite as fast paced as something like DOOM or Turbo Overkill, this is an arena movement shooter through and through, and an extremely brutal one at that. Even though its primary influence is FEAR, Trepang2 also borrows the extreme and comical hyperviolence of early 2010s titles such as The Darkness 2, because blood flows liberally here. It should also be said that the dev team NAILED the shotgun in this game; its sound effect is loud and vicious, it will immediately ragdoll enemies and if you're close enough they'll instead go flying away from you while blood splatters everywhere. In my opinion shotguns are a litmus test for a given FPS's quality, and the shotgun in this game definitely delivers, especially when you unlock the ability to dual wield.Thankfully, 106 has a couple tricks up his sleeve to counter the vast amount of enemies you'll be fighting. Not only can you slow down time for precise strikes (and refill the meter by getting more kills) but you can also turn invisible for a couple seconds in addition to being able to jump, climb, and slide around the arena. I was skeptical with this ability at first, and I'll also say the game puts its worst foot forward with it. The opening level has a mandated stealth section that's not too difficult, but it's annoying that this is how you're introduced to the power. Thankfully, once you're past it, invisibility becomes an indispensable tool in combat. It lets you reposition without worry, and even sneak up on guys and grab them as a human shield (you can unpin the grenade on any enemy and send them flying forward with hilarious ragdoll physics before they explode in the middle of a group of their friends; this is never not hilarious). It also comes in handy when you go up against some non human enemies that function like standard zombies, running up to you and not really deviating from the path they're on.And this is where Trepang2 stumbles a little bit. There are sequences that become more like horror games with dim lighting, monsters you need to fight or sneak past, and no traditional combat to speak of. It's not that these sections are bad, but the core combat has such a great flow and so many fun ways to dispatch your enemies that these sections feel stale pretty quickly. It's not enough to derail the game, as the majority of what you'll be doing is the amazing fire fights, but I can't help feeling that Trepang2 would have been better off not homaging the horror parts of FEAR so blatantly.That's about my only major complaint with the game though. It looks generally great, with each level having a distinct setting and a frame rate that didn't dip on me once even with dozens of enemies on screen. The combat is excellent and chaotic in the best way possible, with  a wide enough arsenal that if you get bored of using one weapon, you can easily switch over to another. It's on the shorter side, but most of what's here is insane, extremely enjoyable action for people like me that can't get enough of fast paced, brutal shooters. The ending doesn't leave a lot open for a sequel, but if this title does well, I could easily see Trepang Studios coming back and refining their already excellent foundation to deliver a true classic of the genre.Oh, and this should go without saying if you watched the trailer, but the soundtrack goes really hard.

_childDocuments_.review: Completed 2 or 3 main missions so far and tried the side missions. This is a blast.Sound: 5/5Elevators ding with warped pitches, enemies scream and taunt you, the guns sound great and the soundtrack is metal.Controls: 4.5/5Response is fast, the game flows a bit like Doom. Keys are re-bindable. You cannot aim down sights or lean.Graphics: 4/5Decent for an indie shooter, nothing fancy but it looks good and does the job. Stylistically takes inspiration from FEAR and Black. The shotgun liquefies enemies and their organs fly through the air, the amount of blood is gratuitous, absolutely satisfying. You feel the recoil and the muzzle flash / trajectory of the bullets are very visible and well-executed. It could be better optimized, but should run on any rig without a major issue.Gameplay: 5/5Mechanics work well, a good amount of story missions - some of which you can do in any order you choose. The base you return to after each mission reminds me of the one from Splinter Cell Blacklist. Side missions unlock weapons and are a ton of fun to play. Think Killing Floor / zombies. You get a sprint, melee, a jump melee, a slide that knocks over enemies like bowling pins, slow-motion and active camouflage. You can also take hostages and throw enemies that are stunned. Alternating skills in fights will allow you to play at higher difficulties with ease and outflank enemies. You can unlock cheats by playing the story in various difficulties, all of which scale fairly well. Unlock attachments throughout the course of the game by finding the corresponding parts. There are tanks and bosses, stealth sections, escape sections and more. Lots of replayability.Note:There is an immense difficulty spike at the end of the last level, had to drop from hard to easy with cheats. Too much.Overall: 9/10

For a small dev team this outshines a LOT of recent AAA big budget titles, and I hope to see more from them.

_childDocuments_.review: A reminder to game developers: One of the parts of the original FEAR titles people disliked the most were the ghost sections. Not that they were hated, but just that they weren't unanimously liked, either. It's okay to have spooky horror in your shooter game, but I need to emphasize that it's a good idea to meter out the horror and mix it in with a healthy dose of the shooting. People played FEAR to get FEAR gunplay and FEAR firefights, not to get put into a spooky indie horror title.That being said: Site 83 is easily the worst mission in the entire game, both because of the fact that the devteam apparently thought derailing the plot and the story to have an obligatory shoehorning-in of the Backrooms was a good idea, and because they try to cram way too much forced participation in a horror segment down your throat when you're probably just wanting to get back to shooting bad guys. Having an ominous black cloud move towards me before putting a JPEG jumpscare in my face isn't scary. Sticking me in the Backrooms and having a ghostly jpeg outline of a corpse twitch towards me isn't scary, either. What it is, however, is annoying, because your game has trained me to expect firefights and shooter encounters because it's a shooter game and so all I'm doing is backing away from the ghost jpeg with both my shotguns aimed at it because I'm expecting this thing to turn into an enemy I can shoot and kill at any second or to start attacking me. When you have it do neither and just make it keep relocating to the edges of the player's vision and make all those little rapsy breathing noises, again, not scary, it's annoying. The effect of that section was ruined because all I did was back away from it until I found a beam I could duck under where it wouldn't follow me.If you've played the demo of TREPANG2, then you already have a good idea of what you'll be in for. There's not so much a story here as a playable outline for a bunch of levels to take place within, and as was quoted by a friend of mine, "the devs built a really good vertical slice and now that's just the entire game."And a word to the developers: The whole point of the Backrooms was that you were entirely alone in it and unable to escape and you'd be stuck wandering aimlessly until you died of starvation or dehydration or punched your own exit ticket somehow. The horror came from the lack of monsters and the lack of threats alongside the lack of anything else living, the whole grand idea of it was that you were isolated and doomed to die alone in a deafening silence. This was before the internet got its hands on it and decided it needed 9 billion levels and god knows how many crappily designed monsters. Bandwagoning on with internet clickbait creepypasta horror isn't a good way to add a horror section to your game.Remember, kids! Sometimes the simple and conceptual horror is better, and if you also can't make something better than FEAR's ghost sections...You probably shouldn't include spooky segments in your game at all.Also I was going to recommend this but being forced to participate in a Backrooms wannabe horror mission derailed both the mood and my drive to keep playing so much I can now no longer recommend it. I still remember when the Backrooms was a joke survival level put in during the demo just to mess with people! It should've stayed that way. Anyway, besides site 83, if you like FEAR-esque gunplay in an indie-priced package? Sure, you'll like it, just know it's not perfect and you will find some points where it's...Rough around the edges.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of fast-paced action and this game has that in spades. Combine that with horror elements, satisfying guns and weapons, and you have what has become one of my new favorite games of all time.The common vocabulary to describe this game is "," and that really is the best way to summarize Trepang2. But don't let the comparison to F.E.A.R make you think this game doesn't stand on it's own. If anything, I'd say this game surpasses the OG F.E.A.R., and that's coming from someone who loved the F.E.A.R. games (except for F.E.A.R. 3).However, Trepang2 isn't without some flaws, for starters, if we're comparing to F.E.A.R., one of that game's best features was the enemy AI and how with the map design, made them some of the best enemy AI out at the time, and can even put enemy AI in some modern games to shame. But with Trepang2, while the enemy AI is by no means dumb, I don't think they are as "smart" as F.E.A.R. enemies. But I believe this is more so due to how chaotic the combat can get. There's only so many ways a video game enemy AI can handle a player that can slow-down time and slide across the floor like they're covered in oil. But again, the AI is still competent. It's clear that the F.E.A.R. enemy design was a huge influence with the Trepang2 devs. Even their combat dialogue is similar to the dialogue you would hear in F.E.A.R.But the biggest criticism I can give this game is the difficulty. You have a few choices, Easy, Normal, Hard, Very Hard, Extreme, and Rage Mode. Easy and Normal are barely a challenge, especially once you get the hang of the combat flow and the various enemy types and how to deal with them. But on the higher difficulties such as Extreme and Rage, they are borderline impossible, requiring the player to play perfectly to finish the mission. But to be fair, the game itself does warn you about this, and none of the major unlocks really require you to play on these difficulties. There are some, but nothing that will prevent you from playing the full game.And my last criticism, is that the game is too short. Not that it's not long enough to justify the price, but just that I want more. Which is a good problem to have. But if anything, I do think the game doesn't quite fulfill the whole, "F.E.A.R. meets SCP." You fight some monsters and SCP like things, but I feel like there should have been more chances. The ones you do get are quite memorable, but it feels like it's only scratching the surface. There is planned story DLC coming soon, so perhaps it will add more encounters, but for now, I can only hope.Overall, Trepang2 is what I would consider one of the best action FPS games out there, and I'm excited to see what else these devs make in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I had an absolute blast while playing the demo. The combat felt very smooth and fluid, while also being chaotic. It got me really excited for the full game. Unfortunately, after beating the main story plus all the side missions, I can't really recommend you buy it for $30. While it is a fun game and the combat is fun There's just too much that I found wrong with it to justify buying it for $30. For instance:I spent about 30 minutes trying to my volume levels right. This game is  and it sounds off. To elaborate, I had my effects volume at 32% and my music volume at 28%. There was a part where the music was pretty bad ass. So I turned it up to 30% and the music started to drown out gunshots, explosions, and even voice lines (voice volume was at 63%). I know this sounds nit-picky but I was constantly having to adjust volume levels throughout the game.This one really bugged me. The prologue had a pretty good setup while adding mystery about who your character is and certain organizations. It established the tone that you're the bad ass in an action game and are a part of a secret organization but there's more going on yada yada. After a few missions though, the game switches to horror for like one mission, then goes back to action. Then, it just grinds to a halt in a slower paced horror themed mission. That fast paced action that you've been enjoying is just taken away (literally). The atmosphere in this mission is really cool. But I hated it because I expected the game to trickle in elements of horror throughout the entire game. Not just throw me into two horror missions, one of which slows down pacing both for game play and story.The story probably bothered me so much because of the above issue. It's as if the story wants to be mysterious and tell you the ending at the same time.  It's almost as if they try to make a bunch of things red herrings but it ends up being the answer because you can figure a lot of it out pretty easily which makes ending really lackluster. One thing they do keep mysterious is some of the side quests and one main quest. But it doesn't matter because it's never mentioned again. There's only about 3 or 4 of these missions and weirdly enough its mostly the horror themed one.There's more I could talk about, but I don't want to sound nit-picky. All in all, I can't recommend this game for $30. If you don't care about the story or the any of the stuff I mentioned and just want it for the combat, then I would still wait for a sale. Or hell, if you just want to kill people and enjoy the combat  bad, just download the free demo. It has a side mission and the combat simulator and in my opinion, already have the best weapons in the game. I ran around with the pistol and shotgun for like 90% of the game and the main game doesn't even add that many extra (what I found to be useful) attachments to the demo guns.

_childDocuments_.review: There are few games out there that support the way I like to play, running in guns blazing and tearing everything apart with ease. Sure you can technically do that in plenty of games, but not like this. There's no minmaxing character stats to create the ultimate build, there's no working your way up from a weak character to the ultimate hero. Right from the start, you're not just the biggest threat in the room. You're an unstoppable force of nature feared by both your enemies and your teammates. Your skill with your character's abilities will determine just how much fun you'll have. Play this like a standard shooter, you'll get bored. Play aggressively, tactically, and gruesomely? You'll have an incredible time.Trepang2 is an absolute power fantasy of a game. The gunplay is phenomenal, with every gunshot feeling weighty and powerful. On top of this you have the ability to cloak, and use focus (bullet time) to slow down time and allow you to outpace and outgun your enemies. If this wasn't enough you can both slide into enemies to knock them off their feet as well as take hostage of an enemy by either getting behind them or disorienting them, allowing you to use them as a human shield or a weapon themselves by tossing them at other foes. You can even set off one of their grenades, using them as a free explosive when you toss them. The combat of this game is visceral, and intense.Trepang2's skill ceiling is high. You have almost all of your abilities right from the start of the game, so playing through it is less about getting stronger and more about mastering your toolkit, understanding combat and learning how to manage your resources. This game actively encourages you to play on the offensive, allowing you to rebuild your stamina and focus by killing enemies in quick succession. Doing it fast enough will overload your stamina as well, giving you a brief period of time where you can sprint and slide indefinitely.This game is focused on replayability, and gives me a lot of vibes of some older games which were focused on a mission to mission structure. If you run through the campaign on one difficulty, then you'll be over and done with in only a couple of hours. Doing this will certainly mean you will miss unlocks and secrets the game has. Replaying missions on higher difficulties will net you unlocks that you can take back with you to previous levels, letting you replay them with a preferred set of custom equipment. This can range from a bolt launcher with grenade spikes, to dual wield shotguns with incendiary rounds, to fully automatic pistols. You can also unlock clothing customization, and cheat codes by completing certain parameters depending on the reward.The enemies in this game are fairly varied, and have some very strong AI. Just like in F.E.A.R. (Which this game pulls a lot of inspiration from), you can hear enemy chatter of all sorts to get an idea of what they're doing. If enemies know where you are, they won't just rush you down, but will instead group together and try to flank you from multiple points. The devs built a strong system for how enemies handle confrontation, including returning to cover while firing at you with a sidearm if their primary weapon needs to be reloaded, and even alerting their teammates if mines have been placed, shooting them to destroy them. Enemy behavior can change if you've killed the rest of their squad, and in certain missions this can mean the enemy trying to flee entirely from combat. Their communication expands from directions and information, to reactions to the player. While hostile, enemies generally have fearful reaction toward the player. But when bullets and grenades start flying, expect to hear plenty of screaming and panicking.The story of Trepang2 is interesting, although predictable. Subject 106 is a super soldier on the loose, freed from the Horizon corporation and on a revenge mission to destroy everything they're built on, assisted and supplied by their rescuer's known as Task Force 27. As you are sent to dismantle them, you learn that Horizon is dabbling in all means of supernatural forces to try and "better humanity". Their experiments delve in all means of horror ranging from biological weaponry a-la Resident Evil, to anomalies of SCP, to cosmic monstrosities that could come out of H.P. Lovecraft. Because of this, many levels feel different and disjointed as you run around performing clean up crew to Horizon's experiments gone wrong. While gameplay doesn't explain much, the logs you find scattered around levels further explain what's lead up to the accidents and terrors you encounter. Though as you progress further in the story, you begin to ask who the bad guys really are.The music in this game is phenomenal. It's frenetic, and helps pump the adrenaline through you as you mow down enemies. When it needs to slow down, it does. The theme of the game "Serenity" is a beautiful, but haunting song with few lyrics that do have some meaning for the character of Subject 106. Brandon McKagan did an incredible job with the soundtrack, and it's all music I'd listen to outside of playing Trepang2.I've enjoyed this game a ton, but there are a few changes or improvements I'd like to see. I'd like to see some more custom options for the combat simulator, for example. The combat simulator lets you complete horde style levels on any difficulty, but I'd enjoy it more if I could change some things such as the timer between waves, or allowing me to run an infinite horde mode. I usually end up just playing the side missions over and over, since they allow me to experience this sort of gameplay easily and in a much more intense fashion that what the combat simulator gives. I'd also like to see more done with the main hub area. People complain that there isn't much life to it in general, and I can understand that. An example of something that could be interesting is if the Database was moved from the main menu, to a computer in the hub area. You could collect up intel from the levels, and come back to the hub after to read them on a computer in the peace and quiet between missions rather than in the main menu where the music is constantly blaring. I'd also appreciate if there were more methods of tracking progression, maybe something like a checklist in the database that come up for each level I've completed. This is done already for intel, but I'd also like to see if I've missed things like weapon parts. I'd also like to see more opportunities for ammo recovery in levels. While you can bring any weapon into a mission that you want, in many cases that weapon might not appear in the mission, meaning you'll only get to use it for as much ammo as you have when you came in. If there could maybe be a one or two generic ammo boxes added to levels, that'd be real swell. As a silly idea, I think wall jumping would be a fun mechanic. Your character can kick off of enemies during combat, and sometimes this can send you pretty far. Being able to do this off of walls as well should definitely be tested.Overall, this game is incredibly fun. I'd highly recommend it to anyone who loves high octane shooters. It might not have the most incredible of stories, but it had just enough intrigue that it can be fun to read up on about and see what people have discovered. If you're ready for a game that can push you to your skill limits, then Trepang2 is for you.
