_childDocuments_.review: When I saw a cool looking modern shooter with a mix of paranormal, just like the amazing F.E.A.R. game, it was on my wishlist in a trigger-pull. It's stayed there through a delay or two. But I remember the dev stream assuring us it's nearly ready. Well, it didn't matter. I didn't buy it on release, instead I bought the soundtrack lol Things I Dislike: - WAY TOO SHORT. My 11hr playtime is my first try, looking for secrets, all missions and side missions done and even taking my time, playing some of the survival modes. All on Hard difficulty, Very Hard for campaign and even the first mission on hardest difficulty...10 hours! Give me more! - The ragdolls are too powerful. You can slide into an enemy, knock them into the ceiling or on top of a high ledge, and they can get back up and shoot you from up there. Really ♥♥♥♥♥ up the harder difficulties. - No ADS/forcing CQB. I've heard there's an unlockable 'cheat' that allows it, but I've stood in a hallway and shot at dudes at the other end with an assault rifle with the forced hipfire and it just does not work and looks silly. You also can't unlock anything with cheats on, so I feel like they took away some freedom here. - No leaning around corners/cover. - Unexpected crash after respawning sent me to my desktop with an error message. What better time to leave a review.  - There's a friendly AI limit to one squad in survival mode. I like big battles. Things I Like: + 10/10 Soundtrack. You will be bobbing your head as you kick down the next door of a secret lab. + The spirit of F.E.A.R.: Mysterious armies of mercenaries and the depths of science and supernatural make for an awesome combo. + Customisation: Plenty of difficulty levels, FOV, camera shake, blur, a few weapon attachments, change gloves/arms/legs/boot colour and of course keybinds makes for a great experience. + Enemy AI: There are limits to their intelligence, like when you're hiding behind a wall and they don't do anything to flush you for a while. But they do swap weapons when you attack them as they're reloading. They do all fan out in larger areas to avoid bunching up. And that hallmark of F.E.A.R., when you can hear the enemies chat and react to you over the radio - calling out to their men as you pick them off one by one. + 3 Extra Modes: 20 Wave survival. Endless survival. And another objective based survival mode (DLC). There are a lot of maps to play on too! And in the survival modes, you can buy squads of friendly AI to help you battle. Very fun. + Unlockables: Lots of outfit items. Each gun has a few attachments, you have to find them during levels. They also have skins to unlock. And you unlock more survival mode levels as you play. + Blood, guts and gore. + Some really awesome and memorable levels+ Solid writing. I love the ally's banter a lot. + Fast loading times. + Slo-Mo is a godsend. + Dual-Wielding unlocked after a couple missions+ Achievements and Cards+ Music and visuals all come together to create some very sombre post-modern military/supernatural vibes. I can't quite explain it well, but I love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Very strong mechanically and incredibly polished.  I would recommend this to anyone who enjoys fast paced shooters like Counter-Strike, modern Doom, or Titanfall.  Many people have also rightly compared this to F.E.A.R.The only bad thing I can say about it is the fact that every single NPC in the game uses the same walking animation that makes it look like their pants are full.  Aside from that, nothing really stood out in a bad way.  The game is too short for asset repetition to become an issue and every location feels distinct enough from one another, but it's as long as it needs to be, I think.Given the short length for completing the main story and 'side' campaign stuff (that feels the same as the 'main' story), there should definitely have been a Trepang1, and there should still be a Trepang3, but there's already a lot to do here, and what's there is replayable for a decent bit.  I'd have enjoyed an expansion on the story, and as-is it's a little short, but if the goal was to make it playable and consumable in a single sitting, I think the devs did that well (at least for people who are decent at these kinds of games).  It doesn't feel like there are really any truly 'slow' portions or any buildups that lack a payoff, the game is paced properly and strong throughout.  Everything you can do in the game feels like it received the same amount of care.The developers clearly had fun making it and the game doesn't ever take itself too seriously (or shackle itself to reality or the logic therein.  Like having a giant skyscraper on an island all on its own in the middle of nowhere), but also doesn't devolve into Reddit-tier self-deprecation / verbosity / repetition humor, or lampshading of such plotholes.  The story is as interesting / deep as it needs to be, and there's some 'logs' written about it so the people interested in lore can explore that avenue, but the game almost entirely focuses on the shooting, and handles it well.If it matters at all, much of the game's story / setting content does feel derivative; there are a lot of tropes and references that make up a majority of the game's content and even major story beats, but it's mostly hand-waved away or just not mentioned, as with most of the story.  It's mostly flavor, though.  Every story needs a setting, and I suppose if you just want to shoot dudes, this is perfectly serviceable and funny at times.My recommendation is to learn the game on "Normal" and then play the rest on "Rage Mode."  Most people could beat normal mode without dying once as long as they're paying attention.  "Rage Mode" is still absolutely doable but requires you to actually use all of your abilities and tools effectively, on top of playing smart, rather than just jumping around everywhere and grab-throwing everyone you see.  Treat it like STALKER; "Rage Mode" is the standard difficulty, everything else below it is just different scaling in the favor of the player.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game but it just fell flat. Trepang2 bills itself as a successor to FEAR while incorporating gameplay elements from Crysis but ends up being a mediocre imitation of both.The core gunplay is decent but is let down by the anemic weapons and enemies so spongy they can soak up an entire SMG mag and not die. Every automatic weapon and pistol in the game feels like it's shooting .22, and the SPAS-12 feels like it's loaded with snake-shot. Is it so much to ask for .45 to hit like .45? Or 5.56? Or a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 12-gauge? The only way to kill any generic enemy with any relative immediacy is to headshot them. Or if they are heavily armored, do a dive-kick into their chest and then mag-dump into their face while they're on the ground. The enemy AI is great, but the gameplay is so sweaty due to your own impotence, you can't appreciate it. Consumables such as grenades are unreliable and you can't carry many or multiple types like you could in FEAR. Also, your slow-mo is extremely limited and can only be re-filled by killing bad guys, partially negating one of FEAR's greatest aspects. Your cloak is even more limited, to the point where it has no utility whatsoever and I question why it is even in the game.My biggest gripe is that Trepang2 is a twitch arena shooter when it wasn't clearly marketed as one. You move into an  arena, bad guys spawn and you kill them, advance to the next arena. Occasionally there's a boss fight that is more annoying than challenging.My third biggest gripe is the unlock system. In Crysis, if you found a weapon with a particular attachment, it was yours permanently. Silencers, laser sights, optics and so on. In Trepang2, you can only get them by finding them as collectibles on the map, or by beating levels on higher difficulties, which leads my to my final complaint.Higher difficulties only makes enemies even spongier while increasing their damage. THIS IS A CARDINAL SIN OF GAME DESIGN.5/10  Just go play FEAR or Crysis

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 is a game that you understand within the first 5 minutes. You are a badass, you have superpowers, fill the bad guys with lead.That is as simple as I can possibly put it and there is clearly a narrative here and a specific direction the game will go in, but what struck me immediately was how unabashedly good the shooting felt. This is one of the best feeling games I've ever played and I've played for less than an hour. The developers are clearly fans of F.E.A.R and the game more or less apes the combat mechanics from those games but refines them with speed, finesse, and flow. Sliding, grabbing. kicking, jumping all happen at lightning speeds unless you're in bullet time, and it all feels absolutely fantastic.Only gripes and these can range from major to minor depending on who you are:Audio cuts out at random for a second at a time. I don't know what causes this but it's certainly caught me off guard multiple timesThe game has a screen tearing problem. With or without Vsync screen tearing is persistent and quite noticeable. I'm sure the dev team will fix this soon as the game just launched but keep this in mindotherwise I'm thoroughly impressed by an off hand purchase I impulsively made and I can easily recommend it to anyone who is a fan of F.E.A.R or first person shooters in general.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying I'm not big on Singleplayer games by any means. However Trepang2 is one of the VERY few exceptions to that for me. The aesthetic and environments are quite unique for each level.The story itself starts weird but as you progress you realize theres something VERY weird going on. It takes some crazy turns which I didn't really expect either. There are also "Cheats" you can unlock that add a lot of replayability especially if you like to challenge yourself. Simply put, if you like intense shooters, you will LOVE Trepang2. I cant stress enough how much fun I've had playing this game. ALSO DO YOURSELF A FAVOR AND BUY THE DLC, ITS 100% WORTH THE LOW PRICE FOR WHAT IT ADDS TO THE GAME!

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 is a first person shooter with crazy over the top stylish gameplay set against a background of battle between two factions with knowledge of the supernatural.Trepang2 has a limited story, but the general gist of it is you are a superhuman killing machine with the ability to cloak yourself and slow down time, being used by a government organisation to crush various enemies and stop supernatural entities that are used for nefarious means.The gameplay loop of this is a standard FPS but with lots of style and panache, combat feels amazing, some of the best it has EVER felt in a FPS its that good. It oozes style and sophistication, you can launch enemies in the air, blow their limbs off in slow motion before they hit their ground, shoot brains out their heads and other awesome moments. There are boss fights where you must use the environment to defeat the bosses, and side missions where you mostly just battle waves of enemies within a time limit to unlock new weapons for use in the main campaign. The side quests are by far the weak point here, but there aren't many and they don't take too long so they aren't a deal breaker. The main missions while sadly a bit short-lived (the game takes about 3-4 hours on normal) are all amazing and have some breathtaking moments. Visuals and audio are excellent with a buttery smooth frame rate making the action look even better and some cool voice acting, gore effects and just excellent production values for an indie title.Replaying the game on higher difficulties unlocks more weapons, outfits and cheats to use to make the game fun but it's probably a bit overpriced despite how fun the title is.Overall Trepang2 is F.E.A.R for the modern generation with slick amazing combat, fantastic visuals, a decent story and some jawdropping moments of horror and violence. It's amazing!

_childDocuments_.review: The best game there is at making you feel like a scary psycho super soldier, here are some of the things you can do:- You have bullet time that refills with each kill.- Superhuman speed that lets you sprint, slide into a group of soldiers and send them flying over your head (and even kill them all before they hit the ground and are desperately helpless flailing in the air using bullet time) and jump/mantle faster than your enemies.- You can dual wield shotguns and grenade launchers and almost every other weapon in the game (after a certain point in the story).- Strong enough to dropkick peoples heads off to launch yourself up into the air (to mayhaps trigger bullet time and shred through everyone else in the room before hitting the ground).- Grab enemies as hostage and throw them across the room or against their comrades with enough strength to make them knock each other down like bowling pins (you're free to pull the pin of the grenade they have on their vest before doing so).- Brief Crysis-style cloak feature that lets you relocate mid firefights and catch your enemies by surprise.- Nail people to the wall with explosive bolts as they scream in agony for a brief moment before being plastered all over the walls and ceeling by the explosion.- Mince and mangle through both the environment and your enemies bodies with a robust gore system and particle simulations that absolutely clutter the screen and light it up the room like fireworks, enemies are left filled with holes or dismembered screaming on the ground squirming and kicking clutching at their missing limbs (sometimes they just get pulverized and their organs spill out everywhere so there's that I guess) as their remaining comrades try to flank you and flush you out with grenades, it's pure chaos.- Wield a mean looking katana that dismembers enemies with ease and has a dash attack that lets you close in the gap with anyone and perform air assassinations (comes with the bladekisser DLC).Combat is extremely fast paced and brutal, weapons sound mean as hell and the visual feedback is vicious, main missions are all varied locations across the world from castles, to offshore facilities reminiscent of Metal Gear Solid 2's "Big Shell", to well lit and slick office interiors with and art style that remind me of Mirror's Edge with it's clean extremely readable aesthetic and are incredibly designed overall they never overstay their welcome and changes up pace quite a lot. There are very horror focused segments and boss fights and setpieces which were cool but never reached the heights of the combat against armed opponents.If there is EVER a new FEAR or Crysis game, they have a lot to live up to because this game plays better than all of them, personally a new standard in FPS shooters gameplay-wise, addicting as hell.

_childDocuments_.review: For a $30 story, it's a fun 6-7 hour quick run through with enjoyable gunplay.Fans of FEAR will find this to be a spiritual successor - others will find a shooter that turns horror with slow-mo tactics and freedom of weapon choice.Guns are violent, they feel like they have proper recoil, movement is moderately free and the slow-mo allows you to fine-tune your shots or appreciate the graphic fidelity put into it.Only down side is that the horror of it (while great near the end) took while to build.  Original FEAR built this early and was fantastic at playing this throughout.  If the team makes another, I think they could easily incorporate a similar model.  Still love it though - excellent job team!

_childDocuments_.review: An electrifying FPS experience awaits you in this game, marked by its thrilling action, though it does carry a somewhat forgettable story and just five main missions. Despite these drawbacks, the game successfully delivers intense and engaging gameplay. Yet, certain elements hold it back from achieving a higher rating. The side missions, confined to repetitive fighting arenas, lack the intrigue needed to fully captivate players, leaving a desire for more substantial main missions to offset the game's brevity. The attempted incorporation of "horror" elements failed to resonate with me as well. Nevertheless, given the game's affordable price and overall content quality, it stands as a compelling and easily justifiable purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I just picked this up (completely missed this release, just stumbled on it the other day) and I say it is definitely worth a purchase. I honestly think they could have gotten away with charging in the $40~$50 range given the quality of both the game play and graphics. For $29.99 I think it is a great deal for such a high quality FPS (i'm only about 1/3 of the way through but am thoroughly enjoying myself). I'm not certain if the visuals are considered to be on the absolute cutting edge, but I think it they are excellent overall and definitely one of the game's many strong points.I hate to be probably the 597th person to reference F.E.A.R. but I can't help but do so as I am a huge fan of that game (and it's sequel for that matter, albeit to a slightly less degree). I feel that this channels much of what made those first two games great. Namely, intense and satisfying gun play, beautifully complemented by a satisfying slo-mo mechanic and brutal array of melee attacks.My one and only critique would be that visibility can leave something to be desired at times. The general darkness of some of the environments, in addition to the flashy lighting and particles (which do both look fantastic don't get me wrong) can make it somewhat difficult to pin point enemies in the heat of the action.All in all though I find this to be an excellently crafted game, easily the most fun I've had with a first person shooter in quite some time!

This game was a great refresher coming from the current slop of AAA single-player shooters that have been released in the past two to three years, none of them have been an extremely memorable expirence, besides DOOM and Ultrakill. This game pleasantly surprised me with excellently implemented mechanics and great-level design. The only drawback of this game I can think of is the story, the story isn't horrible it's just basic, which is the best way I can put it. When I finished I craved more from the story because the world and the lore in this universe are somewhat interesting, and I hoped it gets expanded on further in future expansions or perhaps a sequel. Moving on from the story the soundtrack is AWESOME! An absolute melody that greatly improves the massacring experience. Trepang has a decent amount of repeatability if you like to test your luck on harder difficulties and hunt for lore points, like intel and drones, or achievement hunt. To the team at Trepang Studios, you guys have made an absolute banger of a game and I'm excited to see more from you guys. This really felt like a AAA expirence when games had some seblance of a soul. But this game is made with love.

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 is a spiritual successor to F.E.A.R. and not a sequel to Trepang1, as the title might suggest. It's hard to avoid making comparisons, so how does it measure up?For starters, the gunplay is fantastic. You've got the signature slo-mo ability, a cloaking device, and the ability to grab stunned enemies and use them as meat shields. The combat is everything you'd want it to be: visceral, gory and LOUD. Every weapon is beautifully designed and packs a hell of a punch. The blood splatter and dismemberment is immensely satisfying, turning a soldier into a fine red mist has never been more fun!Judging the arsenal as a whole however, it feels a bit lackluster. There's no equivalent to the Repeater Cannon, the beloved Penetrator has been downgraded to a weapon mod with very little ammo, and there aren't any rocket launchers or cool exotic weapons like the Type-7 Particle Weapon or Laser Carbine.The enemy AI does not quite reach the levels of their F.E.A.R. counterparts, but they do a good job at flanking, retreating and attempting to outmaneuver the player. There were a few times were brain.exe stopped working, and they acted a bit derpy, but those moments were few and far between overall.The game features a self-contained mission structure with a hub. The hub itself is okay if a bit barren, the main levels are really well-made. Each mission offers up variety in locales and enemy types, and the side missions were well realized. At first, I thought it would just be wave survival maps, but I was pleasantly surprised by the hacking defense mode which features some unique enemies and mechanics to keep it from feeling stale. And without spoiling anything, the Unidentified Structure mission taking an unexpected horror turn was a very welcome surprise.The bosses were a bit of a mixed bag. Some of them were very good and intense fights, like the Mothman, Patriarch and Horizon one. Specter 3 was a bit annoying as he just kinda runs into your face and deals massive damage, while being a bulletsponge.The final boss, Subject 107, was a huge letdown for me personally. The mechanics of this fight felt so antithetical to the rest of the game and didn't really make sense. First off, the player is handicapped for this fight, losing access to your full skillset. The boss is invulnerable, deflecting bullets with a katana in what feels like a silly anime moment, and that caused some tonal whiplash. He's also a massive bulletsponge capable of downing the weakened player in 2-3 hits, and the only real way to avoid his attacks is by abusing the slide. The devs also seem to have forgotten to put a loadout box before the final arena, so if you're ill-equipped to deal with him, your only real recourse is to redo the entire mission. Overall the fight was a disappointment and made the ending feel rather anti-climactic.But despite the final boss souring the experience, this is still a amazing game worth playing for any shooter fans. Given how long the game has been in development, I felt like it was a bit on the short side, and definitely wouldn't mind some extra content or DLC in the future. 8/10, highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I heard about this game several months after launch from a friend and after one look I was sold. It is everything you want in a shooter designed to make you the badass and it has what many shooters and games in general can lack; replayability. As of writing this review, I am nearly finished completing every level on the highest difficulty (by far the most hilarious warning from the devs for that difficulty and they mean it too) and I've enjoyed every minute of the 101 hours I put into this game. Fun factor is through the roof and more content is added for free as time goes on, not to mention the OST is fantastic. If you like the new, modern DOOM and Wolfenstein games, you will most definitely enjoy this game. The store page tells you everything you need to know and I would easily pay $60 for this game but it costs half as much. Worth at least a look if you have any inclination towards single player first-person shooters.

_childDocuments_.review: Great F.E.A.R. wannabe that's trying too hard.Thing to note, that game was made by a team of 4, so from that perspective it's almost falwless. It is amazing how modern indie shooter can look and feel despite the manpower and budget contstraints. That being said, the game is worth more than 4 dollars, so it does not exist in a vacuum. I'll go with a boring numbered list for clarity. And it's not hash criticism, just things you should expect from an indie-FPS heads-on. It's a fun little gem, but certainly not new F.E.A.R.1. Gunplay is stellar and, frankly, the sole reason for buying the game. Guns are meaty, shotgun is godlike and everything feels smooth and just right, you know. There are tons of things on screen, you can execute gun-fu combos and with slide/grab option every gunfight is very fun. 10 points for grenades, they are very well-controled and predictable in unfolding chaos.Overall, you can feel that the shooting part of the game was fine-tuned to the max. Kudos to the devs.2. That being said, AI is moronic (limitation of the engine, I guess), arenas are kinda primitive and game resorts to quite dumb arena design very quickly. There are clear spawn points on every arena that you can supress in advance, there's no true verticality because you can outrun the enemies on higher ground. Also, in original FEAR gunfigth pacing felt more natural, there where no clear 'arenas' and enemies were quite sparse, honestly. Here, you will drown in meat, Trepang2 is clearly designed around the concept of an FPS sandbox, so it's throwing a lot of enemies at player and it's up to you to find a way to deal with them. If you expect some meaty setpieces or a director's touch behind every gunfight, drop your expectations right from the start.3. Some mechanics are there for the sake of being there. Stealth? Lol, good luck with that. It works for like 5 seconds before bullets start to rain. Gun upgrades? Who will use a supressor on a shotgun HERE? This is pure underdeveloped bloat that the team never properly flashed-out into a proper elements.4. Not sure that I'm digging the art and visuals all that much. The game is clearly aiming at FEAR, but FEAR was way more restrained in it's use of a sharpening filter. It was also way more subtle with shadows, midtones and overall gamma. FEAR still looking very crisp on a modern 4K monitor and still holds up well with it's shader effects and flashy VFX in general.Trepang2 is trying too hard to emulate LithTech Jupiter EX quirks with strange graining, agressive oversharp, ridiculous amount of particles and very agressive light sources. Sometimes it works, but most of the time it's a pure mess for the eyes, especially on my OLED screen. Thing is, FEAR was way more restrained and fine-tuned visually. Good AAA game is still an AAA game even after all these years.Don't expect much from the animations either. They are ok but nothing to write home about. Enemy's run animation is almost comical. Player FPS animations are stellar though, especially gun reloardings.5. Story is there, but once again, it's a game from a team of 4. It's just there. Cutscenes are primitive and cuts to the actual gameplay are jarring.All that things aside, if you will correct your expectations despite the glaring reviews elsewhere, Trepang2 is a terrific indie-FPS with a big heart and bigger shotgun. But please keep your expectations in check, this is not new FEAR or an FPS messiah.

_childDocuments_.review: The next step in evolution for 2000's shooters. Compared to its spiritual predecessors, it solves several problems those games struggled with:- Trepang's implementation of the cloak ability, I've come to realize, is actually great. HALO felt it was supposed to help you hide. Crysis felt that you should be invisible forever. BORING! Subject 106's cloak is an essential part of his MOVEMENT kit, especially on higher difficulties. At first I hated that it fully drained your meter when you manually decloaked, but after playing a while it makes sense (don't want to trivialize encounters by feathering cloak).- This is a personal take, but FEAR's horror sections sucked. FEAR also had an extremely understated soundtrack. Not so with Trepang! The tension of firefights and scares are amplified by the engaging pacing and frenetic soundscape. Also, I love hearing the enemy commanders melt down over the comms after I slaughter an entire stadium-seating section of their elite soldiers. Very Ace Combat of you!- Of course, the game also looks fantastic. Really happy with how the game looks - 90% of the time. The courtyard/library level felt the weakest in this category. In addition, on some darker levels, guns and bullet impacts will vomit out an obscene amount of glowing vfx all over your screen. Not the best environment to be clicking on heads while on a tough difficulty, but I imagine it could be toned down in the graphics options anyhow.-Main HUB between missions to try out your unlockables that you gain for each completion! No more FOMO mid-campaign when you pick up a cool new gun, it's probably waiting for you back home! Trepang, however, does suffer from a couple issues. Some could be argued to be subjective:-Spread and recoil are very punishing on automatic weapons, the SMG in particular is basically unusable for anything further than kissing distance. A lot of upgrades will also push more accurate guns in this direction towards becoming the SMG (high recoil drawbacks, automatic mode upgrades, low damage drawbacks, for not much benefit). The SMG itself, when fully "upgraded", becomes the SSMG with even lower damage, more punishing recoil, and a cute little laser sight.-Inconsistencies between explosive weapons. The grenade launcher is a room-clearing nuclear bomb, while the proximity mine refuses to go off unless someone is tucking the damn thing into bed - and it'll only kill the surrogate father, leaving his 5 buddies standing near him untouched.-Silencers are so cool, but will gimp your damage for no benefit on Very Hard and up. :(-No mission recap? -Wish the Backrooms level was more original. Very disappointing interpretation. Lots of different directions to go in, what with the Ancient Aliens, biomass energy generators, computers programmed with rapidly mutating DNA, but we got the standard meme narrative.-No hyper-weapons, like FEAR's Super Cooked Skeletonizer Beam Gun. Don't they realize I have a primal need to render digital meat into its constituent elements via railcannon or similar implement? Especially in slow-motion.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall fantastic game. 8/10Disclaimer: I have never played any games in the F.E.A.R series, so some of my points might feel irrelevant.Good:>Gunplay feels tight.>Weapon customization >Sound design is fantastic, especially the Shotgun. >Difficulty level is manageable. I never played any of the F.E.A.R series, so I am rather fresh to these type of shooters (Cleared most missions on Very Hard difficulty).>Atmosphere is some sections of the game are done well (site 83, Pandora Institute etc.)>AI works for the game. They do make attempts to flank and toss grenades in your general location if they lose sight of you.>Cheats! After clearing some sections on certain difficulties, the game provides some cheats to change up gameplay a little. They range from beneficial ones (Infinite Cloak) to detrimental ones (No Cloak) to spice things up.>Sandbox mode, something I really enjoyed. Spawning NPCs to fight each other was more fun than I expected.Not so Good:>The story is short & weak. I recommend going in with low expectations because it is the weakest part of this game.>AI Grenade spam is insane even at Hard difficulty. I'd argue it's even worse than World at War Veteran nade spam.>At times the atmosphere of the game is ruined by cheap jumpscares.>Stealth feels almost entirely useless. Enemies react so quick so getting shot it makes trying to stealth any mission other than the first annoying and pointless. >Weapon customization is a little lackluster. Some attachments are outright useless (suppressors).Overall:The pros greatly outweigh the cons. As mentioned I never played F.E.A.R, so as a fresh player I still had a blast. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang(squared) is an amazing game.I went in not knowing much about the game, all I saw was the demo and that's it.So here's what I have to say about it:it's hella fun, the enemy designs and everything are top notch.the gunplay is amazing, this is my type of game. as an avid gmod npc battle enthusiast I can say that this game is perfect for me.the horror elements are not really scary, the atmosphere in them is very good tho. strangely the only time I felt scared was in that one house with an underground bunker mission. the story is bad, it's not well connected and I was able to predict pretty much the whole plot after I first got into the safehouse and getting my first impression of TF27, though I don't care about the story that much, you shouldn't either, it's not a story focused game. it has one if you want one but just kill things ok.the game is quite short, I completed it in 5 and half hours, if you are just starting out, I recommend putting it on hard difficulty minimum, normal was too easy for me, so I switched to hard then to very hard midway to through the campaign. the game does have replayability, the combat simulator is neat and TMOD is amazing. tmod is a sandbox cheat you unlock after you beat the final mission on very hard difficulty. as I mentioned before, I love fighting and watching npcs fight in gmod, so TMOD is perfect, it allows you to spawn many things in from the game and some extra stuff when it comes to NPCs.the game has refferences that I found very cool, first of all the Horizon Excavation and Construction Unit (HECU) is a reference to half life 1's HECU, I am a big fan of all things half life and this was a very welcome surprise, alongside that: you encounter a lone 'Blue Sky Agent' in the backrooms. this guy is a reference to the clear sky faction from STALKER, I also love all things stalker, so this was ehh-mazing. in TMOD, you have an npc category called 'creepers', in it, there are lots of npcs from stalker named slightly differently. the hazmat soldiers are such a vibe, I cannot describe how much I like all of the human enemy designs(but cultists, they suck ass. a bunch of nerds if you ask me)I am definetly going to play this game more and I can't wait for more content!

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun, chaotic, blast of a game. A game I played the demo of back last year and instantly wish listed and eagerly anticipated, was it worth the wait? well, yes. Spoilers aheadThe TLDR first: Amazing soundtrack, good movement, Guns that feel punchy, a good story, Poor AI difficulty scaling, boring bosses, overall Very goodThe Detailed: Bad out of the way first;- The harder difficulties ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ suck. The AI are extremely lethal as expected however you're extremely reliant on Focus to keep you alive as the Cloak rarely matters, the Enemies often prefire where you come from and as a result can get you killed in a heartbeat, as well as One shotting being EXTREMELY common, as well as Enemies tracking your through walls with perfect accuracy and their reactions, while inconsistent can lead to unavoidable deaths- Bosses, mainly side bosses or HVTs are very, very boring as they function almost the exact same as the regular grunts that you face with just some slight differences, HVTs don't feel like HVTs and 1 main boss is just killing waves of Grunts. Thankfully most of the main bosses are Unique enough they feel fun. - Side missions aren't very interesting and are mainly only there for HVTs- I wish the Cultists were used more, especially the Flesh Golem, which are used Twice in the entire game. Now for the Good Stuff:- The Soundtrack goes hard. it can get a bit repetitive in some missions however OVERALL they did such a good job with the rock, with some choir, religious aspects depending on the mission and just overall the intense OST fitting the game oh so well. - The Movement and Gunplay in this game is the reason why I love this game so much, now during the downtime the stamina is very limited which is my only gripe but when in combat, I love that they added the unlimited stamina for killing enemies, removing the clunky moments of having no stam and unable to slide. Gunplay too in this game is SOLID, it has poor moments like with Melee in this game being extremely inconsistent with it's tracking and sometimes the guns can feel  frustratingly powerless due to RNG but it is a meaty feeling game and every gun packs the punch you expect and mixing in with the movement, it creates an amazing, grounded feel almost like DOOM but with it's own unique feel. Definitely the highlight of the game.- The Story, it's nothing remarkable but it is a nice concept, it's not the forefront of the game and isn't the most fleshed out but this is a £25 game and for what it is, it is good and makes you feel some emotions on your way throughout the game. I enjoyed the villains, I enjoyed the characters, it's a shame you can't interact with them more but I think we all know this game isn't about RPG elements.Overall, the Game is just super solid and fun. I've beat the game, gotten both endings and done all the side missions, I'm just missing the cheats and 2 HVTs which require you to be on the highest difficulties to beat as well as the combat simulator missions. Worth the money, fun to play and well worth the wait for this game. Another Worthy Indie Classic.

_childDocuments_.review: I could write 3 chapters in this review or I could sum it up like this:If you liked Doom, and you would like a traditional level based shooter with fun mechanics and intense action that brings out your TF2 Heavy laugh, then you've read enough and should definitely buy it.It's not cover based, it's kick ass action, and I honestly expected less than I got.If I had one gripe, I think the story is possibly more complex than it needed to be. I was gripped for the first level, but from then on I'm a bit lost and don't feel much investment, yet the game clearly expects me to be totally invested. Could have benefited from staying on a one man army revenge mission.That said, it is still really good, the game play is awesome and the levels feel like it's some kind of mid 2000's gem that's been dusted off and spruced up for 2023's market in all the right ways.Honestly, for a game like this to leave me very little cons except the story is so impressive I'd nearly call it under priced

_childDocuments_.review: What a phenomenal release! I played the demos for this game for countless hours, and now that the game is out i can say with 100% certainty it was worth waiting for, but the game is not without it's flaws, for one i hope that all the maps from previous demos make an appearance in one way or another, maybe as 'legacy' maps in the 'combat simulator', though what we have now is really good, i'd just like to revisit these maps for nostalgia related reasons.Furthermore there are two other criticisms, the campaign is rather short, though you can expand on your playtime by also playing the side-missions, i finished the game in a little over 7 hours and that is a single playthrough for all the maps available on the normal difficulty.The last criticism is related to the sandbox mode, why is it locked behind replaying missions on the hard/very hard difficulty? clearly this should've been unlocked after beating the game once as a reward.Besides that this is a high recommendation, if you love 'F.E.A.R.' or 'Severed Steel' or really any game that utilized quick movement speeds, dual-wielding and slow-motion, this will be your dream game.I hope and pray for more future content for this glorious masterpiece, easily a 9 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing however a word of warning: don't expect this to play like FEAR because that's not what it is. _childDocuments_.review: This game is just weird. Unless you watch the trailer for this game, you'll have no idea that this is partially a horror game, and to me that is one of it's biggest flaws:This game feels disjointed.Half of the levels are exactly what the devs promise, a gory military fps, which is when this game is at it's best. However the other half feels like I'm just playing a worse version of Resident Evil. The horror segments of this game cause it to slow to a crawl.Not to mention a story that feels nonexistent, teeth-grindingly difficult combat, that I (someone who has beaten Titanfall 2 on Master difficulty, so I'd say I'm pretty good at FPS games) couldn't beat without multiple checkpoints and retries on  difficulty. A protagonist who's gameplay makes him feel both simultaneously over & underpowered. None of the levels actually lead to one another, save for some vague overarching plot that I didn't even understand / have pull up until the very end (for real, I forgot who the main antagonist was until the end of the game), and the hardest bosses I've ever experienced in a video game every due to how unfair they are.To give this game some credits however, it's short, which is nice, I finished it in 2 days. And when the gameplay works, it really works, but unfortunately, that's not often the case.Ultimately, Trepang2 is a game that feels like it doesn't know what it wants to be, and that doesn't know what it's story should be. But what it is is hard, and not in the fun way.

_childDocuments_.review: Drawing inspiration from classic shooters like F.E.A.R., Trepang2 drops you into the boots of an amnesiac super-soldier, armed to the teeth and ready to unleash mayhem. The game’s combat is where it truly shines—smooth, responsive, and satisfyingly violent. You can slow down time, slide into enemies, and execute brutal melee takedowns, all while the environment around you gets torn to shreds by gunfire.The game’s visuals are sharp and stylish, with dynamic lighting and detailed environments that keep you immersed in the action. The enemy AI is smart and aggressive, making every encounter feel tense and challenging. Whether you’re gunning down waves of enemies or facing off against tougher bosses, Trepang2 keeps the pressure high and the action relentless.What sets Trepang2 apart is its commitment to delivering an unfiltered, raw action experience. The game doesn’t hold back on gore or intensity, and the pacing keeps you on the edge of your seat. While the story is intriguing enough to keep you engaged, the real star here is the gameplay, which is pure, unadulterated fun.If you’re looking for a shooter that’s all about high-octane action, Trepang2 won’t disappoint. Trepang Studios has crafted a game that’s as brutal as it is exhilarating—a modern homage to the best of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mixed as of which way to point the thumbs. I get it, it might be an art/genre direction, but I'm not in on it; my eyes hurt. So gamma up it is. It could use some r_fullbright 1 sometimes.Gunplay is fun at least! Simplistic, unlike CoD. Maybe a bit too simple though. Okay don't have like 148 attachments to 39 weapons but 2 is equally limiting :D Especially as none have been unlocked in the 4 hours. Nada. Zilch. Progression anyone?Normal difficulty is a nice challenge, some additional features (Big Head etc.) would require completing levels on at least hard - nope, no patience for it. Normal enemies are spongy and numerous and accurate and blend-into-the-environment enough where ammo is just barely if at all - balanced to make use of melee. Melee is good. Peruse it. _childDocuments_.review: Alright... so lets just get the biggest complaint out of the way. This is short. I finished it in just about 3.5 hours playing on normal. Can easily see higher difficulty settings leading to a longer play time.. I also didn't go and do ALL of the side missions. I did three of them and then just did campaign.So is this worth the 30 dollar asking price? It depends. The moment to moment gameplay is stellar, seriously one of the best single player shooters I've played in awhile. When you get into the groove of using your various abilities and taking on whole hordes of dudes.. slowing down time.. going invisible to drop threat to reposition.. running in grabbing a guy and yeeting him across the room into three other dudes while you power slide into them with an explosive shotgun round watching the body parts scatter and them screaming in agony as you just keep on trucking right into the next group.. it works..Like really well.. the gunplay is excellent. The only complaint I have about the gunplay is that dual wielding didn't really work for me. I used it twice and quickly found that I just preferred the single weapon. The incendiary shotgun was my bread and butter, it was absolutely obliterating the bosses and entire squads of dudes running at me.The game runs smooth, the gunplay is smooth.. when the fights are going on all cylinders and the metal music is pumping and you're just dumping into groups of enemies.. its fantastic. Its just the short campaign.. but when I beat the primary campaign it did pop up giving me a selection of "cheats" to use and various "combat scenarios" to take part in.The only boss battle I felt was really much of a challenge was the final one. No spoilers but I was obligated to actually use my entire set of abilities to dodge and weave around him and giving myself openings to damage him, it was alot of fun and executing a perfect dodge into slow motion as you slide under his attack and take off a huge chunk of health as you 180 mid air to shoot him was great.I personally say at 30 dollars its worth it as I enjoyed it and to me if I'm enjoying something even if its short its worth getting it just to help support the team that made it. If they can give us a few expansions to this one or a sequel or something... that price tag is worth it.HOWEVER I wouldn't blame anyone for waiting for it to go on sale, you get this bad boy down into the 20 dollar or lower range and you've got a hell of a game for a good ass price.

_childDocuments_.review: TREPANG2 is a really fun and hardcore Shooter where gameplay is paramount and everything else is there just to accompany it. If You're okay with this, you'll have a great, although short, experience.In spite of everything, TREPANG² is kind of my GOTY and the most fun I've had with any shooter this year, everyone will say that it's got some serious F.E.A.R. vibes and would be right, but I'd say it's more like a F.E.A.R.-lite, TREPANG² has got the looks and the gameplay and then it kind of develops it's own thing (I mean, dual whielding fire spitting shotguns while sliding and tearing through a bunch of baddies is oh-so-awesome), also I like the sort of scary or tense moments, but it ultimately fails to really deliver, it feels like there should be a scare or creepy thing to come that never shows up, story wise it's nothing to write home about, I liked it, it's ok although a little disjointed.What really makes this game is just the awesome gunplay and responsive AI, the fantastic slo-mo, and the cool particle effects that make you feel like you're in a John Woo film. I just wish it was a little longer and that it had a better-told, more linear story with stronger horror elements; then it would've been a true F.E.A.R. sequel. For now, it's more like a hommage, but a really fun one that anyone who likes FPS games or played F.E.A.R. way back then and loved it should try.I really hope to see more content for this awesome game.

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 can feel like a different kind of FPS depending on which difficulty you pick. On Easy and Normal, it's a power fantasy where you absolutely wreck mercenaries and cultists as an escaped super-soldier. On Hard and Very Hard, it's a fast-paced and thrilling shooter where your mobility, cloaking, and slow-motion powers are put to the test against durable and intelligent enemies. On Extreme and Rage Mode, it's a brutal uphill struggle where you fight dirty against tough, relentless foes with high-damaging weapons and fast reaction times. And, above all else, it's a great game.Trepang2 is an indie FPS where you play as Subject 106, a supersoldier freed from a blacksite run by the sinister Horizon Corporation. Alongside your allies at the mysterious Task Force 27, you fight to dismantle Horizon, going from classified research centers to eldritch locations to wreak havoc on their assets. The anomalous nature of Horizon's work leads to all sorts of horror-filled encounters, like fighting your way through mutated human experiments that have been buried beneath a Horizon medical center. Though there are only 6 main story missions, each one is memorable and distinct with its own atmosphere and unique mechanics.Trepang2 takes cues from FEAR, another horror-action FPS. As Subject 106, you have a mix of standard FPS abilities and superhuman powers that give you an edge over most enemies. Dealing damage and scoring kills fills your focus meter, which lets you slow down time Max Payne-style. You have a regenerating cloak meter that allows you to sneak around enemies and flee from gunfights undetected. You can also take enemies hostage, letting you use them as human shields or improvised grenades. Enemies respond accordingly to hostage situations, not firing unless they have a clear shot or you've already fired on them with the hostage.You can only carry 2 weapons at a time, but after the 3rd level you can dual-wield almost any weapon. This extends to the DMR and the Grenade Launcher, fueling the absolute insanity that some gunfights can create. Weapons also have attachments that offer distinct advantages and disadvantages, making the relatively small arsenal feel much more complex. You can also carry up to 5 throwables at once, ranging from your typical frag grenades to "rat bombs," which are basically the snarks from Half-Life. You can melee attack enemies with any weapon, and your mid-air melee is a powerful kick that sends enemies flying.For all your advantages, your enemies don't pull any punches outside of the first 2 difficulties. Soldiers communicate with each other, attempt to flank you, flush you out of entrenched positions with grenades, and drop chemlights to keep you from hiding in the shadows. Their tactics are just good enough to keep new players scrambling, but in time, you learn how to counter them with 106's powers. Fittingly, the enemies feel like they're employing realistic tactics against an unrealistic enemy.Enemy variety is pretty good. Aside from the standard soldier enemies, you get a good number of bosses and unique targets to fight. The "Talon" black ops soldiers act as tougher opponents, relying on stealth and speed to overwhelm you. "Juggernaut" foes are your typical heavy enemies with a prominent weak point (a gas tank on their back) that they try to protect. Specialists appear in side missions to halt your progress on completing objectives. The Cultist faction also has its own unique enemies and weapons, like suicide bombers and rapid-fire grenadiers. This isn't even factoring in the supernatural threats or the HVTs, which appear as special encounters depending on which difficulty level you are playing on. Not all HVTs are that memorable, but there are some truly special ones like the time-traveling Horizon soldier in Site 83.And the soundtrack! Don't get me started on Trepang2's soundtrack. It's a gorgeous mix of metal and choir-like backing voices, creating all sorts of gripping tracks you'll hear in combat or when idle. Brandon McKagan went all-out when making the music for this game. "Horizon Hail Mary" is a chaotic rollercoaster of a song that plays during a climactic raid on a skyscraper. "Server Technician" is a cold yet funky track that escalates as you hack into more of Horizon's servers during a side mission. Even the pause music is stellar! You'll end up getting caught up in it while reading intel and tracking down your next HVT.I've had so many good things to say about Trepang2 that it would seem like an instant recommendation, but there's an elephant in the room - the story. It starts pretty strong and gives you compelling reasons to fight against Horizon and their allies. Coming across hundreds of death records of human experimentation victims, some as young as 14, filled me with a visceral disgust I hadn't felt since Ready or Not's Valley of the Dolls mission. It's satisfying to tear into the antagonists across the main missions and story missions. And then, in the final 2 story missions, the game's tone takes a complete 180. It makes the baffling move to paint Horizon as a victim and you as the aggressor. An undercooked, surreal twist ensues where Task Force 27 was evil all along, and Horizon & the Cultists were somehow underdogs fighting against the odds. The game goes hard on the guilt-tripping with 0 buildup and little foreshadowing, making the finale feel unearned and unsatisfying. It's a massive misstep that comes out of nowhere, though the Bladekisser DLC adds 2 missions that offer a lot more buildup and validity for the twist.Trepang2 is still absolutely worth playing, even at full price. The content you get out of the main/side missions, intel & weapon part collecting, combat simulator challenges, and sandbox cheats is well worth the price of admission. I would also recommend grabbing the soundtrack DLC. The atmosphere, inspired gameplay mechanics, and thrilling combat more than make up for its disappointing story. However, to maximize your enjoyment, I'd suggest completing the side missions before the main story missions - they make the plot's progression feel more natural and extend your enjoyment before the awful twist ruins the atmosphere built up so far. I would also suggest starting the game on Hard and not moving up on difficulties until you've beaten the game. "Rage Mode" isn't just a name that the developers made up for fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Man its a little sad that I have to give this a negative review but I want to be honest and give feedback for potential improvement.So first of all, the game has all the things that it needs in order to be really really great but the big takeaway is its inconsitency which makes it an overall really mixed bag.Positives:Amazing game and gunplayAmazing gore, voiceactingCool assets and locations in generalOverall idea and posibilities and potential the game hasNegatives:LeveldesingVery inconsisten leveldesing.What I mean by that is that the game often fails to pace its levels in a way that I find enjoyable to play.With the very few real campaign levels that it has most of them are a little sucky.Only the second level and the castle one is really good in my opinion.The game often suffers from long periods where nothing is happening and where the gameplay comes to a halt. And since the gameplay is really the only thing that this game is really good that, whenever that happens thats a negative thing because its boring.It tries to be scary at times but when the game forces you into sneaking and hiding from an invincible ghost type enemy that kills you instantly or resets you, thats really the opposite of fun because your not actually playing the game. It should focus even more on its core gameplay loop.The game doesnt need to be F.E.A.R because it fails at that.Generally the game tries to many things that its not succeeding at in that regard.SoundThe sound mixing and mastering is terrible. The game constantly changes its behaviour when it comes to how loud certain things are. For example when people talk everthing else gets really quiet, which makes sense. But other times the game and some effects are insanely loud (last bossfight in the game or chopper loading screen) and it feels like the game gets in a bugged state where when something has happened to the sound it just stays this way. For example that all of a sudden every person that talks is really quit, even in the safehouse and then the next line of dialog is really loud again.VisualsThe game is not really good at hinting you towards the things that it wants you to do.I very rarely get "stuck" and dont know what to do but it happened so many times while playing this game.I know it helps with "emersion" if the game doesnt tell you exactly where to go but sometimes things are happening and you just dont know what has changed or what to do next because of zero markers. (hinting towards the ghost level in siberia with the pillar)This transfers to pickups which just dont set themselves apart from the gerneral background enough.They are really easy to miss and are in weird places.I get that these attachments are meant to be rewards for exploring... maybe I dont know but I found it to be really annoying looking for those.I dont mind searching but make them more obviouse in their appeal.Other thingsI think the movement could be so much more fun if the running speed was a little bit higher and if the movement would be even faster in general.For example being able to make walljumps with kicking mid-air and maintaining that speed, or grenade boosts and maybe bunnyhopping. Not saying that it should be like Titanfall but I hope you get the idea.I think it would fit really good since you are a genetiaclly modified super soldier that can slow down time and regenerate stamina upon killing people.Another thing would be that it would be cool if ammo refills on those crates where you can change the attachemnts or on those other boxes where you can change your weapons.For an ammo refill you need to go to the box, open its menu and reselect the same weapon that you already have in hand. Same goes for grenades. (Auto refill in base)Enemy AI is weird and just walks past you in certain levelsEnemies running away from you in arenas so everthing takes too long to be funGenerally too long arena sectionsWeird enemy spawns in most arena levels. They dont give you any real position to be when they just spawn from everywhere and the level has little to zero "cover" or structure besides being an open boxOn all hacking targets the bar just progresses no matter the enemy wave. You can just leave the alive and wait things out. The waves just keep on spawning once you start the hack which is really really weird. The fix for that would be to just spawn waves after waves until the target has been hacked. And after that a small break for you to refill stuff and trigger the next sequence.Bad UI and mistakes everywhere, for example in the character customisation screen the descriptions of the items dont match their appeal. (label says white shoes but the pictures shows brown/grey ones)the game has amazing assets, gunplay, gore, movement but it just cant put all those things together and make it work to make something great. If these things get tackeled we have one of the best fps games ever for sure. I really want to like it more but currently I dont. Sorry...I understand that it is a small team but many of the things I have mentioned could have been ironed out with all the time the game has been out. I think selling a DLC before the very foundation is good to go (sound issues ...) that shouldnt be a concern.Wouldnt recommed this for 30 bucks at all, the overall "amount of game" you get and the level of polish and quality doesnt deserve such a price tag. Quite cheeky to ask this much...Maybe for like maximum of 15 bucks.I would like to say that I would gladly pay more to support a small team but with the sound issues and what not I am unsure what the team will do or deliver in the future when it comes to polishing.

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 is a love letter to John Wu and Monolith's F.E.A.R with an extra dose of adrenaline. The plot is simple. Your Subject 108, here's your gun, go shoot all the things. Nothing too ground breaking if you want to dig deep into the lore and motivations which feel more like a side dish, where the action and gameplay is the main course. From start to finish your tasks are quite literally reduce X amount of goons into crimson paste and skedaddle back to home base, usually this fights have you facing off against boss enemies and other eldritch horror's that do come out of left field, but besides that the game is just that, a fast paced shooting gallery, where you are a meat grinder on legs. Nothing more, nothing less. It's damn good fun for an almost 10hr game with horde/survival missions to keep occupied post game, as well as some fun unlockables you can still earn through challenges. Highly recommend.

There is a story, which I cannot comment on as I haven't beat the game yet. There are also collectible logs in case you like 100% your games, or if you just like learning more about the world you play in. All in all. a solid game worth your money so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I consider the original  to be one of my top ten favorite games of all time, so I was very excited upon finding . It seemed to have the same "moody/bullet time-thing" going on and the critical reception was generally good, so I couldn't wait to get started.First off, I definitely appreciate the graphical advances that have taken place since 2005.  is much better looking game, with excellent models and particle effects. However, it's a very different beast from  It's more frantic and reactive, and enemies have much more health and armor. I'm one of the very few players who preferred  to it's faster-paced successor , so this style of FPS is just not as fun to me. Potential players should take seriously the adjective "frenetic" that the developer uses in the description.I played almost to the end of the first Task Force 27 mission before deciding that I'd had enough, but it took me perhaps 2-3 play sessions to even get that far. I kept closing the game to go and do something else, as the game felt frustrating, exhausting, and messy to me. I'm sure that fans of the game will tell me I need to "git gud" or whatever, and that's fine. However, I paid $30 for the game, and there may be other players with nostalgia for Monolith's masterpiece that could benefit from knowing what they're getting into.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, not worth $30 bucks.This game is a solid 5/10 worth $20 at mostThe story was mediocre at best and there weren't enough main campaign missions. All of the optional missions are full of this same repetitive horde mode that gets old very quickly. Even the main story missions lack that aching thirst I expected from this game. They were good, but I kid you not, you get chased by a spooky dark cloud for about 3/4 of the 2nd to final mission where if you get caught sprinting or moving by it, you get jumpscared and have to reset from the first checkpoint.On the contrary, there were definitely some great aspects of this game. While I don't enjoy the horde modes, it's a good thing to do to try to squeeze as much value as you can out of this game. The guns feel amazing and were the main reason I bought the game in the first place. Out of the 5 missions 3 of them had very little flaws and a rewarding progression. _childDocuments_.review: In brief;A generally solid shooter that I certainly recommend.Critical feedback;It's inability to decide whether it's FEAR, DOOM, or at the very end, DOOM Eternal, can lead to some awkward clashing of mechanics in some fights and for one entire side mission, Bosses are all the same too. Run around and dump rounds into the bullet sponge affairs. The final one not with-standing as that's a blatant rip-off of the axe demons from DOOM Eternal. Not then helped by the fact that this game can bug out sometimes. AI stops shooting, bodies mid-air, audio drop out, mines not detonating, super speed enemies, random and very harsh frame drops from stacking effects or just looking the wrong way. It all lead to me needing to take a couple breaks when playing through this earlier than I would have some due to some moments of frustration.The narrative is mostly white-noise to prop up the violence and occasional horror moments that were frankly under-cooked. The spooky bits usual build up tension before deflating it with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ looking creature that has no threat before either going right back to the combat or in one case, a prolonged, "The Backrooms", section which feels like it's way too proud of itself. Then the next mission is you murdering people to secure a crashed plane with the same thrash metal loop you've listened to the entire game. The interesting part of this game is it's supernatural elements, but it's like the devs actively tried to suppress it, "Ya ya, spooky over. Now back to the arena shooter!". I don't care for an extended arena fight at a plane crash. Ya, it's fun, but I can get a similar experience with the 80 million boomer-shooters on Steam these days. Be ye FEAR or be ye every boomer-shooter? Give me more of the missions in blue-lit, stark contrast science facilities with monk chanting and a sense of dread. Murdering hordes of my fellow man out of bewildered fear more than a power fantasy.It's still fun. Very fun in-fact. The fact that you can blow your ears out with the sheer volume of everything, the gore effects, excellent weapons, dual wielding, screaming and future-brutalist architecture all makes it a moderately competent shooter. But that's all it is. It's a blend of gameplay and story ideas from FEAR, DOOM, Crysis, Thief, SCP and horror memes. But that's it's biggest problem. It couldn't make it's mind up on what to focus on. Couldn't pick a solid direction, made worse by it's technical flaws.In here somewhere there is a genuinely spooky shooter campaign that has a unique approach to blending the two and it's one of the greatest shooters of all time. For now, Trepang2 is simply good. Not bad for a first showing.

_childDocuments_.review: Cons:* Developer has retroactively added Epic Online Services to this game. Sad to see. I will no longer purchase products from them moving forward. * I didn't see a place to turn subtitles off, so that's a little annoying seeing that line of dialogue at the bottom whenever someone talks. * Kind of a limited story at least in terms of much detail - you're mostly learning about things via little items you pick up during missions as you read them (e-mails, etc.)* There are sections of the game with monsters / mutants and I didn't find those parts of the game all that enjoyable - if they do a sequel I'd love to see more of a focus on fighting humans, etc. Those were the battles I enjoyed the most. * Didn't really enjoy the Mothman boss fight - too limited ammo and even with cloaking you can't really hide very well; kinda reiterates my feelings that I'd prefer to see more combat against humans rather than monsters. * Combat is pretty frantic - think a combination of the original FEAR + Doom Eternal and that's what you'll have - the enemies move really friggin' fast and it's just a chaotic fight, particularly when monsters are involved. The human combat is a lot better. I think the game could benefit from a little bit of a slow-down in that respect to make it a little more enjoyable and less crazy. I enjoy the fast paced combat in Doom, but in that game, the combat area is exponentially larger and you have things like gravity launchers making it so you can fly across the map whenever you need to put a little distance between you and the enemies and you can't really do that in this game - a brief cloaking device is all you really have and when I say brief, I mean brief - like a few seconds or so and it takes a while to recharge, and then limited slow-mo as well, which is a life-saver, but when there are enemies coming from every direction it can be a little overwhelming, especially in dark areas with monsters, etc. * The final boss fight is...awful. It is so unfairly designed that unless you're an expert at the game, you're going to struggle with him even on just Normal difficulty. Think The Marauder in Doom Eternal but then give him the ability to cloak and fire at you from 2-3x further away and he takes a good 75% of your life in one hit....all the while you're in a tight environment and he can find you even if you're cloaked. L.O.L. I play FPS games all the time and am generally pretty good at them, but even I struggled. It took me 5-6 times to beat this boss, and that was with a little help by reading some suggestions on the messageboards. This battle is so bad that it took the score down about 20% for me, making it very nearly a thumbs down. Be advised. * Wasn't a huge fan of the ending. Won't add any spoilers, though. Pros:* No performance-impacting Denuvo* No "woke" stuff* The environmental feel of the guns, sound, and damage of the guns is probably what sets this game apart - the combat environment is fantastic - it's like FEAR, both re-made & re-mastered in terms of the design of the combat system - and combined with Doom / Doom Eternal in terms of the fast-paced combat. * DLSS Support - make sure you set the quality to custom so you will get some additional settings including DLSS. * Weapon modifications are very good - similar to Crysis - guns that aren't particularly enjoyable or effective become much more effective with attachments. * The gunplay in general is just awesome from the different types of weapons to the way the recoil feels, etc. * Nice seeing a good solid game like this from a smaller AA studio. I am happy to support studios like these that, as noted above, don't push anti consumer tactics like Denuvo & third party launchers or exclusivity to trash storefronts like Epic Games, EA, or Ubisoft. * Once you get the hang of the combat, you'll be fine outside of the final boss fight - you just need to understand that you don't play this like FEAR where you were kind of slow-moving, using cover, etc. You play this game like DOOM Eternal but with FEAR bullet-time / slow-mo elements with a brief cloak to help you re-position in combat - constantly move, and move fast, you can zip across the map and then cloak / slow-mo as needed to re-position. Briefly use slow-mo to take out a couple guys, then turn it off and keep running, etc. It's frantic, but fun once you understand how it's intended to be played. Game Length: 11 hoursFinal Rating: 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that I've had the most fun I've ever had in a long time just slaughtering people (in game of course). It's a very fast paced shooter where you are a super soldier mindlessly fighting every enemy that stands in your way. The gunplay and gun feel are very solid and make you feel powerful. And once you're able to dual wield weapons you just feel like you're satisfyingly unstoppable. The various levels that the game has to offer are mostly pretty good and intuitive to fight in, albeit there are some not so good levels I'll admit. The enemy AI are pretty smart, flanking you and communicating with one another. In the higher difficulties (I played on Very Hard and a few levels on Extreme), you will be forced to use everything that your character has including sliding, cloaking, and focus mode. I would highly recommend anyone to pick this up, especially if you're into fast paced shooter games.

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 may look like a tactical shooter, but there is nothing tactical about the chaotic shooting galleries the game puts you in. Trepang mixes the slow motion effect and enemy AI of F.E.A.R. with the spectacle and  super soldier powers of Crysis. Your screen will often be filled with enormous shock waves of explosions and bullet trails.There is no leaning or aiming down the sight of your gun like in most modern shooters, only hip fire or scopes. You can even dual wield most guns! Enemies will try to flank or corner you by throwing grenades and communicate their movement. Sometimes they do move a little awkwardly in groups, making them an easy target for your grenades. You can put a suppressor on your gun or sneak around a guard and whack them on the head, but once your cover is blown, you'll need to go guns blazing again.There's an OK assortment of guns and grenade launchers to choose from and a handful of attachments to spice things up. I was a little worried the missions would solely consist of office buildings and corridors, but there are quite a few different environments.If you are looking for a fun shooting gallery with a lot of spectacle, then Trepang2 is a solid buy. Not sure about the replay value, there are some unlocks for playing on higher difficulty, which adds a nice challenge. Fully recommended on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: Both ridiculous and incredibly badassTREPANG2 takes movement-based single player campaign shooters to another level in terms of enforcing just how much a force of nature the player character 106 is. With some incredibly fun core abilities like invisibility and slowed time, enemies scream for their lives as you make your way inevitably through them, and this feeling of capability doesn't change drastically with difficulty either. The voice acting is one of the best parts of the game because despite pretty basic dialogue and simple writing, characters feel alive as you prepare them for the afterlife--they definitely do not want to die. In a rather different way than other games like DOOM or ULTRAKILL, TREPANG2 motivates the player through this incredible voice acting and simple dialogue which is constantly reminding the player just how dangerous 106 is even if you're getting skill checked by your select difficulty. I would know after suffering through RAGE MODE. Although I say suffering, I actually enjoyed my time more than I would have on easier settings because of how much the said difficulty emphasizes the use of 106's abilities and selecting specific equipment. There are even special enemies and events that occur on RAGE MODE missions that often match the goofier aspects of the game. Speaking of goofy, there's a lot of humor to be found in TREPANG2 simply because of how simple it is. The plot is very generic with token bad guys doing token bad things for token good reasons, but the story never takes itself too seriously--both the player and the game are aware that the story is just a necessity for this kind of game where the player goes on missions to kill bad guys without any deeper reasons than revenge. But what's there is still really cool. It has the same vibe as watching a godzilla or John Wick movie. Cool stuff happens with just enough reason and video game/movie logic to justify it. And there's a LOT of COOL stuff. Last note about horror sections, since F.E.A.R. is probably the most comparable game: the game isn't really scary. For me, that's because 106 is just as much of a living horror as anything else the player comes across. Overall, what a fantastic game. I loved every moment of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought Trepang² whilst trying to find games similar to the FEAR games and not only did this satisfy that itch, it completely smashed my expectations.The game play is fast-paced and incredibly fun, whilst still offering a good challenge, it comes with a few curb-balls to change the pace of the game however, if you're a fan of horror, you'll enjoy it. You can cloak or slow time, you have superhuman strength and speed, the formula is basic, but it's by no means bad, it's some of the most gratifying gameplay I've experienced in any recent releases.The soundtrack is just chef's kiss. It takes clear inspiration from Doom Eternal, however posseses it's own unique identity, and absolutely gets the adrenaline pumping, even if you decide the game isn't for you, I do recommend still checking out the soundtrack.My only real criticism is that the game is short. I just wish there was more, I was having so much fun that I didn't want it to end, however make no mistake, what is there is absolutely worth your time. The game allows you to also unlock various cosmetics, cheats and weapon upgrades via multiple replays on different difficulties and in simulator modes however, so there's a ton of replayability.And the final cherry on top for me was the entirely hidden secret backrooms level, but I'll leave that for everyone else to find.If you liked the FEAR games, or even DOOM, absolutely pick this game up.
