_childDocuments_.review: This will be an uncharacteristically long review for me, one that will take a lot of effort to write. However, the devs of this game clearly put in 200% effort so I will be doing the same. I will be keeping this review fully spoiler-free.If the below text seems too long, just read this: This is easily my GOTY 2023 and I will be recommending everyone I know play this. I've not passionately fanboyed this hard over a game in quite some time..GENERAL OVERVIEW:Trepang2 is a shooter made by a start-up indie company with a premise that on its own merit already sold it to me - a modern revival of the kind of visceral heart-pounding action we'd seen in F.E.A.R. back in 2005, the same kind of insanely dynamic, brutal, and action packed combat we'd seen against the Replicas in F.E.A.R, combined with the fast-paced movement mechanics and superhuman strength we'd seen in Crysis.On its own it is a very promising premise, and it already had me hook line and sinker when the demo for the game first dropped. What I didn't realize then that I realize now is that Trepang is not just an imitation of these classics, it is a modernization and improvement upon them. Trepang has used the evolution of video game tech to bring us the type of action-movie esque shootouts that games like F.E.A.R. and Crysis attempted to deliver on, and now with the technology at hand and the talented team behind this game that vision is fully realized.Trepang2 without exaggeration has the most satisfying gunplay of any shooter I've played in the last decade, and it's not an exaggeration to say I've played hundreds. Making shooting FEEL right is an artform, and Trepang's devs are Leonardo Da ♥♥♥♥♥♥' Vinci in that regard. DIFFICULTY:Trepang2 as a game does something I appreciate a lot, and not many games bother to do this - it has difficulty levels tailored to all levels of gaming experience. Some people scoff at things like Easy Mode being in a game, but because it is I can do things like recommend Trepang2 to people who I know love the themes and style this game has but perhaps aren't overly experienced with video games. Then you have options ranging from difficulties for people who play FPS games on occasion to people who can play them with their eyes closed. This means that, in my opinion, Trepang2 is just right for everyone.I found that Very Hard is the ideal difficulty for me, just the right balance of challenge. I've never been super good at kinetic shooters yet Trepang fit like a glove once I got used to it. There's plenty of replay value to be found in challenging yourself to beat previous levels on the higher difficulties once you've mastered the game mechanics.GRAPHICS:When I played the demo, there was one worry I had - the environment seemed somewhat bland. I was worried it'd fall into the same traps as its inspiration F.E.A.R. by falling into the pattern of overusing easily-repeated industrial areas with no eye candy. I can gladly report that after having beaten the game - I can confidently say my concerns were foolish.The environments in Trepang2 are breathtaking and varied, and the amount of detail and destructability in the environment is mind blowing. I am particularly partial to the gore effects in terms of graphics, but the environments are all masterfully created.For "generic bad guy" type designs on the typical enemy soldiers there is a surprising amount of love and detail to be found in their models. All of the character models in this game look fantastic. Honestly with how good the game looks it puts a lot of triple A games coming out these days to shame. The graphics  are assisted by good art direction and level design utilizing the assets to their fullest. AI:This will be an important category for longtime F.E.A.R. fans like myself coming into this - does Trepang deliver compelling and intelligent enemies who operate in squads effectively? Yes! And if you loved the quirky replica soldiers making tactical callouts, you'll love the way the enemies in Trepang communicate. The voice acting is phenomenal and the lines are so numerous and varied I was still hearing new ones up to the very end of the game.The AI will use squad tactics and attempt to utilize a variety of engagement tactics, from having someone rush you while others cover, to using a well placed grenade to cause you to run out while the whole squad has you in their sights, there was no shortage of challenge and excitement in the gunplay.I find myself enamored with the combat in Trepang to the point I keep replaying levels with different strategies and play styles just because the game is so fun no matter how you go about playing it. I am personally a very fast and aggressive player and the game rewards that in its own unique ways - for example, regenerating stamina when you kill enemies.SOUND:The sounds in Trepang2 are actually flawless. The gun sounds couldn't be better, I don't think anyone should even try to do better than this. We've peaked.The environmental sounds and music are also absolutely perfect and accentuate the carnage. There's plenty of wet meat slappage when things get gory, too.I didn't have any audio balancing issues either, and this is probably the first game I've played in maybe six years where I didn't manually need to change the SFX/Voice/Music volume balance. It's amazing what a game being made by talented passionate people who know what they're doing can be.STORY:It's good. Not the best I've ever seen it's good enough I felt invested in it, and you can feel the passion and inspiration the writers had for it - there's plenty of funny references and memorable moments throughout the campaign. I wouldn't say I got too emotional at any point but the detachment is somewhat expected when the game is primarily you turning people into red mist in the most creative ways you can imagine.Conclusion:So yeah, that's about it. Play Trepang2. Do it. DO IT.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, one of the most fun games I've played. The story is really engaging and while the ending is fairly predictable the process of getting there was quite enjoyable. Only issue I have is that despite your character being a supersoldier, they have the stamina of an asthmatic old man. Still a great game tho. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 is without a doubt the best FPS game I have played in years. It is so refreshing to see an arena shooter get so much right and almost nothing wrong. The only bad thing about this game is just how criminally short it is -- despite the obvious influences within the story, I still feel it had a very creative spin to it. I was a fan of the Easter Eggs, both the on-the-nose ones and the more hidden ones. But to get to the real meat of it, the combat was simply fantastic. The adrenaline rush never got old, and though the mechanics are really simple for an arena shooter, the beautiful arenas and their thoughtful layouts and designs, as well as the different enemy types, weapons, and utility items keeps the combat fresh through every single encounter.If you're a fan of FEAR, DOOM, Half-Life, SUPER-HOT, or similar games, this is absolutely a game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nowhere near as good as F.E.A.R,Things I didn't like.It's too dark most of the time. A dark area here and there is fine but 90% of the game is dark. It needs a lot more props. I saw the same coiled up extension cord model about  30 times in my brief time with the game. If the game doesn't want you to go down a hallway then there will be a bunch of crates blocking your way. Who puts a bunch of crates in the middle of a hallway? No story at all. No opening movie. Combat isn't fun and the AI is nowhere as good as it was in FEAR. I refunded this game. I'd rather play FEAR 1 for the 20th time than play this game once.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;drTrepang is very cool and funYou play 106, a mysterious mute super soldier who is rescued by TF27, a task force designed to dismantle HORIZON; a corporation secretly utilizing anomolous means and human experimentation to achieve cutting edge advancements for mankind. _childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: If FEAR and Doom had a baby.That's it, that's all I have to say.Okay jokes aside, Trepang2 is a pretty solid shooter. And honestly it's impressive to see what such a small team accomplished. I mean there's literally more voice actors in the credits that developers. I've had little to no bugs or crashes in the game so far, and it's visually impressive.Gameplay wise, Trepang is super fast paced like a old school boomer shooter, but has the slow motion mechanics of games like FEAR, which is the games spiritual predecessor. And like it's predecessor, the AI is solid. Enemies will shoot at your last known position, suppress you, and try to flank you. They'll also respond to various situations, like the player taking a hostage or squad members being killed. The game offers a few boss fights that are simple but entertaining at least. There's only a handful of weapons, but all of them are satisfying to use.My only gripe with the game at the moment is the main campaign story mode. It feels like a lot of really good ideas kinda just, jumbled together quickly into a single narrative. The second I start to understand it, it throws a curve ball and I lose the plot rather quickly. It's by no means bad, and all the characters are spectacularly voice acted. But, it just seems kinda, nonsensical to me. It's not a very long campaign, but that's not necessarily a bad thing. Overall, it's a super fun game. Good music, good combat, kinda lackluster campaign. But I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: A wild high intensity shooter that evokes F.E.A.R. with slow-mo, slides and drop-kicks; as well as mixing in horror elements between firefights. It even expands on the F.E.A.R. formula with cloaking and stealth mechanics.Trepang is one of the best shooters to come out in years w/ fabulous, responsive, high-speed movement with excellent audio and animation feedback on weapons and enemy's taking hits react appropriately, stumbling, getting knocked over and shouting out to each other.Speaking of enemies, the AIs are relatively clever, often trying to flank you, giving each other covering fire and flushing you out with grenades. Seriously the game-play reaches the heights that even AAA games often don't reach.My only complaint is the lack of more "exotic" weapons like F.E.A.R.'s penetrator, laser, railgun or auto-cannon.Though there are some pretty beefy pieces of artillery in Trepang, almost all of them are your average ballistic weapons w/ the exception of the spear gun and grenade launcher; there's even what appears to be a futuristic vibro-blade seen at the beginning of the game that you can't take. Don't get me wrong, they all handle well and feel good to use, just wish there was some more interesting weapons in the mix.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun shooter. As much as I liked it, I'd recommend buying it on sale. Combat is the highlight and selling point of the game for me, but the graphics, sounds, level design, etc are all great. The only thing I felt the game could use is more missions and more complex endgame content aside from just grinding out harder difficulties for cosmetic rewards. P.S the game runs pretty damn well on high, even on a mid-low end PC.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: Another banger shooter from the indie scene which inspired heavily from the F.E.A.R series with awesome gunplay, kickass music and a decent story to drive you through the not so long (5-6 hours on "very hard" difficulty) campaing. Whiie they managed that in the setting, the gameplay seems to be waaay more inspired by DOOM. So the tactic becomes jumping through an arena and shooting at whatever is in sight. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games of all time!I don't care what anyone says, the pure lethargic joy that comes from blowing someones head off, in slow motion!Then going invisible, sliding behind someone grabbing them throwing them with there own grenade attached to em in to his own team mates then shooting the grenade on him to make it blow everyone up...Its better than sex.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang2 is the John Wick/John Woo Sim we all never knew we had. My only gripe with the game.. the lack of a mission marker button, sometimes you get lost easily and wander aimlessly like some bumbling psychopath who needs an epipen shot in order to 'duel wield', yes in order to use your second hand.. you need some insulin. Thankfully after your one-time 'dose' of hand juice serum.. You can duel-wield shotguns. Yes. You read that right. The physics, hilarious, watched a grenade send man cart wheeling through the air at like Mach 5. He hit a wall and you heard an audible 'crunch' as his body crumbled to the floor... but he got up. So sprinted over to him, grabbed him, and threw him back across the court yard directly at his friends. He flew beautifully as he screamed during his entire flight. I sent a few grenades along side for good measure and I watched as he rejoined his friends by clocking one straight in the face, knocking both to the floor confused and dazed only for 3 grenades to assault them with a hailstorm of shrapnel comprised of the finest IKEA office furniture before finally being turned to what I would describe as 'the worst strawberry Jam grandma ever made'. Red Stains7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This review does have spoilers for some of the general things going on in this game.Trepang2 is something special. For me, it's rare that a shooter has a decent story. Trepang2 has a brilliant one. The story itself is short, but the individual missions are long and incredibly atmospheric. It weaves fantastic gun play and abilities together with moments of "downtime" where dialogue is delivered or supernatural things happen. Wayyy to many shooters try to get you to listen to dialogue while fighting, so this is highly appreciated by me.Some levels are very shooter-y and some levels are very haunted house-y. Both are done well, but I loved the scary ones. You always fight at a few points, but it goes through a lot to build up the vibe and give a surreal experience which hits well when it finally delivers. There's only two jump scares (done right, no bright flash or loud noise) and that also goes highly appreciated by me.I think I only have one problem with this game and it's the loading screen music. The bass is so deep it shakes my entire desk through the speakers or entire skull through my headphones. Luckily, load times are seconds and the game is incredibly well optimized, even on my old Lenovo ThinkCenter. They really worked some magic to make it run so well.

_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: You SHOULD play this. No seriously. If you want a fun FPS and like paranormal/Horror on top of it, you should  get this. I got this game with good but not amazing expectations. But I was so pleasantly surprised.PROS: Gameplay is fun but challenging, you can double-wield weapons while shooting enemies in slow-mo, which is already sick as hell. I didnt think there would be much of a story and while it might not be the most intricate, its solid. Probably couldve been a bit more fleshed out. Design is great, you pretty much always know where to go and what to do and I know some of this might sound like it  go without saying, but then you see some AAA 70€ FPS absolutely fumble stuff like this and you suddenly appreciate how much the devs concentrated on making this a great experience overall. I like the paranormal enemy variety as well. With games like this theres always the risk of just fighting zombie-variant no. 9000 for like 20h and that wasnt the case here. CONS: Some minor sound bugs and once or twice I had some FPS drops, but nothing too bad or even frequent. The bossfights could also use some work, since the overall gameplay lends itself more to fighting multiple weaker enemies instead of one strong one. My only real complaint, if I had to mention one, is how the game handles weapon switching. You can pick up any weapon dropped by an enemy at any time. But putting the weapon in your crosshairs doesnt work, instead you have to kinda stand on top of it. Which works until there are 3 weapons on top of each other, 2 which are out of ammo and you have to awkwardly shuffle around in the middle of a gunfight, trying to grab the 3rd one. I never died because of this, and using melee to kick the weapons apart mostly works. I am really only mentioning this in case theres ever a sequel, which I am really hoping for.But yeah, Id say this game is a good 7/10, maybe 8/10 depending on what your priorities are. I am currently trying to get all achievments and playing through the game on higher diffuculties and am having a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game to come out for about a year, since I played the demo I fell in love with the game and have over 110 hours on the games demo.This game is amazing, sure the concept of 'First Person Shooter, kill bad guys, guns! WOOHOO!' is a bit overused and very repetitive, Trepang2 really made it feel like something new, you don't see bullet time anymore really and it kinda makes me sad. But hopefully with this will revive a fallen genre of Gun-Fu.What I like about the game:The game-play is a BLAST, I mean that in the most sincere and meaningful way, its just too fun. The level design compliments the game and its combat mechanics very well and it gives you new ideas with every replay of a level. The guns feel good and powerful. The gore and blood is TOP-NOTCH it feels so visceral. The games blood doesn't disappoint. Enemies explode and their vital organs and other internal parts just come out in a satisfying way. The movement is basically what the game stands for, you can jump, slide, kick, dropkick, and of course run. Voice acting is amazing for an indie game, the cultists sound like insane cultists as they should and Horizon's voice acting sounds really good and fits their aesthetic. THE MUSIC, the music is a masterpiece, its a work of ART. Brandon McKagan did an amazing job with the soundtrack and I want it on physical CD.Here are my critiques:for how long this game was in development, I was expecting a larger campaign with more missions and game-play time. Just playing the main missions without the side missions, the game boils down to about 2 and a half hours of campaign, its kinda underwhelming but its still a blast to play through. I understand how time consuming it is to make maps and campaigns because I'm a map designer. No hate to anyone, I was just expecting more.The story is kinda all over the place, and with more campaign and missions it could've made more sense. (No offense to devs)Lots of the OST was scrapped and never used. Brandon McKagan made some FIRE tracks for the game but I never heard some that I wanted in the game. In all I think this is one of my favorite games ever made, if Trepang3 is announced I will pay for it and cherish the game. This game also did something that no game has ever had me do in a while. I was exited for the release and was going crazy until the release. I was satisfied and I want more. Thank you Trepang Studios.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: -GAMEPLAYTrepang2's bread and butter is gameplay. It's is very thoughtfully designed and gives you plenty of flexibility to solve its combat puzzles. Once you get into the rhythm of kicking, punching, shooting, sliding at and throwing enemies (all of which have useful and unique tactical benefits), you'll understand that the game is far more interesting mechanically than the game's marketing presents it to be. It's best enjoyed at a difficulty you can barely handle. Checkpoints are never too far apart.-NARRATIVEThe game's narrative presentation admittedly lacking, but it serves the gameplay very well and doesn't waste your time. It doesn't add to the experience nor does it take anything away from it.-PERFORMANCE/GRAPHICS:Optimization is honestly superb. The devs really knocked it out of the park in this respect. If you have anything resembling a modern gaming laptop or desktop, you shouldn't have any trouble getting 60FPS+. My PC ran the game at 100FPS+ most of the time with an i9-9900 and Nvidia 2070 Super with high settings and at a high resolution. In terms of aesthetics, the game looks like something out of 2018 or so in terms of tech... not impressive and not disappointing. What the game lacks in graphical flair it makes up for in performance.VALUE:The game is priced fairly at $30. The campaign and side missions are on the shorter side, but there are challenges available that unlock cheats, gameplay modifiers, and player cosmetics that should give any fan more than enough reason feel they got their money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: People keep hyping this game up to be "the next FEAR" because of how the gunplay flows and how the story is told.I enjoy fights against standard enemies on most difficulties. Unfortunately, higher difficulties do not make enemies behave smarter, it just makes their health numbers higher and yours effectively lower alongside giving them stupid accurate aim. Artificial turn-based RPG balancing in a shooter is lame no matter how you spin it.Boss fights are a joke. Bullet sponge that can only kill you if you decide to stop pressing your WASD keys. Snore.Don't get me started on the story. This isn't the next FEAR. This is a middle school band kid's very clearly FEAR-inspired AO3 fanfic. By far one of the most "Yeah, okay buddy, whatever you say" lore bits I've encountered in years, and I've played some hot garbage recently.And finally, the most egregious sin this game commits:Why in the hell does the Kriss Vector have vertical recoil?Instant downvote, non-negotiable.

But they all are made better by using the dual wield spas shotguns with incendiary rounds.With the variety of settings there is also a variety of enemies ranging from tacticool PMCs, Bio hazardous failed experiments and anomalies, All defeat-able by dual wield spas shotguns with incendiary rounds.TLDR; dual wield spas shotguns with incendiary rounds.

_childDocuments_.review: Been tracking this game since the first demo released where all you had was a fairly basic room with a bunch of enemies re-spawning to fight, took a while but it finally reached its finished state and it's damn good.If you ever played FEAR, just imagine that but quadruple the action and quadruple the speed of the combat. Feels incredibly fun to play and no moment ever feels like padding or wasted time, some of the also spooky parts of the game are fairly well done too.Though, the game is fairly short, you're looking at a 30 euro game that will take you only 5 to 6 hours to beat on hard difficulty.There is a horde you can play to earn more cosmetics and the game has a LOT of much harder difficulty choices to let you replay the game on harder settings but if you are someone who doesn't care too much about doing a 2nd run of the game, you might feel a bit short with the length you get out of this, especially with the asking price but the content on offer is really top notch and well made, definitely a large focus on quality over quantity approach.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: Trepang's combat is where it excels and feels like an evolution of where F.E.A.R. left off. Sliding around, grabbing enemies and blowing them into chunks never gets old. For those simply wanting a satisfying combat loop with little interruption, this game should do the trick. The levels feel very "drop-in, drop-out", with emphasis placed on unlocking gear and playing in higher difficulties.Personally, I would have liked to have seen a more fleshed out story/world. The hub lacks NPCs (even passive ones) and there's little story to experience, making the game feel a little arcade-ey and lightweight for my tastes. If this game is a commercial success, I hope the team puts the funds towards a story-focused sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: Even with a slightly low budget feel, Trepang2 absolutely nails the feedback and power fantasy of the FEAR games. It tries with its story, but kind of feels adorable in how flimsy it all is, but with gunplay and weaponfeel this good who cares? It's an absolute riot and carried entirely on just how great it feels to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: - A labyrinthine map of courtyards, libraries, great halls (and even what appears to be a model American suburb under construction for military training exercises) that are a joy to fight through.- Cool mini-bosses and a new enemy type.- Great plot moments and  twists, delivered mainly through really well written and acted radio chatter, from TF27 and Horizon's point of view, that motivate you to push forward and find out where this mission is going to end.- The introduction of a new game mechanic: - A cringe meme antagonist who taunts you throughout the level, who is genuinely a ton of fun.- A nice final showdown and a cliffhanger ending.The best games of the future aren't going to be delivered by the console giants, or the big triple A studios. It's passion projects like this made by the bois. GOTY 2023.Buy the game, buy the soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. Feels very similar to FEAR in the setting, but the gameplay is more inspired by DOOM. The tactic is often to quickly run around and shoot whatever is in sight, and enjoy some more creepy horror inspired settings inbetween fights. Unfortunatly the game do struggle with its pacing. As you do have a stamina bar, so while the doom playstyle is your best bet, you still have to stop and regain stamina in the corner every 10 seconds (melee kills regain stamina). There is a slow motion abiltiy as well, but i never found a good flow to keep my stamina and slowmotion up throughout an entire fight.
_childDocuments_.name: Trepang2

_childDocuments_.review: If I see one more negative review for Trepang2 on the basis of the game "not being FEAR" I am going to set fire to my PC. While inspired by the FEAR games, I must emphasize that Trepang2 is something.....different. The gameplay is more modern, the assets/development are clearly indie, and the atmosphere is frequently absurd with an occasionally morbid and borderline comedic tone underpinning it all. It borrows inspiration (or even gratuitously takes) from a variety of different sources, including but not limited to; a Backrooms level, a Half Life reference vaguely disguised as an oil rig level, etcetera. It's a short, sweet but replayable and personable game, with all the expected flaws and hitches that come from indie development.Which brings me to say, Trepang2 is unique. It's great, dare I say one of the best games I've ever played. But it is -not- FEAR. A metamorphosis? Sure. An evolution? Maybe. A passionate callback even? Absolutely. It is completely fine to not like Trepang2; I would not call it perfect myself. But for the love of god, if you give a game a negative review on the basis of it not living up to your expectations of being a completely different game, get your face away from your catalytic converter and stop inhaling exhaust fumes. There are several good reasons to write a negative review for this game; "bUt MUh fEaR" is not one of them.

_childDocuments_.review: While I have not played the original FEAR, this games great. The gunplay is very satisfying. The stealth takes a bit of a learning curve to mix into the rest of the action, you'd think they'd be conflicting playstyles, but its good to get heat off you and flank, or pick off some troops before a firefight. It has some big weaknesses though. The bossfight sections are pretty consistently terrible. They are always very bulletspongey, and damaging them doesn't earn you focus or armor so you're operating on extremely limited pre-set supplies. Not to mention one boss, on top of just not having enough autosaves in the final sections of the fight which are very long, just decides to shut off all your mobility fun as you have to literally stand still to bait out attacks. The horror is a little hit or miss, but when it hits, it hits. There is a section of the game which is just a blatant reference to a horror trend, not in the way it might be SCP or control inspired, just "wow, this is X", and it feels a little out of place and hard to take seriously despite how it still manages to be unsettling. The story itself is very predictable, but thats not a bad thing. I wish it leaned more into the supernatural aspects of the setting more than the military squables, but theres always room for that in the future if they continue to add content or make a sequel.

name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis
detailed_description: THESE WALLS CAN’T FALL Set in the medieval world of Gloria Victis, Siege Survival: Gloria Victis sees your country invaded and your city under brutal siege. A small group of civilians are trapped in the only remaining stronghold and are the last source of hope for the defending troops hanging on for dear life. You might not be fighting the invaders yourself, but the fate of the city lies in your hands. Support the last soldiers standing against overwhelming enemy forces and hold out until reinforcements arrive. Build your camp, manage resources, craft supplies during the day and scour the fallen city for resources and new civilian recruits at night. SURVIVE THE SIEGE Defending what’s left of your city are a few tired troops in dire need of arrows, weapons and armour; along with treatment for the wounded. You need to keep this last bastion of defenders supplied and supported in every way possible ahead of their battles every few days; otherwise, the enemy will eventually storm the keep. Not only that, but you also need to protect your civilians and your camp, as you are assaulted by waves of flaming arrows and giant boulders. MANAGE RESOURCES & CRAFT SUPPLIES You need better weapons, a roof over your head, hot food and all the other trappings that just existing entail; and the only way you’ll get these is if you and your team craft them. But resources are limited and you'll need to sustain both soldiers and civilians, so find ways to preserve food, develop your infrastructure and use your supplies more efficiently. SCAVENGE THE FALLEN CITY Venturing out from the safety of your keep, you have to explore the ransacked city at night to collect precious resources and help the surviving citizens – or exploit them. But be careful, enemy patrols keep watching the streets; you must be smart to remain unseen... and alive. Unlock routes to other districts, enlist new civilian recruits and make it back before dawn so as not to be caught. YOUR BACK AGAINST THE WALL Help is coming, but it’s weeks away. And in a siege like this, one dilemma can quickly spiral into another and very soon you will face tough moral choices. The fate of your companions - and that of the city - is in your hands alone. There will be hunger, wounds, disease and despair, but also growing tensions between the civilians and defenders. Sustain your troops or keep your civilians alive? Only you can decide. TELL YOUR OWN STORY Siege Survival: Gloria Victis is developed on a game editor platform that will allow modding and community-generated content at launch. Create your own unique scenarios and stories from scratch and expand the universe of Gloria Victis.

_childDocuments_.review: Medieval version of ''this war of of mine''.If you enjoy both of those things, this is certainly the game for you.But how does it compare to ''this war of mine''?It is similar because of:- Resource management, leave your castle/base to scout the map for building materials, food and weapons.- Day/Night cycle. You leave during the night to find stuff. You use what you found during the day to build up your castle to become more self-sufficient.- Recruitment. New characters can be found and recruited during the scouting missions at night outside of your castle.- Stats. Manage your survivors health/hunger/thirst/energie(tiredness)/morale- Enemies. You can choose to fight enemy soldiers or dodge them by staying in the shadows.- Speciality. Different survivors are good at different things. this makes you think about how you want to bring on a mission with you.-----------------------------This game is different from ''This war of mine'' Because of the following  pro's:------------------------------ It's medieval times!- Instead of chosing 1 location at night out of many, night time is set on 1 big map with different area's. i like this better cos sometimes i had planned to go to 1 area, but could not pass because i did not have a shovel or there were to many guards. so i just changed my plan and looted a different area. Very nice.- Supporting the troops: There is this whole extra dimention to the base management where you don't only take care of your survivors, but also have to plan ahead to provide the soldiers that defend your castle with the right amount of food, gear and medical support. This makes it more strategic. when you go out at night to look for Loot, do you focus on building up your buildings to have an easier late game? or do you bring back what the soldiers needs right now? again, very nice.- Catapult!: though the mechanic is very simplistic. it feels satisfying to see those enemy numbers subtract when you fire that thing.- Top-down camera: more freedom of movement. It brings more tention to the game. The way lighting and the camera works adds to that. You don't see what is around a corner before your character can see around it. Sometimes i thought i figured out the patrol route of a soldier, only lose my ♥♥♥♥ when i turned a corner and ANOTHER soldier came my way. - More good things you should find for yourself.-----------------This game is different from ''This war of mine'' Because of the following  con's:------------------ Emotion: The game does not bring the heavyness and bleakness of war that TWoM has. That might be the astetic choice, which is fine. But it also does not let me feel as connected to the characters as i wish it did. TWoM has character logs that update every day they go through something. This game gives you a character log from the start about the character. but it does not record their opinions and feelings. i would love to see that.- Morale management: Morale in this game is a almost a throwaway stat. The only way it went down in my playthrough is when 1 of my characters died (which happened once). Which also brings me to my next con...- Game is too easy??: i played the normal story game mode and finished it in 6 hours. Which is a good time for 1 play through imo. However. i never felt like my survivors were ever in any REAL danger. The only reason i lost 1 of my dudes is because i gave him no food/water or sleep for a few days, just to see what would happen.  **SIDENOTE** the game has new game plus and other modes/game starts what should be harder. i did not play those so i might be wrong here.- 1 base: Where TWoM has multiple maps and bases, this game has only 1 Base and 1 map. Now the map is big enough to where you (or at least i) need multiple playthroughs to find everything. But i hope it doesn't get boring on multiple playthroughs.---------------------------------FINAL THOUGHTS: (minor spoilers for ingame story)This game is a wonderful taste for those who enjoy This war of mine or just medieval settlement management/stealth games in general. The music and estatic is great. The whole concept of defending a castle by doing everything BUT the combat is a welcome new mechanic that i would love to see done more and expanded upon. I would love to see the game pull me in more emotionally though. At some point early in the game you meet a soldier who goes missing at some point. it is clear to me that the game wants you to care a lot about him and hope for his safe return. But it had failed to make me connect to him enough to make me care. This could be helped by having this soldier be part of your survivors for a few days. Or make him add something to the ''daylight'' phase that is really missed when he is gone. Also i feel like the game has GREAT potential for MORE gameplay. Add more maps. new/bigger castles. A winter mode where you also have to keep your people WARM as an added mechanic. Heck add some voice acting to both castle mode and nighttime mode so i can hear soldiers talking when i sneak by them. I would recommend it. But i would feel even better about recommending it if the developers announce more content.Cheers

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly have no idea why there are so many negative reviews of this game. It's not AAA, but its at least a B+, and they deliver exactly what was promised. Yeah, there is a lot here to remind someone of This War of Mine, but this game is it's own standalone experience and it does have new and interesting elements. Unlike in TWOM, Siege Survival requires you to affect the outcome of the siege rather than merely being a passive victim trapped inside of it. Is this better? Not necessarily, but it is different. I encountered no bugs, I found the scenarios replayable (though they should develop more of them), and there is an acceptable range of challenges from easy to hard. Don't let the negative reviews dissuade you, this is a solid game.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not understand all the positive reviews. At best this is a solid neutral -- it looks decent, it plays okay, but holy crap is it tedious and unrewarding. It's like it is trying to be 'This War of Mine' in a fantasy setting, but it fails in too many ways. You will finish scenarios without having the time to explore more than 2/3 of the map and it'll not matter. None of the characters mean anything to you, at all (you really got attached to some of them in TWoM). None of them have any statistics or character perks that really seem to matter to the scenario, it is very telling that there isn't even a player guide listing all the characters with each ones traits or perks they're so irrelevant -- sure you can get one that crafts faster, but who cares if you don't have enough of those materials or really do not need to craft anything with the materials you have? None of them interact with each other, none of them have a back story (a tiny blurb on the character info screen IF you bother to click the fountain pen on their portrait). Upgrading the defenses seems like it would matter, and it does to succeed the scenario, but it's not rewarding to you in any way -- not even a "feels good man" for getting within a point or two of the enemy numbers. You never see the enemy outside of your night time raids, and even then you don't care who they are they're just faceless character lacking "something bad" you don't see any of the defender battles, you don't see anything that makes you care about your side or their side. Was expecting "this will be great!" based on the "very positive" but it's just bland, boring, and entirely no replay value. I've only finished two scenarios and that is enough for me. Bummer.

Go to keep and craft items with those materials and keep your defence number higher than the attackers. That's it. No way of sabotaging the enemy attackers except the Trebuchet which frankly was boring to use anyway. Don't starve to death and become self sufficient. Add in some features (Kill an guard/officer to disorganise the next attack, acquire intel from an enemy tent to find the details of the next attack) So many things that could be added instead of "Check this box to scout the enemy line" with no consequence other than they get tired and must rest. Something to add in some challenge or story get an atmosphere for the game.I've done 1 run of each story and although I enjoyed them that's me done with it. Yeah I might play again in a few months or so but until then it's given me 20 something hours of entertainment and I'm finished.

_childDocuments_.review: It's potentially worth a play at the asking price, but it's ultimately a forgettable experience. It might be better to wait for a sale or just play This War of Mine. I'd give a wobbly-sideways-thumb ehhhh rating if I could.For good and for ill, this game heavily borrows mechanics from This War of Mine (TWoM). Siege Survival isn't a direct clone of it, but it does copy the theme, mechanics, and core gameplay loop. That means it offers largely the same experience as TWoM, albeit with a different setting and aesthetic. There's only two key differences: the player has to repeatedly sacrifice supplies to the siege defenders, and the night time map is a single open world space rather than a collection of disconnected levels. I personally prefer the aesthetic of TWoM, but that game has significantly worse pacing issues than Siege Survival. I'd recommend playing whichever one visually appeals to you the most. There's little reason to play both as Siege Survival doesn't do enough to feel meaningfully different, and unfortunately TWoM already released 7 years ago.The siege setup works great, and is the probably the best aspect of the game. Constantly feeding and supplying the AI defenders gives a necessary resource sink that's often lacking in similar games - being self-sufficient wasn't good enough, I was forced to scavenge daily so I could repair equipment, fix the wall, and give the soldiers a warm meal. Unfortunately I found this aspect a little too easy to manage. I'm already familiar with this kind of game, and I didn't struggle to utilise resources efficiently (especially time - the most valuable resource). Efficient resource usage and good/lucky future planning enabled me to cruise to the ending without any setbacks. I never had a food shortage, I always had enough gear for the defenders, I never lost a battle or a defender, etc etc. This is probably fine for less experienced players, but I was wishing for more difficult choices. For example, there's a point near the end where the player is told to do A or B for the defenders because they can't afford both. However I easily did both, and still had leftover resources to mess around with. I also looted over 90% of the city resources according to the end game stats.My own problem with the difficulty might have been resolved on alternative/harder scenarios. However, the game forces players to do the default scenario before unlocking the other ones, which feels like a mistake to me. I experienced the majority of the content in the first playthrough (all events, all areas explored), so I have little desire to replay it with different characters. I'm lead to believe the scavenging map is static with no alternative areas to explore, and it's unfortunately not as interesting as TWoM. Whilst the open world map feels more natural than TWoM, it's also more boring. There's no functional difference between different districts in the city, especially as all resources can be found in all districts. The disconnected levels of TWoM had a lot more character, more interesting dynamic events, and more important decision making for the player. I don't miss the RNG components of that game, but looting a bandit-filled warehouse felt very different to grandma's cottage. Choosing a level in that game would lock the player out of other options for the night too, whereas the Siege Surival city is small enough to reach any resource node from any starting point. The player is encouraged to systematically sweep the entire city too, as resources don't respawn.One thing the game really lacks is dynamic events, or some kind of external pressure to throw a curveball. The player has to supply the defenders, but all attacks come on fixed days. The player knows when they're going to be attacked, and how strong the attack will be. Food rots over time (both in the base, and in the scavenging map), but it's plentiful enough to not be an issue. By the time all the external food was rotten I had already setup a permanent long-term solution in my base. Beyond this there's no changes over time. The scripted attacks get stronger, but the player is continually supplying the defenders with new and better gear anyway. It's fairly easy to grow the defender's strength faster than the attacker. Siege Survival feels like it's missing the winter of TWoM, the storm of Frostpunk, or even Rimworld's Randy Random. No NPCs visit the base, no enemies sneak behind your lines, no traders turn up with supplies, nobody appears in desperate need of resources, no areas of the map get blocked off, etc etc. Some scripted events happened at the start of a few days, but these were just the defenders telling me to keep giving them resources. They were functionally no different from a popup saying "Keep playing the game!". All the guards in the city are identical too, and every character can easily run away from them. This unfortunately made the resource cycle too deterministic and solvable on a first playthrough, and also lead to an unexpected ending where the game suddenly told me (with no buildup) that I'd won the game. The achievement for winning also triggered before the narrative told me I'd won, which felt odd?Speaking of the narrative, it's non-interactive and almost non-existent. Both the scenario introduction and opening FMV suggest the enemy leader is a prominent character. However, this person never appears in-game, is never mentioned again, and doesn't seem to have any relevant to the plot. There's no further story beyond 'you are under siege, don't die'. There's some scripted events around the city, which are ultimately either a) choose between free resources or not being a ♥♥♥♥, b) get bonus supplies/player characters, or c) unlock a trader in the city. There's no other variations, and these choices don't narratively matter. My characters robbed some innocent survivors, and had the 'sad' state for the rest of the game. This didn't seem to have a mechanical or narrative effect. Player characters have no dialogue, story, or quests. They're little more than robotic workers and are 100% controlled by the player. Don't expect any 'plays guitar' or 'addicted to coffe' NPCs, like TWoM. These characters don't even appear in the ending - they might as well be called Backpack, Builder, Trader, and Useless 4th Guy. Nobody uses their names, and they never have anything to say about each other or their actions.Some of those unlocked events also felt weak. Whilst I could unlock some traders around the city, and even a player character who specialised in Trading, I rarely felt trading was worth it. Backpack space is too limited to trade for bulk crafting materials, and the general price of supplies is too expensive. It wasn't worth sacrificing food or equipment to get trivial amounts of building supplies. I traded off the (useless) 'valuables' item for meat, but otherwise didn't engage with the trading mechanic. These traders also didn't make narrative sense - why wasn't the enemy army attacking them, and where were they getting all their supplies from? They aren't scavenging at night (since they're sitting around to trade), and the game overtly says it's impossible to scavenge during the day due to the occupying army. One of the traders is even a single mom with a baby - how haven't they been noticed? What are they eating and drinking?Overall it's okay, not great. I might replay it with a different scenario at some point, but I doubt I'll remember this game in a few years time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best survival games out there. If you liked This War of Mine then you will love this. It is the same concept but in the middle ages. The interface is also top-down which makes it a lot more fun. Pros:- Main scenario was just the right length, not too short and not too long.- The difficulty was well controlled, making you struggle just enough so that a big mistake will cost you everything but a small mistake will just make you suffer a bit.- Interface was easy to learn and master- Editor included. You can make your own scenario or make a modified copy of the ones you have.- I encountered no bugs while playing.Cons:- There is only 2 Tiers in the building upgrades, which makes the game less complex.- The simplified interface hides so much information that it hurts sometimes. Which food gives the most nutrition? No-one but the Editor knows.- The perk tooltips are useless, telling you nothing! You can do nothing because you know nothing!!!!- The editor needs some TLC. It is pretty easy to use but still lacks a lot of features and has some bugs here and there.- The saving mechanism sucks. Either Iron-man (save constantly) it or allow me to save whenever. Saving only at the beginning of the day forces me to play the entire day before I can exit to go on with my life (sleep, food, work...)All in all I really love this game and hope it continues to get improvements. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like a bad attempt of "This War of Mine". For it tries to show you the civil front of a war with survival aspects but it lacks on the "emotion" side. There are nearly none moral conflicts and very limited events. After I finished the game and started with a different "Scenario" I felt like I wasted my money when I realize they just changed the location of events and they are completely same with the previous scenario. When I say "events" please don't expect something impressive. They go like: You saw a pace, it was X's bla bla shop. You enter inside and hear a voice, what are you going to do? -I will search. +You realize it was not what you expected but a simple mouse... And some critical resources! What are you going to do? -I'll take them." They mostly are 2 to 3 paragraphs of 2 to 3 pages with very simple choices. Allowed choices feel really bad too. There was a corpse with an axe on him, his mother tries to bury the person. You are only allowed to "Take the axe" or "Help with burying". I would take the axe because the garrison needs it and bury the corpse afterwards because I'm a good person. But game only wants you to choose between absolute good and absolute evil. ->So as someone else mentioned in the reviews, you need a better writer. The rest of the events are a cheap versions of "recruitment". But there is also a problem with that too. You are not allowed to have more than 4 characters which is not warned by tutorials. You learn it when you already have 4 characters and interact with the possible recruitment. The game automatically blocks the recruitment choice and forces you to pick the "annoy the other person because you don't want them" choice and as a result interacting with the npc is blocked forever.  ->You could add an option to convince them to join the garrison. But no, you force the player to tell the npc "You are a drunken bla bla. Get lost" There a lot more to criticize but I want to end with a summary that the game lacks the atmosphere and feels. It failed in what it tried to do.

_childDocuments_.review: It's what I was expecting, but at the same time not as much fun as I was expecting.Build mode and interface is a hot mess, instead of placing blueprints and assigning builders, you select a guy, click on work bench, wait for guy to walk over to work bench, place blueprint, wait for guy to walk over to blueprint, to start building. Every action feels like it takes too many steps, and there's too much waiting in between steps. The game also isn't real time with pause, meaning every second you spend guiding one person through their 8 step build process, something else isn't getting done.Scavenge mode is ok, it could actually be fun, but it's stuffed full of false moral choices to seem deep and thoughtful, but has the moral depth of the average early 2000s RPG. You can help bury a dead dude, or you can take his axe, you can't do both. If you don't rob a grieving father he'll go bury his son in the back yard, although the house is surrounded by an enemy patrol that will kill on sight, didn't seem like a good idea, but whatever.Also, in 80 minutes of play time, no less than two doors that 'can only be opened with a key' and a 'this door is barred from the other side." The player is supposed to be scavanging ruins, there's no window to fit through or a hatchet anywhere?

_childDocuments_.review: Many people claimed this is just a medieval This War of Mine. But this game has a feature which, in my opinion, makes it drastically better than TWOM: War effort.Yes, yes, I know TWOM is sending a message that war is bad. But it has forgotten IRL civilians CAN contribute greatly to the side they supported! (Such as Polish & French resistance in WW2.) When I played TWOM I've always dreamed of an idea that if I sell enough weapons to either rebel at school or military outpost, I can break the stalemate and end the war sooner. But NOPE! TWOM forces me to believe any civilian contribution is useless and every Polish & French should just lay down and suffer under occupation.In this game, however, I can tip the scale of war by giving food & medicine, forging better equipment, providing intels, recruiting stray soldiers in some events, and even joining the fight with trebuchet. The outcome of the war will even change depending on my contribution, from pyrrhic one to completely rofflestomp the enemy, which I absolutely adore. After all, this isn't some 2012 apocalypse which is beyond human control. This is war, something that everyone CAN do their part.There's another thing that makes this game better. In TWOM, base raiding is just some text telling me "congrats, you lost xx because RNG hates you" which players has no real control except leaving weapons and manning guards every night. In this game, however, you can actually feel like you're under attack when war cries rage in the backgrounds as rocks & arrows are thrown into your base. You also have direct control on how much damage will be done by ordering your characters to take cover, putting out fire, burning the corpses and collecting rocks to fix the wall.There are only some flaws I'd like to point out. First, fixing the trebuchet takes too long. Often time even if I poured precious resources into tons of tar pots and spare materials for fixing, I couldn't throw more than 3 shots per battle because the battle will already be over before I'm done fixing. I'd suggest shorten fixing time so I can better convert my resources into result.Another flaw is the reward of killing guards is too little. For a broken axe (which will go obsolete in late game) and a single night of no patrol, I'll get tons of patrol for the next several nights without any change in enemy strength. I'd suggest either giving us better loot like a broken sword or valuables, or having an impact on enemy strength (more guards killed or on patrol = less people attacking the wall)I understand you couldn't spare too much time on this game because of the publishers. I'll be patient and keep supporting this game. Good luck with your MMO!

_childDocuments_.review: How to best explain this game?A survival type game only?  A resource management game? Perhaps a RTS type game?In truth, it's all of these genres, and none of them.  And I say that with a sense of sadness in what I had hoped for this game.But let's first talk about why I even bought this game.I love the medieval era type games.  This game is truly faithful to that era. It gives you a sense of what people had at their disposal back then.  The graphics and sound are solid and enjoyable.The problem with this game is how it limits you by its own limitations.What I mean by that there are certain design choices and game mechanics that make you scratch you head and ask 'why would the developers do it this way?'  An example of this is the way the camera is limited when scavenging in your fallen city at night compared to when you are in your castle.  Another example is that you can only zoom in so far, so you never really get to see the detail in the artwork.   And of course, the camera's limited ability to of freedom of movement.Let's talk about Resource Management.The other limitation is in how you handle your characters in the game.  Throughout the game, you may come across new characters to bring into your sieged castle and help with resources.  However, you are forced to individually take care of each person.  If they are hungry or thirsty you have to click on them, then tell them to go eat or drink, or tell them to sleep if they are tired.  It is an annoying resource management.  I would rather just focus on keeping food and water in stock.The only real forward movement in the game is clicking on each of your people to make them go cook food, or chop wood, or repair armor, or whatever other menial task you have for them.   And why must they do all this?  For 2 reasons: the first is to keep them alive... the 2nd is to supply your army who still defends the castle.Another annoying design is that shovels are probably THE MOST important tool.  You can't progress through the scavenging city without a shovel.  Sometimes you will find a shovel to use, but for whatever reason, when you return back to the castle, your shovel is gone.  So you are forced to build one.. however you can't because you need resources to build it.  But to get more resources, you need a shovel to open a path in the scavenging city to find more resources.The other annoying thing is that no resources in the city will spawn the next night.  Once you scavenge an area, it no longer holds a purpose.  At some point, you reach a dead end in the game's design and have no choice than to restart the game all over again.So in summary, I bought this game because I've always wanted a medieval era game that focuses on trying to keep your castle from being taken.  So many games focus on just combat that I thought it would be a nice change to focus on just keeping my castle running.Unfortunately this game feels like a demo of a specific part of a march larger castle/keep game.  I was hoping to be able to explore a castle, protect it from outside invaders, recruit castle defenders, or perhaps even have some type of diplomacy tactics while secretly buidling up my rebel force and supplying them with weapons until they take back the castle.Instead, I'm given truly dumb characters who don't even know when to go to sleep, eat, or drink without me clicking on them constantly.This game is a pass... it makes you wish for more than what it is.  My only hope is that the developers use this to build onto something of a grander scale.  Let me build my own castle, use people to gather resources, setup defenders, control uprising of citizens, etc...

_childDocuments_.review: I first heard of this game during the Steam Game Festival back in February and I spent maybe 2 dozen hours trying out the demo before getting the full game.Siege Survival is heavily inspired from This War of Mine, and incorporates many of the same looting and resource management aspects, such as base-building, scavenging the city at night, trying to keep your people alive until the end of a war, and more.+ . There are a lot of objectives to focus on. Some of them are identical to TWoM. Others are unique to Siege Survival, such as sending supplies to your bastion's defenders so they are better equipped for upcoming battles, sending civilians to scout enemy camps at night, dealing with enemy projectiles that can damage your buildings and characters, and possibly repairing and firing your own trebuchet to attack the enemies during a battle. You send supplies to the defenders that your civilians scavenge or produce themselves, from food to medicine to weaponry. I feel like this interaction between the civilians and defenders is quite unique and works very well from a gameplay perspective. It has some unexplored potential from a narrative perspective too.+ . I like medieval/fantasy settings and sieges/wars are interesting events from both historical and fictional standpoints, in my opinion.+ . The map is (mostly) contiguous and you can choose where to spawn and where to loot. Since resources don't respawn or regenerate, you have an incentive to look further and further out from the first spawn point you unlock and possibly find more. I like the idea that you have access to almost the whole map from any spawn point, barring special events and paths blocked by rubble.+ . While this may seem like a minor point, I think this bumps up the visual polish of the game significantly. The shadows and light/reflections look pretty cool in my opinion, and having the day get progressively darker/brighter as time goes on is a nice touch. Rain, clouds, and storms are also part of the weather cycle and can cause characters to get sick, and fill up your water collector quicker.+ . Leading on from the previous point, I like the fact that the scavenging period doesn't just abruptly end once it's morning. Rather, guards will spot you and chase you to the exit. I prefer this to TWoM's approach of just abruptly ending your scavenging run once it hits 5:00am and informing you the next day through RNG whether your character made it out well or not.= . This aspect is theoretically the same as in TWoM such that enemies will hear/see you easier if you speed up your actions. You can wait for a guard to go further in his patrol and loot pretty much any pile you want on the map; you could literally never fight an enemy and still finish the game with an abundance of resources while I felt this was more challenging to do in TWoM.= . I like the concept that if you are spotted in an area, the patrols will get increasingly vigilant on following nights. I also like the concept that killing a guard raises alertness across multiple districts, which (rightfully) discourages you from fighting guards because it gets harder to scavenge safely on following nights. I do wish, however, that enemies didn't just lock on to you at daybreak. It makes sense to me that patrols will increase every morning or that enemies can see further in daytime vs nighttime, but just having every guard on the map bumrush you at the first ray of sunlight, , is a frustrating/unintuitive experience. It would feel more intuitive if  led to multiple guards rushing you because they could call out your location to each other, but I realize this may have been a balancing decision because otherwise players could arguably loot for too long.= . Pretty basic, just like in TWoM. You click on the enemy and smack him with your fists/weapon until one of you runs out of hitpoints. It's not very expansive or complicated because it's not the main focus of the game; you aren't supposed to fight enemy soldiers as a civilian, so this mechanic is understandably not given much depth. I do wish that you could see your own character's healthbar like you can see your enemy's healthbar rather than just seeing the 'wounded' status effect changing.= . The basic story scenario is honestly not too difficult for players experienced in this genre, even on the first playthrough. Some of the additional scenario presets are more challenging, and there are many customization options for players that are interested in challenging themselves with more gritty/unforgiving scenarios. Quite standard for this genre of games.- . This is probably the biggest one, since it is directly responsible for player immersion and engagement. The plot is coherent, but very basic. That's not a huge deal, but the issue is that the player has little control over where the plot goes except for 2 (quite minor) choices at the beginning of the story. On some days, you meet certain characters that remind you of your obligations to the castle, and tell you to "do your job", which honestly isn't very helpful. You don't really get to engage with these characters because there are no meaningful choices or interactions, either within the conversation or beyond it. You either listen to what they tell you because they have introduced you to some new, powerful, previously inaccessible mechanic (e.g. scouting enemy lines, repairing broken equipment, upgrading some buildings, etc), or you don't listen and set yourself up for defeat. Nothing else really changes. Your characters don't appear by name anywhere in the story either.- . This is somewhat part of the narrative but I wanted to address it separately. The special events in Siege Survival are identical to any 'Choose your own Text Adventure RPG'; you get a few choices which follow a set pattern: (1) be mean to an NPC and get some resources, or be nice instead and get something less valuable; (2) meet an NPC and do/say what they want to recruit them, or make the wrong choice/tell them to get lost and never see them again; (3) make a dangerous/risky choice, or come back with better tools/character with better perks to get free resources; (4) Trader. I personally really like text adventure style games so I actually enjoy the aesthetic, but some of the choices felt forced/stilted. For example,  Alternatively,  There are some other such events too.- . There is some great modding potential for this game. However due to the gaps in the narrative and little to no variation in the city map, there is limited reason to replay the game other than unlocking characters/achievements or attempting higher difficulties.Overall, a solid game with fun mechanics and an interesting setting, but also with some gaps that could be better filled. I give it a .

_childDocuments_.review: With this game I really tried. I really wanted to enjoy it. I love This War of Mine and think the concept of doing a survival every-move-matters style in this setting is really cool and could work well. I tried two separate campaigns, both the primary siege survival in the keep as well as the scenario where you're in the desert and have to hold out while rebuilding a destroyed ship.But ultimately I was ground down by the interface, the controls and a few aspects of the gameplay. In this game, every passing moment of time and every move you make/thing you craft is decisive in determining whether you're scraping by or in deep s***. To that end, the game demands tight controls and effective ways to determine what's happening and take action. The gripes:-My biggest complaint is that there is no direct Pause/Unpause... You can slow time down to paused or speed it up, but you have to constantly be aware of what dial you're on, and because there's no toggle you can't set the spacebar as pause/unpause which is amazing because this is the case in literally *every other game that has a pause feature* (I had rigged it so that "spacebar" slowed the speed down and capslock sped it up but it was still too unwieldy and headache inducing). -To get anything done and understand what's going on in camp you have to stay zoomed out, but if you're zoomed out all your characters look the same and you lose track of who is where. I barely played off anyone's strengths or weaknesses because they all blurred together for me. Selecting survivors and assigning them tasks feels clunky and unclear.-This War of Mine has you scavenge across discreet map areas at the start of each night. Gloria Victis has you start at the same point on a single large map and have to work your way around each night, which would be even cooler and more realistic in theory but the nights pass way too quickly and it's incredibly frustrating to spend 2/3rds of your nights just traversing the map areas hoping the one place you earlier identified will have something worthwhile in it to then haul ass back to your base in the little time that remains. In short, scavenging is too unforgiving even for a game like this and is some combination of frustrating or boring since guards are virtually no threat just an annoyance to be hid from (which further eats up your precious time).-Keeping track of which resources you have and what you can afford to spend on building and crafting is a nightmare: I had to use a physical pen and paper to keep track of what I could spare and what I needed to look for at night which could be a raw and cool feature in theory, but not really since I was already struggling with controls and general uncertainty of what to do/where to focus.It does feel very cool at times during the battle sequences where you really feel like you're tipping the scales in the battle by providing that extra few bricks, meal and two axes. Holding your breath to see the outcome and even participating in the assaults is the game's most innovative feature and is certainly superior to the nightly raids of This War of Mine. It's a good step in the right direction for the genre.Ultimately though, even the payoffs are minimal with how annoying everything is to juggle and staying on top of everything comes to feel like a chore since there are essentially 0 quality of life controls that can help you manage the situation. For all these reasons sadly I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: On the first playthrough, which took about 7 hours, I experienced a lot of emotions.At first it was scary to wander the streets at night. I hoped all the time that I would not be noticed.During the day, work going on inside the castle, and if at the beginning of the game it was difficult to find work for all characters, in the middle and towards the end they worked tirelessly. I lost my first character to thirst. My second died in the fight at night. It was quite interesting to explore the city. During the battles I tried to help the garrison as much as possible and to supply everything necessary, although it suffered from starving and suffering from the lack of water for almost all siege.At the end of the first campaign I got acquainted with the mechanics of the game and already knew what and how I should do.The second campaign was the Scavengers scenario and it was pretty easy. The environment and the world seem to be quite realistic, the level designers have done a good job. Music also conveys the atmosphere well.But the overall integrity of all this is spoiled by the fact that there is no general feeling of belonging to what is happening outside the courtyard of the castle.Here, a good option would be to simply add soldiers on the courtyard walls, and add advancing enemies during battles. And the characters. You don't have time to get used to them, and in general they turn out to be impersonal, and differ only in bonuses and debuffs. A good way to differentiate them would be to add their comments when an event happens, similar to the way it is done in This War of Mine.In addition to being compared to This War of mine. In terms of mechanics, the game is pretty close to it, and there is nothing wrong with that. Still, this game has slightly different goals. In addition to surviving, you need to supply soldiers so that they can fight off assaults.But in This War of mine, the atmosphere is much heavier and deeper, you can feel the tension throughout the game.  In general, economics is simple, and almost all of its elements are useful. Almost, because I have not found a normal use for pigs.  While exploring the city, it is intuitively clear that in a heap of stones you can find building materials, in a heap of boards, logs and firewood, in a chest something valuable.A little about food and water. At the beginning of the game, you sometimes need to make special forays for water and food, but with the opportunity to build mousetraps and water collectors, you can forget about food.  It's good that the game has a built-in scenario editor, but so far I haven't tried much to do something in it. I caught a couple of bugs that as a result my work was saved as an empty map, and when loading there was nothing but a landscape.It would also be nice to add the ability to move exactly the buildings on the map so that you can create your own cities or change the existing one.+ The game is addictive at the first playthrough+ Interesting bastion support mechanic+ Well-made city+ The economy is balanced+ May be replayed - Loss of atmosphere when you get used to the game- There is no involvement in what is happening during the assaultThe game will definitely appeal to fans of the Middle Ages and survival. You can immerse yourself in the life of the besieged with sorties and attempts to survive. It's hard to tear yourself away from what is happening. As a game for a couple of nights it will go very well.

_childDocuments_.review: As others have mentioned, this does feel similar to This War of Mine, except 3D and set in the medieval time. Game-play wise I actually had more fun with this one.Your town has come under an unexpected attack and you with some of the guards have managed to take shelter in the town bastion. Now it's up to you to survive the siege!During the day you build, craft, manage your resources and provide supplies to the bastion defenders (witch you don't control or see). Time is limited and there always is something to do to keep your survivors busy - rarely did I have anyone standing idly by with nothing to do.During the night you sneak out to scavenge the town for resources. Inventory is limited, so you have to be picky with what you choose to bring back. The streets have guard patrols, so stealth is required, but to be honest, after some experimenting, the stealth system is really generous, so no need to slowly sneak everywhere (since time, once again, is limited). Night time is also where you will run into events - small text adventures that can result in new companions or some extra loot. The cool part about the night map is that all the areas are connected - over time you will open up new paths (via shoveling debris or burning bodies or events), so planning and executing night runs has its own excitement.There are 2 story scenarios and some challenge variations of the scenarios, where the paths, loot and events are switched around the night map to spice things up.I would say that one scenario run takes about 5 hours, so if you are not interested in the challenge runs and replay-ability, then you can expect about 10 hours of game-play. If that's not enough value for full price, then definitely grab it on a sale!

_childDocuments_.review: I would describe this game in one word: tedious.It tries to be a medieval "This War of Mine", but fails on pretty much every level. Let's start with the mechanics: instead of having to just keep your characters fed, warm and happy like in TWOM, now you have to support the castle's defenders who you never see and are just a background mechanic. This also means there's a lot more resources/items to manage than in TWOM, which brings me back to the tediousness. Resource management is not fun, not intuitive and very annoying. There's simply too many different types of resources to keep track of and the characters' backpacks are too small to handle the amount of different stuff you need to loot. Also the balancing feels off compared to TWOM (and yes, I will keep comparing it to TWOM, because it's clearly ripped off a lot of the ideas from that game, but made them worse).Now let's look at the other aspect: story/characters. The "lore" of this game couldn't be more uninteresting if they tried. The characters are bland and I didn't care about them one bit. This is in stark contrast to (you guessed it!) This War of Mine, which made you care about keeping your characters safe and fed in an unjust war environment. Also This War of Mine had moral dilemmas, "do I steal from this old couple to keep my people fed?", "do I steal from the hospital?", "do I kill someone to steal their weapons/food/medicine?". All this is missing in this game. Here there is a clear "good vs evil" vibe. Your people are the good innocent town/castle being attacked by some evil faceless invaders, there's no moral choices, you don't go out robbing other survivors to feed your own, the only enemies are the faceless invading soldiers, which you can kill, but which doesn't even give you any useful loot and is only a disadvantage, cuz they will increase patrols the next night, so basically the right way to play is to evade them instead and just collect crap from the loot piles all over town, which again is very tedious because of limited inventory space, slow movement speed and short day/night cycles.So overall I can absolutely not recommend this game. If you want something like this, play "This War of Mine" instead and if you already have, don't be fooled by the idea that this game will scratch that same itch, because it won't. It's inferior in every single way and I had to force myself to even finish one playthrough instead of abandoning it right away.
