_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure there's any real replayability here after beating the main campaign in 8 hours.Occasionally either I, or a guard will get stuck walking a path with no way to correct this bug. So the guard will get stuck trying to walk a path that's unwalkable, or my character will get stuck and will not be able to walk forwards or backwards. I've had to reload from last saved point a few times now because of this, it's not game breaking but it is absolutely annoying.Gameplay itself is fun, but only slightly challenging, its a pretty basic survival game, collect resources, and bring it back to base in order to craft new items. It's heavily similar to This War of Mine, and one of the searching sounds I'm almost positive is the exact same audio file from TWoM. It's kind of hard not to notice that the developers are borrowing alot from TWoM, and the game more or less plays like a watered down version.There's supposed to be a penalty for killing enemy guards, where the entire city is searching for survivors and on lookout for your character, but I've yet to notice a difference in either amount of guards or their vision.I think at one point there were supposed to be night events, but the developers must have given up on this feature for some reason. TWoM would have night events where your survivors were raided, no events, Lost survivors would return, ETC. This game always says in the morning, "The night was uneventful...." I don't know why the developers wrote that pop up there, it's just an annoying pop up I have to click to start my day. I kept waiting for an event to have triggered in the night so that this pop up would mean something, or for the night to not be uneventful. ~9 hours into the game and I've got nothing.Major Con:I'm not sure there's any real replayability here after beating the main campaign. You unlock about 9 new campaigns, with new starting characters. HOWEVER: The base never changes, you will always have the same base. The city more or less, also never changes, you start at one of the 3 tunnels, and then have to find the other 2 that after your first playthrough, you know exactly where they are.  The guards routes more or less never changes, the developers seemed to have given guards pretty arbitrary routes so again after your first play through you know the guards routes. The story also seems to never change, even with a different scenario, I get the same intro, the same basic 2 literary choices to start the game. Which to me seems like lazy writing and lazy development. You couldn't at least write a different literary intro that affects starting values of the game for each scenario? I can't imagine it would have taken long to come up with a new paragraph for a new scenario and writing new if then statements to affect starting resources.Don't get me wrong, this is a good game, and I enjoyed it, but it's probably never going to played again now that I've beat it and realized there's no significant changes in the other scenarios. There are "event" triggers through out the city that I have yet to discover and I wasn't able to find keys that unlocked certain events, but the fact that a replay wont let me discover new areas, change my base at all or unlock new literary story choices. I'm unsure if this game is worth more than a 15 dollar game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. It's not very challenging but the dynamic story telling greatly makes up for it. The question of "How am I going to survive the next day" lingers through the entire game with resources scarce and often requiring improvisation and tough decisions. The hardest choices being who you turn down for safety as each story you will be forced to choose. Some mechanics are however very silly. A trebuchet that needs repairing after 3 uses? Having to dry herbs instead of just ripping bandages you don't need apart for fibers. The fact the butchering table has no use as catching rats is a more stable source of meat than keeping your animals alive. It literally is insane resource wise. One unit of rotten food can turn into one unit of meat and this extends to up to 4 meals. So one rat trap with rotten food can feed your full group for a day. But the chickens might lay one or two eggs that might turn into 4 meals with double the firewood consumption. It just makes no sense resource wise.Overall very good. Looking forward to the community content.Would love to see an endless mode with replenishing resources through supply drops from smugglers who drop it on the shore. Perhaps a greater focus on combat. Taking down enemy guards could for example give you free intel. It could weaken enemy moral, not a fun thing to hear one of your mates got shanked by a civie.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: An interesting take on the ‘This War of Mine’ survival as a peon game. Rough around the edges, but charming and interesting enough for a few days. The basic premise of Siege Survival: Gloria Victis (SSGV) is “What if ‘This War of Mine’ was in a 3D explorable space… and medieval… and you were actually important… and it was significantly easier.”We have survived a brutal assault by an invading force. Most of the guard and citizens have been put to the sword and the city is ablaze. Only a few survivors have holed up in the keep and need to do their best to keep the surviving garrison alive and in battle ready condition.By day you tend your makeshift camp in the bastion. By night you scavenge for the resources you need to keep everything going. Find the odd survivor to grow your team, find traders to barter your goods, and even try to take on the odd patrolling guard if they’re on their own and you think you can recover from the injuries. All the while balancing the needs of the scavenger with the needs of the army protecting them. SSGV is not a game for people looking to be the hero, or kick in the door guns blazing. This also isn’t for someone looking for a grimdark and brutal take on siege warfare. While you can quietly take out a lone guard here or there, the combat isn’t the focus.This is a game for people who enjoy stat juggling survival, base management, and the challenge of keeping as many alive in desperate times as possible. I recommend it if you enjoyed This War of Mine, for sure.Overall I give this the thumbs up, I enjoyed the loop and the gameplay. While the game isn’t as good, as meaningful, or as unflinching as This War of Mine, it does a good job of trying to be its own thing, and is somewhat less depressing. It is, however, much slower with more running about.  with reviews by genre. In case you want to find more games, or even reviews, like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice concept, but disappointing.Story and writing was mediocre.The text events were dull and with minimal downside for negative choices. (Might need to apply a bandage and sleep for a day while other characters did work)Scavenging at night quickly becomes tedious with the limited inventory space and easy-to-avoid guards.After the first week or so when you build each building and upgrade them, the days also become tedious. Constantly clicking characters between numerous buildings, with no automation for your characters.By far the biggest disappointment was the difficulty. After the first week the game became ridiculously easy, I sprinted around all night and never hid. Even after being unlucky and having a catapult kill all my pigs on the second siege I had an absurd surplus of food and water from massing rain catchers, rat traps and crops - to the point where I never had to scavenge food/water. The only shortage was materials to craft iron/bricks, but even that was not a great concern as I had enough to equip my men and easily won all the sieges.At the 30 day mark the final siege was the first point I had concerns, as the enemy's force was finally a bit larger than my own and I actually had one of my defenders killed during the fight.. then the game ended. All in all took 7 hours to complete, but I feel I had peaked my enjoyment after the first 2 hours, wish I refunded when I had the chance.

_childDocuments_.review: I am tempted to call this a knockoff of This War Of Mine in a medieval setting because it does copy most of the mechanics of that game, though to this game's credit, they put a lot of polish into the mechanics and thus it has a smoother feel to it. It has a lot of the same design elements. There is a day and night cycle where during the day you are building up your base to make your life easier while during the night you are sneaking through the city and scavenging for supplies. This game adds a twist where you are supplying your local soldiers with food, medicine, fortifications, and weapons so they can better combat the invading enemy. It is well done and a fun experience of waiting out a tense and prolonged siege, though I am keenly aware of its similarities to This War of Mine.

_childDocuments_.review: I just 100%'d this game as part of my Steam Achievement Tidy Up, and it reminded me how much I loved it when it came out. It's basically This War of Mine but you're in a castle. You've got characters with strengths and weaknesses, who you've got to keep fed, watered, healthy and unharmed while supplying a garrison of troops - if you don't keep them prepared enough, the next day of the siege you're currently weathering will whittle down more soldiers or their morale, causing an eventual break and a loss. During the night, you go out and scavenge parts of the city for food, water, medicine, weapons and crafting materials - or stay in bed because you're knackered, all while dodging enemy patrols or resolving neat little choice-based encounters. During the day, you craft various workbenches, repair broken gear, make new gear, feed the animals, cook - or stay in bed because you're knackered.It's a really satisfyingly tight combination of game mechanics that deserves a chef's kiss.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start with this game I am not sure it is a mixed bag but overall I would start by saying my experience with it has been negative overall. That said, out of the gate I understand this game is supposed to be difficult but their is a combination of factors that I believe made it more difficult than they have intended it to be or at least should have; meaning that it is so difficult that it is more frustrating to play than an enjoyable experience here is what I mean:1) There are zero tool tips explaining what the things you can build really do there is the crafting guide that shows you kinda where things come from but how are we supposed to know how often your rat trips will get meat for example? More importantly does the type of food I put in the trap influence how often they come through it because I have never even had one trigger 8 days into building it and every building chain has similar questions I see no way to answer without running through the game 10 times which is annoying because their is no real additional incentive to play this more than once outside of making it through the story.2) Scavenging is just horrible overall worst thing about the entire game for certain; for one you have no clue where to find certain things really the map says "there is an abundance of this or that" in their overviews but it seems to me like generally every single area has the same crap which is spoiled food, wood, etc. nothing advanced or actually useful you'll find a chest in generally every area with broken armors, defense items, etc. and almost universally everyone hates the 5000 clicks it takes to walk through a single area, would of made much more sense to use arrow keys or wsad instead! 3) The "events" at least the ones I have found are all either to save someone and get another useless worker to use up your food/water supply or a merchant which wants to trade you stuff for food that you'll never have an abundance of that I can see to give them in the first place. No real immersion or meaningful exchanges that really impact the narrative or even provide you a response that makes you feel like a choice is meaningful in any way. 4) Maybe this is on purpose and you are suppose to barely survive the sieges at this point but its presentation to me is that I am just screwed once you make it past what it calls the interlude; all of a sudden my fairly matched bastion is outgunned 30 to 45 which it tells you that you'll need to get some advanced weapons or something but I needed to know that 10 days ago not with 2-3 days to prepare.5) This is my last and most important point which is the patrol guards there is a point in the game even if you've never been sighted they are just everywhere to the point you will not want to even bother. The guards aren't that hard to escape really to be honest but this mechanic feels like lazy design with no real purpose than to annoy the hell out of you. You want it to be fun give me the ability to knock them out or hell even better let me use my weapons from the bastion to kill these guys if this is about survival we can become cannibals to get the elusive meat that is impossible to locate.To close my rant, most games that bill themselves as difficult provide you the tools and knowledge to come up with a strategy for how you'd like to approach the challenge that make it genuinely fun to play or maybe an engrossing narrative that makes you really dedicated to making it another day to find out what happens next because you are so into the lore. But with this game we have two sentence monologues from randomly named guards for a story and nothing in way of mechanics that is ground breaking or entertaining enough to make you want to give it more than 2-3 attempts before it wastes away in your library.

_childDocuments_.review: The story starts with a medieval-ish town being attacked what is essentially vikings in that world and it ending with said vikings laying siege to the garrison of that town. And that is where you come in: you're put in control of a bunch of survivors in part of the castle whose task is to make sure that the defenders are well-supplied so that they can resist the invaders until help arrives. The premise that follows then is fairly similar to that of This War of Mine: A bunch of survivors of a war-torn town under siege hunkering down during the day while they try to survive and make things as comfortable for themselves as best as they can and sneaking out during the night to find whatever supplies/materials that they may need while dodging the patrolling guards of the invaders. So far, similar enough to TWoM, aye? However, it's a little more complicated than that here. In TWoM, yor only concern is the survival of your little group of people... But in this game, your concern is not only your little group, but also the aforemented garrison, which you must keep supplied with weapons, armor, food, water and medicine and bandages when the situation calls for it, among other things. So expect having to work a bit harder than in TWoM.Much like TWoM, this is a game that is all about being smart about how you pick your resources and how you handle them. For example, early on it is a bad idea to grab stuff like dirty water, fertilizer and tresure whe´n scavenging at night. Why? Well, the first two will only be of use by the time you have built up things a bit and the last one is only usefull if you know where the traders are which you won't the first time you play unless you've looked that up - and even if you do know, it isn't necessarily a good idea to pick'em up and bring them back with you or use the trader the very first days unless you absolutely have to. But while these things can take a little while to get the hang of, you eventually will grasp it and use it towards making your playthrough more of a success. Also, unlike TWoM, you don't just get access to limited parts/sections of the town  as the game goes on. Instead, the whole town is technically open to you from the start. I say technically, because parts of it will from the start be blocked off by stuff that has to be cleared with either a shovel or a torch and determining which parts of the town to unlock first can also play an important part in the success (or lack thereof) in your campaign. For example, clearing one path could allow you to add a new character to your group while another path could unlock a trader or some valuable resources for the garrison. Which to unlock first?  Assuming you'll even know which path would benefit you the most to open first...The game has two scenarios - one being the main campaign, Edring's Last Stand, which then has some variations of it available, which the player can unlock as he/she completes the first few scenarios, with said variations all having their own challenges and focuses to them. And then there's The Caravan, a scenario similar to, yet diffierent in some ways to Edring's last stand that players can go for once they've completed the main scenario. The option to create custom versions of both of the aforemented campaigns is also there, as is the option of importing community scenarios, so there's a lot for players who take a liking to the game to do with it.All in all, it is an entertaining game, though not one that is high in tension for most of the time. That said, there are come complaints I do have about certain things in the game:- The warnings you get about some of your food 'getting smelly' is, alas, kinda useless since it seems like you can't ACTIVELY select said smelly food and use it before it expires...- Sometimes, when you're trying to ambush an enemy guard from behind, the 'attack' option doesn't appear at all! In at least one case, this seems to be a bug, but for the rest of it, I'd conclude that the enemy soldiers just have a fairly small hitbox or something, which I wish wasn't the case...- Speaking of ambushing solders, it's a bit of a pity that there's no 'attempt to hide the body' option after you kill'em. Yes, it'd take some in-game time and the even in the way I'd like such a thing implemented at least, there'd be no guarantee of the alert-level not being raised, but it'd be a possibility.- It's a pity that you can't actively do much about the sad/depressed condition - This War of Mine had the same condition, but unlike Gloria Victis, it offered ways of cheering up up the characters. No such thing here, but fortunately, the condition isn't all that debilitating, so it's not as big a problem that it could/should be.- But speaking of the above, I'd have liked if alcohol was part of the game, in part as a way of cheering up the characters and improve the morale of the defenders. It could have been possible to make alcohol like ale, lager, beer and/or moonshine for morale-improving reasons among others. Or alcohol such as those mentioned but also wine could have appeared as rare loot that could either be given to the Bastion or to our merry little gang for morale-improving reasons...- The Lost Caravan scenario is interesting, but it is a bit of a pity that it has no achievements to it unlike Edring's Last Stand...So, as a final note: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis is a game worthy of being added to one's collection, but it is especially recommended to those who look for a game similar enough to TWoM.

_childDocuments_.review: So...it's an alright game from what I see. Got it on cheap for the steam sale, and I'm noticing it matches the trend I've seen in some games of: "well if you don't do it perfect your screwed"Main items to let you know what I'm talking about: Shovels and TorchesYou'll find quick those are main items you need, cause exploring town at night is actually how you survive and thrive. You walk around scavenging resources, which at first seems plentiful, but if you don't immediately use those shovel and torches on those EXACT nights you get them, you'll find you run out of resources, cant upgrade, which you need to do, and have to restart your game probably to actually surviveThe game itself is very scaled down much more...you have less control on things. I'll just say it that way. You collect resources, have a straight run, it looks like, and just get resources, use those resources to build a set amount of things with only certain uses per those things. It is a simple game, so its not hard to learn, however, outside of some control over your smarts on what to use your resources on, you are very very limited.You have to feed you, the other guy with you, and your pigs and chickens, whilst you have minimal food and resources, with no way to really get ahead like a boss or anything like that. It's all very minimal. Which, I honestly laughed at in my game cause the beginning of the game gives you a choice in the story of: safeguard people vs resources. I chose resources, and somehow I'm not ahead on that. Its very dumb on thatFor a newbie, having to do a perfect run from the beginning, is not a good game build to me. A newbie should be able to learn, which the game has a good tutorial, and be able to make some mistakes and still be okI'd say right now, one major thing that doesn't make sense, is you can make a torch, you can have one, or have a shovel, and somehow not be able to use it at all in the town you explore at night. You have to i guess have it active in the person's inventory, which you don't have control over for the night. So...major flaw in the gameSo, main point, major problems in the game, very very tight line of what you can do and thus the game itself is incredibly limited feeling so it is a mediocre game at best, with no real feeling of control and therefore real earning of success.For a siege game, honestly disappointed. Would return it if i could, but took me 3 hours to get to this point in the game to realize all these things, so can't.

_childDocuments_.review: This is as hardcore of a survival game as you’d ever possibly encounter and I’ll be honest, I struggled immensely and still haven’t found a way to balance the needs of my people , the animals and the bastion . Speaking of the bastion , that in itself was a huge headache and I felt like it often took away from the game because you’re literally trying to feed 25 men on top of your animals and everyone of your characters. I would have liked to have an option to completely turn off the siege scenario and just play and learn the game before having to take on the huge task of providing for an army of people.  You start with two more but there’s scenarios where you’ll run into different people to recruit them but I don’t suggest doing that until you have consistent sources of food and water because the bastion is extremely demanding . You’re not only having to send them food, water but you need to fix their weapons , armor and make them arrows which you first need to upgrade the storehouse , then make a furnace and then wait for an entire day to receive the materials to make them . You also have to constantly have shovels because there’s tons of areas that are blocked off and if you don’t have a shovel you’re completely stuck which happened to me numerous times and I end up dying and losing the siege as the army fell on day 20 . I will say that the UI is easy to learn and they do a decent job at teaching you the ropes . I did find myself confused at times where I should use the shovel because it’s only a one time use item that you don’t get until you’ve upgraded the work bench and like I said , there’s quite a number of areas blocked off by rubble . If you liked this war of mine , dead in Vinland , help will come tomorrow , you’ll enjoy this . I do wish it was a little easier and thankfully you can customize the game to the difficulty that works best for you and being able to pick how hard the battles are , how many resources are available, your starting characters and they also have many different locations which I didn’t expect but I loved , as well as 3 different story modes in unique and fun environments . I definitely recommend but be ready for a bit of a learning curve your first couple play throughs

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the campaign. As others have mentioned, the game is similar to this War of Mine, except that it is in medieval settings. It is decent fun, and I would recommend it when it's on sale, especially if you enjoyed TWoM's gameplay. It doesn't feel as polished, balanced and atmospheric as TWoM, and it does feel very linear. I haven't confirmed this myself but another review mentioned that the salvaged items you get from each area / spot is the same for each play through, and if so, it would limit replayability significantly. The game doesn't really explain very well how to play the game, so your first play through is likely to not succeed. Also, often times, you will find that the objectives you are presented with will lead you to not to play optimally, so while you try to meet these objectives, be mindful to manage your build order and facility upgrades accordingly. Facility upgrades are crucial as it makes their use more efficient (i.e. higher output / less resources needed to make something). With resource being fixed and very limited, you'll want to eke out any efficiency that you can get. All in all, expect about 10 hours of gameplay from this game. Not bad for a game I paid $2.50 for.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked This War of Mine, you'll feel right at home with this game. The mood is the same, the music is very atmospheric and mechanics feel familiar. You are villagers trapped in an city under siege. During the day you must take care of the needs of your fellow villagers (up to 4 can stay in the castle) and you can craft items and feed the animals which in turn supply you with food. You also have the option to give supplies to the last defenders of the castle, who keep you save, supplying them with food, repair their weapons and so on. You have to juggle the need of your own villagers to those of the defending soldiers which gives an other tactical option to the game, as resources are scarce.During the night, you can send one villager on a scavenging run, where the invaders are patrolling the streets. Should you be spotted, or kill a guard, the guards will send more patrols in the city during the following nights. There are bushes in which you can hide and several loot skites scattered around the city. Furthermore certain places have events which give you the option to trade, or recruit a new villager. You must use shovels to get to other areas of the vast city, and burn poisoned corpses to reach certain loot. When morning comes, you have to get back to the escape route into the castle for if the day breaks, the soldiers will most likely spot you and swarm you. You have to decide if that loot point over there is worth it, with the risk of you can get back in time. You start with one entrance to the city, but you can unlock more entrances during your campaign.The game saves every start of a new day so if you want to quit the game when night comes, your whole progress of the day is lost. Plan accordingly.When you survive 7 days, new game modes unlock and the game ends after 14 days (if I am correct). There is a expansive editor though, which lets you make your own campaigns and edit text-based quests and objectives, etc. Here you can also change the names of your villagers. Just make a new campaign using the original game and edit every PC or NPC. The community will no doubt make new campaigns so that will mean more replauability in the long run. One minor nitpick is that you cannot edit the names directly in the main game, which means as you do it through a mod, the schievements are disabled.But other than that, it is a nice game. It has decent graphics and the managing and choice-making mechanics work flawlessly. I am enjoying my time and like I said, if you liked This War of Mine, you will also like this game. It is great and the Devs are very responsive on the Steam discussion forums too. I say: Don't delay, buy today!

_childDocuments_.review: I covered this game as part of my coverage of the Humble Choice for June 2022This war of yore.Siege Survival is a Medieval tale, where a Bastion is under siege by enemies, and the player has to survive, assist the knights fighting on their behalf, and scavenge goods in the large town as enemies hunt for them.  It’s a concept that made me wonder before I realized that this is just a different variant of This War of Mine.The thing is this is a different take on the tale.  Siege Survival focuses more on a more direct representation of the siege.  Players will give arms and feed the soldiers defending their encampment.  The enemy will sometimes bombard the Bastion with trebuchet fire, and players will manage their soldiers’ wants and needs.  While there is depression and pain, it’s not so recognizable either, and that’s a good thing.  Pick this up if you want a more relaxed version of This War is Mine, or just want a simple survival game during wartime.   Where This War of Mine tries to make a direct statement, Siege Survival is more of a pure game, and I want to thank my follower Royal for that point because it focuses on the difference between these titles.  This isn’t meant to say one is better than the other.  There’s room for both a thought experiment and a game in this space, and in that area, I think I prefer Siege Survival as This War of Mine depressed me quite a bit, though I fully understand why someone might see it differently.If you want to see the video this was taken of, or more from me on the Humble Choice or Game Pass, check out:

_childDocuments_.review: This is a different, and challenging strategy game, and I recommend it to anyone who likes resource management style games.I tried the Demo of this game, and was enjoying it so much, I was bummed when the demo ended.  I promptly wishlisted the game, and picked it up the day it came out.  I was pleased it was reasonably priced at about $20.So far, I'm not disappointed:  I've not played this style of game before (although I've seen other reviews that reference another game this one seems similar to), and I like the different playstyle.  It's a great strategy game: you have to balance keeping yourself and your little team of people alive, versus the needs of the garrison, and the needs of your animals (which supply materials to keep you and the garrison going).The nightly stealth forays to scavenge for materials get much more difficult if the enemy spots you (don't let them see you!) and you have to balance getting more materials vs. the time you have out--and later, vs. scouting the enemy.And what materials you will use as well:  do you keep that axe to defend yourself on forays... or give it to the garrison?  Do you use your fibers to make a torch to burn the corpses in town (that spread disease) or build something new to make more/better items? or repair the garrison's weapons and armors?But if you are still on the fence,  the demo is still there, and if you play the demo, you can continue right where you left off if you elect to upgrade the game...

_childDocuments_.review: Short Answer: I'd argue that this game does everything "This War of Mine" does, but better."This War of Mine" does do a good job at what it set out to do. Don't get me wrong. It's a fine piece of Art, but Siege Survival takes everything TWoM did good, and does it  better.EZ recommendation. Not a question! If you're uncertain, wait for a sale.... Long Answer:Remember when This War of Mine got meme'd on? I do. From small details completely derailing what the game set out to do (The game's whole tone was "War Bad", and during the 2010's when the game came out, that was definitely the train the game decided to ride), to a variety of other reasons, as a result, the game ended up suffering under it's own weight a little, due to War being... well, i dunno - Also, the Muscovite-Ukraine Conflict would kick up in 2020, where Moscow announced their infamous "3 day operation" (now entering it's 3rd/4th year, and as of this review being written, is still ongoing), which, uuuuhhhhhhhhhhh...Yeah. Try approaching a Ukranian and tell him "War bad. Just don't fight" and I hope someone has a camera to videotape the absolute beating you'd rightfully get.Which is also extra ironic, because This War of Mine actually had a fundraiser for Ukraine... which resulted in them alienating their audience, because "War Bad! Context disregarded!" tends to draw in a crowd of people who... uh... are good at disregarding context. So yea that got them backlash for zero good reason.Because yeah, no ♥♥♥♥ Sherlock. War is bad, but as time marched on, life has proven that there are high amounts of exasperatingly diverse (and above all, ) reasons to FIGHT when wars inevitably crop up, .That was the brick wall that This War of Mine hit face-first, and hit so hard, it broke itself on. That kinda happens when your whole game is nothing but "War bad, regardless of context!"Also, we might even start seeing wars over water soon, due to infrastructure being built that would redirect tons of rivers, resulting in lots of people dying of famines in the countries dependent on those currently existing rivers.And let's be real: if the Price of peace is your extermination to feed the existence of someone that hates you for the crime of existing... why SHOULDN'T you go to war against them? You have a right to exist if nothing else!Yes, today we have tik-tok footage of people being blown up by drones with people editing CGI fortnite dances over people dying in IRL wars. Yes, today we have bombs. Yes, today we have guns. But we also have human rights and lines that we at least TRY not to cross.Back then, such lines just weren't a thing. Siege survival centers itself around, as the name implies - Siege Warfare, the game nails everything This War of Mine was going for, without running into its issues. This game does a damn good job keeping that specific horror of war front-and-center, as you play as a bunch of stragglers trying to help the Garrison fight against the enemy in any way you can. Sure, the Garrison and Lords of the Castle ain't exactly paragons of virtue. It's implied that the only difference between them and the invaders is that the garrison genuinely doesn't want to kill you (or at least doesn't have a good reason to).Considering that you are caught in the middle of a siege, and that the Garrison isn't the force that burned your life to the ground and killed people for the crime of being in the wrong place at the wrong time... I'd say that's reason enough to stick around and do what you can to help avenge the life and lives lost at the hands of this seemingly random invasion.Sure, your characters can't exactly fight, but they don't have to. Fighting is not even in your job description (or oath as a serf to the Lord, or however Feudal society citizenship worked. I don't know).All you need to do is scavenge the city for whatever the Garrison needs, so they can do their job until the enemy army runs out of supplies, gets bored, and eventually leaves (which was how you won when being besieged, back in the day).As you search the city, you can just... what the enemy army has done.It wasn't done with bombs, or planes, or modern technology.Remember what I said earlier about pre-Napoleonic war being more horrifying than modern war? This is what I mean: No context is ever given. The poor guy is just  there, because he was in the wrong place at the wrong time.Back in those days, you were not going to get shot with a gun, or blown up with grenades, or killed in a drone strike. Instead, you were  by other people. If you were lucky, you died to shock. If you were unlucky, you got to live long enough to watch them repeat the process to someone next to you.The besieging army committed these acts with their own hands.This War of Mine felt off because everything felt way too detached, the characters felt like massive hypocrites, and very obviously the developers did a good job with what they had, but a lot of things fell flat, didn't fit, didn't land, and then world events would kick off which then lead to the game aging in a particularly bizarre direction, where the entire game feels like you are somehow playing a half-truth, or you were never getting the full context to what was going on.Siege Survival: Gloria Victis on the other hand, everything feels up front and PERSONAL.The enemy army PERSONALLY hung a random dude for the crime of being in the wrong place at the wrong time.The enemy army PERSONALLY locked people in their homes and lit the buildings on fire, where you can find their remains - why? Because they were serfs to the wrong Lord.The enemy army PERSONALLY did these horrible things, and did them with their own hands.The "War is bad" theme remains intact, but now you have CONTEXT. You have a damn good reason to still participate in that war without killing anyone yourself (which is awkwardly true to life), and that is where This War of Mine failed."War bad cuz humans bad" is just another half-truth.Personally, I blame games like Spec Ops: the Line for pushing railroaded "you should feel bad for playing our $60 paperweight" narratives that just  which is also bad because Spec Ops: the Line was criticizing video game violence-heroism that had oversaturated the 2010's market at the time and the entire game didn't even have a war going on - it was just a FUBAR situation where the character Martin Walker has a 4-hour long schitzo episode and drags the player along for a wild ride that blames the player for playing a game that the player spent money on.Siege Survival: Gloria Victis on the other hand gets it correct. It doesn't run into the same problems that other games have, and it doesn't attack the player through the 4th wall for playing it and I love Siege Survival for having the balls to commit to the "War is bad, but you must face it" angle.I want more games that refuse to shy away from how god-awful war is, but at the same time, give you, the player a good reason to fight it. "Get off my lawn" as we're seeing with Ukraine VS Moscow will always be one of billions of good reasons to fight a war - in that case, against a foreign aggressor.As time marches on, we are going to see a "rebellious teen" phase of games that will do similar things and I hope I'm still alive to see it.I don't think the Devs are gonna bother reading my review, but if you do, hey! You guys did an awesome job, I think you nailed what you were going for, and thank you for this unique gaming experience that actually accomplished what other games failed to do!God bless, and thank you for your time.

_childDocuments_.review: A great concept and a good experience. Should only get better., especially with the built in mod support.The game is rather enjoyable and I hope to keep playing additional twists on the theme and mechanics of Siege Survival in the future, but atm what is there is a bit limited to 2-3 play-throughs or so.I would love to see more depth added to the city layer, as well as additional considerations towards longevity of play like dynamic events. What is there already is a good game and a fantastic framework for more stories and challenges depending on how future updates go.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a terrible game, there's just not a lot to it. They obviously saw the success of 'This War Of Mine' and thought they'd make a medieval version of it, but they've left out all the heart and story. It's just busy work for several hours and then it presumably ends. I'm not sure I'll sit through it all, to be honest. I'd ask for a refund, but it technically works which means Steam has no legal obligation to give a refund, and so they won't. I should have bought it on Epic...--Update - I finished it. No change to my opinion, despite the developer having a little cry and trying to guilt trip me into changing it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's sort of 'This of War of Mine' in Castle Defense setting: manage resource at day time, stealthily scavenge at night. _childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to recommend this game. In short, it's like This War of Mine, except way worst. I mean, the idea is pretty nice, but the execution is terrible. You can't be stealthy if your character doesn't respond.It's not a bad game per se, but it is clear that this lacks a TON of polish on the character control side. I guess that for 5 bucks that's OK. So this should be an OK review rather than a negative one, yet Steam does not have such.

_childDocuments_.review: Moddable, kinda infuriating though. _childDocuments_.review: I refunded the game. For nearly 30 bucks without discounts this game has little to offer. the sneak mechanic is fun for a while, but it only goes so far. I just thought there would be more. More to discover, more to build but as long as you aren't stupid or greedy 4 nightly walks are  almost enough to set up your infrastructure.This game is just weird. while some parts of it are beautifully crafted (for example the interactions and the black and white scetches.) others are downright atrociously rendered (castle interior). One last thing which has been bugging me since i saw and played the game: WHICH INCOMPETENT GENERAL WOULD LET THE ENEMY LEAVE THEIR FORTIFICATION DURING A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SIEGE! Seriously the whole premise of the game is just so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid. The idea behind a siege is to starve the enemy out, not let them wonder about .... that defeats the purpose.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: This game is LITERALLY 'siege survival'. You have to survive a siege on your castle and scrounge together what little resources you can, to re-supply your troops on the front via periodic transports... if you fail to keep the troops on the front supplied & stocked, then your castle is overrun and you die. That's literally the game.The game requires very precise resource management and there's very little room for error. Your characters can get wounded and if those wounds aren't treated then they die. Your characters also have to constantly sleep, eat, drink, etc. in order to remain productive members of the castle, or they die.I have to say that none of the time I spent with the game, was enjoyable. , and no fun was had. It's not to say that games like these won't appeal to a certain demographic of gamers (like those that play Dark Souls, etc.), but I am simply not one of those gamers that enjoy this type of tedious game, and so I can't recommend the game. I play games for fun, and this simply wasn't fun. If you enjoy punishing games like Darkest Dungeon or Dark Souls, then maybe this is your type of game. It's not a BAD game, but I simply didn't enjoy my time with it.Here's my 'first impressions' video: For more reviews, visit my curator page: For my full recommended list of games:
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: This is a perfectly functional game that didn't I enjoy enough to play past the first 7 in-game days. It looks like it's balanced enough that the find resources->craft items, repeat cycle would eventually get to the end of the campaign. But it didn't feel like a particularly rewarding journey to go on. The build tree was straightforward verging on simplistic, the pace was slow, the inventory for the gathering runs were too cramped, and it never felt rewarding or fun. It successfully captured the feel of always being on the edge of not having the resources to feed/repair/restock enough to survive the next wave, but I didn't make me feel engaged enough to see the process through. I feel like an auto-loop of "Gather nearest resources, craft into items in lowest supply" would have taken care of most of it without me needing to be there.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Greetings and Salutations everybody!Today we're taking a look at This War of Mine.Oh sorry. *clears Throat*I mean we're gonna take a look at This War of--- dammit!Okay this game is basically This War of Mine but with a medieval setting rather than a modern day setting.Does that automatically make it good? NoDoes that automatically make it bad? also NoOverall I think the game is pretty good. It does what This War of Mine did but it also builds upon it and adds to it. It's also very realistic and logical when you think about the overall idea and theme they were going for. Basically everything makes sense.Everything looks good sounds good feels good and works good.I really enjoyed myself and I intend to keep playing it.This game is a lot of fun but it's also a lot of trouble. It's a very difficult and harsh game. If you're looking for something simple and easy then this is definitely not for you. But if you're looking for a gritty survival simulation game that challenges you and shows the genre to you in a different way then You're going to get a big kick out of this game.I highly recommend this game if you enjoy survival simulators. It's a good one and could possibly become a great one. And worst case scenario if you still don't believe me I have two more options for you. First you can look at my video on Youtube which has gameplay and a more in depth look with more information (link below). And after that if you're STILL not sure, then download the free demo and give the game a try. Thanks so much for reading and I hope I was able to help you spend your money wisely.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Plays a bit like a mobile game; repetitive, yet strangely fulfilling and a little addictive. You manage a small group of survivors defending a keep, helping wounded, gathering food and water, making and repairing weapons and armour and scouring the ruins of the city at night. It does feel like there was plenty of room for expansion, but it never happened, for whatever reason. I wouldn't recommend it at full price, but during a big sale, it's a good buy that'll occupy a fair amount of time.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting game, very simple mechanics but, as you advance, they become complicated. It does not have the same emotional impact as "This war of mine" of course but it reminds that game a lot where a group of survivors has to face every day deciding how to use the few resources available and, often, we continue trying to remedy mistakes that have been made in previous evenings.It's a game with incredible growth potential, leaving doors open to future DLC or scenario expansions with a multitude of mechanics that could be implemented. Really a great job, considering the small team of dev
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: I kind of want to recommend this game, and I absolutely do for people who prefer a "this is my story"-approach to games. Subjectively though, the game bored me. The gameplay felt repetitive and the interface somewhat clunky. I liked the story, but the "game" aspect felt ... stretched? Not sure. The excursions into the city, while interesting at first, got quite boring as well (run and rotate camera until a guard was spotted, walk or hide, repeat). I think I'm just not the target audience for the game. If you liked This War Of Mine or other games that explore the "background" of war and disasters, you should play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Good idea, horrible result. Day: guys walking around in a courtyard, going from one building to another to find out you lack some resource and you can't do what you planned to. Night: some guy walking around in a city, slowly trudging from a garbage heap to another, rummaging in the hope of finding some stuff to complete at least one out of ten tasks you need to do by day. Seriously, I liked "This war of mine", but this isometric attempted ripoff has no action whatsoever, almost all time is wasted and it makes you wish you could betray the city and open the gates to the Ismiri. But you can't.The game is so damn slow that I wasted three hours hoping to find some redeeming quality, and now the time limit for refund is gone.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game, I enjoyed my time with it. It's just the right length for what it does, and you can pick it up and finish it in two sittings, for the base scenario.Pros:+ Good atmosphere, great soundtrack, nice graphic design+ Difficulty is well-balanced, you can bounce back from small mistakes but you're always under pressure+ Scrambling around the map to get what you need and unlock new routes in time is funCons:- I wish inventory capacity wasn't so overwhelmingly important for scavenging runs, I only sent one character out the first few days, then I found another with a bigger capacity, and then I only sent him out for the rest of the game.- If you play well, the last few days of scavenging will leave you with nothing to find. By that point you've probably won already, but it's a little frustrating compared to all the other days up to that point.- Map is static, nothing new happens once you've explored an area and guards have the same patrol routes.Overall, if you think you might like it, try it.

At this  moment this is good game with great potential and mechanics which  need to be futher developed.

_childDocuments_.review: A survival game in a medievil setting. The atmosphere of the game can get one hooked. You try keep your survivors (which includes pigs in chicken) alive. Daytime, you take care of the needs in the castle inhabitants and try to strengthen the defence by supplying the defending soldiers. At night you search for dire needed resources and try to evade the patrolling enemy soldiers. Later in the game you can also support your army with a siege machine. Overall an interesting game to try out.The down(?)sides:The crafting system is quiet straight forward, so you basically discover the possibilities quiet quickly, but just need more and more to support your soldiers and to keep your pupil alive.You can start discovering into every direction of the city. It is not linear. So the difficulty is settling at the point when you understand how to evade the enemy guards best.The game time for the default scenario for me was like 16 hours. I played it once for 5h to get to know the game mechanics. Then I restarted and was able to min/max the early days of the siege. Maybe I spoiled the atmosphere of the game for myself this way, as I had no issues to support the bastion (full weapons and armor, full stomachs) for the final fight, and my workers were mostly healthy. But there are still some more scenarios advertised. So maybe I will try the other scenarios some day for another challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm just over 20 hours in and still really enjoying it.  I purchased this game at the release discount price of $20 so I'd say I got my money's worth, but I would absolutely pay the full price for this game as this style of game play is right up my alley.I played the initial story mode twice through the story mode with the intro tutorial, after failing the first time I learned some strategy and succeeded the second time.  I then proceeded to the story mode without the tutorial.  You learn from the mode choice screen that one of the starting toons is different between the two modes, but once you get in the scavenging town the areas are also different even though the town itself is the same.  These changes make a huge difference in the strategy used to play the game and I failed spectacularly my first two times attempting this new story mode (currently in my 3rd attempt and doing much better).  I was happy to see the change up with the scavenging in the mode change, it really kept the game feeling fresh.My only beef with the game is it can be a bit finicky assigning the characters to their various chores.  Sometimes I THINK i've assigned someone to do something only to find them idling because I didn't click something quite right or it auto-switched me to another toon just as I clicked the action so the action didn't 'take'.  Not a game breaker but it happens just often enough to be annoying.Overall, though, this game is a solid *buy* from me.

_childDocuments_.review: I reset my play through a few times as i worked out a good build order, scavenging method, ext. I got down a good method and was able to scavenge nearly the entire map by day 20. Had the fort fully kitted out with everything except for swords and plate… However after this point the game quickly lost interest for me, gameplay felt repetitive and boring, thus I dropped playing it befor I reach day 30. For the price tage the game was worth it, but I found it rather dull compared to something like “this war of mine”. As another note, the UI was frustrating, commonly i would miss click stuff I wanted to loot due the constant shifting camera while I was constantly having to double clicking everywhere to make him run. Would also at time miss click the faster loot button causing him to cancel the looting action, I feel this could have been fixed with some kind of auto loot hotkey (loots closest pile), a toggle run/sneak hotkey and a loot faster hotkey. I know I have a lot of negative things to say about the game but honestly for the price and the first 15 or so hours of the game I really did enjoyed it and that’s why I’m giving it a thumbs up.

The game has an interesting story, very nice graphic and is move very smooth. Some suggestions if will be ok for devs:- the day and night duration to be longer then is now- a possibility to save the progress when user desire, not only when day/night ends- a system that will give to the player high abilities(resources) or LOW abilities(resources) depending on what he select on the dialog storyAs I said is a tactical strategic game so you have to know all the elements of the game in order to can have success. Not bad game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo for this game, when it was available and  since then I was waiting patiently for the full release. Its  very addictive game that's is not very forgiving on mistakes. One or two wrong decisions and your whole progress will suffer. But that's the fun part. I like the stealth mechanics, the AI of the guards is very well done so even if you are not near them(in their sight range), make loud noise and they will definitely find you. As for the resource management its similar to other games but the siege part is something I really enjoy.Its  fun to  run around trying to evade arrows  and  hits from rocks. Also repairing your buildings from the damage taken during the siege. Aside form the main story there is a sandbox mode that gives us the freedom to create our own scenarios. The art style is great and the gameplay pretty polished (no bugs, crashes and instabilities). Overall a great game in which i spent my night, already 5 hours in and cant wait to play more :D
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Played a couple hours so far and I like this game a lot. it's challenging and definitely different from the standard strategy experience. You aren't the direct defenders off the castle. You control various townsfolk trying to both survive and play a supporting role to the troops defending the castle, you can fight a guard or two but you aren't controlling bad-ass killers just average peasants sneaking out at night to find water food and materials to build and repair things with the next day. During the day you order the townsfolk around doing things like making food, bandages, repairing weapons and armour for the soldiers then sending them out. hopefully that helps clarify what is different about the game as I've seen so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, lacks some detail and could benefit from more features and options. Often compared to "this war of mine" but decidedly lacks the atmosphere. Characters are just tools for you to use and have no impact on the story apart from their skills and weaknesses outside of their intro narrative. The days are very rushed and once you get the max number of characters, it becomes difficult to find something for everyone to do. You can't recruit every character you meet, which is a huge bummer. It'd be cool if there was at least some sort of option to recruit characters you didn't want to directly use, like make them "permanent scouts" or something that at least allows a small passive benefit to having recruited them, and allows you to "swap out" characters. But alas, you must leave characters to their own fate if you want different characters.

_childDocuments_.review: This would have been more a lot more fun if it had some element of combat and strategy. As it is you just slowly walk peasants around, one by one, and click icons to build things. You go out at night to scavenge but again you just slowly walk around and click icons. There's no real challenge, the pacing is slow, just boring really. If this had been a 2D turn based game it would have made the pacing a lot faster and the game more interesting. _childDocuments_.review: The walls and armaments need repair, the morale is low and the castle is in disaray. How long can you hold out? Just a night? Just a few days? Defending at day and scavenging the town at night for supplies, i love it.

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said, the same mechanics as This War of Mine... mostly. A few GOOD key differences: integrated map locations, you can start in one and move to another. Uses an 3d top down graphic style rather than 2d. The Bastion 'support the soldiers' element is interesting but not onerous. The first mission easy and will take about 6-8 hours. From there the game opens up to a second castle and map, and at least 5 variants on each mission, including characters, distribution of resources and the events and blockages on the map. Story was good enough too. The BAD: Doesn't have the same heart to the stories as TWoM. Nor the same atmospheric feeling of oppression. The characters don't seem as diverse as TWoM either - but perhaps I've just not mastered that element yet. Although there is replayability, I suspect that once you get to know the few map variants and variances it becomes fairly easy to drive an easy victory - but the same can be said of TWoM too.All in all, I'm glad I bought it and will enjoy a good few replays - but probably not straight away.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very interesting and entertaining.It has good graphics, intuitive interface and beautiful music.If I had to give you a quick notion of what the game is it would be this: If this game was an act or mission in a CRPG it would make that game absolutely stellar. Defending a castle? Sneaking out for resources to build a supply outpost? Sounds pretty good. The only issue is that this game just has this. No character creation or progression, no actual combat, no party management.. It's just grind and build during the day and grind and loot during the night. At no point you'll gather your party and go back to fighting your enemies.When it comes to the mechanics, it's pretty surface level. Sneaking is just for flavour. There's not much to it. Each area has like 1 or 2 guards that are easy to avoid. You can surprise-attack them but it's not necessary.Building is a bit bland. There's not a lot to build and you'll more than likely build the same stuff in similar order each playthrough. Same with crafting.The story is alright. You have to make some decissions but they don't feel very meaningful and there's very few "events" like that.Still, the game has a lot of charm and it's very well crafted. It also has an editor so that's a big plus. If you enjoyed the base game you can always make your own story adjusting it more to your liking.After having finished the campaign, I think it's a peculiar game and honest about what it offers. So if it catches your eye I'd say it's a solid purchase on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, That is a fun game.  It is a struggle to survive for sure.   I turned the speed to lowest setting so i could micromanage better.  I really liked the story and the layout of the game was very entertaining to explore and advance.   I got lucky and survived a siege.  I almost lost several times, scrambling to keep The soldiers fed and equipped between each attack was a harrowing experience.    A must for any survival management buffs out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Siege Survival: Gloria VictisThe alarm sounds and before you can begin to process what is happening people are running for their lives. The enemy is here and you join the mad dash to try and reach the keep as flaming arrows rain down around you. The town falls quickly, so quickly, and you can hear the cries of the dying all around you, people you called friends. You barely make it to the keep after moving from hiding spot to hiding spot and bar the gate behind you. You can’t be the only one that made it can you?Siege survival: Gloria Victis is one part base building, one part survival crafting, and for those of you who are fans of This War Of Mine, the mechanics of the game will be very familiar. The game does an excellent job at making you feel the desperation of the situation you find yourself in and you must work for every bit of progress.By day you must try to maintain the keep and provide supplies and equipment to the men guarding the wall. By night you must sneak out into the occupied city to collect resources and recruit survivors while avoiding enemy patrols. Time and resource management is critical in this game and it may take a few playthroughs to strike the balance the game requires.Every few days the enemy mounts an attack where you must avoid siege projectiles and hope that the parts of your base that are in the open are spared and the wall holds. The outcome depends on how well you have stocked and fed the defenders of the wall and what repairs and improvements you have undertaken. The graphics of the game are done in an isometric style and done well with the cut scene animations handled nicely too. I am a bit torn on this one if I am honest, whilst the game did nothing wrong, I came away wanting just a bit more of everything I got. I never really felt emotionally invested in the characters and the choose your own adventure style dialogue options did not help with this. Some of the moral choices I faced felt a bit forced or contrived and I feel just a bit more polish here could have really improved the narrative and made the characters more than a mechanic to be managed.The pacing of the game is pretty good and the build during the day scavenge during the night cycle means you are never short of things to do. I did however find it to be rather repetitive after an in game week and wanted something a bit more dynamic to break this up a little bit.The game has a single small area where you build your base and a single town where you scavenge at night. The town is quite large with various sections and would likely take more than one playthrough to fully explore and loot. An average playthrough seems to be in the region of 6-8 hours and there are other options that are unlocked after your first run. That being said, with the same base, map and skill trees I am not sure  that I would pick the game up again, at least in it’s current state, and that’s a shame.If you enjoy this style of game and the ability to not lose a lot of time with multiple playthroughs then this is certainly not a bad game. For me, I found myself wanting just a bit more variety, depth and complexity.It is worth mentioning in closing that a small dev team have put together this game that has no bugs that I have come across on release. They are very responsive and receptive, and are planning to address many of my areas of concern in future updates based on the feedback they have received.This is not something to be sneered at and I will be keeping a close eye on the progress of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm apparently just getting started after 4 hours of this. But it's already an easy upvote. If only for the extremely captivating music, which I'd give a 10/10. It's simply beautiful.Other than the GREAT things (the music), let's see some other good stuff:- Artstyle: 8/10.It works really well. Very informative and to the point, everything is there for a reason, and it really complements the gameplay and the information to the player. All the little information icons on badges or things in the world seem a bit weird at first but once you get to work with them, it's really a less-is-more situation that simply offers you exactly what you need to know, if you know where to look.I do very much like the great drawings that accompany the little side mission dialogs.- Graphics: 7/10.Fine, albeit somewhat outdated/simplistic in the detail/texture quality. Like the weird green fog around a poisoned carcass. But it serves the artstyle nicely and it makes the game really clear. Lighting is beautiful!- Controls: 6/10. It's a bit counterintuitive how to work with the crafting stations and how to manage inventories, and the pathfinding has issues. But as the game has that less-is-more simplicity, it's easy to work with and only slightly immersion-breaking. Also, no way to set paths, queue actions or perform teamwork in crafting (get that just-in-time-delivery pipeline going...) Nothing bad, just could have been better IMHO.- Gameplay: 9/10. Great pounding gameplay with lots of pressure on getting things done in time, forcing you to make choices that really matter in keeping your people alive and productive. The scavenging runs at night time provide a fun alternative to the resource management at day time, and again, both modes complement each other well and keep you on your toes. Seeing that I'm just starting, there seem to be other game modes available to unlock which will probably keep me coming back, if the main game stays interesting.- Sound: 9/10. The sound is almost as great as the music. Lots of things makes little noises that inform you if you just pay attention, which is a detail that can really make or break a game like this.- Voices: 7/10. It's ok, there just aren't a whole lot of them. Most of the dialogs are text-only. Which is fine with me, I typically end up skipping the voice-acted sentences after I've read them.- Tutorial: 9/10. This is another thing that can absolutely make or break a game. I want to learn it BY PLAYING, dammit. Which is what this game offers. And when it asks me to read stuff, it gives me a clear screenshot and 1-3 sentences of clear-cut information, and then lets me play again. THIS IS HOW IT SHOULD BE DONE. I don't much care if it's all voice acted and animated, I just want the world to open up around me gradually so I can play AND learn. Sure, it could have been animated and voice acted *as well* and it'd be the cherry on top, but hey, these developers knew how to prioritize their features!- Storytelling 9/10: the stories are told in the same effective way. No endless back story or pages of lore, just a few sentences describing the character, a few describing the situation, and a simple choice, leaving the whole peril that everyone is in to the player's imagination (fed by the music and the gameplay pressure). Again, these developers are masters of "the art of omission". This is how you do immersion.The "less great":- No quicksaves. If you quit, your day's progress is gone. I guess it's to keep the pressure up, but guys, come on, not even a "save-on-exit" so you can continue where you left off if you have to answer the phone or something? This should definitely be in there.- Yeah, so for me it's not really the "page turner", "just-one-more-turn" kind of thing that many other of these games have. It's like "I'll complete in-game day and then I'm good for today (irl)". Now it's like "am I going to sink another 20 i.r.l. minutes or do I stop here?" ... and then I stop, where a save-on-exit could have kept me glued.All in all, this is a great game, and even if I never play another minute (which I will) the purchase price is a no-brainer for the fun I've had in the first 4 hours alone.It's a game that knows how to make the whole greater than the sum of its parts, and a game written by people who know what's important in a game, and what can be left out and/or replaced by suggestion and stimulating the player's imagination. Like the whole battle at the front, which you don't actually see, but still you feel like you're a part of. It's just good.For me, it has the whole direness vibe that games like Frostpunk or evoke in me, combined with a fun trade-off between a resource manager, a choice text adventure, a city builder and a simplified stealth strategy simulation. It's just hard to describe, and that's a good thing in this case.TL;DR: Go and play this thing. If only for the music.

_childDocuments_.review: The description of the game makes it feel like a free-roaming world where you are scavenging for resources within the walls in order to protect against the ongoing bombardment of the enemy outside. It sounded like an amazing mix tactical strategy and resource management. Unfortunately the actual game lacks many of the attributes implied by  that description that would have made a great game.This is NOT an open world style game. During the day you are confined to a small area (I think it's the "keep") where you can build tools/weapons, prepare food, and/or rest. At night you can send a single character into the city to scavenge for resources. But the city feels very restrictive and clunky. Also, the day and night feel like two separate games that don't meld well together to form a whole game.There is also no variety to problem solving. For example you must use a shovel to get past a pile of rocks to get to a new section of the city. No shovel - no getting by those rocks.Also you have no control over the actual army. You're only supplying them with water, food, weapons, and resources to reinforce the walls. So there is no tactical strategy in the game at all. You don't even get to see the battle!Overall, very disappointed. This feels like an RPG style game without any of the fun parts. Would not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Time moves so fast, the controls are tacky. For example you cannot suddenly stop the character (for example with space bar?) while scavenging. So when he encounters a tacky enemy that you spend half day hiding from (apparently it takes most of the day just to move a character from the safe zone to the hen house to collect an egg), he cannot instantly stop making noise, but the map keeps moving, making it more difficult to aim to click at a nearby bush to hide. There is no pause on either day or night. The characters move so slowly compared to how much of the day/night cycle bar progresses. So without pause, most of the gameplay is premeditating "where to start walking towards", planning it carefully with maps and whatnot, as most of the day could be spent just moving towards a crafting area. Rest of the game is watching the characters slowly craft things. Looking at the craft progression bar will keep you at your toes, because as soon as it finishes you need to start making most of the day to start slowly walking towards your next destination. Speeding up the game wont help and then the day/night cycle progression bar will run and the day will end super quickly.So for one character the day can look like this (if babysitted properly, if you know what he should do and where things are, and if you immediately start moving and don't let him idle): you look if he needs anything, although he can begin to need things in the middle of the day too, he moves towards where he can drink water, that's 5-10% of the day there, he drinks water, then he moves towards firewood making place,  makes firewood awkwardly 1 by 1, that takes 20-40% of the day, then he moves towards cooking place, slowly crafts cookables, unless you need to move back to make more firewood or to get more food. Then the day is probably finished! You can swipe the sweat for now, but alas you had time for nothing else!This game is not a good game, seems to be like an Early Access, but apparently it is a full release. I do not recommend buying it. Unless of course you want to look at characters moving to destinations, and watching craft bar progressions or trying to click bushes to hide in.Oh yea, despite the characters handling like an RTS, the map keeps moving around you, the rotation keys seem inverted, and the is no drag box selection, but you actually have to aim, click and hit to select a character, but if you miss, your preselected character will move from wherever he is to where you just misclicked!Also if you character is doing crafting, and you need to collect the 2 water droplets (to gain more water), then he wont stop the craft even if you click the water thing, but you must first make him move to ground, then click the water thing, then same going back, but you lose the day by that walk alone, moving from the craft to the collector to the water thing. No time to walk to collect the egg! (let alone craft chicken fodder from chicken eggs). In my opinion just skip it, it's not worth the trouble of trying it.If you are wondering if it is a good game, I think it is definitely not a good game. I did like TWOM but even that could have been much better. Seems this game caught what was bad in it. F.e. the day time crafting could have all been instant to the player, without hurry or babysitting a doll house, but instead progressed the day bar for an amount. But instead here we go, babysitting characters again. How lame.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like this game, I did, really. I think the hours speak how much I tried. I gave up a few times on the hardcore mode because while I didn't mind a challenge, I didn't feel like doing the siege again, but harder.I understand, and it wasn't a bad idea to try to mix This War of Mine and Medieval siege. But the problem is, well, you kind of lost the point of T.W.M. when you tried this. That war is ♥♥♥♥, and stupid, especially as a civilian that has no horse in the race. When you're the  of the siege, forced to pick a side, and it's so binary who's right/wrong, the message is lost. It's a typical story of "us vs. bad men" and  where you dropped the ball. The events are binary right/wrong as well, pick the obviously right/morally good choices and your rewards are a mood boost plus a benefit. Versus a mood debuff plus a benefit. Closest to "conflicted" I get to a decision is the rat event where you either go for the food that can make ~12 meals and get lightly scratched or don't. You never talk to an Ismir raider to ask them why they're raiding us, what they hope to get out of it, and what they say to justify it all. You meet one, but he's too wounded to talk philosophy or reason which admittingly did amuse me when I thought of trying so with a notebook and pencil in my hands."Sir, what philosophy would justify slaughtering innocent civilians like myself by the hundreds?""Blergahrgehhhh.""Fair enough."T.W.M. does manage it's storytelling by letting you witness it unfold in front of you, and let you decide who are the enemies to fight/evade. T.W.M. does present opportunities that going bad might make your survival chances easier or harder (rob an elderly couple or pass up a looting spot? If you don't rob them, who will? How low will you sink and how will you justify your actions?). This does not manage it well with guards who are static searchers long as you don't let them hear you, and just become heat seeking missiles when the sun comes up.Gameplay wise, it wasn't . Unfortunately I'd use the word, "mediocre". As I said, the guards are amazingly static and do not change at all unless pathfinding gets bothered by detecting a noise. The only satisfaction I felt in gameplay was just when you make the bar on the siege go to the right, but that might be just my weird brain. Combat is only effective when you ambush them, just like T.W.M. (Unless you have a sword, but are you really gonna do anything else but bonk them from behind with it?)It's weird, an experience that went on for thirty-one and a half hours, and I feel like I'd have more to say on the matter. But I guess because when you beat it in roughly eight hours in the first scenario, that's it. The other scenarios just turn the numbers up or down, and different characters show up in events, but that's it. Just like T.W.M. other than specializing in something (usually) they're not fleshed out enough, especially to be fleshed out for the emotional state to be a good thing.Maybe I should say it on the T.W.M. page, but I might as well say it here too. The emotional state is not a great idea  you flesh out your characters enough that you feel like they're people and it matters to you how you feel. Note down in the log, tell us what we did that's wrong, but don't make other characters be our moral compass when we as players decide how low we are gonna go. It works for games like Fallout New Vegas because those characters have personalities, ambitions, beliefs, philosophy, inner conflicts, and of course, A VOICE! One you can respond to and debate with! But these characters in these two games aren't at that level of depth.TL;DR: T.W.M.'s point missed, be extremely sure you want to try this if you want it.
