_childDocuments_.review: Review -->  Siege Survival: Gloria Victis"This War of Mine" meets a medieval scenario! Here, too, it is important to collect resources in a hostile environment, where every step can mean your own player's death. You also constantly stumble over emotional decisions, should you help, or should you look the other way in your own favor or even be attacked? All of this for their own survival behind the castle walls and to support the few remaining soldiers who sacrifice themselves against the overwhelming power that threatens to break in.In the world of the MMORPG "Gloria Victis" this strategic resource management and survival game plays as a welcome offshoot. A hostile and superior force has invaded the native lands and taken and devastated everything except this last bastion. Behind their castle walls, the few surviving citizens sit and try everything to expand their site during the day, to carry out helpful handicrafts and to repair buildings that are damaged by fire and stone projectiles during everyday attacks.At night they set out to spy on the enemy, which at least can bring small advantages in the fighting, and to scour the devastated city for remaining resources, utensils and possible helpers.In order to keep the interior of the castle "running", food and water must be provided or produced. For this purpose, a small bed can be tilled, chickens and pigs cared for and a rain catcher can be constructed. For better tools and weapons or armor, craft benches are gradually being built and upgraded, and beds are being created to relax.In addition, you can work on a tribok, which is used in defense. Many upgrades are also based on rare finds in the ruins and abandoned houses around the bastion. Trips to the island of pitch cookers to find “ammunition” for the Tribok can also be worthwhile.This will soon create a progress tree and an economic cycle that can hopefully be well maintained so as not to starve to death behind the walls and to continuously support the frontline fighters. Because if the citizens do not regularly provide the soldiers with food, drink, medicine and bandages and repair their equipment, the last line of defense will soon come to an end. Therefore, it is often necessary to put aside your own needs and send everything to the soldiers. But watch out, the animals bring meat again when they starve themselves, but then that was it with the regular supplies of eggs and dung. And when the most skilled craftsman dies of thirst or the warrior with the most extensive backpack dies on a foray because he does not dodge the roaming guards skillfully enough, everything becomes all the more difficult.Fast, fast, nimble, nimble helps at most in the first 2 or 3 days / nights, but then it must be precisely calculated and assessed which resources can be used and how and which risks can or should be taken.Historically, every new day is started with short stories or reports and the current situation is explained, usually by the commanding officer in charge. At certain points in the largely deserted city, there are also event points that require decisions from the player or offer options (e.g. a shorter route through tunnels from the bastion to the market). Many areas first have to be shoveled, as the intruders' fury of destruction blocked accesses with rubble. Good for those who have happily found a shovel or who can improvise one with an improved workbench.If a citizen was spotted too often during his forays through the night (even if he could still run back quickly to the bastion), the patrols become increasingly sharp and the cones of vision of the controlling guards take almost every path, so it hardly seems possible there still to get through.So it quickly becomes extremely difficult to hold out the days until the rescuing reinforcement, as there is always a lack of resources. And if you can't get ahead in the city, there won't be any more supplies.The level of difficulty increases a little too quickly, but of course it also prompts the patient to do more repetitions and thus in a certain way increases the incentive to replay if the frustration does not win.The medieval world is graphically very beautiful and, above all, detailed on the screen and the animations are also excellently implemented. The controls and general operation are soon internalized and the general game processes are quickly recognized. The fine-tuning of plundering and economic activity results in subsequent games, but luck is also part of it. Those who are persistent enough will learn a lot of strategically influenced and entertaining bad hours. The story is always the same, of course, but the course of the game changes a bit due to different approaches.

_childDocuments_.review: Seems most negative reviews are from players who found the game too difficult, and i agree the game is certainly difficult, but thats exactly what i loved about it. If you just wing this game and scavenge randomly like an carefree explorer, you will fail.Compared to this war of mine, i much preferred the gameplay, having to supply and feed the defenders, rather than just getting a silly message at the end of the night saying  "You were robbed and your stuff is gone" which i really hated about this war of mine. In this game i actually felt like i had marginal control over the outcomes of the battles, rather than feeling like i just rolled low on a dice throw.Its not perfect, the scouting was a little too simple, enemy soldiers are like really stupid, easy to avoid and manipulate once you know their mechanics, and also the game ended far too quickly, i would have like to see the siege stretch on 2 or 3 times as long, also some of the objectives are vague, like the one saying you have to repair the boat to leave the island, only to stab you with  a 'gotchya' moment as a sidequest appears after it saying you actually need 3 crossbows before you can sail the boat, which made no sense, and really i should have had some prior warning that they would need such weapons.But all in all, a solid fun game with replayability and actually takes some thought and planning to beat. It plays like This war of mine mechanics wise, but the gameplay and challenge made it feel more like frostpunk, i enjoyed it and absolutely worth the price on discount.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the definition of a hidden indie gem. It's not just a unique idea, but that idea is also well realized.Stumbled upon this game randomly and was intrigued.Then I saw that there was a demo version available for free. Which is something that I greatly miss about current day games.So huge props to the dev team for making the right choice, and (rightly) showing confidence in their product. The demo allows you to play through the first week of the story. It gives you a good idea of the general mechanics, and what the gameplay is like. Some features aren't available in the demo, since they only unlock later in the story, but a majority of features is available even in the demo.That fact alone already earned the dev team my respect.But the game itself is also really fun. Like mentioned earlier, it's a unique take on survival/rts games. I don't know any other game that's similar.It's straight forward, and simple, but doesn't feel incomplete or overpriced. There is also the fact that the devs communicate and continue to update the game, so the future probably holds a lot of things that add to the replay value.Having played for a bit now, there don't seem to be any bugs, so far the game has behaved exactly like I'd expect it to. The game also comes with a fully functional scenario editor, that allows you to revamp and modify the story as you see fit. That editor is also very user friendly and intuitive. Some things require documentation to understand, but even without having read any documentation, you can already do a lot in the editor.Definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Siege Survival GloriaVictus is a game that I find trouble fitting into a genre/category.  You play as some forgettable character that tries to fortify a castle (or a keep or something) from being destroyed and its played from a top-down perspective (its sort of like an RTS but not really).  Your goal is to collect resources such as food, water to feed your "troops" which you never get to actually see (the troops fight "off-screen").  You also need resources to feed your own workers which you recruit over the course of the game and these workers need occasional rest too to be efficient.Half of the time, you play within the castle courtyard during the daytime which is just one big area that can probably fit on your monitor.  The other half of the time you play outside of the castle in the night time trying to "steal" or gather more resources to bring back to the castle.  During the daytime, you build stuff and feed your workers and troops while defending yourselves from the "siege".  During the night time, there is no building or anything, you're just sneaking around outside by yourself collecting stuff to bring back.  In both cases, there is a time component so you DO have limited time to work and setup.The plot of the game is forgettable, there are some RPG-ish dialog thrown in but you''ll likely just skip it all as it doesn't really affect the gameplay other than forcing you down more battles (which are all the same pretty much).  The battles become extremely easy as you progress as the enemy doesn't scale with you.  Once you get your resource engines online with your buildings, you pretty much become unstoppable, and this happens about 1/3 of the way into the game and thats exactly the point in time where the fun stops.  There is no more challenge once you have most of the buildings in place, and the game mechanic just becomes a hindrance at that point as you will have already known you will win (but physically can't until the game "plot" progresses you to the final battle).  So at 30-50% of the game, you're really just sitting there doing nothing the rest of the game just to get toe the final battle so you can be rid of it once and for all.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently had the pleasure of playing Siege Survival: Gloria Victis, and I must say, it exceeded my expectations in every way. This strategic survival game developed by FishTank Studio truly captures the essence of survival amidst the chaos of a medieval siege. With its immersive gameplay, stunning visuals, and intense challenges, Siege Survival is a must-play for any fan of the genre.First and foremost, the game's attention to detail is truly commendable. The meticulously crafted medieval setting immediately draws you in, with beautifully rendered environments that bring the siege-ridden city to life. The atmospheric soundtrack further enhances the immersion, creating an unforgettable gaming experience.One of the game's standout features is its unique blend of resource management and tactical decision-making. As a player, you are tasked with managing a group of civilians trapped inside the besieged city. Your objective is to keep them alive by allocating scarce resources, assigning tasks, and making crucial choices that impact their survival. The delicate balance between resource gathering, crafting, and defending against enemy forces provides a challenging and rewarding gameplay loop that keeps you engaged for hours on end.The game's strategic depth truly shines during the night phases. As darkness falls, the city becomes even more perilous, and you must plan your defenses wisely. Assigning survivors to guard duty, constructing traps and fortifications, and managing limited supplies becomes a matter of life and death. The tension that builds as you try to fend off enemy soldiers while ensuring the survival of your group is incredibly satisfying.Furthermore, the character development system adds another layer of depth to the gameplay. Each survivor has unique skills and abilities that can be improved over time, allowing you to tailor their roles to suit your strategy. The emotional connection that develops between the player and their survivors adds an additional sense of urgency and attachment to their well-being.The narrative aspect of Siege Survival is also noteworthy. The game effectively conveys the horrors and hardships of war, exploring themes of sacrifice, resilience, and the human spirit in the face of adversity. The well-written dialogue and compelling storyline keep you invested throughout, making each decision feel consequential and meaningful.Lastly, the developers have done an excellent job of providing ongoing support and updates to the game. They actively listen to player feedback and address any issues promptly, ensuring a smooth and enjoyable experience.In conclusion, Siege Survival: Gloria Victis is an exceptional survival game that successfully captures the intensity and challenges of a medieval siege. With its immersive atmosphere, strategic gameplay, and captivating storyline, it offers an unforgettable gaming experience. Whether you're a fan of survival games or simply appreciate a well-crafted and engaging adventure, Siege Survival is a must-play title that deserves recognition. Prepare yourself for a truly epic struggle for survival in this remarkable game!

_childDocuments_.review: Check out my video review for Siege Survival: Gloria Victis here: So from what I gathered, Siege Survival is kind of a genre spin off from Gloria Victis, which is an MMO that was released in 2016. That game is still in Early Access by the way and currently the recent reviews are Mixed. But that aside coming from fresh eyes to the IP, how does this game play?As mentioned before, this is a Resource Management Survival game. Kinda think This War of Mine mixed with Real Time Strategy elements. Basically a lot of familiar ideas all mish mashed into one pretty good game in my opinion.To quickly sum up the story, your kingdom is being under siege by a strong rival army and you control civilians who hold up in the castle grounds. It’s up to you to defend the place. Scavenge for food, materials, build farms, repair items, and keep your bastion well prepared with weapons and armor.There’s a lot of scenarios to choose from after getting through the tutorial which teaches you the ropes. These different settings change up your starting characters, how often you’re attacked, resource scarcity, and other modifiers that make you want to attempt future playthroughs or challenges.There’s two major phases in this game. The day phase, which is primarily spent fortifying your base with new structures, upkeep, and surviving attacks; And the night phase which is used to explore the kingdom in search of loot and other special events.To give you a better idea on how each phase works let’s go over the basics of each part. For the day phase, you control characters in real time. You have to manage their water and food intake. If they’re hurt then make sure to have them rest and heal up.You have to spend your time wisely though, there’s a lot to do and not a lot of time to do it with. Feed animals, harvest crops, build structures like workbenches and water gatherers. You’ll also be tasked with keeping your defending bastion fed, healthy, and supplied with weapons and armor. They are attacked every couple of days and a battle is simulated with losses and gains. If they ever lose it’s game over.The second part of the game is the night phase. Here you’ll enter the kingdom map and you’ll choose tasks for each character to do. You’ll have one gatherer which you control directly and the others can either sleep or scout for future enemy base attacks.While scavenging it plays like a stealth game, you have to stay out of the line of sight from enemy guards all while grabbing as many resources as you can in your very limited backpack. There are obstacles that require certain tools like torches to burn bodies and shovels to open paths, you’ll have to prepare in advance what to bring during the day in order to make sure most use of nighttime.There are special events scattered throughout the map which can be a number of things: trade posts, resource spots, and even new characters to add to your base. The farther you go out the harder it gets to not get spotted.Honestly this game is a pretty big challenge the first time around. You’re not going to know which is the best course of action in terms of where to build structures that won’t get destroyed and in which order is the best to upgrade for maximum survival efficiency.There’s a lot of choices to be made and that contributes to my overall satisfaction when playing the game. It’s up to you to decide which resources to leave behind, do you have enough time to scavenge or should you hide because the guard is coming by?This is a very addicting game and the fact that most of it is real time and goes by fast only adds to the tension that the game provides. It could be pretty stressful at times because you’re always sacrificing one thing over another.Overall, This is a fun game and I had a great time with it. If you like real time strategy games and survival like This War of Mine or They Are Billions then give this one a go.  Disclaimer: I received this game for free. I was not paid to promote or write a review. All thoughts are solely my own. Thanks!

_childDocuments_.review: Very accurately compared to This War of Mine. The mechanics are very similar, even down to the epilogue roll. Definitely a must try for those who enjoy TWOM.That being said, I'm into my third run at about 13 hours in. And I've gotten bored. I keep trying to figure out why I can continuously replay TWOM but this 3D near-clone doesn't have the replayability feel. There's a little less story and depth, to be sure, but I can get past that. I think the best part of TWOM was the simplicity - it hit a spot that the mechanics were simple enough to not overwhelm yet at the same time not be tedious. And tedious is what it feels like with the 3D movement and clickety-clicking everywhere to find that one supply dump you missed.A few suggestions that could streamline the mechanics:1) Left and right click each trigger stealth walk or run, respectively. All the double clicking is just carpal-inducing. Or allow the use of the shift key for this.2) More interactive map. See buildings and possible supply hiding spots so you at least have a goal and don't wander all over the town. You could even describe the buildings or points of interest - a stack of hay, an armorer's shop, saw a chest here, etc. And maybe only those chests or special points show up when you go within a far range of it, far enough to see but don't have to go up to, so you're still searching but you can see places you might have missed.3) Add directional arrows to buildings in the castle. So many times I've trapped characters in a slowdown against the wall because I didn't remember which rotation put the front forward.Some variety in the epilogues would be nice too. How many times it said that I had an outright victory in the same picture, same wording. Going to come back to this for sure. Hoping to see more content and easier controls. Great game in the making, and hopefully another blooming studio capable of producing quality games like TWOM hit.

_childDocuments_.review: The confusingly named , which should be the other way around because  is the name of the franchise and  is the name of the game, is a tie-in to the  low-fantasy indie MMORPG.  Other than also being a role-playing game set in the same universe, the two titles have relatively little to do with one another, as  is a largely combatless stealth-survival game.You take the role of a Not!British peasant who has made it inside the castle of a besieged city after the city is overrun by angry Not!Vikings.  While within the castle, you have a short amount of time to both attend to your character's -esque survival needs and construct buildings like workshops, farms, and forges to produce and process supplies.  Those same supplies -- food, water, wood, weapons, reinforcements -- are in perilously short supply, and so to supplement your dwindling reserves you need to venture out of the gates to forage in the occupied city when night falls.The game alternates between these two phases for the entire duration of its ~5-hour campaign: a timed stealth section where you need to sneak out past the Viking guards and raid the city for supplies, and a timed management section where you eat, drink, sleep, and build facilities to process those supplies.  Stay overlong in the stealth section and daytime arrives, making all the enemies aggro you and start homing in.  Stay overlong in the management section and you'll be automatically shunted to the stealth section, even if your character is starving and sick with a broken leg because you didn't fix any of that during the day.Every once in a while, the management game features the enemy attempting to break into the castle with catapults, arrows, and ladders.  The game does not feature combat in these sections; rather, the friendly guards fight off the enemy for you while you do peasant things like run bandages to the wounded, refill the archers' quivers, and put out fires.  It's more like a higher-pressure modifier on the same management mechanics than it is a true mechanical twist.Manage your supplies poorly and fail the keep the guards going during the assaults, and you'll get overrun and lose the campaign.  Hold out for long enough, and you win.  That's the game.Kind of.   is one of those games that I'd sooner describe as 'engaging' than 'fun,' because most of its gameplay loop is about avoiding punishment more than it is about forward motion.  The tech tree in the management side of the game is fairly limited, and very deliberately no amount of resource-gathering stations can actually make your operation sustainable in the long term.  You need to always be exploring more of the city to bring in more supplies from the stealth section; the amount and quality of resource gathering stations that you build in the management half just makes a game-ending disaster into a potentially-salvageable disaster if you have a bad scavenging run or two.  It's not a game about a winning , it's a game about losing slower.The timed element also helps with engagement; each phase is short enough that there's a strong 'one more turn' cadence to it, breaking up the experience so that you don't feel motivated to log off when surviving another day is right around the corner.Needs must be said, it does a very good job at conveying the feeling of being a miserable peasant trapped inside a perilous warzone.  If that sounds like an interesting experience to you, then one run of the main campaign will at least suffice to entertain you for a weekend.A quintessential 7/10 title.  Buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautiful in terms of subject and gameplay. The developers have worked hard so that the game will be difficult. There is no problem since it is difficult, but the game locks itself unless we can find resources and at this point I lose the feeling of continuing the game. Normally, when I'm beaten at difficult strategy games, I can't wait to find the method and try again. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best ressource management games out there. Maybe the best. It combines ressource management, a bit of stealth, a (mostly) plausible setting, base building and worker placement mechanics and everything works flawlessly. (Almost...)Variety among the ressources is excellent. There are enough for it not to be trivial and not too many - you do not need Excel spreadsheets for this one.There are excellent overviews to see which crafting ingredient goes where. Those are compact, easy to read and you get one for each "direction" (input material first, production place first, output first).There is not much story aside from "you are under siege" but there are two scenarios that are quite different.

_childDocuments_.review: A coin toss victory! if i had a chance i would give mixed. It feels like This War of Mine, except it's graphically superior but depth wise shallow. You have two timezone, at night need to scavenge supplies and find survivors and daytime goes for crafting and supplying garrison of soldiers. Yet there are some glaring issues. For example, 14 man garrison requires less food and water than your four people support team. In fact it's around quarter or less. After a week, you can easily craft every station you need and upgrade them without any problem. Give another week and i was hunting soldiers at night and had so many supplies that garrison was returning my packages telling me that they're full. Give or take you can finish this game around 5 hours or so without straining yourself. After the main scenario there are new game+ and custom scenarios if you like the game. IF you like it ofc.

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem among medieval strategy games. This time you don't control the army and you don't fight the battles. Instead, you play ordinary townsfolk in a bloodily occupied town, trying to scrape through. Will you support your soldiers enough to give them an edge? You still need to think of your own food - if you starve, you die. If your soldiers starve, you die as well since you'll get overrun by the enemy. The decisions could be brutal.Base management during the daytime, stealing supplies from an occupied town during nighttime - two gameplay systems are neatly put together. You'll likely be always one step from the death's door and the game does great a job to keep you on your toes. Just one more night, one more alley to 'liberate'...this is how being the ordinary folk could have looked like. Hang up your fantasy swords and try actually living under siege!

_childDocuments_.review: After playing through the base scenario, I still wanted more. Luckily there is a 2nd developer made scenario available with some nice twists in it!This game is lovely for the engineer or master strategist. It also has its thrills however when you get to sneak around the map looting trying not to get caught. It took me a while to feel "comfortable" in my first play-through and that is a much loved feeling! Once I feel like I have everything under control, I grow bored. This game presents challenges consistently and always presents you with new issues that need to be taken care of. Learning the crafting trees was a blast. You aren't penalized too harshly either as dismantling buildings you ended up not needing withdrawals a fair amount of the materials put in back!If you enjoy micromanaging and medieval games, this is a wonderful combo worthy of your 10ish hours.In terms of complaints, I don't enjoy the pace of natural timer. I turn it all the way down most of the day and play as efficiently as possible-- so it gets boring waiting to scavenge sometimes. I'll finish more than a days work in a day and just be waiting for nighttime-- but I can't do that! I still want to manage even though my characters have nothing to do. It's a curse I put on myself I suppose, but it's the only time I'm bored.Inventories being so light at first was annoying, but after seeing how long a siege can last, it was fair! I looted 90% of the loot-able items in the game my first play-through so it worked out well.Lovely game. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis is an interesting game to play it similar to This War of Mine, with some variation aside from going back in time to the Medieval Era. The main concept of this game is during the day you stay inside the Bastion and help try to improve the Bastion and support the Defenders against the enemy forces. At night you go out and scavenge for supplies to bring home while avoiding enemy soldiers. At the same time while venturing out at night you have the opportunity to find new members to bring back to join your team as each character has a different sets of pros and cons (Ex: Bigger Backpack, better fighter etc, gluttonous). The game at times may feel repetitive but overall, it a decent game with decent replay value as you switch up who you recruit and there a custom mode where you can adjust the difficulty level along with different forms of game modes as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: This game has good play-ability and replay-ability. There are currently two main scenarios with minute options that can be changed in further play throughs. I find myself wanting a bit longer scenarios or more engagement with the morale of the Bastions guards, as you play as the civilian support structure that keeps them fed and armed. There are over a dozen characters with their own backstory in which you can have up to four of in any play through in the first scenario and five in the second which leads to interesting choices in who to let in your team. I recommend this game for those who are into stealth/scavenger games or base building. Engaging Developers is a definite plus, still hoping for much more of this single player content to explore the world they have built.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Great resource management / roguelike set in the Medieval world of Gloria Victis. Craft critical resources for your soldiers by day, sneak into the occupied city to collect parts and pieces by night. You need food, water, weapons, and bandages, not just for your soldiers, but for your team. Can you afford to take onboard the trader's wife, the cowardly parson? Lots of hard choices: food is scarce, water is limited, and the clock is always ticking.For the beginner, the instructions are clear and concise, yet they are easily dismissed for the veteran who just wants to get on with fighting. If you're looking for a game where decisions matter, look no further. Siege Survival brings the reality of Medieval warfare home, where the clock is always ticking and where one wrong choice means the difference between victory and destruction.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis is a glorious mash up of what tastes like This War of Mine and some Mount and Blade flavor, all packaged in an enjoyable and visually attractive Survival-Crafting Management game. With beautiful graphics and art as well as gameplay filled with various tasks and a large city to discover and scavenge through as you avoid being caught and supporting the soldiers fighting the siege just outside the castle walls. You’ll be spending most of your time doing tasks and building things and gathering the bulk of your supplies in the night beyond the eyes and ears of enemies patrolling the city. During the day behind a castle wall, you can do tasks that range from eating to crafting and repairing items to tending to livestock to hopefully maintain a passive source of food. Some days you’ll encounter trying to evade potential trebuchet attacks or flaming arrows while doing tasks. Supply the remaining soldiers who are defending in hopes that you can build up the Bastion and defeat the Ismir.The amount of time in the day is short so you have to manage your time wisely. I found myself restarting the game a few times before really getting everything down. There's quite a few things to balance. Some things were not obvious to me. I had daytime goals to help the Bastion but I didn't know where to find it, only after pressing a couple buttons to find out you need to press “B” to bring up the menu and tutorial. I think it would make more sense to have a tutorial before that goal is presented. This game will have moments that feel grindy and maybe repetitive but I think that's part of the nature of games in the genre to get to the later thresholds of gameplay. Sometimes some of the areas that you can venture into are difficult to distinguish on my first playthrough. There are some graphical things that could be implemented. Like for example the area in which you sleep in a bed you've crafted, you just lay on the ground. I made that bed, I want him to lay in a bed!! Really not that massive of an issue but I noticed.  The art styles in general whether it be a dialog screen or the saturated and detailed environments that you sneak around in trying to find goods that will help you on your fight to survive the siege! This game has a lot of style and charm oozing out of it and I can tell a lot of heart and soul went into the production of this game. Because of the way the game was written and designed, it leaves an amazing framework for future and community content in the workshop with already high replayability and discovery. Highly Recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Generous turnout of playtime for your money. good mechanics, nice scavenging bits that switch places with the daytime "base building".This feels very very much like "This War of Mine". It is essentially the same thing but set in medieval times and bird's eye view.One thumbs down for the workshop though. It barely has any (not to mention good) player-made full szenarios - A look at the editor quickly showed why, it is not made for casuals and as such the (at least currently) low player count shows in the barren workshop display.So expect to finish two szenarios, not more. (still, over 30 hours playtime)
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. The first game in this genre for me and I loved it. In this game you scout areas, scavenge supplies, craft, build, farm, fight and generally just try to survive. You play as a rag tag group of beleaguered survivors just scraping by while under siege from a foreign horde of invaders. The whole atmosphere is dark, grim and unforgiving. The story telling and little pieces of the world that you uncover through the various quests add some nice depth to the game. Had lots of fun playing the story and would love to see more content for the current game. I highly recommend picking up this one either full price or on sale, you can't go wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: So satisfying. I love this game.I played a lot of This War of Mine, and this has similarities. Same genre, you could say. Except this isn't a 2d side scrolling game, this is 3d. Fantastic. I beat the first scenario, and working on the second, so more enjoyment to come, just couldn't wait to give a thumbs up on this game. I wish I'd found it sooner!It's just good, and I recommend it if you liked This War of Mine, get it. Lots of great interactions, decisions to be made, and a very satisfying story to play through.Edit: I came back to add a bit more. The graphics are very nice. The detailed textures, roof shingles, sod roofs, wood posts, and so on. It surprises me every time I play how well they turned out. Also, I love how the paths sometimes go under overhangs on buildings, and just where you go shows the care put in to make sure that if it looks like you can be there, you can almost certainly be there. They didn't slack off on this, no invisible walls or "There's nothing there, why am I circling around that spot" going on. Those things always drove me crazy, and there's none of it to be found here. This game should be WAY more popular, maybe Steam isn't pushing it at enough people, but it should be BIG, imo. Over time I'm going to have more hours, both in the shorter term as I continue playing, and when I come back  to replay it again in the future.One final point. It has an "Exit Game" button. Also an "Exit to Menu" button. So when you exit the game, it actually exits the game instead of being 2-3 different steps to just stop playing. I know, not a huge deal, but it's pretty rare these days and I appreciate it.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: A small but really fun game. The gameplay gets a bit repetitive but I already know that this is a game that I will return to a few times a year for the forseable future. _childDocuments_.review: Many games have tried to push a vicious need for survival on people- but then make them gods with too much loot and food.Now, i have managed to get comfy during a few days in, but it quickly gets worse n worse no matter how comfy i get, giving me an all mighty urge to do anything i can to survive.Its a good damn game~
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Always a good sign when the developers release a demo. I tried it and liked it so much I bought the game straightaway without waiting for a discount and I wasn't disappointed.It feels very realistic and, as another reviewer said, it really seems to capture the desperation of trying to survive a siege.The tutorial is very good at teaching the mechanics, but it doesn't guide you to the right strategy to win: you have to work that out for yourself.The balance between the exhilaration of the scavenging phase (guiding a character around a city at night, dodging guards and picking up whatever can be useful) and the daytime building phase in the bleak remnants of the stronghold is excellent. Some say that the game doesn't have much replayability but I absolutely love it and found all of the different variants very enjoyable, even though they are much the same.Following the European siege scenario there's a desert-based scenario. Whilst the graphics are excellent, this scenario doesn't resonate with me the same way as the main game does. It doesn't have the tension of the night-time scavenging, or the bleakness, and there are very few guards to dodge, and I've gone back to replay the original scenario rather than finish this.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10Its great I enjoy my runs and the resource management that is happening Its get way easier in the late game but overall its great. There is no replay ability as the game play is just the same issue to tackle, same map, same spawn points but with a bit tweaking. Its fun the first 2 run but after that it become too repetitive and easy.I play a total of 30h  for achievement but generally you can finish the game around 4-6h for first time playersShould you get it ? Sure man go get it if you have $10 to spare but honestly Id rather spend on "This war of Mine" for a cheaper price and more value

_childDocuments_.review: Glory To Midland, The Bastion shall not fall ! This is a decent game. It's not perfect, but it's still good. I had fun through my run but i can say there are things that don't "work".Many people compare the game to This War of Mine and , i won't lie, it's a very similar kind of game, only in top down 3d environments. And that makes moving around sort of a pain in the @$$. Many time i ended up clicking on what looked like the road to advance to get that weird noise notification that i couldn't move there. The decor also doesn't turn "transparent" when it's between the camera and your character so while you are passing through say, a gateway, you end up having to readjust your camera on the fly to be able to keep advancing.   Combat and Killing Patrols in the city is pointless (and potentially bugged ?), at least in my run. The few patrols i killed Instantly raised the watch level of neighboring zones AND added Patrols the Second the guard was dead. I would've understood it to happen the next night, but passing the marketplace (which is empty), killing the guard in Golden Corner, coming back through marketplace and running headfirst in a patrol that was never there at the beginning of the night felt cheap.  Nightime raids feel too short. You barely have time to go from Point A to point B and then have to run back to the bastion. Those might just be personal gripes, but i feel they hold the game back slightly . Still would recommend it as a nice "medieval" survival manager.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent balance of resource management and just enough of a knife-edge balancing act to work. The atmosphere is solid, the story does enough to feel oppressive but not overdone, and it forces you to think about what you really need to gather each night to keep progress going.My only critique would be the building cover system. About 1/3 of the space for buildings is "safe", and can't be hit by enemy threats. The rest is vulnerable and can be. However with careful placement I was able to fit everything into the covered area, with only my water collector and a compost head left vulnerable. It's a very minor point, but a different arrangement of the space might have forced me to build more in that area.This minor quibble aside, I would happily recommend this game to fans of games such as This War of Mine, with which it shares a lot of mechanics. Thoroughly enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Challenging survival game with a lot of gameplay and UI similarities to This War of Mine. It took me a couple of playthroughs to get familiar with the time and resource management, and I'd recommend a 'story mode' run to learn the map a little and the timeline of events so you can plan more effectively. Note: you won't be starting in the same place every time, so learning the map doesn't make it automatically easy mode. Nice to see they have more challenging options and customizable scenarios right from release, and I liked the breakdown at the end letting you know how much you've still got to build and discover - good motivation for another playthrough ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Good resource management/crafting game. Love the resource gathering phase at night, and how it translates over to what is happening during the day. Well there is no direct combat the game manages to keep you on edge with the coming siege attack every few days. Keeping your front line soldiers fed and crafted up with weapons,armor and bandages becomes a issue as the siege goes on.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

It's still very enjoyable and the new setting is interesting.  The click-to-move controls are a bit wonky, leading to unintended running during scavenging. _childDocuments_.review: Saw a lot of negative reviews but loved TWOM (people drew similarities) so I watched some Let's Play videos prior to purchasing. Looked great so I picked it up and was very glad I did. 10.2 hours in 1 day playing it and after a couple restarts have a firm grasp of the mechanics and now that I do it is very fair. _childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: Stunningly engaging game with a simple formula. They managed to suck me into caring about the Bastion soldiers and wanting to do my best for them with the simple storytelling of drawings and written text. The base building resource management sim of the days and the Thief-like sneaking at night is a great combo that repeats at a perfect interval to keep both from getting stale. Tutorial is extremely well crafted to teach about the ins and outs of the mechanics without overwhelming you. The granular control you have on settings for further playthroughs is also great. If you like resource managers or survival of any type, you should try this game out. It's a good deal for the price especially.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed "This war of mine", you are likely to like this one, as they are very much alike. You play as a small group of civilians trying to keep the garrison of a besieged castle fed and supplied in every way to allow them to withstand assaults on the castle. This means you need to produce food and water, repair armor and weapons, craft arrows, craft more weapons, craft better weapons, craft more armor, craft better armor and so on.At the same time you need to keep your civilians alive as well, as you need them to keep the supplies flowing. So at times you have to prioritize, does the garrison or you go hungry for a day? Do you use the iron you just found to make arrows, or to upgrade your civilian buildings? The game is divided in two major parts, during daytime you upgrade inside your castle, build water collectors, foundries etc, and make the supplies needed by both civilians and the castle defenders.At night, you chose which civilian will scavange the surrounding city while trying to avoid the besiegers, which civilian gets to sleep in bed? And who do you send out to scout the enemy positions?The game has several modes, including a "create your own", so you have some choices as to how your game will be. Hint : finding and clearing hidden paths to the various entrance points to the castle is quite important as the night is not long enugh for you to always take the long route through the city.
_childDocuments_.name: Siege Survival: Gloria Victis

_childDocuments_.review: So I recommend this game, but with some caveats.While the gameplay loop and general mechanics are very similar to "This War of Mine", this is not as polished of a game. Especially the "explore the city" looting aspect. It feels like I'm playing a game from the early 00's in how clunky the character movement and navigation in general are handled. It's extremely frustrating when you face consequences (detection) because you are fighting the game. The near-isometric movement was mastered decades ago, yet this game wasn't able to implement it effectively.However, I really love the direction they have taken the template of "TWoM". I really liked the base-building and overall "supply your defenders" aspect of the game. It's more than just your own personal survival, you have to keep your troops supplied so they defend you. This creates a lot of opportunity for new resources, items, etc. I would love to see this general revisited with a AA budget as I think there is a ton of potential. However, I'd only recommend it for those who are familiar with, and enjoy, this type of game.

_childDocuments_.review: So far the game is great, bug free and runs smoothly. I like the combination of stealth scavenging, base building and survival. _childDocuments_.review: I really liked "This War of Mine" where it shows the perspective of the common man in war and this does the same for medieval times. It's quite good, the atmosphere is very effective; I've never played the MMO this is a spinoff of, but I might now. The gameplay is a little clunky, if there's a way to tab through your characters in the Day mode I haven't found it and I found myself constantly clicking the wrong character. The perspective is good but sometimes it blocks the UI (When trying to tell different people to sleep, unless you move the camera, it's constantly getting in the way of itself.) In Night, the Camera also can be a small issue, but mostly only when going under archways. But overall it works fairly smoothly. The story and themes are pretty good. A few things don't seem matter, for example, I'm not sure what picking the general in the opening set of decisions does, morale drop perhaps? But we never hear about him again and it seems like he'd deserve a mention. On the whole, I really enjoy the game and once you unlock NG+ it's a lot of fun to mess around in.

_childDocuments_.review: You loved "This War of Mine" and were eagerly waiting for some more goodness with the same survival/crafter-formula? Well, wait no more and get Siege Survival. :)As others said before, it is obvious where the roots of the game lie. But it still adds some personal touch.Most notably: the Scavenger Scenes take place in one big interconnected city. You have to decide for yourself how you progress through this city, which blockades you remove and which route you will take. The game offers various scenarios, featuring different placement of items/passages/events/etc, which make for a somewhat fresh experience in every run.Well, yes, I have to agree to the negative reviewers, who say Siege Survival falls short on story, depth and moral choices, compared to its spiritual ancestor. Also the game plays pretty much the same, once you have figured out the buildings, the gameplay and some survival tricks ... but hey, TWoM wasn't a lot different in that regard. ;)The limitations in ressources still make it a decent challenge and the design of the medieval city has its charm in its own right.Decent ... yes, thats a good summary. Siege Survival is a decent experience if you love the TWoM-Formula or want to try something new in such a medieval setting.No "game of the year"-thumbs up, but a solid one indeed. At least for my taste.

name: DAEMON X MACHINA
detailed_description: 'Welcome to your battlefield.' You are an Outer, a new breed of human being that appeared in the aftermath of the Moonfall calamity. As a mercenary for the Orbital organization, you are on the front line of a desperate war for humanity's survival against the Immortals—corrupted AIs that have rebelled against their human creators. Piloting a fully customizable mech known as an Arsenal, you must team up with mercenaries like yourself and complete missions to defeat the Immortals once and for all. But be careful—in a war fought by mercenaries, today's allies can become tomorrow's enemies. From the visionary minds of Kenichiro Tsukuda and trailblazing mech designer Shoji Kawamori comes a new generation of high-speed mech action combat. GAME FEATURES Soar across the battlefield and engage in frenetic, high-stakes mech combat against corrupted machines and gargantuan Colossal Immortals. Fully customize your Arsenal mech with a variety of weapons and parts to your exact specifications. Salvage defeated enemies for parts and weapons, which you can use on the fly on the battlefield. Customize your player avatar with a variety of cosmetic options. Go under the knife and receive extensive body modifications to learn new skills at the cost of your human appearance. Team up with players in online Co-op Mode to destroy bosses, or take on Exploration Missions together to map Immortal bases and unlock powerful gear. Battle other players in 1 vs. 1 or 2 vs. 2 Versus Mode and climb the leaderboard rankings to become the top mercenary.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this after having completed the story campaign. Haven't played any of the multiplayer elements, and don't really plan on doing so. I have had some basic experience in older Armored Core games, so I may make a few comparisons to that series.Solid. A lot of the fights are well paced, with basic AI enemy fights being quick and destructive, Arsenal fights being fast but with an emphasis on being evasive to avoid missiles and other enemy fire, and the Colossal Immortal fight being slower with more predictable patterns.The only fights I found lacking were the Colossal Immortal fights in the story. While they did carry a Monster Hunter vibe, Monster Hunter adds a lot more subtle variety into most large monster attacks which require similar adjustments. Daemon X Machina has some variety but you don't really have to adjust to the enemy's attacks that much; just keep wailing away at armor and expose weak points. The only interesting one I could find was the fight with Rebellion, but only cause you could pick up his sword after blowing out his right arm's weak point and smack him with it for huge damage.The Arsenal fights are more entertaining. You have to keep up on your toes and manage your Stamina well in order to keep damage low while dispensing more of it yourself. It definitely feels "Armored Core"-esque and without the tank controls to manage, there's a lot less frustration early on with movement.Good customization options for your Arsenal, but the way the progression is mapped feels kind of odd. I like the variety in the arms, which are more calibrated towards what weapons you plan on using, but the rest of the armors feel lacking. Maybe it's more interesting for PvP oriented players.The weakest part of this game by far. The main plot of the game is understandable, but the smaller plot points lack a lot of the punch they need and the character cast is quite bloated. In particular, certain Reclaimers will mention that they "Have died several times before" in a offhand comment, and some characters question them about it, and then the subject will get dropped after the mission with them is done. Later, a mission will come up where you discover where and how they get revived, but once the mission is over, no one brings the technology up or says anything about it. Something like this should be ground breaking, but it's treated as something that just happens. Its doesn't seem very well thought out and feels added in as thematic filler.As for characters, a lot of their interactions between missions feel ... disconnected. Shooting an Arsenal down doesn't affect your relationship with them through the main story, and often times you'll find yourself fighting one bitter pilot one mission, only for them to be chums with you the next. This happens twice, with Johnny G early in the game and Savior towards the middle. Both of them express some sort of disliking towards you during or after a mission and then suddenly it's gone next time you see them. The only characters who seem to have consistent personalities are Grief, BG, and Guns Empress, and it's no wonder since they're central to the main plot. The story needs to be expanded more. I wouldn't mind the campaign taking double or even triple the time to complete if it meant getting missions where the supporting characters are fleshed out more and where plot points feel a little bit more connected.One thing I liked about the story though were some of the small choices you could make throughout the missions, which would influence how certain missions played out. Some of these are plot important and change what rewards you receive, so i will leave these out as spoilers.Really good. Really intense rock songs with a little techno feel to them. "Grief", "Shell", and "Mercenary Life" are the one I thought stood out the best.Overall a good game. I'd definitely recommend it for the gameplay, but if you're looking for a good story you'd be better off buying something else.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I saw a lot of promise with DxM and to be fair, I wanted an AC game on PC, and ignoring the aesthetic difference and ugly shadowing on faces, I got what I wanted plus more... but after getting familiar with the game theres SO much that doesnt make sense at best, is broken at worst.If youve never played Armored Core, this is a 15 story that is similar to other mystery heavy Japanese stories in that it is incoherent until the very end, but has some very satisfying, fast paced, mech action gameplay with a decent ammount of customisation, and theres plenty of extra things to do afterwards, but for w/e reason its near impossible to find a MP game.If you were conned like I was by New Gundam Breaker being a PC game and were traumatized by its controls, fear not! PC controls are excellent and remapable.If youre familiar with AC, this is a mix of AC 3 and 4, where the mechs can fly permanently, you can boost to high speed in some designs and you have a lot of older, AC 3 style design elements, such as the enemies and underground levels, you'll definitely get a nostalgia trip no matter what AC game you played as long as youre not expecting AC 5.Before I talk about the issues heres the the  The game is less than perfect, it has bugs and strange issues that will likely never be fixed, but if you want an AC game or a fast paced mech game where you can use some quality PC controls you will definitely get your moneys worth, and I hope we get a sequel direct to PC.Now let me talk about the problems... first and foremost, there is a bug that makes at least flame throwers under powered, its tied to the frame rate as it does damage very quickly and so if youre playing above 30fps youre quite disincentivised from using flamers, and it might even carry on to similar weapons such as the tesla and beam weapons but who knows.I'll preface this next paragraph by saying if you dont care about min maxing in a game where you can easily run out of ammunition in some boss fights (so you should), you can skip it.Next problem is the stats and balance, you have several variants of each weapon, the problem is that these arent standard across the weapons, so while all "L" variants have reduced damage and increase ammunition, these are hand picked values that dont match each other, so while arm weapons that are "L" variants all have -8% Damage, -24% Bullet/Laser Damage and +20% ammo, the generally desired end result when choosing a weapon of "Is this boss going to die before I run out of ammo", will be different for each and every weapon, then the values change again when youre outside of arm weapons, as shoulder weapons of the "L" variant have around -14.8%, -34.5% and +33% respectively.Honestly, in general, weapon stats make no sense, especially melee weapons, you have outer upgrades (which are upgrades for your actual character) which say they increase "Melee Range" but they dont seem to effect melee weapons "Charge Range" which is the closest thing thats actually in the game because "Melee Range" isnt, or having arms that have "Melee Support" which only decreases the cooldown of melee attacks, that is if you arent using particular melee weapons... or if youre not duel wielding... its all vague and inconsistent and no one really knows what actually does what completely.One thing that Armored Core actually got right and Daemon X Machina didnt here is that in AC you could bring up a help tool tip for each stat to explain what it actually did, and in general there were no strange exceptions and stats done what you expected them to.Let me talk about Laser weapons... boy do they make no sense... they in general arent particularly better than ballistic weapons in any way except generally having no range drop off for damage, not a very exciting benefit when Assault Rifles have quite nice range and the majority of heads wont let you lock on far enough to care unless you use SMG's, so its not much of a benefit compared to the disadvantage of it costing you "Femto" to fire, which is a resource you passively generate and can actively increase generation by staying in specific areas on certain maps, and you use this resource for other more important things like having a body double of your Arsenal that seems to actively attract attention away from you and does full damage with all the same weapons you have, so it tanks for you doubles your damage, pretty useful compared to not having a damage drop off you never worry about.I have some smaller gripes like, I wish there was a greater variety in parts... where are my tank, hover, quad and reverse legs... or blade and missile arms, gatling guns, and hand held missile launchers... what about the mechanics that were overused in AC5 that made playing a heavy AC fun such as legs that had armour for heavy weapon stances and those heavy weapons... when you look at the list of railguns you have and realise there is basically one 1 railgun in the game... how you cant customise the glow colour of your mech because "its Femto derp!" but the flames produced from that red glowing thruster are blue... metallic colours being an uncustomisable monotone option that you have to unlock individually... you having to rebuy all your Outer upgrades after paying $20k to reset them... the shop... omg the shop its just confusing... being completely dropped from an online lobby because your internet died for a few seconds... there being no online lobbies for w/e reason...In the end, DxM is a good game that suffers from some port issues, it doesnt bring over everything that made AC great over the years, but it brings enough new things to make it stand out.I hope we get a sequel and I hope it adds some of the really great features of Armored Core from over the years such as the Arena and the particular parts that arent in DxM that I mentioned before.

_childDocuments_.review: The 74 score on metacritic seems appropriate. It's a game you really want to like but there's quite a bit holding it back. The customization is cool and the fights with giant immortals are pretty fun and have a sort of Monster Hunter feel. That said, the game's seriously lacking in some areas. The weapons are seriously lacking in any sense of impact. If I'm piloting a mech carrying an assault rifle that would splatter a man if you so much as dropped it, I expect a thunderous report, not a soft "whumph whump whump" like someone hitting a pillow. Other weapons aren't much better. A lot of the escort missions are downright awful. The first free escort mission has you escorting three cars with basically no health that get instantly destroyed if you even brush against them (Not an exaggeration. They literally explode if you touch them and to add insult to injury you start the mission right behind them so your first time playing you might just accidentally take out one or two of them simply because you made the mistake of boosting forward).Finally there's the controls. For the most part things handle fine but swapping weapons can be outright annoying. It shouldn't be complicated. You've got weapons for each hand and then weapons for each of your two "pylons". You'd think it'd be straight forward right? You'd think it'd be a simple matter of hitting one button to switch between your left hand weapon and your left pylon and then another button to switch between your right hand weapon and your right pylon right? Wrong. First you gotta hit z or c to select a pylon, then hit z or c to choose which hand you want to swap that weapon to. In the heat of battle this can be extremely annoying as you wind up trying to juggle your weapons around trying to put them where you need to go. It's stupid and could be simplified immensely by just having one button for each.Lack of weapon impact, awkward weapon swapping, and annoying escort missions aside, I've still be able to get a fair amount of enjoyment out of the game and it's enough to scratch the itch for mech building that some of the more recent mech games have failed to deliver.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's another Armored Core vet review of DXM: I didn't like it.It was gifted to me as a birthday present in the hopes it would fill the void after FROM abandoned us old fans, after all there's one or two AC devs in this team. I started playing co-op with a friend right away and was immediately taken aback by some bizarre choices like a pilot editor and mission hub similar to Monster Hunter. So we start some missions and it's the same explore factory mission over and over. Turns out you're supposed to play single player first, so why allow us the co-op? It just caused confusion and frustration.Everything from the recycled sound design and generic metal music, to the weightless gameplay and shallow customization left me upset that  was supposed to be some bastion of hope. I took a break for a few weeks and came back to it determined to keep trying it, so I started story mode. The human characters were a mistake, all this addition did was allow for more cutscenes and dialogue - something DXM needs significantly less of because holy crap does it bombard you with character introductions and cutscenes, all of it can even happen mid-mission. Real pacing issues in this, so after meeting like the 10th person and hearing the same dull voice acting, I just started skipping everything. The story isn't even interesting either, something about a rogue AI from the moon taking over Earth tech.I'm sorry, I really did try to give it more time because I desperately wanted to like DXM. Armored Core is a very special franchise to me since I grew up with the entire series, even playing the AC1 demo on those PS1 Interactive CD Samplers. I've grown to despise FROM, but I also miss AC and was hoping this could fill that void. Not by a long shot, visuals are nice though.Armored Core is dead, mecha is dying. I wish it wasn't, but I have to accept this and move on.Edit: Forget what I said, Armored Core is not dead. I'll see you all in Armored Core 6!

_childDocuments_.review: Daemon X Machina is mech combat game that has varying degrees of quality overall but has interesting gameplay that I have not seen much of in recent years. Nonetheless, I do not recommend this game, especially for it's 50 dollar price tag. (I bought it during a sale which lowered it to 30 dollars). This isn't to say the game is devoid of fun but... 50 bucks is a high price.Daemon X Machina takes place on a ruined earth where humanity is forced into walling themselves off from the outside due to a fatal material known as "Femto". This material came to be when fragments of the moon crashed into the earth and strangely enough, this material even made A.I systems turn onto their human masters. In the game, you play as an Outer, a person who went through various medical surgeries to become immune to the Femto material but aren't considered human anymore. As an Outer, you sell your services to various companies while piloting an "Arsenal", your mech. You can also meet other Outers with many of them having their own world views and ideas of what will happen after the A.Is are defeated, of course, some are just in it for the money. Positives-The customization and armors available for your mech is vast and plentiful, combining that with the weapons you're able to hold, you'll be spending a decent chunk of time in the garage. This doesn't take in account of paint customization, decals, and Outer customization that you can play around with too.-The art direction is pretty unique as many mechs have small details or gimmicks about their design-Gameplay is tight and combat encounters can be varied, you'll feel like you're traveling as fast a bullet once you get in the groove.-The music is pretty good, I enjoyed many of the tracks with some of them standing out among others.Negatives-Many of the mech parts are physically similar, parts such as quad legs or estranged arms would've really helped in customization and style but your mech will look humanoid no matter what you do. -Although there are some standout missions, there are also an equal amount of "this sucks" sort of missions, especially with how jank some of them are.-You are able to customize your Outer but some upgrades will override the visual appearance you chose, leading to a "Should I look good or perform better in the battlefield?" situation. This can vary as you might end up liking the cosmetics but an option to not undergo visual changes would be nice, even if it costed in-game money.-Some soundtracks are in lesser quality than others, with some generic tracks being played over boss fights. Sometimes it's understandable but when there's a special event going on in the story, it gets a little annoying to hear the same track you've been hearing over and over again.-Characters have varying degrees of quality, some being ok, meh, and then very bad or annoying. Some character tangents don't really get brought up again or are resolved weirdly and how they resolved everyone felt tiring. On an off note, this game does have dubbing and it's what you'd expect from a indie type game.-Minor spoilers, nothing too serious. Daemon X Machina, after my gripes with it, turns out to be a good game with frustrating story beats and missions. I want to give it a thumbs up and say that I enjoyed the game, but I cannot deny that I felt like I was slogging through the game at times. I hope that the developers are able to make a good sequel or at least lower the price of this game, but until a sale or the game cheapens, you should avoid buying this game at full price. Perhaps in the future I may come back and reverse my review, but I cannot help but doubt it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR version - Do you remember a little anime-as-hell mech arena combat game on the original Xbox called ? Did you like Phantom Crash? That's how you start a Steam review, with OG Xbox deep cuts. Anyways...As far as ports go, this one is functional. The UI is clunky with no mouse support, so be prepared to keyboard shortcut your way through everything. While the game's graphics options are limited, it does support large displays and high refresh rates (I'm running 1440p @ 120hz). The port otherwise seems stable, and performs well (largely due to it being a port of a Nintendo Switch title originally meant to run on middling mobile hardware) mostly cause it's not a very demanding game. So long as you aren't running on integrated graphics, it is still an Unreal engine title, you should be more than fine. The cell-shaded aesthetic looks good, and mostly covers for the decidedly low-polygon models used throughout the game. No crashes, bugs, or other major performance issues to speak of.Do you like anime? Cause this game is anime as hell. The game itself is super light on story, and leans heavily on anime tropes for visual and narrative shorthand. All of your favorite (and most hated) archetypes make an appearance to dump either exposition or trade banter back and forth around your very silent avatar. There is a fairly robust level of character customization, that can be entirely altered (including gender swapping) with an amount of in game currency; so if you ever get bored, a makeover is just a few credits away. Anyways, something about killer AI's and a chunk of the moon exploding and crashing down to Earth, and now competing corporation nation-states fight each other and the AI for what remains of this post-apocalyptic hellscape. How do they fight each other? With giant robots piloted by mercenaries, of course. Why do you care? Doesn't mater, you wake up from a cryo-pod thingy and right into your new day job as a mercenary pilot that everyone incessantly refers to as 'Rookie' (get used to it).But who care's about that, you're here for some hot mecha on mecha action! Well, there's some of that. Enemy mechs, called  in DXM, are few and far between, compared to the legions of drone tanks and attack craft you'll be destroying. But as you progress, you'll unlock more systems for progression, and acquire more gear. Either by researching new gear, buying it, being rewarded with it, or even scavenging it from the burning hulks of destroyed Arsenals in the field. Missions mostly consist of a closed off chunk of the environment, effectively creating a sizable battle arena for the mission to take place in. And yes, I do mean arena. You aren't out on patrol, moving over a large space, waiting for things to happen or for a story beat to play out. You are just selecting a mission, watch the cavalcade of anime tropes show off their archetypes to one another during the pre-mission briefing, then you drop down into the combat area with a specific objective to accomplish. You might get additional objectives that change during a mission, but for the most part, you aren't going to leave that area until the mission is done. Fortunately the combat, and the mech customization that facilitates it, is pretty entertaining. Again, if you remember the fast and nimble circle strafing and lock-on management of , you'll feel right at home. Except now, you're in third person, and you can basically fly at will. Also, if your Arsenal gets too damaged you can eject and try to make a comeback, if your pilot can manage to commandeer another Arsenal. You have a selection of weapons available across a number of different equipment slots (left/right hands, secondary left/right hands, wings, and shoulders), in addition to swappable body parts for the Arsenal itself. It has what you'd expect, managing a capacity limit for your gear, and parts that differ in how they balance offense, defense, and mobility. Want a fast and nimble scout? Want a lumbering tank of a weapon platform? Want a chunky melee brawler? Have fun! Your options will open up as your arsenal expands, and it always seems like you're getting something new to play around with.So I would recommend this, especially if you're looking for a good mech fix. It's quite a bit more forgiving than Zone of the Enders is, and is far more arcady than something like MechWarrior. If you just want to jump into a badass customizable robot while doing rad anime ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, Daemon X Machina will do you right.

_childDocuments_.review: If I were to use a meme to describe this game, it would be: "My disappointment is immeasurable and my day is ruined."I had such high expectations for this game and at first it met them with flying colors. Combat was well done and fun, the story was good and had great potential, the music was fantastic, etc. However there's a certain point in the game that everything just went to ♥♥♥♥, as if the story writers quit and someone who didn't know how to tell a story had to take over the job and certain game mechanics became troublesome due to glitches, which the devs seem to have no interest in fixing. Luckily, the music is good through out all of it, but the story never recovered. When I reached end game, I discovered that there's no replayability either. The end game is multiplayer, which might not have been a problem when it came out. However, no one plays multiplayer anymore, except maybe pvp, but the pve is dead, which is all that I might have cared for. The bosses you need to fight to get unique gear are only for multiplayer and you really need at least a couple players to beat it and there appears to be no interest from the devs to fix or add anything new to the game, not even new game+.My suggestion for others:If you love a well crafted story and single player games, don't touch this or you'll suffer the same disappointment I faced.If you don't care about story content and just want to go do multiplayer and have friends to play it with, great! You'll enjoy this immensely. If you do decide to try the story, just don't do Rank A missions, cause that's where it fell apart.

_childDocuments_.review: Well being an Armored Core fan from the PS2 days, I obviously had to pick this up. I recommend you do too if you're a fan of AC, Chromehounds, Earth Defense, etc., basically any mecha game.The game is solid, but as you can expect, the campaign is lack luster. A lot of the characters are typical and lack any real depth, the story isn't clear, and the final fight was underwhelming in my opinion. But even that isn't really an issue for me as I have fun with mech building in general, testing em out and trying new things yada yada. The real issue is that theres really no content after you complete the campaign. Once you do and tackle the multiplayer boss battles and Reclaimer missions, all you have is PvP and 2 "dungeons" that you can play through. The dungeons wouldve honestly made the endgame a little more bearable if it wasn't just constantly  running through an underground facility that "randomizes"(only thing that changes is whats in the rooms, you always stay within the same facility setting) yet leaving the same final "boss" which is just Arsenals (not Strais) that you've fought before. There's honestly a lot that could've been added to the dungeon idea that would've made this game have an endgame worth $60. I couldn't tell you much about the PvP as the game is pretty unbalanced in terms of melee vs guns. I have played a good handful of PvP matches and they all just used blades and I die in 2 hits in 2 seconds. And not for lack of piloting skill or femto stance swapping. Swords are just nuclear sticks in this game. But all-in-all, if you're looking to scratch the Armored Core itch, especially with rumors of a new one on the way (KEYWORD "RUMORS"), DxM will get the job done for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I cannot recommend this game unless you're like me and absolutely desperate for some Armored Core action; though even in that regard, this is a bad Armored Core game.Daemon X Machina is all style and no substance in just about every regard. I really feel that it suffers from the fact that it was initially designed as a Nintendo Switch title, as I imagine that severely hampered the scale of the game overall. Battle arenas are in general pretty small and repetitive. Combat is okay, though it feels slower than some of the more recent AC titles. The story is frustratingly linear and talks way too much; at multiple points in the game an enemy will become invulnerable simply because they haven't finished their long-winded diatribe. In addition to this, the game is especially grindy. Everything is expensive and certain blueprints require the blessing of RNG, of which can be a cruel and fickle god. I stuck around hoping things would open up, as it seemed like there would be some sort of faction-alignment system eventually, but I was ultimately left disappointed. I really wanted to love this game, or at least like it. Sadly I can't even say that I enjoyed it. Were it still possible I'd opt for a refund. If you're an AC fan, odds are it'll disappoint you too. If you just want some b-list anime mecha action, maybe this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not very hard. For people coming from the Armored Core franchise or some of the previous Gundam games, it'll probably be a walk in the park. At first, I kind of hated that. While AC definitely beat me into the ground on several occasions, I always felt like there was some kind of strategy I could employ to at least pass the mission with... decent scores. This game is not like that at all. I'm fairly confident that someone could run this entire game with the very first, basic arsenal with no real trouble. Progression doesn't feel very tangible from the lowest rank all the way up to the highest one.But I think that's kind of the beauty of it, because there is a decent variety in weapons and arsenals that can be customized. After a giving the game a second shot I really do enjoy it. Because the game doesn't feel terribly challenging (and because there are no difficulty options), players can approach the missions however they want. In fact, I personally feel that someone who wants to have a min-maxed, super optimal build might actually have a worse time than someone who just throws whatever they want on their arsenal. You want to run a top heavy, machine-gun armed, missile-launching WMD on legs? Go for it.What about a super light, super speedy assassin arsenal with a sword in one hand and hammer in the other? Just keep zipping around and you're good.How about an arsenal with a twin linked laser canon on its back holding a shield in each hand to prevent it from taking too much damage between blasts? Just get the gaia-ray and two shields. Honestly you can run virtually anything and it can work. You can certainly give yourself just 4 of the "best" weapons and shred everything in seconds... or you can take whatever you want and still probably shred everything in seconds. Sometimes I play with all 5 weapon slots filled (2 arms, 2 pylons, 1 back) and use all the special abilities that arsenals have. Other times I try to play it like a basic Gundam GM or Zaku: 1 shield, 1 rifle and no special abilities. I find both instances fun because the game doesn't really force you to play a certain way. If you want a hardcore, super customizable, mech/mecha sim then this sadly won't be for you (I definitely felt that when I first picked it up). But if you're looking for a fast-paced "hero mech" shooter with a ton of basic customization options then this is pretty great. And  honestly the library for this type of game is pretty limited on Steam so... yeah
