_childDocuments_.review: Tl;DR: If you played Armored Core as a child, this is the closest thing you're gonna get until From Software lets the devs make an Armored Core VI. And it does a pretty good job so far.I think that the fact that some of the previous AC devs left to make this game really shows, except for the art style being very manga/anime-esque, which might turn some people off but as a Borderlands fan I think they really make it pop. It actually sort of reminds me of Risk of Rain 2. You've got a ridiculous amount of stats and build potential, while allowing the game to be easier to access for those who haven't really played the earlier Armored Core games. You can feel differences when your weight goes up for example, you'll hit the ground faster and be way slower. Put lighter framework on and you'll realize just how much faster you could be going at the expense of armor and durability. I thought melee was a trash option until I got more parts that increased my potential melee damage and swing speed. It's the kind of game where you just collect parts and yeah I can see the game's mission structure to get repetitive especially when grinding for items, but I also have a fat chunk of hours played in Monster Hunter and I didn't get bored of that either.I feel like this review is biased because this is a game genre that didn't really hit hard with western audiences, the same way early PSP versions of Monster Hunter I played religiously as a child somehow have really awful reviews.If you like the mech building genre, I think it's worth it. I've heard people say that there's hundreds of hours of content if you actually want to do and obtain everything, so we'll see about that. So far though, It's a pretty good time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mixed on this as Daemon X Machina's strongest aspects is the Arsenal/Mech combat , concepts for combat encounters, its visual artstyle and its music. I enjoy all of that.However everything else ranges from mediocre to boring and awful. This will most likely sour the taste for most a bit.Its the negative you see every other review talking about. Daemon X Machina and Armored Core 6 have extremely similar plots, but the former executes it in the most boring, unimaginative way possible. The story in this game suffers from a lack of subtlety with regards to telling the player exactly what is going on as it does so with mind numbing paragraphs of exposition by extremely uninteresting characters (will get to those later). In addition, the story itself suffers from major inconsistencies with regards to tone as some scenes and characters feel extremely out of place in certain scenarios.Final issue the story has is its predictability (and this will tie into gameplay but we will get there). This game tries its best to throw a plot twist or a surprise at the player around every corner and they all land flat because most of the time you are expecting it already. So overall it feels monotone, flat and sort of lacking in focus.Characters in this game falls into two categories.In my opinion, DXM voice actors and actresses are extremely talented. But the problem is that the material they are given along with the directing is so poor and awkward that they cannot save it.Dialogue especially have a tendency to keep going for too long and especially into philosophical territory.This game is plagued with escort and defense missions that are so irritating to play that you will want to take a break after you finish them. Couple with this is the fact that the game, just like the story, likes to throw curve balls in these missions nonstop. Perfect example I can think of at the top of my head is one where there are two objectives to defend and two enemy mechs present. Your first instinct up until that point is to fight these two but guess what, even though they appear on your radar and screen as enemies, you can't damage them but they can damage you. What you are suppose to do is the busy work by killing extremely small groups of fodder enemies coming towards the objectives while you hear your allies fight and argue with those 2 pests of mech pilots.There will be a ton of moments (like every two missions) like this where you the player feel like if you have little to no control over the game you are playing and everything is heavily scripted. It is infuriating because you will be playing the game how you think you are suppose to play it but nope, let a cutscene play and the whole mission changes and you probably wasted your ammo on that one guy for no reason.This game is filled with too much filler enemies that cant really do much to you unless you stay still and spread your cheeks. And they literally throw nothing new at you.Arsenals are the mechs you along with non player characters pilot in this game. The enemy Arsenel AI however ranges from good to "No thought, head empty". I have no idea why they sometimes just stop moving or doing anything for the matter and let you hose them down with the wrath of our lord and savior.Bosses in this game are spectacle for sure and are auditory feasts. But that is all they really are. Other than being giant bullet sponges, they really don't do much to attack the player per say so they come off as boring. DXM's combat is essentially Armored Core i.e., 3 dimensional movement via the use of boosters but your body will always be oriented mostly parallel to the X axis and you have 4 weapons at your disposal. DXM's twist to it is that it has implemented a heavier emphasis on moving throughout the air so you see why some other reviews say this feels like a mix between AC and Zone of the Enders (that has a lot of air combat).In addition, its combat has additional features not present in AC games such as the femto modifier system which essentially allows the player to augment a feature of themselves mid combat to perform better in that aspect which can be seen with the clone you can spawn of the movement modifier. All of this is great tbh and it will make anyone want to keep going through the negatives to finish the game.You've already seen the artstyle and its great. Though it kinda bites the gameplay in the  a s s  as it can be a bit difficult to see what is going on sometimes. But nonetheless, its great. Music is fantastic as well as well.Daemon X Machina is a good-ish game carried by its strong fundamentals with its arsenal combat, visuals and music. However, it is held back badly by those negatives. I have mixed opinions on it and I do recommend you get it. However, if you gonna buy this, get it at a discount. I hope they improve a lot of the gameplay/negatives elements in the future as I know the story writing and character quality isn't going to.I like the game but it needs some work.

_childDocuments_.review: DAEMON X MACHINA is not a groundbreaking adventure by any means, but it's about as solid a mecha experience I've found in the last few years, which is unfortunate any way you look at it, but I'll take what I can get.If you've played other greats like Armored Core, you'll find yourself wanting more - though sometimes, it DOES feel like Armored Core, at least for a little while.If you're new to the genre &/or your interest is piqued, there's some definite fun to be had. Customizing your mech (which they refer to as Arsenal) is its own fun - mixing & matching parts to fit your playstyle. Options include melee weapons, firearms, explosives, & more over-the-top stuff like regenerators (for field repairs), shoulder-mounted laser beams, mines, additional boosters & so on. There's also the ability to hop out of the Arsenal & run around on foot, which is rarely useful, but novel nonetheless.The gameplay itself is entertaining the first few times around & a positive loop exists. The enemies, locales, equipment, & boss fights are fun - but expect to see them recycled with new colors, starting from the opposite direction, same gun but it's a little stronger, etc. I had fun from start to finish creating the fastest Arsenal I could with all sorts of machine guns, strafing enemy AI & pilots alike. Also, I have to highlight how the online Co-Op is still functional in that the game offers the player's choice of AI companions in case no other players are online (I've only ever found 1 other person). A fun distraction with a decent grind for in-game currency & decent loot.DAEMON X MACHINA also boasts a good soundtrack with low-intensity thrumming instrumentals in the garage/hub area, sufficiently reflective / suspenseful briefing music, & enjoyable up-tempo battle themes during sorties. It even fits in some dramatic orchestral bits for significant developments of the plot.Unfortunately, that's the biggest weakness of this title by far: the story's themes, ideas, & plot points are great on paper, but the execution is so terrible, you'd think it was on purpose. I don't know how they have a cast of 3 dozen characters & every single one manages to be insufferable, be it how they sound, what they say, or how their motivation & emotion 180s over the span of 5 minutes. To be fair, the voice acting itself is pretty decent. Also, just about everyone has the annoying tendency to invite the Rookie (the player) into the conversation, but given their less-than-tactful way of doing so, it comes across as the cast just talking at the player, much of the time. In addition, much of the story is glossed over, or dumped over the span of a conversation, with maybe 80% of the game's plot given in the last quarter of the game - let alone significant plot developments that make no sense or ones that the colorful cast... doesn't react to. To summarize, the game boasts some tinkering & enjoyable mech action - which is sufficient, if that's all you're looking for. If you're looking for a little more, like an enjoyable story or likable characters, this title is lacking. As of writing this review, the game is on sale for $30 - which is worth it, but not at the full price of $60. If you're looking for customization & experimenting with your mechs, I'd say MechWarrior / BattleTech have more to play with.

_childDocuments_.review: After many, many years of Battletech pseudo-groundedness, I've recently gotten into the mood for something more Macross-y and started looking for suitable games, of which there seem to be precious few on Steam. Of all the ones I looked at, DxM stood out both thanks to its intense visuals as well as the range of features it offers -- ranging from extensive pilot customization (preventing you from yet again being locked into playing some stereotypical dude a la MW5), to online coop gameplay (allowing you to enjoy the game with your friends), to gameplay features like throwing cars or disembarking your mecha that are almost silly in how inconsequential they are yet so very, very much appreciated for how well they fit to the genre. In other words, options that may not be considered necessary at first glance, but surprisingly important just for giving you so much more freedom to enjoy the game.Aside from missing collaboration DLCs, the one downside that needs mentioning is that this game is, of course, a Switch port. Don't get me wrong, they've certainly upped the graphics and the actual combat controls are smooth as butter even if you're playing with mouse and keyboard (as one does). Out of combat, however, you've got the usual console relic of buttonmashing through countless menus and sub-menus, which really doesn't feel very elegant especially considering how many there are. Mouse implementation in the UI would have been very much appreciated, and hopefully, praise the steel, will find its way into the planned sequel.Still, the horrible menus do not take away from the excellent combat action, and whilst the story seems a bit difficult to get into at first, Marvelous did some really cool worldbuilding here, creating the perfect basis for the player to act as a freelance mercenary who gets to interact with a host of other mercs, sometimes as an ally, other times as opponent. Many of the characters - most of them belonging to teams with such colorful names as Bulletworks or Panzer Crown - are walking tropes, but this only makes the game feel even more "anime", so if you want to feel like you're in the midst of some Gundam show, DxM has got you covered.Recap:+ Solid, high-octane action gameplay+ Captures the "anime show" feeling well, thanks to its cast of characters and cutscene directing+ Lots of mecha customization (no Armored Core, but it's enough)+ Character customization that'd make even some MMO RPGs envious+ Optional Coop and PvP modes .. if you can find someone to play them with- Clunky console port UI- Lack of promo DLCs (in theory you might be able to mod them in)- Glowy "Femto" resource on maps devalues otherwise gritty post-apoc environmentsConclusion: Get Into the Damn Robot/10

_childDocuments_.review: As a Long time fan of the armored core series and a general fan of mech games, this game clicks ALL the boxes. I sunk nearly a thousand hours into Armored Core For Answer, hundreds into the 5 and Verdict day series, and hundreds into the Ps2 titles. Needless to say I was hungry for a decent mech game, and then I got into PC gaming and discovered there were almost no mech games even comparable to the games I loved. Gundam games are few, not a single AC game and emulation is still incomplete....Enter Daemon X Machina. The spirit successor to ACFA. Speed [check], customization [check, check], story[check]. It's got everything I missed for ACFA as well as things I didn't even know I wanted. A loot system keeps the game fun, mission replayability is always thrilling with new builds, and pilot customization is pretty good with a skill tree based on human augmentation. My only complaint is the game is short, but I can forgive that. 50 Hours in and I haven't nearly gotten all the gear or all the upgrades, so these missions will hold me over for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: DAEMON X MACHINA

_childDocuments_.review: Get this game, at full price. It's worth every cent.Daemon x Machina is the latest entry in the Armored Core series by designer Shoji Kawamori (series mechanical designer for the  Armored Core series) and producer Kenichiro Tskuda. And it scratches that Armored Core itch oh so well.Needless to say, this isn't quite Armored Core--that would be copyright infringement on the part of Marvelous and XSEED--but for all intents and purposes it is. The same mechanical aesthetics are there, the same "feel" is there, along with the plot-line of mercenaries in giant robots fighting as contractors fighting for territorial dominion, and often against a looming AI threat. There, also, are the devs from the Armored Core team, responsible for that series' best games.What has changed, though, is the addition of the ability to customize one's own character, along with the Armored Core, which in this game is referred to as an "arsenal." In addition to simple gender and appearance customization, the game has a host of cybernetic "upgrades" which can be applied to the character him or herself, and which improve combat performance. Also notable is the addition of the ability to fight outside of one's mech on foot, in a similar fashion to what was introduced in Mech Assault on the Xbox. All of these are improvements, despite the relatively cliched anime tropes which are also in service in this game. Gameplay: 8/10Story: 6/10Graphics: 10/10Overall: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Get AC6 if you're hungry for a mecha action gameLong version: This game is so close to being good. The combat has good bones, it looks good, feels mostly good to play, and the customization game is decent. The two main issue comes from mechanical progress being gated behind random drops, and the missions feeling like something out of a f2p mmo (extremely formulaic and repetitive).The game also pulls this weird move where they hype up the bosses as indestructible monsters, forcing you to cherry-tap them down for ages, only to have an NPC swoop in in a cuscene and one-shot the boss after you've done all the work.Can't really talk about the story much because I only made it 3 hours in, but the writing is pretty awful. Characters will continue to talk for minutes in after mission cutscenes without saying anything relevant or interesting.I hope the devs eventually get another chance at a mecha action game, because there's good bones here, but post-AC6, "mediocre Armored Core but at least it's on PC" is no longer a valid sales pitch

_childDocuments_.review: Daemon X Machina was an interesting one, it's a game that has it's issues and takes a good second to get into but once you do it becomes fun enough to play and the story is intriguing enough that you end up wanting to know more dood.Let's see combat was fun but definitely had it's issues, for starters Arsenal (that's your mech) against arsenal combat is highly flawed with how some missions are laid out, use a bazooka or explosive weapon and it knocks them back with a fair amount of damage, good right? sadly wrong as after you do that it means you can't hit them for a set amount of time for any damage, many timed missions or even normal missions make this way harder than it needs to be, especially if your AI team has them too, it was for PVP purposes I'm sure but it really didn't need to translate into the main game as enemies are often stacked with health and even when they aren't that kind of advantage is rather large and never benefits you the player outside of taking less damage in combat at times dood.To continue with weapons and the like Femto (energy in this game) it's an interesting mechanic that comes into play but sadly all it's uses are oddly limited in too many ways, for laser swords it's perfect as they don't run out of ammunition and take a limited amount but then femto is taken for what's known as the mirage system too, as well as the three mode types you can use it starts to get almost complex when it comes to managing it in all the chaos around you, then even worse than that are laser type weapons, if they were infinite ammunition and just used femto they would actually be rather fun and useful to use, especially at certain points in the game where ammo becomes rather scarce despite enemies dropping ammunition, it's really a case of a great idea implemented a little poorly dood.Guess what? you guessed it more weapons! yeah weapons are pretty key in this, I tried out many types that I unlocked along the way and they do suffer from a rather large issue and that's some just aren't versatile enough to warrant using over others, why use the shotgun when the sword does more damage and closes the gap, why use the sniper rifle over the assault when enemies move so fast that sniping them is impossible with how long bullets take to travel, why use the arc/stun gun when after very few uses you run out of ammo leaving you a gun short, lot's of weapons end up like this and there are some handy combinations granted but often you'll find there's a better option and leaving a sword behind is nooot an option dood.Okay onto something different and actually something I felt was well done even and that's Armour parts which consist of head, body, left and right arm and then legs and a special part that determines your speciality, such as lock on speed, lock on range, how well your arms adjust to firing among a few other things, each part can have multiple uses whether it helps how well you shoot, throw or use your sword for arms, how well you can jump and move with legs, how well you can target with head and how much memory which is what allows you to equip weapons, the legs arms and head, as well as attachments to weapons, this is all governed by the body/chest part, what's more durability, memory and typical effectiveness of a lot of things is governed by weight, I ended up with a nice balanced arsenal, maybe not great for PVP stuff but durable, carried many weapons, great memory but if you wanted to it would be easy to go for a sniping speedstar or as I started a tank of a warmachine, they did that aspect well dood.Okay so next parts up the main game, decent variety of mech types, AI controlled which is story integral but I won't say why because of that, Arsenals controlled by humans and one more type you'll see pretty early on in the game that's pretty darn awesome to look at and fight, I will say they go into boss level design enemies later on that will test both your skills and your ammo count at the same time, they are fun for sure but also somewhat frustrating dood.To carry on as to why this is frustrating, there are times you'll have timed or protect missions and enemies with too much health to handle, granted losing at those missions has no real impact so to speak outside of dialogue as far as I know and you will still clear the mission, if you want to retry you will have to make sure to press retry before you lose (which isn't always clear when you will) or wait until you beat the game and try it again, it's not the worst thing in the world but I can see a lot of people getting bothered by that to a degree dood.End notes would be I can't say anything about PVP or CO-OP missions legit because I can't play them for personal reasons sadly overall the main game though is fun, real fun even when you get into the story, what's more it's the right amount of challenging when it isn't forcing you to do a protect or timed mission which suffers from poor AI not doing their jobs which was crazy to me because during combat situations they actually did pretty darn well which was nice to see, other than that will you have fun with this game? if you're into mecha and some surprisingly decent story with some interesting cast on top yes, should you pay a lot for this game? it's a full game, there's no doubt but it's limited too, you see other games which I won't be rude and mention the games names here and you get some better visual customisation, more varied weaponry of which are a little more usable among things I'm sure I'm forgetting but it has a lot of heart put into it despite that and interesting ideas so I'd say yes and no, it depends on how much you're willing to spend which is rare for me to say, I will often call out games for their exuberant price tags and say yeah wait for a discount but in this case it's a game I feel could be worth it to pay a decent amount if they really like the look of it and my description, thanks for reading dood ^-^7

_childDocuments_.review: A good successor to Armored Core, even if it's far more anime than AC was. Good things:Characters are diverse and interesting, even if the writing suffers from the nature of the game's episodic/mission based narrative.Customization is fun, but it'll take time to unlock enough gear to really feel like you're making frequent value judgements.It's visually striking.  The 2D design, like the UI elements, kick so much ass.  The robots are also awesome, and the hot topic color pallete really sets it apart from other games in the genre which lean heavily into grey/military aesthetics.The one criticism I have is there isn't enough of this game and, by nature of it being limited in scope, you probably will find a single robot design that works for you and will never need to change things up.  I've nearly beaten the game now at ~20ish hours, so that should give a good idea of what to expect lengthwise.  Not bad at all, worth the money, and I eagerly await this franchise's next iteration.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't Armored Core, it's not a big game despite being on a known console.The game will never measure up to the vision in your head, but it's here all the same asking for a chance.In a world with very little in the mecha genre, we keep an eye focused for hidden gems.While I don't think this is a bad game, if you are a veteran of Armored Core or other JP mecha games this probably wont tickle your fancy. But it scratches the itch until something else will come along and possibly do better.Is it revolutionary in its gameplay? NoDoes the gun play and overall combat feel close to the above games? I'd say it's a floaty AC4 with air capable mechsWill the story floor me by being amazingly good? No, but there's Char. The other voice actors are serviceable in the jp dub too.In general the combat against enemy Arsenals that I've experienced is pretty ok, difficult but not overwhelming with friends. I'm sure people who spam "use da meta" would probably tell you the game is easy to cheese. But what game isnt these days?Not that my opinion really matters in the end to anyone knowing what they're looking for.You want justification for playing? Just enjoy yourself and let the game give you your own opinion.In a world where everyone just checks reddit or a forum board or youtube for opinions, games like these are just another pale imitation to them.If you want it, get it.But it's a fine game with some good weight behind it. It's not a big name, but it could be one day.

_childDocuments_.review: Any old major reviews that came out from big names like IGN and many popular youtubers is typically unreasonably harsh on the game. It could just be because I am bias to the genre, but one review said the campaign is only 14 hours long. Doing all the side missions (some multiple times), most campaign missions up to rank A and messed around with the online play a bit, I'm at 35 hours. I may spend a few minutes in between missions to tweak weapons, armor and augments, but I feel like saying the game only has 14 hours of play is selling it very short. Anyway,I suspect I am getting close to the end of the game and feel like I've got my money's worth out of it. It has high replayability for grinding for the parts you want or just to try the story again or a specific mission with a new build you came up with. The one major drawback to this game is the online play. No one is ever online. PVE lobbies are very few and far between. I haven't tried PVP modes yet so I can't speak to those. Fortunately the PVE content can be solo'd but obviously you're more efficient with help. Playing with friends is the way to go to enjoy the PVE content to the fullest.Overall, if you were a fan of the Armored Core game series, or a fan of mecha themes all together, this is the game for you. How much enjoyment you get out of it is up to you, but you will most certainly enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Port is solid as all hell. If you're into mech games, or the concept of flying around huge mechs and fighting stuff in them, you can't really go wrong with this game. I'm super glad the game is basically getting a 2nd chance on Steam now, because I feel like it really deserves it.The difference between this game on Switch vs. PC is absolutely staggering. From a barely stable 30 FPS cap at 1080p, to (in my case) a framerate I have yet to see dip below 120 FPS at 1440p. The game just feels so smooth to play now, and that's on both KB+M or gamepad.Regarding the gameplay itself, it's very fast and fun. I will say the starting bit of the game feels a bit slow and underwhelming, but once you're past it, it really starts to pick up.Story wise, yeah, don't expect to get something deep or meaningful from this game. It's very "anime" and honestly pretty cheesy and tryhard, but in a way, that's why I've been enjoying it so far. It's at least been enough so far to keep me interested, and some of the characters are legitimately pretty interesting, and that's all I can really ask for.A real highlight of this game though is the music. It just hits all the right marks concerning tone for this game, and it's one of those OSTs you can easily listen to and enjoy outside of the game itself. A lot of it is very guitar driven and/or electronic based, but there are some little gems of variety that stand out here and there. Honestly, I'd buy the OST if they ever decided to sell it on Steam.The only sort of negative I can think of so far would be the game throws A LOT at you mechanics wise, and there's a lot of made up jargon and who knows what, but it's not something that's impossible to overcome.Overall, would definitely recommend giving this game a go. I can understand if you'd think $60 (or your equivalent) is too steep for this game, so I'd at least recommend you keep this game in mind the next time a Steam sale happens.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good but has problems. You can fly and not fly. You cannot raise and lower on the Z axis while in flight mode which makes flying which is otherwise good one of the most difficult mechanics in the game. You can attempt to fly down making ur self a sitting target or drop making ur self an unmenuverable sitting target. Enemies have unlimited ammo and you do not. The maps are big until you start fighting then ur constantly hitting the edge of the map. Even though the game has difficulties the games story missions are all easy accept for the last mission which is extremely difficult. No ammo or health provided, enemy hides outside the map, enemy move to fast to track or shoot the bottom floor of the map has bumps which cannot be walked over which forces you to switch between flight mode and walking making you a sitting target if you try to fight their. These bumps look like you can walk over them but you cant they act like an invisible wall. The enemy will ignore you if you stand on some surfaces and just hide and shoot missiles at nothing. Their is no way to tell were the enemy is because their is no method built into the game to alert you of an enemy's location on the maps Z axis. That last one is a problem threw out the game but its most annoying when fighting the final boss who can move extremely fast. Ur just left looking around while getting attacked relentlessly. The system used in Zone of the Endars is an example of the best target tracking in a game to date. Their is target tracking and even missile tracking on the radar which is not bad accept for the lack of altitude tracking and all of the outside maps and the final maps are extremely tall. Over all I reccomend it, Lots of voice acting, some animated cut scenes and a deep story. Theirs are two multiplayer modes I have yet to try and theirs extra non story missions as well. The inventory is mostly OK but their no mouse capability in them which can make them a little tedeus at times. Its not easy to use the item creation because you cant compare items you want to create to items you have equipped with out going back and fourth between two completely different parts of the menu system. Further if you want to use Items you have equipped to create new items you are forced to unequip them in a different part of the menu system then go back and create them... But still over all good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool graphics and presentation, but shallow substance. I had my fun, but I also can't ignore the negatives/wasted potentials.(+) < what I like(-) < what I disappointed aboutI'm writing my experience so that you may form your own opinion. I will review this as a single player experience.(+) Cool ~2010 anime aesthetic with contrasting flat colors.(+) Cel-shaded graphics. High-speed robocombat felt really stylish.(-) Stiff character animations in cutscenes. The characters in their Arsenals uses body language when talking in cutscenes. It looks so dumb because they're waving their arms with their weapons still attached, making the weapons feel weightless.(-) Characters have the same plugsuits (= pilot suits), no exceptions. The difference between them are the colors and their body types.The meat of the Daemon X Machina hot dog.(+) High. Speed. Robot. Combat. It's really cool and really fun zipping around the battlefield, raining deaths from above.(+) Awesome giant boss fights. The fights felt like MonHun/Soulsborne-ish boss fight because you're killing these behemoths with death of a thousand cuts while dodging their dangerous attacks. These bosses have relatively hard to access weakpoints, so it can be a rewarding challenge to maintain your position.(+) You can also brute force them by shooting/slicing at their non-weakpoints body parts if you want. They have no invulnerable parts.(+) This makes taking down these bad boys even more fun with friends.(-) There's two type of bosses: named Arsenals, or the aforementioned giant bosses. Both are bullet sponges.(-) You wouldn't know you're fighting the giant bosses the wrong way until you're already out of ammo.(-) What's more ~fun~ than bullet sponges? Bullet sponges who zip around the screen of course! All named Arsenal fights are a chore. You pixel hunt your screen trying to get a lock-on on them, while your own missiles and explosives mask them with visual FX. The last 2-3 Arsenal bossfights can literally disappear from your lock then instantly appear 90 degrees to your right.(-) Your average controller schemes literally can't keep up with your and your enemies' movement. You either 1) crank your sensitivity to an uncomfortable level then git gud to be able to get a lock-on on those Arsenals, or 2) get keyboard and mouse. Switching to K&M made my endgame bearable (and frankly more fun) at the cost of tired arms.(-) The last boss fight is actually a gimmick boss fight, but you wouldn't know it because of the aforementioned bullet sponge problem. This is actually the last straw that pushed me to write this review.(-) Outer (pilot) mode is a glorified spectator mode. It's really useless except for reviving your own Arsenal I guess. And some missions force you to only be in Outer mode.(+) Decent customization options for face shape, hair, eyes, etc(+) Crossgender voices! You can use female voice pack with male body and vice versa. I don't use it, but I felt that it's unique enough for character customization.(+) Easy to redo appearance. Costs only in-game Credit and you can do it anytime. Even voices and gender!(+) Your Outer has its own passive skill tree. It affects your Outer form's parameters but also your Arsenal's. The Arsenal bonus is significant enough to complement your build. Can be reset easily using only in-game Credits. Readily accessible at the start of the game.(-) Bad body customization options. Two body types with fixed proportions: male or female. Then, two (free) full body plugsuit options, with 3 color channels. But then,(-) Your body customization will be overwritten by your passive skill tree anyways. When you advance your skill tree, some part of your body gets replaced by cybernetics. It looks so jarring compared to your biological body parts. Especially bad when you're in cutscenes, because no other characters have mechanical body parts.The stale bun of the Daemon X Machina hot dog.(+) (For Armored Core fans) Shoji Kawamori. The Arsenals' design felt at home.(-) Linear part progression. Some parts/weapons are clearly superior than some earlier parts. I don't feel like I'm building my own personalized murderbot, but just doing patchwork job to push through my next missions.(-) Looted parts may have additional Attachment Slot(s) to further tweak the part's parameter... . The effort to get an Attachment is just too big/too much of a hassle for just an insignificant amount of stat bonuses.(-) Obscure stat parameters. How much difference will I make when I raise my "Bullet Defense" parameter from 100 to 200? What's the difference between "Defense" and "Bullet Defense" parameters? No idea. The parameters are just so many, with nebulous and arbitrary numbers, you can't really be sure upgrading this parameter over that parameter really makes your Arsenal better suit your playstyle or not.(-) (For AC fans) To be fair, this parameter problem also presents Armored Core. DXM made it somewhat worse because they didn't even try to explain what a parameter do.(-) Limited appearance option. You can color your individual armor parts differently, but you only have 1) preset camouflages or 2) flat colors with 3 color channels. They can only customize about 80% if the part's color anyways. The rest 20% are uncolorable black joints and red Femto emission glows. The Femto glows can really kill your color coordination if you're serious about that.(-) Can't color your weapons.Oh my God. It's really insipid.(+) I enjoy some twists/developments along the story. For example, when I finally learn about the main AI enemies' true nature, I go "Huh, that's interesting".(-) But that's it.(-) Really cliched shonen anime storyline.(-) DXM has a lot of characters. Most of them are annoying stereotypes/flat characters. There's maybe 1-2 characters that I felt had a character development, but they're shallow.(+) One of them is Guns Empress. She's easily my favorite character in this game. You see, if you're served a rancid mixed salad, even one slice of unspoiled lettuce felt godly in comparison.(-) Boring characters make "emotional" scenes cringy as all hell.(-) Some important background events are told through in-game Mail. When the S hits the F at the endgame storywise, you get lots of Mails from people saying they're screwed. I feel like this really dampens the impact of the events because the Mails are boring the way they're written.(+) Good Controller rebind options. There's even a Shift function. It's necessary as this game uses many buttons, and many functions should always be accessible without the need to remove your fingers from both analog sticks.(+) Decent Keyboard and Mouse rebind options. This game can bind Alt keys (some shooting game cannot), but strangely not the ` key. And it's encouraged to use K&M in combat. See my complaints in the Combat section above.(-) Awful menu navigation. The worst example: to use Attachment you must go to the Factory menu, not the Garage. It also has a miniscule credit cost when you want to attach/detach, making you go through a confirmation popup hoop. Tied to my complaint in the Arsenal section above.(-) The Outer customization is on a different terminal from the Arsenal options. You must physically enter the Lab. There's also no tutorial/in-story pointer to the Lab, so it's entirely possible to play without ever realizing that your Outer can be (re)customized.I really, ,  wanted to like this game, I do. I'm hyped for it when it first appeared on Switch, and bought it day 1 when it appeared on Steam. So imagine my disappointment when I finally cleared this game.

_childDocuments_.review: (Note that I have been playing this game since it came out on the Nintendo Switch) I've been waiting for a long time to get an Armored Core style game on PC. Sure, the game isn't as complicated or as deep as the old Armored Core titles, but it does a good enough job of emulating the style while simplifying it enough so that you get to spend more time blasting enemies rather than staring at stat screens.There are a few minor issues with this port (and the game as a whole), some could be deal breakers for some players:1 - Mouse sensitivity is regulated to a single value. You cannot set separate values for using scopes. You can work around this by using heads with longer lock-on rages, but for those who like to manually aim precision weapons, it is a problem.2 - The game's price tag is a bit steep for the content it gives you. It's good fun, but there isn't enough here to justify the steep price.3 - The HUD was clearly designed for a handheld device. You can customise the size of the icons and their placement, but getting something that looks good is very time-consuming.4 - The game's story is bad. Like... REALLY bad. Thankfully you can skip it and some of the characters do have a bit of fun banter. Thankfully these issues are offset by a mountain of positives!1 - The soundtrack is amazing. I never knew how well metal would fit with an Armored Core style game until I played this (Arms of Immortal is a standout track).2 - Boss fights offer lots of spectacle, and make you feel like a bad-ass. Although they aren't quite as big as the Arms Forts in Armored Core 4A, they are still lots of fun and have different phases throughout the fights. 3 - The game has a nice difficulty curve with a few skill-check missions peppered throughout to make sure you're learning how to pilot your Arsenal effectively.4 - The randomly generated dungeons allow you to loot late-game parts right from the start of the game! Useful if you want to hop into PVP asap (don't tell anyone). You can also find chips that can upgrade your owned parts to three-slot parts in these dungeons (three-slot parts can install 3 chips to buff their capabilities. Think Armored Core's FRS tuning). 5 - Co-op missions are good fun with friends, and range from NPC team fighting, or massive raid bosses. Useful for farming 3-slot parts, boss parts and high-level chips.6 - The mech designs are fantastic, but what else would you expect from Shoji Kawamori?7 - The game runs beautifully, and can run at a silky-smooth 200fps!If you can get passed the admittedly minor issues, love mecha, or are an old school Armored Core fan, I highly recommend that you give this one a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Think of this as Armored Core Lite.  A ruined world? A nebulous story that you can pretty easily just flash through? Giant butt kicking robots? It has it all. There isn't nearly as much deep dive into the stats as AC had, but it should definitely satisfy your giant robot needs.  Combat feels fun and agile, although the height adjustment in flying a bit rough and could use some fine tuning IMO.  There are a few cheese builds/weapons that simplify a lot of the game, but just about anything is viable in a PvE build so just pick what you like and roll with it.Where it really shines is playing online with friends.  The end game coop stuff is a bit light, you won't spend months grinding on it to beat it, but you can definitely sink a lot of time into trying to get maximum level upgrades.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of games, and with no hyperbole I can say this is one of the worst games I've ever played while still being technically functional.The good:. Flying around is kind of fun and controls decently well.. Depending on your preferences you may be into the visual aesthetics of the mechs and robots and destroyed city environments.. The fights with other mechs are the only moments where the game kind of comes alive. They're not great by any stretch but they are at least a little engaging.The bad:. The story, writing, characters, voice acting, and animations are all abysmal. It took no time at all for me to start skipping cutscenes filled with pointless dialogue, terrible jokes, and cringy deliveries. There basically is no story, all you get is that part of the moon crashed into earth and now AIs are going crazy and there are some evil factions. You have no idea what your goal is, and your character is just some generic mercenary who may as well be faceless and nameless if you didn't pick those in character creation.. Ok maybe people don't play this game for the story, writing, characters, or voice acting. How's the gameplay, and specifically the combat that is presumably the reason people will really want to play this? Well, it's terrible. The guns handle like complete garbage, even an assault rifle fires more like a pistol and has no good sound effect or impact on enemies. The enemies themselves hardly ever even attack you outside of enemy mechs, so most fights are just a ceremony of moving towards each enemy and firing at it till it explodes. You have missiles which are similarly non engaging and just take the edge off of the enemy crowds, and you have an ability to spawn a doppelganger to fight alongside you temporarily but you don't control it so it may as well be another NPC ally. Speaking of the NPC ally, they're kind of too competent, and can just take your kills in some missions which makes you wonder why you're even here.

_childDocuments_.review: Game's really bad. Tedious. Full of pointless grindingI bought this long time ago because it's fill what Armored Core (before AC6) doesn't. It's available on PC. But alas, what I get is far below my expectation.Gameplay sucks. It doesn't have weight. Bullets feels like a pea shooter, it just hit and there's some pop up with indicate how much the damage is. Bullets also doesn't go where you want to go. Here's an example: You fight Rebellion, you want to shoot his elbow, either  it's still has an armor or it's already has it's weakness exposed. Here's a catch, his tower shield still up, but you still aim at his elbow from behind regardless. Guess what? Your lock on system will lock onto his shield and your gun will become David Beckham. It's gonna curve it's bullet onto your lock on target which is the shield. Missing entirely from your intended target.Melee is stupid. You need to make some distance to make some damage. The more far you are (depending to sword max distance) the more damage you deal, but not too far or you'll miss your slash because of range. Also, you slash while also dashing. Good luck with that. I miss 2/3 of my slash because of that mechanic. The melee weapon also has "Max Cumulative Attack" or something. You'll think it makes the melee makes more combo slash but nope, it just makes you can chain your attack more to DIFFERENT TARGET (WHICH HALF OF THE TIME DOESN'T WORK).Knockdown feature is stupid. In AC6, you got stagger. Which when you fill your opponent stagger meter, you'll be rewarded with a paralyzed opponent which can't do anything for a moment and receive an extra damage (depends on your weapon's direct hit damage). In Daemon X Machina you get a knockdown which when you make your opponent knocked, you get a sleeping robot. Yes, just a sleeping robot. No nothing. You can't damage them. A knocked robot gets an invisible frame until few seconds after they get up. Yeah, it can be utilized as a mechanic where you knocked a robot onto a lava or something. But, here's the catch, you never fought another robot above a lava floor (or similar), you only fought them on land.Movement's sucks. The only way to boost is forward. Want to lower your altitude? Press descent button, but I hope you have a lot of time and patience because descent also remove your ability to hover in the air. Want to hover again after adjusting your altitude before? Press jump. Well guess what? It's a jump, dummy. You activate your hover in cost of GAINING A HIGHER ALTITUDE BECAUSE IT'S A JUMP. Combining that feature with the lock on feature, you have a game of balancing your altitude so it's not high enough you lock onto another target than intended and not low enough that your gun is blocked. Want to avoid all of that hassle? Equip your auxilary slot with Down Booster instead of anything more useful. You can descent faster without down booster with descent+boost but it will make you descent diagonally (as in forward) instead of vertically (as in adjusting altitude). I hope you'll enjoy the movement because the AI mecha sure do love move all over the Z axis.The menu navigation is left to be desired. You want to attach your equipment with some attachment? It's on Factory which on an entirely different menu from Hangar which entirely consist of EDITING YOUR EQUIPMENT. Why can't they make it the same menu? They surely can do it, I mean, changing your armor to changing your weapon doesn't need to go to different menu. You can just press Q/E (in keyboard) to swap from Armor Menu to Weapon Menu. Why do I need to go to an entirely different menu to attach or detach an attachment which you will do a lot unlike Monster Hunter World nor Rise which you'll attach and forget. You will detach a lot of attachment from loot because that's the only way you can get attachment besides fighting Colossal Immortal.Loot? It's sucks a lot. Tedious. Stupidly annoying. It's like Borderlands 2 94 Sham but it only got you normal Sham and you start your farming not from the BNK-3R checkpoint, but you'll do it from the bottom. Lot of advanced gear is locked behind exploration II, which you can't finish it by yourself because the final boss consist of 3 bullet sponge mecha. And I  hope you get the 3 attachment slot because you sure do don't want to farm it again.TL;DR Just buy Armored Core 6, don't bother with this game. Co-op doesn't mean ♥♥♥♥ if what the game does is bore you. Or you're just a jerk who wants your friend to suffer alongside you (which kudos to you, I guess).

_childDocuments_.review: As a lover of the PSX era of the Armored Core franchise, I was initially skeptical of buying into DxM despite knowing that it was developed by people who also worked on those aforementioned titles.  Anime character tropes?  No hidden gear to look for on missions (well, almost none)?  No Karasawa?  A fricken ice cream parlor?!  Hrrrrrm.But, after deciding to purchase it recently on sale and finishing the main story, I must say that this really is a solid love letter to the older AC games: while mech customization isn't quite as expansive (bipedal designs only), there are definitely a lot of parts to play with and the controls feel very responsive.  The conversational back-and-forths between the various personalities and the Shatner-esque dramatic scenes did nothing for me personally besides give my ocular muscles a workout, but they didn't detract from the fun of simply flying a mech around and showering enemies with munitions while avoiding return fire.Now the big question: would I recommend paying $50 USD for this?  Not with AC6 right around the corner, no, but that would be the only caveat for me; this is a really fun game with lots of content for single and multiplayer to chew through.  If the folks at FromSoftware somehow manage to drop the ball with the upcoming AC6 game, then at least the mech lovers still have Daemon X Machina to enjoy.Well done, Marvelous!

_childDocuments_.review: Since Armored Core 4 I've been wanting something even close to a good mecha game. Tried lots of different promising titles but they all felt clunky or lacking in someway or another.DXM isn't one of them. There's tons of customization options so you can build to your play style. Wanna go fast? build a zoomy mech. Want to be the heaviest stompiest, beam laseriest boy? You can do that. Want to just punch other mechs in the face? You do you boo boo.Game's got a hilariously anime campaign that I appreciate. There's a variety of coop missions separate from the campaign along with exploration missions, all of which let you keep all the salvaged equipment and credits you earn and bring them into your single player game. There's even PvP here as well to enjoy.My only gripes with the game are:1) They don't let you color weapons. You can color your entire mech but the weapons are going to be whatever color they come with. 2) The campaign has no coop. It would probably be too easy then but I'd still like to play it with friends.Other than that. Great game. Absolutely worth the money. Hoping lots of people support it so we see the game get expanded content or sequels to play through.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is all over the place poorly done.. I am not quite sure how this gets such good reviews but in all honesty this is not worth full price.. not at all. Graphics: Anime but not the smoothestControls: Flow Freely but overall mechanics make things clunky especially using weapons like meleeSound Design:dreadful.. reused sound assets for multiple weapons make things dull and boringMusic: the only good part about this game yet it gets drowned out by the game itself.. recommend you change this in settingsStory: some of the worst I have ever sat through in many years.. the story of this may as well not exist with how cringey and awful this is.. you may as well have had a 10 year old write this while playing with action figures.Gameplay: Neat at first but gets boring very fast, extremely repetitive, AI cheats nonstop and will dash even without stamina, artificial difficulty later on in the game with ridiculously tanky AI that use unlimited stamina for some reason you can barely scratch, some portions of the game have the AI actually be indestructible, AI when knocked down cannot be hurt yet your friendly AI and you yourself will consistently knock them down causing long lulls of no damage waiting on them to be able to be hurt again, EXTREMELY grindy later on especially on the exploration mission for the better stuff or boss running which gets tiresome fast, lacking longevity as the game itself is very short around 8 ish hours if you skip the abyssmal storyBuild Variety: honestly extremely lacking.. I see this game get compared to armored core.. this doesn't hold a candle to the customization capabilities of armored core and other games in that league. Weapons feel lackluster and like your punching sandbags theres not real impactful punch you get out of them and in terms of different armor a lot of them look similar in terms of chest, though arms and leggings do look quite different. Statistically theres really no point in worrying to much about build variety in this game as you can beat it by just blindly throwing things together.. as long as you can last the bullet sponges your fine. Not like it matters really though when half the weapons are pretty terrible to begin with and you realize that rather quickly with how the flow of the combat goes nonstop. PVP: pvp? yeah no.. thats a complete joke and a half. I mean, sure.. if you don't mind people who spent hours grinding mindlessly to get the best stuff fully outfitted to the point they practically 2 shot you sure.. fights last very short intervals its not even worth doing thisCoop: this is literally the only fun portion of this game outside of the wow factor at the beginning. This grows tiresome fast but is the only reason worth buying this game. The coop fights are interesting and all but youll burn through them in a few hours and be done with itPrice: not worth $60 not worth $40.. wait till this thing nose dives in price to like $25-$35 before picking it up if that..I would refund this game honestly if I could, my friends got me to play it with them and every bit of it was levels of irritation and not fun. Half the story is more of a tutorial that is extremely poorly written as they fail to fully introduce all the game mechanics off the get go. Highly recommend you avoid this game.. sucks this genre is so niche I love mecha titles but this just doesn't do it right

_childDocuments_.review: Would be a neutral review if possible. Outstandingly bland. Obnoxious voice acting and a rambling, mediocre story. What starts off as fun mech combat burns out in the next 10 or so missions as it hits you that it's all there is to this game. The missions almost tease interesting objectives before bait-and-switching to "destroy thing" and very occasionally "destroy thing quickly" or "destroy thing, but without destroying other thing." About 10 enemy types, 6-ish bosses, wonky and sometimes really easy enemy mech AI, and only a handful of weapon types. The balance is poor and many times the game will turn off (or massively handicap) your damage without telling you to progress a plot. Launchers also seem to be bugged (for both player and AI) and regularly stop doing damage after the first hit. That said, it's easy and pretty hard to fail most missions (aside from the final boss) if you back off from combat occasionally.Took me 14 hours. I don't regret it, but I won't be going back either. If the entire time I'm stuck in a loop of "Man, (Armored Core / MechWarrior / Front Mission) did (x) better, I'd rather be playing that..." it's a not a good sign. It's bizarre that a game that came out after that era seemingly lacked so many good aspects from them and instead opted for an extremely simple approach with a few stats being useful and about three bars to manage (health, stamina, and energy). There's a decent replay factor if you want to collect parts or upgrades, but that's it.I did not play online (though I did do online missions solo) - having cooperative missions and modes in a game like this is huge, and a big upside though.Solid 6/10. Pick it up on a sale and lose a weekend or two.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most fun mech action game I've ever played. It may not be Armored Core since it's more arcade-like(which is not a bad thing. In fact, I wish there was more of these type of mech games coming out), but it's enough of it's own thing that it can stand on it's own. Something which I prefer instead of being a straight-up AC clone. It's a damn shame the game suffers being flown over a lot of people's radars thanks to Marvelous Japan's video copyright strike ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥(during the Switch launch).If there's something I wish this game had is a bit more variety in the weapons. While there's more than enough weapons and even armor parts to build something unique(although there's the cheese factor in the form of the Gun arms), the Melee category consisting of only swords, whether beam or solid, big or small, and just one blunt instrument can be a little stale in terms of variety. Long Range weaponry is much better in this regard, but there's still a bit more room to improve. The swords are fun, still, but I would like to see other types like pile bunkers and javelins or so. But the action more than makes up for it. The mech customisation, once you get a hang of things, is easy to follow(for me anyway), Controls are smooth, gameplay is solid, the design has it's style that i like, and the bosses are fantastic. Feels like a mech Monster Hunter as well. Downside is the mediocre story. There's some dumb silliness in there, but to be honest, everything else in this game overshadows it. If I remember right, you can either mute the NPCs or just skip the cutscenes via first playthrough.I'd still recommend this for being a fun mech game. We need more mech games like this. Seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it on the advice of a friend, refunded it while giving advice to my friend not to buy it.Game looks perfectly fine, controls are pretty good (controller user), and that's about where the decency ends. The writing is sad, consistently dipping into cringey (stop calling me a f*cking rookie, I'm better than all of you...), and the characters are just B-grade anime rejects. The dude who talks by shouting made me skip the story because I just couldn't bear it. The story is completely mundane, and as said, just fodder for that Esc button. I did give it a chance, but when the most likeable character is MS Karen, you know you're in for a bad time.Now, leaving that crap aside, let's get into the gameplay. OOoooooh boy. Tutorial level. They show you 8 screens, each with every button combination, map legend and HUD description, hope that you've memorised it without any practice, and then tell you to get ♥♥♥♥♥♥, but it's okay. Just jam those f*cking triggers down and never let go, and fly forwards. The game auto-locks and auto-shoots targets in your FOV, you can equip guns that make it so you don't even have to press a button to shoot (lolwhy), and the enemies are BLISSFULLY easy. The only challenge is trying to figure out what the ♥♥♥♥ the AI "allies" are even with you, when they won't STFU, and seem to exist to just keep filling your screen with dialogue. So yeah, don't play this game for the combat.The mech building is probably interesting, but you know, it would be nice if they explained what the arbitrary and random stats actually did, or if there was some kind of screen to see the individual attributes of the piece of gear, rather than having to compare the two and do some damn math on them. But it doesn't seem to really matter, since gear just gets progressively better at everything, with almost no downsides to just equipping the most recently-acquired piece.There is a store. It doesn't sell weapons or armour. Yup.There is a factory. It only makes armour and weapons you already have. Yup.The bosses are garbage bullet sponges that punish lapses in concentration while you spend 10 minutes shooting the same 4 areas of it, which is apparently a suitable replacement for challenge. And the age old JRPG tradition of "beat you in the game, lose to you in the cutscene" is very much alive and well, just exacerbating how killing swarms of mindless AI just to get bitchslapped by this episodes bad guy means absolutely nothing other than attempting to trick you that the pre-programmed series of events had any reason to be gated behind "gameplay".And my absolute ultimate gripe. $80 AUD game. $80 of DLC on LAUNCH. That's completely unacceptable. I don't care if they're skins, or if they're actually gear, it is truly pathetic to release an EIGHTY dollar game, a triple-A price for a severely B-grade game at best, and then try to gouge another $80 out of you because you're greedy. Have some damn respect for the player base of this trash, please.Also, Co-op, but not for the story, why please? Just don't add co-op if you can't play the damn game with your friends outside of the grind. Apparently the PvP is full of hackers, which for a game that's a month old is pretty pathetic.And the shotgun sucks. Easily the part of the game that just put that final nail in the coffin.I would consider buying this game for $10-20, no worries, but $80 for this is daylight robbery. Go play Mechwarrior or MH:W or something. (MW:W is actually cheaper than this ♥♥♥♥, and it's made by CapCom, an actual company, with actual DLC)

_childDocuments_.review: It's Armored Core except it isn't. It wants to be 4/A but then handles like AC2. Combat is clunky, but the scenarios are easy. Progression is awfully slow, as it wants to be like a looter shooter, or in more recent memory Monster Hunter. The shop function is a joke because of that reason. Weirdly enough I hate the story. It's not like previous AC had any real plot, but it was at least simple and to the point. Devs here wanted to actually flesh out "what if members of the Ravens Nest actually interpersonal relationships?". Well, sounds cool, but we end up with too many forgettable characters, most of which have awful personalities due to following their character archetypes to a tee, then really hams it up to drive a point home. Voice acting is decent, if it weren't for the awful writing.Scenarios and gameplay are probably the worst the game has to offer, as every mission boils down to 3 main variations: kill everything, escort, defend. You might ask, isn't that kinda what we had before? Yes, but no. Kill everything is okay if the game didn't treat most of those missions like a musou game, where you just slog through maybe a few hundred enemies in a wide open area. Sure theres some verticality, and the maps actually have terrain. But there's little incentive to do more than "move forward, lock on, shoot". Maybe that not so friendly Raven throws a wrench in the works, but the AI can't defeat circle strafing. Or terrain. At all. Literally I've beaten Ravens because they got stuck in geometry, or even a wall.Escort missions are mundane, since most missions are actually canned.Defense missions are what I described above, with an added objective to keep safe.Sometimes the game mixes it up with some boss encounters, or just straight up duels between other Ravens, but it's nothing more than a damage race.I don't know, I could keep going, but ultimately the Anime aesthetic isn't doing the Dev's any favors here. I've been told some members of the dev team actually hail from the old From Software team, but that only does so much good. I played the game on Switch, and it was about the same on that console. A sad let down of a dream to revive Armored Core of old. I don't know why people are giving the game so much praise now that it's on Steam/PC. Is it because we're so starved and desperate for an Armored Core game, that this is the closest we've been? Is it so desperate that we've completely given up on From Software ever giving us another Armored Core?I want to believe so badly From Software will come back someday, but it's been almost a decade since ACV, and even more since For Answer. The dream is dead.

_childDocuments_.review: In no way, shape, or form, is this game worth the buy. Gameplay is a tedious mess across all fronts, all the way between the core loop of starting and finishing a mission to simply examining equipment to think of a build. The equipment system itself is a car fire of half-implemented and shoddy ideas wrapped in a mess of menus, with equipment upgrading clearly extended to encourage some sort of grind. The story itself is no better: every character some sort of ridiculously cheesy uninspired cliche and/or caricature, and delivered as if it's a manga adaptation made on the cheapest budget in existence-- every cutscene might as well be still frames, with elements and events clearly cut (amazing considering this was supposed to be a stand-alone work). That Isekai anime you despise probably has a more compelling and interesting story than what they ended up with here. Stay far away, and even if you see this on some sort of bargain-bin sale or are unbearably desperate for some fast mecha action, you are better off not wasting your time with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't hate this game but it really has too many points of annoyance for me to recommend it at all. As someone who hasn't played Armored Core at all, this gets points from me for being fun mech action! But there's big problems.- This might be the worst written video game I've played in years. There's a million characters with unexplained backstories, misdelivered reveals, mistimed climaxes, and non-existent motivations or loyalties. Things just sort of happen. There's tons of dialogue and none of it serves any purpose. This game would have, sincerely, been better if the dialogue involving pretty much the entire supporting cast was cut completely.-The game gives you a lot of options but you rarely need to actually use even a meaningful number of them. In the later game, I basically blitzed the entire thing using two built-in-SMG arms to just bullet-hose everything to death. There was never any reason to learn how to use my Femto abilities, or to really use shoulder weapons, or any auxiliaries that weren't "passively start with more ammo".-The game is incredibly easy. Case in point -- the paragraph up there. The only times the game is ever "difficult" is when enemies behave inconsistently without apparent reason. Grief is the worst offender -- the only NPC mecha pilot who uses the teleport ability (and uses it constantly!) and also doesn't seem to be beholden by the game's normal stamina pacing (whenever he runs out, he seems to recover it all the instant he touches the ground).-There isn't really any depth or repeatability to the game's missions or the 'post-game'. Tactics are largely unimportant, and there isn't really any incentive to try and tackle certain missions certain ways. Special victory conditions are largely based on doing the mission quickly/efficiently rather than tackling it in unconventional ways, nor does there appear to be any consideration for how a mission was completed or how an enemy was defeated when giving you rewards.Ultimately: if you can get this for like twenty or thirty bucks it might be a fun time, but I don't think it's a super great game as a whole. I would give this a "ehhh" if I could, but being left with Yes/No as my only options, No is definitely the more appropriate choice.

_childDocuments_.review: I have not completed the game, and I don't think I have any motivation to do so. The problems I have reached a breaking point in Rank C (the game has a ranking system for missions you go on to bracket the reward and difficulty). To start with the weapons are really lacking in good feed back. Every melee weapon I tried felt like it just had one attack, A lot of the guns feel odd as well not helped by how easy it is too shoot enemies. I never felt I had a satisfying weapon and ended up using lots of missile and rocket launchers to deal burst damage. The assault rifles seemed the worst of them all with some weapons rate of fire being pathetic.All of this made researching new armor and weapons, or caring for the upgrade trees hard. The costs got extreme fast or required items you would either be using or didn't have. This meant doing free missions to farm money and gear, which normally would be fine, but again the combat grew more and more dull as nothing was really that interesting to use.I got to what seemed like the near endgame in rank A (for all I know this is the half way point) and the plot got more cliche. Normally I dont hark on an action game to be written like an action movie (hit or miss dialog, random plot twists, and big speeches) but when the gameplay is lacking, its hard to get infested. One enemy I wont name was just dull as all they would do is move above or below me very quickly making aiming tedious. They were really not a threat but by Rank A and mech v mech fight became very spongey so this constant up and down or trying to find something small far away killed any fun,To top it all off, the Mechs themselves are bad. the range of design is just a scale between thin and bulk. If you came here from a Gundam Breaker 3 recommendation, dont bother as it has nothing like the option in appearance as base models do in that. Weapons and armor have no identity of their own to be honest and you would need to farm alot to get parts with slots and attachments worth wild to build anything that might feel unique. The closet the game gets to variety is gun arms which just removes the option of a backup weapon. The game needs a lot of polish to UI and a lot more variety in design before it can make me more motivated to play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: Full controller support: There is no ALT-F4 for Armored Core.Odd that it says partial controller support on the store page. I've played mech games since the 90's and I'm very happy with this game in my collection.Takeda's calligraphy was a nice free DLC surprise (check him on insta). Other DLC is cosmetic and you're not missing out without it. Both Japanese and Eng vocal tracks are enjoyable for me. If you're not conversational fluent, it's probably best in English as there's talking in the missions; it's hard to read subs with all the missile chem trails in the sky.The only letdowns: Lack of a photo mode or video replay mode in missions. Afro hair is male only. For example, my female character has a natural fro but small sideburns are obviously visible if the hair is anything but black (I,e.: matching the skin-tone closely). Afro hair is absent from many games (there's only a couple of do's in RD2 for example), it's good to see it in, but please, remember women's hair!  It's a bit expensive at £50. _childDocuments_.review: 100%d the game on switch just after launch, really fun Armored core successor.Speaking of AC, it's not quite as complex in fine tuning/upgrading as that wondrous series, but has its own interesting ways of doing similar things e.g attachmentsThe Story is pretty schlocky, like its not the worst but its full or tropes and reaches a bit further than its arms can manage. The dialogue is slow in that way any in engine "cutscene" is (characters line is meant to be cut off but theres a second delay for the event to trigger)The Combat is good, has the potential for real fast-paced AC madness but a lack of difficulty means this is rarely put to full use.The Monster hunter style RNG for blueprints and such is pretty annoying, especially when its put right beside a % progression bar (why couldnt it just be that again instead of RNG?)Overall though i do love this game, its unpolished and very visibly made by a smaller team but does the job of filling the AC void well for now.Shame the online is dead though....

_childDocuments_.review: THIS IS THE RESURRECTION OF ARMORED CORE; THE TRUE SPIRITUAL SUCCESSOR. I loved armored core; I wasn't the best but it made me feel smarter and more strategic. This game gives me the same rush but is much more fun! PROS:-Armored Core but simpler-Pilot Customization (see CONS)-You can exit your mech and walk around as a pilot! YOU CAN EVEN DRIVE SOMEONE ELSE'S MECH IN MULTIPLAYER IF THEY LEAVE THEIRS ALSO!-Surprisingly Engaging Plot (if you can deal with plot points being all reveals and no buildup)-Bosses are super fun, diverse, and on harder modes actually challenging-Actual post game content like extra bosses for new equips-Gameplay is fun, smooth, and much better balanced than Armored Core was; if you go high speed, your lock on time will be slower so you can't dominate a tank player. Likewise, slow, tanky mechs will have a hard time locking on and finding a fast mech, but has lower lock on time. Another example is in HP vs Defense; squishy players aren't 100% glass cannons; with low HP, they get higher defenses. Heavy parts give high HP, but may not have the best defense.-Multiplayer is nothing but fun quick runs and raids; no toxic players (yet)-PVP AND Dueling after missions gives both competitive and casual fun-Is basically Mech Monster Hunter but faster and less committmentCONS:-Graphics are designed for switch, so it looks cartoonish-Less variety in your mech; no tank legs or quad legs/only humanoid mechs-For whatever reason, painting your mech is separated by a PAINT and a PATTERN option. If you want super shiny, glossy parts or a fun wood and camo finish it can't be done; have to get a single gloss color/camo on your whole mech.-Post game will end up being a bit grindy, like Monster Hunter-There are skinned weapons in game, but they are found at random with random skins in an online mode only-Pilot Customization. So you can basically forfeit your humanity to become a cyborg to varying degrees. This adds to your mech abilities like movement and perception. It basically makes you better for a cost that isn't really a cost. And if it was supposed to be a cost, they could implement some bonus' or something for staying human (like myself).This game has serious potential to revitalize the mech genre of games. I hope that the devs continue to pump out more content and work on sequels. I, and would ask any and all armored core fans or curious ones, to support this project as well!

_childDocuments_.review: From my time playing the demo on the Switch, it was enjoyable, but was held back by the joycon controls and the poor framerate.Luckily, these aren't issues with this PC version, and it runs amazingly. The port is really good, setting aside the lack of 21:9 support and a completely uncapped framerate option (Which at least goes up to 200FPS), but both of those issues can be fixed rather easily. The gameplay is made a lot less tedious and more enjoyable by the keyboard/mouse support being great. Basically, this is another Vanquish situation, where the PC port is a MASSIVE step ahead of the original console releases.Bonus points for this being developed by ex-devs of the armored core series, and having Shōji Kawamori (Who is the main man behind Macross, and also did designs for Nero's arm in Devil May Cry V) as the mech designer.Pat on the back for Marvelous. Now they should put this much attention into the PC ports for Senran Kagura.

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who has played Armored Core should at least give this a look. While many veterans consider the game watered down compared to the old Armored Core games, it's more approachable, and is still a blast to play.The primary game play loop is building out your machine with parts from salvage or research, then going on missions with your new Arsenal build, and then tweaking it again based on how well it performed for you. Various styles are all valid, some people like heavy bruisers, and others love speedy close quarter combat machines, all work and are valid. Boss machines are fun to fight, and varied. When defeated several times unlock unique equipment.Visit the ice cream shop to unlock bonuses to your stats for the mission similar to the Canteen from Monster Hunter World, do this enough and you get some rewards beyond the stat buffs. Multiplayer has co-op in the form of boss battles, basic missions, as well as pvp. multiplayer monsters are upgraded versions of the single player bosses who unlock better versions of equipment.

_childDocuments_.review: Character: You can either pick male or female. Character design is okey and fine. Not so complicated, just simple outlook as all the anime out there. Color picking is there too. Voice choice is included as well. If you don't like the picks you did and want to redesign everything, there is no need. There is a room you can edit and/or exchange your character again. More unlocking items appears, as you progress your story or unlocking stuffs.Story: The whole planted that you are in are been corrupted by bad AI's. You are a human as everyone else , but as a mercenary. Your mission is to restore the planet by destroying the bad AI's. You can hire NPC with you, as long you have some in game money. The story has a few twists in it. The concept is fine/ok. Few drama's going on in the story as well. If you made some mistakes, or are curious the choice you did or want to rerun the story. No need to worry, you have to complete the whole story first. This allows you the options to pick any story line since you completed the game. it sounded like a butterfly effect, but some missions in story have two different ending. Depend how you accomplished. But the story is still one road ending, with different result in missions.Combat: High speed action, flying, lock on target, 3D-shooter, melee.Mech: You can customise your own robot, gesture, coloring, showcase and name it. Equipment, weapons, armor by buy or finding parts from other destroyed robots you just destroyed (pick up from it). It has to be some specific robots. You randomly get the choice to pick only one. Either weapons, armor and boost equipment. There is over 100+ equipment to choose from. Each parts in your robot have different stats, so choose wisely to what to equip in your robot that suits you best. Face Bosses to unlock special prints to upgrade some specific equipment. Do it alone or in co-op missions.Multiplayer: You can have only up to 4 player in a same lobby/server/channels. Non-story in multiplayer. Expedition in a RNG room each mission. Nice way to grind/farm parts and/or equipment with peoples. Or doing specific bosses.
