_childDocuments_.review: A decently solid mech game. For someone who is familiar with Armored Core, it calls back to it a lot. Which makes sense, given that several people involved in the development of those games is involved with this game.Pros:+ the gameplay is solid, stylish and very smooth.+ Mech customization is decently solid and gives a good number of options on how to approach a situation.+ A sizable number of missions, which means it will give you a decent run.+ The lab allows you to upgrade your character outside of just customization.+ Nice stylized graphics+ The online bosses are quite fun.Cons- The story is not good.- While the gameplay is solid and stylish, it lacks depth compared to the series it takes from. This is due to the fact that you have a very few "tricks" for mobility, and few things to worry about due to the energy system.- There are a fair few questionable missions and the story missions have some very specific and annoying flaws  that detract from the gameplayOverall, this is a good starting point; however, this has some very specific flaws that make it weaker than it should be.EDIT: I just wanted to expand on one of the positives, and negatives. The game, when fighting against regular enemies, is at its best with STAIs, and the other pilots. The later part of the game throws boss battles at you with enemies that have pumped up stats. There exists cheese to deal with this, but it is rather aggravating.

_childDocuments_.review: SINGLEPLAYER:The singleplayer is just awful. Arsenal progression is agonizingly slow for a mech game, the dialogue and story is essentially a bad anime. Everyone betrays you, you win, and then you're friends again next mission. There are multiple missions where you are not supposed to defeat the enemy arsenal and yet doing so is incredibly easy, so of course the game just makes their VP(HP) never drop below 1. Repeatedly after defeating someone who has betrayed you, immortals, or other arsenals someone will swoop in say, "You did a great job holding out this long!" Before finishing off the boss.There's no tension, everything is easy and yet the dialogue is constantly condescending to the point of annoyance. Not to mention again the countless betrayals that we just make up afterwards. Oh there's also an icecream shop to give you bonuses, I resolved to never use it. Don't do that, you need to eat 20 cones to unlock an important section of the factory to design more arsenal parts.MULTIPLAYER:Allows for progression in both currency, blueprints, and parts. All progression is significantly faster than the singleplayer campaign. I highly recommend getting to rank C, eating your ice cream, and then never touching the campaign again in favor of multiplayer.I bought the game for PvP and I am skeptical that there's any real depth there but I haven't had enough experience with it yet to know that for sure.GAMEPLAYArsenals take no damage when knocked down.. Why? Knockback and knockdown are incredibly annoying, even after building an arsenal to resist these things it happens too often. The AI has its resistances boosted through the absolute roof in comparison to players, what hits players for 1000 might hit an AI for 100, the AI also do drastically less damage to you than another player will. It's extremely jarring to the point of almost being a different game.Flight is awful, I can't stand it. It takes some serious effort to make flying in a game not fun, but they pulled it off. For some reason falling is faster than trying to fly downward. If you fall to hit the ground you get locked in an animation (stats available to reduce) but it's impossible to get on the ground quickly because if you try to turn your thrusters back on at the last moment it thrusts you upwards. That's right, anytime you activate your thrusters it boosts you straight up a little, you can't just activate them to arrest your fall or stay level. So going down is this awkward dance of falling, boosting up, and then flying back at the ground slowly. Maneuvering around is way harder than it ever should've been for a fast mech that can fly.
_childDocuments_.name: DAEMON X MACHINA

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to give this game a positive review but it barely scratches the "ok" bar for me, the core mechanics are solid and the movement system is nice and of course the music is great but thats where the praise ends.The shop and factory system are largely irrelevant since you'll end up looking for parts and weapons with slots to add up more stats to them so you'll be mostly unlocking blueprints as a side thing and even then you may end up using just one particular set of parts and never upgrade from those.While I wasn't expecting for a stellar storytelling the campaign is just terrible I'm sorry, you play as the regular silent mc who doesn't even gets to say anything during the, very barebones, interactions you have during mission briefings leading to not be very invested in anything you come across the whole game even when you're meant to "feel" something and the story in itself pretending to do a "2deep4u" without actually being deep at all and having a very superficial narration on top of being extremelly linear without any kind of deviation, you don't even get branching missions which is weird considering they obviously took a lot of inspiration from AC.If you're looking for a somewhat mindless mecha action game with storyline sprinkles then grab this game during an offer.I'm really sorry since I'm more or less a mech junkie but this barely made it into an "serviceable" category.

_childDocuments_.review: Decided to give this a go since it reminded me of Armored Core back in the day. Here are my Pros & Cons.Pros:* The combat feels great in both long and short range battles.* Being able to customise your mech and also harvest parts from other mechs is nice.* Graphically pleasing, even for scenery far away in the distance.* Multiplayer is decent.* Up -gradable items are cool.* Melee is awesome but does feel very overpowered.Cons:* Shop does not work as you cannot buy anything!? _childDocuments_.review: I'm afraid I haven't really enjoyed much of the game.While the combat has a number of elements that could make it interesting - multiple resources to manage, a variety of weapons that are effective at different ranges, the ability to equip your mech with different parts to suit different roles - the actual combat itself doesn't feel good. The machineguns sound as though they're using a stock machinegun sound - very weak and slow for what should be a hail of bullets. Enemies don't really react to damage - they either die or they don't die. While the player can suffer conditions in battle like mech limbs breaking, this doesn't really seem to happen much with the enemies. The one foe I've had trouble with so far was only difficult because he kept dashing around the place, which made it hard for me to lock onto him.This means (for me, at least) that combat is about keeping the enemy close enough and in my field of view. Then I just press 1 and hold down both mouse buttons until someone needs their mech repaired. Occasionally I tap Q in the hopes that it'll speed up the process. It usually doesn't do much.At one point, two out of the three mechs I was fighting fell into water and drowned. It wasn't even a map with a whole lot of water in it.The Ice Cream Parlor feels completely tacked-on. Its bonuses have nearly no impact on battle (how is being 3% faster at throwing grenades going to help me?).The Exploration mode feels... unpleasant. The corridors are nearly all identical in appearance - if it weren't for the fact there's a map, I would've gotten lost. As it was, I merely got stuck - I assume I didn't find and kill every enemy I could and thus some doors wouldn't open. But weapons and equipment are most plentiful in that mode, so I feel as though I have to play it in order to progress.The story didn't do much to pull me in - largely because I didn't care much for the characters. Several of them seemed stock, one-note, or both. The guy who's a professional, the guy who only cares about money, the guy who's devoted to protecting humanity, the guy who's serving the guy who's devoted to protecting humanity, the sister of the guy who's devoted to protecting humanity...That, and the mid-battle quips that play in gameplay would play regardless of the story - so a character could be deathly serious in a cutscene, and then silly in battle.On the one hand, DAEMON X MACHINA does allow you to be a giant mech skating around a battlefield dual-wielding mech-sized machine guns. On the other hand, those mech-sized machineguns don't feel very strong, and the combat felt almost too simple.There are other things that do deserve merit, despite all I've said. The designs of some of the enemies is interesting - I especially liked the aircraft that could contort itself like a dragon. But the game as a whole is not something I'd recommend for $30 USD, let alone 60.

_childDocuments_.review: TL, DR; If you're into mech games, especially ones that make you feel like a freakin' robot superman, then this game is for you. everything that isn't the gameplay could probably use a bit more tweaking, but the moment to moment gunplay, mech customization, and super satisfying movement makes this the best mech game in years. Buy it on PC! This game was aggressively marketed on the nintendo switch, where it really just kinda fell flat, limited by the console. But now, oh boy, it's glorious 1080p, 200fps, mech-shootin-lootin goodness. it's optimized well and is incredibly fun and satisfying to play.PROS:-this game runs very, very well, especially compared to the original nintendo switch version it's ported from. I played the demo on switch and genuinely enjoyed it, but terrible performance issues plagued my experience and I never ended up buying the game. thankfully, it was announced on PC, with a max FPS of around 200 (buttery smooth in my experience, even though I capped it at 120 for stability). the game runs super well, with some stunning visual effects that are beautiful to look at in 1080p. this is the definitive version of the game.-the gameplay is simple, yes, but addictive. there are bad enemy robots. you shoot and murder them. some special enemy mechs can be looted, and you can grab their gear and make it your own. you can find machine guns, pistols, armor, helmets, and even some really f*cking cool swords that kill pretty much anything in a single hit. it does get monotonous at times, but the core gameplay of being able to zip around, launch some missiles, shoot some lead, and slice and dice feels great, especially on mouse and keyboard. this game feels so amazingly smooth, and has a great amount of customizable options on PC as well.-the movement is FRESH. you can surf along the ground, and just zip through the skies, all the while destroying anything that stands up to you. there's even a really nice training area where you can test out new weapons, armor pieces, or modified parts that can change things about your mech (for example, your max speed, or a faster falling option). you can also pick up cars and toss them like baseballs at your enemies. what else do you need to hear?-customization is GREAT! There's a pretty robust character creator, even though you really only see them in headquarters, cutscenes, and a few select missions. But the mech customization is what everyone's here for. and it is amazing. sometimes a bit overwhelming, but there is a plethora of options for those looking to create a badass machine of destruction or those who just wanna min-max the crap outta their metal monster. you can find gear off fallen enemies, or buy new ones, or [ay to have it researched. you can get guns, armor, and supplemental abilities for your mech this way. thankfully, you can carry multiple weapons as well, so you can carry a katana AND a bazooka. or you can dual wield bazookas. do that. it's great.CONS:-the gameplay, while good, can get a little monotonous at times. sometimes it feels like a grind, but its the most damn fun grind i've had in a long time.-story feels generic and somewhat predictable. it tries to be deep and existential (like, say, neir: automata) but fails miserably. it definitely has its moments, and some rad as hell setpieces, but ill be thinking more about the gameplay than the story.NEUTRAL:-this game is anime as hell, right down to the over-the-top voice acting and sometimes cringy dialogue. But i genuinely enjoyed some of the lines, and even if the writing falls flat sometimes, the voice actors went HARD on this game, and each character fully delivers. if you love anime, you'll love this. if you don't... this game may be a bit much for you.-the music is mostly hard rockin' guitars. i'm here for it; it gets me amped as hell. it's a good fit for an over the top game.-ONLINE! haven't played it yet, but there's apparently PVP and PVE coop missions, so that's gonna be rad.in closing, this is the best mech game you can buy right now on steam. it has a ton of awesome customization, as well as meaty single player and multiplayer options. support this dev and show them they made the right choice bringing it to steam, the way this game was clearly meant to be played. nintendo, i love you, but this game belongs on PC, and i wouldn't have it any other way.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely hold off on buying it and wait for a sale. If you're really looking for a fun arcade game, or wanted to try the Mecha genre out, then you should maybe consider sticking with similar games like EDF that has a great game loop and is entertaining throughout.The combat works well with mouse and keyboard, but it feels like the game had controller in mind with auto-aim and more focus towards an effective range for each weapon, which is of the likes of the MHW port. The game starts off slow at first as getting weapons can be tough if they are gained solely through the main story, but it later picks up after the first few ranks. Where the gameplay starts to decline is towards the latter half of the game once you start getting used to the game. The focus shifts to a more repetitive mission structure where enemies become similar and fights become more drawn out, only interrupted by some unique events and boss fights that are far and few in between.Most of the negative reviews, which there is only a handful to my surprise, describe it as "bland". This is probably the best way to describe the story with its large cast of extremely shallow characters. Even if it is typical for a game like this to have little story, there was so much missed potential with the factions in the game. The characters, which are in their own mercenary groups, and even the minor characters in the form of corporate-like consortiums, tease you at the beginning of the game that you could join them, summarizing who they are and what their philosophies are. The problem is that they do not influence you in any way other than tricking you into thinking that the missions are not carbon copies of each other. It feels if there was a way to actually interact with the characters, it could give the story at least some depth and something to strive for instead of moving along with the story as some freelance merc who is going along with every mission without question.With that being said, I could tolerate that the story was linear and may not have a strong cast of characters. But after completing the main story, I found that there was not much else other than going into multiplayer to farm out bosses exclusive to that mode, in order to get end game equipment. The only thing that motivated me to continue playing after finishing the main story was the customization options in the game for the mech and even your character with a lot of bizarre body modifications which essentially turns you into a bulky cyborg resembling your mech.I enjoyed the game for the mech combat and customization, but this is not a game that I would recommend at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: DAEMON X MACHINA

_childDocuments_.review: The true sequel and successor to the Armored Core franchise right down to the gun arms and snipers that were left out of AC6. This game has everything the older AC games had without the dumb souls-esque bosses and stupid flask/repair kit system. The Arsenal which is the mech even has momentum behind its movements like the old AC games and unlike AC6 where the armored cores hold no momentum and can do a 180 while assault boosting instantaneously. DAEMON X MACHINA is a love letter to fans of the genre whereas AC6 is a hate letter.

_childDocuments_.review: My hours are a lie. I have an additional 370+ on Switch, plus however long I spent on my playthrough of the Epic Games version.  You can also throw in the 65+ hours I spent playing the game's prototype.It goes without saying, this is basically Armored Core lite. Though on the other hand, this is also, generally, a love letter to the mecha genre.From the fast gameplay, to the various niche references you could find here and there, to Char and Amuro's Japanese VA's literally being present, heck, even Shoji (Macross & Armored Core) is here as the mechanical designer.But, in my opinion, this game is basically Armored Core X Ace Combat X Zone of the Enders X Mobile Suit Gundam (with a hint of Evangelion, maybe.) It helps that the composers previously worked on Ace Combat 4, 5, 6, 0, and Assault Horizon...Plus the fact that getting into this, I was coming from Ace Combat X: Skies of Deception.Specifically, I would say this is Ace Combat X Armored Core, but more-so Ace Combat (story-wise at least.)The gameplay, I would say seems like a mix between Armored Core 4/ For Answer, and Armored Core V/ Verdict Day. Heck, the mechs in the games, Arsenals, look a lot like the ACs from Armored Core V.Customization, while lacking in some areas, is also something that can be played around with. Not to mention the game breaking builds you can find in, say, PVP. Moreover, I wish parts had more variety, both functionally and aesthetically. There's slight differences, sure, but people aren't kidding when they say the silhouettes are more or less the same. (Still, I guess Armored Core isn't that much better in some places, I suppose.) Meanwhile, even if kinda useless, I really wish Outer Plugsuits and Edit Arsenals were more diverse. I'm talking collectables that you can get and whatnot. But, they're reduced to DLC...Is the game easy? Yeah, pretty much. But I feel like it's by design. Remember, when this came out (2019), mecha was kinda "dead", untouched. Though, difficulty lies in the Coop bosses. (Especially Eclipse and Zeruchroar.) Either way, you end up feeling like a Demi-God or a Demon. (See what I did there?) The game feels great to play.Is the story cheesy, over-the-top, and convoluted? Oh, totally. Frankly, most of the actual lore is in the sourcebook, and thus, can't be found in-game, sadly. Even so, I enjoy the world-building. Just wish it was expanded upon.Is the game flawed? Of course. No game is perfect, and frankly, this one was developed in a span of 2-3 years. But, I wouldn't have it any other way. Even if a base, it's pretty damn good for what it is.My main gripes with DXM have to start with the lack of Outer usage/ Outer combat, mechanically speaking. For those who don't know, Outers are basically super-humans. (Possibly a reference to New-Types, actually. Perhaps even Enders-- Yup, I hear it now, lol.) Basically, you can get out your mech in this game, but you can't exactly do much. Like, just imagine if Outers could fight each other with some form of CQC. After all, our characters in the game are quite powerful on their own. I'd like to see that portrayed to its fullest. Heck, in the story's ongoing retelling, Star Reclaimer, it mentions that they're strong enough to punch holes in walls and dent the ground.Still, I really love the perspective of things as a mere human compared to the machines you face or pilot. I like to think that the devs scaled everything according to the Rookie. Things like buildings, stairs, seats, even cars, they're scaled properly, for the most part. There's even some stairs you can walk up! Albeit they're only present in like 3 maps max, but still.Secondly, I feel like the lobby especially is lacking. Would've been cool to see more of the world outside of the Battlefields. Something reminiscent of the "Daily Life" mode from the Attack on Titan games.Then, obviously, while the story is interesting, it's also pretty lacking. (Though, personally, I still don't get the "too many characters" complaint. I mean, you're working alongside 4 large consortiums and about a dozen Mercenary groups. If anything, the roster's rotation is a little too fixed. Still, I guess that's why the other players exist. To fill the void. (Would be nice to see cannon fodder mercs though...))Speaking of players and the story, it would've been pretty cool if you could go through the game with at least one other player. That's a really common complaint, actually. But, who knows, maybe someone'll mod that in, if possible.Another thing that would be cool is a proper single-player arena mode, to take a page out of Armored Core's book. The lack of it just feels...odd. Maybe at least an endless mode of sorts.Lastly, I  wish you could freely explore the maps. Say Free Flight from the Ace Combat games. I mean, some of the maps are huge. Back during the prototype, I got a kick out of just walking through Grace City as an Outer. The Black Lotus missions gave you much space too. And the fight against Grief on the mission "Prevent Data Capture" is my favorite...Even with his plot armor. And like, imagine just traversing the area as an Outer, indulging yourself in the lands of Oval, your Arsenal sitting at a distance, almost watching over you from afar.And overall, I just...really love this game, man. [Edit 2: And the fact that I played through the story again just to get the achievements (since they didn't auto-unlock with the cross save) translates that much.] I just wish it utilized itself more, and that it was more popular...I'd say this is my first mech game, but I played LBX on the 3DS prior. Plus some of the Transformers games, if they count. Even so, this game reintroduced me to mecha, and man, what an introduction...I really do want to see this newfound IP built upon. Here's to Titanic Scion....I've spent about 2 hours writing this. Geez...

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about the story and the anime cliches, so I'll address that first. You just have to accept going in that it's going to be cheesy. It's going to have characters waxing poetic about the futility of war before getting into their 30 foot robots to do battle. It's going to have caricatures of stereotypes that will make you cringe at times. If that REALLY bothers you, this game probably isn't for you. If you can accept it and just enjoy the schlockiness of it all, dive right in. Also, if you set the VA to Japanese, you'll probably recognize a lot of the actors and actresses from popular animes and other games. For everyone else, here's what your money gets you: A fully voice acted campaign (Japanese and English), an in-depth character and mech customization system that rivals some RPG's, a meaningful progression system and tons of SOLID mecha gameplay. PVP and PVE online as well to keep things interesting. The "Arsenel" mecha, as the game calls them, are nimble and deadly, and can be customized with decals, numbers, colors, and every flavor of destructive weapon you can think of. Want to build an air superiority mecha that spews hundreds of missiles in every direction as it rips around the sky? You got it chief. How about a super-heavy, thicc-armor explosive boy? Absolutely. This game lets you approach each mission however you want. The campaign is satisfying and will teach you how to progress in the game, but the replayability comes with the multiplayer. It's sometimes tough to find a lobby because this game doesn't have a ton of people playing, but the co-op maps and boss fights are so much fun, and the rewards carry over to your campaign mecha (and vice versa). Your actual character plays a role besides just the hangar, too, you can spec yourself out to be a force to be reckoned with even outside of your mech. The upgrades give your character cybernetic enhancements that visually change the model in addition to the bonuses you receive.I highly recommend this game, and will even recommend that if it piques your interest you should consider it at full price to let more publishers know there is a market for this sort of game.The only real "Con" that I have come across, for me, is the lack of FOV selection. The game is a console port (don't let that scare you, it's a good port), but one of the relics of that process is the narrow and sometimes restricting FOV. Other than that, it runs perfectly, the "cell-shaded" stylized graphics add to the charm and hide the lower poly environments really well.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game with a deep and incredible plot, you won't find it here.  You won't really find much in the way of tolerable characters in the single player portion, either.  But what you will find a proper, enjoyable, and fantastic high speed mech action game.Character customization is solid, with many options to pick from for both sexes.  After starting, you can make modifications to your character that both affect stats and abilities (even adding new abilities that you otherwise wouldn't have) and change your appearance.  But, while the modifications do grant benefits in various areas, if you don't want your character to look like a full android at the end, it's very viable to play without getting many or any of them.  And if you decide you don't like how you look or what your stats are, you can reset them to become fully human again, though you do have to purchase any mods all over again (it is a full reset, after all).Now, to one of the most important pieces of a mech game, the mech customization.  While this game doesn't have the level of customization and tuning as the likes of Phantom Crash or Armored Core, it's still excellent.  Each piece of equipment has its own stats while affecting the overall performance of your mech.  Each part is swappable, and each part affects its appearance.  Now, your mech will always have the same overall design, but each part has its own look.  Just note that if you're using a skin (such as the Prototype Arsenal), you won't see any appearance changes unless you remove the skin.But the biggest question is: How well does it play?  Simply put, it's fantastic.  I bought it for the Switch before and enjoyed it, but found it cumbersome to play using the Switch controls.  On the PC with a keyboard/mouse setup, it feels just so....natural.  This is the proper platform for it without question.  The settings options are lacking, but it performs incredibly well on max settings on a 3 year old PC.  And the gameplay itself is fast and furious, but never overwhelming.This game gets compared favorable to Armored Core, but I don't think that's quite fair to either.  That said, if you like Armored Core, you'll also like Daemon X Machina.  It's a fantastic game that stands on its own merits, and it's a rare port that doesn't just work, but is almost flawless.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Armored Core, Front mission Evolved or other fast paced skatey mech games, this game is for you.As stated in negative reviews they slam the characters, which is sort of warranted however they still hold this game in the same boat with AC which still had bad character though.At this moment this game is very approachable for people new to this genre unlike the entries of AC, there still is alot of specialization that can be made to perfect your mech for a mission but its not as important for the majority of enemies.as an AC fan is this game on par, eh sorta, arcade mech fighter yes, amount of attention to detail and specialization sadly no. but it makes up for it. For being the only modern AC like game on PC.By far the best fast paced mech game on PC, I am a long time Armored Core fan and with nothing on the horizon for that I had to look else where and what I found is amazing, the art style is unique and actually works. The gun play is engaging and managing incoming and outgoing fire is a feeling i havent felt since my days on my xbox360 being able to boost side to side and dodging or making a super heavy mech and just soaking. pros>skating mechs>indiscriminate fire>ultra light, light, medium and heavy mech types>Huge amount of weapon types and modifications >Huge amount of armor sets and you can change each individual module eg. Left arm, right arm, legs, torso, head, processor>Gun arms FREAKING GUN ARMS >custom pilots>dogcons>cant pet dog> a fair bit of release DLC though, none are game impacting just alot of cosmeticsin short, i cannot recommend this game enough it is a god send to the pc platform for mech games, if you enjoy AC games you will enjoy this. _childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is decent, on par with most mech games I've played. The early game is quite enjoyable, but once you get to C-rank and above, it basically becomes a gacha (gambling/farming) game-- next enemy is high spec, so you need better parts, and those parts can only be constructed by other parts, which have an X% chance of dropping from a few specific enemies in like two levels. This makes getting any pieces of advanced weaponry/armor for your mech nigh impossible, unless you get a lucky loot drop or are willing to farm for a few hours.My final gripe with the game is the story, or what passes for it. _childDocuments_.review: Disappointing.• Gameplay is very floaty. You never feel like you're piloting a mech ; feels more like a human-shaped spaceship, with no weight or momentum whatsoever.• Game is VERY easy. I haven't cared about the cybernetic augmentation system, or the Factory, or the Shop, nothing. Just been playing using the starter weapons and I'm deleting almost everything. I don't even have to dodge; I often just a-pose in the air while shooting the objective and ignoring all enemies, and they are so weak they can't even scratch my mech. Did the devs even test this game? I am under constant fire in most missions and yet they seem to never really do anything to me. Why is there a system to go on foot if my mech has some kind of god mode?• NPCs are incredibly annoying. They're just anime stereotypes who never shut up, yelling overly dramatic lines trying to convince me that the mission is REALLY exciting and challenging while I'm just holding down forward + the fire button and facerolling through the entire game. • Songs are cool but feels like there's only five of them and the game just keeps them on loop with no rhyme or reason.• Pacing is awful ; you don't fly to the mission objectives, the game spawns you on top of them. Every mission so far has just been, spawn, shoot the enemies around the spawn, loot and leave.• Graphics are pretty meh. My phone has games that look better than this. Should we really celebrate this runs on 60fps? I feel like the playstation 2 could've ran it just as well.The only reason I'm going forward with the game is because I keep hoping it will get difficult and interesting somewhere along the road but all my friends either refunded or warned me: it stays braindead easy all the way. If you want a game that challenges you, asks you to learn about its mechanics, or has a mech that feels like a mech, stay away from this overrated noise.TL;DR: I expected Armored Core meets Deus Ex, got some braindead phone game instead.

_childDocuments_.review: The game mixes a lot of things in the right way, and some not right at all. The story is almost non-existent, and told through flat, boring textboxes. The "cutscenes" are just characters making random gestures while spitting badly acted lines at you.The multiplayer is almost completely dead. You can still link up with friends, but good luck finding anyone in the lobby.There's almost no native controller support, so unless you have an XBOX controller, you're stuck with KB+M controls which are horrendous. Or you could use Xinput or something.The graphics, while not very impressive on a technical level, still look amazing. The cel-shading really makes it feel like a mecha anime.The music is hit or miss. I liked some of the tracks, but it's mostly metal with some techno beats over it. It fits with the atmosphere but if you're older than 15, you'll probably be over it quick.The combat and customization is where this game shines. Like many other players, I do see the Armored Core influence in this game. The difference is that in AC you feel like you're driving a tank with limbs. In DeM, it's a bit quicker, and more fluid.This game is fun. Maybe not $60 fun, but it is a catch for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that wears its inspirations on its sleeve, the only sequel Armored Core will probably ever get due to Dark Souls exploding in popularity, and overall a damn good game that suffers only due to it's brevity. I like to compare this game to Armored Core: For Answer due to the fact that just about every mech you could think of can work so long as you have enough ammunition to actually complete a mission. Heavy tank with smgs and homing rockets on your shoulders? Sure go for it. How about a frame as lightly armored and mobile as a wasp with a sword arm and a sniper rifle? Absolutely, just make sure to not get slapped around or you'll die like the bug you're masquerading as.If the very short single player is the only reason you're buying this, consider buying it on sale, as you can beat the entire story within 10-20 hours easily, even if you wind up grinding for parts and whatnot.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a good Mech Game for the first in a series, similar in play style to Armoured Core.   Jet Mechs More so than Tank Mechs.This part of the game is actually really good. Once you have started unlocking gear by developing enemy dropped gear  in the factory,  you have a bunch of options to choose from that can allow you to mix and match the best features of every mech to make one that completely fits your play style. The story is very Japanese in the way Final Fantasy is.  Some of the Characters are interesting. But most of them are Japanese Anime Cliches. They keep you in the dark for as long as possible, to build tension, and and wonder, so that you have the same perspective as the character But that does cause some problems. the Game has many characters and because it tries to take its time at the begining, towards the end, all the character development happens all at once. and so even the big reveals on the best characters don't have enough time to stick.  The ending is open. The themes are very reminiscent with Nier Automata. Themes of Fate, choice, what it means to be human, but it doesn't take enough time to fully develop them, it leaves you wishing for more in that regard.  The Music Is killer. The Gameplay is fun. Its a Good Mech game and it runs pretty damn great on a steam deck too! I look forward to Daemon Ex Machina 2 . Now that they have some experience with this IP, and learned in creating this game, They should be able to make something really amazing with the next entry.

_childDocuments_.review: I know that one of the people in charge of the project was an old Armore Aore dev. So obviously there's a lot of things that remind me of the particular series.The part it gives out more then AC are those; pilot customization and gameplay. Actual characters design, cinematics and some new weapons that armored core never did. Great easy controls, some interesting way to collect parts and fight giant machine which in some case you can deconstruct and use their weapons. Oh and being able to lift cars, trucks and containers to use them as bombs. Its always funny to kill something by swinging a signpost at them.It does lack though, the rich variety of parts that AC has, the model for the mech is mostly the same humanoid, with the regulard knee joints. (AC goes from reverse joints, four legged, hover and tank thread.) The sheer amount of missions that AC has vs DXM is pretty telling and ac tends to have a more in depth tit bit story telling. DXM though manages to make a pretty good story that I enjoyed, but linear and didn't make you work too hard to get it.All in all loved the game, a bit short, but its kind of the game that I love because it shows some soul and good concept that I hope they can improve on in a possible next installation. Mech games are few and far in between and this just made my week.

_childDocuments_.review: The producer of the Armored Core series brings you Armored Core with the speed cranked up to 11. You know, because From Software is too busy printing money with Souls games to make another Armored Core any time soon. That's pretty much what Daemon X Machina is.If you were interested in Daemon X Machina, this is the place to get it. The high speed was actually a problem on console, since keeping on target to mecha boosting around was pretty much impossible with a stick. This is no longer an issue with mouse and keyboard.That said, if you actually asked me, I would still say I prefer the PS3/360 Armored Core titles over Daemon X Machina. While I love Daemon X Machina's aesthetic (though I don't know how I feel about the shading), it's missing some of that heavy war machine feel of the Armored Core games. The control feel of the mecha are on point (with some intentional clunk built in, like having a short recovery time while landing hard), but the sound design doesn't quite pack the punch of a proper AC game.Still, this is the closest thing you've got to Armored Core since Verdict Day, all the way from back from 2013, and it's the only notable option on PC.As a note: The translation isn't great, so if you're a stickler about this sort of thing, that should be noted. It's not like it totally misses the mark, but there are some parts where I'm pretty sure the translator(s) just didn't have enough knowledge to properly translate bits, like translating "aa" as "ah" despite it being used as an affirmative in context, meaning it should have been translated as something like "yeah", or "right". Otherwise there's constant general inaccuracies (or rather non-direct translations) that can probably be chalked up to "localization" choices or attempting to get proper lines for lip syncing (the inaccuracy persists in scenes where you don't see character's faces directly though, so that can't be all it is), since the general gist is correct. You can just set the language to Japanese if you can handle doing so though.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great Armored Core style mech game, but it lacks content which has already killed the player base. You will complete the main story in about 12-14 hours, and then focus on unlocking all of the multiplayer boss gear. While unlocking gear, you will also pray to the RNG gods that better equipment modifications drop as well. The only problem is that it seems like only 3 other people play this game, and all they want to do is grind the exploration mission "Unidentified Facility II" and PVP. You can grind the bosses with the support of three other AI support units, but they are worthless. You pretty much have to solo the bosses at that point. That being said, I would advise anyone on the verge of buying this game to wait till it goes on sale. I don't foresee a massive influx of new players anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: This game kinda blows compared to the AC series as a Mecha game. _childDocuments_.review: The game itself is fairly okay. Some of the design decisions are definitively a little flawed, but the gameplay loop is alright. Destroy mechs, get new parts, improve your mech, take down bigger, badder mechs.However, where this game completely flops is the cooperative part. YOU MUST PLAY THE GAME IN SINGLEPLAYER TO PLAY WITH YOUR FRIEND. I'm not saying like, you need to do a tutorial or two and then you can play. I mean the ENTIRE game is locked on your single player progress. This means that if you and your friend buy this game, you both need to finish this game on your own to play the multiplayer content.This is a major flaw to a "cooperative" game. Why was it impossible to provide a full-coop experience the entire game? Instead, you and your coop parters are either forced in tight dungeons or large open maps that are completely separated from the main story and focuses only on getting better loot.If you think you can enjoy an average mecha game taking down plenty of robots SP only, then you still should've fun with this one. If you went in thinking that you'd have fun with your friend - think again.
_childDocuments_.name: DAEMON X MACHINA

_childDocuments_.review: Not amazing, but if you're waiting for a new armored core game this can tide you over for a while.Story is weak, most of the characters are uninteresting. Some interesting plot threads are in there, but most of them don't lead anywhere.The gameplay is fun, but a bit shallow. Combat feels pretty fast, but is very straightforward.Your Arsenal (mech) has some customization, but is not as in depth as I would like. Fairlyshallow weapon pool, with most you get through the game just being a better version of an existing one.The "skill tree" feels pretty unimpactful, and forces visual changes to your character. There is one mission where you are not in your mech, and I guess some of the skills could help there. The blink skill at the end of one of the trees is kinda nice I guess.I ran the Exploration dungeons a few times to grab some parts, and they are a decent way to spend some extra time. But they are just procedural tiles, and the difficulty feels pretty random. Sometimes the final enemy is just one basic unit, other times its three enemies that dash across the room in .2 seconds and blast 1/5 of your hp per hit.Overall the game is fine. It's fun, but not amazing. Worth if its on sale, iffy at full price though.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has very cool designs for mechs, weapons, and characters. The DLC isn't necessary, and only adds cosmetic features. Most of the bosses are just as durable as you, or moreso if you don't make a proper man's Arsenal with high durability (or you're fighting the BIG immortals), so don't just expect to melt every problem in a few seconds. Upgrading weapons and Arsenal parts is a must, but it isn't terribly grindy if you know what you're aiming for to begin with. The last bossfight is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slog though, and if you don't use the containers on the ground around the center of the map you are going to rip your hair out as you get hit by yet another power laser from 4 directions.Other reviews pointed it out already, but yeah, the overall story is confusing as hell, and I genuinely can't grasp what the goal of the (actual) antagonists really was. Also, avoid AI allies that use a lot of weapons that knock down and blow back enemy Arsenals, because there is a period of time where an Arsenal in invulnerable while getting up but can still be knocked back again, effectively dragging out Arsenal battles for far longer than they have to be.All in all, a fun game, if not a little frustrating at times. 7.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Daemon X Machina is one of the best mech games I've played. It's the first (on PC anyways) to really give you a Eastern Mech experience. The mechs in this are more Gundam style. They aren't giant lingering mechs you typically see in Western games, but rather nimble, agile mechs with a plethora of weaponry, capable of zipping around the battlefield both on land and in the air. Anyways, you've probably already heard of this game as it was previously only available on the Nintendo Switch, and yes, this is a PC Port of that. However, the PC Port is actually REALLY good. I haven't experienced any issues and get a stable 120 FPS with no problems (my monitor is a 144hz, but is set to 120hz) and the game does go up to 144 FPS if that's your thing. GAMEPLAY-The gameplay is straightforward, you make a character, you're a mercenary piloting a mech, fighting both human enemies and AI enemies (as in, like, an AI in the story is controlling them, no human pilots in them). You can customize the loadout of your mech, meaning each armor piece can be chosen, same for weaponry, and you have the ability to carry 2 backup weapons into battle, which you can switch between on the fly, for a total of 4 main weapons. You also have support weapons (i.e. missiles) and auxiliary gear (think boosters for example). Primary weapons range from large mech-sized guns to giant metal Swords and Shields. -You also have a skill tree which affects both your human character (both gameplay and cosmetic changes) and your mech. -You can eject from your mech in battle (default key G), so the destruction of your mech is not necessarily the end of the fight. -Combat against AIs is pretty simplistic, as they're all easily countered and dodged, however human enemies tend to be a big step up in difficulty, as they have varied weapons and can range from blasting you with rockets to zipping up and slashing you. As a sidenote, if you slash an enemy mech while they're slashing you, you get an awesome QTE where you mash "F" to overpower your enemy's blade and deal a heavy blow to them. -Customization As I stated earlier, you have a fair bit of customization with how you play, choose your favorite weapons, armor, and pick a playstyle, but you also have a decent character creator and the ability to use preset appearances for Mechs which override individual armor pieces, although some cosmetics are locked behind DLC though. It's got decent customization for mechs, although I'd call the character creator for your human characters OK, not great, not bad, just OK. Also, while I'm on the topic of human customization, your skill tree in the game features cybernetic enhancements which do affect your appearance, so by the end of the game your human character will look like something out of Deus Ex or Cyberpunk 2077, only Anime'd up. It could be a positive or negative depending on how you look at it, if you want Robo-Legs, Arms, Eyes, and Cybernetic enhancements on your character, you probably won't mind, but if you want to be a pure, no cybernetics human, you can only really be that if you neglect the skill tree. Overall I'd say it was worth the 50 I paid for it. It's the Gundam Mech Game I've craved to have on PC for so long. Don't get me wrong, the western mechs in Battletech and Mechwarrior are cool and all too, but zipping around in a Japanese Gundam Style Mech is far cooler IMO. This game delivers that.

_childDocuments_.review: As many people may wonder, "Is this game like Armored Core"? The answer is "sorta". This is a game where you build a mech from pieces, and load it out to your playstyle. But at the same time the gameplay is both shallower in some areas and deeper in others. I personally like the game very much, and if you like mech games in general this should satisfy that itch. But it does have some things to consider.For example, you will only have two weapons in your hands, your "heavy" weapon (missiles, railguns, drones, ect), and a support device (which can be a weapon, support item like expanded ammo, or even support thrusters). So the mech building is more simple then how games like Armored core got, and ammo is more forgiving as in arcade fashion some enemies will drop ammo on death. However in other areas the gameplay is a bit expanded. You now have an avatar pilot, which occasionally will need to exit the mech to perform actions. Or if your mech goes down you basically can eject and fight a little longer, although as a pilot you will be very limited on foot. At first. Because you can spend money in skill trees that will not only help your pilot perform better in the mech but also grant cybernetic enhancements that can expand what your pilot can do on foot. Such things like have a lase blade in their arm, fly, cybernetic eyes, and so forth. Which also change the avatar when you get such enhancements. The biggest change is how you acquire new parts. Some will be researched in the hanger, some will be by buying them in the shop. But the biggest and fastest mechanic for getting parts is off defeated enemies. When you down an enemy mech you then can take one part off that mech for yourself. Which also has an RNG aspct since these weapons can not only have different versions but slots for putting in enhancements. Which in turn also are gotten from equipment off downed mechs. There is also some quality of life things like you don't pay for repairs or ammo spent. Which is offset by the fact that enhancements for your pilot cost a lot of money. So while you are not spending as much you still will simply be spending it in larger chunks when you do.So long and short, yes I recommend the game if you love mech based games, and/or enjoy building a character into your own playstyle. It may not be quite as complex as the game it is obviously inspired from, but it is an enjoyable game in it's own right. You also do NOT need to get the DLC to enjoy the game, but if you do get it I recommend during a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: An okayish kind of game, if you heard about people comparing this one to the so beloved series of Armored Core, forget about it, since the game isn't that close to complexity. Music so far is not bad, graphics are acceptable, anime styled.  Gameplay wise, the game feels like a mixed copy between AC and those random old Gundam games, so you don't get that entire feel of piloting a styled mech the way AC did. Still, the game is fun on its own, but lacks of parts/guns variety, you will end up not bothering of upgrading your mech and will keep playing with one combination of parts until the finale.  About the story, it is just an underperforming script loaded with lots of anime-like cliches that just make everything cringey and even pulling you out of the main course of the story, making the ending uninteresting.  If you are going to get it anyways, just make yourself a favor, set the voice language to Japanese, this will make the story overall more tolerable than hearing the cringyness of the English dubbing (since the characters you find throughout the story will keep talking, even during missions). 6/10

But enough of these generalizations, lets get into the ratings shall we.Categories For Rating:Combat - 10 PointsCharacter Customization - 10 PointsMech Building - 10 PointsStory - 10 PointsBonus Content - 10 pointsPossible Total Score - 50 PointsCategory Scores after listing pro’s and con’s.Combat: 9/10Character Customization: 7/10Mech Building: 7/10Story: 5/10Bonus Content: 7/10Total Score: 35 points.TLDR: The game is very enjoyable to play, and really the story is the only place I have any major complaints, but for whats inside, I would highly recommend this as it is a very fun mech game, and has a lot of great replay-ability for the long term.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the summary I find describe in a general way my experience with DxM:-Fun but limited gameplay, -Non-sensical history, -Terrible pacing and presentation (most of story is just watching dialog boxes and lackluster game engine made cinemas)-Bad story ending (DxM has two endings, both equally disappointing), Should have included pre-rendered better cinemas for this part at least-Limited to pointless character customization. There are very few times you get to see your avatar during gameplay, as most of the time you are in your arsenal. You only see your avatar on missions hub only or by exiting your arsenal (which is not advisable unless story forces you to). This exacerbates after making "body enchantments" (where you receive physical augmentations) as these overwrites most of your character aesthetic changes.-Acceptable to good weapon diversity,-Lack of DLC (why most of the docs is not available on the west or limited to Switch version only?), -Dying community (it's not a very popular game/genre, so this was actually expected) -Unbalanced PvP (players with full arsenal loadout will demolish newcomers), -Quick matchmaking online room system  (haven't had any issues playing online besides the expected lag while playing with people from distant regions)At the time of writing this (August 11th, 2023) I would only recommend this game if you don't want to spend 60$ on Armored Core 6 (which I think is going to surpass DxM in every aspect) or are just waiting for a sale to acquire it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for a modern Mech game on PC for quite a while. This game definitely scratched that itch.This game is like Zone of Enders and Armored Core had a baby.A lot of people have complained about the story, that it made no sense, it was poorly written, and the voice acting was even worse. I have to agree with most of these points. Yet still I loved this story.The story was definitely designed around the personality of the characters, instead of the characters driving the story. You can tell they had a lot planned for the storyline that never came to fruition (probably because of budget and time constraints). My favorite moment in this game is when I realized that the AI for the characters of the story matched their personalities.While the storyline definitely came up short it did feel like the developers left a lot to be read between the lines, and to be fair my past playthroughs of Armored Core and Zone of the Enders involved skipping all of the story. This story is fast and easy to digest for those that aren't looking to sit and watch, but actively play, and it can all be skipped (with the exception of in battle dialogue, which adds a nice distraction and doesn't need to be skipped). My takeaway from the story is that it left too many things vague and others too direct while being too short. Despite that I still enjoyed it, I wasn't expecting a good story from a mech game anyways.The models for the Mechs in this game are amazing, you can tell this is where the budget ended up going.The world design was lackluster and empty, but the story and location somewhat explain this (very poorly).The textures in this game were ported from the switch and you can tell, even on maximum.The character art design was decent and matched the cel shading style that the rest of the game uses.English Voice actors tried. I'm gonna leave it at that for VA.Music is fine for the genre.Sound effects were good, but nothing special.The AI is a little lack luster beyond the personality point I mentioned earlier, AI Mechs tend to get stuck sometimes until an enemy target is near them (I personally didnt notice this until later in the game, where I had to rely on them more).The difficulty of this game seemed to find a sweet spot, it allows newer players to the mech scene a good time to learn what they like and play around with things before it starts getting difficult. The end game ramps the difficulty up to what I feel is a fair level.This game runs pretty well for being a PC port. The port was done right.Progression could have used some more work, but few modern games are balanced well anyways. They did a good enough job here.I personally think this game deserves a sequel with a better story despite its flaws. Don't buy this game for it's story. The gameplay is fun. The AI is adequate. It is the Modern Customizable Mech game we needed on PC.

_childDocuments_.review: so, coming from being a big armored core fan, and with this being the only thing we've gotten close to it in close to 10 years, its acceptable.  There's two major things I would personally change though.  Less focus on aerial combat being the most major.  It feels so good to zip along the ground in this game but its never really useful or it will have you just repeatedly slap into buildings, and the aerial controls are pretty wonky.  At times it feels like you cant just go from ascending/descending to staying still while in combat because you have to release all of your controls.  The other part, is the story and characters.  ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ are they so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying with a really uninteresting story to go along with.  I love a good ol anime character, but jesus christ they are so cut and dry boring and run of the mill edgy characters.  I find myself skipping literally every cutscene/brief because I can't sit through it.The good though; game looks pretty solid.  A bit much on the particle effects at times but that's where things are going nowadays it seems.  Controls feel very good (aside from flight) and the weapon variation is very entertaining.  The mech parts and weapons all look really nice too, but it would be nice to see some more designs that aren't literally just a white glint slightly altered though.If you want a fun mech game to bide time until we never get AC6, then this is pretty solid.  If you want story and characters to follow, stay the hell away from this mess.

_childDocuments_.review: Capsule Opinion: Buy on sale ($20 or less), the game is only about 16 hours long.Gameplay is a pretty solid hybrid of Armored Core's 1 and 4 with a much heavier leaning on 4.Story is absolute anime-trash and completely worth skipping, every character is a one-dimensional stereotype given flesh.In addition to the story there's a free mission options that effectively lets you replay missions with the story gutted.  There's also a 'rogue' styled mode with procedurally generated bases to explore, as well as a full co-op campaign with various difficulties of each boss.The janky part in comparison to armored core though is the garage system.There is no traditional 'shop'.  Instead when you destroy another mech you can salvage one part of choice from it.You can either use the part, or give it to R&D to experiment on.Any part developed by R&D is given to you free for letting them do work, and then becomes available in the store.So the only parts you have to grind for are the super low level parts to start your research tree.The grind though is a bit silly, you'll always be procuring new toys so you will have new parts, but the cost of everything is super prohibitive.You can also augment your pilot mechanicus style for passive bonuses.  Some much better than others.  I'm like 80% through the main story at this point and I've only once had to actually play as my pilot outside my mech - and like half the augments are pilot improvements.Chain melee is also worthless.Melee is fine, just the chain upgrade for it sucks as it bounces you between nearby enemies (not hitting the same target multiple times)

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Armored Core V or Verdict Day for PC. Like really.For better or for worse, this is a game for Armored Core fans; in other words, if you don't enjoy mech CUSTOMIZATION games, this probably won't be your cup of tea. Inversely, if you're tired of "mech" games that are just reskinned TPS or they just show up as enemies, this should satisfy you nicely, as this is pretty much the only game on Steam to offer both in-depth customization and decent gameplay.As mentioned at the start, the gameplay and overall flow reminds me greatly of ACV/VD than others, although the designs are much closer to AC4/For Answer, and the degree of customization falls somewhere between them. No stabilizers, limited decals (only 1 per part), and greatly simplified assembly; Generator and all boosters are smushed into the Body category, and you can only equip one Back weapon (implemented in DxM as "Shoulder"). Just like ACV/D though, the pylons can store any handheld weapon, so you can have 4 of the same weapons at once. Weapons also come in different variations (Plain, S, L, F, and most recently, M variants), with most spawning with 0-3 expansion slots, which lets you equip enhancements, adding variety and replayability (and grind). (Armor doesn't have variants but can spawn with slots, and Auxiliary/Processors don't have any variations)Gameplay is, well, very Armored Core: they send you to an often reoccurring location, with different mission parameters. Story missions ("Offer Missions") can only be replayed after completing the story, but Free Missions can be repeated as often as you want to grind parts (which you primarily pick up from Arsenal wreckages), money (Rose Queen gives a 25% bonus to Credits, so take her for 25k+ missions), partners (you get many of them by shooting them down in Free Missions), and boss loot (you get research points by killing them, and they rarely drop Blueprints, which allows you to actually craft it).Online/Co-op has 2 components: Exploration and "Multiplayer". Exploration lets you and 3 others fight through a procedurally generated complex, destroying enemies and picking up loot, to face off against 3 super tanky Arsenals at the end; this gives multi-slot equipment for parts that may not have spawned in the Story mode. "Multiplayer" is either playing a playlist of online specific bosses/encounters, or PVP, and is the place where you grind out harder bosses to get exclusive loot (as some Exploration gear can be obtained from normal gameplay).Campaign is anywhere from 20-30 hours (assuming you didn't skip the dialog); the story is a convoluted mess trying to mimic the good ol' From Magic, but falls short in execution. That being said, the English dub is exceptional quality, displaying emotion where appropriate. Overall, if you've played an Armored Core game in the past, you will know what to expect; if you're new to the genre, and flying around with your own customized mech sounds appealing to you (and actually enjoy the Japanese styled robot aesthetic), you could certainly do a lot worse, especially on Steam.8/10, would buy sequel
_childDocuments_.name: DAEMON X MACHINA

_childDocuments_.review: Wow!!! As expected from a team that includes a former producer of Armored Core! This game is HELLA fun for the mecha obsessed! Beyond the builds though, this plays very differently from Armored Core. Daemon X Machina with its own unique features, tying into the plot and world, is successful in establishing an identity for itself.Story is intriguing although a rather confused mess much of the time. But this game is all about the action! Plays really smoothly on high settings on even some of the lower end systems. Not as tough as some Armored Core titles, but not as easy as Another Century's Episode (another From Software mecha series). With a kick-ass soundtrack to boot, as well as multiplayer, you can find yourself spending hours to unlock everything. And a lot of those unlocks are more than just cosmetics!!!!!You want some of those crazy builds? Try the Multiplayer Co-op. No friends or connections? No problem!!! The game even gives you the ability to make a room for yourself and even have AI partners. A pseudo-multiplayer singleplayer! And the co-op missions are unique and provide tough challenges. You can of course take players on in a Versus mode as well. Spec your unit the way you like! Max fire power tank mode, or the speedy melee monster! Perfectly balanced, or harmony in mismatch! Your mech, your style, your rules!!!
_childDocuments_.name: DAEMON X MACHINA

_childDocuments_.review: Small sized mechs? Rock-paper-scissors damage types? Fighting giant machines that can level environment?By all means Daemon x Machina is basically a spiritual successor of Armored Core V/VD but far more digestible.In our present where this kind of 3d mecha action becoming a rarity because a certain company busy with their other franchise, Marvelous First Studio came to the rescue with a quality product.Like shown in the cover players can build and fight in their own mecha. Not only that, players can exchange their own humanity for more legally obtainable enhancements. All of that while thrown into fully voiced intrigues from competing factions. The story itself is simply servicable and the characters can be pretty comical however having said characters so expressive combined with the colorful palette made the world more welcoming.The mech we build have the standard arms on both weapons plus shoulder weapons and an auxiliary. If you were in this rodeo before all of this will be familiar. The unique stuffs are Femto stances which can give you short term tactical options (don't sleep on this) and Outer Body combat or simply on-field pilot combat. Yes you can get out of mech anytime and despite a more niche option you can continue your combat that way. Oh, parts also drops from enemies which is neat. Once you're done with the story and side mission there's one more challenge, the co-op missions. The multiplayer is pretty much dead so you can ignore pvp. Exploration is pretty much for farming and can be done solo. Co-op mission mode however is another beast, it's a monster hunter mode. You can challenge monstrous creatures, well most of them are already went past mere machines, either solo or with other players/AI and experience over the top combat like in the final mission many more times.
_childDocuments_.name: DAEMON X MACHINA

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: Buy the game on a strong sale. Do NOT pay the full price tag of flipping 60 euros. Even if you are a mecha fan. No.. ESPECIALLY if you are a mecha fan. I am really conflicted on this, but I've decided that I disliked this game more than I liked it in the end.pros:- very strong start for a mecha game fan - great and immersive combat for the first couple hours- the voice over team for the English localization was incredible! Clap- amazing soundtrack that makes your head cinema go wild - the concept and idea of piloting mechas in an anime setting... I don't even remember the last time I played a good mecha game, so I was excited to pick this up- the game is enjoyable in coop mode with a friend. Up to 4 people can play together in one lobby.cons (oh boy):- story, the quality noticeably started to drop... further and further... slow and steady. Up to a point where it was impossible for me to understand what was even going on anymore. Characters betraying each other left and right, joining back in with opened arms for them, characters dying/killing each other and coming back with no further explanation.- the ending was an utter disappointment to me. Thats all I can say without spoiling I guess.- the last series of missions and fights (so about the last 10 or so before the final fight) were the same mechanic copypasted over and over. Actually, the whole game was just like this: Fighting the same arsenals over and over and over again. And the AI makes me wanna scratch my eyes out sometimes. They zip around the map like on cocaine, dragging fights out for so long... Stick with ground combat, guys.- characters will just change their personality or view on different topics however they feel like in the moment, in one minute they work together, the next one they kill one another. Everyone is ALWAYS talking about killing each other (because I guess mercenary talk?) but they NEVER actually do it. And if a murder happens which almost feels like an accident everytime, its portrayed as something horrible....?!? The reasons for their actions are absolutely incomprehensible to me most of the time and comes out of the blue. The game adds lore to them whenever it wants to and when it sees trouble to justify confusing plot actions.- cheesy dialogue with badly animated cutscenes. Most of the dialogue happens in a briefing voice channel, which felt like I'm in a virtual novel or something. No effort was put into trying to make these scenes feel at least a little bit lively (text messages with voice over, static avatar pictures of game characters) - very, very limited weaponry. First you think "wow, theres quite a lot of weapons and armor in this game!", then once you figured out the best weapon/armor types, you realize.... you are literally stuck with them throughout the whole game, theres no progression or anything similar, theres no point in equiping or experimenting, you wont get any better weapons than that. And you get them quite early on in the game, too. I wont spoil that, so you can see for yourself.I could think of a couple more things that still nag on me, but I dont wanna deal with this game anymore and be done with it. So heres my warning to you. But then again I did have my couple hours of fun... Get this game on a strong sale. It is definitely not worth 60 euros.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good fix for an armored core type game. At its core its a mech building game, however its also got a heavy anime style to it. This game isnt as demanding as an armored core game, but it fills the void where a literal decade without armored core was (at the time of writing the last armored core game was released in 2013). This game also did some interesting player customization where you could upgrade your character which made you less human and more machine, which is a very consistent theme with the armored core series, however this has a lot less to do with the topics of corperate greed and more to do with being cool mech pilot. Overall this scratched the itch, I would give it a 7 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating 6.0. If you really need a Armored Core itch scratched this is the game. Mechanically identical to AC it was very easy for me to pick up the controls and i had alot of fun with combat. The game doesnt take long to turn stale though. The gear option quickly became limited with very few guns and equipment options. Still overall the combat is where this game shines with enough varying mission objectives to keep its relatively short run time interesting. Now the story on the otherhand was far different. Now i never really played the Armored Core games for their story this game is on a different level of bad. From the ridiculous character designs to the non nonsensical plot, It was by far one of the worst video game stories with some of the worst video game characters of all time! _childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible and unfortunately overlooked at lot of the time. While the game's mission structure can be considered repetitive, the core gameplay those missions center around is the real meat here. Even on my sub-par PC the game runs smooth as butter, and it controls just as smooth. Combat against enemy mechs is frantic and fast paced, while taking on the gigantic boss enemies can fee like a dance once you've figured out their patterns. When it comes to customizing your mech, all the armor pieces, save for the initial starter parts, are all side-grades that focus on different stat layouts instead of being straight upgrades. Meaning you have a huge range of possible options to fine-tune how you want your mech to perform as you collect more armor parts. Weapon progression is a little more linear in upgrades, but is relatively balanced in that stronger high tier weapons have smaller ammo pools than lower tier weapons, which can matter in certain missions that have you fighting tough enemies with few ways to restock your ammo. Keeping a melee weapon on-hand as a back-up is recommended if you don't want to have to resort to punching. The story gets pretty convoluted as it progresses, but it isn't too hard to keep up with if you're paying attention (mostly). The ending gets a bit wack though.

_childDocuments_.review: I am pretty surprised at how positively reviewed this game is.  There's a lot to be desired with this title to the point where I no longer want to play it.  The "bad" simply outweighs the "good" for me.The Good:-Great customization with mechs with body parts and weaponry-Decent loot mechanics-Co-op with certain game modesThe Bad:-In instances where finer movement is needed it often feels like you are fighting the controls-Terrible "Flight Mode" controls where vertical movement is concerned-ATROCIOUS sound design to the point it feels like your weaponry/actions has little impact (eg, your hand weapon firing a caliber the size of tank-shells sounds like a pea-shooter)-Basic AI-"Slamming it until its dead" feel of game-play-A cell-shaded art style that is beautiful at certain times, then horrific at others (especially with certain characters)If you can truly forego the negatives, then I implore you to never buy this game at full price.  I think the game has a lot of positive reviews due to Armored Core nostalgia goggles, which is well and fine -- but it is grossly misleading for a game that does not feel it has earned a Triple-A price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the Armored Core games, this game is for you. It is a spiritual successor in pretty much every way. Combat is fast-paced and fun, and building your AC (uh, excuse me, Arsenal) is almost as fun as blowing nerds up with it. Just now starting to dip my toe into multiplayer but it looks fairly straightforward, with coop and versus options.Unfortunately, in true Armored Core fashion, the story is utter garbage. Seriously, just skip all the cutscenes and all the inane dialogue breaks in missions, because you will not be missing anything. The characters are wooden and impossible to care about and there are TOO MANY OF THEM.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure there are already droves of armored core related comments giving you an idea what this game is like. They are true it is very armored core light which given the state of armored core games this is a rather nice treat to scratch that itch. You have mech combat, customization options, Corporations fighting with each other and you stuck in the middle. That being said I do want to emphasize the light part of armored core light. The customization options are there, but they are not as wide ranged as armored core. Enough you can make a build to fit your play style, but nothing to deep. The weapons are not all balanced very well, as I could do 1800 dmg with my swords while the one shot per clip sniper rifle did 60. So some builds can feel weak. The story itself is also a bit light. Mainly it needed more time to cook and rushes for emotional payouts without building the frame work. Constant reveals and twists about the other mercs, but I didn't get to know any of them well enough to be invested. One character near the ends comes out acting if he has had a huge revelation and change and is suddenly side by side with you at the end and I swear I had met that particular merc TWICE before the end and was confused. It really feels like the middle of the game might have been cut. Further, It is very japanese with all the weird and wonderful that comes with that in the story. I do recommend this game as it is not a bad experience at all. It is not a must play, but given the options for armored core fans this is what we have and i'm am glad we got it.

_childDocuments_.review: So far so good. It feels like your standard anime mecha game and that is a good thing. I will update as I get more time in.Okay while the story seems to be just okay the combat, oh my the combat. Want to circle strafe around firing twin machine guns and rocket pods? Yeah you can do thatt.Switch to sword and shield or two giant katanas and dash in on a giant crab mech boss? yeah that is a thing. If you like fast gundam style mechs why are you still reading this? Buy Daemon X Machina already!
_childDocuments_.name: DAEMON X MACHINA

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game by itself, but it is a disappointing one.I am a massive Armored Core fan and this game is clearly trying to emulate that appeal. But it doesn't understand what makes Armored Core good.In Armored Core your core dramatically changed the way you played. You could spend hours just squeezing out the perfect build. In Daemon X Machina your build hardly matters. More often than not it comes far more down to the skill of the player than the build they use. Most battles take place in the air because there's absolutely no limitation for how long you can fly and you have the ability to hover in place.If the idea of a looter shooter in a mech where you fly around appeals to you, this is a good game. But as an armored core fan this disappointed me and made me wish the AC games were on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: DAEMON X MACHINA

_childDocuments_.review: The story's kinda meh. Campaign missions are repetitive, but the the grind for better gear is what makes this game fun I guess. However, there's a good chunk of the end-game parts that are only found in co-op missions. You can solo them for sure, but it's really time-consuming and arduous. On top of that, the team mate AI is absolutely brain-dead. A colossal will have a sliver of health left, and it'll take them 10 mins to gun it down. The fact that the higher difficulty iterations of the bosses are basically DPS checks makes it worse. So naturally, most people opt for a full team. But here's the thing- co-op is all sorts of clunky and finding rooms is a pain. If you enter a room where the member are already dispatched on a mission, it'll just display "Arsenal on Standby". There's no option to leave the room, so you'll have to restart the game. Now, let's say you do find teammates. After fighting a boss for who knows how long, you get sent to an eternal loading screen and the loot that you get isn't even saved. This all makes for a very frustrating gaming experience. The 1.0.5 update also renders it unplayable for some people. Won't even launch. In its current state, I can't really recommend it to people who are looking to play with friends. If you don't really care about co-op and love the solo grind, buy it by all means (but on sale). However, if you're someone who doesn't have hours every day to mindlessly grind, I don't suggest that you pay anything for this game at all. No wonder they gave it for free. Hopefully, they'll fix these issues in an upcoming patch.TL;DR update poopoo, don't buy until they fix it

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing AC for years one of the first games I ever played on the PS2 next to two towers but thats not important. This game overall I do enjoy from its simple design to some hybrid of metal ( Best song is arm of the colossus, fight me). The story is vague to semi understandable at best only because you aren't given much detail other then some dispostion here and there, cut scenes are simple most of the time, i will say for a mech game it had a very Evangelion esquire story finale ( It tries but its alright at best.) Combat is the most solid part about this game, the best part is your Mech doesn't drain your boost gauge for simple hover and fly which is so nice, older AC's where punishing on boost builds. The pilot game play could be better/ expanded upon, it has a few nice quirks but not much reason to actually leave your mech to play your pilot and the way the ending is you think it would tie into pilot gameplay better, still cant complain about combat with AI for the most part still trying to do pvp to see what that mess is like.     All in all its a nice off shoot of AC with its own issues, if it got support or expanded I feel the game could be much better. They just need to clean up/ expand the story which doesn't make since but if you saw how it was presented you would understand, combat simple, easy, and has a skill ceiling( assuming for pvp) dependent on your dedication. Does have controller support. Favorite thing though is the chibi anime cheeseburger decal.
