_childDocuments_.review: Excellent soundtrack, great gameplay, memorable characters, but lacking in content, quality of life, and has a weak story.The mechs, called Arsenals, control very freely in the air compared to other mech games to the point that you could hover in place if you wanted to or execute tight-corner movements with ease. Shooting is very intuitive where you have a wide reticle and targeting assistance to keep up with the fast action. Melee is similar to Armored Core, but now you will change direction mid-dash to track targets so that it's more viable against mobile targets. Only real complaint of the controls is that you are very slippery on the ground and it can be a pain to come to a complete stop on precise areas.Customizing the mechs are a mixed bag. I love Shoji Kawamori's designs but they are definitely skewed more towards thin and sleek than bulky and powerful like I personally prefer. Once more, many parts are visually identical to others save for a small piece of added armor. The decal system is great but I would have liked being able to change the glow color of my Arsenal.Relatively new to mech games like this, you can customize your pilot to the point of giving them cybernetic enhancements and abilities with those enhancements. These abilities have great utility, but some are more useful than others and some may affect your pilot in ways you don't want them to. These enhancements use growth tree system where you can only choose the closest items to what you already have, which I see no reason for. This needs some quality-of-life features like being able to preview what an enhancement will look like before you purchase it.The lack of content boils down to three factors. First is the missions are replayable and the storyline is weak. There are multiple endings but they only come into affect with the very last mission, not that the story is strong enough to make one care as almost nothing is explained during gameplay and instead through text-wall data entries. Replayable missions is great for wanting to get that one specific part but it weakens the experience for more narrative-focused players like me.This content problem extends to the multiplayer where the mode that gets the most play besides raid bosses is a randomly-generated dungeon. Said dungeon has a largely homogenized and uninteresting look to it that fails to impress and is easy to get lost in.For the sequel, I'd like more unique parts, transmogs for those parts (since we have purchasable skins anyway), a campaign with more linearity and worldbuilding, and less slippery controls on the ground. Finally some simple quality-of-life improvements for cybernetic enhancement, like being able to choose an enhancement based on level instead of proximity on the development tree and being able to preview how this will visually alter the pilot.As it is, I can't recommend the game at full-price. It is, however, worth buying on a sale.

It's simplified armored core with a splash of gundam flavor.For all of that, it's a stupid blast of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Right up front, this game is not worth the current asking price. It's worth probably $25-$35 in my view.That being said, the small amount of content that exists is pretty fun and it's a shame there isn't more of it for $60+ dollars.The game needs more coop content, period. There are fewer bosses than they say, many are recycled with minor differences. The single-player content is ok, as long as you skip all the dialog and cut-scenes. PvP will be dead on arrival given the lack of multiplayer cheat protection. This is all before you get into some of the shallow mechanics.Outer (small human) fighting is neat, but not thought through and not fleshed out enough. Some weapons are simply not viable for doing anything at all, some weapons are massively OP. No amount of mods will make some weapons worth it. Lots of the weapons/armor progression is like that, and feels like filler. That said, finding all the armor parts is obsessive if only for looks. Most, however, will use a tiny fraction of any of the armors or weapons. Note that DLC you pay for, namely plugsuits and Outer cosmetics, will mean nothing as you level your Outer. Parts of your body get replaced with mechanical parts, which is cool but why would I ever buy cosmetics no one, including me, will ever see?Overall this game has a lot of unrealized potential. I enjoy what's there but I'm not terribly price conscious on taking a risk with $60, and I do love big mechs. At the moment, I can't recommend this title based only on the small amount of multiplayer content. We need more exploration maps, and more coop boss battles that aren't recycled. Especially for a $60 price tag. Also, if you're going to include PvP and ranking maybe include some form of cheat protection. Without central servers, I'm not so sure effective cheat protection is even possible here.Also, the exploration and boss battle terminals need to be on the same terminal and we NEED a proper lobby browser. As is it's tedious to look for any kind of multiplayer, and it shows in how often you can find a game.
_childDocuments_.name: DAEMON X MACHINA

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna preface this with the fact that I'd really like a midway between "Yes" and "No". I definitely think there's something for specific folks here, just not really me.I've not played many mech games to compare this to, so I'm just going to sum it up in terms of what I got out of it.Pros:-Character and Mech customization-Decent number of weapon types-Short mission structure allows for pick up and play (Great for folks with Steam Decks and/or short available playtime)-Fast movement and boosting with simple controls make it pretty easy to jump into-Neat mechanic in that destroyed mechs (specifically Arsenals) can be salvaged to scavenge equipmentCons:-Game tosses a lot of characters at you who so far, don't feel like much more than a bunch of anime tropes spouting random nonsense or very generic "life is hard" sophistry--Secondhand, but they don't ever really flesh out most of these characters-Mission structure is repetitive and maps are samey looking and feeling. Feels similar to various hunting games on PSP/Vita such as God Eater. Not really an issue if you enjoy the gameplay, but something to note.-Boss and enemy design at least so far is bland-Mech designs will all be pretty standard 2 armed, bipedal. This with lack of real distinctions between weapons makes things feel samey-Weapons don't particularly feel good--Weapons also don't really feel that different within categories, but the slight differences feel like there's immediate winners (Rifles and SMGs dumpster everything in PvE, Shotguns and Handguns feel generally kinda pointless, and melee is just kinda slow and clunky feeling, but powerful). Laser weapons aren't all that good and use two resources instead of just ammo so generally ignored.--No dedicated rear weapons, just extra slots to store other weapons. There are auxiliary and missile slots, but you can't get too fancy, they're basically passive equipment and things like boosters, and then... missiles.-Scavenging leads to grinding as a lot of equipment is just RNG salvage items-For folks who want mechs to feel a bit weightier, this isn't itOverall, I think it helps fill a niche of "Eastern Mech Games", aka not Mechwarrior, aka your mech isn't a lumbering behemoth, but it feels overall kinda shallow. Melee weapons attack a single time with no real combos (later weapons, have the ability to at least chain attack into groups, but only into groups), which make them just feel and look pretty bland, and overall, I'm just not really vibing with it much.

_childDocuments_.review: Daemon X Machina is a fun mech game with lots of customizability. Want to fire missiles and blow your opponents to oblivion as a chonky boy? You can do that. Want to be super speedy and play a glass cannon? 100% an option. This game even has sword fighting if you're ready to start a duel. The one thing I dislike about this game is that I find it to be easier than I like, but I've heard many people say that the difficulty is perfect for them. If you're coming here for a game that'll beat you to a pulp like Dark Souls than this game might not be for you, but if you dislike suffering, love crushing your enemies, and hearing your ally scream "I'M THE CREAM OF THE CROP" every 7 seconds this game is perfect for you.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about Demon Versus Machine?It’s a game about mechs, AI, either the dumbest plot ever conceived or the worst translated plot since Final Fantasy VII Remake, stamina somehow being a stat on a machine, and spending eighteen minutes figuring out how to place a decal of a pizza on your crotch only to find out that new leg piece you got places decals in the grundle instead.Damon Ex Machinations: Human Revolution is a game that I played a free demo of once on the Switch and was gifted on PC. Having known this game was on Switch first I no longer ask why the trees look like flags, or why the UI takes up approximately 33% of the screen. The game has some very pretty effects and visuals since it seems to go for a half-detailed half-cel-shaded vibe. I really like the way my mech looks gliding/roller skating along highways, cavern floors, and the desert. I really like the controls on controller, and from what I can tell from my friends and eventual migration, the controls on PC are easy to get a hold of too. The game performs tight, which you have to appreciate in an age where not a lot of Armored-Core-type games exist. Speaking of ol’ AC, there’s a lot of weapons and gear, or at least there seems to be. No one is going to beat the classic AC inventory, or even Chromehounds inventory, but the inventory (so far) seems to be grindy enough to warrant additional playtime rather than begrudging playtime. The only downside to this inventory is that the guns sound like ♥♥♥♥. Unfortunately one of my biggest gripes in this game is that Resident Evil on the PS1 has better automatic rifle sound effects than this game—hell, Final Fantasy VII (1997) has better automatic gunfire sound effects—what is this ♥♥♥♥? Each gun sounds like a child recorded it, gave it to their dad on a USB, and converted it into a MIDI. I’d kill for an assault rifle, laser gun, or missile launcher that sounds like an adult or professional made it.Maneuvering through the game is fun, enjoyable actually. Once you get past the absolutely-dreadful briefing you’re in a fairly open map that allows you to glide/skate or fly against a buffet of enemies while the AI/Squadmates help you understand why most people drink after work. If you can get over that you are treated to a variety of ways to harass and destroy your enemies, including throwing vehicles at them, throwing their friends at them, shooting them, blowing them up, beating the stupid out of them, and shooting them. If you have friends you can even go online and play missions together, which consists of either straightforward similar-to-the-campaign side missions, and dungeons that occasionally drop you face-first into the Pillar Man equivalent trio in this game. The gear and money you earn from these missions with friends can be used in campaign, and I see this mode as a way for you and your friend to grind gear and money together rather than a campaign experience.Playing with friends also helps me see the different variety of playstyles in the game, which is always interesting since multiple ways and loadouts accomplish similar results, or compliment eachother quite well. For example, my friend has SMG’s as their main weapons, and pilots very fast, quick, and up-close while dodging rapidly. I meanwhile have a shield and long-range rifle, shooting and locking on from afar which worked well as he took on aggro. Once my shield was destroyed I swapped to another rifle, preferably with autofire, and often did this when fighting in close quarters. My friend I believe had different weapon categories to swap with rather than backups, and this worked out really well. A lot of our hangups had to do with bad plan execution, steep gear disparity, or no plan. It’s a game you can really get lost in with friends, but after a while you get tired of not making progress and kind of want to make progress in the campaign so you can get more equipment and gear…which leads me to my next problem.Someone could breathe in the campaign and I could groan. I think the last time a game had me hating the story this much was Monster Hunter Worlds. Think of every NPC as the handler, either putting in too much when they shouldn’t have, or too little when they should be going over-the-top. There’s parts of the script that straight up make no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sense. No one talks to eachother like that, and no one works with a guy who openly states to everyone in the company and strangers their intent to commit murder upon a present coworker. It’s in this magical anime bubble thing where there’s this cast of absolutely dumb, bizarre characters that are like the guy at Best Buy who bows to you after you say you don’t need any help looking at Blu-Ray discs. Why are they doing that and who told them to do that? Did someone think they wanted this, or that real people did this, or that it’s believable? The only person who I like in this game is Big Bald Big ♥♥♥♥ Basuzo. I don’t know his real name, but you’ll know him when you see him. He’s the only one who is believable, plays as someone who you actually see and would be forced to work with in real life, responds to everything believably, and his VA in English nails it.Now I know what you’re thinking, ‘If you hate the dub why not switch to Japanese?’ Because then the script will be stupid, but the people saying dumb things will be saying it in a language I don’t really understand. This kind of suggestion helps games like Persona 5, where they previously had good voice actors and skipped on this installment, but when the script is bad you might as well play it in Klingon, it doesn’t change that the script is dumb and is trash.So where does that leave me? Right now the game is on sale for $38.99 USD. I think that is a really good and fair price for this fun game with an awful plot and script. If you can get over that, it’s a solid investment.4/5 – Get in the Robot Nikky.

_childDocuments_.review: Many reviews are calling this a spiritual successor to Armored Core, and to be honest, they aren't too wrong about it. The game does play and feel very similar, but the depth of those games just isn't there yet. If more games come in the series it could really have potential, Armored Core wasn't what we all remember it to be in its first installment, so I'm looking forward to what else can come from this new franchise.What is this game? Daemon X Machina is a fast paced third person mech action game focusing on customization and playing what kind of robot you want to play. You'll do missions and follow a very simple story but it works to push the game along. The game overall feels very simple  and the AI isn't too difficult to handle even in the late stages of the game, but if you love building custom robots you might find a lot of time and enjoyment from this game, but I find it a little bit short and lacking in content to justify its full 59.99 (at the time of writing this) price tag. If you are wanting a mech game badly like I was it could be worth that price to you, but if you're undecided a sale might be the best for you. That all said, I've enjoyed my time with this game and I'm loving building my own robots again, I would recommend it to any fans of the Armored Core games (NEW AC WHEN FROMSOFT? WERE WAITING), just don't expect the depth and complexity of a game like AC For Answer just yet.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not the spiritual successor to Armored Core. Not even close. It couldn't even hold the tip of AC's 10 foot metal ♥♥♥♥.The gameplay just isn't there. You are piloting mechs, but it really doesn't feel like it at all. There's no weight to anything. You might as well be fighting with origami mechs for how floaty everything feels. Engaging in combat with another mech just feels wrong. There's no heft to your attacks or yours. And the weapons are not distinguished enough from each other either. Using a bazooka doesn't feel that much different from using your rifle or MG. On top of this. the control scheme is weird and not particularly fun to engage with. The game commits one of the cardinal sins of gaming to me: during missions where you're battling other named characters, they routinely become invulnerable until they finish talking. And they do this repeatedly in fights. And they never shut up with their inane dialogue.The customization of the mechs is very limited, both mechanically and visually. There's so much fewer options compared to what you could do in Armored Core. And the options you do have just aren't satisfying, to boot. I don't really feel like I'm doing much at all in creating the mech I want to use. And getting new parts is tied to looting. But the looting is odd and poorly implemented. And there's so few options of real merit. I beat the game with only changing parts a few times. And at no point did I feel like I could create the mech I wanted to create. With AC, it was so much fun getting money from missions and buying parts. And then using those parts to tailor your mech to exact specifications. There's so few parts here and everything is handled so broadly that you'll never even remotely touch AC's sophistication. It's just too damn simplistic. It is ridiculously short. Ludicrously short. It took 10 hours to beat it. Now the only thing that remains are multiplayer missions, but the problem is that multiplayer is dead. So good luck with any post-game content because you'll have to solo it all, which it isn't designed to be solo'd.I have nothing to say about the story. It seemed utterly absurd and vapid with silly anime characters from the first moment I started playing. So I skipped all of the story as much as I possibly could. I generally don't like most anime, except for stuff like Berserk or One Punch Man. And this game seemed to fall into the stuff I hate in anime.The game is a 4/10 at best. Get it if it is $10. Don't pay more than that for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Received this as a gift.To begin, I mostly wanted this as I have played most of the Armored Core games and have been a fan since the 3rd installment. While perusing Steam, I had found this game, and it looked pretty similar, so my review is  biased - however with that in mind I would still recommend this to anyone interested as it is pretty fun.To keep it brief-ish, this game is pretty dang close to that experience being presented on the PC. Having also played Hawken briefly, both definitely have the robot design down, and the combat is just as fast-paced, but this game can flaunt the one thing Hawken didn't have that makes it quite close to the AC series; that being the customization.The parts are broken down into 6 Armor subsections (head, body, l arm, r arm, legs, processor) and the weapons are broken up into 6 as well (l weapon, r weapon, l pylon/l backup, r pylon/r backup, back, and support/utility) - these also being split further into type (bullet, laser, etc.). Additionally however, this game sports additional "Inner" customizations for your pilot that changes their appearance as well as adding bonuses to your pilot/armor.All things considered, I would give it an 8/10; basically the closest thing I think we will see to Armored Core on PC for some time, and it does what it does quite well. Only thing that maybe has fallen a bit flat so far (and this could be that I haven't beaten the game yet), is the part list feeling more streamlined and how you seem to be locked into a single quest line with the factions (unlike AC 4 Answer for example having some missions that even failing was an outcome that lead to other end-games). Great game though all things considered.

_childDocuments_.review: I already like games where you pilot giant robots, so I'm kind of bias with this review. Been wanting this game after looking for new up coming Mecha games (last year?) but when I saw it was for switch I thought it wouldn't come to pc what so ever. Yet, here it is!Now that I got a chance to play it, here is what I think about it.TLDR:It's vary fun to play, that looks like it can work on just about any type of computer made in the last 10 years. If you have an interest in giant robots, being able to mix and match parts, with lots of gun play. This is a game for you. If you are someone looking to test the waters however, this can either help you love it, or hate it. ( Though I hope more on the side of love it. XD ) : End TLDRFor everyone else. The game is a mix of single player/co-op made by Xseed, and if you have ever played an Xseed game of that type before, then you will know that there is going to be a hub room. In this case it's called a "Hanger," but you know it's not fooling anybody. So yeah, as generic as that is, when you collect more and more weapons the walls and racks in the hanger start filling up with the weapons as you collect them. So that's an interesting touch I like about it.There is a Character creation at the start, and I don't think it's worth talking too much about it. Just saying it so you know it's there, it's nothing too complicated, more on the simple side as far as CC goes. Also at anytime you can change how your character looks, it cost a little money from the in game missions to do, but besides that you aren't restricted to only hair cuts and clothes.For single player *so far for me anyway* It seems fine, I'm still in early parts of the story as of making this review but so far it seems to ease you in, giving you simple missions that won't hurt you if you fail. I do wish some things could be explained control wise more clearly at the start though.Co-op/PVP stuff is interesting Though I haven't done enough of the PVP stuff to know if you get anything out of it in ranked for winning. Though most likely just for bragging rights. I also haven't dipped too far into the co-op stuff, however there is a Co-op mode that reminds me a little bit of Half dead. The Map can be seen however each map changes and the rooms have different types of hazards, but it's also a place to get a lot of parts and weapons for your mech.As for What I don't like, it would have to be player to player communication. So far it seems you can only do text communication. Normally I would be okay with it, Not the best thing in the world but it's something. What makes it fall into the "bad" is how it's needlessly limited to a idiotic degree. There is a vary small letter limit when typing messages. Even with that limit, messages can't even fit in the quick message window. With that said, Discord, Team speak, or what ever you use to talk to people in game well be your friend if you want to do any kind of meaningful communication beyond a "Hello" or "need revive." Quick add on: The game's story is like watching a 1990's-2000's giant robot anime. May be cool for some younger people, and is fun to joke on if you are an older anime watcher. However it may turn some people away.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy mecha games, then this one is definitely a good choice - though if you are looking for something particularly gritty, you would be better off going with Armored Core, as while Daemon x Machina doesn't stray far from the usual existential anime feel, the art style and story could have certainly used more time to cook if they were really trying to go for something foreboding.As other reviews have mentioned, there's a lot of (sometimes quite unnecessary) dialogue - and unlike games like Armored Core or Ace Combat that have similar mission formats, this dialogue is not short nor sweet enough to be properly condensed into each mission's runtime, leading to cutscenes, random breaks in the combat, or periods where you outright can't damage the enemy because the dialogue hasn't caught up to a specific scripted point. This can be irritating, but in general it doesn't actually do a whole lot to risk your score or completion time, so there isn't any real harm done besides forcing you to listen to a bunch of generic anime chatter. I wouldn't consider this a reason NOT to get the game, since the gameplay itself more than makes up for it.When it comes to gameplay, the difficulty is determined by your build, first and foremost. I beat every mission on my first try, but that's because I was running a build that focused on evasion, healing, and whittling down the enemy from outside of their range. Overall, DxM has a high amount of variety, though it pales in comparison to Armored Core because most of this title's equipment options are simply upgrades of previous pieces of gear, and there are few unique weapons that actually have special attributes applied to them. Additionally, in Armored Core the shop system is significantly more useful, but in DxM you're effectively forced to spend time and credits developing any gear you want, unless you're lucky enough to loot it off of the battlefield. This makes obtaining specific components quite difficult for someone who wants to have a variety of specialized builds. DxM brings infantry action to a couple of the missions - and a whole tech tree for upgrading your own character as a cyborg. However, these are so few and far between that it's generally pointless to focus on these mechanics with your already limited resources.Soundtrack is a banger. 10/10 with no complaints in this regard - aside from the fact that it's better off being listened to outside of the game itself because there's no way to drown out all the sound effects and dialogue otherwise being layered on top of it.In conclusion; get the game when it's on sale if you can. It's great by Nintendo Switch standards - but it just didn't have enough time in the oven to compare to the true titans of Mecha.

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely a game for mech fans who enjoy the giant robot being able to defy physics outright and make it fast so it doesn't end up just being a human-shaped missile-sponge. The game is fast-paced and emphasises quick movement control over precise aim or tactical use of cover. It has a very much "have fun going ape and wreaking havoc like a one-mech-army" vibe to it, at least early on in the campaign missions. Ammo is technically limited, but enemies also conveniently drop whatever type your equipped guns use when they die (usually by exploding). Even early on you get pretty quick access to everything from ballistic guns of various types, to missiles, to literal giant swords and shields, so there's not much closed off to you tactics-wise.TL;DR Version for folks in a hurry: Anime-style giant robot shooter. Avoid if you want "realism" (or at least what little you can get when dealing with giant mech concepts), but a must-buy if you just want to go ballistic and have fun dodging, weaving, and blasting.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're familiar at all with Armored Core, then you should know what to expect here.You're a mech pilot, your mech can hold 5 weapons, 2 active ones, 1 special and 2 backups, and a supporting equipment slot that can damage or augment abilities. Every mission you do earns you credits, every mission you'll be able to pick up pieces of wrecked mechs for your own purposes. So the goal between missions will be to optimise your mech the best you can, not just min maxing stats for your playstyle, but designing different loadouts for different missions.One mission may require you to race to the finish instead of killing everyone, another may feature powerful lasers you can't dodge easily. Your "briefings," if you can call them that, won't give you much of a clue of what you're running into, but you can always make some pretty reasonable guesses as you learn how the game operates.Customisation to even the smallest detail like the initial acceleration when you boost versus your normal boost speed are all factors to consider. The problem is acquiring these parts, I already mentioned salvaging during missions but the best way to upgrade your setup will be through cannibalising parts for better ones through the factory menu. It's cheaper than buying parts outright and usually has better than what the shop offers anyway. Though eventually money won't be a problem when you beat the main story.The game does have an online function, such as it is, but when i played it was mostly dead, the only real benefit from online play i saw was the ability to find better parts, but its pretty difficult. There could be a comeback one day, lord knows many bought it at full price for that to be possible, but I would not go in expecting a robust community. There is barely enough of one creating guides for it.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has sunk 50 hours and completed the game, I cannot recommend this to anyone, especially at it's current price. And here's why;Protaganist:Protaganist is an overstatement to your character. You have your usual character customisation and gender selection, so that's good but none of that means anything. Your character doesn't speak or react in any way, and I mean, in any way. At one point a character is giving a huge spiel about his grand plan right in front of your face and dropping huge plot points and earth-shattering truths. How does your character respond? By standing perfectly still, with their arms locked by there side, never blinking, never speaking.Story:It's nothing special, a group of mercs called Reclaimers fight for factions over limited resources after a piece of the moon fell to Earth. It ends with the BBEG trying to wipe out humanity (sort of) and you fight to stop him. That's it.Characters:This was somewhat decent, a wide array of fully voiced characters each with their own goals and aspirations. But it boils down to nothing really since they betray each other and at points even contradict themselves. An example is when a certain lady wants to destroy a tower, your team calls her bluff by destroying it for her and she begins to scream at you for destroying the tower. Honestly there were a lot of moments like this that made no sense.Also the characters are broken down into factions, factions that you cannot join despite everyone gushing over how skilled you are, none of them want you on their team. You are factionless, in fact you are the only factionless character in the game.Gameplay:At this point even amazing gameplay could not save this game, which is lucky because the gameplay sucks. The flight mechanic is clunky at best, there's so many stats to keep track of it's hard to tell which is beneficial and which is bad. When the community has to make guides on customisation and stats then you've done it all wrong.Melee is boring as it comes, you charge forward and swing the sword, you then repeat this exact same animation again and again. Equip two melee weapons and you can perform the cross-slash where you charge forward and swing both swords at once for increased damage. That's it, nothing fancy like combos or QTE melee combat.Guns are pretty boring, you have a selection of bullet, laser, flame, acid etc. Except other than range and damage they don't differ much. I went the whole game just using bullets after experimenting with each since it's just a point and click game. Oh, there's snipers but the opponent arsenals move so fast you'll never land a shot at range, not that range matters since the enemy rushes you constantly.Overall:I'll forget this game, it's characters and plot within the week. If you really want to try it for yourself, wait for a sale and thank me later. It was a borefest that I forced myself through, the final boss was lackluster and there's no endgame content other than re-running past missions.If you want an arbitrary score I'd give it a 3/10, it couldn't get much worse.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird one. I am recommending the game even though I have refunded it. I don't even know if this review is going to stay after the refund process is finished. Still, let me tell you why.The game is, as numerous others have mentioned, basically Armored Core. I myself is also a keen fan of AC and so only naturally did I preorder DxM. The game is fantastic in many ways. The toon shader works surprisingly well with the mech genre, and the action is just buttery smooth. Performance is wonderful, and variety in machines is not bad.What didn't work for me is that the game is made too easy with the auto aiming system. With how terrifically maneuverable arsenals are (absolutely love how smooth all the animations are, btw), I truly think auto-aim is a function that at least needs to be able to be switched off. I mean, auto-aim for handguns and sub machine guns? Sure. Works for high speed action. Assault rifles? Hard to swallow. Sniper rifles, even? What in the world? Using a melee attack also gives you a nice boost so that you instantly get up close to the enemy so that you can slice them, but that imho kills the fun of chasing down the enemies. IMHO, DxM (or mecha games in general) needs to be more like Ace Combat instead of a Gundam VS game. Armored Core is more like the former, and DxM the latter.Also, the narrative style of DxM mimics AC in certain ways, but the execution is not as nicely done and is too cryptic of its own good. Having played Japanese games (in Japanese) my entire life, I am used to stylized dialogues and what not. DxM's lines are what I would categorize as cringey, as though the game doesn't have any better way to tell the players about the characters' traits. They're over-the-top even for a Japanese game.Still I believe what I bad-mouthed about DxM is just a matter of taste, and I can see why others would fall in love with it. It is a great game, I have no doubt, for some but I'm just not one of them sadly. Therefore, if what I said is of great concern to you as well, I recommend making good use of Steam's refund policy to take a good look at it with your own eyes.See you all again in AC6, if that is ever going to be a thing at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Cutting to the chase, is this game worth it? It depends. For me, it scratched a particular itch no game has managed to since Armored Core (I've played those since the PS1). For that reason alone it's worth at least a look.Aside with some issues with the port (Mouse Sensitivity is tied to frame rate), and a few (bugs such as shifting audio volume in menus) and supposedly issues with flamethrowers at anything above 30fps (I didn't notice any problems at 120), the port is fairly solid. The game runs well, it supports higher resolutions, I believe you can force a higher render resolution in the configuration file, as well as enable sharpening. In 32 hours of playing, I didn't have a single crash, or any game stopping bugs.I haven't tried any of the online components of the game, but from what I've read they can all be soloed with the right builds. To be fair I wasn't aware they were in the game at the time of my purchase until I encountered the option in game.Overall the mech customization is quite nice, character customization is decent, game plays quite well. Missions tend to be the same sort of go here, do this objective, collect your reward, without too much variation in most of them; but they were the same way in Armored Core for the most part.It took me about 32 hours to finish, taking my time including some part farming and attempting to complete every side objective for Free Missions. Finishing that would probably take up another few hours, longer if I go for other unlocks.If you're a fan of Armored Core? This is the first game in about a decade to really come close, not to mention the first to release on PC. I'd buy it.If you're not a fan of Armored Core, watch a few gameplay videos and make the choice, if collecting parts, modifying your mech creating new builds which can play fairly differently; doesn't sound appealing, it's not the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Armoured Core is slower, more deliberate. The pacing and thorough anime styling of this game puts this firmly in the zippy, needs decent reactions and has you flying about like a mosquito on crack approach. This is much closer to things like Virtual On back in the Saturn Era or Namco Bandai's foray into the more Arcade approach with ACE COMBAT 6. What it is, is excellent, there's a lot to like here (and a few things to dislike, like the fact the DLC that got released with the game will run you nearly the cost of the game itself, and because this game does deal heavily in appearances, that does suck a bit).You are an Outer, a human who's been blended with Femto (which sounds like an antacid) giving you unique properties and abilities to control Arsenals (that's this games term for mechs), who can zip around the battlefield like mosquitoes on coke and unleash barrages of firepower that would put your average Texan to shame. The weapons start off fairly modest but before long you'll be using shoulder mounted cannons that can obliterate opposing arsenals in a handful of shots, and laser rifles that look like they would be better served being mounted on orbital platforms, as opposed to being held in a single mech hand.... and the story is enough to make you cringe so hard you'll want to fold in half. There's points where you think there's an inkling of a good story, but no, this is bad, and not in the "bad but good" way that Idea Factory handles Neptunia and ends up with lots of KAWAIIIIII =^_^= moments (oh god, I typed that, I feel dirty), but bad in the sense of "someone came up with this, someone was paid money to come up with this?"Thankfully you can skip the vast majority of it, along with the characters, most of which are ones you can live with but there's a few, a few that are walking caricatures that make me grind my teeth as I clench up whenever they're on the screen. One is clearly trying to emulate a cartoon version of the Hulk but ends up being a terrible version of some roid rage sunday morning cartoon bro-smasher. The other is the ditzy Harley-Quinn wannabe who has daddy issues and just wants to smash things for the lols. If these two were any more obvious and two dimensional I could fold them up and make origami animals from them.My Danboard collection has more personality than those two clowns and they're inanimate pieces of plastic.-exhale- Okay. Let's put the horribad story aside.Downed mechs can (and need to) be accessed to loot parts, weapons and equipment, doing so allows you to research further upgrades at the factory which then can be bought repeatedly at the shop (this brings me to bugbear number one, some of the more basic parts need looting repeatedly rather than being unlocked at rank up, WOULD IT REALLY KILL THE GAME TO PUT BASIC ARMOUR AND WEAPON PIECES IN THE STORE AS YOU LOOT THEM?.However, as you do the store gradually fills up with your potential arsenal of goodies and there -is- a massive arsenal. Both in terms of armour and in terms of weaponry, with a wide variety of options to fit all playstyles. You can go from slow and tanky with big heavy weapons that have slow re-fire rates right up to going quick and melee focussed and turn into a mecha-ninja.Tuning, adapting and customising your Arsenal to your own personal taste can become a time consuming and rewarding task, with the payout for getting your setup "just so" being that the game willingly accommodates you as you rampage through level after level, showering you with more goodies and more parts as you go along. Better yet, you can physically upgrade your Avatar, your Outer, so that you can take benefits onto the field, both for the pilot directly and in terms of translatable benefits for any Arsenal you pilot. Some of these upgrades will even physically alter your pilot, so you can end up somewhat looking like an extra from Cyberpunk as you become part human, part Arsenal, being an extension of the mech.The gameplay is well worth the time and effort, and finding that sweet spot that fits you is a satisfying feeling. The enemies range from cannon fodder right up to huge, screen filling monstrosities, complete with breakable weak points that further serve to work with your playstyles, encouraging you to constantly upgrade and adapt.Yes, but if someone puts together a montage of all the cutscenes. Imma cut a scene of them, being cut, in slow, bloody scenes. I swear, the cringe is real. The pain, even more so.Verdict:

_childDocuments_.review: It is not Armored Core, but it is still decent.The game shines on a technical level. Its colorful, loud, runs fast, and controls great. The music stood out at first, but was soon forgettable. The voice acting is clear, and not as annoying as most games with a anime twinge. The addition of dialog with characters before, during and after missions helped make the plot more comprehensible than most Armored Core were.The missions are small and quick.  This helped the game never feel like it bogged down, but also suffered when a mission would end just as you were really starting to get into it.  The large bosses were entertaining, but the game could have always used more of them. Mech on mech fights were pretty weak in comparison.That all said, the game was absurdly easy.  You could very likely beat the game without ever changing your weapon or mech parts. The game has all sorts of stats listed, but they seemingly have very little impact on game play. Mech parts felt more cosmetic than having any real impact.  Weapons fared a bit better, but once I found a style i liked, I was mostly switching from a "MK1" to a "MK2." It does not help that new equipment has to be salvaged, and outside of boss weapons the factory/shop system felt pointlessI'm satisfied for what I paid. But what I thought would be a core aspect - building my own mech - was made trivial by a lack of any real challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: DAEMON X MACHINA is a third-person mecha action game. While I had fun during my playtime, I honestly have no real desire to go back to it. Overall, I found it to be an okay game with some good and some quite noticeably bad features. This was a chore to sit through as I was equal parts bored and confused. The overall plot is middle-of-the-road but the way it is told is atrocious. The game's backstory is that part of a moon crashed into a planet’s surface, causing a natural disaster that released a lethal radiation across the planet that caused A.I. to become sentient and attack humanity. Some people have become immune to the radiation- known as femto- and can actually absorb it to become stronger. You are one such person and have become a mercenary operating within the contamination zone, known as the Oval Zone, for nebulous reasons. The actual plot of the game then proceeds to follow your misadventures. You will meet a very vast yet shallow cast of other mercenaries. Everyone can literally be described in a few words as they are not very well written. These people serve as both your teammates and opposition on missions. As mercenaries. the person screaming at you for beating them can be your teammate in the next mission. This makes things feel very weird as your relationships with people seem to be constantly rewritten, making it even harder to connect with them. Likewise, they all have rather bland or melodramatic speeches in mission briefings or in the field that take a while to get to the point. No one really “grows” as a person in the story and even those who did had a very predicable and shallow arc. Similarly, some characters solely exist to spout cryptic exposition at you and hint at a bigger, more sinister scheme later down the line. Once the story gets to a plot twist, it proceeds to exposition dump while still not answering the important questions. For example, one faction is functionally immortal due to some sort of super-advanced tech. They all fight to protect their immortality and spout cryptic lines but none of it has any meaning due to the poor pacing of the story. Why are they immortal? What’s the backstory? All we are told is that the towers we were sent to destroy is the key to it all. The game then proceeds to usher us into the next mission and drops the sub-plot entirely. It honestly feels like the game lacked the proper budget to tell the epic story it seems to want to tell. Gameplay is quite smooth and beginner-friendly. You have your mech, called an Arsenal, and can customize practically all of it. You choose your body parts, its 2 primary weapons, 2 optional weapons, a shoulder weapon and an auxiliary device for support. The overall parts selection is okay. This game takes 3-dimensional combat very seriously so learning basic movements is tantamount for victory. I do wish that maintaining a consistent altitude were easier and tracking enemy elevation on radar were smoother. Boosting takes stamina; depleting your gauge causes you to stop all movement and drop to the floor. You cannot do any advanced movements until it FULLY replenishes. You can also harness femto to create a body double or use 1 of 3 buffs for your Arsenal.  Actual gameplay consists of piloting your Arsenal and destroying the corrupted A.I.’s in your missions. They honestly don’t pose much of a threat and are only dangerous in swarms. There are mini-boss mechs called Strai that are a very minor challenge as they can use Arsenal weaponry. Defeating a Strai or an enemy Arsenal allows you to scavenge ONE part from its wreckage. You can equip weapons you take to your reserve pylons for immediate use; Arsenal parts are sent to your hanger back at base. Parts also randomly spawn in 1 of 3 varieties AND with 0-3 modification slots. Thus, there is a lot of variability in drops which makes scavenging fun, albeit VERY RNG heavy. Enemy Arsenals are regular occurrences and provide most of the challenge in missions. You will often have to fight a full team of 3 in a mission with your 2 AI partners. Arsenal fights are fun, but the AI for both allies and enemies really needs work. Sometimes they refused to move, got stuck, or just couldn’t hit their target.       Story missions aren’t terribly difficult once you get some decent gear. One annoyance I had was that some fights were unwinnable; you could whittle an enemy down to a certain percentage then they became invincible so the dialogue could play out. However, there is no indication they have become invincible and they will continue to fight you, making it seem as if the fight is continuing. In Post-game, you can: I dropped the game because post-game is only grinding for better parts and doing the same bosses/ dungeons over and over again. The game uses a cel-shaded art style that is rather pretty. Nonetheless, some textures look rather bland or blurry. Likewise, some lighting can look pretty weird, especially on faces. Nonetheless, I definitely feel that the art style helps set the game apart from other mecha titles and serves the game well. Animations were overall good, although everyone has exaggerated body movements when in their Arsenals. I absolutely love all the battle damage on the Arsenals whenever you get a close-up shot on them,  Overall, the soundtrack was nice. Music felt appropriate and there is a nice variety of genres used here, ranging from moody orchestral tracks to sick guitar riffs for faction themes. Voice acting was mostly well-executed in the English dub and made the characters more bearable. However, everyone also dramatically pauses after a text box/line which makes things rather stilted. The sound effects were typically good, but gunshots feel really flaccid. The default mixing is terrible- sound effects drown out dialogue during missions. The game ran well for me. Mysteriously, you can only access the full options menu from in-game. Controls can be fully rebound and your HUD is fully customizable. However, there is no “return to default” option if you mess up. There is an okay amount of graphical settings for PC although you’ll have to deal with a preset slider for overall quality and changes.  While I truly enjoyed my time with the game, the lack of a coherent story and grindy endgame made it hard for me to keep playing. Nonetheless, the actual gameplay is quite fun and can be picked up easily by a beginner to the mecha genre. Alternating between fighting chaff A.I. units and challenging Arsenal squads is a blast. Graphics overall look excellent due to cel-shading and the soundtrack makes certain moments pop even more. All in all, if you like the mecha genre, this game is worth a look. Just be sure to temper your expectations going in.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm leaving my review as negative to grab your attention and help people avoid my mistake of buying this game in the hopes of finding an Armored Core-like to scratch that long-neglected itch (FromSoft pls!). That and the game just didn't stick with me for the right reasons after all was said and done.Yes, you can customize the parts and weapons of your mech with a wide variety of gear like machine guns, explosives, shields, and even swords. That's about where the similarities with Armored Core end. There are online features like Armored Core V and Verdict Day, but this game's online is also effectively dead so good luck with that. Even if you and a friend buy the game together, co-op is limited to either 2 options for procedural and yet very repetitive "dungeons" to explore, or playing slight variations of the story mode's boss fights as well as a few other bosses that aren't noteworthy for anything aside from being extremely annoying or gimmicky to fight. These also feature the game's most obnoxious RNG aspects: beating the boss gives you a random amount of blueprint progress for special parts, but there are also items that only unlock via a drop chance after beating the boss - I had to beat Aviator over 20 times in a row just to get its unique SMG, and often gave up on some of the unlocks from the more annoying bosses. Now, this game does have a leg up on Armored Core due to your mech being more lightweight and maneuverable (and having unlimited flight time), feeling more like you're piloting a jet-propelled exosuit as opposed to a massive human-shaped tank. Unfortunately this led the game devs to make your mech enemies zip around like gibbons on meth and pull maneuvers you can't even keep track of let alone do with your own mech. There's also the option to disembark your and fight on foot but there is basically no reason to do this unless your mech is destroyed or you invest heavily in skills that allow you to repair yourself. Oh, and your mech body parts can suffer cumulative damage and be destroyed during missions, but you can salvage mech parts from fallen enemies, mainly your arms and weapons. However, to my knowledge there is no way to specifically target an enemy's parts to disadvantage them or prioritize their most dangerous armaments. This whole game feels like they jammed in as many random ideas as they could instead of refining and thoughtfully incorporating them, resulting in a complicated mess. Speaking of a complicated mess, the game's story is abysmal. They set up an interesting post-apocalyptic setting but let it down by making most of the world building come in the form of exposition from a ton of mostly-forgettable anime characters that won't shut up even outside of cutscenes. From what I can remember, some kind of crystal burst from the moon and emits some kind of energy that kills normal people but powers your mechs' special abilities, so now mercenaries that can pilot mechs are the go-to to deal with runaway AI that are also being caused by the moon crystals. Sounds good until something like 90% of the story missions have you going somewhere to do something only to - surprise! - encounter one of the other mercenary groups that "aren't supposed to be there" according to you but you're also not supposed to be there according to them so you have to fight them. Hope you like that "twist" cause they pull it with every merc group at least once throughout the story. So yeah, I liked this game's visual style and potential to fill the Armored Core void while FromSoft continues to milk Soulsborne as long as it makes money (god Elden Ring was so good though...), but would advise people to look up videos of gameplay and other reviews to really know what you're getting into, or as well as wait for a sale.A sequel has already been announced, so here's hoping the devs learn from mistakes here and DXM2 improves on the disparate, jumbled features.

_childDocuments_.review: In a world where the last Armored Core game is almost a decade old, Daemon X Machina can definitely scratch the mecha itch, but it has some serious problems in two areas: production values, and variety. The voice acting and writing is bad, like old saturday morning anime bad, but not in an endearing way. At one point, a character unironically says something to the effect of "Mercenaries serve a higher calling" and I can't imagine how that made it through the original writers room and the translators. Also, there are a dozen or so npcs who exist to show up and say a line according to their character trope before/after every mission. It all feels like your character is just an extra, witnessing someone else's anime drama, but only came in 2/3 of the way into the season. Any dramatic tension is ruined by the fact that as something is happening to a character, I find myself asking, "wait, who was that?"In terms of variety, there are only a handful of basic weapons with very slight variations in stats. More unique weapons show up near the end, but no real gamechangers. None of the armor will drastically change the way you play, so you can't really go full on tank or jet, just the same basic mech with more or less clunkyness. The small enemies mostly exist to feed your ammo reserves, and some of them literally just move around like a target at a carnival stand. Boss fights can be more interesting, but still end up being a bit too much of a damage race, since there's rarely viable cover and even dodging is unreliable for all attacks. Nearly all of the fights against other pilots are trivialized by a flamethrower.Finally, a lot of the ideas in the game just seem extremely half-baked, from getting out of your mech, to the boss weapon grind, to the ice cream buff shop. The first is like a down-but-not-out mechanic, but it might as well just let you die, and is used in a few stealth missions, that are again pretty terrible. The repeated boss grind only really reinforces how light on content the game is, and the ice cream is secretly just another aspect of grinding for parts. At the end of the day, I can't really advise getting Daemon X Machina in its current state if you want a serious mecha game. If you are ok with something more lightweight in that vein though, I'd say pick it up on a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking to scratch that Armored Core itch you really are better off just trying to use an emulator at this point and just replaying the past titles. Trust me when I say DxM is not the game you are looking for. The story and characters are miserably bad, mission design is pretty awful, the music is forgettable, and overall will just feel like you're forcing yourself to play it. When half the comments and reviews for this game equate to "it became semi-tolerable when I muted the voices and skipped the cutscenes" that isn't exactly indicative of a good game, lmaoMission design is flooded with escort/defend this types of objectives, and there were /enough/ missions where you aren't even piloting your mech for that to bother me as well. Shouldn't even be in the game. Who the hell wants to run around as the pilot?There's pilot skills you can unlock as well that wind up changing your appearance. These appearance changes can't be turned off or customized, are incredibly expensive to unlock, and re-speccing costs ingame $ while not refunding anything. The unlocks don't feel super impactful despite their descriptions either, but the game is so mind-numbingly /nothing/ that I'm probably just not noticing.It's honestly just not worth it imho. I really don't think I can push myself to finish this one, and that's saying a lot.EDIT: I finished it. It didn't get better. By the way; cheese the final boss with dual swords. It's a bullet sponge and you'll never have enough ammo to actually kill it. Absolutely abysmal fight.

_childDocuments_.review: spent a bunch of time customizing my mech in multiple loadouts (like, a few hours), and then the game just randomly deletes all of it. if i want to get back to where i was i just need to spend all that time again, but the game will probably just delete it anyway, completely ruining the aspect of customization for me.Cons:* the combat's nothing to write home about. it's like a worse version of Earth Defense Force, with less variety of enemies, less interesting options as a play to choose from, and less reliability in things like enemy health. instead of throwing more enemies at you, just make them randomly stronger for no reason.* enemies are super samey and spongy.* every boss so far has a gimmick that basically disengages the fight, instead of making them extra vulnerable during an attack, they just run away. for example, there's a big jet that you fight that literally flies out of the level every 5 seconds to do a big attack that is super easy to avoid. bosses are just a mess.* none of the weapons feel cool or powerful, and every new weapon just feels exactly like the last, but with a slightly different number attached.* your mech simultaneously feels really heavy, but with 1 button it goes into anime speed, but even with that feeling of clunky weight, every weapon feels like a NERF weapon.* the voice acting is complete trash, the characters are the most bland characters i've ever encountered in a video game, and they won't shut the ♥♥♥♥ up. the story is not bad, it is *the worst*, and every mission has like 5 minutes of story attached and 3 minutes of actual game.Pros:* Honestly? I don't have any pros. If all you want is Armored Core, go play Armored Core. If you want fast-paced 3rd-person shooter action (possibly with friends), go play Earth Defense Force. If you want fast-paced mech combat and deep, DEEP customization, go play Warframe. This game has nothing going for it that another game doesn't have. If it were $5, maybe, but the price tag on this thing is way too high for what is almost offensively abysmal quality in nearly every aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah I don't know, there's a lot I could say about this but I think what sums it up best is: This game is a decent skeleton of a much better game, but a skeleton lacks meat by nature.The story is trash, but I knew that going in. It's your typical "20 plotlines at once" 6/10 anime tripe that sounds like it could be ironically enjoyable but just ends up being glorified background noise. That's not the issue though, the issue is that the game is just uncompelling for many reasons:- Movement feels weightless, which is fine if that's the style, but it's also not exaggerated enough to be the fun kind of weightless like a pure action game. Moving doesn't feel like "moving" so much as just adding a constant speed to your character, if that makes sense. There's no physicality to it.- Gunshots sound more like pops than bangs and nothing does much damage. In fact damage feedback in general is bad and it's hard to tell if you're dying without looking at your health bar. Thankfully it's rare to be threatened at all.- There are some "magic" abilities that don't feel entirely well thought out or necessary except the clone for when you get bored of whacking on bullet sponges. Maybe they're more useful later but at this point I don't care.- Customization is shallow, "+250 stat A, -100 stat B" doesn't translate to me doing anything differently and most parts look alike. They somehow even made gun arms boring. Paint system is woefully limited, even compared to something released over a decade before this game like AC4. Ironically, your pilot gets better customization than your mech.- Melee weapons feel bad to use. They basically just dash you at something jankily then swing, and have only one attack animation each. They also seem to do surprisingly low damage to certain enemies.- Enemy designs are largely generic tanks and drones except the giants, who are okay but not all that unique.- The UI is astoundingly bad. You know those memes with the whole screen covered in garbage? It really does feel like that most of the time.And so on. The entire thing just looks and feels cheap, almost like 1-2 steps up from a Unity asset flip. I can generally forgive a game with a terrible story if the gameplay is good (ex:Borderlands 3), or even a game with awkward or unsatisfying gameplay if it's good in other ways (ex:Deadly Premonition), but this is a game with a story pulled straight from the bargain bin of MAL and gameplay systems that feel like they were conceptualized and coded in a week then left as-is. I am 100% certain that, given the source code and assets of this game, a studio could make an incredible mech action game from what's here. However, that hypothetical game is not this game.I think I'm just going to stop buying Switch ports, I feel bad for the people who paid full price for this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is overall really well done. The controls are smooth, it has a huge selection to customise your mech, lots of different weapon types, and fantastic music. The Story is pretty good but it has some over the top characters that water down the experience a bit but if you overlook that you will enjoy the story more. Online multiplayer is fun, so far I've only played the PVE but I'll update this review after trying some PVP - from what I've seen it seems pretty fun but as always meta's tend to ruin the experience. My only real complaint with the game is the "ceiling" in levels. Its invisible and really easy to hit, once you hit the ceiling your mech starts to free fall and you lose some control until your back in the playable zone. I'd prefer the ceiling to hard stop you so you could still fly horizontally but it's not that bad once you get a good idea of how high you should fly up. I'd also prefer if the levels were bigger overall and the boundary walls were hard stops as well since you can fly out of the zone and just die if you don't make it back in time - sometimes enemies you want to loot are outside of the area because they decide to run out of bounds just before you kill them. I'm surprised this wasn't implemented since missions are instance based - this makes it easier to have larger levels since its not open world. All in all this game is worth full cost if you like mech games, if you are curious just grab it on sale before Armoured Core 6 drops.

_childDocuments_.review: I regret every penny I spent on this.I'd only recommend picking it up below $20.What's wrong with it?Everything.Story is mediocre, voice-acting is typical, cut-scenes and dialogue is cringe.Okay, I could live with that, tell me about that sweet customization you say?There is advancement in parts quality. The actual variation of customization for different mech builds is feels almost non-existent.The variation in offensive and defensive methodologies is not only suffering the same problem, but is also redundant. If it shoots fast and far, get it, because you don't need to develop a strategy, just fire.Everything new you get renders the previous version obsolete. Maybe I'm just not far enough in the game, though I'm far enough not to get my money back, so there's that.It's just a bit boring to bother going further.Okay, but combat? At least? Please?Do you like firing haphazzardly at a couple enemies that barely constitutes a swarm, doesn't fire back unless it's another mech, and doesn't actually force you to use any tactical maneuvers or approaches? Do you love bullet-sponge bosses, lacking sound effects (seriously, one sound effect for every bullet weapon), sparse and uninteractive environments with cheap borders, and a complete lack of any reason to get out of your mech even though you can? This game is for you, then.Everything is homogeneous cookie-cuttery in this game. The only thing that it has going for it is it looks kinda cool. Even that is sullied by the lack of placement, design, and graphics.Forget reliving even a semblance of Armored Core.Heck, the targeting system is even garbage.Bottom of the barrel scraping shonen anime writing with a plastic shell of armored core and no internal parts.

_childDocuments_.review: IT'S ARMORED CORE BAYBEEliterally, too! some of the directors of From Software were the creative heads that made this happen, because Fromsoft will likely never make another Armored Core again, and if they do, it's gonna be some miyazaki-directed Souls-gentrified LAME version like they did with Armored Core V.Shoji Kawamori, the guy who did all the mecha designs of every Armored Core since the start, and Kenichiro Tsukuda, the executive producer of Armored core 2 and on, are the two main creatives behind this.This isn't LIKE Armored Core so much as it, from staffing to design, IS Armored Core!And free to make their own new setting to work with, all the new design choices expand upon the complexity and risk/reward tension that AC is famous for. It's got a strong uniqueness to it that makes it unlike any previous AC entry, yet enough familiar design and signature to feel less like "AC Spinoff" and more like "AC6: The One Fromsoft Will Never Make".Soundtrack slaps, too, of course. _childDocuments_.review: If you like Gundams, you'll probably enjoy this. At least, you'll enjoy the actual gameplay part, not so sure on everything else. Could do with a fair bit of polish and most of the cutscenes desperately need help, but otherwise a thoroughly fun game about flying mecha around and killing unholy amounts of AI. IF you've ever watched a mecha anime -- Gundam (especially 00), Code Geass, Robotech (Macross, Masters, NG), heck, even Evangelion -- then you will really enjoy how this plays. It's high-speed and explosive, action-packed, I can't say that any of the missions genuinely bored me, even if a few did have me just about tearing my hair out.   Don't pick this up for the story, which, although I found pretty decent, isn't its main draw by any means -- it's the combat and customisation you want this game for. Many of its storytelling/plot moments interrupt the gameplay quite abruptly, and a LOT of the worldbuilding is delivered via text only. These aren't dealbreakers by any means, but they can be an annoyance. Speaking of the story, I enjoyed it quite a bit. Although parts of it are definitely very predictable if you have any significant experience with mecha anime, other parts aren't, and there are some genuinely good twists and turns in the plot. When it comes to the player character, the body modding system is interesting, but the choice to make most of the really good perks have a severe impact on the player character's actual model is... interesting. I think that this is a cool idea in theory that's not nearly as cool in practice; giving players full control over their aesthetics is probably a better idea -- giving them the ability to "opt into" the appearance changes wouldn't be a bad idea -- but the system as-is isn't bad either. Story-wise, I like the way it ties into the actual main story. It's not like you absolutely have to get every body mod, it's still perfectly possible to beat the main story without any, but in PvP fully modded players will definitely have the edge over non-modded ones. One thing that shouldn't have been done is charging the player actual in-game currency to change their appearance. It's not expensive, but it's still annoying and kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.And there are far too many escort or pseudo-escort quests. Savior is best husbando and a total chad. Also, the crab boss is just not fun to fight. If any devs read this, please don't put it in a sequel. Please, please, please don't put it in again.TL;DR: If you want to be a gods-damned Gundam pilot fighting Anime Skynet and don't really care too much about silly things like plot or polish, this is the game for you. 7/10, Remove Crab.

_childDocuments_.review: Being an old fan of Armored Core - had to give this a try. It definitely has that AC feel - but it also feels more streamlined, for better or worse.Controls are super slick and the combat is fun and kinetic.Missions are fairly repetitive but then, from what I can recall of Armored Core, it suffered the same thing. Not sure how much endgame there is - I've seen the repeatable coop boss fights and randomized coop dungeon crawls - but it doesn't appear there is a whole lot to either of those modes to warrant playing them for too terribly long. The story is a predictable anime mess of too many characters who, most of the time, aren't even sure what they are doing or why.Overall its been an enjoyable anime mecha romp - but I'm not entirely sure it's worth the full $60 price tag - feels more on par with the $30-40 range.

_childDocuments_.review: Get it on a special, don't pay more than $30 if you can help it. We probably won't be seeing actual Armoured Core games on PC any time soon. The game does have the feel of AC combat but it's hampened by other elements.It's probably unfair to compare it directly to AC, the game is a spiritual successor but is it's own thing at the same time. The graphics are pretty mediocre (it's a switch game apparently, which may explain that). The actual Arsenals look pretty slick but everything else is rather bland. There is very little visual distinction between Arsenals and limited ability to customise. There's approximately three maps and you have very limited exploration of said maps. Everything quickly becomes samey. The enemy designs outside of bosses is pretty uninspired.The boss fights are the main draw, split into Arsenal on Arsenal fights and massive robot fights. The bosses are fairly unique and a real thrill to fight so I'll give you a quick synopsis of each to help you understand the appeal.Gunfort - Giant spider tank, will use it's massive legs to quickly run away from you and maintain distance then stun lock you with it's immense mass. Attack it's weak points for massive damage. Spec in for fast movement and melee to keep up with it.Nightmare - Giant bird tank, will use it's massive wings to quickly run away from you and maintain distance then stun lock you with it's immense mass. Attack it's weak points for massive damage. Spec in for fast movement and melee to keep up with it.Snatcher - Giant train tank, will use it's massive tracks to quickly run away from you and maintain distance then stun lock you with it's immense exhaust vents. Attack (oh wait, you HAVE to play multiplayer for it to have weakpoints, disregard). Spec in for fast movement and melee to keep up with it. Bolt - Giant flying centipede tank, will use it's massive fins to quickly run away from you and maintain distance then stun lock you with it's immense electrical skin. Attack it's weak points for massive damage. Spec in for fast movement and melee to keep up with it.Dreadnought - Giant mole tank, will use it's massive drill to run away from you and maintain distance then stun lock you with it's immense stinky fart clouds. Attack it's weak points for massive damage. Spec in for fast movement and melee to keep up with it.Rebellion - Giant human tank, will use it's massive boosters to run away from you and maintain distance then stun lock you with it's immense constantly jumping. Attack it's weak points for massive damage. Spec in for fast movement and melee to keep up with it. Aviator - Giant plane tank, this is where the amazing diversity in bosses begins to shine. You see, Aviator isn't like other bosses, it will use it's massive aerodynamic shape to run away from you and maintain distance then stun lock you with it's immense taser face. Attack it's weak points for massive damage. Spec in for fast movement and machine guns to keep up with it. The rest of the bosses are designed for multiplayer, meaning they basically don't exist unless you take the painstaking efforts to game the system, find out you can load in AI team mates then get roflstomped flat as most of the bosses are specced around the idea of four people firing on them and your AI team mates exist exclusively to catch stray shots. Spoilers from this point on (you've been warned).All of the base game boss fights return revamped with more hit points and occasionally a new trick like running away even faster and maintaining distance even more persistently. You will also need to be aware of how small the in game maps are, as most bosses at this level will actively try to ring you out (Gun Fort makes electric walls that push you, Nightmare will flee the battle arena and hope you're so catatonic that you follow it, Bolt's taser skin, etc..). You will need to be adaptable and able to mix you skills up on the fly. Consider speccing into MORE speed and check out the factory in game so you can spec your melee into more melee for more melee damage. You may even have to engage with what ever the hell the ice cream store is (spoiler warning, I hope you've been buying tonnes of ice cream because all the secret gear and weapons are stored in a secret factory secretly in the ice cream store). There's no real reason to worry about the actual ice cream, 1% boost speed is nothing and you and I both know that. Back to bosses.Dominator alpha - The last boss from the base game tank, will use it's massive crystal chandelier to run away from you and maintain distance then stun lock you with it's immense wall of guns tactics. Attack it's weak point for massive damage. Spec in for fast movement and melee to avoid running out of ammo.Zeruchroar - The ice cream store secret factory tank, will use it's massive moving very fast to run away from you and maintain distance then stun lock you with it's the battle arena is now lava. Attack it's weak points to deal any damage. Spec in for fast movement and melee to avoid running out of ammo. Eclipse - Ball tank, will use it's massive geometrical screaming to run away from you and maintain distance then stun lock you with it's laser light show. I haven't seen it's weak points yet. Spec in for uninstalling to avoid running out of patience for this game. Of course, these brilliant and witty opponents are only half the equation, how you build your arsenal is the other half. You will want to select armour based around how big the top number is (this is your movement speed I think) and ignore the bottom number (this is hitpoints I think), you've gonna get bionic legs that let you blink in and out of existence any ways, so you won't be getting hit unless your the kind of masochist that would actively engage in the end game content (at which point I recommend you uninstall the game and just tell people you beat it). For weapons you will want to jump straight to melee and grab the brightest and most shiny of the laser swords, you should have purples ones by the end of the base game, these will be your mainstay for all game content. You might consider putting some bazookas on your pylons, you won't be able to see ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ but it will let you experience ranged combat enough to know why I refuse to use anything other than melee. There's this whole social thing going on with the outers (that's the dudes piloting the Arsenals, I think), you can collect them like action figures (this lets your customise your bullet shields for online content). If you collect them all, you can get a limited edition Solomon and I was almost reminded of what it was like to play videogames back in the 90's and early 00's and I swear I damn near had fun. I don't want to give this game a thumbs down, I really, REALLY want to like it. Baiting me this hard with potential AC content ultimately hurt me more than it helped with the itch. It's like playing AC with cardboard cores. Everything feels weightless, like it's made of cheap plastic. In contrast, rather than being about tactics and decisive blows based on how well you specced your core to the unknown challenges of war, it feels like spamming melee until the health bar is finally empty. The worst thing is, back in AC I would deliberately spec into low armour, high speed with melee only options. It was fun because you WEREN'T supposed to do it and felt like an achievement to make it work. This game makes you do it and it feels like a hollow victory each and every time. I don't care how drab the AC environments were, they were a thousand times more fun to explore than these kaleidoscope boxes.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent Mech Act Rpg, takes alot of inspiration from armored core, at least mech design wise, the story also overlaps alot with the first AC's plot. It has alot  of Modern Japanese storytelling to the plot, which brings down the story by alot.The player based upgrades don't really offer much and detract from the cosmetic aspect.it is possible to  to pick up ammo and health mid mission which makes the game far easier then most mech games.You will find most of your upgrades and equipment from defeated Mechs and this may lead to replaying missions in order to build your designed loadout, but you can buy duplicates of anything you have found in the previous stage as well as new cpu chips as the story progresses, as well as "Developed" by  trading in old parts and some money and waiting a mission.The game is roughly unbalanced in terms of combat and close ranged combat is very scenario based, mostly only being useful for fighting bosses.There is also a system that allows you to get out of your Mech and battle on foot, although it is very limited in terms of usefulness.A overall enjoyable game with massive flaws for its Genre. 6/10.
