_childDocuments_.review: recomend? yes but no, its the closest thing to armored core on pc but it lacks in a lot of aspects, comparing it to AC might be unfair but this was supposed to be a spiritual successor, so my review is going in that direction, maybe I had high expectations from it.Short: is a decent game that needs lots of polishing, dont come with high expectations, 3 days of fun is as far as this game goes, hopefully sequel is improved in music and story specially, grab it on discount if you like mechs.Cons: -music, the music sucks, is very monotone and repetitive, it doesnt succeed in that aspect compared to armored core-story, I couldnt care less about characters, is like that thanos meme "I dont even know who you are", theres a few characters that hate you for no reason-customization, very simplified, maybe too much, everything works in a mision or nothing does, overheating is nonsense, it doesnt punish you enough so you can just fly braindead, (having internal parts like LR would have made this more interesting) this game had the chance to have a Glamour/Layered system which armored core games always lacked, this game has it, but you have the default design that they chose, therefore, no freedom/expresion, and they are dlc.Pros:-closest thing to armored core or if you like mech games that are not turn based.-if you want armored core on pc this is as good as it gets if not by emulating actual armored core games.-it has style, graphics are not a big deal at this moment, AAA games have already reached photorealism, kinda, at this point the style is better than graphics, and this game is a great example-great way to exercise your pinky, for all the boost that you will be doing if you play with m&k

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun mecha game that plays similarly to Armored Core: You play as a mech pilot mercenary who takes contracts for various factions, and you get paid a flat sum based on main objective and option side objective completion.Though compared to classic Armored Core, the mech movements feel a bit 'floaty,' in that there is plenty of inertia when you start moving and when you stop moving, on the ground or in the air (AC Ravens don't have this kind of movement inertia in Armored Core). It can take some time getting used to, but it's not a serious problem that gets in the way of enjoying the combat loop due to all of the ballistic weapons and missile launchers and laser weapons you can equip. (Though, the first major boss fight is a giant quadruped titan tank that leaps around and can cause a lot of contact damage if you're not constantly moving around the battlefield, so...)Story is easily the weakest part of the game, as many other players have noticed that it's an odd abstract anime sci-fi tale that gets told in a roundabout way through all the cutscene dialouge, but the gameplay itself is solid. I enjoyed the free release on Epic, so I got the game on Steam during a sale, and I plan on finishing the Daemon X Machina campaign while I wait for Armored Core 6 to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't get passed the underwhelming sound design on the weapons. This is a very good example of how powerful sound design will effect gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: Short review as I've finished the story.Should you buy it?-If you like mechs-New Gundam Breaker was hot garbage-A good pc port for once-Good-Game runs great, up to 200 fps and 4k support. The story seems good at the beginning but slowly turns a bit strange at the end not gonna lie. Gameplay is fast, responsive and customization is cool. Stats seem to matter but the biggest things that actually feel important is Durability HP and Boost speed in my opinion. -Bad-I have had 1 crash early in the game during a random mission but i couldn't figure out why it crashed. Never crashed since. There isn't a difficulty option so everything kind of becomes fodder once you get used to the game even bosses as the patterns are pretty much 1-2-3 for phases or attack options. While there are a decent amount of armor sets which can be mixed and matched, you'll probably either using a full end game set of one of the high tier sets or a mix of them. The characters feel like they have personality at first but usually stick to their cliche as the edge lord, punk, family fodder or etc. -Overall-It was interesting and fun enough that I actually blew through the story in 2 days so definitely wasn't a bad buy. I wish there was more to the story like a post ending ark or something but maybe they will have actually GOOD dlc post story who knows. Is it worth the full $60? ...ehhhh hard pass I'd say get it on sale for 47 and under for now. It's polished enough for that but not more than that. It'll definitely fill your mecha itch if you like gundam, armored core or just wanna zoom around and blow stuff up.7.5/10I'd give it a 8/10 but the story kinda brought it down to be honest.*EDIT*I do want to add i played this game with PS4 controller. I don't think i could have played this with keyboard and mouse big FYI.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to tip your toes into a Armored Core-like game in anticipation for Fires of Rubicon, this is a Ok start to the franchise as the older games are harder to get. But a majority of your experience and expectations here will not carry over to Armored Core.At the moment, this game feels like the combination of Destiny & Armored Core (namely For Answer / Verdict Day), with parts being lock behind a "looter-shooter" mechanic that leaves the player constantly wanting for a part they'll never get. The problem with this system is that it locks critical parts like the body and weapon types to this "part drop" system, and leaves the "buy" section of the shop almost empty until you get to B rank or so. By the time the player reaches B rank they'll be already locked into a particular playstyle as a result of either their preference, or their bad luck forcing them into a set path (and that is usually a dual assault rifle build). TLDR; Good soft-entry to the Armored Core franchise, but was not able to capture what makes Armored Core fun with the customisation aspect of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: There hasn't been a new Armored Core game in YEARS so already this game is a bucket of water to the face after wandering a desert. Especially since the Developers added their own touches that fixed alot of the frustrations that Armored Core always had. Multiplayer is the big suprise. It has PvP as you would expect, but what I didn't expect was a PvE Dungeon crawler mode with up to 3 other players. It's like running the Bloodborne Chalice dungeons but with your friends! Now why is that cool you ask? Because this game uses a quirky loot based Salvage and crafting system to acquire new equipment in a manner that ALMOST reminds me of monster hunter. The game isn't without it's flaws. Primarily I found the Single player missions to be repetitive and the storyline DROWNING in stale Anime Cliche's. Still, It's a welcome addition to the Anime Mecha pantheon and I hope to the lords above that it gets a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, new Review. Starting with what is good, and then what is bad.-GoodMechs look generally awesome, only sometimes will you have the 'didn't go to leg day' issue, but most of the time, your mech looks great.It's a very pretty game.Voice acting is actually REALLY good, especially if you compare it to other mech based games.It's not New Gundam Breaker. Seriously, you'd think this isn't a compliment, but you'd be wrong, any mech game that isn't New Gundam Breaker is automatically decent. Character customization is fairly alright.Decent story, you get interested fairly quickly, and then.. a little confused.. but still interested.MOVEMENT! Is super fun to skate across the ground, that's just neato.Jack is a good boy.-BadAlright..so, I tend to be a fairly negative reviewer unless I LOVE a game to death, so.. grain of salt folks.Mech customization is too limited. While it's really good for what it is, there are certain RNG elements that make it a grind to get your mech looking the way you want it, otherwise you'll usually be stuck with 2 or 3 specific mech looks.Combat is kind of trash, like.. it's messy and HYPER fast paced, like.. I'm fine with a fast paced game, but this is like.. too fast for the human eye my dude. The A.I. will dart around you at extreme speeds while perfectly locked onto you and firing every possible weapon at once, all of them hitting you. Unless they're a turret, then either A- they will A L W A Y S miss, for no reason.. or they will have pin point accuracy and be able to predict every movement.Fighting the Immortals.. on one hand? It's a SUPER RAD (I D E A) that you would fight GIANT ROBOTS, with your smaller, but still large, robot. B U T, all of the SUPER SIZED ROBOTS are WAAAY faster than you, to a stupid degree. Except for the very first one you encounter, and even get to pilot... that thing is like stupid slow. The issue is, due to the combat being hyper uber fast, you can't look, or F e e l .. cool. Instead you are chasing around a giant robo spider, or orca aircraft thingy. And it doesn't feel cool.. it feels cartoony.. like how in some cartoons a mom will try to chase down her kid to get them to take medicine. You just don't feel cool.Weapon sizes. Ok, some of you will love how weapons are stupid big. H O W E V E R, they ALL lack that... UMFH, y'know what I mean? Alright, when you fire a weapon you should.. FEEL that "THUD" or that "BRRAP" or.. in some sexy, sexy, SEXY, cases.. that "BRRRRRRRRRRRT" but.. I haven't felt any of that.. I have fired "Charging" lasers, I have fired "Machine guns" I have fired missile pods.. an "Ogre Breaker Cannon" . . . .and like.. a dual shoulder BEAM CANNON. . and none of them feel . . "UHMF" I've fired a bazooka too, and it felt like nothing. This game lacks that... Kick back.. that feeling of "WHOA I just fired something that could kill an island." Y'know? I get none of those feelings when using weapons in this game, EXCEPT, when using the Mace. . The way your mech readies the mace and slams it down into somethings face is almost comical. it's slow.. and then "BATTER UP" gone. hilarious. . . but still lacking.Speed vs Health/durability. So.. either you can dodge almost anything.. or you get hit by everything, those are your choices. . . and even then you still can't 'dodge' everything.. And if you think you'll be a tanky bugger, you are wrong. You will melt like butter.Laser swords in this game are dumb, and feel like trash... actually almost every melee weapon I have used feels that way.. so do shields. feels... lacking.Combat feels like you are being punished for wanting to go through combat. . .it's.. dull. Lack of tips and tricks. I am fairly sure the game didn't fully explain using up or down on my D-pad or arrow keys would give me new, special abilities.  .  . so that sucks. Lack of information in general. There is a plethora of info in the game.. however.. it doesn't explain how, or why, or what certain things are, or really do. Like Blitz, I still haven't found a "Blitz" weapon yet, but in the Chievos I see "Psychic" so.. Idfk. Oh, and be careful in the lab, you might end up looking really really dumb with those "upgrades" Lack of entering your awesome Mech. _childDocuments_.review: Before I start talking about "Daemon x Machina", I would like to talk about my experience with "God Eater 3" for this paragraph. When I first saw that game, I didn't think much before buying it. It was a hack-and-slash anime RPG, and I was very much captivated by it at first glance. But upon some days playing it, I got to a conclusion: I hated it. It was too repetitive and too bland. I wasn't roaming a world, but rather, I was stuck to a home base from where I would be sent to the same small environments - over and over again. Missions were timed, and I would fight gradually harder enemies at each assignment. Things got to a point I couldn't take that anymore: the game was aggressively boring, and I had no pleasure completing its repetitive missions.Now, why am I talking about "GE3" in a review of "Daemon x Machina"? Because when I started playing it, I felt a strong déjà vu with that game. I was placed in a hangar, from where once again I would be sent to small scenarios. I was apprehensive this game was going to be "GE3" all over again... but to my surprise (and relief), the game was much better than that. I would even say this is the game "GE3" should have been all along.For starters, the combat is absolutely awesome. You really get to live that mecha anime fantasy in this game. You can fly, swing swords and fire weapons at all will. The combat makes for a game very pleasant to play, and in case you're wondering, keyboard and mouse are just fine (in fact, the precision of the mouse helps a lot at shooting). When you start the game, you have this bland mecha at your disposal, but as you progress, looting new accessories and buying new items, you can customise your mecha to something more to your liking. I favour high fire rate weapons, but some others may prefer swords and they'll be covered.Body parts can variate from light and nimble to heavy and resistant. And they can totally be destroyed if they receive enough damage, giving you a disadvantage during combat. You can't repair broken parts during assigments, but you can replace them should you find the right pieces near you.You can loot weapons and body parts from fallen Strai - enemy mechas that are decidedly harder to beat than common foes. You can also buy items at your base, and even research for new ones at the lab if you have other items from which they'll be build from. There are also attachments that can significantly improve weapons and body parts - provided that they have the proper slots for them.The missions usually request you to dispose of enemy AI in an area, but there's actually a welcome amount of variation to the missions. And better still: there aren't time restrains for the vast majority of the missions, meaning you can complete them at your own time. You have your traditional search-and-destroy, boss battles and surprisingly non-frustrating escort missions. You don't feel like doing the same missions repetitively: in one mission, I actually started outside my mecha, and I had to infiltrate into an enemy base to steal a mecha.Speaking of which, you can totally leave your mecha during missions, specially if your mecha is down. You become much more vulnerable, obviously, but you're not defenceless, since you still have some means of defending yourself. You can even upgrade your human character to become more powerful on their own, but some upgrades will change the very physical appearance of your character. So if you like your character as they are, be warned of that (but you can undo such changes).You'll also have side missions - known as "free missions" - that can provide you with extra rewards, like more credits, new decals for your mecha and even new mission partners. Side missions come with optional objectives that if completed can grant you more credits. And once again, such missions are variate: in one of them, I actually commanded a giant mecha (albeit it wasn't as fun as it sounds).The environments are not so variated physically: they're in the majority of cases open areas for you to fly freely, but they still have boundaries you're not supposed to cross. Otherwise, a countdown will start, alerting you to return the mission area. There will also be some missions that take place inside large corridors, with plenty enemy turrets in the way - these missions are much more linear than the others. Once you complete a mission, then a countdown will appear, and this is your opportunity to grab the loot you didn't have the chance to get to during combat."DXM" also has this oddity about it: the ice-cream parlour, which will be available to you soon in the game. In it, you can order ice-cream for a small price. But it does serves a gameplay propose: the ice-cream can provide you with certain boosts for your next mission, depending on the flavours you ordered. Why did it have to be ice-cream, instead of something more technical and coherent with the themes? Maybe it was for some good old-fashioned anime humour.Then, there's the story. Now, I left it for last for a reason: it's kind of superfluous. The story is presented mostly before or after missions - sometimes there will be a cut-scene during the levels. There'll also be a lot of dialogues presented in online chat form, and characters have that anime swagger about them, just to legitimise this game as anime. But a game like this feels all about gameplay, so the story feels - once again - superfluous.All in all, Marvelous Inc. did a marvellous job here. "Daemon x Machina" pulls you in with its mechanics, and it keeps you invested with its customisation. It's a very fun game... plus, there's an adorable doggo at your hangar. How can anyone say no to that?

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Biased in favor of anything with big stompy robots.Daemon X Machina seems to be an attempt to rekindle interest in a previously abandoned subgenre, of which Armored Core used to be the flagship of. As such, a lot is picked up from those series. It appears that many aspects of the game were intended to be grander than they are, but the studio probably run out of funds, time or both. The most dramatic casualty of this is the story, it is so bad it's physically painful. Trust me, you are better off skipping all dialogue, cutscenes, turning voice volume to 0 and shrinking the communication dialog box on HUD settings. Whatever you can conjure up in your imagination, is going to be an improvement.Past that there is robot fun to be had, customizing, smashing, slashing and shooting your way thru both single and co op missions. Do keep in mind the thing searches for matches using your steam download region. Forget about PvP unless you organize matches via the discord server , because the game lacks any anti cheat.On the flip side, lacking any anti cheat, means you can use cheat engine to bypass some bad design decisions, such as the mandatory visual effect of cyber upgrades on your pilot, and the multi layered RNG frustration of a loot system they put in. What happened to just using ingame cash to buy your stuff?Anyway, this is getting a thumbs up from me mostly because the mech genre is starved for choice. But, frankly, if you haven't experienced Armored Core you are better off firing up an emulator and playing that instead. I'm kinda already way too familiar with those.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish I could recommend this game, but it lacks any kind of long-time play value in it's current state.TL;DR : A beautiful, well designed mech fighter wrapped inside a shobby story, non-existent endgame, and shallow multiplayer modes.The actual combat is fun and smooth, the mech customization is well designed with plenty of ways to fine-tune and configure your mechs to give them a unique and individual feel to them. These two things are the fundamental cores of mech-warrior style games, and they nail both of them down to the tee.Then they give you absolutely nothing to do with it.the story mode is short, redundant and mediocre in plot and storytelling, with little replay value in missions.Getting the best possible versions of weapons and attachments involves running through "explore" missions with up to three other players. It's basically a proceduraly generated dungeon crawl that will have you going through the same dozen room configurations to grind enemies for their loot. Of course, there's no actual point at the moment to grinding the dungeon for the best versions of equipment, no enemy in the game is difficult enough to need a maxed out build, and competitive multiplayer feels like an afterthought for the developers. You have the option of a 1v1 deathmatch, or a 2v2 deathmatch. and that's it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's nice to finally have a decent mecha game again, been too long since AC4A (thanks V...).Daemon X Machina is a quite in depth mecha game with many unique systems which take some getting used to at first. The game takes the typical stance of a lot of mecha games where you are a self insert rookie rising through the ranks, gaining new and improved weapons, armor (mech body parts), attachments (perks), and body modifications (this one is a little bit odd, but essentially you can augment your pilot with mechanical upgrades that make them more powerful but at the cost of changing the look of your character to become more of a cyborg). In the game you encounter general grunt like units (cannon fodder), AI mecha (lightly challenging), Piloted mecha (minibosses - bosses), and giant boss machines (which are interesting to fight, but soak up a lot of damage, similar to arms forts in AC4A)The game is fast paced and fun, and while the systems within take a bit of getting used to, makes for a unique experience. I've had a lot of fun with it so far and recommend it to fans of the armored core franchise, or mecha action games in general.I don't normally want to write a review for a game I've played so little hours in. How ever I think I've played enough to get a feel for the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent purchase, if it's discounted. The game's short comings for as far as I've played are as follows.HUD/Screen Clutter:- All HUD elements are inflated for maximum clutter. You can fix this by going into a menu and down-sizing each element individually and moving them about, but I'm not sure why it's so bloated to begin with. A slider to reduce the size of all elements at once would also be handy to make the task less finicky.- The player's mech is also positioned in such a way that it obscures a lot of the left side of the screen. I believe this could easily be solved by letting us zoom in and out to determine how much of the mecha model we really want to be cluttering our screens, and providing a FoV slider which is sadly lacking from this game. All action-oriented games should have one, as even third-person games can induce headaches or be difficult to enjoy with a default FoV of 70 or less.  - It gets really difficult to keep track of things in all the clutter, also because of how thin the lines of the lock-on markers are, it makes it difficult to distinguish them in all the clutter while there is a lot going on at once.Characters: - The NPC characters which form the majority of dialogue in the game are stilted and inflated tropes with little personality of their own. Story:- The player is treated as a spectator to a story they have no reason to be engaged with or invested in. - The player character is barely recognized by the game aside from off-hand remarks about how awesome they are as a rookie pilot. It doesn't really matter if you're fumbling your way through the game or not.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've watched Gundam 00 and you're into that kind of robot action, Daemon X Machina is probably your type of thing.Gameplay is fast and responsive while still having a good amount of "clunk" to it to make it feel like you're actually piloting a robot while being considerably more beginner friendly than the Armored Core series. While customization isn't "put-spider-legs-on-your-mech" crazy levels, there's still a good amount of room for you to specialize your arsenal to your playstyle and experiment with the ups and downs of each type of build. There's also an incredible attention to small details and things you can do in the mechanics, albeit while a lot of them are somewhat impractical, can lead to some guerilla tactics and moments you manage to barely clear a mission thinking outside the box. Being able to upgrade your pilot to be able to do things outside the mech leads to some fun cheesing in missions, and sometimes you get really cool moments like throwing your ammoless weapon at the enemy and picking up a weapon that's dropped on the map to replace it.Unfortunately for a game with solid foundations, the surrounding content might've understandably need some more time in the oven. There are simply not enough missions that feature unique circumstances that really test your arsenal building skills, with one of the missions where your build actually matters screwing over a tank build without warning you beforehand. After the story modethe worthwhile missions are the online ones, and even then you'll see all the rooms in the dungeon crawling missions rather quickly, and people aren't going to be online all the time to help you take down the more difficult bosses. It actually makes me wish there was DLC content.The story starts off in an interesting setting with characters who had potential but sadly it's botched by the story jumping to a different plot thread every 5 second, thanks to that all the late game twists come feel incredibly lame and empty. The late game lore exposition is mostly dropped by a villain who tries to make himself sound deeper than he actually is so that's no help at all.Overall it's a game that aims hard at people who are interested in mechas, if you aren't already into mechas then this game might not do much for you because the game is lacking in areas outside the combat, but if you're already into mechas I'd say this game is almost a must buy.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game with many potential, a game that seems fun, the armor core like designs, the swift action, the quick to action intro are all great.If you are hoping for a good mech game, keep looking, this is mediocre, not bad, but not good either, it has a lot of issues, most of them stemming from the fact that it is trying to be armor core, while also trying to be an Evangalion anime game, this makes the game some what annoying, especially with the story, the characters only makes things worse.Let's get started with game-play, it is not bad, but it does not do anything to make the game easier to get into, nor does it do anything to allow hardcore gamer's to do something cool to show off on their skills, so it is generic as generic can get, switching weapon's is not necessary as all weapons are viable for every scenario, just make sure you can keep a distance from enemies and you can easily wipe anything that moves, however, melee enemies are overpowered, as they can instantly launch to you without needing to close up to use their melee ability, you can't do this by the way, you actually have to get close to use your melee, this makes this game just feel like it wants to be a souls series while ignoring what makes a souls series great.Story, no.Characters, I think the voice lines were purposely design for torture, because I ended up just ignoring the story on this second run of the game, I played the game on switch, this is my second run on PC.Overall the game is mediocre, it is not bad, but neither is getting sick and missing a day to go to a job you dislike, just don't spend anything above $20 and you will be able to enjoy some of this game knowing that you did not spend the full asking price, because this is not a $60 game, no where near that.To the developer's; I see what you are all doing, it is a game with potential, but stick to perfecting the game before release, and here's a little secret, we American's aren't going to avoid your game if you don't have English voice actors, we prefer voice actors that don't sound like they were picked straight out of modern day Nick Jr. to take up roles for our game, also please concentrate your story, sit down, does it make sense, create drama relevant to the player, drama that forces the player to want to care about what is going on, customization needs to not just be visual but actually make sense with how it effects the mech, and limiting customization to only a couple of things and creating mech models can create more things for the player want to save credits for them to buy in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw reviews calling this game "Armored Core Lite", I was initially excited, as AC4A is actually one of my favorite mecha games ever. What I wasn't quite prepared for is how "Lite" this game truly is.Dumbed down customization, specs, components, story, etc. Take everything great about the AC franchise and look at it at a surface level only, and you have DXM. That isn't to say the game is bad, but it doesn't quite satisfy that itch. That... Want... associated with a new Armored Core game. In fact, the game left me wanting. Wanting an actual new AC title to play, since it has been many a year since I sold my 360 to play Armored Core 4A and V. Let's get into the nitty gritty:Gameplay:All the core components of an Armored Core experience are here, but the default controls on gamepad are kind of... lackluster. Button placement in AC is just better. Part of the issue is that your thruster movement is on RB and your shoot is on RT, making it a little awkward to play, especially if you regularly are trying to do both at the same time.Other than that, no real complaints. As stated, it's basically watered down armored core. No core stats to really pay attention to. Energy Consumption, etc aren't things that are really affected by what you install, and are instead tied to your character and the body modifications they try to force you to take. Basically, the game tries to make you look like a cyborg if you actually invest in that particular tree. And you don't get previews in the game for what you're buying into, so hope you like what you get after you get it? My advice? Try to save scum it for what you like.Graphics:It looks worse than AC4, so.... I mean, take it with a grain of salt. AC4 came out in what? Like 2007? It's just the cell-shaded style that kind of makes the game look dated. I can't look at it without thinking of retro Dragonball Z games like the horrible Ultimate Tenkaichi, or Borderlands.Audio:Kind of get the same audio vibe from Code Vein? I guess? Just a little more heavy metal thrown in.Customization:Lackluster at best. Component selection has options that are DEFINITELY better than others, rather than being tradeoffs for various aspects of gameplay. Paint pallets are tied to only three customizable colors per part on your mech, Definitely a lot less than what you got in AC or even competing titles like MASS Builder (Though MASS Builder has much more of a Gundam aesthetic, and plays a lot differently). Decals especially are bad here, as there is only one decal you can place per part.Story:Kind of like the corporations and various factions in AC, particularly noted in 4A due to them being completely integral to the story, DXM has similar. Corporations control areas within the sphere of where the remainder of humanity resides. Various mercenary factions accept contracts from these corps, and there is a core sphere of influence that mediates everything. It's great on paper, but most of these organizations seem very two-dimensional, particularly with the "Good Guy" and "Bad Guy" gimmicks. In AC, Organizations like ORCA introduced you to truly grey areas within the ongoing conflicts, and the branching paths of the story gave you multiple playthroughs within it.Overall, while I feel like there's a lot to complain about, it is by no means a bad title. Just very shallow. I hope this studio makes a sequel, and I hope it is much more in-depth than this one. This one just left me wanting so much more.If you are an AC fan interested in this title because you like AC, I will say, this game didn't do it for me, but it might for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start with this one? Its honestly a mixed bag of a game. On the outside we see it as an Armored Core spiritual successor. On the inside, it really tried, but didn't fare so well. The game fell pretty short of what I was hoping it'd be but not much one can do. The devs had an idea, and they really squandered the potential it could've been with...well we'll get to that in a minute.The first largest problem this game has is the characters. Theres just way too many of them, and you're constantly interacting with them. They have "story" yet their stories aren't really ever panned out because of how one dimensional their personalities and attitudes are. Its like the devs took the most archetypal stereotypes they could imagine, and cranked them to 11 making them insufferable. It makes no sense, who wrote the lines for these characters? None of them had growth or development really. One minute you're fighting to the death with some of them in one mission, next they're all buddy buddy the next. The characters just don't fit in the game at all. The voice acting, it was pretty good? They had some decent voice actors. I saw my main man Richard Epcar voiced Brigader General. But other than that, the characters themselves, could've done without them. Some of the lines they had were so cringey I can't imagine how the voice actors could even take the job seriously. The gameplay itself is fairly ok? It sort of feels like an Armored Core game. It sorta Looks like an Armored Core game. But don't be fooled. This is NOT an Armored Core game. The game on a scale of 1 to 10 for difficulty, 1 being least difficult and 10 being the highest difficulty. I'd rate it as a 1 or 2. There was literally only 2 parts of the game I needed to redo because I had the wrong weapons for the missions or didnt pace myself properly. The game is a cake walk. Armored Core games used to be super hard. But thats coming from From Software, not Marvelous. Marvelous had the chance to make it difficult but they completely blew their chance with this one. The game's enemy AI is so stupid its a wonder they even bothered putting any enemies in the missions. May as well have just made you take constant health damage instead because you could've probably finished any mission and still had plenty to spare. The missions were easy, predictable and had no real variety. Considering almost every mission you're constantly meeting the other mercs one way or another and always teamed up with them. There was no danger at all. There was no risk. Every mission is a joke of difficulty.The entire story itself was a mess. The game made no sense, a lot of things are never fully explained or if explained, its very poorly done. They leave so many things unanswered because they shoved too much into it. Too many characters that take up too much time between eachother. It made no sense and I'm still left in the end scratching my head what the heck just happened? Why did any of this happen? The story could honestly use an entire rewrite or something because as is. The game literally cannot be taken seriously.Other parts of the game were poorly implemented too. The store? Why is the store a thing? I've beaten the game and the only thing that populates the store are new processors, and nothing else. What goes into the store at all? Its never explained because it seems more or less you use the factory more than the actual store which confuses me. Shouldn't new items be available for purchase? Guess not it seems. The crafting seems ok...for the most part if it didn't require sacrificing other items to build it. And those items seemingly never appear in game half the time. I'm still missing a ton of parts because stuff just doesn't seem to drop off of enemy ai arsenals or the other mercs. The ice cream parlor? This just doesn't even fit the game setting at all. A fluffy fuzzy bear mascot and ice cream that boosts your stats. Of course this had to be added? No thanks, i could've done without it. Actually I went completely without it. I never used it once. I never even bothered upgrading my character themselves. You get to step outside of your arsenal...2 times in 2 different missions and thats it? Theres really no benefit using our character outside of the arsenal in missions.The game also supposedly has mods you can put into your weapons and armor yet half of them are unavaiable. Its not made clear where or how you get them aside a few from finishing bonus stuff on time for some specific missions but that seems rare and possibly one time only? The games mechanics are all over the place and a mess. None of it honestly makes sense. Theres no real tutorial to tell you how some of these things work.The sound design I honestly have not much to say. I didn't feel much for it. I barely noticed much of the games sounds. Most of it just blew past by me because it seemed fairly generic. The only thing that stood out was the sound of the large shoulder beam weapons, other than that I felt pretty underwhelmed by the games sounds. Music too. I never caught anything that seemed to be catchy. Armored Core used to have such great music and this one? I never really found a single track that was played during any mission that stood out.The UI in mission also was pretty much a mess. Having the weapon and ammo in the near center of the screen was a bit frustrating. You can get rid of UI elements if you wish, but honestly you needed it in some missions because you have to watch your ammo lest you run out in missions where no enemy ai units spawn which give you back ammo. Most missions it isn't an issue but some you will run out so knowing so you aren't burning through your ammo is a decent idea. But otherwise if the positioning of the ammo counter annoys you, please turn it off. It can get grating having it there all the time like that taking up screen space. It felt like having a bit of a blind spot constantly staring me in the face.Would I recommend this game? Honestly? Not really. If you are an Armored Core series fan, and want to play a game that tickles  your fancy. Go back and play some of the PS1 / PS2 / PS3 Armored Core games instead. What you want cannot be found in this game unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:1.) Highly customizable Mechs known in-universe as Arsenals. Parts can be mixed and matched to suit any player's needs, provided that they find the right parts on missions (be it single player or multiplayer).2.) Weapon variety and weapon pylons allow for players to quickly switch strategies on the fly.3.) Highly optimized even at maximum settings. Can run good frames even with just a basic laptop.4.) (EDIT 2022-12-29 A.D.) If you bothered to listen in, the soundtrack is actually pretty good. Wouldn't say it's the best but it is serviceable for most situations.Cons:1.) Parts are hard to come by and barely show up in the shops. I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong, but I'm already at Mercenary Rank A and still I've not seen much updates from the in-game Shop. Aside from the upgraded Processors, barely anything new in terms of body parts and weaponry can be found there. Compare this with the Armored Core games where most if not all parts are available on the shop from the start and the players only need to grind for money to get the parts they want. In Daemon X Machina, you get no such comfort and instead have to grind on countless missions and the best you'll achieve are parts that are either serviceable at best or parts you'll have to sell eventually. Only rarely do you get parts that are actually worth keeping on missions.2.) Attachments and upgrading parts is an iffy affair. Good luck finding the exact Part/Weapon you need to upgrade since the loot system can be very random depending on your runs.3.) Story isn't that investing, especially when one considers the connection between the main antagonist and the player character. There was only one moment of interactive dialogue and that was all the way back in the beginning where you can ask Four (the A.I.) three questions. (EDIT 2022-12-25 A.D.: After completing the final mission, which was an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of attrition, the player is once again given a choice which alters the ending depending on which choice the player made and considering that the main antagonist doesn't exactly endear himself to players, I don't think many chose the second choice the first time around).4.) Loot system isn't that great. You can only loot one part per scrapped Strai and good luck even finding some good quality parts on even higher difficulty missions. (EDIT 2022-12-29 A.D.: I'm aware that this is for multiplayer so that each player can get one part from each downed Strai but as someone that prefers to keep things in the single player portion of things, this limitation can get rather annoying.)5.) Damage system is rather confusing. While the raw damage value is understandable, having it be split to Bullet and Laser Damage can be jarring, especially against fights against enemy Arsenals (be it A.I. or actual players) as you are unable to figure out immediately which is better suited for the occasion. Melee is the only saving grace in that most of them besides laser blades just rely on the raw damage values. And good luck even getting into melee distance to begin with.(EDIT 2022-12-25 A.D.)6.) Okay, it didn't bother me that much but the bosses are far too tanky when using builds that do not play into whatever meta the game has. It's not that obvious with most bosses, but two stand out in particular: Rebellion and the Dominator. In Rebellion's case, you encounter it late into the story and it's a big robot with a big sword and shield that makes use of its size to crush anything in it's way. In Dominator's case, it's (spoilers) the final boss.In both cases, dealing with them is less about figuring out the challenge they put out to the player and more of a battle of attrition as it will require most (if not all) of your ammunition and good luck if you do not have at least one melee weapon that isn't your Arsenal's fists. In a special case for the Dominator, unless you are using a build with high levels of armor and VP as well as being equipped with enough ammo to wipe out the entire United States of America, have fun swinging your fists and swords at him like I did while being very low on VP all while being harassed by what appeared to be an unending supply of drones. Seriously, I've wasted a good chunk of ammo in one failed attempt getting rid of them and for some reason, Dominator's little friends kept respawning as some artificial way of ramping up an already artificially difficult boss.Final Verdict: It's a good game but the listed cons do take out the enjoyment of it. And the lack of meaningful progress in terms of parts and weapons acquisition (especially through the Shop and Factory) does make this game less enjoyable overall. That's not even getting into the boss fights which do not have the balance of challenge, difficulty, and enjoyment that the larger boss fights of the Armored Core games and are instead basically just massive bullet sponges without much else to add onto them.If Daemon X Machina 2 releases, I really hope the devs actually address these since there are far more cons than pros in my own experience.Daemon X Machina has some good ideas but the execution is sloppy in notable areas.

_childDocuments_.review: Daemon X Machina is a game that I feel like came out half-finished, the sort of thing you'd see in the bargain bin in the final days of the Xbox 360/PS3 era. It's got a lot of jank, not a whole lot of depth, and developer priorities that don't make any sense.Right away, you can tell that the developers dropped a lot of money and time into the cutscenes and the plot, which is a total waste because there really isn't one. There's apparently some kind of prequel anime that's supposed to explain the game's setting, but that isn't included in the game itself. The Japanese voiceovers use a lot of big-name anime voiceactors which clearly cost the developers a good chunk of their budget. The cutscenes themselves are really confusing and a lot of them are never really explained. The basic premise behind the plot is that the moon explodes and part of it impacts Earth, spreading a substance called "Femto" which is basically just Tiberium from Command and Conquer. Femto kills most things exposed to it, except for some people who become "Outers" and can pilot giant mechs for no apparent reason. Honestly, there's not a whole lot of rhyme or reason to the plot other than "fighting giant robots is cool".The issue I had is that a lot of times, you'll do a story mode mission and there's a cutscene before and a cutscene after the mission, both of which are usually longer than the mission itself. They're always the same, too: most of the missions are an AI telling you to do something in your giant robot, then having other giant robots show up out of nowhere, and then fighting those giant robots. The game hypes this up with a bunch of cutscenes of generic anime people talking vaguely about seemingly important (but vague) events like it's Lost or something. I finished the singleplayer mode and I feel like I still didn't understand half the plot.The game itself really isn't deep enough to hold interest for very long. As I said earlier, most missions in the singleplayer mode are "Hey you, go do this" and then giant robots show up. The missions in story mode are usually under 5 minutes long and consist of holding down the gun button until everything dies. The enemy robots aren't really well-programmed enough to be challenging: most of the time they wind up burning through their stamina bar and sitting on the ground at a standstill or glitching into level geometry and letting you get a ton of free shots off at them. The mech customization is a thing, but it's also not great. There's maybe twenty or thirty parts to pick from for each "area" of your mech: head, torso, arms, legs. Most of them are very similar to the point where unless you're using a melee-spec arm for guns, it's not really going to matter much what you use unless you're doing PVP. The online for this game was pretty much dead on arrival, so good luck even finding someone to do that with. Even if you do, the meta is to be very fast and pack two of the fastest-firing assault rifles and then click the button first.The weapons in this game are the polar opposite of the armor. There's a bunch of different weapon types divided into three categories: bullet, laser, and melee. The problem is that many of the weapons are downright unusable. Sniper rifles in particular can't outdamage an assault rifle even if used optimally, shotguns do no damage even at point blank range, and flamethrowers have their damage tied to the framerate and do virtually nothing above 30 FPS. It's unlikely the developers are ever going to patch that last one, or patch the game at all. Most people tend to use either assault rifles (or SMGs) for PvP and fighting other mechs and the bigger charge lasers and cannons for bosses. Part of the problem I have with the mech customization as well is that there's no real sense of progression. Apart from maybe one or two weapons, you're capable of obtaining everything from the get-go through the game's random dungeon mode. This means there's not really going to be a whole lot of difference between your mech at the start of the game and your mech at the end. Oh right, there's bosses too. The bosses are all really giant robots, typically several hundred times your size. Most of them are a total joke and can be taken down very quickly. There's also a series of multiplayer-only bosses that drop the best gear in the game. Good luck ever fighting them with the online being dead on arrival. Worse, the boss drops aren't a "one-and-done" thing: you have to fight them a minimum of four or five times to get enough "combat data" to make them. There's not much of a reason to even bother grinding them in the first place though, given that once you've grinded through the singleplayer missions that's all the content the game has to offer. Finally, as a PC port, Daemon X Machina is not great. The cutscenes are all done in 720p (the Switch's native resolution) and the game does not have ultrawide support, but even without an ultrawide monitor you'll be seeing black bars every time there's a cutscene. There's no indication that the developers are going to fix any of the PC-specific bugs.Overall, I'd say avoid Daemon X Machina unless it's on sale at a steep discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Spiritual successor to Armored Core 4 and For Answer. If you're looking to scratch that itch on PC without running an emulator, this is the game for you. Coming over from AC the cons are the change in flight behavior with the jump jets lacking the same analog hover control. This is not a huge deal as flight is unlimited (excepting boost) but will be frustrating when trying to jump obstacles or maintain a certain altitude. Lack of shields has removed a dynamic of customization from the game, wherein it doesn't really feel like there is an importance to tailoring your mechs as much though the customization is still there. While there is an abundance of free missions, the lack of arena 1 on 1 with choice NPCs is vexing. While there is multiplayer support, the lack of player base leaves you alone on missions designed for multiplayer blocking crucial gear upgrades. With some updates and quality of life improvements this successor can be truly worthy. The story was generic tropy anime plot B, however being cast by a wide range of big name anime voice actors, it was nice to hear some of my favorites in there. I wouldn't change too much about this game... I would just add to it. It's the best you'll do on PC for an AC kick.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun mecha action game for anybody wanting to scratch that feeling of a good Armored Core game. Combat is great and the mech personalisation is fun. Graphics are nothing amazing (I mean, it’s a port from a Switch game) but the art style is solid enough to not make it look ugly. The game has a mission structure that puts you in relatively small maps, so missions are short, but entertaining and the variety of objectives is ok, a little repetitive by the end game but nothing awful. Game has decent length, not too short but not needlessly long either. Now the one terrible thing is the plot, from cutscenes, dialogue and narrative in general it’s just awfull and borring, wolrd construction is nonsencical and character development is either non existent of just plain stupid. It’s been sometime since I’ve felt so utterly annoyed by a game narrative, really just pure garbage.So a decent game, not amazing but far from bad, terrible plot and characters but fun gameplay. A solid 7/10 for me, would recommend a good discount.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an okay game, but I don't think its worth getting it for the full $60 price.What I liked:-Combat areas are spacious makes flying and zipping around feel really great.-Mobility was responsive and fast.-Body Augmentation System is awesome-Building and Balancing your Mecha-Not a grind-fest-Game is skill based. _childDocuments_.review: A true Armored Core spiritual successor with the closest in term of gameplay and customization and probably one of the best Mech game on PC right now.ThIs game used to be Nintendo Switch exclusive, but it's on PC now with up to 4k resolution ,200 fps cap, and rebindable Mouse and keyboard control. Gameplay is quite similar to Armored Core V / Verdict Day mashed with 4 / For Answer with a feels of classic PS1/2 era Armored Core, with advanced feature removed or simplified, like, overheating which basically just a debuff in this game. Also you can get out of your mech and fight with your pilot character or swap / hijack your friend mech in multiplayer.As for Customization. It's very simplified. For example, there's only biped leg, your lock on screen size is depend on your head parts and you can't change the color of your mech glowing parts. But there's Chip customization which allow you to strengthen parts  and customize parts and weapon stats.The story and characters is kinda sucks, so i don't really pay attention to the that. Amuro and Char Voice actor are in this game and you can unlock and use their voice for your custom character.Multiplayer Co-op and Exploration is really fun and basically the main course in this game (at least for me).In Co-op Mission you can fight a team of Ai Mech which you can salvage their parts, and fight a giant boss where you can unlock their blueprint and farm chips.In Exploration, you fight in a more closed space of randomly generated room with random effects and enemies, where your goal is to either take down the boss mech at the end area or explore every single room where you can salvage random drop from fallen mech and obtain some strong chip attachments.As for PvP, I've never really try it, but there's only 1v1 & 2v2, and ranked matches only available on 1v1.Soundtrack is pretty cool, but not nearly as epic as Armored Core 4 / For Answer incredible soundtrack.Pros-High speed mech shooter-Exit the cockpit and fight as the pilot-Mech and Character Customization-Fun Multiplayer Missions-Easy & Smooth Control-200 fps cap & 4k resolutionCons-Simplified version of Armored Core-Not much armor parts, especially just bipedal leg type-Story is lackluster and characters have typical anime personality-Ai is pretty dumb sometimes-You can get stuck in a mission, if you exit your mech at high place and fall, you're stuck as a pilot with no other way to reach your mech except if you already upgrade your character ability with jetpack or double jump.-Weapon Balance (some weapons are op, some weapons are simply not nearly as useful as the others)-not much of contents or something to do in the game (most of the time you just grind bosses for blueprint or explorations for parts)Overall, it's an amazing mech game but not nearly as depth as Armored Core to be called a sim game, it's more of an Arcade Shooter with Mech theme and a bit of looter shooter because of the chips customization and RnG based loot. Definitely a must for Armored Core fan or Gundam fan. But due to lack of contents currently, probably wait for sale.
_childDocuments_.name: DAEMON X MACHINA

_childDocuments_.review: About PC port:It is [almost] peerless. Customizable frame rate up to 200, up to 4k support, fully rebindable controls, standard UE4 graphics options, nothing to complain about.Except there is apparently a mouse sensitivity bug, that you can circumvent it by adjusting your camera sensitivity and locking your FPS to constant valueAbout the game:This is basically Armored Core Lite. It follows the same principles, but is smaller, shallower and simpler game.It goes for everything - customization, combat, world building, story, even characters, despite them having faces now.Does that mean it's a bad game? No, just smaller in scope than AC fan would expect, especially compared to Last Raven or For Answer.Will it scratch that Armored Core itch? Yes.Can it stand in for AC6? No, not really.Between that, and obnoxious DLC policy I recommend this game on sale, unless you're huge mecha fan, in which case you already own it.50 hours update:While my first impression was that it's a poor man's Armored Core with less everything, after I completed every mission and got MOST of the unique equipment pieces (some just won't drop) I gotta say my opinion of this game changed quite a bit.For one I still stand by the notion that customization is inferior to AC. In both visual and gameplay terms. No internal parts, limited shoulder slot control, no different types of legs, inability to paint certain areas and emissions etc etc it's all still present.If laser swords powered by femto can emit blue blade, there is no reason why I can't paint my mech's visor blue as well. Pilot customization kinda sorta patches it, but not really.BUT.In terms of game's progression, replayabilty and gear acquisition it's a huge improvement over AC formula.Looting parts and weapons from enemies is much better than just buying it from the shop.Giving unique items to farmable bosses is much better than finding them hidden in the missions that you won't be able to replay until you finish the story.Randomly generated dungeon is pure gold. I just wish there were more tilesets and room types for it, but it's the single best game mode in the entire package.Being able to dismount mech and do stuff on foot is fantastic and accentuates vehicle status of the mech, rather than it being playable character.And most importantly movement and combat, the single most important aspect of all and every game, is a straight up improvement over Armored Core. Combining better parts of 4th and 5th generations, while discarding the bad, it's truly a pleasure to control your custom-built mech and blow stuff up.In the end I think this game improves over Armored Core. Dumbed down customization is a fair price to pay for better core gameplay and better gameplay modes.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic Mecha game, plenty of customization to change how you play, and hidden choices to be made throughout the story. I have to say I was actually a little impressed with what they did with the plot, despite it being a little cheesy the entire time. However I feel like the main draw this game has is not in fact the story, but the PVP and PVE; there's only so much repetition you can go through with the main story stuff before you get bored, but Fighting other players and exploring Labyrinths, which are missions aside from the story you can do with other players, are what will keep you playing the game just that extra bit longer.TLDR; Good game, cool mechs and weapons, interesting ways to customize your play style, wacky story that you can fiddle with, and don't be afraid to dip your toes into multiplayer.

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly fun mech game. Basically you set up a mech from different combinations of head/arms/core/legs, weapons and modifications and use it to shoot down all kinds of enemies.If you come from the Armored Core series looking for more like it, like many, it is similar but with simplified customizacion and easier combat. Still very much worth playing through. At least while we wait for FromSoft to get bored of milking souls-like games and pop another Armored Core.As for the main campaign, the story is ridiculous. It’s not that it doesn’t make sense, by the end you get a good idea of what happened and why. It’s the narrative exposed by the ridiculous characters that makes it hard to take seriously. I was laughing at most of the scenes that seemed the most serious because the dialogue is just ridiculous. Approach as if the story was a from a B movie.

_childDocuments_.review: Daemon X Machina is pretty close to what I want from a modern mech fighting game, but I'm mostly hoping for a Daemon X Machina 2 to smooth out some of the rough edges. The story is a mess, the equipment variety is a bit thin, and the maps are basically just backgrounds for you to fly over and rarely if ever touch down on. It feels like they had a great idea for the game, but ran out of budget before they could really make that idea a reality.Don't get me wrong, it's a great game and it's a great stopgap if you're starved for ridiculous anime robot battles (I miss Armored Core so much), so if you're feeling the void this game's probably worth a look.

_childDocuments_.review: Like armoured core? Like high mobility games with customizable builds and play styles?then there is a high possibility you will like this game.if you arent too sure that you will like this game, it would be best to wait for a sale.but its definatley a solid grab if you are a fan of mech fighting games -PROS--boss fights are pretty good. nothing insane but most of of them are visually pleasing and have interesting enough mechanics to keep you engaged-Combat is fantastic, really snappy and responsive, with the option for a lot of mobility. and most of the weapons feel like they have a lot of weight behind them especially the railguns and shoulder mounted lasers.-graphics are nice with the small exception of most of the character faces as they are quite rigid and animationless and can have some wonky lighting but luckily these moments where you have to look at character faces arent too frequent because a lot of the dialogue occurs within this "chat" where only still images of their faces appear whilst they say their piece. but most of the weapon effects like lasers and explosions are top notch (although bullet type weapons are quite bland) and mechs look fantastic each with cool aesthetics for your preference.-Art direction is good too, which ties in well with the last point. lots of the weapons and mech designs mesh well, and manage to make most things pop out quite well with nice use of colour which is an interesting approach compared to armoured core where everything looks kinda gray or brown.-UI design is fully customizable to your preferences, all the menus look well polished with the hanger menu being a fantastic example of this.- Voice acting is suprisingly above average. although the dialogue writing definately isnt (generic anime stuff. nothing too egregious). But none of their vocal performances are noticeably bad despite the kinda cringey things they tended to say (looking at you Diablo) which i let slide.- CONS -- I feel as though the base game is a bit short, which can be a real deal breaker for the people who want value for money. only took me about 12 or so hours for the main campaign (although i am fairly experienced with games like this). I would have also enjoyed more difficulty options and some more arcade like modes to improve replayabilty outside of the exploration co-op missions.-if you liked the faction features and choices like in armoured core for answer. well your not gonna find it here. there is basically only 1 moment where you can make "a choice" but its an illusion of choice thing. no alternative endings or character side quests or anything of that sort. which is a real shame since they introduce different factions that are supposed to have different goals and ideas but none of them lead to anything, with no real choices regarding the politics of said factions.-Weapon variety is unfortunately quite low, especially when comparing it to the armoured core games. i took it that weapon variety was reduced in favour of making the game more accessible, but its very noticeable when looking at the shoulder mounted weapons with only really two viable weapon types that you would want to use (shoulder mounted laser cannons and missiles), since the others tend to be underwhelming in comparison. you get your typical weapons like cannons, shotguns, sniper rifles, machine guns, swords and lasers and only a few special type weapons like a couple arc guns, a flamethrower and an acid gun (just a green cannon explosion basically) which are all pretty underwhelming other than the arc gun which can stun things like arsenals for a fairly long time.- ability variety is also similarly massively lacking. you get various attack modes which increase things like mobility, defense and attack. but ultimately your best option is just to stick to attack mode when playing PvE. your "ultimate" ability is called mirage which is alright.... I guess. no variation or choice in that matter and its just kinda bland, would have been nice if there were more options based on mech hull or some other manner of upgrade allowing for more specialization in what your mech was capable of. - story-wise this game is weak (it was expected though). its gonna have your typical anime-esque cliche stereotypes with the character depth of a puddle. its enough to keep me interested but i would have much rather had a smaller cast with greater exploration of their character rather than dumping 15 people on you one mission after another, with little to explain their goals other than vague "i want to get stronger" crap. Essentially none of the characters feel like people, they are all pretty one dimensional with little to offer in terms of world view and perspective on the events in the story, but is instead as predictable as you would expect which is a shame because i couldnt actually bring myself to care about anything that happens to any of these characters. at one point *SPOILERS* a character dies near the end (sargent something or other) and edge lord diablo is real sad and for a minute i literally went "who dis ♥♥♥♥♥" and even looking back at it i actually cant recall at any point where they imply any relation between diablo and this girl yet he is crying his eyes out.-the outer "mode" where one can leave their is all in all a fairly bewildering addition to me. I like the character customization and all (waifu creators amirite?) but all in all i think it was kinda a waste of development time. its used once throughout the main story and you just get straight back into one in that mission anyway. so any ability used on your outers performances is almost like a wasted stat point. but i do like that you can watch as your character slowly gets mechanical limbs and features as they enhance their body to their limits. in the end i think they just wanted something to hook players but ended up being a fairly shallow feature. I am glad they tried something different and it didnt negatively affect gameplay in anyway by forcing this on you. but it just didnt really work.-Soundtrack. is generally average. but way way too short. the amount of times you will listen to a particular song over and over will make you want to rip your ears out. its a shame because their are a few fantastic tracks like the one in the opening sequence, but it is muddled in with generic rock/metal song one after another and gets really repetitive. additionally the game doesnt know how to use the soundtrack and when not to use it. when a similar metal over-the-top song is playing when i am in the hangar deciding what hair colour i want is also playing when i am fighting the final boss, you know something is wrong. just chuck in some quieter tracks and some ambient background music for the hangar area and lesser fights would have done a world of good. in general more variety in the soundtrack was definately needed.All in all though. whilst it might sound like i wanted to ♥♥♥♥ on this game. the truth is, i think its a fantastic game, and if you want a mech game like armoured core on PC, this is you best and pretty much only choice.TL;DR  its a cheap evangelion knock off, wHy wHoULd yoU EveN PLAy ThIS GaME

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great fun for the first 15 or so hours - with a diverse set of characters; each with their own roles in the story. The mech control is very arcadey with a simple control scheme of WASD + Space to jump, double tap to fly & CTRL to descend. The mech configuration is slightly complex but not too daunting for casual gamers. Mech configuration is divided into a few components: head, body, left arm, right arm, legs and processor - the last being more of an add on to complement the build. The mech can wield a weapon in each arm (not seen any two-handed weapons) and two more spare weapons on the back (Left/Right Pylons), a shoulder weapon and a backpack/support item. This set of configurations provides a diverse range of builds from purely melee build, to a good mix of short to long range weapons. The story took around 20 hours to complete with a little grinding on side missions. The story is somewhat okay but becomes a slog near the end - as enemy mechs become bullet sponges even with the best weapons available at that point.Game is great fun during the discovery stages until past 70% of the game when it starts getting bogged down by bullet sponges/annoying enemies. It's a great game with simple game mechanics for mecha fans, but I would recommend this game on a sale for those who are patient.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game. Although I pressed "no" to recommend this game, it's still worth checking out if you want to experience a fun mech game for a bit. Just wait till it's got a big discount or something because I feel like there's not enough FUN content to justify buying it at full price.On the positive side:The gameplay is fantastic. It feels great to fly around while shooting things. It feels the way it should feel as a fast-paced anime mech game. The animations are amazing, the mechs look cool, the music is sick, the graphics are beautiful without being too demanding on your GPU and there are a bunch of neat mechanics like the femto boost or the pilot combat.Although I've kept this positive section short, by no means should these positives be overlooked simply because I've condensed it.On the negative side:The story is told pretty poorly. There are so many characters that are introduced and you barely spend time to know them...not that there is much to know since the characters are the biggest anime sterotypes you can think of. It's kinda funny tbh, but doesn't really work when the game tries to introduce emotional plot points involving them. The characters just feel a bit too flat and unrelatable, making it hard to sympathise with them.The plot itself is vague at times whilst also being incredibly blunt at others. You get hints of what's happening in the form of cryptic messages and the dialogue between characters hinting at things that might be happening, only for the plot to suddenly reveal itself and throw you in the middle of a mech battle. Because of this, it's hard to follow along with the plot or get invested in what's happening.In the end, I think most people aren't playing this game for the plot so it's probably not as big of a deal for most people as it is for me.For me the biggest letdown was the missions themselves. Eventually all the missions started feeling the same. It feels like you're just flying around killing the same enemies in the same way and doing the same thing over and over again (with the exception of the boss missions). I can think of one instance where this was really not the case where the level was designed like a really long tunnel and you're simply running through it as fast as possible while shooting things along the way. That was really fun.I think this monotony is caused by a couple things:The game is easy. You just need to fly around and keep shooting enemies to win. There are cool mechanics and movements you can do with your mech, but I never felt the need to try hard to use them, which is a shame.As mentioned in other reviews, the customization of your mech doesn't really affect how you play. They affect stats like attack, defence and speed, but it doesn't feel like you can build for particular playstyles like you should. This might also be a consequence of the weapon variety in the game. Although there are a decent number of weapons, most of them function very similarly to each other. Maybe this is also a result of the game being a bit easy.One of the main motivations for me playing this game was to unlock more customizations for my mech, but this motivations started dying down as I kept finding (and making) new mech parts which didn't really change anything for me.

_childDocuments_.review: How can I describe this game? I cant quite say lacking, as the other mech games have spoiled me with flashy cool weapons, not that i am saying this game does not have that mind you, but at the same time the customisation is more akin to RPG weapon progression, meaning that instead of super powerful new weapons its more akin to weapons and armor that have slightly better stats. You dont really feel like you get stronger persay, however you do become stronger through your skill. The gameplay is great, fast, and fun. However the main story + all side quests are completed in around 11 hours for me. There is an amount of postgame, but i feel as if i've seen what the game has to offer me. I dont like PVP so I never touched that, so in the end I can reccomend this game trepidaciously. Just, if you are not a completionist or PVP enjoyer, understand your gameplay will end in around 11 hours, maybe a a few more depending on how much you come back for a mission or two.

_childDocuments_.review: At some point the Earth suffered a cataclysm that wiped out most of the planet’s lifeforms and reshaped the land while at the same time a new resource appeared, Femto but also a new enemy, the Immortals. New blocks emerged as Horizon, Zen and Sky Union, consortiums that manage and exploit the resources of their territories, meanwhile Orbital defends these territories from Immortals using mercenaries.Everything seems normal but things will soon start becoming weirder and tenser between the consortiums, the mercenaries and Orbital, what seemed to be a battle for humanity against an unstoppable enemy will soon become something deeper and much complicated, the war isn’t over yet.Story is entertaining but nothing really original, it works perfectly and that’s more than enough, however, some things are too “anime” and that might make some people doubt if this game is for them, I’m going to be completely honest, I didn’t like some parts and elements from it, however, the final result was satisfactory and that was ok for me, a geopolitical conflict, a conspiracy and a bunch of side-stories that weren't bad at all. In general the story and the characters work fine and while this isn’t the main attraction from the game it is always nice to have at least a decent story. Something that could have been better? The relationship between our character and the rest of mercenaries. Our character is completely flat and there is no real evolution, in fact, the game will make those relationships develop for the sake of the story but it feels completely artificial and non-satisfactory at all. You can partner them in missions and they will always talk to you as a friend or a trustworthy person, however, I don’t feel this has been explored enough to feel good or natural, too bad because it could have been a great part of the game thanks to the number of clans and characters that are present in the game generating alliances or conflicts. Let’s now talk to the main reason you might love this game, the gameplay. When people say Daemon x Machina is the closest thing to Armored Core they totally mean it, not only a big part of the stuff of this game was involved in the past on Armored but they also nailed the feeling of movement, speed and combat. Arsenals are fast, really fast, the sooner you understand and get used to this, the better because it will be essential for the best fights, everything will become a rain of missiles, bullets and light trails, once you upgrade your character things like the “blink” will make battles even more dynamic, no matter what kind of enemy are you facing (Arsenal, Colossal immortal or normal enemies) you will have a great battle. Arsenals are also very customizable not only in terms of equipment (which again, I recommend to get used to this system if you want to survive some missions) but also in terms of decals, patterns and colors, you can do really cool things if you know how to. Weapons and Armor can also be upgraded individually with perks and modifiers, while I haven’t used this that much it really helps to balance things and if there’s a piece that is perfect for your necessities and it has available slots for upgrades, then do it because it will make your gear even better. Visually the game is very pleasant, it uses cell-shading so it won’t look as dated as a more realistic game as this is more cartoony, with this PC port the AA helps a lot making things smoother even at higher resolutions and while options are limited it’s more than enough for me in this case. In terms of variety it’s well served, I thought the game would be limited in terms of areas but to my surprise it’s actually varied and with a good bunch of biomes, of course there is a limited number of zones but I think you will be pleased with the number of options, from desserts to dense forests. PC port has been handled by Xseed and they did an amazing job, the game runs perfectly and it’s not very demanding, I’m very happy with this port to be honest.And I think that’s it, in conclusion, I liked this game a lot, it’s fast, it’s fun, it is a very great mech game and it’s the closest thing we have to Armored Core on PC and in general so, if you don’t mind certain things then this game might be your cup of tea. I totally encourage you to buy it, hope you all enjoy it. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD SO FAR:Its armored core returned to us after being gone for so long. If you enjoy mech games where you can build and cutomize your mech a ton, this will meet that itch. So far, it lacks quad legs, treads, and other types of mechs which I find unfortunate. I suggest buying this as these guys have the right idea, they just need to grow as a company and to do that they need sales and money. So support em! I'll add more as I go through the game in the time I have and what I think about it. I like the co-op elements its cool as well. Haven't tried PVP cause I'm still in a junker.THE BAD:The graphics - hate to complain, they look okay, but it clearly was made for the switch. _childDocuments_.review: By reputation, this seems to be the closest to Armored Core 2 available on Windows right now. I don't know the other games in the franchise, but AC2 was awesome and I'd like to play something like it again. And I want to like this game, but can't on account of it being just tedious.Combat feels clunky, at least with the basic Mech you get at the start, which is where I am now, and where I'm leaving this game. It's just no fun to fight against the UI instead of the AI. While the movement of everything around you is fluid, it feels like the player is covered in molasses. This is bound to improve over time, of course, but…This game is as grindy as any I've played. The game has a mission-based system with pilot ranks and non-campaign missions that are unlocked by campaign progress. As is often the case, your equipment is limited by your progress. So far, so normal, but I don't even see any light at the end of the tunnel. The game gives you a shop that is empty, a factory where you cannot build anything, An attachment system but only rare slots. It doesn't feel like you can actually make any meaningful decision.And finally the characters and dialogue: annoying beyond belief. After the first few dialogue scenes, I started skipping dialogue in part or in full because I just cannot bear the dumb lines getting dropped there regularly. Some are probably just badly translated from Japanese, and some of it is just stupid bluster. That was funny when I was 10, but not anymore.And just as a bonus, you can give the pilot cyber legs to make the mech run faster… 🙄

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute cringe of a game. I like mech games, but this one plays so poorly and is so overloaded with cringe anime dialogue and characters, that playing it feels like a chore. There is also a lot of screen clutter, both due to camera being too close to our mech and maddeningly packed interface.All missions feel the same and areas lack any detail. Its all just a bunch of repetitive and poorly paced missions. They are either extremely short or consist of fighting a bullet sponge boss.Among all this I found sound to be the worst offender. The infantile anime dialogue with both Japanese or English voices made me cringe constantly. Music as well feels extremely generic and doesn't match the tone of the game. Already during character creation I was flooded with over the top epic theme that made me want to vomit. At some point I just muted all the voices and started skipping all dialogue.
