_childDocuments_.review: Suddenly, an Armored Core VI game out of nowhere, full of fun online missions.Instead of dropping a detailed review (I only got 1.2 hours in at the moment) I want to point out the greatness that is having a new drop-in / drop-out co-op game in 2020. You can do two things: Explore a facility together with 3 players or fight bosses. Both of these has a number of different, varied missions. The game doesn't seem to have a huge meta so I don't know how long you can play before it gets boring, but just the fact that you can play a typical Armored Core experience together with others in a no-strings-attached online environment makes it a fun time. There's 1v1 or 2v2 PvP as well, but I haven't tried this yet. You can also create your character (males get facial hair features, unlike in Code Vein, a nitpick but still) and customize the look of your mech. All the while, you'll listen to casual metal and rock music which is just very wholesome.

_childDocuments_.review: Written after the completion of the campaign missions, with a fair few multiplayer sessions.To call this a successor to or superior to the Armored Core franchise is an insult to Armored Core. I will try to be concise:The lack of agency you have through nearly the entirety of the story, the inability to choose which corporation/consortium to work for and thus any alternative perspectives on any of the missions, the for the most part linear progression of the parts and weapons and lack of brand or manufacturer specialties, all homogeneous. A mech will ship of Theseus very often like a gear set in a looter shooter or an ARPG.The character writing for all present is standard gundam show writing, which is to say colourful cardboard, anything worthy of note or resembling development occurs at the penultimate hour of the campaign and only then. Overall, Johnny G is a bro, and everyone else you wish you could forget more than just the names of. And get used to pilots you've defeated numerous times to constantly talk smack to you. Oh and you are Rookie The All-Powerful, get used to hearing that.With regards to gameplay, Daemon X Machina succeeds in how smooth and clean movement feels, on the ground and for the most part the air. Fighting machines your size is your own size is enjoyable when their HP is not boosted to astronomic levels so they can get their dialogue out. In the PvP scene however, fighting players (outside the strings of speed-sniper builds) is incredible.An area the games shines a faulty spotlight on, is the online co-op missions, mecha Monster Hunter is an apt description of how its is, though several bosses both in the online PvE and the campaign feel like the ability to constantly be in flight was not originally an intended feature, looking down upon you, Dreadnaught.To conclude, this is not an Armored Core successor, it superficially pretends to be with the rival corporations, mercenary ego battles, and the english lady AI voice, but those are purely superficial. Don't come in with the expectation that this is at all trying to be Armored Core. All that said, the game can stand on its own, and the online co-op should be played, bring your friends. But don't tell them this is Armored Core.

Plus when you get to the end it feels like all the weapons you have been using are exactly the same as the ones you upgrade them from. For example you have the laser rifles. _childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, I cannot really recommend Daemon X Machina.In summary, it's incredibly repetitive with lackluster and unsubstantial customization and progression, with very poor pacing as the cherry on top.Having picked it up in the wave of Armored Core 6 hype, I found myself interested in DxM due to its coat of paint and similarities as a temporary measure until the real deal came out. Part of me was hoping to find good iteration on the sub-genre of games AC comprised. With initial good impressions and an optimistic heart, I was having fun for about 5 hours until I began to feel myself dragging my feet through the rest of the game for my 30 hour runtime. DxM grips you by introducing you to a variety of weapons, and giving you a good handful of parts very quickly. However, past that, it started to dawn that the weapon and armor variety capped out and begins to become stagnant past the point of getting access to laser weapons after the 20% mark of the game. Newer styles of weapons that were *good* were even more scarce beyond that.The majority of the game had myself running 2 assault rifles, a laser, and a sniper rifle due to their effectiveness and relative ease of use. There ended up being nothing new that was more intriguing, powerful, or even *existent*. Barring overtuned missions where a melee weapon seemed necessarily because you aren't supplied any additional ammo, it was hold down my shootbuttons until the enemies died. It was also scathing because any potential upgrades to these weapon genres were either non-existent, or somehow obsolete due to less ammo or fire rate. Any enthusiasm I had for new weapons ended up being quelled because I never ended up pleasantly surprised by a substantial or varietal upgrade past the first quarter of the game.Furthermore, armor parts lacked any semblance of feeling meaningful. There aren't pieces in this game that make you feel like you're playing any differently. You end up just being Gun Shootman unless you want to use admittedly clunky, spammy and sluggish melee weapons, all of which put you at decent risk barring a mace that stunlocks enemies to death. Stat differences in this game aren't brutal enough to really focus on anything like fuel efficiency, armor, speed, etc., unlike older AC games. It's very sterilized and you can end up getting through the game by just picking what looks cool. I ended up being a glass cannon with high speed that evened up trivializing the game ever further. For a game focused on acquisition of parts, it ls barren of any of the fun in customizing your mech to fit certain situations barring the aforementioned back-up melee.The AI in this game also pose no challenge barring post-game missions and very specific story missions. For the latter, my neck broke at the sheer whiplash of dealing with the mecha equivalent of a lobotomized sloth to fighting 3 Newtype pilots on Heisenberg signature meth. That is to say, the game is still 95% trivial.Lastly, the plot deserves an honorable mention. People criticize it for being too anime-like, and they wouldn't be wrong. Though, I don't point to the cheesy dialogue, the edgy names, or the all-star cast for any of the issues. That's standard fare and a flavor thing. It's more that the pacing is so tremendously poor, you'd feel like you're going to vomit at the sudden g-force  when it finally drops high-fear, interesting plot points. To explain, the game has 5 chapters in the form of "Ranks" for your character from E to A. Rank C is the bulk of the game and is twice as long as the rest, with you doing various "kill goons" and "fight other brainless pilots" for about 20~ missions with the same exact exposition each time without any interesting plot development for up to stretches of 5 missions each. You will feel like you're dragging yourself through quicksand until the last handful of missions in the final act of the game give you whiplash, to which I will accredit with being decently captivating, though not enough to say the overall story is salvageable.Overall, DxM is a game that lives in the shadow of Armored Core, following in its footsteps. It fails to surpass, let alone match, the charm and intrigue of the AC games. I would only recommend giving it a try under a very heavy sale if you wanted a few hours to kill, but with the advent of Fires of Rubicon, I would be hesitant to say this game's worth your time at all even if FromSoft's new installment doesn't outright eclipse it further.UPDATE 8/28: lmao yeah it's not even closeGet AC6 if you're gonna be spending close to the amount of money on this game at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of the surprise releases of 2020 for me. A Switch port that runs incredibly well even on lower configurations, with all the bells and whistles, it even supports 4k for that screenshot mania/Fashion Mecha at the highest settings. So, what does DxM bring to the table? It offers some good mecha action from some of the developers of Armored Core. In lack of a proper Armored Core title developed by From Software, we take what we can, especially on PC where this genre is extremely underrepresented compared to the console front.The meat of the game is in the extremely customizable mechs (called Arsenals here) that look extremely cool and can move incredibly fast with the right configurations. The collection of weapons and parts for your big robot is also a key part of the whole experience as you plow through the multitude of story and free missions, as well as online missions that can be played in co-op. (My only gripe in that aspect is the inability to change the color of the light from the arsenals, which is stuck at orange, same for weapon colors.)Sadly, the online component will definitely require to coordinate with your friendlist since it's not very active at all nowadays but if you can get another 3 people or just another pal to play, the co-op missions are definitely a huge step up in challenge, especially after the addition of the new Eclipse boss. (Zeruchroar proved to be fairly difficult even though we were a full team and the Omega variations of the bosses can also get very challenging.)The story has a few twists but the writing and character portrayal is not very good, especially in the way your character feels tacked on. It makes the same mistake as Xenoblade X and the MC there. Don't dive too deep, the concept was cool but sadly the execution left a lot to be desired.Obviosly, we're not here for the story but for the robot battles and I do believe delivers them in spades. For those fans of the genre, it's a worthy pick up and for those unconvinced I would suggest waiting for a bigger sale. The DLC is all cosmetic so you don't have to worry about missing anything.I truly hope we can get a much more improved and even better sequel that also comes to PC day one!P.S.: Curse to all hell whoever devised the destruction achievements and decided to put such small AI enemy amounts in almost all missions so to make it just as bad as the "play x amount of hours" 'challenges'. The grind is real. If I didn't love mechs so bloody much I would not recommend it solely based on that.

_childDocuments_.review: For every thing this game does right, it does something questionably, and for every thing that it does poorly, it does something VERY poorly.I understand that it's an anime story, which comes with an inherent level of unlikable characters, and writing that is cliche at the best of times (one of the main villains literally said "I have no friends, no one understands me") but the insistence upon including the player in the story while not actually allowing the player to speak *at all* is agonizing. It's like being in a room with a bunch of people you know who are having an important conversation which doesn't involve you. Often I'd write off narrative and dialogue like this as dismissible, but it really tries to cram the story in your face at every turn, constantly interrupting the mission so characters can speak when they should absolutely not be speaking. It heavily impedes upon the gameplay.The gameplay itself is pretty good, but always just feels slightly off. It's the same feeling as playing a beta where a lot of things are implemented, not fully fleshed out, the UI is awkward and/or bad, and the balancing is completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥. You wanna know exactly how ♥♥♥♥♥♥? Most of the arsenal of your... "arsenal" consists of ranged weapons, even going so far as to let you equip an arm which is a ranged weapon. A lot of these are redundant or outright bad, but a few are absolute standouts if you build for them. The final boss does not drop ammo. When you run out of ammo, there is no way to get it back. All you can do is resort to melee on a boss that damages you when you get close, and that's only IF you decided to take a melee weapon with you, and only IF the limb holding your melee weapon hasn't been broken. That final boss being so hopelessly unwinnable is where i threw in the towel.It feels so much like a game which is about 75% done, with a story that should have never been assembled. The game would have been overtly better if there was no story at all and all the development resources were put into the gameplay. You can customize the visuals of your character with a decent degree of freedom, but bodyparts get replaced with stat upgrades, so enjoy turning yourself into a refrigerator if you want the best stats. Meanwhile the visual customization of your mecha is absolutely minimal. Not everything has to be MASS Builder levels of customizable, but this is just phoned-in.Even if you can muscle through the horrific writing, and even if you can appreciate the gameplay for what it is, warts and all, you'll have the rug pulled out from under you by a potentially unwinnable boss fight at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10PROS:Daemon X Machina is the shining example of Mech gameplay that other games should strive to match.  Awesome customization, massive slew of weapons, and an unmatched style of combat that somehow manages to effortlessly blend the weight of colossal weapons with the fluidity of free-flight.  While pilot customization leaves a bit to be desired, the fact that cybernetic upgrades drastically change the appearance of your character is an awesome touch I’d love to see in more sci-fi games.  It introduces an awesome system of player choice: how much of your humanity will you sacrifice for power?I positively love how alive and lifelike each character’s vocal performance is.  Despite each one of them only being represented by still images, the voice actors handled them with such professionalism that there’s more than enough to work with to feel immersed in the world.  The allies who side with you are loveable, and those that stand against you are absolute scum, and by the time you finish the story I promise you’ll have a list of mercs that fill you with joy to see, as well as fill you with dread.  You might even end up liking some characters that you hated in the beginning and vice versa.Last thing I want to note is how well the writing is.  Sad when it needs to be, funny and light hearted otherwise, and with no shortage of bad ass mad-max one liners.  CONS:My biggest issue with the game is player interaction within the story.  Despite the first impression of your choices having some semblance of impact, and hints of the game featuring an interactive non-linear story, player interaction is actually almost totally a non-factor.  With only 2 diverging dialogue options, and only 2 instance of being able to chose whether or not you fight an enemy through the ENTIRE game.  The story as a whole is extremely linear, and I found myself in several situations where ‘out of character’ choices where forced upon me.  Without the illusion of choice to supplement these scenes the story of the game, and the game as a whole suffers a hit to quality.My only other gripe with the game is the conflicting playstyles of researching new equipment versus scavenging it.  The game both encourages you to salvage your equipment from the battlefield and punishes you for doing so.  While simultaneously encouraging you to research equipment options, and punishing you for doing so.  It seems the developers couldn’t decide how they wanted the player to progress in power, so they went with both options, and as a result neither of them are as good as they could be... SUMMARY:+Great customization+Unique player customization+Great characters+Atmospheric world+Killer soundtrack!-No player agency-Weak crafting systemStory and Progression issues aside, this is still one of the best mech games on the market. If you’re a fan of big robots with big guns taking on bigger robots with bigger guns, then this game is a MUST HAVE.  Oh yeah! And the music also slaps! Death Metal was a great choice!

_childDocuments_.review: I come back to this game after playing games like armored core 6 and gundam games because I love the combat. its fast, its flexible, I love the ability to leave the mech and run around and repair it. I love the idea that the upgrade system doesn't just stop at putting different equipment on the mech but you can upgrade yourself and as you do so you are replacing parts of your body which I think is something that goes over a lot of players heads when they talk about how the story is told. I'm less happy that the player character doesn't talk or at least I would have preferred that they had a bit more expression when they interacted with the game characters which would better exhibit the distance you put between yourself and humanity the further your character progresses in the game but this concept is a little mute because you can always reset your upgrades for a price meaning you can change the way your character looks and interacts with your missions to play the game the way you want to play it but I do see this taking something from the game where it could push the player to committing to their decisions which would have made for a better story over all. Another thing I found very strange to the game was the ice cream shop which felt a bit forced to add a temporary perk the player could add to their character before a mission. You can run around the hanger and see weapons that you have collected while out in the field but the hanger does feel small and could have extended into allowing the player to roam the rest of the facility which would have been appreciated (kinda like godeater or code vain I suppose). Aside from those issues, there is fun boss battles that feel fun and challenging, being able to pick up weapons from downed enemies and toss your expended ones to be used as improvised weapons themselves is a great feature. the game also boasts a procedurally generated dungeon system which extends the post game completion enjoyment factor by a lot in my opinion. I wish there were more games like this as there are a lot of slow mech games but very few ones that make you feel like a fighter pilot moving at break neck speeds while dodging a multitude of missiles and lasers. some missions have different win conditions that offer different post mission outcomes which is a nice touch.

_childDocuments_.review: I know this goes against the grain here with a negative review but I just don't see how this game is as well-received as it is. It's just a mediocre Armored Core game who's only redeeming quality is that its far more accessible with it being on PC. It's at best a $20 game.The combat in this game has a lot of mechanics and ideas put into it but it fails miserably to do anything interesting with them. The mech AI is pretty basic which really leaves a lot to be desired when you'll be fighting them the majority of the time. And then you have the large robot "bosses" called Immortals which are really cool at first glance but feel basic when actually facing them in-game. And just to add insult to injury there's only like 5 of them in total.  You're also given the option to move around on foot to set traps or repair your mech. It sounds neat on paper but its pretty much never useful except for 1 required story mission and 1 optional. It's really just a "you screwed up" mechanic when you somehow lose your mech. Not a big deal but the game dedicates quite a bit of the upgrade tree to improving your out-of-mech pilot abilities with cool ideas like double jumps, flight, etc which sounds like the developers implying you'll actually use any of it when you won't. It really feels like the actual game content is at like 60% of what it should be.Undeniably the worst aspect of this game is the story, writing, voice acting and associated animations. The developers were trying to go for a serious meta-discussion about "the nature of humanity and what lies in store for us as a destructive species in the perhaps not-so-near-future". This sort of pseudo-philosophical nonsense isn't really new to the mecha genre of any entertainment medium. But it's all just a jumbled mess here. The writing is straight up terrible and I'm not convinced that it's because of the translation. More plausible its just the developers thinking themselves way better at this than they actually are. They were certainly serious enough to hire a number of well-known voice actors to voice the 20ish characters in this game which is really surprising and a little bit impressive. It's just a shame that it's wasted on this particular game. And if you do decide to watch the cutscenes you'll be treated to some of the lamest attempts at dramatic "animations" I've seen in recent times. And no, you can't skip everything. You can skip a lot but there's plenty that you can't.Visually, the game does a good job with the mechs and certain other set pieces but otherwise it's pretty bland. Especially in the environment textures and stylizing during missions. It wouldn't have taken much effort to come up with some visually interesting locations. The game even takes a singular step in this direction with a cool location of white snow, rich red crystals scattered all over with a black sun hovering above. It's aesthetically simple yet striking. But they do this only once and then its back to the boring orange desert for the other 95% of the game. The basic map geometry and low texture resolutions can at least be explained away since this is a port. Some comparatively minor complaints compared to the above: the game tutorial is substandard, the music is forgettable with the exception of the Hanger theme and the character customization is merely passable (with the exception of the plugsuits which suck).

_childDocuments_.review: Personally originally i concluded that this game was terrible a long while ago but to be honest that perception was based on the switch version of this game. The game on the switch is a laggy slow mess.So let me be clear, the PC version of this game is the best version of this game. Fast frame rates, relatively decent visuals (everything kinda has this clay look to it but i guess i can dig it), and fast paced mecha action is all that i really need to rate a mecha title 10/10. If you like Armored Core then consider this game Armored Core Lite as its pretty similar to AC4A but toned down immensely. If your looking for high speed mecha action this is the game for you.So now im gonna put down some of my grips with the game. The AI is dumb as hell, and I don't mean ally AI i mean all the AI. The enemy half the time don't know what their doing and neither do your friends. Arsenal VS Arsenal battles are pretty fun but honestly the AI act so predictable you can just load up on firepower on every mission and just blow people away. Don't worry about ammo as the game practically hand it out to you, makes me wish ammo cost was a thing to use up some of those credits i don't spend. The Store is virtually useless, it never gets updated with stuff unless you build stuff from the factory which means im pretty much not spending my credits anywhere but at the factory to upgrade gear to what i think is best. It really blows to not have anything to spend credits on besides the outer upgrade system which ive not really touched because as much as i want to be a robot my name isn't setsuna f. seiei. The Ice Cream shop seems terribly useless, the buffs are kinda meh and don't really help you due to how low they are, do eat ice cream tho for the titles and such tho. The story is alright, I don't have any real gripes with it since for the most part its kinda taking the route armored core did where the story is mostly background info.The game gets that mecha customization itch out really nicely, not as nice as armored core in general but close enough. There is real variance in the far ends of what you spec into but if your like me then you might end up with max firepower, low ammo, average everything else.If there is anything that this game proves its that there is a demand for mecha games on the market that just isn't being satisfied.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing.  Closest thing to Armored Core we've had in a long time.  Singleplayer is a little underwhelming and easy, but the co-op content is really solid.  Bosses are super fun and the "dungeons" of the game, while being quite repetitive, can still be a lot of fun with a group of people.  Easily went from 15 hours gameplay for the story and optional missions, and now nearing 100+ since moving on to the endgame stuff.  Relatively deep customisation too, nowhere near the level of AC, but again, it's damn close.  Loads of weapons and armour pieces to choose between, and no parts really stand out as the best, allowing for some pretty interesting build options.  Honestly, probably not worth full price, but if it's on sale, pick this up.  It's a hell of a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: As a quick summary : I would say this is a game that you play for Gameplay not really for its story content.If you are a fan of Armored 4 : For Answer, this the title than comes closer in term of the speed of the gameplay in a Mechs Action game. And this is the main rand outmost eason why I liked this game.Compare to that game, this one gives a bit less importance to Armor Part and tunning in general but it adds some strategical mechanics :+ More important one is the Femto mechanic which allows you switch between 3 differents modes for Defense, Speed or Damage. And also a Femto to increase your overboost speed.+ A skill tree to unlock some unique ability for your AC, like double dashing, comboing in Melee+ Mechs Pilot Gameplay (called Outer) with its own skill tree : you can get out of your AC and repair it, set up traps, attacks.+ New different Melee weapons like Mace. The Shield gameplay is also a nice addition.+ Grabing object and throwing it mechanic+ Coop Boss Battles (they can be fun)+ Some interesting new weapon type like charging laser beams+ Lots of destructable buildings and objetcs in the map which is always fun in thos games.- Graphics are mediocres or okay at best.- There is less Mech Parts options, no 4 legs, or Tank type Mechs. Only parts left are all designed for speedy aerial fight- Gameplay wiise, there is no more the booster just frame mechanic (AC4FA) that enhance your boost speed with precise timing release.- Coop missions are mostly boring labyrinths that you farm to have a chance of droping rare items.- Color, pattern and decals customization could have been more deeper, and it's limited, Same for character customization.- Over-Complicated and not really engaging storyline, lacks of explanation and the quality of the ingame cinematics are kinda low.I still find this a good game for a fan of AC4FA like me, because the feeling of a fast pathed mech battles is here and with new mechanics and weapons.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. Here we go. Let's start with the CONS and then move over to the PROS.CONS:1. Story - Story is trash. I mean its hot garbage under the afternoon summer sun.Every character you meet is both unlikable and dull. They treat you like some nobody even though you are doing all the heavy work. I couldn't remember the amount of times I wished I could just put a bullet on each of their skulls and do things my way in the campaign. But you couldn't. Sadly. 2. Progression - Progression in the story is quite slow in the beginning. Progression here isnt like Armored Core were you gain access to more parts and weapons as you go further in the main campaign. In this game, you gotta loot fallen enemy Arsenals to claim new parts. So if you failed to loot that enemy arsenal before the End Quest timer is done, GG!New parts can be researched also in the Factory. The cost would be a base item and some currency.3. The Secret Factory: You need to unlock this to get the best upgrades. But why did I add this to my CONS list? Well, to unlock it, you need to buy a total of 20 ice creams from the Ice Cream shop. How in the blue veiny balls of Poseidon is anyone supposed to know this!? Yeah sure its a secret and all, but the secret factory is extremely useful in crafting powerful gear to defeat tough immortals in online coop missions. And to unlock it you have to eat Ice Cream? SMH.4. Outer mode: This is straight out WTF. Outer mode is when your pilot gets out of his/her fallen Arsenal as a last stand to kill the enemy Arsenals. Its a last ditch effort. But its completely useless since enemy AI and Arsenals can easily gun you down during this mode. They should have just scrapped this one out.PROS:1. Controls - The controls in this game is near perfect. it isnt clunky and the hotkeys fit well as to were they are positioned on the keyboard by default.2. Gameplay: The fast action gameplay totally brings back the memories and joy to those who loved the AC series. Fast paced air combat and dashing and blitzing to avoid enemy fire is such virtual cocaine. With proper customization and speccing your Arsenal to how you play really makes you enjoy each mission no matter how "grindy" it can be. 3. Music: From Heavy riffs ripped straight out of a Fear Factory album to funk metal rap rock, the music and tone fits well to the game's atmosphere and vision. Although, it would be better if they could atleast add some variation to the HUB music. it can get a bit tiring to listen to for the 800th time.4. Character development: Story wise, there isnt any character growth. However, in terms of augmenting your character, you can go full out cyberpunk. Want your character to jump twice? Put augments were he has cybernetic feet. Wanna have him increase melee power? Have his arms gain cybernetic implants. Its pretty cool.5. Its a cross between Monster Hunter and Armored Core lite: Kill big giant enemies called Immortals and get blueprints to get better stuff such as blueprints. and augments.6. Online solo/ coop PVP and a PVP ranking system:If you wanna test your skill and dominate the ladder this game has it. Switch on your Sigma Grindset if you wish to reach it at the top.  And that is all. I wont recommend this game at full price due to the story. Get it on sale.

This game also has location based damage, so if you take too much damage to one part it will be crippled (arms become unusable, movement is slower if it legs, I can't remember what happens if your head or core is crippled). _childDocuments_.review: Underwhelming, but also somewhat enjoyable, this mecha game is just a mecha game. That is to say it has mechas, the combat is about mechas, and it has the bare minimum of what you'd expect out of a modern mecha game.The game feels like it was made using some spreadsheet for anime games. You are the voiceless third wheel in the mediocre stories of other people, just there to kill stuff and listen to exposition. You for some reason operate a mecha, not like you need a reason to do that, and just go through pointless missions in hopes to get to the end of the game eventually.What that amounts to is a "hub" where nothing is going on, nothing that you can actually feel like you really interact with anyway, you chose a mission, you get to the mission, you are done in like 5 minutes and oh woop back to the hub. Literally every online game ever, but what makes it even worse is that the areas in which the fights take place are laughably small. You are driving an enjoyably fast car in a parking lot, essentially.When the core of the game is so boring, the combat can only carry it so far before the obvious flaws pile up enough to drive you away. Thing is, the combat is alright. Just alright. There's nothing that stands out other than the lack of similar games so it gets a pass for not being horrible. With that said, the sense of speed cannot be denied, it is there, but it's just unfortunate that it cannot be savoured due to the borderline claustrophobic map size and often not thought out terrain that even the AI can't traverse.There's a fair selection of weapons to chose from but most of them either feel the same or are not as useful as others in terms of numbers, and some weapons straight up do worse than others of similar quality, leaving you no reason to use them. There is quantity, but there's no balanced quality. On top of that, most kinds of weapons are rather uneventful compared to just swinging your sword around mindlessly.Passable combat, lack of freedom in missions and the objectively worthless story. Almost a disaster. Thankfully, there are a few things that provide a reason to not call this a bad or bellow average game.Customization for your mecha, and your operator, follows the quantity without the balanced quality formula, but at least when it comes to appearances that is not a deal-breaker. If anything, it is a plus. Most importantly. there's a rather unique operator skill tree system that actually changes the apperance of your operator, giving quite a nice representation of progress not just shown on the robot you are piloting but on you as well.This whole skill tree and customization nonsense is one of the few well executed ideas in this game, focusing on the one operating the mecha, giving a nice touch of personalization to the experience. Despite having access to a death machine, the actual operator is not to be ignored, as you'd be forced to fight without it should it get destroyed, and you are quite powerful even on foot, be it just a second-wind situation. The emphasis on the one driving instead of the vehicle itself might very well be the saving grace that makes the game bearable and relatively fun from time to time.Finally, music is good, though repeatitive. There's no attempt to stretch the music out, so your ears will get tired of it fast... That's about it.Even with these few things done relatively well, it remains average, so I can't exactly recommend it unless you really just want your oversized roomba battles, but I also cannot simply dismiss it since it's not offensively mediocre or something along those lines. It is a game that can be enjoyed, but it's not a game that will be enjoyed.

_childDocuments_.review: Bitter sweet. If I could give a middle voting, I'd give it just that. This game is ultimately everything I've wanted in a mech game lately. Massive amounts of customization, MH style grinding towards new things, nice sleek graphics, and butter smooth combat controls.However 17.7 hours in, I have now done all story missions, all online missions, and PvP isn't as popping as it should be. I could continue to go on to try to upgrade my mech even further and unlock all gear; however I don't see the purpose if there isn't anything more challenging to work towards.Digging around the devs twitter and etc, it seems the most of content has already came already as well. Which is ultimately disappointing being that the PC port seemed to boost how people feel about the game overall. Story wise, if you've read at all, is very bland and generic. They are correct, a lot of it had me snoozing and skipping. There isn't a whole lot to the level designs either, not that it really matters in a mech game. The games absolutely shines with the giant boss fights, however there is only a total of I think 6? Really the most you'll be doing is going against over mechs. Which by itself is pretty boring and is really a bullet sponge simulator. I don't regret buying this game, I want to show the devs that I love it and want to support any possible future development for the game. However with this little amount of content, it's safe to say the buzz will die out before we get any further. Hope to see something soon, but for now, unless you REALLY want an anime armored core that's insanely fun but falls short, I'd go ahead and skip over this one.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is quite good, but the story is a resounding meh. One thing I see a lot of people do is compare this game to the Armoured Core games. Now, I never played Armoured Core so I can only take them at their word for whether or not that is a fair comparison. What I can say is that this isn't Armoured Core. It never claimed to be Armoured Core. So judging it by saying "It's not Armoured Core" is a disservice to the game.I will say, while most of the missions are fairly well balanced, and are quite easy if you have the right gear, there are some missions that are downright impossible without the right gear. And there are some missions, specifically near the end, where it is just downright unfair and un-enjoyable. For reference, I want you to imagine the strongest weapon you can take. It has limited ammo, is somewhat difficult to use effectively, and you can only have one of it. Now go fight an enemy that has six of those as its default weapon, with unlimited ammo.I honestly don't feel right saying I recommend this game, but at the same time would feel wrong saying I don't. I mostly just want to put my experience out there for others to see, maybe even for the devs to see. The game is pretty good, but would need a lot of work to be called great.

_childDocuments_.review: Plays like previous Armored Core games with a targeting reticle, no lock-on with automatic tracking here, at least not by default. The combat is totally fine if a little janky, feedback to hits is sometimes a tad limited so weapons feel a little weak even if they shred through enemies like butter. There's a large amount of replayability here since it's pretty much impossible to collect all the armor and weapon parts the game has to offer within your first playthrough. Granted, most missions are fairly generic go to X shoot Y amount of enemies. It gets better near the end. This game was not developed by FromSoft after all, who have perfected mecha combat through the Armored Core franchise. This is very much derivative of their work and clearly not as polished as they would make it. However, do not let this discourage you. There is still a lot of fun to be had here with tons of build variety.The story is confusing. A lot of things happen behind the scenes and the pacing can go from zero to one hundred before you've finished processing it all. The characters don't help much in this part if you make the mistake of playing with the English voices. Do yourself a favor and switch to Japanese, enjoy the line delivery as an anime. If you do you may also be pleasantly surprised to see most of the Japanese voice actors have also performed in the Mobile Suit Gundam franchise, including Tōru Furuya and Shūichi Ikeda of Amuro Ray and Char Aznable fame, who even play similar roles within the story. A lot of story beats can trace their roots back to Gundam as well with Newtype-ism themes. after all this game was made in part with Bandai Namco support.Full price this game is sadly not recommendable, and the DLCs on top of that feel a bit egregious. When purchased on sale its value shines more readily, and is easy to recommend to anybody looking for a mecha action rpg.
_childDocuments_.name: DAEMON X MACHINA

_childDocuments_.review: Daemon X Machina is a mixed bag for me. With the lack of mech games on steam i find myself missing armored core so i bought this game. Many mechanics are exactly what i want while others are a pain to deal with. This game has missed the mark in terms of an armored core successor, but nailed much of the fun of playing a mech game. Story is the weakest element of this game. Cut scenes are boring and the story will make you scratch your head. I found myself wishing many of the characters would die because of how annoying many of them were. Sadly many times after i destroy their mechs they just come back the next mission as if nothing happened. A pain is what i would call the story.Customization is a good point but not great. In Armored core you have many options of customization. You could make a spider mech, a tank mech, or and light fast mech. In this you have the option of making a pretty fast tanky mech or a really fast (one hit will kill me) type mech. At least you get lasor swords and railguns so its pretty cool. You also make a slient protagonist who is named rookie at all times even at the end of the game. You can customize him/her as well making a generic anime character. Your character is good concept in gameplay. You can actually exit your mech and do some decent damage as a human vs mech combat. You can lay mines, throw grenades, and shoot with your laser drone also dodge your butt off because you can die easy. You can make your character stronger by making them more of a cyborg affecting your appearance. It is very costly and you will look dumb while transitioning but will look pretty cool at the end. The strong point is game play. It plays like a faster armored core. Lock on is a little weird at times, and you lose your opponent pretty often even with radar somehow. However, gameplay is smooth and fun. Your mech can fly and boost as long as it has energy. You have weapons, sub weapons, missles/ railgun, and a support slot (which has ammo, mines etc.).Overall this game is a mixed bag. Very fun at time, but story drags it down. Customization is interesting but lacking in other areas. I would rate this game a 7 out of 10 it is a good mech game one of the few on steam, but it has many weak points that keeps it from being great.

Wining because they can't figure out how to get out of the corner is disappointing and losing because the guy with the same gear can move 10X faster with no regards to cooldown is frustrating.), the story should be thought out a bit more (are these guys the mercs or the politicians?), but otherwise, I have trouble finding something to complain about with this game.Other than being rough around the edges, this game is fine; and frankly, if you happen to be an AC fan, it's the closest to AC (as opposed to ace combat or gundum wing) as I've been able to find as of writing this, least for PC.

_childDocuments_.review: Find images on walls that you can put on your mech, throw a car at your friends, play the closest thing you're going to find to an action front mission or Armored Core that you can with your friends vs big baddies.There may be times where some of the other mech AI gets a lil daft, but it's sometimes in your favor and you can just play it off as they had a mechanical, software, or knocked the hell out, issue.Sadly I've not gotten to the PC version as much yet due to some complications, but it's a smoother frame rate version of what went down on the SWITCH and besides some of the colors and enemies feeling like they could use a lil more diversity at times, it's a good game. Now if only I could get a more open world mech game like this where you could visit towns and do a lil extra work aside from just blowing up baddies, but with that said there's plenty of fun here blowing up baddies. Though sometimes in co op missions wanting a lil more diversity in enemies at times, you actually do have a hand full of different ones throughout the game.For that matter you can grab a few of your enemies and throw them at other enemies like some tanks to toss around, and the mech baddies drop fresh new tools to sell off or use for yourself, and that's one of the big highlights here. The way you can pop someone and muster some pretty big ticket items.If there's a mech game that came out on PC in 2020 you wanted to pick up, this is bloody well it. It damn well deserves a sequel, sadly I'm not sure if it will be given that attention. But with that thought, you have all the less reason to not snatch this one up, try and talk a friend into it as well to go in on it co op, and have yourself a good mech adventure. Something we need more of in gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun and enjoyable mech game. I haven't really seen anything on its level besides armoured core, but honetly both games do the same on different level of budget so it really depends on what you can afford and what style you prefer. I'm still waiting to buy AC6 myself, but I think it's fair to say both, both is good. Even if Armoured core is a better game in terms of graphics and content, it's not anime.Game allows you to live your fantasies of flying typical anime mech that slides, slides faster, can fly, with big honking guns and rocket launchers and oversized swords. In the typical anime fashion you get colourful characters with extremely will voiced japanese dub. The story isn't as impressive as random mech anime's but it's enough, although cutscense may be a little bit annoying at times (can skp them all though) You can customise all body parts of the mech and all weapons and even mod these. Tons of potential for creating fan favourites and making your own designs.Missions are short, very short like 2-7 minutes, but there's plenty of them and game is meant to be replayable as opposed to armoured core where missions are longer. Multiplayer is dead for some reason, I assume armoured core again, but regardless you should brace for style, becasue this games looks and feels great if not too easy most of the time. Still for any mech fans I recommend trying this game before others, even buy and return it, just try if the fast paced, modular mech game is fun for you or if you prefer slug paces games like titanfall instead as the gap is huge and it can be a hit or a miss.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:Felt a bit like Armored Core games.Lots of customization for the mech.Fast actionI really like the style of the art/graphics.Cons:All the flaws of armored core games (extremely short missions, tight mission spaces)Story was absolute trash. Streaming this became a meme of "Somebody asked a question! Let's see if they answer or if they're just vague!"In spite of the customization, there is not enough to seriously change the appearance. Felt like the parts were mostly the same, just some with larger armor accents. No quad legs or tank treads like in AC games. Maybe the comparison is unfair.Dead multiplayer. Steamcharts says 90 player average. Got into 1 multiplayer game once. Tried hosting and nobody joined. Official discord server is for other games and there's no role to take for this game.Certain decisions in game design are baffling. Ice Cream shop gives the tiniest bonuses (2% reload speed) for 1 mission. Factory to develop new parts/tech/weapons has a big cost and only serves to unlock it IN THE STORE SO YOU CAN BUY IT.Your custom character is a third wheel to the entire story, just tagging along while all the NPCs interact.Prosthetic upgrades for the character look horrible and you have to look like an abomination to get the bonuses for your mech or when you're out of the mech.Certain points in the middle of a battle, you lose the ability to damage enemies. This is because you're not supposed to beat them at that moment. The game, however, doesn't tell you this so you end up blowing through your ammo until you realize there's no damage numbers popping up on the crowded screen.Overall I'm disappointed. Ending was abrupt and dumb too. No multiplayer to do what are essentially Raids or just general missions. No reason to keep playing.
_childDocuments_.name: DAEMON X MACHINA

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I want to commend this game for having no microtransactions.While the game handles okay it feels pretty unpolished and lacks a unique identity. The mech designs are okay but they come off as generic and all end up looking kinda samey, even with different parts to choose from. The weapons feel underpowered when fighting stronger enemies, especially arsenals or immortals. The story is meh and seems content to bring up themes but never really explore them. The characters are a plus and a good handful of them are memorable but none of them are exceptionally well written. The biggest flaw to me is the fact that certain mechanics seem to not be explained well enough or at all. This comes to a head in the final boss fight, without spoiling the story I can tell you that a central mechanic to the fight (Throwing capsules that line the floor) Is not explained to you at all and the fight is impossible without it. You are never told to use the capsules and since you start the fight in the air you can go several attempts without even seeing them. In line with the theme of things not being properly explained, short of checking the controls tab you won't know how to use any of the skills you purchase in the body modification lab. In addition some mechanics in the game just feel like they don't do anything or were intended to be more than they were in the final product. There seems to be the beginnings of a faction system in terms of consortiums and merc squads, I'd hazard a guess that you were at one point meant to be able to join one of each. The game seems to hint that your choices will effect the ending but I counted two (MAYBE three) Choices in the whole game, not sure if any but the last one mattered. If this game had some more dev time and polish it might have been something really interesting but as it stands it feels like an unfinished build of a better game. I'd give it a 4/10A few inexcusably annoying boss fights away from being an alright early access game.

_childDocuments_.review:
The future of mech-actions games is here. Defend the planet and defeat corrupted A.I. controlled robots using your Arsenal, a fully customizable mechanized battle suit. Choose and equip your Arsenal with a multitude of weapons, obtain more from downed enemy Arsenals, and swap them on the fly to suit your strategy in the face of ever-changing threats that may bring the end of the world. It was the greatest disaster in recorded history The moon tore apart, turning the sky into a kaleidoscope of red light that illuminated all who watched from below. Survive this apocalyptic new age as a mercenary and pilot powerful mechs in this brand-new action game from Kenichiro Tsukuda (Armored Core) and mech designer Shoji Kawamori (Super Dimensional Fortress Macross).

Features:

* The player's avatar is customizable with a variety of options
* Each Arsenal can be equipped with different weapons on its arms and shoulders, as well as reserve weaponry on its back that can be swapped out during battle
* Defeated enemies drop ammo and weapons, which the player can obtain and use on the fly
* Online and local wireless multiplayer modes support up to 4 players

detailed_description: EDITIONS TEARDOWN: ULTIMATE EDITION includes: TEARDOWN TEARDOWN: SEASON PASS TEARDOWN: SEASON PASS includes: TIME CAMPERS DLC - A campaign expansion set in the wild west. Available at launch. FOLKRACE DLC - A campaign expansion that introduces new vehicles and a series of destructive racing game modes. Available Spring 2024. TWO ADDITIONAL DLCS - Available by end of 2024. QUILEZ R0113R ROBOT - A spawnable, transformable robot vehicle equipped with destructive weapon systems and a grappling hook. TEARDOWN: DELUXE EDITION includes: TEARDOWN TIME CAMPERS DLC - A campaign expansion set in the wild west. Available at launch. FOLKRACE DLC - A campaign expansion that introduces new vehicles and a series of destructive racing game modes. Available Spring 2024. About the Game Plan the perfect heist using creative problem solving, brute force, and everything around you. Teardown features a fully destructible and truly interactive environment where player freedom and emergent gameplay are the driving mechanics. Tear down walls with explosives or vehicles to create shortcuts no one thought was possible. Stack objects, build structures, or use floating objects to your advantage. Take your time to create an efficient path through the level, plan the heist and get ready to execute it. Run, jump, drive, slingshot. Do whatever you need to collect targets, avoid robots or steal whatever your clients ask for. But make sure not to get caught! Campaign With your company pressured by increasing debt, you start accepting work from some more or less shady individuals. Soon you are knee-deep in a murky soup of revenge, betrayal, and insurance fraud. Beginning with some more or less legitimate assignments, you soon find yourself stealing cars, demolishing buildings, blowing up safes, avoiding trigger-happy robots and more. Upgrade your expanding arsenal of tools by searching for hidden valuables scattered around the environments. Sandbox Play around in the various environments with the tools you have unlocked. In this mode you have unlimited resources and an abundance of vehicles. No pressure, just pleasure. Challenges Test your skills in experimental game modes. New challenges unlock as you progress through the campaign. Modding Teardown has extensive mod support with built-in level editor, Lua scripting and a Steam Workshop integration. Build your own sandbox maps, mini games, tools, vehicles or try out existing mods from the community. Features Fully destructible voxel environments Realistic physical simulation of objects, debris, vehicles, water, fire, and smoke 17 different tools ranging from sledgehammer, blow torch and fire extinguisher to guns and explosives Campaign with 40 missions in an escalating storyline Sandbox mode for you to roam around in the various environments Extensive mod support and Steam Workshop integration

_childDocuments_.review: This game came out of nowhere for me.  I usually play RPGs and junk, but this one sucked me in. It's essentially a heist game mixed with some "Dad game elements", and physics shenanigans. _childDocuments_.review: Teardown is a true gem! Put your three dimensional puzzle solving and speedrunning abilities to the test across numerous environments with a host of tools at your disposal. There are approximately 10-12 areas in the game that you will revisit throughout the campaign, each time with a new objective that actually ties into a pretty hilarious narrative that's told through emails and work orders. While some missions can prove a little tedious, the overall experience and sense of accomplishment you get from this game after spending an hour and a half setting up a perfect 60 second heist is a truly unique experience. And if it's not a unique experience, please let me know so I can play those games too! I would recommend this game at a full price even, just to support the developers, cause they've made something really special!Did I mention it has workshop support? I just finished the campaign with 198 points of like 210 and haven't even touched any of the community levels. I'll be coming back to this game for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Just here for the 2020 Awards Nomination Badge, but while I'm here let me give my thoughts.Despite the positive reviews I was a bit sceptical when purchasing the game; it was a pretty neat idea but wasn't paired with top-notch graphics like most games push for nowadays. Half the time when I buy games with good ideas they fall flat and don't end up working out too well, but Teardown has done great in keeping me entertained. I start the mission off by opening the map to find my objective, track it down and blow a hole in the wall with my shotgun to enter the house despite there being a door literal inches away. I then proceed to forget what the objective was as I am reloading what now appears to be the last 8 slugs I have into my shotgun, before finishing off the rest of the foundation on the house and watching it all fall down around me. From there I restart the mission and try to actually do the objective before getting distracted again.All in all it's quite an amusing game to play. Despite the cubic "Minecraft" look to everything the game looks just right and runs well too, though I do notice a hard performance drop when destroying too many things at once or within one area. In the end it's your opinion but I believe it is well worth original price, and a good steal if ever on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most impressive destruction physics engine I have ever used in my life. Although it's far from realistic in regard to global physics, it's decent enough to pique your desires in causing mass destruction everywhere you go. Note that this game requires a beefy (literally, almost no computer can run it smoothly when you go on a rampage) device to run. My minimal specification recommendations are:1. CPU =  At least a 5950x. It's a single-core game, so choose the most powerful one regarding single-core performance. For AMD users, go for 7950x in 2023.2. GPU = At least a 4070 Ti for Nvidia cards in 2023. I'd recommend a 4080 or a 4090 for this game, though.3. RAM = Over 32 GB (Go for 64GB)These specs have gotten me 20~50 FPS during cinematic explosion footage in 2K.With Impact Based Structural Integrity (a mod), you can enhance global destruction by a large leap.

_childDocuments_.review: Simple, yet fantastic gameplay. Every Vehicle can be driven, every building can be destroyed and every tree can be burned down. All of this can be useful to create a path which you will need to complete your objective in 60 seconds. If you just want to destroy stuff, there is a sandbox mode too, but you need to play the campaign mode to unlock maps and tools. The same map and the same misson can be played hundreds of times without being the same, it's really up to you how you play and which path you choose.This game is absolutely stunning. Sure, its a voxel game. Lots and lots of blocks. But Teardown took voxels to a whole other level. The maps are beautifully crafted and the ambience is truly fascinating. I was blown away when i first started the Game, and I think you will be too.It does require a very good pc to run smoothly all the time, the FPS go down the more destruction you cause (obviously) to a point where you may have to restart the map (usually only happens in sandbox). It probably will require you to play around with the settings a bit to find the best quality/performance combination for your system.With all that being said, I think its safe to say that Teardown is a great game. It has a lot of replayability, beautiful maps which are great for sandbox players who want to blow off some steam, as well as for people who want to feel the thrill of the campaign and the rewarding feeling of finding a faster path than before. Driving trucks into walls, burning down whole buildings, sinking a yacht...it's simply an amazing experience that I think everyone should give  a try. Only workshop support could make this game better, but im confident it will be added at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: I may change my review at a later date, but as of now I'd warn people before buying that a lot of the starting missions are  "How quickly can you steal things in 60 secs?" I expected much more puzzle physics-based destruction than the simple 2 or 3 levels as I push the 4hr mark. _childDocuments_.review: The first two missions are really fun, but then things got really repetitive really quickly. The next ten missions are some variation of "Get the thing and escape, but watch out for the alarm! You have 60 seconds" on the same three maps with only minor variations each time.By the time I had finally unlocked a new map, the novelty of fully destructible environments had long worn off and I wondered what fresh hell awaited me, rather than being excited at a new environment.I then loaded up Sandbox mode, having heard the later levels are more fun! Only to discover that they were locked and I'd have to unlock them in the campaign.The story mode feels tacked on as an afterthought, but in order to experience all the game has to offer, you need to go through it. I'm sure the experience is better with mods, but I feel like a game that doesn't stand on its own without mods isn't a good game.And any game that makes you put extra effort in to have fun has completely failed as a game.

_childDocuments_.review: This (so far) is the one and only game I have ever played the entire story through. And I have to say the story itself is very amusing yet tense. The game is extremely action packed, requires situational awareness and good planning ahead to complete missions. Even if you don't want to complete the campaign at the moment, you can always use "sandbox" to destroy anything and everything to your hearts desire! I Would absolutely recommend the game, even at the price of $32 it is worth every penny. Thank you Teardown Dev's for bringing my new favorite game to life!

_childDocuments_.review: The tech is really impressive, and the game lots of fun - the missions get a little repetitive after a couple of hours, but the dev is adding more variety each update, and it'll be exciting to see what new ideas come next.The game introduces you to the mechanics in a really natural way - you can see that all your targets are alarmed and instantly snap into an 'I need to plan how this will go' mindset and you start creating your planning-versus-action phase separation intuitively, which is really clever.Sandbox mode is great when racing against the clock becomes too stressful - I'd love some casual puzzle maps to wind down from the heists.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best puzzle games I have played. I just played the expansion and it really reminded me how much I like this game. You go in expecting huge amounts of destruction and explosions, and those are present, but I find the much more enjoyable part of the game the meticulous setup of your route. It really satisfies a problem solving part of my brain, where I have a set of tools and a collection of objectives, total free reign over how you solve the objectives. It also greatly rewards creative approaches. Can't figure out how to grab the objective inside a lookout tower? Simple, don't go to the tower, break its supports, pick the whole house on the top up with a crane, and then drive that over to the exit. While I have heard this game described as "essentially a physics engine demo," the game inside is still a truly enjoyable puzzle that I can easily spend over an hour on per level fleshing out my plan. Would absolutely recommend for anyone who likes games that say "here's an objective and a bunch of tools to solve it, we don't care how."

_childDocuments_.review: I always love a good moddable game. Teardown is a destruction sandbox that surpasses battlefield with it's physics interactions. However, this isn't just a sandbox. Teardown has a puzzle-based campaign where you must think of intricate ways to wreck buildings in order to reach objectives. It got old for me quick, but for those looking for a good puzzle game, it's right here. For those who don't want to melt their brain, the moddable sandbox is as open and free as any other sandbox on Steam. Go wild. Level an entire city block. Turn a mansion into charred bricks and scrap. Chop a 747 in half. Have fun. After all, that's what games are for.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 45 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for Christmas in 2021 from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my character and world and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: Out of the 4 or so measly hours I've played this game at the time of writing this review, I've spent probably 3.5 hours just... wrecking stuff with a sledgehammer. My destruction-addicted alter ego is in heaven and I can't wait to unlock more destructive tools. I hope this game becomes such an enormous success that other game devs start taking notes and emulate it in principle. You wanna know why?Because take a look at current games. Yeah sure, they look amazing, so realistic, so incredibly detailed, especially when driven by hardware that can now support resolutions at 4K and above. Ray tracing that lets suspiciously ubiquitous puddles on the ground (it sure rains a lot if ray-tracing is turned on) and cars and window panes, all polished to absolute perfection, just so they can reflect the world around. In real time, no less, egads! All fancy, beautiful stuff, no doubt......but in the meantime, you aim at a house and fire a salvo of rockets that can level half a neighborhood down and what do you get? A bunch of 2D sprites of blast impacts added onto the texture of its facade and... that's it. And if you fire a bunch more rockets elsewhere, the oldest blast impacts will disappear and that house is once again as good as new, looking perfect in 4K resolution, and especially its reflection in those five dozen puddles on the ground, scattered about just to make extra sure you noticed the ray tracing.In 2001, I was an impressionable teenager who got his mind blown away by a recently released FPS shooter that wasn't really that great of a success, who even at the time had outdated graphics. It was called Red Faction. But in it, if you didn't feel like hunting for key cards or buttons to unlock doors blocking your progress, you could just take your rocket launcher out and blow a hole in the wall next to it. KA-BLAM! Way cleared, proceed and forget about that stupid key card. So long as you had the ammo and creative thought, you could carve a level up and make your own  routes. I can't begin to describe how much I loved that game, and more importantly how excited it got me for the future, where through Moore's law and hardware getting more and more powerful, I hoped, PCs would become able to support much more detailed methods of destruction, environments with far more interaction, more realistic physics and so on. Boy was I disappointed.Teardown is a shining example to me that a game doesn't NEED to look like reality in order to be fun. Some people like fancy graphics and pretty stuff like ray-tracing and that's fine by me. People like me though will appreciate the gameplay mechanics, the freedom granted by a fully destructible environment and the thoughtful physics behind it. It adds to the level of interaction possible in a game, and that's a great thing in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so ive been seeing alot of reviews that dont really go into detail about the game, so...The gameplay in teardown seems to consist of.. well tearing things down, u use tools like hammers, bombs and guns to destroy whatever you are tasked to destroy, the game doesnt let u use all this at the beginning tho, u have to play the campaign and earn enough points to earn a new tool, at first u get one per 5 points but then its per 10 points, now u may think "awee i cant just get everything and blow whatever i want up instantly?" well yes but dont worry, the campaign is fun and enjoyable, it has a funny lore to it that you can read out during the mission 'briefings' if you will, another nice addition is that you're hub (where u spawn after a mission complete or launching campagin) evolves as you play, and so will the actual in game mission locations, its all a nice lovely touch that makes the world feel alive somehow.So no the campaign isnt some quickly thrown together mess as an annoying buffer before you can get to the good stuff, everything is the good stuff, so enjoy.Running on an overclocked i5-8600k at 4.8 ghz and a rtx 2060, the game has quite suprising preformance for how pretty it looks, i get an average of 80 fps and only dip at 40-50 when the conditions are more intense (which is mostly a cpu based issue)talking about the cpu, thats the main workhorse for Teardown, but teardown only uses 2 cores so unless you have an incredibly slow cpu you will have equal preformance.So basically minimum/recommended spec is very accurate and u dont need any more than that to enjoy it.The game is only released recently so dont expect it to be bug free but suprisingly it isnt one of those buggy messes that you see commonly, yes there are bugs but none that ive encountered are game breaking, ive seen smoke shooting trough walls and other objects after they have been set on fire (usually happens inside buildings), some objects like to simply ignore walls if you throw it at that wall hard enough and if the object is small enough.Sometimes when walking over water on a floating object that is slightly under water (like a plank that can barely support your weight) u'l start somehow appearing under water and then back up over and over, so once again a small bug.Those are pretty much the only bugs ive really encountered so far.The game has as ive said only been released recently so it isnt fully fledged and done yet but it has some serious potential, its already extremely fun but it could be much much more fun if it had a few more features, like multiplayer support where you could race friends in custom race maps.Mod support would also be able to release an extreme amount of potential because of the many tools and vehicles that could still be made using the games engine and general foundation.There are also some possible minor additions like some better UI that feels less.. indie, some more maps, more types of missions, multiple hubs or custom made hub using bought items or stolen items (stealing items for hub could be a form of mission/gamemode itself).. and so on so forthI hope this review helped you decide if you want the game or if you want to keep it instead of refunding, if not then im sure the other reviews will be able to help but thanks for reading anyways.Some more notes before i end:Ive been looking for a game like this myself so im fairly optimistic about its future and potential, ive been following it quite closely for a few months so im glad i was able to purchase it on day one.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I don't think even the 95% positive review score does this game justice. I know being in early access puts some people off, but it really shouldn't, because this honestly feels more finished than some fully released triple A games I've played in the past. It can be a little buggy at times (namely being inside a sinking boat can easily phase you through floors, walls and ceilings), and some aspects of the destruction I think could be tuned a little better (namely I think the vehicles should take a little more to destroy them, especially the giant fishing boat thing). But, overall, I cannot recommend this game enough. Every challenge/mission has countless different ways to approach it. I only finished the campaign 2 days ago, and I already want to go back and replay at least certain levels to find a different way of doing it, or to get every optional objective too. (oh and they';e expanding the storyline/campaign with "part 2" which I assume will be similar length to the current campaign, and will be a free update later on). In short. GET. THIS. GAME.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal. I grew up on PC games, and I remember asking a friend of mine in middle school (who wrote Lua scripts for Gmod servers and was my go-to tech guru friend at the time): "Will there ever be a game where you can destroy everything? Like, absolutely everything? Until it's just water and craters left behind?"Teardown answers that question, and the answer is "Yes"The game starts you with a sledgehammer, a yellow spraypaint can, and a fire extinguisher. These tools seemed boring to me when I first spawned in with them, but as time went on I realized these three starting tools are the most important tools you'll be given throughout the game. The sledgehammer can destroy small chunks of wood, drywall, glass, and other fragile materials. Brick, concrete and metal will all be hard to deal with initially, but they are no match for the tools you'll unlock later on.As you finish missions, you will unlock new tools. I will not mention exactly what any of these tools are in my review because I really enjoyed the experience of finding a new tool and suddenly getting tons of ideas of new ways to play.The modding community for Teardown is awesome. People have made many maps, tools and heists for you to try. Some of them are so good I have a hard time believing they're free mods. Devs seemed to have created excellent modding tools for this game.The game takes a decent PC to run. I am using a Ryzen 7 3700K with 16 GB of DDR4 3200 RAM, and an old GTX 970 that I've had since high school. Settings are on low, no raytracing, 100% render scale on a 1080p monitor. Game is running off an NVME SSD, if that matters. I get 50-70 FPS when I first load into a level, and it regularly dips below 30 FPS when things are burning or exploding. During one mission about halfway through the campaign, my frames dropped below 10 FPS for a fair amount of time.One suggestion I'd provide for the devs would be to implement a system for sharing saves with other players. It would be fun to set up a route for one of the heists and then send the save to my friend and see how quickly they can complete the route that I created. This would probably not take too much extra work to implement, and I think it would provide a lot more replayability.Overall, the only thing that I didn't absolutely love about the game is it's length. I beat the game in under 15 hours of total runtime, and that includes all the time I spent messing around with mods in the Sandbox mode before I beat the game. However, the game is in early-access at the time of writing, and from what I understand, the devs will release a "part 2" to Teardown someday as a free update. Even without this, I think this game is absolutely worth the $20 they ask for when it's not on sale. I got it for $16 so even more so in my case. If your rig can run the game, you won't be disappointed.

In addition there is a plethora of mods and a lot of mod support and an enthusiastic modding community. This is a game that I feel really happy about purchasing and supporting the devs. When they say "vote with your money" this is what it's all about, this is the innovation and creativity we need in gaming now. There is really no other game like this in my steam library. I have dozens of fps to choose from, generic indies and a couple of rts games but nothing like Teardown. Tuxedo Labs has outdone themselves with this unique little masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a masterpiece. It's difficult to even put into words. But putting it simply: you are a force of nature in the form of a person that seems to work for some silly human demolition company. Puny mortals have the audacity to request your services sometimes. Luckily for them, most of those services involve destroying *something*, and you happen to greatly enjoy wanton destruction, so they get a pass.You will use sledgehammers, explosives, guns, pieces of wood and more to carve and craft a path - the shortest and most direct path you can muster - through the 100% completely destructible environment in an attempt to steal and destroy a *whole bunch of apparently important ♥♥♥♥* in the fastest possible time.There is no obstacle too tall, thick, or """durable""" for you to handle. Trees in the way? Knock them down. Wall standing between Point A and Point B? My bombs say 'not anymore'. Is the staircase to the next level a little too far for your taste? Make another one that's closer with explosions and ramps. Did the car you need to steal break down? Tear off everything except the chassis and walk it to the finish line. Do you find yourself thinking - at any point - 'if only that <insert_literally_anything> wasn't there'? Then make it so, you silly goose. The only entity that cannot be removed by your shenanigans is the ground upon which everything exists. Everything else is grass, and you are an extremely effective and excitable lawn mower.There's multiple answers to every question - most of them involving explosions - and you need to figure out the best one. It's a puzzle game gloriously fused to a destruction simulator, and probably going to be the most entertaining 20 bucks you ever spent.Have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's kind of amazing.The whole reason anyone knows this game is for its voxel-based destruction system, but what's amazing is how they managed to weave the destruction into a campaign so well. It's not just a sandbox to destroy ♥♥♥♥ in. There are so many ways to make the destruction more purposeful and exciting, which is exactly how the game handles its campaign.The game jumps back and forth from a platformer to an action game, having levels where you're basically just doing a time trial, only you can cut holes in the map to make your route faster, to levels where you're narrowly dodging barrages of missiles from a pursuing helicopter while the building you're in collapses around you, to levels where the goal is actually the inverse of what you'd expect: trying to limit destruction as much as possible.At first I didn't really like the campaign that much, but it really gives you a level of freedom that you wouldn't normally have. Since the game is so free, you can come up with some really fun and creative solutions to the problems it throws at you.The destruction system has gotten much smoother over time and now I don't really experience too much lag when breaking buildings apart. It used to be an issue a while ago but now I can topple gigantic towers without so much as a stutter from my PC.Of course, there is also a sandbox mode and there are plenty of mods too, so you can really customize this game as much as you like and do whatever you want. It's really impressive and limited only by your creativity.My one complaint is that there's no stress simulation in buildings. They'll just stay floating until you completely sever them from the ground. There is, thankfully, a mod that adds a stress system. In fact, there are a lot of mods that make this game way, way better, so I'd recommend just trying a bunch of them too.

_childDocuments_.review: Teardown is basically a heist game. You will be tasked with stealing X amount of safes, or X amount of cars, or destroying X amount of paintings. Each spread out across a detailed and dense map.The key aspect is that everything in the game world is realistically destructible. You can smash through walls, build bridges, blow up buildings, etc. It's an incredibly fun combination. The vast majority of your time will be spent "casing" the level, figuring out the best route, clearing obstacles out the way, building quicker routes across and through the scenery. Then you have the mad dash of trying to actually accomplish it in the time limit.
