_childDocuments_.review: Original EA review:Picked it up last night and I'm having some pretty brutal performance hitches when moving around. I expect it's a mix of a slower hdd + cpu bound stuff when loading the world? Also I'm seeing brutal visual artifacts and performance drops around any surface made from glass for whatever reason, and once the timer kicks in it somehow gets worse? It's also unfortunately got an incredibly aggressive sleep condition which can make physics objects come to rest in really weird states, and really large objects tend to remain stuck rather than fall as expected (for instance bisecting an entire house on the marina level leaves the upper half floating in the air, minecraft style)Also while I'm nitpicking, I'm really not sure about the 60 second timer / route planning gameplay. If there is a way to stealth your way past the alarms and be elegant/smart as an alternative to brutal and fast I go that way every single time. I love it as a thiefing demolition man sim, rather than a perfect execution smash and grab sim. When the timer is on and the pressure rises, all the performance and hitching issues make it far more frustrating than it needs to be.The good news is that it's early access so basically none of what I wrote above really counts :D It's still gorgeous and impressive and fun. The sandbox mode and fire propagation are worth the price of admission alone.Updated review:Runs much better (with some understandable moments of choppiness; this is a complex game!), full of good content, great music and a funny campaign. I also really came around on the 60 second timer thing as soon as I embraced the quicksave quickload planner mindset. There are some bonkers satisfying speedruns in this game!Overall I really have to recommend this game strongly. Huge value for money, unique game design, cool hand crafted engine. Just a very special title indeed.

_childDocuments_.review: Teardown is a game that definitely isn't for everyone, but it's easy enough to determine if you are or are not the type of person who may enjoy it. The fundamental two questions are, "Do you now or have you ever loved destruction physics?" If you were one of those gamers who in previous years absolutely loved when Battlefield: Bad Company came out and displayed their destruction, and/or couldn't get enough of blowing stuff up and deconstructing buildings in Red Faction: Guerrilla, then you will probably get similar if not greater enjoyment from this game.The second fundamental question is, "How powerful is your PC?" Because, unfortunately, I at least have found this game rather difficult to run at a consistent 60. Even with effects on Low, only at 1080p, the framerate will commonly drop below 30 with even seemingly minor destruction going on. My machine, by the way, consists of an i7-6700k as well as a Titan X if that tells you anything. It makes sense that it's hard to run, but even so it's an important thing to keep in mind.This game gives me a childlike glee from just messing around with the destruction physics. If this game or something very comparable to it was out there for consumption when I -was- a kid, I'm sure I would've gone crazy for it. The 'game' that was built around the destruction physics is something I found quite compelling as well, the idea of destroying and shaping the environment to try to develop the most optimal path, placing vehicles and all ahead of time and re-playing your runs to try and shave half-seconds off your time is quite compelling and fun, even though it does have the tendency to be frustrating at times.There are also some things, like the driving physics, that are far better than they have any reason to be. Having followed the development of this game a little bit, it's plain to see that the developer is something of an overachiever in the sense that they are willing to go through great lengths to implement things that they think are cool, or that they just -want- to add. A great trait in a developer, especially in this case where they've actually managed to pull it all off. Vehicle physics, the fire and smoke physics, on top of the game's base destruction physics.Overall it's a great game if you love destruction physics and optimizing time trial runs, and if you have a machine that can run it, but because of that it's not for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: On the surface Teardown is a physics based destruction game where finding the most creative and fun ways to destroy things takes top priority. The game is an amazing physics sandbox where almost everything is destructible given enough effort. This is what I thought when going into the game but as it turns out, this 3D Voxel based destruction-oriented sandbox is really just the foundation for a forced and monotonous heist simulator.This game has a great foundation as mentioned above, but chooses to put all of that aside and force you into very repetitive time based missions where you must complete a set amount of objectives within a 60 second time frame. Those missions might sound fun at first, but when almost every mission in the game plays out like this it becomes very tiresome.  I am aware of the cheats menu which lets you skip missions and extend the alarm timer however, If I have to skip the majority of the game's missions because almost all of them are alarm related, I might as well not play the game.In summary. If you come into this expecting a fun physics sandbox where destroying things is the main objective then you will be disappointed. If you want a really good physics sandbox where timed heist missions are at the forefront, then I suppose it's worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: The campaign is mostly a heist game. You take as much time as you need to plan out how you're going to steal some items and reach the exit within 60 seconds. There's no "right" way to do it. You're given some tools/vehicles, and it's your job to figure out how to make it work. Once you start that 60 second countdown though, it's like a speedrun where even a half-second delay can ruin it. But it feels great when everything goes according to plan.The destructibility of the environment is probably the best I've ever seen in a game. You can destroy pretty much everything but the "bedrock" layer of ground and building foundations. The physics are kind of funny to see in a voxel game. You don't expect a pipe that looks like something out of Minecraft to be flexible, but it is. Performance is pretty good given the amount of debris that can be on screen at the same time.Looking forward to more content.

He asked that I use my chemistry knowledge to cook methamphetamine, which he would then sell using his connections in the drug world. Connections that he made through his career with the DEA. I was... astounded, I... I always thought that Hank was a very moral man and I was... thrown, confused, but I was also particularly vulnerable at the time, something he knew and took advantage of. I was reeling from a cancer diagnosis that was poised to bankrupt my family. Hank took me on a ride along, and showed me just how much money even a small meth operation could make. And I was weak. I didn't want my family to go into financial ruin so I agreed. Every day, I think back at that moment with regret. I quickly realized that I was in way over my head, and Hank had a partner, a man named Gustavo Fring, a businessman. Hank essentially sold me into servitude to this man, and when I tried to quit, Fring threatened my family. I didn't know where to turn. Eventually, Hank and Fring had a falling out. From what I can gather, Hank was always pushing for a greater share of the business, to which Fring flatly refused to give him, and things escalated. Fring was able to arrange, uh I guess I guess you call it a "hit" on my brother-in-law, and failed, but Hank was seriously injured, and I wound up paying his medical bills which amounted to a little over $177,000. Upon recovery, Hank was bent on revenge, working with a man named Hector Salamanca, he plotted to kill Fring, and did so. In fact, the bomb that he used was built by me, and he gave me no option in it. I have often contemplated suicide, but I'm a coward. I wanted to go to the police, but I was frightened. Hank had risen in the ranks to become the head of the Albuquerque DEA, and about that time, to keep me in line, he took my children from me. For 3 months he kept them. My wife, who up until that point, had no idea of my criminal activities, was horrified to learn what I had done, why Hank had taken our children. We were scared. I was in Hell, I hated myself for what I had brought upon my family. Recently, I tried once again to quit, to end this nightmare, and in response, he gave me this. I can't take this anymore. I live in fear every day that Hank will kill me, or worse, hurt my family. I... All I could think to do was to make this video in hope that the world will finally see this man, for what he really is.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has MASSIVE potential. -From the little time I've put it, I can honestly say that there's more work to be added. Although it feels like a complete sandbox game, with what's been used for is a whole completely different deal. -Not only can you cause havoc, but you have missions. I'm not too sure if you're a thief or some sort of criminal, but you get hired at first to destroy am old home. Not a big deal as the game uses physics to do your bidding. Then you are sent to Lee Chemicals to steal three computers. This is where it gets interesting because now, you are on a hunt for three items. -After taking these three items, your next mission is to go back to Lee Chemicals and find three other items. Here is where it gets interesting because the game now allows you to fully utilize your tools. -When you take the first item, it sets of an alarm (still not sure if you can bypass it but it be cool if you can). You use your spray can to make any landmark markings to plan out your heist. After making your plan, you can proceed on your company getaway vehicle, but not after leaving destruction behind. -You can use vehicles that are found in the world to create destruction, there's red gas tanks that you can throw and it'll explode upon impact, you can use boats, trucks, construction vehicles such as cranes to cause havoc. As of yet i'm not that far into the game but it be great to see the following:-NPC's to fight with-Yes, for me personally, the game felt lonely without that computer interaction. I'm already lonely enough, so I don't need to be lonely when gaming. I think that's all the game needs (other than more worlds to explore)-Other than that, the graphics are HOE.LEE.SH*T status, the game play is spot on, and the overall experience left me with a good impression.-Even at this stage you'll have fun as you'll get to see what other wonders the dev(s) get to bring in with future updates. -Oh and it also has Steam Workshop, so there's crazy sh*t mods out there. -Keep on gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by the trailer. 90% of your time in the campaign will be spent carefully blowing up a specific path through a world in preparation for a 60-second heist. This is not an adrenaline-packed game, or a destruct-a-thon. It's a slow planning game. Also contrary to the trailer, the physics are not realistic at all. For example, if you knock out 7/8 of a building's supports, it will stand tall and unwavering until you destroy the 8th one.The missions in the campaign are HARD, but not in a fun way. Unexpected, unrealistic physics interactions will force you to reload constantly. Hope you quick saved! If you fail your 60-second heist, but thought of a better setup that's across the map, well my friend, it's time to slowly walk across the map, make your change, then slowly walk back and run it again, hope it works. Repeat this several times.There are options to skip a mission or extend the timer. Presumably the defaults are the intended way to play the game though, and that intended way is not fun, but more importantly, it doesn't resemble the trailer at all.EDIT: I finished the campaign just to see it through to the end. Part 2 is wildly different than Part 1. It has more variety and I'd argue more forgiving required objectives, which is a weird thing to say about the second half of a campaign. Overall, I hated my time with this game, even Part 2. Perhaps the other modes are better, but don't buy this game for its campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: Teardown

_childDocuments_.review: A physics based speedrunning game in which pretty much everything you see can be destroyed.Most stages in the game go like this,1. Scout out the place, check which mission objectives you should complete in which order to get them done in the shortest time possible. Which item should you pick up first & how are you going to get back to your spawn point.2. Use hammers & explosives to tunnel your way through buildings & build bridges with planks.level buildings that are in the way & move vehicles to strategic locations to help when collecting the mission items. Steal every valuable item that isn't nailed down for some extra $$$.I recommend using spray paint to mark the route you're going to take, really helps with the speedrunning part.3. Pick up the first mission objective & a 1 minute countdown will begin. Collect all of the mission objectives( & maybe some optional ones if you want to be greedy) & make your way to the exit.And you've completed a mission, as a reward you get to watch the route you took from birds eye view & maybe even unlock some new weapons of mass destruction you can use to make your time in the following missions better.You also get to spend all of that money you made during the mission on upgrades for your existing tools.The game also supports a sandbox mode if you feel like messing around, but you need to unlock items & maps in the campaign mode if you want to enjoy it to the fullest.
_childDocuments_.name: Teardown

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good game. They give you a bunch of tools and a list of objectives to complete. How you complete the objectives is up to you. Gameplay wise you use tools to modify the environment to allow yourself to complete a series of objectives. Missions basically fall into one of 3 categories: Steal these things under a minute, break these things under a minute or level the building beneath the specified height. The most recent update added some additional variety such as 'steal things while avoiding drones' but the majority of the missions are still 'steal x number of items under a minute'. Base game aside theres also an active modding community and and fantastic destruction physics so theres hours of playtime you can make for yourself.Story - Its okay but to be honest since it was told through a series of emails I didnt pay too much attention.Theres not much more to talk about, the game is just fun and well made.Honestly the best part of this game was finding the different ways to destroy your own warehouse between missions. The worst part by far was the tornado level, its not really skill  or intelligence based at all, you cant lose and tornadoes appear at random to throw your target and/or yourself somewhere in the map. I hate to complain about one of the few spots of variety but the tornadoes just seemed to be there to waste your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Teardown

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, Teardown is a fun twist on sandbox games. With fully destructible environments (and I mean FULLY), an arsenal of tools to dish out mayhem, and a rather unique heist aspect to the missions, this game sure isn't to disappoint. However, my biggest complaint about the game is that it's a lot of the same, even with mods. The game really just boils down to different flavors of, "blow stuff up". While there are a couple missions in the campaign that require some different, non-destructive tactics to complete, they are the exception rather than the rule. Nonetheless, the destruction part of the game, is still a joy. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this on a whim, as watching streamers and YouTubers really kinda hooked my interest.Honestly I can't recommend this enough and I hope the developer is going to stick to this project for a long time after the game is truly finished. You might only start on a simple job with a sledge-hammer, but even then you might be just as impressed as I was by the physics and beauty the game put on display.Every single job is like a sandbox in which you're going to need to plot your concise route of destruction and will need to use every tool in your arsenal to its full ability, of which there are many! Not to mention the vehicles and natural elements left at your disposal in each mission. What truly might test some though in the later levels is a use of the most formidable tool given to us humans, our brains and creativity. It's not just about punching holes in walls anymore. It's a race against the clock in hoping for a perfect execution and hoping all of the puzzle pieces we've personally taken time to smash, explode and shoot out will fit into one whole perfectly coalescent image of victory.TL;DR:It's an over the top demolition / puzzle game with some at times seriously huge challenge depending on your individualized approach.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really fun!BEAUTIFUL voxel graphics with a huge emphasis on physics and interactions between objects.The game even has a singleplayer campaign that gives you some direction and super fun levels to play. _childDocuments_.review: Introducing:Video Games... 2Folks, this right here is my GOTY pick for 2020. Teardown is the ultimate next step for games like Garry's Mod and Minecraft, and I suspect its influence on the industry is going to be every bit as significant.I seriously can't stop gushing about this game. God. GOD. Teardown has fundamentally blown my expectations out of the water for how you interact with your environment in games. It strikes a truly unbelievable balance between challenge and pure meditative stress relief. The execution is absolutely awe-inspiring, and it's given me perhaps the single most memorable experience I've had with a game in probably the last decade. No Man's Sky is basically my other "favorite video game" but even an infinite galaxy can't compare to what Teardown accomplishes at the smaller scale. I really don't think I've ever found a game that rewarded me for careful planning and patience the way Teardown does. It lets me be John Madden, MacGyver and Ryo Hazuki all at the same time. It was a really genius decision to build the campaign around the concept of "heist simulator". It complements the tech better than I ever could've imagined and justifies its existence pretty much immediately. Just a complete joy, start to finish.Also for one final ultra spicy take: Teardown is the most photorealistic game I've ever played. Maybe this is just my time with Blender Cycles talking, but the raytracing engine is seriously a shock to behold. If people weren't already sold on the potential of realtime raytracing this game is about to change some minds fast I suspect.Anyway. Take my money y'all. This thing is going to be a huge deal. Thank you for this amazing, bombastic gift.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: I like game, sometimes boring, good content milking strat, nice physics and features. Teardown is a really enjoyable game, especially if you play it 5 hours at a time, every 6 months. I may be one of the few who were super excited about it when they saw it for 15 bucks on steam, bought it immediately, played for a month straight, and then forgot about it for a few months. I revisit it alot, but it can't compete in my head with other co-op or multiplayer games with similar destruction. Perhaps a Pvp mode would cause the game to enter a new fanbase(Idk if thats the right way to say it), and would totally make me come back. In addition, while I do love destroying anything that exists, I would like to be able to build things, and that being a part of the campaign/ a separate would be a game changer (for me at least).Regardless, this game was amazing to play, even for my 9 hour interest span. I highly recommend it if you love explosions, smoke, fire, etc. If you're a content creator, with a community who will ask you to do certain things in the game, it would probably keep you interested in Teardown longer than I was.Have a good day, hope this helped you make a good decision!DEVS: Well done, I like the boom effects:D

_childDocuments_.review: Teardown is super impressive! The destruction physics, gameplay and the support the modding community has brought to the game has helped it to become really enjoyable. Smash and blast your way through walls as you plan your heist to collect or destroy valuable items and try to escape without being caught. Or, go rogue in the nine existing sandbox levels or download a sandbox world through the Steam workshop. Destroy everything in sight with your tools in hand and become the Michael Bay you’ve always wanted to be. The developers are very active and listen to requests from their players which is highly appreciated. It's important to note that the campaign is a bit limited as to what the objective is. _childDocuments_.review: Whaaaat? A game that's really fun that doesn't involve killing anything?I love this game!Someone finally designed the game I've been waiting for for decades.  It's always annoyed me that 95% of game environments are static and indestructible.  This game changes that in a really fun way.  I especially appreciate the strategy elements - the designers could have stopped at the "sandbox" stage and had a really fun game.  But they went the extra (more than a) mile and conjured up interesting and challenging goals to figure out in the campaign mode (and I haven't even delved into the custom mods, yet - I want to go through it "legit" first).  And the whole thing has a perfect touch of whimsy & humor to it, as well.  Did they get it all right?  No.  Buildings laugh at gravity, some items are too fragile (e.g. crates and heavy equipment), the behavior of the "planks" can be frustrating, and I don't care too much for the WASD controls - they're fine for walking and running, but not ideal for driving (though for a compromise, they went the right direction).I love the care and attention to detail that went into every aspect of this game.  The sound design is terrific, the music is perfect, and I even love the blocky graphics - not only does it hark back to games I loved, but obviously keeping it running fluidly was a high priority (and a wise design choice because after a while, you don't even notice it).I can't wait to see what these guys come up with next...Bravo, Tuxedo Labs!  Well done.

_childDocuments_.review: TDLR; I can't overstate the value of this game. GPU limitations are pretty significant, so check the specs against yours. But if you can play this and it looks even mildly interesting at first glance (as it did to me), then it's worth the money. It will blow your mind.Man I have a ton to say about this game but the lack of organization to do so. Originally, I was skeptical about the campaign as part of the game. I was so wrong. It's the best thing to play around with. The challenges, unique time limits, hurdles, varied mechanics, and completion-based unlock system blend into a great end result. I cannot overstate how much I enjoy this game (I'm 20 hours in and still not done with the campaign and still discovering new interactions and fun mechanics.Pros:Easily the most robust use and implementation of voxels of any game I've seen or played (mostly noita admittedly)Intelligent design in the way the materials interact and create challenges to overcome.Genuinely surprising and engaging campaign mode. (This mode ultimately unlocks the sandbox levels and tools, though I'm sure workshop content can skip that for those who do not much care for the puzzles.)Honestly I can't sing praises for this game enough. I was gifted it over Christmas, but even on my tight budget, I'd buy it myself. It's truly a new kind of experience and I cannot commend the devs enough for it.Cons:Raytracing is very GPU intensive even for my NVIDIA 2070S (mostly in the heat it creates, but larger structures being moved from their rigid points can cause insane lag very quickly. Only found this to be a problem in sandbox mode.)Campaign can be difficult to get into, but if you stick through it, the early unlocks and exploration-based upgrade system really polishes the hell out of the game.Really I have no major complaints. This is my top vacation game currently. It is absolutely worth every penny if you can run it on your computer.

_childDocuments_.review: Teardown, huh? Now that's a name that's both straightforward and intriguing. It's like a game that's begging for some Duke Nukem-style demolition expertise. And let me tell you, when it comes to tearing things down, I'm the king.This game is all about voxels, baby. Imagine a world built on cubes, waiting for the Duke to come in and wreck havoc. I'll smash through walls, reduce buildings to rubble, and turn the whole place into my personal playground of destruction. Voxels, shmoixels - they'll crumble like a house of cards before my mighty sledgehammer.But that's not enough for the Duke. I'll take it up a notch with some explosive fun. Give me a few bombs, and I'll turn a city block into a fireworks display. Buildings will rain down like confetti, and the explosions will rock the very foundation of this game. Duke Nukem doesn't just break things; he obliterates them!Now, let's talk about the funny part. Teardown? It sounds like a how-to guide for disgruntled contractors or a demolition crew on a sugar rush. But hey, who am I to judge? As long as I get to unleash chaos and leave a trail of destruction, I'm a happy man.So get ready for voxel devastation, my friends. Grab your sledgehammer, strap on your demolition gear, and prepare for the thrill of reducing structures to dust. Teardown is just another opportunity for Duke Nukem to show off his explosive talents. It's time to make a mess, blow things up, and remind the world why they call me the king of destruction. Let's rock, baby!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - A lot of potential, a lot of fun even as is, but poor description of this game makes it hard for me to currently give a Yes. If you are tentative on this, I suggest you read the rest of my review. (If you want to add me and ask questions, feel free but comment on my profile in a way that I know you aren't a bot.)First off, I know this game is in EA and I also enjoy it a lot. If you understand how this game works and like it, buy it! I bought it because it looked fun and I wanted to support these dev's. Teardown fails to tell you exactly what it is on the store page. It explains the clients and your business, but it doesn't explain the fact that it is all a time-trail based game, always 60 seconds, and focuses on running the quickest route to try and complete heists before the security helicopter comes and busts you. There are few actual demolition missions. The "Teardown" aspect of the game really does become minimal IMO as you go.Otherwise, you can destroy things on Sandbox or Challenge modes, but even for people with great CPU's and GPUs, beware of how laggy this game will become due to the physics of this game. Mass destruction can bring massive lag. (Also, if you are hoping for multiplayer in time with this, think again for the time being).The failure to explain this game fully and the lack of people actually calling out the lag issues that plague the destruction aspect of this game, requires me to not recommend this as of now. This has a lot of potential, but I don't think it is going where a lot of people want it to go because of the limits this type of engine brings to things like multiplayer and modding so far, as many of the mods bring on even more lag. Pros-Unique looks and physics.-Good mod-ability (however, be careful for lag).-Interesting and sometimes challenging Campaign. (Not too easy and sometimes hard). -A LOT of potential.Cons-Failure to explain the game well. -Lack of actually Tearing things Down. -Destruction can cause extreme lag, even on high end PC's. -Repetitive game-play without much of a sense of achievement.-A Campaign that for some may result in having to use guides to get through it.

_childDocuments_.review: Destruction sometimes is relieving.Excellent little puzzle and agility game in voxel with great graphics.Only downside: Performance/optimization and graphics settings. Game constantly and only uses 6% CPU on my Ryzen 9 5950X, so around 2 cores, and very frequently shows poor framerates. Sometimes my GPU is the bottleneck, but during action I'm CPU limited, frequently at 45 FPS or lower, even sometimes the game engine slows down time in order to keep up with physics. With one of the best CPUs out there, that's a shame that it's not utilized.Also there are no precise settings for graphics. You can only select between "low, medium, high", and it doesn't help with the framerate in my case, as it only increases framerate when there is no action going. You can downscale using game's engine, but it doesn't use any smart scaling technology (from AMD at least) to do it without horrible blur.Good point is if you got a dual or quad core, you'll still experience the same experience as I did with a higher end CPU. That said, even though that was uncomfortable, the rest of the game and gameplay was so good that I still had fun and finished the game. So I would of course recommend the game, but I think it's better to be warned about performance beforehand.

_childDocuments_.review: SO i went into this game with the expectation of oh i get to break stuff in a world that's all destructible (aside from a few things) and I'm just gonna goof around and see how the physics works. well i ended up playing a game about a man illegally stealing tools cars and paintings all while under the pressure of a timer, while also playing in a massive destructible physics built world. i gotta admit i didn't expect to enjoy this game as much as i do and for someone who is generally busy, putting a stream of 6 hours into a game is pretty crazy for recently purchasing it. my pros are that the game is a world where just about everything is destructible, and it gives you all sorts of ways to solve the challenges on the different levels. the graphics although blocky has a good background with very detailed water and sky with sun shafts. the levels are also tricky enough to make each feel challenging even when revisiting them. the game comes with a nice sandbox where you have unlimited tool uses and can just destroy everything in your path. Now the cons, although i do love this game there are some flaws like every other game in the world. The game is very intense on your machine. I have a gtx 1080 and on low settings i'm often getting 45 frames without doing anything and that fps tanks whenever there is a moderate amount of destruction. This sucks because for a game that's all about destroying your way through buildings i often find myself almost moving in slow motion because my frames would drop so hard. another flaw would be time limits, on most missions there is a time limit after you trigger an alarm and its always 60 seconds, never more and never less. i personally had no issues spending a bit of extra time managing my way through the game like that but it does make a handful of levels very frustrating and i can see why people are looking to change the time limit the game offers. i think with a more specifically tailored alarm system to each level or maybe an in game way to give yourself a little extra time would be great like destroying an alarm antennae would give you an extra 5-10 seconds. as for what i think the game should add would be primarily workshop mod support that would instantly give this game some longevity because as it stands there isn't really much that's gonna make me want to come back and play this over again besides maybe an itch for destruction. Mod support for new weapons to destroy the environment and maps made by the community would allow me to explore and play with new tools in new areas. there is a custom map maker already in the game and have yet to explore and play with that and until i do i will not comment on whether or not it is any good and if there's a way it can be improved.  OVERALL i think its a great game with lots of potential as an addition of workshop mod support would drastically increase the games value, but i would stay clear of it if your machine isn't very powerful. the levels are nice and i discover something new each time i play them but the alarm system has made me frustrated a few times.

_childDocuments_.review: Teardown is suprisingly a game where you don't do as much destruction as it may seem by the title.The key thing to know about this game is that the campaign, the most fleshed out part of the game, is a time trial where you must get to and collect key items in a minute, after an infinitely long planning period. There is a sandbox option and many mods that play more into the teardown aspect of Teardown, but the core gameplay is generally much more tactical, which can be off-putting if it's not your cup of tea.So how is the campaign? It's great. The missions present just enough challenge to not feel impossible, while also feeling very tight (5 seconds, most of the time <1 second left) when going for all side objectives, and it's satisfying creating a path that winds through these very well designed levels. Of course, not  level is a rush to the finish, but I'd be lying if it wasn't the most common.Level design is very key in a game like this. Good news: every map is great. While there's a lower quantity of maps, there's a high quality to each one, constantly changing across each mission with small touches that keeps it fresh. Everything is connected to allow the player to make their own path for each level while experimenting with the tools the game constantly gives you.By completing levels and doing side objectives, your rank increases, which gives you more items to mess with in every level; a rocket launcher, wooden planks, bombs, a leafblower, and a dozen or so more tools keeps the campaign from feeling too similar, and with some of the later side missions, you'll definitely want to use everything you have. Not every weapon or tool is useful, but it is generally solid.When it comes to the graphics... does anything really need to be said? This is fantastic.If the premise of the campaign sounds interesting, or you're down to just use this game as a sandbox, then play this game. It's a fantastic experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I have had a hard time getting into it due to motion sickness, but I have some tips on reducing it and making an otherwise very fun game playable:1) In the settings you can turn off head bobbing, tool/weapon swaying, motion blur and a few other things2) The game is quite intensive to run: if you don't think you could run it stably on low/medium/high then it will feel terrible in general, motion sickness or not. And as far as performance, I think it is well optimized for Steam Deck if that is your thing.3) Changing the FOV and zoom in level can make a big difference. 4) Getting stuck with vehicles can ramp up frustration that feeds into motion sickness. Levels seem to have a decent number of vehicles or alternate approaches, so if you are stuck just move on to some other vehicle/approach.5) There is a workshop and I have tried a mod supposedly helping motion sickness... not sure if it has done much beyond point #1 and #2 but it's something.6) General motion sickness tip: nothing wrong with doing it one level at a time then taking breaks.Overall, once I got a decent PC/Steamdeck and learned about those settings, it has gone from literally sickening to play to a sick game if you know what I mean. Still have to take breaks but the levels I have done so far are bit size chunks about the right length for me to do one or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the early access campaign. After having followed this game's development on Twitter since its early stages, I was so excited to finally get my hands on it. And I gotta say, this game is easily the most technologically impressive game I've ever had the pleasure of playing. The custom voxel ray-tracing renderer looks absolutely stunning and the destruction and physics of the game work beautifully. Together these factors provide an experience unlike anything else.Designing a game around such sandboxy concepts must've been a challenge though. But I gotta hand it to them, the idea of planning and preforming a heist in a fully destructible world works so well and the varied set of missions were a blast to play through. The bonus targets add plenty of replay value and I can't wait to go through and 100% all the missions. The available maps are large, open and distinct and the design of the game encourages getting familliar with and exploring each map, which was an aspect I really enjoyed.The player movement is nice and satisfying. I found that I had to turn some of the more motion sick inducing effects off in order to play this game but luckily all of that is already available as settings, so I was able to tune that experience to suit me. I also need to talk about the vehicle physics. They are among the best of any game I've played, only being beat out by full on racing games while being on par with or better than any other open world game launching for 3x the price. It's super impressive. My only complaint is that they don't always work that well uphill or through very non-uniform ground, so I hope to see that resolved. Aside from that, I love the vehicle physics in this game!Stability was great and the game didn't crash on me even once throughout the 14 hours I've played it. The only two finnicky things I've noticed is that you can't take screenshots of the game properly using PRT SC (but screen recording software works fine) and that physics turn a bit choppy when the game lags, although I know the developers are aware of and want to resolve the latter issue. Again, the game is in early access.The game is quite demanding in terms of GPU and CPU, but I gotta say that it runs very smoothly with stable frame rates and good preformance when not much is going on and with very predictable lag when there are many physics events that need to be calculated. There are no unexpected lag spikes or instabilities to be found here. The optimization work here is very solid, which is impressive considering the game is still in early access.In conclusion, if you like the concept of a fully destructible world where you can just mess around and steal some valueables, this game will be right up your alley. The $20 price tag for the game is a fair price for the 14 hours of gameplay I got out of the early access campaign already, but there will be even more content added before release, so you'll easily get your money's worth. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like what most people don't really mention is just how stunning the game looks. The game has beautifully crafted environments which almost feel real, despite them being built out of fixed-size 10cm voxels and (almost) no curves. The game takes place in a made-up municipality of Sweden, and even though I've never been there I could very nicely imagine it as a real place, both in aesthetic and how alive the places feel thanks to all the details. The raytraced graphics make for some really realistic lighting, which closely resemble the real thing, especially in the more natural landscapes. Sometimes I stand there and just... stare. It's almost like real photographs in some places.The weather and ambiance work together really well, with each map having it's own soundscape. They really did do their homework on this stuff, the sunsets, bright days, nights and everything feel... real. The murkiness of bad weather especially is captured amazingly, and along with some really well-fitting atmospheric music, the game truly has some of the most beautiful scenery I've ever experienced in a videogame.The attention to detail in some places is extraordinary: the walls have layers when shot, electronics have insides when wrecked, valuables are hidden in walls or under stairs, barrels spill decorative fluid when cracked open, snow melts away and vehicles leave tracks in it behind them... Even the little objects seemingly too small to be recognizable are still cutely and creatively mimicked with what little voxels available.Some objects and most signs have little text popups to them when hovered over, giving you details or your character's thoughts about them. These are all little things that add depth to the places and make every map feel truly alive, creating this little story in your head without ever encountering a single soul.The best part is that it's not just some pretty 3D scene render, it's a full-fledged game with really fun gameplay, great mods and amazing physics, and lots of replayability (sometimes I come back just to mess around, but it's also fun to 100% achievements).A lot of people complain about the campaign being too timer-focused, but not in the way you'd think. The most common mission type is a "heist", where you have marked objects you need to collect around various parts of the map in under 1 minute. However, you're given free reign and no time limit to prepare your route beforehand, so the way you'll collect them all is entirely up to you. This is where destruction comes in handy, as you'll be making huge bomb holes, plank bridges and repurposing props and cars to your advantage and create a shortest path between every collectible and your escape vehicle.I personally liked these missions. They're well-designed and definitely beatable, although they do require active problem solving, planning and platforming. I'd say the puzzle-like nature of the campaign is fitting, and way smarter than making the whole thing be "Destroy X amount of stuff, repeat", which you can always do in sandbox. You unlock new tools and you can upgrade them as you go, which makes progression feel fun.While these heists and their variations are what you'll be spending most of your time and brainpower on in the campaign, there's a lot of cool flavor missions with a different objective evenly sprinkled through. Some are easier and relaxed, while others are almost movie-grade chase scenes, without spoiling too much.If you're looking for extra, it's there. While you can complete most missions by only getting the required amount of objectives, there's usually more for the completionists. Sometimes, they can completely screw with your mind, forcing you to really think through your approach and route for hours. It's pretty rewarding when you get everything with barely just a few miliseconds left to spare.If it's too difficult however, there's options to ease the difficulty. You can adjust the time limits, ammo, or enable skipping of levels if they're too frustrating. There's also options to unlock every tool and map from the beginning for those looking to mess around in sandbox, which is great.

_childDocuments_.review: The whole premise of the game, destruction physics, is severely flawed. There is no structural integrity modeling, no collateral damage, there are invincible blocks that cannot be destroyed, the engines of vehicles can never be destroyed, and so on. With all those limitations, I fail to see how it's any better than regular game physics or even how it's any better than pre-calculated physics. There is no dynamism to the destruction. Don't expect to strategically place bombs to take out a building etc. So, destruction is not fun, what about the other aspects? The missions are generally meh, and their entertainment value seems to depend on the destruction itself, which is, as I've explained, not very good. The lighting in this game is perpetually grainy, even on the "High" settings. Maybe it's better at 4K (I'm playing at 1440p) but I doubt it's completely eliminated. The only way I could recommend this game is to buy it at a heavy discount, as a quick "play 10 minutes and quit" sort of game. Anything else, and you'll probably be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: The short version: This game seems like a lot of fun, but I can't enjoy it due to something about the game engine causing me awful nausea/motion sickness issues. There seem to be at least a handful of people in the same boat as I am from looking around online.The long version: I don't get motion sick playing FPS games, I just don't. I've been playing them for the better part of 20 years and this is the first game I've ever had an issue with like this (including a number of pretty intense VR games). I'm assuming it has something to do with how the game engine handles motion, but after about 10 minutes of moving around in-game I start to feel incredibly nauseous and need to stop. There are a few settings you can adjust in the menu (DoF, Lens Distortion, Motion Blur, Head Bob) to try to alleviate the issue, disabling all of them seemed to help a little bit but didn't come close to resolving the issue for me. The closest feeling I can compare this to is trying to play a first person VR game that was meant to be played standing up while seated, and with fluid movement instead of snap movement enabled. Something is just off about how the game handles the graphics of moving around and it really screws with me. It's a real shame too, as I love the concept of the game and really wish I could enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: As of right now, I cannot recommend the game due to a security risk.The developers recently added "featured mods" which downloads a ZIP file from their server, which contains XML and image files.This would be fine, if the developers were using HTTPS for communication, but at this point they are refusing to do that, due to it being "too complicated and requiring too many libraries".This is 2022, it is unacceptable to use HTTP for a public facing service that downloads content to a user's machine. It leaves the door open for man in the middle attacks (MITM)They proposed doing zip signing instead, but that will not do any good should a MITM attack occur resulting in a malicious file being downloaded (recall that there were exploits in the past that only required you to download a file, not interact with it, but simply download it, and the exploit relied on a vulnerability in the way Windows Explorer handled icons.) Even if signing was used, all it takes is a vulnerability to occur in the signing verification or even the extraction of the ZIP file (or perhaps one in the XML/image rendering library the game uses) to pwn your machine.Should all this change and they actually switch to using HTTPS, then I will remove this review, but in the meantime, if you do want to play the game, do so at your own risk, you'll likely be fine, but the risk is always there.Edit 2022-12-16: The domain they use for promos still doesn't support HTTPS.Edit 2023-11-10:So I wanna address a few things because some of the folks commenting here seem to be misunderstanding.Loading the game up, without ANY user interaction AT ALL, before the user even gets to the main menu, a call to the following URL is madehxxp : // promo.teardowngame . com/promo . php?version=<version number here> (commented out the replaced "tt" with "xx" so that no one accidentally clicks it)What gets returned is a link to a ZIP file in plain text that the game then automatically downloads and extracts.In this case it was hxxp : // promo.teardowngame . com/2023-11-01 . zip (again replaced "tt" with "xx" so no one clicks it)Without ANY interaction at all, without even downloading a mod, simply just launching the game, it makes an unencrypted (thus interceptable on unsecured networks, such as public WiFi networks, and let's not forget that because of things like laptops, and steam decks and whatnot, that the possibility of this is greater than 0%, because it's not unlikely that someone might decide to go to a coffee shop or something with their gaming device and play a bit of gaming while they wait for their order or whatnot) request through HTTP (and I have confirmed this with Wireshark).All it takes is someone intercepting that request and sending a spoofed response with a different URL, or hell even running a rogue network that points the promo domain to a different server to send back a malicious zip file (and this is possible because with http the client doesn't need to validate the server that is responding because it's unencrypted).Once again, YOU LITERALLY DO NOT EVEN HAVE TO INTERACT WITH MODS/THE FEATURED MODS BUTTON ON THE MENU OR DO ANYTHING AT ALL BESIDES LAUNCH THE GAME.If you don't believe me, open up windows explorer, navigate to "%localappdata%\Teardown", look for "promo.txt" and a folder called "promo", delete both of them, and then launch the game but don't do anything, and then look at the folder again. You'll see that it will have recreated the folder and file you just deleted, without you ever doing anything to prompt it to redownload other than just launching the game.Hell if you open up promo.txt you'll see the URL, and you'll see it is still using HTTP.I can understand how some people might think it's not a big deal, but when a game gives you no control over disabling it from phoning home (because that's what it is doing, it's connecting to a server that is controlled by the developers to get information about featured mods) and it's not even doing that over an encrypted connection, it's a ticking time bomb just waiting for someone to get hacked.It doesn't matter if the developers hand pick the mods themselves they feature, that it isn't the problem, the problem is the request is not secure and you'll never truly know if the response you got back, was truly from the server owned by the developers, or a malicious third party who did a MITM (Man-In-The-Middle) attack on your connection.And yes, they still aren't using HTTPSEdit 2023-11-19:Checked the latest version, and to the surprise of no one, they still aren't using HTTPS. You'd think with all the extra money they're charging, maybe they could afford to spend some time to actually implement secure communication in something that is automatic and can't be disabled by the end user.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything in this game is fun, except 80% of it's campaign. I really want to love this game, it looks fantastic, plays great, runs... fine I suppose, but the big sticking point, the major flaw it has, is all the timed missions. Now look, don't get me wrong, I understand why they're important, but in a game like this, they aren't forcing hard decisions, they aren't promoting enjoyable playstyles, instead, they legitimately punish you for having fun. If you go in blowing things up, crashing cars all willy nilly, running in guns blazing, you instantly lose. The only way to win most of these levels is to spam quicksave as you slowly drive a car to a specific spot so that you can use it in your master plan. And if it so much as bumps into a bush you need to hit quickload, cause that damage may very well ruin your master plan. In a game about destroying things, you are forced to strategize and plan, and after that, if you destroy a single thing all is ruined. I didn't come into this game to play chess, I came in it to destroy things and de-stress. All the missions involving destroying stuff, fantastic, it perfectly fits the games target audience and works to the game's strengths, but the timed missions flaunt all the flaws. Like the fact that your character moves like molasses and cars are terrible to drive and control, since they have a tendency to brush an immovable object and lose all momentum and break. I have seen a plethora of streamers and YouTubers just cheat in all the items, since no one wants to slog through the campaign. But I guarentee you that by either making all the timed segments more lenient or remove them entirely then many of them would much more likely play through it, the beginning missions set things up, the progression of your house is grand world building, but I just don't want to keep slamming my face into this timed wall. I think one of the best levels I have played so far in this is the one I recently beat, it's the one where you need to get the painting while making sure the lightning doesn't catch everything on fire and set off the alarm. That level shows what all the timed missions should be, missions where the timer isn't inevitable, but rather a hazard that can be avoided, imagine if instead of being forced to sit and stare at the map while slowly crawling around it just to find out the fastest way to get all the main objectives, you simply had to get the items carefully, like if you broke something or did something incorrectly, like broke a window, caught something on fire, tripped a wire. That would be far more engaging than, "If YoU tOuCh MaIn ObJeCtIvE aLaRm Go WeE wOo". I don't want to play this game due to how annoying it's getting, I came to have fun and de-stress, not to plan things out and waste time plotting a long arduous course of action that only barely works with perfect execution and doesn't account for the fact that I haven't gotten any of the optional objectives for any of the missions from car wash and on. Please fix the timers or add an option to remove them, since it takes something that should be fun, and makes it boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Teardown’s campaign is not what you think it is - this is primarily a timed heist puzzle game that is not focused on destruction at all. It's more like "blow a few holes in walls and set up the perfect route to grab a bunch of items in 60 seconds." Or "dodge robots with lasers" for some reason.There are very few missions that are focused on the destruction mechanics/voxel physics, which is, you know, the entire reason this game matters at all.It's also worth noting that the "physics" in this game are not very good. As other reviewers have pointed out, structures do not collapse realistically. Buildings are left standing from a single block. Destruction occurs only from physical contact rather than any sort of weight given to objects.Overall, this game's campaign is very disappointing and has huge wasted potential. However, I do think the voxel destruction mechanics in Teardown will inspire other games in the future that are actually fun to play and challenge you to demolish things in creative ways. For now, we'll just have to wait.inb4 "Play Sandbox": NO. Sandbox is not fun. Sandbox will never be fun. I don't want to play sandbox ever in any game for any reason. I do not care for games that give you zero incentive to play. I want missions that challenge me to destroy things in creative ways, and that is exactly what this game does NOT give you.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game for over 1 year now. Now that I've gotten to play it I'm absolutely loving it. The physics of the the voxels and smoke are incredibly satisfying and the missions are enjoyable and have replayability.My two biggest complaints are:1) The game runs terribly. I have a very good GPU and CPU. I can play nearly any game at high settings in 1440p but I need to run this game in 1080p to stay above 60fps, which is fine. The part that is difficult to deal with is if you try to do too much, the fps will tank. The game is still playable but it's a bit of a bummer when you run a boat into a house and the game starts to crawl.2) The missions are very repetitive. Dont get me wrong, I've been really enjoying the campaign. However, nearly every mission is "collect these things, once you grab the first one a timer will start and you need to get the rest and escape before time runs out." There is a different enjoyable kind of mission every once in a while but the vast majority of them are doing basically the same thing on a few different maps.All in all, I love this game and I'm really looking forward to the future of it. I'm hoping the Developers can make some performance tweaks and add some variety to the missions but the basic concept they have right now is unlike anything else out there.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Revolutionary and fun but gets quite boring.Graphics:It's definitely an acquired taste. If you're alright with Minecraft/pixelated type graphics, it'll look really nice for you.Storyline:It's small and just exists to create some interesting missions. There's not much to it in all honesty.Price:The price is absolutely perfect at $20.Difficulty:It's relatively easy as long as you have a lot of spare time. Quick saving and testing things will be your best friend.AI:It quite surprised me for this game to have AI but it was a great addition. They're not the smartest, only existing to be a challenge (and always include a big weakness)Cutscenes:I don't remember any cutscenes.Fun:The game is absolutely amazing when you first play it, but it slowly decays over time. Imagine a world where you can destroy anything and do anything you want - it's amazing! After a while it just ends up getting boring. You can either do the same missions again and again or just destroy things. There's not much to it.Sounds/Music:Basic but fitting.Replayability:Absolutely replayable... for about 10 hours. I completed the main campaign and then smashed things for about 10 hours before it got extremely boring.Controls:Basic but good. Not over complicated and not over simplified.Performance:It runs as expected, extremely stable when small things are broken/nothing is broken and major lag as more and more physics objects are active. Overall, though, it ran really well for me on an i7-7700 and GTX 1060 6gbModding:Pretty much anything exists for the game due to a really active modding community. There's maps, weapons, missions, code mods, etc etc. I really appreciate when devs like Tuxedo Labs include mod support.Selling Out:The game comes whole, there are no additional purchases.Similar Games:It's like if BeamNG and Minecraft had a baby.Bugs:- You can fall through a few maps- Random crashes

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings on this game but cant say I would recommend it due to how the game performed for me. It is a pretty fun game and I think the right person could get a lot of fun and hours out of it but my personal experience wasn't amazing.My problem was the game performance... I have a pretty decent build (i7-9700K, RTX 2080S and 16GB of RAM). I started with the game on 1440p and high settings. Upon demolishing buildings my FPS drops to unplayable until everything settles. To be more specific, on sandbox mode I drove a tractor through all the brick walls causing the whole building to collapse and my FPS went from 60 to 4 until the rubble settled. So I went and turned the graphics down to medium and restarted the game just in case. Upon trying the same building collapse test my frames still dropped to around 10 FPS. So I turned the graphics down to low and repeated the same process and got about 14 FPS this time.I know this probably sounds like I am just being picky but I feel like in a game that is meant for destruction I should be able to knock one building down without serious FPS drops. My fear is that if I am getting significant frame drops in my first two hours of playing then whats going to happen when I get better at the game and want to cause some major destruction???Once again its a cool idea of a game and if it runs good for you or you don't mind frame drops then you might love it. It just wasn't the case for me personally.Edit- I don't know if my problem was game related anymore... A few days after writing this review I determined my CPU cooler is most likely starting to fail. I've noticed higher temperatures and lower performance on games I frequently play and its progressively getting worse. I ordered a new cooler and if the installation goes good and fixes my performance issue I will definitely give this game another try and updated reviewEdit 2- Got a new CPU cooler and my computer is running great now. Unfortunately I still get major frame drops even on lowest settings on Teardown. I was getting 12 FPS just driving a boat into a building on sandbox. The map was fresh, there was no fires and nothing else was going on that should be causing frame drops. Adding fire to the equation made it even worse. All my other games run great. The frame drops make this unplayable for me. It would be a cool game but based on how it performs I still can not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Teardown is an amazing game. I could just stop there but i don't even feel that gives this game justice. What even is this game? Teardown in it's simplest form, is a game about heists and other similar missions that utilizes it's physics based engine to get the best time with some story\lore sprinkled in missions. Now, Hows the story? Teardowns's story is pretty decent, it aint the best, but it's good. It makes sense, it's cohesive and the way it delivers the story to you is a little unique. Most of the story is delivered to you through several ways, wether it be by giving you pieces of the story through storytelling in the missions or continuing the story in the emails, or maybe it's using the TV and the news stories about your heists. I'm not going to explain or give many tidbits of the story here as I believe you should experience it for yourself. Okay that's cool but whats the game play like? Like I've mentioned, this game's missions are mainly composed of heists, where you are dropped in a mission and are given a specific set of items to steal\get rid of. However there are other type of missions, including: pure destruction of building (usually without time with maybe one exception), "killing" missions, "camera?" mission, "weather" mission, plain just stealing mission. Note: these have been left ambiguous so you can figure out what they actually are with only an idea. I mentioned "destruction" but how? Well put it simply, the game gives you "tools" that you can use to destroy or alter your environment to make your runs faster, or more fun. This game also has a sandbox mode, and EXTENSIVE MODDING CAPABILITIES! I hope this has been enough said, please get the game its good.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting idea for a game, somewhere caught between Garry's Mod and Minecraft (with a touch of Space Engineers thrown in for good measure). Structures, materials, and particles all behave surprisingly realistically. Thanks to the size and customisation of the voxels, the environments can be much more detailed than expected. The only thing you may be left looking for with this game is more comprehensive weapons/tools/ways to blow everything up, as the vanilla tools are rather sparse. The workshop community crucially continues to expand the options for worlds and ways to wreck them, but quality mods can be few and far between as well.Light a fire in a building and enjoy the destruction. Rain ordinance from above with an AC-130 (a la COD 4). Explore detailed worlds like the Dursley's House from Harry Potter. Hide from robots in an office building, etc. Lots of variety in this one. 8.0/10

_childDocuments_.review: Teardown is an absolute gem in the gaming world that offers an incredibly unique and satisfying experience. From its captivating blocky physics to its challenging missions, this game has all the ingredients for an addictive and exhilarating adventure. As a player who loves sandbox games and the freedom they provide, Teardown has left an indelible mark on me.First and foremost, the physics in Teardown are nothing short of phenomenal. The destructible environments are brought to life with an unmatched level of realism and precision. Watching walls crumble, objects shatter, and debris fly all around you is an absolute joy. Every move you make feels impactful, and the attention to detail in the physics engine is simply awe-inspiring.The missions in Teardown are meticulously designed to keep you on your toes. Each task presents a unique challenge, demanding strategic thinking, problem-solving, and creative approaches. Whether you're planning a heist, executing a daring escape, or causing chaos for your own amusement, the missions offer a wide variety of objectives that will keep you engaged for hours on end.One of the highlights of Teardown is its modding community. The game actively encourages and supports mods, and the community has risen to the challenge brilliantly. With an extensive selection of user-created content, including new levels, tools, vehicles, and more, the possibilities are virtually limitless. The mods breathe new life into the game, providing endless replayability and opening up a whole world of creative and sandbox experiences.While Teardown may not be primarily designed as a multiplayer game, the developer's decision to focus on the single-player experience is understandable. The sheer complexity and intricacy of the physics engine would undoubtedly pose challenges when it comes to multiplayer synchronization. Nonetheless, it's hard not to imagine the sheer joy of playing with friends, wreaking havoc together, and collaboratively devising ingenious plans. However, the game's core strengths lie in its solo adventure, and it excels at delivering an immersive and unforgettable experience in that regard.In conclusion, Teardown deserves every bit of praise it receives. The blocky physics, challenging missions, and the vibrant modding community make it a standout title in the gaming landscape. While the lack of multiplayer functionality is understandable, it doesn't detract from the game's overall brilliance. If you're a fan of physics-based gameplay, strategic challenges, and the ability to unleash your creativity, Teardown is an absolute must-play. Brace yourself for an explosive and gratifying journey that will keep you coming back for more. This game is a solid 10/10 in my book!

_childDocuments_.review: I think what is best about this game is the way it forces you to think differently about how to complete your objectives than you’re used to. Traditionally, video games would have you sprinting, jumping and shooting in a very specific way to meet your goal in a certain time. Teardown does not work like this. You essentially have unlimited time to make the map work for your plan. Blast a hole in that wall, move the vehicle there to crash into the target to be destroyed, put explosives here to make this portion of the building collapse. Once you’re done with the campaign, there’s so many good mods to enjoy. There are mods that include entire new maps and game mods and of course new destructive tools to use to destroy things.

_childDocuments_.review: First half of the game can be a little repetitive, but it gets much more varied and fun in the 2nd half! Besides that this is easily one of my top games of the year. _childDocuments_.review: The game functions on two levels: without mods and with mods.  Without mods, you have an incredible, tuned, clever, witty, focused game that leaves you scratching your head in total confusion at some points and staggered with awe and overflowing satisfaction at others. _childDocuments_.review: I can not express how much fun this game is. If you are in doubt, just get the game - its well worth it, especially on sale.Teardown gets you thinking in ways that other tactical and heist speed-run games can only dream of achieving. There is a strong sense of progression as you climb the ladder towards becoming a master demolitions-thief. The game provides you with a slew of useful tools, weapons and utility constructs that you will find all sorts of goofy ways to use to shorten your time crunched runs. The vehicles all have unique design, function and handling making missions feel very 'spy hunter-y' when behind the wheel. This game is masterfully crafted. In the future, I would love to see a multiplayer 'point capture', 'capture the flag' mode or 'race to the chopper' style missions.
_childDocuments_.name: Teardown

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this would be just a big smashy sandbox, and if that's what you want, you can totally get that here.What I wasn't expecting was an extremely clever series of missions that make really full use of the abilities allowed by the voxel engine this game is built around. You are given a multitude of tools, but have to manage their ammo per mission as a resource you have to spend. Shaping every map to the most efficient route, punctuated by intense speed runs through the maps to hit your objectives and get out before the cops show up.I was not expecting a really engaging heist game wrapped around a destruction sand box. This is so much more than just an engine to blow things up, the campaign is well made, interesting missions, with interesting tools, that lets you feel smart for carving out the fastest path through the map.It's also surprsingly beautiful given the voxel based graphics. Sharp crisp lighting, Well directed art design, soft windy snow, moody rainy. It's all really well done and helps immerse you in the mission you find yourself on. The music is fantastic as well, catchy and fun. The perfect cool backdrop to a smooth heist.The writing is really strong as well. the characters you work for well defined, and when you start realizing your playing every side, it's serves as a nice savy layer of humor, where you get to just keep being the middle man, and collecting all the cash as different factions tear each other apart. Also the enviromental story telling is engaging as well. seeing your base expand and get nicer as you progress, revisiting old maps that have changed in subtle (sometimes drastic) ways, usually due to your actions.It would have been easy to slap a sandbox together, give you some tools, and let the game be fun for an hour or two. Even sit back and just let modders build the game for you.The Devs of this game were not content with that option. They went above and beyond and created an addicting, engaging, funny, semi-puzzle heist game built around destroying your enviroment in clever and specific ways that somehow ends up being more than the sum of it's part. Very addicting, very fun, I keep coming back to it.Workshop support has also basically guaranteed that this game will still have legs in the future, even after you finish it's length, wonderfully crafted campaign. AND ITS STILL IN EARLY ACCESS. IT'S ONLY GOING TO GET BIGGER AND BETTER FROM HER.I highly recommend picking this up if you like heists, destruction, puzzles, or speed runs. Especially for only 20 bucks, that's a steal. Looking forward to more from this game AND these Devs in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Teardown

_childDocuments_.review: If physics and destruction are your thing, this game is for you.There is a decent little story to give some purpose to the destruction you're doing, without being cumbersome with hours of dialogue. The story comes in the form of reading emails from various characters that you'll do business with.You unlock new gadgets along the way, and some can be upgraded if you wish. Upgrades cost money, and you earn money through jobs and stealing valuable items scattered throughout the world on jobs. The game gets more difficult pretty quickly as alarm systems get introduced. This is where you may get frustrated if you're a completionist. In order to obtain maximum points on levels with alarms, you'll have 60 sec once the first alarm goes off to finish the rest of the objectives and exit before you're caught. If working against the clock isn't your thing (it's not mine), you can adjust the alarm time up to 2 minutes maximum. This really helps if you are more interested in the destruction and creativity than competing with time. Overall, a very fun, easy to pick up and play game with plenty to do and a lot of attention to detail.

_childDocuments_.review: I generally enjoyed this creative sandbox destruction game, but it has 3 fatal flaws. First the levels are big and walking around is super slow. There's no sprinting. You have to explore a lot to case out the level before even starting to get creative and it is much more tedious than it needed to be. Secondly, when you break things you are left with a lot of tiny voxel debris that catches on car wheels, blocks movement, etc... Cleaning that all up by hand was super tedious. You don't unlock a leaf blower until a good ways in. Thirdly the save system is terrible. You can save on a mission, but when you restart the game you are in your main base. If you try to load your save it won't work. Loading only works if you are in the mission that was saved. So when you restart the game you have to re-enter the same mission, which will be reset, and then reload your save. Just have a continue button so people can play a bit, leave and easily return to exactly where they were.Thumbs up despite the flaws due to the excellent level design, fun tools, and limitless destruction. Plus there were mods that helped make the game less tedious. Would love to see more like this.

_childDocuments_.review: As long as your PC handles it, it's definitely worth every penny.This game is VERY heavy on your hardware.Check specs! It won't run on Intel HD graphics, and even if it starts, expect glitchfest (color bleeding and stuff).Requires MORE than 2GB VRAM (graphics RAM), or you will not be able to load or play on later, bigger maps (it will either crash on load, or just after you try destroying something).Also, due to AMD's poor OpenGL handling (apparently), the game has more stable FPS and generally performs on Nvidia GPUs.Now with technical checks out of the way, the gameplay consists of two stages (depending on the scenario): preparation and execution. Most of the missions are timed, and the timer starts once you break/steal/tamper with one of the objectives. Until then, you can "terramorph" the environment to your liking, to enable you to collect/destroy objectives in the fastest possible time, or at least within the 60sec time window. You have one quicksave slot (tied to the currently played mission, you can't exit the game and load it after relaunch, at least not without slight messing around with files).Both parts are very enjoyable in their own way. Preparation phase can take hours (if you want, to ensure your success on the first try and don't know the map enough) but if you know what you're doing, it can take less than 10 minutes. The second one, you can restart from quicksave as many times as you want to either fix minor problems with your route or just your own small execution mistakes.There is a short but interesting story with specific kind of humor (safe for kids, but they might not get it), accompanying progression (level/tool unlocking). You can also find valuables that will then permanently disappear and add money to your virtual wallet, which you can then spend on tool upgrades. This one can be counted as its own game, because there are so many things hidden in either plain sight or interesting places, like . Be aware that while most of the valuables are indestructible, things like paintings hanging on the wall might be damaged when tearing the wall down, so you should look around searching for things in plain sight first, before going "deeper".There is also a sandbox mode, which gives you the tools and maps you unlocked, with infinite ammo, to have fun with.Another mode is "create", which allows you to run your downloaded mods (although in not-so-user-friendly way, you need to replace one of the existing 5 example mods' folders) or use the XML/Lua editor (like VSCode) and MagicaVoxel to create your own (mostly by modifying examples or looking for modding resources on the official Discord).Better mod support (both tools and more Lua bindings and XML examples) are (hopefully) coming in the next content update.Modders are already doing a pretty good job on this.TL;DR: Ton of fun, huge replay value due to both existing maps being solvable in multiple ways and modding community working hard, very nice physics, awesome lighting (due to the game being fully `raytraced`) and hours of gameplay in the official missions and exploration. Just get it (and if it doesn't start, seek help on Discord or get a refund).Oh, and more content is coming in the "Part 2"... (apparently for free)
