_childDocuments_.review: This game truly deserves its 'Overwhelmingly Positive' rating.The amount of content crammed into this game is completely insane. You have freeroam / sandbox modes, challenging time-based infiltration missions, destruction based modes, and of course, unlimited modding capabilities. Love that the Steam Workshop is put to use in this game. If there was no modding, it would still be a great game, it just wouldn't be a fantastic game.The game only recommends you need 4 GB RAM, and this is true, to some extent - as I've played the main content on my old 2013 MSI GX70 gaming laptop. But, if you intend on playing custom environments, if you don't have 16GB RAM, or more - you might encounter performance difficulties. My rig is: i9, 16GB RAM, RTX 3080, 5 TB SSD.Certain custom levels will lag severely when you perform certain actions - example - there is a mod w/ 3 tall apartment building towers - in each of these towers is hundreds of physics objects - when I knocked this tower over, w/ all of its objects, my game went from about 120 FPS to about 3-5 FPS. This isn't really the dev's issue, as they had no way to know that such large and complex structures would be made. Keep in mind, that you need a pretty strong rig to play many of the custom environments. My fave custom area is probably the massive working jet that you can download - the game even simulates getting sucked out of a plane, despite planes not being present in the main campaign made by the dev. This just goes to show the modding opportunities this game has. Fire is super cool in this game - it devours buildings in the most believable way I've seen fire presented in a video game. Fires will eat buildings apart, often burning all the flammable items, and leaving a big concrete skeleton behind. Fires will burn for hours, if you allow them to - or, you can try to extinguish the flames w/ your fire extinguisher. Probably the best fire-fighting sim game ever made, if you choose to play it in that fashion.But yeah, if you're buying this for the custom levels, PLEASE make sure you have at least 16GB RAM - the game is a lot more resource intensive than you may think at first.The game's destruction physics are voxel-based, and this allows for extremely precise destruction - you can use blowtorches,  hammers, rocket launchers, air strikes (mod), meteors (mod), guns of various types and distinctions, basically you can do next to anything. Drive a car strapped w/ C4 into a building, and blow it up? You can.Call in an AC130 to manually fire shells of different sizes into that small town? You can.Jetpack from house to house tossing grenades on each roof? You can.Shoot out a mall's windows w/ a minigun? You can.Knock down a wall to reach something on the other side? You can.This game's main feature is its freedom. In terms of destruction, you can do essentially whatever you want, the options are truly endless. This is the dream game I wanted ever since I played Red Faction: Guerrilla, those many years ago. So many games say they allow you infinite freedom, but that's total BS - this game truly lets you do whatever you want.Cannot recommend this game enough, it is gorgeous, the gameplay is dope, the only thing I would like is a PvP mode - as the game has such a multitude of weapons, and destruction capabilities, a PvP deathmatch mode could be REALLY cool. Imagine gunning hundreds of rounds into a building, while your buddy is inside trying to take cover - only for said buddy to hunker down, and call in an airstrike on you. It'd be cool if Tuxedo Labs did this, or if the modders made something like this. The game has a lot more potential in this regard.The game is 100% worth the asking price, don't even wait for it to be on sale, it is certainly worth your time at 22.79 CAD.Can't wait to see what this dev will do in the future!Cheers.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, first off, this game is a masterpiece,  if you have a tiny amount of imagination you can squeeze so much out of this. This is part 1 and I have 30 hours in it. 1. You will need a good pc to run this, some people say that they cant run it above 45 fps on a 2080 ti, I run it on 100% render scaling at 1080p and I get above 60 fps on a 1660 ti2. The missions are great, the basic premise is the same for most of them, but you have to execute them in different ways each time. Whether its stealing a safe or stealing cars. Some people say its repetetive, but every time the setting is slightly different which lets you execute your plan in many different ways.3. The sandbox is good, but there isn't as much fun to be had in it compared to the campaign because the map you select is always the same and you cant change the weather. Does that mean I don't have a ton of time in it? Hell no. I have spent probably 1/3 of my time in the sandbox.4. The collectibles system is great. I wish you made money from doing levels but making it so that you have to search for money to upgrade is so good. It rewards you for searching the map, and I have found fun ways to execute missions because of it. There are a ton of secrets as well but i'm not going to spoil them because its fun to find it yourself.Now, my conclusion to this essay: I love this game, about 138 people have complained (at the time of writing this) about a lot of things that are mostly their fault, like not looking at the minimum requirements to run it, or just focusing on completing the mission, this game is about doing whatever you want, mess around, try speedrunning, and do dumb things because that is the fun part of this game. When you blow open a door and don't realize that you just lit the building on fire, you walk in and then the fire alert starts to go and you have to frantically put out a fire so that it doesn't set off the alarm. When you try and load a vehicle on to a boat and the vehicle crashes through the deck and plummets into the ocean. When you try to drive a truck through a building and hit an explosive, which collapses the roof on the car, trapping you. As you can see there is a lot of ♥♥♥♥ that can happen. Pick this game up when it goes on sale or something or get it right now. You will not regret it if you just mess around a lil bit. You will be hooked and keep the memories forever.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good. Main campaign did sorta throw me for a loop though. The game builds the expectation from its trailers that you are going to be doing heists in a highly destructible setting, basically voxel GTA. But this also came with the expectation you'd be facing guards and such. The campaign is not that at all.A very large potion of the levels are you stealing things that trigger an alarm countdown the moment the first object is stolen. But means up till you steal the first item you're free to do whatever you want. you can cause mass destruction if you want. as long as you do not disturb the items you are supposed to steal. This makes the majority of the game "pre-planning" setting up the environment in a way you can most efficiently steal all the objects in time. There's also no guards or anyone stopping you from doing this (which I am going to be 100% honest here) which feels weird, and almost like they didn't want to code guards to a degree. They do have levels later where you have to dodge helicopter fire and deal with drone guards so my first thought does get debunked there and I revise it to more they didn't want ultra violence in the game... Its ok I guess, does feel like something is missing any time you're playing however, and makes the game feel uncanny creepy empty. Like any moment you're gonna get a fnaf jump scare.That being said. Once you adjust to the different style of the game its pretty fun. Its fun coming up with solutions and "making your own door" to accomplish them. I also do love the dev included a timer adjust option that work as a game's basic difficulty adjust. you can take time off the limit if you wanna challenge yourself or add time if you just wanna have fun. They also as mentioned above, you'll deal with helicopters and drones so the challenges do vary here and there to try to keep things interesting. The campaign does start to feel long in the tooth though and it could have probably been shortened a couple levels, but this is personal taste.For those that just wanna watch stuff go boom, we have the workshop, and hoo boy was there a lot of community support for this one. Plenty of new maps and tools to use. even over powered one. you wont be disappointed here.Nice little fun game, interesting concept, with a workshop to extend the life a bit, all for a reasonable price. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: The physics of Teardown are super impressive and the sandbox mode is definitely worth the package for most people, especially with the extensive modding community but what I appreciated most was how the physics played a role in the campaign. This is a fantastic immersive sim that prompts you to use your creativity and versatility through excellence and I appreciated how difficult it was. Despite its small amount of levels, most missions remix and change the settings making it feel fresh all over again and some of these levels are incredibly well designed. The progression system is also fantastic and the amount of destruction/traversal options unlocked by the end of the game makes you feel like a completely new character. While most people will probably skip this mode to go straight to the sandbox mode, the structured single-player content here felt like the real star of the show and I can easily recommend this to any fans of immersive sim games like I am.

_childDocuments_.review: I realize my playtime will seem way too short to make a judgement based on, I would argue that what I perceive as the big flaw is so core to what I would expect from such a game that the playtime is irrelevant, your view on its relevance in your purchasing decision is of course what matters. This game is somewhat obviously centered around the oddly satisfying feeling of seeing buildings and other constructions brought to ruin through one individual's demolition of a built structure's most crucial structural features.Except not, in the first campaign mission I saw the second story of a small house being held up by nothing except for a window frame (not sure if the glass was still there, might've been the crucial egg white of this construction cake). I'm sorry, but Red Faction: Guerrilla could do that in 2009. I'm guessing the key difference that makes Teardown incapable of this with more than 10 years of improvements in computing is their use of voxel-based physics engine, I'm no expert on the subject but I would guess that this decision is a good one when physics-modeling is what you're building your whole game around. What I wonder personally is why make this game if the experience becomes more akin to a 2 y/o destroying (disassembling) a lego castle rather than an actual demolition engineer (not sure of the right title?)? The devs have stated modelling structural integrity would halve your FPS, probably true I'm just a gamer so what do I know, but I again feel the need to ask why did the game have to be made? My best guess is the devs didn't know of these issues before they started development, and by the time they realized they had enough fans they (correctly) deduced it didn't matter.I guess that's the note I'd like to end on; I'm glad that an unique game is being enjoyed by many and the devs probably don't need to bother with my thoughts, but if you think you're going to get an experience similar to videos of real buildings being demolished you should have a look at Red Faction: Guerrilla instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Teardown is a game that, though I enjoy well enough, I believe has a bit of missed potential (Either that, or it's just not for me.) I believe that this game lends itself best to the demolition mechanic, given the fully destructible world and the many tools you have available to you. Despite this, it's actually quite rare that the game focuses on these mechanics. Rather than being a game about demolition, Teardown ends up being more about speed, and stealth. More often than not, you are trying to steal a bunch of items from across the map before the timer runs out, using demolition as a means to make your runs faster and easier rather than as the main point of the game. I had plenty of fun playing through the game's missions, and actually quite enjoyed the helicopter missions, but despite this, I found that I had more fun on the few missions that simply asked you to demolish a building. No time limit, no gimmicks, just demolition. While the sandbox mode does exists for this reason, it feels less satisfying when you're demolishing stuff at random rather than ticking off targets from a checklist. Put simply Teardown is an enjoyable game, but one that offers speed-running gameplay rather than relaxing mindless demolition. Keep in mind what you're looking for before you buy. If you want the relaxing checkbox ticking missions that I was looking for, I'd recommend something more along the lines of Power Washing Simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my new favorite games. While there are plenty of explanations why this game is awesome, i want to shed some light on a few issues I see in the game. -No voxel stress calculations--Entire buildings can be held up by only one voxel connection, regardless of material type or any other factor that would add stress to the connection. Not only is this silly, but its frustrating when you need to search for one little voxel you need to destroy.-Map variety--Some of the maps feel the same, and there's only 6 maps to really play with. I understand they are trying to have everything somewhat similar as they all take place in the same region, but its a little sad we didn't get more variety in the map options. (mods aren't the solution to this issue! i'm reviewing the base game!)-Vehicle vision stuttering--Suprisingly, this game has absolutely amazing handling vehicles, they drift, wheel spin, and the tire smoke is the best I've ever seen in a game so far. However, when driving, your camera doesn't smoothly follow the car, it jitters like crazy and makes it rather difficult to drive precisely. it's not an issue normally, but on the mission where you have to set a lap time on the track under 20 seconds, it's a little frustrating to crash into walls because of how jittery your vision is. That mission was still fun as heck though.-Alarms. On almost every mission--I understand why alarms are needed, but it gets boring because all the missions start playing out very similarly when they all are basically "complete everything before the timer ends after the first object is touched." getting 100% on these missions requires a lot of prep work (e.g: breaking walls to make more direct paths, wood plank bridges, spray painting the optimal route), which i'm not opposed to, but i'd be lying if i said it make the game more enjoyable by having so many of these missions in a row.-Game difficulty is too easy to change--I know this is an odd complaint, but hear me out, I ended up playing the game with the alarm time modifier set at 60 extra seconds, which was enjoyable, but it made some missions too easy and some missions still exceedingly difficult. I don't like falling back on options like this when i'm facing difficult missions in games, and yet i used it exactly that way. I know its my fault too but sometimes game developers/designers need to protect players from themselves. It seems lazy for the difficulty to just be customizable like that instead of having proper difficulty settings, or better still, dynamically scaling difficulty. overall, this is still an amazing game and if you don't already own it, and have a system able to play it, you really need to get it. It's way worth the asking price even with the issues i've described, and i cant wait to see where the campaign goes, because its actually a very intresting story so far.

_childDocuments_.review: i found it hard to recommend this game but i have to say the pros just out way the cons in this situation. i grabbed this game in the summer sale as it's been in my wishlist for a while and figured it was time to pull the trigger. whenever i tried to read the reviews they were always either comedic or not very telling of what the game actually brought to make it so positive! the game starts very well and the mission keep gaining difficulty which forces you to plot out your runs as generally every mission consists of you gathering things around the map then returning to the vehicle to escape, normally triggering a timer as soon as you have picked up the first item. this was perfectly fine for the most part and the missions are generally really good.what really became a drag for me was the later missions where it seemed to me that the level designers/devs seemed to run out of ideas on how to spice up the levels so then just hit you with the classic, "you've just spent all your time gaining these weapons/tools to help make paths easier, but now we've had to send you to this location where, aw, no, you have access to only your very basic items and at most you might need to find some others dotted around the map" this lazy sort of mission design just really sucked after going through a decent flow of standard missions and just really started to drag the game down for me. this, combined with the fact that as far as i can tell, the character you play in the game is human, seems to carry any object in the game as though they have stringy stretch arm strong arms that have been pulled from one end of the street to the other and no longer come into their body. this in itself would be ok, however due to the lack of level ideas in the later game, they start dumping levels of "carry this items from that side of the map to here" which is fine if it's not for the stringy arms and the fact you can only for some reason hold an item as though you are pinching it with a single bit of contact and have to walk around looking at the sky to avoid dragging it/catching it on any and all surfaces!! the other issue is just generally buggyness/ in game issues such as being in a vehicle, trying to exit when near a wall then just being put outside the map with no way back in other than to quick load or restart the mission. these thankfully don't happen all to often, but they do happen and can be a right pain in the hole.some items in the game are quite strange in their structure like propane tanks have all the strength of wet paper and the slightest bump blows them up, yet giant vats of nitroglycerin can be booted about like an old mitre ball at a game of 5s with no ill effect. ALSO! having no toggle to fire button is a bit of a miss step. after completing this game and mucking about with the minigun, i feel this game has literally crippled my hand! can you please add that simple feature? it would mean i could actually play in sandbox mode with feeling like i have to cancel any future plans for my life that involve my hands!!!besides allllll the problems and the downward spiral towards the end, this game is still a joy to play (generally the earlier missions) with the ability to come back later with better tools and try and beat your initial run time/ just blow the living daylights out of things in sandbox mode. the fact that you can driver literally anything that looks driveable, smash anything to bits with the right tool and truly have free roam of maps to create a path to complete the mission on how you think it should be done is a welcome sight and for that i do recommend this game. i would look forward to some sort of DLC or similar with more missions etc if we can just leave the really annoying grab item A and take the escape vehicle nonsense at the door please!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a smash and grab robbery simulator, emphasis on the smash. You're given a list of objectives, and the second you touch one of them a timer starts. You have 60 seconds to grab them all and return to your get away vehicle.What makes this game unique is the level of interaction you have with the environment. Everything is made up entirely of different colored voxels, each with a different toughness. Depending on the tool, you can smash through any of them. There's a mostly realistic physics engine involved, so if you knock out the bottom of a building it will tip over.This gives you an incredible degree of latitude in solving problems. You can get to valuable painting through the front door, or you can blow a hole in the wall and grab it from behind. You can carefully lug a safe over to a window and throw it out into your truck, or you can ram a dump truck through the building and smash the floor under the vault, dropping it into your vehicle. It's a ton of fun, and as you progress you learn a lot of very cool tricks. There's also a steadily increasing arsenal of tools to help you along.Gameplay is organically separated into two phases: in the first part, you scope out the scene and decide your route. Then you quick save, and start grabbing things. To be successful, your route has to be carefully optimized. You will spend a lot of time quick loading, then going and adjusting one or two things, and then saving and trying again. This can be frustrating. The fifth time your route fails because you got stuck on the same stupid shelf and why can't you just walk around it, I could do that if I was there in real life... but then you realize you can just smash the shelf to pieces with your sledge hammer and all is well again. Cathartic destruction and trial and error optimization go well together.Aesthetically, this game is spectacular. The sound design is great, the sound environments are spot on, and even the voxel graphics are weirdly compelling. They're almost photorealistic. It feels like you're wandering around in one of those incredibly elaborate model dioramas that you used to see in children's books.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally leave reviews or anything because I'm just too lazy, but I felt that I needed to give credit where credit is do, there is so much realism in this game. From the variable splosh and splash of objects hitting water, to how the rain hits the ground, to even how the smoke curls around like real smoke, and then to how cars' headlights flicker as the engine turns over. You think you have a good PC? Try slicing a large object in half and watch your computer's framerate absolutely tank because the game calculates where every single voxel goes, it's quite the humbling experience. People be talking about benchmarks, and if your rig can run crisis, but really in my mind this is the ultimate testing application. How many frames will you lose when you hit something big? In any case, I am definitely glad I bought the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A simplistic single-player game that appeals to the audience of the strategically minded or to the dude who likes stuff to explode.For those who like strategy, the campaign includes many levels in which you can plan out how you'll complete the objectives before the usual 60-second timer starts and ends the level. Some levels do not incorporate this timer, but there may be hazards you might have to account for. The later levels usually get harder meaning it gets more importantFor the dudes that like stuff to blow up, you're in luck! That's basically the entire game. Sandbox mode as long as some modded maps will really satisfy this itch. In addition, some of the earlier campaign levels can be completed on the fly while going absolute bananas.Overall, I'd rate the game 8/10. I really enjoyed it, and although it does cost money I am fairly satisfied. It allows me to be more methodical with the missions when I feel like it, or on opposite days, go wild. Only thing I would like more from the game is extra levels to beat as well as a deeper and richer story. The campaign's story was okay, but it's not the game's strong suit in comparison to the game play.

_childDocuments_.review: Once upon a time, a teenage version of myself had read a preview for Crysis, and seen the words "fully destructible environment." How his little teenage heart had fluttered at the thought, imagining the possibilities. Later, as teenage me had laid in bed, a wistful smile on his lips, he had  envisioned a "fully destructible environment." He had imagined, heart filled with wonder, and no small amount naivety, shooting his way through a wall to deliver glorious, assault rifle justice to North Korean militia. Truly, teenage me had believed, he would no longer be bound by such trivial things as walls, buildings, and trees.Then Crysis came out, it ran at 15 FPS, and the environment wasn't fully destructible by a long shot. Not really. And thus; teenage me had wept in betrayal. (Crysis is honestly pretty cool, if we're being serious for a second. AND it still runs at 15 FPS, now that it has a "Remaster." Can it run Crysis, am I right? Up top. Crytek 4 life, the game engine that never stops being bad at being a game engine. Lolz. )Then, an early 30s version of me saw a preview for Crackdown 3, and how my little heart had fluttered. Of course, we all know how that turned out, and the less said about that abysmal let down, the better. Thus; early 30s me wept in betrayal.Finally, a mid-30s version of me saw a preview for Teardown. But, that mid-30s version would not let his little heart flutter. He was older, wiser, and most importantly; he had been burned before. His heart was weak, it was scarred, and it needed protection.Teardown released, he bought it immediately, and, as with trembling hand he double clicked the icon, he allowed himself to again feel that long abandoned emotion; hope. Weakness, some might say. Delightfully optimistic, others might say...But yeah, anyway, you all knows it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome by now. It is, genuinely, a fully destructible environment, and I didn't need anything more than that to love it. My poor heart, feeling deeply betrayed by the claims of Crysis, (and any number of other games that have so flippantly used the term "fully destructible environment," and lied through their teeth,) can again trust... Which is to say; you blow ♥♥♥♥ up, for realsies, and its cool as ♥♥♥♥. The puzzle element is also way more interesting and deep than imagined. And yes, your PC will resemble that Nazi at the end of Raiders of the Lost Ark after a few hours. You were warned.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:The gameplay is as unique as advertised. Like, the only games I can think of that compare are the Hitman games, but Teardown's significantly better focus on planning sets it far enough apart that I can't call it a "Hitman-like".It's fun, too. The missions are both plentiful and varied. I'm 23 hours in and I haven't gotten bored once. Haven't reached the end, either.It also has a great story. I usually steer away from games where you play as a bad guy, but the game does a great job of convincing you that the people you're up against deserve whatever they get.The bad:Accessibility. Accessibility, accessibility, accessibility.Many accessibility options are misplaced (player bob is in controls options!?) or missing (flashing light reduction would be splendid).The graphics menu is stark naked. It's nice that you can toggle blur-o-vision, but I'd love to - let's say - tone down the particle effects.The game's default options cause even decently powerful machines to sputter (RX Vega 56, i7-6700K, 16 GB RAM, SSD).Regardless, this game is one of few I consider to be a MUST-PLAY.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool game. Been following this project for awhile. You should try it.  Best destructible sandbox yet. BUT... Fire Alarms:The fire alarms is an issue. Some maps you just handle the fire caused by the lightning spending the whole time extinguishing fires when you should really be destroying stuff etc. Fine with some challenges to be like that. But you should for the other maps be able to destroy or throw away the fire alarm. (You can see the fire alarm and break it loose and throw it in the water) But it will still trigger if there is to much fire. You can edit the files to disable fire alarms if u want. But it should be an in-game option or to be destroyable / desposable. Collision: Some objects should have a collision detection as if I throw a wooden box at metal it should not break the metal. But it does for some concrete and metal materials. FPS:Also. There will be low FPS drops. Depending on what you do. I would however, Not hold this against the devs or the game.  It is a concept our current standard pc setups are not really made to handle at 60+ fps. If you manage it. Then you are probably above the average in terms of gpu, ram and processor power. Still as a lot of others say.. It is very fun in low fps aswell. Sound Effects could and probably should be greatly improved upon when getting down to certain collisions. Else. It is a really cool start for this type of idea. TLDR.. Cool concept. Need a lot of balancing and realism work. Not at all perfect as it would look to be, looking quickly at the gameplay and at reviews. Expect low fps.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting this game to be so ground breaking. Up close, it just looks like destructible mine craft blocks, however it builds into a more realistic looking world with by far the best destructible environments you could imagine. No other game has this type of interaction possible with nearly every surface in the game. Concrete is tough, wood chips apart realistically and will burn in a realistic way. I really hope this is the future of how game worlds are handled. Something else of note, the entire game is ray traced within the engine, since they are just square blocks, it runs quite well for the amount of eye candy you are seeing. If you like blowing ♥♥♥♥ up this game is worth it just for that, but also, it has really good game play mechanics on top of that. It is extremely challenging at times and allows for out of the box thinking to get things done. If you don't think out of the box, it will seem impossible but there are surely tens of ways to approach any situation, rather than a set path. You really have to play this one

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute blast and let me tell you why.First of all, who doesn't love causing chaos and destruction? In "Teardown", you get to do just that. You play as a thief who is hired to break into various buildings and steal valuable items. But here's the kicker - you're also encouraged to cause as much destruction as possible while doing so.And let me tell you, the destruction is oh-so-satisfying. You get to smash through walls, break windows, and blow stuff up with explosives. It's like being a kid in a candy store, except the candy store is full of buildings and you have a sledgehammer.But it's not just mindless destruction, oh no. You have to use your brain to figure out the best way to get in and out of each building. Do you go through the front door and risk setting off alarms? Or do you create a hole in the roof and sneak in from above? It's all up to you.The physics in this game are also top-notch. Everything feels weighty and realistic, which only adds to the hilarity of watching a building crumble to the ground as you make your escape.Now, some people might say that causing mayhem and destruction is a bad thing. But honestly, who cares? It's just a game, and it's so much fun. Plus, let's be real, we all have a little bit of a destructive streak in us. "Teardown" just gives us a safe and entertaining outlet for it.In conclusion, if you're looking for a game that lets you unleash your inner demolition expert, "Teardown" is the game for you. It's silly, it's satisfying, and it's sure to provide hours of entertainment. Just don't blame me if you suddenly have the urge to go break stuff in real life.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an interesting concept...Usually I write ironic reviews, but with Teardown I just had to write a 'serious' review.Here goesFirst, the graphics.Wierd, a voxel game with ray tracing, never heard of that and I like it, it is very controversial but I like it.The FPS can kill itself pretty easily (even on my high-end gaming rig!!!) but it's fine as you wont notice it after a time.There is a lot of noise because of the ray-tracing which can be a bit annoying time-to-time.Than, the game mechanics.Everything is interactive. Like, everything.do you want to use a physics gun to put a car inside an hotel? Sure thing...Wanna explode some gas canisters inside a 1 million $ house? Sure...You can do almost anything, but you have to play the whole campaing wich is a bit boring. So I just modified my savegame file.The Proton Linux support works better than running Teardown from Windows 10.Sometimes the GUI won't load on Windows while it does on Linux. (Vanilla Arch 64 bit)So, yes. You really feel this is an early acces game.In conclusion:The game is very interesting and is great fun, but, needs a lot of improvements performance-wise.If I'm stressed I can fire up Teardown, load a couple of mods and be relaxed after a few minutes of playing.Thanks for reading this review <3 (less than three)-Sam

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what can I say. I grew up gaming on toasters. My first PC had a 1.2GHz Intel Celeron and no graphics card. Eighteen years later, the time had come to invest in a top-of-the-line personal computer.Equipped with the best machine money can buy in 2020, I purchased two games I hoped would push my new hardware to the limit: Cyberpunk 2077 and Teardown.One of those games was a buggy, early build with plenty of promise but little polish. The other game was Teardown.Don't be fooled by the early-access moniker. With nought but a shoestring, this two-man operation has achieved what CDPR could not with 800 staff and a $300 million US budget. Teardown is well-designed, well-written and, well... fun. _childDocuments_.review: After 35 hours in this game, I can safely say that Teardown is awesome puzzle game with very unique mechanics. Game consists of different missions where you sabotage, destroy and steal different targets. How you do it is up to you. Environment is 99% destructible and you have different tools at your disposal ranging from guns, explosives to vehicles.So what do you do, when you have to get from building A to building B to building C in under one minute? You could blow up holes in the walls to run through faster. Or build bridges from rooftop to rooftop using planks. Or build some weird contraption with planks and cables that flings you in the air, saving you precious of seconds of time. This is what makes Teardown so great. You know what to do, but you get to do it your way.If you think first person puzzle game based on destructible environments is something you would enjoy, then THIS is the game for you.

Then you are clearly holding back too much!This is a game about destruction with a purpose, break things, smash things, pull them apart or if all that fails then just blow it all up!This game is all about planning and then getting it done in 60 seconds, you will have to make paths where there are none, all so you can break/collect the required things all within that 60 seconds to achieve the maxium stars for the mission.  The missions are varied and diverse, although they may use the same map a number of time but each mission is different with subtle changes to the map.The music does its job and the graphics may lag as you blow alot of things up. _childDocuments_.review: What looks fun from the outset turned out to be one of the most boring experiences I've had.  Yes, the central theme of destruction is quite cathartic, but that is only relevant to the theme.The actual execution of destruction is a mindless tedium, as my eyes glaze over and my throat dries after hitting things with a hammer for twenty minutes.  After driving vehicles into buildings for twenty minutes.  After staring at a map, then back at the thing I need to destroy, then back at the map.It is "Hitting things, the game" without the benefit of a strong context as to why you are hitting the things, compelling characters that make you want to hit the things, or a large degree of challenge holding you back from hitting the things.  Perhaps the challenge comes later, but I was too bored to continue.This is the equivalent of being sent into a sandbox to destroy a sandcastle with a pair of chopsticks, alone and with no one to play with or provide much power to stop you.  Then being told you did a great job before being sent to the next sandbox and sandcastle.  An experience so cathartic it descends into anesthetic.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something unique. I've just completed the campaign for this game and I loved every bit of it. This isn't just your typical destruction game. I would call Teardown a destruction based speedrunner/platformer (and more). As the player you must violently carve a path through multiple unique locations in order to complete a list of set objectives before you run out of time. You can do this using a variety of cool tools like a sledgehammer, shotgun, blowtorch, multiple types of bombs, and a rocket launcher! You are also given a few others tools to help you navigate the levels, such as a fire extinguisher and a spray can. I went into this game expecting to be given some bombs and a bunch of buildings to destroy. I did get that, but I was also given an amazing campaign, tons of unique tools to use creatively, a good selection of vehicles with amazing driving physics, puzzles, adrenaline rushes, and so so much more. I can't describe in a simple review the amount of content this game possesses. There are so many unique challenges and game play aspects. Just when you've gotten the hang of things the game throws a new exciting challenge at you. I can't recommend this game enough. Did I mention that only part 1 the campaign has been completed for early access? And that the active devs are working on even more content?! It is definitely worth the price.Lastly, this game has no right being as pretty as it is. Even on the last mission I was pausing to look at how pretty some things were (whilst being chased by helicopter that was shooting at me). You will need a decent computer to run this game without issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, as much as I truly recommend this game I really feel like it can break your PC sometimes. This game is one of the best games I have ever played, The campaign is really good. There is alot of missions every single moth, or every other month. I usually write bad reviews for a lot of games for a "Job" but it really is for fun. This is one of the only good reviews I have ever made. Anyway, the mods takes up the other half of the game though. Which is good in Teardown, it feels like a cheat code in a mario game. You arent intended to play the Campaign with mods. But if you would like to get through a level really fast and you are stuck on it just use mods! There is alot of really good mods, more than my entire save file for this game is just straight mods. If there is a mission that you need to destroy something or anything at all, I would use a nuke or the Airstrike mod. The airstrike mod lets you use different types of guns and bombs based on the situation. If you are looking to just shoot a building and leave a mark in it with bullets, use the first gun. It is a small mini gun that fires way faster than all of the others. The other one is basically a bomb that just takes up a large/medium amount of space. The biggest bomb take about 3 seconds minimum to fire again. There is a lot of different guns and bombs in that mod but that is all I will cover for that mod. Now lets wrap this review up. Overall you could have such of a good time playing this game without mods to be honest, The campaign is all you really need to have fun in this game. Now hopefully you can watch some youtube videos on this game, and if you do end up buying it. Take a look at the workshop! Have a good day. Sincerely, Encore.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; This game does something that NO OTHER game has ever done before. Get it.The game offers fully destructible environments. Other games have tried to do the same before but nowhere to this degree. Of course some areas needs to be fenced off in a game, to actually provide an actual game, and in Teardown this is done beautifully and realistically by using different materials. A very few of them unbreakable.With this freedom comes a lot of freedom, and this is why you should not expect a typical heist-action-game.In most levels Teardown plays more like a puzzle game where you plan your escape, and then try to execute it in under a minute. At first I was a bit annoyed by this "timer gameplay" because I like destruction and action... but as I realized that the game should be thought of as a puzzle game I really liked it.Quicksave in this game is meant to be used a lot, so you get plenty of chances to experiment with different stuff.Even with the puzzle focus Teardown does not cheat you of the great fun you can have by destroying things just for the fun of it. The main game provides you with plenty of funny moments where you trash other peoples property ... also sometimes more than you actually needed to :-D Some reviews mention bugs, but I didn't find some very minor issues during my 14hours of play. The physics engine enables you to cheat in some ways that you are not meant to. This could be fixed.Also the placement of boards can be a bit cumbersome, and could be improved .Other than that I just had a lot of fun.

detailed_description: Deluxe Edition Fight darkness with darkness by adding the mysterious Nocturne to your league. The Deluxe Edition adds this exclusive character to your available roster of agents, capable of traversing the battlefield with teleportation and picking off foes with her shocking attacks. Count yourself lucky that this mysterious skirmisher is on your side - now you see her, now you’re dead! The Deluxe Edition includes the exclusive Nocturne agent, a Digital Art Book highlighting the inspiration and design behind The Lamplighters League, and the full game soundtrack from award-winning composer Jon Everist. Complete your collection and take on the Banished Court in style! The Lamplighters League Deluxe Edition contains: The Lamplighters League Base Game The Nocturne Exclusive Playable Character The Lamplighters League Original Soundtrack The Lamplighters League Digital Art Book About the Game Sneak, steal, and shoot your way through a world of pulp adventure in The Lamplighters League ! Globetrot across a variety of exciting locales around the world and outwit your enemies in strategic turn-based combat - and, if you play your cards right, you might just save the world. Harebrained Schemes , the creators of The Shadowrun Trilogy and BATTLETECH , bring you an all-new world set in an alternate 1930s, where a tyrannical cult called the Banished Court stands on the cusp of world domination. For millennia, all that stood between this sinister cabal and their plans were a band of heroic scholars known as the Lamplighters League. Unfortunately, the best of the best are all gone, so now it's up to the best of the worst. Recruit a team of misfits and scoundrels with unique abilities and unforgettable personalities, and chase the Banished Court to the ends of the earth in a mix of real-time infiltration, turn-based tactical combat, and a character-driven story of adventure and intrigue. Strategy Meets Story, in Style Control a team of unique, dynamic characters and get to know their signature tactical abilities and roles in the team. Learn their stories and the world they inhabit by taking them on missions - every misfit brings their own style to the fight through unique moves that can turn the tide of combat. Explore a variety of thrilling locales and survey the battlefield before things heat up: sneak past enemies in real-time infiltration gameplay, pick off the stragglers quickly and quietly, and position your squad to get an edge for the fight. Use every advantage and dirty trick your agents have up their sleeves in exciting, turn-based combat. Add advanced abilities, gear, and augmentations to your agents to keep pace with the growing threat of the Banished Court! Race Against the Countdown to Doomsday Chase the Banished Court through an alternate-history world of the 1930s, from dockyards and deserts to jungles both urban and wild. Manage your choices at a global level and try to prevent your enemy from advancing their twisted schemes! Recruit new allies from the best of the worst: scour the globe for outlaws and outcasts and bring them onto your side before the Banished Court catches them first! Every mission earns your team new resources and grows their abilities - but be careful, stress and injury can take their toll! Can you prevent the Banished Court from reshaping the world to their twisted will? Find out in… The Lamplighters League and the Tower at the End of the World!

_childDocuments_.review: This game released Oct 23 and the developer and publisher agreed  to part ways by 1st Jan 24So patch 1.3.1 is as much development as this game will get.Which is bad news for any potential purchaser as this game still needs work.From release its had critical bugs with saves where you can lose everything and have to start again. Buyer beware. Overall - there are cheaper less buggy more polished alternative games availableWhich is a great shame as this definitively has potential and with more work could have been a great game.I lost so many hours due to corrupt saves. I came back after patches and spent hours trying to figure out what was going on hoping that if players invested it wouldn't get abandoned before it was up to standard. This was my sunk cost fallacy.What you currently getPositives+ Characters have good personality+ Character game vocals aren't too repetitive+ They nailed the look they were going for+ 1 free DLC character (couple of months after release)Negatives- Day 1 DLC for a character costing 16% of full game to get a character your not guaranteed to get unless you've completed the game and select as part of your starting team- Bugs, from critical mentioned above saves corrupt, game won't loadto gameplay related, there aren't enough pocket slots for the items you can get in the hideout, recon mode doesn't always display information, or minor glitches, where you mouse click isn't were the character goes, can’t place an overwatch where you want, clicking on a characters abilities activate different ones (use the numbers when this happens) etcTactical Gameplay- This game is designed to be played a certain way, if you deviate then there is no risk reward, it's just playing sub optimally. Tactics players like having more tactical options, and getting a reward if they can pull something off.- game gets repetitive, you’ll become familiar with the maps and enemies, you can even have the same map twice in a row. Characters have a limited ability set and its mostly slight boosts to the abilities.- The game is balanced around having 5/6 characters, and best played with an A team, so choose your starting characters well. You’ll play with them a lot.- Battles are the same loop, initial foes, then reinforcements teleport in.- The undrawn hand cards don't offer enough variety to playthroughs to compensate.- Lots of polish could have been done, like seeing character abilities when giving cards out, or pop up tooltips over key words like “Inspired”StealthIs testing your patience with your characters in a safe place waiting for the enemies to go off alert your idea of fun. If not this part of the game isn’t for you.- It kills the pacing of the mission.- Its very simple, this is a tactical game, players want options to create tactics. Stealth offers limited takedowns or sneaking. no throw stone distract etc.- I don’t understand adding a gameplay option to lessen or skip the fun gameplay loop (tactics gameplay)Strategy layer- 1st playthrough this was constant negative feeling, successfully complete mission, and see enemy bars go up. It may be thematic but its not enjoyable and unnecessary. This could have been created with player meters going up so you see some reward more than that scions bar didn’t go up as much as it could have. 2nd playthrough I ignored the bars, all it mean was regularly doing the last stand mission, which was boring and repetitive.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that launched for 50 euros, with Day One DLC, is getting entirely abandoned 60 days later, while Paradox retains the rights to it (but severing any contact with the community), meaning that the League is effectively dead.This is, quite simply, shameful behavior. I doubt that we'll ever learn (apart from what one might sumize from the vague, marketing excuses included in "the final patch" update) what led them to treat their paying custimers in this way, but I do hope that this debacle is not forgotten. The game was not perfect, the "stealth" portion was clunky, the battles not terribly exciting, it felt unecessarily heavy and slow for some reason, but it oozed atmosphere and I am confident Harebrained could have improved it, at least supported it long enough to make those of us who put our trust in their (and Paradox's) track record not feel entirely duped.I would have given the game a mixed review, if Steam decided to give us a third option, other than "thumbs up" or "thumbs down", but as it stands, I cannopt reccomend, in good conscience, that you buy an abandoned game. Assuming you find it HEAVILY discounted, as part of some bundle perhaps, you could give it a go. At its standard price, you can buy other, far superior games for 49,99 euros.

_childDocuments_.review: I get the honest impression that this game is being sabotaged by its own publisher. Not drumming up much advertising fanfare, laying off 80% of the staff months before the game came out, calling it a failure not even a week after it gets released, a release window of which is surrounded on all sides by heavy hitting highly anticipated AAA titles... It's sus as heck.The game itself is a lovely pulp adventure game in the style of Indiana Jones and short stories from the 1950s about Post-WWI action heroes. It has its roots heavily influenced by HBS's previous Shadowrun games and I can see they've refined the fun strategy aspects of those games here. The storyline so far is grabbing my attention and pulling me in. The intro to the game is fast and doesn't hold your hand to heavily, which I like. I hate overwhelming tutorials.The main gameplay loop is stealthing into a location to achieve some objective. There are many adversaries in the game that you can sneak past, quietly take out, or you can go in guns blazing and wipe em all out. There's a lot of opportunity to lure guys into traps, which I like.So far, the only issues I've had are minor. I've had a small amount of stutter in the recon mode that lets you oversee the map. The cinematic action camera during combat also briefly gets placed in walls or other locations sometimes where you can't actually see what's happening. It's a minor gripe and doesn't affect gameplay, though.Honestly this game is way more polished than I expected based on the really awkward reviews I see here. It's odd considering "Less Buggy Than Usual Bethesda Games" Starfield gets a perfect 10 and this gets middling reviews. Why so harsh?I do feel like some aspects of the game could have done with additional time in the oven. But overall, I recommend it if you wanna play some 1930s pulp action fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really wonderful game. I love the world, I love the characters, I love the range of strategies, I love the writing, I love the villains. Everything about it is just a little bit better and more memorable than it has to be. If you're worried that the cartoony aesthetic means a lightweight game, then let that go. The ONLY complaint I have is there are some balance and difficulty spike issues. I wish the devs could have had just a couple more months to balance it, because then it would be truly perfect.It's an absolute tragedy what Paradox did to this game. Shame on you, Paradox execs. In a world of remakes and sequels, this stood out as a fully-realized new IP. So of course the vultures of capital didn't know how to sell it. If any of the game's devs ever read this, just know you created something special.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: I very much wanted to like this game. I'm a huge fan of the X-COM (and XCOM) series. Hundreds of hours in those. Battletech and Shadowrun were great I like the setting of this game, the campy plot, the ideas around the characters, the lore, all of it really.Cons:The real time portion should have been a top down view. There's no need for a recon view. You should be able to scroll out on the map.Your characters walk slow. Very slow. The only way to move faster is to sprint and make more noise, possibly triggering the turn-based fight before you're ready. This makes the game drag along.I don't feel the stealth part works for this. While I'm trying to maneuver one character into position to do something meaningful, another character is being discovered and tripping the turn-based combat. I don't know if difficult is the right word, but tedious definitely is.This is the type game you want to pick up and casually play just for enjoyment - not to have to get good.  It really is not shaping up to be that however.One plus is that it does run great on steam deck.I really wish there was a sliding scale rating instead of thumbs up or down. So... overall...get it on sale. Don't pay full price.Just barely a thumbs down. And not really condemning the game, it's just not holding my attention. And it has all the elements that should keep me glued to the screen.And don't pay extra for the ridiculous day one DLC. Honestly, why is there extra content that must be purchased separately on day one of release?

_childDocuments_.review: Game started out to be nothing extraordinary nor nothing bad, average at best but became more fun as you unlock more characters and discover combos with their skills which is the whole point of playing games. However, the game started going downhill i would say between mid to 3/4 mark of the game where it just became a chore to finish each battle due to the lack of fast forward option and have to wait each enemy to make their moves, imagine 20+ enemies making their moves, not to mention the wonky camera during enemy movements as well. Controller feels better to play this game but using Move in battle did not feel that easy to target properly so i used keyboard mouse in the end.Pros:-Unique art style that fits the theme-Nice music that goes well with the environment & during battle-Good number of characters to choose from for ur own builds-Recon mode available both before and during battle to let u scout the area and view enemy status-Different variety of stealth/sneak skills that makes it unique-Wide variety of mobs and mechanics-Dialogues between characters were nice and interesting as it talks about their backgrounds-Cutscenes are short and sweet-Quest markers to show the way which helps alot-Covers actually works for both me & the enemiesCons:-Lack of showing the accuracy % when moving to a spot if within range of shooting-Lack of displaying character stats like crit chance/dmg-No option for toggle to sprint or auto run-No option to enable auto save after each battle, only have auto save at start of mission which defeats the purpose if ur game crashes or freezes-No option to fast forward, especially for enemies when there are like alot of them(20+) which takes forever to finish and i can't even alt tab while they move since the game pauses-Game is not optimized properly especially during the loading screen, in the later stage of game entering the supplies store & learning new skills lags the game-Feels like the lack of gear that can be bought using Supplies is disappointing as once i bought the tier 2 armor my supplies basically stopped being used, had 3k+ supplies but nothing to spend on at late game-Understand that the doomsday timer is there to prevent overgrind but having the timer to progress most of the time without a good way to push it back due to breakpoints prevented me from finding all characters in the end, thus missing their dialogues -Camera movement is weird and keeps turning constantly, everytime you target an enemy the camera moves from the back of your character to the enemy to show the line of sight, hence if u target multiple enemies the camera just moves constantly up down left right-When enemy moves, sometimes the camera follows the enemy, sometimes the camera goes to where the enemy will land at before it even reaches, sometimes camera doesn't move from where it last was, idk im just confused which is the intended way-Repeated maps for certain missions with the same layout-At one point my animation for shots stopped showing randomly although the damage does appear afterwards like some ghost shellIn the end, at the final battle of the final mission, halfway through the battle after the enemy ended their turn the game just stopped working, not freeze nor hang but it just did not end the turn properly and could not proceed to my turn. Could not even force end turn or abandon mission since its a critical mission and had to alt f4 and guess what, had to do the mission from the start again. I just felt done at this point and dropped the game and wrote this review. Went to youtube to see the ending which was just dialogues, kinda wished there was a mini cutscene or something. Would not recommend to buy at full price, bought at 30% off and still felt that it wasn't worth that much. If you wanna get, would recommend to get if 50% or more discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so yes I'm giving this game a thumbs up. It has reasons for that. But I wanna make sure you know that it's not all perfect.So first. The game is really nice to look at, it's also really nice to listen to. With an interesting story, mystery, well written dialogue and a big game with a lot going on for it, it deserves a thumbs up. But it also has it's problems. The User Interface while seemingly simple is missing important things like tooltips. You never know what an item is or what it's used for until you're in combat or using it. This makes it hard to prepare for future missions.The stealth, in this primarily stealth-based game, is kinda badly designed. With characters popping out of hiding for no reason, not crouching when the rest of the part is crouching, people being spotted way too fast or too early, limited actions you can perform when your not in combat and incredibly punishing for when you ARE in combat it makes the stealth more irritating and annoying than anything else. The gameplay loop is at risk for being repetitive and with no serious choices or dialogue options it makes the replayability a bit of a letdown as well.The game gets a thumbs up because it does what it sets out to do and for the most part it's a pretty good game. But it does have it's issues (like constantly dropping frames while I was playing). Luckily a lot of its issues look like they can be fixed with patches so lets hope they get those patches soon.If you'd like a more in-depth look with legitimate gameplay then please check out the video on my YouTube Channel (link below).Otherwise thanks so much for reading and I hope I managed to help some of you out there spend your money wisely.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished Lamplighter's League and I'm sad there won't be another. I didn't play the game right at launch. I heard it was pretty rough then. But I played through after the final patch dropped (when HBS split with Paradox or whatever), and I really enjoyed this game. I loved the setting, the characters... It felt like The Mummy meets X-com or something like that. There were still some things that annoyed me that I felt could have been improved on. There aren't that many maps for their random battles around the world, and the game could have either benefited from a lot more maps, or maybe some kind of procedural generation---after awhile the random map battles started feeling stale and I just wanted to get on with the campaign. The threat system has apparently been tweaked since launch, which is good. I played a custom game with 'easy' threat generation (but normal combat) and it felt challenging but not TOO challenging. Near the end of the game I'd recruited a roster of 10 agents and Marteau was a hair from victory. The characters are interesting and I wanted to learn more about them. I wish they'd had their own personal missions or something like that. But I enjoyed the conversations in the hideout and the banter between the agents was fun. I'm sad HBS split with Paradox which means we probably won't be seeing another Lamplighter's League---they left it wide open for a sequel. But I mean, I love HBS and their other games and I have to assume they're doing what's best for them. Maybe this means we'll get another Shadowrun game or something like that in the future. Or Crimson Skies, though I think Microsoft still own the rights to that. TLDR: A fun tactical turn based game that feels like The Mummy meets X-com.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot to love but unfortunately has some very obvious rushed out problems.Lets start with the good :- Sound, Music, Voiceovers- Overall theme and level of detail in the environment- Fun tactical element- Card system allows for interesting character buildsAnd then the bad :- A complete lack of choice in viable squadmates on Survivor difficulty, turn economy rules the game and there are distinct winners and losers.  For example, later in the game I ran into a 4v21 encounter with a boss in the mix.  This could not be stealthed past at all.  Stealth kills have a 3 hit cap and because so many enemies were in a small area it was actually much better to simply grenade 7 targets at once. - Never played/don't have the day 1 DLC character so unsure if that applies to above.- FPS drops, especially in Recon mode- Crashes- Resource systems that don't actually have meaningful impact- Threat system on Survivor moves so quickly it doesn't even allow you to recruit the entire cast (not that you ever should, as needing more than 6 agents means you screwed up)- Related to the threat system, its not even possible to complete the latter half of the "tech tree"- Very clunky/buggy controls/inventory management.  There is a delay when switching characters wherein the old icons/skills show up and this can result in skill/item misuse or even weird reference errors which cause skills to replace inventory slots.- Frustratingly unclear targeting in large groups.  A border around the target would help here and theres plenty of prior work to pull from.- Random numbers popping out of characters when armor is shredded, and then character armor numbers reverting to some default font when being buffed.Long story short, buy it on sale.  I played hundreds of hours of XCOM/2 but I won't be replaying this game.  I don't necessarily regret playing it but I don't think it warranted the price and then theres the whole 10 dollar character shenanigans.  Heres to hoping some patches improve the negatives at least.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game deserves better than a "Mixed" review. I put off buying this game for quite a while because of the dreaded "Paradox" publisher ickyness. I tend to walk away from most Paradox games feeling used and dirty. This game actually lets you bypass the dreaded launcher, so points there...My personal experience with the game seems very counter to many of the reviews here. I have played 20+ hours so far and have very much enjoyed the game. I have had zero problems with bugs or janky behavior, the game has run without a hitch. I suspect many people are mis-clicking enemies on the stealth takedown mechanic and getting frustrated. One major way to avoid this is to use the keyboard shortcut when close to them and just hit spacebar to perform a takedown. Using tab to cycle through your agents is much easier than trying to click them on screen.A really nice thing about the game is that it is extensively voice acted and the various characters are well acted, unique, and have personality. The various Agents on your team have unique skill trees and different powers from each other. This was much better than expected. The agents are MUCH more unique and fleshed out than say XCOM soldiers, they are closer to Baldur's Gate characters but not quite that fleshed out. You only take 3 per mission so mixing and matching leads to a great deal of unique tactical options. There are many abilities that provide for synergy between different characters. All characters pull from the same Skill Point pool so its much easier to create builds and there isn't a lot of gaming "who gets the kill" to get xp or background characters that can never get leveled up. Do some Agents seem better than others? Maybe, but its single player, does it matter? While characters can technically "Die" they mostly get debuffs for a few turns for getting knocked down or have to sit out a mission. Basically, overall the Agents are really well done.The theme and the story are quite well done, unique, engaging, and well written. Each turn see's the story play out in addition to whatever action your team is taking. It frequently seems well weaved into the bigger story's dialogue. I see a lot of complaints about the maps being the same. I personally have not noticed this. There are not a lot of different biomes but they are very applicable to the theme. Maybe I don't have a photographic memory but if they are reused it's not terribly obvious to me. There is a good variety of thematic enemies various Soldiers, Agents, Mummies, Other Worldly Creatures, etc. The animations are good and there is a good variety of special abilities and powers with nice special effects. The world map is more engaging than expected more in line again with XCOM with 3 different factions that you are fighting against. Each turn there is a selection of missions to choose from, you can't do them all every turn. If a faction is ignore too much its missions gets more challenging. If you let them go too long you lose the game. There is a decent variety of missions, not huge, but decent. There are story missions, enemies to fight, boss fights, agents to rescue, various resources to gather, etc. There are is a decent amount of base options to unlock and items to be crafted to improve your base and agents. So, a good bit of theory crafting takes place each turn.Overall, I think the game is quite good. It's not perfect everywhere but if you enjoy the theme and don't mind thinking about your agents actions each turn, looking for synergy's there is a lot of fun to be had and a decent amount of replayability in different team makeups. I personally would give it a 8/10, but I am partial to the theme/setting which probably bumps it up a point.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game.I would still recommend it, but I would advise waiting for some patches.Starting with the bad:The pathing of the game is weird. If you ever played X-Com: War of the Chosen, you know how it should be done.You do the most difficult mission with a faction boss and beat them? You just nerfed the spread of the faction a tiny bit (yes, not an event decrease).You do a story mission ==> You barely decrease the spread of the enemy. You succeed in doing a heist and accomplishing all the side mission==> You don't decrease the general faction spread.There are so many missions around mid-game that the factions' spread increases like crazy, and you barely have time to do anything else but the main mission.The problem is that I had to do critical losing missions without even being able to do more than 6 side missions in the whole game. I am still missing something, like 4 companions . I wanted to try other characters and finish the skill tree, but the crazy increase in faction spread makes it impossible.( I am missing something like 15 skill tree improvements hidden behind a specific type of side mission.)I thought I could at least send 2 squads on missions once a week, but there is only one deployment a week.Doing the most difficult missions with Scions presence should really hinder the progress of the factions. Doing big heist should also decrease significantly the spread. Same for big story missions. DLC day one.... No comment.Real time sneaking around is an interesting mechanic, but having a change of camera when you change zones while patrols are moving close to your guys is silly. You better trigger turn-based mode fast, or you're going to get seen and aggro the whole zone.Maps are limited and quite fast, you are doing the same maps with just random enemies in it.It felt difficult to know which effect was affecting my characters, I have no idea if the reload bonus worked on my electro girl for example.The good:Numerous characters have their own mechanics. It is really fun to discover their powers and ways to play.You can customize your characters even further with up to 3 cards, which is super fun. With passive skills or active skills link to every cards.I just wish we could stock some of those cards to equip some characters that are on side line. Since those cards are random rewards you don't know if you are going to get that Flame power you are looking for this mission but if you don't have the companion on the mission to equip it on him, it will go in the trash.Music and voice acting are nice.

The difficulty *really* gets out of hand in some missions, to the point where I find myself needing to abuse the save function just to get through the level without a Total Party Kill.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe I almost passed on this gem due to the mixed reviews.  This game is so good.  An excellent blend of Indiana Jones and X COM with the scouting system of Mutant Year Zero.  The presentation is on point, the story fun, the atmosphere incredible, the card mechanics blends seamlessly with the other systems.  Its really, really good.  I should have known better then to doubt Harebrained Schemes, given their track record,  This is why you should always look at reviews with a critical eye, especially on Steam.  The ultimate 'one more turn' game.

The maps and mechanics are fun, but then you get to levels where it's just too many enemies. Then your characters get stress breaks and wounded status. It just seems to kind of trail off after a while. I've reached a point in the campaign where I've just decided to delete the game and be done with it.

_childDocuments_.review: By the time I played the game - the bugs were by and large gone, presumably fixed in the last patch prior to the devs leaving Paradox, so if you're going into this now - you can expect a reasonably smooth playthrough.And it is a decent, solid, turn based game. Good combination of stealth options as well as fun battles when you do have to engage. Varied Equipment and skillset combinations.One of its main issues, however, is that the game has 12 characters, with seemingly varied skillsets, but in practice the game forces you to pick a main team of 3-4 and run with them the entire game, else you will fall behind. And its not just a matter of skill points. Because you can't give cards to agents that don't go on a mission, part of the overall equipment sent is restricted only to those you are actively using to fight. So you can completely max out your new agent's skills, but because they never got any cards, they're too far behind to ever be useful. This forces you to replay if you ever want to use the other agents. And while the game is decent, its not *that* good to really be worth the replay.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of controversy around LL. It was hyped as the XCOM killer and Paradox force closed the studio when it turned out not to be the case (and instead lost a lot of money).When the game came out it was so bugged it was basically unplayable. Now it is in a very good state, but won't receive further content or fixes, because, well, the devs were dissolved.Is the game worth playing? Yes, maybe not for full price, but 100% on sale.Having played most of the XCOM's (since TftD aka xcom2) and all of the JA's i have to say LL is probably the most fun.: Every agent can become OP with the right cards and items. Every agent is unique, has personality and is fun to play with. It is incredible if combat gets solved with everyone and everything in the right place. Then it feels a bit like setting up a long chain of dominoes. Missions provide a challenge until the very end. Collecting cards is nice, even though a lot of cards are a tiny bit useless (but that it what ink is for).: Aggro out of combat is sometimes very weird leading to long reloads. The game doesn't have window/screen mouse lock and there is no easy way to adjust camera move speed. Some interactions are ... not clear, and encountering them for the first time is mostly frustrating.: Figuring out agents and combos, discovering cards. Mission selection is meaningful with nice trade-offs until the end of the game. Map pressure is meaningful if you try to 100% a campaign. Map design is good. Taking stress broken agents onto missions kind of gets rewarded, the broken card gets recycled to ink at the end of the mission, but they have a malus throughout the mission. This is a fun mechanic, which i wished was a bit stronger overall.: Repetitive if you stay on just 3 agents the entire game. Some maps have AI pathing issues, which can be abused. Personally i did not like the respawn mechanic. It felt overly punishing if you accidentally got into a fight or a pull turned bad. In all other instances it was not meaningful, 3 mobs when i just cleared out 12? Loading and saving times are ... long. Campaign is too easy if you rush to the end. Plus it cuts fun banter. Not finding the one card that would make a certain build work.: Most consumables are not worth using, which isn't a big deal, unless you are a hoarder. There are a bunch of types of resources with odd progression gates. Crafting is lackluster, i only crafted 2 items in 70 hours. Faction gear is a bit meh and i didn't really use any of it. Heist preparation missions are generally not worth it as they cost you a week and don't impact the heist itself enough. Apparently there are additional missions where you have to break out agents that have been captured on missions. Problem is, if you have agents die on a missions, chances are you can't complete it anyways. The final mission is a bit meh and the end is kinda anticlimactic. I guess they couldn't figure out a nice way of saying "well done, you saved the world" without saying "well done, you saved the world!".
