_childDocuments_.review: A potential gem with flawed execution and some issues with interface. First off, the genre - a 1930's pulpy- noir setting is criminally underused in CRPGs and this scratches that itch. The voice acting is good and believable, the music is period-appropriate, and the premise is gold. Some take issue with the character art, but it seems stylized in a way I enjoy. However, some of the missions can become repetitive and you will certainly favor a certain set of specialists to pull all your capers. Graphically, it can be difficult to find/pick up items of interest and occasionally your agents will be stuck in an endless hopping back and forth over objects when using the point-and-click from the mouse. Some missions can 'break' by getting stuck on the "Enemy Turn" screen that forces one to kill the program through task manager (this happened once to me and verifying/reinstalling the game fixed the issue). All-in-all a solid game undermined by technical bugs and unfortunate repetition. I would have loved to see a Lamplighter's League II, but that will never happen due to the abrupt and shocking break between Hairbrained Schemes & Publisher Paradox. Give this a try, buy it on sale, and hopefully you'll enjoy it too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: I feel compelled to write a review for this game. I really enjoyed it, despite a few issues. The most obvious comparison to make is XCOM; you have missions on a strategic layer that you choose and then undertake on the tactical layer. One of the key differences is that rather than recruiting random soldiers, you recruit named characters, each with their own passives and skill tree. I played it on the hardest difficulty and found it difficult to justify wasting time recruiting new people, since the game's doomsday clock is quite unforgiving. Having said that, you can customise the difficulty and one of the options is I believe called "metagame difficulty", which adjusts things like difficulty of strategic layer events and doomsday clock rates. The game really shines on the tactical layer though; each character has their own playstyle and figuring out ways to make them work well together is a joy. There did seem to be some balancing issues, with certain characters being insanely strong and others being kind of underwhelming. There's a decent variety of enemy types, and certain boss enemies that will pop up from time to time. The tactical layer consists of a combination of real time and turn based; real time when you're undetected/out of combat, turn based in combat. Getting to grips with the real time stuff can be annoying, as each character has a different kind of real time takedown depending on their class, which can be frustrating to use. Real time takedowns are limited use per-mission, and you are always better off trying to use them before difficult fights, which can be time consuming and frustrating. Overall, really solid game that had great potential but sadly Harebrained Schemes can't update it anymore, in fact they don't even get money for copies sold anymore. Recommend checking it out if you're into tactical combat games, but maybe wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: I'm thoroughly enjoying the game.  The game feels finished to me.  I'm not clear what the negative press is for?  I take it paradox has said it is not supporting further development...okay.  The norm these days seems to have shifted to early release for titles making the public the alpha/ beta testers in essence, with support coming as patches to games not ready for the public in the first place. Or supposed extras when they are things that were meant to be released in the game. But were not ready in time, and we are made to feel this is extra support from the company.  Having said that some great games come out of public consultation, take BG3.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: To say this game deserved better is an understatement. To say it needed more time to cook is an understatement. I feel I was lucky. I played this game with only a few bugs popping up, most of them amusing rather than game breaking. The worst of my affair was a mission I had to restart because none of my units could climb the ladder to the upper section of the map where the enemies were. Another had an entire pod of enemies never trigger, instead bopping around the map like ghosts unable to touch me (which felt thematic so I was unsure if it even was a bug). I played this game months after release. I am sure had I played it on launch, I'd have dealt with worse bugs. I'm a big fan of tactical RPGs, and this specific kind of pulp, Doc Savage style fair is extremely up my alley. The broader appeal may not be here, but to anyone who likes either of those things, I recommend this game highly. Do so knowing that the game has bugs, it runs rather poorly, and there's holes in the game where content should be. I already spoke about the bugs. My recommendation for having the game run better is to install it in an SSD if you have it, play it at 1080p and not 4k, and maybe fiddle with some other graphics settings. The game is more style than graphics anyway. As far as holes in content, we have over a dozen fleshed out and interesting characters. They talk to each other between missions. But these agents do not interact with each other. There's no system in place to show bonds or growth between the agents despite so much of this game being about the interplay of these agents setting up actions for others. In fact, that interplay is what I think of as the key feature here despite it not being advertised enough. Anyone who says characters are unbalanced or some are better than others don't realize how important proper set up between characters are. Every character that someone said was awful sounds more like a play style preference. The agents also don't have any special missions made just for them. Zhang has a storyline about his brother that, unless I've missed something huge, never is resolved. Perhaps saved for a DLC that will never come? Mission and map variety leave me wanting. In an average game, you will likely repeat a map a few times, but you will definitely repeat mission types several times. And some missions are simple reskins of others. Radio towers and obelisks are the same thing. I could easily see more items, more allies, and more homebase activities. The game is overall extremely good. And especially if you can get it cheaper than listed. (At the time of this review, it is $50. I recommend getting it for $30 or lower.) But only get it if you fall into two out of three of the following: You like tactical RPGs, you like Doc Savage style pulp stories, you are okay with potential bugs. If you only fall into 1 one of those, then I recommend you play Marvel Midnight Suns. A game that overall has much of the features this game lacks and I'd call an overall better experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game during a sale and at the price of 20 euro this game is worth it. The tactics are fun so if you like some puizzling action adventure this game is more than ok. Strategywise however it lacks a bit but maybe i should crank up the difficulty up to max. The story lost my interest however somewhere in the middle and the characters weren't great either. The world itself however was interesting to say the least. So overall a decent 25+ hours to spend
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: Chill and budget X-Com.Old tycoon on a super-secret island hire world-class mercenaries to save the world from evil cult.If the plot seems shallow, it is, but the game still very appealing.Cartoonish noir setting of 1930s, fun heroes, interesting fights, lots of different enemies.Game is super repetitive closer to the grand finale (unless you somehow manage to do all key missions before doomsday), but enjoyable nevertheless.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: When I got the game I tried it and was put off. Didn't really understand it or how to do stuff.  Left it alone and did other stuff.  I saw they finished all the updates so I said "I paid good money for this, I need to understand and play it right".  Watched a couple vids and then tried it again.  Once I figured out the mechanics, what the various characters could do and so on, and who interacted the best with whom, I started to enjoy it.  Yes, it repeats maps, so did XCOM and XCOM 2.  The story is interesting, the Banished Court factions are interesting.  Lots of Cthulhu, Indiana Jones, Pulp Action stuff.  I am enjoying it.  I am playing it on the easy setting cause I want to see the story and experience the whole game from start to finish.  Do I save and reload sometimes when things go south like no-tomorrow? Yes, I learn that from the X-COM games and their point-blank 99% chance to hit with shotgun and you miss due to RNG lol.   Its fun, the two extra characters, Nocture and Issac are neat to play.  Over all .. good game, good fun.  If you liked X-COM and X-COM2, you'll enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game using largely x-com 2 mechanics, with an aditional real-time sneak/explore component, which is a good addition. Fun story with interesting villians. Could have had a bit more video's for key events, some missions around the characters, and it was a bit of let-down that some missions use basically the same layout.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay reminds of XCOM, but with an entirely different aesthetic and style. The characters are rogue-ish and clever, emphasized by the 1920s-style music and setting. It's challenging without being frustrating, and intricate enough gameplay to keep you entertained. Because of company-drama, the game got no advertising and won't be receiving further patches, which is shame: I enjoy playing it and think it deserves a larger audience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the campaign through, took about 36 hours. It is a good game!  I really liked the alternate early 20th century setting, the characters are voiced well and musical score is really very well done.It feels a little like the xcom remake but with more interesting characters. Honestly if you like turn based games just get it
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly well made XCOM clone. The player is presented a variety of interesting mechanics that are balanced and well done. My chief complaint is the game is both too easy and very forgiving. Even with major mistakes, such as clicking the wrong button when fighting bosses, I never lost, even on my first playthrough. This is a good game for strategy gamers who like the XCOM style, but want something that won't challenge them.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: tl,dr. Aside from the price and minor need for optimization, this game is good. There are 3 types of characters: bruisers, saboteurs and sneaks, each with a predefined set of skills that you can upgrade during the game. On top of that, after each mission, you get cards that you can apply to them to give them additional abilities. Good combinations of characters and cards on various missions can result in awesome combos. I played it on Adventurer (medium) mode (twice) and on Survivor (hard) mode once, I still haven't managed to recruit all the characters. So I get to play again.  I was very happy to find out that I had to play differently in Survivor mode where the well-tried tactic of go-in-and-kill-everyone simply won't work. It's even possible to complete certain missions without firing a shot. The death clock is well made, there are 3 clans of baddies that you have to keep in check and upgrade at different speeds. But every (in-game) week, there are a bunch of missions available on the map and it's up to you to weigh whether you'd rather prevent a specific baddie from progressing or get a shinny new piece of gear.I have only one big issue with this game and it is that it could probably be optimized. The Recon mode stutters when panning. That said, the Recon mode is vastly useless, except when you forgot which toon you gave what element protection to. :-)Normal game play  perfectly fine in Full HD high quality on my old 2060.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about to finish my playthrough and have to say, this is a very hesitant recommend. The game is pretty hard (and I say that as someone who's played all of the XCom games and many other TBS); after 15 hours on normal I had to start again on easy as it just felt like it was unwinnable. Part of the problem I think is that team members and cards are down to RNG and if you don't get combos that work well together then you are definitely disadvantaged. I think this was in part why I found my first run so difficult, in my second go I got characters that worked well together and cards that complimented their abilities. Oh and it has a doomsday clock, so you can't really just wait around for RNG to favour you. In short, if you like TBS, a '30's setting and occult vibes, this is a great game. Just keep in mind it can be extremely difficult if you're unlucky and it has some save bugs that can be problematic.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't perfect. Its lacking some polish, and the controls can be kind of clunky, but overall I've really enjoyed it. I think the premise and presentation is original. Film Noir meets Two-Fisted tales via 30's era pulp magazines. I think all the different characters are fun in both play and dialog. Their all stereotypes you've seen before, but that's part of the charm, and I like the attention paid to all their cryptic, half elaborated back stories. The tactical combat is fun and varied. Who you take on a mission will alter your play style to some extent, and who you take will change based on who you find as the story unfolds, who was wounded on the last mission, and who is suffering a severe bout of PTSD. Watching the Banished Court slowly take over the world on the world map adds an element of urgency to the entire thing missing from a lot of games (Ever gotten a main quest from Bethesda and then wandered off to build settlements all game?) None of that here.Over all I really like this game and I hope they do more with it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the game. A new look into trun based games is always a reason to try something new. A few bugs though. In the enemy phase a soldier got stuck running so the game couldn't advance. A thrall appearing when killing a soldier did not register as active. It's image just stood there and couldn't be targeted. Thankfully it didn't count as a soldier so there was no advancement issue.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: I have played for 9 hours now and have not encountered any bugs or hiccups. I hesitated to get this due to the negative comments and the word that the publisher was not planning to go any farther with the game.At least at first look, that's a shame. Like X-Com got upgrades and expansions, Lamplighters could easily get the same.All the same, I am finding the game to be very fun. Yes, it is a bit lighter than X-Com, but it is 100% the tactical flavor of X-Com. Not that you really would want to stealth your way thru an entire scenario, but it seems that you must eliminate all enemies to finish and go home. Not always really needed - I did have a sabotage scenario where I got the job done and could have made the evac point by outrunning the last two guards - but I had to take them out to close the scenario.So far the voice-overs are outstanding, the banter between characters is great (and curious sometimes - two of my characters are making back up plans to bail out on the group if things go south ... Just story or will it happen ? I don't know.If you were looking forward to the release of Lamplighters League - don't let the negative reviews get to you. I made the leap of faith to get it because it is on sale right now - and I am very glad I did.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: Reminiscent of the old Commandos series, solid turn based strategy, with a good dollop of pulp atmosphere. While it certainly doesn't go two fisted toe to toe with then very best the turn based strategy genre has to offer, it's a solid B+, or even A-, easily ranking above offerings like Hard West or Chroma Squad. Expect the game to be an uphill battle as far as difficulty goes, unless you are a veteran strategy player.Overall, I do recommend it to fans of the genre, though if you are not a fan of the genre, I would look elsewhere for an optimal first experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: It's sort of Miasma Chronicles/Mutant Year Zero crossed with X-Com 2: War of the Chosen.  The gameplay is real-time stealth takedowns, until you can't anymore, and then it's really good tactical turn-based.  Between missions it's the X-Com tactical map with allocating resources, improving your agents and gear, and managing threat and deciding what missions to take to keep it in check.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: The Lamplighter's League is a fantastic tactics game, but not without its hitches. I'd likely wait for a sale for this one unless you're really itching for a new tactics game.That said, the turn-based combat is tight, focused and offers a really exciting variety of approach through the cast of recruitable characters. In my playthrough, I only got to see half the characters available, which was a shame, but gives me something to look forward to in a second playthrough at some point.The macro/world map gameplay is a little flat, and I found the pacing of the threat on the map to be kinda weird. Coming from a game like XCOM 1/2 in the past, I was looking forward to this system, but it ended up limiting the amount of exploring side missions a little too much. Could see this being improved in a few different ways.My biggest complaint is the technical performance. I ran the game on a decent system, but the game had a lot of frame drop situations, particularly during recon mode, which seldom was useable. Had a fair few crashes, too, most often during load screens and saves.All that aside, the soundtrack slaps so hard! The game is dripping in style in its environments and audio, and really makes the game stand out as something distinct in the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: A nice surprise!I honestly had no idea this game was even released earlier this month. I'm a big fan of the XCOM series and by all accounts this game should have shown up on my radar on steam. I'm really impressed with the UI in comparison to XCOM 1/2. It feels really smooth in both character movement and camera movement. I'm only a few missions in, but had a hard time putting it down for the night. The character leveling is pretty basic, basically each have their own skill tree that branches 3 times. I haven't gotten into much equipment, but the uniqueness of each character is fun and a bit different from other games I've played. I'm playing on the normal difficultly and the combat has been fun and moderately challenging. The story seems interesting so far, can't wait to see how it progresses. I'd say if you're a fan of the XCOM games and want more of something like that, this is a great choice. If you're on the fence or are new to this style, the combat is slower paced as it's a turn based style game. For me the fun is the strategy component in setting up the battlefield strategically with your team, think D&D combat. If you like fast paced combat, you're probably not going to like this game. Either way I would recommend giving it a shot or adding it to your wishlist for when it eventually goes on sale.UpdateI finished the game and overall I had fun with it, but I also wouldn't call it exceptional. There a few issues for me that had a negative impact on the experience. From the mid-point on for the game, I felt like I kind of sussed out the general strategy to clear the mob fights and I would often see some of the AIs run in the complete opposite direction as my party to where I would end up having to chase them down. You mostly see the bulk of variety of enemies early on in the game and it seems like they just add more armor and/or health to them as the game progresses (with occasional other bonuses). The difficulty of the game did not scale well into the late game, partly due to the easy strategy I implemented, how quickly the characters became overpowered, and the fights became generally less challenging as a result with little variability. I don't want to get into much detail on that to save on any spoilers, but I really wanted a harder fight and just more to the final stage in terms of story content as well. I don't think it's a bad game by any means and as I mentioned, I had fun with it which is what matters at the end of the day. Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, I really do. It is oozing with theme, the graphical style works wonderfully, and the details and lore weaved into the world are fantastic.But, the game is a mess. It randomly lags. The camera does some wonky things. The difficulty ramps up ridiculously. There are crashes and hangs. Mechanics are obtuse and game interactions are completely opaque.For instance, in one mission some enemies spawn that are invincible, maybe? Or, at least, they keep coming back unless you kill them the right way? You're never really told one way or another, at least that I could tell, and need to figure it out through trial and error. In a game where a single mission can easily take an hour, learning through "trial and error" is no fun at all.Maybe I'll try again at some point, but for now, this one is getting shelved. It's unfortunate, really.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: Great theme with lovable characters and fun turns-based action. The sneaking about gets a little getting used to and the enemies get progressively more challenging. The campaign map and research is lighter than XCom without as many options. Like the theme and like Xcom then this is the game for you :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: Overall completing this game on the highest difficulty was a pleasant battle.  It had a good level of difficulty and is an extremely enjoyable game.  Fun characters, and a great story.  I know the XCOM Purists will disagree with how the game is, but I believe that this is quite the gem of a game.   Hopefully they are able to create an expansion for this and improve on it.  It would be unfortunate to leave this game without any DLC or expansion.  If an Ironman mode could be added and a single save slot, that would add to the challenge of the game that would make it even more enjoyable.  I like the idea of the random custom game with random Lamplighters, I just wish there was a restricted auto save feature to make it more punishing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: Well I am really enjoying the game. Yes. It is very very much like X-com, which i loved and still play. The characters are endearing, the art is fun and suits the story and game-play and the mechanics are just peachy.  I like how you can use the sliders to create your own custom game-play features and difficulty A LOT! They are a nice touch.My only real issue is i think the character move a tad too slow. I would like to see their movement sped up by 10%. Other than that I like it a lot. It is a shame that it didn't do better in sales. Perhaps, its a lesson learned to not include your new games in any of the game pass features on Conlsows. If people want to play it they should pay for it, instead of the shameful money grab that Microsoft and Sony go for by bullying smaller companies and upstarts,
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure still if I am doing the right thing, But I love it.  I'm a huge X-Com Fan from back in day.  Except "terror from the deep"  No Aliens, but some super natural things.  I find upgrades a little lacking, but I can't quite put my foot on it.  Rifle rounds weaker than pistol???   Whats with that.  Why can't we pick up different weapons from the ground?
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, Lets deal with the obvious first. I see many people dogging this game for releasing it with a DLC day 1. And yes, that was indeed a ♥♥♥♥ move by the Devs. (I did purchase it however and love the extra character, Nocturne is pretty gnarly!) That aside, I see alot of X-com and similar TB game comparisons. And yep! It is a TB game! However, while I'm sure few people have played it, the game truly reminds me more of Mutant Year Zero. Minus the dog**** ease of the game, my major gripes with MYZ was that there was almost no replay value (missions all very "level specific" and there weren't very many of them. Full game completion in under 24hrs) and the game was astoundingly easy if you had a little patience. The real time movement allowed for narrowing every fight, even late game, down to only 2-4 of the original group of enemies, You simply mosy around the map, watch the patterns, isolate some poor schmuck, 1 shot him in TB style, then return to real time to hunt your next victim. Also there were several high end weapons and gear that it felt like were supposed to be locked behind late game fights but ended up being accessible much earlier due to poor map making/zone control from enemy sight lines.LampLighters League already feels like a world of difference from that. I'm maybe 5/6 missions in and I can already see both replay value from choosing missions from the selection you're given each "week" and the difficulty has already gone beyond the MYZ level of "I can make every fight easy by picking off the majority of enemies slowly." There may be a way to do it in LL, but it certainly wont be easy. And with how much the difficulty per mission has already ramped, I'm not sure it'll even be possible in the late game. (I'm only on normal diff for this initial run, I'm sure hard will be a fun challenge I'm quite looking forward too!)Honestly, if you're looking for another X-com, you could do much worse. Wait till its on sale or hop in now. It's really up to you. If you played MYZ and had the same gripes I did, TRY THIS! Its a huge improvement on everything that was wrong with MYZ. I'm looking forward to finishing my first run and will try to come back and edit this review then to let you all know my impression of the late game. Definitely going to be replaying on Hard as well. Game on!
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: While I recommend this game for anyone who enjoys turn based tactical combat, there are still many parts of the game that need improvement.  The characters skills and trees are well done in my opinion.  The combat moves at a good pace, and with different heroes to find and mix, there is a good reason to replay the game. Voice acting is well done, and the effects are decent.Now the reasons I would not replay until some improvements are done.  The "stealth" part of the missions is such a slog.  Takes forever, and the much highlighted ability to take down enemies only works on the weaker ones.  You quickly find stronger mobs immune to takedowns in stealth mode.  The cards you can find and equip on your people after a mission. There is no way to save them for later, or put them on an agent that was not on mission.  Had to waste potentially good combo ideas from this.  Because the cards are such a big part of the game, that part really hurts.  And finally, I finished the game, but had no chance to run many side missions.  The timers for the 2 factions on normal moved quickly, pretty much forcing me to focus on main mission.  More mission types and the ability to actually run them would make the map more enjoyable.Balancing is an issue for any game, and there are some overpowered people especially at end of the skill trees.  Wont ruin that part, but I am sure many of you will figure that out when you play.   I am hopeful they will continue to improve the game and I look forward to playing more in the future.  No, it is not Xcom, but it is a good game with the potential to be alot more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: Great game set in an interesting story. There is a learning curve and the difficulty can spike, but it's not overly challenging. Clock management is a mechanic that a lot of folks complain about, however if done right isn't really a problem. I think that it's because the missions that reset the House threat meters are discovered via expeditions and it's not communicated as well as it should. Took me a bit to figure this out but once I did the threat meters were not an issue. Difficulty on a few missions is much higher than normal. I think the developers are aware of this and working on it. Don't listen to the naysayers and all the talk about the studio abandoning it. There are a lot of folks who like to complain and compare to XCOM, however this isn't XCOM. Get over it. Voice acting and writing is suberb. Art style isn't my favorite but it fits the noir 1920's setting. Each agent has a unique skill tree and plays differently than the others. Allies add additional skill trees for team focus. Undrawn Hand gives additional options for kitting out your agents. Maps are fun, but there is a little work to be done there as I'm sure the developers know. Overall I'm really enjoying the play and just scratching my head at the negativity. It's a good product that fits in a genre which usually doesn't get a lot of love or IP for that matter. Be grateful and give it a chance, it just released this month!
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: The League borrows from several other turn-based gems such as XCOM2, Gears Tactics, and Mutant Year Zero to deliver a comprehensive experience on the tactical and strategic layer. There is a lot of room for this to grow via DLC, for while the game is complex it could be deeper. As you manage the doomsday clock of three factions it would be beneficial to have more options to reduce threat than by taking missions. For example XCOM2 DLC'd the resistance ring which opened up the strategic layer a bit. Should bode well for this game moving forward.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: Entertaining and straight forward mechanics, making it a pleasurable and easy to pick up experience.  The voice acting is amazing and each character thus far has fully come to life, both on screen and immersion for the player. Have only played a short while on adventurer difficulty, but am already looking forward to the replay ability and my next run.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy themes/settings in the Golden Age of serial adventure, Pulp/Noir, or alternate history timelines, consider Lamplighter's League. LL offers a fun and interesting spin on some classic story ideas and tropes. The game evokes impressions of Indiana Jones, The Mummy (Fraser version), The Maltese Falcon, The Phantom and The Shadow.But: Does it do things differently than other turn based games of similar genre? From my perspective, no not particularly,There are some quirks and technical gaffes I have encountered:- There are shades of influence from XCom2 War of the Chosen's 'countdown' to apocalypse timer. LL's version is something which is handled differently enough that it doesn't feel like a 1:1 copy of the mechanic - but it does feel like an artificial method of ramping up the difficulty.- I had to turn off syncing to Steam Cloud sync for my save games because a corrupted save slot in my first campaign file made the file unusable. I started over after switching off cloud sync and have not had any further problems (knock on wood).- Playing with a controller sometimes button input to confirm when trying to move a character during combat just doesn't register. If I switch to mouse and make a single move then things work fine again. I've experienced this maybe 4 times but it is an odd thing.- The lack of information for when/where you encounter the optional DLC character Nocturne in game play is frustrating and could be better explained. In my first attempted play-through, it wasn't clear that I had to progress past the first 2 or 3 missions which act like a prologue and tutorial before I could search for her during game play. Curiously, in my current play-through Nocturne and other recruitable characters I found in my first campaign have not appeared. I don't know if it's random or what.. but you'd think if you choose to pay for a DLC character (and yes this is a sticking point with many valid reasons), you should be able to access them in any play-through.  I haven't finished a full play-through yet, but I am enjoying my time with the game. The issues above are annoying but I expect some of them to be resolved along the way with updates.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: A Very Fun spin on a mixture of Real time infiltration and takedown mechanics mixed with X-com like tactical combat and a very cool cast of characters who are all quite unique in their playstyles.   Dripping with cool setting and Lore and a great triad of villains with a lot of randomness and variance too it, The Lamplighters League is one of the better X-Com Lites that I have ever had the pleasure of playing.  On the less than stellar side - The game needs some optimization still (some stutters and Jank with the Camera here and there.) but overall No crashes yet on my rig anyhow.   Also I am not (and really no one should be fond of the practice of locking one of the playable characters behind a Paywall at Launch)  That all being said (for myself anyhow) this game is very enjoyable and sports a lot of cool randomness and different build potentials that do make me feel like the game will have fun replayabilty on subsequent runs.Wether or not it's worth the price of admission is subjective of course but I do feel like I am getting my moneys worth paying full price to help support the devs in this case ( I am also fond of their prior Shadow Run and Battletech games.)  but this game has loads of atmosphere and fun factor as it is.For me It's worth it, and if you can get it on sale for 35-40 then that would be 100% no questions asked worthwhile for fans of the genre.  For me this game gets 2 Thumbs up and I (hope) it sells well enough to get a decent amount of future content because bottom line is this is a good game in it's space.  Tactics, Characters and Lore Loving Gamers - Put on your Indiana Jones hat's and Dig into The Lamplighters League for some Fun!
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: A good rendition of the tactical strategy style of Battletech and X-Com.  Set in the 1930's it stylishly represents a sort of Indiana Jones conspiracy and crew of thieves trying to stop the end of the world.  Has been nearly bug free for me (I only had one incident with being able to equip an item to Ingrid before she was capable of having a 2nd item -- this means if she uses an item from base, she can't pick a new one up.)  However that's been it.  Lots of fun for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: Lamplighters is a fun turn-based tactical combat game, with a lot of charm and a few questionable design decisions. Hopefully the later is patched out.Missions are divided between a stealth stage, where you can eliminate enemies using abilities and pick up resources, and the turn-based combat which is focused on using your characters skills to wipe out the remaining forces.Most missions seem to be very easy, if you play carefully and take out as many enemies as possible before the combat starts, with the turn based sections largely being an exercise in mopping up whoever is left. Some missions where the enemy bosses are present are more difficult, as in addition to the bosses there seem to be a high number of enemy units.The aspect of Lamp Lighters which works poorly is the world map. There are three countdown clocks which tick over week by week. You can slow them by completing missions. but you can only significantly slow one at a time. The clock hit breakpoints beyond which you cannot reverse their progress. There are many non-optional missions which mean you are forced to allow clocks to tick over without a chance to stop them. Also, even if you recruit a large number of agents, you can only run one mission per week. I'm enjoying Lamp Lighters, but I'm also hoping that the developers patch out the mission/clock systems in the near future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game is everything I was looking for.  The turn based tactics are not only easy to pick up, but they fit the theme perfectly.  The characters are well-written to the point that I was worried the first time one of them fell and was captured.  The story is intriguing, the weapons and maps pose unique opportunities, and it all fits together like a well-tailored glove.  If you like pulp action, mysterious adventure, and a challenge for every skill level, you'd be hard pressed to do better.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun and atmospheric 1920s-1930s Pulp Era XCOM-style game! So far it's quite interesting and has a lot of the same types of strategies and feel as XCOM, but instead of random soldiers, you have a variety of Agents that each have their own personality, special abilities, and skill trees to work through. And you won't necessarily recruit all of them every play through (in fact, I'm told it would be very rare to do so), so that adds to the replayability. Basically, if you like XCOM and XCOM 2 and you like the theme (including mystical parts of the Pulp Era like mummies and Lovecraftian monsters), then I would definitely recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: The Game is amazing! It scratches the 1920s/1930s Cthulhu and the xcom vibes immensly well. It looks beautiful and once you understand what you need to do it really starts flowing really well. I need to up my agent game currently I mostly just alarm the guards and kill em all. But you have all those options. The characters are loads of fun and entertaining. Really would love to start two missions each week or take 4 agents with me. Maybe I just don´t know how??
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: Its feeding my hunger for xcom like game, but with different theme(pulp adventures), the characters are giving me nice nostalgia for stealth games like desperados and I feel refreshed on how it has more characterization and story element than most strategy games these days(mostly optional conversations between characters between missions)
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: Character driven xcom-like with an Indiana Jones-esque story.It's well designed, characters are unique and the various abilities all feel useful and well thought out. The global map / mission choices have lasting impacts without feeling punishing, the missions seem to fall into a good place of difficult but not prohibitively so.My only issues so far are a few hiccups with the controls, they seem to be designed for a controller instead of mouse and keyboard, leading to some odd missed / incorrect inputs. But these are fairly infrequent.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: Performance of the game could be better (turn off motion blur!), but I feel like it has the setting pretty nailed, and there are lots of ways to progress your agents to make the game interesting.  The stealth aspect is the epitome of tough but fair.  Which means it'll probably frustrate you a bit because you have the ability to take out half a dozen people, and the skill to take out one or so.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is excellent, and the characters are unique and fun. However, the meta game is punishingly frustrating. I don't mind doomsday clocks. They create a sense of urgency, which can be fun, but the extremely tight window for a win makes it so that taking on any kind of time for side quests is not much of an option. It's clear that they make character recruitment a major risk as a motivation for replays. It makes me not want to play at all since I can't make time for new characters during the course of a campaign. I get that you have to make tough choices, but the choices are practically made for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

_childDocuments_.review:
Harebrained Schemes, the creators of The Shadowrun Trilogy and BATTLETECH, bring you an all-new world set in an alternate 1930s, where a tyrannical cult called the Banished Court stands on the cusp of world domination. For millennia, all that stood between this sinister cabal and their plans were a band of heroic scholars known as the Lamplighters League.

Sneak, steal, and shoot your way through a world of pulp adventure in The Lamplighters League! Globetrot across a variety of exciting locales around the world and outwit your enemies in strategic turn-based combat - and, if you play your cards right, you might just save the world.

Recruit a team of misfits and scoundrels with unique abilities and unforgettable personalities, and chase the Banished Court to the ends of the earth in a mix of real-time infiltration, turn-based tactical combat, and a character-driven story of adventure and intrigue.
_childDocuments_.name: The Lamplighters League

name: Boomerang X
detailed_description: We've recently updated our demo — the first third of the game is now available for free! Once you're done, you can continue where you left off in the full game. Carving through hordes of horrors isn’t the only thing your boomerang is good for: once thrown, you can slingshot directly to it, preserving momentum and launching yourself through the air. Slow down time and use well-aimed throws to get around, above, and behind your foes. Speed is everything, and only the nimblest boomerang-er will survive… Fight otherworldly forces and look cool doing it. Impress the boomerang with stylish tricks and it’ll grant you strange powers to let you defeat the forces of the depths with greater ease. Kaspidae smiles upon you and your killer moves… They creep and crawl from crevices, swoop and dive from the treetops, and spray nasty bile at you from all angles. Keep your wits about you — nowhere is safe. Whatever you do, don’t stand still, or you’ll surely be consumed... Fight your way through the bowels of a ruined civilization and stop the nightmares from spreading to the rest of your world. Something lurks deep underneath these ruined halls, spewing corruption… can you defeat whatever it is? And even if you can… will that really be the end?

_childDocuments_.review: I have lost weight through the sheer degree of sweat alone produced by getting through a standard run. If I die from dehydration, know that it was New Game+ that did it.Absolutely frantic once it gives you the vast majority of its movement mechanics and attacks, mercifully couched within smooth as butter control. Very short, but as a result, laser focused on it's arena sweat bucket gameplay.Very nais.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay flow is excellent with minimalist story and fantastic aesthetic. Right from the start I felt like this could be a good game but felt like its little bit too easy but oh boy I was wrong! Later arenas get more insane and tense while NG+ is that but x2. It was a great challenge to play full game hitless and maybe one of my proudest moments of 2022.For some this might be disappointing game because it could be around 1 hour from start to finish but it has ton of replay value for if you are up for the challenge with its fast paced addicting gameplay. Highly recommended for speedrunners or just people who love unique indie games. 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute blast to play, a short experience taking around 12 hours for all achievements but worth its weight in gold. High octane movement/skill based FPS that rewards moment to moment decision making and mechanical skill. If you're a story fan there's not much for you here but don't let lack of story deceive you to mean lack of style or substance, Boomerang X has plenty of that. You essentially go room to room in arena based combat unlocking new skills and facing harder challenges as you progress, with new enemies being added to keep combat fresh. The Boomerang feels great to throw and fight with, as you unlock more moves combat really comes together to have a great ebb and flow to it. A fantastic game for gameplay purists and fans of fun movement systems, pick this up ASAP if you want something fresh but not convoluted.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Boomerang X is the most fun I've had since Doom Eternal. Its a perfect arena shooter esque game that respects your time since its only 3-4 hours. If your sick of 70 plus hour games with mindless fetch quests or filler content look no further this thing is action packed from beginning to end. All in all a solid recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game on my Steam Deck and really enjoyed it. Great art style, smooth controls (even with thumbsticks instead of keyboard and mouse), perfect feeling of flow and movement and no down time during my whole run through the game.I am sorry the developer seems to be closing down because they couldn't find any funding for their next project. I was really interested to see what they were up to next. RIP DANG!
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Crazy ass movement. I love it. Don't listen to those who tell you the game is too short for its price. It's meant to be replayed and gets infinitely more enjoyable as you start to master it. Most achievement also guide you towards playing better or in different ways, I had a lot of fun. Also, it is quite unique in terms of visuals and sound. Very cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: The game's really solid. The basic movement, shooting, and abilities are really well thought and fleshed out. However, its really short. Takes around 2 hours in a casual playthrough, and the New Game+ is just the same game but harder. The amount of content packed in those 2 hours is insane, but I just wish there was more. At the very least, it would be nice if they had mod support.  Buy this game when it goes on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Boomerang X is a super fun and fluid movement shooter coming out in a  good moment for SP FPS games. It comfortably belongs alongside the likes of Ghostrunner and ULTRAKILL, but the lack of content means it's not as essential. Hoping for some post-launch additions, because right now there's just the 2-3 hour story and the ♥♥♥♥-breakingly hard New Game+ and that's about it. Still, wicked good fun for those who want to go zoom and hate frogs.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: DANG! Boomerang X is one of the most invigorating and innovative first person action platformers since Mirror's Edge, and it's made by only 6 developers! Not only if the freeform platforming that's all down to player agency so incredibly liberating, but the narrative is surprisingly intriguing about this interdimensional nomad on an Borroughsian journey who's trying to get back to...Earth? All the context you get with this world is, you see a dark boomerang blade in the sea, and then you wake up on the shore with your arms bandaged up and broken, unusable spears. Where did you come from? Are we human? A praying mantis ancient civilisation? Is this a typical story of dark corruption that wiped out a civilisation? What's up with the expository and light-hearted Tepan, your millipedal friend, who's also accidentally ended up from a different dimension to here? Why are there portals after each level? What's up with the Tuning Room and how does playing a series of notes on strings opens up a door? Why do insect baddies co-exist in the same space with mages, birds, squids, parasites, and dinosaurs? The chapter names hint at deep lore and I just wanted to know more. No matter how weird the levels get though, there is a pleasantly satisfying ending. I love games that can combine the traversal into the combat, and here, your primary weapon is a bladed boomerang that can be thrown at enemies and used as a grappling hook in the same turn. The pacing of the combat arenas is so fast that slow-motion (called Flux here) almost seems required much like in FEAR, so my hats off to anyone trying a no Flux run. My fingers were permanently fixed on the Shift key for the slow-mo to the point of blisters, as I'm darting and zipping around the level, feathering my aim like the coolest platforming blade-wielding ninja. Some of my favourite levels were the more open-ended variety, such as the Yoranwood forest, Incursion of the Great Worm, or the Resonance Engine. A lovely wrinkle to the gameplay are the combo buffs you can dish out and rotate, such as if you hit three enemies in a row, you can enact an area-of-effect explosion, a sniper shot, or if you're killing enemies consecutively while in the air then you become a proximity mine that you can unleash on anything (you'll trigger it even if you hit platforms). So you find yourself constantly juggling which power to use at what time with which groups of enemies. Sometimes you want to save the sniper shot for the tougher enemies or when you've become the mine, you're pretty much invincible until it goes off so you can bump into enemies without worrying about losing health. Each combat arena is a nerve-shredding affair and I would breathe a sigh of relief after nearly every level, especially in New Game Plus. My only frustrations are that you have to stand in a healing circle long enough to get healed and by that time you're standing still, you'll be swarmed with enemies. This is a game of the floor is lava and you're constantly on the move, so it's a risk-reward procedure to heal, but the enemies are so fast. It becomes a game of attrition or making sure you take out either grounded or airborne enemies first before you decide to heal up. I almost wished for a ledge grab in levels such as Atsil's Quarry or Resonance Engine so I didn't have to keep on flicking myself up and around to land on the platform I wanted to get to. The levels and enemies keep ramping up in variety that keeps up the memorability throughout until the very existentially destructive and surreal end. I appreciated the diversity in cultural influences such as Japanese, Middle Eastern, South Asian, Roman, and Norse architecture and music. The music is so well integrated into the gameplay and slow-motion, that it feels like a rhythm game. Sadly, I felt New Game Plus had some missed potential with the narrative because you wake up on the shore this time with darker bandaged arms, which made me think if we are playing a different nomad and might get a different ending but it's just a stylish distinction between the regular game and new game +. Doesn't stop me from trying to complete it on NG+ with its heightened difficulty! Much like the recent Mighty Goose and Olija, it's a short and greatly paced arcade ride that doesn't outstay its welcome and is confident about its design goals, mechanics, and worlds.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so have you ever like had tons of coffee or energy drinks within a short amount of time and you were just bursting with energy afterwards and you didn’t really know what to do with it so you just sorta started thinking about all sorts of things and walking and just doing pretty much whatever you could think of and questioning all your life decisions and…Okay, I can’t do this any longer. See, I tried to convey, via the lack of punctuation and the analogy itself, what playing Boomerang X feels like: fast, because  Within 3 minutes you already have your weapon, you’re already taught the very basics, and you’re already fighting in waves and waves of enemies. And it’s not just the rhythm of the game that’s fast:  - which is weird when you consider one of your main abilities slows down time. Or maybe that’s EXACTLY the reason why it’s one of your main abilities. But anyway, I digress.As I said,  The difference here to the ones you might be used to is that, in Boomerang X you use, shocker, a boomerang as a weapon. Everything revolves around this boomerang, and honestly, it’s a really fun core combat loop. Despite having just one weapon,  You can throw your boomerang, you can call it back instantly, you can slingshot yourself to it, you can drop as you’re traveling towards it, you can charge your attack, get special attacks by achieving certain goals like 3 enemies killed mid air without touching the ground or 2 enemies killed in one throw, and you can even slow down time! aside from the skills that require you to achieve goals. Even the time slowdown can be spammed! It has a limit of a few seconds, but as soon as it’s over you can just… cast it again! Due to all of these movement skills, I will say this: the game is VERY fast paced.  Particularly powerful enemies will have multiple of those for you to hit from different angles. Due to how easy it is to kill most enemies, the screen is always flooded with them, forcing you to never stop moving so as to not get hit. If you can’t see them, fear not: they glow through walls. This is another factor that forces you to constantly be on the move: you need to get to these marked enemies as soon as possible. So in total, we have at least three main elements forcing you to never stop: the tons of enemies, the target enemies, and the fact that lots of these targets have weak spots all over, which forces you to go around them, under them, above them, stun them… there are lots of ways to deal with these, and it depends on the type of enemy.And the best part is, this just doesn’t get boring! There are a few reasons for this. I think the main one aside from what I mentioned about you getting upgrades in every other arena is that nearly every arena introduces at least one new enemy type.  and while not all of them are fun to fight, they’re all very different and unique in a way that I must applaud the devs for achieving. That being said though, beware! You might be super into the combat, but don’t forget you can still die! You begin the game with one health, and get more as you progress, which is very quickly. If you die, you get to enjoy starting the entire arena all over again from wave 1. Well, unless you turn that off in the accessibility options. , containing not only lots of nice visual options but also difficulty adjustment options in case the game is too hard for some people. I really dig what they did there!But what else is there aside from the combat? Well… not much, to be honest! , but it definitely won’t be a fit for everyone. I was particularly entranced by the space musical rooms where you unlock new skills - I put a picture of it down below.  And in terms of story… I couldn’t tell you either! You just start out shipwrecked, get a boomerang and go nuts slaughtering waves and waves of enemies. There is a caterpillar-like creature that does give you some backstory, and the environment does also give you hints if you’re being particularly attentive, but honestly, it’s clear that it was just there to serve as the minimum needed to get the game going. And I say this not as a criticism, just as a trait. Believe me when I say this game does not need a story to shine. And it absolutely does shine.So what will you be doing aside from fighting, you might ask? Well, you’ll be walking to the next fight! That’s literally it. You finish an arena, you walk to the next. In between both, you get your powerups.  But as I said before, this isn’t a bad thing, because  Some of them have environmental hazards, but never once did I feel any of them was unfair. You even get healing spots to replenish your health, but in order to do so you must stay still for a few seconds, so you have to time your heals well.While I do mostly have praises for the game, though, First is that the entire structure of the game might not appeal to some. If you’re not into arena shooters, skip. If you want a solid story, skip. This game knows what it wants to do, and it does it very well… it just might not be what you want. Furthermore, the game only took me , which is a very short amount of time. And I found it rather easy, though that might have just been me., which allows you to pick which skills and abilities your character has before tossing you in an arena where your goal is to kill as many enemies as possible, chaining the kills together for sick score bonuses. I’m not into either of these things though, so for me the game ended at the end of my first playthrough.And that’s it! All in all, I had an absolute BLAST with Boomerang X. It’s an incredible addition to the genre, and one of the most fun ones I’ve ever played. And if you’re unsure if this game is for you, rejoice:  What’s there not to like here? If you do give the game a shot, let me know how it goes!
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Boomerang X is a fast paced arena shooter where you play as a stranded person (there's a minimalist story) on an island with a, you guessed it, boomerang. The character looks like he has striped tattoos, maybe bandages, or maybe he's just a humanoid zebra, but in any case I was astonished by the polish and the fluid combat and its pure awesomeness.The game starts off very quick. Moments after starting the game you'll be fighting off the first enemies. The goal is clear and simple: survive the different kinds of enemy waves by killing the yellow marked enemies. But what seems so simple gets increasingly harder, especially when you keep focusing on the marked ones instead of the regular ones. Because enemies will come from all kinds of directions later on and things will get hectic. Only after defeating the yellow marked ones the next wave will start and the current enemies will disappear. Later on, however, some enemies will also have red gems attached to them. These all have to be shattered in order to defeat them. That is, if they of course also have a yellow mark, otherwise they are optional.Your boomerang is there all the time. You can throw it and it will circle around, leaving you defenseless at that moment, until you eventually automatically catch it. It will also go through multiple enemies so timing and tactically thinking is rewarded with quicker victories, but usually it's a combination of timing and luck. Your boomerang can't be upgraded, but you will earn new moves for it that adds both more variation and new gameplay mechanics to the game. With almost every following arena you'll have something new to try and show off. Think of the ability to jump to where you throw your boomerang or to use an ability that can kill multiple enemies at once. These are acquired by going through some of free-falling portals.Along the way you'll also earn shields. Touching an enemy or getting hit by an enemy removes one shield, no matter how big or small the enemy is. But even with a lot of shields you'll still regularly die unless you've trained a bit.The game is about two hours long, but there's plenty of variety as far as the level design goes. You'll travel through bamboo forests, through caverns, crypts and even temples. All of it gorgeously rendered with painterly-like textures. Unfortunately though I sometimes had the feeling that I was playing a tech demo instead of a full game. Although the game is incredibly polished the short duration of it makes it feel kind of rushed. This game could be absolutely huge if it was more fleshed out and if it was also longer. I know, length doesn't equal fun, but I just wish there was more of it.As I mentioned the graphics are just great. Sharp, colorful and with painterly textures make it stand out for sure. The screenshots do not do this game justice, it's something that has to be seen in motion. Both the environments and characters are looking great and they are perfectly animated as well.There's no actual voice acting. Just sounds and music. The sound effects sound good, but I was so busy fighting off enemies that I didn't pay any real attention to the music. But I think I remember it being fast paced as well, fitting to the gameplay.As for the technical stuff: I never experienced any bugs, glitches or other issues. This is one polished game.Boomerang X is an underrated game and that's mostly to blame because of its high asking price. The other being the length. Something that really could've been fixed by just lowering the price. Even I thought long and hard to see if I wanted to pay €12 for it. I did, and I'm glad, but I can also see why people would be hesitant. For a two hour journey this is still a steep price to pay, even if you don't intend on playing through it more than once. Once you've got that figured out you'll probably also know if this is the game for you. Not taking the price into account I personally do recommend it because it really is a solid and polished game in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: There is an interesting game here, and I think a niche audience might really love it.  I just felt like even with a bunch of added power ups the core game play loop was really repetitive and overall just not my thing.  Its kind of fun to just zoom around the room, but the difficulty felt non existent even when avoiding power ups and after a few 20 minute sessions I realized that I'm just having a meh time and there are better games for me to be playing.With that said, the art style, music, and technical performance were all great, this just wasn't my cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely recommend Boomerang X. It's a blast of a time, for as short as that time is. My first playthrough was only about 80 minutes long or so, maybe shorter than that? And I died about once, on the last level because I am not a smart man. But please do not let that short playtime discourage you from playing it.There /is/ a NG+ mode that is a lot harder than the first playthrough (which I enjoy because my first playthrough I did not struggle at all). There is also an endless mode if you crave more b o  o m  e r a n g  xThe premise is: "You're a mummy or something and you get shipwrecked on an island by a wyrm thing in the sea. You get up, walk forward, and you find the "Boomerang X" (see it's a funny title because it's a bladed weapon that you throw, it comes back to you, and it's an X shape) then the game starts throwing combat at you that is super easy and simple at first, then additional mechanics are added and more complex enemies are added"What makes it fun, though, is the fast movement you get in the air, combined with precise throws you'll be having to do to weave through horde of enemies in the air, to kill enemies with weakspots and charging your abilities to do the aforementioned "kill annoying enemies" faster.You're slowest on the ground. Fastest in the air. I laughed when I realised how fast you move when bunnyhopping. Your air control is pretty solid, but if you find yourself moving to fast you can bring yourself to a deadstop. This doesn't cancel out if you were gaining height or losing it, though, so keep that in mind.I love how the game looks, how it handles, and the music is wonderful for it's chaotic nature. The areas you walk through between area segments are.. actually really good, too? Makes me wonder what happened to the poor bastards that fired up that resonance engine.Honestly, I do find it hard to talk about this game. It's short, sweet, and I wish we had more games like it! I don't think there's any enemy in particular that's badly designed, nor any aspect of the game that's badly designed. Sometimes I have frame rate issues in about one or two areas, but that's the only thing I can think of really!
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to recommend this game only because I think it deserves it. That being said, I was extremely disappointed that my first playthrough took me a mere 2 hours, and I honestly just didn't have that much fun. It has some solid mechanics, but I guess I was just expecting there to be more... Boomerang tech? The game really doesn't do a great job of making the Boomerang feel fun to use... the Shotgun and Sniper "spells" feel good though.I don't want to say its a bad game because it isn't, but for $20 there is a seemingly meager amount of content.New Game + is an option after you beat the game once, but I found myself mostly unmotivated to immediately replay the game on what is essentially the "Hardmode" (NG+).I think this game would be more interesting if there were more mechanics surrounding the Boomerang, because as it is, its basically just something you use to kill small enemies so that you can use your Shotgun and Sniper "spells". That, and it functions as your primary method of movement via your dash always travelling in the direction of your boomerang.I know people are going to disagree with me, but I really just didn't find the combat very satisfying... enemies kinda just disappear when you kill them, there isn't much feedback. Compared to a similar game, Risk of Rain 2, this feels pretty... flat. Maybe if there were more abilities or weapons or something it would be more fun to play NG+, but unfortunately I wasn't hooked by Boomerang X, thought this is perhaps due to my own unrealistic/unfounded expectations for the game, thus the reason why I "recommend" the game. I think it's a fun game, but I can't help but find myself just wishing I was playing Ultrakill or something...I'll probably revisit this game soon and complete NG+, hopefully by then my self-imposed disappointment will have mostly worn off, and I will be able to see this game as the game it is, instead of just wishing it was the game that I thought it would be.This is probably the most mixed I've felt about a game in a long time... I can't decide if I actually like it or not.My advice: Buy the game and play it for an hour. If you dont like it then refund it. If you do, then don't. It's as simple as that.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most fluid arena games I've ever played. It's very fun to play, until you reach a certain point. The game took me about an hour and a half and at about the halfway point I started getting a bit bored. It got repetitive and the enemies didn't have much difference between their designs or attacks. At least 4 of the few enemies in the game all simply float toward you. The boomerang itself is a great weapon but also get's stale fast. I'll admit, I suck at using extra abilities when your main weapon is effective enough so I didn't find myself using the powers as much as I should have except for the fire blast because I only ever stayed airborne. Every arena in this game is unique and interesting but ultimately pointless because you'll be endlessly flinging yourself around almost never going back to the ground except for shield refills which is the only rewarding way to play the game because of the fire blast. Despite these issues, I still had fun. I played through the demo multiple times and have been waiting for this ever since. The art style is incredible, I love the world DANG! has built, the centipede is cute, and, at a glance, the gameplay is fantastic. There's a ton of achievements to unlock and even a NG+ which does the one thing I love about harder difficulties which is adding enemies instead of messing with enemies' or the player's health. In its current state, I say the $20 price point isn't quite worth it, but with just a bit more work this would be one of my favourite games.Edit: went and played a bit more NG+ and it's definitely much better than my first playthrough. Much more difficult, late-game enemies make the earlier arenas much more entertaining, and I've found myself using the powers more often. Most of my issues still stand, but NG+ is way more fun

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of movement shooters like Ultrakill or Eternal this is definitely a game for you.While the game is short (took me a little under an hour to beat on the first run through) it has more than enough content and depth to warrant additional playthroughs. The game is speedrun friendly, challenge friendly, and also contains a NewGame+ mode which adds a bunch of new encounters to existing arenas with your full kit from start to finish. The NewGame+ on its own is a whole new experience, and I would really encourage anyone who beats the game to also play it and not just drop the game immediately after one playthrough.The gist of combat in Boomerang X revolves around gaining certain abilities that you acquire by either chaining kills together, chaining kills in the air, or chaining kills with your various abilities. These certain abilities allow for you to take care of enemies much quicker and a lot of the interesting combat dynamics are managing your way around enemies to gain and strategically use your abilities. One example is how you might use your slowmotion ability to help line up a collateral kill on some weaker enemies, giving you the Scatter ability which you then use to gain the Needle in order to snipe a wizard across the map that normally teleports away from you when you get close. There's also a lot of interesting sort of "kills" you can do on stronger enemies like using the Needle ability to pierce through both weakpoints on the frog enemy or by using Blaze to collide with the giraffe enemy and destroy all of the pips on their body at once. The general flow is less reflex-intensive and more puzzle based with how you decide you want to gain and use abilities with the great assistance from your slow-motion. However, without slow motion, it can be just as fast of a game as you want where you either have to rely on split second decisions with your abilities or precision aiming while moving at mach-10 in the air because of your dash. This game is also very accessible for new players with various accessibility options and a slow-mode power-up that you can use to help you become adjusted to the game's mechanics and fast speeds or to just assist in aiming at weakpoints.This game also has honestly one of the best art aesthetics I've seen out of a game in recent years - it's very pretty. Personally I'm a big fan of the particles that appear around your hand when you have abilities, the UI, and how customizable certain visual aspects of the game are such as being able to change the color of enemy "targets" and silhouettes.I honestly have no idea why there are not more people playing this game which is really what inclined me to write this. Hidden gem here and with an endless mode and more content coming soon the game will just get better.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: It's incredibly fast-paced, and while it does introduce you to each mechanic individually, before giving you a good chance to make use of it, it does not hold your hand. You're expected to learn quickly and make use of everything at your disposal, and to stay focused in every fight. I deeply recommend this game, though it's definitely  short. I beat the main campaign in under 2.5 hours, not counting that I have yet to do the achievements, all the endless modes, or New Game+. If you're looking for the most bang for your buck, this game's short length isn't going to give you that, but if you're looking for an excellent and high-skill experience for a moderate price, buy now. (or buy on sale, might get 25% or more off.)
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: $20 for such a short game is fairly steep (1-3 hours with New Game+), so I can only recommend this game to anyone interested in speed running and gyro. I'd honestly put this game at $5 - $10 max regardless of it being a speed run game. The only reason I paid the full $20 was because of Flick Stick.An issue I've seen brought up is that Flux (slow motion) is too strong. You can use it every time you throw the boomerang. This feels like it was balanced for New Game+ as enemy density basically forces you to constantly use it. Since there is a super meter in the game (Comet Mode), I think there is an obvious solution. Make it so taking out enemies not only fills Comet Mode but using Flux will also drain it. Since the game was made for speed running though, I don't think any changes will be made to Flux.Something that bugs me is how abilities are activated. There are only 2 abilities, Scattershot & Needle. For some reason you are forced to toggle in between them. I'd really prefer if I could directly activate each ability separately rather than waste a binding on a toggle.Flick Stick works fine but there doesn't seem to be any native support for Switch Pro/Joycons on this PC version (which is strange as most people that want gyro come from Nintendo).There are also no accel options for the gyro which is fairly disappointing. Accel is a very useful and underrated tool, especially for gyro.Currently; there doesn't seem to be a way to recalibrate the gyro, so it will drift indefinitely. This is something that can be done with Steam Input by resting the controller for 5 seconds.Regarding Steam Input, it's a shame there is no SIAPI support for Steam Controllers. However, this game is so simple though that it really doesn't need it.Something this game does need though is an accessibility option to lock the UI as KB&M or Controller. This would be great not just for Steam Controllers but Azeron Keypads and other misc. setups.A more obscure accessibility option I'd like to see is the ability to swap the hands in game. This is something games like Valorant have to help improve immersion for left handed players.Overall; if you are just going to play this game with KB&M and you're not interested in speed running, then I'd say wait for a sale. If you are interested in seeing what shooters should play like on modern consoles (other than Xbox), then pick this game up if you can afford to splurge.

_childDocuments_.review: Peculiar and unique little game.It haves a lot of flaws tho.-The learning curve its almost nonexistant, there is no real difficulty here.-The game punishes you for having an aggresive playstyle (The physics and the boomerang starts doing weird stuff when you are trying to play with a quick pace)-Most of the achievements are bugged.-There are no secrets or rewards for doing great unlike in other games like Ultrakill.-2 hours of content and almost no replayability value. [NEW GAME+ is not "new content", its just an attemp to give the game more replayability in the laziest way possible]Still a solid 8/10 for giving me a fresh and fun experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: i beat the game in around a hour and half. it's a shame because i ADORED every second of it. it's so good.i was honestly shocked that it ended where it ended. the final cutscene transports us into a desert dimension. im like "oh cool! we're going to have to fight through a desert world next!" and that the npcs in the distance would fill the same role as the centipede did in the first world. I felt excitement at the thought of the game moving us through dimensions to fight different enemies and bosses.but nope, credits roll. games finished. what? :(going off the final cutscene, it truly felt like the devs had a grander idea for this game but were forced to cut it REALLY shortit's extremely saddening considering the squandered potential because if this game had multiple worlds following the same format as the first (fighting in arenas, talking to npcs between arenas, fighting final boss, moving to new, differently themed world) this would've easily landed a spot as one of my all time favourite movement shooters; unfortunately it ends abruptly after around a hour of gameplayThe proof of concept was present and the combat loop is so well made that it wouldn't even get old by the 3rd, 4th world, even without new abilities. boomerang x has flawless combat and an incredibly responsive movement system. it's such a missed opportunity to only use this foundation for a hour of game and never again. wished we could've seen a sequel, but sadly due to the studio's recent closure i think this won't be happening.the art is beautiful. the npc writing was fun. the combat is immaculate. music was wonderful. i would recommend this if you like movement shooters but be aware of how short this game is.anyways, i plan on replaying this game a few times! it's an amazing yet bit-sized experience

_childDocuments_.review: Boomerang X. This is kind of a hard one.I do love 98% of what Devolver Digital publishes, so I had to play this.This Game was on my Radar for a while when it was still in announcement but I just recently got the time to play it.The Art and Graphics of this Game are not for everyone, I didn't think it was good neither did I think it was bad.It was serviceable.Storywise, expect nothing much. You are a Mummy, you shipwreck on an Island, you find a Boomerang and kill Shadow Creatures and a Centipede sometimes talk to you about stuff you probably don't care about...at all!That's it.Music was serviceable, Sound as well.This Game was short. The Final Boss took me the longest, died like 4 or 5 times before I got the hang of it.Wouldn't it have been for the Bossfight, the Game would've been over in 90 minutes, so now I clocked in about 2hours for the whole Game.Yes, there is a New Game+, no I didn't play it because I saw no reason to. Maybe some other time when I am really bored. The Gameplay is fun and can get at times quite frantic, but after a few waves my hands got tired a little. As short as it is, this Game demands your attention and sometimes Finger acrobatics. It is a very precise Game regarding to aiming/weak spots and overall it was good.Do I think this Game is worth it? Yes.Full Price? No! Get it on sale or if you are a Speedrunner, because I think this Game caters to speedrunners.Not bad at all...
