_childDocuments_.review: My GOTY. While I can see how the number of waves can get tedious for some, I was never left wishing for shorter encounters or challenges. The bite-sized campaign allowed me to jump right into a NG+ which ratchets things up considerably. Like recent Mario games, I imagine that for veterans of the genre the game doesn't start, in earnest, until after you hit the credits. The various achievements seem to reinforce that notion.What's more, Boomerang X is a trojan horse for Flick Stick. If you want to play shooters on a pad more accurately, please use this game as a Flick Stick trainer. The learning curve may feel steep but I was almost immediately better than traditional control pad aiming.

_childDocuments_.review: I have literally no complaints about this game. This is the perfect movement arena shooter. The gameplay feels phenomenal, this game manages to achieve what so many imo fail, which is giving the player near unrestricted movement, without making the game a cakewalk. The amount and diversity of enemies is just the right amount of overwhelming. The way the different enemy types force you to adjust your strategy while soaring through the air is seriously unbelievable. The game's structure is zero padding; From one arena to the next, each arena is super unique and well designed, the progression feels flawless both in terms of power level and difficulty, you can enable accessibility settings if you're not quite good enough, the game is balanced separately for keyboard and controller, the length of the game is perfect, and there's even a cute little story in there.This is simply how you make a perfect game.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Boomerang X is a mesmerizing acrobatic arena shooter that introduces a mystical boomerang as your primary weapon. With its fluid movement and visually stunning environments, the game immerses you in intense battles against otherworldly creatures. The story, although minimal, serves as a backdrop to the action-packed gameplay.The game offers various game modes, including challenging arenas and engaging levels that push your skills to the limit. The boomerang mechanics are the game's standout feature, allowing for precise throws and satisfying combo chains. The ability to recall the boomerang mid-flight, an air dash and the ability to slow time all add an extra layer of strategic depth.The level design is meticulously crafted, striking a perfect balance between verticality and open spaces. Each level is filled with well-placed power-ups and environmental hazards that keep the gameplay exciting and unpredictable. The difficulty curve is finely tuned, ensuring a challenging yet rewarding experience.Visually, this game is a feast for the eyes, featuring captivating landscapes and stunning creature designs. The atmospheric sound design further enhances the immersive experience, creating a sense of tension and excitement.In conclusion, "Boomerang X" offers a unique and captivating first-person shooter experience. With its mesmerizing boomerang mechanics, engaging game modes, and visually stunning presentation, it's a must-play for gamers seeking exhilarating combat and stylish gameplay similar to Neon White.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: First, yes, it's a fairly small game: took me 6hr to beat, and it's a succession of arena fights. But what fights!It's all about aiming in slow-mo, then teleporting just behind the slain target, constantly moving, never touching ground (which is often lava). Despite using only few buttons, my finger would be sore after beating a stage, from the ceaseless tension, with not a instant of respite until the last wave is dealt with.I kinda dig the graphical style, with its flat lighting and simple textures. And thanks to it, the game stays perfectly readable all throughout.This game is as hyper as the bluemchen song.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome awesome and more awesome. This beautiful fast past game will have you flying around destroying a variety of enemies in a diverse set of environments with your trusty boomerang and many abilities you unlock along the way. Lets start with the visuals and music. The game has a unique style which really caught my eye, I loved every location and enemy, all so cool and beautiful. Every time I went to a new place I wanted to live there. The music is great too its not anything mind blowing, but it really fits the tone of the game. Now for the gameplay, and hoowee is it good! The movement is so fast and fluid, it was so fun to move around the environment even when your not fighting enemies. The enemies are unique and you really get a good sense of the best way to fight each type. The boomerang is really fun and so are the abilities. At first the game is pretty easy, but still fun, but it ramps up to pure chaos with tons of different enemies swarming you. It is never unfair, and you have to choose which enemies are the top priority to kill first. It is a pretty short game, I beat it in three hours with only a few deaths at the end. But with new game plus I'm for sure going to replay the levels. The passion that the creators put into this game really shows and makes for an epic thrill ride of a game. So if your a fan of fast paced action games and you have a few bucks to spend, I would definitely pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I was absolutely blown away by Boomerang X.I saw when this game was first shown off on Devolver's Twitter page, and as a Devolver fan, I knew I had to check it out.Soon after that, a demo released for the game that I played at least 5 times. _childDocuments_.review: Boomerang X is an incredibly fun game to control. You can dash through the air without ever having to land, perform combos to unlock special moves, and kill waves upon waves of enemies, most of which die in one hit. The devs have done a fantastic job polishing the core gameplay. Everything you do is consistently satisfying. The way you follow the boomerang, the way you recall it, the way special moves can be aimed to instantly kill enemies with multiple weakpoints, it's all fantastic. That said, the game is not without issues. Movement is power, and you have ALL of it. While this is incredibly fun, enemies don't really feel threatening. Enemies usually slowly float towards you, chill on the ground where they can't reach you, or they just walk around doing their own thing hoping you will fly into it.Enemies don't really work together, they just exist together in the same space, with the exception of the enemy that creates a shield around other enemies. To compare this with a shooter, you may have one enemy with a sniper, shooting you if you are within their line of sight for long enough, another enemy that shoot gas bombs in your proximity denying you area, and another enemy chasing you down at high speeds. Any one of these are not threatening alone, but together they create a hard to deal with situation. While there are enemies that do different things, such as an enemy summoning explosives, they just slowly float towards you, they are never a threat. There is a frog that shoots goop, but it's rarely towards you, and usually the arena you fight in is so large it has no chance of reaching you. The large areas in this game, while they are incredibly fun to move around in, makes it very hard for enemies to reach you. Even if enemies reach you, you have so much health you are rarely in danger, and if you happen to get hurt, there's plenty of health scattered everywhere. In my playthrough, I only died once and that was to the stage I was in, and not the enemies. The game is at its best when you get cornered and have to think quickly. I especially remember one room where a giant sawblade is summoned, goes up and down covering almost the entire area, and you have to dodge it in order to kill it along with swarms of enemies hunting you. The quick and powerful movement can create for some incredibly satisfying gameplay, and I think with some more enemy variety and enemies that are able to keep up with you, this game can go from good to fantastic.I recommend this game, but it comes with an "but". I recommend it to you if you want to experience the insanely good movement, but you are prepared to quickly roll over anything in your way with little challenge. Or if you like speedruns

Squad".

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome if you like fast-paced shooters or FPS in general with super high mobility. The only dawn side it's the duration, it took me less than 2h to complete it with almost no death, but being a high difficult game at the end you may need more tries taking 1 more hour. Anyway, I totally recommend playing the new game+ because it actually extend the game with the same arenas but way harder, making it last way more hours (depending on your skill) instead of just 2-3. _childDocuments_.review: Boomerang X it's a particular kind of first person shooter, developed by DANG! and published by Devolver Digital.The most remarkable thing is the gameplay, super dynamic and addictive. As you overcome arenas, with different waves of enemies, you learn new skills. This, makes the game have a challenging combat system, very fluid and quite unique.It has a pretty cute art and a soundtrack according to the game style. However, the story and the narrative feel that they are nothing more than an excuse to send you to kill enemies (I am not very happy with the Spanish translation).It is quite short (4-5hs) and, although it is entertaining, I feel that something else is missing. It seems to me that the game is more oriented to speedrunners since it brings time trial modes. Therefore, they will surely enjoy it more and can get more out of it.6/10🧁

_childDocuments_.review: -- Spinning and Winning --One of the things I love about Boomerang X is the build up to your full kit. The game uses the slow build up to teach you how the combat flows and to always be moving. By the time you get more options, the game starts throwing you into more open arenas to really go crazy in.What results is a very natural learning curve. I never felt like I wasn’t given enough time to understand how mechanics worked. The game just feels great to bounce around in, any action game that generates its own rhythm is bound to be a good one.Boomerang X also has a surprisingly good soundtrack, full of strings and drums. All timed so that the end beats play when you defeat the last enemy in a stage.Boomerang X is quite short, about 2 hours. BUT, it has a New Game + mode where (as far as I’ve played) the game gets new enemy placements. Even just for the base 2 hour run, it’s well worth it for the price it’s at.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Boomerang X is a game that will take you, at most, 2 hours to beat. That means you could refund it and save those $20, or you could play it again, and again, and again. This is the type of game where your first run-through is more a demo than anything else. The real game is found as you hone your skills by replaying the stages. It offers the mechanical depth to justify the design, and I know that because I played through the original demo of the game that only had 3 stages 20+ times. I will admit even as someone who really likes the game $20 is a bit steep, but if you can sink your teeth into for a while with the promise of mastering it being enough to push you on, I find no reason you won't Boomerang X.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Boomerang X is a fast-paced action battler in which you use, you guessed it, a boomerang to dismantle an array of shadow creatures, in a uniquely-styled world filled with lore concerning the missing Yoran species. Watch my 8 minute review here: I recommend it, but with the concession that I think it’s not perfect for everyone.  If long, fast-paced action sequences stress you out, then this game is probably not for you, but if you love a good challenge, and that satisfying feeling of nailing an immaculate shot on reflexes alone, then I think you’ll love Boomerang X.  It does have a stylish art direction, and an interesting story and history to decipher in between the lines.  For me, I think fans of games like Ghostrunner and Adverse will probably feel right at home with Boomerang X, and with the speedrun and New Game + options, it provides a good bit of replayability too.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game, it's so good.  The movement is incredible, the design is great, the enemies are fun and interesting, and it rewards skillful play in cool ways.  A ton of fun to play, and my complaints don't outweigh the fun I had with it.  I just have a few gripes, though;-No secrets, no bonus levels, pretty short game overall.  I'd love it to be longer.  It does have a NG+ mode which is cool, but you can beat the main game in about two hours.-I would have expected there to be some sort of "endless mode" or something, where you choose a stage and try to go for a high score, since it would be perfect for this game, but there is not.   A little disappointing.-Final boss is kind of ass.  It looks cool, but the stage is kind of frustrating.  It's a difficulty spike I was absolutely not prepared for.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hard sell. I excitedly downloaded the demo and absolutely fell in LOVE, but after telling all my friends about it...they were VERY mixed. It's extremely fast paced and really wild. The demo also was lacking a few of the features that really put the cherry on top (along with being short in general), though.Not to mention the game itself is completable in under 2 hours, at least for me. There was more content like New Game +, which is supposedly super hard and i'll eventually try, but all I can say is that again..this game is a HARD sell at $20, or so it seems. Try out the demo, and if you vibe with the core mechanics, consider picking it up. Once you get 2-3 things you didn't have in the demo, re-assess and see if you think its worth playing. Thats my strongest case for Boomerang X. Personally, I am just in love with the game in general, so I'd give it an 8-9/10. but for the price? Idk. It's short, so I could see it going as low as 6/10 from a more objective standpoint.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is hard to review. On the one hand, the game is amazing. Fast, visceral and full of amazing movement, the game feels amazing to play, and looks even more amazing. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best movement-based shooters I have ever played! The fast-paced gameplay paired with the wonderful music and visuals creates an exciting experience. Each level finds interesting ways to iterate on the previous one as you progress through the campaign with bosses that demand you apply new strategies to defeat them. By the last level, you'll be using every single thing you've learned to make it out alive. Though it's short, I believe the campaign is the perfect length to showcase all the game mechanics have to offer, especially with the various "Endless Wave" modes you have to satiate your hunger for more. What's more is this is an excellent speed game for anyone who enjoys trying to get that perfect run with flawless execution. TL;dr - If you like the frantic, movement-based gameplay of DOOM Eternal combined with the speed of ULTRAKILL, all tied up with singularly focused combat mechanics like SEKIRO (i.e. one primary weapon w/ the boomerang and your handful of secondary abilities), you cannot go wrong with BOOMERANG X.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I enjoyed this game I have quite a few grievances. First things first is game play itself is a 9/10, very fun.  Makes me kinda sad to have to put it negative but imo this game isn't worth the price ultimately. There's a few design choices choices that just make me shake my head at why. 1. Health pads. In a game that rewards you for being in nearly constant motion, why would you make it take 3 seconds to activate the health pads? Even before the 'late game' almost every single time I tried to use one I immediately got hit for at least the 1 damage healed. Seems like a small thing but it's your only healing method in combat so with this you're basically fighting with your base health bar only. 2. Final boss.  3. Length. At about 3 hours of playtime (45 mins on final boss probably,  almost every other stage passed first try, 30 mins not playing). it's just too short for me. Also as soon as we finally get all the upgrades which make combat really sing, we have 1 combat that's real hard and a boss that's also annoyingly hard. I'd like to say that just one or two combats would have fixed that but realistically this game could have been twice as long, and it'd still be a fairly short game. Devs made such a nice combat system but as soon as you master it you're done. There's a new game+ mode, while appreciated, isn't quite enough to say it is good in the category. 4. Price. I got this game at 10$ and for 3.5 hours of play time it's not great value to me. That full price for the length just isn't acceptable.

_childDocuments_.review: A Missed OpportunityWhere should I start?As the title suggests I feel like there is a lot missing from this game but why do I still recommend it?For me graphics do not matter, my friend described it as "goofy" but I think the art style fits the game perfectly because it is never distracting from the intense combat. I prefer this over the style of Ultrakill and other similar games since I felt overwhelmed by the sometimes over-pixelated graphical aspects. Sound design does the job, for a movement shooter there is not much reliance on sound but the effects are punchy and clear. (note: I have an insanely expensive audio setup, but this should be true for all devices)I'm going to touch on the combat and gameplay loop in one segment. The game introduces the player with mechanics after 1-2 stages, you hit strings to make a rythm which in turn unlocks a new ability. The game gives you a really quick tutorial on the new mechanics introduced then throws you straight into an arena. Now this is all good but here is the problem. These arenas are built to make the player learn these mechanics in action but the game never forces you to actually use them. For some this is a good thing since it introduces variety to the combat, but towards the end of the game newer mechanics feel really useless. Here is an example: the Stomp mechanic, you kill 3 enemies quickly in the air to be able to use this, but besides the introductory arena it becomes completely useless since all the arenas coming after that make zero use of the ability. I wish the boomerang "curving" skill gap had more or I should say, any use cases.Basically, there are an overwhelming amount of mechanics for the length and complexity of the situations you get into. I either barely or never used 2 or 3 of my abilities through out my entire 75 minute play through. (Longer if you care about New Game+)Which leads me to another criticism I have. The enemy variety is really low. This would be fine if the game had occasional boss fights or actual mechanics that punished you, but there are like 5 basic enemies who die to like 3 shots worst case and then a boss fight in the end which was meh. I feel like there are a lot of missing opportunities here.My second the to last paragraph is about the story, or whatever it is? Like, you get introduced to this worm character who tries to give you some ideas about the world you are in but even he doesn't know anything and in the end you won't find any answers or anything.Now it might seem like a lot of negatives, but at the end of the day I still had a fun time playing this game. I'd only recommend buying it on a discount though.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 would pay full price for this game.First play through only takes around 2hrs for most being as this game wants people to speedrun it.Lil arcade game about you washing up on a island that was occupied by ant people that all died from a creature in their mines, you find a boomerang as your one and only weapon against said creature and its spawn. The game is made around this boomerang from its movement, instant return, teleporting to it mid flight, and slow-mo during weapon charging being the main tools you'll use.Combat levels are varied in landscape and environmental hazards from lava floors/"falls" or spikes on walls and ceilings  Areas in-between serve up to act good lull periods with small story telling with help from the one and only NPC Tepan a big bug that likes rat bones and paper (whom you have to talk to twice in every area to get a 6% achievement) Tepan gives you  clues on what happened even tho he was there for the last bit of the ant peoples lives.Enemies are varied and each pose unique threats to you, 5 of which can cause major issues if you dont focus them or your time moving around the area will get harder. From  flying blades, squids, jellyfish, bugs that put shields on weakspots, land sharks, rats, wizards that teleport when you aim at them, monsters that summons more squids and more. A giraffe, big bird, frog  and dragon are the main "bigger" enemies that will pose the biggest threat to you.Final boss was a combination of all environmental hazards and weakspot targeting which is a good challenge for the player mastering their movement mechanics and timing. my only complaint with the boss its the upper part of the area is the only viable area to move around and restricts the players movement even more.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall recommended because it is original and beautiful. Think ABZU + combat. However ,it's not perfect. Many reviewers have commented it's short - I don't mind that. What I mind is that the final two areas use unfair/un-fun difficulty to try and extend the play time. When you have a shooter which has (and is built around) amazing movement at it's core please don't make it difficult by removing that movement through small/overcrowded arenas, floor is lava etc (looking at you giraffe guy). I really didn't find these last two areas fun so switched on the appreciated invincibility cheat mode to complete. Shame to end such a good game on a sour note but would still recommend the overall experience, even at £16 (USD 20) full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is NOT Doom Eternal or Ultrakill. It appears frantic and fast on the surface, but it's a series of on-the-fly plans you make as you zip around the arena. It's a blend of different genre staples that just ended up worse off that sticking with one.It's almost like a turn-based game as you slow time to pick the perfect movement to execute.  It walks a weird mix of intentional movement (The kind you see in soulslikes), but placing it in frantic fights akin to Doom, but also slowing down time is almost a necessity during your first playthrough so it takes on a strategic turn-based-esq feel.Controls are good but a bit unintuitive, as it's easy to dash to your boomerang on accident since the fire and dash are both bound to the left mouse button. Deeper movement options are very hard to nail down in a first person view, and I don't think they quite hit the mark considering how important movement and depth of perception is in this game.There were exactly 2 instances where it REALLY clicked. I was in a state of flow, the fight felt fun to engage in. But that was mired under fights bordering on light frustration that made my overall verdict take a dive.One thing I can say is that the enemy variety and abilities you have are very fun, at least in concept. In fact I liken this game to Ghostrunner. Having a single attack that can one-shot enemies just doesn't lend itself to engaging gameplay, at least for both of these titles. There's not much variation possible.Boomerang X definitely has something going for it, but some issues, chief among them being arena design and enemy placement/types can lead to an experience that was confused on what exactly it wanted to be.It was a concoction that just didn't do it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: If you like flying through the air at high speeds while killing enemies, then you will like Boomerang X. I highly recommend this game to any movement shooter fans!What I like:- high degree of air movement freedom- Combat arenas has lots of verticality and environmental hazards to challenging your movement- Creative enemy designs that will test your movement skills- Abilities are powerful but requires some techniques to be effective- NG+ mode and Endless mode offers replayability- Challenging Steam achievements- Gameplay is easy to learn but hard to masterWhat I don't like:- I don't really like the music, but music taste is subjective so your opinions might differ- I don't like staying on the shield recharge platforms to recharge the shields, it goes against the fast-paced gameplayMore information:- This game is short, you can finish it in 3-4 hours- There is no story besides some dialogue from just one NPC in the whole game, and even that is skippable. Your character is just a nameless faceless mute protagonist. I think story is not important in video games, but some people might disagree- This game has a simple progression system: you unlock new abilities and get more shields along the way but there is no way to customize your loadout. I personally think it is a good design choice to avoid cluttering the game with unnecessary features, but some people might want more customization- There is not much stuff between the arenas besides dialogue, ability unlocks and tutorials. On one hand it might seem a bit monotonous to do the arenas directly one after another, but on the other hand adding puzzles and platforming between arenas might stretch out the game with these unnecessary "filler" sections.

_childDocuments_.review: An action wave survival game where you zip around the map using a mystic boomerang and different traversal abilities that it gives you, along with  slo mo and other neat gifts. I just eventually found the game got less fun as the number of waves got larger and failing meant having to start over and do it all over again.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Very basic concept, very short game, go around throw a boomerang at the enemies marked yellow in little arenas trying not to bump into them to lose health or otherwise you die, unlock some abilities along the way, talk to a standing centipede and come across a bunch of giant dead ants.prepare to have your left hand pinky want to commit suicide as you repeatedly hold down the shift key just to line up your boomerang shots in slow mo while avoiding lazer beams and random crap thrown your way.Its an ok game i just can't recommend it as a positive given how short it is plus the pinky pain.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: This short and sweet of this review is: too short. I was able to beat all of the base content in under 2 hours, and typically I tend to adhere to the "quality over quantity" sentiment when it comes to most games. But the lack of structure in terms of player progression, and busted player mechanics does not warrant this game having a $20 price tag. --PROS--1) Plenty of enemy variety2) Maps are well designed 3) Boomerang mechanics are consistent for the most part.--CONS--1) Lack of content2) Rushed player progression, which ultimately waters down the combat3) Choppy performance (not in terms of fps, but the engine seems barely able to handle how ungodly fast your movement speed is)
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay is really fun when flying around with the boomerang, but I've already ran into a bunch of weird design choices when it comes to the arenas and the enemies that you're fighting. The enemies themselves are annoying to fight, either not giving any real threat or teleporting with this game's very inky art style, making them hard to spot where they went to before they teleport again. I've also already encountered several enemies with weak spots that are hidden until they do a certain move, which breaks the pace that the game is trying to go for. I think I would've honestly liked it more as a platforming game instead of an arena shooter.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great art direction and controls amazingly well--even on a controller. Both of these combine for some great combat and I did enjoy the game. However, I cannot recommend it because of the cost. Personally, I feel as though $20 for a 2 hour game is just too much even if the game is pretty fun. Nonetheless there is NG+ and an endless mode with a leaderboard, so if either of these appeal to you the price may be justified. For me, $10 for each hour of fun just was not worth it when there are a lot of other games that will give me more bang for my buck (e.g., Ghostrunner).
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: This game did everything right except two things:- The repetition of the SFX from calling the boomerang back with right-click is insufferable.- It takes forever for the game to (allegedly) throw interesting combat encounters at you.I have no idea if the combat becomes anything more than a snoozing slog, because after the 6th consecutive time being put to fight the same series of waves of boring, generic-looking, uninteresting enemies, looking for the ones the game wants me to kill rather than asking me to kill all of them, or rather, give me something engaging to fight, I ended up quitting and refunding it. Boomerang X felt like biting into a delicious chocolate truffle and finding an olive inside of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most useless purchase I've made in a while. I can't remember for how long I played, but what I did end up playing was extremely boring. I made it to a bit after the multi-kill powerup when I just stopped playing. _childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted another Doom 2016 kind of game but this wasn't it for me.I recognize that some people could very well like this game but i didn't find the gun (boomerang) play satisfying.Doom is the king of impact when it comes to guns etc. The boomerang and the enemies in this game aren't bad but they're not for me.Movement is good but not incredible. Also as you can see i didn't play that much. 1.5/5.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Is Boomerang X great? Hell yeah! Is it overpriced? Hell yeah! It's fun, fast-paced, and addictive, but it's also not even 2 hours long. The movement is smooth and precise. Flying through the air with your boomerang swarmed by enemies just activates the neurons in such a special way. I was staring at my screen at the edge of my seat barely blinking. There's great enemy variety and some cool huge monsters. No matter how busy it gets, it never loses frames. Buttery smooth performance. Levels are basically arenas and they're varied with a unique color theme. The presentation is excellent. The game looks beautiful. It's super sleek and stylish like a painting brought to life. The soundtrack is energetic matching the fast pace. I don't have much to say about the story. What story? There's one NPC who says some vague statements and that's about it. I don't understand what's happening, but it was fun to play. It's just incredibly short. I could probably beat this in an hour honestly. $20 is crazy. Get it 50% at least. (8/10)
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: It's cool, but won't be for everyone. Love the originality of the concept & fluidity of the artwork, but the gameplay itself (the main selling point) is just a bit too weird for me to get used to. I only died a handful of times, but I always felt like I was endlessly flailing around, especially towards the end of the game.With that said - there are a lot of accessibility options for making the game easier or tweaking it to your liking, so you may find a way to make it work for you.Pick it up on sale, if you like shooters!
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Boomerang X is an incredible game. I think it is the most original movement shooter I have ever seen in my entire life! And it's super well executed👌 The game is fun, it's pretty, it's extremely readable (as a game dev myself I'm super impressed by the work you guys have done on the signs and feedbacks). I don't want to get ahead of myself but it might be the best game I have played in this entire year!Too bad the studio had to close, I hope you guys will find the money to make another game someday❤️
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Not counting the demo which is 35% of the game because it doesn't count to refund time and new game + , I got to and killed the final boss in 65 minutes. Now I want to love this game, the environments, the creature design and Tepan are all amazing things but for £16.75? I am a cheapskate but for about 2 hours of content and just re-doing everything with a + smacked onto it that's not value. I won't be refunding however because I want to play endless and new game + for the steam trophies. If you want to get it, wait for Devolver Digital to do a sale, it's usually under £5 then. Last update was 2 years ago and I think the developer went bankrupt or something so don't expect any updates anymore. At a fiver i'd say this game is great value, it's very unique and will probably keep my adrenaline requirements satisfied until Hakita gets layer 3 out for Utrakill. Good game, my scale 6.8/10, thank you FUNKe for shedding light onto this game, if you're even out there anymore (with last video being a year ago).
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Very short game but fairly enjoyable, honestly feels more like a demo then a fully fleshed out game. The core mechanics are fully functional and great, but just when the game finally presents a challenge and finally pushes its mechanics the game just kind of ends. I also felt like a lot of the mechanics end up restricting the way you play, I think the game is at its best when you fly around and hack down enemies, but the game really wants you to be methodical and to kill specific enemies. It will hide the enemies weakpoints and create enemies that make other enemies immune. Later on there are so many enemies that it really hard to tell what I was getting hit by. All of this sounds frustrating but when the game is at its best its really good, due to those annoying aspects I ended up not wanting to replay the game but for those that really like pushing scores and replaying difficult sections this can be very fun.Overall I will recommend this but at a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Short game, but very replayable. The gameplay and mechanics are unique and its really fun to just fly around the room slicing and blasting enemies. The rough visual style and abrasive, somewhat unsettling music fit the game wonderfully. However, do not buy this game for full price. Unless you are going for 100% completion, 20$ is not worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The mechanics are easy to learn but take some time to master. The movement is fluid and the abilities are fun. If all you want to do is one play through it is a short game of about 2hrs depending on ability.If you are like me and you like to 100% some games then there are a lot of fun challenges to do. If I was a better player I'd have done them in less time but here we are.If after getting all the achievements done and you still want something to do there are endless modes with global leader boards to strive for or you could become a speed runner.It has a good amount of accessibility options should you need them.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet fast faced, arena FPS. Each arena feels very unique and presents its own challenges. The art style, while simple was pretty cool, though they don't distract you nor make it difficult to see what's going on in the thick of it. The game controls well and your actions feel snappy. It definitely has that "easy to learn, hard to master" feel to it, that once you get the hang of it, you feel pretty dang cool. This also goes to make the new game plus feel like it is a pretty good add if you do wish to sink your teeth into it. I honestly think that it is good that the game is relatively short as the very high intensity arenas wear you down pretty quick and while new abilities are introduced throughout, the game would get samey if they decided to drag it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Like most of Devolver's releases, the gameplay is tight, the art style is unique, and the soundtrack is catchy and fitting to the aesthetic. Also like most of Devolver's releases, it's way overpriced. There's a dozen levels here (plus a boss battle) that are designed for speed, with additional game modes and achievements for speedrunning. If you're really skilled you can probably beat this in an hour or less... It's definitely worth playing but it's way too short for the asking price. There's just not enough content here to write a meaningful review about; you're given a constant feed of new toys, seemingly hopping between teaching lessons on them, and then the game is done. Recommended because the game is good even though the price isn't.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: short movement "shooter", starts easy but as you gain new ability it ramps up decently fast. A few different endless enemies modes which are cool but I never got into. It has bugs I like bugs (literal bugs not game-play issues I never had any of those) oh yeah art style is really appealing and music is nice. I love the many creature designs did i say I like bugs
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece of an FPS. I hesitate to even call it an FPS because of the style and ideas behind it, but it's a good game nonetheless.The gameplay is difficult to master at first, but once you do, it feels like second nature. I'd recommend getting practice and reprogramming your brain a little bit. This isn't your average FPS. It's more of a skill-based pixel perfect platforming game mixed with very unconventional iterations of classic FPS ideas. It's fast, frantic, energetic, all of it. It keeps your heart pumping from start to finish.Somehow, they managed to fit a lot of abilities into such a simple concept. I thought it was just going to be the boomerang, but they proved me wrong.The music is phenomenal. It switches between atmospheric and driving, while maintaining whimsy and dark intensity through every single note. I legitimately felt like I did better at the game with the music.I wish more games looked like this. The stylized look is unlike anything I'd expect from a video game. It just goes to show: if you have an idea for a unique art style, you should just go for it.Honestly, the only "weak" thing is the story. And even then, it works. It's just not super prevalent. It's more for lore sake, and to explain a final goal, rather than a moment-to-moment thing. Which makes sense, because the game is so short.Overall, can't recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Thumbs up for being a novelty FPS. This is an arena based FPS with a gimmick that often made me break up my play sessions. If there were ever an FPS that made my fingers ache, it's this one. I enjoyed the game in short bursts, often finding myself needing a break. Zipping through the air feels great and there are some pretty cool enemy designs later in the game that will put your reflexes to the test.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Cool, fast paced and fun game. Beat first NG in 3 hours on mostly autopilot but there is clearly much higher levels of difficulty waiting for me. Its fun because of the gradual learning curve of challenges and new mechanics it throws at you until the final boss, so you get to build up knowledge and get used to the controls at your own pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: A very short game with decent difficulty, however after beating new game+ my game will no longer launch. I have seen no one else with the same issue or how to fix it. the game is still good and if you're not me worth the money when buying it on sale as the price matches the quality just not the length.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine in your mind a bubble shaped room with tens of tentacle like floating enemies flying towards the player character. And then imagine player that's only equipped with boomerang that player can throw ahead, call the boomerang back to player or player dash towards where boomerang is thrown, and player swings that boomerang so actively that player never need to touch the ground.When you think such situation, it sounds something you could imagine a kid cartoon tv-show about ninjas/ samuri or anime tv-serie would be pulling off and if you tried to execute it on video game you would face game design problems like tentacles being too slow to show any danger to player or player dashing to enemies constantly which would lead player taking damage and getting frustrated.Boomerang X solves those and many other problems, and fills that promise well and it's a blast 2-3 hours experience that speed runners would never be able to put down.In short Boomerang X is a combat-game that's equipped with distinctive art style, minimal story and long combat encounters where player's only handheld weapon is boomerang. Of course during the campaign player unlocks few upgrades like shotgun blast and ground punch, but in order to use these player must get triple kill or tree kills without touching the ground. Only upgrades that player gets to use are nice additions, though the final unlock called  was underwhelming and I wish it would have cleared whole room in an instant like BFG round.If you are into 2-3 hours long combat arena experience that delivers in it's premise and don't mind lack of highly detailed story/ plot, Boomerang X is great pick on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: The hell? this game is WAY too good to be as short as it is.  feels like it should be JUST starting at Vashkatar, which is one hell of a boss, but a grim reminder at the same time on how short this whole experience is. I can't help but imagine what this game would've turned out to if they had this level of quality gameplay for at least 2 more chapters of the same length. Stings even harder hearing about the studio shutting down. Awesome game, but honestly feels more like a demo than an actual full fledged game. Very awesome nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: One of the sickest shooters I've ever played. Boomerang X looked at games like DOOM Eternal and Ultrakill where you can't stand still and said 'ok but what if you could ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fly' and it works perfectly. It's an incredibly short game but it's hard to complain when the entire thing is perfectly paced without a single moment of frustration or boredom.A flawless version of what it's trying to be, Boomerang X's only sin is that it ends.R.I.P. DANG
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: This was quite a stressful and tense game, but it does it in a way that is fun. You feel a sense of accomplishment when completing a chapter. And whenever I died, I didn't feel angry or wanting to quit. I wanted to try again and keep playing. It's just something about flying around and throwing a ninja star at enemies. The enemies are also very balanced, to where they aren't extremely easy to where it feels boring, but they aren't extremely hard where it feels impossible. Also a wide variety of enemies with different ways to counteract and kill. Definitely not a game to sit down and relax with, but it's very fun nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very solid fast-paced arena shooter. That might be all you need to hear from me to pick it up, but if you need more...Each level places you in a different arena with multiple waves, and you have to boomerang all of the marked enemies to clear each wave. As you progress through the game you unlock different abilities which fundamentally change your playstyle, until you're completely kitted-out at the end. By the end of the game, the floor is entirely optional and you typically just whip around all over the place. Bullet time is an early ability you unlock and it helps a ton, but you can play without it (and you have to for some achievements, if that's something you care about).The main campaign is relatively short, but there is a NG+ which gives you everything to start with and is significantly harder. There's also an endless mode which I found very rewarding -- different endless modes allow you to use only some of your abilities which adds some much-needed variety. The gameplay may get a bit stale near the end once you master all the abilities, but the movement and combat feels too tight and fun for me to care much.$20 USD might be a bit steep considering the amount of content you get -- I have 13.2 hours as of writing, and I have all of the achievements including the difficult endless mode ones -- so maybe consider picking it up on sale. However, I think it's a solid (albeit short) addition to any arena shooter fan's collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: What a game. The movement is so fluid, and you quickly feel unstoppable, flying through the air and dashing all over the place.Don't get me wrong, it's not easy, and you will die. But it feels so good zipping around.And even when you feel like you're on your top game, they'll find new toys and new abilities to give you for you to master.It's a short game, but the time with it is incredible.I know Ng+ has all encounters remade, and i can't wait to get back into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Boomerang X is a wonderfully fun first-person platforming shooter that was very enjoyable to play. I found the art style and graphics to be beautiful and clear for gameplay. Your only weapon is a boomerang that looks like a shuriken, and how can use it to do all sorts of moves and a few combos. There are many enemies to defeat, some of which must be hit at specific weak points highlighted in red by default. Its rather short, taking me only about 4 hours to beat on my first attempt [when first saw the ending cutscene, I thought it would be the beginning of some second level or stage], however it is very replayable and there are other gamemodes to try and achievements to unlock. Overall, it is a great movement shooter that is worth a purchase if you want a fun game to play over the weekend.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique games I've played with a similar feel to "Ghostrunner". Overall just a great game with super fun mechanics and fast paced action/combat, the environment of the game is also great and matches perfectly with the game-play. Despite its short runtime, it remains an “all killer no filler” experience. A tougher new game + mode encouraged me to launch headfirst into a second playthrough immediately.Full Review:

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game with a nice aesthetic, tight controls, and brilliant progression that doesn't waste your time. The base game was quite easy imo but new game+ gave me the fun challenge I was looking for, and lets you use the movement and shooting mechanics to their fullest potential.I got this on sale which was well worth the price. _childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible. The fast paced action coupled with the badass slow-mo "Flux" ability make you feel truly like a powerhouse. Such a simple set of rules and abilities with an almost endless amount of tech you can perform. The progression system teaching you each new mechanic feels very natural and really lets you get used to your new abilities. The unique style of the game adds just that extra special something that truly makes this game stand out from the pack.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty weird and unique indie movement shooter. It's short, but fun while it lasted.I'm not a fan of games that repeat the same boss phases multiple times though, would be better if they created a third (unique) phase instead, but oh well.Would buy on big discount, full price is a bit high for only a few hours of gameplay, unless you want to play NG+ or endless mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet to a masterful degree. The story is interesting and easy to digest, the environments and overall visual style is incredible, and the gameplay is perfectly fast and hectic. There was never an instance where I stepped into a new arena and wasn't impressed or exited to see how the fight would proceed. Only complaint would be the price tag, but otherwise I can't not suggest this game both on or off sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was weary of the weird control scheme but I quickly got used to it due to the almost picture perfect game design. Every time a mechanic was introduced I felt like it gave me the space to learn and understand it and slowly unfolded from me futzing around with a boomerang figuring out how I should move with it to perfectly using each ability in tandem wrecking everything I saw in my way without taking damage almost in a zen like state.If you are into game design this is how you do it even if it's extremely short even on the long end 2-3hrs with deaths I think it's a worthwhile experience. Despite me only having an hour and change I had an extremely enjoyable experienceSadly I still cannot recommend fully at $20 due to it's length but if it's on sale go for it you won't regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: I have completed this game fully. Every achievement and a full no-hit without any aids or assists. I'm a bastard with a death wish, and this game really slayed.The negative reviews say, "This game is so easy" but also say "standing still to recover shield is not intuitive to gameplay," which is a contradiction. It is often risky to stay still for a second for a shield instead of just going ape with your rang. And even when you ARE standing still, you can still fight completely fine. You're just the boomerang monkey from Bloons Tower Defense, buddy. It's also meant to have a super accessible skill floor but a super high skill ceiling, like Ultrakill. The air control is also super intuitive, but you're also fighting your own momentum. You might not be able to turn on a dime when you launch yourself into a lava wall or spike pit because of a mistake. It happens. That's why spacebar is an airbrake and why you can flux, turn around, and pivot on a dime with your weapon.Flux is great because it slows down the game SO much. This is definitely a speed-runner's paradise, because would you rather beat a level in 5 minutes or 30 seconds? Flux is training wheels, like playing YOMI Hustle and watching the gameplay without pauses. This game is Doom on crack, and I highly suggest Endless. The score counter, skill usages, and wave-based system is hit after hit. When things get so crazy that the game is way too fast even in FLUX? It hits. You can even tell what enemies spawned by what instruments are being used in the music score. It's... so intuitive. I genuinely only have one problem with this game, and it's that the boomerang sometimes goes through the ground floor when thrown downwards. Sometimes. This stops you from being able to do pogo jumps, unintentionally ruining your Air Kills and tossing you lightspeed at the ground. Oh, also, more content would be awesome. RIP DANG! This is one of a kind.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! Played it all on the deck in handheld mode and it played very well. The aim assist for controllers can be too strong at times especially when aiming at the door (for some reason it aims above the red dot), but during combat it is flawless. It is a short game (finished it in two hours), but the two hours was paced very well with new mechanics, new powers, and new types of enemies introduced regularly.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Although a short game with a new game+ option that I didn't really care to try much of, it's very fun to fling yourself all over the place with the boomerang. Definitely worth picking up on a sale for less than $10 I'd say. There are some other achievements and modes you can try out if you're more of a completionist, but it's still fun for a casual player too.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Full campaign took me around 2.5 hours, totally worth it. There were several moments where I noticed that I hadn't blinked for like a full minute; it's that kinda thrill. Full-on flow-state chaos!Expect to get your ass whooped on the last level and the final boss. After writing this, I'm gonna tackle new game plus and maybe try for some of these insanely tough achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played a good few movement fps, this is truly the cream of the crop, every single mechanic feels extremely well thought out and fun to use, and although the game can get pretty hard, it never felt frustrating or insurmountable, because no two attempts would ever be the same as I weaved around hundreds of enemies and attacks in brand new, fun ways, and when you finally start to get the hang of everything, this game can make you feel absolutely godlike, so if you love a short and sweet experience with a high skill ceiling, I highly recommend this game, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with tight movement and an amazing final boss, but it is very short. I'm fairly experienced with movement shooters and beat it in 80 minutes. You can literally beat the game before the 2 hour refund window is up, though there is a new game plus mode that revamps the arenas and makes them much harder with different enemy placement, that would probably extend the game to about 3 hours. I can't recommend the game at base 20$ price unless you plan to do every single achievement. Wait for it to go on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: I do think this game is worth it if you like an arena shooter with a lot of movement.Calling this game hectic is an understatement. While you are learning you are zipping through the level with little to no planning, while the later stages require some thinking for them to be even close to finishing them. It has a great learning curve, even when the last two stages are just amazing, while really hard at the same time. If you like movement based shooters, this one is a blast. Has lots of challenge with just the main story and lots to come in the NG+ that makes all arena battles renewed with tougher enemies, while keeping it balanced with your abilities. I really recommend it on a discount and if you want more, try the endless runs. While the NG+ and endless runs are not really for me, I can see the appeal for some people. Piling challenge over challenge. Have fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, fast paced mayhem. Like others have noted, the campaign itself is a bit short, but that doesn't mean the game doesn't offer ways to extend your gameplay. New Game+ mode revamps the enemy set in every single arena, and endless mode offers a completely new challenge. The fun of games like this isn't how long the story mode is from start to finish, it's how long you can spend honing your skills and enjoying the gameplay.After 6 hours, I've run through the story mode and New Game+, I haven't put time in endless mode yet. With few core mechanics to learn, this game is the definition of "easy to learn, hard to master". The mechanics synergize perfectly for fun and engaging combat. Replayability is high.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Fast, fluid movement-Unique mechanics using the boomerang-Slomo in the air allows you to tactically choose your next move and helps aim-Good enemy variety that require different strategies-Good progression of abilities piled on player-Music is great and fits the action-Cute little centipede friend (or is it a millipede?...mmh)-Sick boss fight to end the game with-New game + for extra challenges-Good variety of pretty levels-Really fun when things get hectic and you need to constantly fly around-Easy to run on most machinesCons-Very short (beat it in 3 hrs, +1 hr of new game+), but sweet-Can be pretty hard for people not used to FPS, or action games in general-Story is tacked-on and pretty irrelevant-...honestly I'm trying really hard here but can't think of any other con...-A bit pricey for the quantity of content, but quality makes up for it. Still worth it if you're up for a challenge.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Don't have much to say about it. Amazing game, fun Gameplay that feels like you just had 3 Coffees and need to do something to release all that energy. The Game can be beaten rather quickly (As can be seen by my current time in it) but damn I enjoyed every second of it to the fullest. Great Enemy variety and very responsive Controls combined with a nice Arsenal of "Weapons" (Its more abilities for your boomerang but youll see when you play it) make for one hell of a time.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Boomerang X is a simple, yet satisfying game that you can complete in under 2 hours which is both a good and a bad thing. Good because the game is super fun and never feels like it's dragging on. Where it becomes bad is in the fact that the game is $20 normally. And outside of achievement hunting there's not a whole lot to do in the game once you've beaten the final boss (who is pretty fun to fight against). I'd wait for a discount if a under 2 hour game doesn't sound appealing to you
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: What you're getting here is a visually glamorous package condensed to the core with blades, beauty, and bugs (like the insects). I enjoyed it so much that I played it a second time. I never was one to think boomerangs are cool, and they aren't, but in this game they totally are cool! I'd recommend waiting for a good sale because $20 for a 2 hours is really steep, but those 2 hours are clean concentrated, and control immaculately. Give it a chance and this game'll treat you to a night of hot steamy sensual madness, and the next morning you'll wake up noticing on your cheek the crust of a dried tear that beckons a memory so faint yet forever pierced into your heart. 6/10, $20 is too much, I beat this game in one night.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Boomerang X is one of the tightest, most streamlined, and most to-the-point games I've played in recent memory. If you value playtime per dollar spent you might not appreciate this game as much, but if—like me—you value short experiences that stick to the point and don't overstay their welcome, this game is for you!It gets you to the action quickly, teaches you the mechanics at just the right pace, and then ramps up the challenge so that you always feel like you're on your back foot without ever being too difficult or frustrating. I found I had to tweak the controls a bit to find what worked for me, but from the moment it clicked I was in that wonderful bliss of flow state for the full ~2.5 hours it took me to finish it.Well worth the $12 bucks I paid on sale. Might not vouch for it at the full $22.79 CAD pricetag though.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cool game with a nice moveset. I love the art style and the different worlds feel interesting. Of course the goal is not to explore, but it feels good to progress in this world. The game is a bit short for some, but I like short game so I think it's pretty neat. My only complaint is that the enemies and the combat can feel a bit repetitive. Maybe its my fault for always doing the same thing, but I can't help thinking there should havbe been something else to renew the combat. I don't know exactly what though.Overall great game, I recommend

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game by DANG! Boomerang X is a fast-paced, momentum-driven first-person action game in which you fight waves of enemies in various arenas. The art, creature design, dynamic music, and overall aesthetic are all stellar, but where the game shines most is in its combat mechanics, particularly the flow of the combat and movement loop, which is one of the best of all time, rivaling that of DOOM (2016/Eternal).It's a game in which you never want to stop moving and you never even have to touch the ground. Your weapon is an X-shaped boomerang (go figure) that you can throw and then either recall or warp to, allowing you to endlessly fly around the arena. Additionally, you can charge your shot to make it travel further and while charging you can slow time, allowing you to line up a shot on an enemy's weak point, survey the arena, or dodge fast-coming projectiles like Neo in the Matrix. There are other abilities which I will not spoil and you get a new one just about every level so the combat never gets stale. The difficulty curve feels perfectly tuned and the combat is so intuitive that it quickly becomes second nature, allowing both the difficulty and your mastery of the combat to ramp up at a rapid pace. The later levels will make you sweat but when you complete them you feel like a god.It took me about 2.5 hours to beat but your mileage may vary depending on your skill. I don't have an issue with the length because every second of what's there is so focused. It never becomes redundant or overstays its welcome, plus there's a New Game+, Endless Mode, and a ton of challenging achievements for those who want more. I imagine this would make an incredibly fun speedrun as well. In my opinion, a game of this quality is well worth the $20, even if you only choose to put 2 or 3 hours into it.I'm struggling to think of a bad thing to say about it. No notes. No performance issues, no annoyances, not an ounce of fat to be trimmed from it. It's one of the best action games I've played in ages. If you like adrenaline-pumping, kinetic action games and crave something with creative and original combat mechanics, this is a must-buy.(Note: I'd highly recommend playing with keyboard and mouse, since twitch responses and precision aiming are everything in this game, but there is also an option to balance the game for controller, which is nice. I'd also recommend binding two of the later abilities to separate keys so you don't have to swap between them in the heat of combat.)
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Cool concept, its taken pretty far, but the game is pretty short. Really fun. I wish it had more interesting movement options than just boomerang. But that is the point of the game, so I guess that's just me. Story was a lot more interesting than I thought it was going to be. The boss fights were super cool. This would be a great speed running game.Cool game 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the game in a bit over an hour, very fun all round. I absolutely adore the visuals and the sound design, both are phenomenal. At the time of writing this i havent tried the endless mode, or anything apart from the base story mode itself, but will definitely find myself coming back to this when i have some time to kill and some Boomerangs to X. The arena areas in the main game are very arcade-y (you can get achievements for speed or other small challenges) which is very nice, brings a natural instinct to retry as much as you can to get just under that time threshold.There's a certain muscle memory when it comes to the more frantic arenas in the game, but it works wonders with a fairly forgiving seeming hurtbox for the player, i felt like i was slipping in and out of enemy models half the time, which was a fun thing ngl.Overall, incredibly fun, gorgeous both visually and sound-wise, simple story- doesn't overstay it's welcome and more importantly just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ blast to play.Will return with an edit if i ever feel any different, but its a pretty solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Boomerang X is a very well made indie with a lot of good going for it. The art style is gorgeous and every dungeon is more beautiful than the last. Abilities earned along the way are quite useful (Though you're barred from using one of the coolest abilities if you want to earn all the achievements) and the pace of earning them is well balanced.I feel the games only negatives are a slight repetitiveness, its lack of a real story and the fact that there's only one true boss. _childDocuments_.review: A really unique game that consists of using a Boomerang as your main tool of mobility and aggression, with 4 amazing and useful abilities. _childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I didn't expect to enjoy as much as I did, but it really feels unlike anything I've ever played before. First of all, its fast-paced gameplay really forces you to get good at the game very quickly, and doesn't feel overly difficult. Moreover it doesn't throw all of its mechanics at you at once, it gives you a long fight or two in between where the map and enemies are designed to teach you how to optimize your playstyle and abilities. The art style is very unique; it's simple enough that players can quickly distinguish between each enemy (which is great for a fast-paced game like this), but the style is not visually-cluttered either. It almost feels like a bullet-hell game in first person, which makes it all the more satisfying when you are able to avoid getting hit by an enemy completely. The focus of this game was not the story, it included minimal dialogue with a silent protagonist; I believe this aided the game, as its main focus is the combat. However, the work that went into the diverse maps really pulled the world of Boomerang X together. Overall a very excellent game from an excellent developer!
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely a great game. Definitely short, it took me about 3 hours to beat the campaign, but it's VERY replayable and an total blast to master. It runs great, I didn't encounter any bugs (well, I did encounter some Arthropods), and personally I find the art style to be very pleasing. The movement is difficult to learn, but eventually you'll be soaring around the arena destroying flocks of enemies without even thinking of touching the ground. I recommend Boomerang X to anyone with an itch for a different, fast, and unique kind of shooter. But I can understanding wanting to wait for a sale. I really hope that with some more support we can see an equally fun and even bigger project from this team!
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic gameplay. Constantly flying through the air while chaining boomerang throws and special abilities is immensely satisfying and reminds me of the frenetic gamepllay found in games like Titanfall 2 and Doom Eternal. I had absolutely no interest in the story nor was I forced to engage with it. To me this is a game which is driven entirely by it's excellent gameplay design.

_childDocuments_.review: Immensly fun little gem! Boomerang X really stands out with its unique visuals and constantly evolving gameplay.First, the visuals. I don't have to tell you how unique is this game's visual style, just look at these screenshots! Its very minimalistic and I feel like it really suits Boomerang X fast paced gameplay, by not distracting you with unnecessary details. At the same time enemies are clearly visible with their inky shapes and red weak points. It all gels together perfectly.Music is also a great fit with its tribalistic tones. You can hear it grow more ominous and urgent the closer you get to the finale. Sound design is spot on as well, with each sound serving as a signal of incoming danger or challenge ramping up.Gameplay is the strongest aspect of Boomerang X. Its very unique and fast paced. You are contstantly unlocking new powers, which keeps it all fresh and interesting. One of the first powers you unlock is Flux, which allows you to slow down time, giving you a few seconds to aim your boomerang throw or quickly evaluate your situation. You can also recall your boomerang or pull yourself towards it, which allows you to stay midair almost constantly and helps with getting out of tricky situations.While the game is rather short it offers quite a lot of replayability. After finishing the campaign you unlock New Game Plus mode, which offers MUCH greater challenge by remixing enemy composition for every arena. That alone can extend your playtime greatly, but endless mode with leaderboards have also been added for those who enjoy pushing themselves to the limit. You can also try to unlock some of the achievements by beating par times and finishing arenas without using Flux.Overall I recommend Boomerang X for players who enjoy challenging, fast paced Fist Person Shooters and all manner of speed runners. Its not really a game for casual gamers because of its difficulty and length. I felt like I saw almost all this game had to offer after 3,2 hours of playtime, but I'm definitely replaying it at some point and want to try beating NG+.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this with high expectations, and the game delivered on every front. This is one of the best games I've played all year, and I highly recommend it. If you like games with extremely tight controls and a great sense of movement, then you need to play this. The game starts off simple, with a Boomerang attack, which you can recall, however, the more you play, the game introduces more moves, as well as increasing your health by 1. The game nails the difficulty curve, with the starting levels training you to understand the flow of movement, and with later levels fully expecting you to use every move at your disposal. After a few levels, you'll see little incentive to remain on the ground, and will be flying across the arena, utilizing everything you've learned against a variety of enemy types that manipulate the air around you. Seeing tons of enemies on-screen becomes less intimidating as you learn to prioritize the targets you need to get to, since there are always specific enemies in each wave that you have to take out. The slow-mo ability works pretty well, and you never feel OP, because it becomes downright essential when timing your throws. The world is beautiful, with varied areas, and the game has tons of accessibility options as well. There's also some light world-building, with one NPC you can talk to, but it's more about setting the tone rather than telling a story.The game never felt cheap to me, and you can always see where you messed up. It’s challenging, for sure, and failing near the very end of a level can be a bit frustrating, but it feels glorious when you come back and finish it without barely taking any damage.The game is a bit on the shorter side, but it still took me a good 4 and a half hours to beat it, even though plenty of Steam reviews mentioned a 2-hour length. I think it's worth it, and the level of polish justifies the price.

_childDocuments_.review: The team behind BoomX certainly went out of their way to craft an enjoyably short, but sweet experience. For fans of old arena shooters, or those wanting to try something new to challenge themselves with, this a great little time killer to grind. The combat feels fluid and fun, despite there only being 1 weapon. What you do with the weapon ended up becoming one of my favorite shooter sandboxes to have fun in. Different enemies challenge you to change your strategy as rounds drag on, and can lead to some interesting combat scenarios as by the end you have to fly through the air constantly to survive, and it's a great difficulty curve that forces you into Hugo Martin's patented "fun zone".But what really grabbed my attention was the amazing controller support and the fact that this is one of the first games to natively support both gyro aiming and Jibb Smarts Flick stick. A controller aiming method that can rival mouse aiming for controllers, and is how I've been playing all my shooters with on pc for over a year. It's because of this support for it on not only pc, but console as well that I'm nominating this game for "Most Innovative Gameplay" for 2021's steam awards. If you have a PS4 controller, I very much recommend anyone try gyro and flick stick with mouse difficulty settings for this game. Good luck @DANG!.
_childDocuments_.name: Boomerang X

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal! Boomerang X doesn't overstay its welcome--It delivers gorgeous sketch-like visuals and some of the most satisfying, high-flying, slow-motion combat ever to grace a mouse-and-keyboard. By the final sections, you'll spend minutes without touching the ground!In-between perfectly-paced combat sections, DANG! have filled the world of Boomerang X with fun, subtle world-building and a lonely, lovable centipede.My only regret: There isn't more! I'm not sure if we can hope for a sequel to Boomerang X, but you can believe I'll be in line for whatever DANG! dreams up next.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just blatantly plagiarize some of the other reviews here and echo DANG!, DANG! has made a truly excellent game here! Boomerang X is the best one-sitting experience I've had all year, fusing some truly thrilling action setpieces with a lush visual style that I'm absolutely ga-ga for.  Seriously, this game has such an incredible palette and textural style I was wowed from the very jump, I don't think I've seen anything else pull of this style quite as well as Boomerang X does.Gameplay-wise, the core mechanic of Boomerang X revolves around the iterative improvement of your titular boomerang (X), which starts as a clumsy projectile and ends up as a scatter-shotting tele-fragging rail-gunning dream machine! One of the earliest power-ups you get in the game allows you to slingshot yourself towards your thrown boomerang, which allows you to string together some Spider-Man-esque aerial acrobatics, ducking and anxiously weaving through the entire enemy arsenal to avoid losing your precious life.  It's some of the most fun I've had in a shooter in ages, largely due to the elegance of combining your primary BANG BANG with some funky traversal abilities – that is to say, the shooting and speedy-movement are inherently tied – absolutely brilliant!I've just finished the final boss fight, a truly awe-some conclusion to the game, and I'm already rearing to get back in there for more.  Boomerang X offers a whole host of challenges to keep me coming back for more, most of which revolve around limited use of your bullet-time ability or speedruns of each combat arena.  I'm not usually much of a speedrunning type (fastest mario, after all), but these combat arenas are so tight that I NEED to squeeze the rest of the fun from them – I know there's more to be had!I'd absolutely recommend Boomerang X at full price; when on sale, it's a no-brainer!
