name: Chinatown Detective Agency
detailed_description: Midnight in Singapore. Your contact’s a no show, your client wants answers and your empty bank balance hangs over you like a neon-tinted Sword of Damocles. Welcome to 2037. Welcome to Chinatown Detective Agency. The world is in a state of flux as the global economy nears the nadir of its decade-long collapse. Singapore stands as a last refuge of order but even here the government struggles on the brink of chaos. That’s where you come in. You are Amira Darma, once a rising star at INTERPOL, now a freshly minted Private Investigator in the heart of Chinatown, and your first client is about to walk through your door… EXPLORE A WORLD ON THE EDGE Neon lamp-light reflected in pools of rainwater. The fury of the angry masses manifested in graffiti daubed across decaying cities. The encroaching murk of riverside London and the blinding lights of Shanghai. Explore over a hundred stunningly rendered environments from artist Ricardo Juchem and immerse yourself in the chaotic future of 2037.Travel the globe from your base in Singapore in search of leads, and talk with dozens of uniquely voiced characters each with their own mysterious agendas. SOLVE CASES WITH REAL WORLD RESEARCH The cases Amira takes on require smart thinking and intuition to beat - but what happens when the clues dry up? That’s when you’ll have to look beyond the game for answers. The mysteries of Chinatown Detective Agency require real world investigation, whether that’s an online search for an airport code or tracking down a mysterious quote. You’re not just playing a detective, you’re becoming one. DON’T GO BANKRUPT! In Chinatown Detective Agency, time is a precious resource. Use your time and money wisely to stay one step ahead, and avoid the looming threat of going broke. Every choice will affect the world around you and change Amira’s story for good. Can you save the city from the jaws of panic and pandemonium?

_childDocuments_.review: PLEASE READ EDITED UPDATE AT THE BOTTOMI have waited over a year for this game and I am slightly disappointed. When I initially found this game I joined the discord server after playing the demo since I loved the initial cases, and I have since been caught up on any updates the developers have given on the state of the game, and I've played through the demo three different times. Each time I played the demo it was after an update, whether it be a new case or changes made to the game. I expected this game to be lengthy or at least a few more hours than what I had done in one sitting. As for what I like about the game, contrary to what others may think, I genuinely liked the research aspect and I feel that I've learned many new things about places and artifacts in history. I love the artwork, the soundtrack of different locations and their ambiance, and the challenge of finding answers for different puzzles. My MAIN PROBLEMS with this game are that the game is 1) pretty short, I expected to be lengthier or at least past the 15 hour mark, i'm sure you can replay it but a lot of parts make me not want to despite the great things about it 2) Like many games at launch there are bugs in dialogue 3) Features that were mentioned before such as energy consumption and game play other than research are barely present or no longer part of the game 4) Voice overs are only around in the first few cases of the game and nonexistent mid-game to late-game 5) NO OPTION TO MANUALLY SAVE, you can only save after you have solved a case, which is annoying if you are stuck and want to take a break, you can't leave or your progress is lost from that case.The game also allows you to travel the world to solve your cases, and to do that you have to book flights and manage your time wisely. However, the game also gives you a "Wait" function to skip time. I wonder, what is the purpose of having scheduled flights if you're going to allow us to skip forward in time? I'd like if there were side things we could do like mini games to pass time. The game also tells you you have to pay for renting out the office, and the money to pay for it comes from cases you solve. In the entirety of the game I paid for rent what, 2-3 times? I know that if you fail to pay rent then it's game over, but this mechanic didn't really add much to the game other than taking away all the funds you had just earned after finishing a case that you can't really use to spend anywhere else other than to pay for a bus, call the librarian, and buy plane tickets. What if we could spend in-game money on upgrades to the office, or to unlock extra content? I love puzzles and I'm not new to puzzle games. This game caught my eye for its cyberpunk feel and pixel design, but I'm sad to say that the puzzles were not enough to make me want to recommend this game. The publishers have PLENTY of other games that are well designed and of great quality, and CDA is lacking in many aspects. It seems as though more time was spent on artwork than the actual game play. If you want a visual novel with research game play, then by all means go right ahead. But if you're looking for a full game at a $25 price with more than 7 hours of content in one play through and feels completed, there are better games for you.UPDATE 4/10/2022: I realize now that you can in fact replay it for the different endings, but the crucial thing to do is to manually save after all the system dialogue and before choosing who to work with in the game. The game doesn't allow you to manually save if you're in the middle of a case which still sucks and is a big issue though. For this reason I don't think the game is as short as it is for one play through. I think what happened for me personally was that I began from where I left off after the (now retired) demo and none of the system dialogue that tells you your options played for me, so I randomly called Tiger Lily and thought that was my only option and that I could only choose this path. I still think parts of the game feel incomplete, and the game still has a lot of bugs. The artwork is phenomenal and the story is great too. The puzzles themselves can sometimes be misleading or bugged which can be frustrating, so I'm excited to see how the game improves as time passes.

_childDocuments_.review: .Chinatown Detective Agency is a pixel art cyberpunk sci-fi detective noir in the vein of other recent games such as Lacuna or The Sundew.  In the game, we play as Ameira, an ex-law enforcement officer-turned-private eye, who aims to get her fledgling Singapore-based independent business off the ground.  It is a point+click-style game, but not quite in the traditional sense..  You will need to play the game with your favorite search engine open on steam overlay, another monitor, or your phone.  Almost every puzzle requires some type of searching - while some of them simply involve looking up a basic fact or a quote, others do involve employing creativity and logical reasoning.  In my playthrough, I had to employ character maps in order to google phrases in Greek and Chinese, use google maps to find locations and coordinates, defeat a cipher using a decoding website, and one puzzle had me looking up various Egyptian symbols and gods for 25 minutes.  For the most part, these puzzles are quite well designed, though there were a few that I felt were a tad too ambiguous.  .Chinatown Detective Agency also has a few other unusual mechanics that make for a novel experience if not particularly enhancing the game.  First, there's a constantly-running in-game clock/calendar.  Some cases are failed if you miss a scheduled meeting or skip a deadline; there's also a robust in-game flight-booking system for world travel, and some locations which are only open at certain times of day.  CDA also offers occasional hacking and shooting minigame sequences.  There's also a money system - you get cash for finishing cases with occasional opportunities for bonuses, but flights, train rides, paying rent on your office, and bribes to the librarian who functions as the in-game hint system all cost cash.  Run out, and it's game over.  Notably, early versions of the game also had an energy/food/rest mechanic, but it seems like this was scrapped in the full release..  In the introductory section of the game, players complete one or two unrelated cases for three prospective influential clients.  In the middle section of the game, there's a major story branch, and you must pick which of these three clients you would like to work for on a full-time basis, resulting in three completely different storylines with unique puzzles.  These three possible paths coverage in the final section of the game, the "main story", which plays out a little differently depending on who you chose, and there are at least 3 endings.  This means the game does have a good bit of replayability. the incredible low-res pixel art, which if anything is grossly underutilized, and a fitting soundtrack.  I like how the game was developed by a truly international team, with developers in France, Russia, Mexico, and Brazil, among other places, and I really enjoyed listening to the authentic accents of the actors..  I am writing this review only about a week after release, and the team is working to iron out the kinks, but I definitely experienced some kinks.  Mostly minor.  I had a few bugs related to the in-game email system, receiving duplicates or not receiving the scheduled "rent due" emails on time.  I noticed that some of the walk-behinds were a little off, resulting in some minor graphical clipping in certain areas.  Audio-wise, I ran into some situations where ambient sounds such as crowd noise or footsteps did not stop when intended, continuing indefinitely until I reloaded from the main menu.  Some audio lines seemed to be missing, or sometimes accidentally mixed for only one ear of the headphones, and did not always sync up perfectly to the on-screen text.  In one odd area, my character, deep undercover, was referred to by her real name by the mark in the audio line (not in the text) instead of the fake name.  , Chinatown Detective Agency feels to me like a mostly successful experiment.  It does seem like it was originally designed to be a much bigger, much more ambitious project that had to be changed or scaled back in various ways due to budget/time/other reasons.  The team has also had some bumps - like with the bugs I mentioned.  I backed the original Kickstarter, and there was a bit of an unfortunate delay in the backer keys going out, and it's not too clear if the "Marigold Empire" DLC stretch goal which was reached is still going to happen.  BUT, the game only just came out, and I am confident that it will be patched up.  There's so many things it does really well, and I thought the ending was satisfying, so the best case scenario here is that the developers keep kicking ass in the areas where they're doing well, learn from the mistakes in the other areas, and carry on this momentum into the next project (or a potential sequel).  Thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so disappointed in this game, this is my first review after seventeen years on steam. Barely into playing Chinatown detective agency and they’ve made probably the stupidest choice in a puzzle/detective/point and click detective game I’ve ever seen: “In this game we don’t hold your hand, if you get a clue you’ll have to look it up online to find the answer.”Immediately I was like “oh no they didn’t.” The first clue I had to look up immediately took me to a walkthrough for the game, not only was it the first result on google. Google just snipped it out, and literally made the solution bold, no clicking on anything required. The game was not out for 12 hours at this point.What's worst is, you don't know if you need to look up a clue or if the solution will be found through game play, like you know, a game. So basically this game is played by going through it, then referencing strategy guides for the answer by design.Literally my top three game genres are Point and Click Adventure, Detective and Cyberpunk so I'm really disappointed. I really wanted to like this game, if you're a die hard adventure game player like I am, maybe it's worth it for the story.  I'll change my review if after finishing the story it's good enough to warrant a buy despite there basically being no actual game play aside from a matching tiles mini-game, a substitution cipher where they tell you exactly what to do and give you the key and poorly designed systems laid on top like a clunky airplane ticket buying system. Because that's the fun part of a game right? Waiting at the airport for your flight. As of right now, it's basically a Visual Novel with quizzes you didn't know you were taking so you have to look up the answers to them.The game crashed from opening the menu to save and I had to restart completely, so I'm not that far into it. The second play through the weird plane ticket buying system then waiting for your flight made me miss my flight multiple times, using most my money, but i wasn't that far, so restarted. I'm afraid to open menu to try and save often. On my now third attempt at a play through now.Edit: Tried a third attempt at playing. Can get to my first flight in about 45 seconds now. Try to save the game, save game button isn't there. Weird. Click "resume game" and it crashes to desktop. I guess we'll see if fourth times a charm. Edit 2: Checked forums, no manual save, only saves after cases.

_childDocuments_.review: The future is bleak.. not only in SingaporeA point and click detective adventure in cyberpunk asia? Count me in. Alas - the devs forgot in their quest for "innovative mechanics" (like no manual saves and only one autosave per case, or forcing the player to use the real internet to find out how to solve ingame clues) that many adventure players are old school "creatures of habit". As in that they want to be self reliant when and how long to play the game. Also including internet searches is mostly doing one thing - breaking immersion - especially in what should be a story game.Including annoying mini memory games for hacking is just another good way to push away players who are not frustrated yet.Finally the game mechanic of booking flights to some places in the world and waiting for them to finally start is getting old very fast.. and not in a good way."Chinatown Detective Agency" is a game which "doesnt take you by the hand", which is ok, but which rather annoys and bores the player with quite some questionable design choices.Conclusio: Sad waste of potentialPoint Score: 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: I am from Singapore and wanted to like the game. The art is outstanding, the music is good and the game generally works (by this I mean it didn't crash and wasn't buggy).However, the game disappointed in many other aspects.As some others have noted, the game is shoddy, There were typo errors (eg aneurism) and subtitles not matching voiced dialogue. In the same conversation, some characters are voiced but others weren't, and time sometimes matters but sometimes doesn't (eg characters often say meet me at X hrs and some do not turn up until that time, but some are there even the day before). Overall I found the dialogue to be generally average to bad, mostly corny and too dragged out at times. While it is refreshing to hear Singaporean accents in a game, most people I know do not talk like that.The game save mechanism effectively forces you to replay an entire mission for failing a timed task. Which is essentially several impatient minutes of pressing the space bar as quickly as I can to speed to the relevant part. The money aspect of the game felt redundant. That something cost money to do (whether to fly somewhere, pay rent, or to use the in-game hints) did not provide a sufficient disincentive to doing that thing because your clients pay you well. I got so tired of googling the answers to the puzzles that I used the in-game hints very liberally, and yet at the end of the game I still had more than $30k.Halfway through, I felt bored and irritated playing the game. Unless you have some connection to Singapore, save your money and time and play another game.

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere is great. Graphics are very good, music and sound ambiance are excellent. Voice acting is above par, I especially like the variety there. No stock characters. The cases and the story are intruiging, and I honestly kind of like the aspect of having to look up information online. But: the bugs. This game is *shoddy*. The wrong voice clips playing. Voice clips not playing. Voice clips markedly differing from the written script. Voice clips of one character having a *way* lower volume than others (Tiger Lily, looking at you). Urgent text messages being too long to fit in a window and cutting of the important part. Dates being displayed a day off, giving a nonstandard game over because I missed a deadline. Leads telling me to be somewhere in 3 hours, not taking into account that I have to wait for the first moment of the location actually opening for business. I'll stop here because the list is just too long.This game is really trying to create an involving and appealing immersion, and then there is this multitude of  little but annoying frak-ups that yanks me straight out of that same immersion.Then there are some puzzles that are just too obtuse for my tastes. I have no need to learn how to count in cunieform, or trail-and-erroring the five very related languages that use it, thank you.Finally, it feels really uneasy when you have to google terms and data online, and you've seen minor typos in the script earlier. How am I going to be sure that none of those poison names actuall has a typo, as well?tl;dr: valiant attempt at creating an atmospheric point 'n click visual novel. Marred by too many bugs and small UX inconveniences. Lovely looks and sounds, but too frustrating an experience to finish in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Came here for the visuals,  left feeling unfulfilled. PROS:- Quite like the overall art direction of the game! It's certainly right up my alley and one of the reasons why I was following the game for awhile.- I'm 50/50 on the research portion but at least you takeaway some knowledge through research.- The music. I quite like it. - Okay maybe it's a bit /patriotic/ of me but like seeing Singapore in a game just makes me feel proud (pls when I saw X station I went: YOOOO THAT'S WHERE I LIVE! SO COOL!)CONS:- Maybe it's a personal pet peeve, but I've noticed the in-game sprites vs the character portraits are...different.- [50/50] research portion, I don't know, maybe I do want a bit of handholding when it comes to some of the cases. .- Short and non immersive. The cases are SHORTER than I thought? Not only that, I thought I could decorate the agency a little bit because of how I've racked up about...what...40k until the end? Turns out, I'm just going to be stuck with a dingy looking office lol.- I encountered a BUNCH of bugs. Also, some scenes, there's no voiced dialogue? [eg. Amira was talking but for some reason Justin wasn't. Don't know whether it was intentional or not but felt really sloppy ngl]- Manual. Saves. Not. Being. A. Thing (I blame my fat fingers for force quitting the application but it's so tiring to go through the same thing all over again).- GAME WANTS YOU TO FEEL LONG because you spent probably 75-95% of the time researching.Overall, I guess I wouldn't mind replaying for a second shot (since I only finished Keeran's part) but hope the Devs could put out more content. The game isn't truly worth its price point considering how short the whole story is. Maybe get it during a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the whole game, I think I still wouldn't recommend. Maybe if it was on sale for a tenner or less it would be worth it but not at its current price. Overall, the game is buggy which ruins the immersion and experience.Personally, I liked the research aspect of the game. One moment I'm scouring a Wikipedia page in search for old stamps and reading the history of looters who stole Manchukuoan stamps, and then the next, I'm learning about an ancient script used to write languages in the Middle East. It was so cool to delve into history that wasn't taught in my school. The short facts in the information tags at the top of each city was fun to read through and I liked the addition it made to the "world building". I've played a lot of point and click detective/escape room/puzzle games and this was refreshing. The hints system was set up so cleanly which helped when the puzzles were challenging.I liked the way the story was laid out with three "routes" but still having the same final case. I'm not a huge fan of replaying games in the way some visual novels do it where you have to get different endings by choosing certain options but the rest is all the same. So I'm glad I could still experience the other routes and cases and not have to replay the last one. I would also say the actual story was pretty good too and the dialogue could be funny at times. It's not the best detective story ever but it was effective and does the job.I loved the art and the animation is so beautiful and smooth. The landscapes are really brought to life and are still so detailed despite being pixel art.Other than that, there were a few things I found annoying. As I said at the start, the price. It's a relatively short game and combined with the bugs, does not make it worth the £20 tag in my opinion. Having no manual save option was painful, especially in a puzzle game such as this. The voice lines were often placed with the wrong text, or it would stop in the middle of the conversation. Having voice lines for the entire game isn't necessary but when you're missing a few here and there in a scene that has voiced dialogue, it definitely breaks the immersion. Sometimes, a character would walk the wrong way too in a cutscene which was sort of funny. There's also a bug where if you leave a save file when you were supposed to pay the bills, exit the game and come back to it, the game would think you missed the payment and you'd have to pay double when actually, you're just coming back to the same point in time. While it was annoying, it luckily didn't affect my finances too much because you have a lot at the start.I've seen people discussing the monetary mechanics in CDA and I agree with how it should be improved for sure. It's kind of like an extra thing in the game, you don't really think about it because there's a lot of it and so when you need to spend it, it's like whatever. But then what's the point in having a money mechanic really?

_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to call this a game. It's a visual novel, with very basic puzzles, and most of the game involves booking flights and waiting for them. Unlike some of the best point and click puzzles that involve talking to multiple characters, collecting items and working things out, the game forces players to sit through dull dialogue, then solve a little memory game, or book a flight, and repeat. I kickstarted this game and am very disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m really enjoying this game.  It’s a puzzle detective game where you figure out clues to see where you go next and to advance the story.  It reminded me a bit of the Black Watchmen games, where you need to Google around to figure out the clues, how to decrypt a cipher, etc.  Some were pretty straightforward and some puzzles I found quite challenging.  I like having to go out and do the research to solve puzzles. I thought it was fun.  The cases were intertwined complex conspiracy type cases and I was interested in following through to the ends.You play a case for each potential client and then get to choose one to work for full time.  So there are many more cases than you get in one playthrough and because the games creates a separate save for each case, I am on my second client run and started right after the split and didn’t need to start the whole game over.Playing now after some game updates, I’m not seeing any bugs in the gameplay.  Other than having to type a few answers in and for Internet work, the game is entirely mouse driven for movement and examining things.The voiceovers were well done.  Now, there are some gaps in the voice overs, but it is almost all voiced.  If I had the choice between no voice acting at all and some lines here and there not voiced, I would take the second any time.  It just isn’t that big a deal for me.  The art work was beautiful.  There are so many cities to visit all with their own look and history to read when you get there.  Very nicely done!I am having a fun time with the game and think it is well worth the time and price for the gameplay you get.  Must like challenging puzzles that require some research!

_childDocuments_.review: I so badly want to  like this game. After failed attempts at a memory based puzzle i have to restart the whole mission/chapter as there is no save. I have a problem with patterns and constantly get this wrong. No save mechanic even after the prologue is making this game unenjoyable for me. At this point in time I do not recommend this game, it is moire frustrating than enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty big disappointment. I think I could make a pretty long rant about how I felt this game was lacking. I played through the whole game once, to give it a fair chance, enduring the frustration that had already started having with the game from case 3ish. I really really wanted to like this. This looks like everything I would love with a game, old-school 8-bitty art style, neo-noir, detective game with puzzles. Sadly it felt like it wanted to do more than what it ended up delivering. A lot of elements felt thrown in haphazardly, not fully developed and just a handful of wasted game mechanic that served more as an inconvenient barrier than anything. Examples: - A monetary system that serves no purpose AT ALL. You get so much money as a "poor detective trying it on her own". It doesn't add an extra challenge, it just gives you the extra job of remembering to pay rent which you most certainly have the money for. You cant use it to interact with anything else but the plane trips and the train rides. Which gets me to the next point- So many places to travel to, that just does nothing. Low to no interaction, which makes them, and the work put into the artwork of each scene, a little wasted. E.g. you cant use the money to buy a drink in the bar you go to.- Time as a mechanism, why? There is no point if you are creating a game set with a prefixed storyline/progression. So why put in the element of us buying the first plane ticket, set the next morning, just for us to click on the "wait" button. Clearly the wait button was needed as having 6-9 hours in-game of waiting can't be used to anything. Small details could've been added to the world to change this and make if feel more finished and thought through. Right now however it would honestly have been better to just lean in properly to a "fixed storyline" by removing these mechanism all together. This could've maybe saved up budget, time or focus on the other elements that are lacking. Such as- Voiceovers being all over the place. Sometimes one person in a convo talks while the rest is silent? Or the music is louder that the person talking. Some audio is in worse quality than others. You can barely hear Tiger Lily through out the entire game. - Character design not matching (Sprite different from the person in the game, to no being able to tell who everyone in the title screen is supposed to be). And the art at the very end doesn't match the rest of the gamestyle and honestly just felt rushed and unfinished. It almost makes it feel like the sketches were used instead. - Bugs! So many bugs. Not being able to move, not being able to click on anything, or getting tasked to meet up at a specific location in X hours while the place is closed - leading to the game ending because you missed the event. (Another part of the time aspect that was done half-assed.)- No saving mid case... which is bad if you need to restart the game due to all the bugs. It only loads from the beginning of the case, so you have to redo everything.Other than that I personally also sadly really disliked the story-line and dialogue. It was my biggest gripe with the game. It felt cliché, and very predictable yet very unnatural. The conversations doesn't always flow naturally, and the development of the characters and their deep relationship (so deep that they would support each other even if it could lead to death at the end) makes no sense. It was hard to invest in any of the characters, especially the main protagonist. I couldn't stand her, sadly. Several tropes that grind my gears, such as being a cocky rookie despite having worked for a while in the force, doing several things that would not make sense such as blind faith to some of the people she worked with (the men .. TWICE), running in hot, or giving out secret info (make her character make sense). Felt like the male characters got more developed character backgrounds, and except for with Mei Thing, our female lead seemed to constantly doubt or be rude to other female characters. Honestly her snarky remarks to Tiger Lily pissed me off. You really gonna write a female lead who has been one of the few women working in the force and having to prove her self, so easily just do the dirty work for the rich dude, no questions asked, while being constantly critical and judgemental towards Tiger Lily for surviving in a mans world. Same trope with the temple-storyline. Many times during the game the responses or comments didn't make sense as a follow up to the scene, or the dialogue before that, or to the character them selves... The aspects I enjoyed was the puzzle aspects and the searching stuff. Some puzzles more than others. I enjoyed the museum and stamp task, as it feed my "♥♥♥♥ how did I suddenly sit here for hours on a wikipedia rabbit hole" tendencies. Some puzzle were a little less engaging, tedious or not very intuitive. But I do wish they actually leaned more into the puzzles, but I can see not everyone enjoying that part. TLDR: Did not enjoy. Gave it a fair chance. A game that was trying to do too much at the same time, and ending up missing the mark on most aspects. Should've focused on one thing with their budget and time, either the puzzle solving aspect, or a better developed storyline. Preferably both.
_childDocuments_.name: Chinatown Detective Agency

_childDocuments_.review: Chinatown Detective Agency tells a fairly great detective story which presents unique ideaas, but finds itself marred by underbaked design decisions and abysmal polish. Amira Darma’s adventures and relatability carry through to the end, but that path is unnecessarily impeded by omitted or bugged voice lines, convoluted puzzle solutions, and a money system that feels tacked on. While those only mildly interested in point-and-click narrative experiences should likely steer clear, Chinatown Detective Agency brings just enough for the rest of us to investigate further.If you'd like to read the rest of this review and more like it, check out . Thank you to Humble Games for providing a review copy for this review.

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to wait with the review until I got all the achievements in the game and discover all possible endings on all paths to see how it would impact my initial reaction to the game. It sadly didn't. At first, I thought of the game to be very enjoyable - I enjoyed the cases, the depth to them initially, the different characters, the settings, as well as some of the initial functions demonstrated only in the demo, so I purchased the game. I quickly went through the already familiar content and started the real game. And it fell flat.The cases are really short and really buggy. Some of them I had to restart over 6 times as Amira would not move from her place and I could not interact with anything at all. The difficulty level was fine, some definitely easier than others but with the usage of external browser (necessary for the game) you're bound to find everything.I think the game is too short for its price - yes, you will play more and spend more time in game if you do different paths and reach the end with a different partner and get different endings but the paths are short and the main storyline starts to feel boring after the nth replay with a different character.I think that the idea was nice but not all functions are polished - such as the wait function or rent (which also bugged many times for me and did not allow me to pay), they feel unnecessary and the time deadlines also only work at certain times, while they make no difference at all at other times. What also felt abandoned as a game part were the voice acting and character drawings - only some characters got a voice and if they did it was not present in all the dialogues, only some, mostly abandoned half throughout the game, and the same with art - some characters have faces, others not at all. And even though those are small cosmetic mistakes, they still really impacted the game experience, as they made it feel unfinished.Overall, I'd prefer the game to be longer and more polished, also having the manual save function available more easily than it is now and for the bugs to stop happening because they really ruin the game experience. I was so excited to play it after the demo but left rather disappointed. It's not bad though, it's just not good.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to give this a negative review, but the game is just so unpolished.  The concept is great, the story lines are good, but it just falls so flat on its face.- Solutions to puzzles are either easy from an obvious Google or so obtuse to what you think it should be, you'll never get it.  Most are very easy.  There is also no depth to the puzzles...  I was expecting to have to get sucked into a Wikipedia hole, but every answer is just 1 level deep.- Had a game crash, SFX that never went away across cases, and other frustrating bugs.- Money and travel in the game is annoying and a waste of time- Why is half the game voice acted and the other half not??- Of course, when I hear the city Victoria, I think  and not Canada or Australia!  Lol.- Every case has 1 or 2 puzzles in it.  You finish a case and think, "Wait, that's it?"- Failing a case is really punishing and incredibly frustrating.My issues are the same as all the other negative reviews...  and my takeaway: if you play this game, you probably won't hate it.  But you will have a frustrating experience fighting the game to try and enjoy yourself with it.  And be left with a wonder of what it COULD have been, if it had been properly executed.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the atmosphere and the pixel art. People complained about bugs but that might only be early release issues. I have not encountered a single one. It picks up the Singapore vibes really great and visiting the places I used to see for half a year in a cyberpunky-noire near future really brought back some memories. Apart from that I really love the idea to google and use your brain rather than coming up with arbitrary item options as point and click adventures sometimes use to.I really hope we will see another title with the vibes and techniques used in this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like it, I really did. It had elements of mystery, cyberpunk, and asian representation (singaporean too which you normally don't see). But it has A LOT OF ISSUES. So I'll start off with mechanics. I love puzzle games and OSINT is one of my favorite cybersecurity things, but this falls flat on both. There's only one real type of puzzle and its a matching game, all the other "puzzles" are just doing OSINT or some basic cryptography and not in an interesting way. Good OSINT challenges is fun and pulls you into interesting rabbit holes, like knowing you can track flights or cargo ships. Unfun OSINT is look we got an old stamp, and using the 4 letters figure out where it was sent from---and oh they're using a super obscure spelling of a city. Similarly, cryptography is fun when they use interesting ciphers---I'll admit I did like using the engima cipher, but most of them were super basic and include the cipher key IN the message. Also having someone decode morse code with static in the background by ear is not very accessible to those with hearing issues, esp since it doesnt give you the option to scrub through the audio. If you want to relisten to it you have to start from the begining and its hard to tell where you left off. It also doesnt help that when you have to give the deciphered message to another person you can't have the encrypted message open so you can more easily decrypt. Also with the artifact quests, aside from the stuff you have to read and decipher, they just give a description and not a picture of the artifact. Now I know that would make it easy to find which museum it goes to, but even ludonarratively it makes no sense because your character, Amira has the artifact and can look at it, there fore you should be able to as well. They didn't give her a paper with a description.: I think what they could have done to make it better is utilize the library more. They could've added books that have both useful and not useful information that you look through. It would've also made the game feel more fleshed out because the library under utilized and is honestly a place with wasted potential. . I get not letting people save-scum. but the fact that there are bugs that you need to  restart the game to fix means that it should at least autosave when you quit the game. One such bug is at the end where they tell you to go someplace and after I talked to everyone I couldn't open the Mission Log to see where I had to go (and I forgot where to go tbh) and I had to replay the whole mission. Absolute bollocks. Also the fact you cant save until you finish the "prologue" which is like 5 missions is honestly dumb, because what if you need to do stuff irl?Also the last mission it felt like it was suppose to be two missions (based on the pacing of previous missions) but no. I think its to stop people from save scumming the ending, but honestly the way they did the save mechanic feels hostile to the player So you know stuff is interactable when your cursor turns green, some of the stuff you need to interact with are small. Most point and click games allow you to highlight stuff you can interact with because it is easy for stuff to look like background art.  The game says you can only pick one person to work with full time because time management but like there is so much time waiting for events that I could've easily juggled 3 cases at once. I think they only made this choice to make the game "replayable" You are never at risk of a game over because you couldn't pay your rent unless you're taking a billion unnecessary flights.  You can only call people at certain times, otherwise it'll say their number is not in service???? Sometimes itlll say they don't pick up, but usually it says out of service. Like ???? Also you should be able to call someone to confirm details There's barely any combat and when there is its trivially easy. The target doesnt move and you're jsut suppose to shoot them in the hand to disarm and you get so much time to do it. Next the story: I was honestly more invested in the side characters stories more than the main one. The main one is cliche and frankly boring I understand a small game company can't make something that has the most thought out mechanics, and a Story of the Year, but there are things they could've done to make it not feel unfinished at best and downright hostile at worst (ahem the save mechanic) It was very weird that they paired researching obscure things, basic trivia, and easy ciphers, it's almost like they wanted it to be a challenging capture the flag type game while also being friendly to beginners which doesn't work for CTF style things. It has to either be easy for beginners and teach them some basics, or challenging---or start off easy and then get challenging. I found that tbh the research stuff is mostly easy, the issue is that they randomly throwing something weird at you and think its clever. Also it was very strange that the end game stuff is extremely easy.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the detective / investigation genre so much that I'm usually easily impressed with any game that tells a good detective story and maintains decent intrigue and suspense. And honestly for the first 5-6 hours I played this game, I was enjoying the story and the characters. The actual puzzles felt novel at first because they required you to step outside the game and do actual research online. However, afterwards, these puzzles started to feel more like a hindrance to an interesting story and world that they had built. And I'm not saying these puzzles were particularly difficult, but if the game requires you to step outside it and search for the answers, what's stopping you from just looking at a walk-through to solve the puzzles? Initially I avoided them, but later on it felt like googling "what's the answer to the language puzzle?" was easier than googling "what language are these symbols from?". I am at a point where the mystery is at it's peak but the puzzles have irritated me far to much to proceed. I'll probably push through and finish the game, but a detective story that leaves a sour taste isn't worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: The art, music and animations are phenomenal.The dialogue is... hit or miss, as is the voice acting. But it's still nice to hear voices in what would otherwise be a point-and-click adventure.However, the gimmick of this game is that there are two types of puzzles: tile flip matching puzzles, and trivia. I don't find enjoyment in either, and if the game ends up being too long, these "puzzles" could end up overstaying their welcome.I imagine this game is best played in short sessions to avoid burning through (and burning out on) the game quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: CDA proved to be quite an enjoyable experience despite the current limited save sytem and the weird partial voice overs. The pixel art is amazing, the plot quite thrilling and there is a good variety of brain-teasing puzzles to solve.The devs are currently working on improving the save system, so I would recommend to wait for that update before playing if you want to avoid some frustration.The game is inspired by the Carmen Santiago games. I never played those games myself, but if you have, you should know what to expect.Personally, I would describe the game to play as an ARG such as in the Alice & Smith games.Playing as detective Amira Dharma, the gameplay consists of completing various missions by solving all kind of puzzles. There are a few decisive dialogue choices to make that lead to 3 different paths with their own specific missions but then rejoin later on to end the game with three possible endings. This gives some replayability if we want to do every possible cases in the game.Storywise, the plot is actually pretty well thought and thrilling. It plays a bit like a visual novel, and I quite enjoyed reading through the story.The game also has time and money mechanics. We will have to meet some npcs or complete a task at/before a set time. Most of the time, the game is quite forgiving and actually allows the player to arrive well before the required time, but being late usually means failing a case.Similarly, I found the game quite generous with funds, as we have quite enough to fly to any locations in the game, just dont overspend and dont forget to pay the rent on time, or it is game over!Puzzles are of various types and difficulty: apart from the occasional memory tiles mini-game, we will have to google for info and use real decryption tools or methods to figure out codes and passwords.I personally really liked this aspect of the game as it teached us all kind of RL stuff I wouldnt have ever look into otherwise, like how to read Sumerian numbers, convert DMS coordinates or understand how an Enigma machine works, among other things... This is a really good game to make you feel smarter! :DBut if you are really stuck, or dont want to do too much detective work, there is an in-game npc you can call to ask for an hint or a solution (only available after completing the prologue).Also, you might want to add -Chinatown in your google search, if you dont want to fall on a walkthrough of the puzzle you are currently working on.I absolutely loved the game art. The amount of details and the beauty of the numerous sceneries was a pleasure for the eyes. Each world location/city has 3 possible views: day, evening and night, and some of the sceneries are just stunning. The game autosaves only after completing a mission.Manual saves are introduced after completing the prologue but can only be used when we are not working on a case. We can make an after prologue manual save to explore later on the different story branches, but other than that one, manual saves have not much use right now.Also, there are only 4 manual saves slots and 4 autosaves slots, those getting automatically overwritten as we play.The devs promised they were working on including manual saves during missions, so I would recommend waiting for that update to play the game to avoid useless frustration. There are a few time limited puzzles to solve, and if you fail finding the solution on time, you will have to start the case over. This happened to me a few times. The way I did it was: take screenshots of the clues given, and after failing a case, I just took my time looking for info online before restarting the case and having then enough time to input my solution(s).I found the voice acting pretty well done, except I have no idea if this was a bug or not, but voice overs were only partial. Some dialogue lines were voiced, others were not. Sometimes, we even had dialogues with some character being mute while others were not. This was kind of weird. Hopefully, this will be improved later on.In all, I quite liked this game. It could have used a few extra months of polishing and play-testing. And it feels like the devs had originally bigger plans for the game. But I really hope more content will be added in the future, because I definitely would like to play more of this!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite this game's thumbs up rating, I did not really enjoy it. It is a puzzle-focused point and click adventure game, probably more in the vein of Deja Vu than Lucasarts games.The setting is near future Singapore along with a bunch of global locations for cases. The game predicts the prevalence of things like artificial operators taking over menial and manual labour, drones, surveillance and corporate and governmental greed leading humanity into a dystopia. I like that kind of setting, and I think the game does a good job in highlighting parts that are relevant to the world as it is currently. Certainly, little optional information panels for each location detailing details of various places along with a brief history from the IRL future onwards do a great deal to add to the world building. Plenty of objects and NPCs have option dialogue or descriptions that also hone this world. Good stuff.The gameplay is what I have gripes with though. You'll meet simple matching games made obtuse with nonsense symbols. You'll do this minigame maybe half a dozen times through your playthrough, it becoming easier as you start to recognise and remember the symbols. Other puzzles require actual google searches to solve - looking up facts and information to solve clues and riddles. This ranged from very simple to very obscure. Certain information, for example, was easily within my knowledge-set, but made difficult with nonsensical obfuscation. For example, and here's a puzzle spoiler (for one sentence): One part had me finding a bottle of burgundy red wine - one of my favourites, but the wine shop has all the other wine's labelled except for the burgundy, I believe that breaks EU regulations and and and most bergundy say either that or  on them.  Spoiler over. This is a gripe for sure, and I had a few others, but I'm sure people with other expertises than me will find the same difficulty with other puzzles. I also found the buying plane tickets, and then clicking wait until 3 hours before the flight, then watching the plane go across the map unnecessary and tedious.Graphically, I think that the characters could have had slightly higher fidelity. The portraits used during dialogue were not expressive and didn't show emotion. The normal sprites are retro style, with no detail. I found that forgivable in some games, but here I thought it detracted from the game's emotional impact. I think the devs could have used shaders to add more a dramatic noir and/or cyberpunk feel to the game.The sound design of the game was good, but not stand-outy. Vaguely futuristic beats pulse away during tense scenes or carry you through travel and waiting. Drifting ambient synths drone on during more atmospheric moments. Voice acting was on point - singaporean accents abound lah, though some of it didn't match the final dialogue. I understand - budgeting and alterations.Overall, I think if you enjoy this kind of game, you'll have a whale of a time. But I'll stick with my problem-solving adventure games, rather than puzzley ones.

_childDocuments_.review: CDA is a very immersive and fun point & click adventure. The game is a hybrid of the classic Carmen Sandiego games from the 90s, involving solving clues/puzzles and travelling around the world, along with detective/adventure games like Police Quest/Kings Quest from Sierra in the 80/90s.The pixel art is beautiful, the character portraits and personalities are memorable, the developers have created an immersive future world, especially the soundtrack, which is superb - i hope it is released separately. Most point & click games throw blobs of dialogue text at you, even recent ones, so i applaud the amount of voice acting thats been invested in by CDA, giving it so much character and unique flavor.I did encounter some bugs, presumably due to the deep voice acting, open world mission loops etc. but nothing game breaking.Overall, really enjoyed my first few missions, will surely be finishing the rest over this weekend! Highly recommend for anyone interested in above mentioned genres/games.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has an intriguing story and beautiful aesthetic. Its fun to go searching for the answers to the clues you get throughout the investigations. Would highly recommend to anyone who enjoys a bit a sleuthing.Two issues I have with the game, one being the airport/travel mechanic. The date is set up day/month/year which was initially confusing when I went to book my first flight and couldn't board it, realizing I had booked a flight a month in advance... so I wasted money if I had only known it was not in the US format which was confusing since they use the US currency instead of the Singapore currency. Secondly, you cannot manually save until after you have completed the first three missions. or so the game tells you. I have completed the first three and chosen my full time client. I could not save until after completing the first mission after selecting a full time client. Which is a bit annoying in all honesty. It would be nice to have a manual save at any point throughout a mission as most other games do...That being said, its a lot of fun and will recommend it to all my friends to play. _childDocuments_.review: :::THEY DO NOT ALLOW US TO POST IN THE DISCUSSION FORUM UNLESS YOU'RE A MEMBER:::This should be a red flag right off the starting line. Also, they claim to "review the posts for harmful content" -- pretty much censoring the truth. This game sucks. Plain and simple. This game is a sham. I bought this expecting to solve intricate cases with critical thinking and keen observation in true detective fashion. The game robs you of this by having you search for clues on YOUR OWN WEB BROWSER. This is nothing but laziness in this regard because instead of having to offer clever ways to find clues in-game, they cop out by having you resort to Google, which is filled more with answers rather than hints. This alone robs you of your detective experience.I have bought bad games in the past -- as we all have. I tend to keep them for they may grow on me. However, this game, right out of the front gate, is a rip-off. I love detective-style games and I was eagerly awaiting this one. This is no exaggeration when I say that this is the most disappointing game I have ever purchased. Maybe take the game off Steam, and get rid of our having to use Google by incorporating the clues in-game -- like you should have done to begin with. How did you think this would be a good idea? Seriously? A detective game should give you everything you need to solve the case or puzzle within the game itself. If this was an attempt to change the way people think about detective games by having us look on Google, you've failed. If I wanted to get involved in the cases by resorting to resources outside of the game, I'd join an investigative unit at my local police department, or try to figure out who ate my Doritos last week at home.  If you liked the story, fine, but if you want a good story, you can always read one. The only difference between this game and a book is you need to travel to a location to continue reading -- which the travel is simply an in-game page turn of a book. Fix the game, devs. Come on. What were you thinking?

_childDocuments_.review: So, originally I gave this a positive review, then changed it to a negative one after I got past the prologue because of the number of new bugs and things that hadn't been fixed. Now I'm pleased to be able to change it back to positive, thanks to today's update. I know it's the conspiracy theorist in me, but it does kind of seem like their programmer got online, saw what was happening, and started cranking out fixes on her own. Pity it took until the game was actually out, but this one set of fixes has addressed most, though not all, of my objections.I'm editing my thoughts below to take today's update into account, as best I can.• The closest thing we've had yet to Carmen Sandiego for grown-ups. (I say this as the owner of the internet's oldest and largest extant Carmen fansite.) By which I mean, in part, the setup of occasionally needing to do outside research. People who are ragging on the game for this just... don't seem to get that they aren't the audience for it (I sense some capital-O capital-S capital-G 'Old-School Gamers' who think every game is and should be meant for them) and for those of us who are, it's a huge asset.While I'm still cross with the devs for how they've handled some things, I think they're getting a lot of undeserved flack for this. You don't have to insult them because they made a game that isn't made for YOU. They've even stated specifically that it's not a traditional "point-and-click adventure game," so I'm not sure what those reviewers were pressed about.• The art. The foreign locations' art changing based on the time of day is a particularly charming touch (and one that's reminiscent of the 1996 Carmen games, as well as Seize the Day).• The variety of puzzles: concentration (a.k.a. memory), decrypting messages, deciphering Morse code...• Unlike Carmen, the game has actual mysteries - it's actually more like Nancy Drew than Carmen in this way (as well as some of the puzzles), though you can't really solve the mystery yourself with clues provided the way you can with some Nancys.• The characters, specifically Mei Ting, who is just a delight as the comic relief character. Tiger Lily and Laetitia are especially good ones too.• The addition (since the last demo) of a "Wait" button so you don't have to remember to type W for it...• ...though that button came at the expense of the "Office" button for a one-click return to Amira's office. I imagine they didn't want to have too many buttons cramping the UI, but for me the "Web" button to launch your web browser is useless, since I'll press alt-tab instead (see keyboard comment below) or use my phone. There had to be a better way to do this to accommodate different users' needs.• Moreover, the whole 'wait' system seems unnecessary. At certain points, the game will automatically jump ahead a certain length of time, so why do you have to do so manually at other points? It seems like a remnant of something they didn't end up implementing and never thought to remove.• Bugs. Mostly fixed now, but the one with the Morse code puzzle particularly is irksome that it ever happened.• On that puzzle, since it's auditory, if you're Deaf you're just SOL, I guess?• A lack of keyboard support. Pressing escape, enter, alt-enter, and the arrow keys does nothing. I'm a very keyboard-oriented user (not just for games), and having to use the mouse for everything is irritating.• Another UI issue: the window for text messages jumps to the next text rather than scrolling, so if a message is longer than what fits in the window, it's just cut off with no way to see the end. (Haven't confirmed whether this is still happening with today's update.)• A lack of attention to detail when it comes to the script. Some subtitles don't match the speech (or vice versa), and different characters pronounce names differently. (For instance, Charlene is pronounced both with a "sh" and with a "ch," and Xu as both "shu" and "shi.")• Actually, a lack of attention to detail in general when combining multiple people's work. Another great example is that one of the main characters, Laetitia, has graying brown hair in her dialogue portrait, but red hair in her pixel representation.• The save system. The game auto-saves at the end of each mission, but it's not possible to save in the middle, so if you have to close the game (or if you get a game-breaking glitch, as I did trying to close the main menu after opening it in the airport), you're back to the start of your current mission. This is especially a problem with no "Are you sure you want to quit?" dialog - I once was trying to click into the sound settings, but my finger slipped and I quit instead, so it was back to the start of the mission. (I see this is getting fixed, which is great. Better late than never, I guess.)• Nothing pointing out that the game uses DMY dates (not MDY), so American players will be confused.• Generally, it seems like there was a lack of user testing, and prior to this weekend, implementing player feedback. I was a beta tester for one of the demos and specifically pointed out several of the above issues.• On that note, I find it really inappropriate that paying customers (such as myself) basically acted as beta testers, submitting our bug reports on Discord.• And in much the same way that they didn't do enough play testing (or didn't pay enough attention to the results), they clearly needed a sensitivity reader, because the informational text for the Bugis area originally used a slur for transgender people. This was changed in today's update, but it still bothers me that it happened. It's crummy* to make trans players be the ones to run across that and be upset by it and have to point it out. I also feel an apology for it was in order, more than just an acknowledgment.[*This was supposed to be a word that rhymes with 'bitty,' but Steam censored it. Even behind a "this page may have inappropriate content" warning? Seriously? Well done, Valve. *GLaDOS slow clap*]

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like no other, a game that keeps you asking more questions. It is Nice and Refreshing Futuristic Indie Detective Game. The click and point gameplay give the player tasks to run their own business and solve the puzzles through their own means through the search engine in the game. The game takes place in 2037 10 years after a global economic collapse, following the character Amira Darma who is a former Interpol agent, striving to break free from the cage Interpol has. The low class and middle have all been taken over by automated drones and robots. For Amira to keep the lights on she needs to have steady pay-check coming in through from one of her three clients the player may choose later in the game. Depending on the client is chosen would depend on the storyline you'd receive. Through the game she meets and make friends. One of the main character relevant to the game is Mei Ting who helps Amira with giving hints or helps solve puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: First off, bugs aside, it's a decently designed game.The game sells itself as a point-and-click adventure game but it is unique in ways that either pleases or puts people off. You could see it as a unique twist to the genre or an unwelcome addition. In my view there are two of these. One is, as many have already mentioned, that you have to rely on your actual web browser to play this game. The game asks for real facts (e.g., title of a certain book) or throws at you ciphers that you probably never heard of unless you have a particular passion in those areas and a great memory. What I like about it is that it invites some tinkering and researching on your own, and because these clues are actual things out there, it adds to the serious tone and atmosphere. Having that said, it is clearly not Monkey Island or Thimblewood Park kinda light-hearted adventure games filled with random wacky humor. As someone who inclines toward Sherlock Holmes and Gabriel Knight than those two games, I appreciated the sober setting the game is in.What I don't like about this web-browsing feature is that everytime I alt-tab out of the game to the browser, I get disconnected from the immersion. In my view, this is a critical problem. Any game that fails in terms of immersion is doomed to last not very long in my list of installed games. Although not a problem by itself, this feeling of disconnectedness is worsened by the fact that the missions are episodic. Everytime I finish a mission and get a save in between I feel a sense of relief that I can finally close the game. While the browser feature is innovative, I still think the game should have opted for an in-game browser instead for some manner of control -- both in terms of information and immersion. The game is set in the future. Why not just have the character open up a hologram from her watch or some gadget with a simplified search function?Second is time management. There is a clock that keeps going whether you are on the net browsing for clues or thinking of what one should do next. Many adventure games also utilizes some kind of time function in their games for day-night cycle or whatever, but if I'm not wrong not many use a 'real-time' deadline to constantly pressure you to hurry through everything. In contrast, quick thinking in real-time is crucial to succeed in this game. Some may like the sense of urgency omnipresent throughout this game, that it adds to the realism, but it certainly wasn't what I was expecting from a point-and-click adventure game. I cannot but keep worrying if I've already missed out on something important somewhere because I spent some time doing something else. In every mission I feel like I'm playing a RTS game racing against the clock, and the fact that I can't save during missions brings the stress bar up a notch. Like I said, some might welcome the stress-factor, some might not. I don't.Other than those two personal quirks aside, I like everything else. The tone, setting, art, character, they are great. While I might have expressed things a little too dramatically above, the game difficulty isn't that high (at least so far), and I haven't met any problem with time management. Still, if you're a long time fan of this genre, you should probably go in with an open mind because it certainly distinguishes itself from the classics for better or worse.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game's unique premise, asking you to look up information yourself to help you move forward in your cases. It's a mechanic that, for me at least, really makes you feel smart for finally finding the answers you're looking for after spending so much time searching for it. The pixel art is lovely, and you can tell the artists spent so much time on the locations and characters. There are flaws to this game though. The game was perhaps just a tad too short for my liking. While I did enjoy the story, I feel like it could have branched a bit more. I also encountered a few glitches over my time, such as time sensitive missions failing you early, and lines of dialogue that play at the wrong time, though these can probably be patched. There were a lot of times where I felt like more voice acting would have been well suited for some scenes. I wouldn't be surprised if a director's cut were released somewhere down the line.Still, I feel the positives outweigh the negatives for me. The puzzles are interesting enough, the worldwide locations, when used correctly, are beautiful, and the characters are intriguing enough to keep someone like me invested until the end. If you're a fan of mystery games and figuring things out yourself, I'd recommend checking this one out.

_childDocuments_.review:
Midnight in Singapore. Your contact's a no show, your client wants answers and your empty bank balance hangs over you like a neon-tinted Sword of Damocles. Welcome to 2032. Welcome to Chinatown Detective Agency. The world is in a state of flux as the global economy nears the nadir of its decade-long collapse. Singapore stands as a last refuge of order but even here the government struggles on the brink of chaos. Private detectives are now the first call for those citizens able to afford a semblance of justice.

That's where you come in. You are Amira Darma, once a rising star at INTERPOL, now a freshly minted Private Investigator in the heart of Chinatown, and your first client is about to walk through your door...

Inspired by the classic Carmen Sandiego games of the 80s and 90s, Chinatown Detective Agency is a mystery adventure game that will take you across Singapore and the world in hot pursuit of criminals, witnesses and clues. Solve puzzles and uncover leads using real research and investigation, and manage your time and money to solve cases from clients both well-intentioned and nefarious. Along the way, untangle a web of conspiracies and plots that threaten to push the Lion City over the edge.

name: Carto
detailed_description: Carto is a charming adventure game wrapped around a unique, world-altering puzzle mechanic. Use this power to explore mysterious lands, help a quirky cast of characters, and guide Carto on her journey back to her family. Separated from her Granny during a storm, young Carto must use her innate cartography powers to map and manipulate the world around her on her quest to be reunited. As she discovers new “pieces” of the game map, players can rearrange them to shape the levels themselves - unlocking new paths, puzzles, and story moments. Carto will traverse strange new lands, learn their cultures, and enlist the help of new friends along the way in this hand-crafted adventure. Features Employ a unique puzzle and exploration mechanic: rearrange pieces of your map, and watch the world change around you! Chill out and explore peaceful-yet-mysterious lands across a 5-7 hour story Meet a colorful cast of characters and learn about their unique cultures Bask in lush, hand-drawn visuals across a variety of biomes Experience a beautiful soundtrack with over 30 original tracks to accompany you on your adventure

_childDocuments_.review: A cute, well constructed adventure puzzle game with a generally uninteresting story.The game makes clever use of its gimmick with the map altering mechanics. Although sometimes it recycles the same puzzle concepts for the most part it thoroughly explores the various potential the mechanics have. The puzzles manage to stay relatively intuitive throughout although they are occasionally vague.Players travel to several different places and get to learn the general basis of the various human tribes living around the world. But for the most part the story is just not especially exciting. Because players move around so much they do not get to establish much familiarity or connection with many of the characters. When they do encounter some characters again it's usually only for a brief period, and nothing especially connection-building occurs in that time. Combined with the mostly silent protagonist and the inability to make any kind of branching choices it leaves the story relatively bland. There are some interesting characters and moments, unfortunately the puzzle gameplay is generally the main draw of the experience; with the story being more of an excuse for puzzle gameplay to be there.The art is cute and very consistent through the experience, decent music and some fun examination descriptions for items in the world from time to time. Not really any rewarding secrets or rewards in general for exploration that aren't linked to direct progress.It's nice for a linear puzzle experience but as a story experience it's very underdeveloped and generally superficial, so however enjoyable it may be it's not especially memorable either.If you're interested in finding more games like this I've probably reviewed quite a few on my curator page .

_childDocuments_.review: An inspired premise realised near-perfectly (assuming you're ok with some sweetness).Basically repurposes the Carcasonne tileset into a single-player story-puzzler-...jigsaw i guess, along with hugs (I liked 'em) and also genuine humour. If those things don't do it for you then...ok. Elsewhere, the challenge ramps up brilliantly towards the end and it's the right length to leave you just wanting more. Graphics and soundtrack are great and fit perfectly.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a sweet and heartwarming game that just oozes with charm. Every character is delightful in their own way, even if they don't get much dialogue. I was so taken by this game that I purchased it again on Steam and got to 100% achievements even though I had already played through it on another platform about a year and a half ago.The game gradually introduces new mechanics in a very manageable way. During my first playthrough, I had some difficulty understanding what the environment was telegraphing at certain points; however, the puzzles were well-balanced enough that they didn't become frustrating to solve.The art style and sound design are absolutely exquisite. Despite the main character's limited commentary, her expressions are so lovingly crafted that you can't help but adore her. The setting is incredibly cozy, even as we watch the protagonist and deuteragonist go through the emotional ups and downs of growing up. Carto's narrative feels like a warm hug.My only negative note about Carto is that there's not much gameplay for the price. My first playthrough took around five hours, even though I went through all of the dialogue that I could find. Assuming you paid full price (~20 USD) and considering most puzzle games' lack of replay value, it's about $4/hour, which is arguably more costly than most AAA games. That said, it does go on sale fairly often, so I'd recommend snatching it up when it's priced more reasonably.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super cute. I bought Carcassone (the board game) a few months ago and LOVED playing it with my partner and their family and this game is very similar. There is a lot of flipping the map around and cute little puzzles to do, that do get a little repetitive (I'm looking at you desert level) but overall it was a joy to watch as the story unfolded. Especially the fact that you can go into the Story Chalet and read updates about people in lands you've just left, see what their lives have turned out to be after you've gone through and messed with their maps a whole bunch. The art style is absolutely adorable, the music is charming and not super repetitive. I was able to 100% complete this (using a guide to make sure I didn't miss anything) in just one afternoon. For a quick and super chill afternoon/day of play, this is definitely a good game to get.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Finished it casually. I played it in 3 shifts of 2 hours each. It's not that difficult, but it can appear to be that way at certain puzzles. Just open your eyes and it will be fine, it's not as hard as it seems.The game mechanic is unique and in my opinion a good idea, it sets the course for interesting puzzles. More games could benefit from this map rearranging mechanic.The atmosphere is nice. The doodlelike sounds suit the game perfectly. The characters are very charming and light-heartedly fun. I honestly had a few moments where I thought that if I had a 5 to 6 year old next to me I would play this game with them and teach them how to solve the puzzles. A fun, innocent game with the added advantage of actually keeping your mind active and focused is a win for me.Just one annoyance: when you Tab out to the maps screen and you rearrange a piece of the map you have to place the map first with Space before Tabbing out. It would be more convenient if the map would just place itself when you Tab out. You have to do a lot of Tabbing in and out and rearranging at times (looking at clues in the world and rearranging the map accordingly). In 6 hours I didn't quite get used to it and still had times when I would Tab out and wonder where the piece of the map that I just placed was because I forgot to press Space before Tabbing out.Otherwise, just great.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: 100% achievement No. Yes (10 achievements). No. is a puzzle game where you move map pieces next to other pieces to connect them. Map pieces that were connected will be able to be explored, allowing you to find new map pieces to progress the game. It reminds me of 's Moving-Map gadget, except that instead of houses, you move the entire plot of land within the area. The game has 10 chapters total, showcasing unique tribes with different themes and cultures.- Some puzzles require out-of-the-box thinking to solve- Feedback whenever you are solving the puzzle in the right direction- There are no extra hints apart from the initial one that was givenIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 presents itself in cute-looking visuals. Characters look deformed with the lack of outlines to focus more on the characters' eyes and expressions. The backgrounds are also made in a similar style, with a different theme in each chapter. I like how simple and neat the interface is. It doesn't take long for me to get used to it despite the game having such a unique mechanic to learn.The story is a light-hearted one. Carto, our child cartographer, was stranded on an island and had to find her way back. She'll travel from place to place, meeting various tribes with different traditions and conditions and helping them whenever necessary. I'm amazed to see the different backgrounds and cultures that each tribe has, and how friendly they are with our protagonist.You'll be handed a map that contains rotatable map pieces, which can be used to change the terrain. This allows you to access more places, reaching previously inaccessible areas to unlock more map pieces that you can connect. There is a limitation to the connecting part though: you can only connect both pieces if their edge intersects with each other - water with water, grassland with grassland, and so on.It can be hard to understand how the puzzles work at first. You need to change your way of thinking by translating people's inquiries to rotating or moving the map pieces. The game never gives an extra hint, so you are bound to be stuck if you can't figure out the solution with that. Still, it was easy to solve most puzzles once you are in the right mindset. The game also has a concept of a "labyrinth" area where you need to navigate a seemingly endless place unless if you go in the right direction. You need to infer clues from the surroundings to figure out the direction that you need to go. I like how they are implementing these puzzles - despite being different from the usual mechanic, they are still connected with the cartographer theme. Moreover, the main mechanics will also be integrated into these areas later, giving another unique puzzle to work on.I finished all 10 chapters in the game in 4.5h. The game is roughly in the medium difficulty due to out-of-the-box thinking. I didn't have any problem solving most puzzles, although I admit that I stumbled on some of them, mostly because either I didn't understand the hints properly or the solution was different from the one that I had in mind.  is one of those games that uses unique mechanics and is implemented brilliantly. The game never changes its focus from the cartographer theme, letting you navigate the area with your unique map or the surrounding clues. You need to think differently to solve these puzzles, and it was satisfying whenever you did it right. Despite the lack of hints, the game is forgiving enough to give some feedback whenever you are going in the right direction. If you like to play unique puzzle games, feel free to buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: What a cute and interesting little game! While I'm not very far into it, the concept is great and I adore the art-style. Each level is tackled in a unique way, so if you're a fan of riddles and exploration along with an adorable little story then I can't recommend this game enough. My one gripe is that it doesn't use a mouse, but that's just my personal preference.
