_childDocuments_.review: In the past, I always had some fear towards puzzle adventure games - mainly because the ones I’ve completed until now all had a level of abstractness inside them, which was true to the puzzle mechanics and the story as well. Myst, for instance - one of the most popular games in this genre - while providing a nice experience for me, left countless questions unanswered upon completing it.However, Carto is a completely different case: it has the exact level of depth and difficulty I was looking for with an unusual game mechanic - and on top of that a genuinely heartwarming storyline.In the beginning, we meet a lovely duo consisting of Carto, a little girl, and her grandmother traveling through the world in an airship. However, from nowhere a huge storm strikes them and makes the ship unstable - causing Carto to fall from it, into the unknown - with map pieces, that her grandma uses. Her only companion is a little map, which will be the main mechanic used in the game.Our main objective and the driving force for our little cartographer is to collect every single map piece scattered throughout different biomes and to reunite with her grandmother as soon as possible. She sends her notes occasionally and watches her above whenever she has a chance. While our little protagonist only speaks a few words very occasionally she has no problem making friends in this world - right at the start she gets a new best friend, who will stick with her on the mission! Her charm also affects every single inhabitant living in this world - many great and funny dialogues are spoken through the game - with quite a few of them being rather philosophical!At first look I thought this was mainly intended for younger audiences, however, the tale of the little Carto speaks for everyone - it is essentially an inner journey for her, and for us on the other side of the screen is the feeling of being excited again about new things. It is something that is unique in childhood, and I think is superbly represented here. The aforementioned map won’t just serve us as a companion - it is actually our most valuable help! According to the story, we are cartographers - people who can move physical lands only with their map. This is the main mechanic that is being used here - it has no additional level of depth, and the short tutorial we are given at the start will actually be useful until the end.In the majority of cases, we need to form either a pattern or figure out the pattern itself using the map pieces we find scattered through the already placed map pieces. And this is maybe the most important part of keeping in mind - Carto is a puzzle adventure game, meaning that apart from solving the puzzles you are required to explore the map, in order to progress further. This also gives you the chance to learn more about the people and to find some really well-hidden secrets! While the main mechanic is really easy to understand the game could include some kind of a hint system - many puzzles require thinking outside of the box which is great, but several ones are just feeling too random. One example of this is a puzzle where you are required to uncover the secrets of the desert - I will be honest, I used a guide to get through that, but for whatever reason, my logic couldn’t be applied there. However this is a rare case, so I think the difficulty of the puzzles is fitting even for casual players like me. I’ve seen that some reviewers completed this game with their child, so I’m positive this could also work as a fun family activity - but the puzzles I think are clearly not designed solely for children.The adventuring part is a real blast, given that every different continent has something new to offer. I especially like the fact that the developers made the lore isolated, so if someone is interested they can read it, but it is totally not necessary. And yes, even if it’s simplistic Carto has quite a bit of lore to read up - it’s mostly written in a comedic way but it provides some background to where you are.Some puzzles are only solvable by exploring the pieces, and these were maybe my favorite ones - they require you to focus on the small details, on objects that at first glance would look trivial.Carto is a phenomenal puzzle-adventure game made for everyone - whether you are a vivid puzzle fan or a casual gamer, this title has many things to offer.The storyline, the art- and the audio direction all deserve praise, in my eyes the only negative point is the number of hints given out to the player.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a short, cute puzzle game with some nice art, but it really didn't scratch any itches for me. Most of the puzzles you'll get straight away, and others involve more tedium and jostling things around than properly 'solving' anything. Even the cute aesthetic I found lacklustre, most of the characters feel very flat and uninteresting despite how well they're drawn, and I started mashing spacebar to skip dialogue after a while.This could all be easier to excuse if the game didn't insist on having an awful interface for the map screen - the main mechanic you use to interact with the game. Perhaps this makes it easier to port to consoles, but only being able to move map pieces with the arrow keys is excruciating, especially when a drag-and-drop mouse interface would do the job a hundred times better. Not only that, but the game won't let you place map pieces unless they line up perfectly, and there's no easy way to swap pieces. This means if you want to swap two pieces or otherwise start manoeuvring them around, you have to throw every piece to the corner of the map then start slowly assembling them again in the centre. Why the game can't let you place map pieces illegally but not let you leave map mode until you've fixed all the problems is beyond me, it just makes you do a tonne of unnecessary extra moves to get things into place. Very tedious.I think if you go in expecting some relatively easy puzzles you might enjoy this game, but it really just wasn't what i was looking for in a puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Ridiculously charming. The underlying mechanic - move parts of the world around and stuff happens - is wonderful in its simplicity, and the resulting puzzles are thoroughly enjoyable, with only a couple of times when I impatiently ventured to the Internet for spoilers.The only annoyance is that on Mac OS it doesn't cope with the screen saver kicking in at all well (including during the end credits); you need to switch away and back to get control and sound back.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Cartography is the study and practice of making maps and therefore the clue is in the title as this game basically revolves around moving map pieces on a grid, turning and manipulating them to find your way. Carto and her grandmother are inseparable and live aboard an airship in the sky. One day a freak storm hits the airship and sends Carto hurtling out of the ship. Carto must find her way back to her grandmother. Along the way she will meet numerous characters who will aid her in her quest. My main issue with the game is that I felt it was unfair occasionally. Carto is not a traditional puzzle game where you know exactly what you need to do and the challenge is completing that goal. The game is often deliberately vague with your instructions and sometimes you are wondering what happens next. Once you know the solution it sort of makes sense but sporadically it makes no sense at all. An example, is that I was told to go visit the loch which is shaped like a fish. The puzzle here is to rearrange the pieces of the map to look like a fish and then go there. This is the solution. Now, I am no marine biologist but that is the weirdest fish I have ever seen. Other puzzles are told in riddles so you need to work out the riddle before you can rearrange the map to solve it. I got stuck on some puzzles because a new puzzle element was introduced without any tutorial. One puzzle solution didn’t even work for me until I started the level again then it miraculously worked. I don’t mind shaking up the puzzle genre. I’m all for originality, but I do get incredibly frustrated when the solution seems unfair or the question is vague. Apart from this one big ♥♥♥♥♥♥, Carto is an original, endearing and charming puzzle game with memorable characters and humorous situations. It plays out like an adventure game with lots of character interactions and story-lines. There are ten different chapters and about six or seven distinct biomes to explore. It took me around fifteen hours to complete to one hundred percent.The story and the characters were the main attraction for me. They were all extremely charismatic and you felt empathy for their predicaments. The visual style of the game is also very endearing and the whole game felt whimsical and charming. There are some nice tunes playing constantly in the background and the whole game has a very pleasant feel. Carto interacts with characters to begin brief dialogue exchanges asking her to perform certain tasks. You normally have a bit of a chat with them first and get to know them a little.She has the ability to manipulate map pieces by moving them and rotating them. There are certain rules when moving and turning them. They must match up with like sided pieces. For example, forest areas must touch other forest areas and water must touch water etc.As you progress in the chapter, new pieces of the map are found and you will discover new characters to talk to. The map pieces come in all different shapes and sizes. The more pieces, the more complicated things usually become. A typical quest is to go find and talk to a character. The tricky part is trying to rearrange the pieces so they don’t clash and your passage is not blocked by obstacles like mountains or rivers. The way the maps are designed is extremely clever sometimes.Carto can occasionally pick-up other items along the way. These rarely have any bearing on puzzles however. Usually, these items relate to the story line. Her grandmother often sends paper airplanes with accounts of how much she is trying to find Carto. These objects all enhance the storyline and the charm of the game.Between levels you will often visit the story chalet which hosts a library of books, overseen and catalogued by a story tender. All your adventures and interesting facts you have learnt on your travels will be documented here which you can read. There are a few puzzles to be completed here where you have to move the rooms around to reveal new rooms. Carto is very charming to look at even though the graphics are reasonably basic. The characters still manage to portray a certain amount of emotion through their actions and environments are varied and interesting. There are a variety of tunes playing throughout the game. Usually, one tune is associated with a certain level. They all sound very pleasant and are hardly noticeable in the background but add a nice feel to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I've only finished Chapter 1 and already I'm impressed.For starters, the very mechanic where you can manipulatethe world you play in by rearranging pieces of a map is avery fun concept that so far is taken a lot of advantage of.Characters are both humorous and look out for each otherakin to most Studio Ghibli movies like My Neighbor Totoro.I also can't help but be reminded of Hat Kid from A Hat InTime thanks to Carto. It's thanks to the fact that bot protagonistsare young girls with extraordinary powers at their disposal andtheir main conflict is to try and find their way back home, meetinginteresting and silly characters along the way. Also, because theyaren't much of a talker.The art style itself is also quite eye catching. I have a soft spot forgames that have that hand drawn, almost kids book, type of aesthetic.I recall Nintendo games like Kirby's Dreamland 3 and Paper Mariofollowing a similar direction as far as the art is concerned. Since gameslike those were staples of my childhood, seeing that again in a newergame is always appreciated.I'm so glad I came across this game and I hope you enjoy it too, if notfor the same reasons than at least for some that are similar.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the game for quite some time there's only one issue: the game can actually get boring, the interactions and the story progress is wholesome and the visuals, sounds and playtime is calm. it can get confusing sometimes but it's definitely for those who are looking for wholesome, calm yet mind-challenging games.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cute, chill, and such a cool visual style! 🤩 I got obsessed with the design during and after playing and wish there were more games with a similar style. Music is also amazing, sometimes I play it around the house or on walks.The story is simple but fun. Some of the puzzles are actually pretty challenging, but not punishing if you mess up.The map mechanic is SO well crafted and I haven't experienced anything quite like it before. It was a pretty short playthrough, but totally worth the cost if you're into any of those things.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game,I can say it worth the cost to buy it.The art style is amazing and simple,the story is great and a good ending.My challenge now is to complete all the achievements which could take a while but will be worth it.Word of advice being not to play the whole game in one sitting as you will feel dizzy.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely charming, with a truly one-of-a-kind design, Carto is a game that wants to be enjoyed by everyone, and in large part, it succeeds. Its little odyssey is full of memorable moments, feel-good interactions, and genuine wonder at the cleverness of its map-making mechanic. I had to stop myself from taking a screenshot every few minutes, as every dialogue bubble is worthy of remembering (side note: you will REALLY NEED to remember what the NPCs tell you, or you risk having no idea what to do next). Some puzzles have seriously surprising solutions, so put on your lateral-thinking cap and head on over to the Carto demo. You really won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This is a simple and relaxing story driven puzzle game. it is not too challenging so anybody should be able so solve it. the map mechanic feels very unique and is a lot of fun.Playtime should be ~5h or more if you take your time. The developer put a lot of love in this project but the story could have been a little bit deeper for my taste.it feels like a good fantasy bed time story for a child but is intended for adoults.recommendedt for people who want a relaxing happy time story.children are probablly bored by this games slow pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion this game is a masterpiece. Plain and simple. It's so original and pleasant I'll likely replay it from the start soon after I finish it. The game dynamic feels great and fills you with satisfaction among completion, it's not always as easy as one would expect and the environments are magically beautiful. The music is relaxing and pleasant the entire time.I cannot fault this game. I just hope it's longer than I expect it to be, cuz it's amazing!It'll be hard finding a substitute to this little gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable game about using your magical cartography skills to reunite with your grandma after separated by a storm. You play as Carto, a young, very quiet girl who is separated from her grandma and their airship during a storm. Along with being separated, the map you both use to navigate the world has been lost to the wind! Your mission is to find those pieces in order to reunite with your grandmother. In order to do that, you must manipulate the pieces of the map you have, and help others along the way.This gameplay feels very unique, and relaxing. Some puzzles are incredibly simple, while I did have to look up help on others. Overall I'd say they're more simple than thought provoking, especially compared to other puzzle games. The adventure and characters were very fun, and I really enjoyed the story. I wasn't planning to 100% in, but I was only missing 4 achievements (plus the achievement for getting all other achievements) so I figured why not - the game comes with a nifty 'chapter select' when you finish, so it didn't take long. Overall a very relaxing time!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This game is adorable. The story and scripting are excellent and fit really well with the puzzles. The puzzles themselves were interesting and clear. The puzzles are not super challenging, but this was partly due to the tight design. I never got frustrated with a slow progression or a tedious mechanism. Overall, an excellent way to spend an evening or two.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a somewhat clever little puzzle game with some unique ideas. I liked the concept when I first heard about it and I think it did utilize it pretty well, but there are points especially in the 2nd to last chapter (the ice world) where the puzzles are either so obscure that you have no idea what they even mean or they're so tedious to execute that it's more worth your time to look them up. There were a few obscure puzzles earlier than that chapter as well, like with the fish river, but overall I think the game isn't so bad and I'm still glad I played it.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most pleasant puzzle games I have played so far.It'a about 10 hours long, if you plan on collecting all the achievements. + Adorable style, hand-drawn (a big plus here);+ A lot of interactions and various characters you will meet along the way;+ Good chunk of different locations to visit;+ Great concept of rotating the puzzles to create new paths or unlock invisible areas;- Music could be better. I honestly don't remember any of the tracks that were playing in the background;- A little bit too easy and predictable.- Not enough side quests/things to do. The gameplay felt very linear to me.It's a nice indie gem that everyone should give a chance! You won't be disappointed, if you like shorter games.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little puzzle game that revolves around the mechanics of manipulating your environments (the map is more or less divided into tiles) to progress, mostly by listening to clues and then exchanging or turning the map parts accordingly for certain people or new tiles to appear. I have to admit that seeing these classic strategy/builder mechanics in an adventure/exploration-like game indeed felt kind of fresh to me. Story and characters are sweet, puzzles were satisfying, but not too hard, graphics are nicely hand-drawn, music is equally fitting as well. So I really did enjoy the game all in all, good for a casual time off, not too long, not too short.Two little letdowns I have to mention though. First, sadly 4K resolutions aren’t supported (only max 1440p) obviously because the hand-painted assets weren’t produced with that in mind. So depending on your set-up you might want to stick to 1080p for the sharpest image. And the other thing, I was one of the people who experienced the stuttering/jittering issue of the background while moving (this is a known bug that obviously can’t be fixed easily due to the devs). This only happened in-between, sometimes it was there, sometimes it wasn’t, mostly after switching between the map-tile-view and the normal gameplay. Also going into the settings and back at times resolved it again. Seemed like a kind of de-synching issue in my opinion. Anyway, I couldn’t really get rid of it, no tip from the forum really worked for me, neither limiting the framerate of the monitor nor using V-Sync from your graphics card, so in the end I tried to ignore it. It’s not a complete game-breaker in my opinion, but it definitely clouds a bit of the immersion, so if you’re sensitive of graphical issues, maybe better check out the demo first to see if this happens on your system as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because the reviews were "Overwhelmingly Positive" so that's why I'm leaving this negative review in case you think you should buy it too. The art is cute but not deep, the interactions with characters are simple like in a Zelda game and are either not interesting ("I'm a grumpy old man!") or involve oblique references to how you should shape the map: "she lives in the middle of the big forest!" is a really subtle hint that you need to make your map have a big forest in it. The gameplay isn't hard and for the little I played I grew to despise solving the map puzzle because it meant I had to talk to another character and solve another map puzzle after that.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: As others have described Carto is a challenging puzzle game with adorable graphics and a very creative storyline. Looking for a casual playthrough I do admit to using a walkthrough here and there, when the instructions were too vague to try out a billion different things. That did not at all limit my enjoyment of the game though! In shore - definitely recommend it for both casual and avid puzzle lovers alike!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A cute puzzle game with "feel good" vibes, suitable for players of all ages.Overall it was a bit too linear and simplistic to my taste. If you try to finish it rather quickly like I did, you may get burnt. The game is not overly long, though, so this is okay.I think gameplay-wise there are better puzzle games out there, but I can recommend it nonetheless, especially if you can get it on a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This is really a neutral one, but I'm not willing to giving a negative rating. Would I ever play this again? No. Absolutely not. I vastly over estimated my patience for this kind of walking puzzle, and I don't think that's the game's fault. What I loved was the cute design and music, the little villages I got to see in passing, and the puppies.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: It gets very boring very quickly. If you play the demo you basically already saw the rest of the game. There are more bioms you travel through and some quirky characters you meet but no one stick around for long. Gameplay wise it is really just rotate and connect map pieces. Sometimes there are specific shapes you have to arrange the tiles in but that's about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, cute light puzzle game. Charming characters and world. Good music and writing. Note this isn't a challenging puzzle game - the puzzles are entertaining and creative, but they aren't very hard. I enjoyed that and I think the creators have made that clear from the game description, but I see some negative reviews from people confused about that.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun short game. It's charming with some clever puzzles that don't break your brain, but get you to think outside the box. Overall I would recommend it. It's not one of those games you play for hours on end to finish and that is one of the refreshing aspects of it.So if you want a fun puzzle game with a cute story that does not rely on explosive action to keep you entertained and doesn't torture you with brutally hard game-play, this is a good one.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Charming little game. Clever mechanics that involve moving parts of the actual map around to change the game world. Solving the spatial puzzles also links into the story well. Couple of 15 minute headscratchers but in general this is an easygoing time with an affecting main character and story. Give the demo a try and maybe wait for it to drop to under a tenner.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A well deserved Overwhelmingly Positive, I'd say. The  is (although not quite unique, mechanics-wise), has a good unique style to it. If you were to  part, and replace it with something like gears/nuts/screws, etc., I'd say that the mechanism has already been done before, but this style of  is rarely done with such good execution.Art style, I'm a huge fan. Anything that is hand-drawn, I'm almost always immediately drawn towards it ;)I like the dialogue system in the game as well, short and concise.Sounds, music are on point.I went into the negative reviews to check out what people had to say about it. Surprisingly found a valid negative review. The game might feel like a bit of a chore after a point, the puzzle mechanism will get repetitive pretty fast. But I'd still recommend it. I personally wouldn't go for the full price, just because of the repetitive aspect, else I wouldn't mind the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a wonderful cute little puzzle game just not what I was looking for. I feel intense and focused while playing but I was looking for a relaxing game. While playing I wanted to speedrun it, not relax. I hate to give it a thumbs down because the game is well done, im just doing this so steam knows better what games to reccomend to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo, it was fine. I got the game, started playing and the way they keep presenting new pieces is just not for me...- Dunno what people find charming in here, I was only drawn by the graphic's art.- Bland story;- Mute character (can only say "...");- Lots of RNG;- Glitches;- Be a seer to know where to leave empty spaces;- storms, winds and musical notes will guide you... until you leave an empty space on the right place.I already came back to this game several times, but every time I start a new chapter I start rolling my eyes with the RNG and get frustrated. There's no charm in here!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a gem in the world of puzzle adventures. The story is beautifully woven, drawing players into its enchanting narrative. Visually, it's a treat – the graphics are not just eye-catching but contribute to the overall charm of the game. The puzzles, though challenging, feel like a satisfying brain workout rather than frustration. It's a game that effortlessly balances story, graphics, and gameplay, making it a must-play for anyone seeking a delightful and immersive gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: carto is sucha cute lil puzzle game. i loved the story-line, the music, the art and everything. its the perfect game to play to unwind and relax and its also still challenging. i really didnt want the game to end, but i also did at the same time because i wanted to see the story through. the story is so sweet!! i loved bein a cartographer :) i highly recommend, pls play
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a journey worth taking. It is a wonderfully charming game that leads you through a well-crafted world filled with great characters. The puzzles are enjoyable and the artistic style of the game is fantastic. An overall very chill, very good experience.Carto is an adorable little game where you guide titular character Carto on her journey back to her family. You explore a variety of environments and learn about the stories of the people who reside there while collecting map pieces to try and find your way back home.All the audio (sounds, talking, music) fit the mood/atmosphere of this fun and bubbly game. It's all really relaxing and there's no pressure at all. The art is very stylistic and really fits with the whole cartography aesthetic of the game, while still being user-friendly and easy on the eyes! Most things in the game are signified through iconography which is awesome and makes the game a lot more immersed as opposed to having words spell it out for you.The puzzles are very neat! There are a variety of them, mostly based on the whole map mechanic, which doesn't get old and doesn't punish you for getting a puzzle wrong! There are some other puzzles that mix the map-mechanics with other mechanics such as audio to give the game a little toss-up at times and keeps the experience fresh throughout.The characters are all lovely and they make the game more colourful from their text to their personalities. None are too overbearing or unlikable, which makes talking to them a little more worthwhile.Again, Carto is a journey worth taking! Recommended for those with a want for a good puzzle/narrative game, as well as those with only a handful of free time.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cute little adventure game.The first game I bought on steam was Lume, and this has a similar paper texture!The map segments stitch together seamlessly too.Music's relaxing, and I like how the various musicians fade in/out/accompany the overall bgm.Puzzles are relatively simplistic: you hunt down fragments of the map, then rotate them to create the new map according to  hints from npcs. I'd say it's more story-driven than puzzle-driven because of this.Controller isn't required, but feels much better because there's no key rebinding atm, and default controls use the arrow keys.Price point seems a bit steep, as I'm ~1hr in on chapter 3 of 10, and the mechanics + puzzles so far haven't really been improved/iterated upon, but maybe that'll change.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game, in so many ways :) makes my heart warm and my step lighter.The puzzles are a perfect level of difficulty, and are very varied. The mechanic could get old, but doesn't.This game is a labor of love in such a beautiful, tender way. Highly recommend for a nice dose of warm fuzzies :D
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adorable, is the first thing that comes to mind while thinking about Carto. The character design and interactions are some of the cutest ever in the industry. The music fits perfectly with the games aesthetics.The gameplay is an original approach to puzzles that focuses on spining and placing blocks on a map. I expected a chill game but some of the puzzles are actually very challenging/seem impossible without help, so be warned.Technically, I was disapointed to see no ultrawide in options. The game is perfectly playable in ultrawide but you will have to hack it at every launch.*No native ultrawide support
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I spent not a lot time in it, but anyway I can say the general thoughts about it. It is cozy, aesthetic and pretty game. You will enjoy a soundtrack, graphics and game mechanics, but here are some drawbacks... Even if you think that this game is easy on first glance, you are mistaken. Sometimes you can find it pretty dificult to find a solution for a quiz, it will take time until you'll figure it out. But, it is definately worth to play on calm and chilly evening.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a wonderfully made game. The art style and animation are absolutely adorable and I loved every character. The puzzle's difficulty progression, which is split into "chapters", is well-done. From personal experience, all the chapters were easy enough to where I didn't need an abnormal amount of time to figure out what needed to be done. The story was simple yet cute, and each zone was unique, interesting, atmospheric, and left me wanting to explore even more. My only complaints are that learning the hidden map mechanics can be tricky to find and the controls never really cemented into my memory (played on controller). Otherwise, this game felt very nice to play and has gone above and beyond my expectations. I hope this developer studio creates more games in the future.I would HIGHLY recommend this game to anyone interested in a visual-pleasing puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a very sweet, wholesome puzzle game about a little cartographer finding her grandmother. With hand-drawn graphics, a wonderful story line and quirky characters, it definitely has a lot of heart. The mechanics are pretty simple and easy to pick up, but the puzzles and story manage to keep the game feeling fresh and diverse without relying on introducing new mechanics all the time. It's pretty short and the puzzles aren't that difficult, so if you want a novel game for a chill afternoon/evening, I would so recommend picking this up, especially if it's on sale. I also think it would be a good game to buy for a child, provided you're around to maybe give them a hand on some of the more vague puzzle hints.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: What a gentle, relaxing, cute, cheerful little game.I enjoyed every moment of it. The atmosphere, created by the visuals and the music, filled my heart with joy.The story is lovely, the puzzles are challenging enough to keep the game interesting but easy enough to let you proceed without getting frustrated.Great game to be played together with the whole family or by yourself to relax.I'm still smiling.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10Honestly, one of the most unique styles of puzzle games I have ever seen. Besides the fact that the story is rich with clever and fun characters, the game feels full and exciting despite it's length. I love puzzle games that have replay value, and I have found that this one keeps me interested each time I feel like replaying it. The worlds feel so open and the unique design with the map pieces being movable keeps me wanting to explore. Each new world was so special to visit and being able to tie the whole world and story together makes this game feel so full circle. Seriously, this is a game that I would recommend to anyone, because it is so pure and simple, but there is so much to make it endlessly fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so adorable and relaxing. The very first time I started it up, it immediately illicited the same feelings at a Studio Ghibli movie does. It brings up the same sense of warmth and familiarity and overall it's such a comforting experience. The gameplay mechanics feel fresh to me and I don't find it repetitive. I highly recommend this game if you like puzzles and cuteness.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I'm actually a bit hesitant to recommend this game. For puzzle fanatics, I don't think this game is interesting enough (except for Chapter 9 which is way harder than the others). The mechanism is similar to a board game called Carcassonne, where you would connect the map pieces and the boundaries should have the same terrain on both sides. The concept itself is fun, but the story driving the game and the designed puzzles are mostly lightweight IMO. The instructions are sometimes not clear enough for me to know how to proceed, and some of them will become patterns across chapters. Nevertheless, it is a cool idea and an okay experience that can be improved. If you are happy with not-so-difficult brain teasers, this game is surely a recommendation for you.

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely cute and fun game about a little girl trying to find her ways in the world after getting separated from her grandmother. Gameplay is very fun. There's tons of walking but mostly very interactive and involving puzzles. There might be some puzzles that can be very confusing but that doesn't deter me from having fun to solve it without feeling even a little bit of frustration.The dialogues are great. You can have some funny moments with the other characters in the game. Here's a tip, make sure you try to interact with everything in the game. Sometimes, even a rock or a tree holds a secret within the game.Sound design is amazing. The ambient and environment sounds as well as the soundtracks totally transports you to the biomes the game is presenting to you. The sounds of birds chirping, water splashing and it even have really neat sound effects that lets you know when you're making a mistake during a walking puzzle that does not disrupt the immersion whatsoever, in fact they add more to the environment.However, if there's one thing I dislike about this game is the fact that it stutters all the time. It's not that the game is dropping frames or have unstable frame time, it's just that the game world does not move smoothly with the camera as you move around the world in some biomes. Other than that, the game runs perfectly well on any system.

_childDocuments_.review: Carto, the Carcasonne puzzle game you never knew you wanted, is cute. Really, really cute. Toe to tip, everything you find in this game is a real cutie. You guide a girl who speaks in emojis through some strange and lovely islands, hugging bears and petting camels and making friends and enjoying some pretty funny dialogue that fits very nicely into what I call . It's like a relaxing and fluffy blanket game; there's no real antagonism, no real villains, no fail states, just lots of problems to solve with positive thinking.You'd think map tiles as a puzzle mechanic wouldn't have legs, but Carto manages to squeeze every bit of mileage from the premise without resorting to unnecessary abilities or gimmicks. It also ends pretty perfectly, wrapping up just as the puzzle mechanic can't stretch any further. Finding that right puzzle game balance between brevity and padding is tough, but Carto nails it.I mean, it's cute! What more can I say? It's a seriously adorable game to play over a couple afternoons. It's happy and warm and just plain nice, definitely a good way to cheer up on a rainy day.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: "Carto" has a very unique gameplay gimmick of re-arranging pieces of a map to change the actual game world and fully utilizes it. Presentation and soundtrack is very cute too.The story is divided in multiple chapters that each have their own story going on, but unfortunately aren't very connected to each other so the transitions feel a bit awkward.The game is a bit on the short side, since you can finish it in about 6 hours, so I would recommend to buy it on sale as I did because the full price is a bit steep.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a big recommend. Most of the puzzles are pretty easy, but can get a little obtuse if you're going for 100% - I did have to look up a solution or two for that. The gameplay is simple but quite satisfying (mostly because of the map spinning haha) and I really liked the story - again nothing out there, but it was easy to get into and just want to follow along. Also the art style is really nice! Very smooth animations, great textures and sound effects that just culminate in a very well put together style (and overall game!).
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A puzzle game where you manipulate map pieces in order to change the world around you. This mechanic is very clever and unique. This puzzle mechanic is its strongest part and is constantly used in different interesting ways.Mostly all the stuff surrounding it, mainly the story and characters. The story is nothing special and the characters are not interesting to me. They are mostly a framing device for the actual puzzles, but they take up too much time and drag the whole game out to a slog. Even when just skipping through all dialogue there are parts that are more down time than gameplay and it makes it so not worth it.Another problem is that once I figured out the formula for the puzzles it became a bit too easy for me. I have read that they become more difficult later, but I never got that far. The gameplay itself never became boring since the mechanics felt so fresh and satisfying, but with constant interruptions it broke the flow. It became more and more of a chore to get to the good parts. I made it about half-way and unfortunately I have no desire to come back and finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: My expectations from this game were so low that I never even thought I could love the game this much. Carto truly offers a unique gameplay mechanic that I have never seen before. By using map pieces, you change the positions of the world and embark on various adventures to reunite with your irresponsable Granny. The puzzles become more complex and challenging as you progress through the levels. However, the game is neither excessively difficult nor excessively easy. It's just right. _childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto although short, makes use of every second of its playtime to tell a sweet charming story while being a fun game mechanically. Oftentimes small indie games are able to take one small concept to scopes you would not expect and carto is a great example of that. The art is gorgeous, the dialogues charming and the characters very interesting. The real pull of carto however is how it uses the theme of cartography as a mechanic, making you form maps like jigsaw puzzles, creating a path for yourself to reach the goal. The puzzles never felt frustrating, the clues are hidden well enough but not to a point where it would require luck, the game slowly invites you in by increasing the difficulty in increments. Loved every second of this game and highly recommend you cop this :) i rate carto a certified banger
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a fantastic little title with an incredibly original premise.The world around you is your puzzle. You collect map pieces as you adventure, and you have to utilise these by rearranging the map, flipping the pieces, etc. This affects your world, amd your world changes as you spin and move the map pieces around trying to figure out the puzzles.Some of the puzzles can make you think pretty hard and will make you scratch your head. There's 10 chapters to the games story, with 20 achievements to get, with 10 of them being cryptic, secret achievements.I highly recomend this title for anyone looking for a casual adventure title that will ensure you use your brain at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo for the game and was able to get a cheap key for it. I was eager to play the game as the demo was really fun and the idea of the whole thing is interesting: solving puzzles by manipulating the map. it worked well in the demo and I was looking forward to the rest of the game.Sadly, I was disappointed. While most people seem to have had a lot of fun playing it, my experience differed. The game looks amazing and the story is somewhat there (nothing that special though), music is nice and everything.But: controls on keyboard are HORRIBLE and it becomes such a chore to play this game because of unintuitive keybindings (you can't even change) and constant mistyping. The puzzles also turn out to be very very weird later on. I had to look up a guide more times than not to solve a "puzzle" because the solution was just so... stupid? and nothing i would have come up with myself. Might just be a "me" problem, maybe I think differently than the game wants me to think like but it just didn't work for me. Wanna catch fish in a lake? Better make the lake look like the fish u wanna catch! _childDocuments_.review: To think that one of my favourite games I've played in recent memory would come through a random giveaway I won. Carto is an amazing little puzzle game with an easy-to-understand yet hard-to-master mechanic. With beautiful graphics, touching music and a simple story, Carto over delivers with the absolute charm that emanates from within. I think it's totally worth it whatever the price of this game is in your region. Please give it a try if you can!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended. Its hard to put into words how much i enjoyed this game. While the game is based around this map shifting mechanic, at its heart Carto is an adventure game in the same vein as an old Tim Schafer style of adventure game. Great art style, great characters, whimsical story, and fun logic puzzles that wont stress you out too much but will make you say "that was clever" when you solve them. Just the right length too - any longer and I think this game would have outstayed its welcome. Also very easy to clean up achievements with most unlocked along the way and a handy chapter select that lets you get to exactly where you need to go without any hassle.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing this game for a while, and I kind of forgot about it. I recently went to finish it, and I realized that this is actually one of my favorite games of all time. It's a really cute puzzle game about a young girl named Carto finding her way back to her grandma, who flies a blimp and is a cartographer. She uses the skills her grandma taught her to piece things together and make her way back up to her. It's really fun moving the puzzle pieces of the map together to unlock new parts, and it's always cute to see what her reaction is and who she meets. I love all the little animal friends, and her people friends are great too, I like how they learn and develop (especially one but it's kinda a spoiler). I really recommend this game a lot, it's a bit confusing sometimes but so much fun and very relaxing. You can play it at any pace and there's so much to enjoy I don't see a single person on earth that shouldn't buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and unique puzzle-exploration game with plenty of interesting worldbuilding (in more ways than one), bundled in a cute hand-drawn package--just watch that you don't get too turned around while playing. At about 4 hours to complete, it's a lot of fun to see it to the story's end, but achievement completion will require some less-fun backtracking for not much reward.  is a puzzle game in which you play a young cartographer tasked to shape the world around you to try and find your missing granny, while solving the problems of those you meet along the way. The gameplay is a mix of exploration and puzzle solving that largely revolves around the use of your map, as finding and moving pieces on the world map will reshape the landscape in its image and allow access to new areas in the process. , as all the flipping and turning of map pieces might mess with your sense of direction over time. Each area is also populated by a unique cast of characters, and each one has their own distinct cultures and quirks that will occasionally interact with one another. Thanks to this, , and it's one you'll find yourself wanting to explore further. All of this is wrapped in  that makes you feel like you're running around inside the pages of a storybook. Some of the achievements revolve around secret objectives that are easily missed, and completing a chapter without finding them can lock you out of getting it until you unlock chapter selection after beating the game--though using this will make you replay the entire chapter from the start, puzzles and unskippable cutscenes and all. It's by no means the biggest issue, but the need to replay a good chunk of the game to find something you missed adds just a bit of tedium to full achievement completion. (though I used a guide for hints after a while). Despite my gripes while attempting full completion, reaching the story's end felt satisfying, and I'm glad I played it to the end.  I'm not sure if the crew at Sunhead Games will consider expanding on the world that  built or decide shift their focus to something new, but if they bring the same creativity to their next project that they did here, I'm confident that it'll be something well worth the wait.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute music and nice art style.I was intrigued by the unique map arranging mechanic and expected it to produce some interesting puzzles. However, for the most part the puzzles are very straight-forward and this makes the gameplay dull and feel more like a chore.The game has a bit of a story but it's pretty trivial and uninspiring. I guess the characters were supposed to be cute and quirky, but I found them pretty annoying.In retrospect, it seems that this game's target audience is extremely young children and it's not for everyone. Personally, by the end of the game I was extremely glad to be done with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this was a very nice distraction. Very well put together, inventive mechanics, charming art style, endearing characters, heartfelt story. This little gem has it all. The only two nitpicks I might name are it's pretty short, and puzzles are on the simpler side. But frankly, I needed a break from TIS-100, and Carto delivered.So, this is a visual puzzle game. Most puzzles work like, uh, jigsaw puzzles. Some require you to pay attention to dialogue and a little out-of-the-box thinking, but nothing too arcane. I will admit, I got stuck for a bit a couple of times, but talking to each character cleared those up quickly.So, the good:+ Charming art style+ Endearing characters+ Inventive mechanics+ Engaging puzzles+ Heartfelt storyThe neutral:* Music... it's there. It's not particularly great, it's not bad either. Not something I would choose to listen to on its own, but fit for purpose.* Puzzles are on the simpler side, but depending on what you're looking for it might be just the thing* Pretty short, can be finished in 4 to 5 hours at a leisurely pace.* Frankly, it's on the pricier side for indie titles, at least in my region, but well worth it in my opinion.The bad: uh... there aren't any, not that I can think of.It's a simple game, sure, but it does what it sets out to do extremely well, and then some. Overall, highly recommended. On sale, should be a no-brainer if it seems at all interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe next time you create a chill-out, wholesome and peaceful game... don't put animal abuse in it?So, hear me out: I had fun at the beginning. I really love the aesthetics, the music is nice and the puzzles are easy but still fun. But then comes the volcanic region. There you *have* to kill a beautiful bird by burning it alive. It also gives out a suffering cry before going down. Yeah... right, so peaceful and chill out. After that you have to join the other characters and eat the dead bird. Why tho? It's not a survival game, it's not a realistic simulation game, it’s also mystical and fantastical so you could have created literally any other situation for that puzzle.Well... a few puzzles after that, you have to participate in a fishing contest. Even there you could have made a "let's clean up the ocean" situation out of that, fishing out trash or something like that. But that's not enough... when talking to the people at the event one character glorifies feeding their toddler the offal and eyes of the fish because it's allegedly so healthy.Those things are just sooo unnecessary for such a cute game. Why you opt for glorifying animal abuse in such a way in such a game is just beyond me.Also, the storytelling is quite boring and I ended up skipping every dialogue because it just felt so absolutely interchangeable meaningless.

_childDocuments_.review: Neutral if I could give it.'Cute' and 'wholesome' is almost all this game's described as, and that's about right. _childDocuments_.review: A truely wholesome game ❤️Traveling the world by map - who doesn't dream of it.Carto ist a cozy game with a unique game mechanic: finding your way and solving puzzles by manipulating pieces of a map. The game is completed by its encouraging storyline and charming artstyle.What I particularly enjoy, is the encouraging storyline: a girl getting lost and trying to find her way back could be a very gloomy story, but instead, this premise is treated with such love and hope that it becomes about exploring, confidence, finding out, where your path leads and growing on the journey.Carto is very skillfully crafted and consistent, as the game mechanics and the storyline intertwine and the journey of the game becomes a confidence inspiring metaphor for finding your place in the world.So, don't buy this game, if you're looking for difficult puzzles and fast paced action adventure stories.Definitely, totally buy this game, if you would like to:- solve medium difficult puzzles with great variety- dive into a wholesome vibe- make friends with a lot of kind, considerate and welcoming characters on your way- enjoy the charming artstyle that creates adorable characteres, beautiful trees and varied sceneries of all continents

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a lovely little puzzle game with a fun mechanic - you can control the map pieces like they're Carcassonne tiles. I found myself wanting to come back as much for the next bit of the story as the next puzzle.Recommended if you like light puzzle games.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute and cozy puzzle game with a twist! Using the map pieces as part of the puzzle added another layer of thinking required to finish this game. _childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: What a sweet game! I can highly recommend this to anyone who likes a chill, puzzle game with a simple story, fun cast of characters, cute art style and nice music. It was an easy, but substantial playthrough. They did a nice job of slowly ramping up the mechanics for interacting with the world and even the few times I got stuck on a puzzle (to my credit, often trying to do what was ultimately the right thing, but not quite in the right way enough usually) I was able to figure out the correct solution for myself after a bit. I think this is a nice game for folks who are really into puzzles (like myself) and also folks who are casually into puzzles because nothing is trying to trick you or be sneaky! It also does a lovely job with the achievements (Kudos to you, developers!) and allows you a detailed chapter select after you've beaten the game, which helps you to hop back in right where you need to be to chase down any that you missed if you're interested in getting them all. _childDocuments_.review: A truly original puzzle game about rearranging the tiles of the world map to progress. Given this core mechanic, the developers really put an effort in making the puzzles non repetitive: almost each puzzle has its own original solution, some of which are mostly logical while some others require a bit of creativeness and lateral thinking. Challenging and fun without being hardcore. Also, the overall experience of the adventure part of the game is peaceful: there's no enemies, no time, no deaths, no way of doing things wrong. The only things you need to do are wandering, observing anything that stands out and talking to everyone you meet. This is not only to appreciate the colorful world and some witty jokes, but also because most of the times the people you meet wil give you hints about what you need to do next.Absolutely suggested you like relaxing puzzles with some story and with something different from the usual puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: So this has almost universal acclaim.........and I can't imagine why that is.The game revolves around finding pieces of maps and then rotating and assembling the pieces to alter the in-game level that you are on.  It's a brilliant concept, with cute artwork, and.........well,  music, hampered by minimalistic (bordering on completely unnecessary) sound design, and utterly crippled by (especially in the last three or four levels) opaque puzzle design with 100% frustrating mechanics, poorly explained goals, and (from pretty much the second level onward) puzzles with only ONE solution despite several presenting themselves.In addition to the "" style of puzzle solution, there are a few other crimes that puzzle games can commit on display here, including (but not limited to) puzzles that involve randomly generated pathways that you must go down, and opaque puzzles with no actual hints or clues offered as to what exactly you're supposed to be solving in the first place.  And the final puzzle where you have to manipulate multiple map sections to create precisely one layout, sometimes involving more than a dozen sections each with four degrees of possible rotation and multiple pieces with complementary map components that they could be placed beside........YEEEEESH!!Bottom line, I consulted a walkthrough  times just to complete the game because I was so stymied by the arcane, opaque puzzle design (not all, mind you......some where quite manageable.....but definitely a LOT!), the poorly communicated puzzle goals, and the inflexible nature of some of the solutions.Definitely not recommended, though obviously YMMV considering how well reviewed and respected the game is.

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a game that immediately put me in a good mood when I started playing it. Every pore of it exudes this wholesome childlike wonder I remember from games I’ve played when I was a kid, from the cute aesthetic to the heartfelt and sincere little stories you can find in there. And it’s all expressed through a simple and easy to understand mechanic.At its heart, Carto is a puzzle game, where you have the ability to rearrange tiles that make up any given level and create your own map to traverse and explore. You can rearrange and rotate these tiles around, but for them to neatly fit together, the sides of the tiles you want to put next to each other have to match up. So a land tile can only be put next to other land tiles and not sea tiles. There are obviously appropriate tiles that feature multiple terrain types to form connections between disparate tiles so you can cross over from one to the other.It's a very simple but cleverly implemented mechanic and it’s used with surprising variety. While you start out by simply exploring these levels in order to pick up additional map pieces to place, you also have to solve a variety of puzzle with those pieces in order to find new parts of the map. The puzzles become progressively more involved and a lot of it requires paying attention to the dialogue and interpret some of the things characters tell you. This can for example mean placing a tile at a specific spot to form an island’s northern most spot or aligning a couple of tiles in a certain way to generate new terrain in between them, like in this example, where you’re given the task of finding something in a tile that’s surrounded by snowy flowers on all sides. You then have to arrange these tiles so that the empty tile in the middle is surrounded by the aforementioned flowers, upon which a new tile spawns to solve the puzzle.As you can guess, the game starts out with only a small variety of tiles that gradually expands to offer more terrain types. The game also starts off by letting you move around individual square tiles but then moves onto combining these tiles into larger shapes, with the last couple of chapters having shapes inspired by the tetronimos from Tetris.I like how the game manages to keep a really tight focus on these puzzles, especially whenever you visit the Chalet and get to rearrange the rooms within it or whenever some other puzzle follows the same rearranging gameplay in a different context. Narratively, the game is fairly simple and straightforward as well. The basic gist is that Carto is flying around in an airship with her grandmother, who introduces her to the concept of rearranging parts of a map to change the environment around her. When Carto accidentally combines airship with a thunderstorm, she and a bunch of map fragments get blown out of the vessel, the latter getting spread all around the world. The goal is for Carto to gather up all the map pieces to get back to her grandmother.This takes her around a bunch of biomes to meet characters with a variety of problems that predictably all get solved by Carto through her power to re-arrange the way the map looks. But what elevates the experience is the way the characters are written. Each of the chapters focuses on different biomes that are inhabited by a unique tribe of people. They all exhibit unique characteristics that befit their respective biomes and manage to frame stories that fit their settings nicely. There’s a wholesomeness to the writing and the little stories you get to experience that’s often lacking in many modern games, which is why it made me feel like a kid again.Add to that the gorgeous visuals and soundtrack and I have no qualms recommending Carto to anyone looking for a relaxing little puzzle game that makes you feel all warm and fuzzy inside once you’re done with it.

_childDocuments_.review: That godforsaken grating repeating flute/whistle sound in Chapter 2's BACKGROUND music is enough to justify a thumbs down all by itself.The constant loop of picking up a map piece and opening the map gets old very fast, even before the obtuse tedious "puzzles" on the same wavelength as point-and-click adventures (my least favorite game genre overall) get introduced.Dialogue and cutscenes are unskippable, can't autoadvance, and are even more boring than the gameplay itself.Shame, seems pretty polished otherwise. _childDocuments_.review: Another easy recommendation on account of a free demo. I enjoyed almost everything about this game except for its signature mechanic, which becomes especially tedious with more and more tiles. I can think of a couple ways of elegantly handling the situation of dissimilar tiles against each other (eg. not allowing mode switching until conflicts are resolved, for one), because the added challenge of having to constantly rearrange the board before being able to even try something new was hugely tedious.Puzzle tedium aside,  had a really nice balance of content. The right game length, the correct amount of characters and stories, varied environments, and good ambient music for a puzzle game (except at the very end). Following the gameplay tradition of one full dialogue + single line follow-up per event per stationary NPC kept the progression pace well. Repurposing known locations as the story progressed felt appropriate and I felt easily satisfied by game's end as no side stories were left unfinished.One review I saw before buying the game suggested some of the puzzle solutions would require using a guide, which I did not find to be true (optional achievements aside). It is not always totally obvious what to do and I did occasionally need to resort to screenshots and handwritten notes, but it is at least doable without resigning to trial and error. In fact, that you  need to directly interact with your inventory or guess which item to use in a given situation is one of the game's best features.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for August 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before September 7th, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.In October 2020, I made a joke that if I waited long enough Carto might be released in the bundle. 10 months later, that came true, and honestly, Carto is an excellent game.  Carto’s main gameplay is the ability to manipulate a map and change the world in near real-time.  Moving a map square on the map screen and suddenly everything around our main character is new. Carto is done as a level-based experience, giving players different challenges, puzzles, and goals.  Out of the three maps I’ve seen, each one has a different style and feeling to the story, giving a fresh experience.  If Carto can keep up the solid writing and interesting characters, this will be an excellent adventure.  It’s said to be about five to six hours, so I’m hopeful it will fill that time with a worthy experience. Pick this up if you like puzzle games again, at the same time, this is a bit of a strange style of puzzle where it’s mostly involving moving map pieces around or catching clues from what people will repeat multiple times.  Again if you don’t like puzzles, this might not be for you. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Carto caught my interest, due to its beautiful artwork and very unique map manipulation mechanics. However as I played through it something didn't feel right, but I couldn't quite put it into words.  I finally realized that this game is very hallow. Its like the game creators took a handful of concepts and tried to make an entire game by spreading them out as thin as possible . Most of the map mechanics involve moving putting certain pieces together in a certain way to get a hidden piece to be revealed. After seeing this pattern getting repeated all the way to the fourth level of the game, I realized this what you do throughout the whole game.  Needless to say I was very disappointed.  If you wan't a game that does this concept so much better, go check out a Fisherman's Tale. I know its a VR Game, but it has a very similar mechanic to Carto. However A Fisherman's Tale has far more creative uses for its world altering mechanics and a far better narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a fun puzzle game with a unique mechanic that requires you to create each level's map by combining blocks in order to advance.Although the puzzles in Carto aren't particularly brain-wrecking, some of them might take a while to figure out.As the game isn't very long, and each level introduces a couple of new mechanics, it never gets boring.The story of Carto and all the people (and animals!) that she meets on her adventure is really heart-warming, and with a bit of humour thrown in now and then.The art style, that, by the way, reminded me of Broken Age, and the music couldn't be more perfect for this kind of game.Definitely recommended to people interesting in puzzle games that won't make one's brain boil, but that can offer a new experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A cute little puzzle game with a creative mechanic where you find tiles of the map and place them anywhere to expand the map. The puzzles have you arranging the map in clever ways to, say, find someone in the biggest forest or traverse the desert by following clues.The art style is cute, the character interactions are wholesome, and the puzzles are inventive.It's a fairly short game, but doesn't get too repetitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: It was okay. I think I see why others like it, but it didn't hit the notes I was looking for. Most puzzles were too simple, and the levels seem to repeat their formula to a point where I lost interest eventually. The art style was cute, but I wish there was a bit more depth to the characters than their quirks. I admit I didn't play to the end, but I did get far enough to revisit some settings and characters and they just didn't take the opportunity to develop characters further.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good game but it makes me wish steam had a different way of aggregating reviews besides a binary thumbs up and down. This game kind of falls in the middle. Most of it is great ... but it does an absolutely horrible job of tutorializing certain puzzle aspects. Oftentimes getting stuck on a puzzle in this game is akin to getting stuck putting a regular puzzle together on a table - except that you're stuck because you don't realize there's still a puzzle piece left in the box. Upon checking a walk-through you will be confronted with the solution there is no possible way you could have known existed since it was never present in the game before and never hinted at at all. It's shoddy. They definitely could have used some outside testing on this one to iron that out. The rest is genuinely lovely though. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a puzzle game where you help a young girl travel the land after she gets lost in a storm. By collecting pieces of a map, you discover new places. Simple enough. The hook is the fact that once you have the map, you can rearrange its pieces. This core mechanic informs a lot of how you'll progress through the game.The writing is simple, a lot like the art style, but that just makes the characters you'll meet all the more memorable.Definitely worth a try if you've got about 6 hours to spend and a fan of puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I found myself wanting to play this game constantly once I got started and got into a rhythm with the puzzles. Personally, I found the puzzles the perfect amount of clever and difficult. If replayability is important to you, I actually haven't found myself wanting to replay it, but I enjoyed it nonetheless. I would definitely recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, would recommend if you want to play a chill game here and there. Overall gameplay time is not very long, but depends on how fast you solve the clues. Some of the clues are not that obvious and took me a fair bit longer than others. Great aesthetics too, very calming from the story to the music, artwork and gameplay. Keen to play this game again in a year when I've forgotten the solutions.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I’d like to start off by iterating that this isn’t the kind of game I’d usually play. The only reason I did is because I got it via Humble Choice.Carto has two things going for it; the cute artstyle, and the innovative gameplay. That said, the puzzles get less innovative and more intuitive as the game progresses, which doesn’t work in its favour. For someone dyspraxic like me, a lot of the late-game puzzles become an absolute nightmare for this exact reason. I can count 3 distinct parts where I would’ve given up had it not been for guides, and I’m sure there are more I’m forgetting.I personally found the whole thing to be over-expositive, which I know is a strange comment for a narrative-driven game, but I was done reading all the dialogue by the end of chapter 2. By chapter 5, the novelty had worn off and I was bored.The looping OST of each island, paired with unnecessary hitboxes and intermittent frame drops quickly became irritating. The game is also rife with tedious backtracking; something unexpected in a game where the main mechanic is changing the layout of the world. For the price, I definitely wouldn't recommend it.Once again, this isn’t the kind of game I normally play, so feel free to take my word with a grain of salt.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a simple yet outstanding game, I have loved every second of my first play through, and I'm sure to play it again!the last few days have been really difficult for me, but Carto has helped me feel a bit better, it's a little safe place away from the world. I could not recommend this game to you strongly enough, please, if you enjoy relaxing games, do yourself a favour, and purchase Carto!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an adorable and endearing art style and soundtrack to experience during the ups and downs of following a magic map. The controls are simple and would 100% recommend for people that love series of simple puzzles with a nice adventure plot driving you further into the unknown. I am pretty dumb at times and relied on a guide, but that still didn't take away my joy from playing and the admiration I had for all the small details and interactions the devs put into the game!! FYI: Getting the airship achievement is worth it in my opinion to further see all the hard work put into making such a good game with great art work
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A sweet game about family, togetherness, and community with light-hearted tones and enjoyable scenery, music and gameplay. Wholeheartedly recommend at least trying out since it's not too long and you'll get the feel of it in a few minutes of playing, both tone and mechanics-wise, to know if it's not for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I like Carto for what it is. It's a very simple puzzle game for all ages with a positive story and the occasional hidden secret. It's easy to lose yourself for hours playing this and trying to find the hidden achievements while enjoying the relatively straightforward story.There's a puzzle that uses degrees as a hint, so this probably isn't appropriate for anyone who hasn't been exposed to simple algebra. Say 10 or 11 year-olds or so at minimum.Give the demo a shot. It's pretty spot on for the level of difficulty for the whole game. There are one or two more complex puzzles, but mostly this is a title to sit back and enjoy.Also has a huggable bear. Who says no to a huggable bear?
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A sweet, sweet little adventure that will leave you wishing for much more!The story is heartwarming and wholesome, the puzzles are incredibly clever and super fun, and the art is cute, lovely, and truly refreshing... I literally loved everything about it. Totally, wholeheartedly, 100% recommended! Don't miss out on this little treasure.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: 30/100 This is not really a game.  It's a bunch of meaningless fetch quests, interspersed with a whole lot of clicking through dialog so bad that it sounds like it was written by a 10 year old.  The map puzzles are initially really interesting but quickly grow obscure and tiresome.  If you want a decent puzzle game I would recommend instead Superliminal, The Witness, Tametsi, Hexcells Infinite, or Opus Magnum.  If you want a decent adventure game with dialog and story that puts this to shame, I would recommend instead The Walking Dead or Life is Strange.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Cute characters, cute music, fun puzzles.Most chapters felt like a breeze, some chapters required a bit of thinking outside of the box, and Chapter 9 made me feel like I was testing into MENSA. Also, really like the bonus content you get from collecting all of the "secrets." I loved the time I spent travelling with Carto!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a Indie Puzzle Adventure game and a really heartwarming and enjoyable one at that. The estimated gameplay time is around 5 hours for me, but I really enjoyed every single moment of it. I recommend it if you're a fan of relaxing light-hearted puzzle solving like A Short Hike and Journey. It's on PC, PlayStation and Switch.Also has a good soundtrack. All the single player games I recommend have good OST.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice puzzle game with a poetic touch. A little more than 5 hours to finish it. The difficulty is nice : not too easy not too hard (though some part might be a little hard for some people, like the "angle" puzzle).The only bad point is the fish riddle which is stupid because it ask you to do a fish and you get stuck here a long time because you can't do a fish, the answer is something stupid which is not a fish, had to search on google for the answer.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto was a more-than-awesome game (for me, personally) in terms of graphics, narrative, storytelling and it has a very refreshing game mechanism. Super cute characters and environments! I've never played something like that ٩(◕‿◕｡)۶ Game was fun and it was really interesting to browse around to find different ways to solve map puzzles. One great thing that I appreciate was there was no hint option- the game encourages you to find the solution instead of relying on help.I got this during sales but it's such a gem. Would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a great game. I especially love the presentation and core concept of puzzles that change the world as you explore it. I think it struggled a bit in character development and in the way puzzles are framed. Carto only communicating through smiley faces quickly got old. I don't think she needed to be such a blank slate. The game is often at map scale, so I don't need to identify with the player avatar; she can take on more personality. That would've helped make the relationships which are emphasized throughout the game feel more genuine. I think progression could've been a bit smoother. Points where I struggled were almost always because I didn't talk to the right person enough times or find the right item, not because the puzzles were hard. I think that's not the way it should be. Overall, Carto was a very cute, relaxing puzzle game with a lot of personality and a great core concept. I'm looking forward to Carto 2. There's tons of room to expand on mechanics and smooth out some problems.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto's a fun little game about changing a map to change the world. The puzzles aren't too difficult, and the art style is adorable. Perhaps something could have been done to add onto the current gameplay (stacking map squares together?) so the puzzles could be more complex without feeling lengthy, but it's still a nice game to play if you enjoy cute games with puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute, little, creative puzzler. It's about a 5-hour long story that continues to find ways to change up the puzzle while keeping the basis the same. However, there's not really anything else that makes this game stand out. The story is okay and the game can be bland if you dislike reading conversations.I would pass on this game if you're getting it at full price. But at a discount, if you like the art style, you like games for short stories, and you like simple relaxing puzzles, then this game could be for you.My rating: 5.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game. Smart, cute, touching and imaginative. Good puzzles that require you to pay attention to subtle hints and experiment with the game mechanics. Colourful cast of characters and genuinely good humour. This game is full of funny, touching and surprising moments. A joy from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, cute, light little adventure game with a wholesome story of friendship and exploration, some unique puzzle mechanics, and good vibes all around. Some puzzles that were a bit unclear, but nothing I wasn't eventually able to brute force through. Overall, very pleasant 6 hour journey, would recommend for people who enjoy single-playthrough, light adventure games.
