_childDocuments_.review: Game was pretty fun and had some good puzzles, but the save feature kinda sucked. When you try to save it tells you that it'll only save to your last check point, but I had no idea what the check points were so I just left it open between play sessions. It probably took me 7-8 total hours to play through, not the 47 that Steam captured because I didn't close the game until I finished it
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This game is somehow *even more adorable* than you'd think from the art alone, because the writing complements the art -- they're both simple on the surface, but so well done the whole is seamless and immersive (and often funny). It's also tricksy! Part of the challenge is that the game leaves you to figure out the rules and goals. A mixture of point and click adventure, brain-breaking jigsaw puzzle, and clue-solving.That last part can get frustrating, but there are walkthroughs if the frustration's too much. But! The satisfaction of figuring out a part without the walkthrough is so lovely.I only wish there was more! (And maybe that I hadn't looked at walkthroughs so it would have taken longer!)

_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: What an experience, perfect length for what it offers. It feels like you're actually exploring the world, finding new places, and meeting new faces. Puzzles are clever and use new mechanic each chapter. Secrets are there if you're into that kind of thing. Overall a very enjoyable, wholesome experience.

_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredibly genius and innovated game. I didn't think I would enjoy this game as much as I did for this price. Some how I managed to send ten hours of my life in this game to 100% it and I do not regret it. Its an adorable story paired with such fascinating puzzles that genuinely PUZZLED me! _childDocuments_.review: A sweet little game with puzzles that are just challenging enough to be fun. I would definitely pick this up for a fun relaxing time, would've been perfect during quarantine. _childDocuments_.review: The whole game is a solid 9/10. Simple straight forward gameplay to bring out the story with no excess unnecessary fillers.Can't really comment price-wise as it was included in a humble bundle, but it is quick and simple fun game that takes 4-6 hours to finish. would definitely recommend to pick this up if the price is within your range or on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes a small premise and makes it such a wholesome, world building, intriguing, game. _childDocuments_.review: Strongly recommend this game! The visuals and animations are amazing. The map puzzles went from easy to pretty challenging near the end but that's the fun in this game. Though I must say I used some help from walk-through guides for the second half of the game, otherwise I would be stuck there for hours. The game mechanic was interesting and I love how clues are hidden in conversations and animation. You get little surprises here and there. The relaxing music is great for when you want some game time by yourself. Definitely use help/guides if needed, don't get stressed over it.The only complaint I have is about checkpoints. Some checkpoints are so spaced out that I felt like I had to redo quite a bit if I quit. I had many hidden achievements that weren't done in the first run of completing the game. As the chapter select only lets you pick certain chapters and not specific points in the chapter, it was time consuming to complete some achievements because they were near the end of the chapter.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about Carto is adorable. From the hand-painted characters and scenery, to the cut-scenes, hell, even the way Carto communicates through smileys and gestures is cute. The basic concept of the game is ingenious and very well executed: help young Carto reunite with her grandmother by moving pieces of the map to gain access to new areas - and new map pieces!I found Carto to be a short yet very loveable gaming experience.The graphics are very simple and you can see the sprites repeated on the map (for sand dunes, trees or hills). Nevertheless, I think the game looks stunning. The map you create when playing is absolutely seamless and moving through it is quick and fun. The size of a map tile is also conveniently the same width as my screen, although it might be different for people playing with a resolution under 1920 x 1080 pixels.The art style is delightful. Everything looks like it is straight from a children’s book. In fact, I think if you capture the screen in pretty much any situation the resulting image would do well in a picture book. The characters’ design, the environment, even the sounds and music put the player inside a pretty story book. Heartfelt congratulations are in order to Sunhead Games’ artist and art director, Kuan Hung Chen.The music is light, bubbly, airy. Most of the time in video games, as in movies, music is used either to convey a message, help with scene transition or guide the player (or viewer) to a particular emotion. I found there was little of that in Carto. The music is simply part of the world, so natural that you notice it more when it is gone than when it is audible. You can also hear the fact that it’s a children’s story through its notes. I think it’s quite the feat achieved by Eddie Yu, the composer.Game mechanics form another area where the game really shines. The main character can only move and interact with objects and characters. Her incredible power, though, is to manipulate the game’s map by moving, switching or rotating map tiles. Most tiles are 1 x 1 squares but later on they become more complex.Interactions with some game elements serve to help complete puzzles. Reading a book, for example, or activating a volcano (!!). Other interactions also include speaking with characters but more often than not this is not necessary to resolve puzzles.The genius here is that the map mechanic creates all kinds of possibilities for puzzles. You can move tiles until they are in the correct position, create an empty space where another tile is automatically created, create shapes using some of the tiles, etc. There is a lot of moving around but because you can move the tile where you’re currently located it’s possible to warp Carto very close to where she needs to go without having to walk the whole way there.If you want to spend a few relaxing hours solving puzzles, bathing in the world of a cute picture book, meeting quirky lovable characters all while using some innovative game mechanics, Carto is for you.The relaxing and soothing gameplay. There is no real urgency in the game and everything is so beautiful that playing it always brought a smile to my face. Also, it’s lovely!The burden of moving map tiles around and trying to find the matching one to solve a particular puzzle. While arranging tiles you have to ensure that each tile’s border is next to another tile of the same type. This can mean a slow, painful process when moving several tiles around, as it’s impossible to just remove tiles from the map.Yes, when it’s on sale. I think the price tag is a bit overpriced for the number of hours of play. Note that this game seems like excellent fit for a young child. At the time of writing, you can also play Carto on Xbox Game Pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A unique puzzle game that allows you to rotate, move, and connect pieces of a map, changing the very world around you. Carto was a lot longer than I had anticipated, but it never felt like it overstayed its welcome – with each location and puzzle feeling different, and every character flaunting their differences. The visuals are cute, the music is relaxing, and while first and foremost a casual game, Carto’s puzzles can be quite challenging. You’ll know if this is your kind of game. No real criticisms. Pick up on sale if the price point feels a bit much for a 5-7 hour experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just beautiful, relaxing, hard and fun. It's a wonderful adventure puzzle game with great graphics, beautiful story, little secrets and great mechanics. I can definitely recommend this game. The only drawback is the price - which is absolutely fine for an indie studio - as the game itself is played through quite quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: An unbelievably cute game.  Carto is definitely one of the more heartwarming, cute games I've played, and I really relished it.  It has a great little story, well done animations, unforgettable characters, and a pretty interesting game mechanic.  I saw some other (negative) reviews say that it wasn't so much a puzzle game, and I do somewhat agree - a lot of the "puzzles" are more like riddles.  It's also a bit short, and maybe not super challenging.  But all is worth the uneniable cuteness and warmth of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I ended up enjoying this more than I thought I would. In a sea of re-releases, remakes, "remasters", and games just aping any aspect of Dark Souls, it is refreshing to experience something with gameplay that I can say is original.Almost all the other reviews have talked about Carto's charming artstyle so I don't have anything to add to that.At 5-6 hours of playtime it can be comfortably completed in one session without overstaying its welcome, if it was any longer I probably would feel that it did.I would recommend this to anyone who enjoys any kind of puzzle or exploration type of game, or to anyone just looking for something original.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto starts off fine. Combining map pieces to create islands feels satisfying and promising for the rest of the game. But then it goes downhill. The game gets slow and the map-making mechanic is not as interesting as the trailer might seem to suggest.Do not play this if you...- ... do not particularly like games that try hard to be cute with zero content;- ... expect challenging puzzles;- ... think that any game deserves fitting music and sound effects;- ... think game mechanics should be consistent (so not like in Carto where in one puzzle, spinning a tile creates a tornado, but in another puzzle, tile orientation does not affect wind direction).Oh yes, spoiler: You have to kill a bird by roasting it alive. And then eat as much bird meat as possible (see store trailer and screenshots). That is messed up for a game that is supposed to be 'wholesome' and 'cute'. It felt really out of place and made me feel uneasy.Maybe Carto is suited for children until 10 years old, except for the bird torturing part.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a charming little indie game with an art style that I absolutely adores & a cute story that puts a smile on my face. This puzzle game revolves around a very unique tile-swapping mechanic: think Carcassonne but in a puzzle game format, plus 300% more adorableness lol. The puzzle is also constantly evolving as you progress, becoming ever more slightly harder to decipher, yet always intuitive & reachable esp with the hints provided. The game is also longer than I expected: I am five hours in so far & by the look of the achievements I unlocked, there are at least three more chapters to go. Just the right amount of length imo for a game like this.This gem is very much worth a try if you are looking for a relaxing lil game to enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a charming and beautiful game made by Taiwanese indie company (respect!).It is an excellent puzzle game!It offers unique perspective to solving the puzzles, similar to games such as Hue, GOROGOA, Monument Valley, Framed and Old Man's Journey.It is a fairly short game (~5hrs), with some relaxing puzzles and some that require having a brain.Once again, I left game running over the night ffs.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: The story, art, and music. are all totally adorable. Being able to manipulate the map and change the world is a super cool mechanic. The puzzles were very much on the simple side, but maybe I'm just not in the target age group. I did enjoy the game a lot; I just wish it was longer and continued building on the more complicated constraints introduced in the later chapters.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little game! Not too long, even when getting the secret extra stuff. There is a lot of quality packed into every minute though, so I was happy to play the game for $10. Game is fairly easy, but still makes you think. Also has a great atmosphere from the art/music/characters, but I personally didn't care too much about that.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A cute little puzzle game using map changing gameplay to go through 10 chapters through a few different areas. Puzzles aren't terribly difficult, but can challenge occasionally. Talking to NPCs can help guide you if you're stumped, but I often found myself especially towards the end of the game having puzzles already solved. Let it be known, while I wasn't playing terribly quickly and I was reading all the text the game only took 4 hours, and so some may find the short length not worth the price of admission. There is a meta puzzle designed to encourage replay-ability, but it's 6 random puzzles in each of the themed zones. Completing the game unlocks the ability to replay specific chapters to encourage searching for these. As of the time of review I have not completed this (I did unlock 2 of the 6 during my normal playthrough), so I may return to complete it.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is an interesting game (Thank you to Cas for gifting me this game!). On first glance it seems like a puzzle game, but it's not, not really. It has , but it's not a puzzle game, paradoxically. (I would argue the community 'Puzzle' tag is wrong - but I'm probably more strict about the use of that word)Puzzle games are mechanic-focused, like Portal, like Braid, like Baba Is You, like Antichamber. In these games, as the game progresses you get more mechanics, or your understanding of them does, or the mechanics update, or the complexity of the puzzles increase.In Carto, at first you're dropped into a level with mechanics, and that'll make you think: ah, they're going to add more and more variations of the mechanics. But not really; there's a few levels with variations but most of the times the puzzles aren't figuring out how to interact with the mechanics, it's about understanding the language of the game. It is, like the page itself says, an , and most of the puzzles you do are about interpreting some form of language.So, if you go in with the hope of finding a thinky puzzler (as the Baba is You/Steven's Sausage Roll/etc genre is awkwardly called) combined with an adventure game (like The Witness, but more adventury), you might be mildly disappointed (I was, at first). But if you instead change your interpretation to purely an adventure game with different mechanics, the game is still interesting in a very different way.That's because there's still the mechanic of the game, the way you change up the landscape to progress. This completely changes the feel of the places you visit. There's no real permanence to the structure of the landscape fundamentally. It's an adventure game where two places are arbitrarily close, which makes it really weird in a way. In some sense, I felt like I visited the places, but in some sense it felt like these places weren't places at all. Just claustrophobic tiles sliding around on a grid. The mechanics caused the places to not really be places, even if they are memorable.Still, I think there's quite enough to be enjoyed here. The story is cute, the art is cute, the characters are cute, the puzzles are mostly interesting (if you like adventure-style puzzles). There's also a few secrets apparently, if you're interested in that (I don't think these puzzles are any more  though). It's worth checking out if you're into cute adventure games.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Nice, calm, decently paced storybook; the puzzles are barely that, but the interactivity is good nonetheless. The characters are all varied and overall pleasant, and aside from a specific animal related section, Carto is a great combat free adventure to unwind with. Some of the movements could be a little quicker, as well as the conversations, but overall it never reaches the point of being tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Shorter days giving you the blues? Cold weather got you down? You could try exercising, getting medication, going to therapy....or you could just play Carto* ;) This game is basically digital sunshine. The characters are adorable, the puzzles are clever (and only sometimes maddening), and the core mechanic is unique enough that you probably haven't played anything like it. There's also a lot of content, so if you enjoy head-scratching puzzles and characters that make you wanna squeeze their little cheeks, this is well-worth the $20.My only gripe is the controls. You play the game entirely by keyboard, and while most of the time this works great, it makes manipulating the map tiles kind of a pain. Especially towards the end of chapters where your map has a lot of pieces, it would be really nice to be able to select and drag them with a cursor instead of constant WASD smashing.  * Ok, ok, maybe do those things aaaaand play Carto.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the visual style. However, I found the gameplay to be sort of tedious and shallow beyond the initial fun of reorganizing the map tiles. I also thought a lot of the dialog and story was trying too hard to be cute and witty, but mostly just felt like a knock-off Zelda - with even less subtlety.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I admire the atmosphere and puzzles, so chill and challenging. This game gives a different thought to use the mechanic of jigsaw puzzles, but the combing of jigsaw pieces have different meaning, reminds me a little of Carcassonne, but quite different in many ways, love how you use your mechanic to do it, makes the game solid, and also humorous.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: It's such a cute and charming game and all the characters are so adorable. The puzzles require the right amount of thinking to still be considered a chill game and it doesn't get frustrating because the graphics and the music calms you down. The achievements aren't hard to complete too and if you missed some, it's easy to come back. I'll wait a few more months until I forget about it completely then play it all over again.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. It wasn't very long, but I did enjoy the story a lot. If you're looking for a calm puzzle game then I highly recommend this one. Things don't get crazy tough, but that's what I was looking for in this game.PS. the snowman is more than just a head and body. find the stick arms and hat! I'm not a huge fan of playing through a whole level again to try and get an achievement, so I figured I'd let you know before jumping in
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A warm hearted game which starts with a little girl getting separated from her grandma by a storm. You find yourself playing the little girl who landed on an unfamiliar village with the aim of finding a way to reunite with your grandma. Along the way, you will also help the villagers solve their problems. The gameplay consists of placing pieces of tiles, while making sure the tiles match each other over their roads, terrains, and borders, which will create new paths for you to explore and progress in the story. You can rotate and rearrange them any way you see fit. In essence, like a jigsaw puzzle. Initially they are simple square tiles but later different shapes and more variety of terrains are added. One part involves stacking the correct arrangement of rooms and floors in a building to progress. There are also other simple puzzles and exploration to do to reveal clues on how and where to go next. The graphics are simple but the background music is soothing and matches the gameplay perfectly. I was able to complete the game in 6 hours, after which you can replay individual chapters in case you miss out on some achievements. Despite the short duration of gameplay, the entertainment and fun in going on this adventure of a game will definitely stick with you much longer than most other games out there. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute and charming game. Lovely art direction, and the sound design reminds me of classic Animal Crossing. Puzzles are good. Plenty of Aha! moments without being too obtuse. The only part I got stuck on was  The game did a great job of exploring the possibilities of the map-moving mechanic without overstaying its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous, cute little puzzle game! The hand painted style is beautiful and works well with the storybook themes and living map world. It's nice when every part of the game fits together so well, especially nice since the game is literally about fitting things together!The target audience is obviously children and the difficulty shows. Most of the puzzles are very easy, only a few near the last chapter were ever much of a challenge. Still, even being easy I still had fun fitting the pieces together and seeing the consequences play out. Some harder extra bonus levels would have been welcome.The story is basic children's storybook fare. Coming of age in the sense of just going out into the world. It gets the job done and is always pleasant.The game is short in the good "does what it needs to" sort of way. There is no padding of extra puzzles, or boring steps to complete. New ideas are introduced in each chapter and played with a bit till you get them and then you move on. I really, really appreciate a game that respects my time. My only complaint is that I would have liked a little more story stuff, a few characters are fun and I wanted more of them. Which honestly is a good complaint to have.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cute and peaceful. Its a very light casual puzzler. I walked through level after level rarely getting stuck, but I felt no sense of achievement with any of the puzzles, as the logic itself takes some leaps so I felt like I stumbled on the solution. The mechanic gets quite boring after a while. If you want to switch your mind of completely this is a good game. Otherwise pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Cute. The puzzles are not that bad, even tho I got stuck on two of the easiest ones because I thought the solution was more complicated than it actually was.A couple things. If a sequel were to be made, a border or grid would make the map assembling and rearranging a bit more difficult or challenging. Especially with the snow chapter. I used to have several physical puzzles very similar to how the map worked.If there were more varying map piece shapes that would also be incredibly interesting like triangles. Overall a very cute and entertaining game.  Short, but it was still fun for what it was worth. a solid 4/5 if not greater.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute art, but the gameplay quickly wears thin. Once the initial novelty of the map piece moving mechanic wears off, puzzles reveal themselves to be either insultingly easy, unnecessarily frustrating, or simply tedious. Horrifyingly, one of the puzzles requires you to torture a bird multiple times, moving map pieces in order to progressively burn it to death--and then forces you to click through the motions of eating it!Dialogue is cutesy but harder to skip than it should be, and moments that are supposed to be moving just fall flat. The multiple unskippable cut scenes during the credits is unforgivable.Finally, for a game with so many locales and characters blatantly drawing on various indigenous peoples (such as the Inuit and Pacific Islanders), there sure are a lot of white-presenting character models! I can't recommend this game to anyone, even children.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful artwork and an excellent idea for the whole "shift the map" thing. Love how the plot leads you back to where you've been and see how your previous acts developed in that piece of land. Ordinary but heart-warming story and characters are full of personality. Wish there were more side quests. Still, the gaming difficulty is just enough to feel engaged but not discouraging.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a charming and delightful game that takes the player on a whimsical journey through a magical world. The game puts you in the shoes of a young girl named Carto, who finds herself lost in a strange world and must use her map-making skills to navigate her way through a variety of puzzles and challenges.The gameplay in Carto revolves around using Carto's map-making abilities to manipulate the world around her. By rearranging the map pieces, you can create new pathways, unlock secrets, and discover hidden treasures. The puzzles are clever and engaging, and the game offers a good mix of challenge and accessibility.The graphics in Carto are beautiful and whimsical, with a hand-drawn style that is both charming and evocative. The world is full of vibrant colors and interesting characters, and the game's visuals help to create a sense of wonder and exploration.One downside of Carto is that it can be quite short, with only a few hours of gameplay. However, the game makes up for this by offering a very polished and well-crafted experience, with a satisfying story and plenty of memorable moments.Overall, Carto is an excellent game that is sure to delight players of all ages. With its charming visuals, engaging puzzles, and memorable characters, it offers a unique and enjoyable experience that is well worth your time.Gameplay: ★★★★★★★★☆☆ 8/10Market: ★★★★★★☆☆☆☆ 5/10Social: ★★★★★★★☆☆☆ 7/10Narrative: ★★★★★★★☆☆☆ 7/10Graphics: ★★★★★★★★★★ 10/10Technical: ★★★★★★★★☆☆ 8/10Value: ★★★★★★☆☆☆☆ 5/10Audio: ★★★★★★☆☆☆☆ 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10It is a cute puzzle game with unique design. I love the story, art design, and many little details, especially how the two girls travelling together, and the puppies in the end. More compliments see other people's reviews, and I agree with them.Downside is that the game is too short for the pricing, also not challenging.Another of the criticism (and it is a very annoying design of the game) is that you can't go back to the previous maps once you finish chapter 10. Unless I missed some important buttons, but if I didn't, then this: if you want full achievement, you will have to do it ALL OVER AGAIN. I think it is pointless to punish players for finishing the game too quickly. I missed a few puzzles (I just assumed they will unlock more clues when the game is beat - but it is not the case). I do want to go for full achievement but having to go over again is just annoying.Overall somewhat enjoyable if you don't care about full achievement, or didn't proceed to end the final chapter too early. ----------Update: hidden achievement design is awful. I read all the books twice (uugh) including the little one in the lobby and  didnt get the achievement. Gave up.

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a simplistic indie puzzle game about assembling a map to navigate through areas. You play as Carto, a cute little girl who has the ability to rearrange the world by rearranging pieces of her map. You can move them around and rotate them, and you must do so in order to make the edges match up.The core of the game is going around a series of areas, talking to NPCs, solving their problems or following their hints to rearrange the map so as to unlock new map pieces, and then continuing on. This can be about rearranging things to put various pieces next to each other, creating patterns on the map, putting one piece in a position relative to another, or chaining together pieces in order to keep moving in a direction (going west, for instance, or making the wind blow in a way that you can move along through a piece instead of it blowing you off to the side).Sadly, while the game tries to mix this up in a few ways – as you get to later areas of the game, you start getting into things like two-layer maps or tetromino pieces – in the end, it doesn’t actually end up being enough. The game doesn’t really have all that many tricks, so by a couple hours into it, you’re kind of out of new things to see, and the game never really manages to do anything all that clever.I was left with the feeling that the game was mildly cute, but I didn’t really feel like it was ultimately all that fulfilling – it wasn’t BAD, it was just kind of mediocre. It is all faintly cutesy, but the puzzles felt too simple for me to feel clever for solving them.At four hours in length, this game doesn’t eat up vast quantities of your time, but it left me with a feeling a lot of indie games give me – it was a cute idea, but it ended up being a shallower concept than it seemed like it should be, and was ultimately lacking in overly clever gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I have a single complaint about this one but it's such a obvious and glaring thing that I have to say it: why on Earth can I not change the control scheme?  There seem to be no options for that anywhere and it's legitimately frustrating because I'm left handed and vastly prefer WASD to arrow keys for movement.Other than this one big thing, it's a great game. Charming look, clever conceit, interesting puzzles. Good stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Easy-going puzzle game in which you can change the world around you by rearranging tiles on a map. This clever mechanic is used in many different creative ways throughout the game. Each new world adds its own twist so it never gets boring. The game took me about 5 hours to complete and it never became really difficult, but I caught myself thinking "aaahh that's clever!" quite a few times along the way. Also, the art style is cute, and the dialog is pretty funny without trying too hard. Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This game excels in a few spots. Art Style is absolutely phenomenal. Story is good. Music is great. It's easy to figure out the mechanics and for the most part the puzzles are quite well thought out. However you never get a great deal of satisfaction from solving a puzzle outside of progressing the game, and the excitement doesn't really build at all. That said it was enjoyable, and the art really delivered for this title. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I actually quite enjoyed this game. It's fairly simple and a nice cozy, relaxing game (if that is your preferred genre like me) when you want something not fast paced. My only issue with this game is it's way too short. I was hoping for longer game play, but I'd still recommend this game because I found it amusing and the artwork interesting and different. It's slightly overpriced considering how short the game is, so maybe wait until it goes on sale?
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Neutral review.Game itself is good, but the music is just plain bad (I don't think the composer deliberately did repetitive music to somewhat fit the mood; I think the composer was just plain bad at making music lmao)And what I truly disliked is the text speed is too slow with no way of making it faster. In a story focused game, these two points are quite a big deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute, relaxing puzzle game. It explores its one puzzle mechanic for exactly the right amount of time and has just enough secrets to feel satisfying getting that 100% complete. (Unlocking a chapter select after game complete, and having secrets unlocked globally, are both very good choices, many brownie points to the developers.)
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a cute little story, has a lovely art style, and nice sound track, but the "game" part is pretty light. The puzzles are very simple, and the whole thing is completely devoid of any real decision making. For the first 4 chapters or so I honestly just found myself wondering when I was going to get to play "the game part" because all of the things it had you do were painfully straightforward. I'm leaving a positive rating for the game because it isn't a bad experience, it isn't a bad thing, I enjoyed the back 70%, but its a thing, and doesn't so much feel like a game - more an interactive story/movie/thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Carto. It was a simple and soothing strategy game with a unique mechanic that was fun to figure out. The story was really cute and I had a lot of fun progressing through the chapters. I would recommend this to anybody who likes puzzle games. I look forward to any other games Sunhead Games might develop.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10. Cozy and charming puzzle game that is perfect for handheld gaming. An overall solid production with a clear and consistent art direction. Its cute graphics; animations; sound effects; music and writing all come together to create a believable world for Carto. The game is fairly successful in exploring the jigsaw puzzle genre, and delivered a refreshing and unique take on it. New mechanics are introduced chapter by chapter, ramping up its complexity in a pleasant and gradual manner while keeping the gameplay fresh. All but one particular puzzle were intuitive and fun to figure out on my own.Docking a point for a couple of minor nitpicks. Right off the bat, a non-configurable dialogue speed gets annoying pretty quickly especially if you're a quick reader. Next, managing puzzle pieces was unnecessarily painful. When playing jigsaw puzzles, a natural tendency is to place a non-fitting piece nearby. You can't do this in Carto because the game does not allow pieces to be placed in an invalid position, which is fair. But it also means if you moved a piece from the edge of your canvas and realised it didn't fit, you'll now have to move it all the way back, . That's painful, and it gets worse the more pieces there are on the canvas.  Finally, I'm docking a full point for unskippable credits (twice), which is inexcusable in this day and age.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Its a great and cozy puzzle game, not to hard, though I didt get stuck at times.the fact you can edit the control is great.only thing a bit challenging for acesability is that the end scene fo not let you pause the text, and the bubles change very fast so I missed a bit about the details of the ending of the story.I enjoyed that I could relax and didnt have enamies but all the time in the world.do try the demo to check if you like it, thouge dont think the controls can be changed there.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Easy recommendation. I first played this on PS4 last year, and liked it enough to buy it again recently just to experience it again. Its a wonderfully charming puzzler, with no pressure like time limits or anything to detract from the puzzles themselves. The cartography stuff is a brilliant mechanic thats really fun to wrap your head around. Id really like to see where a possible sequel could expand on the idea
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly cute and whimsical little adventure game with a novel approach to puzzle together a world from map pieces.Maybe a tad short for the price, but I enjoyed it more than other games that tried to artificially stretch their playtime with unnecessary and meaningless tasks.This game is pretty condensed, you can play it in one sitting without getting bored.Solid recommendation!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: ★★☆☆☆ - 2 out of 5 StarsI have tried and tried to get into Carto. I loved the demo when I played it, but after playing 13 hours, I've given up. Not because it was too hard or the gameplay wasn't good, but because it was so boring. I thought I would love this game - I love maps and am good at reading them. But I struggled so hard to remain interested in this game and the story and puzzles. I rarely don't finish games, even if I don't like them, (I hate leaving things unfinished), but I am one or two chapters away from being done with Carto and I'm so bored, I can't bring myself to do it.The puzzles are not great. A lot of them, you have to basically move around the map pieces until you accidentally get something correct. You're basically guessing rather than figuring it out, with little to guide you. The fishing part I just did was enough for me to say, "OK, I'm done here." It was incredibly tedious.I don't see myself coming back to this in the future. Try it out if you like puzzles and cute graphics! Maybe you'll do better than I!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Great, cute, short map puzzle game!For such a short story, the characters are well thought out and there are lots of cute and/or funny moments.The mechanic is simple but there are lots of different ways it's used. There are a couple of not so intuitive bits, but overall, great use of the map pieces.If you like puzzle game, I would absolutely recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Received in the August 2021 Humble Bundle. I make maps for part of my job, so anything cartographic intrigues me. Initially, I got a black screen when starting up the game. I could hear music or sound effects, but saw nothing. I had to CTRL-ALT-DELETE out of the game. While the developers provide some fairly generic advice on how to make the game work, it seemed a bit perfunctory and minimally sufficient.When I relaunched the game from the game's store page, it worked. The art is charming. The music is cute. The story is charming. However, the gam eplay did not hold my attention for very long. It struck me as more appropriate for a console game than a PC game.I'm giving this a thumbs down.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A quaint little puzzle game.Whilst it was a tad linear (there could have been a deeper 'exploration puzzle' element, perhaps tying together two or more of the different areas), I played the whole game in one sitting (it's not 10 hours long, I spent a while AFK). The average player will get not much more than 6-8 hours out of this game, and this relatively short length works well to make Carto a short-but-sweet afternoon-filler.4/5 for gameplay, 6/5 for the adorable story.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto has a cute main character, a soft graphical style which really suits it, and a good puzzle mechanic - shifting and/or rotating map pieces to open up pathways, create particular patterns, or directly trigger a required action. Although it is pretty clear what needs to be done for most of the story puzzles or optional achievements, a few have descriptions or instructions which seemed too vague to me, so I resorted to trial and error, and in one case to a helpful guide. I admit that I did sigh when I saw that the old & lazy standby "Towers of Hanoi" mechanic was used for a linked trio of puzzles, but there was partial redemption for the game in the novel solution for one of these. Overall, though, I enjoyed the game, and I thought it was good value for its sale (as opposed to full) price.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful game, with a wholesome vibe, cute and funny characters, sweet artstyle and a gameplay slightly focusing on cartography.The puzzles are really intelligently made, with the clues really helpful and somewhat straightforward. Some areas were a bit tough to crack, by close observation on the puzzle pieces and its orientations did the trick.The characters in this game are really very cute and sweet. Belonging to very different backgrounds, every characters have a personality on their own, and all of them are very cheerful and supportive towards the protagonist, carto. Finishing this game gave me a really wholesome experience and a sense of positive and cheerful vibe. Indie games like these reminds me why i love games so much and want even more people to join in the experience of a small but really beautifully made artform like Carto. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A solid and enjoyable experience for all ages. On the short side, with a medium-to-easy difficulty level, but very fun with charming aesthetics and a well thought out, well developed puzzle mechanic that is put through several original iterations. Despite being about maps, its not an exploration game - this is a straightforward puzzle adventure. Like most puzzle adventure titles, it won't have a lot of replay value, but it's a great example of how indie developers in the genre are pulling off truly unique ideas with a lot of style and polish.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun little game, with a truly unique puzzle mechanic: you break away parts of the map and put them back together to create new paths, reach areas you could not get to otherwise, or solve different area-related puzzles.Pair this with a cute artstyle, adoreable characters and great music (which dynamically adapts based on your progress) and you can see the love that went into making this game.If you want to take a break from more stressful, action-packed games and play a charming game with a refreshing twist on the puzzle mechanic, definitely check out this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most heartwarming game I've ever played. : ) Cute and beautiful art style, delicate sound design and music, and a humorous but touching story. If you are interested in any above aspects, this game is for you. Secrets / achievements aside, I think you should be able to finish it 5 ~ 6 hours. Not to say the puzzle mechanics don't play an important part or don't pose a challenge; having played this game at various showcases in the past I did have a higher anticipation on the what kinds of mind-bending mechanics down the line will stem from the map swapping and stitching premise - but in the end it doesn't really matter. The puzzles are part of its narrative tool, not to make you pull your hair out! If you can clear out an afternoon and or an evening, just sit down and play the game (even better, with your family) and enjoy the short trek into Carto's world, it will be time well spent. : )
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a little bit to get into Carto, because I approached it as a puzzle game. It has some puzzles, but nothing that you won't solve right away.Once I realised this was a fun, cute chillout game, I got on board for the ride and I really enjoyed the experience. There are a bunch of varied environments and funny characters. It's relaxing and enjoyable, and I spent quite a bit of time just rearranging my maps for my own amusement.The game is excellently put together and well-paced. Progress is steady, and there's no pressure to suggest you shouldn't be playing around when you want to. The main upgrade you get is move speed so you can run around faster, but you can often skip around quicker by moving the map pieces you're on anyway.The main thing I'd like to see near the end is the ability to conjure some extra pieces, just so I can play around with the final map layouts to my satisfaction!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, I have never seen a game with such an unique mechanic before. The graphics are beautifully hand-drawn, the animations are cute and amazing, and the game is really well polished. The atmosphere and soundtrack fits very well too.I will spoiler a part here, however, what I'm about to mark as spoiler can be seen on the trailers, it's just a small game feature, nothing story related. For instance, when I mentioned about the game being polished, one time Later in the game, the puzzles get very clever, but everything can be resolved with hints you can find throughout the game, nothing is impossible in this game. This is the good kind of puzzling, something that can be challenging but that tips are around the world, and nothing stretches out too far, I don't remember being any puzzles on late game that required me to know something at the very start of the game, for instance.I did, however, thought that the later part of the game got a little bit too quick, or in other words, rushed (not in the meaning that it wasn't polished, it was really well polished, it just ended quickly). You can explore (spoiler related to how story progresses in the game, but not about the story itself)  ended somewhat quickly. However, this was balanced with more complex puzzling, I guess I got how the game mechanics worked and didn't had much trouble with later puzzling, which made the end of the game a little bit faster. That does not mean the puzzles were easy, no no, they were pretty clever.It has been a little while I have felt so much love with a game. Everything on this game is amazing. The artstyle, the story, how the characters and story unfold, everything on this game was a great experience. If you are still unsure, you can always try the demo yourself. I wasn't sure about the game when I saw in the Store, I tried the demo, and I absolutely loved it, which led me to purchase it.An absolute gem and unique experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: this game is absolutely INCREDIBLE. the artwork is gorgeous, the story line is gripping, and the puzzle mechanism itself allows for so much variety & creativity. i spent days playing this when i should have been studying, and i would do it again in a heartbeat. without a single doubt one of the best games i've encountered in my life.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a charming (if short) puzzle game. You play as Carto, a young girl with the ability to change the landscape by rearranging and rotating bits of the map, which you do to solve puzzles and progress through the story. The art style is nice. The puzzles are intuitive yet still occasionally challenging to figure out. And the game is pretty short. I beat it in a few hours. So pick it up on sale if you can.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing puzzle game, I stayed up all night and finished it the second I bought it. Snow level is frustrating towards the end but I'm proud I beat the entire thing without using a guide! Only needed to look up some hint to the final few achievements but it's worth it. Highly recommend for everyone, tell uncle Ganga I said hi! :smile:
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Played this all the way through with a couple friends to end off my birthday, and by GODS was this game good. I got tripped up on the ruins portion of the desert and that blasted ice puzzle in the arctic, but i had soooo much fun with this you have no idea. Its very sweet and cozy :) It was super rewarding to have those "ahHA!" moments when you finally piece something together. 10/10 will probably go back in to get anything i missed
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I love it! One of my favorite games of all time, truly! I enjoyed the relaxedness, the somewhat childish playfulness, the puzzle style, the puns, the art style, the story, the world building, the ethics and generally the difficulty level (but the difficulty was probably just me being dumb... :) ).The only real issues I had were that the sound effects were sometimes a little annoying, especially for when the text appears and the controls. Both of these would be solved with more customization options.Other than that, please make more, I love it!Btw: my most played games are games like Skyrim, Total War Rome 2, Total War Warhammer and Age of Empire 2. Hundreds of hours each. This is the first time I've taken the time to write a review. Make of that what you will.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little puzzle game. You move the maps around, it affects the world, and you solve puzzles with that main mechanic based on context from NPCs, like 'so and so lives to the east of this landmark', so you have to lay the landmark with a road facing east, connect a road to the east, and another spot appears beyond that with the new NPC's house. Cute art, calming music.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: CARTO is a lovely, relaxing puzzle game for all ages. My only concern is that it's too short, i took my time going through the 10 chapters but only lasted 8 hours, at an average of 1,5 hours per day, 5 days. If only it had a bit more content.... otherwise i recommend it to everyone when they're feeling like they need a cheer up/wind down.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A sweet medium length casual puzzle game.The graphics are adorable, the gameplay simple and fun and the music is quite nice as well.All in all it's a nice relaxing little game, no timed challenges or QTEs or anything like that.You can take your time to figure it out.The 'puzzles' aren't very difficult, but challenging enough to stay fun.There are a few you have to complete without all the pieces which I found a bit annoying, but never to the point that I felt like quitting.So if you're looking for a casual (simple) puzzle game with enough sweetness to develop cavities, I would recommend this one. It is a tad on the expensive side though, so be sure to get it on sale for at least 25% off.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 game, would recommend I personally loved many different aspects of the game, the way that the story was very hands-off and lets the player figure it out on their own was very enjoyable. I loved the art style of the game and during cutscenes, as well as the diverse character designs and environment designs. I think it was a very creative direction to not give Carto much dialogue and I loved how they expressed much of their emotions through emoticons :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Charming puzzle game with a good gimmick, but also boring and frustrating.---This is a very tentative recommendation. The game got a good gimmick and premise. It's charming. I loved the demo. But the story, characters, locations, and dialogue aren't very interesting. It's a lot of pretty dull reading.The game gets pretty frustrating at times, due to either vague directions or fiddly map manipulations with a lot of trial and error, popping in and out of the map and or inventory. I got frustrated and turned to a walkthrough a number of times.Short as it is, the game still drags on. It needed to be trimmed down or fleshed out more. A number of puzzles needed clarification or streamlining. The whole game feels like it needed another couple passes. But I did power through and the ending enough to inch it into the recommend column.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man, I'm literally in happy tears writing this. I just finished the game and although it was short (it takes about 9 hours to finish the entire game), it was one of the best puzzle games I've ever played.  Adorable characters, heartwarming story, and an entirely unique mapping system that I've never seen used before in any other game.  11/10 stars.  <3 <3 <3 <3
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Simple and poetic casual puzzle game. Really relaxing, I just had a few moments when I couldn't for the life of me guess what I had to do, but they were minor disturbances in a globally charming experience. I would highly recommend. Took me 5 hours to complete the story. Maybe It would take just a little bit more to go through the chapters where I couldn't find the secrets.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an absolute delight!  The characters and jokes were great and the graphics were lovely.  The gameplay was so fun and such a unique concept.  Each chapter presented new and different challenges without the map building and swapping dynamic feeling samey and repetitive.  I absolutely loved it and finished it in two short sittings.  Definitely try this out of you enjoy puzzles!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a game I got through Humble Choice. At first it might not look like much, but it's actually a very charming puzzle game. Its main mechanic of a map in form of squares that you can rearrange is an amazing idea and was also well executed. Besides that you're gonna meet many different characters and here and then play some other minigames as well. I think it would be even more amazing if this game would build upon this mechanic and add another layer of gameplay on top of it such as fighting enemies or something. But I get it that maybe they wanted to really focus on this one feature instead.Nevertheless, I gotta admit that it gets boring if you don't take breaks after every hour or so. Maybe due to the slow movement speed or the generally calm atmosphere and the music that just keeps looping depending on the level so I'd recommend not trying to finish it in one session and instead take your time with it.It took me around 8 hours and there was one puzzle near the end where I got extremely stuck, so I can imagine that other people could finish it in 6 or 7 hours. I think that's still a good length and besides that there are also some secrets that want to be found.Overall, I'd recommend Carto if you like to turn on your brain at times. The main mechanic is definitely the star here, but the cute characters and world also add to it which overall makes for an pleasant experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A short, sweet, super-fun puzzle game about a girl finding her way back to her granny using her cartography skills. Gameplay revolves around a unique mapping mechanic that, while simple, progresses in a way that keeps each puzzle fresh and twisty (and occasionally headache-inducing, but that's probably just me. Still worth it!). Characters and dialogue are memorable, graphics are cute and wholesome. If you enjoy puzzle games, this one's a doozy.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: The story is really amazing. The graphics and character design are incredibly cute. Though I hope there will be Vietnamese as an option in the language settings since my English isn't very good, but it doesn’t affect my enjoyment of the game. The puzzles in the game are truly challenging enough to never be boring. I really love this game
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I finished Carto yesterday, and I have yet to stop thinking about it.Its just... so nice that there are games where there's no Big Bad Evil that needs to be fought, nothing needs to be killed, no horrors or GRITTY REALITY- they have their place, sure. But there's so few games that are kind of just... antagonist-less games?You're a small person whose curiosity mixed with a lack of understanding the full consequences sees you thrown adrift. You meet all these just... all-round nice, supportive, helpful people. And I think that is such an important message- no cynacism poisoning, no "but ACTUALLY" sudden twist- people helping each other.Different cultures, different traditions- everyone having their own little problems which you help in your own way. You make these connections, you bring everyone together- crossing generational boundaries just like you cross map boundaries between areas. Little trinkets you bring between people. Stories you can read.All of this told with a delightful bit of humour woven throughout the story. Even when you have some setbacks, they're never played up as something soul-crushing or causing our character despair- you or your friend are ready to keep walking forward. Determined.The internet, in many ways, has made the world small. We're all a few clicks away from the worst in the world, and it feels like most games and media seek to capitalize on that for shock value and 'being realistic'. But that starts to miss the point of games- an outlet to dream, to see what COULD BE POSSIBLE. Its not good to always wallow in clouds of negativity- I want to believe in my fellow peoples, that it IS possible for us to work together to build tomorrow better than the past we came from. Be curious. Be kind. Be good. We are all in this together.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely recommend this game. First impression was I wanted a beautiful chill game. But to my surprise the game was surprising challenging. The idea of the game making it look as a puzzle and playing through the challenges was interesting. Played with some friends discussed/argued all in good fun! All of us applaud at the end of each chapter when we manage to solve some puzzles very out of the box!. Love it! Try it! Added info- Play time probably less than 20-15 hours for me as a group- Can be challenging try to avoid googling will be more fun
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I tried the demo and instantly fell in love with this game. It's such a unique puzzle game, with lots of lovable characters, that I couldn't resist finishing the game in one go. This game is great for those who love a challenge, but it could also be easily enjoyed by any. The art style is wonderful and the music is breathtaking. I'm sure you'll enjoy it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed this a lot more than I expected to.The map tile rearranging mechanic that mean the changes you make to the map being reflected in the games world is a pretty original idea and I really liked how it ties into the puzzles you solve throughout the game.Although it relies on that one mechanic for most of the game the puzzles are varied enough to keep things interesting with each chapter offering a fresh take on it.While thats all pretty good on its own the visuals, soundtrack, quirky characters you meet and places you go is what really elevates this game from an ok game to really good game.I can easily recommend this game if it looks appealing to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: It was so amazingly cute and adorable! The art style is beautiful to look at! The puzzles aren't that difficult so you can take your time and look around the map areas. No frame rate issues, no audio issues, just no issues. I found literally no issues. 9/10. HIGHLY recommend!!! The game is super wholesome and lovely, too!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: You can expect to 100% the game within 7hours, definitely faster if you get the secret achievements in the first run. I had a great time playing Carto with it's inventive take on puzzles, often requiring me to look at a problem from a different perspective. If you like puzzles with a great soundtrack, great story and a great art style then this is worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely charming and beautiful game. I just downloaded it 30 minutes ago but I have to leave a review here. The perfect art style, music, dialogue and story you could ever ask for in a relaxing puzzle game about moving an rotating pieces of a map to progress the story. I absolutely adore this gem of a game. 10/10. Should you buy this on sale? NO! Pay full price for this gem of a game (I had to say it again) to support passionate devs like these. Mwaaaaah Chefs kiss!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely art style, a cosy little puzzle game for a few hours of relaxing fun. Story is a delight to experience for yourself or share with others - especially delightful with kids but by no means a child-only adventure. Nice amount of replayability unlocking secrets you might have missed on the first play through.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: The game was great. The game had a lot of nice even difficult puzzles. Some of the puzzles were in my opinion a bit illogical sometimes and needed some help from the internet. However, most of them were a lot of fun due to the unique game play.Despite the fact that I do not have a lot of negative feedback I would maybe buy the game when it is on a discount since it doesn't take that long to complete ~12h for me, and I watched a show while playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the most pleasant surprise I've had on a recommended list. The art is simple but aesthetic, the story is adorable and the game mechanics with puzzles is very chilled out to the usual games I play. You get exactly what is advertised in the video trailer for the game, and the demo is a lovely insight for what the game gives you. The story about a girl who is separated from her grandmother and adventures to reunite with her, yet finds herself helping other strangers out, hoping to unite with her grandmother in the convenient spots but just misses her. Eventually, it has a feel-good ending where you feel satisfied on completing the puzzles and uniting with the grandmother. I say the puzzles are simple, but you have to read every bit of dialogue and read it as instructions, or you will get confused, luckily there are YouYube videos online that can get you back on track if you ever get lost. I guess you could look at that as a negative, as it is a linear story, but that is how the story is, you go from 'A' to 'B,' not something new but the story and art make up for that in my opinion. A very simple story, yet it is very innocent, with no annoying characters blathering on, more of a cute and chirpy game than anything else.The only thing I would ask of the developers is for more of a story, there were 10 chapters to the story and I want more. If you want a chill game to sit down, drink a hot cuppa and go through a story, this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Already the end of the episode? The end of the game? I want more, this game is so relaxing. :(  What does the game want from me? I don't understand. Oh wait, I think I get it. (two seconds later) No, wait, I don't get it. WHAT DO YOU WANT FROM ME? (Another location) This makes no sense! (Another location) This is too much. And I can't leave?? Oh my god. Houston, we have a problem. This is too hard.  I know, right? Relaxing, my bum. I'm about to go FERAL. No logic whatsover. The beginning seems so easy & cute, but then it goes downhill REALLY fast. I was about to refund the game but I, unfortunately, bought a retail key (so no refund, I had to play it). My amount of time you see in the game is not because I loved it that much. It's because I was constantly stuck (and looked up solutions on youtube, often without exiting the game). Once you start to understand the logic of the puzzle, the rules change & do everything in its power to confuse you. It's like the developer wanted you to guess what the game wants from you. No proper clues. Add a price that I think is too much for this kind of 'puzzle' (when the puzzle, the main treat of the game, is horrendously bad) & I'm going mad. I'll try to get all the achievements in a while, but oh my god. I do NOT recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely puzzle game. It was challenging enough to be interesting but not so challenging that I gave up at any point. The game isn't terribly long, I had completed it to 100% in 7 hours, but I don't think this is a bad thing, I was engaged throughout and I didn't feel the game had outstayed it's welcome. Aesthetically the game is very nice, I really liked the art style and the music was calming leading to a very relaxed-feeling experience. The controls were good too once I had got used to moving with the arrow keys rather than WSAD (I think this can be changed in the settings).  TLDR: Lovely, relaxed-feeling puzzle game. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Charming exploration/puzzle game where, yes, confusing the map for the territory is the point. If moving Carcassonne tiles around to make shapes to solve puzzles and unlock new areas to explore sounds interesting, give this a try. If it doesn't, I don't know why you're reading what I'm writing anyway.At the time of this writing, runs acceptably in the "GloriousEggroll" custom Proton release on Linux.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game as a birthday present, and I am so happy about it.I've rarely seen something that cute, cozy and relaxing. The story has catched me a lot, and all the characters are so lovely. The puzzles require some thinking, yet they are not too hard. The art style is really cool. A perfect game for young and old ones who are willing to spend a few hours in a peaceful world. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Are you stressed? Do you need a place where everyone is friendly and absolutely huggable? A place where money has no meaning (except for being shiny) and everyone is just living the really good life? Yes? Then Carto will make you happy. It is a relaxing, hand-drawn, wholesome puzzle game, full of cute characters… and hugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Main game play element seemed interesting, turned out to just be thoughtless busy work so you can walk to the next screen where you have to read more pointless dialogue from "adorable" characters. It's like someone thought the filler in a JRPG was the best part. Wouldn't have bothered to leave a review if this didn't claim to be a puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Good presentation and cutesy, I like the little bits of humor and relaxing gameplay. I don't think any of the puzzles were difficult, nothing frustrating about the game at all really. I can understand if people get bored since the mechanics don't change much throughout the game, but I found it a great way to wind down and didn't mind that in a 5 hour game.Played on Deck with no problems.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely recommend this game. It might not blow you away but it's definitely an incredibly charming experience.I would say my main issue is that it takes a bit too long for the puzzle mechanics to really hit their stride. I would have liked for the game to either be longer or to push the concepts a bit earlier in the experience. That said, the mechanical and difficulty shortcomings are definitely balanced out with the extraordinarily charming vignettes in each new world
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Think you've got what it takes to be a little cartographer? I didn't think so...But if my slight dismissal didn't cause you to leave the premises,  let me let you in on a secret of the trade: it's not that hard, really. I mean, look at Magellan! He only crossed the Pacific because of a boneheaded blunder. You? You've got talent...unlike that fraud Magellan.  Most puzzles in this game are straightforward. And if you've got at least one working wrinkle in that brain of yours, well, you're two steps ahead of our friend Magellan. Fun little game, cute music, beautiful art, and enjoyable puzzle mechanics. My son and daughter love helping the old man out. Is it worth $20? Pick it up on sale at $9.99 if you can...or have your friend send it to you for free like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful gem of a game. The conceit of flipping around and matching map tiles to solve the puzzles is so well executed, and the characters are cute and charming. There were a few places that did make me tilt my head, but not so terribly as to leave me stuck for very long, and most of the puzzles were straightforward. It's not going to be a game that makes you feel especially challenged, but it's fun to play through, that's for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a super unique game where you progress through the story solving puzzles using map pieces. I really enjoyed the story and the puzzles were challenging, but not too difficult.Overall to complete the game and get 100%, it took me eight hours. I would recommend getting this game on sale. If you love point and click adventures, you'll love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: I just steam searched "jigsaw" and saw the positive reviews and about 5 seconds of the video before thinking "this looks fine."I wasn't expecting to have my heart warmed in the process of playing this. But my rigid husk of a cardiac muscle is quite toasty now. The story is very cute, the puzzles are interesting, and throughout the game I found myself saying "awww" frequently.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: A simple idea executed brilliantly is how I would sum up Carto.  You have very little influence on the world as your only means of control is moving and rotating the map pieces you find upon your travels but by limiting the scope in such a way the devs have done a fantastic job of focusing the experience.  The characters are all welcoming and good natured people who are a delight to meet on your journey and while Carto's interactions are simple in smiles and dances she still comes across as an expressive little girl.Having clear delineations in chapters where each is it's own self contained little story means you aren't left wondering how to fit pieces together either.  There is no fear of inventory bloat like you might get with a classic point and click adventure or worries of being stuck for overly long on any given puzzle.  The devs clearly have a story they wish to tell and don't wish to hold the player back from progressing through it but still give just enough of challenge to allow the player moments of discovery or joy at figuring out the answer.  The addition of the extra achievement puzzles also giving players who desire to poke at the world the chance to take things a step further with all of them feeling fairly natural to figure out on your own.Overall a delightful little journey that you could complete in an afternoon or over a lazy weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome puzzle exploration game!A feel good, heartwarming, sometimes funny and fun coming of age adventure that will keep you entertained throughout.The puzzles themselves are not too hard and not too easy... you may get a bit stuck at times, but it's just a matter of thinking outside the box... quite literaly. And then, worst case scenario, just fumble around with map pieces and you eventually get there. xDPretty novel concept and idea... really loved this one. I always take a bit longer than necessary in games, so this is closer to some 8hrs of playtime, but at least for me it's the ideal length to keep things interesting and a good time flow.Super recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

_childDocuments_.review: Carto is a short, entertaining puzzle game without violence.Emphasis on short. The entire game leans on a new "build-your-own-map" game mechanic which is not explored to its maximum depth.Even though I am positive about the game I think the full price is way too high for the amount of time it will keep you entertained. The price / game length ratio is the main reason I can not recommend this game.I do appreciate that it doesn't try to bait me into collectible hunts though. It's pretty clean cut, straightforward: Short story with an interesting game mechanic.My advice: get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Carto

Thus, the game takes quite much longer than you thought. So, there will be more adventures that you have to go through & complete.▹ To anyone who wants a rather 𝖈𝖍𝖆𝖑𝖑𝖊𝖓𝖌𝖎𝖓𝖌 big brain game, I recommend you this one. The more chapters, the tougher it gets. ▹ This game is one of my favorite relaxing puzzle games because there is no time limit or urgency in it.▹ Should you 𝗕𝗨𝗬 this game? Yes, but highly recommend it when it's on sale of course. If you're still eager to play this game, then just buy it. I bet you'll enjoy it ( •̀ ᴗ •́ )و  but for me, it's kinda pricey for the number of hours of play.Overall, I give 9/10 for Carto. That's my honest review hihi, thank you! ʕ ᵔᴥᵔ ʔb
