_childDocuments_.review: i love this game a lot but ever since the update i straight cant equip items for some reason.edit: entering inventory holding left click and dragging the item then pressing F allows equipping of gear since the update.credit: steam forums showed me this i was too dense to figure it out just thought i'd edit this and leave this here for others to find and to give the rating the devs deserve.opinion: This game is amazing the builds are robust and different from what we've seen before not necessarily in concept but in function and design. The parry mechanic in the game is initiated at the apex of the enemies weapon swing this can be difficult to see with faster weapons but feels really intuitive. i personally always found fromsofts parry frames initiating when the weapon would be about to make contact difficult to use due to weapons having certain animations clouding the point of impact. furthermore the park system in the game is new to the ARPG formula at least in my experience. This system really allows the player to delve deep into their preferred play-style and no perk is straight up one stat or another as when upgraded then give QoL bonus' as well as dmg or stats or interesting mechanical effects to add to your repertoire.TL:DR for a 3 person studio this game is absolutely amazing ignore the nay sayers and just give it a chance atleast past the second boss or so before you make up your mind, if it feels unfair or hard, you're doing it wrong.

Music is wonderful and gives a sense of dark fantasy throughout the game. Design concepts look great and give character to the world.The "Needs work done." _childDocuments_.review: Bleak Faith: Forsaken is, at its core, a conflict of two key gameplay pillars: the world crafted here is of unparalleled majesty. No game I have ever seen or played has art direction so exceptionally inspired, no game handles exploration as deeply enticing and engaging, and no game has compelled me to push further into its breathtaking labyrinth as this one does. An interconnected world on par with From Software's best, it invokes all the same wonder I had when I first slowly uncovered the sprawling twists and turns of the original Dark Souls.  underpinning this awe-inspiring creativity is an unpleasant, clunky, buggy, and poorly controlled combat system doing everything in its power to make you quit before you see any of this, as shown by the myriad of negative reviews with playtime clocking in at less than two hours. The breadth of quality between the exploration and combat make for a game that challenges your priorities: should you come looking for a souls-like sporting a robust combat model, with a brutal yet fair challenge, typical of the genre, this experience isn't for you, however, those with a taste for discovery, driven solely by curiosity, your only reward being the knowledge of what's over that hill, you are sure to find something to love about Bleak Faith, Forsaken.Although my playtime isn't indicative of a complete playthrough, I've seen a large portion of what Bleak Faith has to offer and feel far more qualified to present a more informative review. Although, should my opinions change upon seeing the credits roll, I'll return with any edits I feel need making.A quick note before the review proper, as an alternative to reading this review and going into the experience truly blind, as is best, I recommend checking out a free, twenty-minute game here on steam called BABBDI; it's a pure exploration experience that is extremely comparable in tone and creativity to my time so far in Bleak Faith's Omnistructure. So if you're still on the fence after reading reviews of this evidently divisive game, I feel your opinion on BABBDI will be the key to help you decide.So let's begin with that fantastic world I highlighted at the top of my review: straight out the gate, the opening surroundings give you a solid impression of the dystopian, otherworldly style. Crowded flats, unevenly and unceremoniously stacked, barely stand, crumbling as they seamlessly merge with the surrounding stone and steel. Grotesque, skeletal monstrosities soar overhead, casting shadows over a dilapidated, forlorn monastery with their leathery wings. Thin, precarious walkways, barely holding on following centuries of erosion dot the landscape, serving as the only path to loot-ridden islands, held only by a needle of bedrock. Later on, we can observe alien structures twisting and writhing just out of view, with even larger abominations circling them. The multitude of vistas I've stumbled across is spectacular to behold: I've enjoyed allowing myself a minute here and there, the subtle and haunting soundtrack complimenting the moment as I scrutinise the horizon, speculating whether I'll eventually find myself there up close.Level design is particularly strong here, giving just enough of a sense of disorientation to keep the exploration from feeling stale, although not so much that you miss out on the satisfying realisation that things are looking familiar and that you've discovered a shortcut or an alternate route. Flashes of inspiration and clarity like these are around every corner of the Omnistructure, giving rise to an immensely gratifying feeling of accomplishment upon learning the ins and outs of these complicated spaces.The three-person team at Archangel Studios are unapologetically and uncompromisingly steadfast in their vision and delivery of this world, for better or worse. Checkpoints are rare, and handholding is not something you will experience in any capacity. When this works, it works flawlessly; it's on you to find the path forward and progress feels great. However, pivotal, main progression is found where you least expect it, obscured by shadow, or down a tight alley, often resulting in aimless wondering, searching for any tiny detail that may have been missed. Occasionally, when I  discover a way forward, I'm met with a sudden increase in enemy resistance, leaving me no indication of whether I should even be here at this time or not.Not everything feels complete either; a dark tunnel leads to an open train station with exposed tracks leading off into the distance over an endless void. Following a good three-minute walk down this rail line, complete with a short stutter (indicating a new area being loaded), you'll find yourself in a dark, foggy area completely vacant besides blurry textures and the general feeling that this area isn't finished. There are other equally bare, though not quite as conspicuous, dead ends peppering the landscape, prompting a wave of uncertainty regarding whether this is intended or not.Combat in Bleak Faith is something you have to be patient with: it starts dreadfully, only becoming slightly less offensive as it evolves. I strongly recommend playing with keyboard and mouse controls. While being decidedly the best option, it takes getting used to and you should consider spending a few minutes at the start studying the key-binds and changing the more awkward ones. When it comes to engaging the enemy, attacks feel cumbersome to use; there's a combo system at play here, one that requires precise attack inputs to string together fast attacks, with mashing leading to a slow and clunky combo. It's hard to tell when you need to trigger the next attack, with no clear visual indicator and relying mostly on you getting a feel for your weapon.With a janky, hard-to-use parry and a dodge without iframes, your defensive options aren't any better. The dodge is just so catastrophically useless, only applicable outside of trading blows to back up quickly or sprint past a particularly challenging enemy while low on health. The parry functions unlike any I've used before, appearing to work during any part of an attack's animation, resulting in me rarely using it due to general confusion about the mechanic.All this being said, there's a certain charm to how awkward the combat is; with hitboxes that seem to only work at random, enemies are just as bad at hitting you as you are at hitting them. Weapon variety is surprisingly good also, and a lot of them come with genuinely interesting abilities that provide good spectacle. Furthermore, customisation isn't bad either; you're able to slot gems into your weapons and armor, fitting them out with minor stat increases. The hilariously janky, large enemies are a personal highlight: the formula for these sizable foes involves bringing them down by swiping at their legs, then climbing on their back, stabbing weak points, Shadow of the Colossus style, until they throw you off, . It just sums up all of what there is to enjoy about the combat being just so unnecessary, so broken and so frequently infuriating, but so laughably cool and unique at the same time.Overall, Bleak Faith: Forsaken is a special game. Not for the faint of heart, it is brutally unforgiving in its exploration, combat (though perhaps not for the reasons the developers would like), and progression. However, amongst a genre done to death, Bleak Faith is a supremely unique game that I strongly recommend, and an experience that will likely stick with me for many years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I wanted to love this game since this small team is from my country, at this moment I can't recommend this game. I loved the music, loved the environment, loved the design of the enemies. As a souls veteran, I had high hopes for this one. You can clearly see the level design is heavily influenced by Dark Souls 1. What went wrong? Ok, you want a souls-like game with hard enemies and even harder bosses?Then make combat playable, when I encountered the first enemy I went:'' Oooookkkk maybe it was just a fluke'', but no. At first, I thought it was cool that even the first enemy can surprise you by teleporting behind you and striking, little did I realize they implemented that because their pathfinding is bad, saw most of the regular enemies moonwalking across the terrain and clipping inside walls, enemies trying to hit you and their attacks go straight through you. Whenever I fought, it was a dice roll whether the enemy's attack is gonna hit thin air or crack my skull. You lose stamina WAY too fast even with no equipment on. You do not have complete control over your character's actions. The combat is just clunky at best. So if you want me to survive in this magnificent world you made, at least make enemies act accordingly. There was this bigger enemy next to a tree that can stun-lock you to death if he pins you in a corner with his stone spike attacks that for some reason track super accurately even if you try to dodge or jump over them, and can even ragdoll you into oblivion.Ok, do you want platforming sections where you need to jump and climb like in Assassin's Creed?Then implement it as clearly as possible. At one point there was an interaction button that prompted me to climb up, I was like ooook that was unexpected, but soon realized it was not working as intended since I climbed at the top and the tutorial said, now just jump up with a regular jump so you can reach higher places. You can't do that. You can't give me a super limited traverse system in this vast open world hoping that I will JUMP at any platform that seems traversable only to find out it actually isn't and I need to look at the interaction button to climb.Ok, you want to equip your gear and look at your character?Too bad, the UI is covering the head of your character for some unknown reason. Talking of UI, it isn't half bad if rather simplistic, could take a better look at pieces of armor when cycling through gear though.The graphics are fine and as I said I loved the music. The environment and huge monolithic-like buildings draw me in and the design is superb, it's a shame the interactive part of this world is half-baked. Don't know if they can fix the combat at this point, they are gonna need a lot of patches to fix this, here is hoping for the best.P.S (talking to the developers in my native language)Momci što bi rekli ovo vam je tough love. Znam da ništa nije savršeno i da za dobre stvari treba vremena. Mislim da ste morali više da stress-testujete igru i provjerite zašto većina protivnika udara vazduh umjesto mog karaktera. Nadam se da vas neće obeshrabriti negativni komentari i da će te raditi na tome da igra bude petchovana i poboljšana. Hvala Vam na radu i trudu koji ste uložili jer je evidentan ali kao neko ko je vaš zemljak neću da Vas lažem i govorim sve je sjajno i bajno. I ja da napravim nešto što ima loše strane, volio bih to odma da mi se kaže da bih poradio na poboljšanju. Vjerujem da će biti bolje. Veliki pozdrav.

_childDocuments_.review: It's so good.I've seen comments that it's boring because it's all grey. It's not. There are some levels where the color seems so much more significant because of the early greyness.I've seen complaints about the movement. If you've played Steel Rising (meh) and noticed that it's awkward at first, this is similar, but you get used to it. _childDocuments_.review: I've thought long and hard on what to say about this game. Its not a BAD soulslike, or a BAD adventure game, or a BAD action game, Its extremely ambitious and some of it is brilliant on paper. The end result however is a subpar game but an extremely unique experience. Let me explain.Bleak Faith recently got an extensive overhaul that fixed alot of issues the game had on release. I bought the game recently for $5 so i can't say if the game is better or worse than it was before. What i can say, regardless of when you play it, this is a VERY VERY indie soulslike. The combat is stiff and borderline frustrating on certain bosses and enemies. The map design is like going out of bounds and exploring unfinished assets. Weapons feel decent with good feedback but fail to really capture any form of weight or strength. Bosses are interesting and some thought was put into them, but the inconsistent hitboxes and some questionable attacks make fighting some of them extremely annoying. The music is halfway decent but i bet i can find a few tracks on a royalty free website's "epic songs" page.Despite all of this, I thoroughly enjoyed my time here. The amount of effort to make a soulslike unlike others while being familiar is 100% felt here. The gameplay is good enough, the music is good enough, the map design is good enough. The game is GOOD ENOUGH to warrant its price. The ideas here are extremely ambitious specifically for a Double A studio. Climb on the back of monsters, swim deep in monster infested oceans, ascend monolithic towers, ride on the back of serpents, cast a tornado to shred enemies, build a character to fit your playstyle. Its A LOT and the end result could have been A LOT worse.Im not going to say the game is a hidden gem that you NEED to play, but if your looking for something different in the genre, i recommend it. $30? Ehhhhh..... $20? Sure why not. $5? 100% a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: The videogame equivalent of the cover of a Burzum album.Its sad people are tanking this game's rating because of poor controller optimization: it has since been fixed, and is still being optimized. It is sadder still seeing all these content creators write this game off-- I can't help but feel these same people that would have been unable to see through the original demon soul's janky exterior before there was enough public discourse around it.That being said, Bleak Faith is without question janky and rough around the edges. Yet, somehow, I find that this element only ads to its allure. I kept asking myself: am I supposed to be here? Is this fight even possible with the gear and knowledge I currently possess? I constantly felt confused, suffocated, and hopeless, which enhanced the ambiance and made every victory as sweet as it was Pyrrhic. The game is a love letter to dark souls when it comes to its structure, but the more you play, the more you come to realize that the devs have their own vision. The game's bleakness is on a level I can only compare to the feeling I got playing pathologic for the first time: it is depressing, brutal, and at times controller-snappingly unfair. Of course I love elden ring and DS3, but the newer souls games have lost something that was present in these first "soulsborne" games atmospherically: a kind of spiritual smothering and aphotic helplessness, the feeling that any and all progress and knowledge involves war of attrition. Bleak Faith brings those brutal vibes back with vengeance, all while offering its own completely unique take on the "dark fantasy" palette. It kind of looks like the art from the tabletop game Scythe + Soviet dystopianism. It also has a puzzle-piece style interconnected world like DS1.In its music and art direction, you can't shake the feeling that something is deeply, deeply wrong. You feel like society and culture have been snuffed out so irrevocably that all humanity can do is start at square one, fumbling at the building blocks of society like toddler with a vague memory of a past life. It is hard to express, but just listening to the soundtrack will give you plenty of insight into what is in store for you.While Bleak Faith doesn't have the polish and sheen of many modern souls-likes, what it nails is the tone, and it is worth cooperating with the rather limited combat mechanics to experience its ferociously hostile, cryptic and wilted world.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had tons of fun with this game, but cannot recommend it in its current stateI was also one of the people who played this game Day 1Pros: + The map is massive and atmospheric and it's really cool to see all the different areas of it+ The way you build your character is really cool: perks, equipment, a lot of the weapons have really cool abilities+ The game pretty much never holds your hand and you as the player get to experiment and learn to deal with the obstacles+ For an ambitious project it's incredible that 3 people did make this+ Enemy type is very varied+ The developers are working hard to fix the many issues.Cons:- Game Trailers and screenshots were misleading of the final product- Your many dead bodies will prevent you from properly hitting bosses as they interfere with attack hitboxes- No matter what I did I could not get the bow to work on controller- While the game is massive it's very empty and doesn't reward major exploration hidden items are thrown haphazardly in boring locations.- Bosses randomly include invisible enemies that drain your life. The bosses should really stand on their own it's poor boss design to include something the player will just run into that is invisible.- THERE ARE TWO 6 MINUTE ELEVATORS where you have to wait 3 minutes for the elevator to come down and then another 3 minutes for the elevator to go back up.- This game has too many elevators and ladders that it becomes agonizingly painful when you see another one.- There is a boss near the end that requires lining up things perfectly with timing in order to effectively dodge attacks.- There aren't enough bosses in the game with the sheer size of the game - There are areas in the game you can access that players shouldn't be able to see- Early game builds feel lacking there isn't much in the way of choice

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't stomach more than what I have on record. As of right now, the game doesn't feel good to play, even on mouse and keyboard. The world is absolutely gorgeous from what I saw but combat feels clunky, movement is weirdly simultaneously overly precise and imprecise, and the animations just feel like the characters are wading through water.I'm sad as well because I can appreciate a janky game from time to time, but the jank isn't really charming here. It just feels unpleasant to do anything. The climbing is what broke me; it was so bizzarely janky and I wound up getting flung to my death just trying to normally navigate the first wall climbing segmentThis game clearly needed more time. The developers have a powerful vision, but it feels like they focused more on the world than how it feels to navigate it. If they actually did this, fair enough, but I feel like they should have brought on members of their community to do testing so that they could nail the general feel and flow of the game.Hopefully the devs iron out the kinks and improve it, and if they do I'll happily revisit it and give it another go. But until then, I'm sad to say I can't bring myself to experience more of it.Edit: NEVER MIND! Turns out there's stolen/recreated animations from FromSoftware's own works in the game apparently. We live in a world where Pizza Tower, a game where every single frame of animation is handdrawn in an incredibly expressive style and the gameplay is extremely tight and responsive, was developed by one dude over 5 years, and Bleak Faith took three guys three years and yet came out significantly worse, complete with stolen assets made by talented people whose work is being used by people who don't have the right to use it.The developers have claimed that they bought the animations from the marketplace for the engine they used, which may very well be true considering how said marketplace has multiple stolen animations from From's own games; however, this doesn't excuse a failure to vet the source of the animations properly and is still a bad look.Great job, bozos.

Which is a shame because atmosphere and visuals are definitely great, but the gameplay/hitboxes/precision/movement/enemies AI and behavior parts are all weak which pretty much define what a videogame is. I tried to play this game on keyboard like how developers suggest and that barely helped situation, although it definitely is obvious that it wasn't made with a gamepad in mind. But still, this is an indie project and there isn't much of a reason to be too critical of it, but if you expect anything resembling a coherently working soulslike title this is not for you. _childDocuments_.review: I'm really torn with this one.I've been following the development of this game for a couple of years, since the premise looked interesting. The art style and the aesthetic are incredible, but everything else simply feels wrong.- The one big NOPE for me is the character movement and the controls. The movement feels really janky, and sometimes there is even some input delay, which is something I cannot  accept in a souls-like game.- The combo system sounds really cool in paper, but it was poorly executed. There are no clear indicators of when the combo windows start and end, so you just end up smashing buttons until you realize the timing.- Some enemies have attacks with very inconsistent damage. Sometimes an enemy hits you with a mace and deals 15% of your health, and sometimes that same enemy hits you the exact same way and deals more than half of your HP.- The fallen-giant combat mechanic is another thing that sounds good on paper but it was poorly implemented. Because of their high HP and the little amount of damage you deal to them, most of the times you need to climb on them 3 or 4 times until you manage to kill them, and if you get caught while on top of them, most of the giant mobs can one-shot you.- There is quite a lot of bugs. This was within my expectations, given the size of the dev team and the scale of the game, but it still ruins the experience way too often.- This one is not necessarily bad but more of a personal taste: the game was obviously influenced by Souls and other games of the same genre, but lacks some basic QoL features of those game that make certain activities less annoying (sliding down ladders, not losing stamina while sprinting out of combat, etc.)- The background music tends to end abruptly and restart, or switches instantly when you enter a new area. There doesn't seem to be any proper looping for the tracks and the transitions between songs are so sudden that breaks your immersion all the time.- The sound effects are just weird. Sometimes an enemy throws a heavy attack with a giant weapon and sounds like gently stepping over some leaves, and other times someone throws a pebble at you and sounds like a tactical nuke landed on your head.I really wanted to like this game, but I cannot recommend it in it's current state. If I had to make a guess, the devs had a very clear vision of the game they wanted to do from the very beginning, but they underestimated the technical complexity of making a game of this scale; but they seem to be pretty receptive to feedback, which is great, so my suggestion for the time being is to at least leave it wishlisted until some issues are patched.

_childDocuments_.review: This is where I wish Steam had a mid-tier option. The game is a work in progress. There is some jank, stuttering when assets load, a few enemies zooming around once in a while, and occasional questionable collision and hit boxes. That said, there's something really good under the hood. Jank aside, this is one of the few "souls-likes" that I haven't really bounced off of super quickly. The aesthetics are interesting and seem like a lot of love has been put into the world itself. The enemies are a bit sparse in some areas - I like to believe its leaning into the "bleak" part of the name. A few items that may be an issue for some - not every item has a description (yet? idk) like a few rings. They ~should~ in theory be self explanatory (ring of gluttony) but it'd still be nice to see more descriptions. The menus (and keybindings for the most part) are not meant for controller and is not very intuitive. I imagine using m&k would be much easier, but its not my jam.  I do feel I got a grip on what layout works best for me, and that took a little bit of changing the config and playing the game until it felt good.The flow of the combat will take some getting used to - its not as crisp as games like Fromsoft games or even Nioh, but it isn't as bad as some of the other clones. The world is very reminiscent of DS1 in that there are many short cuts, and "ohhhhh so this leads me back here" moments while exploring. As far as I can tell, dying doesn't seem to mean all too much other than the checkpoints are sparse unless you use a consumable that makes a checkpoint until you find the next one in the world. Take this with a grain of salt. I'm very patient and generally give games a lot of time before I give up on them (looking at you 40hrs of Elex/Elex 2.) I think this is a nice labor of love and seeing the game have nearly daily updates with fixes makes me hopeful for the future of the game. Give it a go, but don't expect Elden Ring or Hollow Knight. Treat it like the 3 dev-indie game that it is. Get it on sale if you're doubtful, but so far I'm content with spending the full $30 on it and am excited to see what else the devs can do.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been holding off on a review for this game in order to see if the devs truly were dedicated to improving and fixing the many issues with.    I have played it on and off since release for a few hours after every update that they seem to roll out daily (kudos to them), and am now a good 20 hours in.  The game has indeed gotten better since release (I hated it the first 3 hours I played on release day, felt bad), there are obviously still alot of problems and alot of jank (I still avoid combat with giants, it's not very fun and is a very janky roll of dice on whether you live/kill it, or it bugs out and you die for non apparent reason, I digress).  That being said, the potential for this indy game is a hidden gem under all the problems....and even with all the frustration and problems I've encountered, I've also enjoyed myself quite a bit the deeper I get into the game.  And I actually really like the combat system (when it doesnt jank out), at first it didnt feel good to me, but the more I've done it, the more the devs have made fixes, and the more I've improved my gear and perks/abilities, I can really see what they're going for, and it's actually pretty fun....again, it does have some frustrating jank still when stuff bugs out, but when it works, it's got potential and is enjoyable.The world is pretty epic...the crazy verticality actually makes my head spin at times, in a good way.If you're expecting AAA studio, Elden Ring type polish, well it's not here at this point...but if you give this game a chance, and just laugh off some the buggy jank that happens, while also appreciating the work the devs are still doing to make this a good game, then I say give it a shot.  Once you start to get the hang of things and start to progress, it really does get better as it goes.  All that said, if you want to wait and see how much better the game is in a few months or so, then I get it...that's totally legit.  Imo the game will only get better and better, as it already has since it launched 10 days ago....so jump in now and go for the ride of ups and downs, while also supporting the devs, or wait and see...but at some point, you should play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Bleak Faith is a master class in awful.On any given day this game would be appalling, but to be released in the same window as Wo Long, further highlights its shortcomings and is the nail in it's coffin.The best way to describe it would be with a movie analogy; whenever Hollywood releases a blockbuster, there is usually a low budget, poor quality cash in. For every 'Guardians of the Galaxy' movie there is a 'Galaxy Guardians' movie. This game is Galaxy guardians through and through.There are no redeeming features about this game. If you are looking for a reason to buy it? then stop reading now.Bleak faith, is a souls like. To be perfectly honest it is probably the most challenging soulslike game I have ever played, not because the actual game is especially difficult, but because trying to actually "play the game"  is difficult.Firstly, the developers made this game primarily for mouse and keyboard, stating that "if you want to play on controller you may encounter some issues" .... and they were not kidding! I have no idea why, in 2023, anybody would want to play a soulslike ARPG using a mouse and keyboard, but I guess some people do and I think it's fantastic that the option is there. However primarily, most modern gamers, with modern setups, would most likely prefer to play this with a controller.The ingame support for controller does seem to have a lot of options, however none of them actually work. The unwritten rules are, that when you create a soulslike game, you stick to the tried and tested soulslike controller layout.People have poured hundreds of hours into this genre and muscle memory is invaluable when it comes to playing this type of game.Bleak Faith immediately throws all of that out of the window and presents you with a default controller setting which is one of the most bizarre, uncomfortable and unintuitive I have ever used.The button you would ordinarily use for jump, is now an interact, while the Dodge button is Dodge; as well as Sprint and jump.... and never seems to do what it's supposed to do at the time it's supposed to be doing it. Simply trying to walk up a knee height step becomes an almost impossible 'Boss' challenge.I managed to gain some semblance of control over my character by sacking off the ingame and using the Steam controller settings. Even then control of your character feels somewhat weightless and janky. Within my first 5 minutes of the game I had suffered three deaths, not at the hands of any enemy, but simply by falling off the environment in bizarre and floaty ways. Combat is equally sluggish and clunky causing frustration. Not in the classic 'harsh but fair', learn the mechanics and overcome type of way; just in the pulling your hair out why is this happening way. Graphically the game looks okay, it's one of those games where a screenshot is going to look good, but when you're actually playing the game it's all very 'samey'. I will give them credit however, frame rates seemed to be pretty consistent and the game seemed well optimized on PC (which given the current state of poorly optimized AAA releases is praise indeed).At the top of the review I mentioned this came out around the same time as Wo Long from team Ninja. An example of a beautifully balanced and designed game that feels responsive and a genuine joy to play. I have already put over 30 hours into this game and can't recommend it enough.Conversely I had a very hard time with Bleak Faith. If it were purely down to personal choice I would have stopped playing this game after about 15 minutes and apply for a refund however given a professional responsibility for a fair review I played for a couple of hours and quite honestly disliked every moment of it.As a fan of the soulslike genre, it is an incredibly disappointing experience and not one I would recommend to anyone. I am neither a purist nor an elitist I have enjoyed most of the soulslike games released to some extent or another.Some of the indie souls have been fantastic most notably Mortal Shell and more recently, Asterigos. Proving that you don't need a big budget and large development teams to produce a quality and enjoyable game.Unfortunately Bleak Faith, is neither quality nor enjoyable and I can't recommend this on any level.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game made by 3 people, this is incredibly well done. Obviously, if this was a AAA game, the rating would be drastically different, but context needs to be taken into account.Atmosphere is great. The armor and weapons system could use some more variety, but overall, the combat is cool and it's fun to craft an overpowered build. I went for a full bonk build with a two handed evolved halberd and a bow, and enjoyed the experience. The bows in general are very powerful compared to other games.The bosses are generally pretty cool, there are definitely some "unfair" elements, but some of the weapons are so overpowered, like the Arcane Bow, that you can basically sidestep those elements if you don't want the extra challenge. Some boss fights were a little too cryptic in terms of finding the "gimmick", like Wormlord and Nurgel. Nurgel is quite fun once you figure him out, but Wormlord was way too easy on figuring out the gimmick.As others have mentioned, some severe jankiness, but I was able to get through the entire game with only some guidance from the community.The weakest part of the game is the plot, which is entirely incomprehensible. In this aspect, the devs really have little excuse, as plotting a story requires no technical ability.Overall, if you enjoy soulslikes, apocalyptic cyberpunk, you'll probably get a kick out of the game. I think it's a tremendous achievement for 3 people.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful aesthetic. Exploration is well done. Lots of hidden nooks and crannies with something interesting. Very much like Elden Ring has done. The world is very interconnected and i love it. You'll find yourself looping back to places you've been from different altitudes and angles, kick down some ladders (which btw are often long and the game has no quick way of going down them) for shortcuts, etc. Only downside for me for exploration was that i was lead to believe Climbing was a thing and you'd climb most surfaces. But I encountered a really imo, bad section where they teach you climbing and it really feels clunky to the say the least. It's basically context buttons that you press but it feels really finicky.Combat is hit or miss so far. I like it and don't like it. You time your swings proper for less stamina usage and faster combos and the timing feels different for all the weapons i've gathered so far. So getting used to one makes you ♥♥♥♥ at the other until that muscle memory kicks in again. I had to change Dodge and Jump Keybinds because i instinctively press spacebar to jump and it's gotten me killed twice, trying to jump only to dodge off the platform i was on.Hitboxes are both good and really bad. Really good hitboxes against regular mooks but there was one particular enemy that has insane phantom range on his attacks. This enemy is a Corrupted looking Rajang that earth bends and hits you before you even see the visual effects. Its a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fight but easy enough after a few tries. You get a nice reward for beating him. An amulet that gives 0.5 second reduction to when stamina starts to regen. Very Nice.This is one of those games where you open the keybinds menu and see that its for big brained people who memorize the buttons with ease. There's a lot of keys to be pressed and it can become a handful once you get some stuff that uses more of the binds.

_childDocuments_.review: I am changing this review to a positive one because the game has gotten a lot of fixes, animation replacements, and seems like a genuine passion project from these developers. The game isn't well optimized, but it runs pretty well on my machine despite chewing up a lot of resources. I'm glad they aren't abandoning this project, because it has genuinely fantastic level design and exploration once you dig into it. The levels feel massive and interconnected and there are useful crafting materials, upgrades, weapons, and armor to find in every nook and cranny. The combat is pretty poor, but its serviceable once you find a good weapon to abuse. I am focusing on strength and my giant axe does enough damage to kill most enemies in two hits or less. There is some cooldown management involved with spells and special attacks and some strict resource management while you're in combat, but nothing too stressful. I respect the fact that there are no i-frames on the dodge, which gives shields quite a bit of value and also forces you to consider your positioning. There is very little story to speak of so far, but I bought the game to wander around a mega-structure and I got what I came for.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, let me just say, I don't like leaving reviews due to the masses already getting to it. But seeing as how this game is getting a bad wrap, I just gotta. Ill leave bullet points of pros and cons, and a lil side note of what to expect if you are looking to purchase the game.PROS:- Amazing detail and graphics, in my own personal opinion.- A unique combo based combat system.- Free to make your build on the spot with weapons and armors.- Unique M&KB controls that actually work really well with a 'souls-like'- Fluid movements, dynamic camera.- Neat skill system that allows you to interchange what you want.- Kickass soundtrack.- Not Atomic Heart, but robo booty.CONS: - Steep learning curve due to combo system.- Not much story put in your face.- Jumping and platforming can be a bit floaty.- No actual tutorial- Poor controller support- Not enough robo booty.CONCLUSION: If you are looking for a 'souls-like' where all you gotta do is spam r1, and not step out of the norm, Bleak Faith: Forsaken wont be for you. There is more to whats here than meets the eye. Yes it has the standard 'souls-like' feel. Stamina, health, flux ('magic') but that's all it is. In combat, instead of mashing your mouse, the game wants you to time your strikes, for a more 'fluid' feel. If you do it too soon, it wont que. And if you que too late, it costs extra stamina. And the difficulty will be there, it will be rough. But I see that as a valid trade, as you lose nothing upon death. It is the pinnacle of "git gud" You will die, and learn the enemies attack pattern until you can fell them. There is also no I frames, like standard 'souls-like' But lemme tell you, have you tried to roll THROUGH a sword? Ya cant! The dodge system is suppose to give a more dynamic feel, and put you on your feet. Instead of dodging through attacks, you dodge away from or to the sides of them. If you are going to be buying Bleak, adhere to what was said above. Its not your standard dark souls. Do not go into it with that mentality. Take your time, learn from the mistakes made, and get better for it. Get to know the UI and whats in your menu's before stepping forward into the unknown. Bleak Faith: Forsaken is by no means a perfect game, but I see it as a good refresher, and its adding its own neat little twist on the genre. It has a lot of room for potential, and I hope to see the devs continue to work on the rough gem they have. If you want to leave a worthy negative review on a game, go play Wu Long.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically write reviews at all, but this game sitting currently at mixed makes me want to stem the tide a little.Bleak Faith opens on a lonely, dark, labyrinthian mega structure. As the main character, we're dropped into a world with one palpable memory of a beating and not much else. From moment one, the tone is pervasive in every artistic design choice the team made. There's a certain feeling of foreboding and isolation that has rarely been captured so succinctly outside of a FromSoftware game, but the small three person team absolutely nailed it here. Environmental design is so impressive, and more than a few times I've been swiped off a ledge while I stared in awe at the distant spires and buildings jutting out of the landscape.I've found the gameplay incredibly fun. Initially there was some difficult getting my PS5 controller to work. Then I did this:Shifted over from Steam Input to Raw InputTurned on Playstation iconsMapped block to L1Mapped jump to Right TriggerAdjusted camera speed to my preferenceIt took less than a few minutes, and it was well worth it for the amount of fun I've had with this game so far. Getting a shield along with my weapon helped with the rapid walk cycle, which was an issue when my character lacked armor and was essentially unarmed. The unarmed walking made my character really twitchy for some reason, and I kept falling off of everything. Seems to be far more precise when I'm holding a weapon. My character started to move the way I expected her to.Make sure to explore the menu, as the game isn't great at explaining all the options available to you. I wasn't aware of the abilities or perks for a really long time. The abilities really change up the combat, and it overall just made the game a blast. Once I understood the combo mechanic, adding in abilities along with the combos is so much fun. This doesn't exactly play like Dark Souls, and while I understand the urge to compare Bleak Faith to DS because the presentation is so reminiscent, Bleak Faith wants you to play it differently. Go with the game, you'll have a great time if you give over to it.Aside from the combat, the exploration is fantastic. Great labyrinth level design. Once I fully explore an area, I generally can map it out pretty easily in my head which is a testament to the design logic they've incorporated. My absolutely favorite part of the level design is how each area empties out to such a great shift of locale. I don't want to spoil it, but needless to say there is a loooooot of variation in the environments that blend nicely into the design of the enemies in each area.Look, there are issues present, but the bones of something incredibly special is here. It's worth playing now if you're willing to abide by some of the quirks, the hardest of which for me has been the lack of i-frames. Still, the herculean task seen to fruition by the three person game dev team is purely worth the price of admission, and honestly deserves a standing ovation. These folks are going to be a force to be reckoned with in the future if this game is any indication.Go play it, now.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: You know you could have delayed the release, right?Looks interesting and I want to like the game, but there are glaring issues I experienced and see other people comment on as well:- Movement is sluggish with all the fancy turn around animations and slow acceleration, and, at the same time, feels like sliding a bar of soap around the bathtub. The camera is slow to catch up to the player and yet sometimes jerks suddenly, contributing to motion sickness.- Something different has clearly been tried with the attack/combo inputs, as mentioned in the tutorial popup, but it straight up does not work; swinging the weapon by itself feels awful, let alone in a combat scenario. Also why even sheathe weapons?- Parrying seems fairly easy since I managed to hit it most of the time, yet it's also not very satisfying or understandable, maybe a more deliberate animation or some kind of effect would make for a better parry window indicator.- The modern-action-game-style contextual climbing is very insensitive to inputs, I found myself rotating the camera all around and clicking all the movement keys just to have a chance to move to the next rock.- This might be a nitpick but I think it's usual practice to have the Esc key back you out of any inventory menu, which is not the case here. Also having to confirm every equip with a separate dialogue window is annoying.- I'm not sure whose fault it is, but my system meets the recommended specs and I'm still having lag spikes and stutters. Tried tweaking all the settings and issues persist. Maybe include an even lower, potato level of graphics?I hope this gets fixed and improved soon, the game looks promising otherwise!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a recommendation ONLY if you agree to seven or more of the following list. This is a maybe ONLY if you agree to less than seven but more than four.On less than four, it's a hard pass, it's not a recommendation. The list is:- You have a high tolerance for janky gameplay. Not outright bugs (like going through walls or glitches), just a metric ton of jank.- You are a fan of Tsutomu Nihei's work. A BIG fan.- You enjoy immersing yourself in game worlds, allowing your imagination to fill in the gaps instead of seeing said gaps as flaws.- You place a lot of value in atmosphere. It has to be a lot.- You have patience for games that are more than obscure in terms of explanation or tutorials.- You are resilient enough to face constant RNG odds, barely mitigated by skill. Mind you, skill will carry you, but jank will often get in the way between your skill and its ability to mitigate said RNG. This is not a random chance game, but jank means anything can happen.- You have a good sense of orientation.- You are understanding of what a small team (three people!) with more ambition than technical prowess can achieve.- You have enjoyed E.Y.E. Divine Cybermancy or NaissanceE.- You feel like a journey can be enjoyable in and on itself, instead of only finding catharsis in the resolution.I, who wrote the list, agree to all ten. So, I can say that this is a great game, FOR ME. I am profoundly aware of the myriad flaws, the bucketloads of jank, the all-over-the-place textures, the very basic yet somewhat frustrating combat, the long, uneventful stretches, and the dreadful platforming.But in this game I've also found one of the most unique atmospheres I've played, deeply enjoyable soundtrack, a constant sense of wonder, a surprisingly consistent challenge (that is, it's very hard, but never so much that you're stuck for hours at a time in a boss), a sprawling world that gets even bigger inside your head, capable voice acting, and a plethora of cool ideas (some better executed than others, but none so badly executed it actively hinders the game), and what is evidently, a very passionate small team of developers that had very specific strengths and very evident weaknesses, and here they are laid bare for all to see. So, follow the list. If you don't agree to at the very least half of it, this game isn't for you, and that is absolutely fine. This game demands too much from its players, and I don't mean it in a stupid "git gud" way. I mean it in a "this is a game that only people that are a little weird with niche tastes might like" way. No judgment, no arrogance. This is a game that you either love from the start, no prejudice, or you will never enjoy. Arguably, that doesn't make a great game, but for those of us attuned to the particular things this game does very well, there's a lot of satisfaction to be found.If you're not, believe me, every single negative critique is true. But the list isn't there for them. The list is there to let those who might enjoy it, know they might.

_childDocuments_.review: Being that I've only played this game for three hours so far, I intend to come back and update this review after I've finished the game itself. After clearing the first area and its boss, I can say that so far this game is every ounce of what I hoped it to be. Beautiful and surreal atmosphere, incredible level design, interesting enemies, an unreal soundtrack, and a combat system that is unique and robust. It took me a bit of time to wrap my head around the combat and get good, but once I got it I got it. It's not exactly like Soulsborne combat, though it is similar, but it's a fun and satisfying system that takes skill to master. Can't wait to get back into it and play some more. TL;DR if you enjoy Soulslikes like Elden Ring or Dark Souls, I have no doubt you'll enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I noticed majority of reviews seem like they're from people who expected Dark Souls from a 3 developer team. Which is their own mistake. While I agree right now the controller is extremely tough to use but the KB/M however plays very nice and allows keybinding. If you play with some settings the controller can be passable but I wouldn't recommend it. Right now I have almost 3 hours in game so I'll break down my experience from that. A lot of overreactions tho it seems from the reviews I've been reading. I haven't had any of the issues most people say. And the movement/controls are not anywhere near as bad as some people making it out to be. Also some of them have like 10-15 mins played it seems before they went right to write a poor review...From the limited time I've played so far I've enjoyed my experience. Performance has been great. Keybinds for KB/M all worked without issue. The combat is different. It takes some getting used to but I like how you time the attacks and sort of build momentum. The timing of your swings matters. If you just aimlessly spam attack it won't be as effective. I haven't gotten parry down yet but blocking seems fine..Sometimes weapons will clip through stuff, or enemies attacks through you/each other. Movement itself is a bit janky, your move speed can cause you to fall off sides and stuff. There is a walk option you can use when you walk to slowly explore tough spots so I'd suggest utilizing it. Exploration is probably the shining star here. There is a lot to explore and I've had fun just freely going wherever. The graphics are basic UE4 but you can see items/enemies in the distance and wonder how to get there. You can go whichever direction you please. Storywise I have only gotten to the first boss so I can't comment there. I've only met one NPC so far, it seemed similar to Dark Souls with a guy sitting there with the option to engage him in dialogue. The one boss fight I have done was similar to a Souls boss. Have to pay attention to the timings, attacks. They hit a new phase after certain point. The inventory system could use some cleaning up but overall it works fine. The crafting has worked fine for me as well. Also the developers have said the game is meant to be played 60-90FPS..It plays A LOT smoother if you lock your FPS to 60. I didn't have many issues at 120 cap either but its worth pointing out. Overall I think the game is well worth its price point. I'm looking forward to playing it more and exploring what there is to offer. I think the potential is there to have a very good game with some updates/polish. They do have some work to do especially with fixing controller input since a lot of people play with controllers. The combat does clip at times and you and enemies sometimes miss each other. I haven't had any bugs yet. The developers seem to be aware of the controller issue and eager to continue working on the project and fixing any issues people have. I'd much rather support a developer team like this who made a game they want to than most AAA studios that released unfinished/un-optimized garbage they have to take years before its finally in its what should of been released state. I'll update my review as I play through the game if anything comes up.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying myself so far, the visuals are astounding, these guys had an absolute vision to design all this and it feels incredibly immersive. There's definitely something interesting and eerie going on that wants me to know more about the story and lore. Gear and loot is fun, seems like there's alot of build possible and stuff to experiment. Music is also very nice, it grabbed my attention instantly with odd arabic crescendos and badass guitar riffs, most of the time just being this dark brooding ambient. Review bombing this game is unfair, it's a team of 3 people, yes, the controls on controller are pretty freaking bad, it would be the first thing that would need to be fixed. The combat also feels pretty janky and sluggish and I doubt this will ever change. It's hard to recommend this game to anyone that has played only souls/elden/sekiro games because these types of games are based solely on gameplay and Bleak Faith ain't got that, but I really want this game to do well, it's an amazing project and I'm sure if they had a bigger team the products they could potentially make would be awsome. Anyway, continuing the playthrought!

_childDocuments_.review: It's sad to see a Souls-like clearly inspired by Blame! and Lorn be this awful. But not unexpected. The movement and combat looked questionable in trailers already... And in reality they are some of the worst i experienced in a game period. It has that UE tech demo made in a month feeling. But even worse in some places. You slide around, get stuck on everything, there's no weight or friction to character movement (including enemies), dodge doesn't work 90% of the time and you have stamina of a snail. It's just off putting, you should not be allowed to release games this unpolished.It has cool looking Blame!-esque environment (main reason i gave it a chance since i have 0 faith in indie souls-likes, especially of this scale) - but you can still see it was probably made by one guy, it's pretty shallow. Enemy design is pretty random so are their attacks and animations.What's even the point of making a souls game if you can't make combat and controls good? Not even talking about level design and lore. There's none. Just none.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is strange, because on one hand I'd say don't buy it, and on the other if your like me your missing out. Bleak faith rides the line between terrible and amazing constantly switching between both while your playing and I'd not recommend it to the average gamer looking for another "souls" experience. partially because Bleak Faith is not exactly a souls game, It has the skin of a souls game, but the mechanics are not souls like at all in a lot of ways, which left me confused at the beginning because I really had no idea how to play this game correctly. It has a lot of build centered game play, relying on armor rating, buffs and abilities. Which make it almost feel like a traditional RPG where you trade blow for blow, like Diablo or games like it. While on the other side of things some enemies and bosses have complex move sets that require thoughtful strategy and reaction, more like Dark Souls. This is fine on paper, but does Bleak Faith actually deliver a solid enough experience is the question, and to this I would say no. It's way better then when it released, almost not the same game in allot of ways, and the Developers are constantly releasing patches, fixing bugs and improving the game in it's entirety, not just small things either, entire overhauls of levels, stuff like that. This makes me extremely excited to see where the game ends up in about a year or so. But for now I'd say wait to buy it, or if you do, realize it's more of an investment. Either way I'm going to give a list of things I liked and disliked about the game starting withWorld Design and atmosphere. Bleak Faiths best feature overall. It rivals dark souls in some areas for me. While there are some really low points, the highs are seriously high. The way levels interconnect and seem monstrous in size, while also feeling digestible and explorable is crazy good game design. Everything is tied up with a great atmosphere and solid visual effects breathing life into a otherwise bleak setting. unfortunately world design isn't the only thing you have to master in game design, and that leads me intoLevel Design. Bleak Faith really struggles with level design. Where to place enemies is a serious challenge in games like this I'm sure, balancing build types while maintaining a stable structure. Bleak faith puts some strategically placed enemies here and there but a lot of them are just scattered around not really posing a threat and become more of an annoyance then an enjoyable "Combat puzzle" to solve. And it's not that they couldn't fix this, they've definitely improved on their level design since the launch, but it still remains weak.  A good example of this is the Deluge, which is a mid game area. While it looks impressive the level design is not good, leaving you with allot of empty space that could be used in awesome ways. Like abandoned ships should be docked, and boardwalks should be extending out into the water with explorable fisherman shacks. Maybe even a market district type spot for looting, stuff like this makes exploring way more interesting. And having enemies actually blocking your way forcing the player to engage in smaller spaces would make a world of difference. As it stands the game is just too open and without structure. And while the enemies patterns aren't terribly complex, you could do way more with them in closer, more contained areas. Anyways, what about the Boss Fights. A big reason people play souls likes is for the boss fights. And Bleak Faith's roster isn't terrible. There are some decent bosses in this game that use the mechanics you've learned fairly well. Out of the eight main bosses I encountered I'd say just over half of them are decent to mid tier. And the last three are really bad, Not unsalvageable, just in a really rough state right now. Some feel more like proof of concepts rather then finished bosses in some ways. Either way I would not play this game for the bosses or enemy encounters. Bleak Faith as I said thrives on it's world design and ambiguous lore and story. At least some of these bosses, even the bad ones have one thing going for them though, and that'sthe Music. It's a bit cringe at times with some of the riffs coming off a bit out of place in the Sci-Fi/Dark Fantasy world. But there's only one spot in one track that really bothers me, while the rest are excellent. The music really helps this game world feel epic and other worldly. Amazing stuff. It even elevated some of the lesser Bosses a bit, making them feel more epic, and engaging then they actually where. Other minor problems for me is crafting feels pointless in some ways. On one hand its immersive and on the other tedious, balancing it out would take allot of time I feel like, so maybe it's not worth changing but I thought I'd bring it up. Player animations interacting with the world are clunky, they need polished up for sure. Things like the rolling speed not decreasing at the end of the animation makes your player look like hes on a conveyor belt and not actually interacting with the ground.Bugs are an issue, but as of now I don't think any are game breaking that I know of.Anyways, that's my review since finishing the game, It'll get updated as the game changes with time. But currently I'm giving this game a 5.9/10. This game could be a ten, it seriously has the potential, and I'm looking forward to when it's considered finished.

_childDocuments_.review: DON'T LET THE NEGATIVE REVIEWS SWAY YOUR OPINION OF THE GAME(note the game was made for M&K , they have controller support but the game even states before you start playing that its not recommended and may hurt your experience.. also if you don't like some of the default bindings... JUST CHANGE THEM) At the time of writing this i have 2.1 hours into the game, explored the whole first area beat the first boss and got to the second area where you first interact with the girl who allows you to upgrade. Since i first started the game the movement and combat has felt fantastic, it was a bit to get used to at first because its not exactly like other games and your character definitely has some momentum BUT THAT'S NOT A BAD THING it just takes some getting used to and honestly if you have ever played Hellpoint it feels very similar. Now onto combat, the parry feels great and blocking too, personally I wish there was a way to make it so the parry and the block are two separate buttons since there are times where I've only tapped in order to parry but it counted as a hold and started a block which led to me getting smacked but apart from that it feels fine. When fighting you CANNOT spam left click it will lead to slow attacks and a higher loss in stamina, you need to time your attacks to have a better combo and faster combo, the game even teaches you this so if people are having an issue because their attacks feel clunky that's probably cause they didn't pay attention to the tutorial and jumped into the game thinking it was exactly like dark souls and dark souls mechanicsI saw someone mention that the first boss fight has a move that's unavoidable... This is completely false. Unlike most souls like games Bleak Faith has jumping, the attack that slams into the ground and causes a shock wave can easily be avoided by jumping over it. the person who said they tried everything obviously didn't try that.Personally I've encountered only two very very minor bugs in the game, not to say there aren't any others because obviously there are they just haven't happened to me yet. The game JUST LAUNCHED there are bound to be bugs just like there are bound to be fixes and improvements.The first bug I've come across was at some point in the first area enemies just stopped being able to attack me, I couldn't attack them either or even lock on... it was as if they weren't even there HOWEVER I was still able to kill them if i parried their attack and my character auto smacked them.The second bug was during the first boss fight, where after dying he immediately repeated his first line of dialog that starts the fight so it closed off the arena and I couldn't get back in when trying to go back to him... I fixed this by pressing esc and clicking "Respawn" .... this killed my character again and re-opened the boss arena. I've been loving the game so far and the visuals of the game, for a 3 man team It's mind blowing what they have created and I cant wait to see more of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to lie...this game plays like watching cheap paint dries...easiest way I can put it. Trailer had me sold...but like the Big Mac picture...when you get it it doesn't look anything like advertised. The game is very slow and slow paced. It gets stale after about 30 seconds. Let me back up and talk about it for a second. The Mutated Ghoul (the enemy that waved its arm and rocks popped up from the ground) was annoying. About 1/3 of the attacks have no audio cues and the dodge function seems like a hit or miss. Same issue I have with Elden Ring where I would hit dodge and even if the attack would miss my character wouldn't dodge...this however is worse but let me stay on the Mutated Ghoul. Dodging the rocks was a hit or miss and because Audio Cues don't exist when the camera would bug out you where eating a hit that wrecked 1/3-1/2 of your life. Now I'm used to creaming a boss on my first attempt (unless my dodge wouldn't work...ER) so when I die I was like  I was hitting nothing on him and he would spam the rock cross and there is not quick get up feature so if you got hit by that move he would spam it until you died. Sometimes I would dodge, sometimes 1-2 seconds after dodging and taking a step or two I would take damage and get flung up into the air even if i dodged out of range. My record is 48 deaths against all of DS3 and 53 against all of BB...that includes the entire game not just the bosses...28 times in DeS Remake. I typically do challenge runs when I play a game for the first time...So dodging is second nature...same with parrying (Sekiro was relatively easy) so I was surprised I was stuck on this boss for over an hour. Now I was lvl 2 and love playing the hardest routes first (ran Catacombs in DS1 at the beginning and cleared it first). Eventually I beat him but staying on him and essentially being at no stamina the entire time because no matter where you where after 10 feet he spammed his long range attack that had a wide range you really couldn't run out of even when you saw it and knew what he was about to do. It also seemed like as long as the animation was there it was still a hit box meaning when i would dodge and stand up i would get hit be knocked own and die to his next 2 spam attacks. Even sometimes I would get knocked despite nothing touching me, so i beat him out of sheer luck. Most of the enemies by the water are beyond beefy and take about a solid 5 min per enemy and get to the point where they SPAM THE LIVING HECK OUT OF YOU WITH ENEMIES. The design of the world doesn't seem straight forward and I rerun the same areas trying to figure out where to go. Currently I am in the apartment complex area with the stairs.Now the question, why haven't I returned it for it not playing and looking like the trailer?Answer, I will play a game that I bought even if it is awful and damn near unplayable.Why did I get it?Simple it is done by 3 developers.Let me rewind a bit as I feel I came in to hot and shouldn't be to harsh. Now I believe this game was over priced but the theme looked cool and i was hoping after a year it would have some good updates. There is a few things it has going for it...the attack mechanic for perfect attacks and parries is really unique in both aspects respectively. Despite the combat being SLOWWWWWWWWWW and the dodges not responsive and the attack animation being wildly clunky I think the aesthetics work for it. The first main story boss I fought was easy though I died, none of his attacks where really telegraphed and died when he was almost died and the second attempt I creamed him with most of my health. The Sea Leviathans and the 'stab the eye out' mini-game is cool but i either run out of air or it regens its healthy before it attacks again and you can't kill it. The cyborg Super Shrimps are cool and like I said the look of the game is nice. The blood being oil or so it looked and the 'Bonfires' are really cool and I like the out of combat health potion refill mechanic as well. With all of that said I give this game a 2/10, but in hopes of something halfway decent I do recommend this game and will not refund it. I am rating this game based off the price of the game, Half the price of a AA/AAA title I expect half the game, but I got 1/4 of what i expected. I would say if this game was $5 it would be 9/10, $10 would be 6.5-7/10 and so on. I cannot give this game a free pass because of the dev team size, especially after the trailer, and everything they show frames it in the realm of a masterpiece to just catfish its customers. Now many will disagree and I honestly don't care. I am being impartial considering I finished DS2 Scholar of the First Sin....for this game however, I will finish it and I may grow to enjoy it more then I do now. I am holding out hope that they continue and don't take critics like me as an insult or distasteful. I love the game idea and hope they look at what me and other say and make steady corrections for their future games. I want their next $30 title I play to be a 4/10, then 6 or 7 and so on. Perfection isn't birthed from a single game.Developers...if you read this, maybe you will or will not, instead of focusing on better graphics, or bigger maps, or new mechanics, focus on refinement. Continue to make better games. My hope isn't in Bleak Faith: Forsaken, it is in what comes after. I am not recommending this game, I am recommending the developers future prospects. So please...don't give up. I do dislike many of the negative reviews that don't provide substance or call it garbage. I am to diverge from them and provide awhile harsh a more constructive foundation.-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Edit:I am now at the Blademaster, Nurgei. The game seems to feel better at this point though still dodgey on alot of mechanics like the dodge button. The issue i have severely noticed is falling through lifts/elevators, attacks missing despite hitting on screen and the most annoying...the second the boss goes to attack the hit box is egregious and I take damage despite him not swinging yet and the hit marker seems to be a massive box on his sword that beyond fair. Being a full sword length away from his sword or a meter from the edge when he stops and still taking damage in cheap difficulty. Though i tried using long swords dual wield to kill him i wasn't getting past 1st phase marker. Switched to lacerators and got him down to 15% because i tried a pseudo challenge run. I like the boss scaling aspect however he is currently at 50% for sharp damage which seems to be insane. Currently on him I got to a 15x combo 3 times before loosing it each time, and hit 10x combo meter twice before losing it because of a double combo to a yellow strike. each hit i do 40-110 damage depending on crits, frost, bleed, decay debuffs. Now why do I mention this...its a bare minimum of 65 hits and alot of times i only got hit combos of 2-5x. It is a lengthy fight and eventually becomes boring...i eventually stop paying attention and zoning out which got me killed. Sorry for the lengthy conclusion bit, but this leads me to the final part...the boss fights are beyond lengthy and beefy...similar to Nioh,but unlike Nioh you literally get bored to death. When I actually try in games it becomes a walk through but this I focus and after 10 minutes and only down to 60% health I get bored and stop trying and focusing. I would like to see them go a different direction where they add 2-4 more attack patterns, reduce the beefiness of the bosses (Hp or Res). With his resistance up and reducing my damage...he is incredibly beefy...and a lot of issues for Silicon Visage. Though what I do have to say is the audio of enemies, attacks and dialogues is without a doubt, better then most of Fromsoft's game and ties with Elden Ring, Bloodborne and Lords of the Fallen 2023.. Maybe I will add my final game verdict once I beat it.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to start this off by saying I fell off this game when it first came out. I can handle a buggy game but it was to the point that the game started to become too frustrating. Alongside its terrible balance at launch, I stopped playing. However, this game had some sort of curse put on me because I was always thinking about it. So this week I decided to play it again after seeing all the updates and man is it a way better, not perfect by any means, but a way better experience. I'm going to talk about the main issues first because I want to be as honest as possible, while I really enjoyed my time with the game, I can definitely understand why someone else may not like it. Depending on how much jank you can tolerate this game will not be for you. Even though the developers are constantly updating the game there are still a lot of things that can sour your experience. If you have not played a Souls game before you're going to have a bad time, this game can be very demanding and I recommend you start elsewhere. The game's combat is this greatest strength and weakness, and will definitely be the main reason you will not like this game. Your character controls as you would expect. I cannot say the same about the enemy's behavior. The enemy AI is not the best, and some attacks come out too fast (borderline bs at times) and some attacks are just impossible to understand (just straight up bs). I do want to say some enemy attacks are really cool and very fair but that same quality is not found in the entire game. So who is this game for? If you value uniqueness, deviation, and a game that isn’t afraid to try new things, then this game is for you. This game truly looks like no other game. The main draw of this game is its superb atmosphere and level traversal. There's plenty of loot to find and lots of places almost feel like their out of bounds or not meant for you but you can go there and that's a level of freedom and exploration other games just don't have. Back to the levels themselves, it’s really hard to describe what makes it so good, but the atmosphere, level layout, NPCs, loot, and enemy placement just add up to make something that I can compare to the genius of Dark Souls 1 level traversal (minus the gimmicky traps and tricks). I really can't stress how good it is. The music is Chefs Kiss. The build diversity is clever and unique. I had a heavy knight who literally was tanking all the hits of the final boss and just dishing out damage. I saw the potential for so many other builds. I was already imagining a critical dagger build, if I was ever going to do a second playthrough. It's a slow burn to get your build to the right place. Enemy variety is excellent, and the enemy designs are very inspired (nightmare fuel at times if I wasn’t so desensitized to such things).  Constructive Feedback For The Devs: Again, I really like this game. Some of the criticism made towards this game is really unfounded. People are very conditioned to compare this to dark souls and not on its own merits. So I will judge this game on its terms. These are just my opinions. Do with them what you will. There's also a message towards the end that's basically my heartfelt thank you for this game.Your enemy AI needs to stop freezing up suddenly when I hit them. It doesn't happen to every enemy but enough to the point where it feels abuse-able. It’s almost like they're just letting me hit them. My recommendation is to give the enemies some sort of hyperarmor when they want to start their animations. Or have better feedback for when the AI is being stopped by the players' attack.It felt like the build diversity really didn't start feeling noticeable until about mid to late game. Not something you can fix with this game but definitely for a future game. It’s a shame because I think the build crafting in your game makes it stand out and is so much fun to think about. A highlight of the game for sure.I’m sorry to bring up Red Knights because I know you've made changes to them, but they still have some issues. The red knights that show up after re-calibration, really need to not show up until at least handler echo 4. My damage was way too low until that point. Alternatively, you should balance the red knights for the expected handler echo levels for each area. For example, if you re-calibrate in the deluge, the player is still handler echo 2 fighting against a handler echo 4-5 enemy, when the enemy should be handler echo 2-3 in terms of health.Rolling from a dash just feels off. IDK if it's a button timing issue or an animation issue. This was not that important to me because I was mainly dashing for my build, but was very annoying during the times when I did need to roll.Enemies need to have a windup to their animations or some sort of tell in their body language and movement. Attacks can feel very messy and many attack hitboxes from enemies don't work right. Many attacks just didn't hit me when they should have. Having a very nuanced response about a no I-frames system will take too much time, here are my main points. I did enjoy the no I-frames system and understand why you added I-frames in your recent update, but enemy animations did not encourage a no I-frame system. The fact the first boss could do circular spin attacks around himself (and many other enemies), was not a good way to instill the lessons of a no I-frame system. A no I-frame system needs to encourage proper spacing. Enemy needs to have proper telegraphing. I should be able to walk to the left of a boss and avoid their attack if I know a certain attack is coming. Personal opinion, bosses should be designed to be more gimmicky and less roll reliant. If you do want to do circular attacks, I should be able to jump them. With that being said, I understand if you never go back to a no I-Frame system, it's very difficult to get right.Lastly, about enemies, a lot of their attacks are not that interesting or unique. I'm sorry if I can’t be more specific, but it mostly comes down to the fact that a lot of the enemies don’t do anything interesting with their weapons. If I put their animations onto a typical knight character, their attacks would look normal, but this is a game where there are incredibly interesting enemies, and the best they can do is mimic how a knight would fight. The technomancer enemies are a step in the right direction, but even they could have had a larger move set. The spider-looking creature in the desert, can only use their hands to attack? Why don’t they use their legs to attack? I hope you see what I mean. Honestly, this might just be me expecting too much, but I wanted to address it. There are interesting attacks in the game, like the spider that shoots webs. Lastly, if the enemies do have interesting and unique attacks, they are incredibly buggy or borderline bs. To name a few, the giants in the desert whose rain attacks don’t seem to work and I literally can’t see anything. The bone enemy with spikes on their back and their ground AOE attack that is literally undodgeable. Nurgels shockwave, which I couldn’t figure out how to dodge. Message To The Devs: I know you've heard your fair share of negative feedback, which is why I wanted to be very respectful and constructive about it. I really hope that you iron out the issues with your code and use that framework to make a sequel or another similar game. This game deserves so much more love and coverage than it currently gets, and I hate how it's been treated by others. You guys rock and keep up your hard work. If you ever have another kick-starter for a future project I will be there to back it up. Thank you for a truly once-in-a-lifetime experience. I wish your team the best, and for many more games.PS - This game is way better than Lords of the Fallen by a long shot. Idk how three devs managed to have more enemy variety and a more inspired world than a multi-million dollar budget AAA studio.
