_childDocuments_.review: Reviews are HIGHLY overestimating how "bad" the game is.First of all, there's no invincibility frames. That's why you're getting hit even though you "dodged". You need to actually dodge away from the attack, not just dodge through it. This made a boss that would be very easy in a normal souls-like game actually quite challenging and it made me have to think *where* to dodge and not just dodge wherever. Oh, and using the jump is a very great dodge option as well, even outside of the shockwave attacks where you have to use it.Health potions are not renewable, you have to craft them and you can only have two (at least at the start) on you before you need to craft more. Enemies drop a lot of materials for them. To jump and use heavy attack, you need to hold the modifier button (probably not the official term) down while pressing either the jump or attack button. I'm playing on controller, for me it's LT.Attacks have a "combo" system. Not reeaally a combo system, but how it works is you can't just spam the attack button, if you want to do many attacks in a row, you have to properly commit to it and input the next attack at the start-mid animation of the previous one. I was skeptical about this at first, but soon when I got a greatsword weapon it clicked and became really satisfying. For example, doing a heavy attack-to-heavy attack combo makes the first attack stagger the enemy, then the next one deals critical(?) damage and usually sends the enemy's limb or head to fly, it feels great.Also, THERE IS NO LEVELING UP. The only way to "level up" is by equipping different gear. Again, I was skeptical of this at first, but soon I realized how... free(?) it felt. If you die, you just die and go back to the last twitching digital corpse you interacted with. No stressing about and running back to your "souls". I haven't yet interacted a lot with the different skills, abilities, or whatever they're called, but I'm excited. Though I do hope they replace those AI "art" icons on them. Honestly I have no idea why the devs decided the best place to start the game was on a narrow bridge, when the game's worst part, at least for me, is how for a lack of a better term, floaty the movement feels. I quickly learned that instead of fighting on a bridge you should just run back to a wider area.Anyways, the main reason I bought this game was for the bleak sci-fi BLAME! megastructures and it definitely does not disappoint. Easily the high point of the game and probably the most gorgeous game I've seen come out in a while. Soundtrack is amazing too and just lifts the atmosphere even more.If you're not scared of honestly pretty light jankiness all things considered, and a few minor bugs/glitches here and there, give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing experience, through and through, its almost impossible to believe that this game was made by 3 people (mostly 2 throughout development) and on a very very small budget of just 30k.You have level design that is on par with some of the souls games, non linear dark souls 1 style level design with tons of shortcuts, with well balanced bosses and serviceable combat. The game has a nice story that is easy to follow as well.Sure there is some jank in the game and there are bugs, but in my opinion thats excusable as the devs seem to be very on top of fixing things, and plan to add alot of free post release content to the game in the form of updates, on top of that, they are a small team of 3, and cannot polish a game up to the level of elden ring, which had a team of over 100 people.Overall, I'd give the game a 8/10 (would've been a 7, but the final level is so good that it adds a point)

From the lack of a world map to things like inventory management. Inventory in itself is a nightmare to navigate. Parry plain and simple does not function. No i do not mean doesn't function as in i cant parry i mean i lit press the parry button and no action is being executed. Just a slight weapon twitch. _childDocuments_.review: An amazing achievement for a small team. One of the few games where the world you traverse is the actual protagonist, and when approached with the right expectations this game will give you more than you expected. It surely has come a long way since its realease, and what I played was an approachable action RPG with world design that will amaze you you even in a post Elden Ring world. The mystery, the horror and the intrigue can be better driving forces than item or stat progression, and this is coming from someone with a brain as cooked by live service games as mine.It's definitely art, it's definitely slow-burn, but not in a tedious way, it does never try to waste your time. The 35 hours I spent during my two runs of the game were great fun, and having paid full price was absolutely worth it.My single major pain point with this game was audio design. I felt like the mixing was not up to par, footsteps, impacts and certain actions in cutscenes do not have sounds, and that could definitely improve. The soundtrack is a banger, though, and greatly enhances this game even more.Also, please do not expect a souls-like in the classical sense. There is no death penalty, you have a checkpoint you can freely place, and a lot of builds will absolutely wipe everything the game throws at you, ranged builds are also actually ranged, so you can have a huge advantage.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this review I have only gotten about 3 hours into the game, but I can see myself sinking much more time into it in the near future. As someone who is a die-hard-fan of the Soulsborne series including Elden Ring, I can say with certainty that although the game is a bit rough around the edges in terms of bugs, glitches, and clunkiness, it definitely scratches the same itch that the Souls games do. I completed the first major area of the game only to realize that somewhere along the way I missed an item that may or may not be important, but it has made me curious enough that I began thinking of what else I may have missed in the area, and I am looking forward to finding that item as well as many more that I will likely miss throughout the game. I have been waiting for this game for a few years now and I can say that, so far, (especially at the relatively low price point) I am not at all disappointed and it is worth a try for any with the free time to try something you may need to be a bit patient with.

_childDocuments_.review: As of reviewing, I've only beaten 2 bosses, explored 8 unique areas, and killed dozens of horrific looking... abominations.The short and sweet:Want that Souls-like feel from a game, really like the genre, and know the mental-play the game will throw at you? This has it and for the price, you will be entertained and immersed.Want to play the game because you saw the creepy/edgy trailer and want to feel like the stoic lone hero fighting alone against all odds? Maybe wait for the game to get some well needed polish.Now the technical bits and bobs:That souls-like feel is definitely there at the core and the devs really nailed it. 100% play this without any guides cause you will immediately get that feeling of 'im lost' or 'this path is going deep, maybe i should turn back' or 'how many turns did i take' while trying to navigate around, but at the same time, slowly make the connections and find the shortcuts/doors/ladders/elevators.NPCs are sparse and you really get that feeling of loneliness in a vast world of mystery and awe. Every area you will stop for respite and gawk at the grandeur of the environment, wondering what happened to everything.You will get far, and you will die for under-estimating your opponent and that drop in your stomach when you respawn back at the last 'bonfire' will hurt. Somehow the devs were able to pull that feeling off without the use of adding currency like souls/runes/etc.Now the scuff:Yes, the opening of the game can give you that feeling of hopelessness, but some of that will be due to jank controls. I'm a KB+M player but have always used a controller for souls/rogue type games. Do NOT use a controller for this game. It it not even an option, the controls don't work. Even after setting the scheme to Sony and failing to reassign actions, the X. L1, and Start buttons all did my primary attack. Nothing made sense to the point it was laughable. When I died for the first time by falling off a ledge because jump made me dash, I respawned with sonic levels of speed and literally launched off stairs to my death. The scuff was real and it translated equally when learning how to fight enemies too. I shut down the game, went to bed, woke up and tried with KB+M, and everything just started to click on attempt #2 learning the controls and movement. (I don't know why I was getting super sonic speeds after respawning my first play, it stopped happening the following day)Now that I can play the game, time for combat mechanics:If you love hitbox porn, this is it. If the blade/foot/claw/bullet/spell dont touch you, you dont take damage. You will learn quick there are no i-frames. Try to roll into an enemy swing, you will get tossed. Think you can roll in after that axe hits the ground, you gonna bonk your head into the blade and take some damage. Want to stand under a giant and break their ankles stress free, go for it, just watch out if they have magic or not cause you can't see anything while dancing under their loins.My only real complaint about combat would be the combo system. Not fighting enemies, you can get a feel for hitting attack at the right time to combo your swings which makes you attack faster and cost less stamina, but when you fight something, that timing kinda goes out the window. Sometimes it works, other times you get punished. I don't know if there's a hidden mechanic that changes the timing because you are attacking through something which would slow down your swing.I won't get into detail about the 'leveling' system but it is not hard to figure out and pretty intuitive for making your own unique stat build.Other thoughts:Graphics are really nice, and really help set the tone to each area. A few random frame drops if I run through an area and aggro dozens of enemies. Sometimes I'll drop from 150fps down to under 30fps, other times nothing happens. When entering new areas via elevator, the game will stutter for a few seconds but if you fast travel to the area, you get none of that. Nothing to get your jimmies riled up or diminish the actual gameplay experience.Music is fantastic. It's not always present which is a nice touch, you just get to take in the ambient sound and every now and then BAM, you get hit with that darksouls-ish music. Don't know how to explain the different genres that play except describing it that way.Only had one fatal crash to desktop from the unreal engine getting an error in the starting area of the game. I went afk for 30mins and came back to the error window. Nothing after that.Enemy variety is amazing. Twisted looking giant spiders with ghoulish faces, to alien looking tri-pod monsters, to clad in heavy armor knights wielding massive weapons to dozens more. Very much appreciated and sets a vibe for each area ive visited so far.Buy the game if you got that souls patience, wait for optimization/polish if you don't. I've been having a blast after switching to KB+M. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: I keep coming back to this game after every big update and while the updates are improvements, the game is still very very disappointing and still feels bad, the combat, the enemies, just walking around. it all just feels janky and disappointing. It's gotten better than from launch but that is not saying much.I also did not expect much from the game in general but even then it is still disappointing. _childDocuments_.review: I can't, in good faith, recommend this title now.  It's terribly frustrating to give this  a thumb's down, but for paying $30 (the non-sale price), this is far from worth the money.Pros:- Art direction is incredible.  Even despite the muddy textures, the game is quite something to look at.  It's clear this was the main vision of the dev's and is what kept me playing any of this in the first place.- Music is solid.  Not bangers.  Not 10/10, but the mood really fits.  Decent stuff.Cons:- Tutorials: The game gives some tutorials here and there, but there's no way to access them once you've seen one. Quick message prompt with a video example.  Once you see it the first time, hopefully you memorized whatever you read.- Block / Parry: REALLY hit and miss here.  Could partly be an issue from the first con, but it just feels incomplete.  Sometimes I hit the parry and it feels like it registers a counterattack.  Sometimes it feels like it just sort of drops off and forgets to have a counterattack followup.  Couple this with some enemies that were clearly meant to be parried for you to gain an opportunity for attack, and you get the idea.- Hitboxes: Oh boy, a slew of a mess that's beyond my comprehension.  An enemy can be half an inch above you and swings completely miss (also applies for you too).  Sometimes it feels like the weapon is the hitbox.  Sometimes it feels like it's just a cone in front of the enemy that's a hitbox.  Sometimes it feels like weapons are just an illusion and we (the enemy and myself) are swinging balloon toys.   There's a slew of other bugs, like tutorial boxes not triggering in the correct locations, skating movement, the current bug of not being able to equip gear the intended way (as of the writing of this post), and the entire controversy over animation and artwork assets.  I don't know.  There's something here, for sure, but three man team or not, this was not ready AT ALL to be shipped out for a $30 price tag as a full release.  Really hope the dev's do stick with this and continue this passion project, but it feels like 1-2 years worth of work left, if not more.  If you're morbidly curious about the game, I can't stop you from making this purchase, but as stated above, I simply cannot recommend this right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly the game is good. The art style and setting are awesome, exploration is next level, and combat is decent. It introduces a bunch of unique takes on the souls-like formula in ways that work together. Keep in mind that it's an indie title made by a very small team, and it is only $30US.There is some jank here, don't come in expecting a highly polished Dark Souls like experience. Movement IS floaty but not so much it's unplayable, give it an hour or so and you get used to it. Controller support is not great, but they are working on it and it honestly plays fine on KBM. There are a few bugs at times and rag-doll physics weirdness, but again nothing that breaks the experience.Combat is very different than Dark Souls or ER, there are no i-frames, positioning yourself to avoid the hit box is important. You can't swing wildly, it has a "combo" system similar to the first witcher game, time your next attack input right and your attack speed is boosted and stamina cost reduced, time it badly and you swing slowly and will get whacked. There is no leveling up, no exp to gain so nothing to really loose when you die, so don't be overly afraid of death. Character progression is done via your gear and equipment, with gems etc. being used to boost your stats and define what your build is.All in all it is a fun game in an amazing dark techno-knight setting with a huge emphasis on exploring the world around you. I would definitely recommend it, nothing here is "unplayable" as some put it, people seem to think that if the game doesn't play/feel JUST like Dark Souls or ER or something that automatically means it is bad, keep yourself open to the potential of a new experience and I don't think this will let you down.

_childDocuments_.review: I still feel frustrated playing this game filled with bugs. I understand that it's a 3-man team, but that does not give the excuse that the game is in this state. They had all of the time in the world to polish it, yet they have decided to release it raw. I don't care if it's made by 1 person, or a 1000 person team, I expect quality content for the things I buy, and this is not it. I won't refund this game because I want to support the devs into making this game great. For now, here are the list of bugs and jankiness I've encountered in the 2nd time playing:- Terrible UI/UX. One prime example is the inventory menu. I have to press the select button on my gamepad to enter it, but the only way to exit the inventory is to press the start button? This makes absolute no sense and very infuriating- After dying to the first boss, the boss fight immediately started again. When I respawned, I was softlocked out of the arena, which forced me to kill my character- Way too many dang ladders that take minutes to climb. Why not just implement elevators or teleporation devices- One of the first boss' moves had frame cuts, which makes it look like I was watching a powerpoint presentation - Terrible enemy lock-on system. Once an enemy is locked on, the camera only changes horizontally, not vertically. So if an enemy jumps up in the air while locked on, I can't see where they are until they fall back. Plus, if you have multiple enemies, there is no way to quick lock-on to another enemy like in Souls games. You'd have to exit lockon and reenter it- Rolling gives no I-frames. If that's intentional, then there's no reason to have rolling since there's already dashingI was really excited for this game, but man I am very disappointed. Within my first 30 minutes of playtime, I've encountered many bugs and jankiness  - Gamepad controls work fine for me despite other complaints about it; however, the menu buttons resemble the keyboard buttons (ESC, ENTER, etc), not my Xbone controller (X, B, Select, etc), despite in my settings that they were set to the Xbone's- Character movement is way too sensitive. When I am platforming and would go a certain direction, my character would zoom that direction, causing me to fall off the cliff- Missing sound effects for attacks. An enemy I was fighting did an earthbending attack, but no sound was played- Lots of awkward camera placement. An example is running up a steep staircase, but the camera is positioned at my character's legs - Most of the controls on the gamepad have missing bindings- Sometimes the character model in the inventory menu can be way too zoomed in, and other times it isn'tI will continue playing this game and will update this review as I go on, but this game should have more development time. Dodging doesn't provide I-frames nor does it cover a good distance, some enemies have movesets that are easy to walk around but others feel copied from other souls types which rely on I-frames which this game doesn't have. The traitor boss has some spin attacks that I found fun to jump over, yet the later rotations of the spin are too high to jump over. Enemy movesets should've been planned around the no I-frame dodges and parries, rather than darksouls with no I-frames.The game would've been better without climbing on large enemies backs. After climbing an enemies back there's nothing to do but spam left click and jump off before the invisible timer decides it's time for you to die. I feel forced to use this mechanic by the pathetic damage done when not climbing. At least give the players the OPTION to damage enemies without climbing them.Honestly the only good things about this game is the scenery (minus the bland tunnels, atleast make them feel like a sewer or something) and the price is only 30 dollars. Part of the reason I'm giving a positive review is all the negative reviews the game is getting, but I can't say I really disagree with the negatives.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello to everyone that reads reviews, I'm gonna keep this brief as possible for my review but touch up with points about what's good and bad about this game. For the brief portion this game has A LOT of jank and doesn't help when you face certain enemies (spoilers when I reach the bad portion of this game as I will cover certain enemies that spawn in mid-late game). With that being said lets go over the main review starting with the good!What is good with Bleak Faith: Forsaken?-Weapon and Armor DesignThe equipment you find in this game is absolutely fantastic and unique to the game, lots of armor you will find will be off the enemies you kill. Late game enemies will drop higher level weapons and armor (Take this with a grain of salt though as there is also something negative about this aspect as well).-World and graphicsThe world of Bleak Faith: Forsaken is gorgeous at least if you like dark gritty techno structure. I have found other areas as well that go against this design style however in terms of most of the area's you encounter especially in the beginning of the game you will be surrounded by buildings and grey to black surroundings. -CombatWith that being said that is it about the good, now we move on to what could be improved! This is pretty much whats bad about the game currently. I won't go over on how to improve it as I doubt the developers have the time to read all the steam review on there game currently. Warning! There is a lot that could use it!Improvements-HealingHealing in this game is reminiscent to that of bloodborne, however, when you start the game you have only two! yes two! healing items until you get an upgrade for the healing items that requires you to kill a boss first which makes it to where it is required to have this perk unlocked which makes builds that are constitution heavy at a huge weakness as you get very little healing that heals you for very little to begin with until you get this upgrade.-Stats and character improvementCurrently in the game your only way of improving your build is to upgrade your armor and then slot a stat increasing item. Whats wrong with this is the fact that the items that you acquire to slot into your armor to increase its stats is difficult to acquire even after killing ~5 bosses I'm still only getting +1 stat increasing items. From what I have been told by other players is that you need to acquire crafting recipes to gain these upgraded stat increasing items. What's wrong with this is that to gain the stat increasing items you need to kill random enemies out in the world and not the bosses themselves! This basically handicaps the player till they find the specific enemy that they have to kill to gain the ability to upgrade the stat increasing items! With that being said this gets even worse when you complete a certain objective in the game and it spawns mini-boss type enemies that are now all over the place that chunk health even if you are wearing heavy armor and also drink a potion and they also take very little damage! YAY! -ExplorationThe exploration in the world of Bleak Faith: Forsaken is to say at least terrible. You have no map and the open world is HUGE! (That's what she said, haha) with no map for showing what you the player have already explored you can easily get lost and not find where you need to go and do. This gets even more convoluted when you have to fight certain bosses to progress and all of a sudden you reach a boss that you don't have to kill and end up dying multiple times to said boss and wasting time.That's all I have to say about the game currently I don't recommend playing the game currently until these core issues get fix and improve the player experience. However, if you do have the money and the game is on sale you should get it then as the game is still fun and challenging just know one wrong move and your entire experience can become more difficult without you even knowing about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Here are my first thoughts after the first two hours in the game. I will update it later once I played more hours, and after hopefully a first patch has been released.TLDR: Great world-design, game has lots of potential, but bugs and lack of good controller support are lowering the good experience I had. Feels like an early access game right now, but with huge potential.POSITIVE:- The world: After discovering some shortcuts leading back to areas you have visited an hour ago, it felt like Dark Souls again. Super world design, great atmosphere. The biggest pro of the game currently.- Nice ambient music, fits very well to the overall scheme of the game.- Good first boss, I hope there's more of good bosses later. - Fair price with €26 currently, especially if they fix the issues (see below).NEUTRAL:- The gameplay needs polishing, it just doesn't feel good. The hit feedback needs to be better, and the camera sometimes is too buggy and doesn't stay on the locked enemy.- Can't say anything on the story so far, as I haven't found one as of now.- No iframes, it's harder to impossible to dodge attacks, but it might be that I just need to learn it better.NEGATIVE:- It's hard to believe that there is no perfect controller support, as 90% of all soulslike gamers typically use one. If they'd have perfect controller support but wanky keyboard+mouse, I guess the number of complaints would be way less. I got it to work somehow after some 20-ish minutes, but it still feels not as it should.- While I didn't have any crashes or major issues, there are a lot of minor and medium bugs in there. Some examples: 1. At some point in time all enemies became hollows which couldn't hit me and which I couldn't hit and I needed to restart. 2. I can't use an elevator as I am glitching through it. 3. Enemies are sometimes stuck in walls. 4. Some walls in general are incorrect, only parts are loaded and I can see through them, although it looks like I would fall through them but actually I don't. 5. The lock-on camera in fights sometimes stops moving, and I have to move it manually. 6. While walking over a bridge, the scene immediately turned almost black for a few seconds, and then was illuminated again. Same applies to the inventory, sometimes my character is just pure black and I can't see the equipment I am wearing.- The inventory and character menu is very uncomfortable to use and looks like an Excel table, this should be optimized big time.- Please implement that you can slip down ladders, especially as yours are so long.I will not refund the game as I believe at some point in time it will be a good game, but it might take some months. Hopefully with the funds the 3 developers get now they can hire a few more people to polish it. It would have been better to release it as early access first in my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an auteur piece, and one of the strongest ones at that. It couldn't have been done by a large team. It oozes creativity and more often than not feels like nothing else on the market. It is also janky as hell, UX is an afterthought and it asks the player to accept it's rules (interface, floaty controls, unique control scheme, early input combo system, no or almost no iframes, questionable collision detection...) or stop playing. This is the price you pay for concentrated goodness of the creative genius behind it.Bleak Faith's uniqueness reminds me of Scorn, but with a smaller team, smaller budget, and much less cutting on creative vision and playing safe. Hostile verticality, surreal environments and amazing music! It is unapologetically weird and hostile, and I love it. A three-man team making a 100-people team game, and not cutting any reasonable corners. We have rarely seen this type of mad ambition after the early 2000s. Not for everyone, but if you are looking for a fever dream come true - look no further.

_childDocuments_.review: Bleak Faith: Forsaken is an amalgamation of some of the most ambitious video games I've played.The developers have crafted a world that surpasses the inter-connectivity of Dark Souls 1 - the level design is arguably phenomenal with great expanses to explore and take in, as well as some of the best verticality I've encountered in a game.The color palette, while perhaps a bit limited when compared to other titles, works very well here, especially when accompanied by the moody soundtrack the game has. This, coupled with an art-style that reminded me of E.Y.E: Divine Cybermancy & Berserk to an extent, works to create one of the most atmospheric and visually unique open world games I've seen. Not since Stalker & E.Y.E have I been so enthralled by a game's setting.Expanding on the above, the graphics are hit or miss, but this greatly depends on the player. I for one prefer a great art-style that easily draws me & immerses me in the setting over graphical fidelity. And while I did find unfinished textures, especially when going beyond the scope of the explorable world - which can happen more often than one might think - I never felt that an asset or visual element was out of place. Everything that's there to gaze at & explore has been crafted with great care.After finishing the first level (the monastery area), I continued to be greatly incentivised to explore every corner, every building that I could - and the rewards for all this exploring did not disappoint. A complaint I have would be that it would sometimes be difficult to gauge what item or equipment piece I looted - as the log for newly acquired items is tightly showcased in the lower right corner of the screen. This is made worse when you're looting items in quick succession, as some some of the items picked up aren't highlighted properly by the log. Other than that - there's always something interesting to find by checking every nook & cranny.Narrative-wise, the game seems (at least to me) to heavily draw from the theme of causality that has so famously been explored in Berserk before. And similarly to both old & recent souls-games, Bleak Faith presents its narrative in a show don't tell fashion, but with a greater emphasis on the abstract nature of the omnistructure (the setting of the game) and the disheveled state of the world.None of the above would matter if the gampeplay wouldn't be good. To that end, I believe that what these three developers have achieved is nothing short of astounding. Barring glitches & bugs, Bleak Faith has a lot to offer gameplay-wise. The exploration is a joy, and never becomes a chore as the player is given what basically amounts to a mobile checkpoint item that you can place almost anywhere as long as there are no close enemies nearby; you reckon the mob/boss or platforming bit ahead will give you trouble? Simply throw that mobile checkpoint down and try to succeed to your heart's content.Combat itself is quite good, and has deeper mechanics than one might think at first sight. Different types of weapons have different weights to them and mobs react differently when hit by them. A blow from a short sword might be deflected by a shield, but throw a heavy attack with a two-hander embedded with weight essences & you'll either break their stance or send them flying back several feet. Beyond that, there are a significant number of weapons that have their own passive & active abilities, and I did not expect them to be as good or entertaining as they are. Even the bows have some really good actives that give the melee and stave weapons a run for their money.There is also quite a bit of customization, and though while most of it comes from your choice of equipment, there are also Perks that can be acquired after defeating game bosses; these give out some very interesting and arguably powerful feats, that greatly help in rounding out whatever character 'build' one might try to create.There's a lot to say here, and most of it is good, but if I were to compare the combat of Bleak Faith to other games, I would say that it is a combination of the combat systems one can find in the Gothic series & Severance: Blade of Darkness. If you liked the combat in those games, chances are you'll probably love the mechanics here as well. If however, you are more of a fan of the Souls-combat with its invulnerability frames, then this might disappoint you.I've heard that the controls for the controller are bad - I wouldn't know, as I've played on K&M, as I play all other games including every souls-like barring Demon Souls & Bloodborne. What I can say, however, is that the K&M controls are really good - and no I'm not bullshitting, to me the controls feel very smooth, especially after the recent pathches. Before the patches, I did have trouble when trying to move away from ledges by pressing A/left, as that would trigger my character to dash in the opposite direction - this did not happen if you had the weapon ready/drawn (any weapon). The parry system is well done, there's layers to it, and it's basically an improvement on every other parry system out there, barring Sekiro - although I think it's called deflection there.Length-wise, I've completed the game within 28 hours, however, I did not explore everything there was to explore, I believe I missed at least two optional areas. I'm keeping them for the next playthrough.Don't get me wrong, the game does have issues, mostly if you play with a controller (although I hear that's being focused on and being improved as well). You can also get lower frames from time to time, but mostly it's stable (locked for me at 90 fps), which is more than every other Souls game out there. Bear in mind, I've not had one single crash in almost 30 hours of playtime. Whenever I dropped frames, I would just alt+tab > alt+tab and that simply fixed it. As a tangent, the control scheme might not be everyone's cup of coffee, and by extension neither the combat mechanics presented. That said, for me it's different story - as it simply fits me like a glove. The developers seem to have a good grasp regarding the feedback received from the community & they are actively engaging with the player-base. They have already released a series of patches and hot-fixes throughout the weekend, that have greatly improved the game's presentation & mechanics. They seem to be sticking to their guns and want to further improve the product they have - which I greatly appreciate it.With all the above in mind, if like me you enjoy a show don't tell narrative presented in a very unique setting that oozes a bleak atmosphere, then you might just get immersed in Bleak Faith like I did. If like me you enjoy combat in the style of the Gothic games & Severance: Bladed of Darkness, then this game will provide the fix. It's not perfect, but it is incredibly ambitious and delivers on a multitude of levels.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Now 18hrs into the game, finally have to set it aside to sleep and eat. My conclusion so far remains the same -- the game feels great to play, I've gone through nearly a dozen different zones at this point, accumulated piles of equipment, decided on a build that I've customized and upgraded, and beaten several bosses, completed one of the primary milestones of the game, and worked my way through obscure areas to find hidden items. It's an enjoyable play that has had surprisingly few bugs. Quite frankly, the game has notably fewer bugs than most releases these days, and the initial fix for the controller issues was released after the devs spent 12 hours creating it right after the complaints started showing up. That tells you what you can expect for the future of this game -- diligent attention to the needs and wants of the community. My original review is mostly unchanged, so see below:I'd recommend reading this whole thing, but skip down to the CONCLUSION if you want a quick summary. I'll likely update this later on once I finish the game.There are a lot of people complaining about controls, so I'll address this first:This game does NOT play like a souls game. Positioning is important as you don't have i-frames from dodges, and attacks don't automatically chain -- it is a combo based system where timing your attacks actually matters, otherwise you'll end up wasting stamina on slow attacks instead of pulling of rewarding and effective combos.Blocking and parrying also matter, and I personally recommend (at least at first) keeping a sword/shield as one of your weapon sets (you can have 4 things equipped, with 2hand weapons taking up two slots).If you try to approach combat like this is yet another soulslike, you will have an awful time of it.I have had zero issues with KBM. The game feels responsive (when you're actually timing things right). You currently can't bind to mouse side buttons, however the devs are aware. Controller issues seem rife, however, the . So, if that is your concern, just wait a few days. By next week I expect those issues will be fixed.I touched on this before, but combat doesn't feel like dark souls. People forget that before the Souls games were around, ARPGs were still a thing. This game shares more with the ARPG genre than soulslikes, in my opinion. Timing combos and abilities to effortlessly cut through enemies is exceptionally rewarding and feels smooth and fun. Again, PAY ATTENTION TO POSITIONING. Hitboxes are quite precise (unlike Fromsoft), which means that where you stand matters a lot. The first hard enemy you encounter can be pulled to fight on stairs, which will make it much easier as some of his strikes will miss you if you're below him. Moving to the side slightly will often be enough to dodge attacks, while fully dodging backwards is also sometimes necessary.UPDATE: "Technomancy" (magic) and Archery both feel amazing. I'm running a fusion of both, and it's quite fun. For me, movement feels great. I can alternate inputs fast enough to jiggle around in place, tweak myself along narrow beams above a fall, and sidestep boss attacks with precision. Your movement is tied to the weight of the gear you have -- heavier gear means slower movement and shorter jumps/dodges. So far my only complaint is that you cannot adjust your trajectory while in the air from a jump, so be careful. Additionally having your weapons out vs sheathed will affect movement too. Climbing is rather Assassins' Creed -- not everything is climbable, and you'll need to use combination inputs to move up, down, sideways, etc. Just remember that "dropping down" doesn't mean climbing down, it means literally dropping. XDObviously I'm not that far in, but I have a few armor sets and weapons as well as got my first perk point after killing the boss. All my accessory slots are full as well. Aside from Perks, which you unlock using points you get from bosses, EVERYTHING is tied to gear. This means that starting out in the game you're not going to be as fast or capable as you will later with better gear. Unlike games like Elden Ring where stripping down to your undies can be the best option sometimes, that is NOT the case here. Gear matters. A lot.Definitely the strongest suit of the game, it's absolutely amazing. Visual and sound design are spot-on and second to none for this style. Honestly can't say enough about them so I'll just leave it with the fact they're breathtaking.THE CONTROLLER ISSUES ARE BEING FIXED BY THE DEVS AS WE SPEAK. They're aware and working on it. KBM feels great to me, but you have to not try to play this like a normal soulslike. I massive recommend the game for a fresh take on soulslike combat and design as well as simply AMAZING style and visuals, but if you have concerns with the controls, I recommend waiting about a week. They'll be fixed by that point.Lastly, I remember playing OG Demon Souls, and OG DS1 on PC. Those were games from an established studio with many existing titles to their name and still had a lot of jank. This is the first game by a 3 man team, and so far (*aside from controller issues) has less jank than those and feels better to play.

_childDocuments_.review: In a world where there are so many incredible experiences to be had, I look back and wonder why I gave Bleak Faith so much of my time. Although when it comes to this game, that question gives way to layers of even more layered questions, like why are the main areas sometimes indistinguishable from the out-of-bounds? Why does my character stay locked on to enemy's corpses? Why can't I move my lock on between enemies during combat? Why does the parry mechanic only work 50% of the time? If the parry is so inconsistent, then why am I expected to evade enemy attacks with gaming's most pathetic dodge? Why are there instant death pitfalls in Uranopolis that hinder the enemies more than they do me? Why does the hilt of a bosses weapon hit as hard as the blade? Why are there so many interesting yet under baked mechanics present like the giant climbing? Why are so many of these mechanics either poorly explained to the player, or just not mentioned at all? Why does the Deluge exist? Why are there invisible floating men who damage me when I walk into them? Why is this game's music so good? Why is the world so interesting and the atmosphere so strong? Why is the combat sometimes fun despite the jank? Why are the levels sometimes incredibly well thought out, but other times are just long corridors filled with enemies? Why are there so many secrets to find? All of this, and more that I'm likely forgetting. As much as I tried to like it, I can't recommend this game, however I still think that what the devs achieved for what is presumably their first major project is actually extremely impressive. Unlike a lot of studios that would take a more conventional approach, Archangel Studios deserves praise for trying so many different things in one game, even if most of them didn't pan out in the end. Like I said, those questions from earlier have layers. Even in my criticisms of Bleak Faith, I can see what the intent might have been behind some of these design choices. Like the lack of i-frames on dodges makes evading a bosses' attacks more about positioning, rather than phasing through their swings. The swimming portion of the Deluge can be tense, leaving you feeling helpless because of how vulnerable your character is underwater. The unbelievably large areas make you feel small, and their lack of boundaries help sell the illusion that you're able to explore every corner of this fascinating world. All of this could have come through better if the game had spent more time in the oven. But speaking realistically, I think this game would have drastically benefited from a major decrease in scale, so that more focus could have been put on making the overall experience better.I hope that the devs don't take away the wrong message from this game's negative reception, but instead continue to experiment with not just this game, but whatever else they make in the future. Just hopefully with more polish. Ultimately Bleak Faith's highs are tremendous, but the same can be said for its lows.

_childDocuments_.review: coming from the likes of dark souls and eldenring, i have to say im disappointedControls are clunkyEnemies sometimes dont have hitboxes (although this seems to mean that they also cant hit you) combo system has no discernible timing to actually make use of it, dark souls and elden ring's combo system is better. having "points" to do combo sets with is honestly trash in comparison to being able to freely do movesets. you cant even practice move sets without a target. you'd think theyed atleast put practice dummies around if they were going to enforce this weird combo point system. certian loot pickups cant be interacted with.Climbing system doesnt actually exist, or atleast not yet.  Magic as far as I can tell is useless due to being so weak and the only real damage comes from melee, although magic from enemies hits 10-20x harder than magic available to the player. No I-frames when dodging, I can understand why this was a design choice but it was honestly a poor one. However there are random times where a hit SHOULD have landed while dodging but didn't according to the game's lack of I-frames. Similarly there are times a hit SHOULDN'T have landed being far out of range of the enemy's weapon but landed on you anyways.Certain concoctions wear off far faster than advertised. EX: a 90 second buff will wear off in 30 seconds. There doesn't seem to be any kind of leveling system or "soul" system, and no apperant death penalty either. From what I can tell your character progress is dependent entirely on finding new equipment.This could probably be a fun and interesting way to keep a challenge if the rest of the game wasn't so buggy. The only real work I can see in this game is the environment which i think is where the main brunt of the production time went. environment is beautiful, but thats about where my enjoyment ends.This game is not worth it full price, wait for patches, Or a sale.

But personally i dont mind what i encountered.The combat is rather slow and reminds me of old schools dark souls, maybe not everyones cup of tea but certainly not bad. Just expect it to be more tactical rather than relying on fast reflexes like sekiro or recently wolong.Here comes the jist of it.. If you can get behind these things just mentioned there really is a beautiful game here. And i mean that in a sense that it awaken a curiosity in me to always see whats around the next corner and the next corner and the next corner.The "omnistructure" is perfect for this. You get from pitch black tunnels, into something that resembles a train station, into a giant room filled with water, into a deep trench into a desert. All in one structure and all inter twined together. Right at the beginning you instantly get met with more paths to choose than you can go. The scope of everything is also something that contributes to the visuals. _childDocuments_.review: Incredible project by a three-person indie studio: BLAME! + Dark Souls 1For those who are concerned about "jank" -- it's miles better than Cyberpunk and plenty of other AAAs were at launch, and the devs are very actively fixing bugs, putting out sometimes multiple patches a day.I'm a Soulsborne vet who gets those old Dark Souls 1 vibes: getting lost and overwhelmed in a massive interconnected grimdark world, dying foolishly, and getting back up and persevering.  This doesn't play quite like a Souls game (e.g. there are no souls dropped on death, and no i-frames), but it has some nice additions to the formula (e.g. timing combo swings to use less stamina).If the videos get your attention, plunge down from the plank -- it's one of a kind.

_childDocuments_.review: Refunded because:1. NO good controller support, you pretty much have to play keyboard&mouse or the game plays pretty bad. Getting RSI in my left hand after an hour of subtle adjustments of WASD and doublepressing for dodge. If I knew controller isn't rly supported or intended, I wouldn't have bought this.To be clear, you CAN play with a controller, but there's something seriously wrong with movement using left stick. It's like the game is designed for movement in 8 directions, not the freedom you're used to on a controller's stick. The character trips over themselves and movement is erratic. Tried messing around with options but the devs just failed to design a good movement system...2. Movement and platforming feels pretty terrible, even on keyboard.Especially when jumping, there's something really janky with your momentum, tons of glitches that throw you off the edge. It feels more like a parody at times, a Goat Simulator, than a souls-like. Except you gotta run back to the same place after throwing yourself off a cliff.To put it in other words: imagine you're riding Torrent all the time. Has he ever thrown you off the cliff? Yeah. Now make it 3X worse and more janky and add glitchy jumping.I do challenge runs in Elden Ring for extra difficulty. I died more times accidentally throwing myself off the edge during this game's tutorial than I did fighting Malenia in my last challenge run. This dude just don't walk straight.3. Combat feels strangely disconnected.Enemy attacks sometimes look like they're clipping through me and not hitting, other times I take dmg when I didn't expect to. Not sure exactly what's wrong but it feels the opposite of clean, tight and responsive. Very disappointing, I was hoping to have a blast at release but this is way below my expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: For a long time, I have wished for one game to give me a similar feeling of wonder and discovery as my time with Dark Souls 1. For years I have searched, and as the market filled with countless soul's-likes, I was still unsatisfied. Because they strive to fulfill different criteria of what makes a soul's-like truly great in varying degrees. Except for a single Indie RPG. Bleak Faith: Forsaken.A unique soul's-like made by 3 developers. And one I feel has nearly enough to stand next to Fromsoftware's beloved Soul's games for an indie RPG. Yet, the recent release has been unjustly, unfairly, and unreasonably panned by many users on the web for bugs and an Epic controversy. The former has been hyperbolized beyond disbelief and gatekeeping, while the latter is a rabbit hole; I'm not going to discuss it here. Despite, these major claims, I sought to review the game based on its own merits upon release. This is my review of Bleak Faith: Forsaken after 34 hours. For full disclosure, I did not ask the developers for a review copy since I wanted to experience it with everyone.Primarily an open-world survival horror action third-person RPG. A cross between sci-fi and dark fantasy. A ‘Blame! By Tsutomu Nihei’ meets ‘Berserk by Kentaro Miura’ game. You will explore the omnistructure and discover the history behind this unforgiving world. Embrace the unknown and risk your life multiple times against powerful adversaries. That’s the main gist of what I can glean. And for the most part, it is pretty true in exploring the omnistructure. It does share similarities as a souls-like. However, there is enough content here to differentiate itself from being another soul's clone.You don't level conventionally in Bleak Faith. Instead, the game runs entirely based on the gear you find in the world and the equipment you earn from enemies. This is an interesting take on the gameplay formula since it eliminates the need to go to a stationary safe zone to allocate stats. Instead, it enforces a bold approach where players must venture to explore the Omnistructure. A vast world full of verticality with medium-large levels. And where some can quickly become lost in the sheer scale of wonder and discovery. In my experience, I was captivated by the level design and appreciated the environments of sci-fi megastructures to the mix of fantasy elements of technomancy. I became lost in the narrow corridors while searching for better loot and taking in the sheer scenery of places. At times, you will need a mental map of the levels you encounter. Nonetheless, sometimes your curiosity might lead you to find a great treasure or a hidden shortcut to unlock. I love your character abilities here and the perk system. They visually affect different playstyles to become extra powerful or subtly with stat upgrades. For example, I could pick the Vamprism perk, granting my character life steal. One perk: Increases the number of health potions on my belt, a passive chance to create illusions. Dual weapon & heavy weapon masteries to increase damage.For bosses. They are threatening and do a fantastic job of giving you a good bit of trouble. But, not to the point of being insurmountable to defeat. Simply upgrade gear and weapons, and have enough items on your belt to increase damage, armor rating, and etc. Help immensely to turn the tide of battle. And for the most part that was enough for me. Attackers are also varied and I did not see a lot of copy-paste here and there. The whole world evolves in a way I didn't expect as I progressed deeper into the game, making new foes appear.Speaking of epic. The soundtrack slaps. And I dearly want to buy the soundtrack A.S.A.P.Now then, as much as I want to go on praising what works effectively here. There are some things I must critique. And granted, the developers have already fixed the controls and Giant's bug. Two major complaints I had, were gone. During my playthrough. This is very satisfying to hear and quickly resolved too. Instead, I’ll focus on other matters. First. Inventory updates. Occasionally will not show what I acquired from an enemy or what item found. I had to check my inventory constantly and discover, “when did I get that item?” All items should pop up clearly. So I do not need to check my inventory and double-check.Minor to somewhat troublesome bugs. Compared to the exaggerated claims by some users online panning the release as unplayable due to the number of bugs. Quite frankly, I didn’t encounter that many. And when I did they were largely fixed by the re-spawn mechanic you have innately. You can spawn one nearby when there are no enemies. Nonetheless, I did experience falling off the map, not intentionally mind you two to four times, getting outside level boundaries two to three times, and collisions with the enemy where I am stuck to them about three to four times. These all occurred throughout my thirty-four-hour playthrough and one crash to the desktop. And suffice it to say I didn’t lose a major amount of progress either. Granted my playthrough could be different and I’ve seen different reviews from other reviewers who have played to end credits stating different experiences with bugs. So this could be a ‘your mileage might vary’ type of deal. Be that as it may, most reviews on Steam still have negative thumbs-down ratings. When the developers have already fixed a good number of those complaints regarding the controls, floating while jumping, and instant death from climbing giants. This is a gentle reminder to read other reviewers' impressions of the game who have played extensively. And provide clarity and logical reasoning. There is a clear difference between ten to twenty minutes of playtime to two hours or less and then compared to those who played five, ten, twenty plus hours. The next points I'll cover can be a hit or miss. Not a negative or a positive. All the same, I have decided to say here for transparency. To start, hitboxes can be a hit or miss. Sometimes the weapon I am using is just a tad bit short. Other times it is great when evading an enemy. Could be better.I wish there is a 'perk reset' button or drinking a unique consumable to revert perks. I made the mistake of clicking one perk thinking, "This will be good." Except it's not. And now I'm stuck with a perk for my whole playthrough. Granted, there was a warning attached of picking a perk being irreversible. So that's on me. Has jank when it was good. But also jank when it is bad. Yet, I still had a lot of fun throughout my playthrough and didn't reach a point of frustration to the degree I wanted to gatekeep this indie RPG for good. In several cases, I had jolly good laughs on some jank occurring. Some of which work in my favor!I wish there was more story here. Seems, the narrative can be vague at times. And while I appreciated the cutscenes greatly, more dialogue to explain some lore or more NPCs to flesh out the world-building could do wonders in immersing me further. And that’s it. My final score for Bleak Faith: Forsaken is an 8/10 So! If you are on the hunt, for an indie RPG souls-like in the vein of Dark Souls 1 just as I was. A mix of sci-fi and fantasy with a cross of Blame! & Berserk. And don't mind the occasional jank here and there. Then I recommend Bleak Faith: Forsaken. I have faith that the developers from Archangel Studios will come out with something great in store for us.

_childDocuments_.review: Of course Bleak Faith will have it's first release bugs, but even with that, four hours in and I might be a heretic but I like this more than Elden Ring to be honest. It really delivers on the bleak (in a good way). Bleak Faith was clearly a passion project, the foreboding music, the atmosphere, the armor and weapons have a grittiness to it. Even the burning fires have something that most games do not that make you want to stare at it [and take cool photos of your character with the embers and lens flare]. I actually feel small inside this massive omni-structure and it is kind of reminiscent of BLAME! manga. I cannot wait to get deeper into the game and experience more cutscenes and more of what this story has to offer. Game play wise it was mildly janky for me at first, as I was using a controller, but actually I now prefer to play it with keyboard and mouse now. It's much more intuitive than I think most of the Souls type games in the genre. I was initially worried about running across narrow passageways and plunging to my death due to the jank but upon moving to mouse and keyboard, only me accidentally hitting the roll button will do that now... or an enemy. I recommend if you are trying to play with controller to just move to mouse and keyboard.Overall for this game I give it a 9/10, and honestly with only a three man team working on this. A solid 10/10 as I know the team has some work ahead of them and will most likely get fixes in for bugs ASAP. This feels a lot like imagination manifested into a reality but in video game format and I wish many other AAA studios would take their time with their products like what was done by Archangel Studios.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly like this game, but I wouldn't recommend it to others unless they're Soul-like lover like me.The combat is really bad. Apparently the devs initially don't want rolling iframe (which is something they reverted later on?), so all enemies are built around this concept. As a result, enemies' attacks are very floaty and janky, their hitboxes are all over the place. Your attacks needed to be chained with proper timing, else you would lose out on stamina and damage output, which is a redundant mechanic. Build crafting is surprisingly fun, but held back by the lack of perk reset: you got all these cool looking weapons, armors, skills, etc... while also having a lot of upgrade mat, can even reset your attribute, but for some reasons you can't reset your perks - the thing that dictates your playstyle - so you can't really experiment with other builds once your build has come online.However the world is a joy to explore. I struggled to see its merit at first, but roaming around the Monastery a bit finally made me understand. This place, the Omnistructure, is a maze, its landscape is not supposed to make sense. I love that the world scale is so big, it drilled a sense of wonder and loneliness into me as I roamed through long bridges, enormous cities, sky high towers with nothing to accompany me other than a few sting rays, flying serpent, the amazing OSTs, the sound of rain drop, or my own foot steps. Speaking of serpent, riding on its back as it swam across the sky has been one of the most memorable experience in gaming for me. I can see it, and understand it - the devs visions when they made this game, and it makes me kind sad that they can't fully realize it due to the lack of manpower.So even though I dont recommend this game, I'm certainly eager to see what Archangel studio can do in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely mental, definitely a gem of a Souls-like that has its own character along with many nuances. It's Dark Souls meets Hellpoint meets Shadow of the Colossus if I had to make comparisons. The difficulty level is extremely high on this one, so brace yourself. Patience is key with this game. Giving into the jank and just letting things happen and fall into place is crucial. Love the visuals and atmosphere. That's the best part of the game. Combat can be janky sometimes and no i-frames, but for three devs, this is a massive accomplishment. Could probably use some balancing still and co-op, but I'm not complaining. Looks like co-op might be coming in the future? Stay tuned...

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent entry to the Souls-like genre and an easy recommend for any fans of it, with the single main caveat being combat and character control in general is less polished than would be ideal but the devs are still tweaking this in 3 recent patches. The immersive setting that draws you in, the huge breadth of content, the fast combat, the interesting build variety, and the constant progression as you find and enhance your gear make it a thoroughly engaging experience.  Being able to place your own save point in a limited fashion, an auto replenish-between-combat crafted consumables system, and PC optimized controls are all excellent additions to the genre.Read the full and follow  for more unbiased reviews by fans of the genres.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem. Almost 30 hours in (first couple zones)...taking it slow to explore and enjoy it. World design is stellar...artstyle, interconnectivity, shortcuts...music and atmosphere is mindblowing. Game doesnt hold your hand at all, throws you in and says gitgud, love it. Gear progression is awsome (its also the leveling system, you upgrade and socket your gear to increase attributes or get some cool mechanics, which creates some crazy build diversity).In terms of the genre, one could say it a soulslike...but its so much more then that, it has its own soul and bone.Combat is solid, magic/range/melee...if you spam attack you get fu***...you get slower attackspeed and much higher stam consumtion, so peeple who say combat is slow and clunky did not understand the combosystem (succsesfull combo is displayed in the leftdown corner of the hud with crossed swords icon)...timing is the way. Controlls are extremely snappy and responsive (you can cancel each action with other action) Game does NOT have I-frames, at all (dodges and rolls)...which implies that hitboxes must be razorsharp and they realy are, as far as i can tell.However, game lacks polishing...animations, collisions, AI can bugg out, stuck and clip in the walls, clunkiness is your companion so to speek. UI and controlls over it needs a good, loving overhaul...those things are not something devs cant fix and im sure they will...Highly recommend everyone to actualy play it for yourself...the price for the amount of content you get is more then adequate.

_childDocuments_.review: My first experience with the game was very negative, infuriating even, and it stemmed from the mind boggling design choice to not allow the respeccing of perks.I picked out perks that  good, but ultimately weren't and had no synergy.My best advice for anyone's first playthrough would be to find the staff in the zones before the first perk essence boss and picking the technomancy path, as it's much harder to mess up.Before playing I'd also recommend looking up what stats and armor values do and gearing and gemming up accordingly.It's one of those games that could benefit from a manual, but at least there's a good FAQ I saw somewhere on steam.It's a very rough-around-the-edges-kinda-indie-game, with a floaty feeling to movement and combat, with a lot of jank and numerous bugs, but for what it is, it has a surprising amount of depth and replay value.The atmosphere and soundtrack are on point for the majority of the game.It's now my favorite Serb-like.I'm slightly tipping towards recommending the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable although it's missing something I can't quite put my finger on.First of all I'd like to say THANK YOU for the devs pushing keyboard/mouse support first.  As someone who has played pretty much every souls-like game out there on KBM (including Bloodborne, yes there are ways to use KBM on consoles) it's so rare to see any support for KBM (queue the Wo Long disaster at launch) that a dev actually standing behind KBM for this type of game is just incredible.  Controller players, don't think you can't use KBM, you just need practice (and vice versa if I was ever forced to use a controller), but you can at least finely manipulate the camera and won't need heavy aim-assist to aim. Anywho, with that said the other parts of this game are terrific, but sort of not fully baked.Combat:  Another THANK YOU to the devs who did NOT implement iframes.  I never really understood iframes much myself, even after years of souls-like games.  You dodge and become invincible?  Yeah I get it, I'm trying to inject reality into games featuring dragons and magic.  But you get my point, WHY do you become invincible by dodging? It never really sat well with me, and is why I usually choose to block and parry in these types of games.  Which brings us to parry, unfortunately it doesn't work well.  The timing is just so ambiguous and doesn't seem to work most times, honestly I have more luck spamming the parry button than actually trying to time it.  Dodge isn't great either because of the lack of iframes, but that's good, you just have to learn to actually dodge backwards sometimes if there is a mid to low attack that does 360 degrees, which seems like a large part of attack patterns. Jumping over weapons also works.  But the best tool IMO is dashing, which is just like it sounds, a quick position change.  Devs for some reason decided to tie dash to dodge, one tap for dash, two taps for dodge.  This makes dodge even more useless. Anyhow the combat is very clunky due to these design decisions and in all honesty after you get some strength you are going to just 1-3 shot most non boss mobs anyway. Graphics:  Extremely nice, very well done with a really good variation of enemy types.  Level design is decent, although it struggles a bit creatively and the palette is pretty much grey and brown which might be a little too much even for grimdark lovers. Still, the level design has something missing that I can't put my finger on that makes it a tad more boring than a souls like game.  I think these guys just need to hire a good level designer when they get some more money in. Story: Well they ventured too deep into the "no story" of souls like games, but this didn't really bother me much.  For those who like lots of cutscenes, storytelling, plot twists, and scattered lore you ain't going to find it here.  But there are a LOT of shinies to keep you happy. Lastly: What's with the big to do about the "stolen" assets?  My God, who the F cares?  Every other post in the discussion forum is how a new asset like a sound effect or another animation was stolen.  Look there is a robot in the game, oh no they stole all their assets from Nier Automata.  Look there is a dragon in the game, they stole all their assets from Skryim. Please...Overall:  It's $25, much less than a good lapdance, what do you have to lose?  But please give it a chance as it starts to grow on you the more you play it.  Expect jank, although the devs have been super good at patching stuff the past few days, still there is a good amount of jank. Although not an excuse, three (3) freakin' guys made this game, that's just amazing and they deserve mad props. You'll notice that reviews over a few hours are generally much higher so try and filter out the ones which are less than 2 hours for sure, but even half a day isn't enough to bite into the good stuff of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Bitter sweet. I like this game, I really do, but it suffers from some REAL problems.First and foremost, it's impute on keyboard and controller are awful. Maybe it's a user error (and I'm willing to take those lumps) but for some reason, you cannot just select the impute you want, ESPECIALLY for game pad. The system just wont let me. Additionally, there is not option to impute held actions buttons/imputes. The game just assumes certain imputes are held like sprinting, instead of toggles. In fact, I can't say there is any toggle options except stealth, which is never held.This alone has left to so many frustrations when playing the game. Perhaps that's part of the "difficulty"? It's led to more frustration than fun. As a whole, I love this game. The concept and graphics are pretty good. Again, I suggest before you touch the gameplay, go to the settings. I would suggest this for any game before you play, but ESPECIALLY for this one, (see my comments above).Despite having controller input, it is not controller friendly. Good luck my controller gods, good luck.Love the idea, love the concept, love the atmosphere, and it is definitely worth the money... it's just difficult to play because of the impute. As you can tell, it is the only thing I cannot move past. It was a hard decision to decided to suggest the game due to this factor alone really, because it is so bad, it makes me not want to play it. Yes it is that bad. However, this is a problem I think can be easily fixed by the developers, so in the end, Thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: To start, since this is a big thing in this genre, if you *ONLY* like using a controller I would personally stay away from this game for now. Controller gameplay is HORRIBLY janky compared to (still janky) KBM.That said,  I cannot recommend it in its current state. Visually and mechanically the game is extremely janky and inconsistent. The jitter on yourself and the enemies around you completely throw off the flow of the game which is especially bad as the games combat system is based around combo timing which you already have to balance with dashing, dodging, blocking, parrying, etc. you may be able to imagine how getting a jitter where your character bounces an inch causing your attack not to swing could be bad. The UI is...okay-ish, its pretty clunky and a bit much to look at, especially the inventory screen. There is also a LOT of whiffing attacks as well as late hit registration, especially from the enemies. If you're on even a .5ft slope below the enemy, odds are 2/3 of their attacks will go right over your head. Also, don't bother using anything that isn't a boss weapon. The combo timer window on a boss weapon is 3x what it is on a basic weapon, they do like 5x the amount of damage, and come at base with special abilities. No reason to use a basic weapon.Edit 2: While playing more the games issues only become more and more prevalent and once you get to enemies that cast large elaborate spells you might as well say goodbye to all visibility. I figured the game wouldn't be perfect but didn't imagine it would be THIS unpolished. This feels more like a "proof of concept" tech demo than a game. I feel bad for the devs but I wouldn't spend any more than $10 on something like this. I truly hope I can come back to this in a year and have this review be completely wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: It looks great but plays like a badly modded Skyrim. Bad camera interpolation, floaty movement, buggy collisions, physics randomly deciding to throw you off cliffs, ds2 level hit boxes, etc. I am recommending it because I enjoy the janky combat and atmosphere, also because it has a small but very active development team who are constantly improving it. They have been pretty good about listening to their players thus far. Quick tip, like Witcher 2 rolls do not have iframes. It says so in the tutorial popups but apparently I can't read. Second tip, don't lock on. More often than not it just limits your options to evade.Update: They have already made vast improvements to the camera and movement, rolls now have i-frames, multiplayer support is in the works, and I can't seem to stop downloading this every few weeks to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: Janky as all hell with regards to almost every pillar of its gameplay, but somehow the passion behind this project shines through. The world itself is the star here, with enormous scale and bizarre architecture married to deep inter-connectivity (even if there are loading times between zones). Movement can be floaty but you can adjust to it, and combat is...well, it's functional and more than a little quirky (hope you enjoy getting rag-dolled into the literal shadow realm under the games map!). Gamepad support is there but the game feels like it was designed with M&KB as a priority which I feel is a misstep. Even as a majority M&KB user, I would never choose to use them for a soulslike.I've played in both normal and experimental branches (having a blast in coop despite the jank) and the game still needs a lot of work tbh. I hope the devs keep working to improve it but, honestly, the scale and ambition of what this small team has tried to accomplish almost guarantees a less than optimal result. I love it, though. It has a charm far exceeding bigger budget soulslikes such as Lords of the Fallen, and a far more interesting world to explore, even with the utterly impenetrable lore. This isn't Elden Ring, set your expectations appropriately and give this one a go if you like the look of it and can enjoy flawed yet intriguing games.

_childDocuments_.review: Refunded. Character movement is just too fast. It feels too slippery for a game that apparently tries to be deliberate with its combat system. Dodging and rolling don't feel good. You can easily underestimate their length and fall to your death. They just don't look good, and are even goofy at times.Who did decide to make the button to exit inventory be different from the button to enter it? It's a minor thing but still.Climbing/descending on both the walls and the stairs - janky as well. _childDocuments_.review: A rough sketch of a potentially good game.Dark Souls 1, but make it worse. A game that at its current state barely belongs on steam. Cautiously, I´d say Bleak Faith: Forsaken is a good 2 years in development away from being a playable game.A short, but by no means exhaustive list of things that need desperate fixing: - Proper controller support - barely playable with mouse & keyboard. Horrifying keybindings (CTRL+Left MB for a heavy attack? In the name of every game since 2001, let me just hold the button longer for a heavy attack!)- The AI is the equivalent of a toddler with a stick walking mildy angry towards you - no finesse, no "circling around each other in a sort of duel" like you´d see it in Dark Souls/Elden Ring, no punishing of mistakes, etc. etc.- Severe glitches & clipping of especially larger character models - get used to giants clipping through a brick wall, not that they would pose any sort of danger but you´ll be mildly surprised- The gameplay. Oh lord. Your character attacks excruciatingly slow & ruggish, no matter the weapon. If he hits more after the first hit, you may as well toss a coin. I´m aware that there is supposed to be a timing-system in place, but I certainly can not find one. Dodging has no I-Frames, which is okay if the hitboxes weren´t "somewhere between the edge of the blade and australia". The dash apparently has them - why there is a dash AND dodge with only one of which having I-Frames, I´ve no idea. Maybe the purpose was to have more variety in dancing around enemies with dashes and dodging the big blows. We´ll see when it´s finished. I´m aware that the developer team consists of a very small, but dedicated team. And that´s the sole reason that this game isn´t a "return immediately" case for me. Even with the current state of the game, it seems to be on a good path. Slap an "Early Access" Tag on it, drop the price to around 10 bucks & finish the damn thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: The game has changed a ton since I reviewed it, certainly for the better, so I'm updating it. This has always managed to be one of my favorite games, even when it was a bit more scuffed. Now, however, while there may be a tiny bit of jank present in certain scenarios, but it is largely a polished gem now. Furthermore, the devs are STILL active and plan to add more content to the game. The game now has i-frames, but you can use a special upgradeable amulet to restore it to the old positioning-based playstyle if you want, with some special benefits. Combat feels much more fluid, the combo system is even clearer and more refined, it even has running attacks now, and jump attacks may be added sometime in the future. The removal of parries and replacement with perfect blocks and counterattacks feels so much better and adds even more room for varying playstyles. The addition of a leveling system also adds much more build variety.The movement now feels tight and responsive rather than floaty and exaggerated. The world and enemy designs are super cool, and the soundtrack complements everything perfectly to make it an unforgettable experience. It has some of the best exploration out of any game I've played, with loads of pickup scattered around, lots of different gear, and even recently post-processing filters that totally change the vibe of the game and can make for some GORGEOUS screenshots.Please do yourself a favor and don't skip out on experiencing what this game has to offer.Original: It's a really fun game with a really unique setting. However, going into this expecting a Dark Souls clone or Dark Souls-like will probably leave you disappointed. Although there are some elements and inspirations from the Souls games, it plays nothing like them. It is very much its own game. It also plays and runs phenomenally well for being made by only 3 devs, especially now after the constant feedback driven updates the game has had since launch, with more on the way. You can tell it's a passion project in probably the best way possible. It may be hard to get used to at first, and although it's not perfect, the combat is fun and it controls quite smoothly on mouse and keyboard. Although controller play is supported, I would suggest using mouse and keyboard if possible as it just works super well. The level design is also fantastic. It's very similar to that of DS1 with a huge amount of interconnections and lots of rewards for exploring. There's a lot of different ways to play as well due to the perk system the game has and the freedom you get with choosing what stats you want as there is no level up system. Don't let the mixed reception fool you. The devs work incredibly fast and many patches have been released since launch, so the game has SIGNIFICANTLY improved compared to then with a lot of optimization fixes, bug fixes, collision fixes, balance changes, and more done to make it a better experience. The devs definitely deserve the support and you probably deserve a unique and fun experience.
