_childDocuments_.review: Bleak Faith: Forsaken is a strikingly original and immersive adventure that stands out in the crowded field of Souls-likes. From the moment you step into its dark, violent, and unexplored landscape, you are drawn into an intense journey.The originality of the game's universe is immediately apparent. It's captivating and mesmerizing, offering a lot of tension and a great sense of exploration. The world of Bleak Faith: Forsaken evokes the dystopian and twisted essence of Tsutomu Nihei's masterpiece "BLAME!". This influence is evident in the game's architectural design and atmosphere, which convey a sense of endless, enigmatic structures filled with hidden dangers.Beyond its setup and great art direction, the interconnectivity of the level design is very rewarding, creating a cohesive world where every path leads to new discoveries.The depth of the narrative is another strong point. The story unfolds gradually; it’s a minimalist narrative that doesn’t tell a linear story but invites you to piece it together through deduction, exploration, dialogue, and environmental storytelling, which greatly enhances the immersion.Archangel Studios provides constant support for their game with impressive updates. However, there is still room for improvement: at times, the camera doesn't keep up during boss fights. The controls are a bit slippery, and combat feels a bit floaty. I also find that we experience some friction with the environment, especially in narrow spaces, where our character could instead slide against surfaces and continue moving smoothly.Well worth the dive, Bleak Faith: Forsaken is a gigantic achievement by a very small team. A great game indeed! I'm very much looking forward to what comes next! I hope Archangel Studios will carry on with their vision. Kudos!/!\ Bleak Faith: Forsaken is playable on Steam Deck and has controller support <3. "GOLD" on ProtonDB.

_childDocuments_.review: This game wasnt ready for full release or even early access!I get that its only 3 devs but, here are some of the many issues:- It has the option to use a controller but it is not very well set up, pretty much unusable (there have been fixes but when I checked recent gameplay it still looks to "work" the same)- I continued with keyboard and mouse, I recommend checking the settings and making some changes in order to have all controls bound to proper keys (did someone make default controls this way because they wanted to be different from similar games??)-There actually have been some updates but the character continues to look incredibly janky and the animations are incredibly messy and broken.- The combat... the game told me about a combosystem, even with proper keyprompts (because I switched to mouse and keyboard) I tried and failed to find the rhythm. Its either a bug or bad design choices, there doesnt seem to be an indicator of some sort! Even with full stamina my character would not chain attacks together and would just stand there doing nothing, it might be a bug.- Combat doesnt seem fluid enough to fight anything, you dont actually dodge only move a few meters therefore avoiding attacks becomes impossible in close range against wild swinging enemies, blocking will result in you having no stamina. I am a veteran in similar games and find this very frustrating. I dont mind the approach to no i-frames on dodge but this isnt working. Also I dont think there are running attacks or jumping attacks, oh and enemy and your own attacks dont connect at times, a lot actually. Checking recent gameplay videos I can confirm there is nothing...- When you are hit while climbing a ladder you glitch through it and fall to your death, same happens while fighting on slopes and stairs during attackanimations, same with elevators...- You can get stuck on enemies and the ground (?) literally on nothing.- The inventory UI is ugly as hell and I need to check if there is an option to have bigger text... also pickup notifications need to stay longer on screen and have bigger text as well...- The physics in this game are glitchy, you can get flung into the air when a larger enemy dies ontop of you, you die from falling.- The stamina-system is utter garbage, it takes forever to start regenerating and when it does its green and has to regenerate again in order to fill up for real... what design choice is that???? This is unintuitive and feels like its just there to add a fake layer of difficulty to the game.- Level design is non existent, no art direction. Just random buildings, platforms, ladders and pipes strung together. There are massive empty areas, with sometimes one regular enemy in it. Others have said it feels like you went out of bounds. This is awful. Check on YouTube if you dont believe it, and check the updates to this game in case they actually remade the areas! Right now its horrendous.- Enemy design is random, there is not a system there. Nothing makes sense. Some designs remind very much of Dark Souls enemies, like the floating angels or 4 Kings. I feel like they didnt simply draw inspiration from the games, but look at the animations issue:- There is evidence that there are potentially stolen assets in the game. Thanks to the people in the discussion forums that posted about it.Of course it is possible that its Epic that have illegally obtained assets on their store, as it happened before... the devs have adressed the issue and have said that they will make new assets even if Epic investigates it and it comes out as not stolen. Good job on that devs!- This game is lacking any direction and is just a mess. The combat system, which is the most important thing in these type of games, is incredibly floaty, messy, lacking in indicators and unfinished. _childDocuments_.review: Dark Souls 1 but slavic and janky as hell    (note: Ive played 10 hours on a pirated copy before I got it on steam, that's how im able to write a such review despite having only 2 hours of play time on steam)    The art direction and and the soundtrack are great at making The Omnistructure awe-inspiring with it's size, while still having that sort of beauty that only abondoned commie blocks have. I can't remember the last time a game has made me feel so much with it's music and environment alone.   The level design is typical dark souls connected paths that circle into each other, but on a much larger scale. If you see a building in the distance, in dark souls or any other game it's likely just a part of the scenery, but here, you most likely can go there. The hub area, the firelink shrine equivalent of this game, took me 3 hours to explore alone. Though the reused assets copied all over the place and lack of big landmarks in some areas makes it easy to get lost, especially in the city below the hub area.   The combat is a bit weird, the dodges don't have iframes, so you have to use them to reposition away from enemy attacks, instead of dodge rolling into them like you would in dark souls. At first I thought it was a strange design choice, but it quickly grew on me. Now the combat is more about actually dodging the attacks, or not being where they'll hit in the first place. As for the downsides: the game is very buggy, you'll notice it often enough that you'll ask yourself "is this a bug, or a feature?". Enemies spawn before your eyes, get stuck on geometry, and thier ragdolls sometimes jump or glitch out. The lighting is sometimes too bright or too dark and the framerate massively drops in some places. The giant climbing mechanic that is needed to defeat giant enemies is extremly janky, so its better to avoid fighting giants altogether.Despite it's thechnical problems, this game is still worth playing for its combat and art direction. I think it's likely going to become a cult classic.

_childDocuments_.review: Its just not ready yet. A game that clearly takes so much inspiration from the Souls series needs to provide a fluid/responsive gameplay loop and this game very much fails in that regard. There's little to no weight behind any movements, despite how slow your character attacks, the parry system is very finicky (sometimes you'll parry when you want to, sometimes the character will just stand there and take the hit), and the movement feels too fast and floaty, not to mention all of the enemies in the starting area will be fully unable to damage you if you're on a slope below them. The size of the team doesn't excuse the lack of quality here as there are many other games designed by 3 or fewer people that really stick the landing on gameplay. Luckily it doesn't feel like bad design decisions were made as far as the gameplay is concerned, simply that enough time has not been spent bringing it to the quality this genre demands. My hope is that this game will be updated and improved and may be an awesome experience a few months from now, but as it stands I cannot recommend this to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: If you just want another soulslike, then I have the litmus test to communicate whether or not it'll actually be a good soulslike or yet another in a long list of uninspired amateur passion projects that don't understand dark souls's basic underlying mechanics and game design: The second enemy you face in the entire game is one of those "hides within an alley and ambushes you when you walk by" scenarios. THE SECOND ENEMY! How many times are the "I'm making my dream soulslike (please ignore the 400,000 other dream soulslikes)" game devs going to pull this? If you LIKE alleyway ambushes so much, just marry them and get a private room, where I don't have to look at you!That's not the biggest issue, however. This game isn't just unpolished or janky, it's straight-up unfinished. Maybe if y'all had *four* devs...or maybe *one* QA tester, then it might've turned out good.The game starts with a cutscene that goes on exactly 20% too long, shows the same imagery repeatedly, and doesn't tell us anything. Then, it cuts to a heavily laggy camera zoom in into the character, prompting you to start playing. The camera will dynamically zoom in and out during gameplay...for no real reason. You'll start sprinting and the camera will zoom *in*. That's the exact opposite direction it's supposed to go, if any zooming at all. Typically, a camera is supposed to just...stay put.That is, unless it's about to collide with the environment. However, in this game, the camera will just...clip into the environment willy-nilly. I'm kind of shocked. Guys - you just have to adjust the camera's "clip plane" in your game engine. This is really beginner level game development knowledge.Speaking of colliding with the environment - your character will sometimes sink into the geometry. I thought I went out of bounds or something, but no - I was on the right path, and half of my body was beneath a hill. In fact, the entire open world aspect of this game is a complete failure. I know that's a big claim for a guy who played half an hour and quit, but when your starter area has rocks that just...statically float off the edge of bridges (and *not* in an intentional creepy sci-fi way, in a "we put this rock decal on this bridge and didn't care that it overshot the model" way), and when a pathway that *looks* like a road to a secret just ends with...nothing...unless you like falling off an edge...and *this* is your starting pitch...then I'm not going to assume it gets better after hour twelve. The first two hours of your game should be the most triple A experience of all time - that's your refund window. Once you calculated the post-two hour mark, *then* you can get lazy with your level design.Doesn't help that it feels like the game has a stutter with *each* hit you land on an enemy. It very well might not actually have a framerate stutter when a hit lands, but it 100% feels like it.The game looks quite good. If you have it on ultra. Anything lower (semi-ultra, even), and it'll look like an even less inspired version of Mortal Shell. Thousands of different shades of gray, green, and brown, with a protagonist that has literally no visual cohesion with the environment. Tell me it's sci-fi all you want, but the protagonist doesn't look like *any* of the other enemies, or indeed the architecture, or even the same art style. It looks like something bought from an asset store with a visual glitch that makes the head glow oddly white compared to the rest of the body.Speaking of "bought from an asset store," you could apply that general vibe to a *lot* of the visuals here. Certainly the UI, which legitimately looks like a placeholder UI. The item slots for rings and amulets especially look like they bought artwork of rings and amulets from shutterstock or maybe commissioned it on deviant art without showing the artist any singular glimpse of the world's aesthetic or design.The introduction to the game doesn't tell you what each button does, save for rolling, jumping, attacking, and blocking. "Oh, that doesn't sound too bad." Riddle me this: you pick up an item. How do you get to your inventory? You can figure it out by experimenting, but a finished game would tutorialize it. "What, you need a tutorial to learn how to open the inventory?" Yes - because if you *don't* have a tutorial for something, and just expect people who play this game to be familiar with other soulslikes, you're essentially admitting to the audience: "Yeah, this is just another one. Nothing substantially different - the exact same gameplay." Even then, dark souls didn't have inventory bound to the "select" button.Which is where we get into the real rub: If you're going to copy dark souls 1, then you need to copy the base mechanics 1 to 1. I'm not talking about having the exact same combat - I'm talking about stuff like ensuring that you can *switch enemies* while locking on. This game doesn't allow that, which is stunning. If it *does*, then it might actually be tied to something in the options menu ("aiming sensitivity?") which you shouldn't be able to change.Terrible audio-visual communication, as well. You will not know when you're low on health, and you won't know how much a hit did to you. Terrible *audio*, really - this is a problem with a lot of soulslikes beyond DS1, even Elden Ring: there is basically no ambient noise. I don't know when we decided to stop adding that, but when my character's footsteps basically don't exist, and yet other enemies' footsteps can be heard from miles away, I'm thinking that maybe it's time for a change.Overall...this game has really interesting visuals in its trailer. And nobody can take that away from it. But when you actually play the game, it plays like someone took a free Unreal starter pack, inserted a free Unreal character model with rigging and animations, and wrapped the worst elements soulslikes around it. PS - your game has the worst name I've ever seen. "Bleak Faith: Forsaken." What kinda name is that? "Dark Thing: Dark Adjective." You couldn't just post on reddit and ask, "Hey, guys, this is my new soulslike game (please don't look at the other 400k etc), does this title sound completely stupid at all?" Boo, zero points, finish your game.

_childDocuments_.review: edit: game is good, one of my top favorites of this year, but boy it has a lot of problems. The devs have been very vigilant, so i know they can be fixed. Devs dropped 5-6 patches since launch, and have a patch in the works for today (3/14/23). I love the combat and its jankiness, the combo system in particular being incredibly addicting. the hits in the game are very satisfying, and i love the wide variety of weapons i have. i wish the collision physics were better, but they are improving them as we speak. some of the UI needs big improvements. i think the inventory needs a little bit more filters, especially one for individual pieces of armor (although i feel like that is in the game, i just cant find it for some reason). theorycrafters will have a ball with this game. creating builds is very fun and easy to do, since stats in the game tell you their caps and what they affect. i do think some improvements in explanations of certain skills and perks need to be addressed. other than that, the crafting system is very straightforward and you get crafting materials from enemies and loot drops on the ground. farming for materials is very easy once you know what enemies you have to kill. one thing i really want is a help/tutorial menu for the games systems and mechanics. i think that would help a lot of players learn the game, or at least have a reference for mechanics and systems they dont understand or forget how they work (for me included). i also think the game NEEDS a map. i do know how to get around myself really well at this point just because ive put over 40 hours into this game in my first playthrough, but even then i still get turned around sometimes, especially going into areas im not familiar with. i do enjoy the labyrinthine nature of the omnistructure, its actually one of the best aspects of the game, just need at least a local map to help traverse the many, many, many interconnected paths. overall, if youre interested in this game id say give it a try. if the bugs are too much for you, or you cant get a grasp of the mechanics because of the lack of polish, get a refund and tell the devs your thoughts. they work really hard on this game, and with their due diligence since launch with these constant patches, i cant knock them for dedication. they also addressed and swiftly corrected the mistakes that landed them in controversies, and the community was right for calling _childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to pretend that the game doesn't have it's issues, but I still think it's a very impressive feat considering how small the team is, and worth your time if you are interested in exploring a uniquely structured vertically-designed world of mystery and wonder, similar to Dark Souls 1.So here’s the long and short of Bleak Faith on Day 1, after playing for about 2 hours. - visually, the game is real neat. It has some pretty cool art direction and a vertically stacked interconnected design that evokes DS1 in many ways. - The world design and atmosphere alone builds a lot of intrigue, and I’m already very excited to get back to exploring it and uncovering it’s secrets.- Right off the rip there are many branching paths that often loop around on each other. - There’s also a ton of weapons and equipment which allows for a decent bit of build variety right off the bat. Enemy item drop rate is very high - with jumping, stealth and climbing, there seems to be a decent bit of ways to approach traversal and combat, which is cool - this game does not do a good job tutorializing its systems at all. It doesn’t have what I would classify a tutorial area. It just plops you into a world with 7 branching paths right off the bat and says go. There are tutorial pop ups and messages, but since many of them aren’t given with controller support in mind, they can be very confusing- The animations on attacks from the player character and the enemies look good, but they don’t feel good, at least not when playing on controller. - The camera is also all over the place, and it’s pretty easy to get stuck on some weird geometry, or to jump into a place where you just get stuck and have to die to return to. It’s very hard to know where you’re meant to go.- Camera movement is very sensitive on controller. I basically had to turn the sensitivity it all the way down. - It’s also worth noting that the default control scheme is pretty different from other Soulslikes, which can work against your muscle memory a bit, but isn’t inherently a negative. I also ended up remapping the jump button to a LB, and I would recommend just reading the button assignments in the menu before playing much, as the game won’t always tell you which buttons do what- It’s also very hard to know what surfaces are claimable and what aren’t, and the UI is a bit messy and unintuitivedon’t go in expecting something that plays exactly like Souls, or has the mechanical clarity or satisfying animations of one of the better soulslikes, but if you have some patience and can look past some jankyness, it’s a really interesting world that has intrigued me more than any other non-FromSoft Soulslike right out of the gate, and I’m excited to play more now that I have a better handle on the control scheme.It’s definitely a game that will appeal to those who appreciate exploring a beautiful/desolate but intriguing environment, more than it will appeal to those who appreciate soulslikes for their intricate combat mechanics imo. I think it's a very ambitious and impressive project made with a lot of passion and love from the small team at Archangel Studios, but I think it could definitely have used some more time in the oven before releasing in it's current state. That said, the Dev's seem very responsive and receptive to feedback, so here's hoping that the game gets some necessary patches and updates in the coming weeks to address some of the existing issues. If you have the patience to wade through the jank, I think you'll find a pretty unique and interesting game. If you prefer something with a bit more polish and clarity, I'd hold off for now.

_childDocuments_.review: Inspiration is a fleeting thing. The idea of something great might reside in the mind for a fraction of a second, and then be gone, lost amidst our daily routines and more perpetual, tangible things.  is the child of enduring Inspiration, the result of a thought process aimed at creating a very specific whole. It is majestic in its vision, glorious in scale and comes from a team of just three people - the Mastermind, the Builder & the Composer. I know these individuals, I understand their work ethic and admire their efforts. Most importantly, though, I am entranced by the world of this "game".As the lead designer told me during our interview (which you can find below), people can have expectations about the mechanics of a video game, but not about its world and lore - those are the products of a single intellect. How right he was... and how adamant have they been about it during the development and improvement of their work.  has gone through a lot of changes, but at its core, it is now the very best version of its original, undiluted self. I could go on and on about its merits, but I've already covered those in great length, both via my  &  with the studio lead. What I'd like you to take away from this short read though, is this: There are products that come out of a conveyor belt, pieces of media aimed at being consumed by as many people as possible to optimize earnings. This title, is not one of them. It is a labor of Love, aimed at the romantic gamer. It asks you to take in the sights and atmosphere, move past the mundane, and - especially now that it's been polished extensively - *feel* the journey, uninterrupted. It's flawed, like all our thoughts and creations... but in the grand scheme of things, and as its name implies,  is a foreboding trek up and down the Great Unknown. A unique offering, definitely worthy of your time and commitment. - FiOth

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to like this game. It has great atmosphere, good music. There is a lot going in the positives, except when you get to the actual gameplay.I understand as just three developers working on controller support might be hard, but it was not a pleasant experience to realize that playing with the controller would make it difficult, if not almost impossible to play. These sort of games typically feel best in controller (of course, just an opinion) but the bindings for keyboard weren't great either. I did NEED to use m/KB to beat the first boss. The stamina recovery system makes it feel like you need to be selective of your every input because even parrying will deplete stamina. Sometimes it feels after some attacks you almost feel "stuck" and dodging you will sometimes get stuck on in world obstacles (uneven stones)?Combat feels clunky because it feels even if you press the buttons with deisred timing, your character simply wont always attack the way you expect or dodge when you put the input in. For a "completely finished" game, i was surprised to feel like i was playing something in early access..I would be happy to revisit this title in the future if some major work was done to movement, but as it stands right now the combat just feels frustratingly broken to play with.

_childDocuments_.review: Hidden gem now, future classicIt may not have had the smoothest launch, but what it has transformed into (and still gets) is nothing short of awe-inspiring. It had big ambitions from the beginning on - despite of having such a small team - and it just continues delivering more and more.For me, the essence of this game is its atmosphere. From the very first step, it felt like someone finally made a good "Blame!" inspired game. The art style is absolutely stunning, like a dream-labyrinth and a very immersive experience. That is also because the level design is just damn good. Sometimes just walking/looking around and enjoying the artstyle...And then there's the music, a vital part of the experience. It is somewhat random, which track plays and one of the developer stated in an interview, that it is kind of intended to get some "random atmospheric situations" with this approach. I think it works very well and the music is just beautiful.Gameplay wise i have to say that it absolutley had its problems at launch, but meanwhile most of the problems got fixed. Except some enemies clipping in a wall here and there, it plays very smooth. Did not encounter anything really gamebreaking.And not to mention: it's fun to explore and fight in this world.In a world dominated by soul less (hehe) AAA titles, this game stands out for those searching for something different, crafted with love and passion by a small team with a big vision.I can absolutely recommend it to everyone who is willing to give this one a chance. It is different, non-generic, not for everyone and beautiful.

_childDocuments_.review: 'Bleak Faith: Forsaken' is an indie game with an incredible aesthetic, matched only by the ambition of its extremely talented and dedicated three-man dev team. Yes, it has souls-like elements but it isn't a 1:1 replica of the formula. Bleak Faith is attempting to innovate in some ways and there are those who will find those innovations jarring - the main example being the lack of i-frames. The devs have instead opted to favour distancing and timing over having i-frames, and an argument could be made to say that rolling into a swinging blade or explosion isn't realistic. It's hard to acclimate to this after having come off the back of Elden Ring; it's a decision I respect even though I'm not yet used to playing that way.The game is made on Unreal 4 so it won't match the AAA offerings that are built on space stations with a nigh limitless supply of disposal budget (and staff). That said, the aesthetic of the game is excellent, the music is on point, the ambience is top-tier, it runs smoothly and I haven't experienced any crashes, stutters, frame-rate drops or lag.Some of the negative comments have said that price point ($40AUD) is a warning sign that the game will be low quality. Have the blown-out prices for AAA games these days warped our thinking so much that we equate a game being over-priced as being an accurate reflection of its real worth? Keeping in mind that this game isn't releasing five different collector's edition, no microtransactions, no lootboxes, no bait-and-switch purchasable cosmetics that later will be swapped out for XP boosts and other pay-to-win trash. The pricing of this game in this global economy is very fair.There are some areas of the game where it's hard to extend the goodwill though; setting up your controller will take some time. They give you the option of turning Raw Input On/Off which in my case allowed me to fix any controller problems myself. Some of the complaints around using a controller seem to be more user error than anything else (like not reading the menu interface to see how jump works when mapped to sprint/dodge, or that you can still separate the buttons entirely if you prefer), but I'll be first to admit that the controller setup is not intuitive at first but they have still made it available and are looking to patch it straight away.The big issue I find, whether you're on controller or KBM, is the lack of inertia on your character. You move very quickly in the beginning because you have no equipped gear (movement is dependent on equipped weight on a sliding scale) and your character doesn't have sufficient inertia, so you turn on a dime and can shift direction much too quickly. This too is something that can be patched but the game has been out for 4 hours...give the guys some time.If you see the potential in this game and your first reflex is to refund it, it calls into question how honest indie devs are ever supposed to improve their product when their already constrained budget is constrained even further. The game is not perfect but it is still recommendable at this price and has a lot of potential. The things that *are* wrong with the game can be fixed: hitbox issues, floaty movement, controller responsiveness. The core elements like the vision, world, and gameplay are solid, and if they weren't there would be no fixing the game no matter how many patches were applied (i.e. games like Anthem). At least wait a week for them to work around the clock, which they have promised to do, and roll out a patch or two based on player feedback (again, something that indie devs have a hard time acquiring in beta because of limited budgets).It should also be mentioned that the controller (mostly gamepad, but to a lesser extent KBM) issues have largely been fixed. The customisation options now for how you configure either interface are off the charts now, and you have all the functionality of a KBM through your gamepad so long as you spend the time to set up your button config the way you want it. The team have been patching this game every 12-24 hours, only taking one break from patching over the weekend and even then, released two new patches as soon the weekend was over. They have also started injecting more means of comprehending the lore into the game world. They have sorted through hundreds of bugs and QOL matters already, it's unfair to compare it to the game it was a week ago when the early reviews were coming out. It's well worth a try again, and to those impatients types that refunded it after 20 minutes, they owe themselves and the devs a re-install of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I decided to wait until finishing the game before leaving a review, since I wanted to be absolutely thorough and sure on any critiques I might have. I have just done so, clocking in at around 25 hours (although I think it's safe to remove 1-2 hours due to stuff like food and toilet breaks). I like to break games down into 4 categories or parts that make up the whole: Design (the core approach to how the game was conceptualised and designed, which includes level design and gameplay concepts), Mechanics (how well the technical aspects of the game hold up), Writing (the story, dialogue and overall narrative qualities) and Atmosphere (visuals, sound, music and voice acting). The core design philosophy of Bleak Faith is very interesting and innovative, in my opinion. The combat is fairly straight forward for a Souls-like, with the addition of a combo system, but there are some really nice little differences in terms of skills, magic and archery that allow for more dynamic combat than I expected going into it. There's no "souls" analogue (a staple of the Souls-like genre), levels, dodge i-frames or bloodstains you need to pick up after dying. These differences alone would set this game apart from the ever-increasing list of formulaic games that have been multiplying in this genre, but there's even more to this game than that in the form of Outward-styled passive perks, crafting, swimming sections and climbing on various creatures and terrains. All of these combine together to create an experience unlike one I've experienced in a Souls-like to date and, while I believe some of these innovations weren't used to their fullest potential, I think the developers truly created a really unique gameplay experience that I hope will inspire others. This is, at the moment, one of the rougher aspects of the game. There are many bugs, glitches and collision issues that plague the game world, taking away from immersion and occasionally providing some frustration. The most noticeable of these is in the form of terrain collision, where enemies (particularly large ones) often clip into and glitch through walls and floors, but there's also some issues with weapon collision (for the enemies). However, these issues have been steadily addressed and many have been fixed over the course of my play time (I played it as soon as it released on the 10th of March and finished it 6 days later on the 16th). I have no doubt that after a few more patches, many of these issues with collision will no longer apply. As for the mechanics that work well, I think combat on the player's side works very well, if you can get used to the controls (I played on Mouse and Keyboard and have no experience using the controller). The combat relies on a combo system, where you have to input attacks at specific frames of the attack animations. For most weapons I found this to be at the end of the windup to a swing or as the weapon is in motion to attack (although faster weapons have their combo input at the moment they strike the enemy). In terms of other mechanics, there is crafting and, unlike many games, the consumables you craft or find in the world make a big difference in the gameplay feel. I would often save the more powerful buffs for bossfights. All in all, the mechanical aspects of this game are a little shaky still, but they are a lot better than they were and continue to improve.: I have played through the game after the last big Narrative Improvement update and the vast majority of mechanical problems from launch have been fixed. Movement is much smoother, collision is significantly improved and most glitches I found were generally benign and didn't affect my overall enjoyment. The combat has gone from being one of the worst I've experienced in a Souls-like to one of the best, being on par with games like Mortal Shell and The Surge in terms of weightiness and feel, while also having some fantastic skill implementations, reminiscent of games like Code Vein. If this is what the developers can accomplish after 2 weeks of patches, then I am excited to see what will happen after a couple of months.This is by far the worst aspect of Bleak Faith, in my opinion. In typical Souls-like fashion, the story is vague and fragmented, leaving the player to figure out what is going on for themselves. However, unlike most Souls-likes, which utilise environmental storytelling and item descriptions, this game has none of the typical methods of storytelling. The universe is implied to be rich, with lots of different creatures, hints at factions and forces at play that defy human comprehension, as well as characters that ooze personality; but none of it feels even remotely graspable by the player due to a complete lack of storytelling methods. This could be fixed with item descriptions or a glossary (or both), but until they implement these, the writing will be the weakest aspect of Bleak Faith. : In the most recent patch, they added lore notes, additional NPCs and some improvements to several cutscenes. I decided to replay from the beginning and see if these made a difference to my overall understanding or enjoyment of the narrative. Unfortunately the notes are random drops and rarely do anything to support the narrative (outside of 1 series of notes that give some very significant backstory to one of the bosses), but they are a step in the right direction and helped me understand more about the world of Bleak Faith (as well as provide a boost to the already incredible atmosphere). As for the new NPCs, I was slightly disappointed at how inconsequential they were, but their voice acting was fantastic and their dialogues helped flesh out the world a lot more, which ultimately served to make me feel even more immersed in the atmosphere. Finally there are the cutscene improvements, which honestly did greatly improve my understanding and, more importantly, my investment in the story. Overall, I think the patch succeeded in improving the narrative and writing, but I'd like more.This is, by far, the best and strongest aspect of Bleak Faith. The world's visual design is oppressive, gloomy and, yes, very bleak, with concrete structures climbing into a nebulous sky and giant pipes and tunnels leading into semi-submerged ruins. This is further increased by the phenomenal music that plays on loop throughout your time, which never gets old or feels out of place. Making my way through decrepit industrial ruins, wearing full plate armour and hearing a melancholy and sombre Gregorian chant never got old. The enemy design is often genuinely unsettling and creepy, with one of the absolute most disturbing enemy designs I've ever seen in a videogame. All this is further aided by really great sound design, such as the heavy footsteps of plated sabatons, the meaty squelch of flesh under metal and the loud clang of metal on metal. Finally there's the voice acting, albeit limited. Personally, I really enjoyed the few bits of dialogue I got to listen to, with none of the voices feeling like they didn't fit the characters or the world. It would have been nice to have more NPCs to talk to, but I really can't complain about what is currently there already. All in all, this game is nothing short of amazing, imo. The mechanics can be rough and there is practically no narrative experience, but that doesn't hold this game back too much, for me. The few narrative aspects that were there were highly evocative and almost gave me spiritual vibes, and the combat (when working properly) was very fun overall. All this made by 3 people with nothing but a passion for their craft is truly impressive and I hope they go very far in the gaming industry, making more stuff like this. Thank you for reading. I hope I haven't rambled too much and kept things fairly direct. If you get this amazing game, I truly hope you enjoy. Have a nice day!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely not for everyone, especially anyone going into it thinking it's a Souls-like, but it's much closer to a King's Field. Combat is relatively similar to other action RPGs, but the main draw of the game is obviously the exploration and boy does it double down on that.You will get lost, you will run in a big circle, and most of your wanderings will end up mostly giving you a different perspective on where you've been. Items are usually snuck into nooks and crannies, a lot being in places you probably wouldn't have looked since just about all the level geometry is interactable. Does it all have a purpose? Not always, but it doesn't hurt to check most of the time.Just remember going into this that it does have severe Eurojank and a pack of polish in a few QOL areas, but if you're experienced in said jank and can look past a couple hurdles, I'd recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: The exploration and atmosphere of the world are truly remarkable. Having delved into numerous 3D soulslike games, I found this one to be the closest in capturing FromSoftware's essence. From the outset, the desolate yet branching paths evoke a sense of wonder rarely seen in similar titles. While most soulslike games tend to mimic the Souls playstyle, this one distinguishes itself with its inspired worldbuilding and evocative ambiance.I was pleasantly surprised, particularly after encountering the Anomaly, to find that the final level was quite enjoyable. Many games falter in their concluding areas due to time or budget constraints, resulting in uninspired or overly lengthy sections. However, I was impressed by the perfect balance of length and layout in this final segment.While the combat system is fairly basic, I found it sufficiently engaging. The variety of weapon types, some with its own set of arts, adds distinct flavor to combat. Archery is simple yet effective, while magic could really use some additional development.The decision to make perks unchangeable feels unnecessarily restrictive. As someone who enjoys experimenting with different playstyles, I found it frustrating to be locked into specific perks. For instance, I have been maining a two-handed weapon, so I bought the heavy attack perk. Then I changed to Katanas, so I bought the Dual Wielding perk. Later on, I found the Scythe, and I finished the game with that, which made the Dual Wielding perk a complete waste of resources.The Anomaly "labyrinth" proved to be a tedious and pointless diversion. Its repetitive layout, lackluster rewards, and weak enemies made it feel more like an extended loading screen than a meaningful area of exploration.The boss encounters left much to be desired. Most bosses were either forgettable or downright frustrating. The mechanics of certain bosses, such as the Aberrant Knight and the Wormlord, felt uninspired and overly repetitive. Additionally, the final boss, while relatively easy, overstayed its welcome with an unnecessarily lengthy battle that bordered on tediousness.While the team really nailed the more restricted areas, big open ones were a chore to traverse. The Machinarium was the worst offender, but the Desert wasn't far behind.Despite its flaws, I thoroughly enjoyed exploring this game. Its captivating world and sense of wonder overshadow many of its shortcomings. However, improvements to the perk system, boss encounters, and level design could significantly enhance the overall experience.

_childDocuments_.review: To start off I bought this game twice. I bought it day one and refunded it because it was not clicking for me, and then I decided to give the game another fair shot. I enjoyed it a lot more when I came in with a different perspective and have a lot more respect for what the devs (only 3 people) were able to accomplish with this game.The Pros (so far):+ The world and atmosphere are unique and interesting.+ Interconnected world is fun to explore.+ The music is REALLY good and immerses you in the world.+ Enemies so far are pretty varied.+ Combat system is actually pretty enjoyable once you understand the controls.+ More depth then just I-frame dodge rolls and spamming light/heavy attacks like most AAA souls games.+ The ability to cancel attacks into block or dodge at anytime (your not locked in attack animations much at all).+ The keyboard controls are surprisingly responsive compared to similar games (it feels like an early 90s PC 3rd person action platformer, that was designed from the ground up for m/kb).+ Decent enemy hit feedback, with weighty ragdolls/death animations, dismemberment, and pretty good blood effects (its not on par with the surge series but its close).+ VERY good optimization/performance, no frame stutters (besides area transitions), no fps drops in combat, smooth 60fps gameplay...etc.The Mixed:+- the combat will NOT be for everyone. Its not as polished as other games of this type (understandably) and the combo system is more timing based and will feel unresponsive until you understand the systems. Its reminds me of games like gothic 2, or outward where if you don't understand the combat mechanics it will feel terrible.+- the UI is basic and kind of confusing at first. Its not a big deal for me but I know many will not like it too much.+- Movement sometimes feels weighty while other times feels floaty. I have killed myself 3-4 times because my character will roll OVER walls/barriers instead of along them.+- certain weapons have decent animations, while others look very janky (like the 1 handed running animation).+- The story/narrative is like darksouls where its mainly the world building/atmosphere/combat that keeps you going (it does not bother me too much).The Negatives (so far):- Some of the visual effects NEED to be toned down. The lighting effects from spells, fire, weapon sparks...etc are all too bright and look pretty bad, almost like bloom is jacked up to the max. I have not found any settings that lower the intensity of the effects.- Even though its been mentioned by the devs, you are not able to play above 60-90fps due to game physics breaking (like hitboxes completely failing...etc). This was actually what led me to my first refund, because I was playing at 120+fps and all animations were not working as intended.- Some enemies get stuck on the environment pretty easily, making some combat encounters less then ideal.- Some of the UI is unfinished. Like some of the videos that show you how the moves work have not been implemented (small things like this make the game feel less complete).Overall as a 3 man dev team this game is pretty impressive along with only costing 27-30USD. I would compare this game to other AA titles like Hellpoint, Mortal Shell, Ashen, Outward,...etc, but in many ways this game is more ambitious given the small team, and overall quality they were able to put out.If you have an open mind when trying new games, if you want a more "classic" darksouls experience (interconnect world and exploration), and if you don't mind learning/understanding a different combat system compared to similar "souls likes" then you may like this game quite a bit. If you are coming in expecting a AAA souls/elden ring killer your expectations are WAY out of line, and you will absolutely hate this game.It took me 2 purchases/attempts to fully appreciate what this game offers but I'm glad I gave it another chance because I have been enjoying it quite a bit. At the time of this review I only have about 4hrs in the game so maybe something later on make me do a 180 but what I have played so far is very promising with some small issues I would like addressed to make the experience even better.EDIT: After beating the game after 34 hours everything in this review still stands, it was an very fun and interesting game through and through

_childDocuments_.review: For a small team the scale is pretty phenomenal. There is a fairly good atmosphere of desolation as well. As you trudge through each area the newer areas seem to just keep you in awe at their spectacle.Update 7/8/2023Went through the game in it's entirely twice over (new game +). The game has seen significant improvements. The best thing being that you can skip ladders/elevators 90% of the time. The updates steadily improving the game. I still feel relatively the same with this game. My build was basically an intelligence/ability build. This build shreds the hell out of everything. You are a glass cannon, but I prefer that kind of play style. The combat overall to me still feels somewhat limited. The lack of a jump attack feels off to me, but that's just a minor gripe. I never felt the need at any point to adjust my strategy either. Once I put my build together it just worked, and it was "dodge until opening, use my abilities, repeat". All with feeling like I had a fairly limited move set.I tried out an agility and strength oriented build, but each one felt as though it just played out the same. The only difference were the animations and some of the ranges. You can build to get around the exceptional sluggishness of the heavy weapons, but to me, they really don't feel that fun.There are still quite a few bugs persisting, Possibly in the future with some more fine tuning and with the co-op multiplayer there may be a resurgence. I can't really say since I feel as though once I got through the game the first time, there wasn't enough offering for a second play through.  I will say the Skull Knight reference to Berserk had me pretty excited.This game has been a real labor of love and I came into it with an open mind. Initially I felt it needed a bit more time in the oven and I had gripes. Some just subjective and other I felt were valid.The devs really reworked a lot of systems and made steady improvements pretty much across the board. I personally appreciate that they added a more Souls Like leveling system (my own personal bias) and just fine tuned the combat animations and flow.Is the game completely new, not necessarily, is it in a very good spot now? I would argue yes. Looking back on my old review it reads fairly underhanded in terms of what I mentioned about getting it on sale. I would say the game is 100% worth the asking price. From the response the devs have had to the updates and overall attention to the game (which was greater than many larger developers).Good on you all for sticking with it.

In the tutorial it isnt mentioned that you have to craft them etc so i used them wastefully. _childDocuments_.review: Update after full playthrough: This is my full experience from day 1 to present time.I played BFF one day after release. I explored the first area for an hour and I was captivated by the world, the art direction, the scenery, the music, the atmosphere and the interconnectedness of the map were amazing, however mechanically it was wanky, janky, wonky, floaty and all the "-ty"-s you can think of. The actions were weirdly telegraphed and movement felt like I was gliding on water. I literally flew off the starting ledge at least 4 times with a simple tap of the left and right directions buttons both of Gamepad and KB&M.  Combat was kind of not working, Hits were passing through enemies and myself as well. There were glitches, enemies would clip through terrain. Parry block would not register etc. Great potential for a successful title but not in this state. Within 1 hour, I refunded the game.After refunding the game I could not get the world and that feel I got from walking around out of my head. I closely monitored the game and how the devs reacted to the waves of vitriol that came their way. I gotta say that for such a bitter launch they really did the best they could. They sorted out the constructive criticism and started working on the game around the clock in order to push out fixes and patches. For me that meant only one thing, Archangel Studios are in it to win it. They have the passion and will to continue and flesh out the game's potential, polish the mechanics, smooth out the rough edges and bring this home. RE-PURCHASED.The game as it is now is nothing like with what it was one week ago. The combat works much better. It is as they intended it to be. Weighty, with a commitment to every move you make and every hit you do feels deliberate. It has it flaws still like - inability to run sideways while your wep is out, no I-frames on dodge rolls, no designated button for the dodge roll /the dash and roll share the same input you have to tap twice to roll/. Due to these some fights /no spoilers/ do not work as intended. The enemy /a boss/ in this case throws so much projectiles and skills at you that you need the responsiveness and polish and fluidity of Sekiro to pull off the fight by methodically dodging and jumping around projectiles and fight melee with the enemy.  The movement and actions for the most part are very good now, it does not feel that you are gliding on water you dont fly off the map when you try to turn left or right overall it is getting better day by day.But enough about the mechanics, what about my experience with the world, how its built and the story, I can safely say that if you are a fan of Dark Souls 1 you will love the world - yes, it is far from the diversity of landscapes/looks/feel of areas present in  Dark Souls, but the world is tightly interconnected and really revolves around its own axis. You will get that sweet feeling of going back to Firelink from the Undead Churches elevator. Much like it the areas in BFF are connected in the same way, they really took their time to logically attach areas to one another. One think I did not like is that this game is really really not holding your hand. I am saying  that as a big big fan of From soft games. You may think that DS lacks direction but I disagree, you get enough tid-bits here are there to let you know where to go.  In BFF you don't get any hints about this at all. Yes, by giving you no directions the devs give us the freedom to explore because we will always find something even if we stray off the path - but that is not the case in BFF, more often than not there is nothing at the end of the branching path. As for variety and how the different portions of the game look, I will say this: Its an indie game and a lot of assets are re-used. Despite that the creative ability and vision shine through in areas like Uranopolis, Desert, Vermilion dimension, Rainy District, The Abyss /its actually an unnamed really dark area which connects a few others/. The Story - I give the story 4/10 not because its bad or anything, its because I really do not know what it is. I mostly give it a 4 because the story is not in the way /for the most part/ There are 2 particular things you need to do, to progress the game and they are not at all hinted at I found the first one by mistake and the 2nd one by mistake after a person in my chat told me to follow a particular thing. I mean I have an idea about what happened and I know that this is what they intended, but I feel that the NPC dialogue and cut scenes are really out there and are very open to interpretation. I liked one of the last cut-scenes and the visual story telling there which is followed by you going through different dimensions or like states of existence /not sure, again the story is really vague/.Overall, I had fun playing Bleak Faith Forsaken, I will definitely do a 2nd playthrough and hopefully a 3rd, Gotta try the different builds, you know. Despite its issues and indie janky-ness. The game is a fun time and I am sure that if a person who likes methodical, slower paced combat and action of Dark Souls 1 gives it a chance they are very likely to have a great time with it. However, if you are a fan of the polished, fluid, fast paced action of Elden Ring or Sekiro, maybe the game is not for you. Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: Greetings travelers of the Omnistructure.In this review, I'd like to write down my experience and opinions that I thus far had.But for everyone wanting a TL;DR:This game is great and can become fantastic with more time. Currently I'd say it's a rough gem but still a gem. I would wish for everyone to give this game a fair chance, maybe not now, but in the future.It's probably a niche game that can be quite empty at times and not everyone likes something like that.For everyone else:- The Art -A lot of story telling is conveyed through the general aesthetic and scale of this game and I find it to be inspired.It is wast, desolate and the epic scale, meaning everything is very exaggerated and making you feel small and insignificant in comparison. It is melancholic and there to make you reflect.Examples would be something like "Akira", "Ghost in the Shell" "E.Y.E Divine Cybermancy", "Kenshi" and "Shadow of the Colossus".It is being reflected in a rather muted color pallet. This helps make certain colors stand out more especially at the end and is very fitting for a urban derelict yet it needs to be mentioned because it is not for everybody.That being said, I can see how this might be a problem for some.It means longer than usual travel paths with nothing but the sight to take in. Vast buildings being empty inside without anything but your mortality to find in, are but a few things to mention.For me personally though it hit the right spot. I do not mind that exploration in itself is reward enough and I enjoyed looking through the emptiness that manifested outside of my own mind.It's like the moment right before the realisation kicks in that you're dreaming. Impossible architecture, familiar things warped into something slightly unreal..While I wouldn't say that they have created something new or groundbreaking with their designs, I'd still like to point out that everything has been made with a high level of competence.- Graphics -I'd say it's very solid. It doesn't go for hyper realism or tries to do so. It's probably more akin to upgraded Playstation 3 and I think this era is fair to point out.Timeless in a sense and I like it!- Level Design -It is fantastic. Every map is interwoven with another in some way so you have lots of options where you want to go and explore first! This is also very helpful in creating new characters and getting essential items quickly.That being said, it can be confusing at times. Since almost everything has a collision, you are already prone to explore where you are not supposed to, which adds not only more to the big spaces that already exist. But sometimes an unforunate death.While I would like this not being changed because I have a great deal fondness for exploring out of bounds stuff, I understand that this adds another level of frustration to some players.Yet it stays coherent and you can see it again being created with competence. I still have so many places to fall down from.- Soundscape and OST -Very much the same can be taken from "Art" and be said here.The music accents the scale and insignificance one can feel while being confronted by physics breaking structures that escape comprehension. It is there to make you feel melancholic and small and it excels in it. Very great ambience!General sound effect from abilities, combat, the sound you make while walking too is superb.Ofc. there are some minor inconsistencies.Something worth mentioning is the fact that the music playing in the zones is more a playlist than a proper ambient OST. So you can hear the start and ending of a track which either repeats itself again, or starts another track.The bosses on the other hand have all unique tracks and I do not yet tire to hear any of the zones or boss music.- Combat -Probably one of the most important part about the game and one of the most flawed ones.While it being generic to the genere, it is spiced up with the possibility to do combos, which basically means chaining attacks, blocks and parries with each other.This reminded me very much about the combat style of "The Witcher 1" with a mix of Soulslike.Some attack hit boxes being out for too long and ghost hitting you, sometimes a parry counts and sometimes not and so on.It is probably the biggest deal breaker for most people and I understand why. At the beginning it can feel stiff, the timing can feel off, enemies walking up just to turn around and hit the air, this can take one out of the flow.While being good enough, I hope improvements will be made here to make everything more intuitive and fluid.BECAUSE greatness sometimes shows through! I have a more fluid combat feel than Bloodborne in where I am just able to chain attacks into parries flawlessly and it just feel so good!This is why this hurts the most because you clearly see the light in there just to have something scuffed take it away and it shows the most in the bossfights.But in it's defence I have to state: It is very manageable. Not completely broken, not perfect.My hope is to see improvements being made here in the future.- Character developement -The game is going a more unique route. There are no levels and base stats are determined by gear.This enables a flexibility because you can just equip and try out whatever you want.Something very unique to the game is the "Perk System". After defeating a boss, you gain an Essence which can be used to skill a perk or upgrade an existing one!This can be many things: From Lifeleech, to block specialisation, making heavy armor more effective, etc.Each perks is usually a passive.Besides Perks, there are also Abilities. These are basically skills and you can have two of a total of 8 thus far.They can be "bought" through Ability-splinters that you find inside the game world and unlike perks, are interchangeable. As long as you have splinters that is.You can chose where and whenever you want to spend one or more such points.- Bugs and certain Animations -As to be expected from a new 3 man team, this game has it's rough edges. From aforementioned sliding enemies, speccing perks double to have only one benefit, they teleporting themselves into the void, you being grabbed with them, a bug where I wasn't able to target or being targeted, falling through collision, and many more things, there were only a small handfull of times where I was either stuck or died.The biggest bugs I encountered where the non target thingies, a memory leak, being stuck in a wall or big things grabbing me to take me with them into oblivion, nothing was truly game breaking. Usually restarting a game fixed the issue. In total that was like 4 times.Ohh and to it's credit I had in roughly 50 game hours one crash which was probably because of me. Hihi.The truly noteworthy thing here is the keyword "Animations".Because of a animations package they bought which contained stolen assets from other games due to no fault of their own, some of the jankyness can be explained by them using filler animations or downright deleting some because of that.I have to shout out their ability to not only react quickly to this but also having their game run without much troubles. I think they have handled the situation well and I as consumer had very little issues because of that.- Last Words -Thank you very much for reading my review. Please excuse my incoherent ramblings here and there, this is the first review I ever wrote.I hope you found this one informative and might help you to decide wether or not to buy this game.I cannot recommend this game to everyone, it is not too difficult but because of the rough edges. I wouldn't get it if you hate long travel paths and a clunky feeling combat system.That being said, I would like for everyone to give this game a proper chance because it is absolutely worth it.If this game slightly peaks your interest, please give it a try!But I whole heartely hope you do!

_childDocuments_.review: So far, it's definitely unpolished and needs more work, but Bleak Faith isn't too bad. Don't use a controller, controller binds aren't supported but there aren't too many controls so you don't have to reach across your keyboard just to switch items. The jumps feel fine, the dodges are nice. The movement and combat feel floaty at times, it would be helpful to have more natural movement and collision. The menus could be made prettier and more interactive looking. Mechanics such as attacks out of dodging would make combat more fluid, as well as better dodge detection because the roll didn't activate fairly often. The world looks huge and the visuals are impressive. I would start with improvements to the UI and menus and move into collision and audio design from there. The game itself however, for being made by 3 people, is pretty good so far. I can't wait to see the game be enhanced and improved. _childDocuments_.review: Man, I really, REALLY wanted to give this game a good review, but I just can't.Let me summarise my first hour of gameplay:First enemy stabbed me, and his sword was permanently stuck to my back (not in my back, just floating behind my back)Got stuck inside the first boss on four or five different occasions, forcing me to restart the gameMy health flasks randomly decided to disappear from my inventory, so that made the game significantly more annoying.First boss has a ground-slam attack that seems to be impossible to avoid. You can't block or parry it, it damages you no matter how far away you run, and dodging doesn't provide iframes. Combine that with the fact that the game randomly decided that I didn't deserve health flasks, and that made the first boss a nightmare. (Edit: turns out you can avoid this with a well-timed jump, but the other issues addressed here are very real)I decided to skip past the first boss and just parkour down to the following area. (and got stuck on terrain multiple times along the way). For some reason, this still triggered the bosses music and health bar, and he was still yelling at me while I was miles away from him.Found a ladder I decided to climb down, and I kid you not, it took me about two whole minutes to climb down it. Literally the longest ladder I have ever seen. Shift seemed to make me climb slightly faster, but there doesn't seem to be a slide mechanic like there is in Dark Souls. I'd wager at least 20% of my playtime was spent climbing up or down ladders.Also, the controller support isn't very good.I appreciate the fact that this was a passion project by 3 developers, and I'll admit, some of the gameplay is satisfying. Parry feels very good. And the world that they created feels very eerie and makes you want to explore it. Unfortunately, in this case, the negatives far outweigh the positives.EDIT: Isn't this about as close to copyright infringement you can get?

_childDocuments_.review: So, I beat the game. Honest 30+ hours of content, which you wish to be immersed in, and it devours you completely!Spectacular and authentic art design in a perfect tandem with ambient and sound design will thrust their roots deeply in your mind and grip it for a long time.Story is intriguing, exploration and discovering every bit of the plot are satisfying. There is a plenty of "free space" to interpret the aspects of it, which, IMO, makes a great deal for the game to expand the universe and lore.Technical state of the game is not perfect - perfection is non-existent, ever. I've never suffered from severe, game-crashing bugs, FPS drops and/or other bugs/glitches, except minor right on the release ("gliding" and "dislocated" enemies). Apart of the mentioned, the game is a solid technical product, which is CONSTANTLY being updated, becoming smoother and better with every patch.The conclusion I'll leave almost the same as it was at the very beginning of my journey to the game's world (except of the part about bugs - the game keeps improving, and the majority of them are fixed atm):If you like games rich in atmosphere, if you have an "exploration itch", if you value great art (both visual and sound/music) design - you are welcome to try the game and enjoy it!The devs made a great job, and they are willing to continue it, which is something rare these days, and I would like to thank them for it!I'm sure, the game will have it's dedicated fan-base, and if you dare to be one of the Forsaken - welcome to the Omnistructure!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I went into it with low expectation (having been following it since release) but decided to give it a shot after hearing about all the updates. And I'm happy to say that the game is fantastic. Is it super well polished and a very tight experience? Absolutely not. Is it immersive and fun as hell? 100%Things I like:Atmosphere/Art Direction: The most commonly praised aspect of the game is by far it's strongest part. The setting is thick with dystopian dread and makes you very curious to understand why the world is the way it is (I will get to the story in a bit tho). From the robot infested ruins of Upper Blocks to the barren, plague-ridden wasteland of the Desert, this game is never disappointing visually. This atmosphere is also greatly enhanced by the soundtrack.Combat: At first, I was very put off by the lack of invincibility frames when dodging attacks, meaning you have to dodge away from an attack instead of through it. However, enemies and bosses are designed with this in mind and combat actually flows pretty well. Mixing blocks, parries and dodges was very satisfying against the games later bosses and enemies. The combat isn't amazing or anything, but it feels good enough to me.Perk System: Another aspect I was weird-ed out by at first was the perk system. But after experimenting with it for a bit, I have to say that it very much adds to the build variety in this game. There are a hefty bunch of perks you can choose from, each changing your play-style in different ways. Overall, very well implemented mechanic.Voice Acting: I was actually quite surprised by the voice acting in this game. It will often range from decent to very good, with a couple stinkers here and there (through they are quite rare).Things I didn't like:Healing System: So this game made healing items consumables that don't replenish at checkpoints. On paper that's fine. The problem is that you have to craft potions from different items, which only certain enemies seem to drop. Meaning if you run out, you have to go farm for quite a while before you have more. Whats worse is that, no matter how many potions you have in your inventory, you can only have three active on your belt to use in combat, will three more being added to your belt after combat is over. This can be a massive headache with some bosses, because you could have twenty potions, but are only allowed to use three for the very long boss fight.Story: In most souls-like games, the story is told very in a very vague way and it's up to the player to piece it together via the little info you are given as well as NPC dialogue and item descriptions. Usually the player is given some info to ease them into the world and setting. In this game, you will start and end your playthrough without a single clue about what's going on. There is no lore item descriptions, and NPCs talk about stuff like you are already aware of what they are talking about. There are a few lore notes in the game, but the hardly explain anything about the world and overall conflict. When i'm playing this game, I am constantly asking questions like "Why is Upper Blocks dominated by robots?" or "Who is the Plagued Nemesis and why is he stuck in the Asylum?" and "What's up with Wormlord and the giant flying worm?" And let me tell you, not a single one of these questions will be answered at all throughout the entire game. I really don't like this decision and I think it takes away from the overall experience. It's okay to leave some things up to interpretation, but other things need to have some context otherwise they seem completely random.Overall, if the developers fix the issues with the story, this will probably end up as one of my favourite souls-like games. Aside from that though, the game is an excellent, very rough gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: This game somehow manages to remind me of NieR, Dark Souls, BLAME!, Dune, E.Y.E Divine Cybermancy, Shadow of The Colossus and Warhammer 40K all at once, and I didn't know how much I needed that until now. There is a lot of jank, but the solid fundamentals of the game are there, and the devs are already pushing out multiple patches a day, so i'm sure the game will polish up nicely. Worth getting now if you can look past a bit of bugginess and want to explore the Omnistructure.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

They devs (who are just 3 people, keep that in mind) have more polishing to do: the controllers and the character movement. Polish that and you have an incredible game, with a beautiful world.Can't wait until it is ready.

The movement/animations should be smoother.  When my character is walking, I feel like they are moving on ice.Also, please optimize the game for lower-end machines. _childDocuments_.review: As of right now this game still has quite a few bugs.  HOWEVER the dev team is 3 people and they are releasing patches everyday since release.  Its not ideal but they are patching it.The world of this game is special.  Unlike any game I have ever played and its amazing.  The combat is very different from Dark Souls.
