_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: Back when I first played this game, the combat and mechanics felt so off to me, it was clunky and non-responsive. Despite that, everything else is phenomenal, the atmosphere, the world aesthetic and design were all masterfully crafted. Oh boi, the exploration accompanied by the hauntingly beautiful soundtrack, provided an immersive experience that overshadowed any frustrations with the combat system. Made a revisit after one year and the combat is little bit more polished, the parries are satisfying as well, but it still needs some room for improvement.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those uncut gems that do a few things brilliantly, but still need quite some work to feel polished and complete.Pros: + Setting, art direction are very solid. It is an interesting amalgamation of classic sword&sorcery fantasy and post-apoc future.+ Sound design and musical score are easily the best in the genre. Devs responsible for this particular part should be immensely proud for they literally crafted a masterpiece.+ Combat foundation is great.Cons:- Introduction area is rather weird. It is incredibly big and there are many paths you can take, but it poorly introduces actual gameplay features. Unless I somehow missed explanations for core features such as Homunculus (function like bonfires in Dark Souls) and character progression, you get none and have to figure everything out on your own. - Clunky UI and animations. Parry animations in particular are wacky and work inconsistently.To summarise: I like what the game has to offer so far and understand the constraints that come from the limited budget and resources of a 3-man team. It is an incredible achievment actually. I hope that devs will be able to polish the game further.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: All I can say is that its a unique and enjoyable experience. The atmosphere and aesthetics of the game are truly one-of-a-kind, with an interesting combat system that requires some understanding of the combo system. While it's not exactly like Dark Souls, it still offers a fun and challenging experience.The game is a homage to the aesthetics of mangas like Blame! or Berserk, which fans of those series will surely appreciate. It also has a nostalgic feel to it, reminiscent of the Nintendo 64 and Playstation 1 era, which adds to its charm. At the same time, it feels like playing Demon's Souls from the first time, with its sense of mystery and dread that kept me engaged throughout the game.Additionally, the looting system, upgrades, crafting, and skills are surprisingly rewarding and interesting for a game made by just three developers. The world design is enormous and interconnected, with a really cool dark cyberpunk vibe. The exploration itself is rewarding, with interesting loot or horrifying creatures lurking around every corner.However, the game is a bit janky and may require some patience. I found that playing with keyboard and mouse made things a bit smoother, but the developers have promised to improve controller support in the future. Overall, I highly recommend it for anyone looking for a unique and nostalgic gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: Game design wise, Bleak Faith feels great. I mean in terms of mechanics, world design and artistic vision. That said, I feel that this being a full release is misleading. The developers are awesome and are constantly tending to the bugs and areas which lack polish right now. The level design in particular is phenomenal. The world and its design is ON-PAR with Dark Souls 1 easily. it's a wonder to explore artistically and layout wise.The combat has potential. it has fun mechanics, and a really nice blend of bloodborne style quick hops and rolls which blend really well together. The shadow of the colossus style climbing boss fights are really cool, and work well. I really do think that as a game, it's great. it just happens to be really rough with bugs janky camera and a lack of polish that you would reasonably expect from a 3 person team's first game. And the devs have stated that they'll support the game post-launch, polishing the game and adding features and content.I do recommend this game massively, but I also think right now, at 'launch', Bleak Faith Foresaken might not be up to the standards of polish we might expect from Fromsoft Souls games.Give this game some time and I swear it will be looked back upon very favourably.The devs really listen to the community. You can tell just by joining the discord.Think of its current state on march 10th 2023 as early access without the early access label if that helps.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: I don't review many games, but I feel compelled to explain my negative rating. As a whole, I did not dislike Bleak Faith. It has a God-tier atmosphere and some amazing music. The game truly feels bleak, living up to the namesake, but has some gorgeous views too. If I was rating this game from a conceptual level alone, I would absolutely recommend it. However, considering all facets of what makes a game worth recommending, I cannot advise anyone spend money on this yet. It has many bugs and graphical glitches, frame drops and stuttering, and the controls feel very floaty. I cannot count the number of times I wanted to jump 3ft forward towards a ledge and watched as my character plunged off a cliff at mach 5 instead. And this game has mandatory platforming, which makes it all the worse. It does have a lot of nice freedom of exploration, but the exploration isnt as fun when you feel like you are constantly walking on ice or clipping through ledges.The combat was fun, responsive, and included a combo system and lots of customization, but there were times it just didnt work. I had many instances where my character would stand still instead of switch weapons, which often led to a prompt and painful death. I also felt almost penalized for using certain weapons. Early game, I was rocking this massive greataxe that dropped from an enemy and was really enjoying it, but about mid-game the enemies all began moving very quickly, attacking rapidly, and taking massive chunks of my hp off. Meanwhile, my big sluggish axe would deal considerable damage back- but with little to no recoil or stagger. So for every 1 big axe hit I had, the enemy had 13 dozen katana cuts across my face. Eventually, I switched my build altogether to dual-wielding Kamas, and found it works a lot better when I can match the enemies pace. That was fine, and I ended up enjoying that build a lot, but I never felt comfortable trying out another heavy weapon again. Which is a shame because this game has some cool weapons and armors.Lastly, the story is...well, I have no idea. Even trying to piece it together carefully I still felt lost and unsure on who our character is, why we are here (other than because of THE ANOMALY), and why I should care. Some may say thats very in-line with the typical "soulslike experience" but this was to the next level. It was so bad I had no clue who the last boss even was really, and the game ended with me just horribly confused altogether. Tldr; This game has amazing atmosphere, fun combat, and a lot of potential...but just isnt ready yet. Too many bugs, too vague of a story, too many things that need improved or reworked. Maybe try in 6 months to a year from now. Could be sooner, since they did release two patches since I bought the game yesterday, which is promising.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: The controls leave something to be desired, for example the block and parry button are the same button, so if you press the button trying to parry, but press it just a little too long, you will instead briefly block. The movement is rather floaty, I found myself unexpectedly sliding off of things after a brief movement input. In the first area of the game, at a relatively short distance, enemies were already visible sliding around in their neutral position, as it seems their animations only kick in when you get closer. Overall, the game feels unfinished. I will keep an eye on this one as the world and atmosphere seem excellent, but I refunded as is, and for now I can't recommend this game. Thank you for coming to my TED Talk.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great. It is rough around the edges, but that is more than understandable when you consider that 3 people worked on it, starting with two. The devs are very active and have kept tabs on the community feedback in all of the years of development and are ready to address and adjust everything that it's brought to their attention. The controller system is fine, it can be improved and that is one thing that the devs have already addressed on Discord. The atmosphere is incredible and the combat system is fun. I honestly recommend people to try it for more than 10 minutes, remember that Steam allows up to 2 hours of gameplay before not giving the refund, use them.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks fantastic but what killed it for me were the controls. Not the button mapping, although that could certainly use some work, just the feel of moving around. Your character moves at the same speed regardless of direction, slope, or texture so you feel like you're floating instead of making contact with the ground. This led to several instances of falling to my death right when the game started. I'd love to change this review if the dev focuses on improving collision and physics but as it stands, I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: TL/DR Game is beautiful but has a lot of jank. Okay so I need start by saying I have been waiting for this game eagerly for 3ish years. That means my desire for this game to live up to the hype is fairly high. All that being said this game has issues. For starters the controller support is essentially up to the player to configure and figure out for yourself. I do like that they didn't completely force M+K controls on you but they put zero effort into mapping the controls out onto a Xbox style controller. So if you wanna play with a controller you gonna need to put 5 mins of effort into mapping the controls out in a way that feels smooth to you. I will say it is clear they put way more effort into M+K controls cause it plays extremely well without the controller. Game play is solid if you take the time to learn the combo system, you have zero Iframes which changes everything especially if you play a lot of Dark soul style games. But if you learn the spacing and take advantage of the very slow attack animations of the enemy's you will quickly realize you don't need the Iframes to win the fights. Leveling is tied to gear only meaning you want better stats you need to find better armor that buffs those stats. I really like this a lot, but I understand some people will hate this. But if you wanna change play styles on the fly this gear system makes this possible to do. Level design is excellent although I have only beaten the first area and the first boss I can say with confidence that they really put a decent effort into making the paths make sense and connect without feeling forced. it made me want to find all the different ways I could reach the end of the first area. To me that was exciting especially sense I found items I would of missed if I hadn't gone back and kept searching the untraveled paths. Also the art design is un real! This world is breath taking/ visual masterpiece that begs you to look at it. I can tell I am rambling so lets finish this up. This game is a passion project that has unfinished textures, unfinished controller support, and a somewhat janky combat system. But the core of the game is solid and it kept me locked to my computer for 2 hours. I only stopped cause I wanted to show my support for this game. If you are like me and you can't wait any longer to play this game then please jump in and show some love for it, but if you need a AAA experience with zero issues. Then put it on your wish-list and revisit this after 6 months and multiple patches. Cause I truly believe this game will be worth your time at some point.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: The world oozes atmosphere unlike anything else, both level design and music evoking feelings of awe at every turn. The voice acting of the few NPCs I have seen (including a boss) has been very good - it makes me thrilled for uncovering the rest of the plot.The controls take getting used to, in particular the timing of the attacks. Wrongly timed attacks are sluggish, take more stamina and leave you wide open to attacks. Combined with dodges without invincibility frames, this can lead to comically bad first fights where you keep eating attacks and being out of stamina in order to retaliate.Once I have gotten used to the system, though, the difficulty almost evaporated. Once you find good weapons and armor, the game because much more of a breeze - sometimes too much so. The magic in this game is very powerful and I have obliterated my first bosses through spamming my ranged staff attacks. (nerf magic maybe?)Overall, the combat is growing more and more on me. The range of weapons is amazing, and the enemies variety leads to interesting scenarios. I keep getting lost in every new hub in a good way, because it keeps blowing my mind with how strange every place looks and feels like.This game sits right behind Dark Souls 1 on the scala for me, mostly due to the strength of its world and the fun of the exploration. I don't care about the jank or glitches personally, it does nothing to detract from my enjoyment of the game.I will be updating my review as I go through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like that this game contains stolen assets and animations from Dragon's Dogma and the Souls-series. From enemies to bosses, and the player's own attack animations much is clearly taken from elsewhere. There are far too many exact copies of the same animations for it to just be 'some accident', especially if you've played those games. Crashes, loss of save data on quitting out of the game via the menu, animation bugs and more make it very difficult to enjoy the experience. And the goddawful explosion sounds while you stab the giant enemies. That is far too loud for anything, including the flashbang effect added on to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people are saying this game is bad to control and there are lots of issues. I want to say that while it definitely seems like this, especially at first, it is not as bad as people are saying. It takes A LOT of getting used to but after clearing out the first boss and areas leading to it, I have gotten used to the feel of the controls and it feels much better. It did however feel very jank when I first started. That aside, the atmosphere and music in this game is absolutely amazing. I have taken many screenshots already and I keep stopping to look at the surroundings and admire everything. The level design is amazing as well, very much like Dark Souls 1, and that's no exaggeration. Also, the combat is very fun once you get past the control issues, the dodges not having iframes leads to a much more dynamic combat system than you'd get with dark souls, as it requires you to pay attention to attacks and dodge or block them in a certain way. To anyone on the fence about this game who thinks it looks great but is turned off by everyone mentioning the jank, I encourage you to buy it and play for at least an hour to try to get used to it. Worst case scenario you can always refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's my review of Bleak Faith: Forsaken based on my completed 20 hour playthrough, what I've seen on streams, and read on forums/discord. I will provide my summary & conclusion at the start then include my pros/cons list below for those interested.Summary & Conclusion:To put it bluntly, this is an unfinished product. The Devs called this the "official release" but do not be fooled. It is an early access game where you're paying $25 to test a beta. That would be fine if it was advertised as such but it wasn't so, lower your expectations if you decide to purchase. That being said, I don't view it as a total loss. It does capture a small bit of that first Dark souls 1 playthrough where you're struggling, figuring out how things work and enemies are intimidating at first glance. The difference is that in BFF's current state, the frustration and getting used to it doesn't really pay off yet.So my advice is to wait 6 months - 1 year to buy this. It has a LOT of potential but it needs a LOT of work. CONS:- Balancing issues. I would say a large percentage of enemies/bosses lie on the outer edges of either too difficult or too easy with less being in the balanced center. Of course this an opinionated stance but I think most will agree that a lot of things are bare bones simple or overtuned.- Lack of depth. A lot of the combat design is extremely basic. Many non-boss enemies have 1-2 types of attacks and the strategy is to keep a bit of distance until they finishing swinging, then you go in for an easy hit and thats it. Giants are a common type of enemy that can only be killed in one way - you slash their legs until they fall, press F to climb on their back then you spam left click until they die - rinse and repeat. You'd have to royally mess it up to get hit by these guys, there's almost zero threat when you're standing between their feet. Cheap and not rewarding.- There’s basically no story. I’m not a story-driven player but some people are. The cut scenes are boring, don’t explain anything and even I was questioning who my character was and what I was trying to achieve - Fighting on stairs is wildly inconsistent. If you're on a different y-plane, attacks will not land most of the time.- A lot of exploration feels unsatisfying. I'd say about 60% of the time it is unfulfilling and a waste of time. Many places in the game are vast and without boundaries so on a first play-through, you will spend a lot of time going down many dead ends or areas that lead to absolutely nothing. I know not every door/path needs to have something amazing behind it but when it's nothing most of the time, its not the fun kind of exploration. However sometimes you will explore areas that lead you to something new and it feels great when that happensLaundry list of bugs but I'll highlight the most severe:- About a 5-10% chance for bosses to just not spawn upon re-entering the fight- Unexpectedly falling through the ground/elevators- Extreme clipping either with terrain or enemies moving into walls.- Lighting in entire areas randomly goes dark, rendering it unplayable until rebooting the game- Random annoying UI bugs, notably belt slot. It'll show what potions you have equipped on character menu (which can only be viewed out of combat), but on the in-combat UI, your belt slots will often either be incorrect or just blank which was particularly frustrating.- Less common but the camera goes through walls in tight spaces sometimes.- Later stages of the game, i would just randomly spawn with 75-80% HP. Restarting the game fixed it when it happened PROS - Perks(talents) that allow for some build diversity. And what I like about the progression is that I still get some use out of abilities/spells even though I went for a hard-hitting strength build. I had to really think about what talents to pick up because its irreversible but I enjoy that theory-crafting element much more than something incredibly basic. I have a lot of problems with this game but it's world is mysterious and enticing which is ultimately what made me persevere through all the issues. -Most of combat success is determined by prudent and skillful decision-making, i.e. timing your attacks, managing stamina, dodging in the proper direction based on the enemy's attack. So the combat foundation is certainly there, it just lacks depth-I appreciate the art style which was most likely inspired by Dark souls. The bizarre and intimidating looking enemies makes your exploration feel more risky and serious- Stats and gear system is meaningful. I ran a two-handed sharp weapon strength/constitution build and every stat point felt like it mattered and had weight to it. I also felt like I had quite a few weapon options and at no point did I feel like I wasn't finding enough gear
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: So, to start off, first impressions were kinda concerning for me. But let's start from the beginning:The controls: They feel really weird at first, especially on a controller, it's very different from a traditional souls-like. However after an hour or so I got used to them and now I'm having a blast. It's such a shame so many people are negative reviewing the ♥♥♥♥ out of this game just because they only played for like 30 minutes and couldn't get the grasp on the controls. Especially since this is an incredible game. I'm only around an hour and a half in and I'm already loving this game so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ much. So let's dig into the good stuff now.The art direction: The location design, the enemy design, the weapon design, there's so much uniqueness and variety to the design, it's all so damn amazing. This is definetely one of the highlights of this game and why this game has been so waited for and I can say without a problem that they delivered. This is some of the best art direction out there.The area interconnectivity:The location design is really good, everything's connected to itself, looping and swirling around each other to create an INSANELY fun to explore world with many secrets and hidden corridors to be found. It makes me feel like I'm playing DS1 all over again and it's the best feeling in the world.The combat:The combat does feel a bit weird and not as polished as in other souls-likes but it's not as terrible as people are saying. It's actually really fun once you get a hang of it!For now, this is all I have to say about this game, this review is pretty barebones as it's all just first impressions after the first hour and I'll come back to update this review with more in-depth explanation of all the negatives and positives. All I got to say now is: yes, the controls are jank but this is really the only negative thing about the game so far and honestly the way people immidiately go to write a negative comment without giving the game even an hour to get used to the controls is laughable. To summaries, so far I HEAVELY recommend Bleak Faith: Forsaken. It's an incredible game and I can't wait to deep further into it and see what it has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: The map is like a huge labyrinth which I really like, its very vertical and almost everything seems interconnetcted in some way. There's a bunch of very long ladders but you can skip the climb after doing it once, which is awesome. So far there's been plenty of diffrent types of enemies and there's been a few diffrent types of weapons to choose from. The abilities have cooldowns, which is nice since most are long enough to make abilities seem more like an extra thing on the side instead of a spammable basic attack to cheese everything with and the cooldowns make them feel more impactfull when used. Bosses cannot be pairied, which I usually don't do anyways but I'm still not a fan of that. You don't seem to loose anything when dying which kinda mocks the soulslike feeling of the game a little but there ain't really anything to loose since there doesn't seem to be a leveling system in the game. As far as I can tell, you get your attributes from runes you put in you gear at the trader and you can level up the trader by finding items throughout the giant labyrinth of a map. The higher your trader is leveled the higher you can uprgade your gear, which in turn lets you put in more runes, besides granting bettes basic defensive stats for armor and offensive stats for weapons. All in all, besides not being able to lock the camera on giants (on everything else it works just fine which makes it all the more annoying), so far I'm enjoing this game a lot and it's challenging in almost all the right aspects. I bought the game for 25€ which it's deffinetly worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot worse on launch day and I will not lie that I almost gave up due to absurdly dumb decisions  but to my surprise must of the really stupid ♥♥♥♥ got patched out within 2 days of release and the game is already like 20% better in my opinion, I am really glad I stuck with the game, it's still riddled with bugs and probably will be for some time but the world design is absolutely fantastic, I don't think I have taken this many screenshots in any other game, the combat is also pretty good and offers a surprisingly high amount of variety, for it's price tag it's a really good game and it will only get better in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the game and I've loved it! Surreal and unsettling architecture mixed with a nice (mostly) exploration-friendly gameplay style in the Soulslike game. Calm, haunting music will accompany you through your exploration of the omnistructure. Really impressive work for such a small studio, great execution on your vision! Technical notes on the gameplay itself, the movement and combat controls are passable though clunky compared to bigger projects in the same vein (as you'd expect), though combat is nice and brisk with a variety of viable styles so you should be able to find a mode that works for you. Adds a novel and easy-to-use make-your-own-waypoint mechanic to help progression along.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: Blink faith is a fantastic accomplishment for a small team. The world is very interesting and interlocks in many cross paths. I love the ominous environment. It's unfortunate there's such a focus on the "stolen assets", I've put many hours into Elden ring and I find very little similarity between the two games. It sounds like it's just the animation for one sword, which I failed to notice. If you're looking for souls-like fix I completely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of problems here but the biggest I think is that this game's controls are a total disaster. _childDocuments_.review: This is a tough review to write because I agree with most of the criticism levied against this game. The biggest offenders are the jank in the combat and the (sometimes) game-breaking bugs. Despite the fact that the devs have been working tirelessly to make improvements, there is still a degree of clunkiness and lack of polish in certain aspects of this game. If you play these kinds of games specifically for the combat, or if you don't have the patience to deal with bugs forcing you to quit out and replay some sections, I would recommend that you skip this one.However, the level design and exploration in this game are lightyears beyond what you get in most games like this. There are tons of items hidden away in hard to reach places and I was frequently surprised at the ways the levels would loop back on themselves. Every time I entered a new area, I was excited to explore off the beaten path to see what secrets I could find. You won't find the same level of environmental story-telling that you would in Dark Souls, but the environments do feel very carefully crafted to convey feelings of bleakness and decay. If you play these kinds of games because you love exploration, labyrinthine level design, or desolate aesthetics (or if you're a fan of Blame!) then I definitely recommend that you pick this game up

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game from day one and dump hours upon hours into the atmospheric and unique environment the game offers you to explore. It is one of the most unique game designs I have seen from games in the souls-like genre, and even though the game draws inspiration from many other games, the mechanics are souls-y with a nice mix of unique characteristics that I think are really interesting. The combat feels pretty satisfying, and the overall way that the game presents its upgrade system and stat mechanics is another unique aspect to the game that bases it off your progression in the story. The abilities are mostly satisfying to use, and the weapons come with a wide variety of special moves that all feel good. Sound design and voice acting are fantastic; one of the few areas of the game that I had no issues with and was actually pleasantly surprised by the quality of. The cutscenes were cool, atmospheric, and confusing as hell - just as you would expect from a souls-like game. In these areas, the game really exceeded my expectations. Now, unfortunately, I must get into some of the glaring and outstanding issues that smear this game's potential. As I said in my first sentence, I really wanted to love this game from day one and wish the developers had taken another couple of months to iron out the problems with the game before releasing it. I won't go into detail on every single technical or game-breaking issue I had during my playthrough, as quite a few other reviewers have explained many of them pretty well. The one thing I will say in this area is that the game developers have been working nonstop to patch and fix the game since its launch, and many of the game-breaking issues that I experienced were promptly fixed the same day I had them. They have been very active in their discord with the community, communicating directly with people leaving bug reports and feedback to resolve issues and implement different features to improve the quality of the game. They accepted that it was their mistake releasing a bug riddled game, and have been working feverishly to fix the issues and create an enjoyable experience for the player.While I do praise the developers for their hardwork and dedication and commend them for a seriously impressive world for a three-person team, there are many issues within the game that I do hope they fix because they ruin some of the experience. You do feel a bit floaty, but it's fairly easy to get used to. The main issue comes with bouncing off terrain collision and slipping off the sides of walkways, most of which are narrow and contain holes. The beginning of the game teaches you a climbing mechanic that you almost never use, as most of the terrain does not have a prompt for you to climb up. You can still climb up certain rocks, boulders, and ledges to progress to certain areas but this is not always consistent and the areas are not always actually filled with anything. Enemies clip through walls that they obviously shouldn't fit through, sometimes the enemy ai bugs out and they are motionless, and other times the enemies die from even touching you. These are sporadic issues that seem to occur when the gamespeed is having issues, often occurring after I have died multiple times in the area and my corpses haven't yet despawned. Another thing that I hope gets fixed is that there are many areas of the game with elevators or ladders that take an extremely long time to traverse. As others have stated, there is no sliding animation to go down ladders. Some areas of the game have ladders that take over a minute to climb, and some areas of the game have elevators that take over 3-4 minutes to ride up or down. There were many instances of running to an elevator, dying from an enemy right as it went down, running all the way back to the lever just to have to wait for it to finish its descent, and then having to pull the lever and wait another 3 minutes for it to go all the way back up just to take the 3 minute ride down. This is not an exaggeration. I did not time every single elevator in the game, but many of the lifts that weren't even taking you between levels of the game also had ridiculously long ride times. If the elevator is taking you to another level or area of the game, count on it taking around 3-4 minutes. Also count on it being really buggy and laggy when it transitions areas, with the screen going black and glitchy as you stand there wondering if you are even moving. A respawn point was not always close to elevators like this, causing at least 3-4 hours of my playthrough just being riding up and down areas of the game when I kept forgetting where they went, if I died right before them, or if I died right as they started their descent/ascent. Hopefully the developers fix these things as they make performance and quality of life changes to the game, as it really is egregious.My last issue with the game is that while the atmosphere of the game is awesome, it is not very easy to make your way through the entirety of the game unguided. There were two times I had to check the discord or search the internet for help on where to go because the obvious path was not the way to progress. As stated before, some of these areas had the egregious elevators that made constantly riding around to find the way myself daunting and depressing. Without spoiling anything, there are two re-calibrations that the player must complete to progress the story that are shown as a gear icon that displays the distance the player is from them. One of them involves following a fairly well-lit path that shows you the way, but the other involves taking a ride through an area to a boss. The ride is not foreshadowed or hinted at by any of the NPCs that I found in the game, nor any of the lore, cutscenes, or dialogue you experience and is something you would not immediately guess is how you progress. All of the factors from the first re-calibration would indicate that the method of which you obtain this ride would lead to your death. There is also an area of the game that completely bars you from entry without having completed certain story elements, but the game doesn't tell you this or stop you from accessing the area and I had to figure out why I couldn't progress by checking the discord. Because of the various issues that were still being patched during my playthrough of the game, it was also hard to differentiate the bugs from some of the actual game elements or mechanics. This vagueness of the progression system should really be made a little easier to understand by adding hints. As much as I love the atmospheric storytelling and progression in souls-likes, this instance seems like a bit much to expect when the game is in this state.Overall, I really wanted to love this game and ended up just thinking it was okay. Some of the elements and mechanics I really enjoyed, but the experience was marred by bugs and a multitude of game issues. Even with an extremely powerful PC, the gamespeed was constantly being affected by my corpses and was causing rubber-banding issues and fps drops. This is definitely one of those games that I would have felt cheated out of my money had they charged 60$ and would've been a quick refund. Since it was only 27$, I had been huffing copium and hopium for months, and really wanted to play the game, I kept it and played through it in its entirety. Despite all this being said, the attitude of the developers and the constant rate the game is being improved and bug fixed has me hopeful of the game's future. In a year from now with a couple of content updates after the game has been fixed, this could truly rival some the best of the games in the souls-like genre. I can't bring myself to give it a negative review, but its probably best to wait 6 months to a year or so for the game to be smoothed over into an enjoyable game experience. If you do pay for it now just understand what you're getting yourself into.

_childDocuments_.review: I previously played Bleak Faith in October of 2023, following the major update then. At that time I had many problems with it and gave it a negative review for being excessively buggy and unpolished. Following the current Breakthrough patch, I decided to give it another chance. I'm happy to say that the game has been substantially improved. It's still not an impeccably polished game and I did still encounter a few bugs, but the game is vastly more functional than it was before and controls much better than it did before, such that I can now wholeheartedly recommend it for the incredible experience it offers of exploring a massive megastructure that feels utterly hostile to your intrusion.This isn't designed like a Souls game; it doesn't have painstakingly laid out rooms of varied combat encounters with complimentary groups of enemies making you fight for your every step of progress. Instead it feels intentionally haphazard; simultaneously sprawling and labyrinthine in design, enemies often aren't so much of a difficulty themselves as they are a postmark in your exploration of an impressively large, varied, and interconnected world. Some bosses can be difficult, one in particular frustratingly so, but overall it's probably on the easier side of difficulty for Souls-likes, or at least it was for me playing with the amulet that disables i-frames in exchange for increasing your dodge distance.Sound design sometimes feels lacking and this is probably at its worst at the start of the game where there still aren't any footsteps on the surface of the first area you're walking on, but in other ways the sound design can be outstanding, especially the game's ambient soundtrack, and while I can't claim to have understood the story in the slightest, the game's cutscenes have an engrossing level of spectacle and intensity to them.I'm not sure what more to say; in the state the game is in now it still has some rough edges but it provides a wonderfully unique and enthralling experience that's well worth the time of anyone who played Dark Souls and enjoyed it for its atmosphere and exploration which is what Bleak Faith delivers in spades. I'm not a fan of the decision to add standard levelling over the old system of stats being tied to gear but otherwise the game has unquestionably been improved immensely. It's really unfortunate that the game launched in such a rough state and took this long to get here, but I can only hope that it sees success going forward since the devs stuck with it.PS. The bestial miniboss in the first area is probably the single worst-designed enemy in the game. It really sets a bad first impression. Just try to overlook it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ambitious, Atmospheric and Ain't Ready. Stick this one in the oven for longer, chef.Basically, this game is pretty buggy. Within 62 minutes of gameplay, I came across- An enemy stuck inside of a wall- enemies idle_pose back and forth in the distance, until i came within "rendering" distance or whatever you want to call it. They were sliding back and forth at breakneck speeds bro- A bug that prevented me from interacting with enemies at all. I can't attack them, they can't attack me. We just didn't exist in the same dimension. I also fell through an elevator to my death afterwards. (This bug was not "reset" on death, i had to quit to main menu)- a bug that renders my armour and then my own model invisible when i looked at myself from different angles inside an elevator.In a single hour of gameplay inside the beginner area. I hadn't even killed the first boss.However, I still reccommend this game, just as a "wait for some patches to come out" game. It has a lot going for it, its very ambitious, and im excited to see where the game and developers go!Combat is actually not the worst! I personally like this slow, methodical positioning style of combat. Hitboxes are quite precise. It does lead to issues with a few enemies i encountered who could be easily defeated by circling around them. They will never hit you, because they do not have enough different attacks to ever hit you. The same diagonal downward slash that always, always goes over my head.When you're not abusing the lack of attack variety, the combat is decent in my opinion. The game incentivises timing your attacks to continue combos efficiently, by punishing button mashign with slower animations and higher stamina costs. Position well, time your attacks, and victory is very attainable despite the intimidating appearance of those early brutes. Or just abuse the precise hitboxes and lack of attack variance. or trigger that bug so you can't be hit by enemies.The game is Incredibly atmospheric. The droning hum of purposeless machinery meets the disapproving gaze of god church music. You are walking inside the carcass of a technologically advanced empire, wielding primitive blades and bashing people wearing Fallout's Raider Armour. The sense of scale pairs beautifully with the music, grand skyscrapers stretch into the gray abyss above, and sink into the murky depths below. Great metal... spires? Pipes? ...wires...? entwine and follow suit. amidst the planetary concrete monuments sprout little patches of greenery and trees, and quaint little ruined stone castles and temples. Medieval gothic meets grand cyberpunk post apocalypse.However that's about all that can be said to be "good" about the game. It sounds nice and looks nice. and combat is good when you're not abusing the very easily abused precise hitboxes.Bugs are abound like an infestation, as already stated. Beyond that, key features of video games in general doesn't feel good.Movement. Is core to pretty much any game focusing on a controllable character/avatar. While you don't have to make it feel amazing, its generally a good idea to at least make it not feel awkward.My entire sixty minute tour of this beautiful apocalyptic carcass was undermined by the persistent feeling of walking on invisible terrain. It felt like the terrain model/hitbox/collision model was a different shape to the actual terrain that you made contact with. Which is wrong, actually. I think the terrain was perfectly fine and in fact very precise. A slight lip on some boardwalks prevents you from accidentally sliding right off, althouhg you can still press on to your doom.I think its a result of animation and handling of the character. Some ineffable qualia makes it so that controlling your character feels ever so slightly - off. The tiniest winiest bit floaty. Ever so slightly, janky. A miniscule amount of clunk. What the developers ought to do, in my humble opinion, as someone with no developement experience, is flatten out a lot of the slopes. Like, obliterate any rough edges, really get in there with some sandpaper. and work on creating some more dynamic animations for walking on slopes/stairs. Make it so that your legs will actually stand at different elevations on bumpy terrain. What this will do in the mystic depths of imagination, is remove the bumpy floatiness of walking around. Your character no longer slides around on top of the terrain, but the impression of rough terrain is maintained by your character's animations having more variance and depth to them. Just a suggesstion that is surely impossible to implement, and will almost definitely impact nothing other than to make the game objectively worse.Anyway, TLDRLooks GoodSounds GoodFights Good (sometimes)Walks badcall an exterminator for all these bugsI eagerly await patches in future.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't just rough around the edges. It's rough right in the middle where you want to love it. The movement is sloppy, the combat is slow and the graphics are mid. This game isn't for everyone. But if you're into what it has, it's actually a unique and beautiful game.What it has is a level of atmosphere that most games don't. Exploration that gives you a taste of how it felt to play a game as a kid and not have any idea what you might run into next. It just has a level of novelty that's rare and kinda special.You might think you're off the map and then find a new enemy or the best item you've found yet. You might also  be off the map with no way back and have to jump to your death. This isn't a bug. It's a feature. You actually never know what you're going to see next.This game probably should have been released as early access, but that kinda doesn't matter. If you're into what this game does right, the jank is irrelevant. If you're not, you wouldn't enjoy it even if the combat was as smooth as butter and the menus were designed by Steve Jobs.

_childDocuments_.review: ○ Clunky combat○ Littered with enemies around every corner. That means constantly experiencing the clunky combat○ Too many gank fights○ Animations have no weight or impact○ Stamina regen is way too slow. Having to constantly fight enemies (50% of encounters being gank fights), with slow stamina regen makes for boring gameplay. You could say it's challenging, but it's definitely not fun.○ Parry timing is strange.It's a well made game for three devs and there's a lot of potential, but I feel like the devs should've focused more on the strengths of the game: Atmosphere and art direction. The combat doesn't feel good, it's decent at best. If the devs learn from this, their next game could be great, but this game I can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: The soundtrack is enough for me to recommend it.BUT! As janky as some of the animations can be, it is a beautiful game. The weapon abilities and character abilities are flashy, but not too flashy. The lighting is dramatic and the art making up the world is fantastic. Each zone has its own flavor. The combat leaves some room for desire, like the lack of no i-frames in your dodge. Which is a tad sadge once you get used to it... it works.Overall it is more forgiving than some Dark Souls games. It doesn't have a level system, which is a plus for me. Your build comes from where you spend your ability points, which you find or loot. Your perk choices, which are permanent selections, also boss drops for currency to pick them. And your gear, which gets upgraded via a key NPC that would be your blacksmith equivalent, and you upgrade her abilities as your progress. Allowing for better weapon upgrades. You can take any weapon and make it do most of what you want via the socketing system. Want tons of lifesteal? Socket for it. Want all the HP? Socket for it. Wanna do high top end damage with crits? Socket for it!The post apocalyptic environment, Gothic appeal, and fantasy meets sci-fi sells it for me. Also a bonus, unless you die with the perk currency fresh off the boss, you just lose crafting mats, in my experience so far. I might not have noticed something about dying, but it has led me to not fear death so much, and explore alternative paths so I can later come back and retrieve what I left behind.With all that and the developer's word that they will continue to add to it as time goes on... I recommend it. I look forward to seeing this game grow. Maybe it will become the next big name in the Soulsborne community.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: This game seriously needs to be patched. It absolutely KILLS ME to give this game a bad review, but unfortunately in it's current state, I have to. I was (and still am) rooting for these 3 developers, and pains me to see their work of art and passion released in its current state. I REALLY wanted this game to succeed, and I hope there's still time for them to turn things around.BUGS I'VE ENCOUNTERED:- If you get killed while trying to fast travel at a checkpoint, your camera gets all messed up, and you teleport in a completely random location.- After returning to the first area to fight the giant monkey, my healing items don't display properly. I'm not sure if it's because of the monkey, or a lingering irreversible effect from the fast-travel death bug. Basically it keeps saying my healing flasks are at 2, but it doesn't let me heal. Then when I die, it makes them disappear from the slot. No matter how many times I respawn, return to the menu, or close and reopen the game, this bug will NOT go away. And I REALLY don't want to have to delete my save file... assuming even that'll fix it. - If the monkey kills you, the sky stays dark, and you can't open your inventory because the game thinks you're still fighting it. For the non game developers reading this, please excuse my game dev jargon, but it seems to me like the scene doesn't even reload upon death. The game just changes the enemy states from dead to alive, and teleports you back to the checkpoint. Sure, doing it this way means faster respawn times, but it also opens up a lot of possibilities for things to go wrong. And that's exactly what happened after the monkey killed me. The current way death is handled, not everything resets properly after death. If they simply made the scene reload while saving your data from the previous scene instance, this problem wouldn't exist.- I clipped straight through one of the walls in the monkey area. And frankly, it's mind blowing just how many bugs are related to the monkey.- (Take this one with a grain of salt) When I climb onto the giants, and stab them over and over again, there seems to be a 50% chance that I'll just die randomly. I'm not sure if there's some mechanic I'm forgetting about, or if it's just a flat out bug. So if that's actually intentional, and I'm just being a dumbass, please ignore this.- When I try to unequip an item from the quick slots, it'll reappear almost instantly.DESIGN FLAWS:- You can't use items while swimming, the oxygen meter goes down super fast, and the underwater area is so spacious, but there's no indication of anything that will restore your oxygen, no air bubbles, no air in the buildings (at least the ones I've gone to). The game needs to do a better job of communicating to the player what the hell they're supposed to do underwater. Because currently, I have no idea.- The tutorials are good, but there's no way to re-access them once you make them disappear. There should be an option in the pause menu to re-read the tutorials.- You can only run in 8 directions. I'm no expert in the Unreal Engine (yet), but I do have a fair amount of experience with Unity. Depending on how similar these engines are, I really don't think implementing more turning angles would've been that difficult at all. If I were a fourth dev in that dev team, I would've done a Vector2 input system (I'm not sure if Unreal Engine has a different name for it than Unity), so it makes your turning angle the exact angle of your joystick. Because currently, when you walk on narrow bridges, if you make even the slightest adjustment, you'll go straight off the edge.- A lot of the ladders are extremely long, and you can't even slide down them. This game is already a souls-like, so it baffles me that they didn't implement a basic thing such as that. It's so painful to have to slowly climb down, every single time.CONCLUSION:If it weren't for these game-breaking bugs and design oversights, this would've been a great game, and it still can be if it gets patched SOON! I'm fully aware that this game was made by only 3 people, and I feel really bad for them, because a lot of passion must've gone into this. If I made a game that I poured my heart and soul into, and it got a bunch of bad reviews, I'd probably get crippling depression. It pains me a ton, that I might be doing that to them. But the cold hard truth is that they jumped the gun way too early. They should've given it a few more months to polish it up as much as possible. I really hope they patch this soon. It's not too late yet, but the clock is ticking, and they REALLY need to haul ass to fix these bugs before people forget about this game.I really hope I will have an opportunity to write a good review, once everything has been fixed. So please fix it!!! I hope the devs won't be disheartened by this, and I hope these reviews will serve as a valuable lesson for any and all games they make in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I do NOT review games. Because I rarely buy games without knowing whether I will like them first. That being said, the one set of games I will buy sight unseen is "Souls Likes". The reason being, normally, no matter the jank (ala HellPoint) or bad critic review (ala Lords of the Fallen, the old one), I can find a reason to enjoy myself.So it pains me to say, that I cannot in good faith, allow other SoulsBorne fans to buy this game in it's current state. Someone had the audacity to compare the world design to DS1....The nerve. Must be a dev....So here is what I will say....The world is seemingly MASSIVE. And empty. I know it is only 3 devs who took on this project, and I account for that in this review, which is why it sucks that I have to say how awful the world is. Some of the LONGEST hallways of nothing I have ever seen. Just to get thru some of it, I booted up a trainer to access 2x speed. It's that bad...The combat is peak jank. Hellpoint-esque, but Hellpoint combat in a world where they only had 3 devs to design it. If you haven't played that game, then imagine Dark Souls, but in molasses and with horrific fluidity. It just looks bad, and feels bad to play.That being said, it has a few great ideas. The upgrade system, although vague and poorly explained, seems like it could offer many different play styles and lead to high replayability if you get past the jank. Some of the enemies are very cool, and there are a great deal of weapons and armor for loot fanatics like me. With some TLC over the next year or so, this could be pretty good. But for the moment, I wish I had refunded at the 2 hour mark. But it's cool, I support this genre and anyone who gives their all to give us more Souls likes

_childDocuments_.review: Bleak Faith has one of the most interesting atmospheres, it's easily its strongest feature. The only issues I do have are minor and some things that stick out are just enemies missing me when they swing or parry timing but it works more if you're patient and not button spamming or just have a build that can handle enemies in ways other than melee.The developers seem eager to continue smoothing the game out and I'm happy about that. _childDocuments_.review: Yes, it is a game made by very few people. For this, I have a lot of respect. I can understand if there are bugs or other flaws. Consider everything not mentioned in this review as a positive point of the game. But there are major problems with the game design. The mechanics are very unresponsive. For a game, which wants to be "the best action RPG", this is a design contradiction. Action RPGs like Dark Souls, which served here as the main inspiration, are build on responsive mechanics. The game does not provide anything like this. Having no i-frames is actually a nice touch, but having the "gamey combo" attack loop, where the player must click the attack button in some trial-and-error moment so that the attack continues and does not stop for one second, is not a good solution for the challenge-skill-reward problem. The next big problem with the game is the world. It was a very promising idea, but this was realized very poorly. The omnistructure was created to be convoluted, but the level design was generally very bad. Normally, I am not a big fan of "academic game designer", but there were clearly many lessons not learned. No landmarks, many long, empty, hallways, no character. And the enemies are as if someone bought the assets he could find in the UE asset store. I am very, very disappointed. Even if the devs would fix the last bug in this game, added the last missing assets, balanced the last untested mechanic, they will never fix the broken game and horrible level design, because this would mean to start all over again. I am sorry to write that review. The game was very promising, but it does not deliver. Very unfortunate.

_childDocuments_.review: This was not ready for release.Oh boy there was potential here with Bleak Faith: Forsaken with it's really cool visual.The level design seemed interesting with many interconnected areas, sadly the end result is terrible.Unfortunately everything here is ruined by the clunky combat and the unresponsive floaty controls.The animations are mediocre and the hit feedback doesn't feel impactful enough.If that was not enough then you should know that the game is full of collisions and ragdoll glitches, it's so bad it's laughable.Looks like these developers probably don't know analog controls are a thing for controllers because right now this is almost unplayable with a controller.Want to walk slowly to avoid falling to your death making a tight jump ? Forget it walking is not possible here lol.This is a damn joke to release your game with such broken controller support. Refunding as we speak, avoid at all costs.This is worse than Hellpoint and Mortal Shell which are both mediocre games.Don't believe any of the fake paid shills reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: oh boy, where to start...textures from 2002glitches galoresometimes entire button inputs don't registersometimes attacks just don' register. This at least goes for your enemies as well.a lot of environmental objects aren't placed correctly so they either hover above the ground or you can see through the cracks into the mapanimations are janky as hellplaying with controller messes they game up. They might have fixed that but I still recommend Keyboard and Mouse. Feels designed for it.Game ripped animation from the Soulsgames and possibly some others. Devs claim it was an legitimately bought asset pack and are currently in the process of removing the animations.So why the hell am I recommending this game?Because the World Design and Atmosphere are plain excellent. At least for me, the game can easily stand on that alone, even with all its flaws. On top of that, the game still works for the most part. It is obviously nowhere near games like Elden Ring or Nioh but it isn't trying to be. Some games hyperfocus on specific elements. Most recently the game SCORN comes to mind. Similar to Bleak Faith, in focused on presenting a world heavily inspired by H.R. Gigers work (Alien movies) while not offering much in the gameplay department. Still, if you are into that kind of design you can enjoy the game. Actually being there, walking around and witnessing it yourself, even by proxy of a video game character, is worth a merit on its own.Bleak Faith hits the exact same Nail. I don't know what artstyle exactly this game is inspired by but "Bleak" is the perfect descriptor.infinite grey walls of brutalist architecture where gothic churches clash with modern apartment buildings. An infinite complex of stone and steel called the Omni-Structure. Seemingly infinite Hallways snaking its way through its metal bowels. Endless Stairways that seemingly lead into nothing. And when you look up in the sky to breath a sigh of relief your eyes will only witness more buildings, impossibly suspended leagues above you. If you enjoy Souls-like world design for its interconnectivity then Bleak absolutely delivers. Every road has at least two forks for you to explore and its a joy trying to create a mental map of the place.To summarize, if you can get behind the idea of a Two Minute elevator ride (I checked, it's actually exactly two minutes!) and liking it simply for the anticipation of where it could even possibly take you only to be stunned when you arrive... then you are like me and will most likely be able to enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is clearly made to be played on mouse and keyboard with free aim. Target lock only makes it harder, so I can see why people using target lock or gamepad would not enjoy it. The mouse and keyboard controls are very good so i recommend trying it even if your not used to it in souls likes (like me :)). The combat is satisfying but a little janky, however the devs seem to know this as more times than not the jank helps me (attacks miss me that clearly shouldnt). Id say the most annoying part is that you sometimes wont parry if you click lmb a lil too long, but ive def gotten used to it, and even when i mess it up, the enemies dont do enough dmg to kill me off that one mistake (the parry window is also VERY generous).dodging attacks feels great (no I frames so you have to ACTUALLY dodge them, and they are well telegraphed) and you have the upper hand in terms of defensive and offensive stats against most non bosses. Ive only felt overwhelmed by the mobs once and that was when I aggroed too many at the start so I hadnt yet learned to deal with groups, which you can do with a little finesse, no problem. Every other death so far has been entirely user error, IE: forgot to heal, fell off a ledge, was careless with positioning, all things that I easily corrected and non of it angered me.I am not very far in but the game really doesnt seem hell bent on bending you over like some souls likes are, its just a fun, dark fantasy action rpg. The only major problem is how movement and jumping can feel a bit floaty. In some aspects the game feels like one of those physic based games, but not in a bad way.So far the only bug ive encountered made it so I couldnt dmg enemies, but they couldnt dmg me either and a quick restart fixed it. However im only a few hours in at time of review so that may change.I recommend trying just dont expect it to be the next Elden Ring, it stands its own but its not groundbreaking, however the setting makes up for that imo. Remember to play mouse and keyboard, and just free aim, it works really well trust me :).

_childDocuments_.review: First off, expect a little JANK. I walked into this game expecting that and I have been having a blast. No game-breaking bugs, but I have run into an issue where one enemy's loot drop was moving and I wasn't able to collect it. With that being said, the atmosphere, world building, and overall gameplay is fun. Swinging a sword feels meaty and you really appreciate the weight behind a Guts-esque greatsword when you inevitably carve an enemy in half. This is only accentuated by the nice little gore system they have in place. The soundtrack to me is captivating. There are no epic orchestral scores supported by a flew of violins and horns like you get in the souls series. What you get is a dark, depressing and BLEAK arrangement of instruments. There are no I frames like fromsoft games, and it changes the way you must approach combat. It seems so many people here were expecting Elden Ring 2 from a development team of only 3 people. If you were expecting that, STAY AWAY. However, if you are looking for a dark and gritty action adventure RPG to get lost in, then this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wished you could go back in time and get that same feeling you had when you started up the original dark souls for the first time? ever dreamed back to when you constantly died because you hadn't adapted to the game. When you always got lost, died to gravity, and ran in circles for hours only to discover there was a path right there all along, and that you must have run passed it 50 times, before it led you to a great new large area you didnt even know existed!Ever wished the time would come again where you would be so into a game that you would wake up in the morning only thinking about how you could improove yourself and continue your journey?. Thats what Bleak Faith did for me. it gave me something wellknown yet original and in many ways completely genious! For sure these Devs has a very bright future in the world of soulslikes! Ive played MANY, and this is def up there in the very top. if you want a reference id say you mix Mortal shell, Hellpoint, and Back to Ashes with a tiny touch of The Surge (and alot of Souls ofc.) and then you add the most dedicated developers you'll ever come across, who not only listen to and implement the players ideas, but comes up with brilliant original ideas/features  to constantly improove the game themselves.To me this is just a true gem, -not completely polished- but it shines bright in my world. Ive enjoyed every step in this journey, and ill be back for NG+ as soon as its out. (which allready sounds like it will be amazing and add a new twist on how we allready think ng+ should be) I loved the mechanics, loved the visuals, loved the exploration, loved the bossfights, loved the grinding, And also, I am so impressed by the soundscape of the game, which is the best ive experienced in a long time. And yes it still has a few bugs, theres still places where you can fall through the map, and bla,bla bla.. Didnt mean a thing to me, because these devs has caught the essense of souls, and are constantly polishing this beautyful gem. Will it devide people..?  for sure, but keep in mind that many of the bad reviews are from players that spend less than an hour on the game.. then think back..how would you have reviewed DS1 after 30 minutes gameplay? :)  For an indie label with less than a handfull devs this is a 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I have finally taken the time to beat the game in a play through following all the patches and fixes. They may have fixed a lot of the bugs but the way the game plays is still rough and rigid. The combat is sluggish and uninteresting. Attacks are locked into a combo system that makes successive attacks feel so bad that I almost want to call it unplayable, even if that is false. No iframes when every boss is a beyblade is annoying but manageable. The game does not run smoothly AT ALL.Most of this I could just overlook, but the biggest issue is that I feel lied to. Their most recent videos on their Youtube channel show the game running smoothly, that is laughably not the case. Their older videos (which made me want to buy the game and had me googling its progress monthly for years) show a game drastically different than what was delivered. Literally 99% of EVERYTHING you see in these videos is either cut content or stripped down to the point of being unrecognizable. I hope they will someday be able to create the game they showed off years ago because that looks fantastic and is also the only reason I didn't refund this.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing bleak faith since the day it came out, Even back then with it`s rocky release, I had fun in ways no triple A game could ever give me...Have you ever had that feeling when you are playing games for too long, You feel way too familiar with it to the point you can skip over tutorials and still play better than the majority of people that may have took their time to read everything about the game (Tutorials, guides, walkthroughs, etc.)?That to me has become a problem throughout the time, Specially with games akin to souls-likes... They follow the formula way too closely that makes all of them look more or less of the same and as a result I do not struggle with any of them.That is, however, not the case with bleak faith. To the point that even playing with a souls-like mindset will punish you hard and probably leave you frustrated. Though you as a souls-veteran may find this not as something to be recommended, I think the other way around. Having to learn mechanics for the very first time ever again is so refreshing in ways that only someone that went through the same feeling as I did would know.The lack of i-frames, a metroid-vania level design on a 3D Landscape akin to Dark Souls 1, The universe created that features a art direction not commonly seen in games, Their inspirations behind said universe might even become some sort of primary source of art-direction in the future for games with a grim, dark setting. (See games like Nazralath: The Fallen World and Scorn)Some of these things makes bleak faith to be looked upon 10 years later and videos would be made about it as of how this game was a misunderstood masterpiece, I for one knows some of this misunderstanding comes from.Though most are sorely misguided, As you can see in the reviews from people landing them negatively without playing the game not even for 2 hours versus the people that played for 20 hours or so and always recommends them.The negative reviews will also always look massively innacurate due to how the devs always patch things in the speed of light, If only big studios such as EA or Warner could have done the same with their games...Be mindful, THEY ARE ONLY 3 PEOPLE and they are still more swift with their changes than a whole building full of game devs, Let that sink in.Because of that, I won`t specify more ups and downs because the state of the game is ever changing and improving each day it passes... One could simply read the patch notes and see the plethora of fixes and even reworking a lot of the game`s elements... If you don´t feel like buying it just yet, I recommend you to follow this game closely with its updates and buy it when it feels like the right time to do so. (I recommend checking this game somewhere around August and September) Join the game`s discord, Talk to the developer themselves (Not something you would have on triple-A games), Ask for help or even give feedback on what they can improve, They listen.There is already a loving and caring community behind the game to the point that even multiplayer mode is currently in the works now and this is only the beginning for this game, it only gets better from here.

_childDocuments_.review: I suppose I'll have to think twice before spending money on a game made by just 3 devs that's way too ambitious for its own good.Where to start.. unfortunately I was willing to look past some awkward controls early on in the game as well as sort of clunky combat since it's an indie title with a small dev team so I played past the 2 hour refund limit in the first area just taking in the sights. It's really a pity that the splendit art direction in this game has to be bogged down by everything else in it.The game is BUGGY. Controls are floaty and awkward and my character keeps getting stuck into the level geometry, sometimes you get stuck inside elevators or fall right through them. There are levels positioned in such a way that trying to interact with them will shove directly into the level geometry as well, with no way out other than the "Respawn" button. There's instances where enemies will just phase right through me, unable to damage me and I can't damage them, except the mages! The land mine spells they cast can still hurt me while they are immune to damage. Stamina sometimes remains stuck on infinite, it will even regenerate while I'm running, even near enemies. Enemies will just get stuck inside the level geometry or will walk themselves into a spot where they just get stuck and stop reacting, I've had two knight dudes once walk into each other, one of them teleported on top of the other and then remained there in the air, inactive.Those are some of the few among many other issues I've had in the game, including the janky climbing system which barely works.Game design is also very pool in a lot of ways:Check points are just way too sparse and using them does not even regenerate your health or Flux.The UI and how the inventory, equiping etc works is just awful for a game like this. If I click on the right hand item that I want to replace, the game should know to just replace the item in that slot, not ask me if I wanna put it somewhere else.Stats and how they work are not explained at all in any way, shape or form.Combo system with no way to indicate when you need to input the next attack and with wildly different timings between weapons is just a mess and doesn't mesh very well with a game like this, it's a bit awful when Phantasy Star Online in 2001 did it better than this.The staff spell orb attack does NOT go where the cross hair is, it will fly off either completely straight or at an angle if you are anywhere close to stairs even if you aren't looking down, sometimes it will decide to orbit around enemies instead of going straight as well, othertimes I've had multiple instances of invisible geometry eat it up.Enemies don't react at all to any form of ranged attack, making them sitting ducks and boring to fight like that, which is made even more annoying by how awful trying to play melee is in general. I didn't expect god tier AI, but a simple dodge once in a while would make them much better. The first boss was made into a joke thanks to this.Unfortunately, I was pulled in by the excellent tribute to BLAME! this game's art direction is, only to get what is essentially a glorified alpha test.. an early alpha at that. Horrible, do NOT buy at its current state. Come back in a year or two when it's maybe playable.

_childDocuments_.review: Expect jank. Expect clunky controls. Expect bugs.Bleak Faith is something I always wanted. Ever since I read BLAME!, the feeling of getting lost in a distorted and incomprehensibly massive Megastructure has haunted me, and this game finally recreates that feeling. The blend of an absurd array of architectural stiles and fantasy and sci-fi themes is masterfully done.If exploring a world like this in any way appeals to you, play this.
