_childDocuments_.review: Yes! Absolutely recommended. The cons first because the pros are MANY and you should totally get this with the following cons in mind:So firstly, the controls on controller are totally borked, I can't even explain how. So I tried that for an hour and found myself super frustrated. Sometimes the run/jump/roll gets mixed up and the jump almost HAS TO be set manually. There is even a tool tip that suggests to use the keyboard at the VERY beginning of the game that says it was made with the intention of being played with keyboard and mouse and that the controller was not yet optimized. It's true, the tooltip warned me but I tried it out anyway and even reset the buttons and sticks but it was taxing on the nerves Me, as a controller player was a bit disheartened but then once I used the keyboard and mouse after another hour I started to prefer it for this game. That out of the way there are some silly bugs here and there that can be quite annoying. One is that there is possibly a story attached to a weird black sword you carry for all eternity but it was gone after the first cut scene until I found some armor. THE ARMOR almost appears in your inventory goodness knows when. I couldn't even tell you where I looted anything except a few of the upgrade rocks. I went into my craft menu to make some arrows and WHAM I had a whole slew of armor sets like gloves and legs and chest etc. that I had no idea were there. Maybe they were there from the start? Weapons and rings seem to show up in the menu just fine when they are looted. Sometimes the butt flap armor sticks inside the butt and it looks weird, but honestly I hardly notice it when I'm fighting.One of the worst enemies is one you literally can not kill (as far as I know) is a floating translucent body hung in the position of what may look like a depressed man, and you take severe damage when you touch it, and occasionally they move very slowly from one position to the other and sometimes they post them directly in front of an item so when you run into it you catch fire and die. Not a game breaker but man, super annoying to say the least. Worse than that is when you take damage from it your health bar isn't displayed so you don't know how much damage you've taken but usually when you're dead it won't matter. It gives you a sort of fear of just picking up something you see immediately without checking around first.Okay so the pros:It's beautiful. I'm an older man, who played the Playstation 1 and loved the heck out of 'Legacy of Kain Soul Reaver' which this game reminds me of. I feel like the world of Bleak Faith Forsaken is a modern Nosgoth with all the traps and puzzled you'd expect if that city had evolved and then decayed over millions of years. I felt a kinship within the screenshots over three years ago when I first put this game on my wishlist and it held true when I first entered the game and looked around up at the massive super structure. This game was everything I wished 'Dream Cycle' could be and more. The combat feels heavy (especially if you avoid the controller) and meaty, the sound effects are impacting, though minimalist. The music really helps the world shine though, and makes you feel desperate and lonely. The world is vibrant in the 'The Last Guardian' sort of way where you can tell that the place you are in was once a beautiful dream city that has been overturned to decay and crumbling structures litter every abandoned road. Many of the non player characters you meet explain how they aren't certain how long they've been living in the omnistructure which gives it a further feeling of desperation and isolation; Especially how one of them mentions they "miss the wind". The world feels very machine made with a splint of remaining humanity. The visuals are the pure poetry of exhaustion. As if almost to say that the place itself had been tired of hosting humanity for a tremendous amount of time. One of the most bizarre moments too, was when I came across a human settlement after only seeing machines for the first fourty or so minutes and they were all silent, huddling by fires in a small crevice and nearby were expended cans of food with their heads hung low and their eyes wandering to their thoughts but focused on nothing in particular. They completely ignore you too, as if they were accustomed to seeing machines go further up never to return and would make no effort to leave themselves. Another moment of fright occurred when crossing what seemed like an eternally long thin bridge and a low music chimed in with a middle eastern theme that scared me into thinking that impending doom was just across the way. Truthfully so, as when I crossed there was nothing but a ladder that seemed to travel upward for a mile. The fights are usually pretty short, if you fail to execute a combo your stamina would get eaten up too quickly and usually leave you open to attacks, while executing a combo saves your stamina and seems to deal a significant amount of damage as a result. Thus far I've only fought a single boss and it was some larger machine using ice bombs and a giant lance which you get to own, but so far I've not found a use for it myself. Weighty items can end fights quickly with dismemberment. The giant mace seems to be the most effective killing machine, usually smashing off the heads, torsos, and arms of victims it touches, if of course you can manage to actually swing it with any form of accuracy. Every weapon seems to host its' own behavior, so you sort of learn to like something and use that thing as you would with any tool. I also like the lack of a leveling system and the reliance on skill over stats. You can gain stats with gear, but everything falls back on skill. There are points you get after a boss fight which can be distributed among your pool of perks. They are not a consecutive 'tree' either, leaving you with the freedom to build your own status out of what you might like. There is also a weird save point that you can place anywhere (almost) so that you don't have to traverse a mighty distance back and forth from where you die and where you respawn which is nice. I've not the inclination on how to place it effectively yet, but I assume there will be times where this feature is an absolutely imperative tool. After playing it for a few hours I assume that many players would associate this game with 'Dark Souls' or 'Bloodborne' where I do feel some characteristics might be present, however I would like to believe that this falls into its own category. Every action RPG can't just be called 'Dark Souls' because you have a shield a parry and a dodge roll. In this game tactics you'd use from those games will certainly get you killed. Some Ai even set magic traps and lure you across them. Every fight, even the most trivial will increase in difficulty because of how awkward the terrain is to fight in. I am not sure yet, but I think the game hosts the idea that a great war was started with the leadership of the omnistructure and then because of an anomaly and the weird atmosphere, they'd given up and even forgotten the purpose of their war because of how the terrain is explicit in restricting any urban warfare. It's funny that sometimes you'll see an apartment complex riddled with air conditioners but it sits on an inaccessible cliffside. Almost pointing out that comforts were once here but now they are irrelevant.Yes the game was created with a dated engine, in an almost classic style with a familiar theme of more recently produced games scaling up with difficulty and challenge but it lends to the original idea of video games with artwork and profound tantalizing of the senses. You will feel fear, joy, luck, despair, and love just like you did with games made you feel when you were a kid.

_childDocuments_.review: Granted it has it's issues, but I love the tenacity and passion of the three people that made this game. It's got obvious inspiration from BLAME!, with some BERSERK thrown in. Atmosphere, music, scenery, 10/10. I like that it's not a Souls clone. You craft what you need as you go, from Potions to arrows, to attribute gems that you slot into your gear, weapons, shields. There are no "souls" in the game, so you don't lose anything. I love exploring this dark, Claustrophobic Omnistructure, with interesting enemies, and fun(albeit sometimes frustrating) boss fights(they too, have their issues, but those are being addressed and handled). While visually striking, I have to fault the game for some of the control issues it still has, but otherwise I love playing it. I feel like I'm in a Dark Ambient Music album, like Metatron Omega, Atrium Carceri, or Council of Nine(all artists with Cryochamber), and Martel did a great job with the music(available on Bandcamp). 7/10. I look forward to what these very talented and dedicated people can do in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: It's good. Don't be buying this game with unrealistic expectations for a game made by 3 people, it's not fair to the devs and it's not fair to all the people looking for a good indie game to blow some hours on. However, in its current state the game needs work, that's just how it is. Since release the devs have been working tirelessly to put out patches to address bugs and gameplay improvements, and I imagine this process is going to go on for a while. With these things said, I recommend waiting to buy the game, right now it is a nice experience with a truly unique world and some interesting though currently fairly limited build variety. With updates and new content to hopefully be added in future updates, as well as gameplay/input/bug improvement the game would immediately go up in value and be a one of a kind experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a truly unique experience. If you enjoy exploration, a dense atmosphere or just a well-executed souls-like then I would highly recommend you go play this game. Even after release the developers spent a lot of time and effort, listening to feedback, and improving the game, so I first held off from playing it because I feared I would be missing out on stuff they were still adding. I am glad I finally decided to give it a go. After adjusting the controls to my liking (luckily this game has a lot of customizability) I started exploring the world and I was immediately hooked. If you know the manga Blame!, this games seems to be heavily inspired by it.The exploration for me was the strongest point, with breath taking vistas and a huge vertical interconnected world and a creepy and mysterious atmosphere. I’d even go as far as to say that the level design, surpasses the intricate levels of Dark Souls 1. I loved getting lost and trying to piece together a map of the world with all its connections and secrets. The soundtrack is also quite epic and fits the world perfectly.I cannot say that much about the story. I liked the esthetics, but it was very cryptic, and I did not understand a lot. Not my favorite design choice but also not that untypical for this genre.The combat is satisfying with a lot of cool gear and weapons to find scattered throughout the world. There are lots of unique well-made animations for all the different weapons and the enemy variety in the world is also nothing to be shy of. In terms of difficulty, I’d say it is slightly more forgiving compared to Dark Souls, even though the balance isn’t always perfect. I never experienced the same level of frustration as I did in certain parts of the Dark Souls series.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was very skeptical because of the controls and movement. I recommend anyone who wants to give the game a serious chance to LIMIT THE FPS TO 60 (!!) and reduce the mouse sensitivity. Gameplay-wise, there are no major differences from other soulslikes. The worldbuilding and artstyle is outstanding. Don't be irritated by the trolls who literally insult the developers from minute 1 and don't give the game a fair chance. The developers didn't promise anything they didn't deliver and the price is more than fair. It's a very ambitious project and the 3 developers have created something great in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: I'm french but i'm writting this review in English, because the world needs to know.If you check my Steam profile, i've done most 3D Souls-Likes, and most 2D ones too (i know, my whishlist is far from complete yet). That's the game type i like the most. And if you check my profile, i haven't written these many reviews. I'm doing it today because again, the world needs to know.What I treasure the most in souls-likes is the art direction and the journey. And what a journey it was! The art is nothing short of amazing. Yes, there are very low quality textures. Yes, i've ragequit because of the many, many bugs. You may too.But i'll never forget the vermillion ending area with its gorgeous vistas. The genius of the underwater recalibration area. The abherrant knight area. And much more.It's under 30€ for 20+ hrs of gameplay (given you visit every area which I recommend). It's broken, yes. It looks and feels cheap in many ways, yes. But it's been made by 3 people. Three. Give them a break.I've paid 26€ for the game in the initial promotion, and have played 26hrs. 1€/hr. Movie Theaters charge you 10€ for 3hrs tops. If you're expecting 26€ to deliver AAA levels of polish, that's just not fair. If the journey is what you care about the most like me, and you're smart enough to understand & integrate the limitations implied by the small dev team, time & resources, there's no way you'll regret buying it.Thanks a ton, devs, brilliant game. It reminded me of another broken yet incredible journey-deliverer game: Shattered: Tale Of A Forgotten King. Broken games can be unforgettable too.I will not ever forget Bleak Faith: Forsaken. No matter how broken it was when i've played it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: it's honestly such an innovative take on souls that it's a shame the reviews are so harsh. It has its flaws like the lack of controller support and the buggy jank, but the game has so much charm and unique ideas that I think it makes up for it tbh. The combat system removes Iframes and forces you to chain your attacks at specific times so you can't mash attack. The basic fights become so much more engaging when you can't just mash attack and just iframe through all attacks.The level design is also really good. It's better than dark souls 3 but not quite as good as dark souls 1. it's a little TOO slow. Some ladders at the start were so long I thought it was a joke till the game expected me to do it every time I died.It's a weird flawed gem. I love it in my head, but it's much less pleasant when I actually play it if that makes sense.

_childDocuments_.review: They highly improved controller support, even added dead zone options, too bad the dead zone setting don't apply to when you are on menus and neither can you change vertical and horizontal separatedly.The scenario, visually speaking is amazing, original and vast, looks better than any dark souls, even tho sometimes i feel like walking in circles it is because everything is interconnected.For the gameplay movement feels weird but after some minutes i got the hang of it, jump and dropping physics need an improvement i glide when i drop from a ledge, wich often kills me.But the combat feels amazing, remembers me of dark souls 2 my favorite.Last time i tried playing it was unplayable, i spent hours just trying to configure controls and wasnt able to move 10 meters away from the starting zone, now im enjoying myself playing this, good improvements.

It has more or less the rythm of Dark Souls 1, but it's much more about positioning since you can cancel your animation by dodging or parrying, but the dodge doesn't have I-frames.Overall I recommend it, behind the jankiness there's a lot of fun

_childDocuments_.review: the game certainly has its share of problems that desperately need to be adressed asap and some minor bugs here and there but for the most part the game works fine and is enjoyable, performance is good too.the environments, world building and setting are just amazing, they remind me of the BLAME comic aesthetic. im pretty sure they drew inspiration from it. music is very cool too.now it really needs to get some stuff fixed, like enemy health bars sometimes not appearing, UI set on "always" not appearing, getting stuck in rocks and that sort of things. the stamina system could get a bit of attention too since its definitely not ideal right now. max base FOV is really low too at least for my tastes  (80º) but it can be easily tweaked with UUU. the double-tap to roll is ♥♥♥♥ too, hope they allow us to rebind it to a single key click.if youre a souls fans and you liked like mortal shell or hellpoint you will 100% like this.

Have faith in Bleak Faith, its an awesome soulslike game.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:It is a diamond in the rough that needs improvement. Hopefully the development will continue. As it is, it's playable but I think it's better to wait for some patches.To situate myself, Elden ring (with controller) and Nioh 2 (with M&K) player. I killed the first boss of Bleak Faith.Yes, the controls are perfectible, the character's movements are sometimes weird. For example, he automatically climbed a small bump that I thought I had to use the jump on. It's a bit like he was weightless. However, some parts of the game are brilliant and I have tried to recognise this in my scores for each area below.10/10 World / level design / exploration10/10 Game atmosphere8/10 Music8.5/10 Graphics5/10 Game design and mechanics6/10 Gameplay6/10 Fun / enjoyment factor [the most important part of the review]4.5/10 User interface9/10 Difficulty - Bosses are very hard - made even more difficult by the gameplay mechanics and control systems, and you start off very weak. _childDocuments_.review: Preface: I have played more than an hour, some game time didn't log? I don't know. This is also, all my opinion and experience. TLDR: Buggy, Janky, weird and even confusing at times. Still a great time, put together by a tiny team, working hard still to release constant updates and improve the game. I recommend it, if you can afford it and know, you won't find AAA standards here but, you'll fund some passionate devs who have put in a lot of work.It's pretty decent tbh. Some highs, some lows but a whole lot of charm, a whole lot pf uniqueness and a whole lot of jank.It is visually very appealing, I really enjoy the world and the style. It's very distinct. i went in expecting more a medieval aesthetic and it definitely has that of course but, you are also like some weird thing fighting robots with a lead pipe at the start? Weirdly though, it does work. The style is helped by it's, to be honest, way too good level design. For the rest of the game to be as janky and rough around the edges as it is, the level design is really good. Open places with no real linear progression, just look around. The downside is, LADDERS. SO many, so long and no real fast way to traverse them. The levels are layered on top of each other, Central Yarnham style, the ladders are just TOO long. However, as this games lacks any 'souls' equivalent, You lose nothing on death. This changes it in a fundamental way. You aren't now exploring with much risk, leading to a fear of exploration almost. You have literally nothing to lose. So you really are encouraged to look around as much as possible. Which you should do, you will need as much help as you can get.Because, this game may differ from it's inspiration in that fundamental area, it is still HARD. For a a few right, and a few wrong reasons. There a lot of notable things about the games combat. It's unique. I thought the one button for attacking would be weird but, no it works well when you get a feel for it. I quite like it. And a HUGE thing that I haven't seen mentioned much? NO iframes. At all. Dodging in this game is literally a dodge. To get out of the way of the attack. Not go through it. And this is really interesting and unique and makes me play differently to every other souls like I have played. As I have never been a blocker or a parryer in those games. This one forces it on you. Because, this games hitboxes are, precise? accurate? all over the place? I DO NOT KNOW. As far as I can tell, very few attacks have connected that I feel like just missed me. BUT, it feels almost as if the attacks are exactly where they appear to be. What I mean is, I can be blocking, and still be hit. Almost like the attack when below my block. And when this was predominantly happening on low sweeping attacks. It adds up. I am really unsure if this is intentional or not. As the game does also have some attacks which want you to jump over them. The first boss will Jump backward, then forward, landing and creating shockwave that you can't dodge through or block. So I was jumping it. Meaning, am I meant to be jumping over his sweeping attacks aswell? I never had a chance to find out. And there is more, those hitboxes being as exact as they seem means that, you have to get CLOSE to a boss to hit it. With the 2 weapons I used on the boss atleast. If you are not IN ITS ASS you will probably miss. Which combined with no iframes REALLY leans towards blocking being the only viable method. Which means you spend a lot of stamina blocking, and then can't attack when you get an opening. Music and sound design are decent. Music is pretty good, sound design is more than passable enough. REALLY not my area of expertise.There are bugs, pet peeves. Like why is controller support so dodgy, i know it was designed for KB&M but, why is that the method you focus on for a souls-like? Player is VERY floaty in the air, leads ti some deaths but, you lose no souls, like I said so. It doesn't feel as bad.Then we come to the things surrounding the game; price, devs/development, value etc. Is it worth the price they are asking? Probably not, I THINK there is enough content to warrant the asking price (I haven't completed it so I don't know for sure) but, with all of the bugs and jank and things it is lacking (again, full controller support). I see why it's a hard ask. However, this is a unique, labour of love by a team of 3 people. 3 PEOPLE. Who are CRANKING out updates. They are doing updates what? daily? Or something like that. Bug fixes, updates, changes. They aren't always some crazy long list but, they are putting in the effort. This isn't a buggy release because the corporate overlords wanted it out of the door faster. It's because these 3 guys can only do so much so fast. That throws it into a different perspective for me. These 3 guys did some impressive work. And I'm happy with the money I spent, especially knowing it went to people who made this because they WANTED TO, not because they needed another release. I'm not ignoring the bad, but i think I can cut them some slack. ONLY because of the support they are showing the game. If they pushed it out and left it as it. It would be different but, this feels like a project these guys care about. And It's nice to see.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. First soulslike styled game in a long while that truly stands out by setting itself apart in some very cool ways, my favorite being the uniqueness of the world setting and environment that to me gives a neverending feeling of the surreal. Combat is very well done and fun, with lots of varying weapons creating a completely different feel from one another. graphics and art design are great and detailed, doing a wonderful job of making the world feel old and apocolyptic and leftover from a time of being very well lived in, while also creating a feeling of isolation for the protagonist in this current age in which the story is set. _childDocuments_.review: 2024:Most of the updates are simply great, and I love the new expansion of locations. Unfortunately, the game is becoming more and more accessible for the mainstream, with the difficulty decreasing and the need for thinking disappearing. Yes, I'm referring to all those childish simplifications: arrows in the form of lights to prevent anyone from getting lost, the climbing hint on the Wormlord, and now the inability to fall when the target lock is active, just why? For example Uranopolis has beautiful new locations that could serve as hints, guiding players to a spot where they can see that the beast isn't flying aimlessly but stops at otherwise inaccessible towers. Instead, players no longer need to fly, they just walk up to Nurgle, never experiencing that "figure out" moment or the thrill of flying between the towers. If the game just expanded without being simultaneously stripped down, it would be absolutely fantastic.NG+? thats amazing stuff, thanks!release day:Congratulations on the game's success! While I haven't finished the game yet, I'd like to give you my first impressions so far. Please note that this is just a short report and not a detailed analysis.The atmosphere of the game is stunning! Sounds are very high quality and music makes at least half of this atmosphere. Uranopolis is my favorite part of the game, and the level design of these locations is simply gorgeous! However, the Ghost Town location doesn't work for me. It looks cheap compared to the other locations, for example the overscaled assets around the train station, like barrels and fences, are terrible. I suggest changing that location.Some of the models need to be replaced, such as the naked zombie alien with a pitchfork. It doesn't fit in with the game's overall aesthetic. Many of the humanoid robots are also weak models, and there are many cool alternatives available on the market that could be implemented.There are many bugs in the game that could have been prevented easy even with one man army QA. While most of them are tolerable but annoying and impact the gameplay experience, others are really bad, such as the stuck weapon bug, which is a common problem for me.The fights need to be tweaked, and the items and abilities need to be rebalanced. I played through the game like a warrior, not using weapon skills, and only using my flux to activate the Power Armor, which I used only against the Nurgei. I found that I didn't need to change my weapon until I found the Lacerators, which are absolutely brutal when combined with certain perks in my build.There's no reason to change your armor for the new thing you find, which is a game design flaw in my opinion. I was good with a low heavy armor (upgraded) and then switched to the Templar, which I upgraded to Mk. 4. There's no reason to change it again, and I will just upgrade it to Mk. 5 when I find it, like with my weapons (Lacerators with 4x 20% Weapon Weight and Arcane bow with 4x Attack Power).Overall, the game is too easy, which is the most disappointing thing of all. After the very promising, challenging and overall epic fight with the first boss, the game became easy because of easy access to upgrades without the need for boss fights, which is a major flaw in game design in my opinion. I miss the boss fights myself on my way through the game. I have fight Aberrant Knight second in the row and it was very easy to defeat, but the third fight was gorgeous again and i enjoyed it wery well, because it was Nurgei and i was on two perks (Vampirism and Vindicator, still using Faussard weapon dropped from the first boss, what is sad itself) and after i killed him (used Power Armor ability agains the "IK wave") i have activated first recalibration, and the Red Knight was a bit of a challenge. However, most of the other things were a bit too easy. When I went underwater for the second recalibration, I hoped there would appear some black knights or something to fight, but that didn't happen. I decided to look online for bosses I have missed on my way in lower locations. However, this was a terrible mistake, as after I killed the Plagued Nemesis and Silicon Visage (both very easy) and upgraded my build with two more perks (Dual Wield Mastery and Combo Brutality) and finaly switched my weapon from Faussard to Lacerators, even the Red Knights fell down too easily. This lowered the difficulty of the game even worse.Now I'm at the beginning of the Desert, and I hope there will be some new challenges. However, the Red Knights on the start are not promising. Don't get me wrong, i just trying to suggest you to revisit few things, because this atmosphere heavy game deserved it!Thank you for this experience! I will update this report after I finish the game.UPDATE:So here we go :)Wormlord was a super cool fight in a super cool place! At first, I just tried to hit him in every part of his body with close combat until I realized that wasn't the way. So I looked for some mechanic to use, but then I realized that he could be hurt really hard with my Arcane Bow - Arrow Twister, and it was the end of the fight. Arrow Twister just has insane OP damage.Right now, after killing the Wormlord, I realized in the keybinding settings that there are buttons for heavy attack and for parry. Throughout the whole game, I used the Vindicator perk and trusted that every 3rd attack is a heavy attack, so my perk was useless the entire game, and I didn't even realize there were things like heavy attack and parry. It's like a warrior who doesn't use skills and just goes with close combat. I really suggest rebalancing a few things because I don't even know about the core mechanics of the game, and my way through the game is very easy anyway.There is a bug in the desert where some enemies spawn half-drowned underground, and another bug, the worse one, is that combat is broken around the place with "sandwurm." Sometimes I can't hit the enemies, and they cannot hit me until I restart the game. Reproduction is just random.Archinquisitor Belisarius was a super cool fight again, but Arrow Twister is just too overpowered in my opinion and makes it too quick and easy again. All the locations, from the desert to the end of the game, are gorgeous, and the atmosphere is amazing!As I expected before, there was no need to change my gear throughout the game, and it is a pity. There would be situations that force you to change your gear and playstyle to pass them. There is no info about the abilities of the sets or something like that, and everything you need is to upgrade your old gear to have the same stats as new ones. It seems like wasted potential.Active abilities are a mystery to me. Half of them are locked, and there is no need to use the active ones, which is wasted potential again. I also don't find any situation to use any of the 600sec boost potions. I would appreciate if there is proper use for them.The final fight is another Arrow Twister stand-up. Whole fight last only for 1m30s :( Please look at this ability. But the ending is breathtaking, and I have really enjoyed this game so far!There is a bug in the end cutscene, bow UI is present there whole time. Check it out in the following video.Mechyas, Bleak Faith Forsaken, final build and last boss fight, no boost potions.  You guys rock! Best regards, M.

_childDocuments_.review: First impression. First souls like game I enjoy more with K and MS than controller. Secondly, the game works differently than the usual souls likes. 1. Dodges have no I-frames so be careful with spacing2. The combat is more akin to monster hunter in terms of pure flow. You cannot spam attacks since they will not combine. You need to basically input attacks in a sequence somewhat in advance to create a Combo; However other than this quite different gameplay which many in the other reviews heavily ignore (which is a shame), the art design is top notch, sound is great overall, optimization is decent and so one. Cant say much more because of lack of playtime. As a first impression the game is so far a solid 7/10 if you can get on with the combat being different. If you can play games like Outward you should feel somewhat at home with this one

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure how well this game is optimized, but it took a very long time for the game to start up. After i'd managed to start playing, even after setting the graphics to the lowest possible, and setting it to 30 fps the game still lags on my 3090.Things that NEED to be changed:1. Dodge rolling needs more I-frames. As of now dodge rolling feels near useless.2. The Dodge roll and dash should be separated. Its very annoying to press the dodge button      twice just to dodge.3. Enemies using ranged weapons or magic need to be re-balanced/Nerf.4. Enemies aggro range needs to be fixed. Enemies currently will endlessly chase the player     even after being lured far away from their original location.5. There is a bug that causes the player character to become immune to all enemy attacks but     at the same time prevents the player from dealing damage to enemies.6. If possible, being able to use 2 handed weapons with one hand.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is alright i guess unless youre fighting a boss. Then the entire system breaks down. Otherwise, the game is beautiful. If you don't get caught on geometry and pushed to your death by an invisible wall then the world these devs have made is masterful. Really really appealing visually and the actual design and layout have been great so far! The atmosphere in some locations is like nothing else I’ve ever played. Giant underground neighborhoods, shaded forests, foggy plazas. The setting just makes you feel like you’re exploring a city built for a purpose but never meant for human habitation. If you’ve read BLAME! it’s honestly less like that and more like Girl’s Last Tour. The architecture feels so purposeful yet so hostile. It’s been one of my favorite aesthetics for years. It also is probably the best performing game on launch in years for me. Zero slowdowns, zero crashes. The game runs like a dream at 4k 60 all ultra for me. Great job. thats it. This game is sick as hell sometimes but completely incompetent others. Thanks

While the game is still rough around the edges (for now), it is the closest thing to Dark Souls 1 that has ever been made in my opinion. I think some additional tweaks to combat and to the story will take this game to the next level and I'm looking forward to what comes next!

_childDocuments_.review: On the Fence?I've been waiting patiently for the game for a while now. The atmosphere and creature design looks fantastic. The mix of fantasy and sci-fi is too irresistible to me. The music is perfect and I enjoy all the little effects. I've not played long, but I've played long enough to know that the controller works well enough and that is the only way I'll play it. I love all the Souls games, but always lose interest in them. I'm hoping this will be different. Another reviewer compared it to playing Skyrim when comparing certain play elements. It does feel like a heavily modded version of Skyrim, without the RPG questing/talking. That helped to push me over the edge to buy and I'm glad it got me over the fence. Buying the game now is an investment. I want more unique experiences, like this game.  I want more vision and creativity by a handful of developers, rather than compromised, bloated, games as service, commercial ventures. The price point is also great. The developers seem to be doing a lot to support the title. Once I saw the latest controller changes in the update notes, I was willing to try it. My controller is out of buttons for all the actions, so I have to use the space bar on the keyboard for inventory, otherwise, everything works fine. It's super easy to change all the graphic settings as well to fine tune how it runs on your PC. I've played games where you change a setting and you have to reboot the game. Here, you can make a ton of changes and immediately get feedback. So much has already been said about what else this game needs to be polished. I'm not going to continue that and just trust the developers to fine tune it. I'm just really happy the game has controller support on PC (using XBOX One controller) and can finally play it now.  To the developers: I appreciate that the game was only made by a handful of really talented people. The creativity shown in the work is quite an achievement. You got a lot of us to pay money for your art and some fun. While many consumers seem so jaded now days, know that there are plenty of people out here who are rooting for this special game.  Stay positive and good luck to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is very solid, bosses are great. Weapon inpact feels nice. Fun abilities, etc. (+you can climb onto bigger enemies and stabby stab.)Art is great, lots of great scenery and intresting creatures.Level design is really good. Similar to The first dark souls in that you never quite feel like you're supposed to be where you're at (In a good way). Progressing feels very rewarding. (+interconnectedness, just on a much bigger scale.)A bit janky, but sort of expected from a game of this size by such a small team. It's improved drastically the 3 days since launch, but expect some jank and glitches.One of the most solid games I've played for quite awhile.

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals, the atmosphere, the mood are well done. For this artistic achievement, I applaud the small indie dev team. Good work!However, there are caveats. My complaints are more on the technical side of things. The controls are not what I expect. Janky, I suppose. Very twitchy. They are quick and responsive which is good for combat, but not for carefully navigating the heights of an abandoned superstructure. I would prefer to start in a safer place so that I could play around with and get a better feel for the controls.Also, the UI needs improvement. The Backpack icons need labels and the coordinates text is too small.With some more work, this game will be great. It has a lot of potential. I will update this review as I continue.

_childDocuments_.review: *UPDATED REVIEW:After 59 hours, I gave up. I have never played a game so janky before with so many dead ends. I got to the underground desert area but the game glitched so bad that it robbed me of all my desire to continue. I was playing on a top-of-the line 2023 Razer Blade 16 with i9 and RTX4090 - and this game STILL crashed so many times with "Fatal Error" messages. _childDocuments_.review: I love this game. The mechanics are clunky and the game is a bit rough around the edges. That being said the combat is well thought out and fun. There is a big learning curve, and you have to figure a lot of things out for your self. The game definitely reminds me of the first dark souls title, but separates itself from it with a combo melee system and a no eye-frame dodge. My only true complaint is the controller support. I Can't wait to see what future updates bring.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, can't recommend it in its current state... hell, the flaws of the game are so deep down to its core that I highly doubt I will ever recommend it.The clumsy character movement is horrible... uncontrollable would be an understatement. For a soulslike game (one which strong punishes mistakes) this is a terrifying disaster, a game-breaker that is enough to force you to stay away from it.The combat, man... where do I even start. It is one of the most unfunny things in the game. I was blasted with some bizarre hitboxes. It looks like the game draws graphics to let you know the range of enemy skills, but the real hitbox is bigger. The dodge system feels pointless with no iframes. When an enemy does a sweep attack, it is almost impossible to dodge it.Some items, like the shield, work in an obfuscated manner.Looks like the game is full of bad mechanics without a counterbalance to make it just a little bit funnier.Aesthetically, the level design is somewhat nice, too much fog imo... BUT, mechanically speaking, the big problem is that navigating the scenarios feels like walking on a lifeless wallpaper; the artistic composition is fine, but when visiting long distant areas you end up in incredibly empty places with no soul at all; even worse, some areas are difficult to tell apart from others thanks to the choice of colors, so the composition turns in a maze. One can, maybe, tolerate this aspect of the game... until you wonder if that jump could kill you because you are not supposed to go in that way.When, in Dark Souls 1, for example, you unlocked a shortcut, your reaction was more like... a pleasant surprise. In this game its more like a: "oh god, I was going around in circles and now I'm lost".The verticality is another aspect I didn't like. They solved many areas' connections with stupidly long ladders. Feels like rushed and poor-level design.The UI man, holy s. What a neglected aspect of the game. Not only traversing the menu is a nightmare; but sometimes the same button does different things when in different locations. Sometimes a button will go back, but sometimes it won't. Such a little thing can be frustrating and ruins the experience of the game as a whole. Some aspects of the UI are so unprofessional, man, that feels and looks like a child's collage.I can't recommend it, I think it is not a good soulslike nor a good game. The core mechanics needs serious polish, and maybe two years from now the game will be decent.I know they took the risk to work and realize an idea, which is much more than many people who comment here ever did. I didn't mean to be harsh with my opinion, just honest.I feel like they knowingly released the game aware of its state so they could make some money on this platform and dedicate themselves to improving it.I wish they could polish and improve the game, because clearly there is an idea that needs more love and work.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: After not even 24 hours, they already fixed both of the issues below. Devs are working hard on making it run well off the bat, and as intended, from the beginning. With those things out of the way; Bleak Faith is a relatively fresh take on a super saturated soulslike genre, and seeks to shirk that moniker to try and do something all its own, a feat they manage to succeed in doing to great effect.  There's a heavier focus on exploring the open world and environments with significant  moments that get my blood flowing and anxiety spiked like they haven't since playing world 3 in Demon's Souls. It's a pretty brutally hard game early on, but it begins to feel a lot better as you find more gear/weapons because  in a traditional sense: all your stats and skills come from the weapons and armor you find/earn, as well as perk points from defeating challenging enemies. The game is doing its own thing while still having nods to the genre, the world feels, looks, and sounds amazing. I'm still pretty early in on the main release and with the above 'fixes' there's been no bugs/crashes/issues. It's insane to imagine only three people worked on this entire game. Give it a try with an open mind, and you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely not ready. Controls are so clunky you'll end up running off the cliff trying to "dash" because you moved your joy stick 0.00001 mm forward. _childDocuments_.review: The worst PC souls like game I've played. - Clunky controls. - Shaders going haywire or making my gaming unit suddenly lag even with specs well above recommended. - Controls and combat that feels like bumble gum. - enemy Laser attacks have colliders and can stun lock you?!!! - a bug where two music tracks would overlap and would persist beyond the boss fight even up to the main hub..- Enemies for some reason phasing into another dimension (the mesh of the background like a wall or on the floor) AND STILL DAMAGE you with thier attacks- The lighting on some of the efx looks like a flash grenade - and in a painful way (I had to lower this setting but didn't help.)- also the inquisitor boss fight is the most nonsense boss I've fought in a souls game. just add in stupid ads to make the fight  artificially harder, worse you cant life steal from the other ranged enemies - absolutely unfair and just throws in range enemies in the arena coz lol this boSs HarD. Terrible trash boss design. This boss fight made me realize how unfairly imbalanced technomancy + range combat vs a melee buildThe interesting setting, mysterious story and approach to crafting and upgrading stats is good but everything else just ruins that.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't enjoy writing reviews but I do like this game, so while I won't go into any real detail, I will at least say this is more of a 'mixed' recommendation in that I'm enjoying myself and want to show my support to bump up that Steam review score, even setting aside the jank and glitchiness. Still, I'm not really sure I would want to recommend it to anyone else who was on the fence about it - I love the art and the world and the combat doesn't feel half bad either, plus some of their ideas are downright inspired (your own portable respawn point found pretty early on that you can just slap down before you go to menace some horrible creature? phenomenal!) but it really does need a lot of polishing and some more quality of life features (ladder sliding, etc) before I'd feel comfortable wholeheartedly telling anyone else to buy it, even if I'm personally having a great time. I'm rooting for you, devs!

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Souls and Nier Automata had a baby together and its name is Bleak Faith.If you like either of the aforementioned, then you will like this game too.Just try and look past the initial feeling of clunkiness. That's mostly a stamina issue you can mitigate as you level upPersonally I wish the game had co-op, because there is 1 boss that is incredibly hard and I've gotten him down to 1% 4 times and everyone who finished this game knows who I'm referring to.For anyone reaching this point in the game I advice you to have a good stamina build, because you're going to have to dodge roll and jump a lot. Warning to people with Epilepsy like myself;Make sure you medded up. There are a lot of bright red/blue/yellow flashing lights during some fights, especially the one I've mentioned above (extremely bright firetruck red). I have the night version and I still, with meds, had moments where I had to take a break because I felt dizzy.Other than that, this is an absolutely awesome game and I can see this becoming a cult classic. Even if the community is small.I sincerely hope the devs will expand upon this universe, because its so appealing. And those gritty dark ages, dystopian and futuristic styles mixed together is amazing. Especially all that concrete and steel.By the way devs; swimming down into the abyss dodging those baddies was really scary. Well done!
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a bit janky, a bit bugged, and still needs a bit of work on the combat, but  if you can go past that:The atmosphere is absoulutely incredible (even more so if you like the manga BLAME), I mean I would've bought the game for the atmosphere alone.If you discovered Dark Souls or Demon's souls when they were not really known by the public, and you treasured them for the clunky, weird, uncompromising thing they were, this feels a bit like that. If you can argue that the souls like genre has become mainstream now, this is the niche side of it.Also tremendous achievement for just a team of 3.

I like many other people were expecting this game to be finished and play like the trailers and early footage, but were instead treated to a broken mess that was completely unplayable.Lets start off with whats wrong!1. Gamepads and controls will not work no mater what xbox and sony I tried both.2. Keyboard controls a buggy at best.3. The camrea randomly spins when controllers are plugged in and yes I tried the fixes4. inventory was completly broken for me and I could only equip armor no matter how hard I tried I was stuck with the base weapon.5. Bugs and glitches everywhere such as enemies spawning from breaking creates and boxsWhat bleak faith got right!1. Bleak faith has a absolutely dark but beautiful world and story brimming with potential making one feel a sense of wonder.2. The graphics are actually pretty decent.3. fps and game runs pretty smoothly.4. Enemy types seemed pretty interesting and not to boring.5. The games difficulty from what I could manage to play was that of what one would expect from a souls borne6. Sound design was decent at best from what I could tell.In conclusion I would have really loved to play this game if it wasn't so broken!I think given time this game could have lots of potential if they seriously overhaul the controls and bugs.Sadly though I will have to make this game the first game I have ever Refunded on steam, I can not bring myself to play it any more in its current state.If the game ever gets fixed I will however think about picking it up once again when it is on sale to give it a second chance. _childDocuments_.review: Summary6/10, atmosphere carries this entire game, combat is barely playable. I would recommend this game just for the atmosphere alone, but prepared to die and for no reason that is yours.Pros- Atmosphere is the best I have seen in any game to date.- Level design is amazing, competes with DS1 and I would say surpasses it. I find myself always getting blown away by the amount of routes available and how they all connect together. Everything fits so well together to feel like a maze but also be connected.- Create your own checkpoint system. Amazing idea to be able to create your own respawn location. The level is massive, and being able to place a homonculus anywhere is fantastic.- Enemy design is extremely unique and actually freaks me out. Most other games have classic enemy designs that don't strike too much fear into me. The enemies in this game, are truly terrifying. - Upgrade/Armor/Weapon Items are abundant enough to insensitive trying out other play styles, but rare enough to feel useful.Cons- In a game revolving around combat I would have hoped the combat was better. Input delay and unregistered inputs ruin the flow of almost all combat experiences.- Button remapping, DOES NOT WORK. (Edit: updated came out 03/11 which fixed this, helped with combat a lot. Controllers are now viable.)-Bosses sometimes do not spawn at all, locking you in the boss room forcing you to die to make the boss respawn. Some of these runs could be very long if you did not create a respawn near by, you have to go through the entire level again.- Enemy collision is inconsistent. Enemies walk through walls and items all the time. The giant enemies can kill you if you jump on them and they walk through a wall to fall through the map. - Elevators will kill you randomly. I have fallen through elevators, also if you touch the ground below an elevator, even if it is at ground level with you, there is a death wall.OverallThis game has unrivaled atmosphere and level design. I have never seen a more beautiful and interesting game. Since I stepped into the world, I was hooked. I wanted to explore everything and understand everything, But the combat is some of the most frustrating and unfair I have ever experienced. I find myself dying not by my own mistakes, but by the games inability to function.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. It had a rough start and I avoided it for over a year until they released a major patch fixing a lot of issues but I kept my eye on it the whole time. _childDocuments_.review: Its rough giving a non-recommendation on a game that is obviously a passion project.I gave it its two hours but decided to refund.Despite a stunning setting as well as impressive character armors and weapons this game struggles with just not being polished enough. The UI and menus are odd to navigate. I found myself being frustrated just trying to see what I do and don't have. To be honest, the UIs look like what you would find in a starter UE4 project.When I was fighting the first boss a basic enemy glitched through the wall and attacked me. Frequently when looking at my character he would be holding his weapon with his hand out of place and the weapon kind of floating.There might be a setting for this but to block/parry you first have to pull out your weapon by attacking, which makes responding to surprise threats difficult.The movement feels quite floaty and I found myself jumping off edges on accident over and over.When climbing ladders my characters legs would glitch and kind of teleport around.The combat system is actually quite fun - having to time attacks to extend combos is a neat way to engage players and make them focus during already intense fights, but stamina management in this game just felt awful. I wanted stamina to not have such a big delay from recovering after doing anything as this grinded combat to a halt where I would dodge a big attack, not have enough stamina to do anything, and sit there for a solid 5-6 seconds and stamina slowly rose back to full.Finding that balance is really hard I understand, but to me it felt too slow to be enjoyable.Overall, I think this is the shell of a really fantastic game that just needs either more time or a slightly larger team with specialized abilities in the areas where the game is struggling. I am willing to revisit this game in the future and purchase again if the quality rises and I genuinely wish the best for the devs who I can tell worked hard on this.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty good so far. There seems to currently be an issue with high fps so I strongly recommend keeping it at 90 or 60 fps. Going higher will make movement feel very floaty and you will go much faster than is intended. Other than that the combat is surprisingly good.The world is great, certain areas are better than others but in general the world is interconnected like Dark Souls 1. The design of the world is the real highlight though, you will encounter some very unique architecture and level design.There are no levels, your character's power is pretty much purely based on your gear. Which is nice as you can switch between builds whenever you want.As long as you are not expecting a AAA game this game should live up to your expectations. The game is very ambitious, which can lead to some things feeling half-baked but everything comes together well enough.Note: Highly recommend using keyboard and mouse for now. You'll get used to it pretty quickly. Also when you get access to placing your own homunculus make sure you use it often. Save points are pretty sparse, you are intended to make use of your ability to place your own temporary save point.

_childDocuments_.review: Only 2 hours in, I already noticed some major game-breaking issues. Mechanics are super laggy, and the game is bursting full of bizarre bugs. The visuals and animations are very jerky and are severely lacking in fluidity. They are even out of sync with the audio. There are a ton of weird combat delays, where I am being hit by attacks several seconds after they happen. During the rare periods that combat seems to function somewhat normally, combat feels like a boring slog. With seemingly no iFrames, I am running around enemies in circles or running away from combat in the hopes of finding a small opening to attack, since dodging is so unresponsive and completely pointless. Everything about this game is unfinished, and it feels like a chore to play. For 3 developers, it is an impressive project, but unfortunately, the game does not hold up to its advertising at all. I hope that it will be drastically improved in the future. Until that point, I have returned Bleak Faith for a refund, but will be watching the game as development continues and more patches come out to address the game’s core issues.P.S.As a massive Elden Ring enthusiast, I can 1000% confirm that this game was using assets/animations developed by FromSoftware. The most obvious might be the first boss using part of the Banished Knight moveset. I am glad to hear that the devs supposedly replaced all these animations though, and I hope that this is true.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: Great game overall - worth trying if you are interested in the genre.  It still has some rough edges to work out with bugs, but Devs have been pretty good continuing to fix bugs.  Also, was good to see they focus more now on fixing bugs in latest patches and not focus on nerfing perks or player.  At first they were focusing too much on nerfs to player perks and overbalancing which was not good, but now they are better focusing on fixing bugs lately which is better and most important.  Also it's good they will focus on adding newgame+ and coop in future it seems too - these are good and best things to focus on also.Pros...- Very Cool unique game world and environments.  Mix of old souls style with future dystopian landscape- Good combat - even though some of the controls aspects are a little different, I was able to adjust to it and enjoy that it has some different aspects to this and is not exactly like other games- Well designed levels with many paths and shortcuts to explore- Good variety of cool looking gear and weapons and items- Nice Boss and enemy design- Good balance currently, its not too easy and not too hard, nicely balanced at the moment - hope they don't alter that and overbalance or mess this up, but right now it is decent- Lots of value/play time if you like to fully explore the levelsMedium things...- There are some cool perks and Abilities as they are now, but a few other perks feel a little useless and needing bumping up or adding some new additional effects to feel more noticeable when chosen.  I would say though that anything they alter should not remove any aspects of current perks, only add effects to needed ones or buff.  Don't nerf any because picking a perk on character is irreversible currently and that is a bad blow to players if they reduce/nerf any perks or change them completely and player regrets choosing it because it changes their build and they are stuck with it - so at this point they should only buff or add new additional effects to perks-Also some abilities show as locked and cannot be unlocked at all yet it seems, so they will add these soon I hope for more variety - we do need more abilities to choose from- Great Soundtrack, but could use a few more tracks so we get more variety.  The music there is great I just hope they can add a little more for variety- Hope we get some unique new gear/armor/weapons that has new abilities added with newgame+ to increase build variety and give us new things to find and increase game longevity- Coop online and new game+ not there in game yet, but seems they both will be added.  This will be cool when it happensCons...- Still has some bugs.  I have had a few freezes where game crashes, possibly due to a memory leak.  At least I can then shut it down in Task manager, but this still needs to be fixed because you can lose progress since last save and also its not cool when any game crashes.  - Possibly still could use some general optimization too.  CPU usage can spike pretty high sometimes leading to higher than normal CPU temps and random ramping up of CPU fans.  This is more noticed here than on many other games I own which are just as demanding graphically.  Hopefully they can find a way to reduce this a bit and even it out.  Also, one rare case in underwater level where this happens with GPU briefly also, but that is just a short time - the CPU temps/usage thing is more often and hopefully can be adjusted in patches.Overall a good game.  Recommended and worth supporting and hoping the Devs continue to fix remaining bugs and improve and support it.  Hopefully they will add new content in the future as well after the bugs are fixed and after newgame+ and coop are added.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Dark Souls 1? Can you handle a little bit of insignificant jank?If yes, GET THIS GAME WITHOUT SECOND THOUGHT.I liked this game made by 3 people way more than other soulslikes from much bigger AA studios.It does have some jank, graphics aren't anything special (but they serve their purpose), it's not super polished, but gosh darn it it's a great game at its core. I had noticed the game long ago, but I did wait to get it after all these updates and I'm glad I did, I can definitely recommend it at its current state, I suppose a good amount of the negative reviews were written about older versions.Exporation, atmosphere are definitely its greatest qualities as many have already said. I'm not big on indies, smaller games etc. and if something doesn't play well enough to satisfy me, I will drop it (I found Atlas Fallen clunky for example, a game by a much bigger studio and I dropped it after a couple of hours). I had no problem with this.I don't want to write much, I think the best way I can sum this game up, is that it's a smaller AA Dark Souls 1, with even crazier exploration and a great sci-fi, gloomy atmosphere with huge brutalist structures. If that sounds like something you would enjoy, game is an easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Preliminary thoughts: I'm only about one hour in and am really enjoying it. World design is very cool so far, the focus on item stats VS levelling up is a unique take in this genre, and the first few shortcut loops I have found have left me very excited to explore more. I have a few gripes with things like dodging off ledges, the free camera when locked on an enemy, and some UI confusion (still no clue how to equip a secondary weapon like a bow despite the controls listing a switch weapon button).  Despite all the warnings about controllers, I have found using one completely fine, though the locked axis movement that was clearly designed for a mouse + keyboard experience does take some getting used to.I will likely come back and update this once I am further or have finished the game, but as it stands I'm finding it well worth the relatively low price of admission. And the devs seem very keen to make this the best experience they can, so it's only going to go uphill from here.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleak Faith: Forsaken

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful, expansive, and full of interesting and frightening enemies. The world is as much (if not more) vertical than it is horizontal; and several areas are so unique and strange they approach non-Euclidean design Things I've Done In This Game:Climb on the backs of giants to defeat themCompleted Parkour puzzles for sick lootRan from massive lasers as I fight off enemiesPlace a custom spawn point right before a tough battleRide an absolute unit I call Carter from the base of an area to the topBugs I've encountered in the game (Day 1 Release)A Boss didn't spawn once out of 12 times I tried to fight him, had to reset.I fell through an elevator and died of fall damageI placed a custom spawn that put me under the map (It was on rubble and def a place I wasn't meant to have climbed to)Overall: This is an absolutely HUGE game. 12 hours in and I've found 3 bosses and beaten 2. There is at least 20 different areas. And this game was made by 3 people. I am flabbergast a dev team this small has made something, that I think, is as good or better than Dark Souls 1 was on release. PS: Went to sleep after playing 11 hours straight day 1. Woke up day 2 and there was already a patch. Devs made this game as a labor of love and that isn't stopping because the game is out. Please, PLEASE give this game a chance.PPS: If you do try this game I recommend a couple things:1. There are no I-Frames. This is a choice. Be careful with positioning cause if an enemies weapon comes in contact with ur character model, you WILL take damage. Even if you are midroll.2. The combat is not a button masher. Every weapon requires different timing to complete combos. Combos properly executed cost less stamina and can do extra damage. The combo timing will take practice on any new weapon you pick up, but once you get a weapons timing down, man is that a sweet feeling.3. Find a new weapon ASAP, the starting pipe has a very short range. {[Mild Spoiler] A decent claymore can be found pretty early by trying to go up as much as possible when you start out}

First of all the style and setting. it is so epic, so charmed and reminds me of impressions from the movie inception. Those deep urban residential structures of the 20th lying in ruins, piling up to surreal heights, the brutalism (architectual) and the audio (ambient and music) are at the highest level of synergy i have ever seen. This makes you feel like seeing the world for the first time as a kid. Greatness doesn't even touch it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a bit late to the party for this game, I did not grab it when it first launched, and I heard there was a lot wrong with it, so I gave it a hard pass. I am glad I waited a bit; this game has seen some meaningful changes from my understanding, they added a leveling system and boss scaling, there are a lot of bugs ironed out(granted this game still has bugs). I can say throughout the entire playthrough, I never crashed once; the only issue I found was that enemies would not attack me for some reason, and I could not deal damage, though a restart did fix this.Overall, I really enjoyed my time with it, the atmosphere was amazing, the world was something fun to traverse and I never felt like the game put damage sponges for enemy encounters in my path. The soundtrack was amazing as well, the hard guitar riffs when I was tackling multiple enemies at once or running for my life, brought about a sense of dread. Not without mentioning the ominous choir vocals in the background while traversing a desert castle, there was so much to this game, and I feel the only problem that I truly had with it is the entire starting area, it’s bland and disjointed, then the leveling system seems kind of out of step with the game as I maxed my level before moving on to the fourth zone, just exploring picking up items was enough to get me maxed out in under a few hours.Good Game in its current state, I recommend it while it is on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: HI,I m a big fan of this style of game and I finished this one. _childDocuments_.review: Okay, it is somewhat janky, but so far I really enjoy it. The movement does feel a bit floaty. You feel like you are moving across the ground, and not walking/running on it. It took a bit to get used to in the beginning, and I don't think I should default to walking with my weapons drawn just to feel like I am walking normally. Sometimes I question how I didn't hit an enemy, and sometimes I question how it didn't hit me. It feels weird at times to go down a long path and have it be a dead end. That is where my complaints end, though. The atmosphere scratches an itch I didn't know I had, and it scratches it good. I feel compelled to continue exploring, and it feels like an adventure in an unknown land in all the best ways. Getting new gear is really satisfying. Once I got heavy armor, it felt like walking in the game was a bit more natural. I think the devs didn't quite no how to make a fast character work well. Combat feels like it has impact most of the time. Many paths circle back and connect to old previous areas in neat ways. I'm really excited to see where the adventure leads.Also, it runs pretty decent on Steam Deck. Turn down Anti-Aliasing to High and Post Processing to High and leave everything else at High/Epic as the settings default to, and framerate generally averages to 36-40. I will come back later for a final review.

_childDocuments_.review: Double edit: with the latest patches getting controller support working really well (along with other improvements) I'd say this is my top favorite soulslike, period. It gave me flashbacks to my first DS1 run, with all the fear and mystery. This team NAILED the vibe that I love. As you play, you'll realize how much of the map is open to you right after the first boss. Great replayability, as once you're past the intro you can basically dash to anything you want for your build, so long as you've memorized the sprawling maze of a world!Edit: With a good bit more time into the game, I want to add that the world exploration and freedom are just incredible. It's very reminiscent of DS1 in the best ways. I found an unassuming ladder well hidden behind some set dressing off the critical path and instead of leading to an item it lead to an entirely new area. Surprises like that are frequent!It's got rough edges for sure, but the atmosphere and exploration are really top notch. Took a bit to get used to playing with mouse and keyboard, and I'd like it if controllers got better support in the future, but everything works well enough to have a lot of fun with. I especially liked the first boss. It also runs very well on my machine - 4k with everything maxed and a rock solid 60fps - much better than a lot of recent AAA releases on PC. I hope it keeps getting touched up with patches, because I think it's worth players and developers to stick with.

_childDocuments_.review: For me this game is no less than visionary. The vision of a game I always wanted to play, of a world I wanted to explore and experience, with this kind of atmosphere to completely loose myself in. Bleak Faith Forsaken does all that. It does it in a way of using elements of existing ideas, yet creating something absolutely unique and special. The feeling of both unfathomable vastness, mystery and insignificance accompanies every step.If this game was developed by From Software, it would most likely be my favourite game of all times (those before at least). But it wasn't. It is only three people with big ambitions. Too big? I don't think so. Though I won't ignore its flaws - and it still has a few - I would much more regret if this concept had never been put to life: a playable fever dream for those susceptible.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, now that I've beaten the game I can finally give it a proper review instead of just posting a meme bashing the latest Fromsoft title.Bleak Faith: Forsaken is an action-rpg from Archangel Studios, an independent developer team which consists of approximately 3 people (I haven't been able to find exact numbers and I don't want to go on their discord to find out). Game takes heavy inspiration from a lot of different titles, from videogames to manga, but ultimately it manages to be its own thing.Story is pretty much nonexistent. You get a basic premise and there are some NPCs that give you a few sentences talking about what they're doing, but beyond that you're free to explore the omnistructure on your own. Lore is also lacking, primarily because items don't have any description. While in games like Dark Souls or Nioh you can read item descriptions and get some idea of what they were used for or who they belonged to, here you get none of that. Find a weird looking item or equipment piece? Good luck figuring out what the hell it is or what it was used for, because game sure as hell won't tell you.The visuals are a mixed bag. Game can look gorgeous at times, primarily due to its artstyle. The underwater area with bioluminescent snakes and the towers with a giant dragon flying around along with Ghost Town that felt like something out of Silent Hill were particular highlights. A lot of areas also have extremely low textures to the point that it looks like you're not even supposed to be able to walk on them. See a rock with blurry texture in another game? It might be an out of bounds area and may not even have collision. See a rock like that in Bleak Faith? Business as usual, it's the intended route, obviously.Gameplay has also received mixed reception from a lot of players. Game certainly isn't balanced well: fast, agile weapons like katanas or daggers are preferable to heavier weapons like claymore or heavy axes. Both the player and enemies have poise, but enemy poise can be easily destroyed with quick attacks, even if you are using an actual toothpick. Player on the other hand has incredible amount of poise even with light armor. I tested a fully upgraded samurai set, which is categorized as light armor by the game, and I could easily tank through the final boss' hits and kill them off. I can't even imagine how the game plays if you have a full heavy armor set with associated perks. A lot of weapons also come with special attacks, similar to weapon arts from Dark Souls 3 or Elden Ring or various combos from Nioh. They require mana to use and can be absurdly powerful, though they do also require upgraded intelligence, so later on your standard attacks will likely outdamage whatever special abilities your weapon might have. It should also be mentioned that while game has been compared to Dark Souls a lot, I didn't really feel like it plays that similarly to the Fromsoft titles overall, unless we just count any action game that's not a character action game like DMC a soulslike.Another issue is that game has a lot of different mechanics that are ultimately underutilized. There's climbing, with actual proper animations for it, but it's only used 2 times in the entire game, including the tutorial. There's swimming, but it only exists for a single area that lasts for maybe 15 minutes at most. On the other hand your character can climb ledges at any point, even after jumping, though which ledges they'll actually grab feels very arbitrary. Either those were set manually by the developers or game doesn't detect ledges properly, and considering that I've been able to get out of bounds that way, I highly doubt developers set those ledges manually. Another underutilized mechanic is giant climbing. It sounds like something out of Dragon's Dogma or Shadow of the Colossus, but in reality all you do is get on a giant, mash attack and pray that you get its HP down before it throws you off and potentially one shots you. There's no strategy involved in fighting giants. At best it's a waste of time, at worst it's a chore.Game also features perks and special abilities your character can use. Perks give big buffs to specific abilities, such as dual wielding, or might grant you vampirism, though some of them are either very weak or downright bugged. For example, illusionist, which is supposed to create an illusion when you attack, barely worked. I know that the chance is low, but at times I forgot that I had that perk in the first place. As for abilities, they are special skills that you can use similarly to the weapon abilities. Strangely enough game has 16 slots for them, but 8 of them are locked and I didn't unlock them even after beating the game. Either it's cut content, they are well hidden or developers are planning to release a DLC, which, considering the game's overall reception so far, is a very bold move. The camera can also be an issue at times, particularly when fighting giants, but overall I didn't have many issues with it.Bosses are for the most part pretty forgettable and there also isn't a lot of them. They do have pretty varied movesets, and game does try to give them unique gimmicks, but overall they aren't really anything special with maybe one or two exceptions. The music is great. This I can say for a fact. I enjoyed the ambient tracks, I enjoyed boss tracks, everything really.Game is very buggy and has a lot of jank, both in combat and in controls and overall movement. I personally haven't encountered anything gamebreaking, but my friend did have some bugs that soured his experience, and I've seen people have issues like falling through elevators as they're moving, though that only happened to me when I tried jumping on  one, and even then it only happened once on a very specific elevator, so your mileage may vary. But this is in no way a polished game. Keep that in mind.Overall, while Bleak Faith has a lot of issues I personally had enjoyed it a lot. Exploration and combat were fun, visuals could be very impressive at times, and game has a good variety of enemies. Do however keep in mind that I have very high tolerance to janky games, so unless you are a huge fan of the genre or have been following developers for years, maybe wait for a few patches to sort things out.

_childDocuments_.review: Unplayable. Please look at my profile, I live for Souls-Like games. It's not a skill issue like some of the people with two braincells who can't do anything but simp for gamedevs would have you believe. I've done no death / SL1 runs in many of the Soulsborne games.These are the worst controls I have ever experienced. It's not a different approach to RPGs like the devs say in their release post, it's simply horrible. A different approach to the souls formula is something like Sekiro. This game is floaty, unresponsive and unprecise. If you dedicate four years of your time to develop a Souls-Like you would expect that they at least sort of understand the basic principles of what makes the combat of these games so good. Just adding a simple stamina bar is just not how this works. Lock on is inconsistent, your characters attacks are camera locked and there's no weight to your / your enemies' attacks. I was ready to forgive a lot due to the 3-man dev team. Dark Souls and Dark Souls 2 can both have some serious jank and I was expecting similar jank from this game. I feel like in half an hour of playtime I experience more jank than I have ever in all Soulsborne games combined. I was ready to have the world design carry this game, but the combat is so bad that even if the world design is 10x better than Dark Souls it won't be able to justify the state of the combat."Oh no but he has only 30 minutes of playtime". If something is bad, it is bad. If my arm is broken and twisting the wrong way I dont need to run around with a broken arm for 2 more days just to be sure its broken. Same thing applies here.If the physics are locked to the FPS then why is the game not automatically locked to 60/90/120 or whatever the FPS for the intended experience are?JANK/10
