_childDocuments_.review: Title: Embarking on an Epic Journey: A Glowing Review of Final Fantasy IIn the vast realm of role-playing games, there stands a timeless classic that paved the way for an entire genre: Final Fantasy I. Developed by Square (now Square Enix) and originally released in 1987, this iconic title has left an indelible mark on gaming history, captivating players with its rich narrative, innovative game play mechanics, and enchanting world.From the moment you step into the shoes of the Warriors of Light, Final Fantasy I plunges you into a fantastical realm brimming with adventure and mystery. The game's story line is a masterclass in fantasy storytelling, weaving a tale of prophecy, ancient evils, and the enduring power of hope. As you journey across the land, encountering diverse landscapes and meeting a cast of memorable characters, you'll find yourself utterly immersed in the epic saga.One of Final Fantasy I's greatest strengths lies in its innovative game play mechanics, which were groundbreaking for their time and continue to captivate players to this day. The game introduced the revolutionary concept of party-based combat, allowing players to assemble a team of diverse characters with unique abilities and skills. This strategic element adds depth to battles, requiring careful planning and coordination to emerge victorious against the myriad foes that stand in your way.Furthermore, Final Fantasy I is renowned for its iconic job system, which allows players to customize their characters' abilities by assigning them different roles, such as warrior, mage (white, black, or red), or thief. This flexibility encourages experimentation and strategic thinking, as you tailor your party to suit your preferred play style and tackle the challenges that lie ahead.Beyond its captivating narrative and innovative game play, Final Fantasy I boasts a timeless aesthetic that continues to enchant players with its charm and beauty. From the intricately designed character sprites to the stunning environments and evocative musical score, every aspect of the game is crafted with meticulous attention to detail, creating a truly immersive experience that stands the test of time.In conclusion, Final Fantasy I is not just a game; it's a landmark in gaming history, a testament to the enduring power of imagination and creativity. With its captivating story line, innovative game play mechanics, and timeless aesthetic, it's no wonder that this classic title continues to captivate players across generations. Whether you're a seasoned veteran or a newcomer to the world of RPGs, Final Fantasy I is an unforgettable journey that deserves to be experienced by all.

_childDocuments_.review: GREETINGS FELLOW ZOOMERS.Slight disclaimer I haven't touched a JRPG in ages if not decades.Did you play Stranger of Paradise, A Realm Reborn/Endwalker or XV and want to get into the series?Are you too young to know what a NES is? Or how to emulate it?Did the original prove to be too much of a CBT session with your least favourite dominatrix and you wish for something better?Then, fear not: the pixel remaster is the choice for you! With ground breaking QoL features such as a minimap, easier levelling and an auto battle function you can now enjoy the first entry of a classic franchise without much hassle while detracting little from the original experience.The spritework is good and easy on the eyes. I liked the effects a lot, some were really flashy and cool.The music is great, a lot of rather melodic pieces that really give an "old jrpg vibe" such as Chaos Temple, boss battle themes and the overworld theme. The story is initially played straight and it only gets weirder as you progress. The dialogue of some NPCs and interactables is rather amusing and some NPCs even give hints on how to progress the story.The gameplay might prove lackluster for some as the difficulty was definitely lowered, but it's perfect for someone who wants to get into the series and not suffer reloading saves every other battle and crafting complex strategies. The random battles might be slightly annoying but I'll just say it's a product of its time :DPersonally, I enjoyed it at a casual pace and definitely recommend to anyone who is like me and wants to get into the Final Fantasy franchise and enjoy the story without grinding endlessly or following intricate walkthroughs.See you in FFII

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy is a classic RPG and the start of an impressive legacy of games given the FInal Fantasy franchise this game spawned. The game itself is solidly build with plenty of repeatability built into the game. There is something that one picking up this game needs to be aware of. This game was first released in 1987 making it a retro game. This is not a bad thing in and of itself. I got it myself for nostalgia and still enjoy when played with my modern RPG game library. However, the fact that this is a retro game means that certain expectations need to understood when playing this game. First, the graphics are are very obviously pixels with a rather narrow range of colors. Roughly half of all the monsters you fight are re-skins of other monster sprites. If graphics are high priority for you in the selection of your games you might want to pass on Final Fantasy 1.Another thing to consider is the game length. A player that pays attention and has an Idea of what they are doing can complete the main quest line and the couple of optional quest lines in 8 to 10 hours of game play. Someone who is good a speed runs can probably trim that time down a bit. This is not a problem with Final Fantasy 1 in itself. The game is epic in length for its time. Technology has simply marched on with standard RPG game lengths significantly increasing as a consequence.I have had loads of fun playing this game and will be playing it more in the future. I have highlighted the negatives in this review because one needs to be aware of the limitations when getting a retro game. FF1 is one of the oldest computer RPGs still available for modern computers to my personal knowledge. Any fan of RPGs will enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I always liked RPGs, be it pen-and-paper or in the form of video games. I was vaguely aware of the subgenres of the latter, but never much cared. Turns out what I was playing all my life were CRPGs. And ARPGs. The odd MMORPG in between. What never crossed my screen though were JRPGs. And, yes, having no real connection to Japanese culture for most of my life, the “J” in JRPG put me off rather than enticed me – being heavily biased by (false) preconceptions of the “world of weeb” – I have seen enough hentai to know where this is going (I have not). All this of course while being blissfully ignorant of the fact how many staples of video game history, many beloved by me, originated in Japan. What can I say, I was a hypocrite, plain and simple.Getting older, maybe wiser – definitely more daring – while not necessarily taking a plunge, I dipped my toes in the odd body of otaku water. An anime here, a manga there.Finding out about kawaii metal. And it wasn’t that long ago when the “J” in JRPG completely lost its terror, being replaced by curiosity. And where better to start my journey into a genre I have been neglecting all my life than with the OG (albeit the pixel remaster): Final Fantasy.To cut to the chase: I had a lot of fun with the game and don’t regret a minute spent on it. The revamped pixel graphics are simply gorgeous and the soundtrack… oh, the soundtrack! Did I mention how great the soundtrack is? It is! Great, that is. The soundtrack. The gameplay over all is what nowadays probably would count as bare-bones, yet entertaining. You traverse the game world with a party of four, teetering from random encounter to random encounter (and the occasional boss fight), collecting XP and money to spend on new gear and spells in the next city. The overall story is nothing to write home about (something that would change a lot over the course of the series from what I’ve been told), the game mechanics are fine, from movement and inventory management to the strictly turn-based combat.This game is a great way to spend some nostalgia-filled hours listening to beautiful music and enjoying the sights. If you are looking for a more fulfilling JRPG experience, it might be wiser to start with a game like Final Fantasy IV or Chrono Trigger and go from there, with a (slightly) more intricate combat system, fleshed out characters and overall story.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this on Steam Deck, and it worked perfectly fine. For this review, I'm going to ignore the fact that this is a Final Fantasy game, and judge it on the merits of the game itself. This is the "pixel remaster" of the original NES game. The graphics are reminiscent of a SNES game and look very good. The soundtrack is also completely reworked, featuring full orchestral records of the OST. The gameplay is very solid, and didn't feel too grind-y (I was 100% the game though, so your results may vary). The story is nothing to right home about UNTIL the very end - it gets very cool by the last dungeon.My main gripe is the same issue I have with most older games: there always seems to come a point where you need to progress by finding a specific pixel on the map. They made it easier in the remaster (I've played the original game) with context clues from NPCs and not having to use certain items in certain places; but it does feel like a chore when you get lost for an hour because you didn't go to a specific spot to trigger a specific cutscene.All-in-all, I'd recommend this for old RPG fans. It's short, it's sweet, and it's aesthetically pleasing

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played FF1 before now. It was an enjoyable experience, overall... There were times the next step in game-play was unclear, & I traveled the entire map, so it became a real grind battling the same monsters over & over again, & I still didn't find any clue as to where I needed to go next. I ended up needing to refer to online forums to eventually figure it out, & I needed to do that many times after that, so I took the fun out of discovery, (but it was either that or continue grinding seemingly endlessly). There is a feature that allows you to battle automatically, but it isn't without its flaws; it follows the last choices you made were, which may or may not be ideal for the monsters you're battling. It became boring toward the end, but I eventually made it to the final mega-boss. By then I had become lazy & died the first try, but soon discovered the final boss was a real challenge, which once again made the game interesting. I also like to be able to complete all challenges, but for as thorough as I thought I was, somehow I missed some treasure chests & some beasts, that was disappointing, because I really don't want to play this game from the beginning again.

_childDocuments_.review: From an original Final Fantasy VII fan this is a great game for fans of the final fantasy franchise.As the First of the Final Fantasy games it has broadened my view of the final fantasy universe, while the story and combat is what you would expect from a game built for the original Nintendo console. You really get to appreciate how much love and detail they invested into this game that was designed for a platform with such limited hardware capability.This is the original story of the crystals and the "Warriors of light", I love that they could design Garland to be such a interesting three dimensional character.The music is great and the pixel art is very nostalgic.I recommend this game for all Final Fantasy fans to play through at least once based on the nostalgia alone.but I would not recommend it for anyone expecting more then what this.

_childDocuments_.review: Gotta be honest, as someone who grew up with this game (PSP version, only got about halfway through back then), Ive got 0 nostalgia for this game, and thus it was pretty painful to get through, but I told myself I was going to play at least 1 version of EVERY mainline FF and I mean't it.That being said, I still recommend it because it's nice to remember where we came from. Just not at full price, maybe at like half off.To talk about that actual game though, music, art and battle system were great.Dungeon design, length, and the final boss, awful.While playing my wife looked over and thought I was playing an indie game with randomly generated dungeons. The final boss was so cheap for no reason, and yes I understand that older games can be cheap for no reason by design to artificially inflate playtime, but this was just nonsense.Admittedly I did use a guide at times to keep from getting lost as I have a full time job and am not interested in wandering around talking to NPC's hoping i get some clue as to what direction I might need to go, I value my free time more than that. The sense of exploration is definitely there, but to a bit of a detriment if you don't like wasting time.A fine game overall, but painfully outdated, highly doubt I'd ever revisit this game now that it's checked off my backlog.4/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly flawed game. There are way too many random encounters and there are so many balance issues that I won’t even bother listing them. Combat is fairly boring.Despite this, I greatly enjoyed my time with this game. It oozes charm. The music and character design are amazing. It has a real sense of adventure. While it might not have much of a story, it can create great stories. Here’s an example for what I mean by that:My Warrior and Thief were poisoned, I was out of antidotes and barely made it to a tavern thanks to the healing from my white mage. Nothing special. But the way I decided to remember this was that Glitz dragged an almost dead Morgan and Arael into bed, their bodies ravaged by the poison, while Aeneas prayed that they would make it through the night.I played this game to prepare for playing Stranger of Paradise later this year, but I ended up loving it so much that now I want to play through all of the mainline Final Fantasy games. This game lays an amazing foundation and I can’t wait to see how other games expand on that.

_childDocuments_.review: If an update is mostly graphical, aside from a few awful gameplay changes, then what's there to critique besides graphics? So, the game uses a pixelated art style, but the text is all in a standard, non-pixelated font. That and the part where some graphical effects don't account for how many pixels *SHOULD* be on screen for the game to look consistent, it's like if you saw something hand-drawn in its proper size but haphazardly slapped onto an SNES game. That's all graphical, though, but don't worry, the gameplay's messed up too! You get EXP a lot faster and the level cap is increased making the game much easier, or at least it seems that way until you encounter a boss and they buffed it in a really stupid way so now the final boss has 10 times the health he's supposed to. Stupid port, I would genuinely rather play the original NES version, which is wild to say when this is supposed to be some sort of "definitive" edition and is way newer than the nearly 40yo original.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game without ever playing, looking at, or knowing anything about the Final Fantasy series. I just heard someone mention it one day and I wanted to give it a try and see what these original games were all about. This game is excellent, making it hard for me to understand how it's such an old game. There's something nice about the simplicity of the game. The vast majority of turn-based RPGs out on the market nowadays either have a really high learning curve, or require you to know a ton of mechanics and material. This game has none of that, instead opting for a simple combat system that doesn't take much brain power at all to learn. Of course, this simple combat system combined with very easy ways to grind levels make this game extremely easy and it is one of, if not, the easiest RPG game I've ever played. That doesn't mean it's bad though. I greatly enjoyed it, especially once my mages started learning powerful spells and began flattening everything. There's about 150 unique enemies that you will encounter ranging from goblins to robotic death machines each with their own strengths and weaknesses and 12-16 bosses with varying degrees of difficulties.Sadly, the flaw in this game lies in the sheer amount of random encounters. It is incredibly irritating marching  5 steps only to encounter a clump of enemies. It makes backtracking EXTREMELY tedious especially if you forgot to go grab something. Going to restock at a place only to be interrupted by 6 different groups of goblins gets real old, real fast. There are also enemies that have extremely low spawn rates that are needed to complete the bestiary which is also super annoying. I spent a whole hour trying to find a dinosaur just so I could get the achievement. Besides that though, this game doesn't really have any flaws, and it makes for a fun one-time playthrough.Final Grade - 8.5/10 - Excellent
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking to re-experience the original game, this isn’t for you, as it might as well be an entirely different game wearing the original Final Fantasy’s clothes.What makes it so different is in large part the bug fixes. The original Final Fantasy was absolutely riddled with minor programming errors that mostly resulted in battle calculations not working as intended. However, because none of those completely broke the game, it had a certain balance to it that has been completely upended in this remake. That's not to say that the remake is unbalanced, but it will feel different for anyone familiar with the NES original.There are other changes, including some substantial tweaks to the stats of major enemies and a lot of modern conveniences. These further skew the balance compared to the original. In particular, the ability to do a quicksave anywhere and constantly reload it means that you no longer have to fear difficult encounters near the end of long dungeons. There is also an autobattle feature that will allow you to simply steamroll the many, many random encounters.Now, if you just want to experience the story of Final Fantasy, for what little there is, then this is probably the best version to do it on as those same modern conveniences mean the game is easily completed in 10 hours or less. The only major hurdle is the final boss, which is a massive step up in difficulty and can trounce an unsuspecting player (I highly recommend taking a White Mage in this version!).That is a very slim recommendation, but it is a recommendation nonetheless, and one that would suggest waiting for a sale rather than buying full price. However, if you are instead interested in the retro aspects of the series, I recommend finding a way to play the NES original.

There is no way you can convince me not to kill Chaos. Killing Chaos could not possibly be anymore me. I want to kill Chaos, and nobody can convince me otherwise. Why anyone would try to argue that I shouldn't kill Chaos is beyond me. If you held two pictures of me and killing Chaos side by side, you'd see no difference. I can safely think of killing Chaos every day and say "Yup, that's me". I can practically see killing Chaos every time I look at myself in the mirror. I go outside and people stop me to comment how much I want to kill Chaos. I chuckle softly as I'm assured everyday that I want to kill Chaos in every way. I can smile each time I get out of bed every morning knowing that I've found my identity with wanting to kill Chaos and I know my place in this world. It's really quite funny how much I want to kill Chaos, it's not a hope or a dream, it's like a hunger. A thirst.

_childDocuments_.review: The game that launched a franchise and saved a young Square from near-bankruptcy.It's hard to recommend this version, though, to the point that I have to give it a thumb down if only by a hair. I'm coming at this game after playing the other games in the bizarre order of 4, 5, 2, 3 and now this. Like the others is has the jittery scrolling (use UnCapFFPRemaster to fix) and the garbage font that you have to fix yourself. It is also very no-frills like the others to the point where really the only really genuinely good point of this version is the new music, which is excellent. But even that is still pretty clearly based on the older Dawn of Souls/PSP remakes.To wit: I cannot recommend this version because you should play Dawn of Souls for GBA or the excellent PSP remakes instead. You essentially get the mostly same experience as this but you also get additional bonus dungeons that are quite good.Do note that whatever version you pick they are all still at their core a 30+ year old game. Very basic in terms of mechanics, very maddening in terms of level design. My nostalgia from playing the original on my NES (pretty sure I still have the cart in a box somewhere) carries me through, but I can see it being a turn-off depending on your expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: If steam has a meh option i would choose that.The remake is amazing, the music is just perfect, game play feels refined and has nice quality of life features. No fast forward mode but battles feel quick enough you don't really need it. Its a simple game that offers enough challenge. The problem however is the technically issues, they are not big enough to make this a negative review but its enough i feel bad for giving it a positive review. The game has no v-sync you have to force it through your graphic card. The game always starts in windowed mode, every time you have to go to the settings and set it to full screen. I'm using an Xbox wireless controller and sometimes it would only show keyboard prompts not Xbox prompts and wouldn't even let me access game pad setting even though my controller does work in the game.If you want it i would recommend it as i was able to play through the whole thing but i'm just hoping a patch fixes the technical issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what initially made me buy all the pixel remasters but I did. Even though I haven't ever played a JRPG all the way through once in my life I ended up buying them and they have sat on my steam library for probably a whole year before I launched a single one. I have zero insight on this game and the whole series honestly, only hearing what friends or streamers are saying about the games and I never really looked at game play. I just knew that they all are their own individual stories. When I saw this game in my steam library the other night just sitting there never to be touched I caved in and said I'm ready to dive in to the FF series and I want to play them in order of their release dates so I can see how the series evolves (or devolves from what a heard about a couple of them) and use guides as little as possible to get the full experience. I'm not gonna write a book on the whole playthrough, just gonna highlight a couple things. I chose my party to be a Warrior, a Thief, and two Black Mages and almost immediately I realized that I couldn't heal with spells and just said screw it I wanna make it work and make it MY playthrough. This made me farm a lot more than I probably should have since I wanted to stock up on five times the amount of potions that you would most likely have since I didn't know of any other way to heal. (I didn't know until the Flying Fortress that you could activate items during battle to get their buffs and effects I thought they were all passive rip) So I'm slowly but surely progressing through the game, exploring every area and 100% every dungeon before I moved on to the next, constantly saving and checking the notes on beasts to try to be the most effective with the tools I have and I noticed one thing. Even with all my backtracking and farming the same enemies, It never felt boring to me. I enjoyed every second of this game through and through. The music is great, even hearing the same couple of soundtracks from entering combat, and going to towns to restock it never got old to me. It's amazing to me how this game is so simple yet full of charm and character. My only complaint throughout my entire playthough was I felt some bosses were too easy but I think that was from me farming WAY to much and 100% every area before moving on. I had 99 of every potion you could buy from the merchants and 999,999 GIL when I entered the final dungeon, so yeah I don't know if that's normal or not. All that being said I had a blast and would recommend this game even if you aren't heavy into JRPGs. I personally feel this is a good starting point since it's pretty easy to understand and navigating the world and finding out where to go next is fairly simple but doesn't feel like it's being spoon fed to you. I'll definitely being checking out the rest of the series in due time.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: This was an excellent remaster of the original Final Fantasy. The QoL improvements made the game better and more playable. The only negative for me was the highly reduced difficulty in comparison to the NES version. I quite enjoyed reliving the classic but, with the reduced difficulty it constantly felt like something was missing. Unlike the NES version, I never felt like I REALLY "earned" new gear or boss victories...more as if I was just cruising through and enjoying the old school style experience. Overall, for the price it's worth the money, I'm just hoping they don't tone down the difficulty of the other remasters.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: For a Final Fantasy game it is quite short taking only about 10 hours to get 100% completion which does make sense because it is the first in the series. the combat can get a bit repetitive after a while but the remastered visuals and soundtrack add to the experience. I think this is a great game and worth playing if you are a fan of the series, but if you are not the only way I would recommend it would be if you ether got it on sale or in the I-VI bundle
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent remaster of the first final fantasy game. Perfect for getting new players although veterans beware, the game is much easier then the NES release. This may be disappointing to many but there are mods online to bring it more in line with the original.But for new players to the game, this is the best version. While many encounters are much easier I find this more of a boon then burden, after a while the encounters and grinding do get dull and the easier difficulty means you spend less time farming mobs to survive your first run into the Marsh Cave and more time making progress.The updated graphics are phenomenal, and the final boss is a surprising challenge that really ends the game off like a nice ribbon on a present!
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: The most stripped back, barebones Final Fnatasy but with all the quality-of-life improvements to make it a smooth experience for the average modern player.However, I think it's necessary to note, historically speaking, that this version pales in difficulty comparison to the original release, the one lacking auto-target and running and saving anywhere and so on. So when you pick this game up for a trip down memory lane or see what your grandparents' fuss was all about, just know, this is the Ritz compared to sleeping in a dumpster. That dumpster was a masterpiece of its time and laid the foundation going forward, but remember your roots when you play this laid-back version of the game. You are spoiled with this lovely remaster and you should be grateful to exist in the same world as it. Just a thought.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: Loved playing this game. I wanna play the original NES version again just to see what i missed, but this game is alot faster, prettier and has some fun SNES sound effects. So the biggest plus this game has is auto-battle. It makes the grind alot more fun to watch and makes it go by fast, doubling the battle speed and making the animation entertaining while doing so, though it'll still get repetitive, the battles last mostly from 10-30 seconds unless you really mess up the auto-battle, which is another challenge in itself. Alot of monsters are cookie cutter, but you still have to know your monsters well enough that you don't end up doing something bad during auto-battle, like fighting those frost wolves that snowstorm your team to death.Certain teams are literally BUILT insanely well for auto-battle. others not so much, like White Mage (until late game), and for NES/remake veterans, they made some changes to classes and bosses from what i've seen in anticipation of this. Bosses are not as easy as they use to be and are far more tanky than the original and have some more gimmicks. While they can still be auto-battled, the game gave them more attacks to throw the player off. Gotta becareful of that.Thief got a much needed damage buff while Black Belt got a damage and health nerf, but once he becomes a master he's back to the insane number damage god he's known for - though with less health.The game has the same short events that were introduced in Origins, but at least they help out incase players don't pulls a "Oh crap, forgot the lute" mistake and make it easier to remind new players "This is important"This is a small thing, but i love that character names are 12 characters now. :heart:that aside, the pace of this game was amazing. I'm reminded of how it took like 5-7 days to beat the original and now it only took two days. also helps that you don't have the "Can't target the dead monster" Targeting system from before.If there's one thing i both like, but also complain about with this game is the introduction of phoenix downs and ethers. They help so that a White Mage isn't so badly needed anymore, but once you get to the late game the items are so blasted cheap you're raining in them. To make up for this though, the items I notice aren't as gamebreaking as the white mage. Even if you use ethers mid-battle, boss fights are good at punishing that tactic.To top it off, the items are single-target. just need the cash to take advantage of them.9/10 for me. Fast, fun and was not a total push-over. The remade music and the SNES sound effect bits were also outstanding. Very nostalgic, but also somethign newer players will greet with open arms.

Everything about it felt like a massive adventure where the fate of the world was on my hands, The game play was very unique for its time and still holds up even today especially with this pixel remaster, the battle system is very well thought out, It's very satisfying to me to have well played out attacks and magic spells destroy my opponents, and I love how simple yet effective the leveling system is. the story for an nes game, was actually really good and quite complex for its time and by the end of it, It made me so satisfied  that I succeeded in saving the world. it was also a fairly smooth ride as well, I only died maybe once the entire game, so for new players I'd recommend this one honestly. overall love the heck out of this and would play it again.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nothing short of a technical achievement. I understand that this has been remastered and has had pixel graphics added but the idea that this vast world, this combat system and this narrative existed on the NES is honestly mind-blowing. The original Final Fantasy came out in 1987 and I am writing this in 2023, does it still hold up? Absolutely. I was concerned that because the last time I played it I played the PSP version (which is probably more than a decade ago now), I would think this game was dated or annoying but this game, this franchise even, is so ahead of the curve that this game will be a joy to play in 2090, too. Mark my words.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the ♥♥♥♥ out of this game when I bought the NES version back in 1990. Now, all these years later, I'm playing the pixel Remaster. The visuals are great, and the remaster did an awesome job. The change-up with spells from the original game are not unwelcome, they just take a little getting used to. Still, if you are a fan of the original, this will be like a trip down memory lane, except everything is better. I recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, cannot recommend in its current state. I want to love it. And I do, to a certain extend. I like what they did with the graphics and the soundtrack, it looks and sounds great. It's polished up to feel more modern but at the same time stays true to it's original look/listen and feel.The balancing is slightly off in my opinion tho, especially the bosses are too easy now, and the whole thing feels not as well balanced compared to the original. The real dealbreaker are the functional bugs though.Manually saving the game sometimes does not work for whatever reason. Upon relaunching, the game reverts my manual saves to their previous state. Super weird. And yes I definitely do save manually. And I do so frequently in multiple save slots and with a thorough obsession. ;)At first I thought it might be an issue with Windows Defender, but as it does not happen 100% of the time, it can probably be ruled out. Only confirmed with FF1 PR so far.Seriously SQENIX, these kind of basics really should work on day 1 at release. Same as Fullscreen settings not being saved across game sessions. Why am I back in Windowed mode whenever I come back to it? And Quick Save being randomly corrupted sometimes. Wtf? Guess I'll spend my time with something else until they fix their ♥♥♥♥. VERY annoying, coming from a big company like this, a certain quality standard really can be expected. This low quality is becoming a habit with their remasters. Secret of Mana Remaster was released in a horrible state too (much worse tbf) back then. Why not just postpone the release and instead make it a decent one? i Don't think I will buy any SE Remasters anymore, not worth the money. Unless it's something i really want and it's gotten patched and/or confirmed to be free of major bugs after some weeks/months after a release. Real shame that SE quality cannot be trusted anymore. :/EDIT: Well, it looks like disabling Cloud Save for each of the games individually fixes the issue. As this is obviously a known issue, why do I have to search for this info somewhere in the depths of the Forums, instead of having SE communicate this straight away? If they can't fix it before release, that would be the least they could do.Will try out if that really fixes it for more than 1 attempt. At least that would make it playable now.EDIT 2: I see neither efforts to fix nor to at least properly inform customers about the issues and their workaroudns. Instead, I'm running into even more gamebreaking bugs. How can a graphical glitch that prevents me from seeing where I go be a thing in a whole dungeon, unless the REGION OF MY OS is set to USA? *facepalm*
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully remastered OST, Pixel Graphics handled with care and polished instead of overhauled, and great QoL changes make FF1 Pixel Remaster the best way to relive the glory days. However, I will say the lack of content from newer games is a bit upsetting. Dawn of Souls on the GBA added a lot of content that is distinctly missing from this. Not to mention a lack of end game. I understand they wanted to be more faithful to the NES original, but it is disappointing to say the least. Perhaps the chance of DLC in the future, this game could be considered even more complete. Either way, the game is worth it, just don't go looking for much past defeating Chaos and getting all of the achievements!
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy 1 has been a wonderful time through retro goodness but I have a few problems with it, lets start off with the one everyone complains about; there is content that was put in other re-releases of this game that did not get put into this version, and while yes this is frustrating I don't think it should deter people from this version. Next complaint that I have is that for portions of the game you are wandering without clear direction, some points I had no clue what to do and though there were possible ways around this problem it was still frustrating to say the least. Aside from those few problems this is a great fantasy retro series that has some good fun to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: It begins here!Final Fantasy 1 is nothing short of a classic and despite the changes it still remains so. The challenge has been lowered from the original and while that can ruin things for anybody looking for a pure experience it doesn't RUIN the game in fact I would say anybody who HASN'T played it yet or is looking more for a casual run this version of the game will be exactly what they are looking for.So far the only real problem I can see is a slightly strange interface (for example if you wish to quit the game you'll have to go into the in game menu > config > scroll to the bottom and THEN click exit). Is the very strange V-Sync issue, cut scenes you can't skip at all and the more modern text.Aside from all of that the game is worth the money and worth your time.I'd give the game a solid 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: Closest thing you can get to the classic original, the names of spells has changed to the modern ones, and the look has gotten an update, but they kept the retro feel of the sprite work while also adding a few extra visual bells and whistles to keep things looking nice, and a remastered sound track directed by the original creator. Still a classic JRPG and worth any one's time that's interested in where things started state side with popular RPGs, the characters never talk but there is enough going on in the world that they don't need to, you just need to know what the next leg of the journey is going to be.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a classic styled, minimal direction JRPG, the Pixel Remaster makes it the most painless/convenient way to enjoy, with so many quality-of-life tools at your disposal, including encounter rate control and map controls.Just don't make a Red Mage unless you want them to absolutely suck. Also conveyance and end game story points are quite oddly executed.My final thoughts: A fairly warmly nostalgic and reflective JRPG romp with notable shortcomings in both direction-conveyance and end game story beats.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: By modern standards this is not a good game, but its not a horrible one either. It is obviously made during a time when games waste your time and get you lost in order to squeeze as much "gameplay" out of the money you pay forDespite this, I still recommend it because it is the most playable of all the iterations of FF1. If you are curious where it all began, its a good bit of perspective in video game history. If you dont want to get lost however, I do recommend peeking through a walkthrough every now and then.

_childDocuments_.review: The Co-op Final Fantasy Marathon Review, Part 1In 10 hours and 27 minutes history was made as me and another final fantasy afficionado killed chaos dead.The game that we assumed would be a painful start to the journey ended up being an entirely enjoyable experience. Little did we know that the game would change our lives forever when we began the journey. With exception of the ice caverns(♥♥♥♥ you ice caverns) this was a great experience that will set the tone for the rest of our final fantasy marathon. Even in 2022 this game still holds up as a fantastical rpg experience that sends you through time to a place filled with swords and sorcery, but sadly very few nunchucks. Too bad that tavern inflation has resulted in the cost of resting in Gaia going up to two and a half ogre encounters.Overall a fantastic experience that we rate as an 8.5/10, and wholeheartedly recommend you try.

_childDocuments_.review: Something is just missing…The game is a good attempt of bringing FF1 to the next generation of hardware. But at what cost?Features are missing, the Font is ugly, the graphical settings are limited to a fullscreen toggle, movement is stuttery, vsync must be activated in (my case) n vidia control panel, bonus dungeons are missing and the graphic style is… lets say original… the psp graphics where phenomenal, at least integrate the option to switch.A big developer like Square should really be able to do better! _childDocuments_.review: 9/10 Great classic JRPG, one of the OGs you could even say. The remaster feels and looks good. Ultrawide and controller support work great and had no bugs or issues. My only complaint is the main menu music when launching plays at full volume regardless of in game volume settings.You can 100% this game in 20 hrs or less. One piece of advice, the final boss is a HUGE power jump from any previous encounters you may have had. Make sure to save before you fight it, and get all of the best gear/magic you can before fighting it. Would also recommend your characters be at minimum lvl 60 (mine were 72 and it was still tough) just to have high enough max health or it will easily one shot your guys.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad to say, just like the Pixel Remasters I played before this one, I enjoyed this one as well. Again I'm personally not the biggest fan of the character sprite style but its not that big of a problem. I used mods for this one and it ended up being a very nice experience (I used the warrior of light skin from dissidia specifically and it was very fitting for the knight upgrade). This version of the game has gone away with mp to go back to the spell casting system. I like that this version goes back to it, the game is a little more challenging than before. However, its still not that challenging. I blasted through this game pretty easily which is a surprise because I actually challenged myself this playthrough. This time around I used the warrior, thief, monk and red mage meaning healing and offensive magic was a lot harder to take advantage of. But no, the game was still quite easy. I think the game is a perfect challenge for beginners, however I think a hardmode would've made this game a little more interesting. Of course I have to mention the music. Its all real instrumental versions of the ps1 music and its incredible. Again, the best version of the ost, however I still have a special place for the original ps1 music in my heart. The bonus content from the gba and psp versions aren't present, which is a little bit of a bummer but its not a big deal. I think the dawn of souls dungeons didn't really fit that well into this game specifically, even if I enjoyed them a lot. I would've liked to have them here as an option at least but its not the end of the world. FF1 on PSP will always have a place in my heart (Said that again lol), and as much as I enjoyed playing this one, I think I'll continue to play that version a little more often, that or the gba version with the spell cast system patched in. I do suggest this version to beginners and people who want an experience of ff1 more atuned to the original.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of the original Final Fantasy on NES, this is a must have.This game was so much fun to play, that immediately after beating it for the first time, I went right into a second run with a different party setup. The gameplay is a whole lot better than the original, and the fact that many of the spells actually work now makes fights incredibly fun. My only issue with the battle system is that they removes ineffective attacks. This added a lot of strategy and thinking to the original, and the fact that it's gone makes the fights more of a "mash A to win" fest. Still, the bosses (especially the final boss, which was super challenging in a good way) were a blast. The art too is also great. While I prefer the original in some cases due to the 8-bit charm it has, the new art is still great. There were many times where I stopped and looked at how good some of the battle backgrounds were and some of the attack animations. The music however might be my favorite part. I don't know what they lined the soundtrack with but my first thought after getting to the temple of chaos was that this NEEDS to be on spotify or somewhere (thankfully there is a music player, which is nice). Even though it's just the soundtrack from the PSP version of the game (which is on spotify, funnily enough), these new versions are so much better. My personal favorites were the bridge and final boss themes.I know the remake isn't perfect, I'm aware of some bugs that really shouldn't be in a remake like this and missed content opportunities. But coming from the original, where half the game just doesn't work, I'll settle for some screen-tearing and missing items.But please install the mod that fixes the font like I did. I know that the basic font is nothing bad, but my dumb brain hates seeing it and I needed that pixel font. It just feels wrong to play this game without it, even though the font changes very little about the game itself.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: After 12.5 hours playing a full playthrough of the remaster, I can say confidently that this game has withstood the test of time and aging of other games in its genre. -The rework of the pixel graphics from saturation to sharpness is perfect. Every character shows its new light while still remaining true to the original design.-The 3D attack animations for magic attacks mesh incredibly well with the pixel graphics of traditional attacks and provide a huge sense of intensity.-Enemy designs are amazing but seem more...reserved than prior. I left myself questioning some of the changes, such as Lich looking more cartoony than its original frightening demeanor.-The font choice is.....bad. That's it. It's bad.-The remastered soundtrack provides incredible depth and immersion with every battle you encounter, though I'm reminded how repetitive the battle sequence music can be. The music of every area fits so perfectly and you can't help but hum along.-I'll be honest, I have absolutely no idea why mouse support was included in this remaster as it's more problematic to use than simply using the keyboard alone or a full controller. I highly recommend controller for best playability. Also, the new diagonal movement mechanic is an extremely well-needed touch.-This game stays true to the original difficulty of prior installments, right down to being so squishy in the early-game that you spend a solid 2-3hrs leveling up to prepare for later-game.-The inclusion of the map feature is incredible and highly utilized throughout the game, such as standing in a doorway and opening the map to reveal all chests in the area.-The addition of new chests to discover is a welcomed touch.-There's an achievement for completing the entire bestiary, but there's no bestiary in-game to monitor or track enemies. Big let down.-A major drawback in the late-game is the removal of all use for the town of Lufenia, commonly known as the location you receive the "Full Life" and "Flare" magic. All shops and buildings are now closed off. These skills were vital and are now removed entirely, thus affecting the entire last boss fight where these skills would be utilized most. Not a welcome change.-The endgame Chaos fights don't appear to be in-game as they were from prior releases.-Opening the game in borderless windowed still shows the top-window bar. Users have to go into configuration, set it to borderless windowed again, and confirm to restart to fix.-Airship, overworld, and dungeon audio will sometimes cut out. Rare, but closing and reopening the game fixes this.Final Fantasy continues to deliver with every remaster it brings and is like a fine wine - it only gets better with age. -Jake

_childDocuments_.review: This is a simple, straight foreword game, yet it's the humble origins of the iconic Final Fantasy series, and a major cornerstone of the RPG genre.So, I'm not gonna pretend this game will blow your mind if you're as well versed in Role-playing games as I am, the gameplay is easy to wrap your head around, and it isn't that hard with a few rare exceptions (And nothing you can't solve with a little level grinding I ought to note), despite this, I've had fun and perhaps a part of that stems from the ease with which one can jump in, no long tutorials, no complicated mechanics you have to memorize, one could say that Final Fantasy I is simple and clean.Now we discuss the story. Four champions of light go on a world spanning quest to restore balance to the land... and that's about it, despite Final Fantasy (And many RPGs as a whole) being lauded for the stories they tell, it's very ironic how the first game in this long-runner of a franchise has such a bare-bones story, characters and world-building, the game's plot is basically a rookie Gamemaster's D&D campaign... but to be honest, it doesn't bother me, as I've said earlier, I had fun.In terms of other aspects of this game, each class feels unique, if a little unbalanced, while magic buffs work wonders for the party, debuffs are kinda... pointless. The art is bright and upbeat if a little smudged at times (In my mind at least) and the music, which includes the option of either the original tracks or their remastered versions, is pleasing to the ears, and the game features quick saving which is great.  Final Fantasy I shows its age, not because the mechanics have aged poorly, but because as I said, this game is a cornerstone to an entire genre, that has grown and evolved over five decades. It may not be to everyone's tastes, but if you are new to RPGs or are a seasoned player wanting something more simple and bite-sized, give this game a chance, I'm glad I did :)

_childDocuments_.review: Edit/ Update: Everything said was true, however, there is a hack to *fix* the font. It's still not great, but MUCH better to see. It seems I was having some type of bug related to my 4K displays, but when I switched to a 1080p display the UI sorted itself out. Though, being forced to use a blue background was still making the game very hard for me to see, as I rely heavily on contrast.The game is too easy. There is 0% chance of challenge. You fight, you win, you autobattle, you win. You can even avoid upgraded equipment regularly and you'll still win. With no grinding I made it to chaos at level 58, and pretty much just used attack and killed every monster in 1 hit (save for a few high defense monsters) which took 3 hits. The bosses are a joke at this difficulty and at no point did I feel very 'engaged' with the game. Also, the added items like pheonix downs make the churches pointless. Being able to refill your magic on the fly spits in the face of how challenging the original game was.It's fine for a remake I guess, looks nice enough, sounds great. But I wish they'd upped the difficulty or cut the amount of random encounters. You could play this blindfolded and still win.Alright, rant over. I guess my final thought is "It's super easy, barely and inconvenience." I hope they give us a little more UI control in the other games, it's 2021 and accessability is huge part of games and life today, it's a shame that this one missed the mark.There are no accessibility options at all, none, not even changing text box color. The UI is small and does not utalize any screen realestate at all, leaving a very small hard to read font which completely destroys any pleasure you might otherwise have had with the new musical arrangement. Considering S.E. is a titan in the RPG community, one would be easily fooled into thinking a newbie with RPG Maker created this mess of a project.

_childDocuments_.review: Got the game on a whim to see what all the fuss was about. Never played a final fantasy game before. It seems very random-combat based with random encounters every 5 steps or so. Exploring the continent gives ample opportunity for gaining experience, but when you're between towns and run out of potions you run the risk of losing a party member, who then misses out on the experience and then the experience gains for the party as a whole runs out of sync, which is really annoying. After the first continent, there's not really any direction for you and you just kind of have to fumble around until you get to the area that the game wants you to be at. For the first bit of the game, the random encounters provide value but after you get past a certain level, they become a nuisance and I wish that there was an opt-out function. The difficulty seems pretty low, with the exception of the poison status effect which was the only cause of death for my party members throughout nearly the entire game. My only gripe is the difficulty spike at the very end for the final boss and it seems like the game doesn't have a solution for the damage output they give except for either random chance or to go back outside and do random encounters for however many hours it would take to level up high enough to mitigate the incoming damage, and at that point, it's not a game anymore.. it's just annoying repetition without any story value, probably added by the developers just to pad the run time.The story is well done and I liked the twist at the end. I think it is pulled off well. There's plenty of lore in talking to the townsfolk and it allows you to infer a deep backstory to several townsfolk you come across and that was a pleasant surprise for this first game. All in all, 4/10, held up by the story. The random-encounter combat becomes pretty repetitive early on and I wish that there were more areas and towns to explore that would get your party to the appropriate level for the ending. The game is pretty engaging early-on and then it falls off pretty dramatically towards the end, where I sigh every time a random encounter pops up and I just can't bring myself to finish it. It just seems like a time sink at this point. Your mileage may vary. If that seems like your jam, more power to you.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not FF1, but it's not it's not bad either.I ventured into this remake a bit skeptical.  As of this writing I'm 39 and still able to remember playing the original FF as a child.  Since then, I've played that same version here and there in different formats and always loved and appreciated the game.  In many ways, this new imagining of a classic works and improves upon the original.At a glance, I wasn't a fan of the new artwork and felt the change unnecessary, but immediately once I began playing my feelings changed.  The new visuals work and weren't nearly as jarring as I expected.  Everything is smoother and fleshed out a bit more, without betraying the aesthetics of a game this old.The music is an immediate improvement and brings the score in line with more current titles.  There's nothing to complain about here, it's wonderful.  It still maintains the familiarity of the original, but elevates the music to the standards the franchise is known for.Several quality of life changes have been made to streamline the gameplay and this is where things become problematic.  It's important to note that the original English version of Final Fantasy was a watered down version of the Japanese original.  Apparently, the developers thought that American audiences weren't prepared for the challenge and created what they felt was a more approachable difficulty curve.  This new remake takes that watered down version and opens the flood gates.The ability to save anywhere, a faster paced auto-battler, and streamlined shop purchases all seem like glowing positives and they're all well implemented, but they intentionally or not take some of the strategy out of the game.  The original FF wasn't a great game by most standards and relied on grinding for experience and gold.  Additionally, by design or not, time was what you were most often playing against.  The game forced you to decide how to manage your time, either buying items (seriously, it really did take a long time), choosing to run or fight, or if you had enough time to explore a dungeon and perhaps more importantly escape said dungeon alive before it was time to turn off the Nintendo.  Quality of life improvements in this remake remove all of these questions and significantly shorten the gameplay experience as a result.Here's where things get sticky and I'm not sure where to point the finger.  It's possible the above quality of life improvements made the grind so easy and unnoticed that I didn't realize how overpowered my characters were becoming.  I find that unlikely though and imagine the difficulty was eased yet again.  How easy is it?  I had a total of three knockouts during my playthrough.  Once while on auto-battler and just had a series of bad rolls on the same character.  The second two were instant-death abilities.  That's it.  During the end game, I completed each of the Fiend refights on auto-battler and didn't lose a single guy...  To be clear, using the auto-battler means your casters are going to be using their weapons.  The grind to find Warmech took longer than expected, but was another easy fight.  Chaos actually did put up a fight and that was nice, but why wasn't every boss like that?  This is easily the biggest disappointment of the game and could easily be a game-breaker for some.It looks good, it sounds amazing, and it's very nostalgic.  That said, if you're going to play the game on auto-battler, maybe they've already played the game for you and you're wasting your time.  I enjoyed myself and I'm looking forward to FF2, but I'm hoping this ease of difficulty is an anomaly.

_childDocuments_.review: "THE GREAT CATACLYSM FAITHFULLY RECREATED!"For as old as this game is for the original NES/Famicom release, a lot can be said for one of the faithfully recreated classics. Sure, it's a very basic enough story and will lose players who don't interact a lot with the NPC's to figure out the spots where they need to go to next (and don't follow a guide), but there's something to be said for the simpler times and the simpler games that came along with it. Easily a 15 hour playthrough for someone semi-competent with RPG's and not all that complex in mechanics or strategy either.And yes, there are none of the issues of the past iterations of the game in this one. Magic works as intended, items can be used in battle for their intended purpose, thief isn't borked up and you can still (probably) do challenge runs if you feel like it with this one. This version of the game is very much the ideal way to experience the origins of the massive behemoth that is Final Fantasy.

In summary, a well done remaster totally recommended if you are into it.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most formative games of my entire life; this was the game that young me became obsessed with, the first JRPG, the first game with NPCs and inventory, leveling up, and turn-based combat. The first game with dungeons and overworld travel and a grand, overarching quest with a final boss. This is the game that set me on the path of craving adventure, storytelling, character development. The first game I lied to adults about sneaking out of bed to play far past my bedtime. It set me on the path that eventually led to my career in gaming. It probably doesn't hold up that well to modern gaming standards and may feel contrived and boring to younger gamers but just understand: this is where it all began for SO many of us. The pixel remaster is the absolute PERFECT way to re-experience this game if you have fond memories of it. The nostalgia factor is off the charts.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY

_childDocuments_.review: We're Here to Kill Chaos.These are the words that got me to get Final Fantasy 1, coming straight from Stranger of Paradise I can see why this game is an instant classic. To my surprise as well it's crazy to see the series mainstays that came from this game. Now with this being a remaster there are some slight changes and upgrades to the original but rather than listing them all here I'll link to a full list of all the changes: Getting into some things I liked, whilst it's not for everyone I enjoyed the heavy grind at the start of the game. it really set the feeling for me like you are preparing for this massive journey ahead of you. This even extends to finding new towns, you get there, grind for a bit and then eventually leave after finishing the quest in that area. Really feels like you're putting your roots down in a location before fully exploring. Getting the mystic key was the first big moment of the game clicking for me, being able to go back to unlock all these rooms I had seen before was a really cool moment. Then, was getting the airship and aside from the really cool remastered visuals you can now get around the world lightning fast letting me explored a ton of stuff i'd missed. I really enjoyed it. One thing I had no idea about and probably the best thing was the class change in FF1. Was a genuine moment of "What?? This is in THIS game??" and of course there's a throwaway line about Cid being an airship pilot.A few things I wasn't so positive about however and this could just be due to personal taste was some of the battles can be a little overwhelming, not in a difficulty way but more how they can be one after the other. I would've maybe liked to have see a way to skip battles like in other FF games, also finding some of the quest steps can be pretty obtuse sometimes. _childDocuments_.review: Nostalgia is a powerful thing when it comes to video games. I was hoping one day FF1 would be remade so I could return to FF1. I played this as a kid when my mom accidentally bought me the wrong game for my birthday one year. I knew the picture cover of the game I wanted from playing on a NES at my friends house, and tried to describe it to her. She thought it was this game, and I was disappointed when I opened it seeing it being the wrong game. I even played it a little, and put it down realizing it wasn't what I wanted. A year or so later when I was about 8 or 9 I gave it a second chance. After blowing in the cartridge to make it work on my aging NES I gave it another shot. This time I stuck with it quite a while, and I managed to get to the air ship. I beat several dungeons and got 2 out of 4 of the crystals. Back then we had no guides, and the game was much harder than the Pixel Remakes(gil was much harder to obtain, no maps, no auto-battle, only saving at Inns, etc). I couldn't figure out what to do next so I just kinda stopped again, but it was fun...Fast forward about 26 years...I grabbed the Pixel Remaster, and just beat it killing Chaos. The Remaster does a good job mostly staying faithful to the original NES version, but adds some much needed QoL to the game us 30+ year olds need having full-time jobs and families. The graphics look great, and the music stays faithful which I was afraid it wouldn't after hearing about them changing it. The maps are a great addition, as well as the auto-battle to speed it up a bit at certain points in the game so it doesn't feel as grindy. Of course there are a few negatives I found as well throughout the game. The balance is horrible, and the game is way to easy up until you fight Chaos. I managed to plow through the game WAY easier than I ever could on the NES version. Mostly because of the saving anywhere addition(which is nice, but it does honestly detract from the original experience), and because of how much gil you get. My main gripe is them tampering with the gil given from chests. It's ridiculous how much I had, and I never had to worry about gil during my play through besides an hour or two at the very beginning of the game. Overall a fun experience and easily worth $10. Highly recommended to anyone that likes old style RPG games.

_childDocuments_.review: A remake of the one that started the franchise! I’ll start by saying I have a LOT of nostalgia for Final Fantasy I. When I was a kid, my first ever JRPG was the GBA port of FFI and II, and Final Fantasy taught me how to play in what would become my favorite genre of games. So perhaps my review may have some bias!Overall, Final Fantasy I is simple, but solid! You choose your classes at the beginning, and are thrust directly into the world, standing right outside your first town. You can’t leave that town without having a guard take you to see the king, but they let you discover that on your own!Ultimately, whereas there is a path of events you follow, Final Fantasy I feels like your own adventure of discovery in a way modern JRPGs just don’t anymore. You go to towns and dungeons of your own volition, talk to people for clues on how to proceed, and eventually solve the situation to move to the next town. All while growing stronger and stronger, watching those numbers go up and buying equipment and spells.Final Fantasy I is probably the purest “old-school JRPG” there is in Final Fantasy’s catalogue. What narrative there is is very light (although it does have one twist at the end), and it’s more about the joy of adventure and exploration.If you want something simple, and true to the roots of JRPGs, Final Fantasy I is for you! If not, I think you should still give it a go to see if it might be something you didn’t realize you needed!All in all, Final Fantasy I is a good, enjoyable JRPG. Simple, but solid, as i said earlier.

_childDocuments_.review: This version of Final Fantasy 1 is based on the PS1 version. _childDocuments_.review: This is definitely the purest form of the game I've seen.  No fancy gimmicks, no added DLC, just the core game with quality of life added.  The music is very stunningly beautiful and while the sprites are a little flat on the characters, they were still nice to look at and didn't detract me from the overall game.  The font should have been fixed though. The Japanese font wasn't compressed so I don't know what they did when they translated it, but most people by now know how to fix it themselves.The blue haired elf character has been lost to obscurity for 30 years and finally makes his return!  I know most people remember the thief in the robin hood tunic, but I will always remember the blue haired elf in the brown tunic.  That's how I know how genuine this game is.  What's also good about this game is they fixed the thief to be almost as competent as the fighter, and all the broken spells from the NES version are all fixed and working properly.The game is a lot easier than the original title, especially with the added Phoenix Downs, Ethers, and X-potions.  I feel though that this game can be customized for the player's experience.  If you want, you could not use those items at all, you don't even hate to promote, and you can even solo run it if you want to, though it would make for a much harder game, but it's all up to you.  The game isn't forcing you how to play. You can make it your own experience.I will say this though, not having a White Mage in your party makes the game extremely difficult.  I had an unpromoted party of a Thief, Red Mage, Fighter, and Monk, and it took me until level 61 to win, but still it was my choice to make it that hard and it will still fun for me.  This is game is tailor made for newcomers and veterans alike.  If you want a game authentic to the NES version but with visual and game improvements, this is definitely for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Where the legacy all began... Final Fantasy [Pixel Remaster] is a fantastic game that really brings about the classic and feel-good way of RPGs how they once were, with set classes and a world that was just the right size, feeling concise and focused in both its narrative and gameplay. While I'll admit the story sort of got super loose after the first few hours of the game, the sense of adventure stays true throughout and rarely waivers throughout its 12-18 hour experience. Old-school RPGs like this have always had a soft spot in my heart, and it feels great to go back and witness the stepping stones of a genre that's evolved so much in the decades since then yet still yearns for the classics. It's why a lot of the retro JRPGs now I can't help but feel an admiration and attraction towards. KEMCO, for example, has basically made a legacy and identity publishing and developing almost exclusively old-school JRPGs, and I'm a sucker for them all.It feels weird having to pick apart a game that is seminal to the genre's growth and the IPs strength, though for all it did well it wasn't without mishaps. I don't know why but it seemed like a lot of RPGs back then just simply didn't give a flying ♥♥♥♥ about debuffs despite giving the option to do so. There are a lot of items that are found throughout chests and purchasable through the world's various towns that truthfully feel absolutely pointless and like a waste of time, or so rare to the point you ask yourself "why?" when you can just stock up on a variant (for example, I may have found two Dry Ethers throughout my playthrough, which replenish 5MP, but a regular Ether costs 150 gil in shops, which, if you know how to manage your gil, is nothing at all, especially later in the game.). Going back to debuffs, they were absolutely pointless throughout the game, with miss after miss after miss no matter the enemy type or level. I expected it to be fairly common with bosses, but the general overworld enemies were also dodging them like it was no one's business. I think all I was able to successfully do on occasion was Slow. Otherwise, literally every other spell in existence - and mind you I bought just about everything - was DOA. Any sort of attempt at paralysis, petrification, death, sleep, blindness, etc.? Please. Buffs, however, work as intended, but those debuffs were nothing more than on-screen text fillers. Thankfully, though, Final Fantasy back then isn't as sophisticated as it is now, so you don't really have to be too strategic to make it through the game. There's very few times you'll actually struggle, and any time it did get particularly tough, it felt like a proper skill check instead of a difficulty spike (at least until Chaos at the very end of the game).Final Fantasy [Pixel Remaster] is a great game through and through, and with all the quality-of-life enhancements added to make the game more accessible and approachable for today, it feels like a must-play for fans of the genre, and certainly those devoted to the Final Fantasy franchise that want to see where it all began.

_childDocuments_.review: I started up a new game of FF1, with CHONKER the Fighter, Punchman the Monk, Dr. ZombiKil the White Mage and HailSatan the Black Mage. Here's my hot take after about 20 minutes of gameplay.Cons:- There was an issue with Vsync (I have a very old Nvidia GT 710). The menu in-game has no option for it, and I was getting some screen tearing when in Full Screen. It was easy to fix, though, I just turned Vsync on Globally in Nvidia Settings, and told it to use my settings rather than letting the applications decide, and it stopped immediately after that.- "Now Loading" on startup takes a bit of a long time. Eh. Not so bad.Now, the Pros. Keep in mind, I played FF1 when FF4 was still new and FF6 wasn't out in the states yet.- The "Classic Filter" looks great. It's a conservative 'scanline' effect, striping horizontally across the screen, doesn't look bad at all, and doesn't interfere with the brightness of the image (which is also adjustable in the Config Menu in-game). There's also a bloom filter that is applied to it as well, which does make it look very CRT-ish. As an avid user of RetroArch and Reshade, thank you for not making me work, SE.- Some Battle Animations can happen concurrently, fleeing, one monster dies while the next attack occurs, etc. That's new. Feels very fluid. More than one monster can flee at once, and you don't have to be comically over leveled for them to do it.- There are new monster packs, or some kind of RNG? I have never encountered 6 Goblins and 3 Goblin Captains in FF1 before. So, surprises lay in store... very interesting.- When a character's natural evasion rolls successfully, there are dodge animations a la FFV. Nice touch!It's good, you can get it, don't worry. Yeah the font is kinda doofy, but if it bothers you just replace it. :) Have a fun!

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game for the music aloneIf you are new, this is a nice introduction to RPG, the game is simple and easy to understand overallIf you are an old fan and have some doubts, I think you should still buy it, the nostalgia factor is a big plusBut IMO there is one minor difference from the NES that change the gameplay a lotOn the NES, if you target a monster that is already dead, you'll miss the hit, there is not any auto targetingSo you have to think in battle about how to attack, and make calculation on how many hits a monster can take before going down, if you constantly press A without paying attention, you will probably die In this version, they auto correct, and if a monster happen to die and you have another character that hit that same target, it will hit the next monster instead, so you can do battle mindlessly pressing A and not even paying attentionIn short, the battle system have been downgraded a lot IMO just with this simple mechanicThe game is less immersive because you have to pay less attention to itIf this isn't to complicated to put in, I think there should be an option to make that possible, but I understand why they did this ... nobody do this nowadays for a reasonAnyways, that's my opinion but I haven't completed the game yet, so maybe there is a new game+ with that mechanic or something, and probably a mod will eventually happen to do that too at some pointHave a good one guys, hope you enjoy the game 😀

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played the NES version from start to Finish, I can confirm that this game does a great job of finding a good balance between the old and the new, many visuals have a fresh coat of paint while keeping the original feel and not to mention that all of the magic and equipment bugs are fixed which makes picking spells much easier as I don't have to look what spells I have to avoid to stop myself from effectively wasting a spell slot every 5 minutes anymore, also not to mention that all of that weapons and armour show you the strength and accuracy increase/decrease which helps me better understand what weapons/armour I should consider keeping and prevents from constantly needing to look up the strength/defence values of equipment to know if they are of any use also the enemies occasionally dropping items upon defeat is a little neat mechanic as it can give players an incentive to farm certain enemies instead of just defeating whatever they can find for EXP and being able to switch equipment in battle without wasting your turn is an unexpected yet welcome addition and auto battle is a great feature if you want to cut down on button mashing or need to tend to something else for a moment but want to keep playing afterwards. There is not much in the game I find to be a negative change apart from the fear spell apparently doing nothing and the flying fortress sacrificing its metallic, space station-like feel for a more traditional castle type setting is something I am not sure if I like all that much as the plot twist of the sky castle being a literal space station was so cool but it still looks appealing and doesn't affect gameplay which is a relief. Overall this game does a good job of keeping most the stuff I enjoyed in the original final fantasy while adding in little features that have made the game so much more enjoyable and unique enough to feel like its own experience as opposed to a cheap reskin, heck even my sibling is starting to become obsessed with it. 10/10 would recommend definitely.

_childDocuments_.review: In Summary: if you're new to the Final Fantasy series and you're looking for a modern way to experience the first installment or you want to replay FF1 with some modernization tweaks, this looks to be a fantastic choice. For those looking for a more classic FF1 experience or some of the bonus content that came with certain releases, there are probably better options for you out there.FF1 is a game that I look back upon pretty fondly. As a young child, I remember the excitement I felt when I finally beat the first boss only to find that the story most definitely didn't end there. I could write a novel on all of the incredible gameplay experiences I had in each dungeon and the feeling of accomplishment when I finally beat the entire game. To say that FF1 is something that is near and dear to my heart would be an understatement. It's with this in mind that I was excited and nervous about the pixel remasters.I've only reached the second town as of writing this, but all of those old school feelings I had for FF1 came back in a strong way during my play session. The art is incredible, the modernization of a few different aspects makes the game much more approachable and playable in this day and age, and the new soundtrack is nothing short of phenomenal. I've tried to play FF1 on iOS when it was re-released on that platform, but I'm having way more fun with this version. To be excited to play and want to complete a game from 1987 in 2021 speaks a lot to the complete package of this release.Some reviews talk about how SE changed some aspects of the game (most notably the leveling system and triggering specific encounters), but I'd wager a bet that most people who feel strongly about those things already have a preferred version of FF1 that they already have and play. For anyone else who's interested in trying FF1 for the first time or is interested in playing FF1 with some modern tweaks to be more playable in this day and age, I think this version is spectacular so far.
