_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourites in the series. Square-Enix have done a great job at staying true to the original version of the game, while still updating it enough for modern audiences. It looks and sounds amazing.A few have pointed out that it is too easy, and I won't disagree. However, I will say that breezing through the game allowed me to really enjoy the story and characters of FFIV, without worrying much about anything else. After the self-insert characters of FFIII, it's nice to once again follow a group of named individuals on their quest. Character personalities are much more distinctive, and everyone has their own voice. From the knight Cecil, who must battle to overcome the darkness in his heart, to the dragoon Kain, who spends the entirety of the game struggling with unrequited love, and his own feelings of inadequacy. Kain's issues seem oddly realistic in this game of space travel and magic dragons, and I found myself empathising and appreciating him a lot more than in previous playthroughs. Another great character is Rydia, who experiences tragedy and trauma early in her life but draws on these experiences to grow as a person, becoming more compassionate and heroic. These themes are explored in more depth with later games in the series, but it's great to go back and see where common Final Fantasy themes and character archetypes begin.If you're still bothered by the easy difficulty, then might I suggest the 3D remake, which not only is much harder than this version, but also contains many added features, such as the ability to customise character abilities.Either way, the Pixel Remaster series continues to be great.

_childDocuments_.review: It's just as a I remember it, except remastered in 2D form, and keeping true to the superior SNES version. Why do I say "superior"? Because I never really appreciated the 3D version they came out with all those years back. To me the original SNES port will be the best version and I appreciate that they went back and remastered it.I love how they kept the original portraits and look to the characters. I never liked the 3D rendition of the characters AT ALL. For example, Rydia looked horrible in the 3D version, but here, she looks great.I like also how they kept the difficulty the same as the SNES version. It's as a game should be, so as long as you know what strategy to use, you'll do fine. Unlike the 3D version where it's based on pure luck if you win (half the time).One thing I can say that I don't "appreciate" is the remastered musical score so much. Now don't get me wrong, it's beautifully well done, all of it, but the Elemental Fiend's boss music (for example), which I consider to be the most epic boss music of all time (on the SNES port) has been damaged here. The remastered score just sounds weak and not nearly as intimidating or powerful. I was disappointed greatly...however, the rest of the music is great. They did an amazing job.The dialogue has mostly been improved but sometimes feels rushed or that they perhaps skipped a bit. Maybe it's my brain playing tricks on me, though. Edward was more useless in this game than the original SNES port. Not sure why they nerfed him so badly. I remember he used to be semi-decent once you levelled him up on the SNES port, but not here. He sucks all the time in this game.I like how they added extra abilities like they also did in the 3D port. However, Cecil's darkness attack does very little damage...so that was disappointing. I haven't nearly played half the game yet, but I can tell already that I don't need to in order to give this a proper review. Again, they've kept true to that port and I've played the original SNES version to death. So if you're like me and love the original, then you'll love this game too.

_childDocuments_.review: FF4 is the first in the series to really start feeling like a Final Fantasy game. _childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV is a great game, but this is a bad version of it.This game stutters when you explore the environment. Somewhere, a team of people created this in Unity. That team might not understand what frame pacing is. One setting in Unity is called "Fixed Timestep." The default value for this setting is 0.02, which means the camera will update 50 times each second when it's attached to a 2D "Rigid Body" such as the player character. If the camera updates 50 times per second and the game engine updates 60 times per second, the game will stutter. This experience feels similar to swallowing a small piece of hair in your soup. Some people don't notice, but others notice it stuck in their throat. These pixel remasters seem intended to represent how much Square Enix cares about it's Final Fantasy fans. Maybe they won't notice a hair in their soup if the hair is small enough.Digital Foundry explained this phenomenon on October 4th, 2021:

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10FF4 is definitely an overall step up from the first 3 games. There is a larger focus on story and having meaningful character arcs. Some similarities to prior titles like the crystals being a main objective and the bad guys wanting to get them for their own evil plans. However, IMO the journey of the story is much more fleshed out and interesting than earlier games.Combat is the same turn based FF experience, the main difference being your characters have a set/defined class. Your characters gradually get stronger and unlock more powerful and unique abilities to their class such as Edge's ninjutsu or Rydia's summoning. I would say the combat experience was the best so far for the first 4 games. There was not any huge spikes in enemy difficulty like some prior titles. Didn't need to grind much to keep my characters power in line with the areas I was traveling to. The equipment you get as you progress through the story is plentiful and impactful. While your on screen appearance will not change with new equipment, same as earlier games, you will see and feel the growth in strength and toughness of your characters.The world at first seems a bit sparse until you realize the overworld map is not the only map.  They also did a much better job of placing save/tent locations in longer dungeons or in end game to help you from being stuck in any long multi hour struggle fest.Overall this is a great classic JRPG and would highly recommend for anyone who likes FF or JRPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV is kind of my favorite Final Fantasy game. The characters are locked into their jobs and magic is learned as you level up. It feels more like a traditional role playing game than a video game you can mix up at any time. As a former AD&D DM, I always found it goofy you just change your job and skills on at random to adapt to situations with overpowering effect. If you're working as a gas station cashier wearing rags, you don't suddenly change to Amazon CEO wearing Gucci suit because you needed gil to pay your rent! LOLThe story isn't really amazing, but I feel it's more interesting than previous games or V. The music is some of my favorite (Red Wings) and Kain... Well, ok, most of the characters, including a spoony bard that could probably kick the **** out of Exdeath. While not realistically the best FF game, it remains my favorite. For that, you'd have to look to Final Fantasy VI.

After finishing the game the story was terrible all the way throug, god awful game i would never recommend it or play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great remaster of a classic.  I remember playing this game in 1992 and this is just an updated version.  The music score being redone with full orchestra makes the good music great.  There are little changes here and there from previous remakes but nothing obnoxious.  So far it is playing a far bit easier than the original but that is nice.  Mostly the change is in the amount of time you need for leveling up and collecting money.  This is in my top 5 all time RPGs and would recommend for anyone who is a fan of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: edit: Oh, yeah. There is a sort of stutter when moving. Like, vsync and screen lag combined. I dunno. It's bad. I power through because I like the game enough but if you're sensitive about it definitely give one of the games a go before splurging on a package deal. Apparently only some of us notice this, so just FYI. The game? Yeah, it's one of the better RPGs from the era - grinding is not necessary but it can be fun and useful and the story is pretty good for the time. Music is, well, iconic. I played it back as a wee lad and it was called Final Fantasy 2, so I'm biased. As for the remaster bit? Surprisingly good. New score is nice, not a lot of unnecessary changes. One issue I have though; the fonts. You now get a selection of two fonts, one modern and one pixel and they are both a solid Meh. I was hoping for something close to the original at least but the best I can do is mod in a font. That said, they're not bad, just very mediocre. I really appreciate the attempt though. So much better than their weird mobile-looking ports they did a while ago.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say, it's Final Fantasy IV a classic gem of a game. If you are a fan of the series, this will scratch the itch. I am enjoying it but there are some things that I really do not appreciate. The difficulty level seems to have been nerfed. I think it's just because you get more xp per mob but that helps you level faster and thus makes it's easier. I wish they had done an original difficulty mode and a pixel mode on all of these releases. They did that with FFI when they released FF Origins, not sure why they couldn't do it here. It's very disappointing to be able to just auto thru bosses with no issue at all. It's not supposed to be easy but I digress.I recommend it if you are a fan but if you have not played it yet, go play the DS version that is also on Steam. That was a challenge and it was fun when you accomplished something. tl;dr Have fun. Despite my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I am enjoying it.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: This is my personal favorite Final Fantasy and this is the best version of the game ever released. If you love SNES or 16 bit JRPG games, this one is 1000% worth it. Fantastic music, a fast paced story that keeps you moving through the game with interesting characters. Some of the writing is dated and the store leans into melodrama, but it is just so charming and enjoyable, that I can't help but love it.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: One of my childhood games, Final Fantasy IV was FF's start in prestige video game storytelling. Playing it now, the story is simple, but there's still that feeling of great adventure the series has always been known for, a journey with colorful characters you can care for, coming together to stop a great evil in their world. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV is the the first game in the series that truly shows what Final Fantasy is capable of. To put it simply, Great story, interesting characters, and we FINALLY have the ATB. The scope of this game surpasses even FFIII, which was ambitious in it own right and that's mainly due to the much higher power of the Super Nintendo. Cecil is the first main character that I feel like we can connect with as well, and seeing how he and his party members are changed by the journey is interesting. This port seems to remove several annoyances from the original like the fact you could lose equipment on party members that left your party. However, the postgame is still painstakingly slow in that you have to grind insane amounts for certain items for the 100%.I would still highly recommend this game and it's a worthy addition to the Final Fantasy series.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy 4 is the first game of the snes era for the series, you'll find a lot more content here than the first three, and more solid gameplay. Unfortunately the story has not aged very well, the characters are pretty shallow as is the story itself.This is the first game to use the ATB gauge in battle, which means you play your turns as they come rather than submitting inputs in for everyone at the start of the turn. Gameplay wise, the exp was incredibly generous on release, and led to overleveling just by playing the game. This has since been patched as of august I believe, and the difficulty is much better than it was on release.This version of the game brings back the extra commands for each character that were missing in the original US version on the snes. Most of these are useless, but you do have the option. The world progression is pretty linear, there are only a few optional things you can do and most of them require walking through some very annoying dungeons. Overall I'm pretty neutral with this game, but I still recommend it. It's far from the best and far from the worst, you could do worse than ff4.I am very tired writing this right now, normally my thoughts would be more cohesive but this is what I wrote. Decent game, Worth getting if you're a fan, skippable if you don't really care that much.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: I'm generally pretty hesitant to play re-releases, because to me a lot of the nostalgia is about the time a game was played rather than the game itself - back when I played this game on the SNES, my biggest worry was homework in junior high, not feeding a family of four and staying afloat in a pandemic.I'm also not a big fan of taking an old game and re-releasing it on a new engine, with completely revised graphics, either. So I liked the idea of the Pixel Remaster series, where it's just a small bump in the pixel graphics and an improved soundtrack.FF4 was my intro into the JRPG genre (which "back in my day" was simply the RPG genre), but the Pixel Remaster series is a good trip down memory lane. The developers have done a good job keeping it true to its original style, while still improving on where they can. The magic effects are beautiful and the music is really well done.The criticisms for how easy this game is are valid, because I haven't really gotten stuck on any boss, which is not what I remember from the SNES game. But to be honest, I don't have much time to grind away endlessly anymore between work and family life, so this is a change I don't mind.If you're okay with that, you'll probably be okay with this game. Personally, I'm enjoying it and am looking forward to the FF6 Pixel Remaster.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Not without it's flaws, a brilliant piece of history and storytelling re-captured by the awesome devs who did the pixel-remasters. I never played the original FFIV and it was awesome to come back and see this first "SNES" launched FF game. As you play through these games you can see the evolution of the game systems, combat, character progression, etc.  I'd say confidently that FFIV represents the first "modern" FF game.  Playing this will show you so many of the original moments of inspirations, characters, locations, and key items that carried through to the later games.  Definitely worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV Pixel Remaster is a beautiful remake. The graphics are gorgeous, the music is terrific, and it feels great to play for a thirty-year-old game. To say it came out on the SNES, it feels deep and fun to play, well, mostly... It suffers from the same issues as the earlier games, and it's too easy to get lost and forget where you're trying to get to, especially when the game opens up into the three areas. But the ridiculous difficulty spike at the end took points away for me.The story is nonsense, but it doesn't hurt the game too much, and I enjoyed it overall. I'm looking forward to giving the next one a go.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: I would say this remake is amazing:1. Remarkable pixels graphic with smooth moving.2. Truly enjoyable remake music.3. Now have chinese language support, this make me could fully understand about the story line, I still remember last time I play Japanese version...4. Truly with a lot of joy, the story make me almost cry.5. Childhood memories is the thing never forgot, thank you Square Enix remake such of good games again...Hope to see Final Fantasy V & VI coming soon, always love the classic Final Fantasy games.Regards,Lee
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: There isn't much I can really say about this game that hasn't already been said.  It's an all-time classic and a watershed moment in the Final Fantasy series.  My only gripe is I've played through it so many times that going through the Pixel Remaster seemed like a block I had to check.  As for the remaster itself, it's rock solid, in my opinion.  Apart from the font issue, which is widely known at this point, I have no complaints.  The soundtrack is superb, the controls and gameplay are smooth, and the pixel art style suits this game perfectly.  If you're new to the Final Fantasy series, this is a great one to start with.  I'm still partial to VI for being the best in the series.  That said, this one successfully does what the problematic Final Fantasy II (Japan) sought to do, which was to create an immersive story and not just a D & D knockoff.  It plays like what you expect a Final Fantasy game from this era to play like, but also has an engaging (albeit simple, by today's standards) story that overall creates a rewarding and fun experience.  It's also possible that I'm leaving a glowing review for this game simply because I got the Pink Tail after 10 attempts.  If you are a completionist, get ready for a serious grind to get those hidden Summons.   One last point: this is a remaster of the Japanese version of Final Fantasy IV, not the watered down US version that was released on the Super Nintendo.  If you've only played the Super Nintendo US version, note that there are several new items, status ailments, and an overall more challenging experience compared to that version.  This is still absolutely worth playing if you've only played the US version.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Playing through all the pixel remasters and wow this is a gem. Great story and characters and I enjoyed the interactions between them. The way they work story stuff into battles is cool too. Some of the places they go in this game are wild.ATB I'm not 100% sure is that impactful overall but it does provide some added tension during boss fights when playing on active mode which is a nice change of pace after playing the first three FF games though I wish there was a little more to it.Great game though that I highly recommendPS: Lay off my man Edward he's just trying his best
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad I finally played Final Fantasy IV. It definitely isn't my favorite FF game, but it's fun to play through as a piece of history. I remember back in the 90s friends would talk about the myth of this game. There wasn't a good way to access the game back then, and everything we heard about it sounded so cool. You start on the bad guy side, switch sides, and ride a whale to the moon. That sounded AWESOME back in the day.Playing it now the game is definitely showing its age. The plot is really thread bare, everything moves pretty fast, a lot of things are kind of disjointed, and the way the party works is super annoying. I kind of wish I would have gotten the chance to play this when I was a 90s kid. I bet I would have been more stoked about it because back then there weren't a lot of games like this. Now after playing all kinds of different RPGs over the years I can't ignore how simple this game actually is. I don't say that in a bad way, I just say that to mean that by today's standards it really doesn't hold up well.I still enjoyed my time with this game. While playing it I really felt like this is the first FF game where Square really started to  hammer out their plot formula. This game 100% feels like the outline rough draft of a great FF game, and that is super interesting. There's plot twists in this game that kind of repeat in the later games, and it is clear that the later games took the experimentation from this game and honed it in their way.If you are buying the entire pixel remaster collection this is a good time. If you just want one pixel remaster to jump into I would recommend starting with one of the first three or start with six. Those games hold up a bit better by today's standards. But hey, if you want to experience the history of this series this is a really interesting one to play through.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing like grinding the optional summons with auto-battle on and watching some videos for this 100%..A favorite title of many fans, but not mine. FFIV tried several new things and succeeded in some aspects, but personally the story and its elements felt off to me. Its like the whole epic was about continuous betrayal and forgiveness, be it the MC, BFF, GF, Antagonist or the silly ever changing cast. FFII was a nightmare for me due to its changing cast as well. Only FFIV did it a lot better. But I prefer a solid group.Nevertheless, as a game FFIV is still a good classic and if you like Star Wars, go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to recommend the game with reservations for a couple of reasons.First, yeah, the game isn't very hard at all. It's easier than the first North American version for the SNES, which is saying something. But the story is unchanged (the localization has been vastly improved), the music has been updated, and the graphics are very nice. I'm not expecting Dissidia NT quality 3D modeling here, the 2D with the odd 3D effect will do fine. They've done the hard part of building a brand new graphical engine for multiple systems and reproducing the audio, so it shouldn't be too hard for SE to do the sensible thing and add difficulty settings (or make them an unlock for those who grind Zeromus to dust in 10 turns). It's just a comparison and a table of numbers, how hard could it be?(I will admit that, now that they have our money, they really don't have any incentive to do this other than social media PR)Having played the first remaster on the DS, I kinda miss features like learning new abilities (e.g. putting Twincast on Rydia and Rosa since you only have the twins for a short period). But I've played the original to the end without those extras, so I'm fine without them.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of my favorites in the entire series, right behind III (or VI..whichever you wanna call it).I have played this game all the way through probably at least 5 or 6 times before playing the pixel remaster, and enjoyed the pixel remaster just as much as I always enjoyed the original.  The cast and music for this game is up there with the best in the series in my book.  Coming back to it as the pixel remaster, and hearing the slight polish and overhaul performed with the music alone, was both nostalgic and refreshing.Awesome story, awesome world design, some of the best music, and plenty of secrets and things to find.  Spells and summons also took more of a front seat in this game compared to the previous few, and the effects for those are really cool to watch.All in all, it was every bit as satisfying to play this time around as I always remembered it being, with the added bonus of simple quality of life tweaks and some extra polish around the music and some of the art/dialogue.  Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Everything that the last couple of "NES" Final Fantasy titles come together to create probably the first real "narrative" Final Fantasy with cut scenes and en attempt at real emotional impact.  It's an alright port, though not a perfect update of the "original".  At the very least though, it doesn't turn into a complete cake walk of a game like the first three PR games halfway through.  Probably a side effect of the constantly changing party.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: While I like the FFIII battle and job system more, it was really amazing seeing the change in how the games changed from the NES to SNES variants. I think one cannot understand why Final Fantasy became the giant it is today without seeing firsthand how it was unafraid to change and grow. But please never make me farm rare summons again thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: You can see the progression of storytelling between III to IV. Complete character growth, showing flaws among themselves, and overcoming their weaknesses. A lot of key moments that pivot everything you would expect from a fairy tale. This is also the first title to swap out multiple characters instead of having a guest character. This puts in different balance aspect throughout the dungeons that kept in mind when you were mostly physical or magical party; thoughtful level design.My very first FF that will always have a place in my mind.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: 100% in 17+ hours with some planning/guide. 12+ hours to beat the game. The newest patch massively cut down the grind (and you will have to grind) compared to before. Played offline for awhile but this one is easy to mess up.First game in the series to tell a legitimate story and have actual characters. Rotating cast of characters in and out with no choice of your own on who to take. The story is still pretty basic (protect crystals) but there is a lot of dialogue between the characters. The battle system introduces the ATB system which can be hard unless you set the game to wait. Enemies will attack very fast and hard while you pick commands unless you do so. The game is fairly well balanced just fighting the enemies. But if you want the level 70 achievement you will have to grind. I was low/mid 50s when I reached the final boss.Achievements are annoying but significantly better than the original release after a patch. You can buy Sirens now instead of wasting time grinding them. The drop rate on the secret summons is much higher. I found 2 in normal play and the other 2 in less than 10 minutes trying. Pink Tail is still a grind but now that you can just buy Sirens RNG will dictate this. Found 2 in one battle in 45 minutes. Bestiary is very annoying still with many missables for certain locations and floors/rooms for spawn points. For your sanity please look at a missables guide.It's a good game but 5/6 are better. If you are only going to get a couple out of the entire collection those are the ones to get.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite FF games story-wise! Cecil is such a great character and I LOVE his and Rosa's arc! Mt. Ordeals is my favorite moment, and so is the Lunar Whale! Quite a few odd twists, but they make this game so iconic! At first I wasn't totally into the structure of "all characters are their own class" since I loved the first 3 FF games for their party customization! Honestly enough though, the story really makes it the best, and the friends we meet along the way!
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: For me, this is the ideal version of this game. Graphically, this game faithfully maintains the artistic integrity of the original game's aesthetic with only SLIGHT tweaks that enhance rather the SNES/SFC classic's assets. This version has more accurate/natural localization (devoid of The Big N's censorship,)  I happily played through this well worn classic, knowing what was going to happen the entire time, but still remained spellbound, as the new character dialog really gave the story more emotion, maturity, and nuance.The quality of life improvements were welcome, and didn't get in the way.  Being able to sprint around, see the maps, have access to the bestiary, and treasure/item count just made the game a bit less tedious.  I think you could easily ignore these features, if you felt so inclined.Lastly, the gameplay/mechanics I think are bit more in-line with the original Japanese release, as opposed to the "easy mode" we received in the US market.  Each of the characters kept their individual skills that some lost in that US release, for example: Rosa's "pray," Cecil's "dark," Tellah's "recall," and so on.  Add to this the single-use battle items that we regain here, and I think this is the game as it was originally intended.  Very pleased to see these features return.All in all, playing this game was an absolute delight.  I enjoyed the various other ports of this game, but feel that this version collects the best features of all of those, and adds some of its own.  A freshened up version of an all-time masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Great remaster, I would say the definitive version so far. Stayed true to form but cleaned it up respectfully. The soundtrack is jaw dropping. The QOL additions a great, and toggleable. My only complaint, the game just seems incredibly easy now. I got through it in basically one sitting, finishing at around 12 hours, including side quests. You can just push through the entire thing. Only had to grind, very briefly, before the final battle, 2-3 levels. In normal play, without much exploration i reached that point at lv 60
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: I do not know how I feel about this version.  This game has been remixed more times than carter has pills.  This version almost looks less advanced than the original.  However, it does look good.  Sometimes it looks exactly the same.  The music is amazing.  In conclusion, it is not as much of an overhaul as the first three entries of the pixel remaster series.  It is also missing content from the later versions of the game.  If you love this game like I do its a must have, but at the same time...Its one of 15 that I already own and may not be the best.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this version of FF4 and feel it's definitely the best way to play the 2D version of the game because it adds great quality-of-life features like sending equipment back to your inventory when party members leave and now since the game has been updated you can outright buy Sirens which are practically needed to farm some optional stuff and achievements for the game.FF4 is the first Final Fantasy, in my opinion, to actually have great engaging characters and a very well written story. It also has the best failed translation that is now too famous and nostalgic for SE to even fix.You spoony bard!
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: I think this Final Fantasy game needs a next-gen remaster, the most mainly to overhaul the writing. I love this game. Its gameplay is fun and brought it to the table and has fun jobs and skills to use, but the writing has so many issues. (this part is a spoiler) I think Golbez is an excellent character, along with Cecil and Kain. Each has different but similar stories of changing for the better; Rose and Rydia are also pretty good characters, but everyone else is just alright; they fake deaths and come back in the end or don't serve the plot like Edge. Along with the characters, sometimes scenes are poorly paced and shown, like the scene before everyone goes to the moon where Cecil tells Rydia and Rose that they're too women to go but then when you get to the moon, they're still with you, and they say "ill be fine" and Cecil like "okay" it could use some more scenes and better overall characterization because at its core this game is excellent. It paved the way for the formula that Square still uses today with the series, and most games have done their extended cast better. But this is an old-ass game, and everything it achieves is fantastic for what it is. It's worth playing as a fan of JRPGs or as a new player.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV stands out by delving deeper into its narrative compared to its predecessors. While the overarching themes in Final Fantasy games may share similarities, this installment goes the extra mile with its engaging introduction and a roller coaster of a story leading up to the climactic finale.One commendable aspect is the level of detail put into the characters and their arcs, offering a more immersive experience. The constant influx of characters joining and leaving the party could have made level grinding a tedious task, but the game manages to strike a balance. The level grinding is not overly demanding, allowing players to enjoy the evolving roster without the burden of excessive grind.My playthrough took around 40 hours, and while I thoroughly enjoyed the game, I fell short of completing all 30 achievements, securing only 22. This, however, speaks to the depth and replayability the game offers, leaving room for future explorations. Final Fantasy IV has undoubtedly left a lasting impression, standing as a testament to the series' ability to captivate players with its rich storytelling and gameplay dynamics.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is a classic that I have loved for over 30 years, so this is a review specifically of the pixel remaster elements. Good: The music is amazing. I was a bit reticent about a reorchistrated score, as I loved the original, but they did excellent work. The graphics and animations look good, one of the things I hated about previous ports (like the atrocious mobile port) was how they altered the graphics. Here they still have all of their pixel sprite charms while looking cleaner. There are numerous quality of life improvements, such as the ability to walk diagonally, a sprint button, the addition of an ATB bar, and such things that just generally make it a more pleasant experience.Bad: They seem to have standardized the spell animations between games. So far I’ve only played FF1 and this, but they seem to have made spells have the same animations between games. While the animation looks good, it takes away some of the unique flavor of the spells. Also, console editions of the game have further quality of life improvements that they have not given to the PC edition such as XP boosting, turning off encounters, and original soundtrack options. Over all this is an excellent remaster, and the best PC version ever produced.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just get it out of the way that if you want a challenge this is not the game for you.  Try the version for the DS, it will destroy you.However, if you are looking for a version to give you powerful flashbacks to the first time you played FF2 on the SNES, this is perfect.  The translation is amazing, the music is beyond incredible and the graphics are gorgeous.  The game is about the same as FF2 was with a few of the FF4 attacks for characters added back in.  It will not challenge you but it really wasn't intended to.  You no longer need to grind levels and if you do expect that you will annihilate most bosses in a couple of hits.I however, enjoyed every second of it. FF2 was the very first RPG I truly played.  I repeated it time and time again throughout the years after playing it first in the early 90s.  Playing this brought all those feelings back to the point I almost broke into tears knowing that the final boss theme was about to play because it was my favorite for a long time.  They did not disappoint with this rendition either.  I can't wait to see a FF5 version like this.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: A great RPG. Coming from the first three Final Fantasy games, it took a while to adjust to the active-time battle system. I got the hang of it, but it's still somewhat more error prone and reduces the amount of time you have to think about your next move. The music is decent and the story is pretty good. There used to be some particularly grind-heavy bits needed for 100% completion, but a recent update has significantly reduced the grind. Overall, I strongly recommend playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: I can't even count how many times I bought this game; it's not even my favorite game in the series, but this is a good version of Final Fantasy IV. This version does feel easier than the original, so I would recommend this for anyone that is new to JRPGs. One quality of life change that has improved the game is the fact that you only have buy 1 arrow. I remember having to buy tons of arrows because you would use 1 every time you attacked (at least that's how it was in the original Japanese version). The star of this remaster has to be the music. I can see myself loading up this game just to listen to the music (soundtrack included in main menu) while playing Magic the Gathering on my phone. I only encounted one issue so far when the game crashed on me; I have been saving my progress quite frequently.TLDR: It's pretty good. If you liked FFIV back then, you'll still like it. Nobuo Uematsu is godlike.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: In my process to play, review, and finish every game that I own in my library...Final Fantasy IV.I'll start by stating my expectations for this entry were higher compared to that of the first three as my friends have done nothing but sing the praises of FFIV Story. They did nothing but sing praises about this game and - a part of me - agrees. FFIV felt like the first 'Final Fantasy' which tried to insert cinematic fights into it. It was the first Final Fantasy to introduce the ATB Battle System and the first where the character actually has a personality of their own.I recommend Final Fantasy IV for everyone who wants to see just how far the series has come from the release of IV. I do this, however, with a few words of caution. The Active Combat System is a trap which - while good in some cases - can lead to major problems in others. There are fights where an enemy will cast confuse after being hit. So assuming you don't one-shot kill this mob, it'll cast confusion and cause havoc in your ranks.This same mechanic is in play for a mob that casts nothing but Toad so while you can never lose the fight, it'll never end until you get the necessary attacks to land by chance as, unlike in other games, you don't get the status resistant gear until much later.TL;DR - I recommend Final Fantasy IV despite certain encounters spiking the difficulty without any good cause and/or reason. Just be prepared for a frustrating fight every once in a while.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV is a landmark in the Final Fantasy series. No longer are you in command of a party of blank slates; no more are you a faceless Warrior of Light. No, in FF IV, you are Cecil, the Dark Knight turned Paladin, fighting to save not only the world from Golbez's clutches, but also to save Rosa, his love. Cecil doesn't stand alone either; he has a whole squadron of fighters at his side, including both loyal allies like Kain and new friends joined in a time of need like Palom and Porom. This is the first Final Fantasy where the story really takes off and you can tell the developers were having fun with it.I want to start with the gameplay. Guess how this game plays. Just like Final Fantasy 1, 2, and 3, and guess what? I don't care. It's a polished version, sure, but at its core, it's the same turn-based JRPG combat you're used to. However, each character now has a distinct class and identity. For instance, Edward? He's a spoony bard. Regardless of who's playing the game, what decisions they make, how they like to play- Edward is, and always will be, a spoony bard. Final Fantasy IV has such a defined story to tell, and it was a welcome change. Seeing Cecil's inner struggle when he realizes his actions may not be as just as he believed turn to seeking salvation through the way of the paladin was an awesome early story beat, and really set the tone for me. You aren't defined by your past, and it's cool to see the gameplay take advantage of that. On the flip side, Rydia is traumatized by her past, but learns to accept herself and harness the power she was gifted with. She trusts Cecil and fights for righteousness using a power she previously thought evil. It's really cool to see Square incorporate gameplay mechanics into the story like that.The writing in Final Fantasy IV stands out as a strong point to me as well. Sure you meet a handful of characters that join forces to defeat the big bad, but each of them also have stories to tell and relationships to discover. Not only is the spoony bard helping Cecil to save the world; he's also doing it to honor his love's dying wish, (Notice a pattern? Final Fantasy characters get ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥). There are tons of these moments where you forget about the looming threat that is Golbez and instead start to care about these characters as individuals. When something tragic befell a member of my party, I took it personally, and I pressed A nearly twice as hard to hit the attack button for some time afterwards.My journey through the Final Fantasy series thus far has not been a short one, and though it has its ups and downs, experiences like Final Fantasy IV are why I began this journey in the first place. I wanted to see firsthand the charm and storytelling that has enraptured gamers for decades now. I love that I'm able to play such great games so early in the series, and am excited to see what other heights Square Enix has in store.Cinematic playthrough here:

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV Pixel Remaster has a nice story, and beautiful ending, but there are deep scars within its gameplay and graphics.No, I just cannot recommend this version as it really shows what a low effort Square actually put into this.The game contains many graphical glitches and errors of which some exists since the GBA version. Yes, just like it was in FF1PR and FF2PR, also FF4PR´s the graphics is mostly based on 2005´s GBA version. However, it means that it still bears all the errors of that version meaning some weird pitch black areas in some textures or green dots in the hills texture that stand out because they were put there by mistake in 2005. Square Enix did not bother to fix it in the remaster released after 16 years later. Also there is a significant error in the forest texture as it cointains a pattern of the grass texture and Square acts as if it was OK.Despite some really nice visuals (for example the background areas visible from Mt. Ordeals), Final Fantasy IV Pixel Remaster is the worst looking pixel remaster version released to this day. Especially the overworld map is totally disguisting as the graphics of this place is directly taken from the GBA version with no improvements or changes, except the water effect. Just compare the grass texture or the hills texture in FF4PR with FF3PR´s. A significant quality downgrade.I do not like at all what Square did here. The Pixel Remaster series is about remastering the old visuals to much nicer looking pixel art. That is ok. They did a good job in FF1-3, as they had to remodeled all monsters and characters. But here it is different. The GBA version of Final Fantasy 4 had already contained monsters redrawn in the style of the original ones so Square just used them in this pixel remaster. I call it laziness. The autors just redrawn the original characters´ sprites, tho I admit they look very nice (I love Yang´s moustache), so it is pity monsters did not get the same treatment as well.Gameplay-wise, the game itself (no matter what version) is a step backward compared to FF1-3. Final Fantasy 3 provided players with the very nice Job system - you could acquire new jobs and then change it whenever you wanted. In Final Fantasy, the things are different - In Final Fantasy IV is everything adjusted to the story. Characters have their own jobs added to them immediately from the beginning as even their classes are a part of the story. If you are careful enough you can discover why Cecil is a Dark Knight, why Rosa is a White Mage or why Kain is a Dragoon, etc. It is not bad, it is interesting, but on the other hand it is not good enough. Compared to Final Fantasy III, this game is too limited, linear and characters´ development is not that interesting - actually it is pretty boring, except mages who acquire new spells by leveling.When it comes to gameplay aspects in Final Fantasy IV Pixel Remaster, the game is (no surprise) easier compared to the original game. The amount of exp required by characters to level up was halved, so it means you level much faster, you get stronger much faster than previously, but the stats of enemies were not changed. Due to this fact, the game´s balance is basically non-existant as you are overleveled immediately. Do you remember how deadly were bosses and the torturing final dungeon in the original game? Well, you will be laughing how ridiculously easy they are now. But in Square´s defense I have to say that the final boss was much more difficult compared to what I remember from the times when I played the original game.Not that the number of deaths ever determined a game´s quality, but it should have been challenging at least a bit more, if not much more, which I would prefer.This pixel remaster contains everything what the previous remasters did. The minimaps, you can save everytime and everywhere, quicker movement and also visible secret passages. But hold on! This is quite interesting as secret passages are only visible in towns or castles, secret passages in dungeons like caves are not visible. Something tells me this was not done on purpose and Square just forgot to make these passages in dungeons visible as well.  As before my wireless Xbox Series Controller just does not work with this game.There are two highlights in this game, one is related to the game itself (1) and the other to the remaster (2):1. The story/lore/characters are just fantastic. The game does very good job in storytelling and also it is not worry of showing death of various important persons, or even children. The story is much more mature compared to FF1-3 and due to the game´s fantastic lore it cointains several very interesting and surprising plot twists. Very very good! And what an ending this game has! Be ready for tears!2. The music is just fantastic. I absolutely love how they remastered the old soundtrack. Now it sounds how it always should have sounded! Tho I am not sure who is responsible for it, as I did not notice Nobuo Uematsu´s name in the final credits. Please correct me, if I am wrong.Beautiful ending, very nice story, beautiful lore, fantastic twists, superb characters, this is which Final Fantasy IV excels at. Gameplay-wise, well ...the role-playing aspects are directly connected to the characters and plot, so it would make no sense if there was an option to change classes, but characters´ development should have had more interesting "rules" and the game itself a bit less linear. 65%

_childDocuments_.review: (Before I start the review, I want to make myself clear: This review will be of my own, and it will be comparing Graphics (visuals, battle backgrounds, UI, sprites and gfx), Presentation (story, animation and cut scenes), Sound and the Gameplay of this release to the Super Famicom and the US SNES releases of the game (happily known as Final Fantasy II with a Sword as the T))Another thing to point out that FF4 PR suffers the same issues as the other FF PR games as of September 22nd, 2021: awful font and screen tearing on full screen when moving in the overworld, both of which can be fixed by enabling vsync in your graphics control panel, and a font mod, but you shouldnt be fixing something if the company didnt botherSo, it finally came out, and I’ve been playing the game since its release with pauses here and there, and managed to get the Pink Tail before writing this second version of the review, because the electricity died on my end so everything I wrote is now lost.(Just as a heads up, this review  contain spoilers)So without further ado, here is my review of Final Fantasy IV Pixel Remaster!Graphics:4 Pixel Remaster is a new release of 4, and just like every other release of 4, the visuals are differentthe Overworld of 4 looks GREAT, colorful and vibrant, the underworld didn’t receive that much of an upgrade I feel, it looks somewhat similar to the original, just that the visuals are slightly modern, but not enough to make it better like the overworldThe Moon surface is better in comparison to the Underworld, so thats a plus.Dungeon wise, Id say they got the better treatment compared to the overworld, stuff like the Underground Waterway, Tower of Zot, Giant of Babil...etcBattle Backgrounds on the originals were fine for the time, as the game in NA came out 3 months after the SNES came out in NA, and its looks nice Ig, with some notable ones like Lunar Subterrane F1 ~ F7 and F8 to F10, overworld and Tower of ZotIn PR however, the battle BGs are pretty good! stuff like the underworld, castle, caves and the Lunar Subterrane F8 ~ F10, which is a plus....if they were new to begin with.And here is where one of my first complaints of this release rise up: these are straight up, the GBA BGs, literally.One look at the GBA battle BGs and another look here makes it seem like they just copy-pasted the entire thing here with no effort. I don’t get why they even did that, since they bothered to make new sprites (we will get there), so it kinda comes off as being lazy, but whateverThe UI is pretty much stuck to one color, and no, there is no option to adjust its colors (I tend to make it black or gray on my playthroughs of any release), but its a minor nitpick anywaysGFX is fantastic in here, and I like how spells looks like when they are being castedPresentationRemember moments ago when I said "the first of my complaints?" because here it will be full-on in this portion:I will say that this is easily the worst part of the entire game for me personally, the story is still the same FF4 story with all of its good parts, the weak ones, and its quirks.Examples include , Kain betraying the party , Golbez managing to steal the crystal in front of the party in the underworld (unlike the original where the arm was slowly but surely going there, his arm goes by too quick and grabs the crystal to continue the plot) and the . I still like the story because it does what it does, with all of flaws, its straightforward easy to follow, and thats fine I guess.What isnt, however, is the sprite animation♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ what happened here?! character movement animations that were once smooth in the original, are now a stop-and-go ones in the story, and I dont get how a system that is weak by 2021 standards, is capable of smooth character movement (assuming there isnt that many sprites on screen at once) in comparison to a NEW RELEASE OF THE SAME GAME IN 2021, with an animation that stops for a frame and continues, and its jarring to see it in some cut scenes where characters are walking, and the moment you see it, you will never unsee it.in-battle character sprites seems to have been simplified...somehow, as seen with Rydia and Edge casting their spellswith Rydia no longer moving her fingers when casting her spells, her mouth only, and Edge not wiggling his finger, but instead just...opens and closes his mouth? its a minor thing, but I just found it weird to have been taken outAnother thing to point out about the story again is that the script itself, is pretty much the GBA version’s script, not based, but mostly the same one with minor tweaks here and there, to make it its own "translation". (This extends to other things btw)SoundNow that we are done with the worst part about this release, we go to talk about sound4 soundtrack is simply put: fantasticUtilizing the SNES’ S-SMP chip in conjunction with the SPC700, and you get so many good tracks. Namely the overworld, battle theme, boss theme, the Elemental Fiends, story-specific tracks like sadness, the theme of Golbez, and much, MUCH more. It was a fantastic showcase for the newly released system in 1991 (US), and one of the best soundtracks made early on for the Super Famicom in the same year, as it was, to my knowledge, the only big name RPG at the time, with next to no competition. the SFX was nice as wellSO...How does the Pixel Remaster of 4 holds up by comparison? It doesn’t, at allIn fact, it doesn’t compare to it, it surpasses the original for me.Most of the soundtrack (save for the black chocobo theme, its better in the original) are better than their original counterparts, examples include Damcyan castle, Overworld, Boss battle, the normal battle theme, Troia and the Underworld.And in the case of other tracks like the Elemental Fiends, the Giant of Babil and ESPECIALLY the battle with the Final Boss against , those outright, without a question, are a replacement to the original.Was half of the budget of this release been made specifically for the music? I don’t know, but they made sure this was still a great soundtrackSFX is also just as good.Gameplay:FF4 PR decided to keep everything from the SFC original, now without a limited inventory!...but only one stack of items at a time (99), unlike the original where you could get more stacks.Abilities wise, Pray got better healing now, instead of it being just Cure, it kinda comes off as either failing or CuraRegen seems to no longer have a weak healing amount, as you are at the end of the game, so having a party member recover HP by an amount under 30 is kinda pathetic, especially considering that you have a  as your party member, so in PR it goes by at least 150 from my testings4 PR ended up halving the EXP amount needed for a level up, as you can level up faster.This might be a good thing for beginners or people looking for an RPG to start with, but there is a challenge awaiting the moment you reach the underworld, and Lunar subterrane isn’t a pushover as wellFor veterans it comes off an easy mode of the game, especially since you can dish out damage so fast bosses cant go to their next phaserip for GBA extras as wellOverall: FF4 PR comes out a weird version for meIs it trying to be a newer version of the SFC or SNES releases? is it a PC GBA version with no extras? is it trying to be own thing? After all, its a mixture of every 2D release at one thing, which means no developers office, lads. 0\10For new comers? I would recommend this release or the SNES ver due to being easierfor veterans, it’s eitherTry to limit yourself more for some challenge, play this like it is, or skip this release entirely and find another 2D version to play the gameIt depends on if you like FF4 or not, and I do like it myself, as I own every 2D release physically. (US and JP)

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game, still holds up in a lot of areas. This game assigns a specific class to each character which works well, though it does have significantly less freedom than FF1 and FF3. This leads to an uneven experience though since your team comp is constantly changing due to story events. Personally, I prefer sticking with a more static party composition but I understand. The game is still fun with plenty of enemy variety and interesting zones to traverse.This is the first game in the series to really go all in on the narrative and it works. It's a bit basic by modern standards, but pretty clearly sets the stage for what JRPGs (and even the Final Fantasy franchise) would become. It's pretty short, and feels focused with no need to stretch out the game unnecessarily. Overall, probably my favorite in the series thus far and a solid JRPG that anyone can enjoy.7.5/10 - IV > I > III > II

_childDocuments_.review: The introduction of the ATB system and the first Final Fantasy released on the SNES.With characters closer to FF1 (Each character has a defined role) rather than the free-growth nature of FFII or the Job system of FFIII each character is allowed to grow into their own roles and niches.FFIV has a rather simple storyline that traces the Heroes' Journey that holds up relatively well given it's age but was definitely shorter than i expected given the depth that others have explained to me over the years. All in all, it has more depth or nuance than its predecessors while still being relatively easy to follow. Each character has their own goals or motivations for why they're joining the party or acting the way they are, which is a nice changeGameplay wise, while the game is based on the original release, it has been tuned to make it a fair amount easier and accessible to everyone. The downside to the approach they took (making it easier to level before using the exp modifiers) is that if you stop to grind at any point, you'll end up overleveled for the areas you should be in. This isn't hard to do without grinding either. This leaves several bosses the inability to use their gimmicks or invalidates the approaches you had to take it previous releases as you are now able to brute force your way through them. The ATB system is a departure from the turn-based nature of the previous games and feels somewhat clunky in it's first appearance. What doesn't help this is that when casting magic, there is also a timer before the spell goes off, so not only do you have to wait for the caster's ATB gauge to fill so they can take their turn, you also have to wait a period of time determined by the spell before it takes effect.Overall it was a fun game and it was nice to see where Final Fantasy started to really take off.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV: one of my top three games of all times. ironically my 2nd and 1st favorite are from the 90s too. But FF4...I've played each release of it.And honestly, I was going to come here and give it a thumbs down for making a fatal mistake. In the beginning (this really isn't a spoiler, since if you didn't know this happens..then you didn't even watch the intro) we have our main character trying to change...to be good. So he is then instructed to deliver a package, not knowing the contents. But not here. Instead  this version goes like this:Cecil: Why must we make others suffer, king?King: Quiet, deliver this bomb to the village northCecil: Ok, that sounds totally harmless. I mean it is just a bomb...no evil intent or destruction sounding like it will happen there...But I continued and found I was pleased with this version. Ironically i actually like the SNES look of this game more. Also you seem to level up a lot faster in this version. When I acquired the 5th member of my party, he was a good 10 levels below the lowest other in the group. And the rare summons seem a lot easier to find too...which is a nice treat.But lets address the big question. There are two version that you can get: this pixel remaster, or the 3d version. Which should you get?Recently I played through the 3d version and I am just about to finish this version. This version lacks the 3d look, and the abilities that you can equip on party members....which the latter is a nice treat. I am not crazy about dragoons jumping, because they are good damage takers, and by making them jump...you lose them taking damage, and increase the chances of mages taking the damage for them. So being able to pass something like focus from Yang to Kain in the 3d version was really nice. So if you want 3d look or the abilities, then go there.Also this version feels a lot easier than the 3d version. Now, i put some extra grinding time into the 3d version, but it took a while to get up to the 80s in levels on it. Most people won't get that high. Here I am at like 1/3 of that time and halfway up the 60s.But there are three big reasons why I recommend this over the 3d version:1. This version runs a lot smoother. The 3d version feels a bit off in speed and control. Which leads to 2 and 3:2. I ran into a major problem with the 3d version selecting targets on its own for me when an enemy is eliminated. If i am choosing who to attack with one character, and another character kills an enemy, the whole list will close and sometimes the game will choose whomever the attack list was on at that moment. This has led to issue with spells hitting the incorrect target and healing them. You won't have this issue with the Pixel Remaster.3. The 3d version's area of view is much much smaller....causing you to have to run around the area more to see what is there. And it also gives you benefits for mapping out 100% of the area...but that means you have to spend extra time running from left to right just to map out the area....which means slower dungeon runs and more random encounters. Basically, compared to this version...the 3d version feels like you are in a small box, rather than seeing the big area. it never feels comfortable or right in all the hours played.But there is another factor to take in account here: The After Years. There is no Pixel Remaster of The After Years. There is only a 3d version on Steam. So if you want to continue the story, you can either get the 3d version and try to make that feel normal...or accept that playing The After Years after this version will never feel normal, and you will never like it.This final thing to consider is price. The Pixel Remaster stand alone version is a couple dollars more expensive than the 3d version.....but becomes cheaper when you pick up the I-VI bundle. So if you are going for the bundle...its a no brainier.Like I said at the beginning, this is one of my top three games, so I felt the need to play through both version. You can do the same if you have the extra cash or they go on sale. But if you only want one version and aren't sure you will even go through The After Years....then get this version.....and hope and pray one day The After years will get remaster love.

_childDocuments_.review: For a long time, Final Fantasy IV (2) was one of my favorite games of all time, even over VI (3).  When it was new in the US, the story did things that had never been done before in console games (sacrifice, death, and betrayal), and I loved it for that.Today, having played IV in it's proper place in the canon, it is clear that everything it did was just a natural progression from the prior games, and it loses some of it's shine in the process.  I still enjoyed my time with the game, but the story feels painfully dated and rote today.This is the "full" Final Fantasy IV, not the simplified US Final Fantasy 2 version.  Playable on the Steam deck, although name entry screens require a bit of extra bother.  (They could have at least partially fixed that problem by adding a keybind for Enter = A.  It would still be a pain to enter unique names, but using default names would have been seamless.)  Mostly playable 1-handed (right), except running from encounters requires the use of both the left and right shoulder buttons (which is a completely unnecessary limitation).

_childDocuments_.review: Went to the moon, and nobody cared. This is the game where the story and characters are first given emphasis. But it really highlights how bare-bones it all was. The world exist as little more than a stage/prop for the plot to happen. Somehow Mystic Quest's world felt more alive. The game will be remembered for the opening. The single story-aligned class change. And the strangely high number of heroic sacrifices.  But its all front loaded. You go to the moon, and a giant robot attacks the planet. But it might as well just be another day by how little the game acknowledges it. The challenge is up from the first three games. But a lot of that is due to having your party replaced at times with under leveled characters. A couple of bosses have hidden counter mechanics that were annoying. But once discovered it made the encounter trivial. The final boss being the stand out. Overall, the remaster is fairly good. It would be difficult not to be. This game just does not benefit from the PR graphical upgrade as much. The music is great, but never caught me off guard like the third game. Probably due to be much more familiar.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV is my favorite in the series, but this has to be the worst version of the game in my taste. Graphicly it is inferior to the old 16bit snes Nintendo version, and made more of in an end of nes life 8bit pixel style. The re-arranged music also seems inferior to the original snes version or any other version. There is none of the addition content from other release or difficultly changes. This version has the same difficulty as the America release on SNES, which is too easy and requires no thought, in combat. There is a Bug that seem to exist in all the Pixel Remaster games so far, when using weapon or items like fire rod or ice rod as a item. They cast the spell and does minimum damage or effect, instead of scaling with your status or item placement in the game. The graphic or animations also seem slow, compared to other version of the game. Best way to notice this is when you get into an airship. The air ships in other version of the game fly around the world map very quickly, they seem to drag in this version and take 2 to 3 times along to travel from place to place. I noticed this also in the Pixel Remaster version of Final Fantasy 1. I don’t recommend this version of the game. Pick up steam 3ds version of the game instead, while that version, I don’t think is all that great either, you get a lot more for your money, with additional content, voice acting, new game + mode, and a significate boost in difficulty making combat more interactive then, just picking the attack option.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: The Pixel Remaster art style works really well for Final Fantasy 4. Moreso than any of the other versions of this game (PSP version, GBA version etc.) the visual style here captures the beauty of the original while modernizing subtle effects (spells, lighting etc.). The music in this version is also phenomenal. Easily the best Final Fantasy 4 has ever sounded. Now, these are new renditions of the classic songs so they won't be 1:1 remakes. For some people this may not be a positive but personally I love the new mixes. The quality of each track is top-shelf. As for gameplay, the game plays mostly the same as the original US Final Fantasy 4 (2) release with some additional elements from the original Japanese release. There is also less grinding required in this version due to faster XP gain. For people who are familiar with the game they might criticize this choice but it makes getting through as a first timer much less annoying.As with all of the Pixel Remasters, this is a must buy if you're a fan of Final Fantasy. If for no other reason than to listen to the amazing soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This was the first time I played FF4, and it was pretty OK. This game introduces a lot of ideas that will be heavily improved upon in later titles, but it still does a great job by 1991 standards. Would recommend this version to Final Fantasy fans who want to experience more of the series' roots.The best and worst thing about this game is its focus on its story. By the SNES's standards this must have been quite revolutionary for its time, but nowadays it still comes across as quite simplistic. There's a nice bit of drama sprinkled throughout the main plot, but its constantly dragged down by weirdly out of place humor and completely ridiculous set pieces. That said, while the plot is hard to take seriously, it's  It's hard not to smile at some of the nonsense this game throws your way.As the story progresses, characters  filter in and out of your party. It makes it very difficult to form any sort of strategy, and you kind of just have to accept the cards that you're dealt. To "make up" for this handicap, most characters are very simplistic in what they do, some having only a single basic ability, and the vast majority of this game is  easy. I'd rather the game be easy than unnecessarily frustrating, but it does kinda suck that for most of the game you can just auto battle through every encounter.The Active Time Battle system is a welcome addition to the game, keeping the pace of combat fast, however there aren't many ways to interact with it. I certainly hope they improve upon this system in future titles (they do). Otherwise, the gameplay really takes a backseat in this game, man I miss the job system...Best part of the game:- The assault on the - The absolute gauntlet of a final dungeon this game throws at you.- Worst parts of the game:- - - Having to recast float on your party.Overall pretty good/10 but watch out for FF14 spoilers.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time fan of the Final Fantasy franchise, Final Fantasy 4 was always one of my personal favorites, starting back in the days when it was known as Final Fantasy II on the Super Nintendo.   This remastered version, is everything the old game was and than some.   A more direct translation of the original classic, with some of the missing elements reinstated, Final Fantasy 4 is so much more than just a remaster, it's the game we were always meant to experience.   Easily recommended to anyone seeking to play a classic game again, or for the first time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a massive step up in most areas compared to the first 3 titles in the FF series. The music, story, characters and combat were all leagues above the previous games. The writing was the most noticeable upgrade, having likeable characters makes a big difference. Also I got the pink tail after using only 4 sirens. Didn't get the Bomb summon for almost 3 hours though!
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: FF4 is where the series really started taking off. Pretty much every single element of the game was improved.Gameplay has some significant changes. The game is no longer purely turn-based, it's now using so called Active Time Battle system, which allows characters to perform actions once the action bar is filled, which depends on player stats and status effects. It makes combat more dynamic, while still keeping the strategic approach. The job system from FF3 is gone, you can't change jobs, however each character in the story has a specific "job" assigned and a unique set of abilities. Similar to the previous games, FF4PR suffers from being fairly easy.The story is where the biggest improvements have been made. It's no longer just something that's supposed to give you a slight reason to go into the specific area. It's a fully-fledged story with interesting characters, motivations and emotions. The music is absolutely fantastic. The PR renditions of the classic FF4 themes are simply beautiful, much better than the previous 3 remasters.All in all, it's a well remade version of a great classic jRPG.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: The game overall is good. The battle system, characters, and graphics are overall good and is what you would expect from a remaster. However, what brings this down is the lack of Advance content that I wanted in a full on Final Fantasy IV remake. There is no Lunar Ruins, no character swapping, no Cave of Trials, which ends up giving it no replayability and end game content the original needed so badly. If you just want a Final Fantasy IV that is simply a refined SNES remake and you have no other version, this is the game for you.If you want a definitive Final Fantasy IV, versions like the GBA and PSP are preferably better (despite them being impossible to get at this rate)

_childDocuments_.review: Purchased the pre-release bundle which stated on the store page, "Purchase the bundle now to receive all soundtracks and wallpapers from FF1-6!" The bundle included the item titled, "Final Fantasy IV: OST & Wallpaper". However, the bundled "OST"/"soundtrack includes only a few songs... which amounts to deceptive advertisement at best, false-advertisement at worst. A few songs out of a collection of many does not make a soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Purely as someone that has never played the original or the 3D remake and only looking to play before FFXIV Endwalker comes out - it's okay. It's almost too simple in places and the plot feels like it moves along at a million miles an hour but I expect that's more a sign of its original age than anything to do with the remake itself. I will say it's not very difficult, however. Outside of a few obtuse mechanics I had to have a quick google, encounters are quick and easy and offer very little challenge. It does what it has to, and the remastered soundtrack is top level stuff so I can't really make any major complaints.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: It's Final Fantasy IV! You're familiar with it. I'll just cover what's different, for better or worse:Pros: - The soundtrack. Soundtrack of the year, as far as I'm concerned. Even more so than FF5 Pixel Remaster, which is also out as of this review. - Leveling is easier. Better if you're old like me, having played the game back in 1991 and nowadays just want to cruise through it.Cons:- Worse graphics than the PlayStation Portable version. A downgrade from that, though better than the original SNES version.- Missing all of the added content from the GBA and PSP versions. Also, nothing from the two semi-sequels ("The After Years" and "Interlude").- Buggy. Font issues. Screen tearing. Fixable with some hacking but why need that in the first place?

_childDocuments_.review: Its pretty decent, but out of all the versions, i believe this is literally the easiest, i auto battled all the bosses and beat them very quickly, i DID NOT grind at all, because it was very unnecessary. _childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: As a game, its great, albeit rather aged. It has a nice charm to it, but later games do it so much better.As a port, its really weird. FF4 has to be one of the most remade games in FF. You have:-SNES JP Original-SNES US (FF2)-GBA-PSP-DS ("3D")and now the PR.In my opinion, I still think the PSP version looks the absolute best and I half-wish there'd be a mod of just that, but I will admit the PR does have a few nice quality of life changes. Mod support ( you can toggle random encounters, which is something I can't live without anymore), infinite inventory (which makes the fat chocobo useless but w/e), infinite arrows, an updated auto-battle, etc. I do wish the option for a non-orchestrated soundtrack (another +1 to the PSP version), but theres modding for that, thank god.As for the price? Jesus Christ. $18 is a hefty price tag for a game thats relatively short, and it seemingly never goes on sale. The 3D remake is cheaper and debatably has way more content. I can only hope for a price drop (and a console release) in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this many times over many years, so with this version the first thing I did was go to the music section to see how the new tracks sounded."Within the Giant" invoked massive feels"The Final Battle", "Battle of the Four Fiends", and all other battle themes were masterfully rearranged"The Lunarians" sounds whimsical, and mysterious."Dancing Calbrena" is as creepy as it has ever been.The character themes are all incredible.  As for the game itself, well its basically the same as the original.  FFIV is where the franchise really started to dip its toes in the storytelling medium.  While it isn't the most well written story especially in the modern era - there is still a nostalgic kind of charm the entire journey has which I believe will still be enjoyed by both returning players, and newcomers alike.  While I wouldn't recommend FF1-3 for anyone outside hardcore FF fans, Final Fantasy IV I can easily recommend to just JRPG fans in general.  Might not be the best game in the franchise to most, but it is certainly worth your time.

_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I thought it was cool, but I wasn't super happy because.- The game is improved graphically, but the gap between the first 3 FFs and the remaster is way bigger than with the fourth game. The improvement is there, but it's subtle.- The game's soundtrack feature lots of brass, which i wasn't too fond of. I was expecting more flute, strings, harpsichord and electronic elements. It sounds a bit fanfare at times.- It's more easy than it was and the game was already not very difficult, so, at times it seems like overly easy, in an exaggerated way.That said, I still enjoyed the experience, because it's a viable take on Final Fantasy IV, and while not everything is my cup of tea, the music is still better than it ever was and the graphics are beautiful and play hommage to the oldschool. Also, the special effects are amazing. Someone on youtube pointed that the Black Hole is similar to those NASA images that went out recently. Also, there's a bit of very strong moments visually or sonically, I won't say which one to avoid spoilers but some things were VERY well done.Also, there's of course the same quality of life improvement: the maps and auto-battles.Also, looking back I find that it's a great historical hommage to a game that challenged the genre and made it what it is today. It's done in a beautiful way and the poetic essence (music, graphics and storyline) is intact.For those who don't mind the level of difficulty and play for the sake of following the story, it's a perfectly great version to get introduced to the game. I think it's still my favorite, even though it's not A LOT better than the other versions. I think that I was just expecting too much about this remaster. Now let's wait and see for V and VI.
