_childDocuments_.review: "Final Fantasy IV," known as "Final Fantasy II" in the States, is a classic that needs no introduction or recommendation for anyone who’s already familiar with the series. This game is a timeless masterpiece, and anyone playing it is doing so with a deep appreciation for its legacy.As a devoted fan of the Final Fantasy series, this game holds a special place in my heart. The characters are unforgettable, with Cecil's journey from a conflicted dark knight to a heroic paladin, Rosa's steadfast courage and compassion, and Rydia's captivating evolution from a frightened child to a powerful summoner—always a beloved character for me. Each playthrough is a nostalgic journey that often brings literal tears of joy as I relive the memorable moments and emotional story arcs that defined my childhood gaming experiences.The narrative depth and character development in "Final Fantasy IV" set a high standard for RPGs. The intricate plot, filled with twists and turns, keeps you engaged from start to finish. The musical score, composed by the legendary Nobuo Uematsu, perfectly complements the storytelling, enhancing the emotional impact of every scene.The gameplay, though rooted in the traditional turn-based combat system, remains engaging and challenging. The strategic elements and unique abilities of each character require thoughtful planning and execution, making every battle a satisfying experience. The introduction of the Active Time Battle system was revolutionary at the time and adds a dynamic element to combat that keeps you on your toes.For me, this game is more than just a nostalgic trip down memory lane; it's a testament to the artistry and storytelling prowess of Square Enix. It's a title that I revisit time and again, each playthrough reaffirming its place as one of the best in the Final Fantasy series.In summary, "Final Fantasy IV" is a masterpiece that has stood the test of time. Its compelling characters, emotional storyline, and innovative gameplay make it one of the greatest titles in the Final Fantasy series. For any fan of the genre, this game is an essential experience that continues to inspire and captivate.

His whole pattern invalidates multiple characters in the party and makes all the grinding you did for high level spells/summons seem pointless. Worse, when you die (after 30 seconds) and then re-spawn to try again...you have to sit through 10 minutes of unskipable cutscenes. It just reinforces how badly this was designed. Pixel folks should have updated this encounter. For clarity, I'm level 60+ with my party and have BIS gear. It's just terrible design.

_childDocuments_.review: This was my favorite blast from the past, but after playing the other three remakes, the first Final Fantasy at this point feels like the freshest one with the changes. Always loved this Final Fantasy the most in terms of story, character, class, magic and leveling. I noticed compared to the Super Nintendo games of old that this game's battle system is alot easier as well and alot smoother. The introduction also of the RTA system makes taking turns very fun and with a better idea of the turn order compared to the older games without it.That being said, though, this game is the first of the four that shows some actual flaws: The repetitive nature of the games. I personally started noticing that battles, magic, dialogue and menu choices start to show their repetitive side alot more when compared to the oldergames, so hopefully the future games don't fall into this trap as much. _childDocuments_.review: Overall, a good version of FFIV. Not the definitive version, however. That title belongs to the PSP version.The Pixel Remaster would be the best "true to classic" version for the game, and definitely not a bad way of experiencing the story, although I'd argue that the NDS remake has the better presentation and gameplay (it's really hard). The Pixel Remaster has a superior rendition of the OST, hands down. The NDS 3D remake is available on Steam, but it's an inferior port that looks a lot worse than it should due to it running at a much higher resolution than the NDS, for which the 3D graphics and textures were never designed for.If you've only played the SNES version of the game and want a more polished, better looking, better sounding, and more challenging version of the game, this one is for you. If you've never played the game before, this is a really good starting point. Otherwise find yourself a copy of the PSP version of the game if you want the "definitive" version, or a copy of the NDS version for a far more immersive experience overall.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing remaster of a great and influential entry in the FF series.  I found this one unexpectedly easy, but accidentally grinding into obscurity may have been a factor.First, in terms of a remaster, this is awesome.  The screenshots don't do it justice.  The graphics are beautiful and fluid, and faithful to their roots on the SNES.  The music is amazing, the localization is good, and the subtle QOL improvements are welcome.FF4 set the bar for its era's JRPGs with puzzle-like encounter design and ludonarrative storytelling -- that last bit sounds like a buzzword, but very few RPGs even now blend the gameplay mechanics with the story the way FF4 did.  With other bold innovations like the ATB System and the large ensemble cast, it's easy to see why this title was so influential.With that said, I have to say I feel like this isn't the best version available; the 3D remake was so good that I find it difficult to recommend this version over it.  The only thing the pixel remaster has over the remake is that it's closer to the original, so it might scratch a nostalgic itch that the newer version can't.  I found this was made even worse by the achievements which, while obvious, encourage you to grind until such a point where the final encounters are made trivial.In summary, can I recommend this?  I'm not sure.  If you're looking to partake in some SNES-era nostalgia, you certainly can't go wrong, but if you had to pick between this one and the 3D remake which is a few bucks less as of this writing...  I'd go for the other one.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic.  I believe my final save had approx 25 hours on it which included completing all achievements and killing the final boss.  I recommend Ilyat's guide to be certain to not miss any of the missable achievements.  I'm sure most reading this are familiar that this game was titled Final Fantasy II for the SNES in America even though in Japan it was called Final Fantasy IV.  I can't imagine going from FFI to FFIV during the initial US releases, but it must have been mindblowing.  Fantastic story, longer than you think, and not to mention getting to see the origin of some ideas that persist throughout later entries in the series.  Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Probably THE game that put Final Fantasy on the map as a franchise. The first game in the series that became famous for its story. Well, there wasn't much to choose from since FFII & III wasn't released outside of Japan originally. A good choice for someone that have never played an old-school JRPG before. A very streamlined experience. There's no customization. No selectable jobs. Your party members are decided by the story. Good for people that don't want to deal with min-maxing and plays RPGs for their stories. Bad for those that value gameplay more. Pros:- Remastered soundtrack supervised by Uematsu.- Auto-battle feature that speed up battles.- Map screens for all towns and dungeons. Makes navigating more streamlined.- A "classic" screen filter that emulate the look of a CRT TV. Personally a must have for these sprite based games.Cons:- None of the bonus dungeons and superbosses from the Game Boy Advance and PlayStation Portable versions are included. There's no postgame to speak of. You finish the story. That's it. - No ability to choose your party members like the fore mentioned versions. The story decides what party members you have,- No in-game V-sync setting. You have to force it through your GPU driver settings.- There're some performance problems. The screen scrolling isn't as smooth as it should be. I recommend that you play in Fullscreen mode, force V-sync and limit the FPS cap to 58 in the graphics card control settings.- Very small and thin font when you have the game language set to anything other than Japanese. You can do some quick modding by copying the Japanese font file and rename it to the language you play with. This works for all six games.A good game but if you have played FFIV before, then this remaster doesn't offer anything new aside from the potential for mods since all six remasters run on the Unity engine. The most underwhelming game in the Pixel Remaster collection. It lacks bonus content and/or the increased difficulty of the 3D remake.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Some really interesting changes in this one that make for another very fun game. Combat is revamped this time, departing from the strictly turn-based formula of the previous games. Here, enemies will attack as time goes on, and each character has a gauge that fills up over time, and when it is full they can act. It's still sort of turn-based, but it punishes you for overthinking and rewards you for quick thinking. I'm not really sure that I prefer it over regular turn-based combat, but it's similar enough, and still a lot of fun. The best part about this game is the story. This is the first game in the series where story takes the forefront. Party members and their class are determined by what happens in the story, and it has well-written characters, emotional moments, and what feels like real stakes. It's nice to see this, since the first few games had minimal or mediocre stories. A minor complaint is the grind that is needed to get a few rare drops, but it only took a few hours total and you would only need to do it if you are going for all achievements so not a big deal. If you liked the previous Final Fantasy games, you're gonna like this one too. They've all been consistently very enjoyable so far.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: My most favorite game of ALL TIME!!  I own literally ALL versions of IV including the rare Wonderswan versions and the Special Edition Gameboy Micro. As for the graphics, I would say they are on par with but slightly less than the PSP version.  However, this is the version to get!  I can't stress how this tale of Cecil, Rosa, Rydia, and Kain has lasted the test of time; it had a huge influence on me back in 1991 and I still have those memories today thanks to this re-release.   This game is simply a timeless masterpiece!

_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: [REVIEW UPDATED AGAIN]The first three pixel remasters set a very high standard. Not only that, FF4 in and of itself was naturally more advanced than the original three games to begin with, especially the soundtrack, so criticism of its remakes tends to be more harsh. I will say that this is probably the best-looking version of the game; the graphics are noticeably improved even from the GBA/WSC version.The music is good, of course. It's just... the original soundtrack is one of the most iconic masterpieces in gaming history. I don't think it can really be "improved" upon. This is lovely music, but the original will always hold a special place in my heart. The town theme does have a very nice, laid-back Celtic vibe, I'll say that much. I'm just glad the battle theme actually uses brass, unlike that funky remix on the DS.There are some glitches, notably the world map forest tiles missing a piece, which is a real eyesore. You can ignore it, but it could've looked so much better. I hope they do fix it soon. Ironically, the battle background for the forest is very cool.There are an annoying number of back attacks and ambushes. Maybe you'll like that it makes the game a little more challenging, but I personally find it a bit irritating.All in all, just what you'd expect from FF4, and that's very good. I'm very interested to see the graphical enhancements (and soundtracks) for 5 and 6![UPDATE]Upon finishing the game, I wanted to remark on the difficulty. The game is mostly much easier than other versions, though the optional underworld dungeons and especially the moon ramp up the challenge pretty nicely. The last dungeon and final events were satisfying as always. :)[UPDATE 2]I replayed to get an enemy I missed, rushing through without gaining as many levels and skipping a lot of treasure. The challenge, I found, was a lot more satisfying. So while, if you take your time and explore, you'll probably be overleveled, the game does offer a greater challenge if you're more familiar with it and advance the plot more rapidly. Nice! :)
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing this in late November and only got to finishing it a few days ago prior to this review, so please bear with me. Everything is the same as my previous reviews of these remasters. So I won't go too into it with things. The translation is based off the GBA version if i'm not mistaken and has been improved upon. The sprites are more detailed then the previous PRs. But that's due to IV being the first Final Fantasy made for Nintendo's second gen console, the Super Famicom. Graphics are nice and clean, animations are fluid and neat and the music is amazing. (Look back at my previous PR reviews for everything else as I don't want to repeat the same spheal for every remaster.)I'll go into the cons I have experienced. The screen tearing that was in the previous remasters still exists. You'd think Square would get to the bottom of this issue. It could just be my hardware, but given these games were originally running on 8bit and 16bit hardware, it's hard to imagine modern hardware having issues. (even as dated as mine) As I stated before, I first started playing in November. There was a bug where many monsters and enemies were not registered in my bestiary when I was first playing. So many one time encounters and even bosses were absent from the record. Leaving me with two acheivements unobtained on my account. The issue has since been resolved though. But it still had an effect on my overall experienceAside from those two issues, I highly recommend this game. It's quite fun and has a nice twist towards the end for new players.

_childDocuments_.review: so first thing's first: if you're looking for the most up to date, "definitive" version of ff4, this is not it. it's more or less the vanilla snes game with some audiovisual and quality of life upgrades and a slightly tweaked version of the gba game's english script, and features none of the new content that was added for the gba and psp versions, if that means anything to you. for my money, though, this is the best way to experience ff4, primarily due to said quality of life upgrades and the stupid good music. the font sucks, but you can easily mod in a better one with even basic knowledge of how to use a computer.as far as final fantasy iv itself goes, this has always been one of my favorite final fantasys, somewhere in the top 3 but i'd need to go through the others again to be able to say for certain. the constant fakeout deaths get a bit ridiculous after a while but it has an engaging story, good dungeon and enemy design, and a fresh (well, for the time) and surprisingly deep combat system. definitely a bit on the easy side for the most part, (anyone saying this version is significantly easier is mistaken, ff4 was always a generally easy game) but that's about where my gripes end.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 2: Found another complaint. Unlike some of the remakes, I can't swap party members in this version, so the final party is stuck being Cecil the Paladin, Kain the Dragoon, Rosa the White Mage, Rydia the Summoner, and Edge the Tissue Paper. .....actually, I take that back. Tissue paper is FAR sturdier than Edge is. It'd probably have better MP usage than his Ninjutsu, too.Edit: I forgot there are instances of grinding I may have to do, when are we getting that EXP Boost update thing that the console ports got, Square Enix?Okay, so, I haven't beaten it yet, but I can say this much. This is my favorite entry in the entire series. Yes, even more than 7. Is it cause of nostalgia? Yes.So, obviously there may be some adjustments I'm not too fond of.The visuals are a mixed bag for me. Environments and some scenes look absolutely BEAUTIFUL, but then we got Palom's eye in his portrait looking bad, the visuals for some of the spells look bland, and I feel like it's a bit harder than I remembered from when I played it on the GBA. Then again, when it came to the GBA, I used a Gameshark(it was largely cause I wanted to enjoy the story without any struggle, I'm sorry), but still.On the plus side, everything story-wise is as great and engaging as I remembered, the ATB system that some GameRant article claimed V did first for some weird reason keeps me on my toes(even when set to wait, believe it or not), the music is SO freaking good, and somehow I drained my Steam Deck to 10% battery during a single session, which is odd cause I saw it was 43% and then I could swear that not long after it ended up hitting 10%, but screw it, this just shows how much I love this game.I also learned a few things I don't think I've known about, such as the fact that Mist isn't very damaged when you return there(I could swear I've gone there and saw it damaged in the PSP version, but I guess not?), and that if you talk to the Dancer in Mysidia after recruiting Palom and Porom, they also become pigs(no I didn't know this, I've never talked to the dancer after they joined the party, I only saw her after cause I forgot where she was).I also learned about the new feature here where you don't lose equipment when a party member leaves on accident, too. I just opted to not worry about the Staff Tellah had equipped, only to find out on here that it's in my inventory again. That's honestly really cool.My only other complaint is this PR doesn't include The After Years, nor the still PSP exclusive Interlude that connects the 2 games(and the fact that that's not a thing for the 3D Remakes is something I'm also sad about). _childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV is a game that's endured the test of time as one of the greatest JRPGs of all time. It was a jump in quality both in the story and music, playing kind of like a soap opera at times. As far as the story goes, it set a tone for the future game down the line. Romance, tragedy, and spoony bards were some of the prominent themes tackled throughout the game. FFII had taken a similar approach to story-telling, sharing some common themes and character archetypes but IV nailed the landing; especially when it came to character building. The music helped set the tone as well("Theme of Love" is so good). IV decided to take a different approach from its predecessors and lock characters to designated classes. The story uses this well when characters use aspects of their class to progress the party at roadblocks or give dialogue. I don't have too much to say that hasn't been before. It's definitely a game worth playing if you haven't. The feel is also different enough from it's DS remaster to warrant a replay as well if you've gone that route.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best entry experience out of all the Final Fantasy’s in the entire series. An extremely short game for a JRPG but that did not detract from my enjoyability.  FF4 does not have a great story to be fair, it is simple and for sure better than its predecessors but... it’s nothing but a sincere sweet story with a ton of plot holes and repeating side notes. The combat of the game is fine, one of the few FF's to give ability gains from leveling up each individual character. Because of that, it felt nicely bundled together. However, you were often given an extremely powerful party member early and because of this there wasn't a great RPG progression experience. Casting firaga isn't that impressive when you were casting it realistically 30 minutes into the game. Personally I feel like a lot of 4's unique qualities have major downsides that overall leaves it kind of a less substantial piece in the series then what most fans claim it to be. However, I think you can never take away that when 4 came out, it was easily the best Final Fantasy the series had gotten thus far, and that speaks well.

_childDocuments_.review: Great port of the game. Best reason to try this version is it has the classic pixel look, but they've been upgraded and have special effects that weren't possible in the original game. Another equally good reason is the music which is all seemingly orchestrated.This game is much easier than the original FFIV, though, in my opinion. I played through and never once had to stop and level up to get through an area or a boss. I died at a boss a few times or some random enemies but I just had to try again and be more ready strategy-wise, not EXP / stats-wise.A great new feature that wasn't present in the original game is the Auto-save that appears after dying. It seems to auto-save each time you go into a room or area. Died at the end game boss? No worries, give it another shot. In the original you'd likely have to back track a long ways before getting another chance, and lose exp and items that you would have gained up to that point.Definitely recommend this to Final Fantasy fans, or if you're interested in experiencing something closer to the original FF4 while having better music, graphics, and features that make the game more enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV has long been one of my favorite games, though this playthrough was my first time going all the way.      The story, the characters, and the soundtrack are all among the very best in all of Final Fantasy and the Pixel Remaster definitely does the original game justice. This is the first game to feature a lot of the elements that would become staples of the series, like ATB and general MP pools instead of magic levels. Even though the PR version includes an auto-save feature which helps to make the game a little easier and a lot shorter (you don't have to load from a save file if your party gets KO'd), it's still much more of a challenge than the previous PR games. You're gonna have to plan ahead and strategize for this one, especially in the later stages of the game.     If you're only gonna play one Pixel Remaster game, this is the strongest contender compared to the previous ones (FFVI makes it hard to say this is absolutely the one to get overall). It is a fun journey with lots of playable characters that really affect the battle dynamics as you go through the game and lots of memorable NPCs as well. Definitely give this game a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: +Remastered music is great+Nice touch up to the sprites+Added some QoL upgrades (fast forward/autobattle, beastary, arrows are infinite so you can actually use the rare ones)-They increased the XP from battles makes an already easy game even easier, though a patch fixed this somewhat.-Like all the PR versions, this does not include the GBA bonus dungeons.Overall it's a still a good game all these years later, but it's not very long and not very difficult so wait for a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV is the first game of the so called "SNES Trilogy", and it's the first Final Fantasy game that broke the ice of JRPG's. I believe Dragon Quest IV and Final Fantasy IV were the beginning of the golden age of JRPG's.The first Final Fantasy game that had named characters. No longer were your characters a blank book, now each character has its own story, its own problems, it's own characteristics. FF IV introduces a new way to tell the story. Back in the day, Final Fantasy IV blew people over how different the story was. It introduced complex things like your characters actions that brought consequence to the world, the redemption arc of the characters and plot twists all over. While by today's standards some plot twists in this game are predictable, I still think the story holds some water and it's quite good for those willing to jump into old school JRPG's.The combat is much more fluid, with this being the first game to introduce ATB or Active Time Battle. No longer do you make commands to your party members before they all take actions, now the fight is actually being fought in real time. This means you have to think a lot faster and plan moves in advance, which makes the game more challenging and fun. The bosses actually require an actual strategy, they aren't your common tank and spank bosses, so be prepared that if you are going blind, you might die a few times. Luckily, the game has a quick save option, which gives you an opportunity to try again quickly. The last boss was pretty hard, not as hard as Dragon Quest VI boss, but I would say he does give you a good challenge.Music is very good. Though not as memorable as Final Fantasy VI music, it has some pretty good OST. Old school JRPG fans will love it.Overall comparing to previous 3 Final Fantasy games, this one brings a whole new level. I haven't played V yet and I still regard VI as the best final fantasy, but IV would probably be in the top 5. The story is great, the gameplay is fun, I really liked the characters, especially the main character , and I recommend this fully.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: The Pixel Remasters seem to be pretty great ports/rebuilds of the classic Final Fantasy titles that deserve improved accessibility given their age and previous releases on outdated systems. Whilst not accurate to the old original pixel style, these Pixel Remaster games sit somewhere between the authentic visuals of a 90s 2D JRPG and the somewhat more romanticised visuals that fans of the series recall in nostalgic memories. On top of having their own good looking art style, the visuals are augmented with modern animation and effects to improve things such as water / light sources / spell effects. Also worth noting is the new Soundtrack arrangements present, these sound fantastic - some arguably superior to the originals (The Giant of Babil in FF4 specifically comes to mind).One final point, is that these games appear to be very easy to mod, and there is a very active modding community (find the 'VG Research & Modding' discord via the steam FF Modding group). I suggest every player replaces the default font package to one more to their liking (your favourite old FF fonts are likely already available). I would also urge people to mod FF4PR with the script from the FF4 DS Remake by Tom Slattery as it is far superior (I used a mod called 'Retranslattery'd', again - easily found and implemented via the discord).Overall the Pixel Remaster games are a welcome addition and a pretty good way experience these early series entries for the first time, or revisit them for a replay. They can be easily made nigh on perfect to your own preferences if you spend a little time modding them too.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent remaster that brings a classic to the modern era, looking and feeling as close to the SNES original as a modern game can.It is almost impossible to put aside my nostalgia for one of the first RPGs I ever played. If Final Fantasy 4 was part of your childhood growing up, you'll be happy to know the remake does an almost perfect job recreating it's look and feel from the SNES. The changes are subtle but feel authentic, like the character sprites, which feel improved and looking like how they were 'supposed' to look. Character abilities that were removed in the US version of the original are restored, like Cecil's Darkness and Rosa's Pray. The game's difficulty I feel matches the original, as it is pretty easy up until the 'Magnetic' cave, which as I kid I thought was insanely hard. The environments are also greatly updated, matching the original but with even more detail and many more flashy but fitting visual effects. It also still has that feature where you can see through the floor of some maps and see the floor below you.My only complaints lie with the new music remixes. The vast majority of it is great, but some songs, like the main boss themes feel too whimsical with the new instrument choices. I wish they had the option to use the original OST. (The Final Boss theme however, is one of the good remixes). There's also a lack of any real 'new' content, like other remasters have done. I would have liked to have new stuff, but the game is still great as-is.For the story, the new translation of the script is also a vast improvement, possibly even better than the 3DS remake. It can't quite fill the rather large holes in the game's story, but it goes as far as it can to make the characters sound more like real people, and sprinkle in a bit more personality and character development.If you haven't played this game before, this remake might be the best way to experience the game as many of us experienced it back on the SNES. While its story is full of tropes and stereotypes, and you can see all the twists a mile awhile, there's still an enthusiasm in how it presents this story and its characters. I still smiled and cheered when the cast had their big moments or just bounced around the screen. I have no real way of knowing if you will enjoy this game as much as I did, but I can say that so many years later, it's still a great game, and I'm glad they recreated it, flaws and all.

_childDocuments_.review: FF4 is my first Final Fantasy game, the brutally difficult DS version to be exact. It feels great to finally beat the game after over 15 years. So how does this hold up?FF4 didn't have the job system introduced in FF3. But it has fully defined characters that have pre-determined jobs with the job ability system from FF3. The caveat is that more skills are unlocked as you level up with the exceptions of summons. Unfortunately, lacking in player agency or build crafting makes it one of the least replayable Final Fantasy game in my opinion. Even the 3D remake struggles with making the game more replayable.I greatly despise the counter mechanics that many enemies have in this game. The final dungeon is just riddled with these, which makes it FF2 was the first Final Fantasy game to have a quite intricate story. FF4 was the first one to have that paired with an unforgettable cast of characters. Paired with that is the introduction of the Active Time Battle system - very iconic and used by many other RPGs afterwards. This game also greatly expanded the puzzle bosses concept that were first experimented in FF3, which I'd imagine to be quite a novel concept at the time. It's pretty flawed however, since a lot of the bosses can be very cryptic without any clues as to what you should be doing in the first place. It's very out of place for a Final Fantasy game to have cryptic bosses like this, but it's very much a relic of a game in the strategy guide era.Did I also mention mid-dungeon save points? It's such a massive lifesaver.----------FF4 truly is a great game for all its flaws. I just wish the game has more player agency to make it more replayable.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: I'm of mixed feelings. On one hand, this game has been a lot of fun and I have enjoyed experiencing final fantasy in the classic setting. On the other hand, some of the encounters too feel over tuned in favor of the ai, like behemoths and the final boss in particular. It was miserable and unfun to fight the final boss and the expectation was to basically not use magic I'd built up all game or grind. I think it comes down to allowing certain bosses to break the rules of turn based combat(i.e. counter attacks) with harder to read triggers and unclear timings for my own magic/attacks. Kinda sucks and kinda hurts an otherwise good time.7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't mind the remasters of FF1-3 for multiple reasons:No nostalgia for any of them (FF4 was the first one I played), and its hard to not improve on clunky Famicom-era menu interfaces and - in my opinion - on the music (retro-chiptune obsession with the FC soundchip over all over chips made me really tired of the chip's sound).So, this could have been quite close to the original, with re-arranged music. Unlike the previous remasters, where - naturally - the difference in orchestration is huge, it is much less noticeable here, with few exceptions (e.g., the town theme's more celtic touch, especially in the B-secion).However, for unfathomable reasons they did feel a need to rebalance the numbers game: more exp, less encounters, enemies act later into the battle than they should, etc.This makes sense in, say, FF2, which was an unbalanced mess anyway, but not so in FF4, which is one of the rare RPGs that are not broken in some way or another. As a result, I breezed through the game, and most bosses weren't able to pull of more than one action. Although FF4 always was on the easy side (as FF games tend to be), this felt comically pointless.This isn't a problem modders couldn't solve, but judged from what you get "in the package", this is the worst version of FF4 you could possibly play *if* you actually want to play a game, and not just rush through the story.Also, the continue-checkpoint system plus savepoints feels really...wrong.I'd go with any other version instead (PSP, DS, GBA/SFC, in this order), if the option is available.

_childDocuments_.review: Some people don't like the changes, and those people need to get over themselves. I played FF4 when it was new back in the 90s, and I loved it. When I found out about the Pixel Remakes, I was like "okay, yeah, that sounds awesome." Then it comes out and it gets praise, except by some people who are like "oh no, they violated my childhood because it doesn't sound like 16-bit chiptunes anymore."This game is awesome, it tells the story of a dude who doesn't know who his father is, which I guess is pretty cliche. He's got a best friend who has a rage-on because he wants his best friend's girlfriend, and she's not into manlets. They meet a little girl whose mom got double teamed really recently, so she's a bit messed up in the head from witnessing that. Then they meet an old dude whose daughter ran off with the lead singer of the local metal band, so he's hot on the trail.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: My favourite Final Fantasy game to-date. I played the original on SNES (back when it was ironically called Final Fantasy II) and since then it's sat in my mind as the gold standard for a sci-fi/Fantasy JRPG. FFIV does everything right, and this remaster makes it a more digestible experience while keeping the original charm. It's still at times a difficult game if you don't grind out a few more levels here and there, or if you don't equip the proper weapons for the area (like the mage masher for example in bahamut's cave) but the flow of the story is good by today's standards. If you enjoyed the original, this remaster is a nice 15+ hour stroll down memory lane.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: This is game is incredible. A game created in a time where the story and character development actually mattered because the creators couldn't rely on graphics. So many awesome, epic, funny twists and turns. This pixel remaster has been nothing but a delight to play. I am nearing the end of it just in time to go play the remaster of VI and I can't freaking wait! For reference, I had played FF7, FF8, FF9, FF10, and FF14, (and some of 13) prior to starting this entry. This story is easily top 3 out of all the Final fantasy games I've ever played. _childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly good!Final Fantasy IV is my favorite game of the series, so I was going in expecting to have mixed feelings. However, things were quite nice! Music was done really well, though it did admittedly take a moment to get used to as I have the old tunes so ingrained in my brain. Graphics are spot on, however. Some obvious enhancements, but nothing that I found jarring. The difficulty was a concern. Some previous remakes made it way too easy compared to the original version of the game. This was probably easier than the original FF4, but it felt very balanced and not 'easy' like the original US release was.It isn't quite perfect, however. I realize this is a nitpick, but I'm not a big fan of how they've recycled battle animations so heavily between these remasters. As simple as they were, I've always enjoyed the spell animations in each game, particularly FF4 and on, as 1-3 were a bit lacking for obvious reasons. Seeing FF4 reuse spell animations from the previous 3 felt cheap. As I continue to work my way through, I'm hoping that this will change, at the very least with FF6.Overall, not QUITE the definitive version, but close! Probably the one I will play going forward when I get the itch.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Just as I remember it. FFIV was my very first entry within the Final Fantasy series back in the very early 90's. Hell the USSR was still around when I played this. FFIV PR has been an improvement in almost every way save one aspect. The music. While sound quality improved the music quality itself more or less fell through the floor. I think the only song that truly out did its original was Within the Giant. Even the original OST from the SNES would have been a better choice to go with in my opinion. But beyond that, sprites look great, back drops are more crisp and clear, new animations for spells feel more powerful, UI is lightning fast in responsiveness, etc. etc. Script stays on point for the most part (You Spoony Bard is still very much alive). Story doesn't deviate from the original, so it definitely should work for most purists out there. Although certain translation quirks are gone (ie Meteo has been corrected to Meteor). So for those of you who enjoyed the charm that these woolseyisms brought, you'll be a little disappointed. Game play wise, it feels easier this time around as bosses seem less beefy than they were even in the SNES edition. So if you get that feeling you're not alone. Heck my first game over didn't happen till just after getting the Lunar Whale and getting Zantetsukened by Odin. So expect a noticeable drop in difficulty.All in all I give it a 9/10. Although I wouldn't put a lot of stock into that score as I am obviously going to have a bias towards this game.

_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: "Mixed" more than a true "thumbs down"Good:- massively reduced grinding- OST improvements are pretty good (not as good as the first 3 Pixel Remasters though)- it's still FF4 and so nostalgiaBad:- translation is actually terrible, no idea why they didn't just use the 3D translation which is 100x less awkward- more bugs. Unfortunately bugs are a recurring thing with these pixel remasters. In this case, item magic is completely broken and doesn't function correctly. Stardust rod, the best Rydia wep, does around 60 damage. I also had 2 occurrences where fights completely softlocked and I had to quit the game as character ATB was not moving and no action could be taken.- endgame is completely trashed. All the good QoL from the 3D version is removed which was an awful idea. The rare summons and pink tail needed for the achievement are back to being 1/1280 chance and sirens can no longer be purchased, meaning there's no good way to farm these items without spending potentially 50-100 hours praying for a miracle. They also kept the achievement requiring you to collect them so, yea. Unless you want to spend 3-4x the length of the game fighting the same mob on repeat the 100% achievement is unattainable.TL;DR:IMO, buy the 3D version and stomach the weird chibi art, the 3D version is overall mechanically a huge improvement over the PR version.EDIT:Drop rates and sirens being purchaseable have been fixed, making for a substantial improvement. I still prefer the 3D version but the achievement list is now pretty fine in this game, if that was a dealbreaker for you.

_childDocuments_.review: A huge leap forward for the franchise. An amazing sequel with solid storytelling, world building, and mechanics.I have to say this has been my favorite of the originals so far. Being my 8th FF game to play (only 5th finished though) I enjoyed this one from beginning to end. It truly feels like they pulled everything that worked from the prior games and utilized the better tech available to create a near perfect game. The story is not dissimilar from the prior 3, and is nothing to write home about, but the storytelling and worldbuilding are the best yet. It's the same old fated heroes tasked with saving the world from evil, and it involves crystals. This one changes things up a bit though where you start out as a dark knight, on the wrong side of things and makes the decision to leave that path behind. All of the characters feel truly unique with pretty decent dialogue. This one also offers a lot more storytelling through cutscenes (including battle sequences) that truly add to the depth of the game. The story is fairly linear, with an open world, but there are some side quests you can miss out on if you're not paying attention. The end game was a challenge, but was pretty rewarding in my opinion.Gone are swappable classes (or jobs), and magic is no purchased this time around. You learn new magic at certain levels based on the characters predefined class. Though characters swap out in your party throughout the game, it did not feel like a burden. You had a pretty consistent core of characters with one or two that change periodically. There weren't a whole lot of puzzles, and the dungeons were fairly straightforward, with secret paths throughout. Combat felt really good and varied. You had to use your characters abilities and specialties more, and it didn't feel forced. Mini-bosses and bosses felt like a proper challenge, and progression made feel like you had to grind too much to continue on in the story. Exploring the world was pretty straightforward as well but you get an airship much sooner. There were a number of dungeons littered throughout the world, and a couple other zones related to the story (no spoilers).The game felt cohesive, challenging, interesting, and fun. All of the game systems, story, and world made for a remarkable experience.I played this entirely on Steam Deck and it ran flawlessly. 60hz/60fps and didn't break a sweat (not surprising, but still nice). I had 0 crashes or frame dips. The deck is tailored for this kind of experience. It took me just over 22 hours to complete.Overall, this is one of my favorite Final Fantasy games. It had awesome storytelling, the progression and combat felt solid, and it was just a fun experience. Highly recommend for any RPG/JRPG fan.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Every single early Final Fantasy I play (with the exception of II) is getting exponentially better with each and every release, IV is no exception. It continues the tradition of having a better story with more involved characters and world building; The gameplay is again another step forward directly from III and begins to exhibit the trend later titles enjoy of swapping out party members as the story demands, keeping things from getting repetitive by "shuffling the deck" so to speak.I honestly don't really know what more I can say, I loved this game A LOT, enough so that i'm likely going to buy the pseudo-sequel The After Years just because I want to see more of the characters and world that Square built here. I'm incredibly excited to get to V and VI and see what else they managed to create.I do wish the price was about 20% lower though; either way I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible remaster with just a few small quirks. The art is fantastic. The buildings, sprites and environments feel like a proper "pixel" art style that really honors the original game but you can see drastic improvements in things like the water and fire. The combat is fun and grindy (in a good way) like I would expect from a Final Fantasy game.The music might be the best part. Nobuo Uematsu has really outdone himself, as is his wont. There are minor problems such as the font. It's off and distracting. Luckily it's a very easy fix just by changing a couple files but it should really be an in-game option. Some areas of the game also have some "jitter" or choppiness when the screen is scrolling. It seems worse when the game automatically pans the camera but I've noticed it a few times while I was controlling it as well. It does this only occasionally and even when it does it's not the worse thing. Could stand to be fixed but it's not a deal breaker at all. An amazing story with a satisfying feel and soundtrack for less than $20. I certainly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Its a proper classic and the first Final Fantasy I played as a kid that felt like it focused as much on the characters and their relationships as saving the world.  The writing is a little dated, but the gameplay for me is a lot like a warm blanket on a cold day.  Players totally new to the old Final Fantasy games may find some challenge in keeping the game moving forward and some combats may prove difficult if trying to rush through without a care.  One of the better games for easing up on "mandatory" grind, Final Fantasy IV still retains a sometimes frustratingly high rate of random encounters.In the end, Final Fantasy IV takes the player on a journey that is short enough to stay invested and long enough to feel satisfied when the credits roll.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot which this release of FF4 does right. The pixel artstyle is gorgeous and also maintains the look and charm of the original game far better than any of the other rereleases, the remixed soundtrack is almost entirely great, way better than the one from the 3D version (though I would still appreciate the OG soundtrack being there as an option). The menus are easy to navigate, movement is super snappy, animations are quick and on point. Basically on a surface level its a great remake of an established classic.However where the game does fail as some others have pointed out is the completely and utterly gutted level of challenge, the original FF4 was never a difficult game to begin with and could easily be completed with no grinding required as is the case with most old school JRPGs, with the multiplied EXP gains you basically get an entire dungeons worth of EXP from just a few encounters in this version which makes you so overleveled so quickly which turns both normal encounters and boss encounters into a total joke, dying is a very hard thing to do here. Furthermore as far as I can tell you can now run away from any given normal encounter with 100% certainty before the enemies have even a chance of touching you, basically making the encounters entirely pointless if you so choose, I get it that there are people who don't like random encounters in their RPGs but if them being optional is the idea then wouldn't it be a better idea to just include an option to completely eliminate random encounters? it would achieve the same exact result for those people without having to run away from battle after battle after battle and people who actually do like to have enemies to fight in their dungeon can still do so and not have an immediate "get out jail free card" at their hands at any given time. Being able to run away from battles is an important part of the dungeon crawl experience but it should not be free like this. For the late game in particular some of the more powerful spells like "Curaja", "Flare" and "Bio" have had their cast times removed for whatever bizarre reason, not that it makes much of a difference when the game is already so easy but it seems like a very pointless change that just completely ignores the game's defined rules for the players benefit. There's also the always present dungeon map which on a base level I think it a good improvement, however I think it would make sense to make it so it'd fill out as you explore the dungeon like it is in the 3D version instead of just spoiling the entire layout immediatedly, and as it is an option of being able to completely toggle it off would be very much appreciated.Also as a small extra nitpick for a rerelease so focused on quality of life improvements I can't believe that there is no way to sort your item inventory ingame, later on the thing ended up being so messy it took an unreasonable amount of time to find what I needed.It's such a shame all in all because I think in many ways presentation wise it truly is amazing version of the classic and would no doubt be my goto, but without the challenge there isn't much of a "game" to enjoy here and unfortunately it is for this reason that I would never play this version of the game again. Unless you're just here for the nice pixel graphics and the soundtrack this version of FF4, sadly, is a waste of time.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice nostalgic romp through the foundational tropes of Final Fantasy and JRPGs in general, with the added wrinkle of the main character starting out as a fantasy special-forces war criminal for an imperialistic state who (unknowingly) incinerates a bunch of innocent people within the first 30 minutes of the game.  There's a lot to FF4 that's surprisingly dark and complex for a game from 1991, but sadly despite the strong opening, a love for melodrama, death fake-outs and falling into well-worn tropes made the game go from truly great to just OK for me (of course, FF4 *invented* a lot of these tropes*, so it's more the case of a 30+ year-old game showing its age).  It's also incredibly easy, with only a few difficult fights and spots where I needed to grind.  Still, I liked the characters well enough and don't feel like I've wasted my time playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV is my favorite game in the series.I cannot recommend this version.I've been playing my way through the Pixel Remaster series, and so far my impression is that the folks doing the remastering don't always understand the thing they're working with.  in this particular case, it's even weirder because now that we're in the SNES era, the "remaster" isn't really any better quality than the original material.The graphics are mostly a draw--sprite changes are either subtle and unnecessary (in the case of monsters) or middling to slightly better (in the case of PC sprites).The effects are largely worse.  Yes, the spellcasting has higher-fidelity, mostly more complicated FX, but it lacks the immersion and character of the original material.  It's like removing a supporting motive from an orchestral rearrangement--it just doesn't feel right.Speaking of orchestral rearrangements, most of the soundtrack misses the mark entirely.  The best tracks are the ones with the fewest alterations (e.g., Into the Darkness), while the worst are the ones that completely miss that decide to add backbeats to what are decisively brassy orchestral numbers.  The arrangers appear to have completely missed the day in class where they discussed dynamics as well.And speaking of dynamics, the various cutscenes are completely devoid of them.  There are several points in the plot where the timing of the character animations is meaningful and contributes to the tone of the scene.  In this version, pretty much every possible pause between character animations is simply omitted, making the result jarring and lacking emotion.The translation is another hit-and-miss.  Some parts are definitely improved over the original Woolsey.  Some parts are definitely not.Honestly, you're better served either getting hold of an original SNES cart of this, getting the GBA version, or playing the 3D version.  (I assume the 3D version here on Steam is essentially a port of the DS version, and the latter is actually very enjoyable considering how different it is.)  Skip this remaster.(Starting to have some trepidation about playing V and VI PR now....)

_childDocuments_.review: FF4 is the culmination of a couple of strong ideas that came from FF2. Among the pixel remasters, this title is when you start to really see the noticeable progression of ideas from game to game.The rotating/temporary party members in particular were done really well as a plot device as I found myself way more invested in their individual stories that tied into the big picture. This is also my favorite FF story-wise from the first half of the mainline titles particularly because it presents a balanced dose of both tragedy and resolution with an ending that leaves things open without delivering a cliffhanger.I really enjoyed following Cecil's emotional journey as he grew through his inner turmoil combined with the help of the cast. I think one of the most important factors leading to this was how he was repeatedly taught (some may even say it was too much) the value of a life not to mention his own. To say that FF4 made me feel at peace is an understatement and after playing all iterations of this universe available on Steam, the Pixel Remaster is definitely my favorite version.With regards to the music, FF4PR also features my 2nd favorite overworld theme (next to FF9) that really stands on its own. I know a lot of people prefer the older OSTs but the overworld track in particular shows how much detail you can add to a any modern rendition. The track featured expert use of woodwind instruments that really shine through the longer you listen to it. It doesn't have my favorite overall OST, but it was a pleasant and balanced experience through and through.Please check this pixel remaster of FF4 out! If you are a fan of a good story, then FF4 can serve as a spiritual starting point for anyone who wants to peek into the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a LOT to talk about when it comes to Final Fantasy 4. This is an incredibly important title for multiple reasons. This is the first real final fantasy to come out on the SNES, everything before that was Famicom/NES, not only that but this was also the 2nd game to finally come outside of Japan. It even was the first FF game to change the turn based combat system to the more active ATB system. This means that this was a major step up, from a technical, graphical and audience perspective. For many people this was the first final fantasy they saw and/or played. This is the only Final fantasy game in the pixel remaster series that I had any experience with prior to playing it. And I remember having a lot of fond memories of it. Does the game live up to the build up I am creating? Kinda.Lets start with the biggest change to the previous FF games, story. Before this game there was almost nothing to talk about, the stories were lacking and suffered a LOT of problems for different reasons, FF 2 had the only salvageable story and even that didn't turn out all that great. This game completely changes that around, the story is MUCH more involved, its much more linear/handholding, and it is much more fun. I seriously love the story of this game even nowadays, its pretty simple but there is a lot more character to everything, there are so many small details in the animation of the characters which gives them a lot of personality. The characters get more time to get explored, even the villains are much more interesting this time around. The protagonist, Cecil, feels extremely iconic and has a lot of depth for it being the first real story of the FF series. There are much more scripted cutscenes and battles, this can sometimes become a bit too much and mess with the pacing of the game but its much preferred over the completely static world of the previous games. Overall this is the first FF game with a unique story to tell. Years later it still holds up relatively well, even if some parts of it haven't aged as well, like how some plot twists end up feeling pretty random.Dungeon designs feel much more interesting, with a lot of them being tests of resource management of MP and items. The dungeons will also provide a lot of items. It sucks that many of the equipments you unlock don't feel all that exciting, they will usually just provide you with a small amount of extra attack or defense, this is something the game definitely could have done better.One other gameplay aspect I have to cover are the side quests and optional areas, there are a lot more of them compared to previous games, even with the game being linear, the game will sometimes just let you explore a bunch and during those moments you will find a lot of extra stuff that is completely optional, there are even some optional cutscenes/conversations that you don't have to watch if you don't want to but that seem pretty important to the story. Its quite fun to see and its one of the more rewarding parts of the game.Not everything is as fantastic as I remember it though, as I said the game is much more linear and much more straight forward. There are no real Job systems like in FF 3. Instead the game sets characters into very specific roles, this means the battles feel less unique and more like a puzzle you have to figure out. Especially the bosses feel like real puzzles you sometimes have to figure out, it can be pretty fun if you don't just stomp the entire fight. If you play the game with the standard settings, you will quickly figure out that this game can be really easy, especially with things seemingly being more toned down compared to the original. I recommend looking at the settings menu in game and changing the battle speed and setting the game to active instead of wait. This changes the speed at which battles happen and makes it so enemies will keep attacking even as you select spells, this is the closest you will get to a difficulty menu in the pixel remaster series and it might help create a more interesting battle dynamic.One thing I can't forget is the music, this has been standout in all pixel remaster games, but FF 4 gets the first real mention because a lot of its music is incredible, some scenes are carried by the music alone, the theme of love has stuck with me all these years, its like my childhood flooded back to me as I looked at these characters and heard them speak to each other over this song. Characters and scenes I should barely be remembering came back to me like a flash of lightning, an entire romantic relationship is told just through this song alone and its stunning. I know its nostalgia speaking, but I guarantee you will probably feel something equally as special in your own unique way. The passion that was put into this soundtrack still gives me goosebumps even today.I am also one of those people who had this game be their introduction into the series. At the time I had to watch a lets play of it because it didn't come out in Europe for a very long time. But this game was so incredibly important in the creation of my image of what an RPG is and could be. There are so many characters, scenes, songs, fights and even side quests that stuck with me for all this time. Its a true testament of what games can mean to someone and what a good game is. FF 4 might not be perfect, but its still incredibly good and a fantastic starting point into the world of Final Fantasy. Out of all the FF games, this will be the first one I can wholeheartedly recommend, even if you don't have the nostalgia I have for this game, I am sure you will find something to love just like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: THE BENCHMARK FOR THE FRANCHISEAfter watching the ending, I'm blown away on how many things the story throws at you. Loads of lore from previous games come together in this game, creating a more believable, alive world. Without spoiling anything, I had fun with the world and some moments throughout the game.What about the game itself? Final Fantasy IV is where the franchise found its footing after having the foundations laid up by the first three games. Unlike its previous installment, Final Fantasy III, FFIV omits the job system and had a more focus on story. The story is much better than the previous games. Characters have backstories and their own development. But still, I can't help notice on how many moments aren't that well fleshed out. Each character, although very likable, only have like one big moment. And then they just when quiet and being a normal party member. Not all the characters are like this tho. Some have well fleshed out moments while others have moments that just... happened. But still, turning off your brain and having fun with the adventure will grant you a hell of a good time.This game is the first one to introduce the Active Time Battle combat. Unlike the Tradtional Turn-Based from the first three games, you now have a more active and reactionary turn-based combat where the time still moves in combat. You hace to decide fast on wether to attack, cast spells, use items, etc, since you will be attacked if you're not fast enough. I have no problems with the combat since I've experienced the ATB system in its prime from FF7. But its fun to see where it all starts.Speaking of combat, I like how they tackle challenges in difficulty in dungeons. All the dungeons have their own hazards and every one of them never felt the same (Except for some art designs but we'll get there.). I'm not gonna spoil but, some dungeons will make you have cast certain spells in order to safely traverse it. This also applies to enemies where not every mobs and boss are the same. Each enemy have their own set of attacks and unique battle mechanics which can test how fast you can adapt. Some may be immune to magic, some may have forms which is undefeatable. All the bosses have their own unique attacks and is a strong point in the game.In dungeons you also have save points, a room where you can set up a tent for your party. This can ease up your travellings especially for some very harsh dungeons. Speaking the travelling, the whole overworld is huge and fun to explore. I'm not gonna spoil, but had a lot of fun experiencing some twists and areas throughout my adventure.On the downsides, some artstyle and designs kinda felt samey especially in the earlier parts. For example, the first two towns, caves, dungeons, have exact same artstyle and I kept getting confuesd if I have venture here or not cause everything looks the same. I've mention the second downside on the story part where I found things that are not well fleshed out.Obligatory gush on how AMAZING THE SOUDTRACK IS. Nobuo Uematsu please notice me!!!Overall, this game is where I felt where Final Fantasy take its form, mainly because of its focus on story unlike the first three. Had a blast overall throughout my gameplay.4/5

_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV has been one of my favorite JRPGs since the mid-90s.Is this the best version of the game? Absolutely not. It lacks a lot of the extended content we've seen in other versions, but it does have its own charm, though subtle. FFIV the Complete Collection for PSP is arguably, in my opinion, and maybe many others, the best way to play FFIV in its entirety and extended content.That being said, this is the stock version of FFIV [mostly] with some added quality of life improvements [dungeon and town sprinting, auto-battle, cleaned-up UI, etc.]I'm a fan of some of the remixed and modern tracks [one of the most consistent features in these pixel remakes] but it's largely hit or miss. The standard battle theme starts every time with a particularly annoying set of horn notes that becomes more and more grating the more you play, but I've learned to tune it out mostly. The final boss theme, might be one of the best remixes I've heard in awhile - it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BOPS.I'm unsure of which version of Final Fantasy IV this is, since it should be noted that it's [incredibly] easy compared to the other pixel remakes. I don't remember FFIV being quite this easy, but it could be the QoL improvements that I'm overlooking. The only challenge comes from the final boss, and maybe a few monsters in the final dungeon who have the potential for party-wiping abilities [no matter what level you are] but even that wasn't much of a bother.I will note that the way these games calculate damage and defense is pretty mind-boggling and irritating. I suppose we all got used to balancing and being able to generally accurately estimate numbers at a certain point in the series.I played this mostly for nostalgia, and that was enough of a purchase for me. Do I recommend it? It may or may not be for you. It IS in my opinion, when the writing for Final Fantasy started to get particularly interesting and good and characters start to feel more fleshed out and alive. For me, it was a trip back to my pre-teens. For others, it might be a bit of a slog.Choose what you will.Strong 6 / Weak 7 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Faithful recreation of the original cart with updated graphics. No additional features was a weird way to go, and continuing with the incredibly difficult RNG of a certain late game item was also a bummer (over 100 fights so far and still nothing), especially without a way to purchase a certain item. Adding back in the features not found on the classic FF2 American cart was cool though. Reorchestrated OST is a nice touch and leaves me excited for the eventual FFVI release, quick save function is ultra useful as an adult with limited time to play the game.Buy it if you missed out on other updated versions, avoid if you don't want to spend money on another version. Just enjoy the game.

Gold and exp rates are insane, there is no challenge whatsoever. why cant we get a mode with the original difficulty!? I don't mind an auto battle necessarily or a fast walk, but there is nothing at stake when the difficulty is so easy.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: My issue with FF1-FF6 is1: Not exciting battles, if i were you. Only play this for 3 hours on saturday morning, then do something else after this. The only game thats slightly fun is FF2.2: Main reason "Few frames of animations in battle, with blinking JPEGs enemy i dont consider the most exciting gameplay". Because even by those standards then there were better RPGs like Shining Force or Phantasy Star SEGA game.But if they make you happy then i wont argue!
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy 4 is by far the best instalment in the Pixel Remastered series by far. It allowed me to relive my childhood RPG that I will always cherish in my Super Nintendo era years of gaming. Personally, I didn't like hearing my favourite ost soundtracks get butchered with the remixes. If they had an option of keeping the original snes tunes or using the new remixes would have been great. Remixes sounds great too but I still prefer the old school if I was playing a game for Nostalgia. I do appreciate the animation in some parts of the game that made it look really cool. I do like the map that reveals how much treasure is in each area. The patch that came out on October 2, 2021 made the summoning and pink tail grind much easier. The person who's guide I was following showed a screenshot of putting in 70 hours of grinding spells and that put a lot of non-motivational thoughts in my head. After 3-4 hours of grinding I was able to get the pink tail and all 4 summoning spells (Cockatrice, Goblin, Mind Flayer and Bomb). I found Goblin to be the hardest one to grind for some reason. Pink tail is hard to grind cause the mobs a high level end game baddie that requires you to be around the 70's for an easy farm grind. It all comes down to using Bahamut with Rydia with a few physical attackers to finish the battle. Story was epic and entertaining to be a part of. It's a major improvement from Final Fantasy 1-3 instalments.My favourite thing about this game was characters learning spells at a certain level. No crystals that gives you like 20+ jobs that annoys the heck out of me like in FF3. Characters got better back stories too and when a certain npc dies you kind of want to cry as well. Pros: 1. Great music2. Great story3. Great main and side characters (Edward can go hang himself with his hide ability). Cons: 1. Grinding summoning spells sucks. 2. Pink tail grinding sucks just as much. 3. Game is way too easy in this version. 4. No extra contentAll four final fantasy games up to this point I just auto attack the final boss while sitting on the John. It was that easy and it felt like it needed a bit of tuning up.    Well looking forward to playing Final Fantasy 5.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: just an overall great version of a great game.  FFVI may be the better game, but this game was such a huge leap that to me it was the first real example of how much better the SNES was.  Such a great story and characters brought to life, except Edward.  Edward can go hide an an Ant Lion's bum for all I care.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Played the original FFV when it had its release here in Canada. Major nostalgia playing this again. Yes the combat is easier than usual, I noticed some missing abilities and how overtuned your weapons/abilities are versus the Japanese or even the US release. Too easy to gain XP but in some cases this is welcome (Magnetic Cave comes to mind)All in all, this game and everything about it hit the spot for me. I didn't mind the pace of the play, I think people are a bit taken aback because the difficulty is eased a bit from the US release but they are also progressively more skilled from the last time they played this game and I think that played a major factor in my playthrough this time around.If you love FF4, this is a must have.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Avoid wasting money on this and go play the SNES and PSX emulators instead.Or if your feeling so bold,Try me and accept my challenge.  . How can one prove this? Your steam game "time played" will show less than 2hours and with 100% completion.Do you accept my challenge? comments will be opened.My review:1) Ruined the nostalgia cause I didn't get my expired can of whoop-ass included.(adverse effects of whoop-ass)2) There are Trainers already available, and I used it to speed up the farming for those abysmal summon drops. (mind flayer in particular, and for bomb cause I never had it)3) This game is too easy. You can play the story normally, and not struggle /ever/ unless your being stupid or are distracted. Ex: I accidentally used Darkness, killed the enemies, but died due to mechanic. and that was it.4)When I grinded, I was surprised I could hit lv25 within an hour, without ever passing the first story trigger (past a cave)5) Music is upgraded versions, which aren't bad but no options available for the classic SNES versions. not /everything/ has to be upgraded, improved or removed.6) Final achievement is indicative of the last save; not the final strike. be weary of that.Additionals:I think this is the original NES version, because Edward will use Cower, and /NEVER EVER ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ATTACK!/. but the game is to easy for that to be an issue;i.e. all party dying and edward being low health and last man standing. GG there bois. But unlikely in this version.The EXP is halved for all characters. I remember playing the SNES as a 9 year old, and  at lv75+, she learned it at lv65, and I was lv65 before even touching the  area let alone the ship to get there. so i think skills are learned stupid early.Game could really use some elemental resistance sheets cause ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. You could wear everything for fire/ice but it blatantly states one weakens, so what if you mix and match? you'd literally have to do personal tests.Speaking of elements. Its sad when the ele are pushovers because of their elemental weaknesses, and it's so sad this is what this game has become. I will first handedly admit that the game for older generations such as myself who had played before, would have been able to know whats up, and with out educational advances (knowing what certain stats, and benefits meant more clearly.) yeah the game could have became easier. but the state it is in right now.It's too easy, it should have been left untouched EXP-wise. Because to put it bluntly: If you start grinding for your summons. You WILL over level. When you want certain items... YOU WILL OVER LEVEL. when you want beastiary spawns YOU... SHOULD make a 2nd save and not effect your levels. mostly to avoid missing 1 time zones.

While this, like 6, might seem cliche by today's standards, this is one of the games that started those cliches and influenced many games that came after it.The Pixel Remaster is amazing. _childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the last 3 game i subjected myself to 100% this one. This is one of my favorite games in the series how ever it's one draw back if your going for 100% is the rediculous low drop rates of items for the achievements that may have you pulling out your hair or ressort to the cheating method which i've read people do. Do your self a favor and stock up on sirens. They will be of great help when farming a certain enemy for a certain elusive pink tale later on. Be sure to have a check list handy for the missable stuff and those one time only dungeons. you will need it  :)  With that out of the way the game is still pretty good and holds up well today.  If you played the previous final fantasy games then you've basically already played this one. The remastered music is once again well done. The story is a little better here then the previous 3 games with the characters having actual thoughts and feelings on current events.  The next 2 games will step this up a notch but we will get to those when the time comes. If you are new to the series this is a great starting point as it have all the basics here that you will want top learn and it's not all that hard other then those stupid drop rates which they may patch later? Just buy it  :)
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: I don't remember the game being this short originally, but I guess it kind of is.  But much like the other entries in the PR collection, the updated graphics, animations, music, etc is all fantastic.  I do wish it had some of the content from the later editions of the game, such as the Cave of Trials.  It's card to call these the definitive version with cut content.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: If you never played Final Fantasy, this is a good one to start with.  It's one of the more basic ones in the series and is easy to play.  Story isn't that complicated with less big twists then the others.  Battle system is very simple and doesn't involve a lot of decisions in what options to choose until much later in the game.If you are a veteran of this one in particular, you may want to skip it.  It doesn't add much to the previous iterations and is more or less a faithful recreation of the Snes version of the game.  It comes with a few QOL changes within the menus and battles but other than that just the same old FF4.If you are like me and can't get enough of FF4, then you'll pick it up anyways and experience it yourself once again.  You'll notice the little nuances they added to the pixels, cut scene animations, spell effects and dialog.  Ye old Spoony Bard is still there!
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike the 3D version, I experienced no issues at all while playing this (with the 3D version, I suffered frequent crashing). I agree with the other reviews which claim that this version is a bit too-easy. The only grinding I did was at the , for the rest of it, no grinding was required, and Rydia had all her spells, plus a few more levels by the time I was at the end. On the PSP version, I recall being nowhere near this point, at the end of the game. I don't think she even knew Flare.Overall, I'm very happy to have Final Fantasy IV on my laptop, this time being playable and experiencing no issues.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Note: On a journey to 100% ALL Final Fantasy titles on Steam~This Final Fantasy deserves to (and has) go down in history for the introduction of ATB (Active Time Battle) system, and all the praise in the world (Thanks Hiroyuki Ito!).It also feels like the first HUGE Final Fantasy. Content-wise, I don't think it's that much more than Final Fantasy III, but there is so much more character interaction which creates a nice immersion and engagement with the story and environment, in a level I could not get from the previous titles.I also feel this is the last Final Fantasy where doing more than the base game is still a chill experience. Later titles will be introducing harder chest/bestiary/blue magic/mini-games and other quirks (I am looking at you FFX lightning mechanic), that make end-game items and optional content sometimes super hard/grindy.My one gripe with the game is that battles sometimes felt hard without good reason to. I am not sure if it's the current Steam version, or the battle system itself, but I suspect it's the combination of two great things:5 active Characters + ATB on the same game. There are so many actions and menus to scroll through, and it can be almost stressing at times juggling everything successfully, especially when certain enemies seem to make more than 1 devastating action right after another (This can be offset if you plan to 100% this title due to the grind needed alone)!If you plan to 100% this game, I highly recommend the achievement guide posted by lylat on Steam! I have followed their guides for a number of games, and using this one is highly recommended.I hope I was able to provide some unique perspective for you, and was able to help you decide whether you should play this game if you were on the fence!
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: The game works fine no issues with completing it or experienced any time during the game play through. It is more expansive world than FF3, the characters are only slightly better. This title does not feature the jobs system and you are stuck playing the characters as they are and cannot really customize what jobs or magics they use. You are also bombarded with several different "guest" characters that will come and go from your party periodically. As for story it is standard fair for RPGs, it is not great but not horrible either. Overall a good recommend for the final fantasy franchise, especially early games.
