_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game (then called FF2) being played on the Super Nintendo system at a young age, I remember being so excited that my godmother (who pampered me A LOT) bought me the system AND the game. I credit this game as the spark that started me on the road of computer gaming, and the love of role-playing games above all.Just 60 minutes into this remaster, and I am in love all over again...
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV is a soap opera. It's grandiose, absurd, bombastic, and very charming. There is a lot of appeal in playing an older title with a simpler structure that just....works (and works well). The xp, gold, and damage curves feel very tailor-fitted to making the experience smooth. The quicksave feature, the optional boost settings, among with other adjustments make this a very accessible introduction to old Final Fantasy games. It's about a 20-hour game, and was quite fun throughout. Looking forward to trying the next title.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: While I believe I owned FFIV on the GBA, and definitely played but didn't own it for the SNES, my only reliable memory suitable for comparison is the 3D remake, as ported to iOS. The first thing that struck me is how much time 3D Final Fantasies spend on pre and post battle animations. Suffice to say, and especially with the battle speed settings in conjunction with autobattle, you can grind really fast here. Others have said that the exp to level or exp from enemies has been adjusted to take about half the time as well. Anyway, leveling is fast. It's probably for the best, because of all the FFs, IV constantly swaps your party members in and out leaving you never feeling like you're all set.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: The music is some god tier stuff here and I've liked the songs in the previous games but damn this takes the cake so far especially the into the darkness!The gameplay here is just a bit different compared to the previous games but that's how every one of the pixel remasters were and you will just to it finely, there's quite some tactics needed in combat but nothing too difficult!If you are interested in going through all mainline FF games like I do this is a great journey for sure and the remasters of V and VI is coming which I'm excited about!Go get it
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy IV is my favorite game from the first six games.  I was not disappointed with this game at all.  The sprites and graphics are very close to the original, so much so that its how you might think that this is how the original looked had you never played it before.  I have played FF4 so many times over the years and had a great time playing the remaster.  The music is absolutely wonderful.  The script is great.Are there improvements that could be made? Sure!  Give the player options for the font, the window background color, let us switch to the original score if we wanted, and an option for auto-run would be great.Hopefully we will get some DLC that can add in later content from the GBA and PSP versions!I had an awesome time with this game, anyone that loves Final Fantasy IV should give this a chance!
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: The recent update that includes features from the console version fixes any grumbles I've had with the pixel remasters.  The new font options give an alternative to the otherwise hideous default English fonts, and now you can also toggle between the original soundtrack and newer "remastered" songs.  It's great both options are here, the original OST is incredible and the newer versions are also a treat.As for the game itself?  This is one of my favorites of the "classic" Final Fantasy games.  You get a beautiful fantasy setting, challenging battles, wonderful music... everything that set the standard for these games.  Rydia made summoning cool, no other final fantasy summoner has the street cred of surviving the attack of a legendary monster as a kid, and eventually growing up to beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of the same monster and summon him for a handful of MP.   Other summoners just have flashy attacks from stuff they find, Rydia made monsters her ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite out of the entire series.  I was very pleased with this Pixel Remaster, and this is the easiest so far when compared to FF1-3.Some changes that I noticed aside from the updated graphics and animations for spells....The entire music score is updated.Arrows are now infinite if you choose to use a Bow.They added a vendor before the 4 Elementals in the Giant.Could be wrong here, but in the Bahamut cave I believe they removed the "random" Behemoth encounters and placed a few at set points you have to defeat to move forward.I'm comparing this to the SNES Version of FFII(FFIV) after many years.Absolutely reccommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: I have played many of the versions of FFIV (basically all them starting with the SNES, this is one of my favourite all time games): and I am enjoying this version as much as any other I played. I like to turn on the classic effect for the graphics, but I would recommend you try both and choose what you like best. The remastered music is excellent, one of my favourite aspects of the pixel remaster, If I could make one suggestion it would be to provide an update (or even a modestly priced DLC) that has the extra dungeon from the GBA version.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good remaster to a classic. It is the SNES version, so no bonus content at all. But the new music is oh so nice. Only a couple tracks hit my ear wrong. But overall, the soundtracks keep being amazing in these Pixel Remasters. The graphics are ok, and highly recommend you seek out the Final Fantasy mod discord to tinker with anything from the fonts to restoring the SNES (or even DS) soundtrack. Hit all the right nostalgia notes.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Music is great, graphics are very nice, and the gameplay is still solid. A great remaster... except it's very easy... like the other 3 pixel remasters currently out. FFIV is my favorite JRPG, and I've beaten the original, about 15 times. I can recommend this version to casual players, or new players. It's more challenging than some of the other remasters so far, but it's still way too easy. Play this if you love FFIV, not if you love a challenge. I beat this in about 12 and a half hours, so I can't recommend it at it's current price however.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend, but less than the other FF pixel remasters. It's the first Final Fantasy to really have a full-formed, character based narrative, which is impressive but leaves it a bit antiquated. _childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy is my favorite franchise, but there's still a couple I haven't played. This was one I never played until this pixel remaster and I've now played it through twice both here and on PS5. I think it's the best of the classic era FF (though I still haven't played V at the time of writing). Very cool story that I somehow never had spoiled for me and would have blown my mind if I'd played this on the gameboy advance back in the day when I had a chance. It feels like the right amount of story and characters fit into it where VI personally felt just a little too long.Pros:+ Very fun and classic FF story + Some amazing characters+ About as awesome an 8 bit game as there is+ Some of the coolest Final Fantasy tropes are here+ great soundtrack Cons:- It's that style of older game that may require a guide at least at some points - solid combat that feels familiar from later games, but nothing too special
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Full nostalgia check here. The updated pixel art is fantastic, the soundtrack is incredible, and the optional battle automation and dungeon run button make grinding/and dungeon crawling much more enjoyable. If you liked the original, you'll be very happy with this version.*no GBA extra content, though. That's kind of a bummer.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: I was screaming with joy, when i saw, that this game gets a pixel remaster. The nostalgia hit me like bazooka. It was awesome. Untill.... i realized 3 things: First: The Challange dropped way too much. Bosses are way too easy now. should have kept it at the difficulty level it was before. Second: you can't change your characters as soon as you get fight Zemus. And most importantly THIRD: WHY NO POST GAME????????? This was like the best part of the game. Unique tests for everyone of the Characters. Made with so much love and detail and live. Sorry but the Lack of these 3 Things puts the enjoyment of the Game down about 60% for me.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY IV

_childDocuments_.review: Four elemental Crystals, each possessing awesome power, lie scattered throughout the realm. However, men are quick to covet things which offer strength, and easily corrupted by the might which they possess. Seduced by the promised power of the Crystals, the kingdom of Baron begins employing unprovoked force to seize them from peaceful nations. The dark knight Cecil - Lord Captain of Baron's elite force, the Red Wings - is ordered by his king to obtain the Crystals, but soon begins to question the monarch's motives. Stricken with grief at his own actions, yet burdened by his loyalty to his country and his personal sense of honor, Cecil at last decides to turn from the path of darkness and destruction. Enraged, the king accuses him of disloyalty, strips Cecil of his command, and sends him off to slay a mysterious beast that lurks in the nearby Valley of Mist. Cecil embarks on a fateful journey that will bring trials, betrayals, friendship, loss and self-discovery. Can Cecil open his eyes and become the man of honor that he must be? Dive into the first RPG to incorporate the innovative Active Time Battle system, now further enhanced and refined for the Nintendo DS. Train and customize Whytkin by playing a variety of mini-games and challenge another player to head-to-head battle via local wireless connection.

name: FINAL FANTASY V
detailed_description: FINAL FANTASY I-VI Bundle Purchase the bundle now to receive all soundtracks and wallpapers from FF1-6! Soundtracks and Wallpapers will unlock in line with each title’s launch. See individual store pages for details. The games that inspired a generation come to life once more, in the ultimate 2D pixel remaster! Purchase the bundle and receive FINAL FANTASY FINAL FANTASY II FINAL FANTASY III FINAL FANTASY IV FINAL FANTASY V FINAL FANTASY VI This bundle lets you purchase all six games from FINAL FANTASY 1 to FINAL FANTASY 6 at a discount price. It also contains a sound track, featuring total of 20 tracks and total of 14 unique wallpapers. Enjoy universally updated 2D pixel graphics and the beautifully rearranged soundtrack. Gameplay is improved with modernised UI, and extras such as a beastiary, illustration gallery and music player allow further immersion into the world of the game. ＊These games are newly developed remaster editions based on the original titles. Some of the changes and additional elements found in other remakes of these games are not included. About the Game A remodeled 2D take on the fifth game in the world-renowned FINAL FANTASY series! Enjoy the timeless story told through charming retro graphics. All the magic of the original, with improved ease of play. The King of Tycoon has sensed a disturbance in the wind. When the crystals that balance the powers of the world are threatened, the king hastens to the rescue...only to go missing. Somewhere a young man and his Chocobo find themselves drawn toward friends that will change their destiny. Building on the job systems of previous games, FFV includes a diverse selection of jobs to try, and a unique ability system that lets you combine skills. Develop your characters with free reign, and master your battle tactics in the fifth installment of the FINAL FANTASY series! ---------------------------------------------------------------------- ■Beautifully revived with new graphics and sound! Universally updated 2D pixel graphics, including the iconic FINAL FANTASY character pixel designs created by Kazuko Shibuya, the original artist and current collaborator. Beautifully rearranged soundtrack in a faithful FINAL FANTASY style, overseen by original composer Nobuo Uematsu. ■Improved gameplay! Including modernized UI, auto-battle options, and more. Switch the soundtrack between the rearranged version, created for the pixel remaster, or the original version, capturing the sound of the original game. Now possible to switch between different fonts, including the default font and a pixel-based font based on the atmosphere of the original game. Additional boost features to expand gameplay options, including switching off random encounters and adjusting experience and ABP gained multipliers between 0 and 4. Dive into the world of the game with supplemental extras like the bestiary, illustration gallery, and music player. (This remaster is based on the original 'FINAL FANTASY V' game released in 1992. Features and/or content may differ from previously rereleased versions of the game.)

short_description: The original FINAL FANTASY V comes to life with completely new graphics and audio as a 2D pixel remaster! A remodeled take on the fifth game in the world-renowned FINAL FANTASY series! Enjoy the timeless story told through charming retro graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: I love FFV, so much that I speedrun the GBA version, participate yearly in the FFV Four Job Fiesta, and play romhacks of it. This remaster does a lot of things well. The soundtrack is great, and many things are faithful to the original. Visuals are great, translation is great. Some design decisions that are questionable were made, like the starting ATB not being predictable, and not pausing when your turn comes up (unless you go into a menu). The unpredictable ATB means many tactics no longer work in this version. Checkpoints have been added for game-overs which is a nice addition. The reason this gets a thumbs down is the massive amount of bugs, some game breaking. The most major is in the Ramuh forest near Istory, the game will sometimes stop reading inputs in battle unless it's an enemy's turn. This means that if you're in Wait mode and go into a menu, you softlock. Additionally there are some random crashes. Everything else points to an untested game released early. When equipping abilities that give Magic stats (like putting !Black on a different class), your Magic stat goes up, but your max MP does not, until you level up. In W2, Fork Tower isn't on the map, but is on the Bestiary map. Ghido's island is hidden in the minimap, until it is removed, then appears on the minimap. In W3 they added a custom tile for the Antlion valley, which shows as an error tile in the Bestiary map. Almagest isn't reduced by shell. Gold Hairpin sometimes doesn't work (but they're patching this soon?). If you !catch and then !control your caught enemy is glitched out. You also can't see the caught enemy in the menu. Chemist mixes sometimes don't stay on death - like Goliath Tonic sometimes stays, sometimes doesn't. Dragon Kiss, Lifeshield, etc don't stay on death, and don't protect you from White Hole. Bone Mail doesn't prevent Berserk with Blessed Kiss. The Reset spell doesn't reset the Wonder Rod. The Reset spell on Neo Exdeath causes the background to go to the Exdeath fight background, and causes you not to get the Exdeath Bestiary entry. Edit: the next is NOT a bug, recently played the SNES version and confirmed this is faithful to the original - Mastered Knight's Two-Handed doesn't work on a FreelancerThese are all bugs that I've personally encountered. There's sure to be many more. Edit: I have seen many more online, with all sorts of bizarre behavior.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice update on a classic game. FF5 has been long overdue a full soundtrack remake, and this attempt is no slouch, with bombastic arranges of similar calibre of the other Pixel Remasters. The various QoL features (minimap, full hidden route display when in one, 8 way movement, quicksave, autobattle, chest/item count) are welcome additions, and the new sprites are nice to look at.For port features, it is rather bare bones (Borderless FS, a single CRT-esque filter). While it has similar font issues as the rest of the FF Pixel Remasters, there are various mods that are easy enough to install that work for FF5PR with seemingly no issues (I recommend Patera Quetzal's FFSilver). The new art style may be hit or miss for some people, and the CRT filter included probably won't change any minds.However, this release seems to only be content scaled to the original Super Famicom release, not including any of the classes and features added with other releases, including the 2015 port. With the delisting of the 2015 port on Steam, this leaves PC players no legal avenue to play a version with these features, unlike FF3 and 4's 3D Remakes still being available for purchase. If you're looking for those features, your only options to  it is via Mobile, GBA rereleases, or old 2015 Steam keys on other sites.

_childDocuments_.review: I said some very unkind things about the iOS port of this game that's been available on Steam for years.  Try as I might, I couldn't get past the touchscreen UI and obnoxious character sprites in that version.  I am quite happy, however, with the pixel remaster.Very little, visually, has changed from the SNES version of the game.  The improved battle scene backgrounds from the GBA version are present, and small effects/changes to different parts of the game have, so far, been an additive quality rather than a distraction.  The subtle glow of red around a recently impacted meteorite and cracks in the earth alongside it; spell and weapon attack effects that feel like they could be from the 16-bit era despite being a marked improvement over the SNES originals.Character sprites are faithful to the original, which is saying something considering how many different battle sprites there are for the playable characters.  Certain story NPCs have also been given unique sprites to help differentiate them from regular NPCs populating towns/villages.  All in all, these are very nice changes that only improve the visual experience playing a game that, rightly, belongs firmly in yesteryear.UI changes are much improved, too, with a cleaner menu interface and a much handier after-battle report that showcases stat improvements on level up in addition to showcasing how much EXP and ABP you need to the next character/job level.  The configuration option that allows players to opt into a 'classic' view with CRT scan lines is very welcome for anyone like me who misses the fuzzy warmth found in standard def.  Since the sprites in this remaster don't differ all that much from the originals, the scan lines options really adds to the enjoyment.The music remaster is perhaps the best part of this entire release.  Even the sound effects are stepped up to a more modern quality that still feels very SNES-like.  It's been stated elsewhere, but the audio quality is what the game music sounds like in your head with 20+ years of nostalgia coloring your memory; truly incredible work.I heartily recommend this iteration of FF5.  If you can't or don't want to load up a ROM with either the DeJap fan translation patch, or the GBA version, then this is the version to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy V is my favourite in the series. This port is a buggy mess. Softlocking in combat has happened more then I can count, with the latest being the fight before getting the savepoint in the final dungeon, meaning a half hour progress and some rare steals just gone. It has an autosave feature, unless you have to close the game due to a softlock. I even had one during a climatic story moment in the second act that, if you know the game, you know which I mean. FF5 is fun. I really enjoy it. But freezing up in combat and in dungeons just sucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, alright, alright, sit tight everyone.  I never write reviews, but I had to write this one.Where do I start man?  My love for the Final Fantasy franchise is a bottomless pit.  With the introduction of the pixel remastered series, I've thoroughly enjoyed the releases.  Albeit, I've only beaten 3 and 4 as I wasn't interested enough to the play the first two.  Those two remasters were phenomenal, and I enjoyed my playthroughs.That being said, I was doing extremely well in FF5, and progress was great!  I've gotten to the point where both worlds merge and I decided to pick a fight with Bahamut.  Well, somewhere in this fight it generated a bug and it perma-confused my Lenna (No status indicated in battle that she is), and keeps her health at 0, but still active in battle.  She's also in a perma-berserk status, so I can not choose commands upon my will.  I've tried sleeping in the inns and restarting the game, but it does not resolve the issue.  If I had a prior save point I would load it all up there, but I do not.  I typically save 4 different slots and over them, but would not have expected a bug such as this.  It has made the game virtually unplayable at this point, so I have decided not to continue.After putting 22 hours into the game and have this come up, it's nothing short of disappointing to see happen.  I just don't want to invest the time to start all over again as I don't have a lot of it.  I have to ask if anyone else has had this issue, and I hope no one else is going through it.Overall, my love for the game is there.  It plays as your standard turned-base FF with all the nostalgic characters and lore.  Had it not been for this one bug, I would've had a great time.I'm so sad.

_childDocuments_.review: I played and platinumed all six Pixel Remasters, and wrote a review for each! Read them all for comparison and context, or skip to the one you came here for!This is the most barebones of the series, no pesky characters or plot to get in the way. Kill some enemies, level up, next town, new gear, next dungeon. It is also probably the second easiest. Not going to complain! Short, sweet and to the point. Just over 18 hours for all achievements. You start out with your four nameless, silent,  little pixelated heroes and choose a class for each of them. I chose warrior, “thief,” white mage, and black mage. I did some research and as far as I can tell “thief” is Japanese for what roughly translates to “broke-ass warrior.” I would recommend new players to opt for two full warriors as to have a party of 4 instead of the 3.5 that I ended up with. Sure, his defense, damage, HP, and set of equipable weapons were all worse than my warrior, but his agility was slightly above average, so I had that working for me!Level-ups come in the traditional way, classes are well defined, spells are bought at shops. Instead of having a global MP pool, each tier of spells has a limited number of casts (recharged by items or at an inn).Music was good, but nothing remarkable. Verdict: 3.5/5 “thieves” This is the weird one where you level-up a skill or weapon by using it repeatedly, Bethesda-style. There are no classes or jobs per-se but each character gets good at what they have been doing. It’s not my preferred way of doing business, but I didn’t mind too much. For their second entry in the series, they actually bothered to have some sort of plot! There seem to be people in the world who have lives, roles in society and care about stuff. You have your war, an evil empire, and a magical tornado, oh my! Your “characters” however are just pixelated bundles of stats who barely speak. That’s fine, just swing those hunks of metal and wood at the things I tell you to swing them at. Uh, Maria… your bow is pointing the wrong way. A pretty easy entry in the series, with a weird difficulty spike at the end, but even that wasn’t too bad. You can quick-save between fights. Buy your spells at town. Cast them with a global MP pool this time. Cost is based on how much you have leveled the spell. (Spells are are trash btw in this one, but a few enemies are highly resistant to physical.)Again, music was par for the course.Verdict: 3.5/5 evil empiresOur third entry here seems to be the birthplace of jobs. A job is like a class but a bit more focused and you can swap in out of them at any time. Your job levels up independently of your character level, but character level has much more barring on your effectiveness, so you are encouraged to bounce around jobs from time to time. This was definitely the easiest of the six games, and just barely the shortest, clocking in at about 18 hours for 100% achievements. Auto-battle, Hello. Much like the first, the story is bare-bones and player characters are just stat-sprites. Just bellybuttonless palette-swapped clones who occasionally grunt. The magic system is the same as the first game. It’s probably the weakest entry in the series, unless you're into the whole “brevity” thing… man.I caught some of the music, but to be honest I was listening to the Cyberpunk 2077 score for much of this game. A little weird, I know…  Moving on!  Verdict: 3/5 floating continentsOh sh*t, here we go! We have characters, they live, they love, they suffer, they grow. Romance, betrayal! Ok, sorry, let’s start over. The third entry takes a big leap forward in terms of characters and story, as in, it has them. You have your  main characters and then some guests that come and go. Jobs are gone, and the characters each have a set, permanent class. The classes are well defined with unique abilities and equipment sets. Spells, for those who can use them, are learned naturally through leveling. This is probably the second best game in the series. Challenge and length are moderate. The story, characters, and destinations are all well above average. Some extremely unforgiving RNG from the original has been toned down significantly for those of you interested in treasure-hunting all the treasures huntable. The music takes a big step up at this point in the series. The moon music is strange yet awesome. The “giant” music is epic and gorgeous. Could it be that this is just the nostalgia factor due to playing this game as a wonder-filled, wide-eyed child? Nope! Verdict: 4.5/5 spoony bardsJobs: checkAcceptably life-like characters: checkHigh concentrations of chocobo: checkVerdict: Not yet? Ok. This is the hardest game in the series, and second longest. We’ve jumped up to almost 57 hours for all achievements! *sigh* What am I doing with my life?  Annoying status effects abound in the later dungeons (where are those damned ribbons?), and optional superbosses make their first appearance! Think Ruby and Emerald in FF7. As mentioned above, jobs are back. And how. There’s a ton of them, and you’re going to master every bloody one if you want that final achievement. Yes, even the geomancer! Especially the geomancer!! One really great thing is that you can master certain abilities or passives unique to one job and then “equip” it on another job (one at a time only). Buy your spells at the local grocer. Standard MP pool is present. If you enjoy a grind and a challenge, this is the one for you. The music quality remains high, especially on a certain larger-than-normal bridge, and when fighting one not-so-mysterious swordsman.  \m/Verdict: 4/5 cartoonish, one-dimensional villains We made it. Here we are at what is definitely the crown jewel of the Pixel Remasters. Maybe even the best RPG of its era? I would still argue for Chrono Trigger, but elder millennials and gen-xers of good faith can disagree. Where to start? We have a massive cast of memorable characters (including the best villain of all time), romance, comedy, tragedy, and the best spectacle and story-telling in the series. The locations, the towns, dungeons, forests, and factories really come to life through excellent art direction and detail. And the music is stellar! “But this isn’t the end of the review...” Don’t care!Note: Some reviews mention a strange rainy town filled with thieves and liars. Never heard of it. Not in this game. My only gripe with VI is the class system. There really isn’t much of one. Every character has a unique ability, but equipment sets have huge overlap, and characters are frequently rotating in and out of the party. So you never feel like you have clear defined combat roles. Really, it’s nitpicking though. This is the longest of the games, though it ends up feeling appropriate. Difficulty is middling.Now, I know you're dying for me to tell you how magic works in VI. Well, dear reader, for that you will have to subject yourself to a fairly minor spoiler.  Well, that’s it! The music is amazing. The overworld theme, the blonde’s theme, the villains theme. And the town that doesn’t exist has terrible music!Verdict: 5/5 16-bit laughs, 5/5 opera-loving octopi, 5/5 B-day suits. I can’t decide!

_childDocuments_.review: Running a comparison today between this new Pixel Remaster, the old Steam version, and the original Super Famicom version, the clear winner in both video and audio was the new Pixel Remaster. I won't dive into gameplay, since this is just an early impression, and I will be playing this later. But things I noticed:1.) Characters are smaller now, to fall more in line with the original SF version. The old steam version the characters appear to be almost twice as tall, and this actually obscures some things, such as I noticed with the campfire in the beginning. 2.) Gone are the character portraits seen in the old steam version when there is text conversations happening. This was not in the original, and since the PR is based on the original SF version, it makes sense. Still, this is one thing I would have liked brought back from the newer versions. Not a big loss though. 3.) Animations are clearly better in the PR  for environmental effects. Character animations seem to be the same between SF and PR, but the world effects just have a much cleaner QOL look. Not sacrificing the old school pixel look, but just making it look better. This is one of the ways the old steam version kind of falls flat, as it seems mismatched in some areas. Things for example like the way the crystal explodes, or the meteor comes toward you, or the water effects and campfire, and other cool little things just look clearly better in the PR version overall. 4.) One thing I noticed, and hopefully this is not isolated, is that when you are in the forest at the beginning, the trees appear to have more depth in the PR. this is thanks to the better coloring and better use of shadows. It does not seem out of place, and matches perfectly.And as for the audio, while some may prefer the chiptune of the original SF version, I find the new arrangements to be really pleasant sounding and having more emotion. I'll finish up with an actual review later when I play this some more, to touch on things such as gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I came to FINAL FANTASY V (Pixel remaster) with some knowledge about the game, like gameplay mechanics and a bit of story from FF-FFIV. I have recently just completed the first 4 FF (pixel remastered) games and I loved every moment of those games. After completing each game I moved onto the next game with even more knowledge on how to play and what I am looking for on each game for items and such. When I came to FFV I knew it was going to be much more story based and I hoped for it to be a little bit more tuned. Was it? Yes it was!⚫Again, like all other FF games, the soundtrack was amazing. You get to listen to all the songs in the main menu and some of them are just so heartwarming.⚫The auto-battle option is a welcome addition to a game like this.⚫The UI is so good in this game. I had a look at the older UI that was used... yeah... this new, improved, modern UI is a much needed welcome for new players like me but I do understand why some people want the original SNES version as an option.⚫You can dive into the world of the game with supplemental extras like the bestiary, illustration gallery, and music player.⚫Final Fantasy V continues from FF4 mechanics such as "flow of time" during battle and the ability to target multiple enemies/Allies with black or white magic spells.⚫The amount of story based content and lore behind this game is unreal. How much effort they put into the characters and their backstories. Not just the characters... also a majority of the MAIN enemies such as - Shinryu. Gilgamesh. ExDeath. It is just phenomenal how much detail and backstory is behind these unforgettable characters.⚫There is an item you can get called "The World Map". This was a MAJOR "W" for FF5. It showed all available areas you could visit with a little grey dot (turns yellow when you visit). So, that means you could not miss out on an area playing the game. Fantastic!⚫From the start of the game the story had me hooked instantly. There was no silly side bits that would make you lost and the games story was AMAZING from start to finish.⚫This game has some of the most memorable villains, characters and fights I have seen to date. Whenever I hear someone talk about FF14 or in general about FF, somehow they mention a character, villain or such from FF5 I have noticed. Most of the time its Gilgamesh or Shinryu or even ExDeath. Occasionally its Bartz or Krile. Amazing that it has stuck for generations!⚫I want to mention this because it was a nice little addition. Outside of a town called "Istory" I found Ramuh in the forest. Now, I already had Ifrit at this point and while fighting him he had dialogue with Ifrit. Ifrit said "Lend us your strength" and Ramuh's reply was "We have never been enemies Ifrit". I found this a really cool interaction between Primals.⚫The job system in this game is just incredible. Each job comes with its own unique "Ability" if you would call it that. Now for example - Beastmaster has "control" and Blue mage has "Learn". Combine these two classes and you can help the blue mage learn Blue magic spells. The combinations are insane and how in depth the job system goes in FF5 is incredible.⚫Time limited dungeons. For "Castle Walse" early-ish in the story you have 10 minutes to go through this area or its "O V E R". Now, whats even more annoying is that there are chests, enemies for your beastiary and BLUE MAGE spells to learn. ALL in 10 minutes. This was an absolute nightmare for me as I wanted to collect everything.⚫You have the ability to "STEAL" from enemies. Now, You have a 40% chance to steal and item, or 80% if you have the Thieve's Gloves equipped. If you are successful you have a 123/128 chance to steal the "NORMAL, COMMON" steal item. Rare items have a 5/128 chance of being stolen - 4% on successful steal attempt. Not all enemies have normal and rare steals, some have only one or the other. Now, why have I mentioned this? Well - its pure luck. Its tedious and not needed. I had to power level a "TIME MAGE" to spam the "RETURN" ability to reset the battle until I got the "RARE STEAL". I am not pleased with this mechanic in the slightestAs a new player to the FF series, after completing FF1-4 and no knowledge of 5-13 this was an amazing journey for me and I loved every moment of it. I would recommend this game to anyone that likes turn-based games and the Final Fantasy series or to anyone like me, that's wanting to learn all these references and experience an amazing game series.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm now 5/6 of the Pixel Remasters completed and the more of them I finish, the deeper I fall in love with the full package.FF5's main feature is a vastly improved job system that corrects the gaps that were present in FF3. Exploring and mastering the different jobs is less tedious and the equipment distribution, considering all the options, is a marked improvement from 3 to 5. These improvements do a great job to encourage trying out different combinations throughout the game.It also features a relatively strong story that is more evenly paced compared to FF4 and does a good job of sprinkling comedic elements without detracting from the experience. It has a slightly lighter tone compared to FF4, but does not fall short in the storytelling department. I personally laughed and cried along with Bartz and co. while exploring the twists and turns this title had to offer. If I had to describe this title, I'd call it "Just gorgeous!".While this version does not have the extra content as the old version that's currently no longer being sold on Steam, this PR does balance it out by streamlining a lot of good features that are present across 1-6PR. I loved all 40h I sunk into this game, and it definitely ranks high among my FF completions!

_childDocuments_.review: Note: On a journey to 100% ALL Final Fantasy titles on Steam~To everyone telling me to skip FFI-FFV: In this game, you get to experience the most beautiful depiction of the job system yet, as well as a true Final Fantasy that is feature complete, with the top high's of the previous titles, blending together in a superb masterpiece that young me was not able to fully appreciate back in the day. It's such a nice blend of leveling and combining jobs with actual character levels, I loved planning my characters' evolution on this many layers!If you've played this game before, you don't need to read my review, go ahead and give it a go. This is a solid stable release!If you are thinking to give this game a first try, I think it is more than a worthy continuation of previous Final Fantasy titles, as well as a good starting point, where you get all the amazing features we've come to like and expect of this series, as well as a true retro experience!If you plan to 100% this game, I highly recommend the achievement guide posted by lylat on Steam! I have followed their guides for every single Final Fantasy game, and they never cease to amaze.I hope I was able to provide some unique perspective for you, and was able to help you decide whether you should play this game if you were on the fence!

_childDocuments_.review: The Final Fantasy Pixel Remasters are absolutely wonderful re-releases of the original final fantasy games, and 5 is no exception. If you are a true fan of the franchise, you will love this recolor/remaster of the game. This is by far, one of the best Final Fantasy titles, and one of my personal favorites! It has a Diverse class system with a lot of ways to play, an amazing score like always, Beautiful recoloring to make the game far more vibrant than ever before, more unique ways to play than usual, and is all around, one of the best in the franchise in many ways. Honestly, this is an amazing title for any fan of the Final Fantasy franchise. I Highly Recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: As  is the second  game that was originally released on the Super Famicom (back in 1992), I wondered just how much it’d match its predecessor. I especially hoped that the  were improved upon, as the games got longer and longer. However, as it turns out,  instead focusses on bringing back an old friend: a job system. of  I praised its vast job system, offering 22 (!) different jobs – although some were simple “upgrades” (e.g. White Mage -> Sage). After  tied jobs to its characters, not allowing changes, it’s surprising to see  doubling down on the idea of a vast job system: once again there are 23 jobs to choose from, without any simple “upgrade” jobs this time around.However, simply offering this huge amount of jobs isn’t enough for . The arguably most interesting aspect of the game would be the feature to mix different job abilities in order to create unique job combinations.Let me explain: In addition to the usual experience points gained after won battles, which increase character levels, you’re now gaining “Ability Points” (APB) as well. These increase the level of the job each character currently has equipped. Raising a job level unlock unique abilities (like being able to equip a certain weapon type or using infusing your blade with magic), which can be equipped even when changing to a different job. For example, levelling the Red Mage job to its maximum level unlocks the “Dual Cast” ability, allowing the character to cast spells twice in one turn. Switching to the Black Mage job and equipping this Red Mage ability thus means I can cast powerful black magic twice in one turn as well!Considering how many abilities these 23 classes offer, you’ll quickly be able to create unique job combinations – like a barehanded Black Mage fighting like a Monk or a Ninja with the Dragoon’s “Jump” ability for example. It’s a great system with more depth than I am able to convey here with this little space but also quite easy to understand & use.That said, while these great customization options are really fun to set up and experiment with, they’re also limited by two major issues: For one, you’re not told what abilities can be unlocked by levelling up a job beforehand, which means you have to use  in order to be able to properly plan your jobs. Second, levelling up jobs takes up quite a lot of time and grinding. A normal story playthrough, even considering optional content, is not enough to max out even the majority of your jobs without additional grinding. Of course, with proper planning, you’re still going to be fine – but it’s a shame that a lot of grinding is needed if you want to experience the full extent of the job system.One of the new classes  introduces is the Blue Mage, which offers to ability to learn specific abilities used by enemies by experiencing them (ouch!) in order to cast them yourself. In theory, this is a great idea but - just like the new job system - it’s an idea that’s not entirely thought through – because you’re not able to determine which enemy abilities can be learned and which not. As such, if you want to learn all available blue magic, I’d suggest using a guide.Apart from the new job system, little has changed regarding gameplay however.  features the usual mix of (mostly linear) dungeons, overworld and random encounters. I do feel like random encounters are a little bit too frequent though, especially in dungeons you can barely walk a few steps without entering yet another battle. This is especially annoying during exploration and I wish there was an option to turn random encounters off.  is also (once again) not great at always giving you an idea of where to head next, which is why I recommend using a  in order to know where to head next – and because quite a lot of bestiary entries, items and chests are missable otherwise (boo!).One last gameplay-related aspect of  I want to mention are its two superbosses.  was the first game in the franchise to feature these optional encounters which are even tougher than the final story boss of the game. I want to mention this specifically because the second (& actually hard one, as the first one can be continuously stunned by bards) is quite devilishly placed: The second superboss of  can be encountered as  – a bad surprise to those hoping to just snatch up an item and haven’t saved in quite a while. Apart from this unfortunate placement, my only complaint about these optional challenges would be the missing build-up – apart from a short note in the game about their origins, there’s no story regarding them.Speaking of story, after praising the good-albeit-flawed new job system I do have to be a bit more critical here. While  offers enhanced story presentation with characters beginning to have (few) animations outside of battle (e.g. big eyes when surprised, touching their head, etc.) and even flashbacks (!), the story told is cliched and drags on far too long. Characters are once again not receiving any character development and while the main villain is at least not thrown in like , there’s little beyond “they’re bad” here.Considering how  is the longest of the  games up until that point, I had hoped for more. Instead, especially the latter portions of the game overstayed their welcome and I just wanted to get to the end as fast as possible. For those who mostly play games for the story, like I do, be prepared for some frustrating moments of “why is this still going”.A fun fact I thought I’d mention here:  is the first game in the franchise to receive a sequel: An anime OVA called  continues the games’ story and released back in 1994 (in Japan, though it also came to North America in 1997/1998). However, I'm with  - the OVA isn't good and doen't improve the story of the original.Lastly, let me once again praise the faithfully upgraded graphics and music as well as the additional features (maps, auto-battle, etc.) added by this Pixel Remaster version. While I would recommend  only to those interested in the franchise or the job system, there’s no doubt that the Pixel Remaster version is probably one of the best ways to experience this game that’s .

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy V is a great game and is my favorite Final Fantasy game. However, this is not the ideal way to play the game in my opinion. If you've come in from playing the PS1, or Snes version, this game will be superior version to those ones. But I'd recommending finding ways to emulate the Gameboy Advance version (And VBA is notoriously easy compared to other emulation). This version of the game lacks postgame content that was introduced in that version. The lack of it, is extremely jarring as this is supposed to be the definitive edition. While I bought this version and played it for a bit, I feel the GBA version is overall just an upgrade as this doesn't do too much more special. Additions feel unnecessary, while some aspects, like the bestiary being inaccessible from in game and has to be accessed through the main menu, (When this game has plenty of drops or steals, you may want to grab the rare steal, but you won't know they have a rare steal until after you save and return to the menu. Against bosses this can be a pain to have to go around).  The awful IOS port that was originally on Steam even had the GBA additions. So delisting that one (while it was awful) is just a weird move if they didn't want to bring over the postgame. While normally, postgame isn't that important in most Final Fantasy games, this is the game where you are constantly improving the same four characters to the point you feel absolutely overpowered mastering the classes. If there was any Final Fantasy pixel game that needed it's post game, this would be it.So while a good game, I wouldn't recommend spending too much time on this version. Buy it so you have a clear conscious when you emulate the GBA port I suppose.

_childDocuments_.review: I think I audibly breathed a sigh of relief a few times while playing . Before playing and severely disliking the first and fifteenth entries last year, it had been some time since I had touched , and I was concerned that my appreciation of the series was entirely nostalgic. It was thus quite gratifying that  turned out to be pretty entertaining, confirming that the series just has a clear golden age with walls of trash on either side of it. It was especially surprising, because the centrepiece of the game is its job system, which always seemed a little quaint from the outside, given that it had been present in some form in games  and .The difference is that the system is massively expanded and refined here, and the game is structured with these changes in mind. Characters can equip a learned skill from a previous job on top of those granted by their current one, and there’s no penalty or restriction on job-switching, so players are encouraged to experiment. Simply coasting on an ideal setup at all times will reveal the game to be relatively easy, but its true engagement lies in trying a little bit of everything and making any eccentric combination work for you. It’s not a coincidence that this is where several now-iconic jobs with unorthodox and unpredictable play styles were introduced. Even if you do insist on playing it “traditionally,” there are a healthy number of gimmick battles sprinkled throughout the campaign to liven up the static menu-based combat.The easy-going approach to gameplay is matched by the tone of the story, which was arguably appropriate but understandably controversial. Both dramatic events and character development are present, but they happen at such a breakneck pace, and the villain is so uninspired, that it can feel a little silly at times. It can also come across as apathetic acceptance of technical limitations compared to  and , which largely transcended those same limitations. Speaking of which,  doesn’t benefit from the  treatment as much as the NES/Famicom titles. The visuals have been mildly improved, but the gameplay and soundtrack were already mostly functional and terrific, respectively, so little to no revision was needed there. Some small subjective issues remain (I wish every dungeon in the third act was 30% shorter, for example), but regardless,  is a solid diversion and a worthwhile entry in the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10Final Fantasy V was one of the games I did not expect to enjoy this much tbh, It has the least played of the pixel remasters, and it seems like nobody even talks about the game whenever talking about older ff games, especially since right after this game was Final Fantasy VI tbf. However, the class system, mechanics, and even characters were done really well to the point where I did all the extra content even though they were a bit grindy simply because I wanted to play more of the game before I finished it.Story/CharactersWhen I praised the game, there is one aspect that I cannot overlook... while the characters are pretty good, the story itself is just mediocre. It is your typical 4 crystals and evil bad guy at the end, and while the story is still very interesting in terms of how it is told and the bad guy's motivation, it is still the weakest part of the game by far, and I can barely remember any noteworthy story moments apart from the bridge fight cause of the music. The characters were however actually very interesting, as they went thru many development, deaths, and overcoming hardships. I loved their arcs, with the main complaint being that other characters that weren't the main cast, even Krile were just not that interesting or fleshed out. Even so, while I loved their character, near the end they kinda stop being developed, as their arc is solved around the 3rd act till the end credits when we see what happens to them.GameplayEASILY the best part of FF5, the class system is AMAZING. So much creativity as you are allowed to mix and match other classes, level them up and make basically your own team at the end. The game also has that classic old school balancing, so while the majority of the time, it had a pretty nice difficulty and apart from being pretty challenging from the previous games while also having really hard (albeit easily cheesable super bosses) bosses that had interesting mechanics, it also had those few mechanics that when you realize, really break the game in terms of balance, but in the fun way as you have to work for it before you get the power scaling to the point of whooping superbosses' asses. There were some downsides, as some classes were just straight up ass compared to other classes, also the dungeons were really fun, but this game's annoying mechanic were pits that made you fall down them and waste so much progress. I know that the Geomancer can avoid pits with his passive, but I never used him to those setbacks were really damn annoying.MusicThe music had its bangers in this game ngl. The Bridge fight especially, exdeath final boss theme, chocobo, the first time we see and hear the Moogle theme, and some other songs. However not as many songs that I LOVED compared to ff3 and the doga theme, or ff4 boss theme, but still pretty good overall, just not as memorable... but I did love that Lenna's theme and especially the desert pyramid theme were used in ff14 that was awesome to realize.Nitpicks/Last Positives-Some Enemy having insta kill moves were just damn annoying, but I didn't stumble across enemies that were game ruining annoying compared to previous entries-Wish Gilgamesh had a better ending, I know about his arc and I did like it, but he just straight up sacrifices himself and is never mentioned again, not even in the wiki it just ends LOL.- Lava tiles suck, but float fixes that-I did not like how bosses gave like no EXP or AP sometimes, didn't feel satisfying to beat a boss, then see 0 Exp and 0 AP-Loved Galuf's character, but his Daughter Krile kinda has wayyyy too little development by the time she is introduced, and his death's impact doesn't mean much gameplay wise cause Krile has 1 to 1 of his abilities anyways.- Chemist's Mixing is such an old school mechanic, so much fun to use as many times it was just really broken, and it was obvious it came during an era when the internet wasn't a thing and you were supposed to discover them alongside, but still really fun.-Kinda wish the super bosses were more interesting mechanically, they were just bosses that had like 50k hp and moves that dealt over 2k or even 8k hp, which were insta kills unless you had specific gear to counter, but all it comes down to is that unless you are high asf level, cheesing them is the best way to beat them instead of doing a long boss fight at the level stage you are in.ConclusionFF5 is the first time I can actually see myself replaying the older final fantasy games (from this point). While the story is meh, the class system was so much fun to explore and play with, that now thinking about it makes me giggle about how broken Ranger's rapid shot + Ninja's dual wield was, did SOOOO much damage it was crazy. I am still very excited to play FF6, but Final Fantasy V is a game that I do believe, is heavily overlooked whenever people look at past ff games.8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Pet abandoning simulator. Poor Boko and Hiryu.Gameplay-wise, this is my favorite classic Final Fantasy and it's a faithful remaster of the original, complete with beautiful renditions of (mostly) great music and a lot of quality of life features, such as a Bestiary that's shared across all save files. The job system is awesome and I really enjoy that mastering a job enhances the Mime and Freelancer for that character, and mixing classes is good fun. Freelancer with Swordmaster + Rapid Fire + Dual Wield is supreme!It's an interesting twist that leveling up your character only increases HP and MP, so you need to master jobs and get good equipment to actually get more powerful. I enjoyed playing so much that I really took my time (112 hours, though I left it running a lot) and leveled my party to level 70 even, and got 100% of the achievements.As so many others have said, this is one of the best job systems in Final Fantasy, yet too many people just play IV and VI. The Pixel Remasters really do the originals justice.The story is often goofy and silly, and overly lighthearted at times, but I still enjoyed it and it has plenty of meaningful, sincere, and heartfelt moments. The story feels like 1 part tragic or serious and 1 part comedic relief, complete with the fairly dumb (albeit lovable) male protagonist trope who's the Butz of many jokes. Compared to FFIV or VI, however, V's overall storytelling, dialogue, and plot is inferior.My main complaints is that the game can be very easy, too much of the dialogue is mediocre or bland, and that a lot of the names sound very basic or dumb. For example, Bartz might be the worst protagonist name from any FF (yet still an upgrade from his original name transliteration, Butz), and neither Galuf or Krile sound fitting or good either; Tycoon Castle/King Tycoon is weird and unoriginal; the list goes on. Far too many names felt like random letters were slapped together by a 5-year-old.All in all, none of the negatives are particularly bad to me. This is a worthy addition to a wonderful series, and absolutely worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy V is another great addition to the series.The job system is back. Weird that we see it in FFI (but it's permanent), we lose it in FFII, we get it back in FFIII where it takes center stage, we lose it again for FFIV, and now it's back for FFV. Though it's worth mentioning that the job system is so much better now. Mastering skills in one job allows you to use those skills as a secondary ability when you choose another job. In effect, each job can be built many different ways. You will likely find yourself switching jobs and abilities around frequently in mid to late game. It's a great bit of added strategy, but it can make things tedious since you may find yourself needing to completely overhaul your party's 1) jobs, 2) abilities, and 3) equipment for a particular battle.The characters are good, but it's not quite up to the standard of FFIV. They're still memorable and fun, though. Galuf in particular adds so much to the humor of the party... and there is a good bit of humor. It tends to be more lighthearted than FFIV. Which game you will enjoy more will be up to your personal tastes. Not that it isn't without its sad moments as well.Some battles are effectively cheesed with certain strategies. Some battles will be nearly impossible without certain strategies. You will find yourself needing to work on your party composition and strategy more than your party's levels to overcome certain challenges. Other battles are simply not fun. For example, the zombie status effect cannot be cured by esuna. What's worse is that a zombified party member's attack will count as their action, meaning any strategy relying on mimic may cause your healthy party members attacking other healthy party members because they saw a zombie do it. Auto-battle is not your friend here. You will want to keep lots of holy water on hand to avoid frustration.It's also worth mentioning that the Steam achievement counters for this game were not implemented correctly. If you're following a guide to avoid missing content (you will need to use a guide to avoid missing content for most of these games) then keep in mind that you can't rely on matching up your achievement counter with the guide since some chests are not actually counted by the game, and other things are counted as a chest when they are... not really a chest.Overall I recommend this game even though it's not without its issues.

_childDocuments_.review: ***Coming back to edit this with a big old preface. The PR version of FFV has some very bad bugs, and not the fun kind. I recommend this game, but you'd probably be better served playing the SNES or GBA version at least until they roll out a patch***My all time favourite game and possibly the best FF game available.I've played this countless times on GBA and SNES.Insane amounts of replayability, stemming from being able to build a party with whatever you want and have it be viable (see quad white mage or quad zerker runs) mix and match job abilities for utterly busted combinations (like spellblade, dual wield, rapid fire) with bosses that can be as easy or as hard as you want by abusing vulnerabilities or AI script.The story is whatever, but the gameplay itself is quick to ramp up and very much on point. Once you unlock a job, it's ready to be used immediately, and the game doesn't make it hard to find spots to grind out gold, exp or job levels, and there are spots in game that make it easy to do one, the other or all of them if you know where to look.There's tons of side content, hidden content and gear available to you much earlier than you'd expect if you know where to look or what to steal.In addition to all of this, there is a great community behind the game, specifically with the yearly charity event Four Job Fiesta, which challenges you to run through this game under various restrictions.Help a good cause, run a cool game, have fun, find out you really like a job you weren't sure about, and learn how to break one of the best RPGs out.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm tempted to call this  definitive version of the game.TLDR; If casual, get this version of the game over any other version. If doing a lot of Four Job Fiestas, maybe stick to an emulated version so you can fast-forward through cutscenes and grinding sessions.Pros: Updated/Re-recorded OSTFast-forward mode (still not as good as going 20x speed on an emulator, though)Mini-maps all over the place + big map screen that tells you how many items you can get in any areaMenu screen and victory screen tell you how many points you need to level your character/jobDiagonal movementBestiary from the PS1 without the PS1's loading times.Updated graphics (water looks kind of out of place in some areas, though)Bubble pops over your head when you can interact with a thing (à la FFIX)General QOL improvements (no more need to hunt for a single tiny square when you want to land you airship on the catapult! Close enough is good enough! Secret passages light up entirely once you enter them!)Cons:Most cons are minor thingsThe biggest con is that you're not longer told, when gaining an item in the victory screen, how many instances of that item you already have.Cannot change the color of the panes, so you're stuck with blue (I usually have a different color for all my FJF runs)The shortcut mode for commands (from the GBA version) is gone :(Edit: The more you play, the more bugs you'll notice, especially if you have another version to compare too. Boss mechanics sometimes don't work as intended, virtual levels are lost and unrecoverable (we're talking dragon power levels, here), !mix as a whole is now considered magic (probably more of a design choice than a bug), if activating an ability/item while it is also being used by another character, the cursor disappears and won't actually use your ability/item, you may lose items without using them 'cause the fight ended between you issuing the command and the character using the item, a lot of small things that end up adding up to a lot, but I would still recommend this version ONLY for a casual playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: As per usual with the early FF titles, you control four Warriors of Light. Bartz, a traveling adventurer; Lenna, heir to the throne of Tycoon; Faris, the pirate captain; and Galuf, an amnesiac warrior. Though this party dynamic drastically shifts throughout the story, the four warriors come together to combat the crisis of the elemental crystals shattering and therefore causing chaos across the world and eventually revealing the greater threat behind these occurences.FFV is also noticeably the first Final Fantasy that I would view as being a bit derivative of an earlier title, as many themes of it are being shared with FFIII—not merely the gameplay elements of its job system. This is generally a nice touch and feels like an instance of internal development within early FF titles.While FFV can certainly stand shoulder-to-shoulder with other contemporary Final Fantasy in terms of the broad quality of its story, it is a lot more comedic in nature, which is to say that it also handles this comedy quite well by being muted enough to not take away from serious moments. More so, the party dynamics lead to a lot of chemistry between the characters, which is genuinely a joy to watch even as the stakes are raised higher and higher. Regrettably, FFV’s villain is a bit weak; while he shares a similar setup to FFIII and IV’s villains, respectively—as more of an incarnation of the void and of hatred and all such nice JRPG things, he is also a lot more talkative than both of them, which comes to his detriment due to his dialogue just coming across as very juvenile. At the same time, Exdeath enjoys a lot of screentime, which some other FF villains have lacked, which does give him a much better presence in the story, even if it is at the cost of him sometimes feeling a little bit like a Team Rocket kind of character, merely showing up for a few moments to laugh maniacally and then leaving until the next episode.Overall, FFV is broadly average when it comes to its story; the main plot being a bit on the weaker side, but the player party’s writing more than making up for it while also managing a rather difficult tightrope walk with its tone; managing to keep it entertaining and lighthearted while still delivering on the kind of JRPG story the older FF titles are known for.FFV is one of the most fun entries to play when it comes to turn-based gameplay. While regrettably it did not carry over the fifth party member slot of FFIV, it refined III’s job system to almost perfection. That is to say, any of the four Warriors of Light can take on any of twenty-two jobs that unlock as the game progresses and switch between them on a whim. More gimmicky jobs, like the Blue Mage, who learns spells as they are seeing them cast by enemies, are also unlocked very early on and therefore allow for a lot of flexibility past the usual Warrior/White Mage/Thief/Black Mage setups. It is, however, also a bit regrettable that some jobs didn’t make the cut to appear in this version of FFV.Level-ups aren’t very impactful, as they merely marginally raise basic attribute values. Instead, players gain the majority of their power via leveling the different jobs, which now not merely increase their combat potency but also eventually unlock further active and passive abilities that can then also be slotted onto other jobs to create powerful synergies.Naturally, the ATB gauge as the determiner of turn-order remains for FFV and can further be augmented by the gear players equip to their characters. FFV altogether is still at the top of turn-based gameplay in the series and can easily compete with later titles like FFIX and X just due to the sheer freedom in party building it offers while maintaining a consistently solid level of challenge.While FFV keeps all the same amazing changes of the Pixel Remasters, such as vastly updated sprites and spell effects, as well as a much appreciated gallery with official artwork to browse, I still find it a little disappointing that SE has not done a little more to harmonize this version of FFV with its predecessors, such as by featuring the amazing Yoshitaka Amano portraits.Regardless of the missing portraits, FFV also features a bit of an odd, consistent mismatch between the official character artwork and the character sprites. This is, however, a very minor complaint.Music is, however, fantastic as per usual. With extremely iconic tracks like  originating from FFV, as well as excelling at thematic, environmental tracks like Faris’ excellent theme .I had very few issues with FFV, just as with any of the other Pixel Remaster titles. FFV did, however, softlock twice on me due to what I believe is a bit of a bugged main menu screen, which twice during my playtime became simply unresponsive and forced me to reopen the game altogether. One more miscellaneous annoyance is that the game appears to be slightly stuttering when moving vertically on the overworld. This is not actually the case, but rather a side effect of how the overworld moves alongside your screen.I really enjoyed FFV as a bit of a reinterpretation of III. It doesn’t feel wholly unique in its take on FF’s early stories, but rather an attempt at refinement, which I can definitely appreciate. Of the early FF titles, it is also the game I straight-up had the most fun with when it came to its boss design and gameplay elements, with its biggest downside really just being whether people can stomach the lighter story in favor of more reactive character writing.

_childDocuments_.review: +1 Positive review for Pixel Remasters yet again - a bit buggy but I'd much prefer a few mistakes here and there (which they've quickly rectified! the end credits bug mentioned in other reviews has since been fixed) and a slew of balance and QoL changes over lazy mobile ports that look like utter trash. _childDocuments_.review: I've been playing all the Final Fantasy games for the first time recently, and I've fallen in love with FFV in particular.While I *liked* the previous four games, FFV did everything right for me. The job system is fantastic, the world is fun to explore, it's just a great game.The story is great, and in my opinion doesn't get enough credit. Yeah, it's goofier than other FF games - but that's part of WHY it was so good! We get to see these knuckleheads pal around and just hang on, and that makes them feel like an actual group of friends - so that when the heavy emotional stuff DOES happen, we're already invested and we care about them. So to me, FFV has the *strongest* Final Fantasy story so far.The characters themselves are great too. My favorite is Galuf, just an all-around awesome dude.If you're on the fence about FFV, I say give it a shot. I had so much fun with this one, and spent over 30 hours on it. _childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, but it does have a lot of flaws. That said, let's start with the positives. The game looks and sounds great. It also has a pretty charming story, although there's not much to it. The job system is also very cool, even though I didn't use it to its fullest potential. There's a lot you can do with the various classes. That's my problem with this game though: It has so much potential, but doesn't go anywhere with it. The story is laughably thin. You'd think the story would be more substantial, considering it's a SNES Final Fantasy game, but it's barely there. This is especially disappointing, coming from FFIV. Heck, the main villain is called Exdeath. It's so ridiculously stupid. When I first started the game, I was loving it, with pirate ships, adventure and whatnot. I was excited to see the story evolve, but it's a typical, bland cartoony story.Then there's the pacing. It takes a dive in the second half. The game starts to feel bloated and keeps going on and on after a while, making you wonder when it's going to stop. Not only that, but the game is filled with gimmick bosses. A lot of the time, I was overleveled with good gear, but I still couldn't beat certain bosses. Ahh, but there's a trick to this boss. He attacks you every time you use physical attacks, or he can only be damaged by magic and so on. Felt like so many of the bosses didn't take any skill, you just had to know the right gimmick to take them down. This is pretty disappointing when Final Fantasy bosses have always been great in the sense that you feel like the whole team is coming together with good equipment, taking down bosses, giving you a satisfying feeling, but instead, you just have to find out the gimmick. A lot of bosses were annoying like that.All in all, not a bad game, but certainly one of the weaker Final Fantasy games. Get it during a sale if you want to try out the cool job system, just don't expect a deep story like in IV or VI.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so it took me quite a bit, but here we are, my review for Final Fantasy V PR. We have quite a bit to unpack, so let's sit down and discuss the elements:Magic crystals that power the natural world with their elements begin to crack and shatter for mysterious reasons. In this adventure you'll join a world-travelling wanderer, a princess, a pirate captain and an amnesiac old man, on their quest to save the crystals and save the world in a light-hearted, colorful adventure. Come see for yourself what keeps players engaged!The translation of the game is based in the GBA version, with some adjustments here and there, so that's a plus in my part.The graphics look pretty much vintage and similar to SFC FFV. It brings a feeling of familiarity, unlike the previous FFV version of PC. It has some fancy new effects and stuff, but nothing too spectacular. It meets the purpose of replicating the vintage look of the original, which for me, it's enough in my eyes.Oh, yes, the meat and potatoes of the game, the gameplay. Final Fantasy V brings back the Active Time Battle bar, which determines the order in battle. Unlike the original SFC version and the GBA version, the ATB works like in Final Fantasy VI and latter entries, where the bar starts at 0, and the agility and weight determines how fast the bar will fill, which makes some skills more versatile than in the original, like Haste. The battle system, otherwise, is mostly similar to the previous entry, in which you insert your commands to use, either to attack your enemies, defend, or serve as support.As we mentioned in the story department, this game brings back the Job Class System from Final Fantasy III, but more refined. Each class has its own set of abilities (in battle or outside battle), strengths and weaknesses. Let's take for example the six job classes you get at first:- Knight: A strong physical-based class, with high-enough stamina, albeit rather slow. They have skills that can help to cover your party members from physical attacks, or guard physical attacks for a turn.- Thief: The fragile speedster class. They can steal from enemies and attack swiftly with knives. They're rather weak physically (both in strength and stamina) to compensate. In the overworld, they have the ability to find secret passages, and adding more running speed to the character.- Monk: The brawler of the group. They're really strong and they have the highest stamina of the job classes in the game. They have abilities to attack all enemies, focus for a stronger attack, or to defend. They have a low defense due to a lack of good equipment draw, though.- White Mage / Black Mage: Squishy Wizards. The former being pure support with its healing magic, while the latter serves as an offensive magic class. They're kind of slow, and rather squishy physically, but their magical prowess compensate those traits.- Blue Mage: This job class is rather unique. By itself, it doesn't seem too spectacular, but... don't underestimate the power of the Blue Mage. They can learn skills from getting attacked by some special attacks from enemies, which doesn't seem too crazy, until you realize that they learn some rather nasty spells and some amazing support spells, so they become one of the most versatile job classes in the entire game, carrying both offensive and support treats.Unlike in the original FFIII (Famicom version), and like FFIII PR, you can freely switch your job classes to your own liking, and make your own combinations to suit your strategies. Some of the characters have some better stats than others at certain ones, but the differences are rather minimal, so you can make party compositions the way you want to, and the more you progress into the game, you get more and more job classes to play and experiment with. Give it a try! It's quite the robust system, all things considered.And of course, let's not forget that this version of the game brings the usual QoL features from the previous PR games: A map to check on treasures, a permanent quick save and an auto save on each floor of a dungeon, auto-battle that repeats the last action made by your characters in battle, between others.Just a fair warning: At the time of this review, there's some glaring bugs that are going to hopefully be solved in a future patch. I'll update the review when this happens:- Multi-hit attacks that can do more than 3 hits can break enemy and boss scripts.- Enemy attacks that can cause status ailments, if you use Guard or Golem, they will nullify the attack, but you'll still get afflicted by the status effects. But otherwise, it's quite an enjoyable experience in the gameplay department. There's things changed here and there about some mechanics, some balance changes, between other things, but it's a minor thing in the grand scheme of things.As per usual, the arrangements on FFV PR are quite top notch. Some melodies ganed some new flair that the originals didn't have (Sorrows of Parting gained a wailing choir in the second half of the song), some got interesting changes (like Battle on the Big Bridge got some whimsical trumpets in the last third of the song, which represents the goofy nature of the opponent which represents this melody, not really all that bothered by this change, honestly, as the rest of the song is pretty top-notch, or Harvest ganing some flair from a festive song with the bagpipes and a whistle right at the end, to represent somehow the end of a dance), some more or less stayed the same (The Evil Lord REDACTED still sounds as menacing as ever, same with The Final Battle, Dear Friends, between others), and some songs reached a high pinnacle on their arrangements (The Dawn Warriors is a stand-out arrangement for me, Prelude to the Void gained a better sense of emptyness, which makes it more eerie, and the Ending Theme being more amazing than the usual flair). All in all, a superb soundtrack arrangement, with melodies for each moment.Do I recommend this game? If you haven't played another version of the game before, I will recommend it. If you had the previous version of the game from Steam before it got delisted, or if you already have another version of the game, I'd say, stick with those versions, but for what it is, I'd say that the Pixel Remaster version is still a recommended version for me. I got a lot of enjoyment from this one, and even if the grinding to complete all the job classes was a chore, I don't regret doing this a single bit.
