_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy VI has been one of my favorite games of all time, since my stepbro and I first played it on my SNES years ago. I'm now six hours into this version, and here are my thoughts so far.Pros:The game looks AMAZING! The updated graphics really shine and pop. Backgrounds are more detailed, sprites looks much better, and the entire game gleams with a new coat of polish. The music is spectacular. It hasn't been "remastered" it's been remade, with actual instruments instead of midi files being played by a sound chip. There are unfortunately two exceptions to this, that I will get into below. The game plays like you'd expect. No gimmicks, no tricks, no changes. It's just Final Fantasy VI as it was meant to be played. All the slowdown and other issues from the PS port have been fixed, so the game runs smoothly at 60fps with nary a stutter.Kefka's awesome laugh is firmly in place.ALL glitches have been fixed. This is a pro and a con, and I'll explain more below. Cons:The cons are all minor things, which can be easily ignored for the most part.Combat has fake difficulty now. My characters miss more often, and the enemies get more turns (No, I didn't change the battle speed.) and when they use multiple back to back turns, they like to use higher level attacks one after the other. I've nearly had a party wipe a few times because of it. This is a minor annoyance, and not a deal breaker.Two of the game's songs are completely wrecked. The Chocobo riding theme sounds godawful, no other way to put it, and the voice actress hired to voice Celes' lines during the opera needs singing lessons. She has a nice voice, but she doesn't know how to use it properly. The game has no graphics options, so I can't do anything about the constant horizontal screen tear that is always present, nor can I switch the background to the easier to read gray background. You're stuck with the default blue - sorry demon chocobo fans. The text is not right for this game, but it's still perfectly readable - at least on my huge screen. People with smaller screens might have issues. They used the GBA translation for some reason. It's still a good translation, but some of Woosley's lines are iconic and should have been left in.  For example, Kefka now says "Son of a sandworm!" instead of "Son of a submariner!"As mentioned above, all exploits have been patched, so I'm going to have to deal with Wrexsoul the old fashioned way. This is a total nitpick, but with all Nintendo censorship removed (Cafes are back to being pubs, characters in said pubs are drunk.) they decided to not show Celes' beating, which the original game left in. I'm confused about that one.Conclusion:If you have a copy of the SNES original and a working SNES to play it on, do so. After that, however, this is the best port of the game available. Looks good, sounds amazing (with the aforementioned exceptions) and plays great. If you're looking to experience Final Fantasy VI for the first time, and you can't get a SNES copy, than I highly recommend this version.

_childDocuments_.review: Better than Final Finatasy VII... someone has to say it :3seriously - nostalgia (my age group) aside. _childDocuments_.review: This game was a treat to replay! :DFinal Fantasy VI (FF III depending on where/when you first played it) was a game I was worried about revisiting for the longest time. This was mainly due to it's age, as well as the various ports and remakes that already existed not having that same charm as they did back on the SNES (imo).However, I can thankfully say that the Pixel Remaster of the game has really pulled it out of the bag and has put a very subtle, but needed coat of paint over the game while also adding a few QoL features which it didn't originally have.Visually the game is amazing! All of the delicate spritework created/remade for the Pixel Remaster has honestly done wonders for helping set an appropriate tone for the story elements as well as for the gameplay itself. This combined with the strong plot and the fun and quirky characters you're presented with, it's a win win! From a gameplay standpoint, it's very old school Final Fantasy, but that still translates well if you're ok with working with a turn-based battle system. The inclusion of quicksave features also help if you need to leave suddenly or you want a more pin point place to reload your saves.If you're looking to try the game for the first time, I can assure you that the game will ease you into things easily and you won't be expected to know a million things about Final Fantasy going into it either.  With that being said, if you're a returning Final Fantasy fan who wants to try this one for the first time, then there will be a lot of little easter eggs in there for you too :) Rating: 8/10 (Great)Game MVP: Mog the Moogle

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy VI will forever be my personal favorite. But overall, it's now the best version of the game that's been released. It still looks the way you remember, but has beautiful updated animations for every spell, item, and action that can be taken. While it doesn't have the additional features offered in the advanced version, they aren't needed. The game was awesome well before the advanced release. While this version does provide a great reason to replay it all over again, I still hope to eventually get a remake like FFVII got! Sometime before I die from old age would great Square Enix!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR This game is a must buy if you are a JRPG fan. Quite a few improvements, and some minor nitpicks to consider.For perspective, I've previously played the SNES and the GBA versions of this game, and I loved both versions despite their limitations.This game feels truly successful in keeping with the spirit of the original version closer to how I remembered it.I really enjoyed it. Most changes are for the better, especially the revamped music, it's just even more awesome. The visual effects (especially battle animations) have received a very welcome update that keeps the retro aesthetic. The more vibrant color palette may not be liked by everyone, though. Personally, I don't mind it. The 2D-HD additions to the Opera Scene are nice as well, I would've loved some other scenes with this style. The gameplay is also slightly altered. Cyan's bushido techniques are now charged in the background while you select commands for your other party members, while Sabin's combos for his techs are now shown basically as very forgiving QTEs. This was quite helpful since I have terrible memory when it comes to fatalities and such in general. Bugs such as the vanish-doom glitch have been corrected, and there's also an auto-battle function as well.Now about the bad stuff... There are a few things. The font does not match the game at all, that's the worst aspect, but fortunately you can mod it. The rest are actually nitpicks for me. As of version 1.0.5, the bestiary can only be accessed from the extras menu, this means you can't access it during normal gameplay (unlike the GBA version), you must save and exit to the main screen, access the bestiary, then go back and load your save. Really cumbersome if you're trying to complete the bestiary (which I didn't care about fortunately). Another issue is that every time a party character is presented, you'll be prompted to choose a name for them, just like in the original version. However, you can only do so with a keyboard, even if you're playing with a compatible controller.  This was annoying as I like playing on my bigass TV sitting on the couch, and I had to keep reaching for my laptop from time to time. A nitpick just because this was only occasionally.Now for the more subjective stuff, the bonus dungeons from the GBA version are not included. Personally I loved those so this was a bummer for me. But maybe, as many other people, you hated those, and their omission is a plus. Some people say they found the bosses way more difficult in this version. I didn't find that to be case but I did grind a lot so that may explain it. I would've loved a new game+ or a very hard mode to keep me coming back. Still, I enjoyed my time with this game quite a lot. It was really nice to experience this story all over again with improved graphics and music. Now I'm just crossing my fingers for this game to be ported over to the switch.This remaster is a 9.5/10 for me, but the game itself is still a 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently it's a good game and i'm not time travelling back to release to praise it since i'm playing it 30 years later.  The music and story is good.  I personally care about gameplay which is mediocre for the following reasons.  Before you get to customize your characters via espers the gameplay loop is grueling: random, uninteresting frequent encounters combined with often-obscure 2D static backgrounds made me want to quit.  Some points in the game are confusing and can give you the run around which destroys immersion and motivation (i.e. finding Terra in World of Ruin in an obscure place, Zozo contains a puzzle with clues given by people who are known liars).  Remembering which town is which for purposes of story or shopping is annoying since most towns look the same.  This game has no post-game.  The final dungeon contains the hardest content, there are optional areas for various characters that aren't as difficult.  What happens is you can just grind and curbstop every enemy in the game with nothing to truly challenge you. I will say the customization system with accessories and espers is pretty good but there's no payoff.  Finally the espers themselves seemed very weak (except for one broken one) which was lame.  Crystal Project is better.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the new best way to play FF6 after the original, completely replacing that iOS aberration we no longer talk about.There's good and bad here.- The UI is in line with the rest of the pixel remasters, lacking any of the original's customizations and just being generally awful to look at. The fonts are inconsistent, which is weird since the damage numbers are clearly in the correct one, and there MUST have been a better way to do the name bubbles, like... wow. The auto-battle icon is really invasive, as well as the unneeded auto-map that can't be permanently turned off.- The new opera was meh. The 3D looked fine, but kind of jarring since the rest of the game isn't, and the new vocalized songs didn't have proper lyrics. They were just prose sentences put to a tune. Kind of strange to go to the lengths they did to update them, and then halfass the most essential step. It's not a dumpster fire, but it's pretty amateur imo.- Glitches were everywhere. Weird turn-orders, unexpected softlocks. The memory cursor often didn't scroll to where it was last, leaving it off-screen, but on the proper spell. I could semi-reliably CTD just by looking at the bestiary, which is annoying since that's such a big part of the achievement hunt. The bestiary map also has a few monsters listed on inaccurate land masses where they don't appear.- Shadow's Interceptor counters aren't a thing anymore. I don't know if it's a glitch or intended, but they just can't be triggered. They gone.- There's no controller method for entering character names. You need to swap to keyboard, even if you're using controller for absolutely everything else. This needs addressing asap if you ask me.+ The music is ridiculously good, comparable in quality to the originals, but different. The new Narshe theme was my favourite of the bunch, but there were no misses.+ The way Cyan's Sword Techs work is MUCH better now. You pick them from a list, and then go do other things while they charge, which is also much shorter than it used to be. Tempest (Quadra Slice) is now a genuine force to be reckoned with.+ The graphics look excellent outside of the UI, and finally bring a decent version of the game into 16:9 (not to mention PC). The overworld looked a bit radioactive compared to the original, but it didn't bother me as much as I expected.+ Vanish/Doom/X-Zone can no longer be used to cheese your way through the game. Even Intangir is immune to doom, bringing his difficulty back up to intended.+ The difficulty seems buffed in general, though I'm not sure if I'm imagining it. I could swear a few fights, like Magimaster, were much more balls-to-the-wall than they used to be, but maybe that's just because I did them at a reasonable level this time.+ You can buy Shadow's elemental throw items now.So yeah, that was a scattered list of things I liked or didn't. I'm probably missing a lot of things I wanted to comment on while I played, but yeah. Overall the game is pretty worth the time and price if you're not about the SNES + CRT life.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: What can be said? It's an amazing remaster of an amazing game.  The translation is better than the SNES original, it retains its SNES look while working in a few visual upgrades like water animations smoke etc. Character models look almost exactly the same aside from a few like Kefka and Leo, and the OST sounds great.Other Quality of life improvements are things like Sabin's Blitz having the imput onscreen to help prevent incorrect imputs, Cyans Swordtech charges after making a selection enabling other members to act while they charge, all in all great choices. If you were a fan of FF3(or6) or if you just like JRPG's and havent played this one yet BUY IT! Definantly one of the best titles in the franchise.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: Good for what it is. Final Fantasy VI has always had a lot of hype. It's a decent RPG, but nowhere near the best. It's not even the best Final Fantasy. That title belongs to FF9. And even the best Final Fantasy is still not as good as the worst Dragon Quest. This remaster is good. It's worth a purchase if you like FF6. I got bored after a few hours of play, as I usually do with this game. I bought it because I'm a collector and I like the new music. I had this game for the SNES back when it was called FF3 and it was okay. This version (imo) is a little better. Just don't listen to the fanboys. This is not the best RPG ever. Not even close.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games in the series. It is superior to every previous game in terms of presentation and storytelling. It tells a compelling story from the standpoint of multiple characters. Gameplay-wise it's really good althrough I still prefer the customization from FF5. Job system is gone, each character has their own unique set of skills and you can assign everyone an Esper which makes them learn new spells and increase certain stats on level up. There is still potential for character builds however it kinda makes every character a mage and it isn't as deep as the previous game. Music is (as usual) a bliss to listen to, remastered tracks are great.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: There will be spoilers in this review. I finally got around to playing Final Fantasy VI, widely regarded as one of the greatest RPGs of all time. So what did I think? Well, it's mostly positive, but I definitely don't hold it to as high regard as some other people. Positives first. I loved the visuals and the music. Nobuo Uematsu once again shows why he's the GOAT. The story is great for the most part too, but I did find some flaws. The first half was excellent. I honestly had a great time, then Kefka destroys the world. While definitely an insanely epic moment, I thought it was only going to get better, but then the pacing of the game slows down to a crawl and now you have to explore the whole world on your own with very little indication on where to go. I never use guides for games. It's extremely rare, and I usually only use one to get unstuck from certain parts, but I'm not kidding you when I say I had to use a guide for the last 50% of the game. I had no idea where to go at all. Apparently, half of the game is just looking for your partners. I did not find that terribly exciting, although the stories definitely are good. I was just lost most of the time. I also mostly just used my favourite characters in combat, which became a problem later on. More about that later.The combat is very fun, although I think there's a bit too many characters to *really* get into any of them. I only felt like a mastered a few of them, while many of them hardly got used at all, which was a mistake, because you need them all at the end. Or, well, at least 12 of them. And because I had only used my favourites, I had to go level up for a while. How long? 15 minutes? 30 minutes? No, I leveled up for several hours. It took forever, even with boosters on. I can't imagine how long it must've taken on the SNES to get all the characters up to an acceptable level. It's not like I'm bad at RPGs either. I just beat Final Fantasy 1-5 before this, and those didn't require much grinding at all. Well, except FFII. Ugh.The game also had some annoying parts. First of all, the raft section. Just standing on a raft, choosing left, right or middle while fighting enemies over and over again wasn't very fun to me. Also, later, you fight waves of enemies on an airship, then two bosses, and if you fail at one of the bosses, it's everything over again, and that section takes a while too. I felt like some sections could've been designed better, but there are very few annoying parts at least.Then there's Kefka. Such an entertaining villain, but I'm disappointed he wasn't more in the game. He shows up a lot during the first half, but you don't see him for pretty much the entire second half of the game, except for a few minutes at the end. I found that extremely disappointing, but he's still a fun villain. I also found Kefka's Tower a bit annoying, spamming bosses left and right, plus a bunch of annoying enemy types. Not exactly the way I wanted the game to end, but the last fight was epic as hell at least. Definitely had a blast with that. This is actually one of the few times I think people are slightly blinded by nostalgia. I go back to old games all the time and have a ton of fun, and I did have fun with FFVI. Just not one of the greatest games of all time kind of fun. For instance, when I went back and played Chrono Trigger and EarthBound, old RPGs like that, I fell in love and they became some of my favourite games. Their age didn't matter at all. With FFVI, I'm noticing some cracks here and there. For me, Final Fantasy IX is still my favourite, but I'm still very happy to finally have played FFVI. A great game for sure. Score: 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, folks, buckle up for the ride of your nostalgia with Square Enix's latest stunt – the Pixel Remasters of Final Fantasy I through VI. And oh boy, Final Fantasy VI is like the cherry on top of this pixelated sundae. They didn't just slap on some HD makeup; they went full Broadway! The opera scene? It's not just beeps and boops anymore – we've got actual singing! And not just any singing, but multilingual crooning that'll serenade you in your own language. Talk about personalized entertainment!Now, for the gameplay. It's like the good old days but without those quirky bugs that let you wear a drill as a fashion statement on your head. Yeah, sorry hardcore fans, no more DIY headgear for an unfair edge. And for the Western gamers who missed this hilarious bug, trust me, it was a 'drilling' experience in the Japanese version.Graphics and audio? Chef's kiss! The visuals are so polished, you'd think your screen had a spa day. And the music? It's not just remastered; it's reimagined. It's like they took the original tunes, fed them a fancy diet, and now they're strutting down the red carpet.Whether you're a Final Fantasy veteran, reminiscing the good ol' days, or a newbie about to dive into what might just be the peak of the series (yeah, let's be real, things got a bit wobbly after FFVII), this version of FFVI is where it's at. So grab your controller, and let's relive the magic, minus the head drills, but with all the pixelated charm and operatic flair!
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: Long one of my favourite games in the series, this is a solid port.The visuals are fine.  They are slightly controversial, but I find that overblown.  The audio is excellent: a strong enhancement over the originals.  The gameplay is mostly the same, but old bugs are fixed.  To my memory the script is pretty similar, but I think there may have been a few tweaks here and there.For those who have never played the original, this was one of the greatest 16-bit RPGs.  A huge cast of characters bringing their own unique skill sets are played through an epic story.  It captures the gameplay and story themes that had been developed over the previous five games and delivers the best experience to that point.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing FF7 for the first time and getting back into FF6 right after (2nd full playthrough of ff6) I have to say FF6 is the best FF game for me between the two. Story is engaging, and interesting, well constructed. You care about what happens. The characters are colorful and diverse. The soundtrack is a bliss to listen to, the cut scenes and events memorable. This remaster doesn't overly temper with the original but enhances it and is a respectful to it's source.If you like RPG's this feels like one you shouldn't miss.My only issue is a technical one when I launch the game sometimes it hangs and doesn't actually boot the game. I need to force close the process, I give it another go and it's fine. Hardly a show stopper.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: The critically-acclaimed (no, not that one) Final Fantasy game has a port. It exists.This is my favorite FF game of all time, even above VII - I'll die on that hill. The story is rich with a dark tone and gut-wrenching moments, the characters are (mostly) fleshed out and lovable, and the game does a great job at world-building. There's a scene that's actually voice-acted AND in pixel 3D that had me in tears after playing it again after so long.AND THE SOUNDTRACK. OH MY GOD, THE SOUNDTRACK. REMASTERED IN FULL GLORY. it's beautiful.There are also auto-save and quick-save options that make the game much less painful and more of an enjoyed experience than a meticulous grindfest. Say goodbye to not losing progress!However, the one complaint I have is that the default text is jarring and takes away from the immersive experience. Without downloading a mod for a SNES font, it looks cheap and a lot less impressive. Other than that, it's worth your money. Please play this masterpiece for yourself. I'll be listening to Dancing Mad again. <3
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing ff6 since I was a child on my snes, I have played ever port and version of the game and finished the mainline story at least 50 times.Thoughts on this one.GFX are improved, best out of all the ports and versionsSFX and Music Improved, best of all of the versionsControls Not trash but not the best, Blitz input is wonky (you must enter it slowly).Extra Content, Trash compared to the GBA version, super bummed they didnt include any of that, no Dragons den, extra summons etc...Overall 8/10, if you dont have the GBA version its worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: Coming into this version proper after all the QOL updates and honestly, this version is extremely well done. a very faithful remake, chock-full of quality of life features that cut down the tedium of the old-era jRPG design and make the grind so much more accessible. All that on top of what is already a solid 8/10 jRPG. I very much reccomend this to those either looking into getting into the series/genre, or just those having enjoyed the original and want a fresh replay with more freedom to try for completion.solid 9/10 for me, maybe wait for the occasional sale but doesn't usually go off for more than 25% tbf. _childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: I am only at the dinner party in this remaster so far, but FF6 is among my fave games of all time and I have played through it countless times.It is more true to the original than any previous re-release that I've played, only making minor edits to the original game, aside from a completely redone opera scene. Gameplay wise it has been almost identical to this point, with the difference being some great QoL updates to character abilities, auto battle (basically the same as mem cursor and holding "a" in the og), and the sprint button (sprint shoes still give a boost and save your thumb). Maybe most importantly, it retains the challenge of the original.As far as the downsides, the biggest is the loading times. I have it on a corsair mp500 pcie3 nvme drive, with 32gb of fast ram. I shouldn't see loading times on a buffed up SNES game. There are also some colour palette mismatches between character sprites and other things, but this can be fixed with mods.Now, that's all fine and good, but the reason I recommend this version even if you've played all the others:THE MUSIC.Uematsu himself led the team remastering the music for this game, and it shows. The score has never sounded better. You could listen to it all on the 'tube, I am sure, but discovering it anew as I play through the game gives me much of the same feels I got playing through it for the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy VI is my favorite video game of all time. I played through all 6 of the Pixel Remasters, and overall I was very pleased with the remaster. I didn't mod it at all. I didn't hate the fonts as much as some of the other reviewers. If you've never played Final Fantasy VI, I believe this does the game justice. There are some things that are done different than the United States Super Nintendo version (released as Final Fantasy III in 1994). I'll note them here:Overall I believe it to be an excellent remaster of the game, and I'll probably come back to it for future playthroughs of Final Fantasy VI.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: I probably don't need to say much because this is an iconic old school 2D RPG. If you like those, can't go wrong. You can quicksave the game and it also autosaves, which comes in handy, since it tends to crash every now and then. I enjoyed the game and finished it, but you will have to put up with the typical things. The game can be a bit cryptic and items/dungeons can be hard to find. The equipment also does stuff it doesn't say in the description. If you occasionally use a guide the battle part in itself isn't hard, even trivial, if you have everything unlocked. The party will get broken up, so you will be playing with several characters. The game does not have a clear class or job system, so anyone can learn the same skills save a few. This makes things a lot easier but it also diminishes the need to build up a unique character. The mazes only have a few splits at most, but it's still a bit annoying to get clobbered over the head with random battle after battle while exploring. Overall a pretty nice game, certainly for the time, but if you like to build a rainbow kit for a boss battle like in epic battle fantasy, that one is better.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: So I've heard a lot of people refer to FF6 as the best Final Fantasy. I think the most accurate description is, it's the most polished Final Fantasy. They made 5 games trying to work with the same formula, then they just nailed it with this. All the characters have their own arcs, the atmosphere is so much heavier then in previous entries, the plot doesn't pull its punches, and keeps the pace steady. I still personally think I prefer 7 for the world and overall mechanics, but 6 truly is unlike anything that came before or after. Go play it.

_childDocuments_.review: FFVI is the best RPG of all time for me.This remaster is almost a yes, but sadly a no.Pros: - Some of the BGM was re-imagined very well.- Animations in battle bring new excitement.Still a great experience, but let's go to the cons:- World movement and in-town movement is a little wonky. The diagonal movement somehow messes up the experience instead of improving.- REALLLLY not liking a lot of the audio.. especially the menu selection, battle music, and victory fanfare.- While some of the BGM was good, overall, they overdid it on most of the music...which took away from the game.- No option for original BGM/Sound Effects.- What is up with the font and the way the chat window behaves?If you've never played the original, then you'll still really enjoy the remaster. _childDocuments_.review: It's nice to see such care and attention put into updating the game while staying true to the original vision. This can be seen in the sprites, the music, and especially the spell effects. SNES spell effects have a really particular look to them, and this game manages to stay true to it while jazzing them up.HOWEVERThis game suffers from what quite a few Unity-based games like Actraiser have, which is this really distracting judder while scrolling. The game IS running at 60fps, but the camera doesn't update at 60fps, it updates at *50* fps, creating very distracting stutter anytime the screen scrolls, which is  *checks notes* ALMOST ALL THE TIME. It's distressing that an updated port of a game that I'm running on hardware that is literally millions of times more powerful than the original platform runs substantially less smoothly.  I sincerely hope it's addressed in a patch and soon, because I'm really liking everything else but the stutter just makes it feel terrible to actually play outside of battle.

_childDocuments_.review: I've got mixed feelings on this. They messed with the writing that made Kefka (and other moments) so enjoyable from the first iteration of this game. (FF3, FF6J). I feel like that, by itself, is not sticking true to the original game - which really irks me, given the spirit of this one. (It's not a remake, it's a Pixel Remaster. Writing should have never been changed.)That aside, this held many of the great gems I remember from my childhood in it. If you are pining for FF6, or just want to experience what the golden era of 90's JRPG gaming felt like, play this game. This is one of the final masterpieces before Squaresoft became the trash company that is Squenix today, and it shows. This game is packed to the brim with content, especially if you know where to look. I'm pushing 40 and found out three things I missed through MULTIPLE playthroughs of this game as a child/teenager. (Ebon Rock, Shadow/Relm connection, and Cid's....uh, potentials with Cid.)Squaresoft, may you rest in peace. You were a juggernaut of a company and you are sorely, sorely missed.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommending this with HEAVY concessions.Yes, the game is good. It's not the definitive version of Final Fantasy VI, but it's not the worst. The remastered music is wonderful, and Kazuko Shibuya's spritework for this title is far and away better than the other Pixel Remasters.Unfortunately, the game is littered with so many bugs. I've soft-locked so many times, including just now when I was mid-way through the final battle of the game. Steal rates also seem to be broken against the player, because it can take upwards 20+ minutes to Steal a rare item from a boss, even when fast-forwarding with auto-battle. Enemies like Ninja opponents will often use abilities like "Dispatch," an instant death move, on themselves instead of on your own party members. There are more issues I can't even remember.As I recommend this, I do it with heavy caveats. Know that there are issues with this version of the game and what you may be getting into. The bugs are extremely frustrating and heavily detract from the overall experience. Be wary.

_childDocuments_.review: Day 1 Impressions of FFVI PR:Visuals: 8/10- The game is looking quite good so far, and the return to the original sprite style is a step up from the old steam/IOS version. I have noticed some stuttering when the screen scrolls and in some of the NPCs walking animations, however that could have been intentional on the developer's end. My experience with this game is on an SNES with a CRT TV so the scan lines may have made the animations look smoother im not 100% sure on that. Speaking about the classic look of the game do not use the classic graphics filter it looks really blurry and is pretty disappointing. With that being said, the character sprites that I have seen so far (Terra & Locke) have had great color and smooth animations both in the overworld and in battle so I am happy with those. Environments aren't changed much from the original but that's great as they were fantastic already.Audio: 9/10- I love the remixed tracks so far, but an option to use the original OST would have made a lot of sense so I don't know why that isn't there.Translation: 10/10- They used the definitive translation for the game which is great (GBA I believe). As far as the font goes there is an easy way to improve the default using one of the more popular guides right now.UI/HUD: 10/10- The menu navigation is great so far, I enjoy the layout and once the text is fixed I think it's likely the best version of the menus so far. Overall FFVI is a masterpiece and this pixel remaster is shaping up to be one of the best ways to play the game, I recommend this release of the game especially to those that have only played the IOS version.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:The music has been beautifully remastered.An overall refresh to the graphics without losing the aesthetic is a welcome change from the IOS version.The addition of an auto-battle option, while quirky at times, is a much needed improvement.The opera scene is fantastic!The bad:None of the new content from GBA is included, such as the new espers and Dragons' Den.A couple of achievements don't seem to be working (but I'm sure they'll fix that in time).Overall, I enjoyed my time revisiting this beloved game from my childhood. It remains my favorite Final Fantasy, and of the versions available I think this is the one to play if you want to experience the game, even without the added GBA content.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: This game was like a giant renaissance painting telling a sweeping, epic story.There are so many things I loved about this game. The music was theatrical and memorable with surprisingly fun combat and a beautiful story with lovable characters.My favorite aspect of the game was the overall theme and message the story has. Kefka is the living embodiment of nihilism who creates chaos to destroy all hope within the main characters and the world around them. Seeing the experiences and story archs of the main characters and how they move on from their pasts and restore hope is inspiring, especially for a game that came out in 1994, it was unheard to have a story that was so large and impressive.The pacing of the game is perfect too, the story doesn't drag but its also not too short. I beat it in about 30 hours while also doing some side stuff and it felt perfect in terms of pacing.Despite some characters only existing to fill in a role within the sandbox of combat variety, there's so many moving characters like Edgar, Sabin, Locke, Shadow, Terra, Setzer, Cyan and probably my favorite character, Celes.Celes had some of my favorite story beats in the whole game. The Opera House part and how it lampshades her relationship with Locke is fantastic and also the beginning of World of Ruin with Cid and Celes was gut wrenching.Not to mention, the final fight in Kefka's tower was insane. The music as well as the sprites and backgrounds were gorgeous, it goes back to what I said about the game feeling like a renaissance painting.The only issues I really had with this game were random encounters being a little too annoying, especially in areas like Zozo and also some really vital story beats between characters can be way too easy to miss sometimes, especially with a character like Shadow who is implemented in a really temperamental way gameplay wise.Despite that, the pros outweigh the cons so much that I think this game is almost perfect and I loved my time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: Above all the other Pixel Remasters, this one is the closest thing to a true  of them all. There are a few cutscenes which, while still faithful, are completely "upscaled" to Square's HD-2D style. One of them might even be slightly controversial, where . I liked it, but others may prefer the original scene.However, the game is surprisingly buggy at the time of writing. Some of these bugs are harmless, but I've also encountered a few soft-locks. So far, nothing I can't recover by simply force-quitting the game and reloading a save, but still worrying.The quick TL;DR is that the game is still great, but it's very unpolished at the moment. I've had a lot of fun with it as a way to experience one of my favorite games with a fresh coat of paint, but if you're wary of glitches, you might wait until some patches are released.With that out of the way, here's a more detailed breakdown of this Pixel Remaster.The game you're getting here is a hybrid of the updated script from the GBA port but with only the base content from the original SNES game. This means that several confusing lines, typos, and broken translations are fixed, but many of the fan-favorite lines from the original translation are absent. This isn't a deal-breaker for me because the characters' personalities still shine through, and in some cases are better defined (e.g. Setzer's motivations when you meet him), but I'll always miss some of the cheesier Kefka lines. The extra content of the GBA version—bonus espers, dungeons, stuff like that—is not present.I definitely noticed a couple of missing touches that the original somehow did better. One minor example is that flails/morning stars use the punch sound effect for attacks instead of the powerful "kachunk" sound used in the SNES version. But overall, it's a very faithful new version of this legendary game, and everything is recreated well.Despite my nitpicking the minutia of a game I've probably played 15 times over the past 25 years, several aspects of the remaster are improved over the original in really impressive ways. Some of the sound effects are new and improved; heavily inspired by the SNES version, sure, but with more depth.The new soundtrack is almost entirely fantastic. Some tracks, like the one for the Veldt, are absolute masterpieces. However, I found that a few of the really  tracks, like Battle to the Death, are a little under-mixed and flatter than I was expecting from such bombastic, dramatic songs. They're  more complex than the original SNES tracks, but a few of them lack the flair and punch of those crunchy digitized originals. I haven't made it to the final battle, so I don't know yet if The new character sprites are great: my nostalgia goggles initially told me "these look exactly the same as the originals" until I went back and actually played the SNES version again. They're still chunky pixels, but they fit much more detail into the sprites. Kefka, for example, looks better than ever. Gestahl still looks like a dog, though. (If you didn't think so before, now you'll never unsee it.)Spell and ability animations are absolutely top notch. The spell animations are reminiscent of the originals while being better animated. The sounds for the spells (like Ice, which IMO is strangely iconic to this game) are perfectly redone with more layers while retaining the essence of the originals. Sabin's Blitz animations are even better, Cyan's Bushido attacks are great, you get the idea. You'll definitely notice a couple of things that bother you if you're as invested in the original as I am, but if not, you won't even know the difference. Picking up from where Final Fantasy IV left off, this game is the strongest of the series to this point in terms of its narrative. This is true both in terms of complexity and scope; lots of characters get plenty of screen time in this story, and by the end you'll legitimately feel for them and their dreams. That's not to say that it's a masterwork of storytelling or anything; it was still limited by the possibilities of the SNES, after all. Final Fantasy VII surpassed this game's story in several ways. But, despite that, it manages to have some earth-shattering set pieces. Compared to FF V, which focused on a much simpler narrative compared even to IV, the plot of FF VI is absolutely huge.Gameplay: it's a JRPG through and through. Early on, each character is basically coded as a job class from the previous game, but before long, you're able to customize your characters significantly. Going into  you customize them is a bit of a spoiler, but know that the job system of FF III and FF V are not present here. Characters keep their special "job" abilities throughout the entire game, no matter how you customize them.Perhaps the most important thing about FF VI, if you haven't played it before, is how much the last 40% or so of the game opens up. After a certain major event occurs in the plot, the game more or less points you in the direction of the final boss, gives you a swift pat on the back, and sends you packing to figure out your own way. NPCs in towns become essential at this point for helping you gather resources and party members to prepare for the final dungeon. This is, in my opinion, one of the best things about the game. By the time you get to this point, you're ready for the training wheels to be removed.Speaking of training wheels, however, FF VI is pretty easy. Especially once you realize that you can start permanently tweaking characters' stats using certain items introduced about a quarter through the game, you'll start beefing up the strengths of your team or balancing out their weaknesses. It's not unusual for an end game team of FF VI characters to be absolute gods, dealing max damage on every attack—and that's without reading a walkthrough. For some extra challenge, I highly recommend playing the game in Active Time mode (instead of Wait). Enemies will be able to hit you while you're picking commands, but they need every handicap they can get.If you've been paying attention to the Pixel Remaster games, you'll know by now that you need to mod the font. The default font is hideous. There are plenty of instructions on the internet for how to do it, you don't need me to repeat them here.As I mentioned at the top of the review, this is by far the buggiest of the Pixel Remaster releases. I played FF I, III, IV, and V at release and never had anywhere close to the same issues. I won't repeat the list of bugs I mentioned earlier, but that's just a small sample of them. The harmless bugs won't bother you much, but when you soft-lock after accidentally insta-killing a boss which is supposed to be immune to instant death, you'll probably get pretty grumpy if you didn't save recently. Still, there is a save point near almost every boss, right? Right? ... Ultimately, Square Enix needs to get some fixes out for this game ASAP.If you've read this far, you already know my thoughts. I paid for the game and I've been enjoying my time with it. I also save- and quick-save-scum like crazy, because I'm always afraid the game is going to soft-lock. The game is overflowing with merits to make it a recommendation, but if you don't think you can handle the bugs or paranoia of maybe encountering them, I'd give it a pass until some updates address the major issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to play through the game completely before posting a review on this.  Here's a pros / cons list from someone who played it decades ago on the original SNES:Music remastering is great and done by the original composer Nobuo Uematsu.  There's a nice balance between honoring the old material and remixing some of the instruments and tracks.  Some songs have new segments to the music as well which made it really neat to play through and listen for all the differences.  The opera scene is done justice with an actual vocal accompaniment, though the English version is one of the weaker offerings and there isn't a way to set the language in game to hear the others.Redrawn pixel art looks good, I know the internet may argue otherwise.  Fit the art style while adding some more detail / colors.  All in game effects for battle scenes and events use modern graphic techniques vs sprites on the SNES.  Contrast to new pixel art and effects and backgrounds isn't nearly as noticeable as in the iOS version where resolutions didn't match up and the elements didn't fit together.There are some very minor quality of life improvements such as walking diagonally and a fast forward mode for the battle scene where your characters can repeat their last performed move for those grindy experience gathering sessions.  Really helps with leveling and doesn't detract from the experience.  Other weirdly specific bugs like Gogo not being able to lift the curse for the cursed shield seem to be fixed.The extras were nice as well - there's an art gallery with some pictures I hadn't seen before and a music test.  There's a bestiary as well if you gotta catch em all.Probably the most noticeable one is how the game really isn't optimized well in places.  I experienced some slowdown on menus later in the game when my inventory and spell list started getting complicated.  3D elements such as the world map scrolling and the airship taking off and landing (looked like a flat sprite pressed up against the ground) seemed kind of odd and out of place compared to the SNES.  Nothing game breaking, but some immersion was lost.  Loading a saved game was much slower than I expected as well - took maybe a second on most of the other platforms I've used before.  Restarting the game and loading a save took maybe about 30 seconds total to complete in the pixel remaster.  I didn't experience any bugs or crashing on my 50 hour play through, but I am a bit late to the game and suspect a lot of that's been patched out by now.Another thing that will stick out like a sore thumb to veterans of the game is the absence of the intro credits as the magitek armor walks into Narshe.  I get that they probably don't have the rights to acknowledge programmers from a different company who wrote decades old code for a game that may not even use their specific contributions anymore, but if you're going to remove them completely at LEAST put something else in its place.  It's a really neat dramatic effect in the original and comes off as a confusing and boring waiting game without a purpose as is.Censorship - yeah I have to mention it at least a little bit.  To be honest, its not such a big deal in this version.  Many of the esper and boss sprites with vague nudity remain covered from the USA SNES changes made decades ago.  They took out soldiers saluting with one arm in the Terra hypno crown flashback scene and changed some of the dialogue (which was sort of oddly translated on the original release anyway).  The only one that really stuck out was the scene with Celes where you no longer see her being chained to the wall and beat up by soldiers in her jail cell.  Now the characters just stare at eachother standing around doing nothing instead.  Completely removes any sense of urgency someone might have with saving a traitorous stranger in captivity and ruins the flow of the story.  If this is a regional change for regulations in japan, why not leave it in the game for the USA audience?  They clearly release different hamstrung versions of the game for each region, no reason to censor the scene here.Overall, if you haven't played the game before, this is a fine place to start.  The SNES version is probably the most coherent experience, but this will appeal to modern players a bit more with the quality of life, music and graphical improvements.  Works great on the steam deck as well.

_childDocuments_.review: The final game of the pixel remasters, and the last 2D mainline Final Fantasy. I'm aware this game is very special to many people, and I want to be clear before saying anything else: This is a good game.Music is consistently good, probably the best of these first 6 games on average, that much I'm comfortable saying. Shadow's Theme is sick. 1 or 2 standout bangers, the rest I've already forgotten. My favorite song of the pixel remasters probably remains from FF4 (Boss theme), but the rest of the music in that game is pretty forgettable.Plot is unique to the series thus far, no elemental crystals keeping the world in check, this time it's statues (lol). I will say that the game is very interestingly structured. The first half of the game is very cinematic and linear, while the later half feels slightly less story-focused and more open-ended. For this reason, the plot seems to pause halfway through the game, instead taking time to explore some of the characters on a more individual basis. Not every character seems equally treated in the eyes of the story, and that's honestly expected given the rather large roster in this game. Overall the plot is interesting but the pacing of the game felt awkward about 3/4 of the way through. You feel like everything you do after a certain point is largely unnecessary way before you've done everything. It's like the first half of the game is a delicious cake, and the second half is all icing. It's not exactly bad but the game somehow feels too long and too short. The actual time clocked in at just under 40 hours, and I skipped a dungeon because honestly I was OP already. The first half is pretty strong, and does some interesting things with telling concurrent events from different perspectives. I think the game feels short because almost all of the plot is over by the 20 hour mark, but you still have another 10-20 hours of game left to play. It drags a bit, but not unbearably so.The characters are mostly good, again some are given more love than others (Terra, Locke, Celes, Setzer, Cyan, Shadow, and Edgar, probably in that order). Almost all of these characters have some trauma that they deal with, and it's the exploration of this trauma and how it affects them that makes the better characters shine. Inter-party interactions could be more frequent, it's easy to feel like most of your party is incidental to the story at hand for basically all of the 2nd half (Again because they actually are), despite that, most characters gets to interact with each other at least once, and they have defining features that make the interaction interesting, mostly (Strago and Relm are weak characters that just have a bond together as both of their primary character traits). I've already talked too much about characters, but despite his relative short screen time, Shadow is probably the most interesting character of the whole cast. With Shadow, less is more. In very few words, and a couple actions, you can appreciate his character so much more because the conclusions you come to about Shadow are formed in your own head, rather than the game beating you over the head about what to feel. There's a restraint and a realism to Shadow that I deeply appreciate, he has agency, he leaves your party when he feels like it, he makes his own decisions. He doesn't over-share for the sake of 'building his character' like so many other characters often do in fiction. He has a past that he doesn't want to talk about and he is arguably the most tragic character in the whole game. Shadow is my pick for best character in this game, and by extension all 6 pixel remasters, for sure.Combat system is pretty interesting, they try to do something new for many characters. I like some of them in theory, but not so much in practice (Trace and Bushido come to mind). Blitz is wild, doing fighting game motions for the Ki-blasting monk character is kinda awesome in a stupid way. ATB is somewhat more simultaneous in this game, letting you pick actions during other actions, which is nice (albeit buggy sometimes, I've softlocked like 4 or 5 times playing through FF6, and maybe once in all 5 previous games). Every character gets their own gimmick, some are good, some are lame. Most of them are good, but most of them also feel like they don't get enough progression, there's just too many characters and not enough game for them to have a satisfying growth. On that note, Magicite is the primary new feature that shapes FF6 and it really just feels like they tried everything they could think of and didn't really make enough actual magicite to make the system really feel core to the experience. It's how you get all your magic (for the most part), but it also determines stat bonuses on level up (Which I don't like because it creates some anxiety when a character levels up with a sub-optimal Magicite for the stats but you were having them use it to train the magic it has), and it ALSO has a mega-ability of sorts that can only be used once per battle. Magicite is an interesting system that I really think is doing just a bit too much. The game doesn't give enough different magicites to be switching them out enough to not just be sitting on ones you already learned all the magic for. It also kinda makes for a strange thing where literally everyone is caster, and it just muddies the waters a bit on character roles when everyone can learn every spell. Just a sorta clunky system that is one layer too deep and not quite wide enough.Overall, FF6 tries to do a lot, and is sometimes not quite sticking the landing. The first half is really strong, but the second half is just okay. There are strange features that kinda don't feel like they really work that well or aren't fleshed out enough (Veldt and Gau, Coliseum, and Magicite to a lesser extent), but they are largely ignorable and don't ruin the experience. It's easily the best FF of the 6 pixel remasters but it isn't perfect, it does everything it's supposed to do, it's only losing points on execution, compared to previous games where there's massive voids where some features/story/focus should be. FF6 is ambitious, fun, has some good characters, and tells a better story in it's first half than any FF before it did in their entirety.

_childDocuments_.review: FFVI is one of my favorite JRPGs and probably the best Final Fantasy game. While prior ports of this title have been disappointing at best, this Pixel Remaster version finally gives the classic the attention and polish it deserves.I really only have a few criticisms, and they're minor:- The completely back to basics approach here means none of the improvements from other ports are retained, which means no text box portraits or additional content like in the GBA version. YMMV on how necessary these are, but you'd think a "definitive" version would incorporate some of these.- As others have pointed out, the font is still pretty bad, and while this is fixable on your own by replacing the font files, it's a shame this isn't a built-in option.- The music is MOSTLY really good, but I find how inconsistent the adaptations are on a track to track basis really jarring - some tracks get the full orchestra treatment, but some don't, leaving tracks like "Save Them!" feeling really out of place by comparison. Or, some tracks will sound otherwise great and then a sampled sax will show up, when it seems like it should have been simple enough to just get a real sax. Or the battle theme itself - the brass sounds good, but the strings sound bad. Like I said, the music is mostly very good, but it seems like it perhaps needed a little extra time to cook in order to deliver a consistent sound.- As much as I like the remastered soundtrack, an option to switch to the original music would be neat. Same goes for the other Pixel Remaster releases.- Removed credits from the opening sequence - look, I get that all the Pixel Remasters did this, but the scene was specifically created to support a credits sequence in this case, rather than 2 minutes of nothing happening. I'd really consider putting these back.- Needs a vsync option - as with the other Pixel Remasters I get a lot of bad screen tearing with this. If they could include a vsync option that would really help...All in all - pretty great, though a patch to iron out some of the items above might be nice.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: One of the best entry of the series, the PR (Pixel Remaster) manages to keep the sprites looking true to the original, while the soundtrack and SFX are only improved, keeping the game truer to what memory serves. It is important to note that NONE of the GBA content is available in this version.Story: While it's not impossible to resume the story of the 14 playable characters, it's probably better to keep it vague and only say what the main character's goal and the game's is mostly about. You start out as an amnesic and controlled soldier who eventually manages to free herself from the grasp of her captors to discover who and what she is. It is during a time of rebellion where many peoples and characters will have their own reasons to join the fight, only to eventually have everything turned upside down. I also remember that for its time, this game dealt with somewhat dark themes, so it won't feel as childish as some other games of the time did, so there's that.Gameplay: It's the basic JRPG of its era; wait for your turn and select between attack, magic, skill or items.FFVI differentiates itself from the majority of the JRPGs of its time because of the sheer amount of skills and abilities that the many characters have. While some characters can absorb spells, another can do an input sequence to do a specific skill, another use a slot machine, another steal, another can.... dance. You can build your favorite team and, most of the time, stick with it. There's a total of 14 characters, including 3 missables, so it is important to care what decisions you take, but the game is still very playable with the minimum amount of characters. There is an Esper system (somewhat like Summons), this is how you will learn your spells. Each fight grants you xp, money and random loot, yes, but eventually will also start granting you AP, which is added automatically and modified by your Esper's specific spell multiplier which you currently have equipped. When it reaches 100%, you learn the spell on the spell table of the equipped Esper. Example: If you equip Siren as an Esper, you can learn Silence which has a x8 rate on AP gained, Sleep x10 (and a couple more more spells), meaning if you get 4 AP from a fight, you'll get 32% learned on Silence and 40% learned on Sleep. Additionally. some Espers have a stats bonus whenever the character that has the Esper equipped levels up, they can range from +1 strength,+ 2 speed, + w/e all the way to things like +50% HP. Sometimes it can be better to hold off on leveling so as to have better end game characters to profit from more powerful Espers' bonus stats. There are guides on the matter and they are recommended if you want to build strong characters, though in the end, the game is old and balance is not its forte.The PR also offers nice little additions like quicksaving anywhere, as long as you're not in combat or during a dialogue, boosting xp, AP, and gil income, which can screw you over if you do it too early (no bonus from lving w/o the proper Espers, remember?). You can also sprint with a button press now... Which is kinda funny because if you equip the Relic to go twice as fast, you can now go 4x as fast as could could on SNES version. Apart from the Espers and individual skills of each characters there isn't really anything noteworthy, gameplay wise.Graphics: While they are improved, I would've thought I would notice more differences. The sprites, menus, fonts and environment all look like the original, but are remastered in a manner that won't hurt your eyeballs and actually fit your screen. Still, I would've appreciated some of the effort that was put into the GBA version (like having the character's face on their text bubble or the Espers). The elemental effects, encounters effect and many other little details all have been improved upon and are very noticeable details. Even the flashes have been dampened.... stiiiiiill, I feel like not including the GBA content was a strange choice.Audio: I've been whistling Terra's Theme for well over 20 years now, so it was nice to hear it remastered. Heck, even the Opera scene is a full on score, that was a wtf moment, and a good one at that. You're still reading? Ummm... Uuuh, ok. Uuuuh... Well, I never owned this game back on SNES, I rented it every weekend and always had to start over because save files would get deleted... It was nice to finally finish it. So my opinion might be a bit of nostalgia speaking, but I would put this game just between FFVII and Chrono Trigger. Its drawbacks are the balance of it, but the game makes up for it in character depths.

_childDocuments_.review: The finale of the Pixel Remaster series. Final Fantasy 6 is a fan favorite in the franchise and with the huge quality of life updates from the console version of the game brought over onto the Steam Remaster it all feels smooth and complete, retro fonts and all. Story wise the game is a bit longer than the first four titles and a good chunk shorter than Final Fantasy 5, which is refreshing as it even in that lesser time still told its engaging and enjoyable plot. In comparison to the first four games and even Final Fantasy 5, the story is again way different from previous entries, yet told in a simple and straightforward way. The visuals as alwasy are on point, love the Sprites and Artwork used. _childDocuments_.review: EDIT 1/31/24: With various game version updates, certain changes have been made that were previously points of criticism in this review. Chocobo maneuverability in Mode7 is improved; Esper bonuses altered to better-suit different playstyles; missing Lore casting animations have made a return; bestiary entries accessible from the in-game configuration menu.Of all the FF pixel remasters available on Steam, it feels very much like FF6 PR had simultaneously the most and the least attention paid to it visually, for better and for worse.While the graphics are largely unchanged (a testament to the visual quality of this game upon its first release in 1994) there are some jarring edits that will likely catch veteran players off-guard - and perhaps even newer players when the care and consideration of the visuals in the other PR versions is taken into account.The choice to add boulder outlines to cavern entrances, in and of itself, isn't a bad idea, but the appearance of these outlines does not mesh well with the existing background palettes and seems like a rush job.  Given the apparent care put into similar efforts in the PR versions of FF4/5 one assumes deadlines were fast approaching with no compromise from management.There also seems to have been some apparent difficulty with replicating the Mode7 view used for chocobo, airship, and certain cutscene sequences: these play out more slowly, and the hit detection for impassable terrain on the chocobo is particularly shoddy.Other strange choices include a reuse of the white magic casting animation to signal Gau entering the use of a Rage state, which adds needless delay to attack execution and results in bizarre errors in the flow of combat unseen in other versions of 6: characters attacking after Gau enters a Rage but before he executes his first attack, sometimes resulting in the attack failing to execute at all with a "no effect" message.  Similarly, Strago's Lore spells reuse the same white magic casting animation, and considering the remade blue magic casting animation in 5, that nothing was done for that in 6 again suggests a hard-nosed attitude about deadlines.Other quibbles include Maranda and Tzen not having their BGM updated to the standard upbeat town theme during the brief period following the banquet at the Imperial Palace, but prior to boarding the ship at Albrook (a missed opportunity to make use of Maranda's original Troia-like theme) and a decision to not cloak Albrook itself in darkness following the ascension of the Floating Continent.Yet there are are positives concerning minor graphic changes, too: while most of the other PR versions reuse the same animations for all spells across all titles, 6 retains its unique spell animations.  Blizzara still cloaks a target in a solid wall of ice before shattering apart.  Firaga impacts like a roaring meteor leaving behind a fiery explosion.  Chaos Wave radiates outward from Maduin's core, and Absolute Zero encroaches from the flanks of a battle scene before cloaking the entire view in a frigid chill.  The attention to detail here can't be faulted, and when it comes down to it, one can overlook poorly-placed cave boulders next to the beauty of these updated attack visuals.There are other QoL improvements, too - while veterans with, potentially, 30 years of muscle memory may stumble the first time they're asked to execute a Blitz, it's important to note that players new to the game will have an easier time following an onscreen guide for these inputs.  Auto-battle saving Blitz commands without the need to consistently tap them in encounter-to-encounter is a welcome change and eliminates much of the tedium with random fights.  A carry-over from prior re-releases on Cyan's Bushido techniques means you won't have to watch a bar take an agonizing time to slowly fill while other characters' turns languish awaiting inputs, and the change to Raiden's level-up bonus almost makes up for the loss of the 4 bonus Espers from the GBA/iOS releases.While there is still some consternation over the change to Celes' introductory scene, it should be noted that this change was made nearly 20 years ago before the GBA re-release in accordance with updates to Japan's own games rating authority policies, not any misplaced contemporary grievance.  Having played this game on the SNES, the GBA, and now the PR version, I do not believe that loss of this scene negatively impacts Celes' character to the extent some may claim: the implication of what she's endured is still very apparent, even if we aren't direct witness to it, and when it comes to older games like this, implication is often all one has to run with anyhow.Overall, I will recommend this version of 6 to prospective buyers.  In the grand scheme of things, the complaints about certain minute aesthetic changes pale next to other, positive changes. This is easily one of the best FF titles in the entire franchise and it remains a gorgeous game that serves as the gold standard the visuals in the other PR titles aspire towards.  It is certainly the darkest in tone among all the original NES/SNES entries and serves as a foundational basis for many of the more mature FF stories that followed in its wake.  If you choose to play it, I certainly hope you enjoy it as much as I have for nearly three decades.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn’t the first time I’ve played this game. Hell, this isn’t the first time I’ve reviewed this game on Steam. Thinking back, I think the only version of this game that I haven’t played is the Game Boy Advance version (which is likely the definitive version of this game, but more on that later.)I say all of that to say that I’m a big fan of this game. In fact, it’s one of my favorites of all time. With that being said, I’ll cut right to the chase: if you’re a fan of classic console RPGs and you haven’t played this game, I demand that you do so immediately. Go ahead. I’ll wait.…Did you do it? Good. Now I can nitpick/fanboy about this version without worrying whether you’ve played it or not.So, yes, this version has several graphical improvements over the older versions (hence, the  appended to the title). Those, however, aren’t the only improvements: the inclusion of an auto battle mode, mini-maps pinned to the corner of the screen, treasure tracking, bestiary, etc., all make this an improvement over most of the versions that are out there. Compared to the other version that is widely available on modern platforms, it is technically an improvement over the Android/iOS version, which was available on here before but can no longer be found on the store page. (I was one of the handful of freaks who didn’t fly into a rage over that version, mind you. I thought it was fine.)I would stop short of calling this the definitive version of the game, however. Once again, just like the previous version, it’s missing the (admittedly hokey) CGI animations from the PlayStation port. Now, on top of that, this one is missing the extra content from the GBA version. That stuff might not be necessary for this to be a good game (it’s not), but, as a long-time, hard-core fan of this game, I was hoping for all of it to be included in one package. I guess I get to keep on waiting… Though the next version of this game will likely be a remake that will cast all that stuff aside, anyway. With all of that out of the way, this version is the best version of the base game that you’ll find. There are some additional things that will appeal to people who salivate over this one, too: an improved soundtrack, original artwork by Yoshitaka Amano, and a new interpretation of the opera scene that is guaranteed to make you mess yourself. This version just lacks a few things that would elevate it to “perfect”.So, is this the version that you should play if you’ve never played the game before? Probably… but that depends on the resources available to you. The GBA port is likely as close to a definitive version that we’ll ever get. But, if that’s not feasible, this is the next best choice. Whatever you do, you should play this game, whatever version you can get your hands on because it is, objectively, one of the best games ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone whos never actually beat this game, I can tell you that this was an amazing experience. I ended up using mods anyways, which there are a ton of by the way, and they're easy to install on top of that. The music of course was wonderful. The SNES music was beautifully translated to real instrumentals and the result is incredible. I was blown away when dancing mad played and I was stunned during the fully sung opera sequence, which yes, is as cool as it sounds. Its even in 2.5D. Its worth seeing. The quality of life updates were really nice too. I actually liked that some of the characters movesets were simplified, like Cyans moves being changed so that you select THEN wait, and like how Sabins input moves have been made way more easier to do. I understand the argument that it takes the challenge of playing as them away, but I prefer it simply because I'd probably not be able to use them previously. All that said, I do kinda wish there was an option to have the bonus content from the previous versions. To be completely fair, this game has a ton of stuff to do in it as is, like collecting all of the espers, getting the extra characters, or doing the bonus dungeons that are already there. However, most of that content is to give the player more stuff to use during battle, but outside of that magic tower and the final boss, there aren't a lot of places to use these things. I get why this extra content was removed, but I feel it would've been better if they left it as an option or something. However, the content isn't needed. The game is spectacular as is. Its my favorite version out of the ones I played, so if you're on the fence, go for it. A wonderful experience.

_childDocuments_.review: In a shocking twist of fate, the FF6 pixel remaster actually seems HARDER than the original. Some remixes are almost as good as the originals, while others just fall flat. As in the other remasters, the woodwinds remain a strong point (such as in the town theme). I was also very impressed with Setzer's theme.The battle backgrounds are beautifully redone, and the rest of the graphics (most notably the grass) are subtly improved, especially the panoramic backdrops in the world of ruin. They did really good on the searchlights in Kefka's Tower, too. And of course, the water sparkles. It was nice to see that they properly updated FF6's original spell animations, instead of reusing the same ones from the first five games.One major complaint is the lack of menu screen customization, a hallmark of FF6. I always enjoyed getting creative with the wallpapers and colors, but that's all gone now. For most people this is probably no issue, but I did miss it.Some have complained of censorship; personally, I couldn't care less. It never hurts to exercise caution and sensitivity. But when I see people posting hashtags on the forum like "#BeatUpCeles", that's really disturbing, and only lends credence to the decisions made. Listen to yourselves.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy VI has been a favorite FF entry for many and for good reasons. But it was also a game that hasn’t had a “perfect” version up until now. The SNES original had lots of strange bugs (even though some very beneficial) and a few translation quirks, along with the name change to Final Fantasy III in NA (PAL region didn’t get the game at all). The Playstation release had problems of its own, along with the slowness of the CD media. GBA release made a lot of compromises to get the game on the platform and its additional content, as was the case with the rest of the Advance releases, was of questionable quality at best. And the previously available 2014 PC and mobile version was ugly and had new issues.Pixel Remaster version finally provides us with the perfect Final Fantasy VI you can play today. It gets the same improvements as the rest of the collection, like beautifully recreated pixel visuals scalable to high resolutions and with new awesome visual effects and particles. The already fantastic music is impeccably recreated with live instruments and, in case of the famous opera scene, sung vocals. Said opera scene also contains an unexpected use of the 2.5D look (think Octopath Traveler) which wasn’t really necessary, in my opinion, but does look nice. And in general, there are even more little details and layers to many scenes that go perfectly in tone with the original game look and feel.The gameplay is mostly unchanged, while featuring the same improvements the rest of the PR games received, like the “Auto-battle”. Yet, a few of the character abilities were tweaked to be more intuitive in use. Sadly some things remain flawed: Gau is still annoying to play without a guide in hand, as none of his 200+ Rage modes have a description (and learning them is slow). But overall, the gameplay feels improved.Chronologically VI was the first game in the franchise to give you control over who can be in the playable party. It was designed with the concept of not having a defined main character and while arguably it has been the case for the majority of the series up until that point (IV being the exception), the story still dictated who belongs to the party of heroes saving the world at any point. In VI, though, at many points you can switch characters around any way you want, including attempting to play the game with just one character. Each character, just like in IV, has a specific job (class), but in addition to that the concept of magicite stones was created that provides a chance for almost every character to learn magic. So while each character had completely unique abilities, almost everyone could be an efficient mage.It’s a really cool twist on the way learning jobs worked in V and a basis for how VII and IX would work later, but this approach has some flaws. The biggest one is that in their attempt to make every character job and abilities interesting, Square has created an issue where some characters feel less useful or fun to play as. In IV the game was balanced around knowing which classes are available at any point. While V and III made it possible for you to have a party of Dancers for one particular fight in the middle of a dungeon and switch jobs immediately after. In VI if you put a Dancer in your party, you’re stuck with them until get your next chance to change the party structure. Plus, it doesn’t help that one third of the characters feels forgotten about for most of the story and they don’t get enough, if any, unique moments.Speaking of the story – FFVI is most praised for its storytelling, so did it age well? Quite well, actually. The story, the characters, some of the topics and the overall structure of the plot still feel amazing today. The Big Thing That Happens still has few, if any, competitors. Its ensemble cast, while far from perfectly realized, is shockingly varied in the way they are written and explored. And the pacing of the game is really well thought out, feeling fresh and doing unexpected things even when being linear.Yes, being so much more detailed, personal and mature than previous entries, there are ways this storytelling could be improved. Where IV and V are perfect as they are, with no real need to expand or go deeper, VI can occasionally rush things in ways modern storytelling wouldn’t allow. Events can jump from one beat to another with little to no transition and at times you can get moments, where you can get confused about how one moment lead into the other. So sure, while Square would get better with the pace and the cast in Chrono Trigger, that was released a year after FFVI (now that’s a game that demands a full Pixel Remaster treatment), this game is still so good that you forget about the flaws entirely.So if you’ve never had a pleasure to play Final Fantasy VI before you’re in luck as Pixel Remaster is the best way to do it anyway. If you have, maybe it’s time to revisit one of the absolute best Final Fantasy games in the series with this shiny new version. Or, better yet, play the entire collection if you get a chance.
