_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game!This game is my second introduction to the series, the first being FF4. FF6 is definitely the one that convinced me to get more into the FF games in general. I don't have much to say on whether it being a pixel remaster is an upgrade or not because I have never touched the OG games, but the music is amazing, UI is decent, and the sprite are nice and expressive.It's very interesting how the game doesn't really have a main character and you bounce around having different leads. While I enjoyed it, a lot of the characters are kind of bare bones and left up to interpretation. Which for some people is better and even more fun but I just want more. Although it is understandable that this game is decades old and couldn't add EVERYTHING they wanted. Honestly, most of my problems with this game are because of hardware limitations so, not really appropriate for a review.Cons for me:The UI is very simple but sometimes lacks information, like what status condition does the enemy have.This game kind of suffers from having too much in some parts. Too many characters, some having way less involvement than others, and even some having lore hidden in different parts of the world and locked depending on if they are in your party. I like the magicite system but man are there A LOT of abilities you can learn.Another problem is that a lot of the locations are kind of boring? There are some fun NPCs now and there but a lot of small villages and towns look the same. None really stood out to me save for a few.My last issue is that the game is kind of difficult. Since it is kind of open world, you can get jumped by monsters higher than you, but even so, there are some monsters that require a specific strategy that you either get through trial and error or reading the wiki.I can see a lot of these not being a problem for people or them even enjoying this, so it really depends on who is playing to see these cons.Pros:Enough of the cons though. This game has great music and pushed me to get the full soundtrack just to listen to. My favorites are mostly the battle and character themes but there are a good chunk of area songs that I have on repeat. I love the idea of magicite and how it works. The soul/essence of Espers which you can equip to get their abilities and also summon them to aid you in battle. I love summoners and summons but this is a unique take on it.A lot of great party members that I keep reusing and an interesting reoccurring main villain. The characters with specific jobs and roles are fun to mix and match with. A few of them I'd remember forever like Terra, Celes, Locke, etc. The main villain has a TOP TIER hysterical theme song and then an insane battle theme. I love the game sometimes letting them enjoy themselves or be silly even with whats going on in the story and they did great showing it through sprite work.This game has a lot of stuff that rewards players who like to check every nook and cranny, rewarding you with weird items or even story bits. Which I love and hate at the same time (Since I could lose out on something cool because I didn't have guide open)For JRPG the game didn't feel too long or slowly paced. A good combination of character and then world building got me through the game fairly quickly (for this genre). A nice story on going through heavy struggles and recovering lost hope.FF6, while not my favorite game, is a REALLY good introduction to the FF series.

_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: as a first-time player of FFVI, this is a wonderful way to play the game for the first time and I think it's become my new favorite final fantasy game right after FFIX. the new OST is amazing, i really like what they did with the color palette and sprites compared to the SNES version (which seems to be a point of contention among those who grew up with the original), and lots of the new QOL is heavily appreciated as someone more used to later JRPGs. i didn't encounter any bugs besides some weird controller support issues, and the updated translation is pretty solid as well from what i've seen. i only have a few major complaints, one of which is the text; that weird modern FF remaster font sucks so bad and makes all the pixel remasters look immensely worse, imo. however, it's an easily fixable problem as people have made custom fonts that bring back the FF6 style, and it made the game look so much more palatable. my other gripe is that i wish that some other scenes got the opera scene overhaul treatment; they went absolutely nuts on updating the opera scene (for good reason, considering how renowned that sequence is) with sharp 3D backgrounds and actual opera vocals, but there's so many other scenes that could've been given a similar overhaul. i wouldn't have minded waiting a couple more months to see scenes like  updated to have the 3D backgrounds that the opera scene had. it's a small gripe, really, and it doesn't take away from how great this remaster is.if you've never played the game before, and you're not too concerned with playing something true to the 1994 original but rather something more updated, this remaster is totally worth your time. just be sure to change that font!

_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: Update - The opera scene being done in HD2D/Octopath-type style with the actual singing gave me goosebumps! They took an amazing scene and made it next level! Also, the minecart sequence in the Empire that always looked blocky and weird is 3D now and absolutely what I had always wanted it to look like!Almost 10 hours into it and I'm enjoying this timeless masterpiece to its fullest! A few notes: Kefka's laugh from the SNES version is intact, the soundtrack is AMAZING, translation used is the GBA version (which is fine with me though I'd love to see some Woolsey-isms thrown in there too), gameplay is pretty much spot on save for a bit of stuttering, so far I've seen completely new battle animations apart from the other Pixel Remasters which is really great to see, and the enhanced graphics and map animations are just pure eye candy. This is my favorite game of all time and one of the greatest games ever made. Oh, and one other thing for those of you like me who think the world map is a bit too bright, go into the in-game configuration and lower the brightness to 45 or so. It'll look far better not just on the world map but overall, and better matches the aesthetic we're used to.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: Even to this day, Final Fantasy 6 is damn near perfection. What Square were able to achieve on the snes was and still is truly amazing and this remaster only enhances the experience. Smoother graphics, remastered music, an auto-battle feature for grinding, and plenty of Quality of Life features. I have never finished the SNES or PSP versions of FF6 only getting about halfway through on them but I feel I can safely say this is the definitive version of this jrpg classic. My one gripe with this remaster is how they change the famous Opera Scene, now I dare say the new version is superior, it has some Octopath love, real vocal performances, and entirely revamps the entire scene, but I'd be lying if I said I didn't miss the original. There's something genuinely magical about how Square were able to make such a moving scene using such restrictive hardware, it's a magical scene and I really do implore everybody to go and at least watch how the scene played out originally.With the base game itself, I find the latter half of the adventure, the World of Ruin, to be pretty damn tiring at points, especially Kefka's tower, the way it splits your party up, forcing you to use characters you probably haven't used at all, meaning they'll be underleveled, likely have no good magic and you won't know how to use them, it makes the area a chore, especially when the rest of the game is so easy, just get Phantom Rush for Sabin, Chainsaw for Edgar, and have Terra and or Celes on healing duty and you'll never wipe again, except for Kefka's Tower. Luckily the final boss is phenomenal and, at the risk of being crucified by Final Fantasy 7 fans, way better than Sephiroth, which is a hard bar to beat for me personally. Overall FF6 was an amazing game, given new life with this remaster, I simply cannot recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: This new ost is amazing and the new effects are really cool, but that's where my positives end. I wasn't expecting them to do this but giving more graphics options would have been awesome, to swap around the color palette and adjust the contrast. also for whatever reason the boss kill animations are just, gone?, idk what reason there was for taking that out but that was one of the most satisfying things about beating a boss i really struggled with in this game, just that sound of the repeated cracking and then the boss crumbling down with a super basic animation. Now the bosses just fade away like any other enemy which is just weak... Also, UI, the UI here is horrible, idk if its too much to ask fro square to just make a new one that looks more thematically appropriate rather than recycling the same bland one for all pixel remaster games, but yeah its ugly and disrupts the otherwise excellent sprites. Despite all that this is IMO the best way to play this game. It's accessible, and unlike the old ports, faithful to the original game pixel art. I hope some mods get made to just add fixes to all those nit picks I have, the lack of options for this nearly 30 year old game is really annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: FFVI is one of those games that I'd recommend to anyone I can find with /any/ minute interest in classic JRPGs or Final Fantasy, or nobody at all. _childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: + Great update overall.+ Fantastic remade soundtrack with a few exceptions.+ Auto battle ends up taking a lot of the repetition out of the random encounters and can help with the grinding.+ Great visual enhancements that make FFVI's world look the best as its ever been.+ Great story with arguably one of the best villains in video gaming, period.+ Fair difficulty with a great leveling and ability system.+ Faithful script to the SNES version.- There are a few tracks that don't hit as hard as the others.- The saturation on the over the world feels too bright but it's easy to overlook. This can also be fixed via a simple mod for PC.- Font is horrible but can easily be patched on PC. Also, screen tearing issues but NVidia Control Panel can fix that if you own an NVidia card.By far this is the best version of Final Fantasy VI. They delayed this port to add extra polish and it shows. While the other pixel remasters were good, this is near perfection. While there are some very minor issues, a few of the songs don't hit as well as the SNES version, the rest of the OST is fantastic. The visual enhancements they did decide to implement look wonderful but you'll probably wish there were more. All and all it's a very, very faithful remaster that has the quality of life improvements that further make this game's world that much more immersive. Despite the few small issues it does have, it is a great remaster, and if you have a PC I'd highly suggest picking it up because it's the best way to currently play FFVI.If you never played FFVI before, this is your chance and you'll see why it is regarded as one of the best; many people's personal favorite in the series and one of the best JRPG's of all time. The story is still relevant, the characters are all well written with a few exceptions and it has one of the best villains in a video game, followed by a detailed world with great world-building and one of the best twists in games.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving this remaster.It's the same game I remember from the SNES, but cleaner.  Better translation.  Controller support that is spot-on. _childDocuments_.review: 4/4Final Fantasy peaked as a franchise with this game, and, especially looking at the first 10 games in their catalog, it is clear how each game that followed this masterpiece was inspired at its core by the aspects pioneered here. It is the epitome of sprite RPG combat, with distinct, unique, and memorable characters. The speed/turn based combat is not my choice of UI, but it's balanced in this game, it does not feel slow, and it's often used as a vehicle for character development and story. The story is one of the first in video game history to bring a true epic to fruition, that both unfolds in long-form and develops each one of the cast of characters in context of their world, a world which changes as the characters move through it. In short, fantastic game, highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: The Good: Outstanding OST, even compared to the original SNES version. Some great QOL additions: Sabin's Blitz input is easier. Shortening of the Bushido charge time means Cyan is now actually a viable character. Quicksave can be really useful especially for first-time players. Auto-battle can reduce the tedium of grinding and going for rare steals/drops significantly.  The Bad: The added content from the GBA and previous Steam version was not included. There are a few (minor) censored scenes, though you probably won't notice them unless you have played FF VI before.The Ugly: Bugs. Lots and lots of bugs, some of which can unfortunately be game-breaking for many players. Fortunately, some of them have been patched already, but many others still remain.The Verdict: Get it now if you are a die-hard fan of the FF franchise. Otherwise, you should probably wait until all the serious bugs are fixed.Overall, I would give it a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The best Final Fantasy game ever made, and the remaster only made it better. _childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: This has been my favorite game ever since it came out in the 90's, and I feel this version does the original much better justice than the previous "remaster" with the mobile graphics and UI.  Instead of trying to "update" the graphics like the previous version, this one just "polished" what was already there and it looks so much better for it.  The UI has also been restored to something closer to the original version (though selecting Blitz and Bushido commands from a menu took some getting used to).And the music... holy CRAP, the music is PHENOMENAL.  Much like the pixel sprite graphics, it's still mostly the original arrangements, just with an update to the synthesizer engine.  Music with unique instrumentation like Shadow and Cyan's themes sound amazing in this version.My only real gripe is the text.  The font size is almost unreadably small (thankfully, there is a mod for this, but I wish font size was an accessibility option in-game).  Also, unlike previous versions, dialogue text just "appears" on the screen all in one block now rather than the "filling in" animation it's had in all previous versions, which causes the "cadence" of the written text to feel awkward to me.Still, the good far outweighs the bad so far and I'm glad to see this classic get a new and respectable re-release.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through all of the Pixel Remasters and earned all of the achievements, including this one (as of last night).  In short, once the early bugs get fixed, this is the *definitive version* of the best Final Fantasy game.Square Enix put love and care into recreating this gem.  That's evident from the soundtrack alone.  I had a great time playing it and look forward to dusting it off in a couple years for my next play through. If you enjoyed later Final Fantasy games but never ventured into the 2-D ones, you *must* try 6.  The story of 1 through 5 all seem primitive compared to 6.  This title is the game that laid the groundwork for the tone and feel of 7.  It's such an important title and helped pioneer video games turning into an art form.  If you're just now starting to play it, I recommend that you check out the forums and keep backup saves until some of the early bugs get resolved.  Square Enix seems to be aggressively fixing them, so I anticipate this game will be close to flawless in a couple of months.PS - Kudos to Square for finally making Cyan a useful character by letting his special ability run in the background. For the love of God, fix the RNG on Setzer's slots.  That achievement was BRUTAL.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily my favourite Final Fantasy game. It is certainly the best of the 8bit/16bit era, the best of the remasters, and in my mind the best Final Fantasy overall. I haven't played 2 or 8 for context. I completed this game dozens of times back in the SNES era. The characters are all memorable. I recall the producers stating that their is no main character, all the characters are the main character. It is absolutely true. For the first 1/3 of the game there appears to be a clear main character, but it shifts a bit afterwards to the point in which all the characters' stories are given equal share of the stage. Each character has a pre-set of skills that are unique to that character. Basically each character has at least one unique battle skill. However, the game introduces a mechanic in which you can mould any character how you wish by enhancing their core stats.The story is amazing. The game has three defined acts and you could argue an epilogue involving the final dungeon. It has slap stick humour, powerful emotional developments, character growth, genocide, politics, family drama, ultimate evil and betrayal, hopelessness, hope, love, and sacrifice. You will find yourself selecting plot scenarios to complete in any order, multi-party battles, and using dialogue to influence a cease fire between two warring parties. Oh, and this game has the best FF villain hands down. The game play is the best of the early FF games. Battles use the trademark Active Time Battle system, meaning initiative for enemies and player controlled characters is influenced by stats (generally speaking). You will have to understand general enemy weaknesses and the strengths of all your party members to succeed. Generally, this game is on the easy side. Some locations and bosses present a true challenge, but overall, you can muscle your way through most locations without much grinding. Lastly, and not least of all, the music. Simply the best. In the SNES era, the music pushed the hardware beyond what anyone thought it was capable. The enhanced music sounds great. I wish there was an option to switch between the two music types. Only so myself and others can enjoy the originals in one package. If you never played before: it is the pinnacle of FF. Avoid spoilers and go in clean. There are so many twists and turns that I can't tell you how jealous I would be to experience for first time.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: i'd been playing various iterations of this game since its initial release. i have to say I am always happy to take a stroll down memory lane with ths title.  for those who seek a bit for bit conversion from the original source material, you might not find as much enjoyment for really only two reasons.1. the text is reformatted, making it difficult to see for those like myself with poor eyesight.2. the remastered music is quite nice but hits a little different than the source material.these are absolutely minor critiques. square enix did a fine job here
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: Awful port. Ugly sprites, really bad screen tearing, weird design decisions where the sprites and environments are washed out (they pretty much used the tileset from the GBA, so the overworld is discolored to make up for the GBA's bad display), UI is this weird mish-mash of minimalism and dated 90s UI so it's a pain in the ass to look at.Like, is this a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ romhack? You can go to nexusmods to grab the SNES sprites, tilesets and other mods to make the game less terrible, but you can absolutely tell this was a rushed, multiplatform job they did with a batch of other PR titles. They also recently did an update a few days ago that finally implemented quality of life changes they had on the consoles for 7 months already apparently, but from what I read, this is the last update they're making for the game, so it's essentially going to be abandonware from this point on like the android/iOS phone port they shelved a while back when the PR was going to drop.Thing that got me was when monsters die, the fading out effect is very grainy, like, it's way, way less smooth than it used to be on the SNES, and I have no idea what's with this screen tearing, I know it runs off the unity engine, but this old game that used to fit on 3MB cart is now 1GB in size for a sprite game. Like, the mod to change the battle/overworld sprites alone was what, 165MB? What inefficient garbage is this, lol. I'm strongly considering getting a refund, it's that bad right out of the gate.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

Overall, I would recommend this for FF6 veterans and newcomers alike. This remaster may not be perfect, but it still mostly captures the essence of the original game, which was damn near perfection.

_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: A very faithful reissue that has most elements from the SNES version I put a thousand hours into over the past 30 years. The pixel art, audio, and gameplay modifications are so elegantly done, that you might not even notice how much was tweaked if it has been a while since you played the originals. A big thumbs up to the devs for keeping the bones of this game intact while improving some things (some previous remakes were quite awful imho).There's a fair bit of dialog/story that has changed, I'm not sure how much is net new vs. coalesced from other versions and remakes that occurred over the years, as I've only ever played the snes NA/FF3 version on original hardware and emulation.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: The best 16-bit JRPG ever made. An immense, deep, soaring masterpiece of a game. And I particularly don't like RPG's, but I've been playing this game since it came out, and I have to say, this is my favorite re-release of the game. Widescreen support, a fully orchestrated score, remade particle effects, and a new translation. It's funny, sad, goofy, deadly serious, with one of the best ensembles in gaming rounding it out. An essential game for any RPG fan. Top 10 of all time.Pros:- Huge cast of characters, sweeping story- Complex and surprising systems for a 16-bit game, especially with magic- Amazing characters, all get their own backstory and side missions- One of the best game scores of all time- Truly mind-bending mid-game twist that changes entire gameCons:- Translation from GBA version, despite being more accurate, loses some of the silly charm of Ted Woosley.- Grindy magic system with too many useless spells.- Some cheap exploits persist, trivializing some encounters.- Certain characters are worthless to use, unbalanced abilities.

_childDocuments_.review: This could have been a decent remaster if it wasn't for the embarrassing amount of bugs. Among them I can count: softlocking by loading a cutscene as a regular game map, duplicated dialog messages, displaying NPCs at the wrong place during cutscenes or characters at the wrong position during battle animations, and  softlocking basically every time I had to switch between screens or when prompted for a character's name. Perhaps the most outrageous soft lock occurred at the end of the final boss battle because some characters were off screen due to the Jump command when the boss was killed. Quite a shame, because the previous Final Fantasy Pixel Remasters didn't suffer for nearly as many bugs and performance issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy VI’s impact on the industry zeitgeist cannot be overstated. It was initially released in North America to rave reviews in the fall of 1994—30 years ago—and as demonstrated by Square Enix’s (developed originally by Squaresoft) ability to monetize it in apparent perpetuity, the game’s overall influence clearly continues today. At 30 years, a masterpiece; why not 40? Why not 50? And beyond. FFVI’s ascendancy through the RPG collective remains irresistible. Its groundbreaking character work, rich narrative, and mechanically sound gameplay have set standards few games will ever touch. It’s no wonder that when consumers forage for the best RPG, or indeed, the best video game of all time, they often find this title on a rankings list by [insert your favorite gaming influencer here]. FFVI’s narrative structure is unique not just for 1994 but also for 2024. Unlike most RPGs, and most story arcs ever written, FFVI rejects traditional plot composition by removing a singular protagonist. Of course this isn’t purely novel; this tactic is occasionally attempted in plot structure, particularly in fantasy—A Song of Ice and Fire being the most popular, contemporary example—though often by the story’s resolution, a clear protagonist and antagonist eventually emerge. This is to say nothing of “good” and “bad” guys; instead, there is someone we follow working toward a goal and, alternatively, someone trying to stop them from achieving that goal. Not so here. From the enigmatic Terra to the noble Celes to the charming Edgar and optimistic Locke (and beyond!), every character contributes mightily to the tapestry of FFVI’s world. In this, the game is always an overwhelmingly rich and immersive experience for new and returning players because sound character arcs never go out of style.This characterization-by-community method would fall flat if all the heroes didn’t feel uniquely refined and independently motivated, but they do. Which is remarkable considering the sheer lot of them; this remains the most extensive playable cast of any Final Fantasy game to date, at 14 total party members (NOTE: two toons are easily missable and I wouldn’t include them in the aforementioned praise).  As characters, Celes and Edgar shine in particular as each, notably for their era of creation, represent a clinic on hero presentation. In themselves they teach a masterclass on characterization, showcasing depth and complexity through the lens (or burden) of leadership—Celes as a general, Edgar as a king. Celes overcomes catastrophe with compassion and raw determination. Edgar masks tragedy with wit and charm. Both are so remarkably…human? So much complexity. And still so necessary.Of course, no FFVI discussion of characterization is complete without deconstructing the title’s iconic villain—Kefka. Many consider Kefka to be an early video game case study on evil. This is somewhat limiting. Kefka is objectively evil, yes, but his central philosophy is that of pure nihilism. He’s the unloved bully with a gun who sees no true meaning to existence and who regards the whole of society as baseless. While dimensionally, he’s a bit of a misnomer compared to the game’s heroes because he lacks a backdrop of reason, and thus, we’re not as attuned to what led to his madness. But this hardly matters. Some of his misdoings present as so twisted and cruel that his madness begets more madness. The trail of death tells the story.Kefka represents a true force of nature. He is a raw sample of our collective cruelty, entropy, and unchecked ambition. He’s also more successful than all other Final Fantasy villains before or since. It’s not a spoiler, merely philosophy, to suggest, at least on some level, no matter what you do, Kefka…wins? This alone separates him as a unique Final Fantasy villain. No one can stop him. Which, alarmingly, serves to prove his world view. It’s creepy.  : characters become unnaturally “fast friends,” which plays somewhat awkward. Indeed, it is sometimes loveably clumsy, moreso to modern audiences who may expect more nuance. But rest assured, it will pay off. As was standard, FFVI uses a traditional turn-based combat system. For many, this is a turn-off; for others, it is a highlight. Despite the discontinued design, FFVI should be commended for how differently each character plays.All characters do something in combat that others cannot. This means balancing issues may occur as clear “better” characters emerge. However, I think this imbalance is intentional, or a happy accident, because the story separates the characters so often by beats and geography that you’re rarely not obliged to use a character you’d probably have passed on otherwise. The game’s not interested in letting you off the hook that way. If it features a playable character, it makes use of them. At least for a bit.This pixel remaster enhances the game’s visual and auditory experience, bringing its timeless aesthetic to new heights. With beautiful sprites and a remastered soundtrack, you're allowed to rediscover the world of “Balance” and “Ruin” in stunning detail. For returning players, the nostalgia is overwhelming for the senses. I could have cried during  opera scene. The PR is also equipped with an OST player.And even if these “changes” aren’t for you, this version allows you to opt for the original aesthetic. It’s your choice.As a historical RPG milestone, FFVI has, for generations, enthralled players. Its legacy is a testament to the power of video games as a medium for storytelling and artistic expression. And its sheer influence (even within its titular series) may be felt in the countless games that have followed in its wake.  From the bustling streets of the city of Narshe to the wasteland of the World of Ruin, each location emotes detail and atmosphere even for a new player in 2024. And if you remain unmoved by the visuals, the score also works on you—Terra’s theme in particular oozes artistic romanticism. And make no mistake about it, FFVI is nothing if not romantic (again, in the artistic sense). There’s a verisimilitude to all its bells and whistles that invites players to traverse every corner and uncover its secrets. You join the world. The experience feels participatory. A true quest.While the main storyline follows a linear progression, the game includes many optional quests and hidden challenges that offer a welcomed diversion from the main narrative, allowing players to uncover new secrets and unlock (occasionally overpowered) abilities. In particular, FFVI’s endgame teems with non-linearity and additional adventuring, providing players a supplementary opportunity for exploration and discovery.I must venture a mechanical criticism/warning here: over-leveling all your characters in the endgame may, and most likely will, trivialize the final dungeon. This is obviously not unique to FFVI, but it is a warning for completionists—reaching for all those achievements will absolutely break the endgame. No amount of Kefka’s evil posturing and self-aggrandizing can stop you. FFVI continues to enthrall and unite players across generations. It is an all-timer for the older among us, and—at a minimum—a great RPG for everyone else.Kefka asks, “Why do you build, knowing destruction is inevitable? Why do you yearn to live, knowing all things must die?” Play the game. Discover the answer.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy VI PR is the finest version of this classic. For any newcomers, I would recommend this version to be the one to try if you are interested in trying this SNES classic. This could be said for all the other remastered ports of this series. The only negative I would say (it is really nitpicking) is how it is missing the GBA/PSP extras. This includes the dungeon and extra Magicite.The gameplay is intuitive and easy to learn. The turn-based combat is still engaging and the difficulty was increased just a tad that caught me by surprise. Controls are as basic as they come so there is no learning curve there. The pixel graphics are gorgeous in this version and the sound design cannot be matched. This is Final Fantasy VI at its finest. You can tell they used the Octopath style HD pixel art for specific scenes in the game which is a nice touch, but makes you wonder why they didn't use the style for the whole game. All in all, if you are a fan or a newcomer, this port of one the best in the Final Fantasy series is the best version. Nuff said.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, FFVI is one of the greatest rpg's of all time. And this remake contains the story and adds some nice battle animations. _childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy VI is still a personal favorite, and one I go through again every once in a while as easily as a good book or movie - and considering it's 25-50 hours per play (First serous play was 80 back when I was learning pre-online guides), that's saying a lot.As for this version... Cons:-The combination of old and new graphics are jarring, and breaks the flow somewhat.-Some animations (Especially running) are kind of janky.-Usual bugs from a computer port.  Save a bit more often than on console versions.  Rare, but a possibility of just crashing out.  It's very stable from a modern computer standard, but not console levels (Then again, nothing is as stable as a cartridge console).-Longer load times (Nothing compared to the PSX version, but more than others.  This was on a decent comp with an SSD, so I had the minimum possible time.).-Small removals of content (Mostly due to ratings issues, but purists will definitely notice).-On a purely mechanical level it's on the lower end of covers of Final Fantasy VI.Mileage may vary:-More difficult than the original by a small margin.  Expect physical attacks to miss far more often (Mostly due to evade bug fixes, but still much more common than the GBA version where the fix was introduced).  As VI was one of the easiest Final Fantasies, it's not as harsh as it sounds.Positives:-The soundtrack is worthy of the original.  Since that turned SNES chiptunes into a literal opera, that's saying a lot.-New translation (How much is translation and how much is modernized I don't quite know) is excellent.  Characters have more defined aspects.  Celes in particular has a stronger arc, but all are easier to follow.  Mind, Woolsey was working on a frankly impossible schedule and pulled a miracle, but the time they gave this shows.-The opera house scene.  They absolutely did it justice and even improved it. Could do without additional quicktime events and pseudo-3D, but modern day and all that.-Rebalanced espers (Really they only added a stat to one)  allows all stats without holding out on something the next room over (Not spoiling it).-It's Final Fantasy VI.  There's never been an outright bad version.It may not be the absolute top of your lists, but if you need a copy of FFVI, haven't played it before, or just want to try another version, it's worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great remaster and the quality shows! Another neat feature would be to have the original soundtracks for these games that you could switch on/off to relive the old days.  I was apprehensive about vocals being added to the opera scene but I was pleasantly surprise and happy they were included!As I have now thoroughly completed all the pixel remaster games I can say without a doubt they are my favorite versions and will act as a replacement when I wish to go back and replay these games in the future. _childDocuments_.review: One of the most open and non-linear Final Fantasy games, it gives you a lot of freedom to advance in your own way, in the order you want and how you want. It's a good thing, I consider it a virtue, but I don't see it as essential as many who criticize other games with more corridors or less open like FFX or FFXIII. This is because being so free has a downside, that having the possibily of having different characters formations, different story order and so creates a less profound story, blank spaces without a real drive and more generic dialogues, since it has to adapt to many diferent paths, instead of just the one that was studied deeper and taken much more care since it was the only option. This is also related with having 15 playable characters, on the one hand it is good in terms of different types of formations, using several teams in the same dungeon, but on the other hand many of them do not get to know each other well or develop too much.It has powerful moments narratively, but they do not have the audiovisual magic that later generations on PS1 or PS2 give. The places and the art are beautiful (one of the peaks of its time) but at the same time those environments do not manage to transmit as much as the graphic possibilities of later generations.The music has very good themes, but as a soundtrack as a whole I do not consider it one of the best in the saga.Final Battle is surely the best final boss in Final Fantasy, really epic battle, but that's it, there is no endgame content after it.The beginning of the golden era of Final Fantasy that ended with FFX included. 7'5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy VI was my first and favorite RPG game of all time.  I used to rent it multiple times from Hollywood Video for the Super Nintendo system when it was known as Final Fantasy III.  I enjoyed it because it had interesting characters, challenging bosses and the best music soundtrack.  I will always remember all the words sung in the opera scene.  Now after all of these years I can finally play my favorite Final Fantasy game with this Pixel Remaster version on PC.  Final Fantasy VI Pixel Remaster looks how I remembered it  with the exception of better looking backgrounds during battles and a few extra pixels adding extra colors for the main characters.  Game-play runs smoothly and is still challenging and seems a bit more balanced with less bugs.  The music has been upgraded to real instruments and voices and some of the tracks has a little extra bit to it which I thoroughly enjoyed.Of all the Final Fantasy Pixel Remaster games available I recommend playing this one because it captures my favorite things I love about this game.  It has a great story, characters, challenging combat and one of my favorite music soundtracks of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy 6 is a really important title. It has a huge amount of critical acclaim and is the last mainline Final Fantasy title to be in 2D before the playstation era takes over. As a result this is like a love song to the 2d style of play. And I have to say its a fantastic farewell.The music and visuals are the best looking out of all the 2D games. So many memorable tracks and moments that just stick with you. There is a really unique style where mechanical parts mix in with the classic final fantasy style buildings. That style carries itself along to create some incredible locations that are super fun to explore. The cutscenes feel much more emotional and there is a lot of optional stuff you can easily miss but feels super satisfying to find. Overall the presentation is just fantastic.The gameplay is fantastic. It still holds up really well even years later. It gives you a lot of freedom but doesn't take that level too far like FF 7 does with its Materia system. Characters still feel unique in battle and they all have specialized abilities that give you a preference in how you want to build that character. Battles feel fun and diverse and your choices throughout the game feel like they seriously matter in so many of these fights. Dungeons are the best they have been in the series and they are really well paced with a lot of fun rewards to find. My only problem is that each characters unique trait starts to matter less and less the longer the game goes, towards the end of the game I barely used the abilities of my characters because there were just stronger general abilities later in the game that all characters can use and those abilities feel much more powerful.The story is pretty great but it does feel like after about 50 % of the game it starts to slow down. At that point everything feels more open ended and the pacing feels a bit slower. I never felt bored or like the game dragged on, but the story at that point felt like it was fading into the background in favor of the exploration you get to do. Its the side stories of the characters that really gripped me, this is the first game in the FF series to put this much attention to all of its side characters. Its the main thing that differentiates all the cast even if they can't always do that in combat.The last thing I want to talk about is bugs. I didn't experience a lot of them but there are 2 weird things I felt I should talk about. The first is that every time you load a game there is like a 5 - 10 second window where I just couldn't move my character. I believe the game is loading but it feels weird how long that takes for such an old game. The 2nd thing I wanted to mention is that there is a character late in the game that bugged out when I was fighting the final boss. The character was berserked and for some reason the game just kept asking me to select a move for that character even though there are literally 0 choices that could be selected, due to this I was stuck for like 5 minutes fighting the final boss not being able to do anything.The weird bug aside the game is still fantastic and those bugs didn't detract from the fun I had throghout my journey. Even if this game is much longer then the other pixel remaster games, it still felt like the most fun. It feels like a mix of the best parts out of all the games up to this point and creates a super fun world to explore. I highly recommend FF 6 and put it as one of the best Final fantasy titles out there, a must play if you enjoy RPG's.

_childDocuments_.review: Does an inspiring job of reminding me why this was my all-time favorite game growing up.  The updates to the translation, music, and even minor tweaks to the old sprites, are completely welcome by me.  Not to mention all the quality of life improvements like walking diagonal, and auto-battle that (mostly) works.  Could have used a "Load" option from the pause menu, but I also get that save-scumming isn't really true to the spirit of the game.  Yeah, where the old sprites are recycled leaves them looking really outdated, but on the other hand, the completely unrestricted remaster of all the spells and special effects are incredible.  Made me want to hunt down every spell and get enemies attacking me, just to see what it would look like.  lol  And damn... that opera scene.  This is still one of the most passionate (and ballsy but I won't spoil more than that) Final Fantasy story-lines to date.  Easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY VI

_childDocuments_.review: The best version of a game I just can't stand.So there are some pros and cons:Pros:-The re-recorded, live performed soundtrack is great.-Cyan's combat moves are simply a button press in a menu now, meaning you won't be wasting time with waiting on his gauge to load before executing.-There are some small tweaks (equipping Relics has been made part of the general equipment menu rather than being its separate menu etc) that do help the game play just that bit more smoothly.Cons:-It's still Final Fantasy VI, beat for beat, missing the opportunity to improve on the original's flaws to any extent.-While the original game's graphics were murky and unappealing to look at, the Pixel Remaster went to the opposite extreme and brightened up the graphics to the point of nuclear green grass and the hideous World of Ruin overworld colours you can see on the Steam page.-The opera suite has been reinvigorated with live vocals and lyrics, but the final boss theme scraps lyrics that were present in previous live orchestral performances. That inconsistency isn't major, but it does bug me.-Screen scroll stutter is as obnoxiously present as ever.-The opening credits scene has no credits in it, which just looks weird.-AP grinding for Esper skills remains as tedious as ever, and autobattle doesn't really help reduce the tedium as much as it just reduces the length of battles a bit.All in all, the Pixel Remaster series is not one I would call the definitive versions of the classic Final Fantasy games.While there are some nice tweaks to the formula and some welcome updates in places, the screen scroll stutter that pervades all of these releases is just one of many symptoms of a lack of polish in this collection.Lack of cohesion, terrible font choices, none of these things are a gamebreaker on their own but it is suspicious that for such a high-profile release so many issues collide at the same time and so consistently.I will not knock the new versions of the soundtracks for these games because they are genuinely lovely, in my opinion.And I do have a lot of appreciation for the 2D remake of Final Fantasy III, which genuinely surprised me with how well it was done overall.But I've played PlayStation, Game Boy Advance, DS, PlayStation Portable remakes and even mobile versions of many of these old games and honestly?Those versions tended to iterate and build these games up further.This is halfway between an upgrade in terms of tweaks and updates and a total downgrade in how there was a reversion to just the base game.I really wonder if there was any cohesive artistic vision behind this Pixel Remaster project, because the final released product sure didn't feel like it had any.And it really sucks because these are likely gonna be the versions of these games we're gonna be stuck with for a long time, with no official access to older versions on any digital storefront.The mobile versions of Final Fantasy V and VI had issues, but the mobile version of V had some unique, awesome hand-drawn enemy sprites that none of the other versions did.That those versions had to make way for these Pixel Remasters is understandable to some extent, but it'd have been nice if people who bought them had a way to upgrade to the PRs for free or half off.Instead, they got trashed, forgotten about and ♥♥♥♥ the people who paid for them I guess.So if I have to rate Square Enix's stupid-ass conduct on top of this already flawed collection that I spent money on?♥♥♥♥ this. Just pirate the originals, ROM hack some bug fixes and tweaks into them if you want.It's better than wasting money on a corporation that can't even be arsed to give a development team a decent budget and time to rebuild one of its major flagship series.

_childDocuments_.review: A remake of one of if not the best Final Fantasy games from the main series.  It is not a perfect game, in that the Magicite system (introduced later), for the most part, encourages limited styles of play, and many of the hidden secrets of the game are a bit too well hidden if you don't want to do a lot of trial and error, or seek out a guide from friends or the internet (though that has you covered well if you don't mind such).  The gameplay is by no means bad though, but the job system of Final Fantasy V allows for a lot more variety for example, while Final Fantasy X goes back to a turn-based system and mostly does a better job of keeping the characters well defined (at least barring a lot of sphere grinding).  If you're looking at pure gameplay, there are better options, but there are definitely much worse ones as well.While later entries would have overall better combat and growth systems, at least in my view, this game makes up for in a number of points.  First of all is the story, which is easily the best story out of the main series, with almost every character having growth, development, or at least being likable... and not just the player characters but the NPCs around the world as well.  The choices you make can matter, albeit not to the extent of other RPGs like Chrono Cross.  And there are many moments that can bring a grown man to tears, or shout for joy.Alongside and complimenting the story is also the music, which is one of the best soundtracks out of all the titles, and the remastered music here does not at all disappoint.While grinding for experience, searching out secrets, etc. is largely optional in this game (and sometimes too obtuse) they are also highly rewarding both in terms of what you can find directly, and the potential impact or revelations you can discover for the story as well.  Plus, the Veldt, a prime spot for experience grinding, has a unique song track that is quite enjoyable if you ever feel the need to take advantage of it.  Even if you don't want to do such things, the story is still just as "complete" a package, for the most part, and the progression of the game is never too quick nor too slow for the pace you want to go at.This remake also does resolve some of the original bugs and glitches, making it "safer" to play with Relm's "Sketch" ability without glitching out your game as a prime example.  Visually it feels and looks exactly as it was promised to be, a finer-detailed version of the original game, though there are some other differences in presentation that players familiar with the old might enjoy discovering.  Certainly this is the best version of the game available for purchase on PC, and at a very reasonable price even without a sale (at least at time of writing).

_childDocuments_.review: FFVI just never can decide what it is.The fights are either tedious bullsh*t where the strategy is to know what the enemy is going to do so you can preemptively equip the right gear and queue up actions to account for the incoming instakill or cakewalks that you can cheese in three seconds.It's the one notorious for having "the best story" and "the best characters," but then throughout the second half of the game there is almost NO meaningful character interaction, and the cast is so massive that not even HALF of these characters get properly fleshed out.The developers specifically built up the Esper and Relics system so that almost anyone could be almost anything and players could always keep their favorite characters in the party, but then they give characters unique gear and abilities that only they can use and certain characters are still clearly suboptimal for certain situations.The world is supposed to feel more lived in and alive than ever before, but then there's a ton of recycled dialogue that's more designed to tell you what to do than to make the setting feel immersive.To state the obvious, FFVI is one of my least favorite Final Fantasy games.I'm also going to say that the Pixel Remaster makes the early game a huuuuuuuuuge mess. Combat is set to Wait mode by default, and this setting breaks abilities such as Celes' Runic. Enemy encounters are tweaked so that they use special abilities more often, so sections like the Lethe River where you have to keep Banon alive or instantly lose become a matter of chance (there is a common encounter here with an enemy that can one-shot him with Fireball, and even if you level him to the point where he can survive it, it's also possible to encounter two of this enemy, and you can't change his gear or do anything to counteract this besides either overlevel before you even recruit him or simply keep retrying the section until you get lucky and this doesn't happen). There were some really good things going on here. The concept (if not the execution) of the second act was groundbreaking. Figuring out different builds for your party members towards the end of the game can be very, very fun. Forming three parties to take on three different paths in the final dungeon and forcing everyone to contribute a little something is awesome; if only we didn't have to leave behind two of them (the bonus characters who have a total of about five spoken lines between the two of them were an obvious choice on principle).I know some people will say FFVI was a product of its time and so it deserves a little leeway, but I have a hard time doing that when it's coming after FFV, in my humble opinion a nearly perfect game. After six titles, I just can't excuse making the same mistakes that had been pointed out as far back as FFII. There's a reason every single person who adores this game talks about the characters, story, and music. It's because FFVI as a GAME is kind of a stinker.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended. I considered FF6 to be my favorite game of all time.  Growing up I played through it a dozen times at least.  This is the first time I've played it through in probably 15 years.   I can no longer call this a favorite game of all time though 2022 eyes.  There are too many questionable design choices, silly story choices and just a lack of character development.  That said...this game as an overall package is still excellent.  I think the sound track is an absolute masterpiece and overwhelmingly carries this game.  Its probably still to this day my favorite soundtrack ever.  The game is loaded with memorable moments as well.  It was a lot of fun to play through but as I replay these FF games I don't think it'll end up topping that list for me any more either.  I won't know that for sure until I revisit them all.7.5/10 Recommended. I think anyone who knows about this game understands its strong points.  I'll detail a bit why I scored it the way it did beyond what was already said about the character and story beats.  The mechanics in this game are a bit dated.  No shared XP is a big hit that nearly every game has corrected over time.  More to the point the Espers granting ability modifiers is a HUGE problem with this game.  If you have an ounce of min-max nature in you it'll take a lot of joy out of this experience.  The game promotes that you swap Espers when you master spells (which is fine and fun)...but also that you swap espers on level gain for every character...which is just an absolute mess of menu management that is not welcome.   I couldn't keep up with it and had a better time with the game once accepting that...but it didn't make the game more fun knowing there was a much better and vastly more rewarding way to enjoy this game. Add to that the fact to so few espers carry stat bonuses and that teams and gear sets are constantly changing seemingly every 30 minutes.  The flow of this game is completely at odds with its progression system.  I feel like this game would be an excellent choice for a true remaster.  Flesh out these characters.  Improve this menuing flow...the game has the potential to be my favorite game of all time again.  But as it stands its merely very good and worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This port is a disappointment.Let's get this out of the way, I will not be reviewing the game itself.  The game is already well known to be a classic, and has existed in multiple formats over nearly three decades.  It is a shining example of what JRPGs could be, and one of the masterpieces of the 16-bit generation.So how is this port?  Well, it's a lot better than the previous port on Steam at least.  But it is far from the definitive edition I would have hoped.  To start with, the game is riddled with bugs.  Even after the patch.  Some are game-breaking, such having encountered a soft lock in the Yeti fight.  Some are annoying, such as the "Slice" attacks, such as Odin, having multiple graphical errors.  Enemies stay on screen when slain, and in an edge case where it was used on my party members that were immune, they still had the animation go off and spent the rest of the combat invisible.  Relm's "Capture" attacks to not originate from the captured creature, but from Relm herself, which causes issues such as when the creature is killed after selecting which attack.  Many of the graphics from this are taken from the GBA port, and thus have their colors hyper-saturated and overly bright to compensate for the GBA's screen that had no lighting, and were not color corrected for this version.  Some of the colors of the characters are a bit off as well, Edgar's sprite in particular.  Most of the graphics are fine, in fact I like the improvement to Narshe's overworld entrance, though I dislike the adding of rocks around any cave door to highlight them.  The Opera scene is both greatly improved with the music, adding vocals to the tracks so we get the real singing, and the scene itself was rendered in the "HD-2D" style of Octopath Traveler.  However, I find the latter to be, while a nice look, a bit of a strike against being a "Pixel Remaster".  They removed the extra content from the GBA version, and yet altered that so drastically.Speaking of content being added or removed, not only is the extra dungeon gone (something I think would have been nice to add as an option for the players that want the "Advanced" version or not), but some features available in previous versions of the game.  I don't expect the CGI cut scenes from the PSX version to make a return, they haven't aged particularly well anyway, but that version included a list of Lores, where to get them, a list of the Espers and their effects, as well as a catalog of fights for the Colosseum, something that was a great improvement to allow you to see what you were going to get with the bet and who you would face.  Good extra features to supplement the Bestiary, however those are missing here.It also does not help that, at least as of yet, the extra options included in the console ports of the Pixel Remaster are not available on PC. [Edit: These have finally been added into this version of the game.  However, I have not played the game since to compare them.]So, yes, this is a disappointing port.  Square-Enix could have done much better.  But it's still a worthy version to play.  You'll likely encounter bugs, several of them.  And they very likely won't be fixed if they haven't been by now.  Squenix squeezed this one out the door, in my opinion incomplete, and have washed their hands of it.  But until something better comes along, this is the version to play.I'm glad I still have my GBA cart.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is a mixed/positive review. The game can be a drag to play through in the first half. It has not aged well. However, its 2nd half is a great game with great story telling.What this game has done well:1. The premise and world is probably the darkest out of all the FFs I have seen. Kefka, the villain is a victim himself of the warmongering ambitions of the dictator emperor. Mind control, war crimes, betrayal, slavery, experimentation of an entire species are all themes that are prevalent in FF6.2. FF6, with all its flaws, is worthy of an FF title unlike some of the really divisive titles after FFX with poor writing that accompanies terrible, simplistic, and forgettable themes.3. Music is dark and FF worthy.4. Many Characters means a large list of abilities to explore and play around.5. The theme of standing back up after a devastating event is relatable in modern day.6. The game accelerates and gets a lot better and more intense late game, despite its slow and boring start. 7. The art direction in the gallery is beautiful.What FF6 does poorly1. Slow pacing of early story - there is nothing really excitable in the series of events until the "banquet" event. 2. heavy grind (check out Gau Bible to see how much grind)3. Too many characters need to grind out skills base on enemy encounter and battles (lore, Dance) though the skills are pretty interesting. Too many characters (14 in total) need to level and gain AP. It feels grindy even with 4x boost. Though one may argue to use only a few of them, the game routine requires usage of some of the non-trained characters.4. Some of the characters have some of the worst designed skill kit in the entire FF universe (like Setzer who can cause instant death to his own party).5. The game basically only "begins" in the 2nd half.Overall, FF6 has very good themes and a good villain. The 2nd half of the game is particularly emotional with real consequences for certain characters depending on the player's actions then. However, the pacing and gameplay does not hold up to modern games that have improved on many aspects of gaming. Getting through the first half is a slog, but if one is able to reach the 2nd half, the game will be much more interesting and well worth the time invested.Hype almost killed this game, but I can fully understand why some would regard this as the best FF in the series. It is epic. It is beautiful. It is FF.For those who completed the game, don't forget the ps1 FMV:

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy VI has continued to be one of my favorite JRPGs, and replaying it has shown me why. The story, environment, and characters all merge together with classic gameplay to create a powerful narrative. While some parts have aged and certainly have their critiques, they are meager compared to the whole experience.Like Final Fantasy IV, Final Fantasy VI the ATB gauge determing when you can take your turn and having the active combat system. What makes the combat different are the differnet combat abilities each character has, whether it is Terra's trance, Locke's steal, Gau's rage, or more. This varies greatly from its predecessor, Final Fantasy V, which allows you to build any member of the party how you see fit. While this may be considered a weakness due to the lack of variety, it instead allows you to be more decisive on your party formation. Do you want to steal something with Locke? Do you want to use Sabin's blitz? Is there an ability that Strago can learn? All these add a layer of decision making that the player gets to make.However, not all character ability's are created equally. A common challenge in this game is to go to Veldt and get of all Gau's Rage abilities, which allow him to copy other enemies, but this is incredibly tedious and also requires you to understand what few Rage abilities you care about, and how to obtain them. Along with Strago's Lore, or Blue Mage ability, it becomes a chore to gather many of these abilities. Along with the two optional characters, Gogo and Umaro, who are mainly gimmicks for their specific abilities, you can see where the abilities can fall short. This especially true later in the game, where some abilities shine more than others. Despite this, its still nice to have that variety and be able to play with many of the characters throughout the game.Outside of abilities, there are also spells and stat increases characters can get through hold magicities, the last remains of an Esper's power. These spells and stats increases are gained through battles and leveling up, and is where most of the grinding occurs, trying to get enough Ability Points (AP) and Experience Points (EXP) learn spells and improve characters simultaneously. While it can be fun to plan out what abilities party members get at a specific time, and how to get them to learn it as quick as possible, it typically becomes a grind fest to bring all your partys at the same pace.Overall, the combat is fun and varied, and shines midway through the game in between the World of Light and World of Ruin, but by the end it is how many poeple do you need to cast Ultima or battle buffs. This isn't atypical for Final Fantasy, and can be varied through limiting what abilities you use or how much you grind, but it is fairly easy to learn and get these abilities late game. Combat is still and very entertaining, if less challenging by the end. 7/10The story, in my opinion, is where the game shines the most. From the opening shot and introduction of Terra, to the Returners and Banon, the intermingling conflict and war between nations and individuals, as wells as a final half that brings all the themes introduced in the first half to light. While there are some moments that can make a modern audience cringe or roll their eyes, I think they are few and far between.Almost all of the characters are well developed, some coming off as naive to world-traveled by journey's end. This can be seen with Terra's relearning of compassion and love, or Locke's growth, self-forgiveness, and new found relationships. I think Celes emphasizes this the most, being a traitor-general upon meeting, to having an ununsual part in an opera that would echo the rest of her ordeals and themes, that are similar in the ordeals that many others face.While Kefka is not the best Final Fantasy villain, I think he plays an interesting roles as this flat nihilist, . There are also several tidbits of information that allow the player to guess or assume parts of the world, as well as fan theories .I can not emphasize how much you should play this game just for the story alone. One of the best Final Fantasy stories in the main series. 9/10The music for this game is great, with several amazing songs that are a staple to not just Final Fantasy VI, but Final Fantasy in general. I could go into Kefka's theme as this constant reminder of the evil in the world, or Celes's theme focusing on given motifs, but I think you should look for the main theme as fantastic example. Not only is a great piece of music, with several motifs built within it, such as Terra's theme, but also gives us Omens, the first part of the main theme which shows how different this world is from past Final Fantasies, and giving us a glimpse into the war-torn landscape. It plays on the drama incredibly well and sets the tone fantastically. 8/10The 2D graphics are one of the best for the SNES, and the remaster cleans up the sprites and animations while keeping close to the original material. Also, the sprites and art as part of the game is amazing, especially many of the enemies and villains, ranging from the magitek armor in the first scene to the final battle .  8/10I love Final Fantasy VI, and after replaying it, I can say the remaster definitely holds its weight.  8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying this is my favorite game of all time.  So I may be biased.  However, I feel this allows me to be knowledgeable enough to successfully critique this version of the game.  With all that said, they've done a remarkable job with this remaster.  The graphics are clean, yet still harken back to the original sprites (and so much better than the previous remake attempt).  The controls are very responsive and game functions quick, so no load times like the old PS1 version.  This plays smoothly like the original SNES version.  A few minor changes are a bit annoying if you are used to the older mechanics (I'm personally not a fan of how they redid Sabin's Blitz, but I do like the improvement to Cyan's SwordTech aka Bushido).  The music...just wow.  They took what I think is the best OST of all Final Fantasies and made it even better.  I could write an entire length review just praising the music alone, so I will leave it at this.  The music is fantastic.  Overall, I highly recommend getting this version of the game for those who have played it before.  For those who haven't, I recommend it even more, as this is pure classic Final Fantasy at it's absolute peak.

_childDocuments_.review: i first played final fantasy 6 back on the PS1 when i was like, 6 or 7, something like that. could barely get past Mt Koltz when i was that young, if i got that far. like its younger brother FF7, this game has been with me for my whole life. and with the pixel remaster i have FINALLY finished it. what's really remarkable about FF6 by itself however, is just how ahead of its time it was. you compare this to a lot JRPGs today and it still blows them out of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ water. the expressive sprites, the fantastic music, the beautiful enemy and esper sprites, and the great characters. admittedly its characters are a little more simplistic than later games in the series, but when you have a cast of 16 characters i think what is produced is astounding. especially seeing as newer games with half the cast (octopath traveller lol) have even more barebones characters with worse writing. (side note, octopath traveller is the worst jrpg i have ever played.) i still kind of cant believe just how good FF6 really is. the entire world of balance is fantastic, it sprouts a huge and interesting world that feels interconnected and personal. i always loved the way Nikeah and South Figaro have a trading route between their ports, and I love that the towns on the outskirts of Vector have been colonised by the empire. there's a real understanding of the towns are neighbours to each other which only arguably FF4 had before it (and even then not to this degree). the flow of the story is great and its set pieces are brilliant. Sabin's route after the returner hideout is genuinely one of my favourite ever video game experiences, and i think the only thing wrong with it is that its not longer or got more to it lmao. it is a whole mini story by itself which is so impressive, and the phantom train is soooo gooood dude. phantom forest is a beautiful piece of music, and the very experience there is weird and fun and interesting, and totally unlike anything else i've ever seen in a game. the games comedic moments between sabin, cyan, and gau are whimsical and delightful. just think about when you recruit gau and have that whole shindig with him, a game like pokemon could NEVER even BEGIN to dream of that kind of stuff. and this game came out in freaking 1994 dude!!!!i wont go on about the entire world of balance but, needless to say, it is unabashadely fantastic. (the opera scene in the pixel remaster is also amazing, people have noted they wished the whole game was done in hd2d but to be honest i'm glad it wasnt. we've only got two games right now in that style and i'm already sick of it! plus FF6's art direction is part of its charm; i dont think it necessarily needs changing)on FF6's game design, i only realised for the first time THIS playthrough that the only way to get stat gains on a level up is to use specific espers on each characters. having come off the ass of FF8 with its weird stat gains i was a bit worried about this, but its simplicity does it favours here, and allows you to grind specific stats in a satisfying and noticable way. have the right espers on and levelling up twice makes you notably stronger. bueno nice or whatever!!!!FF6 is of course, not a perfect game however! there are pacing issues around the world of ruin time. in particular i think it does start with the world of balance, the way strago and relm join your team and then immediately leave it is a tad disappointing. like most JRPGs the later party member additions never feel like they have the weight the starting lot do, and FF6 suffers from this. the lack of story content in the world of ruin definitely is noticable as well, the difficulty spike and the lack of story hits this game hard but thankfully if you like it enough to get to the world of ruin, you'll probably see it through anyway. unlocking the ultima spell makes the game totally trivial too; it is ludicrously powerful, cant be dodged/reflected, and hits all enemies lmao. busted. next time i play i will be smashing up that esper into a sword instead.anyway, i love this game. i would probably write more but i have to go to work now. bye!

My only issue with this remaster is the censorship. They removed Celes's beating while under Imperial arrest in South Figaro.The Esper system: The one and only. _childDocuments_.review: Played this on an emulator a few years back as I was not born when the game came out. Out of every Final Fantasy I've played (I, IV, VII, XIII, XV), this is by far my most favorite one. Replaying this remaster not only evoked the same feelings in my first playthrough, but it spoke to me even further as a more jaded person compared to when I first played it.The story and characters are top-notch. Twelve out of the jaw-dropping fourteen characters all had arcs and moments that enforces the "no main character" rule of this game. Everyone had a chance to shine and cement their importance in the overall narrative.The music. God, the music. It was so, so, so much better in this remaster. I felt like I was a child again when the iconic moments from the game played with the updated music. I went through all the emotions I had all those years ago. Hearing a full orchestra successfully and respectfully translate 16-bit sound into a modern symphony was amazing. No words can completely describe my satisfaction with the music.The gameplay is what one would expect from an old-school Final Fantasy game. In my previous and current playthroughs, I overgrinded a bit too much but was still almost killed in the final dungeon a good few times. Overall, I felt this remaster was a bit harder compared to the original.The quality-of-life improvements really shine. They make the game less tedious to go through and allows one to immerse themselves in the story without much interruption.I am satisfied with this remaster, despite the exclusion of certain elements from the GBA/Mobile/Old Steam versions of the game. If you have not played this game, please do. Its narrative, characters, and music are arguably the best in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played every iteration of this game; from the SNES FF3 cart, to the Anthology, the GBA version, various ROMs, and this. I'm somewhat biased here, because I prefer the SNES cart as it was my first experience. That being said, I will try my best to give a fair assessment here. Quality of life enhancements are great. I also greatly appreciate the updated graphics and spell effects. They're done very well, and don't seem out of place for the tech used to make the game. So that's cool. A lot of (if not all of) the odd bugs are 'fixed'. MBlock% works, and all of the stats seem to work as intended. The side effect here is that a lot of battles seem a bit more difficult, as now without end-game gear, it's actually a bit more difficult to gear for full immunities. A lot of the name changes were a bit jarring for an old-schooler like me. I remember combinations like Gem Box and Economizer, and now have to remember new terms. Not a big deal, but I'm already old and useless. Haven't run into anything game-breaking at all, and I feel like the pixel remaster stays true to the original(s) without overstepping with fancy QoL improvements. My only two gripes. Sabin's Blitzes are a bit clunky. In the original, you select Blitz, do your Street Fighter input, and hit confirm. In this one, you select the blitz you want to use, and follow the same input they give you (more or less) but the detection is a bit clunky and you have to input it very slowly and deliberately. My other gripe is Strago's Lore magic used to have a unique casting animation and SFX. They took that away and made it look like white magic. Again, nothing game-breaking, but that was a minor annoyance. I picked this title up with the bundle of remasters and I absolutely see myself sinking 200 hours into the game easily. For nostalgia alone I'd recommend. If you've never played this title and love FF, you owe it to yourself to really dive into this one. For some folks, the first half of the story may not feel like it gets going quickly enough, but it's a great game. There is something for everyone here, and the character development is absolutely worth it.
