_childDocuments_.review: (Preliminary review) Graphics Section___________1. Character Sprites are brighter than the over-world and other backgrounds making them stand out too much. This ruins the original game ascetic of dark and dreary. 2. Graphics on the world map, character sprites and specifically doorways/doors are way too over-saturated with color. They stick out like sore thumbs and detract from the otherwise very nice non-world game maps, battle backgrounds, etc.3. The battle animations are very nice but slow at times on screen and are not synced up with their sounds correctly at times. 4. Most maps are nicely done and just about every battle background is nice looking and I'd say an improvement over the original.5. The character sprites are cartoon like and have actually less definition than the original SNES sprites which is very sad to see. They basically air-brushed the character sprites and in this title sticks out badly.6. The opening Mech crawl, an iconic scene, is very bad and isn't even the same night-time scene from the original. It is done very badly and has scrolling issues that ruin that part. Result for graphics: ZERO - so many bad choices that ruins the game experience for me and the good graphic portions don't make up for the terrible mistakes. Music and Sound ___________1. The music is poorly done. All the instruments in each song are one flat volume and seem to be competing at times for dominance. Real orchestrated music has the instruments change volume at times for emotional impact. The conductor is out to lunch or asleep. 2. The instrument choice in some songs are just plain wrong. Don't vacation in places with their own style of music and then try to adapt what they have perfected into your own. Stick with your own style. The original game music from the SNES version is actually better for most, not all, but most of these songs and that is saying something. The music also has horrible noise like sounds or off-beats that stick out at times in the music and sound like mistakes. 3. Sound effects are mostly very nice and true to the original game which is a nice touch. Some sounds are terrible, but most are actually a very nice improvement over the original. 4. Some sound effects do not sync up with the animation correctly. If the SNES version could do it so could this one.Music and Sound Result: ZERO - The sounds are actually great, but the music is so badly done compared to what is possible that it seems lazy and cash-grabbie. Music also is missing the bass and treble of natural sounding instruments and these instruments sound so fake. At least the original music made me feel like the music was orchestrated and that is saying something. Gameplay _______1. The game does play like the original and has the same mistakes in battles so far. I am not counting exploits at this time. 2. There are serious scrolling issues everywhere in this game. If an SNES can scroll a game better than today's tech than that is saying a ton. 3. The fight where Sabin is introduced is an epic fail. If you use the pummel move first you get a message about having to do the same move and have to execute that move a SECOND TIME to get the battle finished. This is a failure to TEST your games. 4. The opera house scene is trying to imitate another game with this simulated 3-d to 2-d mashup that looks terrible and causes this game to have an identity crisis. Be your own game and try not to rip-off other titles. 5. They actually "fixed" the invisibility and death or x-zone spell combo. However, they did not manage to change the wording in-game from the beginners house that tells you all spells are guaranteed to hit on invisible monsters/characters.  Gameplay Result: ZERO - Scrolling issues, battle issues, crashing when entering the auction house at times, battles that were never tested out.Story ____1. The original story was a real work of art. This story re-working or re-imagining, however you want to put it, is bad. Imagine taking a Shakespear play and taking random lines and reworking them to fit today's slang. It would be just plain awful and ruins this game. Now some new lines are nice I will say that, but they are too far few and in-between. 2. The story actually TELLS YOU what is going to happen next. The surprise of the original is lost. The scene in the beginning of Edgar's Castle and just before sinking into the sand and then a Sandworm reference instead of a sub-mariner joke. LAME!3. A few lines are nice that were changed, but most of the story is badly re-written and just plain terrible. Someone with no degree in creative writing clearly wrote these re-writes. Story Result: ZERO - A childish rewrite that most people could do better on. This lazy hack of a story rewrite makes the original story much better, mistakes there and all. The original story was re-written to English to fit the smaller cartridge size. Japanese Kanji can tell a lot more in a smaller space than English can. The SNES re-write was much better since it did away with unnecessary and superfluous language. A simpler message is more powerful than an over-explained one. Attempt at being true to the original game ____________________________A poor lazy attempt and improving a classic game. Some of the graphics are very very nice and other are just plain silly and childish.The music is a total waste as any intern could have done better. The musician has no idea of what an orchestra is and has never even seen a play let alone studied one seriously for the music and the story writing. The gameplay works, but has issues. Attempt at being true to the original game Result: ZERO - Sure it looks similar and sounds similar, but if I wanted to go back and play this I'd just play the SNES or PS1 version as they are better is so many ways. FINAL RESULT: ZERO -A shameless cash grab by a company that took so little time to actually make a classic better that they actually made it worse. A true artist NEVER listens to the crowd. Artists are unique for following their own path and this game failed ironically with the octo-path traveler nonsense and so many poor artistic choices - like hey lets just be different, just to be different. ____________________________Small side note: The opera scene was crap, even in the original and I always muted it. Now I mute it even harder... LOL

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy VI is only listed as playable according to Steam on Steam Deck, but I haven't had any problems. This is probably one of the best games released for the SNES when it first came out. Unfortunately, it never made it to Europe, and it took me a while to play through it, but it is a fantastic game.The story is gripping, and if you explore the world well while playing, you will quickly exceed 50 hours of playing time. Of the games included in Pixel Remaster, this title is the one I like the most. At the same time, it is probably the one that received the most minor changes in terms of graphics. I hope the game gets a 2D HD remake in the visual style that Octopath Traveler has, which has become popular with fans of Square Enix games. Here they have only used it for the opera scene, but it mostly feels like an appetizer for what it could have been. But probably, the price would have been significantly higher, and it feels as if the remake of Dragon Quest 3 is a bit of an experiment for the company to see how big the interest is, which may not feel entirely fair as it is not a series that is as popular in the west as in Japan.But if you're prepared that this is just a port made primarily for mobile phones, it's still the best version you can play (the port made for mobiles before looked terrible, on the other hand). Also, unlike several previous titles, Final Fantasy doesn't have some extra material on previous releases that are missing here (apart from the credits in the game's opening), perhaps most evident in the previous games.Extra praise for the game's soundtrack, which now sounds fantastic and has been entirely re-arranged and gives new life to the music. If you belong to those who are more old school gamers, the original music is included as an option.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic and belongs in the library of any STG lover or anyone remotely interested in the genre. The balance between novelty in innovation, and familiarity in classic STG design, in this game is impeccable. There's something in here for almost everyone, so this game is highly recommended for beginners and veterans alike.+ Innovative and clever design+ Outstanding graphics and music+ Many options for customization+ Fun and interesting stages and bosses+ Highly suited for STG newcomers, without mitigating the experience for veterans!This game is a massive step in the right direction for STGs. One of my main concerns about STGs is that they rely too heavily on following a design philosophy that stems from the arcade era, which is now long gone. I personally do not mind that, but it makes STGs as a genre much harder to sell to people outside the niche, and it leaves very little room for innovation. To an outsider, every STG looks more or less the same. You shoot and you dodge. This is why I am extremely excited about Qute's approach to STG design. They are very keen on innovating on the format and try to challenge some of classical tropes of STGs. Instead of playing the entire game all in one go with very limited resources, the Story Mode lets play each stage individually, as well as choosing your loadout before entering the stage. Now many oldskool/hardcore STG fans will think this is very out of the line, so thankfully, there is also an Arcade Mode which lets you play every stage in succession, making sure as many people as possible are pleased. All in all, it's very refreshing to see a STG that is specifically designed around console/PC gameplay and exploits that fact, in the same sense that arcade STGs had to exploit the fact that they were on arcade platforms.All the customization options for equipping your ship, combined with the experience points you get on the Stage Experience Level gauge and your own Player Level gauge, are amazing tools to get you hooked and to make sure you stay motivated to continue pushing forward. Even if you die at the very start of the stage, you get more currency every time you play which you can use to purchase and upgrade your ship in order to get the perfect loadout in order to beat the stage and its boss. It might seem like you're purchasing yourself to victory, but the truth is that it's just masking the boring practice, as you get better and more familiar with the stage every single time you play. Even if you go in with extra shields, you'll end up getting hit less often for every time you play. It's quite clever.Adding bullet trajectory lines as a new age Quality of Life feature is great, even if some people find it to be quite distracting. It's a great tool for newcomers who are not used to predicting bullet trajectory, and people looking to memorize specific bullet patterns. Being able to see enable a spawn marker for enemies is also quite helpful. Normally in other STGs, you only see these sorts of markers when enemies will spawn behind the player, but not anywhere else. These sorts of QoL features is something I feel has barely been experimented with in most STGs. Most of the QoL features we want in STGs are usually derived from emulation (i.e. save states, replays), rather than something inherent to the games themselves (i.e. hitbox marker). I think this game could've done with some more QoL features, like hitbox marker and quick restart for stages, but it's nothing that bothered me much.The game looks stunning and is likely the single most prettiest STG I have seen, especially with 3D graphics. That's not to say there aren't other beautiful looking STGs, but this game is able to stay extremely vibrant with detailed landscapes in the stages without mitigating the gameplay or bullet visibility. One big issue I have with many shmups is that stages often feel weirdly flat (due to forced perspective) or the stages end up feeling a bit anonymous, as if they're not a real place one could visit.The music is also extremely rad. I really love the "modern retro" FM sound that Yousuke Yasui has in his works. Not to mention Kobayashi's great sound too!In conclusion, I think this game is the closest we have ever gotten to a high quality AAA-tier shooting game. The game does its best to provide stepping stones for people who have never played a STG before in their, while also providing an intense experience for veteran players. The game innovates by being designed from the ground up for home consoles and PC, instead of blindly following design sensibilities of the arcade era. The game looks very attractive, feels excellent to play, and has a lot of ways to keep you very hooked. I love this game, and hope you do too!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really accessible SHMUP that you can just sit down with and have fun. It builds upon the mechanics in Ginga Force, but makes them better in my opinion. Weapon combinations and upgrades make sense and you can unlock them with fair progression.The menu and interface in this game is also a real pleasure to use. All the menus are accessible using a controller only and the level select lets you switch between difficulties by moving up and down the tree for each stage. Just one screen and one menu to do it all: great work!The game narration is only in Japanese, but there are English subs. _childDocuments_.review: I'm normally not one for horizontal shmups, vertical danmaku is my territory and what I'm good at, but natsuki chronicles is an absolutely excellent shmup, and one that makes me willing to come out of my comfort zonethere's one thing I wanna emphasise: accessibility. being able to set any movespeed in either movespeed slot and select toggle or hold (plus having full analog control for those on controller, not me, I play on arcade stick) is something almost unheard of in the genre and it makes certain you can find a configuration that is comfortable for you. this is what ginga force was most sorely missing, alongside a robust arcade mode, which natsuki chronicles also has. the game also has proper support for high refresh rates and isn't 60fps-locked like most shmups, though attempting to cap its framerate even with external tools proves problematic, making it run at a toasty average of 700 frames per second on my machine, but this is a relatively minor issue as fullscreen + vsync locks to your display refresh rate properly (unlike windowed). especially with how fast bullets start moving on extreme difficulty, high refresh rate is a major aid in visual clarity in this game, and it's an absolute treat to be playing a shmup that runs that smoothdon't expect a particularly thrilling story, it's fairly barebones, and in my opinion while the core lives system is great, the ex shield system is a little clumsy for story mode, and I feel there should've been a way included to practice smaller sections of the game at a time (at least the stages aren't AS long as ginga force's)DO expect very interesting stage design, the smoothest controls, a robust arcade mode, very interesting special weapon mechanics, amazing OST and fantastic visuals9/10, even if not entirely my usual cup of tea, undeniably one of the best shmups from the past decadealso bullet lines are kinda neat even if I ignore em 99% of the time

_childDocuments_.review: This is a shmup modernization done right. It's hard to move the genre forward without compromising the purity of the experience. This game offers a traditional Arcade mode which is very good, and a story mode with some light RPG elements, but without overburdening the core mechanics. Weapon loadouts and buying new weapons before each mission for example.Another great innovation is the bullet trails and enemy formation warnings. This reduces the "trial and error" aspect of many horizontal shmups like R-Type and Gradius.Only downside is that the art style feels a bit generic. I'd rather have a well drawn pixel art game.

_childDocuments_.review: Natsuki Chronicles is a prequel/side-story to Ginga Force that involves one of the boss characters you encountered in the first game. It plays almost the same as Ginga Force - you still grind for improvements and weapons in the story mode and you need to be able to destroy all the enemies that comes in formations to improve your scoring when climbing up the leaderboards - but you do so with a side-scroller perspective instead of the top down view. Just like Ginga Force however, the story is really nothing special but it's cool that a lot of character interactions happened during the stages themselves as you are playing the game. Qute has finally provided us with a real arcade mode for this game where you don't have to keep going back to the stage select screen - in this mode, you just play through the entirety of the game, which is something sorely missing in Ginga Force (Qute, please add this to Ginga Force, it's not too late!). With nonstop action, cool bosses, a ridiculously epic final boss, and awesome soundtrack (complete with a sweet remix of Gallant Gunshot, the best music in Ginga Force), this is without a doubt, the best shmup released on Steam this year. It's also my nominee for Steam's 2021 Game of the Year Award!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun side-scroll shooting game. The 3d graphics are well done and the background environments are cool. There is an traditional arcade mode and a story mode where you can play each stage multiple times and unlock weapon options over time.

_childDocuments_.review: Really great shmup. Various difficulty settings to assist people new to the genre, along with very intuitive enemy approaching indicators and bullet trajectory lines to help you visualize where is safe in a pattern. Your ship has a 3 "shield" regenerating lives system. If you can clutch it out through a pattern, you get more chances than in a traditional shmup. Dying many times and failing will still contribute score for level study, higher levels unlock additional EX lives that do not regen so that you can brute force through and get many additional chances.Customizing ship parts can help you change your ship to suit the situation. Certain weapon types can trivialize very difficult sections so it's good to experiment. If you are a homing type fan, power hitter, precision or wide shot player, etc. it's all represented here and all feel balanced enough to work.The music is phenomenal, I'm a huge fan of Yousuke Yasui's tracks. They're always perfect for these types of games and fun to listen to.Visuals are decent, not a ton going on but the enemies are distinct enough and when things get hectic in the later levels it's an impressive light show to maneuver through. Customizing your parts changes your ship visually too which is a nice touch.The story intersects with Ginga Force, it's nothing to write home about but is a serviceable backdrop to give you reason to go all the locales. "Police pilot realizes the system is corrupt after brutally killing environmental and human rights protesters without thinking about the consequences then comes to her senses" sums it up. (Uh oh, political)tl;dr if you like Eschatos or Ginga Force you will probably like Natsuki Chronicles, too.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing ! It reminds me of U.N. Squadron for the SNES also known as Area 88 in Japan, which is  one of my all time favorite horizontal shooters . I use this comparison due to the fact that you can upgrade your weaponry , although I wish that changing planes was also an option . The game play is truly the star of the show , the controls are precise ,the graphics are great and the boss battles are extremely challenging . If your having difficulty completing a level , level up your weapons and additional shields are awarded to make the battle more manageable .  I would highly recommend this game to anyone is a fan of the horizontal shooter genre of games .

_childDocuments_.review: Natsuki Chronicles a very good shmup but it doesn't feel as good to play as Ginga Force for various reasons. The ship feels much more fragile because the shield is much weaker and the player hit box is larger. As a result the patterns can't be as crazy as they were in Ginga Force without feeling somewhat unfair. Later in the game the patterns do get really crazy and it does feel a little unfair. This difficulty can be offset a bit by the bullet line prediction feature but I think this feature caused the devs to change their mindset a bit when designing patterns since they expected people to rely on the new systems.On the positive side, both the the weapon and health systems have been greatly improved. The weapons no longer rely on the strange ammo bars from Ginga Force. There is no ammo but firing both weapons at the same time reduce both of their power giving the player a real reason to fire one weapon at a time for some situations. The health system is more forgiving and allows for comebacks. When the player is below 3 shields they slowly regenerate shield over time, meaning as long as the player can dodge successfully for a little while they can go from near death back to safety.I'm was a little disappointed by this game after experiencing the masterpiece that is Ginga Force but it's still a fun and interesting shmup with plenty of exciting patterns and interesting systems.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Tyrian created a Gradius game. That’s basically this game in a nutshell, and it’s done fantastically! The gameplay is frantic, yet satisfyingly challenging, has a great leveling system and controls, a difficulty curve that’s mostly correct and a good number of options to chose from. The music, graphics and overall presentation is clean, bright, riveting and everything else you expect from a Japanese video/arcade game from the early-to-mid 2000s, but modernized.Like Tyrian, you can save your progress, purchase and customize your loadout from a plethora of weapons before you head out on the mission and, the most important thing of all (and to quote Ross’s Game Dungeon),  That’s right, your ship is equipped with a shield system that recharges over time and the game gives you the option to add additional, albeit non-rechargeable, shields when you level up your “Stage Study level” of the stage you’re tackling on. Not bad for improving yourself on a particular mission! Of course, that doesn’t stop this game from gradually getting harder in a near-bullet-hell style in the later missions, even on easy mode. Fortunately, you are also equipped with sidekicks that act as additional shields against most enemy shots (which can also be purchased (or this case, programmed) as various forms of defense, attack and guided version), and you can turn on bullet trajectory on the gameplay settings so you can plan out your movements a lot better while focusing on your target more! And like in both games, you do need to be aware of the in-game collision in this game, something the bullet trajectory option doesn't showcase for obvious reasons. .If there’s any downsides to this game, the overall storyline is a type of shonen anime plot that’s trying too hard at best and incomplete at worst. Tyrian’s plot can be just as wacky in combination of its sometimes serious moments, but at least it’s complete and you are able to read it in between missions. That’s way better than trying to read and shoot at the same time, which is a huge no-no in concentration unless you love multitasking.Anyways, there’s also an arcade mode if you like the classic style of taking on the game and the high score junkies out there will have a field day breaking those online leaderboards. Unlocking more credits for this mode is a huge plus as well!Overall, along with Raging Blasters, this is a great Shoot-em-up to add to you own arsenal, even better when it’s on sale! Now when is Tyrian coming to Steam so I can try it out more? DX

_childDocuments_.review: Revisiting the game. It's been a year and a half since I played. Yeah, game still sux beyond Easy Mode. Heck, even Easy Mode for a casual is going to be bonkers. Level difficulty is just all over the place. The game absolutely requires multiple failures to gain more lives so you can eventually beat the level. The hitbox is too big for the amount and size of bullets.The shields respond way too slow. You know how at the last millisecond you can drop a bomb to save ur on literally every shmup, well, here they got rid of anything useful  from Ginga Force, and they give you a shield that must be activated helf-a-second before being hit otherwise the bullet goes thru the shield, and you take a hit.On Extreme, warning lasers drain an entire hit point even tho it is not a full laser blast. In previous difficulties and literally, every other shooter, a warning laser animations doesn't do damage. Here it does, and there's no warning for the warning laser animation (i mean obviously its the warning for a laser in the other difficulties). And it is always in prime attack vicinity so uber cheap. It is a super slime red line, and it takes an entire hit point. Stupid.Way too many battles that require attacking from the rear. This isn't like r-type attacking with an enemy here and there, this is like entire fights from behind the ship and the rear weapons just aren't that powerful.The grind for all achievements (includes buying every weapon) is just beyond absurd b/c there are just so many levels for each weapon, and the money awards (outside of grinding the ending boss on Hard or Extreme) is pitiful. Some weapons you would have to beat a level 30 times for one new weapon or beat the final boss 8 times. This is basically like Ginga Force in this regard, but in Ginga Force purchasing EVERY SINGLE WEAPON is not an achievement requirement.If you care: Here are my original reviews...The game is fine, and I will play it a bit more, but it would have been nice to have an English dub b/c while do-able to read the story on Easy mode during battles, it is not preferred. 2/3rds of the story is the character saying, "I can't believe RDF, my elite killing squad, kills criminals. Would Maraget have been okay with this?" Like how do you go to an academy for 4 years to become a pilot, and you don't have any idea that this is the type of work you'd be carrying out. I mean I get what they were trying to write but it's def not pulled off. Weapon customization. Biggggg let down after just playing Jets'n'Guns Gold. It's advertised as having hundreds of options lol, yeah, okay. Big lie there. There's like 25 weapons you can upgrade, and half or more are worthless.I wish the developers would have decided if the green shield and green shooty shield were going to dissolve bullets or not. It's like it dissolves some bullets but not all? When there are 3 different types of bullets getting mixed into a slurry soup, it would be nice to just have them all go away; rather than, dissolving blue ones this time and leaving the pink and purple, and then next level the pink and purple bullets get dissolved but the blue bullets don't. Next, crit is the UI.  Man, I hate having to click  "a" on a 100  pop-ups every time I beat a level in Story Mode. Shoulda lumped some of that info all together. There is a Bullet trajectory/projection option. It's an Interesting idea until you put red bullets on top of red projections and you also have the occasional red laser. There have been a few occasions were I'm at a loss at what jacked my ship, then I redo the boss or whoever, and I realize, "Oh, that wasn't a red line projection that was actually a laser being fired." So I turned off that option.Alright, positives... good looking foregrounds. Nice and smooth, plays at 144hz. Ship flies well. Level design is breezy for the most part though I did have to play a couple bosses multiple times (mostly due to hard to discern bullet trajectory vs  lasers and bullet trajectories hiding red bullets).::edits:: GEeezzus, this is a hard game on Normal for a casual , but looooong-time shmuper. Heck, even a few parts of Easy mode are difficult. Most of it boils down to the limited movement options available if you do not memorize when and where an implementable laser will fire that you can not dodge. Story. Duddddeee. I want a story in a shmup. This one claimed to have a story. BullCrapolo! You even told me after beating it on Easy to beat it on Normal to get the TRUE ENDING. What a FREAKING CHAD MOVEEEEEE. Yeah, you dropped one line about losing hope, and you added a sunset background rather than a night time background. And I had to grind like 2-3hrs for this. BAck to the graphics. Yeah, it runs in 144hz , 60fps, 2k, but everything is low-poly design so I mean I like but it's not like Daaaayummm.Arcade Mode: ...so many symbols. Are special weapon limited use? They keep dying on me or maybe when I take a hit I lose them? Confusion looms. Also, the player ship needs to shut-off Collision when taking a hit or running into walls. On Stage 4, I got stuck behind a dropping door for the first time. There were 5 more doors after it. My ship could not pass through the closed doors. I lost 4 hit bars in 2-3 seconds lol.If the difficulty wasn't such a donkleberry, then I'd recommend despite all of it's flaws, and yeah, maybe on a deeper sale under $10 I would recommend, but there's just too many lies in the marketing and description about what this game is.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I originally got this game through being interested in horizontal shmups and Qute-style shmups. After completing it, I'm not sure I'd recommend it for others in the same position. At least it ran totally fine on Steam Deck.I'd categorise this game as "hard, but forgiving". Now, what does that mean?The game is hard. Bullets are numerous, quick, and chaotic, especially at higher difficulties (Not in a bullet-hell way, but in a classic shmup way). The difficulty itself may seesaw between stages, and may vary depending on your choice of weaponry. Enemies may appear from unexpected angles, such as dropping on you, advancing from behind, or hiding behind stage obstacles. There are some very strange design decisions, such as a survival stage where you get a heavily-armoured ship and are expected to survive a barrage of bullets, but it feels more like a waste of time as you have too many shields to care.These issues are especially evident in the Arcade Mode, where you go through all the main stages in order, where you can't deterministically pick your loadout, and are instead beholden to power-up RNG.However, the game is also pretty forgiving. By default, you have a set of 3 rechargeable shields, which already makes the base experience much easier for newcomers. During your regular playthrough, each stage and difficulty has a separate level which you gain experience through playing it. Higher levels give additional layers of shields which don't recharge.The Arcade Mode gives additional Continues each time you fail, but power-ups also give layers of shields. If you lose the shield, you lose the respective power-up too.The game also features a variety of weapons and defensive options. Unfortunately, many of them are direct upgrades of lower ones, which are unlocked through grinding stages. It felt like this game had the opposite problem of Ginga Force in that department, where in that game weapons are only unlocked by clearing higher difficulty stages.Finally, this game features an option to enable bullet trails, either for the more powerful shots or for all shots. Ostensibly this is meant for newer players, but I'm not sure how effective it ended up being for me. Many times even the lesser option felt overwhelming, and didn't really help me in dodging them. Thankfully, you can turn it off completely if you prefer, and for the vast majority of my time with this game I did so.Overall, if you are interested, I'd say to wait for the occasional Seventia bundle sale, where both this game and Ginga Force are discounted to a couple bucks together. It's not quite for me, but it might be for some.If I could give a mixed recommendation I would, but I think the drawbacks aren't too numerous, so I'm still recommending it.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Natsuki Chronicles, which is at first glance a more polished and streamlined follow-up to Ginga Force, is overall a letdown for me. It's a good game still, but has none of the ambition and charm that made Ginga Force so special. The story is abysmal instead of cheesy, the stages have lost the unique personalities that made them stand out, and the difficulty is all over the place. All the characters are so bland compared to the bubbly and energetic cast seen before. The UI looks and feels more polished on first glance but has regressed in so many ways:Complaining aside, I still love Qute as a developer and hope they keep creating more. This game is good too - it's just that it's regressed more than progressed from Ginga Force.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: "This is a great shmup with great story, lots of weapons, innovative, and great for newcommers"What great story? I hate Natsuki's whiny victim mentality, that "wah wah I don't want to kill people but my boss told me to". Have fun listening lame chatters while playing meh shmup.Lots of weapon, yeah, none of them fun to use. You need to experiment a lot using which weapon for a certain stage and it's boss. What's good for the stage, doesn't mean good for beating the boss. You think the locked weapon is good because of the weapon preview? Tough luck, after grinding for the money, it's sucks not as good as you think. Rinse and repeat.What's the new innovation for this game, huh? Configurable ship's speed but with analog movement? That's an unbelievably dumb idea. Good luck trying to move straight line using analog stick.Good for newcomers? Which feature is that that doesn't exist on other shmup? Each time you died in a certain stage, you will get an additional shield. Is that a really beginner friendly mechanics? What's the difference with unlimited continue? Bullet trajectory is more of a visual annoyance instead of being helpful.This game really pissed me off, because of the unnecessary abundance of customization, this game doesn't have a clear identity. This game asked you to tackle each stage however you want, but doesn't give you some feature to experiment with your ship's equipment. I wish there's rewind feature or change weapon in the middle of the stage or what not.I haven't tried the arcade mode, maybe I won't, because the main attraction and based on others review is the story mode.This is another example how I should avoid overhyped positif review on Steam (the closest AAA STG? what are you smoking?). There's a reason 1 year old game only have 75 reviews.Buy this game if you curious about a "casual" shmup game. Avoid at all cost if you wish to have a good story on shmup game.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I really like shmups where you can gain levels and get stronger- I think it's a great way to get new players who are turned off by high difficulty into the genre, kind of like what Symphony of the Night did for Castlevania games...if you get stuck, just do some grinding to level up. It's fantastic in every way except the for the visuals, which are a big weak point in my opinion. The game just has an extremely basic, sterile look, with very little detail and no textures. And it has some of the worst looking explosions I've seen in a shooter. But it does run really well on my system. Overall, the gameplay delivers, but I'd like to see Qute's next game step up the presentation.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: A tightly produced new entry in the 'Seventia' series of games by Qute that also includes Ginga Force and Eschatos (plus maybe Judgement Silversword- all of these games are available on Steam). The 'world building' (sekaikan) of the games is cohesive, and the storylines are engaging with tonnes of original Japanese voice acting, tranlated with subtitles. Graphics look great on a big or small screen, and as others have noted the framerate is rock solid throughout.It's worth noting that this is a Sci-Fi Anime world with tasteful SFW artwork, not 'bewbs'. A big selling point for me.The main draw is 'Story Mode', where you can approach the 10+ stages one by one, locking in your results without ever having to do a full run. Each stage is challenging, and you will need to use your Shmup hobby skills of analysis to the fullest, even to clear 100% of the missions on 'Easy' difficulty. Your efforts are rewarded with a host of unlockable, chunky weapons (offensive and defensive) which physically change the look of your player ship as you equip them- another nice touch.If you really can't live without an arcade style score challenge, you can attempt a full run of all the stages in Arcade Mode, complete with leaderboards. Just remember that Story Mode is your Practice ground at all times.If you are looking for a route further into the Shmups hobby, I can't recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun little shmup. Like in developer QUTE's masterpiece Ginga Force, Easy Mode is just about perfect difficulty for me. Normal gets quite crazy about halfway through the 10 stages, you'll need perfect loadouts to survive. Like in GF, you keep grinding stages to upgrade your ship until you can clear them. If you're struggling to even reach the boss of a stage, you probably just have the wrong loadout. The soundtrack is okay, but you may want to roll your own. It's not quite as epic as Ginga Force, but it is a very good game in its own right, albeit a shorter and arguably less ambitious one from a game design perspective. There are some truly great boss fights in this game, especially the final one. Finally, I get a nasty windows error if I launch the game without a mouse attached, which I often do, because I'm playing in Big Picture on my TV. Other than that, it runs extremely well and like GF can be played on any old potato PC. The game goes on sale for as low as $1 so keep an eye out.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant game! Graphics, Music, Controls all brilliant! Plays like an utter dream straight out of the box on my Steam Deck with no tinkering. Its the most perfect old skool side scrolling shooter that I have been looking for. Both this and the sequel Gingaforce run fantastically well - both games should be 100% proper steam deck verified immediately! Everyone should buy both games!
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Peak shmup. Kino. Cinema. Idk. This game is amazing though. It pretty much takes every gripe I have with Ginga Force and smooths out the experience to end up being one of the best out of the entire genre. Not only did they manage to squeeze out another quality game after GF, but they managed to improve upon it in every conceivable way. The only thing that one has on Natsuki Chronicles is that its vertical scrolling and that's just preference at that point. There is so much variety in what you can bring to a level and you're heavily incentivized to keep trying new loadouts whilst simultaneously improving at the stage. It's a really genius way to encourage the player to naturally get better. There's also no more annoying ammo system. You can run either of your weapons at full power or run them both together with mitigated effects. It gives you far more control over the power of your weapons than just waiting for ammo drops in boss fights in Ginga Force, which hurt the experience a ton watching your weapons turn into pitiful pea shooters.Another big positive is that characters don't yap as much as they did in Ginga Force. That was extremely distracting. That being said, Ginga Force is still definitely worth playing just to have a more context as to what this game is about.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Really great shooter. Can't believe I got it for $1! Very reminiscent of the best stuff on the PC Engine, Aero Blaster especially. I was surprised by how good the (pretty based) story was, though it was hard to follow the subtitles during the frantic gameplay. Excellent soundtrack as well! Visuals are a little simple, but they work for me and everything is readable and runs great at higher framerates. The way that weapon unlocks require a bit of a grind is a bummer, but there's still plenty of options at your disposal from a single playthrough to have a lot of fun and the rest come as you practice and improve. If you're wanting to max every weapon out and blow through in a single run or two, that's not going to happen though. I do wish clearing stages on higher difficulties gave new unlocks rather than player level, because the first run seems to give you fun new stuff at every turn and then things slow way down on replay.Still, a pretty minor complaint for me. I loved this one and really hope the dev has something new in the works because I'll be there day one.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: wow... I've always been "curious" about shmups or bullet hell genre - it's nostalgic. But I've never been able to really get into any of the "recommendations". This game just has something that pulls me in for one more round everytime I fire it up. There's a sense of progression. It has multiple difficulty levels that can ease someone new in. I really like it. Looking at the dev team, it's really impressive that such a small team can accomplish something so polished. Totally recommended for someone who wants to dabble into this genre. Modern and fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: It's an animu style side-scrolling shoot em up. Not too serious. Story seems light, but it's hard to follow in between all those bullets. Voice acting is a plus. I found the "normal" difficulty quite challenging, but the good thing is, the game rewards you for failing. You still get the exp (just less) and you also gain level-specific exp, which gives extra shields for subsequent attempts. You can retry a specific map any number of times you want. So, eventually you can pass it, even on hard. Music and graphics are good too. Story mode was a bit short (about 4h).Good:+ Looks and sounds good+ No crashes or slowdowns+ Adjustable difficulty+ Voice actingBad:- A bit short
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Great horizontal classic shooter. Another great game from qute. I don´t like it so much as eschatos/judgment because it lacks the simplicity of them, as there is ship configurations and some grinding to get money. I strongly suggest the use of cheat engine to get currency, or else you have to replay the same levels again and again. The graphics are great has they have visual clarity and the art style is low poly (wich is a great style to endure the test of time). the music is great. The acessability options are great for newbies.  the bullet patterns are great and in a era that we almost see only bullet hells , qute is a company to respect.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Natsuki Chronicles is a a sort of companion story and game to Ginga Force.  As such, it shares a lot of the same elements.  With the most noticeable difference is Natsuki Chronicles a horizontal shoot 'em up compared to Ginga Force being a vertical one.Each mission is a story element with a some flashback missions of the protagonist's time in flight school which also serve as a bit of a tutorial for some of the games mechanics.  These mechanics aren't complicated, but it's nice to be made aware of them.  Your ship has a primary, secondary weapon as well as a special item.  Weapons range from machine guns, bombs, grenades, wave and ring weapons as well as a few lasers.  Primary weapons are forward facing.  While secondary have rear and wide shot options.  The special weapon ranges from a type of minor shield to a powerful attack.  I didn't make much use of the special item save for attacking the bosses.Natsuki Chronicles has a leveling and weapon buying system.  Each time a mission is entered the player earns XP, additional shields and credits to upgrade weapons.  So even if a player is struggling with a level, the game offers a little aid each time they try again.  Which is nice.  But this also doesn't make the game a push over.  With all the weapon options, it can be easy to select a load out that can make even the easy setting of missions kinda tough.My biggest complaint would be that I would prefer some transparency in the weapons damage and damage per second in game.  I had a difficult time knowing which weapons delivered a lot of damage and which ones offered something else like better crowd control.  Even after completely the game, I couldn't say what weapon delivers the most damage per shot.  Something that would make the boss fights much easier.Ultimately, Natsuki Chronicles is a good beginner shmup.  It's not super hard and rewards trying again and again.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: you have to replay shumps many, many times in order to get good.  or at least i do.natsuki chronicles is one of a few shumps ive encountered that seems to realize that the human brain loves seeing bars/numbers go up.  as in, you get tangible rewards - in the form of unlocks and currency - every time you try and fail miserably, in addition to getting slightly better skills-wise.youre even given extra health (usable only on that stage) the more you try.  you dont have to use that bonus, but if you really cannot crack a certain stage, its great to have that little boost.this game gets it: if youre a shump expert, its a hard-as-balls bullet hell.  if youre just a chump who loves shumps, you can get by anyway with enough effortoh, and even judged apart from all that it would be one of the best shooters of the last two decades
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Grab everything that was good in Ginga Force and made it good for the less hardcore/more casual players (upgrade shop with a nice amount for customization options for shots and shields, forgiving life system, emphasis on level by level play instead of the whole arcade run) while ironing out almost all the flaws (no more weapon decay, clearer bullet visibility, removal of extreme 3d angles, better life system due to only needing to play the stages instead of grabbing them, upgrade shop now not being locked behind level progression) and also adding things of its own (your last 3 lives recharge after some time and a really neat danger indicator for both enemies and bullets)Also it includes an actual arcade mode unlike Ginga Force which is a welcome addition.Though you now have to bear with the fact that you're sorta kinda the bad guy this time around.If you liked Ginga Force this one is even better, highly recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: A vastly improved prequel/side story to Ginga Force. While on the easiest difficulty, Ginga Force has a massive difficulty curve that will put off a lot of players before they manage to reach the final level. Now with this game, that goal is certainly manageable.On top of that, this game is a horizontal shooter, taking elements like stage layout and firing options from the likes of R-Type, Darius, Gradius and even Border Down. Customisation is one of the biggest parts of Natsuki Chronicles, as it was in Ginga Force, and choosing the right loadout for each stage - or run - is key to mastering this game.The presentation has seen an upgrade from 2013's Ginga Force, as this new game was developed and released around 2020, taking advantage of the latest technology to output the best graphics they could possibly craft. The music is once again no slouch, I'll say that much. Some stuff like SFX is pulled from Ginga Force (and therefore Eschatos) but manages to fit since both games are related.Overall, a very nice side scrolling shooter that you definitely should try out, even if you haven't had much experience with Ginga Force.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, the soundtrack is a complete banger and really carries the game.  This is quite possibly the scariest shmup Qute has devised as of yet and can be pretty brutal even by other game's standards.  Some would assume after noticing 4 difficulties that Normal would be a cakewalk with minimal investment, but it really isn't 100% free.  This game is gonna give you a serious run for your money in the middle until you learn some of the level layouts and figure out how to use the weapons more efficiently.  Basically each difficulty you see is more or less relative to being 1 difficulty higher in other games, so if Normal feels like too much you'll be better off just swallowing your pride and playing Arcade on Easy first until you clear or Story on Easy so you can get at least some credits before returning to Normal.Talking about more things that aren't just the game's difficulty, there are actually some nice changes to the gameplay since Ginga Force for those fully aware this is from the same people and universe (obviously not talking about how GF is Vert and NC is Hori).  You now have the option to set your speed 1-9 between two speed settings and super game-changing you can use Toggle which is default and how GF worked with the change speed button, or Hold which is like a traditional Focus button in other SHMUPs and OH MAN it makes a world of difference which I highly recommend trying out.  You have several options for bullet and enemy warnings on screen, which you can leave on if you like.  Bullet settings can be a warning for all bullets flying in your trajectory with a red line, only dangerous bullets, or none if they end up distracting you too much (I personally get distracted by them badly but the middle option might be better to try out later). Score Attack is gone since Ginga Force however, and the game no longer has a focus on stage-to-stage competition.  Arcade takes place of Score Attack and here you play through Natsuki all the way in one sitting like a traditional SHMUP.If you consider yourself hardcore, pick this up whenever.  If you are not confident in your SHMUP skills but you hear and like what you see, maybe wait for a sale if you get frustrated easily playing one stage a few times aka story mode things.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: New dramatic horizontal shoot ’em up that takes place in the same setting as Ginga Force. An immersive story that follows protagonist Natsuki. Discover the story of her past as a rookie pilot up to present day with events that are parallel to those in Ginga Force.
_childDocuments_.name: Natsuki Chronicles

name: Little Kitty, Big City
detailed_description: A peaceful catnap turns into a whimsical adventure! Will you make your way home or will you explore what the big city has to offer first? I mean, getting home is obviously your main priority. Obviously. Well, it's one of your priorities. Maybe more of a guideline... It's definitely on your To-Do list somewhere! But first? Exploration! Features: Explore the city at your own pace in an open-world playground filled with surprises! Make friends with a colorful cast of chatty animals. Complete quests, help your animal friends, or cause a total ruckus. It’s up to you. Customize your Kitty with a plethora of very adorable hats! Take a nap in the sunshine. Find a way home...?
about_the_game: A peaceful catnap turns into a whimsical adventure! Will you make your way home or will you explore what the big city has to offer first? I mean, getting home is obviously your main priority. Obviously. Well, it's one of your priorities. Maybe more of a guideline... It's definitely on your To-Do list somewhere! But first? Exploration! short_description: You're a curious little kitty with a big personality, on an adventure to find your way back home. Explore the city, make new friends with stray animals, wear delightful hats, and leave more than a little chaos in your wake. After all, isn't that what cats do best?

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely delightful cat game. Fun, lighthearted and thoroughly enjoyable. Definitely recommended!The premise is pretty much what the game description on the Steam store page says. You play the role of a little kitten, and you need to find your way home. The story is set in a fictional city (Japan somewhere) and there are lots of nice cultural references (the Devs have paid attention!).By far the most delightful part is the kitten's personality. The animations really capture the whimsical, playful nature of a young cat. The sounds of miaowing and purring are spot on, and really bring the character to life. The facial expressions are really good and the attention to detail is superb. Background music is light jazz-style and it suits the setting well. The sound effects are good and the art style is very consistent. The other characters you interact with are fun, and the dialogues are laced with witty, gentle humour. It embraces the curious, cheeky nature of being a little cat. This makes this game vastly better than . Vastly better.In addition to the main story, there are sidequests and collectables, to ensure you either explore fully or you have different things to try after you make it home. There are lots of Steam achievements too (some people reported problems with these... but they worked fine for me, and the Devs are activity fixing bugs).And the city does feel rather big. Although you sort of start recognising areas, there is a lot of verticality and hidden places and you get the impression of it being overwhelming (in a good way). It took me about 12 hours to do my first playthough. If you use a Walkthrough Guide, you could do it faster, I suppose, that that would totally defeat the purpose of exploring, playing and simply having fun. I only got 32 of the 39 achievements on my first game, so I'll certainly be going back to explore.One thing to note, is that the little kitty can't get hurt, making it suitable for children or those who want some escapism. That said, your little cat can certainly get up to some mischief!I won't go into details for risk of spoilers, but the last scene is truly charming.In summary,  is a super-cute cat game. I definitely recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. It was super cute & well done. I really love cozy games that have quests & aren't just farming or sandbox games. I loved climbing around the city and feeling like I was part of the world. There is no voice acting but the dialogue was fun to read. I 100% the game but if you aren't interested in that then the this game will be shorter. Personally I think it is worth the full asking price if you're interested in 100%ing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a cat. That automatically makes it awesome. However, there are some other things that make it great. The art-style  is amazing and incredibly cute, the characters all have distinct personalities that you can easily recognize,and the general gameplay is very well done (I played using keyboard and mouse, so it may be even better on controllers). My only complaint is how short it is, even then I hard focused on getting the fish, so I ended up exploring less than I could have before completion. Either way, amazing game 10/10 silly cats sitting on my keyboard would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Bought right as the clock hit 0 for launch, And with close to 1 hour i have been playing- Its super fun, cute, enjoyable, And its really simple to pick up and enjoy anytime on any controller input! So far, I have ran into 2 bugs and 1 of them made me have to alt-F4. But other than that and me spamming buttons around everything, Its really smooth and really fun to play and guide your fellow feline character around the big open city!I would say, Get this game if you really do love cats, city animals, exploration, collecting, messing about, And just overall love cats and playing as em!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: >I'm a kitty>In the big city>Trying to find my way home>Can talk to other animalsKino is served.For real, though. It would be so easy to make a "le cute catto game" for a quick buck but the game actually gives you an objective, storyline, likeable and entertaining characters with strong personalities, activities and, get this, actual level design.Sure, I may be an OCD masochist with a heart of coal that loves punishing himself with hardcore games on the highest difficulty but there is no way I can't appreciate this wholesome this labor of love.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute, fun, relaxing game that's not too long. It's mostly about exploring, platforming, collecting, doing side quests, committing mischief, and having cute funny conversations. You might like this game if you liked Stray, Untitled Goose Game, or Donut County. You might not like this game if you want high stakes, heart-pounding action, or mind-bending puzzles. It's a more casual game, good for relaxing over a couple of afternoons.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: You can sit in boxes and have a quest to remind people that you shouldn't put breakable things on shelves. You can make biscuits.Also, as a cat I feel like having your trinkets you like is important. This game allows you to collect random objects and place them places, when you save the game and return later they will still be in that exact spot. This among other things you will run across your adventure in the big city really show how much attention to detail the developers had with this absolute pure show of passion.If you like cozy games that have a bunch of activities to do and collect the achievements, this jaunt in the city is a purrfect time!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I waited quite awhile for this game to drop, wasn't too disappointing. I love the style, the stories are super cute, but for how long it took to develop I thought there'd be more, I'm not complaining though, it's still a really cute and fun time consuming game, I've already 100% completed it with just 11 hours of playtime :)
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This may be the perfect game for me. It's adorable, and they give you objectives, but your main objective is . I am normally a person who is obsessed with my objective in games -- I want to know exactly what my objectives are, and I go after them with dogged (catted?) determination. I love it that the objectives in this game are clear, and that they help you keep track of them. But also, I've played about two and a half hours, and I keep just getting lost in the  of it all. I can play for a long time, collecting shinies and breaking pots and alternately tripping and nuzzling humans, and suddenly realize I've forgotten my objective entirely. I love this game. Worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Existence of this game makes me question the existence of Stray even more.LKBC is a wonderful game about a cat. It's a lighthearted exploration/achievement hunting game with pleasant visuals, rewarding gameplay loop and, surprisingly, really nice writing.I've completed the game in 5 hours and even after I had a thought "Ugh, I'm not gonna do that" after I saw that "Recycle 100 cans" achievement... I still did all of that and never actually got bored even for a second.Controls and physics could be a bit junky at times, but that's what I can happily forgive. Now this would be one of these gems that I played in one seat and that would stay in my heart for years. Thank you, Double Dagger! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: If you like cats, and adorable things, and cats doing adorable things, this game is for you. For a first playthrough, basically never having seen more than the first five to ten minutes, it took me a little over four hours to reach the official end and watch the credit scrawl. I'm not particularly good at games, but this one just felt great the whole way through. It's constantly heaping more cuteness on you throughout. If you don't like cuteness or cats? Uh, you probably aren't going to enjoy this game and I would not recommend it to you. I would however recommend coming around to liking both cuteness and cats. _childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game! and while it's recommended to play with a controller, I played for over three hours on keyboard + mouse and it controls pretty well! _childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not deep. It's not particularly tight or polished. It's not even very long (I'm 5 hours in and have 70% completion). Despite all that, this has been the best singleplayer gaming experience I've had in months.The map is fairly small, but it's absolutely PACKED with content. There's scarcely an inch of wasted space in the game, and I still haven't even explored every nook and cranny yet. On top of that, it's overflowing with heart and charm -- the dialogue, characters, animations, and humor are all top-notch. It's just good wholesome fun, and probably the best "cozy" game I've ever played.My only real complaint is that there's not more!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This wholesome and adorable game has changed my mood and day! You play a little kitty that explores a big city, completing quests and trying to find a way back home after you fell from your balcony.The game has beautiful graphics, and lots of collectible hats you can find in secret areas or from NPC's. The soundtrack is also very catchy and matches the game's style and mood really well.Not to mention, you can also use emotes that you can collect from other cat or dog NPC's.To me, this game is probably the best exploration game I played and definitely the most wholesome game out there. I have also noticed that the game's graphics and soundtrack sounds/looks very similar to a game called Untitled Goose Game (check that game out too!)In conclusion I definitely recommend this game to all those people that want a cozy experience while gaming and to all the cat lovers! ♥
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a solid game. Rather short (even if you wanna 100% the game) so I don't feel like the overall pricetag is justified. I finished the game with about half the achievements done in about 4 hours. That being said: It's like Untitled Goose Game, but you're a cat with hats. Cute, fun, and an overall great game. There are bugs though, and some of them pretty much soft lock you from gameplay features**SEMI SPOILER**There's a character you meet early on that you help out, and in return you gain access to a game play feature. THIS EVENT WILL VERY LIKELY GLITCH OUT unless you prepare for it ahead of time. And if it glitches out, the rest of the game can get a bit aggravating as it seems to branch out into other weird glitches/bugs (clipping through environment, getting thrown across the map by something, etc). As spoiler free as possible: You need to collect a bunch of an item BEFORE interacting with this character.All that being said, the game is a fun little romp and worth the time (maybe not the price tag for some).Side note: My review is positive, but I'm leaving it as a Thumbs Down until that potentially run ruining bug is taken care of. I will change it when that is fixed so others can be aware of potential issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Game is very cute and charming but definitely lacks polish in some areas. Worst offender that comes to mind is the weird collision when trying to climb/jump up to get to the top of buildings. Climbing buildings is definitely one of the more frustrating parts of the game because the collision in this game seems to be quite jank. There was time where i was trying to jump from a fence onto a pipe and despite landing on the pipe, after half a second i got flung off onto the opposite side of the fence I had just jumped off and somehow tripped over a nearby person despite not even being near them. If it wasn't so funny, I would have definitely been annoyed.If you're patient enough to overlook the random instances of ragdolling off things when trying to get to achievement objectives, the game is still plenty fun and worthwhile playing.

_childDocuments_.review: If you focus on returning home, then you can beat the game in a couple hours.However, thankfully, you can continue to play after you return to your home.The total area to explore is less than a game like Stray.  However, there is no life bar and I think this game is more suitable to children as well as those who don't want to see the main character (or other cats) get hurt.  I think both games are good and Stray definitely has better graphics; however, due to the combination of open-ended tasks and light-hearted gameplay, I think I am currently more likely to play "Little Kitty, Big City"  if I want to casually be a cat for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and endearing if pretty short experience. There's plenty of kittiness to be had, and admittedly that's the game's main selling point. When the game focuses on a cat being a cat (bugging humans, napping, catching birds) it's an inexplicably relaxing and cute adventure, but when it tries to build character through long-winded dialogues, it risks overstaying its already short welcome.I found the beginning to be strangely frustrating, as the kitty can barely jump and can't climb anything worth a damn. It took me a while to get comfortable with the controls, and the moment I could climb ivy, the game got much, much better.Getting the climbing ability requires you to collect some "shinies," which can be a frustrating experience until you get this essential tip: You're welcome.Once you start climbing, the world opens up a little more and it doesn't feel so constrained anymore. The game really shines after this point, trying to reach high points and chasing ridiculous achievements around town. The kitty's bubbly and curious personality is endearing, and I honestly felt myself de-stress just looking around for hats and stalking birds by baiting them with bagels.Recommended on sale or when you have a lot to think about and no physical kitty to take your mind off things.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Realistically, Little Kitty, Big City is probably a 6/10, maybe a 7/10. It's not doing anything particularly new or interesting. The platforming is rote and sticky, it's buggier than it should be, the music is nondescript amd it's very short (maybe three hours if you're not going for all the achievements. Counterpoint: cats are cute and I like them.Perhaps that sounds like I'm being deliberately facetious, dismissing any possible criticisms of the game with flippancy. But I honestly believe that the theming and charm of Little Kitty elevates a flawed and generally average game to an experience that had me consistently smiling for four hours. I've resisted the temptation to compare Little Kitty to Stray so far, but it's a comparison that is as necessary as it is inevitable. Where Stray felt like a pretty bogstandard linear adventure game with the idea of a feline protagonist added in later, Little Kitty's design document is probably just the word "CAT!" written over and over. Every interaction in the game is designed to evoke true kitty immersion and it works. From a varied selection of cat nap spots, the ability to catch (and release safely) birds, the ability to knock fragile things off of shelves, all of these and more combine to provide a deeply entertaining digital depiction of an animal's whole vibe akin to what Untitled Goose Game did for geese.Overall, Little Kitty, Big City is a fine game. Its building blocks are nondescript, but the sheer amount of charm pushes it to a higher level than you'd expect. I do still wish the game was a little bigger and that its moment to moment interactions were more varied, but in the end, I had a great time and I will likely think back on Little Kitty a lot as time goes by. If you adore cats, then you've probably already bought this.

_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful, charming and cute. This game has a great sense of humour as you play a cute little kitty wandering the big city.There's a few bugs here and there, but none that were game breaking and the artistic intent of the game still shone through.I've played about 3 hours and done a whole bunch of stuff, but there was a lot more for me to do and I think once I'm done playing a long game I'll come back to this and complete some of the extra quests.I definitely recommend playing by yourself as it's short and charming enough to be something nice to play between two bigger games. _childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I've previously played and finished the game "Stray", and I have a real penchant for cat-themed games. I've been waiting to play this one for about three years now. I first spotted it on Twitter, and it seemed quite promising. I finally bought it during this summer sale, however, playing with a keyboard was tough. You have to click the mouse for interactions, which detracted from the experience. The game strongly recommends using a controller, which offers a smoother gameplay experience.Surprisingly, the game is relatively short; I was taken aback by how quickly it ended. Speedrunners finish it in under 5 minutes without glitches, which is funny. The story felt a bit lacking, but I enjoyed going for all the achievements. If you're someone who enjoys striving for perfection and achieving 100% completion, then this game is definitely worth considering.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game is short, low-stakes adventure of a tiny cat in a small corner of a Japanese city.It is clearly a work of love that invites you to take in all its little details at a leisurely pace while you guide the titular little kitty on its distraction-filled way home. The animation of the kitty is "quintessential cat", the other animal NPCs are hilarious and even the human NPCs, faceless as they are, have enough character to be a joy to mess with.I used a keyboard to play and it worked fine, despite the game recommending a controller.What is also notable is that since the initial release, the devs have been very responsive to glitches and bugs reported by users.I've seen a few reviews lamenting that the price is too high for how short it is, but I've spent more for games with more hours to complete / replayability that I didn't bother picking up again after the 2-4 hour mark. I'd argue my money was better spent on the one I enjoyed enough to complete it.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: the game has some glaring bugs, one of the achievements is extremely difficult to get due to the game's mechanics, and the controls and movement are pretty clunky, even when playing on controller (really not a fan of games favoring a certain set of controls). these issues can be distracting and frustrating. in my experience, quitting and reloading the game would usually reset most objects and npcs and allow me to continue progressing.despite all this, i still would recommend the game to almost anyone, except, ironically, younger children to whom the controls would be difficult to teach. it is adorable and the npcs are funny, helpful, and unique in their personalities. the quests are fun, and messing with people (swatting the humans and making them fall over made me laugh out loud more times than i'd probably like to admit) is satisfying. the game is small, and can be completed in a day. it's really just a silly, cute, entertaining game that i enjoyed consistently. i hope the devs continue to put their efforts toward the game as it is a novel little world and experience worth expanding and polishing.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as a gift.It's colorful, adorable, fun, cozy, an exciting way to spend your time playing.Reminds me of the Untitled Goose Game, and I'm saying this as a compliment as I did love playing both games.Way better than Stray in terms of easy-on-the-eye and cat mechanics.Good cat game overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. Is this game good? Absolutely. It's fun, it's cute, it's relatively well-controlling, the story is simple and to the point which gives leeway for exploration, and the side quests are all quite fun too.BUT.The game is buggy. VERY buggy. So many times did I subtly clip through walls while climbing, or my jumping cursor would go off and do whatever it wanted, which, while a little iffy on the quality control department, is fine, and with how fluidly the cat moves everywhere else I would've been able to brush it off, but the tipping point for me was climbing onto a rooftop and realising that one of the doors that should've stopped me from going in was LACKING ANY COLLISION and I could just walk through it out of bounds. If you get stuck like this by the way, just hold jump and get the cursor close to the stairs, you can easily clip back through.and, as much as I hate to say this, the game is so short for the price tag. Unless we get some free DLC, it feels like most of the budget went towards quality of life improvements, and not enough went towards actual game development/QA.Is this game bad? Not at all, in fact I had a lot of fun with it, but the amount of bugginess keeps me from recommending it, ESPECIALLY at full price.With less bugs and a cheaper price tag, I would happily recommend it, but on its own right now? It's really only worth it if you can pick it up on a sale. Sorry.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: A funny little romp, it can be a little rough around the edges with the movement system but overall it was well worth the money. You can tell a lot of love went into this game, the aesthetics, humor, and gameplay make it a worthwhile  buy for anyone who likes a short(ish) and sweet game with achievable achievments!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed review.Cute game, characters are full of personality, dialog is fun.Fun and silly objectives and stuff...However, collisions are pretty jank, and I clipped through wall many times on accident within a single hour of playtime.Also got my save bricked by being saved while out of bounds. In less than one hour of playtime.So, I'll skip for now... Might grab it again once things are fixed a bit, or on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable cat with unwanted always-on "noclip mode".Negative: - You really clip through everything. Falling through buildings, into buildings, getting stuck in buildings, it feels like 20% of my play time was a frenzied "oh no, I gotta glitch out of here again!". Potentially game-breaking, alas truly 👎.- Minor NPC issue with somebody loving you, then tripping over you as they try to walk away, then somebody else tripping over as well, sometimes leading to "generating energy" and catapulting the human out of the map, just to immediately gummy-warp them back into their last position. More absurd / funny, though.- When not glitching, humans are boring and predictive.Positive:- Really great kitty, a lot of cat-lover effort went into the rig with animating it + all the kitty things you can do, including yacking (lol)!- Awesome idea / storyline of many puzzles with some hints of positive psychology and animal friends you meet having certain relatable struggles.- It's just fun to go have the zoomies and break things like a real cat would!From a strictly "playtime vs. price" category, a bit pricey. The "noclip mode" bug would've lead to a bad rating if this was an AAA game.However, this is a small team / indie devs - not over 9000 people as you'd have with an AAA title... And the developers of "Little Kitty, Big City" sure put a lot of love into this game. It's just not very polished, but I believe in indie game studios.Alas, I consider 50% of the price to be for the game, and 50% a donation to the team - hoping to see more kitty things in the future!⭐⭐⭐⭐★
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly charming and relaxing to play. Game play is mix of parkour, exploration, and (light) puzzle-solving. The cat is incredibly cute and has a big personality. The city is interesting to explore and the art style is attractive. The simple, chill music complements the graphics, environment, and gameplay nicely. My only criticism is that it's a rather short game. The map isn't as big as I expected, although the developed crammed a lot into that small space (yet it doesn't feel crowded). Overall this is a fantastic game and I would recommend it if you're looking for something relaxing and low-threat.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

There's nothing fancy, neither in the gameplay, nor in the 3D Modeling and animations.There's also still some bugs I noticed 2 :- first of the fans, one threw me off the map, so far away that I had to walk back for 10 min, I tried reloading the game it didn't teleported me back- second off the hidden achievement fruit fall, you will see no humans slipping on the banana, u just have to make the banana collide with the feet of a human, but it doesn't work most of the time, it took me 20 min to finally complete the achievement because the collisions didn't work.If I had one last thing to say, it's a really funny game, but it's not worth the price.
