_childDocuments_.review: Cutest game I've ever played. They put so much care into the animations and environment, I've never taken so many pictures/screenshots.Its surprisingly enjoyable just running around town collecting stuff and being a cat.HOWEVER! I can see that on the horizon the game will be pretty short. While I will probably revisit it once and a while, it would be nice if they added mini-games of some sort to keep the game fresh. Playing catch with the dog, racing other cats around town, catching as many bids as you can in X minutes, stuff like that. As the game is right now, mostly you're collecting stuff and solving very simple puzzles (which is still fun, just not super engaging long term)I think its a little misleading for the trailer to say there's "infinite" playtime when a lot of it is based on how much fun you can make for yourself after all the side-quests are done.All in all I think the price is worth it for the work they put into it, but I would love to see some expansions in the future.Edit: There are a few bugs with the map, but you kind of have to go out of your way to find them. _childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game for a long time, and I was elated when it finally released but... It's just not there.As others have mentioned, the games TOO short. Little Kitty, Big City --Actually Little Kitty, Three Blocks. It's really cute but its a pretty meaningless collectathon. Every character has one trivially short quest and then you're done. And there's only about 10 of those in the game. It does everything I really wanted this game to do but, there's just not enough game here. As of writing this review, I'm 3 hours in, and I think I can probably finish the main quest. Now I'm just wandering the map ticking off achievements. There's no substance here. There are cool ideas but each of them you really only use once in an obvious puzzle before wandering off 5 seconds later.  And even wandering is proving difficult.If it goes on sale for $10 and you want a cute little game to unwind with, pick it up, but at full price, I can't recommend it.Addendum:I 100%'d the game and it took just over 5 hours, and a good chunk of that was the really tedious quests (Looking at you, recycling quest). After I finished I wanted to see how long it would take if I just ignored the sidequests to see how long it would take for me to beat the main story. From starting a new save to seeing the credits roll, it took 22 minutes and 31 seconds.EDIT: My graphics driver was out of date

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing and OverhypedI went into Little Kitty, Big City with high expectations, but sadly, it fell flat in several areas. While the concept of playing as a mischievous cat in a sprawling urban environment is undeniably charming, the execution left much to be desired.The biggest issue is the lack of depth. The world, while visually appealing, feels shallow. Exploration gets repetitive quickly, as there isn’t much variety in activities beyond basic fetch quests or knocking over objects. The lack of meaningful progression or challenges makes the experience feel more like a tech demo than a fully fleshed-out game.Additionally, the controls feel clunky at times, which is frustrating for a game where movement and physics interactions are central. The novelty of being a cat wears off fast when you’re fighting with the camera angles or awkward mechanics.To make matters worse, the game feels unpolished. I ran into several bugs, like objects clipping through the environment and interactions not triggering correctly. These issues break immersion and make the game feel rushed.Finally, while the art style is cute, it doesn’t make up for the lack of engaging gameplay. It’s hard to recommend a game that feels like it relies more on its adorable premise than on providing a well-rounded experience.Unless you’re a hardcore fan of cat-themed games or don’t mind shallow gameplay, I’d say skip this one or wait for a deep sale. Little Kitty, Big City is a missed opportunity.Rating: 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This was a beautifully put together game that encourages exploration, adventure, and all sorts of meow-inducing shenanigans. Curiousity doesn't kill the cat, it just gets you a samurai sword to run around with and terrify the locals! Meow!I noted many comments about how people said that the game was too short and to that I say it was a great game to spend the evening enjoying the adventures of a little kitty in a big city. Not every game has to be a 150hr+ grind fest that steals and wastes your time. We've all spent more money on more disappointing AAA games in recent times, so I'd rather support smaller developers who make shorter but better quality games that make an evening of joy while I, as a little kitty in a big city, trip up unsuspecting business people to steal their friggin' sandwiches and create pleasant chaos.It's a cute game with interesting mechanics that encourages all the peak cat behaviour. Pounce on all the things! Knock everything off all ledges and shelves! Wear fashionable hats! Receive pats. I hope it inspires more Cat and/or Animals Protagonist adventure games in the future, because it's a nice change of pace to switch off from the woes of the world and just knock plants off of shelves for a while.Now if you'll excuse me, I'm off to go nap in a satellite dish.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted this game from the moment I saw it.  I thought $24.99 was a little too much but it might be worth it. It went on sale 20% OFF for $19.99 and so I purchased it. After 60 minutes of game play it was all coming clear that the video of the game was way better than actually playing it. The colors and and visuals are great! The game mechanics, not so much. The control of the cat is very clunky. Doing the little side missions are quite arduous in reality. In theory swatting a ball around sounds fun, reality is swatting results in a few misses and then when you make contact it rolls an inch or two. Sometimes you get a good whack and it'll roll a foot, but not in the intended direction. If that was all that's required then meh, but swatting balls around for the mission objectives becomes tedious and unfulfilling. Knocking pots off of ledges and breaking them was fun for a while. Also the interactions with other animals  became tiresome with the lengthy dialog that accompanied said interaction. I found reading what each character was saying was a chore in itself.  With only 90 minutes of play time I can't say I've really experienced the game. I just couldn't enjoy it because of the clunky tedious nature of the play. IMO this is not a $24.99 worth game. $9.99 Maybe. $4.99 Yes.

At least to my standarts.Will definitely check news regarding this game in the future if devs decide to expand it.Could be great to have more replayability here
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so so much. The cartoony style, the models (especially the tanuki and the cat ones), the humor, the animations and the mechanics are all top tier!!! Just a few bugs like the cat standing on top of nothing in some areas and I also accidentally skipped a tiny part of the game because I found a way to get past the city before giving the crow 25 shinies but it's no big deal. I absolutely love this game (breaking vases is actually the best feeling in the world and we should stop blaming cats for doing so).
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: ive seen negative reviews talk about game length and movement being issues, i can somewhat agree to an extent about the latter, but the former certainly not. saying that you can finish the game in 2 hours is outrageous, because yes, you can finish the main quest in that timeframe, but you'll have done none of the side content nor the exploration or goofing around, which is the main draw of this game.as for the movement, it can be capricious and clunky sometimes but it's still more than serviceable, at least on controller.played perfectly fine on steam deck as well.you'll want this game for the cuteness, the surprising effort into the dialogue and characters, and the medium size neighborhood you can explore at your leasure, while being a cat.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Those complaining about playtime obviously have no children. Even doing nothing she comes back to this.Also seems she thinks cats are swatting your legs kind of monsters. _childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: its wholesome, adorable, fun and interactive and knows how "serious" it is and i absolutely loved it. this is one of those games that gives a burst of life to the gaming community the same way stray has (at least in my opinion) and i highly recommend if you are looking for a cute game with a wonderful little story!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This game has GAME BREAKING BUGS and is VERY SHORT for the price. I feel bad for giving this a thumbs down because this is technically a decent game and I only played it for 2 hours but I did my research and I feel like I should give a warning to anyone who's thinking of buying this at full price on release, it's just barely misses the mark and I feel like it's getting a pass due to the fact it's a cute cat game.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game, lots of fun, and I really REALLY wanted to love it... I played the demo a year ago and have been hyped ever since, bought it day of release.... and essentially 100% the game in under 4 hours of play. That wasn't me rushing either, i really took my time! _childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, relaxing, silly game. Easy to pick up and put down whenever you have free time, and very forgiving. Every character has a lot of personality, and there's no rush or time limit to complete any tasks in the game. This is one of the few games that I enjoyed 100%'ing, as none of the achievements feel grindy, excluding the recycling task. The rest is rewarding the player for exploring and collecting things on the map, or from being silly. It's not a very long game, but it's definitely a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game.On two personal notes: I both once lived in Japan for a while, making the environments feel very, very nostalgic to me. It felt a lot like strolling around an idealized version of the neighbourhood I used to live in. I also had a lovely black kitty myself (who unfortunately passed away a few years ago), so the protagonist got me right in the feels. All the feels.Aside from those personal notes, this is the cat simulator I always wished for, with just the right amount of wholesome and whimsical. No bugs that I encountered, and a lovely story, and cat-centric silliness that anyone fond of felines can relate to. I kept going "aw!", and the ending made my cry happy tears. Also, quite a good size of game. There should be more short, cozy games. It took me five hours to get through, and while I will likely be back at some point to explore more, I definitely feel it was worth it, and it didn't feel in any way too short. Not everything has to me a 150+ hour epic slog.10/10, would steal those fishies all over again. Buy it, and take your time playing it through.(Review dedicated to Talvi the void, who is missed.)
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little game. I've been waiting for this game for almost 2 years now and now that I have it. I'm sad its already over. It's a very fun little game with a bunch of cat humor that made me chuckle. I hope the studio decides to make another game like this or even a add-on. Would 100% recommend for any cat lover!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game where you explore the city as a cat in unfamiliar territory. Gameplay is well thought out. It's neither too open ended nor too scripted. Just the right balance. The environment is well made with a pleasant design and a lot of hints to future abilities, achievements, and the advancement of the story. As a casual player and a cat lover, I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished 100%ing this game, and I must say it was a blast! Very simple game play loop, feels like a mash up of Untitled Goose Game, Banjo Kazooie, and Breath of the wild.  Some slightly tricky jumps that took multiple tries here and there, but mostly quite easy. The focus is more on exploration and interacting with the world around you than solving puzzles or doing platforming challenges. An incredibly cute and cozy game that just OOZES charm. The graphics, sound, and writing all compliment the theme very nicely. The cast of colorful characters are fun to interact with and listen to banter back and forth. For anyone intrigued by the trailers and general concept, I highly recommend checking it out,as it delivers on what it promises.I Beat the main game in ~5 and a half hours, doing a lot of the side quests and extra achievements. About doubled my time getting some of the more tedious achievements like recycling 100 cans and getting my picture taken 20 times. Would definitely recommend keeping those in mind while working through the main story. My experience was mostly bug free, but my friend had to replay the entire game to 100% THREE TIMES because a key item (a bird nest from the sticky business quest line)  wasn't counted when he collected it on multiple run-throughs, leaving him stuck at 99.9%. He also struggled to get the Fruity Fall achievement to work. I got it through random chance early on in my run, but he spent hours trying to grind it out. When I tried to get it a second time, I simply couldn't get it to happen again no matter what I did. Very well done for such a small indie team. More functional on day one than several AAA games from giant studios in recent years. Excited to see what the devs will do next.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like cute cats? Do you enjoy exploring and tormenting humans as a cat? If yes, this game is for you!This game is freaking adorable and I cannot recommend it enough! It took me around 8 hours to do all of the achievements and I had a blast the whole time. For a day #1 launch, the game is remarkably polished, with only a few minor hiccups. If its this good on day 1, it only gets better from here!12/10 Wholesome
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: In many ways, this is a great, hilarious game. Similar to Goose Game. Things that annoyed me though:- controls, jumps have a clear direction that you can tune, which is slightly tedious. Jumping up boxes without tuning, and you get a trivial jump slightly off, means the cat jumps and reflects itself, often res tting your entire climb back to the ground.- camera, several times the camera goes into first person, e.g. close to a wall. Particularly the part with the two fans are annoying, you need to pass quickly but can't really see where you're going. Also, past the fans, you can't turn them off somehow, but have to do this bit every tedious times.- one of the achievementswith fruit is buggy. Since it's also a secret one, it's almost impossible to find it as doing it unlikely actually gives you the achievement.- conversations, the animals make animal sounds and there's a lot of tedious reading. Would be nicer if they were either audible or shorter. I skipped most out of lack of patience.- add an option to get all hats out of the vending machine, this is just unnecessary repetitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun, casual exploration game with a few puzzles and platform mechanics. The story is fun, the characters are interesting, and the graphics are really cute. I wish the game was longer, though. There are 2 areas where you can't explore, but I hope that means that there will be DLC. It would be fun to see sequels where there is a different cat in a different city, perhaps even in different countries.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Clumsy controls.This game is cute and has a lot of fun ideas, but I quickly got irritated with clumsy mechanics and (*really short*) jump controls. It just makes me want to play "Stray" again. The last straw was getting soft-locked into an early area of the map, which is a lot less open than I thought it would be. Personally, this game is just a pass for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely LOVED this game!!!A bit buggy here and there but it wasn't anything game breaking.One bug that bothered me was the Fruit Fall achievement. No one was tripping over bananas. Only way to trigger this was to knock the bananas off the stand right when someone passes by. Only way to get it it before they can fix it!100% this game on day 1. I had to before kitty went home!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Little Kitty, Big City is a Game that I've followed development on for a while, and I can say I'm very happy and very excited with it! I've always wanted, ever since I was a little kid, a video game where I could play as a cat. I played just about any one of them I could get my hands on, or that my family knew of, and I can say, without a doubt, that this game is absolutely something that I would have loved all those years ago.It's short, yes, though it's quite adorable even with every little quirk, and the main character you play as reminds me so much of my own black cat that I couldn't not play it. It's a nice, relaxing game experience and while not absolutely perfect, like any game, is something that's enjoyable and comfortable. The environment is warm, and its fun finding all the little places you can get to, and overall, despite it being a generally short game, I absolutely adore it!

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. I spent a lot of time exploring before actually beating it. I 100%ed the game in about 6 or 7 hours. I personally think it was really worth it! _childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: The game is cozy, fun and adventurous. You can explore the city, get all the collectibles and just straight up do cat shinanigance. My biggest complaint is that it isn't longer, 3 hours in I had completed the main objective, then I spent another 5 hours goofing around at catching the rest of the objectives to 100% the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun! Easy, relaxing, silly, and lighthearted. They use real cat meows instead of just some guy saying "meow" (looking at specific other games...) and the cat's movements are very realistic. Gameplay gives Stray vibes but it's relaxing instead of intense. If you love cats, you'll enjoy it. Complaints: - The game was very short. I was able to 100% all achievements in only 7 hours. If infinite gameplay is advertised, I feel like it should take at least a little longer than that. More side quests would be cool. - The climbing is janky. There are several parts where Kitty will just get stuck on some invisible collision bug and you have to drop down and start over. - For the Litter Picker achievement, it's next to impossible to get it without reloading the game a few times. (unless you want to spend countless hours finding and trying to trip NPCs carrying cans) There ought to be more litter scattered around, or they could make it so you can recycle more items such as cell phones, bagels, or the random toys, instead of solely cans. Making people reload the game for an achievement doesn't count as more gameplay. Even on sale at $18 I feel like it was just a tad overpriced considering the short amount of gameplay, but I still enjoyed it and overall I don't regret paying for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I love the idea of this game. I think that the art is adorable and the mechanics are very catlike; very cute. I just don’t think the amount of gameplay you get from the game is worth the price. I finished the game in 2 hours. I don’t tend to 100% things but it just didn’t feel like it was worth my time to do more of the things available. Given the way the trailers were it seemed like there was more content in the game than there was. I don’t really think I expected it to be dozens of hours but it didn’t feel good that a 2 hour game cost $25, especially with as many physics bugs as I was encountering, to the point where I got soft locked at one point due to clipping into a platform that I couldn’t leave.Overall it was a cute game but I’m not happy with how much I paid for it with how little there is to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This game has kitty movements and habits down WAY better than Stray did.  There is a dedicated zoomies button.  A dedicated meow/stretch/roll over/puke up hairball button (press it and move the stick in your desired direction).  There are quests for sitting in boxes, knocking stuff off shelves, taking naps, pouncing birbs (and releasing them), basically anything you would want a kitty to do, this does cutely with the best animations. There are also baby ducks to waddle after you.  Basically, I love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: There is no way I can play Little Kitty, Big City without drawing comparisons to An Untitled Goose Game, but this game feels like a progressive upgrade to that game.The controls are satisfying and responsive, and everything is just calm and relaxing. Long Term tasks, such as collecting feathers and Shinys are given to you by different animals in the city, while more short term tasks, like “Become An Artist” happens more in the moment.The game rewards you experimenting, like bringing recyclables to the Blue Bin to get shinies, and swiping at the feet of Humans to get bread.In the end, Little Cat, Big City is a nice, calm and satisfying little game. Would definitely recommend a play.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Steam doesn't have many cat themed games and this is one of the best ones, as you have story line to follow but free to explore on your own. This game is very enjoyable and relaxing, I love the graphics and characters. The story line is relatively short, I wish there would be more characters or story development in terms of space travel as its an interesting take. However, even if the story goal is simple it is very entertaining to follow. The map isn't complicated making it easy to remember and explore all the areas and secret spaces. The game has different hats placed on the map making it fun and interesting to explore the city, but I also wished there would be different clothes items not just hats. Most of the tasks and controls are straight forward, apart from pushing things on ground (football balls) as its not very accurate. (controller)
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo and fell in love, I was sooooo eager to get this!I can only play a few hours on fridays but I LOVE IT!You know how people often advertise "relaxing games" buit then they somehow end up getting you stressed anyway, because you can't let go?THIS game is the first and only one in many hundreds of games I played that truly achieved this! I am SUPER relaxed and at the same time very happy to find secrets and discover every nook in my own pace - this is a gem! Very well done, devs!12/10, can't wait to finish it and get right back into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: The characters are cute, the hats are cute, the cat is cute! Lots of fun to just cat around. The game controls fairly well, there's a weight to movement that feels just heavy enough. As well as a slight slide to when you come to a sudden stop from running, that looks and feels very cat-like. I never felt like the games tasks were difficult, but I still had fun with them, and there's plenty of achievements and hats to collect that'll keep you busy. The climbing and interacting with people are a little wonky, but not so much that it's unplayable or annoying.Overall it's a fun game! Totes worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I am the kitty in the city, very small and very lost  Lots of collectibles, some are just currency based unlocks and farming isn't overly engaging or hard, and the return home is very short if you go straight to Fish, your obligatory BotW stamina meter. Still, the game is a good bit of healthy fun, even for some quirks like the difficulty in knocking down humans or how generally unpredictable pedestrians can be at times dragging it all out a little.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Watched a friend play, and thought it was super cute. Bought it tonight, and really like it. It's very relaxing and simple. The perfect kind of game to play when you've had a long day and don't want to play something that takes a lot of brain power, or has the stress of "important" objectives or a death counter, etc. Sometimes you just wanna be a silly little cat trying to find its way back home, you know? The level of detail with the game is surprising. Knock a bottle of washing liquid into a sink? It makes bubbles! Smash a jar of jam, and you leave paw prints! Little stuff like that shows just how much care the devs poured into the game. Being able to hide in boxes and nap in sunny spots...it's all so thoughtful. Definitely one of those games you can replay over and over for a good destress.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Best relaxing game after a stressful day. The kitty will do ALL the kitty things, like sit if fits, nap if warm, pounce if bird, but also more daring kitty things, like truce with dog-kind via bone offerings, adorable duckling retrievals and courageous high-risk climbing. In the end of the day, it will keep you delightful company and help you land on four or fewer feet.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: It's such a cute game.The gameplay is good, but the controls could be a bit smoother.All in all it's a cute and successful game with unfortunately a bit little playtime, I wish it was longer and you could do more cheeky things.All in all, I recommend it and hope that there will be more titles like it.However, for what the game offers, 22€ is a bit much. I got it to 100% relatively quickly and am a little disappointed. Nevertheless, I give the game an 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This game rips. I don’t even particularly like cats, and I thoroughly enjoyed causing trouble for the inhabitants of this neighborhood in this game. The developer gives players enough agency that they can h choose to do cattish things, instead of just playing a platformer where the character looks like a cat. It reminds me of Untitled Goose Game, in the best way.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This is a quality not quantity game - my play time as of typing this (4 hours) is casually exploring and completing most of the tasks without a guide and I suspect the game could be speed run run around 2 hours or less if you know what you are doing.As for the game itself ?If the idea of playing as a cat - with all the potentional for mischief that entails - is something you think would be fun then its worth picking up, more so if you can get it at a discount.This game has more in common with Catlateral Damage then stray if you wanted something to compare it to.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: LKBC (Little Kitty Big City) Is a relatively short game that only takes two hours to beat. But that's up to your decision. The game is meant for you to explore and have curiosity (you know like a cat). I'm not too sure what to say, It has very memorializable characters and interesting missions to do. And generally it's very fun. Only problem I have of this game is that it's kind of buggy, I'm pretty sure I got an area that I wasn't supposed to go in just by abusing the parkour system. And other bugs I experienced were: Levitating, Clipping through certain objects, Moving while doing an emote, And jar of money not breaking when hit ground. To summarize it: cat too powerful, cat break game, game cat cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This is what Stray should have been - a playground of collectibles and shenanigans. Movement is open.The main story can be very short - find four fishes to get enough climbing power to get back home, But just doing that would be a MASSIVE DISSERVICE.Find all the extra stuff, steal human sandwiches, and more that I don't want to spoil.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: i'll give a good rating because i think its unfair since i actually enjoyed the time i played it, but just a warning, it is VERY short and VERY buggy, dont expect more than 6 hours of gameplay till you 100% and you will most likely clip into walls atleast twice, its also not one of those games youll play more than twice. overall i dont think it deserves the 25 dollar price tag, i think 10-15 would be more fair, but the game is pretty fun until i completed it and had literally nothing else to do. 6.5/10, could be better or cheaper.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a delightful experience. Though the controls weren't always great I still had a delightful time playing through this. The story is simple and cute and I really felt like I could interact with most things I wanted to interact with. I definitely recommend trying it. I think my biggest "issue" is that it's quite a short game for the price. I spend 7 hours in it to 100% every little thing, but the main story could be finished in 2 hours, maybe less even. Probably worth it to wait for a sale. I loved collecting the hats as well, very fun to customize the kitty as the game went on, it felt very rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: So the first question you probably going to ask... "Is this like Stray?"The answer is: Kindaaaaaa, but there is a lot more to Little Kitty than Stray. While Stray is a darker story, Little Kitty is a lot more cartoony and funny (with lots of puns). You have more control over your cat in Kitty than in Stray and both control great. You can do a lot stuff around the city and all sorts of funny interactions and references to find.Bottom line: Both games are great in their own right! Get both!In my Stray review... I said "11/10 - will Cat again"!! (or something along those lines) And Little Kitty delivered!So once again: "11/10 - I will Cat again"!!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: A short, but very cute game! Slight glitches here and there but this review was made on day 1 of it releasing so I'm not bothered. It's definitely a collectathon with a bunch of cute characters and missions, even a dedicated meow button!  Not only that, but you can find and collect hats for you to wear! Who doesn't love a bit of customization?
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much charm, and is great for anyone of any age.Graphically beautiful.Intuitive controls.Fun characters.Sadly, I wish it were longer. My play time does not entirely reflect how long it took me to beat the game, as I took a few breaks. It only took about 3 hours, and I was trying to explore a lot.I hope more content is added, because it has so much more potential.That said, I cannot recommend this more for what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: A very-very cute and sweet game.The game is not difficult. The city is interesting to explore. Everybody is friendly and everything is good. _childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: (Thanks MMMMMMMMMMM for giving and continuing to remind me to play this game!)I have absolutely no qualms with the game itself.  The game is a great concept of a kitty exploring the big city.  You run, jump, meet other cuties, do tasks, find hats and eventually make your way to the final goal.It's great and awesome, even when my own cat goes on a hunt for the "other cat" every time he hears the kitty meow in the game.  (Which causes me to play without sound...  XD)The problem lies within motion sickness.  I can barely play the game for 15min.  I tried adjusting the settings and even forced myself to "try and get adjusted"...  Only to make it worse.That said, I will have to play the game periodically and in very small increments. _childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: played it first time yesterday for a few hours ! My only gripe was the slow motion pounce for when catching birds, I wish there was a way to turn that off or for it to speed up a bit more. Was ok the first 3 times but for it to force slo motion every single time can be very irritating given collecting those feathers are important for unlocking fast travel points. otherwise, this game is very fun !
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: If you wish to take a break from serious games and play with something fun and cute - then "Little Kitty, Big City" is definanetly for you.It doesn't matter which genre you prefer: shooter, RPG, quest, diabloids or anything else. "Little Kitty" will provide you with warm emothions, mixed with a potion of normal (not hard) platforming and tasks. Moreover, the quests themselves will also be joyfull. Animal characters are very original, with their own strange (but cute) temper.Additional Big Plus for the average time of gameplay. The authors made no attempt to make it long, very long or very-very long. Made no attempt to create "adventure for 40-80 hours".It takes 10-15 hours to complete main story with additional tasks.----------------Verdict: 10 fluffy kitties form 10!And "Meow!", recommended for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Bubby GamingLooks good, runs nice, you play as a void bubbyThere's a couple movement bugs with jumping and a few softlocks (running around in a circle and taking a picture, one time i tried jumping in a trash can,  but was too close so Kitty just froze waiting to jump in and never jumped. Ultimately cats IRL have buggy movement like this too so I'll excuse it.It's a fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: My daughter and I have been playing this game together and I feel it is wholesome and fun - a great game for adults, and suitable for elementary aged kids to play together with a parent or older sibling. My kiddo has a lot of fun catching birds, and isn't too focused on the tasks and how to achieve them... ;)With regard to tasks, I will say it is difficult sometimes to figure out where things are located within a building - while I understand the map is supposed to be somewhat crude based on the storyline, it can sometimes appear that an item or character is in the next building over. So far we haven't run across a quest that has proven extra difficult or impossible, but as I said, younger kids will probably need some help. It's been a fun adventure and has a lot of nice little touches that cat-lovers will appreciate. I'd be interested in a DLC if one becomes available or sequel where perhaps you play from the perspective of another of the city's residents.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say "cat, what a good game!" but I just can't. Controls are sadly very bad, both on controller and keyboard. Main character doesn't feel like a cat, no. It feels like you are playing a robot in cat's skin. Back legs just "follow" your front ones, jumps have to be manually adjusted every time, movement overall is clunky and feels stiff. Spyro feels more cat-like than this cat character.Another negative thing is how you get those non skippable animation of "terrified cat" whenever you get close to the water and some items. I would say, like, fine, whatever, but sometimes the water hitbox is not even in the water! You get launched from it even from afar! Nonsense with cucumber where you on your own drop it and get scared by it is also very annoying. Honestly, its overall very annoying with how it's used everywhere with how long it is.   Bugs, many bugs. You go through walls, through items, through everything. Jumping is a complete disaster in that case as well - have fun flying through the map.  Missed customization opportunities: hats, yes, cool, but there could be so much more - coats, costumes, other types of fur. I am a big fan of animal games and I've been waiting for this one for a really long time but those issues beat even my wish to play...

_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Little Kitty, Big City is undeniably charming, offering a whimsical and delightful experience that captivated me from the start. As an adorable cat exploring a vibrant urban environment, the game excels in creating a fun and engaging atmosphere. I thoroughly enjoyed my time playing, relishing every moment of the cute antics and clever puzzles.However, despite its charm and the enjoyment it provided, I find it difficult to recommend this game to others, primarily due to the playability-to-price ratio. After completing 31 out of 39 achievements and taking my time to explore every nook and cranny, I clocked in only around 7 hours of gameplay. This included two crashes that slightly delayed my progress.Given the game's price point of $25, I expected a bit more content to justify the cost. While the game is a delightful experience, its relatively short duration leaves much to be desired for players seeking a longer, more immersive journey. If the price were lower, it would be easier to recommend, but as it stands, I feel the game doesn't offer enough value for its current price.If you're okay with a brief but enjoyable adventure and don't mind the higher cost, Little Kitty, Big City could be a great addition to your collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR : It's a good game, if you feel like you might enjoy it, give it a try. However, if the price scares you, abstain until you feel the purchase is right for you.Edit, 100%ed the game in 6.8 hours, my judgement still stands, though a tad disappointed.I've just finished the game, and what a great time. I'm surprised myself I've only played three hours of the game, as it truly felt like I had played more. I have almost all the hats, finished most of the main quests, and plan on trying to 100% it.The graphics are rustic, cartoony, delightful really, they don't try too hard but achieve exactly what they set out to do, and honestly I have no complaints, the game looks even splendid at times honestly.The world and level design is intricate, full of surprises, there's always something hidden, you might not always succeed in everything you set out to do but through failure you might discover something new !The interactions are quite fun as well, the game through its world makes you feel like you being a cat is at the core of the experience, couldn't really replace the cat with a small person for instance.And the characters are simple yet delightful, and the ending really makes you feel like you got to know them and everything. And because of all of that, I really really recommend this game, it's no masterpiece, but you have a really good time with it.However, I have a few complaints, which I feel is a shame.First, the movement. The movement is easy to pick up, hard to master. I'm very much fine with that, I'd even say it plays an important role in the enjoyment of the game. However, for something that is at the core of the game, many times I found myself glitching into colliders, not properly climbing an object or simply not climbing an object that I thought perfectly climbable, and which is, but some dark magic prevented me to climb it, other times, I'll be sent flying around. This often happens because I jump and run at the same time, and it's very much possible the developer did not imagine that a troglodyte like me would try to run through the entire game.The other complaint I need to voice, despite honestly not feeling like it is a fair complaint, given this is an indie title that is well worth its price if we account for development time and everything, but society yadayada... is the price to completion time ratio. While I have not finished the game, I have seen most of what it offers in 3 hours, if anything, I could have finished it in 2 since I didn't need the extra stamina and did not care for some of the extra stuff. But, as stated previously, I plan on 100%ing the game, and honestly I think those who have paid for the game will want to as well, to make their purchase worth the price, and also to honor the devs, cause this is a really fun game.

Also jumping and the kitty not catching correctly sucked big time. I think they had too little time to make decent quality assurance in a hurry to publish and get munny. _childDocuments_.review: It's a rare game that makes me want to achievement farm just so I have a reason to keep playing it. Despite its jankiness in some areas (like clipping through the world geometry and getting stuck, being flung into the middle of the ocean from a fan turning on right next to you, or the glass jars containing shinies that simply refuse to break), the charming art direction and simple yet engaging gameplay draw me in in a way I can't, and indeed don't want to, resist. I've beaten the whole thing twice now just so I can see the ending again.The devs are working on ironing out the janky bits but the game is wholly playable from start to finish. You can do everything there is to do in a little less than 6 hours, maybe more if you get stuck and have to restart (rare, but I've seen reports of it happening). If you know what you're doing, you can plow through everything in a brief couple of hours. It's a snack of a game, but well worth the asking price as far as I'm concerned.

_childDocuments_.review: Given my two options for a review, I feel more positive than negative about Little Kitty Big City, but the game has some notable issues a prospective player should know. Firstly, my positives: the game seems to do all it set out to do; it is a light, fluffy game about playing as a cat. It is a third-person sandbox platformer (with notable goat simulator inspiration) with some mildly funny dialog and characters. The art style works well for the tone and is consistently nice to look at (witness the kitty, for they are adorable). I also want to commend whoever did the camera, as it worked fantastically with almost no issues throughout my entire playtime.The most important negative is that the traversal feels terrible to me. The traversal system is based on a charged and aimed jump that ends up feeling super clunky and is combined with a BOTW/TOTK style climbing system (the climbing is fine, but it feels super slow). On top of this, sprinting and clipping a wall (or sometimes the air) results in fully losing your momentum and bouncing back with a stun animation that is cute the first few times, but quickly gets annoying when you are just trying to get around.Overall, I would say not to expect anything revolutionary, but I had a somewhat positive time and was able to 100% it (with some frankly tedious grinding) in a weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Little Kitty, Big City is a fun, vibrant bite-sized adventure. You play the eponymous Kitty who falls out of a window and must find the way back home. On the way, you come across the many denizens of the unnamed Big City (or is the city actually named Big City? It's unclear but I like the idea), many of whom are friendly other animals that give you missions, items or gameplay tips. The presentation and writing are so endearing, that I found myself smiling the entire time I was playing this game. While Stray would be the first game that may come up as a point of comparison, the better analogue would be Untitled Goose Game. As the player Kitty, you mostly annoy or create mischief for the inhabitants of the Big City on your way home and it is honest to goodness, pleasant sandbox fun. The controls are solid, aside from a few janky portions, and I had a great time scaling the buildings and patrolling the streets. It should be noted that most people will likely complete the main objective of this game within 2 to 4 hours and probably need 5ish additional hours to mop up all of the optional content. This is not a deterrent for me, personally, because I love a nicely crafted unique experience even if it is not a long game, but I know some players may balk at the game's price given that information. Regardless, I would recommend LKBC to anyone looking for a nice breezy time, even if it is not a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, it's great 🤣 I mean, what would you expect from the game that let's you be a cat? To cat, of course, and that it does quite well Aside from shoving everything down from high places, zooming and hitting walls, chasing tail, jumping when scared or stepping into the water, there is also a storyline, but obviously it's not as important as catting around. Oh, and you can hunt birds, **but** you always release them after, so sweetThe controls are quite responsive and allow for some precision when needed, at least with the controller (the game recommends to use one). There's some getting used to it, for instance jump will be precise if you hold it and it will not exactly follow the trajectory you see. Crawling on top of objects is a bit lacking but I guess that may change later in game.I will update a review when I'm further in game or finished it, but so far it's a great fun without much thought behind. _childDocuments_.review: A fun, wonderful and adorable little game. The cat controls smoothly and behaves much like you'd expect a cat to. Gameplay consists of solving some relatively simple environmental puzzles and collecting items to progress by speaking to NPCs.This game should particularly appeal to a younger audience. It's not complex, and offers a lot of room for some sandbox fun being an adorable little menace. Some of the writing feels very current and might date the game significantly or go over younger players' heads, but it doesn't detract from just how fun it is to be a cat.

It doesn't really have a big story, but a lot of funny moments, and again, a lot of opportunities to be a little cat doing cat things. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and would love to give it a positive review, but there are 2 major things that make the game more of a meh experience.1. The Movement - the movement of the cat feels clunky and is a bit buggy. More often then not, the jumps are not smooth and the cat will not fully climb onto an object like it should. Trying to get up to great heights is more of a pain then an enjoyable experience. Curbs are also one of your biggest enemies. There were many times I was running across the street and I would get stopped because the cat could not automatically step up onto a curb that was only a few inches tall. _childDocuments_.review: Little Kitty, Big City is basically what happens when a cat decides that world domination starts with knocking over trash cans. Every leap, pounce, and knock-off-the-shelf moment is a reminder that cats truly rule the world—they just let us live in it.In short, Little Kitty, Big City is a hilarious, purrfectly chaotic adventure where being a tiny menace has never been so fun!

_childDocuments_.review: This was a cute little sandbox game where you play as a cat. It's a great little open world, that opens up the more you play around and explore. It's got a lot of little objectives in it to play around with, and stuff to discover. There is no health bar, you can't take fall damage, you can't die. You're just a cat lost in the city trying to get home. You will meet many animals who have personalities that liven up the conversation parts of the game, which isn't a ton. It's well made, and pretty looking in its art style. The cat's meow is very cute. The achievements for the most part are easy to get, outside of one bugged one, and 2 tedious ones, so there is replay value. You can get all the achievements depending on RNG (for one of the tedious ones and the bugged one, RNG is a factor on it) in probably 6-15 hours. It took me 10 hours playing leisurely and not really rushing. You can "Beat" the main game in about an hour and a half, which is the goal, go home. This of course means you go straight home without exploring or having much fun. There aren't skins to unlock for the cat, it's a black cat, which I like black cats so that's fine with me. There are tons of little hats to unlock though.Cons:1: 1 Achievement, where you get someone to slip on a banana is bugged. It's very RNG dependent if it triggers. I did the same thing for 30 minutes and it just popped eventually, with no change.2:1 Achievement where you get 20 people to take a photo of you is also very dependent on RNG. Most of my NPCs would just scold me, and it seemed I had to carry scissors in my mouth to startle them, then drop it and meow spam til they took a photo. While the rest of the game's achievements are easy and lax to do, it's weird to  have two all of a sudden you have to "grind" for. This of course only matters if you want to 100%, if you just want to play around this part doesn't matter.  It's a cute little game so I wanted to get them all.3: Another achievement "Litter picker" is a bit tedious, but it's not hard at all. Just odd that everything else requires 5-20 things, and this one requires 100. Not hard though at all, just a minor gripe.4: I found a few bugs. The first of which the emoticons have to be selected a few times before they actually work. Another bug, is the pounce mode for birds, which is arguably not fun to do, sometimes you get stuck in pounce mode. Sometimes also the slow motion for pounce mode triggers at random even when not pouncing at a bird. Lastly, I found a place to fall through the map. It's easy to get to, early game, and easy to replicate every time. If you do this, you have to load your last save. You can't die, you can't respawn, you can't warp back or fast travel. You have to reload the game. Which if you haven't saved or have auto-save off can be a big bummer. I got there by just exploring, I thought it was part of the map. I got on the train tracks and was walking and poof. Then I found out you're not supposed to get on the train tracks, but like I said it's really easy to get to.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was absolutely delightful. Now before I start, I don’t think it is worth the asking price, I bought it on sale and from there I cannot recommend enough. Don’t expect an action packed game with high stakes, it’s definitely not that, but if you’re in the market for a game called “little kitty, big city” you’re probably not expecting that. This game is for cat lovers and I say that as an adult male that has no shame admitting this is one of the best experiences I’ve had gaming in a while. It is essentially an open world sandbox cat simulator, you’ll make friends with various other animals and do cat things, like sit in boxes, find places to nap and either claw or cuddle humans.Some of the quests are definitely satire and out of the realm of realism but it is also a cartoon, which is fun and adds to the vibe of the game. It is also a short game.Not much in the way of a story, except that you fell from your home apartment and have to find your way back up. There’s no risk, or violence or any twists and turns, however this is actually a really nice change of pace. Most games I play these days are kill X person, drive to Y etc. so having a fun innocent game is really refreshing. I decided to go with this over Stray for the warmer and more upbeat tone, they’re like sister games in a way, Stray being the darker/edgier older sibling.Now the game definitely isn’t perfect, it is from an indie developer and that can be felt. There are some bugs and the movement isn’t always fluid and can feel clunky. I have gotten stuck in walls and had to reload save files, luckily the save system is extremely quick. In 100%ing the game some of the achievements can also feel a little tedious. I also noticed a spelling mistake/typo in some of the dialogue text.Lastly I played this game on the Steam Deck and it runs great. Doesn’t take up lots of storage and ran at full speed on a 6W TDP, meaning you can play it for a long time without running down your battery life.TLDR: This is a great, fresh and innocent game for cat lovers of all ages that runs great on the Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: I only just heard about Little Kitty, Big City about a week before it was to be released, but due to my love of Cats, Platformers, and Sandbox Adventure Games, it seemed like something that I would most likely enjoy, so I figured that I'd check it out eventually, but once I learned that it was to be included with a subscription to Game Pass, I knew it was something that I had to check out as soon as possible. So without further ado, let's get into the Nitty-Gritty of Little Kitty, Big City.Little Kitty, Big City is a rather graphically simplistic game by modern standards, but that's fine because the real meat is in the gameplay, where it belongs. Nevertheless, the game manages to have a cute, charming, and endearing artstyle which is pleasing to the eye. While there isn't a whole lot of detail in the graphics, there's a surprising amout of variety in the overall design of the city itself, so the overall attention to detail is actually rather impressive.The Jazz music that makes up the game's soundtrack suits both the slinking feline protagonist as well as the urban environment of the city perfectly, although I can't quite put my finger on why that is exactly. The sound effects are mostly what you'd expect, although the odd "whoosh" it makes when you jump or climb sounds rather awkward, it is if nothing else, unique.Little Kitty, Big City is best described as a hybrid between a Sandbox Adventure Game and a 3D Platformer. As Kitty, you explore a open world environment both by running through the city, crawling under gaps in fences or through narrow cracks in walls, climbing vines, jumping between various objects, grabbing ledges and pulling yourself up/over walls. It's fun and engaging without being too challenging or frustrating for less experienced players to enjoy. There are no injuries to be sustained, no nine lives to be lost, and therefore no GAME OVER screens for failing to make a jump and falling from a great height. In typical feline fashion, Kitty always lands on their feet after a fall, thus making the game accessible and fun to players of all ages.As you travel through the city you'll find a number of friendly animals who need help in various ways and will assign Kitty with various tasks, offering a variety of awards for completing them. You'll collect Shinies — assorted bits of metal — which serve as the game's main unit of currency that can be given to Crow in exchange for cosmetic Hats for Kitty to wear as they traverse the city in style, Fish to increase Kitty's stamina which enables them to climb for longer periods of time, and Feathers — earned by sneaking up on birds then (harmlessly) pounching on them — which can be given to Tanooki in exchange for opening up manhole portals, enabling Kitty to fast travel between them.One lazy affternoon, while taking a nap on the ledge outside of their master's apartment window, Kitty carelessly slips off the ledge and falls a great distance to the city streets below, fortunately having their fall broken by landing in trash can. Upon climbing out of the trash can, Kitty finds themselves too weak from hunger to climb all the way back up, but fortunately a friendly Crow offers to Kitty some helpful advice as well as assistance on how they can find Fish around town to eat in order to replenish their Stamina. From there, Kitty embarks on a wild misadventure, traveling through the City, making new friends along the way, on a quest to return home before the day is through.Admittedly, the game is not without a few bugs, but fortunately I experienced nothing game-breaking during my playthrough. Mostly just a few mildly annoying issues with collision detection which would prevent Kitty from grabbing onto ledges reliably or colliding with solid objects correctly, which made progressing through the game take a bit longer than it otherwise would have, but fortunately didn't set me back much. One extremely helpful bit of advice given to me by a friend is to SAVE OFTEN, especially during sequences which require a lot of platforming, that way if something goes wrong you can just reload your save without having to start all over.Little Kitty, Big City is a short yet sweet game which can be completed within about 4 to 6 hours, yet could last up to 10 hours for a Completionist Run. I enjoyed the game so much that I decided to go for 100% in order to really get the most out of the game. Once I had finished, I was so pleased by the experience that I decided to purchase the game on PC, just to support the Developers and have another go at it at a later date. It's currently included with a Game Pass Subscription, so I highly recommend that you check it out while it's still available on Game Pass, but it's definitely worth full price at just under $25, let alone any sale price it may receive at a future date. If you love cute animals, open-world sandbox gameplay with platforming, items to collect and objectives to complete, then don't miss out on Little Kitty, Big City.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an adorably fun game about a cat exploring a small part of a Japanese-themed city, solving puzzles, and interacting with some other furry (or not so furry) friends.  It's very wholesome with simple controls and mechanics, and if you are looking for a cute game with engaging exploration that won't take up too much of your time, you're in the right spot.The game itself isn't very long.  I 100%'ed the game at 8.3 hours, minus two grindy achievements that I just don't want to do.  Finding everything will probably take 5-10 hours for most players depending on playstyle.I expect many "non-gamers" will want to try this game, so I'll mention that there's nothing (so far) that requires any particularly quick reflexes, the controls are simple and easy to learn, and the gameplay is generally quite intuitive and uses common sense.  My non-gamer mother is playing as well, and while she got lost in the tutorial area at first, she got up to speed with everything quickly after.Finally, you will NOT like this game if you are looking for a fast-paced, difficult, AAA feature-length game.  If that's you, don't buy it then complain; you were warned.

_childDocuments_.review: Took me just under 8 hours to 100% the game. Would've been about 7 hours if I had skipped the last two achievements.Fantastic art style and a very engaging environment. _childDocuments_.review: Excellent 3-4 hours of fun traversal and exploration, that might end up being more if you want to go achievement hunting.  Well-written and memorable characters.  Fun and interactive world.  Has an over-arching goal, but really lets you enjoy just being "Cat" for as long as you want without pressure.  Mechanics are simple and rewarding.  The world is well-communicated through visual cues.  If you see something you think should be worth exploring, it usually is.One of the more satisfying little fuzzy romps I've had recently.  10/10, no notes.  Would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Kitty, Big City exceeded my expectations. I highly recommend to the casual player like myself. It's easy, fun, and cute with small challenges to keep you engaged and easy to walk away from and come back too. I'm pretty sure one of the "hours of playtime" I have (when I wrote this) was I just let the cat just nap for like, an hour while I went and made myself dinner. The dialog is cute and made me chuckle/laugh a few times too.It is like Stray in that you're a cat that explores the city and is trying to find a way out. Its a bit less stressful, though (nothing against Stray at all, I loved that too!). I recommend it especially after a long day and you just want something to take your mind away for a while. I also recommend it for cat lovers/owners for (hopefully) obvious reasons.Good job devs! I really like what you did and it was done very well! You can tell that you put a lot of love into it too! Thank you for making something fun and lovable! I hope you had as much fun making it as I am playing it!

_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:1. Role-playing as a cat is fun2. All of the animals are cute3. The city feels distinctly and cohesively Japanese (with the exception of all the trash everywhere). They nailed just about everything, down to the curvature of the guardrails on the side of the road.Cons:1. Movement. The platforming complexity is very basic, which is a necessity given the control system limitations. Every jump is a charge-up, which interrupts movement flow constantly. Every jump also has a targeting parabola, but it's imprecise. It's practically impossible to do a running jump. It's possible to wall jump, but it's never useful and very easy to do unintentionally - and often actively harmful, since they project you very far from narrow ledges which inevitably sends you back to the ground. Running leads to frequent head bonking, which again interrupts movement flow constantly.2. There isn't much to do. There's an hour or two of meaningful content at best, with game time padded out heavily with item collection grinding. There are some interesting locations to explore, but they are surprisingly small and few. The city is so small that you can run anywhere in a few minutes.3. Controllers. I couldn't emote at all with PS5 controller, which hurts a lot of the cat role-play fun.4. Clipping. There are invisible boundaries, invisible surfaces, things that look like surfaces but don't support you. I also fell through the ground a couple times. Thankfully there is a debug menu that can teleport you, and the pause menu seems to sometimes do some sort of "unstuck" thing as a side-effect of the camera shift.It's a mildly entertaining game, but price is very high for this quality level. Unless you are committed to role-playing as a cat, there are many other games that provide better value. Unfortunately, I'm still waiting for an animal simulation game with fluid controls, non-trivial mechanics, and a satisfying amount of content.

The enviroment is rather cartoony with strong coloured version of Japan. A pleasant place to have the zooomies and explore, and there are charming and funny animal friends to get to know. The humans are all faceless, a little creepy, other than that they are just props for the majestic cat adventure and achievements.Capturing birds and then realse them, no harm done!ALSO SO MANY CUTE HATS!! <3Is fairly easy 100% the game, but is a little tedious. Recycling 100 cans takes long time to collect, either trip people to get their cans or restart the save to bump into vending machines.I forgot to mention the music in my previous iterations of this review.. Is just chill jazz music, just one track! But is enough for this game, it does not feel annoying or repetative. And just melts into a background sound.Tripping the humans, was either too easy - accidentally tripping them when getting petted.Or difficult to trip - I want to make them faceplant, or slipp on a banana .. An achievement got bugged, and I had to replay the game to 100% it. One is to complete the whole to do list. It was comepleted but it did not get registered. Also the dumpster diving achievement did not trigger either. I had accidentally headbutted a trashcan, not diving into it, don't know if it effected the achievement or not, yet the list in game saw the diving as completed. I was also playing offline, but other achievements worked fine except for dumpster diving.. All in all though a relaxing game 8/10And best played with a controller

_childDocuments_.review: Take the art style and cheekiness from Untitled Goose Game, mix them with an adorable feline protagonist and silly physics-based shenaningans from Stray, and you get a cute, relaxing game about a little kitty searching for his way home, and making a lot of friends along the way.+++Pros-the main quest can be over in less than 4 hours, if you want to (but that would kinda defeat the whole cozy vibe)-after you end the game, you are free to keep exploring and completing side quests at your leisure-the art style is simple, but works really well to create a really chill cartoony atmosphere-it's clear that a lot of care was put to create moments that will make you go "awwww" and fill your heart with glee-interaction with other characters, both human and animal, is always amusing-you can be a cheeky little one and break stuff/trip over humans/steal food-the photo mode gives you full control of the camera, so you have total freedom to create any kind of shot you want!-hats! ---Cons-Some bugs with jumping/landing happen sometimes, mostly just visual though (cat jittering, reclining and so on)-Jump projection UI not very precise, you might miss some jumps that seemed feasible-Interaction range is sometimes weird. I had issues with the crow that sells you hats specifically, having to find the precise spot that would make the interaction available. Another time, I was able to gather Shinies through a closed gate. I'm sure that most of the cons are bugs/polish that will be addressed with future patches/hotfixes, so I wouldn't mind them too much. tl;dr being a cat is great and the game is fun and relaxing, I recommend it :3

_childDocuments_.review: Is "cat" a game genre now? Because it certainly should be.Little Kitty, Big City captures the essence of being a cat -- being a total nuisance, that is, while simultaneously charming the heck out of the humans both in the game and in real life. The risk-free exploration and cat-friendly city made gameplay chill and relaxing, and it's a perfect follow-up game for Stray after all of its stressful moments... and look, I love Stray. Stray is easily in the top half of my "best games ever top 10" list. But it tied my stomach into knots and made me ugly cry, and after finishing it the first time, I was literally shaking and sobbing.But this? This is just pure bliss. No danger. No risk. Just cat doing cat things, messing with the city and its people, meeting adorable silly critters of all kinds. This game is soothing balm for the frayed nerves.🐾  If yes, the game is well worth the full price despite its short playtime.Otherwise, I would consider:+ game is very cute!+ gameplay is fun!+ no collectable or achievement is too frustrating to get- wish the city was larger and there were more things to do and to collect

_childDocuments_.review: Little Kitty, Big City is such a joyful game! Playing a cat who does typical cat things and is a little mischievous but overall is there to help others out as well on his journey to find a way back home.  ~5 hours 1/10 1 Yes, I used  No Yes, 1 achievement: talk to the ducklings before doing the objective to bring them home. Each one has a small quest before they will follow you, talk with them first, that way they will tell you why they won't follow you instantly and that counts toward the "hello" achievement in which you have to talk with all the animals in the neighborhood.  The one to get 20 times photographed is a bit grindy, but if you wear a hat as soon as possible and meow to every person with a phone in their hand, you get already a bunch of them while doing the rest.  No No No No No difficulty setting, but there is no combat or anything else that will make you fail NoI love that we see so many wholesome games in which you play someone who is a little mischievous but in general, a good person/animal while exploring their world. This game reminds me so much of Lil Gator Game, Tiny Terry's Turbo Trip, and Rain on Your Parade. The open world in which you're free to explore but find a bunch of things to do is so addictive to me and it offers so many directions for a game to take. You play as a cat in this game who was sleeping but then falls out of the window and you don't have the strength atm to climb back up, you first need to eat something. so your main quest will be to find food, but on your journey, you'll meet several other animals who all can use a little bit of your time to help them out. I adored this little kitty and the typical cat things you can do, like swapping items so they break or stretching in a typical cat way. There also is this meow button to get the attention of the humans that walk around in the city. some of those are happy to see you, others ignore you or are even angry already... let alone if you let them trip :P. The only slightly negative thing I can think of is that jumping feels a bit awkward, but it allows you to hold the button down so you can more precise jumps, which I almost used exclusively at the moment I stopped with just pressing the jump button as an automatic response. So it took a bit of time to unlearn the normal quick button press to jump but it gave me more control over my little kitty. I struggled a bit with finding my way in the city, but this is totally a "me" problem. I am very bad with having a general sense of direction and a lot of the city quite looks the same. somehow I always thought the fisherman is South, but he is NorthWest as an example. And the way the map opens with the turn of the camera from your view to the map made it a little more confusing. While the arrow on the map correctly shows you which way you're looking, so it shouldn't be a problem, but it was just not making sense in my head. I love the type of achievements this game has. Just doing a bunch of stuff and getting achievements for doing them. The achievement for meeting every animal can be missable (as far as guides online tell me) but who wouldn't talk with the cute ducklings before pulling them out of their situation and taking them home? Knowing that you have to talk with those 4 before "saving" them is enough to play the game without a guide. However, I would highly recommend wearing a hat as soon as possible and start meowing to everybody who holds a phone from that moment on, because there is an achievement for which 20 people have to take a picture of you. I highly recommend first going for the fish and going home, because after you finish the main quest you'll see the collectibles on your map, which just makes it so much easier. The rest of the achievements are basically just for helping everybody and collecting all the hats. I give Little Kitty, Big City 4 out of 5 stars. A short but wonderful adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly fun and adorable, however I cannot recommend it in its current state or at its current price.The game is plagued with bug, game breaking and otherwise, that make playing it incredibly cumbersome and unpleasant. Platforming frequently breaks or fails to function correctly. More often than I would care to have kept track of the game dumped me off the side of a wall or a perch for no reason. Jumping feels horrible most of the time and for a platforming game to have fundamentally busted platforming is a bad sign. On top of all that, movement is broadly cumbersome and I frequently would teleport through walls when the game couldn't figure out what to do with me if I turned around close to a wall.Secondly, the game is INCREDIBLY short. While taking my time, getting stuck, and exploring every nook and cranny I could find I beat the game in 2 hours. I feel like it ought be said, $25 for a barely 2 hour game is just too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ much. I'm not a fan of measuring a games quality on a dollar-per-hour ratio or whatever, but for a game this short and buggy, $25 is not worth it.I hope to be able to recommend this game in the future, maybe with some patches and hopefully some content updates this could be a really fun and worthwhile game, but until such time I have refunded the game and would not recommend buying it for more than $10, and honestly I wouldn't buy it for that either.

_childDocuments_.review: Little Kitty, Big City is set in an endearing world filled with charming characters and a delightful atmosphere. The design of both the environment and the characters are cute, which adds to the game's appeal. Each of the characters possess distinct personalities, and I looked forward to meeting the next character on my kitty adventure.The game reminded me of Untitled Goose Game, another game that shares a similar whimsical tone with mischievous gameplay elements. The game's pacing maintains a steady rhythm that kept me engaged throughout. Each objective felt purposeful, ensuring I always felt I was making progress. Despite its brevity, the game concludes before feeling repetitive.I did experience some occasional bugs, including clipping through walls. Fortunately, the game autosaves frequently which mitigated these setbacks, allowing me to resume my progress without losing any of the items I had collected. One aspect that fell short of expectations was the climbing mechanics, which felt sluggish and prone to frustrating falls. Despite this, Little Kitty, Big City is undeniably a fun experience and worth full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: What a joy!Is it a little clunky in places? Yeah. Did I care or did it ruin the experience? Nope! I had so much fun running around the city, interacting with everything, and just generally being a menace to everything and everyone around me. If you’ve ever watched a cat push things needlessly off the edge of surfaces and thought: why did they do that!? This game answers that question. It feels so good to be this annoying and adorable at the same time. There are parts of the game that I genuinely found so funny, and the millennial internet cat humour kept me amused. I’d probably recommend getting it on sale as the content is completed pretty quickly but if you want something cute, silly, and cosy to pass the time you’ll be pleased with LKBC.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so what is Little Kitty, Big City? I'm not going to go into a lot of detail, as it's a very short game, only taking at least a minimum of 3.9 hours to complete, so don't expect my full, exact opinion on the game.First of all, the visuals: It's cute, charming, and not to mention the hats just make even it better, by an entire tenfold.The audio is generally great too. The music is good, the (supposed) "voice acting" of the many animals in this are good, and it's just generally a good quality of the game.Second: The gameplay. This game is honestly pretty fun. The gameplay (like the visuals) is generally charming, and fun. While, yes, there may be some bugs, those bugs (as far as I'm aware) don't really do much, besides from slightly messing up the animations for 1 second max.Third: Replayability. While this game is marketed as a sandbox game (I think), I don't feel like it would be very replayable of you've already finished the whole thing.So, what do I think about this game? It's really good, honestly. Has a lot of good qualities to it, the visuals, audio, gameplay, and just overall, a lot of aspects are good. And to the one singular person who thought this game was bad, and just a general joke that costed 20 dollars, just wanted to let you know that your brain must be made of compressed Chic-Fil-A Sauce if you SERIOUSLY took 2 whole f###ing hours to get past the first part of the game.9.2/10, would recommend to silly little goobers who have way too much free time.(i finally finished the game!!! :) )

_childDocuments_.review: I've already seen bits and pieces of lets plays, and I'm sharing my initial impressions based on the experience of watching and playing. Pros:Visuals: The visual are truly pleasant and enjoyable to immerse myself in, if a bit derivative of the goose game at times. The Main Cats movement animations are excellent, and really capture that cat feel. Music: The music is calming and suiting for the game. It's the sort that I think I could enjoy just leaning back and reading a book, or enjoying with a cup of tea. It adds to the overall chill vibes of the game. Gameplay: On the whole this game handles great and feels good to play. The character flows around very smoothly, and the environments are fun to explore and visually interesting. The tasks range the full gambit of familiar cat activities, which make for surprisingly appropriate gameplay loops. Similarly the way you slink around the city from the felines perspective really satisfies a childhood daydream that I'm sure we've all had. Cons: Glitches. There's a lot of them. I experienced my first two game breaking glitches within the first 30 seconds of booting up the game, literally. The first was that my PC was properly recognizing my controller, but the game wasn't. The second was that my character was animation locked the moment he came out of the trash bin. One required a reboot, and the other required that I quit and reload. Writing. Some of the writing is a bit poor, and tedious. Audio. There is an ASMR quality to some of the sounds that I do not like. They are quiet, but still sharp on the ear. Nitpick:The game has a lot of clipping, even in the very first zone, and a subtle lack of polish to it. EDIT: Got all the achievements and finished the gameThis an a great game that nonetheless falls just shy of its promise. The world progression is quite good, and well handled, and the set pieces are really nice. There's some clever stuff in here like the builder not chasing you off if you're wearing a helmet. The content density in the world is just about right, with just the right amount of backtracking to rediscover things. On the other hand, Some of the movement isn't quite organic.Some of the sounds could use some polish to be less repetitive and less harsh on the ears. That ASRM quality to some sounds can be quite unpleasant at times. There's a lot of small stuff that lacks polish, the way the balls move feels bad. The way some of the vents affect you feels bad. Some of the quests don't quite feel right. This game needs another hour of gameplay or so to feel fully realized (And feel like good value for money.)
