_childDocuments_.review: This game was a really relaxing and fun experience!Gameplay:Straightforward and easy, I played with keyboard so the movement did feel a bit heavyhowever they do recommend a controller, it was still a good experience and pretty easy to control in the endGraphics:Adorable, the animations are super clean and the overall style is consistent. Only complaint I would give is there are several objects Z fighting which is a bit spacey to look at (for people who don't know what it is, its when 2 objects are at the exact same spot, thus the computer is not sure which one to load and thus it starts to flicker)Story:Simple and to the point, I personally enjoy this a lot as its really a laid back gameTime to complete:To just finish the game I would say it is about 1-2 hours, for full completion about 7 hoursachievements:Overall pretty easy and fast, my only complaints are the NPC related quests, some NPCs I can not knock over as I just clip trough them and a lot of them ignore me when I try to get their attention. This made my last achievement the most tedious . This achievement entailed to get pictures taken from 20 NPCs.I would not have mind it if the NPCs responded more consistent and did not have a 50/50 chance to have collision or notPrice:I personally think for the amount of enjoyment I got and as someone who 100% it, it was pretty worth it, especially to support a smaller game studio. However for the amount of playtime without achievement hunting I think it is a bit more on the pricier side, I do 100% recommend it as a purchase when it is on saleConclusion:Game is pretty fun and relaxing, super beginner friendly and beautiful, I 100% recommend it if its on sale or if you want to 100% the game, if you are just in it for the story then I am not sure if you would get the 24,50 out of it.Full price I say its a 6/10On sale: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: In the grim, dark future of Little Kitty Mega City, there is only war... no, wait, wrong game.At its heart, this is an interactive children's book.  You explore a pretty, vertical cityscape (reminiscent of Shashingo, if you played that, but much larger) with no scary moving automobiles; you talk to animal friends (and they are all friends, though some dogs are initially scary); you do some very gentle platforming.  The animations when unlocking a new hat are especially charming.  The concurrent hat-unlock dad jokes, well, maybe a little less so, but that's my only complaint about the writing.  Grimdark, this ain't.I played it on a Steam Deck, in a series of hotel rooms near a major metropolitan hospital, where I was supporting a family member.  It was and still is cute and comforting, and very comfortable on the Deck, though it drains battery much more quickly than one might expect.  I look forward to picking away at the achievements as the hospital visits continue.I would recommend this to anybody who finds comfort in children's writing and enjoys the cat nature.

_childDocuments_.review: Pure, uncut cuteness and feel-good whimsy injected right into your ears and eyeballs.It's a short experience, but so much kitty joy packed into every moment.  Every detail is lovingly crafted from obvious cat fans, from the simple trot of our kitty's walk cycle, to the various emotes and idles, and even the meow itself.  And yes, there is a meow button.The central plot of the kitty wanting to climb back up home at the upper floors of a very tall building is engaging enough for as long as it lasts, but much fun is also to be had just exploring, collecting, and achievement-hunting.  There are other animal friends to find, and they're all full of character and delightful detail.Easily accessible for players of any age, there's no violence or sadness to be found anywhere.  Catching birds is "catch-and-release", there are no moving vehicles, everything is cartoony and bright, and there are no time constraints to be found.Such a good time. <3

_childDocuments_.review: Little Kitty, Big City, developed by Double Dagger Studio, is an enchanting and delightful open-world adventure game that captures the playful spirit of a curious cat exploring a bustling urban environment. With its charming graphics, engaging gameplay, and heartwarming interactions, this game is a must-play for cat lovers and adventure seekers alike. As you guide a spirited little kitty on a quest to find its way home, you'll discover a vibrant city filled with surprises, new friends, and countless opportunities for mischief and fun.The game invites players into a beautifully crafted open-world city that feels both expansive and inviting. The detailed environments, from bustling streets to serene parks, are brought to life with vibrant colors and whimsical design. The city is a true playground for exploration, offering a plethora of hidden nooks, interesting landmarks, and interactive elements that make every moment spent wandering feel fresh and exciting.At the heart of Little Kitty, Big City is its intuitive and delightful gameplay. The game strikes a perfect balance between guided objectives and freeform exploration. As the little kitty, you have the freedom to roam the city at your own pace, complete quests, help fellow animal friends, or simply cause a bit of chaos—true to a cat's nature. The game's mechanics are easy to grasp, making it accessible for players of all ages while still offering depth and variety to keep seasoned gamers engaged.One of the game's standout features is its cast of colorful and chatty animal characters. From wise old dogs to quirky pigeons, each character you encounter has a unique personality and story to share. The quests you undertake are varied and entertaining, ranging from simple fetch tasks to more intricate puzzles, all infused with humor and heart. These interactions add a layer of richness to the game, making your journey feel meaningful and rewarding.A delightful aspect of Little Kitty, Big City is the ability to customize your kitty with a range of adorable hats. This feature adds a playful touch to the game, allowing you to express your personality and style as you navigate the city. The hats are not only cute but also serve as collectibles that encourage further exploration and engagement with the game's world.The game excels in creating a relaxing and wholesome atmosphere. Whether you're taking a nap in a sunny spot, engaging in playful antics, or simply enjoying the sights and sounds of the city, Little Kitty, Big City offers a soothing and enjoyable experience. The gentle music, charming visuals, and lighthearted tone make it a perfect game to unwind with after a long day.Little Kitty, Big City is a charming and heartwarming adventure that captures the essence of what makes cats so beloved. With its immersive open-world design, engaging gameplay, endearing characters, and delightful customization options, the game offers a purr-fectly enjoyable experience for players of all ages. Whether you're helping animal friends, exploring the vibrant city, or just causing a bit of harmless chaos, this whimsical journey is sure to leave you with a smile on your face. Dive into the playful world of Little Kitty, Big City, and let your inner feline adventurer roam free!

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with the game! It's a bit short and janky, but it's very cute and fun for a casual playthrough! The gameplay is pretty neat, and I had a lot of fun traversing the world as a cat! I especially liked the platforming you could do. Yeah the platforming is a bit janky and hard to completely control, but it's satisfying when you're able to make jumps you didn't think you could make!I mentioned the jank a couple times, and for the most part it's not a big deal. Honestly the jank is a bit charming. However, I did face one big issue with the game, and it has to do with it being janky. So early on in the game you meet the Tanuki who can open up fast travel portals for you by giving them feathers. The first interaction requires 3 feathers and teleports you nearby behind a fence, and this is the only time you won't teleport to another manhole cover. This is basically supposed to be the only way to enter the construction area for the first time.Well the issue I faced was that, to get out, you're supposed to pull a box that was covering a hole in the wall that you could crawl though. I pulled it a little bit, and my finger hit the crawl button while pulling it, so the cat crawled through. The thing was, the box was still technically in the way of the hole, so I couldn't crawl BACK through. And since you can't use the teleporter to get back to the construction yard, I had to find another way in. The way I found was only after I had already gotten max stamina and could climb up a nearby building and jump off of it into the construction yard.Fortunately the construction yard doesn't have too many important things (besides the ability to unlock the game's photo mode, which I missed originally), but I do feel like that was an oversight that is pretty big, since it basically locks you out of an entire area of the map. And the jump I had to make to get back in was janky as heck since the nearby building I jumped from was surrounded in a thin fence (so I fell off the building multiple times just trying to attempt the jump).But besides that issue, the rest of the game was pretty smooth for me, and I had a lot of fun with it! I'm hoping the devs can update the game to give us some new content to mess around with in the future, but even if they don't, I still think it's a fun game to just chill and enjoy! Plus you get to be a cute cat, how cool is that? I'd give it an 8/10 if I had to use numbers. :3

_childDocuments_.review: You are, indeed, a Little Kitty in a BIG CITY.This game is purrfect in every way, and absolutely exceeds all expectations. I didn't realize I could climb things until reaching a box I COULD climb: I thought I'd have to pounce!The game otherwise runs so smoothly, the animations are incredibly charming, and I'll be updating my review once I've played more of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Purr-fect super-cute cat-simulator.Difficulty ☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆ (no deaths, no failing)* nice characters* awesome artstyle* cat movements well made (like in Stray)* lovely details and cat jokes* a lot of funny cat-stuff things to do* well made city also in vertical direction* no missables (you can play on after finishing the game)* portal system* you cannot prevent cat from jumping down edges (why not make it possible to sneak to edges to get at the most outer point?)* bird hunting could be more challenging with various bird types* would have wished that the city would be bigger and more stuff to do (game felt too short, needed 8 hours to 100% it)* collecting trash quest took too long* story and soundtrack just suits its general purpose nothing more* would be pretty fun to have an online or local couch coopIt is nothing with a lot of action, but exploration and little cat adventures that focus on a smooth atmosphere having fun doing cat stuff (good and evil things). _childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed it so much! it really is the type of game to play kicked back on the couch with a controller and a big screen... or atleast that's how i see and did it :3The premise and the story is pretty simple, the gameplay is pretty short, relaxing and filled with silly and friendly interactions which makes it so much fun to go through and i genuinely wouldn't have had it any other way.The level design is great and the freedom of movement (since you're literally a cat) really just makes you want to explore more and more to collect new hats and various collectibles... this has to be one of my favourite aspects of the game especially with it being closely linked and part of progression itself.Everything's all topped off with beautiful, yet stylized and simple visuals, smooth animations and a great soundtrack.My only gripe with the game is that the movement mechanics for climbing and just travelling generally can get a bit clunky, slow, snappy and repetitive at times, not only making the animations act in weird ways but also breaking the enjoyement as it can get a little too tricky to get through certain obstacles... this in my opinion gives it a little bit of an "unpolished" feel... but other than that i can't recommend this cute little 3D platformer enough!

It does have a few bugs, and it is possible to stick yourself in strange places and inside things but it never gets too annoying or happens so often that it ends up sticking in your mind for long. The kitty and the creature friends you meet on the way all have nice cutesy designs and it looks nice and consistent throughout.It's up to you if it's worth the £21, I had a nice time with it and I'll say that the 4-5 hours to 100% it at a relaxed pace were nice enough that I'd say I got my time out of it, but everyone's standards there vary. _childDocuments_.review: I don't want to stop playing!If you're in the mood for something lighthearted and simple (yet engaging), just being a little kitty doing little kitty things, this is the the game for you. _childDocuments_.review: I've been on Steam for maybe 15 years, and have been playing games since I was a kid and learning computers. I can confidently state that few other games, ESPECIALLY in recent memory have as much soul as Little Kitty, Big City does. A little game by a small team, yet  a passion project that was created by people who WANTED to make it exactly as it is, and they poured their hearts into it. Every aspect of it brims with love and attention.  In a sea of corpo box-ticking, to say it's a breath of fresh air is a big understatement. There is an insane amount of detail and care put  into every aspect of the game. You have the incredibly natural idle and movement and emote animations (and purrs, trills, meows!) of the Kitty itself,  the fantastic sounds design as a whole, and kickass jazzy soundtrack that is RIGHT up my alley, beautiful visuals that carry their own unique style, adorable character designs, fun, lighthearted and engaging dialogue, the myriad of references (Quack Fighter 2 theme is still stuck in my head!)... Not to mention the tons of  really small things that add up to an even more impressive package, too - (for example, if you wear your little hardhat, the construction worker dude doesn't throw you out of the construction site! Or, if you spin in place, the kitty gets dizzy and has to shake it off. Or how about when you nap on the printer, it prints out a kitty loaf where you can see your tummy and paws on the paper? Also, waking up and stretching after you load a save. The accuracy of the Kitty's actions to a real cat cannot be overstated)There is actually quite a bit of content for the size in the game, even though it's set in a few streets, because it kind of uses the Metroidvania formula to entice you to explore and get rewards, so you can explore even futher. Yes, you could rush it in a few hours, but I can't imagine doing that - it was the exact opposite for me. I was thoroughly engaged and wanted to take as long as possible exploring everything and doing everything I can. I loved the little side quests of the animals, and I really liked their interactions with the Kitty, and helping them felt so rewarding. I basically never fast-traveled, because I enjoyed just walking through the city and brightening people's day when they stopped to pet the Kitty. And obviously, all the mischief you can cause just never gets old. I even managed to make someone angry with me slip on a banana somehow, I laughed out loud at that. As a final note, I've rarely been able to play more than a couple of hours, even on off-days for, more or less, years. Even games I like don't engage me that long, so I end up doing other things. I basically completed LKBC over two big sessions, and I was fully engrossed. Played on Deck, and the performance and experience were utterly flawless without a single hitch. Wholeheartedly recommended to basically anyone who can appreciate indie passion, naturally, cats, and soul. Thank you to the devs for this amazing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming and relaxing. Reminds me a bit of Untitled Goose Game, but with less or slightly easier puzzle elements. It is very lighthearted and easy to play. A great game for kids or people who don't play a lot of video games. It's more about exploring and causing mischief than action. The art is great. All the animals are very cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: You're a cat exploring the city while trying to get home to your appartment, it's cute. The dialogue is a bit much at times, and the physics are a little bit wonky now and then, but as a whole the game delivers on what it promises pretty well. The side quests are mostly fun, but the achievement hunting gets tedious fast. It's what you expect it to be, if maybe a little less polished than I would have hoped for, and a little bit expensive for what it is. I got it at 20% off and I felt that was appropriate.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I love it, we need more games like this <3 Super funny and enjoyable game. I loved the world, various mechanics, all the quests and little side challanges, interactions, characters, dialogues (seriously, dialogues are the best, silly and funny, yet serious). Every aspect of the game seemed to be refined and fitting the the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: It was a fun game, I still have some achievements I can go to unlock but I’m not sure if I will or not. Although the game is cute and enjoyable, the shortness of the story makes the enjoyment turn into lacklustre and I became bored quick after completing it. Running the same street back and forth while trying to avoid the water puddles got old real fast.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played this a short amount of time and I love it. You get to be a cat. You get to knock things over, be a menace, and do all these fun quests in a free form environment. Sure there's a "main quest" but you aren't ever made to feel stressed about finishing it. Also there's fun hats! :D  I am going to have to collect everything and get all the achievements. Also the art style is super cute and the dialogue of the animals you meet seems pretty well thought out. Love this! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Little Kitty, Big City is a really cute little game about being a cat who is lost and trying to find their way home.  If you're looking for a cute, no consequence game, this is the one for you.  Bonus points if you like cats and especially black cats.The only complaints I have are some minorly janky physics sometimes and that the city isn't really all that big in the long run.  I was able to 100% the game in 8 hours and I really wasn't trying to be fast per se.Even so, I bought this game during a Steam sale for $20 and I don't regret my impulse buy at all.  I can absolutely see myself replaying this game again in the future.  Luckily there is an in-game achievement tracker so I assume I can achievement hunt again in the next playthrough too!Something I only found out later in my playthrough, the briefcases can be opened with a few swipes.  There are some interesting things inside!  I ended up with a whole pile of stuff while I was trying to get people to take pictures of me.  I also ended up with a pile of phones from those who didn't want to take pictures of me. >:D10/10 - Would steal phones from people who don't like cats again
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly what you think it's going to be. Lighthearted, casual, cutesy. You're a cat doing cat things. I haven't played something this chill and comfortable since Slime Rancher. Wandering around, being a menace to random townspeople and stealing anything that isn't nailed down as I search for my next fish is a healing experience and I think the only thing I won't enjoy about this game is when I'm done playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: First things first: unlike Stray, in this game your kitty cannot be harmed or killed! For some cat lovers, me included, that is already a huge distinction.This is a sweet game, with an adorable little cat, trying to get home and so gets into shenanigans. Interacting with humans and other animals, waging a war on pottery and people too stupid to look up from their mobile phones. It's a quick game - 5 hours if you really push for all "quests" (and leave it running while have dinner) and to finish it, then another 3 hours so far to round out a fair chunk of the achievements. It's replayability is debatable, apart from going for 100% achievements. Whether the purchase price is worth it, is up to you: for less than what a movie tickets costs nowadays, you get to have fun, and laugh and smile, with a cute cat (who reminds me of my own wholly black youngun with bright green eyes). Worth every penny to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like it shouldn't be over 20 dollars for a game this short. I managed to complete it within 80 minutes, which, is not long at all. I understand devs wanting to make money off of a game they spent a long time on, but 20 dollars for this type of content is just, way to much. Not only that, the movement is very, very clunky, and I have fallen off things I shouldn't have fallen off. For reference, I have been using a controller for this game like it recommends. It just wasn't very enjoyable to play due to the way the cat moved around. In general I do not recommend this game in the current state. Maybe if they add more things, or make the movement less clunky I will, but not currently.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: BUG REPORT: My katana clipped out of the world when placed under a fruit stand in the market. No way to recover it. Locks out an achievement --------------------Could have done without the implied danger at the beginning - thought the cat would just take a nap in a truck or something to get lost.Game's great, I'd give it 4 of 5 stars purely due to control issues. Jumping feels sluggish, jumping and some running stops feel like they're under too much drag. Lot of accidental impacts. Some animations taking a bit too long to get you back into action don't help with that. If they would tighten up the controls to be snappier, I'd give it 5/5.Would have liked more normal hats instead of the fruits and stuff. Not using the majority of the collection options.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: #29 Game in my Pile-of-Shame Challenge!I - LOVE - THIS - GAME ! ! !The music, the story, the characters, the gameplay ... and oh boy, THE ANIMATIONS. The humans are lame but the cat you play IS TOP TIER! As a cat mom myself, i loved to see common cat behavior and movements in the little black cat i played. The way you squish yourself through holes in walls... priceless!The gameplay is simple, same with the story, but I enjoyed it alot. It's quiet a cozy game with lot's of humor if you take your time to find out everything the game has to offer.With almost 9h of playtime, it's a bit expensive with 25€, BUT if you really like cats or just really want a cozy game: get it! Or wait for a sale. Either way, it was worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little cozy game, some fresh air in the market.Completeable in under 3 hours including collectables, all hats and almost all achievements (so not including grinding stuff with rng, like getting someone to take a photo of you)Controls are clean (K&M), i dont know what some ppl are talking about.It's nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone in my family really enjoys playing as Kitty and looks forward to the next time they get to play. It's super cute. Fom the way Kitty is animated, to the various noises for things like climbing or jumping, every session is delightful. The controls are easy enough that all of my kids are able to play and feel like they've accomplished something (pushing stuff off ledges, knocking people down, our just running around meowing).If pressed for a complaint, the only issue that we have, other than it not picking up our PlayStation controller for the prompts, is that there's not a ton of content (probably 10-15 hours to 100%). While we're thrilled going to get much more than just once playthrough out of it, it'd be nice to have more areas and things to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Simply Adorable, loved the animation and the rendering/composition of this game's art is just so incredible there are plenty of problems to solve in the world, was such a cute blast and the writing was pretty humorous. Not sure it was worth $22 strictly speaking, but its definitely something i would recommend getting if you think it looks cute and fun regardless of my qualms with the price.I definitely wouldn't mind more of this game or more of the silly universe its in!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Game is very buggy and clunky, which turns it quickly into a frustrating experience. - cute cat, pleasant color palette- town is small, but nicely designed and I knew my way without the map quickly- collecting hats and wearing them is fun- collecting shinies was fun, too, and there are a lot- cat emotes- meow button- absolutely hilarious dialoges with the animals- jumping feels a bit assisted, which helps getting around- good animal sounds- got hardlocked after 30 minutes of playing because I fell through the map after platforming out of bounds accidentaly (I'd suggest to the devs to remove boxes , because it truly looked like an ingame path to follow)- this game saves your position, an unstuck button doesn't exist, being stuck means restarting (I read people get stuck in vents often, did not happen to me)- music settings are only master volume and music volume- sound effects are too loud in my opinion, cannot be changed- I saw several birds fly through walls- every time you jump the cat goes mmrrp. It is not funny after an hour- got screentearing on high settings despite vsync- sometimes jars or pots don't break when smacked to the ground (jars contain shinies)- weird collision/physics can sometimes bounce you off walls unwanted- sometimes the slow-mo jump on birds was over 5 seconds long- jumping out of a box got me stuck in its corner every time and only a precision jump got me out- very short game: after 4 hours you will have done everything (collecting 100 cans just bloats playtime)- achievement 'fruit fall' is bugged for me- drawn map is bigger than the real city, there are two parts shown you can never get to- cat itself is somewhat weirdly animated, the back parts 'slides' into position, no step taken- there is a tiny triangular corner at the riverside with a puddle and a vending machine which almost got me stuck, because the cat kept on jumping away from the water into the corner on repeat (fixed itself after waiting a few minutes, glitched out)The short playtime, small map and the bugs do not justify the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Soundtrack is amazing and it's a cute game. Just maybe wait on a discount because it can be really short. Sure, you can always goof off and just do your own cat thing and that is totally fun (when the physics work, sometimes they're really... well not that great, which is still fun and all that because cats but yeah, not fun if you want to climb stuff and keep falling) but yeah, maybe wait a little bit before you buy it. Still a great game in then!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game, but refunded due to how buggy it is.  In around 90 minutes of play, using the the pet network sometimes caused soft locks or pull me in even without interacting with it, the cat got stuck a few times, a quest wouldn't update, and the camera randomly disconnected from the cat, behaving more like a free cam. _childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever wanted to become a cat for a day - this game is definitely for you!It's a short game, I completed the story (although I didn't get all the objectives or do all the side quests) within 4 hours. And it essentially is about you finding your way back to your window at the top of a building. It's such an adorable play - You get to knock over stuff like pots & cans, and you can make people trip and fall over. You're able to find different hats of sorts as well for the kitty and it's adorable seeing the cat having different hats on, and you get to meet different animals throughout your journey.The graphic is super cute, but obviously there are going to be some errors with movements and controls etc. but other than that I really really enjoyed the game and I would play it a second time to complete all the side quests and find all the hats. Meow!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: i cannot even begin to describe the overwhelming kitty euphoria this game bringsi am just a lil kittyin a big lil cityto try and puts my thoughts into a proper functionits a genuinely cute story and its fun to run around, causin some mischief, helping other animals, i like the writing and interactionssometimes moving feels a little bit finicky? but that might just be a me thingi suppose i could say i expected the city to be a bit bigger? hence little kitty BIG city, but its packed with things to do and collectables to find, a perfect amount for an indie project and suchoh and if you hold both left and right swipes at the same time, kitty does a little glitch where both their paws move super fast and ill be so very sad if its ever patched outive been excited for this game for months the moment i first heard of it and im so sorry to everyone around me who i havent shut up about it in the weeks building up to its release
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: They overhyped this game. I didn't encounter any bugs or any game issues. Its just not really fun. The promo videos on tiktok made it look so fun and engaging so this was really disappointing. They kept delaying it release but its got cats in it so I was stoked. Not worth the 30.00 wait for a steam sale. Environments: Comparing it to a game like Stray for example (same price point, concept and about cats) the environments in Stray are much bigger and more realistically scaled to the player. The same thing could have been achieved here if the environments didn't look they were being crammed into a sardine can and still kept it nice, bright and colorful.  Gameplay: A bit awkward. I really tried to get into this game and stick with carrying a rubber duck through the parts I played. I have 2 black cats who constantly carry stuff with them everywhere. Having to constantly drop what I'm carrying before I can do ANYTHING in the game was annoying. But I'll be damned if I was losing that rubber duck. Pouncing on stuff took some working out because it doesn't tell you to hold the button down. Just LB to sneak and A to pounce. This cat also can't jump to save its life. Cats can jump pretty high irl. This cat jumps like a senior cat with a joint issue in its back legs. Its like playing super mario and he can only jump like a little in the air but if you hold the button down and release it he can magically jump a tiny bit higher.  It gets old really quick when trying to do the platforming bits. A nice detail they added though is the ability to knock stuff off with either your left or right paw. Some cats are actually left pawed (prefer one paw over the other) so the ability to do either one was a nice touch.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Meowtastic! _childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This was such a great game to play! The animation style is charming and whimsical, and the gameplay really hits all the quirkiness of cats right on the head. _childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little game and I do mean little. I could have finished it in a little over 5 hours. I wasn't trying to beat it as fast as I could. I was exploring and looking around. Regardless of the size it is very cute and fun. I am a keyboard and mouse gamer so using a controller felt awkward. _childDocuments_.review: This game is certainly fun! And playing a fuzzy chaos gremlin of the likes of Goat Simulator or Untitled Goose Game is definitely worth the time. _childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Cutesy, fun, but very shortIf you loved Stray for being a cat, then you'll love this too. But unlike Stray, there is no complex plot or drama: you're just a house cat looking for a way home, messing with humans and meeting other street animals. The main goal is simple: return home. But there's lots of stuff to do along the way and these quests are funny and cute. Loved the writing, dialogs are well-written and fun. The kitty gameplay is exaclty what you would expect: run around, meow, hit things with your paws and nap in cozy places. The only downside is that the game is very short. You can strive for 100% achievements, but some of them are pure grind (I'm looking at you, 100 cans) and honestly quite boring. If you want to have a nice evening, get this game and enjoy meowself!

_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just too cute. It's entirely too fun running- sorry, ZOOMING around the city. It is a little short, but they can probably add more stuff later if they want to. _childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much! It was so cute and fun to play. I don't know why some people were disappointed because I enjoyed playing it a lot! _childDocuments_.review: I'm going against the grain of reviews here to point out some annoyances and pitfalls of this game, despite liking it overall. It's a cute game, but not particularly good value. IMO needs more content and polish.Cute, if not oversimplified Japanese neighborhood. What this game lacks in complexity and nuance, it makes up for in charm. Unfortunately, the "big city" is really only a few blocks, bookended by fast travel points that really are not every helpful, as you can traverse the whole map in a few minutes. Takumi the fast travel wizard is goat character though, love her mysterious aura. Super simple, a bit kooky. Cat fell from balcony, needs fish for energy to get up. Funny characters help kitty out, but lack depth. TOO MUCH DIALOGUE, so much backstory setup for no plot progression, just cheeky if not drawn out text dumps. Could be a matter of taste here, as there isn't really bad dialogue, just a lot of it.Kinda glitchy and unpolished movement, a buff to jump speed and more fluid movement, improved hitboxes, would help alot. Feels like a beta, to be honest. Not unplayable at all, but prepare to get glitched off a few platforming challenges or clip through some objects. Just jank, wouldn't notice if there were less platforming puzzles that depend on certain movement mechanics.Cute, if simplistic and short, plot and town to explore. Not so much a city as much as a few blocks of suburban Japan. Animal characters are fun, but the gameplay loop quickly gets repetitive and you'll end up running through the same sections alot. A bit expensive for what it is, I think this should be a 10-15$ game for the 5 hours of gameplay this offers. A few deeper side plots, quests, and easter eggs would really go a long way in making this worth the money.Buy on sale for a fun kitty platformer, but dont expect a fleshed out city and deeply nuanced story. I hope updates are coming, as this is a really promising little game that would benefit from a bit more love.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: If you like cats and cozy games, this is for you. It is easy to pick up, and you get to interact with almost everything in the game. You can choose to speedrun it (my fiancé completed it in 6 hours, for example) or take your time. The hats you can collect to dress your character in are adorable, too!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This review will have minor spoilers for characters.Very fun game where you get to play as a cat.The characters are cute, the interactions are wholesome, the hats are fun.Why do I not recommend this game? The price tag. As of me writing this review the game is 10% off at $22.49. I played it for <5 hours and have every hat, over half the achievements, and finished the main storyline. This game is 100% NOT worth the price tag. If it was $10 or less I could easily recommend it.Despite the cute name, the city really isn’t that big. Being able to climb vertically definitely adds to the game but not enough to feel BIG. Once you open the area up it’ll take you under a minute to walk from the top of the map to the bottom.On top of that there are a lot of weird glitches that happen. The collision is wonky so you’ll bump your head on slight inclines if they don’t have a ramp or, even worse, the dang tanuki. Because the potholes are in the middle of the street you can be running full stop and suddenly slam your head on where she’s suppose to pop up. Yes, this game put an invisible pole over the potholes she comes out of. You can’t go over them even if she isn’t popped up.On top of that, some environmental interactions are… interesting. There are some fans around the area, not all of them, that will push you away if you get too close. Most of the time it’s only until you’re at the end of the air stream but there have been multiple times where I jump and the fan starts and it throws me ACROSS the map because I was airborne. This cat weights as much as a feather, I swear.Despite these issues I still had fun. It’s a great little brain teaser and platformer AND you get to wear cute hats, even if half of them are just ones you buy from vendors for random junk you find around you.TLDR: Cute cat, fun hats, wonky physics. Buy the game if it goes on 60%+ sale. It’s not worth over $10.
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoyed this game! It's really cute and funny, and is great if you want something a little relaxed. Playing as a cat in a game was a new experience for me and the animations for it was so fun to look at (cat parkour was epic). The interactions you have with the characters are all so silly and fun too.If there's anything I would change, I would add more things to do and explore and maybe giving the player some momentum when you run or being able to increasingly run faster the longer you run. I 100% it in almost 8 hours and I just wish there would be more playtime but I still liked it a lot anyways. I hope that maybe an expansion could happen soon or something that would be so legendary!
_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: This probably the first review I've written on Steam? (That says alot) So here we go! What I Enjoy About the Game:This game has a very simple art style which I love, it's not overwhelming and perfect for a rainy day in.I love ALL of the characters, the ducklings are my favorite, they're very goofy but wholesome. I think my favorite little interaction is when you find them on the balcony and they debate how to determine who is a grown-up. I laughed out loud so kudos on that. Even though the main objective is quick to complete, there's plenty to do and some of the achievements are a little tricky to complete if you're not pay attention.  The soundtrack is curated beautifully and adds to the cozy wholesome vibe I mentioned earlier. Some Things I Think Needs Improvement:I did encounter a one minor bug, the camera, when taking photos my kitty bugs out and their eyes pop of their head and I cant see their face even if I zoom out. (Freaky stuff) It fixes when I disable the camera and reactivate it but I dont like to have to encounter that when I want to take a photo. I assuming that will be fixed soon.  I think some mini games would be cool to keep players coming back. Ones that involve beating highscores and stuff like that? Just a suggestion :DOther than that, great game 15/10 need more games like this.

_childDocuments_.name: Little Kitty, Big City

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little game to play. While I have yet to 100% this game, I have reached the ending of the game in less then 5 hours. You can reach the ending quicker, and I am pretty sure completing the game in its entirety isn't going to take much longer. What I want to say is that 25 Buckeroos might be a little much for the games length. Anything between 15-20 would have been more reasonable. To justify the pricing there needs to be some form of free content update or something of that kind.Conclusion: A little expensive for the length, but still a good, neat little gameEdit: I don't like making these kinds of comparisons, but regarding the pricing again: Stray, another game about playing a cat, which is longer (both in 100%ing the game and reaching the ending) is only around 2-3 doler more. It took me 8 hours to reach the ending in Stray. Both games in controls and mechanics are pretty similar to each other. Little Kitty Big City is a little janky and finicky, and these bits of 'jank' aren't rare, but not game breaking or don't ruin the experience. Stray on the other hand has barely any jank and the controls feel good. In my opinion the graphics in Stray are more pretty, but I think that comes down to which art-style someone like more. Conclusion (but for real this time): Little Kitty Big City is a neat little game, but might be a little too expensive when comparing it to the game Stray. _childDocuments_.review: Little Kitty, Big City: A Charming Cat AdventureCalling all cat lovers!  Little Kitty, Big City is a delightful game that lets you experience the world from a feline perspective. You take on the role of an adorable kitty who has accidentally tumbled out a window and into the bustling city below.A Purrfect PlaygroundThe city becomes your playground as you explore back alleys, rooftops, and cozy shops. You'll encounter other animals, some friendly and some a bit grumpy, and hidden surprises around every corner.Climbing, Swatting, and NappingThe game captures the essence of being a cat with simple mechanics that let you jump, climb, bat at objects, and of course, take relaxing naps in sunny patches. It's a chill experience that's perfect for unwinding after a long day.Homeward BoundYour main goal is to find your way back home, and along the way, you'll help other animals and complete quests to earn new toys and accessories (think adorable hats!).Cute and CasualLittle Kitty, Big City is a casual game with a charming art style and relaxing soundtrack. It's not a super challenging adventure, but that's part of its charm. It's more about soaking up the atmosphere and enjoying the simple pleasures of being a cat.Is it Worth It?If you're looking for a cute, relaxing game with a strong dose of feline fun, then Little Kitty, Big City is definitely worth checking out. Just purr-pare for a short experience, as the game can be completed in a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on sale for $22.50 USD. It's a complete mess. Buggy, unfinished, and boring. I can imagine this game has an audience, someone who doesn't play video games all that much, wants a fully relaxing experience, loves millennial lingo and humor, and loved animal crossing. If that person is you, and you don't care about $25, then I hear Power Washing Simulator is a real decompressor, and Dave the Diver is getting insane reviews. I personally recommend Sky: Children of the Light. It's not finished on steam yet, but its got more content than this! And it's finished on mobile and switch. That game seriously helped me through a hard time in my life, not because it's aimed at emotional healing, but just because it was so cozy. It gave me something to do that let my stress leave me without filling me with artificial dopamine hits. It's a wonderful game. I'd also recommend Exo One, a super soothing, short game that doesn't demand the commitment that Sky does, and provides a much more potent soothing spell.The best I can say about this, though, is that it didn't fall below my low expectations *that* much. Well, it did, but not by *that* that much. The reviews seem to be very positive, and from what I've seen people say on social media, the gameplay was pretty smooth and freeing. But once I got into it, the horrors of 3d platformer movement jank were so much worse than I thought they could ever be. Turning around makes your character look like a snake. You randomly bump into nothing and get stunned for 0.5 seconds when running up stairs. Jumping decreases your speed. Jumping onto a surface higher than the one you jumped from completely removes your speed. Falling from one surface to a lower one halves your speed, going through small gaps requires you to way through a 1.5 second animation. And despite the small map, there are a lot of places that look like you should be able to jump onto that you can't. Plus the CAMERA. Listen. Every single 3d platformer has it's camera complaints. And this one is no different. It's not the worst camera I've ever seen in a game, but it's down there. It doesn't let you zoom, the camera does that automatically, and badly. Sometimes the camera is waay too zoomed out, sometimes its too zoomed in and I can't see what I need to. The camera, like in many other 3d games, is just not well thought out. But while these complaints aren't the most unique to this game, and they show up in many 3d platformers, this game is kind of a worse offender in my opinion, because you're meant to be playing as a CAT. The most agile non-avian animal that most people ever come into contact with. I want to be gliding over the streets, jumping up fences, quickly jumping on a fridge, knocking something over, and then jumping off before anyone knows I was on there in the first place. I want to MOVE. When I play this, I have the same control of the cat's body that those cats with severe wobbly-cat-syndrome have on tiktok. It's just so disappointing. I really wanted to move like a cat but I'm moving more like a 60 year old with asthma, that is to say, slowly, and with frequent stops. Also, I spent the first two hours doing most of what the game had to offer except for the climb back home, and then I figured out how to get out of bounds and spent the rest of my time exploring that. Which was a bit more fun than the rest of the game. This game is maybe worth $10. Get it if it's mega sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I find this game extremely adorable. Everything from the interactions, the characters and the art style. The story isnt a core aspect of the game, which i like. I wrongly assumed that the first rubber ducky you find was supposed to be placed into any kind of water. I placed it into a puddle, making it permanently stuck (the character cant walk over puddles). Because of this i could not 100% the game. I did not figure this out until late into the playthru, where i had to just suck it up and make a new save file. During my second playthru, i ran into one of the old bird nests. This destroyed the bird nest, but did not give me any progression towards the achivement. Like with the ducklings, i did not realize this out until late into the game (this was the ONLY quest i had left, and now im figuring out that i'll be stuck at a 98% game completion until this bug gets fixed OR i start a third save).There's also some movement-related bugs. You can get stuck in the air when jumping out of a container (trash bin, cardboard box, fasttravel system, ect) (you can jump to get un-stuck). Sometimes, when jumping into the bottom of a fence, you'll get stuck trying to nose-dive into it (you can jump/look away to get un-stuck). The game just feels generally unpolished.IMPORTANT:I saw a bug-thread on the official subreddit, where alot of the comments had the same issues as me. _childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, I wishlisted this game when it was first announced for release in the near future, which was quite some time ago. Since then, I have been patiently waiting for this game to appear, despite having little interest in games like Stray where the main character is a feline or a fully tracked animal character. This game is adorable, but could it be too adorable?I don't want to post a bad review, but I also know I won't be able to play through and finish it (it's very short) because I don't enjoy it at all. Cute, hilarious, but not enjoyable. It is sometimes frustrating. When I play some games, it's almost like a gut feeling. If I yawn, it usually implies I'm not getting the vibe of a game; if I get lightheaded, it means I'm not feeling it because it feels like a children's game and I am forcefully pushing myself to play something I thought I'd really enjoy. In this example, the answer is the latter. Once again, this game is charming; you can meow, knead muffins, and be a threat to society, but it's really a repetitious collectathon featuring a little kitty with often times janky controls that have you falling off buildings because it overshot your movements and bonked you into a object sending you backwards off a ledge and then back up you go again, being more on the slow and steady style of gameplay.I really wanted to like this game; I've played so many games comparable to it in other formats, such as "Here Comes Niko," "Frog Detective" and hell even "Little Gator Game" all which felt very childlike but so full of content for such a reasonable amount which range from ridiculous and goofy little games to downright wholesome and emotionally story-driven. However, after only an hour of playtime, I had the idea that this game was intended for highly impressionable children or individuals who are obscenely obsessed with cats. There is nothing wrong with that what so ever, but there is a problem with the price tag, content and just length.Just because I couldn't like it doesn't really mean you won't either, give it a try.It's disappointing that I can't recommend it, because for the price and the quality of the game, it just doesn't feel polished, with falling through walls, off ledges when it was clearly a climb to napping for a minute somewhere in the city, and the cats' X and Y axis shifting every few seconds moving them around and through objects if you left it long enough while afk.If you have a child or are very impressionable when it comes to animals, this game will be an excellent fit for you. The gameplay consists of collecting shinies for birds to earn hats and more fish to climb back up to your home. If you're seeking for more depth than this, there isn't much to enjoy. The marketing for this game was fantastic, it just sucks that it couldn't deliver.

_childDocuments_.review: Its an alright short game but that is about it.The story is you fall down a window from your home which conviniently is the tallest building known to human kind, you need to climb back up. Your sole obstacle is vines that you need to climb, but to do that you need Fish to eat. That is about it really. Its a part platformer part puzzle solver [well puzzle in the lightest possible terms] and its, fine. On your journey to eat the 4 fish that exist in the whole city, yes 4, you meet various animals that you can help, pokeballs that give you hats, and bunch of scrap to unlock things.There is nice interactivity all around the map, and its a pretty nice size, and it also looks good, although honestly the Humans are the least interesting part of it, but hey the few animals you meet are very nice.Although for a platformer it controls kind of poorly, jumping is kinda jank, sometimes precision is also weird and often you can just kinda not hit a jump, momentum is also a big problem. If you run and jump all momentum is lost and you always do a weak jump which is very off putting, but if you latch on to a wall and try to jump off it you will be flung off, most of the time while trying to jump up a part of something, not hitting a jump, cat latching on and then being launched of.Its also short, i did the side content i found, tried collecting hats i saw so i did not even rush and i just passed the game in 2 hours, im not sure if i could top 4 hours if i now just went and did the little content i did not do.Its not a bad game but for 20 euroes or more its a tough asking price, id get it on a sale personally if it was like 10 or 5 euroes, otherwise there are games that are just as charming, and probably better platformers as well.

The game does also have some other bugs here and there, but overall is very playable and one of the best game's ive ever played on launch.Would Highly recommend, this is a masterpiece of gaming.Post-Ending ReviewThis is easily one of my favourite games of all time. (lethal company is still better i think)It's one of the cutest games i have ever played. There is alot of customization with hatas for your cat, the scenery is awesome and the NPCs are fun to trip upThe sidequests is a really fun part of the game, and I genuinely love to look for and do sidequests for other NPCs. My favourite Side quest is easily the Chameleon (which i kept calling a Gecko), which makes you go on a whole ass hunt around town. The clues are fantastic, and cryptic enough that you feel accomplished after finding them, yet not too hard so it becomes annoying. The other puzzles in the game are also rewarding to complete. I also really enjoyed the Duck's mission. Easily my secound favourite mission after the Chameleon. The Game's scenery is awesome. I enjoyed messing around with the camera function, just taking random silly photos. I have never used a camera function in any game as much as i've used it in this game. My steam screenshot folder is now full of silly cats and i love it.This is one of the first games that has made me want to 100% complete.Oh, and the final climb. The final climb is the last challenge of the game, and trust me it's a challenge. Due to a multitude of reasons, including some bugs i had to restart that part of the game several times and i feel from the top several more times. But, it was rewarding enough that i kept trying, and eventually got it. The ending of the game was also amazing.10 / 10, Would Recommend

_childDocuments_.review: Little Kitty, Big City is a very charming game. With a great great soundtrack, cute characters and silly shenanigans, there's a lot to love. This would make for a very good comfort game. I've got a knack for wanting to support indie developers so I wasn't too upset at the price tag myself. However, unless you've got that same knack, wait for the game to go on sale. It's got a pretty hefty price tag for the 3-5 hours of playtime (given you only focus on the main objective and a few quests). If you go for 100%, you could easily squeeze 10 hours out of the little kitty and his big city.Pros:- Cute Art style- Runs Good (at least on my system but the map is small so I cant imagine there's much to render)- Plenty of quests/achievements- Good music- Cats!!!- Designated meow button Cons:- Short game for the price tag- Clunky movement at times. I find that I'm often missing jumps or nearly clipping into walls. Ground movement is fine but be careful when climbing - Minor bugs. but every game has those so I can't nitpick- I hope you like fetch quests (theres a few)- Sometimes its not clear where you have to go when climbing or getting into an area- Small nitpick, but I feel like the binds for the triggers and the bumpers should be switched. My finger instinctively wanted to use ZR to run (I was using a Switch Pro Controller) and I couldn't, for the life of me, get the button mapping thing to work. That may just be user error on my part, though. Overall, aside from the short playtime, I can't imagine the devs aren't working on a patch. I'm optimistic that we'll see updates that make the game a bit easier to play. I've got to recommend this game because I did genuinely have a lot of fun with it. The out of bounds softlock was fixed!!

_childDocuments_.review: Little Kitty, Big CityPlaytime to get through the story: about 6 hours (if you also take the sidequests of all the animals)Achievements in total: 39 - I already collected 32 after my 6 hour story-runCost: ... a little bit too much for a 6 hour game (I probably have only 1 more hour of playing and then I will habe this game at 100%, and compared to other games they offer more, f.e. Dave the Diver 19,99 and I have over 20 hour of gametime and am still not done with the main story and even Untitled Goose Game, who is almost has the same amoung to offer as this game, gets you more playtime to figure things out and is available for nearly 20 bucks, even less where I am from) -> so better wait until it has a discountRecommended?Yes, but wait for a discount. But I would definetly recommend it to parents who are searching for a game for their kids.It is cute, easy to understand, the dialog goes with the time, the challenges and riddles are something that will keep kids probably busy for a longer time than an adult/ gamer. Is it cute as the title sugerates ?YES!Is the concept of the game easy to understand ?YES!Are the controlls nice and smooth for the controller (can't speak for keyboard and mouse) ?They are good and mostly smooth. Here and there you have a few minor issues when it comes to controlling your little kitty while running. What are some good benefits of the game?It is easy to learn without needing much of a tutorial. You can figure out most things on your own. The main focus of this game are of course the animals in this city. So interacting with humans is very minor and comes down maybe a handfull of interactions that repeat. For that you have of course the many animals. In total you can meet 15 of them. Some offer you longer sidequests and some other get you only a sidequest that maybe last 10 to 15 minutes at best. The dialog is funny and cute though. The design is gorgious, also the animation. Though the city is very small designed (or at least the part we are playing in) it often goes into the vertical direction, so there is still much room to explore. The develepors had apparently a love for dad-jokes, which you get with the hats and used some funny memes that are known about cats (I just say cucumber). One of my favourite sidequests was the one with the chameleon, followed by the duckies and the shiba inu. I recommend playing this game together with another person and let your inner voice actors come to light. It is a lot of fun and makes this game entertaining. The dark side of the game? (jk, but here are the bad parts)The kitty makes the Assassins Creed move when it can't climb up somewhere and just jumps the opposite direction. Extremly frustrating, expecially if you are high up and suddenly you are back to 0 and have to start over again.Running is a challenge sometimes and steering that kitty seems feels like a bobby-car sometimes.The game has here and there some glitches where suddenly the music buffers or the game freezes. (I thought it might be bc I was streaming this game on discord for a friend, but even Final Fantasy 14 runs smoother and without any freezes if I stream it, so can't be my PC)Lastly the cost, but I already covered that on top.

name: Pixel Ripped 1995
detailed_description: It’s time to get on the most nostalgic gaming ride of your life! On this Virtual Reality nostalgia trip, you have to join forces with our hero Dot to save the gaming world as we know it from the clutches of the evil Cyblin Lord and become the hero of Far-of-a-Land! During your adventures, you’ll find unique characters, games, and gaming systems that will guide you throughout the good ol’ 90s! Explore the human world in full virtual reality The gaming and human worlds collide and you have to manage each situation in this game within a game Get inside a plethora of 16 and 32-bit games and adapt to each genre they bring to the table Discover the lore of the Pixel Ripped franchise in this rich story full of plot twists and funny moments Witness loads of WTF moments that will get you laughing while playing Gorgeous scenarios with a vibing soundtrack 8 languages support for in-game interface and subtitles! (English, Brazilian Portuguese, French, German, Spanish, Japanese, Korean and Simplified Chinese) Amazing 90fps on Quest 2!

short_description: Pixel Ripped is back with a brand new nostalgia-fueled virtual reality game-within-a-game, this time in 1995! Help our hero Dot face challenging throwbacks to all your favorite 16-bit and 32-bit classics while surviving the struggles of a typical nine-year-old kid.

_childDocuments_.review: Who was a gamer in 89 was still a gamer in 95!Pixel Ripped 1995 is the second game of the franchise that brings us the nostalgic experiences through VR, where we stand in front of an old block of a TV (Or even Arcade cases) or sit on the floor or on the bed in your bedroom!Watch Pixel Ripped 1995 gameplay here: Moments from the childhood of many gamers who are now in their 30's - 40's,Spend hours wearing a hollow gamepad in your hands made of hard plastic with colored buttons on it, connected to a classic retro console with an extra long cable that was in the way of everyone in the house.*Don't forget to clean up the cables when you are done" Is what is engraved in my memory. (Luckily we can now replace certain cables with 'wireless cables')Playing classic games on retro consoles on blocks of TVs is something we will never experience the way we used to despite the opportunities we have, I suspect aging plays a part in this, or you may still be a lot too young to know what this was like.Anyway, VR brings us many possibilities, and this classic gamer experience also thanks to Pixel Ripped 89 & 95!You will also have to take the position with your hands with both VR controllers as if you were holding a real gamepad,one reason why you shouldn't keep a real gamepad in place is because you'll have to use the motion controls as well and because there's no gamepad that's visible in VR like the VR controllers or other trackers, should such a gamepad ever come out for I would buy this game without a doubt!In Pixel Ripped 1995 you will have to pass 6 levels each of which is a tribute to 2D & the then new 3D gen games,Tight attention is also paid to adding the best known and most played genres of that gaming era such as action RPGs, space shooters or racing games to even combat games.Just like in Pixel Ripped 1989, you will also have to defeat a boss at the end of each level, or boss level, who will then fly out of the game again and let it play in the environment around you.You will also have to ensure that your game session is not interrupted by, in this case usually your mother.Pixel Ripped 1995 was partly determined by the community that likes this game, so they voted to be able to choose their favorite year, and so 1995 was chosen,I keep my fingers crossed for another vote, my next favorite year is 2000 - 2001.
_childDocuments_.name: Pixel Ripped 1995

_childDocuments_.review: Pixel Ripped 1995 is pure nostalgia greatness, and more than that!!Ana Ribeiro and the development team have created a sequel that delivers so much more than the previous game.  A better narrative, character development that is way more involved than the first game (which works out, considering the first game was based on older games that didn't have a heavy narrative to them), and a longer adventure that spans great ideas and cool VR surprises that I won't spoil for you here in this review.There's a TON of pop-culture references both visually and in the voice lines that will just make you smile, because they seem to cover everything that was going on in and around 1995, it really makes you feel like you're a kid growing up in that time period.This game deserves a place on ANY VR player's digital shelf.  It's one of my personal favorites, and I can't WAIT to see more from this team!!

_childDocuments_.review: It was a time of great strife, and conflict. It was WAR. It was, the Great American CONSOLE WAR. Arguably the most well known of them all. Two console enter. One console leave. But the one that left was neither of the two that entered. But I digress...This game will take you on a digital nostalgia world tour, and if you're old enough to remember these times, you'll no doubt feel like you're seeing old friends for the first time in as many years. Your "Brothers in Arms"  from your old War days. Console War days. If it was iconic, it's likely here in some recognizable but not copyright infringing way. This includes the main character, who is herself something of an amalgamation of Samus, Link, and Megaman. Because I WAS THERE. But what if you could play the game, INSIDE a VR game? Kinda cool. Now - What if the lines between these two game worlds youre simultaneously playing were being torn down mid gameplay? This, in a nutshell, is the Pixel Ripped 1995 experience.  Be a young soldier during the console wars in VR, and nostalgia/historical video game pop culture cameos galore, while the game within a game begins to be forced into the game in VR.

_childDocuments_.review: So the positives: Game is good fun.Graphics are good.Music is good and immersive.Story is pretty decent.The fights got rid of that seizure inducing flashing from the first game that tried to test our ability to survive in real life.I liked the arcade and beat-em-up section.I liked the throwback to Castlevania. :) That was fun. The section with avoiding waking people was fun for a few minutes, but ... what kid in the 90s didn't know to get up and just mute the TV if the remote wasn't working? That was annoying.The not so positives:The tracking needed a good bit more work. I was constantly being warned about losing control. I have three trackers, that shouldn't happen. I don't know if this was an Index thing, but there were a good number of times I'd have preferred swapping to my controller when it kept  happening.Wish I could have told Mike not to come over or be around, and I wish he could have been shot more. And I wish I could have left him to his fate.Negatives: The final fight. Combined with the controller constantly acting like I was taking one of my hands off, the perspective was really bad. We have to maneuver planes, jumping, AND on the Index the controls are slightly tilted - so I kept falling off, and aiming was a pain. If I could have paused and just moved the world, or adjusted the field - that would have been great. Without that, the final fight was honestly the worst of them all. Again, if I could have swapped to my controller and used a D-pad, that might not have been so bad. As it was, it was.Would I recommend  it though? Yes. I did both 89 and 95 in one sitting and it wasn't bad. I was able to compare it directly to the first game and it definitely showed all the extra effort they put into it. The U32 was great, I loved the throwback to PS1 graphics and that era. It was really fun, I'm glad I played it, and if I knew others who had PCVR, I'd probably send it to them. I'd give this a solid 8/10. There are points off for tracking, some story aspects, and the final fight. Points are added for the mother being a great representative for Karens. :D One thing I hope to see in the next one though: MORE voice lines. I got annoyed hearing the same one so many times. I'd also love if it opened a mode where I got to play those arcade games after. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Upvote, but I am not so positive about this game.It is relatively similar to 198X, except it is in VR. PR 1995 is more focused on storytelling (non interactive dialog) and environment.90% of the time in this game you are the kid playing his games on a TV. The game does break the 4th wall all the time though (this is a feature), so sometimes you are "in" the games. Gameplay-wise, these are generally the best levels.This game does well at transcribing the 1995 vibes, there are definitely things you should be able to relate to, even if you were not at child (either too young or too old) at that time. The storytelling is simple but fun.The game is lacking in two areas, though.First, while being the kid who is playing his game is fun in the beginning, it kinda gets old. Playing flat-screen games in VR works, but is not very fun (it is like watching a concert or drama on TV as opposed to IRL, except it is worse). The games the kid gets to play are not very fun. They are extremely simplistic, and some just feel bad (same issue as 198X), almost like filler content - hopefully they are not too long.Second, while the music and voice acting are good, graphically this game is disappointing. The game runs natively on Quest headsets, so there might be that. The 3D environments are below-average, and the characters are really really bad. They do not look very good and the animation is dreadful.Overall I think this is worth a try, this is a short game (2~3h of gameplay), not worth full price (20€), though.Like 198X, it is not quite bad enough to avoid completely, but could be so much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Did enjoy, going to get into details of what I didn't appreciate. If you are in any way someone who is easily made happy by nostalgia, this is something you won't regret experiencing (especially if you grew up during the time period it takes place. Even if your looking for a fun story, its pretty good. However if your looking for a solid game experience its inconsistent.  This game is pretty well thought out the undertaking in development of many sub games under one tent is mostly what works against it. It fails to consistently decide what it's parodying and things such as frames of animations in the sprites just wouldn't stand in 1995 standards. While the recreations may be offensive to the time period its trying to hit on in terms of technical ability and consistency / not being cheap / spawning you inside a damage pixel the developers and designers definitely seem to have had a good time making this and that rubs off on me while i'm playing it in a positive manor.  The story line and situations you get into as David are quite comical and relatable as someone whom grew up in the period. I couldn't help but be fond of memories I admittedly forgot (such as how much games I played as a kid while mom would endlessly make phone calls in the background, or stealth snes playing at bed time).  While many parts of the game are genuinely fun, there are parts where I fail to grasp what they thought would be fun and these parts get shoved down your throat and are made to redo, redo, redo them with no checkpoints. Anything that has to do with punching (arcade,bikes) or getting punched is missing any wind up "I'm going to punch now" animation/frame so its just like: "Hit". And when there are many of these punching things on screen keeping track of which one is likely going to punch you first is more of a chore than anything else. Specific to arcade, you can also just punch and wait a third of a second and punch again until the enemy dies, because they will not fall to the ground if you delay, and if they fall to the ground they will sometimes instant punch frame when they get up -- this breaks the skill again here. By far the worst part int he game has your character completely blocked by something infront of it your intended to shoot with arm cannon, but your character has to also avoid being hit by drones and not falling off into spikes -- again it just isn't something you can get good at in an enjoyable fashion. The worst part about these moments mentioned again is that they penalize you by making you start from basically the begining. Specific to the arcade segment, if you turn the game off, you get sent back to the very start to the pre-tournament, not that that is much worse that getting sent back to the tournament tournament when you die. I get that games were hard back then but a saving grace to the rushed gameplay that the games being parodied didn't have would be to make them quick to get through. I believe the developer knows this becuase they don't revisit at least one of these mechanics.  So there, I probably made the game sound bad, but its more notes for the developers. I had to push myself through and just put up with the lacking stuff but the nostalgia quality and interesting take on perspective was what kept me putting up with things. I do wish it recreated the time better though, it does feel like they had less rom to work with which i don't know how to an make excuse for.  If the trunk fight was gone or made shorter and things ended after the bed time session the game would be highly recommendable, but everything past that feels broken and like a chore.
_childDocuments_.name: Pixel Ripped 1995

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful. This was an epic game, and for anyone nostalgic for the 90s (or even 80s), I would say this is a  game! Also, I immediately downloaded the soundtrack. As with many 90s games, the soundtrack in this game truly is what makes it complete. A+++ to Moonsailor and all involved in the creation of the genius that is the Pixel Ripped soundtrack. The journey that we go on through these sounds are simply awesome; from the 8-bit intro, through 16-bit gaming, and ending up with 32-bit. In my mind, you've successfully placed your art in the same tier as those epic soundtracks we all grew up with (Zelda, Final Fantasy, TMNT, Actraiser, Star Fox, etc). The vibes here capture it perfectly. Aside from the award deserving soundtrack, the gameplay itself is masterfully done and encompasses so many head-nods to various games & styles in the 90s. The side-scrolling fighter like TMNT, the F-Zero type racing game, Castelvania, Sonic, Fantasy RPGs like FF, Secret of Mana, and of course the epic 3D world of Star Fox, etc. And while it's totally a nostalgia fest and a non-stop onslaught of references & easter eggs, it's also got some well thought out and cool mechanics that only a VR game in 2020 can deliver. This merging of VR & retro is a recipe that creates something that can only be described as true magic for anyone who's nostalgic for a bygone era. The fact that they were able to pack so much into such a relatively short game is miraculous. For me, the total playthrough time was only 3-4 hours -- but it was 3-4 hours that were well worth the price. Honestly, I think this game is a hidden gem.The Pixel Ripped Series is my top recommendation for VR nostalgia, seconded only by Duck Season -- but honestly, with Pixel Ripped 1995, it's a close tie and you really have to experience both.
_childDocuments_.name: Pixel Ripped 1995

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what an amazing trip down memory lane...A true blast from the past in VR! _childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic title that stands to greatness due to the sum of its parts. As others state this is extremely nostalgic feeling, and it really hits that spot quite well for anyone who was a child in the 90's. The music also fits quite well and never feels out of place. There was a part of the game where you have to swap between consoles, and I absolutely loved the concept and execution of that part.If I were to issue any complaints they would be that sometimes the individual genre game-play that you bounce between can be bland, but you can absolutely know what game(s) it is in reference to. Additionally the "RL" interactions took a more noticeable of a backseat this game compared to the first except for the bedroom level, where I felt it was equally obnoxious  and amusing.Overall these don't overly detract for the game.I absolutely endorse this game for anyone who has a love for gaming nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: FULL VIDEO REVIEW AVAILABLEFor the original fans of Pixel Ripped 1989 here’s my quick answer if you should buy the sequel. It’s a massive yes from me! Everything you know and love is here but it’s been turned up a quite a few notch’s and I’m assuming after the deserved success of Ana Ribeiros Pixel Ripped 1989 developers ARVORE have doubled down and expanded on what made the original really really special. In my mind this is a must buy.Far-of-a-land is again at peace but the  evil cyblin lord has other ideas and has a plan to get his goblin like hands on the Pixel stone once again and it will make him more powerful than. In 1995 There is definitely a bigger focus on story and character relationships outside of dot and your Master wizardy bloke and I thought it was great to feel part of David Kenes family. Some of the dealing with Davids mums current fear that video games are rumored to be bad for you makes playing games to save the world not easy and similar to 1989 you will to use real world distractions to keep her busy. Once again the feeling of inception is present. I felt like I was sitting in the room playing that video game and this is the magic . You will also see the return of large inventive boss battles and during my play I didn’t release how much I miss video games rental stores. _childDocuments_.review: Pixel Ripped 1995 is a super charming game that actually manages to replicate that feeling of being a kid in '95, while of course, embellishing with some silly mechanics and jokes.I haven't played the previous game, so I'm unsure if the story is a continuation or not, but it does seem more or less standalone.You play as Dot, a hero from a video game world. The villain has broken out into the real world, and so Dot has to synch to the best player alive, in order to reach said Villain. So you play as Dot, in a child's body. It's a really crazy and funny concept, and the game does a good job at playing with that.You get to manifest objects in the video game you're playing into the real world, while also being transported into game-like worlds yourself. The writing and voice acting of all the people around you is a lot of fun to listen to, and sometimes can be too real. (Like when your neighbor tells you he's playing the latest secret version of a new game)The music is great, and the aesthetic is fun look at.Overall I think the game is a lot of fun. I will update my review accordingly as I play more. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great tribute to 90s games.  Really enjoyed this one.  It only clocks in at 2-3 hours, so grab it on sale.I played 1989 first and didn't really like it.
