_childDocuments_.review: A delightful homage to a bygone era of video games. More specifically, a tribute to not just the games themselves, but the experience of being a part of gaming culture during this period. Pixel Ripped 1995 is a great iteration on the ideas and presentation from Pixel Ripped 1989. Loads more polish (even if the mocap is still a little uncanny) and smoother pacing that keeps your gaming within gaming engaging. I love the emphasis on the sort of dramatic irony behind playing a game about 90s games on a device that said decade fantasized about. To that end, it’s a decently humorous game and I caught myself laughing out loud a couple of times.However, playing games that are built around a d-pad using a VR controller’s joystick doesn’t translate too well or feel authentic to many of the scenarios. Part of me wished there was an immersive way to still perform external actions with your hands (throwing/shooting) while playing with a standard gamepad.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique perspective on retro gaming. The core of this game revolves around playing SNES, Arcade, and PlayStation -esque games on a television while also dealing with mechanics in the surrounding world (nagging mothers, annoying kids, etc.). _childDocuments_.review: WOW! This game is so underrated, I really wished more people experienced this or at least talk about it more. This game definitely deserves to be praised more. Definitely one of my favorite VR games close to Boneworks and Half Life Alyx in my opinion. This game is so unique that brings something new and amazing that no other game has done before with its whole aesthetic and game mechanics in VR. For the gameplay, I was really impressed with how well it turned out from using the player's controller with your VR controller. With the ability to let go of the controller and grab the things around the (second real world?) to either distract or clear obstacles in that second real world or the actual game world, really blew my mind. The fact that the game world goes into the second real world was such a cool and unique experience. As for the graphics, it's not the best or realistic, BUT it doesn't have to be. When I look for VR games, graphics would be one of the huge decision maker whether I get the game or not. While this game is not the best in graphics, the whole aesthetic, music, and game mechanics made up for it greatly. This honestly opened my eyes in VR games, and made me think that VR games don't have to be super immersive through graphics, but could be really immersive and equally enjoyable through those elements such as the whole aesthetic, music, and game mechanics.For the music however, the music is especially good! I had to download the OST and was very happy it was free, but extremely sad that I couldn't pay to help and support the amazing team who worked on this game. This is not really important in a game but, as for the humor in this game, I practically laughed the whole way because of the character's dialogue, especially the Mother's because it was so relatable, and I enjoyed it even more because of that.Definitely worth the price, but really sad it was short which is about 3 hours to beat.I cannot wait for more from the team of ARVORE, whether it's a prequel, sequel, or an entire new game. Amazing piece of work!!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a unique VR experience unlike anything else on the market. While those who remember the systems and games that Pixel Ripped is paying homage to will get a kick out of the nostalgia, from a purely VR enthusiast perspective I think this is an experience everyone should try. I got 1995 and after playing 1 level I decided to buy 1989 so I could play through the whole story.This game is not just one and done either, it has replay value in the form of things to collect in the levels you play in the game, and achievements to accomplish in the levels as well. There is even a side game you can play that has a playful but also kind of intense horror element to it.I wont lie, this game can be a challenge, but this is part of the throw back to the 80's and 90's when games had more simple mechanics, but also often much more punishing ones. Its not insanely hard, but it doesnt hold your hand either.
_childDocuments_.name: Pixel Ripped 1995

_childDocuments_.review: So much fun! So much MORE fun than than the first game 1989. That is to say it's a fleshed out game, more so than a gimmick or demo. It should be noted that this is the PERFECT game for SEATED play (and is the only option)! You don't need to play the first game to enjoy this game. I think that $20 is a great price but any more would be too much. In my opinion, 1995 is faster paced and more interesting than the first. More stages and less keep-XX-busy-to-play, though there is still that too. I would LOVE to see an RPG spin-off in the style of Zelda/etc in first-person like some of the dialogue scenes in this game. Full disclosure: I was born in the 80's but raised in the 90's and I didn't play that much of 1989.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game but it lasts only 3-4 hours and has no replay value. The controls are also extremely frustrating and NOT plug-n-play. Also, it would be nice if it didn't make you take your hands off the in-game controller so much. The distractions are a nice gameplay mechanic, but I couldn't keep the controller in my hands no matter what I did!Overall, for $20, it's a bit pricey for what it is, but it's a great experience. No need to play the original. You can skip to this one if you want to. Both games are a lot of fun.

name: Stirring Abyss
detailed_description: New Enemy Now Available About the Game Stirring Abyss is an indie tactical squad-based game with strong RPG elements in which you uncover the ancient mysteries of the depths depicted in the classic vein of Lovecraftian horror. You take charge of the surviving crew of the USS Salem, a U.S. Navy submarine that sinks while on a top secret research mission during the early years of the Cold War. They find themselves surrounded by the ruins of a forgotten civilization, their vessel too badly damaged to escape the seabed. In Story Mode, you slowly unravel the mysteries of the depths in a desperate quest to rescue your missing crewmembers and fix the crippled Salem. The choices you make determine the fate of your crew - and the entire world. Every expedition lives or dies by the strength of its crew. You have a diverse array of character traits and skills at your disposal, each opening exciting new options in both combat and in story events. As you delve ever deeper, you may also subject your crew to powerful but grisly mutations; the price of survival is high, and no one escapes the abyss unchanged. The horror and the void which hide in deep waters can become too much to bear, and your crew may experience episodes of exhaustion and insanity. Will their psyche get stronger, or will it be forever damaged? A game of dice with Fate itself will determine the outcome. Salvaged resources can be turned into weapons, armor, or other useful supplies - or they can be used to repair and upgrade the Salem, giving your crew a crucial edge in the fight for survival. The more you explore the abyss during the missions, the more chances you have to find the lost treasures of the deep. The hauntingly beautiful environment holds many secrets and mysteries to explore, but danger lurks just outside the feeble circles of light you bring with you. Be wise, and use your skills to scout the black waters and light up the path: unseen terrors may be hiding just out of sight. The Endless Mode pits your crew in a roguelike battle against an army of neverending enemies that only grow stronger as you progress. It is the ultimate test of strategic ability, as you not only choose how to improve your own squad, but also pick your poison as to what powers your foes gain.

_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetic of this game recalls Sunless Sea, but the gameplay is pure XCOM Terror from the Deep, for those of you old enough to remember that. You progress through a series of missions to find members of your crew and uncover the mysteries of the deep in time-honoured turn based fashion. One thing I especially like is that the game is a challenge even on normal difficulty and enemies often feel overpowered. You need good tactical thinking to make progress. The game also implements a few measures to get you to scuttle around the map faster than is ideal. Air is limited, although there are vents to refill your supplies scattered around the map and perks to replenish it. And there are timed upgrades to pick up, a bit like Meld in XCOM Enemy Within. Apparently there are 13 main quest  missions but at least that many optional sidequests, so a run through will take in the vicinity of 15-20 hours.In short, if you like XCOM or turn-based tactics, then Stirring Abyss is a must buy.EDIT: 19 hours to complete the game on Normal and I enjoyed every minute. I'll definitely play this again on Hard and I look forward to some DLC in the future. This really scratched the turn based itch for me...

Do you remember when you in old  trained soldier's  or ? Or how soldier's fatigue and encubarance affects his ?  is simplified. It isn't just that undemanding flat map-design.The game is also quite brutal and you are intentionally kept away from controlling the situation: hidden and random skills, random mutations, fighting against time, very limited vision and movement range, a constant struggle with resources... This could be really interesting if supported with deep writing and immersive character introspective. Imagine a -like story! Or maybe at least some  personality scars and effects? _childDocuments_.review: Terror from the Deep meets Lovecraft meets... well, insert a rogue-like with fairly punishing difficulty. I have to add, it's a pretty neat game, although not flawless. Well, obviously no games are flawless, but here some minor adjustments could go a long way to enhance quality of life. Either way, feel free to grab it, lite crew management (equipment, RPG-ish elements) and base management with lots of underwater TBS missions.Negatives for me:- I would really appreciate some voice over, at least for the captain/narrator.- Even after 5 hours of game it's pretty hard to distinguish some resources from the scenery.- Fog of war is one thing, but already explored areas out of your direct visibility are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dark that I can't properly check if I missed some areas or resources or whatever.- I understand that it's a rogue-like and difficulty is intended, but implement a decent undo or limited save/load game system, please. It happened me multiple times that I accidentially misclicked and it did bring doom on me. Like literally.- Some crucial game elements are NOT explained at all. Like to the level that you can seriously miss important things.Some hints and tips, so you don't fall victim of lack of explanation:- Start on easy. Seriously, on easy. I mean it.- You can scan for side missions multiple times. Do it, you can get stuff like additional crew members, chaos reduction, etc. If scan fails, stating that there are no side missions, ignore, scan again. Without the rewards and associate things side missions deliver (additional crew members, XP, resources, etc) I doubt that one can finish the main storyline.- Chaos can be reduced via enigma board researches or by side missions (found the latter one and multiple scanning options with very high chaos, can't say that I was happy that I had to go through all these ♥♥♥♥).- Get torpedo room up and running as soon as you can. Also, you have to have torpedos to use them. Still no idea how to obtain it, though, again, lack of explanations throughout the game.- Always have an oxygen canister with you, since level design doesn't guarantee that you won't run out of air, especially if you get into long(ish) brawls with the enemy.- Get dice upgrade on enigma board asap, although I would really appreciate for a clear description how the ♥♥♥♥ shrine rewards work.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.  Exactly the type of game I was looking for - lovecraftian mythos meets turn based strategy and it pulls it off brilliantly.  Really not sure why this game isn't higher rated.What is strange though is the difficulty.  I've seen complaints on the forums that it's very difficult so I was cautious going in, as I know that for these types of games like XCOM, if you mess up early you could end up circling into a defeat spiral.  And even the way you choose difficulty is a bit strange.  You have 4 options, narrative, easy, normal and hard.  But the default setting is easy, and the devs even say on the tooltip that it's the recommended setting for your first trip into the abyss.  Undeterred, I set it to normal (for veterans only the tooltip says), just to see what it's like, and if it's as hard as everyone says then I would go back and walk it back to easy as it recommended.  But I never needed to.  And I'm no gaming expert.  It starts out tough enough but after a few missions it becomes decidedly easy once the side missions open up after mission 3, allowing you to gather extra resources and experience, and fight back the ever increasing corruption meter.  It goes up to 9 over time but because I was doing loads of side missions it never got above 4 for me.  I don't know how it's possible for the game to ever get to a high corruption meter, as it seems to only increase with time in-mission.  But you're never able to spend huge amounts of time wandering in-mission because you have an oxygen meter, so the game seems a bit out of balance there.And the game basically signposts the way to break the game.  You unlock team-wide bonuses on whats called the Eldritch board, by cashing in 'clues' (not-so-subtle nod to the arkham horror games I figure).  And these are significant upgrades.  Everything from how easy skill checks are, to armour, oxygen supply to weapon damage, to more esoteric upgrades like the number of invocation points you have to use special abilities.  But anyway, you pick up most of your clues by killing enemies.  So naturally you speed towards getting the upgrade which DOUBLES the amount of clues from killing enemies.  And it becomes painfully obvious how useless most melee combat is useless in this game (until you unlock some key upgrades/mutations on your tanks), so you gear 3/4 of your crew around ranged combat as soon as you're able.The mutation system is very cool - you can spend void marrow, a special resource you pick up in-game (and which the game also signposts unlike other resources), to add special abilities to your team, and the mutations are visible on your characters in-mission.  The crab claw is by far the coolest!But all in all it becomes very easy to max out the level of all your guys, load them up with mutations and the best eldritch upgrades, and just steamroll through the game to the end.  But regardless, the setting is fasntastic, the resource and ship management is fun, the combat is engaging, and it doesn't overstay it's welcome.  Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? It is an indie challenger to X-COM, the reigning champion of squad-based strategy titles. The publisher is Slitherine, who manages a large library of historic wargames (but not much else). I am glad they decided to publish this Lovecraftian horror story - the turn-based combat is highly strategical, after all.Stirring Abyss takes place in the late 50s, when the submarine USS Salem suddenly sinks into an abyss in the middle of the Atlantic. You start the game by taking control of an officer, who awakes alone on the ocean floor, fortunately wearing his diving suit. Actually, it is more of an underwater walking suit. You have no idea what happened, as have the other crew members whom you might find during the game. Some had some very strange and intensive dreams, though. Finding the USS Salem, you can start repairing the submarine and finding more of the crew... and maybe something else lurking at the bottom of the abyss.The submarine is your hub, but it is flooded and you start with access only to the conning tower. With enough power (regenerating over time) you can unpump rooms and with stuff recovered on missions (metal, copper, supplies, chemicals) you can repair damaged systems. Starting with the control room, which enables you to move the submarine (for little distances along the sea ground), the submarine comes alive again room by room. Select your divers and their equipment for undersea missions. Divers come in 3 classes - crewmen for close-range fighting, officers and scientists for long-range fighting and support functions. You move them around on tiles and explore the seaground. Limited air supply (air sources can be found underwater) adds a time pressure to the missions. Of course it doesn't take long until you discover hostile creatures. While the first ones are just aggressive jellyfish, the enemies soon become more... strange. Submarine skills (like a searchlight to see far away tiles or amplified sonar to find enemies over a distance) can help you during your missions. Your aim is to find missing crew members and collect ressources to repair the USS Salem. Gather clues to upgrade equipment using the enigma board in the submarine and don't let your characters die - once dead, they stay dead.Your divers have an inventory, abilities, health points, an oxygen supply, and... sanity points. Like in many Lovcraft inspired games, they can go nuts if the horror is too much for them. After each mission, your surviving divers may have earned enough skill points to upgrade their abilities. There is also a strange power under the sea... that actually helps you and gives you invocations - they allow you to improve your divers. You can also mutate them to make them stronger... but at what price? The corruption level of the abyss increases as the game progresses. This makes enemies stronger and your chances of survival smaller...The visual presentation is really nice, you can zoom out for a better overview or watch your characters from close range. Zooming and scrolling is smooth and fast, the camera doesn't jump around wildly during combat. Your characters comment on the events, text windows describe what your crewmen experience during the missions, eery background sounds support the atmosphere. Saving during a mission is possible, and the game automatically saves when you finish a mission. All in all - not bad for an indie game.Is the game realistic? No way. Is it fun to play? Yes! The heart of it are the turn-based tactical fights, but the devs managed to add base building (repairing the submarine), RPG (improving your crew members) and finally a Lovecraftian horror story to it. The difficulty is... quite challenging.Underwater turn-based strategy inspired by the old XCOM: Terror from the Deep. And H.P. Lovecraft. Cool.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovecraftian X-Com Terror from the Deep? Eeeh yes and no !Let me start by a big "this game is a blast !!", it feels good, the music adds to the dark atomosphere, the story is there, the graphics are pretty good (well, look at the screenshots, the game has it's own art style and I love it personnaly)Other than that, the game isn't easy and if you barely start, I highly recommend the easiest difficulty because it is brutal (your divers are still going to die and it's still pretty challenging on story mode). The game is a classic turn based tactical RPG in the likes of X-Com, along the way, you'll find some resources which will allow you to repair your sub and eventually build new rooms.You can use the "clues" resource to make research and globally upgrade your crew, your crew are going to earn XP and level up along the way. Other resources will be used to repair your sub, craft equipment and heal or train your crew.After that, you'll just go to your next mission or scan around to see if you can get some timed side missions to get more ressources. Very X-Comy in the heart.There aren't many missions but they're pretty long (the size of the maps isn't amazingly big either but some have caverns to explore). Afterwards, you can play the endless mode which makes the game a very good deal no matter the price.When you level up your crew, you can chose to mutate them with pretty fun stuff like tentacles and powers.During your mission, you can also use your submarine's powers to help you and you will have access to some other stuff like your equipment and incantations which are powers for the entire team.You'll have to monitor the life and the sanity of your squad at all time because some pretty bad stuff can happen.Another thing you'll have to fight is the darkness around you, basically it is a fog of war, because you'll always be blind and won't know when you'll find enemies or not. You can use flares and your submarine's search light to avoid making useless steps in a direction especially when your divers have limited oxygen which they can replenish at an air vent (with limited supplies) or by using oxygen tanks. This is worth mentioning for any X-Com 2 fans out there  because the light radius is very small and since the maps also are and your team is limited to 4 instead of that large team you had, you won't be able to throw light grenades everywhere and blast everyhthing in sight with explosive weapons.You also have a counter who will gradually fill as time goes on, this counter is a difficulty indicator, the higher it is, the harder the game gets so planning your moves and your every step is vital.Now, is it everything we want from an X-Com title? You could say it lacks of depth ! Ironic for an underwater title in the abyss. Well, you do not have to manage a worldwide crisis, the world map is pretty small and base management, your submarine, is basic to say the least. Equipment lacks of variety and there isn't many research to do but they're pretty expensive. The tactical phase suffer of the same problem, because of the fog of war and the nature of enemies, you'll oftenly be fighting hand to hand. There aren't really any cover to use either even if you can fight from a distance, hand to hand will still be your main fighting technique.Now, does the game feel lacking? Absolutely not ! Of course, the game is far from being as deep and complicated as Terror from the Deep but it's still a blast and still a pretty good and enjoyable X-Com wanna be.Definitely give this one a try, the game is still a pretty good gem. (and there is demo, if you really like it, you can purchase the game and continue from where you left of I believe)I just hope the devs are gonna think about a sequel with more complex ideas because after playing this, I only want more !

_childDocuments_.review: Stirring Abyss is a turn-based strategy game with base management and a Lovecraftian story. The story is told through texts. Sometimes it feels like your collecting pages of a book. When you click on a body, for example, it opens a text which is very well written and could be written just like that in a good book. The writing overall is very good and interesting. This is a game that depends heavily on the story and mixed with the sound effects and music it delivers a really good horror experience. If you don't want to experience the story, there is also a roguelike mode available for you to play through I would advise you to play the story mode.Even though Stirring Abyss is an indie game, it competes with the big names of the TBS genre. Fights are pretty standard compared to other TBS games, which is not a bad thing. It does what the good games of this genre do. Explaining every little detail is unnecessary here, the game teaches it to you very well and fans of the genre will feel like coming back into your hometown. Aside from the battles, you need to explore the world under the seas. Different creatures and other mysterious things will surprise you on your journey. Maybe you'll find resources to gather or missing team members? You'll never know before. But one thing is for sure: oxygen is limited and every turn, you'll lose some. There are a few wholes where you can refill your tank but sometimes that will be impossible to do and you need to evacuate your team. This adds another layer of strategy to the game. There is also base management involved in Stirring Abyss. It's basically like the base management in XCOM. It looks like that (though, it's a submarine in SA) and you need to vacate rooms first. After that, you can get the room to work with different resources like metal and copper, which you'll find on missions. Another resource is energy. You see, it really is like in XCOM. Skill trees of characters give you two options per level. There is also an overall "skill tree" where you can unlock upgrades.Another feature in the game is called "rot". The stage increases throughout your run which will make enemies stronger and missions harder. All in all Stirring Abyss combines the best of both worlds: A good horror novel and a good TBS game. It's worth the full price and these devs earn every cent for their hard work.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun little turn based X-Com like which is set on the bottom of the ocean where you face off against some horrible mutant fish monsters, collect resources and sometimes even locate missing crew members. In between missions you have a side on dissected submarine to expand and construct room by room, and potential items to build using the resources you've gathered in the missions.Your sailors can level up gaining new abilities but can be "improved" in other ways... ways that some might consider... unnatural.There are two modes.Story mode - Follows a set number of "missions" with story line plus the ability to locate additional side missions in between which provide you with more resources or lessen the amount of corruption.Endless mode - Gives you three crew, a flooded sub and a map to travel around on until you die horribly!The difficulty can fluctuate wildly and you can be, on occasion, swarmed with enemies, resources become tight and you have to send your sailors out while they're half dead and their sanity is having by a thread and then they miss that 95% chance shot... but that's X-Co... Stirring Abyss baby!

_childDocuments_.review: X-COM: Terror From the Deep but with a much stronger narrative focus. Definitely worth the time of any Turn-Based Tactics Fans and Cosmic Horror Fans, and a must play for gamers who fall in both categories.Other reviewers have found the game exceptionally difficult even on Easy. This wasn't my experience, but I avoided melee combat entirely, which may have had some influence. Don't rely on finding spear guns; prioritizing crafting them (even over repairing rooms!) can be a huge boon. To be clear, melee absolutely is viable, and a number of mutations exist which significantly improve melee capacity.The game has a fully functional debuff system, allowing the player (and enemies) to reduce or boost movement speed, defense, absorption, accuracy, and damage, as well was stun, charm, and berzerk opponents. Overwatch exists for all range weapons, and attacks of opportunity occur if an opponent attempts to move out of melee. Consumable medikits, flares, oxygen tanks, and turrets, eldritch powers and individual mutations round out the player's toolbox.There *is* a cover system, though it is more line of sight based and plays a smaller role than in other games. This feels appropriate given the characters are in bulky diving suits. Most enemies are melee based, and the few that aren't don't tend to be as threatening.While no element of Stirring Abyss feels deep per se, when taken as a whole, there is a complete toolkit available to deal with almost every tactical situation, including two mechanics that mitigate killing blows and outright death respectively. I can't speak for other reviewers, but I found Stirring Abyss to be a well tuned and enjoyable tactical experience where failure felt like a consequence for my mistakes, rather than because the game screwed me. The campaign ran me around 15 hours, though pursuing more side missions might stretch that by several hours. Also most missions are procedural in their layout, allowing for a degree of replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: 13 hours deep... This game is fun ! the atmosphere, art and story are all very enjoyable. Atomic age Horror at the bottom of the sea ! It offers skills, and mutations for crew, upgrades for your vessel/Hub/Base, and brutal combat. The things you face will always do more damage than you do , and there will always be more of them than your away team. There is a Sanity Mechanic, and a Pyschic/Sorcery type mechanic as well . I am currently on my fourth attempt to play through the story mode, set to easy. This is a very challenging game , I recommend it to anyone who enjoys everything ive listed , and likes turn based tactical combat. You can save in game . I am playing on a 2 1/2 year old HP Pavilion Laptop 7th gen I5 core/ 12GB DDR4 SYSTEM MEMORY With no technical problems at all, everything is smooth . I have not encountered any bugs thus far.Update, finished main story line ,really enjoyed it , I am happy with this game, now to try Endless mode. would love to see future content for this game !

_childDocuments_.review: *** Review from my blog. Not my personal review ***Stirring Abyss, by Sleepy Sentry and Slitherine Ltd., is a turn-based tactical RPG with a story mode set in an underwater region, following an attack on a submarine that leaves the crew scattered and stranded. The intent of the game is to find the missing crew members, including the captain who may or may not have something to do with what happened. In addition to the story mode there is an endless mode which allows you to choose between a pair of missions until you fail three of them. The game functionally is similar to the XCOM family of games but adapted to the setting and themes of Stirring Abyss in a functional and effective way.** Pros- Art and gameplay combined well in presenting an evocative and thematic setting- Fun and interesting boss fights- Tight, challenging gameplay doesn’t overstay its welcome ** Cons- Game is difficult with the potential to get into a death spiral leading to a slow, inescapable defeat- Oxygen system and the potential to death spiral encourages saving and reloading when things go wrong and tedious, slow moving exploration- View is static, and weird color choices make game state difficult to properly make out at timesCHECK OUT THE FULL REVIEW:

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem if the many facets of this game are appealing. - Lovecraftian to the max. The devs nailed the dread, fear, and mental toll that typifies the genre in addition to the ever-present fear of suffocating. The artwork, unpleasant organic sound effects, and music all play into the unnaturally creepy ambiance. - Procedurally-generated maps are utilized, although there can be a sort of sameness of blocks of maps, which still feels overall fresh in each mission. - Three different character archetypes based on abilities, with ranged, melee, and utility emphases, but characters can still effectively perform roles of other classes if spec'd properly. - A slow plotting/plodding push-your-luck tactical system that, in most turns has one reluctant to take just one more step, balancing timers whether intrinsic (running out of air) versus specific countdown missions. Maximizing efficient execution is vital for success. Movement economy is tight, with every step possibly impacting mission success, and yet when out of combat the movement allowance relative to map size feels appropriate and not too slow. The tension of moving, which may expose enemies within the fog of war, and activate them if they can also see you, is heightened by a two-phase movement system, where the initial higher movement point phase still allows for a one-point action, but the second only allows for movement. You will find yourself having unsuccessfully pushed your luck with your last character to move activating 3-4 enemies regretting that you got greedy and wanted to expose just a few more spaces to set up your next turn. - It has a robust combat system of melee, ranged, and qualitative utility abilities, adding to your tactical decision options.- Character leveling-up systems are exciting, especially the mutation mechanisms which feel like a twisted birthday present every time you harvest the weird transmogrifiable material (which can be used during a mission). General party skill tree advancement is present covering offensive, defensive, and utility factors. Objects in the environment also provide skill checks to change character and world states.- There is limited, but crucial, base building enacted by repairing the rooms in your damaged submarine. - Health, sanity, and buffs/debuffs systems affect character performance.- Mission types vary offering different loot, perks, and new characters.- Crafting is present. offering useful items that meaningfully affect missions. In some games picking up a flare is trash loot, but here such items can mean the difference between mission success or a wash.Stirring Abyss is a masterclass in Lovecraftian, as well as general game, design principles. The only criticism I have is Salvage-type missions are too luck-dependent, where one mission allocates the recoverable objectives close by, whereas others have them spread out throughout the map, basically ensuring mission failure. I usually try to avoid such missions, or if put into an unfair mission design, scum-save by hard closing the game which resets it back to start, and then try to more efficiently collect the items. As much as I adore this game, some gamers might not fit well into this slow tactical style of playing, and fast run-and-gun tactics will likely lead to a mission wipe. Also, it can be a tough unforgiving game, and if literal/virtual step-by-step planning feels dull or too time-consuming, then this game will likely not be appealing. This certainly is on my hidden gem list and if my description is mostly appealing it may soon be on yours! ...and yes there are tentacles, just not the Hentai-kind.

_childDocuments_.review: You have 4 crew members during your first boss fight (that I'm aware of), you heal a marginal amount between sorties (until you unlock more sub quarters), and medkits heal a pathetic amount of health, so most of your men will be half dead by the time you even start the mission. That doesn't even mention the several enemies you have to fight to even get to that boss. On top of all that, the boss fight has a seemingly infinite number of spawning mooks who attack you while you have to destroy some buildings that are also immune to damage until you either damage their shields enough, or they drop their shields after a certain number of turns, all while you're managing health and air.I don't mean to sound like a loser, but this game is unfairly difficult very early in the game, and you're not given the resources to try and mitigate this difficulty in some way, and I don't have the patience or time right now to dedicate to figuring it out.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally gave this gave a negative review, but I soldiered on and, in the end, I decided it was worth the time and effort to persevere. The game gives several types of tools to the crew to fight the monstrosities of the abyss. The sub is the base, which requires resources found on missions to develop. The crew up to 4, go out on missions that progress the game story, though I never had more than 3. It is a turn-based tactical combat style. Crew can take either physical or sanity damage. When you develop your sub, do not consider losing sanity nearly as serious as losing health. When a crew member loses their sanity, they go berserk for one turn and then recover full sanity. When the health is gone the crew member dies, forever. There are tools and weapons one can build from resources collected. The crew can go on special non-story missions to gather resources. The player needs to find the special spear gun from the special mission 'soviet stash', as this is necessary for future boss fights.Crew can also add special mutations to enhance their abilities. Also, investigating mysteries will enable the crew to unlock special crew-wide abilities. So, there is more to his than meets the eye at first. Also, this game, despite its graphic art style, gets closer to the feel of a Lovecraft story than most games. Though the story will be the same, there is a certain replayability. 80/100

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★☆☆(Good, relatively short Turn-based RPG)============Review:Stirring Abyss is a turn-based RPG game with a nautical theme.Essentially it gave me similar vibes as X-Com Terror from the Deep, but it's significantly simplified and more story driven.Audiovisually the game is good - I really like the art style of this game. It's this sort of Pseudo 2D style that just looks good in my eyes. The sounds do their job just fine, and the music is also good - and it feeds into the atmosphere that you're exploring the underwater abyss while there are dangers lurking in the darkness. ============Gameplay-wise it's also good. But for comparison, It's not a strategy game like X-Com TFTD, it's instead of a story driven "Squad-based RPG". You do have a "Base", sort of.. in the form of a submarine, but it's very limited in terms of building things. It does have a tech tree of sorts, which is generally just passive upgrades for all your characters (It works but isn't very innovative).You only control 3 characters (4 later), which gain levels and have attributes and traits.As is typical for today's XCOM-esque style, each character has 2 action points they use for movement and firing. It works and it's easy to understand.The game is also relatively short, like if you play the story mode and do every optional mission, the game takes approximately 12 hours to finish. Of course if you skip the optional stuff you can complete this much faster. It does have a endless mode too, if you're interested in that.Sound good so far? Well the problem is (in my opinion) that the game simply lacks "meat".There are very few weapons and equipment available. The characters are randomized but you'll quickly see all the available traits. There are random mutations also which spice up the game a bit.But.. the thing is, you will very quickly see everything the game has to offer. It becomes repetitive quickly. Well, some people like repetitive games, and they have the Endless mode to play. I'm not one of these people though, I get bored of repetitive games quickly. This is why I actually appreciate that the game is relatively short - I can just finish it quickly and move on.===========Overall, I think Stirring Abyss is a good game. It's not amazing or anything, but it's a good, short game to play when you feel like you need some turn-based, XCOM-style RPG.It could be an excellent game if it had more content. Like more weapons, armor, traits, levels, research, enemies.. you name it. As is, the game feels like it's lacking something, but it's fun enough to play through once.So yes, I recommend the game but I think it's a bit too expensive and you should wait for a sale to grab it.============Summary:The Good 👍+ Gives TFTD Vibes+ Atmospheric music+ Good lengthThe Bad 👎- Not enough content- Repetitive

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a ton of fun with this game.  It really does have a great Lovecraftian feel to it.  It definitely reminds me of "The Temple" by Lovecraft and some work by Lin Carter.  The game feels claustrophobic as the familiar "fog of war" plays tricks on you.  Baddies seem to pop out of nowhere at the most inconvenient of times, making spreading your crew out not such a great idea.  There are plenty of creeps with unique abilities and upgrading your ship is a lot of fun.  Does this game has as much depth (excuse the pun) to it as Xcom?  No - but it doesn't try to.  This is more along the lines of Fell Seal: Arbiters mark without as much customization and classes.  Don't get me wrong, there are still skill trees and mutations that make each character unique but this is definitely a "lite" version.  Where this game really shines in the story.  I'm having a lot of fun seeing the characters go mad and it makes me want to dive into (yes, another pun) a good Lovecraft novel.  I'm really happy that I snagged this game up.  It's a lot of fun and, in my opinion, a real hidden gem.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry to give a negative to this, but unfortunately I didn't like it. In 3,5 hours the game wasn't able to capture my attention.PROS:- Good atmosphere and immersion.- I liked the visual style, the presentation and the short stories about the characters of the submarine.- The game mechanics works well: attacks, dodges, oxygen, skills. There are many of them but they work well, it's a solid gameplay. CONS:- The aesthetics of sprites is disappointing. Charachters are ok, but monsters are really awful, they seem drew by a baby. It's a deep loss of immersion.- The game is super repetitive. I played almost 10 levels, always encountering the same monsters, and the scenario is literally the same: the bottom of the ocean. Surely, it's interesting to understand this by yourself, but here you really don't have much information about anything. I lost a lot of turns (and missions) only to understand the basics.In summary, I'm sorry to pass on this because it's my kind of game, but I don't know if I will touch it again.

_childDocuments_.review: An isometric tactical turn-based game where we take control of the surviving crew of a US submarine. While trying to find a way to fix the damaged submarine and find all the rest of the missing crew, we delve deeper into a world of unknown with strange phenomena, dangerous creatures, and many mysteries. This is enhanced with elements of Lovecraftian atmosphere and Cold War setting.The main focus of Stirring Abyss is on the tactical gameplay with some RPG elements. It’s very much like XCOM and Final Fantasy Tactics mechanics put into an underwater Lovecraftian themed story. Outside of the missions, we can spend resources to fix the submarine, craft gear for the crew, and also level them up.During the missions we travel through the area on an isometric grid in a turn-based manner. Walking drains portions of each action point bit by bit, whereas actions themselves used up an entire action point. When in combat, both melee and ranged attacks are possible.In addition to this, a few other mechanics come into play: 1) Madness mechanic - each crew member has a sanity bar. When their sanity drops to zero, they spend one turn moving away from an enemy or attacking allies and then recover the next turn. 2) Limited air mechanic - since our characters are underwater, their air supply is limited and it drains at the end of each turn. Air supply can be replenished by finding air vents in missions or by carrying spare oxygen tanks. 3) Mutations - after finding a specific type of item during missions, it can be used to give mutations to the crew members. They grant additional bonuses or abilities to use, such as a tentacle grab or ability to consume corpses to recover health. There is a permadeath feature present, so losing a crew member in battle means they die for good. The levels are also randomly generated for the most part (although objectives themselves for main missions are the same). It's a nice tactics game, though it can get pretty repetitive towards latter stages (same actions, same enemies, same-looking environments). It also has some difficulty spikes in places, and losing crew members could put you in a stalemate where you're left with not enough crew members or left with weaker ones, making it impossible to beat the same mission again upon a retry (leaving the only option to restart the campaign from the beginning). A few bugs and glitches are also present, though will likely get patched up soon.Visuals and UI are slick, atmospheric, and thematic. Music is also very good at generating tension and intrigue.Generally a nice isometric turn-based tactics game, though there are better games out there in this genre which are worth playing first. Would recommend it to those who have already played through many tactics games and want something new.For a more in-depth review, check here:
_childDocuments_.name: Stirring Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game. All looks like hand drawn in a very good way. The effect of as looking at it thru water works flawlessly and adds greatly to the immersion. It's close to Lovercraft's books. Ancient horror lurking in the deep. The tech is like from Jules Verne books but a bit modern. This game creates a sense of nostalgia. Music is not very dominant, it is there to support the above described feelings. You get to hear at times various sounds of the ocean. All in all you have free hand in a lot of things here. You can develop new technologies, like weapons, gadgets, medikits. And craft them after wards. There are also 3 unique items that are worth it and you can find them in special missions. You have an Enigma board where you can after finding clues (which is a resource of its own) evolve all your divers in very substantial way. Your divers level up. You can select attributes, abilities and you can even mutate them. That broadens your possibilities greatly. There are 4 categories of divers: captain, officer, cook and soldier/diver. Game mechanics work flawlessly. There is an random element to each game you start. Race with time: check, the difficulty can rise as you are "stirring the abyss", if you are not careful and are making wrong decisions or it is taking you simply too long. So it is up to you how bad it will get. Be careful and you will be rewarded. Be reckless and wait for the surprise. Now a little bit from my guide to better describe few details: This game is not very hard. 3 diffs, so I played at normal. If you ever played X-com, Incubation or Jagged you will feel at home fast. There is option to save and load at any moment, without ridiculous mechanics as in new X-coms. No limit to saves makes it a little bit too easy, but hey, who is forcing you to load it (and it's nice not to have to resort to ctrl+alt+del to force quit without save). From the in-game menu you can load only last save. This is not working very well for autosaves after completing a scenarios like "Seal Defense" to reduce corruption and you just beat it, but don't like the results of the Eldritch dice throw and want to reload it, you do the "Load last save" and see that corruption level was not lower as it should be. Or when you found the torned from within diver suit (who had torch at that time must have been lucky, hint: when you select the greedy option, you just pay for it with equipped medikits, worth it) the result is lost upon loading "Load last save". In such situation and others, go to main menu and there use Load option. You have whole list showing all of your saves. Here you can safely load the "Seal Defense" end save or others. It is nice to remind yourself to delete that "save and exit" save, polluting the list- when not needed. Whenever you feel the game is not fair with the dice rolls you can try your luck again. Or Bard's tale mechanic: No, this is not how it happened - load :) .First thing to do when a mission starts is to save it.When you complete a mission it is autosaved on board of U.S.S. Sallem.Especially during "Salvage" mission it is handy to do few turns by dispersing your divers to cover more ground and spot places, then reload and do your tactic with saved turns and electric power.WHY? BECAUSE TIME IS OF THE ESSENCE in this game. Why? Apart from health you have air. with each turn you spend 1 air. This is clear. You have also Corruption counter ticking away since the first turn. After certain number of turns it increases. When it increases the level of spawned enemies increases too. You can find it is good when it is in the middle so you wont get bored with challenges. But as it increases so does the spread of corrupted ground - or semen reefs as I like to call it :) . When you step on it, corruption counter increases. The higher the corruption level the more Vessels appear instead of normal un-corrupted Scyphozoa and from their corpses more semen reef. And cover more ground. You see the mechanic and algorithm, right?! So be quick with it, unless you want more challenges.Craft a second Speargun ASAP, I did wait till I build Equipment room to allow 4 divers but I recommend to do it vice versa. It will give you much more tactical advantage, not to speak about dmg output.Save before Scanning for missions, they roll randomly. Load when you don't like the one you get. When you are low on Supplies go for Salvage mission. When you discover Soviet divers go for Salvage mission to get one of the 3 unique items that are worth it. From start go for Rescue missions. I am not sure how the roll works here, but I got in one game 1 more Commander, in second just the starting one and one more officer and all others were cooks. Funny and np to beat the game with it. I will be recalling fond memories from this beautifully executed game for many years. It won high rank in my memory and will be referring to it very often. It is not easy to do a great game, but this was it. I will be remembering it as long as old Incubation for example.
_childDocuments_.name: Stirring Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: I have looked into the Abyss... and I fell in.So, firstly, a disclosure that I was an alpha and beta tester for this game.  Stirring Abyss is a squad-based tactical game that requires you to bring together all the lessons you learn in the early game to face new enemies, more dangerous exploration and new challenges as you proceed through the depths towards the end. The game challenges you in different ways as you progress by putting your skills to the test against strange and eldritch creatures, the mental demands of walking where man is not meant to go and I greatly enjoyed my time with it. I will note the boss encounters as definite highlights of the experience - you'll see what I mean when you get there.Each run will also be quite different in what crew traits and skills and mutations you have available, so there's plenty to experiment with as you tackle the monsters of the deep and explore the strange world below. The submarine is the base of your operations. Damaged by its arrival in the depths, you are left with a choice on what to repair and when with your limited resources that you find on your missions. These rooms give various bonuses and materials for your crew and there are several convertible rooms which can add new gameplay options (Hint: The torpedoes are pretty cool). Furthermore, there is the Enigma Board which can be unlocked during repair of the submarine which allow you to research upgrades for various features of your crew. I played on Normal primarily and even with my previous knowledge found it a solid challenge. I think its a game that after a few starting runs, you definitely get a feel for how to play and that learning curve feels good. This is a game that each time you come back to it you'll get better at with what you learned before. There are also a number of difficulties - including a Story difficulty - which might help people ease themselves into the Abyss. I won't say too much for fear of spoilers but I felt the story and atmosphere were very well crafted throughout with great sound design and writing.It follows your crew of the  through their journey under the sea, engaging in the mystery and madness of the depths as they try to figure out what's going on and how to get out alive - if they can. The game definitely evokes that Lovecraftian ideal of cosmic horror and the strangeness of the depths and I had a feeling of immersion that built with each step forward.There's definitely a lot to dig into with the story and what's going on - even in the side missions which you can undertake by scanning from the submarine.Overall, it certainly kept me going and interested throughout and I especially enjoyed the ending I got (of which there are two).  Stirring Abyss is a fun squad-based tactical game with a rich story and depth to its gameplay elements that kept me coming back for just one more turn. And now that it's released, I'm looking forward to giving it another whirl and seeing what the developers add in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a [X-COM] in which aliens become test subjects in the end. It's scary and merciless in the setting of HPL + deep sea. Well, in that case I can lower the difficulty to 'easy' and then enjoy. Yes, I'm enjoying it, slaughtering every gruesome creature. It's not to exploit. I have no choice in order to overcome the overwhelming horror I face. May you too anyhow enjoy the horror, since the game is too good to miss.

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem of tactical-turnbased games. Stirring abyss is nice mix blend between Rouge-like, tactics, turnbased and resource managment\survival games.Premise is simple - one submarine, bunch of people, and horrors from abyss. Story is simple - repair sub, get what you can and get out. But what mysteries and revelations will be unleashed is up to player.Game have nice graphics and music - feeling vibes of classic X-Com Terror from the deep yet looking even smoother and nicer in modern visual.  The scenery ain't static - air bubbles, decorative sea life sometimes blend and mix hiding your enemies in bushes of sea flora. Ancient ruins, derelict ships or caverns of multiply layers - all made with nice touch and leave good aftertasteSound design a bit simplistic but it's all understandable - who need a lot of sonds if he surviving under layers of unfriendly sea. Tactics and rpg system are nice - most of time your crew is outnumbered by underwater horrors and you should stay on your toes to be not outgunned too. Your crew also level up and gain new traits and skills. As cherry on pie you also can do otherworldish mutations on your crew giving both boost for combat yet making some equipment unsuableThere many rouge-like mechanics, random missions and randomized loot and goals yet all is pretty nice and quite atmosphericIn total overall if you eager some true Lovecraftian + X-com experience - Styrring abyss is your dish on plate to taste. Highly recoomending
_childDocuments_.name: Stirring Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: This may be my favorite game. It is often compared with 'XCOM' games, but it is much more than that. There is no research here, instead there is Ouiji board and leveling up your characters. Your weapons never get any better than when you start.        Compared to other tactical turn based games, you are seriously underarmed. The reliance on strategy is greater than most of its competitors. Trying to mantain your air level and sanity add twists to this game.  Every mission is a 'night' mission. Many missions are genuinely scary. if you love 'XCOM' games, you owe to yourself to get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it from the start, with some reserves I will further explain. Pros: - Great lovecraftian vibes- A sense of incoming catastrophe which permeates the whole story- X-Com mechanics (battle, base management, enemy research) crossed with Darkest Dungeon mechanics (stress management, resource management, base management)- Skill selections and skills in general really matters, you need to use them at their best- Mutations are great and improve your guys- Great graphic- Good music- I beat the game in story mode, narrative difficulty, without encountering much challenge, except for the last battle which I had to repeat once. Then the game was over, and I did not have the chance to craft and research all weapons, completing research tree etc and I was a bit disappointed. Game looked short. but then i found out there is another completely different game mode with a different map, different missions, and this looks promisingly long and challenging, so I am looking forward to start this new mode and continue my adventure. Cons: - I encountered few enemies types and few bosses in the story mode, I hope there'll be more in the other modesI bought this game on christmas sale and for now I feel that is definitely worth the price. Props to the developers for such a polished, funny, immersive game that brought me back the feeling of old X-Com playing along with my favorite Lovecraft moods. Game is 8/10 to me, a must have if you are fan of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Stirring Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying this game.Pro:Combat system. Is neat and enjoyable. I've played some other turn base games, and I think Stirring Abyss is clearer and effective. The Rpg progression of your characters is very good. There are many upgrades and many ways of upgrading. When you're presented with a choice and you spend some minutes agonizing on which bonus would suit the character better, you know they've made a good job. Balance: It's a sweet spot. Not frustrating but I feel all the time you're on the verge of defeat. The idea of having you character running out of oxygen really gives you a lot of tension every time you get out of the submarine. Story. There is a quite involving mainline quest plus sidequest mission (you have to mind a tradeoff between sidequest mission and the overall corruption levels. Missions never get repetitive.  Story is rather engaging with some nice twists. Cons: not totally sold on the graphics and animation, but they are solid.Needs some variety on the characters portraits.Some balanced is needed on the crafting system (too expensive and not competitive with other upgrades, in my opinion). Conclusion: a very neat, well made turn based lovecraftian underwater game. Loads of decisions to make every turn and they will matter.
_childDocuments_.name: Stirring Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: Could not resist this game after trying the demo. It sits at the intersection of an odd Venn diagram of underwater adventure, Lovecraftian horror, and turn-based tactical squad combat (a favorite subgenre of mine). Three wining elements all together in a nice package, along with a decent - and sometimes funny and grotesque - RPGish character build system. Part of me would have preferred a more realistic, darker art design, but the pulp comic book style grew on me and goes well with the Cold War period in which the campaign takes place. I've read complaints about the high difficulty. Can't speak to those as I only played the campaign on Story Mode and the Easy/Normal Endless mode. Both were manageable, but the difficulty increase between them was quite noticeable.
_childDocuments_.name: Stirring Abyss

_childDocuments_.review: "Hey mummy can I have some cash for a new game that just came out on Steam ?""Sure my little one, what kinda game is it ?""Its based on the works of HP Lovecraft, you know about crazy creatures and death and losing your mind that kinda stuff.""Oh that sounds nice, ok heres the money."Hah ! fooled her.Little does she realise what kind of game this truly is dear reader.It starts of with you on board a US sub the Salem in the late 50`s when you encounter a mysterious underwater mountain.You lose control of your sub and wake up an indeterminate time later on your own. You have to find out what happened to the rest of the crew.Of course this means traversing underwater in your diving suit with limited oxygen which you can replenish sometimes with air pockets.Whilst doing all this you have to gather any scrap metal on the seabed to repair your sub and thus gain more advantages such as sonar and searchlights...Whilst this is going on you will also encounter the hostile creatures of the deep which have different abilities such as spitting poison etc...Combat is a deadly affair with you using various abilities and weapons found and crafted.The maps are proceduraly generated thus providing a fresh experience each playthrough.Also your crewmembers are different each game.There is also an endless mode which I have not tried yet but sounds like fun.The game itself ran really well and I did not notice any bugs so far.It plays very much like the original Xcom which is a good thing.I like the fact that you can also lose your sanity as you witness the horrors from the deep.This game is a real bargain at about £16 and it has a lot of depth....get it ? Depth...joke one.Seriously though it will have you hooked once you realise what you have to do...Hooked...er...ok.Just buy this and you wont regret it.Oh one moment dear reader my mum is knocking at my door....."Yes woman what do you want now ?""Im just checking to see if you like your new game my little cherub.""Hahaha you poor fool. You really have no idea what evil you have unleashed upon the world. I shall devour your soul. MUahahahahaha !!!!!!""Honey...?...your voice sounds strange...are you ok...unlock this door at once..."Door opens..."Honey I cant see you your room is so dark...are you there..?"She steps inside the darkened room."Hun..?...what !!!...oh my god!!!!!!......AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA......"
