_childDocuments_.review: This is my first Shiren the Wanderer game and I'm really enjoying it! The only other Mystery Dungeon games I've played have been from the Pokemon Mystery Dungeon (PMD) franchise and wow, this game is a lot harder than any of those. I'm enjoying the challenge though!This is a rougelike so if you die, you lose everything in your inventory. Not just a portion. EVERYTHING. Later on you can tag items to get again but this is so brutal and not for the weak of heart. This game also requires a lot of inventory management. You'll have to constantly use items to clear space. There is also a ton of grinding to get your gear up to spec in the later dungeons and if you lose them, you have to do it all over again. This all also applies to your level and experience. Every time you leave, finish or die in a dungeon your level and exp is reset. You also start from the beginning every time and progresses the same every time. Manekineko Village > Destiny Trail > Tower of Fortune > Town > Dungeon. Like I said though, I've been enjoying this (so far). I'm about 8hrs and 4 dungeons into the game as of this review and it hasn't destroyed my spirit (yet).The Tower of Fortune and the Dice of Fate originally came out on the Nintendo DS so this is an updated port. It includes 3 new dungeons to challenge you. The Bladeless Wasteland, where no weapons drop and physical attacks do less damage. The Cloister of Certain Doom, where you set a target number of turns to clear the dungeon and an end game dungeon, the Garden of Destiny, where monsters killed in one attack give you huge exp but the more attacks you do, the less experience you get. It also has a Music Collection to listen to tracks at any time (not while actually playing the game). A Live Display that is designed for streaming and possible use for speedrunning. It shows your status, items, abilities, gametime, and turns spent in the dungeon. I've been using the Live Display as I stream the game and it's been wonderful! I would honestly just play it normally with this display on. Being able to see your bag at all times is super useful! Like the PMD games they have also added a rescue system. If you die in a dungeon you can send out a request for help. You can also generate a code to give to others for help. However if you do this you have to wait for help and cannot continue playing until you have been rescued. I have honestly never used this system in any game as I always want to continue playing. The last new addition this updated port has is a ranking system. You can compare scores and fight to be on the top of a leaderboard, if you're into that.Graphically this game boasts its older pixel style and I personally love it. This has not hurt my eyes while playing but I could see it bothering others with its brightness, so look at gameplay videos or screenshots to see if you may be affected by this. I've had no issues running this game, no screen tearing or anything. You can run it fullscreen, windowed fullscreen or windowed in any size. It's a pretty light game, you don't need a beefy system to run it. The soundtrack has actually been very nice. Even though you're going through the same areas over and over, I have not become sick of any tracks and actually quite enjoy them. I will be checking out the OST to listen to while not playing. If you've played the Pokemon Mystery Dungeon series and want more of a challenge or just a challenge, definitely pick this game up. You can also find it on the Nintendo Switch!
_childDocuments_.name: Shiren the Wanderer: The Tower of Fortune and the Dice of Fate

_childDocuments_.review: So for those that don’t know, Shiren is one of the original Mystery Dungeon games, before any of the Pokémon spin-offs were a thing. In fact, the first Shiren game came out all the way back in 1995. So here we have an updated version of the 2010 release The Tower of Fortune and the Dice of Fate, the fifth Shiren game overall and the first time the series has made an appearance on PC.Let’s start with the gameplay. You start each run by entering the Tower of Fortune with the goal of reaching the very top – the end of the game. Each floor has a randomized layout with a bunch of enemies, items, and other little secrets and stuff scattered about. The gameplay is turn-based, with each movement and action using a turn. Equipping an item, for example, uses a turn and allows enemies to advance one tile, as the movement is grid-based. If you’ve ever played a Mystery Dungeon game, you’ll know what to expect here.Shiren, however, adopts a more traditional approach to the roguelike genre: that of high difficulty and punishing gameplay. You start each run at level one and when you die, you not only lose your level progress, but all of your money and your entire inventory as well, effectively resetting your progress back to zero. It’s pretty brutal, but there are a few things you can do to lessen the impact. For one, you can stock up on items to auto-revive while in dungeon or offer an escape upon collapse. Additionally, you can pay certain NPCs to “tag” items in your inventory to be retrieved from the dungeon upon your death.This is good because each weapon and shield has its own specific level and, if managed effectively, you can power level that one weapon or shield and keep it through future runs even if your level resets. In fact, this is pretty much what you are expected to do as otherwise you stand no chance at the higher floors. The difficulty may sound frustrating, but the options here were enough that it never felt like I was at a complete loss.Aside from the difficulty though, Shiren has a ton of gameplay depth. This is the kind of game where you are constantly discovering new things, whether they be items and enemies, or entirely new mechanics. What’s cool is how all of these interact with one another. For example, I could pick up a weapon and sell it for its value the next time I find a shop in the dungeon, or I could hold it until I find a synthesis pot and combine it with my main weapon to further its stats. Or maybe I’ll run into an NPC who offers to take my weapon and upgrade it on the promise of returning it at a later floor.Then you’ve got day and night cycles, ability slots, ranged weapons, magic, companions – it’s honestly a bit of a strategy game with how much you have to keep in mind while playing, but that’s really where it shines. The sheer depth behind the pixel graphics is what I’ve come to love about the Mystery Dungeon series. And while on the topic of graphics, I quite enjoyed what was offered here. They’re simple, but effective for this type of game and honestly a bit nostalgic. The music too, it really brought me back to the days of PSP and DS RPGs, and I mean that in the best possible way.However, the game isn’t without fault. The core gameplay itself is fun, but inventory management is not – and that is something you are going to be doing A LOT of. You get 20 inventory slots and that’s it. Given that those slots can be filled up in just a few floors, you’ll quickly find that a lot of the game is shuffling around items, figuring out what to take and what to leave behind, and really just staring at a menu for minutes at a time. You can expand your inventory through preservation pots (which can hold up to five items), but you still have to shuffle items in and out of these pots from both the ground and your base inventory. It’s not enough to ruin the experience, but the inventory management was definitely a pain.That and the PC port is also not the best. Although it runs at a smooth 60 fps at 1440p, there are a number of smaller issues that really add up. For one, when the game is running in borderless window, you’re able to drag the window around with your mouse, which doesn’t sound like a problem at first until you accidentally do so and can’t reposition it perfectly. I had to fully restart my game a few times due to this.Then you have the controls, which are all over the place. I wasn’t a fan of the default keyboard controls (which cannot be rebound and are limited to three layouts), so I opted for an Xbox controller, but that also has its issues. The right stick is supposed to let you look around the map freely, but in its current state it simply doesn’t work. It goes off in random directions, sometimes the opposite of what I input, but sometimes it does do the right input, I honestly have no idea what it’s doing. The PS4 controller is worse in that the button settings do not appear to do anything and don’t match up with what is in-game. Oh, and the right stick does not work there either.However, if you can get over the technical issues and the rough inventory management, there is a fun game here. Complex mechanics, classic roguelike gameplay, cool graphics – it’s not a bad game, it’s just a game held back by a less-than-stellar PC port. I would recommend it, but it might be worth waiting for a few patches first. The game currently has a beta branch testing some fixes, so you might not even have to wait that long. If anything, I’m excited to see if this paves the way for more Mystery Dungeon on PC.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: Classic Mystery Dungeon game finally on PC. I'd imagine if Rogue were made today, it'd be Shiren the Wanderer. This game is absolutely fantastic and absolutely brutal. You're going to die, you're going to have unfair things happen to you (had a tank monster specifically nuke my weapon after tripping on a trap and dropping it), but that's part of the fun. Don't expect a run to be successful, because it probably won't be.There's hundreds of different weapons and shields, all of which do their own cool things. You can use an item melding system to create randomly generated "New Type" gear that you will then find as drops. You can tag your gear to eventually get it back when bad things happen (unless it gets obliterated by a tank bomb, that is).I heard some issues with controller configurations but I can't say I've noticed any with my Xbox Controller.This game is fantastic and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Shiren the Wanderer is not a hard game, but an unforgiving one: I made it to the final floor of the last story dungeon on my first run, before succumbing to my own stupidity: YADS (yet another stupid death). A player unfamiliar with the game loop may believe grinding is necessary to overcome the challenges, and it is an option, but it is not the only way to play. In Shiren item interaction is key. You'll go far by filling jars with staves and deploying their spells effectively. Every enemy encounter is a puzzle, and you'll be going into your menus a lot to select the right item for the job. If you do desire to grind in order to ease your progress, the inclusion of multiple dungeons makes this a bit less fatiguing. As of writing, I lost a +20 shield to a dark monster. The game wasn't being cheap. I just was being cocky. I went in with an escape scroll, and I had meant to bail as soon as I got some loot for what would have been my final run, but I wasn't paying attention and walked right into it. But I won't let the setback stop me from going in for another run.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, highly recommended to any roguelikes fan!It looks simple at first, but its complexity arises with time passing. Lot of traps, items and consumables to discover and experiment with.Recognizable monsters that each have a unique ability, ensuring you will not enter the dreaded "auto-pilot" state that will inevitably kill you (I'm looking at you Angband...). The food clock seems well balanced and the ID minigame is challenging, due to the sheer number of different pots types.Cool chill out music, awesome retro graphics and UI.Item/storage management is sometimes a bit tedious as you will have to insert & extract items into/from countless different pots.(tip: use the "Lock diagonal move" key/button to select several items in your bag . It also works in shops!)Not a fan of the night mechanic though... but it seems you can create powerful combos with abilities.Also, I haven't played with NPCs a lot, but from what I saw the AI is not great.Compared to other roguelikes I've played (Brogue, DCSS, Angband, Cogmaind, Infra Arcana,...), the main story is on the easy side (I beat it after 27h of casual play, without grinding too much nor using custom-brewed "new items"). The first boss killed me twice. I beat it on my third try then went straight to the end of the game in the same run.Then, there's the real stuff: around 30 (!) post-game dungeons with different rules and 99 floors, most of them not allowing to bring in items, for a complete and authentic roguelike experience. Once you try those side dungeons, you will quickly discover that the main story is just a glorified tutorial, and that the game will challenge you for a LONG time.Playing on a linux laptop, it works with proton! I just had to customize the launch option command with: "PROTON_USE_WINED3D=1 %command%" (minus the quotes) to bypass a crash at launch.ZERO crash encountered so far, I'm playing with with the "Keyboard (Type B)" input option, which only use the keypad, so I can hold my beer in the other hand!Awesome game, buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the original game, I was really excited to play this.While it has moments of being as stomach churningly difficult as the original, it's a lot easier and more accessible with it being a lot easier to retain your items and get party members, There are a couple of glaring flaws though, I was very excited about being able to rescue other wanderers who collapsed but the game makes doing so incredibly complicated and the mechanic of it more than a little dissatisfying. I feel like it should be enough to want to do it and it should just let you resurrect others, it is frustrating that it's only available at the beginning of the game when your unlikely to have any items or any gold left over after dying. Another issue is that not only do you not get to keep your experience level after defeating one of the towers but you're not allowed to return to the easier towers after you've beaten them. This just doesn't make sense, it would be understandable that your levels are wiped when you die but why should they be wiped if you were successful?Shiren isn't really an rpg that's about grinding but at the same time there is a certain amount of grinding neccesary to be strong enough to survive the first level of the tower of the future. Thus one spends a ton of time that feels unnecessary trying to build up your character on the first few levels. nevertheless this is a lot of fun and very addictive if more than a little frustrating

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long time fan of the Shiren games. I love mystery dungeon, but Shiren is my favorite style. I played the DS version so often as a kid. I enjoyed the Vita game, but it lacked accessibility... Until now lol. I did play Shiren 2 a bit, but it was in Japanese (so I could not read it). I've always wanted more Shiren ever since I touched the series. I love it's strange quests, style, enemies, etc. Turn based combat that feels like a big game of dungeon crawling chess... The weapon/equipment mechanics make your grind feel worth your runs, and the rage that ensues when you lose it all is LEGENDARY. The tagging system in the Tower of Fortune helps that a bit for players that hate losing it all when they die. I for one, enjoy this aspect of the game. It brings difficulty not found much elsewhere, and sometimes forces you to make a difficult sacrifice to save your run/items. Each run is RNG monsters, items, NPCs, and floor layout. Some areas are pre-set, but most places in the dungeons are randomized. So no matter how prepared or safe you might THINK you feel, always be ready to get knocked back to floor 1 at Lv 1 with no items! :)) Shiren as a series (for me): 9/10!This game though? 7.5/10.Cons:-Limited inventory-Limited Storage-No other multiplayer or social modes (like item trading, excluding the password systems)-Port took WAY too long to release, MORE SHIREN PLEASE .-.Pros:-Great art style-Easy to learn, hard to master-Rougelike (Rougelite)-Interesting enemies, difficult night time dungeons, and cool rare items-Has massive potentialI can't wait to see if they do more games in this style, or the old DS style. I know they probably won't, but its fun to dream.

_childDocuments_.review: An unforgiving mystery dungeon rogue-like with permanent death. Shiren requires careful thinking and analysis of each move, and when you die, you know you could have done better. Sometimes, you get lucky with RNG that help you progress further. The game offers many tutorials and puzzles at the beginning, which are optional but useful for mastering the game's mechanics. It also includes some gimmicks, such as this one  Inventory management is crucial in this game (to increase your chances of being safe), so be prepared to carry a lot of useful items, especially pots that increase your inventory space. The biggest challenges I faced were the traps and curses that ruin your gear. It takes up bag space and I found myself having to toss away those items. I recommend this game for those who like old style japanese rogue-like games and want a challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Shiren the Wanderer is fantastic, it has a lot of the elements that makes Nethack fun for me, but a lot less bloated and way more accessible, with good music and graphics. There are a lot of interesting mechanics if you want to dig in, but you don't really need them to succeed. The most important things can be found through trial and error.I don't really play with the meta progress mechanics, which makes the game even harder than it is normally. Extremely unforgiving. Mid-to-end game you will absolutely find yourself saying "How on earth could I have possibly survived that situation, I had no chance", but that's pretty normal for traditional roguelikes in general, and if you keep trying you will realize that no, metaprogression or luck was not required, just some skill and knowledge and preparation is enough (I'd say 95% of the time) to succeed during those moments you thought were absolutely impossible before.But even if you don't want to ride the struggle bus, and don't even want to deal with the tedium of upgrading items over multiple runs, you can just lean on your allies that level up and retain their levels throughout all your runs.There are tons of dungeons of various lengths outside the main story dungeon, many of which have genuinely interesting challenges. Some of them give no option for meta progress or allies or anything, and there's even some dungeons that are more puzzle-style than roguelike. All these shiren games are pretty much the same besides the extras, and this one has some great extra dungeons. I don't really 'get' the day/night cycle and spells stuff this game has in some parts. Overall it's great and I bought this game both on steam and on switch without hesitation.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is actually one of the OTHER variants of the Mystery Dungeon (Fushigi no Dungeon) series, the most popular one being Pokemon Mystery Dungeon. This is the only variant with original characters, as opposed to all of the others being licensed, and the vast majority of them being Japan-only.I don't think this is the BEST Roguelike (no, the genre isn't called "Mystery Dungeon", the genre originates with a much older PC game named Rogue, and other genres with these elements are "Roguelites"), or even the best game in the Mystery Dungeon series, but it's actually ported to natively run on PC, which surprisingly isn't too common for the genre, despite originating on PC.The Mystery Dungeon series in general is way more accessible than some of the more older, as I would call it, "Traditional" styled roguelikes, like Elona, Nethack, Ancient Domains of Mystery (ADOM), or Caves of Qud. However, I don't think this is the best place to start for a more, as I dub it, "console-style" Roguelike. It's REALLY hard to actually describe what I'm talking about, because the entire Roguelike genre is one of those genres that needs more division.So if this isn't a place to start, what is? I'd suggest starting with the PS1 game Azure Dreams, despite it's really dated 3D graphics, it still has compelling and fun gameplay for a Roguelike, and holds up quite well despite it's age. Other great options are the Pokemon Mystery Dungeon games, from within this series, which are unforgiving in places but still designed for people who are new to the genre. However, the high level dungeons in those pale in comparison to the actual nightmares of high level Shiren gameplay.Nonetheless, while this entry isn't my favorite, it's still very solid as someone who likes Mystery Dungeon a lot. No real complaints here, other than that the Shiren subseries as a whole tends to be more unforgiving in a lot of ways, but that's more down to my personal preference of subseries. If you know what you're in for, buy this game, if you aren't familiar with Mystery Dungeon, don't start here honestly.7/10 - "For series fans, not the highlight of it's series, and not the highlight of it's genre, but respectable in it's own right"

_childDocuments_.review: Step 1 - Get the point card in the second villageStep 2 - Get 70 points (will probably have to escape the dungeon for the first one)Step 3 - Buy Undo Grass and keep it in your inventoryStep 4 - When you die (you will) do NOT revive and just warp back to townStep 5 - Go back to step 1 and repeat the grind on equipment/partyNot following these steps will likely lead to a lot frustration and losing all your equipment every death. _childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty great but there are some drawbacks.I've always wanted to play a mystery dungeon game in earnest. Shiren is the most classic example of a mystery dungeon type game from the modern era, so I went with this game. I got exactly what I expected and more. This game is full of interesting characters, difficult encounters, and endless combinations of situations to try new strategies. There is no shortage of surprises here. There are a few glaring flaws with this game that are hard to overlook so I'll lay them out.This game contains a lot of bells and whistles but fails to implement them in a compelling way. There is a shop in the village, which is rendered nearly useless to the player. Once you enter the dungeon there is no way to get back to the village with all of your things unless you find an escape scroll, during my 8 hours of gameplay at the time of writing this review I found only one of these items. The other way to continue playing is to be rescued by another player who is both willing to rescue you in the dungeon and also has an item capable of reviving you. Such items are just as rare to come by as escape scrolls. The player base of this game also happens to be too small for player rescue to be a feasable option.Every time you die you must start over from the village. This is fine and actually the appeal of roguelikes, but you are robbed of any sense of progression by the fact that you are able to use none of the features within the town without return by one of the aforementioned methods, at the beginning of every retry you are stripped of all your items leaving you with nothing to sell and nothing to use for the villager quests.Don't get me wrong! This game is actually fun, the experience is there, it's just that everything besides the core gameplay is icing on the cake to put it bluntly. Any side-quest or character encounter that happens outside of a dungeon exists as a garnishing. The real meat and potatoes of Shiren The Wanderer is in using your strategic mind to overcome the randomness of each dungeon and their escalating difficulty. This alone makes Shiren worth it.I am going to recommend this game and give it a solid 7/10. If you love strategy games, board games, mystery dungeon games, roguelikes and especially difficult games. Shiren The Wandere: The Tower of Fortunge and the Dice of Fate is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: So i've played about 20 hours of this on Switch. I truly want to love this game, but it does everything it can to be detestable. I am an experienced roguelike player, and I love the concept of permadeath, but this game goes so far out of it's way to punish you for dying that it is un-fun. Meta progression is item based, with weapons and shields leveling up. The leveling is intensely slow, even slight improvements take many runs and escapes. The dungeons are also filled with a type of trap that permanently undoes all this grinding in an instant unless you are lucky enough to be able to "plate" your equipment. You can "tag" these weapons to appear in a "lost and found" if you die, but it doesn't always work and the game doesn't explain why. The game would be better off without this meta progression if it were balanced to start from scratch on each death.After the initial portion of the game there is a day and night system. At night, your view range is restricted to 1 square, and the dungeon becomes infested with monsters that can 1-shot you. To compensate you're given "abilities" that can only be used at night. Unfortunately they aren't powerful enough to reliably kill these "night monsters" and regular weapons always hit them for 1 damage. The inventory is extremely restricted and you will spend more time shuffling items in and out of containers than you will actually adventuring. The game gives you "party members" but they don't do anything most of the time and frequently wander off and get killed. Once you are forced to recall or get one-shotted by a night monster, the game will make you slog through 14(!) floors of too-easy content before you get back to the meat of the game. During this slog it will throw dozens of useless items at you, and you'll be forced to deal with a permanently clogged inventory the whole time. "The Tower of Fortune" is full of half-baked ideas and gimmicky mechanics and feels much more un-focused than the other Shiren games. I tried everything I could to enjoy this game but it tries to do too many things and doesn't do any of them particularly well. If you're looking for a good roguelike I would say get Tangledeep or Jupiter Hell over this.

_childDocuments_.review: For all the good that this game has to offer, and the clear inspiration and innovation the series has provided to the mystery dungeon genre - it pains me to give this game a thumbs down. There is just too much going on outside the player's control, too many small inconveniences that add up and weigh the rest of the game down. Go play Genso Wanderer or one of the various Pokemon mystery dungeon games and save yourself the frustration of dealing with the nonsense that is seemingly around every corner here. Who knew that enemies teleporting you from hallways into instant kill boxes could have been annoying? If you're looking for a "fair" experience - you won't find it here.

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really, really wanted to love this game.The world is very charming, when the gameplay is good, it is really good, and I was a huge pokemon mystery dungeon fan.So why did I end up leaving this bad review?Honestly, there were many problems.1 - the game drops you then and there with close to zero explenations."Oh no, my girlfriend is going to die! I need to help her" says the first companion you can have.Quick question, I have met you for a grand total of 30 seconds. Why should I help you?but, let's say, I'm the one being a naughty naughty boy, and I'll help him.Once that first scene is over, the game goes "right, you've got enough exposition. go do the tutorials."Aside from one or two extra text boxes when you speak to the other teammates, you know nothing, and it really strains my wish to know more about this game.2- The first companion is mandatory!What I mean by that is that you absolutely 100% have to save him and keep him alive in main story dungeons.It means you always have two party members on hand, and if he died at the end of a level, congrats, you're doing it all again without him until you reach his floor again.This wouldn't be too bad if...3 - this game is a roguelike, not a roguelite.Same thing right? Well, a roguelite lets you keep a few things inbetween runs to help you handle the tougher challenges of the game without making you do it all again.This, is a rogue like. the only thing that carries through each run are the allies levels.You go back to level one, you loose all your equipement, and when your companion ends up in a grave and you have to resurect him, you always get a nice little message that goes "hey, I know you don't have any item or any money. but do you have any healing items to throw at the guy?"4 - the RNG in this game is something alright.When you are lucky, it feels great. but that's the thing. you're only lucky. no matter how skilled you are, if you have ♥♥♥♥♥♥ luck, you are royally ♥♥♥♥♥♥.it feels more like luck is key, rather than knowledge and reflections.If any of this doesn't sound too bad, go ahead. it is a gave I would like to give a mixed score, but I can't so negative it is. but, if you like the punitive roguelikes that don't give two ♥♥♥♥♥ about the story, this game might be for you

_childDocuments_.review: I played the Vita version before this one. It's basically the same game except the rescue system is not backward-compatible with Vita. It is sideways-compatible with the Switch version, though, so go out there and rescue your Nintendo brethren!As for the game itself, it is a dungeon crawler with a very streamlined control scheme. At first the game might seem clunky, but as you play and learn more of how the items and monsters work, you gain the ability to whizz through it. There are also a lot of ways to deal with permadeath (rescues, revival items, tags for valuable weapons) so it's not as punishing as older Roguelike games (but don't worry if you're here for something hardcore and dangerous -- there are post-game dungeons that only experts can clear.) There's some very relaxing music too.This game has something for everybody. Newcomers get several tutorials, people who've played dungeon crawlers before get new items and monsters to mess with, and experts get to compete with each other to be the fastest.

_childDocuments_.review: I had heard good things about the serie of games "Shiren the Wanderer" in the past, and I've always been a fan of roguelikes, so when this newest instalment was ported on Steam, I thought it would be a good idea to try it out, and get my first taste of this "roguelike serie".Unfortunately, it soon became clear that the game is not at all what it says on the box.A run of Shiren makes you starts at level 1 and you're tasked with climbing up a randomly generated dungeon (the titular Tower of Fortune). It is played turn-by-turn, so you're supposed to think before you act, in order to escape the various traps and monsters that you're gonna meet, using your wits and your inventory. If you're not good enough, you will die, be ejected from the tower, and lose everything, thus being forced to start again from the very beginning. This description, at first, would indeed seems to fit the mold of a roguelike, so very much something I would enjoy playing.However, soon, the differences with a proper roguelike starts to appear. First, you understand that you can buy equipment at the start of your run. Then you figure out there are ways to avoid death and escape with a variety of loot, so that even if you fail a run, you can start the next run with that equipment and a large variety of items on you right from the start. Finally, you will understand that there are many different ways of improving your equipment, and that theses upgrades can also be carried from run to run.Thus, your first runs will be scary, as you start with no equipment, at level 1, and you're constantly scared that you could fail, die and lose everything. However, after a few runs, you will start having more and more powerful equipment right from the start, making the first levels 100% safe and moreover, you will know that you do not risk anything, as there are several ways to either escape the dungeon safely with all your loot and equipment, or even if that fail, you will be guaranteed to get back most of your equipment.The only thing that actually get reset with every run is your level, which impacts your HP, but a good armor will protect you against most dangers until you can get back to a decent level. So, as time goes on, the game feels less and less like a roguelike, and more like monster bashing, where your overpowered equipment make a mockery of more and more monsters. Moreover, the game doesn't have that much diversity in terms of how to deal with monsters and dangers. There are a lots of items, but most of them can be divided in a few categories (equipment, healing items, and a few spells to mix things up). As for the environment, while there are various traps strewn around, they do not affect monsters, so it is rare to get an opportunity to use the environment to your advantage. In the end, 99% of the time, the solution to any problem is "bash the monster on the head with your big sword".This is not at all the careful, thoughtful play that a roguelike player is used to, where the various items and environments are ressources you can use to create some new and interesting trap for monsters. Here, raw equipment numbers will trump everything. As you progress in the game, you will understand more and more of its inner workings. It will become clear that there is only one path to victory: Constantly improve your a sword and a shield, and use that to clear levels. To avoid spoilers, I won't delve into the mechanics of how you can improve your equipment, but let's just say that there are many ways of doing that, and that they both allow you to improve raw numbers (attack and defense), but also adds more effects (like applying effects to enemies or protecting you from specific effects). Moreover, the way it is done, you're clearly pushed towards having one very powerful sword, and one very powerful shield, and only use those two items.Thus, the actual gameplay of Shiren is revealed: it is a grinding game, where your purpose is to constantly improve your inventory (which is mostly your sword and your shield, but also include some other things), so that you can take on more and more difficulty floors, until you reach the end of the dungeon.This is not a game about subtle gameplay, it is a game of numbers. Have big sword, will bash monsters.So, in conclusion, I have been very disappointed with Shiren. It is advertised as a roguelike, but it is not. Being turn-by-turn and having randomly generated dungeon doesn't make a game a roguelike (like Nethack or Dungeons of Dredmor), or even a roguelite (like FTL)Shiren an RPG where you're grinding for better equipment. This is not in and of itself a bad thing, but this is very much different from what the store page, or even the beginnings of the game, would make you believe. If you like grinding, or getting powerful equipment that makes you feel super-powerful, then this a game for you. However, if you want a game require careful consideration of danger and clever use of your inventory/your environment, then Shiren is definitely not for you, and you should look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted so badly to like this game since there's so few Mystery Dungeon games on Steam, but if you're expecting something like Etrian Mystery Dungeon or even Nightmare of Druaga then this is not for you.For one thing, YOUR LEVEL RESETS TO 1 WHEN YOU LEAVE DUNGEONS. Oh, and once you finish one of the towers, you can't return to it. That may not sound so bad, but if you die you lose everything you had on you which means you have no way to even go back and grind for gear to replace it before tackling a harder dungeon. So once you die, you're all the more likely to do it again.Your partner characters are also dumb as a rock. You have to position them next to enemies yourself by having them follow after you, they have no autonomy or initiative of their own. Even worse they can get in your way and get hit by your attacks or end up with status conditions that make them attack you. The latter would at least be understandable for a roguelike, but again they're barely good for anything at the best of times.If you want a game that's relentlessly unfair, you may like this, but it wasn't for me and I say that as a fan of Mystery Dungeon games.

_childDocuments_.review: No. I'm going to be the dissenting voice here.This is not a good game. It would have been good in 1994 but not for a game released in 2010. Why did this series not bother with any quality of life updates whatsoever? Navigating every menu, using any item, equipping anything, managing your items, learning what your items do, or comparing equipment - it's all trash. You're going to be putting items in jars, breaking jars, storing items, and swapping items, and often times you'll have no idea what the item actually does, have a clear understanding of how to use it, or even to identify it. I get that Shiren is a classic series and this is Mystery Dungeon at its purest, but please - does it have to play like a game from two decades before its release? I'm fine with it looking like a Super Nintendo game - I love retro games and graphics, but this game is painful to manage.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend it...with some caveats.First, the control issues. Unlike most modern ports I've played, they aren't modular; instead you get a single layout for a controller from each manufacturer, and the option to invert button options like Confirm/Cancel and Target/Menu. However, the settings aren't even honest, depending on your controller: in my experience with DUALSHOCK 4 and multiple Nintendo Switch controllers, I have to invert one or both options to get the displayed functionality.If you don't mind fiddling with these and dealing with layouts constructed for you instead of making your own, then this is not an issue, and I still recommend the game on this score; the controls themselves are fairly intuitive once you're used to them and play quite nicely. I do, however, highly recommend a controller. I simply could not adjust to the keyboard layouts, but that may well be purely a skill issue on my end.Secondly, I find there are at least a couple of items with names that do not entirely communicate their purpose at first blush, while others do so just fine. "Transient Staff", for instance - I understand that transient can mean "staying in place only temporarily". However,  From the name, I don't think I would have figured out that it paralyzes and warps a hit target when used.There's also "Otogiriso", which the only reference of I can find is another piece of media developed by Chunsoft. This isn't an item I can tell you the use of - it's a fun fan reference in place of an item name. The fact that a horror game [sound novel, apparently?] has its name used for a health recovery item is also more than a little confusing. Ironic, as it cures the confused status.I will admit, however, that this may not be a big deal to you either. Items aren't usually meant to be identified by name alone in a game like this; we have Scrolls and Jars of Identity for that which properly reveal their descriptions to us, which then detail their purpose in clear text. If the occasional name being confusing or not quite right does not bother you, I would still recommend the game on this score.Thirdly and finally, the boss fights. Maybe it's just because I came from Shiren DS1, where we didn't really  these, but the boss battles can be hit-or-miss. For me, they are very much miss.The first boss summons additional monsters in a game where you can only reliably hit one target at a time, and smacks you for more damage than any of them can dish out in a single hit. However, this does not stop you from having to tank hits from the other monsters, who are  nothing to sneeze at. Your multi-target abilities are limited to items which are one use per, and magic which cannot be used during this fight if I recall correctly.The boss itself is immune to all status effects, in that if you spend a turn inflicting one, they will soon enough spend a turn removing it, if not immediately doing so. So incapacitating them while you deal with the summons is right out. Which, don't bother doing that, as defeating all of the summons simply triggers...another round of summons.Lastly, you're babysitting an NPC this entire time. The entire plot hinges on him being alive, so you  keep him alive. You won't fail the fight if he's got his grave marker on the map, but I don't recall the plot progressing properly when I won with him defeated either. At least I didn't have to rematch the boss...I'm not looking forward to future boss battles. However, maybe this sort of challenge entices you - I admit I may be an outlier. If this does not bother you, or you think it's worth bearing, I still recommend the game.Overall, I do  Shiren games. The gameplay itself is solid and the progression feels good to me. The above three caveats are just things that really get under my skin about this particular entry.If you think you can put up with the first one, aren't bothered by the second, and/or might even enjoy the third, then by all means - buy this game. But if it all sounds like too much of a bother, I'd say wait a while. Play some of the other Mystery Dungeon entries - it's a wide enough franchise that you have options.I hear Pokemon Mystery Dungeon is basically Shiren with Pokemon trappings. I mean...Shiren's pretty old at this point, so it wouldn't surprise me. Maybe give that a try if this isn't your cup of tea?

_childDocuments_.review: This game presents itself as a more traditional roguelike, even with the "enemies move when you move" turn-based system  you might be familiar with if you've played say, Dungeons of Dredmor or any of the other Mystery Dungeon games. However, pretty early on you'll be able to reliably get an item that lets you keep your money and items when you die (You're still thrown back to level 1, however allied NPCs are .) This turns the game into a quest to abuse the item synthesis and upgrade systems to build the baddest sword you can manage, then hope that one of the handful of things that can still take it away from you doesn't happen. At this point they throw a wrench in your plans by introducing a day/night cycle, where night exclusive enemies basically have to be defeated by abilities that you have to manage, and can only be used once per floor (Although there are ways to recharge them with items, obviously.)  If all this isn't enough, there's a bunch of optional bonus dungeons which were DLC in the 3DS/Vita versions, some of which will have limitations like not letting you bring in any of your own items. So fun times, basically.

Only downside is the window is sort of a fixed size you set when opening the game, but I can't honestly say I care about that.

_childDocuments_.review: If you get this, remember to SUSPEND your game NOT alt+f4 before quitting. Also make a periodic save backup from time to time. Crashes, just like power outages are super rare, but no one wants to be the guy who lost his progress on a 99F dungeon with his tagged 99+ gear.This is a 10 year old Nintendo DS game from an almost 30 year old series, that started off as a Dragon Quest spinoff. The Tower of Fortune and the Dice of Fate (Shiren 5) was ported to the vita with extra content (Shiren 5+), then switch and steam with a little more extra. In addition Steam and Switch use the same servers and password system, so you can rescue each other; no cross-save however. If you're a fan of the Pokemon Mystery Dungeon games there's a big chance you'll like this one too, since both are made by Chunsoft and play about the same. Game can be really unfair at times, where half of the fun is overcoming those unfair challenges. There is no shame in cheesing, but there is in being KO'd realizing you could have cheesed.Mystery Dungeon community is also a small but friendly group that can offer you help.
_childDocuments_.name: Shiren the Wanderer: The Tower of Fortune and the Dice of Fate

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the games in which the roguelike definition as a game similar to "rogue" totally applies. It is the mistery dungeon system you can find in other series like pokemon mistery dungeon or chocobo mistery dungeon, but in this title difficulty is harder and you need a bit more preparation to finish the game.I find the mechanics extremely good, but story wise it is a bit simple. I miss more story elements and unlockables.In about 30 hours I reached the first boss twice I am able to see when to desist and scape a dungeon. However I wasn't able to beat it. These 30 first hours passed really fast: I enjoyed it.Next day spent 5 hours and two runs, one to gather items and a second one to beat the game (mid and final bosses). Then started to organise items for more future runs. So in 40 hours you can complete the game and you still think on playing more in the mid-future.At first I did not like the night mechanic. But it gives the game variety and emotion in the final part. At the end you take advantage of itThis is a true gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Shiren the Wanderer: The Tower of Fortune and the Dice of Fate

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and played it start to finish over the course of 3 days any time I had free time. The gameplay is challenging and can be punishing if you are not careful but this is a game where knowledge is more powerful than levels especially considering your character level resets to 1 after a dungeon is completed or you are defeated. If you end up losing mid-game there are optional side dungeons you can play through that allow you to keep a few items and can be very helpful for recovering from losing your gear. There also are plenty of items that help you survive or keep your gear when you are defeated and a tagging system that can be used to give a chance to recover lost gear.As for how you can become stronger even after getting reset to level 1 it all comes down to upgrading and leveling up your sword and shield. They gain experience of their own to rank up to 8 ranks. Weapons can be augmented with runes to inflict status effects or hurt specific monster types. Shields also have various runes you can apply to them to defend against fire or explosions for example.On top of all that the music is excellent and the amount of content in this game is vast featuring many post game and optional dungeons and there are even 150 puzzle dungeons if that is your thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Shiren the Wanderer: The Tower of Fortune and the Dice of Fate

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!Haven't been playing a lot yet, but the time that I've spent with the game so far has been fantastic. The presentation is wonderful which is unusual for a game of this genre, the pixel art is nice and the music is pleasant and relaxing. I've been playing a lot of the original Shiren from the SNES era and this game expands on everything that makes that game such an enjoyable experience.The game is also very well suited for couch play, controller support works flawlessly for me (using xbox 360 controller). The game lets you change the font size of all ingame text so that everything is easily readable from the couch even if you have bad eye sight. You can also change the UI to classical which makes all the numbers bigger and easy to read from the couch. There is also an option to make the minimap bigger and more transparent, which is great for couch play.Overall, I'm very happy with the game and I can see myself playing this for a long time to come. I will update this review later on when I've gotten to know the game more. I wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone who is familiar with the roguelike genre or anyone who is curios about this type of game. It also has a very comprehensive tutorial for newcomers.
_childDocuments_.name: Shiren the Wanderer: The Tower of Fortune and the Dice of Fate

Said to dwell in the mysterious Tower of Fortune, Reeva decides the fates of all mankind with a trio of magic dice. Lead Shiren The Wanderer and his sidekick Koppa in their quest to conquer the Tower of Fortune. [Playstation.com]

name: Bright Memory: Infinite
detailed_description: Story In the year 2036, a strange phenomenon for which scientists can find no explanation has occurred in the skies around the world. The Supernatural Science Research Organization (SRO) has sent agents out to various regions to investigate this phenomenon. It is soon discovered that these strange occurrences are connected to an archaic mystery - an as-of-yet unknown history of two worlds, about to come to light... Gameplay Bright Memory: Infinite combines the FPS and action genres to deliver a high-octane experience. Mix and match available skills and abilities to unleash magnificient combos on your enemies. Your trusted sword allows you to slash through crowds of enemies and even repel their gunfire. The guns you come across in-game can be customized with a variety of ammunitions. Choose between incendiary bombs, sticky grenades, homing missiles, and more to suit your situation. Development Created by FYQD-Studio, Bright Memory: Infinite is the sequel to the popular Bright Memory. However, the sequel features an all-new world, along with newly created improved battle system and level design. Developer Comment For Bright Memory: Infinite, I wanted to focus on adding content to give players a more satisfying experience. As a result, development took three times as long as Bright Memory. This process allowed me to learn how to create a strong game while dealing with time and financial constraints. I spent a lot of time thinking of ways to maximize whatever technology and resources available to me in order to deliver an unforgettable experience through the game. As such, Bright Memory: Infinite represents the culmination of FYQD Studio's growth. Finally, I would like to express my gratitude to all my global partners and those who have provided technical support to me.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot stress this enough I have no idea what I just played. So many things were happening, and I don't know what I felt probably pure adrenaline and excitement. This game is not even a treat, it's a feast Its pure rush and a combat system that just makes you piss yourself. You're gonna be asking yourself the entire game wtf is happening, and I love it, there wasn't a second in that entire game that I made me feel bad or bored nothing just pure excitement just the best feeling I've had playing a game in a really long time.The only complaint I can possibly give to this game is the fact of the game is incredibly short at only two hours to complete your first run and the fact the story is pretty garbage but other than that it's a thrill ride. The gunplay is amazing, the swordplay is *chief's kiss*, getting to use 5 different weapons all with secondary fire mods, the sheer amount of different ways to kill your enemies, the ways to engage oh my god. This game puts Doom Eternal to shame I'm not even joking (combat wise). The bosses are difficult and require you to know the games mechanics in order to survive, and while upgrading the rocket punch to Level 3 will greatly improve your survivability, you still can't fling your sword around like crazy expecting the boss to die. The graphics look amazing, it looks so good it pushed my computer to the limit to the point where I had to even disable ray tracing because if not, I feared my computer would actually blow up from just the insane ♥♥♥♥ that was happening on screen. So much different ♥♥♥♥ is happening throughout this entire game that you're just in awe you have no words anymore for it. why is the boss spawning pythons and why does he have an eagle perched on one of his arms and he's punching me with it. Why am i all of a since doing swordplay on a plane in the air. WHYYYY? This game is amazing please please please play this it is so worth your money, on a sale though because while it is an amazing experience it's still only two hours long and if you to do multiple runs to get the 100% completion then that's up to you. I'm at a loss for words after playing that and I swear if a VR update or mod comes out for this you best believe I'm coming back, and I don't care if I get motion sickness, I will fight through that for this game was an experience like no other.

_childDocuments_.review: Some time ago, I got my hands on Bright Memory. Back then, it was supposed to be the first chapter of what we now have as Bright Memory: Infinite. I liked it and decided I'll give Infinite a try.The game feels and acts a little bit like Shadow Warrior, but with the obvious indie feel. You can play it as an FPS, and you also use a sword and some powers, although both the sword and the powers are secondary to the firearms.The story is okay, and it has some funny over-the-top WTF moments (no spoilers). The graphics are good, especially with RTX and DLSS turned on. The level design is nice, and the sound effects are okay. Unfortunately, the game stutters from time to time, and this can ruin the performance, especially when your screen is full of enemies.Depending on what difficulty level you pick, the game can be quite easy, especially when facing armed enemies. The boss fights, however, can be frustrating since most likely, you'll end up without ammo, and you'll have to run in circles, looking for some, or using your sword and powers and avoiding getting hit.One thing that I didn't expect is that the game is very short. You can finish it in 1 and a half hours if you know what you're doing and in about 2 and a half hours on the first playthrough. Given the fact the initial Bright Memory had around 1 hour, I was expecting this to be at least 5-6 hours long.I guess it's worth playing if you're looking for something short and on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics look great. Much better than a lot of current AAA games. Although the main character model is a bit blocky.It has nvidia's Reflex, RTX and DLSS 2.3.0. But can be updated to use DLSS 2.3.4It also has an option to turn on Epic's TAA Gen5. This is the first game that I've seen that has this option in game.Optimization is good. With everything maxed out, RTX off, DLSS in Quality mode, 1440p, I'm getting 100-144 fps.But RTX on the higher settings is very heavy.Combat is great and a lot of fun. It reminds me of Shadow Warrior.There are so many ways to kill enemies, that sometimes I have trouble choosing what I will use next. :DWeapons have a nice feeling to recoil. The sword is awesome. And the powers are very cool to use.Sound and music are good.There are a few annoying quick time events.Story is a bit of a mess. Characters have no depth.Dialogs are pointless. And things happen because of no reason.There's also a good amount of cutscenes, that are unskipable.Most are pointless. Seems like the dev put them in, just because he thought it was cool and to chow he can do it.But I would rather have less of these, and instead, have more levels that would increase the game's length.I also saw in a review that there is a stealth level, that is really bad. But I haven't reached that point yet.I can't justify paying 17 euros for this game. Mostly because of it's short length.I got it for a fraction of this price, because I bought the original at a discount, some time ago. So I'm happy with what I got.Maybe pick this up when it shows up at a discount in a Steam sale.

Only problem is how short it is and there are a few glitches here and there such as a certain Emperor constantly knocking himself out of the area towards the end or the archers firing through obstacles. _childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend getting it on sale. Outside of the default look for your hero of the game, the art direction in this one is magnificent. Moments like driving, flying or jumping from plane to another plane defies physics and yet still, way worth doing. It's just that there should have been a lot more. What it gives you isn't horrible at all, but you just want more of those moments in order to justify the kinda monotone story telling being used to keep your attention away from doing those amazing things. I'd say it's a little short in overall game play for that reason. It fills it with talk and even some repetitive fire fights as it progresses towards the end. I think this game's pure arcade style is worth experiencing on any given rainy day for the right price.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun and the combat is fun and gives players a fair amount of challenge. The combat is fast and flows really well, allowing you to experiment with different combos and skills. I also like the proper shooter/melee gameplay. most FPS devs' idea of "melee" is a knife stab. I like the ability to defend, deflect and combo with your sword. This game is a lot of fun and I would recommend it to anyone looking for something different in an FPS instead of "shoot enemies and occasionally stab with knife".  My biggest complaint is the length of it. I'm a super casual player so it takes me a long time to beat most games, but i beat this one on violence difficulty in 2.8 hours. I understand that it was done by a solo dev so I hope that in the future once the dev has more resources and people, they release free updates to expand the campaign of Bright Memory.

_childDocuments_.review: This has the makings to be up there with Half Life 2 and Titanfall 2 for some of the best FPS action on PC.  Seriously. _childDocuments_.review: So I received this free after buying the "demo" for this game. Demo is in quotes because there isn't a whole lot that transferred over oddly enough. The combat in the demo had way more interesting things going for it - while it had many of the same abilities they just felt more organic in the demo and the way you used the sword was much cooler IMO.I assume most of this review is going to be basically what everyone else will sayPros:- It looks pretty good. It's Unreal though, so of course. Water looks a bit janky but overall the game looks good.- Very stable frame rate. I was able to run it on the highest settings with ray tracing, DLSS Balanced, and Reflex with above 70 FPS the whole time. I have an RTX 2080 and a Ryzen 7 2700x CPU.- Despite the fact that I feel like combat got a downgrade, it is still pretty fun.- Music is pretty intense and fits the feel of the combat well.Cons:- Why does the game start with a QTE during an opening cutscene (after a cutscene that doesn't require them) and fail you if you don't do it fast? The icon that lets you know you need to be doing something also needs to be bigger and flashier because I honestly didn't even see it for BOTH of the QTEs in that cutscene.- Why is there forced stealth that resets when someone sees you? Why are you holding a meat cleaver that covers 60% of the screen during forced stealth? This whole section feels weird when the rest of the game is fast paced run and gunning- In the stealth area if you rub up against the wrong texture near a wall you character will stand up, and you'll probably get detected.- I'm 1.5 hours in and have most of the upgrades unlocked already, meaning the game doesn't have much time left.Neutral:- Story doesn't make a whole lot of sense. I mean, it doesn't really need to or anything since it's sci-fi. The way the demo went I really thought there was going to be more to the story though. I did expect pretty massive changes as more trailers were released for the full game so it wasn't too much of a shock or anything.- Voice acting is pretty decent for a solo dev project- There are a bunch of skins for your weapons and character, a few are DLC. It's a first person game but it does cut to 3rd person pretty regularly so you will still see the skins kind of frequently.- You unlock weapons in this order: Assault Rifle, Shotgun, Pistol (???), Sniper Rifle. I feel like we could've started with the pistol or something, and maybe just not have seen it's alt fire ammo until later to keep things balanced.- The enemies with shields can usually be scooped up into the air with the slide attack and taken down as if they didn't have shields. I feel like they should be immune to being lifted up until the shield breaks- I didn't experience any crashing or instability at all, but I do see others having issues. Maybe the DirectX 12 version is more stable or something?Overall I'd like to give this a neutral rating I think. For $20 I bought Risk of Rain 2 and have gotten hundreds of hours of fun from it. I think almost everyone will be able to 100% Bright Memory in under 10 hours (which includes beating the game multiple times) and afterwards I'm not sure how much replay value there will be. It might be worth $20 if you know all of this and still are interested in playing the game. I am clicking "Recommend" because this game was made by one person and is still a pretty great accomplishment in that regard

_childDocuments_.review: This game unites “shooter” with “hack and slash” into a high-speed action game.We use firearms, melee weapons and supernatural abilities to carve our way through the enemies.While the gameplay incorporates rather common game mechanics, overall it provides a very good impression. It has a very good dynamic, which always keeps you on your toes and gives a lot of fun.The game has very detailed high quality graphics, which is very enjoyable. It uses bright colors, recreating cozy China landscapes. In particular, the game has very realistic weather effects: wind on the grass and so on.All this beauty comes with the perfect optimization. The game has no sign of lags or freezes, running surprisingly smooth. With so many moving objects on the screen, it feels hard to believe sometimes.The game uses Unreal Engine, which is quite common, but this is definitely one of best visuals created with it.Overall impression is very good, however you can still feel the lack of resources of the small development team here and there.First of all, AI is quite basic. I can not say enemies are exactly stupid, but they can not be called smart. They do not attempt to use cover, seek for a good position or anything else.The game has a short stealth mission, during which we should sneak behind the enemies and take them silently one by one. This part of the game does not look impressive. The enemies behave quite stupidly and have a poor awareness. It is hard to tell why developers put all this into a game, as it does not actually fit its main gameplay. Perhaps they wanted to show their skills, but the result was rather poor. The game would be better without this semi-stealth.The game does not bother to present a lore or world history. Can’t say it is actually important for the action game, but it spoils the impression. Who is this “general Lin”? Why does his name ring the bell for the heroine? Who exactly are we fighting here and why? We can only guess.The game has some minor bugs, mostly with animations and physics, but nothing really crucial. Overall it runs quite stable.This game has only one real drawback - it is too short. Entire story takes 2-3 hours to pass through. If the game was at least twice as long - it would be almost perfect.Objective evaluation for this game is 7/10. But thinking that this one has been done almost single-handedly, just blows the mind up!What the hell is going on around the gamedev industry, if such an amazing project created by a small team, while large companies release junk? The developers of this game put everyone else to shame.Unless you have a specific detest for action-like games, you should definitely try this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory: Infinite is a FPS game, where you playing as a skilled agent and you need to stop the takeover of the world.I got this game for free, because I own the original Bright Memory game.Okay, let's start with the obvious one: the game looks gorgeous. Everything is so breathtaking and alive it's unbelievable for a one man project. Okay, there are some times, when graphics is not works as intended, like when you destroy a box, or an enemy / item get stuck into the wall or to each other, and characters emotion could have been better, but still it looks really awesome. Sound wise this game is on point too, especially the soundtrack. Really fits for the game and it's style and when it's a boss fight... oh man, it's great.Controls are easy enough and there were no problems when I played this game.Now, about the gameplay... in general it's okay. You need to finish the map, meanwhile you kill enemies along the way. You get a bunch of tools, some weapons and skills to deal with them and you need to use these in harmony to get through the army of bad guys. At first, I thought it's going to be super easy, because I felt like a god, when I used these skills, but actually the game's difficulty is pretty challenging at some parts, especially if you play on Violent at first, which I recommend for sure. Also, you can upgrade your character by collecting different resources along the way, which is also great. And basically that's the game, nothing more nothing less... just killing some enemies, a few bosses, getting some kind of story and you realize, that was the game. The best similar game to find for this game, is probably the Serious Sam games, but with less enemy types and weapons. I enjoyed the game, if I want to be honest, it's difficult enough, but it's short and even the story is not making this any better sadly......because it's really incoherent. I mean, you can get a basic idea about what is going on, but some elements of it either useless in the story or doesn't fit. Didn't quite liked this part of the software, but this is mainly an action game, not a story.And I didn't even mentioned, that the game is still not complete, there are smaller bugs and the unoptimalized, especially at the last chapter, where it crashed non stop. It's a common problem sadly, and hopefully it will get fixed.So, is this a good game? Well, I guess it is yes... it's fun for sure. Is it worth it's price? Well... I'm not quite sure this time. For 2 and half hours, I think 16.8€ is too much, but maybe for 10 or less. It's still an amazing game from ONE person, but I thought it will be more... at least I got it for free and I enjoyed it for that.

_childDocuments_.review: It's funny i almost did not play this game off of a youtube game review prior to release but im glad i did! personally i think the game is wonderful for what it is even though i ran into some small issues. pros: beautiful boss fights specially the last boss looked and felt amazing on max difficulty with a unique fighting style without just flooding the field with small enemies. _childDocuments_.review: Just finished this game and I had such a blast playing it!!! Absolutely love it. _childDocuments_.review: Most of you (myself included) already bought Bright Memory and are getting this game for free. This review is not for you, just play your free game. This review is for people who are going to spend $20 on this.I'll start with positives, because I mostly have negative things to say.1. Visuals and overall presentation are great2. Performance is fantastic, very well optimized3. General gunplay, attacks, and attack animations are solidThis game previews very well and makes for a good tech demo. When it comes to gameplay and how fun the game actually is, it all falls apart.If you enjoy Call of Duty campaigns you may not mind this, but for old school fps fans like myself this is just more janky scripted events, buttons prompts, and nonsensical fail states. It's a struggle to get more than a full minute of gameplay without events like these and do nothing but break immersion. The worst part about these is the game constantly breaks its own rules for the sake of scripted events. Like one wall is destroyed with a melee attack, the same exact wall later on is an interactable. You can crouch under a fallen tree and then 30 seconds later the same looking tree is another interactable. I hate stuff like this.The entire game is a giant corridor, there isn't even any opportunity to flank or take different routes. All level verticality only takes place during platforming sequences, in combat all levels are just flat with a couple pieces of cover thrown in.The game throws in tons of these beefy melee enemies that are just giant sponges unless you parry them, and really just ruin the well crafted tools the game gives you. Typical stand there, wait for the giant telegraphed attack, parry...Wow good gameplay. Not to mention the game will just spawn tons of ranged enemies shooting at you while you try to do this, and will use this tactic across almost all boss fights, requiring dumpster ads to introduce any kind of challenge.Yep, I beat the game in like an hour and a half, and the asking price is $20. What a joke. I wouldn't have an issue with this either if it was a good hour and a half, but it was just half baked and repetitive.Just to wrap this up, I think the developers largely mismanaged a small team and tried to do TOO much. This felt like an attempt to make a AAA Call of Duty campaign with like 1% of the budget, it just didn't work. The core gameplay and character controls were good, but the entire game surrounding and supporting them are not. This game could have been quite good actually if it stepped on the breaks a bit and delivered more of a sandbox, old school experience without all the presentation and scripted events.If you got the game for free, yea just play it. For $20, no, this is not worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished Bright Memory Infinite in one go. It took me 2.5h and judging by the presented score at the end this game is meant to be played multiple times in order to beat your previous scores. First of all, graphics feels like it's from the PS4 age, fundamentally, but it is cranked up to the very maximum of what the best PCs of today can handle. Details are incredible and texture resolution is sick (in a good way). Raytracing is used in a spectacular way all over! The game being made by one man (or so they say) feels like over-delivering on all fronts. I expected graphics to be as flashy as they were, but I expected the story to be more shallow than it was. It was still shallow, mind you, but a level above my expectations so that was a plus. Fighting felt a lot like Sekiro meets Crysis, as my friend commented in our conversation and I agree. The game being a first-person shooter definitely felt good to handle. I started with a mouse and keyboard, but ended up switching to a controller mid-game because the button layout didn't quite feel natural and I didn't want to remap the keys while I was already playing. The controller worked really good, though, and I expect this game to be pretty polished once it hits Xbox, supposedly next year. One thing reminded me of old-school fighting games where you would fight at a wild background scene like for example on the airplane wing. I mean, c'mon! But a cool touch nevertheless. Overall I would definitely recommend checking this game out, especially if you like competing with yourself and your friends in high scores. I will not give the game a numbered score because I don't believe in numbers, but I WILL tell you that the game is worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: [Gameplay]Absolutely fantastic game, loads of fun and the gun play is top notch! Movement is really responsive and fun, being able to strafe with a small cool down makes you feel like a badass.The melee combat is great, pair that with the Cyber arm abilities, then you've got a really engaging system. Being able to deflect bullets is great when you're in a tight spot.You can really become a master at it with multiple playthough's, there is many ways and options to taking down certain targets, it's really fun.Animations are super clean and well done.I've never had such a interesting FPS experience before, It's beyond any AAA ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that's being pumped out recently. [Story] It's there but it's very flat and the characters are below average, even the main character is lacking a lot of personality, nothing memorable.[Performance] - Ryzen 5600g/2060/16GBThis game's performance here really surprised me, I saw the beauty of the game and didn't expect to be at highest settings at 120+ FPS, for the best experience it's obviously best to turn on DLSS [Quality], get's rid of some of the shimmering on edges and boost your FPS without taking away details. I had Ray tracing on low and it looks great, but I did get down to the 100 - 90 FPS range.You will encounter some random FPS drops sometimes, it was pretty rare though, happened maybe 6 times though out the whole 2.8 hour play though. [Visuals]The game is absolutely beautiful, really crazy to see what such a small team could pull off here. Sometimes though, all that beauty can get in the way of what's actually happening in front of you, sometimes I couldn't tell at all where someone was, but that's a little more because of the games biggest issue for me..THE SHAKING!!! Obviously the creators are trying to make it immersive and somewhat realistic, but it just takes away from the gameplay for me, there really needs to be a settings to just turn it down! If you get shot while you're ADS, then your whole screens just throws it self miles away from the target and becomes very frustrating near the end.This "feature" doesn't need to be completely taken away, but just let us turn it down a bit.[The worst mission] That one forced stealth mission in every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game.. I really hate these types of "missions" It's not the games strong suit at all, so forcing people into a stealth mission for me personally is always bad.It pulls you out at the worst time as well, just as I was getting use to the gunplay and combat, it takes it all away from you.. really the only thing I think is game did that was a mistake.Overall I do really like this game a lot, most things here are nitpicks honestly.. expect for that one mission -_- It's a great game and is differently worth your money and time, also it has really easy achievements! I'm gonna personally try and complete the game fully :)

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of promise devolving into a terrible "finished" product. I bought the bright memory demo for $10 and received Infinite for free.I wanted to like this, but there is simply too much wrong with it. Admittedly, it is impressive that this game started off as a one man tech demo, it's a long shot from being good. I don't give partial credit for wasted potential or for being impressed one man created a demo which turned into a full game. ===The good=== - Impressive visuals- Multiple combat options other than shooting- Neat combat skills and upgradable skill tree- Special ammo for guns with diverse effects - Fixed the control issues of the demo- Optimized pretty nicely from the demo===The Bad===- The controls can still be a bit awkward particularly for Tier 2 skills. Example: For Tier 2  you have to press and hold LB (controller) while sprinting for the Tier 1  and after releasing the Tier 1 attack first then you have to press and hold LB a second time to charge the Tier 2 . In what universe does this make sense?- It's awkward when trying to switch between Tier 1 and Tier 2 skills in combat since you are pressing and holding the same damn button. - Tier 2 skills require too much charge time to be useful in the majority of combat situations. They're cool skills albeit useless in the heat of battle. They're only good to use when the number of enemies attacking is less than 3. - Maps and missions tend to be too linear- The platforming is terrible. A lot of the time it's not easy to decipher where you're supposed to go next and you're scanning the background as you look for faint white text for a contextual action. - Instead of progressively more difficult combat situations the A.I. just tends to mix different enemy types together and send them in waves. You will have the same combat situation, but just more waves of enemies. - The game just drops you in the middle of this lore rich universe without any baseline for understanding any of the lore. After clearing the game one time and starting a New Game+ there are still so many questions. Who are the SRO? How did Shelia get her Exoarm? Why does she belong to the SRO? Are they a group of good people are just another fascist organization seeking world domination? It doesn't matter how many times you play through, you won't get any answers. ===The Downright Ugly===- I don't have a single reason to care about any of the characters including the main protagonist, Shelia.- It's too mediocre of a generic Sci-Fi shooter- I want to know more about the lore, the game assumes you're already familiar with the basics of a larger overreaching story arc as if you have already read a book or a companion literature. - Even the combat skills offer little variation to what is a by the numbers FPS game and can be a one trick pony.- Zero replay value. I'm going to suffer through this mess multiple times for one or two more outfits and some weapon skins? Hard pass.- Some of the additional outfits and weapon skins are paid DLC. This game is nowhere near good enough to justify spending additional money on it. ===The most offensive flaw===- It will delete your New Game+ skill progression. At the end of each playthrough you're graded on your performance and the number of deaths counts towards your overall rating. I had started a New Game+ on a harder difficulty and very early on in my second playthrough I had gotten a BS death during one of the horrible platforming segments due to bad controls. I decided to start another New Game+ and it erased all of my skill progression from my completed playthrough. Nope, that's it, I'm done.F**K YOU FYQD STUDIO, F**K YOU CCP, and F**K YOU BRIGHT MEMORY.
