_childDocuments_.review: This game has lots of potential, emphasis on the word potential because while I enjoyed the whole of the experience there were a lot of factors that made it significantly less enjoyable than It would have been otherwise if they were addressed. For example: the game isn't optimized for mouse and keyboard, what do I mean by this? The control scheme, positioning and some of the combo routes require you to do press + hold inputs, hold some keys that are further than they should from each other or simply aren't well thought. I can see why it comes to this seeing as the game works much better on a controller, but for a shooter that was originally born with PC in mind I would like a revisit of the control scheme If possible.There's also some instances I didn't particularly enjoy: mostly the "press F to grapple" or the lackluster and constricted wallrunning sequences (please do add more of them and give us more freedom to do some parkour around, that would make this game even better than it already is) or the fact you can't cancel the slide animation into a jump, I don't like being locked in place while the animation finishes when Sheila is supposed to be a one woman army on an exo suit, it made her feel a lot less dexterous than her design visually communicates in cutscenes or when performing acrobatic feats on QTEs. I wish we could get a few more options in regard to movement, as the combat could really benefit from having a constant uninterrupted fast pace. Being able to shoot while wallrunning, having some extra skills for jumping on top of enemies as a way to reset your aerial momentum for example. Sky's the limit, the developer already did a great job setting the foundations and I think expanding and refining them would make this game concept a great service.Overall the combat and movement for me felt better while fighting against bosses or the ancient soldiers, I wish I could have styled on the SAI goons but the control scheme and some of the animations get in the way. I wish they did give me a bit more freedom to move around and turn those sequences into something that isn't your typical shooter campaign, especially in higher difficulties.However: I did finish this game in one sitting and it kept my attention through and through, If I noticed so many areas that need polish or stuff that could be better it's because I had a great time and most of my complaints could have killed my mood If the game itself wasn't this fun.  I'll probably replay it later on a controller since the game seems to be designed with it on mind.also Sheila is waifu, a red/blue coat skin would be dope.Dear Developer, If you read these reviews please keep making games like these and keep honing your craft, this was an awesome experience and I hope to see more in the future.

I kinda rushed and all that.I also listened to the audio language on English, Japanese, and Chinese, all of which was well done. I think Chinese Sheila is my favorite, especially since the game looks like it takes place in China. Chinese seems like the OG Language.The game was about 4 missions long, really 5$ per mission basically. (mightve been 5 missions).NEGATIVE: The lazy parts of the game are the shortness, the lack of Physics Knowledge, as there is a black hole that somehow hasnt sucked up all of earth into it.. and then you parachute down softly to the ground. That was one of a few Physics errors I found. There was a lack luster car level, where you get some hightech tesla looking car and it drives really slow... and you drive it in mud and water... makes no sense. There could've been more weapons and levels. Not to mention at the end, if you have not played the game before this one, OG Bright memory and its like.. 2 levels.. WHICH SHOULD'VE BEEN INCLUDED, the ending will make you scratch your head. Then, in unsatisfying fashion the game just takes the protag back to her apartment... and leave NO ENDING... there was no closure. Then there was a section of the game that the music loop would STOP for a sec or 2, and then start over, it was really annoying to listen to.POSITIVE: The graphics are really lovely, the models are nice and smooth, the female protag is modeled well, as well as the enemies and the vehicles and world in general. I loved the atmosphere and the weapon play with the sword and the power glove, the guns were nice, but I feel like the game shouldve given use fire-select, I hate Auto-Pistols and wouldve rather it been semi-auto. As well as the lack of a SMG, would've liked to see that, or some weapon mods, changing sights, adding attachments, etc... would've been nice. But the guns preform well enough, really nice, good balance.The movement is nice as well, it is all really well done in this aspect. Sound design is also really well done, aside from that one song I mentioned in the Negative. I really enjoyed the gun play, movement, the graphics and weather and the voice acting. Aside from the English, English voices from Asian characters make me cringe hard.I would recommend it, but not for anything more than 15$Even for 20$, I feel like it was a bit too short. I mean, 3-4 hours maybe, if you take your time...but really, if they added the OG Bright Memory to this game, it would be worth the 20$, not to mention some more missions that bring some Closure. What happens to the black hole? I guess it just vanishes, game doesnt tell you, what about the general? he dead? dont know, game doesnt have ANY closure. It just is the shortness and lack of closure that really annoys me and makes me say NO, do not buy it. There are better FPS games out there.*AND* if they added some more things to do, that would've been nice, like the idea about weapon attachments, and such... would be nice to customize Sheila a bit, change her hairstyle, hair color... besides 2$ Outfit changes, would be nice to see some more Free content in the game...

_childDocuments_.review: I played Bright Memory back in beta and called it the best game I'd played at the time. Bright Memory is a game so good it made me better at other games. The mechanics are amazing, graphics are gorgeous, titty physics are good (clearly a lot of time was devoted and I want to acknowledge that) - but mostly those smooth AF mechanics. But Bright Memory is a little fragment of a game. It's a demo. So, I was hella excited to play the full version when it finally appeared in my library.Bright Memory: Infinite is exactly the same thing with exactly the same problem. Beautiful, smooth, fun to play, but the whole thing lasts at most barely 3 hours if you die a lot (which I do). What I wanted from Bright Memory: Infinite was what was promised on the label - more. Infinite. I wanted more time to spend in this world with these mechanics and this cool aesthetic. But I honestly think Bright Memory: Infinite might be shorter than Bright Memory.The story changed some. I think - if i have this straight - Bright Memory was the work of one incredibly devoted dude. There were a lot more names in the credits of Bright Memory: Infinite than there were in Bright Memory. I don't know why we didn't get more when there were more people working on it. It is kinda interesting to see how that changes the dynamic.Still, it's a fun way to kill an afternoon and it has EXTREME replayability. Just kinda with there was more playability than replayability, if you get me. It's like they're saying "why do you want more? Just replay what you have?" and honestly, I would respect that if it were a full game. But it isn't. It's still a demo.But yeah, I recommend it. Definitely worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Unreal engine's tech demo. Short, stupid and boring linear first-person shooter. Its story, game mechanics and AI behaviour are of level of 1990's DOOMs. No kidding. Move in to new room, kill a dozen of bullet sponges, repeat. Even worse than 1990's DOOMs because that games allows player to provoke friendly fire and "loyalty cascade" between monsters. This game seems not to.Nevertheless I do recommend it. Why? Because this "game" clealry shows what clear and radiant graphics along with a decent performance is a composition of technologies that are built into GPU, frameworks (like .Net) and dozens of runtime libraries. You can see what even ad-hoc, underdeveloped and unoptimized levels still will look nice+ and give good frame per second ratio if game using at least somewhat modern hardware features. All in all, this "game" shows what if publisher of AAA title justifies price using nice screenshots then publisher of that AAA title blatantly lying to you. Play this and you will see. Good, not cheating AI and nonlinear story is what hard to develop. Good graphics with high FPS mostly is bought already with good GPU.

_childDocuments_.review: The mechanics and gameplay are great, Although there are some major bugs that on the day of release as I'm writing this, really piss me off.1. "F" button doesn't work at least 30% of the time. Picking up ammo, grappling hook, whatever the game wants me to press F for is constantly not doing working. Instead it fires the secondary ability. It happens so often it's super annoying. Even when the prompt on screen clearly says "Press F to pickup Ammo: or "press F to grapple" the game just fires the secondary ability. I don't mind it here and there, but like I said, literally 30% of the time it doesn't work and you're left sitting there spamming F and moving around until it finally works.2. Laser Glitch: Enemy snipers with lasers, when you turn your back to them, their lasers comes through walls and buildings. In intense firefights it's impossible to tell which lasers can actually shoot you and which are just glitching through walls. From what I've seen this happens in every place in the game with every lasered sniper enemy and is very annoying glitch. The lasers tracks your character through the walls and appear or disappear when you turn your back to where the enemy is.Overall still giving this game a thumbs up because it's still fun and the graphics are amazing, but it's definitely lacking the play testing and bug fixing to make it fully polished. When fundamental parts of the game don't work, like picking up ammo, it gets super annoying. Hopefully it gets fixed with a patch soon.

_childDocuments_.review: So.... this is a tough review for me to write. On one hand Bright Memory: Infinite (BMI) is a fun action/fps/hack and slash game with some really interesting mechanics and an art style that can at times be gorgeous. I really did enjoy my time with bright memory infinite and would recommend it to anyone that enjoys fast paced nuanced combat.BUT as a caveat this game is 2 hours long and I would probably recommend it at $9. _childDocuments_.review: I am very surprised how well-received this game is. Of course the combat is quite crisp with the quick movement, melee and ranged combos, dodging, double jumps, etc. Even boss fights were okay. But there are many downsides to the game as well:Extremely short - under 2 hours, with no real reason to repeat it unless you are a thirsty achievement-hunter wanting to grind to 100% completion. The achievements are really boring and are made in such a way that you will need to replay the game to grind out the kill requirements.The plot - there basically is none. Feels like the story was written by a 5 year old (or Michael Bay) trying to recreate an action movie. It makes no sense, everything is exploding and you must be ruuun!! Drink a short every time a random rock explosion happens and message me if you manage to survive the alcohol poisoning. No idea how they managed to cramp so much nonsense in such a short time.The dialogue and voice-acting - every time I here the protagonist's name, I want to die. SHEE-LEE-UH. The dialogue was definitely written by someone who wanted things to sound cool and military-like. But it was definitely not a native English-speaker. The enemies spawning in random locations that are visible to you - crazy. Many times enemies had spawned literally behind me, while I was in a corner. And I am talking about the military (human) enemies, not the otherworldly enemies.Boss fights - while they were definitely entertaining to some extent, their bullet-sponginess wasn't really fun. No weak-points, no phases, just keep on spraying and dodging!!Don't get me wrong. I got the game for free since I bought the 'demo' so this was definitely fun experience. But this review is for people who might be thinking of spending 17 euros on this. Really not worth it at that price point. The effects and ray-tracing are nice, but the game feels like a visual remaster of an old game with some touch-up. Or a short demo of what they could work on. If they brought in someone who actually knows how to write the plot. Besides the combat (and even that can be debated), there's nothing close to the AAA production people keep bringing up in the reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: This game brings up a lot of *theoretically* nice features and then ♥♥♥♥♥ the bed almost every time.1. Gunplay feels sleek, reloading looks fine and doesn't take too long, the guns generally feel powerful. Once you meet bosses though, it becomes a grindfest and you should hope that you scavenged enough ammo or you're confident in melee.2. Melee combat is fluid, feels powerful and can do interesting things. It requires some getting used to and thinking on the fly, which in and of itself is nice, were the thing you have to get used to not the totally insane keybindings that need you to start sprinting to charge certain attacks. Feels like a piss-poor controller port.3. The game gives you a lot of movement options - double jumping, running along walls and a grappling hook - which you then use to navigate extremely linear levels.4. Speaking of levels: the game looks beautiful but there are alpha walls everywhere and getting stuck is a common occurrence if you try exploring even in the slightest.5. And speaking of mechanics: the game throws a lot at you, way too much, senseless QTEs and a car for example. It features many different styles of combat, yet the achievements are uninspiring, grindy junk. Even the tech demo "Bright Memory" featured rather interesting achievements, what stopped this game from having a sword/skills only, a no damage or a timed achievement?In summary this is a fun game for the first playthrough and it gets worse the longer you look at it. I want to like it but as it stands I can't in good conscience recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's story-line is like a classic 80's Kung-Fu movie mixed with Mission Impossible. Surprisingly, it works out. It's a fun light-hearted adventure with really good gameplay mechanics and a large enough skill-tree for multiple play-throughs. You could do guns only (of which there are 4), sword abilities only, exo-suit abilities only, etc. The skill trees are pretty expansive too for a variety of move sets - it's not like you just hack and slash with a sword. Pros:+ Lots of varied gameplay (from sneaking, to vehicle combat, to sword fighting and guns plus more)+ Fluid combat+ Feels like a movie at times+ Lots of weapons and gameplay styles to choose from+ Fun story (albeit cheesy)+ Fun boss fightsCons:- Short - about 2 hours of gameplay per run- Limited enemy pool- Price - Interactive cut scenes (never liked them)Conclusion:I really enjoy the game. I only did one play through where I focused on melee sword combat and almost entirely ignored my exo-suit and guns. It will be a fun game to come back to when I want something somewhat chill to play but still challenging enough. The story made me laugh at times because of how outlandish some circumstances are.  Boss fights in the game are pretty enjoyable too and work well with the game's mechanics.The pros definitely out-weight the cons. There is limited content and that's reflected in the retail price. I suggest buying the game on sale (which is what I did); although looking back, I wouldn't have been disappointed if I bought the game at full price. It's a fun game that has basically every gaming mechanic you can think of - which is why I wish there was more. Since there are so many game mechanics, it can sometimes feel like you're playing a very cohesive demo. Luckily, there is a level-select so you can play whatever you want over again. Overall, it's a buy from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory: Infinite is not a sequel to Bright Memory but sort of a full version of that early tech-demo game we saw years prior. This game came free to anyone who bought the original Bright Memory but to everyone else this game cost $20.The strongest suit of Bright Memory: Infinite is the amazing visuals and the explosive combat, probably one of the best form of first-person shooter combat. Fast movements and satisfying gunplay on top of being able to swing around your sword gives me a mix feeling of Devil May Cry and Metal Gear: Revengence. This is insanely impressive, given how this game was developed by a single person. WIth the impressive use of ray-tracing, this game give us a glimpse on what future games are capable of.However, even with the impressive visuals, it is mostly due to the lighting and water effects. Otherwise, the in game models and even environmental textures aren't all that impressive. The game is also a tad buggy in some areas but nothing too game breaking. The biggest sin I encounter is the fact that the game is very inconsistent with performance. In some areas I was able to clock in about 120fps with ray-tracing at the highest setting where in some areas I would struggle to even stay above 30fps while turning down the ray-trace settings.The story is as nonsensical as it can get making Kingdom Hearts look straight forward so don't expect to go into this game to get a good story or understanding anything. The world is a mix of ancient-chinese, magic, and sci-fi so its cool enough as a presentation but thats about it. Voice acting is... there. Not really great but the protagonist gets a pass at least. I also wish the game just stuck with the already great combat system all the way through but there are two instances where instead of letting us enjoy the combat we were forced into a bad stealth-mission and a terrible driving mission. The game strongest's suit is the combat and such they should stick with it.Finally, the game is able to be completed in under 2 hours which is incredibly short, especially given the price tag. However, keep in mind that this is still developed by a single person who was able to give us a visual and adrenaline pumping treat. If you want a fast-pace action game this is great to play at least once, but I would recommend to get it on sale rather than paying the full 20 bucks for the game. The DLC costumes are completely unnecessary to buy as you won't even see your character often so unless you're that down-bad horny, just buy the base game when its on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory was an impressive tech demo that was in Steam Early Access a couple of years ago. It had a scantily clad female protagonist (which doesn't do anything for the game honestly) and a mix of sword and gunplay in the first person which felt fast-paced and punchy. Infinite is the fully released game, and it's basically a much longer tech demo. You can finish the game in 90 minutes and this leaves nothing for story or character development which is almost non-existent. All I gathered is that there's a black hole forming near-Earth and you must stop an evil military guy from taking some sort of artifact that will bring Earth back to Feudal Japan? I'm honestly not even sure.The best part about the game is the gunplay. The swordplay kind of takes a back seat and is only needed in certain situations. You get a standard arsenal of four weapons. Automatic pistol, auto-shotgun, assault rifle, and sniper rifle. Each weapon has an alternate ammo type that's usually explosive and does massive damage which is best saved for larger enemies and bosses. The weapons feel heavy and punchy, and they are fun to shoot and use. The gunplay was so good that it kept me wanting more from the game. It had a AAA budget quality to it that's not seen in many indie shooters. The swordplay consists of mashing a single button or launching enemies into the air. There's a tacked-on afterthought of a skill tree that lets you unlock abilities and upgrade your alternate ammo firepower, but in 90 minutes you upgrade almost everything pretty quickly so it feels trivial.There is a grapple line for traversing long distances which are scripted, and you can wall run. These ninja acrobatics feels a bit stiff and not as refined as the actual gunplay. In fact, all of the animations feel stiff and like they were hand done. The faces almost don't animate and thankfully there are less than 10 minutes of total screen time where the camera shows any faces. Your main character, Shelia, is questionable in the sexy department since you hardly ever see her and there are DLC costumes that seem pointless due to the short run time. You can go through the game again on higher difficulties, but I don't see the point.The issue with a short game like this is there is no incentive to come back. There are no modes, no multiplayer, and hardly anything to aim for. The visuals in the game are fantastic with great use of ray-tracing, but again the animations are weird. There's a short scene where you drive a car and it feels really janky and half-baked. Overall, the boss fights are fun, but there are literally only four types of enemies in the whole game so it gets repetitive quickly. At a sale price, this could be a fun evening, but that's about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite not recommending it, I like this game.There are a lot of good ideas.However :- To me, there are too many abilities. I didn't end up using half of what I had unlocked, which is kind of sad because they all are cool, but some needing to charge up a lot really breaks the momentum.- There are a lot of bugs. Now, this game was made by a very tiny team, so that's to keep in mind. A lot of the melee enemies have a much longer reach than what the animation may lead you to believe, for example.- Platforming is clunky. Shelia sort of "snaps" to ledges, the wall jumps are hard to pull off, and jumps feel weird.- It's very short. I cleared it in three hours on "hell" difficulty.- Some scenes made so little sense I actually burst out laughing. Fighting on the wing of a flying plane, for example.- Optimisation issues at times. The game runs smooth as butter most of the time, but sometimes the framerate just drops to the pits of hell down to less than 10, for several seconds. Usually you die if that happens because a lot of inputs are dropped.Now for the good parts :- The moment to moment gameplay is very solid: the combat is pretty cool, abilities and weapons are diverse enough to provide options and really mow enemies down once you get the hang of it.- Graphics. This game has really beautiful, albeit repetitive, environments.- Bossfights. They have cool concepts and are decently hard (before you understand how to cheese them).I received this game for free since I bought the "demo" that had first came out. I'm not sure I enjoyed the full game more, sadly.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first half on Steam Deck and the second half with a proper mouse and keyboard. The plot, and stealth section, give off heavy  vibes but in the superior FPS format. The guns are straight , very punchy, and satisfying to use. The movement mechanics are spiced with , including dodging, melee blocking/attacking, executions (although these are more scripted), and something that is basically a lasso to yank enemies toward you as well as being able to yeet foes into the air. All feels very solid, though I do wish the dodging was a little more refined. You can't  dodge while sprinting, only after stopping your run and pressing the button again. Honestly I think they would have been better off just making sprint the default speed rather than a dedicated sprint button, and allow forward dodge so as to act like a dash. I think that would have made things flow a little better in the combat arenas. The setting and sword play feel very  and it all mixes together to form a very fast paced and exciting, though sadly brief, campaign.A couple of minor bugs and a crash during a loading screen were experienced, but this only occurred on when playing on the deck and it was nothing unforgivable. Oh and the vehicle part was just kind of annoying, I would have preferred just more of the fighting over that. The combat mechanics are good enough that you don't want a break. However, it's only one small part. Aside from those minor gripes, this game exceeded expectations. The boss battles are frequent and epic.The tiny size of the team makes it all the more impressive. It might be very short, but it's still a AAA experience. For the price tag, definitely worth it. I just want more levels, hitting the end of the campaign leaves you hungry for more.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a positive review but it comes with a lot of caveats. It's a short game that focuses a lot on visuals, and this comes at a cost of substance. I normally would give this a negative review, but the game is a passion project developed largely by one person and so I give it a pass. I still think that the pricetag is a bit high personally and I would wait for a sale.Overall the game is a fun experience, but there's a bunch of nitpicks I have gripes about that lessen the overall gameplay feel. Things like the controls being unintuitive on M&KB, it's very clumsy to have so many attacks mapped all over your left hand, between exo suit, sword, etc. There isn't a large difference between using exosuit skills vs sword skills, the inputs are similar and the effects are similar (stagger/suspend). So there isn't really a meaningful difference in using many skills between the two. There's no input buffer when transitioning from a melee slash to blocking, which feels really bad. Enemy hitboxes are large, imprecise, and bulky, making for precision maneuvers around the arena kind of bad. The overall mobility you get from dashing backwards vs sprinting forwards is weird for game balance because you can get way more speed going backwards than forwards which doesn't make a lot of sense. Overall you can tell the dev was more focused on a pretty experience than an experience that plays well. But for a solo project I have to give kudos where it is deserved.

_childDocuments_.review: If you didn't know, this game had a lot of controversy around it a few years back. I was genuinely surprised that the developers stuck to their word and gave those who bought Bright Memory (which came out before Bright Memory Infinite as what was essentially a tech demo) the full copy of this game. That being said...it just feels to have been left in the oven too long. After waiting for as long as we have, I didn't expect the game to be just...a generic shooter with slapped on "combat mechanics". The graphics are admittedly great, and once you remove the Frame lock, it's astounding to look at. The gameplay, though, has just not aged well. It's an incredibly generic level by level shooter where you kind of just walk to one area after another shooting everyone. Bullets work better than any of the initial mechanics introduced, and the constant tutorials are just annoying. The fights are all boring and short followed by clunky and unnecessary terrain traversal. They have a wallrun that only works where you MUST wall run, and a grapple hook that only exists when necessary. Honestly, part of my salt comes from this. I couldn't beat the second level because the grapple hook was broken by my FOV. I couldn't get past an area filled with electric, insta-gibbing water because my FOV prevented the grapple hook from ever being in range on the last jump. When I tried to hop across some enemy boats that were in the river, guess what? I noclipped through them and died! I went through the same boring fights 5 times only to die 5 times trying everything my power as a player to make that grapple work. When I lowered my FOV back to default, it instantly worked without falter. I didn't get far into the game, and it's genuinely a bit unfair to review it so early on, but even this brief play gave way to all I personally needed to know. I wouldn't play this unless I had absolutely nothing else that I wanted to play. This feels more generic and streamlined than most CoD games campaigns, and that's really not what I expected from this type of game. The melee combat is clunkier than I remember from the demo, and you're punished more than anything when even trying to do more than just shoot those that are shooting you. The combat instances are all short and confined to small areas that just make for a bland experience. The cutscenes aren't even worth while because they're using antiquated QTEs to make them "interesting". As soon as you start up the game, you're greeted by 4 Quick Time Events before even firing a single bullet. For how long we waited, the game just doesn't feel like more than your average 10$ shooter made in the Unreal Engine by an indie studio. It certainly doesn't feel like something that has been worked on for years and costs 20$. This game isn't fundamentally broken, but it's just boring. It's fine to play if there is NOTHING ELSE at all that you want to do with your time, but it brings truly nothing to a table of shooters that already has some decent titles on it. All in all...it's just a generic shooter with pretty graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory: Infinite is a mindless popcorn flick in video game form that lets you switch off your brain and enjoy the show. It’s fast-paced and beautiful, but also woefully light on content: there’s a distinct lack of enemy/boss variety, the campaign is both linear and only a little over two hours long, and there’s pretty much no storyline to speak of. Long story short, the game runs out of ideas pretty fast. I lament its regrettably short length, but at the same time, if it was any longer, it might’ve become too much of a chore to play; this way, at least it ended before it could become overly repetitive. I'm giving it a thumbs up because I did have a decent amount of fun with the campaign, but be warned that if you’re looking for a meaty, fleshed-out FPS experience with tons of content and variety, this might not be the game for you.For more honest indie game reviews, check out our Curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: Short game with nice graphics, the combat is really good, the levels are not too complex.All the levels are set in the same location and it's always raining and windy, would have been nice to see some different locations to mix things up. The end boss has a habit of trapping you in a corner which can be annoying.TAA is the only AA available and you cannot turn it off.Played on 1660TI, RYZEN 5 4600H, 16GB RAM and there were performance issues, the biggest culprit was "Particle Lighting"  I had the game locked to 70fps the game would drop to as low as 53fps during cut-scenes and when using the charged up fire punch, turning Particle lighting off the fps stayed around 60fps for the most (also when using the fire punch) part but did drop below 60fps in other places.My only guess is the game needs more optimising here and there but especially with the particle lighting, the game supports ray-tracing so it seems not too much optimisation went into the stand alone particle lighting as RTX cards will take care of it, if you don't have one well turn off the particle lighting (at least with a 1660 TI laptop).Note: There is also no low,med or high setting for the particle lighting setting, it,s just on or off.UPDATE: Turning the Reflex setting to on and enhance gave a slight boost (extra 5fps) with Particle lighting on.I will test the game out with my GTX 1080 TI and see how it performs on that setup.UPDATE 2: GTX 1080 TI maxed outLowest fps: 83 (two parts)Stays above 100+fps for the most partHighest fps: 240The following Paragraph was removed from this review by Steam, my only conclusion is that the developer might not have been happy with it, not sure why as it's helpful information for both the developer and the player."However the game has an issue loading in assets which causes notable drop in fps when loading, this is not as noticeable with VSYNC off with the 1080 TI but it is with the GTX 1660 TI (GTX 1660 TI laptop has M2 drive), 1080 TI build HDD, so obviously an optimization issue."Conclusion:The game is short but also fun despite the performance issues, I would recommend getting it in a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game combines gunplay with swordfighting all in a first person perspective and it works to make it into a really cool and fun action game. You get 4 firearms throughout the game, starting with an assault rifle and subsequently unlocking a shotgun, an auto-pistol and a sniper rifle. These guns have two fire modes with the second being a special kind with some kind of effect. This is really useful when you have multiple of the larger health pool enemies or the bosses you face during the game. The sword is used not only to slash at enemies but also to block their melee attacks and even their shots. You also have a skill arm, you could say. It's an arm that can pull enemies, fire off an EMP (it's more like a shockwave that freezes the enemies in air, but it's called EMP in game). The game revolves around combining the use of these three systems and you can get some sick combos with them. There is depth to the combat and that makes it really fun.The story is basically non-important for the game. It exists, it's there but I personally didn't find it engaging. It also suffers from some voice acting being a bit stiff, and the same can be said for the facial animations and some third person animations. What can be a sore point is the length of the game though. The game has 4 difficulty levels, with only 3 of them being available before beating the game. I played on the hardest difficulty that I could choose and I beat it in just short of 2 hours. It does have new game plus functionality and, as mentioned before, an unlockable difficulty and combined with the really fun gameplay means it's absolutely replayable.

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that this whole thing was made by one dude still boggles the mind. Bright Memory Infinite is a phenomenon amongst indie games.Pros:1) The combat mechanics are an absolute blast.2) The graphics are downright gorgeous and are right up there with AAA games.3) RTX implementation is solid.Cons:1) The story is...there? It honestly seems a little random and never really gets too deep.2) There are a couple of janky bits in the game that were clearly added in just for a short sequences to provide variety, but never really polished.3) Picking up ammo is manual, but I feel a game like this should have had auto-pickup to add to the flow of combat.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5/10From my understanding this game was made by a very small team, and for what it is the game is pretty solid. The biggest reason I didn't rate this game higher is honestly just the missed potential of the mechanics and how short the game is.Gameplay - Pretty solid as far as gunplay goes, and the secondary features of the weapons are useful and make them all feel really powerful. The swordplay and abilities however almost seem like an afterthought. Many of the abilities just straight up don't work on anything larger than the normal human sized trash mobs. Of the ones that do, some have very long charge up times that just make them impractical to actually use. The time spent trying to use them would be better off just unloading bullets into somethings face. The sword itself isn't so bad when used to parry attacks and follow up with simple sword strikes and maybe a few rounds from a guns powerful special ammo.Sound - The music feels atmospheric, but honestly I doubt I'd ever really remember much of it. The sound of the guns and combat in general feels pretty good.Graphics - The graphics look nice but aren't anything cutting edge, and the scenery is fairly pretty. The animations can be a bit wonky sometimes.Story - This is where the game takes the biggest hit. This game is short, very short. I spent a lot of time looking around for hidden pickups and the such and still managed to complete the game in about 3 hours. As for story? There isn't much of one. No context is given for anything, the characters involved are basically all throwaways who don't really matter. All you know is there is a black hole that suddenly appears, and it's your job to stop it (wtf, how?). Random antagonist general shows up at some point with no context, and is your typical herp derp erma rulz da worldz villian.All in all the gameplay is solid, but could really stand to have a lot more development time to put together a better story and make a longer more immersive experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very solid, but short game with A gameplay loop that's genuinely enjoyable, being able to facilitate many gameplay styles, but is ultimately rather shallow. It also has some amazing tech behind it. It's very optimized and I commend the dev for putting it all together the way that it is.It's very graphically advanced, but it's also dense, which could interfere with gameplay. It's kinda nice seeing someone shooting through a cherry tree's leaves to kill a bad guy but actually doing it is kinda frustrating, and that's on top of the screen shaking that can't be disabled.I say this in regards to both its gameplay and story, but neither of which are worse off for it, to be honest.Gameplay wise, enemies have simple, understandable behaviors and attack patterns, easily affording you the ability to fight and counter them in single combat, and challenging you in different ways when encountering groups of enemies. However, taking them out using the usual methods of attack, guns and melee, although affording you the ability to choose between the two, makes fighting groups, especially those of bullet sponges, to be rather static because of how defensive you'd need to be. However, the abundance of bullet sponges in this game allows you to damage-dump them in creative ways, and the game really does have a lot of options in regards to how you want to murder them, which I think is the point.Narratively, it's just an unabashed mess, through and through, but it takes its nonsense and rolls with it, not expecting you to keep up with it at the slightest. It really comes off like it's a thin veil so that there's an explanation as to why things are happening, and i'm okay with it.I've beaten the game and I don't know anything about the protagonist other than that she's a government agent (I think) with cybernetic enhancements. I also don't know why she only picks up specific weapons off of tables to add to her arsenal, and I also do not understand why she has an extended arsenal of cybernetic enhancements that are simply blocked off from her until she decides to pick up enough jade artifacts to care enough about them to use them. There's also this faction that gets introduced that just gets glossed over for no apparent reason, and there's also this main antagonist type guy who Is just sort of there, and then just starts a "Rivalry" of sorts with the main character just to get her to fight him? This whole game's story is weird and it doesn't make sense and it doesn't expect you to make sense of it so i'm not holding it against it in the slightest.It's a good game that focuses on being a good game, and does well at being good in other regards too. Buy this if you got some money to blow.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review that needs a middle option. It's good - for a demo.Bright Memory: Infinite is a first person shooter made primarily by one person. However, the entire game is only 2.5 hours long, and feels more like a well made tech demo. Some very good ideas that just needed to be fleshed out a little more. I got the game for free from buying the original Bright Memory for less than $10, but it still feels like both Bright Memory, and Bright Memory: Infinite are merely well made demos. I'm hoping FYQD can capitalize on the foundation he laid, to give us a well made, fleshed out, full length experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I hadn't realized there were two games, so I haven't played the first game yet. Because of that I won't review the story. I bought the Ultimate edit, but the DLC is just the standard cosmetic outfits and skins that you see on a lot of Chinese/Japanese games. Nothing really worth reviewing.Pros:1) Combat is very fun. It has a similar feel to Doom, but still pretty different. Ammo packs are placed throughout the levels, and it's more than enough for you to fight (aside from the special ammo, which as expected is a bit more scarce). You have no armor (enemies do), but your health regenerates. There is a pretty standard mix of enemy types: a few different heavies, a sniper, a basic soldier (basically fodder), etc. However, not too many attack you at once. Just enough to make an average player sweat a little on the higher difficulties. Combat is focused on dodging and countering. You can block/reflect standard attacks, but be careful with elemental attacks.2) Soundtrack was pretty good.3) It has a skill upgrade system with some pretty fun skills to learn. However you can't upgrade things like basic health or damage values. Only things directly related to the skills.Cons:1) It has a stealth level that doesn't fit with the rest of the game, and the story reason why it happened doesn't make sense to me.2) It has a driving section, which you can see from the trailer. It's very clunky, but it's only a few minutes. However, be careful after destroying the third car. The fourth and fifth cars glitched for me and they got stuck together. I then ended up glitching through them while also being slowed to a crawl. And all this time they kept shooting me as I couldn't do anything but crawl forward.3) The game was very short. I  took my time finding collectibles and I still beat the campaign in under 3 hours.In conclusion, I think the game is a fun way to spend a few hours. If this was a $60 game I would be mad, but for $20 (I got it on sale for $16) it's not bad. Especially since this is a small developer. I might replay it again sometime on the highest difficulty now that it's unlocked.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to give this a slightly positive, or even a neutral, but since Steam's voting system is black or white, I think it would be much better to give it a negative because of the issues I have with it. The main summary of why it's a negative is because it's trying to be too many things. It's really trying to be a mini Devil May Cry, Doom Eternal and CoD all at the same time.1. The combat is a bit all over the place. While the skills/sword implementation is cool, it really doesn't mesh as well as it could with the game play. And the main reason is because of the reloading mechanic. If you start shooting then combo using your power/sword, after your energy (used by sword/powers) runs out, you can't combo back with your gun, because it cannot reload during power/sword usage. The game would have been much better if it just didn't bother with reload or ammo, and also used some kind of energy mechanic per weapon to force you to use all of the guns, as well as have them combo much better with the melee/power gameplay.2. Weird mishmash of genres. It feels an overly ambitious execution. You have a driving section (that's only used once), which is also a little clunky, and a stealth section (also used once). The driving part is pretty bad, but straight forward, while the stealth is completely out of place. Imagine playing Doom Eternal and suddenly being forced into a stealth section. Not to mention, the weapon you use during the stealth section (a meat cleaver), also blocks most of the centre of your screen, making it hard to see. How this got past initial play test is beyond me.3. Length. The game is also really short and with no replayability I would say. Wouldn't mind getting it on a discount, but full price is pushing it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a NEUTRAL Review, and here's why:Rating*: 15+Controls: DS4Windows required for DS4 ControllersBugs: A few were encounteredOK, so I'll dive right in with; It's an OK Game, but it has issues. The Final Boss Fight got to be boring, and rather Annoying, with the Insufficient Ammo situation. Basically, this will Destroy your Controller during said Boss Fight. The ending pops up with a rather insulting judgement of your Stats, just based on having died a dozen or so times. The Final Boss Battle is where I got killed the most, for lack of enough Ammo to do the job.The Controls can't be changed, which kind of messes with the whole experience. It uses R3 for Crouch, and there is no Prone. It uses L_D-PAD and R_D-PAD for Weapon Swap, which means that you need to grow a third hand to play properly. Then you have the issue of, you can't Evade-Dash forwards, only backwards. This means that you can't Evade out of a corner that you've been backed into.There is no Map Display for the sake of situation awareness, and it's all first-person, so you can't see what's around you anyway.The Game is 'OK' but it's very linear and short. If it wasn't for the 'Spending 2 Hours fighting the Final Boss' and other situations similar to that, I would have completed it a lot quicker.OK, bugs list; Getting stuck on Invisible Stuff, Controls colliding with each other and thus reducing what you have available, and then a sprinkle of Graphics Bugs. I won't say that the Game is Buggy, but I won't say that it's perfect either. One of the issues I found means that one of the Steam Achievements can't be acquired, but it's hard to describe what that issue is, or even confirm if it's due to a Bug or just missing Code.If it's on offer, then it might be worth looking at, but at full price, find something else.* Ratings: I've Rated this Game 15+. Contain mature Content, and one of the DLC's is also orientated to a Mature Audience. There is also some Graphic Detailed Melee Attacks, and Heads do explode with Headshot's.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Bright Memory (I guess the demo?) a year or so ago and loved it. It was a great mix of fast paced action hack and slash and FPS combat. This... feels worse. It LOOKS amazing. But it handles poorly despite having gotten it for free because I paid for the demo. The Good- As stated the visuals are stunning. The environments are great, enemies look cool, the weapons are detailed.- The combat is usually very fluid, and the your exo arm and light sword abilities are fun to use even if some are rather broken overpowered. The Bad (list is a bit longer)- This game is just not optimised well. My computer specs are well above the recommended settings and come mission 2, the game slowed to a CRAWL of 5 frames per second regularly. Pausing the game didn't do anything, dropping all settings down to the lowest didn't do anything. Know what fixed it? Death. I'm not kidding, dying would fix the frame rate issues... until they started up again that is.- Mission 2 begins with a half baked stealth segment. It really was not needed. This is a fast paced hack and slash FPS. So let's throw in a very slow, boring, and easy stealth section right in the start of level 1 because... well I don't know the reason honestly but it sucked.- Immersion breaking. The constant reminder of where my objective are, mission updates, the commander talking to the player character as if she's totally inept at figuring anything out herself. It all just rips me out of the game world.- The second boss the Giant King... oh boy. At first I never thought I'd beat him. Why? Well come phase 2, my game would drop to 5 frames per second. Okay well I know the solution, just die. Nope. Didn't fix anything. I would respawn with 5 frames per second and not be able to do anything. HOWEVER the update as of the day I post this review fixed this. So why is this still here? Because once I beat the boss (first try once the FPS didn't tank on Revenge difficulty I might add) the game crashed. I loaded it back up 3 more times. 3 more times it crashed when I won. Fitting that a boss who's entire difficulty is composed of spamming trash mobs at you when he's near death, it utter trash himself.- I've heard the game is only 2 hours long. Well I've only actually PLAYED about an hour. My other hour and a half were constantly dealing with crashes and frame drops so if I've seen half the game... I don't really want to see the other half.- The difficulty is a little unbalanced. I can drop some enemies in 2 bullets on Revenge difficulty and they can barely scratch me, then one guy comes along that takes 10 mags and a bunch of my sword and parrying, who can kill me in 3 hits. Huh. Okay well is he a boss? Nope, the bosses are nowhere near that level of difficulty. The bosses, well the 2 I faced anyways, were just slightly harder than the regular trash mob soldiers.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved Bright Memory (BM), I loved Infinite (BMI) less. BM was simple, really enjoyable, it was about platforming with or without -relatively easy- puzzles with clear fight sequences and the occasional moments of "rest". Even on higher difficulties the fights and bosses felt not much more bullet sponges but reliant on strategy you learnt previously. However, sadly, BMI tried to take it a step further but all it ended up being was a still quite really good linear platformer devoid of puzzles and filled with nonstop enemies with a forced stealth section with bad stealth AI and a car sequence that's barely ok, with bosses being a bit too bullet sponge-y on highest difficulties to my taste. Even then, if BM was a solid 4/5, BMI is a soft 4/5 at best and a hard 3/5 at worse. One of its core strength (like BM) is that . First, do a regular "just looking at the story" easy/normal mode while getting used to the controls and gameplay, then go in again on Hard to unlock "Hell" difficulty, and then go in again on Hell and the game just keeps getting better and better each time. I even started  (my 3rd and last playthrough) by  and it  trying to figure out all the possible weaknesses of each enemy and that one is ; I even made it to the last chapter without any upgrades and kept all my ~30 "skill points" unused till halfway through the last chapter (still then only upgraded all secondary bullet type damages and EMP+Sword Slash because I expected the last boss to be the worst bullet sponge which it was so much that I ran out of every ammo and had to finish with sword long-distance slash but that's all I needed really and none of the extra skills).For 16.79 €, at ~2-3 hours per playthrough with at least 3 playthroughs like I described, totally worth it. Do not waste your money if you are going to play it once and forget about it, wait for it to drop under 10€ for that, this game needs to be played at least twice IMO. That's what I think makes it worth the money. The second playthrough is the real playthrough, take the first one as a tutorial.

_childDocuments_.review: Considering this was made by one guy, this is a great indie game. They definitely put a lot of time into the graphics and it really shows. However, I am not a person who cares too much about graphics, I always put gameplay first. So, how IS the gameplay?Firstly, this is a hack-n-slash and fps/3ps game. The the shooting does feel really good. Taking cover behind objects always felt effective. Enemies were fun to fight, and punishing when you tried to go doom guy on them. The weapon selection is pretty nice too. You've got a basic rifle, which has the most ammo and will most likely be your main weapon. Then there's the shotgun. I have to applaud the creator for making shotguns feel useful at multiple ranges, not just point blank. There is also a sniper, which is just that. Then there is the pistol. I didn't use it a whole lot, but it was interesting. And, it has a mini rocket launcher mounted to it. The 3rd person mechanics felt a bit more janky, but still fun to play. Being a person who prefers third person shooters, I felt satisfied. Now, how's the hack n slash stuff. It's okay in a good way. The blade combat definitely feels a bit stiff, but it can be fun too. I also do not have a lot of first person HnS experience, so I cannot comment well on this aspect of the game. I can say that it was fun. I did think that the parry system was a bit odd too, as it seemed to not work half of the time. Next up, how do the enemies fit into the gameplay? They were pretty good. My least favorite experience was, unfortunately, the bosses. Boss design is a hard thing to get right. But, the dev fell into the classic boss trap of making them "harder" by adding in adds. The bosses had very simple movesets and were easy to run away from and plink at with your guns (wish I had those for elden beast). So, to combat this, I assume the dev added in enemies to keep the challenge present. However, this did not increase challenge as it increased annoyance. The grunts were easy enough to dispatch before going back to the plinking. I'll go into this later, but the movement did not help with this either. The normal and special enemies were pretty good too. My least favorite being the shield soldiers. They follow the ever hated mechanic where a shield means a shield for every body part, even exposed limbs. So, they were never fun to encounter. Luckily, they don't show up too often. The other specials provided fun challenges in discovering the best ways to take them out while managing the basic guys.Generally, the grunt enemies were good, and the bosses were lacking.As for the movement, eh it's serviceable. This was the least fun aspect of the game. It functions and doesn't hinder the gameplay, but is still the most under polished thing here. The "traversal" segments are pretty iffy, and I accumulated most of my deaths from the 2 required jumps (maybe 3?) in the campaign. The grapple is only used in scripted sections, but could've been fun for combat. The "dodge" mechanic has no i-frames, so you better plan ahead for attacks. The running is also fine, but bosses are just so huge and have large swings that running ain't enough. The double jump also feels weird. Keep in mind, I love titanfall 2, so you can see where my comparisons lie. Even so, there is much to be desired with the movement systems in play. For any future updates or releases, I'd say add some i-frames to make boss encounters a bit more interesting, and work on the movement system to make it more crisp. The music is pretty good too. I do love this style of music. It did feel a bit repetitive at times though, but it didn't hamper the experience.The narrative however, is nonexistent. It kinda acts like you, the viewer, are being dropped into an active story and learning stuff along the way, but it goes nowhere. Then, suddenly, the game ends and the threat (which you still never learn much about) is suddenly gone. And the villain which was teased earlier, gets an elbow to the back before you learn much about him either. This game definitely places no importance on the story, it's just there to give some sort of purpose to gunning down soldiers and mystic warriors.Overall, the game is alright. I had fun with it, and the dev should be proud of what they made. However, it is sooooo short. I have just under 5 hours in the game, but that is from fiddling with mechanics, skins, and just farting around. My end time for my first playthrough came under 2 hours. For 20 buckaroos that is too short. I'd say, in terms of value for your purchase, get this on a discount like I did. However, if you wanna support this dev, then feel free to drop the extra 10. Generally, it was a fun game who's flaws did not harm the experience (apart from the bosses). This dev clearly has talent, and I think they can be even better with a future game. All I ask is for a longer campaign (which'd mean a more fleshed out narrative), improving the melee combat, and touching up the movement system to have i-frames and/or titanfall-esque traversal (not wall running, just the fluidity of it).Edit 1: I forgot to talk about performance. It ran so well I forgot to talk about it lol. I am currently on a basic tower with a 1050, and I could run this thing fluidly, 100 something fps, zero crashes, and on pretty good settings. No ray tracing of course. But, as I said earlier, graphics aren't a huge concern of mine. This was really well optimized, kudos again to the creator.Edit 2: My apologies, I keep forgetting stuff. The game also suffers from no post game content. Such content being something akin to a survival mode (like cod zombies) or a replayable mode like mercenaries/raid from the RE games. That was a major factor in reviewing the price. I hope the dev ads some form of replayable content in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I think Bright Memory is really impressive for a game that was developed by one person. On the harder difficulty, I clocked in just under 3 hours.Unfortunately, the story is pretty shallow and you're not really invested in the characters or what is happening.While I do think this game has some highlights, I can't recommend it at full price. _childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome, and I can't speak highly enough about it. The gunplay is polished to an extreme (think Titanfall 2 combat - but better), and each of the weapons can feel like a cheat code if used properly. The movement is buttery smooth - so much so that I actually felt like I was running around like some genetically-enhanced super soldier. There are a lot of games with similar mechanics (wallrunning, double jumps, crouch slides, etc.), but none feel quite as good as this. Finally, the crowning achievement in this gem of a game is the visuals. My god does this game look incredible. Knowing that this is a small developer, it is truly an amazing accomplishment what is pulled off here. Every part of the game looks like it was ripped from a tech demo for a new high-end graphics card - but this ♥♥♥♥ is actually playable! My only complaints are the length of the game, and the forced stealth and driving components. Ironically enough, the former mostly excuses the latter, seeing as the two segments I didn't like took me maybe 15 minutes to complete, but it is a shame that they were included in a game that took just over 2 hours to clear. This short length is excusable because the other aspects are kick-ass, but it is a bit of a let down because the original Bright Memory was already a short experience - one that was billed as a sort of demo for this installment. With this in mind, it does suck that we got yet another demo-length entry, but the low cost helps that pill get swallowed. Ultimately, Bright Memory: Infinite is a worthwhile purchase, and a ton of fun to play, but it is disappointingly short. Hopefully future installments are full length features rather than lengthy demos.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is INSANE. In every sense of the word, really. It's SO much fun. I got Bright Memory: Infinite for free because I owned the first Bright Memory on Steam when this one launched, so I basically got more content for no extra cost - therefore, absolutely worth playing. But as good as this game is, I don't think it's worth its full price for less than 2 hours of playtime. Definitely worth getting during a sale, though, and I hope the developer continues this series, because what we've got here is truly unique!All my praise goes to the gameplay, graphics and environments, though. Those are the best parts of the game. The rest of it is a complete mess. The story doesn't make any sense, it's told in an awful and confusing way, and tons of things are never explained at all. It doesn't really matter, though. Just jump in, slash and shoot some bad guys and have fun. Pretty cool setpieces too. The weird "waifu" stuff is... pretty weird though. _childDocuments_.review: I know it says .1 hrs on record, but I played this entirely offline while deployed so I have actually played through the campaign multiple times on all difficulties.TL;DR: It's a fun couple hours to kill with the exception of a god-awful "stealth" section shoehorned about halfway through. Recommend you pick it up on sale if you decide to at all.Keeping it short, there's not a whole lot here. It'll take you about 2.5 hours *maybe* to get through the main campaign and that is with the few cheap difficulty spikes here and there. The game does a fantastic job as a tech demo, especially with environments and modeling. Some improvements can be made for facial animations but this team is extremely small, being able to get a game look like a AAA title with an indie team is a feat in and of itself.Gameplay is a mesh of FPS and hack n slash that is executed pretty well. You have 5 total weapons: assault rifle, shotgun, sniper rifle, handgun, and sword. All the weapons are fun to use and have interesting secondary fire effects that are all useful in the end. What would make the gameplay better is more verticality and mobility options because it seems like that's what they're going for here. Aside from the main weapons you have the exo-arm  that has its own abilities in combat ranging from an EMP stun to a massive fireball that destroys any close enemies. The initial controls are a bit awkward, I bound the defend and melee attack keys to the thumb buttons on my mouse and didn't have issues from there. Aside from that the controls are fairly standard and not very difficult to work with.

_childDocuments_.review: is a first-person shooter (FPS) that stands out for its high-quality graphics and detailed textures, thanks to the Unreal Engine 4. This game engine is renowned for its ability to produce photorealistic visuals and smooth performance, which are fully on display in this title.The game features a minimalist and clean user interface (UI), with options to hide certain elements to increase immersion. This UI design, combined with an excellent lighting system and an adjustable field of view (FOV) up to 100, provides a visually impactful and immersive experience. The aesthetic is reminiscent of , but with its own futuristic theme. offers fast-paced FPS gameplay, blending quick and precise gunplay with melee combat using swords and special abilities. This dynamic and fluid gameplay focuses on action and intensity, sometimes at the expense of narrative depth. The frenetic combat showcases the potential of modern development tools, especially when wielded by talented developers. Notably, a significant portion of the game’s development was carried out by a single individual, Zeng "FYQD" Xiancheng, making the achievement even more impressive.The combat in  is both dynamic and fluid, requiring players to switch seamlessly between shooting and melee attacks. The advanced animations contribute to the sense of fluidity and realism during combat, enhancing the overall gaming experience.The game's duration is relatively short, typical for intense action titles. On the easiest difficulty, many players can complete the game in about 1 hour and 40 minutes. On higher difficulties, especially when players have unlocked various skills and weapons, the campaign can be completed in approximately 1 hour and 19 minutes. The higher difficulty levels offer a more significant challenge and can extend gameplay time, providing a more engaging and demanding experience.During my first playthrough, I encountered several bugs that affected the overall experience. One specific bug caused me to fall through the map when performing a combo, forcing a restart at the last checkpoint. Additionally, there was a recurring issue where I couldn't switch weapons or pick up ammunition and relics, which required me to either finish the level, return to a checkpoint, or die to resolve the problem. These bugs occurred 4 to 5 times during the nearly 2-hour campaign, which was somewhat irritating. Although these issues are easily fixable with an update, a patch is not yet available to address them.The game offers wall running and wall jumping mechanics similar to those in , but these features are underutilized and can only be employed in specific situations, limiting their overall impact on gameplay.The game was showcased at E3 2019, where its trailer highlighted the advanced graphics and intense gameplay. While some areas, maps, or enemies shown may have been altered or refined in the final version, the presentation was a faithful indicator of the game's visual quality and design.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start by giving a big disclaimer: this game is short. And I mean very short. I don't think that's a bad thing, but if you're going into this expecting a AAA story spanning multiple hours, you'll be disappointed. That being said, I think Bright Memory: Infinite is a very fun game. The gameplay is actually really good for such a short game. It's incredibly chaotic and hacky/slashy, and it's really a blast to play through. I genuinely enjoyed the combat in the game, even if it was infuriating at times. I think where the game falls short is when it comes to the platforming and stealth sections. Even though you're given a double jump, it's more of a small thrust that doesn't really carry your momentum too well, so you'll find yourself falling short of a few jumps, especially at the end. The stealth sections just feel out of place. It feels super weird to go from chaotically slashing and shooting your way out to suddenly having to sneak around and hiding from enemies. Outside of that, I think there is a very strong future for Bright Memory. The game is visually stunning and it's clear that the studio has a direction for the story. I highly encourage anyone to at least try the game, and experience it for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory: Infinite is a fun, good looking, fast paced FPS with your basic classic weapons: Automatic rifle, semi-auto shotgun, automatic pistol and a sniper rifle. That's it. All of the weapons have a secondary function which you can upgrade for extra gibbing and then a sword and some spectacular superpowers that you can also upgrade as you progress. It lasts only 2 hours, it's very linear and the story makes no sense. It is fun to play, mechanics are smooth once you get the hang of it, there's a decent variety of enemies and final bosses are bullet sponges that look awesome.You feel OP at times but if you leave your guard down the game will punish you very quickly, which i appreciate.Combat is gory as hell, it's satisfying to shoot your fully upgraded secondary HE pistol round and see 3 dudes turned into confetti.Note that sound is good, AI is pretty dumb and there's a pointless stealth mission that i hate.You can replay the game carrying your skill points from your last playthrough which Steam achievement completionists will appreciate.I don't think it's worth the full price, probably half the price would be more fair.Finally, i wish AAA FPS were half this good. This same concept with a larger funding that allowed for more polishing, a better story and longer play time would be an instant classic.

_childDocuments_.review: This game wastes no time! You get thrown into a conflict and shoot, move, shoot, slash, shoot, slash him up in the air, grab him with a emp powered fist, at this point the pipa starts jamming 'bong', shoot some more, climb into this hole, booty shot, sprint, jump and slash... Read further for a chilled out review.Map/Story/Character-Art-Music: The game has solid graphics and some really stunning designs of real Chinese landscapes and buildings. Most of the fighting takes places in rural areas and has a nice mixture of terrain you fight on. Its a pretty straight forward map you wont get lost and plenty of markers to help you on your way. You are part of some task force and get orders to investigate a strange hole in the sky. Mediocre story, voice acting (English), writing but all that is fine wont ruin the game for you. Shelia suit and design is great. The enemies with Youxia Chinese warrior style design was cool to see and different. As I mentioned before the lovely Chinese music kicks in and goes along with the tempo of the game nicely.Gameplay/Weapons/Skills: The gameplay and mechanics is what makes this game great. Everything flows nice from shooting, sword moves and skills. It has a fantastic flow that allows you to switch in between all three styles to defeat your enemy. How Shelia runs and jumps kind of like Titan Fall 2 pilot but not as smooth. Simple but fun amount of weapons which are assault rifle, shotgun, handgun, sniper rifle and sword. All of the guns having a special type of ammo. Leveling up the skills are super easy, by absorbing relics or finding them, minimal grind to level everything up.This is a very fun game. I did bump into a few bugs where I got stuck in the map or fell threw but lots of check points and you would just waste minutes of time nothing major. The game is very short. You can beat it very quickly, including all of the achievements. Hope you have fun, cheers! Bong!

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory is an FPS with excellent shooter and combat mechanics hampered by a confusing and lackluster story. The shooting mechanics of this game is excellent and the guns feel punchy and powerful combined with its melee, dodge and parry mechanics make this a really engaging game.Unfortunately, the excellent gameplay is severely lacking in any purpose. This isn't a multiplayer game where the gameplay is the focus. This is a single player game with a story and that story is utter garbage. It feels as though this game is supposed to be part of a larger narrative, a source material that explains the world and why things are happening the way they are. It doesn't explain what the organization is actually supposed to do. Loading screens say it's an investigative team but that tells nothing. Somehow the game involves time travel(?) or dimension hopping but based on the lack of reaction from the characters this is somehow normal. The story lacks any form of context that explains anything. Even the characters don't have anything to go by except their names. This game can be improved dramatically by the addition of a lore tab but as it is, it's just confusing as all hell.Overall while the gameplay is excellent, the game lacks a narrative through-line to weave it all together.6/10 soft recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite my thumbs up, my actual experience with the game is more lukewarm, though I'm ultimately giving it a "recommend" because I did have fun with the game. Bright Memory Infinite is a game I've been sort of looking forward to because I played the original game, Bright Memory (thus I was able to avail of the free "upgrade" on PC, which is actually a completely separate game from the original), and saw that it was a game with potential to be great. Bright Memory Infinite is the supposedly "complete" version of Bright Memory, with a longer playtime, more levels, better graphics, and overall more polish. Good things out of the way first: Bright Memory excels has amazing graphics, which given that the game was programmed and made mostly by one guy is impressive. I've yet to see a one-dev indie FPS game that looks this great in all aspects being nearly equal to many AAA FPS games, and there wasn't much in the way of jank or bugs to speak of. Basically the game is very well-done on the technical and graphical front, and at least on my end didn't give me any issues of note. However, story, what story? Somehow I feel the game has even less story than its predecessor, and you can pretty much ignore it while you're location hopping from place to place since there's really no rhyme or reason to the entire thing and operates only on rule of cool. Shelia seems even more of a yes-girl than in the previous installment, whose entire personality is built upon stating the obvious and relying on her commander to think for her, and the majority of dialogue has nothing of substance to it. Considering how they actually went through the trouble of giving the cast voice acting and cutscenes, it's kind of a wasted effort I feel due to the story being as vapid as it is. The gunplay of course is one of the main selling points of Bright Memory infinite, mixing rather functional shooting mechanics with a more involved melee combat system that allows one to do stuff from slashing enemies while in midair Devil May Cry style to performing powerful ground slams. The combat system feels amazing to play, especially with the various powers available at your disposal, and controls well for the most part with MKB. Unfortunately the encounter design and enemy variety never really fully takes advantage of the combat system, as the amazing abilities you get don't really seem to mesh with the enemy encounter design in a way that makes them feel needed, and as a result they come out looking more like gimmicks you do only because they're cool. I haven't played the original Bright Memory in a while, but I kinda remember it not being nearly as bland in its encounter design due to having stuff like flying enemies and other such stuff that give diversity to the combat and provide a reason for game mechanics like aerial combat to exist. The game tries to vary it out like having a stealth segment, but those feel like they were forced in without thought just to showcase that the game has those. Nothing about the level design or enemy characteristics and variety bring out the potential of the mixed combat system. Bright Memory Infinite definitely plays like one man's playable game portfolio that they created just so they can get hired by a big gaming company, and so they crammed whatever they can into the game to show off what they can do, logic and consistency be damned. If that was the intent, then they certainly succeeded, and I'm sincerely hoping that FYQD is given more opportunities to make games with more resources in the future. As a product by itself though, Bright Memory: Infinite is only barely worth its base asking price for the reasons above as well as its short length, and I'd personally argue it's a game you should only get on a discount. It's a game you should get if you have 3-4 hours to waste on a game with flashy combat mechanics and/or want to support an indie dev, but it is hard to recommend if you're after meatier, more well-thought out experiences.

_childDocuments_.review: Eh, this one's more of a "support indie devs" recommend than anything. (Bought Bright Memory - the demo - so that's why I've marked this as "received this for free")If you want to go purely off of value, it's hard to recommend, as Infinite is very short for a single playthrough (2 hours), though there is a difficulty option locked behind completing it on "hard", if you're into playing on the hardest mode.  If you previously bought Bright Memory (the initial proof-of-concept/"demo"), then I should say that this game is very different, as this leans towards a run-of-the-mill FPS campaign experience, versus the more abstract scoring and XP systems of the demo. (though, you still unlock your weapon/skill upgrades via enemy drops and searching around for "artifacts") If you want to unlock all the non-DLC cosmetics and achievements it might take you 6 - 8 hours (i.e. 3 or 4 playthroughs).The fidelity is... pretty awesome for a project created mainly by one dev. Slicing and dismembering enemies is pretty awesome, and the explosive secondary ammo type on each weapon is cool, too. The shotgun and handgun feel way more OP than the AR and sniper IMO. The Exo Arm upgrades in general are nice to play around with for a bit as well.There are some annoyances in game design I personally had with it though. There is a forced stealth section if you're not into that sort of thing, but I got particularly frustrated at one of the boss's arenas that has a lot of blocking terrain, and the boss just does not care about terrain as it breaks everything, so why is it there except to block me from moving...Overall, I'm alright with this game (not what I had expected coming from the demo, but pretty good nonetheless). I had planned to support this dude from the moment I bought Bright Memory, so keep doing good, my man.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong. This game has some pretty top-notch gameplay, excellent sound design, a decent world, pretty nice level design, good character design, and pretty visuals (though I honestly don't think the eye candy should've been a priority), and I'm genuinely impressed that one person was able to create this.But it's obscenely short, and the story is actually probably one of the worst ones I've ever seen, it manages to be worse than OTHER M, and that's saying something. I do recommend getting this game and playing it, however, because it's honestly super fun. And it's clear the developer put their heart and soul into it, but at the end of the day it just feels lacking.My main gripe is the fact that it's a completely different story from the demo, as well. The original story and world were ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing, and I was honestly genuinely intrigued and excited to see what happened next in the story. But this game changes it to a far more dull setting, and it honestly hurts because the original world is a huge part of what convinced me to buy the original.Either way, Infinite is honestly a pretty solid game, and it's pretty fun, despite its glaring flaws. It's technically impressive, has unique gameplay that gives it its own unique identity, and it's insane that one person was able to do everything except the soundtrack and voice acting.
