_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory: Infinite is the full release of Bright Memory, . Everyone who owned that game got this one for free when it released. I want to start this by saying congratulations to FYQD-Studio, the solo developer who has done a fantastic job of coming this far. So much of my feedback was addressed and this game is leagues better than the original. But as much as I want to be able to recommend it, I just can't.I'll start with the positives. My biggest issue with Bright Memory was the gunplay. Infinite has completely changed how it all feels. You have four weapons, a fully automatic assault rifle, a semi-automatic shotgun, a full-auto machine pistol, and a semi-auto sniper rifle. All of them have character now. They actually deal damage, even on the hardest difficulties, and they genuinely feel great. Each weapon gets an alternate fire, giving them all optional utility. The rifle gets tracking rounds, the shotgun gets an incendiary cannon, the pistol gets a rocket, and the sniper gets a sticky bomb. Each are valuable resources that are given just enough that you can use them but you wont have them every fight.The abilities got a great overhaul. Now there are two distinct lines of abilities: those tied to the gauntlet and those tied to your sword. Gauntlet includes things like stuns, attracting enemies, and punching them. Sword includes directional slashes, a boomerang like blade, and a block that deflects incoming attacks. These are great and have a lot more depth to how you combo them compared to Bright Memory.Enemies were addressed. Lots of variety now and the AI has been improved. They aren't perfect, but it's still a big step up. They also have way less health (Hooray!)As with the original game, visuals are fantastic. The game ran flawlessly for me (3700X, 5700XT, 16gb RAM) at 1080p with ultra settings. I usually play at 1440p but the game is gorgeous even at 1080p. The weather effects are great, the aesthetic details are fantastic, reflections and the lighting are amazing. It's better looking than tons of AAA games.So what's the problem? The content. Or should I say the lack of it. 6 hours and I have finished the game three times and gotten 100% of the achievements. The gameplay can be amazing (and it is) but if there's no way to really experience it then it falls flat. And that's exactly how the game feels.The pacing of the story is awful. The game's plot is non-sensical at the best of times. I'm not expecting gold, but I was hoping for something coherent. The game doesn't explain who you are, who the voice over the radio is, who you're fighting, or what you're doing at any point in the game. The developer seemed to have confused "fast pace gameplay" with the need for a fast paced story. You need quiet time between fights and scenes to let those scenes have any time to sink in and be enjoyed. No joke, in the mission Close Call you  None of it makes any sense. I could forgive the story if there was more of it, then maybe the gameplay could have the time to actually be enjoyed. It's this lack of content and incoherent story that means I can't recommend it. It feels like a second demo or a trailer for the real game rather than the full release.Pros:- Visually stunning- Good environment design- Amazing gunplay- Visceral abilities- Good music and sound design- Solid voice actingCons:- Way too short (Can be finished in under 2 hours easy)- A 5 year old could make a more coherent story.- Seriously, the story is better explained on the steam page than in game.Overall, I don't think it is worth it at the price they're asking. Maybe in the future we'll see a Bright Memory 2 where they will slow down the plot and allow the characters to have depth.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun game with an interesting set of abilities, gun-fu, and decent difficulty, and amazing graphics with a very realistic art-style. The music is really well-done, and both the sets and boss designs are fantastic, with the Chinese influence very clearly showing through with all of it. The biggest flaw with the game in my opinion is how short it is, because I really would love to be able to play more of it, and I'm really excited to see what other thing FQYD will be making in the future. The story is also relatively light, and not super easy to follow because of how little there is, but honestly, that's not why you play this game. The setting is interesting, the gameplay is great, and the graphics are stunning, and that's why you're playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and kickass action game. The story and dialog is kind of whatever, but it's okay because the combat is some of the best I've ever experienced in a game, especially in a first-person game. Shelia is very mobile and has a lot of options and abilities to use, including an EMP force push and pull, aerial melee attacks, a super-fast slide, wall-running, and so on. You're able to string together abilities to create a variety of combos. This game is a great power fantasy and you feel like a total badass the whole time, except for a weaker-but-short stealth section. This game's aesthetic is awesome, and the graphics are great.Would love to see more games in this series, and would love to see more first-person action games feature mobility and expressive combat like in BM:I.

_childDocuments_.review: legitimately one of the most intense experiences of my life, this thing is non stop from beginning to end, in fact, I'd say that the skeleton a real amazing 7th gen style game is already right here, and all it needs are some low octane (but still fun) filler scenes/missions, as well as more coherent cut scenes to give the whole thing a more satisfying length and tolerable speed. love any game where you get to play as a cute Asian girl with a gun and a sword ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°) haven't tried the DLC but got my eye on the bunny girl one perhaps?gun/swordplay is awesome, and the special abilities are fun as well, though it's a bit difficult to trigger their more powerful effects with the combo like button inputs. enemy variety was suitable enough for it's length, though enemy placement was a bit annoying at times, especially during boss fights when I'd be "this" close to killing him but then a random archer snipes me or whatever. the 1v1 bosses where much better imo. also, speaking of boss battles, too many of them started with an unblock able aoe attack which should be fine except when you revive to try the boss again it starts you right when the aoe attack hits and so your always starting a fight with half health which is pretty bs. love the mechanic of blocking attacks with your sword to clear their defense bar, and the multiple ammo types is always a treat in games, not enough try that. pistol grenade launcher is OP BTW so make sure to upgrade it early, it was the only way I got through half of the bosses. the developer (One guy??!!?) is Chinese so it probably didn't seem creative to him, but the Chinese setting was awesome, and I would love to see more games, hell more media in general, take place in there. also you get to grapple hook onto a plane twice 10/10 game

_childDocuments_.review: A nice follow-up after Bright Memory. I like the concept idea that mashes up between FPS and hack and slash, especially the map and level designs that can inspire. Even if it is buggy, it looks hard at first but I can picture all of this as if it were to be easy. The scenes reminded me a lot of AAA games I have sought and played before. The music is really good for the setting. Though, the story is pretty meh and straightforward. The gameplay could have been more challenging and slightly longer, but the Hell difficulty is easy when you can memorise when the enemies appear and defeat them quickly. While it looks motivating and promising, its relatively short game does not have much what it has to offer after finishing it for the first time or on Hell difficulty. Bright Memory: Infinite may look like it should have more additional content or features that can improve its overall package.I recommended this if you like Bright Memory or any other hack and slash games. I got this for free for purchasing Bright Memory before, but it looks like it is best bought if it has a nifty discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Good looking game from a Chinese indie studio. As a fps it's not really fast paced nor cover based: most enemies need many bullets and special handling to get them down. Some drawbacks of the game are unresponsive controls; twenty fingers keyboard scheme; some bugs and the hefty weapon sway and vibrations. In the end boss fight all these negative aspects come together which makes it unfair hard.Rating is more neutral than positive / negative. I hope that the studio pays more attention to a more fluid combat experience in a this or next game.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory Infinite is an interesting game that relies more on style than substance, meaning you have a cool DOOM like shooter set in a Chinese themed world but a very thin story that barely tells you anything.Remade from the original Bright Infinite this version had quite a lot of new additions.PRO- It's very cinematic from the way the "story" is told to the gameplay which is very similar to how you see games like CoD base themselves on Hollywood blockbusters.- There is a nice combination of first person gunplay and melee fights which blended together can make for some very fun and gruesome combos.- There's a nice variety of gameplay from straight up action, stealth and even driving.- The music was really nice and set the scenes well- You can play in English, Japanese or Chinese for full immersion- There are several boss types that were interesting- Owners of the original Bright Infinite were given this version for free which was a nice moveNEUTRAL- I played on standard mode and I found it to be pretty easy with the amount of ammo it throws it you. Most of the time I had at least 200-300 bullets for each gun.- Achievements are a little buggy as I got "Kill 80 enemies with an assault rifle" as I was killing with the sword- The story seemed like it could have been really interesting but it wasn't explained wellCON- I finished the main game in just under two hours so maybe best wait for a sale.- A few glitches happened which weren't game breaking but had to reset checkpoints once or twice- The ending is pretty abrupt. I won't spoil it but it just sorta happens and isn't explained much either.For a one man development it's very impressive. Not just the game play but the visuals too which look really nice. As much as I admire his talent and want to see the series continue in some way, it's not exactly worth the asking price. But if you have an itching for a good shooter and catch it on a sale then got for it, it'll be worth your time.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Yo, I understand that many others don't enjoy this game or feels like its a "glorified tech demo". I get it, I really do. But to be completely genuine, I honestly really loved the game and thought it was pretty fun. For it being a solo project it still has beautiful visuals, immersive environments/scenery, creative foundations, and a complex game play system that kept me wanting to get better. Now, just because its a solo project I do understand there's still no excuse and there are serious issues with the game.Big factors I see people point out with this game that they don't enjoy is: 1. The game is too short.-While yes, I mean quite literally its facts that the game is very relatively short. Do I wish there was more? Absolutely. But to me, I meannnn shoot for 2 hours of pretty cool game play, immersive environments, and cool ideas, i'm pretty intrigued. Idk I rather play this than waste like $20-$40 bucks going to a movie or any other forms of entertainment. But hey, that's just me though. While the game falls completely short and it can make it feel incomplete, for the short run time I had a fun time learning the slashing and shooting mechanics and I loved the boss fights of intertwined realities. I personally thought that was really sick. 2. The game play is just too much.-While at first I'm not gonna lie, I did feel this when I first hopped in. Just the whole sword melee mechanics on top of the different move sets for it, WITH gun game play mechanics and titan fall like movements felt very overwhelming. Feels like a damn blender of just everything. I found myself not really even struggling with the enemies but me just struggling with myself to try to do a free flow combo or have a rhythm with the controls. But in the midst of chaos, I did find peace. I enjoyed learning how to flow it all together and I liked the challenge and flexibility. I understand for others it can feel unbearable and feels like the game is trying to do too much, but to me I liked the complexity it gave, freedom, and almost a sense of learning curve with sitting down and actually practicing these different combos felt rewarding. I felt like a bad ass going into a fight and just shooting down a few guards, up slashing another while doing an air combo and then just raining down air slashes to remaining enemies made me lose my marbles type beat. It feels like a lot because it really is a lot, but with a lot, I feel you get more freedom and diversity on what and how you want to act in any battle. 3. The bugsCan't defend this one.The game has some pretty bad bugs, i'm gonna keep it solid with you. Multiple times I found myself fighting enemies that quite literally spawned out of nowhere, wonky movement detection like wall running and jumping just felt a bit off, and one that i'm not too sure if others ran into to, but I seriously cannot change my button layout. I tried to change the parry button to a different key command but it just would not work, like at all. So I have no comment about that. Yes, the bugs are buggy and there are here. But with all that being said, I personally had a lot of fun with the game! I feel like it has lots of ambitions, foundation, talent, and creative work to be something truly amazing. While flaws like short overall game time, overwhelming game play, and bugs are in the way of it's success, I really do think Bright Memory is an ingenious game. If any of y'all ever played freestyle gunz, I felt a lot like that with this game but more of a PvE feel of course with boss fights and enemies. A really fun mix of slash and gunning game play with some quick and slick movement to tie in some sick boss fights. To me, it just felt fun. While not a complete feeling game at all, it left me wanting more. I do hope to maybe see its seeds sprout somewhere else or grown again.

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet, just the way I like it.I believe I originally purchased this game for 20 dollars, and for roughly 3.5 hours of content, I enjoyed myself. The guns were satisfying to use, the melee combat was okay, although I never used the full arsenal of abilities I had.I have minor criticism, the main one being that the F key is used for everything from picking up ammo, interacting with stuff, using the grapple hook... It became a little annoying while trying to pick up ammo, and I would just constantly "FUS RO DAH!" with my telekinesis ability, and it was ESPECIALLY annoying during boss fights, where the telekinesis ability does absolutely nothing.Perhaps increase the precision of picking up ammo, or use something other than the F key for the telekinesis ability. Another option would be to disable the telekinesis abilities during boss fights, as it's kind of useless, and that would make picking up ammo IMMENSELY easier.I don't think it's called telekinesis, but I finished this game in one sitting, and I'm not firing up the game and waiting for the loading screens just to check. _childDocuments_.review: The game janky af, feels like a chinese Crysis knock off with a weird melee combat and as any chinese media, it has a completely nonsensical story.The game, is kind of bad, completely unstable, in less than a hour I managed to unintentionally glitch out of bounds and got a crash during a cut scene after defeating a boss. Gameplay has potential but someone decided that the unique combat mechanic is not that good and a forced stealth section and a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ contextual parkour is a better idea. While those parts are not that long, it destroys the flow of gameplay, I just started having fun with the combat, why take me out of it for a game mechanic so generic and basic that feels like it was bought off an asset store.In terms of story, it seems than there is one. I wouldn't know, even tho I didn't skip any cinematic. You get to an island with a black hole in the sky after going through hyperspace in a plane...I don't know what is going on neither who is this people. They keep mentioning a general that seems to be the antagonist, but I never saw him neither I know what he is doing, as far as I know, he could be a figment of the radio guy's imagination. The only thing I know is there is soldiers and I must kill. And for some reason, there is ancient magic chinese soldiers, yeah...Also, the voice acting doesn't help, I have seen TTS programs have a greater emotional range than these people.Lastly are the graphics, the visual effects are decent, even good, but the 3d models look like they are from 10 years ago and the animations feel stiff and unnatural, like they where made by a junior year student from a law college during their free time.The only thing this game has on it's favour is that is dirt cheap and it has an interesting combat mechanic that has unexploited potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game, and was looking forward to this after the first game. Graphics are amazing and game play is really fast paced. The guns are super solid in shooting and accuracy. Sword play is also pretty smooth but reminds you of a generic hack n slash. But dismemberment is pretty cool. The story is unfortunately below average and will take you about 2hrs to complete. I didn't fully understand what was going on, and the ending seemed a bit...rushed. The difficulty is really only relevant when the bosses and mini-bosses show up. The general enemies are cake walk to dispatch. Though don't get too cocky cause they can still kill you pretty easily since you're health is pretty small to begin with, even on Easy. The final difficulty I felt was a good challenge and the bosses REALLY gave me a run for my money, especially that final boss!No major game breaking bugs. Only minor bugs such as the Boar part, the final boar didn't spawn or might have gotten stuck and I had to checkpoint load about 3 times. Enemies getting stuck on objects, and enemies popping in when spawned. Noticed this mainly on the early mission 'Changes' when coming down the steps to fight enemies. On the driving part, ramming into the tank when coming down the hill caused it to just disappear.Overall a really fun title and I look forward to future works from the developer.

_childDocuments_.review: For an 1 man studio this was a very brief technical ray-tracing preview that features the following pros and cons:- Somehow got Ishikawa Yui (Mikasa Ackerman) to be VA. Ends very abruptly with a meme time travel cutscene- Impressive bosses big and small that sometimes cheat by vacuuming you with their attacks You should buy this if you:- Thought Ishikawa Yui's voice was irresistible - Found yourself pondering at what one man can achieve with enough effort and dedication - Came to sad realisation that there aren't any decent AAA ray-traced game to play this holiday season

It's not worth $20 for that, but like $5 tho.As an actual game tho the experience is between mediocre and painful. _childDocuments_.review: Slashing and shooting through an ancient China is strangely fun! Especially when you're accompanied by a hyper-sexualised super agent XD !+ Brilliant lighting effects!+ Ray-Tracing makes a very evident and visually enjoyable difference with negligible framerate drops!+ Shelia is hot!+ Stylish hack 'n' slash mechanics interestingly mixed with FPS elements.+ Many abilities to mix up for spectacular combos!+ Honestly surprised by the stealth segment.+ Multiple difficulty settings for all challenge appetites!+ The music composers behind God of War 3, Resident Evil 2, and Devil May Cry 5 went CRAZY on this one!+ Decent replayability thanks to new skills, difficulties, achievements, and skins.~ Relatively short (roughly 4 hours, maybe less at lower difficulties), but replayable.~ It was pretty much single-handedly developed by one person: Zeng Xiancheng (FYQD Studio)! RESPECT! - Unsynced lips during dialogue cutscenes.- The enemies' corpses disappear lamely (no animation).- Bad collision detection (e.g., plants often fuse into walls, rocks, etc.)- Some textures lose too much sharpness up close.- Rare environmental glitches.- Narratively unsatisfactory connection with the villain.- No photo mode! Damn!

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory: Infinite : By Triple F"Bright Memory: Infinite". the successor to the FYQD-Studio developed Bright Memory, is a whirlwind of ambition. Combining frantic first-person shooting with sword-wielding melee combat, it throws players into a technologically-advanced future filled with supernatural phenomena. While the game boasts impressive visuals and a unique central mechanic, it stumbles with repetitive level design, a convoluted story, and technical hiccups.The narrative unfolds in the year 2036. A mysterious occurrence, dubbed the "Black Sky Incident," has cast a shadow over the world. You take on the role of Agent Shelia Xiu, a member of the Supernatural Science Research Organization (SRO) tasked with investigating this anomaly.The story unfolds at a breakneck pace, bombarding you with technobabble and exposition dumps. Intrigue is hinted at – references to a long-forgotten civilization and a parallel world pique your interest – but the narrative never coalesces into something coherent. Major plot points are introduced and then abandoned, leaving you with a sense of confusion by the time the credits roll."Bright Memory: Infinite's" core gameplay is its saving grace. Shia wields a powerful arsenal of firearms, from standard-issue pistols to grenade launchers, that feel impactful to use. Enemy design is varied, with hulking brutes, agile snipers, and shielded adversaries forcing you to adapt your tactics.The true star of the show, however, is the Environmental Combat System (ECS). This ability allows Shelia to manipulate objects in the environment with her mind and launch them at enemies. Imagine flinging a shipping container at a group of unsuspecting foes, or whipping a stray traffic pole into a flying battering ram. The ECS adds a layer of strategic depth to combat, rewarding creativity and quick thinking.Unfortunately, the thrill of combat is marred by tedious enemy respawns in certain sections and repetitive level design. Environments, while visually striking, often feel like glorified corridors, limiting your tactical options.  The boss battles, while visually impressive, are more tests of endurance than skill, relying on memorizing attack patterns."Bright Memory: Infinite" is a visually stunning game, especially considering its small development team. The futuristic cityscapes are drenched in neon lights and teeming with detail. However, the technical aspects are a mixed bag. Frame rate drops can occur during intense firefights, and occasional glitches can pull you out of the experience.The voice acting is uneven, with some characters delivering convincing performances while others sound phoned in. The soundtrack is a mix of forgettable techno and orchestral bombast that fails to leave a lasting impression."Bright Memory: Infinite" can be completed in a single afternoon, offering little replay-ability value beyond a new game plus mode with slightly increased difficulty. While the core combat mechanics are undeniably fun, the repetitive level design, convoluted story, and technical shortcomings prevent it from reaching its full potential.All in all, "Bright Memory: Infinite" is a game of contrasts. It boasts impressive visuals, a unique combat system, and an intriguing (but ultimately unfulfilled) narrative. However, technical woes, repetitive level design, and a nonsensical story hold it back from greatness. If you’re looking for a short, visually-striking burst of action with a dash of environmental manipulation, "Bright Memory: Infinite" might scratch that itch. However, for those seeking a more polished and narratively satisfying experience, it’s best to wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I waited a while as most of us did for Bright Memory so we could play it but I have to say I'm quite disappointed with the end result, the graphics are fantastic the weapon mechanics are interesting and cool but that's all I can say good about the Game. Its a glorified benchmark for Nvidia to market Ray Tracing and DLSS.-Firing mode changes to explosive without me selecting it-Wants you to break open crates but there is rarely anything ever inside them-Very Clunky Gameplay-Enemies are bullet sponges so are the bosses-Bosses have second lives (I would prefer a harder boss then to re-fight them twice-Picking up ammo is the same button as the power move and picking up the ammo is delayed (Very annoying)-Getting stuck on enemies which causes a delay in switching weapons and blocking (very annoying)-Weapons feel like they do hardly any damage, the best weapons in the Game are the Sniper Rifle with explosive rounds and the machine pistol.-Reload animations don't sync up which causes a delay in the bullets actually loading into the weapon-On occasion picking up ammo bugs out and it won't let you actually pick it up-Bullets don't always hit the target-There is a death delay on some enemies -Switching targets is clunky-Voice over is delayed-Driving is SUPER clunky, car handles like its driving on oil-On occasion the fire button will stop working after switching weapons-Grapple can only be used when prompted, I would prefer to use it when I want to-Getting hit pulls you into a enemies and you get stuck on occasion then get wreaked-Sometimes enemies do nothing till you get really close to them-You can't attack then block then attack again, its like it doesn't register then you get stuck-Shooting and aiming is very clunky and the slow down effect is off putting and doesn't sync up at all Story is kind of stupid and uninteresting, I didn't feel any emotion towards the main character during playing through it at all and the stealth section feels like it was put in there well, just BECAUSE. I found the stealth part and driving part to be quite tedious and annoying. This is simply a glorified benchmark to promote Nvidia Ray Tracing and DLSS as I said at the start of the review, the graphics are very nice and the weapon mechanics are pretty cool but the Game itself is flawed. The level ups on your abilities are pointless since the Game is so short (2.6 hours and you're done) I'm glad its over tbh.. Its great that the Dev gave the people that backed the project the full Game for free but tbh its not even really worth buying unless you just wanted to test out your RTX GPU because the RT implementation is actually very well put together.That's who I recommend this to, people who want to test an implementation of Ray Tracing that actually works pretty good. I played on a Ryzen 9 3950x and EVGA FTW3 Ultra RTX3090, it ran pretty good for the most part at 1440p Max settings Motion Blur turned off. I didn't test DLSS because imo it makes my Games look washed out.I'm going to give it a thumbs down as a Game but as a benchmark I'll give it a pass as long as you pick it up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this post, Ive only put about an hour in, but I feel that is good enough for me to gauge it for now.This will probably be the best example in my mind whenever I think of a game that looks great, but feels bad. The moment to moment gameplay feels just shy of being worth continuing. There will be great moments when I have multiple enemies floating in the air and dicing them into a fine mist, but then minutes later there is a pile of boxes and maybe half of them just wont break to the sword so I have to shoot them.There was a point early on when the ground is covered in electrified water and you have to jump from safe spot to safe spot using the grapple mechanic where I got stuck for a few minutes. The last grapple point of the section just wasnt working for reasons that the game didnt tell me. After ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around for a bit, I discovered that I had to destroy at least one of the many boats that the (all long dead) enemies rode in on and for some reason I cannot fathom, that is what allowed the grapple prompt to activate for me.The combat too can be very wonky. I can shoot one enemy in the head several times and do basically nothing and then shoot the same kind of enemy in the head once and their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cranium explodes. The knock up with the sword is trash as well. In the tutorial you slid into range to get the enemy in the air, but any time after that I had to plant myself within ball-smelling distance just for a chance for it to work.Even the looks of the game arent perfect. Bullet trails consistently go through walls making me think Im not ever really safe. There are constant little cutscenes used for transition that feel entirely unnecessary and waste your time.The last straw for me was during what I'm assuming was the first stealth section of the game. I picked up a cleaver and the way the character holds it plants the flat of the blade directly in the middle of the screen so you have to look around the thing just to see whats going on.All in all, Id say this game is like a very pretty glass sculpture that someone dropped and glued back together. Its pretty, but  it's rough in some spots and sharp in others. It's nice to look at, just dont touch it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is best described as a Swiss army knife.  Jack of all trades, master of none.  For example, there are just so many ways to kill an enemy that it's unnecessary.  It's like the game tries to be something like League of Maidens, where it incorporates skills and guns into the same dance, except it fails to execute it properly.  For most part I just went around grabbing soldiers with the F key, releasing F key, and they were dead.  Other times I just spammed the blade attack, blocked to instantly reload my ammo and the spirit energy, and continued.  I did not use any of the fancy moves until the very end.Another instance is where the game tries to force you, yes force you, to be stealth.  This reminds me of Skyrim with some kill move mods, where a successful execute shows a 3rd person kill move animation.  I don't know... playing this as first person, just did not give me the same excitement as it would if this was a third party perspective.  Something wasn't right about creeping up behind enemies while uncertain that something will jump out at you.  Also, once you get caught, game over.  Add to that some tall grass so that you can't see !@#$, make it a night time of a day, and you have a recipe for a facepalm.Jumping was painful.  I just... did not enjoy it.  This game tries too hard to be Tomb Raider but it just fails.  You'll get this vibe immediately from the start where the game forces you to press some buttons to avoid stuff or execute a move, just like you would in Tomb Raider.  However, by the time the game actually begins, this mechanic is lost and forgotten. After beating the game, you'll be treated to an ending and credits that you cannot skip.  I don't think I've ever played a game where you can't skip the ending credits.  Like, ever.Finally, towards that end, I've discovered that there's costumes.  "Oh cool!" I thought to myself wondering if I'd ever pick this game up again, but maybe just to see a costume on an otherwise cute protagonist.  -What's this?  DLC?? As in paywall?  Facepalm... oh brother.... Once again, the game tries hard to be something like Resident Evil 3, where you'll even get that vibe with the game time played and a grade towards the end, but it just doesn't deliver.  I've modded Resident Evil 3 to oblivion and enjoy spending 2-3 hours beating it each time with a new modded costume.  Trouble is, RE3 is fun to replay and Jill in outfits created by different modders leave little to the imagination.  I just could not get myself to replay this game.In all fairness, comparing this game to RE3 is unfair.  RE3 is a paradigm AAA title and a standard of how games should be made.  Bright Memory: Infinite, is a game that's taking notes and trying hard.All in all, the game is good.  It's worth the $15.  To the authors, if you are reading this, pardon my brusque criticism and please know that despite everything I said above, I have high respect for you and this title.  It's a solid game with no bugs that just needs a direction, but otherwise is a solid piece of software that puts many other established games to shame.  Thumbs up!NOTE: I did receive this game free because I bought the earlier WIP game (work in progress) called Bright Memory (without the "Infinite") and by such, this upgrade was for free.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the culmination of so many refined FPS mechanics, and yet it's gone in under 5 hours.  There are 100 enemies in this game.On top of crisp gunplay, the player is given a sword, power fist, and some fun movement mechanics.  The melee combat is excellent, and gives rhythm to longer engagements in between shooting.  The grunts are stupid, and you consistently fight them in the same bland corridors.  The special units and bosses, however, are very engaging and fun.  There is an optional third person perspective you can use for movement and shooting (not melee), which can be enabled in the settings... it's fun but should really be an in-game toggle.  The level design is pretty whatever.  You get to fight wild boars.The presentation is impressive, boasting heavy visuals with amazing heat and water effects, as well as raytracing and DLSS support.  The story and writing are pretty absent.  A portal opens up spitting out ancient Chinese spirit warriors and some emperor seeking to make his return.  You punch your way to him just to tell him "".  The end.  Still a neat setting though.  The motion blur is great during melee combat, specifically parries.Due to this game's length, I do not recommend purchasing any upgraded editions or addon content unless you would like to support the developer.

_childDocuments_.review: I won't pretend it's the game of the year. But honestly, for one guy alone that is.To make it short:Pro:-It's really beautiful, with nice effect everywhere. Even without RTX.-Some very interesting gameplay idea-the OST is chinese inspired. A nice change with the actual product and it usually fit the action -No bug to report (crash or technical)-Polished game: no wrongly placed texture or zone with misplaced asset.Neutral (not bad as it is, but could be better)-The combo system could be improved. It's cool as it is, but don't really "flow" sometimes. The strikes don't chain naturaly. It could be insteresting to have a system where we can chain the effect for different result (damage, crowd-control, AoE, etc...). The problem is that we unlock some skill, but most of the need a charge, which break the flow of a combo.Now it's not bad, as it work. But could feel better if it was chaining naturaly without interrupting the momentum of the action.-Some invisible wall: it's neutral because it's a one man made, not open world game. But some invisible wall aren't well placed (zone that we could clearly visit without the "wall")Bad:-The end could use more developpement. Either the creator will make a sequel or it's rushed.-The story is very basic, despit some interesting moment.-The characters are barely touch in their developpement. Even the context lacking (what exactly is the organisation we work for, why the MC is working for it, why is she badass?). A "simple" introduction level with a bit of detail about the what or the why would have been appreciated.-AI could be perfected. Having more move to feel more challenging.Conclusion:For a 20$/€ game, made by one guy, it's an impressive piece of work.No bug, well polished, great chinese inspired OST, artisticaly as well as technicaly flawless (at least in my playthrough), interesting gameplay (though it might need improvement)... But very short and story need developpement.Still for that price tag, I would say it worth to support this man for another game or a sequel of this one, should you agree to do so, considering the game is 2h-3h long (if you don't stuck your forward key to speed run it, but don't try to find every collectable either).

_childDocuments_.review: Not one to write reviews but here goes as this was something remarkable. First off, I ran this on a Dell G7 7700 (RTX 2060/i7 10750H/16GB RAM), The game is seriously optimised - LIKE SERIOUSLY. I ran this at 100% MAX settings with 75-85 FPS. This is something that most AAA studios can't seem to get right. The graphics - I mean, you got this game for its graphics, its pure, the RTX on makes a huge difference. It just throws it in your face its that good, so good in fact that it is almost fatiguing to play, not just because it is more intense than DOOM at times. Gameplay - REMARKABLE - It plays just like a £60 AAA game for not even 1/4th the money (I did receive it as a upgrade from the demo though) - There were times where it did seem to be a bit slow to register clicks or input but that was not even one percent of the time. IT LEFT ME WANTING MORE! This is a rarity for me, so much so that the last game that made me feel that way was made in 2005. The ending was perfect and left a desire for a sequal or an update to lengthen it. I did it in just over one hour on Violent. OVERALL this game is something that FYQD should be extremely proud of, I really hope that this guy gets everything he put into it.

_childDocuments_.review: It is year 2019 while most AAA developers were busy releasing buggy, unfinished games and aggressively promoting live-service as the way to go for all gamers, an aspiring developer from China decided to create a masterpiece call Bright Memory.The game was sold a mere 5 dollars and the aspiring developer emphasized that he plan to release a complete updated game with all its earnings. He also promised free copies to all previous buyers. Unlike most aspiring developers who operate based on greed and arrogance, he established a studio while recruiting like-minded talents to assist in his project. While faced with allegation of using stolen art assets by other jealous professional developers (yes that blessed online developers), he openly admit he initially treat the original game like a passion project while combining countless fun mechanic from various notable games. However most gamers who played the previous game understand that there's limit of one person can do but for what he achieved alone with the original game, we all respect his dedication while looking forward to the release of Bright Memory: Infinite (2021).When compared to Bright Memory (2019), Bright Memory: Infinite (2021) is indeed a more polished game except some occasional crashes during cutscene. I believe it is due to the newer codec by Nvidia but it doesn't really affect gameplay and the launch time is fast. Some of the negative reviews I read claiming the control is too hard and plot is linear are rubbish since most games today are designed with similar philosophies but more buggy.On voice acting in this game, I will be honest. I tried all three voices and only the japanese voice acting is believable. The English and mandarin voice acting feels like a VA reading script blandly but it is still tolerable. The overall game experience is fantastic and I heavily recommend anyone to try out this game. Gameplay:   8.5/10 Graphic:       9/10Sound Design:  8/10Voice Acting:  4/10

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game for so long, and I am so happy to finally give this review. It's a short game, but what it does have is absolutely incredible. For something that was made by a single person in their spare time, this is amazing. The visual style and graphical fidelity of the game is top-notch, better than most AAA studio titles of the modern day, save Ghost of Tsushima. The gameplay can be a bit clunky with the strangely strong gravity when jumping and moving, but Deflection/Defending is so incredible satisfying and feels amazing to pull off. The gunplay is fun, and mixing in the various powers that Sheila has makes it all the more engaging and thrilling. The overall fast-paced and adrenaline-pumping action in this game made it well worth the wait. There were many changes from the original Bright Memory, but, I believe that most of them were for the better. The only things I would find bad about it would be the really absurd strength of gravity and clunkiness of wall-running. The gravity makes jumping and getting over some areas really difficult because it will immediately and relentlessly yank you down. It makes it hard to keep or generate proper momentum to keep moving, but, it doesn't make the game unplayable. Overall, despite a short experience, it was a tremendously fun one. I hope that the developer is able to make more games like this full-time, creating even bigger stories, and just as fun gameplay. Maybe even a sequel for Bright Memory could be on the horizon.Now, time to 100% the achievements. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Overall impression: 67 D+. The wonderful graphics and few inspired moments do not make up for the game's many flaws. As a tech demo and proof of concept, Bright Memory knocks it out of the park. As a 'game,' it is not enough for a recommendation.Positives: Great graphics and smooth game play. All of the the weapons are functional and fun to use. The swordplay is great and adds a welcome layer to what could have been a standard shooter. The foes you face are not bullet sponges, but they are not cardboard cutouts either. (They are a bit on the predictable and dumb side, but that's fine.) While there is not a large variety of foes, there are enough to keep things interesting and their designs are spectacular.The whole game feels like you are playing a B action movie that gets just about everything right, but is crippled by the lack of a larger production budget and production team.Before I get into the negatives of the game, I want to stress there are many aspects of this game that are done far better than AAA, big name projects. The graphics are impressive. The combat, when it flows, is fun, over the top, and makes you feel like a super soldier. There is part of me that really, really hates knocking any part of this game due to the obvious love and care that went into aspects of it. I DO NOT DISLIKE THIS GAME. I just cannot recommend it when there are so many better alternative short single player shooters out there.Negative Aspects: I beat the game in less than three hours. I have played demos for far longer. This would have been a marvelous sales pitch for a much larger project, but as things sit the game is far too short, has no coherent story line to follow, and left me wanting more rather than scratching my shooter itch.There were some weird bugs that popped up time to time through the game. However, the vehicle section of the game was rife with them. At one point it was almost funny as the game's engine would make the enemy vehicles bounce around like they were super balls, but it made completing the section tedious as the bugs also seemed to make it difficult to navigate.The basic controls are great. The controls for the secondary attacks for the sword and power suit feel out of place and can be hard to pull of in the middle of combat with a keyboard and mouse.Most of the combat is fun and fluid and the impact of using the sword on the lesser and medium sized enemies was satisfying. The bosses, however, lost that feel. They would shift from not seeming to feel blows to staggering at the slightest touch, depending on where they were in their attack pattern.To be honest, in many ways the 'completed' game felt as if it had taken steps backward from the demo product released a while back.Bright Memory is by far not the worst game I have ever played. However, its brilliant and fun moments could not overcome its short play time, bugs, and sometimes awkward controls, leaving me unsatisfied overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory Infinite is almost an incredible experience but falls short in a few ways. Firstly the movement is solid enough with plenty of movement options such as crouch sliding, dashing, and double jumping. Wall running is also included, but lacks the polish or usefulness required to really take traversal to the next level. The play environments, whilst stunning to look at, lack any real verticality therefor not making wall running a necessary part of traversal. Playing Titanfall 2 might have soured me on this experience more than someone looking into playing Bright Memory Infinite without having experienced how good FPS movement can feel. Lastly, there are many moments where the game insta-kills you for not navigating a traversal obstacle correctly. Most of my deaths were via strange oddities with movement, like wall running not working or double jumps throwing me way too far or not far enough. Speaking of instant-kills, there is a forced stealth section. These are almost never a good idea, and the protagonist goes from a one woman army to nearly helpless if a guard so much as glances at her for more than 2 full seconds. It's a total pacing killer as well that feels added to create more variety in a game so short it never needed it. The gun play is solid enough, but the lack of interesting environments to creatively funnel enemies through combined with a somewhat gimped movement system and lack of overall length make this a very hard game to recommend unless you got it as a free upgrade. But ultimately, you will have fun with the game despite these flaws, and many of the critiques I've made in this review are easy to look past if you remember how small the team is working on this game. It also has incredible visuals pushing ray-tracing and DLSS making it a great test piece for new GPU owners. Plus who can hate a game where a kawaii girl goes full Metal Gear Rising meets Shadow Warrior on some cyberpunk looking guards and ancient beings?

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory: Infinite is an incredibly mixed bag. The game makes it pretty clear to players that from the get-go, that its narrative is not going to pack much of a punch. I truly have little idea what was actually happening and why. As such, the game-play and the graphics tend to do much of the heavy lifting.The gameplay is a very big bright point for this game. everything feels very fluid, swift, and decisive. Every gun the character uses feels great to use and serves their own respective purposes. The game also gives you decent array of different skills to play with that you can upgrade/unlock throughout the game, each being great tools to add to your arsenal. However, your character can easily feel overpowered and overturned, especially after getting the variety of upgrades. There is almost no enemy that is going to present any danger to you. Unfortunately, this is mostly true for the bosses as well. each boss can easily be stun-locked and is not going to present any challenge. The challenge these bosses largely have comes from the difficulty setting you are playing on. Even on the highest difficulties, the only thing that realistically changes is how long the fight lasts. Nonetheless, the gameplay in Bright Memory is by far its greatest asset.Despite how impressive the gameplay and graphics, there are most definitely a few glaring holes. I truly wish there was more substance and the game was a bit more fleshed out. Unfortunately, the game does not take very long to beat. You will likely spent about 2hrs playing through the game and then additional 2-3hrs if you are going for all the achievements. Nonetheless, if you are looking for a decent action game to shut your brain off to, I think you will enjoy this. Score: 6.5/10 (Okay)

_childDocuments_.review: FIRSTlY AND MOST IMPORTANTLY FOR ANYONE WHO HAS THE GAME OR DOES GET THE GAME ANYWAY: Shotgun+light blade slash= nearly infinite stun lock. If you're more interested in not playing the game as intended literally just push the light slash button and shoot at the same time with it and it just trivialized every boss and "tanky" enemy in the game.I will say I did enjoy the game. I paid for what I got in the end truly. But....Second, I'll check the box indicating I got the game for free. But I will agree to the pov that I didn't really get it free since I bought the "demo" (which really means I only paid like $7 for this $20 game). Which is important for understanding my reason for giving it a thumbs down. I won't go into too much detail with my review because there are plenty of people who have reviewed the game since release. But I would not recommend this game to anyone at full price. This game feels like a demo of the showcase that the original creator made afew years ago and, while I commend the creator for going through with making a "full" title it honestly kinda sucks that I cleared a $20 game in less than 2 hours. It would have only taken me a little longer had I played on a harder difficulty and not abused THE EVER LIVING HELL out of what I can only assume to be the not-so-intended feature of combining the shot gun and the light slash which literally just turns everything in the game into a damage sponge. In conclusion: The game is just waaaaaaaay too short and there is absolutely no explanation as to what the frick is happening. I can forgive a lot about the lack of quality everywhere else considering the background of the games development but a game that took this long, being released for $20 and there being literally no explanation for anything happening, and there being day 1 ♥♥♥♥♥♥ dlc which is a complete scam on top of the fact the game is literally 3 hours long MAX I'm leaving a thumbs down for now. And as a side note, I have a 3070 from a prebuilt so I'm not sure if that could be considered a factor in this but playing the game on medium settings with low ray tracing will cap my frames at like 60-80 fps max. Okay, a little on the low side for such a small game from an indie dev I guess. But playing the game on medium/high settings with raytracing turned on (even going between low and medium) it utterly breaks the game and nearly crashes my computer. And the GPU is the only thing I've shucked and haven't had the ability to stress test yet so I think I'm going to blame the games opmitmization for this as most games I play get over 100fps.

It also feels like a chore to play through- Enemies (except a select few) have terrible accuracy and AI- All enemies are bullet sponges- Unskippable cutscenes (an issue when you are playing for the second/third/whateverth time)- Minor bugs and glitches (like seeing enemy lasers through walls/buildings)- Pacing issuesʲᶦᵍᵍˡᵉ ᵖʰʸˢᶦᶜˢGame crashed at the end of Giant King boss once and I had to redo the second phase. _childDocuments_.review: Aloha, this is my review for Bright memory and FPS action adventure. Plus, the protagonist is hot and jiggly, which is nice to see. The game has lovely graphics with great special effects. _childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing when viewed from the price given. Maybe the playing time in this game is still not long enough for some people, but in my opinion this is more than enough.In terms of gameplay, it's actually fairly ordinary, just like most FPS genre games with a fast pace. If you feel the full experience of this game, I suggest playing on the "hell" difficulty.For AI or enemies in this game they tend to surround us when they want to attack and are very annoying if we have to face the existing boss fight, because their attack combinations are practically random and different every time we face them. There is no benchmark for the health bar condition of the boss fight, they can attack you with their special attack at the beginning. I think this is very interesting.Continue to the combat system in this game, speaking with the combination of special skills and leveling owned by Sheila is quite balanced.The weapon variants are basic, enough to represent various types of weapons that are common in FPS games in general. but one thing that is interesting is the special bullets that each weapon has and it turns out that this actually makes the game even more balanced.In terms of graphics, this game has pretty good graphics considering the price given. The RTX implementation in this game isn't bad either.For the voice actor in this game is quite good and I appreciate the Japanese version of the voice actor which is better than the other versions. Oh yeah, don't forget the soundtrack in this game, play at a fast pace but feel more relaxed when you hear the soundtrack.Actually what is lacking in this game is the control it provides. In my opinion, combining two combinations of movements in one button is quite disturbing the comfort of playing. Especially the sprint and dodge buttons which actually have to be separated, or if you want it's easier to make a double tap on the button movement to make it simpler. Because for players who use hold for several buttons it is quite difficult when they have to dodge using the same button as sprint. Maybe in the future we can pay more attention and it will be even more interesting if we can implement the macro button on the mouse as a control in this game.One more thing that is lacking but I understand it more, namely in terms of the facial expression that Sheila has, it's too flat. never matched the voice over presented hahaha

_childDocuments_.review: If they add a horde/wave mode and fix the bugs, I will probably change my recommendation. The gun and sword play feel really really good with the exception of the charged launcher attack which seems like it misses and you don't know why until you realize it only works when the enemy is in a certain state. However, boss fights are very bullet spongy, and don't have a lot of unique mechanics to them outside of just looking really intense, so a lot of your abilities feel kind of meaningless.You have a grappling hook mechanic that is literally only used for moving from point A to point B at some points of the game, and would've been really cool to implement during boss fights or even clearing packs of mobs, but instead you're stuck with gun and sword play.You also have a dash that is very similar to Doom, but you only can use it in the 180 degrees behind you. It's very nice and again feels good, but I would've preferred the Doom approach where shift doesn't make you run forward, you're always running and have a walk button, and this dash can be used in all directions.There are also quite a few very noticeable bugs that ruined a little bit of the experience for me. Apparently if you're clipped out of bounds on accident, the way the game resolves it is by just pushing you upward until you are no longer clipped inside of the walls. This happened twice in my one playthrough, one of which ended out being okay, but another which soft locked me behind a barrier that would not allow me to advance or go back so had to reload the checkpoint. Lots of times enemies will also just kind of get stuck in the environment and not move.With all that said, the overall quality of this game considering the small size of the development staff is pretty mind blowing. Omitting the story here as there's not really much to talk about there, the game looks phenomenal and is super fun to play, but it's just a little too buggy and not enough content to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this off by saying I hate steam's binary yes/no rating systems that forces you to slap one of two  grades on these reviews.If I could properly rate this game it's be somewhere in the middle but considering the relatively small team behind this game and the effort and passion that went in to it I can't bring myself to give it a negative grade so there, overall positive.The synopsis: The game's a very pretty first person shooter with kinda but not really super powers a kinda but not really magical sword and a linear story. You move through scripted set pieces, killing dudes with an occasional boss.The pros:The environment looks stunning both from the visual and audio aspect.The guns handle well although primary fire on some of them lacks a kick.The movement is smooth and well crafted.The powers feel great to use.The difficulty is slightly on the easier side but overall it's fine.The Cons:The length. The game's short, from start to finish It took me less than 3 hours to pass it and that's after giving up trying to fix issues with it for half an hour on day one. (Thankfully said issues have already been fixed).The price. It's 20 bucks for a 2ish hour experience, not the best bang for the buck.Lack of replayability. Once you finish the story you can play again if you want to but that's about it.The lack engaging mobility mechanics during combat. Wall running/jumping and using the grappling hook only happen during scripted events optional grappling locations or walls to run on during boss fights or just normal enemy encounters might make the running about the place and shooting about the place elements of the game blend better together.The upgrade system is boring and the points are so plentiful you'll have almost everything upgraded by the end.The facial animations aren't nearly as polished as all the other visuals creating a jarring effect.The Odd (Mostly nitpicks):The lack of a forward dash? Like hold to sprint tap to dash has been a staple in many games, it feels weird that it's not a feature here.The mandatory stealth section that can mostly be cheesed by rushing like a maniac and 1-2 shotting enemies before they have a chance to shoot you twice.The mandatory vehicle section that's entirely too easy, too short and honestly just not very memorable.The mandatory press F to continue bits... Like... what do these even add? Why do they happen so many times?Boarded doors needing to be meleed to progress. Why does shooting not break the planks...?So overall the game's fine if it's 5 bucks on a sale or maybe even 10 then consider picking it up for a very short albeit pretty experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, had fun for most part with the one specific exception that I will talk about later.The game opens with a weird sequence of cutscenes and QTE, the devs what they did look stunning so these first minutes is purely made to take your breath away with its graphical fidelity. I tend to hate QTE in video games and all those mechanics that takes away the control of my hands so it kind me feel uncertain about what I was about to play.After falling off from your plane the game throws right into combat with some "FREEZE HERE'S SOME INSTRUCTIONS" type of tutorial, wich left a sour taste in my mouth, I was really about to give up the game, but when I started actually playing I got hooked. The combat is just fun, fast and intense, you have access to a sword for melee, fire weapons like pistol, AR and all that good stuff, also have some jedi like abilitys that makes your being pushed or pulled away from you, sprints, slide, project reflection, parry, double jump e wall run, wich gives the game a great variaty on how to aproach combat.Shooting feels precise and satisfying with some heads being poped here and there, unfortunely the melee feels a bit unresponsive with some weird limitations, like if you are close to a wall or if the area you are fighting has ceiling, you are not able to perform a launching move, wich is weird. Since you need for most enemies break their armor gauge to be able to combo on them, the game saying "nono" for you during the opening you created doesn't feel right. You can combo of an enemy after launching him into the air, but both rising slash and aerial combos feels weird to land most of the time, but nothing that will ruin the the experience, after getting used to how things works, you are able to do some crazy stuff.Sometimes the combat areas can feel a bit messy visualy wich makes spoting enemies, even with the yellow stripes on their helmets a bit hard, and yeah things can get really intense, remember that I said that the enemie variaty is good, so while u r fighting some bit dudes with shields, you also be facing some smaller dudes with ranged weapons or mid range stuff, fighting all these enemies plus the visual polution can be annoying at times, dying from a dude that you wasnt able to spot can be a thing.After each combat zone you will face yourself in a small section without enemies and with stuff to collect, just a small room to breath between encounters, wich is very welcoming.Bosses are hella fun, they usually push yourself to do some crazy ♥♥♥♥ against them, fun stuff."Why there is an stealth section in this game? WHY SOMEONE WOULD PUT A STEALTH SECTION IN A FAST ACTION GAME, WHYYYYYYYYY?"Yes, there is an stealth section in this game, wich is ok to add some gameplay variaty, but in case of games like this, it just feel like the devs cut your arms off, they took away your toy and said "no more fun fo ya kiddo". For the most part is passable, you can at least sprint and slide for a fast stealth kill, but damn, they added the famous wait the enemy turn kind stealth design, wich can be really boring, specially after playing female Dante on crack, and no, you can't sound the alarm to have fun, you are stuck with kitchen knife at this section and everytime you are spoted, it counts a fail and you need to restart the section.I would talk about lore and stuff, but I'm to lazy to pay attention to dialogues, there is a goblin inside my head that only wants to press buttons and kill stuff.What an intense experience this game provides, really polished, has stunning visuals with some fast and crazy combat.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite bad to be honest. Love and dedication is apparent in every inch of it, but as much as I respect the developer the game doesn't deserve a Very Positive rating. I recieved the game for semi-free just as the majority of reviewers and I can't imagine paying 20$ for it.PROS:1. Skills and Gunplay are genuinely fun. A considerable number of offensive abilities and each weapon having an alternative firemode rewards experimenting.2. Variety of mostly fun to fight enemies. Armored and shield wielding foes effectively force you to move.3. Some boss fights and some sections. The game has it's moments. The final boss fight is very well done. Plane section while abruptly cut serves as a neat surprise.4. Environments. I don't often have shootouts in flooded chinese village with a black hole looming overhead.CONS:It took me a little under 2 hours to complete it on Violent difficulty however the length is the least of it's problems.1. Awful level design. The levels are divided into corridors or two-dimensional arenas. The game is painfully linear. Invisible walls are everywhere and I mean it EVERYWHERE. To the point where a thin patch of reeds and a small fence are counted as a wall. There's usually one exact route to follow, especially when level incorporates any sort of verticallity.2. Underdeveloped movement abilities. There's edge grabbing, wall running and grapel hook. All of the these aren't very organic as they can be preformed in few predetermined spots.3. Pointless stealth section. Suddenly an EMP takes away my weapons and sword so I have to grab a random cleaver and make my way through a parody of a modern AAA "Must have been the wind" stealth section. I suppose this was done to increase variety in gameplay but really should have been skipped in favor of something else to break up the shootouts.4. A few visual glitches/bugs. Some effect was constantly stretching edges of my screen during cutscenes. Gun animations during slow motion were visibly choppy and low-framerate. I got stuck in a door frame and had to reload the save. Addionally observed one T-pose, some levitating bodies. 5. I won't be spending money on additional outfits that should've been locked behind challenges and progression. Missed opportunity for more replay value - something that kept me replaying the original 4-5 times.6. Also the dialog with Chen and objective names are laughable. "Where are you?" "I'm in a reed field". > Jump down the hole> Hide near the left wall> Go to the rightThe game while being painfully linear still does handholding by drawing arrows on walls to signal climbable spots.Grab it on a big sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I had more fun with this than any Call of Duty campaign in the last 10 years or so.  Had a few moments of budget jank, but for the most part, it ran well on a mid-range PC at max settings and low raytracing.  Combat is fast and frenetic, reminiscent of Bulletstorm with grappling, melee combat, and really satisfying gunplay.  Sounds good, looks good.  The story seems Google translated but the dialog and voice acting are functional.  The environments are extremely repetitive and the game is REALLY short, only about 2 hours, but it was still some of the most fun I've had with a single player FPS campaign in a long time. I really miss mid-tier FPS campaigns like this.  Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t like to negatively review a game, unless it really is bad. I always try to find the charm in it, the silver lining. However, this is one of those exceptions. Bright Memory: Infinite, is a 2 hour fiasco with no thought out narrative, no real build up or character progression, and gameplay that became repetitive even if it was fluid and dynamic.When I bought the game, I wasn’t expecting a AAA blockbuster, I was expecting a small little adventure with a unique premise and fun journey. If it was marketed as a demo product, an external adventure from the full release title, then I wouldn’t be so harsh with it.I’ll give credit where credit is due, the visuals look stunning, the core mechanic gameplay with the abilities and weapons was enjoyable. The boss battles were challenging, yet intriguing, and the varying minor enemies was a nice combative challenge, if a little repetitive. So there are good qualities about the game, but they are overshadowed by the core premise.It probably hurts it, being only a 2 hour game. The narrative is vague, if at all prevalent. The main protagonist is nothing really memorable, and in some ways a little generic. The starting cutscene had me hooked to begin with, but as it started to play out, as I started to realise the end was already approaching, that the story was already ending, I soon fell out of touch.It’s my opinion to see it that way, and as someone who sees the narrative and character development of a game as a core fundamental, it really was nothing to shout home about. All in all, if you want gun focused gameplay, futuristic abilities, a mythology inspired landscape and characters, all in a 2 hour package, then by all means play it. If however you see this as another narrative rich adventure, with a potentially good premise lasting for a fair few hours, you might be better off elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Bright Memory: Infinite is pretty much the final version of what Bright Memory is meant to be. If you bought the latter back when it was still in development, you pretty much get this game for free. You use Sheila, who's pretty much trying to investigate some convergences between worlds, while being pursued by General Lin and his army (what happened to Carter though...). Along the way she has to fight against enemies, whether its General Lin's troops, or some ancient Chinese warriors with strange abilities. She has various guns, each with secondary mode of firing, in addition to her exoarm that is capable of telekinesis, or just being able to land devastating blows. You will collect some orbs and reliquary to upgrade Sheila's weapons and skills, to boost their effectiveness as well.Unlike Bright Memory, there is a clear Chinese theme here, from the character names, the environment, buildings and even the monsters here, which is pretty much given, as the developers are from China after all. There are also changes to some gameplay here, such as skills having pretty much have no cooldown here, instead they are kind of limited by your exoarm energy, which is a pretty nice change compared to the cooldown present in Bright Memory. Double jump here is done by tapping jump twice, instead of holding jump in Bright Memory. She also can parry attacks, which helps to refill her exoarm energy bar, and replenish ammo as well. Wall run are present in some places for manuevering purposes, albeit not much. Scoring system is no longer present here, and lastly, you can reconfigure key layout here. Finally.Unfortunately, it kinda suffers from one big problem as Bright Memory; its too damn short! For a full game, you can complete it in 2 hours. There's also some weird checkpoint mechanics here where if you die, you will restart the checkpoint... with the amount of ammo you had left right before you died, instead of how much ammo you have when you reached the checkpoint. Some part also have unskippable cutscenes, as it may have some QTE, which is a bit annoying.Despite that, I did enjoy this game. It's not too bad, and its quite fun. As in Bright Memory, the Japanese VA for Sheila is still Yui Ishikawa, which is a well known VA. Coupled with workshop mods, you can use a 2B mod for Sheila and it will fit really well with the voice. If you want to get this game, perhaps you wait for a Steam sale to try it out.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing you need to know: This game is SHORT! On Violent difficulty (essentially Normal difficulty), I beat the game in 2 hours and 1 minute. It'll be longer on harder difficulties and/or if you go for all achievements, but it's still very short.Secondly: The game is BEAUTIFUL. This game was created by one person (voice acting, music, and publishing not included). It looks like a Triple-A title. I was able to get the game to run mostly smooth, though there was a little slowdown in areas with heavy weather effects (RTX 2080, i7-8700k, DLSS balanced). The visuals are jaw-dropping.On gameplay: The game is a lot of fun, but if you played Bright Memory (the original game), keep in mind that the combat is different here. Combos aren't really a thing as far as the score is concerned (you can still create combos, they just aren't as integral as they were in the original). The skill tree exists but is much different. Weapons function a little differently too (they all have special ammo with effects that can be upgraded within the skill tree). None of this is negative, though, just different.Also, there's more gameplay variety in BM:I than BM. Where as BM had that one puzzle (that I never figured out and randomly hit buttons till I solved it), BM:I has no puzzles. Instead it has a stealth sequence and a driving sequence (plus a few timed escape sequences). You also fight on two moving planes at one point.The music is... it just is. It's like standard action-movie music, no notable tracks to my ear, and no themes. I'm a big video game music nerd but you might not care.The story is strange. It's cohesive and you can follow it, certainly. You're not likely to get confused as to the sequence of events, I guess. It's somewhat barebones, though. There's serious depth to the story and all the characters that doesn't really get explored. We know Shelia is part of the SRO, but how'd she join? Who runs it? How does she already know General Lin? Et cetera, et cetera. There's actually no character exploration in this game whatsoever: Not in Shelia, Chen, Wake, or Lin. We know how they matter to the game's story but absolutely nothing else. The best you get is the little tidbits of info during loading screens. The game is replayable. After you beat it, it gives you your time and death count, and gives you a grade. If you want to try and do better, go for it. Overall, I have two ratings to give this game. If you got it free because you played the original Bright Memory, 9/10. If you didn't and are looking at playing 20$ for it, 7/10. The length of the game is the real factor here. You have to keep in mind that if you didn't get this title free, you're paying 20$ for a beautiful, very fun game that only lasts two-ish hours. If you've got extra money, or if you find the game on sale, I'd go for it.EDIT: Forgot to mention, but this game is also extremely linear. It tells you where to go and you go there. There are no alternate routes or secret paths. It is extremely linear from beginning to end.

_childDocuments_.review: There are shooter games (for example, Ghostrunner) that focused on high rhythm and fast paced movement with according traversal systems. But developers of Bright Memory decided to combine all known mechanics in high paced temp shooter without coherent, consistency and deepness. This game doesn't know how to use its own arsenal of mechanics, has oodles of moment to polish, lots of stuff to cut. This game has, for example, wall run, but it doesn't use it almost at all. Ghostrunner had absolutely less mechanics than Bright Memory, but Ghostrunner combined them in different ways and diverse approaches. Bright Memory is perfect example why developers should remember about the rule "Less is more"p.s. From the narrative design perspective, Bright Memory has no good moments to remember. It's the example how we shouldn't make the story, even if the game is not about the story first of all.

_childDocuments_.review: I justify this game to be 5 to 10usd, and this review will tell you why I think so.As someone that was trying to play this game on slightly above the recommended specs(no-ray tracing 1080p) it surprisingly was very stuttery, upon upgrading my hardware and everything, the stutter disappeared. If you need an idea on how important this was to do? It was more than important to enjoy the pace of the game. Where fighting and parrying enemies are much harder when your having some spikes in frame rate. Then again there is a lot going on in this game and you can justify it's optimization in some very specific scenes.First thing is first to give you a perspective, it's going to be a 2 to 2 and a half hours for your first play-through, this will include deaths and finding secrets. It's a very short game, and I was disappointed by that. I was hoping it was going to be a 4 hour game.To start off, the weapons are super satisfying, all of them feel how they should, this is a run and gun kind of game so it's not hard to mess that up as long as things do good damage. Just don't make things do too much damage, like the secondary ammo, where I've used the secondary ammo for bossing, and it just melts health., all it takes is good aim and bosses kind of become a joke. The first boss is harder than the second so it makes the second disappointing and the 3rd boss . Also, ammo drops and storage count are way too plentiful. it makes the ammo system not really need to exist unless you're using the secondary ammo, even then. the secondary ammo feels more balanced than the normal bullets because their so limited.(this could be different on higher difficulties, I'll post an update if it is.)Unfortunately the game is quit buggy, I've gotten stuck on nothing and I'd start to run without making a single bit of movement. Sometimes I'd get stuck because I wanted to try something and my way out was just using the blade-uppercut. It's a fairly inconsistent game sometimes. I've died more to mechanics not working than from actual enemies in my first play-though alone.The Story is very weak, some stuff happens out of nowhere some scenes seem super unnecessary. The sections that aren't exclusively Running and gunning doesn't feel like it should be in this game, , and overall design of enemy spawns and pathing can really break immersion, I was once dealing with 3 enemies all cluttered together in a corner and being stuck where if I looked at them I'd start to get mowed down, so I had to peek to kill them.All of the fun kind of comes down to how fast you can clear the game for me after my initial play-though and farming some achievements,(I'm thinking of doing a pistol only run, then see how often I have to go into sword combat.)graphical quality can be iffy, the game itself looks good overall, it carries one art-style(realistic), which will feel dated in a few years, the animations on cut scenes are very clunky but game-play parts are very good animation wise those are phenomenal. The facial animations are quite bad, but it's hard to get those right anyway(why most studios use people to do the animations instead).The DLC outfits seem a bit expensive, I'd rather they all be a single pack that is maybe all together 3usd just because they don't really do anything apart from change her model, even then there is already a modding community for that sort of thing.First off, the voice acting makes the characters feel very disconnected from one another, and it hurts the tone of the moment, what do I mean? Well, the opening scene the dude on the phone(The name isn't memorable) says "Shelia" at the beginning of every sentence and it's as if it's the beginning of the conversation at times, I get they want you to remember her name, but it's not natural in any way. Sometimes the delivery of the conversations also feel super disconnected. Where one moment a character is super panicked and suddenly the tone changes into a super calm one as if everything is ok,  The delivery of everything is quite comical in that kind of degree.The world building is also kinda meh, there is one mission that ruins it for me. and the sections that feel pointless I think would be better if the game had a better approach really, . I do see this game having potential, but it's full of so many ideas the 10% of the game-play that isn't just running around and shooting kills the flow of the game it screams the speed and intensity to a halt and you're suddenly playing a different game.(Note to the devs, don't stray away from the pace of the game, with a section, just redo the section and add a weapon or something that is exclusive to that section that might feel like a mini-boss without being in an arena)The bugs are also super annoying, Where grappling wont work randomly, interacting with things being binded to the same key as a skill just uses the skill instead of picking up ammo, especially when in the middle of a boss-fight makes me have to run around more and refrain from the single gun that is almost out of ammo that I like to use the most.I'll add more to this review if anything comes to mind.
