_childDocuments_.review: A really great intense experience that doesn't feel like it wastes your time.Other than some noticeable, yet not too intrusive bugs, this game's really bloody good. Compared to the original "Tech Demo", this one's more approachable, faster and much more bombastic. Though it's also called mindless by some, I've found out. Graphically it's beautiful. Every frame a painting and all that shenanigans. It runs pretty decently regardless of its detail and generally great visuals. The combat involves a bunch of various abilities that then in turn have extra varieties for each of them, including upgrades to all of those as well. Due to how short this game is, the upgrade points are just given to you like candy and while it might seem like it's rushed, it always served to keep the game intensely varied with changes coming to the game every time you get bored of the previous stuff.The story is generic, inconclusive, non-committing and just plain forgettable. In fact I can't remember much of it already.Honestly, I don't know what people are whining with the length. What's with the need to drag out the same amount of content across 40 hours? The game's replayable enough thanks to its length and features like timers and stat tracking. So at some point the question arises: Why is there so much complaining over the fact that the game knows its limits? Why is there so much reverence over 12 hour games that have actual content for 6? Why is there such desperation to spend time more and more and more while I doubt anyone has trillions of hours to go through everything we'd want to do?Literally every month, there's so many deals and services that with literally only $10, you could get a solid dozen video games that are well received. That's not to even mention things like Xbox Game Pass and Humble Choice and so on. That's just if you only like video games as a way to spend time. A good product leaves you wanting more and a ♥♥♥♥ one fills you up with watered down garbage until you just can't hold more. But since it's not the length of an entire workday, I guess this game's supposed to ♥♥♥♥ off. With this in mind, I'd say this game succeeds and even more. If the main complaints are that people want to play more of the game that has systems to encourage more play, then what the hell else is there to demand? Quality over quantity. You won't be grinding an area of side quests for 6 hours on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - The presence of QTEs in a game released in 2021 is sort of a microcosm of how I feel about this game as a whole. The game made me hate it in less than an hour, and it feels like it's held together with elmer's glue and rubber bands.Less is more. Don't clutter your game with a bunch of unnecessary ♥♥♥♥ that doesn't need to be there, especially if you're a single person making a whole game. The combat feels clunky and awkward cause there's too much stuff going on at once, and while it's a lot better than the demo, it would have been better if it were reined in a little more.On that less is more / game is too cluttered point, there's a lot of situational things where, for example, you would expect to press E to slash some boards or crouch under a thing that looks crouchable, but for some arbitrary reason the game decides it's an F command. "Press F to break in", I look at the boards and press E by instinct, doesn't work, read the prompt, press F, and she ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ walks through it. There is also a point near the beginning of the game that is EXTREMELY unintuitive. I got softlocked at the electrified water part several times because for SOME ungodly reason, the game arbitrarily decides here, for no reason, that you can't use the grappling hook that it just introduced. Not until you make a specific boat explode by shooting at it. Never mind that all the enemies are dead, you can't grapple until you make that boat go boom. WHY?And on that note, I really hate when tutorials either force you to do something by arbitrarily disabling other options, or disable things until you're prompted to use them instead of letting the player naturally figure it out. Having a game not let me jump until the tutorial says "press A to jump" will never not piss me off.Not to mention the grapple hook is just broken to begin with. One one of my attempts of the electrified water part, I pressed F too early and got stuck, it wouldn't let me move because the tutorial says so, I couldn't even move the mouse, and I couldn't use the grapple feature so I just had to sit there for a full minute while the enemy shot me in slowmo until I finally died and was able to sit through the sonic 06 loading screen to try again. After that, if the game slightly doesn't like your timing with the F attack, it just breaks. It's extremely clunky.Anyways after that you get into a fight with an ancient chinese emperor/general who has superpowers and speaks english. It's a dark souls boss in a game that's not good enough to be dark souls.Did I mention the sonic 06 loading screens? Every time you die, you have to sit through a loading screen while the game loads the area you're already in. The loading screen lasts just long enough to be irritating, even more so because it's unnecessary as the area is already ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ loaded.I got it free because I paid for the demo before the game came out. If you're thinking of picking up this game expecting something that's fun and polished, and playtested, don't. You will only get frustrated.There's a lot of clunky mid-2010's game design cruft in this game, and it's not much better than the demo. The thing is it could be much better, but for that, the dev would have to get other people involved. Like playtesters and better programmers and someone who can sit down and cut out all the unnecessary crap. Like I said, the presence of QTEs in a game released 2 years ago is a microcosm of the game as a whole. If you aren't willing to cut out the QTEs, at least add an option to disable them. A lot of players, myself included, hate QTEs and see them as obnoxious and lazy game design. Less is more. It's better to have a handful of game mechanics that are well-implemented and work well together than a ♥♥♥♥ ton of game mechanics that are all glitchy/clunky and only work in isolation and might break or softlock the game if the player attempts to use them at the same time. QTEs are another example of suddenly inventing new game mechanics in the middle of the game, or the tutorial arbitrarily disabling features until it tells you to use them instead of letting the player play with them beforehand. If you're having to write 200 lines of special case code just to do one small thing, you need to rethink.

I feel like there's a severe lack of intuitiveness and cohesion which is a really bad thing to miss if you're taking as much inspiration from games like the Devil May Cry games as you are.In terms of gunplay, everything feels overkill. The "this will be graphics in da future!!" particle effects, the intense screen shake, the lack of usefulness of the handgun outside of the alt ammo melting every potentially interesting encounter, it just doesn't really feel great in practice. Titanfall 2 is a good place to look for that (and for the movement which is too scuffed for me to even want to get into.)The tutorials, visual prompts telling you where to go, QTEs, and the voices either telling me what's on the screen or how to progress feels really not great and unneeded for how intentional and straightforward all the level design is. Just cut like 90% of the dialogue and the visual prompts and let people take in the world. If dante threw out a "phew just wiped out this group of demons, better go to the right door to progress" with really stilted delivery every encounter I don't think i would've made it as far as i did. It's a preference thing in dmc5's case but it's one of the few things i didn't like was the amount of "walky and talky" for repeat playthroughs there was, and this game cranks that up to an 11 because it won't shut the ♥♥♥♥ up when i'm trying to do anything.overall this is certianly one of the most games i've ever taken the time to beat, but if you want a vaguely pretty game to try and validate you spending a ridiculous amount of money on a scalped 30 series, this game does just sorta throw a bunch of visual clutter and particles on the screen and jingle keys in ur face saying "wow lookee here it's just like devil may cry but first person and also guns"

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying I had a fair bit of fun with this game. I'm not upset by any means that I bought into Episode 1 and got this for free, and I think it's a decent showing for what started out as an entirely one person project. I deeply enjoyed the original demo and I even enjoyed this despite it's flaws. That said I feel that those flaws hold it back too much for me to recommend it to anyone as things stand. Even people I know would have fun with it.The good:The game is very pretty. It runs really well, and both the movement and the combat feel good. The ability to block, parry, and reflect attacks feels very good as well, and the fact that doing so refills ammo and suit energy is a great touch. All of the weapons feel like they have a place in your arsenal and aren't just there to fill up space. Some of the special attack skills you get I didn't really end up using but that to me felt more like my choice in which ones to unlock than anything else. The bad:The gameplay areas are very linear. More often than not you're fighting in a fairly tight corridor against a handful of guys with no real verticality or interesting features to speak of. You kill them, you move on to the next corridor. There's a handful of more interesting open area fights but I found myself missing the more open arenas of Episode 1 and the more DOOM like freedom you had to traverse the space in a fight. I also found myself missing some of the more interesting abilities of Episode 1 as well. While the gameplay feels good, the enemies are either useless cannon fodder that dies in a short burst or the beefiest bullet sponge to ever exist. There's not really any in between. I was playing on Revenge, the hardest initially available difficulty but I don't feel like that was the reason. Even most of the bosses boiled down to "Wait for the big telegraphed attack, parry, spam your hardest hitting weapon/ability, run away until the next big telegraphed attack." repeat until dead. Only one had any kind of mechanics you really needed to worry about. A couple had random ads that would spawn during the fight to complicate things, but that's really it. The verdict:It's not a bad game by any means, and it is very fun. I think the developer has a lot of potential and I hope they succeed. But as things stand just after launch and as much as I want to see more games with this type of gameplay I just can't recommend the game in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the original Bright Memory a couple years back while in early access, and as thanks I received Infinite for free upon release. I really enjoyed what was offered for the most part. The gameplay is fun, the visuals are incredible, story is a bit of a miss and could be fleshed out a lot more. Considering most if not all of this game's development was handled by a single person, then it truly is a feat to be applauded. If the dev is given the time and resources, I'm sure they will be able to make something incredible.However, considering that I completed the game on the 2nd hardest difficulty in less than 2 hours and the asking price is $20, I really can not recommend this at full price. I'd suggest waiting for a sale to try this out because it's something you will finish very quickly, and unless you care about achievements, there is little to no replay value. It feels like a huge chunk of the story is just missing. There's little to no explanation as to why most of the events in the game occurs. No backstory for the protagonist, or antagonist, or the enemies in general. You can piece an overarching plot together near the end which just boils down to "big bad want big powerful to rule the world mwahaha" and that's about it. The story ends on a bit of a cliffhanger so hopefully there's more in the works and I hope it gets added to this game for free to add more appeal to the $20 price tag.The boss fights are also a little lackluster. There are three bosses in total, one of which you fight twice in the game, with the other two basically feeling the same but one has more attacks to throw at you. They're all massive bullet sponges and can be defeated pretty easily by just circle strafing and unloading into them which is a shame as the spectacle is there. Perhaps if there was more of an incentive to use your abilities against them it could be more engaging. Grappling a boulder out their hand before they can throw it at you to stun them, maybe one of them becomes temporarily immune to gunfire so you have to use your sword. Simple stuff like that can really help spice up some of these fights.Overall, it's a pretty solid experience even though it's short. If you don't care about the length and money is no issue then by all means pick this up and enjoy it, the two hours on offer are pretty solid. However I really don't think the value is there if you want a longer, more fleshed out experience. Hopefully the dev keeps working and adding onto this release because there is massive potential here.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the first Bright Memory back in the day, this game is extremely underwhelming. Infinite is a game that tries to do too many things and ultimately fails at bringing out what could have been an amazing game while also not flushing out their story and gameplay. Infinite tries to sell itself as a game that involves guns + powers + stealth(?) + driving(?), the last two also only last for 1 mission which is forced upon the player to play through, along with their story of how a mysterious black hole that has appeared and is ripping things apart. The game which can also be completed within 2 hours is extremely short.    Except; nothing is really worth mentioning because all of that is never really flushed out. Your main villain(s) in the story have no background to them and their motive is literally just "I will become the new ruler of the world after it gets remade".  Your character and partner(?) are from an organization that is specialized in......nothing except having the latest technologies? There is no real story telling here which is what you would expect, so then what about the gameplay?    The gunplay while nice, falls off after the first 20 minutes or so. It becomes repetitive. It does not feel fun to shoot your weapons anymore which is part of the core gameplay. You smash that shoot button and literally that's it. Enemies line up for you. The tanks get shredded with a shotgun. Snipers can be 1 shot by you. The power ability is slightly better in terms of gameplay since you can do some midair plays that makes the game a little more fun but it's not enough to carry it. There is also a forced stealth mission that just forces you to crouch throughout the entire mission or you can just run through it since the stealth doesn't properly work with detection at all. After which you are forced into a driving mission which also is pretty bad as the moving left/right will turn your car almost 90 degree instantly and you have a locked camera that has about 70% of the screen filled with the interior of the car.     Bright Memory: Infinite is a game that is just not ready enough to be released. I got it for free as I bought the original back in the day but for those who spent money to buy this game, it is not worth it. If they held out for maybe another 2 year and put more effort into creating a decent story with decent characters and decided on how to flush out their gameplay more efficiently this game could have been much much better.

_childDocuments_.review: I regret to say that I cannot recommend this game. I had such high hopes for this game long before its release, but it has a few fatal weaknesses. It was extremely short in length, I usually take a lot longer than other people to finish a game, but even then it only took me 4 hours to complete. Glitches are plenty, and game breaking at times. I think I tend to be pretty forgiving with this, but I got stuck in the level's geometry multiple times without even going off the beaten path, forcing me to restart. The relic system could be explained better, I could not figure out what the blue orbs were for. There was no in game guide that I could revisit after the initial explanation, and I couldn't even find anything in Google to explain. Certain cut scene animations were stiff, and some dialogue sounded cheesy or forced. Although to be fair, the latter is a subjective opinion and maybe it was because I listened to it in English. The plot felt very shallow with little to no exposition on setting or characters, I didn't even care about most of what happened or if your helicopter buddy (Hack, I think?) died. Bright Memory Infinite had a lot of potential, I mean the game play mechanics alone can really make you feel like a swiss army knife badass with the options available to you. It is still really impressive that this was essentially done by one guy, and if this is what he pulls off alone then I look forward to what he can do with a team! I will treat this game as more of a tech demo for any possible future releases, and will keep an eye on the dev from now on.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, the gameplay is really fun and flows well, dodging is so intuitive that you'd be using it without thinking since it's bound to walking keys and shift, the guns are really nice and all have a unique fire mode how ever aiming is a bit clunky since if you hold the ads button then an animation plays, the gun won't ads after the animation, you'll have to release and press ads again. I also managed to get out of bounds by accident, this game has a fair amount of jank and it's short, but don't let that deter you, its worth it, I haven't experienced a game breaking bug and the game was incredibly fun, the sword combat is almost perfect, and the ground slash is the ultimate tool to deal with those pesky shields. _childDocuments_.review: I'm going to recommend this game, but not at the price it is at right now. I purchased Bright Memory, the precursor to this game, so I got Infinite for free. The game has great graphics, it ran steadily at 144 frames per second, and I only had one crash. A stutter here and there, but nothing major in any way. I beat this game in a little over 2 hours. I have been waiting for this game for a long time, and I commend them for not abandoning, but this is way shorter than I thought it would be.The graphics, animations, and features have all gotten a nice upgrade since the previous game, with the game including DLSS that works seamlessly. As for the game itself, it gets monotonous pretty quickly, but if you are more of the creative type, you will enjoy this more than I did. I'm the simple type that does what works which was always use a gun. The game gives you plenty  (a massive amount) of ammo and I never worried about running out. You are supposed to do perfect blocks and wear the enemy down with your blade, then kill them, but I mostly just used a gun. All enemies, including bosses can be gunned down without blocking. Which is a good thing, really, play the game the way you want. If you like using everything you've got, all the moves, all the powers, all the different types of ammo and explosives and guns, then you will definitely enjoy this.In short, is this a bad game? No, not at all. Is it a good game? Yes, yes it is. Is it a great game? That's debatable. What I can say, though, is I don't think it is worth the $20 price tag it has launched with.

detailed_description: More Games About the Game The spider - mankind’s most ancient and deadly nemesis. As a licensed Kill It With Fire exterminator, it’s time to fight back! Assemble your arsenal of increasingly excessive weapons, track spiders across suburbia, and burn everything in your path! To defeat spiders you must exploit their one weakness: FIRE. Or bullets. Or explosions, throwing stars, gettin’ smushed by stuff...pretty much anything, really. But that doesn’t mean it’ll be easy - first you’ve gotta find the spiders. Use state-of-the-art arachnid tracking technology to pinpoint your target's location among hundreds of potential hiding spots - then, torch everything and smash the spider with a frying pan after it runs out. It’s the only way to be sure. Features Tons of unique weapons and equipment. Eight different spider species. “Realistic” fire simulation system. Gratuitous chaos and destruction. Dozens of optional objectives. Loads of hidden upgrades. Battle in the Arachno-Gauntlet! A secret ending?!?! (...shh!)

_childDocuments_.review: Do you see a spider? Kill it with fire!Out of ammunition? Don’t be shy! Then just kill it with a frying pan, a laser sword, an anvil or any item you can find around. I know, you wanna do it… just don’t get used to these killing methods. You really don’t want to use a RPG against a spider crawling out of a dark corner of your home. 5-6h, no serious grind required, this is actually the playtime the game offers with all the challenges needed to be done. 3/10. It is possible that at the first time you will think that some Arachno-Gauntlets challenges on the levels are hard. Then you will unlock the energy drink utility item. Nope, you won’t get wings, but the world will slow down around you. Now hitting fast crawling spiders with shurikens suddenly starts to be an option:-) Yes, there is one for achievements, one for collectibles. Those not properly updated tho, now some extra weapons and abilities earned on last level when decorating the christmas tree there. This action is required for the 4 “get all” types of achievements and not mentioned in the guides.The gameplay is quite simple. Kill spiders with various weapons, utility items or anything available on the level. Reach a set kill amount to open the door to progress to the next level.That is not all though, each level has many alternative and funny tasks, the areas and the items you can find around are destructible, and just like in any games, there are some secrets, hidden rooms and some very basic puzzles.As you progress on your spider killing adventure you will find new weapons, upgrades and bonuses, these will aid you in your pest control mission:-) Some of these upgrades offer alternate game experience, like tiny mode which makes you just as huge as the spiders (yeah, that mode is scary:-D).While you can’t take any damage, so this is a fun oriented, humorous game, the only thing still missing for me is a fight at the end against some bigger, mutant spider.Relatively short game, fairly priced and actually quite funny and entertaining. The playtime is just enough and probably a longer game would just repeat itself and could become boring. 7/10 6/10, dont not start it with a headset and adjust volume, else you will be deaf, and turn off jumpscare sound effects if you have problems with your heart. 8/10. Do not play the game while suffering from arachnophobia. 3/10,  zero on win10 I think I not played any similar games yet but you don’t need any other game to know what can you expect, just try the free demo first:

_childDocuments_.review: Okay I have one massive complaint to get out of the way first: why is there no lose condition? The spiders are clearly a threat, like, a "destroy at all cost" threat, as evidenced by the Omega files. But in game they're all... harmless? Even the one that jumps at you can't even hurt you, it's just a cheap (but effective) jumpscare. Once you get used to the spiders all fear factor is gone, in a game designed to incite arachnophobia. When a spider vanishes it isn't panic inducing, it's just an inconvenience. The spiders are clearly meant to be threatening, but they just. Aren't. Threats. But this game isn't about living in fear of the spiders. It's about exterminating them with extreme prejudice. No matter how many times I cover an entire room from floor to ceiling with gasoline and light 'er up, or sprinkle C4 throughout an entire level and kill every single arachnid ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with a single detonation, burn a pregnant queen alive and watch her entire brood burn alive the second they burst out of the womb, or simply just whack a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with a frying pan, it just never gets old. A lot of the weapons are just useless (The vacuum's nearly harmless, A lot of guns can't aim for ♥♥♥♥, the weedwhacker is useless when it has the same range as the frying pan, etc.) but every one is at least novel. You're never going to realistically need the suicide bomber drone, but it's still a suicide bomber drone, you know what I mean?This whole "extermination" thing is kinda undermined when you only have to kill around 50% of the spiders in a level to leave, there's no penalty for leaving some alive and no reward for getting every single one. Not even an achievement, just nothing. I get that it's hard to be thorough at the start when all you have is a clipboard and a useless spider tracker, but come on, leave a reward for those that decide to go all the way. Upgrades are found through collectibles across the various levels and completing tasks, but if you REALLY want them you need to put your bloodlust aside for a moment to search thoroughly. You've got pretty much no chance of finding or accomplishing anything once you trash the place. It seems antithetical to the game's design but it gives an excuse to reply levels so it isn't too bad.That's all I really have for the game, it's just a fun silly goofy time where you enact a systemic genocide of all spider-kind.

_childDocuments_.review: /əˌraknəˈfəʊbɪə/extreme or irrational fear of spiders.According to Wikipedia, arachnophobia affects around 3.5 to 6.1 percent of the global population. Out of 7.9 billion humans, that percentage equals a lot, making it one of the most common phobias out there. So what does this game do? It take that phobia, amplify it ten times, but at the same time they gave you an arsenal of weaponry that is enough to supply a small army. Welcome... to Kill It With Fire.Kill It With Fire is played from a first person perspective, which I despise because it makes the scares much more effective. Looking at the screenshots, the game appears to be a sandbox game which you're given free reign to incite chaos everywhere. While that is true, half of the game is played more akin to a hidden object game as a good chunk of the game's objectives, collectibles and upgrades are hidden in plain sight. The main enemy of this game is of course, the spiders. They are literally everywhere: inside a pizza box, behind a picture frame, underneath crops, etc; if it's an object, there's a good chance these bastards are sticking on it. To make things worse, there are different types of spiders with each one exhibiting a unique power such as the Zombie Spider that can revives previously dead spiders, Jumping Spider that likes to leap quickly to your face (this one's the worst for me), and Exploding Spider that, well... explodes. Fortunately, the game is kind enough to provide you with a tracker that allows you to monitor these creatures very, very carefully.On to the weapons. The wacky selection of available weaponry that I can use to bring down hell onto these spiders is very versatile. It definitely reminds me a little bit of the Dead Rising games where you can pick up the most mundane of objects and use it as a deadly killing machine. From the humble frying pan to the rapid-firing assault rifle to the exquisite saw launcher, there's a weapon that can cater to everyone's playstyle. In fact, there's a whole category of weapons that is solely dedicated to causing fire such as the flamethrower, C4 and the freaking lightsaber (or laser sword because copyright). There are a total of 10 levels in the game ranging from the backyard of a house to a gas station. Each of them are brimmed with details and filled with hundreds of items that can be pick up, examined and rotated around. Level design is absolutely fantastic. Never once do I felt like the levels are copy-and-pasted as each one have their own recognizable identity. Some levels even provide shortcuts to the starting area, preventing you from getting lost.  Every level also have their own selected set of objectives, collectibles (in the form of batteries) and upgrades scattered around. Completing the objectives and collecting the batteries give you points that you can use to upgrade yourself and your tracker. This is where the hidden object aspect of the game came into play. I do admit that I used a guide for this one as some of these are fairly well-hidden. You really have to search every nook and cranny to 100% this game.Yes, there is a story in the game. They're presented as snippets of breadcrumbs by finding the Omega Files and through environmental storytelling in the levels. In a nutshell, It took me around 10 hours to complete the main game and get around 80% of all of the extra content. After that, I used a guide to collect everything else that pushes the playtime to 13 hours in total. As for replayability, there's a big potential. The game is a great stress reliever and serves well as one of those 'pick up and play for half an hour' kind of games.Kill It With Fire exist for one purpose: to give you endless amount of way to inflict endless amount of pain onto the eight-legged creatures. The rest of the factors; graphics, music, animations, etc are serviceable at best. But that's completely fine, as the game's main attraction is the pure gameplay, and Kill It With Fire executed it excellently.

_childDocuments_.review: Kill It With Fire is a rather simple game, where you fool yourself around some static locations and kill spiders that are infesting all the world around.It is very short, and with every new level, you'll be unlocking some new equipment - read 'the ways for a complete spider extermination'.The spiders can't fight back! There is no way to get a Game Over which makes your 'fight' a pure spider-o-cide. Don't think you're a good guy around. You wreak havoc and destruction. It is fun, though.The level of destruction is noticeable, but nothing really exaggerating. Despite the fact that you can't lose, you need some aiming skill and fast thinking, to get some of the challenges aka 'gauntlets', when your actions are strictly limited by the time limit.So, to summarize: it's another simple and quick game to complete for achievements, if you care for that stuff, or just let off some steam, destroying some furniture and whatnot to get some little annoying posters. Plus, some cheap Steam cards. I don't think you need to rush for it, especially for the full price, but if you get it via some bundle or big sale - it's not a bad game to have, after all! Nothing too fancy, of course, my mark is 5.6/10, but... it's definitely not some shovelware. Just a small game for some silly joy, for an hour or so. Oh, and you can always get the overall impression just by downloading a demo version, a 'teaser', from the game's store page.

_childDocuments_.review: Kill It With Fire~~~~~~~~~~~~Kill it with fire is a fun FPS. The game’s world revolves around the premise that there are spiders everywhere and you must hunt them down. It’s a fun, light-hearted game with some unique concepts. Right from the get-go, you will be thrown into a locked section of a house, landmark, or outdoor venue, and your goal will be to exterminate the critters hiding around and while doing so you will have to perform some tasks, riddles, collect items, etc.  Plot: Spiders . . . mankind’s ancient nemesis, deadly and sneaky; as a licensed exterminator, you have been given free rein to go around and exterminate these sneaky critters by any means necessary. Assemble your armory and go to war. Burn down everything that dares to cross your path; a bit of expensive property damages won’t hurt.Gameplay:  Kill It With Fire’s whole gameplay is based around simple traditional FPS machines with quite a few fun tricks up its sleeve. In the beginning, you will be wielding a Clipboard; the most used and important item in-game. As you progress on each stage, more and more tasks will appear on the board for you to complete. As you complete each task, more rooms and areas will be unlocked for you to venture into. Each task and each room/area will bring in new possibilities, weapons, ammo, puzzles, etc. Apart from a few general tasks like collecting items, the rest of the tasks are unique and fun. For example, one of the tasks was to deal with a spider species they call jumping spiders. These little critters are tricky to deal with when you see them, they jump a good distance and then tracking them down in a messed up room was a hoot and a half.  In the beginning, you will come across a spider tracker, which works as a radar; at first, it seems kinda pointless because if you’re in a small room, you can clearly hear the spider making noise. However, as you progress through the different areas and upgrade your radar, things become more interesting as the radar does a lot of the work for you. Being without the radar in the later stages of the game would have been a nightmare. Progressing through each stage requires a few tasks to be completed, such as exterminating a number of spiders, exterminating a selected species of spider, items collection, riddles, puzzles, damaging selected items, etc.As you progress, you will start to earn points and unlock upgrades, and the trackers upgrade. Each upgrade brings in different state boosts for both you and your handy tracker, such as gel for back pain relief and a Sigma module for providing your tracker with a better display.As you browse through the menu, you will be shown how many tasks to complete before unlocking the next stage. A fine addition to the menu UI that I would like to mention is Equipment, which displays your unlocked gears and weapons. Weapons: From a simple Clipboard to C4 explosives, Kill It With fire is providing players with many options to go through. As you progress throughout the game you will come across a lot of unique weapons either out in the open or hidden around and behind objects, closets, doors, etc. which makes the game more interesting and exploration fun. This system of exploration kept my interest peaked for hours until I messed up the rooms. The wide selection of weapons and explosives in this game are unique and hilarious, as you won’t use most of these while trying to hunt down a tiny critter. For an example of how ridiculous things get in-game, you will get to use an Assault rifle, C4 explosives, Molotov’s and Shotguns, setting the whole place on fire with a jerry can full of gas, etc.It’s ridiculous, it’s funny, and combined with how one thing interacts with the others makes things more insane. Arsenal management and selecting seemed easy enough with Q to access the inventory, and clicking 2-5 while an item is selected to equip it. And as you progress, you will unlock more slots to assign weapons to. World design: Colorful, light-hearted, well-polished world design. The playable areas are each unique and well designed, and each comes with its own flair and fun elements. Some stages are set in a small room and others in and around a large gas station. Other than a few minor graphical hiccups, the world looks good and the game runs well. Considering all aspects of the game, Kill It With Fire turned out to be as it was promised, a fun casual FPS, set in a colorful world, and the game offers an enjoyable gameplay full of critters to crush, burn, shoot, fry, stab, RPG, etc. Other than a few graphical hiccups at the very beginning where items seemed burned even though I didn’t have any weapons on me, and the fact that the game is short and needs more content updates, I have nothing to complain about; and the game provides as promised.Positives: + Fun gameplay+ Colorful world design + Variety of weapons to go through + Fun puzzles and riddles + Good selection of music and sound effects + Variety of spiders to crush Negatives: - Minor Graphical hiccups at the beginning - Short game; needs more content Hunt down humankind’s ancient nemesis, the spiders. You have been given free rein to burn, destroy, and crush everything . . . this is war! (A bit of expensive property damage won’t hurt!) 8/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: I say we take off, nuke the site from orbit. It's the only way to be sure. But since that wouldn't make for a good game, burning the house and neighborhood down will have to do.This is proof that taking a simple meme and just going with it can end up in an really fun game. Going from room to room leaving nothing but destruction and little eight legged corpses behind has something really satisfying and almost therapeutic.The low-poly art style is just enough to almost trigger my arachnophobia, make me feel slightly uneasy, or flinch when a spider jumps straight at my face. But anything more would too much. If I wanted spiders that make me scream, look away, and Alt-F4 asap I'd book a vacation in Australia once tourism is an option again. The sound design and music are absolutely on point, specially the changes in music when you get closer and closer to a spider that thinks it's clever and can hide. I only hope that evolution never gets around to produce spiders that are this loud and produce those nightmare inducing sounds.There's some thing that might be nice to see in an future update or DLC:- VR support. Not that I have the hardware, but this almost begs for it.- While spiders are an easy target due to their high position on the phobia scale, what about wasps, roaches, ants, ...- Challenge modes and leader boards. E.g. lowest collateral damage, fastest time, ...- A map editor and Workshop integration.If you are still undecided I'd say play Heatwave or the demo and play the first three levels for free. _childDocuments_.review: After 100% the whole game, this is what I got...Anything has to do with spiders is fantastic.The weapons, trackers, upgrades are just fun to mess around with even though you could just fry-pan everything in your way.This game just gives you the tools to go all out just to kill some spiders.With that being said... Everything that DOESN'T involve spiders is rough, sometimes.Lets talk performance first, I played 12 hours with V-Sync off because it made my frames die on the inside. So half my screen was trying to escape from the other half, the whole time (you just get used to it).Although the music was BANGIN, for some reason, the main menu music was waaaaaaay too loud.I streamed the game, so I literally had to change the game audio every time I ended up at the main menu.(Every time I booted the game, the music would jumpscare me)The objectives were cool, it gave some specific ways to KILL spiders or it required so other things.Some objectives either required too much, too long, or worse... BOTHThe shotgun as a weapon sucks... But then you add the "kill 2 spiders with one blast" mission and you die on the inside (Pssssssssst, get the energy drink from future levels first, then come-back).Don't get me started on the cut the lawn mission, where I had to do it twice (there's an achievement, too, that shoulda triggered the first time).weird bug that happened three times (on 3 separate attempts) where on the same level, the tracker would tell me that there's a spider inside an object but no matter what, it would not die.Now I do like me some collecting, but there's just waaaaaay too many things to collect in a game where I just want to murder some toxic spiders before they zombify other dead spiders.I catch myself sometimes and get a moment of awareness that I'm doing more collecting (Christmas light, batteries, upgrades, collecting for specific missions) more so than actually killing the spiders.(Yeah, I know, some give you really cool things but damn... Just remove the batteries and that might solve it).The spiders themselves are REALLY cool (some are clearly weak... I'm looking at you web-spider)But it made me approach certain ones with caution.Regarding AI... I don't like the spiders just expose themselves when I'm just near the area doing objectives. Most the time, I didn't know they were there because the objectives are soooo demanding, so I just get a free kill.Other AI thing is when you're unable to kill them and they try to hide again so you follow them to their next hiding spot but then POOF... They disappear under an object and re-appear somewhere else.I didn't like that since you can't really get the jump on them again or follow them if you miss your shot.I think everybody in the S T O R Y is dead since you can't see anyone.Gibs, for some odd reason, came back after skipping town just to hire you and then disappear again (prolly dead)... Speaking of dead. We die at the end and then we get to play as the co-worker? Since there's an empty office.Unless you're a cockroach and survived the nuke, then you're GONE.Which now we have a roach problem. Is that why the alien spiders want our help?"Oh, even though your friend killed us, we need your help against these roaches."Is that where the story is headed? Or is it just killing the rest of the spiders... IN SPACEidk, cool game overall. I know I was dogging it but that's how I felt.Everything with the spiders is cool and the rest just left me perplexed, often.Loved the modifiers (that Australia and Tiny mode combo IS NASTY) loved the tracker upgrades, the self upgrades, the weapons. Even though some parts were tedious, they always unlocked some new for you to toy 'round with, which is why I kept doing them.Can't wait for da zequel... With a z.It really made me feel like Batman.

_childDocuments_.review: The novelty wears off.At the first, the game is pretty fun and interesting - you get some laughs, you get some fun, you figure out what you're doing. Things start to escalate, and your still having fun... but then you'll hit a point where you'll stop and go 'What am I actually doing?'. The game play, at it's core, is just 'pick up objects, rotate them until spider is detected, then proceed to kill spider with increasingly zany weapons'. Puzzles and challenges are interspersed but they all amount to 'pick up objects, walk them over to the right area, then put them down'.And it's just not a recipe for a long amount of fun. I lasted an hour. The core game play is just not varied enough to make it worth the time or money.I'd improve it by adding risk of some kind and more environmental effects/methods. The spiders can't actually do anything to you except 'blind' you with a little web every now and then, and it just means there's no real challenge to anything; and actually killing the spiders is boring as hell after a short while, even with the increasingly ridiculous weapons.5/10, it was okay I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: Funny casual game where you need to kill all spiders. To find them all, you'll literally have to turn each stone, open all drawers and move all furniture. Luckily you'll find lots of stuff to help you. There's a spider-scanner with plenty of possible upgrades, and you'll find better weapons after a while, going from an improvised flamethrower to a shotgun and molotov's. There's no need to be careful of the environment, so putting things on fire is often the most effective (and most satisfying) way to kill spiders.Each level also has several objectives, which you need to complete to unlock new stuff. Some of these objectives are clever puzzles, but most of them are rather boring and repetitive. More creativity and funny ideas could have made this game so much better! Still, Kill it with Fire is fun to play in short bursts, especially if you hate spiders and love to see them burning. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I have never had a good working relationship with spiders. Outside, we coexist for the most part, but inside, we wage war. I do appreciate their efforts to take on other pests, but that’s like putting out a fire with a grenade. Kill It With Fire instead gives you the fire and the grenade and lets you make all the aggressive moves. Now you’re playing the Predator and focusing your three-dot laser scope on the eight-legged nuisance that has seemingly taken over the world.Abbreviated Review:  As a member of the Kill It With Fire Exterminators company, you singlehandedly are responsible for removing seemingly limitless spiders from households and businesses. There isn’t a lot of explanation for what exactly is going on in this environment. It is devoid of any other humans, though it seems they just left. Signs of life are everywhere, but the only things still moving are spiders.Kill It With Fire is split up into nine levels, each of which is relatively small. They do seem a little larger at first since you don’t have a sprint function until you unlock it. Each level provides you with a checkbox list of tasks to do, but virtually none are required to finish the game. The only thing necessary to reach the exit of each level is killing the requisite number of spiders. Several doors have this same requirement throughout each level. The more spiders you kill, the more rooms you can access.While you can skip out on many of the checkboxes, most can be marked off by doing what you’d normally do. Usually, at least one task is simply to kill “X” number of spiders of a certain type. Completing all of the objectives for a level has more effects though. Sometimes it will unlock special crates containing new weapons. Finishing them all gives you the option to tap a boom box and start “Arachno-Gauntlet” challenges where you have to accomplish a task in a set time limit. These usually require using specific weapons and tools in the process.The weapons and tools you unlock are often the most enjoyable parts of Kill It With Fire. It seems like that was one of the primary goals for the design of the game. Though you can easily make progress falling back on any handful of weapons, even the clipboard you started with. The frying pan became my go-to weapon since it was both effective and didn’t require any ammo. However, it didn’t stop me from using nearly all of them liberally.There were points in the game where you were required to use certain weapons such as for the main objectives or challenges. Some of these were a breeze to get through while others were seemingly impossible. Only after you unlock the “energy drink” item can you easily complete some of the tougher ones. The most difficult challenges required you to hit these tiny spider-sized spiders with guns as they zipped across floors and objects. The time-slowing property of the energy drink was the only way I was able to be successful with these.The precision aim requirements for most guns can be rough but overall aren’t too detrimental to Kill It With Fire. I ultimately found myself getting much better at using them after some practice. However, the real fun is in things like the flame-throwing spray can/lighter combo and the rocket launcher. Tools like these, the Molotov cocktails, C4, and even the somewhat random weed eater were a blast to mess around with as I hunted down those sneaky arachnids.There are a variety of spiders in the game, ranging from regular black ones to red ones that explode like a grenade when they die. Mixed in are queen spiders that spawn babies when killed and web spiders that launch webs at your face causing temporary blindness. These, among other interesting designs, are all fun to track down and obliterate with all of your tools. The issue is that they can’t do anything to you. In fact, nothing at all can.While it’s sometimes nice to have a game that’s not all about dying to enemies, it feels a bit out of place in Kill It With Fire. I had the expectation going in that, maybe the early spider opponents wouldn’t do damage, but later ones would. That was not the case. There isn’t even collateral damage from nearby explosions. There’s no player health to speak of. I feel like the game could have had a great deal more depth (and probably longevity) if it explored a fail state that involved surviving deadly spiders.The result is that Kill It With Fire presents a fun experience for its limited run time, but you can easily reach the end and do practically all of the extra stuff without breaking a sweat. You’ll make it there in a matter of a few hours. Then you’re left with little to do but revisiting old levels with all your gear. That doesn’t provide much additional entertainment. As it stands, Kill It With Fire is worth playing through, but it might be hard to justify doing that even at its fairly low price. If you have $15 to throw around though, it’s an experience that doesn’t fail to entertain, even without a lasting effect.

_childDocuments_.review: "Kill it with Fire" is a first-person action game developed and published by Casey Donnellan Games LLC. The game is all about finding and killing spiders in different environments using an arsenal of weapons and tools.The plot of the game is fairly simple, and there isn't much of a story to speak of. The game is more focused on the gameplay experience of hunting down and exterminating spiders. While the lack of a deeper plot may disappoint some players, it's not necessarily a deal-breaker for a game like  terms of gameplay, "Kill it with Fire" offers a fun and engaging experience. The game is designed around the concept of hunting spiders, and it delivers on that premise with a wide range of tools and weapons to choose from. The controls are easy to learn, and the game offers a satisfying sense of progression as you unlock new items and upgrades.One of the highlights of "Kill it with Fire" is the game's presentation. The graphics are bright and colorful, and the game's environments are well-designed and filled with interactive objects to discover. The spiders themselves are well-animated and realistically creepy, which adds to the tension and excitement of the gameplay.The music in "Kill it with Fire" is also worth noting. The game's soundtrack is suitably tense and atmospheric, which helps to build up the tension as you hunt down spiders. The sound effects are also well-done, with the various weapons and tools sounding appropriately satisfying as you use them.However, there are a few negatives to consider when playing "Kill it with Fire". The game can feel repetitive at times, with the same basic gameplay loop of hunting down spiders and destroying their nests repeating itself over and over again. Additionally, some of the environments can feel a bit bland and uninspired, with little variation in the layout or design.Overall, "Kill it with Fire" is a fun and engaging game that offers a unique and enjoyable gameplay experience. While it may not be the deepest or most complex game out there, it's certainly worth checking out for fans of action and adventure games.

_childDocuments_.review: 8,5/10Spiders, small eight-legged carnivorous beings known as arachnids that can be found in a wide variety of sizes, colors, habits and almost everywhere in the world. People's relationship with these beings is varied, some like them, others are indifferent, some don't pay attention because they are part of the cycle of nature and while others don't like them at all and try to kill them at first sight, but for those who can't or don't want to even come close, there are Exterminators, people paid to eliminate undesirable beings like spiders. ^^This is the case of our protagonist, an Exterminator hired for what seemed like it would be just another typical case of eliminating some spiders in a typical suburban house, but little did he know that the situation was much worse than he thought, with a real infestation of several and the most varied species of spiders. Therefore, it is necessary to use unconventional methods to carry out the service, such as fire, firearms, explosives and many others, which really made me worry whether the owner of the house has insurance that covers all types of damage that were caused, in the hunt for the terrible spiders. ^^+ A simple but really addictive and fun game.+ A vast arsenal of classic weapons and others that are not normal to use to eliminate spiders.+ Various species of eight-legged beings to eliminate, each with their own unique abilities and sounds.+ Various improvements that can be found throughout the stages to help in the hunt against the little creepy beings.+ Environments that can be destroyed without any remorse, after all, anything goes to find and eliminate the spiders in this game.+ It's perfectly possible to return later in a level, with a bigger and better arsenal to finish all the challenges you weren't able to do before.- Unfortunately, even if you find all the points to spend on improvements, it is not possible to have them all at the same time.- Even with the improvement that allows the finder to find useful items, sometimes it can be very difficult to find them, as some are really well hidden.- Some of the challenges during the levels are really difficult, requiring several attempts in my case.In this way our work begins, having to eliminate the spiders but also carry out some somewhat dubious work, which begins within a humble house but soon expands to other locations with their secrets and objectives, in the hunt for beings with eight legs. Furthermore, as we explore we also find new ones, some normal, others not recommended if used at home to eliminate spiders, but our client only specified that he wanted the spiders eliminated, he did not specify how, so the player can use literally any method they wish. ^^Along with the objectives and small beings, we can also find items that release improvements throughout the phase, some just aesthetic, others items like the improved detector, and others very useful like infinite ammunition, the improvements can be equipped and removed at any time, between phases, then they are at the player's discretion. Another highlight are the challenges, each level has a different challenge that can be done after completing all the objectives, the first ones are simpler but as the stages progress they become more complex and difficult, even need to complete all the challenges to being able to do the final challenge and see the true ending. ^^Produced by the Casey Donnellan Games studio, the game features somewhat simple graphics as is clearly visible in round objects that have several straight lines but are well done, portraying well the different scenarios, weapons and species of spiders that we can find, in addition to the fire and destruction effects of the scenery, which are always caused by the player. As for the soundtrack, nothing I would call spectacular, but pleasant to listen to, the game even has a sound effect that plays whenever a spider enters the player's visual field, which can be deactivated if desired. ^^Kill It With Fire was a funny case for me, because in fact my first contact was with the Demo of the sequel, after that I decided to give the first one a chance and I must say, I had a lot of fun looking for the arachnid beings for each thing, while the story and the weapons that were released were getting more and more crazier, all with the aim of eliminating these little furry beings that can cause so much headache, although I must admit that the destruction I caused was much greater than any that the spiders had made. Anyway, it's a game that I recommend, very crazy, chaotic and fun and I can't wait for the sequel that will be released soon, which just from the Demo, I could already see will be even crazier and full of spiders. ^^

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, it's a pretty silly game. Yes it's very short. No, it's not particularly challenging. But there is something about chasing after spiders with a hairspray flamethrower that's a pile of fun.I'm a big fan of escalation in video games, where you think a game can't top itself just before it does exactly that. The missions in Kill It With Fire definitely follow the pattern, moving from silly little rooms to complex environments jammed with moving pieces. The weapon progression also perfectly nails escalation absurdity, upgrading from household objects to army surplus and beyond. I could hardly wait to unlock each new, shinier, shootier toy.Because that's what Kill It With Fire is: a toybox. The puzzles and goals are amusing enough and lead to some pretty hilarious levels, but it's ultimately about experimenting and playing in your dumb spider sandbox. I don't know if everyone is gonna appreciate this game, but  certainly appreciate Kill It With Fire, and that's what counts.

_childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend this game for any experienced gamer.While fun at first the game doesn't hold up for very long.While I found the story and theme interesting, the core gameplay feels like doing chores in a mess that you yourself made.Very rarely did I feel like I was experiencing the game's fantasy of being a unhinged exterminator.It just doesn't play as fun as it is to watch.This game is more of a look for hidden objects and clues sort of game, which isn't exactly what I signed up for when I got this.However I would recommend this game for people who are more new to games, as there is are no real dangers or risks of failure and the scares are ultimately harmless and even funny at times.The one thing that does keep me interested in the game is the story and how they use level design to build narrative tension.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for July 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before August 3rd, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Spiders everywhere.  This doesn’t look like a horror game, but it sure plays like one.  I’m not arachnophobic but this game had me jumping early on, and there’s no way to die or no chance of failure, but, damn it, they still got me, so if you hate spiders this is probably not for you. At the same time, Kill It With Fire is oddly fun, there are a lot of different weapons, items, collectibles, as well as secrets, and locations to explore.  Players can move almost anything and there are multiple different quests per level, only a couple are related to the spiders themselves.  I found myself enjoying this game as time went on.  The push to find everything, complete everything, and kill more spiders was enjoyable, and once I got the hair spray flamethrower, I no longer was scared of the spiders but was having fun wrecking a house. Pick this up if you want a dumb fun game, I think they could have gone more in the direction of scoring how much destruction you did while destroying the house.  I also appreciate the arachnophobia settings, but at the end of the day, you’re killing insects, namely spiders, so if that will skeeve you out, this is not for you.   Truthfully it’s probably the reason I won’t return, but I was never one for horror games or even pseudo horror games.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Introduction (3.5/5):"Kill It With Fire," developed by Casey Donnellan Games LLC and released in 2020, is a first-person action game that turns arachnophobia into an absurd and humorous experience. With its over-the-top approach to spider extermination and a variety of unconventional weapons, the game aims to entertain while providing an outlet for those with a fear of eight-legged creatures.Graphics and Presentation (3.5/5):The game employs a cartoonish and colorful visual style that complements its comedic theme. The environments are varied, ranging from suburban homes to offices, each filled with destructible objects and, of course, spiders. While the graphics may not be cutting-edge, they effectively serve the game's comedic atmosphere.Gameplay Mechanics (3.5/5):"Kill It With Fire" offers simple and accessible gameplay mechanics centered around the satisfying destruction of spiders. Players are equipped with an array of weapons, from everyday items like books and frying pans to more extreme choices like flamethrowers and explosives. The controls are intuitive, allowing players to easily unleash chaos on the arachnid invaders.Spider Variety and Challenges (3/5):The game features a variety of spider species, each with its own behavior and challenges. Some spiders are fast and agile, while others may explode upon contact. The diversity in spider types adds a layer of strategy as players adapt their extermination techniques to different arachnid threats.Mission Structure (3/5):The game follows a mission-based structure, with players tasked to eliminate spiders within specific environments. Missions range from simple spider hunts to more complex challenges, adding variety to the gameplay. While the objectives may become repetitive over time, the absurdity of the missions keeps them entertaining.Weapon Upgrades and Collectibles (3/5):As players progress, they can unlock and upgrade an arsenal of weapons to exterminate spiders more efficiently. Collectibles such as hidden objects and spider-related achievements add an extra layer of exploration and replayability. However, the upgrades may not drastically alter the core gameplay.Humor and Absurdity (4/5):"Kill It With Fire" excels in delivering humor through its absurd premise and over-the-top reactions to spider encounters. From the exaggerated fear of the protagonist to the comical weapons at their disposal, the game successfully turns arachnophobia into a source of laughter.Sound Design (3/5):The sound design contributes to the comedic atmosphere, featuring amusing spider noises, quirky background music, and humorous voice lines from the protagonist. While not groundbreaking, the sound elements enhance the overall lightheartedness of the game.Replayability (3/5):The game offers moderate replayability, particularly for players who enjoy completing challenges, finding collectibles, and experimenting with different weapons. The short mission structure and the limited variety in objectives may impact long-term engagement.Performance and Technical Aspects (3.5/5):"Kill It With Fire" generally performs well, with smooth controls and minimal technical issues. However, some players may encounter minor bugs or glitches that, while not game-breaking, can affect the overall polish of the experience.Overall (3.4/5):"Kill It With Fire" successfully combines humor, absurdity, and arachnid annihilation in a quirky first-person action game. While its mission structure and objectives may become repetitive over time, the game's comedic approach and variety of weapons make it an entertaining experience, especially for those looking for a lighthearted way to confront their fear of spiders.

_childDocuments_.review: Gotta be honest, at first I wasn't sure what to think about this game. I figured it'd be fun for 10 minutes and then I'd move on. But honestly, I found myself quite enjoying to blow up spiders with a ridicoulus amount of weapons at my disposal and absolutely not paying any mind to my surroundings. Blowing up a gasstation to get rid of some spiders? Oh yeah absolutely! I ended up kind of forgetting the time with this game, even tho the game itself is not very long, only 9 levels in total, I was fully immersed, doing sidequests and killing as many spiders as possible in very creative ways.As someone who's terribly afraid of spiders, it was nice to feel sort of overpowered against them for once. I'd definitely recommend this if you're into silly games or short fun experiences. Might not be yours if you like fully fleshed out long games with an indepth story. Although I must say, this game did sort of have a story too, which was a nice suprise.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this as part of a recent monthly Humble Bundle. I assumed it would be bad; I was pleasantly surprised. For what it is, it is fun. While I didn't complete all the achievements, I made it to the end of the game in perhaps 5 hours. If you hate spiders, love to set things on fire, and cause mayhem, this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Burning room of fireSpidey senses:Is it a bird? Is it a plane? No, it's a Spider! Upon starting this game, I quickly realised its charm from the suburban feeling of the first level, to the grandiose soundtrack, which was when I realised the treat I was in for.Spy-der story:You may think a game about killing spiders doesn't have much of a story, if any at all and you'd be right to think that. The game is purely just kill said spiders to progress to the next stage of the game; however while there may not be a plot per-se, that doesn't mean there isn't a bigger arc going on here. In fact, the ending surprised me in a way I never could have seen coming. There are eight files that delve a bit into the story to make the world feel a bit more lived in but not much else.Take it for a spin:Now we get into the meat and potatoes, by which I mean the gameplay. The premise is simple; Start a level, get a weapon and whack some spiders. You start the game with no weapons at all but promptly find a clipboard, acting as your first weapon and your objectives list for the level. Soon after, you will be tasked with finding the spider tracker (think the EMF reader from Ghostbusters and you're golden) which will help you inconsistently track them down at first.During your playthrough, you will come across a plethora of weapons, from frying pans, to an assault rifle and RPG, (yes, you read that correctly) to the downright strange in balloons and cheese puffs. It all works fairly well but when using the majority of guns, I found it quite indecisive and hard to hit your targets as you are trying to hit a target that moves like the wind and is roughly a couple of centimetres long after all; I mean, have you tried to bullseye a womp rat in a T-16? It's not easy. With all those weapons at my disposal, I did find myself using the frying pan the majority of the time due to its sheer size and hitbox radius, making the guns a bit less relevant.Your main goal of every level is to kill spiders, naturally. You need to kill a certain amount of these eight legged menaces to access different sections within the stage. Each level comes with a variety of optional tasks to attempt and they are a fun way to break away from the main goal of the game, with objectives such as destroying all of the dishes in the kitchen, to scanning $100 dollars worth of shopping at the supermarket. Completing them all unlocks the Arachno-Gauntlet which is a challenge where you have to kill as many spiders as you can within a set time limit with a specified weapon. Aside from being fun, the best reason to finish all the tasks would be the upgrade points you receive which you can use to purchase...well, upgrades. Some are useful whereas others didn't seem to bring anything major to the table.We can't talk about this game without talking about the spiders themselves, and during your playthrough you will come across nine different variations, each with their own quirks. Some just scuttle around giving you that uneasy feeling, whereas some fill your screen with webs, others can leap towards the screen, while some even explode (Michael bay would be proud). Whether you're a full on arachnophobe or just slightly phased, Kill it with fire genuinely does a good job of making you shiver at the sight of finding a spider on the back of a photo frame; so much so that there is actually an arachnophobia setting so you can mute the shrieks they make as well as completely get rid of the scarier variants of spider.Web design:The first time I booted the game up, my mind immediately went to a spy movie as the jazzy sounds bellowed through my ears. Whilst in game, as you unlock new rooms or find a new weapon, the music turns into a kind of superhero-esque style, similar to the cartoon Batman screen transitions (If you know, you know). While I did enjoy the over the top style of music, I did find it obnoxiously loud, even after turning the music volume right down to the point of almost turning it off completely.Although you don't hear spiders make any sounds in real life (thank god), the screeches they release along with the sound of their eight legs scurrying along trying to evade your traps make you just want to shudder.While this isn't best looking game by any means, during your time in the eight different stages the game presents, you will be thrown into loads of colour filled environments. The developers have opted for a more cartoony/polygonal style of visuals which work well and add to the games allure.Spin a new web:Do you like collecting everything a game has to offer? Well, there is plenty here that will keep that urge to keep going and 100 percent the game satiated. Upgrades to be had, weaponry to find, challenges to complete, collectables to be found in the form of batteries and omega files which delve into the backstory of the game for those interested.I completed the game and all it had to offer including getting all the achievements in about six hours, even after struggling to find those final elusive batteries; seriously, check everywhere. You can either attempt to hunt down everything first time or if you'd prefer, you can freely switch between any level at any time and keep all the items/weapons you previously acquired to help make tasks easier.Should you play it?50/50Verdict:Kill it with fire is fun filled, charming and terrifying all in one. There are instances where the repetitive nature of simply killing spiders may bore you but challenges and tasks help break away if only briefly from the slaughtering. Gunplay may be a bit weak but overall you're playing for the sheer madness that is this game. If it sounds like your cup of tea, give it a go and have some good, mindless fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Funny and very simplistic indie title for those who hate arthropods as much as developer does.Gameplay: basically, you seek out (with the help of your ears or locator) and murder the aforementioned specimens with extreme zeal. Each of 12 levels offers you some funny side quests to do including puzzles and some relatively challenges (arachnogauntlets) of varying difficulty, while plenty of unlockables and funny achievements will definitely keep you focused and entertained.Graphics&Design: as I've said before- it's all about simplicity with this game, and it makes very appealing in it's own way. Different spider types and gameplay configs are all good fun and offer some additional value, while smooth rock'n'roll and jazz soundtrack keeps it cool and enjoyable.*) My only complaints are about last 2 levels, because I think they are worse than others, but that's just my opinion.Overall- this game receives my recommendation and praise. As a fellow arachnophobe, I enjoyed killing arthropods way more than I thought I would!                                                                                             8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Kill It With Fire

_childDocuments_.review: If Kill It With Fire wasn't so very focused on challenges, I actually would've liked this game much more. Seriously, if I could just hunt all the spiders down in a level I'd be content enough. But the overabundance of challenges just takes away from the core game way too much.Shoot 2 spiders in 1 shotgun blast. Find the 'hidden room'. Find 5 batteries. Feed cheese puffs to 3 spiders. 360 no-scope a spider with the assault rifle. Collect all equipment and tracker upgrades. Go outside and touch some grass. Insult your neighbor's cat. Stare into the sun for 5 minutes. Oh and don't forget the 'AraCHno-gAuNTlEt', which adds yet another annoying challenge to every level.All jokes aside, the game itself is actually pretty fun and uniquely creepy, but all those unnecessary challenges just drain the fun away for me. After completing the first 3 levels I can already say I'm done with this game. I just can't focus on the gameplay when there's so many checklists surrounding me. Even If I ignored the challenges and just played, I feel like I'd miss out on at least 50% of the game. Not that one can easily ignore them, since most challenges are put as an 'objective', and completing them is the only way to unlock lots of areas in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Another great and goofy game published by TInybuiild and is developed by Casey Donnellan Games LLC. You go from level to level ranging from indoors to ourdoors in the hunt to eliminate the spiders. Is indeed a funny game with there being ridiculous ways to kill the spiders from torching them, as well as objects around you, shotguns, smashing them with your clipboard etc. Is just fun wrecking havoc in the area, throwing things around in order to find the little critters. Gameplay is great as within the levels you start off in a certain area and as you kill a certain amount, new areas open up until you have eliminated enough to gain access to the exit. There are several other little missions to do as well such as killing multiple spiders with a single shotgun shot for example. The more you complete, the more points you earn for upgrades after completing the levels. It is also cool with there being various techniques and tools for hunting the spiders, like luring them in with cheesy puffs. There are also various kinds of spiders like normal spiders and ones that spawns many more when first killed. A hilarious and chaotic game which is very fun to cause mayhem in.

A shotgun blast right at a group of spiders kills none of them.  There's very little in the small environments that is destructible, you can burn hay and break a few dishes and pots, wow. _childDocuments_.review: This is far more fun than it has any right to be. But it works and it works well and somehow sustains it. The closest comparison I could think of would be Luigi's Mansion, though that's a bit of a stretch given that this is first person and has no real boss battles (that I know of). But you are constantly unlocking new stuff, really searching every nook, and it's just a blast to play. If you like exploring, especially all the small stuff, then this game may be for you. I see a lot of other reviews comparing it to other 'joke physics simulators' and I feel that if you buy this for that, you may be let down. There's also no way to lose, which, I absolutely didn't notice or mind until I read some reviews. I really like that aspect, lets me stay focused on the exploring and puzzles, etc. If there was ever a fantastic argument as to why games don't actually need a fail state to be fun, this is it. Explore, set it on fire, hit it with a frying pan, solve a puzzle, explore some more, pour gasoline on it, try to shoot it with a pistol and miss because it's a spider and it's small, explore more. Definitely worth the asking price, but I got mine as part of a humble bundle.

_childDocuments_.review: In general, the concept is a lot of fun! I only beat the title and did not complete the 100%, but I am confident that some players will enjoy the sandbox aspects. The only disappointing aspect for me was the lack of expected destructions, which means that you can only move objects, not even furniture.In general, it's a nice little indie title with a lot of humor and fun mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Achievement Completion: 100%Kill It With Fire is a comedic and extreme take on the one thing a great majority of us fear: Spiders. In our HOME. Did you see a spider in the corner of your room? And when you went to grab some bug spray or a shoe, it was gone? Burn the whole house down. Kill it with fire!This game gives you a whole arsenal of weapons that can vastly vary in destructiveness from a gun to explosives. Kill as you see fit, but one thing is for certain when playing this game: No spider will be left alive whether you choose to leave the property relatively safe from collateral damage or decide to just go for the M.A.D. approach and take the house down with the spiders... just to be safe.
