_childDocuments_.review: I played Kill It With Fire a while back, and honestly, I still can’t stop thinking about this game every now and then, it really is a favourite game of mine! While my memories might be a bit hazy, the sheer joy of hunting down those pesky spiders with an outrageous arsenal is unforgettable. The game is so over-the-top in the best way possible! There's a spider, let me use C4, crazy!The creativity in how you can take down these little critters is just fantastic. From using everyday items to ridiculous weapons, it’s all about finding the most entertaining way to squish those eight-legged foes. I remember laughing out loud at some of the wild ways I could go about it!The levels are cleverly designed, filled with surprises and little details that kept me on my toes. Plus, the goofy sense of humor shines through, making the whole experience feel lighthearted and fun.If you’re looking for a game that combines chaos, creativity, and a whole lot of laughs, Kill It With Fire is a must-try! Even after some time away, it still holds a special place in my heart. Highly recommend giving it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Kill It With Fire

_childDocuments_.review: Kill It With Fire : By Triple F"Kill It With Fire", developed by Casey Donnellan Games, throws you headfirst into a comedic and surprisingly strategic quest: eliminating every last spider from a suburban home. While the premise might seem absurd, the game's quirky humor, surprisingly deep mechanics, and over-the-top destruction make for a surprisingly addictive experience.The game takes place across several increasingly cluttered suburban houses, each overrun with various species of spiders.  Presented in a cartoony first-person perspective, you explore the environment searching for your eight-legged foes. The humor shines from the start, with the protagonist clad in a hazmat suit and wielding an arsenal of increasingly ridiculous weapons – from flip-flops and fly swatters to shotguns and even fire itself.Despite the seemingly simple goal, "Kill It With Fire" offers surprising strategic depth. While some weapons are perfect for direct confrontation, others like aerosol cans and fireworks can be used to flush out arachnids from hiding spots or create environmental hazards. Managing resources, like the limited ammo for firearms, and strategically using the environment become crucial for success in later levels.The game thrives on its over-the-top destruction. Setting furniture ablaze, blowing up walls with grenades, or accidentally setting yourself on fire while attempting to torch a spider all contribute to the chaotic hilarity.  However, this focus on destruction can lead to some technical issues, particularly on lower-end machines.  Frame rate drops and occasional glitches can disrupt the gameplay flow."Kill It With Fire's" campaign can be completed in a few hours, offering a concise and satisfying experience.  However, the lack of additional modes or procedurally generated levels limits replay-ability. Additionally, while the humor lands most of the time, some jokes can feel repetitive after multiple playthroughs.Long story short, "Kill It With Fire" is a unique and hilarious take on the pest control genre. While the short campaign and occasional technical hiccups might deter some, the game's quirky humor, surprisingly strategic depth, and over-the-top destruction offer a genuinely fun and cathartic experience, especially for arachnophobes (with a strong sense of humor).

_childDocuments_.review: I first bought this game back in April, when it was, I believe, about 30% off, thinking I'd just give it a whirl. At the time I just didn't find that it was my thing, and I ended up returning it.However, when I saw it was on sale again, this time for much cheaper, I decided to try it again, figuring at least I could work towards getting some more achievements.I'm not sure if there were significant improvements since the first time I played or if I just got really into it, but I ended up really liking this game a lot! The controls are straightforward enough, as is your goal: Kill all the spiders! While it is definitely not for the arachnophobic, the simple premise and fun gameplay kept me enthralled for a solid 8 hours of gameplay. And if killing spiders in your downtime relaxes you, I suppose there is some potential replay value in just going back through and playing again as well! I didn't find it to be a particularly relaxing game. The sound effects and music kept me on my toes. The music is very suspenseful, but by the end of the game I had turned it off, just to give myself a bit of a chiller time.Overall though, I enjoyed playing it and I'm glad I revisited it. Definitely worth picking up on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: If you have a fear of spiders, this game is NOT for you! They jump out at you, hide on the objects you pick up, and run like there's no tomorrow. I must give credit to the developers... it is like the real thing, except instead of your house having one or two spiders, there are dozens! I'm afraid I'm not fond of spiders, so I played the first level and had to stop. This game gave me the creeps far more than any horror, FPS, Thriller, or adventure game I've ever played.That out of the way - the game is a FPS where your targets are small, very fast, eight legged little buggers. You are given a huge variety of ways of killing the spiders. Even in just level 1 I was able to find dozens of ways to do it. Squishing them with the clipboard was my most common way because it was also on hand. But the hairspray blow torch was amazingly fun, and made it easy to clear a room (just light everything up). The gun.... well, let's just say if your aim is remarkable against small, moving targets, you'll love it. I did not. I'm giving this game a thumbs up because it is exactly what is described. Not for me, but I could see how others would very much enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: 9-8-20 I now have all the achievements and like I stated it took about 8 hours to do everything and get every upgradeAmazing game. Finished the main story in a little over three and a half hours (Playlist here  ), but I also played all of the demos which are the first three of 8 and a half levels (As per the dev he counts the last level as half.. It'll make sense, promise) and also watched Casey play level 4 on a preview dev stream a few weeks ago, so I breezed through the first few levels. First time seers may take a little longer to do your first play through. First playthrough? YES you will likely need to replay all the missions in a challenge like mode to do the the last half mission (trying to avoid spoiling). There's minimum 8 hours of stuff to do in the game based on my redneck math (not including achievements which seem challenging but doable). Overall an amazing, polished game. It has improved greatly from the demos, but not without bugs (not just creepy spiders). The physics are wonky at times but it was more funny than infuriating. Oh and some feedback for updates,dlc, or heck a KIWF 2: Multiplayer would be fire(heh) though I do understand that is a whole 'nother beast in game dev. A level editor and steam workshop would really add to the games longevity especially with the ability to make destructible levels and the kind of weapons you already have in the game would be fun even if spiders were not involved (but I think they should be). I saw a review saying a prop hunt kind of mode would be awesome. I agree with that. The game has the objects already but again multiplayer may present it's own challenges. Like a team of spiders vs one human where spiders can either turn into objects or hide like the AI ones. Just spit-balling btw. I think the fact I even want a KIWF2  or DLC ALREADY speaks volumes of how fantastic this game is.Also thank you to Tiny Build who gave me a review copy to play for my channel! TL:DR Me and my community loved it don't hesitate to buy it especially since it is on launch sale.9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Kill It With Fire

_childDocuments_.review: There's really only one way to eradicate spiders; complete destruction!While I received KIWF on the basis of live streaming it before release, I did actually enjoy the carnage in my mission to rid the world of these creepy critters as well as the challenging objectives along the way. Not normally a completionist, I found myself going back to past levels to find the remaining items and gear and to complete outstanding objectives. That ending too...unexpected!
_childDocuments_.name: Kill It With Fire

_childDocuments_.review: and now onto the short review//Description//Kill it with Fire puts you in the spot of the world's worst or best? exterminator in the world. Use molotovs, air sprays with a lighter, C4, rifles, pistols and anything provided to kill spiders!//Graphics, Sound & Artstyle//To start off with the graphics, it's not very appealing- it has it's own distinct assets generic look but the sound makes any scenario nerve wrecking. Horror themed sounds will pop out whenever a spider is visible.ALSO- play with headphones. Much more satisfying.//Gameplay//Kill it with Fire is a simple game of the yesteryears filled with objectives in an area with many hidden secrets all about. You shoot, flame, blow up or straight up hit spiders with pans. //Price//14.99 USD//How many hours estimated//So there's about 9 levels in the game- with maybe a hidden one or two. Each level has taken me approximately 20-30 mins to get through. I've only completed one level for 100% as they are objective and hidden item based. Easily see myself sinking about 10-13 hours trying to complete the game//Final Thoughts//Well- Kill it with Fire certainly is a niche game mainly for streaming or a game for friends taking turns destroying a level. It's fun, frantic & funny as hell. It's a game you shut your brain off for if you're not a completionist, but if you are- it'll sure take your brain to exercise mode because some of the hidden objects and objectives are HARD but not frustratingly hard (which is a good thing). At first I thought that the fire weaponry was just too OP until I met up with the exploding spiders, as they are not affected by fire. I have no real complaints about the game other than since it has a physics engine, often key items for an objective get lost. For a single player game I wouldn't normally pay the 14.99 USD asking price- however if it were co-op or multiplayer id happily pay even up to 19.99 USD. The game is fun, it's fluid, easy to pick up on, Truly one for all types of gamers (especially those who suffer from Arachnaphobia).

_childDocuments_.review: A game for a few laughs, built on an old internet joke, and... that's it.Kill spiders with various weapons of increasing power, and while on paper the idea is great the execution missed the point by a large margin.You see spiders you kill spiders, you see more spiders you kill more spiders with more and more powerful weaponry, not exactly rocket science here.It’s your below-average first person shooter, there’s not much else to say.Spiders are incredibly tiny and almost all your weapons either have incredibly limited ammo or too precise to hit them reliably.In short I wanted to  not , after the second level the game should have handed me a flamethrower instead of waiting until the very last level to do so.12.50$ are easily expendable for a bundle of infinitely better games, and I don't recommend this title for that reason, not because it's bad, just a little boring compared to other stuff you could get.

_childDocuments_.review: Kill it with Fire is obviously a silly game in concept, but actually provides some fun objective-based gameplay.You are tasked with killing spiders, and the game does it in a funny, while at the same time terrifying way. You can hear them squeaking at you, and they can push objects around. You also have a radar that detects if there's a spider close enough to you.It's such a funny feeling of dread when you see the signal is full, and are looking at a giant shelf of objects. The spider could be anywhere. So you then have to pick up each individual thing, and slowly rotate it and hope you don't get jumpscared by a spider. Or you can burn the whole thing down.You are given many ridiculous tools to rid of these arachnids. Guns, explosives, hair spray with a lighter. You do have finite ammo, so while you can have fun, you can't be completely wreckless with just any weapon.As you explore a building, killing spiders unlocks new rooms, which might contain their own new upgrades or weaponry. This cycle is quite satisfying, as you always feel like you are working towards something.In every level, you also have arbitrary objectives like breaking 10 picture frames, or killing 2 spiders with one shotgun blast. I found these fun to try to achieve.Different spider types are introduced every level, which keeps you on your toes. Some spiders will burst into small baby ones, while others are invisible and barely spottable.Overall, while the game could've simply been mindlessly put together for a 5 minute laugh, there's actually thought put into it. It plays with your expectations with spider encounters, and has a fun and meaningful progression system. It's a lot of fun, and I recommend it!

Because of this I would probably have refunded it if it hasn't been part of a bundle but your experience may differ.Sadly, I can not recommend it based how annoyed I was every time the freeze occurred.

_childDocuments_.review: Kill It With Fire is a free mobile app that's been dumped on Steam as well, as if it was a real PC game (it's not)... it's a cash grab from greedy mobile devs.  This mobile app is a simple first person action game where you kill low poly spiders in low poly environments.  I guess the game "works" but there's a few reasons why gamers will want to avoid this mobile app. From a technical perspective, as a mobile app, this doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.The mobile app features lazy low-polygon "retro" assets, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the mid 2000s.  It's unclear why the developers weren't able to arrange high quality, high polygon count contemporary assets for the mobile app (although the requirement for this to run on low end mobile phones is a factor), and also irrelevant... what matters is that this looks bad as a result of their decisions, a compromise PC gamers shouldn't have to put up with.Because this is a mobile app, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the iPhones that the mobile app was designed for.  These are unfortunate handicaps and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was an afterthought for the iPhone developers who are to blame for this.  The mobile app is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for mobile phones forces upon a game.  Once more, mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone.  I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone.Special note: The developer of this mobile app released a demo for the game (as if it was a fully fledged game instead of using Steam's demo capability, an unethical act in itself), and that demo behaved as spyware and collected "telemetry" and personally identifying information.  There was no way to opt out of the developer harvesting data about you, it was spyware.  It's unclear if this full version of the mobile app is infested with the same spyware.  Should you trust the developer?  Of course not... if they had any concerns about user safety and privacy, .  Another note: The developer, tinyBuild, has colluded with Tencent backed interests to withhold some of their games from Steam in a brazen act of anti-competitive behaviour.  Worse, in the past they first advertised their games on Steam to drum up consumer interest before pulling the rug out from gamers, cancelling the Steam launch and abusing Steam for free beta testing, then screwing gamers over.  This is harmful to gamers and to the gaming industry, and is completely unethical behaviour intended to cause this harm for short term profit.  While games absolutely should be considered on their own merits, as I have in my review above, gamers must be cautious when buying games from unethical developers like this.  There's no telling when they will accept more bribes and pull their games off Steam again... they've done it once, they can't be trusted.  Gamers have a right to know about this.  If you buy this mobile app you may be putting your money at risk.Think of this as someone coming into your home, installing a camera in your living room, and refusing to tell you who will be watching it, if they will record the footage and where they will post it.  You have no control over your data once they take it from you.  Do you trust them?So, should you buy this mobile app?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Once more we see greedy mobile devs trying to scam PC gamers. On Steam, this is $13 USD, on app stores, it's free. Mobile devs must learn PC gamers are not here to be gouged, and can't be expected to pay a premium for a free mobile app just because it's been lazily dumped on Steam.  This is unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers.  Because this can be played free elsewhere, and because of the other defects, it's impossible to recommend.THIRTEEN BUCKS FOR A FREE MOBILE APP.  That, as far as we know, may be infested with spyware like the demo was.Just who do they think we are?

_childDocuments_.review: This should have been a really fun game - hunting down eight legged freaks with a bountiful arsenal of melee weapons, explosives, fire, guns, and more before you even consider all the natural weaponry found in each level.Instead Kill It With Fire felt frustrating and like it was trying to drag out the time it got to stay. Each mission will have a couple of door plus the exit that get unlocked as you kill more arachnid foes that all take several seconds after clicking on them for.... a bar to fill up on the door before it actually unlocks? And you can't start this process before hitting the kill goal. Even confirming a level restart of that you want to finish the level takes several more seconds than it needs to before you can say yes and it all just adds to a feeling of making you wait for the game to be ready.That feeling gets dragged out further when most levels ended up feeling like, even with the radar, I was hunting down the last few available spiders to move onto the next section or to complete an objective instead of just getting to enjoy the main selling point of killing spiders.Pulling objects off tables, shelves, shifting boxes, and more to find spiders leaves lots of clutter around in levels. You'd think the amount of fire you can pour into a level would help with that, but fire it oddly disappointing for a title weapon. If it spread through the whole environment naturally it would make things far too easy but it would be nice to have it do more than set one thing on fire, maybe something directly touching it, and burn itself out in a few seconds leaving the object blackened but otherwise unharmed. If it could clear some clutter then at least it would make it easier to hunt with other weapons but as it is? You might as well try and leave the furniture intact and use your other weapons. Guns will need you to aim consistently below the crosshair though as an FYI if you want to take on each levels challenges. Shuriken are still a mystery art form that only felt possible with Energy Drink bullet time.The game's also designed for revisiting levels between the challenges (which are much easier with both energy drinks and, counter-intuitively, not killing anything before starting the challenge so you have more foes available for the time limit with less hunting required), objectives (one even requires visiting every level after reaching the end of the game), and clutter that get in the way of the fun.I played the game to the end of the story and considered trying for some more of the achievements but quickly felt like I was doing it for the sake of doing it, not because I was having fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The flow of the game does not work. "Smash 20 dishes" I feel like a home intruder hunting down the spiders as they cower in their own home and destroying everything for no reason.The reward for killing the spiders is a boombox that starts a challenge, get kills with a revolver which that I did not find the entire rest of the game... _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. The concept itself would make for a hilarious arcade-style destruction fest, something short and sweet. But this is not that. This is tediously searching around for spiders using a cellphone signal symbol that increases when you get closer, instead of an actual radar. Not only is this slow paced, which does not work for the concept, it also entirely revolves around completing chores in order to unlock things. Some of these are fine, like burning items, and spiders, etc., or even testing out a new weapon. Others are just busy work that is there to pad out time, like putting trash in a dumpster, or trying to scan $100 of items with only ten items max you can scan. It's boring, and wastes time, and is annoying. And you NEED to do these things to unlock upgrades for your character and radar. This is compounded with the tedium of basically playing a game of hide-and-seek, and the fact that the hitboxes of the spiders and the area of effect on your weapons are too small. A double barrel shotgun has the SAME AOE as a revolver, which also requires you to shoot at the dead center of the spider to actually hit it. Same with AN ENTIRE STACK OF BOOKS! unless that spider is in the center, it will survive being hit by anything you throw at it. Did I mention the reticle you aim with is grey and blends in with the floor and several of the spiders, making it hard to see where you are aiming? So you not only have to deal with the sluggish aiming controls, tiny hitboxes on the spiders, tiny aoe for the weapons, but also a reticle that is hard to see because the devs did not make it a different colour than most everything else. On top of this, you have no time limit, save for the frustrating gauntlets, and nothing hurts you. You literally can not lose, so you have no challenge, or feeling of accomplishment. You just spend nearly 20 minutes per level wandering aimlessly until you get everything, then do the same thing in the next one. All of this combined makes this game just an absolute slog to get through. Which is sad, because it did not have to be this way. Faster pacing, and focusing more on blasting hordes of spiders with increasingly more insane weapons would have been much more entertaining, especially if they could actually fight back. As it stands, this game was boring within the first five minutes, and frustrating after that. I finished three levels, and I feel like I wasted roughly an hour of my life that I am never getting back.2/10 The concept is funny, the execution is terrible.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly fun, but short game. Not too much thinking involved aside from trying to kill the spiders with whatever you have. You get to kill spiders and for the most part, there usually aren't any major issues in playing. That said...One note is that you never seem to obtain enough upgrade points to obtain everything. This isn't an issue for your tracker, as you can get all but one upgrade and that upgrade is redundant once you obtain all upgrades, but for your personal upgrades, you are quite short on points.  (Also, one of the tracker upgrades doesn't seem to really work very well and one upgrade seems to sometimes not work all the time (it only seems to work if the spider is completely behind an object/wall, so if a leg is sticking out, it won't work. Ironically, it works through windows)).There are some bugs that can occur (such as floating enemies if you end up launching an item onto a solid box that doesn't actually exist with the spider attached) and some missions are annoying to complete unless you have very specific loadouts and luck.One late mission requires you to kill 10 spiders with 10 different weapons. One of the weapons you receive on that level seems like it would be useful, but I never managed to kill with it (some weapons don't do damage by themselves). Best thing to do is to first do some prep work and clear the area of any unnecessary clutter as these can shield the spiders. You might keep one item to throw, but you'll want to go into your menu to swap weapons. Do explosives last as you want to avoid accidentally killing spiders you need (Also, fire weapons don't actually do damage, they burn, which takes time and can cause unintended casualties).An early mission requires you to kill two spiders with one shot. This can be somewhat difficult with your gear at that point in the game as you need to bait the spiders and if you fail, you may want to just finish the level or quit the level and start over. Now, it is certainly possible to naturally obtain that, but it is much more difficult early on.Also, the Reflex Sight makes your clipboard ranged. Also, as a side note, I'm not sure if the spiders can actually do damage to your character as I don't recall ever failing due to taking too much damage from the spiders.

It's a lot of fun (there are arachnophobia options; turning them from semi-realistic spiders to blobs made of little spheres), though a bit short and a pain to 100% (I gave up on the second to last 'Arachno-Gauntlet'). Still, it's worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: My expectations were vastly surpassed. On the surface, this appears to be another one of those cheaply made simulator games. But underneath the exterior layer, the game offers engaging gameplay, explore-worthy environments, and a variety of weapons and features. As a person who can't get rid of spiders in his own apartment, I'm thankful that a videogame with this concept has been developed. I was so intrigued by the game that I refused to look at guides and instead insisted on experiencing everything for myself. It's impressive how much world-building went into something like this.

_childDocuments_.review: In Kill It With Fire you go around killing as many spiders as you can with a large variety of different weaponry you collect through out the levels. The game play doesn't really evolve much so what you get at the start is what you'll see in the end as well, you'll just have easier time to kill spiders with stronger weapons and other upgrades. _childDocuments_.review: A decently fun romp that feels a bit let down by the lack of stakes near the end. Not story-wise, that ramped up well enough. But it's pretty clear this is, above all else, a game about killing spiders. They can't hurt you; at best they can cover your screen with a nasty web, or perhaps leap at you when threatened. Very cathartic fun, from getting the first kill in a silly manner, to whipping out some decidedly overkill weaponry in order to handle some li'l creepy-crawlies. The inclusion of a "creepy spiders" toggle is welcome, though I'm not really arachnophobic like some people I know, so I can't comment on its efficacy. I got it as a gift, but I would say it's worth the price of entry if you aim for 100%

_childDocuments_.review: A shortish but quite entertaining game which really revels in the sort of humor that only a video game can really do. You are an exterminator trying to kill spiders. Your tools include firearms, explosives, and an aerosol can with a lighter in front of it. There is no penalty for causing property damage. For the target audience, that should really be everything that needs to be said about the game.Obviously, trigger warning for anyone with arachnophobia, but this is somewhat lessened by the fact that the spiders can't actually hurt you. There's a bunch of different kinds with different special abilities, but the only offensive power any of them have is one kind that can throw webs that gunk up your screen for a moment and make it hard to see.

_childDocuments_.review: Best survival horror game ever made. 10/10For serious though, "Kill it with Fire" is a very smart and fun game. The premise is pretty simple, but the different spider varieties, unique objectives, and absurd equipment to unlock keep things interesting throughout the 12 hours it took me to find everything and get all the achievements. It has a pretty laid back difficulty while still posing enough of a challenge to feel meaningful, which I really appreciate. Spiders can't actually hurt you, and there are no lose conditions outside the handful of timed gauntlet challenges, but hunting down spiders in itself is a satisfying enough challenge, and a number of side objectives as well as the gauntlet challenges are skill-based (though an item allows these to be cheesed quite easily, which I also appreciated). It would have been cool if there was some sort of time attack or challenge mode to play with after finding everything in all of the levels to really test your spider hunting skills, but as it is, I definitely think this short, goofy little adventure was worth the cost of entry, and I am eagerly looking forward to the sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW #51Kill It with Fire----------Here's a really fun one.Kill It with Fire is a first-person action game centered on the elimination of one of the world's most feared creatures: spiders. There's a handful of locales, starting at various places in your house and then moving on to public places, like a gas station and a farmer's market. Each location has its own objectives to complete, such as killing a number of spiders with a certain weapon or setting a set number of objects on fire.The game has wacky physics and a great comedic, over-the-top style, making it more entertaining than terrifying. A majority of your weaponry will fall into the "overkill" category, like a shotgun, a hairspray/lighter combo, a riding lawnmower and explosive flying drones, and using them for spider murder is hugely (and morbidly) satisfying. There's also a nice selection of upgrades and variations to apply, including holiday themes. On top of all of this, the developer has gone so far as to add "arachnophobia" options that affect how the game behaves when a spider is in view, such as removing horror "stings" from the background music when a creepy crawler is spotted hiding somewhere.Overall, Kill It with Fire is pretty solid from both a gameplay and a technical perspective. The developer has done a really good job of improving and debugging the game. With that said, I still encounter a random glitch or two during play now and again, although it's never anything game-breaking. A good example is from a recent play session, where my spider detector told me where a spider was, and I could hear that it was nearby, but even after setting everything around me on fire, I just could not find and kill the sucker. (This didn't halt gameplay or progress, mind you. I was just being obsessive about it.) I finally accidentally killed it, but I don't know how I did or where it was....but yeah, Kill It with Fire is one of those games that you'll only plan on playing for 10 minutes and wind up playing it for 30 because it's fun and addictive. I've even started another save slot after completing everything because I just want to go back and do it all over again. There's a free demo available, and I highly recommend downloading it and trying it out to anyone who likes a light-hearted action game, even if spiders give you the jibblies.

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance this game looks like it's purely streamer bait, but it is actually quite a fun game. It's basically a violent game of hide and seek with some spiders.The levels are pretty fun with them being set in pretty mundane locations like a kitchen or office but they all get burnt, smashed and shot up as you chase the spiders about the place. Theres a really good variety of weapons from a frying pan to RPG and there are also quite a few types of spider each with different abilities.As you kill a set number of spiders more parts of the level will open up and aside from killing spiders each level has different unique objectives to complete alongside the spider hunting. So one level might ask you to find bags of rubbish and chuck them in a dumpster or there might be a puzzle to solve. Theres also upgrades to hunt down which improve your abilities and spider tracking device.So if you just want a light hearted fun game and dont suffer from arachnophobia, this might be a good choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off interesting, then becomes boring at later stages.This game starts off as you being a spider exterminator, except you're cool and you use guns. However, at later stages, this game turns from you being the hunter, to you wondering "what is the meaning of life?" It's a hide and seek game, and the reason it's fun in the beginning of the game is because the hide and seek place is tiny. But at later stages, finding spiders and completing side objectives feels like agony. And you need to complete all side objectives to progress. That being said, there are only over 10 levels. If you know where everything is, you could complete this game in under 2 hours. Which is not good for a game that costs more than $5. If you don't know where everything is, and are just good at hide and seek (or just lucky), you could complete this game under 5 hours. Which is still not a lot, since most of that time would be spent on you being in agony.And the updates? Oh, this game receives no updates. Despite the devs being very active, making a VR version of this game, and a couple bug fixes every now and then, the game hasn't received any updates for a long time. Since it got released, to be exact. I remember playing the demo for this game, and there were over 10 levels, with 8 of  them being locked. Guess how many levels total there are now? 10. It's apparent that the devs are only in it for the money at this point, since making a VR version of this game is way more expensive than adding a level or two. Especially for a game with such low graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: Kill It With Fire is a very humorous game that is also quite fun. Here's a few bullet point Pros and Cons.Pros:You get to wield weapons of mass destruction... against spiders.You can make the spiders not realistic looking in the settings (which I did).Everything in the game is relatively easily accomplishable once you have the right tools and know what you're doing (the energy drink always helps).Cons:This game contains spiders... though not for long if you're good at it.The Perplexing Puzzle objective that requires you to go to every other level and find a hidden code part with the blacklight is annoying (especially if you do it before getting a certain tracker upgrade, which I did).And that's about it, hope this was informative.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, really fun, gigantic variety of weapons, really fun level modifiers like low gravity or double the size of spiders. Really cures my hatred towards spiders and wanting to burn everything down in a fit of rage. After you finish the game you get a blacklight which you need to go back in every level and find a hidden code that you need to unlock a vault in level 4. That was really fun to search for.One thing i really liked was the fact that the strongest weapon is literally a stattrak shoe that you need to upgrade by killing to unlock its full potential being : everytime you hit something it sends a nuclear explosion towards the spider. Toilet destructability is 10/10.The only thing that i didn't like was the fact that fire is EXTREMELY unoptimized. It lowers the fps at least 2 or 3 times. For a game called "Kill it with fire" and having several weapons that create fire you should've invested more time into fixing that issue. And i don't really think that for a game with such basic graphics you need a Nvidia 3080/90 gpu to have more than 60fps when you light the map on fire.

_childDocuments_.review: A short, well made little casual game where the fun comes from experimenting with all of your various tools to creatively delete those little a-holes from reality. There isn't a ton of depth, it's more of a sandbox than anything - you can't die, there's not really any true fail states, and you can still get achievements when using the more cheaty upgrades. However, I don't think the point was to have any challenge. It's just a fun, satirical little game.There are a couple issues with it - for some reason, it's rather performance intensive even on my stronk rig and there isn't an FOV slider, which was giving me headaches/eye strain after a while during long secret hunting sessions. Nothing gamebreaking or anything though - your mileage may vary. I also feel like switching gear could've been more intuitive, I don't know why there's even a strict limit to what stuff you can have in your hotbar.I recommend it and hope that if there's a sequel of some kind, there'll be a little bit of added depth for those that want it, in addition to the more free form gameplay this had.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this review short and sweet just like this game.This game is essentially a big game of hide and seek with a tonne of spiders. At first it is quite stressful but as the game progresses you get more and more useful and chaotic methods of both finding and killing the spiders. There is no self-damage in this game so you can go crazy and destroy the entire map without punishment. It took me around 8 hours to leisurely waltz to 100% but it was fun for almost the entire run.A couple of issues:When the maps get very large, this is where the game is at it's worst. This isn't an issue once you have the upgrades and weapons that make this trivial, but the equipment available to the player at the time of starting these levels isn't useful enough to stop these levels from being tedious. My advice for new players would be to not worry about 100% the few large levels on your first run and just go back later with more equipment otherwise it might put a sour taste in your mouth. Another issue is that some weapons and upgrades are pretty much useless and you will find yourself completely ignoring these during your entire run.Also if you ever find yourself struggling, remember to use the energy drink. It is a life saver for timed challenges.But overall it is a very enjoyable and wacky game that doesn't take itself seriously and neither should you. Also with the addition of the Christmas and Halloween updates, the game feels full of things to do, even for the short time you'll be playing for.When I Stopped Playing: Completed 100%Rating: 8/10Bare in mind that my ratings are purely scored on how well the game in question achieves the goals set out by the developers. This game succeeds regarding it's hide and seek mechanics, mayhem, short and sweet pacing, variety in weapons and maps and it's use of spiders for creepiness and cathartic murdering.For example this 8/10 isn't comparable to an 8/10 game that focuses on a deep story or city simulation as they don't share the same goals.

_childDocuments_.review: Continuing with small indie games that I don't even remember I got in bundles. Now we got Kill It With Fire.I enjoyed my time with it and that's why I'll recommend it. But I'd only get it on sale because €12 is a bit too much for what it is.It's a very short game that was certainly fun for those 2 hours but even then it started to wear thin in the end. Nevertheless, the game is quite enjoyable and it mixes up a lot for such a short and small game. The first few levels were the least enjoyable for me because you don't have a lot of weapons yet. But when they start rolling in the RPGs, flamethrowers, upgrades, etc. then it was a whole lot more fun. There are also quite a bit of challenges in each level that you can either choose to do all of them so you can eventually get the supposedly true ending or not. Personally, I don't care about such things, so I tried to do every challenge in a level but when I didn't find the missing piece or whatever the last challenge would've been, then I went to the exit.Gameplay is probably the most attractive thing that's to see here, and it's decent enough for those 2 hours I played.The visuals are okay, nothing mind-blowingly unique but not certainly not generic.The soundtrack is pretty good as well, not a huge fan of it either but it gets the job done. What I do want to point out is the 'dynamic' music, whenever a spider is running away there's going to be a violin track and that was pretty cool.Sound design is good, weapons felt impactful, sound effects of things breaking are great, spiders all sound good.The story is not really there, I mean it does tell a story through visual storytelling but it can easily be missed, especially in the first few levels.Overall a decent game that might amuse you for 2 hours or maybe even more if you're really into it. Do get it on sale however because personally I find it a bit too overpriced but that's completely up to you.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Get if you want a hectic, silly, relatable destruction game and have either mild or no fear of spiders. Probably skip if you are arachnophobic....So I'm arachnophobic and have been since I was a kid. I was on a med as a kid that made me hallucinate that I, my bed, and my entire room were covered every inch in spiders until my mom heard my screams and ran to the rescue, turned on the light and the hallucination went away.It's gotten better over the years, but I am still at a constant war with spiders. Sometimes I have the will to catch it with my spider grabber and put it outside because I know spiders are our friends and that they are the reason more annoying bugs like flies and mosquitos are not a worse issue. Other times the adrinaline and the fright are too much for me to not do the tap dance of my people upon the thing while screaming like a banshee. Though that in it's self is an improvement... because up till a few years ago I couldn't even get close enough to a spider to kill it.I got this game in a Humble Bundle but I had been looking at it for a while. I though it might be cathartic. A nice way to let loose some steam. I can identify with wanting to absolutely destroy a house to kill a spider. I thought it would be a funny way to deal with my phobia too.Nah man ♥♥♥♥ that lol! I say recommend on this game because it is fun, suspenseful, and relatable. The mechanics are good other than me not quite understanding how I'm supposed to kill a spider with a book in the first mission other than by dropping it cause I can't seem to find a way to swing it around. It's a good game.I will say though that it did not help with my phobia.... it triggered it something hard lol. So if you are like me and have ACTUAL arachnophobia and aren't just "scared of spiders" maybe tread carefully? If you just don't like spiders. They gross you out or you find them a bit creepy. I'd say definitely get the game. I imagine it's fun to play if picking up the items in the game don't make your skin crawl and cause you to look around the immediate area around you as if the game is gonna spawn them in your own house.Like the fact that the last two spiders I needed to find in the starting level were behind picture frames... and legit once I hang something up I never take it down because I KNOW there's a good chance there is a spider on the back... made me nope the ♥♥♥♥ out lol. If there is an area where they have those covered ceiling lights that you have to unscrew a glass dome to get to the lightbulbs..... nah nah nah XD there's a reason I make my husband do that because literally ever time I've ever tried to change those lightbulbs there's a spider in that damn dome. If I hit a level where there was a spider in one of those lights... I'd never finish the level.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely for a cheaper price, while the good ol unreasonable explosive mayhem is naturally fun, the gameplay loop doesn't evolve much with new levels and toys you get.The idea is simple joke idea, you have annoying insects in your house (and othe locations), which you would like to get rid of. Smacking them and throwing all kinds of stuff at them does the job, but it's not necessarily the most fun or efficient method.Before you can kill them, you have to find them, you have a sensor to help you out, but its usefulness improves greatly with upgrades, at the start you will be picking up a lot of objects and rotating them (or throwing) to find if the buggers are hiding on them. They can then try to escape while you chase them.The movement is pretty damn slow before you get the sprint upgrade, so it may push you towards trying stealthy methods, and once you get firearms, sneaking up and sniping the spiders is the only sensible way to use said guns.And yeah, you shoot spiders, and of course going further you will get other more outlandish tools to murder them. C4? Check. Molotovs and flamethrowers for pre-firing shelves with many items? Check. Bomb drone for scouting and exploding? Check. Cheese puffs you can use as bait and mind control? Check. Rocket launcher? Check. Huge rideable lawn mower that's barely usable on any maps besides one? Also check.The gameplay relies on humor, and trying out dumb sounding strategies. The spiders have also several types, they don't impact the gameplay much, but it's a nice variety nonetheless.Besides smacking spiders, you get a list of objectives per level, secret items for upgrades, as well as a gauntlet challenge once all objectives are met. It's a blessing that previous objectives stay completed when replaying levels, as you can miss some the first time around.It's best played in short sessions, as the novelty can fade quickly, and there is no second idiot running around with you. They packed hefty amount of content in it, but it ultimately lacks depth for the 6 hours or so it asks of you to get most stuff done, while coop would not fix this problem naturally, it's always a good friend to go along with dumb mayhem in games.Visually it's a little on the bland side, barely textured and surprisingly low poly in almost every place, it's not very pleasing to the eye, but I will gladly take this anytime over a visually busy version, given that the game is about finding small 8 legged **sholes, and as much clarity and as little visual clutter is helping the gameplay part immensely. Animations are present, but rather unremarkable, what you will mostly see animated is spiders, fire and explosions, and your weapons, so that part of the visuals is extremely unremarkable as well, then again, often the spiders you hunt are the only thing that moves, which helps with chasing them.Sound is okay, sometimes cuts out oddly, a lot of it is rather silent, besides the weaponry and spider's squeaky noises. The impact of the weaponry is a bit uneven, some weapons sound extremely punchy, while others with explosions, oddly less so. The songs are decent, a few of them during last cutscene and credits are actually surprising bangers, enough so that I might check them out outside the game.Lastly I would be covering the story, and while there is surprisingly an attempt, the whole game being a joke kind of made me uninvested in that part. I know what happened in it, but I couldn't be bothered to read the secret lore files. As you might've expected, there was some spider experimentation, hence all the mutated types, with a certain remarkable one you might miss if you don't look at the ceilling near the end. Since you're an exterminator, you do what must be done to this insect threat.I said quite a bit about it, mostly because it's a neat idea and game, there is a lot of charm to it, and enough to keep me interested over several short sessions. That said, I don't think I would recommend it at any high prices, unless you're willing to refund it if the 2 hours won't work for you, though it definitely has a slow start.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amusing little indie game about killing spiders using increasingly absurd and destructive weaponry. Lots of fun for what it is with ridiculous spider slaying and lots of hidden secrets. Unfortunately the game isn't particularly polished and I've encountered multiple glitches like the attack button not working at all until I restarted the game, and some polish issues like the crosshair/hitbox for guns not really lining up properly making shooting spiders far more difficult than it should be. Some of the spiders can also take multiple hits from an AR which, just no.Weapon progression is also not great, with high power revolvers coming before frying pans. Objects don't break as much as I would have liked with the amount of firepower available, and I was also expecting some kind of giant spider boss at the end or something.Some of the challenges in the levels are super annoying seemingly for the sake of being annoying, with me spending more time trying to find the spiders in the limited time than killing them, or having to fight the awful gun aiming mechanics. I used the level complete debug option described in a recent announcement to skip the more onerous ones and it made the game much more enjoyable.Overall, still a fun game for the Humble Bundle discount price I got it for. Not sure that it's worth full price though honestly.

_childDocuments_.review: IRL, I make attempts to save every non-poisonous spider I can in order to help me wage war against annoying insects, very much an "enemy of my enemy" deal rather than love for the eight-legged lifeforms. KiwF allowed me to escape this reality for a few hours, and unleash many a method of disposing my current allies, should they become a liability.The formula is straightforward - eradicate as many spiders as you can find within the given environment while keeping an eye out for upgrades to your arsenal. Upgrades will reward you with new methods to hunt your prey as well as new tools to execute them with, keeping the gameplay varied through each level with a  shiny new toy or two to try out each time. The game can range from easy to mildly challenging, depending on if you want to complete every little thing in it or not. Nine levels are available, each a rather unique location in which to run wild. If you are more of a non-completionist, any given level shouldn't take more than 20-30 minutes. There are mini challenges along the way to kill X amount of spiders within Y amount of time, some with a specific weapon or other stipulation. Files are also hidden in each level relating to a backstory of sorts, if you are interested in such a thing with this kind of game. Hunting for these will certainly help you to get more mileage out of your purchase, especially since some of the more wild and inventive upgrades will require looking around for all the items and completing all the objectives.Maybe steer clear of this one if you have severe arachnophobia. Otherwise, as long as you think you'd be content with it's gameplay loop and/or you secretly desire to murder any and every spider in your path, Kill It With Fire is a fun diversion if you find yourself with some time and money to burn.

However the challenge missions could've done with a little tuning down. For such a silly casual game, the challenges were actually a bit difficult. I can imagine that being a solid miss for some people playing this game. I never did like it when silly games like this suddenly expect the player to actually do something difficult.Not saying there can't be no challenge at all, but for example, shooting small fast-moving spiders with a very accurate firearm 5 times without reloading (you can only afford to miss once) is a pretty dang difficult challenge for people who don't play first person shooters.Even as someone who plays a lot of them, they were pretty hard. Can't imagine that this will go over well with the main crowd this sort of game will attract.At any rate, fun game. Lots of destruction and chaos, the jumping spiders actually are pretty scary and they made me uncomfortable enough that whenever I found one i'd just blow the little hellspawn up with c4.

_childDocuments_.review: Kill It With Fire is funny, it's well set-up, it has a great sense of humor. So much that I wanted out of this game was delivered. A bit of craftsmanship went into modeling all of the objects in the levels. While the graphics put you in a passive neighborhood setting, the game's music and sound effects are dramatic, the music accentuating the moment as you find your next murder device, and creepy violins playing when a spider is on the loose. The game's story is told very impressively. What is once a silly game about killing spiders escalates into a more sinister and shocking as you find and read the Omega Files hidden in every level. If you haven't already been shocked because you didn't find those files, then I'm sure the events of the last two levels will do it for you.The main complaint I have is how short it is. For a game priced 15 dollars, I expected something with a little more meat on it. There's a good amount of collectibles in each level, but perhaps the issue is that the only thing you have to go through for each time you replay a level (besides the penultimate one) is kill enough spiders to unlock the exit. That, or the fact that this is one of those games where you can't die. But did I have fun the entire time? Yes! Yes I did!

The escalation of spiders is very interesting and leads to a fun bit of figuring out what to deal with first, and the challenges are all pretty amusing, while upgrades are great rewarding fun!Then I unlocked Tiny Mode and shrieked as I knocked my headset off because of a jumping spider.I had fun with it, would recommend, and I'm hoping for a sequel or DLC <3

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - It's a short game, the missions are fun, and trying to 100% the game is a little tedious.Okay, with that taken care of, let's begin.  Minor spoilers ahead, but nothing regarding the end of the game.You are an exterminator, but unlike the ones in our pesky real world, you're the exterminator seen in just about every cartoon.  You have a huge variety of wacky weapons to smash spiders with. At first, your loadout starts stupidly simple: it's just you and your trusty clipboard.  The first mission will give you the Tracker (used for finding spiders, pretty useless until you get some upgrades for it), and some hair-spray.  Complete enough of the objectives, and you can unlock a drawer with a revolver.  This is pretty much the format of each level.  You walk in with what you've unlocked, you find new weapons in each level, you kill spiders until the exit opens, rinse and repeat.If you want to replay a level, don't worry.  All of the gear you've found is yours to keep, and even if you got it after the level you wanted to replay, you still have it.  Want to wreck Domestic Duties with a rocket launcher?  You can.  Can't complete one of the Arachno-Gauntlets because it's a bit too tough for you?  Use the Energy Drink from Major Inconvenience to slow down time and make things a bit easier.  Just in the mood for a bit of casual fun?  C4 and First Contact is a great way to blow up some spiders and blow off some steam.So, a word to the wise: Don't bother with the Arachno-Gauntlet challenges until AFTER you complete most of the levels.  You'll do much, much better once you have a few of the later-game items.How would I rate the game, personally?  About an 8 out of 10.  It's short, it's fun in short bursts, the challenges aren't too hard once you realize there's a lot of things in later levels to help you, but it is brought down a bit by a couple of levels that, honestly, just weren't fun.For me, my least enjoyed level is Garden of Evil.  Sure, the spitting spiders are fun and have their own gimmick of making it just about impossible to see, but this is a game about smashing spiders, not solving puzzles.  For anyone else who gets stuck looking for the "puzzle" after you get the objective "Strike Swiftly," there's no puzzle at all.  Kill a spider with a shuriken.  I spent close to 20 minutes in that level moving stuff around trying to 'solve' a 'puzzle' that didn't exist.Some of the objectives in the other levels aren't so fun, also, but at least the good thing about objectives is you only have to do them once.  Once they unlock, feel free to ignore them in future runs through the level.Once you've beaten the game, there are some endgame upgrades that are there just for a good bit of fun.  I won't spoil them for you.If you're looking for a spider-smashing game that you can have finished in a long afternoon, this works. _childDocuments_.review: Is it cruel to laugh at someone else's fears? It's no secret that, while being an undoubted source of endless misery for those who suffer from them, neurotic mental ailments have a tremendous potential for Comedy. Not least of these is the idea of phobias. While certain phobias like claustrophobia and hydrophobia can pose such major social barriers that they have long been the subject of Thrillers and Horror films alike, other such irrational fears also have the potential for infinite mirth. The reason for this is not so much the case of the phobia itself but rather the way in which the terror these phobias provoke can summon forth ridiculously disproportionate reactions. This concept of rational people being motivated by irrational fears to act like idiots is the key premise on which the entire narrative of Kill It With Fire is based. Playing as a nameless faceless protagonist afflicted with a truly severe case of arachnophobia, players take on the task of eradicating the seemingly rampant plague of spiders which have apparently infested not only their home but their whole community at large. Whether these "eight-legged freaks" are real or merely fear-induced hallucinations is never specified, but what quickly becomes apparent is that your character is ready, willing and able to do whatever it takes to hunt them down. In terms of game play, the best way to describe Kill It With Fire is that it plays out like the final act of one of those big budget Comedies from the 1970s where, unable to think of a decent ending, the writers decided that the narrative should just descend into anarchy and have the actors completely obliterate the set. Thus, players are given almost free range in waging their path of destruction. Almost every single set piece can be picked up, thrown, smashed or burned. The resulting mess left in their wake at times feels like it belongs in some kind of twisted cartoon, especially when coupled with the colourful art style and the apparent revelation that your protagonist is invulnerable! There is also some degree of variety with the selection of spiders as well. While none are based on actual spiders, it is intriguing to see the mix of crawlers on offer: jumping spiders, web-spitting spiders, exploding spiders! All are equally vile and all are heralded by the shuddering, grating whine of a shrill string-set orchestral score when they make their presence known. Is it really any wonder why you would want to use ever more ridiculous methods of dispatch against them? The downsides come when trying to play on higher spec settings. The frame rate isn't ever compromised in any way, but the soundtrack is buggy (no pun intended) and often cuts out. Another issue comes in the form of the combat animations. Playing both the Beta tests for this game, I found that when performing melee attacks that the animations for it would glitch and the fact that this problem hasn't been patched yet is a little concerning. It's also advised that you play in window mode to help with the resolution. Perhaps living in Australia (home to the ten most deadly species of spider on Earth) colours my view a little bit in this regard, but playing Kill It With Fire really does hammer home just how silly such fears can be and this game is just that: silly, absurd, crazy fun. Let's just home with Summer on the way that life doesn't eventually imitate art...

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the game some more, I am ready to revise my review:I figured out how to assign weapons to keys, you have to press Q!The unlocks section of the menus to see what you have is purely aesthetic and does not have any function at all!Also there are still many bugs, besides those pesky spiders running amok.1). There are inconsistent amounts of delay between selecting an option and being prompted with 'yes' or 'no.' I could not get my credits back from upgrades because the options to verify or deny that I wanted to do so never showed up. I could however press escape to try again, but if it didn't work before, it wouldn't work the next time I tried.2. Playing the game from the eyes of a duck is not very good. Screens are completely black and you can't enter the pin code to unlock the safe door. The bug is mainly visual for the pin code never changes, but it should. 3. There are still many weird collision/momentum bugs.a). The wall rubble of the convenience store can be used to send you and objects flying even though this is completely useless.b). You can still get 'stuck' in the floor but is visually fixed when you crouch and uncrouch. c). There's probably others but I don't remember.4. I don't understand why gasoline doesn't light the object on fire. It's like the object was coated in a magic bubble and the bubble was charred while the object underneath is just fine.  In addition to gasoline coated objects not counting as burning, but objects touching the gasoline catches on fire and counts as burning is the incendiary ammo also doing the same garbo. If you do a gauntlet where it's gun based, when you set a spider on fire and it dies to the fire and not the gunshot wound, it doesn't count as a gun kill. Even though it was the gun that set them on fire? 5. Also I am currently struggling to complete the last gauntlet. What does it mean when I have to kill spiders in 10 different ways? I used 10 different methods, but it didn't count. It makes me wonder which weapons count as the same kind of kill. Is all fire one method? If so, why? I flattened one with a clipboard, bashed one with a pan, exploded a few with C4, burned down an entire room with a flamethrower + gasoline on half, shotgun + pistol + M4 with infinite ammo, and a RPG missile for good measure into the other room, but yet even with a finishing blow to a stunned spider with a shuriken it wasn't enough. What else is there to kill with? 5 of the weapons sets them on fire, if they run into each other they set each other on fire. What other method of destruction is there? OH yeah, there's also the saw launcher which set a spider on fire while another spider ran over that fire and set everything else on fire. What's that all about? I wasn't even using incendiary ammo on that one. Pssh. I still had fun. And it's extremely satisfying to not have to reload with infinite ammo. I would've thought that it meant I could reload as many times as I wanted. Which is not to say that I would be looking forward to a nerf to this infinite RPG clip, but if that ever does come into existence, might it be paired with an addition of a faster reload speed upgrade and possibly a DLC. Burning down an amusement park sounds fun. Or maybe even setting a tomb ablaze with a torch that would set cobwebs on fire if you whacked them with it. There's much potential with this title, and I will patently sit and wait for more. Hopefully around the next steam sale, holiday or summer.  4/5

_childDocuments_.review: +Great soundtrack and audio design+Variety of weapons and equipment+Surprisingly immersive+Fun for every level of gamer+Reasonably priced-Ultrawide support not optimised since Demo-Spiders are not a threat-Lack of FOV and motion blur optionsKill it with fire is a first person spider killing simulator (playing loosely with the terms) in which spiders that are harmless to you are hidden all over the house and you are tasked with killing them, as well as completing various other objectives as well as a spider killing challenge in the end upon fully having completed the objectives for that mission.There are various spiders with unique elements such as the white spider that is a one hit kill spider, the black spider that takes 2 hits to kill, the red with a black stripe spider that spawns 4 white spiders upon its death and so forth. There are several different environments that come with each mission. The more spiders you kill the more rooms you unlock, including inevitably the exit. Still, stick around and explore some before you head out the door. Try to complete all of the objectives for that one mission. You have various equipment and a skill upgrade tree. You can use a hairspray flamethrower, different handguns and shotguns, bazookas, ninja stars... the list goes on. The developers have gone all out with the types of weapons you can use. Even though the spiders are not able to harm you, chills running down your spine are still most likely to take place. Not to mention if you have an irrational fear of spiders you are definitely bound to feel the freak. This is a low stakes game that ultimately will get forgotten in the sands of time, but not without making a considerable impact with its unique concept and fun graphical design.I am disappointed on the fact that aspect ratios did not receive any attention. Ultrawide aspect ratio is just zoomed in, hiding elements of the game in the process. Anything past the 4th line on your objective clipboard is hidden away due to the zooming in that takes place. In the menus, half of the phrases that explain what an upgrade will do is also hidden. There is no FOV slider, no motion blur settings in the menu, and no individual graphical settings besides a preset one. That being said, the soundtrack is surprisingly enjoyable. The audio design overall is also great. Hearing the spider chirping when it is near you while you are inspecting objects is considerably immersive. The art design is also satisfactory. It is non offensive with no risks having been taken and yet accomplishes to put together the game in a way that is a pleasure to look at. I can see how this game will excel as a fun VR title to play with your friends in short sessions. For the asking price, especially with the 10% launch discount, I say this is a good investment.#killitwithfireSteam Group:Curator Page:

short_description: An Open world Action adventure combining exploration with puzzles and dynamic combat. Go on a journey across a sprawling continent as Kaku, a boy tasked to restore balance to the land. Brave the four elemental regions with the help of Piggy, his powerful companion and conquer their lords.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the four elements of wind, fire, water, and earth, the game is set in an ancient fantasy world. Players take on the role of Kaku, a young man from the snowy mountains. He dreams of seeing the world beyond the horizon. In order to regain the power of the elements, Kaku must embark on an adventure with a magical flying pig named Piji after accidentally passing a test. Along the way, you'll be tasked with finding the right equipment and mastering legendary skills. It's now your destiny to face powerful monsters that have absorbed the power of the elements, and each of these areas has its own problems. The goal of Kaku is therefore to solve these problems in order to bring the elemental core back to the flying island and to solve the mystery.As for the gameplay, it's a third-person action-adventure game. You use melee and ranged weapons (clubs and slingshots) and different types of armor and shields to fight different types of enemies to achieve your goal. There is a decent variety of equipment and abilities, some of which change depending on how deep you are in the skill tree. Once we are in an area, we are basically free to choose the direction of our journey. As we go, we will come across ancient shrines where we will find small trials waiting for us that are specifically designed for that area and it's theme. We will also be able to find Crystal Towers, which serve as fast travel points. The completion of these towers will reward you with items that are relevant to the story. In addition to the shrines and towers, there are also "Ponpon Camps" along the way. These are enemy camps waiting to smash your face, and sometimes they are protecting a chest.Ancient shrines are the best activities, though. Entering one might involve solving a puzzle, a series of encounters, or a platforming timed trial, and they're consistently clever enough that I loved jumping into each vault, even when they were brutally difficult or I got stuck. To access optional chests, some require upgrading Piji's short skill tree. The physics-based nature of some of these puzzles can lead to some fun improvised solutions, like using my upgraded stamina to brute-force a jump. This has also led to some frustrating moments where blocks line up in a wonky way, but the physics are for the most part consistent. The larger vaults on the main path are also substantial and challenging, and each one has a gimmick of its own. Crystals are another important aspect of the open world. Blue, purple, yellow, and red crystals can be found at every corner and are essential for upgrades. Red crystals, for example, will help us to increase the power of our attack with the club. Purple crystals are used to create various ammunition for your slingshot and increase the damage of your slingshot attack. Yellow crystals will increase the amount of herbs you will be able to carry, and blue crystals will increase your defensive power, allowing you to take less damage.Another aspect of the game that really brought this colorful world to life was the audio design. The swaying of trees and grass and the natural-sounding gusts of wind all help to create a sense of soothing solitude as the player explores their own path. There's also the music, and while most of the songs don't stand out in any particular way and sometimes take a long time to restart, they still add to the sense of atmosphere and wonder of the world. The game's calming soundscape brings all of this beauty to life.Despite the above, I feel that the feedback on your hits in combat is a bit lackluster. It does not affect the scene as much as it should. This is especially true when trying to slingshot. The rest of the attacks sounded bland and anticlimactic compared to the satisfying thud you hear when you land a special ability strike on an enemy. Another point of criticism is the subtitles outside of the cutscenes, which are very fast and therefore hard to read.This adventure is filled with gods, elementals, powers to wield, and a beautiful world to explore. From the elements, to the gods that have been transformed into trees, to the sheer number of bosses and monsters, KAKU: Ancient Seal is a joy to play. It is a real treat for Tak (Caveman Story) lovers. It's got personality to burn, and both the puzzle and combat design are capable of supporting it mechanically. It's a shame that the platforming can be a little frustrating due to its "floating" nature and that it has a few minor technical issues, but these are both problems that can be fixed in future updates, and a quick reminder: it's still in Early Access. For me personally, KAKU could easily—and surprisingly—go down as one of the best games of the year once a few patches are released and some quality of life features are added.

_childDocuments_.review: It probably won’t win any end-of-the-year awards, but Kaku: Ancient Seal’s 1.0 release is still a consistently enjoyable (albeit shamelessly familiar) open world ARPG.   You are Kaku: a perpetually hungry tween caveman kid thing who underwent some impressive cosmetic surgery during his year in Early Access. After a rushed opening hour in which you'll chase a tiny pig while getting chased by a big pig before killing some medium-sized pigs, then combat a plague of dark magic, murder some pinecone-wearing “ponpons,” unlock an ancient temple, battle its stone guardian, befriend said stone guardian, realize your pig has superpowers, and unlock an interdimensional realm of jumping puzzles that allow you to upgrade your cooking and combat skills (seriously, that’s all in the first 52 minutes), you’ll settle into a more digestible pace of exploring four environmentally-themed regions. There’s the lava-covered Flame Mountains, sandy Dragonbone Desert, zombie-ponpon-infested Misty Swamps, and icy Howling Snowfield. Each region spotlights a supporting character, all of whom have a sympathetic backstory but none of whom amount to being very memorable, in part due to the game’s pretty predictable plot, and in part due to its poorly-translated script that’s brought to semi-life by oogabooga caveman voice acting.  But that’s okay because, (A) Kaku’s Zelda-based inspiration ain’t exactly drenched in Shakespearean prose, either and (B) you loved Switch-era Zelda anyway thanks to its fun combat, inventive non-combat mechanics, incredible puzzles, and massive, detail-stuffed world.   In these areas, Kaku mostly holds its own. While he can’t climb for ♥♥♥♥ and lacks a glider, Kaku’s flying piglet friend allows him to leap large gaps, disguise himself as a ponpon to make it easier to raid their many camps, and even envelop you in a big bubble that allows you to run across water. God help you if you touch deep water without your bubble, however (but a little lava is, for some reason, perfectly fine!).  Combat, meanwhile, benefits from a fun skill tree with dozens of perks and combos and even ultimates to unlock, but each realm only features a few unique enemy designs and a ton of reskinned repeats, meaning you’ll go from fighting white pigs to red pigs to blue pigs. But there’s more to Kaku than swine! During your explorations, you’ll encounter a variety of resource types that you can auto-loot with your slingshot, as well as a number of points of interest, including crafting benches where you can restock your ranged ammo, cooking pots to replenish health and stamina-restoring foods, ruins you’ll activate to unlock shrines in that interdimensional puzzle realm I mentioned earlier, and fast travel waypoint towers you can unlock by solving sliding block puzzles.  At first, I thought Kaku’s puzzle fun would end here, but then I reached my first temple and boy did my jaw and or balls literally drop. As was the case in with BotW and TotK, there’s a fairly remarkable leap in quality when you reach Kaku’s temples—not just for the creative jumping puzzles, but for the boss fights, too. Each temple boss features multiple health bars and movesets, but enemies won’t scale with your level or gear (at least, I don’t think so), so don’t feel too defeated if the first one kicks in your wonky cavekid teeth. Just collect more gemkeys and beat more shrine puzzles, get a corresponding HP/stamina boost, and then go even the score. Alas, in between these excellent temples, Kaku throws hours of unfun fetch quests at you as you sprint from one end of each realm to another completing errands for that realm’s featured companion. Don’t expect these so-called friends to lift a finger, however, even if you’re both ambushed by an army of ponpon warriors.  As for style, Kaku is a bright, colorful game with occasionally beautiful backdrops that highlight the game’s varied biomes. On closer inspection, a lot of textures lack fine detailing, but the overall effect is still a pretty one. As for music, I enjoyed the game’s lighthearted if forgettable, xylophone-heavy soundtrack, though it grows a bit repetitive as your adventure unfolds. Finally, the game’s sound design ranges from meh to bleh.  In the end, Kaku: Ancient Seal is a fun if overly familiar rehashing of what made the last two Zelda games so special (on a fraction of the budget). But, while Kaku in no way fills Link’s figuratively massive and literally tiny boots (dude is 5’2” tops), it’s a solid game in its own right and should net you around 20 to 30 hours of playtime. For $20, consider me decently impressed with Kaku’s overall value. I’m giving Kaku: Ancient Seal an aggregate MEGA score of 3.2/5 (full scoring breakdown from "Plot" to "Sound" available in the video review). Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Beautiful visual delivered trough a cartoon art style, imagine golden age pixar placed in a fantasy prehistoric setting+ Vast world to explore, the four elemental continent are large and content filled, rewarding exploration with quests, gear, upgrade materials, secret bosses and fast travel points+Likable cast of characters, from young Kaku and his friends to the four great elementals, each character is visually pleasing and while simply written shines in the qualities or villany they have to express+ Great quantity of gear, skills and rune upgrades to costumize your Kaku to great extense, from life stealing to glass cannon to pure rock tank+ Tight combat mechanics that use a simple yet effective version of a soulslike system, combo, dodges and parries are all at the player disposal+ Great platforming puzzles, most of the temples and ruins you'll explore have extremely enjoyable platforming session that constantly mix different hazards to keep the player interestedCons:- The use button is the same as the run button, a weird choices that will have you reuse an item you just interacted with simply because you wanted to run away from it- For some reason young Kaku can walk on lava for almost a minute but dies instantly in a bit of deep water :P- Use of stamina out of combat is a bit of a frustrating problem, considering how large the continent are, you want to move as fast as possible, it would have been nice to not consume stamina while running if Kaku was not in combat-Rushed cutscenes that do a disservice to the enjoyable story, it sort of feels as if they were done really quickly in terms of tempo and writing-The game has a serious powercreep, even playing at hard once you reach around the 55/60% of your adventure if you have not neglected your upgrades and stat increasing puzzles, young Kaku becomes an unstoppable prehistoric teen badass that nothing, not even that world Gods can even hope to defeat and while this can be enjoyable for some, it may make the game too easy too soon for othersKaku and the Ancient Seal is a great little Zelda-like experience that uses likable character, a great presented fantasy prehistoric world and tight well made mechanics to offer a 25 to 30 hour long content pack adventure that if you are a fan of the genre should not be missed.Fully Recommended at a 8/10
