_childDocuments_.review: A little short but getting strong Life is Strange 1 vibes![EDIT] EP1 didn't catch me enough to ever play EP2. Still recommend the game though.EPISODE 1 REVIEW:So full disclosure: I'm biased. I'm a trans woman and this is literally the first video game I've ever seen with a trans character that isn't just a punch line. So far I'm REALLY happy with how they've handled Tylers character. Extremely relateable. The transgender theme is a little more visible than the LGBT theme in Life is Strange 1 but it's really well written. DAMN is it nice to see a trans character in a prominent role.The episode is a little on the short side. 3 hours with lots of exploring. Not sure I found everything but definitely looked at as much as I could. It does suffer from some of the issues that the other Life is Strange games do such as occasionally excessively blunt writing. Something dramatic and unusual can be said and everybody acts like it's normal and moves on to the next scene. But mostly that's not the case. There are 3 areas in this chapter and they're all paced very well. Lots of info without over staying their welcome. The fantastic art style from Life is Strange 1 and 2 is here. Feels maybe a little less detailed than Life is Strange 2 visually but thats really just me nitpicking. The game has a gorgeous half realistic half painting style. If the game has a weakness it's the powers.They don't really do anything and you have no control over them. Power 1 is that they can talk to each other telepathically. That's not really used in an effective way in this episode but I can definitely see how it could be used for effective story telling later on. The other power is shared memories.You walk around the level and get prompts that allow both characters to see a memory at the same time. The memories are cool but... the characters are literally just remembering things. That's it. The mechanic isn't well explained either. Early on there's a part where you can choose what order to watch 2 memories. Later there's another part with two memories but suddenly your deciding which memory your going to watch and the other is not available afterwards. Can't think of a good reason not to be able to watch both and there ARE consequences to which you choose.Look, so here's the drill. You do NOT follow up a masterpiece with another masterpiece. It just doesn't happen. Life is Strange 1 is a masterpiece. Life is Strange 2 stumbled mightily (but NOT for the bs reasons everybody says!). Tell Me Why is definitely a return to form. Is it on par with Life is Strange 1? So far the answer to that is no. But it's REALLY good, it leaves you wanting more and there is DEFINITELY masterpiece potential.But that ending... damn! Thank GOD we don't have to wait months and months for chapter 2! I am a little concerned they're going to have to rush the story to cram it all into three chapters.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite not playing Life is Strange, this game is very similar in atmosphere and gameplay. If you enjoy a fun little narrative story about some twins investigating the fallout of a crime long past then this game is worth a go.This is  game of choice and there are numerous occasions you can make choices... But, the choices you can make are often small and don't have much of an impact on the overall story since they are typically about the way a character remembers something happening. I found  of the characters very charming too and I was convinced of their stories and personalities the second they appeared, even if they didn't play a huge role in the narrative. There are a few emotional beats and plot twists that will get your jaw dropping at points but on numerous playthroughs - since your choices can never change these - it gets old quite quickly. I don't have much to say about the soundtrack. It was suited to its purpose but I didn't find myself dancing along to any tracks like I have done with other soundtracks. The art style on the other hand is absolutely beautiful. And the game knows it. There are so many points in the game where you'll be sat down overlooking a gorgeous snow covered lake or watching the sunset past the mountains and I nearly missed a few dialogue options because I was in awe of the setting. The highlight is the storybook imagery though - if you're going to put some reading-heavy elements into your game, this is how you do it. You'll see what I mean when you play this game...Gameplay is really straightforward. I played with a keyboard and mouse but I haven't had a chance to test out a controller yet. There are no QTEs or short timers to answer a question, you may have around 10 seconds to respond in a conversation but this is plenty of time to consider all options. Tyler and Alyson are really great protagonists and I found myself siding with each of them at different times. They aren't as simple as "one good, one bad" option characters and I appreciate that in numerous protagonists. The story itself is quite slow and occasionally the dialogue feels quite scripted but as a whole, this is a nice, calm game to play on the side if you want to wind down wit a mystery narrative.

The story and plot that kept bringing up more questions than answers than being resolved at the end of Chapter 3 while still leaving some mystery to memory. _childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is very similar to Life is Strange 2 and features two playable siblings. Only this time around, they are twins and different genders.The characters are psychic and able to mindspeak to each other, but there are no powers in this game otherwise. Unfortunately, they reused the storybook motif from Life is Strange 2 in a way that seems highly derivative. If you played that game, you know the intro to episodes starts with a, "Once upon a time, in a deep dark forest...." and then recaps everything that happened in a fairy tale format with the human characters drawn as animals. Tell Me Why does literally the same thing, only it's more than just intro sequences. It's very unoriginal.The choices in the game do not matter and may as well not even exist. They don't affect the story in any meaningful way, and are often presented in such a way that is heavily biased toward one option. For example, you, playing as the brother can choose whether to forgive your sister for not coming to visit you sooner or to just be an A-hole and sulk about it. You already know by this point who the playable characters are, and I highly doubt that most players in a blind playthrough would intentionally create more conflict between them. There are multiple endings, and it's very telling that there is no meaningful choice when 98% of players got a "good" ending on their first playthroughs. You have to go out of your way to be rude and contrary to get a "bad" ending.In terms of story quality, I'd say it's passable. 7/10. The story starts out with an emotional scene of family violence and promises a mystery behind why it happened. The reveals and ultimate solution to the mystery don't really fit together for a satisfying conclusion though, in my opinion. Without going into spoilers, it seems like the writers wanted to have their cake and eat it too with portraying characters as both depraved and sympathetic. They also fall into soap opera cliches for family conflict. Overall, I didn't hate the story, but I didn't find any reasons to love it either. I'm not even going to bother with a second playthrough unlike the Life is Strange games where I was invested enough to go back and try different dialogue options.As with Dontnod's previous games in this format, they went above and beyond with crafting rounded characters of different cultures and backgrounds. My favorite character in this game is an Inuit lad. The LGBTQ+ community may be thrilled to know that one of the playable characters is FTM. (This is not a spoiler. You learn it within the first five minutes of the game.) And there is another well-developed queer character you get to interact with.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: I love it. It doesn't have as many artifacts as Life as Strange, which is my only negative, because I like learning things through the journal entries. It is dramatic but not too miserable. Great characters. It is hard to make choices sometimes because the actions have the opposite effect I mean to have and there is no way to go back that I've found, except the start of a chapter or leaving before it saves.

I tried to finish it but ultimately the game failed to make me care enough about what was happening to make me want to force myself to sit through another cringe inducing scene of having to put away store inventory and stock shelves while getting hit on by a dude with as much metal in his face as a Cenobite. :trainbowbarf:

_childDocuments_.review: is one of DONTNOD’s latest games and we can say it's inspired to the more famous . It shares the same concept: two intriguing characters having powers that affect who they are, the choices they can make and the world around them. The story, the way the characters are and their relationships are all shaped by your decisions.▲ = Positive▼ = Negative▲▼ = Neutral is set in a fictional town named Delos Crossing, in Alaska. It is a multicultural place, home of some Alaskan native communities such as the Tlingit, Haida, Tsimshian, Eyak and many others. The town, as well as the surroundings and every building or environment in the game, is portrayed beautifully, with much attention to details and small things that merge to create an immersive and atmospheric experience.The game focuses on two main characters, named Tyler (previously, Ollie) and Alyson, who’re brother and sister. Tyler is a transgender man who spent a decade in a juvenile detention center after being considered responsible for a family tragedy shown at the start of the game, when he was still a female kid (Ollie), not transitioned yet. When he’s finally granted to exit from the center, he rejoins his sister in a wholesome sequence and together they go back to their hometown, Delos Crossing, where Alyson still lives, determined to find the truth about the tragedy and try to understand the reasons behind it. In this journey, they will face many obstacles, and realize they’ve been lied to by several people. Will they succeed in finding the truth about their tragic past? It depends on you. Be prepared to find out how it all ends.One important thing to mention is that both main characters share a power called “the Voice” which allows them to communicate only through their minds, without speaking. It also gives them the possibility to relive their memories in a direct, powerful way. They can basically experience them right in front of their eyes. They will use this power at their advantage as they try to discover what’s really behind their tragedy.I’ve said at the beginning that Tyler is a transgender man. In fact, the game is brave enough to do a step forward and try not only to represent the LGBT community, but also discuss what being transgender means, how being able to discover your true self affects you from the inside and often deals with the problems this can cause with other people, relationships and political/religious ideas. Other things related to the same issue are also discussed: therapy, conversion centers, conservatism, lack of psychological support, the importance of family and close people who really understand you. There’s also a secondary character named Michael, whom you’ll discover later on in the game, who’s gay. You can learn more about his background story too, if you decide to talk to him in different scenes of the game. So.. the question comes spontaneous: is the game “political”?The answer is: yes. And the game doesn’t try to hide it, even if not the entirety of  revolves around this topic. It’s what the game is and you can’t do anything about it. So what I recommend is that if you have certain ideas about the LGBT community and you don’t want to give this game a try to understand more about the topic, then don’t buy it. If you’re willing to open your mind and to experience a story that also deals with this, then you’re free to try it.Apart from this, another issue you can run into is the start of the game. It’s quite slow and can lead you to consider the story boring already, without trying it further. The more you progress, the more everything gets interesting. At the end of the day, it’s a very subjective story. Personally, I liked it. But I can’t say for sure that you will like it too. It’s something you have to decide for yourself if it’s worth to try or not, based on what the game is about and your ideas. If you’ve never played a similar game and you’d like to try the narrative episodic genre without necessarily trying , I highly recommend you to check out the  series first and then come back to this.I would love to make a detailed, in-depth description of the gameplay but, unfortunately, there’s not much to talk about. Most of the game either consists of cutscenes, dialogues, or long walks and interactions with objects and memories through the power of “the Voice”. While the quality of animations and lip sync has significantly improved compared to previous  titles, the quality of writing in dialogues has seen a decrease in my opinion.But let’s talk about the core of the gameplay: Choices.They are the most important thing in the majority of , as they drive the story forward and progressively shape what your ending will be. However, in , I consider them a waste of time and a wasted opportunity. While the story itself can subjectively be appreciated, the choices don’t really do much in building the direction of the story, and in the end it all feels worthless, as if these were just a forced insertion in the game to let the story progress. There are only two endings to the story, and while the voice acting felt great, the overall package of the gameplay just isn’t enough in my opinion, as the value of your choices is tremendously disappointing. Expect a full story-based game but don’t expect your choices to matter that much in the end. is known and appreciated for putting a huge amount of effort in enhancing their games with remarkable, original soundtracks. However, this is not the case for . I’m not necessarily saying that the track selection is bad, but it certainly isn’t memorable at all, none of them was really magnificent and overall they felt basic and underwhelming compared to the previous titles of the same studio.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty decent, I didn't really get into the characters all that much like the LiS games. Hell I even enjoyed the LIS 2 brothers more than these two. I just couldn't relate in any way shape or form. That being said, the story was actually pretty gripping the further along it went up until the end. The endings were about what I expected. That final part and series of puzzles was pretty fun. I never felt particularly challenged but I got this game super cheap so I didn't really expect anything at all out of this. Other than another edgy DONTNOD story. Which I got and I'm happy with. This had better plot twists than LiS 3 imo. The music was unmemorable if there was much at all. The controls a bit janky as usual with these games. Some game break glitches requiring restart were present and no cutscene skip makes that REALLY horrible in some spots. Decent on sale, just be aware of transgender heavy stuff so if that's not your bag then avoid it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: Dontnod used to be one of my favorite game developers. They made the Life is Strange games, the first of which is one of my favorite games of all time. However, this seems to take a detour from their usual quality standards. I cannot speak to the quality of the entire story, because I could only make it through the beginning before I got too bored to go on. The game has that same classic Dontnod feel both in terms of visuals and controls, but the story is just not great. Dontnod has a history of tackling important societal issues in each game, which is good, and that remains true here, but that seems to be the entirety of this story. It feels more like a love letter to certain topics rather than an actual game. Another problem is that the characters are just not relatable. While the aspect of gender identity can be relatable to some, just going by how the characters in the story act, it's hard to understand them. After playing three hours of the game I still know very little about the story of the twins, apart from what was divulged in the opening exposition of the game. Additionally, the twins are both just not nice to each other. I get that sibling rivalry exists but it seems that every other line of dialogue between the two comes off as a jab to one and other or a backhanded compliment. It's hard to become invested in these characters and care about them when, from what you see in the first three hours at least, they just aren't nice people. I wish I could recommend this game, but I can't. This is an odd left hook to Dontnod's usual work and it seems that their quality is beginning to go downhill, just like so many other companies. It's truly sad to see. I was fortunate enough to pick this game up for free during a sale, but if you are considering spending money on this, just don't.

It also tackles some heavy subjects that might not be for everybody but seems to do so respectfully without trying to tell you what to think about it.Overall it is not a masterpiece of the genre but it is a nice experience if you enjoy interactive stories

_childDocuments_.review: "Tell Me Why" is a fantastic game with a gripping story that keeps you hooked. The characters are well-developed, and the emotional depth is impressive. Go for it!
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: Tell Me Why is like Life Is Strange but in a different way. In this game you get to play as two characters. You either get to play as Alyson or Tyler which both of them are heading back to their childhood home in rural Alaska at Delos Crossing. The twins are back in their childhood home hoping to sell it but instead find some interesting clues about their mother Mary-Ann. That's all I'm going to say without spoiling the rest of the game.This game is amazing and I love how the twins work together in order to solve the mystery of their mother. This game is quite similar to Life Is Strange. I definitely recommend playing this game. The 1st episode is free but you have to buy Episode 2 and 3 on their own. Luckily for me I got this game and Episode 2 and 3 for free during the 2021 Pride Month special.

_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: A very weak story overall. While Dontnod seems to want to tackle difficult and emotional tales, its pretty clear that their writing department isn't up to the task. The game starts by introducing one of its two protagonists, a trans man named Tyler who The key mystery of why the twins' mother tried to kill Tyler? What remains is a drawn out game where you're solving a mystery that barely makes sense, following characters who are difficult to sympathize with (both of them often getting into pointless bickering with each other and those around them), with gameplay that proceeds at a snail's pace and whose biggest moments could have easily been predicted hours earlier.I see a lot of people who seem inclined to support this game because of all the hate it got from transphobes. Despite the stupid reasons they may have for disliking the game, I advise against hailing this as some sort of milestone in story telling and representation. The game uses it's LGBT-positive elements as bait to get positive coverage and reviews, only to cast them aside in the first 2 hours all so Dontnod could tell a story that's mediocre even by gaming standards.I got this game for free and I still feel ripped off. Do yourself a favor and don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently played " Life is Strange " by DONT NOD which was followed by the second one, Life is Strange: Before the Storm developed by Deck Nine. The first Life is Strange had me at first with its setting, Max, its main character, her day-to-day struggles (but also, growing up story) living as a teenage girl becoming a young woman / art student, I was enjoying the story, that was for more than half of the game, until... the later part became , which was not done well in my opinion, and felt very sloppy and cheap.And Max’s superpowers which were never really explained nor made any sense (not even in a fantasy setting) would change logic out of nowhere almost as an excuse to move the story in different directions.This was not a " plot twist " but more like a lazy writing mechanic.I did like the main characters, Max and Chloe but in the end, I didn't like the story. A very different thing was the second game "Before the Storm" which was done by Deck Nine. You can check my review for that game for the details, but basically the game took the same characters but with excellent writing and the story elevated itself to unexpected heights. The main character in the game Chloe Price and her relationship with Rachel Amber was written in a way that felt more raw and sincere and didn't shy away from showing a heartfelt love story between two teenage girls. Even if that game was just a secondary story to the first one, it felt so much more meaningful and emotional.Tell me why is the second game I play from Dont Nod, and sadly I see the same problems I saw in the first Life is Strange. (still have to play the third and fourth ones)Tyler and Alyson are the two main characters of this story… It seems to be about them, at first, about their childhood being twin sisters one of them being queer and the other loving him no matter what.The story soon devolves into one of the secondary characters struggles, and so, Tyler as well as Alyson are practically relegated to the back, just being spectators (the same as us, the players) in everything that happens because the game soon devolves in just a long road through memories understanding the past of another character.Now, this could be perhaps a misunderstanding on my part, but I was under the impression that the game started as one story and ended up as another.The narrative was always from the brothers point of view, yes, but it was really about someone else.Maybe because of that, or just how the story was written, the main "story" itself about this other character to me always felt bland and uninspired. It had a thing or two to " reveal " at the end to the brothers but it was too little, too late.One of the two twins, Tyler being transexual, wasn't really something that was featured prominently. The game kind of markets itself at times as being " LGBTQ+" friendly and it even has a loading screen reminding you that they consulted with GLAAD about trans representation and also telling you that you can seek help if needed.It is a double edge sword I believe... because it certainly fills my heart to play a game with a trans main character since I love to play as a woman or trans or any other character besides your middle age/young man. But, trying to lean too much on it without being that much important, seems to be a disconnected narrative, putting the " label " to it to something that really isn't.Also, the trans character having “a tragic past” and being afraid of being himself because of how difficult it was being trans, while it is something realistic it’s also becoming something tiring and repetitive to see really quick.As a trans person myself while I value the struggles of being Trans shown on media, I would also like to see Trans people just being themselves, doing any other thing (other than being sad) having a relationship, being happy, being sad, being funny, being a good person, being a bad person, just being, a person like anybody else. And not be pathologized and put in a “box “because of being “trans“. That’s like assuming any gay person needs “help“ because they’re gay. I think that way of looking at trans people has to change.And, to be clear, this is not a complain about the story in Tell me why being " not trans enough " but more about appearing to be going one way but then going another way. If the story is not really about Tyler being trans, and more about this other character, it is completely fine, but then it should be more focused on what it really is.This is more a family drama; two twins have a traumatic family tragedy when they were young... they reunite later in life as young adults to take care of the family house and so they investigate what really happened.... oh, and one of them happens to be trans.If you want to play a game with a story centered on at least one aspect of being Trans I recommend “If found “a small game by dreamfeel which feels much stronger on what it wants to say to you and doesn’t hold anything back from telling you an honest story from an honest point of view.In Tell me why, it is important for Tyler’s character to be trans, absolutely. It defines much of him as a character. But the story is not really about Tyler, is about . So, in the end the message is mixed, it dilutes as it happens, and while the game is beautifully done, with some great visuals, some good music and nice voice acting, as usual by DONT NOD, the story falls.

The game handles a lot of sensitive topics very well and they do not feel forced or in your face, they feel like a natural part of the story. _childDocuments_.review: This game was an huge disappointment. It started quite well, to the point that I was hoping it would be a LiS1 spiritual successor (sorry Dontnod but LiS2 was just a big nope), but it was not the case.The two main characters had potential but turned out to be pretty bland, the story overall is highly predictable and the two main endings are actually just one ending with an alternative version that doesn't make any sense and invalidate the whole point of the story ().I guess some people may like it, especially thanks to the whole queer aspect of the game (Dontnod is well-known for this afterall), but overall it was yes, a pleasant experience, but not noteworthy at all. Graphic is okay though, and the setting (Alaska) is very nice. 5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend for anyone who loves interactive stories that really make you think. I was especially impressed by the developers who went out of their way to portray the trans masc experience with so much accuracy (at least for me, cause everyone is different :) So thank you to the devs who gave us some good representation!
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to love in this game. If this was a 10 scale, I'd probably give it a 6, because despite the game's beautiful environments and compellingly original story, there are some huge flaws in the design. First of all, no ability to run or change the pace of the game at all. Secondly, the lack of facial animations make all the characters look like robots (despite the excellent voice acting). The dramatic rise and fall needs a lot of work as well. Characters are angry or jubilant in very brief moments, which makes conflict seem a bit unrealistic. Otherwise, I found the game's world truly enjoyable to be in.One more thing: the local Alaskans don't pronounce Denali correctly. This is a bit embarrassing and clearly reflects on the otherness of the game's creators.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting story game with stunning graphics, good sound design, and a compelling narrative. However, the puzzles varied strongly in difficulty and most annoying of all, the game constantly hurried you along. You can't stand still for longer than a minute without one of the characters saying stuff like "what are you waiting around for?". As a regular player this would have been annoying enough, but as a streamer? This pissed me off so much as I got interrupted constantly from talking to my chat. It's unnecessary for such a pretty game in a scenic location to not give the player space to breathe and do things in their own pace. This is my second game by the same developers and this issue is a new one. I might replay Tell Me Why in a few years but for now I have my fill. Amazing though that they gave this game away for free in Pride Month, well on!
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: This "game" was free when I first played it (and was the main reason why I played it in the first place. Because it was free). Its about a story of two twins and their past. The environment looks good, animation is great but there are times when the faces of the characters didn't have the needed emotion for that particular moment (this is apparent in non-event sequences).Unfortunately, this game genre isn't my cup of tea. The artistic value and the portrayal of the story deserves praise, but I tend to get drowsy really fast on these things. I'm going to play this every so often but I won't binge play this one for hours. Once my curiosity on the story ramps up again, I'm going to continue playing/watching.All-in-all, this is basically an interactive storytelling 3D movie where your choices in-game will change the story/ending as it unfolds. If you like the "choose your own" adventure books and gender identity crisis, then this might be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: A thrilling game that kept me on my toes till the end! I loved the story, the setting, the animation. _childDocuments_.review: Almost gave it a thumbs up, it's not a bad game, but it's just not a good game.An easy-going enough game but short, choices don't change the story too much and both endings proved disappointing. A lot more could have been done with this game, their "power" should have been linked with some other supernatural elements, and without it it kinda makes their power pretty lame. Quite a good story (in theory), but not very exciting in the present time and had me bored reading the side stories. The biggest issue with the story is there is no real closure, regardless of which ending you achieve. I guess the developers did this on purpose to be like, sometimes these terrible things happen and we never really get closure, but this is a game that's meant to be story heavy. Sorry but the ending was bull-poop.This game is all about the beauty in its subtlety and slow approach, and it does that very well. Still worthwhile to play if you pick it up cheap but certainly not as cool as it could have been. Just ONE action scene would have been a great complement. An easy game to play when there's other things going on in the house so you're not fazed when you miss some dialogue but enough to get you to the finish line. Just don't expect to be rewarded when you get there.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and am rather surprised about all the negative-leaning reviews.Sure, this game does not feature the most intricate storyline or hours of playtime, but you'll have a good time depending on what you expect from it. Also: It's NOT Life is Strange, it's its own game, and can't be compared to the original LiS.When I played Tell Me Why, I was stuck in a depressive episode and really just looked for something to distract myself with. From an LGBTQ+ point of view, it's well-made and somewhat relatable. It actually gave me a lot of comfort. It's nice that you get to learn about indigenous cultures as well and the Alaskan scenery is stunning.The whole storybook thing was nice as a concept, liked the characters and art, but having to read quite a few passages got a bit arduous at time.I feel like some questions were left unanswered at the end which I didn't mind too much since I guess you're supposed to imagine that for yourself.Overall, it was a nice couple of nights I spent binging this game. It's not the greatest masterpiece of all times by far, but it is honestly just nice and humble. Thanks for creating one of the first games with actual trans representation <3

_childDocuments_.review: In its entirety, Tell Me Why transforms choose your own story games from dramatic, dramatic choices to a more subtle, gentle experience. There is a lot of magic realism in the game, but its most magical moments come in its human moments. While the first, introductory chapter sometimes feels shallow, later chapters are bursting with depth and shape your character's experiences more than their actions.In addition to being one of the first trans characters to lead a major studio's game, Tyler Ronan is also one of the first trans characters who is well written, and he comes with no strings attached. His transness clearly shapes him, yet he is much more than that.Alyson plays a crucial role as well, especially in Chapter Three of the game, although Tyler steals most of the spotlight, including two important conversations in Chapters Two and Three that break new ground in the area of queer representation in major video games. GamePass' hidden power is evident in its miniseries style presentation, the ending reveals, and the clever puzzles.The film is a masterpiece, non-technologically, but emotionally, story-wise and artistically.Second account I play it on and its just amazing!
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: "Tell Me Why" is one of these games that hit me right in the feels. If only it was a bit longer, then it probably would've even surpassed Life is Strange in my opinion. But even as it is, it's a very special game. The main characters are the twins Alyson and Tyler who meet again after being separated for ten years. As they clean out their childhood home for sale, they uncover the trauma and memories connected to the place. Which is also their superpower. They can visualize their memories together, as well as talk to each other in their thoughts. I really like that superpower, it totally fits the whole story. Instead of feeling like an extra subplot,, thingy, it's implemented really well. The relationship between the twins is probably my favorite thing in the whole game. Despite being away from each other for many years and being a bit awkward at first, you can really tell how much they love each other. Maybe it's the twin thing, but compared to the siblings from Life is Strange 2, their relationship felt a lot more fleshed out and "real". But not only the twins but also the side characters feel like real people. Whether you like them or not, they fit the story perfectly. My favorite side character is Michael - if you play the game, you know why (i don't think it's possible to not like him lol).Now to the more heavy aspects of the game. Without spoiling anything, the game opens with Tyler as a child sitting in a police station, claiming he stabbed his mother after she tried to kill him. So yeah fair warning, there is a very strong focus on the traumatic childhood of the twins. Also later in the game  deals with panic attacks, which are portrayed pretty realistic in my opinion.Tyler, who is a trans man, faces microagressions with basically every second person he meets, so there's that. He handles it pretty well though and there are no trans slurs or openly transphobic attacks against him. No dead naming either, which was a very pleasant surprise. I want more games like this that treat trans characters like normal people instead of some special thing, that needs to be explained like the audience is a bunch of three year olds. Last but not least, the sceneries are so so beautiful. Dontnod games just get more and more impressive with the graphics, it's amazing! I can't help but explore every location, especially the outdoor ones. Since the game is kinda short, there aren't many locations though. Basically, perfect game, it's just too short. I wish there'd be a sequel but that's probably not gonna happen. I'm really gonna miss the characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: This game has beautiful locations and environments. Characters are very likable and they feel like they could be real people. The story is alright, but sometimes it just felt too easy to uncover some of the secrets that had been kept from the twins, as the puzzles are not that difficult (if you take your time to skim through some of the short stories in 'The Book of Goblins').I had hoped the choices you made would have made a greater impact. The only choices that really seem to matter are the ones that affect the relationship between the twins.Overall, this game was a really great experience though. Playing the game, replaying for different outcomes, and completing all achievements will take approximately 15-17 hours, and seeing that it is a bit unlikely that I will play this game again before at least a couple of years, the price is just a bit high in my opinion. I still highly recommend this game for those who enjoy DONTNOD's other games.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly think this game could have been built with 2 extra episodes and essentially be called Life is Strange 3. It really gives out a LiS vibe in every sense: the environment (Alaska this time), LGBT representation, the narrative, the paranormal experience and of course the potential of a strong bond between protagonists depending on the player's choices.To boot, a much stronger reference to mental health this time It's a compelling story packed with the usual, intense emotional rides, but as many players have pointed it out, it does lack a bit of punch and plot twists, which is why I think a game befitting of Dontnod's standards could have used a couple more episodes to develop the story a little more. I think a lot of disappointment from some players stems from the fact that Tell Me Why struggles to live up to expectations set by LiS 1. I'd be wary of such criticism, as it doesn't showcase what the game is actually like.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: wELL, That game was a gut punch in the feels! Kinda flabbergasted. I'm not a great gamer and I enjoy easy point and clicks that have a good narrative. More often than not they don't actually have much of a narrative and are just a lot of puzzle solving and hidden objects. But this was so so so good. It touches on a LOT of triggering content and I related to the issue of having a now passed mentally ill mother. This thing had so many layers to the story. The puzzles weren't hard but they actually worked them into the plot and went ahead and fleshed out a back story as to why the character created the puzzles. The characters were well developed and interesting. The soundtrack was great and the setting was stunning.My only two complaints are that you could progress the story without meaning to when you were hunting for collectables. Hit the wrong thing and the story goes ahead whether you've finished searching or not and you can't go back and get them. My other complaint is that who the twin's father is was pretty obvious since the cast of male characters in that age bracket is so small and they rule some out very quickly. So by chapter 2 I knew who it was. Other than that this game kept me hopping and tackled some really difficult subject matter in a really great why. It reminded me a lot of a tell tale game with the choices and branching. I admit, one scene had me tearing up too.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: The game was better than expected. The story dipped into the LGBTQ line as a teaching moment only occasionally. It wasn't put there for ideology's sake, in fact it wouldn't have worked without it. It was integral to the story as a whole and understanding the characters, their motivations and fears. Reaching the resolution was rewarding and even the steps along the way were worthwhile stopping and taking in like the fairy tales and locations.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a game that combines a truly outstanding story with thought-provoking social commentary, look no further than Tell Me Why. This game tackles important issues related to transgender people, indigeneity and mental health in a way that is both sensitive and insightful. The plot is advanced in meaningful ways by incorporating these themes, making it feel like an organic part of the story rather than a performative gesture.One of the standout features of this game is its voice-acting, with Tyler's voice being one of the most pleasant ones I've ever heard. Although at times you can hear the echo of the actors standing in a room, it doesn't detract from the overall experience. The game play is easy and relaxing, making it a great choice for those looking for a more easy-going gaming experience.Fans of Life is Strange will definitely love this game, as the mechanics are largely the same. Players will find themselves making tough decisions and using supernatural abilities to navigate through the story.In conclusion, if you're looking for a game that is both entertaining and thought-provoking, Tell Me Why is a must-play. With its outstanding story, meaningful social commentary, and enjoyable game play, it's sure to be a hit with gamers of all kinds.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ok so far. It hasn't really interested me enough to spend $20 on each chapter 2 and 3. And this is coming from a diehard fan of LIS. I got absolutely emotionally invested in all three of the LIS games and they are some of my favorite games. The first was great, I rolled my eyes at the 2nd's political implementations. The problem I have with this game isn't so much the story, the story was actually starting to get good at the end of chapter 1, but I do not relate to the characters and particularly Tyler's struggles. I don't know what he is going through and it prevents me from getting emotionally involved into this game. These games are created trying to drive a point home so hard that the developers don't care if you lose connection with the main character or are sucked out of the game every time you hear a stereotypical line from a stereotypical character.The first 3/4ths of the first episode was slow-paced and boring and had no hooks and I kept feeling like I was just waiting for the end. Even their "powers" are just blown over like it's no big deal. The end of the episode was a good hook, but by now I'm already wondering if the other two episodes will be as slow-paced and hard to relate to. And at $19.99 an episode, the jury is out on whether I will buy them or not. Similar games are usually priced $5 an episode with slightly shorter episodes.I can't recommend this game because I don't even know if I will pay for the other two chapters. I was not emotionally involved after the first episode and I am pulled out of the game constantly due to various reasons because of the choice of main topic in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game to anyone. It has the original Life is Strange 'Vibe'. But thats all it is. After playing it, I see it only played upon my nostalgia of Arcadia Bay and offered no subtance of its own.You play as a transgender character which is unique, if you come from a certain political perspective you will find this game connects to you very well. In its defense I can say they did not take it as far as the could have, as far as for example Life is Strange 2 did take it.So if you are doubtfull of enjoying a game with a prescribed point of view you have to ask yourself if this story if for you to begin with.The gameplay is a strange mix of little busiwork, tiny puzzles and button prompts. It cannot be overstated how bad it is. If you place it side by side with other games in its genre you might see similarities. But you have to realise that "picking up the trash" in a narrative driven game is only exciting gameplay if you are either: Still contemplating on wtf just happened to your character or super scared of what might just happen next. the spell of the storyline is so easily broken that most of the time you spend uninterested and just clicking through the gameplay.The story is a crime mystery, supernatural experience, tale of two sisters and a transsexual transition all in one. It is all over the place. It shifts incredibly fast from one to the other, and leaves you out of the loop and in total disbelief of the protagonists and their reactions. Or of those of the people around them. This makes you disconnect with everything that is happening. (Alysson can tell Eddy a certain something, and then walk out the door within 20 seconds without it having any effect on the story)The setting of Alaska, its locations are beautiful, like i said in the beginning, this game does have the Life is Strange vibe. It will enchant you for a bit but theres just nothing there to hold ur attention for 9 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: This was an interesting approach to explore various aspects regarding gender identification, the fallibility of memory, the interplay of tangled cause and effect and interpersonal relationships. In other words, Tell Me Why told a realistic story filled with the messy nuances that drive personal decisions and outcomes. It did not get sidetracked into advocacy and let the player make choices that felt true to themselves rather than 'what the game wanted'. Thanks for the opportunity to thoughtfully explore so many shades of grey.

_childDocuments_.review: I found out about this game because a news article announced that all eps were free for June 2022. This game is quite heavy, but extremely beautiful, in graphics, audio, and story. I fell in love with the twins, immediately, and the environment and atmosphere made me want to hop on the next plane to Alaska. I am 100% convinced that, even if I didn't get this game for free, I would totally pay for it. Worth every hour.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't reviewed a game on steam in a long time, but having completed the game, I felt compelled to write something about it. I started the game since it was free this pride month, and have been wanting to play through a story based game lately. Being transgender, albeit transfemme myself, I was definitely looking to get something out of this connection to the story/characters, and it definitely delivered on that front. This is a very well crafted story that will definitely stick with me for a long time. The story is sad, and very relatable at times. I can't think of a time a game like this actually made me care about collectables by the end. The ending kind of tore me apart, usually choices in games like this are not *that* hard for me to make. I just wish it could've been a bit longer, just so I could have a little bit more time with certain characters. I cannot recommend this game enough, and will definitely be making some friends of mine play through it.

I tried a ton of troubleshooting things for over an hour and a half: run Error Check on the drive I installed the game on, Verify the Integrity of Game Files through the game's Steam Settings, move the installation folder from my secondary drive to my primary drive. _childDocuments_.review: A very artistic and mindful game, with extremely rich stories and for the most part, great representation. It felt gratifying to see Tyler's transition story. I appreciated the focus on emotions, empathy, grief and not knowing the whole truth. I appreciated how every piece came into place in painting the tragic portrait that became Mary Ann's fate. I absolutely LOVED the story book. I want to do this for my kids.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: This game is terrible; I think the first life is strange was an accident because everything don't nod made after in a similar format failed to capture what made it such a good game. Firstly, the most glaring issue is pacing; the first game always managed to get straight to the point, Chloe gets shot within the first 30 mins of the game Max receives her powers. Before the first episode even ends, you have the Rachel amber conspiracy, Max's powers, Nathans's drug problem already set up. You were never stuck in an area doing nothing, you could look around and read things, but the plot was always moving when you were ready. Your power is cut scenes in "tell me why"; you spend the first 4 hours wandering around a house. The most egregious is the convenience store where you have to walk around looking for cut scenes; it's tedious and annoying. The second problem is this dual protagonist; the Max/Chloe dynamic worked because you were Max first and foremost, so you had a degree of separation from Chloe. You also suffered solely for your choices. In this game, you alternate between shooting yourself in the foot and having a chip on your shoulder about it. You can make a choice as Tyler, then switch to Alyson, and suddenly for "plot," Tyler negates your prior intention and causes a conflict. It means you aren't invested in either because there are four main characters; the Tyler and Alyson you play, and the Tyler and Alyson in the cut-scenes.Tl;DR don't bother with this game or this studio; they don't know what they're doing.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: This game really helped me deal with some person issues i am going through, I enjoyed the puzzle without giving much away towards the end of the game, and the mystery throughout, alot in the game keeps your attention.It makes you think, in some parts it could have been better, but I am one of those gamers who does it for the fun of it, i use walkthroughs, as yano iam not that good....yet, anyway i like the issues tackled in the game, and finding myself becoming a dontnod fan girl.I enjoyed playing life is strange one and two, and having a break before starting true colours, I also enjoyed twin mirror, but that's another review, it too has it flaws, but hey just like us humans, the games we play cannot be perfect right? If you enjoy choice base games, and just having fun, with a bit of self psychological analysis thrown in this is the game for you, i played it for free, but would easily pay for it.Overall you see the characters go on a journey where what they thought was truth, turns out not to be, which mirrors real life, you see some character growth, there is a bit of a supernatural element which is always a bonus in with me.Yes a lot of things could have been done better, but its a good story line in general, yet its a solid game for those who play for the fun of it or like getting out of their comfort zones.I think were alot of people go wrong when gaming is thinking that each game is going to be the same or comparing them to another game for me, i see each game as its own unique world, and get submersed in that world,  with each world be incomparable to the next, this helps me take enjoyment from each game, even if yano i played one before that had better graphics, narratives etc...Yes having played both life is strange 1 and 2, and get the review which says this game and its choices do not have much effect on the ending unlike LIS 1 and 2, yet there is more than one ending in tell me why.And i believe it can be healing for those who had a abusive/absent parent, struggled with their own gender expression or identity, support of or part of the LGBTQIA+ community or have people close to them who have been or going  through these things, for me it was psychologically, emotionally and spiritually healing....but I am that type after all, lol.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mess. before I go in depth and spoil the story, if your even thinking of playing this, just don't. you are much better off watching a youtuber play this(if there even is one out there that has played this game) than sitting through the HOURS of gameplay. at least that way you can skip pointless gameplay and nonsense and just have a good time listening to the story. i'll start with the few (and I mean VERY few) things I actually did enjoy about this game.firstly I think that the team did a very good job with the visuals, a lot of the backgrounds are stunning especially the mountains and other scenic views you get in this game. The art style used for the children's book illustrations in this game are also really lovely, especially the secret loft you find nearing the end of the game.Another thing i have to give credit to the developers on is the book of goblins, i thought it was a really neat part of the game and actually ended up reading through the entire thing. You can tell a lot of time went into the illustrations and stories and making sure they lined up with the greater story the game was trying to tell.The puzzlesthat match up with these stories are one of my favourite parts of this game as well, i thought they were really neat and would have definitely loved to see more of them. I alsodo think that this game had some really emotionally compelling moments that are definitely worth seeing and Aside from all the issues i have with this game I do truly think theyhad a good story to tell here, just too many problems that got in the way of making it the great game it could have been.Those are, However, the ONLY positive things I can truly say about this lacklustre game. My first major issue with this game has to be the dialogue. So manytimes while playing this game I found myself having to pause and take a moment to CRINGE from some of the absolutely TERRIBLE dialogue. Cute moments between siblings reminiscing were fine but my problem was more with the language used in some areas, like how during a conversation between Tyler and Michael Tyler actually uses the phrase "oh my god shut up!!" like ♥♥♥♥♥♥ teen girls do in teen Disney films like high school musical.This isn't the only issue with the voice acting for this game either,the voice actor for Tyler gives such a poor performance it hardly seems like he feels anything at all most times unless he is angry in which he will be yelling. He's alwaysso monotone and delivers lines really terribly, this plays into the cringe factor of some scenes as witty banter becomes a horribly awkward moment of the player having to stop and go "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ why would you say that" because Tyler's line was not delivered correctly. The game also has really terrible timing with its dialogue, so many times did I assume a conversation was over because the characters have such a large pause between their lines. Tyler would say something to Ashley and it would take almost a wholeminute to go by before she would say her answer. Aside from Tyler though i did think that a lot of the other voice actors did a phenomenal job, Tessa had a really convincingmoment when she falls to the ground and begins crying for example. My second issue with this game is how terribly unlikable they make the main character Tyler, through thegame i had my issues with Ashley but she really stepped up near the end, accepting blame and realising some issues with herself that she needs to fix, this character development is something we do NOT see in Tyler. Meanwhile Tyler is a self centred,self righteous, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who thinks he is better than everyone around him.Tyler getsprogressively worse as the game goes on, making choices and decisions that hurt everyone around him in a sick game to make sure him being trans inst the reason for his mothertrying to kill him. Tyler shows time and time again to have zero regard for the feelings of others,literally sending his sister into a spiral where she begins hallucinating and having panic attacks. Any of the choices you are able to make for Tyler all feel wrong and you find yourself sitting back and just yelling at Tyler alot, I found myselfgetting so annoyed with him that anytime he spoke in the background scene where I was playing as Ashley I would yell at my screen telling Tyler to shut up. Hes so arrogant and self centred,even when his sister was breaking down in front of him, crying and begging to stop digging into that terrible night Tyler KEEPS pushing her! Having one of yourmain Protagonists who you are SUPPOSED TO LIKE be so terrible and just unlikable does not make for a good game at all. It made me really disconnect from him as a character because you just can't relate with someone who is such a blatant ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. There's no change in him by the end either to show growth, maybe the only part we see this is whereyou as the player can choose to accept the police officers apology and hope the family bond will get better with time but it just feels sour because of how blatantly ignorant Tyler has been to him this ENTIRE game, it feels fake and disingenuous how fast it switches up. I feel like this is the major reason I felt like the game just keptgoing on and on and on, I didn't like one of the main characters so I didn't care about his relationships or dialogues, this made the game feel longer than it should have.I'm not event the only person I know to feel this way, my boyfriend said the same thing and its the reason he couldn't bring himself to finish the game. Some of the visuals for this game also aren't the best. On a regular basis characters facial expressions just did not match with what their voice or lines were implying, clothes clipping in and out,and mouth movements not syncing up with what the character was saying.I think the game had a very good concept and a very interesting story but it was simply executed poorly, with an unlikable main character, bad voice acting, and all in a gamethat felt simply far too long it just was not a game worth anyone's time. Had this game not have been free i would NEVER have played this.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I ventured into Tell Me Why, I was unsure: is Dontnod creating a game with a transgender person just because they want to get fame or noticed? Because diversity is currently being internalized in the minds of more and more people and they hope to make an easy profit? Will and can they even present this important topic respectfully? In the end, I came to the conclusion that they succeeded in their implementation. Tyler's character is not reduced to his gender alone, rather it is part of his character development. This is especially evident in the first episode. Unfortunately, the overall storyline is weaker, which in my opinion is too short. In the last two parts of Tell Me Why, however, the focus is shifted and tells a well-written, tragic family story. In the end  I felt like being glued to the screen and enjoyed accompanying Tyler and Alyson on their quest for the truth. I can only recommend this game to all fans of the Life Is Strange franchise would rate it a 9.5 out of 10.

Maybe some other day when you're not emotionally vulnerable....Also the best and most sensitised way to describe this game in words would be,"The story of a trans man and his twin sister, who go on an emotional and numbing journey after coming back to their hometown, finding more and more about their mother..."

Many players have complained about the inactive role they have throughout, but honestly, you should expect that from a Dontnod game. _childDocuments_.review: First of all, the graphics in the game are very beautiful, and the scenery is also very good. Some details are very good, such as walking in the snow will leave footprints. The plot is like a movie, and then tells us slowly. At the same time, there is a method of combining fairy tales with the real world, constantly paving the way, and finally telling us the whole process. We are like Tyler and Alison, discovering the truth through the digging of the memories of the past, and then let ourselves bravely welcome the future. The final truth can only be explained from the perspective of other people, because their mother is no longer there. It's too long since then, and everyone can only provide a little fragment of memory. However, what we should understand is that the situation is not that bad, love exists, but everything changed too fast at that time. At the same time, Taylor has experienced so much, and finally found out the truth with his sisters, but also met someone he likes, which is a better ending. In any case, life must go on, and live with the love you once had.It's just a pity that the length is relatively short. However, I personally still like it very much. For those who have never played, you can try it if you like a slow pace.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: This game was obtained for free as part of a Pride Month promotion in June 2021.Tell Me Why is a slow-paced adventure game developed by DONONOT, the creators of Life is Strange 1. The game’s gameplay is very similar to LiS1’s, but features some new twists and a completely different story. How does it actually stack up, though?Gameplay is a fairly typical modern point and click game. Your character is in a certain location, and in order to proceed, he or she must explore the area to learn more about the area, discover a problem or create a plan, and find a way to solve the problem or execute the plan. It’s simple, but fun. You also have conversations with other people, where you can pick responses to what characters say. The controls for this can be a bit awkward, as you have to press a button on initiate a conversation instead of the response prompt appearing automatically, but it does allow for things like responding to someone while you explore instead of accidentally canceling a response prompt because it appeared just as you began examining something.The choices affect you make affect small details of how the story works. For example, being nice to characters will make them more willing to open up, while being a jerk will not. However, no matter how you play, it will have very little impact on the ending, which is determined solely by a choice you make at the very end and a choice near the middle of the third chapter. It’s disappointing to see that the developers didn’t really learn from Life is Strange and made most of your choices irrelevant at the end again.There is also an option that lets you psychically communicate with your twin during conversations in order to unlock alternate dialogue trees and ways to solve problems, such as calming down a situation that could lead to the person you’re talking to becoming belligerent. Unfortunately, this cool feature is underused, making it feel more like a gimmick than a proper part of the gameplay.The twins’ psychic abilities can also be used to conjure up memories in order to advance the plot. These are not only used to create in-game flashbacks to events (which is important, since this game is all about discovering what actually happened in the past with the twins and their mother), they’re also used choose how certain events played out. While fun, your choices don’t really lead to much.Finally, there’s a sort of “karma” system that tracks your responses on certain things. In theory, the idea is that certain choices that are nice to the twin you’re not playing as will improve their bonds, while ones that are antagonistic to the other twin will weaken the bond. Part of the ending changes depending on how strong the bond is at the end of the game. While a neat idea in theory, most of the “correct” choices are about sucking up to Tyler and saying he’s right, even in situations where he might be wrong or the answer is not clear. Only a few “correct” answers are about how Alyson feels, so the mechanic feels more like “how much can you kiss Tyler’s butt” like you’re trying to befriend a companion in a Bioware game than actually building a strong bond between the twins.The game’s story focuses on a set of twins. One of them killed his mother when she attempted to murder him as a child ten years ago, and is now leaving juvie in order to help his sister, Alyson, sell the family’s home. However, the events of 10 years ago are not what they seem and the people in the small Alaskan town the twins live in are unwilling to discuss what happened that day and the months leading up to it. The game is as it’s peak when it has the characters directly involved in the main plotline, investigating what really happened the night the twins’ mother was killed. Looking through old memories and documents to piece together what happened and using what you’ve learned to get the truth out of people unwilling to spit it out is very fun. Chapter 2 is filled with the nitty-gritty of the investigating, making it the most fun chapter out of the three.However, the game does not spend all of it’s time on the main plotline. In fact, the main plotline does not truly start until the player is deep in the first chapter! Instead, it spends a lot of time focusing on more personal moments. This would be fine if the moments were fairly short, but they end up eating too much time in the story. Having moments to cool down between investigations is fine, but these parts seem to drag on forever with nonsense like “slowly walk around the twins’ house while labeling things and listening to the twins make witty comments with each other”, “calmly explore a general store”, and “yet another dull romantic sequence with Tyler’s love interest”. These makes the game feel like it’s more interested in spinning its wheels than moving things forward. Life is Strange 1 managed to hit a good balance between investigations and more personal moments, so it’s disappointing to see Tell Me Why completely fumble it.Early on in the story, the twins (re)discover an old book of homemade fairy tales created by them and their mother called “The Book of Goblins”. What should’ve been a cute background element instead plays a vital role in both the gameplay and the plot. At some points, your characters will have to solve a puzzle, and conveniently, the solution is found in one of the stories in The Book of Goblins. The solutions are not just in the story, but also in the art included in the stories. These slow down the game significantly as you crawl though the story the game tells you to look through to find a solution. It feels like a hackened way to tie the gameplay into the overall story that just drags the game down as a whole.The Book of Goblins leads to another issue with the story; there are a ridiculous amount of mechanical puzzles in a cabin located far away from civilization. It’s understandable that the developers need to add puzzles to the game so there’s more to do besides examine objects and talk to people, but it’s pretty ridiculous that a two-story cabin seems to have as many obtuse puzzles and mechanical devices as Resident Evil’s Spenser Mansion or Raccoon City’s Police Department HQ. Did the twins’ mom work for Umbrella Corporation or something?The biggest issue with the story is how much it makes Tyler the center of the world without giving some sort of good reason why. Based on how the story acts, you’d think that Tyler is some chosen one that everyone needs to ass-kiss, but he’s just some nobody that never earns the characters lining up to stroke his ego. To his credit, he is the main agent that keeps the plot moving forward, but the amount of focus and love he gets becomes grating fairly quick.Tyler is special enough that he gets his own romantic interest, Michael. Michael is probably the most pointless character in the series. The scenes he’s in drag the story and pacing to a crawl and contribute almost nothing to the overall story. His voice acting is about a step or two about porn acting, and he dresses like a tremendous tool. Tell me Why starts off with an interesting premise, but seems to be unable to stick to what makes it work best. Between underutilizing an interesting mechanic, too much focus on one of the twins, and uneven pacing, the story and gameplay is just too uneven to really recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a nice narrative game by the creators of Life is Strange. Although it it not in the same universe, the gameplay mechanics and storytelling are roughly the same. It is shorter than the the other titles, so I found it to be a pleasantly length experience.Tell Me Why has you playing as twins, Alyson and Tyler. They are seeing each other for the first time in 10 years and are reuniting to sell their mother's house. They are burdened with a dark secret in which they killed their mother as she was threatening to kill Tyler. They originally thought that she was going to kill him because he wanted to transition, but they start learning that it may not have been for that reason. Now they seek to find answers on what really happened that night and the truth about their mother.Like most DONTNOD games, our protagonists have strange abilities. One is them being able to telepathically speak to each other, and the other is to playback memories of themselves to gather more information. However, just like normal humans, sometimes they remember things differently and the player has to decide what they believe is the true memory. Now I know most reviewers have groaned about SJW this and checking off tick boxes for the LGBT community that, but lemme just squash that here. I think that it was awesome playing as a transgender character in a video game. The writing in this game is not as strong as LiS, however, just having the representation is at least a step forward. Not every game has to be some 5 star home run, sometimes just the attempt is good enough.I think most of my writing issues stem from not enough screen time for Alyson's character. I feel the game focuses a lot of Tyler and Alyson barely gets the spotlight. I also feel that some story beats were rushed as some scenes that felt that should have been stretched ended way too quickly.The last of my gripes are some graphical glitches (had a phone stuck to Alyson's hand for one whole scene which was funny but distracting). I also didn't like the puzzles in chapter 3. Throughout the other two chapters I was fine, but in the last section of chapter 3 they bombard you with puzzles that are very tough and back-to-back and by that point I was just ready for the game to end. I also felt the ending reveal was slightly weak, good, but weak.Final verdict? I think this game is worth checking out when it's on sale OR if you're looking for a decent story with LGBT/Transgender characters. While it may not have been DONTNOD's strongest tale, it was still an enjoyable game for me and being only 3 chapters long, didn't take too much of my time. Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Short Review - If you liked Life Is Strange, get this; it's good!Long Review - See below:Like many other reviewers, I received Tell Me Why for free during the June (Pride Month) 2021 free download period. I was intending to buy it during the 2021 Steam Summer Sale, anyway, so of course I picked it up for free when I saw it was available. Even so, I would still say this game is very much worth the money when it's not free. If the game is still free to get and you're reading this, considering if you want to download it, I would definitely say "Go for it!"Without spoiling the story, Tell Me Why is a narratively-driven, cinematic, soft-adventure walking simulator, with heavy emphasis given to character choices and environment exploration. Created by DONTNOD studios, it is very similar to another title from the studio; Life Is Strange; both in positive and negative aspects. From the negative side of things, Tell Me Why - like Life Is Strange - is a bit clunky and slow, but that comes in part with the territory of being a walking simulator, and being "realistic" (i.e. if you were sorting out real life drama, you probably wouldn't sprint across the room to talk to everyone involved). There are many more positive aspects than negative, but it's worth addressing the media and review response thus far.While it may have spawned a lot of negative reviews (in reaction to accusations of supposedly needless "woke" representation, etc.), the fact that Tyler, one of the main protagonists, is  really doesn't affect very much of the player's experience of the game. It of course affects the story and the context of the game, and the actions made by characters both prior to and during the events of the game, but it really only affects the early narrative. Later on in the game, I would argue it becomes quite easy to forget the fact. Personally I found it quite refreshing that this aspect of Tyler's character could be very visible yet comparatively a minor detail, even if it does still significantly affect the origin of the game's events and the characterisation of the protagonists. But it isn't given more significant weight than it should be due, and many other aspects affect the characters in similar significant ways. Further, the fact that characters have mental health issues or belong to indigenous North American communities is an influencing aspect of some characters, but it does not significantly influence the game's story apart from its context, nor does it mean the game is "pandering" to any specific audience. I am personally in favour of the normalisation of these demographic traits.Moving on more to gameplay and game design aspects; it is quite slow to start, but like many stories that could be called a "slow burn", it is still very much enjoyable, and this does not take away from the capacity to enjoy the game (assuming you like the genre and find the story engaging). Like Life Is Strange, this game has a "supernatural" mechanical aspect, this time being the ability to revisit the memories of the protagonists to find out more about the story and uncover some mysteries. I feel this was done quite linearly, and I think I would have appreciated more "Easter Egg"-y implementations of the ability, but it was still an interesting interpretation upon how memories can be both traumatic and open to manipulation and divergence from "true" events. This is also reflected in the later story, where some "facts" to the game's narrative are somewhat left to interpretation or to player choice.While the graphics look a little dated for the game's publication date, it still certainly doesn't look -bad-, and the Alaskan setting means that the environments allow for plenty of scenic shots, which are enhanced by the decent atmospheric sound design and lighting. This is contrasted by a fairy-tale-esque metanarrative, with an accompanying in-game story told through 2D art created by an character related to the protagonists. This is seamlessly interwoven, and very much added to my enjoyment of the game.To summarise my largely disjointed thoughts: it's a somewhat clunky game with a good and engaging story, "soft" and enjoyable audiovisual design, simple but effective mechanics, and solid characterisation and character development. It is held back only by the inherent limitations of the genre and the somewhat dated-feeling graphics. It is obvious that the developers put a tonne of effort into this game, and I think it was evidently a labour of love, created by people who cared for the subjects they weaved into the story. Would I give it Game of the Year? Probably not, but it's still great, and I would encourage everyone to play it; at the very least, the raw dramatisation of events and people that could very much exist in the real world will perhaps be able to educate some audiences on nuanced topics that are often simplified or understood in most mainstream media, particularly video games.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet three-chapter adventure, Tell Me Why is another game by Dontnod Entertainment, creators of Life is Strange, about twins with a special bond of their own, and a dark past to revisit and come to terms with. Much like Life is Strange, the game is consequentially choice-driven, made to impact future events within the storyline.Tell Me Why, with its heartwarming, cozy moments and prettily rendered graphics and sceneries, boasts two protagonists, Alyson and Tyler Ronan, who have been excellently portrayed by their respective actors, Erica Lindbeck and August Aiden Black. Erica's emotional delivery and August's charm helped deliver the story to realistic ends, giving much life to it.This game is also notable in that Tyler Ronan is also the first transgender playable character from any major studio. Representation was so carefully done that it wasn't quite in-your-face, and that I found him good enough of a character to view him past his gender identity - it is part of him and his story, but it doesn't entirely define him. Tell Me Why interestingly granted me a degree of perspective about being trans that I haven't looked into before.Some issues I have with this game are mainly technical ones, like the characters just awkwardly snapping into position when they're about to do something, imperfect lipsync and character movement, which at this point seems like a Dontnod staple, and them mispelling "Manilla." To see such a mistake as a Filipino myself is quite bothersome.Still, the twins talking about turon and bibingka made me especially giddy - being a fan of both Filipino treats, hearing mention of them in any international media is a very pleasant surprise.Reflecting on the game, to me, it does present itself as a reminder of both how beautiful, but unreliable memory can be. With its charming leads and its mesmerizing Alaskan backdrop, Tell Me Why is an intriguing tale of family bonds, trauma, and moving on.I rate the game 7.5 out of 10.
