_childDocuments_.review: At first glance, I thought this was just about family reunion between twins. Turned out to be more than that. A dark story, twisted concept of memory here and there, a serious murder, about forgiven and hatred and what a person can do when it comes to his/her life & relationship within. Honestly, DONTNOD Team has put in this game a decent story. It hurts me when it comes to problems relating to family, and especially who we are. Thank you for making this piece of art. This game, somehow, hurts me like hell in my playthrough; however, I DID make the choice that nobody decides to take at the very end, and I'm happy with it. After what they have been through, Tyler and Alyson are still my fav twin this year, I bet. Thank both of you for making my 10.2 hours playing this game meaningful. I mean it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: I played Life is Strange this year for the first time, so yeah very late, and I loved it, it is now among my favorite games ever. After finishing LiS, I was a bit sad and was feeling a little "empty" because I liked the game so much that I was missing it, and then I didn't know what I could play, and I stayed without playing any single game for a few weeks... A month ago, I gave a try to Tell me why, because it's from the same studio, and I had not heard about it before. Honestly I wasn't sure if I would like it, but in the end I did, it is awesome if you like narrative games and emotional characters. The 2 heros are twins, they like to compare themselves with 2 cunning goblins, and their family and friends with animals, which results in the game in the writing of a fairy tale book beautifully illustrated by them and their mother. We use this book to solve the mystery of their past, to discover the childhood that led Tyler to transition, sometimes to solve puzzles, and to learn more about them and the tragic events that led the twins to be separated when they were kids, and to be reunited together in this story. They decide to investigate to try to remember and understand what happened to their mother in the past, and finally learn if it all happened because of them or not.Honestly I find this game perfect to play around Christmas. It takes place in wonderful environments in Alaska, with snow everywhere, mountains, a frozen lake... , but still it's very warm and cozy to be with the main characters in their house talking of the past next to the fireplace. The game is quite slow, you have plenty of time to enjoy the places and it talks a lot, but in a good way, like in a movie. I hope my message can convince a few ones to give it a try! There is no QTE.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: The first chapter is surprisingly longer than I expected it to be, which was nice to get a decent way into the story. Graphics are amazing, controls are good, story is engaging and interesting although a little predictable at times, and the voice acting and character animation is great. Upon finishing the first (free) chapter, I was keen to get back to the store to finish the story off...However, the ONE downfall is that the DLCs are about $29 each, and that's just far too much for what this is. I mean, it's beautiful and well made, don't get me wrong, but if you read the story book about the little goblins, you can pretty much guess the full story if you've played as many games and watched as much crap on TV as I have- so the excitement really comes from uncovering who the characters are (like when  ) and the little details behind what actually happened. You can get other FULL games by the same devs for cheaper than the DLCs here, or the plethora of other games along this genre/style for far cheaper with considerably more gameplay features.I recommend because I got this for free, and it was definitely an enjoyable experience. I'm sad I won't be playing or reviewing the rest unless there's a good sale on them. If I'm even still interested at that point.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: Tell Me Why comes from the same studio that developed the brilliant Life is Strange, and it’s a spinoff to that series in a lot of ways.Here you play as 2 reunited twins that have a connection superpower. Thing is, 10 years ago they got separated because one of them killed their mother in self-defence. At least, that’s what it seems at first, and you spend a lot of your time uncovering the truth of what happened and why, by relieving (foggy) memories, talking to witnesses and solving puzzles.It deals with some emotional themes, like guilt and revenge, and one of the twins is transgender, so it also has some identity themes, but without focusing on it too much. Compared to Life is Strange, the game has a smaller scope, with fewer locations and characters (Alaska was nice though), but that means the game is more focused, with less side plots. But it also makes the final reveal predictable. It has some choices, but they mostly only have consequences during the finale.While it’s an absolute must if you’re a fan of strong narrative-focused games, it is a bit expensive full-price, considering the first episode is free and the entire game was free during pride month. But with a sale, the price feels more balanced.

_childDocuments_.review: There is nothing interesting happening in this game worth recommending.The game starts with two siblings who meet after a decade of separation. You have no idea why they have been separated, or why they reunite. All you know is that they are going to look at their old house and make it ready for sale. It's complete boredom from the start, and nothing to motivate you to play beyond the intro.When I had no other game to play, I fired it up to give it another chance. The further into the story I got, the more little breadcrumbs of interesting mysteries I found. So all the hooks that I expected from the start where spread out along the story. At the end of the first episode, I had enough interest to keep going to the next episode. But just barely. The second episode was worse.The story in the beginning is about the siblings and their relationship with their deceased mother, and there are some question marks regarding the mother's attitude towards the fact that one of them is transgender. It's extremely thin. More question marks appear at the end of the first episode, when something potentially supernatural is seen. But is it supernatural or only someone's imagination? When the story about the mother has been dealt with, it changes focus to who the father might be.You walk around, look at things, talk to people, and watch memories play out as cut scenes (which rarely intrigues me). All for the purpose of remembering what happened a decade ago. And that seems a bit weird to me. The siblings seem to remember everything from the start, but still need to "figure it out" by walking around and look at stuff.So far, no good. There is really nothing to be had here. If things improve as I play further, I might change my review.

_childDocuments_.review: So far this is much, much better than Life is Strange 2. Characters seem much more well-written and fleshed out, unlike LiS2 where most came off as 2 dimensional caricatures at best. Still get a few stutters here and there like all DontNod games but 95% of the time I get a solid 60fps @ 1440p max settings. Landscape is beautiful and the various locations are all well designed and interesting. Choices mostly seem to center around the relationship between the twins, hard to say how this might pay off in the end but the system is compelling so far.Chapter 1 has me hooked and I'm looking forward to playing the next chapter this week. Definitely recommend if you enjoy other Dontnod games, this may be their best one yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Life is Strange, Life is Strange 2 and Before the Storm, and so I also loved Tell Me Why. During the first 10 mins the scenery is just jaw dropping, and continues to be so throughout the game. I'm also jelly I can't go live in that house. The imagination world and characters the twins have hits so close to home it's just crazy. I used to be similar, and in some way I guess I still am. It wasn't even my childhood home and yet I felt nostalgic from the moment of crawling beneath the house and finding old treasures from there, to the point of going inside and exploring every corner.Some people seem to be complaining about the Book of Goblins, and I'm here listening to that just like confused Jackie Chan. What the heck? Like, that's one of the best things in the game! When I found the book, I read it right away from the beginning to the end. When the first puzzle came and you had to check something from the book, I was like oh nice I just read it all, lol. Needless to say when I entered  I felt like a little kid in a candy store.When it was revealed more characters than the obvious two goblins of the book , the whole thing just got 9k x more interesting. Tell Me Why was - at least for me - one of those games you gotta binge play because it's so hooking and you just must find out asap what the hell is going on. Characters were interesting and relatable, and despite knowing the story is gonna be heart-wrenching in this game (too), and especially when it started to smell it was close to ending and I didn't want it to end, the ending felt still satisfying.Defo recommending and also gotta mention that there ain't many games I like so much I could take a tattoo of them, but Tell Me Why is that kinda game.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★½ (5-star scale)This was a pretty solid game. I loved seeing the beautiful landscapes of Alaska while playing. I loved Alyson and Tyler, and their story. I loved the artwork and some of the animations (the nightmare sequences were super well done, and the loft scene was absolutely beautiful). The voice acting was really well done, ESPECIALLY by the voice actor for Alyson. The gaming mechanism of focusing on memories and getting the option to choose which one was the “correct” one was unique. However, I feel like this could have been executed better in different ways: - First, when plot twists were presented throughout the game, there wasn’t really any shock value (or elements added to emphasize shock, such as music stopping, zooming in on characters’ faces, characters audibly gasping or being in denial, etc.). It was like these moments were grazed over by the characters, immediately accepting information as things became unraveled - which felt disingenuous to reality. - Second, the facial expressions could have been animated a bit better. It seemed like the main characters rarely made eye contact with one another too. - Third, I wish there were just a few more main characters added to the story. The plot twist at the end (when Alyson and Tyler discover who their dad is) didn’t really feel like a twist at all? Because there were so few characters, it was easy to narrow down who their dad could be - which was disappointing. Despite the negatives of this game, I did enjoy playing it. I definitely recommend this game to those who are big fans of the Life Is Strange series - since this was made by the same creators.

I honestly didn't know about the brother being trans, and I don't have a problem with that, unless a game/movie/show pushes it so much it messes up the gameplay, and I am happy to report that the devs did a great job with not making it hella LGBTQ and still making it an enjoyable game. Another big thing is the "superpower" the telepathic connection between the 2 is an intresting part of the game, DONTNOD loves gives super powers to the player, and I honestly like it, talking to each other in your mind while trying to sneak around, thats cool.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't bad, it is just way too forced. From the weird brief romantic interjections all the way to the suicide/homicide discrepancy. It feels like certain elements have just been put in or brushed over without them building up to eachother or correlating well with eachother. Unlike an logical comprehensive storyline that fits together well and keeps you immersed and empathatic towards the protagonist like in LiS or LiS:BTS the story gets divided by puzzles. Puzzles from their childhood stories. Solving these puzzles and understanding the storyline better requires a lot of reading. Turning the puzzles into the most tedious job ever. Even the main characters start to complain about it. Maybe it isn't as much the reading itself as it is the fictional stories that are boring beyond belief. If you don't like reading during gameplay don't buy and don't try.I think it stands without reason that having two main characters actually doesn't benefit immersion or the ability to empathize with them, their different recollections don't help with that either. Giving you the feeling that there is no progression and no truth to be discovered through memory. How can you empathize with someone when you don't know if what they experienced was what they actually experienced. The music is okay but it doesn't match up to any of the LiS series. Unfortunately I can't recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: **Tell Me Why: A Deep Dive into Mystery and Memory**Unraveling Family Secrets in Small-Town AlaskaIn the narrative-driven world of video games, "Tell Me Why" emerges as a poignant exploration of family dynamics and buried memories. Developed by Dontnod Entertainment, this episodic adventure game delves into the intertwined lives of siblings Tyler and Alyson Ronan as they navigate the complexities of their shared past.A Tale of Twins and TragedySet against the serene backdrop of a small Alaskan town, "Tell Me Why" follows Tyler and Alyson as they return to their childhood home to confront the shadows of their past. The mysterious circumstances surrounding their mother's death serve as the catalyst for their journey, compelling players to unravel the layers of secrets shrouding their family history.Memories as Key MechanismsOne of the game's standout features is its innovative use of supernatural visions as a gameplay mechanic. Through these visions, players gain insight into the siblings' memories, piecing together fragments of the past to uncover the truth. These visions not only drive the narrative forward but also challenge players to confront difficult choices that shape the course of the story.A Tapestry of Choices and ConsequencesAt the heart of "Tell Me Why" lies the intricate web of choices and consequences that shape the relationship between Alyson and Tyler. Every decision made by the player influences the siblings' dynamic, affecting not only their past but also the trajectory of their future. This emphasis on player agency adds depth to the narrative, fostering a sense of investment in the characters' journey.Crafting Emotional ConnectionsDontnod Entertainment's signature storytelling prowess shines through in "Tell Me Why," weaving a tapestry of complex characters and emotional arcs. Much like their previous title "Life is Strange," the game masterfully balances supernatural elements with real-world themes, inviting players to reflect on the intricacies of memory, identity, and family bonds.A Profound Journey of Self-DiscoveryIn summary, "Tell Me Why" transcends the confines of traditional gaming experiences, offering players a profound journey of self-discovery and introspection. Through its engaging narrative and innovative gameplay mechanics, the game invites players to unravel the mysteries of the Ronan siblings' past while reflecting on the power of memory and the enduring bonds of family.

_childDocuments_.review: This game from DONTNOD starts Alyson and Tyler, two twins who become separated after an incident occurs back in their childhood. 10 years later they get back together to sell their family home, but they release that they have a power that let's them remember moments from their childhood and sometimes these memories are different, but why???. The game is divided in 3 episodes, this format works amazingly since it feels like you are playing an interactive series. The story is really good overall takes a lot of time to develop, but when the story gets to a certain point it starts throwing punches like crazy, episode 1 is the slowest one, but it sets up what is to come masterfully.Pros:-The Story is Amazing-The Characters are great -Great Visuals -Low specCons:-By chapter 3, the last 30 mins feel kinda rushed, but does not ruin the overall story -Decisions should have held more weight - The areas sometimes feel small Neutral:-Linear GameThis is one of DONTNOD's best games to date, it captures the feel from Life is Strange, but lays the ground for more unsettling themes and a more mature tone. This game is an experience in interactive story telling topics like depression, respect, forgiveness, who you are, relationships, friendships, family problems and mental illness are all present. This is a game that should be experienced by everyone.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels as if made to service the needs of the LGBT community in the beginning, with slow build-ups and a general sense of wasting time, being served irrelevant options that moreso define your character as opposed to influencing the story. Life is Strange suffered from many of the same issues, both the original release and its sequel Beyond the Storm, but their stories revolved around more than mere sex transformation, instead at least trying to draw you into something darker and more concrete, touching on real issues. The quality of protagonists seems to be deteoriating with each release from Dontnod, no matter the praise received. Unnecessarily long dialogues and segments that make no sense from the get-go (why'd there be a puzzle to solve to permit entrance into any adult's chamber again?), Tyler and Alyson apparently being supernatural with their ability to communicate in the way they do, and all for nothing.Good luck with the upcoming Life is Strange, Dontnod. Make it more like the first and less like this. <3

_childDocuments_.review: First, to address the elephant in the room: This is not Life is Strange 1.5, it isn’t even a Life-is-Strange type of game. Don’t expect that or you will be disappointed. There are things that remind you of it but nothing more.Tell Me Why is a story about two siblings who meet again after ten years and have to come to terms with the traumatic experience that forced them apart when they were still children. The game is described as a narrative adventure and that’s exactly what it is, with heavy emphasis on “narrative”. Again, don’t expect action and crime like in Life in Strange. Yes, there is a mystery to solve. Yes, there is a supernatural power that helps the twins solve it. But this is a game about people and their relationships to each other and to the world they live in. The mystery is a very personal one and stays that way till the end.I loved how you get to decide how your character acts and develops. I think if you want to you can make them a total jerk. In the end you decide how the twins close the chapter of their childhood.The supernatural aspect takes a backseat in all of this. It is there and it plays a part in solving the mystery, but most of the time it only provides clues. What I found great was that the developers integrated the fact that memories aren’t always reliable. It adds a nice touch that forces you to think about what the twins remember.The most important part of the game are the people. How they act around and think about each other. How relationships can be poisoned or saved by them. And if they let memories dictate how they live today. For me it was a potent mix that pulled me into the story very well.Then there is Alaska. The game loves to depict the beauty of the land and takes its time showing it off, especially at the beginning.  I spent quite some time just looking around admiring the scenery. But it may not be everyone’s cup of tea.The only thing I think needs an overhaul is the timer when you have to decide something. Not all decisions are timed, so you don’t expect it when it first happens, and the timer is really, really easy to overlook. It is very small and not where I expected it to be. But then that may just be me.To wrap this up: If you like to lean back and take your time exploring places while looking for clues and talking to people, then this is a game for you. If you like heart-breaking mysteries and decisions with consequences, then it is for you. But if you want another Life is Strange, then maybe stay away. It is very possible that you will be disappointed.

With that said, this is an incredibly beautiful and deeply emotional story with likeable characters, pleasant voice acting, and an enjoyable plot. The music was well placed and well chosen, helping to drive the mood in the direction the story felt it was going, without overshadowing the environmental ambiance. _childDocuments_.review: Got this game when offered free in June for Pride. I really enjoyed it - it's not perfect and doesn't flow quite as nicely as Life is Strange did, but well worth playing. The flaws are mostly minimal - bit of awkwardness controlling the characters, occasional freezing (on my PC at least, and only for a few seconds). The first episode was a little lacking, but things picked up for the second. I suppose there could've been a bit more interactivity on the whole. The cut scenes were many, possibly too much for some, but at least the story was engaging enough. By the end up the first chapter, I was engaged with the story and had to keep playing. The setting is beautiful and peaceful, and the mechanic of the story book was delightful.I found that the characters were portrayed respectfully and maturely; nothing exploitative, just real life. Nothing is "shoved in your face", as a few other reviewers have suggested. Don't order a salad then complain that there's lettuce on your plate.I can't remember how much this was full price, but certainly do pick this up if it's on sale. Again, I didn't enjoy this quite as much as Life is Strange and I think it was a little shorter, but I definitely enjoyed and do recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really hoping to like this game since Life is Strange was one of my favorite games and had one the best stories in any videogame I have ever played. So my expectations were honestly high. However, despite the game looked good and the voices and acting were pretty impressive, the story behind it was dumb, dull and unintesresting. None of the characters are likeable, not even the main characters. There is nothing you can really think of to connect or relate to with them, as opposed to those from LiS for instance. Here they do not have personality, and many are just secondary ones with absolutely no relevance whatsoever in the game. Although it touches upon many controversial issues (suicide, transgender, alcoholism, etc...) many situations feel forced, not making sense or feeling too real, as though they were just fillers. But the most important thing about this game that really got up to my nerves was the pace of the gameplay. It is extremely slow and boring and 90% of the time you basically do nothing but either passing lines and reading or walk around looking for objects or persons to interact with, most of which are completely skippable and/or irrelevant. Sometimes you can even end up getting stuck in a loop conversation that cannot be skipped, or just have to walk at a very slow pace to one place to the other, or end up passing an invisible no-return point and you miss whatever you left behind. At some point, without realizing I was yawning and wishing the game ended asap to move on. I thought, well maybe it gets better and the story has a big turnout in the end or there is a twist-plot or something. But I was wrong, the end is meh and it all comes down to basically choosing what to believe or what you think is more likely to have have happened. The "remember things" ability seemed interesting and could have been something quite useful, similar to what happened in LiS with Max and the ability to go back in time. However, in TmW it only serves to see short flashbacks, nothing more, quite a waste to make something cool out of it honestly...Finally, decisions do not matter, maybe one or two at some points and very minor, but the big majority do not go beyond having slightly different conversations or lines from specific characters without any influence on the story. Overall, it was quite a disappointment, boring game, bad story and forgettable characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, I was quite apprehensive to play Tell Me Why for a while. The trailers didn't particularly entice me; I wasn't jumping at the opportunity to explore an overly-saturated indie sub genre for the sake of hearing a trans kid argue with his twin sister. Furthermore, I was very underwhelmed with the second season of Life is Strange. Despite the first Life is Strange being one of my favorite games ever, I had kind of moved on from DONTNOD as a developer. With a bit a dry spell in games that I wanted to play, and finding myself repeatedly going back to old favorites, I noticed Tell Me Why was on sale. Given the fact that it had been a while since I played a slow-paced story driven game, I decided to take the plunge. I'm glad I did, as it proved to be much more than I anticipated, and I found myself serendipitously engrossed in its world, story, and characters. I'll preclude this by saying that it's really best to go into Tell Me Why knowing as little as possible. In light of that, I'll be very vague in expressing my thoughts. The most important thing to realize is that this isn't simply a story about identity or changing people's beliefs; that is one aspect of it, yes, but the core of the story is actually about uncovering the truth behind a dark and twisted mystery. I wasn't expecting this at all. I desperately wanted to finish the game just so that I could put all of the pieces together and find out what the hell was going on. The game also dives deep into psychological horror and trauma in an unfiltered and unabashed fashion that feels almost intoxicating. Playing through the chapters felt like peeling a never-ending onion, as more and more layers to the intricate tale are continually revealed. Somehow, at the end of it all, there is real closure (at least in my playthrough with my choices), which was certainly satisfying. It's worth noting, however, that player choices may lead to a resolution that feels incomplete (at least in my opinion). This comes from doing some research into the possible endings. The animation is mostly superb. A number of the environments are oozing with detail. There were some instances in which I thought the lighting or color pallet felt a bit off, but overall the presentation adds quite a lot to the experience. The voice acting is also a highlight (despite the fact that some of dialog doesn't flow very well), with emotional scenes handled beautifully by these talented actors. The characters in the game get far more interesting as the hours play out. The two leads, Alyson and Tyler, are noticeably better than I was anticipating. Whether they're joking, being sentimental, arguing, or fraying at the seams, their expressions feel genuine and authentic.  There are a number of bugs in the game. This is where you might expect a person to say, "they don't really take away from the experience though"...but that is definitely not the case here. Visual bugs were annoying and distracting (although, they were very infrequent). In one case, Alyson and Tyler literally got stuck against a wall together, and neither could move or progress, causing me have to restart the game and redo that whole segment. The audio has the most issues, as sometimes Alyson and Tyler had conversations out of earshot of each other, and I literally couldn't hear what the other was saying. This happened far too often. Truthfully though, I'm far more impressed with Tell Me Why than I would have ever expected. It was absolutely a story that I'm glad I've experienced, and I was gripped almost the entire way through. It's by no means a revolution in the "episodic walking simulator" sub genre of adventure games, but it's without a doubt worth slowly moving around in circles hearing random thoughts about random crap in order to unravel the convoluted web of this excellent narrative.

I was also really excited about Tyler, the trans guy protagonist, so that was also a big selling point.While some of the dialogue is cheesy/cringey, ultimately I found the story to contain a very compelling mystery. The first episode felt a bit slow, but revelations at the end of episode 1 got me hooked. KEEP PLAYING if you're finding it a bit boring. The game is very similar in gameplay/format to Life Is Strange or those made by Telltale Studios. It's WSAD/point-and-click action with some choices peppered throughout each episode. Your choices mostly manipulate the character relationships vs the story itself.The puzzles are pretty fun and not overly complex, though they do require reading some in-game text.Visually the game is gorgeous and incredibly detailed. It makes me want to visit Alaska. Not just the environments, but the designs of the puzzles, the effort put into the story book crafted by the siblings' mother, etc. It's all very beautiful.The only minor complaint, and I'm not sure if this counts as SPOILERS, but...Your choices can determine whether or not the siblings become closer or grow apart. What that means in terms of game mechanics is you have to agree with whatever your sibling says. If you're playing Tyler, you have to agree with whatever memory/opinion Alyson has. If you're Alyson, you have to agree with whatever Tyler says. If you disagree, you grow farther apart. I suppose that is a fairly straightforward system, but it lacks nuance.All in all though there was a lot of effort and love put into this game. Most every character you meet is quite layered, and if you fully explore the world by interacting with every object and/or exhausting as many dialogue options as possible, you'll learn quite a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly positive. If you are looking for a game to play involving beautiful scenery, to play as two different people along the way, and story based games; this is for you. I play this at work, so the fact that it follows a story where you don't have to be too directly involved helps. Really enjoyed the mystery puzzle feel, without it being a Nancy Drew game. I liked this better than Life is Strange, but I didn't like how you felt inclined when playing as one twin to side with the other. Also the potential love interest for Tyler looks like they need some work on. The graphics are beautiful except for the person's terrifying, 'cow looking at an oncoming train' expression. All-in-all, its really easy to feel for these characters, and honestly made me feel a little bit different about my own siblings. I think the concept of chosen family was also a really great touch to this game. I wish you could skip scenes though. There's been times I was playing on my laptop then when I got to my desktop, only part was saved. So unless I'm missing something, I would really like being able to skip scenes. Like an 8/10. Would buy again.

_childDocuments_.review: These are just some of the feelings which are strengthened in this title, where a pair of siblings return to their roots amongst the snow-covered Delos Crossing, a town located in close approximity to Juneau, Alaska, to not only face their past, but also to prepare for what is yet to come. Developed by the creators of Life is Strange,  if you enjoy episodic adventures with just the right amount of supernatural, I would highly recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much I could say about this game, but overall? Made me super emotional, but I loved every second of it. I streamed and played with my two best friends and it really helped having a consensus of what we wanted to answer and how. The puzzles and stories were cute and very interesting! _childDocuments_.review: As a trans (NB) person, I have actually never seen the subject handled better in media, especially not in video games.  The first chapter perfectly captured both the reactions one gets to the subject from more close-minded, conservative people and the non-reactions you get from people who want to be supportive but also just don't know how to broach the subject. The story gets pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dark but it's honestly an amazing story from start to finish, I lost count of how many times I teared up. I love the Life is Strange titles but always felt they were very hit and miss when it came to talking about difficult subject, but this time the devs truly nailed it.

_childDocuments_.review: (beat the story at a friend's place and replayed the free episode 1 myself hence the low time)First of all, I see many people came here expecting a video game. This is NOT a video game, despite what the devs may say. It's an interactive story. As if you're watching a movie that occasionally lets you move its characters and make some choices for them. So if you're not okay with that, don't play this.Second thing I see is many people disliking the game just for daring to tell a different story that's almost never told in popular media. And this story feels real (excluding  of course). Look, if you:- haven't had any childhood trauma,- are cisgender,- have no siblings,- have no experience with anxiety,- never moved places and/or had to sell the old place,- didn't grow up in a broken family,- or didn't spend your childhood in a tiny conservative town, it's definitely gonna be hard to relate to the story and it probably won't leave as much of an impact on you as it would if any of the above things happened to you. Especially if you have conservative beliefs, you'll see the devs' telling of a story with trans and gay people as propaganda, which I can definitely tell you this isn't. These people do exist in real life, you just haven't allowed yourself to meet and get to know them as human beings. Besides, the focus of the story isn't even on Tyler, and what there is of his part has definitely been interwoven in a realistic and non-invasive way.Of course, the endings are Also, the graphics seem a bit nicer than LiS (though they can definitely be even better), and the puzzles you encounter are a nice addition as well as not being that hard to begin with. All the goblin art is also super freakin' adorable! Love the chosen art style.Some things I do admit suck are how cutscenes aren't skippable (especially when you're not watching them for the first time) and how it auto-pauses when you tab out of the game. Or how you can't run everywhere. But I think the skippable cutscenes could easily be added with an update? All in all, Steam STILL doesn't have a scale rating so I'm just gonna write mine here, 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an incredible, thought-provoking experience. Its narrative perfectly illustrates how childhood trauma can distort our perception of reality into adulthood. It also encapsulates the unsettling truth that most things in life aren't black and white and other people are rarely simply friend or foe. It has characters that are the most accurate representation of people who are LGBTQ that I've ever seen in video games so far. Also, I found the mental health aspect very relatable, particularly in the final episode. If you're someone that likes character-centric, walking-simulator type games that take you on a bit of an emotional rollercoaster then I would definitely recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is much more grounded than Life is Strange (you could even say "boring," if you're looking for thrills and plot twists), but ultimately I had a much better experience with this game than LiS. TMW is a wonderfully character-focused story that explores how our memories, despite being so pivotal to who we are as people, are easily subjected to our beliefs and imagination. It may be less heart racing than LiS, but TMW's limited story allows it to nicely tie up all its knots in satisfying ways (can't sayLiS did the same). I especially love how Tyler's trans identity is explored--you could accuse it as being preachy at times, but ultimately it is treated with respect and accuracy, and that's all I really ask for.My one gripe: I wanted to get myremaining achievements, and without thinking I pressed New Game. Doing this deletes your entire save file, including all your collectibles. In fairness, the game did warn me, but I had assumed New Game would just drop me in the beginning of the game, not delete everything!! Why would anyone want to delete their entire save file that easily?! Oh well, it's just achievements, I can just watch YouTube for the extra content. Let my mistake be a warning to you all.

_childDocuments_.review: Dontnod have a talent to build their whole games about a narrative, and at the same time have that narrative be complete piece of dog waste.While not as disastrous as whatever the hell LiS2 was, this one just wasn't good either. Pacing is once again awful, even more panning shots of silence, even more "flavor" dialogues that taste like tap water, even less choice with consequence, and even less at stake. This game despite featuring a transgender protagonist is not immune to criticism, HELL, I'd say it's worse that their representation is realized in just a really bad game.Since it's a Dontnod game, we had picking up groceries in 1st ep, instead of collecting bottles, what a "welcome" return of the dullest sections in their games. All locations feature the objects that your character just looks at and comments in the utmost obnoxious and obvious ways. Nothing of value, just like way back when I played LiS1. I almost couldn't believe that terrible formula didn't change at all.Between that and dialogues about constant reminescing (also featured in all of their ♥♥♥♥♥♥ games), you get choices to make (that are compared to choices of other players), which will give a different animation, dialogue, at best a different scene, mostly of no real consequence. I literally can't believe that the devs decided to devolve their gameplay ever since 1st game, Sands of Time rewind in an adventure game was the only thing setting that apart, that and a cop-out of an impactful choice resulting in character's death, or survival (if she survived, you got just one scene with her near the end, phenomenal, ground-breaking).So in LiS2 and Tell Me Why, such a big thing is not there at all, neither a real mechanic, or a choice of similar level. In both you decide the ending in the last episode, just like you can decide to be a communist mass murderer in LiS 1, in order to save your selfish waifu.Here you get to decide, the events of the past? It's weird, but the characters power is remembering stuff wrong, and then deciding which is right (sometimes it's just simply wrong, without a choice). They also have telepathy, nothing original with it, they just can communicate over short distance, instead of needing to whisper to their ears.The characters are also once again ranging from annoying, to dumb, to surface level, to literal straw-men, to walking contradictions. You can only get snippets of good things about their writing, in the bigger picture - they're just tools, whose personality is just their member berries about the past they can't stop spewing throughout the game.Funnily enough, the locations on later episodes are reused all the time, and also the siblings here are represented by goblins, copied from sibling wolves in LiS2, really makes it feel all the more fresh.The sounds are there, nothing special, you will 98% of the time just hear yapping. Music is ambient, mixed with the alternative bands copyright stuff sprinkled here and there. Once again, very original, never before done in their game.The visuals is the only thing I have real praise for, the improvements are huge. The face textures finally don't look like a muddy PS2 mess. Animations are better, environments as well, probably mocap was used, since faces are the most striking difference during the playthrough.So, I played 1st ep for free, saw rest of the game on playthroughs online. Anyone can play the first ep really, see what they think about it. Rest of it is definitely not worth the money, seeing it done 3rd time in a row, really makes me think that LiS 3 will once again be cut from the same template, with once again - nothing worthwhile added.BUT - most importantly, I would rather see next 1000 copies bought of Tell Me Why, than see another one purchase of LiS 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)"Tell Me Why," developed by Dontnod Entertainment and published by Xbox Game Studios, is a captivating narrative adventure that intertwines a heartwarming story with a touch of the supernatural. From the creators of "Life is Strange," this emotionally charged game offers a poignant exploration of family, memories, and identity, leaving players deeply moved and engaged throughout the journey.Set in the small, picturesque town of Delos Crossing, "Tell Me Why" follows the lives of twins Tyler and Alyson Ronan, who reunite after ten years apart. Players take on the roles of both siblings, exploring their shared past and uncovering the truth behind a tragic incident that shattered their family. The storytelling is masterful, gradually revealing secrets and intertwining the threads of the twins' memories, which players must piece together to uncover the full picture.What sets "Tell Me Why" apart is its focus on character development and relationships. The bond between Tyler and Alyson is beautifully portrayed, and players become emotionally invested in their journey as they reconnect and heal old wounds. The game's writing is heartfelt and authentic, tackling sensitive themes with grace and empathy, making it a poignant experience that resonates with players long after the credits roll.The use of supernatural elements adds an intriguing layer to the story. The twins share a unique ability to communicate telepathically, allowing players to revisit past events through their memories. This mechanic not only serves as a gameplay device but also adds a surreal and dream-like quality to the narrative, making "Tell Me Why" stand out as a memorable and imaginative adventure.Visually, "Tell Me Why" is a treat for the eyes. The detailed environments and character animations bring Delos Crossing to life, immersing players in the serene beauty of the Alaskan wilderness. The game's art style complements the emotional tone, reflecting the melancholic and nostalgic atmosphere throughout the story.In terms of gameplay, "Tell Me Why" strikes a harmonious balance between exploration, puzzle-solving, and decision-making. The puzzles are cleverly woven into the narrative, offering just the right amount of challenge without disrupting the flow of the story. The decisions players make have real consequences, affecting character relationships and shaping the narrative's outcome, encouraging multiple playthroughs to explore different paths.While "Tell Me Why" is an unforgettable experience, it is not without its minor flaws. Some players may find the pacing to be a bit slow, particularly in the early chapters, as the game meticulously sets the stage for the emotional journey that lies ahead. Additionally, certain technical issues and occasional graphical glitches may temporarily break immersion, but they do not detract significantly from the overall experience.In conclusion, "Tell Me Why" is a powerful narrative adventure that showcases Dontnod Entertainment's prowess in storytelling. Its poignant narrative, deep character development, and imaginative use of supernatural elements create an emotional rollercoaster that leaves players questioning their assumptions and reflecting on the nature of family and identity. If you are a fan of captivating, emotionally-driven games that resonate on a personal level, "Tell Me Why" is an absolute must-play.Pros:Masterful storytelling and character developmentTouching exploration of family, memories, and identityImaginative use of supernatural elementsBeautifully detailed visuals and art styleMeaningful decision-making and multiple story pathsCons:Pacing may feel slow for some playersOccasional technical issues and graphical glitches

_childDocuments_.review: I downloaded this game when it was free in June because my coworker told me he thought I'd like it, and after being directly recommended it a second time, I binge played it in less than 24 hours. I expected that I would like it, but I wasn't prepared for it to become one of the best stories that I've ever played in a video game.It wrecked me emotionally in the best way possible; I was able to predict bits and pieces of the full picture the further I progressed in the game, but there were still parts that left me shocked, and many times where I had to choke back tears while I was playing.I can't recommend this game enough, especially if you enjoy LGBT+ representation in your media. But after spending my time with it, I don't regret my time with it at all. A beautiful game, through and through.GOBLINS4LIFE

_childDocuments_.review: So the story isn't terrible, actually pretty good, but I do have some complaints.You play as two characters, and the girl is, to put it plainly, a wimp who can't be confrontational.These characters have set personalities, which means you can't do anything they wouldn't do. Which makes sense, but most the games I play, and I reckon most the games others play, allow you to approach a situation how you would.It's very stressful, to say the least, playing a character that doesn't know how to stand up for herself. Very similar to when your movement speed in a game is so slow, and you can yell at the screen to go faster, but you'll still be going at a slug's pace.Let me stress that I don't dislike the game. It just isn't worth buying, in my opinion. I got it when the game was free. So if it ever goes free again, then yes, I do recommend it. Just know (and I believe the game tells you as much) that you'll be seeing some potentially triggering content for those struggling with anxiety, depression, etc.Good game, but certainly not for everyone, not for me, and I can't recommend that you spend a dime on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Touching story. I found all of the characters interesting and fleshed out. The only thing I would have appreciated would have been a bit more... of a thoroughness involved with the twins processing their/their mom's past through their storybook/its characters. But I also appreciate that a lot of the narrative was focusing on the themes of... some things, you just don't get to know and you have to move on anyway. I appreciated the ending I got. I'll admit I wasn't motivated to play through more than once, but I was curious enough to look into the alternate endings and also appreciated them, so people with more patience I think could easily satisfy themselves with multiple play throughs. I am moderately satisfied with the story branches. It doesn't feel like you're cheated in the end/like your choices didn't matter after all. Definitely glad I played it.

_childDocuments_.review: i gotta start out by saying the representation in this game is amazing. they portray tyler so well, and do not use a deadname for him ever, even in flashbacks. they also make his personality more than just his identity. diving into the actual game itself, i have to say this was a really intense game. the twins start questioning everything they knew about their mother, and it really makes you think too. one thing i didn't like was that the most logical ending (in my opinion) was given as the memory of a character you should dislike by the end. it almost makes you not want to chose that option. i think the puzzles were super cool, especially since they related to the whole storybook world that mary ann created. i won't say much, but the attic was such a cool piece of the story, and i love how it serves kind of as a note to the twins. i cannot believe i was able to get this game completely free due to pride month, but i am so thankful i did,
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: I was presented with this title as a free offering for Pride Month by steam. Now, being that I am a genuine fan of the work DontNod creates I was quite happy to give this title a run. It plays like most of their titles, as it relates to choices and consequences. I think however, this story is an interesting perspective and offers insight into the family dynamic and how people who are not necessarily born in the right body must not only see the world, but be seen by the world. I am a straight, male, who has known my whole life I am a straight male. I can't begin to relate to the struggles of individuals and families with transgender members. I have so many questions and no real way to get answers, unfortunately. While I have completed chapter 1 and I am now only a few scenes into chapter 2 I can say for sure that I encourage anyone to step outside what may be their own "comfort zone" and spend some time with this title. I can't relate to the plight of the main characters but I can empathize with them, having seen first hand the effects of a person knowing they are not living the life that is right for them.Tell Me Why, will take you on a journey of emotions, self reflections, and perhaps even offer you a perspective you may otherwise never have had the opportunity to experience. It is an important title and I hope that in some way, this may help some who are struggling with understanding their own feelings regarding their identity in this world.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: Another mature Dontnod title. I would manage to espress my feelings in an accurate way if only the game hadn't been that emotional to me. Brief, yet exacting. Its richness in story plot is valuable, its texture enjoyable. In spite of the tardiness its technical gameplay offers, i would definetely recommend the game. Play it. Explore it. Live within its fables and don't forget to always look where you would not expect another untold truth to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Tell Me Why

_childDocuments_.review: Deserves more recognition for its powerful story, strong personality, and progress in trans representation. Its by no means a perfect game, in particular, theres some voice acting issues, but nonetheless I found it to be very enjoyable and in a sorta...uplifting...wayEDIT: After beating the game--Id like to double down on my stance. It was a great story, loaded with real meaning and strong emotional themes about grief, trauma, and memory. All of which really comes together for a satisfying conclusion. If you can look past the handful of minor bugs and immerse yourself in the story and the ideas being presented--you'll have an awesome time with this game.And as a note on the voice acting; I love the voice actors, but there are marked discontinuities that seem like one characters dialogue was taken from an entirely different take than the others and gives this effect of the characters not being in the same room during some scenes. It wasn't too hard to ignore this, but it did take some of the emotional weight away by bloating certain climactic moments, which is why I think its worth noting.

_childDocuments_.review: As a trans person myself, even though "in the other direction" if we call it that, this is a fantastic game to showcase daily struggles while being extremely exciting to play due to the mysterious and deep tragedy that you set out to uncover with the twins. Tell Me Why makes you ask what it's title does, why are people like this, why did that event have to happen the way it did, why do I, why do we have to suffer through these harsh trials when we honestly just wish to live our lives happily in peace. Nobody ever asked to be born, most are thankful, some less. Why were you born the way you were? Why were you raised that way in those circumstances. And most importantly, how do you deal with it a decade later? How much do your decisions still matter? name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow
detailed_description: Antiquarian Thomasina Bateman is writing a book on the barrows of England, documenting the treasures she finds buried within. When an intriguing letter summons her to the small village of Bewlay, tucked away in the remote countryside, she sets off by train with her assistant a day behind. Upon her arrival, however, the mysterious man who summoned her is nowhere to be found. Her assistant never arrives. A stubborn landowner refuses access to the barrow, and the locals are wary of this woman who is traveling alone and (gasp!) wears trousers. The excavation of Hob’s Barrow is off to a rocky start. And then Thomasina starts having strange dreams… A dark , complex and evolving storyline featuring interwoven elements from real English folklore. Traditional point and click adventure game puzzles and interactions, with an easy modern interface. A cast of intriguing characters , from suspicious villagers to sickly vicars to lordly landowners, all with their own unique stories and motives. A distinct folk horror tone and grounding. Evocative pixel-art graphics, featuring cut-scenes and engaging animations. A suitably atmospheric original soundtrack from The Machine. The Demon. - one half of the duo behind the award-winning 'Football Game' soundtrack. Fiends in the furrows, the smell of damp soil, and a cat or two.

The first 3/4 of the game had more "social" puzzles, while the end of the game had more "puzzle" puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow is a nice little point n click. It's definitely worth at least 2 playthroughs just to notice all the little story details. The story itself is pretty good, has a nice mystery to it that will keep you playing. For the gameplay itself, it would be nice to be pointed in the right direction with certain clues as to what to do for specific items. But I guess it fits the theme of the game, where certain people are pointing you in all kinds of directions in a small town full of mystery.If you want to play a short Lovecraftian-esque adventure game with some puzzles, it'll be up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A Lovecraft inspired folk horror story set in rural England that is absolutely worth your time. The game has an appropriate and mysterious build-up to an ending which makes for a memorable conclusion. The team behind this game clearly understand what makes Lovecraftian stories work and it shows. My only complaints are that some of the point and click puzzles in the middle can be a little frustrating and I'd recommend being willing to look up solutions when you're stuck. As an aside, I appreciate hearing English accents from regions that aren't commonly represented in media and genuinely wish more games chose rural Britain as a setting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent dark horror game, not very heavy on the puzzles but dripping with atmosphere.Fantastic performances all around from the voice actors, and a dark and depressing script that had me questioning what was real and what wasn't.The pixel art is also fantastic, excellent use of muted colors to convey the dreariness of a lonely little town in the moors.Highly recommended but don't go in expecting a happy story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic, atmospheric point & click adventure game.  Really nails both a particular setting and mood in a way that makes the genre truly shine.  Little flakes of a wonderful "infinitesimal (wo)man engulfed by enormous nature" sentiment are sprinkled throughout, including a scenic overlook over the vast lands that's not particularly meaningful in any specific way, and yet still just perfect.  Puzzles are generally rational, and the emphasis is on the story and lore as much as the atmosphere.  Truly well done!  A definite treat for fans of the genre who like their games on the less frivolous side.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I've edited this review.  Initially I recommended it, but after finishing it and reflecting on it for awhile I have to change my review.The game starts off so well.  The setting is eerie.  The story is intriguing.  The pixel graphics are beautiful.  The voice acting is well done, and I enjoyed speaking with the townsfolk and learning their stories.  There were even a couple of moments that I felt were truly heartfelt.  The puzzles, too, were pretty fair and I never once had to rely on a walkthrough.But then I finished it, and warning, there are mild spoilers ahead.The game ends way too soon.  I don't expect a game in this style to be 100 hours long, but I finished in 5.5 hours and that's with me actually listening to most of the dialog and not just reading and clicking through, and rarely making use of fast-travel (the locations aren't far apart so you really don't even need to use it).  The short length also leaves some of the lore feeling like it was left unexplored, and some questions unanswered.While the puzzles never felt unfair, they also never felt all that challenging.  I think I was only really stuck once, and that's because I didn't notice an item that I had to pick up (the game isn't bad about that either, unlike some point and click games, I just didn't notice this one).  The solution to puzzles usually made itself fairly obvious after a few minutes, and some of the solutions were so obvious that I felt like I'd already played the game before.But that's forgivable.  What wasn't was how the game ended.  Without venturing too deep into spoiling, towards the end of the game you are warned that something you are intending to do might not go as well as expected. However, you can do nothing with this information.  You just go forth and do the thing that you were intending to do, and it indeed does not go well, as you were warned.  And this is how the game ends.The fact that you're given no choice in the matter, except to watch events fold out in the way that they do feels ♥♥♥♥♥♥; worse, because they unfold in a particularly ♥♥♥♥♥♥ way.  The ending left a bad taste in my mouth and I was warned that it would going in.  That tarnishes what was otherwise a wonderful experience.The game could have been great.  It was just too short with a bad ending.  If the game were longer; if instead of ending where it does, that was only the end of the first act, it could have answered some of those unresolved questions.  It could have fleshed out the lore more.  It could have ended on a better note.It's a real shame, too, because up until the end the game was fantastic and I wouldn't have hesitated to recommend it.  All that said, if it's ever on sale for half off or more and you're looking for a beautiful point-and-click game, it's probably worth a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely outstanding P&C adventure. Dark, Menacing, Brooding with a story that draws you in and characters that are familiar in their strangeness. Everyone has a secret or a reason to hold you in contempt or deny you assistance. awkward northerners abound in this odd village. What lies beneath this quaint looking pixel art adventure is a gripping tale of the paranormal and the occult. Voice acting is exemplary, the graphics are beautifully retro without being cliched, the audio is atmospheric and often chilling and the pacing is spot on. The puzzles are rarely taxing which makes progression a joy. There's rarely a moment when you have to put it down and have a bit of a think about a puzzle which is either a plus or a negative depending on what you need from your adventure games. Highly Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent graphic adventure, from beginning to end. Being that I was playing the new "Return to Monkey Island" with an enthusiasm to match, it turned out that I reached the end of "The excavation..." much earlier because it really caught me much more. Why? Because this adventure has the right perfume that old school gamers are looking for: good story, good setting, well-driven, good dialogues, gripping, immersive, lovecraftian touches, and crafted with pixel art. And... You won't have to look for walkthroughs to finish it. However, yes, towards the end, I googled some Latin stuff to successfully solve a puzzle (it's evident that it's done on purpose and it's very rewarding to solve it this way). Beautiful ending, if a bit predictable towards the end.I recommend it without a doubt.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Nice world despite the mediocre pixel graphics. It goes many years back depicting a remote village of England. It manages to create really good atmosphere of a community that hates visitors and sticks to tradition and tales. You certainly feel stranger and not welcomed.- The main concept and setting are interesting and they're getting you immersed right from the begging creating peculiar, mysterious vibes. Storytelling isn't as good though.- Well built characters with vivid personalities and a cool protagonist.- Nice, convincing voice acting performances that fit to each character.- Well written dialogues. They're mostly short, but interesting with flow. You never get bored of speaking to another person.- Great control mechanics. Walking and interactions feel responsive and fast unlike to a lot of slow burn point and clicks adventures with problematic controls. There's double click for instantly jumping to the next screen and fast travel to some locations. There is also a button that reveals all the interactive objects, so annoying pixel hunting is avoided.- There are interactive objects per screen that the protagonist can comment on, even if they're not used for any puzzle. All these interactions make the world feel a little bit more alive and interactive.The bad- Except form the very last part, puzzles are mediocre, unimaginative and easy overall. You mostly collect items and trade them to people. It's pretty straight forward as there are only few screens in the whole game and the dialogues clearly reveal you of what to do next. There is no particularly clever use of items and only few easy combinations inside the inventory. Also, some items like the trowel and the knife are used way too much.- The main concept is cool and creates a lot of mystery, but storytelling and pacing are problematic. There are not major events and it fails to create plot peaks. You're main goal is the excavation right from the beginning and you have to overcome random obstacles from villagers by performing various chores for them. Even those flashbacks seem rushed without adding much. They're a cheap solution to make it more emotional.- Towards the end it gets too grotesque for my taste. I found it a bit silly with cliché elements that don't fit the calm vibes of the rest game.- Pixel graphics are decent, but bulky. The world lacks details and feels a little bit empty. Only some close ups during cut scenes are really nice.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow is pixelated horror point and click adventure game. Art is pretty good, though in the cutscenes people look bit horrifying. Not that it's wrong choice in a game like this though.The game manages to blend strange and mundane (especially in the beginning) and quite compelling way. Bit like Stephen King does in his stories, though the game is more British than American.Puzzles are mostly logical, though towards the end there's puzzles where you first don't have any idea what to do. Had to consult walkthrough few times even before that.While the story doesn't falls bit flat towards the end, I'm still recommending the game. Games with intriguing stories are not that common, but this one really worked for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed my time spent with this game.If like me, you have a nostalgic love for point and click adventures, this is worth both your time and money.Charm oozes out of every pore of this game. Cloak and Dagger games seem to excel with every release, they have really honed their craft here and i eagerly await their future efforts.The characters are memorable. Story unfolds slowly and is rather unnerving, as a great lingering horror novel often is. _childDocuments_.review: The game is short, well structured, well voiced and the pixel art is absolutely gorgeous.I only have two nitpicks: Firstly, some segments are fairly long and a bit tideous, since there is no new discoveries to be made and you are merely doing classic point-and-click busywork trying to figure out who can give you the relevant information.Seconly, the end is (as far as I can tell) fixed - you can not improve the overall outcome by being clever, researching well, or discussing the right points with the right people. That means the finally feels a bit cruel/cheaty because it happens the same way no matter what.  That does not detract from the ride itself, though. The buildup of tension is slow but effective, there is a lot of story to be found between the lines and in the hints dropped at well-known folklore.I recommend playing this game, because for 10 € you really don't do anything wrong here, even if you end up disliking it.

_childDocuments_.review: Spooky. Good puzzles. No dead ends, like in Sierra games, or dying; it's like LucasArts, but not comedy. What they've done with the Adventure Game Studio engine is amazing. _childDocuments_.review: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow absolutely nails tone and atmosphere. From the moment Thomasina alights the train in the remote village Bewlay you feel the visceral gloom and simmering terror. The characters and dialogue are excellent and evoke that particular kind of dread one feels as an outsider trespassing in old lands where the past has been forgotten by the outside world. Only the insular natives offer cryptic clues of folklore passed down for generations. On the surface, tey seem like normal people in normal village. But it's impossible to shake that niggling feeling deep down something is very wrong. The deliciously moody soundtrack makes an excellent complement to the pixel art, which moves between sparse and grotesque. The story built on top of this atmosphere is quite effective too, even if it's not treading new ground.The gameplay isn't as strong. Too often The Excavation of Hob's Barrow falls back on the old-school adventure game trapping of turning what should be a simple task into a series of arbitrary errands. You want to milk a cow, so you find a pail, but the pail has a hole in it. You bring it to the blacksmith who says he would fix it except some kid ran off with his hammer, so you have to find a toy to trade to the kid to convince him to give you the hammer. Those kinds of sequences make up most of the puzzles. While there is skill involved in terms of listening to the dialogue and carefully observing the environment, the contrived nature of these sequences drags down the pacing and clashes with the somber atmosphere. Some of the later puzzles lean into archaeology themes, and those are more engaging. To it's credit, The Excavation of Hob's Barrow never becomes esoteric. You're unlikely to get stuck if you pay attention and experiment a little.Overall a solid old-school adventure game that's well worth a playthrough, especially if you're a fan of atmospheric horror.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. If you like story-driven point and click adventures that seem a little off and have puzzles that aren't full of moon logic but do still stretch the logic muscles, then this game is definitely worth a try.The graphics are full of great stretches of land surrounding an insular village, the voice acting is absolutely on point. Thomasina is a very likeable MC that doesn't take nonsense (and you have the option to give the man propositioning her a little slap). There is a great mystery that you will be compelled to solve.Definitely one for fans of The Wicker Man and The League of Gentlemen.I received a free copy in exchange for my time spent helping to beta test the game, this does not in any way impair my review.

_childDocuments_.review: This is hopefully a spoiler free review. This is one of the best point-and-clicks I've played in a long time. It has charming retro style graphics that makes you think of 90s adventure games, and it is fully voice acted with charming accents (it puts me in mind of The Dig). I did not encounter any bugs in the game at all, which is impressive since most games tend to have something when first released.The good:- An interesting story- A compelling main character- Some actions and choices have consequences in dialogue options (I like that a lot)- A living world (for example, when you walk in the woods, there are animals that seemingly randomly appear on screen, making the world feel more inhabited and natural)- The puzzles feel logical and fair, so hints are not really needed and they can be solved if you follow a certain way of thinking (except for some in the final act that were quite tricky).The bad:- The story and mythos are a bit derivative and predictable (if you've ever read any H.P. Lovecraft or Lovecraft inspired stories or even read/played the Cthulhu RPG/Vaesen RPG you'll know what to expect)- The lack of multiple endings (the main character has plenty of reasons to act differently than she does in the last act. The information makes the ending railroaded)Still, this is a game that you should play! Especially for the horror elements and the homage to the adventure game point-and-click era. Well done developers!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't exactly remember how I found about the game, but the overwhelmingly positive reviews on Steam convinced me to buy it. I definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a horror themed classic adventure game.The first thing I noticed is the voice acting, as it is the best I've heard in a while. The accents are great and I never felt like skipping any of the dialogue. Other audio is great also. The village has ambient sounds, like dogs barking and birds singing, that makes it feel like an actual place. The music emphasizes the atmosphere with some nice ambient pieces. And that acoustic piece in the middle of the game was a nice touch.Visually the game is like you see on the screenshots. The graphics are straight from the early nineties and they work well. The game is not very colorful, but uses faded colors to create a picture of a forgotten, small countryside village.The story starts a bit slowly and ends a bit too fast in my opinion. The end feels like a straight path towards the finale with some puzzles thrown in as obstacles. I did like the ending, but felt like it could've used a bit more work.In general, the puzzles are not too challenging if you are used to applying some adventure game logic. The game even keeps track for you of things that you need to accomplish. But like mentioned earlier, towards the end it feels like you are solving puzzles just for the sake of solving puzzles, while earlier the reasons for doing so felt more organic. Luckily there's no need for pixel hunting and even without the hotspot highlighting everything is easy to find.

_childDocuments_.review: is a very solid folk-horror point-and-click adventure game, at an interesting intersection between retro stylings and very modern sensibilities.In a lot of ways, it plays like a less abrasive  (1996) or  (1998).  It exists in obvious aesthetic tribute to those old-school point-and-clickers, but with unobtrusive quality-of-life improvements that make the experience more like you  horror games of the era being than what they actually were.  The low-fi pixel art is quietly accentuated with very modern anti-aliasing and particle FX.  The backing instrumentals are synth-heavy to evoke the low sound quality of older games, but with crisply-rendered modern vocals that could only capture this level of nuance in a modern game.  It's a cool thing to see a "retro game" handle these little improvements so subtly, deliberately accentuating the strengths of older titles with modern tech.At a gameplay level, this is very classic  or  fare, where the character is constantly collecting and combining items in the environment to achieve sometimes very goofy and unintuitive gameplay outcomes.  For the first two acts of the game, these 'puzzles' tend to be of a social variety: use  on  to get information out of him.  Use  on  to exchange for an item you need.  Use  on  and she'll show you a path through the woods.  This is because the majority of the game is spent in a rural English farm town where everyone is hiding something, and so puzzles are naturally character-heavy and dialogue-driven as a way of buoying the plot.  In the final act, this inverts: the main character steps beyond the pale and into the explicitly supernatural (this  a horror game, after all), and it is here that the game's most conceptually interesting, -esque puzzles can show themselves.I found myself wishing that the puzzle quality was more consistent throughout , even though I understand  the best puzzles were backloaded; because the game has more conceptual space to work with when it's no longer grounded in a tone of bucolic realism.That leads us nicely into the tone and story of the game, which are just aces.   sits nicely at the triangular intersection between 'Gothic Horror,' 'Lovecraftian Horror,' and 'Folk Horror,' with a unique Industrial Revolution setting where "modernity" and Enlightenment philosophies are being spread by arrogant, conquering would-be explorers to the "dark corners" of the world.  Main character Thomasina Bateman is one such explorer, an archaeologist whose aspirations are more local: to pick up the work of her father in chronicling the barrows of pre-Christian England.  The story that unfolds as Thomasina attempts to navigate the isolated and untrustworthy rural locals will strike as very familiar if you're a fan of English folk-horror like  (1973) or  (2011), but it has just enough twists and turns to remain fresh, and the voice-acting performances are stellar throughout.  It's also reminiscent of those films in that the story is fully linear; don't go into this one expecting a swath of alternate endings or a moral choice system.With Halloween coming up, this is a great bite-sized horror experience, particularly if you prefer a more low-fi aesthetic presentation.  A hearty recommend, despite my criticisms.

_childDocuments_.review: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow is an excellent point and click adventure with a captivating story and lovable characters. As the daughter of a former archeologist now working on your own essay about the burial mounds of England you - Thomasina Bateman - are being invited to the village of Bewlay to examine and excavate a local landmark: Hob's Barrow. Permanently being somewhere between the well liked but  just as often unpleasant intruder you maneuver yourself through the inhabitants, the market place and the "Plough and Furrows"- the local inn of the town of Bewlay. As metioned in former reviewes the voice acting is so extremely well done that even the oddest character can become likeable during the time you spend/talk with them (Yeah, I'm having old Cyril in me mind writing those lines!). Since I played the demo in the first place I had the game on my wishlist. And I honestly don't care if Cloak and Dagger's next game will be a sequel with the main character Thomasia Bateman or her little brother Adam, or if those developers will come up with a completely different and new story...I am definitely looking forward to whatever may come!

_childDocuments_.review: I believed in Cloak and Dagger Games, but I didn't think he would make something so great. _childDocuments_.review: I don't know how I feel about this one. Once again I am stuck on the middle ground, wishing steam had an in-between button. The vibe of this game is right up my alley, pixel point click adventure with some mystery and horror, how could anyone not love that? The story itself is intriguing and I've enjoyed uncovering the mystery. **spoilers**I am one of those types that if the ending is not clicking with me, that can ruin the whole game for me. Unfortunately this is one of those times. Not all endings need to be wrapped up in a big bow with happily ever after, but my god was this ending bleak. The bad guys won with the main protagonist  life destroyed. There was no good here at all. I could forgive this if there was just a sliver of good out of the situation but I guess there was not enough time for the team to make this, so we are left with a bad ending overall. I really thought initially my actions would affect the games ending but upon reading the statements from the team, there is only one ending. This is the most depressing ending. I do want to point out there are also some questionable paths that were taken that doesn't make it believable for me. After she finds out what is planned for her needing her blood, obviously these people lied to her, and want to set her up as a sacrifice. She's not that stupid. Why would she continue with the excavation? I do not understand that, that for me would have been an opportunity to put multiple endings with a choice. There is also some dialog that makes you think you have a choice. Why she's asked to take a drink but I tried to pick a polite decline option but the guy convinces here anyway and she drinks, what was the point in even having the option??What about the feral people? What was even that about? It was pretty much left off without explanation. There was even a point I would have thought that they would have helped her but I guess not. I do understand your team has lives but you can have easily pushed this back to make a proper ending. I really don't like when people make a game and decide just to throw out whatever because the rest of it is to hard to work on, but again people will like this, but to me there could have been a whole lot of choices inputted in the game wouldn't have made this seem so hopeless in the end. So with that I'm going to have to not recommend. If you don't mind an unsatisfying ending then yes I do recommend but if you are like me that needs some kind of good ending or at the very least some silver lineing then I suggest you pass this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent point and click horror adventure. I happen to have a soft spot for these. It builds up the tension quite nicely, one frustration being that the player can see where the story is going a mile away. When the right thing to do would be to pack your stuff and leave, you have to keep going. I guess this was the intent, inevitability and all. The other thing I don't enjoy very much is the ambiguity. There is a popular belief that not knowing what's real and what isn't is a good storytelling technique, but honestly, not only is it overdone, it limits the story. So ultimately for me "Hob's Barrow" is a very nice build-up to a little disappointing finale.
