_childDocuments_.review: -	Thomasina (the protagonist)The Excavation of Hob’s Barrow, the title spells out what happens in this game right off. It’s an atmospheric and eldritch story with beats that are sometimes charming, sometimes macabre. I found the story to be so gripping that I was racing ahead of myself towards the end just to get to see the final climax. The game has elicited a wide array of emotions out of me. Fear, passion, love and awe. It’s a moody title that establishes a strong atmosphere with subtle touches like music, long silences between characters, suspense, self-narration, beautifully drawn art, of that which comes to my mind. This game was a rare one which achieved the goal of keeping my mind busy with deciphering its narrative long after I stopped playing it. In that regard, and the fact that it has a fixed story, it felt more like a suspenseful short novel than a video game.This game’s story is its pillar and strongest point. You play as Thomasina Bateman, a refined lady who follows her invalid father’s calling of archaeology (specifically excavating barrows). I found her to be an acquired taste. Her matter-of-fact personality grew on me, and over the course of the game the player will get to know more and more about her and the vicissitudes of life  that brought her hitherto. The story unfolds both as the player progresses through the game and in retrospect, concurrently. Thomasina will retrospectively narrate parts of the game each day, revealing to you quite a bit of what to come without giving any tangible detail. Suffice to say that you will know this game has a bad ending from the get-go. But the way it unfolded, and knowing how it will end has succeeded in enthralling me throughout my entire playthrough.The story is set in stone, you will only unravel it. This is my biggest gripe, and I wish there was a branching storyline with multiple endings. Looking back at the game, I feel like the story was so good that this may not be such a significant issue, but the current story has some writing problems, such as ones I discussed in the cons section (the protagonist going very OOC in the final act).If you replay the game, you will notice a significant amount of foreshadowing to the ending, which succeeded in capturing my interest when I was going for 100%. This subtlety was exceptionally well done, and added a lot of depth to characters that felt very basic or simple before, and made me speculate a lot on the motives of some characters and/or what was their place relative to the game’s events. Some characters are red herrings, some others are wolves in sheep’s clothing, and once the cat was out of the bag, it made my skin crawl interacting with some of them knowing their treachery, and I regarded the rest with curious suspicion over their complicity. I have a lot of emotions towards this game. Sometimes, it felt like just another cool game to me. Sometimes it was more. I spent great lengths just listening to its ambiance of St. Edmund’s or the music. It’s a unique experience, an eldritch tale presented in a muted way. Its writing is what makes it. If a story feels completely contained and well structured on itself that it is told in retrospect, and once you go through it again you see all the threads that were right there before your face before but you never made that connection, then I’m willing to heap a lot of praise, because this is unfortunately uncommon with video game narratives.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, a pretty good old school horror point'n'click. The pixel art graphics are nice and a good fit for the story and the way it's told. I would say the atmosphere is the strong suit of the title, somewhere between gothic and lovecraftian horror. It's pretty short, but that's to be expected from this kind of game. It took me 8 hours to complete it but i'm the kind of player who likes to explore every nook and cranny and deplete all the dialogue options.The riddles are quite easy and straightforward. All you have to do is read the clues you find and think a little. The main challenge lies in not missing any important item in the scenery, but you can press space to highlight the things you can interact with and it helps tremendously. I enjoyed the fact that the vast majority of the riddles were logical and that i didn't have to do stuff that didn't really make sense at first glance to progress, like it sometimes happens in point and clicks. This said, seasoned players of the genre might find it too easy, complex riddles clearly aren't the focus here.I also would have liked the choices you make to have more of an impact on the story. Basically, the game has close to no replay value because .So yeah, at the end of the day i'd still recommend it, but if you're having second thoughts about its few weak spots, maybe wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little adventure game, similar in style to other Wadjet Eye publications. The puzzles are relatively easy as far as adventure games go (i.e., a guide is not really ever needed for an average player, unlike some other games). Still, there is some thinking to be done, its not over-the-top easy. The main merit of the game is its somber atmosphere and bleak mood, rooted in the rural English moors which provides an evocative backdrop for the Lovecraftian storyline that slowly unfolds. The dialogue is amusing and interesting to read, but I especially liked all the voice acting, top-notch really. I really like the characters in this game. I hope this genre of retro-pixelated adventure games with a Lovecraftian twist never dies out. Wadjet Eye, please keep this up.

As the story progress you're always riddled with questions regarding the setting of the game as you can't really be sure which direction the game will take from a specific point onward. You get to the point of suspicion where basically anyone can be the culprit, and the game definitely delivers a great grip to its storyline. Let's go over positives and negatives:* Outstanding story and narrative* Amazing voice acting* Interesting characters* Great protagonist that you actually care about* Somewhat weak riddles* Too long, filled with unnecessary tasks that could easily be left out* Only one  ending* Lack of choices and objective opinion If you're fan of point-and-click adventures like this one then I definitely recommend playing this game. _childDocuments_.review: An excellent and engrossing P&C game with a lackluster ending. Cloak and Dagger Games and Wadjet Eye Games have made some of my fav modern P&C games.  This title certainly has all their respective marks of quality and attention to detail.  -Good use of quality-of-life features (double click fast travel exit, object highlight function, autosaves, color blind text option)-Retro pixel style with up-to-date features makes for a nostalgic yet modern graphic experience (note to self: start writing wine reviews)-Excellent cutscene animations with rotoscoped elements-Professional Voice acting-Atmospheric soundtrack and excellent use of ambient sound effects.-Engrossing Pseudo-Lovecraftian story and gameplay-Good game flow.  Very few "what the hell am I supposed to do" moments.  -I liked the original title for this game, Incantamentum, better.-I've said it before, and I'll say it again: I F****** HATE AGS SETUP!!!  A BOX TO SELECT HOW I WANT TO PLAY MIDI MUSIC?!? WTF IS THIS, 1992?!?!?!?...... But I digress, this is an issue with AGS not this game. -The ending, Period.  For a game that had such an engrossing story, I found the ending to be a shock and not in a good way.  -Related to the ending, there were several loose ends / unexplained events that never get a resolution.  I find adding things like to this to an engrossing story only to not resolve them to be a faux pas.-Overall game play time for me was around 6 hours including getting all achievements.  This is about half of what I would have liked it to be.  I think there was room in the setting to pack in an additional few hours of gameplay. I want to reiterate that I enjoyed this game and I think any P&C afficionado will feel the same.  When I look at the list of pros and cons, it makes me think that this game might have suffered from a case of "Deadline-itis".  Let’s look at the facts from this point of view:-Game has a title change seemingly late into development.  This is not rare but is a strange sign.-Several unresolved events in game that go nowhere and are never explained.-Signs that there was potentially going to be more gameplay/features but did not get included (things like all the extra buildings you can knock on the door but no ones there for example).-Gameplay should have been extended by at least 2-4 hours.  -And again, the ending.People think that because these are retro pixel style games that they are cheap.  They are not.  They also think they should take less time than a more graphicly intensive game.  They do not.  I'll also point out that the development timeline for this game overlapped significantly with that little pandemic we went thru...That being said I have no idea if I'm right or not.  I also don't care.  This was still a fun game and I recommend it to all my fellow P&C fans.  👑  👑⠀⠀⠀
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: What a superb game. The folk-horror mystery-solving storytelling is spectacular and more so because of the absolutely incredible voice acting and plot development. The whole ensemble cast is wonderful but special mention has to go to Samantha Beart who plays Thomasina Bateman (Big Finish, Torchwood, HHGTTG etc...) for the sheer amount of material she has to get though. Loved the authenticity of the regional accents and small detail like 'Bakewell Pudding' as opposed to tarts (Anyone who has been to Matlock, and Derby UK knows what I mean). Have really enjoyed the whole day 1, 2 etc structure and it's become a real mystery story with some clever logical puzzles that lead on to the next plot points. Some shocking moments of horror as well! Be warned! Musically I really enjoyed the live audio: some amazing fiddle playing which was absolutely stunning and fully authentic/believable, but there is confusion over whether the score conjures Stranger Things or a more 90s 8/16bit vibe. Occasionally the ostinati needed to change chord underneath a harmonic change (I only noticed because I'm a composer! but it doesn't detract and overall it's successful. Sound design is spot on apart from one segment in Day 2 where the noise level of music and fx goes above the dB of the comms.Fx are great and pretty authentic (love the goat being milked!). 5 stars for me!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A real gem of an adenture.A most memorable Lovecraftian folk horror tale, reminiscent of classics like The Wicker Man. Very well paced and slowly sucking you into its abysmal center. The way days progress is well constructed, as is the scenery. The town and surrounding moors and woods are misty in the mornings, characters change their spots as a day progresses. The puzzles are straight forward and never obtuse. Since one seldomly gets stuck on a puzzle for too long, everything keeps chaning, which seem very natural. During your stay you start getting to know the townfolk and the town itself better. The nice ambient soundscape further the immersion.There's lots of other things to love here: intelligent writing and fletched out characters, impressive pixel art animation (the first pixel art rotoscoping I've seen), good music and excellent voice over.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Hob's Barrow. I'm a huge Broken Sword fan, and there are very few new point and click adventure games around these days, which are actually good! The voice acting, atmosphere and creepy art style really elevated this game. It's got a Victorian gothic / Wicker Man / Lovecraftian style to it, so if that's your thing, definitely pick this up. Tip: the space bar is your friend - it shows you all the items you can interact with, and it's also worth looking at stuff, not just interacting with things. I hope they develop another game of the same style and quality!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: It's an adventure game with a Victorian supernatural theme. It's very likely you've seen similar stories told in a variety of ways. This one isn't that special, but it's competent. One thing that surprised me was graphics and thier effective use, you'll know what I mean when you see it. Another thing is that nowadays most of the games like that try to be light on puzzles - not just because they don't want to be hard but because puzzles are often immersion breaking. This one isn't too bad but its oldschool puzzle design is often non-sensical and clashes with the tone of the game.Overall it's a decent game. You get what you pay for.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a great recommendation if you're a fan of the developer (which you should be) and looking to play another in their arsenal. Great story but the game play just felt a little underwhelming. The puzzles at the end were great and reminded me of The Dig/DoTT/Indiana Jones/Full Throttle, but the buildup to that felt more obvious/linear than I normally like.Still overall a good game, if it's on sale grab it if you want a few hours of entertainment.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give a "meh" instead of positive/negative. I mostly chose negative because I think the current rating of 95% positive is misleading. It's not a bad game and if you enjoy the genre you'll probably enjoy the game at least somewhat.There's plenty of other glowing reviews so I'm going to focus on where I think the game stumbles.1. The puzzles. I don't like cryptic puzzles that plague other games but this game goes too far in the other direction. I'd say at least 75% of the "puzzles" are so easy you don't have to think at all, the solution is immediately obvious. The remaining 25% are actually really good puzzles in my opinion, but so much of it just felt like tedium to delay and because it felt obligated to have "puzzles" like every other adventure game. Moreover many of the puzzles followed this pattern: "Do X. Oh I can't do X, I need to do Y first. Oh, I can't do Y I need to do Z first. Oh, I can't do Z I need to do Q first." X was all you were really trying to accomplish to progress the story but artificial roadblocks keep being thrown up. Again it feels like these puzzles were implemented only out of obligation and an attempt to pad playing time.2. The story. Much like the puzzles, there's some really good story here. There's also a ton that doesn't get explained at all, which is to be expected to some extent to keep thing spooky, but still unsatisfying at the end to have so many events completely unexplained. There seemed to be more to the story hinted at in a lot of places but they never get fleshed out or explained, you only get the core story resolved. My biggest complaint is that toward the end of the game, the protagonist, who up to that point had been a lovely character in whom I was invested, suddenly comes over with a bad case of the very very dumb. It's a seemingly small bit of the whole overall story but one small scene ruined the ending and destroyed any empathy and investment for the main character that had built up. I've kept it vague but it's definitely still a spoiler: I don't think it's a "bad" game per se; most of the positive reviews I'd agree with a lot of what they liked, but it's definitely not perfect and has some big flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Though I am usually not very fond of the horror genre I played the whole story in one weekend, because I couldn't let go. Graphics, story telling, atmosphere, voice acting and the love to small details are all 5/5.The puzzles are all not very hard, so they don't interrupt the story (that's a good thing in this kind of point & click game)A real gem!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow is an old-style adventure game. It presents a simple and efficient interface, balanced puzzles all along and a nice atmosphere. The story, however, is a bit superficial and lack some depth. Characters, in the other hand, are not overdeveloped but are well characterised and do "accomplish their mission" in the game, with a set of great voices that suit them well enough.In summary, to me, and even not being a reference point in the genre, the entire game sounds, feels and plays nice, with a lot of entertaining moments. No doubt it's a GOOD experience and definitely worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A very captivating experience. Very immersive. It feels like you're in the midst of it, and eager to hang out with the village folks in the local pub every evening. The end was a bit more intense with the riddles, but otherwise an extremely relaxing whilst thrilling game. I can thorougly recommend it <3
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like someone reached into my brain and made it just for me. Folk horror? Check. Spooky synth soundtrack? Check. Victorian Derbyshire? Check. LucasArts'-style gameplay with plenty of references? Check. Pixel art that is well done and not hokey? Check.There is much to love in this game. The cutscenes in particular stand out. I'm not sure I've ever seen a pixel art game with cutscenes as good as this. The storytelling is ace. A lot of is told through mood, and that's really how this genre wins.Some of the puzzles are a little obtuse and the ending is a bit fragmented, but overall it's a fantastic game. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: i really wish that i liked this game more than i did, but it falls flat in more ways than one. alot of the game play is fetch quests that have steps only to pad the playtime. the main reason i didn't like it that much is that the actual excavation of the barrow is the main point and the whole game is to lead up to that. however once you actually make it o the excavation it take only 20-30 minutes and then rushed into the end of the game. the story is also not as great as i hopped; with the mystery of the barrow hyped up as this giant thing but then u spend little time there and its not at all satisfying. i wish this game did more but it feels like it ended prematurely and didn't expand on its mystery well at all. 6/10 tbh.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Art, music, story, atmosphere, gameplay, all excellent. Puzzles are not that hard but some endgame ones might feel a bit cryptic. If you like Lovecraft and old-school adventure games you won't be disappointed. I only wish it had extra endings depending on your choices to add more replay value, but other than that it's pretty solid. Hope they release something similar soon!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, the graphics is amazing. The animations. The voiceover is incredible. The atmosphere is... possibly the best I've seen in an adventure game! I've played for only two hours, still exploring the place. I can say the first impression beats even Monkey Island. Let's see how the puzzles are...Update after finishing the game. Finished in 11 hours (which is a lot). The game stays very good until the end. When you think it's finished, a whole new part starts, which reminds of Atlantis in Indiana Jones. Really well done. This game is one of the best adventure games in recent years. It only has one (very subjective) flaw: it is too easy. You never get stuck for more than 10-15 minutes. This is considered optimal nowadays. Even Return of Monkey Island is like that. What the authors are missing, IMHO, is that, if you don't get stuck for days, several times, the game doesn't stick with you. Monkey 1, Monkey 2, or Fate, would not be so unforgettable if I hadn't been stuck for days, several times. My two pence. Anyway, as I said, this is one of the best adventure games of the last 10 years.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good point-and-click adventure game. It is more story-heavy than puzzle-heavy (the puzzles are fairly easy). The story builds up really well and, without spoilers, has quite the eye-opening finish. There is some gore, body horror, and depictions of suicide, but no jumpscares. The art is top-notch, with some nice pixel art and really good voice acting. My only pet peeve is that it gives cats a bad rap.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This game was amazing.  Worth every penny.  Elements of old school, pixelated point and click puzzles but not too hard so it doesn't ruin the flow of the story.  The story!  It was amazing!  It started out M.R. James (and I counted at least 3 references to a Warning to the Curious) and by the end it was all H.P Lovecraft.  While it pays homage to those authors it tells its own original story.  Congrats to the creators of this amazing game and story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I think I would recommend this game, but there are a few things I didn't like. Overall, the story is excellent (aside from one significant flaw in my opinion), the art and voice acting are exceptional, and the gameplay is fun. I think you'll probably enjoy your short time spent in this game.The best part of the game is its atmosphere. The overall atmosphere of the game is creepy, unnerving, a little bit gloomy (in a good way, if that makes sense?), and intriguing. It definitely earns its horror label, but I wouldn't consider it over-the-top scary at any point, although the horror does ramp up at the end. I have one minor complaint here that there's one point in the game where it could have been more frightening than it was (and should have been, in my opinion) but made the artistic choice not to be. But that minor gripe aside, the spooky folk horror atmosphere and intriguing plot were fantastic.As for the gameplay, it's pretty good. The puzzles are not too difficult. I needed a guide for one or two, but usually I was just missing something that the game did try to tell me. There were a couple puzzles where I had the correct solution, but needed to do an un-related thing before the game would allow me to do that thing. Thankfully this only happened once or twice.The writing is also truly praiseworthy, but... I  a little annoyed about a few parts that nearly ruined it for me. The characters are great. All of the characters feel like they fit well in the story's world and the decisions they make are logical from their point of view. Mostly. There's one point where this isn't true, in my opinion. This is the one main thing that I didn't like. Since I do recommend this game, I don't think I should go into full detail, but I'll put more details in the spoiler tag below if you . If you haven't played the game, do yourself a favour and try to avoid spoilers. This didn't completely sour me on this game even though I think it was a bit of a miss on the writers' part. I think if you enjoy folk horror, or just enjoy point and click adventure games and don't mind things being a little scary, you'll enjoy this game.OK, mild spoilers ahead. Seriously, it's better to not spoil it if you haven't played it yet.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: ok so overall i really like this game, it does everything right when it comes to classic point and click adventures: story, ambience, characters, dialogues, all fine. unfortunately i didnt like how the (only available) ending is enforced on you...it felt like i knew what was going on and my character should also know better than to do what is finally done. welp guess thats what they were going for and its okay for what it is, just wish there was a final choice of some sort. player agency when it comes to your fate.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A fun lovecraftian point and click game that is  and will run you about 4-5 hours of quality enjoyment. The weakest elements are definitely the lack of areas to explore compared to other adventure games, the lack of epic, overarching puzzles and there could definitely be more content and character development in the story. It's a decent recommend for most point and click fans, but also would recommend if you are new to the genre and want fully voice acted and accessible.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Great voice acting but there are no choices in this game that make a difference to the end which is one of the most flat endings I have ever experienced in point and click adventure games. In fact the final few minutes of the game are borderline terrible in my opinion and really derail the story. It feels like there was a great idea here for a story but they weren't quite sure how to wrap it up. I'm still a bit baffled by it. I understand the ending. It just feels cheap. Trailer gives away a good portion of the major events in the game, way too much revealed in those 90 seconds. As far as I can tell there is no way to miss anything in the game. There is no peril. Having the horror tag on it is almost a stretch.  There's actually no reason to ever save your game either since the game autosaves before every major storyline event. All the puzzles in the game with the exception of one, are probably the easiest puzzles I have ever experienced in my life. Easy like if you came across a puzzle where there was a hungry mouse and the only thing you had on you was a piece of cheese. Gee what could you possibly do here?? That's the depth of the puzzles. Overall I feel the like the game never got out of first or second gear. It just goes along and it's not long until you can tell pretty much exactly how the story is going to go with the exception of the  ending. When it's in a bundle in a year it will be worth picking up but I found it to be very toothless and unremarkable in every way with the exception of the voice acting which was fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow is my first foray into the realm of Wadjet Eye Games, known for their point & click expertise, and if the rest of their catalog is anything like this, I am eager to see more. Hob's Barrow has you take the role of Thomasina Bateman, an antiquary who travels to rural England for an excavation of said barrow but soon finds herself mixed up in the local mystery and intrigue. The game is broken into chapters that span several days with final day being the excavation of the barrow itself. This final chapter is probably the weakest point of the game for most as it is much more linear than the rest of the story and has a much higher focus on puzzle solving. I still enjoyed this portion of the game, but it lacks what makes the rest of the game so great and that is the gallery of colorful characters.Voice acting is great across the board, even for child characters, and the majority of the characters are memorable. The music and sound design do a good job of setting the tone depending on what events are taking place. There are dialogue choices here and there though I don't believe any of them have any long term impact on the story. The story itself is well paced, not overstaying its welcome and never feeling like it is hitting a rut. I was always eager to see what would happen next as the plot developed and new twists were thrown at me. The art style of Hob's Barrow is quite charming as well and while I wouldn't call the game "scary", there is some imagery that is certainly unsettling and creepy. Besides dialogue, there is puzzle solving to be found in the game, the most complex of which is found in the barrow itself. These puzzles are well designed though nothing here is overly difficult to solve. Many solutions are very intuitive and Thomasina will offer hints or clues to point the player towards the solution when trying something that isn't correct.I don't want to say much more else I would be diving into spoiler territory. I know Wadjet is well known among Point & Click fans and I look forward to playing more of their roster, but for those who are looking for their next adventure fix, look no further and give Hob's Barrow a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty well-written Point and Click Adventure with an intriguing mystery at its core. The characters are great, the voice acting is superb, the protagonist especially. The graphics look pretty and the art and animations are very good.gameplaywise it takes a bit to get going and there definitely could be more challenging puzzles in the first half of the game (the whole game is not particularly difficult). The conclusion is very lovecraftian so if you know what to expect from that you won't be disappointed.this is more of a creepy mystery adventure though. I wouldn't really call this horror. If you played and liked other wadjet eye/ cloak and dagger games you probably will like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I quite enjoyed playing this new opus from Cloak and Dagger Games. Its thrilling creepy story gave me very strong the lost Crown and the Last Door vibes. I have no idea if this was intentional or not but the game gives lots to think about even after completing it.The game is very polished. Graphically, this is definitely the most advanced art style from Cloak and Dagger Games, and the voice acting is excellent.Gameplay is mostly linear and straightforward until the final part of the game that requires a bit more brainstorming to complete.There is nothing particularly scary in the game but the atmosphere is somewhat dreadful and mysterious, enhanced by occasional creepy cutscenes. I can only recommend it if you like atmospheric horror games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: WOW!!! I've been playing Adventure games forever, and this is probably one of the Top Best games I've ever played! There are dozens of locations, dozens of characters, a long sweeping novel or movie style complete story. It's a bit of adventure, mystery, (light) horror, and it's nice and atmospheric. It's super cozy too. You can cuddle up with a blanket and some soup or hot chocolate and really get into the game. The town people change throughout the game and the bar even has a warm cozy fireplace like in the 1st Monkey Island and Calahan's Crosstime Saloon. I really hope this developer makes another game like this. It's unbelieably awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A really solid point-and-click adventure with good writing, sensible (and straightforward) puzzles and quality of life features like being able to double click to exit a location immediately. A nice length for the narrative and the ending literally gave me chills! If you are a fan of this genre, I highly recommend picking this title up :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly I do want to say that I love the art style and characters of Hob's Barrow! The pixel art is lovely and the animations are perfectly creepy. The plot itself was a bit weak for my taste, but the characters did help give it some additional flavor.However, I believe these above points are all dragged down by the gameplay. While I love point and click adventures, Hob's Barrow is too unintuitive for my taste. Being forced to wander around to various areas is one thing, but doing this with little to no direction is another. It's a challenge to get players to do what you want them to without explicitly telling them, and Hob's Barrow seems to struggle with this. If I didn't use an online walkthrough for some places, I doubt I would have had the patience to complete the game (getting elderflower was a nightmare!)You can tell that a lot of time, effort, and passion went into this game and I definitely don't want to minimize that! I do just want to say that its unintuitive gameplay makes it a difficult game to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game to someone who likes 90's point and click PC games like Monkey Island, and enjoys reading (especially Lovecraft).  Thankfully the puzzles aren't too difficult or obscure to figure out. The only thing I wish was slightly different is that there is only one definitive ending. Also, the voice acting is great. The main character is voiced by Samantha Béart who is also Karlach from Baldur's Gate 3.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A solid point-and-click adventure with an immersive story and intuitive puzzles.The story gets darker as you progress through the game, with horror elements more present, including jump scares. However, I'd say it's pretty tame compared to, say, Rusty Lake games. By the time you get to the truly horrifying stuff, it's mainly through cut scenes.I'd say the puzzles are intermediate level. Not too beginner but not overly advanced either. The more complex puzzles happen at the very end of the game, but even then you have enough hints to get by. Personally, I didn't need a walkthrough at all for this game, which is something. Everything felt very intuitive, and the one time I got stuck it was because I forgot an area of the map existed because I got a little too reliant on the fast travel.I will say I appreciate that this game offers a button to show all the interactable elements on the screen. I'm sure there's people who'll claim it's hand-holdy, but I like that I don't have to scour every pixel to figure out what I can interact with.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cool point and click adventure game.  The story is intriguing, the writing and dialog are well-written and performed, and I love the unnerving art style they use for close-up shots.  The puzzles don't really ramp up until the very end, but I think making the puzzles harder would have slowed the narrative momentum for me.Well worth your time if you enjoy old ScummVM type games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Received as part of the April Humble Choice, so not for free, but cheaper and with a bunch of other games.Very much enjoyed this lovecraftian, mystery, horror, point-and-click game! Pixel art is great and used really well for certain scenes. Well-written story.Puzzles aren't too challenging, though I did get stuck at one point.Only complaint is that by telling characters no, you just miss out on some stuff, so I feel bad for picking the option I wanted.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Every once in a while, I look at my giant pile of unplayed games and ask myself if I shouldn't cancel my Humble Choice subscription in the name of frugality.  Then I remind myself that game miser is not a healthy aspiration.  I must not simply slavishly add keys, but instead should go looking through the lists and install something that catches my fancy.Thus, in an excavation of my own barrow of games, did I stumble on this fine example of video game as art.  For the past two nights, once the little ones are asleep, I have had the joy of returning to my deep gaming roots to point and click my way through a virtual world presented in pixels of yesteryear size.  We live in a time of great plenty, when, for less than the cost of a bad burger, can story can sit unopened on a virtual shelf, patient and waiting.  Virtuosity is bundled with the prosaic, you just have to dig a bit.  Here is a delightful bit of prose married to art that may not be high definition, but that is compelling.Thanks Devs, for the joy.  I bought the rest of your stuff as a tip of the hat, and will make it a point to make the time to click it.  You've got a customer for life in me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great "Wadjet-style" adventure game! There's a real sense of mystery that pervades the entire game, with a conclusion I loved. It's classic style RPG-maker gameplay with some puzzles and some hunting for what's next. You may like the amount of puzzling and exploration on offer, or you may wish there were more as it's not stuffed with them. But the atmosphere and storytelling are really what set the game apart.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Guys this game is brilliant!!If you have the chance and you like nostalgic and engaging exploration and mystery solving, I promise you won't regret buying this one.I honestly kept searching for more games like this at Steam and I was not able to find any that were this good.The pixelated artwork is >very< detailed.I don't know how to describe it, but every scene feels like it's straight out of a framed vintage painting that you'd see in a farm cottage made by the grandfather of the previous owner. It just has this vibe, and I love it.All characters are voiced and the VAs did a really great job, especially the main VA. Sarcastic, funny and witty lines are all over, as well as capturing the weight of each life, of their memories, and when they share their stories.You won't regret playing this one! Go ahead, and have a great excavation...Don't forget: the answer lies in the soil...
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Credits just rolled and holy cow. The Excavation of Hob's Barrow is an immediate modern point & click adventure classic, a master class in video game storytelling and as of right now my game of 2022.Unnerving and gripping with dashes of warmth. Populated by wonderfully realised, layered characters and wrapped in an ever present sense of longing. I could go on and I absolutely will, but for now I'll leave it at that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: It's not often I leave reviews for games but The Excavation of Hob's Barrow definitely deserves one. A fantastic point and click that doesn't over stay it's welcome and keeps you gripped right up to the end. The voice acting is fantastic and the art style is beautifully done. This should be the standard that indie devs should strive for. Can't wait to play more bu the dev team.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This is an intriguing narrative point-and-click adventure, where Lovecraft, , and folk horror merge into a charmingly existential and desolate atmospheric puzzle game with a touch of psychological melodrama. blends the concept of scientific exploration meeting the unknown, told through a letter dictated/written by the protagonist, Thomasina Bateman, as she is invited by a mysterious character to an isolated area of the north of England to excavate a local burial site - Hob's Barrow. Things - as they are in folk horror tales - are not always what they seem...The story really fits into the Lovecraft style whilst taking its beats from folk horror rather than the Cthulhu Mythos, and the art style is a lovely throwback to older point-and-click games. The voice acting and soundtrack is top notch too. The puzzles were intriguing and neither too easy or hard to progress.I have to say I disagree with reviews that think this game should have choices, or an alternate ending for the following reasons: is not a particularly long game, so would be a nice one for a rainy weekend. I would definitely recommend this to people who enjoy a relatively quick dip into kooky Lovecraftian/folk horror narrative stories in their games through a point-and-click format.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A game with a very good and interesting story at the beginning, but it ends up being a bit dissapointing at the end.I find myself in a weird position where I'm not even sure of whether I like or not this game.I think that 'Mudlarks' will remain my favorite full-lenght Cloak & Dagger game so far. That game was extremely suspenful from beginning to end, and the ending was better than this one (at least in my opinion).
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Played this in a wet October in Yorkshire and conditions could hardly have been more suitable! It's an excellent, moody folk horror tale told in fine detail and with expert pacing. The only downside for me is the throwback late 80's/early 90's art style that has been done to death - even if Hob's Barrow does feature some of the most atmospheric pixel art I've ever seen - although it must be said that the cut scenes and animation are very good throughout. The puzzling will feel very gentle for aficionados, but that serves the pacing rather well and when the real puzzles ramp up in frequency and become more traditionally 'adventure genre' towards the end, it only serves to build excitement levels as you push on to discover the game's final secrets. Anything but hogwash. Ta-ra!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Ran into a bug that didn't let me progress on day 2. Well, I started all over again, game was good enough to justify that.Then I ran into another game breaking bug just before the finale. Ye, no thanks. Found no way to contact the dev so...UPDATE: got in contact with the dev who helped me troubleshoot. Really appreciated that. Now that I finished the game I can say it was worth it. Really great mood and setting, good writing. Hope they improve on the tech side of things though
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A modern classic. I'm really enjoying this. The voice acting is great. Im not too far in but so far the story seems smart and intriguing. Graphically, obviously they are going for the specific style and they nailed it. Having said that it is a shame that it isn't in a more up to date style. I would love to see this story and acting in the style of the Monkey Island remasters. Having said that, as you play you start to forget it. I'd liken it to watching a film in black and white or with subtitles. A few minutes in and you don't notice any more.Overall, very enjoyable so far, looking forward to getting further in.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The Excavation Of Hobb's Barrow is one of the best horror titles available in 2022 and you owe it to yourself to play it.This is a point and click adventure game with amazing pixel art, a fully voiced , brilliantly voiced cast (everything is fully voice acted) and a gripping story that will have you on the edge of your seat to it's horrific and clever conclusion.Thomasina Bateman travels to the Northern English town of Bewley where she has been invited by a mysterious local in order to excavate a barrow (an ancient British burial site). With many heinous myths surrounding the local barrow and a dark secret apparent to everyone, Thomasina attempts to go ahead with her plans without heeding any of the local myths and legends. This is the story of how that happens and what is in the titular Hobb's Barrow itself. The gameplay is mainly dialogue based with some basic puzzle solving. You explore Bewley and the surrounding moors overcoming various obstacles n your plan to excavate the barrow, remembering memories of your past and interviewing the somewhat unusual townsfolk to discuss your objectives. Puzzle solving is mostly very logical and while a few of them are based on pixel hunts I was never stuck for more than 10mins at time and things gradually clicked into place without too much thought. It was refreshing to play an adventure game without any ridiculous puzzle solutions. The games stand out more than anything though is it's plot. It has a sense of creeping and impending dread very similar to The Wicker Man and Midsommer with a similar "Pagan Horror" vibe as the story progresses. The story has some great examples of both subtle and fairly extreme horror (including some amazing body horror) and is very strong. Excellent writing is prevalent throughout. In the end I can't recommend this title enough, UK folklore needs more games and this is an excellent example of how horrific it can be. It's one of the stand out horror titles of the year and a must play for fans of scary games and even just point and click titles. Phenomenal stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The basic concept of "folk horror traditional adventure game" was highly attractive. But, despite having some memorable characters and genuinely beautiful moments, the overall experience falls flat from the cliche'd central narrative and the lack of exploration of the villain's motivations and ideology. There's something to love throughout the whole game until the finale, which completely throws out the realism that it maintains rather well to that point, replacing it for a cliche'd, thematically incoherent, puzzle dungeon. Unfortunately, that something is never the needlessly irritating and unrealistically foolhardy protagonist, or the entirely unnecessary flashback sequences which serve only to rob the plot of its mystery, both of which get a lot more focus than the genuinely interesting inhabitants of the town, the unrealized potential of the religious conflict that the plot rests on, and the joy of exploring a spooky rural setting in Victorian Britain. If the developers just explored what they had that was unique, instead of trying to do something that fit the conventions of a genre, it might have been great.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow is a wonderful short point and click focused on building a richly deep sense of dread and mystery. The full voice acting and music sound superb and the moments of detailed animation suitably grotesque. Puzzles are rather simple for the most part, which works well so the player is constantly pulled forward with the narrative. Though some points can leave you stuck just long enough to actually have to think. The ending comes rather fast and may not be to everyone's liking, but I felt it fit the themes of the story well. Some loose ends do seem to not get resolved, but perhaps this is in the nature of a story focused on unravelling the mysteries of a folk-tale.Would defo give this a recommend now the spooky season is upon us! 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The good: killer theme song, some genuinely scary scenes, all of the puzzles make sense.Stop reading here, support a small developer and buy this game. The less good: the stacked fetch quests not only were annoying, they made the game much too long. Bringing X to Y several dozen times didn't do anything but kill the momentum and vibe.Still an unqualified recommendation, but could have benefitted from a tough editor.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with a lot of classic 90s style point & click adventures, so maybe i'm a bit biased, but:Damn, The Excavation of Hob's Barrow was an exceptionally good game. I loved it! It feels like all the classic horror stories you find in old books and it looks and plays like the classic point & click adventures from the 90s.Atmosphere, voice acting, writing, pacing, puzzle design, art style, music... it all fits perfectly together and this might become on of my all time favorite horror adventures, sharing that position with games like The Last Door Season 1 & 2 and the original Black Mirror from 2003.It's not a too difficult game, but it still has some challenging puzzles. But the main focus is the story. If you like pixel art, the games mentions above, old gothic horror stories or Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis: This might be the game you're looking for.2022 has been a great year for point & click adventures so far because of games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Not since Primordia have I been so engrossed in a point and click adventure game, but The Excavation of Hob's Barrow had me hooked. _childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Finally! A Lovecraft-based work that isn't all about space tentacles or Cthulhu. Unlike other games or works of art inspired by the Cthulhu Mythos, this game tries to stay truthful to the style of Lovecraft's works, focusing more on the fear of the unknown. The story is all about building tension and suspense around the mythical Hob's Barrow, and the final reveal is done in a really heartbreaking way. It reminds me a little of the style of endings of most protagonists in Lovecraft's Dream Cycle. There are a lot of references to other Lovecraftian stories, such as 'The Call of Cthulhu,' 'The Shadow over Innsmouth,' 'The Cats of Ulthar' (a Dream Cycle tale), 'The Colour Out of Space,' etc.I highly recommend this game for any Lovecraft fan, as it utilizes the author's style well. Recreating the atmosphere of his works is challenging, and not many games do it well. For point-and-click adventure fans, this game features nice puzzles that weren't hard to solve, except maybe for some of the puzzles in the final area. However, I never checked a guide, so they aren't impossible to solve.I give this game an 8/10 because I would have liked more puzzles that made use of the 'combine objects' mechanic. Additionally, I would have liked the dialogue choices to matter more for the story, but it's not a deal-breaker for me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A great game, a well flowing narrative piece with intriguing "what's going on", a constant unease of atmosphere, game full of mystery with perfect level of difficulty.I really enjoyed playing it, I was so enthralled and curious, and wanted to know more and more until the finale, the balance is just perfect, the visuals, the atmosphere, the story, and voice acting is just perfect. Well recommended for a Point-N-Click classic.:)

_childDocuments_.review: Initially,  suggests the experience ahead is a little rote: An archaeological dig that will undoubtedly uncover some terrible secret and doom the protagonist to life in an asylum. Y’know, the Lovecraftian trajectory. The likes of , , and  all came to mind. As in those tales, we  where we’re going, and we know  how it’s going to end.Badly.But that’s its best trick. Because there’s no saving our hero, Thomasina Bateman. The game makes that clear from the off. Compared to the inquisitive, plucky explorer of the present, the Thomasina of the future is drained of everything that made her who she was, enduring a kind of living death. And so, we set out from a glum train station in the Yorkshire moors to trace the grim path laid out before her.Something about  it, rather than reading it, makes the familiar dark descent a whole lot more interesting. Because unlike a character in a novel, we ostensibly have agency over our hero, and maybe, just maybe, we can find a way to circumvent Thomasina's fate. It’s that tension that holds the game together as we search for the barrow she wishes to excavate, ever knowing that nothing good can come out of it.Thomasina’s destination, the town of Bewlay, is a strange place. The kind of strange that comes from somewhere so isolated as to exist within its own pocket universe, where everyone knows each other, and its customs are its own. Londoner Thomasina is a fish out of water here, and the game’s writing has a lot of fun with it. When you find the tavern you’re going to be staying in, you can almost smell the heady mix of ale and tobacco. There’s a warmth to the place, a sense of community, and most go out of their way to welcome you.And yet something is amiss. Some sinister secret none dare speak of but one that binds all of Bewlay’s residents together. As Thomasina searches for the eponymous Hob’s Barrow, that secret slowly simmers to the surface – and from a very unexpected place.The game’s inventory puzzles are well-placed throughout, neatly threaded with the many story scenes. They’re inventive, too, drawing inspiration from the setting. There's a small puzzle that involves creating a tincture out of local ingredients that I particularly enjoyed.The setting, both Bewlay and the surrounding landscape, captures the windswept vastness of the moors, with their muted greens and greys, better than any other game I can think of. At times I felt a little bit like Florence Pugh’s character in 2016’s , cold and wet and alone. It's beautiful, really.As the game approaches its finale, the game’s latent horror themes amplify in a big way, and something dark and malevolent swaddles Thomasina’s journey. I knew it was coming – how could it not? – but it was nonetheless deeply unnerving. The writing, sharp and slick, makes the inevitability of her doomed journey work exactly the way it needed to.Whether you’re into adventure games or not,  is a dark, gorgeous game worth dipping into it. It’s all a bit , actually - a comparison underlined by the excellent score.  relocated from the Pacific Northwest to middle England in the Victorian period.And when you put it like that, you realise just how ingenious the whole thing is.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing HP Lovecraft inspired story contained in a graphic package reminiscent of 90's point and clicks. I really don't understand the hate the Act 3 gets in the reviews, for me it was by far the most atmospheric (albeit smaller) Act of all. You have the first two Acts learning about the world and trying to understand what and whom you trust and who not and then you get smacked with a literal nightmare of happenings. The only thing i disliked is the lack of a real choice. Any "choices" you make are virtual, unfortunately the ending is only one and you can do nothing to change it. A big shame since this type of story and our protagonist deserved a chance to have an ending that you can alter to your liking. Especially since this could be done in a manner of what person you lay your trust in and who you believe is an honest fellow. Nevertheless, i wish there were more types of games like this out there, with that strong a feeling of cosmic dread. Hoping to a sequel!

_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Opened that Barrow yet?Is it all superstitious hogwash, or is there something more sinister at play? The mystery of this small town and its residents is compelling throughout. The atmosphere perfectly captures that small English town vibe, tandem with the strong feeling that you're not welcome here.The creepy close up shots introduced at times help add to the menacing atmosphere. This game doesn't need to rely on jump scares to get to you. Just an unsettling feeling that follows you as you get further into your investigations.There are some excellent quality of life features here to modernise the point and click genre. When you use a key once, you don't need to pick it up and use it again. Items are discarded when they're not needed anymore. If you need to retry a puzzle, the item you need won't need fetching from somewhere again. You can fast travel using the Map feature (next to inventory, hover at the top of your screen).There's a to-do list, so if you leave and come back you're not screwed if you forgot where you were up to. You can ask someone where to find something if you forgot. These are small things, but they make the game much more streamlined than point and clicks of old. Items are combined without you needing to click on each individual item. There are good visual indicators of when you may need to revisit an area. For example, small animals.Voice work is excellent. The accents can sound over the top if you know anyone from oop Naarth but it's still well done. The actress for Thomasina especially managed to convey emotion and personality wonderfully. Music and other sounds accompanied things well enough, but didn't make a huge lasting impression on me overall.The game runs excellently on Steam Deck. My only issue would be that it can sometimes be hard to discern items due to the pixel style. Press Y on Steam Deck to show all interactive items on screen to make things a bit clearer.Puzzles all made logical in game sense, only 2 took a bit of trial and error but nothing too annoying. Always grateful for point and clicks that don't use moon logic!A compelling mystery, that doesn't waste your time. It took me just under 7 hours to complete. I have my own thoughts on the story, but I want to keep this review spoiler free.Games with similar themes I'd recommend are: 'The Last Door' and 'If On A Winter's Night, Four Travelers' (which is free!) I hope to see more from this Developer in future. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow was a delightful surprise! I saw it on my store feed, and sorta impulse bought it based on the art, and wanting to play something spooky in spooktober. The story was engaging from the get-go, the writing was good, and the voice acting was actually superb! The game took me just over 8 hours to complete, but I got stuck at a couple silly points that probably added an hour over most people. I thought those 8 hours were well worth my time, and I'm very glad I found this game. The game is generally eerie, but not actually spooky for the most part, until near the very end. In the earlier parts of the game, the spookiness comes mostly from knowing that something bad is going to happen. But aside from the sometimes ominous music, nothing overly unusual is occurring. There were some mysterious happenings that went unresolved, but I am missing some Steam achievements, so perhaps I missed them.I thought the pacing was a little off at times, and either the 2nd or 3rd day has you doing some fairly tedious fetch tasks that I didn't feel added anything to the game. That day could have been almost entirely removed I think, to the game's benefit.All that said though, if you're reading this review you should probably play Hob's Barrow. :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game in almost every possible. It starts off on just the right foot and gets better as it moves along. The voice acting is very well done. The slow burn of tension and horror is managed perfectly. The characters all feel very alive and real. Basically, this is well-done horror movie with interactive features and puzzle-solving.As for the puzzles, there aren't too many moon logic ones. A few times, especially at the end, I had to consult a low spoiler walkthrough for hints but generally, you had all of the information you need to solve a puzzle at your fingertips. I don't want to spoil anything by discussing the ending but I'll just say I put it down quite satisfied.It worked perfectly on my Steam Deck and the cloud saves meant I could always play it on my PC with no problem if that was more convenient. The Steam Deck screen is exactly the right size for this game.

_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: While the game setting you to something amazing (Graphics, OST and VA), the story will be nothing more than the most obvious boring plot that was made time and time again, spoiler  . _childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A well polished, concise adventure game that doesn't outstay its welcome, rarely frustrates with its puzzles and provides a decent, compelling mystery plot.Enthusiastic antiquarian and barrow specialist Thomasina Bateman journeys to the damp, misty moors of Bewlay Village in England following an invitation by an unknown contact to investigate the local "Hob's Barrow". Along the way she meets a hell of a lot of people that don't want her poking around, and a few that do, but clearly have their own agenda. Also she seems to really enjoy being rained on despite having an umbrella hanging right there next to the front door of the inn she stays in.As a classic point 'n' click game, Hob's Barrow is streamlined as all hell. The game is normally quite clear in what you have to do next, where to do that thing and who might be able to help in that regard. In the rare times when this does not happen, a quick jog around the village talking to everyone about everything normally provides you with a clue, if not an outright answer. The game is very linear (I don't mean that in a bad way) and does not lend itself to endlessly clicking every inventory item on every gameworld object, unlike some games of this genre.The sound, music and graphical presentation are all worthy of note. A wash of dull browns, greys and greens coupled with chilling ambient music and rural foley combine to create a....a.....the only real word I can think to describe it is "damp". This game is "damp". I felt cold and wet and shivery just playing it.The story is not incredibly original by any stretch of the imagination, but it does develop and progress at an enjoyable pace. This is a short game but it works a lot into its runtime.My only real criticism is regarding the story which I've placed in the spoiler box below. PLEASE DON'T READ IF YOU HAVEN'T PLAYED THE GAME. Overall, if you enjoy mysteries or point 'n' click adventures, I do recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game. The art is beautiful, but the story is superb. Puzzle difficulties are quite simple. Gets harder by the end of the game but nothing too complicated. Indiana Jones influences are very noticeable, which is great in my opinion as it reminded me of my early years playing adventure games. Great job to the developers, this a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic point-and-click adventure with a spooky atmosphere, and one of the very few games I've been able to clear without looking up any cheats! (came close, but had an "A-ha!" moment just short of looking for hints! ...achievements are a different matter, to be fair). Literally about the one negative about the game is the ending is practically announced by Thomasina over the course of her monologues, such that the twist is not really a surprise, but in my opinion, Herbert alone is worth the cost of entry =D

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game but I don't recommend it.This game tells a story about a female  antiquarian  who  arrives in a litte town and does some exploration. Before the seconed day after her arrival, I  enjoyed the playthrough. There are so many vivid characters and good rainy atmosphere.But after that ,things just become worse and worseTo put it positively ,Mc is very brave and determined.However,the truth is that she is just being  foolish and stubborn. since the first day she arrived, everthing has seemed ominous.The unwlecoming local people,weird dreams and unfortunately loss of her money.Besides,  Every single person with decent sense of judgment would have turned back, but she didn't.And she was pretty surprised that others abandoned her while exploring the mysterious area.It's almost laughable—why are you even surprised, lady,given that it was obvious they would do thatBy the way , MC's father was being unconscious for 25 years, which means her mother was the one raised her and gave her the opportunity to learn.But apparently she only cares about her father and think her mother was"a coldhearted woman".LOL,dare I say ,such an ungrateful child she is.This game contains a lot of puzzles, espcially when it comes to the mysterious area.Given that it features pixel graphics and is quite dark, it can be difficult to spot tools lying on the ground. And MC doesn't gave any hints to guides you solve puzzles. you have to walk back and forth to find clues and eventually you might  gave up and check a guide.Due to lack of love for MC, it feels like I was forced to solve the problem for her ,which is  painful After all ,I just really get tired of those stories where MCs sacrificed themselves to save others while others try so hard to persuade them to go back and be safe.If I was MC's father, I wound rather have her stay out of trouble than make the same mistakes I made just to save me.I get tired of this game and don't care what the truth is.I hope this review could helpe somone who is woundering buying this game or not.For the people who cares , I don't think this game can  pass the bechdel test.All the female charaters are so boring and plain.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Very mid-tier writing, not exactly boring but close, and unsubtle. Puzzles and progression are far too easy most of the time, and the rest is borderline moronic (having to talk three times in a row to a single character to make the story progress, feeding a cat a severed hand for no apparent reason, and so on). Characters are uninteresting and lack depth. The game tries to create a folk-horror ambiance resembling The Wicker Man, but constantly breaks it with stupid characterization.Overall, not an absolutely bad game, but a mediocre one for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I just loved this.  It goes to show that a well written story doesn't need fancy animations (or 3D)  The pixelated characters had plenty of emotions and showed them well so that by the end of the game they were truly people that one might know. The story was engaging and compelling. The  background scenery was enchanting. So much love and effort went into this game ; it excels!! I would love to see a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Another knockout emotion gut punch from cloak and dagger games! i took too long in checking out these guys games but after finally playing Sumatra: Fate of Yandi a while back i was hooked, and played them all even  the mudlarking game which was quite good. So when i saw screen shots for this game and played the demo i was very excited for this one ,and it did not disappoint.So glad wadjeteye took on publishing this , having  the voice acting really took it up another notch . The story , characters ,music, art,puzzles are all amazing .I'm not sure i want to say much else to avoid spoiling anything . there is a commentary mode so there potential replay-ability .I've nominated it as my game of the year. hence finally getting this review iv been thinking about, written.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I loved it. Not perfect, but an amazingly enjoyable experience. After the release of the new Monkey Island and my ensuing disappointment with the horrible art, I had decided to set aside adventure gaming for ever. But I then I just chance on Hob's Barrow - my faith in the genre is restored. I just couldn't put it down. Only Simon the Sorcerer and Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis kept me so hooked. Those are far more difficult games, but I'm older now, and I have little time to spend on gaming. So the difficulty level of Hob's Barrow is actually perfect for me. Thumbs up guys!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Another Wadjet Eye adventure game that does not fail to deliver a short and picturesque story. The game has a nice pace, characters and dialogues are very well written and believable and there are a few twists and turns. The puzzles are not impossible but also not always simple. If you like adventure games, buy it. you will enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The Excavation of the Hob's Borrow is a pixel art mystery that initially captivated me. The story, while intriguing, took a peculiar turn towards the end, leaving me somewhat bewildered. Although I'm not averse to tragic endings, this one felt off. The gameplay itself was solid, but the overall experience left me with mixed emotions. While I still recommend it, I'd caution potential players about the potentially unsatisfying conclusion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: It's an OK game. Manages to stay suspenseful and mysterious throughout, though the ending left much to be desired.The puzzles aren't overly complicated and I didn't find myself having to look up walkthroughs until the very end of the game as puzzles got quite obtuse. The voice acting is pretty good, graphics aren't bad and the detailed close-ups for some scenes definitely heightened the unsettling tone. The soundtrack is simple but compliments the game well.MINOR SPOILER FOR ENDING: It's not too long, can be completed for achievements in 1-2 playthroughs though I'd recommend using an achievement guide if you don't want to miss any during each chapter. Dialogue choices don't seem to matter except for certain achievements. Overall 6.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: An amazingly well thought-through and beautifully executed game. The concept, atmosphere, story, art and sound design all come together effortlessly. The attention to detail is immaculate in all aspects of the game, from storytelling (the suspense, the reveals) to programming (excellent use of special effects). The praise the game has received is thoroughly deserved - this is a so much better game than big studios have been recently releasing, do not miss it. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Hail, Abraxas Rex!That ending was certainly something.A fairly short and simple point & click adventure game set in the moors of rural England. You are a barrow digger walking in your fathers footsteps.I believe this game was made using AGS (adventure game studio); so think indiana jones and the fate of atlantis for visuals.Gameplay wise this is a very simple game; I don't believe there was a moment when I didnt know what to do. There are no typical nonsensical puzzle solutions or pixel hunting. This is more of an interactive story. Story was ok as is the voice acting. The setting is great; with good ambient sounds.*edit: soemthing to something
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game for about 6 hours.This is my review. Overall 8/10. A really good game.Story is 10/10Voice acting is 10/10Sound and music is around 7 or 8/10Seriously, the voice acting is perhaps the best I have witnessed in an adventure game.I was not impressed by the pixelart/graphics. It was okay maybe 6/10, but not impressive. Thinking about some of the pixelart quality people "out there", I found it lacking. Wished for higher quality, but it's not total bad. Compared to the developers other games, I think this is one of the best.I wish the puzzles were harder, and I wish the ending was "brighter". You kinda end up with a depressive feeling.Overall, a game you must try. Price is not expensive, so no excuse.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Another Gem from Wadjet Eye. Incredible storytelling and a plot that kept me guessing throughout, questioning everyone! Delightfully frightening, and engaging. I loved the ending, and as expected, the dialog is not only believable, but so well performed. I'd kill to see a mini series adaptation. It's much better than the garbage on TV now.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Wow... wow. That was... absolutely incredible. The artwork is amazing, the voice actors were phenomenal, and the story line... wow. Once again, brought me to tears. Thank you for this beautiful piece of art. If you are looking for an incredible story point-and-click horror game, Cloak and Dagger games never disappoints! This is by far my favorite of all of the games that you have created, and I loved each and every one of your other games. Bravo!!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this! I really enjoy both point-and-click adventure and folk horror, so a game that combines them is right up my alley. Hobs Barrow is absolutely brilliant in every way. Wonderful pixel graphics, a great creepy atmosphere, clever, but not obtuse puzzles and a cracking story. Oh, and that ending!If you enjoy horror and this genre of game you have to play this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little slow-burn horror game in the pixel-graphic, point-and-click category. The puzzles are reasonable to solve, as you'll generally come across the items you need naturally and apply them intuitively. I ended up checking the walkthroughs a few times for hints when I got impatient. The dialogue can be a bit contrived, but overall the plot and voice acting are positives, as are the music and ambience. Not a magnificent game yet still worthwhile - I would definitely play a sequel or check out the next offering from the studio.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game from a friend and got through it in one sitting. The story was interesting and engaging... for a while. I quickly found I was getting  annoyed trying to find the right place with the right thing and the end itself left me going "Is that it?" For having built up a beautiful mood and sense of suspense, the finale was disappointing.For free, I'm only a bit sad for having lost the time. Watching someone play might have been more satisfactory? Maybe not.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an interesting story and builds its atmosphere slowly. The puzzles are never too hard, except for one obscure puzzle related to some herbs, which was a bit of a bump in the road. The voice acting is excellent, and the characters feel authentic. The last portion of the game is a roller-coaster of puzzles, and the ending is satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Great story, with some great art and voice acting. I haven't played a good old adventure game in quite a while and was pleasantly surprised by this. Unfortunately, it still has some pacing issues with some boring fetch quests and silly puzzles where you just mix random stuff together until a coin comes out. But the story kept it interesting until the very end. Lovecraft would approve of this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully eerie experience. It evokes perfectly the feeling of reading an old Victorian era horror story. Not overly scary but that underlying feeling of something being wrong is a constant companion.The art fits perfectly with the theme of something unsettling hiding behind a mundane facade. The wide open spaces communicate well the feeling of being all on your own, and the occassional oddities that only have a sinister connotation because you're already looking for something to be wrong add to that atmosphere.And of course, the music is very good and the voice acting excellent.A very fun and engaging spooky time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 for atmosphere, characters, and setting. It's a short-ish game, but doesn't feel like it. It's the perfect adventure game for anyone who enjoys a good supernatural mystery set on the moors. The puzzles can be challenging, but are always satisfying to complete once you figure out the answer. No moon logic nonsense here.I played the whole thing in one sitting and would honestly play a whole series in this setting. I look forward to seeing what game Cloak & Dagger creates next!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow
