_childDocuments_.review: Despite some flaws, this is a short folk-horror adventure game that's definitely worth experiencing if you have any interest in the genre. I wish the game wouldn't have played its hand so early. If you've read or watched some horror and strange/weird fiction, then you'll most likely be able to predict the entirety of the plot pretty early on. In contrast, the main character, Thomasina, is left in the dark for the entire duration of the game, which feels pretty jarring and greatly reduces the impact of certain story beats and especially the ending.As far as point-and-click adventure games go, I wish the puzzles were a bit more unique, but they're all variations on things you've definitely seen before, not very challenging, but not annoying either. Thankfully, the game just oozes eerie atmosphere, the small foggy village of Bewlay being brought to life by great pixel art, good sound design and an appropriately authentic cast of characters with impeccable voice acting. Again, if horror's your thing, I recommend playing this, it's the equivalent of a good short story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent voice acting and atmosphere; I enjoyed the story and narrative of the various characters. Cyril will remain in my heart. The only criticism I can give is related to some points in the ending; I would have appreciated the product even more if various conclusions and unlockable events had been included depending on the "faction" chosen. As for the rest, nothing to say. For me, it is 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A shallow narrative which will punish and mock you for decisions you did not make and feel you would never have made, if you had control. That’s actually pretty much a no go.No actually it’s a disappointment. I would refund if I could. But let’s get a little into the details.The game advertises with something of a "lovecraftian" theme? Like so many. Well don't get me wrong, some Ingredients are there. A mystical setting, suspicious characters, convoluted schemes, trust and betrayal, and some more, all there in a kind. It’s just not set up well. (Or at all)Characters, motives and reasons, all things you would want to add a little depth to, I think. (But that’s me being naive I guess) Most of these are as cliche as it can get, real paper-cutouts. The few Characters fleshed out a little, are inconsequential for the story. That’s actually not the H.P. Lovecraft school of storytelling.He actually did put some emphasis on quality there. So I expected at least a story slightly better fleshed out than the stuff that can be found for free on amateur Forums (Including a certain one for Adventure Games) Now here is the problem.If the Player knows that something is not a good idea, you often can ‘roleplay’ it (“I know that’s not clever, but does my character know?” “Nah ‘Narfel the Ox’ is a 5-int cave dweller, who doesn’t know anything.”). Now that’s impossible if the Character is explicitly told about something in game.You are not really left in the dark about what will happen next. (hints are as wide spread as they are inconsequential). You will literally be told whom not to trust (I still don’t understand why that was inserted; it looks like such a useless and forced insert; it’s not the only one) Speaking of inconsequential inserts, that do not improve the story, the puzzles or give further insight in the Lore (which starts pretty vague and will stay that way) there are some of these. Inserts which look like they were copied from stories with similar setting, but better setup (means stories in which these scenes made sense) If you want to write an ending like this, don’t give it this particular kind of “happy ever after”. Your NPCs are laughing at the player, who was literally forced into this ending. (again a very strange decision).But in the end this is an adventure game. And this medium of storytelling follows its own rules. Most storytelling follows the normal pattern of fetch this, get that, acquire some of those, the puzzles are mostly ok, a few quite good.Nevertheless, if you do this amount of foreshadowing and make things so painfully obvious, the player starts to expect some kind of control, some kind of agency (it’s a Game after all). It’s not even that this game has the ending it has, but that players will be forced into this ending by literally taking away control. (serious, it’s effectively cut-scenes, “you’re welcome” I guess.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: a fairly simple, short and easy adventuregame, but i really liked it. its very much a 'classic' (cosmic)horror shortstory in adventure game format. theres an argument to be made, that a bit more gameplay couldve enhanced the experience quite a bit, especially in the third chapter, which is very linear. the pixel art is pretty good, the cutscenes take the prize though, they have this weird kind of movement/animation, that looks really unsettling, and just works great.probably pick this up on a sale, since playtime is so short 13€ seems a tad high
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The setup and buildup for the story are both incredible, and the atmosphere is backed with beautiful visuals and quality voice acting.The puzzles are interesting and thought out and I only fell into the adventure game trope of "I know the answer but I don't know how the game wants me to give it" twice.The only big criticism I have is the lack of payoff for choices. Throughout the game you make a series of choices with various characters which feel like they are building up to uncovering some deep secret in the plot and avoiding the conspiracy. To give a particular example: But no such option exists. While the ending is powerfully dark, I would have liked at least the chance to confront characters with the evidence I felt I gathered, even if it doesn't change the ending.Regardless, I would still recommend this game as it was an overall positive experience which kept me engaged from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent horror adventure point and click game, with a dark story and excellent voice acting. The game can be finished in 5-6 hours. The puzzles are not complex and are mostly complementing the narrative and the atmosphere. Highly recommended. Just be aware the story is heavily inspired by Lovecraftian horror, so calibrate your expectations accordingly...
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games where a promising starts sours by act 2, and by the time the credits roll one feels only empty disappointment. Was that truly it?The game is professionally done without being clever or ambitious. Many praise the voice acting but unfortunately that is the only truly bright spot. This is no Monkey Island or Broken Sword.The puzzles are easy, the setting limited and game miserably short. Some supporting characters are engaging but they all drift away without much payoff. Our hero Thomasina is not particularly interesting, and by the end of the game I was sick of her and her issues. Is there no other way to develop a character than flashbacks screaming daddy, daddy?Animations were limited and bit ugly, often one could see that corners had been cut.As for the so-called plot, too many questions were left unexplained. What was the deal with the violin-girl? Why your assistant never shows up? Coincidence or conspiracy? Too many flashbacks and too little sense.And finally I must wholeheartedly agree with other naysayers - whatever little satisfaction I received from this game was spoiled by the ending that was both idiotic and unavoidable. Forget those S, A, B, C and D endings that other, more lovingly made games feature. No sir, let us present you with this supremely unsatisfying E- ending full of failure and ugliness. Enjoy your misery and depression.Storytelling is a rare gift, perhaps the rarest. This as an unfortunate example of untalented people trying way, way too hard.I recommend this game to those who enjoy lingering bad tastes in their mouths.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This delightfully creepy game had me fully captivated from start to finish. Reminded me of a horror Curse of Monkey Island! The puzzles were interesting without making it too difficult to solve on one's own. I don't think there was single overly long cut scene in the entire game--everything was neat, polished and interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it because I really enjoyed the Blackwell games. This has a different feel as it is more of a horror theme, and it does that well. Never expected to feel that much suspense in a pixel art game! I found it more story focused than puzzle focused, though it has a few good puzzles. If you like point-and-click games that tell a good story, this is a good one (Also go play the Blackwell games by Wadget Eye!)
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to Cloak and Dagger's next game since Sumatra, and I'm so excited to be finally playing this. Especially after playing the first chapter demo earlier. I'll leave a fuller review when I'm further in, but wanted to leave a review early since their games really deserve to explode in popularity. They're truly masters of their craft, and no-one else makes games quite like them.Following up after finishing the game, and it absolutely delivers. Had me hooked until the end. Folk horror is such a natural fit for these guys, and the addition of voice acting really elevated it. Gameplay flowed nicely, no frustrating puzzles, just short puzzley bits to break up the investigation nicely. Excellent all round!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent point and click mystery! Keeps me guessing a lot, and on my second playthrough, it's truly a "oh now it totally even makes a lot of sense." The voice acting, especially, is top-notch. The art/graphics/pixels are just marvelous! It was obvious this was made with so much love, so thank you very much for the wonderful experience!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, exciting but ultimately terrifying adventure reminiscent of the golden age of point'n'click games like Indiana Jones & the Fate of Atlantis.Don't expect an adventure as sprawling as that of Dr. Jones however - the story of Hob's Barrow is a contained, personal one and the better for it. Its grotesque cinematics, cold wave soundtrack and great voice acting give it a polish that makes the experience linger in your mind.The puzzles are easy enough so as not to halt the flow and the developer's commentaries call for a replay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Some things are best left buried beneath the ground.I will always continue to adore these point and click adventure games and the fantastic pixel art.The Excavation of Hob's Barrow ist not that difficult compared to other games in the genre. What makes this one special ist the story, characters, overall atmosphere and voice acting.It takes an almost lovecraftian approach to horror with an atmosphere that makes you uneasy, anticapating something awful around every corner but leaves most of it to your imagination.The characters fit the time this takes place in well and the voice acting is satisfying to listen to. The narration of our protagonist Thomasina feels so full of emotion and she did an amazing job especially as the story progresses.If you love these kind of games you will definitely enjoy this one.For Steam Deck Users: This runs great with the default controls.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: First off, the voice acting and writing were SO good!  *chef's kiss*  This game completely surprised me.  I was completely engrossed in the characters and story.  The puzzles were not overly challenging and were fairly logical (I only smacked my head a couple of times :-) ).  I highly recommend this...it was a gem and a joy to play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow is a fascinating little game, filled to the brim with a rather intriguing story (that I won't spoil here) and surprisingly decent voice acting from the entire cast. Clear Lovecraftian inspiration is scattered across every inch of this experience, without once feeling too derivative. Some of the puzzles felt a bit too long-winded, but the fault for that rests with me, as I neglected to use the fast travel provided in the game effectively. End of day, I'd recommend this game if you're a fan of point-and-click adventure stories with a horror twist. It may be short, but it's very much enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Engaging writing, logical puzzles, excellent voice acting and a decent pace make this one of the best point-and-click adventures I've played. I buy everything Wadjet Eye publish without reading reviews anyway because their games are always good but this one stands out. The best mechanic is the "map", a list of visited locations so you can very easily fast travel across the game world, something that is often lacking in this type of game. It's just as well as there is a lot of to-and-fro with the various fetch quests and often you need to talk to everyone again when a new clue is revealed. Definitely recommended and a steal at this price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Set in the rural English countryside the game starts off as though it were a biopic of real life Shropshire folklorist Charlotte S. Burne. The main character comes to a small community to follow her career ambitions and is none too pleased with their quaint and superstitious ways, only to begin to doubt herself as events take a turn for the Lovecraftian. Generally excellent, dialogue feels quite natural and all the characters believable. Some threads can seem to be unrelated to the main plot especially if you miss certain lines of questioning or avoidable interactions. Personally, I feel the plot fell apart in the last few minutes, resolving to something that was more ridiculous than the truly terrifying reveal the game initially appeared to be leading up to; however, for the vast majority of the playtime, if you have the attention span to engage with it thoroughly you'll get a lot out of it.Absolutely standard as point and click goes; I've never played Monkey Island though I've seen it compared. I have played Pyjama Sam however and I was right at home mechanically if not thematically. Puzzle resolutions all made sense, I think the longest I was lost was about 10 -15 minutes, never needed a guide. Aesthetically very pleasing, though often appeared a little blurry even at maximum settings.Never crashed, never experienced a glitch, ran perfectly even when abusing the skip dialogue and quick exit features. The main character fills the usual 'strong woman' shape we see everywhere these days, being often rude, condescending and obnoxious to the villagers, she even makes a point of getting out of her dress and into trousers at the first opportunity. However, to give credit, she is an actual fully formed character with desires, goals and even flaws; the fact that she has a real life historical counterpart in C. S. Burne that she is almost a mirror of, makes this totally in place and believable, even if not likeable. A worse offender is 'Horace', the ethnic labourer, out of place and out of time especially in such a rural location, within the game he is the greater sin as he works to undermine the parochial attitudes of the villagers towards anyone perceived as an outsider. However, again, if such a character were possible it would be as a labourer for a local lord, who sometimes brought them home from working their investments in the new world.I am forced to conclude the writer either was lucky enough to portray history accurately by accident, or actually well read enough to know what they're talking about. Overall, if you like Point-and-Click adventure games, Lovecraftian Horror, or English Folklore, then you'll fine plenty to appreciate with this game, I'd love to see more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This was the perfect game for spoopy szn. The voice acting was fantastic, the story compelling, and the atmosphere really great. The setting of northern moors in Victorian England made for the desolate and familiar but creepy portrayal of these people and their town. The puzzles range from super easy to nearly-head scratching, but definitely not too much to put me off really enjoying this game. I've seen a review or two complain about the ending... but unless the only stories you consume are Marvel Potter, you won't be disappointed. $15 for 6 hours of great fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This point & click adventure is a great example of how a slow paced horror story still works in a gaming environment, if you have fully realized characters, puzzles that make sense and don’t try to frustrate you, a storyline that slowly, subtly moves forward until it turns into an avalanche and amazing peaks of terror in between. Above all, The Excavation of Hob’s Barrow is beautiful because opposed to so many Point & Clicks, this game manages to be warm and heartfelt, so all the terror hits you twice as hard. Also, the voice acting, SFX and music are absolutely gorgeous. This feels like a classic horror story, in that its environment and characters draw you in as much as the mystery does. If you like to watch me gush over this game for 6+ hours, here’s my lets play:
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up in Yorkshire and knowing the Moors, it was the A++ Voice acting and Accents that made me really enjoy the game. There is so much dialogue, you got really interested into each of the characters in the village. You can tell the Developers really did their research and poured interesting and relevant lore into the game. The Story line is dark, and i wish players were able to make their own decisions, especially by that ending which left me wanting more with lots of unanswered questions. Sometimes you felt enraged by the decisions made by your character, and some of the puzzles were quite out of the box and took longer to solve. Nevertheless, this game is really worth experiencing and will stick with me for a long time!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Mmh, mixed feelings about this one.As a point & click it works well. I never got stuck for too long and the puzzles are logical, so it is pretty good gameplay-wise.Not so much story-wise.Narratively, it's a mess. There are lots of characters, but none of them matter if not to create fetch quests. She could be all alone in the village and the story would have unfolded just the same. There are also many objects, details, elements, hints, and stuff that are also useless to the plot and only exist for the puzzles.So, it feels like there are two games, where one takes place in the village, and the other at the barrow. The former was interesting but, again, had no incident on the latter. The latter was on point gameplay/puzzle-wise but made the entire first part felt like a waste of time.And because of that, the ending sucked (and although you have choices none of them bear any influence on the plot).Positive because it was somewhat good, and because I do hope the devs will polish their craft for their future projects.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Has some nice moments and does a good job of feeling atmospheric with the pixel art, but ultimately doesn't quite flow as a story. Too much of the actual payoff at the end of the story is reliant upon sympathy with a father-daughter relationship that we get given through frankly annoying flashback scenes, and there's pretty much no player/protagonist agency as the story nears its end. It sets up as a dark mystery but nothing is surprising and those mysteries it sets up are either forgotten or simply, unremarkably, resolved. There's no sense of getting deeper into the mystery as it goes on; there's just a bunch of stuff that suggests that what you set out to do at the start is a bad idea, but then you do it anyway. You could skip to the penultimate part of the game and nothing would be any different for not having played the beginning or middle. Feels like a swing and a miss - I'd say give it a go if it's in a sale, but compared to other Wadjeteye games I found this a disappointment.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A truly great adventure game, completely enthralling. Highlights being a fascinating and fleshed out cast of characters (complete with incredible voice acting), a genuinely suspenseful and intriguing story that feels literary, and how they totally nailed the Folk Horror atmosphere and setting. We need more Folk Horror in games! This one is a shining example how to do the genre right. If you're at all interested, pick this one up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This game ticked every box for me, as if they secretly spied on me as a target audience and tailored the game with:  -- A Beautiful retro graphical feel-- An exceptionally well-researched Victorian Occult Horror story-line-- A protaganist with character depth enough to identify with (so that you forgive mistakes you might have avoided)-- An easy-to-use point and click interface that keeps the story-line and puzzle elements front and center while game mechanics slide into the background until needed.  I believe this is Cloak & Dagger Studio's most ambitious offering yet, and builds on great work done with shorter mysteries like "A Date in the Park" and "Football Game."  I am so glad I checked in!  Well done Cloak & Dagger + Wadjet Eye Games!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Every time I hear about the death of the adventure quest genre, the mere memory that there are teams like Cloak and Dagger and many, many other incredible young development teams warms my heart with faith. I am extremely happy that every time Cloak and Dagger create original finished stories, thoroughly understanding the essence and laws of the genre, bothering very much with the development of characters and the world of their games, giving a truly incredible experience. Each of their games is unlike the other in anything, be it the setting, the genre of storytelling, visual features. Creative hunger, the desire to create something original is the quality of a true artist. And these guys are hungry, trust me.The Excavation of Hob's Barrow (which used to be called Incantamentum, which I liked better, but we'll leave that out of the picture) is a journey into rural Victorian England that seems serenely pastoral on the surface, but hides dark secrets in its depths. Our main character will have to reveal them, for whom it is also intertwined with muddy shadows from her past, persistently looming over her shoulder. And these shadows don't whisper, they scream. The suspense here builds slowly, as if corresponding to the spirit of that sleepy village in which you find yourself, where no one is in a hurry, no one interferes in other people's affairs, but get out of here and don't go into our secrets. As in the last big game of these guys Sumatra: Fate of Yandi, the level of scenario persuasiveness here is so elaborated and serious that this game can easily be filmed even tomorrow. There are no insignificant things that exist just like that, one way or another, even minor activities should form in you a certain feeling of this game world. And they do, it's incredibly nice to be here. The characters speak and act like living people, the strength of the main character is not that her strength is a MESSAGE, but that she is a strong and intelligent person who does not boast about it and does not try to exalt herself over others. The narrative here is so fluid, lively and smooth that the eye does not have time to catch on the plot seams, perceiving the story as something exceptionally whole.The game design is again close to flawless, the only blot for me personally is that sometimes the game is a little carried away by numerous dialogues with different characters, feeding them one after another in a continuous wave, instead of splitting them using items or a puzzle, but puzzles will already flood in the barrow like a tsunami on you. Collaboration with Wadjet Eye Games has brought results - the voice acting of the characters is simply amazing, these voices of the actors can be drunk like honey. Visual. I loved the visuals in their past games, especially in Sumatra, here they took a new pinnacle of quality. And once again I was convinced that it is not the visual that breathes life into the world of the game, but the game and its authors breathe life into the visual. Pygmalion brings the beauty of Galatea to life, not the other way around. The fantasy of the authors, the heroes of the game, the details - they make the visual pulsate and live, so for me this author's unique visual picture is more expensive than any multi-million empty graphics, behind which there is nothing. (damn, I already wrote this in a review of Sumatra, it's time to finish the review). I really liked this game. I, perhaps, am even glad that she was delayed for 3 years, but she got her current look and voice like this. I hope your journey with Dave Gilbert is long and rewarding, guys. Looking forward to more amazing stories.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked it! The atmosphere, the voice acting and the story were very good. Loved the close-ups and the portraits, looked very eerie and disturbing sometimes but amazing. I would like it if you could replay the game from chapters though.. I missed an achievement but my saves were either too early or too late so I couldn't 100% it :(
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: If you like point & click adventure games there is no way you should miss this game. Play it right now. Since you spend a fair amount of time in a pub maybe it's a Pint & Click? ;)Hob's Barrow is bad ass. I just finished and it took me about 8 hours. I got stuck 3-4 times for half an hour or so but did not resort to looking up hints or solutions. So the 8 hours feels like a "real" time.The story, writing and characters were great and as good as you're going to get in the genre today. The setting was fantastic. I loved the small northern England village full of locals who distrust outsiders and the locations were fun to explore.The mood and atmosphere in the game is great. It's not a comedy. it's gloomy with an air of something sinister and a slow burn story that unfolds bit by bit but it is never boring. The sounds and music area appropriate and support the setting.Easily stands as part of the two best PnC's this year with Hob's and Return to Monkey Island. Hob's is well worth your time and money if you like the genre. I've been a fan of Cloak and Dagger for a few years now since Sumatra/Yandi (Play that game too). Teaming up with Wadjet Eye here to boost production quality (voice recording) was a good move and hopefully the game will be seen by more people.Puzzles? Early on it's a bit slow and you don't do a lot as the game opens slow and talks a bit. This is fine. You start to get more involved and deeper puzzles and there are some good ones in the middle. The ending is great and the game ends very strongly both in terms of puzzle density and quality and story/location. Resist the urge to use any walk-throughs and study your items and surroundings.Some nice modern features like a To-Do list (came in handy) and a Map (which let you teleport to other locations instead of walking through 10 rooms). You can also double click on exist to load the next room. Space Bar will show y ou all the hot spots (but I disliked the little delay before they came up). Minor nit.Dig around in Hob's Barrow and get your hands dirty. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice Point & Click Adventure with a touch of an old film. I like how Thomasina is basically like a Dana Scully from the X-Files, there are no curses or mysteries in this small village.Oh yeah i should also mention, that i mostly played through the game on my Steamdeck.It works really great on it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing atmosphere, it reminded me a lot of the movie The Wicker Man, with a spoonful of eldritch horror added to it.The pixel art is very well done and the puzzles are all very logical (so they're quite easy as a result but it's not a bad thing).I was so into this game, I completed it in 2 days. Strongly recommended if you're intrigued by the setting!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Not what I expected: most of the game is just wandering around a sleepy village, running mundane errands for the villagers, with only a few hints of something unnatural afoot. This might not sound exciting, but it works: the slow burn allows the player to grow to like the protagonist and the other characters before... it would be a shame if something happened to them... Anyway, great writing, visuals, and music. This game brings the atmosphere of classic Gothic literature to life.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome point and click game. I got into the story as soon as I started. The music is also very fitting to the scenes and I thought the main voice actress was brilliant. My only grudge, if I ever had one, is that the puzzles are really too easy although, that might be a plus for some people. I prefer easy puzzles over convoluted moon logic puzzles anyway.This is a must buy to any fan of point and click adventure games
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: So, I normally love Wadjet Eye games. Unavowed and Technobabylon are probably my favorite adventure games of all time. But this game is terrible. I have no idea why people are praising it so highly, particularly as a horror title. It is full of terrible cliches and hardly any good or interesting horror. This writing is Baby's First Lovecraftian Horror Story (including the classic trope of "it was so horrific it drove people mad and I can't even describe the horror!!!"). And if you've watched the trailer, you've already seen nearly all the scary imagery this game has to offer.This game has Wadjet Eye's dumbest protagonist featured with what is probably the most repetitive (goofy-looking) jumpscare I have ever seen in a videogame. The jumpscare became more humorous than frightening by the end. There are also odd, repetitive close-ups of her eyes throughout the whole game, which -- while startingly the first one or two times -- became annoying in their overuse. And of course, what horror game would be complete without the old cliche of "traumatizing flashbacks of an ill family member"? Because when I think "fear", I think of harmless people in a bed! I don't know why this cliche is still going this strong. This game is spent more on sentimental flashbacks than actually frightening scenarios.And when I said she is the dumbest protagonist, I MEAN the dumbest. To be clear, the villains completely outline their plan and it is revealed to her....and yet she still willingly goes through with it. As a player, you are powerless to stop it and just have to sit there rolling your eyes at her sheer stupidity.  The whole slow-burn build-up is ruined by the blatant villain plot reveal, and as such it goes nowhere unexpected or interesting at what should be the most tense and climactic part of the game. The villains are literally reduced to cartoonish evil laughter by the end. There is also very little payoff and hardly any conclusion for most of the characters you have grown to know. There's even several unexplained mysteries which go unanswered, including the origins of some random feral child you meet. An all-around disappointment.Weird minor gripe, but for some reason the title menu art is insanely low resolution, despite the fact that it is obviously an illustration converted into low res pixel art. You can see clearly the proper illustration on the store page and in the trailer. Why they decided to convert it to a blurry mess is beyond me, but it looks terrible on a full-screen monitor.The few good things about this game are the excellent voice acting and fair puzzles. But that's about it. Instead of buying this, you're better off playing a better horror adventure game like "Gabriel Knight: Sins of the Father". If you're looking for something Lovecraftian, the text-adventure "Anchorhead" is far more horrifically frightening and tense. Or if you're even just looking to raid tombs, play "Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis". All are miles better than this.Or honestly....maybe just read Lovecraft.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful pixel art, great voice acting, and with such an intriguing story. Tension and mystery are built up excellently throughout the game's length. I don't think there are enough video games about folk horror so I am very thankful this game exists.Perhaps the most straightforward point and click adventure game I have ever played. Don't think I really got stumped for more than a minute at any point in my playthrough. I do really wish there was a bit more of a challenge in the puzzles. I found myself really enjoying the puzzles in the final act which made me realize a lot of the gameplay in the previous acts was something more like very engaging fetch quests.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Samantha Beart did an excellent job voicing the main character, Thomasina Bateman, and the supporting cast was excellent as well. It was engaging, I dig the pixel art, parts of it were f*cked up in an excellent kind of way. I had no idea what to expect, but the puzzles were pretty satisfying, and the story was enjoyable. Fairly quick play at 7-8 hours. Would recommend for any adventure game fans.

_childDocuments_.review: "The Excavation of Hob's Barrow" is a construction kit drag + drop game.  The "developer" used the craptastic Adventure Game Studio video game construction kit, using premade "child's play" design tools and filling out templates instead of doing real game development.A strong argument can be made that construction kits like Adventure Game Studio should never be used to make games for profit, as the "developer" has done here. Construction kits are intended to teach people some of the basic principles of game development, to make small demos to pass around with friends. They're not intended to replace the work of real, professional game developers. It's inappropriate when amateurs try to use these for profit, without any actual, real game development effort taking place.Case in point, Adventure Game Studio is a one trick construction kit, it's designed to let amateur "developers" who don't know anything about game development to make ripoffs of Monkey Island and Day of the Tentacle, which is pretty much what this is, except replacing the interesting and amusing game concepts and great writing with really badly done pixel "art" (like, the "art" here is so bad they didn't even bother hiring anyone who can do pixel "art" properly and just tried to do it themselves or something... needless to say this looks bad even compared to the other pixeltrash on Steam) a godawfully boring Victorian mystery theme. There's also some of the worst writing I've seen since reviewing asset flipped RPG Maker anime fan fictions.I suppose I should be fair, Adventure Game Studio can do much more than make Monkey Island ripoffs. There's also templates for Sierra games, so you can make Kings Quest ripoffs, Beneath a Steel Sky... pretty much any old point and click adventure, Adventure Game Studio makes it trivial to make a ripoff.  Does that result in professional, contemporary video games? Nope. There's a horror theme to the game, but the true horror is that someone actually thought it would be okay to use a construction kit then publish it as if it was a professionally developed game. So this is a badly written pixeltrash construction kit hammered out probably in the space of around a weekend. Even if the presentation wasn't awful, the weak game design should be enough to put gamers off. Sure, we can attribute some of the defects to the choice of using a construction kit instead of hiring anyone who knows how to do game development, and that's fair. Adventure Game Studio has never been used to make a AAA game, or even a modestly successful game, everything made with this is immediately relegated to the shovelware section of Steam and generally ignored by the 12M+ gamers on the platform. That's understandable, most gamers have good taste. Let's stop for a minute and ask why Larian studios didn't use Adventure Game Studio to make Baldur's Gate 3. Oh yeah, because they're professional game developers. Night and day really, isn't it?But what about the technical execution? That's a hard fail.Due to the choice to use a construction kit instead of doing real game development, there's a number of defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.A choice was made to use obsolete, decades old retro pixel "art" as a substitute for contemporary PC graphics. It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget or talent, regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is extremely low as a result.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality. Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standard for any modern PC game.So, should you buy this game? Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?"The Excavation of Hob's Barrow" has the almost unethical price of $15 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games. Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend. For comparison, the $15 asking price for this game could get you games like "The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt", "Prey" or "Final Fantasy XIV Online". This weak construction kit game also costs more than any of the Monkey Island games, Maniac Mansion etc... there's simply no reason for any gamer to waste their money on this.The developer has weighed in to inform everyone they didn't read the  for Steam "partners", or they deliberately ignored the part where Valve says:The developer breaches Valve guidelines to let you know that he is THE MAIN CHARACTER. Steam isn't here for the 12 million gamers who support the platform, no, Steam is here to stroke the ego of one guy who doesn't even know how to develop games using professional game development tools, and had to use a construction kit instead. Steam is not for gamers, it's to satisfy amateur developers who aren't even talented or qualified enough to gain actual employment as professional software engineers. That aside, the developer admits they didn't hire a team of talented staff to produce the game and tried to do the whole thing with only two developers, instead. This is a lot like boarding an airplane, and halfway through the flight, having the pilot come out and serve peanuts. It's going to end in disaster. It requires a team of competent people to do a complex job properly, and that's not what has happened here... another explanation for the poor quality of this game. Imagine if Red Dead Redemption 2 was made with only 2 people. It would be a disaster. Just like this construction kit flip is. That explains that.Remember, this is a PAID PRODUCT. This amateur is trying to profit from using a construction kit and pretending they're a real game developer. And they're upset when someone points out construction kit garbage is construction kit garbage. The developer whines that telling gamers about the low quality of bad games is somehow harmful to developers. What about the harm caused to the gaming industry being flooded with this low quality construction kit pixelcrap pollution? Nope, only the developer matters. There's simply no regard for anyone else here. The sheer self absorbed arrogance is an insult to gamers and to the professional game developers who work long hours, sometimes 7 days a week to produce high quality games for gamers. They whine that they aren't very good at game development and it took them three years to use a construction kit to pump out something that could have been knocked out in a weekend.  The only thing that matters is the quality of the resultant product And that's just it... ultimately it's not whether the developer has a terrible attitude or not (they do), it's about the quality of the game, and what's good for gamers. This game fails on its own merits, as my review explains.Nothing in the developers pointless breach of Valve guidelines changes any of the objective facts of my review. My review stands unaltered. I cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow is a very enjoyable point and click adventure game. It has beautifully detailed pixel art and animation depicting the rural village of Bewley in Victorian England. The voice acting and dialogue for all characters were executed very well with their own quirks influencing whether they are trustworthy or not. It does a smooth job of settling the player into the game to engage with members of the community and help them in exchange for clues or information about the mystery of Hob's Barrow. The puzzles throughout were also well-executed as they mostly connect together to reach the main goals. The occasional multiple choice responses implemented in the dialogue between the characters have minimal impact in the bigger picture. It could have been really interesting for these to be fleshed out to show the impact the relationships have on the story. Overall, a great game that will make you try and untangle the narrative after finishing it.Verdict: 8 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. The graphics and animations are great, the voice acting is fantastic, characters are memorable, atmosphere is thick, puzzles are elaborate without ever descending into moon logic and the story is really good... until it very suddenly isn't.SPOILERS:There's a cutscene right before the game's final act where the conspiracy at the centre of the story is revealed in its entirety to the main character. She proceeds to do absolutely nothing with this information and wanders right into the trap. I know 'if I were in a horror I'd just leave' is trite but at that point she logically should have just said 'yeah I'm good' and bailed; plenty more barrows in England to write about, after all. Get rid of that cutscene and the ending would have been a lot more effective, instead of just making her seem a touch dense.I also feel like the ending itself was overly cruel. True it's horror and it's not supposed to be a happy fun time, but I thought it could have gone in a more interesting direction.There are also a handful of plot threads that aren't really resolved in any way... to give one example, why does the game make a big deal of the the priest throwing up when you first meet him even though it goes nowhere? What was with the guy strung up and stuffed with flowers? Again, never explained.END OF SPOILERSDespite those issues, I'd still recommend the game for the reasons listed at the top. It's a good length and a fun, memorable adventure. Props especially for all the authentic Yorkshire accents and dialect.

_childDocuments_.review: This is kind of a neutral recommendation from me. This is a retro style point and click adventure game and it looks great (though I didn't really care for the rotoscoped closeups) and has nice music and voice acting. The atmosphere is great, but the actual gameplay feels VERY adventure game-y in terms of doing these extremely long fetch quests to get a simple item and I found that parts of the story weren't communicated all that well considering the conceit that the game is Thomasina’s letter to her mother. There are dialogue choices but considering that this has all already happened, you get “but thou must”ed along to the next part either way.I know this sounds like a lot of complaints but overall it was a nice bite-sized folk horror game in a neat setting. Recommended in a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one for meThe game gives you the vibes of  90s pointNclick games, the atmosphere, the writing, the characters, and the VA are all TOP NOTCH.The ending, however, leaves you with a bitter taste, I wish there were 2 endings, a 'dark' one and a 'less dark' one, it feels underwhelming that you cannot change what is about to unfold in the final chapter.They could've made the choices you make during the game affect the final outcome, but the choices made feel meaningless if they are not going to change anything.Also, there were multiple questions left unanswered and unexplained.I will give this a thumbs up because I love this genre, but I warn you that the ending might be distasteful. _childDocuments_.review: This could possibly be the best modern point and click adventure! Its as close to perfect as the genre has come since the Lucasarts classics of old. Pros:*The most gorgeous pixel art graphics I've ever seen, with lovely fluid animation* Voice acting so good, its no surprise it was nominated for so many awards.*A story that keeps you riveted right from the start and keeps you on edge till the credits roll* So much atmosphere, like a good horror game should have. Genuinely kept me on edge at points.Cons:* NoneFor people warning about a poor ending, all I will say is its very Lovecraftian in its execution, and as long as you like that style, the ending will pay off for you in spades!If you like gothic horror, graphic adventures or just a good story, buy this game now!

_childDocuments_.review: The Excavation of Hob’s Barrow definitely oozes quality from the jump. The art and music are great and really lend to the folk horror vibe the game has going on as you explore an isolated British village out in the moors. The game manages to capture the desolate expanse of the moors so well with relatively little scope.  The writing is also quite good for the most part; the protagonist, Thomasina, is well fleshed out and a good chunk of the supporting cast have some nice depth to them too. The voice-acting is also top notch, as expected of adventures games published (as well as developed by) WadjetEye. The puzzles are also pretty solid, there’s one puzzle that I felt was a bit too obtuse in finding the item you needed, but it wasn’t too bad. The puzzles are mainly interacting with the characters and inventory puzzles. The endgame goes more into logic puzzle territory but I thought those were fine. The game does has some nice quality of life stuff too like fast travel and a hotspot button.What prevents the game for achieving true greatness and what soured the experience for me though is its complete wet fart of an ending. It’s a horror story, I’m not expecting happy endings here where the protagonist gets away unscathed, but Hob’s Barrow’s ending is Regardless of its full pratfall right before the finish line, Hob’s Barrow is still quite good and worth playing, especially for the Halloween season. Do kind of hope it gets a remaster/patch down the road to fix the ending like Kathy Rain did though.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a terrific game. The story had me sucked in from the beginning and was very hard to step away for a break when needed. The voice acting is top notch and again without out that being so high the game may not have been so amazing either so very well done. The gameplay is varied and never wanders into being too difficult that it halts the story for too long. Classic adventure game tropes are very welcome in this vein. Overall, without any spoilers, this is such a tremendous experience inspired by some classic British horror movies (Wicker...) and even reminiscent of an awesome game on Steam 'The Lost Crown' which has this beautiful, yet dreary, British landscape to house such a intriguing mystery.Buy it, play it, and never forget it

_childDocuments_.review: "Hob's Barrow" is a highly atmospheric but rather flawed horror adventure game that's still well worth playing.PROS:+ A great plot set-up.  You play Thomasina Bateman, an antiquarian and archeologist in Victorian England who has come to the fictional village of Bewlay in the North of England to excavate a local ancient burial site, for reasons both professional and personal. You immediately know that you're in for an old-fashioned rural horror story (think "Wicker Man") and you're keen to get stuck in+ BRILLIANT atmosphere and setting.  Bewlay feels incredibly well-realised; the lo-res graphics actually contribute to the despondent beauty and quiet unease of the place and there are so many wonderful graphic touches (rustling leaves on trees, rainfall, lit windows peering through the mist that descends at night) that I actually found myself ignoring the handy map shortcuts in favour of wandering around the village because I loved being there so much.  The understated music and sound design added to all the above+ Likewise, a varied cast of suspicious locals are brought wonderfully to life through a combination of good writing and quality vocal performances (with the regional accents only wavering very occasionally) and they add to the horror atmosphere / gameplay by being believably reluctant to help you on your mission+ Thomasina is a charming and determined protagonist portrayed brilliantly by experienced voice actress Samantha Beart; I had huge fun playing as her+ The puzzle design is, for the most part, nicely paced and integrated; I felt challenged enough but I never got stuck or had to resort to a walkthrough; (spoilers ahead!) CONS:- Towards the end of the game, the puzzle design started devolving into a series of fetch quests: "Get A to give to B, so that they'll give me C which I need to give to D, who in turn will give me E to give to F, who will then give me G, which is the thing I wanted in the first place" sort of thing.  While the quests allowed me to spend a little more time with the Bewlay villagers they also felt increasingly disconnected from the main story, always a disappointment in a mystery / investigation-driven plot- Speaking of which, unfortunately the main disappointment was the story, which starts very strong but finishes weakly.  Spoiler-y opinions ahead:1. 2. So despite my cons (particularly my reservations for the story), why do I still recommend it?  Because what's good about the game really is very excellent; the developers are clearly talented and have poured a lot of hard work, detail and passion into this game, all of which made it immensely enjoyable to play, despite my misgivings.  My sense of excitement and involvement at the beginning was so great that I played the entire game through in just two sittings.  I also want to see these developers succeed and go on to make other adventure games, hopefully learning from and building on their experience with "Hob's Barrow", and I will absolutely be back to check out further Cloak and Dagger games in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: If Wadjet Eye Games publishes something, I tend to pay at least some attention. I didn’t like every game they’ve ever published and not every game they’ve ever made, but they do tend to pick the titles that have something interesting about them among many a project made on Adventure Game Studio. So when The Excavation of Hob’s Barrow got announced, I was curious as to what it might be. My curiosity only increased during the first hour of the game and I was hoping that the game will remain as interesting throughout. It didn’t.The concept for The Excavation of Hob’s Barrow is pretty simple, but there’s nothing bad about its simplicity. It’s a story about a young antiquarian/archaeologist being invited to a remote English village to dig and explore a supposedly famous (at least locally) barrow. Except, when she arrives, the town is far from friendly, there’s no one to meet her and everyone says that they’ve never heard of the place. It’s nothing novel and the story does go the obvious and predictable path, but for the first hour there are enough bold storytelling decisions and atmosphere to keep your interest piqued. The game got me on the first unexpected jump cut transition and unorthodox choice of music, somewhat reminiscent of John Carpenter, but with a more folk English twist. And for a while I was hooked.Unfortunately, and I don’t know if this was a choice made out of want or need, but despite being such a story and atmosphere driven game, mechanically it rather quickly devolves into a rather generic puzzle solving type adventure. As in – you do solve problems, rather than abstract puzzles (well, until the final part anyway), but you do that in the most obtuse, stupid “find some item to use elsewhere” way that never fits the character or the mood. So instead of you consciously solving a problem, you might need to wonder around and do unrelated things in unintuitive and narratively conflicting ways until the solution to your initial problem will manifest itself.Sadly, the predictability and uninspired nature of the story also becomes more notable, especially by the end. Where you feel that this whole story would’ve worked wonderfully as a horror story that you read from the perspective of the main character. But feels incredibly stupid when you have to play it out interactively, because as a player you have a completely outside perspective and you’re never given enough reason to truly “get in the shoes” of the character, or be blinded to some things the same way she might be. So what would read as a tense and terror inducing event, plays out as something really dumb.But overall, The Excavation of Hob’s Barrow isn’t bad. It has a cool sense of style, the pacing is relatively good and the atmosphere it builds at the start is fantastic. It’s just that, in the end it feels like a really bland game and a mostly wasted opportunity. I got reminded of how wonderful The Last Door is in comparison, despite it being a far simpler and more minimalist title, but with a similar atmosphere. You probably won’t regret playing The Excavation of Hob’s Barrow, but there’s also a high chance you won’t remember it soon after completing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Dive into "The Excavation of Hob's Barrow," where you play as Thomasina, a stubborn archaeologist who ignores all red flags in pursuit of digging up something truly ominous. Navigate a village full of charming yet suspicious locals, all while piecing together puzzles that range from the whimsically folky to the downright eerie. The pixel art style evokes a nostalgic charm, but beware—this isn't just a cozy Victorian dig; it's a descent into madness. Perfect for those who love their point-and-click adventures with a side of existential dread and a sprinkle of folk horror.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic period piece in the vein of MR James. This point and click adventure is beautifully set in the Victorian era and moves much like a horror story from that era. This is a somber dark and slow paced story that can end only one way. It feels like a classic point and click adventure game, with a mostly linear plot, but after you finish the game, it makes a lot of sense thematically. A more open world game wouldn’t be as satisfying or fit the story this particular game is telling.The voice acting is fantastic and brings the pixel art to life. The music fits the game wonderfully, and while none of the tracks are going to stick in your head hours later, you’ll enjoy them while you play the game.Hob’s Barrow reminded me of classicHorror adventure games like The Lost Crown, Dark Fall and the many games The Adventure Company/Dreamcatcher published back in the day. I recommend it highly to fans of the point and click or horror genres.

_childDocuments_.review: This game absolutely nails it, this is exactly what I was hoping it would be.It's like if Black Mirror was made by Lucasarts, with the careful attention to detail and professional voice acting that implies.Anybody who enjoyed The Dig or the old Indiana Jones games will like this - except Hob's Barrow has a couple of little QoL improvements to make it suit modern expectations.It's not too tricky either, so a good place for people who aren't already familiar with the genre to start.  Couple of puzzles require the player to be familiar with certain concepts before playing but it's nothing a puzzle fan won't figure out.If I have one critique it's this: The trailer contains spoilers, and that makes the publisher look amateurish.There's a fine line between drawing attention to potential buyers and giving too much away.  If you're reading this and didn't watch the trailer - Don't watch the trailer!  Just play it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are ridiculously easy for point n click veterans (especially if you've ever come across Gnosticism - or Greek, at that), and the clues are on the verge of being nonsensical (and, in one case, plain wrong; it's Sigma, not Epsilon), but none of this is to say that I didn't enjoy myself enormously and would wholeheartedly recommend the game simply for the gripping story and the quality of the writing, voice acting, music, and sound design. This is, overall, an excellent effort which puts narrative first and puzzles second. And so what? It's an excellent introduction to a genre in which far too little is published, but I'd wish for an updated version with harder puzzles, where one has the choice between easy and hard.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Atmosphere and voice acting were excellent. They also do a great job slowly increasing the sense of unease as the story progresses. No annoying pixel hunting or deranged adventure game logic moments either.Puzzles were for the most part really straightforward and not particularly difficult to figure out, whether that's a pro or a con is up to you.My only major gripe is that stupidity is basically the only option when it comes to the story. Thomasina ignores some really blatant hints that there's something terrible in Hob's Barrow and is then surprised when setting it loose makes everything worse. Hopefully we'll get a sequel where PUNISHED THOMASINA has to go and set things right.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feeling about this game. Hob's Barrow is a classic Point&Click game with beautiful pixel artwork. The story is about Thomasina Bateman, an Antiquarian writing a book on the barrows of England, documenting the treasures she finds buried within. Upon arriving at the village, she noticed she was not welcomed, they dislike strangers, but being as stubborn as she is, she kept asking around to find the man who had invited her to discover the secret of Hob's Barrow.. little does she know it is all connected to her bedridden father. I enjoyed the artwork and the scenery, although the areas are limited. The voice acting was outstanding and one of the reasons why I kept playing the game. The story however was all over the place, especially the last part very unsatisfying. The puzzles were easy, but the errands were way too much, it felt as if they made it to stretch the game and make it seem long. There are some of the characters who I still don't know what is the purpose of them.Pros:+Good pixel graphics.+Dark story with twists.+Good soundtracks.+Great voiceovers.+Ok puzzles.+Steam achievements.Cons:-No reply value.-Too many sides fetching requests that don't add up to the story.-Lots of backtracking-No map.-No hinting system.I found myself having more questions than answers after finishing the game, there are some areas that were not clear to me, and some other items I didn't use. I'm not sure if I missed something or if it was intended. Overall, I recommend it only if you enjoy these types of games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Oh this is a painful one. Recommended for a great first half, excellent voice work, an evocative setting with gorgeous pixel art (especially the close ups which are used to great effect.Unfortunately the game is let down considerably by not leaning into the intriguing bones of a story during the setup, winding up with a railroaded finally that was devoid of any more conversations or logical puzzles. The ending removes any agency from the character while also making the puzzles in the first half seem useless and the villains seem excessively stupid and obtuse. There are generous readings you can make to explain things, but far too much happens offscreen, leading to a lack of emotional punch.More care should have been taken during writing and revisions to consider the players emotional involvement and response. I hope the team can get it right with whatever they do next - there are so many good elements but they do not land here.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This game has flaws but overall was a very fun adventure game, if you want a full review of this game head to the message board here on the steam page for this game. I go into great detail as I play. Overall the game is pretty easy puzzle wise and took me about 8hrs to beat. I would give hobs barrow 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A great horror game with a properly unsettling ending. Voice acting and art were wonderful, and I enjoyed the musical parts. My only complaint is the sudden stack up of puzzles in the last leg of the game because it interrupted the flow/challenges that the story had been using up until then and didn't quite fit in with the rest of the narrative. But that would only be about 10% of the game and 90% solid game is great odds!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A really solid folk horror point-and-click game. It scratched an itch I didn't know I had.The Excavation of Hob's Barrow captures the mood of The Wicker Man and does a good job of weaving in some cosmic horror along the way. The ending was quite linear, but I feel its inevitability was narratively justified by solid groundwork in the first two acts.It's a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been playing point and click adventure games since I was a kid in the 90s on my Commodore Amiga. This is with out doubt the best point and click I have played since the original Monkey Island, maybe this is even better.Emotional story that keeps you gripped from the start, genuine laughs and genuine scares, logical puzzles (unlike in some point and click games) and at the same time relaxing to play. Ironically as it happens, I live in a small village outside Bakewell, near to a barrow and I’m sure I recognise some of the characters on here from the local pub.All time classic. Just buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it was okay. Three quarters of the game is fetch quests, and it becomes a bit ridiculous by the end of the town section. Final section of the game is cool, wish there was more of that, you know, Lovecraftian archaeology stuff, which is essentially the promise of the title. Instead you spend most of the game running errands for people in a sort of Wicker Man homage. Voice acting is generally good, but too many characters are clearly voiced by the same person with almost no variation in their voice. Protagonist is likeable. I'll give it a solid "good," as it did generally keep me interested throughout, even if a lot of that was because I was waiting for the more interesting parts to kick in, and it's overall just well made.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A point and click horror game where you play as Thomasina Bateman, an antiquarian archeologist whose latest excavation brings her to a remote village on the Yorkshire moors where something sinister is lurking.  Anchored by a great atmosphere, strong characters, and compelling story but let down by the last part of the game and ending.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic! The Excavation of Hob's Barrow has a real feeling of nostalgia about it with the pixel graphics and point-and-click interface, but with stellar voice acting and puzzles that are enough of a stretch to hearken back to the old favourites without being complete moon logic. I was sad to think I'd overestimated the spooky factor at the start, though I still enjoyed it; I'm glad I stuck it out, because it definitely ramps up as you uncover the mystery. I loved every minute.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I always look forward to a new game by Cloak and Dagger, as I know it will be a good adventure with quality writing, a compelling story, and reasonable puzzles. I became a fan of theirs after playing Legend of Hand ... a very clever game with a martial arts theme.With The Excavation of Hob's Barrow, I was not disappointed. It takes place in Victorian England and follows the adventures of Thomasina Bateman... a woman who is ahead of her time. She wears trousers and tromps through the countryside, on her own, in search of archaeological treasures. The dialog is intelligent and witty, with outstanding voice acting. The story is a bit confusing at first, with flashbacks that seem unrelated. Then, as you progress, the pieces fall into place and you will want to keep playing to see how it all turns out. The artwork is well done and I remain  impressed with how much can be expressed with lower resolution, pixelated graphics. Each time Thomasina primped in her hotel room, I had to smile.The game follows traditional point-and-click mechanics with quite a few 'find and use' puzzles as well as multiple 'fetch' errands. There is enough dialog to develop the characters and story, but not too much to be distracting. There is a map for fast travel (updated as locations are discovered) and a task list to help keep the player on track. In addition to an intermittent auto-save,  multiple slots for explicit saves are available (a feature I always appreciate). Most achievements are story-related, with a handful that can be missed. If you are using multiple save slots, completionists can circle back to pick up missed achievements without replaying the entire game. All and all, it is an excellent adventure that is intuitive and enjoyable to play. I would highly recommend this game to those who enjoy traditional point and click adventures with a compelling story and an intriguing main character. The story takes some dark twists and the atmosphere is rainy and gloomy. All, in all, it should hold your interest until the very end.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Very good point and click. I recommend this to everyone that enjoys point and click adventures and wants to play a new one. Artstyle and voice acting are great. The riddles were never unfair and overall the game felt rewarding and made me want to continue playing. Only the last part of the game was not as good as the rest in my oppinion. Overall i clearly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Uhhhh I didn't really like it but I don't think it's a bad game-The voice acting is good and it's fully voiced-The art is nice -There's so many achievements that it's satisfying, and it's easy to 100%But -The story is really slow and sometimes there's too much dialogue/information, I found myself losing interest-I was lost on what to do a few times, and some of the puzzles were difficult to figure out. I had to use a guide several times-I expected it to be more horror but it's not really 'scary' until the last 30 minutes or so-I thought the ending was dumb xD I thought it could have been better hinted at throughout the game and the MC didn't react as much as I think a real person would haveOverall it's not a bad game, I was just expecting more
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute gem of a game. If you enjoyed early 90s point and click adventures (particularly LucasArts & Revolution's earlier outputs) then this is a must-own game for you. If you're not a fan of that genre, this could well be the title that changes your mind.It's hard to find fault with The Excavation of Hob's Barrow. A strong story, excellent retro graphics and superb voice acting deliver a genuinely interesting game. Puzzles are well-balanced - some are easy; others a little more challenging, but none feel unfair or overly obscure - only once did I need to check a walkthrough for a solution. The story progresses at a good pace and the game is packed with interesting characters, against an increasingly mysterious and sinister backdrop. The interface is well-designed and easy to pick up and there are a couple of welcome additions that make it slightly less frustrating (e.g. the ability to double click on an Exit to go straight through it, rather than have to watch your character walk all the way over to it or holding down the space bar to see interactive objects, rather than having to pixel hunt)Since this is a review, I'd better try and find something negative to say, so here goes: if you don't like this style of game, then you might feel it still suffers from some of the restrictions of the genre (lots of talking to people to pick up clues, lots of examining things on screen). That said, it's definitely one of the more accessible examples, so if you're prepared to approach it with an open mind, you might still enjoy it.A complete play through took me around 8 hours and whilst (like many adventure games) I'm unlikely to ever play it again, I enjoyed every minute of it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic!  Not too difficult/relatively easy puzzles; gameplay is usual PnC fare - Loved this game!  Definitely a must have/play for adventure gamers.  I think older gamers, like myself, would find this game to be quite a treat.  The story is great, where you may think it's going is exactly that and done in the most superb way.  The game is approximately 10-20hrs in length.  Kudos Wadjet Eye, Kudos!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I did finished the game, but I really lost interest about halfway through.  The voice acting is great.  The art is surprisingly good and functional for being the 8-bit look.  I like puzzle games but this was a little too much "yak shaving" for me.  None of the puzzles are difficult and they do provide a handy log if you lose track of how far down the chain of nested tasks you are, but it caused me to lose interest.  Maybe my sense of just wanting some quest chains to be over made the dialog seem too slow.  It just felt like there were very long pauses for no reason sometimes.  The ending is also pretty well foreshadowed about halfway through, so that was the point where I kinda wanted it to be over with.  The fact that, from the very beginning, you are pretty much forced to exhaust all possible dialog and interaction options meant that there was only going to be one ending and the foreshadowing is not subtle.  Anyway, it's not terrible, I did finish it, but I doubt I'd go for a second one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a Wadjet game without Abe Goldfarb! The game is very well made, the creators sure have an eye for details. Beautiful pixel art graphics, captivating story, set in a mysterious English village. Can also wholeheartedly recommend the other games of this developer, but this one is their best. Looking forward to their future games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This was practically made for me. Fantastic art, casual puzzles, lovely voice acting, and a sense of deepening dread that builds slowly as you explore this isolated town and its creepy secrets. My favorite horror manages to touch on the spooky, dreary imagery that i loved as a child without making my ethics-conscious adult self cringe, and this game accomplished both as if by magic. (Or to be more blunt: whether you hate or love Victorian tomb exploration, you can enjoy this game.)

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good point and click adventure game. As to be expected by this publisher. _childDocuments_.review: Wow, what an unexpectedly engrossing experience! The Excavation of Hob's Barrow is a point-and-click adventure game that has elements reminiscent of The Wicker Man, The Rusty Lake games, and H.P. Lovecraft. If that description sounds like something that you would like then I feel pretty confident in recommending this game to you. If you don't like traditional point-and-click games, however, then I would be cautious: This game is definitely classic point-and-click adventure, and suffers from many of the classic problems (a bit more on this below). Alternatively, if you like classic adventure games for the puzzles but not the story then be advised that this is on the easy side. If the previous two sentences didn't scare you away then don't hesitate to give this game a try.What impressed me the most about The Excavation of Hob's Barrow was how skillfully it was at instilling a sense of dread. It is clearly an indie game made by a small team, and the narrative isn't perfect, but I felt like it had a vision of what it wanted to accomplish and really excelled at doing that. I was put into a very strong setting and got to experience a really compelling story in an interactive way.I felt like the first half of the game has the strongest game design. From a gameplay perspective it is pretty easy, but I felt like most of the actions I was doing generally made sense in the context of what my character would do and helped to advance the plot, which is what I was interested in. The second half of the game, however, starts to add many more of the classic point-and-click tropes, where I found myself wandering around to every location again and talking to every character again to see if there was anything new and trying to figure out how to satisfy some of the artificial-feeling obstacles. If you've played other point-and-click games this is nothing new (and still on the easy side), but I did feel a little disappointed because it took me out of the narrative experience and reminded me that I was playing a game.In terms of narrative design itself, however, I really feel like the game does a great job of advancing things through to the end. I don't feel like I can say much about it without spoiling anything, but there is one section in particular towards the end that just does such a fantastic job at building the feeling of dread through subtle things, and trusting the player to pick up on things. Again, for such a small team with limited resources I was really impressed with their choices of what to focus on.The Excavation of Hob's Barrow isn't perfect but it perfectly delivered the thing that I value most in games like this, which is to feel like I was transported somewhere and got to experience something compelling. Thank you, developers!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Watched Gab Smolders play this and bought it in hopes that the developers will fix the absolutely awful ending somewhere down the road, because then it would be worth playing. The music, voice acting, atmosphere and build up are all fantastic, but the ending is one of the most depressing and unsatisfying endings in gaming I've ever seen. The story does not really progress in any way during that time. You're constantly presented with choices throughout the game, but none of them end up mattering because there's only the one ending, which again, I cannot stress enough how crappy it is.If you're curious, this is how badly the game ends, no joke:

_childDocuments_.review: To be fair I really did like this game up until the last 10 minutes. This game has a terrible ending and it's something you should be aware of if you're actually spending money on it. The game plays great and the voice actors are like as good as they could be. I actually laughed at some of the dialog, but the writer and artist both gave up on landing this story as authentically as it started out. At the 50% mark you're given around 5 fetch quests or so to finish the game, these are quite simple and flesh out your understanding of the world. Immediately after that little tangent you can go ahead and forget everything about the story of this game and earn yourself a pitiful ending via a 30 minute final descent into the worst variant of an M Night Shyamalan plot twist. Choices do not matter to the story and nothing will affect this nonsensical ending. The dialog drags on in a few places. I'd say I clicked through 25% of the dialog boxes. Some lines are truly wonderful and nice though, again it's simply how terrible of an ending this game has it's not worth the slog. The game is fully voiced and the actors are great to be fair. In part the artist decided not to depict the finale for some reason, like what a difference that could have made possibly, but the writer went on to toss the story into a ditch and leave it, taking this game from being an easy 7 or 8 out of 10 down to like 3 out of 10 I gotta knock that whole score down a lot for such a terrible ending to an otherwise interesting story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: An atmospheric folk-horror point and click, with excellent voice acting and some good moments. For me it was good rather than great. The crystal-maze style puzzle solving of the final act undermined the horror elements, and I was rather frustrated by the lack of choice in how the story progressed, but it was good fun and reasonably memorable.
