Make sure you only get if on discount.Edit: I feel like I wasn't clear enough, During the game there is narration from the main Character, the games length along with the narration lead me to believe the game was building up to something bigger, I finally get in the barrow, okay now the game can really begin! couple of easy puzzles (given what I had to do to get here) go through, things are finally happening annnnnd game over, the end, screw you, your choices, and your attachments to characters, everyone was an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ working against you, your choices had no meaning other than to prevent you from getting all achievements in one run to artificially increase playtime to prevent refunds, if you know what you're doing you could easily beat the game in less than an hour and refund so achievements are the only thing they have to stop you doing that, honestly don't listen to my prior advice to buy it on sale, buy it from a key reseller for $1.50, really disappointing game and hard to believe it came from the same studio that gave us the amazing Blackwell series.

_childDocuments_.review: While I think that the point and click genre makes it difficult to sustain a mood of fear and tension, The Excavation of Hob's Barrow is definitely a well-written, well-made old-school P&C adventure with a great sense of atmosphere. The puzzles are fine, even if I didn't necessarily think they all worked altogether well in concert with the plot, the characters are well written, and the ending is effective. For someone who loves both P&C games and folk horror, this is pretty much a must-buy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I quiet enjoyed it.It's definitely not among the best point&clicks I played, but It's decent.I would say though that visuals were the thing that made me hesitate to buy this game (those eyes with out of prespective lashes were put everywhere on the marketing materials and I hope it wasn't rage bait), but I heard good reviews about the plot and decided to give it a chance. Story is interesting, narrative is well-done. Actually learned something new about the antagonist and the British folklore. It would be better to see a second ending and there was a way to do it, right at the end without making the player miss much of the content, but the way it went is also okay. Pretty Lovecraftian, even.Gameplay too easy for my taste, not once have I had to look into the guides, but everything is intuitive and works for the story.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying this is a very easy recommendation for fans of point & click dark / horror games.The voice acting is really great, perfect fit, it's the soul of the narrative (or maybe it's the narrative that's the soul of the voice).The pixel art is also very well acomplished, the foggy, gloomy, sometimes washed/pastel colour choices. Special praises to Thomasina's sprite and animations - extra movements/reaches are always lovely to see.The SFX and music are also a very good fit with the rest of the Art and environment. The pieces of the puzzle fall into place at with a very good timming, giving the game a wonderful pace. It only gets better the more you progress, which speaks to a very smart story architecture.Difficulty was also good. I had to go back and forth a few times but never felt stuck. I should probably have used the map more, but "travel by map" wasn't available at this time and I wanted to keep it historically accurate.There are some small polishing issues like: some hotspot text partially offscreen, some sounds are played too soon and give the impression of cutting the previous ones (would feel better with a little pause/fade), some minor animation glitching, Thomasina facing the wrong way on some movements/interactions, some letters in the fonts strangely big for lower case, some perspective issues here and there... Thankfully none of these issues damages the experience seriously.I would like to end by saying I'm not even the biggest fan of horror, and I still loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as I saw the trailer for this game I knew I would buy it. I haven't really played too many point & click games so far, but this one still sparked my interest.The art style looks really pretty and it certainly manages to convey the sort of creepy and mysterious atmosphere that stretches through the entire game.The gameplay was pretty good, it wasn't too easy but also not too hard. Just the perfect balance! There were some puzzles I had to think about for a while but it usually didn't take too long.The (in my opinion) most important aspects that made this game unique were the story and the incredible voice acting. At first I was a bit worried the game might not be able to bring the story to a satisfying end, but that worry was totally unjustified. There's a clear plot that slowly develops and all the mysteries are revealed at the end of the game. During my second playthrough (wanted to complete the remaining achievements) I noticed a few details that you only understand after finishing the game. I love the attention to detail here!The voice acting (and soundtrack) was one of the highlights for me. It made all of the characters really unique and conveys a lot of emotion while still managing to feel very natural.I can definitely recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The Excavation of Hob’s BarrowAs far as point and click adventures goes, this one was a breeze. Solutions seemingly falling in your lap, as the puzzles present themselves to you. Still I would recommend this one, because there is nothing like a good mystery.Everything is just right! A secluded village, steeped in folklore and superstition, bordering on the vast and unexplored moorlands. Looming in the background, a story, an analogy for the place we’re in. Throwing us between the clarity of reason and a stygian gloom, something is not quite right here. People seem friendly but also secretive. Maybe they’re just not used to outsiders.From the very beginning, the game will suck you in, making you as explorative as the protagonist you play. The story is fantastic and everything from the ominous ambience to the hand drawn animations will transport you and keep you there until the very last breath of this experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly well-done point'n'click adventure game. I especially enjoyed how (with a few exceptions) Thomasina always behaved like a lady and didn't suffer with typical adventure cleptomania. The story was good, although I would have behaved differently in her place. Atmosphere was top notch and I enjoyed the visuals which fit for me really well with the period and settings.Also a lot of detail went into individual scenes with subtle changes here and there when I was strolling through the scenes, bringing in welcome life and feeling of an actual place. While I wasn't too happy with some puzzles (especially myst-style puzzles) overall the game felt often logical and believable (given the theme and setting). I also wished some of the threads were better tied together - the game has that typical rollercoaster point of no return leaving some things unexplained. Another minor detail is that achievements were a bit gimmicky (basically shadowed the linear story progression) and I felt there were too many of them.Still, those are very minor gripes, comparing to the experience. I was able to get through the game in 5.7 hours but will play again to check if I missed anything.I am definitely looking forward to play more from Cloak and Dagger games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the better adventure game releases of the last few years. If you like Wadjet Eye games such as Unavowed and the Blackwell series, you will probably like this as well - it has a similar strong atmosphere and interesting story.I thought the setting was a standout and very evocative of a small village on the moors of England. I really liked the interactions with townspeople, and many of the settings were beautiful with the rain and fog. There were a few things that I thought were odd: there are many places in the game where you have to decide whether or not you want to confide in someone or otherwise make a choice in how you approach a situation. I haven't replayed the game, but from what I have read it seems as though there is little branching, and only one ending. I liked the ending, but I would have liked a little more weight to these choices - perhaps if I had chosen to keep one person's secret, that would have affected the story later, or perhaps if I had not been as receptive to another person's advances, that would have changed a scene later with them. It's possible that this is in the game to a degree, though.There is another character who does some unsavory things - making unwanted advances on the main character while being married, for example, and yet at the end the main character is calling him "noble." Why? I felt like my thoughts and the main character's had kind of diverged, which is also the issue I thought with the plot leading up to the climax - the character believed one thing, while I knew (as the player) that something different was going to happen. I thought this was all right, but I was hoping for a little more.The section leading up to the climax also had a lot of "puzzle rooms" to get through, which is common in this genre of games but I personally tend to dislike as I think it affects pacing. Some of the these puzzles I thought were also obscure, like a musical puzzle. I have played the violin so I think maybe that experience led me astray when solving it.Overall, though, this was a lovely game - beautiful, professionally made, interesting, with strong characterization and atmosphere and a nice sense of dread or foreboding. It was like playing through a story by Lovecraft or Colin Wilson. I thoroughly enjoyed my time with it, will probably play it again, and would recommend it to anyone who likes point and clicks or narrative-based games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Wooooo this one is a doozy.If you like visual novels or point'n'click adventures but you want a little bit less cartoony nature then look no further!I think what I want to gush the most about is the atmosphere and setting, it's just very rare to see in games. It's very rural Midlands England, complete with the full experience of most people not wanting to talk to you and telling you to *expletive* off mostly.The story progression is unlike most I've ever played and feels very natural but unnerving in delicious ways. The creepy horror elements are mostly subtle but definitely get under your skin. The music is perfect, the pixelly low-res style is pulled off wonderfully, a lot of subtle details are beautifully rendered while a lot of the cutscenes are ugly as sin but it gives the exact effect desired. The voice work is excellent all-round, the writing and characters are really charming for mostly uncharming people!There's a little more I wish was there but I'm more than satisfied with what I got, would recommend if anyone wants a short but tense creepy game to play!About 8 hours with no getting stuck and letting voice lines play out
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Hello.  I just finished the game after 11.1 hours.  It's been a good long time since I played through a point and click adventure and this is easily one of the finest I've ever played!  The story, writing, atmosphere and pacing are all excellent.  The artwork is not only charming but sets the scene in such a beautiful, yet unsettling way.  The story is so genuinely engaging and not at all what I expected,  I was unable to predict the events, so strong was the story.  Puzzles in this title are pitched to perfection.  There are no "moon logic" moments to frustrate and disengage the player.  All puzzles are well crafted, satisfying to complete and all honestly earned victories on our way to the conclusion.  I'd recommend this to anyone who enjoys a truly exceptional story, remarkable setting and expertly paced puzzle game play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far my most enjoyable adventure game I've played for ages - and usually I just replay Quest For Glory and Kings Quest so IMO the bar is pretty high.Hob's Barrow has a powerful HP Lovecraft Cosmic Horror vibe, and somehow creates a perfect mix of character, mood, puzzles, and intrigue to create a complete game. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Not finished the game yet, but am currently enjoying it.  It takes a little to get used to the retro display style, as I'd preferred a little more detail of the characters.  And notice that there's a map button which lists your locations that you're aware of.  I hadn't noticed this and have been working off a hand drawn map to get to locations.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Without giving anything away this a truly delightful adventure that is perfect for this time of year.  The story-line keeps you coming back for more and the graphics throughout are beautiful.  I'm sure it can be completed quicker than the 7 hours it took me but I just wanted to dive into every corner to discover more.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game for some time and sometimes it just feels as if a game was made for you. This is one of those games. It has everything that I adore about British folk horror. Slowburn suspense in a village full of strange inhabitants, intrigue, mystery, omens and an ending that left me speechless. Thomasina is a wonderful protagonist, carried masterfully by her voice actress Samantha Béart, surrounded by a fascinating cast of equally well-voiced characters.I finished the game in one sitting because I just couldn't stop. The puzzles, both dialogue and item based, are always fair and the story moves at a great pace building up to an explosive finale that doesn't disappoint and also features some of the toughest puzzles in the game. If you're a fan of classic folk horror movies like the (original) Wicker Man I can't recommend this game highly enough. It's a damn near perfect point'n'click adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, haunting, stomache-churning blend of folk horror & cosmic horror, part 1973's "The Wicker Man" and part "The Shadow Over Innsmouth." As you advance you realize just before the protagonist what is unfolding yet you find yourself powerless to stop and incapable of turning away. That said, I got my PhD in exactly the sort of ancient Mediterranean magic that this is supposed to involve and, while they get the trappings mostly right, they make some ridiculous blunders that took me out of it -- e.g.: Abraxas/Abrasax was not pre-Roman, but rather a direct product of the later Roman Empire; the game uses the Greek "sigma" for "epsilon"; the pre-Roman temple uses late-Roman Latin along with Attic Greek; etc. Etc. I know those are the sorts of things that probably only bother someone like me, and I love everything else about it, but it did take me out of the game several times. Still, 8/10. Would excavate again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: While the game overall is really excellent and compelling, the final act leaves a lot to be desired. Kind of tedious final puzzles, and I didn't much care for the ending.Without spoilers, the main character becomes an idiot in the last act of the game, deciding to ignore any and all possible warnings - including a very, very direct warning that indicates that she's being manipulated - and goes ahead with the dumbest possible decisions she could make. This, after the game was built on choices you made all throughout, no choice is offered in the final act. Apparently, there was an alternative ending planned, but it would have been against the "point" of the game, whatever that happens to be.The ending ruins an otherwise great game. Real ball drop.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game.  Most puzzles were logically connected and having the ability to see any interaction points on screen prevents the annoying "pixel hunting" that can often be a problem with this genre.  Reading comments in the discussions and other reviews, the ending may not be to everyone's taste, but I found it consistent with the narrative and a satisfying conclusion.  It's a fun ride. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: This was excellent. The voice acting was amazing, artwork is right up my alley. The moors brought to mind Wuthering Heights, one of my fave books. The story was well written and gripping. Puzzles were not overly challenging, but I enjoyed applying my knowledge of Shakespeare & Latin! Would recommend! Not too spooky, but certainly has some unsettling moments.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Folk horror is underutilised in video games, so Hob's Barrow was a a wonderful change of pace. Brilliantly voice acting, and excellent animation all lend to the game being immersive. There is a fair bit of moon logic though. Some of the puzzles towards the end just become ridiculous. Use a guide, and you'll still have fun while not wanting to tear your hair out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting a dark turn, and they delivered more than I expected. The story was captivating and they did such a good job building the tension up until the climax. It kept me on the edge of my seat. I love a good point and click with voice acting (saves me from a sore throat haha). The VAs did an amazing job. The pixel art was so detailed, it made for beautiful backgrounds and close ups. The music was very eerie and fit well with the setting. I will say this tho, there was something about the sound mixing that was kinda distracting. The music would stop each time a character would say something then pick back up when they stop. I would have prefered if the music kept going the whole time or it stops when we say hi and picks back up when we say bye. Sidenote: This doesn't affect my rating of the game, but why did they have to make Thomasina so annoying? Where's the option to not have her say Hogwash each time another character explains a superstition or belief system she doesn't believe in? Why you gotta disrespectful like this? You can't just go to a random town that doesn't like strangers and mock their superstitions like that, Thomasina. Like we get it, you're r/atheist.Overall, I really enjoyed the game and any fan of point and click needs to play this ASAP.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent adventure game with a very surprising ending. This game clearly has taken some notes from H.G. Lovecraft and have implemented them into the game well. The writing is superb, the artwork is beautiful, the voice acting is top notch and the game isn't overly taxing.I did have a few ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with some rather bizarre triggers for progressing through some tasks but they didn't detract from the game too much, they were a little frustrating to work through and wasted some unnecessary time.If it wasn't for these I'd give this game a perfect score but it doesn't deserve any lower than 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A creepy little game with a gloomy vibe of doom. The puzzles/obstacles are intuitive, though require a little more deduction towards the end. Less about the all-out horror and more about the creeping dread of being somewhere you really shouldn't be, going into places you really shouldn't go, and doing things you really shouldn't do. Classic!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed this. Thoroughly enjoyable game from start to finish. The dialog and music is all beautifully done. Begins innocently enough as a girl following in her fathers footsteps on an archaeological dig and slowly turns into something a lot more sinister.Well worth a play through.My Light is his Light!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and the way it took me 20+ years back into the past. The logic of the puzzles is actually logical and I only had to look up one solution to a problem. The story progression from light almost whimsical village adventure to a darker turn is also really fun, with a good slow build-up of tension. On the top of this, Thomasina is a likeable character, who behaves in a believable way - for example, I found it really nice touch you have to introduce yourself to an NPC first, before pestering them with your questions. And even then the (brilliantly voiced) reply is sometime 'mind your own business!'.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Hob's Barrow has a compelling start and manages to keep up the tension for a while, but falls flat as the game goes on.Most of the game justs consists of convoluted fetch quests, which don't really advance the story. The worst part however is the resolution in the end, where the main character just flat out acts completely unreasonable.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I very rarely play P&C adventure games, despite genuinely loving the highs of the genre, because they tend to be riddled with nonsensicle dead ends and unfair logic. This is far from the case with Hob's Barrow. Every single moment of this game is packed with love and care for the genre. The art is incredible, the sound design is jam packed with soft touches that underscore and outline a quaint english village in the moors. The tension slowly bastes and builds as the mystery of the plot unwinds itself before you. The writing, the dialogue, the voice acting are all completely perfect at making a wholly terrifying and compelling experience from start to finish.the only issue i had was with a minor bug that seemed to just fast skip through all the text in a conversation, but it only cropped up twice and i was able to go back and relisten to those conversations quite easily. If you have any love for point and clicks, any love for gothic horror, or even any love for the old school sierra art style made fresh and new, this game is an absolute must buy. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A very qualified recommendation. The plot is pretty straightforward and while the elements of the presentation are strong they don't come together well enough especially after the middle of the game. Many scenes felt unnecessary (for instance the many flashbacks). If you like adventure games and horror you will have a decent time. But, I do think movies have presented similar stories in a much better fashion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A very entertaining point & click adventure.   The story is effective at building up suspence, with effective use of pixel art.  There is full voice acting throughout.The puzzles are intuitive and straightforward, and rely more on common sense than moon logic.  I've only had to look up a solution once, and then I felt bad about it, since the solution was easily found within the game.  If you enjoyed other adventure games published by Wadjet Eyes, this is absolutely worth getting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember pushing a 5.25" floppy disk into an Apple IIc, hitting "Enter" and waiting for the next scene to appear? I do. Once you'd seen all of the fixed backgrounds, it could get tedious. However, if you persisted despite the mild tedium and tried everything you could change something, something new would happen: a door could open, a character might say something they hadn't before, or the next time your character crossed that wall on the edge of the screen, a scene you had looked at a hundred times before would have *something* changed about it . That's why I played this game, thirty years later: that feeling when something shifts, and something different is revealed.Oh, and the snippets of awesome Badalamenti-esque soundtrack in the trailer!You, too can have that fantastic feeling; whether you remember (and long for) the early days of adventure games on stacks of disks (packaged in hardcover book-sized cardboard slipcases, with ornate manuals) or not. In fact, much of the mechanical toil has been eliminated, freeing your mind to focus on solving in-game puzzles and wonder about the world you're suddenly immersed in. Go ahead, sink your fingers into the soil, what's the harm if a little bit of this place ...er, game, gets under your nails? ;-)
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Hob's Barrow is an adventure where it starts very promising and ends rather uneven with a taste of being short and empty. It could have been clearly better. It does what is says though.The pluses:-The story is very nice, and it scales well,-It's a classic adventure of the 90's, with Easter Eggs from Monkey Island series & Indiana Jones 4,-Easy UI, although it is better for the left mouse button to LOOK, and for the right button to ACT, not the other way around,-Some riddles are really good, the others are ok,-Voice acting is very nice indeed!-Some characters are vivid.The minuses-Graphics! The analysis was too small for my 2K monitor, I even switched to windowed mode but still it was horrible! Luckily, I found the WINSETUP file in the game folder (you can change many parameters from there) where I put the windowed scale to 4X (1280X720), and the analysis was more pleasant to my eyes. I am not expecting 1080p analysis but why did the game was designed in 320X180 pixels? That's way too few. Better would have been 640X400 or 640X480 or sth similar.-The game is rather short. They could easily have added another day, some extra puzzles, thus enhancing the story even more with the same number of locations.-A thing that annoyed me a lot. When you go to a rural area, it is obvious at the beginning that the locals  will not tell you much. But after a few days, you will get to know them, you will expect to get invited to some cottages for tea, for gossip, thus further developing the story. Nothing of this short! In fact the only buildings with interior locations are the Church and the Inn! (Okay, and the Barrow). That's why it feels somehow empty. Open 3-4 cottages, open the manor with 2-3 locations, add another day, and the game becomes way better. Food for thought for your next adventure Cloak & Dagger.Last 2 hints:-When I went to the farmer's house for the first time and I knocked no one answered! I went around the village doing nothing, went to the farmer's house again, and this time the farmer answered. Bug perhaps?- On the third day in the Inn there are 2 extra things. Press SPACE to surely spot them. I didn't and I missed them...Final grade 3/5. Would have been 5/5 if the analysis were doubled and open 4-5 location inside the cottages for more richness of the story. Old schoolers like me definately like it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Woah nelly is this a treat. If you like point and click adventures, and you're up for something unsettling, I cannot recommend this game enough. It feels more like the Christopher Lee Wickerman - where the people are just off but not sinister.  The majority of the game is actually quite pleasant - I really loved the environments and the ambient music - and the puzzles are quite fun.  I only got stuck twice - and one involved not clicking a dialogue option.This is a delight, especially for the spooky season for people who do not like horror or high stress situations. _childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I've played many point and click games over the year, and honestly loved this. The story line is gripping, the voice acting is brilliant and the art work is beautiful. The story telling is very good, and is obviously building up to quite a shocking, but not unexpected end. The puzzles are good, but not too challenging, as it feels like the story is more important.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The pixel art, eerie music, excellent voice acting, and slowly unfolding mystery makes this a wonderfully creepy and atmospheric game.  Is is scary?  Not really, more of an unsettling vibe although the story itself has disturbing content.  It's slow, but I liked that about it.  It introduced you to all the characters in town and got you attached to them.  The ending is good, despite being a bit rushed.  The second half of the game, once you are in the barrow itself, is the best part in my opinion.  The puzzles were fun, the atmosphere was eerie, and the music was amazing.  I would recommend if you like puzzles, pixel art, and creepy vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of work must have gone into this game. The graphic art and especially the voice acting are very good. But ultimately, without a good story and good game play, these were not enough to make it worth my time. The puzzles throughout the game were bland and the majority of them were of the go-fetch-something variety -- and often cascading in a predictable way. _childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Eeeeeeeeh... I think the game is overall good and all, but I honestly wouldn't recommend it to most people just because of ending. One of times I'd prefer it if there was option between "yes" and "no". I ended up on "yes" since I think some people might prefer ending this way, but I personally wouldn't recommend game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a couple of point and click adventures by Cloak and Daggers games so had a vague idea of what to expect mechanics-wise. What I didn't expect was to be completely absorbed in this League of Gentlemen-style village with its strangely endearing mix of characters. Arriving in the village on a rainy day sets the tone for the rest of the game. I completed the entire game in one sitting, and was left completely bewildered by the end. The puzzles are intriguing, and for the most part relatively easy but always fun to work out. The dialogue is excellent - laugh-out-loud funny and incredibly descriptive and immersive. The whole game is like a long audiobook with extra steps that you just can't switch off. Big kudos to the creators, what a gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The kind of horror that I like.Instead of relying on lots of gore and jumpscares, it carefully builds a deeply unsettling athmosphere from the start.Loved the story, the puzzles were the exact right difficulty (for my taste, at least) and the soundtrack and voice acting are the cherry on top. Just great work by everyone involved.One of my favorite point and click games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Hob's Barrow has a killer atmosphere. That's definitely the strong point of this game. Old England, Rain, weird locals, folklore, the creeping discomfort growing into fear... All of this is working. Yet, it fails as a game : point and click mechanics are weak, puzzles do not exist, the pacing is horrendous. I wish Hob's barrow offered a more captivating tale than this drag of a scenario. 90% of the game feels like an introduction to the locals, 10% like the actual beginning of the game... and then it's over. I felt disappointed : the game is not bad, it's just not really worth your time unless you're really into that groove.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow's is a story-driven adventure game filled with mystery and dread. The game takes place in the small rural town of Bewlay (England), and follows the story of Thomasina in her quest to excavate Hob's Barrow and uncover its secrets. Not only is the game's presentation a sight to behold (especially for those who enjoy pixel art), but the narrative will keep you engaged from start to finish.  The puzzles are abundant (as you'd expect from a game of this nature) and seemingly challenging without ever being frustrating. Also, a note of appreciation to the voice actors for their work in elevating the narrative to even higher heights.As for the cons, well, the fact there's no way to significantly alter the events of story kind of renders the choices we make throughout the game obsolete.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. There's a little bit of poopoo moon logic here and there in the first two chapters, but it's really not that bad. You can always use a guide if you just want to experience the story. The writing is great, and the voice acting is also exceptional for a small game like this. Music is a little weird, but not bad. There is even a weird bondage scene with a milkman if you are into that sort of thing. Definitely check it out if you're an aging loser like me (though I have a massive p****).
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Give this game a play 100%. It's a much longer, slower burn, akin to something like The Last Door. But it doesn't overstay its welcome as a point and click adventure game with obtuse puzzle logic the way something like Rusty Lake games might. It does a good job of enchanting you and making you like the characters, the back and forth through various areas with the beautiful pixel art gives way to admirable details in the environment while still having that ethereal quality about the town. Is it all just small town superstitions? Is it fake? It almost brings forward an element something like...The Wicker Man (1960's variation) of a happy small town in the UK that's very isolationist and a bit odd for some reason. Generally people seem happy, but something's off. The horror is well understated and the writing of the characters is pleasant. While there will always be SOME backpeddling in point and click games this one makes the most of its environment and unsettling aura with very little. Additional props for not killing the cat.

Following in your fathers footsteps as an archeologist, you arrive in a small remote town to excavate Hobs Barrow.Great voiceacting and story. For the pixel puritans, this is one of those rare gems that respect the pixel ratio.If you are into the point and click adventure genre, give this one a go.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

Played 2 hours on my first go, and I am really enjoying it.If you love point and click mysteries, this one really satisfies.  It's my favorite game from both developers.  Recommended.

The more you progress into the story, the better it just keeps getting. Voice acting is amazing! Contender for GOTY for sure. *You know I'm gonna say it, it's game of the year for me. My wife and I have played several Wadjet Eye games, and they all seem to be good if you like adventure games. _childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this a lot. A really great weird fiction/cosmic horror story, with that perfect sense of inexorable creeping dread, told through a very classic point and click adventure. Lovely visuals and voice acting. Puzzles are a good level of difficulty that requires real thought without being unreasonable (there was only one puzzle that crossed over into being a bit infuriating, and it's a rare adventure game that has none at all).  If you like cosmic horror and/or point and click adventures you should definitely play it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The cognitive dissonance in the original Space Quest games between the box cover art telling you that "Roger Wilco is hapless!" and the player's necessary mental exertion involved to solve the puzzles, is laid bare the moment you can type in the name you will be called by in the game.It's one of the hardest lines to walk when narrative is the main driver of an interactive work:  balancing the player's actions with the personality of the character they are directing in a world that is clearly alive, regardless of the players's presence.The Excavation of Hob's Barrow's succeeds in this fully with the denizens and everyday life of the town of Bewlay.From the moment Thomasina Bateman starts recounting the events that led to her writing a letter to her mother, any ambiguity is dispelled: the player is helping Thomasina relive her time in starkly bucolic Bewlay. But as players spend more time within the memories and stories Thomasina shares, the more off putting the narration becomes. It's not just that Thomasina is an unreliable narrator—the implications of the traumatic events that occured at Hob's Barrow are still a puzzle to be worked out. This is the strength of the narrative design and writing in Hob's Barrow: as entertainingly crafted as linear story or film, but with eartnest player engagement required to work out what's happening in the very deep shadows of this cursed place.The fantastic writing is supported by equally fantastic pixel art, music, and some of the best voice work I've heard in games…ever? The codgers, critters, and countryside all sound fantastic, the bleakness of the moors churning from peaceful to menacing with expert orchestration. Visual direction is solid, too, with sparingly, effectively used pixel portraits and closeups to highlight details both grotesque and filled with character. The dark undercurrent of humour throughout the game also adds some replayability for achievement hunters: some encounters are worth revisiting!I played this entirely on Steam Deck, mostly curled up in bed at night, but enjoyed the grand finale while docked on my TV. Performance and control was flawless, regardless.One of my favorite games released in 2022, and definitely one of my favorite adventure games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing through The Excavation of Hob's Barrow. I love the art style and found the voice acting excellent as well. Most of the puzzles felt logical and well-balanced. There were only two or three situations where I felt "stuck" and had to either wander around for a few minutes or put the game down and come back with fresh eyes to find the solution.I liked several of the interface choices as well, specifically the map feature that made it a lot easier to get from one location to another and cut down on unnecessary walking around, and the to-do list that did a good job of keeping me focused on what I needed to do to progress.I found the plot interesting, and it was revealed at a nice pace over several chapters. While none of the twists were completely unexpected, the pacing and characterization was well done and spread out over a few solid hours of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: It was a cool little game and a great achievement for the team so I don't want to give it a negative review. I did however find the story quite frustrating, (pretty severe spoilers, please go into the game blind if you're interested in it for the full experience)  Overall a really nice setting, great voice acting, some really cool imagery. If this is your first point and click adventure game its a pretty great introduction to the genre but ultimately might be a little too frustrating for people looking for something a bit meatier.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Another great title from Cloak & Dagger/Wadjet Eye. If you've played any of their other games you'll know what to expect with Hobs Barrow. The story and voice acting were excellent. The continuously creepy atmosphere and feeling of impending doom throughout the game was very well written.My only issue were the puzzles go from a decent level of challenge through the game, into a super hard continuous string of puzzles during the last moments of the game, for which I had to keep checking a walkthrough for hints. Not a big deal but quite a jarring change of pace compared to the rest of the game
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the voice acting and how it all unfolded.Somehow i am still very unsatisfied with a) the playtime and b) the last quarter of the game.When you finally come to excavate Hob's Barrow, it felt kinda "rushed" to me.Also the "outcome" felt kinda strange to me. I was like "seriously? This is how you explain stuff now? This is how the folks really were all the time?? Common..."Like "we need drama but we haven't found a way to let this thing end in a really great way".I was entertained for around 7 hours but this game will not stay in my mind like for instance the glorious "Memoria".Really wanted to like it more but in the end it was a quiet cheap story, i am really sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun playing this point and click horror game, and rather sad it's already over. Just as I was starting to get know the folks in Bewley it was already time to go. I'm not sure if any of your choices really matter in the game as there's only one ending, but I wonder if I might have missed some important details. I find that there's a number of significant questions left unanswered. Nevertheless this game really charmed me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The story has a very intriguing beginning, especially because I happen to read the Ruth Galloway novels featuring a female archeologist at the time. It kept my interest as long as the excavation actually began and Thomasina enters the barrow. Until then, there are a few events that could have been dreams or visions or something unexplicable through science, but then it becomes clear that  with some rooms and puzzles thrown in that didn't make much sense. Who would build those and why? I wish the story would have stayed more realistic until the end.Other than that, the voice acting and the general mood of the game are fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is a weird game. The first and second acts follow typical point-and-click tropes. It's pretty straightforward, and a lot of fun. The third act goes off the rails. It's hard to follow and really weird. It probably needed more time (writing and playing) to make sense, which it never did. However, it was weird enough to make me look up the mythology related to the story, and it's crazy!The third act doesn't work, but it does make you curious. Don't plan on a satisfying ending, but do look into the mythology.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Had promise, but:- frequently got stuck: plenty of aimless wandering + backtracking despite having the required items- little player agency: there's obviously some questions/dialogue that's unproductive to ask certain villagers, but it's annoying that it's more efficient to ask them regardless, so you can more easily narrow down what you're missing. Didn't seem to be any negative consequence for tipping your hand too far.- plot "twists" you couldn't miss a mile away, whilst the overall story was relatively short, lacking any semblance of depth- (missable) achieves requiring minimum 2 playthroughs, despite linear storyline- text / audio glitches where it'd speed up the text & disappear all audio until it came to a choice fork- absolute dog endingIf you're going to give the player so many quirky achievements why not just tie a couple to alternate endings, so that the multiple "required" playthroughs actually fulfill a purpose besides making achievement # go up. Really annoyed you can't just leave town. It was completely obvious how this was going to end up by the end of the first day, and I'm pissed that it just bludgeons you over the head with it rather than having any sort of nuanced development. Experienced archaelogist and she just goes full rarted so many times. Even the epilogue sequence makes little sense and is propped up by plot armor. The voice acting was good. I liked the flashback sequences, and how they were included, and the puzzles in the final chapter were fun. The village felt well enough "alive" with the various characters and subquests. But the half-assed plot and other issues detracted from this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Take on the role of Thomasina Bateman, a renowned archaeologist who is writing a book on burial sites and has received a mysterious invite to a remote village to dig up a local landmark known as "Hob's Barrow". Upon arrival, she gets stood up and has to investigate the area on her own. During her investigation, she has to contend with the unhelpful locals, the loss of her assistant, and a series of horrific dreams as she seeks to excavate the Barrow and uncover the mystery behind it all. Cloak and Dagger have gone for pixel art with  and, for the most part, it works. The pixel art is good, I've seen better, but I've also seen a whole lot worse. The village of Bewlay is small but realistically laid out and is populated with a good assortment of landmarks and interesting areas. The bleak moors landscapes are well done and help create a huge sense of isolation. The character models are simple but detailed enough that each one has subtle distinct features to help add some life to each person. The animations in the cutscenes are a bit wonky and can lead to the feeling of the scenes being odd, which can undermine the horror element a small bit. When it comes to the sound design, I have to give full points to the voice acting, it's superb. All the accents are all spot on, and even the child voices are great. You believe these are real, living people, and it gives the story and atmosphere so much more traction in your mind. There's genuinely not a single weak link in the entire cast, and that's a huge achievement, especially when you see other games, often with budgets ten times larger, completely screw up their voice acting. But good voice acting is wasted if you don't have a good script and  has an excellent one. The dialogue is all believable and conveys a huge amount of information in quite a short space of time. It's tempting with games set in this time period to end up with all the characters speaking like they're over-acting in a Shakespeare play, and I'm delighted to see they've managed to avoid that here.  All the music is subdued and adds perfectly to the brooding atmosphere. It doesn't intrude on the dialogue or the action that's happening on screen. It knows its place and gives a real emphasis to the emotions in each scene.  The storyline is superbly written dark gnostic folklore. It's a subject we don't see a lot of despite it being a genre absolutely stuffed to the gills with deep, rich lore and story potential. The mystery behind  is an ancient one and brings in aspects of witchcraft, fairy tales and the sort of local mythology that tends to prevail in remote areas like Bewlay. The plot unfolds as you explore the village, talk to the locals, and the secrets of the Barrow are slowly revealed. The pacing is very well done, and you're kept engaged as each new scene adds more to the puzzle with each answer adding two more questions. My one gripe about the story (and I'm only mentioning this because I'm struggling to find anything wrong with this game) is that, when the reveal is made, there's no option to try to change things despite Thomasina knowing full well what's about to happen. It's a pure point-and-click. You can only talk to, pick up or use objects. There's a wealth of design choices to make the players' life easier and to help getting through the game as seamless as possible. There's the option to spring across the screen by double-clicking the scene exits. There's also a map which acts as a fast travel and cuts down on the amount of back-tracking you'll have to sit through. These decisions are excellent and show that the devs had the players first and foremost in their minds when putting this game together. As a whole, it's a linear experience with no alternate endings or choices to make. Your dialogue options only change how the villagers react to you from time to time. In conclusion,  is an exciting, engaging folk horror story that I'll be recommending to virtually everyone. It's a story based in an area and time period that we don't see much of, and it's a real treat to experience. At a little over six hours, there's a good amount of story here for you to get into, and it'll keep you hooked from start to finish. The game looks and sounds great, and the flawless voice acting goes hand in hand with the gameplay in what is surely one of the better games to be released this year. It's certainly one of the best indie games I've played in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not one for point and click games usually, but I thoroughly enjoyed the Excavation of Hobb's Barrow. Took me 8 hours to beat, and the puzzles were satisfying but not overly frustrating. That's not to say that I didn't spend certain parts of the game wandering around in search of something having changed, or that some clues were a little too easy to overlook or even hard to spot in the first place. But generally, I was able to find my way after 20 mins or so, and again, that's coming from someone who doesn't usually play these types of games.Hands down, the game shines in its story. An excellent folk horror, lovingly crafted and fully voice acted. I was pleasantly surprised at how good the direction on the voice acting was, and the detailed cutscenes were wonderfully off-putting. This story could easily be just as engaging as a film or miniseries. I definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game and it felt too brief, I wanted it to go on for another 10 hours! I would have liked it to expand to a different location or elaborate on some briefly touched upon characters. The horror story was great and just mysterious enough. The puzzles were just the right amount of challenging, and I never got stuck. There are many achievements to get as well which is always fun, although most are achievable as you progress through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. It sets a creepy vibe early, carrying that feeling through to the crescendo at the end. You are pulled along the linear story with a sense of inevitable ruin from the start, which to me makes the narrative all the more compelling. I love the pixel art style, and the voice acting is top-notch. Choices made in game are tied to game achievements, rather than outcomes, as there is only one ending. But the conclusion of the story, in my opinion, was excellent. It has stayed with me even after I finished the game, lurking in my brain. I suck at puzzles and am fairly impatient, so there were a few times that I was at a loss as to what do next and had to look it up.If you like spooky games and point and click play style, you should definitely buy this. It is the perfect thing to get in the spirit for Halloween.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: It's my first time playing a game from the devs Cloak and Dagger Games, but I've had good hopes since I noticed the game was being published by Wadjet Eye, who had published Technobabylon - one of my all-time favorites - some time ago.My suspicion was correct.Without spoiling anything, as going in blind is REALLY the best way to go about it - The Excavation of Hob's Barrow is an excellent title that reinvigorates not only the adventure game genre, but the horror genre as well.I was hooked in from the start and just kept going.If you're not experienced with adventure games you might get stuck in a couple of spots wondering what you're supposed to be doing. My best hint for you is: If you can't do it politely, consider breaking the rules instead.Well worth the price. I hope Cloak and Dagger will make more games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

The fact that there is only one ending given the absolutely incredible short sightedness of the main character makes it only worse. _childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Horror is not my genre and I was hesitant to dip into a game described as dark, gloomy, and gritty, but I'm really glad to have taken that dive - I was NOT expecting to get so emotionally invested. I was brought to tears on more than one occasion, and literally spent the last five minutes of game play with my mouth agape in shock. Great storytelling, excellent art and sound design that create such a perfectly eerie atmosphere (from cosy to horrific), and all the voice acting is superb! Thomasina Bateman has my heart forever, and I'll be muttering in Northerner for weeks thanks t'all the NPCs. The game play itself is very good - it maintains the classic point&click look and feel, but smooths over the clunkiness of old adventure games; I never felt annoyingly stuck, having to hunt for pixels, wander aimlessly around the game world, or guess an impossible solution to a puzzle. Speaking of the puzzles - they were never too tricky, and that was good: I got just enough of a challenge to satisfy the need and continue to push the story forward, which was the most important thing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I was debating on whether to give the game a positive or negative review for a while, as I had some mixed feelings; however, I gave it a positive review because my gripes were more of my own preferences not being met rather than the fault of the game. I should mention that am not a frequent Point & Click player, but the premise caught my eye and I decided to buy it.To start with the good, the quality of the game is top-notch. The art is detailed and pretty, the voice-acting is genuinely very good, and the mystery of the game kept me intrigued until the very end. The characters were very charming as well and I found myself exhausting everyone's dialogue just to hear what they had to say.  The puzzles required logical deductive reasoning, making them not too difficult but never too easy That being said, I had bought the game with the hopes more emphasis would be placed on the "horror," as that is one of its highest tags. Looking at the game, I was hoping for a point & click horror with an English folklore theme. I did not want to be jump-scared, far from it, but I wanted to feel tense and creeped out. Unfortunately, most of the game's runtime centers more finding and answering questions/mysteries. Only about the last hour or so of my 6-7 hour play-through was the "horror" part of the game, and while it was certainly more tense than the rest of the game, I still found it a little lacking. Additionally, I was hoping for more folklore inspiration, although I admit that was more of just my hope rather than the expectation set by the game.Overall, if you are fan of Point & Click Adventure games, then you should definitely give this game a try. If you are looking for a mystery horror game, then I'd suggest waiting for a sale and playing for an hour or so to see if the game is for you. If you are looking for a horror experience heavily inspired by English folklore, unfortunately, I don't think this game is what you are going to be looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: A charming game with interesting characters and an evocative atmosphere that works very well. The audio section, both the music and the sound, barely meet expectations. As for the puzzles, it's unlikely to pose a challenge to anyone; you can solve everything through simple trial and error, and you don't even need much of that because the inventory is very small.That being said, if you're in the mood for a peaceful adventure lasting about 5 or 6 hours with intriguing characters, a good atmosphere, and a touch of classic horror with references to The Wicker Man, then don't hesitate. I had a very enjoyable time playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing short game set in the gloomy and mysterious moors of England. It's a great combination of a classic point-and-click game with an exceptionally rich narrative. The graphics are a bit crude, but they fit well with the dark, horror-like story. Its puzzles are on the easier side but still somewhat challenging, and they are perfectly balanced. A strong recommendation for people looking for a great narrative experience and cozy storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and it was an immersive experience. The rich 19th-century English setting really intrigued me. I particularly liked the game's well-written narrative and professional voice acting; it felt more like living an interactive novel than playing a conventional adventure game. Puzzles weren't particularly noteworthy, but they didn't detract from my overall enjoyment. The game stands out mainly for its narrative quality.Highly recommended for lovers of story-heavy games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the excavation of Hob's Barrow, the story isn't innovative but cleverly told.The main characters are believable and have  good background histories unfolding during the game.I especially liked the voice acting, not one didn't fit and even the local dialect worked very well within the story.The riddles are on the easy/medium side. Except near the ending of the game I had no problems solving them, sometimes it needed just some time to find out where to go next.There are also some clever modern features like the map to get fast to the next place you need to be as well as a to do list and the possibility to teleport to the next screen instead of just walking all the way.If you like old school point and click games with modern features and a clevery told story this one's for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: as much as i wanted to like it, it left me feeling unfulfilled and disappointed. so many things left up in the air, lots of areas that should've been explored or expanded, most characters needed more depth. and the ending makes the whole story feel like a waste of time.unless you just REALLY love mediocre pixel art, i'd avoid this game
_childDocuments_.name: The Excavation of Hob's Barrow

_childDocuments_.review: The best point-and-click I've played for a long time. In terms of gameplay I found it much more respectful of my time than the adventure games I played in my youth - I rarely found myself getting stuck and resorting to talking to everyone and trying every item on every person/thing etc, but at the same time it wasn't excessively easy either. The story has a lovecraftian tint which I really enjoyed, the voice acting was superb, art & music I also loved.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite game from this dev because it has everything I love 💗 Old time periodFemale protagonist Kinda spooky scary 👻 Simple gameplaySoothing soundtrack that make me feel like I’m outside without being outside that’s the bestOh and fully voiced too!
