name: A Plague Tale: Requiem
detailed_description: Embark on a heartrending journey into a brutal, breathtaking world twisted by supernatural forces. After escaping their devastated homeland, Amicia and Hugo travel far south, to new regions and vibrant cities. There, they attempt to start a new life and control Hugo’s curse. But, when Hugo’s powers reawaken, death and destruction return in a flood of devouring rats. Forced to flee once more, the siblings place their hopes in a prophesized island that may hold the key to saving Hugo. Discover the cost of saving those you love in a desperate struggle for survival. Strike from the shadows or unleash hell, overcoming foes and challenges with a variety of weapons, tools and unearthly powers. ● Sequel to the award-winning adventure A Plague Tale: Innocence ● A spectacular grounded tale twisted by supernatural forces ● Use a variety of tools, sneak, fight, or unleash hell and rats ● Stunning visuals combine with an enthralling score

_childDocuments_.review: So I initially wrote a lengthy review discussing performance and all, but I'll try to give the most important parts about the actual game and let you decide if the performance is good or bad:If you adored the first game as much as I did, give this one a try. For me, it's a mix of 100 thumbs up and 99 thumbs down. Lucas and pretty much all of the new characters are fantastic, but ironically, the 2 main characters can be annoying at times. Amicia and Hugo's bond feels off – maybe they should've been partners, not siblings?In short: the story is alright, and it emphasizes world-building more than its predecessor. That's cool, but it becomes repetitive and silly later on. Side characters? Super likable. Combat? Solid, but occasionally glitchy. Level design? Hit or miss, with form often prioritized over function.If I had to give a score: 7/10. I don't regret playing, but better level design, story, and main character appeal would've been nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Runs like ass!I have a 7900XTX and no FSR in the game at all!AMD users have a hard time without any form of upscaling with RTI should be able to max this game but it's so badly optimised and their in game resolution scaler makes the game look worse.UpdatedSo it seems RT Shadows on this game are just broken no matter what GPU you have lolThe issue I was having is when enabled RT shadows i'd get a constant stutter even with fine FPS.Turn that off and the performance is fine, still I don't see why I should have to mod FSR into the game myself when the Devs should include it.If they are going to include RT make sure it actually works well properly then yeah ?If it's running badly on Nvidia GPUs, even the 4090 with RT shadows turned on then it's pretty obvious that high end GPUs like my 7900XTX ain't the issueThe game itself is decent so far, I really enjoyed the performance of the first one and the game itself.This one is just a bit of a headache when i've had to fiddle about to find the best settings, nothing to do with my hardware it's actually the Devs giving us such a bad choice if you're using AMD, terrible AA in the game without DLSS and even FSRNow Metro Exodus I actually had to add FSR into the game since it wasn't present but at least that game ran absolutely fine once I enabled RT Ultra and then the game looked great anyway at native. So that's why I didn't leave anything negative on that gameOnce I add FSR in it does look great but performance with RT is the main negative with green artifacts on quality mode on their in game TAA

_childDocuments_.review: It is a great game. It is heavily story driven, so if youre not planning to get immersed into your next game, it is not for you. It is also a very stealth heavy game with little direct combat, so this might be another minus, depending on what youre looking for. I got immersed in the story, had a lot of fun trying different approaches and finding different paths through the sections, getting creative with the combination of combat utilities and styles and just thoroughly enjoyed the amazing voice acting and narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: No? I don't recommend this? Why the **** not?First of all, I'd recommend it. What? Bear with me. It's good, but the devs need to work on it and I really wanted to warn future players about the faults.OK, it was very touch and go, I'll tell you. I loved 'Innocence', apart from the final boss fight. I {i}so{/i} much wanted to love this game... but it fell short.I've now played part way through NG+. I think I can write a proper review, now.{b}The main game pros...{/b}1)  It's beautiful, if a little hard on your PC. I have a Ryzen 7 3700x, RTX 2060 super, 32 GB DDR4 RAM. It's cool, but this game runs my PC hotter than most. Huh! I''m upgrading to a 4070 super and 5700x shortly, so I can't complain, personally. However, I think game makers should think about why they're pushing gamers to more power hungry rigs: there's a planet to consider. Ahh! I shouldn't start on that...2) The story. It's firm and leads to 'A Plague Tale: Restoration.', or similar title, based in London, perhaps, with the 'Bubonic plague'.3) I think there'll be a third game!4) Don't discount the voice-acting. It's superb. Congrats to the actors!5) It's compelling, but frustrating at the same time....The  cons...{b} Game mechanics.{/b} Why couldn't they get this right? After the first game and all?1) Alicia walks too slowly, when crouched. I get that there's a skill to improve this, but, what the fu**! It's ridiculous.2) Our protagonist stabs people and her knife always breaks! What? Maybe there's a chance of it happening, but no way will a knife break every time! Give her the knife back, most of the time. If you're playing for stealth, you won't need them much anyway. It's frustrating to end up at a special workbench and not be able to open it because you broke your one knife stabbing an enemy, rather than re-do ten minutes of gameplay to sneak past him.3) There's a point where Amicia gets into an armoury. She is unarmed, looking for her sling. She finds boxes of swords and knives. She refuses them. For f***'s sake! At least give her a knife! No, she takes nothing.3) Poorly made climb points.There aren't many, but they're annoying. I'm talking about when Amecia approaches a climbing point and gets too close. The option to climb disappears and she has to back off.4) Companions. Jeez, they get in the way. I got spotted so many times because the f***ers were in the way! Not good. More on that in my 'bugs' section. {b}Bugs{/i}Ooooooh! Here we are again. Bugs in a fifty quid game? Who'd have thought it? Skyrim? Witcher 3? Cyberpunkl? Bugs are prevalent in all games. It's really hard to  make a game without one. I know. I've made mods for games. The main thing is how they're dealt with once people play it.There are many in this game. They seem worse because  the game is so slow and relies on a checkpoint system. I don't want to list all that I've found, but to prove a point...1) companions can get stuck. They won't move. You're f***ed at this point. 'Restart from checkpoint'! That's your only option and it can get frustrating.2) The devs seem to have calculated time to do some actions. If you do it faster, although it looks safe, you'll die. One example of this is running for the climb behind a flaming haybale . Get there ahead of time and die.{b}New Game plus{/b}1) Nothing much to add, except that when you upgrade all your gear, it f***s all the timings up and they haven't accounted for it.  If you could run to a chest with a burning stick before, loot it and get back to a fire... now you can't. You need to recycle the tool, if you have all upgrades... and you will. It takes several seconds. You can die...,   ... It would be nice to get a random alchemy ingredient when you don't need pieces.2) Why find pieces to upgrade when you've got it all? Give me alchemy ingredients instead.3) I'd personally like more crafting. Unlock three more tiers with NG+. Tier 4 aggression kills helmeted enemies. Prudence unlocks something like invisibility, but only once per section.  Tier 4 opportunism unlocks  "Silent kill': Enemies killed won'rt be detected.That's it.I'd recommend the game, even though I flagged it as not recommended. The devs need to polish it a bit and it'd be great. Part of me believes, or wants to believe that some silly accountants are behind the lack of polish. I've encountered just that issue in my career as a professional engineer.Buy it, but it has flaws, unfortunately.It could be a masterpiece, with a few tweaks.

_childDocuments_.review: Plague Tale: Requiem is a work of love that is worth experiencing despite its flaws.When you look at this game, you have to keep in mind that Asobo Studios do not have the same resources as Naughty Dog or other AAA studios. They even use their own engine.Especially the outdoor areas look fantastic, the lighting seems like an Unreal 5 tech demo and the composition is often just perfect. That doesn’t mean the whole game looks superb. Characters also look great and their animations are good, but like some wrote facial animations can be a bit stiff in extremely emotional situations, most of the times I found them really good enough though.The voice acting is great, especially Amicia, and it’s true that Hugo’s voice can get annoying, but he is a young kid and that’s just quite authentic. An underlying issue makes this just more of a problem than it should be: The constant topic between Amicia and Hugo is the same and they go over and over and over it. If this was a 2 hour movie, it would have been fine, but 10-12 hours of the game is simply too long to let the characters exchange the same fears and topics again and again. At some point even a NPC tells them to shut up... so the writers were quite aware. Sadly, they also changed to British accents, which takes away some part of authenticity.Sound and music are well done and support the medieval theme and mood greatly.I would say that the story is presented well and quite emotionally touching, but definitely not a great one (will get to that later in detail). Dialogues are written in a simple way, which is often alright, but sometimes certain word uses gets repetitive and there is definitely squandered potential.And the gameplay? Well, you can craft now more useful ammo types to either control the rats or the lights (on/off). The AI and the sneaking part remains mostly the same, its formula is applied in different ways, but never gets you really excited. Why is there never an urgency through time pressure, for example? Or why do the soldiers never actively burn the fields? They could have done much to break up the stale formula of the stealth gameplay.The skill system has a balancing issue at least with the upgraded crossbow, which will give you back all your bolts back from corpses and then leads to just shooting everyone dead without any hassle. Also, they had the idea to connect it to the story and have people tell you constantly, that you should control yourself and so on. Of course, the writing team wanted to avoid the same problem as in Tomb Raider (2013): A young woman becomes a mass murdering machine, but is actually a quite nice and normal person. Let’s just say that also Asobo Studios didn’t solve it and by rubbing your nose into it, they just made it worse.The riddles are another part of the gameplay and I did like one or two, most of them were more of the same from Plague Tale part one and some were really a drag (the four cranes!). Unlike others, I didn’t fear the rats (anymore) and I was tired of getting from light to light in some artificial way.Sorry, but after that long time with the rats Amicia didn’t think to purchase a simple steel torch??? Or just keep the ones along the way? With that tool they would have walked through the whole game without a hassle. I know, it’s just a game, games are gamey, but this shows where games need to improve.And then there is the option to control the rats through Hugo, which I thought would be the new selling point of this part, but no. You can use it kinda 1-2 times and it’s also not that fun actually.And the fact that even in fights you hold hands with Hugo is clumsy from a movement perspective and in reality you wouldn’t do that, especially if you want to protect the child...The story: Unlike the first part, Plague Tale: Requiem is about superlatives. A bigger part of the game is a constant chase which almost feels like a rollercoaster ride, meaning it doesn’t care how much sense it all makes and focuses more on the spectacle.The “treasure hunt” for the truth about the macula is even for Indiana Jones standards illogical and the conclusions about the clues from Amicia more than far-fetched. Also, the underground architecture is ludicrous. Of course it’s impressive and a wow-moment when you look at it, but for me it’s just a step too far and it breaks the immersion a bit. Same goes for the rat chase sequences, which are so obviously fake.Personally, I am fine with the ending and it actually takes away some frustration from the fact that you actually did not find a cure. It's just a simple story about people fighting the inevitable.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the first game, A Plague Tale: Innocence. It came totally out of left field; a cinematic third person puzzle adventure game with a dark story about two siblings trying to survive the Black Death. Apparently it sold well, because the sequel, A Plague Tale: Requiem, went full AAA. I mean that in both the good and bad sense.+ Amazing visuals. Haven't played anything this beautiful since Red Dead Redemption 2 or The Witcher 3.+ Impressive, emotional acting. Hugo is played by an actual child and he sells the role, which is usually not the case with child actors.+ Fun gameplay. Basically the same as the first game, with some additions.+ Excellent score. Music is both haunting and beautiful.+/- Cinematic and epic. Nice cutscenes which are a feast to behold. On the negative side though; obligatory turret sections, multiple chase sequences and explosive moments that rival your average Call of Duty campaign. Overall feels more like Uncharted than Plague Tale, if that makes sense.- Pacing. This game is long and feels it. Twice the length of the first game. Some chapters could be trimmed or cut entirely. One open world-ish chapter felt unnecessary.- Story is pretty meh. This is the most controversial for me. It has its moments but feels a little too "blockbustery" for my tastes. I much prefer the down to earth tone of the first game. Less is more. The first game is quaint, it's basically a story about two siblings trying to survive a bad situtation by using their skills and wit. The sequel is full of prophecy and ancient temples  and dream sequences (yes, I know there's a dream sequence in the first game) and even the apocalypse. Half the time I didn't know what I was doing, and the characters didn't seem to either. "Let's go to this place and maybe there's something there, I dunno." In Innocence you're fighting the Inquisition, but in this game you're fighting everything *all the time*, city guards and slavers and religious fanatics and even random bandits. I guess the dark ages were tough. Some characters make 180 turns. The moral of the story is confusing, as well.Overall, I would recommend this game. It's a visual spectacle and feels good to play. The story is hit or miss (mostly miss), but satisfying despite its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost never buy a game full price AND during the moment it releases. The game did not disappoint!It is almost nothing like it's predecessor, which was far for more concise, focused and not so grand in scope. This may be something that will turn people off. Amicia and Hugo's connection is what gave the first game it's endearing moments. It's what made it so memorable to play and it stuck with you after it's conclusion. This sequel explores that same relationship but from a different lens. It will also explore the consequences that follow because of it.Asobos really outdid themselves with this sequel. The only criticisms that come to mind is that the pacing is all over the place and that the game is almost too long as you're constantly wondering when it  will end. IN regards to predicting the story, what you think will happen, you'll definitely be WRONG.From a technical aspect he game is quite polished but will push your system to the limit. Mechanic wise I only experienced a few glitches from enemies being stuck to several crashes cutting to desktop without warning.Graphics: Absolutely beautiful! Every location is dense with detail and scenery which is often one of the strengths of linear games.Audio: The voice acting is superb! It does most of the heavy lifting to carry the terrible lip syncing and dead eyes the characters still seem to have just like in the first game. The music is beautiful and memorable.Game play: If you like stealth (cat and mouse) this is your game. I first wanted to try and not kill anyone to see if there was an achievement for that but after a while though I found myself becoming more and more aggressive killing everyone I came across just to get to the next location. The side characters never like you doing that and will tell you so. Enemies are predictable and slow, but the linear aspect is much more broad in how you want to navigate through those moments.Combat: Rather than coming up with a versatile approach when it comes to "boss" fights (quality) the game begins to throw a never ending stream of regulars (quantity)  at you which, by the end, becomes very tedious as you scramble to find resources to take them down. This become very annoying.Puzzles: The puzzles are not at all difficult but doing them allows the side characters to shine narrative wise and it is a nice break from playing hide and seek from enemies once in a while.Replay-ability: Knowing how the story ends it will be difficult to recapture the same experience. Any replays will be for me to lessen the difficulty and just enjoy the narrative again while enjoying the breathtaking locations.Indy to AAA: With the growth of Amicia's character you will certainly get Tomb Raider vibes now that she can kill efficiently. Side characters that witness your savagery will certainly be impressed and will tell you so, or they will scold you. The scope of this game is much more massive than the first. There is actually one area/hub you will be able to explore with king Hugo which will branch off to different locations. Asobos may have bitten off more than they can chew as what is lost in this sequel is the magical charm the first game had. Any other sequels that they may or may not be planning will be difficult to decide creatively, however, my guess is that it will be even bigger. If you do play to the very end of this game you will probably agree.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent sequel to the previous title that takes many aspect that worked in Innocence and improves or expands on it. Requiem is one of the best looking single player games I've played so far. It is a current-gen only title and it definitely shows. We get to experience a bigger, more detailed and colorful world with simply breath-taking landscapes. The art style is gorgeous just like it was in the previous game, although, I think I've liked the darker, more somber look of Innocence a bit more.Goosebumps and a river of emotions. Olivier Derivière did an outstanding job once again. It fits the story, setting, combat and captures the brutality, hopelesness and beauty of it.Worthy of a vinyl purchase.As mentioned above a lot of mechanics received improvements or were expanded. The ai is smarter this time around (though, it stil needs some polishing), which can make stealth or enemy encounters in general, more challenging. The game also gives you multiple ways how you can approach different situations and that is tied to an all new skill tree, which I found great and can also add to replayability. Although, it is more of a one-time experience. Certainly more difficult and longer than it's predecessor, long enough to tell and fulfill its narrative. The difficulty though had some werid spikes, that sometimes can take away from the experience.The story-telling is where this game excells and succeeds the most. The well written characters, top tier voice acting.. all makes up for a beautiful and immersive story. It makes you feel for the characters, even for the side ones, and will make it hard for you to put it down.(Yes, the ending made me cry like little b**ch.)Short summary: After the conclusion of the first game and escaping their homeland, Amicia and her little brother Hugo, lived relatively in peace for a few months until the disease in her brothers body has awoken once again. After being forced to flee once more, the siblings are hoping to find a cure on a prophesized island and save Hugo.Of course, the optimization could be better, but for a game that looks this good, I can forgive that. Overall it runs smoothly.Worth the full/release price.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall impression: a beautiful follow-up to one of my favourite video game stories. It fleshed out the universe and characters and expanded on a lot of the best mechanics while maintaining the perfect atmosphere of the original.Will I play it again? ABSOLUTELY. I did a balance of murder and stealth the first time around according to what felt right in the situation. I'd like to do a pacifist run as a personal challenge and one as an absolute slaughtergoblin.Pros:The story! I was initially concerned that another round of "Things seem to be going nicely but, oh no, someone was ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and it stressed Hugo out so now it's the apocalypse and we need to get him to a doctor" would be really samey, but Requiem did an amazing job of fleshing out the nature of the Macula, the history of the plagues and the alchemists, as well as the trauma Amecia goes through keeping her little antichrist alive. The writing and focus on character is even stronger than in the first game.The variety! Although this is predominantly a sneaking-past-danger kind of game, it generously mixes in opportunities for tense battles and crafty platforming puzzles--all of which benefit from an expanded alchemical crafting system with tools to open new paths, pass undetected, or kill people horribly. Most situations have a few right answers depending on your style.The visuals! When the game wants you to feel nice, the landscapes of medieval France are breathtaking. Then, when it finally pulls the rug, the way subtle horror starts to creep in is worthy of a top-notch indie film.The friends! Without spoiling too much, all of the characters who join you on your adventure give a very different feel to their levels. There's the nerd who offers you lore tidbits and handy recipes, the wiggly child who can get into secret locations, a badass guard-stabber, and an unexpected beacon of light in the rat-pocalypse. The level design is already much more varied than Innocence, but the companions make it feel even more diverse.Cons: The moral system is a red herring. I may eat my words after more playthroughs but, from what I'm hearing, whether you go pacifist or slaughtergoblin doesn't actually change much in the story. Your in-game companions will act all judgy in the moment, but the only real consequences of doing horrible ♥♥♥♥ are further traumatizing Amecia. I mean, for me, that was enough--but some of you out there are sociopaths.The scale of some levels is too ambitious. For a game that really encourages you to stick your nose in every corner for treats, throwing in a wide open hub world in the last few acts of the game seems cruel. I spent an unnecessary few hours running around that island trying not to miss anything before triggering any plot advancement. Pro tip: if a companion is nagging you to go a certain direction, just do it. Don't suffer my fate.

_childDocuments_.review: So let us start with the big point. System requirements. Played on maxed out settings(which includes raytracing) with my 3080 ti, got murdered quite hard during the times where graphic demands are high but averaged somewhere around 70 and reached into the 120 at the low demand areas.A lot of the wow factor comes from the beautiful landscapes and details so I would not recommend playing without at least the recommended parts. But if you do want to play it anyway, wait for a good sale.Now let us move to the actual gameplay itself. It is in most ways identical to Innocence, except most features are expanded and/or reworked. If you liked the first game, then you will likely enjoy this one too. I didn't go on an adventure to seek out every collectible but I did finish the game fully, plus epilogue. It is much more combat oriented than I remember Innocence to be, but it is not necessarily a bad thing as they did expand on your combat options.Not yet decided if I will call it a 7 or 8 out of 10, but definitely solid.

_childDocuments_.review: Not to sound too much like a mother, but this game frequently depicts the sufferings of death, violence, and anxiety happening to children. If these kinds of events disturb you, please consider refraining from buying this title.That being said, this title has very good artwork and graphics engine.  For many, it may be challenging for their PC system. The story in this title is good, but less grounded than the previous title, Plague Tale: Innocence. For the latter half of the game, I felt like the game was being dragged on unncessarily for a story that was beginning to feel "strung out."In terms of actual gameplay, there is crafting, stealth, and some combat. The play style is left largely up to the player, but there were many instances I personally found that it was more convenient to eliminate an enemy solider or whatever.This title is interesting, disturbing, scary, moving, daunting, and many more adjectives, which are amplified due to the protagonists being young people (young woman Amecia) and a child (Hugo).  I would not recommend children play this title.

_childDocuments_.review: delves deeper in pursuit of the answers to the plague. A continuation of the first adventure, , the story naturally begins where the first ended. It is difficult to distinguish one from the other and therefore, I would recommend playing the games in order of release. That is unless you do not care about the character development of our protagonist. The progression is again linear but many scenarios have multiple pathways for the player to choose. In addition, there are new abilities and we even see a new weapon. The choice between killing and letting an enemy live affects the progression of prudence (stealth), aggressive (combat), and opportunism (crafting). Opportunism progression is weird and seems to be increased the best by letting half enemies live and killing half the enemies in each encounter. Regardless of what skills you go for they cannot be completed in one playthough and will require approximately half the game to be completed on new game+. A single bug appears in chapter 10 that is eerily reminiscent of the first game. An invisible barrier once again halts progression but this time it is at the top of a staircase. In order to continue I had to use Sophia's skill on a torch and cancel couple of times to get through. Once again, the bug must not be important enough to warrant a fix. It's not game breaking by any means but annoying in an otherwise highly polished game.

_childDocuments_.review: A Plague Tale: Requiem is a successful sequel to its predecessor Plague Tale: Innocence. Where the game often lacks is when it tries too hard to reuse or recycle content (animations or sequences) which made me personally bored through the early stages of the game. However, it takes a massive leap in story and gameplay the further you dive in, infact the final chapters feel so much better than the rest of the game almost as if the first portion of the game was left overs of the first game and the later portions were all newly made. _childDocuments_.review: A Plague Tale Requiem is Innocence turned up to 20, because 11 was way too tame.I finished the game in its entirety in about 20hrs except for NG+, which I found it was too much a hassle. I know this is a negative final opinion, but I hope whoever reads this understands why I do it, and the effect I hope it has.Let's start with the positives:The graphics are simply outstanding. It's rare for me to stop on my tracks and take pictures the same way I do so IRL, but this game, the lighting, the particle system, the vistas, they all lend themselves to stopping and just taking pictures, it's THAT good. The levels, while lineal as all hell are truly a wonderful sight. A wonderful, dark, grim and grotesque sight, but a wonderful sight non the less. At first I thought the game was running on the new Unreal Engine 5, because I couldn't for the life of me tell apart when the LOD kicked in. It turns out I was looking at the wrong things, and the engine (proprietary) pushes Parallax Occlusion Mapping in a way I never thought possible, using extra triangles only where necessary, and faking the rest. This doesn't necessarily mean the game is easy on your PC; your CPU will be begging you to stop looking at the rats, which honestly is a bit difficult, when you will be facing TIDAL WAVES of rats (I did mention Requiem turns things to 20!).The graphics engine is paired to an amazing sound and voice casting, played thankfully by the same actors as before. Every action is paired to a very distinct sound, and pretty much all voice lines are delivered nearly perfectly, with some lines standing out for their emotionality which caught me off guard. While lip syncing is not perfect, it shines where it is needed the most and manages to hit at just the right moments too. Bravo!Gameplay wise, Asobo Studios has really enhanced the experience as a stealth game, and while IT hasn't necessarily been refined (much of the old antiques still work just as in Innocence), Amicia now has a much more varied arsenal, not just in weapons (with a Crossbow) but also alchemy, allowing her to turn off fires, turn on fires, invigorate them and more. Your sidekicks also get to have a hand in the play by providing their unique abilities and making each "stage" more of a challenge in creativity rather than difficulty. I do wish the game were harder in that sense; it seems there are TOO many opportunities now, and it doesn't help that the enemies, even when they spot you, are slow enough that allow you to do as you please and retreat when you need to. There is a new system implemented too, that gauges how you are playing (stealth/aggressive/alchemy) and using that to improve on certain passive abilities related to that. I thought it would have an impact on the story, but alas, it does not. Now, let's get to the reason why this is a "negative" review for me.One thing that Innocence did right, was character development. The game centered around Amicia and Hugo, how they got to know each other and protect each other when they needed it the most, and thankfully, Requiem follows on that trend, with excellent dialogue that reflects a relationship you would have with a child that doesn't quite understand what is happening in this dark, grim world. The problem lies in what I described to a friend as "AAA syndrome".You see, I started counting the AAA game tropes in Requiem, and at some point, I lost track of them. Chase scenes? You got them in spades. Last stand scenes? Oh yeah. Turret scenes? Well sure, we'll add a few more of those. Usually I can turn a blind eye if they are just one of each, but when you get a chase scene, and less than 20 minutes later you are doing ANOTHER one, that's just lazy.Another thing that was lazy, and at this point, utterly frustrating, was the amount of Ex Machina moments that sprung up throughout the story. Deus ex machina, (Latin: “god from the machine”) is a person or thing that appears or is introduced into a situation suddenly and unexpectedly and provides an artificial or contrived solution to an apparently insoluble difficulty. This applied both ways, either as a solution or a problem. You are about to sail ahead? Well too bad, the boat is stuck. Got it unstuck? Well too bad, the sail is stuck. Got that untangled? Well too bad, there's a storm. You are escaping from a deadly situation? How lucky, a new character approaches and saves your life. The list goes on and on, and it's not a good feeling when it happens for the third time in a row. To me, it indicates the writer/s simply added some padding to a game that could've lasted a few hours less if not for all these artificial problems.It really is a shame, because were it not for these contrivances within the story, the chase scenes, the turret sections, all of the "AAA" game elements and the inexplicable amount of Ex Machina moments, the game would have been incredible! The main beats within the story are good, and while several key moments needed me to increase my suspension of disbelief really hard, it managed to drive the plot forward and have its emotional moments (once again, thanks to some amazing voice acting and absolutely gorgeous visuals).The sole reason for this negative review, is because I KNOW the devs can do better for next time, and because no matter if everything else is amazing, when the story is mangled between so much crap, it's hard to appreciate it for what it is.I still recommend A Plague Tale: Requiem though. Maybe I'm just getting old (?).

_childDocuments_.review: In short: This game has very tedious game-play with a decent story. I feel like in my 18 hours of the playthrough, it was 8 hours of cut scenes, and slow walking while talking and the rest is what I would call "puzzle combat". There's basically only one way from A to B that you have to sneak through and engaging in combat is frustrating. It's a very one-track game.I found myself about 2/3 of the way though and got very bored of the same gameplay and used a mod for unlimited ammo/supplies and crossbowed my way through the rest of the game to get through the story.Graphics are decent, but even with motion blur off, there seemed to be a halo or blur around moving objects and other strange anomalies. Running this game on a 7900 XTX and it struggled at 4k, had to bump down to 1440 or turn the dynamic resolution to balanced or performance to stay close to 144 fps. The game did crash on me twice and would sometimes hang trying to load new areas. I don't think this game was well optimized for AMD.Overall I think the game was worth the sale price of $25, but I wouldn't pay full price. It reminds of "The Last of Us" as a story driven game, but with worse gameplay, graphics, and not as engaging of a story. Let's hope the next one is better.Too bad there wasn't a "meh" recommendation but I'll barely give it a yes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simply fantastic to say the least. I'll be honest with you guys I have never played the previous game, due to the fact that my PC when Innocent was released could barely run it on low, so I decided to watch a playthrough instead.Anyway, back to the review.First of all, the story was very heart breaking during some chapters and I admit that I was crying my eyes out during the last chapter. Very nicely written characters(Not every) and some splendid plot twists and discoveries. Though I admit during a few events I was not phased at all, maybe I got used to all the sadness,depression and betraying. Yet, I still really enjoyed the story and was very difficult to stop playing sometimes when the story got sooo interesting, especially during chapter 11 when everything took a turn to the worst. Lasty, I legit got spooked at some occasions and encounters, especially with one big bald man.Second of all,  the graphics are phenomenal. I can't say anything else, the game looks beautiful. However, I own a powerful PC now and I still had FPS drops during some parts of the game,but well what can you do, hope the publishers will fix it somehow, but if they don't it is still enjoyable.To put it in short, Plague Tale Requiem is a superb game with some excellent combat,story and atmosphere, but it still has some fixable problems. Should you play this game? Absolutely. If you enjoyed the previous game you will enjoy this one as well,maybe even better.  I had to leave this review, because the game left me with strong emotions and I had to let them out, even if its in a way of a review. It became quite a long read, but if you read it THANK YOU for your time and enjoy this masterpiece :)

_childDocuments_.review: This was a painful, heart-wrenching story, filled with sadness, and rage. The music sets the emotional heights of this game so well too. Voice acting was stellar. I was left feeling a bit empty and on the verge of tears at the end. It's a pretty long journey - Requiem took me around 21-23 hours to complete compared to around 14 and a half for Innocence. Maybe my constant checkpoint resetting contributed to that but, oh well. Can't help wanting to be my stealthiest.Combat and exploration have been expanded with a new weapon type, the crossbow, and additional ammo types for both that and the sling. It took me quite a while to get used to the weapon/ammo wheel on PC, it was a bit of a challenge on its own.The game has impressive visuals, certainly, but this also meant it came with a hefty graphical demand. The game had me wishing it also had better optimization.I loved Lucas in the first game, and I still do in this one, and now, I like Sophia too. She's great.All in all, I would rate this emotional gut punch of a game an 8 out of 10. Highly recommended, especially for fans.

_childDocuments_.review: First I would like to thank the Developers and their team for creating such a beautiful, impactful, and amazing story. The entire time I was playing, I was fully emerged into the game. I kept commenting to my friends about how much I loved the second part of the game for it's development. You can clearly see progress through each and every character, it does not feel rushed and it does not feel like it's "plot convenience." I felt attached to each character unlike the previous game where I only cared about Amicia and Hugo. They made the game more difficult in terms of stealth and confronting enemies. It's not like the previous game where you can run through it all and pass. I did not experience any bugs with the environments, with the lighting, with any of the enemies, with any of the characters  or even auto saving. The character's facial expressions were realistic and emotional unlike most games. You can really tell how much hard work and time they put into this game. It feels complete and not rushed at all. I really loved this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game implements a forced "Resolution Optimizer" that cannot be disabled. It does not state what type of upscaling technology it is, nor the version. _childDocuments_.review: Plague Tale: Requiem - A Haunting But Beautiful Journey (Review)Just finished my emotional rollercoaster ride through Plague Tale: Requiem, and here's the breakdown:A Brutal But Beautiful World:  The game takes you through stunning medieval landscapes, but don't let the beauty fool you.  The plague is ever-present, creating a dark and dangerous atmosphere.Following Amicia and Hugo:  You play as Amicia, protecting her younger brother Hugo who has a mysterious connection to the plague rats. Their bond is the heart of the story, and it can be both heartwarming and heartbreaking.More Than Just Running:  Sure, there's some sneaking around and avoiding giant swarms of rats, but there's also crafting, puzzles to solve, and even some light combat. It keeps things interesting.Get Ready for Feels:  This game doesn't shy away from tough themes and emotional moments. Be prepared to shed a tear or two (or ten).A Few Nits:  The story can feel a bit slow at times, and the enemy AI isn't always the brightest. But the atmosphere and story more than make up for it.Overall Verdict:If you're looking for a beautiful but deeply emotional adventure game, Plague Tale: Requiem is a must-play. Just be prepared for a dark and intense story with some heart-wrenching moments.  But the bond between Amicia and Hugo, and the stunning environments, make it a truly unforgettable experience.  Grab some tissues and get ready for the feels!

_childDocuments_.review: First I want to say there is 1 of 2 players reading this. Player 1 has already played the first game and, quite frankly, is going to play this game to finish the story so far; so this review is less for you. Player 2, on the other hand, is sizing up both games in the franchise to see if it is worth it and, despite my review being negative, it is worth it; just be ready for an abysmal experience in this one.First, gameplay. This game takes the great stealth mechanics along with the interesting puzzles utilising Amicia's sling that made the first game so exciting and, like, "sort" of uses it. The game attempts to go into a more "actiony" approach (which I guess makes sense with the story), making it easier to just kill your way through from the beginning, which sort of makes the stealth component feel underutilised. However, and this is the big let down, about 50% of this game is just a walking/running simulator with dialogue going on, or perhaps some big landscape in the background with some quick time events sprinkled in. Seriously, at one point all that separates two cutscenes is you pressing the spacebar... and nothing else; just make it 1 cutscene!Second, graphics. This brings me briefly to the appearance. Of course the game is gorgeous, but I'd say even the big landscapes you see in the first game were just more jaw-dropping. What's more, for a game that attempts to make you engage with long cutscenes of character interaction one would think they'd focus on making the faces seem less... stiff. A lot of the time it looked like they were talking through their teeth. The expressions were really lacking compared to games like Bauldur's Gate 3.Third, story. The story is... ok. The story in the first game was far more intriguing, gripping, and had more cool lore dumping; however this is just my opinion, clearly many really liked the story so that's really for you to decide. This instalment, on the other hand, while developing more on the macula and Hugo, is distracted by the majority of the story being the conflicts between characters; the first 5 acts just being a prolonged fight between Amicia and her Mother. Though, and I will admit, I did feel like I was quite interested from act 7 - 9, but acts 1-6 & 10-17 less so.Look, it's not bad it's just a bit of a letdown after the first, and I know a lot of these reviews are raving for it, but for some perspective only 65% of the players who own this game made it halfway through the game, with less than 50% actually finishing it; as can be seen from the achievement received for completing each act. I think the negative experiences just haven't left reviews, or lost interested and didn't engage with the store page.So, for the short review, do I suggest getting this game? Sure, but on a great sale, and really just because I so HIGHLY recommend playing the first game that playing through this one to continue the story will be something you will want to do.

_childDocuments_.review: Now this is how you do a sequel! The first game was already really good but this continuation is just fantastic. At the start it does feel a little like they’re just doing the first game again but that changes fairly quickly and it becomes seriously good.The gameplay has roughly the same basis, sometimes you sneak around, sometimes you go on a killing spree and occasionally you get a simple puzzle. You keep being fairly weak in general (which is good story wise) and have to use the environment to make your way through the areas. It’s mostly the same pick-one-off-at-a-time-while-avoiding-detection mechanic but they added a lot of new elements to it like the crossbow and companions that help in different ways. While I’m normally not into stealth games I do think this game strikes the balance between stealth, action and story really well. The gameplay loop feels solid and satisfying.The story is great (if not slightly predictable occasionally) and continues Innocence’s story without the typical “oh ♥♥♥♥ we need to make a sequel” problems where some games that do better than expected have to suddenly figure out a new reason to keep going (sequel syndrome I think it’s called). You keep going through Amicia and Hugo’s (and co) adventure trying to survive and find a cure for Hugo while everything keeps getting worse. It’s an endless fight against something seemingly unbeatable or unavoidable that just keeps getting darker. You explore and try to figure out the origin of what is happening and if it has happened before. The game portrays the heavy exhausting fight against the world really well and every hurt leaves a scar (mentally and physically). The characters get wearier and more worn down the further they go. The writing also does a good job at having the characters aged a little since the last game and a little less naïve while still acting fairly young with the whole “surviving in a world against adults who just don’t understand” vibe. Probably a poor explanation of what I mean but oh well. It’s good and a natural progression from the first game is all I’m saying.The voice acting is brilliant, especially the angry whispering (for some reason that stands out to me) and has a lot of emotion. The voice actors really did the characters justice even despite the lip syncing and facial expressions sometimes being a little off (maybe mocap not done by the voice actors? Idk. But that is such a small thing, barely worth mentioning.)The music is in the same boat, really well done. It fits the game and setting perfectly and is dynamic to whatever is happening on screen. They have a unique and recognizable theme and they are sticking with it and remixing into multiple forms and moods throughout the game. The sound design in general (ambience, sound effects, etc.) are all really good too and there is plenty of details to be found there.Lastly the visuals. This game is absolutely stunning from all angles you look at it. The lightning is just amazing together with the sharp texture quality, facial expressions and just the right amount of grain. I honestly thought it was built with Unreal Engine 5 as it has that “look” but apparently it’s their own in-house engine, which makes it even more impressive. The techniques they use (and disguise) for rendering the crazy amounts of rats is really well done and doesn’t tank the performance at all. The performance on my i5-9600k + RTX 2070 was splendid with mostly 60-100 fps running on ultra (without ray-tracing) at 1440p (with a little DLSS). Really impressive. The art style and character designs also work wonders. I especially liked the details in Amicia’s clothes during the second half of the game combined with the graphical fidelity of it. Though the front flap thing kept clipping through her legs which bothered me as it is such a visible thing and would barely have taken any effort to fix. HDR looked really sweet btw.In summary I’m very satisfied with this game. It took me 20 hours (double the length it took me to beat the first one, for some perspective) and I enjoyed it. Can definitely recommend, though you have to play the first game first, otherwise nothing will make sense.

_childDocuments_.review: In what seems like an endless sea of open world, Ubisoft level spam mediocrity and AAA devs / pubs chasing boring online only MP GAAS trends, A Plague Tale: Requiem was SUCH a breath of fresh air. We just don't get these linear action / adventure games anymore. Loved every second of it, it always left me on the edge of my seating wonder "what's next". Game didn't feel padded out or dragged out either. It was the perfect length which is also another rarity for the gaming industry that seems to push for more hours = better.There is one set-piece in particular that I had legit goosebumps and my jaw was open the entire time. You will know what I am talking about when you see it, new games just don't have these kind of special moments anymore. But that wasn't the only setpiece. The game is constantly a roller coaster of awesome moments and environments fueled by an excellent gripping narrative and story. The rats and the tech behind them continue to impress. At points, there must have been tens of thousands of animated rats on screen at once.The jump from Plague Tale: Innocence -> Requiem really does feel like Asobo's "Uncharted 1 -> 2" moment that Naughty Dog had all those years ago. Cannot wait to see what's next from the Plague Tale team, whatever it may be. Strongly recommend checking out Innocence and then Requiem if you haven't already.

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing story, so full of love and care for its characters. Yes it has a flowers and feathers to collect, but these are a means to maintain Hugo's sanity and morale. _childDocuments_.review: The first game was a good game with a great story, and this is a worthy successor.There's more to it than the story, but if you enjoyed the first game's story then this one is... wow. It's not often that I can truly feel with the characters in a story, but this one hit me like few story games have done for quite awhile. The twists & turns, the connection to historical events, as well as the character development... I enjoyed every moment of it.Part & parcel of it are the three-dimensional characters with their own drives and reasons for acting the way they do, while the story is also explained in light of actual, historical occurences. In this way, this game takes you for a ride, with both tragedy & heroism. As the saying goes: "Et in Arcadia ego".On top of that, the game play has improved. In the first game, it was almost always a matter of deciphering what you should be doing in order to progress. Parts like that still do exist, but this game also contains parts where it's up to you to decide how to solve it. If you want to sneak, there are several choices. You can also go violent and kill what stands in your way, however, or use more distracting tactics, or a combination of them all.Even if the end goal is the same, you now simply have more choices in how to reach it.Writing this, I'm expecting (and hoping) for a third game.

_childDocuments_.review: A really enjoyed this sequel though it is so far from perfect. From the first game they really followed on with continuing a compelling, unpredictable story. I especially credit the writers for not being afraid to make some really bold plot choices that drove the story to new levels.The combat, though similar to the first, has been expanded upon with a new range of abilities coming from both Hugo, and the companions you meet along your way. It really compels you to constantly adapt your play-style throughout the 17 chapter journey and presents you with new ways to play in a well-paced manner to where nothing gets stale.The voice acting is sublime, each actor falls perfectly into their respective roles with the likes of Hugo, Lucas, and Sofia standing even higher above the already high line! Their work elevates interactions between various characters and takes the relationships between them to new heights, they have a well-measured chemistry between them!However, you read reviews to find out what's wrong with the game. Here it is:The performance is absolutely atrocious, even on high-end systems. Unlike every other game released in the passed year it doesn't seem to be a vram issue so much as it is general CPU optimisations.Playing on a 3080ti and a 16-core 12900K, when playing on high (not even ultra!) with ray tracing enabled (only off/on options) I get consistent HEAVY frame drops in almost every outdoor scene in the game, which is about 4/5ths of the game, woohoo! Though the beautiful lavish scenery, which is by the way some of the best I've ever seen, is absolutely breathtaking and adds wonders to the world building. Seeing it drop from 110fps to 15fps when I move my camera 30 degrees really ruins some moments.It does become bearable in some of the slower-paced scenes once you get used to it, however, in some of the chapters such as IX, which are heavily combat/stealth focused it lead me to getting spotted and quite quickly subsequently murdered which is infuriating.Overall I'd say it's a definite buy on sale as the performance doesn't too heavily undermine the rest of the glory this game shines in! It took me just under 26 hours to reach 100% achievements, around 20 of which were my initial play through of the story. I think playing without ray tracing is a solution others have taken to, there are numerous steam guide dedicated to improving performance consistency. I do however refuse to play without it given what I'm playing on and expected better of the developers in this regard.

_childDocuments_.review: The Search for a cure to Hugo's sickness continues in this new adventure. The rats have more tricks up their umm... Look, you're in for some action that's all you need to know. I will say halfway into the game i realised it's got a certain quality to it that i liked. Kind of like Uncharted 4. 7/10The focus for the cure that first game established carries over and hard choices will be made. If you want a much better review in more detail then i recommend  7/10The overall gameplay and combat is more of the same but better with improvement made to mostly everything. Go check out my review on the first game  8/10Check out my review for more details ^^^Ok so yeah this game is very demanding in comparison to the first one and it's probably my first game to bottleneck with the specs i have. But i'm getting ahead of myself so let me back up. The game clearly got a bump up in its engine because the sheer amount of rats the game produces is insane. The team over at Asobo Studio push the tech far enough to produce some impressive graphics and physics with the destructible environments that you may want to check your specs for this game. I played this game at 1440p at 155hz on mostly high settings with some mix of lower shadows. Dlss was set to quality and i also enabled Nvidia Reflex even though i didn't really need it but wanted to give it spin. I played this game on an i7 9700K (stock) with a Rtx 2070 Super graphics card (stock) and let me tell you this game was chugging my rig in many areas. Seriously, out all of the games i have played and reviewed this one i really felt like i needed more juice to run. It's so demanding that i mostly was averaging 60-80 fps. It ran mostly smooth until the game started to flex its muscle a bit with the rat spawn. Anytime the game throws a lot at you or spawns tons and tons of rats, my fps would tank dramatically to 30 and under. My lowest drop was 14 fps. After a while of playing i observed something i'm not used to seeing in task manager. My cpu was mostly 50-60% utilisation while my gpu was chilling at basically 0% utilisation the entire time. But when the rat spawns, my cpu would shoot for 100% and the gpu still at 0%. I would experience some minor stutter but i realised this could be a bottleneck if it's hitting 100%. My cooler ramped up as a result which is nuts. I thought initially that it's probably misreporting since the game was still new. But after a while of playing and watching others with similar spec go through levels where lots happen that i concluded it's a bottleneck. My cpu temps at the highest was 65c so it wasn't like over 80c i like i thought it might me if the cooler was kicking in at 100% cpu utilisation. There's one cutscene that also tanked my fps down to 14 for like 5 secs and there's this one mansion for some reason that caused my fps to drop depending where i look to like 26 fps. I even tried it in photo mode. Other times during combat with so much effect going on or when i light up the ground on fire it would also tank my fps under 40 for a few seconds. There's also the fact that i was playing in 2k. But yeah that's my experience with my specs. You might have a completely different experience in your playthrough. I would suggest you check your specs before getting this game lol. Also if you have similar/better or same specs to me plz let me know if you also had issues. Curious to know if this is just me or not. Dlss might have saved me now that i think about it. Happy how my rig handled all this. Oddly, i remember this game was supposed to have Rtx. But it never got this feature. I wonder if that would break the game lol. 7/10 Remember i said the game got a bump in its engine? Well the graphics got so much better that you would think it's AAA quality. Because it's from a AA studio and it's impressive to run through large area when nothing is burning or chasing you and just sit back and take screenshots. I took many. Seriously in 1440p this game really shines. 9/10 It's ok and fits with moment to moment gameplay. Great. 8/10If you liked the first Plague Tale then i think you will like this one as well. There were ideas and location i felt wasn't fully used well or didn't go anywhere at all that i was left wondering what was the point. Almost as if some ideas were scraped. Beat the beat a few hours ago. The dlc isn't worth at all but if you really liked the first one then go for it.Cpu - i7 9700K StockGpu - Asus ROG Strix RTX 2070 SUPER StockRam - 32GB 3200Mhz Xmp enabledMonitor - Asus XG27AQ ROG Strix 2560 x 1440p 170hz

_childDocuments_.review: I am really torn between giving this game a thumbs up or a thumbs down – hopefully, I can make up my mind by the time I finish writing this review. Some people have suggested that Steam should introduce a neutral grade, but even that wouldn’t help me in this case, as it would suggest the game is “meh” while it’s anything but.I’ll start with the good stuff. Gameplaywise, Requiem has improved a lot since the first game. Enemies’ perception has been worked on, meaning the developers could reduce their numbers rather than having them all over the place (like in Innocence) to make it hard to sneak past them. They spot you from quite a distance and respond to most noises adequately. However, they still don’t hear you falling or opening crates, and tall grass is still “safe ground” as they will fail to see you there even when staring directly into your face. They also don’t care about any visible movements of the grass, and the only person they ever notice anywhere is you, meaning that your companions are invisible to them, leading to some unrealistic moments. (For the record, that’s not really a complaint. I’m not quite masochistic enough to want any of these things changed. :)Combat has remained mostly the same, but there is more variety of enemies and more means at your disposal to deal with them. Combinations of archers and guys throwing Greek fire to get you out of your cover are especially challenging. I loved these bits despite being focused on sneaking past everyone whenever possible.Graphically, this is hands down the most gorgeous game I’ve ever seen. I don’t think I even need to explain this, just look at some footage.Well, what is wrong with the game, then? I was a huge fan of Innocence, as it had a very nice balance by contrasting gruesome and gory events, and… well, innocence. The protagonists were likeable and there was a clear villain they were fighting. In Requiem, I can’t help but feel that the creators missed the mark and broke that delicate balance by trying to make the game even darker. The heroes walk down a path that shakes them to the core both physically and mentally, and it also leaves a mark on their character. That sounds like a natural consequence, and indeed it could work with the right story, but as uplifting moments thin out and eventually disappear, the game becomes a very exhausting experience to play through. Even from the beginning, there are signs that the game is trying too hard for the shock value (why make the characters sneak through a slaughterhouse of all places when there are plenty of other gory scenes anyway?), but in Chapter 12, I felt for the first time that the creators went very much overboard with the violence, and the narrative fails to explain how your character recovers miraculously so you’re soon up on your feet and fighting again. I’m sure it could be explained in some way to make more sense in the context of the story (maybe being a Protector should come with some regenerative powers), but even that wouldn’t have helped the broken balance I was talking about.The ending feels somewhat rushed and predictable, and the characters' choices that lead there do not always seem well grounded. Interestingly, while both Innocence and Requiem are fully linear games in which the player has no control over how events unfold, there is one minor, inconsequential choice you need to make at the very end of the second game. I was left wondering why that choice is there at all, and if Requiem could have worked better if the developers had added more possibilities for player decisions. I may have walked away from the game feeling less sour if I had been allowed to mitigate the sting of at least some of the dark events by making the right choice.I am aware that most of the weak points I mentioned in my review are a matter of personal taste and preference. Overall, I feel that Plague Tale: Requiem is a very well-made game that is not for everyone. Not for me, perhaps? Either way, I feel relieved to have finished it and move on to play a more uplifting game next.

_childDocuments_.review: The only good thing about this game is its awesome visuals. The rest consists of way too long story with a load of boo-hoo moments, repetitive gameplay, and mediocre stealth.In terms of , the first game was as short as it was immersive. The Requiem is different. It has twice larger locations that feel empty and populated with the same props. At first glance they are open for diverse approaches; however, there's no sense in it. Unlike the other notable stealth games, no shortcuts or exclusive ways may be unlocked with a skill check. Every unlockable skill is combat- or craft-related. Every location consists of several rat swarms, a dozen guards, random torches, and tall grass for hiding, all mixed up in random order with changeable backgrounds. The same approach was applied for every location except for the prologue and epilogue. As a result, I had a strong feeling of running at the same level by the sixth chapter already.The gameplay itself is just a single runaround from one cut-scene to another. During these runarounds, you are supposed to complete the same-looking puzzles. Moreover, there are plenty of decisions throughout the story when the protagonist starts completing another puzzle or walking an extra hundred metres in darkness that swarms with rats instead of simply kneeling to pick up a torch from behind or getting over a waist-height fence. The protagonist, who can slaughter an entire garrison with a sling & stone or escape a city guard over some castle rooftop edge, cannot cross a small fence and walk through the beach in sunlight towards her score. As a player, I should not notice and question such moments. However, when such moments are questioned even more than once, it's the alarm for cheap game design.And of course, you can sprint only when the game allows you to do so. Taking into account the story length, not being able to sprint through neutral areas makes it more of a challenge rather than a joyful playthrough. Such moves do not add an extra point for being detail/pace-attentive, they artificially increase the total playtime and become boring.The  feel like a joke. Asobo wanted to press on the drama meter as much as they could, and even more. There are a lot of moments when the plot takes a 180° turn with absolutely no explanation (kudos to Todd Howard). Moreover, even the protagonist herself hardly justifies her mostly spontaneous and irrational decisions. The protagonist is a destructive person who is dangerous to her close ones. Her hypocritical and childish moves, paired with cheap drama moments, make the whole story look like a bad joke. For example, below is one of many anecdotal moments from the game.Overall  is nice except for a couple of points. Some dialogues have the character voices reverbed. I assume the voice-act recordings were slowed down a bit to match the cut-scene events instead of re-recording the speech. Another con is fake voice echoes. When the characters speak outdoors with at least two walls near them, their voices sound as if they are in a cave or an empty metal capsule. Immersiveness is ruined at this point.---It's a torment with good-looking graphics and it's definitely no-go even when on sale. I'd better see Asobo release a sequel to their Ratatouille instead of them delving further into dramas with deep moral storytelling.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately I do recommend this game, even though my opinions on it are unfortunately quite mixed. The game overall is good, and worthy sequel to its predecessor. It is often beautiful, both literally in its graphics and more figuratively in its story. It's greatest strength is probably just how earnest and genuine it is. The game is sloppy at times, but there's no denying how ambitious the developers are with one. There is clearly a large amount of love and care that went into this, and its hugely respectable how much they attempt with this story, even if it doesn't all come together as well as it should. This review is going to sound quite negative, but the game is overall an enjoyable and interesting experience, easily worth your time if you enjoy these types of games, and are willing to excuse a fair number of annoyances.The issues I have with this game are mostly in the poor execution of a lot of its big, ambitious ideas. The game wants to be cinematic, with high stakes, lots of drama, flashy set pieces, and "next gen" graphics. It's mostly successful at all of these things, but unfortunately it just doesn't have the proper AAA budget to pull it off without lots of missteps. It gets there in the end, it really does, it just stumbles the entire way getting there. This is evident from the very beginning of the game from the graphics alone. This game can be truly beautiful, with gorgeous environments especially. Draw distances, textures, HDR, and much more is all very well done, although PC performance is poor, and I cannot enable the ray-traced shadows without consistent stuttering. Characters models are mostly great too, but this is where the lower AA budget of the game is most apparent. Animation quality throughout this game is simply poor, shockingly so at times. Characters can look really great, photo-realistic at times even, but they animate roboticly. Facial capture is simply nonexistent, and the lip sync is quite bad, with many shots framed to deliberately hide someone's mouth when they speak. You get used to it quickly, but its jarring for a while.This mismatch is a consistent theme throughout the game. Many of the cutscenes are great, but they transition poorly. Big moments happen suddenly and can feel rushed or even sloppy. Tension is rarely built properly, and things don't feel as cinematic as I imagine they intended them to be. There are many moments of great characterization and story telling, but there is an equal amount of melodrama or contrived plot points.  Things overall just feel awkward at times, preventing me from investing in the story completely. As an "indie" game its so impressive, and as a "AAA" game its so sloppy, and it feels both ways at the same time, all the time, even though it doesn't feel fair to judge it that way. The reason this all matters so much is because the story here is 90% of the experience, and the gameplay is always secondary. Its so unfortunate to me that the presentation of that story can be so at odds with itself.The gameplay overall is honestly really not great. There's nothing overly problematic, but the combat and puzzle solving here is simply not that engaging, challenging, or rewarding. Puzzles are almost always moving a crate, breaking a lock, or manipulating rats. The combat is overly simple, with a few basic enemies types and literally no boss fights in the entire game. There's at least one moment where a character is developed over the course of an hour to clearly lead to a boss fight, only for them to die instantly in a cutscene instead. There are moments where you need to fight waves of enemies, and the game simply respawns equipment for you if you don't have enough, and it will do this repeatedly, even on the hard difficulty setting. The game is well aware that it doesn't have a good aiming system, cover system, or even a good balance of available resources, so it just automates all of these things. While there is technically more options here than in the first game, I remember the first having several more interesting and engaging combat sections.Overall, I have obviously written a negative review here. It's a huge credit to the game's strengths that I am still recommending it. I can't really go further into those strengths here, as they come from the story, and I don't want to spoil that. Believe me though. the story is good. The characters are good. The environments are good. As sequel, it is good. Anyone who enjoyed the first game should play this as well. But for everything good the game does, it does something equally poorly. The negatives stand out to me and bother me more than they otherwise would because they are interrupting something I otherwise quite enjoy. It's unfortunate that I couldn't love the game, but I still enjoyed it. I just wish it was more.

You now have countermeasures to employ against hostiles when caught (no more being insta-killed) and a few new alchemical tricks to distract or incapacitate them. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely top notch experience!The gameplay is what it is, it's fine and serviceable, everything is pretty much one-shots and there's a soft lock-on to weakspots, but every kill still feels satisfying (I played it on Hard).Now where the game really shines is the story and the voice acting, the acting from Amecia and Hugo really is some of the best I've experienced. Almost drove a grown man to tears in certain spots. I did miss the french accents a lot. Playing through the first game it felt like such a big part of the characters it really helped set the world in France, now outside of the names it really could take place anywhere in Europe.It was quick to get used to though and my god do they do an amazing job, the amount of feeling they can project into these characters is staggering.A few practical things a buyer might want to know: It took me 14.8h to complete and the game crashed on me a single time. In the later stages of the game autosaves started to freeze up the game for a few seconds and since the autosaves are pretty generous, it got a little annoying. The save freezes might just be because the last session was about 7hours, restarting the game might've solved it.The game can be played without playing the first one (A Plague Tale: Innocence), but I would recommend playing that first though. You can probably rather quickly piece together what happened in the first one based on the conversations in the second one, but really I think it better to know what they are already talking about so you can focus on the conversation itself.I would say the game is worth the asking price, it's not a cheap game and you don't get many hours out of it, but I think it's absolutely worth it. Though I can certainly understand if the price to hours ratio will put somebody off.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game...Pros: The graphics and locations are top notch, beautifully crafted and put together, forest, deserts, snow and sea. _childDocuments_.name: A Plague Tale: Requiem

_childDocuments_.review: I did not enjoy this game. I really enjoyed innocence and was excited to play requiem but it's not very fun. I feel like the narrative isn't good enough to carry the game. You do a lot of waiting through boring dialog only to walk forward a bit or press a button for more narrative to happen. It's more like an interactive movie with some game play sections in between. The stealth is very frustrating and doesn't really work. It feels very 'gamey' rather than immersive. Enemies for some reason can't see you in one place but can see you in another. They hear some things but not others. You can run away and hide in a bush right in front of them and they don't see you. The rat mechanic feels more annoying than challenging, trying to get the light to work and you get caught in places that don't look like you should get caught only to die instantly and restart gets old pretty quick.There is a lot of Amecia doing her thing to protect Hugo, not being able to and Hugo having a tantrum to save Amecia only to pass out and need protecting from Amecia which is tiring. The combat is annoying because as soon as you get cornered there is very little you can do, you don't get the armour dissolving sling either so you can't remove helmets. You just have to hope there is something useful on the ground.The ending is disappointing as well. Overall, it's not enough action to be an action game, the story isn't strong enough to be a story driven game, the stealth doesn't work well enough to be a stealth game. It just ends up feeling boring and frustrating with a bunch of elements that could have been cool but aren't fleshed out enough.
_childDocuments_.name: A Plague Tale: Requiem

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write detailed reviews but a friend asked for my thoughts, so here are them in a nutshell:The game is almost of the same quality as its predecessor, the improvements have been made graphically, and the levels have been expanded. Apart from that, I did not find the writing quality and the pace of the game, which are the most striking points of the first game, of the same quality in this game. I didn't enjoy most of the script. Unfortunately, the gameplay remains and feels the same. The limited gameplay wasn't too a problem as the first game offered a concentrated 10-hour experience. Unfortunately, Requiem offers a playtime of 20 hours or more, which annoys the player at some point when the game runs out of new ideas. Even though I was satisfied with Innocence, I did not enjoy Requiem most of the time, which is very sad for me because I highly anticipated this game. Requiem is not a bad game, but I can say that the rating of the game drops for me when any game stays the same quality as its predecessor.My Curator Page:

_childDocuments_.review: The best movie I've ever played, a 33h movie at that. It is dark, it is gruesome, it is hopeless. It is everything I wanted it to be and everything a story like this deserves to be. Even got me teary eyed at the end, that's impressive, as the last things that made me shed a tear was Interstellar. Truly great, wholeheartedly recommend. A perfect sequel. Will age like fine wine, already one of the all time greats that everyone will remember.Asobo Studio aims extremely high with the scale for game, arguably maybe a bit too much. This gamble to aim so high just about pays off as many parts of the game are done to an extremely high standard but things that are only done to a good standard stick out, not because they're bad but by comparison you can see what got AAA amount of attention and what was left on the back burner, mostly the facial animations when not in cutscenes. Better than something like Mass Effect Andromeda but that's not such a high bar to reach in the first place. Cutscenes are so damn pretty, jaw dropping.Trailer in a way is very misleading, damaged expectations in a way. I worried at first that they turned Amicia into a straight up Mary Sue killing machine who has no issue taking down men double, triple her size. That's not strictly the case. While she does get carried away with her killing sprees because of course she does, she's still a traumatised little girl who has too much responsibility for her age and knows that violence gets her out of situations, not that the same violence solve the deeper issues that cause the violence or that there aren't consequences after it.Still pleased to inform you that she's still an environmental opportunist glass cannon, like how she should be. I only played on hard difficulty and stealth was an extreme joy to play. Asobo plays safe with the formula but this familiar stealth is elevated to great height thanks to how well the rats and soldiers can play off from one another. Really unique experience. Those mindless meat bags from the old game have been replaced by somewhat competent guards. They will check tall grass, walk through them, check new shortcuts that you've opened, inform other guards of something being off , legit so good I wanted to accuse the AI of cheating without having any solid proof. Just wish the AI had the ability to burn tall grass if they suspect you were hiding in it. Tall grass being a safe place is a trope Asobo sadly sticks by.Levels are solid, your general  structure, just one defined entry and exit point. The only picks I'd have is  Would have been a nice little achievement if you did though.Game also dabbles its toes into a pseudo open world section, that is very well made but does have a few pacing issues. Not bad for a first try though.Wikipedia says that the writing team is the same but there has definitely been a change, a hugely positive one at that. The first game clashes a bit with themes, ideas and execution of ideas and literal execution of some characters. A lot could be forgiven for a AA game, especially a first try. By comparison, the story in this game was everything I wanted, dark, hopeless and sort of a psychotic spiral. Fits in very well with the theme of children dealing with traumatically scarring experiences, without the ability to sit down and contemplate what they mean, how it makes them feel and why they act the way they do. Their position in life has defined their purpose in life. Extremely good job in the writing department. Shame Béatrice feel like a weaker character this time round.Some of my favourite reviewers say otherwise, but I disagree on their subjective opinion. I feel like the story is much more intertwined and less left field ideas like a few things were in the last game. Story has a hint of Hellblade.Story and gameplay progression does clash a bit, meaning resources are always plentiful. The game will never risk a halt in the narrative pacing just in case you ever have to back track if run out of resources. Metro Last Light certainly managed this tension of  much better.Voice acting is incredible. God of War is a good game but voice acting should have gone to Charlotte McBurney and the Best Score and Music should have gone to Plague's Tale Requiem. Absolute robbery. Will have to wait till Ragnarök comes to PC to see how much my bias plays favours.Game ran fine for what is a next gen title.  If there would be a DLSS or FSR setting I bet I could have gotten even more. Talking about graphics. Please, for the love of god let us turn of the grain and sharpening filter, really unpleasant to look at.
