I wanted to see how the story unfolded, following the two main characters; Hugo and Amica. However I was throughly dissapointed. They tried to give the game a new aspect to it, such as the controls and crafting. I felt like it was a bit too much. Meanwhile the chapters are exhaustingly too long, some taking over an hour. _childDocuments_.review: My favorite game of the year. A Plague Tale: Requiem is a worthy conclusion for this epic journey. It has been 5 years, ever since I saw the first teaser during E3 2017. The world has changed since, for better or worse, and we all need a touching story like this. We followed Amicia and Hugo along the way, trying to find a cure for the Macula (I will not spoil anything). The de Rune siblings are such lovable and relatable characters, that's why it makes me care so much.Requiem is much better than Innocence, in terms of story, length, control mechanism, visual, and emotional depth (love the first game as well). Highly recommend this game and Innocence. Hopefully, we will get a third installment of A Plague Tale.

_childDocuments_.name: A Plague Tale: Requiem

_childDocuments_.review: Bigger, better, prettier. This is sequel done right.I really enjoyed previous installment and I was looking for this one and oh boy it did not dissapoint. If you liked previous one, there is like 98% chance you will like this one. Because previous game was like AA game and this one is on level of AAA games with ambitions to take on Naughty Dog games. Just look how pretty this game is.First of story, the main thing of this game. Once again we follow Amicia and Hugo few months after events of last game as they are looking for cure for Hugo's disease. I won't tell you more from the story because it is beautifully told with great pacing and great twists and turns. During it's duration you will meet diverse cast of characters with fully fleshed personalities. One thing that many people won't like is how much fake endings this game has.From gameplay side Requiem is very same with upgrades that make the gameplay loop entertaining. Your arsenal got expanded and level design for encounters is much more open and invites you to play your own way (lethal or non-lethal, stealthy or ultimate killing machine). The game even rewards you for your style of play and some companions even comment if you are on killing spree. Requiem even got puzzle that are very familiar to puzzles from Naughty Dog games (move cart from point A to point B), which keeps the pace going.One thing that could use some work is the optimization. While I had no issue expect some FPS drops some minor bugs, others have much bigger problems with it. It's pitty because rest of the package is really amazing.And as Czech who knows English a lot, I still appreciate Czech localization because it is very rare these days.Simplified:+ Graphics and its graphical design+ Story and its characters+ Soundtrack+ Performances by actors+ Level design+ Gameplay loop- Optimization- Facial animationsIf you have stronger rig, I definetly recommend you this game especially if you liked first game. It will take you through many beautifull locations with dark emotional story in this story driven adventure game set in France during 14th century.10 / 10
_childDocuments_.name: A Plague Tale: Requiem

_childDocuments_.review: The game is stunningly detailed, graphically pleasing, and obscenely long and story rich.It take a very different and refreshing approach to the typical OP main character who seemingly has infinite luck. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful game, with an amazing sound design. While the game obviously requires A LOT to run, i have to say playing the game in 4k with a RTX 4090 have been an absolute blast. The game have some of the most beautiful scenery i have seen in any game, and i think the sacrifies in performance requirement is absolutely worth it. _childDocuments_.name: A Plague Tale: Requiem

_childDocuments_.review: Hugo and Amicia continue to struggle with their difficult fate. In the second part we will have to continue to fight the plague. In the process of passing the game, enemies will become friends and friends will become enemies. The ending of the game is heavy, few will remain indifferent. Now let's talk about the gameplay. I didn't really like that the locations became too big. Yes, they are beautiful, but often dull. Speaking about the levelling design, I would like to say that in some places it is unslabbed. Throughout the game there is very little development of the main and secondary characters, and I would like to get to know them better. Overall, the game is good. Comparing the first and second part, it's hard to say which one is better. Each has its pros and cons. I advise you to go through the game! Maybe it is tightened, but it doesn't stop being interesting!
_childDocuments_.name: A Plague Tale: Requiem

_childDocuments_.review: The best game I've played so far this year, and probably one of my favorite games of all time. The story is deep and builds beautifully on what we saw in the first game. Hugo and Amicia are amazing protagonists and their story is heartwrenching, it will really play on your heart-strings. The story is definitely the best part of this game, and hopefully, this wont be the end of the story, without spoiling anything, there are still a lot of ways they can continue the story. The graphics are beautiful, the first game looked amazing, but this is just leaps beyond that. Immersive environments, beautiful level design and detailed textures. Character models look excellent as well.While I really enjoyed the action-stealth gameplay, its definetly one of the weaker parts of the game, but it is by no means bad. And then there are the rats, millions of rats on screen at once and the game still runs smoothly, that's a serious achievement, and it's breathtaking to look at.If you love great storytelling, and deep characters, then you will love this game. Can't wait to see what Asobo does next.
_childDocuments_.name: A Plague Tale: Requiem

_childDocuments_.review: Holy hell, the Plague Tale games came out of left field for me, having acquired them via Humble Bundle. What a story! _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely Outstanding!This game is an absolute gem, offering an unparalleled experience. However, it's essential to note that its primary focus lies in storytelling. Don't expect intricate combat systems or extensive item management – this is a narrative-driven masterpiece.To truly appreciate the narrative depth, I highly recommend playing the first installment, "A Plague Tale: Innocence." Your overall enjoyment of the story hinges on this precursor.Here's a breakdown of the key highlights:Positives:    Graphics:        Undoubtedly, the visuals remain unparalleled in the gaming world.    Story:        The narrative is exceptionally well-crafted, drawing players into a captivating world.    Soundtrack:        The music is not just background noise; it's an integral part of the experience, enhancing the overall atmosphere.    Collectibles:        Discovering collectibles is seamlessly woven into the narrative, adding depth to the storytelling experience.    Language Options:        The availability of European language dubs provides a diverse and immersive language experience.    New Game Plus:        A boon for achievement hunters, the New Game Plus feature adds replay value to the game.Negatives:    Excessive Walking:        At certain points in the game, there's an abundance of walking, which may test your patience.    Alchemy Skill Progression:        Acquiring alchemy experience creation skills could be made more accessible, providing a smoother gameplay experience.In summary, this game stands as a testament to storytelling mastery. While it may not cater to those seeking complex gameplay mechanics, its strengths lie in its narrative richness, stunning visuals, and immersive soundtrack. For an optimal experience, dive into the predecessor and brace yourself for a gaming journey like no other

Playing it on easy mode is recommended, since I dislike the gameplay. Hiding, sneaking, getting detected and killed... Restart, retry. Multiple times. My 2080S was running pretty well in ultra wide, sitting around 60-100fps depending on the level and environment, but had a few fps drops here and there and a couple of crashes. I also will note the loading screens between each level were somewhat long in some instances.The visual and art style was amazing! All the locations looked incredible, especially the bright outdoor ones and going through the towns. An issue I want to point out tho is that I felt like there wasn't enough facial expressions throughout some cutscenes which would've made it that bit more emotional.The soundtrack was outstanding as always.Overall, I loved this series and I do hope the developers consider a trilogy! _childDocuments_.review: I love the first game. It's in my top 5 games (of all time). I even reviewed it on steam (I rarely review games on steam :P). I also absolutely love the sequel. Is it as good as the first? Well...there's good and bad and I'll briefly explain why.I've completed Innocence at least 3 times now and it's one of my favourite games of all time. I loved the bond between Amicia and Hugo and the struggles they had to endure in a bleak and terrible world. The great thing about the first game is that it's quite short. An initial playthrough can last more than 12 hours, even less on repeated runs. That's what made it lovely, short and memorable.The second game continues the story of Amicia and Hugo. The graphics and environment has doubled and it's a treat to witness how much has improved since the first game and how much of the gameplay mechanics have been refined. I loved the fact that they were able to continue their journey and meet more side characters along the way as well.I do feel that the length of the game is both it's strength and weakness. It's pretty much almost doubled in game length (for an initial playthrough, less on repeated runs) than the first game. Half of me wanted to see the game continue just a tiny bit more, the other half wanted the story to be over already.Some parts of the story kept me guessing, others you could see coming a mile off. I loved how the game ended and what transpired from their journey together. I think (personally) the anticipation and hype of this game was probably more than the experience to be honest.Will I play this game again? Definitely.Was it more memorable than the first game. Unfortunately, No.Do I still love it the same? Absolutely.Is it a contender for GOTY? Definitely.Is it my GOTY? Unfortunately, I loved Elden Ring just a tiny bit more.Kudos for creating a sensational and memorable game, tho.Definitely worth checking out!

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting to finish the game before posting a review and now that I have done so... What can I say? What a masterpiece. I don't know how it didn't get more appreciation at the game awards.First of all, I would like to start by mentioning a few things that bothered me a bit, not complaining, just constructive criticism.SPOILER ALERT1. Combat is somewhat clunkier and less enjoyable compared to Innocence. In Innocence you could knock enemy's helmets down with your sling. In this one, you have to use other methods when an enemy wears a helmet. And sometimes, to kill the full armoured guys, you have to use three weapons. Crossbow is really cool though, my favourite weapon so far.2. A bit more of character development of Arnaud and Beatrice would not have hurt. Their deaths were kinda painful, but not as much as the creators expected or wanted us to feel.3. I liked the ending, not gonna lie. But it kinda ruins Amicia and Hugo's whole journey and struggle. In the end, the Order was right and Hugo died as Voudin had predicted he would. They tried so hard to avoid that ending for him, but it happened anyway.On the other hand, the game really excelled on these aspects for me. As I said before, it is a masterpice and a must-play if you're a fan of action-adventure and exploration games:1. The setting. OMG the f... setting. I'm a sucker for medieval games, and this one was really well made. Medieval France is always a good choice when a game takes place in this dark era. The developers nailed it.2. The graphics. Asobo are absolute geniuses when it comes to graphics. They craft landscapes and towns and cities in a masterful way. The alleys, crowded neighbourhoods, the people from this dark era, the clothing.... They didn't miss any detail.3. The story. The story captures you from the very beggining and it's like you're there with Amicia living the same adventures and going through the same hardships as her. It had everything you hoped for in a good story: captivating storytelling, interesting and well written characters, twists everywhere along the tale, abundant violence and death. Again, enthralling and fascinating.4. The characters. They are so well written and masterfully created that they made me feel the same emotions as them. It was like I was experiencing the same pain and grief Amicia was suffering, the same rage when her brother was hurt or in danger, the sadness accompanying Hugo the whole game because of his unintentional destroying nature... For me, Amicia and Hugo were like friends along the way, and it was painful to see their fates unfolded like that in the end.I hope Asobo make a new A Plague Tale game and am sure they will. I also think Amicia deserves to end the trilogy. In what way? I'm not sure but she deserves to be the one at the centre of it, to be her last dance.

_childDocuments_.review: The first game was OK This time they outdone themselves it's good, not much gameplay but it fits so well because the story is wellwritten and you connect with the characters, it's a cute game filled with good sentiment and i think this is their strong suit.Sometimes i told myself it starts to resemble Tomb Raider, and i was like "So what, why not ?" It just works well with what they have. they even added they touches some existing mechanics and it just works so well and i saw they didn't made these improvements redundant but rather short to avoid repetitiveness. Very well thought.Again as the first game the English voice over is on point. I speak 4 languages and French is one of them but the British accent fists super well the actors they have found are really good especially the voice of Hugo (the little boy) just wow he has a cute design and the voice feels so innocent and filled with goodness. :')The music was amazing from start to end, very very very good, amazing work you have done here guys.The map design was beautiful, you added extra filters and effects (particles, fog, etc...) which i'm fond of because so many games started chasing just good graphics when you can embellish a game so much with these. I remember suggesting that in one of my reviews of the last Tomb Raider (Shadow of the TR) which lacked any designer's embellishment touch. And i was astonished seeing the developers that did the previous game Rise of the Tomb Raider which actually had these filters which made if look like it was more realistic to me than the newer game. I don't know maybe a rush game, lack of resources, who knows. Anyways, keep going, you got yourself a Franchise now, and i cannot wait to play the sequel!Good work to everyone in your team, i wish you the best.Few minor inconveniences :-The early game sometimes feels crippled because you don't have the skills/tools so you feel forced to adopt the Stealth mechanics (same as the first game) Example : early game when you have to find Hugo i think i've done that section over 20 times because sometimes the NPC stay stuck trying to find you which make sense, but what's strange is doing nothing to bait the NPC is sometimes just easier which makes you wonder if it's not a bug.- Some of the  armored NPC are invulnerable which is again forcing you to either be lucky and have a knive(s) (but they are not that common) or play it stealth. And only unarmored enemies can be strangled (feels bad moment)- Crafting, i wish you could craft bolt, sure it makes the game easier but i could force you to choose where you put your resources, i don't know i'm afraid if this part is changed it could cascade into worse (i'm not a developer so i won't insist on this part) Every changes has a trade in positive and negative.- Since the game is story driven, it feels bad sometimes to want to explore and fall into a one way drop which cancels the exploring because you have 50/50 chances to either fall onto a chest of equipment or the way to continue the story.It's not annoying or anything but you're like "the 'ohhho' of slight inconvenience/disappointment" and you move on.It sometimes makes you wish to have the firewood spawn of Tomb Raider or similar games to come back there but again it could break the pace of the game and the story-narrative would be as smooth.- Price, forgot to talk about that part, which is important because i felt initially reluctant which is why it took me so long to buy the game. But it was worth the time, 22hours to finish the game (13hours for the previous game)I capitulate and admit that your worked hard and took the time to refine the game which is a big plus especially nowadays in the industry where everything feels rushed. Bravo!

_childDocuments_.review: I am Amicia de Rune, and I bow to no one!I unlocked the combat perks early on because, what can I say, I'm violent in video games. The graphics are top notch, only hindered by some slight bugs here and there, although perhaps it's because I'm playing on a 1080Ti?Music is in a league of its own. The raw emotions you will feel from the score alone only serve to accentuate those you will undoubtedly feel toward the story.And with that comes the meat and taters: The story is worthy of remembrance. An analogy for addiction, the love and bond of brother and sister, all weave together beautifully.  I would give it a 95/100 as certain parts (knock-out sequences) happen far too often, but are very much overshadowed by the overall themes with which the player is drawn into.  You will leave this game changed mentally. The story hit particularly hard for me as I have a family member who has struggled with addiction for many years and the game made me second guess my own choices when it came to supporting them.  Overall, even if you didn't play Innocence, I believe everyone owes it to themselves to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! I was captivated the whole time! Exquisitely rich story telling, sublime voice acting, beautiful art. The game mechanics are not difficult and save points are frequent. First run through took about 28 hours  and there appears to be some "replayability" with increased difficulty (and more opportunities to obtain achievements). If you like a story-rich game with likeable (and despicable) characters that might make you cry, I highly recommend it. Not for those who have a rat/ rodent phobia, obviously or those looking for complex game strategies or puzzles. This game is all about the immersive and sometimes heart-wrenching story of Amicia and Hugo. I plan to give it a second play in French to see if the voice acting is as good.
_childDocuments_.name: A Plague Tale: Requiem

_childDocuments_.review: To start, this is hands down one of, if not the most beautiful game you have yet to play. The story telling is captivating, immersive and profoundly moving. Game mechanics are simple and yet even a seasoned gamer will be challenged. The developers really did an amazing job, making it obvious they aggonized over ever detail, from plot to sound, to game play. If you enjoyed games like the Witcher 3, you will most likely find a new favorite in this title.This is not a button masher, slash and dash style game. It can be unforgiving, requiring forethought, planning and situational awareness to survive. Health bars are non-existent. You basically are one-shot killing or being killed (although there are certain actions to counter a would be demise). This game focuses on stealth, problem solving, with the occasional blood lust rampage opportunity for someone looking to repaint the ground in their favorite shade of scarlet. Just to forewarn you, this is a difficult game to play, even on the easy setting. Dont let that sway your decision though, just be prepared for many "How in actual the F**k do they want me do this?!" moments. It is well worth every second of frustration and challenge! Like I said earlier, this game is very unforgiving on a Dark Souls level.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really reminds me of spec ops the line. At the point in the game that I'm at, the game is showing that what you do in the game matters, and the characters feel reactive to your playstyle.  The story is good, and I'm invested in what actually is going on and all of the characters. I think it is necessary to play the first game however, so the story and characters make sense. Gameplay is good. You can be stealthy and non lethal or be a killin, albeit the melee is a consumable, and the sling won't kill enemies with helmets . There is a skill tree that slowly unlocks new stuff you can do.  Throughout the game there are a variety of different tools you will have access to, which lets you come up with creative solutions to getting through levels. You can extinguish fires or light fires and manipulate enemies and rats into eachother, or you can use the rats to block enemies off from a section of the map, if you're methodical enough. Technically speaking the game runs pretty good on my laptop which is a 3060 and a i7 10750 but I did have to turn off the ray traced stuff as it killed my frames. There is an obscene amount of rats in some sections of the game and it baffles me how many moving rodents they can render on the screen. Even if it's faked the devs did a really good job making it look perfect and still run really well on a midrange laptop.

_childDocuments_.review: A Plague Tale: Requiem is an emotionally charged, visually stunning, and narratively rich experience. From the moment you step into the world of Amicia and Hugo de Rune, you are drawn into a harrowing journey of survival, sacrifice, and familial love amidst a plague-ridden medieval landscape.The storytelling is where Requiem truly shines. It beautifully blends a dark, emotional narrative with moments of hope and tenderness. The relationship between Amicia and her younger brother Hugo is at the heart of the game, and the voice acting is exceptional, making their bond feel genuine and compelling. The way the story delves deeper into their struggles as they try to escape the horrors of the Inquisition, disease, and supernatural forces is both heartbreaking and gripping.Visually, the game is a masterpiece. The attention to detail in the environments—whether it’s the decaying villages, lush forests, or terrifying swarms of rats—is breathtaking. The lighting and textures enhance the atmosphere, creating an immersive world that feels alive, even in its bleakest moments. The use of color to contrast the beauty of the world with the underlying dread is incredibly effective.Gameplay in Requiem balances stealth, puzzle-solving, and action seamlessly. The stealth mechanics are more refined, and there is greater variety in how you can approach situations. The introduction of new tools and abilities makes each encounter feel fresh, and the puzzles are cleverly designed to challenge players without being frustrating. The tension of evading enemies and navigating through rat-infested areas keeps you on edge, but the game also offers moments of calm to appreciate the depth of its world-building.The soundtrack deserves special mention. It heightens every moment of tension, sadness, and triumph with hauntingly beautiful compositions that linger long after you've finished playing.In conclusion, A Plague Tale: Requiem is an unforgettable experience. It blends a captivating narrative, outstanding visuals, and refined gameplay to create a game that is both emotionally impactful and mechanically rewarding. It’s a triumph of storytelling in gaming and one that will stay with players for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Rats... RATS!? RAAAAAATS!!!This game compared o the prequel is more chaotic... but let's resumé my experience about this game:Ok, I'll say this first. If someone to decide to make a drama/horror movie about "A Plague Tale: Requiem" with the actual cutscenes and the dialogues in game you would made a pretty good movie. While there are some minor details that you can tweak or disagree, the overall story is great.Anyways, moving to the story. I could describe the events per to per and tell you what happen, but since I don't like giving spoilers or be spoiled (even the names), all I will I say is the following: The story is about two siblings trying to find the cure for the younger one's disease, but in order to do that they'll have to overcome diverse obstacles, facing more ferocious enemies, and they have to make some harder choices in order to survive. I would point out that this game on your first playthrough, the story will have some outcomes that will leave you intrigued, shocked, etc (this I won't define exactly because it depends on each indiviual and not solely on me).About the gameplay, this game offers you so many options on how you pass a certain sections. While some puzzles you have to find the logic answer, in certain sections (let's say "combat zones) you can do whatever you please. If you want go sneak sneak, you can do it, if you want to obliterate anyone you can, you can choose how you want to approach basically. Also I want to stand out that if you want to do 100% like I did you'll have to do 2 playthroughs to unlock the levelling achievements (you'll know which when you start playing).If you want to know more about the story about what happened before, I would also suggest you buy the prequel "A Plague Tale: Innocence" or watch on YT to have more depth about the story telling in this one.Overall, (and I'm sorry if I'll sound biased, but that's on I like this game) if you ask me if you should buy this game, I wouldn't even blink and say yes to that question, because the story itself will hook you into the screen and the gameplay itself is actually solid.

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion this is a better game than the first one. Contrary to other reviews I have seen, the game ran flawlessly for me at Ultra max settings with no crashes or performance issues whatsoever. In fact, in a 2022 year which saw more games released broken or bugged than any other year I can remember, this was one of the better releases.The game is much longer than the original (which is a positive) and much more immersive. The visuals are impressive, the story is great and the combat has been slightly improved but nothing drastically different to the first game. There are skippable cutscenes which is always a bonus. At times there were slightly too long periods which saw you experiencing no combat and too much dialogue and walking, but overall its a small gripe and the game is balanced well. The characters are good, the setting and scenery is amazing and there is a nice twist at the end.For the 100% achievement hunters, make sure as an absolute priority over everything else that you focus on your Opportunistic Skill in your first playthrough. This will drastically reduce the time you need spend in playing your 2nd playthrough by a lot of hours. You do not need to complete 2 playthroughs, but you will need to replay some of the game again in order to max out your 3 skills which is impossible to do in one playthrough.The opportunistic skill requires you to kill 50%-60% of all enemies in each section of the game using any method you like. In a section with 6 enemies, you must kill at least 3 or 4 of them but not all. In a section with 15 enemies you must kill at least 6-8 of them but not more than that etc etc. Once you see the checkpoint symbol appear after a section with enemies, check your Opportunistic Skill and if it hasn't moved up, replay that entire section again. This will be your biggest grind if you don't focus on this particular skill from the get go. The other 2 skills are easy. Upgrading your crossbow to maximum lets you recover your bolts from dead enemies which makes going for the Aggressive skill very easy.Overall it is well worth a play if you liked the original.

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed the first entry in this series and my excitement when finally getting around to playing this title was at an all time high. I fear as though those expectations may have tainted my experience a bit and my shaky memory on the actual game-play of the original game may also have skewed my play-through. While this game does built upon many of the mechanics presented in the first game in a great way I found that my main issues with this game stemmed from its midsection which unfortunately housed the longest set of chapters in regards to playtime. While some of the experimental changes in the combat and stealth formats resulted in a lot of my favorite sequences both narrative and game-play wise I found myself becoming increasingly bored and agitated at times. This was due to the slow as ever walking pace some of the sections have that you are unable to avoid. i understand that some of them are necessary for dialog but for there to be more of those sections than not in the most lengthy section of the game just takes you out of the experience. Another huge drawback to these sections for me was the fact that even with the slow walking pace if you continue forward without any stray from the path or pause you are likely to trigger the next dialog sequence before the first one even finished with was even more frustrating. These sections were also usually the darkest sections of the game from a visual perspective and the fact that the fires did not effect the corners of the room and I felt the need to walk into those dark sections of rooms in order to not miss something just for there to not only be nothing but to not illuminate until I was standing directly in that area was also a huge frustration. All that being said the story and this world are still extremely enjoyable and the characters in this game are just as well fleshed out as in the previous game. Despite my issues with some of the sections I still found this title to be a great blend of stealth combat and narrative. Jesus gives this 6.4/10 burgers.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stellar game. Even tho I liked the first one, this is just miles better. Great graphics (legit one of the most gorgeous games I've ever laid eyes upon), amazing mocap (unlike some other AAA games (looking at you, Assassin's Creed)), nice gameplay, compelling characters and a nice story.2 things I'd like to highlight among my praise: The characters (especially Hugo) and the puzzles.Usually games make me really dislike children because they're always portrayed as the most annoying element in a 100km radius. Not with Hugo though. He is a child, and definitely doesn't come off as older than that, but he still feels like a whole character that doesn't get on your nerves - imo they did an outstanding job in writing a likeable child (God of War did this far worse imo). The other characters also feel extremely coherent, which I feel isn't the norm anymore. So I really appreciate that we have characters that actually act like real humans would.Then there are the puzzles. They aren't really that difficult but the developers added an option to make these puzzles a bit easier or harder. They achieved this by simply letting your companions tell you what you should do. I'm beyond happy that this is an option because with alot of modern gaming titles, I felt they pretended I'm an idiot (looking at you again, God of War! Seriously, those 2 games are awful in this regard) while playing who can't solve the most basic puzzles. Here, if the puzzles are hard, you can turn the option on to have them tell you what to do more often or off if you want to solve a puzzle in peace. Really, from the bottom of my heart, thank you to the devs for *not* treating me like an idiot, I greatly appreciate this.All in all, this is a great game. I buy very very few titles at their full price but this one really deserved it.

_childDocuments_.review: It finally arrived, the sequel to the game about Rat Boi and the girl with a sling that might as well be shooting 5.56 NATO. The first game moved a couple million copies, it deserved to move 200 million.Usually this is where I'd do an intro of some sorts but, if you are like me, you have no time for that nonsense. You have a burning question, an inquiry of most importance, if you will, that needs answering above any other..."Mr. BudgieGaming, how is the murdering in this one compared to the first game?"And yeah, I get why you would wanna know. After all, that's how the first game won the most trigger happy of us over, with a glorious mission in an English camp that revealed that the game wasn't only a stealth puzzler, but also someone's very specific interactive manifesto on the true power of slingers in the Middle Ages. Well, I'm happy to announce, there's a whole new cornucopia of ways to make those frenchmen pay for their sins of joining the army and wanting to own land in the normandies. If the first game peeked into sweet lethality while never fully indulging in it, like that friend of yours who said they hate anime but watched Attack On Titan because "it's the only good one"; then this sequel is straight up just dunking its head in that lethality, just like how that friend of yours ended up binging Komi can't Communicate two weeks later.Not only does Amicia upgrade her 5.56 sling to a 50 cal crossbow at some point, but she can now take certain enemies in melee and can even learn to use ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥  . At some points, it definitely delivers on the experience of a medieval Last of Us, only with poor conscripted provençals playing the part of cordyceps infected. You would think that there would be more of a difference between killing soulless monsters and killing fungi zombies, but you will verbally smack 'em down after a stealth strangling just the same.The best part of all that, is the way they have approached rewards based on style of play. I still resent Dishonored for punishing me for going the lethal way, like, what was I supposed to do, not style on the ♥♥♥♥♥ with my cool ninja powers and fire arrows? But there is none of that nonsense going on in Plague Tale Requiem, no sir. If you opt to redecorate the environment with the burning and half devoured corpses of the locals, guess what? You get upgrades to help you do it even better next time! The game barely cares about how you choose to approach the situation, aside from some admonishing comments from certain NPCs. Especially Lucas, he's constantly going, "oh no Amicia, don't kill those murderous psychopaths! that's bad!" Shut up, you Timothée-Chalamet-on-coke looking ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, you make me wish that there was friendly fire in this game.But, no matter how absorbed you are in your glorious impersonation of a medieval Predator, there is something that will put pause to your rampage, often. And that is, how the game looks. It looks  . It looks so good, that it is probably illegal to show screenshots of it in some countries. Somehow they improved on the lighting effects and the athmosphere of the first game, while improving its biggest weak point, the facial animations. They actually emote well now! In fact, they do it great! Some characters, especially Amicia and Arnaud, look absolutely top of the line. And, just you wait until you get to the sections where you walk around towns with all the people and huge amounts of unique objects everywhere. Jesus.But this is PC, so of course we have to talk about one of the most disliked effects in the PC space... Chromatic abherration. As you probably already know, the first game went (being generous here) a tad too hard on the effect, while offering no setting to disable it on release. I chalked it up to Amicia being canonically, perennially drunk, she comes from the land of wine after all. Anyways, that has been, thankfully, corrected in this one: Not only does it have a setting, it also offers a halfway option between Off and Full, for those who don't mind the effect when it is used subtly. I can confirm that the Full effect, especially on the second half of the game, goes basically as hard on the abherration as it did on the first game. I'd say I can imagine some people getting slightly disoriented or uncomfortable with the effect in full, so I'd recommend rolling on Low. I played it with Full CA and enjoyed it, but I also have a positive review of Resident Evil 6, so it's not like you can trust in my taste.With those crazy production values and the relatively moderate length and content of the first game, I was expecting merely another good, moderate length linear game out of this. So you can imagine my surprise when it ended up being basically twice as long as the first game. Which is great, in theory...But.In many games, a longer length ends up eventually working against them. Either because the novelty of the stuff you can do wears off, or because the length ruins the pacing of the narrative. In my opinion, both of those happened to this game to a degree, unfortunately. That's the only negative part of being a highly efficient medieval Terminator I guess, eventually, you sleepwalk in your last couple of encounters with the enemies, in no small part due to how absurdly overpowered some of the upgrades can get. You can somewhat compensate for this by playing on Hard to try to put a bit more emphasis on the resource management, I'm kinda wishing I did, honestly. But if I had done that I couldn't have challenged myself to see how many multikills I could get with medieval napalm, so I guess that evens it out.As for the narrative, unfortunately a combination of the length and very unfortunate structuring makes the story nosedive on the second half. However, the first part had so much momentum coming out of its ass, that it had been rocketed to the stratosphere before it started plummeting, so the game ends before it can crash into the ground. I'd go as far as to say that the game salvages the story overall at the end, although I can see how many would argue against that. But opinions are like soldiers after they bump into you in this game: There are a lot of them, and all of them are full of holes.All in all, I could sit here for a while listing all the ways in which I feel this game improved upon the promise of the first (like the wide combat arenas with lots of options and resources to loot, the rebalancing of puzzles that allow you to use your resources and tools as shortcuts if you don't want to find the optimal solution...) but that is a point in itself. The fact that, as any good sequel should, this game took the bones and shortcomings of the first game, and smartly delivered on the potential it had with greater production values and more resources, while correcting its negative aspects wherever it could. Yes there are still issues, and not insignificant, but there's great potential in this series if it continues and this sequel was an excellent showing of them intending to deliver on that.And most importantly, it sure looked cool when I tricked that fool into burning three of his friends in a bush with a XIV century grenade.

_childDocuments_.review: I love and hate this game.  I love the visual design and world building.  Truly impressive setting, incredible environments, and really interesting story (if a bit broken and stuffed with a lot of filler).  Some of the "run why things fall apart" sequences are really fun.I hate the stealth and combat.  It's clumsy, slow and just doesn't feel intuitive.  It really makes some of the encounters really frustrating and a lot more difficult then they should be.  It also has a brutal checkpoint system in many places forcing you to redo a lot of stuff over, including conversations and cutscenes.You can tell there are a lot of things they just added to extend the game because there are either back to back repeats of of certain types of gameplay with generic dialog, or extended cutscenes that offer little to the progress of the story.  (How many times are we going to see the protagonists get hurt from combat or falling or whatever and limp around for 5 minutes asking if everyone is alright - the answer is A LOT. LOTS LOTS LOTS ([Lara Croft doesn't fall and get hurt this much).They also use a lot of tropes that really suck like the painfully slow "I have to go five miles but I can only limp" and the "ooh, bent reality and things are blurry for ten minutes while I wander around just so exposition can be relayed" with a bit of "hey, were's gonna make you do this exact same thing over and over and over because ♥♥♥♥ you, that's why".Oh, and you walk for about 3/4 of the game.  You can sprint...but only is the devs say you can.  So much forced walking.  It's as much of a walking simulator as a 3D action game.It's ending is also anti-climatic, like three or four times.  And the narrative feels like it works against itself a lot, but it's still a fascinating concept.Still, this is a gorgeous game with a great world and great story that stumbles from a clunky steallth/combat system and some boring, unnecessary filler.

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece in storytelling. This game continues Amecia's and Hugo's journey from the the original, leading the player on an emotional and thrilling journey, filled with danger, hope, joy, and tragedy. The gameplay has been improved from the original by encouraging different approaches to  gameplay, including some familiar, and some new weapons and equipment. The maps are little more open which encourages exploration with chests to discover and optional collectables and memories to find. With the added content and longer story players can look forward to putting in many more hours compared to the original. The haunting and almost sorrowful music adds another layer to the narrative and what's happening on screen. Both new and familiar characters were well voiced and interesting. I only ran into one major bug that prevented progression and which forced me to restart a particular section of a chapter midway through the game. Any other bugs were so small it's hardly worth mentioning. I will mention one thing which annoyed me, however, which was the lip sync was off quite noticeably when compared to the original when characters were talking, although it was only noticeable if you focus on the lips. This proved a little distracting and immersion breaking for me, particularly in an emotional scene. Aside from that, this game was an excellent sequel. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: A Plague Tale: Requiem is, in my humble opinion, the rare sequel that tops the original. And I ADORE the original.Where Innocence shines through simplicity and restraint, Requiem is longer, bigger and often even better. It juggles far more moving parts and manages to make them come together as a cohesive whole. The bigger scope occasionally makes it less focused, more uneven, and the higher stakes make one or two sections feel grandiose compared to Innocence’s understated style. But make no mistake: Requiem is still an intensely emotional, beautifully human tale, and it has affected me in a way very few stories have. I wish I could tell you more about how natural the characters feel, how much the themes permeate all aspects of the game, all of the little setups and payoffs, the intimate moments, the good times and the bad…but I’d just spoil things for you. Please, play this.Gripping, thematically rich story that builds well on the events and character development of Innocence-	I had A LOT of trouble putting this down, which almost never happensExcellent and nuanced character writing, near-perfect character performances-	You get less companions, but more quality time with them compared to Innocence. Each brings their own energy and skillset to the groupJaw-dropping soundtrack that builds on the old and brings in the new, accompanied by immersive but unobtrusive sound designStunning presentation with plenty of colours, landmarks, vistas and other natural varietyExpanded gameplay with minor quality-of-life tweaks and improved AI-	Most enemies now take 2 hits to kill Amicia instead of 1, giving you a chance to fight back-	All ammunition types can now be combined with all delivery methods, giving you vastly more options-	Materials are much more concentrated in chests, so while exploring and checking nooks is still beneficial, you’re less likely to miss materials because they were sitting around in a small box-	Upgrade materials and ammo materials are now separate—no need to hold back on using either-	A new skill system tracks your playstyle for each section and levels up one of 3 skill lines automatically. However, they’re designed to max out before the end of the game if you focus too much on one approach. This is a marriage of character development and game design: you MUST adapt to the current situation like Amicia does, doing everything you can to survive-	There are more enemies and they’ll remain on guard once you’ve been fully spotted once, pushing you out of your stealth bubble-	Companions are now invisible to enemiesVery few bugs encountered on my endAccessibility and difficulty options exist—nothing as advanced as certain AAA-games, but much better than InnocenceA handful of voice lines feel stitched together from different takes. This is rare considering the sheer quantity of lines, but when it happens, you notice itMany of the tools and tricks you get are front-loaded; it might’ve been good if the game spread them more. The upside is that the areas don’t hold back when it comes to giving you optionsBecause you’re allowed to stealth a lot, Requiem doesn’t always teach you how to defeat certain enemy types, or at least not well. This is an issue during a few chapters that force you into a head-on fight. However, I very much like the increased variety—and quality—of enemy types compared to InnocenceFacial animations and lip sync are much improved, but still lag behind the overall presentation in scenes where they haven’t been touched up (in scenes where they HAVE been, they look great)Rarely, an enemy will bug out and either walk against a wall (making sneaking easier) or turn around rapidly over and over (making sneaking harder)The French-sounding accents from Innocence were dialed back. This allows the voice actors to be more expressive—and they absolutely are, so I think it’s worth the tradeoffSome sections are hard as balls to pacifist-stealth through. Remember: adapt to the situation, don’t be stubborn like I wasPerformance is reported to not always be great for people (I never encountered this, because I upgraded my PC to play Requiem)

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. After the first one “Innocence” turned out to be a surprise for me, since I never though I would play it (because I was scared of rats) and it wasn’t like that at all, I had fun with it and I had great hopes for A Plague tale Requiem. Innocence showed me that it wasn’t just rats. There was a place for some light and beauty among the darkness. There was also some color, and it was because of it, those moments, every time something like that appeared, it was special and beautiful, but very much in tone with the rest of the game. Gameplay was another surprise, the game was not only about stealth, you were given some tools and chemical gadgets to help you along the way. You would have some choices on how to advance each level creatively and because of that the gameplay never felt dull.Requiem visually and technically is so much better than innocence, it is quite possibly one of the best-looking games of 2022. The cast is excellent, Charlotte McBurney as the voice of Amicia and Logan Hannan as Hugo are, as before, the secret sauce of these games. They are the emotional reason you do what you do in game.  They are not alone in their journey though, as there are great supporting characters such as Sophia, Arnaud and Lucas from the previous game too which are all very well done and make the voice cast in this game one of the best. It is a shame then, that the motion capture is not done with the same cast but with different actors which are good themselves, but felt sometimes somewhat distant from the “voice performance” similar to watching a dubbed film. The music finally is emotional and timeless, really a beautiful piece. Another noticeable difference between this game and the first one. Amicia’s voice doesn’t have French accent anymore (speaking about the original English cast) which is strange since Charlotte did such a great English “French accent” in the first game (which is almost never the case in other games). It was one of the reasons I liked her performance so much. After hearing her voice for hours like that it  is somewhat confounding to hear her with an English accent. Still her performance goes to incredible high emotional moments this time, so much more than in the first game.It is here then, that comes one of the big flaws for me, which is the writing. While the story for the second game is interesting where it wants to go (in principle), I think the way it handles it, it is not good, and the way characters are dealt with…. not good either.I liked Amicia in the first game as a character, but in Requiem I ended up not liking her very much. I understand she’s obsessed with finding a cure for her brother and feels very strong and passionate about it. Also, she’s dealing with incredible emotional distress for sure…But in terms of writing she’s just going blindly from point A to point B without much reason, ditching suddenly important characters that were accompanying her for like half the game “just because” or probably because the game now needs to introduce this new cool character and can’t come up with a good reason for it. It’s not that there are no reasons for Amicia not to like someone anymore or change company, but the way it is handled (and the reasons themselves) are poorly written, and it begins to show off just too much. So, the narrative loses any credibility, and you start to see the game behind the scenes pulling the strings, saying “ok, now we need this, please ♥♥♥♥ off this character, we don’t want it anymore, now put this other new character, we don’t care why, just put it”. And it feels like that for most of the game. This reaches even some of the more dramatic moments of the game, which are very grand and powerful, acting wise, but story wise are very much stitched together barely hanging out.This problem with story was sadly made worse with gameplay elements which this time, didn’t worked that well for me. The mechanics are mostly the same as the first game, with new elements of course. The new elements are good, especially the chasing scenes were very well done. But in general terms I had frustratingly annoying moments here and there trying to advance in certain levels which were not fun to play. And the frustrating part was finding out that it wasn’t a difficulty problem but just that i wasn’t doing what I was supposed to be doing, or going where I was supposed to be going. The game failed in communicating clearly what it wanted the player to do and that affected gameplay.For these reasons although Requiem has some incredible music, visuals, a great voice casting and some good gaming moments, it is finally a mixed bag and sometimes a struggle to play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game broke me.TL;DR: Overall, 9.5/10. After about 19 hours in the game, I can say Plague Tale: Requiem is worth playing for its story and beautiful, immersive world - possibly the new high standard for games. And incredible, inspiring, unforgettable characters, of course. :)Story: 10/10World: 10/10Characters: 10/10User Interface: 10/10Gameplay & Controls: 9/10Graphics & Sound Design: 10/10Mobs: 8/10Bug-free: 9/10STORY: Devastating. Beautiful. So engaging. I love the protagonists and the writing really is very good. They interweave not only the wonder and innocence of childhood but also the pain, fear, and responsibility of adulthood - great adult writing. I've not played the first one but I will be once I'm done since this one is so good. Makes me want to know about their first journey!WORLD: Beautiful. Just gorgeous. Definitely a AAA game, and possibly the most beautiful I've seen in a long while. Not to mention it's set in Mediterranean France, which is quite possibly the most picturesque place on Earth. The design and attention to detail is astounding. One of my favorite parts was the faire in the first city we arrive in, where I found myself wandering and exploring just for the fun of it, as if I were really there. Astounding quality and immersion.CHARACTERS: Very real feeling - in dialogue, antimations, logic, and personality. I love the brother-sister (and really, mother-son) dynamic between Amicia and Hugo, and the supportive role Lucas plays for Amicia. It's so much fun and makes me feel very connected to them. Can't stand the mother, which is why it's good writing (lol). I also like that they wrote a strong female protagonist without making her toxic - she's strong, yes, but also human. She feels, and she has fears and even has a panic attack at one point, but she perseveres to save her brother in spite of all that. Very real.UI: Beautifully nonexistent. Of course it shows up when you need it, like in combat so you can choose your weapons, etc., but otherwise it's so nice and clean. I get to see the world, the characters, and everything happening without anything getting in my way. Perfectly done.GAMEPLAY & CONTROLS: Controls feel really good, a little like Hogwarts Legacy or RDR2 but more natural. However, this is a stealth-heavy game in places. If sneaking, avoiding detection, and not being able to really fight like in an RPG are your thing, definitely get this game. Even though that's not my playstyle, though, I still had fun. I kind of pushed through the combat/evasion pieces to get back to the story, but that's just me. It's mostly a story-driven game, though, so it wasn't too bad for me. It's just the few places where you have to sneak that are annoyingly full of rats and guards.Photo Mode is actually a pretty cool concept. I had fun taking photos in the woods or wherever I thought was beautiful, though the controls were a bit awkward.GRAPHICS & SOUND DESIGN: Lovely! Like I said, the world is beautiful - possibly the most beautiful game I've seen with its combination of textures + lighting + animations - and on ultra settings it runs smoothly for me even on a hard drive. This is a new standard for realistic games. The voice acting is great, sound quality is great (can even hear the tinny echo of soldiers' voices in their helmets), and I LOVE the soundtrack. Really moves me.MOBS: Nothing interesting. There is variance between enemies you have to fight or evade, but it's mostly rats and guards, which are rather boring. Could be some improvement there, just so I don't get bored when the fights start. Again, the combat isn't the focus of this game, so it's not a huge issue. Just know that if you're looking for a game with interesting things to fight, this isn't it.BUGS: None game breaking that I've found, only a couple visual bugs that resolved themselves immediately or weren't distracting. Just know that it's a pretty heavy memory and graphics hog, so make sure you meet the specs and maybe download it on an M.2 or SSD rather than HDD like I did. Game kept crashing - but an SSD should be fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Well. 12 hours to complete it. Do I think is a good game, yes. (No spoilers) Do I think the ending makes sense? Yes, it is. heartbreaking but the only way after what happens. Do I think is worth it at the moment? Sadly no. The performance is all over the place and to really enjoy the game you need it to at least be stable which is not unless to fiddle with the settings quite a bit and you are willing to make sacrifices if you have a lower gpu. I played the game in 21:9, 3440x1440 at 60 fps with several performance issues along the way but smooth roads in between, this is of course with DLSS activated in balance or performance. First time you encounter the rats in the game performance will be terrible (chapter 2) and the end of chapter 4 is a slide show. Stutter is your enemy in this game more than the rats. Even with a 3080, playing this game is a challenge and you can'y expect people to buy the 4090, or the new 4080 when they release, just to play this game by using force power to overcome this badly optimised game.The story is a bit of a repeat in terms of character arc but evolves into its new thing 1/3 into the game. Many people is complaining about the ending. It think it makes sense. It is a hard choice to make, but one that makes sense and at that point I believe it was the only way to go.I think the game is worth it and I like it a lot but the gameplay forces you to sometimes fight when the gameplay is not fully design for it. I'm sorry but I am a soldier and my enemy only has a sling, I would take cover and charge my way to Amicia to take her down, I would not just walk to her slowly. There are many times where rats are not around but soldiers are and they just walk to you when they detect you. Yes you can fight but resources in some areas are limited and you need specific ones to defeat some enemies so your only choice is to run to the exit of the section you currently are. I can forgive you take me out of combat and force me to run because you are after all, still a child even if Amicia is a capable one. But you give me a crossbow at some point, you want me to fight and yet you still hold me down. You give me infinite rocks for the sling, but you make more and more enemies wear helmets or full armor. And I can say the same for the other alchemy tools at your disposal. It is a never ending cycle.Requiem is a really good game that can only be fully enjoyed if you were not so worried about destroying your gpu with the bad performance. Should people buy it? Yes, when most people can play it. When 60 fps, 100% stable is a thing for people, then yes please. Go ahead an buy it, it is a good story, one that is hard to see its conclusion but one that makes sense. For me, it was mostly smooth, but I have a beast a PC that most people don't have and is just not fair for those people if I say: " go ahead and buy it!" and until this game gets some work done, I won't say it.

_childDocuments_.review: When I started in PC gaming back in the day, many years ago on a CRT and co-axial LAN cables; there were a lot of amazing titles created – kudos to each one. Amazing details were focused on in each game, from the anxiety of escaping the mentally insane in Outlast or the sudden startling of the paranormal in F.E.A.R and the conflicting moments of Fahrenheit and Max Payne. But never in my life have I experienced each emotional chord so perfectly played as in A Plaque Tale – Requiem.At first the game play was somewhat different from the RPG norm and was something to get used to, and for some reason my Corsair 5000X with all the glorious fan RGB did not work with the iCue feature of the game, so I fiddled about an hour to fix it – but at the end I got so involved in this game that the LED effects were the least of my concern. This is not your open world RPG game with millions of quests and billions of stuff to carry in your bag with infinite capacity and all the stuff that goes with that. No, this is a real story playing through your emotions and with your finger tips on the keyboard; taking charge of one of the World’s most important quests. Of course you are allowed to wander – which you should do to pick up the hidden items to make your quest more bearable and to add that special emotions to cut scenes. Also the “level up” is no distribution of points but rather the evolution of your game play, increasing feats in your style of play. So as a dad gamer, who plays part time after spending time with my kids especially my energetic little boy, I savoured every bit of breath taking scenery and amazing visual effects (Hence the review so long after the release).  Where you are the one who carries this little boy’s (Hugo) life in your hands (see the emotional connection here), passing through the most beautiful valleys and in the next moment thrown into the darkness of oblivion, with a master piece sound track that only plays so much sweeter with the emotional chords. Play this game with at least a 32” monitor at 1440p to savour the beauty – 7.1 surround also adds that touch. As I lived myself into this game I kept on saying: “When this is done, I’ll definitely start it straight away, again – it is amazing!” Yet, after the end I decided it was just right – the emotions are so deep, let it rest. For now I am done, maybe again in the future. Kudos to the developers, studios, actors and every one – the first game in my 25 years of PC gaming that brought a tear to my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: A Plague Tale: Requiem is a third person adventure game, and is the sequel to A Plague Tale: Innocence. The story continues a short time after the end of the original game, and is once again focused on player character Amicia De Rune and her younger brother Hugo.When the plague infecting Hugo reawakens and summons more swarms of deadly rats, Amicia must try to find a cure before the rats devour her brother and everyone around him.•	Throughout their journey, Amicia and her companions will be attacked by swarms of rats, and enemy soldiers who want to use Hugo’s power for their own agenda.•	Amicia’s main weapon is a sling which can throw rocks and other special types of ammunition crafted from raw materials.•	Basic soldiers armed with swords or bows can easily be headshotted with a single rock, but stronger soldiers equipped with a helmet, shield, or heavy armour are more difficult to kill. Later in the game you’ll find a crossbow which is more powerful, and unlock the ability to craft fire bombs, but of course you’ll often be outnumbered by several enemies, and your weapons’ rate of fire is slow.•	It might be safer to use stealth to avoid enemies entirely. You can hide in long grass, crouch behind low walls, and distract soldiers by throwing objects to make a noise.•	Rats are scared of fire, so you’ll need to throw ignifer at flammable objects to create safe areas. By themselves the rats are pretty easy to deal with, because as long as you’re close to fire they can’t hurt you. They only really cause a problem when soldiers are in the same area because the safe path through the swarm might not be very stealthy.•	However, sometimes the rats can be used to your advantage. Most soldiers carry torches to keep the rats away, but you can use extinguish ammo to put out the fire and cause the rats to kill them for you.•	During some sections, Amicia will be followed by a companion who can be ordered to use their special ability to assist, for example a soldier whose sword and shield makes him strong in melee combat, and a pirate  who can create a distraction by using a mirror to set fire to grass.•	While progress through the story is linear, each area feels much more open than the original game, with multiple potential routes to take. You can also explore to find secret areas containing crafting materials, which can be used to upgrade your weapons.•	Normal difficulty is nicely balanced. I died more often than I’d like, but I still made steady progress. And honestly a lot of my deaths were my own fault because I’m not always very patient in stealth games, so during the second half of the game I learned to just slow down and take less risks.•	The story is very well written and features many interesting characters. While the story is focused on Amicia’s personal quest to save Hugo, the plague also poses a greater threat to the world as the massive swarms of rats can quickly destroy entire cities. •	Amicia is a very likeable protagonist. You can see how much she cares about her brother,  and how she feels guilty for killing enemies, even when she had no choice.•	Voice acting is excellent.•	Cinematic cutscenes are high quality, although the lip syncing during conversations could be better.•	Requiem took me 17 hours to complete, which is significantly longer than Innocence.•	Controls are fully rebindable and work well with mouse and keyboard.•	Graphics look fantastic as you travel from towns and cities crowded by people and animals, through wide open and colourful countryside, and down into dark underground caverns.•	The framerate was mostly smooth with most settings maxed at 1440p, although I did notice a couple of annoying issues.•	The camera doesn’t always pan smoothly sideways like most games. It seems to stick briefly when focused on certain nearby objects or points of interest, which gives the feeling of framerate stutters, even though the framerate is stable. •	I also noticed quite a few short stutters when the game auto saved at the start of some sections.•	The game crashed to desktop once (no error message), and a couple of times when moving to a new area (when you have to interact with an object to lift and squeeze through a narrow gap), my companion bugged out which prevented me from progressing, but fortunately because of those autosaves I only had to replay a couple of minutes.A Plague Tale: Requiem is an excellent game which has enjoyable gameplay and one of the best stories I’ve played in a video game for a long time. Even though there are a few minor technical issues which the developers really should attempt to fix, I still rate the game as a must play.As the story continues directly after Plague Tale: Innocence, you should definitely play that game first.

_childDocuments_.review: Very much more of the same, so if you enjoyed the first game you will very likely enjoy this one. The game world itself looks gorgeous. The movement animations can sometime look rather janky and the npc modles themselves look very dated and low effort. A last small annoyance I have is the protag talking to herself so much, now and then I can understand, but she just doesn't shut up. That said, I have had no technical issues and the game runs fine and smooth for me at max settings on a 3070ti. The max my GPU temp hit was 53 °C, my CPU temp never went over 40 °C so I wouldn't say the game is that demanding as others have.I'm only half way through the game I believe, so unless the chapters following stretch out further, I don't feel it is bigger than the first game.  I could be wrong, will come back and edit if so. We gives it 8/10 yes-yes!

_childDocuments_.review: "A Plague Tale: Requiem" continues the saga with the same atmospheric brilliance that made its prequel, "Innocence," a standout title. As a fan of the first game, I couldn't wait to dive back into the haunting world crafted by Asobo Studio, and I'm pleased to say that Requiem exceeds expectations.Pros:Compelling Narrative: The storytelling in Requiem is as enthralling as ever. The characters, particularly Amicia and Hugo, continue to evolve, and the mysteries surrounding the plague and the Inquisition are expertly woven into the plot.Stunning Visuals: The graphical fidelity of Requiem is remarkable. The detailed environments, lighting effects, and the portrayal of the plague-ridden landscape are nothing short of breathtaking. It truly adds to the immersion.Emotional Impact: The emotional resonance from the first game persists in Requiem. The bond between characters is beautifully portrayed, and the voice acting is top-notch, drawing players deeper into the narrative.Innovative Gameplay: The gameplay mechanics maintain the delicate balance between stealth, puzzle-solving, and narrative exploration. The integration of new elements keeps things fresh without straying too far from what made the first game enjoyable.Cons:Pacing Issues: At times, the pacing feels a bit uneven. While the story unfolds beautifully, there are moments where it seems to rush or linger, impacting the overall flow.Minor Repetition: Some gameplay elements may feel a tad repetitive, especially for those who played the original. However, the captivating story compensates for any perceived monotony.Conclusion:"A Plague Tale: Requiem" is a worthy successor, captivating players with its narrative depth, visual prowess, and emotional impact. Despite minor pacing and repetition concerns, the overall experience is a testament to Asobo Studio's commitment to delivering a compelling and atmospheric gaming journey. If you enjoyed "Innocence," Requiem is a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: great story & characters, solid gameplay, great graphics; performance issuesStory------The game continues the story of Innocence, playing a few months after. It is strictly linear like the first one, with no lengthy distractions. Which is a good thing, because the story gets pretty intense from time to time. However, there are a lot of relaxed moments to balance it out, and even some longer segments where the focus is just enjoying the environments instead of fighting or stealthing. Parts of the story are often still predictable, but less than in the previous game (you might want to look out for spoilers). The characters and their relationships are fleshed out further, and in my opinion they act more naturally.Overall the story feels pretty fresh and manages to improve over the previous game a good amount. I needed about 20 hours for a slow and thorough playthrough.Gameplay-----------The gameplay is a step up from the previous game. Battle environments feel bigger and more varied. There are more things in the environment to use, and just more things you can do in general. Most items from the first game make a comeback. The sling can still be used, as well as throwing items by hand stealthily. A big change is the crossbow, where its arrows can also be combined with other items to create various effects. Additionally you can now combine all the items with pots as well, to create a more potent form of the item. Another big change is Hugo, who can now help the fight by highlighting enemies and controlling rats. This can be used as a weapon, but also strategically to remove rats from a specific location.Companions work like in the previous game; they have individual skills that may help in battle or traversing the map. But this is not a huge thing in terms of gameplay; they are mainly there for the story. Other than that there are some escape scenes or stealth scenes that mix up the gameplay a little more.Difficulty & Balancing-----------------------While I found Innocence to be a little easy, the normal difficulty in Requiem felt exactly right to me. The fights were engaging, but not unfair. However there are some lengthy battles without checkpoints that might get a little frustrating.There are many hidden stashes or collectibles to be found. If you go out of your way to search for secrets, you are usually rewarded. One thing to note is that maybe 2/3 through the game, there are suddenly a ton of items to be found, and my inventory was full constantly. You go through a ton of items during longer battles, but that still didn't balance it out.Graphics----------Definitely the best-looking game I have played this year, and that is saying a lot, because I played it on low settings (see below for a remark on performance). Even considering that, I frequently stopped to admire the scenery. There are many different environments to see in this game. Some of the rat scenes look simply insane.Characters models look better than in the previous game, and Amicia's design evolves over the course of the story.Photo Mode exists too which is a lot of fun.Audio------Played this game with French audio and English subtitles which is definitively worth it.Music sounds good and is well integrated into the game. Sometimes you can tell when rats are arriving before seeing them simply by the change in music.Performance and Bugs------------------------While I enjoyed playing the game, I can't call it a smooth experience.I played it on a GTX 1060 on 1920x1080, which sits somewhere between the minimum and recommended requirements. All settings on low (except the volumetric lighting because it looks so good).Even with the low settings the game did not run at a stable 30 FPS. Depending on how much is happening on screen the FPS can vary noticeably, especially with rats involved. The game was still playable, but in some intense action scenes I would have enjoyed a few more frames.But the most jarring thing for me were the load times. Entire levels took ages to load for me, in the worst case I waited 3 minutes. This happened several times over the course of the game. And the game did not run smoothly after the loading screens either. Often, things are loaded while you are playing, for example cutscenes or parts of the environment, where the game should continue seamlessly. Sometimes I just stood there waiting for a building to load that I had to enter, or I saw Hugo interact with rats that weren't there yet, or I stood in front of a door waiting for Amicia to go through. Even in the cutscenes, the audio sometimes did not load properly, and the dialogue lines played a few seconds too late and overlapped each other. It was still possible to decipher the meaning of the scenes, but some of the immersion was lost.I might be at fault for trying to play this game from a 5 year old hard disk instead of an SSD, but the load times still seemed excessively long, not comparable to other graphically intense games I've played like Cyberpunk 2077 and RDR2 (albeit I have not played these games right at release).Apart from that I have not encountered a single bug in my 20-hour long playthrough, and only had the game crash on me once.

_childDocuments_.review: Requiem provides a stellar story that is ultimately stretched too thin, leaving a campaign that is about twice as long as it needs to be. Fans of APT: Innocence will find more of the same here: engaging stealth, gorgeous environments, and of course a feelsy story. All of these things come together in a way that is sure to impress. However, it simply overstayed its welcome. The equipment, crafting, and looting systems are largely unchanged, leaving a gameplay loop that is very simple in its design. The "playable movie" formula is one that I do enjoy, however the key to nailing this design is pacing and that is where Requiem faceplants. Beyond the predictable story arcs and repeated tropes, there were 3 separate times where the story seemed to be surely at its end...but then it wasn't. As a video game, it is for sure worth the money. However, as a narrative adventure, it repeatedly trips over itself, limiting its own potential. I won't downvote an indie game at an indie price for being "too long" (I clocked 15+ hours and the average reported playtime is 17 hours). I'm fully aware most people will see the length as a positive an that's just fine. The game is visually stunning and devoid of bugs, making it an excellent release worthy of praise. I just think it's too much of a good thing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one incredible looking game, easily the best I've seen in a long time. You won't get any kind of recapitulation, just as a caution.Like the first game, there's still very much a linear path to follow, but the sense of scale you get in some of the environments is amazing. The gameplay is noticeably refined, and so is the voice acting. The young cast have obviously grown into their respective roles.It's also a considerable longer game than the first, but this didn't bother me at all. The pacing and story beats, are for the most part great throughout.

_childDocuments_.review: Guards. Guards. Guards. Guards. More guards. There's so many guards.Innocence was an amazing journey and I loved every second of it. I felt a strong bond with the characters, the gameplay was simple but addicting, and the setting was fantastic.This game ruins the mechanics in my opinion. I'm nearly 8 hours into the game and most of it has been a little bit about rats, a lot about obscene numbers of guards. The first game had guards of course, but there were few in the areas where there were lots of rats, there were only a few levels where guards were prevalent and those levels worked well. Here, guards are spammed, which I think makes the experience slow and unpleasant.The weapon selection is also switched up, which I liked at first since it felt less cluttered, but over time it becomes a little annoying to have to sift through different elements and your hand, sling, pot, etc. There's also a heavy reliance of using your weapons and materials to make your own path through the rats without the help of permanent light sources or movable braziers, which sounds like it'd grant the player more freedom, but in reality it makes for a more clunky and less satisfying puzzle-based system.Overall, I'll try finishing the game despite it not really being fun at the moment and see if I change my mind in the later chapters, but as of now it really doesn't have the same magic as the first game.Also why the ♥♥♥♥ does Lucas look like a cartoon?
