_childDocuments_.review: As with A Plague Tale: Innocence, this sequel fulfilled my expectations.I think it is the most beautiful game ever, I am totally blown away, it is an absolute beauty. The visual side of the game is literally at an absolutely top level.The game has very detailed environments, from abandoned villages, ruined castles, forests and ruined roads. Great details, character models, excellent lighting, realistic lighting and reflections. In addition to the visual aspect, weather such as sun, rain, storm and fog also contribute to the overall feel of the game. But unfortunately the only big downside to all of this is the very poor optimization.Musical compositions create emotional depth, heighten tension and help build atmosphere and support drama. So the music in this game is a hugely important element that supports both the story and gameplay aspects.The gameply is much more varied and gives me more options for solving individual situations. Innovations are also in the skills, which bring much more options and more variety.These skills are gradually unlocked and include your stealth, combat and alchemy abilities as you perform certain actions.Unfortunately, there are a number of flaws in the gameplay.Artificial intelligence is among the most serious. Your companions can often do things that make you angry or laugh, especially in stealth passages.Some secondary characters are also not well developed, they have no deeper motivations that could interest the player more. Their involvement in the plot can be considered not so important, so they seem to appear and disappear immediately for no reason, which makes me sad.However, it can be challenging for some. There were a few gameplay sections that were a bit annoying. Stealth mechanics and some passages can be frustrating for players who prefer fast action. Also, some parts of the game can feel linear and limited.Compared to Innocence, Requiem is better in practically everything, offering nicer graphics, more atmospheric music and better gameplay.A Plague Tale: Requiem is a unique experience, a great ride from start to finish. So if you enjoyed the first game, the second part will definitely not disappoint you. I think this is one of the best titles of its kind, it can hit our emotions a lot in the strongest way, nothing can ever top it in my mind.

_childDocuments_.review: This was an excellent story. Top marks for the acting and the music and the design.  It is a beautiful game.  it is one of those games where I just sort of sat in silence as the end credits rolled,   Together with "Innocence" this story has so much to offer; suspense, horror, religious horror (the first game has the catholic backdrop, this one a pseudo pagan theme) historical fiction, family bonds and responsibilities, revenge, love and redemption.  And Amicia... I love that girl.  she gets her ass kicked again and again and keeps going.Game play wise,... What I liked from the first one was back, Very strong stealth mechanics.  Finding the right path through an area riddled with soldiers or figuring out the sequence to get through a sea of rats was fun.  I liked that Sling stones were no longer a resource, and the equipment crafting element was whittled down to finding just a single material (and recycling excess ammo) instead of the multiple materials of the first game.  The addition of the crossbow was a nice touch, and finding a place to use it in the level design was too.Unfortunately, for me at least, the new emphases on combat took some of the charm away. I have yet to find a stealth game where forced open combat is enjoyable, and this is no exception.  You can still head shot enemies with no helms, but most wear helmets now, so you will need crossbow bolts, as the the caustic bullets from the first game are gone.  There are a few new enemies including shield bearers and heavy knights, the latter which needs to be distracted and then a week point found, hit with the sling (some times there are multiple points) and then swapped to the crossbow and shot... This wouldn't be so bad if pulling up the ammo wheel paused the game as you usually need to cycle not just weapons, but ammo types as well while trying to out pace the enemy.  You can do this without the wheel, but either way, the baddie is barring down on you, sometimes a few at the same time.  There is also a Knife now... that is single carry, single use, making it the most useless knife in history. You can find them in the different levels, but they also act as keys to pry open locked carts, so you must choose between a last-ditch save weapon or getting that extra loot... I had a minor gripe with the upgrades, as it is all or nothing.  You start with only 2 crossbow bolts. Just two. Real RE ammo management vibes here. But with a single upgrade, you carry up to 9.  Ammo materials go from 8 to 22. This is done so that upgrade tiers are pricier, but then third tiers are kinda lame, depending on your playstyle. I like to sneak, so the grenades were pointless.My only other big complaint was the first act, nearly half of the game, was a slog.  The first game had a nice progression in tension and action, a nice mix of highs and lows that slowly built up the whole way through. But here, especially jumping right in after finishing the first game, it started at a 7/-8 and stayed there too long.  All the new mechanics, styles and rules needing to be learned while at a high pace was a bit much.  This also meant that exploration felt stifled early on.  The couple of levels and you are going through a condemned towns and its set piece after set piece as you are herded from point A to point B without feeling like you are in control.  There's just no breathing room in the first half.  Thankfully, the second act opens things up, there's free roaming sections to explore, a few secrets to find and even some new equipment.  as the story continues it focuses back in and the action builds again nicely to the climax and conclusion.  But that first bit just needed some pacing and tension adjustment.That said though... I loved this game as much as the first!  Highly recommended for the story alone.

_childDocuments_.review: I already played a little before the release on the PC, I had access to PS5 versionIf you had to choose your most anticipated game in 2019, it probably wasn't among them the one from the French company Asobo Studio called A Plague Tale: Innocence. But if you had to choose a game in 2020 that surprised you the most in the past, your choice could rest on it. Neither the developers nor the players had any idea that A Plague Tale would become an award-winning and beloved title that would see a sequel called Requiem three years later.But such enthusiasm also carries with it a considerable responsibility; because where else can you introduce the sequel to surpass essentially the ideal, in a genre and a world that is also very limited? Surprisingly, you don't have to go far. And Plague Tale: Requiem proves that even with the same game you can bring something unique. A Plague Tale: Requiem is a third-person action adventure game set in a very linear world with strict rules, in which you will often find yourself in the middle of stealth, difficult battles in which you will especially appreciate your slingshot, crossbow and alchemical ingredients, environmental puzzles and really diverse locations . If I didn't tell you that it's a sequel, you probably wouldn't even know from the basic description that the game differs from its predecessor from 2019. And that's just it: get ready for the second part not to innovate, but rather to grind and it refines the existing game mechanics, the way of storytelling, the art style and the locations associated with it. That might be a problem if he wasn't doing so damn well.The story takes place approximately six months after the events of the first volume. Siblings Amicia and Hugo, along with their friend Lucas and mother Beatrice, want to find a place they can call home where they won't be plagued by the spreading plague. Hugo is still fighting the poison in his blood and Amicia is trying to find any way to save her little brother. And here I would like to directly answer the question that some may be asking: yes, you have to play the first part; or at least you should. And I'm not just saying this because Innocence deserves it, but you'd very quickly cut one of the title's greatest qualities out of your experience, and you'd be hard-pressed to find sympathy for the characters. In addition, the title accompanies you through the story perfectly, it manages to introduce a limited number of characters, but each of them is believable. And just like that, he manages to build some story twists.We should have high-quality story processing, but that is only one of the three things that a proper action adventure game should have. Therefore, prepare to devote most of your time to stealth, action, and Requiem also invites exploration into the holy trinity. But not only the one you use when collecting raw materials or objects, but also the exploration of locations triggered by a puzzle or for your pleasure. The developers managed to conjure up locations and moments that, even with their binding rules, enchant you and make you feel like you can go anywhere; even though it isn't. At the same time, the game can come up with locations in which you do not want to spend even an extra minute. And that's where you'll use the aforementioned stealth or action. In particular, stealth itself is a large part of the gameplay, or at least the developers will very often create a suitable background for it. Stealth is fun, and while straightforward at first glance, you get more practice with subduing or bypassing it as you progress through the game; you can go through the location silently without touching anyone, you can try to take out most of the guards quietly and smartly, you can use some of your allies, or you can go into open combat yourself.And I would be very careful here. There are passages where you can't avoid a fight, because the game itself will cause the fight; such parts are more challenging but manageable. But if you initiate the fight yourself, and often in the middle of a passage that is obviously designed for stealth, you will honestly have a hard time managing it. But there is a reason for that.First of all, you will realize that you are still playing as children. Both Amicia and Hugo have had a thorny journey, but that doesn't change the fact that they can't do much against the armored guards of the Inquisition. You will often feel helpless, regardless of how many Ignifera you make and how many arrows you carry, and the fight can seem clumsy to you, and the question is to what extent this is intentional. But you soon learn that you have to deal with guards differently; either you lure them away, turn off their lights and let the rats take care of it, or you use Hugo, who directs the rats straight away. But if a fight is unavoidable, the crossbow, which I liked, will definitely help you this time. It is stronger than a slingshot and can overcome more demanding opponents and new obstacles. The only ailment is that you can't handle too many darts and you have to learn to save them. You will regret it all the more when you have to use such an arrow when solving puzzles, which are plentiful in the game. Sometimes the game lets you cross a passage infested with rats, sometimes it locks the main entrance, sometimes you have to help an ally overcome a certain distance; the puzzles like the first part have not simply disappeared and continue to beautifully break up the constant stress of stealth, action and even rats.That would have all aspects of the story and gameplay. And now the more demanding part, which is the graphics and above all the technical processing. Personally, I don't understand how a game can look this beautiful when the technical processing is not in everything at the level you could expect from a game from 2022.But I was fascinated not only by the graphic styling, but also by the music after a long time. But this is not because I personally like the music, but because of how well he works with locations, situations and above all musical instruments. In the background, you'll hear the interplay of instruments that make sounds reminiscent of doors creaking, metal rubbing, and impending threat, and that's something that's downright unpleasant when you're surrounded by piles of bodies. On the other hand, you will listen to a multitude of stringed instruments, which perfectly describe the scenery of beautiful locations full of colors and greenery. In both cases, the music itself underlines the main idea that the story is conveying to you. But this is not always easy, as the title has prepared quite a few obstacles for players, both in terms of gameplay and psychologicalAnd we  could say the same about other aspects that A Plague Tale: Requiem brings. From a really well-thought-out story telling to straightforward but fitting gameplay to beautiful and actually disgusting locations. Almost no one expected A Plague Tale: Innocence to become a great title. But I think most of the gaming industry already knew that Requiem would be even better. And fortunately, the developers from Asobo Studio knew it too. Instead of complex experiments that an action-adventure in a linear world wouldn't be able to handle, the developers took what was best about Innocence and just smoothed over the minor flaws. They didn't get rid of all of them, it must be said, and a certain frustration simply won't leave you in the heated passages. And yes, if you didn't enjoy the first part, you won't find any salvation in the second either..

_childDocuments_.review: There’s rarely a game these days that take me on a journey like this. When i played the first A Plague Tale Story it took me only seconds to fall in love with Amicia & Hugo. It felt warm and so good to finally see those characters again in Requiem. The Story that continues here is nothing short of amazing and i enjoyed every hour i played like a good bottle of whiskey. Gameplay wise it’s still more or less the same with the difference being the change in Amicia's character to a point where she’s been through hell and is more than ready to kill or defend herself. Most areas give you the option to avoid detection and save resources or go in with full force. Amicia has her trusty sling and all the alchemy from the first game plus some new stuff to deal with enemies in a wide spectrum of ways, plus a new weapon „The Crossbow“. Hugo's Macula Powers can also be used  later including a radar to sense enemies behind walls to learn their paths and sneak past them or control a swarm of plague Rats to devour enemies in seconds. The puzzles are not really new but on a few, i definitely had to think a bit harder before solving them successfully. Amicia's equipment can be upgraded on workbenches as before to make it stronger. Depending on how you play, her Skill Tree will automatically upgrade itself during your playthrough. It’s a rare treat to be able to enjoy titles like A Plage Tale: Requiem in a world where AAA studios release unfinished and terrible games to make a quick buck. While not perfect, this game is simply a masterpiece and i love it so much that i dare to say it is even better than the first one. From the bottom of my heart, a BIG Thank You to everyone at Asobo Studio & Focus Entertainment for bringing me yet another product that shows exactly why Video Games are Art. Charlotte McBurney who plays Amicia and Logan Hannan portraying Hugo for the English version of the game both did and outstanding job once again with their voice acting and brought the characters to life. In fact all the voice actors are fantastic. The Music by Olivier Deriviere is on another level once more and just perfect. It’s hard to rate a game you enjoy & love so much objectively even with some flaws so i kind of don’t ;) I hope they make a 3rd game one day. 12/10

_childDocuments_.review: Objective interpretation, hardware report, and total game progressA Plague Tale: Requiem is a 3rd person action adventure game. The game was ran on an Intel 13900k/Nvidia 4090. No system crashes noted and 5 crashes to desktop occurred. One full play through was completed at 4k resolution, with max graphical settings, no DLSS enabled, and steam achievement perfection was attained.9/10 overall score and steam review template is posted below the subjective interpretationSubjective interpretationSuch a wondrous experience of elation and subsequent despondence that this game provoked. An exemplary feat to be sure, but Plague Tale Requiem did have a blemish in its otherwise flawless execution, and that would be the games stability. This game crashed frequently, and I encountered many instances of graphic bugs. Bugs such as flickering, sudden transient  polygonal model distortions, frequent fps drops with stutters, and graphical artifacts. No actual game play bugs or soft locks though. All bugs in this game were graphical and the graphics of this title were phenomenal. The world of southern medieval France is resurrected with the sheer amount of effort that went into the art design of this title. Every objects texture was of high quality, and besides the bugs, there was little in this game that broke my visual immersion. Some assets were frequently reused though, such as guard models. Maybe 2-3 different models for the type of enemy would helped with this one instance of immersion break, but now lets talk about the sounds of this game.I played this game voice acted in French, as the French voice acting feels more emotive, and people speaking French in France helps with immersion. The voice acting was fabulous. The fear, anger, despair, and happiness in the voices of the characters felt genuine. The voice acting is also paired with a wonderful soundtrack that consists mainly of violin music with some percussion instruments. The music fit the narrative setting well, and it supports moments of sorrow, while also hyping up the player for moments of conflict and adversity. Everything just flows together so well in this game, and this includes how it plays. The game play of this game is action packed with moments of having to deal with multiple threats in a certain order that is conducive to survival. This game is quite easy, but it is a smooth play that places the player in many different scenarios that keep the experience fresh and ties into the story quite nicely as well. The overarching plot of this game is ludicrous, but this games narrative strength does not come from an intriguing story. The strongest narrative aspects of this game is the connection to the characters state of mind, and how the player empathizes with how the characters of this title feel. Simply put, the player forms a connection with the characters, which provokes emotion in response to what is occurring in the game. I would say the genre of this tale would be tragedy, and the user should steel themselves in anticipation of the feels that are rampant in this game. Story telling that provokes an emotional response is amazing, and this game deserves to be commended for accomplishing this. Of course as consumers we can commend the developer by buying the game at full price, however this game frequently goes on sale, thus my recommendation is to buy it then, but if you want a graphically magnificent game right now that is very emotionally provocative feel free to buy at full price. All in all this game is wonderful experience that feels strong in every category except software stability. _childDocuments_.review: You need quite a bit of patience for this game. I was pretty much regretting my purchase after the first few hours, but then it came back super strong and the story got me really involved. The gameplay itself doesn't seem to know what it wants to be though.+ beautiful visuals+ atmosphere + excellent set pieces.+ exciting action sequences+ good story with quite a few twists+ interactions between characters really add to their personality+ companions make you switch up your play style+ love the contrast of the place before and after the rats come- gameplay can't decide between being a stealth game, a shooter or an arena brawler- pacing at some points doesn't feel very good- the difficulty of the puzzles is pretty much nonexistent - early chapters can feel frustrating- auto saves are very random sometimes-  apparently 2 stray rats can devour a human within 2 seconds (it can be frustrating sometimes)I really liked the tutorial because it did a good job explaining the mechanics, showing off the beautiful landscape and introduce the characters at the same time.After that, I struggled hard to keep my motivation because of these issues with the first few chapters:- a bunch of fetch quests that do not seem to progress the story at all (and dragging on)- you don't have all your tools and weapons yet- some enemies are simply invincible at this point and getting spotted just means death- if you're sneaky, you're most likely missing out on upgrade partsAfter that, when you got most of your tools (and are not doomed because the wrong enemy spotted you) the game becomes so much better.- The story gets actually interesting- Your skills and tools give you more ways to approach a situation- different companions can support you in different ways and entice you to try different play styles- the map opens up quite a bit and gives you some choices on where to explore

_childDocuments_.review: A Tale of Emotion and BeautyA Plague Tale: Requiem is a true masterpiece that stands out for its breathtaking atmosphere and storytelling. The graphics are absolutely top-tier, with stunning detail that brings every scene to life, making you feel fully immersed in the dark, medieval world of the game.The story is one of the game's strongest elements. Deeply emotional, it builds incredible relationships between the characters, especially between Amicia and the adorable Hugo. Amicia is a remarkable protagonist, full of depth and strength, while Hugo is a character who steals your heart from the very first moment.The music is another standout aspect, enhancing the emotional weight of each scene in the most magical way. The soundtrack pulls you into the experience, adding layers of intensity and making every moment feel even more powerful.As for the gameplay, while it might fall slightly short compared to the exceptional storytelling and audiovisual presentation, it’s still enjoyable and engaging. It may not reach the same heights as the narrative, but it remains a solid and pleasant experience overall.9,5/10

_childDocuments_.review: so, game's been out a week now and i've finished it so here is my unfiltered opinion the matter.Graphics: this game is an art piece even on the lowest settings, the imagery is perfect for the story from the dark rats to the bright sun, especially the lighting in dusty and dark places looks on point.however there is something amiss, the facial animations and lip sinking is not so great, especially if it is not a forced facial shot, i looked at their faces when Amelia put Hugo on her shoulders to see the dancers and it was not a pleasant sightPerformance:with all that this game is and does it will destroy your graphics card, think of it like arma 3, it will run at -30 to 18 and you will like it. unless you have a PC that left your wallet crying in the corner, then you'll get to stick to the 30 range.Gameplay: the controls can be very frustrating at awkward moments, the first example that comes to mind is in the chase sequences the controls are relative to the camera rather then the character, meaning S is always toward the camera and W is away. you can get used to this but i imagine this caught a lot of people. the combat is a similar story, the enemies melee attack range feels too big and you will get caught trying to duke them alot. also the movement can feel delayed and sluggish, not necessarily a downside as it does aid in making things feel more grounded and weighty, but it can lead to anger in the later combat sections.story:here is the true gold of this game, the story is clearly a labour of love, everything is as it's told and not death felt guaranteed, they knew when to give rest and when to create panic. though after playing the first you will have been conditioned to expect disaster at every turn, though it is not always there, the bare possibility will keep your heart rate up.as a side note the music was used beautifully to aid the story and atmosphere. though you will have a heart attack every time you hear a sharp violin On the other hand, you have the near constant handcuffing...the game essentially forces you to play one way.My biggest problem with this game is the "I don't need no man" modern feminist stance that Amicia has.  It was hinted at in the first game, but it flat out slaps you across the face with it in this game.  Several points in the play through Amicia shouts that she "doesn't bow to any man."  Girl, do you know where and when you are?  You are a teenage girl in the middle ages.  You will bow when it is commanded.  Modern military is like that today.  You respect the rank, not the man.  All the men in the game are considered bad and die.  The only exception would be Lucas, but even he is portrayed as weak.  You CAN have strong female characters without denigrating the other men.  There are a plethora of bugs.  A good portion of them are game-breaking and forces you to reload from the last save.What props this game up from being a trash game is the voice acting (though even that gets a little annoying sometimes), graphics, time period, and music.  I am a Roman/Medieval historian.  So the fact that the Byzantine/Roman Empire was tied into a medieval game is right up my wheelhouse.Scoring system:Music: 10/10Story: 7/10Voice Acting: 8/10Difficulty: Super easyGraphics: 10/10Replayability: 0/10Inserting modern woke feminist ideals in a medieval game: -10SCORE:25/50Overall, buy the game if its 50% or more off.  I am nervous about how the 3rd game is going to go.  Dont get me wrong, the first game was excellent...absolutely loved it.  It pulled on the heart strings a lot.  The second game just made me angry and frustrated.  Its almost like a completely different studio worked on it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the original (A Plague Tale: Innocence) though I did find the boss fights a bit disruptive to the story-telling. On this and other fronts Asobo have taken on board feedback in making Requiem. It's generally a better game, and although it does have its weaknesses like before, it's still an excellent story-driven game and great to play. It's not quite as linear which isn't a bad thing as there are some open areas where you have options of how to find a way through. Some mechanics have gone: you can no longer concoct materials to make guards remove their helmets. The substance to attract rats to an area has very limited use in this game, but is still available. Some new mechanics are good and a sensible progression: being able to fill pots with other ingredients and using them against enemies provides more options for escaping or progressing along. This was a neat addition.Graphically it has improved a lot with some superb visuals and attention to detail. Here good graphics are not wasted, as it adds greatly to the sense of place and grounds the story because of the obvious care that has been put into details that would probably go unnoticed by most. Wet sand looks like wet sand. Rain falling on a soldier's clothes does nothing, but makes a tiny ripple on his metal armour. Somebody made that choice, but it works.Story-wise it continues 6 months after the first game. There are new characters to help Amicia and Hugo in the form of Arnaud and Sophia. The downside of this is that Lucas doesn't feature for a lot of the game so doesn't play much of a part in his friends' journey. The original characters have to take a back seat from the story for dubious reasons. The story is good, but I did find some of the dialogue pretty forced at times where Amicia or Lucas are explaining something and it's not clear how they would know what's happening.  The pacing of finding out information felt more natural in the first game as the plans of the Inquisition and their hunt for Hugo were steadily revealed. In this game the characters just know things sometimes and it's clear that they're providing this information to the player, not to each other as characters. It's exposition dumping, and is somewhat jarring. The first game did a better job of "show don't tell". Similarly some of the emotional dialogue feels like it's trying a bit too hard to dispense wise or profound statements in response to events, rather than being fitting of the characters or situations. This happens quite lot to the extent that at times the characters just aren't reacting like real people. The story needs you to know that Amicia and Hugo are brave, so it slaps you in the face with it.This game does flirt with Amicia's struggle to deal with the number of people she's killing to protect her brother. It's built up that she might be losing her mind, but then it just kind of fades from the story and nothing more really comes of it, although it is picked up again right at the end. I think it's a case of trying to bring in too many things, rather than the story being bad. It isn't. It's just not as tight and focused as in the first game.We still have rats of course, which were a key part of the game and its Plague-ridden setting, though there's a bit more to the game this time in terms of stealth mechanics and dealing with guards, so it feels like there's a better mix of things going on as Amicia and Hugo's journey to and beyond the island progresses. There are still some instances where a slight misstep can lead to a few rats killing Amicia but I found it more forgiving than the first game in that regard. Having so many rats on screen is impressive, but the running sections where hundreds of thousands of rats are flowing like fluid and destroying everything (including buildings) in their path were a bit silly. Sure, rats bursting out of the ground in their hundreds in the first game wasn't a realistic portrayal of 14th Century France but it felt pretty grounded compared to rat tsunamis in Requiem, because it was set against backdrops of utter plague misery as Amicia and Hugo confronted the effects of the Plague on the towns. Here there are torrents of rats because that's how Plague comes to town and follows Amicia and Hugo in their journey. The rat tsunamis are impressive to behold but also over the top. Just because you can render 300,000 rats at a time doesn't necessarily mean that you should :)There are more sections in Requiem that involve shooting out a succession of guards (and one toward the end which goes on for too many waves), and a couple of boss fights that are more balanced than before. They didn't detract from following the story as much, which was a plus.The soundtrack is excellent, and is just as big a part of the game as in Innocence. On the whole, an excellent continuation, but a bit mixed at times by attempts to do too much. I hope there will be a third game because A Plague Tale was refreshingly different. Fixing some of the problems with the first game was good. I think a third instalment just needs to dial back from try to cram in too many new things, and keep focused on a tight story with these excellent characters.

_childDocuments_.review: [bGraphics/Performance:[/b]I gotta say I don't understand how some can say that this looks just slightly better than the first one. I played them back to back and the difference is rather huge. I played both on maxed settings (only 2,5k tho, since this 4k won't give me 60fps anymore). This game looks really good and for me at least the performance was actually good(especially if you compare it to UbiSoft games). I had some micro drops in fps but never in a situation where it would be harmful.The ambience/music fits, the sounds are good. Nothing spectacular, but still very solid.The first game was rather short with around 8 hours. Which is actually not that bad compared to many other story games. The second one took me roughly twice as long. I'd say the focus shifted a bit towards gameplay and away from story. All in all the length was good. Towards the end I was ok with it ending, which in my book is a good thing (especially compared to wanting the game to end).Whereas the first game didn't have too much gameplay. In the sense that it often felt to much on rails since the paths were pretty linear. The second one opens areas up a bit more. This leeds to more ways to get to your goal. Overall the gemaplay shifted more towards  a balance between stealth and combat. Some people seem to have problems with stealth but I feel it is overall more realistic and I actually liked it. Do enemies see you from too far away? Compared to some other games maybe, but in reality it does feel mostly ok. I would argue that they sometimes are way too blind. And they are sometimes quite stupid but all in all that felt good.I gotta say some spots are kinda tight to stealth trough, but nothing felt bad.Combat is probably the only thing I really did not like. Now by combat I mean actual combat with an enemy that has spotted you. In most cases it is fine, but for some reason the devs decided to add a few closed arenas where enemies spawn aggroed. I rember two of those quite well since they are annoying as hell. One big problem here is that stealth does not work at all which removes a huge part of your repertoire. Another big no-go is that you cannot doge anymore (Did she forget how to do that since the first game?). Combine that with the scripted (in the sense that they are always the same, slow mo and all. And you cannot dodge once the animation starts) melee hits you take and you have a mess. The enemies walk slightly too fast and the aernas are slightly too slow to make this feel good.Aside from that if you happen to get to one the harder arenas unprepared (too little special ammo) you're gonna have a rough time. These two arenas almost made me wanna quit. I pretty much speed run the start of them(since it's always the same) and fail right on the last 1-2 enemies due to missing a shot/throw. It seems some people dislike this story alot. Some say the story is too unrealistic. Quite frankly I don't see how the first game is more realistic than this one. I would argue that is is just the logical evolution. The endings doesn't suit some people as well. I won't spoil anything, but I did like the story and the ending. And I thing that any other ending would have not been a wise choice, since that would have either made less sense or made sure that any folliwing game sucks.By the way I do like that the devs quite obviously like games like Uncharted. The changes in pacing felt good. I think most people that dislike this story/game simply expected something different.If you liked the first game and you like games like Uncharted and you don't want another empty open world game with a nice story and nice pacing than you should give this one a chance. Especially since this game does not cost AAA money. ;)Oh and btw since I am sure there will be some that say "This is bs". That can very well be true for you since after all this is very much subjective. ^^;

_childDocuments_.review: The Plague Tale Series provides a stark contrast between hopeful characters and a grizzly, sobering atmosphere. This series has always felt "raw" in the best of ways due to the amazing writing and characters grappling with visceral issues. Where the first game was about losing their innocence in a war for survival, this game focuses on Amicia and Hugo embracing their violent side as they pursue a larger goal of finding out who they are. This is reflected in the new crossbow Amicia is sporting and her equally bad temper.So what kind of game is this? Well it's a lot like the Last Of Us. A story-driven game with a strong atmosphere, and a lot of tools or companions to help you navigate levels and distract enemies. It's an immersive game set in medieval France about the rise of a plague, except oceans of rats are destroying towns and eating people. You navigate levels stealthily or aggressively, killing everyone in your path or letting the rats do the work for you. The rats avoid light, so this leads to a lot of great puzzles and ways to take out enemies.This is where the game really shines, you navigate wide open levels full of options, crafting materials, and enemies. This game has really mastered the puzzles and tools from the first game, making for some really creative paths. You can upgrade Amicia in a couple ways: Gathering materials and upgrading her equipment(Sling, Crossbow, Alchemy Pouch, Pockets, etc), or there is a new skill tree that levels up automatically based on how you play. (Super cool!) This means if you kill everyone who stands in your way, Amicia will become more battle-hardened. Prefer to use alchemy to dispatch your enemies from afar? She learns how to hurt more with her concoctions. Or you can avoid fighting altogether and become a stealthier version of her. This adds a lot to the game, I found myself bouncing between upgrading my weapons, crafting my alchemy, and checking my skill tree to see my personal playstyle.All in all, the Plague Tale games are masterful puzzle solvers full of heart, detail, and a fair touch of gore. This sequel does everything a great sequel should, it feels more grown up than the original in both the characters/level design and gives us a lot more agency in how we tackle enemies. I must say, any game where a terrifying enemy is chasing you through an ocean of rats is a unique experience, and even cooler you can extinguish that enemy's lantern with some homemade alchemy and rats will do the rest like a true homie. (Honestly, the rats are the heroes of the story.) Anyways, yay rats and boo anyone that dislikes this game. 10/10

Game isn't made for it, even though it likes to rub your face in being too violent. Being so strict with myself on such an self-imposed rule just led to a lot of frustrating reloading. _childDocuments_.review: Rating:- 9/10 ( Must play if you like story/drama based games. Don't play if you don't want to spend hours upset after finishing the game because of 1. how good it is 2. spoilers so can't discuss)Pros:-1.)  Artwork - Close to being insane. From painterly environments to jungles, forests, forts. 2.) Visuals in general - Extremely beautiful game (max settings with high frames really lets you enjoy this)3.) Story - Man. I'm not even gonna bother. Real tearjerker and a wild emotional journey.4.) Audio and Voice Acting - Absolutely top notch. For every character who is not a random goon. 5.) Gameplay - Lot of hidden pathways and clever little puzzles all around the map. Some really well hidden puzzles too. Combat is fun, sneaking is also fun. And there are multiple ways to handle combat encounters and some puzzles. So even if your way isn't the best way, it is still just as effective.6.) Side Characters :- Really well fleshed out side characters.Cons1.) Crashed twice so..2.) Some AA studio jank is there in character movement at certain sections of the map. Nothing too major though.3.) Sometimes in order to be great, certain story trajectories have to go in the direction of tragedy/grief. This isn't really a con as such since you kind of already know what you are signing up for but damn, a certain part of this game left me with a heavy heart.TLDR: Tearjerker/10 game. Play if you love stories.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first launched A Plague Tale: Requiem, I couldn’t tear myself away from the screen. The game was very beautiful and exciting, but for some reason I abandoned it. I think it was because of the slow start. However, when I decided to play it to the end, I was absolutely delighted. I played it three times in three days, completed all the achievements at 100% and would gladly play it again.It was an amazing journey, full of emotions, tension and unexpected turns, especially at the end, when two wonderful characters died. It was very sad and offensive. The game tells a touching story about two children, Amicia and her younger brother Hugo, who are trying to cure him from a mysterious disease Prime Macula in 14th century France.The graphics in the game are simply magnificent. Each scene looks like a painting, and the atmosphere of medieval France is conveyed so accurately that every step can be screenshotted and admired. The gameplay also does not leave you indifferent. Puzzles, stealth mechanics, and the need to think on your feet make every minute of the game exciting. The player can choose to kill all enemies or take minimal casualties, which unlocks various skills that help in the gameplay. However, sometimes you still have to kill, and in some chapters it is necessary.The relationship between Amicia and Hugo occupies a special place. As the older brother, I do not always understand how she loves her brother so much, but maybe this is my perception. The soundtrack deserves a special mention. The music and sound effects increase the tension and emotional depth of the game. The acting, especially the voice work, conveys the characters' personalities and emotions perfectly. For example, when Amicia cries, her voice sounds appropriate, which adds realism to the game.The music in the main menu is something special. The game is very cool, and although at first glance it may not seem very attractive, I definitely recommend it for passing. I assure you, you will like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the greatest stories I have played in a game next to RdR 2. Although the game doesn't reach some of the highs of the first, I think it's is better in almost every other way.Grand scale, some of the best graphics, and well paced gameplay. And imo, this is one of the most unique and boldest stories told in a game
_childDocuments_.name: A Plague Tale: Requiem

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only about ten hours in, so take my words as you wish..The GOOD:1) The game is a VISUAL MASTERPIECE! Hands down one of the most beautiful games I've ever played (if you've got the hardware run it on high or ultra settings). Honestly some of the areas and vistas in the game are like walking thru the Renaissance art section of a museum. 2) If you've played the first game then the combat is very much the same with a little bit added on here and there to spice things up. Now this can be taken as a negative too depending on who you ask. However for me drastic changes to a combat system that had no glaring issues (more on this later) to begin with is not my cup of tea so I'm not mad about them keeping things very samey.3) Amecia's (the main protagonist) character development is very good. I won't spoil much, but i'm liking where they are going with her.4) The musical score is top notch (special shout out to the first area of the game in which you fight hostile enemies).The NOT SO GOOD:1) The story is kind bland (so far). Like it's not as good as the first game, but not bad either. Just wish they developed it a bit more and spent a little bit more of that 'make the game pretty money' on better writing. Cuz after all there's only so long you can stare at visual piece and be awe struck.2) The supporting characters are a bunch of whiners. The dialog could've been better. It's not good, not bad...just blah. Like I honestly couldn't give a rat's ass (see what I did there) about a lot of them. 3) The combat while good enough could've used mild improvements to how clunky it can be in the heat of things. Granted this problem shouldn't really be an issue considering that stealth play is very much pushed onto the player by the game. Like your'e not supposed to be Xena the warrior princess, but the option is there if you chose to deal with the fact that your'e a 15-16-17 (don't recall) year old young girl going up against adult armed guards. 4) While the game is less linear than the previous title and they offer up more pathways for you to get from point A to point B. There is virtually no reason to quote explore an area (aside from minor side collectable content, which as far as I know has no bearing on the main story) which is a shame considering how gorgeous this game is. Like give me a reason to go frolic in that field of flowers besides just for the fun of it.All in all for $50 bucks you get an interactive and very, very good visually appealing work of art with an okay story line. I would only recommend this title if A) You've played the first game and want to finish the story. B) You've got a good hardware setup that can showcase what the devs clearly spent most of their money on. C) Both of these. All other players not in those boxes. I'd wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Following on from the last game, 6 months pass. The game itself is brilliant in its environmental design, music and puzzles. However, much like the last game, I lost interest in caring about Hugo toward the end because of how unruly and annoying he had become. If that was reigned in I'd've labelled this my fave game of 2022. The game itself does follow a lot of the stuff from the last stealth-wise but cranked up a bit more. And the enemies! Such a good challenge. Amusingly this game keeps the rat memes from the last where you can make them stack super high.Only real thing I'd ask to change is maybe a higher texture pack for the animals since they look so poorly rendered that it does draw away from the game.Overall, 100% worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not as easy of a recommendation as the first game.This game starts playing mostly like the first Plague Tale. However, as we advance through the chapters, more and more cut-scenes and unskippable dialogue creep in. It gets to a point where the player is barely allowed to intervene, just to press A here, press Y there. The story is also very strictly linear, with minor choices that don't affect the outcome. Eventually, there are "combats" where only one type of weapon is allowed.There is one particular chapter, after which a good % of players seem to give up, and I don't blame them. And I promise you, there was no big complicated puzzle nor difficult fight... just insanely long cut-scenes.If you, like me, are curious enough about the story (which I found very interesting), and wait patiently through the cutscenes and dialogue, most everything in the game has been improved from the first Plague Tale. The graphics, the music, the voice acting.The ultimate hide-and-seek game. Absolutely glorified horror hide-and-seek, with beautiful scenery, "some" combat and "some" puzzles.IMO the best thing would be that they made a TV series adaptation, like The Last of Us. You'd lose the haptics, though. The choice is up to you. Just be warned: after you press play, very little choice will be up to you.

_childDocuments_.review: After plaything A Plague Tale Innocence on PS5, I was excited when I found out a sequel would be releasing. I am fairly deep into the chapters at the time of this review and feel confident in providing a review based on the gameplay mechanics, visuals, HUD, audio etc.The gameplay provides a similar experience to the first game except more enhanced tools on the weapon wheel is the big difference.The game feels smooth without ray tracing on (maybe due to my GPU AMD 6950) but I would rather sacrafise that and have ultra settings and 3440x1440p resolution. The UI is very friendly to navigate.I am playing the game using a DualSense controller and I love the fact the developers have supported the enhanced haptic feedback vibrations.I am also playing this game on a 21:9 aspect ration (34" ultra wide monitor) and EVERYTHING including the cut-scenes is in ultrawide! only thing that isnt is when the game first loads up.Highly recommend this game for the attention to detail, breath taking environments you'll be part of, amazing story and endless customisation.Some of the downsides:The pause menu and the menu when you die in game is a bright white background which can be very disturbing especially when playing in a dark room (which I do).The characters seem to lack correct eye contact and emotions if you were to look at them whilst playing. _childDocuments_.review: A Heart-Wrenching Odyssey - A Plague Tale: Requiem  - ReviewOverall Rating: 10/10"A Plague Tale: Requiem," developed by Asobo Studio and published by Focus Entertainment, is the highly anticipated sequel to "A Plague Tale: Innocence." Continuing the harrowing journey of Amicia and Hugo De Rune, Requiem delves deeper into the dark and treacherous world of medieval France, fraught with danger, despair, and a relentless plague of supernatural rats. With its compelling narrative, breathtaking visuals, and refined gameplay mechanics, A Plague Tale: Requiem cements itself as a powerful and emotional continuation of the De Rune siblings' saga.Narrative and Storytelling : 10/10The narrative in A Plague Tale: Requiem is both heart-wrenching and immersive, building upon the emotional foundation laid by its predecessor. Amicia and Hugo's bond is tested like never before as they face new horrors and uncover deeper mysteries about Hugo's curse. The story is rich with character development, and the dialogue is beautifully written, drawing players into a deeply personal and affecting journey.Atmosphere and Setting : 10/10The game excels in creating a hauntingly beautiful and immersive world. From the sun-drenched fields and bustling towns to the eerie, rat-infested ruins, each environment is meticulously crafted to evoke a sense of dread and wonder. The attention to detail and historical accuracy in the setting is commendable, transporting players to a vividly realized medieval France.Gameplay Mechanics : 9/10Requiem refines and expands upon the gameplay mechanics of its predecessor. The stealth and puzzle-solving elements are more intricate and varied, requiring players to use a combination of wit and strategy to survive. The introduction of new tools and abilities for Amicia adds depth to the gameplay, making each encounter feel fresh and challenging. However, some players might find the increased complexity a bit overwhelming at times.Combat and Challenges : 9/10The combat in Requiem is more dynamic and engaging, with Amicia's expanded arsenal offering multiple ways to tackle enemies. The tension of managing resources and strategically using the environment to overcome foes is palpable. While the combat mechanics are well-executed, the real challenge lies in balancing stealth, puzzle-solving, and direct confrontation, creating a satisfying blend of gameplay elements.Visuals and Art Direction : 10/10Visually, A Plague Tale: Requiem is a masterpiece. The stunning art direction, detailed character models, and breathtaking environments create a visually rich and immersive experience. The lighting and weather effects are particularly impressive, enhancing the game's atmosphere and emotional impact. The use of color and shadow adds depth to the game's storytelling, making each scene visually compelling.Audio and Music : 10/10The audio design in Requiem is exceptional. The hauntingly beautiful score, composed by Olivier Deriviere, perfectly complements the game's emotional tone. The voice acting is superb, with standout performances from the cast that bring the characters to life. The ambient sounds, from the distant cries of villagers to the skittering of rats, further immerse players in the game's world.Replayability : 7/10While Requiem offers a deeply engaging and emotional experience, its linear narrative structure may limit replayability for some players. However, the richness of the story, the beauty of the environments, and the depth of the character interactions may encourage multiple playthroughs to fully appreciate the game's nuances and hidden details.Conclusion : 10/10A Plague Tale: Requiem is a powerful and emotionally charged continuation of Amicia and Hugo's story. With its compelling narrative, stunning visuals, and refined gameplay mechanics, the game offers a deeply immersive and unforgettable experience. While its complexity may be daunting for some, the overall journey is one of profound emotional depth and storytelling excellence that is sure to leave a lasting impression on players.

_childDocuments_.review: The good: Very good world building! You really feel for Hugo and Amicia. The game looks amazing, and I loved how well the characters are written.The bad: The game has terrible pacing issues, having a lot of "endings" strewn throughout. You play a few chapters and you think this is it, but no goes on. Then you play a bit more, another huge scene that is build like an ending, but it goes on still... After the 5 "big ending" I kind of wanted the game to end already. A feeling I never encountered before. I checked online to see how many chapters there are in total and I think I had 7 more... There are 17 in total.All the "endings" made it feel longer than AC Valhalla, which is not even close regarding playtime.THERE IS A WHOLE CHAPTER AFTER THE FIRST ROUND OF CREDITS :)) ! Then, after the second round of credits, there is another cutscene...I think I wanted this to end more than Amicia and Hugo.Still loved the game, though.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish I could give this game a 10. In every respect it is a 10, the story, the characters, visually the music... But there are just too many performance issues. First and foremost, this game is VERY poorly optimized for PC users. In all honesty it never should have been release in this state. I'm running top of the line hardware and still experienced regular stuttering, frame drops and crashes. Secondly, the AI is just awful, NPCS constantly get stuck and ruin the pacing of the game which in turn results in having to restart a section. Lastly, the achievement system is just broken. It shouldn't take THREE playthroughs to get 100% completion. I'll give this game a 9, though it should be a 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy this game if:✅ You were looking for a sequel where a more direct / less subtle approach to stealth based areas is allowed ;✅ The claustrophobic environments from the first game weren't that much up your alley;✅ Even though you've enjoyed the previous game, you are now looking for more linear and less stealthy game;Don't buy if:❌ You wanted to see a deeper and meaningful story;❌ Character development is a "must have" when playing a sequel for you;❌ You're not into games with a way stretched plot, made unnecessarily long;❌ You've loved the first game graphic, horror and thrilling elements; they're mostly gone into this game, which is much more linear and cinematic;Verdict: a stretched 7.5 (just for the voice acting and the graphics/environments)Time required to finish the main game: 15 hrs (advice: do not play at the lowest difficulty setting);Time required to complete it at 100%: 22-25 hours (a NG+  is required to max out skills and tools);1- Let's start with what's great: scenery and voice acting:Hugo's and Amicia's journey touches now more cities, verdant bluffs and pictoresque cities from the South of France and (i guess) northern Spain, leaving back (for the most part) those chaotic and rotting places you've seen in the first game;Voice acting remains suberb and the details, animations and costumes kept being well done and a real pleasure to be seen;a) The change in scenery and atmoshpere is for sure a welcome surprise, however this messes up the whole story a lot . Forget getting into the Bishop's laboratory and the older battlefields, those are completely gone to push Amicia into a whole different character;b) Amicia (especially in NG+, even at the highest difficulty level) becomes a war machine, thwarting/ negating the stealth mechanics in some chapters;c) All The Rune's family members are grown into their role....probably too much, becoming even more bonded and self absorbed than before (yes, even their mother) but heavily influenced by one another, swinging from temper tantrums to other destructive, nonsensical and homicidal tendencies with too much ease;d) The plot was too stretched: out of the 17 chapters which constitute the game, only 7-8 were actually impactful and needed, both from the gameplay perspective and from the story and lore side, which felt well shown visually, but poorly explained.

_childDocuments_.review: In the short amount of hours I've invested in this continuation of the first Plague Tale, I will say this much:the story continues to follow this intricate path of engaging dialogue while managing to display both emotional and physical conflicts. If you've already played the first game, be prepared to ride the roller coaster of pain and depression. While I will refrain from posting any spoilers (to allow others to enjoy the game), I will say that the trauma surrounding the siblings is a rather depressing slope. Aside from the story itself, the graphics and ambiance of the game are beautifully done; the concept of a safe haven and the spread of the Bite throw the players through a constant loop of false hope and security. Through the game's narrative, its characters, and the teetering balance of right vs. wrong, it's a beautiful game overall.

Could not share much with spoiling, so i'll leave that out.For music, those bgm, i can see the team puts in dedication for the recordings, is well composed. Especially the one playing for the main menu, and the other one entitle "No Turning back".So yea, enjoy the game, but expect some issues here and there.

_childDocuments_.review: I was already a big fan of the first game with it's mature way of telling a story and I'm glad they kept it that way. Innocence, the first game in the series, had some flaws and was a bit rough around the edges but still a lovely game about some children losing their innocence by being thrown into a war, a plague. But the developer Asobo Studio pretty much ironed out all of those flaws and added new mechanics on top of that fit in very nicely and make the game much better and smooth to play than the predecessor. The voice acting in general is one of the best I have ever heard in a game and is so wonderfully played especially from the main cast. It's almost a shame that in some in-game cutscenes the facial expressions don't match the emotions they go through with their voice. The soundtrack is one among the best and captures every moment perfectly and gives it the musical support it deserves and needs for a game like this that heavily depends on it's atmosphere and mood to tell it's story.Story wise it is a bit hard to give a comment on that since it's a rather subjective matter if you like it or not. It's not a fairy tale and like I said in the beginning the tone is rather mature with some heavy topics that are not for everyone. I certainly throughout enjoyed it and always wanted to know what is happening next and it left me in tears at the ending. But I can understand if some people don't like the pacing or some turns and decisions the characters take but at least for my understanding it all makes sense and the fact that some decisions turned out to be wrong or even disastrous makes them even more human.Graphically as you can see in the screenshots it knows to impress with it's great lighting effects, detailed character models and beautiful environments. It's rather demanding especially at 4K resolution but there is no stutter due to shader compilation whatsoever, which is not too common for games that are using the Unreal Engine unfortunately. Only a couple of short traversal stutters are present when you progress to a next area but that's definitely okay and also doesn't happen very often. Frame delivery is super smooth and thanks to the vast options for upscaling technologies and even DLSS Frame Generation the relatively high requirements are easy to keep in check without compromising the visuals too much. The game does look still fantastic on medium settings mind you.Ray tracing was added later with a patch but it only consists of ray traced shadows which in all honesty don't look very impressive and tank the performance quite a bit. The game also began to stutter every now and then when I turned the camera due to the RT shadows after I enabled them. Would've loved to see some ray traced reflections instead of the mediocre looking screen space reflections or maybe even some ray traced global illumination but what the studio delivered without ray tracing in mind is super impressive and I would recommend to just turn RT off and go for some higher frame rates. HDR on the other is a big bonus if you have a display that is capable of that but of course it is not a must.Would I recommend this game? Hell yes absolutely! I hope more games in the future will go this direction again as this gives us a glimpse what is possible for modern video games to tell their story. I didn't mind that the gameplay takes a step back to favor atmosphere and story but that doesn't mean that there can't be games that offer both a good story and good gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I very nearly cried at the end, and that's a compliment.If you've played Innocence and are browsing reviews to see if this sequel is any good - there's nothing to worry about. Requiem is more of the same gameplay- and quality-wise, with innovations that work, and a lot more playtime than the first one too. There were several points where I was like "Happy ending, now I gotta wait a few years for the next one", and the game went "Nah man, take another chapter". ♥♥♥♥, it should've ended. That doesn't mean the game went on for too long; it just means that it had a few opportunities to end itself, but decided to keep going and to break my heart with its ending.With that said, on the technical side the game feels a bit less optimized than its predecessor, and especially in sections where many rats load in at once I had some FPS drops. My PC is significantly below the Minimum System Requirements in some categories though, and I was still able to enjoy the game at mostly stable framerate with a few graphical concessions. This is the unpatched release version though, so it might've improved by the time you read this.

_childDocuments_.review: A Plague Tale: Requiem is truly a next-gen game visually, and very few other games have created such evocative imagery. It feels like every scene is graphically stunning. I thought the story was generally very well put together, and the characters all had well rounded arcs and development. The voice acting was also beyond incredible. The soundtrack also perfectly compliments every scene. The gameplay isn't incredibly different from the first game, but this is not your stereotypical first person shooter, so I wouldn't go in expecting the combat to be like that. I feel like A Plague Tale: Requiem is strongly driven by its narrative, and it is stronger for it. I don't have many complaints, but I did feel like the game simply didn't give enough resources for you to do substantial upgrades to most of your tools. I also would've liked a little more closure at the end of the game. I thought that this was to be the final game in this 'series', but it definitely felt like there could've been some more wrap-up. However, that's not to say that the ending was not satisfying, just that it could've had a little more.Overall, I would highly recommend picking up A Plague Tale: Requiem, especially if you are a fan of games that are narrative driven with well done stories.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first game, you will definitely love this one. Everything except for maybe story (and only because you already know what's happening) is better: visuals and animations, cutscenes and narrative, gameplay variety, level design and secrets/collectibles.The only downside is that you cannot get 100% achievements in one playthrough, so you need to start a New game plus. And NG+ is a letdown: it has absolutely the same encounters and gameplay as the NG, but the enemies have lower reaction times, which is not a problem at all because by chapter 6-7 of NG+ you will unlock absolutely all upgrades (actually, it's the exact reason why you can't get all achievements in one playthrough).Also, it seems not possible to unlock all secret chests in NG+ (because there's not enough knives that open them), so be sure to find and unlock them in NG. Also, even though they are not displayed as collectibles in chapter progression menu, you can actually replay the chapters to unlock the chests you missed on your playthrough.Other than the NG+ being too easy and too samey, the game is a great adventure, and I totally recommend it along with Plague Tale: Innocence.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely feel compelled to write reviews;usually I only go to the trouble when a game is exceptionallybad and/or overrated, and the hate is still flowing thru my veinsafter all the pain and suffering the game just put me thru playing it. A Plague Tale Requiem is one of those exceptions; and I feel a responsibilityto warn other sensible players out there from wasting their time and money.I was very excited about starting this game afterhaving played the first one, with at least a modicumof fun. (The First Game has a lot of issues too, andis also terribly overrated, but it is WAY better thanthe sequel).So let's go thru all the flaws of this game, one by one.Serious Design Flaw 1: The Autosave is UnreliableIn one Chapter the game's autosave didn't save properlyforcing me to replay an entire section when I cameback for the next session.Serious Design Flaw 2: The Game Is Poorly Playtested and Flawed In It's Very Fundamental Game DesignI got softlocked twice in this game having to replay entire sections, simply because either the devs or the playtesters (maybe both..)couldn't make sure that each "section" of a chapter the player gets to has enough resources to get youthru to the next one. In both cases it was the clay pots that softlocked me in certain areas. Ifyou don't know how many clay pots you need for a certain area before you get there, you will simplynot be able to progress. And you need to know that beforehand (How in the F@kk will you know that beforehandif you've never played the game before?)This is a cardinal sin in game design, softlocking a player due to lack of resources/materials. But the devsof this game, did just that, thru sheer incompetence.Serious Design Flaw 3: In Chapter 10 I Experienced A Gamebreaking GlitchIn the 10th Chapter I came across a gamebreaking glitch where one of your follow-along-NPCsgot stuck (and at first I didn't know that was the issue, so I had to waste about 15 minutesin absolute frustration; trying everything under the sun to progress until I eventually wasforced to reload the game, which got it unstuck.) Such a bad game.Serious Design Flaw 4: There's Just Barely any Gameplay here, and the little that is Is Incredibly DULLThe absolute biggest problem with this game is that the gameplay is just straight-up boring. Imagine extremely dated gameplayand clunky controls from an average game from the PS2 era, and you getthis game. Such things as pushing boxes/carts, pulling/switching levers, outdrawn and boring stealthsections with BAD Ai enemies, dull repetitive "puzzles" where you have to getpast the rats... etc.. the list goes on.... The Second game is short (albeit slightly longer than the first one), yet, I was only 4-5 hours in before I had started to get boredand fed up with it and just wanted it to end. Not because the game was too long, of course,but because the gameplay was all so mindnumbingly boring and bland. The only thing that keptme going to the end was the story (which by the way is much worse than the story ofthe first game.. but it was still the best part of the game..)The Game also has tons of sections with forced slow-walking where your characterwalks at the speed of a geriatric snail, and there's nothing you can do about it. So if that's something you like in your games, you're in for a treat.Serious Design Flaw 5: The Game has ZERO replay value.After a first playthrough there's no reason to evercome back to this mediocrity of a game. Maybe if you'rea trophy hunter you would come back to it once to 100%your trophy collection, but aside from that there'sno reason to ever come back. The Gamehas no other game modes, the story/gameplayis fully linear; and the gameplay being as repetitive and dullas it comes, you wouldn't come back for that either of course.I gave the first game a 7 out of 10 score. Which was a very generous score,and most of those points came from how beautiful the game looked, and the qualityof the story/characters/voiceacting - NOT from the gameplay.This second game however, I will not give more than a 4 out of 10; and once again,most of those points comes from the same things the first game got its points from.It's such a shame; I was so hopeful about this sequel.. but it turned out to beone of my biggest gaming dissapointments in recent years. If there ever isa third game in this franchise, I probably wont even pick it up on a sale. I payed about 22 euro for this game on a sale, and I felt like I had thrownmy money in the toilet still; had I payed full price - I would have goneto the police and filed a lawsuit for highway robbery.It's just incredible to me that this game has recieved so much undeserved praiseand it makes me think that players who rates this game highly are either bribedreviewers or people who's never played a good game in their life...If you like watching people falling apart with rage and dissapointment as theyplay a game then here's the link to my YT channel and my playthrough of this game:If you like story-focused games; a game I would heartily reccommend over this oneis "The Forgotten City" by Modern Storyteller. That's how a story-based game is supposedto be done. My memory of playing that game is so fond that I will probably come backto it one day and 100% the trophy collection, even tho I'm not really a trophy hunter.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game immediately after the first. The graphics are breathtaking and the character models are improved. Models in the previous game felt lifeless at times, but these models seem much more present, their facial expressions more animated, though sometimes their eyes still seem dead. Each environment is careful crafted, down to the bricks in each house. They are very impressive and everything seems unique and not recycled. Amicia's outfit and hair changes many times throughout the game, which I thought was a nice touch. The performance issues I had with the previous game appear to have been corrected in this game, despite it's superior graphics.As with the previous game, the music is quite good and does a great job to accentuate the mood of whatever is happening. The story is awesome and you grow to care about the characters and their relationships. Just like the story of the first game, this story is a series of tragedies and hardships and it's hard to believe that there could ever be some semblance of closure by the end.There are a ton of new gimmicks that are introduced in this game. It gives you a lot of diversity as to how you can complete encounters. There are almost so many that it's easy to forget some. And some gimmicks are used rarely for progression, one gimmick was actually only used once. I wish they had perhaps toned down the volume and tied them more into the encounters in a puzzle fashion, it would have made it more satisfying to get to use these gimmicks more consistently.While the encounters are still fun and challenging, I didn't care for the encounters as much in this game. The game ties you into a specific way of playing in order to guarantee growth development in different skills. It encourages an emphasis on stealth through NPC chastisement, but it doesn't feel like you can actually stealth successfully all that easily. Being stubborn, I tried to finish out this skill tree first, which led to much of my frustration. I just find stealth to be so boring and slow, especially when you are trying to comb a large area for key upgrade items and collectibles. And there are a lot of materials that are locked into circuitous routes with lots of patrolling enemies, and you have to keep obtaining them if you mess up. I ended up just blowing past a lot of nice chests out of frustration. The previous game, each counter felt like a puzzle with a specific solution. You explore each encounter using the tools and tricks you have, eliminating threats, figure out how to deal with the rats, and moving along, which I found more satisfying. IIRC correctly, the upgrade materials were never in an encounter, and if it was there were checkpoints at each phase of the encounter so they were easy to obtain again if you messed up. In this game, without trying too hard, I was unable to obtain all upgrades and skills, which is sort of dissatisfying.Some issues:1. This game has integration with iCUE. Which is fine, some games do, like Diablo 4. I like when games do cool things with my keyboard. However, all this game did was turn off my lighting settings on both my keyboard and mouse. They immediately return to normal when I exit the game.2. If  you bind a key to something that is already bound, the game gets frozen on the screen notifying you of this. The game should either swap the bindings or blank it out, but leaving them the same and giving you a notification that is bugged out is frustrating. I had to mash space and escape to get out of this each time.3. The amount of times Amicia thanks the lord got old. I know I'm not a 15 year old French girl in the 14th century, so my ability to immerse myself in the role is limited, but I really don't want to hear that amount of religiosity come out of the main character's mouth, even if it's historically accurate. It doesn't add anything to the game.4. French accents in the first game were charming and are missing in this one.The game took me  around 28 hours to complete with 65% achievements. There is a NG+ option, but I'm not interested in that. The game is really high quality, so the asking price is probably fair, but I would still wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: A Plague Tale: Requiem

_childDocuments_.review: Asobo picked right up where they left off. Literally, and in terms of intensity, incredible character design (& development), insane ambiance, great soundtrack and unique story. It is hard so say whether Requiem is better than Innocence. They are both equally amazing and need to be played together to fully appreciate anyway. And not only did they pick up on the good parts that Innocence already displayed, but they improved on it. Not just the graphics got better (they are freakin' phenomenal! - and it ran smoothly on my PC, no crashes, minor stuttering in one Chapter) but the whole feel of it. They take the story to a whole new level and, in my case, I could not stop playing it. I sometimes had to, simply to catch my breath. Because that's just what it did, it left me breathless. The intensity is well balanced with tenderness and humor. And it builds up to an incredible climax that, to quote a brilliant song from my favorite band (Motionless In White) shatters your heart and leaves a crack in your smile. I do not want to spoil it for anyone, but I do have to say, people calling the ending 'out of character' is absurd. Try going through what Amicia and Hugo have gone through... and then call it 'out of character'. It is humane. It is brutal. It is beautiful. My heart will always ache. And I will forever consider A Plague Tale Requiem a masterpiece. 10/10 from me. And I shall never see rats the same way again *shudders*

_childDocuments_.review: While this game looks great, it is a missed opportunity in my eyes. The story is depressing, but sometimes the main protagonist is frustrating or annoying. The stealth gameplay can be fun, and while it fits the characters in the game, it is a bit repetitive. At times, I felt like the game was a bit clunky in the movement, or intentionally forced you to not be able to move fast or run for no reason.The most frustrating part of this game is the main story. It seems to be attempting to pull on emotional connection with a character, while this character is literally causing huge amounts of destruction and death. Perhaps its not the type of game that I can enjoy, which is fine, but the main story is just unappealing. It would have been really awesome to explore the world more, see other civilizations, and honestly, where is the cult that is attempting to kill this character that is spreading misery and death? I wasn't able to make it to the end because it didn't keep me hooked. I'd strongly recommend only picking up on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute masterpiece in terms of narrative and story, character development, visuals, art design and Oscar-worthy performance from Charlotte McBurney. I haven't played a better story-driven game since The Last of Us Part II, period.What an achievement from a team of just 70 people and without backing from huge AAA publishers or a platform holders such as Sony and Microsoft. Can't wait to see what's next.I think this must be said cuz not only is it a extremely well crafted and written story-driven game, but it is also a game which you'll be playing. So, Asobo sure have fixed some stuff the first game suffered a lot from. Checkpoint system is WAY BETTER now, plus you can't die in combat from just one or even two hits from enemies, so Requiem is a much MUCH LESS frustrating game to play (but it still can be in some very few instances, though it is not as bad as in Innocence). Asobo also somewhat expanded stealth system, so now you can way more easily runaway and hide from enemies not only in high grass, but also under tables and stuff like that, which is extremely usefull. But it is still not a pefect game in terms of gameplay and design of some stealth encounters (some of which are very restricting and poorly designed). Moreover and outside of crossbow (which is good), the sling mechanic is just not good for combat, it's just isn't, for some puzzles or environmental stuff here and there... yeah, for sure, but not for combat.There is a fix if you don't like combat at all and it can be activated in accessibility options, but it's more like a cheat which allows you to play the game so that enemies can't kill you (only environmental stuff like fire etc.). Overall, I'd say gameplay this time around is 50/50 for me, there is good stuff I like, but there's also not so good stuff which hurts the gameplay (primeraly the sling mechanic in combat and some poorly designed stealth encounters), but Requiem is still a better game than Innocence, where combat and stealth became somewhat tolerable only after about 65-70% way through the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an exceptional, brilliant, suspenseful, beautiful game full of heart and characters one can't help but enjoy and care about. I loved absolutely everything about it.  Dialogue and story telling are masterful.  This is a sequel that in every way honors the first game and improves and builds on all of it!  This is definitely now among my top 10 favorite games of all time.
