_childDocuments_.review: The game is very exciting at first. Especially if you played the first part. The whispers of children are still amazing, especially when playing with headphones. Quixel's world and megascans are top notch. The gameplay is intense at the beginning and has interesting mechanics.But over time, the game starts to get boring with its imposed stealth and incomprehensible AI behavior. I played the game on purpose after six months of its release in the hope that there would be no bugs and problems with optimization. Unfortunately, there are frequent drops in FPS on my 3090 and rizen 5950x. This is very surprising considering that I did not set the graphics settings to maximum. Also, once something happened to the game and half of the NPCs were not visible and the game just hung over time or slowed down. The support team recommended checking the files, and it worked.Constant problems with the gamepad  xbox seris elite 2. I used to have to turn off the controller, restart the game, and turn on the controller again. Now the game does not support my xbox series elite 2 and regular xbox series at all. It's blasphemy to play with a keyboard and mouse. So I decided to just uninstall the game before I even got to 60%. Very sad, because the potential of the game, especially the first part was very good.
_childDocuments_.name: A Plague Tale: Requiem

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't necessarily hate it. I remembered liking the first one. But yeah, this game has some flaws based off my time playing it.- Optimization: Seems a bit lacking. It didn't run too bad for me, some frame drops and early on the game went into Not Responding in Hugo's dream with the bird. Not too sure on if there's any other big issues, as my playtime is low.- Characters from the first game noticeably re-cast. Particularly Lucas, who also is barely recognizable from the first game. And I haven't even played the first game in a while.- In this game the characters should be aware by now that the rats follow Hugo, and destroy everything. But that's okay, we can talk about how everything we do is for Hugo and we all love each other.- The combat system... okay, the rats are still the same. Avoid/defeat them with fire in some way. Kinda the same thing every time, sorta like the first Alan Wake game. But that's okay, it was there in the first game! Eh, I can let that part slide personally, but maybe some additional new ways to combat the rats would be nice, other than throwing pots and throwing sticks. Particularly because they seem to ignore a soldier's torch when they are re-introduced... and the characters state they are supposed to be stronger. But that's okay, I guess. And then the guards/etc. are either avoided by stealth mechanics not really changed since the first game, or taking them down with your sling, only if they are not wearing a helmet. I don't remember all of the stuff of the first game, but this feels like again... more of the same, possibly a downgrade.- Knives... are supposed to be a game changer, but are apparently rare. I surely didn't find many in my time playing. I sure hope the sulphur to craft wasn't also rare.- QTE prompts. 2022 game btw.Lastly, I had the ending spoiled for me reading through other reviews. Which makes the events of BOTH games... largely a waste of time. Great, thanks Asobo and Steam reviewers.

Requiem gives you such an in depth look at a fictional 14th century France, where the main characters, Amicia and Hugo embark on a journey to find the cure to the "Macula" that Hugo withholds inside of his body. name: Little Town Hero
detailed_description: Got any ideas, hero? The story is set in an isolated village on the edge of the world. The only gate leading outside is heavily guarded by a castle, and the villagers are not allowed to leave. Most of the villagers don't give it a thought, and happily go on with their everyday lives. However, the protagonist is a little different from the others - he wants to see the world outside. One day, a 'Monster' appears in the village, shocking everyone because until then, no one knew such creatures existed. The protagonist is able to fight it using a mysterious Red stone he found in the coalmines. In the course of his defense of the village, he gradually unravels secrets of how the stones and the monsters came to be… 　 Unlike most RPGs, there is no need to fight weak monsters repeatedly to level grind in 'Little Town Hero'. Instead, you will need to have a good strategy to fight each boss monster one on one. ...Will the protagonist live the adventure he craves and escape the humdrum village life? - A challenging battle system which relies heavily on coming up with new Ideas and strategies. - Compact story progression designed with the busy gamer in mind. - Soundtrack by Toby Fox, composer of the background music for UNDERTALE.

name: Pneumata
detailed_description: Prepare to question what is reality, and what is insanity in one of the scariest psychological horrors in years. The tenants are going missing, screams echo and blood seeps through the walls of Clover Hill. As a detective, unravel the truth that lays within and recover your fragmented memories, or succumb to the horrors that lurk in the shadows within this sinister blend of Survival & Psychological horror. Pneumata will scare even the most seasoned horror players. Features: - Cosmic horror that makes you question what's real and what's not; the line between reality and alternate worlds begins to blur. - True survival horror: scavenge for weapons and supplies in limited quantities and run/hide to survive by any means necessary. - Examine crime scenes and piece together clues and evidence in order to solve a series of gruesome murders. - Explore a realistic and gritty apartment building and discover hidden areas and pathways in your search for the truth. - Diverse AI: fight or hide against entities that are unpredictable and use your environment to create distractions. - Gruesome horror around every corner and an unending feeling of tension and helplessness as you explore deeper into the complex.

_childDocuments_.review: Pneumata thrusts players into a psychological nightmare where reality and insanity blur. As a detective with fragmented memories, you're tasked with unraveling a series of gruesome murders in a sinister apartment complex. Tenants have disappeared, screams echo through halls, and blood stains the walls of Clover Hill. The narrative unfolds in disjointed fragments, mirroring your character’s descent into madness. You’ll question what’s real and what’s hallucination as you explore the building’s eerie, labyrinthine layout. The story grips you early on, but suffers from a slow burn that may lose less patient players.In Pneumata, the primary gameplay loop revolves around exploration, with a heavy emphasis on navigating eerie, abandoned environments. The game’s strength lies in how it crafts a tense atmosphere, where the fear of the unknown drives you forward. The apartment complex, with its dark hallways and decaying rooms, is designed to evoke a sense of isolation and unease. However, this is also where the game stumbles, as exploration can become frustrating due to poorly lit areas, repetitive level design, and a lack of clear objectives.The game does not provide a map or navigation aid, meaning players are left to wander through corridors that often look very similar. While this might have been a deliberate design choice to heighten anxiety, it sometimes feels like it impedes progress unnecessarily. You can easily lose your sense of direction, especially in the sewer sections where the dark, repetitive environments make it difficult to distinguish one path from another. The absence of any clear markers or guidance creates a trial-and-error loop that can break immersion, leaving players more frustrated than frightened.On the positive side, the pacing of exploration is methodical, with moments of silence interspersed with sudden scares and environmental storytelling. For players who enjoy slow-burn horror experiences, this aspect of Pneumata works well, as it encourages thorough exploration and builds anticipation for the next unsettling encounter.Combat in Pneumata is serviceable but unremarkable. The game features basic gunplay, where you’ll primarily use firearms to fend off enemies. While the shooting mechanics are straightforward and responsive enough, they lack the satisfying weight and impact seen in other survival horror games like Resident Evil or Dead Space. Encounters are spaced out, and enemies are often more of a nuisance than a real threat, as the AI can be erratic and sometimes even unresponsive.Like many survival horror titles, The game features a resource management system where players must be mindful of their ammunition and health supplies. While the game does an adequate job of giving you just enough resources to survive, there are moments when it ramps up difficulty by stripping you of your items, leaving you vulnerable. These segments, where you’re forced to run or hide rather than fight, can be particularly intense. However, the lack of clear direction during these moments often leads to frustration rather than fear, as you struggle to figure out where to go while avoiding enemies in the dark.Puzzles in Pneumata range from simple environmental challenges to more complex brain teasers. While some puzzles are well-designed and integrate smoothly into the game’s narrative, others can feel arbitrary and disconnected from the rest of the experience. For example, some puzzles require you to find codes or items hidden in the environment, which works well in building tension and rewarding careful exploration. However, there are moments when puzzle solutions aren’t clearly communicated, leading to unnecessary backtracking and frustration.Enemy encounters are sporadic throughout the game, with a variety of supernatural entities to face. The design of the enemies is creepy and unsettling, with a definite nod to classic survival horror aesthetics. However, the actual experience of fighting these enemies is often underwhelming due to the poor AI. Enemies can be slow to react or even glitch out entirely, breaking the immersion and reducing the threat they pose.Where Pneumata truly excels is in its atmospheric horror. The use of lighting, sound, and environmental design works in harmony to create a deeply unsettling experience. The jump scares, while initially effective, lose their impact over time due to repetition. There are only so many times you can be startled by the same tricks before it starts to feel formulaic. Still, the game manages to keep you on edge, especially during the quieter moments when you’re not sure what’s lurking around the next corner.Visually, Pneumata manages to create a moody and oppressive atmosphere, which is crucial for a horror game. The art direction captures the decaying, haunted environment well, but the game suffers from some technical shortcomings. While some areas are beautifully detailed, others feature low-quality textures that break immersion. Poor lighting—while contributing to the eerie feel—can sometimes obscure important details, making navigation and puzzle-solving more challenging than necessary. On a technical level, it’s decent but not groundbreaking, with performance issues in certain high-intensity scenes.Pneumata brings some interesting ideas to the table, with its moody atmosphere and tense exploration capturing the essence of survival horror. However, it also has significant flaws, particularly in terms of level design, navigation, and story cohesion. It has potential, and I am happy to see that the developers are also active on Steam reviews regarding the feedback. Rating: 6/10Appreciating the tension, but wishing for more.

_childDocuments_.review: It tried. Here's the problem with making games in inspiration to RE7. Your bar is RE7. Pros:Atmosphere. Really nailed world building. Good bones. Gun models look good and feel good to use. Decent performance. I can tell they really did try to give it an identity. Cons: Like every other Unreal Engine passion project - the AI is just simply awful. It's the exact same problem with all UE games that rely on store bought or Unreal Marketplace assets. It just kills the mood. They're goofy. The placement of AI is very amateur and feels unnatural The lighting outside is borderline pitch black. Half of the start of the game is running around in the dark outside. Voice acting is very bad. The forced cut scenes also kill the mood. They're jarring. So to end it? This is a bargain bin game. I'd maybe pick it up for like $15-$20 if you're bored and into very, very amateur re7-likes. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: First of all I understand game development is expensive and complex, I appreciate all the effort that went in this game. But to be honest I didn't have fun playing this game. Games need to be fun and enjoyable, this was not that. I had so many frustrating and annoying moments during my game play that I wanted to stop and uninstall it but decided to finish it and it after seeing ending it disappointed me even more!I played this game around 7 hours and I think about half of my gameplay was about figuring out where to go and what to do. Finding stuff in a mazed like and very dark environment. Enemies were dumb and annoying, too many repetitive jump scares, so many areas with poor lighting and no map to help you navigate just added to my poor experience with this game.The game tries really hard to be RE but unfortunately it is not. It doesn't have any fun elements of RE games and just added so many annoyances instead. I think the game is very expensive for $35, if you are really interested to get it maybe wait for better sale. I think the graphics and visuals were ok, nothing extraordinary or next gen but the problem was most of the areas were too dark to notice any details, there were many objects with very poor quality textures in the game like keypads for example and many other surfaces. Enemy design were good but again nothing new, seen these in many other games. Some areas were designed pretty good but the most of the time the lighting was very bad that could barely see anything, not sure if it's true or not but I felt my flashlight turned weaker after a while and was not bright like the beginning of the game!This area was most annoying part of my gameplay, as I said before half my gameplay spent on finding where to go and what to do. Game doesn't tell you properly what is expected which is fine I think but the problem is the level map design is not really good, there are lots of areas that basically copy pasted and very similar to each other, specially in sewer area where there is no sign or anything you have to try so many times to find the proper way. There is no map in this game which it could've helped a lot.The gun play is not bad it's ok, but there are some moments that you lose all your items and game throws many enemies at you and you have to run away and find an escape in all those dark areas with little hint, it was so frustrating to try figure out what to do in those moments. Game also introduces blocking and dodging in the beginning but honestly I never tried them once and forgot about these mechanics, I was able to kill enemies or just away from them through the whole gameplay.Enemy AI is also very bad and many times they stuck and didn't react to me. The last boss fight was honestly not great. It was just run from point A to B and shoot, I understand that designing boss fights is really hard but again it could and should've better, specially since it was the ending of the game. One of the reasons that I kept playing this game was to get a proper answer to the story at the end which I did get nothing, I mean nothing at all. Game did a very poor job telling or describing what has happened there. There were minimum hints or anything during my gameplay. I was really hoping to get a good disclosure to all these hours but unfortunately I did get nothing. Sound and music was not great, there moments that music and effects were too loud and some times too quiet. There were random effects of doors opening, pages turning when I passed through some areas, door locking and unlocking. The jump scares were fun for 2-3 times but keep repeating the same thing over and over again doesn't make it great, it makes it annoying. Specifically during gameplay when you had camera footage. Performance wise game was good, I was getting 75fps at 1440p and high settings with 3090 but at epic it went down to 60. Turning on DLSS didn't help much in both settings. I encountered few bugs during my gameplay, like for example I reload a save in apartment area after gathering all keys and stuff and when tried to get elevator working it didn't let me, I had to go to all rooms again and get all the stuff that I gathered before to make it happen again. There were some areas that game had subtitle but majority of my gameplay I didn't see any subtitles which was really weird. I saw in some gameplays that you get an objective text on your screen but for me that didn't happen at all.There is no replayability value in this game.CPU: Intel Core i9-12900KMB: MSI Z690 Edge WiFi DDR4RAM: GSkill 32Gb DDR4 3600MhzGPU: Asus GeForce RTX 3090 StrixMonitor: Samsung Odyssey G7 32" 1440P 240Hz

_childDocuments_.review: Big ambitions for a game that set out to be a Resident Evil clone falls flat.While I enjoy what the dev was looking for in this game, there were some major UX issues that ultimately led to me really not enjoying the game and wanting to uninstall and post this review. First of all, navigating the map was a complete pain. If you are expecting players to backtrack for certain items, I would almost recommend that you include a map that we can go back to (boltcutters specfiically were a complete pain)Secondly, the voice acting is not great. I have played worse but I have also played a lot of better indie games that have better voice acting. This takes away from the immersion in a huge way.Thirdly, did the developer not play test the game when going to the computers? I found the keycard #3 and gained access to that computer, but then I was unable to exit the computer even when I selected EXIT. Playtesting is vitally important to games - something this simple probably should not have happened.Last but certainly not least - the gunplay and enemy AI. This particularly feels uninspired. Throughout the beginning stages of the game you are being chased by what looks like psychos with pig heads on, but one of my major issues with the enemy AI has to do with one of the bigger enemies that was delivered in a cage. The monster design was pretty cool, but on my playthrough I barely got a good fight with this guy. The guy aggroed immedietly after his cutscene and then proceed to get stuck attacking through a gate - talk about anticlimatic. Once again, basic playtest issue. Overall, I am not sure if this game is worth the price tag that it is coming with it. It almost feels like it should be a F2P or $5 game. Purchase at your own risk.

In Gears Tactics, Jack changes the dynamic of the encounters, with 20+ new skills ranging from empowering auras to hijacking and controlling enemy units. New powerful enemies – Deviant enemies are introduced in Gears Tactics, adding a new layer of challenge in the battles, with special abilities that will defy the players’ strategies. New Supreme equipment – The new Supreme equipment rewards players with powerful gear to play through the campaign, defying massive bosses and facing the new Deviant enemies. Enhanced controller support – Optimized experience for Xbox controllers on console and PC. Special Offer Get your free Armored Gabe character skin for Gears 5 multiplayer when you complete or have completed the Gears Tactics tutorial. The character skin drops in Gears 5.* *Character Skin requires Gears 5 game, and its use on console requires Xbox Game Pass Ultimate or Xbox Live Gold (each sold separately). About the Game Complete the Gears Tactics tutorial and get Armored Gabe Character Skin for multiplayer modes in Gears 5. Gears Tactics is the fast-paced, turn-based strategy game set 12 years before the first Gears of War. Cities on the planet Sera are beginning to fall to the monstrous threat rising from underground – the Locust Horde. With the government in disarray, a squad of survivors emerge as humanity's last hope. Experience the intensity of one of the most-acclaimed video game sagas in an exciting new way. Immersive and character-driven story: Play as the defiant soldier Gabe Diaz, rescuing and building your troops in a journey of leadership, survival and sacrifice. Customizable squad and equipment: Prepare your troops to face tough enemies, upgrading their skills and outfitting them with loot collected in challenging missions. Aggressive gameplay: Command your squad in fast paced, turn-based battles, advancing and surviving intense and visceral encounters with the unstoppable, swarming enemy. Massive boss battles: Defeat towering deadly bosses that defy your strategies and completely change the scale of the battle. New content: Jack joins the fight with over 20 skills to combat new, powerful enemies. Improve your weapons and armor with Supreme equipment. Xbox Profile Required. _childDocuments_.review: Gears Tactics is the "mobile" version of XCOM2 and unfortunately tries and fails to copy what actually makes XCOM2 a good game. 👍 +Voice acting.+Visual effects.👎-Boring and repetitive to the bone. -The story is incredibly weak.-The mission design is atrocious. The story is a prequel to the events of the first Gears of War but more importantly, it's a prequel for the characters in Gears 5. The main characters are Gabe Diaz and Sid Redburn and you're tasked with dealing with a certain locust leader called Ukkon. Of course, this would not be a Gears game without some obvious twists here and there that hardly matter but for the sake of it I won't spoil it. The summary of the story would be, get strong and kill Ukkon which you do and the end. When all is done, it just feels eh, that's it? I did like the characters and the banter between them whether it was in a cutscene or in-game and they are obviously carrying the weak story on their shoulders.Also one short fyi, the actual story, the cutscenes themselves, out of 25hours of game time, take about 1 hour if you put them all together, just so you know what you're getting into. There was a trailer that promised lots of story content but it was straight-up ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Shocking right? I didn't expect good story content but even then I was still disappointed. Story rating: 6/10I called Gears Tactics a mobile version of XCOM2 and here's why: It has the basics of turn-based combat, the cover mechanics, the overwatch, and whatever else you are familiar with. However, the developers have no clue what makes XCOM2 great.It's not just the combat and the "missed at 90% chance of hit" moments we hate and love but the tactical layer of how missions are designed and the tactical urgency of creating a base and saving the world, you know, actual management? Gears Tactics lacks, well, tactics, in my opinion. No base building, no base management, no crew management besides choosing their skills and their looks which are pretty generic and I would even go as far as calling the skills rip-off from XCOM2. Shameful really, no originality whatsoever minus some combat moments such as execution which do spice things up a bit.You have 4 I think mission types and they're all the same with no spice, no flavor, no difference from one another besides enemies. You're put into this huge repetitiveness over and over just so you can finally advance the few minutes of story which aren't even worth your time. The few hours are good but it goes downhill from there. Now don't get me wrong, it's nothing bad but it's boring as hell. I honestly could not play more than 3 missions per day. Grab the loot on the map and finish the mission, kill all enemies, grab the loot and finish the mission, rescue exactly 2 soldiers every single time and finish the mission. That's all you'll ever play over and over. Then you head over to your "base" equip the item upgrades and level up your characters and repeat. Now me being a dumbass, I assumed difficulty might spice things up a bit with the enemy AI. Wrong. Nothing changes in the AI with difficulty. To make matters worse, Insane difficulty pretty much one/two shots your heroes without a chance of revival which makes the Support class, pointless. You know who is a Support class? The main hero. Don't waste your time playing on that unfair difficulty, the enemies will never do anything special other than overwatch nonstop or just enter your own overwatch stupidly. Tactics my ass.  The boss fights were cool, sorta. They feel like a chore as well but at least, it's different. The good thing about the whole gameplay is that it works and it feels on rare occasions quite impactful. It feels like a Gears of War game, duh, that gruesome combat you like. It's bloody and messy and sometimes satisfying to execute and kill enemies. If you can get past the lack of tactics and treat it as a generic turn-based game I'm sure you might find more enjoyment out of it than me. Gameplay rating: 6.5/10The soundtrack is very strangely designed and I'm not talking about the songs themselves but how they are played. When it's an enemy turn the music changes and amps things up a notch but when it's your turn it's mellow and mostly silent. Not sure how to feel about it. The songs themselves are okay but they get a bit repetitive just like everything else. Voice acting is great though and not just for the main characters. Every banter, grunt, and whatever is well-acted. The voice actors clearly put some effort into their script and I gotta appreciate that. Sound effects are all pretty good, the guns and bullet impacts especially sound great and there's hardly anything to complain about.Audio rating: 8/10Visually the game has its ups and downs. Levels themselves, the textures are pretty weak in the sense that you'll see them over and over without any creativity. The visual effects, on the other hand, are quite great. The rain, the puddles, the reflections, how sand stays on your armor, the character details are all nice to look at. The game also comes with a lot of video options and even on the highest settings the game performs quite well. There some issues with some of the more demanding effects such as the reflections and shadows but those two were always impactful in gaming so feel free to lower them for almost no visual difference but with a huge boost in frames. Since I compared the game to XCOM2, there is one thing that is visually less impressive and that's the physiscs in the game. Compared to insane levels of destructibility in XCOM2, Gears Tactics is a baby. You can only destroy a few wooden covers and that's about it. As for bugs, surprisingly the game has very few and you'll hardly notice them. Graphics, performance and tech analysis score:  7/10It's a shame really, I knew what I was getting into sorta and I still felt bored. Gears Tactics is not a bad game per se, however, it's a very boring game in almost all aspects and the price on steam is frankly a joke. Do not buy it at full price, the most I'd say you should spend on it is 30$ and if you have gamepass well feel free to try it. As it is right now on Steam, I cannot recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding game. It has a lot of fun factor due to excellent presentation (the combat for a turn based game is very intense) and a challenging decision tempo. The game strongly promotes using teamwork on the battlefield. Sound effects are excellent with very meaty explosions, and some nice dakka dakka dakka from the guns. There's a good variety of bad guys, and the AI is fairly decent to downright dastardly (from time to time). MIssion variety is acceptable, but a few more types would be welcome.The game has no strategic layer, but I think that shows such games do not require a strategic layer if the tactical game is exceptional. A great tactical layer is better than a good tactical & strategic layer (at least in my opinion) since that where the real gameplay is for a turn-based tactical shooter.My gripes:1) The UI for equipping gear is pure rubbish. I somehow doubt it can be patched because of the changes that would be required, but it is awful. Sorry devs, bad design.2) I'd like to see some randomization added to loot simply to promote the end game. Once you have all legendaries, then what? An extended progression for your soldiers would be welcome as well (e.g., they could get stat points to improve accuracy, etc.) Obviously this means eventually the game would be too easy, but perhaps additional difficulty to be added. In short, while this is under "gripes" I can see me playing this game for a VERY long time, if there were a reason to play it for a very long time.All in all, the game for me would be a 10 out of 10 except I have to deduct a point for the UI because it really is that bad. So, 9 out of 10. If you like turn-based strategy games, and can afford the price, then it is worth getting. It is a load of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I am a huge fan of turn-based tactical games, so I enjoyed Gears Tactics. These sniper shots are really REALLY satisfying! One tapping a mob from far away and being able to reset make you love killing scrubs.Also, the game has some nice ideas, not revolutionary, but interesting nonetheless. For instance, once you played a side mission, your squad will not be available for another one, until you played the required number. Another example? You have optional objectives to achieve to get more equipment, and your squad really works cooperatively (some skills can be used on another squad member to buff the owner of the skill: nice!)However, the game is far from perfect. First, there are very very few side mission types (3 as far as I remember), which makes the Veteran mode very repetitive. Also, only few equipment options are interesting, the other are not worth it. Which brings me to my last point: equipment farming. This can be understandable in the game itself, but very annoying in the veteran mode (again, making it super boring). It is as if the devs wanted to make the game longer, without putting efforts into it. Sad.In addition to this crappy veteran mode, I also had to disable the blood (first time I even do this in a game), since it is... well... ugly. Like not well done at all (reminded me these very old pixelated 3D games from the 90s). Finally, bosses' strategies are more repetitive than challenging.Well, you have been warned. To me, it doesn't make Gears Tactics a bad game, but not as good as some others (XCOM series), especially if you are not fond of the turn-based tactics genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those times when I'd like to give a "thumbs sideways" for "meh". It's not bad. In fact, if you are a fan of both turn-based tactics and the Gears of War franchise, you'll likely enjoy it a great deal. But I am much more the former than the latter. Gears of War always felt kind of simplistic to me---flat characters, simple plots. It will occasionally make vague hints at moral complexity, but never adequately explore it. And Gears Tactics does little to improve that impression. I am a big fan of XCOM, and while *tactically* Gears Tactics does live up to the standards of the genre, its *strategic* gameplay can't hold a candle to XCOM. There are very few meaningful strategic choices to make---as far as I can tell, you can't even switch out a character's weapons (!?)---and since soldiers don't get injured or fatigued, you have no reason not to bring your best troops on every mission. Unlike XCOM, you never have that tense feeling of wanting to take all three missions but knowing you can only do one and needing to decide which one is really most important. The story is completely linear and the pacing is almost entirely out of your control. This also makes it far less replayable than XCOM, since every run will end up being mostly the same. Also, the use of Heroes, while very in keeping with the themes of Gears of War, raises two problems I consider serious: (1) There is no reason to train up the rest of your roster, because your heroes are just better and most of the time you're required to use them anyway, and (2) It becomes extremely dangerous to play on Ironman because if a Hero dies you lose the whole campaign. There's no way to recover from a serious failure---if a Hero dies, it's game over.  One of the most satisfying things about playing XCOM on Ironman at high difficulty is having an utterly catastrophic mission where everything goes wrong and all your best soldiers die---and then coming back from it and winning the war anyway. That's impossible in Gears Tactics.If you like both tactics games and Gears of War, go ahead and buy it.If you like one or the other but not both, wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I have hundreds of hours in tactical games, especially XCOM, and overall I have to say this one is severely missing some key things.  There's a good game here, possibly, but its mired under some bad design decisions that leave me wondering if the developers have ever played a single tactical game.1.  Graphics: 10/10  The game is on the unreal engine, so there's not much to say.  Its beautiful as only the unreal engine can do.  No complaints.2.  Sound: 8/10  The guns sound like guns and have a satisfying bass to them.  The voice acting is fine.  No complaints.3.  Gameplay: 2/10  Whoo boy.  You're allowed to "recruit" multiple characters to your roster, but because of the glacial leveling you're going to want to use the exact same people over and over because everyone on your bench is underleveled.  There are no "covert actions" or side missions to send them on to build them up, so whats the point?  Why give me recruits and a roster and then penalize me for using them?  Bad design.  There is no base building or resource management of any kind.  There is no "researching technology" or literally any form of "command and control" to the game at all.  The campaign is simply a linear path with no replayability or strategy of any kind.  Enemies get airlifted on top of you and then get a free turn to attack.  Your "strategy" often devolves to just doing the mission over again until RNG rolls in your favor.  And on that point, the game has a forced checkpoint style saving system.  Get to the end of a mission and misclicked, killing a crucial trooper?  Tough luck, do it again.Replayability:  0/10.  This is a one and done.This game is going to get better reviews than it deserves because of fans of the series as a whole, but avoid this game.  Play XCOM or buy it on sale if you have to.

_childDocuments_.review: The user "VULCAN" made a big crybaby negative review about the game. It's a turn based game. There are a lot of factors that influence how it plays. Balancing mechanics have always been a topic of discussion with these types of games. There isn't really an issue with the balance. It's designed to make you think about your move, and how you should use your little skills or perks or whatever you wanna call them. it's NOT designed to be easy, or use just one type of skill/tactic. If however you feel there is an issue you can mod the game and manually adjust values to tweak it how you'd prefer, including lobbing 'nades on the other side of the map if that tickles your pickle. Some parts of the game are harder than others....that's how games are. Generally the farther you get in the game, the harder it becomes. upping the difficulty OBVIOUSLY makes things harder. THAT'S THE POINT. why would you cry about a game being HARD when you chose to play on a HARDER difficulty? There are many other games that play like this. This is just the GOW version. it's a good game. It's fun, and can be challenging at times. I'd recommend playing through the game on the "normal" difficulty setting first. if you've never played this type of game you could bump it down to an easier difficulty. once you are familiar with the mechanics and confident you could certainly bump the game difficulty up, but beware it can be VERY hard at times, such as fighting a Brumak on the hardest difficulty, trying to draw it's fire constantly in order to get shots off, while also dealing with enemies that spawn in and surround you, making your moves hard to calculate when the Brumak is blanketing almost the entire area with bombs. One thing that can make it tricky is enemies can and do respawn a few turns after you've wiped the area, and they do spawn in different places. It makes you think and plan your moves carefully. For me this is preferred, as having things too linear is a problem, leading to boring gameplay. you might get away with "camping" for a bit, but eventually you'll have to move and change things up. The exception to this would probably be if you're playing on the easiest difficulty. you get better gear which helps a lot, so whenever possible i'd do everything you can to get the better gear. it makes a HUGE difference in the late gamegame is fun, challenging at times, and def worth a play IMO. maybe not worth $40 or however much it's going for now, so if you can get it on a discount, go for it. I say not worth the $40 because at the end of the day, you'll play the game for a while, and eventually quit because once you've played it, there isn't much desire to keep playing it due to poor replay value. there are DLC options, I haven't tried them so I can't speak on them, but you can't play with friends and there aren't multiplayer options obviously.I played this quite a bit and once I was done it made me wanna play the Gears franchise games instead. you most likely won't put hundreds of hours in this game, maybe 50 hours. if you put more in it's probably because you've opted to play on the hardest difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game BUT I found out that the $60 price tag is meant to make the Xbox Game Pass look more appealing while it has a $1 special. So if the Xbox Game Pass interests you, you should probably get that instead of paying the $60. Not the best business tactics but that doesn't have to do with the game itself. The core tactical gameplay is very, very, very good. It's an improved XCom. People knock it for being similar to xcom, in my book taking the xcom model and improving it is a great thing. The main advantages are three action points per turn and being able to do actions in any order. However, the second huge advantage is the changes to Overlook/Overwatch. Now you can actually pin enemies down and suppress enemies using overwatch, much more realistic and opens up tactical options. Your enemies also do it to you, so you need to figure out how to get the suppression off your key Gears or maybe just take the hit. My only gripe about the combat is that frag grenades are utterly necessary at higher difficulty and a little overpowered. I get it's a Gears of War game but there's no need to have imbalance because of the lore or third-person shooter version of the game. I don't think a tactical shooter like this should force the player into abusing any one skill/gadget. Cons: The stuff outside the combat isn't nearly as fleshed out or good as XCom. They do need to do some work in this area to improve the out-of-combat depth. I expect that to come with time, but if it doesn't I wouldn't say this game is quite worth $60.

_childDocuments_.review: Figuring out how to rate this game is hard. On the one hand, the story is solid. It's a strong addition to the Gears franchise and overall storyline, and is visually compelling. This is one of the few games where I will turn up the sound on cutscenes and pay rapt attention. The balance between story and action toes a good line, and you get the exact amount of gore that you expect from Gears. On the downside, the gameplay is stale. For an X-COM style game, they missed half the features of the legacy X-COM series. Character progression is stale, and I have no commitment to any of the non-story team members. Unit effectiveness is driven heavily off of what attachments I can put on a gun, which somehow makes me care more about finding a legendary wrapped barrel as opposed to getting my team proper training or technology. Progression after the first half dozen levels is a slog. Aside from telling my gears who to shoot, there is no sense of player agency in this game. I want to finish the game to get the story, but the gameplay itself isn't keeping me interested. I will finish this run, but likely wont be back. I'm going to not recommend this game. Anyone who is deep into the gears franchise will buy this regardless of my review, and they would be the group who will have this game be worth while. Its worth the play if you can get it on a steep discount, but there are a half dozen other turn based games I would return to before picking this up.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:The gameplay is solid; it's basically an evolution/ripoff of xcom. Having 3 actions per turn is really fun. It allows you to pull off more crazy plays. The downside is that the combat is much less symmetrical than xcom. Multiplayer is not an option, because the 3 actions + ability to shoot 3 times in 1 turn means you can do ridiculous amounts of damage in one turn. Fighting the AI would be insanely dangerous if they used their options to the fullest, but they don't for balance reasons. The game looks quite good. You can tell they used a lot of pre-existing assets, because the environments and models look great.The bad:The weapon upgrades are lame. There're multiple versions of each upgrade that look exactly the same but with increasing stats. The system for managing your squads equipment is also very clunky. Luckily these things don't really detract from the gameplay. The worst issue is the AI, because of the way these games work, even a dumb AI is dangerous, but man are they dumb. They'll walk right into a killzone and end their turn with an overwatch, run right into your overwatch cones, and sometimes even take cover on the side of cover facing you..Overall it's enjoyable, I'd recommend it to xcom fans, but it's not perfect by any stretch.Edit: One more con. There're wayyy too many filler missions. I'm on hour 60 of ironman mode. I've never failed a mission and the game is dragging on and on. Like: "we need to make special grenade to fight this guy", then finding the casing, the chemicals, and the detonator are all separate missions, and as if that weren't enough, between those missions you often have to do 3 side missions which have no story at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Man this has to be the biggest surprise game of 2020 for me.  Never heard a thing about this till a few days ago.  Takes quite a few things from the ever evolving "Tactics" style gameplay, most recently of course the XCOM style that has become popular and there are some great systems that really set this game apart.  The main of which being the class system and the major focus on action points to give a soldier an array of tools to excel and if you plan out your classes and their respective skills can REALLY combo out like a vintage magic deck.  A great example of this would be the "Hunter" Marksman and the "Paragon" Support.  The support can give the marksman extra moves if they kill and enemy and the hunter can also use abilities to add more moves to their pool.  So combine the two and you have a sniper who can one-shot smaller enemies and give themselves 5 extra moves to reap mayhem.  My only dissatisfactions, and they are small are a few gameplay choices that can punish someone playing a mission for the first time or even the slightest bit of a misstep is when reinforcements arrive they immediately take their full turn and with the very "Whoops my guy got one-tapped" nature of this game you can easily have a Grenadier drop out of the sky, move halfway across the playfield, and one-shot a critical hero and have a pack of grunts IMMEDIATELY execute your hero before you can even respond, instantly ending the mission.Overall a solid game, that if their dev logs on the end game hold true will be a favorite of mine.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great XCOM game, with fantastic graphics, quality voice acting and very smooth combat...The biggest problem with this game by far, is the fact that they FORCE you to bench your 'main squad' and then to play with other characters... I HATE THAT... if I want to play with a certain set of characters that I like, then DON'T force me to play with others... this is one aspect where XCOM2 is superior, since XCOM2 gives you the freedom to play with whatever group setup you want and 'Gears Tactics' actively blocks you from playing with certain characters and certain classes!... so yeah, that's a massive problem with this game and honestly it's the BIGGEST contributor to me giving this game a 'not recommended'... if you don't mind being told with which character you can and can't play with, then you'd probably like this game a lot more than what I did... There's MANY missions with modifiers like "no heavy class" or "no sniper class" or "no vanguard class", and that means you'll have to do the entire mission without your 'preferred setup'.More cons: #2. Weapon mods aren't interchangeable at all... so if a legendary weapon mod drops, then you're like YIPPEEEEE! until you see that it's for a shotgun only, and nobody on your squad uses a shotgun... that's very stupid, and once again, XCOM is superior with this regard as with XCOM all weapon mods are interchangeable between characters... #3. There's no saving and no loading... you heard that right... no save states, and no load states...#4. There's occasional 'line of sight' issues ie. the game isn't optimized 100% correctly because I've had several instances where I am unable to shoot at an enemy, despite him being in my 'line of sight'#5. The level of recruits actually INCREASES as the game goes on... so unlike in XCOM where a newly recruited recruit stays level1 until you play with them... in 'Gears Tactics', the recruits in the late-game are actually more powerful than your active squad, which is not only illogical but also disheartening because it makes the active squad that you've invested 10hours+ into seem like wasted time.#6. You're YEETED out of the map when completing it, which often results in you losing out on the chests that are still uncollected on the map, so they don't give you a chance to collect loot at all and that sucks as I've lost out on probably 20+ loot items this way so far#7. There's friendly fire if one character is standing infront of another character... this is unrealistic, because if somebody stands infront of me, then I'll just shoot over their damn shoulder... but characters in this game seem incapable of doing something so basic, so instead they blast eachother right in the face#8. You can actually close 'grub holes' before they open, but at no point does the game tell you this.#9. You can't skip in-game cutscenes#10. There's WAY too many fluff-missions in this game... the actual main-campaign only takes a couple of hours to finish, yet you're FORCED to do MANY hours of side-missions. There's literally no choice... you HAVE to do the side-missions, and only after doing about 4-7 side-missions, does the next main-story-mission unlock.#11. There's no building or base management like in XCOM... this isn't a big drawback, but it's something that I liked in XCOM and I feel that this game would be benefitted from it#12. The game has character customization for your squad, but it's only about 30% of what is available in XCOM2.With everything considered, the gameplay is good, but too many mistakes were made in game-design, which makes the game extremely restrictive and doesn't allow you to play the game the way that you'd want to... that's why XCOM2 is still the better game by a significant margin and why after having played 10hours+ of this game, I actually went back and played more XCOM2... it's just betterFor more reviews, visit my curator page: For my full recommended list of games:

_childDocuments_.review: Great turn based game. My point of reference was XCOM (the 1st one), and I can't decide if my new point of reference is Gears Tactics. The game warms you up to the rules, and then lets you play. It will challenge your strategy, but will not make you feel like trash for every little mistake you'll make. It will keep you in the game so it can push your strategy more next time you'll play right.I love it.Maybe I prefer XCOM's system of evolution of the various classes. It's more simple and clear. Here there are two tendencies in each class (similar to XCOM), and each time you upgrade a character you choose to evolve toward either side. But the pool of special features is very large that I get lost. Eventually there will be a soldier to recruit along the story line that has some feature that I'll like. Only then will I notice it and keep it in mind as an upgrade option for next time.I highly recommend it for action turn-based / chess-like (but nothing like it) enthusiasts :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is not X-com. Definitely X-com one of the best representatives of TBS and it still better than GT. But you should pay attention to this game. And that's why:- New chapter in well-known Gears universe. This time isn't a new shooter, but the turn-based game. Same setting in the different angle. - The Story  is a prequel to Gears. Here we'll know about secret of locust origins (if you didn't know it before). Characters are good, they have firm convictions and motivation. It's a rare situation when none of protagonists annoys me.- Graphics is beautiful. I liked these summer sunsets maps. - Good optimization. - Addictive gameplay for many hours.And, of course, the game has problems too. From time to time you will catch bugs. Some of them are small or unremarkable. But some can give you a lot of negative emotions. I have played on the top difficult, and sometimes I had to restart the level from the beginning. It happened 5 times or about it, but when the game doesn't forgive your mistakes, I don't want to do it too. Now I tell you about difficulty. Of course, I have chosen this way willingly and managed to beat GT. But this is not ok, when an enemy can kill you from one shot. Or, for example, a sniper shot you to a death from range where you even can't see. So, if you want a fair challenge - don't take the highest complexity, take something between it and medium. I warned you.Last thing, I want to tell you is sameness. You'll notice even during the campaign levels are repeats. Your tasks on side-missions will repeat too. I accepted that and beat the campaign, but after I didn't want to farm new improvements for weapons and armor. That had no sense anymore.The bottom line is Gears Tactics deserve your attention even with weak sides I have written above. I spent a lot of time before bored.P.s. 97% hit probability = 97% miss probability

_childDocuments_.review: Tl:Dr: It's a nice new 'aggressive' take on the genre.While XCOM encourages you to stop and smell the roses in setting up the perfect ambush, Gears Tactics throws a gun in your hand and forces you to shoot all the roses in sight. Turn based strategy games more or less have a similar feel, but where Gears separates itself from the pack is in its aggression. You are encouraged to take risky moves that grant you/your team more action points. Each turn emphasizes action points - how many actions can you take that get you more actions to kill as many enemies as you can? Although that doesn't sound as flashy as XCOM's "use a cool overpowered ability to kill all the enemies," it is just as satisfying when done correctly.The only real gripe against this game is that, in-between missions, it's not very fun. There isn't a heck of a lot going on and the menu system leaves a lot to be desired. You can update the gear/attachments on your roster, update ability points, and open loot chests. Bland stuff. A part of me wishes the 'in-between missions' part was similar to XCOM, but at the same time, Gears Tactics really shines in its gameplay. Overall I wasn't spending much time in the menus to begin with. Gears wants you jumping into the missions more than micro-managing.At the end of the day, if you are a fan of XCOM, this game will be a nice new take on the genre. It doesn't have the same replayability or base building mechanics, but it is just so freaking fun. The gameplay is extremely solid - you would be missing out if you didn't give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Execution system is really neat, and adds a strategic flare. Always looking for the action point stack, making combat much more interesting and dynamic than Xcom.Like that only a few missions have times, don't like timers, I am good with almost any other mechanics timers are annoying. Over watch revamp is very nice.Being given 3 action points to move and shoot as you would like was really satisfying, instead of the hard restrictions that other games of this genre put on the player. I think the world of this game is perfect for a tactical game like this. Con: Restricting hero's feels a little too arcade for me.Inventory system does need some work, it is very clunky and could due with some refinement. Funny: I noticed that there is really not much of a gender toggle, that is an interesting choice. Some of the models are pretty square jawed to be female. From a design aspect saves on model making time, I see what you did here.Side quest map variation gets a little stale, not a fan of not being able to use equipment during missions for arbitrary reasons. Add environmental mechanics, something else.Not being able to level to max level before the final fight. You only have a certain number of missions before you will get to the final fight, and I was unable to max any character out before then. So you go into the final fight of the game not at max strength. ----Thoughts: I would say they have a pretty good formula here. If they put in something to do other than from one combat mission to another they have a game that I would continue to buy. Currently it is very combat centric. While I like the combat, I recommend just scaling it back a little bit and give us something else to focus on.Because it is so combat focused, you can get combat fatigue in the game, with very little other aspects to focus on. Pacing could use a bit of work mainly in the leveling up area, When your champions hit level 5 it is almost as if someone said whoa level 5 creeps up kinda fast, lets put the breaks right there. You then hit what feels like a brick wall leveling to 6.I recommend this game at full price as the boss battles are very fun and a nice addition to this genre.I highly recommend this at a discount. If you are an Xcom fan, this is a game for  you as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I love a turn-based tactics game. I'm cool with the Gears mythology. So, a turn-based tactics game set in the Gears universe? Sure. I'll give it a go, if it's on sale. Here are some random thoughts:Gears Tactics is, apparently, a scenic tour of the courtyards of Sera (with the odd square and piazza thrown in). It looks good, and bits are destructible. The lack of variety in the maps becomes more and more noticeable as you take on side missions and, especially, in the post-campaign veteran mode.Speaking of the campaign, I got 40 hours out of it and played every side-mission on offer. Your mileage may vary. I'm currently 20 hours into the post-campaign mode which is just ... more of the same really. You get four randomly generated missions (of which there are, essentially, four types) with randomly generated conditions for success and optional objectives (e.g. no grenades, complete in 15 turns or less, use at least one Scout, use no Heavies) for randomly generated loot. Each is rewarded (in Jacked campaign mode) with a piece of supreme-tier equipment and a piece of epic-tier (I have had one or two legendaries). After completing three of them, you get a Veteran main mission which ... it's the same. You're doing the same thing. Ad nauseum. Ad Infinitum.There's a fair amount of customisation you can do to your squaddies, within limits. You can't change their face or voice, for instance. It's OK. Just don't expect XCOM 2 levels of variety.Inventory (and barracks) management is rudimentary. Once you get to the post-campaign level you'll have lots of stuff. It can be a pain in the @$$ to find it, manage it, move it ... it just becomes a pain in the @$$.Bugs. Had a few. A couple of crashes to desktop. I've had enemies get hung up on bits of terrain while moving and all I could do was reload the last checkpoint. Frustrating as hell. Not as frustrating as the enemies which can overwatch - and shoot - through walls and other bits of terrain, but pretty irritating.There are a lot of other bits and pieces that I could mention but, to cut to the chase, it's a decent game that's really, fantastically over-priced. I understand why (consistency across platforms) but that doesn't change the fact that it's too expensive for what it is ... which is actually a pretty reasonable turn-based tactics game. There are lots of areas where the devs could make quality-of-life improvements and add easy content (maps!). Maybe fix a bug or two.As it stands, half price is the absolute upper limit for what I would consider paying for it. A tentative thumbs up; more content and / or some QoL improvements (or a steeper discount) would change that rating.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid XCOM clone. It irons out some of the more obnoxious problems that XCOM had, while setting the action in an established universe that I already liked. It will delete your save if one of the main characters dies, so maybe don't play that mode. I played through on the normal difficulty and didn't really struggle. I would reccommend the setting above this if you want a challenge. You do get a steady stream of high level recruits so if you do lose people on missions they are easily replaceble, which suits the gears vibe really well. Finally, this game lacks satisfying endgame content. The endgame of XCOM with enemies that could mind control your units and that you have to be very flexible to deal with are sorely lacking here. So there was no point where I felt my work to optimise my builds was really paying off.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - 5/10. The first five hours are insanely fun - until you realize the 25+ hour game is roughly your first 2 hours repeated over and over. You will be doing the same 4 mission types the entire game - even the "story missions" follow this formula with scripted conversations making them "Unique". There is NO strategic map or gameplay which makes the tactical battles cumbersome and dull as you complete the game. Quick Thoughts - Is it fair to compare the game to XCOM 2? Absolutely - we measure progress by the improvement of a product compared to its competition. You wouldn't buy pinecone toiletpaper just because it was new. That being said, the following are issues Gears Tactics has,There are roughly 4 mission types - Rescue two Soldiers, Outrun a creeping explosion, clear a map of enemies and hold a control point. You will be doing these four mission types roughly 40 times over the course of the Campaign. The scenery and maps are randomly generated, so the missions will not be exactly the same, but your objectives will not change. There is NO strategic map or market - In fact, the only planning you will do outside of battles is deciding which units go on which mission. There are 3 Acts with each having 8 Chapters. Approximately every other Chapter will have 3 missions for you to play. You cannot unequip COGS you send on a mission during these Chapters, so you have to plan your equipment, your troops allocation and your order of execution.  After completing the campaign I have no desire to continue playing these same missions. The game is severely lacking in Player choice and variety, Each mission rewards you with gear - which can be nice to give COGS some strong buffs. The gear system of picking up "crates you find on the battlefield" is the number one way you improve your COGS - and since very few missions have a time limit picking them up becomes a priority. While you cannot improve your units with technology upgrades or by training, you make them stronger with what you found in prior missions. I personally did not like this - I had very little control over building the archetytpe of COGS I personally enjoy. The story is... OK I guess. Big baddie is creating baddies, so kill big baddie. It's literally nothing impressive. It's Gears, so I wasn't expecting Shakespeare, but at the same time I would have liked some sort of innovation. The big appeal is the boss battles, which have a nice feeling to them, but only comprise 3 missions in total. This means that out of the 50 or so missions you play, only 6% of the game are these epic fights. The skill tree is really where this game shines - your COGS will get some insane skills that synergize really well. Each of the four classes can have multiple playstyles, all of which can play off other classes and weapon mods in some fun ways. I beat the game fairly easily by utilizing Support classes to grant Action Points to Snipers who regained Action Points everytime they hit or killed a unit. This made for some deadly combo's that was fun to play with - Skill Trees are definitely a strong suit of the game. I really have to complain about the Recruit System... Until Act 3 Chapter 6 you do NOT want to keep COG Soldiers you recruit. Every Chapter the recruits you can get are one level higher than the prior Chapter. The COGS you send on missions gain experience very slowly, so your COGS are quickly eclipsed by 'fresh COGS' that appear in the barracks. More importantly, the fresh COGS will come with unallocated experience AND blue / higher tier equipment.... meaning you want them for their versatility, level and equipment. This cycle continues every Chapter, meaning COGS outside of the main characters will come and go. For a Tactics game this is unacceptable - you will not grow close to your COGS at all. Final Negatives - No psionics, no cybernetics, no damage types, Snipers and Scouts are insanely broken compared to the weak Vanguard, Frag Grenades are extremely broken with no repercussion for spamming them.Final Positives - Great graphics, initially fun battles, interesting Skill Trees.

_childDocuments_.review: So, played just about 11 Hours or so, and I gotta say, I'm actually enjoying it. _childDocuments_.review: Gears of War Tactics is a turn-based tactical RPG that offers a fresh and engaging take on the Gears of War franchise. As someone who has spent over 30 hours playing the game, I can confidently say that this game is a great addition to the series.The game's graphics and sound design are excellent, creating an immersive and visually stunning world that is full of detail and depth. The game's art direction is also impressive, capturing the gritty and intense atmosphere of the Gears of War universe.One of the standout features of Gears of War Tactics is its engaging gameplay. As you play through the game, you take on the role of a squad of COG soldiers, each with their own unique abilities and personalities. The game's combat system is well-designed and challenging, requiring strategy and skill to overcome the game's enemies.Another standout feature of Gears of War Tactics is its customization and progression systems. As you progress through the game, you earn experience and resources that can be used to upgrade your soldiers and equipment, adding a layer of depth and strategy to the game's progression.The game's storyline is also well-written and engaging, exploring themes of loyalty, duty, and sacrifice. The game's characters are well-developed and memorable, adding depth and personality to the game's world.Finally, the game's multiplayer mode is worth mentioning. With a variety of modes and maps to choose from, the game's multiplayer offers endless possibilities for customization and competition.Overall, Gears of War Tactics is an excellent turn-based tactical RPG that offers a fresh and engaging take on the Gears of War franchise. Its engaging gameplay, stunning graphics, and deep customization systems make it a must-play for anyone who loves tactical RPGs and the Gears of War universe.

_childDocuments_.review: It's SO close to being an amazing game, but tends to just miss the mark in some aspects. While I found it enjoyable to begin with, getting to the end of the game was a relief. Gears of War is built on being an extremely over-the-top cinematic game play experience: big characters, big weapons, large explosions, beating the odds, etc. I think if this game just pushed the envelope further it could've been an amazing game, but instead it seemed to play it safe and was set back to a slightly above average game IMO.Give me MORE enemies at once but let my squad be MORE powerful. Allow the missions to be LONGER at times and have MORE variety. MORE enemy types, MORE weapons, MORE customization, it felt like the game is scared to go over-the-top.As a turn-based game it is pretty good with good flow, UI, and graphics! I think if they got rid of most of the required side missions and just got to the meat of the story missions, it would also make this a great game.Could've, should've, would've, 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this game, it just could have been so so so much better. The game tries to be XCOM without being the difficulty of XcomMain Characters: If you have main characters obviously I'm going to want to play with them, why even give me temp characters?Temp characters: you're going to be discarding them often. every level you can recruit new characters. my initial thoughts: "cool, very xcom like for when I need to replace my dead... Oh, these new characters come in at a higher level than my current characters." Why even bother leveling up these side characters when I can get characters that are better than my original temp characters. Why even get attached to that one guy who ran into 5 grubs and killed them all himself?combat: I've never felt like this game was difficult at any real point in time. I've yet to have a character die on me. I dismiss temp characters and move on. I currently have a level 6 sniper and she feels OP enough to win me the entire game. 2 different passives that reduce skill timers on kill. 4 different skills that reset and add action points. This one op sniper class has made the rest of my squad worthless.restart mission: if you ever feel a mission is too hard, just restart it. or even better go back to your main base, there's no penalty for just retrying a mission over and over again.Items: You get items after every mission. at some point it become tedious to get the new item thats slightly better than the current item, and then that sparks a whole chain cause now you're giving the slightly better item to your main character. then you move that to the secondary character, then the third and rarely used character. you're going to do this after every level, or be like me and just hoard items and then once every 3 missions do the tedious busy work of giving items out to people. which of course makes me ask of "what if i want to buy a different item, or sell these useless ones, a store would have been super useful right now."side missions: holy boring camole. The game forces you to use those temp characters we talked about earlier to do repetitive hold the area, collect the items, or rescue randoms allies. Personally the rescue ones were my favorite cause thats where the only difficult missions lay. "how can i take on a whole squad of enemies guarding this area using only 2 starting units?" But then at some point you realize that the rescued gears dont earn EXP cause they're not part of your team yet, so every kill they get is uncounted for.exp: your kill units will get rediculous amounts of exp. while the main, main character gabe will be a low level champ the entire game because you need a healer, and healing gets nearly no (if any?) exp. far as i can tell you get exp for reviving, killing and downing enemies. enemies: like i stated earlier, the enemies dont feel like a  threat. Chuck grenades, plant them and walk away, overwatch. whatever. The enemies run head first into planted grenades. They'll run straight into your overwatch even if it can be avoided. over watch is insanely op in this game, it will literally stop a unit from performing any actions causing them to be "interrupted". The thing that really bothers me though, is that the moment I see an enemy, unless i see their squad behind them.  the single unit will attack me without any help. in order to make the game difficult I have to send one unit ahead to see the enemy squad so they will all react and begin to fight me. otherwise I can just take them on one at a time vs my squad of 4.  Why cant the enemies see me if their nearby allies see me?all in all I like the game. Can i recommend it? no. Could it have had way more potential than it gave me? oh yeah. Why am I playing? after 24 hours on record? honestly it is JUST barely enjoyable enough to help the quarentine time go by a little faster.

_childDocuments_.review: Really great Tactics game, just a shame that it's linear without much replayability. What's there is great, and other Tactics games could learn from Gears' quality of life UI features (an overwatch cone) and fast moving enemy turns, where multiple enemies move at once and trigger overwatch together. I'd give the battle gameplay a 9/10, it's really great.I'd give the campaign a 6/10 it's fine, the loot system is quite RNG heavy, but there's some interesting story/missions on occasion.

_childDocuments_.review: Very well made Tactics game. Xcom, Final Fantasy Tactics, Ogre Battle and Vandal Hearts have been my favorites in the genre over the years. Gears Tactics is right up there with the best of them. It is pretty unbeliavble what they have been able to do with this game. From the graphics, animations, story, cutscenes and polish they have made all those aspects better than xcom. Combat is about even, super fun in both. But Xcom still has an advantage in things you can do outside of missions where it has more depth (Such as base building,etc..). I have been wanting more big Tactics style games to come out and The Coalition and Splash Damage have done a splendid job on this game. Runs super well, super fun to play and it looks just gorgeous. There are tons of graphics settings to mess around with, the execution and chainsaw kills are great and the game overall is just very impressive and a blast to play. For a sequel i would love more to do in between missions like base building and some of the other stuff xcom does so well. I have been grinning non stop so far while playing this game, well done devs. I can't wait to play more and I am excited about the future of this genre more than ever, this game is fantastic! I have to go make some lunch and I am itching to get back and play more, this game has sunk its teeth in like the titans of this genre know how to do. I was expecting a lesser xcom in the gears world, but I have gotten though is a game that stands on its own, brings some great new things to the table and also does tried and tested elements extremely well to, hats off to everyone who worked on this game.I look forward to more tactics games having this level of graphics, animations and overall polish/optimization! Do a proper $30 expansion campaign down the road I will support it. There is LOTS of good here to build on for a sequel or an expansion, great start to a wonderful series I hope! I can see some people coming up with some epic builds that work together from class to class really well, I have already found a few small ones.9/10 so far for me after 6 or 7 hours on the game, it is a more polished and better looking xcom, with no basebuilding pretty much, Two Thumbs WAY up. Reminds me of a mix of Xcom and Fallout Tactics, but set in the Gears world. lastly, I have only run into a few minor bugs, nothing game breaking, on top of everything else this game does so well, it also is optimized very well and has a small amount of bugs. _childDocuments_.review: Gears Tactics is, so far, the best XCOM clone I've played. XCOM 2: WOTC is still the king, but Gears Tactics fits in a nice spot. It's different enough to be feel fresh, but familiar enough to fill the XCOM-shaped hole in your heart. It does a great job at being accessible to non-Gears fans (like myself) but is still very much tied into the universe in a way that will please existing fans (like the friend I played with). In particular, I felt Gears Tactics actually does one particular thing much better than XCOM: the difficulty curve. In the Firaxis XCOM games you'll often hit a point where your squad becomes an unstoppable monstrosity. Gears, however, does a much better job at keeping the playing field even without feeling artificial. Perhaps most importantly, though, the game (mostly) manages a consistent difficulty while still preserving the feeling of growing more powerful. Conversely, Gears greatest weakness is it's unfortunate padding. Despite being only about 20 hours, most of the story missions are broken up with a required "beat 3 randomly generated missions to unlock the next story element" thing. It's not so bad early on as it gives you gear and XP, but later in the game it becomes incredibly tedious since the XP requirements for a new level are very high and the gear isn't as useful.Either way, Gears Tactics is a worthy entry into it's genre, whatever that's actually called.

_childDocuments_.review: Gears Tactics is a solid turn-based game with just enough familiar mechanics to make old xcom players feel home right away. But it does many things in its own way and so it is also a refreshing new experience. The gameplay is challenging but fair.There is no strategic layer and no base development (as per end of chapter 1 at least). But this game tells a linear (and somewhat generic) story with a ton of cut scenes in and between missions. It actually sometimes feels like taking control of the action in the middle of a movie.It is a little on the low side with regards to explaining key elements of gameplay and the briefing for upcoming missions. That makes you sometimes show up with a knife to a gun fight. Not a big fan of the boss fights though. RNG combined with the usual boss-mechanics, restricted ammo capacities and the random placement of reinforcements and E-Holes can seriously screw you up. I do not like replaying the same fight over an over again just because one random enemy group showed up at exactly the one spot where it would cause an unsolvable problem.Unlike in Xcom, in THIS game not having the right kind of grenade at your disposal in certain situations REALLY makes a difference....All in all a good game and I have not encountered a single bug so far. Thumbs up - solid craftsmanship!

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't really bad so much as it is just PAINFULLY mediocre. It does plenty of things right, plenty of things wrong, doesn't really excel or flounder in any particular area. It's just all around flat. The way classes and skills work lead for very aggressive strategies right from the start, which was pretty fun at first, but it just stays completely static the whole way through, and even though a new enemy type is introduced every few main missions, your strategy remains the same throughout the game and doesn't really require much actual thought, planning, or improvisation.Despite not being very long, the game really seems to just drag on. There are 3 acts made up of 8 chapters each, with each chapter consisting of one main mission and the occasional side missions (despite the name "side" they are completely mandatory, as much as I would have liked to skip them by the end). In act 1, you have 1 side mission between main missions, act 2 you have 2 each, then 3 in act 3, and by that point I was just so thoroughly sick of them, accomplishing little more than artificially extending the length of the game without really adding any real content. There are only like 4 or 5 mission types in the game, so you would pretty much average out to doing 10 of each mission type over the course of the campaign, just really repetitive and overall tedious. On that note, soldiers level bizarrely slowly. My four hero characters weren't even all level 7 by the time the campaign was over, and the two dozen nameless grunts you bring on have no chance to actually level up, so you just end up replacing them with new soldiers that are leveled to your heroes so they can keep up, as the only time you ever need to use the grunts are on the side missions. Heroes for the most part are always required for the main missions, and cannot die, so you have to reload if any of them happen to die.The end of each act has you face a massive "boss monster" type of mission. I don't really know anything about Gears of War but I would imagine these bosses are pretty much pulled right out of boss sequences from the main series, but they just honestly don't work in this style of game. The bosses just chalk up to shooting over and over at a bullet sponge while you move your soldiers around to avoid it's attacks as endless reinforcements come in. The bosses just really suck, I get it's not easy to make large set-pieces for this style of game, but this is really not the right approach.The only real selling point for the $60 price tag on this game is the big name IP and the graphics, and it really just doesn't stand up at all to XCOM 2, which I would imagine this game was trying to make some competition for. This game is barely even good as an introduction to XCOM-style games, unless you're a big fan of Gears of War or just really itching for more XCOM, don't bother buying this game, and only ever if it's on a big sale.They've since dropped the price to $30, which I find is a much more reasonable price tag for this game. I'd say it's worth grabbing on a sale at this point.
