_childDocuments_.review: What can I say that hasn't been said about this one.  It's a masterpiece.1.  STORY -- The story is good, not great, but very good.  The writing is excellent, though you won't be reading a book here.2. VOICE ACTING -- Everything, main story and character backstories, is developed solely via character dialogue.  And the voice acting is just wonderful.3.  GRAPHICS --It's the Unreal engine, used properly.  The character faaces, while gritty, are not "Bethesda Faces".  Light on long female hairstyles (there's one), but OK, this isn't Earth and it isn't the 21st century.  You can pick decent faces, the main characters have plenty of facial "character" and are easy to get close to.  There are customization options that expand as the game progresses,   Weapons mods appear on the model.  The terrain palette is a bit on the brown side, but this planet is beat to s***, so it fits.4.  GAMEPLAY -- This is turn-based tactics with cover.  Think XCOM or JA, and you'll be right at home.  And it's good stuf, with a lot of unusual attack and defense types, both melee and ranged.  Units synergize with one another and the addition of the Jack bot adds even more.  I love turn-based games, but I'm not really good.  But the Easy difficulty setting is just fine for me, so I imagine the higher difficulties will be good for most.  The enemies, while not geniuses, are competent on Easy seeing.  And you'll always be outnumbered to begin a battle.  You've gotta manage your cooldowns too.  The side quest segments force you to manage your roster, as a gear can only go on one side mission per segment, and you'll need to choose your missions (like 3 out of 4 presented).5.  MODS -- Weapons are specific to a class, and can be modified by 4 slots.  There's a grenade slot, and one each for helmet, chest and boots.  Some mods can update stats, and/or add special abilities.  And you'll need to make some choices, because that magazine that gives you a ton of damage also reduces the size of your clip.  Your roster of gears expands as you progress and you'll need them.6.  PvP -- It's there, apparently.  I don't do PvP, so no comment.CONCLUSION:  This one is tough to beat.  If you like turn-based tactics, engaging characters, plenty of loot, great voice acting and a decent story, then this is the game for you.  Concluding as I began:  a Masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: I generally go for $1 per hour of fun as my benchmark for recommending games.  This barely squeaked by, 26 hours for $24 that I got on sale.I would *not* recommend full price.  It's a short game, with some high quality cutscense and fun x-com like combat.  However, it's missing a very critical part: Base building.  Gear is random, and very... meh.  There 4-5 classes with each one getting *one* of 4 possible skills.  The side missions get.. un-fun really fast.  They are clearly filler just for fillers sake.  Inbetween real missions you'll be *forced* to go on 1-3 side missions with extremely bizarre requirements like: "You can only have 1 character!" and "You must outrun bombs... but you now only get 2 Action points per turn"  And to make it worse, you can't use the same characters in each side mission, forcing you to use back benchers that suck.  And what do you get?  Trash loot.  And a pittance of XP.  My highest level char when beating the game was 7.It's fun, in small doses.  Was *really* ready for the game to end... then FORCED to do 3 worthless side missions just before the final boss.  -_-

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Easy on the eye, very easy on the brain. Ham and cheese sandwich. OK but not worth $60 (and requiring Microsoft login is a douche move).  Edited OP after playing longer:+ Overwatch works nicely (but not as well as PP)+ Although character customisation is limited it's at least all visually coherent  + Tactics / combos get more interesting as skill trees develop and new enemies appear + Even though art design is not my thing, textures do look very purdy on ultra and runs well+ I haven't encountered any bugs yet and it feels polished and finished (as games should!)-  Very easy; it's more of a casual game than a deep tactical one (and has zero strategy)-  Good variety of enemies but they are all extremely dumb and will rarely surprise you-  Script writing and voice acting very hammy (character's yell things like 'let's get tactical!') -  Narrative arc is about as engaging as Doom, just go with it :p-  Art design makes Warhammer look thoughtful and restrained-  Inventory management and upgrading is a grindy chore and doesn't feel good at all-  Side missions are pretty limited and quickly get repetitiveOn balance, I'd give it a just-about-thumbs-up-for-something-to-kill-a-few-hours-during-lockdown except that it's far too expensive at $60 and requiring a Microsoft sign-in to play is just not something I want to support as a player (that said, after the first time you sign in, it is possible to play in Steam's offline mode if you prefer). So it ultimately gets a thumbs down from me on the grounds of price and evil corporate douche-baggery.

_childDocuments_.review: Really excellent turn-based strategy. You've probably heard this comparison before, but it's a stripped-down XCOM with a Gears wrapper. I played through it first on Experienced difficulty and found it to be an excellent challenge with little to no RNG nonsense that couldn't be puzzled through. Pros: -Tells a bit more of the GOW story. Neat! -Combat presents a fun, strategic combat puzzle.-Solid gameplay UI and systems that (mostly) make intuitive sense. -A gun with a chainsaw on it. Tactics! -Boomers shout BOOM before attacking.-Giant meatfridge men/women sliding into waist high cover and shooting at aliens. -Really fun boss battles.Cons: -Unit customization UI is SUPER janky and hard to navigate. -Not terribly complex combat mechanics, and no base-building between missions. -No active reload from the mainline series, so therefor the amount of times someone shouts "OH YEAH" after slamming a magazine home is lower than I'd like.-Boomers take approx. 3 minutes to move before they shout BOOM and attack.-The main character, Gabe, has apparently seen a ghost by the white streak in his hair. _childDocuments_.review: Only a few hours in...This is not XCOM. It is a squad-based tactical game that mostly focuses on the AI being a constant onslaught of attacking enemies. There is strategy and tactics to be played here for sure, but not in the ambush/setting up a cascade of events style of XCOM. It's more about positioning correctly and being able to survive long battles and interrupting your enemy. Overwatch in this game is your big interrupt tool, and you'll use it very often. So will the enemy.I do like it, but it's very frustrating and feels a bit unfair even on the lower end difficulties. Enemies will spawn and get a move in the same turn, things like that. I do want to say though, you have to play by this game's rules and not XCOM. You will have a much better time.

They took a turn based game and really made it their own.The combat is fun and the boss battles are a highlight to that combat however the game is not without flaws.The gear system is kinda boring and there really is nothing to do between missions (aka no base or research, etc.)  The story is fine but it does really love to drop the "fascist" word for no reason other then its popular to say so lately.The game was fun but kinda short-medium length, coming in at 25 hours for myself.  A-lot of this from side missions which are okay but repetitive, the actual main missions though were always way more fun.  I hope to see more of this expanded in the future and hopefully with some added home base sort of stuff.  overall 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Chainsaws.It's like XCOM or Mutant: Year Zero, but you don't have to constantly hide and be afraid to move. Or play save-load-save-load game. Gears Tactics actually rewards you for being super-aggressive, and this change of pace is very welcome. I mean, I never knew I needed that. You missed a shot, or you miscalculated a move and your unit is pinned and will most likely lose all health - you don't need to press 'restart checkpoint' - you can recover, fight your way out of this mess and kill the remaining survivors with brutal finishers. Shoot their heads off. Blow them to bits with chainguns. Cut them in half with shotguns. Cut their heads off with Retro-lancer. Turn them into red mist with grenades.This game also has chainsaws.Boss fights. Boss fights are amazing. Boss fights are actually there - every chapter ends with a boss fight, unlike any other turn-based game where crucial missions differ from regular ones by simply having more challenging enemies.Did I mention this game has chainsaws?Insane customization options, dozens of builds. There is no base. No base management. No base at all. All you have to think about is character builds and perks and synergies. Make your sniper shoot like a dozen times per turn? Easy. Make your scout move undetected, blow scores of enemies up with grenades that regenerate every turn and give you AP whenever you use them? You got it. Turn your support into unstoppable unit-buffing healing machine? Here, do it. Enjoy.And while you're busy doing that, bear in mind that this game has chainsaws.Some side-missions become repetitive AF at some point (I'm 30 hours in, so some things are getting old already), you can still miss with 95% hit chance, some textures take a bit too long to pop up, - other than that, this game is really really good. Chainsaws.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say Gears Tactics is a great game, and if I'm being completely honest, it is really good. There's so much to like, the story, the characters, the customization, the unique ways you can build your characters, pretty decent levels of variety. It's a great tactics game. I might even like it more than X-com.GT stars 4 characters for the most part, I wish it starred who you wanted it to star, and that is one of its biggest failings, while that does annoy me, that Narrative is pretty good, so, I forgive the controlled way GT handles story missions. Your main Character is Gabe Diaz, a Motorpool Soldier. He's not keen on the COG's well... COGiness. He gets picked to do a mission, and in normalized Gears fashion, with the usual level of drama involved. In all honesty the story's far better than I expected. I like the majority of the cast, and the voice work is well done as well.Basic UI for the main menu allows you to elect units and missions, selecting units allows a full set of customizations in Helmet, Armor, and Leg Armor, Main weapon, Secondary Weapon, and Grenades. For non story characters you also can customize just about everything on a person save the skin tone, voice, and facial structure. There's a lot, and you unlock more as the game moves on. In this menu you also can upgrade units. Each level gives you 2 customization points for their abilities, each ability is outlined in the menu pretty clearly and follows a path selection method(Must have adjacent to be selected as an upgrade). This can result in having to take abilities you don't want, but, most abilities are useful in their own right.Along with this, Equipment has abilities of it's own, and the rarer the equipment is, the more powerful its stat boosts and latent abilities will be. Generally speaking, Armor has "lines" meaning, it isn't randomized. So getting a specific chestpiece with a specific ability in the "rare" class, will be identical to anything else with that name in other classes.The basic turn structure works like this: Your team moves, and can interact with any of their abilities on your own turn, there are abilities that allow your team members to act in very specific ways on your opponents' turn, but in general, all combat on your side, is done on your turn, and your opponents have the same restrictions. You can move and take cover with your units (1/2 and full cover) with each level of cover adding more defense, and evasion. You will have a specific number of action points to perform actions for each unit you have. Once all are spent, or you pass, your turn ends. The CPU then gets to act, and when it's done, control is resumed to the player.In general I'm being somewhat vague because rules are basically meant to be broken. You'll learn pretty quickly that starting AP and cooldowns are somewhat meaningless as you can artificially boost them in a ton of ways. The ability to customize your characters to this extent is glorious, and really makes playing the game fun when you're on largely equal footing, and the game's giving you missions with somewhat rational levels of enemies for the difficulty you're playing at.And now we get to the boss fights. Every single boss fight on higher difficulties is a slog. Notice I didn't say "hard" I didn't say "cheap". The game in my opinion, is balanced poorly for these fights. The Bosses themselves are trivial. But the bosses have abilities which make you move your characters or risk damage/dying. So you have to move, which consumes AP. But the game also tends to drop obscene amounts of enemies as well. So not only will you need to move, wasting AP, you'll need to also take care of enemies as they're released, which eat up AP, leaving you very limited AP to deal with the boss. Sometimes none at all. Coupled with mechanics in the game that it will blatantly tell you to do to soften the boss up, despite those things effectively just wasting turns and putting you at further disadvantage, Boss fights tend to be irritating battles with RNG rolls because no matter what level of accuracy you have, your characters are all blind. This is fine in general play. This is NOT fine when the entire battle strategy can hinge on one guy landing hit at 67% and you get unlucky 2-3 times. This usually ends up with someone downed, and it's all downhill from there. Losing your foothold on crowd control will likely break the rest of the battle. There's only so much positioning can help, when optimal position often isn't possible to choose due to battlefield control by the boss. Like I said, this isn't as prevalent in the main game, though it can happen, and there, it's usually much more your fault.But if anything, that's the only real failing. Perhaps the issues I've mentioned can be fixed. I'd just play on Normal if I could go back and tell myself anything. I didn't feel challenged by the boss fights, I just felt annoyed. Coupled with the in general, very limited levels of strategy I'm allowed to use in them on builds, they damage the experience considerably. Killing 8 mixed enemies, moving, and still having enough tenacity left to shoot the boss's kill me button every 2 turns is an exercise in tedium, not in challenge, and it mars an otherwise great experience. You'll blow through act after act, no problem only to be stuck replaying the boss over and over until the battle can be cheezed through with broke as heck character builds, or you manage to go through the RNG with the required level of failed shots, which is generally limited.After the game, veteran missions increase challenges for your squad, and give you more of the side missions you've come to expect. Giving you rarer and rarer stuff until you're kitted with pure legendary. If that's your bag. But there is an endgame for those interested. There doesn't seem to be a new Game Plus however. You can up the difficulty again and restart if you wish, but, again, as I've stated, I think than in it's current form, just makes things more tedious, not actually harder, and generally only on boss fights. Everything else... is largely fine, You can break this game quite handily enough on any difficulty selection. It just depends on how much you want your life to suck at the beginning in that case.Do I recommend it? Absolutely. But just know higher levels of difficulty are... less rewarding than they could be. Also, don't go into this thinking it's a knock off of Xcom. It is, but it isn't as deep into R&D, nor character building. But it has still got plenty to play with and mess around with if you like that sort of stuff. There's definitely min-maxy stuff for those people, but the way cases generate for new equipment is random, with no way to force creations, and sadly no way to sell crap tier equipment either, which is annoying because you can't "Build" a team member, you just have to hope you get the parts you need to min max their build through RNG. Thankfully, there's no microtransactions anywhere I can see.But, this series actually works pretty well in this environment. Worth a play.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the X-Com games, and a lot of other turn based games so I thought this would fit into my tastes, and it did perfectly.I really dig the gear and skill progression systems, and I really enjoy the combat, although playing the game on normal difficulty left me completing some missions without taking a hit. Maybe with a bunch of experience with turn based games, you should try a tougher difficulty setting. The voicing was quite good, and I experienced a very glitch-free game. It felt like they made a really good, well polished turn based shooter with some fun grindy post-game to enjoyOn the negative side, the missions started feeling kind of repetitive sooner then I would have liked. There are only a few different mission formats, and they get cycled pretty regularly. It had me scratching my head when I was being chased by a creeping barrage for the 4th time. Another part I didn't like was a system they have that forces the player to change up who goes on a mission. Basically you alternate between doing a single story mission (you can pick anyone, woopwoop!), and then having to complete 3 missions of a selection of 4, but you can't use the same unit twice. So your active roster is 12 different units. This wouldn't be too bad, except you "recruit" new units quite frequently that start at a higher level then some of your existing units, so you're constantly retiring a chunk of your active roster. I'm not sure what the idea there was. Maybe you're supposed to have units die fairly frequently and constantly need to fill your roster?I feel like over all, I really enjoyed this game, even though the mission selection can feel repetitive and I didn't get to bond well with a lot of the non-story units. If they had a paid DLC that added more content, I'd buy it for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Gear of war tactical should be the entry game for people to learn how a tactical top down strategy game works without too much of the repercusions holding you back from experiencing the real value of this game. Gears adds a personal mechanic to the game where executions, something the Gears genre is known for, gives you extra action points you can spend on your turn.I played the game on the almost hardest difficulty with only minimal pre-knowledge of the X-COM Genre and a lot of knowledge about the Gears genre. I was able to finish the game in about 30 hours and due to the great story and untold story in any others Gears game I had to finish it in one weekend. (My GF, was my PC for that weekend)All by all, there were a couple of bugs that certain combinations you would think work, didn't work, but overall I would really recommend to play this game to people that are:- Big gears of war fans and want to see a story that was never told before- People who want to experience a tactical top down shooter for the first time but think X-COM is too agresive or punishing - People that just want to have a good time playing a single player video game and take a break from online toxicity.I would give this game a solid 8.5/10 as there were a couple of bugs / sometimes the game didn't give enough hints on how to finish certain end bosses causing me to lose about 2 hours into something pretty obvious. some levels could also only be completed with maximum points / stars once you reloaded a checkpoint a couple of times because suddenly a E-HOLE opened in the most stupid location possible. I think the score would have been lower if I did not was such a Gears fan as the story for me was the most important. 8.5 might be biased, but a 7.5/10 would be a more generic score I would guess.

_childDocuments_.review: The good news is: It's a Gears turn-based strategy game. The bad news is: It's a Gears turn-based strategy game.What you get is an almost adequate re-skinned XCom, in which good graphics, smooth functionality and useful skills barely compensate for repetitive missions, constant map re-usage and occasional but insomnia-curing boss combats. All of this is wrapped up in the classic Gears aesthetic which was bad enough to make GOW an instant uninstall & refund failure and has hardly improved with this - pre-teen fantasy wooden cliche meatheads fighting slightly differently textured wooden cliche meatheads. Whereas, say, MYZ had instantly endearing characters, WH40K Mechanicus had fresh and interesting races, and BTech had ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ battlemechs, the characters in this were half-heartedly loathable straight away and this improved only marginally with the distant perspective and acquiring helmets to cover their moronic visages. You can't polish a turd and serving that turd in a different format is scarcely better.If you've played all the vastly superior TBS games in the last few years and want yet more generic TBS to pass the time, this may well serve that purpose (as it did for me, with a lot of very casual hours in). If you've played all the Gears games and want yet more Gears, this will serve as a timely remind to book your lobotomy appointment.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a ton of fun. Very similar to XCOM but with the focus more towards the fun action side and less on the unforgiving tactics side. Be warned that there are quite a few bugs. The game froze several times on the enemies turn causing me to have to reload to a past checkpoint or start the mission over again. Additionally, a few of the achievements did not work either. For example, I beat the game but I did not unlock the achievement that I killed 10 enemies. So will this game is a lot of fun and an enjoyable experience, do note that there are a few issues.

_childDocuments_.review: It was good to a point, once you complete the story line the game is over. There is veteran mode, which I thought ends. It doesn't and is the same repetitive missions over and over again. The actual story is fairly basic but doesn't really allow you to get your gears levelled up past 6. Highest level I think is 10. I am a massive XCOM and phoenix point player so didn't really find it overly challenging and compared to these titles, it doesn't come close. No base building, just gears on a map doing tbs. Weapon mods/armour mods/customising skills is the only thing you get to do. Would have been nice if it was more XCOM with Map phase and choosing missions that had consequences down the line. The story is ok, not overly exciting. Would buy it on super special or if your a Gear head(not the rick and morty one).

_childDocuments_.review: PRO: The combat system is very, very interesting compared with anything we've seen before. That execute mechanic is like a double edge sword. The enemies are very interesting and smart, you will be surprised how many times they will flank you instead of going straight into your overwatch. Lots of maps to play around, the story is very good, boss fights interesting, but a-bit easy imo. Lots and lots of equipment to customize your troops and probably the coolest thing, is the amount of variation in specs. Each class can be divided in 4 sub-classes, each one will have a different style of play. CONS: This is not X-Com2. Period. I would't say is better or worst, it's different. (again, the combat system is very good, probably better that X-Com). The most noticeable difference is the lack of any MAP or BASE mechanics or game-play. Another aspect, it will be the amount of extra recruits you have for free. Most of them just can be recruited at your current level, making the connection with older character, a-bit strange. For devs: Please add some filters for all that equipment. Is a-bit hard to navigate through all of them before each battle.

_childDocuments_.review: Many reviews claimed this game is like Xcom. It's true in the same way halo is like Doom 2. It's clear that Xcom revived the tactical RPG genre and became the new canvas to draw from, and many of the ideas you already saw in Xcom. However, the game , in my opinion , is doing enough to iterate on those ideas that it manage to stand out as on it's own unique experience. And how is it ? So far, really good.What I really liked is how much movement and freedom there is on the battlefield . Your movement isn't limited to a grid, you can move freely as you like and that only thing that counts is distance. The same is true for cover. While you can find the usual square rooms and boxes covers , you can also find covers placed more randomly and on an angle, making it feels more like a place and less like a level. Physics also play some role, I shot at an enemy, and it cased him to stagger and fall down an hole. I expected the game to glitch , but instead he ragdoled and died. It's not half life, but I was impressed when it happend.Lastly, GT goes for a more traditional story approach, There's no strategic layer like in Xcom and other games that tried to be Xcom,  instead you get a linear story line with premade missions. And  I think it's was a good choice. Not any tactical game needs to be like Total war, sometimes it worth having a well made series of missions, and so far they are well made. Overall I'm really impressed and enjoying the game so far.

_childDocuments_.review: My first  experience was about three years ago with , and the only games I've played since then were  and . I also love turn based tactics such as  so it is the perfect game for me. I usually play them in short bursts (1-2 hours per day), which is why it took me so long to review the game. I completed the campaign on "experienced" difficulty and it was a blast from start to finish.::This game is actually a prequel and takes place 12 years before the events of the first  (and is somewhat related to characters in ). You mainly play as Gabe Diaz, and your objective is to recruit and command your squadmates in missions and battles to locate and hunt down , the mastermind (and very one-dimensional) monster and locust leader who creates locusts and other horrid monsters. The story is okay and simple to understand, there aren't any big surprises along the way so keep your expectations to a minimum when it comes to story.You will meet and recruit important side characters in the game, such as Sid Redburn, a Gear of the Coalition of Ordered Governments (COG) Army who will assist you in various missions and boss battles. Unfortunately, characters such as Sid are very Cliche and not very interesting. However, the cutscenes are solid and I like some of the banters between the characters, as the voice acting is excellent in this game. Overall the story is alright, nothing groundbreaking and doesn't really add anything new to the lore, if you don't count Ukkon and Gabe Diaz.If you are familiar with  then you will feel right at home. You can choose up to four soldiers, and every turn is filled with tension; your every move can lead to different surprises and consequences, while keeping in mind the risks of missing a shot from your weapon and/or the appearance of more enemies mid-battle. I played the game on "experienced" difficulty, which I highly recommend for your first playthrough, and you will unlock the "insane" difficulty (literally) once you defeat the final boss. Every soldier has three actions per turn (or more depending on the soldier's skills), and you have to use them wisely. You can use the action points to shoot three times, move to a different spot, use special skills or abilities, overwatch, heal or revive your squadmate, or a combination of them. One cool feature is that if one soldier executes a downed enemy, it will give an extra action point for the rest of the squadmates.:There are two types of soldiers that you can control in the game: Troops and Heroes. Heroes are characters that have a role in the story and take part in the cutscenes, and there are only four of them (five if you count the preorder bonus). They are not different from the troops when it comes to gameplay and skills, but if a Hero dies in a mission then it's gameover and you have to restart. However, Troops are soldiers that you can recruit from the recruitment pool between missions (or from the Rescue missions) and they are expendable, so if one dies then you can continue with the mission like normal (depending on the mission's objectives).There are five different classes in the game: Support, Vanguard, Heavy, Scout and Sniper. Each class has its own type of weapon, customizations, skills and abilities that you can unlock while progressing through the campaign. The customization options in this game is great, as you can change and customize your armor and appearance between missions, and they will even appear in the game's cutscenes. Each class use its own weapon and cannot be changed, but you can upgrade it with mods and upgrades that you find in the field or from mission rewards. :There are a total of three acts in the game each act has about 7-8 story missions (or chapters). Every now and then, you have to complete different side missions to progress and unlock the next story missions. Those side missions can be daunting, as you will be repeating the same four types of missions numerous times during your playthrough, especially in the final act. There are only four types of missions in the campaign: Control, Scavenger, Rescue, and Sabotage/Incursion (Kill all the enemies to sabotage/collect their cache). It would have been better if they made them optional instead of a requirement to unlock the next chapter, or add more mission types instead. The "endgame" after defeating the final boss is disappointing, as it is just multiple side missions that you can complete to earn better gear and upgrades for your soldiers.:The game has a good variety of enemy units, and it forces you to think creatively and set up new strategies when certain enemies appear during missions. There are more than ten types of enemies and all of them are well known in the  universe; from the common Hammerburst Drone to Tickers (insect-looking suicide bombers). You can pick up dropped weapons from certain enemies, such as the Boomer that carries a heavy impact grenade launcher, which can be a great gameplay advantage. The enemy AI is smart and can definitely pack a punch (especially in the experienced/insane difficulty), it can be creative and flank you from all sides and pin you down, even the weakest enemy (Wretches in this case) can be the most dangerous when they attack in large numbers.:There are a total of three bosses in the game, and you fight one at the end of each act. The bosses already exist in the  universe and two of which can be seen in the game's poster. However, the identity of the final boss really surprised me and it took me roughly two hours to defeat the boss, and it was an intense battle for sure. is a beautiful-looking game with very detailed environments and excellent in-game cinematics. You have almost full control over the graphics settings, and you can even see before and after pictures if you want to tweak some of the settings. It ran beautifully on my GTX 1070 Laptop. There were a few minor bugs in the game, from audio sync issues during cutscenes, unable to move a certain soldier (only happened once before the first patch) and a soldier's helmet was still showing even after turning the visibility off, but nothing game-breaking.  is very well-optimized with buttery smooth 60 fps, and never crashed during my playthrough. The soundtrack is fine, similar to the previous  games and not really memorable, but it fits with the game's moody atmosphere and intense gameplay. It took me about 30 hours to complete the campaign and I am surprised how good it was, considering that this is  first strategy game. Whether you are a fan of the franchise or not, or a fan that never played a strategy game like  before, it is a good one and definitely worth your time. Fun and intense gameplay, amazing graphics, and just a damn good turn-based strategy game.and I can see myself replaying it later.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 - Serviceable entry in TBT genre+ Gameplay mechanics tantalizing with novel new ideas introducing squad combos and super combos+ Stable engine, well optimized with no crashes+ Great setting with wonderful lore spanning back to GoW+ Enemy variety fantastic each suggesting different tactics+ Good gradual difficulty curve with unexpected endgame spikes (side-missions /w limited toons)+ Shiny gameplay UI enhances the experience without clutter+ Excellent usability and tutorial to ease you in+ Skills, gear, classes and mission types provide extensive variety of bloody fun+ Boss fight Hollywood style set pieces glorious+ Great to see migration of down/revive systems re-purposed- Ugly art direction- Darn ugly characters- squad size of 4 is a huge step back from even modern xcom(6) - compared to apocalypse its laughable(36)- Loot box-style items in a single player campaign - putrid- Mission variety vanilla and grows old fast - goals generic and derivative of better predecessors- Story aimed at pre-teens; dialog repetition of cliché after cliché- Game embodies 'generic' - devs playing it too safe

_childDocuments_.review: Both Gears 5 and Gears Tactics pleasantly surprised me.Great games both of them, though I played Tactics more.The game is similar to X-COM in terms of its gameplay; isometric, turn-based, with RPG and progression elements. The gory nature of the Gears series really shines through, and better than X-COM, the hit-chance percentages are consistent with what you see on the screen (i.e. no one step away from enemy -> %50 hit chance).The game looks great, plays good and is responsive; the story seems to be OK as well, though I definitely focused more on the gameplay.One downside is the rather limited gear progression. Skills are expansive and allow for variety between the same types of soldiers, but the weapons and armor are mostly drops that you get as bonus pick-ups in missions or for mission completions. X-COM offers an amazing variety in that sense, however, Gears Tactics still pulls through as a great representative of the genre.

You get so much equipment and it is so often upgraded that optimising your loadout before each mission is a chore.The variety among classes and the different skill trees within each class are great and I have enjoyed exploring the various options. _childDocuments_.review: Finished the campaign on Experienced. This is one of those games that I actually really enjoyed playing till the end, but unfortunately cannot recommend it at it current state.Being an avid XCOM fan, I was really looking forward to this game. Promising top-notch graphics, a story-based campaign,  a more *active* gameplay through the execution mechanics, lots of customization options, endless replayability through the veteran missions, needless to say I was very excited, they don't make these kinds of games enough.Let's talk about the positives first:+ The game *looks*, *sounds*, *feels* and *plays* great, which I cannot really say many tactics games have all at the same time.... aaaand, yeah that's about it. Now about the negatives:- The squad. You can only take a maximum of 4 units in a mission, and some missions even force you to take 2, or even 1 unit. In most campaign missions, you are stuck with the hero characters, which is not necessarily a bad thing, but to me it just feels very limiting. Reducing the number of units to 2 or 1 could be nice for those looking for a challenge, but it just does not feel *fun* to me.- The story. For a game which uses "story-based campaign" as one of its main selling point, the story feels really lacking. It's like, it's just there.- The missions. Wow, I thought those Day-1 reviewers were exaggerating when they said that the missions were repetitive, well they weren't. There are only several types of missions, scavenger run, rescue, incursion, sabotage, control, and even the campaign missions are a variation of those types, this is really disappointing.- Leveling up. Takes waaaaay too slow, and you get new recruits who outlevel your veterans very quickly, even after you take said veterans in most side and story missions in the hope of leveling them up. Kinda pushes you to dismiss veterans and take in new recruits since you'll just be handicapping yourself by sticking with the ones you had since the beginning. For a role-player, this sucks.- Inventory. It is kinda cumbersome, but it doesn't bother me too much. I sure hope the devs will not abandon the game and expand upon it with updates. I wouldn't mind getting DLCs and expansions if they add a substantial amount of gameplay and address the issues mentioned above. Please take a look at other tactics games, see what made them enjoyable and successful, and expand upon those aspects.For those of you interested in the genre, I would recommend that you either try this on Xbox Game Pass, or wait until it gets a few more updates and gets more fleshed out before you commit. If you don't have high expectations and are mostly okay with the negatives above, by all means get it, but wait for a sale. XCOM and XCOM 2 are vastly better games, and they are much much cheaper and frequently go on sale.I sure hope I will be able to recommend this game in the future.EDIT: Minor additions and formatting.

_childDocuments_.review: Right of the bat, I got this for $60 CAD bundled with Gears 5 and I haven't played a whole lot of it yet. Here are some things to note:I play on an Asus Predator 3440 x 1440p, 120hz monitor.I have a RTX 2080ti paired with a Ryzen 2700x and 16GB of Ram.All of my games run off of a 1TB SSD.The game itself supports ultrawide not only in game play, but also in the majority of cut scenes. The cut scenes can also be locked to 30 be set to unlimited frame rate if you so desire. There is a built in benchmarking too which is pretty much accurate, except for the GPU usage from what I found. My GPU in Rivia Tuner was saying 95% usage while the in game bench said 88% usage. Its not a huge deal, but something to keep in mind if you worry about that kind of thing. Playing on high settings I was able to get around 80 fps while in ultrawide at 3440 x 1440p. By default with ever preset vsync is turned on so be sure to turn that off if your monitor has gsync or freesync. The majority of the high presets are actually ultra so if you're struggling you may want to actually custom set your visuals for high as opposed to just going with that preset.Game play wise, I used m/kb. Keyboard is used to move the camera (along with the mouse. Its an either or situation) as well as used for hotkey to weapons. the LMB is used to confirm each action. This is pretty basic stuff for a turn based tactics game. The game play loop is your basic Xcom style where you kit out Gears, upgrade their skills, and even recruit new Gears all from your base. Then you go on a mission. Each mission opens with a cut scene, every time a new enemy type is introduced you're given another cut scene + enemy title card and every mission ends with a cut scene. One thing I have found, and this may just be user error, is that I'll kill off the majority of the enmies and the game will update the mission to simply reaching the goal marked out at the beginning of the map. Then after a few turns new enemies are put on the map and I found my characters out of position. It could be user error like I've stated, I just feel as though there is no distinction between when you've killed all the enemies & need to move to the end point to continue and when you're moving to simply spawn the next enemies.Over all the game is visually amazing. The sound is top notch. The story moves along. The abilities are fun to use, its great that cut scenes can be customized to the users liking and I highly recommend this game for a purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Gears Tactics is a very enjoyable turn-based tactics game in the XCOM vein, and as a first entry into the genre by this dev team is well worth your money in the next sale. As XCOM is the big name here I will be comparing the two games throughout this review.The tactical battles are very like XCOM, with a few tweaks, all positive. The versatile three-action system makes the battles feel slightly deeper than XCOM's simpler move-action. The cover-moving is clever and kinetically satisfying. The best addition is the show-off executions of enemy units that give all other units a bonus action. This keeps the gameplay flowing very smoothly and energetically, a far better and more organic solution to the overwatch-creep problem than XCOM 2's much-hated timers. This is aided by the enemy units here generally being far weaker than XCOM's enemies relative to the player's units, which adds to the sense of glorious carnage. It is a similar feel to XCOM 2's missions against the Lost. The key exception to this is that Gears Tactics has boss battles. These are a little grindy, as boss battles tend to be, but make a nice change of pace.Unlike XCOM, there is no strategic layer other than upgrading your troops, both their skills and also their equipment using looted items. You can't even sell unwanted loot, or craft them into better loot. They will just stay clogging up your interface forever, which is a loss to the game. The five player unit classes cover the necessary bases and are very similar to XCOM's four classes. The skill upgrade system is very well designed and allows for each unit to be customised how you would like. During the main campaign I felt that XP should be earned faster, but after the campaign you can continue to play indefinitely in veteran missions, so the slightly slower pace of XP gain makes more sense now. However, be aware that you will constantly get free units that are far higher rank than your existing squad, so don't get attached to your minor characters, and don't waste time bringing them on missions unnecessarily to train them up. This is a minor balancing issue that could easily be fixed if they make a sequel.The story is extremely silly, honestly. I gather this is a legacy of the game's setting in the Gears of War franchise, which I have not played, and ties in closely to the plot of that series' later games. This silliness does not get in the way of the enjoyment though. As with most strategy games, it starts to drag just a little by the end of the campaign, especially because there are slightly too many side missions and not quite enough variety in the mission design. But the campaign ends at about the right point overall: there is less dragging than in most other similar games.The graphics and art design are very beautiful, though the Unreal Engine is a little plasticky as usual, and there is insufficient variety in the look and feel of the levels. Perhaps this is compelled by the Gears of War setting; I don't know. Whereas XCOM benefits from a wide variety of maps, Gears Tactics' maps are all ruined sci-fi cities in yellow deserts. This is fine at setting the scene, but does not aid replayability.Overall this is a very good entry in the turn-based tactics genre that will be enjoyed by XCOM players who want to focus on the battles without the strategic layer getting in the way. At launch, the game cost 50 UK pounds (US$ 60). This was frankly far too high, and the game soon fell in price to £35 (US$ 40). That wouldn't be a wholly unreasonable price in itself if you're keen on XCOM and looking for another game like it. But in the Steam sales Gears Tactics can now be had for as little as £8.74 (US$ 10), which is an absolute steal. If you like turn-based tactics games at all, you should absolutely buy this without a moment's hesitation the next time you see it available for such a bargain. A good time for a low price: what more could you ask?

_childDocuments_.review: Gears Tactics is an odd paradox of sorts. The game certainly tries to make itself different from XCOM (specifically two, lets be honest) but fell into some of the same pitfalls early on. While Gears Tactics has much better performance, it is certainly lacking in the departments that matter. I certainly felt more on edge when playing this game, but for the wrong reasons. Not because the game is hard, which it isn't for the most part. The only difficulty I ever felt playing this game was The Act 1 Boss Fight, and certain Side Missions with absolutely brutal modifiers. I felt more on edge simply because the checkpoint system is absolutely terrible. While it certainly stops me from save scumming (we all do it, lets be honest) the checkpoints are so sparse that often half the mission will only be considered a single checkpoint.Overall, is Gears Tactics a good game? Yes. I think so. Should you buy it for the full price? Probably not. I would wait for a sale. Until The Devs add more things to the game or hell, allow mods, I think Gears Tactics will be a worthy competitor to XCOM. But until then, Gears Tactics is an interesting, but inferior, game to XCOM 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game if you're into XCOM. The story is pretty bland but the graphics and cut scenes are excellent. Still feels a little anti-climactic.  I like the direction this game is taking and I hope the developer can focus more on cool boss fights, the first big boss fight (Brumak), was amazing! Pros-Great soundtrack. At times the music made it feel like "Starship Troopers" the movie. -Awesome combat system. The combat system is well put together and there are times when living or dying boils down to a single choice you make. Very exciting and satisfying to slice and dice enemies.-Great level design. Most of the settings take place in the desert or bombarded cityscapes. Visually pleasing to navigate through the levels.-Great boss fights. The bosses are unique and well thought out. Giant "stranger things" spiders, and huge monsters with cyborg helmets! I loved the boss fights, and to me they were the highlight of the game. Each boss has a unique weakness and you need to think on your feet and act fast!-Great concepts and skill tree progression. There are 5 different classes (support, vanguard, heavy, sniper, scout). Each with unique skill tree perks. Each class can be divided into 4 different sections, for example, a scout that use stealth or a scout that focuses on explosives. The perks actually make a difference during the missions and are pretty cool to see them in action.-Challenging, I played this on Hard and I really appreciated how challenging some of the missions were. Cons-Too few boss fights. It's a shame there were only 3 big boss fights. They were what made this game amazing. If they had around 8 unique boss fights, I would give Gears tactics a perfect score.-Actual story is not deep enough to get me attached to the main characters.-Inventory system is messy and confusing. When you get a new item and try to search for it, the item gets lost in a sea of weapon mods or equipment mods from previous battles. The developers should find a better way to catalogue weapon mods and equipment.-Side missions are mandatory between story missions. These side missions are the same between every mission. Rescue survivors, outrun the enemy bombs, capture and hold 2 points for a set amount of time and a "reach the gate and eliminate all enemies". At the earlier stages of the game, theses were pretty fun but because they are mandatory between the story missions, it gets repetitive and boring after a while.-Customising unit appearance means absolutely nothing. Because the game is played from a top-down view, the units appear pretty small. Unit size isn't large enough to see the changes you've made to the unit.  -Low replay value. Unless you like rinse and repeating the same missions, there isn't a big reason to replay this game. -Must login to Microsoft account in order to playI advise you all to wait till this game is on sale or until they add game changing DLC like XCOM War of the Chosen. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If you, like me, having been looking for a turn based game that comes close to the joy that XCOM brings Gears Tactics come pretty close!   Gears Tactics brings a lot of goodies, great graphics, decent story, excellent combat mechanics, and it's just plain fun.   Since this is essentially an XCOM clone in the Gears game world it does come up a little short when compared to XCOM.  Depth is a big one,  you don't have near the depth of gameplay that you do in XCOM.  No research trees for equipment or management of resources to build equipment.  I did like the skill tree approach in Gears and that each class has up to four sub classes based on skill tree choices, however like some other reviews have mentioned I never felt committed to any of my squad member, you are often rewarded with classes that come in at a higher skill than those you have been working with and it's just easier to swap them out (and you don't feel bad about it either).  Game Balance seems pretty good but I never felt the game was that difficult except for one or two missions in the beginning.  There are some slight movement bugs that caused me to restart a mission twice (enemies get stuck and mission won't progress).  The only other 'con' is that I found this game main campaign VERY short when compared to XCOM.   This may be why I didn't feel very attached to my squad members,  by level 6 you have essentially completed the entire game.   At full price that is not much bang for you buck.  I grabbed it on sale and even on sale I felt the game ended to quickly....on the plus side you can continue to play missions.   Environments do become repetitive pretty fast, there are only a handful of side mission types (hold, rescue, scrap collect, sabotage, intel collect).    Still this is a great addition to a limited field of quality turn based action games (IMHO).

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't get all the comments and mostly disagree.Ok, it lacks a bit of the "open-endness" of XCOM, but there are so many interesting elements they brought to the table that XCOM never bothered doing.Just to name a few :* Actual lines of sight and bullet trajectory. Yes, you can shoot your own allies in the way by mistake, or take down 2 enemies at once because the first one got killed by first bullets and second one was behind. This is also true for reaction fires.* Maximum health reduced when you get revived in combat (up to 2/3 reduction after 2 revives, 3rd one is death)* There are less fancy customization options, but the one present are deeper (choose material type for the armor to name one)* Hard difficulties are actually hard and unforgiving. Not ala "You spawned a second wave because you moved too far like in XCOM", but more because combat is brutal and you got to think your engagements* Free movement (no square based grid)* Execution mechanics in battle, which inspires allies and give them back some action points (interesting mechanic to realy think about when playing it the hard way)* AP system (yes, you can shoot twice if you want without a stupid perk) - and AP can raise above 2* Reaction fire actually depending on your action points* Gear pieces with actual buffs, not only stat changes* HP mechanic, no "4-10" HP soldiers loosing 3 HP on hit. Here it counts in hundreds and is an actual calculation to think of when engaging* So many others.I know it gets repetitive (as XCOM does, maybe a bit quicker though) and doesn't do everything perfect. There are also some bad sides. But there are so many interesting new approaches that it feels very fresh, and touched my XCOM vibe after getting so bored of XCOM.If you're a hardcore XCOM veteran you should give it a try. It is definitely an interesting take on the turn based squad battles.Actually there were so many people complaining about its difficulty at release, that it may just be some XCOM fanboys getting teared apart by having to think different and more tactical, now bashing the game for no apparent reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets compared to Xcom and while similar this is a inferior game. I started playing this right after beating Xcom Chimera squad.ProsNon gridbased movement - Xcom should learn from this. Looks better and feels better to move.AP spending - Your given AP to spend how you choose baseline Fire, move, Fire vs move, fire.Gore - Who doesn't like some ultra violenceMehTalent Trees - Not bad but not excitingConsPresentation - Gears isnt really known for its story and this isnt helping. All missions are presented linearly and inorganically like a mission select screen. Each  will have a side objective for extra reward but it doesn't flow naturally like an Xcom game would. Ex. Xcom - Pick up the data from the console for intel bonus while you fight. Gears - Don't have anybody go down for a loot box at the end of the mission.Lootbox - While not the traditional pay for a random reward lootbox each mission your given a random loot crate with gear from white to rare. This could easily become spend money for lootbox in the future.Gear - the gear you get from lootboxes isnt easily classified onto who can use what so youll be fishing through several members and gear lists to try to figure out what all you can equip. Fortunately the game reminds you that you missed equipping so you can try again.Gameplay saving - This system like Xcom has the % chance hit so its inevitable you'll miss two 80% shots leading to a wipe and a load assuming your not on ironman. You can't manually save so you have to go back to a checkpoint which can be several lucky turns ago.Gameplay grenades - Grenades are the most reliable and effective form of damage on a cd which is fine but they are also the primary way of dealing with "Grub holes" which infinitely spawn enemies. Without foreknowledge or grenade hoarding being unable to deal with these the turn they spawn will lead to a load. After a load, I had to keep an enemy alive for several rounds just to wait for my grenade cd so i could deal with what came next. That isn't tactics thats game exploitation and shouldn't be necessary.Side Missions - Wth are these. Mandatory filler missions in between story missions that have no context for lootcrate rewards. Ex. Stand on two spots to fill a supply gauge while enemy forces spawn infinitely to stop you. Why are these spots supply spots? How were we able to leave after completing this?TLDR If you like Xcom and looking for a tactics fix, pass on this game, For 60$ I cant recommend this game to anyone at 30$ this would be more forgivable.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr I've been playing tactical games since X-COM: TFTD and Gears Tactics is...fine. Buy on sale if you like this genre or are a Gears of War fan. Gears Tactics has a very streamlined game-play loop. If you don't like the mucking about in the strategic layer that many games in the Tactical genre have then this is the game for you. You go right into the action with very little overhead between missions. Simply pick your classes, kit them out and go.The big downside of this design decision is that mission fatigue sets in quickly, I found myself having to take a break after 3-4 missions because I was getting tired of doing them. There is nothing else to break things up. Thematically this is a Gears of War game and you absolutely know it the entire time you're playing. A++ on atmosphere. The missions themselves are your typical tactical fare: move your squad, find groups, take them out in detail, deal with any reinforcements. The twist is that the enemy density is pegging the meter for this genre. You are literally mowing down hoards of locust. There are a few different mission types: Control, Rescue and Sabotage to slightly mix up the kill all locust formula. As the game progresses you will also encounter mission modifiers/restrictions to artificially increase the difficulty. That being said, if you're looking for something challenging, this is not the game. The plethora of abilities and ways to break out of the action economy tends to make things very easy despite the number of locust. If you're familiar with the FPS Gears of War games, this is very On Brand for the franchise. You send your squad in against overwhelming odds and they mow down the locust hordes and sate your need for a power fantasy. Lather, rinse, repeat.The maps get repetitive after a while (but this is an issue with almost every game in this genre) but are well designed and have plenty of interesting bottlenecks. In true GoW fashion they are absolutely covered in chest-high walls.The boss battles are honestly; quite tedious. They are basically giant damage sponges with telegraphed AoE one-hit kill attacks that force you to constantly reposition and drag out the encounter. The skill trees for each class are deep. Like...crazy deep. Each class is broken into two subclasses with a couple dozen skills each and you can progress in either or both sub-trees. The abilities are very thematic, synergistic and tend to make your soldiers feel very powerful. This has the downside of making most missions trivial in difficulty. There is some fun to be had in seeing how degenerate you can be in comboing abilities. The game is jam-packed with items, so many items, more items then you know what to do with. By the time you're halfway through a campaign you'll be drowning in items and most of them are trash. I feel like this game thought it might be a loot shooter for a second and decided to go crazy with the mission loot. With so many pieces of armor and weapon mods being thrown at you its really easy to get bogged down in the clunky item management screen. Its a Gears game, its damn pretty. Especially for a game in this genre. Also seems to be well optimized. Ran smoothly on my mid-range PC at high graphics settings. This is a Gears of War game you won't be allowed to forget that for one second. It's got all the crass humor, foul language and excessive gore you would expect from the series. Exploding heads, chainsaw dismemberments and curb-stomps galore. The execution mechanic is very visceral, satisfying, and will remind you of the FPS games in the series. Its technically got one but you won't be playing this game for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I've put a fair amount of time in to the game, but am only about half-way through. But given that nothing new has been introduced mechanics wise in the latter missions, I think I know what I'm in for with the rest of the game.Summary: The game is basically a cookie cutter copy of just the squad maintenance and combat mechanics of XCOM 2. It lacks variety, doesn't do much different and is missing a ton of stuff from XCOM that help break up the experience. It also lacks a lot of "convenience" features for things like managing equipment inventory and a large roster of units. If you all want is a new skin and JUST the mission combat from XCOM then maybe you'll like this. For me, it's a slog and it just reminds me how I should just be playing XCOM 2 again. Pros+ The cinematics are very pretty. The character faces are incredible.+ XCOM 2 style turn based tactical combat.Cons- It's a turn based tactical RPG and it needs a tuning guide to run smoothly? What?!- Very difficult to manage equipment inventory. XCOM had the handy "unequip" all button so that you could put your best equipment on your current squad. In this game, you have to scroll through long lists, try to remember what the equipment abilities are (you have to hover over them and read the tool tip) and also scroll through a separately sorted list of items other squad members are using (who aren't on the mission.)- The game is JUST the squad management and tactical combat. There is no tech research, no base building, no world map to break up the flow of just one combat mission after another. Maybe people want that? But the next con is also a drag...- Not a lot of mission variety so far, I'm at the end of Act 2 and the same side missions repeat over and over again. Collect some boxes. Rescue the hostages. Seems like there is maybe only 3 different types of side missions.- Graphics: The cinematics are great, but man the actual game play graphics. Everything is brown. Character models are really tough to tell apart from each other. No way to zoom in on anything. I've had to customize the characters with silly color coded armor so that I can tell the squad apart during missions. - The only way to easily see type an enemy is to remember how many hit points each type of enemy has. You can't click on an enemy at all. You can't zoom. The models all look pretty similar.- Many missions so far and the first boss fight, there is no way you'd be able to beat them without losing to them multiple times. Maybe this is Gears style but XCOM manages to do this pretty well where you always have a chance in a fight.- Very little equipment variety in actual play. No choice in weapons. Class determines your weapons and you can put some slight mods on them, but they are all mostly the same. You get the exact same gun/armor mods dropping over and over again making the inventory list even more unmanageable. There is no concept of getting rid of equipment. I assume by the end of the game I'll have 100s of items that worthless in the inventory list. - (updated) As others have mentioned, there is no point in wasting time on the non-hero squaddies, you'll just continuously be replacing them with new squaddies you find that are higher level because gaining levels is so slow.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: As a large fan of XCOM and tactics games in general, I have to say I'm really liking what gears is bringing to the table here.I may be a little biased because I already enjoy the gears series... but here is why I think this game is worth a purchase:1) Faster paced gameplay than most tactics games for multiple reasons:    - The AI is just flat out faster to react in this game than in XCOM or similar games. This way you spend less time during         the 'Enemy Turn' phase    - 3 Action points per turn combined with multiple Gears style '1 hit kill' moves makes clearing waves faster.2) The 'execute to add ActionPoints' mechanic adds an unexpected amount of depth to tactical gameplay. Sometimes you really have to think about how you can get the most out of your action economy.3) Skill trees, customization, and weapon / armor gadgets make your army eventually feel like your own and adds some weight to seeing a rookie get gibbed.4) So far (act 1, 4hrs in) the cinematic quality in cuts scenes puts Gears tactics somewhere among the top 5 when it comes to tactics games.There are cons however....It has some serious Zero day issues that I'm sure will be patched shortly.1) In my 4 hours of play time I've had the game crash on me upwards of 6 times with error code GT102.    This says 'update your graphics driver'..... Doesn't help. My Nvidia Driver was already up to date.  2) The game got into a weird state (fixed on restarting the game) where all audio (dialogue) became completely out of sync with lip movement of the characters. Weird...Still. Would recommend for tactics fans. Thumbs up.

Some of the conditions change (ala FFTA on the GBA advance), but its like..."Really guys? This is how you expand it." The game and story is genuinely good, but the padded missions really do make you cringe. I started this morning to wrap up...I did Ch 6 and 7, then I was greated by these 3 options...just finished then...but its like "I only had 3 missions to the end, then you pull this?"If they really wanted to expand it...they should have done it like Tactics Ogre...you are in this section of the castle trying to advance, and you have a boss for each section. Because they rehash the same thing multiple times, it really brings down the experience...anyway just wanted to share the update. ----------I need to qualify the 'recommend' tag I've given this. As a game, its good. Great mechanics. Visuals are fantastic for a tactics game. Story is decent too. I like the main characters and where the arcs go. What's annoying about it is - how they space out the levels. There are about 22ish levels/chapters on this...and staggered every 3 or so, there are 'optional side missions' which aren't optional at all. There are 4 of them, and you need to complete 3 to advance to the main chapter again. I get why they do this...you can't use the same characters again, so it forces you to have a grander squad and level up 'other characters', but...oh my lord is it annoying. The side missions are always the same 1. Go hold two requisition points for 4 turns2. Go rescue 2x  survivors (but you can only take 2 of your squad)3. Go collect these 5x crates4. Go sabotage the enemy virus facility. Come to think of it, a lot of the main story is that too. While I don't mind it so much, when it gets nowhere and the rewards are average...its fairly meh. The thing to stress is 'this is all filler'. If it was truly optional, it wouldn't be bad. The fact that its not...its just annoying. I'm playing on a steamdeck and its silky smooth. My patience is probably higher than if I was playing on a PC, as when it gets annoying, I just put it in sleep mode and come back to it when I'm not annoyed. I'm presently on Act 3, CH 6 (pretty much the end). Again...I like it, but oh my word, did they pad this up...more padding than the walls of a mental asylum at Arkham...FYI - the bosses are pretty cool. I don't want to spoil what they are...you'll know if if you are a gears fan, and the execution is pretty good for being challenging. Overall, very good and would love a Gears Tactics 2...I just hope they can put some actual story rather than padding. I'd rather the game be shorter and without the padding. As an aside, the level up system is fairly trash. The points system is great, but you don't really get enough points...also...you don't really have to level up your side characters, as you can just dismiss them and hire those that are a higher level for free (as such, why waste the time? Just a thought). This is just food for thought and hopefully they do a sequel. I'd buy a sequel if they released one. There is much more good than bad. I've been a massive tactics fan for years (I love third person shooters too), and Final Fantasy Tactics, Tactics Ogre have been games I've loved. It's not an easy format to deliver on. I didn't like Triangle Strategy. Fire Emblem Three Houses didn't grab me either. It's supposed to play like Xcom from what I'm told (I have it, but I just got annoyed with it - I found this better than Xcom 2). It's also a little like Valkyria Chronicles...similar, but, different at the same time. For what my comments are worth to anyone...I'd give this a 7.5-8 out of 10 overall. It's a good first crack by the team with this IP, but it needs some tuning to be great. It's very close though.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It's good, I'm really enjoying my time with it! The Gears universe is captured perfectly & the varied mechanics and classes are fun to experiment with. 8/10If you're not a fan of the Gears franchise, this probably isn't the game that's going to convert you (full disclosure, I've played all the games and really enjoy the franchise). The story and characters are very "Gears" and while its nothing outstanding, the plot is good enough to keep the action moving along.The gameplay is your fairly standard "XCOM" type combat/missions with enough new elements to make things fresh. Using all of your characters varied abilities to perfectly pull off a perfect "combo" of shots, stuns & executions just feels damn satisfying. This especially came to a head in the various well designed boss battles which had me tense the entire time.A favourite element of mine is how distinct the various classes feel. The classes all have rather large skill trees and pairing up different squad members to form a perfect team is key to pulling off the satisfying "combos" mentioned above.The game does seem a bit easy at times, with some missions being a total cakewalk (though even those easy missions are fun, nothing wrong with absolutely steamrolling a bunch of grubs). I've played several tactics games like this before and while I'm not terrible at them, I seem to be doing much better than I would usually be doing in XCOM 2.Some base building/managing elements would have been nice, but not having any isn't detracting at all from the enjoyment I'm having playing the missions.Also, all the executions are awesome!

_childDocuments_.review: Bloody Good Fun!I've played XCOM EU, XCOM2, and Gears 1-5 for a total of at least 600-700 hours, so I was thrilled to a game like come out with great EXECUTION :DPros:-The combat and strategy combination is incredibly satisfying. In particular, the pace of the combat and sheer number of enemies makes it a complete blast, while also maintaining a surprisingly good balance. Having 3 actions (along with bonus actions from executions) does a great job of bridging the play by play strategy of XCOM while also retaining the intensity of Gears of War.-Takes is source material seriously. The story is okay, but I love how true it stays to Gears of War lore itself. The enemies, AI, sliding into cover, executions, and chainsaws are all reused well and with honor to the original 3rd person shooter. -No grid based system. The maps flow and the game feels sleek without having the grid system seen in XCOM. This was a huge win for me personally because it just makes the game feel far more immersive than XCOM in a combat situation.-Static design is both a pro and con for me. It's a pro because the map design is quite pretty, and the missions themselves feel well put together. The choke points, layouts, combat situations, and design feels quite solid.-Combat focus is another pro and con for me. There is minimal work outside of the missions to level up characters and to build a squad, everything else is beating up grubs in various missions. Again, I like this because the gameplay is super fun, and I like that it doesn't make you wait around for more missions to play.-The game looks and sounds great. Play the game with some bass and enjoy the effects. The visuals are outstanding as well.-Bugs are minimal. I encountered one minor bug where I couldn't switch from character to character during a boss fight. Going to the main menu and coming back fixed it. It has also been patched, so well done on the Devs for being responsive and making a pretty clean game.Cons:-I haven't beaten the game yet, but the campaign is most likely not going to be as replayable as XCOM since missions are more static. Though I can see spending an extra 30 hours beating it on a higher difficulty as well. -Combat Focus - Because there isn't a base or research like XCOM, the progression itself is more linear and not as game changing as XCOM unlocks. You'll get a more consistent experience at the cost of variability.-Side Mission Variety - You will replay the same side mission types again. The mission types are fun (rescue, hold down supplies, grab n go, etc). However, it won't take long before you see repeats, albeit with different enemies and maps.Feedback to other reviewers: "This game isn't worth $60". Like everything else in life perspective is key. To some, $60 is a lot of money, and I respect that. However, if you have the money to spare (or invest in the game pass) I can absolutely recommend this game for the price. For 2 dollars an hour, you get 30 hours of solid entertainment at least. Bowling costs more than that at an hourly rate, so I don't know why people gripe about price so much. This doesn't even consider the fact that this game has ZERO micro-transactions or other BS. You get what you pay for which is a well made game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those titles that makes me wish I could rate it something between "thumbs up" or "thumbs down". It feels like an X-Com/Phoenix Point-lite as it's missing the base management, research, and meaningful soldier progression. The campaign is nice enough and the cinematics are a great addition, but it's pretty light on content for the price tag. Which leads to my biggest gripe about the game and the main reason I rate it thumbs down: the "side" missions.The "side" missions in Gears Tactics are not actually side missions. You don't have any option in whether or not you complete them, you just get to pick which mission type you'd rather do from a limited pool of 4 or 5 different templates. The side missions are there to make the campaign feel like there's more meat to it and provide a source of weapon and armor mods that are useless once your main heroes are geared up.The other big issue for me is the lack of meaningful character advancement. Unlike X-Com or Phoenix Point, available recruits scale in level with the campaign. You never feel the dread of losing a soldier you put so much time into leveling up because you can always find a replacement of the same level, often higher level in the recruitment pool. I have yet to actually lose a soldier so I'm not sure if death is permanent or not, but survival of the heroes is often a mission requirement so there's no permadeath for those main characters at least (who eventually fill up your squad anyway.Overall the game is nicely polished (comms often clip into the characters' faces in cinematics) and the gameplay is decent  (the boss fights were a lot of fun but there weren't enough of them), but the game is certainly not worth $60 without either multiplayer or a more fleshed out and varied campaign. Definitely worth picking if it goes on sale for $30.

_childDocuments_.review: * A relatively engaging campaign with both new and old characters* Decent turn-based combat* Extensive weapon and armor customization complete with colors, patterns, metal types and even toggles on armor details* Well-translated Gears of War gameplay to an Xcom format complete with executions/chainsaw kills* Certain missions limit squad sizes for no reasoning other than "we don't want to give the player six soldiers to use" * Overly limited number of respec items, which can be tedious when you receive or recruit soldiers with undesirable traits * Heroes are required for most missions, leaving relatively little room for your own custom soldiers* Mission types can be repetitive with very little variety between them * Lootboxes. Lootboxes, alongside equally randomized mission rewards, are your  means of acquiring new weapon mods and armor pieces. Armor and weapon mods have stats on them that modify gameplay and become essential to certain character builds. You can go the entire campaign without seeing essential armor parts. A single-player turn-based-strategy game is no place for a lootbox system.* Virtually no replay-value. Once you finish the story campaign, you get access to "veteran missions" that are just regular side missions from the campaign. No new-game plus to romp through the campaign again, but with better soldiers* While armor and weapon customization is well done, character customization is a tad limited. You can't choose skin color, voice or various facial features.  Overall I'd say this game is worth a buy, and I'm hoping for a sequel.
