_childDocuments_.review: Gears Tactics is a Turn-based Strategy game set inside of the Gears of War universe.  A sentence I never imagined I'd be saying but yes, even Gears is touching on Turn-based games these days.The game is centered around "you", Gabe, a COG Gear (Basically a Soldier) that works as a mechanic when he's not killing Grubs.  One day he is tasked with the assignment of picking up important documents in a building that is soon to be blown up from the beginning of the Hammerstrikes (Essentially Orbital Bombardment).  Upon doing so, he finds another COG Veteran, Sid, who is now tasked with aiding him in the mission located in the recovered files, finding a local Locust Warlord by the name of Ukkon, this is where the story begins.Over the course of the game, you will be clearing missions, gaining weapon attachments, and leveling your soldiers as your roster of Units expands and as you unlock more and more characters of different classes.  Each class in the game has 4 skill branches that you can divide your points gained on Level Up into as you see fit, until you complete the game for the first time, you'll have limited Resets for the Skill Tree.  Within the progression of Main Missions, you will also unlock more Character Customization Options.As a player of a lot of Turn-based Tactics or TBS Games, I selected the highest available difficulty and got a surprisingly good challenge for what was being presented to me.  The game Utilizes the Overwatch System of a game like Phoenix Point, with the ability to set the range of the arc of your Overwatch, which I've heard some people like a lot so, I'm mentioning it.  On the Difficulty I was playing on, Enemies were easily able to down my Units if I made a tactical misplay, and even when playing Safe, sometimes I was caught off-guard by enemies that were concealed, or perhaps poor management of things like my grenades and skills would sometimes put me in sticky situations.  That being said though, the game was not exceedingly difficult, and learning good Unit Cohesion and what abilities are at your disposal, as well as how to properly utilize the Movement System, will allow you to have an edge against your opponents.The game does a lot of things very well, combat feels pretty good, it's not terribly long, but it's not too short, and it's got a fair bit of danger to it, while still giving you some safety nets for any accidents that may occur.  Should a character go down, if you immediately swap onto the defensive, you will likely be able to resolve the Combat Engagement fairly effectively.  Enemy Variety is okay, in my 40 hours of playing, I likely saw somewhere between 10-15 different types of enemies, not including the One-Time Boss Opponents.  The combat can be hard, and does require a bit of thinking, but when applied you can do things that are very cool, and sometimes turn dire situations around by conserving the use of a skill until the right moment.All around this game does a lot of things right, and I can't complain excessively about many things.  The story is passable (In True Gears Fashion) and the combat feels good, but if I had to address any problems, it'd probably have to be the play-time, and the side missions.The game doesn't have much of an exterior strategy layer outside of managing your soldiers skills and their equipment.  The only means of getting equipment is by completing missions and picking up Gear Crates.  This means that between each mission, you're gonna be just putting on the better set of the same armor set that best fits your characters, while also customizing any new characters you wanna add to the Roster.  This means that by about 2/3s of the way through the game, your characters have gotten all the way to the end of at LEAST one skill tree, and you've encountered most enemy types, have seen most mission types, and have pretty much played most of the content that is there to offer.  This wouldn't be so bad as long as the story kept you going but by this point you need to do 3 side missions in between each main mission, so if you're getting kinda worn down and just wanna progress the game?  You have to do 3 of the 4 available side missions first.  The Side Missions have unique modifiers that make it more interesting, such as what units you can or cannot deploy, how many guys you start with, and other unique stuff like doubled enemy accuracy at max health, less Action Points, or more damage from Overwatch shots.  These do a decent job at making things different, but ultimately, they aren't things that make it more fun, just more annoying or difficult.  It seems almost as if it was an effort to make the game come to a close even slower, but I can hardly say I have the evidence to support that; Regardless, by the time you are at the Last Boss, you are ready to be done with it.TL;DR The game is a lot of fun while the new content keeps coming in but eventually, it starts to get stale and all of the difficulty just feels like it is there to keep you playing for longer.  It is still a VERY good Turn-based Strategy game when you consider what might of been created from an idea like a Turn-based Gears of War game.  I can recommend it without feeling too bad about it (Though waiting for a small sale wouldn't hurt anyone now would it?) Game gets a 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. This is a surprisingly fun game. Ammo is unlimited (with Reloads being very important and taking an action point) and grenades are on cooldown.What I like that it does different from XCom are the executions and melee with the chain swords and bayonets. _childDocuments_.review: A few hours in, I loved this game. It got repetitive as there are only a handful of "Mission Objectives" between the different maps. _childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the campaign. The cut-scenes and story are great, much higher quality than other similar games.It's worth noting that your character types (heavy, scout, sniper, vanguard, support) will use the same "weapon" and you'll modify the weapons through add-ons. There are a ton of these add-ons / modifications, which meaningfully improve their skills, but aren't significantly unique from each-other.This is pretty linear, where there's a main story, and between each main mission you go on 1 - 3 side-missions to help get better equipment and level up. These missions really fall into a few categories:- Hold 2 points and collect equipment- Move as quickly as possible, avoiding bombs falling behind you- Rescue two characters and get back to the drop-off point- Kill all the enemiesAs the levels get higher the side-missions have different modifications, like characters only get 2 actions instead of the normal three, or full heal by executing an enemy.These aren't procedurally generated levels, and it's great to have maps that feel more like a puzzle to figure out. I wish there were more verticality, or maybe that it was easier to move around to different areas without constantly trying to handle overwatch.As I neared the end, I definitely got a bit tired. Missions felt similar, and the extra equipment wasn't much better than I'd originally had.As you level you you can choose additional active and passive skills (2 per level). This essentially drives you down one of 4 skill trees per character. By the end of the game my characters were at Level 6, and the 12 points were enough to fill one quarter of what was available.I'd definitely recommend the game, and had a great time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give this game a thumbs up. I really enjoyed playing it and, compared to similar titles, the mechanics of the combat is flawless. That being said this game really is not worth $60. I bought it on sale for $30 and even that felt like a bit too much. While it took me over 20 hours to beat the game, which is kind of on the short end of what would would expect, there really just was not very much content. The main issue is that there are not many unique levels or bad guys to fight. Where the traditional Gears of War games have novel level designs and a bestiary of big bads and boss fights, this game seems to be lacking in all categories. The highlight of the campaign is 3 actual boss fights, however they all feel pretty interchangeable with nearly identical mechanics. The bulk of the game is the same 3 mission types on the same 4 maps over and over again. What is weird is that the levels in the first act are far more unique and differentiated. It is almost like they gave up half way through development. This is evident from the abandonment of the emersion hole mechanic in act 2. One of the strongest points in the game was the leveling mechanic of the 5 classes, all of which were pretty fun to customize to different play styles. I wish they had taken this mechanic further. The max level of your characters is essentially 6 and each of the skill trees is not very long, which made this aspect of the game feel minor. To make your missions consequential your none hero characters perma-die if they die in combat. This would be an awesome mechanic if there were not rosters of higher level characters readily available. Overall, this game falls just short of being really awesome. I hope they do something with this in the future because the engine they crafted makes combat so much fun and their up close kill cams make the great graphics really stand out.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Very short campaign that has loads of unskippable side missions that make the game unfun.  Honestly, the gameplay is pretty decent and the character progression is neat as well. Comboing off with the sniper and shooting seven times in a turn feels good, but having to play 3 vanilla side missions before progressing the story does not.  Side characters are worthless other than to play the side missions.  The first half of the game is fun because it isnt bogged down by side missions yet and by the time you get to Act III you don't want to play anymore.  Is it worth $60? Absolutely not and if you NEED to play this game, then wait for a sale that brings it below 20. Unless they add more content, you will be paying to play the same 5 maps with the same 5 objectives.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, but when XCOM 2 exists, there is no reason to play this. XCOM 2 has way better customization, a better skill tree that is not unnecessarily complicated and with more interesting skills and decisions, much better presentation during its cutscenes and in combat with Overwatch etc., way better design of enemies, characters, weapons and armors (in GEARS everyone is a wrestler and enemies are all the same monster looking thingies and everything is grey and brown). XCOM 2 has insane enemy variety compared to this game, much better mission variety (levels are procedurally generated, much higher replay value). XCOM 2 has a million times better macro game with the base building and world map. All of XCOM 2's mechanics are so tightly woven together that it makes this game look amateurish. XCOM 2 has destructible enviroments. XCOM 2 has insane mod support. XCOM 2 has a lot of small design decisions that make it a more pleasant experience, for example when you attach an attachment to a weapon, you can't remove it. In Gears you can. Why is that so bad? Because you get a million attachments in Gears and in theory, to play optimally, would have to go into each character in every single mission and choose the best weapon attachments for each character every single time. XCOM 2 has that too, but only for armor and equipment which doesn't have to be changed nearly as much. In Gears you get flooded with trash loot. Since the replay value of XCOM 2 is nearly infinite, I constantly just wanted to stop playing this game and start a new XCOM 2 campaign instead. I'm sorry, but XCOM 2 is just so damn good and this game can't stand on its own strengths, it's clearly an inferior clone.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Potential was there but too many negatives turn the game into a boring grind. Most of the main characters are decent and the story is standard Gears plot lines. Strong, independent, minority, wamen, good-at-everything-character is annoying at times but after a few eye rolls she is tolerable. Barely. The real flaws are what make the game unpleasant to play.Game restarting bugs (freezing on enemy turn, frozen black screen on cutscenes) shouldn't exist in AAA games, atleast not this long after release. The missions are boring. Painfully, repetitively boring. Same capture the zone, sprint forward collecting packages, finish in x amount of turns rescue missions are forced on you between each story mission. Which is sad, because the story missions are actually kind of fun. The side missions have very little effort put into them, trigger the next group of enemies and pull back. Sit behind cover while they run at your overwatch and die. If you do any other tactic, you'll be rapidly overwhelmed and destroyed. The missions have no cleverness in design and are only difficult when artificially dropping in enemies where the numbers can overwhelm your group. Maps are recycled over and over.The A.I. isn't smart so the devs resort to dropping enemies behind you at random times. Some times this makes a mission impossible but if you restart they enemies will drop randomly somewhere else each time which makes an easy win. No in-between. It just got so boring to play the side missions that I have stopped and not sure if I will play again. Positive is the boss fights are a ton of fun. I replayed the couple I made it to several times just for the fun of it. Unfortunately, the absolute slog of side missions to get to a boss fight are just not worth it anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: We had no business sleeping on this one. This isn't Gears of War as you know it, but it's the best Gears of War game of the past 8 years.No one is saying this game is as deep a tactical shooter as X-Com, but the gameplay is fun and fast-paced, with fun visuals and familiar enemies. Missions are presented in bite-sized, 20-or-30-minute chunks, making it easy to jump into the action for as long as you like without too much interruption from the rest of your life.I bought this one on sale, and it was worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been a wild ride, and I had a lot of fun with it. I will say that I'm not thrilled that this is a Win 10 exclusive, so that will hurt the review a bit, but aside from that I only had a few issues with the game. Toward the end game, the game gets a tad buggy. Textures not rendering properly, characters not responding correctly, the normal. The biggest downside though is that if you're coming here from XCOM, just be aware that there is no system for base management and the character customization is severely lacking. Outside of all that though: the acting is great, the graphics are awesome 98% of the time, and the combat is just as challenging as any mainline GoW game. Would I say this is my favorite one? _childDocuments_.review: You can see a big games studio is behind this game. The graphic and cutscene quality is excellent, the cast performs very well but the story is a bit bland. You get about 30 hours of playtime from the campaign, after that you can play Veteran Mode to level up some more and get some better gear. The campaign is enjoyable, although a bit short. They tried to extend it using side missions between the chapters (3 acts, act 1 has 6 chapters and 2 and 3 have 8), which you must complete to advance the story.The main characters are not customizable regarding name/looks, only their gear and can be upgraded with a skill tree. Other than the story characters, you can recruit more soldiers which are fully customizable which include name-changes and looks (although their head is comes-as, you can however add hair, glasses, bandana's etc.).There is little replayablility though, once you finish the campaign there really isn't much incentive to continue. Unless you are after achievements and legendary gear. The main reason for this is that the side missions are very repetitive. You have a total of 4 different ones (one where you must defend 2 supply points, one where you need to secure an artifact, and one where you must gather loot boxes while running away from a bombardment). These missions come after each story mission and you need to complete 2 out of 3. After the campaign you must complete 3 out of 4. While these side missions are great, the same mission over and over again gets stale rather fast. Most have the same tactics, and the further you get in the campaign, the easier they get. One thing that also doesn't help the mission are the different environments. There are very few biomes and although props are somewaht randomly scattered, the environments all look the same.There are 2 mid-game end bosses and the final boss. They are all well designed but are very predictable to beat. They take quite a long time though due to the massive health bars and the fact minions come crashing the party, but they are enjoyable nonetheless albeit a bit long.the tactical battles are turn-based and you have 3 action points per soldier. You can use these as you like; 3 shots, 2 shots and a reload, 3 runs, etc. Furthermore executions (when you down an enemy) give all party members (except the executioner) 1 extra action point and there are some skills whiooch also generate bonus points. This works really well and clever use of these bonus points can get your soldiers out of quite a few messy situations. When you are downed, you can use a "second wind" ability to get back into the fight (only once per mission though), with one AP remaining. When a team mate revives you, you get all AP's back. Be advised, however, that if you don't revive and something explodes on top of you (or shoots at you), your soldier will die and in the case of story characters, you will fail the mission.Overwatch is a bit OP, especially if you set your team up in a choke point and also explosives are very powerful. Every skill has a cooldown, so grenades cannot be tossed every turn, but in the endgame you get so many rocket-launcher-like guns, it's a bit ridiculous. The battles themselves are enjoyable, especially with gore on as there are some very brutal alien killing animations. The ragdolls behave a bit awkward at times though, but these are minor nitpicks.I experienced no bugs whatsoever, the game told me I couldn't play it on my GTX1660Ti, but I played it on "ultra" settings with no hiccups whatsoever. I can only justify the price for the amount of window-dressing the developers put into the game. The graphics are really top notch and you can see this is a big title with a big budget. As most AAA games are priced at 60€, this title is not overpriced in that regard. The campaign is a bit short though, but that is with most titles with a fixed story. Hopefully they will release a follow up with a more global, sandboxy scale (like XCOM 2) as the battle system, character models, animations, gore and graphics are really great. Mod support would also be nice as this game has much potential and the battles are really fun to play.I had fun, sometimes the side missions were a bit of a drag later in the game, but customisation of soldiers, levelling them up and the battle system makes this game great to play. Recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Game was bought during sale for 50% off, and review takes that into account:Gears tactics has a solid foundation, unfortunately it lacks substance. The game starts interesting enough, the gameplay is different enough to make it stand out from the other Xcom-like games, but once you get through the first few story missions (which are all unique) the game starts to grow stale.It relies on just 3-4 random mission types which are extremely repetitive and predictable. There are always the same number of optional gear crates, enemies always spawn at predictable intervals while completing objectives, it gets old fairly fast.It wouldn't be so bad if there was more to the game, like the base building / research / recon etc that other tactical games have, but progression is in Gears is limited to random mission drops; It's and RPG-lite system which ultimately feel unsatisfying due to the relatively slow progression.It's fun for a few hours, but it's not worth the AAA price tag (I even found it underwhelming at half price). I would recommend trying it on the game pass rather than paying for it; if you're dead set on picking it up on Steam wait for a sale.

There are plenty of good cut scenes, voice acting and all the things you'd expect from a decent AAA game. Performance is good and I have encountered a complete game breaking bug which is not letting me finish the last match but hey... it was fun till then.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Xcom but somehow lacking something.The maps are very repetitive, you feel like you go to the same gate, open and kill all.Story was OK, good graphics, good cinematics.Progress of your chars is lackluster, many times feels better to just recruit a new guy with +1level than do missions with your old roster.It's still fun to play if you like Xcom type of games.It's a 7/10 but makes no sense to play it after you finish the SP story line (around 27hours).
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game - a really well done AAA game. Clearly recommended, without any doubts one of the diamonds in my turn-based tactics collection.What I like:1. The game is beautiful in every aspect - characters, maps, customization etc.2. Tactics potential is huge. It's like playing chess - the rules are simple, yet it takes a lot of mastery to win. I can't stop combining skills and armor/weapon bonuses, the game is awesomely well designed for this.3. Sound is good especially if you have good headphones or speakers. Play this game to find out what godd sound design is.What I don't like:1. The story is a typical American cliche of cliches. Fortunately, I can use escape button to skip the most of the cutscenes. 2. I wish AI could improve in response to my polishing the mastery of the game. At some point I had to manually edit the settings to add more enemies to the "insane" mode. A game mechanic as used in Phoenix Point is wanted.3. I wish I could visually edit the main characters.Thanks to the devs for the great pleasure I have playing the game and the Veteran missions! Please keep up developing the game. I can clearly see how much more this wonderful game has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, basic, get it on a sale.What it does, it does good (except inventory management, brr)What it doesn't do is depth."Crazy customization" is sales BS lolIt has a super bare bones story..but it has one.No strategy map or things to do outside of combat, it's just one after another.Combats which are good...but start repeating very early on with not all that much real enemy variety.You get the same enemies with a different paint jobs and more bullet spongy...and new abilities.Not a huge deal in and of itself... but when that's all the game is? lol.I have not finished it yet and I am not sure I will because of the repetitiveness, despite the good combat.Don't regret the purchase though. Just don't go into it thinking it's xcom with gears.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're an xcom fan then this game is a must. between the fog of war, turn based combat and new enemies every few missions Gears Tactics manages to keep you on your toes. Characters are xcom accurate but like xcom the skill tree is where your Gears really start to shine. you get everything from stealth demolition experts to bayonet charging damage dealers that heal themselves by dealing damage.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: As others have said this is XCOM 2 in Gears make-up. Which means it's terrific! I do wish they would have fleshed out the in between missions with more things to do like in XCOM but it's not a deal breaker. The game play is solid RNG, win some and lose some. You can customize each soldier with various armors, helmets, and weapon parts for various buffs. You can change the color of all their gear. I love watching my angry old guy tearing up grubs in his bright Pink armor. Like XCOM it is perfect to play anywhere (runs great on Steamdeck!) because it's turn based so you can do other things while playing. I play at work because it doesn't need my constant attention. Here's hoping they will some day release a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I love Gears of War! I've been playing it since the 1st one came out! Got this for 75% off (10 bucks baby) and lemme' tell you... I had no clue how they could translate Gears gameplay into a tactical strategy game like this, but it just works SO well. Still I know it is a SHORT game. Too short for full 40 dollar price. That being said!...The executions, the movement, the animations... Class-based soldiers, abilities. It all comes together perfectly to weave all the cool stuff you'd be doing in a classic Gears game without making it feel clunky, awkward, or weird. At face value it 'looks' like a knockoff of XCOM, but so far (with some gamepass time too lol) it FEELS like a real Gears of War game. Even more so than the last few in my personal subjective biased opinion. So I give it a fat thumbs up if on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Great turn-based game, both mechanically and visually! While the story is nothing special, and the missions are quite repetitive, the core gameplay is fun and engaging enough to the point where I didn't care much about anything else, beyond having more targets to shoot at! Recommend if you like tactics and turn-based combat!
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Unique spin on the genre. I don't get why people compare it so harshly to xcom. As someone who loves xcom, gears tactics does a lot of things well. There are so many abilities/passive abilities that meaningfully change your character. The classes are unique. The action economy is interesting. I'm playing on the second highest difficulty and recommend it highly for a first playthrough if you're experienced at this type of game. The story lacks some depth(so far) but that's not necessarily a bad thing because the atmosphere and setting around the characters is compelling. I would definitely say its an easy buy if you like tactical games.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this by saying that I have been a longtime Gears of War fan, ever since the first game dropped on xbox. Most recently, I completely enjoyed playing Gears 5 and this has been another amazing installment to the Gears franchise and an amazing addition to the Gears universe in terms of adding a little more to the lore and the story of how we got where we are now.I love the mechanics and the ability to easily jump into the game with very little time needed in orientation. If you enjoy games like XCOM, this will be a familiar setting. Unlike XCOM however, Gears Tactics has stripped out much of the macro level strategy and management and for this setting, it works. Gears Tactics has a higher focus on getting right into the fight and feels like you are playing a regular Gears game but from the chair of a commander.This game is all about violence of action, swift tactics and the ability to adapt. What this really is, it is a love letter to Gears fans and merges that with a strategy title that is well worth the purchase, even if this is the first exposure to a Gears game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Repetitive very quickly, character lines are WAY overused with only a couple of lines being recorded to make it especially annoying. _childDocuments_.review: First played through on the Xbox, now replaying on PC, awesome game but feel it needs more depth, upgrade the base, could use deployable weapons etc, because of the story you have to keep alive the hero characters, so feels a bit pointless to invest time into the others you can recruit, needs more mission types
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to force myself to finish this game because I didn't want to feel that I completely wasted my money - it didn't work despite me being a completionist at heart. I got about mid-way through Act 3 and couldn't take it anymore. I bought this half off and I'm glad I didn't pay full price because I really expect a lot more from a $60 mega corp game. I played the "jacked" version of the campaign. This game starts out mediocre and ends up boring as hell. The first act of the campaign is interesting: the mechanics are fresh, you're learning a lot about the different enemies, classes, and builds - so far so good. But after a while you realize that there are only a few mission types and they just repeat. Even a lot of the landscapes are the same. You figure out that frag bombs, overwatch, and support healing are OP and you just grind out every mission without much of a sweat.Cons:* Super linear campaign* You can't save this game manually - it just has an auto-save feature. You literally have to go to exit the game, open up the hidden folder that this game creates in windows, and copy that. * Many mission types are repetitive - I just couldn't take it anymore after a while* Many landscapes are repetitive* The enemies are the same every fight* The reinforcements are predictable for every mission type* Very easy if played defensively, only a few units force you to be otherwise unless you want to cheese the game, which is very easy to do most of the time.* The gore is disgusting and distasteful - I had to shut it off even though I'm quite used to that kind of thing. Watching someone get chain sawed in half for the second time onward is really not interesting.* Leveling is based on each soldier's personal kills. I find this very annoying as it noticeably takes a lot longer to level up some classes. XP should be shared with a small bonus to the one with the killing blow.* Leveling non-heroes is mostly pointless as new ones just come that are higher level anyway and you can just respec them. _childDocuments_.review: Solid 6/10. Which is a "no" coming from a big company.Buggy and unbalanced as all Hell. Let me point out that if you have Jack use Shock Capsule on a Ticker, the game proceeds to absolutely crap itself and locks on the enemy turn because the devs forgot to implement "If AI cannot perform any action, their turn ends".Customisation is like if Enemy Within got sent to prison. You can change shirt, tattoos, hair... but not skin, gender, voice, or anything else to make your character truly yours.AI are programmed to have a default bonus to hit you VS you hitting them, which is always set to low. And that's not me being petty, a Scout at point blank flanking a Drone WILL miss, and might even hit their own ally. Because the devs saw the worst part about Wasteland 3 and wanted to make that a whole game.In missions, you can only restart from the very beginning or a preset checkpoint. Game break during a boss fight? Back to the start, dumbass!The telegraphing of enemy Overwatch and other attacks is completely off. Sometimes the game will forget to even paint the cone, resulting in Locust just taking random shots at your sniper (and, of course, instantly Critting them). With a later boss fight, the characters treat YOU like an idiot if they get hit, but 50% of the time the boss just attacks without actually telegraphing anything. Sorry I'm not a psychic.I had to add this in because I forgot; the actual area telegraphing (when it works) is useless. Here's a big circle, in a game where you can move freely. For Overwatch cones you do get a "!" to show if you're going to set it off (sometimes, because sometimes your character moves before shooting, which will trigger Overwatch despite it not saying it will) but for big targeting circles, it's a guessing game.Mission modifiers and the type of mission aren't restricted. Sounds great, right? No. The "Supply Run" mission type forces you to keep moving past a huge wall of instant death, while picking up crates (which always takes 1 Action at least) AND fighting the Locust, which tend to spam Boomers, Theron Guards and Wretches in this particular mission type - IE, getting thrown around a lot and requiring many shots to bring down. Not undoable normally, but sometimes you get a modifier that means your units only get 2 Action Points. That's barely enough to overtake the death wall, let alone engage or run for crates. God forbid you bring a Heavy.This game has so much potential. But it well and truly flushes it all down the drain.

The side-missions i've seen so far can be: Control / defend two areas at one time, rescue units, destroy an objective, and solo missions. You have to plan ahead, as some units can't be used every mission, so you need to upgrade other units and loadouts, and think of combos in the skill-tree.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! I'm a big fan of XCOM 1 and 2 (finished both) and Gears Tactics manages to pave its own path, apart from the XCOM series. The focus of Gears Tactics is fluid, moment to moment action, so the game encourages you to get multiple kills in one turn (unlike the XCOM series which wants you to play tactically and carefully, making you afraid of losing your units). Let's face it: save scumming is the name of the game when you're playing XCOM, but I find myself doing very little of that when playing Gears Tactics. I can't wait to see how they evolve the series in the next iteration of this new franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to give this game a positive review.It has done the tactical battles right and improved on so many things over other similar games.Gears Tactics truly sets a new high bar for all other tactical games out there in terms of mechanics.However, I am giving this a negative because of these reasons:1. So many bugs that broke my mission. Turns that cannot end. Enemies that suddenly become invulnerable. Crashes.2. Recycled missions. 85% of the game missions are the same thing. Defend 2 points. Rescue 2 people. Destroy an item. Run and collect loot while being air bombed, etc.3. No hotfixes to fix some of these critical bugs listed in point 1.4. Garbage loot system with generic stat boosting item properties.5. Horrendous UI. The game makes you manage your troops and items constantly, yet the UI makes your life very hard to do so. You can't easily tell who has what gear and hard to compare your current equipment with another equipment. Every time you scroll down to delete a troop, it jumps all the way back up, forcing you to scroll aaaaaall the way down again. I don't feel like playing this game again after 1 campaign playthrough because it hurts to use the UI.Now, if this game was around $40-$50, I'd give it a positive review. But this game is $100! Are you serious? For this price, I expect a polished game, with more content and better technical support.Wait for a deep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent melding of the Gears world with a turn-based strategy format. Graphics are excellent (and there's none of the weird "firing bullets at right angles to the gun" silliness that you get in the XCOM games), and the game sounds take your imagination right back into the main GoW series. Unfortunately, the limited number of enemies and relative lack of variety of mission designs makes some of the later 'players choice' missions a bit of a grind, however the story missions and the boss battles make it all worthwhile - and the tactical flexibility allowed by the skill trees makes for some good replayability. The (free DLC) addition of Jack to your squad is also an interesting addition that provides some additional tactical depth. Having just finished the main campaign, some of the troop build lessons I learned from the final encounter itself make it tempting to go back and take another run through the campaign straight away.Well worth the money at full price... if you find it on sale, I'd say jump at it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I am writing this review after completing the campaign on Insane and getting most of the achievements.The good.- Beautiful graphics. What you would expect from the Gears franchise.- SoundFX.....love it. Grenade sounds chunky, gun sounds heavy. No complaints here. - Gameplay is very fast paced since you get 3 actions per turn and shooting is not turn ending. So lots of flexibility in terms of combat. Very interesting boss fights mechanics at the end of each act. The bad- Limited customization options. You can't swap gender, race or even faces. So, you can't make the squad look like your friends. - Maps are kinda static. Seems like there are a limited number of map pools and after a while it gets kinda dull seeing the same maps again and again. ConclusionGreat game if you can get it during sale. Not sure if its worth the full price at the moment (probably better to get XCOM EU/EW, XCOM 2: WOTC or XCOM: CS if you have not played those yet). All in all, great game on sale if you want to scratch that turn-based strategy itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: While initially enjoyable, Gears Tactics fails to maintain interest. The missions are incredibly limited in their variation, and worse they keep the story, which would be better if it weren't paced this way, locked behind these meaningless, repetitive missions. The repetition wouldn't be so bad if the environments weren't just randomized versions of one of a small handful of maps which are all the same theme with predictable assets. Hope you like barren desert with random outposts if you plan on playing beyond the first few missions. Another thing that really Grinds My Gears(ugh) is the frequency at which you can take on new recruits that are the same level or better than your existing ones. In XCOM, if one of your recruits dies there is an emotional attachment which gives the death drama. In Gears Tactics, not one of my recruits has died, but every other mission I end of getting rid of a recruit or two that I only sent on a few missions. This is all unfortunate as this game, mechanically speaking, is incredibly tight. The skill trees are a bit sloppy but other than that, it plays well. This game could be very good with some generous patchwork. Naturally I will likely revisit this title whenever I notice a new patch. There's gold in them hills, and based on the first few missions it seems like they just hit it before pushing the game out to meet a deadline.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Is the game good? Absolutely. is it worth $60? Definitely not. I paid $30 on sale and I am still not sure if the price was worth it.This is a great first attempt at a tactics game based on the Gears universe. The enemy design, combat, upgrade system, and all the micro-systems have had a lot of work put into them and you can definitely tell. Of course the graphics and sound design are up to Gears quality. These reasons are why the game is overall pretty fun.The story is decent too, although short if you rip out the filler BS missions. This is the biggest and most glaring issue with the game that really ruins what would be an otherwise stellar game. There are way way way too many filler missions that have basically nothing to do with the story. There's 3 or 4 generic missions that are recycled ad nauseam in between story missions. They are fun the first time or 2, but get old incredibly fast. What's worse, they make up probably 50% of the game. Half of the missions in this game are generic, boring, and repetitive missions that hold absolutely no weight. I do hope that Coalition makes a sequel to this game because the actual gameplay itself is fantastic. Hopefully next time they can focus on making the rest of the package up to par.I still have to mark this game as recommended, but only if you can get the game on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of tactical games like this so I was excited to try this out. It was good... but barely. I'd give it a 6/10. I played it once on hard mode through the end, this is the sort of game I would normally replay in higher difficulty settings after but am already bored of it after one play through so that says a lot.Good things:- Awesome graphics- Great sound effects- Great gory animations- Solid voice acting- Pretty good story but with a major caveat- Some cool new tactics mechanics like the execution of enemies to give your team extra moves and some pretty innovative abilities- Cool boss battlesThe bad:- There are almost no strategic choices in the game which makes multiple play-throughs really unappealing, even the class system because since you eventually get to pick out at least half of all the skills and a lot of them are straight up bad, another play through would feel overall the same- Encountered multiple bugs- The inventory system is awful, makes itemization annoying just because of how bad the menu is for figuring out who has what equipped- There are only 3 mission types, and they all play pretty exactly the same, so it gets repetitive FAST- The animations ARE SO DAMN SLOW, and unlike other games of it's kind there is no option to speed it up, yes it's cool to watch them the first few times but do game developers not understand that eventually you just don't want to watch the same thing a 100 times in slow motion?- I enjoyed the story but it could be so much better with more world building, the narrative is so narrowly focused on the present character's storyline that you learn nothing about the larger world which makes it way less compelling

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit concerned with the price tag on release, however, after a small debate with myself I decided to take the hit. In hindsight, I am extremely happy I did so - after launching the game I was astonished at how smooth the graphics were. Choice of colour scheme, gradients, move animations, combat animations etc compliment each other to no end. I was immediately engrossed in the story you're quickly thrust into, introduced to a dynamic but fun group of characters. That's hardly the tip of the ice berg though. Customisation in this game is incredibly fun and detailed! You unlock armour through loot found scattered throughout the game map or earn as rewards from missions. You will struggle to get all of these as you progress due to enemies and mission priorities. Not a problem for me as it provided a challenge and extra scope to the game. AI in this game is also very good. I noticed one or two tiny incongruities with enemy movement and placement, in contrast however, there have been hundreds of nail biting moments. Sparring with the enemy AI as you attempt to keep squad mates alive and use your movement and action points efficiently, generates fun to no end. I expected game play to get monotonous early on or repetitive but it is kept refreshing and challenging with the implementation of boss battles, various and challenging enemy types, as well as mission constraints you can either follow, if you want an extra reward at the end of the mission, or ignore. (Note: some mission constraints have to be followed for special missions). I am roughly 2-3/4 through the story mission and enjoying it thoroughly. Overall, the game easily earns it's price tag and I would highly recommend as a purchase! Ideally would be cheaper but hey, I know I'll get 50+ hours out of this which makes it worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge XCOM and XCOM 2 fan, I wasn't expecting much from Gears Tactics but it really surprised me. All five classes feel well balanced and compliment each other well, the customization is great, and every mission type is fun in its own way. I loved the original Gears trilogy and wasn't sure how the series was going to translate to a turn-based game, but it's still a lot more Gears than XCOM. Personally I'd just like to see more customization options, including an easier way to earn gear, the ability to change your soldiers' race, gender, and voice, and the option to customize or design your own missions. Hoping for more content down the road but as it is it's a fun game that's surprisingly replayable. Highly recommend if you're a fan of either the XCOM or the Gears of War series.

But I have never played any of the Gears games and did not know what to expect. However, the screenshots looked great and, obviously, it's a genre that fits me perfectly.You know how a game can look fantastic on screenshots but not so good in motion? I'm happy to say Gears Tactics delivers in graphical prowess, overall polish as well as mechanics. Long story short - it's brilliant in almost every aspect.You control a small squad of soldiers who are moving around a warzone in their APC, doing various missions and fighting the grub (remember, I am a complete newbie with the lore) enemy. Gears Tactics took a slightly different approach to the time units and actions you usually see in these games. Each unit gets 3 actions (sometimes more, sometimes less), which you can spend on movement, shooting, throwing grenades, etc. This might not seem so much different than what the new XCOMs are doing, but there are nuances. Firing a weapon or doing pretty much anything does not end a unit's turn. You can spend your action points in whatever way you wish, on any tasks. Movement is also slightly different. No hex or rectangle grids here, it's all free-form, which feels great. And the game's UI does an EXCELLENT job at letting you know how far you can move with one action point, so you don't waste 2 by mistake.Getting your soldiers into cover is easy and intuitive. The UI will let you know what kind of cover you're going to (half, full or breakable). However, unlike in the new XCOMs, where a target can either be fired upon normally or flanked, if you can get around them, in Gears Tactics, getting a nicer angle on your enemies will mean their cover will be less effective and more bullets will make contact (and vice versa). This mechanic feels great and very rewarding because you're not forced into either taking pot shots at enemies or going gung-ho attempting to get to that magical 90 degree to the enemy's cover to get a flanking shot.Melee attacks are a thing and quite spectacular (and gory). After killing an enemy, sometimes they will be knocked out, which means you can perform a melee finisher. This exposes your unit (usually) but also grants everyone an extra action. A very interesting and, in the end, strategic mechanic that's fun to use.There's also overwatch, which will make the unit fire on enemies as long as they have ammo and action points left. I'm mentioning it because it's extremely satisfying (and fluidly animated) to see enemies strumble or even fall over when being shot at by overwatch. Sometimes, you will not just do damage to them but actually interrupt their action (whether that was lobbing grenades or trying to shoot you), which makes it very useful, but it also can be turned on you!The graphics are crisp and gritty, the animations very fluid. In fact, the animations when characters interact in melee are so well-done, you will never notice the little pop when two models position themselves to have a melee spat. It feels natural. The sounds are great, even though I'd sometimes wish my weapons had a little more oompf to them.I usually don't mention things like the options menu in reviews but I have to in this case. This game probably has THE best options menu I have ever had the pleasure of using. Not only does it give you an explanation of what the plethora of options do, but they give you the expected performance impact on your GPU, CPU as well as video ram. Not just that, the menu also provides screenshots to reflect how changing options will impact the look of the game. Truly excellent, if you need to change things to get better performance.There's no base building, which is a bit of a shame for me (I love the mechanic). You get to recruit other soldiers and you pick up equipment cases (which stink of lootboxes and microtransactions; I don't know whether that's just a coincidence or it was a mechanic they wanted to implement but then decided against it - there's zero microtransactions in Gears Tactics), which provides mods for your weapons, new armor, etc. There's also extensive customization of armor, weapons and the characters.All in all, the game feels great, sounds great, plays great, has very satisfying mechanics and combat, and is polished. I can very much recommend Gears Tactics to anyone who enjoys X-Com type games.Video review:

_childDocuments_.review: When I first heard of it, I expcted it to be a half baked cashgrab milking the fanbase. The enemies, the maps, the very customizable iconic weapons and armors are so detailed and so... Gears. Everything seem to be in the right place, depth of gameplay is good, theres not too much and not to little. The game is very easy to pick up and catch on all the quirks of it. Overwatch mechanic is a fantastic feature. The game does gets repetitive after a while, and might be a drag for some, but it is still very satisfying. The other important thing is - the game is a complete and final product, through and out -and it doesn't feel like it needs months or years of content updates or bug fixes, which is a very, very rare thing nowdays. However i have one complaint that might be a dealbreaker for some - most achievements are simply bugged, not triggering or not tracked on steam. Apart from that it's a great game and i hadn't have so much fun with any other game in a while now.I would highly reccomend it to anyone who is new to either turn based games or Gears Of War franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: My initial review of this game was positive, as I am a huge XCOM fan, but after playing this quite a few hours, it is very grindy, and it's very repetitive.  As you may have seen in various reviews here, the mission structure is quite limited, and you do the same things over and over again.   The repetitive grind is the biggest negative, but additionally, there is ZERO incentive to develop any of your ancillary characters, because as you progress through the missions, you constantly have a chance to Recruit new people, and their level is always higher than your existing characters, as they scale automatically, where your characters do not.   So, you have your 4 main characters, and that's really it.   It's also very taxing to have to spec out the new "recruits"after you already did so 20 times already with the past recruits.   Lastly, the UI for the gear and weapons, and armor is very awkward.  You have to swap into multiple different screens to do so.    For this price, and limited gameplay and functionality, I really cannot recommend this game.   On a positive note, the cut scenes are nice, and it's not too buggy, so at least they launched a game in a fairly decent state, unlike Bethesda and EA !!

_childDocuments_.review: Unless you are a Gears of War fan, there are better games in this genre to play listed above. While Gears tactics has plenty of potential for a sequel, this game ultimately falls short for a few reasons. First, the story (main missions) and every side mission is extremely scripted (or linear and repetitive). As a result, replay value is low and the game starts to feel like a chore to complete. Not only are missions scripted, but each mission often has some kind of restriction on how you can play. For example, a story mission may require you to bring specific squad members (main characters) or a side mission might require you to not use your grenades for whatever reasons (increasing difficulty). Therefore, once again we have an extremely scripted game limiting how you can play. And for the record, the "side missions" are not optional meaning that you have to complete them to progress the story. As for the gameplay, it can be quite frustrating even on normal difficulty. No question about it, the computer has an unfair advantage in many scenarios (especially when you enter a mission with only 2 squad members because the mission restricted more than 2 squad members). During a mission, there are (what feels like) endless waves of horde that spawn in various locations on the map every other turn. Unfortunately, most horde unit types are brutes that just get as close as possible to you in order to deal maximum damage (not making use of cover or actual tactics). The other type of units just spam cover and overwatch without trying to flank you. To defeat these endless waves of enemies, I often found myself spamming grenade attacks or using a long range sniper or close range shotgun (my mid-range units felt useless and always missed their shots). Anyways, the enemy doing a zerg rush gets even more frustrating during boss levels when the boss is limiting your movement with AoE attacks. Overall, I only suggest this game is you love the Gears of War universe or if this game is on a major discount.

_childDocuments_.review: A Gears of War Turn-Based strategy? I thought this game was going to be trash.  Who made this garbage? Splash Damage - ok, Halo 3: ODST was trash, Reach was alright, Brink tried some new things but never caught on, and Hey Batman was pretty damn good. I’m a little interested. The Coalition – Gears 5, meh.XBox Game Studios? Hey, hey - that kinda sounds a lot like Microsoft Game Studios. The same company that brought us Mech Warrior, Mech Commander, Dungeon Siege, Asheron’s Call, Age of Empires, Crimson Skies and Starlancer. A lot of great memories there.Sure enough, they changed their name. Microsoft Game Studios published a lot of good games during the dark age of PC gaming. They were the only publisher that was buying up innovative devs that were trying new things and at the same time EA was began buying up studios and bleeding IPs with their signature rehashes.  I didn’t remember MGS ever publishing a low quality, low effort title. There were some titles that I didn’t care for, but never bad.First Impression – I’m pleasantly surprised. The combat system works really well. I’m going to withhold judgement until I have many more hours playtime, but I think this may be a contender for the best turn based strategy. It has a really good mix of skill progression, items and Warhammer-ish strategy. I’m playing on experienced difficulty and the gameplay can be a bit frantic.I'd like to see a Gears Tactics 2.

_childDocuments_.review: This is alllllmost a thumbs-down review.  I'm giving gameplay and story more weight so that tips it towards a positive review but Gears Tactics would be a solid "meh" rating if Steam offered such a thing.First the good.  Gears Tactics is a surprisingly detailed turn-based tactical game.  There are a number of main characters which is always a plus, but there are also expendable lesser characters that come and go as the game progresses.  The gear upgrade system is very detailed and the player is incentivized to continue upgrading as enemies get more difficult.  The gameplay is fun** (**see below), and the story is engaging though nothing groundbreaking.This brings me to the bad - it is insanely repetitive and this kills the fun factor.  There are only a handful of maps (though you attack them from different directions on different missions) and a very small variety of mission types.  This is a common complaint but it would be totally acceptable if it weren't for the absolutely ridiculous amount of mandatory "side" missions.  They hold no story significance and they implement a character ban system which forces you to upgrade other characters outside of your core group to progress.  I will have around 28 hours played at the end of the game and I guarantee over half of that time will have been spent in meaningless mandatory side missions that serve as nothing but hollow filler.  Optional side missions would fit perfectly and I would've been satisfied with a 12-14 hour main story.  However I nearly gave up on the game out of side-mission fatigue.  Too much of a good thing is very much present in Gears Tactics and that is a shame because otherwise it is a very fun game.Pros:+Detailed gameplay+In-depth loot system+Decent story+Great graphics+Very optimised/no bugs encountered at all+Can completely skip the opening credit scenes on launchCons-Forced meaningless side missions that total more than half of the total main-story completion time-Making it a second bullet point.  Cannot stress enough how annoying the side missions were.-Forced usage of non-essential non-main characters that made character upgrades feel like a chore

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable take on the turn based genre.Not overly strict for mission set up or load outs which is nice.Game design focuses more on fun I think rather than being punishing if you don't make every move exactly how the designer intended.Loot crates are an added incentive during mission to aquire without being frustrating.Quality game and an easy recommend.

The forced side missions get repetitive and definitely overstay their welcome by the 2nd or 3rd act, so I recommend you pace yourself a bit to avoid mission burnout in the late game. _childDocuments_.review: I'm 34 hours in currently and the game is a slog. You'll quickly see the gameplay formula they've put forth: Do a story mission that involves some macguffin and then do 2-3 side missions of which there are only 4 types. The missions have modifiers on them but they do very little to change up the gameplay.The game suffers from some massive issues with unit recruits. It takes forever to level up a unit, but doing so doesn't feel very rewarding since you get access to fresh recruits of higher levels as you progress the story. There's no incentive to keep your original units around since the new ones come in at a higher level and can have their skill points applied any which way you'd like. You'll run into the issue of having a bunch of level 5 units that are halfway to 6 that you just toss out once you get access to the level 6 units. There are no bonds between units or anything so there's no reason to keep them around. The leveling simply takes too long and doesn't feel fun.The game looks beautiful on the unreal engine and runs without a hitch.As a competitor to games like XCOM, Gears Tactics simply doesn't have enough juice in the tank. There's virtually zero replayability and they've made no attempt at bringing famous modes like Horde over from the main series. Hopefully they'll add lots of content and balance patches over time or at the very least open the game up to the modding community, but I'm not holding my breath. This game is definitely not worth the $60 price tag in its current form. Right now Gears Tactics is a flimsy 5/10 experience - go play XCOM instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Gears Tactics has great combat, story, and graphics. The game feels balanced except for grenades, which inflict exceptional damage and are easily favorable over the stim (healing) grenade. You can also customize your characters, although you cannot give them custom nicknames or choose their physical appearance. The primary issue I had with this game was the end game. Following the campaign, which I completed on normal difficulty in about 30 hours (including time spent customizing, managing, etc.), the game allows you to play exponentially in "Veteran" side missions. These are side missions with difficult modifiers and allow you to obtain legendary gear for your gears. Unfortunately, these missions become tedious because of their difficulty and boring as the game slowly evolves into a narrative-less Gears of War PvE combat operations simulator.  While equipment upgrades vary per campaign, the story mission map layouts stay the same and the side mission map layouts are random but the pool of maps appear to be small. This makes replaying the campaign relatively pointless. This was quite disappointing for me because I recalled seeing an advertisement claiming the game had an 80+ hour campaign. I can only assume they included veteran missions. I really want to keep playing the game as it is fun, entertaining, challenging, and overall different than other turn based strategy games, but it falls short after initial completion. I think DLC could provide some extra gameplay hours, but I think the game would need to add randomization in terms of map layout and include other concepts of randomization for longevity. I would recommend this game for anyone who likes Gears of War and turn based strategy games. But I would not recommend purchasing it at its current $60 price tag. You receive far too little for what you pay for.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give it a solid 7/10.A lot of negative reviews come from people complaining about needing an Xbox account, it's 2021, multiple platforms are needed for both TV and Games and even music now, time to get over it.As for Gears Tactics, it's like XCOM and it isn't. You get a bit more freedom in Gears Tactics I feel, in terms of positioning and action points. Being able to redeem action points through executions also adds another layer of tactic to the game.The armour customisation is phenomenal, you can make some really badass looking gears with the different colour and decal scemes.There is little to no character customisation though, unlike XCOM you can't change the gender or race of the characters you recruit, so making accurate (somewhat) looking versions of your friends can be difficult. (Use helmets and long t-shirts to sorta overcome this).The gameplay is satisfying with all the sound effects and animations that we've grown to love over the years since 2006. The story is alright, some people don't like it, I personally think it's not bad; very middle of the line, if you're not a Gears lore fan, it might be somewhat forgettable. The Boss fights however, I feel, take far too long. It's not that the bosses are hard, it's just that mobs spawn in during the boss fight, forcing you to deal with them, which just creates artificial length. However there is an argument to be had that the bosses might be too easy without these added swarms.Tickers are a genuine threat in this game as opposed to the shooters.Overall, a 7/10. Get it on sale if you like a XCOM or Phoenix Point, or even if you like Gears and want to broaden your horizons a little.  I don't think you'll be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Completed the campaign around 25-30 hours.GameplayThe core gameplay is fluid, impactful and fun.Of cause, it is heavily inspired by X-Com, but the devs have make enough changes to the formula so that this game feels unique and not a copy cat.There are quite a lot of interesting skills and you have the freedom to try different builds.One thing I dislike the max squad size is 4 so I don't get to send out all my favourite gears.Also, there is no research/shop/base building so you progress by fighting and getting loots only.Map/stage designSome story maps are excellent. They are both fun and challenging. However for many side quests the maps (and objectives) are VERY similar and could feel repetitive.VisualAs a X-Com -like game, the graphics, music and visual effects are excellent. StoryThere is an actual story which is rare in this genre. The story is alright, not exceptional but not bad either.VerdictThis game is what happens when you put AAA production value into a turn based tactical game.While it could feel a bit shallow/repetitive at times, overall its still a fun experience.If you like turn based tactical games this is a must-try.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this blind, saw a few videos and it seemed like a great game, especially as someone who's played XCOM 2 for 1000 hours. And I've gotta say, I love this game.Pros:-Amazing story and character work, I was invested right away-Story blends into gameplay with a mix of 'hero' characters and random characters you can get-Solid customization which makes for some really cool looking soliders-Different boss fight mechanics and mission modifiers to make the game more interesting-Multiple ways to build characters through the skill trees-Really great gore, the executions never get oldCons:-The game balancing isn't that great when it comes to side missions later on in the game right now, mid-late game some of them are literally impossible to win due to the modifiers and type of mission. This doesn't break the campaign though, you only need to complete 2 or 3 side missions, so you can drop the impossible ones-Bugs, it's gonna be there, and they're really annoying, though fixable. In my entire campaign run (about 20 hours) I only had one bug that forced me to restart the mission, other bugs you can fix by going to the main menu and loading back in-Repetitive missions and map design toward the endWhat I love most about this game is how it blends cinematics for the story along with the classic tactical gameplay that still makes it feel as if you're playing an XCOM kind of game. I don't know how I'll feel about this in the long run with replayability and all, I'd love a co-op survival mode of some sort down the line. But comparing the campaign to the XCOM 2 campaign, I honestly like it even better than the XCOM one. The story and the extra tactics really did it for me.I'd predict that it won't be that great anymore once you keep on playing and reach 100 hours, but who knows, I'm hoping for extra content in the form of updates, rather than DLC. If you don't love the genre, wait for a sale because it's really costly. If you do love it however, definitely grab it.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Requires Windows 10 to use. Despite being able to run it, not having it makes it unable to read my graphics card and allow me to play the game. Shame that my PC doesn't want to even download Windows 10 when I did try installing it.UPDATE 1: I have since been able to get Windows 10 to work on my PC. Game works decent on my older PC with upgraded parts, but it pretty much wants you to buy the top of the line PC like you would usually expect. I've only reached Act 2 and have a few issues such as the push for 'Hero characters' that are unchanging and critical (Who you will always give the best loot to), and the normal grunts you pick up and are limited to having. Weapons are limited despite the increase of the options added in later games. Lancer, Retro Lancer, Mulcher, Longshot and Gnasher are your only options for loadouts with the Snub Pistol as a secondary for all. Boomshots and Torque Bows are provided by the enemy or Jack if you wish to play with him. Grenades as well are limited to Stim and Normal. Hammerburst and Gorgon SMG is used by the enemy, but cannot be used. No Boltok pistols, Sawed Off Shotguns, Breechshot rifles, Markza, or Ink/Incidenary Grenades.As well, Gears level up when they go on missions. There is no other option to have others train while you are gone and no real system that requires you to swap them around besides side missions between each major mission which has them marked as 'Traveling'. So the only use in collecting more is because you would expect them to die... But the game is rather easy and most of the time you will be using your 'Heroes' who are not allowed to die. Maybe it's much different later in the campaign and on the hardest difficulty, but most of my guys get 'downed' and have the option to 'Second Wind' if no one is around to help them out. It makes the game feel more like "Mario & Raddids" (which was more a puzzle based game) then the 'Xcom' inspiration. Xcom as well atleast had a reason to train more recruits, as your troops would get 'Shellshocked' or 'Tired' and become less effective going on mission after mission.There is also some story beats that I don't feel really work. I like the Scavenger Sniper gal, but I hate that she is the trope of "Dumb White Military Meat head consolts the wise Black Lady for help" and think it would have been cooler if she actually was part of the COG and one of the other characters was the angry man not wanting to have his group of civilians turned into conscripts for the missions. Redburn would've worked better for that, a man discharged from the COG for what he knows and curses him and Ukkon.Other complaints I have include the types of 'Side missions' you go on are all the same, Jack feels REALLY OP at times, especially since he is my 'go-to' to collecting all loot on missions and completing objectives. Execute animations are not only all the same, just changing depending what weapon your gear is holding at the moment, but are basically imported from GoW and I feel like you could've gotten more creative with that.Is there stuff I like? Yes! The actual missions are really solid and the scaling option for Overwatch really brings more thought into how to set your sights as you can technically 'overkill' units crossing into it which leaves other troops to sneak by and get close. Grenades has the Gears of War feel with hucking them or planting them for strategic defence options. Plugging E-holes feels just like how I remember it and the Boss fight that I had was somewhat unfair, but I felt that rush of victory for overcoming an impossible obstacle and for thinking outside the box (Which was abusing the 'Second Wind' mechanic by having the sniper chick plant a grenade at her feet so that a pack of Wretches would explode with her instead of mauling her to death normally)Should you get this at full price? No. When it is on sale? Maybe, But I'll update this when I finish the game as it is feeling like there isn't much replayability value to it yet...

_childDocuments_.review: This game has no glitches no bugs so far and I've just finished the main campaign, about 42h. I've enjoyed myself alot - a great game. Buy it if you're into xcom-like games or gears of war or both.edit: the overwatch-mechanic is brilliant and revolutionary. It actually feels like fighting for fire superiority (like in an actual battle) and not as static as it is usually done in games where one unit attacks, than returns behind cover, waits for the enemy to attack, which can hit you behind cover (which is unlogical btw). Here, cover means alot, you really need to flank or keep fire superiority over the enemy by using the overwatch mechanic so the enemy can't leave cover, neither to fire at you nor to switch position or eventually will be shot by your troops who are ready and were aiming at them.It gives it a much more dynamic, realistic touch. And wonderful cascades of overwatch fire. The enemy tries to do the same, to pin you and to make you bleed.

_childDocuments_.review: I barely recommend this to fans of the tactics genre.The main draw of the game is the combat itself. It's very action packed and offers a unique powerfantasy, unlike most games of this type. This is mainly because unlike most other games, here the enemies are generally weaker than your units, becoming a threat only if you don't kill them off fast enough. Therefore the moment to moment challenge isn't surviving an encounter but rather dealing the most damage.This falls apart in boss battles, which are completely different and do not make use of the main advantage this game offer. This makes them feel tedious to an extent.Where the game falls apart is in tackling the bigger picture. I would like to tackle a few points here:1. There is no feeling of progression between the missions. In most tactics games you know why you fight as there is usually an external reason, like delaying a "doom timer" or increasing your fame. Here, missions are simply a linear progression through a narrative, making some of them completely interchangable and sort of meaningless. To add to that, your performance in missions, apart from getting bonus objectives mean nothing. Winning with 3 downed units is the same as winning with no scratch as all units are ready for action for the next battle anyway.2. Your units are meaningless. In most tactics games units gain levels during the campaign making them almost irreplacable. Here, you get new recuitable units the same level and sometimes over the level of your current units. This means you can easily dismiss your roster for fresh, stronger units after each battle with no drawback. What makes the problem worse is the fact the new recruits even come fully kitted with good gear.3.  Gear upgrades are uninteresting and tiresome to manage. The gear in the game doesn't change each unit playstyle much if at all. The difference between "rare" and "epic" gear could be a simple number upgrade making choices mostly trivial. Moreover, you cannot control the gear you get after each mission as gear is awarded in a "loot box" fashion. Noted by their absence are utility items which could greatly mix up the way a unit plays, the biggest choice you make is between a healing grenade and a damaging grenade. Lastly, equipment UI is terrbile and you need far to many clicks for each upgrade.TLDR:Only buy this if you are 100% sure the combat can carry you through because everything else is subpar.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally, I groan when I see "turn-based" because how many more XCOM clones/wannabes do we need? However, GEARS TACTICS is a refreshing surprise in the turn-based market. Its NOT trying to be XCOM but instead, a combat-focused journey of blood, guts and guns in the company of soldiers you can't help but grow attached to. Gears Tactics is deeper and more flexible than XCOM as far as character builds and strategy development goes while being set in the Gears of War universe makes it 10x times better. It's all about the combat here and this is turn-based I can get behind and recommend to guys like me; Rambo adepts.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic and appeals to either gears fans, or turn based tactics fans. The simple addition of a third action per turn increases the pace and has this progressing much faster/gives you more options. (most other tactical games give you two per character per turn)The execution mechanic is also awesome for really maximizing your turn: sometimes when you kill an enemy, they will get downed, and you can send a character over to execute. Doing this uses an action from that character, but gives the rest of your team an additional action point to use that turn. By chaining these together sometimes you can really do a lot in one turn. The cinematics and graphics are amazing quality. There is am audiobook available to really flesh out and give background to the main character, but honestly the game does a good job of filling you in to the important parts.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend it, but I'd probably wait for a 50% sale to get the most value out of it.The reason being it's a good game, the core gameplay loop is there and the tactical part of the game is supreme, satisfying and feels like true gears combined with the best of xcom 2.The problem stem from missing QoL things and bad design, an example of this is that after every mission you get recruits, but they dissapear after 1 mission, now here's the real problem with that: they spawn with better than default gear (which you can't craft, only loot), so combined with the fact that your roster is limited to 10 soldiers you end up dismissing 1-2 current soldiers, to recruit these, strip their gear (manually each component for each gun), dismiss those and do the next until you worked through the recruits.The reason you do this cause the lootboxes are very RNG, and this is an additional loot income.This bring us to the 2nd major issue, they've stopped supporting the game 1 year after release, they released like 2 hotfixes and then a bigger patch that added recolored enemies as new ones, jack as a free 5th squadmate and supreme weapons and weapon mods which are even better then legendaries but what's probably the best is that they added infinite procedural missions, so you can keep playing with your top squad.So the reason I recommend it is because it's a decent and enjoyable product, the reason why I say wait is because it could've been more, doesn't live up to what it could be if the developers had stuck with their product for more than a meager year.
