_childDocuments_.review: This might sound weird but this game reminded me of "Into the breach" rather than "X-Com" to me.Let me explain, Gears Tactics fundamental concept is pretty much like... well... Gears of war.4 Macho men and Women fight against an endless horde of more metal version of orcs and goblins. That's pretty much it. One of X-Com stronger aspects is you start as a small underequipped, obsolete tech, and practically weaker than your enemies then working up by stealing, scavenging, and researching your own weapons. Your soldiers also fragile and inexperienced, They are learning to be hardened veterans on countless trials by fire.On the other hand,  Gears soldiers are already heroes units. Equally (if not slightly better) equipped than enemies. So enemies are mostly overwhelmed you by numbers and rush tactics this alone makes them feel very different in design.This is the beginning of Gears Tactics it's own both advantages and disadvantages. First off, this game presentation alone gives X-Com series a kick in the nads. It looks AAA (obviously it use a lot of Gears 5 aspects). Optimized and run pretty well for the most part. And the sound design is gritty and meaty like other Gears. If you are a fan of Gears Series, this might not seem so impressive. But for TBS players, This one takes the cake in terms of presentation alone. Second, This game brought some interesting gameplay mechanics on the table. Non-grid-based is nice and intuitive (some knowledge from usual Gears also applied like dashing from cover to cover to reach further.) Weapons range somehow feels a bit too close for effective range (but hey! it's Gears! right?) The most unbecoming part of this is they try to "Gears" this game too much. I have to admit that this game feels and plays very Gears like. But Gears background is very mindless compared to X-Com. In Gears Tactic you kill, kill, and then kill some more. Objectives pretty much rely on a handful of templates (rescue, gathering, raid run, sabotage, and some couple more templates.) This is pretty much the same with "Into the Breach" you fight, you kill, you upgrade your squad and move on. Nothing more than that.This on the surface also feels like X-Com. But should I remind you that X-Com templated side missions are involved in much deeper strategic layers? They are doing this for other reasons than big fat loots and leveling up soldiers (which is pretty much only Gears Tactics does for side missions.) The story kinda moves on its own and other than that feels like Borderlands grinding loot mill. This makes side missions feel repetitive pretty fast because it doesn't stop the doomsday clock, unlock story mission, weaken enemies armies or boost your research (which doesn't exist.) One more downside of focus only on killing is it makes the skill branch seems pretty limited in the terms of substantial ways you can mess up your enemies. Don't get me wrong, Gears Tactics has a lot of skill branches to learn and you will end up very powerful as you like. But they are mostly statistic adjustment of pretty much the same thing you do (example for snipers, skill are like fire with more hit% or fire and reload or fire with additional damages to non-damage target.) There are many skills to be played with (and I like that.) But In X-Com, your snipers can fire with high power, can extend overwatch by friendlies sight, can create a Killzone and if you are going for it, Your snipers can be customized to grappling hook themselves on the high ground and can be a close quarter gunslinger. Can you see my point? X-Com 2 even with War of the Chosen DLC might seem lacking content for hardcore TBS fans. Yet in practicality X-Com has much more stuff going on than gears (Hacking, mind control, stealth, abduction, 3rd party allies you named it.) In summary, Gears feels like a mindless"kill kill brute kill" with customizable trapped in its own lore. And where is the tech drone class? I want that badass Jack drone just like in Gears 5. It does make sense in lore terms so where is it? Where is smoke grenades? Where is the mortar? A flame grenade to zone the enemies would be nice? Oh, how about that crazy hammer of dawn pointer laser? My point is for the series that well known to go for some crazy-ass weaponry and try hard to offer new ways to kill. This seems pretty "tamed" to me.But what happens when just mindless kill Gears stuff is enough for you? Well, you will have a really good time here. The gameplay is solid. The story is nothing to write home about (as well as other Gears.) Every action you take is meaty and so much more smooth than X-Com. There are a lot of grubs to be killed (and I mean a lot.) The game is challenging unless you found broken builds which to be fair existed on almost TBS games. The progression system needs to be fixed right away (your soldiers always weaker than recruits.) The biggest disappointment is this game lacks ambitious, it feels like they just testing the water here. The area they are focusing on is nicely interpreted and crafted. But with about 40% content compared to X-Com 2 on the grand scale, this doesn't seem fit to be a $60 title (a very appealing 40% is still 40%)Why did I recommend this? luckily I live in the region that this game cost only around $20 (lucky me eh?) Then again you might not want to buy this game on Steam for now. If you are worried about a $60 price tag, you should try this game on the Xbox game pass (for PC) first. I am pretty sure you can beat this game in a week and play Forza Horizon 4 or something for the time left. Replayability is non-existed so don't bother buying a full copy if you don't want to.Is this a failed attempt to competed with X-Com? I don't think so. Even it can't decrown X-Com today, Gears Tactics is going to leave a large bite mark on the aspect of "How next-gen TBS should look like". The difference is very clear when 2K just decided to release X-Com: Chimera Squad right before this game and show how outdated it looks. Unfortunately, TBS players (at least for me) don't play this genre of games just for how pretty it looks alone. But if you don't have to pay too much I'd recommended just try it.For now it's a pretty decent TBS game that too humble to shine through. 7/10 I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: Tragically unpleasant. Gave it a fair try (see hours played), but they f***ed this up on various fronts.- No world map, just a linear campaign with no replayability.- Randomised gear system where you can't go do extra missions for gear, so you're stuck with what you get despite the campaign ramping up the difficulty. Did that extra hard mission for a legendary? got a useless piece? too bad! You can't redo it.- No buying gear. No rerolling gear. No crafting. Gear is hyper important and you're completely at the mercy of the RNG.- Limited xp, but they disable party members for missions so you have to waste xp on hired NPCs that you'll never use again.- Incredibly slow leveling. You can go in on an extra hard mission with massive penalties to your characters, nail all the optional objectives and have no-one faint...then be rewarded with like 25% of a level. Then you get told you can't use that character in certain mission. Great.- Progression is terrible. New enemy types have WAY more health, better weapons, better range, etc. Your characters don't get extra HP, movement, AP, etc when leveling at all. Your level 8 star character dies as easily as your level 1 character, but fights things with twice the health that fire without penalty from a screen away.- You get forced to use the story characters on bosses, so why the **** do I get forced to level other characters? Max party size (when they let you use it) is 4. There are 3 story characters.. Why do I have to manage a barracks when you won't let me use them when it matters? If you ever (ever) stop leveling the 3 story characters you are completely ****ed.- No saving and a random checkpoint system. Get used to redoing chunks of the mission because an enemy scored a lucky critical hit. Yeah, read that: no save and continue. Not on any difficulty level. Checkpoints in a game where a single misclick can get you killed.- They force modifiers on your missions: can only use 1 character, can't use grenades, enemies get more damage, etc. These are not optional. They range from annoying to absolutely crippling, and often waste xp. They get applied ON TOP of the basic mission templates, which are pretty much designed to destroy any sense of fun:Defense missions:- Enemies only need half the points you do on defense missions, spawn near the objectives and are infinite. This is fine when you're fighting basic enemies. This is not fine when you're fighting large groups of enemies that require cooldowns to kill. The further you get in the game, the more cancerous these missions become. There's even one you have to do with only half a party. **** off, devs.Scavenge missions:- Run through a map while being chased by a never-ending carpet bombing run. This is in a supposed "tactics" game. Nope, you're now playing a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ flash game where you're guessing where the enemy will spawn as you run through a maze of chests. Gotta split the party to get em...did you send the right characters to the left? no? **** you, better restart the entire mess because they just dropped an entire group of enemies on you.Rescue missions:- These are about as much fun as dental work. Whoever balanced these needs to sit down and re-evaluate their career. You like timed missions? You like timed missions where you can only take 1 character? No, because no-one does. You get 15 turns when you're fighting basic enemies at the beginning. You get 15 turns when you fight elites mid-campaign. See the problem?The only fun missions are the ones where you get to use the characters you want, don't have arbitrary loss conditions forced on you and don't have mandatory penalties that cripple you. That's like, 20% of the game's missions. Maybe.The customisation, the gear, the skills, the visuals, the audio...that's all great, which makes this game so frustrating. There's a decent game here, mired by absolutely boneheaded design decisions by someone who's never played gems like Enemy Unknown, Silent Storm, Final Fantasy Tactics and XCom. I hope this game is moddable, because otherwise it's just a waste of money at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first turn-based strategy game I've played in a long time that didn't feel like a copy/paste or palette swap of XCOM. It's definitely a little rough around the edges in spots (cutscene audio doesn't sync properly for me), there are some enemies that could use a little balancing (looking at you Locust grenadier), and there are some design decisions I find questionable (a weird drip-feed of cosmetic customization options, mandated characters for missions, and bosses that ignore/invalidate the core mechanics of the game (a gaming cardinal sin IMO)), but these are all small enough to be overlooked to see Gears Tactics for what it is: an interesting addition to the genre that's simple enough for new players to jump in but complex enough to keep long time strategy fans engaged.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the Gears of War series, I was excited to see how Gears Tactics would translate the gritty, cover-based combat we know and love into a turn-based strategy game. In many ways, it succeeds brilliantly, offering intense tactical gameplay while staying true to the essence of the Gears universe. However, the repetitive mission structures prevent it from reaching its full potential.Gameplay:At its core, Gears Tactics retains the series' signature fast-paced action, but now in a turn-based, strategic setting. The emphasis on cover, brutal executions, and using your squad’s abilities to outflank enemies feels like a natural extension of what Gears fans are used to. From frag grenades to chainsaw bayonets, the visceral, satisfying combat is ever-present, and it makes each encounter feel dynamic and cinematic.The game's highlight is its depth in tactical options. Managing your squad, customizing their abilities and weapons, and making tough, on-the-fly decisions in combat feels engaging. It’s particularly satisfying when you chain together combos, use teamwork to eliminate enemies, or execute enemies to gain extra actions.Story & Atmosphere:The game’s narrative serves as a prequel to the original Gears of War, focusing on Gabe Diaz and his team as they track down a ruthless Locust leader. The characters are well-developed, with solid voice acting and engaging banter that stays true to the tone of the franchise. The dark, war-torn environments are beautifully rendered, perfectly capturing the gritty world of Gears.Issue: Repetitive Game ModesDespite the strengths, one area where Gears Tactics stumbles is the repetition in its mission design. While the tactical combat is fun, the game relies heavily on the same few mission types, particularly the objective-based missions like rescues, holding key points, or escorting units. After a while, these missions start to blend together, and the lack of variety in objectives can feel a bit monotonous during the longer campaign. It would have been great to see more diversity in mission types or unique challenges to keep things feeling fresh throughout.Visuals & Sound:Gears Tactics is visually stunning, with detailed character models and environments that feel ripped straight out of the Gears universe. The familiar sound of Lancer chainsaws revving and explosions going off during combat brings a sense of nostalgia for series veterans, while the soundtrack sets the perfect tone for the intense, high-stakes battles.Verdict:Gears Tactics delivers a solid and exciting strategy experience that translates the brutal, cover-based combat of Gears of War into a turn-based format surprisingly well. For fans of the series, there’s plenty to love here—from the gritty, immersive world to the intense tactical battles. However, the repetitive mission structures hold the game back from being a true masterpiece.If you’re a Gears fan looking for something different but still grounded in the universe you love, Gears Tactics is worth your time. Just be prepared for a bit of repetition as the campaign progresses.

_childDocuments_.review: My take on the game so far is, after getting to Act 2 I think the game is pretty good and it doing a fairly good job of keeping me entertained and on my toes.It stands on it's own mertis, so for people saying it's XCOM but with a Gears of War paint job.... they are in for a big surprise. At this point it would be like comparing XCOM to the BATTLETECH game that is on the store front.The story is as you can expect, very in line with Gears of War. No bull, just get the job done.There is a storytelling element, like the Gears of War games, and when you load up a mission it gives you a little bit of info about what you need to do as well.The game is unique enough that if you did not play any type of XCOM game before, or any Turn Based Tactics shooter, you are going to struggle with this game, as their are many things that you will need to learn and how to deal with them and counter them.I am playing on Intermediate difficulty and I am enjoying the difficulty creep as the game introduces new enemies and how they engage you and how you are told on how you need to learn how to combat them effectively.I can see that with newer players to the Turn Based Tactics type of games, you might want to play the game on the easiest difficulty to learn the mechanics of this game as I can see people are going to make themselves very angry simply for the fact that they don't listen to what the game is telling you and trying to teach you, so play the game on easy so you can get a hang of it, then come back and play on a higher difficulty setting.An example of this, is their are some reviews from people who to me, are people who just play Call of Duty and expect things just to go their way, or just don't listen to what the game is telling you, but there are enemies in this game that will attack you if you run too close to them, or if they get too close to you, and that you need to deal some damage to them first like the Locust Grenadier before you can go near them, and also, you have to remember the enemies get the same amount of AP points as you do, so they will run towards you, fire at you, and then do another action, everything you can do, the enemies in this game can do too and them some, so you REALLY need to pay attention to what the game is telling you because if you die, and rage, and blame the game, just know that everyone that is playing this game, is just going to look at you and know that you are an idiot because you chose to not listen to what the game is teaching you, and that is on you.It has it's moments of you being in a tough situation, where you only have 1 guy vs about 7 enemies, and you are racing against the clock to rescue your soldiers, or you will have a mission where you need to defend two places at once with your 4 guys to get the bonus objective completed to get the rare loot crates (No there are no microtransactions in the game, it's just crates that you pick up on the battlefield like you did in Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War II if you played that game, and you got weapons, armour, etc from them to customise your soldiers at the hub).You can't superman your way with 1 dude like in XCOM 2, you need to be able to think a few steps ahead before you start running off into the abyss. Pick your fights properly, use one of your guys as a scout before you start running and gunning and MAKE SURE, you are using your soldiers abilities to their fullest potential, that will be the difference between life and death in certain circumstances in this game.I have not had any problems with the game in terms of stuttering or crashes but, funnily enough the only reason why my game did crash was because Steam stopped responding if I tabbed out and started to look through things on steam and that caused Steam to crash and that in tern caused the game to crash, so I am not sure what is going on there but apart from that no issues thus far.I am running a GTX 1080TI 11GB, a 32GB DDR 4 3600ghz RAM and an Intel I7 8700 and it's running smoothly at Max setting, with no stuttering or anything like that.For the price of the game, considering I am on ACT 2, and I think their are only 3 Acts or 4, and I have been playing for 6 hours, you will be replaying the same game after you have completed the game.You do have the option of playing Iron Man mode which many XCOM players do, and a few other things when you complete the game, but for someone like me where money is not a problem, I was happy to buy the game outright on Steam, for others though, maybe try the Xbox PC (Beta) launcher and download that and go with the game pass and try it out for yourself before you decide to purchasing it on Steam or what have you.All in all, a nice standalone title based off of the main series of the Gears of War games, and a definite must have for fans of the Gears of War series and fans of Turn Based Tactics games.I hope they continue to support this game, I know I will be trying my hand at modding this game and maybe adding some new units because I think the Locust Bolter Drone, the Grinders and Maulers would make a nice addition to the game.If I had to rate the game at the moment, around about near enough the mid 7 point mark going on to 8 I think.

HIRE more  creative designers to bring better games to the public in the future please!! 2/ Recruits = bad design decision. Yeah I have a big problem with the recruit system. It was NOT thought out well and is honestly plain dumb. As the story progresses, why am I able to hire recruits that are higher level than the ones i've been using and working on leveling up? Why did i just spend time renaming them, equipping them, painting their armor and weapons.... Waste of TIME! Why even bother having you hire recruits if they are just going to get out-leveled and become useless? This is just a DUMBASS design decision.      HOW THEY SHOULD HAVE HANDLED IT:  Don't allow us to hire recruits at all and if we do they shouldn't be higher level then our other recruits or main characters.... How about just having us rescue them in the side missions. Then they get added to our roster. And if for some reason all our recruits get killed, then and ONLY then, allow recruits to be added to the roster. 3/ No crafting and no technology to research. One word for why they didn't include this = LAZY!!! Don't charge us $60 for a game that you were lazy in developing. This game isn't worth more than $39.95, maybe $29.95 in it's current state! I'm sad to say i'm changing my recommendation to this game to a NO until the price matches the time the developers put into this game and the content it currently offers. I'm sorry i just feel like it's a ripoff to pay $60 for a game that could have been sooooo much more!  Please for the love of GOD....either add more to this game... or drop your price appropriately.UPDATE 5/11/2020 - Just passed the final act and i'm still going with a thumbs down due to: 1: the price is too high for what they offered in this game, 2: the missions felt very repetitive in nature and the re-use of maps in missions as well. (e.g.  rescue two recruits, hold two points consecutively, lower the bridge, get to the gate, rinse and repeat, rinse and repeat, rinse and repeat.) and finally 3. The missions are too linear in design. 4. Low replayability. 5. There is also a huge Lack of variation in enemies. I think there was only maybe 7 or 8 different enemy types besides the bosses. Disappointing!  I'd forgive most of the above if the price point on this game was appropriate to what they designed. I'm sticking with a fair price point of $34.99 to $39.99. They cheated us on $20-$25 for sure on this game. Otherwise, it was a fun ride. I did enjoy the story plot, the heroes, skill tree, and abilities. I do wish there were more variation in the weapon choices.  (e.g. Scouts are stuck with shotguns, no other gun can be used, etc.) Anyway, I just can't recommend buying until they drop the price and add more variation in the missions.

_childDocuments_.review: I am fully enjoying every single mission i deploy into. Every round feels challenging and different. Even though sometimes predictable behaviour from AI, there is still tons of fun elements and rewarding combat system. Every single hit, grenade, shot just feels like it had a massive impact. Maybe a real time strategy game would have been a better avenue, but otherwise playing a gears game on a turn by turns pace is actually incredibly painful and frustrating.Most units get around 3 actions per turn, and overwatch isnt really limited other than ammo.  What this means is 70% or more of the time, you will always be using overwatch for your last point.  Great feature, not very fun.  This game has fog of war, i know, i forgot that existed.  It's that weird fog of war where people can't see beyond 8 feet for some reason.  It's also just a faded white overlay not even a cool effect.  I have played all the Gears so i get the story. _childDocuments_.review: It's actually pretty solid. I'm surprised. The biggest downfall that I have with it, is that it has the same "problem" XCOM Enemy Unknown / Within had where you'll be fighting on the same maps over and over again.The fights do function a lot like XCOM, but imagine if you actually had more defensive options which makes for more interesting combat when the response to win isn't just "blow everything up before it gets a chance to move." _childDocuments_.review: Gears Tactics is really fun and very well-made. It addresses some of the shortcomings of X-COM, while changing enough stuff to put its own Gears-flavored mark on the genre. 18 hours into the game, I've noticed a few things I view as being superior to X-COM, and a few that are not quite on the same level.Pros:The game has great production quality in-line with a standard Gears game, and runs well on my graphics card despite the warning that pops up at the beginning telling me otherwise. The gameplay loop is fun and addictive and thankfully they have not monetized the loot system, as their obnoxious marketing has pointed out. Customization options for your gears are fleshed out, both in stat trees and cosmetics. The boss fights are also well-done, especially the first one, which is one of the most metal experiences I've had in a game. There is a certain weight to the shooting in this game that is not present in X-COM that I also appreciate.Cons:The game overloads you with troops, which on insane difficulty/ironman might make more sense, but on easy, normal, and hard just serves to clog up your barracks as units will so rarely die. The game is very generous when it comes to soldier deaths, allowing you many chances to prevent it. Additionally, your squad size is permanently affixed to 4 soldiers, which means you will have a lot of people sitting in your barracks that likely never see action. There is also an issue with experience gain, as the game consistently shoves new recruits in your face that start out at a higher level than your favorite troops can keep up with. It's of course possible to ignore them and stick with your favorite troops, but at the cost of going into missions with weaker gears.Also, it will come down to personal taste, but I have not enjoyed the writing in a Gears storyline since Gears 3, and the trend was unfortunately not broken here. The story isn't offensively bad, but it's fairly generic and hard to see anyone getting attached to any of the story characters. It's also important to note that there is no base-building in the game. It's just mission-to-mission, and there is little in the way of 'stuff to do' in between.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: This game is god awful.  Genuinely don't understand how this has such high reviews.  This game is profoundly boring.  And here is why: terrible story line, mundane gameplay, repetitive missions, and zero immersion.  I've played the gears games, and this games story line is just profoundly boring.  The characters aren't interesting, their goals you don't really care about, and the devs never did anything to make you want to care about the characters.  The gameplay is what you would expect from a game like this, turn based combat, but that's not why its bad.  It's bad gameplay because the missions themselves have boring objectives, (eliminate all hostiles, grab this crate, blow up this tank, kill more enemies, run back to your car).  Each mission is rinse and repeat the same thing over and over.  And the combat doesn't even make sense. You'll riddle a guy in the back with a machine gun and suddenly he'll explode with his legs flying off.  There's no correlation between the weapons you use and their impacts.  Everyone just explodes when they take damage, which is insane because this is a AAA game priced originally for $60.  I even bought this on sale for $35 and I am still disappointed I purchased this game.  The voice acting in the missions just further makes them worse, because you're not interested in watching the cut scenes because the acting is so poor and the story is so poor, that the combat you engage in right after just means even less.  There's also lots of bizarre poor design decisions.  Take character progression. You spend all your missions playing your favorite characters to level them up, and every mission that you rescue a new character they're automatically a higher level than your current ones.  So if you want to play your favorite character it logically makes sense for you not to, because the game is giving you more powerful characters that you haven't even grinded to level up.  That's a super poor design choice.This game is worth a $15, MAYBE $20 if the game becomes much more fun in the latter half of the campaign, but no where near $60.  It's evident that the dev's put very little creativity into this.  This game is just a cash cow.  It was created with minimal thought, using a formula created by other dev's like the xcom games, with boring story lines, cliche character classes, and a combat gameplay experience that is just xcom all over again.  It's xcom but with a different aesthetic.  But xcom had a interesting plot.  This is just boring, not at all compelling, and its clear that they are catering to a fan base that is young enough not to care about wasting money on a poor game.D-After I get my moneys worth I'm never buying another gears game again

_childDocuments_.review: Its an okay game. With good systems, good mechanics but pretty poor Tactical and stage progression.For people used to games like X-Com, you will have some fun but quickly tire out of doing side missions that are basically the same thing every few story missions.They made a formula for gameplay that is just "dead" from a story perspective. An example from the game is "Oh we gotta make grenades, so lets use 2-3 missions to collect the parts to make grenades". Im at 80% of the game right now and the story seems to be all about catching 1 bad guy while you walk around collecting resources to beat in generic missions.The stages feel generated following the same rules everytime with barely any real surprises after a few maps.Its still a good game engine with some interesting soldier mechanics, unit leveling and gear leveling system and pretty interesting enemy designs all around, which makes me even more sad that the story to level progression is so devoid of life and creativity.I wish they took the time to work on unique stages with twists and turns more instead of making the game artificially longer with missions that just are not interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I almost didn't buy this game based on some of the negative reviews. Frequent crashes, shallow strategy depth. Repetitive missions.I love the Gears of War series and have played them on hardest difficulty to get most hours out of the game and for the full omgwtf experience. Turn-based tactical and strategy games also happen to be my favorite genre (wooo Jagged Alliance, X-Com series, Disgaea & FF Tactics). I ended up pulling the trigger and got this game with mixed expectations.Does it have infinite depth with tons of replay value? No. You don't see multiple layers combining strategy with tactical game play like you would with X-Com or even the Total War series. But boy is it ever satisfying to flank and shoot the 100th drone when you nail positioning and combine your skills for most effective action point usage. I haven't grown bored of it yet and have had plenty of tense moments where I thought one of my guys was gonna die because I got too greedy. And endorphin rush when I somehow managed to get them out alive. The game does not feel unfair (so far). Whenever I screw up I know exactly why a mission went south. I give it 2/2 thumbs up.NB: I have an nVidia card and have experienced no crashes so far in the first 12 hours of playing. So I consider myself lucky. I can easily see how this would be frustrating reading some of the negative reviews about this game.So far I have only seen minor bugs and a few game design oversights (difficult to discern enemy units when zoomed out - I have to identify them by their health pool).
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: You know, when this game came out I was pretty excited about it. The thought of the Xcom gameplay in the Gears universe was pretty awesome, I played on Experienced and by the end of the game I just wanted it to be over. The boss fights are tough sure, but they are tough because of the insane amount of health, the AOE attacks and enemies that spawn in.  The difference between the normal grub enemies and the enhanced units is insane. Example: a normal grub goes into overwatch, and you can run through the gunfire with minimal damage and chainsaw him. Then enhanced version will stagger your unit, stopping the action and with massive damage. If you do manage the chainsaw kill, it automatically reduces your units damage by 70% for 2 turns. Should mention that there is a pretty big gap in health between the units also, enough that chainsawing a full health enhanced grub and taking the debuff is preferable in a sticky situation or taking a shot from it.For a lot of the missions, taking hero units is mandatory and the normal soldiers are just their to supplement the ranks.  Soldiers that fall behind in level get stripped of their gear and kicked out because the amount of experience required to get them up is just to steep. I had one soldier I took on every mission I could because there isn't a Heavy hero class (favorite class). Knowing that the heroes units would be mandatory for boss fights, I wanted to take them on every mission possible to get them experience.  By the time I got to the final boss the heroes were level 6. Mandatory side missions and the modifiers that come with them. You are already consistently outnumbered and the game will give the grubs 200% accuracy at full health or stay ahead of the nemesists bombardment and give you 2 movement actions or can only take 2 soldiers + Jack to go up against a force 10+.  It's all doable, but is more frustrating then fun.Finally, the story is meh, the characters have personalities of boulders with LEDs strapped to them. I did really wanted to like this game, the original Gears trilogy was my high school years but once it gets uninstalled I'll probably never play or think about it again. I'm not mad, just disappointed, 5/10. Going to see if Phoenix Point will satisfy my Xcom cravings.  Oh something positive! Executing a downed enemy grants a bonus action to everyone in the squad except the executor, planned and played correctly, you can chain a massive string of kills together and it is satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really difficult to recommend this game at its full price, as many of its shortcomings can cause the game to feel like working an Excel spreadsheet. On the other hand, Gears Tactics has moments that show the potential to outpace even XCOM's addictive nature.At its best, Gears is an aggressive tactics game with extremely polished animations and environments alien to what you've come to expect from strategy games, against oppressive enemies with dozens of interactions. Kicking explosive enemies into eachother, rushing to mini-boss weapons, and finding the perfect solution to a combat puzzle by leapfrogging action points across your party all looks and feels really good.At its worst, the mission generator fails to place challenging enemies and objectives, you've figured out that some class skills are horrendously overpowered, and you're spending too much time re-equipping  for  of your   that you bring on a mission. Mutators either make for a fun challenge or only exist to band-aid unbalanced playstyles. You never grow attached to any of your characters as recruits often become available at a higher level than what you have, and each character of the same class plays exactly the same if you were to optimally give them the same build.Definitely a game for enthusiasts but absolutely not an alternative to XCOM in regards to longevity and variety.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid turn based strategy game with convincing graphic and sound. I like the skill trees for the different classes, as well as the weapon and armor customization for the soldiers. The battles are fun and well paced.  It`s quite enjoyable to combine the different  skills and attacks  to set up kills zones to mow down the hordes hordes of enemies the game throws at you, or to focus down an elite enemy. I actually enjoy the gameplay more than X-Com 2, it feels less random and i have bigger control over the situation with the tools at my disposal.At the time of writing this review I am in chapter 2 of the campaign and the story is OK so far, but nothing to write home about. I never played an other game in the Gears series before, but i find the universe interesting enough. Definitely recommended, esp. if you can buy the game during a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A person that has bought the game should not have to activate an XBOX account in order to play.  Steam should label any game that requires an XBOX account clearly so that customers can avoid such games.  If the developers want to use some features of XBOX, at least make XBOX optional.  Microsoft does too much spying so I have no wish to activate their products like XBOX.Despite the above the intense tactical missions make the game entertaining.  Requiring certain soldiers on many of the missions does make it more difficult to get lower ranks promoted.The game runs very smoothly on my Windows 10 system with 16 GB of RAM.The must win condition for every mission, since there are almost always two units that must survive, Jack being one of them, makes the game very tough. The time limits on some missions are so tight that very dangerous risks must be assumed to even have a chance at success.  Sometimes not all the conditions of a mission are given before mission start.  My last mission had a seven turn time limit, but gave no indication that I would lose the mission when the limit expired.  For most missions it just meant the secondary objective was not accomplished.  There is another mission where the enemy has massive artillery coverage that advances so quickly that it is difficult to fight back against the enemy effectively.  Running at full speed will only result in getting decimated by the enemy.Despite the above the game is fun to play, but does not really provide settings for true beginning players.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. I really did. I've had two incomplete playthroughs.The first had ironman mode on. Coming from an XCOM background I thought this would be a fun way to play - lose a character, have to fight on without them later. Turns out, what this actually means is if any story characters (which are almost always present) die in a mission, the entire campaign ends. That was the end of my first run.My second run ended when I was deleting some potential recruits from the recruit tab (DO NOT DO THIS!!!!), as they were lower level than my current roster so I figured why not. Well I found out why not. The very next side mission required a team larger than I was now capable of producing. The mission is not skippable, there is no autosave before I made my roster mistake, and there is no way to add recruits. I literally lost this campaign by clicking some wrong options in a menu.It's otherwise fun! But I can only have so many runs get bricked by game-breaking oversights before I give up.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is addicting and is a fun callback to the old Gears games, cleverly implemented if you ignore some big plotholes. Unfortunately the mission system and technical glitches make it incredibly tedious and it punishes simple mistakes (not a down side if you like a challenge but it gets incredibly frustrating)Jack is prone to freezing the game with it's abilities not deploying, or softlocking with no option to end turn. There were times when an ability would disappear completely. And with no manual saves a checkpoint revert could cost you the last 20 minutes of playtime. The boss fights are designed to be health sponges with add waves that ramp up as you go further along meaning you'll be stuck for hours trying to beat the boss and they're disappointingly basic.The skill trees within each class are streamlined to be powerful and cater to your playstyle with fun combinations to steam roll missions; that said, there's almost no reason to not bring your hero units for the entire game since after every mission you can recruit Gears that will be at level or higher than units you've had from the start. This means there's no incentive to get attached to any unit if you can just toss them out when you get a replacement with the same skills and extra skill points to spend into after every mission.Weapon and armor mod combos are great, and the customization is a nice quality of life if you want to personalize your troops. Mission objectives are not too varied and the story is done after 42 missions; the game does become endless after you beat the story acts.

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy entry in the world of squad tactics games. Superficially like XCOM and its ilk, but rewards rather than punishes aggression and (measured) risks. Feels fast-paced and engaging due to the three action point system. I know next to nothing about the Gears franchise, but enjoy the setting and 'tude.Yay: - Excellent engine and graphics with great flexibility for a variety of rigs.- Missions that rarely feels tedious or routine, and inherently satisfying "feel" to combat that other genre entries lack. Easy going missions are a good opportunity to show off your capacity to humiliate the grubs with brutal execution chains and bold moves. Difficult missions require careful consideration and adaptive strategies.- Overwatch is balanced and useful for both your squad and enemies.- Excellent skill system. No two soldiers of the same class play exactly the same, and there are tons of combinations to try out.- Just plain fun, even when you're getting crushed.- I personally like the checkpoint save system, as it removes the urge to save scum but allows for the opportunity to try new strategies if your initial effort failed to impress.- Good controller support with full customization and combo buttons (if you care about such things). Meh:- Grabbing Loot boxes seem like a chore when I'd rather be annihilating grubs.- Linear missions and overall campaign.- Fair cosmetic customization options, but not for hero toons and largely pointless for generic gears due to constant recruit shuffle.Boo:- Inventory UI is abysmal, highlighting the lack of things to do between missions besides tediously equip and unequip gear.- XP gain is painfully slow, to the point that its futile to try to level up non-hero gears as you will be able to recruit ones at a higher level sooner than they will level up even if you bring them on every mission and farm kills for them. Wish there was XP rewards for finishing missions quickly/efficiently rather than just for kills.- Constant stream of new gears strips them of imagined personality or accomplishment. Hard to tell them apart because they all spawn with the same green color scheme.- Forced hero toons of a specific class severely limit options for squad composition.- Too many enemies (especially "miniboss" types like Zealot and Boomer) have immunity/deterrents to melee attacks. I wish they simply took less damage from chainsaw/bayonet rather than instant execution instead. - Expensive for a game without a lot of depth.Musings:- Having played tons of XCOM:EW/2/WOTC and finishing Chimera Squad right before this, I vastly prefer the way GT handles combat and action economy. Chimera Squad was a marked improvement with interleaved turn orders and turning "pods" into "breach mobs," but suffers from vastly overpowered free-action items trivializing encounters and poor squad ability balance. - I do wish there was any sort of strategy layer in GT, as inventory management is a major drag and I feel very disconnected from the "build a plucky outsider army and strategize against the big bad" storyline that plays out in the main missions.Updated Veteran Mode Thoughts:- Highly repetitive due to limited map/sitrep/mob structures, but weirdly engaging to grind, if only to experiment with squad/skill/equipment combos that weren't possible in the campaign.-XP gain still painfully slow.- Way too many Nemacyst bombing runs, the absolute worst mission type. If you're going to play this mode, gather as many scouts as you can and build them for Sprint/Nimble.- Continuing to get Rare loot from missions/boxes for the most part makes optional goals/grabbing boxes pointless when you're after legendaries, which there are only a couple of each "cycle."- An amusing treadmill, but would rather have had New Game+ mode. I hope more content and game modes are released eventually, the core gameplay of Gears Tactics is very strong, but so many things feel like proofs of concept that don't feel meaningful in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Soweit ein gutes spiel es hat aber auch seine schwächen.Von der Grafik her sieht, das Spiel sehr gut aus die Sound sowie Kill ist echt sehr gut gemacht. Die kleinen Video Szenen im Spiel sind auch sehr gelungen. Die Story ist auch soweit ok für ein Runden basiertes Spiel.Was leider nicht so toll ist:Alle drei Boss kämpfe ein und das selbste Prinzip und Schema man kämpf so gar nicht gegen den Boss sondern gegen seine Truppen bzw. Verstärkungen die in einer endlos Schleife immer & immer wieder kommen bis man die drei Phase des Boss besiegt hat.Das nächste sind die Truppen am Anfang hat man Sid & Gabe was auch ok ist. Dann später kommt eine Scharfschützin und im letzten Akt plötzlich eine Späherin und vorher kämpft man mit anderen Level sie aber kann nicht wählen mit wem man den Boss Endkampf führen will. Sid & Gabe das die dabei sind ok aber, dann hätte man dem Spieler selbst wählen lassen sollen wer die anderen beiden sind.Das nächste die Missionen wiederholen sich ständig ab Mitte Akt 2 fällt das immer mehr auf da dann Nebenmissionen kommen die immer alle gleich sind sowie die Story Missionen hier wurde leider sehr viel Potential  verschwendet.Fazit es ist kein schlechtes Spiel aber auch kein gutes Spiel man kann damit sein Spaß haben. Grafik sowie Sound und kills Szenen sind gut gemacht sowie eine nette Story die euch bekleidet durch das Spiel. Man muss damit aber klar kommen, das Missionen sich Wiederholen und die Boss kämpfe immer das gleiche sind nur halt mit anderen Figuren. As far as a good game, it also has its weaknesses.From the graphics, the game looks very good, the sound and kill is really very well done. The little video scenes in the game are also very well done. The story is also ok for a round-based game.Which is unfortunately not so great:All three boss fight one and the same principle and scheme you do not fight against the boss but against his troops or reinforcements that come again and again in an endless loop until you have defeated the three phases of the boss.The next are the troops at the beginning you have Sid & Gabe which is also ok. Then later comes a sniper and in the last act suddenly a scout and before that you fight with other levels, but you can't choose with whom you want to lead the boss final battle. Sid & Gabe that they are ok but then you should have let the player choose who the other two are.The next one, the missions repeat themselves constantly from the middle of Act 2, that is more and more noticeable because then there are side missions that are always the same and the story missions here, unfortunately, a lot of potential was wasted.Conclusion it is not a bad game but also not a good game you can have fun with it. Graphics as well as sound and kills scenes are well done and a nice story that dresses you through the game. But you have to come to terms with the fact that missions are repeated and the boss fights are always the same, just with different characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the game for about 40 hours and I am about 2/3 of the way through. This is one of the best tactical turn based games I have played. The story is interesting, the cinematics are of high quality and progress the story well. But the tactical battles are simply where this game shines.Not once have I felt that the AI was cheating me. All the times I was struggling was not because I was up against countless enemies or enemies that had an unfair advantage, but because I simply made bad decisions. The beauty of the game though is when I realised what I was doing wrong the game gave me the mechanics to turn the battle around in my favour.Let me also clarify some misleading info about the save system. Battles in the game, like many tactical turn based games, can take upwards of an hour for each fight. While you are unable to make manual saves in mid combat the game does make a suspend save if you quit the game during battle. So if you need to turn off the game for whatever reason you can return to the battle exactly where you left it. Personally I find this totally acceptable as some games have no save mid battle at all. My gaming time can get interrupted quite often so being able to have a game save my position when I exit it is an almost necessity for me.Also most battles will auto save at a pre-determined checkpoint but I don't know how that works as i have not had the need to revert to a checkpoint save in my game.So while this review was mainly to clarify the info about the save system I hope to renew my feelings once I finish it.In the meantime I recommend this game without any reservations if you like tactical turn based rpg's.

_childDocuments_.review: It's painfully clear they had a few good ideas with this game, then just ran with those for as long as possible. There are three acts to this game and it becomes abundantly clear that they needed to fill time about halfway through. There are only a handful of mission varieties, all of which you'll encounter again and again through forced side missions that artificially pad out gameplay length (especially in the final act). I don't know, I'm so mad at that. There's nothing wrong with a shorter game if the short bits are fun. The final act isn't fun. There's nothing fun about the last 50 percent of this game. Pirate it, get it on Game Pass, or steal a friends physical copy and play it for an afternoon if you like XCom or strategy games alike. Never play it for more than a few hours. Don't give it the satisfaction.

_childDocuments_.review: HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.I have over 800+ hours into XCOM2, but GT has set the standard for what 'tactical shooter' should be. The core gameplay of taking cover, setting up overwatches, disrupting movement, action point economy, chaining executions... is a thing of beauty. XCOM is almost better described as 'tactical puzzle' by comparison. The core game runs about 40 hours and there's not a ton of replayability, but 40 hours is pretty damn good for any game. Some of the mission types get a tad repetitive, and there's unfortunately not much of a strategic layer. It tells a scripted story with scripted characters, and that's all. This is not the XCOM experience of emergent storytelling and mod support is minimal, limiting you to just tweaking weapon and enemy values. But if you want the pure uncut cocaine of tactical shooting, GT is the gold standard. If they ever make a GT2 with a deep immersive strategic layer, XCOM3 will really have its work cut out for it to compete.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a truly good turn-based team tactics game. Narrow in its scope, but what it does, it does really well. Things to note:- This is a purely tactical game with no base-building strategic element like X-COM. You go on missions, get gear, and go on more missions.- The story is totally linear.- There is SOME procedural generation of maps, but you'll end up seeing the same general map a lot.- Camera movement, character movement around the map, and versatility of action points is all superior to X-COM. Where the game feels small in scope, the tactical play is really well polished. - There's a "Veteran Mode" after the campaign players have the option of pursuing. It's just going on random missions for a chance at high-end loot, though. It honestly gets pretty repetitive. This game is going to shine with an expansion or two. For now, I'm not sure it's worth $60, but I don't regret the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Gears Tactics.First off, it is not Xcom 2: War of the Chosen but that is pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ high bar for a new game. Secondly, I know very little about the Gears franchise aside from what my stepsons told me, so I can't say if the story meshes with the main gears line or not. That aside I am happy with my purchase.Pros:* The three action system is interesting. It has a very different feel than Xcom or more traditional move + action systems. Reminds me a bit of Pathfinder 2 TTRPG in that respect.* Character skill trees are good. Class balance is good. If you combo abilities with the right pieces of gear you can kill for days.* Executions allow you to stretch your turn in a unique fashion, giving game turns a very elastic feel where you can go on wondrous kill streaks.* Graphics are nice, benchmark system is amazing, and character details are lovely.* Kicking tickers back into enemy lines never gets old.* Free Play after you finish the main story!* 2/3 of the story bossfights were fun.Cons* Could use a few more enemy types. There are quite a few, but maybe some visually distinct common mobs would be good.* Some classes seem really weak and boring initially, which might cause you to overlook how good they are later on.* Some of the random mission types are way more rewarding that others.Ironman is especially fun in this game, since if one of the main characters gets killed you lose immediately.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game.It is somewhat repetitive with the side missions. Would be a whole lot shorter campaign without doing the same rehashed scenarios in between each main mission, but the strategy by necessity changes from mission to mission due to choice of units, terrain, and luck. I found myself repeatedly being challenged by side missions because i did not plan ahead and used most of my best troops in the first one. Then they are locked (as each of the three missions are supposed to be taking place simultaneously) and i was forced to use units i was unfamiliar with. So even though you'll find yourself collecting crates, or running in front of an artillery barrage a few times, each time is different in scope and strategy for how you actually defeat the mission. It is a very challenging game often as not.In game combat is good. Everything is balanced. Some locust troops have an obvious and painful advantage, but they are, by design, few in numbers. Target them, or crowd control them while you make work on the little guys. My only other complaint is they did not add a game mode like Horde in the original Gears of War. This platform is perfectly setup for it. Why is there not a wave survival game mode? Seems like a missed opportunity. Multiplayer too. Several of those side mission types would make great multiplayer matches.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is a great game but its been smoothered by some really poor design choices by the devs, few tweaks and this game could really shine however for £50 your money is better spent elsewhere. I would value this game at around £25 maybe £30 if your a real die hard fan but in its current state this is outright robbery. More info below.Recruits seem pointless to focus on as you can just recruit a better 1 within the next 2 or 3 missions plus with only 4 slots in the mission you will be using 3 of those for your heroes (the main characters) so you can keep them leveled up.Boss fights are surprisingly good although quite simplistic and easy to do, however it does provide a nice change of pace.The actual gameplay itself is very good and feels quite solid, yes there are a few moments of RNG hell but generally these are very few and far between, the combat side of this game is very nicely done with the whole leveling system in place which is fairly good and how abilities are used to prevent some OP nutter chainsawing their way through an entire horde. The combat side of this game is great, its the rest of it which makes it fall flat on its face.Menus are quite clunky and awkward although once you get familiar this issue resolves itself but its just awkward.What the game is missing is some meaningful strategy layer when not in combat as currently its just apply gear and go into another mission but for a strategy game this is woefully inadequate. The potential for something incredible is right here yet it has all life choked from it by a horribly linear storyline with forgettable faces everywhere. Maybe if the game had some form of strategic map which you went across doing randomly generated missions then story missions to ensure a better leveling experiance then this would make the game more enjoyable but it is literally mission equip loot mission equip loot mission choose 1 of 2 side missions now equip loot now mission etc and this chokes the life out of the game.This game could have been so much more I can only hope the devs learn from this and improve for their next tactics game

_childDocuments_.review: There are some solid ideas and mechanics, putting their own twist on the XCOM formula but the balance is awful with some pretty bad pacing and content variety issues.It also doesn't help that the "loot" feels tacked on, the gear customization UI is horrendous and the character customization is about as shallow as it gets.It's like they tried to be "high production value XCOM" but never really went further than that or finished the game/design.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: On the whole a great translation of the Gears style into a tactical game but it has a few stumbles. Tactical battles are fun as is the customization of loadouts and skills. But the enemies are not very dynamic as every class of foe will behave relatively the same. Boss Battle are somewhat fun but go into a formula. Story is actually decent but the pacing is terrible as you have to do 1-3 side missions before moving on with the plot ones. They will also sometimes limit which characters can go on missions and this lead to a few random troopers out leveling my heroes, it also hurts that a key character is introduced halfway through the final act with little to no expansion of her backstory that is only hinted at, I guess she is important in Gears 4 and 5 game, but Ive yet to play those. Gameplay gets a bit stale in as it goes into the 3rd act. It doesnt quite get to the Xcom level but I am glad the IP decided to break the mold into a totally different genre and hope they continue this trend in gears and possible other IPs. Pick it up at a sale, or buy if you really want devs to make more stuff like this.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love xcom or the gears games then this game is a must buy for you. It's like these games had a baby because its the turned base fighting you come to love in xcom but in the gears universe. This game is done so well its way more fast pace fighting, way more enemies and types you have never seen before. Plus my lord does it feel good to get those executions and watch your squad go to work with that extra action point you just got. This game also has an amazing story that makes you go no way the more you play, the more secrets you uncover you never would of found out without playing this game it just ties it all together so well.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: I played a lot of TBS games since the playstation X era and played Gears of War 1-3 back on Xbox and I can honestly say this is a solid game that's feels both like a TBS and the third-person cover shooter I used to play and love.Solid upsides of this game include but are not limited to- There are rarely gamebreaking or campaign ending bugs in this game, especially compared to XCOM2 and WOTC.- Auto-save checkpoints means that even during the event of a power outage you don't lose that much progress.- Ticker kick is still in the game and by god I love it.- Lootboxes in this game don't cost money so no predatory monetization tactics that's been creeping up on the industry for years.Solid downsides of this game include, but are not limited to- Weird graphical bugs when managing your roster that might take you out of immersion- Auto-saving and checkpoints means that even on a non-ironman run it's still pretty much closer to ironman even on regular gameplay (An upside for me but I know a lot of people like save-scumming like I used to do)- At the time of this writing, there is currently no steam workshop mod support, so no crazy hardcore Longwar/Longwar2/LongWaroftheChosen like mods here compared to XCOM/XCOM2/WOTCPick it up if you enjoy TBS and the Gears universe.

It has some solid game play, but some of the features I just wish were implemented in a different way or just left out entirely. _childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for an XCOM-like fix, this game unfortunately isn't it. There is a lot to like about the choices they make for the tactical combat system. But as someone who has spent a lot of time with the new XCOM series, I grew board with this one at about 10 hours of play.Why?Missions are very same-yEnemies have very little varietyGear management is tediousLinear story - you just jump mission to missionNo strategy layerIt's a fun little ride and as all the mechanics were novel to me, I was enjoying myself. But 10 hours in it feels more like a chore. There are simply not enough decisions to make along the way for any kind of replayability.I went looking for mods to improve this and QoL but unfortunately the game either seems tough to mod or lacking a community investing the time - or both.So, if you're an XCOM fan, you can _mostly_ skip it but it might be worth it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: This is a ported game, but overall its done pretty smoothly. Ive had a couple of CTDs but thats pretty common in ports. The game itself is very stable and theres no discernable difference from the console version. The game itself plays very similar to XCOM, and you can see how the game borrows various combat mechanics and rehashes them for its own purpose. Movement feels smooth, combat is often rapid and explosive and reflective of the gears universe as a whole. The game tells the story very very slowly and the few cinematic parts are generally pretty short, so you spend alot of time on side missions just leveling up and getting better gear. All the classes are pretty strong, and certain gear goes with certain classes way better then others. The inventory management system in the barracks is kinda messy, but the concept of putting the best loot on your guys is pretty straight forward. Customization options unlock as the game progresses, but you can never fully edit every detail of your non-hero pawns, which is a let down. The games main draw back is likely its linear story, and limited replayability. After a certain point combat can feel "too easy" and thus repetitive, simply because your heros are that strong comparred to the grubs. You can play 1 campaign normal and then another with "Jack", a support drone that allows you to do alot of shenanigan things in your battles. After this the game doesn't have much to offer. Good if youre looking for a new spin on the xcom combat system, bad if you want something you can play for 200+ hours
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Gears of War spin-off turned to squad-based tactics.Suprisingly, well done Xcom-like strategy game with great squad customization (no base) with many missions connected together through classic GoW story.The combat feels great with several different classes and satisfying mechanics like close combat and overwatch. You can really feel GoW from this, from characters, graphics, gore, boss fights to overall tone. Game is not too long and you can continue with endgame veteran missions hunting for supreme equipment. Only downside, which is common for these types of games, is limited number of mission types which cycle on regular basis.Would love to see regular RPG (like Fallout, Wasteland) where you travel through world with your squad, fighting locust, saving outpost etc. Gear Tactics definitely shows such game could have potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: Despite it requiring an Xbox account to play, I was surprised by the production-value of this game. I was expecting a janky cash grab but the animation, art, graphics, and sound design show that a lot of attention has been paid. There is a substantial plot here which feels consequential to the overall GoW story. The characters are well acted, well modelled and well animated. They feel alive in a way that XCom 2 characters do not. The gameplay too feels lean, with all abilities being useful, and each class feeling valued.
_childDocuments_.name: Gears Tactics

_childDocuments_.review: The combat/tactics are great. I don't love the art style, but I like how tactile the game feels compared to XCOM, et al. The complaints about repetitiveness are unfortunately correct. It feels like they made a $40 game, but had to pad it with a bunch of filler to validate a $60 price tag. Still, I enjoyed it.

name: Phantom Breaker: Omnia
detailed_description: WISHLIST PHANTOM BREAKER: OMNIA JOIN OUR DISCORD OTHER GAMES IN THE PHANTOM BREAKER FRANCHISE About the Game Phantom Breaker: Omnia, a massive update to Phantom Breaker: Extra, a 1-vs-1 2D anime fighter originally released by Mages in 2013. The game features 2 guest characters, Kurisu Makise from Steins;Gate and Rimi Sakihata from Chaos;Head, as well as two brand new characters created specifically for Phantom Breaker Omnia. 20 Character Roster! Includes all the characters and guest characters from Phantom Breaker: Extra like Kurisu Makise from Steins;Gate and two brand new characters created specifically for Phantom Breaker: Omnia. Choose from 3 different fighting styles: Quick, Hard, and Omnia! The 3 different styles in the game can drastically change your characters’ speed, power, and mechanics. Retuned and Rebalanced! The ability to pull off amazing combos and special attacks has never been easier as Phantom Breaker: Omnia's fighting system has been overhauled and rebalanced. Dual Language Audio! A Phantom Breaker series first, all the characters will have English voice acting. The game’s text will be also translated into English, Japanese, French, Italian, German, Spanish, Simplified and Traditional Chinese. Modern, Remixed Soundtrack! The background music for each character has been redone and remixed with the option to play the original background music. The Complete Experience! Players can immerse themselves with the stories from both the original Phantom Breaker and Phantom Breaker: Extra. A mysterious man, known only as ‘Phantom’ appeared in Tokyo —the capital city of Japan—and manipulated vulnerable adolescents into fighting each other, bestowing upon them mystical weapons of great strength known as ‘Fu-mension Artifacts.’ In exchange, he promised to grant their wish if they survive. Unbeknownst to the combatants, the fierce clashes between Fu-mension Artifacts caused distortions in space-time, which compromised the boundaries between parallel universes. The collapse of these parallel universes would ultimately break the seal, unleashing Phantom’s destructive powers.

_childDocuments_.review: It is rather unfortunate to have to say this but this game suffers from a major lack of polish. The controls issue goes beyond simply scrambled gamepad controls, this would barely even be an issue if for example the button settings menu were significantly better - The best way to do button setting is to show actions and assign buttons rather than show buttons and assign actions, this has been established for a while now. The fact that this game does not do it this way makes working with the scrambled buttons when reassigning far worse than it should be. The whole package is just a tad weird. There's no command lists for characters, some of the animations look a tad weird, some of the characters seem to be 3D while others are sprites? There's no rollback but that's the least of the issues. I understand the circumstances of the port and international release must have been hard but I can't help but wonder if going out of your way to add English voice acting was necessary for a title this niche and if resources could not have been allocated better to (if not rollback) at least polish up the gameplay package and training mode. Despite I love for such niche fighting games I have to give this game a negative review but I do so with hope that things will improve in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The combos flow well for the style of the game, better than Blade Strangers and Umineko I guess.Neutral is finicky probably because the game has several different mechanics. It's different but I'm sure I'll get used to it overtime: * Press forward as you're getting hit to evade (A parry, also not too sure as explained below)* Press forward while blocking to dash, evade or something (No clue how this works* Able to dash through someone and it also evades and I guess clashes with some opponent's stuff like their own dash* To add onto the previous point there’s three dash attacks, one for each button and they have some kind of armor propertyThe game does not have a tutorial of ANY KIND and everything is inside an in-game glossary.  It's overly designed and there's too many pages so it's hard to take in and retain information.I honestly cannot tell you 100% how the different character modes or the game’s system mechanics work,  Found out that the Genei Jin (Yun) mode applies to all modes and not just Quick.I'm a hands-on person so I won't be able to remember all the mechanics easily, doesn't help that the glossary's presentation is a POS and is too many pages..  of all things is locked behind this glossary. Yes special moves are homogenized but they could extend the list with command normals and system mechanics.I can remember +R's or other game's mechanics that don't have an extensive tutorial but there's many different things going on in Omina. There isn't even a combo trial mode, embarrassing.Not even the macros in the controller settings tell you what they do..There's no Instant Rematch in Local, no round animation skipping at any point, max resolution is 1080p, no Alt-F4ing.Even for the lower than MSRP base price on top of the discount I can't recommend it right now. I'm just surprised that it has controller hotplugging unlike BBTAG. Command Lists are only found in the glossary... I can’t tell you the amount of times I went into Genei Jin mode expecting to do something cool and just have my combo dropped. _childDocuments_.review: This is a hard game to recommend. Let's get the big ones out of the way. No, this doesn't have rollback netcode and it's not going to be added later. No, this doesn't have the same level of polish as top tier anime fighting games like Guilty Gear Strive. I'm not even sure I can say the combo system is as complicated as its contemporaries. Another thing working against it is this is kind of a definitive release of a 2011 game. This is not a fresh new game from the ground up. It's going to be missing some polish because of its more than a decade old roots. I don't think the game looks ugly by any means but it's going to look dated in comparisons. And it's a mostly bare bones PC port lacking in resolution and graphical settings you usually expect. This feels like a console game running on my computer. So why the recommended rating? It's scrappy. There's some head scratching decisions but there's something about it that feels like a game made by a smaller team trying to swing big.The fighting is in line with what you'd expect from many anime fighting games. It's pretty combo-centric, quick, and hectic at times. But this has a more simplified input approach. There is a universal control scheme for all the characters. There's no traditional inputs for special attacks but more a platform fighter approach where one button is responsible for the different specials. SP and left, SP and right, and SP and down are the special moves for everyone. Super moves also follow this pattern except with adding in the heavy attack button (SP + H + Left, etc). This control scheme is going to feel very basic if you're used to most other fighting games but there is a benefit. Once you get the universal basics down, you can jump in with any character. Instead of spending hours either blindly rolling through all the directional and button combinations or combing through move lists in a menu to see what you missed, you already know how to do everyone's attacks. You can start learning the characters immediately. There's no guessing if one input combination works for one character or another. I've got a long enough history with fighting games to learn moves the traditional way. But, I'd be lying if I said I didn't miss Phantom Breaker's approach when I started another new fighting game recently and beginning the study up process on a whole new roster of characters.Speaking of roster, Phantom Break Omnia has a decently sized roster even with a couple of characters being a Ryu and Ken kind of deal. The characters have weapons that were given to them or magically generated so there's some variety in what everyone is using. The English voice cast has done a great job as well. As usual for my ear, they sound a bit wacky when shouting attack names in the middle of a fight but they absolutely shine in the story mode. Every character has their own story section to go through for the character backstories and world building. But it's definitely for relaxed play. They want you to be able to win and enjoy the story. The difficulty is to be found in the other modes so hit those up instead for the game's challenge.I bought this game with the intention to put it in an arcade style build. And surprisingly, I didn't have any issues with my usually finicky 2 player arcade setup. The devs have put out a guide to follow if you do have issues but it seems like a problem with Steam's remapping or controller emulation not playing nicely with the game. Your experience may vary there. And I'm also not going to be heading online with this game as that's not what I do in any fighting game. I only play casually in person. Others may not be happy this game will not have rollback netcode and that's something you have to decide if you can (or can't) play without. I will freely admit the launch discount is what made me to decide to get Phantom Breaker now instead of later. Full price for a game that I basically never heard of was not something I was going to jump into. You may also feel like waiting for a sale and I can't say I blame you. At $40 USD, It does have a higher profile price for a game that (at least stateside) doesn't have the same high profile name.I like this game. It has flaws and it has shortcomings once you put it out against the rest of its competition. But the characters have some variety, the music is pretty good, and it's just nice to jump into without a larger upfront learning investment. There's many familiar concepts that I can slot my existing skills into so I feel already experienced with the game. Your opinion or experience may differ but I've enjoyed my time with the game so far and look forward to learning more about this lesser known series. I don't think it's my next obsession like Guilty Gear has been but that's okay. Not everything has to be a mega smash or all time favorite. A game can also just be a decent game and provide some hours of entertainment.
