_childDocuments_.review: Phantom Breaker Omnia has finally hit our shores Stateside!  And means diving deep into the story and lore between a host of characters, and dazzling attacks, and visuals.  Now don't me wrong this isn't the most perfect port of a fighter.  But, the brand new English localization, comprised  EN, JP  voice acting, a good control scheme and soundtrack were (in my eyes) greatly improved upon.   Players get to duke it out in classic Phantom Breaker venues, ones which dedicated fans will recognize and want to throw down in.  Well, how does it compare to other fighters out there?  I'm glad you asked that:   Phantom Breaker Omnia brings it's own unique flavoring to the mix of fighters out there.  Again, it's not going to take home Best Fighter of the Year, unless they seriously rework the netcode.  There are some noticeable bits of slowdown in gameplay when the fighting gets heavy.  And whether or not the Story mode is your thing or not.  Your overall  enjoyment will vary.   Playing through the Story Mode is where most of your time will be spent.  Unlocking artwork and as well honing your skills in classic 1 v 1 matches against a CPU that can be very aggressive.  Even on the lower difficulty settings.  With little to no Input Lag should you desire, every button press will either deliver crushing blows or well timed counters.   The controls aren't traditional in the sense of most fighting games.  You have your standard Light, Medium and Heavy attacks, or Shoulder Buttons and/ Left and Right Triggers executing your Special attacks.  You can change the D-Pad or Button layout as you wish. Since I use an Xbox 360 controller it's relatively easy.     As of now, regarding the absence of rollback netcode,  I haven't the strongest opinion as to why it's missing here.   Both the offline and online portions are fully functional.  I have no idea if online matches are dropped due to poor bandwith or not.   In terms of graphics quality the character sprites and backgrounds look as sharp as they did in Phantom Breaker Extra.   It looks pretty good in 1080p and that's fine with me.   Each character has their own unique set of special attacks with one or two palette swapped characters being unchanged.   I hope that Rocket Panda Games will take into consideration some of the lesser known, or not as big contributors and increase the player roster.    Despite it's serious nature, the violence is toned down, so don't expect MK style finishing moves on the battlefield no matter how badly you want to pummel your opponents.    As for the soundtrack it's the icing on the cake,  in both sound quality and tempo.  Perhaps a few tracks might warrant as skip, but, it's enjoyable nonetheless.    This is a full fledged anime fighter with some playful jabs and fourth wall breaking added in.  Each Story mode scenario is laid out with at least 8 different rivals to face off against.  I started it with Mikoto just to get a feel for her personal motivations, and was pleased with how well they treated her dialogue.   You can choose to continue each fight should you lose.  No sets only single matches allowed in Story.   Auto-save will do the rest, so with each victory or defeat your progress is being recorded for posterity's sake.   Including the 57 achievements, feel free to experiment with as many Overdrive attacks or turn back the tide with Perfect victories or Slip shift escapes. Training Mode is decent, you can Record either player's movements, or combo strings which is standard fare for fighters.  You set the CPU from Very Easy to Hard or set up a Standing non-blocking dummy to go ballistic on.   Another feature Rocket Panda Games took into consideration is allowing players to switch the games BGM from Original or Remixed tracks in Options Menu.    Next, it's time for the negatives -No Character Trials,                                                      No Command Lists                                                      No Spectator Modes                                                      No Replay Galleries exist at the moment.   You might get bored of watching the same attack animations with little to no damage rendered to the sprites.  Fighters get knocked out and that's about it.                                                        No clothing deterioration  or armor piercing attacks, and as I said before no finishers.    The Emergency and Overdrive attacks are staples of Phantom Breaker you pretty much comfortable with them.   The pros will be able to deal or swat off damage with relative ease.                                                            Again, since I have a somewhat limited presence online I cannot truly share how I feel about PBOmnia's matchmaking capabilities.  This was a low point that affected the overall player base with Phantom Breaker Battlegrounds on Xbox 360 and it's Steam port, years ago.  With some achievements sadly being locked away because there are zero people playing the Battlegrounds mode.  :(  Although I'm willing to bet that there will be plenty of streamers and channels in the weeks to come showing off their skills with the world.  With loads of versus matches to watch.   So, there you have it.   Phantom Breaker Omnia is a capable fighter.  One that the fans like me wanted the developers to bring to us.   With a current 10% discount on Steam and consoles good through 03/21/22 as of this review.  Don't miss out.   Get your anime, magical girls, destiny shaping  1v1 fighting fix on.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDRPhantom breaker Omnia is for Fighting game enthusiast, its mechanic depth is treasure trove but its content is bland otherwise.Phantom Breaker Omnia is a 4 Button 2d fighter that have many mechanics similar to traditional fighter, such as standard attack, and special attacks. Their even super with is par for the course in this genreBut Phantom breaker also have things unique to itself, such dash attack which is rarely seen in 2d fighters, a meter called “Tension” that raises players attack power as the fight goes on. That just the tip of the Ice berg, since player also get to choose a style which add further to game variety. The styles will be the main defining mechanic in phantom Breaker, you can think of them like groove system, seen in Capcom vs SNK2.Though their only three styles to choose, combine with 22 character, the amount of combination is impressive. A short rundown of the style is, Quick style has mechanics that allow  unique cancel option to stay on the offense. Hard style gives certain special endurance by granting guard points and parry mechanic. Omnia gets unique advantage of having  more meter and highest damage output but lose alot mechanic complexity.If your looking for fighter that does " Easy to learn but hard to Master" or if you played phantom Breaker Battle grounds, then your in for a good time with this game. But if your looking for game that similar to Nether Realm Studios or Arc System works, then im hard press to recommend phantom breaker Omnia.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like it. Anime fighter, good character designs, Kurisu; decent enough graphics (though levels are empty and boring), pretty good soundtrack, good cast for the story mode.Unfortunately, it's one of the worst experiences I've had with this genre. It's not that it's bad on paper; there are systems on top of systems, somebody worked hard on this. But it's so stiff. I legitimately can't remember a fighting game that feels worse to play than this. Every input, every button press, it feels like the game is actively trying to get you to either cramp up or stop playing. There is no flow to the combat, whether you button mash or you take your time and exploit the available systems, it feels like two rocks throwing one against another. It really is quite terrible.The available content is the usual Arcade, VS, Time Attack etc, with the Story Mode being the center piece. Sadly, it's not particularly good either. It's Kamen Rider Ryuki, with less interesting characters, terrible dramatic beats and really, a story mode that's written for maybe one or two of the available characters, with the others being a traditional fighting game backstory stretched over ten levels interspersed with very questionable dialogue. If you saw the trailer and thought this was Guilty Gear or BlazBlue, it is absolutely not. Lastly, if this matters to you, the localization is abysmal. I don't know how the English audio fares, but if you play with Japanese audio, the deviations in the text are maddening. It's one of those cases where characters have been forced into peculiar speech patterns, added dialogue that's not in the original audio and, of course, silly jokes that fundamentally change the personality of the characters and the tone of a scene and ultimately make every character sound the same. It's not a great story to start with, it's rife with anime stereotypes and the localization makes the already stupid characters come off as straight-up brain-damaged.I've had this game for a while now. My first impression, playing Mikoto (arguably the main character of this series) was mostly positive, so I sat on it for a bit. But every other second of game in this has been anything from disappointing to frustrating. If you find it for a couple of bucks in a bundle or whatever, then sure, pick it up, you might not hate it. Otherwise, there are so, so, so, so many better options out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Nearly 11 years later, Phantom Breaker makes a proper appearance in the west - this time in the form of Omnia, an upgraded, updated, and revamped version of the original 2011 Xbox 360 game.The gameplay is a bit of a mixed bag unfortunately. Right off the bat, I wasn’t the biggest fan of how floaty and slow it felt. Maybe it’s because I am so used to games like Guilty Gear, BlazBlue, and Tekken, but everything here just felt off. Jumping is a bit too stiff, there’s limited mobility while in the air, and a lot of the moves lack that sense of impact. I wouldn’t say the core to the game is terrible, more so just basic - or even bland.What kinda elevates it is the bit of depth introduced through stuff like fighting styles, emergency mode, evades, and the numerous special moves that you can activate by combining a certain input with a regular move. Once I got the hang of this stuff, I was stringing together combos with ease and that felt good - but that again introduces another key point: auto combos.I don’t know if it is just the audience this game is going for, but every fighting style has at least some form of basic auto combo. This is not something you can disable and while some styles have more auto combos than others, all of them reinforce this “streamlined” feeling. This is further reinforced by the fact that each character has the same command list, just different moves resulting from those inputs.This makes the core to game easy to learn - which can be good - but when that core is as slow and floaty as it is, it doesn’t quite feel right. Compare this to BlazBlue: Cross Tag Battle for example. That one also streamlined its controls and was more beginner-friendly, but had the movement, the mechanics, and the speed to make higher levels of play possible.Or maybe I’m completely wrong here and I just have not unlocked the potential behind this one and with time, other players will demonstrate that. But as it stands, this feels more like a casual fighting game to pick up and play at maybe a party and just have fun messing around with friends. That’s not even a bad thing - it’s just something to keep in mind before picking the game up.This game has 20 unique ones and they offer up a good amount of variety. Speedy types, power types, ranged types, technical types - combined with the three different fighting styles and you’ve got quite the selection. I sampled them all and, while there were a few that I just straight-up did not like playing as, most felt fine and I eventually gravitated towards a select few that I really liked.The character designs are also pretty good and the style reminded me a lot of Under Night In-Birth. That said, I was not a fan of the mixed 2D and 3D characters. I have no idea how that came about, but having a 2D character fighting this 2D, yet 3D CG looking thing was really off putting.The backgrounds are fine too, but I can’t say any of them really stuck with me. The music was a bit better, but this is definitely no BlazBlue, so perhaps not something I’ll listen to much outside of the game.Perhaps the biggest problem a lot are going to find with Phantom Breaker is its multiplayer - and for two reasons. One being that this game is releasing right around a couple other notably bigger fighting games - King of Fighters 15 and Persona 4 Arena Ultimax - and will likely lose a lot of audience to those. And 2 being that there is no rollback netcode here.I’m not some rollback elitist, but for a niche fighting game like this launching in a crowded space, the devs are really shooting themselves in the foot with the potential multiplayer reach. I fully expect there to be maybe a few hundred players for the weeks following launch and then this game just completely dropping off the radar and becoming something you’ll need to make arrangements with another player to actually play online.There is at least a decent chunk of singleplayer stuff. A story mode for each character, your classic arcade mode, score attack, time attack, endless battle - yeah they’re all practically the same gameplay-wise, but at least the options are there. If you’re wondering about the quality of the story - sorry to say but don’t expect much there. You get your little visual novel segments in-between fights and it’s the most basic thing ever and barely held my interest.The 1080p lock was unfortunate to see as someone with a 1440p monitor - I ended up having to stretch the game to maximize it. The framerate was solid throughout, but I did run into a few crashes. I think it might be some sort of bug with the main menu because all three happened there and only after idling for a little bit.Phantom Breaker: Omnia is just okay. The fighting has some depth to it, but feels overly simplistic and floaty. There’s a good amount of singleplayer stuff, but no rollback netcode for multiplayer and this is the type of game that is probably going to struggle with maintaining a playerbase on top of that. Unfortunately, I can’t say it’s one I’ll be coming back to.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: Short Review: Can only recommend to people who has played Phantom Breaker: Battle GroundsLong Review: If you're looking for a fighting game with complex inputs and mechanics, this isn't for you. If you're a Battle Grounds veteran like me, the combat is the same with very minor differences which means you'll feel right at home.The story mode has potential but ends up to be disappointing. I've played 4 story modes so far and every one of them had different versions of events which leads to confusion as to which one actually happened or which one is the actual story of the game. They do not converge to make a cohesive plot. This could be improved by having a "Main" story where every story related character participates in, and the endings being branches of that "Main" story. Like what happened in Battle Grounds or like what Blazblue did.The combat is very simplified, which will turn off a lot of target users(Fighting Game players). Every character is more or less the same(because they all have the same inputs) with the only difference being the three modes Quick, Omnia, Hard. This should be improved if ever they're aiming to make another title. The EX Attacks(Enhanced Special Attacks) are too simple and doesn't feel special to be honest. And the Phantom Breaks of some characters were very lackluster. The UI was not friendly and the menu control bindings cannot be changed. To help the player, they should have a move list of the selected character and the selected mode on the pause screen. They might have decided against that because of the simplicity of the combat, but that would help any players new to the series so it should have been added still. Characters: The 2D characters were done well, very fluid and I'd love to see it again. The 3D ones were done horribly. The 3D resolution was bad, there's aliasing all over, there's no light in their eyes and the skin color was just plain wrong. If it was going to turn out to be this horrible mannequin-like appearance for 3d, I wish they just made it all 2d. I'm still going to continue playing this because I loved battle grounds and seeing my favourite character non-chibi style feels very nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Will update review as I go along!Ten years ago, we got screwed out of Phantom Breaker for the Xbox 360.A few years back, we got kicked in the pants for wanting Phantom Breaker: Extra.This game is everything I was hoping for. Its just like I'm playing Phantom Breaker: Battlegrounds! I love it to death already and have been in Training mode for HOURS. Kurisu, Artefactor, Maestra, and Waka are my favorites so far! Shizuka seems a tad busted, but I don't know how to play quite yet.The Tutorial... is a few pages of very basic instructions with very light reading and plenty of screenshots to show you how things work. Its super quick and easy. Remember, this is an old school, and old in general, fighting game. It doesn't have a tutorial like BlazBlue or Guilty Gear. Those don't really have one in my experience anyway! From what I can recall, there's just a training mode with a combo window, and READING what everything does in the game. So, people are flat out lying about that key difference. Haven't played Street Fighter since 2, so no idea there. Not a Mortal Kombat fan either so.Side note on the tutorial, if its not enough, the publisher, Rocket Panda Games, has extra videos on their youtube channel explaining how the game works a bit more.Combos? I couldn't say. They sure don't hand them to you on a platter though. This is an OLD game. There's no guaranteed combo tutorials out there. Like every other fighting game you would play in the arcades of Akihabara, you get to learn how to do them yourself. Frankly, that's great. It keeps you busy and on your feet. See a clip from someone else that did their own combo? I bet you can figure one out too.Character abilities are all very forward and each character has the same button layout. If you've played Phantom Breaker: Battlegrounds, you'll have a very good understanding of how combat works in this game. The controls were copied from Phantom Breaker. -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------As is standard, Anti-Virus, Core Protection, Anti-Malware services, and Steam itself of course... may affect your experience.MalwareBytes may affect your experience, and so will Core Protection/File System Isolation in windows, so you have to allow Phantom Breaker: Omnia through the software by excluding it. If needed, I'll edit this to add how to do that.There are bugs of course. Xbox One Controller -The controls are acting wonky on Xbox controllers for some reason, but that can be fixed by disabling steam input in the games launch settings from what I've read.PS4 Controller -PS4 DualShock 4 controllers can download DS4 Windows to fix this problem, by checking the hide controller option when you setup!Grabbing is weird. Hopefully they make it a button again.----------------------------------------------------------------------------My Complaints thus far.----------------------------------------------------------------------------Assets are mismatched. Meaning the 3D Sprites mixed with the 2D.Mechanics don't work due to online lag at times. Grabbing is a pain.and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ theirs so much RNG its painful. Fin has so many unblockables due to her missles... its really cancerous.Shizuka can literally combo you to infinity with pressure you can't punish. AKA Avoid Akuadynasty online. Haaaa.Random, but very rare crashes are a minor annoyance.There's two or three people in ranked abusing some kinda lag program I guess because when they're on defense the whole match grinds to a halt until they can get a DP off. Then SUDDENLY, everything's back to normal?----------------------------------The review below is inaccurate.----------------------------------

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I was willing to look past the game not launching with rollback netcode because there's only so much the development team can do, rollback can either be implemented in old games, or it can't. I liked the character designs, I liked the fact they were willing to shell out for an english cast. I liked the passion the developers showed pushing the game's development through a pandemic.However, the breaking points for me is that there is very little depth in the characters movesets, and that the game launches at a $40 dollar price tag. I'd be willing to overlook one but not both. Even with three different fight styles for most characters, they feel basically the same to play short for some differences in special moves and supers. Said special and super moves lack a lot of oomph, leaving me saying "that's it?" after testing out the latter of each character. Autocombos and simple gatling combos seem to be the name of the game, and that's not the kind of fighting game I wish to pay full price for.I feel exceptionally bad for refunding this because of the aforementioned passion the small dev team had, and their intention to bring rollback netcode to the sequel if this performs well enough, but at the end of the day, if I'm not satisfied with a product, that's that. I may pick this up again when it's on a heavy discount.I wish the dev team nothing but the best and hope the game does sell well enough that it warrants another game and they can unleash their true potential and vision as developers.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok...I am going to start this review out with the biggest quests: why do you need Phantom Breaker Omnia?But before i answer that, let me just start by saying I am a huge one-on-one fighter. I prefer playing against the CPU though. And I have been playing fighters since the days of Street Fighter II in the arcades. I have played a lot of different ones...good and bad.Since I am not into Battlegrounds, I view this on the fighting mechanics only.Let me first say that I love the roster size. Street Fighter Alpha 3 is one of my favorite games of all time due to the multiple isms, that make a roster become triple size from customizing your character. PBO does this as well with multiple styles for each character that change their stats to be faster or slower, or stronger in defense....and it does change the feel of how the character works. This is such an impressive feature. Unlike, say, Ryu and Ken in the first of the Street Fighter series, you can easily be two of the same character...and have them play very different.  So massive credit here....However, while the battles are frantic and over the to fun in a way...they are super messy and floatey. This can easily become a crazy button presser fighter. Fighting feels sloppy, and the special reversals, cancels and everything feel more random. I get how it works, but lots of times I canceled or retaliated on something, and have no idea how or why it happened. I guess if I really want to dive into the mechanics a bit more, maybe it will feel less sloppy, but that might be more work than it is worth. The health bar is perplexing. It can be empty but the other character is not finished...hmmm...The characters are standard cheesy looking anime characters, and the game...although fairly pretty...looks so empty. Maybe I miss the cheering people in the background of SF games....but the open space feels too...open. Then there is story mode that seems to only have some of the characters. It sure didn't have mine. Granted, I could have played as another character that had the same moveset, but they are still different due to the styles. So I have to stick with arcade...that is super weird, because if the length. You have to clear everyone rather than just a set amount of stages. As good as it sounds to have a long game....it just starts to drag on a little too long.Well..then, back to the big question:  do you need PBO? No..no you don't. If it is on sale, then maybe pick it up...but other than that, pass.So to quote my character: you're not that great.

_childDocuments_.review: Review posted at Back in the day I used to attend several conventions a year, where all forms of gaming, anime and related avenues of fandom would occupy a weekend inside the meeting rooms of an unsuspecting hotel. In those game rooms of my past, I recall seeing Phantom Breaker tournaments and casual play amongst the other 2D fighters. Now over a decade later, Rocket Panda Games has teamed up with MAGES to release an updated and streamlined version of the title for the first time in the West. Does Phantom Breaker: Omnia earn a place in today’s crowded field of fighting games? I think to certain groups of players it very well may have a spot. So, to touch back on that trip down memory lane, I remember often seeing previous iterations of this game around but always with either an imported Xbox 360 or later, with Phantom Breaker: Extra on PS3 which was region free. Omnia is that same game but updated for release on consoles and PC with two new characters and a rebalanced system. Since the game was released originally in 2011, it still looks and plays well, but may seem outdated compared to some of the other 2D fighters being released currently. The most glaring example of this to me was the two new characters introduced, whose designs seems jarring compared to the sprites from the game’s original roster of fighters. Their design feels like something more out of a CAVE shmup, and with MAGES being a developer of shmups and visual novels in the past I can understand this occurrence. But other than the title perhaps showing its age, technically the game is well designed and introduces some features that can benefit newer players and perhaps lend additional strategies to more seasoned fans. The mechanics of the game at first glance seem like a lot to process, three styles with their own benefits and special commands. There is Hard and Quick style, which are returning from previous editions as well as the new Omnia style which is a combination of both to some degree. Quick allows for double jumps, cancels, shift dodges and increased speed. Hard offers heavier combos, protection and additional armor. Omnia lets the player use double jump and a special All-Range attack that uses more of your meter but is unblockable. That may sound complicated at first and for me it was plenty of jargon and UI to decipher but after playing for awhile it really does come together naturally. Knowing which style to utilize for each opponent and knowing what character benefits the most from that style is the key to success and enjoying the matches. Commands are simple to execute with only light, medium, heavy and special attack buttons, and shortcuts for multiple button commands are mapped to the triggers if using a controller or can be mapped easily on a fightstick. Players can also use emergency escapes to get out of being juggled around the stage at the cost of meter, as well as clash when maneuvers are thrown at the same time, deflecting projectiles also. To casual players this all can be executed with just mashing some buttons, and they still feel like they have opportunities to succeed which as a very casual player I appreciated. But I’m sure that novices and skilled players could also benefit from these systems and still find some depth to enjoy. The opening cinematic as well as the soundtrack were just what I would hope for from an anime-inspired fighting game of this caliber, and the voice acting is quite good with a lineup of notable voice actors from anime and video games. Many are very recognizable which I appreciated, taking me back to the convention days of fan meetups while browsing overpriced manga and debating on flavor of Pocky to buy. The option for English as well as Japanese voice tracks was welcomed, however I feel that the extras that can unlocked in the gallery were uninspired and do not give the player much incentive to complete multiple playthroughs.   Twenty characters round out the roster with the previously mentioned two new additions as well as the returning guest characters Kurisu and Rimi who are from other MAGES titles Steins;Gate and Chaos;Head. The fighters all have strengths and weaknesses, relying on close- or long-range attacks and disciplines of technical, rush down, speed, power, standard or tricky. The combos that are possible all depend on stacking their unique abilities with one of the three styles of combat. Story mode is rehashed from other versions of Phantom Breaker, with only unlockable cut scene artwork to be obtained by playing through each character’s story. Arcade mode is also basic, and rankings can be obtained by playing through Endless Battle, Time Attack and Score Attack. I feel that the lack of unlockables and no in-depth training mode really shows the age of the game. At the time of the review, online play was not available. We hope to have a follow-up to this once the game is released and more people are playing on PC. For now, I can say that the CPU on higher difficulties provided for many stressful and demanding matches throughout my playtime and learning most of the characters gave me ample opportunity to prepare for online battles when they are available. For the returning fans of Phantom Breaker, Omnia brings rebalanced gameplay and some UI and character changes that I hope is welcomed by their community. It’s also a great entry point for new players, utilizing a simple control layout and ease of play that can keep the inexperienced in the fight. It does show its age in the landscape of current fighting games with not much to offer for additional content and an art style that may not be what is expected in 2022. But I appreciate the developer putting out a title that welcomes all types of players without sacrificing style and mechanics. That said, I think the game is worth checking out, and thankfully new players can avoid the anime convention to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the beat-em-up because it had some fighting game elements, so naturally I thought I'd like the fighting game but nope. _childDocuments_.review: This game is very underrated but nice to see they remake as by merging PB:Another Code and PB:Extra while rebalancing the casts. If you are the type seeking for the fast Pace 2D fighting then I recommend giving this game a try. The OSTs and Vocal Songs are nice. My most favourite are the OP (Let it all burn - Both JP and EN ver). The game mechanics are a good way to learn fighting games, theres a manual explaining how to block and the combos aren't too difficult, its tricky at start but able to learn quickly. The plot is interesting and very lengthy to be very honest. Ive tried Melty Blood type lumina but the story is far rather short. Gameplay wise still love it. Not forgetting the artstyle is very nostalgic. (Also they do have nice art gallery upon completing several chains of single player modes). *Cough*

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend for a casual gamer. Can recommend for a hardcore fighting game fan but only on sale.This game has some creative ideas for the genre. A cool guard cancel mechanic, a burst/install mode, multiple fighting styles, and other neat stuff. It plays well and has a unique flow. It has a depth and is a competent fighter. This game's strength is that it defines itself mechanically and can cater to a niche in that regard. You will not see this mechanics in other fighters on the market.However, the game does not feel very good to play. Hit effects just don't have much of an impact. The stage backgrounds and animation have been done better by other fighters at similar price points. An awful decision was made for the few new characters in this edition to be 3d models instead of sprites. Character designs are very strong though.In short, the game feels cheap and the sprite based animation is severely outclassed when this game shares a storefront with the likes of other sprite based games like Under Night or Blazblue. Hit effects and doing combos do not feel as satisfying as they should.Oh yeah, online is dead and requires matching via discord. No rollback either.This is of no fault of the developers. This series should continue and I want to see more fighting games with creative mechanics like this game. I recommend this game to the hardcore fighting game fan thirsting for more and nobody else.

_childDocuments_.review: People have a tendency to get more attracted towards hate , destruction & negativity . Its far more easier to disregard something without looking at the hardwork put into place to create it . Sadly such is the case with most of the reviews on Youtube & steam . People just blabber anything that comes to their mind without even properly playing the game for a significant amount of time . Phantom Breaker Omnia is a successor to the previous title Phantom Breaker : Battle Grounds . This new title is completely different from the last game as its a pure 2D Figthing game where as the previous title was a completely different style of game . Although you will find all the charachters from the previous title in this new one as well . They have also added two new heroes as well . There are several game modes such as Story , Arcade , Practice & Online PVP Matches . Since I got the early review key so i could only play Story mode as it was before the release date so there was no chance of getting matchmaking online . I finished lots of story missions & i really enjoyed most of the stories .So basically you can choose any hero you like & start the story mode then you have to fight several fights ( Around 8 fights Mostly ) & after each fight there is a 2D  cutscene with lots of pictures & dialogues . Each has a unqiue story with different fights & cutscenes . So basically the story mode is really worth it because 20 Fighters = 20 Unique stories which is really a big + about this game . I have finished like 8 stories so far & i really enjoyed every single one of them .As for the Online PVP - I have not played it so i wont pass any comments on that .Overall Score - 7/10 ( A Good Game ) Its a good game to have in your library as its Single player story missions are really worth every penny but the price point is a little bit off . So , if you are really short on cash & are not dying to experience it rightaway then just wait till it gets a sale then buy it . _childDocuments_.review: I like it. It has easy to start mechanic but with deep enough system that I'm sure will need some time to digest. It's a fighting game that awards understanding of mix up and timing as well as range to the opponent. Oh, try the arcade mode, it feels never ends, lol. You can go offense crazy, but if you want you can sit back and try to find opening via whiff punish. Shame that seems like nobody is playing online. But I had a blast playing through single player mode. The AI is hard enough that each match feels like an intense guessing game.I wish many more fighting games are made this way. If you're looking for a casual, beginner friendly fighting game that you can play offline with some friends, I can't recommend this enough.

_childDocuments_.review: That game is what anime fans should be keeping their eye out. What got my attention is the world, the characters and the story of everyone having a reason to fight. Gameplay-wise, the game starts off a little hard for those who aren't accustomed to fighting games, but with enough time, effort and experimenting with different characters and the three different fight styles, you can be able to fight through either Arcade Mode, Score Attack or probably online. Though I wish that game needed some recognition for online players, that didn't stop me from getting immersed in the world that kept me coming back for more. Time To Let It All Burn!

_childDocuments_.review: I put off buying this one because I usually don't play fighting games but other reviews have said that the moves are pretty easy to execute and they're right! It's pretty easy to mash through and pull off cool moves but there's a lot of depth in the gameplay and systems from what I've played. I'm glad there's a lot of single player content to be found (since I don't like playing online) and the Story mode features some of my favorite voice actors so I can't wait to play through it all. The addition of the Spicy Edition announcer is a funny addition and is a pretty cool option to have (You can always switch to the original announcer if you want). If you're on the fence and just want a fun fighting game to play the single player content or mash against some friends locally this is a great pick-up especially when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I probably shouldn't give this game a positive review as I'm writing this. I'm sure they're going to fix and add a lot of things, but they definitely won't change everything. Be as it may, I do enjoy the game and once they fix enough issues, I'm sure it's going to become a decent fighting game to play with friends locally (since except for discord communities, there obviously won't be anyone playing online).The negatives are as follows, for the most part:- No move list in training (they also need to add unique moves, not just the special moves, like Yuzuha's jumping down heavy and jumping forward heavy)- Apparently broken controller support (I had 0 issues with my dualshock 4 and xbox one controllers)- Weird frame lag issue (it's rare, but I noticed that sometimes my input gets eaten)The devs can easily fix all of these issues. But what they won't be changing are the poorly aged attack animations and pricing. This game should be a 30 USD or around 25 EUR release at most. The biggest one might be the missing rollback netcode which makes the online scene pretty much dead on arrival in almost any fighting game.Now some of the positives:- The soundtrack kicks ass- Character design and overall presentation- The actual combat is fun once you get used to it- They've put a lot of effort into the dub, but the japanese voices are great as well (which is what I ultimately prefer)- The 3 different styles add a lot of depth- Nice character varietyFighting games are niche to begin with and this game is niche within a niche genre. That's not a bad thing, but you really need to bring out your best when releasing a game like this, unfortunately, it's far from perfect. Nevertheless, it's a really enjoyable game, to me at least, I've spent hours just in training mode, figuring out combos and stuff and I'm going to have tons of fun with my friends playing locally.

_childDocuments_.review:
Phantom Breaker: Omnia, a massive update to Phantom Breaker: Extra, a 1-vs-1 2D anime fighter originally released by Mages in 2013. The game features 2 guest characters, Kurisu Makise from Steins;Gate and Rimi Sakihata from Chaos;Head, as well as two brand new characters created specifically for Phantom Breaker Omnia.

A mysterious man, known only as 'Phantom' appeared in Tokyothe capital city of Japanand manipulated vulnerable adolescents into fighting each other, bestowing upon them mystical weapons of great strength known as 'Fu-mension Artifacts.' In exchange, he promised to grant their wish if they survive.

Unbeknownst to the combatants, the fierce clashes between Fu-mension Artifacts caused distortions in space-time, which compromised the boundaries between parallel universes. The collapse of these parallel universes would ultimately break the seal, unleashing Phantom's destructive powers.

name: Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon
detailed_description: Delve with Shovel Knight into the depths of the Pocket Dungeon in an action-packed puzzle adventure mashup like none other! Join your mysterious guide Puzzle Knight as you shovel through scads of foes, procure new equipment, and battle bosses both familiar and new. Explore a tale with endless twists and turns, quest as your favorite heroes, and even challenge a friend for fast-paced head-to-head competition in Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon! - Enter a world of falling block puzzle games, with a dungeon-crawling twist! Bump into enemies to battle them and trade damage in a unique combat system. An all-new hybrid that’s never been seen before. Group foes together for massive chain attacks while grabbing keys, power-ups, and potions to refill your health! - Take control of more than 10 of your favorite heroes from the Shovel Knight universe, each with a unique power and play style. - Equip yourself on the fly with a treasure trove of items and equipment. Mix and match your loadout to prepare for any encounter. - Play in a variety of ways with Adventure Mode, 2 player competitive Versus Mode, a Daily Challenge, and much more! - A bold new visual style complements a new story. Learn the ropes from your pal Puzzle Knight as you attempt to escape the mysterious Pocket Dungeon. Shovel Knight’s signature storytelling and humor are on full display! Puzzler's Pack Update Soar to new heights in Castle Quandary, equipped with new Refract abilities and Quests for every character! Puzzle Knight is now playable, there are dozens of new foes and finds, and Mr Hat's Fancy Shop has appeared, brimming with transformative headpieces. Paradox Pack Update New characters like The Enchantress and Chester step into the fray, accompanied by new stages Lost City and Explodatorium! Find new secret quests, cheat codes, and unlock over a dozen new relics and items. Unleash your creativity with Mod Support!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's Puyo Puyo meets Wario's Woods. I love it.I was hesitant to pick this up, even as a huge Shovel Knight fan, due to some of the things the negative reviews were saying.After playing for about 3.5 hours now, I'm not really sure where they're coming from. I think it comes down to a matter of taste. This is a puzzle game with modern Roguelike elements. It's random, sometimes it's unfair, but I don't think it's unfair as often as others would lead you to believe (though I don't want to discredit anyone's experience with it); and I think that's because it has a pretty high skill ceiling. It is, once again, a puzzle game first and foremost.Enemies and blocks fall onto the board and persist downward (with few exceptions, some move a bit more for various reasons), and you can move anywhere on the board. It's your job to manipulate these falling pieces into chains. Hitting enemies damages you, so you want to clear as many at once as you can to avoid the board filling up. You heal by hitting potions, so you want to avoid chaining too many of those together; as if all your potions are chained then you get fewer to use in a pinch.Each enemy behaves differently. One may have two hitpoints and only deal one damage (meaning you only take one damage to destroy a chain of them, as death-strikes aren't retaliated against), and one may have three hitpoints and deal two damage (meaning if you have low health, you'll need to go top off between strikes.) Later enemies behave much differently; one that deals more damage in chains (so you're incentivized to attack them independently), one that goes from dealing one damage to dealing three damage if you're low on health, etc..You start with an empty wallet and the bigger the chain the more gems you get for it. You can use these gems in shops you find periodically to buy upgrades for this specific run. Maybe a resistance to electricity, maybe an extra point of damage against solo enemies, things like that. There isn't a huge variety but it's enough to keep things interesting for sure. I'd argue that too much variety would dilute the item pool and make things less fun, but who knows because that isn't the game.There are also treasure chests and keys that show up as well. These drop consumable items that can either be activated magical effects or buffs of some sort that work automatically.The characters also play much differently too, in my opinion. However, I'd like to keep this a short review so I won't go into their mechanics.I did want to revisit the "skill ceiling" comment I made earlier too. Sometimes the game is throwing pieces at you in really bad combinations. It just happens, but more often than not I can see where I made a mistake before I died. Playing too fast, getting yourself stuck, making bad trades. There are also some really interesting ways to create chains that having a physical character on the board presents. You can stop falling blocks (using your body as a piece to prop up a chain), and you can also trigger chains in the air as pieces pass by you. I'm sure there are more clever strategies, these are just two that already stuck out to me in my brief time playing.In short: The game is very interesting with enough variety to be engaging, while being short enough to put you into "just one more round" mode. But it's a puzzle game first and foremost. An arcade style puzzle game. If you don't like that type of game, you probably won't like this. If you like Puyo Puyo, Tetris, or similar puzzle games though then you ought to love this.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy. This is a beautiful game. There's unlockable items, a hidden boss, lots of enemies, and characters that change your play styles. Numerous ways to make the game accessible for you!But is the game fun? I'd say no, the game was just ok. I wasn't really solving puzzles so much dealing with a RNG generator. Ironically the bosses felt slower and more boring than the levels, they are a battle of patience, wait until the potions fall - hit them 3 or 4 times - repeat.Would I revisit this game after some patches or dlc? No, probably not. Unfortunately I think this game has some base design problems and not content or quality problems.

_childDocuments_.review: Shovel Knight as a franchise needs no real introduction: put simply is one of the (if not the best outright) indie platformer by the reckoning of many, mine included, standing tall among the greats of the gaming world, like Mario, Mega Man and Sonic. Now, Take everything that was cool about matching puzzles in the late 80s and throughout the 90s and blend vigorously with all the now well known charm and instant appeal that Shovel Knight has earnedand what you end up with is gaming treat that is new, familiar, challenging and endearing.VINE and YCG partenered up to create a puzzle game that is nothing like any other, yet deeply respects and recognizes its many influences. The graphics are made of large, whimiscially animated and colorful sprites that represent both characters and locations seen in previous titles, while the music is again penned by the wonderful Jake Kauffman, remixing his previous work in an all new style to great effect.The game screen is a "dungeon" (hence the name) and blocks, enemies, chests and other interactable set pieces fall from the ceiling and stack vertically, and as per tradition, letting the screen fill up leads to a game over. It's up to the player to keep this from happening by fighting enemies directly by "bumping" onto them and/or using items and special abilities.The player is free to move around the board up, down, left or right, and by selectively battling enemies and stacking them, one can create combos (something akin to stacking Puyos) that free up space on the dungeon area and drop gems (in game currency) proportional to the size of the chain. Gems are used to buy relics from Chester (as in Shovel of Hope), and unlocked relics can appear randomly both in chests and Chester's shop.There are many playable characters to unlock, both well known as well as some fresh faces, and each has unique special abilities and synergies with the varied items and relics that can deeply alter the state of play and how the player tackles the current challenge.Speaking of challenge, another high point of this game is the amount of difficulty customization that the player is allowed to do: one can alter almost every aspect of gameplay, to the core style (either roguelite - one death and the run is over - or with any number of lives), as well the speed of the falling pieces and many other aspects. The game can be as hard or as easy as one wants it to be.The main mode of play is Adventure, where you visit locations (puzzle screens) each with their own music, visuals, enemies and so on. One can unlock characters and relics in this mode.There is also a versus mode, both vs. AI and vs. another human player to get that puzzle combat excitement going, like Puyo Puyo and Super Puzzle Fighter 2 Turbo had so masterfully done before it, as well as daily runs for those that want to shovel their way towards the top of the leaderboards!With virtually limitless fun to be had, both solo and against a friend, as well as incoming DLC, this is yet another crown jewel in the trove of treasures the passionate folks at YCG have given us; a celebration of puzzle joy that is not to be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: Play this game in roguelike mode (no extra lives) as that seems to be how it was designed. It's a roguelike though, so there is a good deal of randomness but the fun comes from gaining skill with the mechanics and making the right decisions. If you can carve out lone pieces and allow a bunch of the same object to get into a big cluster, popping that huge chain is super satisfying. _childDocuments_.review: I really hate to say it, but it really isn't a good game...Pocket Dungeon tries to combine Match Puzzles with Rogue Likes and sadly fails to understand both in the process.You move your knight on grid over the game board, the dungeon, while its individual pieces, enemies, walls, threasure chests etc. continuosely fally from top to bottom. They do that slowly automatically, like in a puzzle game, and whenever you take a step, like in a rogue like.Thus, it leaves you little room to really think your moves through.Another thing it takes from Roguelikes are character statistic. Attack and HP in this case.Say you have 5 HP and 1 Attack. The enemy has 3 HP and 1 attack.To clear the tile of the board, you need to bonk it 3 times (3 attacks of 1 against 3 HP), but that also means that you take 3 HP of unavoidable damage. This means that you can only remove one such tile (And any same one adjacent to it, called a chain) before you die.Your HP can be restored by bonking into potions that fall onto the board like any other tile.Seasoned puzzle game players might realize the first issues at this point:What if the game decides to not generate potions and instead, boxed you in with enemies? Well...you unavoidably die. It's just that easy really.To win a board, you need to kill enemies, to kill enemies, you need potions. So for the basic gameplay to work, it's completely dependant on its RNG. Your survivability is not always in your hand. The aforementioned chests (and keys) contain consumabl eitems that can greatly help you clearing boards, like weapons with ridiculous attack scores, killing enemies before you get retaliation damage.The catch? You need a key for each chest, and they usually spawn in pairs. And yes, that's too good to be true, as you also need to save these keys to unlock the story McGuffin...I could rant about it for quite a while. Maybe because i'm so darn disappointed about it. But in short: It simply isn't a good game. It tried to combine two genres it simply didn't seem to understand well enough to know what works and what doesn't with each.

_childDocuments_.review: What can i say about this game that people probably already haven't said? Yacht Club Games never disappoints in bringing great fresh and new experiences to the table, and they didn't miss with this one! Their partnership with VINE surely paid out, I'm a huge puzzle game and roguelike/lite fan, two of my most played games are both The Binding of Isaac and Tetris, and this game is an almost perfect mix between the two genres (even though the roguelite aspects are minor compared to the puzzle game aspect of Pocket Dungeon, it sure is there and it DOES make a difference!), this is just one of the most fun i've had playing a game in a while to be completely honest.The hi-res pixel art of this game is nothing short but gorgeous, the animations are fluid, everything is shiny and beautiful, there sure is a lot of visual candy and this is a really important part of puzzle games, it's one of the aspects that help making it addicting (and you can be sure this game IS REALLY ADDICTIVE), the way they translated the designs from the 8-bit styled original game is amazing, it's a weird thing to say, but i'd say the art style of this game is really charismatic by itself, really pretty and comfortable to look at.Ohhh, the soundtrack...Jake Kaufman sure NEVER disappoints with their songs, doesn't matter which game he is working on and his previous work with Yacht Club on Treasure Trove was already one of the most amazing things i've ever heard, and in this game, i'd personally say he outdid himself with these remixes of the originals, there are some remixes that i just flat out like a bit more than their original versions. Even the original songs for this game like the Puzzle Knight fight theme are amazing, the modern approach and vibe of the soundtrack really helps to build that atmosphere of a more modern stylized Shovel Knight spin-off with the techno/dubstep/breakcore approach he took with most of the songs in the OST of this game, the production on these songs are really out of this world!And about the gameplay, which i at least imagine is the most important thing to point out in a game, it's just a pure adrenaline rush. People who complain about it simply just don't get it. It's a MATCH-3 FALLING BLOCK PUZZLE game, mixed with ROGUELITE elements, it's not the same thing as a platformer, there is obviously randomness to it, if you complain about RNG on a mix of two genres that are commonly known for having randomness, i don't know what to say to you. I get it, not everyone will enjoy it, but then it's just simply not made for you. At first when i played this game back when it released, i wasn't really in the mood for playing puzzle games but i still gave it a try. It was really challenging. Then i just forgot about it for a while until some weeks ago when i decided i wanted to play this game again and gave it another try, then i stuck with it and something clicked. The more you play it, the more you get better at it, you learn to deal with the procedural-generated stages, and the more you play and fail, the more you get that feeling of "damn that thing i did was really dumb..." or "aaugh, i could've played that better!" and you feel that you're learning intuitively, since the core of the game itself is really simple, the more time you spend into it, the more engrained the gameplay gets inside your brain and it becomes like second nature. And re-learning to play the game with every new character that you unlock is also really, REALLY fun, certainly one of the most fun parts of the game, every character is so unique, it's like you're playing a completely different game since their way of dealing with the game environment is completely different from the standards the game gives you at the tutorial. And even though their playstyles can seem intimidating, if you just go with it, you WILL learn and you will get a lot of enjoyment out of it, even if you have a personal favorite to play as. The amount of replayability is just so huge with only the different characters aspect of the game, add a COMPLETELY FREE, MASSIVE content update on top of it, brand new unlockables, new characters, just a lot of new stuff to enjoy. My only gripe with the game is a really minor one, which can be completely ans easily fixed by the developers if they so will to do it, that is the roguelite aspects of the game, while they are present and really important to give the game it's uniqueness, i feel that the game could have even more variety in the item pool of the game. You can unlock all the relics from Chester in more or less ten hours of non-stop gameplay. There is basically no item variety in the game, and you will be building the same items every time, which while not exactly something really BAD per se, i wouldn't say it's good too. A part of what make roguelite games fun is the fact that every run is completely distinct and while it is true to some point in this game, it's certainly not because of the items, they are really just there and that's it, you don't even really think about them after you're used to them, there will be some point where you're basically not doing any decision-making about the items themselves because you already know what you want to get every run, which certainly takes away some of that fun of roguelike/roguelite games of doing a lot of wacky, vastly different builds every run. But i can assure that is not a deal-breaker in any sort of way, as the game is still REALLY, REALLY fun, it just could be EVEN MORE fun.While i am FAR of having played the entirety of the game, since i haven't even been able to complete the true ending with any character so far (which while also fun, can be a real challenge), haven't completed any of the Quadriportals from the new update or anything like that, i can assure you that if you are a fan of one of, or both genres mixed into this game, you are certainly going to have a good time with it! Don't let some of the bad reviews disencourage you from this absolute masterpiece of a game, for me it's a real underrated gem, both as a fan of puzzle and roguelites and as a fan of Shovel Knight as a whole. GO PLAY IT!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and fluid, not hugely varied but the base gameplay is enjoyable enough to keep the game decently replayable.The game gives players the option to play it either as a rogue-lite or a linear adventure. Regardless of whether players are restarting each time they get knocked out, or restarting each time they choose a new character, the randomized elements of the game make it feel somewhat unique each time. Besides the levels being randomly generated there's also items, hidden rooms and varying boss encounters. Although the game fits really well as a rogue-lite, it doesn't necessarily have enough diversity to make it a fully fledged rogue-lite; but the option to play that way is still nice.The puzzle mechanics are all fairly simple but still leave room for a decent amount of learning and strategy. It manages to keep a solid degree of difficulty to the experience, which contributes to the rogue-lite mode. There also are a lot of unlockable characters to encourage multiple playthroughs, but the limited amount of overarching variety combined with the difficulty makes the game fairly repetitious when playing on the rogue-lite mode. There aren't separate achievements for completing the game in each campaign mode, and I'm assuming players unlock achievements regardless of which mode they play in, so players that choose the rogue-lite mode also have to struggle more just to get the same achievements unlocked by just playing with infinite respawns; via the linear adventure mode.The graphics have a really nice and consistent style to them, they definitely feel very thoroughly crafted. The way the game directly references much of the establish world in the original Shovel Knight is certainly neat and somewhat nostalgic. From the beginning the game also presents a satisfactory basis for the story, along with an overarching mystery to help encourage players to push on. Although the progression of the story feels pretty rushed towards the end. It's also unfortunate that each character doesn't get unique dialogue as they progress, they just remain silent and let others do all the talking.There's nothing particularly fascinating about the game as a whole; the mechanics are simple, the randomized elements are noticeable but not especially thorough, and it all takes place in the same semi amusing semi dramatic cartoon world as from before. It's cute and reasonably entertaining, but doesn't necessarily leave a huge impression.If you're interested in finding more games like this I've probably reviewed quite a few on my curator page .

The player is tasked with clearing baddies as shovel knight (or any of the other 10 or so other knights once unlocked) in combos to get a door to appear and make a hasty exit. The game it'self is good and also carries a rouglite element with runs that end by being killed sending you back to the start, but this can be avoided with a infinite continue method provided by the game before starting your first run(which I'm not using because I don't stink at games and it kinda kills the point of improving). _childDocuments_.review: The game looks beautiful and pretty much what you would expect from a puzzle version of Shovel Knight.  The problem is with the game mechanics.  The pieces either move after a few seconds or every time you move.  This requires quick thinking to properly deal with the puzzle elements and ALSO not die to attacking the wrong enemy at the wrong time.  The timer+movement on your movement is already somewhat imbalanced against you, but the real issue comes from the relics/items you can unlock and find within puzzles as well.  Since time is so much of the essence, whenever you get an item you probably won't know what it does, how it works and how best to use it upon getting it.  The timer requirement combined with equippable items from mid-puzzle is just too chaotic of a combination.  Ultimately, the game just ended up being more frustrating than fun, despite the tease of unlockables, especially for $20.  If the game were $15 or $10 I'd be more willing to overlook this but as it stands, $20 for annoyance is too steep.

_childDocuments_.review: Fair warining : it's a small game that can give you the impression that you have seen everyting in two hours, thus, the price might be a bit steep in that regard.That said, it's a very good game. There are a lot of nuances in each levels that can alter your experience and the randomness of the tiles spawn makes every run feels different.There are a lot of different characters in the game, and each one as a special passive or active power-up that can drastically change your way of playing the game.The pleasure for the long-term players will be improving score and time of runs as well as practicing the play by being more precise and optimized.It's kinda unique and I can understand that some people have been destabilized by the mechanics, but I can tell that there has been a lot of thought into it. _childDocuments_.review: Very unique puzzle game I can only describe as a crossover between Puyo and Dig Dug, wrapped up in a hub-based roguelike.Your character is physically present on the board, needing to navigate falling blocks that are mostly enemy units with unique characteristics. To destroy enemies, you must sacrifice your own HP to deplete theirs -- ideally in chains, which will damage all matching units at once. This requires you to tactically recover your HP by seeking out potions that are also falling alongside foes, regular blocks, and other elements. The goal in every level (except boss encounters) is to keep clearing the board and survive until the exit gate spawns, which takes a few minutes at most.And that's just the basic gist; you also gain unique abilities based on your character choice and the equipment you pick up. You'll also face different challenges depending on modifiers, the challenge portals you find, and the bosses you confront on your run. There's plenty of choices to discover and unlock as you keep playing.Suffice to say there's a learning curve, but keep with it and you'll be clearing boards like a pro in a few hours. Worth mentioning is a large suite of difficulty options to help cushion your runs and let you focus on learning; some will disable achievements, but most don't. I'd personally recommend giving yourself 5 stocks and slowing the idle speed down slightly to ease in, while still getting a decent challenge.I found Pocket Dungeon to be a tightly-designed, action-packed, and rewarding puzzle game. I saw a few reviews complaining that the difficulty is cheap and unfair, but frankly I don't think these players wholly understood the gameplay and settings options. Fully recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: The mechanics are a little hard to pick up due to the nature and pacing of the game. The tutorial does a good job explaining the concepts, but with an ever-shifting board, it's a lot to take in all at once. After a few rounds, everything clicked and I finally had a good grasp of the fundamentals and this game became very hard to put down.The art style has a lot of charm and personality. It has that nostalgic, handheld feel, yet modernized with detail, definition and bursts of color. I love the rogue-like elements of picking up relics and items to build on as you progress. They make each run feel different and you can adapt your play style around what you find. Each character offers another level of strategy, as each knight has their own strengths and vulnerabilities. The bosses are also very engaging and different from the regular rounds, and from each other. Once a run is over, I can't help myself from immediately starting another one.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this should be everything but a roguelike. The RNG is really a make or break in this game, as it can just sometimes screw you over no matter how strategic you are. A lot of this game is just pray for potions, because your HP is also working against you if you want to clear out a chain of enemies. Taking damage is simply unavoidable in all interactions, and it can really screw you over if you play characters that have reduced max HP (why are there 2 damage enemies in the first level?).The timer works much akin to NecroDancer, though you take damage if an enemy moves to the spot you move on in that game. The game pushes you to consider your options carefully but at the same time works you against a fast timer. This timer also leads to some questionable deaths when the board is near-full. Sometimes the game gives you some time to give you breathing room, sometimes it doesn't. There is no indication of a time anywhere on the board as far as I can tell. There is a gem meter counter which serves as a combo timer, but that's it. Sometimes there are enemies that force you to wait on the timer in order to hit them/move to the next tile (slimes, ghosts, etc.)This game has fantastic visuals, characters, secrets, and all of that. It just doesn't mix puzzle elements and rogue elements well. When a run begins to chain into a good run, it's fun, but you need to get really lucky on that no matter your skill. A lot of enemies need you to wait for a potion after you hit them so you can hit them again. Don't have a potion? Sorry, you're boxed in by every enemy and you can't do anything about it but die and fill up the board (goldarmors can do this to you without killing you but it's essentially a softlock as you can do nothing but watch the board fill up). A lot of the times you can't be assed to make a thoughtful decision because you're working against an unforgiving timer. And soon you work yourself to a spot where there are no good decisions at all, then you have to pray for a potion or the exit door if you have a key. The item variety is also very sparse, I buy items in the shop frequently yet I hardly see them in runs, items from chests hardly matter since you lose them if you die (and you will die frequently).

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game was made with nothing but good intentions, but it really struggles to juggle mechanics in a way that works for the format. I don't think there's anything wrong with combining a matching game with combat and Grindstone really managed that type of gameplay super well when I played it, however, I don't think this game approaches both worlds all too well. It simultaneously wants you to pensively gauge your choices to ensure that you are both clearing objects and participating in combat, while also acting quickly to avoid being overwhelmed by falling blocks that stack in a tetris-style. I don't think these two ideas are necessarily mutually exclusive, however, this game's approach feels unwieldy on those fronts. I think one of the most notable problems is trying to quickly assess how enemies function and deal damage while also trying to maintain an awareness of time and pace. The UI doesn't really make their behavior all too clear and struggles to convey information in a way that benefits the quick-thinking needed to be successful at the game. I often lost track of how much damage enemies deal or felt confused by the way damage is dealt because there's just too much going on without enough visual (or other) feedback to help prioritize which tasks should be accomplished.All-in-all this is a lesson that stacking mechanics can be interesting, but it requires a more thoughtful approach to the way information and mechanics engage and communicate with the player.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure who this game is really for. There aren't really builds or notable run variety, so roguelites fans won't be satisfied. Paradoxically, though, the game moves too fast to allow for any depth of strategy, so I don't think puzzle fans will be satisfied, either.SK: Pocket Dungeon does make a great first impression thanks to fantastic audio/visual design, but it quickly becomes apparent that the actual game design (or lack thereof) underneath is a total mess. There ARE games out there that combine puzzle and real-time action elements to great success (an excellent example is Frogue), but SK: Pocket Dungeon is not one of them. There are some neat ideas in this game, but they don't cohere or mesh whatsoever. $20 opens the door to a lot of excellent games in the indie space - skip this one and buy another instead.

_childDocuments_.review: A remarkably failed idea for a game that, instead of the developers dropping or throwing back to the drawing board, they just hammered away at it and kept adding extra lives until it finally became playable and then they're like, voila, here's our game! It's like a skyrise built on a foundation of haphazardly nailed together 2x4s. The fundamental puzzle game just doesn't work from a gameplay philosophy standpoint, it is far too random, too ignorant of skill or strategy, too much just "I hope something comes along to save me because otherwise I'm just dead." 80% of the time you're going to die very quickly and that's it, sorry! To make the game playable, you have to start giving yourself extra lives, which the game throws at you as a recommended option before even sending you out on your first mission, as if to say, hey, we designed this game to be played like this, but it doesn't actually work, so just turn on these cheats before you even start, OK? In addition to the gameplay just not being particularly playable without lots of cheats and bonuses, the content they've created for this game just isn't interesting. New characters are unlocked and somehow each new ability sounds even less fun than the previous one. Any opportunity to even play the puzzle game at its base level is immediately dodged and averted by increasingly bizarre hero powers because THE UNDERLYING GAME IS FUNDEMENTALLY UNPLAYABLE OTHERWISE. It's like if Tetris never actually let you play Tetris but instead constantly threw crazy bonuses and wild stuff and extra lives at you because somehow these Tetris designers managed to design pieces that almost never fit together into complete lines.OK I'm done.

_childDocuments_.review: A classic puzzle game that feels like a classic puzzle game. Everything is simple to understand, but the layers of simple kinks makes for an engaging puzzle that stands tall against the greats.The game is set up like a modern game: roguelike fashion, items and characters all like you've seen in Hades or Slay the Spire. Yet, the game never feels like a modern game. Part of that is the 16 bit era graphics and chiptunes, for sure. But it's not just the look and sound; the game PLAYS like an 8/16 bit game. Grid-based gameplay, minimal button requirements, and level-based progression were the hallmarks of Tetris and Dr Mario, and this sits in perfect harmony with those restrictions. Characters are fun and varied, without being overly complex. One character applies 1 poison damage, one character finds more healing potions, one character dashes at the cost of health, one character has a shield. Simple changes that make you think about the way you play the grid. Items gained while playing are also simple, and well explained. Freeze hammer freezes. Pike attacks 2 squares. Relics are just as simple: extra health, better healing, etc. Apart from characters, everything adds only a tiny amount of extra things to think about.That's good, because the puzzle is where you want your attention. And it will demand your attention for sure. Just like the classics, stuff falls from the ceiling and you can't wait forever to make a decision. Your decisions make things move FASTER too, and you have to know what your enemies will to to retaliate. Some poison, some attack back, some explode, some block, etc. Challenges are a fantastic addition to the game as well, as they feel like integrated "home rules" you'd otherwise have to limit yourself to. Longer battles, tougher enemies, shorter reaction times, barriers, there's tons of ways to make the game harder. Similarly, the amount of customization to the base game is astounding. You can add more lives, slow time, give yourself a "buffer" before death, turn items and relics off, even change the loss conditions. Every little frustration you could possibly have has been considered, and you've been given the reins to create the experience that fits you best.None of this stuff feels out of place for the era of gaming the developers are inspired by. While the roguelite is popular today, it's easy to forget you're even playing a roguelite, or that you're even playing a modern game. There's stuff here that couldn't have been done back then, like online leaderboards, mods, and the sheer amount of content, but it never gets in the way. Incredible value for money.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit skeptical going into Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon, despite loving Shovel of Hope, Plague of Shadows, Specter of Torment and King of Cards, I didn’t really know how I’d feel about this title. Could the devs of this game really translate the charm of Shovel Knight into an entirely different genre? Could they create fun gameplay that wouldn’t be too alienating to the fans of previous Shovel Knight titles? I think by looking at this review you can see that at least in my opinion, they succeeded. This game expertly translates Shovel Knight’s cast and the gimmicks associated with them into this roguelite action and puzzle game, the essence of every character is really intact. Pocket Dungeon uses the iconography of Shovel Knight incredibly well and I found myself really getting sucked back into the world of the Shovel Knight games. The gameplay is incredible! It really forces you to think quickly and apply your game knowledge to solve the levels as quickly as possible. In conclusion, I think Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon is a great little game that is a must have for Shovel Knight fans but a game I can also recommend to people who generally like puzzle games. _childDocuments_.review: Shovel Knight + Puzzle game! How can this not be a winning combination? The simple answer is, it can't! The mechanics of the game are straight forward, having to balance hits, health and potions to ensure that you can maintain the clearing of chains to get access to keys and chests.Along the way you will be presented with a variety of weapons and characters (from the Shovel Knight game) that you can play with, each with different attacks based on their default weapon choice.  The puzzle play makes you have to consider how you attack certain enemies and what might be left in their place which can have further challenges for you (fire and poison).In addition to the standard puzzle adventure affair you can also do a PvP game, great if you want to argue with a friend, not great if you want to remain friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: Insane amount of content for what is a pretty simple concept. There's 15 playable characters that each have a different ability and play style, on top of that there's a bonus game mode where it imagines the character with new abilities so there's more like 30 characters. Now imagine that amount of content but also for bosses, enemies, quests, and more.Only real complaints are that other than the mini bosses, they are all very cheeseable even though they're all pretty unique. Also even though there's a good bit of replayability, I'm not a fan of having to beat the game with each character, plus the 4 bonus campaigns to 100%, but if you don't care a lot about that like me then this games pretty great!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and unique puzzler that takes a bit of time to get acclimated. Nice to see Shovel Knight and the gang back at it in such a unique rogue lite puzzler. Every move is important and there is a ton of customization in how difficult you can make this game. Even when made accessible, the game brings a tough challenge that makes you say: "One more time"
_childDocuments_.name: Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: I used to think that this game was fun, but pretty content dry, so I couldn't exactly recommend it to anyone. But now that this game has gotten some free updates with more characters, items, and relics, I can confidently recommend it for people to play.This game has mod support now so it'll be infinitely replayable once some mods get rolling, but that can be said for most games that get steam workshop so I want to focus on the added base game content, because I think this is the best part of the game. The added characters, side rooms, relics, and items are so much more unique and interesting than the ones introduced in the base game that gives this game so much more replayability to runs that it really needed. From fun minigames and minibosses you can randomly encounter within levels, to relics that completely change how you approach the game, to hats that let you customize the game as much as you want, it's hard to get bored.There's just so, so much to talk about that I haven't even gotten the chance to dig into yet, so if you've seen gameplay and think it looks fun, this game will not disappoint.
