_childDocuments_.review: Post-PARADOX-Patch Review: What the hell happened to my game??? when I bought "Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon" a few years back I thought it was a fun, creative, bouncy game with some cool ideas and some really great music.when I re-installed "Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon" the other day I thought it was a loud, aggressive, ADHD-inspired freak-out with some cool ideas and really obnoxious music. the great Hub Music now apparently has this sub-destroying Skrillex music going on ... not REPLACED but RIGHT OVER-TOP. and in a different tempo. I thought I was hallucinating or something at first. seems the new remix intro music doesn't STOP once I enter the Hub. not a creative choice, surely, but kind of a good symbol for how I feel this game's changed. it's just ... noisier. less focused, more confusing. it doesn't have the same vibe. it lacks the "innocence" that it had at first. it doesn't feel like a lost relic from maybe the late-16-bit age but a gnarly dance club with 20-dollar beer. I dunno. rubs me exactly the wrong way, and not because I hate it on its face but because I kind of hate what it represents. why change a great feel? why risk the game's memory like that? this game had replay value through the ROOF. it's a puzzle game. we don't need constantly updates. or I don't, anyway. really don't like it, but it's still the same fun gameplay, only now all re-arranged. I don't know why we feel we need to constantly update good games into BETTER-ER GAMES. games acting like Balancing As Loud Live Service (B.A.L.L.S. for short) just doesn't work for me. I'm from an age of when you owned a game, that game was yours. if you wanted to change it you could, but that core experience was there on CD. so you had to release a good game, full-stop. anyway. where's my walker at, I'm tired and need my meds. clouds piss me off, man.can I rollback to a different, pre-Paradox version? please?? how about the OPTION to launch as the original version??? eh. I see a cloud I have to chase and scorn. peace.ORIGINAL REVIEW:    for 10 bucks on sale you can do so much worse it's kind of mad. MAN do I suck at it, though. like. . . . MAN.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m just under 7 hours in in the last week of ownership. This one is great. Big fan of rogues (likes or lites!) and have played all the “ones”! This one can scratch a puzzle-y rogue itch or be played a little less like a rogue with the helpful pregame settings. Choose amount of lives, randomizing levels, etc. This is a nice feature allowing for the game to be played how the gamer wants and at what difficulty. As for me, I’m a masochist! I play this game with one life and random levels. It’s a very hard game, but so fun with nice unlocks for that extra dopamine rush! It’s nice to see that Yacht has updated it since release (I had been watching) and that they have plans to continue to. I’d say this game is worth the cost of admission at $20, especially considering the company’s track record, but if you see it at any less, FOR SURE GO FOR IT!

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the game, I can say with confidence that Shovel Knight: Pocket Dungeon is a fantastic little game that will have you coming back for hours on end. _childDocuments_.review: First off, it's Shovel Knight. So of course it's good. Taking the iconic blue digger and putting him into his own puzzle game made me sceptical at first. But after playing through the campaign a few times, i am pleasantly impressed with how well thought out and polished the entire game felt.To describe the gameplay with the simplest terms, its like Candy Crush where everything falls into a pre-determined grid and you have to reach the end to progress to the next level. But unlike Candy Crush this game is actually good lol.Visuals and characters are also spot on with how each of them compliments each other perfectly giving the game a wonderfully upbeat charm. Speaking of characters, every major character you meet along your journey are also playable once you beat them in a duel. Every character sports there own unique quirks that gears you to play them with different strategies than you would be using when playing another. This adds so much to the replayibility and mastery of each character can take a long while but still feel really rewarding.Everything is all so simple but its how all those aspects mesh together that make Pocket Dungeon a fun time killer and a worthy entry into the Shovel Knight spin-off series. 8.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay wise, it has little to do with Shovel Knight. However, aesthetically it captures the fun and spirit of the franchise. As for the game itself, it can be brutally devastating if you are not paying complete attention. This can be very engaging, but also frustrating if you make a slip after 20 minutes of playing. Fortunately, beating the rogue is only around 30 minutes, so it is not a complete time waster if you need to start over. Great visuals, challenging puzzles, and fun boss fights.

_childDocuments_.review: Description:-Shovel Knight Pocket Dungeon is a puzzler spinoff from the hard working devs at Yacht Club Games.  I grew up playing Tetris Attack for SNES and this is the closest thing that I've played since.  SKPD is another charming, well designed, and challenging game that every fan of both Shovel Knight Treasure Trove and puzzler games need to play.What's Good:-The gang at Yacht Club have struck gold once again.  I really love how even in a genre that is so different from what we would expect from Shovel Knight, this game seems like a perfect spinoff.  All of the playable character and villains behave in a similar manner as they would from the original SK game.  Shovel Knight is the most balanced and gets extra access to potions, Spectre Knight heals when he kills an enemy, and Plague Knight poisons enemies.  -The devs opted for a 16 bit aesthetic that feels closer to a SNES visual presentation.  There is charm and love thrown into every aspect of this game.  The HUB starting area really comes to life as you unlock more relics, shortcuts, and playable characters.  I really love the visual presentation of this game.-Although this game is adorable to look at, it's more challenging than you would expect.  I played Tetris Attack for hundreds of hrs, so I figured that this would be a breeze.  Boy, was I wrong.  I got my butt kicked for the first few dozen or so runs before making some progress.  This is a simple game to understand mechanically but offers quite the skill ceiling.-As you would expect from any Yacht Clubs game; this has a killer soundtrack!  I love the sound design and I'm tempted to say that it's even better than the Shovel Knight Treasure Trove soundtrack.  -They have already announced a bunch of DLC packs and updates.  This is great news and should add endless content to the base game.  They have announced more unlockable characters, relics, and more online matchmaking features.Could Use Some Changes:-If you don't care about unlocking all of the characters and completing all of the achievements, than the base game is pretty short.  Most players will have a winning run within the first 3-6 hrs.  You will probably unlock every relic within the first few hrs which is also a huge bummer.  I am less than 4 hrs in, and I've unlocked every relic and unlocked every shortcut which means that there are very few things for me to purchase w/ my gems.-You are rewarded for going fast, but this can lead towards tons of mistakes early on.  As simple as this game is mechanically, it may feel a bit intimidating to those less familiar w/ this genre.  There are a lot of moving parts on screen which can distract from the experience.  My goal for new players is to take your time and not worry about speed.-If you don't like puzzler games or match 3, then you probably won't enjoy this game.  Even if you are a diehard Shovel Knight fan, you may feel that this game isn't for you.  This is just a guess, but I think it probably holds up.Consensus:-Solid Game (Tier 3 and makes up 35% of my reviews).  I've had a really good time w/ SKPD so far.  I plan to play for at least another 8-12 hrs over the next few weeks.  My expectations were slightly too high going in, but as a whole, I've been really pleased w/ my gaming experience.  I won't end up playing this game as much as I played Tetris Attack, but that game was lightning in a bottle for me.  I don't think it's fair to expect to devote hundreds of hrs to this game in the way that I did for a nostalgic game that I played as a kid.  If you love the Shovel Knight franchise or puzzler games, then you owe it to yourself to give this a try.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very addictive puzzle game once you understand the game mechanics enough. the blocks and mobs start falling from the top row, each time you take an action it also advances the game time (basically times move when you move/take action, being idle for a while will also advance the game time). you can clear units by attacking the blocks/mobs most mobs will also attack back, 3 or more adjacent units of the same type and same hpcan be cleared at once.you your goal is to find the portal to exit before the 8x8 playable area is completely filled, once filled, game it is game over. there are many (12?) playable characters with unique skills each, most of them with very different playstyle, there are also items and weapons you can acquire to powerup your character.There are rougelike mode with customizable amount of life or you can basically play the mode with unlimited life.basically Bejewel with some twists but it makes it unique and interesting enough. Unlike some short reviews said, it is a actually puzzle game a quite challenging one if you want to be good at it.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, it isn't the best puzzle spin-off out there - but the quality and charm keep me coming back for more. Definitely makes it much more enjoyable than most other spin-offs! Settings for Adventure mode and VS mode are also pretty modular to suit your play style mood (Turn off the time-movement of tiles, and have more turn-based tactics. Or ramp up the speed to max, and give yourself infinite lives to see how long you can last against the nonstop torrent!)Some characters like Mole Knight or Propeller Knight can even make the game easier if you're having a tough time too!

_childDocuments_.review: while not your traditional shovel knight game this offers a fast paced strategical puzzle game that boggles my mind how something so simple yet fun can exist. the characters work, the music is grand and the experience is worth whatever you paid. and offers endless replay ability as you achievement hunt and challenge yourself with your own crazy rules. get this game it is fun! -Spaghet

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzle games and Roguelikes not named Dead Cells are not usually my cup of tea, but this game completely took me by surprise. SKPD is one of those "easy to learn, difficult to master" games which reminds me of how the original series felt to play for the first time. Even as I died repeatedly there is an addictive quality that kept me coming back after each death, and the amazing soundtrack draws the player into the world. There are a wealth of options to either slow the pace of the game or give additional lives to the player character which do help blunt the initially intense difficulty curve which are appreciated. My only complaint is that there is relatively little to do with the in game currency that accumulates between rounds after all the relics and skins for characters have been purchased. This is not a deal breaker, more so a curiosity as to what could be implemented in the future to make use of the funds. Maybe using it to increase the drop rate of certain relics or to lower the drop rate of others? Anyways, this game is a blast. Check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: just completed a game with one character 6hrs in and it's clear to me there's more to this puzzle game than meets the eye.The basic are simple to grasp, fight to pop chains of like foes and create space to survive. Much like the original Shovel Knight the depth comes with how differently the heroes play, how you build out your relic choices over a run and how the enemies mesh or clash with those systems and choices. The vibrant art and driving soundtrack have made it easy to lose a few hours within. There's plenty to unlock and much to discover for what initially comes across as well polished mobile game, with great flexibility in difficulty by way of slowing down to real time pace, giving you a few extra lives or damage stats a run or even removing the bosses or item and relic systems.

_childDocuments_.review: Arrog is the tale of a man coming to terms with his own death. It’s the story of a life ending rather than one beginning. It’s a simple one, with little dialogue to express what the characters feel, phrases such as  (if they can even be considered phrases) being all you’ll get. This is a game that tells its story through art and sound, not word and sentence.It does a great job at it too, with striking visuals that marry simplistic drawings with a binary-color art style. One scene is almost oppressive, featuring terrifying lightning strikes and wistful rain, whereas another is calm and dreamy, perfectly manifesting the emotions our protagonist goes through on his journey to the afterlife. The music is soothing and calm, sometimes even sad, as if it’s conveying the confusion and longing the man experiences during his last venture. It’s an experience driven by pathos, one that relies on the player’s ability to empathize with the poor man. And in my case, the game succeeded in investing me emotionally in this story about an individual I know so little about. I don’t know who this man was in life, what drove him and what he feared. All I know is that he’s dying, and here I was, helping him on his journey. I think there’s something powerful about that. When it comes to gameplay, Arrog doesn’t do anything particularly innovative, but that’s fine. This is a  type of game. The simple and often easy puzzles were good enough to keep my attention, but they’re nothing but a nice addition that adds a bit of interactivity to the experience. Typically, you’ll have to arrange symbols in accordance with one another or manipulate objects. You’re also often required to interact with the scenes to progress, involving a mouse cursor and a few clicks. It’s eminently simple, but it works well enough to keep you engaged. The experience lasts roughly half an hour, so finishing it in one sitting will be an easy endeavor. It’s not to the game’s detriment, though, since it was never large in scope to begin with and is also very cheap. If you’re looking for an emotional and bittersweet experience, I can recommend Arrog, and I can’t wait to see what the developers do next.

_childDocuments_.review: I first learned about Arrog while watching the IGF Awards Ceremony. As I watched this game win the Audience Award, I was astutely confused. Not because I had any bad preconceived notions about this game, but because I straight up had . Didn't see it on Steam's frontpage, didn't hear any youtubers or streamers mentioning it, nothing. Once I finally played it, I realized why I hadn't heard anything about it.• Game length is very short at 30-40 minutes long• Gameplay includes simplistic but fun puzzles• Art is all done in absolutely stunning hand-drawn black and white animation• Sound design includes calming scores with windchimes and bells, and the soothing sounds of whooshing wind and crackling fireThese are all things that are great in their own right but, what makes Arrog such a special experience is how it interlaces all of its aspects into a game that really effects you: the vague but expressive story about letting go, the way the puzzles come up seamlessly between cutscenes and moments of contemplation, the relaxing soundscape that envelops you. The thing that made me so impressed with this game is how it took all of those elements and brought them together to actually have a tangible effect on my demeanor. I played Arrog on stream after losing a few games Valorant. I went in stressed, worked up, and a little annoyed. I came out with a completely different vibe. I was extremely relaxed. My shoulders were down, I wasn't holding tension in my body, my voice was lowered. I felt unshakably calm. Even going into a different game, that calm demeanor persisted for a good while. It's hard for me to convey the totality of the experience through words, so all I'm left to give is a recommendation for you to try it The best way for me to describe Arrog, is as "Meditation in a Can", it takes serene vibes, cans them, and ships them straight to your door to be cracked open by your brain. It pulls your attention for 30 minutes and once you're done you feel more grounded to the earth. It really is an experience.//////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////I would recommend Arrog to any stressed souls or busy minds out there, you might be surprised at what it can do for you

_childDocuments_.name: Arrog

_childDocuments_.review: Arrog is a game with 2D black and white graphics and a soothing accompanying soundtrack. There are parts with click-through story while others are puzzle-solving. I'm not sure if I understood the entire story, but it made sense to me in bits and pieces, about life coming a full circle, and where death isn't merely an occasion for sorrow. I agree that the playtime is very short but I won't let that take the good away from this game. Graphics were what I loved the most, very ingenious given that it's a 2D black & white game. It's fun to figure out how to interact with the environment in every part of the game. There aren't in-game hints but it's intuitive and the puzzles are easy to solve. Also, full points to the soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Arrog

_childDocuments_.review: Arrog is a wonderful, little game which tells a story of life, death and rebirth through visually charming puzzles and a curious, wistful aesthetic. The scenes are expressive and simple but compels you with emotions. It's a Ghibli-esque story about misfortune, the cycle of life and death, and both celebrating and mourning for it. Highly recommended if you have the time, and it's at a great price too!

_childDocuments_.review: After the open beta, I saw a lot of reviews: "worms messed up; bring turn-based play back; it was better before; no one will play this." I am 25 years old. I've shot worms on the PS1, played golf on an old phone, destroyed forts on my computer. I've been a fan of the series since its early days, and have played almost all worm games. My favorite part is "Worms 4 mayhem" (yes, it's 3D, not classic 2D). How many "step by step" worms have been released? You can always play Armageddon, World Party or W.M.D. Rumble was made for fans like me. The life of the franchise is important to us, not repeating the same thing in order to get money.

_childDocuments_.review: Worms Rumble is an example of how to NOT do a online service. I respect Team 17 and their developers but its very apparent that this is their first attempt for a fully online experience.This game is fun and I really enjoy it when I get around to playing it but my god is the waiting times a chore. If i'm not waiting 5-10 minutes if i'm lucky with 1/6th of the lobby filled, I'm waiting for the game to boot me out of searching for that match to reset the process. The games bugs make the game almost unfun to play half the time. Any projectile based weapon like a bazooka or a plasma gun just clip through the map and do no damage. The shield will sometimes lose its collision box and just become a useless piece of junk and a mark on your back. The fact these bugs have been going on since launch its obvious they're never going to get around to fixing them due to their only interest being cosmetic fluff.The game was basically dead on arrival only ever able to scrape 600 players at launch and the only reason why the game isn't dead is because of Playstation Plus. And, with no interest as it seems to adding more platforms for the game to exist on I doubt the issue of dying will ever be fixed before its too late.Their roadmap is shocking and depressing its almost like they know their game is doomed to fall and they're trying to cover it up. Don't just say more information coming soon and only showing the next month this might be aggressive but your game is dying and it only feels like you're trying to squeeze out every penny you can before it sinks.Overall, Worms Rumble is a sinking ship thats only repairs are with sticky tape and twigs. Take my 100 hours as advice to never buy this game unless they seriously add more then 4 arenas, 5 gamemodes and 24/7 online play which barely functions.P.S: If anyone is interested in knowing what i'd fix in this game I have a link here: Edit: (27/2/2020) This will probably be the last time I address this game but I just wanted to list every bug that isn't fixed to this day and when I noticed them.-Sometimes breakables won't break and you'll clip through them (Launch)-Projectiles clipping through walls (Random, January)-Shield sometimes not working doing no damage and not protecting you (Just swap weapons quickly, January)-Unopenable chests (January)-Being kicked out of queue (Random, January)-Holding swap weapons will sometimes not even give you your item (Recent patch)

_childDocuments_.review: Decent variety of weaponsGameplay feels fluid and fun for the most partDLC packs add more purely cosmetic customisation optionsCrossplatform parties/lobbiesThe real-time style is a stark departure from the typical turn-based fare of the seriesAlarmingly low playerbaseImbalanced matchmaking (likely caused by the above)Don't expect to have good ping unless you're based in EULarge, but few mapsOnline multiplayer onlyWas the writing already on the wall at the time of the announcement? Hard to tell. , announced for the series' 25th anniversary, eschews with the turn-based nature of its predecessors and shifts to a real-time style more akin to  and .Honestly, it's way more fun than it would seem. I've been a  fan for as long as I remember, gaming with my cousins on a bootleg version of , with my school mates on even more , then finally amassing my  collection on Steam over the years. Suffice to say, I definitely miss the turn-based nature, and some of the wacky weapons we got in the past games (among my friend group, I was the undisputed Aqua Sheep king) - but  does partly make up for it with a more concentrated variety of weapons that mostly still feel rather solid.But let's take a look at the elephant in the room. You can tend to gauge how well a game has sold by the number of reviews, even if they only count Steam reviews.  (with 320k+) massively took off, and even though the playerbase has obviously decreased since then, there are still thousands playing the game daily. The same cannot be said for , which is languishing on 1/356 of that amount, and a Steam player count of 2 digits. The only reason lobbies can still even be found are due to the PlayStation playerbase that got it from PS Plus, which at least is the one tactical masterstroke the game launched with.This severely thin playerbase, I'm guessing, is what has led to the matchmaking being seemingly imbalanced. When I tried it out during the free weekend, I admit I criticised it too harshly, claiming it was programmed by "literal donkeys". In retrospect, that's a pretty unfair assessment, because what can you do when there's so few people playing it? You'll just get matched up against the same pros over and over again because there aren't too many players at a similar skill level rushing in to queue into matches; you're just thrown in at the deep end. And that's not including the fact that I can't even find matches for Last Squad/Worm Standing either.Also, I'm based in the eastern side of the world - and searching for matches on the automatic setting just throws me into Europe games because there is no other playerbase; just the EU folk. This results in me having to play at a perpetual ping disadvantage. Fun, eh?In actuality, I do find myself liking this game and wanting it to somehow succeed; this is still a pretty fun addition to the  series, despite this dramatic shakeup. It's just a shame that the abysmal playerbase is causing quite a lot of problems.Unfortunately, I can only suggest to get this on any form of sale. Humble Choice June 2021 was an option (and where I got mine), but it now also goes on 90%-off discounts on Steam. There are too many questions regarding this game's longevity, and getting it at full-price is a questionable decision at best. If you were lucky enough to claim it for free on PS Plus back on launch day, there is no point to double-dipping; just enjoy your copy of the game from there.

_childDocuments_.review: Something needs to be done.I bought this game and all its DLC on Steam, Nintendo Switch, and PS5. I did this because all I want is to see every Worms game succeed so we can continue to see more entries released implementing new game-changing mechanics. Unfortunately it is not an enjoyable experience to play this game in its current state.You will only find matches if you queue up for quick play. Even then it can take up to 10 minutes to find a match, and when it does there will only be at most 5 people in the game. Of those 5 people, at least 1 of them will be a level capped player with upwards of 5 million lifetime damage. The team this player is assigned to will win. It makes it feel like the other individual players don’t matter, as these matches typically end with scores 20 to 1.This issue likely drives new players away, which is problematic because this contributes to the lack of players online. So few players online renders multiple daily challenges impossible to complete. The majority of daily challenges must be completed in specific game modes. Game modes that you cannot queue up for, as the only queue you will find matches in is quick play.Because of this, daily challenges are painstakingly slow to complete, as it’s a coin toss whether or not quick play will put you in the game mode you need to complete the challenge.This makes the game feel very devoid of purpose when everything is solely dependent on luck. Will you win the match? Depends on if you get teamed with the 3,000+ hour playtime veteran. Will the match you waited 10 minutes for be relevant for your daily challenges? Depends on the mercy of quick play.Neither of these issues can be resolved by queuing up with a friend, as my friend and I have tested, two players queued separately for one game mode does not create a new lobby. You will both sit in queue until it times out and disconnects you. The only clear resolution to these issues would be to get new players. Whether or not this means becoming free to play, I don’t know. All I know is that if SOMETHING is not done, this game is going to die.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay Video:  is a 2.5D fast-paced real-time combat, instead of turn-based the franchise is known for, where worms fight each other for laughs and giggles. I played on both PC and PS5 (it was free for PS Plus owners last month). There are three game modes: Deathmatch (free-for-all) and Last Squad/Worm Standing (fast-paced battle royale). I was a little irritated at first that they chose this route, but after playing for quite some time I started to enjoy it.  ✔️  Play Deathmatch if you want to have cause mayhem and kill other worms as much as possible, or Last Squad/Worm Standing (where 32 players are against one another, group of three or solo) and be the last man/squad standing, while using iconic weapons and items from previous games, such as the sheep launcher and the holy grenade.✔️  You can fight other players online across console and PC. Don’t let the steam player count fool you, the game is very much alive and it doesn’t take me too long to find a match, especially since it was free for PS Plus owners last month.✔️  The 2.5D cartoonish graphics are very different and vibrant, compared to the previous games, and they look pretty good ✔️  didn’t face any technical issues, just buttery smooth 60fps.❌  Don’t buy this game if you are looking for some single-player content. ❌  There are only four maps and three of which look somewhat identical to one another.❌  It’s not turn based and require less strategy. On the other hand, I don’t blame them for choosing this route; change is good and there are plenty of single-player  games on steam, plus not a lot of people are fond of turn based combat. There are disconnection issues, according to other reviews. Fortunately, I haven't experienced one, not even on the PS5. In conclusion, if you want to play fast-paced PVP matches, using some of the most ridiculous weapons out there, then I recommend it, especially since it’s only $15. If you are looking for single-player content and some good turn-based combat, then I recommend  and  (my personal favorite).

_childDocuments_.review: Worms Rumble is a battle royale game with cross-play. It's basically Worms without having to wait for your turn and available on Steam, Playstation 4, and Playstation 5.There are three different modes, ten weapons, a handful of items (different grenades, jetpack, etc.), and three maps. You can customize your character with innumerable cosmetic items as well as your weapons with different skins. You level up by playing the game and unlock new cosmetic items which you then have to buy for coins. You can't buy coins with real money. There are no microtransactions in the game!Deathmatch is one of the modes available to play. It works just as in every other game. 8 minutes, respawns and the one with the most kills wins. On the map are several crates with loot in them. That way, you can find better/different weapons, med-kits, grenades, and more. You also recover some health after time. In the beta, you had to wait 15 seconds or more 'til you could respawn. Fortunately, they changed it in the full game. You can now immediately respawn. It's a quite nice improvement and shows that the devs listen to the community. The main attractions of the game are the battle royal modes - Last Worm Standing and Last Squad Standing. The first one lets you play alone against 31 other worms. Just like in other BR games, the map gets smaller after some time. In Worms Rumble, you don't immediately die if you're out of the safe zone. The map shows you which area gets toxic and you'll lose health every few seconds if you're in it. There's enough time to leave the area if you pay attention. Losing early is kind of frustrating since the matchmaking takes a bit longer here. The game recommends starting this mode if you reach level 10 with indicates you're not a beginner anymore. Last Squad Standing is a battle royale with teams of three players. You can either invite your friends to play or get random teammates. One of you decides where your team spawns on the map. After that, it's the same as LWS. This mode is recommended for players who reach level 5 but you can play both modes immediately after starting the game for the first time. Worms Rumble is a multiplayer-only game. Steamcharts shows that the player count is pretty small right now (Not even 1000 players on release day usually indicates the game is dead in a few weeks/months). Thanks to cross-play you don't have to worry about that. The game is well alive and matchmaking takes 30 seconds the most. The game is free if you have PlayStation plus which secures a healthy player base.Having that many customization options is a good thing. Especially since there are no microtransactions and you can get everything by playing the game. It's also very playable with a controller and there is no real advantage for M+K users which makes it a casual experience overall. It's a competitive game for sure but easier for everyone who never got a chicken dinner in similar BR games. I even got first place in Deathmatch in the beta after playing like five matches and chicken dinner in LSS in my second match with random teammates (me having the most kills) and I'm not a pro player by any means. The game is fun and these little Worms are as charming as ever. The one thing we have to wait for is longevity. Will they add more maps, weapons, or even modes for free in the future? Maybe tournaments, special events, or challenges (There are daily challenges at least for now)? If they can deliver new content fast enough, they can make it worth it.Otherwise, I'm not quite sure the game will be fun for solo-players in the long run. Playing with friends is a blast though and it's definitely worth it if you got friends to play with!

_childDocuments_.review: Let's Get Ready To Rumble!!! Upon starting the game for the first time, you will be asked if you would like to enable Cross-Platform Gameplay. It doesn’t really matter which you choose right now as you can enable and disable the feature in the settings. Next, you’ll be asked if you wish to Begin Training or Go to Menu. On the main menu screen along the top of the screen you’ll find, Play, The Lab, Worm and Weapons, Your Rank, Name, Money, Stats, Friends and Settings. On the left of the screen is some of the latest news, along with three daily challenges to unlock. In completing these challenges you’ll gain a gift reward of some sort. Beneath these is where you choose your Game Mode, hitting the Play button will then search for a game. You might want to go into the options and set the matchmaking region to the closest one available to you. There are four matchmaking regions, Central Europe, US West, US East and Asia, if you are unsure of which to choose you can set it too Automatic. The Game Modes on offer currently are Deathmatch, Last Squad Standing and Last Worm Standing. Training can also be found along with the game modes. The Last Man Standing is recommended once you have reached Level Five, while Last Worm Standing is recommended that you be Level Ten.  Selecting to go through training will take you over the basics, how to move, jump shoot, throw grenades etcetera as you make your way through the training area. Reaching the end, you will arrive at an assault course, here you have Target Practice and Armoury. Target Practice is where you need to take out Twenty targets in the quickest time possible. In the Armoury you can mess around with all weapons, grenades and equipment. If you wish you can also take the toys around the assault course for a spin.  There is one more game mode The Lab, each week there will be specific rules and map. This week's Lab Mode is Melee Only Deathmatch where the only weapon you’ll use is the Baseball Bat on the map Missile Mall. There’s also a Weekly Reward, with this week's reward being a Pink Dinosaur outfit (yes, I do look good in it but as it’s Chrimbo Season I’m rocking a red reindeer outfit with snowflakes and a golden nose). While in a match you’ll have to keep your mince pies on your stamina. Rolling and Wall Jumping to get around the map will eat into your stamina. You can always crawl along at worm speed to save some stamina but if you really want to get your botty moving then you’re going to have to start rolling. There are other forms of moving around from place to place if you can get your hands on the Jetpack or Grabble Hook.  You start with One-Hundred health and once it’s gone you die; you will respawn after a few seconds (at least in deathmatch). Collecting First Aid Boxes or Cans of Energy Drink, these can replenish your health if you can manage to get it down your neck before someone comes along and spanks your botty. You can carry two weapons at one time and you’ll get random weapons, equipment from a crate at the start of each round. More weapons can be found after being dropped from fellow defeated worms. After each match you’ll be rewarded with Experience Points and Coins depending on how well you did. You will get a Breakdown of the match and earn experience points and coins in Match Completed, Eliminations, Damage and Position. These experience points will Level Up your character. You also get a Breakdown on any Weapons used, you will gain Experience Points in Eliminations, Damage and Time Held, these points will Level Up that weapon. Gaining experience and coin will unlock new weapon skins, costumes, look and other customisable items for your character. In the settings you’ll find options for Audio - Master, Gameplay, Music, Speech and Announcer Volume Sliders, also here is Audio Output Device. Video - Display Mode, Resolution, Resolution Scale, V-Sync, Limit FPS and Max FPS. Brightness, Render Quality, Ambient Occlusion, Anti-Aliasing, SSR, Bloom, Shadow Quality, Post Process Quality and Particle Detail. Game - Auto-Switch Empty Weapons, Auto-Switch New Weapon, Nameplates, Enemy Health Bars, Roll Toggle. Account – Cross-Platform Play (On/Off) and Matchmaking Region (Automatic, Europe Central, US West, US East and Asia). Accessibility - Colour Blind Mode, Held Buttons and Screen Shake.  Controller - Controller Bindings, Aim Sensitivity, Aim Assist, Movement Aim, Vibration, Left and Right Stick Deadzone. Mouse & Keyboard - Movement, Action and Equipment Bindings. I’ve enjoyed playing Worms Rumble, especially the Melee Only Deathmatch (this weeks The Lab game mode). I chose the Europe region for matchmaking with me coming from England. The game seemed to run pretty smooth, I never felt like I was lagging at all.  Searching for a game doesn’t hasn’t taken too long to find one, a minute or two at most. Although I do have cross-platform multiplayer selected in the options so as to make sure I get a game, which hasn‘t been a problem so far. I haven’t tried to search for a game against just Steam players, I don’t mind spankin’ the botty of other platform gamers using my keyboard and mouse … All Hail the PC Master Race!!!  I have had a Network Error occur three or four times, one of these errors occurred while in game and I was kicked out. While the other times I got the errors when trying to connect to a game. Other than that, Worms Rumble is a refreshingly fun and enjoyable game.  Positives + Fun and enjoyable to play + Nice graphics + Multiple game modes + Cross-Platform multiplayer + Full controller support + Has achievements Negatives - Network errors - No cards currently Take to the arena in thirty-two player cross-platform battles, customise your worm and cause chaos with old and new weapons in Worms Rumble 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: The game is actually really fun, and I wouldn't say it's necessarily "true" to the series in the sense of gameplay because it was basically rewritten all over again, but that's almost what makes it more fun than I expected. _childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Well, it is an online only multiplayer brawler. Can this be an eternal masterpiece? After it's 1995 Amiga release, Worms became one of the larger franchises in gaming history. Now, after about a dozen games in the series, Worms Rumble is the first online-only and real-time Worms. Quite a change from the usual formula. So lets say this clearly - the game mechanics are completely different from older Worms games.You get a real-time, online multiplayer action game. Kill all other worms, excluding your team in the team modes. The roots of Worms are still here - from the banana grenade to the attacking sheep, but if you want slower turn-based Worms gameplay, stay with the (reasonably good) Worms W.M.D. or Armageddon. Worms Rumble comes with 2 basic game modes, either (Team) Deathmatch to score the most kills or Last Squad/Worm Standing to survive, both in Team or FFA mode. The matchmaking is automatic, but you can invite friends. Servers are populated atm, so you will find a deathmatch game with short waiting time. Rounds take a few minutes, and you unlock tons of cosmetic items to dress your worm. There are also a bunch of cosmetic DLCs available, if you still don't like your looks.Gameplay is frantic, the controls are responsive, it is easy to score a few kills even for beginners. Collect the spawning loot boxes to receive better weapons (or health, ammo), jump or roll around the (few) well-thought out and large levels, shoot with your gun/rocket launcher or throw (holy) grenades - that's it, basically. Fun, but probably not a masterpiece.Good online brawler in the Worms universe.
_childDocuments_.name: Worms Rumble

_childDocuments_.review: Quick disclaimer: The player base is rather dead. If you don't want to play only on weekends, it will be difficult to find active lobbies.Nevertheless, Worms Rumble is a really good game. It has the classic Worms look in newer and better graphics. Furthermore, the gameplay is quite simple, but entertaining. Kill the other worms in a 2D map. Everyone moves their own worm in real time, which is a departure from the classic games. The choice of weapons is very large, and it is easy to get into the game. The choice of maps and game modes is also solid.Fun game for in between. It would be best to get the game directly with some friends. I recommend buying the game on sale though.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not even complaining; I mean, for what it's worth the game is functional, great-looking and smooth... However, you'd rather play other "better" party-based online games like "Fall Guys".Being part of the Worms universe (If you don't know Worms, just scroll down NOW), the game remains true to the whole premise that you're in control of an armed and dangerous worm that slithers around the battlefield, killing other worms to win the game. In Worms Rumble, you've got different modes, all of which would optimally require 40 or more players... You can really visualise what they tried to do here: complete rumble and mayhem as 40 or more worms are trying to kill each other for the high score or to be the last worm standing... The game, however, is deserted... with very few veterans still playing it.The queue time is actually short, believe it or not, and the game would start with ten players that probably only play this game, because I've played two games so far with the exact same ten people twice... Ten worms that start with bazookas, sniper rifles, sheep that explode? homing missiles... every single weaponry that looks like it would take you over 500 hours playing this dead game to get... You can imagine my frustration at being able to hit literally nobody with my cute pink pistol that does crap damage lol. Because the game is deserted, you're faced with only one of two options: keep playing the game, getting completely obliterated every single game by the same few people that still play it? Or go play something else. Well, an achievement hunter knows his choices, you should know yours. For the smooth gameplay, I'm ranking this game slightly over a grade that would put it into the red zone, with . Great premise and execution; abandonned too early!

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't want to have to not recommend this game.When I initially saw the trailers for Worms Rumble, I thought, "Ooh, this is a fun twist on the original concept." I figured it was different enough from your typical battle royale to stand out a little more. I even decided to preorder the game, because I genuinely love the Worms series, and Team17 has put out a lot of games I enjoy.Do I enjoy playing Worms Rumble? Yes, absolutely. But can I recommend it to anyone? No, not at the stage it's in. I hadn't played for a while, so I hopped on today to do a few deathmatches. First time I tried to get into a game, I waited a few minutes before cancelling and trying again. This has been an issue in the past that I've noticed. Then when I finally did get into the game, I seemed to be playing with a lot of the same people. Each match was dominated, of course, by a few diehard, level 50 players.This game is slowly sinking, and the devs don't seem too keen on doing anything about it. It's been, what, half a year since we got any sort of update or event? The rewards system is, ironically, unrewarding. And frankly, I'm not terribly interested in investing time into a game that's gonna eventually go offline once there's no profit to be made from it. Once that happens, all our time and money will have been for nothing.So yeah, go play Worms WMD instead.

This player-experience is way beyond plain stupid.The game is realy fun, and would be played way more often, but this missing feature makes it unplayable. I don't want to be farmed by strangers, I want to have fun with my friends.I don't get it, why a pioneer (30 years old) like team17 did this.

_childDocuments_.review: I blame this failure of a game on bad marketing. It's actually REALLY fun! I'm rather upset about it because this is the kind of rumble tournament game I've been looking for (something not FPS or any platform that people have been used to). It would seem the game was thrashed by die hard worms fans because it's not the typical turn based and destructible terrain platform we all love.THERE IS NO ONE TO PLAY WITH! Well, very few and the load time takes forever only to get into a game with way less than the expected 32 player cap. So, this sucks. I hope they make it free-to-play. I could see this game really evolving into something great with more weapons, fighting styles, etc. It's not very clever to adopt a successful game type (battle royale) and then compromise by charging for the game. MAKE IT POPULAR and then have micro transactions....I played more than 2 hours so Steam is being mean and not giving me my money back.

_childDocuments_.review: I always wanted to learn how to ninja rope like the pros in Worms 1999. Now there is Worms Rumble, a real time action game with ninja ropes. The jetpack will probably give you a bigger advantage, but that's ok since ninja roping is way more fun! There were many bugs we came across at the release, but after a week the devs fixed most of them and continue to work hard making the game better. The devs always replied to my concerns and complaints in the forums. There are many complaints about wanting destructible environments, girders, land mines, and other cherished worms related things, but as you can see this is a real time action game and not turn based so I welcome the new changes.The game can be unfair at times, but I think that is the nature of "Battle Royale" type games. The spawns can give quite a challenge when you are randomly thrown into a small area with lots of other players. Look for the ninja-rope or jetpack and get away as fast as possible,  but don't forget to rescue your team mates! For long term playability, there are many hats and vanity items to collect and of course you can change the voice of your worm. I'm sure they have more maps, weapons, game modes planned for the future.Overall it is a great game with intense action, just needs a few more updates to polish glitches in movement/clipping. Most of the time I can play for hours perfectly, but can randomly crash. I recommend it regardless of the issues we had since the devs fixed game breaking problems very quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Worms Rumble

_childDocuments_.review: While I have praised Worms Rumble in the past, as much as I enjoyed my time with it, this game is as dead as the dodo. Matchmaking takes forever. They should at least have bots to play with or fill the gaps. I understand they need to maintain a server, but there are better ways to capitalize a game. There aren't enough rewards to justify playing, other than bragging rights and unlocking, what else, more cosmetics.It's a real shame. I really liked this game, but I can't recommend it to anyone in its current state.And no, the excuse of  doesn't hold water. They clearly stated it's a battle-royale arena shooter, not a turn-based strategy game. Hell, the screenshots and the trailers they show clearly show you what this game is.If you bought this expected something else, it's your own fault.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first this game is not dead like others have said. The player numbers on steam are pitifully low at around 8 but this game has cross-play so i was never waiting more than a minute for a game. This game isn't very new player friendly with new players being put into lobbies with max level 80,000 kill players but I don't think this is a reason to not play. Worms has always being a game you play with friends to have a good time with silly little worms with silly little weapons and Worms Rumble is just that but a bit more chaotic and a lot more fast paced. At the price I paid for it I had a good time but wouldn't pay full price. If you can get it on sale or if it ever goes free to play I fully suggest giving it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a regular Worms game, this is not one of them. If you are looking for a fun Worms spin-off (akin to Worms Golf or Worms Blast), then you are about have a wonderful time! I played both the alpha and the beta of this game, so my in-game time isn't fully accurate. This is an incredibly fun fast-packed 2D arena shooter. There are currently 3 maps and 3 modes:- Deathmatch (get the most kills)- Last Worm Standing (Battle Royale)- Team Last Worm Standing (3-worm team Battle Royale)Each one of those is extremely fun to play, and the only hope is that developers keep on supporting this game and adding content for the years to come. _childDocuments_.review: It's a good game that had all the makings of what could have been a great game but it missed it's mark. Notalgia of playing worms 2? yes!the chaos and unpredictable wildness of the classic Quake arena? sure it kinda has that. Various competitive game modes? they put that in there too! (deathmatch, last worm standing, etc.)It's really a bit of fun to play but there's just one problem... they have to fix the fact that it isn't playable sometimes. If there is no one else online to play, you CAN'T play. Here's the bottom line on the mixed reviews - their match making system needs work. A lot of work. - Matches taking between 5-10 minutes (i'm not kidding)- Deathmatch games having players popping in an out on occasion.- player ranking lobbies are a lawless wasteland. (imagine jumping in on your first game with 5 level 50 players while you're still trying to get a feel for the game). Not fun. Now, this is probably because of a loss of players because the devs may have neglected to add certain parts of the worms franchise that made the game fun. - Setting up private rooms to pick and choose who you play with (friends and/or people in a certain region for instance). - Offline game modes and challenges for new players to get to enjoy the mechanics the devs worked quite hard to polish. - A spectator mode where players can watch on-going matches and possibly learn the maps. I really do like the game... but i don't think i can recommend the game to anyone else I know until they polish up a few things with the game. Beyond that, the game stands a chance to be one of the great games. Really It does. The attention to detail they put into it shows with their audio and visual designs. Personally I appreciated small touches like putting a mild echo on the bathroom areas, adding pinball and arcade sounds in the lobby areas, the grapple hook mechanics were really evident. If the devs ever do get to read this, I hope that they get put more (modes) into it. It honestly feels more like an early access game than anything not because the game isn't good. It feels like an early access game because the game could be so much more than what it is. It HAS so much potential to be one of the greats.

_childDocuments_.review: Worms Rumble has blown my expectations out of the water and it is already my new favorite game. If you have any experience with the Worms Franchise you know that they are mainly these turn-based tactical games and so Worms Rumble is a crazy new take on the Worms formula and it works incredibly well.Instead of playing like the old Worms Games, Worms Rumble is a super intense, real-time deathmatch and battle royale game that is super fun. Also it is just a breath of fresh air in terms of multiplayer games for me personally. The battle royale mode is extremely fast paced which is great and the inventory management system is super streamlined.And I will say the weapons are probably one of the best parts about this game. There are several unique weapons like some classics like the shotgun, assault rifle, and the rocket launcher, but then you have these other crazy weapons like a gun that shoots exploding sheep that run to the enemy, which if you play other Worms game you will definitely recognize.And the attention to detail on these maps is pretty incredible. The 2.5D artsyle is really awesome and all the different areas are visually different which makes the maps feel like they have a ton of variety. Also there are several different maps with unique gimmicks to them so you don’t have to worry about getting bored on the maps at all.In terms of the playerbase, the game seems to be doing crazy good right now, its a free game for premium playstation users in December I believe, and the game is cross platform at launch so with all the platforms together I don’t think you will have to worry about getting in games of 32 people.And so the gameplay is fast paced, exciting, and crazy fun but that’s only half of why I love this game so much. This game has a progression system that actually managed to make me care. A lot of games do the type of progression system tied to cosmetics and normally they don’t interest me at all but for some reason this game just does it right and makes me love it. It kind of works like the progression in COD and also kind of Apex Legends in a way. So you can level up your overall account and that unlocks new customizations for your worm like hats, faces, and even card backgrounds and different stat tracking things to brag about on your cards like Apex Legends does.Also you can level up each individual weapon which will allow you to get new weapon skins for those guns and the final weapon skin is gold which reminds me so much of Call of Duty and I love that because I always liked grinding for gold weapon skins.So for me pesonally this game is just everything I could ask for in a game. You have crazy good and fast paced gameplay, you have super fun weapons to fight with, you have really good looking maps and just an overall amazing theme, I’ve always loved the worms franchise, and a really simple yet impactful progression system that gets you new cosmetics for your worm and your weapons.The only piece of criticism or feedback I would give is that there is sometimes a little bit of downtime between the matches. The game takes a little to find a match and then the loading into that match takes a decent amount of time. It’s nothing unbearable but after playing a couple games in a row I started to notice it and if you die instantly in the battle royale mode it might suck to have to go through that whole process again. But besides that, hands down I would recommend this game in a heartbeat.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend Worms Rumble as a multiplayer game that's fun for players of most any age.  That said, matchmaking has dried up recently.  Even during peak hours, or on the weekend, most matches are only half full at best.  Past that, the playerbase is an unstable mix of total pros and utter newbies, which makes things feel very imbalanced.  I still think Rumble is a fun and inventive take on the Worms franchise, however.  Team 17 is still providing it with some regular support, and I hope to see the player numbers improve again one day. Moving to an F2P model would be a smart step in that direction. Until then, it's hard to recommend Rumble as anything but a "buy it on sale, if nothing else is up on your wishlist" type of game.

_childDocuments_.review: Worms Rumble is a twist from the classic Worms turn-based gameplay, this time it's in full real-time.Some may say "Oooh, it's a battle royale game, how lame!", well, news flash to them, it's always been, last team standing wins, except it was turn based. And the sudden death mechanic where the water rises, the gas is doing the same here except you can't camp the high ground and win because of that. The amount of weapons have been cut down obviously from past entries, but they are all completely different from one another and are a decent amount. However I would like to see a few more personally. There are 3 maps and they're huge, although not completely destructible. In a deathmatch, the map would be gone within the first minute, so that's a good thing, but may seem like a downgrade somewhat. Lastly, there's nothing you can purchase that gives you any bonuses, DLC's are cosmetic only and leveling your worm and weapons only unlock customization. So it's a balanced game. My only complaint is the sentry launcher, that thing is impossible to get kills with and will haunt me until I reach level 10 with it.All things considered, I'm really enjoying this game and would recommend it to everyone that enjoys worms or that enjoys chaotic 2d shooters!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a brilliant spin-off from the Worms franchise.Played a good chunk of the open beta and happily bought the Deluxe Edition because Team17 are great lads.While it's a different style of game, Rumble keeps the chaotic battles that Worms is known for. Lots of explosions, lots of carnage. The game is very satisfying when you get on a roll of taking down a bunch of enemy worms in quick succession.Personally, the deathmatch is where the game shines best. The battle royale is alright, but I believe this game is best played with the ability to get right back into the action.The level design is great, with clever use of vision restriction thanks to vents, crates and other obstacles spread through the maps. I love the mobility provided with the jetpacks and grapple guns, there is definitely a high skill ceiling when you need to make the most of these items while fighting other worms.Sound and visual design while nothing groundbreaking are both solid. The game is pleasant to look at and the classic worms voice line banter is still here.The weapons are fun, but lacking in numbers compared to the turn-based games. Obviously it is rather difficult to bring over many of those weapons, I do applaud efforts like the sheep launcher and the sentry launcher, but overall some new weapons would be great to see.On the technical side, the game does tend to take a while to load most of the time, I assume this is because we have to wait for all players to load in before the game starts, so if people are playing on console or slow PCs, we have to wait a bit. This is another discourager for the battle royale, as those games can be rather short, the play-to-load screen times can be a bit underwhelming.I also noticed a significant amount of lag. I'm playing from Australia and am not sure what the server options are at the moment, but hopefully this can be fixed down the line. Most of the time it was fine, but it was quite common to see teleporting worms and sudden loss of health that was not possible with what was attacking me.Private lobbies would also be a mandatory addition in my opinion, something that should have been included on release, including the ability to only use certain sections of maps to accommodate a smaller lobby than the usual 32 players.A level editor would also be neat!Overall, Worms Rumble is a blast to play and I hope that it lasts a long time and builds a solid playerbase. Well done Team17!

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time Worms fan I came into this game with a few long-held expectations of what a Worms game could be, but it turns out this isn't your typical Worms game. This is a real-time action shooter, and aptly demonstrates how much fun these little guys can bring to other genres besides their own. The action is quick and tight, the game is gorgeous, and the actual FEEL of a Worms game is maintained. If you enjoy squaring off vs a foe in a 1v1 shootout, bouncing, bounding, swinging, and rolling across the map while you each try to take the other out in the midst of a giant brawl (of up to 32 players) taking place all around you, this is the game for you. I loved the game form the get go, blowing past my refund window in only a single sitting before peeking my head back up and seeing the time. This is a game that'll make the time fly by in an instant, and the matches are only 10 minutes each! And while there are a few different game modes to try out, I'm a fan of Deathmatch/FFA and have been spending all of my time there. With Worms tackling a new genre like this with ease, maybe one day we'll see the Worms franchise trying their hand at all the genres Mario seems to master. And with the quality we're seeing here, they're welcome to try.

_childDocuments_.review: ***Pre-Note***While this is marked as received this product for free, it was bought for me as an early Christmas gift.  Money has been parted for this game.Worms has always been a huge part of my gaming life, from the originals on my Amiga 500+ all the way up to the Worms W.M.D. on PC, I have never missed a worms game, I have played and loved them all across various consoles and computers.When I first saw the trailer for the game and saw it was no longer turn based, I was immediately turned off from getting the game, in fact for a few moments I turned into the godfather as I watched and muttered to myself "look how they massacred my boy"  however, now I have actually placed a few hours into it (many more to come) I am not only shocked as to how much fun it is but amazed they didn't swap from turn based to live / real time sooner.The maps are huge, not huge enough so you will struggle to find other worms, in fact they have been smart enough to include a mini map so you can locate where the action is taking place but overall very well designed. The amount of customisation available from the start is good but you also unlock more items as you rank up your worm and your weapons, there are also challenges that unlock cool items too, I'm currently rocking out a Sheriff hat, blue skin and sunglasses (because why the hell not!!).  There is a lot to unlock.The weapons are silly and fun, exactly how they should be from a worms game however I feel the blast radius for the holy hand grenade is a tiny bit too large and I struggled to use it without causing injury to myself but that's not a complaint, just a heads up when you use it.My only real complaint is at this time, there is no in game chat options.  This is okay if playing with friends on PC, you can use Steams voice chat or Discord, however if playing with random players or you have friends on PS4 etc there is currently no in game way to communicate with them.The dev team have said they will be adding something at a later date but at the time of writing this it is not in game.Get this game if you love worms.Get this game if you want a new worms experience.Get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge Worms fan and I knew this wouldn't be my style of game, and boy was I right. Thankfully I bought this game from a key seller website for like $3. This game has absolutely nothing to do with classic Worms titles at all aside from the fact that you control Worms and use some classic weapons and utilities from those games. This game could have easily been made with different generic character models and slightly different weapons and nobody would think for a second that it has anything to do with the Worms franchise. The game has no charm whatsoever... from the menus, to the environments, and everything else. The music is extremely bland, the sound effects are decent but nothing great. The worm movement is weird. Damage output seems inconsistent. Some weapons are far superior to others. The only way I could see myself enjoying this game is back in the days of LAN parties, Playing against randoms is not fun at all and I feel like the general replay value is very low. This is what I would call a 'rental' if renting games was still a thing. It might be ok fun for a couple of days but odds are this isn't a game that you will get hooked on and play for months. Definitely don't buy this unless mindless arena deathmatch games are your thing. I only have about 2 hours logged into the game and I am already bored with it. I've also noticed that with some game modes it's about impossible to find a match. With other game modes, it's messed up. For example: team deathmatch. I joined a few of these today and it ended up always being extremely lopsided teams, like 3 vs. 15 or 10 vs 1. WTF?  Is the matchmaking completely broken? The only mode that seemed to work as it should is normal deathmatch. Team17 needs to get to work making a proper new Worms game that fixes the horrible mistakes of WMD and leave silly side projects like this alone. The old school Worms fans want a new 2D Worms title that can eclipse Armageddon. tl;dr - Only buy this if the idea of a bland 2.5D arena deathmatch game appeals to you. On a scale of 1-10 I'd give this a 4.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Bundle for June 2021. If you are interested in the game and it's before July 6th, 2021, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Team 17 has made a decent number of Worms games and they all tend to have single players with additional solid multiplayer. Worms Rumble skips the single-player content and focuses solely on a brand new real-time multiplayer mode where players can use classic worm weapons to kill each other in real-time.I wasn't expecting to have a great time as the player counts are a bit low on SteamCharts with less than 40 players online since the bundle launch.  However there does appear to be cross-play and Worms Rumble is surprisingly active right now, though I wasn’t matched up with many Steam players.   I still found myself having a great time and wanting to play more.  The issue I see is one of having a consistent player base rather than issues with gameplayIf the player base can remain constant I think Worms Rumble is a solid and enjoyable experience.  The combat is fast but strategic. The character designs are the lovable Worms and the audio was still hilarious to hear.  Worms Rumble has only 3 maps but I still had an enjoyable enough time and I would love to come back to play more and take out new opponents.  Earning customizations through levels and daily missions helps as wellPick this up if you're a huge Worms fan and you want to take a risk on the player base.  As enjoyable a time I had, even playing with some friends on twitch stream, shout out to Bio Hazard Battle, and Royal, I don't know if I see the player base remaining steady on Steam.  It does appear that there is still some life on consoles, so cross-play will help.That was my review for the game as a part of the bundle, however looking at the game on steam as a new purchase, I find it very difficult to recommend a game with a playerbase even this week.  Unless you have a group who are going to actively play this, it's worth skipping in anything other than the bundle, kind of a shame. _childDocuments_.review: the most recent installment in the long running  franchise, and for the first time allows your worm to battle other worms in real-time in 32-player matches.  completely removes the turn-based combat present in all previous games and instead focuses on providing players with real-time mayhem across multiple maps and game modes.  provides a cross-play compatible multiplayer experience to allow more people from any platform to face off and 'rumble'. However, queue times are very unstable, sometimes getting into battle in ten seconds while at other times you can wait minutes.You start with either a handcannon, shotgun or assault rifle and pick up other weapons and utilities around the map, killing other players as you go. There are also plenty of nooks and crannies to roll through to try to avoid your demise. Disappointingly, the maps are lacking variety and I can already imagine a heap of possible maps and game-play features that would have been nice having on the game's release.The game currently has three game modes you can play: Deathmatch, Last Squad Standing and Last Worm Standing. 'Experimental' modes are said to be added weekly.In Deathmatch game mode, you have unlimited lives and seven and a half minutes to kill as many other worms as you can. This mode gives you quick and fun game-play for as long as you want. There are up to 32 players at any one time.Last Squad Standing pits you and two other players against other teams of three worms. As time goes by, areas of the map will become 'restricted' until finally becoming a storm, which will give around eight damage per second in it. In this mode, each player has only one life. The squad who survives wins.Much like Last Squad Standing, Last Worm Standing is exactly as its called. The last player remaining at the end wins, easy as that. Eliminating enemy worms will restore lost health.I experienced no internet lag during online play. has improved the quality of its visuals from previous releases, and the 2.5D styled graphics suits the modern theme well. The game contains plenty of bits and bobs of mostly decoration on every map, making them overall more interesting to look at. Combined with holy hand grenade explosions and bullets whizzing past your head, everything looks great. Graphics are easy to tune in the settings menu. Everything from worm voices to reloading and exploding sounds has been well done. The authentic  "Hallelujah" shout after throwing the holy hand grenade also brings some feeling of nostalgia, as nothing as really does. To improve, more soundtracks could be played on the menu and more worm voices could be added.This game is created to be easily accessed by most people, and is pretty simple to learn and play. No blood or gore is present, only animated violence.  is suitable for kids, teenagers and adults alike, and all can enjoy playing.CPU: Ryzen 3 3300XGPU: Galax 1650 Super 4GBRAM: 16GB DDR4 @2666MhzOther: 1TB ASUS FX60 FPS was achieved at all times and never once did I experience an FPS drop even when I couldn't see anything due to the mayhem going on on my screen. If you have a weaker system, you can always lower the video quality in settings, although it will have minimal game-play impact. was a daringly new gamble for the series, and I can confidently say it paid out. Although there can be some significant improvements made, such as a bigger variety in maps, for the most part the game is enjoyable to play. However, due to the lack of any major goals and game modes,  could quickly loose momentum. Referring to previous games in the franchise,  holds very little water in terms of nostalgia and game-play, lacking any sort of campaign or other single-player option, which may not appeal to some audiences. For a price of US$15, the experience offered is worth it, especially if it will receive further attention for a long time.Rating: 7/10

I inherited a small fortune from my grandfather and bought 20,000 copies of Worms Rumble. One for every person who would ever need one. I have stuck with the Worms franchise for as long as I can remember and I will say, with nostalgia running through my veins. This is the worst game I have ever seen. _childDocuments_.review: I honestly quite like this, it's not worms at all in style of gameplay but it's a fine deathmatch-style game. This game reminds me of one of those old 2D Unreal Tournament flash games you'd see a decade ago except much more fleshed out and polished. There are very clearly bad guns and good ones, don't expect to get many kills with the pistol or assault rifle. This game is pretty easy to get into it's a simple game that you can treat casually or really try your ass off if you want. You can pull off some dope plays with the grappling hook and just absolutely style on people or juke out and turn around on people who are trying to get you. I will say the player desync can be rather bad at times. I fired a hand cannon dead on to someone numerous times only to watch the enemy to completely ignore shots that would otherwise have connected.Gripes: I feel like this game would flow a bit better with smaller maps, ~~larger health pools, and an increased rate of fire for weapons. Maybe not the health increase but the faster RoF would be very much appreciated~~. I also think the vfx are a bit too pronounced and you can easily lose people in the smoke left behind by explosions.Overall, it's a solid game but I can easily see how the playerbase for this would die over the course of the next half year unless the devs actively add content. Enjoy it while you can because Worms games' playerbases die off pretty fast in my experience.As of Dec 3rd the rof for a few weapons have been increased, dope

_childDocuments_.review: I thought that developers did learn years ago on their mistakes to not make a horrible Worms spin-offs ever again. Guess I was wrong.Its so funny how Team17 perfectly knew how much community did hate the idea for this game (Real Time Battle Royal Worms) long before game release. Surprise - almost nobody play it or purchase it in the first month. Yes, Worms Rumble had 649 players on day 1 but that number drop to 30> faster than Bill Clinton's pants. Thats why I say that people didn't really care about the game. They purchase it out of curiousity that "hey, maybe it won't be that bad" or to make a sponsored stream/video or "hey, I want to prove all those haters on forum that they are super wrong and that this game is THE BEST WORMS GAME EVA!!!". Well, lo and behold those people desperately try to say something positive about the game quickly quit playing it.So what desperate attempt publisher can do to save freshly new released online only video game designed purely to chase a dying trend?Well, by putting it on Humble Bundle monthly in less than 6 months since release of course (just shows how devs admit of this game to be a failure).Surprise again - it did nothing for the player numbers. It did slightly increase number of positive reviews but also did increase number of negative reviews, mostly from people who are pointing out extremely low player numbers and boring gameplay.Currently we have a year 2022. Two years after this game release and current player numbers are? 12 players total currently playing. Freaking fantastic job devs and Team17. I hope it was worth the time, effort and money to release a online multiplayer only that EVERYBODY was telling you to not make.================================================================First I want to say about gameplay is that I have zero clue why publisher call this a Battle Royal game when its clearly not. Probably they call it because y'know, to attract audience of Battle Royal genre that popularity is sinking faster than Titanic itself.Worms Rumble is clearly not a Battle Royal game, not even close. Max 32 players on server and you have 10 second respawn time and all players do is keep killing eacher for points.Does that sound like a description of Battle Royal game. Or how about a simple Deathmatch mode to you?Second, by the time of 2021 there are only 3 maps and 13 weapons in the game. I am not gonna lie, calling this a Worms game in 2021 felt SO insulting to this 26 year old franchise.FFS I played Worms on Java phone that had more than double in the amount of maps and weapons than Worms Rumble.The game itself on gameplay level isn't that half bad but to be honest that is REALLY generous thing to say. Worms Rumble is just another dull, generic 2D online only deathmatch shooter in a sea of dull, generic 2D online only deathmatch shooters with nothing special to add to the genre except that you play as a worm doing flips this time (YAY for innovation!).Oh, did I mention that shooting fells both clunky and pointless, especially when melee is so much faster, stronger and overall better at killing your opponents? Yeah, add this to the giant list of issues with this game.In term of visuals, artistic style, level design or theme - horrible. Pure unimaginative thrash. This game feels, look and play like it was made in less than 2 months for the original Xbox by amateur game studio for like 300 dollars. Or it was made by modern Ubisoft  Hyper Scape .For the positive thing about Worms Rumble I can say that there a lot of worm customisation (imagine if there wasn't in a game like this tho) and a lot of that is unlocked by simple playing the game (its so sad that we are living in days that something like THIS is a positive thing to say about the game, that you can unlocks stuff by playing the game and not by paying real money for it).So gladly the game is not filled with micro-transactions (just yet) BUT entire presentation of the game (the FIRST thing you see on title screen is giant daily challenges boxes, YAY for grind because that is THE MOST important thing in the game, right?)and the whole idea for the game ( Deathmatch? In 2020? In the franchise that's the LEAST need that crap? I mean F*CKING REALLY???) is utter garbage not to mention that despite terrible sales and player numbers Team17 decided to shoved into Worms Rumble as much overpriced paid DLC's as possible.================================================================This game was not even a year old and t never even had decent player numbers, it was already on Humble Bundle montly and Team17 still try harding to ask for more and MORE money from those few people still playing the game? The audacity of this publisher lmaoF*cking disgusting. Maybe experience with Worms Rumble will teach them that all this community really wants is just another good Worms game but to be honest I thought they already did learn this long ago so f*ck me I guess.I mean Worms community is literally screaming since 2016 for a new 2D turn based Worms game but Team17 is like "f*ck this, f*ck that, f*ck what our fans want to pay for, we are making a game for bigger audience, its Battle Royal time, BABY!" even tho that fad got old long, long, loooooong ago.Seriously, you want Battle Royal mode in Worms game that badly, Team 17? Why not just make a new 2D turn based Worms game with additional gamemode that is litteraly Battle Royal with multiple players at once on a giant map with like 15-30 second turn and like 5-10 players max being able to move at the same time to cut waiting for your turn.Doesn't that sound already like a million times better idea for Worms game with Battle Royal mode than Worms Rumble?But nope - you rather waste money and time to develop Worms Rumble instead despite everybody in the community telling you from the start how dumb this idea was.Good job at listening your own loyal customers and fans ONCE AGAIN, Team17!Good f*cking job!
