_childDocuments_.review: Worms Rumble – A Colorful Chaotic Combat Carnival! 🐛💥Hold onto your helmets, folks! Worms Rumble is here, and it's like the classic Worms you loved, but with a turbo-charged dose of chaos and a splash of pure insanity! Imagine if your favorite childhood game had a wild party with high-octane combat, and you're halfway there! 🎉🎮Gone are the days of waiting for your turn—now it’s all about real-time mayhem where 32 players can battle it out in a colorful arena that looks like a rainbow exploded. 🌈💣 You can finally show off your skills without the endless wait while your worm buddy decides if he wants to launch a banana bomb or take a nap instead. (Spoiler alert: he’ll probably nap.)And let’s talk weapons! Oh boy, the arsenal is like a kid in a candy store with a sugar rush. From the classic Holy Hand Grenade (because what’s more comforting than divine intervention during a worm brawl?) to wacky new additions that make every match feel like a cartoonish explosion festival, you'll be launching projectiles that would make even the most seasoned soldiers jealous. 🍬💣 Just be careful not to blow yourself up—because that would be as embarrassing as slipping on a banana peel!The gameplay is fluid and frantic, allowing you to dart, dodge, and dive through the vibrant maps like a worm on a mission. The Last Worm Standing mode is a nail-biter; you’ll find yourself sweating bullets as you scramble to be the last worm wriggling. Just remember, when in doubt, just keep rolling! 🐍💨Plus, the cross-platform play means you can team up (or go full-on worm warfare) with your friends, no matter what platform they're on. It's like a digital family reunion where everyone tries to blow each other up instead of discussing awkward childhood stories. 🎊👾In conclusion, Worms Rumble is a delightful, explosive experience that takes everything you love about the series and cranks it up to eleven. If you’ve ever wanted to throw a grenade at your friends while laughing maniacally, this is the game for you. So grab your worms, load up your weapons, and let the chaos begin! 🐛🔥🎯Created with <3

_childDocuments_.review: (Please be sure to read my updates after the standard review as they share light on extra thoughts and clear up some issues)This game is not my favorite. The game itself, alright battle royale game. As a worms game, nope. When I bought a game called Worms Rumble, I expected it to be classic ol' worms with a new spin on it, or maybe a new gimimck added. Well, they did do both of those things. There are a couple of modes: Deathmatch, Battle Royale w/ Squads or Solo mode. No classic turn based strategy and no single player campaign. Not only does this mean it's less unique than most games(It is pretty unique for a battle royale, but in general it doesn't stand out from the crowd too much), but it also can't last forever. Because at least with other Worms games with a multiplayer component, they still have the single player campaign. But even if there was one, what would it be like. Considering the style of gameplay Worms Rumble introduces, even there was a campaign, I don't know if it would be any good.Final Thoughts: If you're a Worms fan expecting turn based strategy, don't buy it. If you're looking for a new Battle Royale or fast paced shooter, it's a fairly worthwhile purchase. Overall I think it's okay, but this is not what I wanted from a Worms game.Update 1: First of all, I'd like to thank everyone who left a comment on my review. Even a dev responded!  You steam community people really molded my view of the game. Anyways, one thing I'd like to address is that I don't hate the game. Yes, despite my harsh wording I don't necessarily hate the game. Second thing. Somebody commented that I should watch reveal trailers and such to get a better understanding if the product I'm purchasing. And if that person is reading this updating review, you are completely correct. It is entirely my fault that I picked up this game without any prior knowledge. Hell, I didn't even play the open beta! But also to that person, I'm not going to refund the game. Why? Well I remember in the steam announcement for the games release, the devs said that they would regularly update the game with new content. I'm actually pretty excited to see what they can do with the game. Perhaps one day, I'll update this review to a recommended one. Once again, thank you to everyone who responded. Goodbye for now.P.S: At the original time of writing this, I hadn't played the game too much. Expect me to edit this review in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Worms Rumble is a 3D rendered 2D platformer/twin stick shooter based on the "Worms" franchise, which we all know is a ripoff of the ancient DOS artillery game, Scorched Earth.   While the game looks okay and the gameplay is slick, the developers failed to grasp a few very basic concepts that lead to this being a colossal failure, given the significant budget dumped into making a game nobody wanted.Developers need to understand 2D platforming is a dead, obsolete genre.  3D graphics were "invented" some time ago, and became mainstream in the 1990s... so why are they trying to make 2D games today?There's no content, either.. it's just PvP.  PvP isn't content, and without other players to prop this up, it's a dead game.  Developers must learn that PvP is not an acceptable substitute for doing their job and creating interactive content. Confounded by an obsolete format, gamers largely shunned Worms Rumble.  At launch the game attracted under 800 players, and they didn't stick around.  There's a confused and sorrowful handful of players on any given day, possibly just bots.  This is a dead game.Finally (and contributing to the utter failure here), there's an eye watering $15 price tag for a PvP exclusive game... ain't nobody got time for that.  There's significantly better free to play PvP games, like CS:GO and so on.  Why should anyone pay for this?

You also re spawn with a basic gun after death too so those players who have way too much hours on the game will just rinse you over and over while you have no game knowledge or experience AND a awful weapon to defend yourself.Though i know this is just my own opinion i do urge people who like the classic worms format to play the older titles because this is so incredibly far from what you'll be used too.No hate to those who like this game but you should definitely get checked <3

_childDocuments_.review: This reminds me of what we tried to achieve in Worms Armageddon/World Party: real time concurrent worm movement sans turns! This is a very interesting spin on the series. But, again, beware: THIS IS NOT CLASSIC WORMS GAMEPLAY! THIS IS A REALTIME FRAGFEST! Very fun and I will be playing this from time to time in the near future I feel.Key things that I feel could use improvement:• The springy showcase behavior in customize a worm (and the very limited rotation degree of freedom)• Perhaps something at least close to the amount of different voice banks and other customization options we had back in the W2 era. Country flags, anyone? I feel like the new T17 worm games are all seriously lacking in that regard compared to 2000s era.• Team balance seems a way off at times but perhaps it's because there aren't as many players online currently.The movement and parkour takes some time to get used to, but I have a feeling that's as good as you're gonna get with a 2D action platformer. It's easier said than done.Overall verdict: very fun; would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Love the gameplay, the cosmetics could have been better, but there are a ton of glitches I've been dealing with that still have had no fix. Rockets can disappear after being shot and then not explode while still triggering the reload, the jetpack and grappling hook get glitched out quite often to where you have to cancel it, re-land on the ground and then try again and hope it works. The rocket shield can also glitch, seemingly allowing players to hit you right through it (before its blown up), and the plasma rifle and sentry cannon could likely use a range decrease due to how many random and unskilled/unintentional kills can occur by launching them across the map. I also believe with a game of this type there should be some kind of global stat ranking system; I've completed 74 challenges and still haven't unlocked the K/D stat card which is quite annoying, I would consider making stat cards unlock based on hitting a target number for that stat, rather than by leveling or reward boxes. _childDocuments_.review: Worthy Update on a classic.Preface: I have been playing Worms games for decades. I have loved the franchise from day one. So, I have tons of Worms experience. My opinion: Rumble is fun and well worth the $15 asking price. It is a fun, fast paced, quick hit firefight. PROS- Worms humor- Fast paced- Smooth combat- Decent variety of weapons- Simple controls- M/KB or Controller support- Customization of worm/weapons- Crossplay- Quick matchmaking- DM and BR and Squad BR modes- ZERO Pay to winCONS- Some classic weapons I would like to see are missing- Doesn't appear to be any ELO- No real progression- Not true Worms style of combat(Not really a con, for me, but some will hate this)- Lackluster DLCIf you are experiencing more of the same ol' same ol,' this isn't it. Yes, it does visually feel like a Worms game, but there isn't much beyond the visuals and basic control scheme that has roots in the old games. Yes, you run, roll, jump, fly and grapple around as a gun toting worm. That is pretty much where the similarities stop. It is fast paced, all action. No turn based games. You will always be on the move and fighting for your life. Imagine a 2.5D Worms level with worms bouncing all over the place trying to kill one another with a handful of classic Worms weapons and grenade variants. Personally, I really enjoy it. I am not in love with the DLC and would not buy any of it, if I had it to do over again. But as a whole, I am very pleased with this game.TL;DR - A 2.5D, fast paced, Worms fight to the death. A nice update on a classic. Worms Rumble isn't going to keep you playing 10 hours a day, or anything like that, but it is a nice change of pace from the BR genre and a great way to spend a couple of hours at a time. Skip the DLC and have a fun, refreshing take on the BR genre for $15.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is actually absolutely amazing!There was a lot of skepticism (and i think there still is) about Team17 going the route that they did with this installment of the worms franchise, and rightfully so, seeing as this is vastly different from the classical turn based worms we've always had. I was also a little hesitant to get it when I heard about it, but I went ahead and got it anyway, and am truly happy with the game and how it plays.It runs really smoothly, looks fantastic, and you don't need a high end machine to run it.The game-play is fast paced and it actually takes a lot of skill/practice to maneuver around the map fluidly, especially when trying to lay down accurate fire while you're flying around on your jet-pack.As of the writing of this review there aren't that many game modes, unfortunately.You've got the classic "Deathmatch", then "Last Squad Standing" where you and two others try to be the last surviving team in the game, and "Last Worm Standing" Where you go in solo and try to make it until the end without dying to possibly win.All of the game modes are very entertaining, and the game itself is pretty addictive. Team17 seems to be pretty involved with the community as well, listening to player feedback and they plan on adding more modes and customization options in the future.I've played all of the other classical worms and have almost all of them in my library, I've been playing the franchise since I was a kid, though never on a serious level. I 100% recommend this game to any old, or new fans of worms, or anyone into the 2d or 2.5d shooter genre, it's an absolute blast to play, and in my opinion, an excellent addition to the franchise as a whole.The only negative things I can say about it as of right now, is that it lacks custom lobbies, so you cant get more than two people in your party, it doesn't really have destructible terrain,  it could use some more game modes, especially some objective ones, like capture the flag or something, and it seems to randomly crash every now and again when you're in a party, and it could use some more customization options, both for your worm and it's guns, and for the HUD. HOWEVER, from what I understand, the crashing thing is being looked into right now, and they plan on making many more additions to the game that will address all of these issues.Definitely worth $15.

_childDocuments_.review: About time this itch got scratched!I have been missing something like this since the days of "Liero" and "Soldat" and it's finally here!Same style, high speed 2d platforming action game with that oldschool feel, requiring fast reflexes, precise aim and ninja-like movement to defeat your opponents. Equipment from the worms universe, like explosive sheep, bazooka, ninja rope etc, nothing too crazy but devs have been promising more content in the discussion forum so hopefully items keep staying relativley sane. Good launch with only a few minor bugs so far and what seems like a large player base, have not had to wait more than a few seconds yet for a game (EU).Some things that could make it better:-More than 3 maps.-Some kind of ranked, or at least some kind of hidden MMR, just to get matchmaking better. Right now it  seems like it just wants to start games as fast as possible but i feel bad for those that are still like lvl 1-2 and  have zero chance. -A few more starting weapons.A bit more cartoony and less "serious" than Soldat 2 but, imo, a lot more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - The game is a great little arena worm fighter. All the charm and idea's are their, just the lack of players, lack of content updates, the lack of love in general is what has let it down.Worms Rumble. A forgotten about game. No updates no love. Last time i saw anything on my news feed it was to do with the Worms Board game, which i am a proud owner of, but that had nothing to do with Team 17 other then the rights to the IP.Worms Rumble was dead on arrival, with so few players you could not even get a game going. Luckily their is cross play, Yippee! If you are lucky you can get into a game within a few minutes, if your unlucky you could be waiting up to 15 minutes.The game you do get into will be a group of level 50 die hard fans who can not put the game down, who know every map, every location, every broken way to get a quick kill, you won't do too well and probably not play again, or if you do, you may be unlucky enough to get a game with a cheater, oh yes, even this dead game does not get away from the cheaters, infinite stamina rolling worms that 1 hit you with full health and shield with a bat, but to be fair, why wouldn't they cheat, i mean it is the second link on google for the actual cheats after trying to find youtube videos of Worms Rumble Cheaters.The game is a great little arena worm fighter. All the charm and idea's are their, just the lack of players, lack of content updates, the lack of love in general is what has let it down. This game is in dire need of going free to play, it is now nearing 4 years old, was lacking players after the first 2 months of release on pc. If it went Free to play with more cosmetics to help keep it afloat, it would do so much better. Even if you don't want to go Free to play, just adding the option for Bots in games would at least keep it alive and give people a reason to buy it, because as of now if you look at your local CD key site, you can pick the game up for £0.60, when it goes on offer on steam it is £1.09, but people don't even want to spend  the price of a coffee if the game isn't going to have a player base. I own every Team 17 worms game, not just on steam either, i have been a long time fan, if i use to see the words Team 17 behind a game i knew i was going to like it more often then not and i really enjoyed this one but i feel as though not enough was done to ensure it lives long enough. It is a shame, i am always hopeful though that one day i see a new update seeing ''AI has been added'' I still recommend the game as when you get into a good match, the game is great and quite fun, all the tactical combat is their and is a laugh.

name: Pumpkin Jack
detailed_description: More jumping, more running, more platforming! About the Game Pumpkin Jack is a spooky scary 3D platformer in which you embody Jack, the Mythical Pumpkin Lord! Dive into an epic adventure through otherworldly landscapes and help the Evil annihilate the Good! Colorful Cartoon Setting: Travel through lurid landscapes in levels featuring alluring atmospheres, each crafted with vibrant color palettes, and high-quality lighting effects Fight For Your Life: With challenging beasts lurking around every corner, players must master the art of combo attacks; dodging, and timing to survive dynamic real-time battles! Players must unlock weapons and choose wisely in order to strike down all who oppose them Don't Lose Your Head: Solve puzzles that focus on physics; gravity, and reflection as Jack, or ditch the skinsuit and just use your flaming head to burn books; hammer some moles, create paths for magic spheres; and more as each level introduces new and exciting challenges Find Friends to Fight at Your Side: Helpful companions are there to assist Jack on his journey, including a haughty hooty owl to guide him along; and a snarky crow, itching to assist with long-range attacks Dive into an epic adventure and help the Evil annihilate the Good! Follow the will of the Devil himself and slay your nemesis in an epic quest that will take you on a journey in the Arc En Ciel Kingdom, a mythical realm shattered by the curse. You will meet friends along the way, from a haughty owl to a snarky crow! Discover Stunning atmospheres in a Colorful yet Spooky Scary Kingdom Travel through epic and dramatic settings, with each level having its own eerie atmosphere. Using a vibrant palette and high quality lighting effects, Pumpkin Jack invents its own unique cartoon universe inspired by the classic PS2 graphic style. Jump, Run & Climb to carve your own way in Unique Levels Pumpkin Jack is a classic 3D Platformer before anything else! Every level will challenge you through several themed platforms, all giving you new trials to complete. Fight for your life against Evil Beasts by using awesome Unlockable Weapons You will have to master the arts of dodging, timing and movement to vanquish Jack's foes. During the dynamic real time battles, choose which weapon you want to use and strike at the critical moment! Face Breathtaking Challenges and discover tons of Original Gameplays Solve puzzles that focus on physics, gravity and reflection. Inhabit a pumpkin head and burn books, hammer some moles, create a path for magic spheres… But also more! In each level, you will be faced with an action sequence using a new exclusive gameplay!

_childDocuments_.review: A resounding "Meh" Graphics are charming and the music is very good. Platforming is okay, fun when its working right, but you spend a lot of the time bouncing our invisible hit boxes off of other invisible hit boxes and getting thrown into the water becuase of it. Combat is...functional, but supremely boring. mash X. You can get through most fights while texting if you wanted too. there are a few weapons you collect as you go, but they all boil down to Mash X, so it doesn't really matter which one you use. But the biggest drawback on this badboy, is the dialouge, the endless, monotonous dialouge. Every character is constaintly trying to crack wise, but they do it by just saying whats happening. In a game where litterally every other line of dialouge is a joke, i dont think its gotten one genuine laugh ot of me. and the characters never shut up, they talk constaintly, with nothign really to say unless they are trying to handhold you to keep you from actually disocvering the next objective on your own. The game has a real visual charm to it, and controls harkening back to good 3d platformers of the bygone era, but its just not there yet. It could be improved massively by just adding a little more momentum control in the air, and removing every line of conversation from the game. Its worth it for maby 10 dollars, but more than that you arent going tog et your moneys worth with how short it is either.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, perfect for the Halloween season. Its a linear third person action game with platforming, puzzles and combat. It has 6 levels, each take around 20-40 minutes and each have lots of collectibles and a different boss.Every level feels pretty cool and unique for the most part, each level has different minigames and puzzles so that's pretty cool, each boss you kill gives you a new weapon which you can swap to at any time. There's also different outfits/skins you can unlock by picking up enough collectibles in the game so that's pretty cool. The game has cool little story cutscenes on each level to explain whats going on and that has some decent voice acting. The rest of the game however is not voice acted so you just have to read text on the screen which can be annoying at times like when you're trying to concentrate on playing and a character says something. The game itself visually looks great and it runs at a nice solid 144fps at 1080p for the most part. Surprisingly the game supports DLSS and RTX which isn't something you'd usually see in a smaller indie title but is very welcome. I didn't have any crashes or anything so that's good, definitely feels like a polished game. There was one actual bug that I encountered I think on level 4 on the second race for some reason there were no enemies so I just got to the end no problem, but otherwise I didn't really encounter any problems with the game.Overall pretty damn good game, I might be wrong but I don't think there's difficulty settings so if you've done all the achievements and gotten all the collectibles there's really not anything left to do. I was pretty much able to 100% the game in around 5 hours so that's the only issue for me however since Halloween themed games aren't very common and this game is actually pretty damn good I think I can excuse the length. If you really want though you could probably just wait for a sale. I'd give it a good 8/10, could have been longer, could have had some more features but overall a solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet 5 hour game with a cool artstyle and seasonal theme.Unfortunately, it has little to no replayability especially if you 100% the game the first time around.My only gripe about the game is you cannot reset a level unless you finish the aforementioned level; this is especially annoying if you miss a collectible in the first half of the level and can't go back to it.Pumpkin Jack is overall a cool game and I recommend getting it on sale, $30 seems a bit high in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I saw this at random on the front page of Steam a little while ago and for some reason felt a strong urge to play it. I don't buy a ton of platformers these days, so it was a bit out of my ordinary picks, and after downloading it and finding some time to sit down, I was wondering if I was going to really enjoy it.Well, safe to say I absolutely did. Game looks lovely, the cartoony design looks fantastic.Platforming handles smoothly and feels great. Double jumping and climbing is fun and you move just fast enough to keep progressing through areas briskly without feeling unnecessarily speedy, and the ability to climb ledges you jump against means you infrequently mess up jumps.Combat appears frequently, and has a vaguely similar feeling to the classic Medievil games. It's quite easy to take damage during fights, but the game is generous with HP drops from the environment so it never felt unfair. You start with just a shovel to smack things around with, but you get a new toy with every level, and I genuinely felt every weapon was fun to use and nothing felt too weak compared to another. More importantly, every weapon was satisfying to bash things with, and had different uses without being too niche to use at any time.The dialogue is fast paced, not exactly a game with long drawn out story cut-scenes, but dotted with amusing jokes that ride the line of mature enough to be fun for an adult but tame enough for a child.Each level tends to have a unique mini-game where you play as Jack's head, attempting different tasks with the same controls each level, so they never feel overused, as well as most (all?) levels having a fun little "traversal" section, where you'll be riding horseback, racing on karts, or so on, which all have a similar structure but different concept, again keeping the situation from becoming stale. On top of that, the music is great. Again much like the old Medievil, music tends to have this feeling of both Halloween spooky, but with an altering theme per area. The graveyard is spooky yet epic, while the North is spooky yet... Jingly. The music does an excellent job of capturing the atmosphere in the area, alternating between spooktown vibes for strolling through a level, before amping up to a rather joyous beat as you jump into a mine-cart and go flying down a pair of rails. Most of the boss themes are a pleasure to listen to, particularly the second boss which has an incredibly catchy theme.My only gripe with the game, if you can call it that, is I wish there was more! I played through the game in a single day, and had an absolutely wonderful time. I love a good "play as the villain" main character, and alternating between platforming and combat was balanced and satisfying the entire time. If you enjoy platformers at all, you should absolutely try this out, and it's for a very fair price as well. While the game is relatively simple, and unlikely to blow away your average person with "wow, this is an amazing concept!", the game is polished, smooth, fun, and charming, and nails the feeling of a platformer brawler. Goes to show that sometimes, a game doesn't need to have a super unique gimmick, ridiculous visuals, or dramatic long story to be an amazing time.Overall, I loved it. Very strong 8/10 from me.

_childDocuments_.review: A nostalgia-fueled dream, Pumpkin Jack pulls from 90's games like Crash Bandicoot, Banjo Kazooie, and MediEvil! The platforming was difficult enough to provide some challenge, but not so bad as to drive you insane. There are enough collection side quests to drive you play some of the levels again so that you can gain all the costumes, music boxes, and Steam achievements, while avoiding being tedious. The alternative game play from the boat and other on-rails sections is entertaining and give a decent break to the standard game, like the bonus levels from old Sonic gamesThe writing found in the banter of the Crow (your companion) and Jack brings some levity to the story and keeps it from feeling lonely. Reminds me of Navi from the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (just not annoying as sin). The dialogue between Jack and the various side characters, bosses, and the Wizard has some clever humor for adults and kids alike. ---Only a few asks to make this game better;*Voice overs for the dialogue, as reading during the action can get a bit hectic sometimes. Imagine some quirky voice acting from a small cast, and I think the characters would be more memorable like the myriad of games mentioned. *Multiplayer in the form of some spooky mini-games akin to Mario Party or WarioWare would be a nice add for replay value. *Co-Op DLC story? *Oh, and of course a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: What the game did right:- Halloween enviroment, sounds, everything.- Platforming akin to Psychonauts and such- Collectaton challenges that impulse you to explore, challenging enough, not too hard, not too easy.- Skins being unlocked by in-game progression instead of paid DLC.- Conversation humor is on point. Got a chuckle out of me in many moments- Translation seems amazing, can't say much as i've only seen english and portuguese, can't understand the other languages- Weapon variety is cool and interesting, got me changing weapons mid fight to strike cooler combos- Minigames were, most of the time, a good break from the constant combat that gets mundane after a while.What they did wrong:- The only map that had some sort of extra dimension was the war one. The others seem boring and flat. They are amazing looking, sure, but i'm talking about gameplay area. Most of them are like a big ass field with a few objectives here and there and some hidden goodies here and there. it feels "flat".- Combat is either boring and repetitive or absurdly scaled on difficulty outta nowhere. enemies can hit you during your attack or dodge, absolutely no i-frames at all.- Catwalk sections slows you down and disables your double jump. I know what they went for in there, but that made me fall down more than it did on any other game with catwalks where I can just hop with precise jumps.- While some mechanics have a decent "safe enviroment" presentation before appearing again in a challenging one (which is how it should ALWYAS BE), some new mechanics are thrown into you with no prior signaling, and they're always the ones that "GO GO GO RUSH RUSH OH NO YOU'RE DEAD NOW". You gotta guess what the game is expecting from you or just die by trial and error. Horrible conveyance.- Boss battles were cool but too frustrating. Some of them have several stages so if you die in one of them you gotta do the whole thing again. Sure that builds that sweet sweet "git gud" serotonin that you all gamers crave so much, but the way it's presented feels shallow, like the dev did that way to cause you to spend more than 2 hours with the game so you can't refund it.- The portal diving sections, oh god. How the HELL do you go through those legit? I did by sheer luck and always with a shiver of health left, after like a dozen tries. I've seen that diving-dodge mechanic in a lot of other games and they always did it nice, this one sucked at it. Again, bad conveyance. Worst of all, some obstacles can hurt you even before the screen clears up (still blinding white after it starts before it fades in)- The final boss ended up being the easiest of every other boss (except the 1st and the 2nd, those are like baby-difficulty)- Replay value is 0 unless you're an achievement aficionado and want to go for all the skulls, and even then it makes me feel tired just to think going through all that crap all over again.Tl;dr: Game looks cool, sounds cool, is funny, but gameplay is either flat, boring or insanely difficult than it needs to be. always the extremes.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great spooky, seasonal halloween 3D platformer. Some of the highlights are the art/design, music, theme and boss battles. If you like 3D platforming found in games like Banjo Kazooie / Tooie, Donkey Kong 64, Spyro, Mario, croc, etc, then you will likely like this. The combat could use some improvements; Jack feels really nice to control, but some of the enemies don't quite react how I'd  expect them to. Sometimes, the difficultly can be a bit spiky as well as a result of lots of mobs stacking on you - though easy to defeat, if you are unlucky you can get swarmed and die very quickly. This is pretty easy to counter with a lot of the double jump attacks, which tend to do a big aoe, but it does feel a little cheap for what is otherwise a cute and relatively light hearted game.I'd also say that I would've liked to see a larger variety of enemies, with creepy and cool designs - maybe some mini bosses to freshen it up a little? There were only a handful of enemy types and didn't offer too much of challenge (other than the previously mentioned swarming that can occur). I'd prefer less enemies that are tougher, rather than just adding enemies to increase difficulty. Throughout the different levels, there are various mini-games that break up the game play - most of them are fairly basic, but overall are quick and don't overstay their welcome. I'd like to see more interesting/engaging puzzles included in these levels.  The dialogue is a bit hit or miss; some parts got a smile out of me and others made me shake my head, but it was fairly harmless and obviously not meant to be taken too seriously. I really yern for the tongue in cheek humour of Banjo and Kazooie, but even successors like Yooka Laylee fail to really capture the magic of that game. The story here is pretty generic, but again, it's clearly not meant to be a heavily plot driven game.The last criticism is that the levels are quite linear and I wish there were a few more collectibles. I also wish you could load into the levels at certain points in the stage to try and find any collectibles you missed. Note this game doesn't really feel like a collectathon, so your mileage may vary here. I'd love to see a sequel to Pumpkin Jack, maybe getting into more of a collectathon, multiple worlds in the spirit of Banjo Kazooie, which would also give an opportunity for new and creative enemy types. Being able to unlock cool new moves along the way would also be awesome to spice up the combat. Overall I had great fun playing this game, especially during the spooky season. I know I went into a lot of depth regarding my criticism, but they didn't take too much away from my enjoyment and really only stated them that in the hopes there is a sequel, we can get an even better game!

_childDocuments_.review: You're playing as Jack. THE Jack. The one whom the devil didn't want, the one whom we got the Jack-o-lanterns to thank for. Now I'm not intimately familiar with the original mythos. I don't know whether corvid skulls were actually used as lucky charms or whether this is just a game thing to give you a reason to collect them. I wonder about the tone of that legend.It's content surely is whimsical, as is the game. It's got that satisfying fairy-tale-turned-humorously-dark-tone. Think Overlord, think playing evil in Fable.Gameplay-wise, it's a 3D platformer with spectacle fighting & some puzzles interspersed. Now the 3D platforming doesn't have the depth of A Hat in Time and the fighting doesn't compare to masterworks of Platinum or Ninja Theory, but it's absolutely serviceable and it more than makes up with it's charm.Certainly the wrong game to get test your m4d g4m0r sk1llz with, but very certainly the right one to have a good time with.

_childDocuments_.review: - Looks like a polished HD remake late-PS1/early-PS2 game in the best possible way. Like a Spirit Halloween store set up shop in a Spyro level- Lots of spooky theming throughout every level and in every character design- The music follows the same aesthetic (think Golden Era MGM horror movie soundtracks), though there's some interesting takes on classical pieces as well- There isn't much voice work, but the narrator does a good job- In this game, you're play as the bad guy. Your mission is to destroy the world at the devil's bidding. That's the basic gist of the story- The game is pretty endearingly goofy throughout. All the evil you're spreading is done so in an appropriately cartoonish way- As you might expect, this is a great game to play during Halloween season- The controls feel tight and responsive. Combat is okay, but you can cheese most enemies with your ranged attacks- Sometimes in 3D character action platformers, there's just no good solution for the camera. This game tries valiantly to--and largely succeeds at--keeping scenery from obstructing your views, but you'll still find yourself taking hits from enemies you had no chance at seeing and risking blind jumps occasionally- There's a lot of nice variety to the gameplay, much like late 90s/early 00s 3D platformers this game pays homage to. There's on-rails race sequences like Crash Bandicoot, long and challenging platforming sequences like Mario 64, big arena boss fights like Spyro, and goofy humor like Gex- I don't know if I'll ever replay the game, but I enjoyed my time with it- Overall, I'm surprised with the highly polished look and feel of the game. I didn't go in expecting much, but I was really pleased with how high-quality the entire package is- That high quality extends to the game's performance. It ran extremely well in 4k at 60 FPS without taxing my setup too hard. A really nice surprise. Definitely worth at least adding to your wishlist if you're jonesing for a 3D platformer that doesn't overstay its welcome

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed feelings for this game but I will give it a positive review because at the end of the day I had some fun, and I only paid 10 bucks for it.Lets start with the negative ones. The game feels empty most of the times, there is some basic platforming here and there but nothing satisfying and not a lot of enemies. I know this is a platformer and they shouldn't focus on making tons of enemies on each level but when the platforming itself is lacking and there is nothing to collect (except some crow skulls) the level just feels... empty.As for the collectables, they are a joke (i 100% the game in 6 hours) they aren't even hidden most of the times or they are poorly hidden. Other than crow skulls there isn't anything else to collect (except for 1 gramophone in each level)..yea no boxes/coins/wumpa fruits etc etc..The only purpose is to just finish the level.Enemies are not fun simply for the fact that you are not oneshotting them..It's a platforming game, why adding bulky enemies? Last but not least, the price is just ridiculous...The game lasts 5 and around 6 hours if you want to 100% complete it and it doesn't have any replay value..It should cost 5 max 10 bucks, so don't make the mistake to buy it at full price. _childDocuments_.review: 'Tis the season for a Halloween platformer! And at Steam sale $4 price, you really can’t go wrong with Pumpkin Jack. It’s a decidedly goofy game somewhere between Disney’s Haunted Mansion and a Hat in Time that still has enough charm to delight children and adults alike. You play the soul of a famous fantasy rogue in the body of a scarecrow. A wizard is causing chaos and its your job to go beat him up and take his lunch money. The overarching story is less visible. More attention is given to the individual boss of each of Pumpkin Jack’s 6 levels. And those 6 levels are… good! Calling back to platformers of old, each has a visual theme, a boss, and a contained story. Gameplay loops in these levels are well defined and swap between combat and platforming with two instances of on-rails sections and puzzles in each level. Each area is wonderful to look at and fun to navigate. Muted tones and darkened skies really give that seasonal feel and each region even has its own distinctive color hue. Moreover, shoutout to level design for effective use of lighting and props that always give an indication of where to go next and what you can interact with. Also, each section is backtracking friendly, which is huge if you’re going after collectibles (which – bonus points -- have a sound effect when you’re close to them). The only downside is that touching water kills you instantly, there's a lot of it, and the game has a tracker for how many times you died with a snarky comment each time. Combat is the weak link. At the end of each level you get a new weapon and while they all have a sequenced move set… only the shotgun seems more powerful than the others. Combat comes down to buttom mashing hordes of dudes who all drop health when you kill them. I never went back to a previous weapon because once you have a shotgun… why go back to the shovel? It’s even kind of weird because each weapon is linked to a color so I assumed some enemies would only be vulnerable to that color, but no. Bosses, on the other hand, are a highlight. They have interesting, fast paced attack patterns and unique solutions beyond button mashing. They’re visually interesting, dripping with campy characteristics, and punctuate Pumpkin Jack with moments of excitement and thrills. Overall, if you’re looking for a game to scratch that Halloween itch, Pumpkin Jack is an excellent choice – get it on sale for $4 while you can and make it part of your October traditions.

_childDocuments_.review: The characters are cool, the music is alright(some tracks are pretty good, and some feel like stock music), and I like the little "cutscenes" with static artwork. And some of the bosses are okay-ish. That's about the best things I can say about this game.The gameplay is lackluster, the combat is boring and simplistic, and the platforming is stiff and clunky. You're better off ignoring enemies unless you're required to kill them to progress.Most of the game is spent doing third person platforming, which feels clunky, sterile and stiff. You also get sections where you control Jack's head and have to solve "puzzles," these sections don't control or feel much better either, and the objectives are very basic.You also get minecart sections, which feel very inconsecuential and slow, and have very little in the way of challenge. At some point you get to ride a ghost horse, but you quickly realise it's basically just a reskinned minecart section.There are also these sections where Jack balances on wooden beams, they slow the pace of the game to a crawl and take away most of your control of the character, making the game feel even clunkier, and even when it looks like you should be able to just jump straight off the beam onto the next section, you actually can't because when you're on the beams you have zero momentum when you jump, I can't comprehend how anyone thought that was a good idea.This game piqued my interest because it looked cool, but unfortunately it is mediocre at best. _childDocuments_.review: If you’re looking for a game that lets you switch off your brain and offers a nostalgic gameplay experience reminiscent of the PS1 and PS2 era, Pumpkin Jack might be worth considering. Developed almost entirely by solo French developer Nicolas Meyssonnier, this game stands as a tribute to the 3D action platformers of the early 2000’s like Jak and Daxter and MediEvil.The game runs for around five hours, which, while short, feels just right. I didn’t find myself needing more time to walk away feeling satisfied and entertained. From a gameplay perspective, Pumpkin Jack delivers solid, if simple, platforming with enjoyable, straightforward combat, offering the chance to unlock various weapons. Boss fights are classic “learn the pattern and hit three times” affairs, which perfectly align with the game’s aim to emulate the charm of older titles. The graphics, too, are well-executed, fitting the tone and style of the game nicely. I played with no crashes or noticable slowdowns on the Steam Deck with shadows set to low and in DX11 mode.There is also a collectathon element where players can seek out Raven Skulls hidden throughout each level, which can be used to unlock new skins. Fortunately, you can revisit levels later, making the collection process much more manageable.It’s important to temper your expectations - this isn’t a groundbreaking experience. However, going in with the right mindset might even leave you pleasantly surprised. The only element I found a bit off-putting was the overly lengthy dialogue sections, which felt more like unedited filler. The humor could have been delivered with much less text. Additionally, the cutscenes between levels felt somewhat redundant, merely summarizing what had just been played.Overall, Pumpkin Jack offers about five hours of entertaining, nostalgic gameplay. If you’re craving a return to PS1-era roots and set your expectations accordingly, there’s plenty of fun to be had with Pumpkin Jack. The game has its charm, and considering it was made almost entirely by one person, it’s an impressive achievement!

_childDocuments_.review: This is truly a breath of fresh air, an incredible platformer oozing style and personality with extremely high levels of polish and presentation.The level design is absolute chefs kiss. After a constant onslaught of open world this, and procedural that, this feels like an absolute reprieve. It was a delight to jump around linear levels, each is the perfect balance of platforming, combat and exploration with secreted away colletibles in each stage. The collectibles are limited to twenty crows skulls and a single gramophone on each level, the skulls being used to unlock a range of skins for Jack.Most of the levels have a great range of diversions placed throughout to break up the core gameplay, from minecart sections ala Donkey Kong and kart racing-esque sequences, to a wide range of puzzles all of which never feel like a chore and are in fact very fun and palate cleansing.Each level culminates with a boss fight, all of which are incredibly unique and fun.The controls are solid, with great weight and feel. The jumping could definitely aggravate people more used to platformers which allow more in air control, but I enjoy having to really commit to jumps and the double jump and slight in air control is more than enough for any precise course correction. It really adds a feeling of skill and depth when doing precise movements, and I never felt as if the controls were sluggish or let me down.The combat is somewhat simplistic, but enjoyable and never feels like a slog. Small sections of combat is peppered throughout the levels that breaks up the platforming which is of course the focus. Even then it's fun to be given options of different weapons, all with different combos and air attacks, including a sassy talking sword.The art in the game is incredibly well done, a lot of time and love has gone in here and its clear. The character designs are unique, the environment art detailed but not overly noisy, and the general composition all comes together well to a standard usually only seen by the likes of Ninty. And the lighting, good spagat the lighting. Lighting is one of the most important parts of any game, and can take a scene from 5 to 11 easily, but the lighting in this game is absolutely stunning work.The sound design is all very classic platforming fair, but with modern twists and great production, and the soundtrack is great and all meshes with the scenes and game incredibly well.The story is presented extremely well through storybook pages an in game cutscenes, and although usually something I don't care too much for in games like this was actually fairly fun. Especially killing Santa.I know a lot of people are going to moan about the playtime, I just got 100% in the game and clocked about eleven hours, which I think is very much well worth it. Those eleven hours were pure platforming perfection, I'm not going to say things such as 'it didn't overstay its welcome' or any of the sort, this game doesn't set out to be an epic or open world game you will put hundreds of hours into and it would be a crime to fill it with bloat or for people to judge it on that.This developer easily could have spaced this content out more, could have filled it with hundreds of more collectibles, added extra space all over the place, and the fact they didn't shows integrity and makes this game nigh on perfect as a result.I have seriously not enjoyed a game as much as I did this in quite a while, and cannot overstate how much I love the fact the pureness of the gameplay and design. Like Vampire Survivors, it doesn't busy itself with what it could be, or the pressures of modern gaming tropes and as a result is truly something special as a result.If you like platforming shenanigans don't even blink, give the devs your hard earned cash because lord knows they deserve it for this masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie, expected a poor Medievil clone and was very much positively surprised.Props to the design team for capturing this magnificent display of a Halloween world, exactly how it should be.Luscious yet perfectly matching hues of green, orange and purple that harmonize into this brilliant work of art.Adding to the already eyecandylike optics is the high quality original soundtrack repertoire that just emphasizes on all the aspects mentioned before and immerses you even more into this gorgeous looking game.Gameplaywise the game delivers a satisfying experience with a diverse arsenal of weapons (and each of them having unique attack animations).The movement itself looks very fluent the only thing that i think would enhance the general fluidity of motion is if the dodging animation (roll) would be replaced by a dash animation (which would also fit very well with the  item).Definitely a buy recommendation!

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy these "collectathon platformer" games, like Spyro and MediEvil. In fact its resemblance to MediEvil made me interested in the game in the first place. 🙂This one will keep you busy for about 5-6 hours. The level design is great, it somewhat reminds me of Rayman 3.You would not be able to tell, but the game was mostly worked on by just one developer, a very impressive feat!Besides showing how much the developer has managed to do on his own, I like that the credits have various screenshots of how the game looked throughout its development.A few negatives then.Some bosses are not that fun and overstay their welcome a bit too long. One of them even reappears later and you have to beat him in exactly the same way as you did before! 😒As for the collecting aspect: there are 20 collectibles in each level and one hidden extra. Most are not very hard to find or are straight up on the main path. Unfortunately if you've missed one, you typically will not be able to backtrack to get it. Instead you will need to replay the whole level. There are no chapters for levels either. Annoying if you've only missed one or two collectibles like I have.A recommendation then from me! Maybe pick up the game on sale if you have a problem with the game's play time.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and satisfying platformer adventure game 👍It is in spirit a lot like MediEvil, Spyro and Crash - funky characters, linear levels with some puzzles and collectibles along the way.The good:- The level design is great - each section I found easy to navigate and I was never confused about where I need to go next.- The platforming is tight - I never really felt like I'm fighting with controls or can't land a jump because of some reason outside of mi control - good job!- Combat overall is simple, but satisfying. The enemies are easy to understand, but sometimes hit like trucks - you can't just face-tank all the hits - this adds a layer of skill requirement to the fights.- The bosses are a variation of the classic "bonk it 3 times" trope that Nintendo is famous for. Not a bad thing by all means - it works for this type of game!- The writing is decent, the characters are distinct, the jokes and letters are sufficiently funny 👍- Short and Sweet. Does not overstay its welcome and is engaging the whole time.- In this game - we help EVIL win and are stopping the good guys from saving the world - rare is a game that spins it this way :)The bad:- Upon loading, Jack sometimes faced the way I came from, making it a bit confusing for a bit until I realize what happened.- HDR is busted - makes all the colors extremely saturated, there's a lot more contrast to everything. I read that it's the DX12 version that's wrong and DX11 is supposed to work fine in HDR, but my Steam Deck OLED would just not load in DX11 no matter what (selecting through the launcher, adding launch commands...) - so I had no way to experience this particular game in HDR.- A few of the pumpkin head puzzles seemed more annoying than they should be. Particularly the ones where you have to roundhouse-whack things to fill up a bar/gauge...the speed at which those bars deplete passively can be annoying...- Would have preferred an in-game option to toggle chromatic aberration off. That effect just makes things unnecessarily blurry.- I understand that Jack is extremely afraid of water for whatever reason - but is it necessary that small  ankle-high puddles insta-kill him?Suggestions:- Add a chromatic aberration menu toggle- Fix HDR- The game could REALLY benefit from a some good voice acting. Someone grungy and creepy for Jack, some spirit-like voices for the other characters - it would probably rule. Think Hades.Overall - an enjoyable little game for a few sit-downs that leaves you accomplished in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game and a fine addition to 3D action platformers. A good game designer knows how to make a game fun. A great game designer knows how to keep a game from being frustrating and great care is shown in that regard, especially in comparing it to its 1990's cohort. It knows when to slow itself down, though sometimes this can feel a bit over-earnest. Crossing the narrow beams takes Jack to a slow creep, allowing a much easier crossing than just sending it over a 200' drop and falling over and over. The mobile setpieces like the gargoyles and minecarts seem as if they were originally intended to be much faster but have been slowed to be more approachable. If you're not having any trouble with these parts, it can seem pretty slow but it also makes it accessible (except for the portal fall which serves as an exercise in smashing into everything on screen). Platforming is tight and movement is predictable, even when the camera moves out. Movement and jumping never felt like a chore. Collectible hunting also falls into an accessible category with each easy to find as long as you keep on the lookout, no need to whack invisible walls or break every crate you see. The combat is straightforward and easy at first but when the game starts throwing a multitude of enemies at you with some painful attacks, it keeps itself interesting. I did wish there were further usecases for the six weapons. There's really no reason not to just rely on the magic sword or shotgun the entire game after you unlock them and it could've benefit from enemy weaknesses or more specialized uses for each weapon (aside from the spear which is specialized in sending you flying off the boss arena/ferry and directly into the water as a convenient suicide button). That said, the weapons are fun and each feels punchy and impactful. The boss fights are pretty solid with some fun mechanics, though many are reused between them, and the setpiece acts are enjoyable and driving, though often used perhaps one too many times each. Being a nearly-solo project, this is understandable and well pulled off.The artstyle is a real delight and it's always nice to be looking at as you move through the worlds. They fit well into the spooky Halloween theme and make great use of light, something especially useful in good game design. Not only was the world well contrasted but I also always knew where I was going and places worth seeing. Characters are well designed and expressive in their movement and Jack feels tough even in the way he moves. The music arrangement also fits the bill, using the right instruments to make it feel spooky and keep up with the theme without being overpowering. The writing is short and sweet, charming enough to bring a smile without being annoying or cringe-inducing. I'd call it kid-friendly, refraining from being crass.Overall, it was a fun experience and I think it could be enjoyed by anyone regardless of skill or ability. I'd love to see more of Pumpkin Jack in the future and believe all the core concepts here not only work well but could be improved even further. And hey, much like A Nightmare Before Christmas, it can also serve as a Christmas game. Double trouble!

But it feels like they peaked on the second level, the rest didn't really live up to it, and the last 3 levels were "ok" at best.Where Pumpkin Jack excels (and I mean excel) is the art design and graphics. The writing was good too, although nothing to write home about, and I liked the overall soundtrack.I'd give this game a 7.5/10, and would highly recommend it on a sale if you're looking for another 3D platformer to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a very fun and beautiful game. Also, a perfect release date right in time to get you in the Halloween mood and absolutely worth the money.Pro's:- Well paced game with a good mix of combat, mini-games, and story cutscenes- The environments look fantastic- Mini games and bosses are very creative- Soundtrack is eerie and whimsical- Incredibly impressive that one person made this thing!Con's:- As with most of these types of games, the combat can be a bit repetitive- The weapon system/inventory doesn't make a lot of sense as you get better weapons each level and there's really no no need to switch to a lesser weapon- I despised everything about the Swamp level
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Fun collectathon! Collectables are well placed and the combat and platforming are fun.-The art and music are very nice, and even at the parts where I wasn't having the most fun I was still able to enjoy looking around and listening to all the songs and ambient effects.-The bosses, while somewhat formulaic, were pretty interesting to fight.-The story was engaging and original, and I liked the characters a lot. Jack himself has some pretty good lines.Cons:-It's pretty short-- it only took just under 5 hours to 100% it. There is replay value in the form of speedrunning modes, though.-A couple annoying glitches involving aspect ratio, where my game would basically change resolutions every time I died and basically reload the application every time there was a loading screen.-While some of the minigames throughout the levels were pretty fun and interesting, others were just annoying to play, either due to wonky camera positions or controls that can only be described as painful on the wrists. All in all, while not perfect, it's a fun game and a noteworthy feat for a solo developer! I don't know about the full price considering the amount of content, but if you buy it on sale (I paid $15 myself) I'd say it's definitely worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Like Crash Bandicoot wrapped in the skin of Medievil, Pumpkin Jack is a spooky yet lighthearted romp that will certainly appeal to anyone who enjoys 3D action platformers. The game never takes itself too seriously and every level is full of different mechanics and simple puzzles that only rarely overstay their welcome, keeping the action relatively fresh and the pacing brisk. This framework reminded me quite a bit of It Takes Two. The art design and style are traditional gloomy Halloween fare, though cozy, vibrant, and never frightening. I really liked the look of the characters too, especially the witch's husband and Jack himself. The controls were satisfactory with snappy camera movement, quick combat and responsive dodge rolls, and weighty jumping; the weapons that make you float off the ground were disorienting, however. I also believe this game would function as an effective entry point for children into 3D action platformers, helping to ease them into understanding simplistic mechanics that are staples of the genre. It only took me about 3 and a half hours to beat so I would recommend it on sale, as the $30 price point is steep. Other than that, Pumpkin Jack was a great time and a commendable effort from the developer.

_childDocuments_.review: Very casual recommend. I wouldn't recommend to pay full price of almost $30, but a deep sale maybe. I bought it through humble subscription so that price I'm fine with.If you know what to expect from this genre of game then you'll know what to expect both good & bad. I'm not really into this genre of games that much anymore, but this game has a theme I like - pumpkin head dude who's kinda evil... in a bright colorful cute most-ages way. If you can control it well enough to keep going then you're old enough for the story.I generally hate platforming, especially in 3D, and this game has many sections of platforming, however it does it competently. In most of the the exploration sections of the game you have control over the camera and all the time you need to rotate it if needed for a better view.The combat you CAN basically button mash your way through which will do a repeating 3 attack combo, but each weapon has a variety of attacks. like after a roll, or during a double jump. Through regular play you unlock a fair variety of weapons you can choose from at a button that feel different.There are frustrations. DIAS Gameplay. (Do It Again, Stupid)Jack is another adventurer who sinks like a rock and insta-dies. Sometimes you want to explore to the side of the main path and can't tell how deep the water is.There's a maze section that the clue leads you believe the opposite of what you need to do. If you go the wrong way you insta-die and start the maze over. You can go the wrong way before you even enter that maze and insta-die essentially upon entering a level instead of putting yet another invisible wall these games love so much everywhere else.During some of the other sections the camera can be an issue. There are magic horse riding sections that are sort of corridors navigating, jumping over, and shooting barriers. The final boss has an attack  The camera angle can make it difficult to judge where you need to be to not get damaged.Overall the level design is fun for the mostly linear with small side areas hiding raven skulls. There's different outfits to purchase for the collectible raven skulls. If you're the type you can do a level select and replay a specific level to try to collect the rest.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, what a cozy, "familiar" game. I'm going to recommend this game because overall I enjoyed my time with it, but my recommendation comes with a couple caveats.Let me talk about what I liked, because there's quite a bit. For someone who grew up in the 90s/00s and played a lot of platformers like Spyro, Mario, Sonic, and some various GBA/DS ones, this feels warm and cozy. It's not a terribly difficult game, and I don't think it's meant to be. I died 16 times going for 100%, and 14 of those were instant death pits or water. The general atmosphere feels Halloween-y enough. The writing is silly like a kid's game (barring a couple curse words iirc), a simple adventure like a 90s/00s platformer.  The music and sound design are great. There's some simple combat elements to the game, every level you unlock a new weapon and you can swap between them at any time. It was a nice touch, and I liked most of them.Each level plays similarly but also varies enough to keep the game fresh and distinguish from each other: A different "theme" with a couple sets of minigames/activities sprinkled within, an easy one early on and then a slightly more challenging one later on. They don't take up too much time and they vary from level to level so I had fun with them. The bosses at the end are also pretty creative and follow a familiar formulaic pattern: Get in 3 rounds of attacking and win. It reminded me of some of the platformers I played growing up. Achievements are also easy to get, just 100% the game and you'll get them all. Now the caveats. $30 for a game that can be 100%'d in ~5 hours with almost no replayability and doesn't do anything "remarkable" to stand out is a strong ask in my opinion. The other caveat is the replayability factor, or lack of in this case. Besides getting the rest of the skulls to unlock skins and finding the phonographs to watch Jack get boogy with it, there's no real incentive to replay. Unlike, say, Spyro where there were minigames that you could get high scores in, and the levels were somewhat non-linear with plenty of pickups that you didn't need to finish the game. As well, If Pumpkin Jack did something outstanding (like say, To the Moon's story being known for bringing people to tears) or added more optional content/co-op, I'd gladly recommend it at full. These caveats aren't meant insult the game's design; not every game needs to be ground-breaking. Ultimately, this is a fun, nostalgic and "cozy" Halloween-themed experience, and I would recommend it if you grew up playing platformers and/or want a fun themed one, but not at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a fun (and unforgiving) platformer game that makes you really want to work towards the ending.Somehow- and I have no idea how -the developer behind PJ has managed to use the exact same format for every single level in the game and still keep it interesting. It's hard not to notice the repeating themes; an escape sequence where you're stuck on a set path, a minecart ride where you're stuck on a set path, a gargoyle kidnapping where you're stuck on a set path; each level is exactly the same but entirely different in its own right, and at the end of each one you get a weapon that is far better than your current.I believe one way PJ kept me interested was those death screens, stuff like the owl telling me "Hoo-hoo, 102 deaths, Jack? This is going on your report." made me want to jump through that portal one more time and give the final boss another go.Overall it's a great game with a great story, stellar graphics (even on lowest settings) and characters you'll find hard to forget.Especially Charon. God I love that guy.

_childDocuments_.review: What do you get when you cross generic platforming with a slightly spooky aesthetic and slap a silly story to it? Well, I'd imagine you'd end up with something like , provided you weren't looking for something actually good. Welcome to another review where I cite a video game for being too problematic to deserve recommendation. Sheesh, this is starting to become a running gag for me, and I'm not sure how I feel about that.To start things off a smoothly as possible,  is a clunky 3D platformer about Jack, a damned soul that the Devil has brought back to ensure that the world remains doomed. That's it. That's the whole plot. It's a platformer, so any degree of plot depth puts it leagues ahead of Super Mario without breaking a sweat. As far as I'm concerned that means that this thing gets a pass for having some sort of story to follow. It's relatively short, and can be completed in around 6 hours or so.Now, the mechanics are... unrefined? Yes, that seems like a good word for it. While it functions adequately as a platformer, it definitely shows weakness in how finicky the boundaries of traversable land is laid out. Some boxes are well established while some require an irritating amount of precision to land successfully with no rhyme or reason to their placement. This leads to an overly frustrating experience of hoping that you can actually land on a platform since the game's basic flow is an elaborate game of . Most of that can be chalked up to the fact that an overwhelming majority of the game was made by a single person, and that kind of polish is entirely absurd to expect from a single developer. Ultimately it doesn't detract from the game being generally enjoyable, but it does make for more frustration than is deserved of any player. What also pushed the title further from  and closer to  would be its unfinished forced travel mechanics. In each of the many stages you're forced into linear travel sequences that function on a bare-bones level to tie zones together. So you're forced to spam two buttons and hope that the game actually does what you want it to without any expectation that it would function adequately enough to count for a success. Again, with the constraints of this game being made by basically a single person, I can understand a bit of the messy mechanics, but not for the base price tag. Mind you, I received this game through Humble Choice, but that doesn't diminish how problematic the hefty price of this game is. One thing I cannot forgive, however, is the heavy-handed use of public domain music with the price tag that this title boasts. I don't know exactly how many times I had to stop for a brief moment and mentally verify that yes, indeed,  or a moderately stylized version of Beethoven's  was playing in the background where it didn't quite belong. Again, I can forgive some corners cut for the sake of finishing a project, even from a single indie developer, but it was usually out of place and made zero sense within the context of what was playing on the screen in front of me. may very well be one of the problematic titles that fits into neither recommended nor not recommended. As an independent title I feel morally obligated to give it some degree of leeway, but its unpolished nature and aggressive use of public domain music leave it squarely in the sights of an overpriced heap of refuse. Look, I'm trying to be as diplomatic as I can about this one, but a spade is a spade, alright?

_childDocuments_.review: Downvoting for one specific reason: No way this game is worth $30.I didn't do my research, and that's on me. I got it on sale, but I already forgot how much. I think I paid $20 for it, and it isn't even worth that.I started it up tonight, and earned 9/33 achievements in 1 hour. That got me wondering about how long it would take to beat the game...According to the Internet, it takes 6.5 hours for 100% completion, 4 hours if you ignore collectibles. I have a simple personal metric for a game's value:$1 per hour of gameplay. If I pay $60 for a brand new, Triple-A title, I expect 60 hours of gameplay. If I pay $30 for an indie, small-team game, I expect 30 hours of gameplay.But SIX-AND-A-HALF!? You're absolutely bonkers if you think that's worth $30.As for the game itself, it's cute. Simple so far, requires a lot of precision and timing. That is made more difficult by the camera being too far from the character, and by the cartoony colors and weak shading that makes depth perception really difficult. If the average player beats the game in 4 hours, though, I don't expect it to get any more difficult than it is now.Pass on this until you can get it for about $5, or $10 at most.

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a half hack-n-slay, half 3D platformer. It comes with okay music and graphics. The story is largely irrelevant, doing more to develop avatar Jack's relations with others than drive a compelling narrative. The game's medium length should have helped concentrate on a lower number but strangely effective level themes, i.e. the few main levels are consistent and entertaining - sort of variability is low among levels but high enough within a level.+ okay music and graphics+ medium length+ mostly good controls with keyboard+mouse or controller+ okay variability of levels+ boss fights pretty standard with some interesting elements+ collectibles+ level selector0 irrelevant storyline0 some mini-games outright annoying, all on repetition- on-rails segments not optimised for keyboard+mouse controls- try-and-error mazeThe different levels come with a few mandatory mini-games (on-rails stuff, musical Simon, lever puzzles etc.). Some of them are outright annoying (tactical rubber-band cart racing) and all of them have zero replay value. Fortunately, you will only redo them to find remaining collectibles. A level selector comes with the status of most collectibles.Each level has a gramophone which offers a short rewarding interruption.Altogether, Pumpkin Jack was entertaining enough and pretty close to what I was looking for to play at the time. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I know the time played is short, but I had to set down the controller and come write a review.   It has been a LONG time since I've played a game like this, Pumpkin Jack is an absolute pitch perfect PS1/PS2 era platformer (And if you were there in the PS1/PS2 era you know that comes as high praise!)  This is Crash Bandicoot.  This is Jak and Daxter.  This is Rachet and Clank.  Spyro.  Gex.  Psychonauts.  Bubsy before it was 3D and bad.  I don't know what to tell you except that I'm a 36 year old man who was grinning like he was 13 again.   I'm not great at game reviews, but here's what I can tell you:    - The controls are perfectly tight   - Interesting level design and puzzles   - The gameplay is simple, but challenging   - Lots of hidden MacGuffins, and rewards for collecting them!   - The graphics are gorgeous, I've taken about fifty screen shots so far.   - The music is understated, but atmospheric, and perfectly fitting the scene.  At $29.99, currently $23.99 on sale, I think it was a good purchase.  It's not every day one steps into a time machine, and it's even rarer that the past lives up to the memory.  This is a really fun game, a simple, old school with modern refinements, fun game.   Edit: Just to add, if you're too young to remember the glory days of the PS1 and PS2, or the golden era of 3D platforming, I'd still encourage you to give this game (or its demo) a try.  The gameplay is simple and straightforward, allowing the player to focus more on enjoying the action than worrying about micromanaging multiple systems or min/maxxing to the third decimal point, it's a game that focuses on fun.  I guess what I'm trying to say that this game is a diamond in the rough, it achieves what so many other games today fail to do, it's just a joy to play, it's FUN, and I put that word in capitol letters for a reason.  In a world of Dark Souls, sometimes it's fun to pick up a Super Mario Bros.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so glad I stumbled upon this game. Pumpkin Jack is right up my alley by having a similar art style and features to ps2 and the sp2 game Sly. I love the Halloween theme of it and the random pop culture references, and the witty interactions with the various creatures Jack encounters on his way to get the damn annoying wizard. The mummy selling Jack skins has to be my favourite, 10/10 for being a disturbing but totally honest (maybe too honest) salesman. Your loyal crow buddy has NO FEAR, until there is a scarecrow....Having the ability to change skins and weapons throughout the game makes the game a true 10/10 for me. I love the fun of having to race against 3 knights who hates their job, drive a minecart like a rollercoaster where there is a higher chance of dying than normal, and try not to get drowned by the ferry owner that I repetitively forced to give me a free ride to the other side of the water, and to ride or more like fly??? a dead horse without getting hit by that damn annoying wizard's spells. Oh, I also love when I have to twist my own neck to make my pumpkin head fall off so I can do "smaller" tasks so I can blow crap up that is in my way and ruin the fun for the monsters I'm up against.The game is a bit short yes, BUT you can spend up to an hour and more on one level if you really try to look for all the crow skulls and destroy every breakable or killable thing you find. The story teller between levels is awesome to listen to, like damn what a voice to own, and it's cool that you follow Jack's story through the levels in a drawn design, just like you´re reading about his stories alongside experiencing them. #OffBrandDisneyStoryTelling. We HAVE TO appreciate the AWESOME skeleton band at the graveyard level. Spotify hit em´ up. Another HUGE PLUS when it comes to music, is that you can find record players that Jack does a swag asf dance to that makes the other monsters rather wanna battle him with guns over dancing, because they know they would be doomed if so, or rather more doomed.If you like colorful and halloween like games, this game will hit home. Time well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: For a team this small, Pumpkin Jack is really a good game, but the reason I do not recommend it is because it's way too expensive for a game this short. I'm currently in the fourth level and I returned to the menu to buy skins, and afterwards I checked the level select option and saw there were only 2 levels left until i beat the game! I know the team is small, but there are ways of solving this issue without giving the game a longer playtime:1) You can make each level have a unique gimmick or different mechanics. I think you really need to learn a few things from 3d platformers that were made back in the 2000s.2) I know you've tried to spice things up with mine cart and ghost horseback rides but I really felt that they were boring, both of them had you jumping and breaking the obstacles occasionally, but it provided absolutely zero challenge. There should've been more obstacles, for example in the mine cart ride you could've tilted your cart left or right in order to avoid running into stuff, or move your horse so you dont crash into something, but those "on rails" instances were so linear and boring. 3) Combat could be a lot more fun too. Right now it's just button mashing and dodging, and you rarely run out of health. Even if you do, there are millions of health pickups around and checkpoints in almost every 5 minutes. I died like 10 times but it was always by falling off a ledge, which brings me to;4) TIGHT CONTROLS! This is a PLATFORMER guys! You can't make a platformer with sluggish jumps, jumping is the KEY to any platformer game! I can't count how many times I had a hard time trying to control my movements mid air to land on difficult ledges. The jumps really aren't that hard, but the controls make them a lot harder than they should be! The jumping height is also another problem for me, my character feels so heavy. Attacking things is another drag, it should be way more fluid and fast, not "standing still and swinging whatever weapon you have".  5) If you're using double jump for every platforming you do, then you don't really need a double jump. Unfortunately this is the situation. Double jumping should be used to jump wider gaps and maybe reach some high ledges. But here, the normal jump is sooo low that every time I jump, I use double jump; rendering the normal jump useless.6) Finally, the soundtrack felt somewhat good in the beginning but you really shouldn't have went with spooky covers of classical music pieces. When I first heard Ride of the Valkyries in the mine cart ride I was like "ok, they made a spooky cover" but afterwards I heard more and more covers of other classical music! This really feels lazy, an original score would be much, much better even if it wasn't exactly a "masterpiece". Again, I know Pumpkin Jack has a small team and maybe we shouldn't expect this much from a game, but so does Hollow Knight, Celeste, Undertale and many other games. They have a small team but they focus on how to make the game "fun". Pumpkin Jack is a really good idea, but it lacks fun for the moment. And it's way too overpriced.Long story short, you should give this game a try if it's on sale like maybe 5-10 dollars. But 30 dollars is too much for this game.
