_childDocuments_.review: A game released and  to be played during Halloween, this short (~5 hours) but sweet game has you take on the role of Jack the Pumpkinman who returns to the mortal realm to wreak havoc and help the evil forces of the world defeat the good guys, once and for all.Pumpkin Jack is a 3D platformer that has simple but satisfying controls that leads to a very smooth gaming experience with a really nice flow. To attack your foes, you'll only be using LMB (faster/weaker attack), RMB (secondary attack) and jump button + LMB (stronger/slower aerial attack). The maps are well designed, which makes the platforming aspect of the game give you a good feeling.The game has a very clear progression system in the form of getting better weapons. Every new weapon you get actually feels like an upgrade over the previous one. You are free to swap between weapons as much as you wish though, so yes, for you hardcore folk, you can play the whole game with the starting weapon.The only parts that can get a bit dull are the scripted sequences, where your character is moving forward automatically and your controls are limited to jumping over incoming obstacles + dodging them with movement keys, however only one of them felt too long.The visuals of this game as a whole are absolutely stunning that will have you stopping and admiring it very often. I bow my head in respect to the small group of developers who made this game, the results are fantastic and the screenshots on the store page are nice, but they  don't do it justice. All the areas of the game are in settings that are very suitable for Halloween as are most of the enemies you meet. If your go-to jam is spooky countryside, haunted mine, dark forest, graveyard etc, then this game is for you.Once you take control of your character and meet the first npc, you'll realise that there is no voice-acting for the characters, instead they make short noises. At first I was unsure what to make of it, but as the game progressed, it didn't bother me and I actually started liking it, as the main characters all had unique noises that they make.The sound effects are suitable for this kind of setting.If you've made it this far, congratulations, as I've left the best part as last. If you are a Halloween fanatic like me and love Halloween style spooky music, then you are in for a treat! From the moment you start the game, you realise that if anyone asked what's Halloween music, you can just play them this soundtrack. There seems to be a mixture of original and borrowed music in this game. Quite a few of the areas have classical pieces of music, but they're with a Halloweeny twist, which only makes them that much cooler! -- I found none, which makes for an even more enjoyable gaming experience.Pumpkin Jack is a game that lives up to its name in every possible way. I have the utmost respect and appreciation for the mastermind behind this game. Halloween is often treated as a DLC or a smaller side area in games but never the central subject as is the case for this game. I recommend buying this game with two thumbs up, especially when there's a juicy discount going on.PS - if the devs happen to read this, you need to do a Christmas/winter holiday themed game next. ;)

_childDocuments_.review: $30? Are we being for real right now? Thank god for Humble Bundle, do not pay full price for this game, not even half if you can manage it.Wonderful artistic direction with really smooth platformer gameplay completely drowned out by some of the worst writing I've experienced in a long time mixed with baffling music choices. Whenever it's not the actual OST (which is wonderfully atmospheric) and instead some sort of remixed, royalty free classical piece straight from a 90s family friend movie I was this |-| close to alt+F4-ing. _childDocuments_.review: It surprises me how well recommended this game is. There's a lot of passion and soul poured into this Halloween themed adventure game, but the execution feels basic and flawed. On paper this should be right up my alley as an action adventure platformer in the style of that PS2 era, but having finished the game, I ended up forcing myself to see it through and never truly connecting. With all the love and intentions, I feel the quality just isn't good enough.Starting with the best: graphics. Art direction is beautiful and original, and the pastoral cartoon style is great. The inclusion of ray tracing and dlss combined with beautiful stylized water shaders and many colored light sources (of the purple red and green etc. variety) really achieves beautiful pictures in many locations. But some areas especially ones filled with basic wooden rafts and beams and grass are less charming and quite basic, the grass especially is plentifully used in the first area but is too basic to elevate the environment to interesting levels. And that carries on to everything. At best, the environments can be very pretty and unique, but on average, they are mostly just decent, repetitive and do little to inspire exploration.The music is Halloween themed takes on known classical scores and Halloween tunes. I personally didn't connect, while the music is varied, it is far too predictable and very little is done to make it stand out. It's almost tiresome more than it is enjoyable or okay to listen to, especially with some tracks during the "running" gameplay sections.The gameplay itself consists of platforming and combat with puzzles mixed in.The game becomes predictable and repetitive very quickly.The core mechanics are too basic. The platforming is floaty, you have a double jump, ledge climb and that's it, as the game progression continues nothing is added and the basic platforming doesn't become any more interesting. Owing to the floaty controls and minimal animation, it does not feel satisfying to me personally, more like just something you have to do to keep moving. The combat isn't much better. Feedback from enemies us poor, impact is lackluster and while the game here does do something to change things up by adding new weapons with different visuals, the novelty quickly wears off and all the weapons don't really stand out other than with looks and animations, which are at least pretty.The puzzles for the most part feel like a chore besides maybe 2. Every level has a type and it's repeated 3 times. This is a theme in my review, you can start to see at this point. Predictability is something everything in the game follows to the point of boredom and it feels like you've seen and done the mostly just "decent and okay" things this game has to offer from the first 10 minutes.Basic Combat, then platforming, usually boring puzzle, boring walk slow over beam part, boring "runner" part (in a cart, grabbed by a gargoyle etc.). The levels are structured too much to repeat these patterns without feeling dynamic. It becomes a chore.I suppose there's a story but it doesn't really matter as you know exactly how I'd describe it - boring and predictable.My recommendation is don't even bother. It's too basic and not well executed enough, search elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want an old school 3D platformer action collect-a-thon game, go play Psychonauts 2 (go play that regardless of what you do with this game). This, however, is not quite up to its price tag.The combat lacks any tactility. Nothing staggers, everything is spongy, and it just feels like it's time to mash a button again. The platforming just feels slightly off, though I can't place precisely why. The humor is ham fisted at times (although sometimes that is deliberate in this style), and hamstrung by the lack of voice acting at others. By that I mean text based quips during an action sequence takes away from either the dialogue or the action, and there's no real way around it short of writing exclusively for stationary or slow moving scenes, or doing it with audio.Despite that, I enjoyed it overall. It's good enough to like what it wants to be, but not good enough to say that it achieved those goals as effectively as it could have.Ultimately, it's a game I would recommend just to encourage further development in this genre, but even so, at this price point, it's just mediocre enough to recommend against it. Catch it on a solid sale and it may justify itself, but you still may find it overly lacking if you're expecting old Rare, Double Fine, Insomniac, Naughty Dog, or Crystal Dynamics here. Baring in mind what it is, it's worth a discounted look, but I can't recommend it without that caveat.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know what to think of when I booted this up but as I started playing I instantly fell in love with all the little details in the graphics, story, dialogue, and music. The game has this homage like mix of all kinds of different playstation 1&2 era platformers such as MediEvil, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro, Jak & Daxter, and many more. This was a solo developer project and it shows that there was a lot of love and care put into the project. The colors are vibrant where they need to be to create a unique and interesting world. The characters are memorable and have some pretty snappy sarcastic dialogue. The music is inventive and catchy. There are some spooky remixes of familiar songs that go along great with the action going on. The bosses and enemies are diverse with their own patterns. The game is primarily action adventure platformer but once or twice per level it throws in a puzzle. Across the six stages you'll encounter different characters, bosses, enemies, weapons, and puzzles. There are even collection items to find to unlock various spooky outfits. The game is one of those cases of high quality for a bit of steep price. Casually going through the game for me took about 4.5 hours and the only thing left is to go through and collect things for extra costumes. I can't say that's a major bad thing in my book because I'll go through again collect everything and probably eventually dust this one off to replay (especially around Halloween) but if a game that will probably take you under 5 hours to non completionist complete offsets you than it may be for you. Aside from that the only gripe I can say I had which is really minor is the combat was a bit lacking. It's fun enough and introduces a new weapon each stage but I guess with the era of more complicated fight mechanics I was just hoping for more diversity in my battles aside from mostly just running up and slash till dead mechanic. Maybe it's honestly meant to be more a callback to the classic days of combat that followed similar mechanics. All in all this is a fantastic project and I really enjoyed every minute of it. It's a fun twist to play the bad guy. The game knows the many platformers and adventure games that came before it and steps out as it's own project that seems to be influenced from the many available. As mentioned above this may take you around 5 hours to clear so if that price is offsetting to you than I would wait for a sale; but the quality and attention that's put into this game makes me want to call it one of my games of the year for 2020. _childDocuments_.review: My let's play series for Pumpkin Jack:For anyone who misses 3D Platformers and relishes whenever a good Halloween themed game comes around like I do, I think you're going to find a lot to like with Pumpkin Jack.Pumpkin Jack feels like we traveled back to the PS2 era and found a hidden gem of a 3D Platformer. It's colorful and vibrant, has an interesting story, it's really fun to play AND it's Halloween themed! This basically ticks all the boxes for me, so I'm going to cut to the chase here and just say I really like this game and if anyone of those things sound good to you, then I think you will too!I said in one of my let's play videos for the game that for a Halloween game to come out and actually be of this high caliber quality is rare. Normally we get those shovelware, jump scare style games that you'll play for maybe 5 minutes before uninstalling it.However, you can hell the TLC that went into this game and I really hope that means they'll be able to do a sequel for it.There are a couple minor things with the game that I would probably change, like adding voice over for the dialog and adding in better indicators for the leaning in the mine cart areas, but like I said, these are more preferential or minor and won't effect your enjoyment too much.Have fun and Happy Halloween!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't hate this game, but since Steam still doesn't allow us to post neutral reviews, I'm going to have to say this game didn't impress me.Pumpkin Jack is a linear 3D platformer with light hack-n-slash elements scattered along the way. It's not really that bad, but there are a number of frustrations all through the game's playtime. Combat sections tend to have lots of enemies, including ranged ones, and often result in simply button-mashing the attack button until all the enemies are dead. There are candles throughout the levels that start fires when destroyed, but those fires never go out; so if you accidentally start a fire on a platform you need to climb on, you just have to get burned and eat the damage. There are also tightrope sections in each level that really only exist to pad the game's playtime. Each level has some sort of chase/driving section which starts off interesting in the first few levels, but get more annoying in some of the later ones. On top of everything, the game has a relatively short playtime.Ultimately, I have to emphasize that I don't hate this game, but I think there are more downsides than upsides. Other 3D platformers such as A Hat in Time or even something like Hell Pie are more worth looking into than this.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game for the first time! Took me roughly ~6 hours and I missed 5 achievements. (Couple skulls from the first 3 levels, full closet and official groupie, gonna go hunt those in a minute.)Quick verdict: Buy while in sale, it's a blast and you can literally sink your evening into it if you have the time to be Pumpkin Jack! (And even if you don't have an evening to plow through it, you can literally quit at any points and not go back far!) There was love, time and effort put in this game and it deserves your time if you enjoy platformers, I promise.[SPOILERS AND CRAZY RAMBLINGS AHEAD!]The games visual and music are wonderful, as long as they don't rip off or rather riff on existing properties. (Even if they're in the free library by now due to how old they are.)There are few places where your inner gamer says "oh, there might be something there", only to realize that no, you weren't supposed to go there! Thankfully the game is super generous with the check points so I really appreciate the fact that there's not that much penalty if you do happen to slip somewhere where you weren't supposed to. QA/QC did a great job vetting the usual troublesome places you'd get stuck. (I found couple myself but hey, I too am a QA so it's no wonder, and thankfully I didn't get stuck in them either.)The collectibles are being hinted at if you look around enough. Most of the mini games are fun! Some are... Well, to put it slightly, feeling like content padding.  I also feel the same way from the beams that are peppered in the levels. It'd be alright if they'd be there for the collectibles but it feels odd for the game to grab you by the scruff and tell you to "slow down". Weren't we in a hurry to find the champion and beat their buttox?? I get it, it's pacing and ensuring the levels load properly in the distance but come on~...Ferry man also felt like a padding with how slow they move, I loved the swamp couple but man was the boss a drag... And about bosses, OH ABOUT BOSSES..! The final boss doesn't feel like it was tested enough due to the second last attack before they starts to load up their final one. The placements of the holes you need to jump/dodge through can spawn on top of the crevasses and you'll either have to have the HP to take the hit or WISH you can react quickly enough that you don't plummet down into the icy waters. (Made me be thankful the game doesn't have a deathless run...) I thought Glutton was Dhor reborn, man did I feel silly after beating him and getting the context clues since it's SUPER HARD TO FOLLOW THE DIALOGUE WHILE YOU'RE TRYING TO DODGE FOR PETE'S SAKE!! (Yes, I knew it was about the sins but come on, I thought you'd get the statue after re-beating him!)The weapons you get from the bosses are cool though! It's nice when you can choose your own play style, but the unfortunate setback is the fact that newer weapons can be stronger... Except when they're not. The Boom Stick is the best weapon by far thanks to it's range and almost required in the last level at all times to reach the enemies. Sure, you get the crows but... Eeeeehhhhhh, they're not that great unfortunately. ;w;'Quick tip: At the graveyard, you don't need to break EVERY tombstone... The achievement is for the minigame. Stress levels were high for real for thinking I had missed one or two in the open. Probably would've finished the game an hour earlier at minimum...Ok, I won't spoil further! 8.5 / 10! Absolutely charming and fun time. :3c

_childDocuments_.review: This is an action game, where we play as an “evil” force, making our way through the enemies, puzzles and crazy races.We play as Jack - an evil soul of the trickster selected by Devil himself to be his champion. Our mission is to prevent the defender of the humans from seizing the Devil’s power and stopping the curse casted into the land. Being dead long ago Jack’s soul is bound to the artificial body made from wood with the pumpkin head, resembling a famous character from the “Wizard of Oz” book.The story is a sort of fairy tale parody, where the commonly “good” guys appear as actual evil, while evil incarnate actually saves the day. It does create a good impression, but it is far behind the famous “Overlord”/”Overlord 2” series.The combat system is quite simple. The melee attacks are chained into a combo, but just a single one. The jump attacks create some diversity, but usually they are useless. To avoid the incoming attacks we can use dodge and jumps.The weapon selection is disappointing. Technically the variation is good: the shovel, the sword, the shotgun, the magic ball. But we acquire each new weapon at the beginning of the new mission, and the one we get is usually the best suited for the current mission ahead and will become obsolete or useless in the next one. In result we always go with what we just got without any sense of switching to something we used before.Nevertheless the battles are quite challenging and interesting. The enemies are mostly the same through the entire game, but each new type of opponent appears in the new chapter adding to the total stack.The bosses are quite challenging, each is unique and requires special tactics to be beaten.There are mini games, which we participate in as a pumpkin head only without the rest of the body. Although the game does not provide any clear explanation why we have to do it this way, it creates a nice diversity in the gameplay. Usually the mini games are about solving puzzles, like navigating a bomb through a labyrinth. But towards the end they reduced to hitting the switches in a quick succession, which is quite disappointing.There are also races: carriage, horse riding and so on. During these events we navigate through the environment at high speed, avoiding obstacles. Some of those are fun, the other - tedious.Despite there being 3 different gameplay aspects, the game lacks evolving: it just repeats itself in the same pattern: fight, puzzle, race, boss, repeat. Sailing the boat with the ghost ferryman also appears several times. Towards the end there is a growing feeling of “been there, done that”.The game has cartoon styled graphics. It creates a good atmosphere, but it lacks the details. It is hard to put a finger on it, but there is a feeling of visuals lacking polishing. Also while the environment looks acceptable, the characters look rough. Jack’s extra outfits are especially disappointing, eliminating any desire to collect raven skulls, required for its purchase.Animation is also poor. The movements look unnatural and unsmooth. Thus the dancing events appear disappointing, which also discourage sweeping the area searching for them.Music is nice. It is quite remarkable how the classic music has been integrated in the action game, complementing the visuals perfectly.There is no voicing for the dialogues, which is disappointing. The game would appear much more lively if the conversations were in sound.Total rating: 5/10.Overall impression is 50/50.The game seems fun at the beginning, but becomes disappointing towards the end despite it being short.It has good ideas and overall setting, but the actual implementation is quite poor: many things look unpolished or require improvement. I have got this game with a huge discount, thus I have no regrets about it. But its regular price is way too high.

I did see some reviews complaining the game was too short. Personally I think they got the length just right. It's not overlong and so it never feels like a chore to try and complete it. But again, it's so nice just having a simple, complete game without having to worry about all that extra faffing about.This is a real gem, and really deserves to be added to more peoples collections.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% game completion with all achievements in just under five and a half hours. Yet I cannot completely endorse this game. Almost.I'm going to echo the words of another reviewer: Pumpkin Jack is bland. Not bad nor terrible, just bland. It's unremarkable, which is disappointing because we seldom see the "silly gothic horror" aesthetic, like from PlayStation's MediEvil.Visually the game looks fine, like a hi-def toony platformer. However, there's lots of reused setpieces. Among the swamps, graveyard, and mines, you're going to see many of the same wooden planks and crates. There's also some very amateur shortcuts being taken with certain animations, like props shrinking when broken instead of shattering into pieces. The worst offender was during the fourth boss when these very simple, untextured polygons appeared to serve as fractures in the ground. It made the game look unpolished.Speaking of reused, you're also going to see the same few enemies over and over. Not enough variety, they mainly just go straight towards you. No strategy, no variety.Combat is just as disappointing. Enemies don't recoil or get stunned, they'll just effortlessly go right through your attacks. And their tells aren't easily readable so you're just going to end up taking hits. While the game does award a new weapon at the end of every level, they're not substantial. They're more of a sidegrade or just an option at best because they do not do more damage than the other. With that in mind, the best weapon is probably the shotgun as the range gives you a little bit of safety but you can also perform a rapid-fire attack after a dodge roll.The platforming and puzzles are very easy. If you're looking for a platforming challenge, look elsewhere. The boss fights are also samey, recycling the same attacks in slightly different ways.And the game's writing/jokes is low effort. The attempts at meta-humor fall flat.Despite all the issues, I will give this a thumbs-up but *barely* just because it's not an outright bad game. Middling. Grade-schoolers might have fun for a bit (if you don't mind occasional use of the word "hell") but you could do better, especially at lower prices.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? YES.The world is cursed, dark and full of monsters. Terror and death everywhere. The devil is happy. The humans living there not so much. So they send an old, mighty wizard on a quest to lift the curse and bring back the sunshine to the world. The devil is not happy. So he offers one of the worst creatures living in hell - you, Jack - a chance to get out of hell. Just kill the wizard and be free. Of course you take the job.With the job comes a new body, and you get the one of the Mythical Pumpkin Lord. Not bad. The head is detachable, which is used for a few mini games. Your first weapon is just a rusty shovel, but that's more than enough to vanquish the early monsters you encounter. With every boss slain in the course of the game, you gain new stuff to play with. One of the first characters you meet is a rather cowardly crow. It needs help to defeat an evil scarecrow (the first boss), but then stays at your side during the adventure. Not entirely voluntarily, but the funny conversations between Jack and the crow get more amicable in every level. The crow sits on your head most of the time, and it is used as a guided missile to attack foes and obstacles. You also meet an owl, sent by the devil to oversee your quest to kill the wizard and give some advice when needed. It believes to be your superior, which leads to some hilarious conversations. The core gameplay consists of 3D platforming. Jump, climb, use the rotable camera to screen the sourroundings. Different monsters block your way, and bosses pose a fighting challenge, although I probably died more often during tricky platforming sequences than during combat. The levels are varied and use different mechanics, including riding a mine cart like Indiana Jones or an obstacle course on a ghost horse. Puzzles are few and generally not too difficult. When you get hit, your life gets reduced, but it is easy to refill because enemies as well as many objects contain life energy when you kill or smash them. Every checkpoint also refills your life energy. Enemies, with the exception of bosses, are only really dangerous when they appear in larger numbers, or when their hits push you to your doom during climbing. There are plague doctor masks to collect, which can be used to buy new outfits. The game is saved at frequent checkpoints, which generally appear directly before difficult sections. When you die, you just respawn at the last checkpoint.The PC is not really the first choice for classic 3D platformers. There are just a bunch of really good ones, like A Hat in Time or the remasters of Crash Bandicoot and Spyro Reignited. I also enjoyed Skylar & Plux as well as Super Lucky's Tale, but the list doesn't go on forever. Now I can add Pumpkin Jack to it. I played in 3440x1440 with a Dualshock controller, which worked flawlessly. Even the PlayStation buttons are represented in the game.One of the best 3D platformers that the PC has to offer. Tight movement control, a funny story and varied gameplay mechanics make this game an easy recommendation.

Also any time you have to push a cart of dynamite alone a track is kinda tedious and is probably the low point for me. The game does try to add a little variety to each level though. Each level kinda follows this formula in different orders but each part is fun and the levels switch between them enough that before you can get bored of one you are already into another to keep the pace going. The game is pretty well written too. Not a super deep story or anything but the humor holds up without feeling cheesy or groan-worthy. While the soundtrack might not be the kind you'd listen to in your free time, each track does a good job of complementing the overall atmosphere. Overall, a super solid game and I look forward to see what this developer does in next because there is a solid foundation here to grow on for a sequel or even a completely different franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on 100% completion and 4.4 hours of gameplay.Would I recommend this game? Yes, it's a decent little game. Even though it's a platformer, it’s super easy, and overall, the game itself is quite simple. This makes it great if you're looking for a quick, stress-free experience.The gameplay is a straightforward mix of platforming, light puzzle-solving, some mini-games, and combat, and as mentioned, it’s all very easy. I enjoyed the game's aesthetic—it has a nice style, good sound design, and the audio complements it well.The game is short, with only six brief chapters, but it's of good quality. I didn’t encounter any issues during my playthrough, and it’s refreshing to see a developer who genuinely cares about the players, which I’ll touch on in the achievement section.Overall, the game is a pleasant little experience. However, I don’t recommend purchasing it at full price, as I think it’s too steep for the content offered. If you can wait for a good sale of 80% off or more, then that would be a much more reasonable deal for what you get.All the achievements in this game can be earned just by playing, aside from collectible achievements, one miscellaneous achievement in the first chapter, and purchasing in-game outfits  You won’t need a guide for this game, except perhaps to help you find the collectibles, saving you from having to backtrack later. If you do miss anything, there’s a chapter select feature, so you can easily return to grab any missed items.If you check a guide, you might notice some achievements like  and  that aren’t available on Steam. I found a developer’s response in a forum thread stating:It’s really nice to see a developer who genuinely cares enough to make decisions with the players’ interests in mind. So, if you see those missing achievements, don’t worry—as of this review, 100% completion is possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is not particularly offensive, but rather completely bland from a game play perspective. The music, environments, characters, artwork, and even the banter between characters are all very well done and entertaining; it makes for a great, spooky Halloween experience. If that's all I judged games on, it would be a complete knock-out, but I digress; Pumpkin Jack is held back by mediocre platforming and combat. The combat in Pumpkin Jack essentially consists of having Jack's bird partner stun an enemy when he's not on cool down, you then mash the attack button, roll dodge a bit, and kill everything. Defeating each boss unlocks a new weapon, but that really doesn’t change the overall pattern I just described. I don't believe I died a single time from combat, outside of boss fights. The bosses are huge, fun to fight, and add more variety to combat and platforming, but they are also easily disposed of and typically defeated after one or two attempts, once the player gets the boss’ patterns down.Platforming is very simplistic and not challenging in the least bit. Platforming really never gets more difficult or creative, it's simply a means to get from point A to B. There are times when the camera will zoom into objects behind Jack, making it difficult to navigate; one boss in particular was really bad with this. The game controls well enough, but the platforming is so basic that it really doesn’t even matter. Jack even has a double jump, but it’s never used creatively, but simply as a way to reach platforms further away, or correct a bad jump. There are collectables in each level: 20 crow skulls (used to buy extra costumes,) and one vinyl record (Really just if you want a cheevo, because all you get is a short cutscene of Jack dancing to the music.) The problem with the collectibles is that the levels are on the long side, with most taking me over a half-hour on my first attempt (I rarely died and didn’t particularly go out of my way to find collectables). A player more familiar with the game can easily knock those times down, but times will likely be much longer for one looking to 100% the game, since the player will be searching all corners of the levels for collectables. Occasionally things get switched up and there are mini-games, such as matching names on tombstones, riding in a runaway mine-cart, or throwing objects through holes of the same shape (just like toddlers do.) None of these mini-games are particularly engaging or well developed, as each one is merely played twice and then completely abandoned for the remainder of the game.I defeated the final boss in slightly over four hours and will not be going for the 100%. I liked a lot about the overall package, but the game itself is hard to recommend due to its overall blandness. Pumpkin Jack isn’t a bad game, but I cannot recommend it because it’s not a good game either.  If you want an inoffensive game with a Halloween theme, then go for it, but otherwise it’s likely not worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'd like to start with the fact that I am probably not the target audience in every sense of the word because I was a little bored with the gameplay and very easy platforming. However, This game still holds a somewhat special place for me after finishing it. The music is catchy, the game has a lot of visual and audible flair, dialogue is what we'll call "natural" because it isn't stiff, the game comes all together and has a very strong and lovely personality to it. And thats why I like it, its not the best, the cream of the crop in anything particular, but it has a soul and it's a lovely one. now, why is the game "special" to me? well because I am an adult and I was a child in the early to mid 2000's I have played a lot of games like this one, only to grow out of them, and in term for them to die over the years (we dont get many games that are 3D platformers anymore), and during my own game dev journey and having less and less time to engage with the hobby, something i can probably call my oldest "friend" that has seen me at every stage through my life, I've grown to appreciate when a game has soul as much as it does snappy and strong mechanics, but I suppose my biggest point of bias, its a nostalgic little romp. So if you're like me, growing up, confused, working, tired, and you want to escape for a bit of that childhood mid 2000s 3D collectathon platformer, then I invite you to try this game. It isn't long, has a LITTLE bit of replayability, but sometimes, a game will hold your attention for 5-20 hours and thats it. and maybe, thats all it needs to do.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game. The art style and overall atmosphere is absolutely stunning, the gameplay is fun, and the story is well told. The boss fights could have been improved. I feel like they could be more interactive similar to Elden Ring boss fights. Less waiting around for something to happen and more dodging the bosses' attacks and counterattacking. Overall the game is absolutely amazing and well done. I would 100% recommend anyone to play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: As a Halloween fanatic, this was a scary season treat for me. A nice, moderately challenging 3D Platformer with collectables and several levels to play through. It was fun to sit back and play this for a while, to go through the game, enjoying its scenery and gameplay. It is a little short and I wish there was more levels, even as a DLC, as the love put into this game is very evident. The levels in question have a good length to them, saving at your last checkpoint until you complete that level, so don't worry about leaving during a level. If I had one issue, it was in the last stage, during its mini-games. The positioning of the player and how close they are to the objects to attack makes it difficult to send them in the direction you want, other than that, I loved this game. Pumpkin Jack will be one of the top "Halloween" games on my games library. If the developer were ever to see this review, I'd like to thank them for creating this and give them props for a well created game. I can tell you cared about Pumpkin Jack, it certainly shows.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Reeally had fun with this game, I'm impressed it was made pretty much solo! Some pros and cons/things I'd like to see after having finished it:Pros:- Nice banter when you interact with NPCs- The spooky atmosphere is spot on. - Music is pretty great!- Platforming is well done.- Unlockable costumes by explorationCons:- Combat feels a bit wonky/floaty. You get used to it but I'd like more feedback when I hit things or get hit. - I'd love to see harder platforming, specially when going after hidden secrets. Most of it felt pretty basic even if it was well done.- Gramophones feel pointless? Other than just something you collect and to see Jack's sweet dance moves. Maybe weapon skins or something could be unlocked with them. - Bosses felt veeeery samey. Maybe some of them could vary on that and actually make you use your weapon or something!Either way, awesome job dude, and I hope this is just the first of many successful games for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant little game, nothing really bad but nothing very attractive either. _childDocuments_.review: Depends on the price. This is a SOLID platformer, that gets stuck down with boring combat and bad boss design. _childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but the nearly 10 hours I took to 100% it were an agonizing ordeal. Pumpkin Jack has some clever ideas and interesting sections, but those are undermined by the fact that it just doesn't feel good to play. Both combat and platforming are quite simple, but the controls are clunky and unresponsive, like they were wired through an actual pumpkin. This gets a lot worse whenever the game tries anything more complicated, while leaving nearly no wiggle room for failure. Definitely not worth 30 dollars.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is a very early 00's crash bandicoot, Spyro type of game, except with 'modernized' graphics. Honestly, it's a decent game but very straightforward and linear, there is no special exploration or thinking, besides trying o find all the bird skulls that are hidden (quite often not so good) to purchase cosmetics. Like I said it's okay, nothing crazy, chill game with a somewhat funny and quirky story, and the characters can be interesting as well. I personally would wait for the sale because I don't think it's worth 30 euros (or whatever your currency is).
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: A very simple throwback to the PS2 days of action platformers, Pumpkin Jack is a decent game thats punching faaaarrrr too high in its price range.First and foremost, this is a very simple game. Combat is spamming attacks until whatever infront of you is dead, platforming is equally as simple with jumping being the only thing that even qualifies it as a platformer. The story itself is something out of a Medievil or some long lost PS2 game. You play as Jack on a quest from the devil himself to destroy a sorcerer that aims foil the devil's plans, simple stuff. The main problem with the game is just how boring it starts to feel after the first hour. The game's formula never changes even with new weapons are unlocked. No puzzles aside from some mini-games that are tedious themselves, the weapons are personal choice with 0 additional features or uses other than killing things, and even the levels start to feel redundant since your doing the same things you did in the last level.The main gripe i have with the game is the price. I got this on sale for around $15, and im somewhat ok with that given its a functional game with some charm to it. $30 though is ridiculous for how little this game does overall. I apparently speedran the game and beat it in 4 1/2 hours, even though i was just playing at my speed. Even if you stop and smell the roses every level, its still only a 5-6 hour game with no real reason to explore unless you want the crow skulls for cosmetics. Its just not enough content for $30, even as a spooky halloween game i cant recommend this as a seasonal pickup given how short and plain it is. I will end with this, its not a BAD game, but it needed more at this price point. Weapon upgrades, puzzles, more indepth combat, so many features that even PS2 games were doing back in the day. On sale for anything less than $10, sure. $30? Hell no.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: This game is kind of fun, and the difficulty is awful. It has stress, because the boss fights are stupidly difficult. The art style is fantastic, the dialogs are funny, and the story is not well thought out. And the problems keep going on. For the price, the story is terribly short and low quality, and the playability for the money is also not great. Something that is common in story games, But Half-Life (an amazing story game) has the ability to be played after you finish the main campaign, So that means that a story game could be played many times if the creator wants to put the effort, which the creators didn't. If there was more to do in this game after you beat, I would definitely say that its worth buying. 29 dollars is just utterly unacceptable for a story game like this where its short, but that's how story games are. I personally wouldn't buy this game without a sale, and a lot of the negative reviews also say this. If you are made of money, sure go buy this, but the price is just a lot. I personally wouldn't recommend this unless you got it for 9 dollars (which is the discounted price.). This review is similar to a lot of the negative reviews, and the negative reviews are complaining about the length of the game and the price tag. The creators have a game that has a lot of potential, they just don't want to improve this game anymore, so I really cant recommend it. I wish I had refunded this after the first week, as I hated this game the first time I played it.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: This is the PERFECT game to play if you want to get into the Halloween spirit! It's fun, funny, has fantastic atmosphere and is incredibly hard to put down.Let me start out by saying I'm not someone who usually plays 3D platformers, and yet I immediately hooked on this game. It's a great example of 'easy to pick up, hard to put down'. The main reason for this is that the platforming and combat feels very responsive and satisfying. The encounters aren't too difficult, but challenging enough to intrigue.I absolutely loved the artstyle and environment design in this game. I think it cannot be understated how amazing the atmosphere of this game is, like it said: it's PERFECT for Halloween! The music and sound design are fantastic and complement the art direction really well. It's a joy to play and I often just walked around looking at the vistas!Another reason to pick this game up is the humor in it - it's really funny! Not in a cringy or done-to-death kinda way, but in a clever and self-aware kind of way. The storyline is weird and wacky, which fits this game perfectly. It works well for tying the gameplay progression into some sort of logical plot. Plus you get to kill Santa at some point! Fantastic.All in all, I would 100% recommend this game. The price may be a little steep without a sale, but remember this is made by a solo developer. Definitely get it while it's on the annual Halloween sale. It's short enough to complete it before actual Halloween if you play like 1-2 hours a day!

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to give this game a positive review. I'm a huge fan of the games that I draws its inspiration from (all the PS1-PS2 era platformers like Spyro, MediEvil, Jak and Daxter, etc. and I love the Tim Burton cartoony spooky vibe.The gameplay is mostly middle of the road, nothing surprising or overly creative, but passable and fun, if lacking in variety. The platforming is made somewhat irritating by an avatar that is more 'floaty" and loose than I'd prefer, but nothing that ruins the experience.The game is very short, even compared to the old games it emulates. Whether that 3-4 hours is worth the price is subjective, but for me, it wasn't quite as much as I'd hoped for.The biggest detractor for me is a consistent stability issue I've run into near the end of the game that has basically made the game unplayable. Since booting up the last level, I've had a consistent and worsening problem with brightness randomly changing and controller input functionality going in and out. Obviously these are serious problems in a game that requires platforming.I really wish this game was more than it is, because I'm predisposed to like the concept and its art direction, but there are too many negatives for me to fully recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: + Fun gameplay+ Straightforward game design+ Nice aesthetic and overall polish- Floaty controls- Disappointing combatAs someone that grew up with 3D platformers and has been disappointed with their decline in the past decade or so, Pumpkin Jack was definitely a game on my radar. We’re now a little over a week out from Halloween, so it’s time to give it a look.Pumpkin Jack is a reminder that you don’t need a bunch of fluff to make a fun video game. It’s designed in the same way as the 3D platformers from decades past and does a great job capitalizing on what made them fun, with solid platforming mechanics, cool level variety, and even a nice aesthetic and sense of polish to top it all off. Granted, the combat leaves a bit to be desired and the floaty controls are definitely a major problem, but it’s still a game I would recommend. If you’re a fan of the platformers from the GameCube/PS2 era, this is one to keep an eye on.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: I appreciate what the game was going for in a platformer, reminiscent of Crash, Rachet, and Spyro but it ultimately fell short for me. Aside from being an incredibly short experience, barely even reaching 4 hours of actual game time, the game was diverse in its art and some of the boss fights. The music was alright but a lot of it was lent from free classical music tracks and didn't blend well. Everything else just failed to impress.The weapons were mostly pointless, providing a bare minimum of variety in combat against enemies that were too weak to even really care about what you were using. The same could be said about the boss fights, which depended not on what weapons you used but simply surviving the phases as they went and hitting the appropriate targets i.e. bombs, and pillars. With the increased variety of weapons, I half expected enemies to react differently to each weapon but was unsurprised when they didn't. The two biggest gripes I have on the game are the price tag and the replayability. With no difficulty setting, a bare-bones attempt at collectibles, and absolutely no extracurricular achievements outside of one, the game's replayability is a zero for me. It took me under 4 hours to beat the whole game, missing 3 Crow skulls total and no gramophones, and then went back to each level and finished it off. If there were different difficulties, there might be something but with the rudimentary combat and wonky i-frames, it sounds like hell. Finally, a game like this is hardly worth 15-20 dollars in my book, let alone $30. I finally bought it on sale and being the completionist I am, went past the refund window. I don't regret playing the game but next time I would wait for a 90% off if that ever happens.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: This game plays like the games of late 90s and early 2000. It's a 3D puzzle platform'er with good controls and easy combat. It's does nothing new and is completely unoriginal. It's a great game! It simply just does all of it's things great.You play as Jack, a henchman of the devil sent to destroy the humans. The story tries to be funny, and it kind of is, but it's absolutely nothing special. There's a death screen that will show how many times you've died and mock you with a funny taunting text.The game is a couple of hours long. There's some collectibles for the achievement hunter. The graphics are cartoonish and great (I love that art style).Even though it plays as a great 20 year old 3D puzzle platformer, it also has the same flaws. I got stuck in some places since the character wouldn't grab onto a ledge. I tried to figure out how to solve the puzzle only to realize that I had to try again, and this time he grabbed onto the ledge. It's pretty much impossible to complete this game without dying as simply stepping in ankle deep water will instantly kill you. However, the flaws are not noticable often.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR version at the endThis is a not recommend for players like me specifically. The game itself is very cute, very casual, and I finished the final stage after 3.5 hours. I'm not going to complain about price because back in the day we used to get a lot less for twice as much... I'm looking at you Castlevania 64. Plus people don't really understand how expensive it really is to make games like this, so I think the full price is justified. The camera feels very smooth, and ground movement feels very good. I would recommend this as a whole to almost everyone who's looking for a nice relaxing experience.However, for those of you looking for a game that is a little more on the challenging and unique side of gameplay, I don't recommend this game. The boss fights are quite literally all exactly the same - You dodge some attacks, do something that hits boss, boss arena gets artificially smaller, rinse and repeat. There's combat in the game, but the combat feels very clunky with the exception of one weapon. Would've much preferred one single weapon done well with some upgrades to give the crow skulls a better purpose. I don't hate the air movement, but I don't like it very much easier. It's very floaty and drifty and seems like it actually hinders level design.There's also no voice acting, which I have absolutely no problem with. What I do have a problem with, however, is in the middle of platforming sections and boss fights when dialogue pops up in the corner that I would like to read but can't because I am trying to dodge attacks or jumping through platforms. I'm sure I missed quite a few enjoyable comments due to this.Lastly... the game is just too easy. I mentioned it in the beginning, this game is for a casual chill relaxing playthrough experience... I didn't even realize that the game has some witty dialogue and keeps tracks of your deaths until I accidentally stepped into some water on the third level.TL;DR - the game is a very enjoyable experience for a casual chill play, but a combination of clunky feeling combat with practically no challenge is just not recommended for me.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game in my opinion, that of course cannot keep up with AAA titles, but in consequence is also not bound to any of the expectations that come with them. Pumpkin Jack is a refreshing tale, that calls itself (and other games) out on phenomena like plot contrivances etc., doesnt try anything too inventive but gives existing concepts new spins. The story is loose enough to not be forceful but also intriguing enough to keep the player engaged. The characters interact in distincitve, often humourous ways and have very different personalities that, even in a tale as carefree as this, set them up for a typical hero's journey. As of writing this I have not yet finished the full game, so I cannot judge the ending, but so far it is worth playing and not knowing whether the end will be good or bad (or should I rather say "conventional" vs "unconventional"?) might actually add to the intrigue of playing the game and should be kept a secret in reviews. I can definitely recommend to play the game, especially if you are (like me) tired of open world games that expect you to sink hours upon hours into them and would like to switch it up a little with a short, linear game that still teases open world features (for example hidden collectables that allow you to purchase new skins for the main character). I would, however, also recommend to wait for sale, as the price is still pretty high for what it is, in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - Wait for a sale, 3-5 hour game with no reason to replay it after completed nor any real difficulty outside of maybe a boss or two.+ Achievements+ Pretty solid platforming+ Collectables- Some maps can bug out- Short game for the price- No new game+This game has charm, looking at it I got MediEvil vibes and had a lot of fun with my play-through.The platforming is pretty solid though Jack feels "floaty" at first but you quickly get used to that to know where you will land.I will admit, I didn't like the sections where you have to carefully walk across the beams, mainly because the camera angle and swaying did make me start to feel sick, lucky there is not many of these in the game but surprised I was effected by it.The combat is ok as well, you have to relay on dodging to dodge enemy attacks in swarms which is nice change from just mashing and winning the fights. You also get up to 6 weapons to choose from throughout the adventure once unlocked so if you didn't enjoy the first weapon, well try the 2nd one and so forth, there is bond to be one you enjoy using more than the rest.There are collectables however I feel too many were put in. In some sections there won't be any only for the next section to have 3 in birds-eye view of each other, it feels like they were just thrown in. But they are a nice thing to go for and collecting them just let you unlock costumes.Costumes are ok, I wish we had more to choose from but not end of the world really, it is still a nice thing to motivate you to go for the collectables.On to the negatives! yes the game is short, around 3 hours if you are not going for all collectables and around 4-5 if you are. For the price-tag this is not good specially since there is no reason to replay the levels after you got all the collectables.There is no new-game+, no boss rush, no challenge mode, nada. It would of been nice to at least given us a boss rush for those seeking something more out of it and would of been a nice excuse to add in costumes based off the boss you defeated.The last level is bugged, if you don't have 17 of the collectables before the portal, you will always spawn into the level after the portal, locking you out of 1-3 achievements unless you reset your game entirely.Often you will spawn under platforms/boats if you died in those sections only to re-die again and can do nothing about it but hope it actually spawns you above it.Lastly, a lot of the maps are not blocked off but kill zones if you explore. Some areas look like they branch off to a secret only to be stopped by an invisible wall or actually killed by a cutscene. If you were not meant to go that way I don't see why it was made to look like you could specially when they have the path texture there.Overall, it is an ok game but not worth full price unless they add in challenges and some actual reply-ability in my opinion. Wait for a sale if you are one wanting the most out of your money but if you want a nice little time-waster and have money to spare, it is ok to buy too for you to judge yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: A refreshing platformer, a bit short yet an enjoyable experience.The game is absolutely gorgeous looking, each level has unique and satisfying visuals, and it feels like any screenshot would make a great desktop wallpaper. The whole art direction is really well done, and the characters designs are well-inspired.The character's movements feels great, and each level bring few new mechanical ideas to freshen up the platforming. The combat plays nice, it evolves less than the platforming but the new weapons at each level contributes to renew it. It doesn't have a memorable plot, but features funny and witty dialogs.Pumpkin Jack won't revolutionize 3D platformers, but it's a honest and enjoyable tribute to its inspirations, such as Medievil.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is an action platformer that has been described as MediEvil meets Jak and Daxter. This is somewhat true, if perhaps a bit misleading. The similarity to MediEvil is very surface level; really it's just the theming. Both games are comedic, however, MediEvil also takes itself seriously, while Pumpkin Jack does no such thing. The Jak inspiration is more tangible with very clear inspiration in the puzzles and boss fight designs, as well as smaller gameplay elements such as rats spawning out of a nest that you must destroy. If, like me, you are desperately wishing for something that will scratch the itch for a new Jak and Daxter game, I don't think you'll get it here but I think you will find a great experience that is as close as we'll get outside of OpenGOAL mods. The final boss particularly feels like a really cool Jak boss that we never got and I just had such a good time playing this game. It took me 7.1 hours to 100% with all achievements, so maybe get it on sale if you feel the price is steep but there's something to be said for a relatively simple but fun game on the shorter side that stays enjoyable all the way through. It makes for a great palette cleanser between bigger games. Would recommend to any fans of Jak but also plans of 3D platformers in general.

_childDocuments_.review: Good little game, with beautiful visuals and a nice small variety of weapons for the easy gameplay it demands.Every level is different and has its own style of theme visually and soundtrack wise, it has different enemies to fight and a cool little plot that is easily followed and unconventional. _childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a great ode to PS2-era action platformers. It reminds me of games like Medieval, Maximo and Spinx & The Cursed Mummy. It has tight controls, creative mini-games and puzzles, and enjoyable boss fights. I really enjoyed the atmosphere and music as well, which is a treat to play around Halloween time. My only complaints are that a few elements were repetitive, like the boat rides, and it's over far too quickly. I did get a bug that tanked my framerate on the 4th level, during a segment I won't spoil, but according to patch notes this was resolved soon after I finished this level. If you're looking for a fun action platformer to help get you into the Halloween spirit, this is absolutely worth your time.

It is not very long but does a good job of not wasting your time.My only complaint is the workshop minigames in the snow level which triggered my motion sickness and made me nauseous. Everything else in the game was great.

_childDocuments_.review: This engaging concoction should end up delighting those who weaned their platforming teeth on late nineties / early noughties 3D platformers. It's quite clear from the onset who 's muse is and throughout the duration of the game it wears that admiration on its sleeve proudly. No one with a set of functioning eyes will not be able to notice the parallels  shares with a much loved PS1 classic -  - from the Gothic inspired humour to the cartoony graphics.  What is even more amazing is that  is a labour of love by one developer - Nicolas Meyssonnier - who given that this is his first attempt literally knocks the ball right out of the park putting quite a few bigger development teams to shame in the process.There are some rough edges though, not all the puzzles sections work and some of the on-the-rails segments can irritate (the cart race being one), where the game will often, and very cheaply, snatch a win right out from under your nose numerous times by cheating its ass off. For a game made under the watchful eye of a solo dev, I was also struck by how fluid and dynamic the combat was. It was not clunky at all which tends to be the case with most of these homemade projects. Having said that, I did find it a tad too simple as repetition does start to settle in near the end. Environments could have also used a bit more variety as they tend to blend into one another, however, I am not going to come down on the guy hard for these because what Nicholas has delivered is a great Halloween romp with side dish of snide and snarky that had me chuckling more than once. Where the game does excel is in the fantastic boss fights at the end of each level. They are creative, fun and mostly frustrationless once you work out each of their patterns. Each level is suitably long too (lasting between 40-50 min) that pushes the game into the 6-10 hour completion range that is perfect for this kind of entertainment as the game never outstays its welcome which could have led it to becoming somewhat rote. may be old fashioned when compared to the likes of today's more modern platformers, which all seem to rely on ever increasingly brutal platforming sections as their mainstay, but those that give themselves over to  will be delighted for the most part whether they are young or old. While  may not be one of the most aesthetically pleasing Halloween treats, it most certainly is the one of the most genuine. There is a deep love here that Nicolas Meyssonnier is trying to convey for the genre and for the most he has succeeded admirably. Definitely worth a look!

_childDocuments_.review: This is the perfect Halloween game! Pumpkin Jack is an action platform game where you guide Jack through six levels in order to defeat a Mage and bring ruin the world in the name of the devil, so yeah in this game you are kinda playing the role of the villain. The levels are very straightforward, you run, jump, hit enemies with different weapons, fight the boss at the end, repeat for 6 levels and in about 4 hours the game is done. I have to say as an action platformer it doesn't break new grounds and the game is overall average: every level has the same structure, the weapons differences feel more aesthetic than utility, the controls are kinda slippery and you might overshoot some jumps and die occasionally and your health can deplete really fast. This are flaws but nothing game breaking, and honestly the game gives me so many Medievil vibes that I just have to enjoy it. Sometimes all you need to have some fun with a game is blasting out monsters with a Jack O'lanter scarecrow dressed like a lumberjack wielding a shotgun.

_childDocuments_.review: I just don't think this game is very good. I'm really adamant about 3D platformers but this is one where it's clear the developers do not understand how to make a platformer that flows. I only played the first level and maybe a quarter of the second level but it's obvious the game is just going nowhere, so I dropped it.First the good. The dialogue is in that sweet spot of being funny without being cringey or trying too hard. So many indie games get this wrong but this is one where every interaction is enjoyable. Second the graphics look like an HD PS2 game, which I promise is a compliment, and the comic book style portraits look nice. I like spooky aesthetics so that's also a plus.Now where the game falters is the gameplay. First of all the game is rife with technical problems, I get a lot of screen-tearing even with v-sync enabled, and on top of that I get unexplained framedrops so it hovers around 50-60 sometimes which is ridiculous and unacceptable for a game of this fidelity. Secondly the combat. Why do enemies take so many hits to kill? The game has one-button no-depth combat so the enemies should take only 1 or 2 hits. Instead they tank like 4 or 5 hits before finally falling. The combat is also weird because it doesn't flow with the platforming, they just randomly have combat sections interspersed where they decide to put a few boring enemies to fight. Now speaking of platforming, that's the most disappointing part of this game. 90% of the time you're just on the ground walking around flat terrain. Then sometimes you have to platform but it's always extremely simple platforming for babies where you have to jump once or twice on slow moving platforms. Then it's back to walking around on flat terrain and boring combat. Rinse and repeat. Even the setpieces like the mine carts are boring, has the dev ever played Donkey Kong Country? Now that's how you do a mine cart sequence. There's no real movement tech in this game, only 1 collectible type which is super easy to 100% since most are sitting in plain sight, and levels are literally railroaded linear as hell with no branching or alternate paths or any freedom. If you have ANY experience with platformers, there is no reason to play this game.The other problem is the game's aesthetic. The first level sets up a pretty good atmosphere, but they use the exact same environments and assets through every single level in the game. You will get very tired of seeing the same hazy blue environments, wooden platforms, and crates reused over and over.  Given the game is only 6 levels long, this is ridiculous. If your game is gonna be that short, you better make sure every level looks and feels distinct. Hell, that's a plus for ANY length game. This game was clearly made on a super tiny budget, yet they want $30 for this? Nah, I bought it off a key site for $2 and I STILL think it was a waste of my time and money. If you want a good 3D platformer PLEASE pick up something like Hell Pie or Hat in Time instead.

_childDocuments_.review: A perfectly adequate 3D platformer than earns a little bit of a bump from a great sense of style & me personally having a lot of fun with the traversal abilities. The spooky style atmosphere is fun & consistent, with a great artistic sense in the modelwork & music. In the gameplay department, I think this offers the bare bones of what you'd want in a 3D platformer but not in a bad way: collectibles, costume options; lots of ways to be a completionist that isn't too time consuming.While I appreciate the briefness of the gameplay time, I do have a few little gripes that popped up here & there that I think mainly involved the minigame content. Some of the Jack's head puzzles were a little irritating to control, especially kicking the bombs or Santa presents due to weird hit detection (but not insurmountable). Also not a huge fan of some of the flying segments but particularly the gargoyle ride where button presses are added (the most irritating part of the game for me).These aren't really huge hurdles though, since I think broadly this game is exactly what I'd want more of in the indie space: shorter but still decently paced experiences with solid controls & design as the focus. Fun time, would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, this game is a solid recommendation. It’s aesthetics, general atmosphere, humour and gameplay are very chill and satisfying. It plays around with new mechanics for different segments, cutscenes which keeps the experience fresh from start to finish.The art design of this game is absolutely incredible, there’s this cartoony villainous feeling that old cartoons used to have, the art style reminds me of MediEvil. The sound design also sells that idea, the soundtrack has a Halloween feeling to it, they are uplifting but there’s a clear shift from the exploration and the combat soundtrack, with different tracks for cinematic events that happen.Talking about these cinematic events, this is what stood out the most for me, this game doesn’t stay clear from experimenting with different mechanics, it wanted to tell a funny story and it uses a lot of different tools to do so. There’s even a funny event with one of the collectables that is such a joy to see, had me smiling all the way through.Combat is simple but effective, enemies have a telegraphed attack, with most of them having two moves, you can dodge, swing around different weapons and use your companion to deal ranged damage.Exploration is very nice too, the world has a few nooky and crannies to look into, which usually have one of the collectables, so you’re not wandering for no reason, most of the time. I did die a few deaths that I felt were cheap with instant death pools of water or a mechanic in the swamp that I had no figured out at first, and also wish the game was a little less linear though, but I get the decision because it has a strong narrative associated with it.I also enjoyed the writing’s humour, with a few fourth wall breaks, the story isn’t anything special but it’s funny enough to keep you engaged.The game has the perfect length for what it does, as it could’ve become repetitive it was longer, that said I got one hundred percent at around five hours so it’s not very long, in case that bothers you.Lastly I just want to say this has a very similar feeling to “The Grinch” on the PS1 for those that played it, but with focus on a linear story instead of exploring the levels.

_childDocuments_.review: In Pumpkin Jack, it is your sole purpose to take control of the Pumpkin King and obliterate the disgusting forces of good. More specifically, your ultimate goal is to take out the awful do-gooding wizard who has promised to protect the Boredom Kingdom from the devil himself. Completely bored and tired of the hum-drum life of peace, prosperity, and safety that the Boredom Kingdom have built for themselves, the devil summons an entity known as Stingy Jack to unleash havoc on the unsuspecting citizens. Though he cannot fight without a proper body, the devil stuffs Jack into the skin of a pumpkin and sends him off to do his bidding.The humour and writing in this release is spot-on. It's not so silly that it comes off cringey or weird, and it's not so dry that it falls flat; there's a great balance here, a feat that's not so easily achieved. Jack is a crabby semi-intellectual pumpkin man who 'befriends' an unwilling crow to aid him on his evildoing journey. He's led along by an owl, who narrates the story from time-to-time, provides tutorials, and sits at cauldron checkpoints. There are five weapons that are gained over the campaign, from a simple shovel to a deadly scythe, and a gun and a magical orb. New enemies become introduced during almost every level as well, ranging from ghoulish floating spectres to vomiting bats, undead snipers, and more. Each of the levels has an end boss, and each one has their own mechanics and unique, interesting character models.Another amazing feat that the sole developer, Nicolas Meyssonnier, manages to accomplish in his landmark release is that you'll never be able to guess what's around the next bend. Whether that be more platforming, fighting some enemies, or suddenly getting swept up by a gargoyle and controlling the height at which it flies so you don't get slammed into obstacles. Or maybe it'll be a ride through the night sky on a ghostly horse, where you have to dodge projectiles and jump over fences. Perhaps you'll have to throw your pumpkin head into a tube and have it play whack-a-mole or Simon says. These are just a few of the mechanics that are continually introduced from the start of the campaign, until the very end.Pumpkin Jack is a title that is very much in the same vein as other vividly colourful, 'spooky but lighthearted' releases such as MediEvil and Costume Quest. The use of colour here is phenomenal, and the bright blues, ghastly purples, chaotic reds, and eerie greens make the game jump to life, while the volumetric fog serves to paint everything in a ghostly light. The aesthetic it houses is inherently cartoony, but it's also flavoured with splashes of crooked-and-bent stylings that are deeply reminiscent of something that Tim Burton would cook up. There are six levels in total, and each one of them has its own atmosphere and vibe; from a creepy cemetery to a bubbling swamp, and further beyond to a twisted winter wonderland. Even if you've played thousands of games, it's guaranteed that you haven't ever seen anything quite as visually captivating as this release. Although the developer took inspiration from other artists, they managed to create a style that's uniquely their own. Aiding the visuals is the incantation-esque OST, which is hypnotic in its bewitching composure. It has been expertly crafted, and rivals any and all AAA soundtracks (aside from DOOM and Silent Hill, of course).When there's nothing bad that can be said about a game, nitpicking starts to occur. While there really isn't anything bad about this title, there are some things that could stand to be improved in the future. For one, none of the weapons feel like upgrades, but they feel like reskins instead; the scythe, for example, does not feel more powerful than the shovel. Some additional moves or maybe one or two more special powers would've been nice as well. Additionally, VSync doesn't stay enabled when exiting and reloading the game, you have to turn it off and back on again. Again, these are extremely minor things that aren't even significant, but I am providing some improvement feedback here as I want to see this game thrive with additional content, or sequels.The entire encompassing experience that Pumpkin Jack provides feels wonderfully charismatic and magical. There is a cinematic quality to the game, much like what is found in the darker-but-still-kid-friendly movies like Nightmare Before Christmas, Coraline, and Frankenweenie. There is an allurement here that has not been present in video games for a while, and it's no wonder that Pumpkin Jack is already capturing the hearts and souls of gamers. The only downside at all is that the campaign only lasts about five hours, making it feel almost like a tech demo for some bigger project. The good news to that is, the developer did leave an open shot for a direct sequel. Let's hope that he takes that plunge, because this is a game worthy of turning into a series. The fact that this game was developed by one person, with the help of a very small handful of others, is astonishing. A deep, full-bodied congratulations to Nicolas Meyssonnier; you should be incredibly proud of what you've created and achieved.The Horror Network  |  Click for Gore

_childDocuments_.review: The only reason this review is positive is that i've got this game from a Humble Bundle and cost me almost nothing.I really looked forward to play this game for some time. While looking at the screenshots from the game i got nostalgic feeling of old PSX platformers, like Spyro or Medievil.The Dev really captured this special feeling into his project... and i feel like it's the only strong advantage of this game.The game is hella short. There are 6 stages, each stage can be completed nearly in 40 minutes with all the secrets and pickups. The level design was kind of repetitive: "arenas" with battle music and literally few enemies, there is racing segment, and there are two pumpkin puzzles - at least those are kind of cool, and are different in every stage; and of course, jumping. The thing is i feel like levels are empty most of the time. The visuals are great in my opinion, but sometimes the line between invisible wall and object i could interact or even jump on is really blurry. About jumping - good platformer cannot be good without proper controls, right? Well, about that...Jumping Jack (teehee) has really strange movement. You cannot change it's direction or velocity, making the double jump the only trajectory correction mid-air.ABOUT GRABING THE EDGES OF THE PLATFORM.HOLY. ****.I died like 20 times just because Pumpkinhead cannot grab the edge, even if he should. Making leaps of faith was the most difficult part of the game.Difficulty speaking i was under the impression that the game was made for kids so i shouldn't be so hard on it. Besides cranky controls there are no real difficulty in the game, killing everything and destroying obsticles give you HP so running out of it in combat is really not that common. I feel like hit oponents should "flick" and cancel their attack - especially when the fights are made in "gangbang" mode.I am not really big fan of a story itself, the dialogues were sometimes edgy but i felt that the 4th wall was broken a few times more that it should be in a good taste.There are few weapons to choose from, but they all felt kind of... laggy. It's not like i hate this game. The game was "OK" and just "OK". I kind of liked the experience, but after finishing a level i did not go to a next one or even search for lost skull(s) - maybe the game would not feel as tiring if the 40min levels would be splitted into Acts I/II. I felt glut after finishing each level, but in few days i come back to play the game again.I would not pay for this game 30 Euro or even 15.If you can get it cheaper or via "family sharing", go for it, maybe you will like it.In this state this short game despite having great visuals, costumes and kind of "soul" of the old Playstation game, is cranky at times and not worth it's price. Maybe with some additional storyline may be worth 30 euro but it's unlikely to happend.And why are we collecting phonographs? No idea.
