_childDocuments_.review: I unfortunately would not recommend this game unless it was on sale (which is what I did— it was ~$3). This is a platformer that you can complete in about 4 hours, so the sale price feels fair for the content. If it’s not on sale, I’d recommend passing on this Pros:- The game’s identity is solid; while I feel the influences of other games of the same genre, it never felt like the game was trying to pretend to be another, better game, if that makes sense. Its identity and theming make it feel unique compared to other platformers. Plus, it’s always nice to have more games for the Halloween season that aren’t horror - Gameplay loop, while repetitive, is consistent and predictable throughout. There was never a part that felt like a jarring experimental curveball that felt out of place. - I like the character design and art direction - Checkpoints are generous - Lots of good ideas here. Clever platforming and level design. Two strong examples are the swamp level and the stone challenges representing the seven deadly sins. Cons: - Jack doesn’t walk; he floats. This causes him to have too much acceleration when moving. It also causes him to be hard to control mid-air and feels very slippery. This makes precise platforming rather annoying. - The challenges come from the unpolished controls and enemy spam. Enemies are also like sponges, with some even taking 10+ hits (ex. The gargoyles)- For such a short game, the game is EXTREMELY repetitive. Every level follows the same formula: Some platforming and enemies, do a minigame/“puzzle” as Jack’s head, more platforming, vehicle section. Repeat this again and finish with a boss. - The bosses are very long. Even though all of them have three phases, they have several attacks. Oh, also, the bosses’ attacks are essentially the same (dodge projectile, dodge melee, minion spam, hit a bomb or something at the boss to trigger the next phase). - Sometimes there is just too much crap on screen that makes the game disorienting. This is especially apparent during the husband and wife boss fight in swamp. Boss fights take place in a circular arena and you can still see the “walls” surrounding the arena. If you are running around trying to dodge the boss’ attacks, the translucent wall is going to be in front of the camera. Moreover, the particular effects on attacks and objects are very bright and take up a lot of space, which will occasionally make it hard to see the ground. During the swamp boss fight, the wife character keeps yelling taunts, which prompts her speech bubble to appear every two seconds, taking up a good chuck of the bottom right quadrant of the screen (I played this game on the Steam Deck, so I’m unsure if the screen size exacerbated this). All the while, her husband keeps popping up to whip you, but the arena walls and other visual obstacles make it hard to see him.- Combat doesn’t have great feedback and generally doesn’t feel good. Enemies will say “ow” but will often not react to your hits. They will continuously spam attacks even while you are hitting them. - The camera angle for nearly all the vehicle sections are egregious. I’m riding a horse or falling into a worm while trying to dodge incoming obstacles…why is the camera angled at Jack’s rear? The push cart race was fine because the camera was angled more over the shoulder/head and allowed you to see the path ahead. However, that section didn’t really have an obstacles, so why did that section feel more polished than the other vehicle sections?- All weapons, except the first one (the shovel) make you stop in place when attacking. There is also no reason to ever switch weapons outside of preference (I only really liked using the shotgun)- This feels like a one-and-done experience. There’s not really any replay value or bonus content

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is an ok 3D platformer, it's just completely lacking in any creativity or fresh ideas. The game took slightly less than 5 hours to finish and I played the whole thing in an afternoon. The game is pretty easy. This is probably a good first 3D platformer that children would enjoy. The levels are all very basic. There's a lot of jumping on platforms and occasionally the action is broken up where each level Jack loses his body and has to complete some basic, mundane task as just a head and tentacles. There's also some cart sections and steering while flying. The biggest problem with PJ is just how dated the game feels. Even 20 years ago this game would probably have seen as generic. All the different mechanics have been seen in other games. PJ just doesn't offer anything new at all. I would recommend this to people that are desperate to play any platformer and they've played all the good ones already. Also, it's a good introduction to the genre for unskilled platform jumpers who want to try out 3D platformers. I kind of enjoyed my time breezing through the game. There are just so many better platformers out there Pumpkin Jack completely pales in comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: I covered this game as part of my coverage of the Humble Choice for June 2022A competent platformer, but that’s it. The minute you start playing Pumpkin Jack you realize you’re playing a solid platformer.  The controls work well, the double jump just feels right, and the level gives just the right amount of hints on where to go next.   And then suddenly you found a secret item where your character does a little funky dance.  This is all part of the DNA of a typical platformer with a bit of a collect-a-thon.But Pumpkin Jack is just that.  A solid platformer that doesn’t stand out.  The art looks acceptable, the level design is ok, and the story works, but that it.  There’s not a lot to buy with the collected items, and the game isn’t that long either.  But overall the game just feels ok.  This isn’t necessarily a bad or a good thing, it’s just average, and that’s probably the biggest issue I have with Pumpkin Jack. I will say this is created by a single developer, which is impressive, but as a gamer, this is a 30-dollar title, and my mind kept asking why I wasn’t playing something else like  A Hat in Time.    I want to see more by the Developer whose name I’d butcher, Nicolas Meyssonnier because he delivered a finished product, but maybe take a little more time with the design as well. Pick this up if you love 3d Platformers and need a new one after playing most of them.  The issue here is more about how much competition there is in the genre and how many have done this better.   The game also throws achievements at the player, I earned 10 out of 33 in under one hour.  Still, I want to stress, that this isn’t a negative review.  It’s just not a positive one either. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a love letter to 5th generation 3D platformers. It's a short, cozy experience where no single aspect overstays its welcome. Generally the pacing is good, you move from small bouts of combat to platforming to puzzle solving/minigames and back quickly, and usually before you know it the level is over. This is a short game- you could probably beat it in 2-3 hours if you blast through it as quickly as possible. But in an era of derivative AAA games that last too long or are broken garbage, there's something nice about throwing a small team $20 for something intentionally designed and to the point (even if gamers still think they should pay $30 for a game that gives them thousands of hours of gameplay).It's also worth noting the team is VERY small. Almost everything was done by a single developer, with a few odds and ends outsourced. With this in mind it's easier to excuse some of the "drawbacks", which are all pretty small/nitpicky anyway. You can't skip over dialogue bits upon replay, the audio mix in the cutscenes is a bit wonky at times, the combat can feel slightly underbaked. But usually as soon as you start to grumble about something you just get lost in the charm again.

_childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others Pumpkin Jack is the solo project of the French developer Nicolas Meyssonnier, a title inspired by games such as Medievel and Jack and Daxter, which had the support of Headeup Studios as publisher and thus made this title reachable to more platforms. And It’s easily one of the best Indie platformer games this year.Right from the start, this title changes around what you would expect, since the players wear the skin of Jack, a charismatic villain who plays the role of the devil’s servant and whose soul was placed in a pumpkin. Accompanied by a rather fearful and chatty crow and an owl as a guide, players will have to cross different levels to reach their main objective.The story is set in the Boredom Kingdom, which even made the Devil super enraged because nothing was going on around that place. Thirsty for turbulence and something more merciless, he decided to launch the terrible Curse of Eternal Night on earth. In their attempt to retaliate, humans summoned a powerful, albeit somewhat dubious, wizard to save them.This is how Jack appears in the middle of this succession of events after the Devil himself has invoked him and tasked with disrupting the plans of the champion of humanityThe adventure unfolds through 6 different levels filled with platforms, puzzles, mini games, and lots of action to the mix. The whole world of this peculiar title literally jumps off the screen with its palette of psychedelic colors combined with the effects and lighting very well achieved. Always with the side of a world full of accessories alluding to Halloween, that is, crows, cemeteries and green and shiny cauldrons.The enemies, in this case, are also beings from the other world, but why do they attack Jack? Well, all monsters attack when they feel a human and Jack still has something human inside him, even though he no longer has a human body, his soul is still present.Mechanically, each level is divided between platforms, combat, and a slope that puts the player in a running position, where it is necessary to avoid obstacles or reach the finish line in the first place. The whole action is very fluid and Jack has the possibility to use a double jump, a dash ability, and one of 6 different weapons. These weapons are distinguished between melee and ranged attack, although the firearms cannot reach an enemy from a great distance. Each of them has a simple combo, where it is only necessary to continue pressing the button and an area attack where it is necessary to use the double jump and the attack button. Simple but effective.Although combat is not the main attraction of this adventure, it reveals a very pleasant Medievel vibe, but somehow superficial. It is really necessary to hit a lot of enemies until they are destroyed, but Jack is also capable of taking a lot of damage before losing his entire life bar. There is not a wide variety of enemies, but the confrontation against the “Bosses” manages to make the delights of the more attentive eyes, due to their attention to detail. The attack patterns are quite easy to memorize, so there is no great difficulty in these end-of-chapter fights.In a game where there are immense platforms and chasms, where poorly measured jumps often equate to instantaneous deaths, Pumpkin Jack does not leave a feeling of frustration, as there are plenty of “save” points during the level, which by the way is still a long journey.This is undoubtedly a fun and a nostalgic title that is perfectly set to be this year’s Halloween gaming session. Although it does not revolutionize the wheel within the genre it is highly recommended for any fan of 3D platforming adventures and the fact that it is the work of just one person, makes this whole experience even more impressive. Mr. Pumpkin Jack deserves particular attention. Unfortunately, it does not have a “photography” mode, but how interesting would it be? I leave the question and the mark of the 50 screenshots I took over the almost 6 hours of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I wanna start this review by saying that his has been one of the games I've looked forward to a lot, it's been in my cart a number of times but I always put off buying it. When I saw it was in this month's Humble Bundle I was THRILLED to finally get to play it. I am not huge on platformers but this game drew me in with the graphics and general style and I really thought I'd like it. Now, after finishing it I am sad that I don't have it in me to recommend it.The platformer and fighting elements of the game are not the problem, those were really enjoyable and usually fun to play. I personally thought the keybindings were a bit clunky (WASD and E to evade, which ends in cramps if you try to keep that up for a fight). I felt like because of the imprecise controls I wasn't able to master the game but that is okay. I can live with weird jumps and redoing parts of a level because I died. My problem were the sequences within the levels. In every level are 2 sequences in which you have to complete a kind of minigame where you control Jack's head. Some of those were meh, others quite fun. And then there a 2 dreaded ride/race sequences that I just HATED beyond anything - more then pineapple on pizza! The first ones were somewhat okay but they got worse with every level. The somewhat wonky controlls also are amplified in these parts that I just kept dying over and over again because of the speed or oversteering of directions. I even ended up doing the last 2 (of 6) levels with a guide (for collectibles) because I just didn't have it in me to play these ride/race scenes again.So yeah, in theory a GREAT game, lovely design, amazing music, cool story, good humor and almost exclusively fun gameplay. These extra sequences just really ruined the game for me. If you like the kind of game, are prepared for the "extras" in the levels then go for it! The game is really well done, I just personally really didn't like some specific parts of it.I also feel like 30 bucks is too much for it. I spent little over 8 hours on the game but replayed quite a few of them. You can beat the levels in ~45 min each (if not less) and there is not too much replayability value in them.

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a 3D platformer that does everything good, but nothing great. It's fairly short, only containing six levels, each of which take around 30 minutes to complete depending on how much you want to explore. The graphics look nice, and definitely remind you of Halloween and there's some funny writing, but the entire time I was playing it, I just felt like something was missing. The controls worked perfectly fine, and the levels offered a good variety of setting, and gameplay but there's not quite enough here for the $30 price tag. If you're a fan of the genre however and want a game that you can complete in a couple sessions then I'd say to pick it up on sale. Pumpkin Jack looks pretty decent. The lighting effects help make the different settings you explore look nice and creepy and the characters are all well designed, each in their own spooky way. The areas that you explore are well varied, taking you to a haunted mine, a graveyard, a swamp, the North Pole, and more. Everything looks very cartoonish and it suits the game and its world quite well. The writing is quite funny at times, pointing fun at itself, and games as a whole. The music and sound design is quite well, with some memorable fast paced tracks (the mine cart section comes to mind here) as well as some good atmospheric tracks.  The core gameplay is very simple and familiar to fans of 3D platformers. You have the basic double jump and dodge abilities, as well as a melee, and long distance attack button. The platforming sections are fairly easy, in part to the very tight controls that work perfectly. I never felt as if Jack didn't do what I wanted him to do or that I wasn't in control at any given moment. The combat sections are fairly repetitive, mainly due to how basic combat is. It turns into a button masher in later levels when you're put against a large horde of enemies. Every level ends with a boss fight, and these are all fairly straight forward with a defense section where you run around dodging attacks waiting for your opening to attack. There are a variety of "minigame" sections scattered throughout the game and while some of these were good changes of pace and were quite enjoyable, others such as the memory game lasted too long, and became more of a chore than something I looked forward to.  For a game made by one developer, it's quite impressive, and it's clear that there was passion behind the project. In the end credits, there's pictures showcasing the timeline of the game from the very beginning to release and you can really see just how much time and effort was put into Pumpkin Jack, but unfortunately I can't help but think that another year or two could've gone a long way in really fleshing out the game from a solid game to a truly great one. The current asking price of $30 is too much for what's here, but if you're a fan of the genre, and want a nice short game for a weekend, get it on sale. For more reviews follow my

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a casual, halloween-themed, 3D platforming adventure game that features the (anti) hero Stingy Jack, an evil and cunning soul stuffed in a pumpkin by the Devil himself, whose mission is to stop the mighty Wizard from breaking the Devil's curse and saving humanity! Since 3D platformers, despite making a comback in recent years, aren't as popular as they used to be, Pumpkin Jack's worth a shot.The first, strong aspect of the game is the lighting - it amazingly sets atmosphere for each individual level, and serves as a neat visual indicator. With dim, simple models and colorful, eye-catching lighting with  we can identify an enemy, a collectible, an interaction, the path, climbable platforms, etc. etc. - it's incredible what Nicolas and his crew made with this feature!The next trait of Pumpkin Jack is its lighthearted appeal - rom characters and dialogue, through spooky soundtrack, to death messages, the game just OOZES with charm. I think I could boldly call this a mix between "MediEvil" and "A Hat In Time".Another thing worth mentioning is the design - the levels are straight forward and simple to progress through, and collectibles will be scattered around to make finding your way easier; but the levels have plenty of nooks and smaller branching paths that are enough for the player to keep eyes on the lookout for possible hidden collectibles, which gives us more opportunities to appretiate the pretty views and the amazing, aforementioned lighting.Moving on, the main gameplay and controls. The main focus of Pumpkin Jack is the platforming and combat.Platforming is solidly done - all approachable shelves and platforms are marked with a lamp and a rope, making them easy to identify quickly by the player during playthrough. Jack has an ability to double jump,and to hoist, the latter being extra useful when jumps end up being tad too short - making the game pretty forgiving, especially since the jumping is momentum based (which I don't really enjoy in platformers, but thanks to these features I hadn't much problem with that).Now, the combat - it 's not bad, but it's not great either. Throughout the game you'll find a couple of weapons, each having its own sets of attacks, and each of those attacks are different (mostly in speed and in range) depending on whether you make a combo, a jump attack, a double jump attack, or a dodge roll attack. And considering the variety of enemies and bosses you'll run into, on paper, all of it should sound exciting, right? Sadly, it isn't - the differences between weapons aren't impactful enough (shame, some of them are very cool), making them but a preference, particularly because the damage they deal is the same, and sluggish moves on some weapons can be annoying to do in combat, since these, aside from range, lack a proper pay-off.After a while you'll end up finding battles dull, mashing attack button and running around to avoid being hit. The fighting is rather half-assed, I'm disappointed to say.To give the gameplay variety, we'll be solving plenty of short puzzles, riding through obstacles or racing other opponents, and battle with a handful of distinct bosses. Each of these events are evenly spaced out and don't break the pace of the game - it's a really nice balance!For many players, the price for the game is questionable, and I agree. It's a pleasant game, but the content is not one I'd call worth almost $30/€24. Just wait for the sale.My personal problem with the game though, combat aside, is the satisfaction at the end. The game is properly challenging IMO, don't get me wrong, but it lacks some  for finishing the game, a small reward for collecting all items. After beating the game once there's no real reason to play it through again, aside from doing "the completionist's check list", as I would call it. But I would lie if I said that I didn't enjoy the adventure, because I did.It was a very pleasing experience, I just wish there was a bit more of it, or revisiting the levels was worth the time.All in all, Pumpkin Jack is a game worth checking, whether you're a 3D platformer enthusiast, or you're simply looking for something fun and casual, but with a fair challenge.PS:
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a solid 3D platformer with a Halloween theme. It's got 6 distinct levels, each taking between 25-45 minutes, for roughly 4-6 hours of playtime. The platforming feels pretty good, and isn't terribly difficult. There are a few spots during tricky sections where the controls can be a little finnicky, and falling often results in insta-death which can be a little frustrating. Each level also has a separate minigame. These of our varying quality. Mostly they're fun. The cemetery level's is a bit annoying. It's a classic matching game where you match names on headstones. It's fine, and not hard, but required a tedious amount of trial and error compared to the rest of the game.Each level also has a segment where control is taken away and you're on-rails just jumping and destroying obstacles, like riding a minecart or being flown around by a gargoyle. These sections are braindead easy, and are a bit too long for my liking. I imagine they were put in to break up the platform -> combat -> platform flow, but they were just a little too drawn out for me.Speaking of combat, it's featured pretty heavily but still feels like a bit of an afterthought. It consists of attacking a few times, rolling away, waiting for the enemy's animation to end, and then attacking again. It's fine, but really simple. The game does give you a few different weapons to play with as you unlock levels, and they all feel distinct.Pumpkin Jack's high points are in its atmosphere and humor.It nails the Halloween theme, the graphics look great and the use of color is excellent. The music doesn't stand out but is appropriately spooky. This game also isn't a horror a game. There's a lot of humor here, and I usually don't like a ton of humor in games but this one nails it. There's just the right amount of dialogue and quips and 4th wall breaking, and a lot of it is actually funny. Levels are broken up with short cutscenes where these dialogues play out, but it's kept to a minimum and I think that's a good thing for this type of game.$30 is a bit high for a 3D platformer with only a few hours of content. I don't think I'd recommend this game at full price unless you're a huge fan of the genre, but if you can snag it at $15 or less it's definitely worth a play, especially in October.

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a really well rounded 3D-Platformer with a nice spooky/halloween theme. Around 2h in (seem to be halfway through already unfortunately) and I've yet to feel frustrated by the combat scenarios or platforming sections which really positively surprises me since I am playing on mouse and keyboard. The game is fairly easy, however your HP can be drained quickly if you're not careful. You do get HP back upon defeating enemies and destroying crates/barrels/... placed around the maps. The platforming pretty much stays the same throughout the game but a twist gets introduced from time to time. The foundation of the parkour sections stays the same but in each level unique hazards like exploding minecarts or new platforming elements like bouncy mushrooms keep the platforming from feeling repetitive.The gameplay and aesthetic really take me back to the Wii, PS2 and PSP era. This game really captures the essence of the games which introduced me to gaming (just that it's a lot prettier and that it has a spookier theme). The only complaint I have is that it's extremely short: just about 4-6 hours depending on how quickly you find all the collectibles (if you even care about them). When I used to play similar games back then I always searched for all the collectibles and that's what I'm doing here in my 1. playthrough. If you want to enjoy the game without having to worry about missing stuff, and plan to get what you missed in your 2. playthrough, you will spend around 8 hours on 2 playthroughs which still is not that much.All in all, Pumpkin Jack is an amazing, yet short, nostalgic 3D-Platformer with a silly cast of characters. The short playtime may be off putting to some players but it's definitely worth your money on sale.

The weapons are all fun and i wanted to use all of the new ones as soon as i got them ( Favourite turned out to be the shotgun).  The puzzles were great and fairly easy and the mini-games were a fun break from the core game.The game took about 7 hours for a blind %100 run and about 5.5 hours were for the story and just taking a little extra time to check nooks for collectables. _childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack starts out as a very good platformer, then quickly fails miserably.STORY: The land is peaceful.  It's so peaceful, the Devil decides to make it chaotic by bringing about the undead unto the world.  A wizard is brought in to combat the evil.  So the Devil sends Pumpkin Jack down to fight the wizard.CONTROLS/GAMEPLAY:This game is a platformer, so controls are easy.  One button is to attack, the other is to jump.  You are also given a bird companion.  He can make an attack from a short distance, or knock down some barriers.  Look out for the skulls.  They are currency, and you can trade them for outfits.  And if you have taken damage, you can destroy boxes or barrels to regain some life.  Checkpoints are not far away, and you can refill your life there.  Occasionally, you will be taken to a different area of the game where Jack is only a pumpkin head.  He can move around and jump.  You have to figure out a puzzle.  It could be pushing a bomb into some dynamite.  Or some mushrooms will glow to play a song, and you have to hit the same mushrooms.  PROS: The story is very good.  The graphics are very beautiful.  And the music gives the whole game a Halloween type of vibe.  This can be enjoyed by all ages.  CONS: I really hate to say this, because the game has so much potential.  The controls are way too twitchy.  Jack will jump sporadically; moving left or right.  He may or may not grab a hold onto ledges.  Pushing the controller even a little bit will have Jack running off the platforms at full speed.  It doesn't help you will be fighting the camera angles every step of the way.  You might have played games like Ratchet & Clank or Sly Cooper on the PS2. That is what you're expecting here.  But Pumpkin Jack doesn't have the polish, and the results will be many deaths as Jack falls to his doom.OVERALL: I put nearly three hours into this game, and it was a chore to stay alive.  Jack has too much trouble running off platforms, refusing to grab ledges, and changing multiple directions while jumping to make this fun.  If these problems were fixed, Pumpkin Jack could be one of the best platformers ever.

_childDocuments_.review: ✅Great spoopy theme/music✅Wide array of puzzles✅Nostalgic 2000’s art look n’ feel➖Rough animations➖Bad combat➖Constant puzzle reuseSPOOKTOBER REVIEW #2Game World: Pumpkin Jack (PJ) takes place in a world that reminds me of early 2010’s art style. Kind of like a mash up between World of Warcraft and MediEvil. In fact, I would say a large majority of the game reminds me of MediEvil. The game itself is a vibrantly colored Halloween-themed world full of skeletons, graveyards, crows, and of course pumpkins. You traverse the world mostly through platforming via double jump. There are about 5 different levels that each have the same spooky theme but with some different settings, like a mine, a forest, a war-torn city, a swamp, and a northern snowy area. Overall, I felt the game world was one of the best parts about PJ. I really dug the nostalgic elements that reminded me of games in the late 2000s. Narrative: At first I would describe the narrative and writing in PJ to be akin to the juvenile banter of a Saturday morning cartoon, which I don’t consider a positive. However, as the game hit the midway point through the end, the writing started to improve and the dialog started to grow on me. That being said, don’t go into this game expecting a deep story. This is a typical good versus bad where you happen to play as the bad guy. The story delivers what you might expect from a good vs bad scenario, just with the outcomes flipped. Nothing phenomenal, just okay. Length: The length is around under 6 hours to beat the game. It could probably be around 4 hours if there weren't so many reused puzzles over and over. Mechanics: I did not enjoy PJ from a mechanical gameplay perspective. First of all, the combat was borderline atrocious. It really feels like an afterthought. There is no enemy stagger, so every fight is just a brawl of dodging and swinging. Especially towards the end of the game you’ll have dozens of projectiles flying at you and some of them are even the same color as the health orbs that you pick up, making combat into even more of a sh**show. You’ll end up with 5 weapons, but they all seem to suck except for the shotgun. Many of the weapons you’ll be locked in an animation when attacking and you have no invulnerability window from being hit so your health will just divebomb. I don’t want to say this game is difficult, because it isn’t but the shortcomings in combat are very evident when there are breakable objects everywhere that restore your health, making any sort of deep system obviously not intended. Aside from the bad combat, there are no upgrades at all and mechanically there is a jump, attack, and shoot crow button. That’s it. By far the worst part of the game for me and why I almost stopped playing. The puzzles are decent, if they weren’t constantly reused over and over. There’s only so many times I can handle a flying/race scenario where I have to shoot/jump over and over. Literally like 15x in the game. And while I appreciate the creativity of some of the other puzzles, like matching 2 tombstone names, or getting the right shape into the hole, repetition is always an issue here. Difficulty: Not too difficult. There are some sections like the bosses or the constant reused puzzle where you will insta-die and have to restart, but the majority of the game is fairly easy and overloads you with health pickups to make up for its shortcomings in combat. Quality: The graphical quality in PJ is pretty bad, think PS3-era graphics at best. It's the art style that won me over. The game really nails the whimsical spooky Halloween setting. Performance: I found the technical aspects of PJ to be adequate, if not lacking a bit. There is the ability to lock FPS, so I maintained a 60 FPS quite easily with no issues of dips. Other graphical options seem basic with no vast improvement. I did notice what appeared to be either graphical bugs or ghost-platforms many times in the swamp level, it was hard to tell, which is unfortunate. i9-13900KF | RTX 4090 | 64GB RAM | 1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSDSound Effects: The sound effects are okay. Didn’t really notice anything noteworthy here. The only voice acting in the game was from the narrator during cutscenes. Music: Musical score was good. There were many songs that were Halloween-themed versions of classical music. Made the constant chase puzzles slightly more endurable. Not too much unless you want to go back and get collectables or achievements. I found Pumpkin Jack to be okay. I honestly expected better, but it looks and feels like a super budget version of MediEvil. At times, the world is so nostalgic and endearing with its spoopyness vibe that it's fun, but other times the annoyingly shallow combat comes around and makes you wonder if it's worth it to finish the game. I would say overall yes, it was a more positive experience than negative, but not by much. Still, the game is definitely worth it when it's on sale. I don’t think you can go wrong for a $4 investment here. You can find my curator page here:

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A pretty cool and fun, albeit a clunky and pretty easy, platform game that feels like a PS1-PS2 era action-adventure akin to something like the Medievil series.Overall: This game is fun, and I do think it is worth a playthrough if you need a breather from all of the FPS, F2P with MTX, minecraft-esque games out there. However, 30 bucks is a bit steep for a game that, if played only from start to finish, is about 6-7 hours without going for 100%, and with how easy it is to get the collectibles it will only take a few hours more if that (it took be a bit longer due to exploring and me just getting older; hand-eye coordination aint what it used to be). Most of the game is very easy, with only a few parts being a bit tough due to some of the clunky controls; games don't have to be Dark Souls, and even though most of the game was a cake walk I still had fun going through it. Here is a list of positives and negatives:Pros: - Funny story and characters that don't take themselves super seriously. It's nice to have a laugh rather than a game trying to be too serious. - Gameplay isn't too bad for the most part. It's a good platformer game. - Game promotes a bit of exploration without having to be an "open world" game. Games can have players explore without having to be a huge, mainly empty plain of existence and instead have a nice, condensed world that has a straight-forward line with a few hidden areas if the player looks around. Thank you, Pumpkin Jack, for not following the open world trope and sticking to the old-school game world concept of the late 90's/early 2000's. - Both the settings and music are superb! Beautiful, rich and cartoony worlds with whimsical and magical music - a very good combo! - That game has character skins... that are earned by playing the game! I know it's hard to believe due to the current game environment with have with MTX (microtransactions) flooding our existence, but there was  time in gaming in which players actually earn their cosmetics through gameplay, and Pumpkin Jack does this!Cons: - Clunky combat and mechanics. I know action platformer combat isn't supposed to be the groundbreaking part of the game, but ugh it's just a slog to go through at times with Pumpkin Jack. I found myself just mashing attack while dodging, and even then I was trying to avoid combat by just spamming the crow magic missile over and over when I could. Enemies sometimes have no reaction to being hit, and thus their attacks still go through and often can almost kill Jack if overwhelmed, and the reason I point this out is that some areas feel like a mob-rush and what I just described makes the player not want to fight in melee range. One puzzle I had an absolute pain in doing was the last level's Santa Present Jack-Head one; mechanics of that puzzle felt way off for some reason, with any time I ran into a present making it hard to hit the thing into the objective. - Weapons and crow friend feel a bit lacking. After a while, I found myself only using two late game weapons (the "Magic Wand" and "The Spell"), the early game weapons felt forgettable. I'm not saying the first level weapon should be on par or better than later game weapons, but I don't see a point of a weapon inventory wheel if the vast majority of weapons are just gonna fall off and no longer be used. Crow friend, on the other hand, is very useful up to the point even the main bad guy has to come up with a way to nerf him, which is a bit telling lol. - Collectibles are way too easy to get. The Crow Skulls, which are both a currency and kind of feel like the blue coins from Super Mario Sunshine, are way too easy to get. The whole point of a collectible, no matter if it is a currency, should challenge the player. Most are just staring right at you as you pass by, and the most challenging ones are just a few platform hops away to get. The Gramophones, on the other hand, actually do this quite well, as they're normally placed on the road less traveled.@ The developer: Here are some suggestions for Pumpkin Jack 2 if you decide to make it - 1. Make the weapons have a secondary "tool" feature. Having the weapons have another function outside of just being a weapon will help with the longevity of usefulness of the item. Example, make the shovel be able to dig up stuff in certain spots.2. Make enemies only weak to certain weapons. This will also give the weapons more purpose, and would give more of a reason for a item wheel. Could make for some interesting boss fights if the bosses need multiple different weapons to take down at certain phases!3. Make enemies react more when they're hit. Im not asking to make the player a "stun-hit god", but if you want players to use melee weapons, please work more on the combat.4. Give Jack and Crow pal abilities! Jack just having dodge and double jump is kinda boring, and magic-missile/Zelda boomerang crow is also boring. Having both earn abilities can make for not only more interesting gameplay, but can make revisiting levels fun as well! For example, making Jack's Head an ability that allows for exploration of levels and doing puzzles rather than being only for puzzle levels.5. Make the Crow Skulls harder to find! I want them to feel like an accomplishment and not just a "Mario Coin". I would rather have 5 every well hidden skulls than just having them float in my path. Look at the above suggestions and use both abilities and weapons needed to get them, that would be fun!Overall dude, you made a good game, and I hope you make another regardless if you use my suggestions of cast them aside. Best of luck, and thank you for a fun game!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly blown away with how much fun I had with this game. So I was scrolling through Steam trying to find something to play and I honestly just couldn't find anything that remotely called my attention. I wanted something in the spirit of Halloween but not too over done (i.e haunted house sims or any game similar to it). Then I suddenly stumbled across this game and once I saw the trailer I immediately wanted it. It looked fun and fresh and you guessed it, Halloween themed. It was all I was asking for in one game. Little did I know that once I would start playing it I'd get addicted. The game not only  has fantastic wholesome visuals, amazing soundtrack and gameplay but it was also highly reminiscent to a lot of games I used to play when I was a kid growing up which made the entire experience feel oddly nostalgic throughout for me. I would highly recommend this to anyone who has the spare cash. My only gripe was that the game was sadly short. I beat it within 4 hours but the replay value does make up for it. Honestly amazing work for a solo developer, hopefully the game gets DLC or extra content in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: This game was incredibly nostalgic, though I had never played it before.It reminded me a lot of the first Banjo Kazooie game, as well as Tooie. There are a lot of similar elements and game mechanics. It feels like an early 2000s classic N64 #D platformer with a modern twist. I would recommend this game to anyone who likes a straightforward, non-intensive game. It was very easy to play and complete.The battles were difficult enough to keep me playing, and the character dialogue was funny and charming. I look forward to playing more games by this developer and publisher.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10A short and sweet, spooky adventure. As soon as i saw the trailer a couple years ago, i knew then that it was right up my alley, as someone who grew up playing and loving a ton of platformer games during the ps2 era, this was like a trip down the memory lane. Beautiful aesthetics and level design. Perfect game for the fall season when it's nice and chilly. Grabbed it when it was on sale but honestly i wouldn't mind paying full price. As i mentioned earlier, it is short and can be rushed through in 3-4 hours so if you're expecting a 10+ hour adventure, this isn't it. But if you're nostalgic for old school platformers but with nicer, modern graphics, getting this game is a no brainer.P.S the game has controller support and i highly recommend playing this game (or any other platformer) with a controller for best experience. i used my xbox controller and no setup was required.

Get it on sale due to length +Steam trading cards (5 drop, 9 to make a badge)Steam achievements (33, single playthrough)Easy to 100% without any guides"Oldschool" feeling (remind me of PS2 games)6 different levels (you can replay any of them from the menu)6 weapons to pick from (shovel, scythes, shotgun, magic and talking sword)6 different bosses with different phasesMinigames to break the pace (races, mining cart, flying gargoyle ...)7 different skins are unlockable by finding collectables in levels Pretty decent options menuI am a huge fan of the soundtrack which twists a lot of classics Voice acted cinematics between missions with pretty well done pictures Each level is about 30-60 minutes Solid graphics I haven't encountered any bugs -The jumping feels off which is a huge issue in 3D platformer Not a big fan of the camera in some situations About 90% of my deaths were because of instakill scenariosIngame dialogue has no voice over 30 euro may be a bit too much for 6 hour game, which can be done in 3 if you ignore collectables The story doesn't have a satisfying ending+/-I had to replay 1 mission because achievements stopped unlocking but I am not sure if it is my , steam's or game's fault

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this game up on a whim for $3.59 and i'm happy that i did. Every level offers a unique mini-game, a scavenger hunt to find items hidden around the map and the player is rewarded a new weapon after defeating the levels boss. With how much i enjoyed the game my only complaint would be that i wish it was longer but for the price i paid for it i definitely got my monies worth because this game delivered above my expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: Severely mediocre!  Gameplay has absolutely no depth; combat is as simple as press LMB/X/Square to string the same 3 attack "combo" together over and over; platforming is as simple as jump up these platforms/boxes to reach the top of this tower, jump over this gap, dodge these swinging hazards and so on.The weapons don't even feel unique because they're all limited by the same 3-4 string attacks. What could be a charming and fun game set inside a uniquely "spooky" world is severely hindered by the fact that the core gameplay is so simplistic that the rest of it falls apart.  The game feels like it's trying to mimic classic early 2000s platformer gameplay (e.g. Medieval, Spyro, Ratchet and Clank, etc.) but it is outclassed by the very games it tries to be.I got the game for free from a friend who had a spare from a Humble bundle and it pains me to say it, but it isn't even worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a definition of 4/10 . You can tell they have tried to make a good game, but every part of this game is mediocre to bad. Combat is boring and unresponsive. Even if the game have 6 weapons they share most of the attacks and all of them feel the same. This game have like 3 types of enemies that essentially just rush you and spam lots of homing projectiles. You will constantly loose health and refill it with breakables around you, which is really bizzare gameplay decision. Bossess are just bad and all of them work the same. Boss does his schtick for like a 30 seconds and then you can stun him and then wack on him until he is invincible again which is repeated three times every bossfight. Levels are just long corridors that are functionally the same from start to finish. There are 6 of them and they are really too long. Collectables are easy to obtain and exist as a currency to buy samey looking costumes. Music is not annoying but really not memorable. Plot of this game tries to be Overlord(game not anime) but less dark humor and more referencess to pop culture. Easiest example to show that is match two minigame from level 5 that uses surnames of characters from LOTR, Game of Thrones,Matrix etc. and expect you to take this as a haha funny joke. It fails at that misserably. Considering this game last around 6 hours to 100%, you dont have runtime to make this world intresting or memorable.  It feels like a remaster of a mediocre action platformer from ps2. I recommend picking up this game if you are desperate for more action platformers and even that at high discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is one of the best indie 3D Platformers out there, no question. Though it may have a smaller runtime for some at around 4-5 hours if you're trying to get all collectibles, the game is beautiful, engaging, with a story and overall presentation that doesn't take itself too seriously. I can easily recommend this to any fans of the genre and if you haven't picked this up yet, good news - it's often on sale making this an even easier recommend.Gameplay-wise you're running and jumping through mostly linear levels with basic combat sections, puzzle sections, and collectibles galore. I'm a huge collectathon fan so Pumpkin Jack certainly delivers on that front. By collecting crow masks you can unlock skins which are well made and I'm happy to see they are purely earned in game. If you don't care for cosmetics, these collectibles offer no other benefit outside of satisfying that collectathon itch and based on some trickier placement for some of these, I was happy to collect close to 100% of them as I went off the beaten path happily. There are also gramophones that are fairly hidden to seek out to unleash those sweet dance moves. If you've ever wanted to see in undead humanoid with a pumpkin for a head dance then I guess this is the game for you!Bosses are a highlight in Pumpkin Jack and offer a little difficulty but let me be very clear, this is a very easy and approachable game, especially for a game that has combat. Combat can mostly be approached with little thought and with a ranged attack, if you want to just let your companion handle most enemies you can do that for the most part. Health is everywhere and can be accessed by destroying various barrels, barricades, and other destructibles. All in all, if you don't have much experience playing 3D platformers and don't want something difficult to play to see if the genre is for you, then this is a pretty good entry point.With fun little puzzle sections and dynamic flying or mine cart sections to mix things up, a fitting soundtrack with a playful spooky vibe, and visuals that are gorgeous with optional raytracing, Pumpkin Jack kept my attention for the entirety of its runtime. It's not the most expansive, groundbreaking staple of the genre but it doesn't need to be. It's a game that captures some of that magic from classic Rare games and MediEvil titles in a tight runtime that doesn't overstay its welcome. I can easily recommend it and I'd love to see a sequel one day!For more indie game recommendations check out my Steam Curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a pretty alright game, all things considered! There were several headache-inducing moments for me, but I still had fun.I absolutely adore the visuals of this game. The models and assets feel well developed, and the character design is striking and unique. It's also very colorful and manages to capture the true Halloween spirit. It kinda reminded me of Nightmare Before Christmas some.I also enjoy the storyline and the character writing. I love the concept of playing as the villain, and instead of being on a mission to save the world, we're on a mission to destroy it. All of the characters have unique personalities, and seeing the way they clash and butt heads with Jack is entertaining.I enjoyed the level design, although I couldn't say I found the parkor particularly challenging, it was all fairly easy. The game is also very forgiving with health, giving you lots of objects to use to refill your health, should you take any hits.Unfortunately, I found a lot of the minigame gameplay sections, like the pumpkin head areas and fast travel via horse, gargoyle, or go-cart finnicky and frustrating. Perhaps that's because I was playing on my keyboard and this game is meant for controller, but I found myself having to change my keybinds during some of the later minigame segments.I also found the boss fights very unenjoyble. They felt incredibly finnicky and a lot of the timed prompts would just barely give you enough time to get them. If you were delayed by even a second, you would miss a whole sequence and drag the fight out for even longer. I ended up spending two hours on the witch fight because Jack's weird auto-aim kept making me miss hitting the potions back and would instead send them flying in a random direction.Overall, I wouldn't say I hate this game, far from it. It does its atmosphere and characters right, and most of the game is fairly enjoyable, especially if you're looking for some Halloween vibes in the middle of the year, or during the spooky month itself, you might just have to be prepared for some brief moments of headache, and also maybe play with a controller and not a keyboard.

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a simple and straightforward game that attempts to claim a spot in the rankings of the oversaturated 3D platforming genre and succeeds with flying colors. It demonstrates a thorough grasp of what made PS2-era platformers work and recreates that magic beautifully while still feeling unique and having its own personality. It merges witty writing and solid gameplay with fun puzzles and challenging but fair collectibles. It even gives you some customization with multiple weapon choices and costumes to unlock to personalize your combat style and version of jack. All of these elements are sewn together beautifully to create an enjoyable game front to back that deserves a spot next to the platforming icons it emulates. My only criticism is that the scrapped jack designs and skins from earlier development stages shown in the credits were not added to the game. they could have been a fun reward for completing the story or reaching 100% on collectibles. To the developer: keep up the good work! Pumpkin Jack is a spectacular game you deserve to be proud of, and i look forward to your future as a game developer.

It takes some great inspiration without falling into a lot of the trappings those games' lack of hindsight could bring about.

_childDocuments_.review: Carefully said, a pretty decent to good 3D indie platformer from a single dev. Yeah, I know, I might be a bit understating, but I’m only saying ‘decent’ in this case, because in comparison to such old and new genre masterpieces like Spongebob, Spyro, Hat in Time and the like, or even mid-Indie ones like New Super Lucky Tale or the beloved (or by some people hated) Yooka-Laylee it definitely shows that the game is lacking in some aspects. I’d definitely rather rank it into the region of smaller projects like Effie, Ginger or the meanwhile delisted Skylar&Plux. But hey, being a one-man-project that’s natural and unavoidable I guess. Yeah, I admit, that’s a lot of judgment for a first statement, so out of general fairness I probably owe it to explain a bit more what I’m meaning. And after all, after that you can judge for yourself if those aspects are a turn-off for you or not. Alright, where do I start. I think the gameplay in itself is rather solid (with a casual to easy difficulty, the only spike being the final boss fight), and you can definitely see how much love the dev put into the game and the different backgrounds/levels, so generally this really makes my heart go boom. The effort literally can be felt oozing out everywhere, no kidding. But, I don’t know, I just wasn’t hooked. Probably the biggest problem in my opinion is the overall repetition of nearly all elements. You see, for example there’s a ride/run in EVERY level, and though they are admittedly a bit different (horse/gargoyle/boat/mine cart etc.), they are still pretty much the same in execution. And this makes the game predictable and boring. Those rides are even often repeated THRICE inside a level. And the same goes for the minigames. As cool as they are, but as soon as I played one, I already knew, alright, I have to at least do 2-3 of them in the next minutes. Good advice to the dev, please don’t overuse those mechanics, as they tire players too soon. And the same also applies to the dialogs. I would have wished for more variation (after playing for an hour, I pretty much read/seen it all).  Hmm, what else. Another thing to work on probably are the fights. Though the different weapons are kind of cool, there’s nearly no point in switching. It’s mostly mindless hack/slash button-mashing (dodging in limited spaces is kind of useless anyway) until the enemies are done, and therefore feels empty. Double jump is imprecise, especially if you try to jump around a corner. Camera angles are awful in boss fights sometimes (like scenery/walls clip into the view). Engine-wise I definitely had some problems as well. The DX12 version crashed when using Gecata and didn’t save my options (especially the post processing was always reset to low when I started anew). DX11 worked, but somehow V-Sync was messed up then (so I had to use my Nvidia Control for that). And another thing, graphics-wise the game was extremely blurry due to the heavy depth of field effects (some people also maybe will dislike the chromatic aberration). Sadly the game has no settings for those, so I had to resort to administer my own changes in the engine.ini file. Seriously, before I really got into playing I literally had to try out lots of fixes to get the game in a state that I could live with.Anyway, I know this all might sound kind of harsh, but nevertheless, all this criticism and the medium length issue aside, I definitely can’t help but to recommend this little game. For a single dev it’s still outstanding work, soundtrack is great, and I’m definitely looking forward to any future projects of him. Just keep all those aspects I mentioned in mind, and also consider if the pretty high price tag is worth that for yourself (disclaimer: I myself got it in Humble Choice, so for me it was absolutely perfect in this regard).

_childDocuments_.review: +-10h 4/10 1 No Not yet, the game is brand new. It is very doable to complete it without a guide.  1 on Astats No No, there is level selection No No No No No difficulty option There should not be any glitchy achievements in the final release. I experienced a problem with one achievement not unlocking while playing a few weeks before the release. This game blew me away. Before I had even played it, I already thought that looked amazing but while playing it for the first time, I totally fell in love with everything about it and it is even better than it had looked. I honestly believe that this is one of  best games released in 2020 so far. It has so much charm and humour. I even heard myself talking back to the game with the same sarcasm it was giving me. For example; the first time you set a part of the surroundings on fire your companion, a crow, asks you; "Do you know that fire burns things," and my first response irl out loud was "Noooo... really?!?" ] The dialogue has a lot of these witty moments throughout the whole game, it is so funny and a sheer joy to play.  is a Third Person, 3D Platformer which has a total of 6 levels, the first one is really quite small but of course, as you go on, they will become a lot bigger. Playing through the game will take you around 7 hours, while you're trying to find as many collectibles as you can. Thankfully, there is a Level Selection, as you may need to go back later on to previous levels, just to find any you may have missed, if you are looking to 100% this game but they are very doable and once somebody makes a guide it will be a piece of cake to 100% the game. What I really found wonderful is how each level is so uniquely different. Not only are the settings different but in each level, there are mini-games where you have to leave your body and play as just the pumpkin head. The mini-games are different from one another as well. In most levels there is also a sort of phase in which you ride along on something and have to try and not get hit by the environment, this can be riding a mine-cart, riding a horse, sailing a boat... things like that. Each level ends with your traditional boss fight and those are also very varied from one other. All of these differences kept the game fresh and so much fun to play through. You just never knew what the game was going to throw at you next and that's no bad thing. During my gameplay,  I did discover a few small bugs but when I told the developer about them, they quickly picked those up and fixed them. It was very nice to see those problems getting fixed so fast and that they even took the time to respond back to me every time I had a question or I had found a bug to report, it is especially nice when you consider that this must be a very busy period, as they will be getting ready to launch this excellent game.I played this game with a controller and had no problems with it at all. Jack can jump further than I expected in the beginning, which is very nice. I haven't tried this game with KB+M so I can't say anything about playing the game with those. Most achievements are acquired for beating the mini-games, the rides and the bosses. The other achievements are for obtaining all the collectibles within each level. So, nothing grindy to report there.As I stated above, I have totally fallen in love with this game, so I have no hesitation in saying that  is totally worth your time and money... Especially for having fun during Halloween or even the Christmas season.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game this summer and planned to play it this halloween for some good old spooky fun. I didn't have much expectations, but the visual style gripped me so much- it couldn't be bad... right?I was absolutely right on the money. This game, whilst no mario Odyssey, is one hell of a 3d platformer! Controls are tight- The jumps feel just rightThe weapons are fun and varied too! (Even if some weapons are a lot more useful than others-) The combat is a fun and welcome experience that breaks up the traversal, even if it is a little shallow after playing it for a couple of hours. Enemies are varied, if a little too underplayed (I would have honestly taken a common enemy type or two), the roll is quite useful and can combo into an attack of its own! (The fourth weapon in particular's is absolutely balls to the walls busted-). The difficulty is nothing to write home about, but this is obviously a game for young children to teen, so I'll let it slide (Pretty much everything destructible in the game gives you health and checkpoints refill your healthbar quite often)The vehicle segments are quite welcome and break the pace! The music in these segments also change to classical music reimagined with a halloween skin and it feels very nice to hear it as you're galloping away into the darkness-That does not apply to the second to last vehicle segment. The music and idea are nice and whilst I aim to not spoil what happens... let's just say that remapping your controls is absolutely obligatory for those who'll play on keyboard. My hand was cramped by the end of it.Let's talk about the music! Eerie, sinister, yet joyful and spooky, the game's music grips you and puts you right into that cute/spooky halloween vibe. Not a single track is redundant, but none stand out too much as masterpieces of their genre. As a whole, however, it may be the most halloween sounding- thing- I have ever heard.Pumpkin Jack's aesthetic instantly catches the eye and makes you travel in a dreary, yet colorful world which'll keep you interested the entire way through. A slight overuse of purple in the beginning, but the game's vistas all look very distinct and have a character all their own.The story is incredibly basic, but serves its purpose and allows you to put yourself in the shoes of an evil lad who's just here to cause trouble (And not tip anyone)In conclusion, this game is a solid buy for your kids or those who dare to stay young and enjoy a cute halloween experience. It is completely family friendly fun who, whilst it doesn't exactly last too long (around 10 hours), is worth your time and money. If you're willing to wait, catch it in a sale and you'll get a steal that Jack himself would be proud of! A comfy experience the entire way through, the best way to play is to snuggle up in a blanket and be willing to let your inner kid take over for the time which you'll give the game.7.5 out of 10Absolutely try it outCongrats to the team!

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a very solid PS1/N64 era 3D platformer. There are some pacing issues, and small graphical glitches here and there, but considering it was primarily developed by a single person, it's really impressive work!Performance wise-Pumpkin Jack runs very smooth. I never saw any dips below 100 fps at 2560x1080 on a single GTX 1080 + Ryzen7 2700X. It supports ,  monitors,  settings, has built in  (60, 120, 144, & uncapped) and you can even toggle between ! One of the biggest issues I had with the game was actually caused by my custom FOV settings. Some boss fights and a handful of platforming sections have a higher, than normal default, FOV. If you play with a very high FOV (120), like myself, you may need to lower it, for these sections-or it could lead to some frustration.Over all, I found the game just too damn easy-excluding the final boss fight. You are constantly given health pickups & can basically button mash your way to victory-using very little strategy. I would have loved to seen a little more depth to the combat-some simple combos, or at least a reason to use something besides the shotgun.I'm happy I finally decided to pick this up. I know my 1 year old son is going to love it, when he gets older. Can't wait to see what you do in the future! Best of luck to you, Nicolas! 3.5/5

Characters you meet through your journey is goofy and they are funny. Interaction between characters always made me chuckle. Gameplay is really good. You start with a simple shovel. _childDocuments_.review: Definitely not worth 30 bucks. If you get it, pick it up on sale. I think it's crazy this dude is charging that much for 6 levels that almost can all be completed within 10-15 minutes. An absolute MAX of 30 minutes if you're really struggling. For reference, had I completely ignored all of secret hunting (I mostly did) I would have beat this game in less than 2 hours. The levels are all very equally repetitive, which drives me nuts for the price, honestly. If you're going to charge 30 bucks for a game, at least make it varied enough to justify the price.  If you do one of the "puzzles", you'll do it again within five minutes, usually with a slight difficulty tweak. The same can be said for any traversal sections, which are all equally monotonous. Levels are incredibly linear with small side paths that lead to optional secrets (crow skulls to buy costumes).I died a total of 6 times. Each time to the environment.  If you fall into water or a pit, it's an instant restart back to the last checkpoint, which can be annoying because the game doesn't have the most perfectly polished controls. The combat is not the strong suit of this game. It's a very straightforward spam-fest.  You get a few different weapons, but in my opinion only two of them actually feel good to use. The other ones are just very, very slow. All of the weapons also feel like they do the same amount of damage, which doesn't really make sense, but I'd have to play through the game again (I won't) to see. A lot of the dialogue repeats and there's no voice acting for anything outside of the cutscenes between levels. I mostly look at this as a negative ONLY because every time there's interactions in game, this massive splash text appears on the bottom right of the screen and can block your view for a minute until it decides to go away. The same dialogue is also usually repeated over and over again. Again, with the repetitiveness, each level contains a boss. Each boss basically does the same exact attacks as the previous boss. Sure, the colors of the AOEs change, but you might as well be fighting the same exact boss as you did in the first level. The ONLY boss I can think of that had any kind of variation was the swamp boss, and if you play the game, you'll see what I mean. Adding to the repetition of this game, you have to do everything 3 times with the bosses. Nothing changes. They don't do any new moves, they don't change their patterns. Yes, they all look different and have different style arenas (though most are just giant circles), but when you're basically just repeating what you've already done 3 other times, it just feels lazy. I will say that the game does look good, but that's really about all it has going for it. It has the vibes of a nostalgic PS2 era platformer, which is the reason why I think so many people enjoy it, but vibes alone don't make a game worth playing. Honestly, I think I would have liked this game more had I not had to repeat every single little thing 2-3 times per level to make any progress. Thankfully, it's not a long game. Had this game been twice the length, I would have just had to put it down and walkaway. I'm also mostly only leaving a negative review for the price/time ratio. There's no justification for charging 30 dollars for a game that could easily be beaten within 2 hours when it has zero replayability (outside of secret hunting.)

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack:~~~~~~~~~~~ The Arc En Ciel Kingdom is just bliss. All the inhabitants are prospering, and the cohabitation between humans and animals has hit a new high! The sky is blue, and nature is beautiful, full of life and colour; it’s truly a peachy paradise! So sweet and so dull. . . That is exactly what the Devil thought about the Arc En Ciel Kingdom. “Let’s spice it up, shall we!” shouts the Devil, bounding off his chair and looking at the pathetic Kingdom.  Then, with a blink of his eyes, he inflicts the region with the worst malediction ever. . .  the curse of the Eternal Night!  But the Humans loved their peachy lives, and so they called upon the greatest wizard of the land to eradicate the evil curse and its monsters. “NO… NO… NO…” screamed the Devil! He too has his champion! The biggest trickster of all time, and he’ll eliminate the wizard. So, get ready peasants, because his majesty the Devil is sending to the Kingdom, Jack . . . Pumpkin Jack! Pumpkin Jack is a colourful action 3D platformer game developed by Nicolas Meyssonnier and published by Headup Game on the 24th of October 2020 on the Steam platform. The game is also available on Xbox One and Nintendo Switch. The game consists of six levels in total, which all include a boss fight at the end to successfully complete them. What an excellent and well-thought-out game Pumpkin Jack is. At the start of the first of level, you have a fantastic, illustrated introduction, and then the pleasure of seeing a new one each time you reach another stage. From the second stage to the last, it will be a recollection of what you went through on the previous level and what is coming up next. I really enjoy this type of storytelling which, by the way, is well narrated with funny dialogue that keeps you entertained between levels. After Jack crash-landed his pumpkin head into Arc En Ciel like a meteor that crashed into another planet, the first level will start. As you can imagine, Jack will be a bit disoriented for a short time, but soon after, he will meet an owl, sent by the Devil himself.   Jack will be able to talk to the owl a few times within each level, which you might give you a few laughs. The owl will also be at checkpoints where you can save your progress.  Early on, Jack will also meet a scarecrow, who turns out to be some sort of secondary weapon, as Jack can send him to attack an enemy from a distance. In term of weapons, Jack will first use a shovel to defeat monsters, humans and other weird enemies, and he will be rewarded with a new weapon each time he defeats a boss.What makes Pumpkin Jack so much fun to play is the way the developer manages to bring us a game that links with great artwork, great storytelling and a spooky atmosphere, all mixed into a variety of gameplay. There is the classic style of 3D platformer where you have to find a specific path (which in this game is basically following the cut ropes), as well as mini-games, races and a couple of fast-paced parkours, all of which is super fun! In all the levels, Jack arrives at some sort of an impasse, and nearby you find a rock structure which has a body of a small well and a pumpkin head instead of a roof. At which point Jack twists off his head from his body and dumps it into the well. The mini games are a great addition and are easy to figure out. Depending on the level, there are also either races or fast-paced parkour twice per level. Not only that, but there are also collectables to find. Each level will have 20 hidden masks and one hidden gramophone.  If you manage to find the gramophone in each stage, Jack will show you his dancing talent, which makes me wonder if there is some sort of talent show in Hell (perhaps something like, Monster Got Talent in Hell). In any case, Jack can groove, let me tell you. With the masks you collect, you can buy Pumpkin Jack new skins when you find the location of the creepy hidden salesman. In terms of the enemy, there are not too many, and I must say they were easy to eliminate, including the bosses. In fact, most of Jack’s deaths in my playthrough occurred in parkours or when I didn’t manage to reach a platform and fell to my death. I think only one boss gave me a couple of fatalities; apart from that I sailed through pretty quickly. I think one big point this game is missing is the ability to change the level of difficulty and as far as I can see is set as one for all. It’s a shame because the game would have been even better with the possibility to increase the level of difficulty, and therefore also increase the level of replayability. Nonetheless, you are able to replay a completed level in case you haven’t found all the masks and gramophones.  I thoroughly enjoyed my time with Pumpkin Jack, and let’s face it, it’s not every day you can play the Devil’s champion.Overall, the game has stunning artwork, great soundtrack and runs well! I didn’t encounter any issues during my gameplay or after loading a saved game. Plenty of options in the settings and the game has been translated into 10 languages, including Polish, Turkish, Arabic and the other main languages. In terms of the length of the game, I finished my first playthrough in about 7 hours, and that was without finding all the masks (I have 90% of them) and gramophones (I’ve only found three so far). The controls are really responsive, and I recommend playing the game with a gamepad. Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Fabulous artwork+	Great levels design with spooky atmosphere+	Great story with plenty of humour+	A good 3D platformer with mini-games and fast-paced parkour per level+	Super fun to play+	Interesting boss fights+	Collectables to find+	Achievements and trading cardsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	Quite easy as you can’t change the level of difficulty -	A bit shortPlay the Devil’s advocate and destroy the Arc En Ciel Kingdom and its wizard champion as Pumpkin Jack!8/10 Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: The Short Summary:  8/10Pumpkin Jack is a short and straightforward 3D platformer that feels like something out of a Halloween cartoon.  The visuals are appealing and the game plays well, but is rather easy to 100% complete.  If you want something casual to play to get you into the spirit for Halloween, this is a great choice. The Full Review:The game is short and sweet.  You play as a character named Jack, whose soul has been bound to a pumpkin in order to grant him a physical body with which to set out on his quest.  At the behest of the Devil, Jack is tasked with eliminating the Champion of humanity, known simply as the Wizard.  Joined by an owl guide and a cowardly crow, you set out to track down and defeat the Wizard, thus dooming the world in the name of the Devil.Now, despite the rather grim-sounding plot, the game actually feels pretty lighthearted.  It feels like a cartoon and the dialogue made me chuckle a few times throughout the story.  The gameplay itself is straightforward, consisting of navigating levels and defeating enemies.  There are several chase sequences where you have to navigate obstacles while, for example, riding a mine cart over winding rails, and some mini-games where you navigate as Jack as just a pumpkin without his body.  The game is also very forgiving, as Jack can grab ledges if your jump is just a tad too short, and enemies as well as destructible objects will drop health orbs to keep Jack healthy.  You get a variety of weapons as you progress, which changes Jacks attacks a bit, but I don't know if any one weapon is more powerful than the rest.  You can switch weapons freely so use what suits your preference. Your crow companion can also attack enemies at range.Bosses are a little less forgiving, but learning their attack patterns and their weaknesses was not terribly difficult to do. I thought they were entertaining to face off against though.You have additional objectives to collect Crow Skulls and Gramophones, and doing this isn't too difficult.  Some are a bit sneakily hidden, but the Crow Skulls have a sound effect to let you know you're near one, and the Gramophones are usually down an alternate path that's easy to spot if you just keep your eyes open.  It didn't take me more than one additional run through a level to find all collectibles.  The levels are pretty linear so its not too difficult to find everything. I don't have much in the way of criticism.  Some may see the story as simple and short, but I don't think this game meant to be some vast epic tale.  Navigating some of the chase sequences could be a little tricky at times, particularly the ones where there are things flying toward you that you need to avoid (especially the final chase at the end of the swamp level.  It was sometimes hard to gauge if Jack was out of the way of the incoming projectile or not.  If you're a veteran gamer, Pumpkin Jack will be a breeze.  But the visuals and humor made it a worthwhile playthrough for me.  I enjoyed my run through the game and may revisit it during an upcoming spooky season.  :)

I either don't make the jump or i over jump by a huge margin. So I have to inch along because I feel like I have no control over the main character. When I stop moving the controller he continues to move for a bit, enough that it's noticable during game play. For a completionist like me it took me a total of 5.8 hours to do everything in the game and unlock every little collectable. Now the game is insanely easy, like the word easy doesn't do it justice, I'm pretty sure a 5 year old could beat this game with no issues whatsoever. But even though the game is quite easy it is extremely fun! :)Unfortunately the game costs 29,99€?????? I love this game, it's one hella of a great platformer game but the price tag is absolutely ridiculous! I bought it on sale for 23,99€ and I don't regret it since it was one good evening filled with lots of fun. BUT I do not recommend buying this game for above 12€. Yes, it's not the best game ever, but it doesn't have to be - it's fine 6-7 hours mid-to-old school platformer with a decent gameplay, serviceable story wrapped in nice looks and all that for a reasonable price.It's not long, so it doesn't overstay it's welcome. _childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely what I wanted it to be!*It got nice platforming*Combat gets tougher as you go along*Each level has unique and increasingly tough bosses*The little segments (carts, horse riding, etc) are all unique to a level, so no feel of repeating something too much*Music hits just right*A lot of witty jokes in the style of Spinker (the dev of this game) and it is almost like you are talking straight to him when playing the game*NG+ to have repeat playthroughs with your favourite weapons you unlocked through the game!*Build in timer for the speed freaks under us*Pretty much no bugs that I discovered in general. Only one I found was when I jumped and got launched through the map, but that was just a minor set back and the only one that comes to mind in the whole playthrough!*Collectibles are neatly hidden, yet still have a nice glow and sound to them to have an easier time finding themThere were a couple things I did not like as much. No deal breakers, just hope they'll get an update in the future:*Minecart sections can be a bit tedious. There is a lack of feedback, making it feel like you sometimes just fail for no reason*The balance beams across some of the levels make you go really slow. I just wish we could increase the speed (and therefore the difficulty to cross the beams) by jumping at full speed.*When muted, the loading screen and menu scroll bar are still completely audible*When riding on a horse for the 3rd time, with RTX on I drop from 90-130fps down to 13fps due to a lot of water. Easy fix for now is just to turn off RTX for that section*I wish that attack combos would be a bit more consistent. Like attacking after a roll gives you a special attack, but not always and it makes combat a bit tedious at times*An added option for us to choose to play the game again without all the weapons unlocked.

_childDocuments_.review: I just got this game on the Steam Deck today as it was listed as Deck Verified.
