_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is an absolute delight and a breath of fresh air in the world of platforming adventures. Developed by Nicolas Meyssonnier, this Halloween-themed gem delivers an enchanting experience that is sure to capture the hearts of gamers young and old on the Steam platform.From the moment you step into the hauntingly beautiful world of Pumpkin Jack, you're greeted with visuals that are both charming and atmospheric. The game's art style is a true standout, with vibrant colors and detailed environments that bring the spooky setting to life. Each level is uniquely crafted, showcasing Meyssonnier's dedication to creating a visually stunning and immersive experience.The star of the show is undoubtedly our mischievous protagonist, Jack. With his charmingly eerie design and witty personality, Jack steals the spotlight and becomes an endearing character that players can't help but root for. The animation is smooth and expressive, adding an extra layer of personality to Jack's every move.But Pumpkin Jack isn't just a treat for the eyes—it excels in gameplay as well. The platforming mechanics are tight and responsive, offering a perfect balance of challenge and accessibility. From thrilling chases to clever puzzles, each level introduces new and exciting gameplay elements that keep the adventure feeling fresh and engaging.The level design is a true highlight, seamlessly blending diverse environments that range from eerie graveyards to spooky forests. The attention to detail is remarkable, and the inclusion of hidden secrets and collectibles encourages exploration, rewarding players for their curiosity.Accompanying Jack on his spooky journey is a hauntingly beautiful soundtrack that sets the perfect tone for the adventure. The atmospheric music enhances the overall experience, creating an immersive soundscape that complements the game's theme.Pumpkin Jack is more than just a Halloween-themed game; it's a masterfully crafted platformer that stands tall among its peers. With its captivating visuals, charming protagonist, and engaging gameplay, this title is a must-play for anyone seeking a memorable and delightful gaming experience on Steam. Whether you're a fan of platformers or just in the mood for a spooktacular adventure, Pumpkin Jack is an absolute triumph that deserves a place in your gaming library.

Kinda reminds me of Banjo-Kazooie... if Banjo were an "evil' spirit possessing a pumpkin. I did have to modify some settings as the jump mechanics and camera angling were awkward, which was a bit troubling for jumping. Also, the game keeps count and announces how many time your character dies which got to be a little annoying considering most falls kill Jack instantly. Overall, I had fun with this game initially. I did lose interest before finishing it, but had a good enough time before that so I'm still recommending it. If nothing else, it's a great game to play in early autumn to get you into the Halloween spirit ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a slightly above average 3D action platformer. As someone who is not the biggest fan of the genre, I can see why other people might like this game, even though it really wasn't for me. I can still see that Pumpkin has both positives and negatives, though.There's a lot to like about Pumpkin Jack. Pumpkin Jack has a strong Halloween design to its level and characters and decent musical tracks that fit the vibe. The gameplay is well varied, with puzzles, racing segments, combat, platforming, and other minigames. The definite highlight of this game are its bossfights - while they're the same old do something 3 times and the boss dies, the fights are pretty cinematic and are the only time the combat is truly challenging.The negatives are just as numerous as the positives. Pumpkin Jack splits its time between being a cakewalk and being frustrating. The combat outside of boss fights and puzzles were so trivially easy that it felt boring to play through, while the racing segments and platforming that wasn't just a straight line felt infuriating without any element of fun. Still, if you're a fan of these sorts of games you'd likely enjoy them more than me. The story is kind of bland, but I guess we don't expect complex narratives from games like this anyways. There were also some technical issues and bugs, but they didn't persist past the initial launch of the game so I can dismiss them.Honestly, if you like 3D platformers like Pumpkin Jack, you'd probably get some enjoyment out of this game. Personally, I can only just barely give it a recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: A Good, but Really Short game. Simple as that.Mostly just platforming & Puzzles, with a little bit of combat here & there, The combat isn't Massively expanded upon, its mostly just "Attack, Roll, attack, Repeat until all enemies dead"There's 21 different collectibles (20 skulls & 1 Gramophone) in each level, Each Gramophone is off to a small side-path somewhere, the skulls are a mix of Hidden, and in plain sight, the ones in plain sight usually require you to kill some enemies around the area, kill them all, you can then pick up the skull.The levels aren't very lengthy, on avg it took me 30~ mins each, but i was also looking out for the collectibles most of the time, so they're even shorter if you're just going straight to the boss fight at the end, probably 10-15~ mins each?The boss fights are pretty simple, Dodge attacks, wait for an opening, Attack, repeat 3 times and its dead, you get a new weapon and move onto the next chapter.I  Recommend this game if you want a quick game to complete and 100%, However; No offence to the devs But i honestly , £25 is an insanely high price for a game this small & short, Hell, even on sale at £10 is kinda pushing it a little. £6.99 would be a more reasonable price imo. _childDocuments_.review: It's a little short... too short. But it's a sweet little platformer. It has an aesthetic very similar to the classic Playstation title "Medievil" (1998). I loved the music and ambience. It got me in the mood for Spooktober, and it will definitely go into my "seasonal" games list.Gameplay wise, it's very simplistic: Explore, jump along platforms, find collectables, fight monsters. Combat is your run-of-the-mill hack and slash. Very simple.I particularly enjoyed the vehicle sections of each level. They were great diversions from the usual platforming.The puzzles in each level were OK, although in some cases it was  more of an annoying obstacle (looking at you, "Match the Pairs" puzzle).I liked the bosses. They were challenging without being particularly hard.What I noticed is that each level followed the same basic structure, but the puzzles, races, and bosses were all different and versatile. I liked that.I loved the humour in the game, and the corny banter between the main character and his minions and other characters. There wasn't much to the story, but it was fun to play the villain in this cute-spooky adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: A thoroughly enjoyable game with a quaint aesthetic and concept. Does not feel too short or too long. Gameplay feels smooth and polished and runs very well. Each mission is a neat pocket world of adventure and fun, and the collectibles are not a slog to collect. The story is passable but a funny and good ride nonetheless. These are the good things I'd like to say about the game, but there's a number of, if not flaws, unfortunate consequences as a result of the way the game was written, played through and designed.The game although not feeling too short or too long, is definitely too narrow. As per classic platformers with linear design and obvious cues, there's no real sense of expansiveness in both level design and storyboarding. What I mean by this is that everything about the game, from experiencing the story, to playing each level, to doing a completionist run, requires one playthrough - and that's it. 8 hours in (with 3 of them I was sitting idly because food or other responsibilities etc.) and I've collected every achievement and collectible in the game. I mean, not that that's really a bad thing, because achievements mean nothing anyway, but the game as a whole lasts you as good as a short Netflix series - shorter still if you don't go for completionist runs. What's even stranger still is that despite the game being short, and me remembering enjoying the experience while playing, I remember next to nothing about the game - and I just finished it 20 minutes ago. Like every level of the game is its own pocket experience, this game in entirety is like in its own special platformer pocket that you forget about and then hang in your closet forever once you're done with it. Another consequence that arises is that the game doesn't flesh out mechanics or game designs well enough to warrant any sort of real idea of progression in the game. This may not be important to some, but it does beg the question on bothering to not only include other weapons in the game, but also provide players the option to switch between them. Perhaps if you want to give yourself an extra challenge to kill everything with a shovel instead of a magic spell - but even that is still rather easily done. And that challenge is eclipsed by the shortlived nature of gameplay. And that brings me to my next criticism - how easy the game is. I can't remember how many times I was walking through a level and was trying to eye out collectibles only to reach structures I've seen before in different skins - like how there's a random tall tower with a path to beyond the level, but there's a "secret" platform behind the wall of the tower that still goes up and there's a crow skull! Or perhaps there's a random bunch of boxes on a platform that serves no purpose - oh wait it's hiding another crow skull behind there! That's one thing on the easiness to find collectibles, but the game itself in a platforming sense serves little to no challenge plus boss patterns pretty much ensured I beat everything first try - bar Dhor - who I thought was the most confusing of the lot in terms of whether what I was doing was correct. Was I successfully hitting him when I jump smashed or was I not? Would my other attacks work instead? I still don't know. The game can be bought and finished to completion in one run without much effort at all.So without banging on about this too much: the game is a little too easy, and it's a little too narrow. But that kind of serves as its charm. Because it's easy and because it's narrow without too much going on, it doesn't feel too short or too long - and it was as far as I can remember a truly fun experience. However, because it's too narrow, and because it's too easy, it feels unmemorable and there could have been so much more, with respect to everything else about the game, that could have been fleshed out. I would still recommend the game however as it is a cute game with a good polish.

_childDocuments_.review: Ladies and gentlemen, let me tell you about this game, okay? It's called Pumpkin Jack, and it's fantastic, believe me. You won't believe the things I've seen, but this game, it's a winner, folks.You're Jack, the Pumpkin Lord, and you're diving into this epic adventure in a world that's all spooky and otherworldly. It's like Halloween all year round, and let me tell you, I love Halloween. Everybody knows that, everybody. And Pumpkin Jack, it's gonna ignite your Halloween spirit, big league.This game, it's a 3D platformer, and let me tell you, it's re-imagined for today, perfectly. You're jumping, running, climbing – it's tremendous. The levels, folks, they're like nothing you've ever seen. Each one's a whole new world, full of challenges that'll keep you sharp.And the combat, it's simple, but it's dynamic, just like me. You've got weapons, different ones for each level. Guns, swords, even a scythe. Lots of variety, believe me, lots.Now, the graphics, wow, they're incredible. It's like a colorful cartoon setting, like something out of a dream. The environments, the lighting effects – it's like living in a piece of art.So here's the deal, Pumpkin Jack is a winner, folks, a real winner. It's an awesome 3D platformer that'll take you on a ride you won't forget. I had a tremendous time with it, and you will too. _childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a game I would recommend to anyone who enjoys the genre, but it has a few glaring issues.I'll start with the good parts. Visually, the game looks great. It has this cartoony, colorful but still spooky art style which I think is gorgeous. This is amplified by the lighting which adds a lot of color and atmosphere to the world.The story is nothing crazy but it's silly, fun and fits the spooky yet cartoonish vibes the game has.Gameplay-wise, the level design is enjoyable, every level has it's own unique mechanic which gives each one it's own identity and keeps the play experience interesting and fresh. The levels are linear but still feature plenty of collectibles that add a bit of replay value to the game.With all the positives aside, I feel like a lot more work could've gone for the game's combat system. It's a button masher. You have one attack button, a roll and a ranged attack with your bird companion. Personally, I almost never used the bird, it has nothing special going for it, it's a regular ranged attack, and it doesn't even do that much damage...That leaves me with the regular attack, the only other attack in the game.. To be fair, you do get other weapons as you play the game but most of them feel very similar to each other and I didn't feel like the game gave me enough incentive to experiment with the weapons.I Think the solution would be to add enemies with different weak spots that require different weapons to get to, separate the combat into light & heavy attacks, to add a bit more flavor, and to make the bird's attack a bit more interesting. I thought of something like Griffon from DMC5, which launches enemies into the air and leaves them open for a combo. Obviously, DMC and Pumpkin Jack are very different games and I'm not expecting Jack to start doing aerial combos but giving the bird something more than "the attack you occasionally use on one-hit enemies" will be better.Something that doesn't bother me but I know will bother some is the game's length. I still haven't finished the game, I'm in the third level, but, apparently, that's half of the game already. The game has 6 levels and according to  it takes 4.5 hours to finish.Personally, I have no problem with this, I don't mind short games if they're fun to play, and Pumpking Jack is a fun game. It looks great, it plays great (outside of the combat) and I would recommend to anyone who doesn't mind the game's length and button mashy combat system.==========================================Again, I should mention that I still haven't finished the gameI'll continue playing it and update this review accordingly==========================================

_childDocuments_.review: This game had intrigued me for a long time. I like 3D platformers and the art style looked fun. After finishing the game now, I’d say it’s just fine. The platforming and combat are fairly basic. Music and sound mostly fit the game but not a ton of variety. One highlight is that enemies are well varied and the boss fights are pretty well done. Some parts are repetitive/re-used but it’s from a solo dev so that’s understandable. The weakest part of the game is probably the mini games, which were hit or miss; luckily, they don’t interrupt the main game for long usually.  The game is six worlds spread across six hours or so of playtime, so you can easily binge it over a few days. _childDocuments_.review: To think this game was developed by a single person is mind blowing given how incredible it is! It’s better polished than 99% of all AAA titles and has a fun gameplay loop and a solid story. If you enjoy games like Medievil and Spyro where you can aim to 100% the world by finding secret hidden items, this will definitely be up your alley as it’s a wonderful mix!
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a really great game albeit short and fairly easy. Overall I really like the game but there are some things that I feel could be changed.For the price I feel like there should be a little bit more content as there are only around 6 levels and I was able to complete the whole game in about 6 hours so I wouldn't really recommend buying at full price unless you really wanna support the dev.The platforming is fine but it does feel a bit floaty and had caused a few deaths during my play through because of it but you will get used to it and it may not even be much of an issue for you. At times the levels felt a little repetitive and some puzzles kinda drag but overall the level design and gameplay are really fun also the music is really great.I recommend that people who love platformers check this one out, there's a heap of cool references and the game feels reminiscent of some of the best platformer games for the ps1 and ps2. Its also worth mentioning that the game was mostly made by one person and I think that Nicolas has done a great job and I cant wait to see what they do next!
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this a lot! The music is dope, the game play is fun, the collectibles aren't SUPER hard to find, the story is funny and gave me a few chuckles, the levels are really well thought out and I really do think this is a project made with love and that shows. The TLDR is I'd recommend this to Halloween fans and spooky game lovers alike...IF it's on sale...and here's why. The weapons don't feel fleshed out. The first upgrade you get, isn't really that much better than the first. I found myself sticking to the 4th one you get all the way to the last level. A few times the earlier weapons even forced me to spin off a cliff because of an unstoppable animation. I also wish there was more variety in the skins you can unlock. They're all kind of the same color palette and...boring. The first couple skins I was like "Okay these are lower end ones and the higher end ones are going to be REALLY cool" and I was wrong. For $30 I would recommend waiting for a sale like I did. 3.5/5.PS: A controller is the way you're meant to play this just IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: The theme, art and music are great but the combat is clunky and the mini games weren't very fun. The gargoyle flight sections are torture, especially with a bug preventing the crow from opening gates, forcing you to take unavoidable damage.It's a real shame, I love some aspects of the game but I can't recommend it in this state.Update: I wrote this review when I had a lower end machine, since getting a new PC the gargoyle sections worked and were fine. I still wouldn't recommend the game if you have older hardware but otherwise it's a decent game.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember "MediEvil" game for PS1 from 1998? Well this is nothing like that, even it may seems so. This game is so buggy it even won't start in full screen - I spent 2 full hours trying everything without success. Gameplay is a joke: the platform part is uninspired and the combat one is clumsy (not that MediEvil was so better...). An amateur product that should have been left as source code in the basement's PC of the developer (it's a one man game and it shows).Stay away from it. To developer: learn how to code, before asking for money.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pretty good call back to the 3d platformers of the 90's and 00's, particularly the Medievil titles.It doesnt do anything particularly new or innovative but it does get the basics right. I found the platforming and controls to be quite good with a controller. The level design is good. Theres a bit of variety of gameplay with some puzzles and cart/vehicle riding sections thrown in. The boss fights are pretty good too.The weakest part of the game is probably the general combat as despite unlocking a new weapon after completing a level it doesnt really change much through the course of the game. Also there a lot of the enemy types are repeated through the game and that doesnt help either.Although its a pretty short game overall with a playthrough of the whole game taking about 5 hours or a little longer if you want 100% completion, the levels themselves are still quite long. Theres only 6 of them but I felt there was a good balance with each level not feeling too short but also not overly long to the point it gets tedious.Overall its a good effort considering it's an indie title and I'd recommend it to anyone who was a fan of the 3d platformers we had back in the 90's or even anyone who wants a fun but accessible game for their kids to play. I dont think it's worth the full price but worth picking up on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the genre, I thought this would make for a fun Halloween themed platformer with a bit of MediEvil vibes to it. What could've been a fun game is unfortunately brought down by its numerous flaws.Starting with the things I liked, the story is very different from your usual platformer plot. Instead of being the hero who has to take down the villain, this is the opposite. It's got some really funny moments that made me crack a smile here and there, while also not taking itself too seriously. The level intro narrations are even fully voiced, although it made me wish the whole game had proper voice acting.Platforming is decent for what it is. Jumping feels responsive enough even though the forward momentum can easily lead you to overshooting jumps if you don't follow a simple trick to spin the left stick to land your jumps easier. You do get drop shadows, but they may as well not even exist given how they blend in with the dark environments so you can't even see them. You can use the right stick for camera control to rectify this somewhat, but you may still find platforming difficult if you struggle with depth perception.If that was all there was to say about this game, it would be an above average platformer that's flawed but enjoyable for what it is. Sadly, this game has many more issues with its core design that make this hard for me to recommend.One of these being the combat. Very few 3D platformers even have good combat in the first place, and sadly, this is not one of them. Most of the combat just boils down to mindless button mashing until all enemies die as well as occasionally evading attacks by moving out of the way and using your ranged attack whenever possible. There is a roll move, but I can't recall a single instance where I ever used it. Fortunately, it is possible to skip most enemy encounters if you don't want to deal with them, but you will be missing out on various collectables if you do, although there are also a few forced fights throughout.The levels were a bit too long for my liking. There's only 6 levels in the whole game, but each one lasts an average of about 30-50 minutes, with levels repeating several assets a second time. I feel like the game could benefit a bit more if each level was divided up into 2 separate acts for a total of 12 levels. They're decent point A to point B linear experiences, don't get me wrong, but the levels start to overstay their welcome halfway in.What's worse is that seeking out all the collectables for those wishing to 100% this game can get on the very tedious side of things. If you miss something beyond a part of the level you can't go back to, you can't just simply quit out of the level and go back in as you'll restart at the last checkpoint you reached, even if you use the level select. The only way you can replay levels from the start is by beating the boss at the end, and even this wouldn't be that much of a problem if the levels were divided in half like I mentioned above.Speaking of 100% completion, I also found fully completing the game to be far too easy. Collectables stick out like a sore thumb and are usually easy to spot, even from a distance. Despite the aforementioned issues, I 100% completed this game in just 7 hours and never used a guide once during my entire playthrough.There are several sections where you take your pumpkin head off and play as just a pumpkin in a small area that Jack is too big to reach. These could've been really cool additions to the game to spice up the platforming gameplay, but these just consist of meaningless filler mini-games. Each level has 2 of these, except for levels 1 and 4 which has 1 and 0 respectively, and even then, the one in Level 1 only lasts about 10 seconds as all you do is hit a couple of switches to open a door.Level 2 has you pushing a bomb to the end of a linear obstacle course, Level 3 has you playing Simon Says with coloured musical mushrooms similar to the Banana Caves in Donkey Kong Country 3, Level 5 has a boring memory match game that's impossible to lose as there's no timer or penalty for mistakes, and level 6 has you awkwardly knocking presents that match the shape displayed on screen. These mini-games don't add to the game at all, which is a shame as I thought the concept of playing as just the pumpkin head had so much potential.Even that's nothing compared to the in-level mini-games. Level 3 has horse riding where all you do is steer and jump which lasts about 3 minutes. Level 5's gargoyle is very similar only you're flying instead of jumping, requiring mashing A instead of holding up or down to fly upward which at first made me think the controls were broken until the tutorial popped up after failing it the first time. These don't really do anything for me and make me miss the on foot gameplay.By far the worst part of the whole game, however, was the cart racing in Level 4. The goal is to beat the other knights to the end of the track so they don't close the gates on you, but these races are frustrating in every way possible. You have to mash the A button instead of holding it down which wears out your thumb very quickly. Control is limited to steering from side to side to avoid obstacles, so track mastery does not play any factor into these races.These races also have bar none the worst rubber banding I have ever seen. You can come to a complete stop during the race and the other knights will just wait for you until you start moving again, whereas if you even so slightly pull ahead of them, they'll catch up the moment they get the chance. This removes all sense of stakes these races are supposed to have considering only the last 15 seconds of the race actually matters. I had to redo this race a lot of times and almost gave up on this game because of that. It just feels like luck as to whether you win or not.These are  optional side missions, either. They are all required to advance through the levels. I have no idea why some of these 3D platformers keep shoving pointless distractions like these that have nothing to do with platforming, especially mandatory ones, when they could've just focused on being as great of a platformer as possible and it frustrates me to see so many games in this genre fall victim to this trap. Variety is nice, so long as it doesn't take away from the core game experience.And that's the single biggest issue I had with this game. Credit is due for being made by one person and I can tell that a lot of hard work and care was put into it, but as a product on its own merits, there are far better options out there for 3D platformer fans. There is fun to be had, but the cons far outweigh the pros. I'd say wait for a sale if you  have to play this; there's no way I would recommend buying this at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game, really put me in a cozy spooky mood, loved the characters and the 3d platforming and the story is brilliant, loved playing as the bad guy! (Although, is he really bad? Or just a bit naughty?) Would highly recommend, I didn't pay full price as I got in a Fanatical sale however I would 10000% say it is worth the full price, has a Christmas inspired level too so will be replaying at Christmas time as well <3 ps: a lot of people say this is a very easy game however I would not say it is *easy* - it is fair and it is fun and the penalties for dying are very minimal (i.e. starting again for the big bosses etc. - normal stuff) BUT you can and will die at some points and you may find it takes a few tries to kill some of the harder bosses, so if you're thinking "this isn't the game for me, it's too easy!" then I wouldn't say that's the case, there are definitely some challenging parts.10/10, will play again, can't believe I haven't played it before, would have brightened up many a gloomy Autumn day <3

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game! And it's mainly made by one person, as indicated by credits. I had a couple of thoughts about it, so wanted to share (also game many wants you to leave a review, so why not?)I kind of adore it in some way. While it's made by of the efforts of a single person, the developer knew what they wanted to create and didn't become overly ambitious with their baby, like many others do. The game is great because of it. It's not trying to achieve an open world or creating a story too complex with crazy mechanics. It's quite simple and pretty polished, and I love that simplicity. The game consists of 7 levels, you get some platforming, some fighting and some collectible hunting, and it's all pretty balanced and fun.Combat, while simple, actually surprised me a bit, as enemies don't really stagger if you attack them, meaning you can't just go ham on them, and you actually need to mix up some dodges and air attacks. Boss fights (past the first one) are a joy, great visually and gameplay wise. Also, the game rewards you with a new weapon at each level's end, and I completed each level with the given weapon(you can swap those, but I chose to try new ones), and I enjoyed most of them. They are different enough to feel fresh, and I liked that you get different animations for moving and jumping with a few of them. Also, you can set stuff on fire, and it's pretty funny, especially when done on accident.Graphics are pretty good. I completed the game on Steam Deck and the game ran mostly at 60fps at what I would call "medium" settings. I liked the draw distance, you can see distant towers that you visited a few minutes ago, and initially, you could have thought that it is just some random background scenery, but no! The crazy fires I left after me are as intense as always, so you can marvel your path of destruction.The story is pretty simplistic, and I liked it, you are a bad guy wanting to do bad things, and you get to do them which is great.The whole experience is very solid and my only real nitpick that water way too deadly in this game. Going knee-deep usually results in instant death, which seems a bit too harsh. But, I guess in many mythologies running water is a remedy against supernatural entities, so this applies here too, or at least it's my head canon.I had a great time with a game and I actually enjoyed watching end credits as I was presented with a bunch of early concepts and dev photos which was interesting to see.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: I would not give this game an overwhelming recommendation, but it was fun enough as a 3D platformer with beat-em-up combat mixed in.The platforming is pretty basic, but I am a sucker for jumping in video games, so it's easy to please me in that regard. If you want a challenging platformer experience, this is not that game. If you want a more casual experience, this may be more of what you're looking for.Combat is pretty mindless. You mash until the horde that's rushing you is dead. In the latter half of the game, you actually need to utilize the dodge roll to avoid getting toasted, but in the first half it's kind of braindead. The interesting thing about combat in this game is that there are no invulnerability frames after getting damaged, so if you find yourself in the middle of a crowd, your health can go from 100% to 0% in legitimately 3 seconds or less. Given that typically the combat is kind of a breeze, those moments are a bit of a shock when they happen because it's such an unexpected turn of misfortune. The lack of i-frames is probably a smart design choice though, because otherwise you would really just be an unstoppable tank as the game is currently built.One of the primary issues with this game is that there is no progression. Jack doesn't unlock new abilities or find cool powerups that offer a variety of types of play. He's just the same guy from start to finish. Jump, double jump, and attack. That's the whole game. Yes, you do unlock 6 different weapons, but they are minimally different from each other and none offers a particularly unique experience.In terms of art, it's a Halloween game through and through, so if you're into that "look," you're gonna love this one. If you aren't really into Halloween or actually dislike it, you will be put off by the visuals.The music was a mixed bag for me. The last level of the game has an absolutely beautiful track that, in combination with the wintry scenery and somber tone of that part of the storyline, created a legitimately amazing mood for the stage. It was by far my favorite stage as a result. The rest of the game generally had good mood-determining tracks as well, though they weren't "special" like the one in the final stage. A lot of the music actually reminded me of Grant Kirkhope's work (Banjo-Kazooie, Yooka-Laylee, etc.), which I enjoyed. So why a mixed bag overall? Because for some reason, the composer decided to incorporate several classical music pieces into the game, and it was all of those "you've heard them so many times you just want to plug your ears and scream until they're over" pieces that should be laid to rest for at least a few centuries.There are 21 collectables in each stage. I did not find all of them in any of the 6 stages of the game. In fact, I only found 77 of the 126 total. I usually have a pretty good eye for collectables (developers tend to all use the same types of tricks to hide things) but I guess the developer for Pumpkin Jack really decided to make them tough to find. And because I liked but didn't love this game, I didn't really care to spend time tracking them down. If I came across them, cool. If I missed them..... well, onto the next stage. 120 of the collectables go towards purely cosmetic skin changes you can unlock and the remaining 6 go towards nothing at all (in-game; there are Steam achievements for completionists).Each stage has some sort of "headless" gimmick where you have to complete a short little section or minigame while playing only as Jack's pumpkin head. The changes of pace were nice in theory, but the execution was a bit lacking. These sections just simply weren't that creative or fun. They weren't horrible, but they weren't great, either.Every stage also has an autoscroller gimmick where you do things such as ride a horse through a forest and try to dodge obstacles, get carried by a gargoyle through a cemetery and try to dodge obstacles, run through a burning barn and try to dodge obstacles, cart race against soldiers and try to dodge obstacles, ride in a mine cart and try to dodge obstacles........ you get the idea. These sections overstay their welcome and become tedious, especially the cart racing one which is way too long and requires you to mash for the entire races (yes, that was intentionally plural *ugh*). Again, a change of pace like these things is a good idea for the game in theory, but the execution just wasn't there. Some of them were ok. Some of them were genuinely not fun.In terms of difficulty, I think I died 23 times, and I would chalk most of my deaths up to "jumping into the oblivion unknowingly because something about the route forward was unclear in my mind." I had maybe 3-4 combat or boss-related deaths out of those 23, so my generally feeling upon death was "I didn't understand what I was supposed to be doing" rather than "I knew what to do and I failed or got outplayed by the enemy AI." This can lead to more of a frustrating experience, but that said, this game is very generous with checkpoints, so you never lose much progress no matter when you meet an ill-timed demise.The storyline and writing was amusing enough. The whole "indie developer wants to try its hands at both making a video game and writing stand-up comedy" style of video game storyline writing that has emerged in the indie scene is kind of overdone. And while it's certainly present here, it works well enough. It wasn't great, but it wasn't bad. Playing as the world's antagonist far less common than playing as its hero, so that's something. I will say that I fully expected Jack to end up betraying the Devil and collaborating with the Wizard to free his soul. But did it actually play out that way? I guess you'll have to see for yourselves.. no spoilers here!The game is short, and yet long at the same time. There are only 6 stages but each takes about 45 minutes or so to complete. In the better stages, this is fine. In the worse stages, it's laborious. I completed the game in just shy of 5 hours.I paid $8.99 for this game and I think it was a reasonable buy at that price. I think the $29.99 full price would be ludicrous.Overall, I think I've said "it's not great, but it's not bad" about several aspects of this game, so I think I have a fitting conclusion for this review.Pumpkin Jack is not great, but it's not bad.

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable 3d platformer for some fun. It does not do anything new and is just fun to play. There are some quirks and frustrations along the way. If you could put up with those it is enjoyable. The jumping takes a bit getting used to but it is manageable. The combat is very simplistic and the boss fights have patterns that are pretty easy.Buy it on sale if you enjoy 3D platformers which are very basic and can do with some odd camera work in some places and repetitive level design and some questionable levels which you might need to pull through.

_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know what to expect before buying Pumpkin Jack. Is it gonna be another Crash? Spyro? Kao? Some other platformer? Turns out, Pumpkin Jack is a unique, gripping game where we play as a bad guy this time and we're trying to destroy the good.The graphics are pleasant to look at, the gameplay is engaging and doesn't bore the player and the minigames are entertaining and not repetitive.Due to the fact that Pumpkin Jack is a short game, each level is a unique experience and I had never felt fed up with the game. I could not wait to play the game again after I finished a session.The collectibles are amusing to look for, you don't really even need a guide for them. They're placed in quite obvious places, unlike other platformers (yes Crash 4, I'm looking at you).Also, pumpkin Jack is not overly difficult, I only died 20-something times over the course of ~6 hours of the full playthrough.Overall, I had great fun playing Pumpkin Jack and I would definitely recommend it to other platform games lovers. Although, the price for ~6 hours of gameplay might be quite high for some players. In this case, just wait for a sale, like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game to play, especially before Halloween! The combat was, by far, my least favorite part. But the game is so short and introduces enough new mechanics throughout it's ~4 hours that the less-than-ideal combat isn't too big a deal. I'm all for the developer getting their money. So pay full price if you're able. On sale, this is totally a solid action platform that is worth having in your library to play during fall. Also, I played ~an hour on Steam Deck, where it mostly ran fine. But (at least during my time) I would say it's more "Playable" than "Verified".
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a great game to get in a Halloween mood. It oozes Halloween, but not in a scary way. It’s a comedic 3D platformer that is really fun and looks really nice. I’m actually surprised at how well this game runs compared to how good it looks. It looks fantastic and even has ray tracing. It’s not a very long or hard game, but not every game needs to be long or hard. It is perfect for what it is. My biggest complaint would be that they force mouse acceleration, followed by a few areas of horrible frame rate dips down to the single digits.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is basic, platforming is engaging enough, and the difficulty may be tuned a little too low for my taste but I still think this is definitely worth playing. The music, art, and overall theme are all so strong through the entire game and all the characters are so full of charm thanks to the silly tone of the writing and fantastic art direction. I'd still recommend that lifelong platformer fans check this one out if you also love Halloween and I really think I would have ADORED this game as a kid when it would have been a bit more of a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Really good small game, not too difficult, I like the aesthetic a lot. Its a chill game to play when you want to take a break, however not too long but that's not the purpose of this game, its a great experience that is worth it when you buy it at a discount because I wouldn't say this game is 30$ worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: If you like platform games, this one's a must-have.It's very impressive to see a developer working alone to achieve something like this.The game is so basic, you'd almost think it was game guru, but in its simplicity, it's perfect.The maps are pretty in a hallway style, but the animation and the amibiance, extra games that come some time, we can't get bored.The game can become repetitive after a few levels, but the fun it offers, and the extra games like the cart or horse races, are so pleasant that the pleasure is always there until the end of the game.The ultimate anti-hero; Charisma, not too much blabla and a Machiavellian spirit in the black humor, everything is perfect, the game to have to spend a good time at haloween.The graphics are very basic, and the maps look very similar, but as I said, the gameplay is so good that the scenery isn't that important. That said, the maps are also perfectly in the mood.Jack's little dances when he finds a megaphone and the hidden zones are stunning.A few hours to finish the game, 10-15 hours to unlock everything to 100% and a bit of fun with each Haloween, Jack's playtime is very decent.I bought this game a few hours after its release and at this period it was only 15% off, but I don't regret it, on sale or full price, buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is an incredibly enjoyable game that stands out with its simplistic mechanics and easy-to-grasp gameplay. The controls are intuitive, making it accessible for players of all skill levels while still providing a satisfying experience. The story is straightforward yet engaging, perfectly complementing the game's whimsical and spooky atmosphere.One of the game's standout features is its excellent music, which enhances the immersive experience and fits the Halloween-themed setting beautifully. Moreover, the game is filled with numerous, cleverly placed references that add a layer of charm and wit to the adventure, making it a delightful journey from start to finish. Overall, it's a fantastic game that excels in delivering a fun, entertaining experience. 10/10

Great, simple and beautiful  3D platformer that one can especially enjoy on Halloween or Christmas.Has a bit of Medievil and Crash in it, as well as Tim Burton.Terrific level design and a couple of annoying but fairly easy boss battles.Jack sounds like Beavis when he grunts.Recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Allow me to preface this review by saying this is not a bad game. It was clear a lot of thought and effort was put into it, and there are many things to like about it: the ambiance, the character design, and the dialogue. Having said that, there's just not a lot of gameplay to it, really. The combat is repetitive, the world design and exploration are simple, and the puzzles and tasks are quite easy. The boss design was cool, but the battles themselves were not engaging, and overall the experience was a tad boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: This is an awesome game, props to whoever made this, the world is stunning and the characters are so charming, game play is fun as well, its not easy enough to be boring and not impossible enough to become frustrating. I recommend it to anyone who enjoys 3D platformers.  Its truly an homage to Halloween.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of fun elements and ideas, but never really used to any great effect. The plot features a variety of vaguely Halloween-y content, but it all feels very token and superficial. You could easily swap out the hero or villain or the entire aesthetic and it would make no difference. The main antagonist is literally "The Wizard" - no name, no history, barely any personality. And the hero Jack is barely any better - he's literally a mercenary with no personal interest in anything going on.The overall gameplay design is generally hit or miss. The base combat and platforming are adequate, though a bit underdeveloped. There's a wide variety of minigames and scripted sequences, which are wisely used to help with the pacing. But seeing as they're all mandatory, and the difficulty varies wildly, they can just as often kill the pacing and turn into annoying roadblocks.The designers obviously took note of modern standards, best practices, and quality of life elements found in other games. But again, their implementation here is very hit or miss. For instance, there's a variety of weapons to unlock, each with unique movesets, and the ability to easily swap them mid-combat. Cool, this is generally a great thing for a hack'n'slash game. But then the game neglects to give you a  to ever swap. The weapons all seem equally effective on all enemies, so you just pick the one you like most and never use the others again. In general, it feels like the developers mimicked a lot of modern conventions without fully understanding them or taking the lessons to heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best indie games I have ever played. This was super fun and enjoyable all the way through. I loved the silly  and the way you unlock new weapons is amazing (I wish more games did it like that). Movement is clean and simple, characters look awesome, the combat is simple yet so incredibly fun! Short but compelling story that makes all the characters likeable with so little time. The game was fun and not tedious to 100% which is perfect. I will absolutely recommend this to my friends!
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Only a few hours in, but wow, this is a lovely indie.Graphically, it looks really nice. I'm playing with a 6700XT and a 3900x at 1440p with all settings at ultra with RT on. Reminds me of a late PS3/360 game taken to its highest peak. Artstyle is easy on the eyes and the character portraits are fantastic.Gameplay is pretty tight too. The combat has just enough depth to it so it's not a bore, chore, or leaving you wanting for more. The platforming is fairly forgiving, but not to the point where it's babymode or handholdy.Music is GREAT. A few classical tunes have been used for setpieces and it doesn't feel too cliche or trite. It was on sale for about five bucks when I grabbed it. What a deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a fun, spooky adventure with a charming story that keeps you hooked from start to finish. Playing as Jack, the Pumpkin Lord, is a blast, and the quirky, mischievous plot is full of personality.With its smooth gameplay, beautiful Halloween-themed visuals, and engaging mix of combat and puzzles, Pumpkin Jack is a great pick for any fan of lighthearted action-platformers.I especially loved playing it around Halloween - it really added to the atmosphere!
_childDocuments_.name: Pumpkin Jack

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, this is pretty fun. If you liek spooky stuff, and have a hankering for some Medieval style gameplay + hijinks, this might whet your whistle. I have a few concerns, namely some cheap 1-hit deaths( lean too far on minecart? dead ) ( touch water? dead ) ( miss a jump on an on-rails sequence bc the camera is not great ? dead.) ( use a certain wep which makes you lunge, and sink into the water, bc the game auto targets enemies? dead ) I actually managed to die within 30 seconds of the game starting, bc i always liek to check behind me in games for secrets, and all I found was an icy cold, 1foot deep grave of water. lol.aside of this, the game is quite fun, it captures the :" spooky scary skeletons " vibe pretty well, maybe closer to the Vanessa's mansion in A hat in time, but for the whole game. It's cute, not so much scary.it's that trickster Jack, you've probably seen him in the real ghostbusters, or Billy and Mandy - but yeah, it's him alright.combat is fine, visuals nail the Halloween feeling well, and the platforming can give you a decent challenge from time to time. Do i finds the bosses hard? heck no, they're actually rather pathetic - more in line with a 3D Mario title - they're fun, but not very hard to defeat.you can find crow heads to unlock outfits, and that's fun. they just look cool, no powers or nothing, no skill trees. but you do find several weps, and they all play differently ( with different attacks, such as one from jumping in the air, to double jumping in air, and your bog-standard mash  Square flurry ) you also have some segments where you're just controlling Jack's head, and these aren't the greatest things ever, but it mixes things up a bit.overall, if you are good at platformers, this game won't challenge you much, but it will entertain you. if you're the type to whine about GAME MUST = X HOURS FOR X PRICE, just move along. go play FTL. nobody cares.

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a great 7/10 game to play during the Autumn weather time. The final area was my favorite in the North but all of it exuded style and the colors were used to create an atmosphere perfectly throughout. Let me set a standard here, this is a game mostly made by one person. So it's just above a platformer for beginners . What is accomplished here is smooth animation, great jumping mechanics and decent combat. I found little to no difference in the weapons besides damage output and certain scenarios like the boat doing better with the gun. You can beat it in about 2-3 hours rushing through it. I took my time trying to get a bunch of skulls but never going too far out of the way and beat it in 4 hours. The bits where you balance on a beam are wonky due to the camera effects and this likewise effects the scenes where a gargoyle is swooping you around. Leading to restarts for no reason other than a crappy camera. There's a handful of bosses (5 if I remember correctly) and they are all quite fun. Some of them use combat, some you must avoid until a certain time. All of them mix up nicely and none are too difficult. All in all, I would recommend this game but it's not as deep or good as a Banjo Kazooie but c'mon.. pretty much one guy with a ton of help persevering to make a game he wanted to is pretty cool.

_childDocuments_.review: Pumpkin Jack is a visually stunning and tightly-made indie throwback to the lost art of 3D hack-and-slash platformers - taking what PS1's MediEvil succeeded in and repackaging it to a more accessible and modern audience. The platforming is engaging, the combat is fun, and like I said - the visuals are totally stunning. Sadly though, where it never reaches the occasional lower points of MediEvil - I don't think it ever reaches the highest points of that series, either. The weapon variety is severely lacking with no differences in how they work, no specific uses for them in each situation and no need to experiment with them. The level designs and puzzles within them are good, but never as interesting or explorative as MediEvil. The collectibles serve little purpose aside from only a few costumes, robbing them of any value or excitement to find them. Then, on top of that, the writing and characters are once again good, but never reaching the heights of wit, humour and charm as MediEvil.If MediEvil wasn't for you, I'm sure that the more streamlined and sleek approach of Pumpkin Jack will be right up your alley. It's a really good time. It isn't too long, it's great to control, the setpieces and level themes are wonderful, and once again, IT'S REALLY DAMN BEAUITUFL. I just wish it had a little more depth, and at least for now, it won't be replacing MediEvil for me as the go-to example of games like this.★★★★★★★☆☆☆

It recently went on sale, for half the $30 price, so I picked it up.I love the atmosphere so much in this game. The art style and spooky ambiance of each stage is soooo good.(I love Halloween)The music though, while a very spooky Halloween feel, mostly seems to run together; each track mostly sounds the same. Good quality and such, but nothing really stuck out... I found myself muting the music and just listening to the awesome (spooky) ambiance of the stages, while smacking skeletons and ghosts with a shovel.The characters are a lot of fun. The Great Jack himself is an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but you love his attitude anyway. The owl is bossy, but adorably animated, with fun banter between he and Jack. The cowardly crow friend reluctantly following Jack into the next big fight... All just fun to watch and listen to... My main gripe in regards to these guys is with the actual story itself... Short, bitter-sweet, spooky Halloween adventure; great to look at and to listen to.... I would love to play more, or see the story revamped into something less bad/deadpan. name: Fire Tonight
detailed_description: Maya and Devin are separated in a city on fire. In the year 1990, before cell phones or Internet. They’re on their own, wondering about the choices that brought them here, how they met, and what the future might hold. Inspired by Information Society's song of the same name, Fire Tonight is a lighthearted but thoughtful walk through the story of a relationship. A story about believing in each other when the whole world tries to keep them apart. Help Maya find her way across the city by car, train, roller skate and rooftop all while avoiding police barricades, traffic jams and the spreading fire. Confined to his small apartment, Devin anxiously awaits Maya's arrival. He reminisces about their time together as he looks at all the mementos scattered around his place. Will Maya and Devin be able to find each other before the city is engulfed in flames?

_childDocuments_.review: Love. One of the most elemental and emotional states of our existence. Under his influence, we often lose the ability to think logically, wars broke out because of it, it was the muse of the masterpieces of world literature, and in the modern age it was also the inspiration and theme of films, music and video games. It’s also the driving force behind the game, in which two lovers try to find each other in a big city hit by fire.First of all let’s examine the length of the content you could get for your money:Game Length: 40-60minsTime to get all achievements: 45-60minsDifficulty to get this game to 100% achievements: 1/10, but the reaction minigame might be annoying to some, but still doableAchievement Guide and walkthrough available on steam?: YesThe gameplay is extremely simple and I wish it would be more. It lacks a bit of complexity, or at least a couple of basic puzzles. Bypassing the nests of fire in a city that has become a flaming hell, picking up a few keys that are extremely easy to find and then opening doors with them doesn’t necessarily praise the creativity of game developers. There are still some variations, because Fire Tonight has some basic stealth gameplay too, such as avoiding police officers required during one level. The level where you need to avoid cars while riding roller skates on public roads also became way too short and too easy.If you still want more information about the content and gameplay, then here is a walkthrough of the game: Short, okish casual indie game for an acceptable price, but actually could be a bit longer or still cheaper, so recommended around at -40-50%. While it was too casual and too simple, I enjoyed it mainly because of the art, this is why the review became positive instead of negative. 8/10, looks cute, the art is clearly the best part of the game 5/10, static, repeated soundtrack. It feels the same soundtrack going on during the whole game. It started to be annoying to me around the half of the game already. 5/10. Pretty casual game, no hard puzzles or challenges, so while it was entertaining, I probably will not remember much details after a few months.  1/10  zero on win10 No voice acting in the game. Level select should list all of the collectibles (Maya’s memories) in numbers so users could see how many were collected there and how many were missed. This is a pretty common feature of similar games and also wished by the users.

_childDocuments_.review: Fire Tonight switches between two perspectives: Maya’s and Devin’s. At the start of the game they’re just chatting on the phone about the past. Maya looking back on the uncertainty of her moving away from her family and everyone she knew, but then the happiness it brought as it ended up with her meeting boyfriend Devin. Looking back at the cute memories they made and captured so far as well has having some cute banter. But just as the conversation was getting good, Maya’s power goes out as well as the phone (naturally). Wondering why that happened, she slinks out from her window and sees the strange sight of the transformer being on fire and then the town on fire. As this is set in the 90s, both of them don’t have cell phones so they can’t just call each other back easily. So Maya has to go find a payphone that will actually send a call out so Devin will know that she’s okay. Though, considering the payphone is all static, she decides to brave the fire and find her way to Devin’s apartment on the other side of town. Maya’s levels are the puzzle sections, which each of her levels taking place somewhere on her side of town. Your goal is basically to find a way to travel to the next area (or level). However, it’s not so easy as just walking to where you need to go. There is the fire, of course, which doesn’t seem much of a threat to the buildings for the most part, but they do reach out into the streets and the back alleys. Blocking Maya’s path. You will also find gates and doors locked so you’ll need to find a key that happens to be laying around and you have to figure out a way to get there. To get around the fire and find a way to the key (which can be tricky), you can go into open doors that will spit you out where its twin is and climb ladders. The game is also set in an isometric view where you can turn the camera to see around corners or behind the building Maya has to get behind. As you get into the other levels, you’ll come across another obstacle where you dodge police flashlights and get a new mechanic where listening to your music will cause certain fire spots to disappear. You do have batteries to worry about (which the music when the batteries are dying was great), but you do basically get an infinite supply. And if you do get caught or hit, you’re just rewound to right before. There are also some interactions Maya can have such as talking with some characters that live in the area, some items that seem to link to an achievement about finding Maya’s memories, and newspaper dispensers where each different one has a different headline.The puzzles are easy, but still requires you to think about what you need to do and when. The only level I really had trouble with was the last where I didn’t realize a barrier doubled as a bridge. I had a fun time figuring out the levels and I’m a bit sad that we only got a few levels.When you switch to Devin, he’s hanging out in his apartment waiting for Maya to call him from a payphone or appear at his front door. Considering Maya’s situation and how he has no idea where she could be, he can’t really go out and help (well, until he does). In his chapters, you’ll basically be examining the items in his apartment, with some having light interactions, to where he’ll say a little tidbit that gives you a window into his personality as well as his relationship with Maya. Also, some callbacks to how the 90s were. His levels were a good way to give you a break from Maya’s and a way to fill in the space where she’d be traveling to the next area, especially since his never left you away from Maya from too long.There aren’t that many negatives Fire Tonight has, but you may run into a quick annoyance of the buildings getting in the way of your view and just wish it wasn’t so short.Fire Tonight is a charming short game, taking me a little bit under an hour for me to complete, that I really wish had more. I did have a feeling it would be short, but I did not expect how much I ended up liking and wanting to spend more time with Maya and Devin, more puzzle areas as I enjoyed them as much as I did when I played the demo, and I liked the interactions Maya had with her two friends you encounter and the short tidbits the other people of the town had. I also loved the art style it had, which was the very reason I was interested in the first place and we even got some surprise animations. It was also nice with the couple tributes they had to the song with the instrumental music seemingly calling back to it (at least how it sounded to me), the level select having the lyrics, and of course the game’s plot following the song.Fire Tonight is a good game to play, either when you want a puzzle game or a quick game to pass the time, but I do wish we had more.

The story is a bit silly, but that just makes it that much more endearing as the characters try to find one another in the chaos. The blues, teals, pinks, purples, and multi-colored buildings, artwork, and signs all catch your eye and make the game even more enjoyable. Absolutely worth the hour or two it took to complete, and would happily play again.

name: Wallachia: Reign of Dracula
detailed_description: Wallachia Reign of Dracula is a retro-styled action platformer/shooter game. It features a cast of professional voice actors including Kira Buckland and Robert Belgrade. The game also features a unique soundtrack, and a story based on the history of Vlad the Impaler, rather than typical vampire myths. In addition to it's action packed 7 levels, the game includes loads of bonus content and mini games, as well as unlockable official crossover content from Bloodstained Ritual of the Night. Players take on the role of a new protagonist named Elcin Floarea to take on Vlad Dracula and free Wallachia of it's tyrant ruler once and for all.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game for 4 hours so far and it's been great fun !I really have nothing bad to say about the game.It looks, sounds, runs and controls really great and tight right from the get go !I have to say, mad props to the devs to actually release a FULLY FUNCTIONAL game right from release. I haven't encountered a single bug/glitch so far and that feels really good in times when so many games release in different states of brokenness !Be aware that the game is crushing in terms of difficulty.This is defnitely not a walk in the park and it's a great throwback to the days of arcade and old-school games from the NES era.You can feel influences ranging from Castlevania to Alysia Dragoon, Shinobi and games like that....Been playing on a PS4 controller and it works flawlessly either with the D-pad or Analog Joystick.Also, having a real story, cutscenes and voice-acting (!!) along with everything else for such a small price makes this game a STEAL in my book. You just can't go wrong by buying this game and I think it's worth every single penny ! Great job Migami Games <3 !
_childDocuments_.name: Wallachia: Reign of Dracula

_childDocuments_.review: Wallachia: Reign of Dracula is obviously inspired by the classic Castlevania games.A nice 2D game in 16-bit style.The game looks and plays exactly as you would expect from a lookalike from the SNES era.The goal of the game is to eventually defeat Dracula by overcoming seven different levels full of enemies and obstacles, but make no mistake, just as similar games on the SNES could be very challenging or difficult to master. playing, this is also the case with Wallachia Reign Of Dracula.watch a short gameplay of the game here: As mentioned, Wallachia: Reign of Dracula is very similar to Castlevania, the gameplay consists partly of platform action, as there are more than enough obstacles in the levels.Fighting also plays a major role, something you do with your sword and bow and arrow.You regularly have to deal with boss fights that can make it pretty difficult for you,Seven levels doesn't sound like much, but you'll certainly have a good time with it.Most of the replayability will have to do with practicing and improving certain parts in levels so that you can progress a little bit.In any case, you will almost never go game over because of the controls.This is fine and responds as you would expect from a 16-bit platformer. Furthermore, the levels are well put together with enough variation in enemies and unexpected elements. The action is also nice and fast, and this together makes Wallachia: Reign of Dracula a very nice platformer.Wallachia: Reign of Dracula is not a game that you will continue to play for months, but the makers have given a lot more fun with the extra challenges. There are also various things to unlock such as costumes and even extra stages.Are you looking for a retro platformer full of action and challenge? Then Wallachia: Reign of Dracula is highly recommended. The game plays nicely, levels know how to continue to fascinate and audiovisually everything is fine. Just remember that Wallachia: Reign of Dracula is hard, very hard.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: The Development team has taken the time to consider the suggestions in both this review, and the comments below, and so I change my review to positive. Thank you, Migami Games! I am otherwise keeping the text intact for posterity's sake. I don't normally bother to write reviews, but this game is so close to being great, I feel like I have to. I like it a lot!Pros:-The action is fast. Decisions have to be made quick; enemies come at you in all directions, and need to be dispatched in the right order to avoid damage. Subjective, but definitely a plus for those in need of a fast paced side-scrolling action game. -Dark, somber, beautiful rock ensemble. There's even synth bass lines that give me that distinct Kukeiha Club vibe, definitely feeling that Castlevania vibe. -The main character is cool, despite the sexist themes of the story (to replicate the times I assume?). There's a great display of solidarity with her animal companion and her design reminds me of Sonia Belmont. I wonder if this was on purpose?-The sprites for many of the characters are well made. Anatomically, they look well drawn, and the enemies' fashion suits the era. Lovingly crafted. -Great voice acting. Even the random foes have many different random blurbs to say as they rush you. Also, Alucard's voice actor has a role!? Pretty awesome.Cons:-The character doesn't handle as flexibly as one would hope. Perhaps this is on purpose, a nod to older Castlevanias, where you have to carefully place an attack in the right position to advance without taking damage? But it doesn't help Wallachia feel any better to play. Here's a few bullets of a much longer list as to why:*You can attack rapidly with your sword. But you cannot turn or duck while attacking rapidly with your sword. You HAVE to swing, wait until the MC repositions herself, then swing at the next thing coming at you. This wouldn't be a problem in traditional CVs, but Wallachia is much faster paced, and fractions of a second in reaction time matter.*The sword sadly has very short range, despite the protagonist stepping forward while swinging it. This problem is even worse when you step into projectiles while trying to repel them at the last moment. Is this an Arming Sword, or a Dagger? Please, make the melee weapon's reach longer.*Upon landing on the ground, you cannot jump again for a moment. I'm not sure if this was a design choice, but it's a much safer option to jump and move out of a projectiles' way than to cut it aside because of reasons above. -Upgrades are immediately lost when hit. This sucks. I understand why this is done; it feels pretty good to go untouched for a while and be rewarded for it. I really wish power-ups were lost on death instead, though.-Wallachia punishes you a bit much. It sucks to die and lose even the increase in your maximum HP in your next life/try, as well as all ammo, and assists. If you run out of lives, you restart the stage from the start. If you run out of continues, you have to restart the whole game... which, I'm assuming, is a design choice made to artificially lengthen the game. This wouldn't be so bad really, if it weren't for the fact that all Max HP power-ups are lost after a single death. Having 4 HP to start with means you're allowed 3 mistakes before your life is over.-Enemies damage you simply by touching you. This was a design choice back in the 8-bit/16-bit era because of limited resources and to cut corners, avoid making attack animations, etc. It sucked then, and it sucks now. The enemies in Wallachia DO have attack animations, cool ones, so I'm not sure why this is a thing. I'd suggest increasing the frequency the enemies attack instead of touch-based damage, but the game is already pretty tough for the average person. Avoid having this in games whenever possible.-The Assist characters are awesome, so it's a shame they can't be used often, or at all if you're unlucky. -Easy mode is unfinished and almost all achievements are disabled in it. Normal mode difficulty is the standard and what I tried Wallachia with instead for this reason. -Only a certain amount of the protagonist's arrows can be shot, and remain on screen, at a time. This isn't a problem by itself, but arrows can be rapid-fired like a side-scrolling shooter, like Contra. Couple this with the fact that the amount of arrows that remain on screen fluctuate depending on the enemies on screen, and it becomes pretty hard to decide how to shoot, and when. At least you can fire while moving, and aim in all eight directions while standing still?I'd go into more detail, but I think I've typed enough. Wallachia is a fun game in my opinion; I had a good sit down with it, and I intend to get farther next try, but I can't really recommend it to anyone without a LOT of warning. Wallachia definitely isn't for everyone; the old school difficulty fills a small niche for the action platformer masochists. But I seriously hope you're willing to git gud, and try time, and time again. Otherwise, try something else. Even for $10, Wallachia may not be worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this game up because I liked one of the trailers and it is reasonably priced. Big Castlevania fan. The old school 16 bit style graphics with more modern sound reminded me of a Sega CD or early Playstation game. If you liked the Brahm Stoker's Dracula movie from 1992, there are a few nods here. The gameplay is pretty simple. Side scrolling platform shooter, more like Contra than the original Castlevania. You jump and shoot. You have 3 lives then you can continue at the beginning of the stage. You grab upgrades, but when hit, you go back to normal. You can switch between magic abilities or arrow power ups with shoulder buttons, like switching powers in Mega Man. Most of which have a low ammo count however.That is where the praise ends. The problem with this game is it doesn't know if it wants to be an enjoyable throwback or an imitator of those coin munching arcade games you have to tinker with just to finish. The game has 7 stages. The last 2 are nightmares that will really test you. The level seems okay, then there are huge swarms of enemies and you need a power up to get by or it won't work. Speaking of which, some of the different arrows are useless. The poison arrow is green and the fire arrow is orange. Meh. Also, most of the bosses have erratic patterns making them act very cheap. The last boss in particular is straight out of those coin munching games. There are also a couple bugs, notably, a couple crashes, and the controls are not responsive at times. Specifically, when I tap the button to shoot arrows, it did not respond. I could sware the double jump is off as well. I have a hefty PC and this is not online, but there is bad input lag. If it was intended for an old school feel, it was a bad move when the difficulty is up so high.The joy gets sucked out quickly. "Count" this game out. This game does not do the Monster Mash and will only be a graveyard smash on your wallet. Don't wait for a sale.  Just go to one of the Castlevania or Contra collections. You will have a lot more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Classic Contra style gameplay with Castlevania's aesthetics and a pinch of shinobi. The game can be beaten under 35 minutes if you know what you are doing but for most people it will probably take 4-5 hours to complete due to trial and error. The bow and arrow is your main weapon with a sword as secondary. Powerups can be found during levels like spread shot, penetrating arrows etc. The Pixel art, arcade style and music are done well. It supports unlimited continues, stage select and multiple difficulties. Most enemies can be taken down by a single hit contrary to the player who can take 4 or 5 hits. One could aim in 8 directions and there is a seperate aim button to lock yourself into place. Levels are quite varied as well. Be aware that it's a difficult game. It's also suitable for speedrunning if you are into that. Well worth a recommendation to fans of Contra. Tip: You can select a stage during the tutorial by pressing right.More Contra-like games: Super Cyborg, Blazing Chrome and Intrusion 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+Great music.+Cool atmosphere and story.Cons:-Poor controls.-Cheap A.I. with attack and sprite hit boxes the size of Mars.-Infuriating trial and error gameplay with almost zero room for mistakes.Wallachia seems like it wants to be Castlevania, but gameplay-wise it feels more like Contra with the running and gunning (bowing? arrowing?), aggressive enemies, losing upgrades when hit, and even the birds you shoot to drop items. This wouldn't necessarily be a bad thing if it wasn't so ungodly frustrating to play.With a more historical take on Vlad the Impaler and the Dracula myth you take control of Elcin, a tough huntress armed with a bow and arrow, sword, and several companions she can summon as she traverses seven levels to defeat the evil Lord Dracula. A fairly short game and to play all seven levels you have to play on either normal or hard, with easy only allowing you access to five levels, but no matter what difficulty you attempt this game is nothing but pain.The controls feel very stiff and sometimes even unresponsive. There are times when you can mash the bow attack and fire and endless barrage of arrows, and other times Elcin will just stand there plucking the bow with no projectile whatsoever as enemies come barreling upon her. The sword does more damage but has a pathetic arc it swings in, only about 2 feet in front of you, which makes it as effective as a toothpick when dealing with large groups of melee attackers. There are upgrades to your bow and sword, but you lose them upon getting hit which is guaranteed to happen a few seconds after obtaining them. The "helper" attacks can be useful, but you don't get to use them much as resource requirements are very steep and you lose all of your gems when you die anyway.The enemy A.I. is some of the most frustrating I have ever experienced. Sure, this is supposed to be a retro inspired Castelvania/Contra homage, but even those games had a balance to them and your patience was always rewarded. Enemy attacks always seem to know exactly where you will be standing or moving, and track you as if the projectiles have a mind of their own. It requires such split-second timing to dodge incoming attacks and if you jump a half second early or late you will be hit. And you only get FOUR health points which can be increased with certain items but good luck holding on to them as they disappear upon death. Projectile and even enemy sprite hit boxes are awful and feel bigger than they should be, giving you almost no room to maneuver around and avoid damage, especially in boss battles with twenty-foot tall enemies who love charging at you.On the positive side, the music is very good, the story and world are well presented, and the artwork is decent. If the developers had spent a little more time balancing the game I would say Wallachia is an indie gem worth your time and money. In it's current state, however, it's an infuriating mess that is very difficult to recommend even for old-school enthusiasts. If you absolutely HAVE to play Wallachia, wait for it to go on sale for REAL cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: 6-7/10 As the review title states Wallachia offers arcade inspired action gaming with loose ties to a Castlevania-Like. Stages are short, bite sized encounters where stage knowledge (Enemy locations, bonus items..etc) is generally very important. Furthermore the total game isn't too long much like most arcade experiences. After finishing the first play through some additional mini-games and challenges are unlocked to give a little more replay outside of the base experience. Some of the games weaknesses I noticed are as follows. Sometimes the arrow shot in rapid succession simply does not work, the character animates but no arrow is fired. Character movement is mid-tier in terms of smoothness (esp at the extremes of a ledge); could be better but its not terrible. Certain enemies have unusually large contact damage hit boxes which cause meaningful stagger/knockback (Strongly evident on the 2nd stage bosses). Also there might be a few too many arrow & helper magic options considering the length of the game. I think the dev should have distilled it down to 1 special arrow and 1-2 helper magics without the level 2 modes. Overall a pretty good action game with some rough edges but that is worth checking out.
