_childDocuments_.review: This review is based on the game's previous update (since launch).Wallachia: RoD is a game that provides a very authentic '90s arcade experience. If you are a retro gamer that wants to re-live that era once again through a modern game, or if you are a modern gamer that is up for a challenge (without having to constantly spend money on tokens), this game will definitely deliver that experience to you.The gameplay is similar to games such as Contra and Shinobi. You can jump (and double jump), crouch, slide, fire arrows in 8 directions, charge arrow shots, attack with a sword that can also deflect projectiles, and summon Helpers with each of their own abilities. The game has 7 stages, each with a fair amount of platforming, and enemies such as the common infantry, archers, and spearmen. Every stage has a boss that you have to defeat in order to proceed to the next stage.The game's difficulty especially when playing for the first time is balanced in my opinion. It will not be a breeze, but it WILL challenge you. There WILL be parts that you will probably die quite a few times, and you are expected to adapt and find strategies in order to proceed. Something to be aware of (especially for newer players to the genre) is that you have a limited amount of continues. Like with most retro games, if you lose all of your continues, it's game over, and you have to restart from the very beginning of the game.The game has a fantastic artstyle and spritework along with a great OST. Keep on playing the game, and you'll also find a neat reference to Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night.Overall, I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fantastic throwback to the classic "Castlevania" and "Contra" games, and others. It feels like something from the 16 to 32-bit era, with gorgeous backgrounds and effects that are nicely made, with one particular stand-out being the burning countryside at the beginning of the second level. "Wallachia" also features nicely performed voice acting with familiar faces from other wonderful games, like "Symphony of the Night" (Hello, Robert Belgrade! Nice to see you again!). The graphics, for the most part, look wonderful. The heroine Elcin's sprite is nicely animated and I really enjoy her static pose. The only minor complaint I have is that her facial portrait during conversations with NPCs looks a bit amateurish. There are plenty of control options to tailor how you wish to play it, whether with keyboard or gamepad, allowing you to map the keys to buttons as you wish. Right now there doesn't seem to be a way to use anything other than the D-Pad if you play with a controller, however.The level design has enemy placement that will challenge players. From the first two levels I've played through so far, my biggest problem with the game is that the controls don't seem to be as responsive as they should be. The game demands that Elcin slide, aim from standing and use her sword to deflect arrows to avoid taking damage, but more than a few times I've had problems where Elcin doesn't duck immediately, but rather continues to run forward a couple of seconds when I hit Down on my Xbox One's D-Pad. I'm not sure if this is an issue on my end or the game's, but it does seem to be a problem when dealing with a lot of enemies on the screen at once. It's a bit frustrating at times, but nothing that has caused me to throw down the controller and shut the game off.If you are a fan of challenging older titles like "Super Castlevania IV", "Contra" and "Mega Man", the game is definitely worth a look, especially at the very reasonable $10 price tag. A nice first outing from this developer that shows a lot of promise.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid old school Contra/Castlevania hybrid. Difficulty: This game is quite difficult. The developers clearly wanted to capture the same style of difficulty of older retro games, but its doable. I think Contra games are still harder, as is Castlevania 3. Difficult but doable and perfect for fans of retro style difficulty. Visuals: I'm a fan of the variety of environments. One of the things I enjoy about the old Castlevania games is that you get outdoor scenery in addition to gothic architecture and interiors, this game similarly has that range of environments. Music: I am particularly a fan of the level 2 theme, but its solid overall. Controls: You get a base 8 way projectile attack like in Contra, which makes you feel well equipped for most challenges that the game throws at you. The slow fall speed and double jump gives you a lot of control in mid-air. Story: My least favorite part. However, the cutscenes at the beginning and end feature a great brushstroke art style, but unfortunately, the rest of the story is told through dialogue boxes and text with overlaying voice acting and minimal character animation. It's not bad but just not as good as the intro and outro cutscenes. Also, props for including known voice actors. One additional thing about the story that I think the developers should consider is the character of Vlad Tepes. Yes, he was a mass murderer and torturer, but he also was born into an incredibly violent world. Most people would be driven insane if they had to live in his shoes. He spent most of his teenage years as a prisoner, his father and brother were brutally murdered, and his captors, the Ottoman empire, brought overwhelming force to all that opposed them. I wish that the version of Vlad portrayed here was a reflection of the world he lived in, instead, he seems like a comic book villain that is evil for the sake of being evil. Missed character development opportunity. TLDR; If you dig difficult old school retro games, Wallachia will fit the bill.

_childDocuments_.review: You may still enjoy this game if you like classic NES level difficulty. Not in the "hard but fair" sense, but in the "brutally unresponsive clunky controls and overly-long locked-in attack animations in a game that requires split second reaction times" sort of obnoxiousness. There's absolutely no reason for any of that crap in a modern platformer. It's like remaking Rondo of Blood, but making a conscious decision to give your character the choppy attack and movement of the original Castlevania because  it's "not a defect, it's a feature." If anything the game is more like the worst parts of the original Contra where success often depends on memorizing what areas and directions enemies and projectiles will be appearing from so you can already be moving and firing to kill or avoid them the instant they're on the screen. I, personally, don't have time for that ****, but if that's your cup of tea... play on.  Me, I gave up almost immediately, after discovering the game has no other volume setting besides "blaring", it crashes into a non-existent mini-game the moment you try to skip past the tutorial, and yeah.... because even the first level was over the top difficult, but in all the wrong sort of ways. Of the two "Castevania with a Bow and Arrow" games I bought this weekend, 'Record of Lodoss War' is superior in every possible way. I invite anyone looking to scratch their Castlevania itch to play that one, if you haven't already.

_childDocuments_.review: What a poorly optimized game. The first problem is glaring, which is it wears it's "influences" extremely blatantly. Between the banner and the intro cutscene, there are no less than 3 Hunger games references, and the back half of the settings are almost exactly Castlevania: Rondo of Blood. NOW for the ACTUAL complaints as to why you should avoid this one for now. This game has an immediate game breaking bug. If you try to skip the tutorial or press a button in any way during, it will take you to a minigame start screen (falling rocks) that never actually starts the game. So you have to let the whole tutorial play out in its entirety to even begin. And the game has a tendency to eat your inputs. You'll find yourself often missing shots or second jumps because they just aren't registering, and it registered other inputs weird. You will often slide (another wholly unnecessary mechanic, but muh Rondo of Blood) when attempting to do a  jumping diagonal downward shot.Finally, the game balance is overly difficult for all the wrong reasons. You lose EVERY power up on hit which (except HP Max, which is lost on death). It's very easy to take hits because the projectiles often are either hard to see or blend in to the background. It feels like not have any form of permanent upgrades or ones with any form of longevity is extremely archaic. Some of the later stages and bosses seems unfair with how much they throw at you at once as well as the patterns they use are nearly unavoidable. Not to mention the checkpoints are quite unforgiving.Over all, the best thing i can say about this game is that the graphics are gorgeous. But it really feels like they blew their whole budget on the graphic artists and everything else just didn't get the polish or QA it desperately deserved. I'd say hold off on this for a few months until they work out some of the issues and possibly rebalance the problem

_childDocuments_.review: A lot to love about this game, but a few things hold it back from being REALLY great, and they're fairly common ones (which you would think we had moved past by 2020, and yet here we are)First things first, the look and feel of the game is great! The main heroine is cool, the design of the levels and enemies is a spot on recreation of many of my favorite Genesis and arcade games from the 90s. It's a fun game, a pretty game.The default button layout is terrible, though. Now, I have been told you can remap the buttons, so I did, and came across 2 more major knocks against the game. One, you can't map your primary and secondary attacks to the mouse button on PC, and the REAL big killer for me is that the devs have taken away the ability to map the jump button to 'space' which is almost unheard of, and makes even a revamped control scheme downright terrible to use. Can't use the alt button either, so the buttons closest to the thumb all cause you to either miss your intended key, or you end up pausing the game every time you try to jump, which kills the general flow of the game, and can REALLY mess you up in certain tight spots. Overall, I would absolutely love to recommend this game, because it has a whole lot going for it, and if the issues I mention were to be fixed, there would be nothing stopping this from being one of the best retro-styled games ever, but the flaws are HUGE flaws, and they make the game near impossible for people like me, who have issues with holding most control pads forcing us to rely on the keyboard and mouse, to play accurately.

_childDocuments_.review: *EDIT - The developer has made some  fixes that I complained about below, so good on them for addressing the issues quickly.   They fixed the pause issue, the game saving issue( I mean how can a game not saver right?), and they apparently made keymapping better.  I can't check this because I had the game refunded and well, these issues weren't the main reason for my bad review.  The game was still generic and just boring to me, nothing new here.  see the original review below:Very disappointing.  I picked this up as a huge Contra and Castlevania fan, hoping to see a great mashup.  But all we got is a lesser Contra with a Castlevaniaish aesthetic, a bad control scheme that was confusing to remap because of terrible menus, no ability to pause and apparently a game that loses all my progress without the ability to return to where I was.  The only menu option is to "start game" and it puts me at level one, despite my history showing I beat the first two levels.  I didn't care enough to replay these levels, so I requested a refund. The game play itself  was OKAY at best, kinda generic Contra style, nothing exciting happening. It's fast paced but at the same time boring.  You get arrow power ups,  weapon power ups and some other kind of helper that I never was able to figure out, I hit every button mapped to my PS4 controller and I never figured out that third power up, and never got around to figuring it out because the rest of the game left me at "Eh".Yeah, I don't usually quit games or request refunds, but I wasn't feeling this game and its poorly designed menu options just weren't doing it for me.  Hard pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Wallachia: Reign of Dracula is a very good action retro styled platformer, now what is the story. It's the year 1462 Prince Vlad Dracula is in his second reign and already he has gained a reputation of being a merciless ruler who has killed thousands, but many people plot against him from the ruler of the Ottoman Empire to his own brother Radu. But among all of them only one young girl burns with a desire to take down the Dragon, a young girl named Elcin, soon this young girl and her rag tag team will venture into the heart of Dracula's domain in order to slay the dragon.Now then let's talk about what's to like about the game, the gameplay is very good, for the most part it’s pretty hard but fair making you take your time and studying your enemies movements and the lay of the land before advancing to the point where you can get through levels a lot easier on repeat playthroughs. The pixel graphic art style is really good it definitely captures the feel of an old retro video game, while being quite detailed with a great use of vibrant colors and gothic scenery; it also does a really good job in capturing a classic retro game.The levels are really good quite diverse with a nice selection of locations to see and explore, with plenty of great detail that just makes you want to stop and stare, it also just like with the graphics capture the feel of a classic retro game.The story is pretty good I also liked that it takes some cues from the real history of count Dracula through the game does embellish a lot of stuff, but still if you're a history buff that has studied Count Dracula some of the things you see in the story are actually pretty accurate. The characters are good each one with their own unique look probably I like how Radu has a sort of Alucard look to him and Elcin was pretty cute looking.The enemies and bosses are very good each one with their own unique look and powers one of the coolest looking bosses in the game had to be Dragomere and Dracula. The music is very good and fits each level very well; my favorite song has to be the first track for the first level. The voice acting is very good does not feel wooden at all and I even recognized some of the voice actors in the game. The bonus features are very good, like the challenges you can do once you beat the main game as well as concept art and getting to listen to all the different music of the game.Now then let's talk about what's to dislike about the game, the only thing I can dislike about the game are some of the achievements, what I mean is some of the achievements are extremely hard to get, especially the sword master achievement and without supply achievement those two feel way too hard and needing more luck as well as skill to get those them, especially the without supplies achievement.Now that I told you this Wallachia: Reign of Dracula is a very good action platformer with a lot to love, from the very good gameplay to the really good pixel graphics and a pretty good story. Now then do I recommend this game, oh absolutely if you're a fan of old school video games this is definitely the game for you and I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: the art is gorgeous and the game has a nice tone but its gameplay is a bit flawed.* controller inputs will sometimes be ignored for no reason, even though the game is running smoothly. * when using your sword the character shouldn't be allowed to turn mid-animation. this causes you to hit the wrong enemy when surrounded, taking damage from the one you wanted to hit first. * enemy hitboxes don't always match the sprites, especially the width. Arrows fly by when they should hit. * the lack of checkpoints before bosses is like... ok, we get it, it's retro, but at this day and age we don't have the time to memorize level layouts and enemy waves anymore.it's a bit unforgiving in that aspect and what I hoped to be an arcade blast turned out to be a home computer frustration.The game isn't bad, but the aforementioned were problems that carried over from Lecarde Chronicles 2. I see the same engine here and the tweaks were minimal, which again isn't a bad thing.If there ever exists an update, sequel or anything built upon the same base, Migami, please consider my advice.

_childDocuments_.review: Great little classic runandgunner. The gameplay is solid as hell but the devs made some really strange decisions.The options menu is quite bad, but especially the button remapping option is absolute terrible. There is a stage select option (for stages you've beaten) hidden in the arcade-style how-to-play demo you get when you start a new game, I probably would have stopped playing if not for it and I only learned about it because I asked if there was a way to save progress in the forums.Another strange choice was to make you lose all your power-ups on death, quarter-muncher style. It only adds to your frustration on your initial playthrough because the game is fair but it relies heavily on memorization so leaving you weakened halfway into a level you haven't played before feels very discouraging.Play this if you miss the arcade classics.

_childDocuments_.review: Wallachia: Reign of Dracula is an overall fun and challenging action platformer. It tends to get compared to CastleVania due to the Dracula theme but gameplay wise, I feel it's actually closest to Revenge of Shinobi and Shinobi 3 on the Genesis. The gameplay is good, the controls are mostly solid and the music is excellent. The difficulty can be frustrating at times but this is a very pattern heavy game. Enemies will be in the exact same spot each level and once you get the pattern down and know what is going to happen, you can breeze through. As for the cons, the controls are mostly tight but every now and then, you'll try shooting arrows and nothing comes out. I think this is intentional to keep you from spamming constantly but it makes it feel like the control is not responsive sometimes and when enemies are coming at you and your arrows aren't working, something feels off. It doesn't happen a lot but when it does, it's frustrating. The difficulty also seems a little cheap at times and when you die, having to restart a level is never fun. That's old school but I wish it would just start you back one screen instead of the entire level. I just don't see the fun in repeating something you just did. These are all minor complaints though and again, once you learn the patterns, you can typically coast through.It's a relatively short game but with the modern renaissance of 2D games again, I think this is a bit of an underrated and overlooked gem that is worth your time and is a throwback to the great action platformers of the 16-bit era.

In character sprites it's once again another. By the end of the game I wasn't sure how protagonists face is supposed to look like.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, Wallachia is gonna give off Castlevania vibes.  However, the gameplay is more of a run and gun.  You could almost call it a Contravania.  You play as a young girl with a bow and arrow, off to take revenge upon Vlad the Impaler.  This game's setting eschews supernatural elements in favor of history.  You won;t fight Zombies and skeletons in the game, instead you'll fight soldiers, and animals.  There is some parts later on in the game that have you battling illusions, but that's about it. The game is very challenging, and not very difficult.  You have a small health meter, so you gotta pick and plan each move.  The game has a great retro feel, and it almost feels like it could have been a Sega Genesis title.  I hope the devs will produce a sequel, because the ending definitely has a hook for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Wallachia: Reign Of Dracula is a really cool, old school action-platformer. It was clearly inspired by Konami's Castlevania series. But it doesn't really play anything like the NES trilogy that other games have tried to follow. Nor does it go the Metroidvania route Symphony Of The Night inspired games have tried to follow. Instead it takes influences from even more retro games and uses these elements along with its own to make something a bit more unique. Most notably to me, Sega's Revenge Of Shinobi, and Namco's Rolling Thunder. My full thoughts are on my blog

_childDocuments_.review: Retro style indie gaming has been doing so well with so many titles that have come out from Bloodstained to Shovel Knight to Gunvolt and more and now we have another game to look forward to in Wallachia: Reign of Dracula! StoryThe Dragon, Prince Vlad Tepes the Impaler, is roaming Wallachia and hunting down all who are of the Boyar family. Prince Dracula slayed the family of protagonist Elcin and took her brother. Elcin runs into Christian Rosenkreuz and a white wolf named Silviv; Christian implores her to join them as he promises to protect her and make her his apprentice. 6 Years later in the court of Mehmed II in 1462, The king demands the head of Vlad Dracula amidst his court of which Christian and Elcin are apart. The king bemoans of Vlad’s refusal to pay tribute to his brother Radu of which Radu proclaims that Vlad knew what he was doing due to his arrogance and admits that he must be stopped even despite being his own blood. Elcin argues for the right to go after Vlad to which the king says that she should stay to serve his sexual needs instead which prompts Elcin to fire an arrow at the king pinning his apple to his throne. Impressed by this, the king tells his guards to give Christian and Elcin all the supplies that they will need and tells Radu and Konstantin to aid them in their journey to hunt down the Impaler.GameplayIf you were expecting this to play like the Lecarde Chronicles or classic Vania then you’ll be in for a surprise as when it comes to the gameplay of Wallachia it plays more like a Shinobi game mixed with Contra. Let me quantify this because from a visual perspective you would expect it to play like Vania but it doesn’t at all and is Shinobi in nature. You have at your disposal unlimited standard arrows that can be interchanged with other arrows that you pick up along the way, you also have access to a sword for close range attacks that allow you to destroy boxes and get enemies that run up on you and it does even more damage when you find the sword upgrade which lasts until you get hit. You also get access to more powerful abilities that you can use that come from your companions that you see in the cutscenes giving you either screen nuke abilities or attack buffs and more but at the cost of points that you accumulate throughout the course of the levels.The bow attack allows you to shoot in 8 directions in rapid succession with the ability to shoot down power ups from birds flying overhead and to hit enemies of which majority of your enemies will only take about 1 hit to go down in Contra/Kung Fu fashion but then you will sometimes get enemies that take between 2-4 hits to take down with normal arrows and they can sometimes hit like a truck but like all retro style games all enemies have patterns which you can figure out after a moment or two.GraphicsThe game looks incredibly detailed with character models with many points of details from the characters clothing to the backgrounds and more. The amount of detail in the animation of the characters is nice as the game has a pre-Koji Igarashi Castlevania look to it; think Castlevania Bloodlines and Super Castlevania 4 aesthetics and there you go. If you told me that this was a 16-bit game, then I’d believe you as it no doubt would feel right at home on the Sega Genesis and utilizing that Blast Processing power! Cut scenes are done in a meticulously hand drawn style that is breath taking to say the least. While shown in stills, it no doubt showcases tremendous detail in displaying action and emotion.AudioThe ambience and stage themes are well done and have a strong Vania-style with its dark and brooding vibe. The voice acting is superb with Robert Belgrade of Symphonia of the Night fame and Kyra Buckland of Nier Automata and more!DownsidesBecause this is an arcade style game, you will die a lot…. ALOT! This is an extremely hard game that will be a boon to fans of the old quarter muncher games but will not be something many newer gamers who prefer hand holding will enjoy. That is the downside, the difficulty. The upside; THE DIFFICULTY! In other words; GIT GUD!WrapupIf you are expecting this to be a Castlevania clone, then you will be disappointed as this is not at all that even if aesthetically it looks the part; gameplay wise its more akin to Shinobi and Gunstar Heroes. If you can get past that part along with tremendous difficulty, then you will find a game with a lot to love, deep lore, fantastic graphics, and engaging and challenging gameplay that will be a game that deserves to be in your collection!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm making reference a lot to Castlevania in this review, but this game is it's own thing. It's shooter oriented, it has it's style of graphics and the historical setting is very present.This is a game for fans of the old Castlevania games (before Symphony of the Night) and other difficult platformers of the time. I didn't got past the second stage, but the athmosphere was great and the dialogues excellent, plus I loved how the historical setting was put upfront. Since I prefer a lot more the later Igarashi Castlevania games, I would have loved a function where you can save between stages, so I can pick my game up later, but I understand the choice of the creators to make it more like an old school 16-bit era action game and I respect that. I don't think I will finish this game one day, because I haven't finished a single old Castlevania title, but I truly appreciate the athmosphere and the historical setting. I'm happy to support the team behind this game and I hope that with their next game, it will be possible to save since it seems to be a metroidvania. I'm looking forward to this next project!For fans of the old Castlevania games don't hesitate and get it, you will be served.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has to be one of my favorites I played so far in 2020. Everything from the music, the graphics, the mechanics, to the fact that I want to bang my head against a wall when I die brings me back to when the SNES and Genesis days. This is the type of game I grew up playing and it really took me back to my childhood. Every single moment of what I played of the first 3 stages seemed to be paced  really well. The game so far doesn't have a slow point or a point where I feel like I am overwhelmed, every death  is a teaching moment and next time you run that part of the stage you have already learned what to do different.  Like most games from the time period that this game emulates, you get power-ups for your weapons as well as health. This become valuable commodities. Use them well and use them carefully, they will save your life and make things easier for you. If you like old school horror platformers, then definitely give this game a try.Pros:Scratches that Nostalgia itch nicelyFantastic musicGreat sprite and graphicsInteresting storyChallenging and fun mechanicsCons:Controls do feel a little stiff (as they were back then)Can be difficult for people not used to this genre of game (keep at it, I promise it will be worth it)To the Developers:Thank you for this, it is a great game with a lot to offer. I don't really have too much to complain about because after 20+ years muscle memory just kicks in and it's like falling off of a corpse cart. I look forward to see how you can improve this game without taking the difficulty factor away. I understand you want to make as accessible as possible but if you have to make an extra difficulty and just move normal to hard, hard to (insert 1 step beyond hard here) then I am totally behind you all doing that. I look forward what you have to give us in the future and will keep playing and recommending this to people I think will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing through this game reminds me so much of the old-school arcade games. The graphics, the sound effects, and especially the difficulty are all on-point for that style of game. If you're looking for a Contra or Ghouls and Goblins type game, this is definitely something to look at. The story is very reminiscent of Castlevania (not surprising with a title like this). Also, the music is perfect for this type of game. I think the only complaint I would have is that there is no save feature. If you die, you just go back to the beginning of the current screen, but a save slot or even password system would have been nice. As it is, you'll have to beat it in one sitting.Overall, I'd recommend this if you're looking for a high difficulty game with great style. The atmosphere, music, and overall play-style really bring me back to arcade games/NES games. If you're anything like me, get ready to die a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Wallachia: Reign of Dracula

_childDocuments_.review: Partial review!So played through a few stages already and it's super fun!!! It's like Contra but in another time period. Fast paced run and gun action! Really cool, high quality sprite work and backgrounds. While I love anime style, it's really refreshing to see this game chose a more realistic look for characters. Decent voice acting. Somehow they even got the voice actor who played Alucard in Symphony of the Night and O.D. in Bloodstained!Soundtrack is very good too. I like it!The levels are varied enough, there are many cool ideas and surprises through the stages. Once you learn the levels, it'll be easy to run through them and you'll feel like a badass! I think this will be an ideal speedrun game too! Upgrades are fun, and some parts of the levels encourages you to use different type of arrows to hit certain enemies easier. I like that you don't drop your old weapon but you can change between them (though other than the normal arrows, you have limited use on them, use them wisely!)It's not easy though, small health bar (can be upgradeable but still not one hit death), easy to die on first few tries but it has the typical addictive nature as old Contra games had. My only complaints are the controls. They are actually really good and super responsive! But putting Esc as a "give up" button? Space as pause? Please, change these! Escape would be better as a pause. I Game Over'd my self a few times because I had to take a short break and I pressed Escape by accident as I am used to it from many games. Not cool.Stand still aiming didn't work with Shift for me. I could aim, but not to shoot! I changed it to another button and works fine. But still, frustrating. Sometimes I feel like the menu controls are not intuitive enough. You can get used to it quickly thankfully. Really nice game! Needs some minor tweaks but it's a good stuff already. Probably this is one of those arcade style games that I'll play through many times. It's casual fun, I guess you can speedrun it pretty quickly when you learn it. I played through Contra many times, I'll do the same with this one too!Ps.: What the **** was the pronunciation of Wallachia?!

Come. Join us. The cybernetic clash of the century is about to begin! _childDocuments_.review: I was very excited for this game when it was first announced and I quickly joined the hype train pretty much only because I know and love Ninja Theory's past works. But my god, this is an awful attempt to compete with games these days like Overwatch, or Paladins. In a day and age where those types of games have 30+ heroes, multiple game modes, stable servers, and strong character design, it is really hard to compete in the genre. Ninja Theory tried and failed, unfortunately. At launch, it was a disaster. Server instability caused matches to lag out. I was joining fresh matches with 4v2 setups. It was awful. I came back month after month hoping to see improvements, new modes, characters, ANYTHING. At the time of writing this, months later we have 1 new character and no other new game modes or incentives to keep players playing this game. It is really sad to see a developer not only cave creatively to their publisher, but also cave monetarily. They knew they would put this as a game pass game, and it almost feels like it was designed with failure in mind. So it really feels incomplete and not worth the full price. I wanted to enjoy this game, I really did, but the developers really failed to deliver what we all expect in this type of game, and lost a fan of their label once I saw what is happening to this game. Ninja Theory now developers quick cash-grab games for Microsoft as a third party. This is the first tile to demonstrate that trend and I guarantee it won't be the last from them. And I it is deeply saddening to see such a hard-working team cave to the demands of the hungry executives and shareholders at Microsoft. I can't see myself buying another Ninja Theory game for a long time. And if I do, it will definitely be on deep sale and not full price. I attempted a refund, but since I spent over 2 hours sitting in empty lobbies, tweaking my settings to achieve stable framerates, and lagging out and disconnecting in matches, I was not able to do so. So buyer beware: This is NOT the Ninja Theory you know and love. They have changed.

_childDocuments_.review: When you're not working as a team, when you're not prioritising targets, when you're just 4 random people running around in the hopes of some solo victory, Bleeding Edge will come of as an annoying game where killing people takes a lot of time and effort, and where everything you do is undone by one healer in a floating chair spouting wall-e jokes at you...But when you're with the right people, when you time things together, when you have someone else's back and they in return have yours, Bleeding Edge shows itself as a wonderful team brawler; the style's great, the character designs are insane in a very endearing fun way, the combat while not always complex has a satisfying feel to every hit, the music just enhances the style, and because of the way ranged characters lock on guarantees 100% accuracy there's this feeling of a very defined set of rules to facing each character; you don't hope the range person will miss, you know they'll hit, and you know how much it's hurt, and you can factor that in to every decision you make as a team. I use a controller and while sometimes the lock on can be a bit finicky and the camera occasionally erratic, the game remains consistently fun, plus being blindsided by a train because you foolishly didn't look can often be a very funny thing anyway. That's the main thing really, the games fun, yes like any team game those matches where everyone isn't quite gelling together (I won't say "when the team your with is bad" because more often than not we're as much part of the problem, let's just be honest here we're all allowed to suck a little, it's perfectly fine if you take it in your stride and still have fun and at least try to work together well and actually be nice to everyone and all that regardless of anyone's, including your own, skill) can be frustrating but the lowest lows can also allow you to receive the highest highs and in this case that is absolutely true, with friends and with the right team and with a good enemy with close matches and back and forths this game becomes a blast :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. It's not for everyone, but it is great. The gameplay is heavily team-oriented; you're not going to get anywhere trying to pull off a solo playstyle because there is no snowballing. At the beginning of the game you're as powerful as you'll be at the end. This can be seen two ways: one could say that it's bad because it doesn't reward someone for being skilled(or lucky) or one(such as myself) could say that it's good because you'll never be put into a situation in which a comeback is entirely impossible short of your entire team disconnecting, which leads to the next topic: Disconnects. Players often disconnect when they're losing and as far as I can tell there is no penalty for this, which is obviously a problem.Next up, the characters: They are all wonderful. They all look as if they could be the main character of their own game. In addition, there's some physical disability representation; Buttercup lost her legs in a vehicle accident, Cass lost her legs to paraplegia and Kulev is dead. In addition, all of the characters have very unique movesets, such as Mekko(a dolphin in a mech) has a kit which revolves around blocking damage with a bubble shield in order to power up his abilities or Azrael, who has the ability to apply "Soul Eater" stacks with his basic attacks, which cause damage over time and power up his abilities(also, he can glide with his wings at the cost of Stamina). Stamina is the resource tied to dodging, which can be used to escape combos; Stamina is also used for a few abilities in the game, such as the aforementioned wings.If you don't like how your character looks, there are many skins to be had if you're willing to grind for them. There is no way to acquire skins with real-world currency; once you've bought the game, you need only to work for the skins. The skins themselves range from recolors to complete costume changes, but the characters are still generally quite recognizable regardless of the skin they're using. In addition, there are skins available for the hoverboards(which most characters use to traverse the map more quickly) which are also bought with in-game currency. Also available for in-game currency are emotes and mods. Emotes are self-explanatory, though mods are less so.You can have a loadout of up to three mods, most of which signficantly alter your character's feel. Some of the effects of certain mods are as follows:-Increasing your character's HP-Decreasing one of your abilities' cooldowns-Increasing the range of your basic attacks-Giving you HP regen while using your Super-And more!Currently, there are two gamemodes available: Objective Control and Power Collection. In the first, you fight the other team over 1-3 objectives(some of which may move throughout the match), with your team gaining points towards victory based on how many objectives you currently control. The second has two phases: Collection and Deposit. In the collection phase you run around the map, destroying barrels with power cells in them which you need to collect. You drop all of your cells on death, so killing enemies to take their cells is always a good thing. The deposit phase consists of going to a dropoff point and standing still until your cells have been deposited. The first team to fifty cells wins.Their are a few maps, all with their own hazards such as two large trains which occasionally run through the middle of the map or gates of electricity which fry anyone who tries to go through. Each match will have a randomly determined map modifier applied, such as randomly appointing one player the "VIP", giving them buffs until someone kills them and a new VIP is chosen.Ultimately, I highly recommend this game and hope that the community can grow larger, that the game might be better-funded and receive more updates. Though I received this game as a gift, I fully consider it worth the forty dollars it costs.

_childDocuments_.review: I love melee multiplayer games. For $30, you are getting a full game. No loot boxes, no battle passes, just straight game. You can unlock new skins, hover boards, taunts, and mods all in game. I grew up on Rakion, Gunz the Duel, Jedi Academy, Blade Symphony to name a phew.This game is essentially a hero team based game. A lot of people might call it an overwatch clone, but its nothing like overwatch.The majority of the characters are melee based outside of a few support and damage dealers. The gameplay consists of capture the point and capture canisters.The gameplay loop keeps the action going constantly and so far I've found it very balanced. I main a tank who uses dual machetes and has a life support system. Think Bane from Batman and Danny Trejo combined. He is awesome at staying alive and stunning enemies and big groups but can easily be kited by good ranged players.There is also a character who can control enemies as his ult. I controlled the enemy tank and made them jump off the map, killing themselves and allowing our team to capture the point.There are only 11 characters now, and I hope new characters are maps are added. But this game is fresh and immense fun. And at $30, it's relatively cheap.I highly recommend buying this is you are bored of games like Overwatch, Smite, Paladins, Battlefield, Counter-Strike, etc. I'm hoping it catches on and becomes much more popular.

_childDocuments_.review: Bleeding Edge comes dangerously close to not being recommended, mostly on its price tag. The mechanics are solid, the setting and characters a wonder to behold, the art style and music astonishing.... but it costs £24.99. That's a lot to pay for a game wherein the players you're teamed up with can make or break your experience, where victories can be few and far between, and defeats are miserable. Whatever good is masked and what ill is exemplified by the matchmaking, and there's quite a few things missing for this to ask for the money it does.Ninja Theory's brawler pits four players against another four, each choosing characters within the Damage, Support and Tank roles. It doesn't take long to figure out character's strengths and weaknesses, or their counters and who they're best suited against. Characters are easy to learn and take only time to master, the hardest part being putting up with a character you're unfamiliar with when someone else has taken your main.There's five maps each with muted gimmicks such as bottomless falls, fiery pits, electrified walls and conveyer belts, capitalising on its funky visual style and hectic audio. Within these maps players will partake in two game modes, both of which are too similar for there to be much replayability if you're not instantly hooked on your first win of the day. Capture Objectives and Power Cells are the essentially the same - capture the marked location and hold it while brawling, and in the latter do the same except handing in vital Power Cells to earn points. It's not the most exciting stuff, but it gets the job done."Getting the job done" is really the best Bleeding Edge can claim to do. Before the likes of Brink, Overwatch and Paladins: Champions of the Realm, Bleeding Edge could well have fit in an industry bloated with grey and brown military shooters. But it seems too late to be a pioneer in any multiplayer subgenre, and too early after the hero shooter/brawler fad.I only recommend this because Xbox Game Pass allows you to experience it for £3.99/month to begin with (£1 for new subscribers' first month). The game suits Free-to-Play with its style and desperate need to grab new players' attention, but doesn't have enough to sell for real world cash. It's between a rock and a hard place, but it's fun enough while it exists. How long that will be remains to be seen.

_childDocuments_.review: Prelude: The game has crossplatform between Steam, Win10 and Xbox. Steam numbers do not reflect real playerbase size. So if you have friends with an Xbox and want to play with them in this game you can do so, even if you have Steam or Win10.Bleeding Edge has been a rollercoaster of emotions for me, starting from the point where i saw it pop out in my main Steam Store page. When i saw it for the first time i was very surprised something like this, a 4v4 arena brawler, got released in this day and age, since the popularity of these kind of games declined over the years. A lot of games have gone past with these exact same characteristics: Gigantic was one of my favourite ones and the most memorable one.At first it was a hard pass for me, "a 4v4 brawler now? There's no way i'm falling for it again"; but i did fall for it. The game kept popping in my head, some reviews also emerged, having the same underwhelming feeling about the game. Then one of the streamers I use to watch started playing it, and there's where everything began. I hesitated, but eventually dropped by wallet and got the game, and i've been loving it so far.It's a straightforward game, yet very deep on its very nature. Simple Rock Paper Scissors mechanics that blend together in unison and make for a great, smooth gameplay. Fights feel organised, complete organised chaos, immersive scenarios and a soundtrack that you didn't know you would like up until you stopped to listen to it.Made by a studio of 20 people, Bleeding Edge delivers a polished experience with a constant support by the developers, with patches pretty much every 2 weeks with balance changes, additions and fixes for everything people have problems with.For a small studio, this game is a careful crafted gem with a lot of love put into it, it is a team based game so it's usually frustrating for the common eye if your team members don't focus on the objective, get picked 1 by 1 for the entire enemy team and so on, matchmaking needs fixing since higher skilled people get matched with newer people making the balance of matches a bit unfun at times.Other than that, it's a solid game with a lot to be discovered, with 2 modes, Battery Collection being the weakest one, and very different characters to choose from; with customization for every single one of them, fun and unique gameplay and very satisfying melee system. If you once loved games like Gigantic and other brawlers, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Aight, so, this is gonna be part review and part "things people aren't noticing", and I recognize that I have barely any time in this so far, but the majority of the people playing seem  clueless (I'm somehow getting top kills with supports) and I think it's important for the health of a game like this that it gets favorable reviews to beat out people who have no idea what the're doing ASAP.Bleeding Edge is essentially a hero shooter with very little shooting. If that makes sense at all. A big chunk of the cast is melee only, and you straight-up lock on to enemies, so mechanical skill is heavily de-emphasized outside of the parry mechanic (It'll be interesting to see how that plays out).The result is a game where teamplay and decision making can shine almost exclusively, and it's been revealing just how awful most people are at understanding how a team fight works (and, in some cases, being around for team fights at all.)A lot of people seem to be making the mistake of thinking that "just walk up to whoever and start smacking them" is a valid idea, and then get pissed when it doesn't work and decide the game's brainless. Who's fault is that?Another thing that a lot of people aren't grasping is when they should and shouldn't chase people down. I've already had way too many games where half of my team runs after the bird lady as she just pulls away from everyone, wasting way too much time, letting the enemy team get tons of objective points in the process. Point is, chasing slippery characters is mostly the job of the DPS, otherwise, you should be thinking in terms of objectives. My most played character right now is the huge Polynesian dude, who can't even dash. Sometimes, with that guy, ranged characters will just plink at you. That's part of the job description, and you need to either waste an initiate on them or hope a DPS recognizes that you're making someone waste their time.Speaking of tanks, a lot of people don't seem to recognize just yet that unlike supports and DPS characters, they don't get knocked away at the end of a combo. They'll stay right where they are. Don't just facetank tanks, even if you think you're some big tank killing murder machine. A tank's biggest weakness is that you can just stay away from them.By the way, I'm pretty sure there are times when you *don't* want to go through your full three or four hit combo, if you're out of dashes and don't want an enemy to escape.Point is, it seems like there's fun times to be had when you get two teams that actually understand what they're doing, but expect a lot of noodling around, which generally makes the game seem much more clunky than it actually is.My one real gripe right now is that abilities that can target the ground have their y-axis inverted. Like, you pull back on the analogue stick to move them forward, and there's no option to change it. It's weird.

But once you get used to the control scheme and take advantage of the parry/evade mechanics, the game is actually really fun. The characters all feel really unique and are satisfying to play in their own ways and the combat actually feels surprisingly good (again, once you get a hang of how combat controls). The time to kill is also quite long which means team skirmishes last a nice while versus some other games where characters seem to just explode instantly. That could be good or bad depending on your preferences, but I like long TTKs in games so meh.Overall it's a pretty fun multiplayer PvP hack n' slash sort of game and I'm pretty excited to see what kinds of new characters and content we'll get later down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: To start this I'm going to say most of my time with this game is on the Xbox Game Pass, I have about 6 hours on that and almost an hour when it comes to Steam. With that short amount of time I'm going to say that I love this game. It's flawed, a bit laggy here and there, and has some technical issues but this game is like your favorite sports team that hasn't won a championship in the last 10+ years. It has heart.The characters are gorgeous and well designed with personality nuances that breathe life into them that let you recognize them on sight. With backstories that delve into why they are the way they are and make you see pieces of that lore in everything they say and do. The skill trees are interesting and are complimented with a small three slot system that lets you tweak how some abilities perform from slight damage increases, added effects, or decreased cooldown time.The game modes although there are only two at the moment are fun and the mechanics are tricky but satisfying.If you go into the discussions you'll see a mix of good and bad comments, and all of them are right. Like all things in life this game is filled with good and bad but the potential it could reach is so good it could outweigh the bad in no time. Technical problems can be fixed, framerate limits can be changed, and things can be added later down the road. I understand that people shouldn't throw money away at a game on a whim, especially if it doesn't seem worth it. But I implore you that this one is worth it. This is that game that at the moment you can come to it and play a few matches and then you can go to Overwatch, Apex, or Smite and get that full competitive edge. It's not a blockbuster hit yet but it'll get there, and you'll be finding yourself putting in big hours like with all those games.I just hope the devs don't give up on this game and listen to their small but hopeful community, and I hope that people will continue to give this game a chance. I was there when Battleborn came and I was saddened when it died, and I would hate to see a game that has even more heart than that game die too.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing. I've put about 10 hours into the game at the time of this review. During that 10 hours, about 3-4 things stand out to me that really makes me want to not recommend the game, and possibly stop playing all together. I'd probably continue though, cause I have friends that still play it, but it won't be something I'll play on my own...unless something changes. And if that does, then I'll update this review. That being said, let's get into the reasons:1) CharactersI feel like the characters in this game are almost balanced...almost. Each of the characters offer their own set of abilities and skills and feel somewhat unique to the game itself; you do not really get the feeling of that one character's ability is another character's ability but <insert reason here>. There is no leveling in the game, but there are loadouts a la Paladins, Paragon, etc. in which you can create a loadout of 3 modifications. Each one affect either your stats, such as increasing your max HP by 100, or affects an ability, like giving an ability lifesteal or a slow. You can also choose 1 of two ultimates that each character has at the start of the match. However, there are three characters that stand out as the most ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in the game: Buttercup, ZeroCool, and Maeve (Tank, Support, and Damage respectively). This is because if any (or all) of them are on the enemy's team, then it's pretty much a guaranteed win, assuming they don't play like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ potatoes. Buttercup cannot be unmounted (btw there is a mounting system in play a la HotS), can isolate anyone on your team to get ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ because she has an obscenely long-ranged grab, and has a huge ass lingering AoE ability that slows you by 50% (80% if you have a mod for it). Plus she has an ultimate which is an instant cast knock-up that is also one of the fastest charging ultimates in the game (it is also her best ultimate). Not only that, but she was buffed shortly after the game launched, DESPITE BEING RIDICULOUSLY STRONG!!!!! Essentially, if you want to guarantee a win, you have to have her in your comp. ZeroCool is a support that whose main schitck is healing, and boy does that little ♥♥♥♥ heal like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥; he is basically unmatched (despite the other two being good picks as well). Essentially, you have to kill him any time he leaves his base because if he is left unchecked he will prevent anyone on his team from dying. I would go more about this annoying gamer, but that is gonna tie into another point I want to make later today. Finally, there is Maeve: probably the most annoying damage dealer in the game. Like Zero, there is something about Maeve that I'm gonna save for later, but right now I'm just gonna talk about her most ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ability: her cage. Maeve has a form of CC which is just a cage that she drops on a person and prevents them from moving; the problem with that is that it is the fastest ability in the game and you literally have no way of avoiding it outside of luck. Like, I've been hit by that damn thing around 100 times and it probably missed me like 4 times, and that was because I was trying to dodge someone else when she used it. Speaking of dodging...2) Lock-OnThis game uses the Lock-On mechanic for practically everything. It is also not the best, as sometimes you will, for example, target someone behind you and do an 180 despite looking at an enemy that's in front of you. There are more inconsistencies with the mechanic, and it is basically a crutch for any ranged character since you even hit anyone if you don't lock-on to a target. However, there is a range cap to a lot of things which means that your only way to dodge ♥♥♥♥ is to get the ♥♥♥♥ outta range ASAP...because...everything is guaranteed to hit you. Also, even though I don't like lock-on to this extent video games, I still wouldn't have had a problem if it wasn't for the next thing I'm gonna talk about: dodging and staggering.3) HealingI know I said in the previous point that I was gonna cover Dodging/Staggering next, but as I was typing this I realized that I should cover this first. In this game, there is no anti-heal (except for one mod, don't remember who it was for though), and you pretty much need a healer to win team fights. It even says it in the tutorial...the same tutorial that tells you to kill the healer when you see them (the same tips that mock you for straying too far from your healer, not protecting your healer, or not killing the enemy healer). This is because they pretty much decide every team fight, and every fight usually ends up with everyone trying to hard dive the other team's healer (and praying that they kill him/her fast enough before their own healer dies). Like I've been in matches where the other team would be like "♥♥♥♥ it" and just run after me, despite one of my teammates being an easier kill. Oh, if it wasn't obvious enough, if you play a healer you better be used to being focused and bullied...it's gonna happen all game.4) Dodging/StaggeringNow to my main gripe with this game. In this game, every melee hit staggers you because there is not any way for melee characters to stick to targets. This would prevent you from attacking if you didn't recover before the next hit lands and also casting abilities. Melee attacks would also interrupt your abilities and sometimes the casting animation (which of course still eats the cooldown ;)). The only way to counter this is to dodge, which will free you from combos and put some distance between you and your attacker (or close the distance between you and someone running away). Every character can dodge, except maybe 2-3 of them, and is charge-based: you will get 2 or 3 charges of dodge, depending on the character, and each charge will regenerate after roughly 7 seconds.Why is this a problem? Well the way it is currently implemented does not, imo, fit well into a team-based game. If you get hit by a melee attack you would need to dodge away to not be combo'd to death. If you do that, they can dodge to close the gap to combo you again and it becomes a dance of managing your dodges better than your opponent (on top of managing your abilities). Same goes for range characters: you can dodge to escape their attack radius, but they can dodge to put you back into it. Again, it becomes a dance, but that is not the main problem. You see, that's a 1v1 scenario, which rarely happens in the game. If you get rushed down by 2 or more people, you are guaranteed dead if you don't have any form hard CC (which there is not a lot of) or your teammates nearby. This is because if you dodge the attacks, they can take turns dodging to catch up to you and locking you down while their partner catches up. You could attack that person first, but just like you can deny them the ability to attack their partner can do the same thing to you. I said earlier that healers are a focal point in the game and have to deal with this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ a lot, but anyone can be subjected to this at any point. Oh, and if you don't have any charges left...Honestly, there are a few more problems that I have with the game but this is what bothered me the most to make a review about it. I also probably didn't describe precisely the main problems of the game for me, but if you do decide to buy the game and play it you'll see exactly what I'm talking about quickly. As I said earlier, I'll probably come back to this later and update the review, but for now I wouldn't recommend it to anyone right now. The game is also kinda dead right now, but that's mostly due to the game not even being marketed properly.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;drA genuinely fun third-person arena combat with fun art style and wacky character design at least worth a try, also the next character gonna get released is a damn dolphin in a bowl aquarium docked into a mech So.... what is bleeding edge ? an overwatch ripoff? another cheap attempt at the Hero Shooter?♥♥♥♥ no, fully comparing this game to overwatch wouldn't do it justice, In Bleeding Edge the combat is more focused on melee and close quarter combat, closer to smite than overwatch, where each member of the 4 man team pick one of the 11 heroes and have a close quarter clash on the arena, Ranged combat is also there, but the normal ranged attack will always lock on to enemy automaticallythe arena is also on the smaller side, i think closer to the stage in splatoon 2 in size compared to overwatch, and currently, there are only 2 kinds of game mode, a control point, and a resource gathering, imagine a PVP version of salmon run in splatoon 2.Every single melee hero's attack looks really fluid and beautifully animated, from the little detail like Miko the shaman healer slightly adjusting her feet and stance on her combo string, to the big rotating movement you can see on the attack string on makutu the cyberpunk version of Maui/The rock on cyber steroid.The character design and the overall art style itself, in my opinion, are really well done, its feel like they take inspiration from sunset overdrive punk heavy artstyle add a dash of borderlands style in there and then crank the wackiness to the max, resulting in a bunch of character that looks unique and memorablewhat else to say, the gameplay is quite fresh , the character is interesting, the combat is really team oriented and when your team finally clash with the enemy team it could get really hectic real fast which is really really fun in my opinionOverall i advise you to try this game with an open mind first instead of just jumping to a conclusion based on screenshot alone and marking it as an overwatch ripoff

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't have a single redeeming quality. What follows is a piece by piece review of this game and why I think this game is completely beyond saving.1. Lock On     There is no aiming in this game. Ranged characters automatically lock onto their targets, so for ranged DPS, all you do is hold left click. Now, obviously this is bad from a skill perspective. Learning to aim while getting good at landing head shots vs reliable body shots is an important part of personal progression in any pvp game.  It makes shooting and fighting in this game really dull. You hold left click and wait for their health bar to go down. This is also bad for balance, since every single attack is guaranteed to hit in bleeding edge, the only way to balance this is to give each ranged DPS miserably low DPS. 2. Damage in general/time to kill     It takes absolutely forever to kill someone in this game. To give you an idea, I hopped into the dojo as gizmo and decided to attack El Bastardo and timed it. With max attack speed, it took TWENTY SECONDS of continuous, nonstop fire to kill him. This is a character that has multiple dodges, shields, and an ult that makes him unkillable for a duration while also granting yet more shields. When a character has multiple dodges, movement skills and a heals, killing them takes all game.      It's not just unsatisfying, it's bad for meaningful gameplay too. Let's say an enemy is wildly out of position. In any other pvp game in any genre, this would be an opportunity to punish this player. So, you hook him, slow him with oil, and your team gets busy. Except, he dodges out of the oil, dodges around the corner, tanks your teams damage for 20 straight seconds, dodges again to avoid all incoming CC and damage, continues walking away from you, makes it all the way back to his team and you proceed with having a standard teamfight.  That isn't an isolated occurrence, that's every single match all day every day. Damage is so low in this game it's impossible to punish even bad gameplay sometimes. Yes, you can kill someone quickly sometime... but in 99% of cases, you're going to be chasing the same moron around the map for 40 minutes, holding left click while your eyes glaze over. 3. The Dodge/Stun Mechanic:      If you're hit by a melee attack, you're stunned. You can dodge out of stuns and parry melee attacks, and dodges grant you invincibility frames. On paper, this can sound fairly interesting, but in practice this can be the worst part of the game.      First off, the invincibility. The problem? It's WAY too forgiving. Pressing dodge basically deletes the last 5 seconds of combat, or at least it feels that way. Slow moving projectiles like Kulev's curse won't catch up, and seemingly just fizzle out. All CC's like Mave's cage, freezing shots, melee attacks - they're all nullified for the ENTIRE DURATION of the dodge animation. Dodges ults, attacks, everything. Some characters have up to 3 dodges AS WELL AS movement skills. Since we already covered the low damage potential, you should understand why that makes for an incredibly annoying skirmish.      Secondly, the stun mechanic. I can see why they'd want to change up the formula here, but getting stunned in any game is something that comes at a cost because most developers understand that being stunned to death is an intensely unfun experience. In this game, there are stun skills (all auto locked...) AND all melee attacks stun on hit.      To get out of a stun you can parry the next strike, or dodge. Parrying sounds neat, except if you have any latency at all parrying is impossible. Parrying also requires you to be stationary, so you wind up just taking more damage trying to parry than you would if you dodged. Half the time the game bugs and it wont even let you attempt a parry, it's incredibly touchy. If you don't combo or dodge, you eat the entire melee combo, which can last for 4+ seconds, and you're fully disabled the entire time. If 2 characters are hitting you, sometimes you get so stuck in the flinching stun animation that you can't even dodge, you just have to sit there until you eventually die. It's not fun, there's no skill involved, it sucks.      What's missing from the equation is skill. You either dodge, or die. There's no aiming. There's no damage, your positioning doesn't matter, and even if the enemy team pulls off a fantastic combo, you press shift and it doesn't happen. It's garbage.4. Balance     You can customize your characters with 'mods' which effect your skills, and load 3 per character. Some mods increase your auto attack damage by 7.5%, other skills give some characters permanent 30% movespeed increases in combat. The balancing is all over the place. 90% of the mods are pointless and the other 10% are broken. Getting mod points to unlock mods takes an eternity. You get 1 random mod every time you level, but each manual mod takes 250 points. Breaking down a mod gives 50, and you sometimes get 10 mod points for "completion" at the end of a game. Nobody knows what it means. Sometimes you win and get it, sometimes you lose and get it, but never all the time. It will take you 30+ games to unlock 1 mod if you dont get it randomly from levelling. It's awful.      Some characters are just better than others. Makutu has no dodge, which if you read the earlier parts, is kinda big. He can't catch up to anyone, can't do any damage. Meanwhile buttercup has a pull, an AoE crippling slow, AoE damage, a fast charging AoE damage ult... what were they thinking? Maeve has a reset mechanic where if she gets a kill her skills reset, but her only damage skill is a slow damage over time skill... it makes no sense. Nobody's kits make any sense at all, they don't mesh well and cooldowns are so long, you spend the entire game just left clicking. 5. Design     The maps all feel the same. They're ugly, all take place in the middle of the day, and you can't really tell them apart. It would be so easy to have some occur at night or sunset, really take advantage of the cyberpunk aesthetic some maps have, but they don't. They're just ugly and uncomfortable. Characters designs are bland too. Sure, some of them are unique, like maeve being an elderly cyberwitch, but they're all just sorta samey. None of them stand out. With a roster of only 11 characters, I still have to look some of them up because the miscellaneous punk aesthetic makes them all so forgettable. It's not good. Sure on paper some of them sound crazy "whoah a voodoo cyborg snake!" but I'm just not impressed with the execution. It's just another british dude and I don't really feel the voodoo in his kit. The game has a way of taking interesting designs and making them boring in execution. Skins are all just ugly recolors. 6. The Community    Sure in other games a bad team will lose you the game, but this game's community is unique. Every team is bad. When you need your entire team to focus a single player down for 40+ seconds to kill him, a bad team means you lose and have zero fun. You can't carry, you win or lose depending on who you get matched with. People have been begging for competitive matchmaking so you can queue with skilled players, but they wont add it and there is none. I was actually going to write a lot more but I keep hitting the character limit. Basically, if they wanted to fix the game, they'd have to redesign half the cast, rebalance every single mod in the game, redesign most of the maps, restructure the reward system, setup competitive match making, fix bugs, redo the entire combat scheme, and so much more.. the game sucks, the combat stinks, its grindy and repetitive, the community is trash and the game is dead - 41 average players on steam.This can't be fixed with some elbow grease, literally every part of the game is designed poorly. I couldn't even fit everything wrong with this game into this post. Pass on this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast! Very impressed at Ninja Theory's first attempt at a multiplayer game. The game is has a very unique identity, with each character standing out from the other. Matchmaking is surprisingly quick, despite the low amount of publicity this game has gotten. The gameplay is fun and filled with action, and sweet music to accompany you during the main menu, loading screens, and during the match. The maps are beautiful and are unique as well! However, there are some issues. There is a severe lack of gameplay variety, with only 2 game modes and 5 maps, alongside a limited selection of cosmetic items that are just re-skins of the default skin. Emotes are also lacking, with some characters only having only one emote to buy. The in-game currency is very slow to accumulate. I played 12 hours and only got 3000, enough for one skin and an emote for one character. There are some framerate issues as well, especially when the two teams converge on an objective and brawl. This game is a fantastic first attempt from this development team, and I cannot wait for this game to get more maps, skins, modes, and characters in it. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly, i dont want to bash this game and i dont have the knowledge to do so.Im going to keep this purely personal and try to paint a picture by using other games as examples to maybe get people to make the right decision on buying it or not.When i saw this game i thought it was basically an overwatch clone and that made me excited. It was advertised as a comp focussed game and im not saying it isnt, because again i have no clue what im talking about on a professional or technical level. The biggest deal breaker for me is the slow paced fighting, it is nearly impossible to solo kill anyone that knows what they are doing when using escapes or knowledge on when to engage or not. As a CSGO, R6, Valorant and Dota player i am used to comp games being very heavily team based in the way of needing other characters strength and weaknesses to beat players/characters that you are not capable of dealing with alone.Bleeding edge has the same idea but in my opinion the damage is too low or health is too high. When you pick a dps character and have a hard time killing a support character alone it does not feel rewarding. i understand that it should maybe be played as a brawler where fights should last for multiple minutes with experienced players and trying to focus dangerous characters on the enemy team but it isnt for me personally. I hope i dont misinform anyone and scare them away from this game, the art style is amazing, the characters have actual character and are a blast to play and customize to your own playstyle. Just dont buy this thinking it plays like other games on the market cause you will be disappointed and stuck with a game you dont play like myself.TLDR; If you play comp shooters or other team based strategic games and are used to fast paced fights and capitalizing on the advantage of enemies being dead this game might not be for you. As many other reviews say this is a casual brawler where solo play is rarely the way to go.

_childDocuments_.review: TEMPORARILY NOT RECOMMENDING, LOTS OF SHORTCOMINGS IN PROGRESSION, MATCHMAKING, ETC THAT WILL HOPEFULLY BE IMPROVED UPON BECAUSE THE GAMEPLAY IS GREAT. Too slow overall for the volume of mods. LEAVERS: No penalties that I know of. I want ranked play with reliable (as far as sticking around) teammates.MATCHMAKING: None to speak of that I know of, maybe just off player level? Either way, the sheer stomps that can happen are horrible, but also tied to the previous point of leavers. Some matches feel like an absolute waste of time. FINAL PLAY/HIGHLIGHTS:I don't even care, they're only on major flaws because they might as well not exist. Highlights aren't 100% terrible, but are pretty underwhelming. Final Play is ridiculous because it could just be you walking in circles during the last 3 seconds of the match. Either need to be removed or in need of some serious love. How is the gameplay so polished with everything else feeling  I really hope improvements and expanding upon existing systems are planned in the future and will absolutely turn this review into a positive if improvements are made.

_childDocuments_.review: To start: I myself LOVE this game.It had been on my radar for quite a while and my initial plan was to pick it up on One X. But I bought it here instead.In its current state, there are a few problems, most of which are team based, since the point of the game is to travel in a group and fight each other, as it's a brawler, which is fine.The problem is that some people don't want to work as a team, and it'll instantly affect your enjoyment of the game. In many games like TF2 this is fine, since it's 12v12. In this, it's more noticeable when you've got some guy that's going the opposite direction. People who are claiming this'll be the next Lawbreakers don't grasp that there is crossplay and game pass, so many people won't have even bought it, and obviously because of crossplay, steamcharts isn't very accurate.The port itself is fine, there's rebindable keys, a rather high FOV, but it's locked to 60FPS in-game, but it runs uncapped in menus. Bear that in mind if you're running a high refresh rate monitor, however Ninja Theory claim they're figuring it all out.When there's more content, the 12th character and more tweaks? Yeah, it's worth £25. It's one of the more unique games that has been released this year, and since I'm a fan of cartoony team based games, I'll probably still be playing it, but if you REALLY want to play it, try it on Game Pass first.

_childDocuments_.review: Bleeding Edge is a delightfully different online, team-based game and I hope it manages to find its audience. It shares a number of familiar elements with MOBAs and team-shooters (class-based heroes, ultimate abilities, capture-the-point game play, cosmetic unlockables) but it presents itself with a wonderfully wacky setting and art style, as well as really accessible control scheme.It's a 3rd-person team-brawler kind of game. It honestly reminds me of what you might get if your crossed Devil May Cry, World of Warcraft and Overwatch. Unlike a lot of MOBAs, the game has been streamlined and kept fairly simple. This is an action-brawler first and foremost...but one that requires teamwork to win. And when I say "requires teamwork", I mean it is absolutely crucial. While individual player skill does matter to some degree, this isn't a game where you'll be able to single-handedly take on the enemy team. Even trying to go 2 v 1 in this game is dangerous.While it is a little lean on content at launch, what Bleeding Edge has to offer is a unique, cyberpunk style, action-heavy game play and good potential to let players show off with team-combos and personal flair. I only hope that the game gets enough of a following that the developers find the confidence to add more content (more heroes, game modes and cosmetic options). Right now, I think the game deserves a fair "B-" but with just a little more effort and expansion, it could really be something special.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a game to have fun with friends, I'd highly recommend Bleeding Edge. Bleeding Edge is an mixture between Overwatch and League of Legends, so if you play one of those games, this could be a game you'd like.With its two game modes, Capture the Objectives and Deliver the Power Cells, the game is simple and straight to the point.The competitive ceiling isn't high, and it doesn't take very long for someone to learn how to play their character.One thing I would highly recommend changing/ looking into is movement. The movement/ game flow is pretty slow, so movement plays a huge role in your abilities especially if you invest into playing an advanced character.The maps are pretty simple, and not that unique, however, with the addition of environmental damage (such as getting hit by a train, being burnt by fire, etc.) you can pull off some amazing plays. The character design is on point and looks amazing. Each character is unique and has their own charms and comes with three abilities. You can mod your characters as well, making them unique to your play style.Bleeding Edge, in my opinion, could be classified as a mid-to-high-tier title (7.5/10)If you're looking forward to trying something new with your friends, give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part, the game is incredibly fun. However, there are some things that need to be changed in order to make it fun and inviting for everyone. Firstly, Maeve is a busted hero. flat out, no bones about it; she either needs to be nerfed or she needs to have her cage or her life steal ability removed or completely revamped to make it so she can't trap you and drain you to half health without you touching her. The sneak abilities are also broken, both on Daemon and Maeve; I believe there should be a caveat for them to be able to use those abilities, such as not being able to while anpther player is looking at you. Dashing in the midst of a combo is also extremely frustrating, especially when the other hero is much faster than you. There are definitely some balancing issues that need to be addressed, but otherwise the game has potential to be an extremely fun, completely chaotic time.
