_childDocuments_.review: Okay so...don't just immediately jump down my throat on this one. I gave the game a solid chance. I was excited for this game and I was hopeful for this game. But as it is CURRENTLY I cannot recommend it. I can't recommend the game to you in its current state. It feels empty, surface level of quality, with poorly managed systems. I don't hate the game. I'm just disappointed at the game. (Btw if you're looking for some more in depth information and a better first look at the game then check out the video I put out on my youtube channel. Link Below)But I think the main problems I have with the game is some of its mechanics. The searching for a match to play in. It's broken. It can literally stick you in a server from anywhere and if that happens and your ping shoots over 150 the game automatically kicks you. And you can't control this. So you'll literally be waiting forever just to get into one match. In my first  30 minutes of gameplay time I was literally in the lobby just waiting. I kept finding matches after several minutes of wait time, then I'd be disconnected and have to do it all over again.When I FINALLY got into a match, it was a bit underwhelming. On my first match, my first game, within 1 hour of gameplay. I was the highest scored player on my team. Which shows that this game is either too easy or has some serious balancing issues.The overall gameplay is a lot of fun. But this game doesn't have ranked play, it doesn't have a very fleshed out progressions system. It's gameplay is fun but not innovative or new. And it's connection matchmaking issues make it hard just to get into a match. So yeah...I can't currently support this game but I hope one day that these issues get fixed and I'll be able to come back and buy into the hype. But for now, I'd highly encourage you all to maybe wait a bit for those changes. Thanks for reading and I hope I helped some of you out there to save some money.

_childDocuments_.review: Heavily team based, strategic brawler, with a high skill ceiling that rewards critical thinking. 'Auto'Aiming system as a legacy of SMITE - devs said on stream the game initially was comparable to it and had towers. -Keep in mind that there's soft aiming and lock on which is important to utilise as to not expose yourself and your team whilst you're casting into nothingness and punching air causing no damage. There are specific builds that put characters out of action for a few seconds as it's enough to change the outcome of the battle and you're doing just that, helping the enemy for free.-I have mine rebound to V on hold, camera controlled(switch to the one closest to middle of the screen). You'll be suprised how fast you'll need to snap focus during fights.-It's an essential mechanic and frankly, you'll never win without utilising it. Yeah you actually gotta aim.That mixed in with their experience working on DmC is the combat. I'd go as far as to call the gameplay asymmetric. With how vast the span of abilities, movement and modifiers are for every character. -Not only that each character's gameplay is different but the mods you pick cater to change that gameplay further drastically.(you pick one build of 3 you have saved, as well as the choice of 2 ultimates, interchangeable mid-game in spawn)-Yes, on the surface, for most characters it's a standard chain of attacks with a few twists here and there. Only that completing the chain gives the opponent a window to retaliate or escape. So you gotta figure out how to mix things up with your abilities, movement quirks and aerial attacks to juggle. It's not that simple since most of the time it's not a 1v1.Yes there is parry even when people are out of stamina but they're unlikely to break your combo that way and those don't seem to actually guarantee the punish.Solid fun maps with lots of environmental hazards and randomly generated objective spawns. I oughta praise the cloak field, powerup and health pickup placements. In a word - Intense if that makes sense.Great use of verticality, created in mind for those quirky characters to utilise.Overall, excellent variety of chokepoints and environments to make your battlefield.Level design is strong with this one.Has a useful and quick context messenger, to tell your team what to do and who to focus on.Posts in chat, marks on screen and the mini-map.Maybe I'll come up with something better to say about Bleeding Edge in due time but so far I'm enjoying it immensely.

_childDocuments_.review: I followed this game for a few months prior to release and was quite intrigued by what it had to offer. This game does a terrific job of looking like it could be enjoyable. However, the gameplay is actually some of the worst I've ever had to endure. Suffice to say I was severely disappointed. Combat and movement are clunky to the point that it's actually tedious to perform what should be simple tasks. There is virtually no balance to the game. Three people can be fighting one person, reduce their health to 10%, and then the enemy healer arrives just in time to fully restore the individual's health. For an ult, sure, that seems reasonable. For that to be one of your abilities that has a cooldown no longer than a couple seconds, well, that's just ludicrous. I understand this game is new. I understand it's a small team that created it. That does not excuse a paid game to provide virtually no content, awful gameplay, and balancing issues this severe. I have never before in my entire life requested a refund for a game. I usually bite the bullet if it's not something I see myself playing. This, though. This is just downright wrong. It's like they spent their entire budget on character design and put zero resources into the actual development of the game. This is also my first review ever, I believe. I advocate giving everything a fair shot. This game does not deserve my money. I hope that you, as the reader, will stay away from this game or that you can find pleasure in it where I could not.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a hero shooter without any aiming.  Much more strategic and skill based, you'll love playing with all the geniuses that don't get that.  Running off alone to 'make plays' is basically impossible.  At this stage of the game, the team that stays together almost always wins the match.  The gameplay is very smooth and solid.. no wiffs or ability timings I feel are off.  The only problem here is that with no aiming, it's pretty easy to hit the skill ceiling with each character.  And once that happens, you're entirely reliant on how smart your team is. I know I already mentioned team reliance, but if you're an impatient team gamer, this is not the game for you.  The content is pretty small.  Few maps and only two modes, you definitly need to like the combat to hang around.  This is a great "buy it intending to refund" game, because you'll know pretty quickly if the price is worth you getting to play the characters.  I find a lot of them fun, so I kept it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the foundation to be great but is lacking some basic fundamentals. For a $40 AUS title it was in my opinion a little steep for the amount of content. Nonetheless, I have spent a few days in Que and am enjoying the combat. I am hoping that there will be a number of future updates that will allow for more gameplay experiences such as an increased shop and cosmetic items, a more robust variety of characters and skills, addition of in-game sound effects such as commentators and kill vocals etc. and a progression system or similar. Unfortunately the game does suffer from a toxic player base already. This is in part due to the lack of matchmaking and unnecessarily allowing you to join a losing match mid way through. I cannot stress how important individual skills need to be rewarded if this game is to be around for more than a short period as well. Currently you can be in an uneven match up and any efforts to participate impact 0 to the overall score or objective, no matter how well you do. If you do not work as a team then there is no chance of winning. In saying this, I have personally found it very enjoyable when you do find a few people to play with in a team. This has led to many close matches and back-and-forths between the teams. This is where the combat really shines and how you play your characters matters the most. I would highly recommend this game (although I would rather it be F2P as it feels like it should be a F2P game with the amount of content available at the moment) despite some flaws that can be ironed out in future. P.S - I am a PC only player and I do believe that there was an error in the decision to auto target opponents with melee and ranged attacks and abilities. It to me is a missed opportunity to showcase skill and it feels less engaging when playing.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR only get the game if you're willing to sit on it for a while and hope the devs make some common sense changes, if you don't mind autotargeting (aka full aim assist) for all ranged attacks, and if you don't mind a mostly controller designed gameJust a note: I only played this game for a little bit before refunding it because i couldn't see myself spending a whole lot of time on it, but I made sure to give proper analysis to its gameplay elements.I actually like the game, and it definitely has big potential behind it, but there are some pretty big problems as well. For one, it's a little bare-bones. Not really that many menu features or customization options, especially when it comes to matchmaking. You're kinda just plopped into a match without any real organization or setup.     In the few games I played, leavers were really really common, and they don't get replaced right away. Being down a player is a massive disadvantage. According to other reviews, there aren't any leaver penalties, so you might just have to prepare to get beasted when your team has a lower player count.    Another thing is that the game was clearly made for controls without any real focus behind mouse/keyboard; aiming the abilities has some really weird form of targeting that's pretty unpleasant with a mouse. The menus are obviously made for controllers as well, though that's not really too big of a deal. It does leave everything feeling a bit "simple", though. The quick comms menu for keyboard is REALLY bad. The default bindings are all the way on the right side of the keyboard, meaning you have to either take your hand off the mouse or your movement to use them.    The gamemode where you collect power cells is also kind of bad. It takes a century to actually deposit them, and any damage you take instantly interrupts it. I think you get a single point for every kill, so it just turns into a weird deathmatch where your teammates are often spread out trying to collect stuff and dying one by one. Control points is control points, though, the same as any game. I will mention that it's way too hard to chase people down. Seems like most mobility for any character is just a single dash in a straight line with a cooldown, so good luck actually catching up to or punishing anyone on their hoverboard. As far as combat goes, though, it actually seems pretty good in general. Dashes are really strong, but stamina comes back quite slowly, so if you spam it you're in trouble, especially because dodging enemy abilities usually relies on your dashes. That being said, getting caught in a 1v2 melee situation is basically just impossible and you'll get stunlocked until you die. I think there needs to be a greater way for a player to survive that kind of situation that isn't just running away. The auto targeting for ranged characters is pretty meh, too. All that means is that they can never give a ranged character a lot of damage or they'll be instantly broken. It also means that there doesn't feel like there's much skill involved just holding down left click while looking in the general direction of the enemy; the auto targeting radius is really big. That's my biggest gripe with the game overall, autotargeting on every ranged single target ability and attack makes it feel pretty unskilled / boring. Aside from the weird mouse targeting for aoe abilities though, the design for those are pretty fun and interesting.    The game is really nice looking, too. All the abilities effects are good, the character models and animations are really nice, texture work is super clean, and the backgrounds and locales are interesting (if not super unique). It's super well optimized, too, and everything feels really smooth. Even if you don't particularly like the aesthetic, the game is pleasant to look at no matter what.All in all, it's a pretty solid MP brawler, and at $30 it's really well priced. It's not for everyone, but for those who can get enjoyment out of it, I think you'll get plenty of time out of it.

_childDocuments_.name: Bleeding Edge

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing visuals and character design, pretty good combat with a surprising level of nuance - especially with combos, and an all-in-all a fun game.I should also point out that while there currently aren't a huge number of characters or skins for them, the character customisation with the "mod" system (not the Steam Workshop kind), as well as different hoverboards, colour schemes per hoverboard, and trails (think Rocket League) - adds up to be a pretty good amount of customisation nonetheless.Mods, which let you pick a combination of three different buffs for your character, and being able to pick from one of two super abilities (ultimates) at the start of each match, definitely adds a nice level of customisability to the combat as well, which I quite like.I also really like the fact that there is no way to use real world currency to purchase in-game cosmetics and gameplay-altering character mods. Instead, you earn in game currency by simply playing the game, and because that's the only way to earn it, it feels a lot more balanced and less grindy than other games, giving a much better sense of progression.Anyone that's complaining about the price point should keep this in mind, especially when comparing it to games like Overwatch (which costed MORE money to buy than Bleeding Edge at launch, and still capitalises off loot box sales with real world money).Honestly, I don't think its fair to expect Ninja Theory to release a game without in-game purchases for free, and I think the price point they did release it at is pretty reasonable.What this game does need is a little more content - maybe an extra game mode like pushing a payload (I know this may draw too much comparison to Overwatch and/or TF2), an extra map or two, and maybe an extra character or two - although I'm more keen on a payload map than I am for more characters at this point.With that said, I still think for something that's just launched, and isn't capitalising off its players with lootboxes and microtransactions, they've done a pretty good job!The content will come, and I'm more than happy to keep playing in the meantime :)

_childDocuments_.name: Bleeding Edge

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very good.If you like 3d team lite-fighters, this is pretty much all there is in the current period.There is no pay to fashion and no pay to win. You can't buy anything in game with cash.There isn't much for character cosmetics (3 for each character), but there are tons of hoverboard options.There are no lootboxes.Some will feel that there is little progression because the game doesn't do the currently popular 'games as a service' model. I think Ninja Theory is participating in good business practices, but due to this choice, this game won't keep you playing just because you want the little skin thing or the digital golden weapon. If that's a dealbreaker for you, you might have a clue about whether you will like this game. Do you like games for the fun, or do you like games for the rng digital item collection? This game focuses on the fun and nixes the rng cosmetics (you buy cosmetics with earned currency).The balance is okay. It's early on but a couple of the tanks are a little undertuned, still, they have ways to uniquely contribute. One of the undertuned tanks has an ultimate that gives the team invincibility, and the other one is the highest aoe dps tank. There are a couple of dps that are overtuned, but one of them is very agro with little ability to flee, and the other one has ults that are either unreliable or low impact if you aren't intentionally split from the group.Other than those four, the balance is pretty close to spot on in my opinion. I expect that the balance will be brought into line, because the rest of the cast is tightly balanced.The game has a small pool of fighters, which is likely why the balance is so good for this genre. This might be a good thing or a bad thing for you.My experience is that every single character is fun to play. Usually, I struggle to find a fun character.You can play fairly different viable comps in this game -- you could swap from a defensive disengage comp to an offensive comp, off the top of my head, your team makeup can viably differ from 3 healers and 1 dps, to 2 healers 2 dps, to 1 healer 1 tank 2 dps to 3 dps 1 healer.So not only is the character balance okay, but the comp balance is pretty good, because it allows you to see fairly different comps that do fairly different things.It is impressive for a game this early on to have better comp balance than other team games that have been out for decades.The game modes are 1) capture the points, in which between one and three points have to be captured every so often and 2) capture the power cells, in which you must collect power cells and turn them into randomly chosen points.I thought I wouldn't like either of these modes, and would rather a capture the flag mode, or a deliver the thing mode (like rainmaker), but it turns out that these two modes are very fun, probably because they force so much team work around the objectives, and decision making about how to position to get the most points from the objectives.The lag hasn't been much of an issue for me. Once every 8 or 9 matches i might see someone teleport out of my combo.Finally, the sound is good. When you cap an objective the music gets louder, which is cool.

_childDocuments_.review: very enjoyable and competitive if you have a team that understands a good team composition. I see people comparing this to Overwatch and I cant disagree more. This is a melee based battle arena, but not base defense like a traditional MOBA would be.  There are two game modes. Objective Control and Power Collection. Objective control is what it sounds like, and power collection has two phases. Phase one you collect power cells, after a certain time period turn in points activate and you must turn in your power cells while you team defends you. Or you kill the enemy team and steal their cells and turn them in. Satisfying to play with a controller and kb/m. I think this game will maintain a stable player base for a good amount of time based on the fact that it is cross-platform. I'm going to call out my fellow PC gamers here.....turn on you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mics and quit being a recluse. This is a team game and communication is key. If you don't have a mic that's fine, We'll have fun destroying your team. As always take negative reviews on steam with a grain of salt, do some research and formulate you own opinion. For the question is always does this game look fun? if the answer is yes, hit that purchase button. See ya out there

_childDocuments_.review: Overall at this early stage BE is a bit of a mixed bag; general art direction and varied character designs are a big plus while F2P-style progression, though without microtransactions/loot boxes (...yet-- again the pace of progression and the presence of a low-output currency definitely feel like the door is being left open for those to be added later) put a damper on things.  Enjoyment at this point hinges pretty strongly on thoughtful team comp and matches can be very one-sided, esp if teammates have a habit of wandering off and your opponents do not, and the smaller roster yields some characters that are strategically varied and relatively simple to learn, even when marked as being more advanced. It's hard to say how much of a long-term future this has-- it's definitely shooting for an Overwatch vibe, and Ninja Theory doesn't have much experience with live service models, but there's definite potential here, and with time (and esp. new game modes/characters/more varied and interesting unlocks) it could develop a solid audience, and my experience overall has been a positive one that I've put a fair amount of time into.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a decent team PvP multiplayer game. The fundamentals they teach in the tutorial are VERY important. I'm not worried about content or lack thereof, since this game has just come out, but I feel this game has enough to satisfy at launch, plus a new dlc character is already on the way. _childDocuments_.review: I really like the fighting mechanics. _childDocuments_.name: Bleeding Edge

_childDocuments_.review: It's actually..really good. From the videos and blogs I'd seen I didn't expect it to be any good; I figured it was another cheaply-made, thrown-together mixed-bag like games we've seen before. In reality, the devs evidently did their best to make the game as fun as it possibly could. No, the game is not perfect, and  yes it does have it's flaws, but no game is and all games do.The fact of the matter is, the issues people are raging their soft little heads about are temporary. People outside of the US having unstable connections is due to the Europe, Oceania and Asia servers having a fault that stopped them connecting; for now, everyone is playing on the american servers.  The lack of players is because most play on xbox, where over 80% of the population is; steam only shows those connected through steam. There are also several popular, long-running games with less players than that that still survive.Another moronic issue I keep reading is that the characters aren't good-looking. ..Why do you care. It's a PVP online game, not a harem anime; get a grip. The game is well-built, the characters are balanced (for the most part. looking at you, nidhoggr you broken little emo douche), and most of the in-game issues described are from the players lack of knowledge and refusal to play the tutorial. No, the game is not auto-locked, you're just ignorant and didn't play the tutorial; if you had you'd have known you can use the LT trigger on your controller to pick targets, and click the right camera stick to switch.Fact of the matter is, most of the people raging in the threads haven't played it, and a good 80% of the issues are actually player-issues, not dev, server or game issues. The game isn't bad because you don't know how to play a tutorial or git gud.Solid 7.5 out of 10 for now. I'll re-rate when the game is older.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleeding Edge

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential. If you like teamwork oriented games then this is definitly worth picking up. The game is heavily against solo play and lone wolfing a situation.  So if you have the playstyle to go alone then this it's not going to be enjoyable. If you want to win you and your team HAS to stay in a ball. If you don't then you get picked off one by one. TLDR; Game is VERY team oriented. Playing with a group = Fun   Lone wolfing/solo play= Not fun
_childDocuments_.name: Bleeding Edge

_childDocuments_.review: So far, playing a limited amount of time in the game, but having quite a bit of moba experience and moba-esque styled games like this, i would say this is at a fantastic start! I enjoy the combat. Despite the autolock, its fairly unforgiving. The stamina system is something that will help separate good players from not so good ones. The game only released just a few days ago so i am sure there is big changes to come in the following months. Something I would appreciate is a big focus in optimizing the game. I have all my settings set to as low as possible and yet my frames still become and issue. Another big problem is the connection to the server. I find it often that everyone is rubber banding or at least the enemy team seems to be. These two issues are massive things that impact all players regardless of background or skill level. Please fix them asap, otherwise the game is at a great point for just released.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleeding Edge

_childDocuments_.review: The longer I play this game, the more I discover and the more I love it.It seemed so simple to begin with. Almost too simple. Soft lock on all abilities and one button combos. But as I play I realise positioning, team play and decision making is where the complexity of this game is. There's also lots of "hidden" combos for different situations (for example Makutu can tap tap tap tap (normal), tap tap hold tap to launch them in the air and kick them away, tap tap hold hold to launch and body slam and even tap hold hold hold for the craziest of hijinks.Again, this is not much if you're comparing it to a traditional fighter, but it's depth I didn't notice on first play through, so worth noting for those coming in cold.The last realisation I had with this game is it's designed for really good melee combat. If you want maximum fun don't play ranged.I recommend this game, acknowledging that it needs to grow and hopefully the devs get time for that. It is also incredibly punishing if your team don't play together, so it can be frustrating for pugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Bleeding Edge

_childDocuments_.review: It has potential, but it needs a lot more content added to it. More game modes, more characters, more customization. Despite it having Xbox and PC crossplay, its Social features are very scarce without any lobby or group finding chats outside of its solo que matchmaking. Purchasable skins are very lackluster with just mild recolors on default skins, unless you got the  preorder skins and both its ingame currencies (one fo customisation and another for mods) are not purchasable and only earned by playing which is unfortunate for people who want to customise their look and dont mind shelling out real money to do so, a missed opportunity for the game.I give it a 7/10 for its characters and fun gameplay, but it loses points in lack of customisation and social interactions and group finding features. _childDocuments_.name: Bleeding Edge

It needs to have hard attacks, I hate to say, it to mix up the combos ( I get it the cool down attacks are sort of that). The supers are there but seems small and not very flashy. I mean its still have some kind of boring character movement, and a shady "lock-on" option, i am accustomed with this type of game and i know that this "lock on hero" mechanic is a bit disturbing as sometimes u cant really actually lock the hero you want, and it is crucial cause some hero in this game is a melee type, rather than a shooter. What i meant is if your are using mouse & keys sometimes you have to really rely on manual camera control (and i like that) instead of using the lock on camera the game provides. But for someone who's not use with this type of camera......welp see for your self the in game players.....just bashing stuff around without hitting anything trying to lock on but needed to keep pressing "hero lock change" button. Well yes theres an option in the setting on whom to lock. But the fact that this is a team game so you need to really precisely know whom to kill first. And in my opinion in this kinda camera movement is, please add a cross hair on the screen, so the camera can lock where the cross hair is, instead of focusing on clicking and switching target then you can pin the target. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a refreshing deviation from the standard Hero Shooter genre like Overwatch. Ninja Theory knows its way around melee combat, and it really shows. I played the first Closed Beta, and though I was a little disappointed that there were no additional fighters to choose from on full release, I have no doubt they'll be releasing new fighters and adding content to this game. Learning how to play each fighter is almost as involving as learning to play a new Overwatch hero. Each fighter has such a unique kit and set of mechanics that over time, your prowess with a fighter will really start to show. That being said, the "Hard Carry" potential in this game is on the low side. Most fighters have a long Time To Kill, even in a 1v1. Staying together as a team of 4 is essential. If your Daemon player thinks he's Genji and tries to go off on flanks, you're gonna lose. Thankfully, I'm sure the MMR system should sort out these weaker players until they learn how to group up. The Mods system allows some awesome customization, and they do let you switch fighters and mod loadouts mid-match. I honestly love this game, though it could definitely use some more content and some work on the region separation in matches. Looking forward to seeing what it will become.

name: OlliOlli World
detailed_description: OlliOlli World is a bold new skateboarding action-platformer that’s bursting with personality. Flip and flow through the vivid and vibrant world of Radlandia, meeting colorful characters as you grind, trick, and air your way to discover the mystical skate gods on your quest for Gnarvana. Traverse a delightful and weird world as you take on missions, challenges, and make new friends along the way. Customize your character’s looks, tricks, and style while you experience explorable levels with multiple paths that provide an array of opportunities for player expression. Challenge the world in Leagues or dare a friend to beat your best tricks on one of millions of sharable levels. Experience the accessibility, depth, and player freedom as you dive into the signature flow state gameplay of OlliOlli World. OlliOlli World marks the third entry in the critically-acclaimed OlliOlli series from Roll7, the BAFTA and multi-award-winning independent studio. KEY FEATURES Take a trip across a lush skateboarding utopia that is filled to the brim with eccentric characters and vibrant locations that are begging to be explored. Find your grind in Inflatable Alley or blaze down Los Vulgas to discover new paths, fresh side quests, rad rewards, and epic trick opportunities. All perfectly complemented by a hand-picked compilation of IDM and Electronica tracks. Super tight controls combine with highly refined gameplay to ensure a silky smooth ride. Not a Pro? Don’t worry – OlliOlli World welcomes you with open arms, allowing new players to tear down streets and pull off sick method grabs without fear of faceplanting the curb. Think you’ve got what it takes? Achieve mastery through millions of unique levels in sandbox mode or compete against rivals around the globe in Leagues with a hugely deep combo system with over 100 moves to master and combine in your battle for the highest score. Cruise through Radlandia's epic skate-haven and prove your skills to unlock special rewards that let you customize your character’s looks, tricks and style. Want to skate in your flip flops… go for it. Want to wear a bumble bee onesie …ok then… no judgement. In OlliOlli World as long as you’re on board anything goes!

_childDocuments_.review: This truly is a video game made with love.  I adore everything about this game from the art style, the characters, the music, the gameplay.  Every level has tons of reasons to replay each and every one.  Multiple paths, multiple lines on each path.  You can play to complete challenges, you can play to run up the score leaderboard and beat the rival it pairs you against each run, or you can just chill and enjoy the level and every play style is rewarding and satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't thank my friend enough for introducing me to this game. It's the kind of game you can enjoy with quick, fun 10-minute sessions, or you can get completely lost in it for hours.I absolutely love this game. It brings together everything I enjoy – awesome music, stunning landscapes, and meticulously designed skateboarding areas, characters, and world. There's also a cool side skateboarding element with increasingly challenging levels that are super satisfying to conquer. You might find yourself going back to certain levels over and over, either to beat them or to score more points and compete with friends.Officially, it's a relatively short game, taking about 5 hours to finish on a PC. But for me, it often takes longer because I'm not great at games that need precise timing. So, you might be wondering, "Is it worth getting?" I wholeheartedly say yes. It offers a fantastic and motivating gaming experience, even in 2D. You'll get totally immersed, with 50 levels to complete, over 100 tricks and grinds to master, and a whopping 200+ challenges. There are also fun modes like Spot Mode and Daily Grind.What I find most exciting about this game is how cleverly the levels are designed. The ability to skate on different surfaces adds a cool twist to the gameplay. I have to mention the unique levels where you race against a bear, both of you sliding on floating objects across the water to reach the finish line.Just a heads up, though, this game only works with controllers – keyboard support isn't available. Once you get the hang of the controls, they feel natural. Just be careful not to leave the game alone for too long; I found out the hard way that an accidental press of the "Y" button can restart a level instead of moving forward.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, high skill ceiling 2d tony hawk skateboarding game in a cool world with a fun story. Unfortunately, I just can't recommend the game because the developers have abandoned it despite highly reported and simple bugs. The game plays well, but once you complete an area, the additional challenges and unlocks cannot be completed. That is, the challenges can be done, but will not count toward completionist unlocks. So you get the satisfaction of completion, but not any rewards. And in the devs words, they "have no plans on releasing any new versions". Just check the steam discussion pages.TLDR; Great game, disappointing developer support that should not be encouraged with your purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, the game is fantastic. I recommend it to anyone that is interested, provided they can deal with the caveats I'm going to mention.The game has a great pastel artstyle that is always a pleasure to look at and focuses on readability in levels above all else, and does it well. It has a good soundtrack and radio that you can change at any time. the characters are charming, but the dialogue parts can get old pretty fast. luckily It's super easy to skip them and it has cheeky little dialogue buttons for the skips too, which are generally pretty funny,The gameplay is amazing, and the way they give you a full moveset at the very beginning while explaining it sporadically throughout the game to not overwhelm you is done very well. I 100% the first three worlds while playing because they were so much fun. There is an interesting thing that clips the games wings a bit though. so, there are 5 worlds that you progress through, and four out of five of them are absolutely amazing. but the fourth one, sketchside, is dreadful. up until this point the worlds have all had fun levels, neat challenges that occasionally gave me some trouble but not too much, and they've all had a theme/gimmick that they focus on. sketchside doesn't do this. sketchside hates you.The difficulty spike is absolutely crazy. the world isn't just hard though, It's kind of just overall bad. not really a fun time through any of it, aside from maybe two levels. the world right after it, the last one, is about the same level of difficulty but stays incredibly fun for most of the levels. sketchside is BAD. sketchside is so bad that from what I can tell from people online and stats from steam a lot of people completely give up on the game there, or do what I did and start just blasting through it without a care for challenges or score or anything. It completely ruins their time with the last world too it seems, cause it kind of sours the experience. The game is still absolutely amazing though. the main reason I talk so much about sketchside is because I want anyone that reads this to go in with the expectation that it sucks, because without prior knowledge it really hits you in the face.Really though, the game is worth a purchase for the first three worlds alone. if you get to sketchside and give up it was still plenty of content for the price and a wonderfully unique experience. the last world is really good though, so I recommend trying to get through it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for January 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before February 7th, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Skating the world in style. OlliOlli World takes a simple concept of skateboarding and creates a unique platformer around it.  This is the third game in the series.  The first two are solid games, but OlliOlli elevated the formula and shines with a style of its own.  Every level looks interesting and the player is left wondering what’s coming next.  The entire game is based around relatively simple controls as well, so players will be more focused on the level than trying to pull off each trick.The one issue with OlliOlli World is that it’s designed around tackling challenges.  If someone was to just beat each level at the bare minimum and move on, OlliOlli World only lasts around six hours.  But once players try to beat every challenge, OlliOlli World will require multiple playthroughs of even the simplest level.  Pick this up if you want a cross between skateboarding and platforming.  This isn’t Tony Hawk, but it’s also not-not Tony Hawk, if that makes sense.  Its focus is on skateboarding and style but mostly on getting through the level.  If you want more challenge though, try doing the entire level as a full combo. There are leaderboards to chase, as well as three unique tasks for every level.This also comes with the Expansion pass, so there are even more levels to check out here. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel: After beating the game, I can say that there's a ton of great levels in the game, beating each level won't be too hard with practice, however around the 60 percent mark, the challenges and required scores skyrockets to really challenge even expert players.  After finishing the game there's a special challenge on EVERY level that is brutal.  So the challenge is there.  Everything else stated in the review remains true.   It's an excellent game.

_childDocuments_.review: OlliOlli World is a great and hugely entertaining skating game and also a promising sequel to the previous installments of the olli olli world series.Gameplay: OlliOlli World is gamer friendly and also for most ages, although you have to deal with usual fails per level but that's part of the challenge.During your adventure, or the story in the game, you will meet several characters who will guide you through the game and teach you all the tricks, although it is important that you are open-minded and occasionally try something new yourself. experience, and this definitely leaves the characters in the game open to you.The world in the game is a top down view in which you go through all levels 1 by 1 according to a fixed route,this route can deviate here and there for more special levels, yes special levels are also present where certain objectives are required.In total, the world has 5 areas at your disposal and per area you can easily spend 1 to 2 hours or even more because I haven't reached the end of the game yet, I think an extensive review is already worthy of this game.Olli Olli Words is a user-friendly introduction to skating (games) and the possibilities of a 'Lord of the board'.Tricks, grinds, wallrides, you name it, it's all covered.Step by step you will learn all the moves and as you progress in the game you will have to use all these moves more and more complicated.The levels also have checkpoints so you don't have to start from scratch every time you fall.In addition to the tricks, each levels also have a number of objectives that you can achieve, for example you will be able to find a number of objects through the levels, stars or something else, which you have to touch or not, there is a variety of things that you can achieve per level.Depending on the objectives you achieve and the scores you achieve, you will also unlock many items with which you can completely customize your character.In addition to the campaign, there is also a sandbox mode where you can more or less let the game generate levels where you can go freestyle or practice.Graphically the game is somewhat cartoonish, the chosen style and some characters also remind me of the imaginative world of 'Adventure Time', skater games often give a rough impression, but in OlliOlli World this is not the case, which also makes it more unique and in this case it certainly succeeded.The game also has perfect support for ultra-wide resolutions, as there's a 2.5D world you have to navigate through, ultra-wide resolution is quite useful for _childDocuments_.review: As a longtime lover of Olli Olli 2 (and to a lesser extent, 1), I was initially a little concerned and intrigued when seeing the trailer for World for the first time. I think my cautious optimism served me right, because even though this game does a lot right, it also feels like it actively spits in the face of series die-hards like myself. To preface, if someone never had any experience with an OlliOlli game before, I would wholeheartedly recommend World. It's super packed with content, with every level feeling unique enough to earn it's place, and the amount of challenges to complete is rather insane. The addition of quarter-pipes and grabs makes a ton of sense and adds a lot of depth to level design, and additions like wall-rides help to really sell that sequel feeling. Another soundtrack of licensed songs is included, and while it definitely works, I don't think the energy is quite as great as with 2's soundtrack.Onto why I feel burned. While this game does add a fair deal of new trick mechanics, some feel kind of out of place. Late-tricks are kinda unnecessary when grabs are already a thing you can do after a trick, and almost feel included to justify the existence of some challenges, which unnecessarily requires the player to start using a button that's never been a thing in these games. With some new trick types being added, it's weird to see things like grind-tweaks added, as grind switching is already a thing and essentially serves the same purpose, and revert manuals have been removed, which sucks as they'd be perfect for landing onto quarter-pipe slopes. Plus another big gripe (even though it was an issue from 1 to 2) is how a lot of the special tricks don't match up with 2's inputs at all.The way I see the design approach is that they needed to move music skipping to the shoulders to allow the right stick for grabs and such, and since the shoulders are now taken up, trick modifiers can't be a thing anymore. But then you could ask, "well, why even have a skip music button altogether? Or why not just put it on something even more out of the way like the d-pad which isn't used at all in game???" The trick system in this game really feels a little 'one steps forward, two steps back' sorta deal, not to mention how terribly spammy one has to be to remain competitive on the leaderboardsI think this game's biggest sins is just having outright unreliable momentum mechanics, and a lot of challenges pertaining to keeping your momentum in check. Too many times a jump will feel perfect only for the player to completely miss the landing and need to restart the level. Some levels in the game are over 2 minutes in length for some of the riskier players, and having a full-combo run get trashed by one speed related mistake the player made earlier in their run can be frustrating as all hell. Also, while I appreciate a respect of players ability to take risks, requiring some jumps to be taken AFTER a grind rail ends feels so strange and poorly communicated. The timing can be finnicky and sometimes you'll think you earned a jump only to divebomb into a ravine. Weird that I have so many things to bash on this game but still feel like it's worthy of a positive score. It's just a lot of fun to play from any angle, just goes against what my beliefs are when it comes to how to progress the franchise. This game is a challenge and it's harder challenges to complete really feel like a crash-course in advanced problem solving. Do yourself a favor, and if you're up for it, go try and 100% this game with no guides. It's a full-ass video game and well worth the price of entry. Let's just hope Roll7 returns to OlliOlli with a little more refinement of the core gameplay. I feel like they could have a new classic on their hands!

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I don't go for the whole "extreme difficulty, chase high score" kind of gameplay, but there's just something about this game that compels me to keep beating my head against the wall until I at long last see all the objectives done on a level before moving on.The game's visual style carries a lot of my willingness to play ball, it's deceptively cute and lulls you into thinking you're going to be playing a chill sidescrolly skateboardy game.  What lies under the hood is a game about efficiency, ability to memorize maps, tricks, ability to maintain speed and combos. Now if you'd mention that to me about most other games I'd probably walk away, but there's just something about the entire package here that has me not only willing to conquer those obstacles, but enjoy doing so. And that comes as a big surprise to me!I'm definitely a "casual" these days. I work more days than I don't, and my days of getting enjoyment from roguelikes and "souls-like" games are over due to the time commitment required to beating them, so a game of this nature sucking up my free time is truly an oddity indeed haha.I definitely recommend this to fans of video games, especially arcady skate-em-ups, whether you're a filthy casual like me, or an MLG hardcore swagscoper. I feel like there's tons here on offer for anyone.EDIT:After a little more time with the game I do have to say, the "challenging but fun" portion of the game comes to a grinding halt when you hit mid Sketchside. The game then becomes a groundhog day emulator where you're replaying the same level for hours at a time, doing the same things but sometimes the jumps have enough air, sometimes they don't. I have noticed some jankness with the physics. The game from Sketchside on seems to just be trial and error.My overall opinion of the game has somewhat soured due to this, but I will leave the review positive because I wouldn't be beating my head against this insurmountable wall if I didn't feel like I wasn't getting some kind of sick thrill out of it. And some people are into this kinda gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I gave the original OlliOlli a 7 and the sequel a 6.5. The second one was too precision based and did not have as good of a soundtrack as the first one, but nevertheless, the skeleton was there in both games.Now OlliOlli World truly improves on the first two in pretty much every way. It has a nice presentation and you get to customise your character at will, with a lot of options and MANY more to unlock throughout your journey. Graphics are super pretty and the soundtrack is good as well. There were some catchy tunes but not many in my opinion. Plus, they get repetitive quickly as this can be a long game if you try to 100%d it. I think it would have been a nice addition if they remixed each track according to the world you're playing in; you know, to spice them up a bit more.Gameplay is fantastic. It's super deep and the more you play the more rewarding it gets as you perform million point combos. It's amazing how they pulled out so much with just a few buttons in your controller. And yes, sometimes you'll mix them up but most of them are pretty natural and tight.Levels? Also fantastic. There are A LOT of them, and they are all very different from each other. There wasn't a single level that I didn't like, except for maybe two or three which had some rather hard jumps, but overall, I loved them all. Each of them has different paths you can take and each path brings their own thing to the table. It was super satisfying and addicting to play through them all.But not everything is pink. The game design itself is where most of my complaints lay.The game is divided into five worlds, each with their own theme and around 15 levels each. These levels may also contain special stages that you can unlock and each level has various challenges: finish it, finish it without dying, three custom challenges, and three high scores to beat. And since I loved the game from the start I decided to do every single thing. Worlds 1 to 3 were very fair with the player, starting easy and then picking up the challenge linearly. In fact, I was able to do everything with somewhat ease. However things started to go bad in World 4. This world is the most challenging of them all, even more than the last one. The challenges are extremely difficult and some levels have these jumps and sections that are extremely hard to pull. Not to mention that you suddenly have to make millions of points in a single run and there's no way to achieve so easily. The game has a HUGE difficulty spike there and I wasn't able to complete even a single challenge in some of these levels. The frustration grew so much that I decided to drop my original challenge and just settle with "doing what I can". I kid you not one of the special stages in the last world must have taken 500 retries or maybe more to even finish for the first (and only) time. And yeah yeah, I know, git gud and all, but this wasn't the kind of challenge that I was expecting coming from the previous worlds. The game didn't prepare me for this and it's the game's fault. The cherry on top is that by the end of the game you unlock a tutorial that gives you a new hint on how to improve your combos. I think that tutorial is not well placed as it should have been explained many levels ago. I get that maybe this tutorial is inviting the player to replay some old levels, but by that time I've had enough. And if it wasn't for the fact that the game is actually very good, I think I would have dropped it altogether.That said, I should also add that I did not pay attention to a single line of dialogue, as I found those very annoying, so story-wise it didn't do it for me. I didn't care honestly, I just wanted my fix of adrenaline as quickly as possible.Content wise is also very well done as I think the game has a lot to offer for what you pay and there are some DLC that you can get for two extra worlds. To be quite honest, I was 100% sure I'd buy them before I reached World 4. But after being used as a punch bag so much by the later stages, I decided I've had enough and that I wasn't going to buy them. In fact, I wouldn't have minded if Worlds 4 and 5 were also appropriately hard and the DLC to be actually hardcore. But make the hardcore thing a DLC, not a base game thing.And finally, in terms of innovation, what can I say? This game is truly Tony Hawk in 2.5D and up to day with modern times. It was actually much more than I was expecting and I'm very happy with my purchase, not so much with my frustration in the end-game.8.5/10 - It has its problems, but it's very good.

_childDocuments_.review: Now given a fresh visual overhaul, OlliOlli World sees the beloved indie skating series return on Nintendo Switch, PC, PlayStation 4/5, and Xbox Series S|X. With a focus on huge weaving levels, quirky characters, and high scores waiting to be smashed, will this game be the beginning of a side-scrolling skater renaissance? Jump on board, strap on your kneepads, and let’s drop into this review.StoryThis is usually the part where I’d completely dismiss the story because it’s a skating game and they generally have little to no story at all, or the attempt at a story instead leaves you wishing there wasn’t one anyway. Surprisingly, that’s not what to expect at all with OlliOlli World! This heart-warming coming-of-age journey follows a group of close friends and at every single moment is simply oozing with charm. It feels strange to say such a thing about a sports game, but that’s genuinely the case.Radlandia is an entire continent dedicated to skate: its inhabitants, infrastructure, animals, and economy all revolve around boards affectionately referred to as the “Stuntwood“. Overseeing the smooth operation of this rad kingdom are five Skate Godz, revered holy beings who have achieved true Gnarvana through their mastery of the halfpipe. Legend has it that meeting all five Godz and passing their gnarly trials will grant a skater passage to Gnarvana, to skate alongside them as a mythical Skate Wizard. One rookie skater is on a quest to join them: you.But enough about the story! We all know skating games are about the…GameplayFlip tricks. Grinds. Wall rides. Manuals. Spins. Grabs. Firecrackers. If you know any or all of these terms, you’re going to be in for a good time. OlliOlli World takes simple side-scrolling gameplay and adds elements of complexity to challenge even the most skilled of players. While it truly is a game that’s simple for anyone to pick up and play, those chasing high scores are going to be pushed to their limits.The game is divided into five main worlds, each of which have approximately 15 – 20 individual levels. These levels can range from simple straightforward linear downward slopes with barely an obstacle, all the way through to complex intertwining, weaving structures littered with hazards. Every single level too has additional optional challenges and scores to beat, often requiring mastery of each trick type in order to succeed. It’s a clever way to encourage players to learn and become proficient at each type of trick, as knowing the bare minimum will still allow you to finish most levels.Conveniently placed ramps, wall rides and grinds are scattered throughout levels to help chain your combo.Starting simple, the first world slowly introduces the player to simple mechanics like tricks and grinds. Each world then adds additional elements to the mix, becoming increasingly complex and pushing the player to make the most of all their acquired skills. By the end of the game you’ll likely be chaining together tricks naturally, with 100x combos allowing your score to skyrocket. There’s nothing quite as satisfying as starting and finishing a level in a single combo and smashing all the NPC scores.Finally, one of the most impressive mechanics of OlliOlli World is track changing. While skating a level, certain areas will feature sections with arrows that prompt the player to change tracks. Tapping Y while skating on this part of the track will take the player down a completely different path, which are often far more challenging but greater reward for those wanting to max out their combos. These “GNARLY ROUTES” are some of the most punishing in the entire game, requiring absolutely perfect timing to master. Attempt at your own risk! Though for players just wanting a good time, these are thankfully completely optional.VisualsWhen creating OlliOlli World, Roll7 knew they needed to stray away from the previous games’ pixel art style in order to achieve more advanced gameplay. In doing so, the game’s creative director took inspiration from another sleek sport game by the name of Jet Set Radio, a game with distinct style that is almost universally praised. Combining outlandish 3D character and environment design with vivid visuals and a touch of the eccentric, OlliOlli World is a visual delight that makes each of its five worlds a blast to explore. I’d liken some of the design choices to Adventure Time, with its quirky characters, absurd world, and vibrant palette of colours.AudioNo skating game would be complete without a killer soundtrack to match, and OlliOlli World certainly doesn’t disappoint with its mix of catchy electronic beats. Created not by a single musician but by an entire setlist of artists, the soundtrack to Radlandia will no doubt help any skater get into the groove. Songs range from electronic music ranging from chill and mellow trip-hop, to fast-paced jazz inspired pieces, and catchy tunes with rhythmic pumping bass.While the soundtrack of OlliOlli World certainly is the highlight of its audio, there are bits and pieces of voice acting and silly sound effects that add to the game’s aural experience. Each level too is packed with simple audio cues to help the player improve their skating game: the clack of the skateboard upon landing perfectly, bonus crystals that shimmer upon approach, and hidden unlockables that can be heard in the distance or hiding on an alternate path.What else?The daily grind is back – a new track every day where all players compete for skating supremacy! This time it’s separated into “Leagues” where groups of 10 players of similar rankings compete against each other. Achieving a high position in the league will award you a point, allowing you to level up your rank and unlock new boards, clothing, or special customisations. It’s a simple mechanic that will keep you coming back for more (especially if somebody beats your score). Players can also compete in an endless mode, able to customise the track to their liking and then share this track using a unique code.To top it off, there are an enormous number of unlockables that can be used to customise your skater. These include staples like creative boards, wheels and trucks, all sorts of clothing and accessories, and even certain skate styles for your character pull off both during and after skating. Unlocking the most intriguing items, including gear of the Skate Godz themselves, requires some serious dedication, as these can only be obtained by fulfilling various challenge requirements on each level or finding and beating harder bonus levels.ConclusionOlliOlli World is everything you could ask for in a side-scrolling skater. Simple and intuitive controls, a tonne of unlockables, and varying difficulty choices based on each track to suit the play style of any player paired with its unique vibrant art style and chill lo-fi soundtrack, and you’ll find yourself in Gnarvana before you know it. Over the course of the adventure, there was rarely a single moment that I didn’t thoroughly enjoy. Where the earlier OlliOlli games re-introduced the concept of side-scrolling skating gameplay, OlliOlli World has polished it, perfected it, and created a game that is truly radical.So, why should you play it?- Linear skating gameplay is simple to pick up but difficult to master.- Old school side-scrolling games tickle your fancy.- Looking for an addictive game with emphasis on combos and high scores.- Gorgeous vibrant cartoon art style and chill lo-fi soundtrack.- Consider yourself a skating game fan? Don’t pass this up.But why shouldn’t you play it?- You prefer skating games that give you full control.- Play sports games for the realism? This one isn’t for you.- May leave you frustrated if you have poor reaction times.Read this review with pretty gifs and more reviews like this over at

spots, collecting outfits and board parts, and getting to know each region's own version of skate culture. the level design is amazing, it manages to be very readable at high speed, throws surprises and curveballs at you without breaking the flow, there are even secret paths that go in opposite directions or loop around... the later levels get pretty mind-boggling just trying to explore all the routes through. and if you know a level well enough to play on autopilot, you can look at the background world and notice a surprising amount of fun details.the skating/platforming mechanics themselves are masterfully designed too. you can organically choose to play casually (and still make a lot of progress) or go after the multiple layers of optional goals, or go even deeper and try to figure out all the micro-mechanics of momentum and hitting angles and maxing the combo counter etc...  the multiplayer league is nice for pushing your understanding of the mechanics post-main-game. seeing what other players can score and watching their replays regularly blows my mind and teaches me new quirks of how the mechanics can be used.the visual style is so fun and nice to look at too, gorgeous colors and environment design that (almost) never interferes with readability. the soundtrack fits great, ranging from jazzy hip-hop to electro house, there's usually a nice pulse going on and it feels good how you unlock new songs as you progress through the biomes.also BTW. character creator and outfits are completely un-gendered, you simply have access to any and all dress-up options you can unlock. and in-game characters avoid gendered terms when talking to/about you. for me personally this is a kinda huge positive detail that makes the game fundamentally more welcoming and affirming, and makes me want to recommend it to other queer & trans players especially.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game from Humble Bundle, and that was a total steal. Even at full price I'd say this game is totally worth it, but if it's on sale there's really no reason to pass it up.Unlike a lot of 3D skateboarding games like THPS, in OlliOlli world you automatically rush forward along a linear level with only a few predefined paths. In almost every level, your goal is to make it from point A to point B, with optional challenges and scores to beat. For the most part, this game is pretty casual - the way you pull off tricks is very simple, and there aren't many controls/buttons to remember, there are usually numerous checkpoints in each level, generally the levels themselves aren't too bad (even though some challenges are very mean), etc. The difficulty ramps up quite a bit, especially once you get to the 4th zone, but it still feels fair and paced well. While you have access to pretty much all of your tricks and abilities from the start, the game slowly introduces you to them over the course of playing, and usually gives you plenty of time to get familiar with them before introducing the next thing.I really just love everything about this game, the gameplay itself is incredible, but also the art-style and choice of music is top notch. It's subjective, but I really can't imagine a more fitting aesthetic for this game. It ties together the whole experience, from all the weird stuff going on in the background to the character design and customization options. The controls are simple but still allow for long, tricky, and very fun combos, and it's a super easy game to pick up and start playing. Even if you're not a fan of skateboarding games, I think there's still a good chance there could be something here for you; I was so surprised by how much I liked this game upon my first time playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fun skateboarding game with cool art style and balanced difficulty. For once i agree with IGN score.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wasn't feeling this game. Tricks are done in this game by rotating the control stick in various directions and then letting go, however the game moves at such a rapid pace that it doesn't feel like you can adequately plan or control what tricks you are doing: rather, you find yourself just swing the control stick around like a madman hoping whatever random crap pops out. My thumb is killing me after only an hour of play. The levels seem designed almost intentionally to make you fail, and falling (because you jumped 1/10th of a second early and hit a wall that soon appears from offscreen) resets a bunch of progress. Like the tricking, you're moving so fast that when obstacles pop up on the screen you often don't really have a chance to properly react to them, most of the time you clear a course it's through sheer dumb luck. The game felt very repetitive very quickly, even after just the first set of levels I was already completely bored, and after taking a look through videos, it doesn't look like anything was changing any time soon. The game feels like a 2D riff on classic Tony Hawk, with doing combos linked by manuals and trying for variety, but in Tony Hawk I felt in control, and I never felt in control here. Despite hundreds of hours in TH, I'd much more quickly jump back into that than this. There is some cool character customization (with a ton of options unlocked from the start), and the graphics are quite nice. There is a *lot* of dialog that I was skipping through: I like the them of "gnarlvanna" or whatever but it's not to me a theme that warrants 20 lines of dialog between every 30 second stage. Lastly, the company that develops this game is owned by Take Two--which they go through great efforts to obscure and hide--an awful company and a destructive force in the gaming industry, one which makes a practice of suing small indie developers out of existence for the most petty of reasons. I do my best to avoid their products, but I was tricked into this one. I wasn't too crazy about "signing" 30 pages worth of legal documents to even open the game.

_childDocuments_.review: OliOli World is not the type of game I typically play, but thanks to a bundle and me really liking the art style, I decided to give it a try. I’m really glad I did.OliOli World is very much an easy to learn, hard to master, type of game. In my 8 hours of playtime, I’ve beaten every main level, probably about half the side quests, and done probably less than 25% of the challenges. Each level has 3 challenges, in addition to 3 scores you are supposed to try to beat. Completing either of these sets unlocks a cosmetic, and that is something I really like about this game. It’s filled with cosmetics, but you don’t get them with your credit card. You get some just by playing and others by being good at the game.The game has frequent checkpoints you can use and many levels, especially the later ones, have multiple paths you can take. This means that most people should be able to beat the game, but if you want to compete in the leaderboards and do every level in a single combo, you’ll probably need to spend a lot of time practising. Like many games, you get a combo multiplier, so chaining tricks together is how you get high scores. When you hit a checkpoint, any points you have fully gotten get saved, but anything related to the active combo is not. This means that trying to do a level in a single combo can get you a high score, but reloading a checkpoint resets your score to 0, since all of your points are related to your active combo.The game does have a few bugs. The biggest being related to timing. You can usually push buttons very early, but if you want to be the best, you need to time things right. This means pressing buttons very close to your landing time. Sometimes, I press it a bit late and my character starts their dying animation, then teleports as if I pressed the button on time. Other times I press it in what I feel is a good time, but I die anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to the ultimate Fingerboard Experience. This is exactly how I feel playing Olli Olli World. It reminds me of the good old times sitting at my school desk and trying to make a kickflip over my pens or grinding my school books.Check out my full video review:If you start up the game for the first time you will be positively surprised by the great character editor. Choose between all kind of items, character attributes, clothes, funny hairstyles, glasses, decks and many more.And of course, you will see the direct difference to the previous Olli Olli games looking at the fresh design. The game is set in Radlandia, a surreal warm coloured world populated with hipster characters. Eye-popping colours, with giant donuts fill up the background for example. It’s a good feeling overall and just comfy to look at.Then to the gameplay. For the first tracks the game gets you into tutorial sessions. Those are mixed with funny narratives around each level and allow to learn the different tricks and game mechanics, without being too difficult or too easy. I crashed more than one time, but OlliOlli World gives you this feeling of “Just one more time, please one more time” – until you crash again and so on. Love it. Hate it. Love it.Let’s get to the very essence of the game: the controls, the combos, the grinds, the tricks. They need indeed skills and training, but feel then even more rewarding. And those combos are fun and rewarding indeed. In case you want to level up your learning curve, you can also check out the controls for each of those tricks or just improvise and see what’s happening. I am an impro guy. I just run the maps and enjoy doing random tricks. OlliOlli World gives you this freedom mostly and this is good.With all these details aside. I will give you my honest opinion. Is it fun? Yes, it is and I see myself spending a lot more time in the game, to learn more tricks, to enjoy the fast grinds, simply the skating and the fingerboard feeling. I am also looking forward to play this game on my Steam Deck. Sitting comfy on my sofa since it is the perfect game for some rounds in between, without getting for hours into some difficult to understand story. OlliOlli World is for me definitely a recommendation, especially if you like skateboarding, fast platformers and you enjoy beat em up combo style controls.Also, the overall reception of the game by professional critics is very good. Metacritic score of 87 for steam.Good game. Worth it. Not only for fans, also very interesting for newcomers to the series.

_childDocuments_.review: After only playing the game for 4 hours, OlliOlli World has been a delightful journey thus far. You enter the game with a very pleasant soundtrack that gets you grooving in your seat. You then proceed to an almost endless character customization journey that evicts the inner designer in you. When you are happy with how you designed your character you finally get to skate! The tricks in the game are all accurate and it's incredibly fun piecing together combos that run up the point totals. Some tasks may seem a little hard but with enough skating under your belt you'll eventually complete those grueling tasks. I would 100% recommend this game even if you don't skate or have never played a skating game, it releases creativity within yourself and you receive a bundle of satisfaction for achieving a high point totals, especially when it happens on the first run.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm having a lot of fun with the game. It's got easy to learn but hard to master controls, a fantastic sense of flow in the level design, really good customization rewards for playing and beating challenges, and an awesome chill hop lofi future funk soundtrack to vibe to. The only real negative is the usually campy character dialogue and the fluff in between levels, such as making the natural option to chat with NPCs when replaying a map. Like, how about don't make the annoying dialogue button the continue button? Why can't dialogue be X instead of A, I don't want to consciously hit B before each level I've already played, it stifles the flow of the game, which is ironic because the actual gameplay is pure flow fun.For example, when I replay a level to get all the challenges, every time I finish a run, successful in the challenge or not, the characters say the same annoying ending dialogue that only made some sense the first time through. Why don't the characters actually react to the run, like say "Clean dude!" for a star run or Mike saying "Gnarly." when you beat his challenges? All we need is a rough tracking of player activities and a short one liner or two from the crew once we're not going in blind. Seeing the same dialogue every finish is really bothersome and it takes away from the immersion and enjoyment of completing a run. A real skate crew would react to the line, have words of encouragement or advice, not be a dumb NPC that says one thing when prompted by the end of the level. Seriously, just add a slew of lines for each instance and have it replace the end dialogue if you skip the opening dialogue, for a game about replay value it sure doesn't seem like the dialogue was considered in the gameplay loop, it's always in the way.If they actually change it for the better, it could represent exactly what the devs set out to make; a super simple yet elegant 2D skateboarding game with an awesome aesthetic. Right now it's all of those cool things but with the addition of some annoying speedbumps between levels, which are easily remedied.Overall, it's super fun and I recommend it for anyone who likes these types of games, but it's not perfect because if it was I wouldn't be listening to annoying dialogue I don't need to hear when I don't intend to.Solid 8.5/10 can be a 9.5/10 if they bite the bullet and make QoL changes for the better. If they never address or smooth out those annoyances, I'd be really pissed because the changes are super simple and will go a long way in preserving the fun between runs. Fun times, make it even better devs, please.

_childDocuments_.review: OlliOlli World is the third chapter of the famous side-scrolling skating series created by Roll7. Whereas the previous games were tremendously punishing and hard to get into, this sequel (or maybe a reboot?) takes a huge step forward by switching to 2.5D and smoothing out the gameplay. It doesn’t matter if you are a skating enthusiast or a newbie, OlliOlli World provides an “easy to learn, hard to master” experience that can be appreciated by both. As stated in the title, the biggest change is the introduction of a full-fledged world that sets the narrative and gives players plenty of reasons to enjoy skating.Welcome to Radlandia, a place where eccentric skaters aspire to become the next Wizard by impressing the Skating Godz of Gnarvana. As the new kid in town, you are welcomed by a funny group of skaters who will guide you through the journey, introducing the tutorial and exchanging a few jokes before and after each level. The world is divided into five regions, each one with their distinct biomes and fashion style. Before starting, you need to design your own character appearance: from skin tones to hair colour, from clothes to skateboards, there is an impressive number of customization options, and you will get many more as you progress throughout the game.The story is sufficient to give players enough reasons to keep skating, but where OlliOlli World really shines is in the multi-layered level design and progression system. As a side-scroller, you are skating down a line doing all sort of tricks (kickflips, grinds, wallrides, manuals etc.) and aiming to complete the stage with the highest score possible. To reach the end you can follow the main path or you can pick one of the many alternative routes; some of them will allow you to make more incredible tricks (and thus points), while others will give you the chance to complete secondary tasks. All stages include extra content, such as optional challenges and hidden NPCs that unlock new side-quests and reward you with awesome stuff you can use to customize yourself. This greatly enhances the replayability while also making levels fun to explore (like in a platform game). Some of these can even turn into a “runner” type of game mode where you need to reach the finish line first. Every stage has its own leaderboard, so you can easily check your position among other skaters, including your friends. The game will even mark the player above you as your rival, so the next time you play the same level you can try to beat their score. Following the tracks of OlliOlli and OlliOlli 2: Welcome to Olliwood, the gameplay has been vastly improved by offering an easy learning curve. Now you can combine epic tricks and moves with the simple use of analog sticks. It still requires good timing and precision, but the game has become more permissive and it’s really hard to fall off the skate. The difficulty increases on each new location, with the last area being an insane rollercoaster of trials and errors. Fortunately, the game comes with a handy checkpoint system, so everyone should be able to complete the story, even if it gets more challenging as you move forward.It’s worth mentioning that the game does not support mouse and keyboard at the moment, but I think that for this kind of game a controller is always the best option. Still, having a choice to select your preferred device would be great.The main story and most of the side content can be easily completed in under ten hours, but the multiplayer features can offer plenty more. Once you unlock Gnarvana, you can access two different online modes: League, which is a daily online tournament that will only reward the first three ranked skaters, and Portal which allows you to create your own level by adjusting three modifiers (difficulty, length and biome) and share it to other players via postcodes. This is obviously a great addition, and it’s really nice seeing yours and other players replay to understand where you failed. What I think it’s missing here is a more traditional multiplayer mode; a common skate-park hub where players can skate freely, share their postcodes and show their unique styles. The amount of customization options is huge, but useless if we are the only ones who are able to see them, and except for the replay and loading screens, there aren’t many moments where we can see other players’ appearances. In any case, the single player alone is absolutely worth the price, and these multiplayer features are just a bonus for those who want to keep skating in this magical world after completing the story.Artistically speaking, the game is very reminiscent of  funky art style and shows developers’ love for the skating culture. Radlandia looks incredibly charming, with all its biodiversity filled with 90s nostalgia, psychedelic trips and cartoonish characters. It’s a feast for the eyes and it gets even better with the incredible soundtrack that further enhances the skating flow. There is a wide selection of licensed tracks, ranging from lo-fi/ambient music to electronic, and you can easily change them on the go.OlliOlli World is a fabulous skating journey with a perfectly balanced progression, rewarding gameplay and fun storytelling. Radlandia is a wonderful skating paradise that can easily attract both newcomers and seasoned veterans. After 7 long years, Roll7 have finally reached Gnarvana, delivering one of the best skating experiences ever made.
