_childDocuments_.review: Sports games? Pah! Score attack stuff? Hmm. OlliOlli World really has disabused me of any notion that I can judge anything so readily off of its genre.  Top to bottom, from its pastel visuals, leave-the-game-on-in-the-background-good soundtrack, and pitch-perfect accessible but hard to master gameplay, this thing is annoyingly hard to critique in any way other than gushing appreciation. Does that make for an interesting review? We'll have to just reckon with the reality. This thing is too good for me to write a fun takedown or balanced take. So let's keep it short and sweet. Like the game itself (if you really shot through it). Leave my words for a trice and take a quick gander at OlliOlli 1 and 2. Back? Yeah, they were fine. OlliOlli 2 is quite aesthetically pleasing, but it's a largely faceless affair. The environments were the characters, essentially. OlliOlli World retains the interesting environments whilst making them doubly appealing for the 2.5D expansion, but also adds character customisation and a 3D colourful cast of characters whose pastel colours, design and colours all appeal in the extreme. If you'd rather skip their pre/post level dialogue, that's an option, but I never found the cast grating. Backgrounds benefit from the new dimension with busy, populated and quirky settings full of bizarre seagullmen, wildlife, and crowds of all kinds doing their thing. The customisation presentation is so charming and even includes animations for tricks, that it's more or less the only customisation page I've ever cared about in a game.  At a minimum you get to the end of the level. If more ambitious, you finish without triggering a checkpoint or hit a high score by keeping your combo intact and performing more risky and varied stunts. But where they really demand multiple plays and explorations is in the Tony Hawk reminiscent 'Mike's Challenges.' These require taking different paths, avoiding or hitting various things, performing certain feats, etc. They're creative, but they also add this explorative aspect to levels.  The beautiful simple single stick-based approach to jumping and grinding gives way to the complexities of spinning, tweaking, landing, etc. The moment I thought I had a handle on the game's demands, it added a new stick, trigger or button.  The leagues in particular are just the perfect cap to the experience. Putting everything you've learnt to the test to get your score into a qualifying place on the leaderboard is so satisfying. Having these smaller, local leaderboards for ten or so people rather than the typical global leaderboards makes these single-day competitions all the more possible for players of average ability like me. Revisiting daily to get promoted to the gold leagues and beyond is the perfect excuse to keep coming back. The kind of constant on the spot, risky tweaking of your jumps you have to do to drive your combo up to get to a league-worthy score makes me wish there wasn't a more headache proof and thumb-friendly means of doing so. Maybe it's just the kind of player I am, but after trying to compete in the gold league all I want to do is have a more laid back exploration of the levels without constant optimisation of every moment and stretch of a stage. High scores are killer, then, but I suppose what's the alternative? A grind is a grind.

_childDocuments_.review: Olli Olli World is a vast improvement over the two previous games in the series. Despite its arcade style, there’s a story this time, though the world-building conversations are completely optional. Along with the newly added customization, including hairstyles and clothing, there’s also board styles, the ability to swap out different grab tricks, and even animations for beginning or ending a run. The electronic soundtrack fits the game well, with elements of house, breakbeat, and downtempo. 2D side-scrolling gameplay now features illustrative 3D art, while the camera often pans out to show off the vibrant characters and detailed worlds traversing 5 unique areas each with their own theme, for example: forest, desert, and industrial.You’ll learn a specific ability in each area, or you can learn most immediately by looking through the Tricktionary; rewarding returning players by allowing advanced tricks and abilities like manuals to be used before the game technically teaches them to you. Then go back to earlier levels with the skills you’ve learned (like wallride, firecrackers, & late tricks) to find alternate routes, some obvious and others secret. A few levels completely change to accommodate newly learned techniques and increase replayability. Other optional side missions are unlockable, which challenge you to get better at specific aspects of the game like maintaining height and speed.There’s around 12-13 levels per area where you must complete a run by traversing to the end without slamming, while consistently performing tricks to maintain a combo. Objectives in each level reward customization options, but are less specific than in previous games, and you often don’t need to complete the level to finish the challenge. Flick the left stick for tricks à la EA’s Skate, but here the sticks are swapped. Flip tricks are color coded based on difficulty, making it easier to practice specific advanced tricks by performing half or three quarter circles. Tricks have been simplified. For example, the double heelflip is performed only with the stick, whereas in OlliOlli2, you had to press a bumper button and rotate the stick simultaneously. Gameplay is a little less punishing now, but still requires fast twitch reflexes. Instead of slamming when you don’t land perfectly, you’ll simply lose points and speed while dropping your combo. Even though chaining a long combo throughout levels is encouraged, checkpoints have also been included which means you can continue completing level-specific challenges even if you slam without having to restart the entire level over again. Though the game is more forgiving, it’s still a very challenging but enjoyable sequel, and is the best in the OlliOlli series.

Hopefully that gets better with patches but it doesn't really detract from the game which does run well where it matters the most.===Having completed the game I think it's worth saying that the game does get quite challenging. _childDocuments_.review: OlliOlli World is a very specific game, an intense 2D skateboard platformer. I feel like the target audience is the people that got really into the Tony Hawk Proskater franchise but doesn't have that much time for games anymore, each stage is only a few minutes long if you can get through it without falling down.Let me start off by saying this game gets HARD. It starts of easy enough by just using flip tricks (which also functions as jump) and grinds. The further you get in the game the more mechanics gets introduced like wallrides, grab tricks, manuals and landnings. You will eventually need all of these just to make it through a stage. The cool thing about this game is that you are ALWAYS able to do all of these things whenever, just that the game doesn't tell you until it's neccessary to use it in order to beat a stage. It's a brilliant design where the stages gets progressively more complex but earlier stages will be more fun to return to the more mastery you achieve over the game.Controller only?I was puzzled by the complete lack of keyboard controls, but once you start playing you'll get exactly why. The left joystick of a controller is used to jump/flip tricks and grind. Depending on the direction you flick it and if you turn and rotate it before releasing you'll make different tricks, making the simple 4 basic tricks suddenly go up to 20+ just from a single joystick. It's a core part of the game and you'll need to use the other functions at the same time, sometimes requiring you to do 3 things at once which just isn't feasible on a keyboard. The controls are very tight, responsive and handle perfectly, never once did I feel like I failed something because of the game, only because I was too slow or didn't pull something off well enough. Gameplay:Every stage have several objectives to work towards. The primary one is just to beat the stage, with a bonus if you never fall down. On top of there's 3 unique challenges catered to every stage, as well as 3 levels of high scores to beat. In the beginning I was having fun trying to get everything in the level, but closing in to the end of the game I'd be happy JUST to make it to the end of the stage. The last half of the game ramps up difficulty considerably, requiring very precise jumps and movement in order to proceed. Since it's a skateboarding game you always want to keep your momentum in order to make the next jump, but keeping a combo going can make you lose speed unless you do it perfectly. At the end of the game, the only way to fully beat all high scores in a stage is to do the full thing perfectly in an ENTIRE combo. Story:The story is very silly and family friendly while making fun of the RAD skateboarding culture of the 90s. It got some laughs out of me and have fun characters in it that you can't take seriously, like the old father of skateboarding simply called Dad, or the skateboarding wizard who gained psychic powers by impressing the gods and reaching Gnarvana. You create your own character who's goal it is to succeed the skateboard wizard by impressing the gods with your rad skills. There's plenty of customizing options to choose from and you unlock a lot more from completing objectives in stages. The fun thing is that other player's character will show up in your loading screen! The story really isn't special but it isn't trying to be, the developers clearly just had a lot of fun with it. A very appreciated function is the ability to completely skip all dialogue if you so wish and go straight to the skateboarding. Even when entering a stage you get an option to skip flavor dialogue and go straight to the stage, or listen to some fun dialogue. The difference between this and completely skipping everything is that some stages have tutorials or introduces new hazards which the characters will ask you if you know about, very handy. Graphics:The visual style is very simple and cute, with vibrant colors that make up a world very pleasant to look at. It really helps that all stage objects are mapped to a certain color, so the floor, rideable walls and grind rails all have their own color to make them pop and impossible to miss. The graphic style is timeless in my opinion. OlliOlli World is a fantastic, short game (3-4 hours) that you can pour LOADS of hours into to achieve full mastery. The controls take some getting used to but are a lot of fun and get super satisfying once you get the hang of it. If you are a more casual player you will need a lot of patience in order to beat the game, but that doesn't mean there's loads of fun without getting to the end as well. If you believe that the pricing of a game should reflect the quality of a game and not just how long it is from start to finish then you should DEFINITELY pick up this game.

_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: OlliOlli World is a World Wonder! It's a departure from the original OlliOlli but it is absolutely magic. Lovely soundtrack, incredible visual style and flair! _childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this on a whim and it has quickly become one of my favourite games. _childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: OlliOlli World is probably my Game of the Year. I haven't gotten this into a game (unlocking every item I can, completing every challenge, etc.) in a long time.The core gameplay loop of flip-tricking into a spinning grab, grinding into a wallride into a manual never seems to get old. _childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to put into words how much I love this game. The gameplay, artwork, characters, and music are all super stellar. Olli Olli World offers players a variety of experiences as you skate through each biome and every level. You can just sit back relax and skate through each level, or you can sit up and focus on grinding out each and every challenge and go for a high score. Olli Olli World offer so much character customization and a deep plethora of tricks to try to master. The replayability for this game is incredibly high and I can see myself playing this game for years to come. Although there isn't a specific multiplayer component there is a robust leaderboard that allows you to view the replays of top scores levels and the replays of your friends who also play the game. If you play with a friend at the same time this allows you to compete for high scores and watch each other's replays.Don't let this amazing game fly under the radar anymore. _childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: I feel bad not reviewing this earlier; OlliOlli World, Rollerdrome & OlliOlli 2 stand out in their niches, all are refined and tightly made, and clearly give hours of fun, even if my playtime here betrays that (I have a LOT more time learning & playing on the PlayStation port)This game is colourful, diverse and most importantly; fun to play. _childDocuments_.review: OlliOlli World is essentially a 2D obstacle course with a nice aesthetic around skateboards. Aside from being on a skateboard, this is nothing like the Tony Hawk games. I don't really get the comparisons considering how vastly different the game play and game design is. It's like comparing Mario Kart to F1 racing. Sure, they're both racing games, but there really aren't any other similarities. OlliOlli World is about completing a 2D track where you go right while avoiding obstacles. Sometimes you go left when transitioning on quarter pipes. The game feels very fast which is fun and enjoyable in its own way but you end up crashing a lot because of how fast you have to go, not giving you much time to react. It doesn't make the game feel like a skateboard game, it feels more like a memory game or just getting lucky if you can react perfectly. You'll often find yourself getting to a jump where you have to experiment a few times to be very precise to see where you have to speed up or let go of your jump for example. The game is specifically designed to make you fail and to replay the game just experimenting timing on jumps and nothing else.Furthermore, the controls are just really boring. The game forces you to play with a gamepad, not that I'd really expect to play this on a keyboard. But all of the controls are based on A to speed up and your left thumb stick for every single move. That's all the controls you need to know... All jumps are pressing the thumb stick in a random direction. It doesn't matter which direction, they all perform a different trick but none of them require more air than the next so you can just press it in a random direction. The only exception is grinding, you have to hold down during your whole grind. I think the game would be a lot more enjoyable if there were actual controls for each trick like in Tony Hawk Pro Skater games. I completed the first world and looking at the achievement list, I can tell many other people also aren't interested in the game. The most common achievement as of the time of this review, which you will unlock on the first stage, has a 94.6% unlock rate. So 94.6% of players have pretty much played the game in some capacity. The first world, which will take you less than an hour, only has a 31.4% completion rate. So basically only 1/3 of players have held their interest long enough in this game to play for at least an hour. Not a good sign for a game that csots $30USD at full price... If the game was truly that enjoyable, most people would continue playing it for at least an hour... Unfortunately, that's about as much as I could go in this one.Oh, and one last thing, I've never seen so many terms & conditions I've had to agree to while playing any game, let alone an indie game. Of course I'm not going to go through reading all of that, who does? But seeing how damn long it is, I'm starting to wonder if I agreed to installing some kind of spyware or something on my computer. Just ignore this one, aside from the aesthetic, which you can appreciate from videos, there's really no redeeming qualities about this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't fun...At least, not for me. It's just a precision platformer with paint.First, the controls are not great. There's only one button used to platform: A. But not to jump. To push with your foot.The Left Stick controls the jump. And the trick.The triggers create rotation.Then you have to press A at the right time along with the left stick direction to do a trick.And it's context sensitive.So you're mashing one button while shoving around one joystick, and hoping the game picks it up in the right spot and that you didn't forget to only use the stick instead of that *and* the button, or was this the one that did need both?Maybe it would make more sense if ... the game explained how any of those things worked. However, it only explains that you push with your foot and trick with the left stick. You need to manual before it teaches you how in order to do all the challenges. I'm not looking to falsely extend my playtime by coming back later... I should already know how it works by the fifteenth level, and I only did because I took time to figure it out.Next, the actual gameplay.I like Skateboarding games for two reasons:1. It feels cool to pull off a neat trick2. It's fun to skate around nice looking levels, especially if you can catch major speed or air.This is a side-view, so it feels very disconnected from your experience. There's no feeling of catching great air. The speed is pretty hard to control, since it's often too slow (thanks to the pushing necessary) or if it goes fast you can't always react fast enough to grab all the challenges in one pass (unless you've memorized the course or have incredible reflexes and eyesight, which is not fun for me in either scenario).It doesn't even look all that cool when you're done. It has a replay feature, but I might as well be watching any other platformer. The tricks that you start with are super boring, and it remains to be seen if it's worth the time or effort to bother with the tedium of unlocking the others.Finally, it insists on a controller. Controllers hurt my wrist sometimes. I need an option to change up what my tendons are doing. Dislike.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an excellent art design and is a lot of fun. However, its short length and uninteresting story make me definitely recommend to wait for a sale.To start, this game's art design is a major positive here. I really enjoyed the Adventure time inspired environments and character designs. It is extremely colorful, and there's a good chunk of customization for your character and board. Just from looking at the previous two games, they really turned up the dial in terms of the art design and environments. Speaking of the environments, the level design in this game ranks near the top in terms of platformers I've played this year. Almost every single level felt memorable, unique, and most importantly, fun. To top it all off, the skating in this game is the ultimate highlight (as it should) and feels really good to control. The tricks and combos are extremely enjoyable to pull off, and as the difficulty ramps up, it makes you get a little creative and the only wrong answers are when you fall or wipe out.Now, when getting into the negatives, we have to talk about the game's story and characters. To be brief, they're both terrible. I mostly skipped through the story a little over halfway through (which is something i rarely do) just to get into the levels, and the characters were just uninteresting as well as annoying. I don't need every game to have an intense, mesmerizing story like the Last of Us to enjoy it. But I definitely needed better than what I got here. Next, the game can only be played on controller (sorry mouse and keyboard diehards, you should just pass on this one). Not really a big deal for me, but I know it is for some people so I wanted to mention it.Lastly, this game's length is short. Granted, there's a bunch of optional content here, but none of it is all that interesting other than the Gnarvana challenges (yes I spelled that correctly). For $30, there should have been more than less than 4 hours of main story content.Get it when it goes on sale for $10-15. 3/5

_childDocuments_.review: This is a soft "no."If you are super casual and game for the sake of burning away the candle of your life AND love skating, this game is for you.Visually it has a superb cartoony aesthetic. It is good enough that you can ignore the usual "indie" mumble dialogue noises over speech bubbles.But ultimately this is a super simplified skate version of Trials (as in the Ubisoft trials motorcycle stunting game). If anything you could go further and say it is a dumbed down Trials with even more dumbed down Super Meat Boy platformer-punishment design elements.The one and ultimate problem with the game is that the levels require full knowledge of the obstacles ahead of time... so you are basically failing multiple times in advance to "learn" a level first before you can time your jumps and make sure your speed is about right for the obstacles that are about to come on screen.. because if you aren't ready by the time they appear = FAILURE to react. That is the part that is Super Meat Boy-ish... it just felt infinitely less satisfying for me to make the effort to learn those jump/speed points.The fact that you get this in the initial tutorial missions is both annoying for those of us that want hand-eye coordination challenges, but also good that you get a heads up right out the gate of what the game is about.The visuals feel like the most talented person(s) in the dev team were the artists/animators.Gameplay itself does not feel unpolished or lacking in terms of input.... but it is very simplistic, and performing tricks can feel a little like a button/thumb-stick mash.My miniscule play time is enough to know that it isn't for me, but unlike the mountain of absolute garbage I have accumulated through a now cancelled Humble Choice subscription, this is a game that is clearly put together well, and will have quality value for the low end/casual gamer.So.. if the above details actually mechanics/elements sound like what you would be into, you can consider this a recommendation to you as a gamer... but if you like "hard" games that make your failure a source of supreme anger AND motivation to succeed and dominate... keep looking.

_childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others OlliOlli World is the third title in the trilogy, albeit without a continuity line in terms of story, and this may well be one of the weirdest Skateboard titles I've played to date - but in a good way. Mixing platforming with a giant repertoire of maneuvers with the possibility to perform giant combos, just like Tony Hawk, makes all fans of the modality and titles of the genre super excited.Ollie Ollie World is set in the world of Radlandia. A skateable continent, which has five distinct and magical areas formed by five skate gods. Chiffon, the skate wizard, who is the character that links the realms of the divine and the mortal, is about to hang up the wheels of his skateboard and it's looking for a replacement tailored to her mythical tasks. The player thus has on his skateboard the possibility of replacing Chiffon and being the new Skate Wizard.This is not just an interesting title for its gameplay. His entire narrative is presented in a goofy yet very involving way where it's possible in all the characters to perceive their personality traits. All this translates into a very fresh experience in every way. The player has the unconditional support of a group of friends, who, although they have only known each other since the beginning of his adventure, help him with their lessons learned from his experience in this magical world.Regarding the gameplay and like its predecessors, it unfolds through a sidescroller screen. Each level is presented in a different way, containing ramps, walls, rails, platforms, giving the player the possibility of maneuvering at their pleased. As expected, the tricks start with a low level of difficulty and as you progress in the adventure they start to get more complicated, but consequently, a higher score is assigned for their difficulty. Even so, the important thing to get more points are the combos that are possible to perform and that's why I mentioned Tony Hawk. Those long lines of text with all the maneuvers that were performed pull the most hardcore side of each one. The problem is if you fall, all the accumulated points are lost. The game has a system of checkpoints during the level, which can help to have a smoother run. In this sense it is possible to adjust the type of approach of each level and compete with friends or even worldwide, to obtain the highest score. Who doesn't like a little competition?There is no feeling of boredom by the repetition of situations. The level design of each world makes things very fresh, with each new stage presenting a different mechanic, such as the possibility to grind or wallride, or the simple fact of presenting secondary paths called "gnarly path", where it increases the difficulty and the hazards. These mechanics are introduced in a gradual rhythm to facilitate the understanding of their complexities, making the whole experience super immersive and fun, where the simple sensation of speed that you can take from riding down a slope or by grinding on a rail is very well implemented.The main objective of each level is to reach the end. However, it is possible to complete a handful of highly diversified and level-specific secondary goals, thus adding a new layer and hours of gameplay.After the end of the campaign, there is a very interesting post content adding to all the replayability that you may have to repeat the levels in order to complete all the side quests of each level. There is a mode that randomly generates content where the player can choose the biome, difficulty, and duration of the stage in order to get the best score. A "key" will be associated within the level, allowing the player to return to the previously generated level or even share it with the community.In addition to all these experiences, there is the online mode where players compete head to head to climb the rankings and consequent league.It is indeed possible to get a lot of enjoyment out of the story alone, but the enjoyment that is taken from understanding each maneuver or combo mixed with the learning curve that it's hard but super interesting to go through is to be praised.In OlliOlli World there is something for everyone, whether you are a hardcore gamer or just want to enjoy the story and reach Gnarvana.

Halfway through the game, I was wiping out on obstacles in ways I didn't really understand. The trick linking system seems simple but I just couldn't get much use out of it. By the third biome, I was skipping the "story" and just rushing to get to the end until I realize I wasn't having fun. And honestly, once you complete the first world, you've seen everything the game has to offer. It just gets more stressful from there. This really needs a Celeste-style assist mode to help people who can't keep up with the twitchy gameplay otherwise, we just bounce off of it. If you're looking for a chill time, this just wasn't it for me. It has a ton of great ideas and neat touches, but I'm just not fast enough to keep up.

_childDocuments_.review: OlliOlli World plays like a handheld console game from the late 1990’s and is game controller ONLY. The game makes no effort to accommodate PC users who use mouse and keyboard. The menus are difficult to navigate because of this. The game begins requiring you to scroll through multiple pages of terms and agreements for your PC's telemetry data. If you don't agree to their terms 3 times you won't be able to play. After that there's a long and unavoidable cut scene that leads to the customise character  options. It's as if the developers hate the idea of a conventional main menu. The art design is best described as yet another clone of the Rick and Mortyesque style, but it's also ultra "inclusive" which might be you're sort of thing. Rest assured you can play dress up and experiment with all the modern pseudo-identities.  Good luck finding a straight looking white guy character with the randomize button though. Personally, as someone who "identifies" as a keyboard/mouse gamer, I demand better representation. They could at least make the menus mouse friendly.The story writing is pure drivel, like something a preteen would make up on the spot for drama class.The gameplay is ok, but everything else sucks. Thumbs up only if you're playing it on a steam deck type device. In its current state it is not fit for desktop so I'm thumbing this down.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay consists of holding and releasing the joystick until you miss a jump, rinse and repeat. You can also press a single button to do a trick in the air. The alternate routes which were one of the selling points are just more jumps and don't feel very different at all. Maybe it gets better but I'm not risking playing more, the game being just as boring and then not being able to refund.The cutscenes are animated in low frame rate which is apparently a stylistic choice but it looks janky and makes me feel like my game is broken. The dialogue is almost as unpleasant so I recommend skipping the cutscenes entirely. There's even a dialogue option saying you don't care at the start of each one which I appreciate.As soon as you launch the game you're met with multiple pages you need to sign. I personally don't care but a lot of people have pointed out the invasion of privacy.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: They made a big hubbub about this game being easier than the others but be warned, that's a lie. About three hours in it gets just as hard as the other games in the series. If you hate yourself (like most modern gamers seem to) then I guess you won't mind. But I'm really angry that they tried to bill this as some chill vibe game when it's just the same thing with a chill wrapper put over the top of it. Downright false advertising.

_childDocuments_.review: Piss poor controls with a trick scheme that can be boiled down to the L(eft) diagonal stick, rather bland artistic direction. The level design is good but the ultra zoomed in nature of the game makes for terrible anticipation in terms of what tricks and such to pull off next, speed can only be increased, you lack any brake ability, a rather jarring lack of mechanic in a skating game.Edit: having playtested this mechaincal failure some more i've found npcs and collectables may become invisible in your runs so you can't see where they are in order to collect them. An EXTREME oversight from what i assume are low tier developers.Malicious design seem to be what's the core practice of the harder challenges. Pinpoint precision is key, yet you have to react extremely fast to get it done as zooming out to better anticipate what obstace comes next just isn't an implemented feature.Terrible design that is antifun and suggest malicious intent rather than fun challenges.All in all, the blandness of the artistic vision coupled with the very shallow and poorly thought out mechanics nets it a 3/10 ratiing.

_childDocuments_.review: I guess I should've read the store page before getting the game in the Humble Monthly.This game doesn't accept keyboard and mouse controls, and if you're like me and don't have a functioning controller (or one with drifting) then you're pretty much out of luck, you can't play the game; it seems a bit of a weird decision specially when you consider previous games in the franchise could use the controller, my guess that the devs noticed other developers adding that banner in their store page and figured, "hey, who's gonna play it without a controller anyway, right?".In the end I'll give it a try once more when I eventually get my controller, because it does seem like a pretty nice game, fairly challenging at that though, and I also didn't like how the game forces down a silly cutscene at the beginning down my throat without an option to skip it, makes me feel as if the developers have a degree of pretenciousness in a way.Like the whole game, as charming as it is, also has this vibe of "this is our game, you either like it and play it how we want you to, or not".

_childDocuments_.review: I quit out of this game mid-level because I feel physically obligated to write a review about the egregious level design practices at play here and why I feel they make this game overall not worth purchasing or playing.The level in question is a side-quest in the first area. The objectives for the quest are simple: pop all the cat balloons. The course is linear, there are no other objectives, no real obstacles or things to interact with, no reason to do tricks; just a flat, linear course with a few dips and peaks here and there, and cat balloons at the peak of your jump arc following a ramp.Besides this being monotonous, bland, and utterly lacking in player expression, the level itself is designed in such a way that is actively malicious to the player. The difficulty curve for the stage is straightly linear, meaning it starts out easy and gets harder and harder as the stage goes forward at a constant rate. What this means, in practice, is that there are two jumps near the very end of the course that are the most difficult, and therefore may lead to you missing a single cat balloon.There is no way to go backwards and retry a single balloon—if you miss one, you have to redo the entire course from beginning to end. It's short, but repeated playtime adds up when the only jump you are struggling with, and therefore interested in practicing, is at the very end of the level. This is, in no other sense of the word, 'bad' game design—it requires a monotonous set of physical tacks the player must complete over and over again in order to attempt the challenge they are currently struggling with. Imagine a game where, every time you want to fight a boss again, you have to solve thirty seconds of math equations. Not initially frustrating, maybe, but after a while you'll be overflowing with the feeling of 'JUST LET ME DO THE THING', and Olli Olli World is rife with this feeling in every inch of its design ethos.My gripes evidenced in a single stage go on: it's possible to do a jump so 'well' that you actually go *over* a balloon, meaning, yes, you're being punished for playing in excess of the developer's expectations, and will have to redo the level. Despite you failing if you miss a single balloon, there's no recognition or indication of this from the level, other than it resetting to the start screen when you reach the finish without completing the objective. It feels like every single stage in the game is designed in this way in some fashion, to punish the player for something they couldn't have known before failing at it repeatedly, and then making them do the same thing over and over again before actually allowing them to attempt or practice the part with which they're struggling. This is in almost every level, and there's no 'practice garage' or sandbox of any kind to allow you to mess around and get a feel for things—not that it would matter much, because the levels won't allow you to explore or be creative either. They're all either singular or binary linear paths that culminate in momentum-based chokepoint jumps usually about halfway through, meaning if you mismanage your momentum even slightly before the halfway point of a level, you will fail that jump, and have to redo the entire stage over again if you want to restore your combo. Despite this being the optimal way to play in terms of score, the game actively punishes you for attempting to do so via its design.I wanted so badly to like this game, but these are flaws I wouldn't forgive in a free game, let alone one I purchased for $40 . No course editor of any kind, an 'expansion pass' for content that should have been in the main game, grindy, monotonous achievements that only result in boring cosmetics and no affect on gameplay... I feel like the trailer for the game even tries to trick you into thinking this is somehow a more open game than it is by beginning with a manufactured scene of a skate park area that does not exist in game. You can't hang out with other skaters and watch them do tricks, you can't groove out in any one area without moving linearly forward (to the right), you can't really interact with NPCs, there's no meaningful inventory... the list just goes on.For some reason people who buy this game seem to really really like it, and I suspect that's because it's largely being purchased by fans of the studios older games. As such, this entry plays almost identically (despite what the advertising would say), but the game itself is built like a slimy cash-grab instead of a genuine product. The levels don't feel playtested, or that they were built by someone who themselves either didn't enjoy playing them or wasn't at a level of understanding necessary to get what actually makes playing a level fun. So many blind momentum chokepoints with giant jumps. So many annoying binary objectives that make it so much harder to trick or move through the level in a fun way. So many level elements thrown in your face and then forced down your throat instead of being integrated with other objects or obstacles and allowed to breathe. So many repetitions in tricks due to the input method hampering variety and expression. So many bad puns and exhaustive pointless lore about a place that doesn't take itself seriously enough for anyone to care about. So much pain. So much suffering.This is the worst I have felt about a game in a long time. Not just mad—ripped off. Like, I actively paid money for this product, and it is offensive to my standards at a level I can't even articulate. It makes me want to lobby a campaign against this studio and their future products based on how terrible my experience was. I'm not going to do such a thing, but it *makes me want to*.Please do not buy this game. Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bad early version of a better clone named Skate City that you can get for half the retail price.  Unskippable cutscenes that are filled with lame skating puns, ugly characters, unresponsive controls and frustrating trial-and-error level design all pile up to make this a generally bad experience.  Wait for this game to plummet in price or go on sale for a significant discount before buying.  As it is, OlliOlli World is just a bad, dated throwback to a troubled genre and better, similar games have come out since that are far better and a lot cheaper.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting much when I bought it, and I was dead wrong this is one of the funniest games I've played in a couple years. It's a super addictive easy to play, hard to master game. The gameplay starts very simple, and you're gradually introduced to more and more complex mechanics (that are here from the get go but are not required to know about in the first levels) that will allow you if you manage to incorporate them to blow up the scores. The level design is very inventive, and even if it's not far from being an autoscroller, there is actual "exploration" with multiple paths leading to various side objectives, loops and scoring opportunities. You can approach the game as you please, either very casually or chose to tackle the side objectives that bring the true difficulty of the game and push you to use every mechanic to the fullest. Aside from that, the artstyle and overall "mood" of the game is super cosy and fun, the music is awesome and there are tons of cosmetics to unlock to dress up your little skater as you wish, it's just adorable ! If you like rich and challenging 2D platformers, skateboarding, scoring games, do not hesitate and go for it it's well worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I feel like I should take back what I said about this game being good for casual players. I just reached Chapter 4 and the game instantly jumped up a MASSIVE difficulty spike. Every single jump needs to be perfect in order to even beat a single level, not even considering the extra challenges, and it can get very frustrating very quickly. I really enjoyed the first half of this game, but I admit, the second half has been brutal.ORIGINAL REVIEW: This is one of those games where the premise is very simple, but the end result is very good. Essentially this is just an arcade game where you try to get the highest score possible, but the simple controls make it one of those "Easy to pick up, difficult to master" games. I think the inclusion of specific challenges is a great way of giving players something to aim for and most levels are very straightforward and short, making the game feel relatively accessible to more casual players. There are some challenges and levels that are more annoying than others, but overall, most of them are pretty fun. The characters and plot are not that deep, but they do add an extra layer of personality that makes the game feel more inviting. Overall, if you're looking for a fast arcade-style game that can be enjoyed by casuals and tryhards, you can give this one a try.

_childDocuments_.review: This game rules! Only really have a few gripes with it. The first one is that the game sometimes punishes you for going a bit too fast or a hair too slow, this can end up resulting in you dropping combos in certain areas. The Other one being that pushing on your board effectively becomes reserved for the start of your runs and almost nowhere else because of the game's emphasis on maintaining your combo rising as you progress. Speaking of Combo's, this game, unlike Skate, THPS, or Session isn't really classifiable as a skateboarding game/sim in the same sense as the previously mentioned titles. This game is effectively a combo simulator, so I guess don't really come into it with the expectations that you might get from something else like those titles. BUT, assuming you've seen any of this game's marketing, I highly doubt that that's a surprise. Overall this game rules, totally should've won best sports game of the year over whatever EA title won.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, I think it's cool and good. I really like the aesthetic and the gameplay. I like that there are no paid cosmetic unlocks, and that you unlock stuff by beating challenges in the game. There is a lot of cool and good stuff about this game, and it would be fine to purchase if you're going to be totally casual about it.HOWEVER,There is a hacker/exploiter who will do one Ollie and get 999,999,999 points, rendering the high score system completely useless. You can watch any of the first place replays on the leader boards and see what I mean.Also, there is a known bug where sometimes it won't track your challenges. The only way to fix this is to completely delete your saves and start fresh, carefully backing up your saves on the regular. This has been known by the developers for at least 2 years without being fixed. I was angling to get this game 100%, but learning about this took the wind completely out of my sails.These two major issues ruined this game for me. I was legitimately having a blast until I ran into the second issue, and now I just won't bother playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: The beauty of challenging games lies in a gradual difficulty curve, drip feeding you new techniques, so that by the end of the game, you’re a complete monster at it without having even really noticed your improvement. When you go back to tackle earlier missions/levels/whatever that tripped you up, they’re a breeze, easy thanks to your mastery. OlliOlli World is cool in that all techniques are available to you from the start. There are tutorials spread throughout the game, but they only teach you them, rather than hiding them behind an abritrary locking system. I picked up on most techniques without needing to be taught them, and enjoyed destroying the early levels. By the third world, I was starting to feel challenged and having fun - unable to put the game down. Out of nowhere, the game slaps you with an insane difficulty spike. You feel as if you’re starting from the beginning; suddenly everything seems impossible. Jumps require near perfect precision to make, especially on off branch “gnarly routes” (I do enjoy the abundance of skater related terms). Wall rides become a vision of torture. OlliOlli World starts to become something you resent, because you’ve made it this far, the end is nigh, but the pixels move too damn fast for your brain to comprehend, and your analogue sticks are screaming out in pain as you yank them up, down and all over trying to string chain after chain not to beat 1/2/3 star high scores (known as local heroes), but just to survive. Go off brand on a gnarly route and find yourself with a nearly impossible jump, and you’ll need to restart because a checkpoint was put within this route. This difficulty spike doesn’t ruin the game, but it comes close. With patience, later levels can be beaten, especially if you stop focussing on trying to combo everything together and focus on surviving. But it feels counterintuitive, the fun here is actually in seeing if you can string together a combo throughout the entire level, not just survive. At times, the controls work against you, especially with wallrides. At other times, you have to accept that you just hit the wrong button because you’re trying to process everything, whilst tricking, at high speed. When it works, it’s fantastic, high-octane fun. There aren’t many things out there as satisfying as nailing a later mission in one single combo. When it doesn’t, it fills you with rage that you buried for years, ever since you first got spawn-killed on Modern Warfare 2 by a pre-pubescent puffer jacket aficionado with both a dole and an attitude problem. Story, graphics and soundtrack are in my opinion all secondary to what’s really important here, the core gameplay. It’s well crafted, if you can stomach the rage and process what is happening fast enough.

_childDocuments_.review: As a disclaimer about my playtime on Steam, I have an obsessively larger amount of hours of OlliOlli World on the Playstation 5, but wanted to actually buy the game to support the developers for making such an excellent, excellent, excellent game.I haven't played the previous OlliOlli games and if you haven't, you shouldn't worry, the story is beautiful, rainbow-vomited, gnarly skateboarding nonsense. The true essence of this game is in its addictive chain comboing you do on your skateboard that uses a combination input with your left analog stick and inputting modifiers with your button inputs and right analog stick. If you were asking why I specifically said analog sticks, then you're right, this is one of those mandatory controller-only games. YOU MUST USE A CONTROLLER or the game will not function at all, ignoring all your keyboard inputs.While the skateboarding gameplay is excellent, it helps that the soundtrack is absolutely mellow, chill, fresh and fun. It sets the tone for the entire game and lets you know what you're getting into. I honestly don't think I've ever played another indie game that had a soundtrack that perfectly matched the game it was paired to.Levels are fun, challenging and allow a lot of creativity in how you want to chain combos. The world is goofy, the writing is forgivably cringe, but this is definitely a game you turn on when you want to chill and not stress out. Every level is as hard or as easy as you want it to be with a lot of replayability.This is my hidden gem that I think everyone should at least try, if not, own.

_childDocuments_.review: Really adore this game but I have to quit for the sake of my sanity in the knowledge that World 4 brings a steep difficulty creep. It's colourful, responsiveness and puts a unique on an age old genre. But it is VERY hard. In no short part due to just HOW many mechanics are thrown at you and combined eventually. I didn't know this when I got it from Humble but I will not dock merit because I'm bad at it. Maybe one day in the future I'll come back it but in my personal aim to  challenge the backlog, I cannot divulge time into games I probably can't beat (It's why I'm scared to go back to Elden Ring lol).: I have since come back and beaten the game a few months later, beelining the last two worlds. It wasn't the most fun way to engage with them but makes me feel better about not having been able to beat it prior. I think the manual slam tutorial is either glitched or very very hard, it's what I got stuck on initially. My opinion on the game still stands, its great and definitely has a high, almost limitless skill ceiling. For people who want to play it forever and master it? You can. But I just wanted to skate and have a bit of fun. And it does that too. Really enjoyed it so, again, big thumbs up from me. Original rating and review stands.

The game is super fun, and will keep your attention with all the challenges and achievements. Rollerdrome and Ollie Ollie World are currently one of my favorite games that I play. I can't wait to see what this studio has in stores for the future. I highly recommend that you try out this game as well as Rollerdrome
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game with an endearing art style that works for it. If you are a fan of the Olli Olli series, Olli Olli World delivers with the same easy to pick up, hard to master gameplay. If you are new to Olli Olli, the main thing you need to know is this is a essentially a rhythm game that requires precision timing and strategy. Many (later) levels are puzzle like and are good for giving yourself a migraine trying to complete at certain points. That being said it is enjoyable for casual players up until you get to Sketchside and Los Vulgas, where the difficulty spikes very quickly and will weed out all but those who are familiar or looking for a challenge. Some small bugs are notable but nothing that has interrupted my own gameplay. NOTE: Olli League is pretty broken due to the sole fact that grabs seem to be the meta. This means most of the top scorers will have a lot of grab spam in their replays which means most top replays are by in large similiar. It doesn't make any sense that you can full tweak a grab on flat ground at all. Would be much cooler if players could have stylish runs that dont have weird grab spam every 2 seconds.Also wtf is Suzes problem lol
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: 25+hours more into it.. look, I'd still recommend the game given how cool the first few areas are, but as you progress through the 4th and 5th world, the 'hard but fair' starts going out the window. The mechanics are still tight, but the runs become either extremely long slogs or require ridiculous pixel-perfect execution to complete everything. If you look at the global achievements, this is a clear reflection that majority of players could not be bothered completing the game. So whilst you can argue 'hur dur git gud' the devs either targeted the extreme players or gave up - especially the fact there are a lot more combo-dropping bugs in the later levels does it indicate that perhaps QA budget ran out.OlliOlli World is a vast improvement over the unfair punishment that was OlliOlli 1 + 2, when you fail in the game you know that the mechanics are solid and failure is caused by you and you alone. There are a few mechanics which aren't explained clearly (don't rotate on stairs, 3 manuals before your combo drops) but otherwise the game is fairly relaxing... until you get to Sketchside (4th world) when the difficulty really ramps up and it becomes a carpal tunnel nightmare. Overall, great game - still grinding achievements; would recommend RSI simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: One or two years ago I decided I'd really try focusing to 100% a game before writing a review – if I like the game, that is. Even when I like something, the sheer size of the backlog sometimes causes me to abandon things I enjoy and this tactic worked pretty well to avoid that. It was clear to me very early on that OlliOlli World would be one of those games, but I have to admit defeat. I expected a challenge, but I didn't expect the game to break me and the strategy I just described. I hate the game a little bit for it, but that's a very personal thing. In the grand scheme of things, the game is everything I hoped it would be.OlliOlli and OlliOlli2 are among my all-time favorite "tough but fair" games. I originally discovered them on the PS Vita – feels like a lifetime ago. I bought the collection of both games again when they came out on the Switch a few years back and finished (completed!) both of them again. The soundtrack, the gameplay loop, the challenging levels… as if they were made for me. So I was incredibly excited when OlliOlli World was announced. Mildly skeptical as the art style was radically different, but that turned out to be no problem at all. Yes, it's different – but it still looks and sounds great. The controls are still tight, and the challenging gameplay is still there.Unfortunately the game fumbles this most important part pretty badly. Not bad enough that I'd consider not giving this a well-deserved thumbs-up, but given how the first two games got this so right I do wonder what went wrong here. The difficulty spike in this game is absolutely ridiculous. As mentioned before, I've 100%ed both predecessors on three different platforms, so I do like to think that I'm not terrible at these games. And indeed I did get through more than half of this game easily. Too easily, in fact. In many levels I managed to complete all challenges in a single run, often the very first run. For the first few levels I attributed this to my extensive experience and having very recently replayed the old games, but even in those I needed many more attempts in mid-game levels. Something was off. And then suddenly it goes from 0 to 100 and you barely manage to even finish levels at all. Your approach changes from completing all the levels in a world to somehow hopefully managing to successfully reach the end of enough levels to even progress any further at all.You do re-acclimate after this shock and get more used to these absolutely brutal levels with ridiculous challenges. And it's weird, because the huge and unexpected spike almost makes me resent something I normally would enjoy. And I did manage to enjoy these as well, even though some of them are either unfair or bugged, sometimes unfortunately both. The new checkpoint system helps a bit, but it's just not fun when you're on attempt #74 for a challenge that requires you to perfectly run a 2 minute long level and then at the end it fails because you hit a clipping/hitbox bug and fall through the floor. It's fairly rare, but it's unacceptable to happen at all in a game with that difficulty. The fact that there still hasn't been a patch for any of these bugs, which have extensively been reported here and on the Discord, leaves a really sour taste in my mouth. Another negative aspect is the completely broken scoring for the multiplayer component, which would otherwise be a neat idea.That said, even with those rare bugs and the frustrating difficulty curve, I have had dozens of hours of great fun in the game. The DLC approach is exactly how it should be: More of the same but with a great twist for a couple of bucks. The game clearly is a labor of love, and while it's not reaching the heights of the predecessors for me personally, it might even be a better entry into the OlliOlli world for new players with its more modern art style and the much easier early levels.I'll continue working towards that 100% completion, but it will probably take a few years if I don't want to burnout and start hating the game. So I had to accept that my "only review after completion" approach needs to allow for exceptions.Edit: I have since 100%ed the game, and the fact that even years later there hasn't been any bug fixes is very disheartening. The DLC levels are even buggier than the late game levels of the main game, and simply falling through the floor at a random point during an incredibly challenging task that takes several minutes and would need dozens, maybe even close to hundreds, of retries even without bugs to finally master is just infuriating. That aside, not just the levels are bugged but your progress in some collectible-like challenges can also get stuck after investing 50+ hours without any chance of recourse besides restarting. For PC, some random stranger actually built a tool that attempts to fix it, on console you're just out of luck. Even with the unofficial tool on PC you might not get achievements unlocked correctly if ever being hit by the bug. No game is free of bugs, of course, but in a game where a large part of the appeal is perfection and skill, I expect a bit more focus on actually being able to perfect your skills without running into such blatant problems. I don't have it in my heart to change to a thumbs-down, but it's hard to justify a thumbs-up.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent platforming/skateboarding game. Music is "French chill beats to relax/skate to". Art looks like this takes place in the world of Adventure Time but in 3D. Lots of challenge based unlockables to customize your skater and their trick selection. The RAD edition comes with 2 DLC that both add new levels and unlockables for your skater. It held my attention for the entire campaign and more.As much as I like the previous two games, I ended up dropping both of them after a short while. If you haven't played any of them, I think this is a great place to start.The soundtrack is absolutely fantastic. I love the character customization in this one. The new mechanics are fun and interesting. Be warned though, this game really does require a controller.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game so I could review it.I really liked the game at first. It has amazing music, a nice art style and more on the comedy side storyline.But as the game progress the frustration increases with it. Olli Olli World is not a hard game, just frustrating with mechanics that force you to replay the same level over and over again so you can get all challenges and memorize the level to get the best scores.If you don't care for challenges and just want a fun precision platformer with a skateboard theme, then Olli Olli World is for you.But if you are a completionist and doesn't like bs mechanics, than avoid this game. Also if you are a casual player looking for a skate game, the precision platformer tag is way heavier than skateboarding.In short: it's not my cup of tea, and use cheap mechanics to increase difficulty. If this approach doesn't bother you, maybe give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so adorable. I love the customization options and the different ways you can earn items. It really makes my completionist heart happy. The controls are easy enough and I constantly feel motivated to complete the different objectives in the levels. I recommend this game for anyone who loves cute animations, 100% completion enjoyers, and anyone who liked tony hawk as a child :)
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful platformer with gorgeous artstyle, great music, and amazingly designed levels. Controls are super tight and every mechanic added through the game immediately makes sense gameplay wise, even for someone who knows nothing about skate. Get the Rad Edition on a sale for the new zones, they add enough to the game and you can get it for pretty cheap. A gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game on Switch last year and just got it for Steam Deck as part of a Humble bundle. OlliOlli World is what you would get if you mixed a Tony Hawk game with a 2D platformer. It feels great to play, and is a classic "just one more run" type of game. The art style is a visual treat and the lo-fi soundtrack fits perfectly.I only had a couple of qualms with the game. While I didn't have any trouble finishing the campaign, the bonus goals and high scores in the later levels increase significantly to the point where I stopped even trying to attempt them. The later worlds also felt less visually interesting to me and were not quite as memorable as the early game.All that said, I had a great time with OlliOlli World, and it's been one of my favorite games in recent memory.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best surprises I've ever gotten from humble choice. And Rad (deluxe) Edition too. It's been a long time since I've truly fallen in love with a side-scroll/platformer ANYTHING. and it's not even that I don't appreciate the genre, I just got very tired of the gameplay after years of repetition. related side-note, i'm not a DarkSouls/Eldon Ring player. It's cool, i just am not one for dying a lot. You'll (die) a lot here, but it'll be surprisingly funny when you do. It's worth it, this game is worth it. Easy plug for Humble Choice; I got it for a steal. If you get it for full price even, you won't be unhappy. Just go read some of the other reviews, or better yet just go read my crazy-@$$ review of DJ Max Respect V, a bit of that applies here.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: I tried getting into the original OlliOlli a few times, but kept bouncing off of it after just a few minutes.  I figured the same would be the case with World, but thought I'd give it a go since I got it in a bundle with some other games.  I'm happy to say that World clicked with me a lot better!  The game feels a lot more approachable to me than the first.  Eases you into the experience while slowly introducing mechanics and letting you get a feel for them as the campaign goes on.  Also lets you make a custom character which I really enjoyed!I didn't end up finishing the game personally, but I did enjoy my time with the game!  The mechanics are fun, and the game has a lot of little challenges to offer and a ton of levels.  I could easily see someone sinking a ton of time into this game and getting a lot of satisfaction from trying to complete every level and challenge.  It won't be for everyone, but if you like the sound of a 2D precision platformer based around skateboarding, it's very much worth looking into.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: The first two games in the series were already good. Solid mechanics and great sound track. Now they improved the graphics,  and let you skate in a spiritual Adventure Time OOO. They added even more game mechanics that work and I really like the characters and humor. Customization is awesome too. This the perfect Steam Deck game.Only thing missing now is multiplayer, but not a big deal. This isn't a multiplayer game and I don't have the same problem with the Nintendo Switch version, which leads me to believe that this is just a DRM.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: You can't play this game is the servers are down, which they often are. It's a completely singleplayer game that apparently only has a lifespan as long as the servers are maintained. Super fun game, amazing visuals and a perfectly suited soundtrack, all locked behind a network error message in a game where the only multiplayer content is highscore leaderboards. It's a little hard to say I don't recommend this game because it's honestly dope, but how can you encourage people to buy a game that can't be launched half of the time and seems guaranteed to be completely unplayable at some arbitrary point in the future?
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute game. I really like visuals and the music, but it seems very fast paced sometimes. I wish there was an option to adjust the game speed or difficulty settings. Nonetheless, it's still a fun and addictive game. I definitely don't have the temper for this game though, as you die quite a lot. Despite the challenges, the game's replay value is high and there's always room for improvement. It's a great way to pass the time and sharpen your reflexes. Although frustrating at times, the game's difficulty adds to the sense of accomplishment upon completion. But if you enjoy a challenge, it's worth a try. While dying frequently can be discouraging, the game's quirky graphics and upbeat soundtrack keep it from feeling too intense. It's a game that's easy to pick up and play, but tough to master.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: this game is amazing. as someone who's not the most technical with button pressing and combos, the stick movements really work for me. of course there's a lot of failing while you improve but the game makes it easy to hop back on your board. it's one of the few recent games where I can actually feel myself getting better and see that high score keep going up.
