_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: The most fun I've ever had in a platform type game. OlliOlliWorld came as a surprise and will most likely stay within my top replayed games list. I'm continuously learning, improving, and skating my way through the levels. There's a good amount of problem solving in here, but it never detracts from the experience. I now only hope that one day I can do some of these tricks IRL at some point. Scratches that skating itch when the weather is not cooperating outside your gamer abode.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Easy to pick up and complete using just basic tricks, but by the end of the game you'll have learned many complex moves. It's a very satisfying game to master. Lots of content, fun DLC, online league system is very addictive, and soundtrack and art style are great to top it off.An unexpectedly brilliant game.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Part of January 2023 Humble Bundle.Really enjoyable blend of straightforward gameplay and challenging skills for those who want to delve deeper into the game's mechanics. It really feels satisfying pulling off tricks and building combos, and just as frustrating when you lose it or keep botching an attempt to get to a specific area on a track. It definitely a game that makes you want to pull just one more attempt or see a new track.Speaking of, I didn't expect the amount of exploration each track has, with different trails showing different areas/challenges you might miss otherwise. There's a lot of care in making these worthwhile and upfront, with some of the challenges being to do something within these alternate tracks.I don't have much to say about issues, mainly because they are probably things I'm doing. I could never figure out the timing for the blue mid-air trick, and I only seem to get it without trying. Even going through the tutorial again didn't help. But that's absolutely a me problem. I'd also say the side quests are just challenges with different characters, rather than a storyline that leads somewhere, but again, that's not really the point of OlliOlli World.One thing I was surprised at was not being able to unlock new hairstyles. With how customizable your character is, I expected new hair and beard styles to open up. But that's such a small thing it's barely worth mentioning. Regardless, I had a surprising amount of fun changing my character's style and board, which is not something I expected going in.The story is feel-good and airy. There to get you from A to B with little quips from the game's charming characters. They play on tropes and archetypes but everything fits into the world, and just like everything else, there's care to keep things on what matters most: the skateboarding.There's a lot to enjoy after beating the game. I went back and got high scores in the first area, which really felt satisfying because I could see the difference between beginning the game and learning the mechanics to beat it. On top of this, there's two, I guess free DLC areas (not sure if that's accurate) you can enter after meeting certain thresholds. I didn't expect to write this much, so I'll just say OlliOlli World was a real surprise for me. As someone not really into these sorts of games I found myself playing this a lot and just being into the whole vibe. The challenges are interesting enough to keep me wanting to return and its vibrant, colorful world is a pleasure to look at. Definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all the Oli Oli games, and this one is my hands down favorite yet!They *really* did an awesome job of expanding the world and gameplay with this one, and I'm especially digging how the transition to 2.5D feels like it actually expands the options, rather than just being a gimicky visual-only change.Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: OlliOli World is good fun. I liked quite a lot about the game - the controls felt great, number of tricks and combos you could pull off is staggering, there are a lot of good challenges and the music fits well in here.Overall is a great great game on offer and most who love skating games have already bought this one.Compliments aside, this game has a big flaw in my opinion - difficulty. First three worlds were the best: they offer good challenges and after playing the game more, and learning new tricks you could beat the third highest score. Because the game is basically an arcade, one of the satisfying goals is to beat that third high score.Then at the fourth world onwards the game basically becomes a "sweatlord competition". It gets very hard too fast. It asks you to complete each level without breaking a single combo (which I find very tough) to beat the third highest score. This is where I'm also starting to have issues with the "physics" in the game. One run I'm flying around and speeding through the level. Fail. Start again. The second time I am slowed down (for some reason) and cannot reach the edge, and drop to see my multiplier score reset to zero. I then have to start all over.I find the physics quite inconsistent and spending about an hour trying to reach that high score on a short level isn't something that I found fun in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay wise, it started out a bit too simple and almost dropped it as a result, but I carried on and it got more fun as more mechanics were introduced throughout the whole game.  Once you start going fast and quickly chaining together a bunch of moves it feels slick and satisfying.The main story or so, (going through the main levels) doesn't take very long. (3-4 hours)  However I could definitely see someone putting dozens or hundreds of hours into this if they enjoy the core gameplay enough and like fighting for high scores and challenges-- of which this game offers plenty to aim for.  Even if you don't have anyone else on your friends list who owns the game, it will find you randoms with scores near yours to be your "rivals" for levels.The dialog is pretty cringe and admittedly I started skipping it all after the first chapter, and the story is comical due to its absurdity and being so on the nose.  (Gnarvana lol)  I'm also not biggest fan of the art style but that's perhaps just personal preference.  You can judge the art for yourself before buying.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and colorful graphics, fun skateboard lanes with lots of weird characters/things to see and sometimes frustratingly difficult. If you don't like fast paced games this might not be for you. But I really enjoy trying to explore all different paths and lanes and see everything Radlandia has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable game that I'd definitely recommend.Controls were unique and I thought fit the game really well (note: this game requires a controller). The first three worlds of this game are absolutely incredible. They nailed the level design, tutorials, pacing, and difficulty really well. It was just challenging enough to be interesting but not easy enough to be boring. Everything feels super fair and I knew I messed up if I failed. The challenges were also super fun to knock out - would recommend trying to do all of the challenges and high scores, at least for the first three major worlds. The plot and characters are pretty forgettable, but at least they don't distract too much from the main game and don't take themselves too seriously.The game stumbles a bit in the last couple worlds - for whatever reason the difficulty of challenges and high scores just skyrockets. Challenges went from being a fun challenge to being this impossible grind and I ended up totally skipping all of them in the last couple worlds which made the game way less enjoyable. It's just not fun to grind through weirdly specific, mechanically difficult challenges, or have to full combo the whole level to get a high score. I much preferred the more streamline challenges that are markers that you found your way through secret paths or show some level of mastery over something the game just taught you. Instead these last couple worlds had a lot of really cruel challenges like "boop eight ducks in one combo while doing three special tricks on three separate grinds without smashing", like chill a little I'm not trying to go pro in Olli Olli world.Overall this game is at its best when it nails the right level of difficulty and you hit that flow state where things just click. I think for the most part this game nails that and so far the DLC has been a ton of fun too.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Games not for me but I can see how somehow would really enjoy this. It makes me pretty motion sick with how fast it moves, so if you are prone to motion sickness, avoid this game. Solid graphics and skating mechanics make it fun to play. Story is kind of tacked on and doesn't need to be there.If you liked the other OlliOlli games then youll like this. Just not for me5/10
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: easy to pick up hard to master, as chill or as sweaty as you want it to be. Lots of levels, challenges and high score chasing here. Unlock things to customize your skater with IN GAME to show off accomplishments. Chill vibes and soundtrack and honestly a really fun game when you learn about the depth it has. Plus randomly generated levels that you pick different options to generate from. I haven't even touched the dlc yet but i love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: I will say, as an Olli Olli newcomer I started the game and thought, "This is it? Seems pretty simple. One-stick controls to do different types of board flips, and that's about it." However, after a while, I started to notice things that piqued my curiosity that kept me playing - how are there people on the leaderboard with scores over a MILLION points? Are they hacking? Am I doing something wrong? Then, OlliOlli World continued to unfold its deceptive depth as I proceeded through the levels. I can do grabs? My character can spin? I can do manuals to connect combos like in Tony Hawk's Pro Skater? Well, now that I know how to do that, I guess I'll have to go back to the earlier levels and beat my previous scores there.Now levels where I used to top out at around 20,000 points, I'm scoring 1,000,000+ thanks to mystery of the additional mechanics unraveling. I'm performing insane combos as I effortlessly glide between giant mountains like a true skate god. I am unstoppable, until I continue through the story whose final levels are TOUGH and Olli Olli World humbles me once again.Between the art style, the music, the satisfaction of finishing a level in one combo after trying for 30+ minutes, OlliOlli World absolutely RULES and I'm glad I stuck with it. The story is forgettable IMO, but you can skip all the cutscenes by holding A and just get back to being the skate god you are.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: This is my game of the year 2022It's so good! I love how this game flows. You get into the action super quick and when you fall a reset is just a button press away. The level design is fantastic, the lo-fi beats soundtrack is amazing and there is continuous action.The definition of easy to learn and hard to master.If you like it, get the "Finding the Flowzone" DLC. It has the best level design in the entire game.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the first 2 Olli Olli games and wasn't sure I needed more since I came to them quite late, but OOW really does take it up a notch. Feels excellent to play, lots of subtleties in the controls, optional challenges to chase, alternative paths through the level that actually make use the 3D space (something I wondered about). Really compelling.I can see why the quirky characters / dialogue might annoy some people but you can just skip over it if you want. The game underneath is absolutely stellar and a gem for everyone who likes nuanced arcade games.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: For the 4-5 hours it took me to shred through it, Olli Olli World is really fun.  I got into a pretty zen zone with it and really learned to like it the more I played.  It's my first Olli game, but it's sure worth the hype and the price (got it on sale for about 10 dollars).Even better, you can skip all the dialogue because none of it is particularly important, so if you want to just get right into it, go ahead.  A top indie game with great graphics, a very relaxing soundtrack, and surprisingly deep mechanics.  It's definitely worth a play for any Skate/THPS fans.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good and not.I think it works very well, tons of things to unlock, levels are interesting and in an abundance.However, the game feels a bit too much all at once. Sometimes you could feel the flow of things and other times it just felt generally frustrating. Like the wall riding seems wonky at times. Switch different directions via half pipes is awkward sometimes, but everything else feels great.I still think you should check it out for yourself, but it didn't hit the same for me the way the first or second one did.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game. Lovable characters, great art style, gameplay is fresh and new (feels almost like an updated sonic).  My biggest and only major gripe that the difficulty ramps up pretty heavily after world 3, maybe they should scale back the challenges a bit. The sidescroller genre needed a masterpiece like this. I can't wait for more DLC! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Addicting as hell to complete challenges and chase scores, Roll7 have really seemed to master making games that are simple to get into but keep you coming back and trying more until you experience the full depth. Between the art-style, music, and tone it's an incredible vibe all the way through that'll have you in a good mood even when it gets crazy hard. Also shout-out to it being an excellent ultrawide experience - it's very cool to see more of the levels and get a real sense of scale.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Merging the arcadey nature of THPS and the thumbstick driven mechanics of Skate, Olli Olli World throws out everything that isn't going to contribute to the dopaminergic rush of pulling off the perfect line.  Olli Olli World hits the 'easy to learn, difficult to master' sweet spot wrapped in a package that can be enjoyed on the go with a steam deck or switch, or compulsively giving into 'just one more run' on TV or desktop for hours at a time.The last few months Olli Olli World has been my gaming comfort food.  Despite playing through a few AAA single player games as well as some multiplayer games, I continue to come back to Olli Olli World whenever I'm tired or frustrated or just want to kick back.  In my 40 hours of game time I've completed all of the retail release levels, a little more than half of their challenges, and just a few DLC levels.  There's still a ton of DLC and challenge content, as well as league play which I just recently began to dabble in.Olli Olli World is highly addictive, 5ins of fun, easily one of the best games of 2022 and, IMHO, deserves to be considered among the thps and skate and franchiaes as one of the best skating games ever made.  The MSRP is well worth the prices, if you find it in sale even better, give it the 2 hour refund window and if you aren't hopelessly addicted at that point come back and thumb down this review.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Are your thumbs bored? Fire up Olli Olli World. Did you grow up playing tony hawk's pro skater and eventually make the jump into EA's SKATE Franchise? Play Olli Olli World. A necessary and welcomed jump forward and breath of fresh air that this series needed to flourish. Added character customization gives you a reason to keep playing beyond just chasing high scores and beating all of the challenges (which is incredibly fun in it's own right.) The art style is amazing and fits the feel and story of the game perfectly. My only nitpick is that I wish the game had a bit more of a diverse soundtrack. I see why they went with the chill ambient electronic sound for the game as it's very much a meditative flow state experience, but I gotta have some ska and punk rock playing while I hop out there to shred the gnar.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! I enjoyed it very much. I 100% completed all worlds except for the last one. By the time I got to that one I was completely burnt out and have to take a break. Will most likely return to complete that world as well. Definitely give this one a go if you enjoy tough games.UPDATE: Beat the last area as well. So now I have everything done except the Radysus challenges. Won't be coming back for those but definitely give this game a game if you're a fan of this type of stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: 2D directional screen games were never really my style and so when I first saw this game I was not excited. However, I work at an indoor skate park (I'm not great but I am loving that I am improving) and this summer I traveled abroad to places with no skate parks and no skateable roads and was desperately missing my daily fix of skate. In a moment of need I bought this game and it was one of the best things I've ever done on Steam. Definitely recommend! Fixed my skate need right up and way less painful! The music I have mixed feelings about. I think its a great soundtrack by itself but sometimes hard to flow with so I listen to more intense music when I am really in a grind. If you've seen my username you can probably guess that I love dreaming about skating that defies gravity and wow! this game covered that. Thanks!
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part this game should be very similar if you have played the first 2 but with nice 3D graphics. There are some new mechanics but they really really got the pacing of the game and the aesthetics down. If youve never played olli olli and want a some simple arcade fun defo reccomend! If you played the first 2 there is more than enough new to look at to make this game worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly unique game that oozes style and character. Wonderfully addictive game feel, with satisfying tricks and combo systems that are fused together with an endearing little story. Each stage has multiple challenges that are optional and give customisation rewards if completed; these are really varied and unique throughout, and have been really satisfying to complete.The overall vibe of the game reminds me of Splatoon, especially all the clothes and gear you can equip.Really highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: I've played quite a lot of the 2 previous OlliOlli games and at first I was a little concerned about the clear pivot in style from those games, but after playing I'm completely stoked about it. It's cute, it's fun, there are a ton of levels, and good character customization. Even with the style change, the core feeling is still there.The first 2 games were quite difficult (in the later levels and to do all challenges). OlliOlli World is a bit more approachable while still giving you the option to go for challenging runs, which I really like.This was the first game I played on my Deck and will continue to be one of my go-to's for quite a while.The only thing I'd really like is to be able to skip the dialog stuff completely. I don't have a problem with it, but I want to just skate and find myself just blowing through every convo. It's a minor thing, but really the only part that I don't care for.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Olli Olli World is Rad.  Go play it.  The Presentation oozes style, the story is easily grasp,  the difficulty isn't as mind numbingly difficult, that you won't want to continue playing.  The challenges, the tricks, the scenery and the customization are top notch.  The developers put their stamp of approval on it.  And didn't have to use actual real-world licensing.  And the music soundtrack is fire.    You find yourself jamming while landing a multi string trick run.  Leaderboards abound, and you can even mess with the graphics options while engaged in gameplay in the pause menu.     If you're on the fence about purchasing it get when it goes on sale.  The bevy of content and features available in the standalone game as well as the newly released DLC are still priced cheaper than most triple A published games.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: This is such an improvement over the last one in many ways - especially visually. It's not an easy game - and often a frustrating one - but I'm absolutely loving it. I don't know if it REALLY scratches that THPS itch considering how different the gameplay is, but at the very least it's the most fun skating game I've played since those ones. The level design can be so charming and full of surprises that I've literally cackled with delight. The character customization options are also absurdly good, and this coming from someone who tends not to care too much about how my character looks. I'm somehow looking forward to Rollerdrome even more now.edit: yeah, this game still ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rules. the sketchside difficulty spike is real but only frustrating if you're trying to 100% the game; you'll still be able to beat the levels (and man they just get better and better)
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Very colorful and cute, gameplay is easy enough to pick up but definitely builds in complexity fairly quickly. As someone who thinks skateboarding is cool but doesn't have the ability for it, and has found most skateboarding games to be a bit too complicated and/or janky, this game is an easy recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Its a rad game. It is a simple game to pick up but hard game to master. You can easily beat the levels but trying to 100% and get all challenges in the level require some serious skill. It makes you want to keep trying to get a better score and beat the challenges. Also, the soundtrack is fantastic and really fits the game.  All in all, I gotta say this game is a vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that is a 2D sidescroller, I was skeptical at first but after playing the game, it's great. The level of detail and intricacy is very surprising and makes for a fun game with a lot of different combinations of tricks and stages. The controls are a bit tricky to get used to since it's pretty much exclusively the left stick that controls what tricks you do (and there are many) but is simple enough for the game to be fluid. Overall it's a fun game that can be played casually or a challenge to master.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: This game is Mad Fun would highly recommend to anyone no matter the age. I'm not really much of a skater myself but I found this game to be quite addicting and has easily became one of my favorites. You don't need to memorize some crazy controls to do some sick tricks just flick the joystick around and have fun with it However, if you are prone to motion sickness I would not recommend playing since there is a lot of fast moving scenes. Also a controller is required so you would need to purchase that too all in all 10/10 I would recommend to anyone
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely great platformer and challenges, perhaps a bit repetitive on that sense.My biggest complain is how slow the game is to introduce the mechanics, but when you get a sense of all you can do and skill level required it is absolutely fantastic.It scratched the itch Remnants of Naezith left, perhaps no as satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you like OlliOlli 1 or 2 you will like World. If you are a new player there is no better time to get into OlliOlli with this title being the most accessible of the OlliOlli titles.If you like OlliOlli 1 and 2 you will like this game as well. It's very similar to the first games however it does not feel like just another OlliOlli game. The developers have done a good job of making this new game feel different enough from the originals to keep you interested without not feeling like a sequel.The difficulty has been toned down somewhat which is a good thing for casual players. The most prevalent changes are to how pathing works. In this game you can choose different "radical" paths that run adjacent or revert original paths. This means you can have different runs on a singular map depending on the way you pick to go.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: OlliOlli World balances all aspects perfectly and is a true gem for skating games. It's easy to finish the levels but becomes increasingly harder to beat all the challenges.The gameplay is easy to learn but hard to master. Pulling off an insanely long combo takes practice, especially in later levels but is incredibly rewarding. The worlds are perfectly built around that. The first worlds gradually introduce you to new mechanics. In my opinion it was a bit too slow at first but that's perfectly fine. At some point beating all the challenges and local heroes becomes a bit of a challenge and I really like that. The level design never seems unfair since it's quite easy to get through the levels but it's difficult to get through the later levels with a good score.The soundtrack is really chill. While the amount of songs isn't all that huge I always enjoyed the laid back tunes. If there really was a song grinding your nerves, you could always skip it at any point in the game.The character customization is cute. You can get quite a bit creative with the different clothes you can use. For my taste, there aren't as many different hairstyles as I would have hoped but I think I'm special in that regard.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Terrific series, godlike game.The whole deal is basically "what if EA's Skate was a linear arcade style 2D score attack game?" The previous ones were so much fun, but this entry re-imagines so much, and hit the nail on the head with all of it, if you love Skating games, smooth combos, or scorechasing, I can't recommend this enough,it has unique and interesting stages, plenty of character customisation, collectables, optional challenges, ranked leaderboards with ranks, and a beautiful new artstyle similar to Adventure Time.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun. It is an evolution of the past two OlliOlli games and is a prime example of how to do a sequel right. The art and music are drastically different and the controls have been overhauled. There's a very wide variety of different tricks you are able to do and the sense of speed is enormous. If you want a good appetizer for the long road to Skate 4, this is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: pretty fun. I like all the hotpants my lil dude can wear. I'm having a blast with it, but that flow state is a little harder to come by in later stages where you're really limited in how you approach them, like it'd be cool if you could fart around a bit more on the flats instead of endlessly grinding out manuals, know what I mean? I recommend it though, it's slick and well designed, with a snappy interface and tight controls. all the jibber jabber from the side characters is irritating, but you can skip that crap, and I recommend that you do, because you get to the fun part faster.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it more than the previous OlliOllis but it's not what I was expecting, not any kind of free skating experience, more of a learn-and-repeat, uber-precise platform game on a skateboard. It's addictive and fun in the moment but it devolves into endless retries to get the objectives and feels very repetitive trying to get the timing and routes learned. The rewards don't feel worth the work you put in. A new level quickly felt like another new layout I'm going to have to learn through trial and error to pass some strict objectives, rather than a fun new place to skate. Outfits and boards in Ch1 were just twee and very disappointing, feels like a lot of work to get a bunny rabbit T-shirt or some cupcake socks or whatever, all so tiny on-screen when you're playing it as to be meaningless. The endless dialogue dragged the experience down and added little for me, and I bounced off the characters pretty quickly.  Looks nice but it's all a bit too Nickelodeon for me. This will be right up many people's street I'm sure, I wouldn't hesitate to recommend to someone as long as you know what you're getting from the core gameplay ... not my thang though.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun, if you just want to play through all levels its quite relaxed and not too hard, but trying to break allhighscores and completing challenges it gets pretty difficult. fyi: You need a controller to play this, I bought one just for this game and it was definetly worth it! Also in love with the Adventure Time -like art style
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: WOW! This game hits all the marks for me. Art style and direction 10/10. Music 10/10. Gameplay and feel 10/10. Overall experience 10/10. I want to find something negative to say to offset my giddiness. I cannot find it. This is the best game I've played in YEARS. I would love to see a modality where you can build your own courses or play courses built by the community. I think that's the worst thing I can say about it.Bought the game for myself. Then bought it for a couple friends. I am all about this game. I want to find something to complain about. I haven't yet. Attention to detail is unparalleled. I am so impressed. I didn't know people made games like this anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Olli Olli World has deep mechanics and a wonderful soundtrack, a smooth and great colored world and is definitely a clear recommendation for all skate or session fans. The only thing i'd wish is to have an option to completely disable dialouge. And have an endless mode. Other than that, Big Thumps up!
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: This is like if Free Rider and THPS fell head over heels in love and then taught their child that life is all about Combo Mambo.In all seriousness, OlliOlli World is a phenomenal game! It's one of those easy to learn, hard to master types that comfortably scratches an itch that the THPS/THUG games left behind for me many years ago. I haven't played any of the other OlliOlli titles, but this is a killer experience as a first entry player. Between the story levels, the League (a time limited ranking system), and randomly generated tracks based on prerequisites you set, this already feels like it has many, MANY hours of replay value and fresh content. OlliOlli World is a highly stylized 2.5D sidescroller that does it right, stays true to itself, and has a chill soundtrack that fits the world that's been set up for us.If you're looking for a game that you can play to unwind after a long day, as well as scoot to the edge of your seat trying to beat a high score on the leader board, look no further.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: OlliOlli World is a very pleasing atmosphere, decked with charming characters, good vibes and dad jokes. A super chill soundtrack accompanies smooth gameplay and makes for a very enjoyable ride, starting off casual and slowly ramping difficulty as you progress learning new tricks and combo mechanics. An impressive selection of character cosmetics are available with even more to be unlocked through the games optional goals and challenges. Take is slow or make it technical, you'll have fun either way.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: More content than the previous two entries combined. Gameplay is generally the same, and fun. Enjoyed the leaderboards and challenges. However, a couple of questionable stages that don't flow the best. Performance is generally good, but some stages have hitching which seems to be the game itself and not the PC hardware that's running it. Big time recommend Olli Olli World.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically SSX tricky but with borderlands-esque graphics and chill music in the background. The story is kinda meh but I basically skip through it just so I can get back to the game! Its super fun and it feels amazing when you are able to chain together a huge combo, espeically once you learn how to do manuals. It does have a bit of learning curve, in that what I found was I would have my fingers going everywhere trying to land tricks. Highly recommend, and I bought the expacs edition and find that it will be worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game so far.1) Lots of customization options. You have a large wardrobe to choose from at the beginning and you unlock more outfits as you discover new areas. There's lots of unique combinations you can create. I would suggest a possible "save outfit" option in the future so it's easier to alternate between our favorite styles.2) Easy controls. It's not hard to get into the game. You learn new tricks as you play, and you have the opportunity to combine everything you learn into combo streaks. The scoreboard lets you compete globally and locally. I really love the scoreboard and rival aspects of the game because this drives you to replay these levels and beat the higher scores (or at least reach relatively close to the top).3) Difficult challenges. As you progress in the game, the challenges get more... challenging. (Seriously, those challenges are no joke as you get deeper into the game lmao) This offers a drive to keep playing so you can perfect everything, if that's your type of play style. I like these missions because it provides more to do, aside from simply completing the track. You're also rewarded new items.4) Ranked mode. If you really wanna get competitive, there's a ranked mode that refreshes frequently, and you earn rewards every time you climb/maintain a streak.So far, this is my review of the game. Despite my hours, I haven't gotten far into the game because I'm slowly working through completing every challenge from the beginning levels, as well as beating the score of the local NPC heroes. However, I really love the game. The style is cute, the music is chill, there's lots to do, and lots of reasons to keep playing. It's genuinely enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Where to begin...i bought olli cause there really is not another skate game in the market right now beside old skate 3, also never played the other ollis, the look is awesome, yep adventure time skate land, cool. In the beginning its excellent, customize your sweet skater guy or gal, then hit the tracks listening to bumping lo-fi, where in the early ones they focus on getting you familiar with the controls and giving you fairly easy challenges. This in my opinion was where the game shined, i could take my time and just skate the level exploring and tricking to my hearts content, hitting a bee for mike here or pleasing a crowd of tree peeps with a 360 benihanna off a half pipe there, cause most time the challenges were so interwoven with the levels that it wasn't hard nor tedious to accomplish them. OK, fast forward that three worlds in, the game has now turned into somewhat of a dark souls type game, where mike no longer cares about your emotions or physical well being and asks you to perform increasingly difficult challenges, wherein the best i can describe it is you need to complete the run EXACTLY as they play tested it, or you wont complete the challenge, im talking maintaining the same speed, using the correct tricks in certain locations, and choosing split hair decisions about which path to take, and if you don't, restart the whole level. THIS is not fun in my opinion, for some (rouge lite fans) it may be, but now i spend on average 3-6 hours a level and all of that is mostly me continuously restarting the same route, not skating or exploring the level to my hearts content,  until i am lucky enough for all of mikes variables to fall into place, so much so that i need to take my shirt off because of how bad i am sweating, and i am not a sweat lol. The game explains this away as preparing you for Gnarvana, which is where you have ascended the earthly bonds of a mere mortal skater and become godlike in your abilities, and the funniest thing brother, IS THATS EXACTLEY WHAT YOUR GUNNA HAVE TO DO. i have ground a wedge in my controllers stick, from this game, and still have trouble with some of the challenges. Now you can pretty much forgo all challenges and trying to beat local hero scores (which also get tedious) to just skate and have fun like i spoke of, but miss out on i would say half the cosmetics, so who in their right mind would do that. I know what your saying, "GET GOOD", well brother that's the tragedy, most the people that win the online portion of gnarvana AREN'T EVEN THAT GOOD, very rarely if at all have i seen any top players use anything these challenges are trying to make you bottle, just spamming stuff like scorpion in mortal kombat...so in the end it makes me ask, WHAT THE HECK IS THIS TORTURE FOR MIKE, LET ME SKATE. I'm in the 4th world, been working on this level for a day and a half just to beat the second challenge, (haven't even scraped the second hero score) and bubba, i fear the 5th world. NOW, all that said, I AM spending 2 days per level, I AM repeating the same course upwards of 2000 times' I AM still trying in online leagues, why? Two reasons, 1. this is a good game, polished (aside from the flying people in league), and can be extremely mellow and fun, and i am excited to see the new content, did buy gnar pass, and i made it sound impossible, its not, i have completed challenges that had me crying, sweating, screaming that i thought i would put the game down for, and that brings me to #2 when you do finally, after the thousandth time, after the sweat, after the finish line when mike notifies you, you completed a challenge, you are a god, you are tony hawk 360 bennihanaing through space and time, and you feel good as you wipe your face of all the shame and sweat onto the nearest fabric, then you go to the next level and it all starts again, usually more difficult though. so like i said, there is two ways to play, dark souls and sweaty, or adventure time with base cosmetics, i cant say they didn't give you a choice, but it feels like an ultimatum.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: EA Skate controls used to make a colorful platformer more about overcoming obstacles than scores. Loved the first two games and this one takes those systems and improves them by adding less punishment for timing, back and forth maps/paths, and a cartoon aesthetic. Pure flow state "hit restart until I complete the goal." Once the rhythm clicks you can't stop playing.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: This game is best recommended to people who:• ... enjoy arcade skating games  platformers• ... love customizing their character and showing them off to the world• ... may be willing to spend hours to complete hundreds of challenges across tons of levels• ... appreciate having replays so you can look back on your favourite combos (or learn how the pros do them)• ... vibe to a downtempo soundtrack powered by talented indie artists
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Feels good.P.S.: Not sure why this game is 30€ though. Credits roll after at most 5 hours and while there is replay value this is more of your typical casual indie title. Game also really didn't need any "gnarly" characters, just let me skate, dialogue at the beginning of every level is really just annoying although you can tell they tried. Also had about five crashes and one bug where I would see debug messages in the dialogue and couldn't start the level..Gameplay itself is really good though and there are some fun levels I might revisit. Initially this game feels too easy but some of the later levels really challenge you to keep up momentum and timing the jumps just right. Also it's really up to you if you try to perfectly ride the level in one huge combo or just get through with a score of zero.________________________________________UPDATE:Okay, this game has a lot more too offer than it may seem on first sight. Going achievement hunting and doing the extra challenges is really fun and makes you look at aspects of the game you may have overlocked in the first playthrough.Mike's challenges: cute, fun, makes you take a closer look at the levels and some of the mechanics :)Radysus': ABSOLUTELY.BRUTAL: Finish this level without using walls/rails, reach a combo of x90 until the first checkpoint, perfectly time these 10 impossible jumps, skip some parts you will need later, better find some rails between your 3 manuals >;) Oh, and by the way, all tricks must be different too, haha.These challenges are borderline insane but also fun and really take you to the limit of what's possible in this seemingly simple game. I don't believe that ever more than 0.5% players even attempt these challenges, but they are actually great and when you finally make it after the 100th try it's a real "OH, so that IS possible?"-moment. It's the ultimate test of puzzle solving by finding doable routes and mastering the mechanics to the absolute limit. I am still to finish all of them..The leagues where you compete against other people's scores were also a cute feature and they have some neat unlockables.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. The inputs for the tricks are like fighting games, think quarter circles, half circles etc. Beautiful aesthetics, great character customization, insanely hard levels, fun online multiplayer aspect and great replay value.  Took me 60 hours to 100% the game and I'd highly recommend anyone to give this game a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: A 2D arcade skateboarding game with a "story", its fun!Maps feels fresh and not too look-a-like and music is really chill and fitting.Alot of customising and unlockables, every map has challenges that unlock new things and keeps the ones liking a challgenge "grinding" for 100%The only thing I feel could be a downer is the price, maybe more things will be added to make the price more worth it but they also have a "season pass", dunno what you get with that tho..So if you dont feel that 30 euro is worth it you should wait for a sale.Game is overall great tho!
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: I have to give the game a solid thumbs up, it is so fun and challenging in just the right way.  The art style is out of this world, the music is just fantastic, and the gameplay is that easy to learn but hard to master kind of thing that makes it feel like you are really making solid progress.  It also doesn't punish you for wanting to just play and chill, even if you aren't trying to grind for challenges the game is just fun and relaxing to play!  Overall its criminally underrated and I wish more people would give games like this a chance because its clear a lot of care went into making this and it is 100% worth your time!
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Took me around 8 hours or so to get through the main story / levels, quite enjoy the character customization, although they could make some minor tweaks to make it a little easier and remove items you don't have access to and flag new items better.Difficulty level gradually goes up and if you like completing everything including all the challenges you'll probably get a pretty decent amount of time out of this game, especially if you then try and get high scores beyond that.Cutscene / pre-level can be kinda annoying as there is no quick skip for dialogue and you have to hold a button that sometimes does not skip everything to then have to press a button for a prompt before holding to skip again. I paid 15.99 and tbf I think that's about what the full retail price should be, 24.99 is probably a little high.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: fun lil game. Finished it normally and was excited to go back, do all the side stuff and complete it but then i saw the pyramid missions or whatever you unlock after beating the game and i was instantly discouraged. The other side tasks are fine but the pyramid ones are laughably hard. Mind you i did one pyramid mission and said ♥♥♥♥ this. Went to see what other levels pyramid missions were like and i instantly know they would prob take 75% if your overall playtime even tho its only like 1% of the game.despite that it's still a good game
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an action platformer in a similar vein as something like Super Meat Boy or Celeste. You will find yourself playing the same level 10s if not 100s of times trying to perfect your inputs to maintain your speed and build the best score you can. It is very fast paced and several different tricking mechanics that leave a lot of room for personal style and flair (a la Tony Hawk's Pro Skater). There is a natural progression at play here as the levels are designed to require new mechanics at a steady pace, while also being enjoyable to go back play earlier levels once you've honed your skills on the later ones. Even after you have finished all the goals, there is still the leaderboard to chase down, and an entire competitive mode where you have a short time to set scores on new levels.If you played any of the previous Olli games and liked them, then rest assured this is a very similar experience. The devs have done a great job making the game a lot more attractive, but it is still definitely the same base game. It feels a bit more forgiving that Olli Olli 2, not requiring as precise timing for things like landing or spinning. They have also introduced a competitive side with some randomly generated levels if you are into that. Or you can play the random levels solo.Now some negatives. While on the surface there are many items to customize your skater, a lot of them are simply reskins or recolors of each other. It is also disappointing that your options for your own skaters body type boil down to just two sliders whereas the NPC skaters have such personality in their builds and physical features.There are some small issues with hitboxes and too vague descriptions of some of the later goals that can be frustrating to deal with. At times it can feel like you aren't getting a goal because you don't understand what you are supposed to do rather than because you aren't able to do it. There are not enough of these to knock down my recommendation though.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: another addition to the skate genre that just does it so well, goes for the high vibe and laid back almost adventure-time esque stylization and theme rather than the underground gritty look that many other skate games do. super indepth trick system with a lot more mechanics than olli olli 2 with a rotating online ranked system if thats your ideal. soundtrack fits well, and the game isnt interested in punishing you for small mistakes but rather rewarding execution and the variety of tricks you throw out in a run. also really sick level/challenge design, love the freedom of customization for characters as well.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: God this is how you do a sequel. Lots of new features, and simply adding on to the previous installment. I was kind of turned off at first, as the art style had changed from a pretty charming pixel art, to this 3D stuff. But what I found was that it didnt bother me that much, especially with a more dynamic camera. Great Game, If you enjoyed the first one, get this one.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Never played the first OlliOlli, but saw an ad for this and thought it looked good so I picked it up. This is now possibly one of my favourite games of the year so far. Great skill curve, and a decent level of replay value. 100% recommend this game to anyone who enjoys skateboarding or high speed platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Great fluid skating, tricks feel super satisfying. Comes paired with a fun soundtrack and beautiful levels. This is definitely the type of game that truly starts after you beat it. Loads of replayability and the online leagues/procedural worlds keep things interesting. Price is pretty steep for what's being offered. This is essentially a high end mobile game and has no business being priced at 40$; considering it doesn't even have real voice acting. I'd like to see some meaningful free content updates to justify the price tag on this. As it stands I would look for a discounted key or something, but if you're into these types of games it's super worth it and a really fun/challenging experience.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Lives up to the previous game + more. Having played the previous two but barely any time on this game and I know it already slaps. The new art style still possesses the spirit of the previous, still upholding it's own unique characteristics in animations and aesthetics. The game provides unique levels, challenging objectives, precise and finely tuned controls, head-bobbing tunes, and a progression-based, ever-growing inventory of cosmetic customization. This third installment is the best by far. Super stoked to play it!
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastically made game with great skate mechanics, a vast number of tricks, extensive customisation and charming characters to take you through the story. Extra modes and increasingly difficult challenges provide good replay-ability, and the love put into this game is evident. All-in-all the best new new release I've bought in a while. Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: An unique skateboarding experience that feels exhilarating even at simple levels of play, but has incredible potential for high skill expression as well. All alongside an extremely stylish and fun setting and look, and music that is pure vibes. Every level has unique appeal, and challenges, leader-boards and alternate routes make every single one of them worth replaying. An excellent, excellent game.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic flow-based platformer, with just the right balance between too difficult and too easy. The skill ceiling is quite high, high enough that I don't stand a chance of reaching, but the entry level is acceptable. And given enough trial and error you get the hang of it. But there's a lot of trial and error. It's pretty much built into the design of the game.The best part is that each level has multiple (6-8) challenges that feature either various restrictions to the runs or goals to hit during the run. It's quite diverse and can really challenge you.If I were to compare it to something it would be either to something like Cuphead, but replace the combat with challenging skating stunts that require timing and precision. The flow of it also reminds me of Sekiro, especially with regards to timing your moves on the playground. Fortunately, even though it has a high difficulty level and you'll be replaying sections dozens of times to get the perfect timing, you won't be very far from your last checkpoint. So it's quite forgivable in that. Aside from the challenges where it actually asks you to do the whole run without any checkpoints. Those are particularly difficult for very long levels. But with high difficulty comes great satisfaction when you finally pull it off.The setting is fine, as far as the skating world/mythology is concerned, but it also feels a bit too derivative of what Brutal Legend did with metal music, on a much much lower budget. They also tried to create wacky characters but I've mostly ignored those since they're not too remarkable. Of course, that's mostly just superficial flavoring. And can be ignored completely. The art style on the other hand is very beautiful. The levels look fantastic, and some get really wacky.Anyway, if you enjoy flow-based platformers with a good level of challenge I'd highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: The team at Roll7 do it again with OlliOlli World, creating another masterpiece of an indie title jam packed with possibly hundreds of hours of playtime, either in perfecting your skill or mastering every course.The gameplay, while still true to its form, shows a bit of a lower skill floor compared to the likes of OlliOlli 1 and 2, in an effort to make it easier to get into, while still keeping the skill ceiling mighty high for those willing to put in the work.Along with all the fun that one could have, there's a whole slew of customization for your player character, from silly drinking hats all the way down to the type of socks you wear, all unlocked through completing courses or in the online "Gnarvana League"And not to mention the art style makes you feel like you're playing something straight out of Adventure TimeAll in all, this is probably the best indie game this year, very worth the $30 for the amount of fun you're guaranteed to have playing it. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: OlliOlli World is really a very fresh game. Controls for doing tricks is very cleverly done, the levels are not hard to complete but completing the challenges for each level is challenging and very fun. Artstyle, the gameplay and everything about this game is well done. The price of the game is totally worth it and I 10/10 recommend buying this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game, but sadly a current bug is breaking the game for me, manual not working after wall-rides, defeats the purpose of  going after high-scores. Than there is the price, even though it's great fun, the game is pretty 1-dimensional in what it offers - what it offers is great tho, but still, this is a 20bucks title, not more. Would still recommend if the bug is getting fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: While overpriced, this is an excellent game that I could easily recommend to pretty much anyone interested. It takes what the previous OlliOlli titles did, makes it more fun, and slaps on an Adventure Time aesthetic. Even after beating the main campaign there's still a ton of side quests to look forward to, as well as the daily league challenges, which will keep you coming back for at least 30 minutes a day if not more. It can become pretty addicting.It's also nice to know that there's two upcoming DLC expansions on the way, which will add a lot more content to the game - Two new biomes, story, and various unlocks.There is a bit of a learning curve, and while it mostly keeps the same control scheme as the previous two titles, there's a lot more leniency on what is considered a pass vs a slam. This change is absolutely for the better and makes the game feel a lot more arcadey and enjoyable to zone out to.This is just fun. In the ranking of skate games I'd still keep the Tony Hawk series as #1, OlliOlli World at #2, and then Skate 3 would sit in #3.As previously mentioned, the only drawback is the price. I'd recommend seeking out a sale before committing to the purchase. Otherwise I love everything that is here and have had a lot of fun with it so far. I do have to admit I'm heartbroken that the developers are no longer with Devolver Digital, however.My main personal complaint is that I wish there was more online functionality other than just the league challenges, or even local split screen would be nice if paired with remote play together.If you enjoy combo mastery and skating this will scratch the itch.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: So far so fun! Never played the other games, but I enjoy this style of simple to play, hard to master mini challenges. Feels awesome when you get in the flow of things! UPDATE: So, I'm still really enjoying this game but there are some odd quirks to the physics that seem counter-intuitive and can make keeping momentum frustrating. There are certain ways to maintain speed off grinds and wallruns that you eventually get used to and it becomes a non-issue, but the game doesn't seem to make these subtleties clear so it takes experimentation (or looking it up online) to figure out how exactly the physics works. Which wouldn't be so bad if the physics felt more sensible. Again, this is a matter of just learning how the game works and isn't really a negative so much but it can definitely be a source of frustration for beginners.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: olliolli world is a fun high score chaser. if you play either or both of the first two, this is just like it with some big tweaks. mainly wall rides, quarter pipes, multiple lanes, and direction switching on quarter pipes. OOW seems like a much bigger game than the first two, with more levels and scores to chase. i really enjoy who in depth the character creator is. with new items unlocking as you complete challenges. i'm looking forward to completing every last challenge and chasing all of the achievements. 1 &2 were definitely no breeze.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with smooth visuals and a compelling game play cycle. I think the small number of reviews might be indicative of peoples' feelings about the price, especially with the additional season pass. I don't regret my purchase, but it certainly didn't feel like a high-value one either. Still, I love the game and can't fault it when judging it on its own legs.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: A feel good game in a time where they're needed. Sure, it can be tough at times, but none of the tougher stuff is mandatory. You could totally chill and play this without a problem.If you like the older ones, I suspect you'll like this one, too. It's kinda more of the same, but with a fun art style, rad tunes and a light story. My one word of advice is to let yourself get into a flow state. Makes the game even better.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: After coming back to this game after almost a year and now having over 30 hours game time I am now giving an updated review.First time I advise you to avoid doing all of the challenges, only bother doing them if there easy or you feel like it but don't be like me and try to do all the challenges.I started this gaming trying to do every single challenge before I moved on to the next stage and boy was it a mistake. I managed to complete 3 out of 5 stages with all the challenges but once I got to Sketchside I was at my final straw and I already started to get fed up the stage before. The game went from being a fun challenge to damn near broken challenges. I don't believe that they had people test these challenges because whilst yes they can be done, a lot of them are not fun challenges and out right buggy or janky. You need to be so pixel perfect extreme percision to the point that it's just frustrating and not fun.It's a shame because I really wanted to %100 the game but I realised all it would do is stress me out and wouldn't even be gratifying.Despite that rant I still recommend the game, infact I would give the game a 7/10. If you play this game avoiding the challenges you could beat it pretty quickly and have some fun. The online can be fun too, but playing this game seriously and trying to beat the challenges is awful. I would have given the game a 10 if not for the challenges late game.TLDR Great soundtrack, great art, great customization, but many buggy levels and the challenges get worse as you go along. Late game sucks. 7/10 but it could have been a 10.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: idk i like it but its very different from olliwood and the first game. definitely longer and more dense in content but leans toward being a more complete game as opposed to the intense arcade-y nature of the first two, which obviously comes with benefits and drawbacks. the game is also definitely mechanically different, the timings for tricks and manuals are slightly different (and off, in my opinion) and they removed revert manuals, which was a very sad realization. Late moves and grabs make up for it though. The league stuff is a good time, but its also the only multiplayer mode as of now, a huge step down from daily grind and splitscreen.This game feels less like a step forward and more like four steps to the side. It's fun sometimes and a little irritating at others, which sucks because they can clearly make solid, fluid gameplay and make it work well. maybe it has to grow on me but there's a lot of subtle differences in gameplay which is drastic for a tech-heavy series like olli olli, not even mentioning the extremely different tone and art style World has embraced.Why can't i customize my guy to look like the guy from Olliwood? The 7 shirt and red hat is iconic.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: First time i heard about this series, the trailers were amazing and i decided to give it a try.Absolute gem right there ! From the art style to the music an the addictive gameplay, oh my god, i'm hooked !Just buy this game if you like "easy" to pick up and hard to master style of game.Again an aboslute gem and the music, can we have more mix please ? MORE MUSIC <3 They are incredible too ! Favourite so far is Adam Swim - Can't Sleep :)
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: i really love this game!great soundtrack (including a kinda nostalgic song from 2015 which surprised me when i heard it)mf  gameplay, gives me the same feeling that old Trials games did in the "hard but fair racing platformer" with the cool-ass input of games in the vein of Skate. really love itin my opinion beautiful artstyle, especially environments - and fun character designs as well, being pretty lighthearted.the 40$ price tag is a bit steep, but i'd say it's worth it. do recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: What a feeling it was to play this for the first time!I love the first two games but this hits in whole another level - it seems like it is made for everyone from kids to hc OlliOlli fanatics. It is so easy to pick up and play - after halfway through it get a bit more challenging but I think that is the whole point that.I love the new graphical style and chill vibe the soundtrack gives. This game just puts you in instant good mood.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. Everything is so good. The graphics are marvelous, colorful. I love that you can personalize almost everything for your character.The flow of the tricks and the map design are really appealing and smooth. But don't get me wrong it's not simple. "Easy to learn, hard to master" is what describe the gameplay the best imo. And finally, the storytelling strangely (or not) reminds me of my years of skateboarding : The philosophy of freedom, the pride of mastering a new trick and the feels of just zoning out with friends at different spots.Probably one of the coolest indy game of this year. I definitely recommend it
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: pretty great game honestly, theres the casual side of just playing through the levels for the lore and then theres the challenge side which are fun and difficult, the character customization is amazing and intuitive, and the art style is very similar to adventure time which is a show i adored, overall so far the game has been wonderful and exciting absolutely recommend
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review: Slick to play with responsive controls. One of those games where it's not hard to play at a basic level but it has a real depth to its controls and the stunt-chaining you can do to get those really high scores. The level generator is a nice touch as are the async competitions (though in my first one I did not fare too well lol). Looks like there are plenty of character customisation options and the cartoon aesthetic looks cool too.
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.user: H O T L I N E
_childDocuments_.review: This game is rad. If you like chill, lo-fi beats, skateboarding, silly puns, and a fun challenge then this game  IS  for you. Skate for fun. Skate for achievements. Skate for hours. Is it worth $39.99? Honestly, no... Maybe $15 - $25ish. I feel like $40 is a little too much, but it is a great game...And it's helping me bridge the gap between now and Skate 4. Buy this game and have a good time!
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

_childDocuments_.review:
OlliOlli World is a bold new skateboarding action-platformer that’s bursting with personality. Flip and flow through the vivid and vibrant world of Radlandia, meeting colorful characters as you grind, trick, and air your way to discover the mystical skate gods on your quest for Gnarvana. Traverse a delightful and weird world as you take on missions, challenges, and make new friends along the way. Customize your character’s looks, tricks, and style while you experience explorable levels with multiple paths that provide an array of opportunities for player expression. Challenge the world in Leagues or dare a friend to beat your best tricks on one of millions of sharable levels. Experience the accessibility, depth, and player freedom as you dive into the signature flow state gameplay of OlliOlli World.

OlliOlli World marks the third entry in the critically-acclaimed OlliOlli series from Roll7, the BAFTA and multi-award-winning independent studio.

 

Key Features:

• Welcome to Radlandia!: Take a trip across a lush skateboarding utopia that is filled to the brim with eccentric characters and vibrant locations that are begging to be explored. Find your grind in Inflatable Alley or blaze down Los Vulgas to discover new paths, fresh side quests, rad rewards, and epic trick opportunities. All perfectly complemented by a hand-picked compilation of IDM and Electronica tracks. 

• Play at your level: Super tight controls combine with highly refined gameplay to ensure a silky smooth ride. Not a Pro? Don’t worry – OlliOlli World welcomes you with open arms, allowing new players to tear down streets and pull off sick method grabs without fear of faceplanting the curb. Think you’ve got what it takes? Achieve mastery through millions of unique levels in sandbox mode or compete against rivals around the globe in leagues with a hugely deep combo system with over 100 moves to master and combine in your battle for the highest score.

• Freedom of expression: Cruise through Radlandia's epic skate-haven and prove your skills to unlock special rewards that let you customize your character’s looks, tricks and style. Want to skate in your flip flops… go for it. Want to wear a bumble bee onesie …ok then… no judgement. In OlliOlli World as long as you’re on board anything goes!
_childDocuments_.name: OlliOlli World

name: The Wonderful 101: Remastered
detailed_description: The Wonderful One: After School Hero (Part 1) Free DLC Get ready for a unique side-scrolling experience in the world of The Wonderful 101: Remastered! This free DLC lets you enjoy a brand new episode in which you experience Luka's story! As the latest member of the CENTINELS, new recruit Luka delivers remarkable achievements. What challenges did he need to overcome to become the prestigious Wonder Goggles? This is a story of love, battle, and growth. Experience Luka's journey to becoming a full-fledged hero! The Wonderful One: After School Hero (Part 2) - Slated for release the following week on Friday, May 26, 2023. Includes the second part of The Wonderful One: After School Hero experience. Important note: This DLC was made possible by reaching the stretch goal of our February 2020 crowdfunding campaign. We would like to extend our sincerest gratitude to the 33,199 amazing fans who supported us on this journey. Time Attack Free DLC A new way to experience the 100-hero Unite Action spectacular The Wonderful 101: Remastered has just made the scene in the form of a free DLC game mode! Key Features Beat stages as fast as possible and keep an eye on the new Record Gauge to see how you're stacking up against your personal best. Non-essential cutscenes let you blast through your stage of choice stress-free. Upload your best time online and see how you compare to Wonderful Ones from around the world! Wonder-Size Cadet Demo The Wonder-Size Cadet Demo for The Wonderful 101: Remastered is out now, featuring hidden team member Wonder-Bayonetta! Enjoy a Wonder-Size TWO HOURS of content, including Platinum-level epic boss battles and a lot of in-game goodies for free! A lot of bonuses like in-game currency and a selection of support items are also available from the start of the demo, so that even beginners can set off on this dynamic adventure fully equipped. Best of all, you can transfer save data from the demo to the full version and pick up right back up! Wonderful Codes Version 1.0.3 added the 'Wonderful Code' option to the in-game menu. Search for the 7 Wonderful Codes to get special bonuses such as Wonder-Bayonetta and more! The codes can be found in the News tab in the Community Hub here on Steam, or on the official PlatinumGames website. Be sure to find them all! About the Game A team of heroes from around the world must UNITE to protect the earth from vicious alien invaders! This band of 100 Wonderful Ones works together using their fantastic abilities to create a variety of forms. Whether it be a giant fist or a sharp blade, they’ll use their wits and power to overcome the enemy’s pitfalls and perils! And the final member of this team of courageous heroes—is you. From PlatinumGames, creators of the Bayonetta series, ASTRAL CHAIN, NieR:Automata, and Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance, comes The Wonderful 101: Remastered! This game will be PlatinumGames' first self-published title, and is a powered-up version of The Wonderful 101, originally released by Nintendo on September 15th, 2013 as a Wii U exclusive. The Wonderful 101: Remastered offers the unprecedented ability to control 100 heroes at once, with the flowing controls and dynamic action that are the PlatinumGames hallmark. It’s all brought together by a pulse pounding tale of heroic bravery and friendship standing tall against evil, and is PlatinumGames’ most ambitious offering to date. Hideki Kamiya, director of The Wonderful 101, has supervised this remaster and added numerous improvements to ensure that this game can be more easily and thoroughly enjoyed by all and on various platforms, and with improved visuals, framerate, and loading time for an enhanced experience on all fronts. Key Features Over 100 unique and dazzling, each with their own backstories and emblems! Change weapons in a flash with the “Unite Morph” system! Draw shapes to switch between swords, whips, hammers, and more to battle with strategy and flair! Unite Morphs can be more than just weapons! Build hang gliders and bridges to cross chasms, and bounce and blast your way to great heights! Use your smarts as well as your strength to solve puzzles and persevere! Don’t forget—a hero’s true calling is protection! Rescue the citizens you come across and your bravery will inspire them to UNITE UP! For a limited time, of course. Your missions will take around the world! Through cities, across the ocean floor, deep in the jungle, and to a host of exciting locations! Grab your controllers and try out 'Multiplayer Missions', a shared-screen co-op mode that can be enjoyed by up to four players at once! Whether you'll work together for the mission or compete for the highest score is up to you and your friends.
