short_description: Lead an army of 100 Wonderful Ones from around the world in this Unite Action spectacular!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game for YEARS back when it released on the Wii U. I never thought in a million years that The Wonderful 101 would have an official PC release. And yet here we are. So how does it hold up?Maybe I'm being biased here but I genuinely believe this is PlatinumGames and Hideki Kamiya's magnum opus. The combat system is extremely intricate and complex but damn does it feel satisfying to master. This is NOT a cutesey wootsey Pikmin-style adventure game. This is very much an action game that ranks up there with games such as Devil May Cry and Bayonetta (2 other games Hideki Kamiya is responsible for. Go figure.). This is a game that does NOT hold your hand whatsoever nor does it do any spoonfeeding. You're gonna get punished. You're gonna get destroyed. You're gonna get nothing but consolation prizes along the way. You're probably also gonna get frustrated with the weapon switching gimmick and say the controls are bad and that it should've stayed on the Wii U where it belongs.BUT!Stick with the game and spend enough time learning to master the controls and you'll tap into an experience so cathartic that it's actually really difficult for me to put into words exactly just how fun it is to discover all the cool and intricate things you can do on the fly. This is a game that ALLOWS you to be stylish provided you got the skills for it. It employs all the stuff you've seen Dante and Bayonetta pull off and then some. Juggle combos, air dashing, STINGERS GALORE.In The Wonderful 101, you control 100 super heroes who are able to morph into different weapons by lining up into their respective shapes by drawing with the right stick. Circle for fist, line for sword, a right angle for gun, etc.etc. At first it may feel overly complex (and to be fair, it is) but drawing the shapes is a matter of doing the gesture, not about precision. If anything, drawing the shapes would be more comparable to that of inputting a command in a fighting game. It's a gimmick that is extremely well thought out because the game takes into account what shape you did and how big you did it and whether you summoned it for yourself or passed it off to another hero for support. All of the characters that represent each weapon have their own charming and adorable personality.Due to the nature of the drawing system, you have a whole lot more freedom in the combat than most other action games. In other action games, you usually swap between weapons at the push of a button but in order to make it less confusing for players, you usually only swap between 2 weapons (Bayonetta). Or, in some cases, if you have ALL weapons available, it's a matter of tapping the button quickly to get to your preferred weapon but if you accidentally pass it, you gotta constantly tap more to get back to it (Devil May Cry). In The Wonderful 101, switching is only done by drawing. No weapon wheel, no scrolling list, no menu. Nope, if you can think it, you can draw it. This can lead to moments where you can do just about anything you want provided you are skillful enough to gesture the needed glyphs. Want to punch an enemy into the air with your fists, switch to guns for bullet juggling before coming down with the hammer to slam them down to the ground? Yeah, you can do that. Want to keep an enemy stuck in slow motion with bomb so you can switch to whip and pick them up, toss them aside and then freeze them with claws? Sure, go ahead. Have fun.All the enemies in the game are beautifully designed too. True to Kamiya's nature, the enemies all come in a variety of agressiveness, some being so reckless you'll need to pay attention to their telegraphing, from the movement they make to the sounds they make, in order to properly counter their attacks. Enemies come in a variety of different sizes and shapes. From a walking giant robot to an armored tank to a giant metallic turtle. All the enemies can be handled with any weapons you got but they've been cleverly designed in such a way that each one's got a weakness to certain weapons that you must discover and take advantage of.It should be noted that since this is a Kamiya game, expect to run into a lot of mini-games. And I mean A LOT. You think Bayonetta had too much? Boy, you're in for a ride. Look, there's nothing wrong with the mini-games themselves as each one lasts just long enough for you to grasp its rules and controls before getting right back to the Wonderful 101 action, but since you're constantly being ranked for these segments just the same as the main game, it can get very frustrating trying to perfect these arcade bits, especially when you set out to do a Pure Platinum run. Some of these mini games can be overwhelming and down right punishing, even on the hardest difficulty where you can die in just one hit! Good lord. For what it's worth, all the mini-games feel just like their classic counterparts. You'll be playing stuff like Punch-Out, Zaxxon, Space Harrier and Star Fox, all for the sake of trying to save the world, so prepare yourself and hopefully you got some good arcade skills to survive.The game's visuals aren't exactly the most amazing thing you'll see. The visual aesthetic employs a heavily inspired American Golden Age comics of the 1950's with the Japanese Tokusatsu action, ranging from Power Rangers (Super Sentai) to Kamen Rider with a chibi artstyle that heavily resembles Viewtiful Joe (yet another game Hideki Kamiya is responsible for. Go figure.). The game feels like you're peeking into a world made of toys, with the characters having a shiny plastic look to them, with the camera using a tilt shift effect to sell that look altogether. The texture aren't the most amazing thing here. In fact, given how this is a game that originally came from the Wii U, there's a whole lot of blurriness everywhere (even some text and screenshots) and it's a bit baffling that they'd be calling this a Remaster when it really is just a straight port. To be fair, I wasn't asking for the game to be remade but you'd think the Remastered title would imply that the game was given an extra amount of polish, which it doesn't.For the PC port, I personally haven't had much issues experiencing the game however I've seen how it runs for other folks. Depending on your rig and resolution settings, you'll probably encounter some weird, unintended hiccups. To somewhat quote someone here on Steam, this port feels like it's being held together with Elmer's Glue. It makes me extremely sad that my most favorite game in the universe has a very shoddy port and while I am one of the lucky few to have a game that runs without any problems, this really falls into the "your mileage will vary" category.As of this review's posts, the bugs that I've encountered include enemies ignoring bomb/hero time effects, the multiplayer camera being extremely buggy and input commands not behaving properly. Another big issue is the game being locked at 59fps. Now, for me, 59fps is a GODSEND because the original Wii U version ran soooo poorly, I would've been OK with the game just being locked at 30fps. 59fps is, no joke, the best thing the game could ever have BUT I know 60fps would've been a million times better and it actually does make me upset that PlatinumGames promised a locked 60fps experience when that's not entirely the case. Thankfully we do have fanmods that fix this little problem and I only hope that PlatinumGames will eventually patch this game to run exactly how it was intended to run.Final verdict: Listen, I love this game a lot. There is nothing that's gonna keep me away from enjoying it. I only hope that if you do decide to jump in, you keep an open mind. This is not a game where you can just pick up and start getting Platinums right off the bat. It's a game that requires time, practice and patience to nail the combat system and if you're willing to go the distance, you'll find a game that gives you a whole lot more in return.
_childDocuments_.name: The Wonderful 101: Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: Take the relentlessly punishing, yet rewarding combat/mechanics of an action game like Bayonetta, a dash of Okami's drawing, and the platforming of Viewtiful Joe.  This is arguably Hideki Kamiya's finest game yet.That helps give an idea of the game's creativity but it doesn't even begin to scratch the surface.Here you have a game that respects your intelligence, yet demands you to take your time to learn what it has to offer. Learning how to dispose of tough enemies with the arsenal of moves provided, while also knowing how to move/keep your team together is satisfying, and fun as all hell. The characters and humor throughout the story is also great, especially if you grew up enjoying Sentai/Power Rangers as a kid.If you're a fan of action games, you would be doing yourself a disservice by not playing this game, especially on each higher difficulty.At one point in time this game seemed like it was doomed to stay on a console that hardly anyone bought.Now that it's on PC, it's a definite must have if you were to ask me.Would save Earth using the  again, and again.

_childDocuments_.review: Kamiya's magnum opus, in all the good and bad ways possible.A hack and slash with a story about family and revenge, it's pretty unlike anything else I've played, a weird mix between DMC/Bayonetta, Pikmin, Viewtiful Joe, and Okami with a load of minigames ranging from shmups to a punch-out clone to break up the action.The game doesn't really hold your hand and tell you what to do, it's a learning experience from beginning to end and the first playthrough is basically a giant tutorial, because like most of Kamiya's other games, the later difficulties start off right where the previous one ends with enemies formerly appearing at the end of the game being placed right near the start.The tone and humor is comparable to a sentai show mixed with some western superhero elements and the voice work is great, it balances goofy and serious moments well. The story is engaging from beginning to end and the game has one of the best finales I've experienced in media.The minigames are very hit or miss, and Kamiya went all out on them for this game, every operation has them in some form or another. The shmup and rail shooter segments can be very frustrating and long-winded while the couple of punch-out bosses are fantastic. Either way they're there whether you like them or not.As of the time of the review, the game definitely runs better than it did on the Wii-U on pretty much any computer, but there are bugs here and there. The camera is in the wrong place at times when you're playing above 1080p, there's some visual glitches with character's suits and masks, and I encountered a crash at the end of the game, still a much better experience than playing on a Wii-U or trying to emulate.Overall an absolutely fantastic game even with some technical issues and iffy mini-game.

_childDocuments_.review: At first this game can seem very inaccessible due to its abnormal controls and original home on the Wii U. Hopefully this review will clear up some misconceptions as well as highlight, in short, what makes this game so incredible. First lets address what I see as the most common criticism, the controls. The game uses a 'drawing mechanic' where, using the right stick you draw a shape on the floor to switch weapons. Each weapon has its own unique basic shape, e.g. the fist is selected by drawing a circle and the sword is selected by drawing a line. On the original Wii U version you could draw these shapes directly onto that systems touch pad. This leaves many with the idea that this was how the game has, or at least is intended, to be played. This is incredibly false, the analogue stick is honestly the preferred control as it allows for quicker inputs and removes the need to move you hand away from the face buttons each time. The drawing mechanic works more like a fighting game input, and boils down to quick and distinct motions that are made to switch weapons. However I don't want to diminish the complexity of the system, which give the game incredible mechanical depth with how your drawing interacts with enemies, where you have to consider your spacing and surroundings to decide which weapons are best suited for the scenario. Now the question is,  Personally i can't speak for the keyboard and mouse controls having played the entire game on a 360 controller, so if you are concerned about that then play the demo and see for yourself, sorry that I cant help with this one.However the second more prevalent issue is with people not giving the controls enough time and investment to learn them properly. I don't mean that in an elitist 'git gud' way, personally I struggled with the drawing controls myself, finding them at best a moderate gimmick, and at worst an unresponsive mess. Well I was very wrong and after a couple of hours it just clicked. Not only did I figure out how to much more easily draw the shapes, but also the mechanic's place in the combat, which changed weapon swapping from an option in a menu to another layer of depth which endlessly rewards high-level play with an infinitely high skill ceiling, whilst being one of the most recently innovative additions to the genre. It something that WILL take some getting use to, but the result is such a rewarding experience with a combat system with hidden tricks and secrets waiting to be discovered, and when you do the satisfaction of intuitively discovering, then regularly using it is incredible. Having played [SEE ABOVE] hours of this game I am still excited to find a new strategy to taking out an enemy. Having to sacrifice the right stick for drawing, the camera is a top down view of your little heroes. The only input you can give to the camera is a simple zoom in and out, which you will always want to be zoomed out. The lack of a movable camera may alert some but the camera will always place you in the middle of the screen, allowing you (most of the time) full view of all the enemies in the battle. You don't have to worry about babysitting a camera and instead keeps the focus on the action. Apart from that I should mention a distracting auto zoom when fighting very few enemies, which fortunately doesn't impact the enjoyment for the game but is a flaw nonetheless. Bear in mind the only character in your team that can take damage is the leader, and they will be circled with a big icon. Didn't expect much from the story, it's not really why I play action games. Going this and similar games I expect shallow characters and overall cheesiness in service to the core gameplay. Keep this is mind when I say  What you get is a charming romp with a likeable team fighting comically evil villains. It is not entirely without depth but only about a couple inches deeper than a puddle.Many make with rightfully criticise the issues with the port, the slightly changed music is a minus, but I really must clarify that this game feels absolutely fine to play, and while you can definitely tell it was a Wii U game, it has no major impact on the PC version. The controls did get some unnecessary minor tweaks it still plays perfectly fine and I will probably add and change this review over time to better illustrate my love for this game. Right now I am going for 100% and can confidently say it's by favourite game of all time. Whilst absolutely not a perfect game (looking at you Tetris), this game just feels so passionate and creative. Exploring so many mechanics and executing them all with a level of perfection and finesse unseen in the genre, I just want to congratulate Platinum Games. Before I go I want to give a few tips to better aid the experience and get you sailing smooth asap I'm leaving the comment open so please leave any question below, and any criticism of the game and my review. I will happily answer them.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: Although this game is a Remaster and port, this review will look at this version’s own merits.The Wonderful 101: Remastered is an action game revolving around controlling an army of 100 heroes in battle to defend Earth from alien invaders. You’ll have to use your wits and reflexes to get the most out of their signature Wonder moves in this action-packed and stylish game by Platinum! Although the premise of the story doesn’t reinvent the wheel, Platinum has added its proprietary Platinum coating to it to give it a very silly yet very bombastic feel. You’ll follow Wonder Red and his team as they trek across the globe to defend the Earth from the invading Geathjerk forces. How far can heroism and teamwork take you? What is worth fighting for? Is humanity worth saving? These questions and more are explored throughout the 9 Operations (around 27 total levels). The overall story is very reminiscent of superhero and super sentai shows (e.g. Power Rangers, Kamen Rider) complete with overly verbose character reintroductions, a narrator that occasionally drones on, cool one-liners and deliciously cheesy melodrama. The story also pokes fun of said tropes, making it much more tongue-in-cheek. For example, characters may start moving around as the narrator gives exposition or a character might slip and fall their way off screen in an epic moment. Overall, it was a really fun journey.This is Platinum’s wheelhouse. Their games have a very high skill ceiling and gratifying, slick and visceral combat. Nonetheless, as someone who has only played a small handful of Platinum games, I was apprehensive when beginning the game. Admittedly, there were a lot of times when I felt frustrated and defeated due to my skill level. However, the overall gameplay is fantastic and kept me coming back for more.The game focuses on Wonder Morphing- transforming your fellow Wonders into weapons to fight the Geathjerk forces. Wonder Red’s is Unite Hand- a giant fist that can pulverize enemies. Wonder Blue’s is Unite Sword, capable of longer slashes and hitting multiple opponents. There are over 8 to discover and play with.   To transform your Wonders, you use the Wonder Liner. Drawing certain shapes on the screen with the Wonder Liner equips the corresponding weapon. For example, to use Unite Hand, I draw a circle which turns red to indicate a valid shape. The Wonder Liner uses your allies as “fuel”, so using more means you get stronger Wonder Morphs. You also require energy to Morph, so combat is a thrilling balancing act of resource management and skillful play. Morph accuracy can be hit-or-miss sometimes due to how the game interprets your drawings.  However, with enough muscle memory I was able to usually get what I wanted on the first try.   Each enemy has a distinct moveset which makes them all challenging to fight. Even basic grunts might shoot at you from off screen if you leave them alone for too long. The simple joy of stringing together combos and doing perfect dodges is even better when up against a varied enemy roster. The camera can be very claustrophobic at times which made navigation difficult if not annoying. You can zoom out, but not having a simple camera distance option is annoying.Miniboss enemies are rather frequent and provide a nice chunk of difficulty. It may be annoying trying to figure out how to approach a specific enemy, but once it clicks and you get in the zone, the feeling you get is quite wonderful as you dismantle them.The boss fights are both spectacles and very satisfying with their own unique gimmicks and strategies. Granted, some hinge entirely on mini-game (which there are quite a lot of) to succeed. You may have to do a shoot-‘em-up section to challenge a huge boss or even a Punch Out!-like game to duel a lone enemy officer. These typically don’t outlive their welcome and provide a break from the core gameplay. Granted, there might be a few that take some time to get used to. There are also some platforming and puzzle sections to test your thinking and observation skills. Being a Wonderful is more than just beating baddies!The game definitely has a steep learning curve, but getting better at it gives a really satisfying feeling of triumph.There is so much more to discuss, but please check out the demo to see for yourself! It’s 1 entire Operation, so give it a test drive to see if it’s up your alley. Words can't adequately convey how it really feels to play the game and even the demo is just a sliver of what you can expect. The overall art style is very unique. Each character model is like a glossy action figure. On one hand, it gives everyone a very distinct and memorable look. On the other, it is also quite low-res. Regardless of both, having an army of toys at your command brings out a very child-like Saturday morning cartoon feel that can’t be found anywhere else.There is a wide variety of levels to discover ranging from typical adventure game locales to more weird and unique ones. The overall art direction is a real pleasure to take in. The trademark Platinum QTEs are also on point here. There is a lot of amazing jaw-dropping action sequences and one that made me burst out laughing near the end of the game.Another one of the Platinum big hitters, the soundtrack for the game is phenomenal. Everything has a very dynamic feel to it, truly making it feel like this is a superhero game. From rousing lyrical ballads about the Wonders to thrilling and intense boss music, I was always in the mood the game wanted me in for the scene. Sound effects are also well-done. Gameplay feels that much more gratifying when you get nice audio feedback from everything. I played with the English dub and it was overall pretty good. It has a campy feel to it that makes it really authentic to the source material. Overall, the game ran solidly. However, I had 2 CTD’s in my 16 hours. Fortunately, the saves still worked after relaunching the game. This is definitely annoying given how sparse save points are and how arduous some rooms can be. The overall graphical options are also quite lacking for a PC port. I was honestly nervous picking up the title with the cult status it has, but I am glad I did. My hand wasn’t held on Normal, but the addictive gameplay of stringing combos and dodging hits kept me motivated. Accompanied with a wacky yet heartful story, epic audio design and a hyper-stylized visual aesthetic, this is one game I won’t forget. For fans of action games and superheroes, this game is a must-get.Earth needs a hero, but it has 100 wonderful ones to save it. Would you do them the honors of being their plus one?
_childDocuments_.name: The Wonderful 101: Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: when i say that this game saved my life, i mean it in every sense of the word. this game holds such a deeply important and foundational part of my being, and i truly can't recommend it enough. for everything that it's done for me, i firmly believe it can do for everyone who plays. our story begins with a rag-tag team of heroes one hundred strong, battling it out with otherworldly threats every other day to decide the fate of the earth. as the game progresses, you get a chance to see the many ways they interact with each other and the world around them. it's well paced and has plenty of twists & turns along the way. replaying the game all the way through will give you context you would have otherwise missed, to boot. this game is a fun and unique experience initially crafted for the wiiU, with the main crux of the gameplay being the unite morph feature; wonderful ones link together in single file line, creating the wonder-liner. by drawing shapes, you can morph your allies into weapons, objects, tools and more. the best way i can think of to describe the gameplay is something akin to super sentai pikmin, what with how you command an army of bite-sized heroes to do what you want. now before anything, what issues do i have with this game? quite literally only one. and it only applies to this remasterthe gameplay translates well onto other platforms, with the sole exception of the fact that the dual screen is clunkily implemented. while on its home console it would be as simple as looking down, the single-screen adaptation of this game brings with it challenge. most of the time you either need to have the screen brought up with a button combination, or have the main screen shrunk off to the side to make room for the sub screen. neither method is particularly well done, but it's honestly decent enough for the purpose it serves. most of the time the main screen is all you need, but it's in those finicky (and honestly gimmicky) moments that it becomes an issue. aside from that, everything else in this game is absolutely stellar. the characters are well fleshed out and engaging, the story is easy to follow with genuinely intriguing beats, and the gameplay is unlike anything else i've seen. by far, this game has some of my favourite mechanics in any video game.combat flows smoothly and rapidly, divided into operations (sections) that provide ample opportunity for things like speedrunning and perfecting your craft. if there's a level you enjoy, you can work at it over and over again to earn the prestigious pure platinum ranking at the end of the level. you can repeat any mission at any time, with most being split into 3 operations. you must play through each operation from the beginning, though; so going through in one straight shot is the only method of grinding out difficult parts. if collection is more your speed, the game provides for you as well; collectables are rife in this game, providing you with lore, gallery pieces, achievements, hidden surprises, and much more. crafting is a smaller part, but it provides you items to use in levels once you have collected enough resources. the game rewards you for exploring through these things. slow or fast, whatever you want; the wonderful 101 provides and accommodates. in that gameplay, there is also room for customization. finding your main and building a kit that works for you is part of the charm. the progression of this kit is resource-based, but well implemented. the crucial bits of the base kit are cheap, and any upgrades to those scale accordingly. now, onto what i said earlier. this game genuinely did save my life. i was 11 in 2013. if it wasn't for the wonderful 101, i would not have been around to celebrate my 20th this year. it's hard to believe it's been that long since the darkest point in my life, but i'm a testament to the fact that awful times can and will get better with a little help. i won't go into detail, but the only joy i found came in watching nintendo trailers with my brother. i think we used to watch them in the 3ds eshop. but lo and behold, the trailer for the wonderful 101 showed up one day. i was obsessed right from the get-go. a team of super heroes that work with and rely upon one another in such an intimate way to save the entire earth... something about it struck me. i watched that trailer over and over and over again, every single day. and when the wonderful 101 extended trailer came out, i watched that into the ground as well. i can still quote it word for word. i played that game every single day. it was my light. when things were bad, i knew the wonderful ones would have my back. i felt like part of something. i genuinely did. the opening cinematic reminded me of that every time i booted up the game. "i knew we forgot someone; you." it gives me chills to this very day. i would seek out any and all fan art, i wrote fan fiction placing a gaudy little self insert into the world of the wonderful ones, i based everything i did around it. it became my life. it was my hope. it was everything to me. that little light at the end of the tunnel. this is a game where the characters are accepted as they are, and regardless of their flaws they were still a part of the team. their unique abilities become something that is worked with, instead of repressed. they still contributed something to the world regardless of what they were. whether they were a teacher, a student, a prodigy, a detective or an artist, they all became equal when they put on the mask. for those unaware, "masking" is a neurodivergent term that essentially equates to pretending to be "normal" in the eyes of others. it involves suppressing your symptoms and ignoring what comes naturally to you. masking costs a lot of energy to maintain. when you let the mask down, when you doff what is expected of you... that is where the true, authentic self is. the symbolism of the mask in this game is present; in the mask, there comes a level of detachment... yet there also comes power in letting that mask down, as you'll see later on in the story. i experienced all of this far before my diagnosis with autism, but i feel that my experience with the wonderful 101 was a major cornerstone in understanding myself and the way i interact with the world because of it. it resonated with me for that exact purpose. everyone in the game is flawed, they interact with their surroundings in a unique way... yet they are not shunned for it. in fact, it becomes a mechanic, this unique individual contribution. this was my first true special interest, and it persists to this day.the wonderful 101 is about finding yourself. finding others who, despite any differences, appreciate and respect you. and it's about working as one despite these differences. more than anything, it's about pushing past the trauma you have experienced, and becoming better for it. over and over again, characters are shown to be broken, hampered, hurt by their past... yet always, no matter what, they push past. they find their stride, and walk that path with power and confidence. finding who you are in relation to your unique circumstances, that's how you grow. that's where true power is. unity, found family, appreciation. that's what this game is at its core. the explosions and supermassive monsters are the fun little cake on top, but that true meaning is there if you look. and it means something different to everyone who plays. that's the magic of this game. replaying and rediscovering this game that means so much to me is like a dream come true. and now that it's accessible to more people than ever before, i urge you to play. i urge you to become a part of the wonderful 101. it might just give you what it gave me all those years ago. putting it into words is nearly impossible, but i've done what i can here. it's something truly wonderful.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this remaster on Kickstarter and have been playing it for the past couple weeks. This review is of version 1.0.0 so far.Platinum's game of a million mechanics, The Wonderful 101 is a character action game of the "what do you mean this is a character action game? It looks nothing like one!" variety that encourages mastering the depths of its weird combat like God Hand, Vanquish, and Lucah Born of a Dream. It's a game that has like 5 different types of progression system to try and not overwhelm you and a game that references seemingly every sci fi B TV show and movie ever made in Japan and some outside of it (like possibly UFO for Alice?) and it somehow all works, giving a lot of ways for you to master it, while being immensely satisfying. It's also the longest game in its genre surprisingly so if you've ever wanted a like... 17 hour for 1 playthrough Char Act game this is the one, albeit the very weird one.So how about the porting... well it's complicated.In terms of core gameplay the port is on point, forget the gamepad, unlike Okami the control stick is the preferred way to play here with its speed that can be upgraded even further, just try to think of the drawing as visualized fighting game inputs if you will. Though I have seen a few glitches where I would use a multi unite only for the user to just stand there, and then when I recall them for their morph to still be stuck to them even when they are disbanded. I'm not sure if that was in the original version or not, but it seems rare, I only saw it about 10 hours in, though I saw it a few times in a row when it did happen.In terms of performance the game runs much better than I expected on my computer... If you install this patch to fix the frame limiting and pacing that makes it play at 59fps initially and then jump up and down across the hours left on until it ends up at an unplayable 120fps on hour 20....And now we get on to the porting bugs and limitations. It's pretty much a mess, and I wouldn't be surprised if it was rushed. If you increase the resolution beyond 1080p the depth of field apparently doesn't scale well. Since this is running on DirectX9 there is no multimonitor support so you can't recreate the separate gamepad screen. All the graphical settings are limited to resolution,  HDR on/off (which is rendering rather than display, so it doesn't support your HDR monitor), and a Low/Medium/High setting where High is the WiiU's setting. You can't adjust shadows, antialiasing, or depth of field separately or even turn antialiasing off so there's really not much control or much to push here. To list the problems that must be fixed before we start adding DLC:NEW 1. Fix the invert X-Axis and invert Y-Axis options. The Invert X-Axis option inverts the Y-Axis and the invert Y-Axis option inverts the X-axis on all parts where the camera/vehicle movement comes into play! Please swap them to work properly. (How did that get past testing?)2. Add controller rebinding (really dang important for a game that controls this dang unusually with this many QTEs in it, especially on consoles and for people with motor disabilities.) This is also an issue with Switch controllers as the 3 presets and start/select button switch don't recreate the layout on WiiU if you use Steam's "Swap A/B and X/Y to match Nintendo layout" and not using that makes the QTE prompts wrong3. Add DS4 prompts (Not sure why the game notifies you not to use ds4windows and instead use Steam if it's not going to have DS4 prompts, once again important for QTEs)4. Fix the frame limiter5. Make all cutscenes skippable (the unlimited form cutscenes are not, which is especially annoying for the first one that explains unlimited form every time)6. Make the game display prompts based on what device you are currently using to play, switching over immediately like other games, instead of only showing them based on what button you press to get past the start screen and what you adjust the "control guide" in System settings to7. Fix the poor scaling above 1080p8. Let us press select to stay in the loading screen to practice like in Bayonetta's port (loads too fast to use that feature) or ditch the loading screen practice and give a new practice mode9. Add an option to make the Zoom in/Zoom out buttons work instantly, it's annoying to hold them.It is DRM free though (yes you can run it without steam), so that's pretty neat.In short this is a successful but messy port, I recommend it for its optimization (with the patch) and for how great the game itself is, but... good gosh you better fix this thing Platinum.

_childDocuments_.review: The Wonderful 101 redefines epic.I can’t believe that an 8-year-old game holds up this well, but I guess it all comes down to how it was created. TW101 was a passion project of Platinum Games and you can definitely tell when playing. The studio peaked at this game and that’s exactly what you’ll get as a result: the apex of action games, the adventure of a lifetime.I played this game to death back in my Wii U and yet I couldn’t resist getting it again on Steam by backing this remastered version on Kickstarter, it is that good. Forget about other modern AAA releases, this game feels like the biggest story you have ever experienced. The soundtrack, the action, the effects… everything feels larger than life and the thrill just never ends. Every time you think the game has reached its limit, it strikes back with an even bigger and crazier scene that surpasses all the previous ones. TW101 contains the most memorable and absurdly over-the-top sequences I have ever played, and this is still true even almost a full decade after its original release.To achieve that, the game does not take itself too seriously, and that’s what makes it stand out. In any other average AAA title, the devs would want you to feel like every event in the game is serious business and all the stakes are as higher as they can get for the characters, but here P* wants you to just let go and enjoy the ride. They want you to feel like a little kid again playing with your plastic toys in summer while shaping the most memorable adventure for your tiny little action figures, and so they go all-out with the story and the gameplay (and visuals!) to create that feeling.In that regard, make no mistake. You’ll be having a blast, but don’t be fooled by all the praise: this is not an easy game. If you want to squeeze the best out of it, you’ll have to earn it the hard way, as the difficulty curve is really steep specially in the first half of the game and almost nothing is explained (definitely not the most essential combat mechanics), but if you harden up yourself and take your time to discover and master its intricacies, it rewards you with one of the most satisfying hack’n’slash experiences in existence, there is still nothing like this game out there.In any case, it is worth trying at least once in your life, as there are very few videogames with this amount of love and care put into every little nook and cranny. The character design is legendary, the plot works surprisingly well and manages to keep some twists and surprises despite its heavy focus on superhero clichés (and has one of the craziests final acts ever conceived), the music is fabulous and magnificent... even the voice actors do an astounding work here, you can tell they were having a blast too while recording all the voiceovers. Every line delivery is perfect and does a great job capturing the essence of the superhero theme, both cheesy and grandiose but with a touch of seriousness.As a final note, if you are a fan of Platinum’s history, this is definitely a project for you as it includes a lot of nods and references to both Platinum and Clover that make the experience even more enjoyable once you start seeing it as a self-referential homage of Kamiya and his team. They had a ton of fun going through all their career memories and so they want to transfer that joy to us by creating an endless amount of unforgettable moments that will remain in our memories forever, and oh boy do they deliver. Just trust the fans, hop on this train.Diplomacy has failed! Team, unite up!!

_childDocuments_.review: Played this on the WiiU originally. This is definitely Platinum's most Kamiya game, which is both good and bad.Pros: + Unique controls that handle well once you get the hang of it. I like using the Wonder Liner, especially once you get the Attack Liner to help build up combos.  + Script is very well written. Characters are great, and Wonder Red in particular has multiple foils with Blue, Vorkken, and the main villain. It's very, very corny and self-aware with plenty of references to other games and the Sentai genre, lots of fun. Worth playing through just to watch the characters interact. + Lots of collectibles and secrets. + Decent challenge. You need to approach most enemies with different tactics, and the minigames help break up the monotony (to an extent, see below). + There's 9 chapters with 3 levels each, plus the prologue and epilogue; minus secret missions, that's nearly 30 levels.Cons (my cons list tends to be larger than the pros list, but that doesn't mean I think the game's bad): - This isn't a remaster by any means. It's a port. Barely any of the textures or models have been modified (I've ripped models from both the WiiU and the PC version of this game, there are no differences between the two platforms in many cases). I only noticed very slight differences, like changing some collectible positions and making Guts/Spring cheaper. - Controls are very, very unintuitive, an issue that plagued my first playthrough on the WiiU as well. I personally think they're fantastic once you get the hang of drawing morphs, but they take a long time to get used to.  A lot of people say that the first playthrough is basically the game's tutorial, which is true but not an excuse. The game is over 15 hours long. - The game desperately needs some kind of (ACTUAL) tutorial section. There's a practice area in the loading screen, but that's pretty much it. Ironically, it can't be used since the loading times have improved so much on the PC port that you only see it for like a second. Beyond that, the game straight-up doesn't explain a lot of its mechanics, like taunting enemies for a brief damage boost. There's not holding a player's hand, then there's throwing them to the wolves. This game does the latter a lot of the time. - There are so many minigames to the point where they start disrupting the flow of the gameplay, especially in the final chapter. It feels like Platinum decided to pack as many things as they could into this game, but there's so much new ♥♥♥♥ being thrown at you the whole time that it actually starts detracting from the experience.- The subscreen ♥♥♥♥ was implemented fairly well on the WiiU, but terribly in the PC port. - The game's HUD sucks in general. At the worst of times, it's very hard to tell what's going on between the character portraits, QTE prompts, the 100 characters you control, the subscreen, the enemy types, and all the other stuff. Like I mentioned before, Platinum went for quantity over quality in this game, and sometimes it feels very unfocused.Other notes: > Graphics are very bright and colourful > Game's assets are mostly low-poly with low-res textures, having anti-aliasing this time definitely helps > Platinum games have a weird frame limiter bug that locks the FPS to 59 and destabilizes over time. Use this to fix it: Overall, it's not one of Platinum's best games, but its charm and unique mechanics makes it worth putting up with everything else. Unironically, this game has SOUL.Plus, it has Vijounne. If that's not a good enough reason for you to get this game, you're probably gay.

_childDocuments_.review: The one word to describe this game is goofy. It is a pastiche of disfunctional superhero teams and entire super-sentai genre, with a healthy dose of japanese humor. The gameplay itself is hard to pin to a single genre. There are platforming elements and fights that require use of special abilities gained by morphing the heroes (by drawing certain shapes, ala Okami). There are even sections where the game plays as a shooter or a fighting game. In any case it is a very responsive and smooth experience, supported by nice looking and easily readable visual style. Audio matches the game perfectly, with music containing themes for heroes and villains and voice acting matching the over-the-top feeling of the game. Any time heroes die, they can be immediately respawned.I really cannot think of any down side of this game. It is silly and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: W101 is an easy recommend but with 101 caveats.  This game is not for everybody.  This game doesn't even always land with afficionados of character-action games.  Hideki Kamiya's games are console spectacles meant to be approached with the cold-blooded arcade mindset.  The games wear his influences unabashedly and usually include a ball-busting boss or a bootleg Space Harrier mission.  While this game is more Kamiya than any game before hand, it's not his peculiarities that drag down the experience.W101 escaped from the WiiU jail, but still bears the scars from that system.  The remaster bumps up the resolution and replaces touchscreen drawing with right analog stick drawing.  Drawing is lenient but every now and then in the heat of the moment you'll fumble drawing a shape or a weird interaction with the environment will throw it off kilter.  The "second screen" is still required for certain puzzle/action setpieces.  They still remain awkward and cumbersome to some extent, although Platinum has given many different options for displaying the screen in different forms.  The isometric camera gives off a cool "model" effects to the environments but fails to find a comfortable distance most of the time.  Due to the nature of the size of the enemies and size of your swarm, you will frequently zoom in too close for comfort or too far to keep track of your leader in the chaos.If you can stomache all that, this game rocks.  Whereas Viewtiful Joe was his spin on the solo hero Tokusatsu genre, W101 takes the Super Sentai/Superhero genre and runs with it farther than you could possibly imagine.  The framing of the heroes as pint sized and just one of a hundred combined with the miniature-like environments sets a scale that makes every stage feel like the upper limit of what the setting can provide.  You'll frequently mistake various enemies for being "the boss" until you get to the end of that set of missions and experience what a boss fight in W101 truly is.  The over-the-top action taking place over many phases feels like it could be the final boss of any other game, and that's just the first one.  The combat is less combo heavy than Bayonetta or Devil May Cry and relies more on positioning, reactions, and focus.  As you get more abilities you'll find you can crack open the system just as well as any of their other games.The story is goofy with bits of seriousness holding the plot together.  It's a comfortable predictability that follows tradition for the most part.  The english voice cast is also stellar and really help the humor land.  This is also one of Platinum's longest games.  In usual fashion, higher difficulties are tuned to be a fresh experience rather than tweaked numbers. Play the demo and then multiply your positive or negative response by 500% to get a general idea of your experience with the full game.  If you don't like playing it, at least watch a playthrough online.  The game is a unique experience overflowing with love and soul from the dev team, and does not deserve to be ignored.

Remastered!" now, in both the intro and loading screens, really what's missing is a 'Classic' mode option, to not have the 'remastered' branding and the old music tracks. I don't own an ultra-wide display, so I can't comment on how dual-mode looks on those. however, there's absolutely zero reason we couldn't have dual-monitor support for the Steam version.In short, these are the pros and cons of the Steam version:+Superior FPS+Superior load times-Inferior soundtrack-No dual monitor support-Bad second screen implementation-Frame pacing is broken (requires SilentPatch mod to fix and has a timing bug)While servicable, this port really needs some work.

_childDocuments_.review: Another Platinum game, where even on a first play-through as you bumble your way though combat encounters you'll hit a stride and come out of a fight with a platinum combo ranking and a smile on your face. You sure didn't ace that time ranking, and maybe blew a healing item or two, but by golly that air combo you accidentally initiated looked incredible, Wonderful, even.I guess I could review this game like a ranked fight:OUR HEROES AT PLATINUM GAMES DO IT AGAINTime: 15-20 hours, not too long, not too short (and if you're a 101%er, triple that number). Some might not enjoy the pace it doles out its story content, maybe for some it lags a bit in the 2nd quarter. But man do we ever just ramp up from there. The story just moves at a brisk, Wonderful pace as we approach the finish line, and boy does it pay off.Combo: 9999, whether you're talking the mechanics, story, music, characters, style, presentation, there's no part of this game that isn't firing on all cylinders. There is no better feeling than seeing that platinum combo pop up. For some it'll take some time, but eventually you'll hit your first big score and man, it just gets better from there. The story just goes and goes and continues paying dividends, and just when you think you're at the end, ohhh no bud, strap in, you're in for a Wonderful ride to the finish line. One I very much doubt you'll want to turn off once you've entered the last stretch of the game. Certainly in no small part due to the music pushing you along, with our Wonderfully orchestrated Tables Turn popping up to help you end out a long chapter. The characters (and VO performances, my goodness), from the Heroes to the Villains who steal the show, the style of it all (so incredibly shiny and spandex-y), and the presentation wrapping it all up with the Wonderful pre-mission briefings, small respites of banter between Wonderful Ones after fights, its a miracle it all holds together so well. Of course there are some shortcomings in some areas, especially the remaster quality, but we save those for...Damage: 999, because lets be real, while its great to have (almost) rock solid 60fps Wonderful 101 for some stylish Wonderful action, there's a bunch of little nicks and dents on this Wonderful package. The buggy camera above 1080p, the 59hz oddity (at least fixable with a mod), and very not remastered visuals are a few of the big issues that at this point are mistakes we shouldn't be seeing anymore. Not to mention the endless debate on dodge/counter moves being unlockables (even if they are basically free).If you can take the (admittedly in most cases small) issues, The Wonderful 101 is another Platinum-ass Platinum Game. That is to say, as most of you'll know by now, these aren't for everyone. But there's a reason we all went nuts when this was announced. Worst case, there's an easy mode, and a fully automatic mod to boot. Which is great, because the story alone is worth the price of admission (but do stay for the combat).Wonderful 101 Rank: PlatinumIt ain't Pure Platinum, but they can certainly take another swing at it after a few fixes.That or a sequel...#WonderRed4Smash

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game, easily my favorite out of Platinum's works of stylish spectacle fighters.-The Good-It's mechanics take some getting used to and due to the generous continue system, this game is incredibly easy to brute force without figuring out how to effectively handle enemies with your large arsenal of weapons.The graphics are simple but very colorful, the low poly Wonderful ones are very aesthetically pleasing even with the glossy tint on a lot of their textures. The general vibe is going for a Saturday morning cartoon/tokusatsu show and while I don't think it's anything outstanding, it is a great backdrop.The characters are fairly one dimensional and their dialogue often gets in the way of what is otherwise well executed slapstick comedy.The game's enemy roster is some of the best in the genre, very few of them feel actively frustrating to fight against as long as you're using the appropriate tool for the job, a vast majority of them can be stunned and juggled into a satisfying combo, including some of the very large ones.The game will somewhat regularly swap gears into different control schemes and even different genres, many being homages to old arcade games.This is often poorly executed in other Platinum games but I found a vast majority of these homages to be exceptionally polished and a welcome change of pace in this game's long runtime.-The Camera-Complaints about the camera are numerous and it's not hard to see why, W101 uses a fixed camera largely out of the player's control that zooms in and out as need be to best focus on what's important.It's not perfect, the player is able to zoom the camera out manually but it will frequently take control back. It'll often zoom in when you'd rather have it zoomed out and vice versa.Despite that, I did not mind the camera too much with the exception of the handful of platforming sections.Most enemies have sound ques to signal their attacks, so once you get used to those, keeping the enemies on-screen in your battle against the camera becomes a lot less important.-The Ugly-This port is quite bad without SilentPatch.And I don't think there's any fan patch that fixes the intrusive A-posing bug upon unite-morphing.The A-posing bug seems to happen consistently in a bunch of areas scattered across the game. (Notably towards the later half of Operation 002-B)It's incredibly frustrating as it doesn't register most inputs while you are A-posing, it's fairly easy to break out of it with an attack but considering how frequently you will unite-morph, it's more than likely to get you hit.The orchestrated soundtrack is nice but there's a couple of tracks that don't fit nearly as well as the original score. (Tables Turn & The Won-Stoppable Wonderful 100)Currently, there is no way to revert to the original OST without mods.They are developing some upcoming DLC, so here's hoping we see some more patches for this troubled version of the game, though communication regarding it has been very sparse and diplomacy has failed.Platinum has not maintained its luster.EDIT: As of May 19th with the patch that dropped with the Luka DLC none of the prevalent issues have been addressed.

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played Bayonetta already then do that first. If you didn't like it then odds are you won't like this, if you did then read on.The Wonderful 101 is unfiltered Hideki Kamiya for better or worse. You've got your deep fast paced combat, your loads of detail/easter eggs, the fun characters, the shoot em up sequences and quick time events. (Albeit the Q.T.E's are no where near as annoying as in Bayonetta) It is long for this sort of game and all the Hideki Kamiya stuff is gonna turn off most people from replaying it but if you can stomach them, you're in for a hell of a ride.As a remaster: The frame rate and resolution bump help a lot but none of the assets have been touched up. (there's a pre-rendered video where they didn't re-rerender it so the resolution drop is jarring when it happens) It does still have a lot of Wii-U stink on it like the frequent loading times (thankfully only a few seconds compared to the 30 on the Wii-U) and the second screen gimmicks are still there via overlay but the worst I can say about it is that it locks you to the remixed version of The Won-stoppable Wonderful 101 and Tables Turn so I'd suggest giving the originals a listen upon beating the game.Also, the game is very bad about explaining things which filters a lot of people so here's some grab bag tips if you care.-As soon as you unlock the store, buy Unite Guts and Spring, they are core defensive abilities and you'll have a hard time without them, the remaster made them basically free and tells you to buy them as soon as you enter for a good reason.-Hand is immune to/can hold fire.-Attack liner and energy converter are great as combo upgrades.-The most expensive thing in the item mixer is a credit card, you can exchange it for any item in the store, useful to get the most expensive items/skills.-There are less invisible walls then the game makes it looks like, wander everywhere for power ups.-Keep your eyes out for permanent recruits, they're all over the place and even at 1080p, they can still be hard to spot and plenty are mixed in with civilian crowds.-You can recruit weaker enemies, circle them as they turn purple and they'll join you and weakening them to that point without killing them is the purpose of your charge attack.-The intended way of levelling your permanent members is to use their unite morph. Open your second screen and you'll see a red bar under the icons for your morphs on the radar screen showing the total ranks there. Levelling members unlocks new moves and raises your health bar.-While it is tempting to do your post game collectable clean up on Very Easy to get it done faster, if you plan to do it in one sweep, you have to do it on normal or higher. Challenge rooms only spawn on normal and above and there's 12 achievements and an unlockable tied to just finding them all.-The enemy weapon held bonus refers to bringing an enemy weapon to the end of the level. You'll get one right before a level end sometimes so grabbing it and bringing it to the end is free money.

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought I’d see the day, but  finally got an encore. It was like the one reason why I hadn’t boxed up my Wii U yet. I even went as far as to buy new pieces of furniture to actually put that gamepad somewhere so wouldn’t neglect it as much. Tough luck though,  is all I ever wanted. is one of my favourite games ever. Heck, it might just be my favourite. Wonder Red has been my Steam Avatar for over 7 years now. The soundtrack never left my music player and the box art serves as my lock screen on my work computer so my students have to admire it whenever I hit that Win+L. What makes  so amazing then? Let me tell you. This is quintessential video games. Colourful graphics, upbeat music, gameplay that is easy to learn but infinitely rewarding to master, crazy story, mad set-pieces and nearly infinitely replayable. It is the gift that keeps on giving.  is mad crossbreed between ,  and  and . You take control of a squad of up to 100 super heroes who can combine into giant technicolor weapons based on the symbols you draw with the right analog stick. Circle gets you a giant fist; a straight line makes for a sword, and a straight ‘L’ makes a gun and then some. The bigger the symbol, the bigger the weapon. You’re limited by your energy, so draw conservatively. You need certain weapons to avoid damage. The fist can absorb fire, the sword can reflect lasers and nullify lightning, while the whip can be used to rip spikes off your enemies. Drawing these symbols requires some practice, but once you get the hang of it you’ll be able to unlock the wild combo potential. Before you know it, you’ll go from having trouble with drawing the hammer, to unleashing 3 different attacks at once while continuously pounding the smaller enemies with your spare forces. And there are enemies to spare. Countless unique enemies and magnificent boss fights are a treat every time. Combat is so involving it becomes an art form onto itself. The game is therefore not shy to demand absolute perfection from you. This is a Platinum game after all. After every battle you’re weighed and measured, and when found wanting, you’ll go home with less than Pure Platinum. This game will condition you to hate the colour gold, but in the end, the reward is pure satisfaction.In  you need to protect the Earth against and alien invasion. You start off with Wonder Red, who is a school teacher by day and a textbook superman in the face of danger. You’re joined by Blue, a swarthy police officer; Green, a portly sniper; Pink, a vivacious socialite; Yellow, shy Russian; White, public weeb and Black, hacker supreme in an effort to repel the unyielding torrent of alien invaders. The story is told through amazing cutscenes with dialog lifted straight out of snappily written Saturday morning cartoons. It is a bit pedantic at times, but amusing all the way through. I can sit through it without skipping every time. The dialog, characters and enemies are also full of Platinium Games references and Easter eggs, so if you’re into their work, you’re in for a treat. What sets  apart from other games is the way it handles its set pieces and the pay off will always make you smile from ear to ear. After a long and intense boss fight where it is all hands on deck, the music rises to the heroic tunes of a newly orchestrated main theme that sets the mood for something incredible and it does not disappoint. Although you may frown on quicktime events,  does them tastefully, with ample time to react, incredible payoff when you pass and hilarious consolation if you fail. Visually, the game is seven years old now. The PC version upscales cleanly to 1080p (I can’t do 4K on this PC) and a heavy dose of anti-aliasing makes it all look smooth. The framerate is also smooth at 60fps on a GeForce 970. A much needed boost from the 30fps on the Wii U. The game is violently colourful and used high-gloss models to give that action figure look. Facial animation is a bit ‘8-bit’, but that’s the trade off for having 100 of them on screen at any time. However, it’s the total picture that counts, the comedic timing and amazing screenwriting really put everything together. Don’t dismiss it for looking cartoony until you have beaten your first real boss. The soundtrack was composed to scream heroism at every note. Brass, choirs, marching drums, it has it all. The principal voice cast does an incredible job selling the insane story credibly. It gets a bit over the top, but at this point, over the top is the new normal.  will humble you the first time through. Don’t feel bad, this is normal. It will take time to come to grips with the controls, the camera, the combat system, how to draw a hammer, dodging, counters and crowd control. It’s a lot to take in. However, do not let that ‘plastic’ trophy get you down. Just get to the end, smile and all, and then go right back to the beginning with all your powers already unlocked and ready to fire. Suddenly you’re playing a new game. No longer are you trying to beat it; you’re trying to own it. Additionally, the game has so many secrets and things to unlock, you’ll be occupied for a while. Take into account that it also includes Platinium Games’ general quality of life care and you won’t need another game for the rest of this pandemic. All in all, I cannot recommend this game enough. Its insanely cool set pieces are worth playing, the music is worth enjoying and the combat is so cool, it is prize to master. The PC version is a simple port, but it did what it needed to do, 60fps, smooth textures and little to no load times. You’ll be doing yourself a disservice if you don’t try it. For me, I’m just happy I can now get a higher definition avatar. It has been  a long time coming.

_childDocuments_.review: I once heard someone say that the first playthrough of a Platinum game is, for all intents and purposes, the tutorial. _childDocuments_.review: The Wonderful 101 is unique beast of a character action game with its team-based mechanics and unique weapon-switching system. It's also one of Platinum's most fun games when you figure out how to play, complimented by a variety of gameplay switch-ups homaging everything from Punch-Out to Space Harrier, a strong, if very Saturday morning, script and liberal amounts of spectacle. Warts and all, I would go as far to say it's the best game the studio has produced to date.I should point out, however, that the "Remastered" in the title is a complete misnomer at best. The game looks identical to its Wii U counterpart, complete with low-resolution main menu assets, and the port job has framerate issues, as well as further issues if you decide to go borderless or above 1080p. I hope that Platinum has the sense to rectity these issues soon.
_childDocuments_.name: The Wonderful 101: Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is very hard to get into  ( and the lackluster tutorial doesn't help ), even if you've been playing similar games before, but it's actually very well crafted.A few aspects of this port are not on par with the overall game's quality :- The Wii-U second screen is relegated to some window you can make pop up by pressing select which will inevitably cover up some parts of the UI everytime you do- The UI is gigantic and there are moments when you'll be able to see 1/3 of the screen- Selecting missions on specific difficulties, selecting specific characters and retrying missions is sometimes wonky- Drawing abilities might be frustrating and you might find yourself fighting the controls more than the enemies.So basically the UI is garbage and it's sometimes an actual hindrance, controls can be frustrating and it's 45 euros.Still, it is a very good and varied action game, so despite all, it's still a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful 101 Remastered:I love this game... from the unique yet diverse combat to incredibly memorable set pieces and epic music I will never forget about this experience. This is the game that made me truly invested in hack and slash titles and PlatinumGames in general. There are so many new mechanics and cool level designs that will keep you engaged throughout the game. Just like other hack and slashes you unlock several abilities by playing and you'll make your own moveset with your own combos and it's very satisifying, this combat system is a bit different compared to other action games and that's why I love Platinum and this game in general it's not only unique but it also succeds what it sets out to do. Story, charachters and the overall presentation is amazing. I don't think the game has a genius plot or whatever but I just enjoyed the characters and moments a lot. From Blue's secret and Red's past to just silly things like Green and Blue always arguing it's full of charm and just overall very enjoyable.Wonderful 101 is the only game I didn't know how to truly feel about it's the most epic game I've ever played with it's set pieces and combat system but I also had some problems with the mini-game sections the game offered. It's been around 6 months since I've played through this game but I think I can look past those flaws and easily say this game is one hell of a time and you should play it.10/10 as in it's one of my favorite games ever

_childDocuments_.review: There are actually some lesser known QoL features added with this port, as weird as the UI is, I don't see myself going back to the Wii U version, ever. A bunch of issues from the original version were fixed like the slowdown, people complained about the framepacing in this version but there's both a mod to fix it, and also the original game was INSANELY laggy. Some of the previously not well explained mechanics are better explained, the game does a better job telling you how important blocking and dodging is, etc.Also, most importantly, new content. In fact, in the year of our lord, 2023, there is new content being released, SOMEHOW. I'd assume the Luka content was gonna be released as a standalone thingie but no, it's a DLC here and it's free. In fact the only bonus content for this version that costs money is Vorkken Mode, which is basically this game's Jeanne Mode, except without the absolute nightmare of unlocking it.This is not an easy game to learn, on this version or the Wii U version, but this is definitely an improved version compared to the Wii U version. It's also a deeply technical and fun hack and slash with some of the most unique concepts I've seen in any Platinum game, which is saying something considering they're known for experimenting. It's not my favorite, those would be MGRR, Bayo 1, and Vanquish, but this one is definitely up there as one of my favorites to return to.

_childDocuments_.review: Game review:PROS: -Unique and engaging gameplay-Varied in gameplay sections, shifting alot of different genres-Great music-Fun and charming story and characters-Long and has tons of content and secrets (around 15-20 hours for your first playthrough)-Probably the best final boss battle everCONS:-Some sections tend to drag on, especially the SHMUP ones-an annoying kid-mission and ranking structure is inconsistantPort/remaster review:PROS:-Runs really well, didn't get any framerate drops-Comes with two orchestral songs, and a remix soundtrack is on its way-Essential abilities are now free at the store (Unite guts and spring, which are block and dodge)-Only takes around 8 gigabytes which is a nice change from the current trend of bloated filesizes CONS:-Some minor graphical bugs. Faces having weird textures or enviroments missing effects-Alot of the 2D assets are at low resolution, can be very pixely-The Multi-Unite ability is now a very expensive skill you have to buy at the store for some reason (Multiple times infact)-Can't put the second screen on another monitor-Can't change back from the orchestral songs to the original ones-For some reason, a character portrait and speech bubble have been added in some of the cutscenes, obscuring alot of the action-While some sections have been tweaked, others more frustrating and needed of a change have been left untouchedFINAL THOUGHTS:If you are a fan of action-games, buy this game. It's one of a kind and has alot of heart and soul put in it. The remaster/port is perfectly fine but could use some improvements that hopefully will be patched in.

_childDocuments_.review: This port is kind of a mess. You need a mod to fix the extremely inconsistent framepacing, there are various camera and visual bugs if you set the resolution above 1080p (probably why it's still limited to 1080p on PS4 Pro & PS5), and from what little I tried the KB+M controls are atrocious and were clearly an afterthought compared to using a controller....But man, the game itself is so much fun. It takes a while to click - even compared to other games in this genre it has a very high skill floor before you start having fun, and some (many?) people manage to finish the game without reaching that skill floor thanks to the extremely generous continue system, but if you put in the effort to learn how to play it well then it pays that back in spades. There are no tutorials beyond basic controls - you're expected to learn through experimentation. That's admittedly not for everyone but I found it satisfying. The combat seems simple at first but there's an incredible amount of depth to it.(Sidenote, this is a DX9 game, so if you have an Nvidia GPU I highly recommend using Nvidia Profile Inspector to force on OGSSAA or SGSSAA which really helps with the 1080p limitation. See the game's pcgamingwiki page for specifics, but don't use the listed "higher quality" AA compatibility flag there because it makes the water rainbow-colored)The game does have flaws - the minigames and genre changes are a little too frequent (especially the shmup and rail shooter sections), the first half of the game feels a little bloated, you have to buy the basic guard and block abilities for some reason, a ton of combat abilities are locked behind either leveling up or the shop, most of the dual screen sections feel incredibly gimmicky, the camera sometimes zooms in way too far during combat, and there are lots of QTEs (though they're  less obnoxious than the ones in Bayonetta 1). In other words, it's a Hideki Kamiya game; you mostly know what you're in for if you've played one of his earlier games, particularly Viewtiful Joe or Bayonetta.
_childDocuments_.name: The Wonderful 101: Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: The Wonderful 101 is an odd title from Platinum. The climax of Kamiya's love to shift into arcade-influenced mini-segments and gimmicky level design, a titan in spectacle and ceaseless self-1UPmanship. It's an odd experiment in action games as well, opting for a few easy to remember input commands from which the game's combos can arise. The influence of or at least the Nintendo target audience is apparent, as Platinum persues some simplifications and leans harder on level craft, but the charm, passion, and heart of the game is its most notable feature.

_childDocuments_.review: + The story, dialogue and general tone are absolutely over the top but completely endearing and with a solid identity.+ Good voice acting that compliments the cheesy tone.+ The overall design of the characters, enemies and levels are really good. The details of the models aren’t amazing if you zoom in, but the fun designs make up for it, and it isn’t supposed to be zoomed in outside of the odd cutscene.+ The core combat mechanics are unique and really solid once you get the hang of it. The combat has good depth and is almost puzzle-like at times where you have to figure out which abilities to use to beat enemies.+ Great set pieces - they’re absolute chaos and tons of fun.+ Good puzzles for you to solve that are neither too easy nor too hard.+ The game has a good way of handling skill - you can die as many times as needed and still complete the missions but with a bad score, and for those who play well and meet certain criteria they can get increasingly better scores./ The tutorials are mostly decent but slip up now and then and can leave you scratching your head. Additionally, not making Unite Guts (block) and Unite Spring (dodge) mandatory parts of the opening prologue was a mistake./ There are quite a few sections with either modified controls or a new set of controls and they can vary quite a lot in terms of polish and fun. Some add to the mayhem, while others really detract from it.- Every now and then you encounter dual-screen sections where there’s a lot going on between the two screens and it’s a bit of a mess on a single screen.- Every now and then you have these smaller indoor sections and they’re really cumbersome to navigate - they really highlight how the game/camera wasn’t made for small interiors and leave you fighting the camera.- There are a couple of timed platforming sections which can be frustrating as it can be extremely easy to lose track of where you are and where you’re jumping around.- In general the game tries to do a bit too much at times and flips between too many different game modes.- Luka becomes fairly core to the story but he’s pretty annoying and detracts from the fun.- The game randomly pauses at times - no idea why. Doesn’t happen that often, but it’s annoying when it does.This game is really great and one-of-a-kind, but with some glaring flaws. It’s a very much larger-than-life presentation which at times tries to do too much. It’s definitely a hectic game, and there are a few sections where it gets borderline overwhelming and can be pretty confusing. If these sections had been reworked or stripped away, it would have been a much smoother game overall.That being said, it’s still a load of fun - from both the cheesy Power Rangers style team and story to the unique and interesting combat. I’ve read someone say before that the first playthrough of the game is the tutorial and I understand the point now that I’ve played it. There really is a lot to learn throughout the game and you’re unlikely to get good scores on your first playthrough. There’s a lot of fun to be had here though if you can ride the steeper learning curve - I would recommend spending time at the start to really get to grips with the basic mechanics so that the extra ones that get layered on in certain sections aren’t quite so overwhelming.I’ve written the below in an attempt to give new players some basic points to look over, but it isn’t a comprehensive list. It might seem a bit daunting, but it doesn’t take too long to get the hang of it if you know what to focus on, and it’s a really rewarding game. You can practice most if not all of the below in the first level (following the prologue) - I would advise getting to grips with this. If you get particularly mauled in the first level, maybe replay it first before moving on. Note: I’ve written the below based on an Xbox controller layout.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna call it Hideki Kamiya's magnum opus, man who is most capable to push Platinum Games and action games.This game's aproach to combat is different and it creates new type of experience and retains everything that makes games like this fun. In a same way Viewtiful Joe was different from Devil May Cry, its different from Bayonetta. Funny how The Wonderful 101 and Viewtiful Joe share superhero theme, change camera perspective from previous Kamiya's game and some game design ideas (heavy dependence on energy bar and how its maximum capacity resets at the start of every stage and player must collect things to grow it again). Actually all those games share DNA in some way, its really cool to see for example Okami's drawing gimmick be reinterpreted in different context, yet serving to kinda same goals. It makes trivial act of switching weapons its own gameplay mechanic that makes player think in a new way.I can talk all day how it also shares DNA with works of Shinji Mikami, who is Kamiya's sensei, but its not in depth piece about auteur theory and Hideki Kamiya, nor it is in depth review on The Wonderful 101 actualy. Its a love letter..And this game is also a love letter, to video games and Tokusatsu, to Platinum Games own legacy and beyond (for example one of its failed QTE animation is a homage to Devil May Cry 3 short video you see when booting the game). Yet it creates identity of its own.This game has character, creativity and burning guts! Uncompromising and unapologetic in its drive to break up its core gameplay with as many distractions and gimmick stages, it has like 5 shoot em up sections with different gameplay styles. You may not like it, but I think it deserves a respect.This is not by any means abstract perfect game and I have my own problems with some choices and execution, nor is it perfect conversion (well depends on what you looking for I guess), BUT it gives me insane amount of joy. Very glad to be playing it again 6 years later!May Platinum maintains its luster forever!
