_childDocuments_.review: 'remaster' thoughts at the bottomIn 2013, Platinum Games launched a quality game that no one purchased for a system that no one bought. With trailers showcasing close-ups of its models made for an isometric perspective, it was easy to mock its visuals especially with the PS4 and Xbox One on the horizon. And despite receiving a Nintendo Direct solely focused on this title and a demo, the lustre vanished quickly due to releasing near GTA V and The Last of Us. But one successful Kickstarter campaign later and the nice oddity of Nintendo letting Platinum publish this on their own, The Wonderful 101 has released on PC to keep shining long into the future. Sticking to director Hideki Kamiya's character action game forte and his love for Super Sentai and arcade games, The Wonderful 101 takes a unique spin on the genre. Rather than playing as one character such as Dante, Bayonetta or Viewtiful Joe in his past titles, here you control 100+ heroes whose weapons and abilities are all performed by uniting up while tackling foes significantly bigger than you. Uniting can be done by either drawing the weapon you want to use such as a sword or gun with the right analogue stick, or take quicker defensive measures such as forming a shield with Unite Guts or dodging with a single button press. Not only does this feature mean you have access to every single weapon without having to use a menu or remember an order, you can change the size of your weapon for greater damage but slower movement by drawing a bigger pattern, or use team unite morphs and have your fellow 100 combatants attack for excellent combo potential.Each of the weapons belong to a specific type of Wonderful One, so if you draw a fist you will now be leading the team as Wonder Red by default or as you find Wonderful Ones throughout your journey, you can switch to them instead. There are some secret characters who modify how your abilities work such as the bomb completely stopping an enemy rather than slowing them down but mostly it's just a cosmetic change. Characters rank up and as your total rank increases across all characters, you unlock specific abilities including launching and thrusting attacks, all remnants of attacks belonging to Kamiya's past games. While the combat system is extensive and no other character action game plays like this, your first time through might not be the most pleasant; the game gets better the more proficient you are. Normally for this genre I would say if you aren't willing to play through the game multiple times, skip it, but the story and characters of The Wonderful 101 should be witnessed at least once by all.Specific character arcs that stand out are both Wonder Red and Wonder Blue. Red was appointed team leader despite being a novice which causes some disagreements. As the story progresses, Red displays the prime example of what a good video game protagonist should be. He prioritises the mission, never lets personal events affect his ability and is able to harmonize the team to be an effective unit. Despite his rather stoic nature, some of his lines are comical and delivered well by voice actor Charlie Schlatter. Video game humour can often be grating with irritating one liners and quips, yet the delivery of lines such as “I'm not done overexplaining” is both relevant to his personality, funny and isn't emphasized enough to remove the humour. Blue on the other hand is a wild card trope yet events will trigger subtle changes in how he speaks and works within the group. There's even minor changes to other characters such as Wonder Green who changes what he is eating per operation and Wonder Pink who begins as a teenager brat, evolves into a mother figure for the pain in the ass Luka. It's a shame about her lovey-dovey role that could be turned down a notch, but even then there are cute additions such as her changes in dialogue when controlling her and fighting one of the games antagonists.With the amount of combat abilities you have at your disposal and the amount of enemy variety, naturally there would be a lot of experimentation on how you achieve victory. Combat can be frantic and fun but the tutorials are presented in a bare-bones manner that can be easy to miss. While it's great to not have them get in the way, if you miss something there's not an area for you to experiment freely without suffering a scoring penalty thanks to the now instant load times that zoom past the training room or even a menu to see all tutorials. For example, there's a taunt mechanic. Perhaps somewhere the game will tell you that, I figured it out accidentally late into the game and still don't understand how to pull it off or what benefit it provides. It may also be frustrating when you are great at the core combat of the game, but not so good at Space Harrier. Your overall ranking will be affected based on something you didn't buy this game for and those sections may feel like a slog due to their repeated use. It's not just combat mechanics that are kept hidden; try failing a quick time event of a unite morph.  I don't know what went on behind the scenes of The Wonderful 101 development, but I can't imagine every single worker either not having fun or contributing to one of the many unique designs of either the level, enemy, Wonderful One or even gameplay style regardless of their position within the company. Kamiya directed a game that is an amalgamation of all his past works and shown improvements while presenting it in a ridiculously crazy new IP with a heavy emphasis on charm. Even some of it's cutscenes are directed like how a child would play with their action figures. It's a shame that at its original Wii U release, serious stories were in the spotlight, and yet even with its arcade gameplay, colourful visuals and silly story, the emotion that's present throughout was treated seriously yet went unrecognised, and The Wonderful 101 deserves to be recognised. (Port/Remaster thoughts)Calling this game a remaster does seem a bit too generous. Having played it at 2k on PC, the performance was excellent, suffered no crashes, had basic visual options and the loading times were almost non-existent. That said, it was clearly lacking in 2D image quality. Text and it's surrounding area are clearly not suited to be scaled to a higher resolution. But this also affects other images in the game that kinda dampen the ridiculously high quality ending otherwise. I've also experienced the occasional bug that forced me to retry a combat encounter, one of which caused all my team members to fly off the map and not come back. The handling of the 2 screen interface from the Wii U days has been implemented well with either a picture in picture or side by side. In a perfect world, I would rather have a UI that implemented everything necessary on one screen but the game does auto-adjust when appropriate in menus and in-game sequences. One issue I have is that your settings don't save. So if you have it side by side like I do, you need to adjust it each time you load the game. It only takes a couple of seconds but it's still irritating. Due to the Kickstarter success, a stretch goal of 2 orchestrated tasks was met and are included in the game. On my first play-through, I didn't even notice! While I enjoy the vocal track of Won-stoppable 100, the new rendition of Tables Turn lacks the kick it had in the original. It's supposed to be a triumphant theme showing you are doing well and close to winning but now it's kinda timid. You can listen to the original tracks in the sound player once beaten the game, so it's sad for me at least that I can't make them the default tracks within the game. Perhaps if you haven't heard the original, you would still think it an excellent piece and might prefer the new versions to the old.While I have issues with it, I would definitely still prefer having it on PC than having to dust off my Wii U, which with this release is now just a Xenoblade X machine.

_childDocuments_.review: Witness how the little people of the big world solve their problems.If people tell you that if humanity wants to unite and do something, nothing can stand in their way except divine power.First of all, this game is a gem left in steam, it is a hack/slash type game made by platinium games, but it has a humorous story and you can get a little bit of vanquish air in the game itself. now let's move on to the review without further ado.Now our game is a game where we manage a superhero, the only difference is that you can manage almost all the people in the city, not a superhero. Let me tell you how it happens, first of all, the combat system in the game is really different and interesting, maybe you have never seen it. The combat system in the game is to use the people or superheroes that we have included in our group to make the shapes that the game offers us and turn them into weapons and fight with them? Let me give a quick summary, let's say you want to use a sword, then you can shape the people in your group accordingly and beat them with it after taking the shape of a sword. This is just one of the examples, if you want, you can turn it into a pistol or a fist if you want, you can gain certain advantages, from that point of view, this is the point where the game stands out, maybe we can say the only point, because the game does not have a very interesting mechanic other than this mechanic, but it offers you a hack / slash and an interesting absurd story of about 6-10 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: What initially seems like an absolutely absurd, incomprehensible mess of ideas that almost seemed to hate those who decided to pick this up ends up being one of the single greatest gaming experiences I've had. Nothing about this game seemingly makes sense, but once you start really getting into it you realise just what you've been missing out on by considering it all as such. An idiosyncratic experience that's willing to push boundaries and experiment a whole lot with its core mechanics to make it stand out strongly from the pack while also showcasing nothing but an unabashed love for the genre. It's got the standard ideas that you'll find in a lot of the Platinum lineup with the way it insists on being a mishmash of differing styles, has an insane skill ceiling that'll make you feel like a fool on your first playthrough, and also going absolutely all out in its sense of pure maximalism. The big difference that separates a lot of what this game does compared to a game such as Bayonetta is the way that it takes extra measures to do as much as possible to unify these styles, while still providing a nice bit of absurdity to the sharp left turns it can take to further reinforce its incredibly full on, over the top vibe.One of the most truly bizarre aspects of this game is the way that almost all of its defining features can be seen as pure negatives when you start off before they eventually reveal their significance once you've gotten a bit better. The weapon drawing is definitely the biggest example of this with the way that it initially seems as if it's adding another layer of complexity to something that doesn't require it that also adds an additional thing that the player could get wrong. There are a few benefits to this however that end up making it extremely well worth it as a mechanic. Most importantly is the way this opens the door to a far more seamless method of swapping between the absurd amount of weapons at your disposal, with the player having access to 10 different ones by the end of the game and then a couple extra for repeat playthroughs, giving the player this method of quickly and easily swapping between them all in a fast paced, chaotic game like this is a perfect fit, not to mention that the additional nuance of the different sizes for each weapon is another benefit of this. Furthermore, additional elements to do with actually drawing are quite interesting too, with enemy positioning and room layout potentially obstructing you and forcing you to make certain compromises or devise another strategy to deal with the situation at hand, providing depth without being frustrating.The other big point with the game that seems bad at first but has its own little positives is the camera, which I will admit feels closer to being equal parts horrible and genius. I'll definitely say that the camera in the game feels too zoomed in or outright misplaced in certain situations and it's absolute agony at times, but there are also other benefits that it has that end up justifying it and make the problem feel more akin to "they just needed to fix up a few spots here and there". My favourite effect of the zoomed out isometric camera is the way that it makes every threat truly feel gargantuan with the way that your army will look like a colony of ants scurrying around against even a lot of the regular fodder enemies that are sent your way. The sheer spectacle of this cannot be understated and also adds a lot to highlighting the game's core theme about teamwork being what will help fight against insurmountable odds. It's also not as bad as it seems because while it might be hard to see your individual character, the morph weapons are positioned in such a way to act almost as beacons when activated, standing tall with these incredibly bright colours that make it impossible to truly get lost in even the most visually busy scenes.Of all the flawed masterpieces that I've experienced, this might just be the most flawed with how often it feels as if the game's almost taking pleasure in slapping you around with outright infuriating scenarios and a mix of genres that sometimes just flat out don't work, but at the same time, the highlights are otherworldly and a lot of the frustration feels far more constructive compared to a lot of other difficult experiences. In most cases, when things feel as if they're taking forever, it doesn't quite feel like the enemies are too much to overcome, but rather than the player themselves are approaching the situation incorrectly and need to further explore the seemingly limitless possibilities of their immense arsenal. So many of the tough moments are less traditional action encounters and more like minor puzzles, asking you to further optimise your gameplay, usually showing off just enough for you to be able to figure things out if you're paying attention while never being too obvious to further make it feel like your own accomplishment with each time you're able to take down these enemies slightly faster than before. This is likely the reason for the relatively few types of common enemy in the game too, because it instead wants the player to build familiarity with this smaller selection to truly master what they can do, because at the end of the day, Wonderful 101 is a game that encourages players to master the systems and dynamics at play in a way that I don't really see too often. It's not really fully content with players just stumbling through to the end, it wants them to fully get a grip on everything it has to offer, and the incredibly forgiving continue system is a huge indicator of this, clearly not really being concerned about whether the player is able to beat the game, but how well they can do it, which I do think is cool in a game as dense as this.Above all, this really does feel like one of the purest expressions of adoration for the video game medium as a whole, and it's a big reason why I think it's a masterpiece. There's an outright ridiculous amount of effort put into even the smallest of details that simply would not be so strongly considered in other games, let alone one where you probably won't even be able to see a lot of it too well thanks to the camera perspective. The fact that each of the titular 101 heroes of the game each have their own unique model and little character bio is one such aspect I love, how even though you're likely not going to be seeing them in any detail beyond "these look like tiny ants", they're fully implemented without any signs of concessions having to be made, each of them also being really funny and charming in how they look. The ever intensifying stakes are also really cool to witness in the way that it's also represented through the gameplay ramping up in ways that not only feel more difficult, but more exciting too.Rather than frontloading the experience in an attempt to hook people with the sacrifice of making the later portions often feel somewhat less climactic and interesting in comparison, the final 2 missions of this game are instead where things get kicked into overdrive with some of the most insane and silly things I've seen in a game. Nothing about the way the game presents itself is subtle at all but I think it works exceptionally well with the way it plays so strongly into replicating the feeling of goofy superhero cartoons, never straying from making clearly dumb jokes or throwing things all at the wall for no reason more than just "I thought it'd be neat", because above all, it just wants to be a fun maximalist experience! I haven't quite played something like Wonderful 101 before and I'm not sure if I will again, but I can always hope to find another game that feels so committed to being such a joyful time that fully embraces and adores games as a whole that I am willing to call it one of the best things ever despite having so many points that frustrated me to the point of becoming an angry goblin creature who wanted to break her controller.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful, albeit unconventional action game, with amazing voice-acting, music, and a surprisingly good story to go along with it. The Wonderful 101 doesn't hold the player's hand, perhaps to a fault at times since it expects the player to pick up on things they may not think about, such as Unite Guts only working on "blunt" attacks because it's symbolized as jello pudding or the Charge attack stunning most enemies once they've been hit enough times, with the stun state being the only way to juggle foes. It's combat starts as a frustrating snowball of constantly losing your Unite Morphs as you learn each enemy's quirks, and turns into a euphoric display of skill as you combine multiple Unite Morphs to quickly dispatch enemies that gave you so much trouble when you first encountered them. Action game prowess is not enough for The Wonderful 101 either, as it tasks the player to master a multitude of different encounters such as shoot-em-up sections or those that utilize the dual-screen function, on top of it's standard action encounters. Not all these sections are winners, but the design of requiring players to demonstrate skills outside enemy control and juggling is enough for me to appreciate them.As a port, however, it does not seem it was handled in the best way possible. There are some bugs, the worst of which require a reset of combat encounters. A lot of assets look like they were just upscaled from the Wii U version, leading to things like text found in the enemy introductions and certain images looking blurry or jagged. Texture effects, like the "energy" beams found on the tentacles of Vijounne's mech, look very bad and distracting when they're a certain distance away from the camera, but these are thankfully few and far between. Technical issues aside, I recommend The Wonderful 101 to action fans vets and newcomers alike. It may not be for everyone, but you'll never know until you try.

_childDocuments_.review: OverviewThe Wonderful 101 is a highly unique action game from the masters of the genre.This is a great port.  It runs at a consistent framerate and the visuals are crisp.  The controls work perfectly on a controller.  You are not missing anything from the lack of a Wii U gamepad.Story and GraphicsThe story is very silly and never takes itself seriously.  The humour is entertaining, although it drags on a bit at times.  In fact, there is a great deal of dialogue.  Despite this, the story ends up being very entertaining and satisfying, with some epic cutscenes.I love the art, which is bright and colourful.  The characters are made to look tiny, and the buildings look like toys.  This enhances the game’s light-hearted feel.GameplayThe Wonderful 101 is a style action game, like Bayonetta or Devil May Cry.  However, it is full of unique and creative ideas.  Some of these work, while others can be a nuisance.Instead of selecting weapons, you draw them.  This enables you to switch weapon mid combo by drawing a different one.  With the right upgrade, you can pull off some neat tricks, like doing different types of attacks simultaneously.  Another unique mechanic is that you can make different sizes of weapons.  Larger weapons hit harder but require a big commitment.Once you unlock more options, the combat becomes both stylish and crazy.  To add to this, there are many epic boss fights.I had a couple of issues with the combat, however.  My biggest gripe with the game is how it handles getting hit.  You control a group of heroes, rather than just one.  When you get hit, some or all of these get sent flying.  It often takes quite a bit of time to get them all back.  While they are scattered, your options are heavily reduced.Another think I dislike is how the game handles large enemies.  As you would expect from Platinum Games, the enemy design is solid.  The problem is that it is difficult or impossible to combo large enemies, unless you have found all the heroes and can make huge weapons (which will not be the case on your first playthrough).  When fighting larger enemies, you are forced to take an excessively defensive approach which feels out of place in a game like this.The Wonderful 101 also mixes things up with unconventional gameplay.  There are many flying stages, for example.  While I appreciate the variety in principle, many of these just are not fun in practice.  I also found several to have poor controls and to be confusing.ConclusionI enjoyed The Wonderful 101 for its zany creativity, despite some issues which hurt the experience a bit.  It has a learning curve to it, and I would not recommend it as an entry to the genre.  If you are interested in something a bit different, and have experience with this kind of game, it is worth a playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun and charming beat 'm up, that doesn't lack in challenge.It may be hard to tell from the screenshots and gameplay videos but: the way combat works and feels, the encounters, boss fights, shops where you can buy and upgrade moves, etc, in The Wonderful 101, is really similar to Bayonetta. So much so even that I can safely say that if you enjoyed the gameplay in Bayonetta, you'll have a blast in this one without a doubt.There is one aspect of The Wonderful 101 that I can see being a turn-off for some people.  The game is a bit overwhelming in the beginning. The main reason for this being, that there is a lot being thrown at you mechanic wise, at the start and the game only briefly explains everything. So you're a bit forced to experiment and figure out things on your own. That being said, once your past the initial learning-curve, it's smooth sailing.In short. The Wonderful 101 is a really good game that can be a bit rough at first. Would highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally bought this game for the Wii U. It was one of the few games that really made me buy one years ago. I had always loved action games like DMC, Bayonetta, and Ninja Gaiden Black, but this game blew me away with it's unique combat and charm (something I don't think any game has been able to match since). Being able to draw shapes with the Right Stick to create different weapons, change weapons by drawing another shape mid-combo, and all the different moves you can learn really make this one of PlatinumGames best. The story, characters, music, and world design are some of the most memorable in recent memory and it makes me so happy that this game finally got another shot off of the Wii U. The combat may seem off at first, but it really starts to click once you have all the main Wonderful Ones. You'll have to play through Space Harrier and Punch-Out!! sections, but they are insanely fun changes of pace. If you like any action game, I really hope you try this out. The Wonderful 101 still blows me away to this day and I can't wait to play the Luka missions when they come out.Hopefully PlatinumGames can get back Astral Chain from Nintendo too

_childDocuments_.review: The Wonderful 101 is both the last good release from PlatinumGames and the last good 3D beat-'em-up imo. This game singlehandedly sold me a Wii U, and that's where many of my hours into it have gone. At the time this review was written, this PC port crushes the original release, not just in terms of performance but also QoL improvements. Much more work has gone into explaining mechanics and making them accessible, and they've done an adequate job getting the second screen stuff to work without being awkward. There's not really a nice way to say it, but this is an esoteric release. Some of the more nuanced aspects to combat will either require time in the lab or external research. It is a hardcore action-game despite looking like toy Power Rangers.As far as who I'd recommend it to, that's kind of an iffy proposition. People who don't like action-games definitely shouldn't play it, and the people who dominate the beat-'em-up scene in general probably hold Itsuno in the highest regard (DMC5 and its Special Edition released recently) and they probably can't look past the lack of a sandbox in terms of movement and cancels. TW101 builds more on DMC1's approach to combat with many enemies being vulnerable to specific strategies (weapon-specific) and there's a high emphasis on juggling which is nuanced and not free to set up in 101. If you have an open mind and you like action-games and you're willing to take this game as it is instead of trying to wedge it into whatever mold your gold standard resides, you're the person I'd recommend it to. For me, it's about a 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me, you lost your childhood innocence the day you learned that Capcom had shut down Clover Studios and there would never be a Viewtiful Joe 3. Well, all was not lost that day; the people at Clover regrouped as Platinum Games, and carried the badass, stylish spirit of Joe, Okami, and God Hand on to the likes of Bayonetta, Madworld, and The Wonderful 101.101 is very much a "Spiritual Successor" to Viewtiful Joe, at least stylistically, gameplay-wise it might bring Nintendo's Pikmin to mind. However, instead of primarily dealing damage by clinging to their comparatively gigantic foes, Wonderful Ones are able to construct weaponry out of their own bodies. Some foes require specific weapons to get through their defenses (only Whip can yank off spiked armor, only Claw can pry open a dragon's wings, etc.) and you get a better score for using a variety of weapons, so the game encourages not sticking to a single one.Despite being such a fantastic game, the original release sold horribly due to being only on the Wii U (an objective failure of a console.) I'm overjoyed that Nintendo allowed Platinum to Kickstart a re-release of this treasure of a game on all modern platforms (BTW; said Kickstarter campaign alone sold more copies as rewards than the entire Wii U release's lifespan.) If you missed out back then, or just want to replay it but didn't want to dust off your Wii U, now's the time!Platinum Fans: UNITE UP!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I originally played this on the Wii U and definitely had a lot of trouble getting the hang of things and never finished it. I think a lot of people expected the drawing mechanic to be exclusively used with a touchscreen but the game plays much better with an analog stick. The moment where it clicked was when I realized that the drawing mechanic is essentially weapon switching in other action games, but much deeper and skill-intensive. I think it's easy to start playing on auto-pilot and run into things that will frustrate you, but if you just take a step back and rethink how you are approaching the game it suddenly becomes more rewarding. It was a struggle unlearning habits and hand-holding that I'm used to in other games. The only parts that don't hold up so well are the genre shifts that require you to look at the gamepad screen. These show up in non-Wii U versions as a picture off to the corner of the HUD and are a little janky. There is also a shooter level late in the game that feels brutally difficult.Besides that, the narrative in this game is really great! There's some excellent voice acting, great jokes and dialogue, and the story moves at a brisk pace, constantly upping the stakes at every turn. The level design gets crazier and crazier as time goes on. The soundtrack is also extremely memorable - I go back to listen to it every once in a while because its so awesome. I think that if the gameplay wasn't so inaccessible to some, the story and characters would've easily propelled the game's popularity. I've heard that the first playthrough is the tutorial, but I've only beat it on Normal. I might try a hard playthrough after getting through all the other platinum games I haven't finished.

_childDocuments_.review: IF YOU'RE ABOUT TO BEGIN THE GAME, BUY UNITE GUTS AND UNITE SPRING AFTER FINISHING THE TUTORIAL, PLEASE.Anyways:How can I even describe how amazing this game is?For starters i can probably say this is one of the best if not the best character action game to ever be made. While it does contain many mini game sections because THIS IS a Kamiya game (gotta love Space Harrier), the core combat is incredible its indescribable how complex and fun it is the more you learn and play. Even during my third playthrough  i was still learning new things about the weapons, strategies and the levels, so many things i cant even list them. _childDocuments_.review: Wonderful 101, a game filled with mechanics, secrets, collectibles, nods to other games, humor, excitement, difficulty, creativity and love, or is it sadism? Maybe bothEarth is under attack by an alien armada called GEATHJERK, a very long acronym that they explain early on but doesn't quite stick, it is up to the Earth's own defense force, the Wonderful 100 to travel all over the world and protect the super reactors that power the energy shield protecting the planet. And yet, everyone except their fearless leader acts dumb in the face of dangerAn interesting blend of Pikmin, Viewtiful Joe, Okami and Bayonetta, you control the Wonderful 100 by moving a character designated as leader, who changes depending on your weapon, you change your weapon by using the mouse/right stick to use the Wonderliner, to move all the characters except your leader to draw shapes (like in Okami), the more people in your team the longer you can draw the shapes which gives the weapon a bigger size. You can also recruit other people by drawing a circle around them, most of the people you recruit are civilians who will leave the team at the end of the mission, but there are also members of the W100 that stick with the team permanently, allowing you to start each mission with more people. This principle of being able to give power to others also applies when recovering team members, when they get hit you don't lose health but they become stunned for a few seconds, which means you have less people to form weapons, you can get them back if you run over to them or use the Wonderliner to touch the unconscious people to immediately revive them, this is VERY important because everytime the leader gets hit, the entire party will get stunned, it will help get the party back together faster because the enemies are not gonna sit around and wait Each weapon has its own basic attacks but also properties that make them useful in order to solve puzzles or counter enemy attacks, i.e. the fist can grab valves or containers or the sword can be used like a key or to reflect lasers, unfortunately, the game doesn't have much in the way of explaining things so you'll have to pay attention to cutscenes that introduce characters, keep an eye out for counter attack cues or experiment with things yourself.Boss battles are very reminiscent of the ones in Bayonetta, where you fight giant enemies and must run on top of them to hit their weak points, and then finish them off with over the top cutscenes while button mashing, there is also the obligatory rival character that can use the same weapons as you, except that he can block your stuff and you can't block 95% of his, might be even harder than anything else in the game but that's what rivals are for, right? Also, obligatory mention of many long shoot em up sections.It runs well I guess? I had no problems with it, graphically it's nothing special but it works, just don't pay attention to the characters in the continue screen, or segments where you're in cramped areas as their quality is greatly reduced outside of cutscenes.They also managed to introduce the second screen from the Wii U version as a toggleable screen with the tab/select button that acts as a map or as a menu to select your leader manually, not sure how it works with KB+M but in controller you cannot directly select options inside that second screen unless you're standing still, so it's not very practical in combatOverall, the game is pretty intense but also very difficult, to the point i felt compelled to put down the game after every chapter or rival character battle (the last one made me quit the game for a few days even), it was a good ride, but when it's not going well it can be quite annoying, I still recommend it, as long as you're aware that this is not as lenient as other Platinum games, still beatable if you persevere, just that it will be a bumpy road. (no but really, that rival boss battle though, what the heck)

_childDocuments_.review: This game somehow manages to find ways to be unique, in a genre already laden with unique games. Even if you’re a veteran of Platinum’s or Kamiya’s other works, I think you’ll find a lot to enjoy and some fun surprises here, it employs the same staples as other Character Action games: style points for manoeuvres such as late dodges and taunts, multiple actions which can combo into each other and flashy, over-the-top set pieces. To supplement this, it borrows the spectacle from the likes of Power Rangers/Kamen Rider and the recent Avengers movies.To get it out of the way first, I found the story and characters to be arguably more involved compared to other Platinum games, each Wonderful One’s not so subtle gimmick making them more endearing than a standard gruff action man. However, this is in service to what I believe is the least important aspect of the game, I doubt many people flocked to Devil May Cry or Bayonetta for the narrative. I like how the game looks and the style it’s going for, it’s not a graphical powerhouse by any means but the vibrant colours of the environment and toy-like features of the characters reinforce the playful nature of the game. Performance is obviously going to vary depending on your setup, but I found it to be not very demanding. Unfortunately, the game locks to 60fps by default with no option to change it aside from modding. Onto the meat of the game, the core loop of the gameplay is going to feel like familiar grounds for Platinum fans, build up your combo by using a variety of actions, dodge, parry, etc. there are however a few changes to mix up the formula. The first of which is how weapon switching works, rather than assigned to one or two buttons, you’re given the Unite Morph ability, which ties nicely into the theme of the game in that you’re using every member of the Wonderful 100 to physically create your arsenal. Assigned to the right stick (replacing the Wii U Gamepad’s touch controls), you draw a rough representation of the weapon you want. I believe the touch controls are the superior method for this feature, but the game is generous enough that I could wing it most of the time, only finding issues with Unite Bomb and Glider which I didn’t use often. Whilst I’ll always prefer simply hitting a button to switch my weapon as I feel it provides an instant satisfaction of continuing your combo and styling on your enemies, the Unite Morph ability adds to the spirit of the game despite some of the annoyances it can cause.Adding to this, Platinum opted for an isometric camera which I feel is another standout difference compared to their other games. I also feel this is a necessary change because of the Unite Morph ability and the way it interacts with the environment, there were plenty of times where I drew a bridge, ladder or a simple line to grab some out of reach items. Also, a lot of the enemies are massive in comparison to the Wonderful 100, so the isometric view also helps here to keep track of all the action.Keeping with tradition, there are also temporary genre changes throughout the game, Shmup stages make a return taking up a decent chunk towards the finale, a couple of bosses also mix up the gameplay with a fun twist which I won’t spoil.Overall if you’ve tried other Platinum games or are looking for something different, I think this game is worth your time, the controls may take some time to get used to, but mastering them and the abilities combined with the escalation of the game make for a fun and satisfying playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Since it's so different to probably any other action game you've ever played, The Wonderful 101 is unlikely to click straight away. Other than teaching the basic controls, it's left up to you to figure out the intricacies of the combat system. It requires time and patience, with even game director Hideki Kamiya recommending players treat the first playthrough as a tutorial. As anti climactic as this might seem, action games like W101 live and die by their replay value. You're expected to revisit it on a higher difficulty. Understandably, this isn't going to appeal to everyone; it certainly didn't when W101 originally came out and it led to a number of misunderstandings regarding its combat. But, once it does click, W101 truly becomes something special. There's nothing else like it. It doesn't just stop at that initial click either, W101 is so rich with depth that you'll have plenty of those moments as you're playing. It only gets better as you get better.However, it being left to you is no exaggeration. I can't recommend W101 to people who want to feel powerful from the get go. The amount of times you'll get your ass kicked in can be frustrating and often times even demoralising due to the resulting low ranks. But it does feel substantially rewarding to get those higher ranks, which shows that you're improving. W101 would have benefited from having a proper training mode, providing a safe environment where you can practise unlocked skills against whatever enemies you've faced so far. Sort of like The Void from DMC5. In W101, the training room you get on the loading screen flies by far too quickly to really train at all, and the enemies there aren't so great to practise with either since they're just cannon fodder.In the spirit of W101's ethos, I'm not going to give too much away. Rather, if you do decide to get it, just try to enjoy the learning experience. It'll feel awkward at first, but with enough time you'll find that the controls work really well. There's plenty of enjoyable spectacle, the story is fairly entertaining, the visuals are full of charm and the dialogue can be pretty funny. That should keep things interesting until you're properly accustomed. There's also no harm in looking up tutorials online if that helps you enjoy the game more, though it might take away the satisfaction of discovering things yourself. A Youtube user by the name of Saurian has a great set of videos breaking down different aspects of W101's combat.Oh, and be sure to zoom out the camera at the start of every level with the left shoulder button! Should be the default, honestly.

_childDocuments_.review: If I can convince one person to take a chance on this game then I’m gonna try. This is one of my all time favorite games (I still own my WII U copy), and the most platinum games experience there is. It has a very Saturday morning cartoon vibe that borrows heavily from things like Super Sentai, and feels like a true spiritual successor to Viewtiful Joe (thanks Kamiya)You control a group of 100 heroes tasked with defending the earth from an invading alien terrorist group bent on eradicating earth. Combat revolves around controlling 1 central character and drawing different shapes with the right stick to use different weapons such as a circle for fist or a straight line for sword. As you go throughout the game you unlock different moves much like other character action games, so even though your initial pool of moves may seem limited the game has depth. The game also likes to switch genres such as a shmup or an all range star fox esque section, which gives the game some variety.  This a truly unique experience and one I will happily recommend, however this game is not perfect and not for everyone. It has some frustrating aspects that may be too much for some people. The game has tutorials on screen by default, but they can be kind of confusing and sometimes not very helpful. This can lead to some confusing puzzles where you take damage since you didn’t know what to do. The game can also be very chaotic, and with the pulled back camera. Combat might be too much for some people to focus on (there can be a lot on screen making tells a bit harder to read). The game also has a high learning curve for it’s different mechanics. Early game shapes are easy to draw with a circle and straight line, but as you get late game shapes it may take practice for you to get them to come out consistently. The S shape and Z shape tend to get confused which can be frustrating under time constraints (time slows when you draw a shape, but not on higher difficulties). Despite these faults this is one of the best action games of the last generation. Once you get the hang of drawing shapes you’ll be comboing with the best of them. The story is over the top action fun with one of coolest rival characters ever (think Vergil). Has a truly unique combat system that’s fun to play around with. Has a tone of collectables and unlockable content/characters. The standard platinum ranking system is here giving the game replay value for those that want those perfect platinum trophies. This game just feels like the complete package and a true labor of love. You can feel how much fun the team must have had making this game. Replaying this game has reminded me how much I loved it back in 2013. I had a huge grin on my face the whole time I was playing it. The amount of times I said “That was so ****ing cool” out loud to myself was ridiculous. I hope that people give this game a chance. It’s not for everyone, but for those that can get past it’s barrier for entry it’s a masterpiece. Stay Wonderful

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty wonderful game as the title suggests.If you're a fan of DMC, God of War, Bayonetta type games then this is one you won't want to miss out on as it offers deep rewarding and most importantly fun combat alongside some of the best action spectcale I've seen in a game.If you haven't played an action game like this I would recommend trying a Devil May Cry or something before hand. This game has a fairly steep learning curve where you need to get used to all of the chaos on screen - playing another action game first would help you get accustomed.What sets this game apart from the rest is that you're in control of a hundred or so Superheros that transform into different weapons, by creating shapes with the right stick, that fight aliens. It takes a little getting used to but it gets pretty fun and satisfying, and as a result you'll see some crazy stuff you wouldn't expect. It's a pretty imaginative system and no other game really plays like The Wonderful 101, and it ties really nicely into the bosses, enemies and puzzles. Experimentation is very much rewarded in The Wonderful 101 - turning at once intimidating things into cakewalks is very fun.  The game opts for a lot of set pieces which can be pretty awe inspiring and the game mixes things up pretty regularly. While for the most part I like this, some gimmicks do outstay their welcome a bit, but not too much to really damper the game for me.There are some things I'd change with the game:The continue system is the first. When you die you're presented with the option to continue or to go to the title screen. If you hit continue then you are sent back where you died with full health and your punishment is weaker rank. But if you go back to the title screen you can reload your save and you are sent to a checkpoint. The game doesn't really tell you that there are checkpoints so I can imagine a lot of people opting for the continues at the fear of restarting from the entire level, which in my opinion doesn't gel to well with a game with a steep learning curve. I learned the mechanics by retrying fights from scratch by going through the title screen but I can imagine some players just relying on the continues and as a result they're never forced to learn and the combat never clicks with them. I would have added in a "Load last checkpoint" option to the game over screen because returning to the title screen does the same thing.The next is its camera. I actually had no issues with the camera but at default it is zoomed in too much and I rectified this by zooming it out at the start of each level. It seems a lot of people complained about the camera so perhaps making the zoomed out camera the default would have been better instead.And yeah they're my major complaints - really just stuff that stopped others from enjoying the game as much. Some of the gimmicks were a bit much and the port has some weird quirks like the 59fps and that it sometimes wouldn't appear on my taskbar when alt tabbed but that's about it.TLDR: Great game, zoom out the camera at the start of the level, try to learn your moveset and apply appropriately and don't use the continue system

_childDocuments_.review: Another odd and insane action game from the masters at Platinum Games. In The Wonderful 101 you'll be controlling a team of goofy superheroes fighting an alien army hellbent on conquering the Earth. The combat system is unlike any other: to switch weapons you have to draw shapes using the right stick (don't even try with mouse & kb, this game needs a controller), a bigger shape will create a more powerful weapon. Each weapon has a moveset (not too big, thankfully) and certain properties that you'll need against certain enemies. The punch can absorb fire attacks, the sword can deflect lasers, the whip can remove spiked armor, etc. If you get hit, your teammates will scatter all over the place and you'll have to revive them before you can resume fighting. You can't fight without your team.If this sounds complex, it's because it is. Don't get fooled by the colorful look and lighthearted story, this game is brutally hard and will kick your ass relentlessly until you learn how to play (or give up in frustration). There are some tutorials but they explain almost nothing and you have to figure out a lot of tricks by yourself. At least you have infinite continues and lots of checkpoints, so you can play through the story mode without getting stuck. Just be ready to see a lot of plastic medals and consolation prizes at the end of each chapter. The game is meant to be replayed and mastered over multiple runs, so consider the first one as a tutorial.The game also has a lot of gimmicky non-combat sections, and I mean A LOT. Some of them are OK, some are bad, some are utterly terrible, like the ones that require the dual screen. Dual screen? Yes, this game was a WiiU exclusive and some sections were designed for the WiiU controller, that had a second screen (in the PC version you play them with a picture-in-picture setup). Some people like them, but imo they are the worst part of the game.In the end, is TW101 worth a try? YES, YES, YES.It has some bad parts and it can be very frustrating at first, but it's incredibly unique and creative, the combat is excellent and the story is utterly insane. It's worth playing just to see all the setpieces, up until the epic ending.Thanks Platinum for this remaster! TW101 didn't deserve to be stuck on the WiiU.
_childDocuments_.name: The Wonderful 101: Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: One of the very best action games ever made, no exaggeration.This game is a product of passion and love, it's got a fantastic soundtrack, great aesthetic, great dialogue, and some top tier voice acting to boot. This game's story didn't have to be good, neither did it have to have good music or voice acting, all it needed to do to be a good product was to have a fun combat system, which it absolutely does, but there is so much more to love on top of that, and it's thanks to the efforts of Platinum games.This game that rewards you for having the patience and persistence to master its vast amount of intricacies with one of the most rewarding, intense and deep combat systems in gaming. This is also the game's biggest flaw, as it does have a steep learning curve and is much harder than its deceptively cartoonish appearance might lead you to believe.The remaster is good in terms of performance. My PC, with an i7 6700k and GTX 1080 runs it at a constant 59 (for some reason) FPS without so much as a hitch. Loading times are instant to the point where you can't even use the loading practice menu, and the game runs stable enough, I only had one crash in my 15 hours of playtime, which is not ideal but definitely not a dealbreaker.If you love action games, like Devil May Cry, Bayonetta or Metal Gear Rising, or are a fan of Hideki Kamiya's other games like Viewtiful Joe or Okami, you owe it to yourself to get this game. If you do get this game, despite how it might not seem to be a story heavy experience, you owe it to yourself to not look up spoilers, especially regarding the game's finale. It's absolutely one of the best endings to a game I have ever played, if not THE BEST, and if you don't know what happens there, don't spoil yourself, trust me, you won't be disappointed.Buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: I love Platinum Games. However, on the WiiU this just never clicked with me. Between the resolution and the performance issues, it just kind of felt like a mess to play.That being said, the core of the game was still incredibly hype. The bosses and set pieces are some of the best Platinum has ever produced. It's one of those games where by the end you're saying to yourself "how did we get here?!" As crazy cool stuff is just happening (such as the best QTE ever put into a video game). Luckily, the PC port fixes most of the issues I had with the original. I've had no technical or performance issues. The loading screens, even on my normal hard drive, are almost instant. And I feel like the frame rate mixed with the higher resolution make it far easier to read the battlefield and not take unnecessary hits. That being said, the "remaster" part is rather disappointing. The assets themselves are still very low res. Luckily the art direction carries this game on it's shoulders. It's a blend of Sentai (power rangers, kamin rider, that type of stuff) and Viewtiful Joe. This still isn't my favorite Platinum Game though as battles still feel a bit chaotic and I still take damage from things that I can't even see. I understand that the issue is mostly with myself and my inability to multitask, but it's never fun to flawlessly fight a boss only to get tapped by an add that was the same size and color as the moshpit of your 50 or so characters. BUT it's definitely the studios most unique and hype game. It was a shame that it had been locked behind the Wii U up until this point and it's great to see it back and looking better than ever. If you like action games pick it up. Just do it. Not only is it a crazy good time, it's also jammed full of content and is probably one of the most lengthy games in the entire genre.

_childDocuments_.review: First, let's get the obvious thing out of the way. Do not play this game with keyboard/mouse. It was designed for a dual-stick controller, and if you use anything else you will have a bad time. One of the key mechanics of the game is drawing shapes to switch to a weapon, and while you would think this would work perfectly on a mouse, the way they have implemented it simply does not work. A controller works much better.With that being said, wow, what a game. If you've liked other Platinum/Kamiya titles such as Bayonetta, Devil May Cry, and Viewtiful Joe, then you will love this game. It has all the action, crazy boss fights, and combos of those games, except it's dialed up past 11 this time. Seriously, every boss fight in this game feels like it would be a final boss fight in any other game. And yet the final battle STILL feels appropriate and not outshined by other fights!For those of you who aren't acquainted with Platinum, this game is an action-based beat-em-up with a focus on looking stylish and over the top setpieces. There are several weapons in the game, and the unique weapon-switching system allows for probably the most seamless combo potential of nearly any game out there. No need to pause the action or cycle through several weapons to get what you want, you simply draw the shape with your right analogue stick. Make a circle for a high-damaging fist, or make a straight line for a sword that's great at taking out hordes of enemies. Because you always have instant access to every weapon, there's a lot of room for creative variety. The story is pretty saturday-morning-cartoon esque, but I say that in a good way. It's reasonably paced, has a consistent tone, and is surprisingly funny at times. While it's nothing ground breaking and is fairly predictable, there is at least one interesting twist. The graphics could have been improved for the PC release, however. The game was originally released on the WiiU and it had issues with performance, so the game used low-quality models a lot of the time. This has carried over to the PC release, and it can appear jarring at times. However, the style of the art is fantastic, so it really didn't bother me much. And a lot of the environments are really well done, and really shine at a higher framerate that a PC can push out. Note that this game is locked to a maximum of 60fps, because like all Platinum titles its speed is directly related to the framerate. I have heard that 4k resolution is also broken in some boss fights, however I cannot say that is my experience as I only play at 1080p.There are a few complaints I do have about the game, however. The main one is that it has too many remnants of its original console. For those of you that don't know, the WiiU had a screen on its gamepad, and this game used it to display things during game. This is kept in the game by a sub-screen feature, but I left it off most of the time as I wanted the maximum room for action and visibility. A lot of descriptions for items and such were on this screen, so sometimes I would totally forget to turn on the subscreen and be unable to see what those things did. I felt they should have reworked the menus to include this information and used forgo the subscreen entirely. Some sections of gameplay do use it, but they could have just turned it on only during them. The other issues have to do with completion. As with most Platinum games, a fair amount of collectibles in this game are located in absolutely ridiculous areas that you likely aren't going to find without a massive amount of time experimenting or a guide. And the final one has to do with scoring. The game grades you in sections based on how well you perform. There are a number of shooters in this game. These are fine during a normal play-through, but it becomes frustrating when going for completion because they test different skills from the rest of the game, so you end up having to spend a lot of time learning how to play these shooting sections effectively if you want all platinum ranks. Anyway, those are pretty small complaints for this great of a game. Although it's notorious for its difficulty, it has lower difficulty modes. I would suggest even non-hardcore players give this game a try, the easier difficulties are very accessible, and the game is pretty great to experience.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the Wii U's very best games and EASILY Platinum's best game ever. It's a blessing this got ported to other platforms. This game is unique in that...you don't have to remember a ton of complex combos like the usual action games (Ninja Gaiden, Devil May Cry, Bayonetta). There's a puzzle like element to every enemy; once you figure out how to take it down, that's that. Encounters are varied enough to test your skill in a lot of different scenarios, and higher difficulties change enemy spawns. It's not perfect, the first playthrough may have a lot of trial and error, it can be hard to see at times, there may be to many gimmicky shooting levels near the end of the game that drag every single Platinum game down. But even with its flaws, there is so much to love here and the game has SOUL. It will make you feel like a kid again because of how inspiring, hopeful, colorful it is. It embraces its cheesiness to the max and the characters actually develop as the story goes on. If I had to give it a number score, it would be a 9/10.EVEN IF YOU DON'T LIKE THE GAME ITS WORTH ONE PLAYTHROUGH BECAUSE THERE IS SO MANY MEMORABLE MOMENTS!

_childDocuments_.review: The Wonderful 101 is a special game for me. It is an action spectacle with all the bombast of Japanese Sentai and a love letter to Kamiya's obsession with arcade games. The cast is a lovable motley crew of heroes, called the Wonderful 100, each with individual quirks that add to their personality. The dialogue is fantastic cheese, with some of the best delivery I've heard in the industry. And the set pieces are frenetic but lead to triumphant moments that get the heart swelling with action hero pride. If I were to reduce the game to its core elements, to borrow from a thread I read from, I would say that it is 50% Bayonetta, 28% Okami, 20% Viewtiful Joe, and 3% Pikmin.In terms of the actual gameplay, the bulk of the game is used utilizing the "Wonder Liner" which is a tool that gives your band of heroes, The Wonderful Ones, their "Unite Morphs." The Unite Morphs use the heroes in your party to generate a weapon to attack foes, and each weapon has special properties that can make them more effective against certain foes or used defensively against different hazards. They can be akin to styles in other character action games, but in order to select them you go through a drawing process, similar to the Celestial Brush in Okami. There is a single button for main attacks that your leader character will use and a team attack for your entire squad. Additionally, there are defensive options that are HIGHLY recommended to acquire from the Wonder Mart, a place to get upgrades. These defensive powers allow you to either block and counter enemy attacks or dodge away from them. There are also a plethora of other tools that can be acquired by ranking up your Wonderful Ones, which can be done by playing through the game and using each of the powers. Finally, after each mission you will be scored based on time, combo, and damage that will award a medal. At the end of the operations the average of the medals will be taken to award a trophy, similar to other PlatinumGames titles.However, the game is also infamously difficult, which can be attributed to the obfuscation of certain useful mechanics that aren't told directly to the player. For example, the team attacks seem like just a way to deal minor damage to enemies, but they also act as a lock on, and with enough team attacks you can temporarily stun an enemy to either throw it or begin a juggling combo. Additionally, common fodder enemies can be recruited to your party after beating them to near death, which is EXTREMELY helpful in certain missions. And this is just the tip of the iceberg. The game requires the player to experiment to learn the mechanics, use their intuition with certain combat interactions, read the enemy files, or talk with other players, which can be frustrating for some people. Additionally, the high number of shmup style minigames can be a turn off, but I find them a fine gameplay change up from the combat. However, they can go on for a bit longer than necessary.While it may not be perfect, its highs out weigh any lows that he game has. The phrase "makes you feel" is overused, but personally it is a game that made me feel young again, and I appreciate that. I am glad that the game has another chance on new platforms, and encourage people to give it a shot. Stick with it and you will find a rewarding experience and one of the best finales in a game ever.TEAM, UNITE UP!

_childDocuments_.review: The Wonderful 101 is an excellent port of a Platinum game positively oozing with style, love for sentai heroics, and soul. The problem is, the soul it oozes is Hideki Kamiya's soul, so that means solidly 90% of your playtime is borderline unplayable trash minigames.Which is rather disappointing as TW101 has one of Platinum's more interesting combat systems. Make no mistake, this game is a stylish action fighter in the vein of Bayonetta. It may look like Pikmin, but all those extra guys are just there to transform into your weapons, of which you have nearly a dozen, each contributing something different to your loadout. You have juggles, blocks, dodges, command moves, it's all the good stuff you expect from this genre, just given a bit of polish and theme of a multi-man morphing hero team. And the way your command this team is quite clever. You draw them, as a physical line on the battlefield, into simple shapes to select your weapon. The whole thing is quite quick, like a fighting game move rather than an Okami tracing minigame. But the ways this line of people interact with the combat are quite interesting and far too numerous to mention in a review.It's not all sunshine and daisies though. A few too many of your weapons are entirely superfluous, used only to break down the barriers around various "color-coded" enemies immune to everything else, a far more restrictive measure than anything DmC ever did. In addition, since you are technically a one man leader surrounded by a team of 100, basically the size of an ant in terms of the action, the enemy hitboxes are incredibly generous, almost as bad as a MonHun boss or a Dark Souls enemy. These are especially egregious when the game sticks you in 1vs1 fights or 1 vs giant monster fights the engine simply cannot do justice to. And if the hitboxes don't get you, the game's woefully inadequate camera certainly will. And, of course, the game locks solidly 75% of your moveset, including vital parts of the combat system and nearly vital defensive/offensive hybrid powers, until you are nearly done with your first playthrough. Worse still, the amount of stuff you have to learn to play this game well guarantees you will not be anywhere near decent at this game until you've played it through a second time. (But don't worry, continues just pick you back up and refill your health where you died. It sounds insulting but given how much of this game there is to learn and how little it teaches you, this is merciful. You can see the end credits thanks to this.)Of course you could learn the game a lot better if Kamiya actually let you play it, but no, he's much more enamored with his minigames. Shmups, racing games, puzzles, once you clear world 2 the game starts to feel like every level is the awful Bayonetta missile level, just with a different new terrible minigame eating up 80% of the play time. He never references a good shmup. No Esprade here, you're gonna get a Zaxxon reference with worse pacing than Zaxxon and LIKE IT. Platinum has literally made a Star Fox game but nope, you get this barely functional Space Harrier garbage. AGAIN. Even the bosses are mostly overscripted kaiju, packed with QTEs, cinematic chase scenes, and just time wasting crap that doesn't resemble the combat system you really wish you could get back to practicing. The game demands replays for you to learn it and appreciate the intricate combat, but has so many terrible minigames that replaying it is almost intolerable.Now, you get Kamiya without anyone restraining him? You get some good too. The story is great, barring a certain character who makes MGSV Huey seem like a personable, trustworthy friend. It's quite funny and incredibly over the top in heroics and style. The finale is, if you are not repulsed by all the minigames, is about an hour and a half of the game constantly one-upping itself into complete Gurren Lagann-esque insanity. It is total nonsense and impossible to not grin and cheer like a madman. They went absolutely all out and it is a great reward for all the crap you went through to get there.The Wonderful 101 is very tough to rate because it is truly some excellent, compelling mechanics marred to some absolute trash design. Nobody has done to stylish action what Platinum has here*, but you have to meet it halfway, even more than you did Bayonetta 1 as it is nearly impossible to play around the bad parts because they are so prevalent. To put a number on this game is a crime, it has 8/10 bits attached to 2/10 bits attached to 9/10 bits and averaging them does justice to none of them, and all this attached to an absolutely beautiful 60 FPS port that eliminates the WiiU's awful load times. But I cannot in good conscience say "70% of this game is garbage and it is nearly impossible to replay in a satisfying manner" and not give it the Steam thumbs down. But this is still a game you probably have to play eventually if you have any love for action game combat mechanics just for the inventiveness here.*I think Astral Chain revised a lot of the clever design in this game and the result is that game I think stands out as Platinum's finest combat to date.

_childDocuments_.review: I always wanted to give this a try back when it released on the Wii U.  I’m a fan of PlatinumGames. I’m a fan of Kamiya. I kickstarted this version.  The game’s story is a bit wonky, but the gist is you control a horde of superheroes and you can all work together to morph into various objects to traverse the world and combat enemies to avert an alien invasion.  This game used the Wii U controller’s screen heavily in its design.  In order to acquire more superheroes into your horde, change weapons, or activate certain abilities, you had to draw on the second screen.  This has now been relegated to the second stick of your controller.  By the way, don’t bother trying to play this with a keyboard and mouse, you’ll have an awful time.  Anyway, this drawing works most of the time since most things you need to draw are simple lines, but there are some that are annoyingly difficult to get right.  For example, drawing your glider, which you need in various areas to glide to another section, requires you to draw a triangle.  Drawing this triangle I found annoyingly difficult, especially because drawing consumes power that regenerates over time.  So, as you sit there failing to draw a triangle, you’ll run out of power to draw, and you'll have to wait for it to recharge so you can try again.  The game also has some sections where previously on the Wii U you’d have to look and control your horde through the controller’s screen, because your view was obstructed otherwise in the main screen.  This doesn’t really make sense to me as to why this was even a thing, but it was.  Here now both views are put on the screen at once and it works about as good as it can.  Controlling your movement in these tight spaces can get pretty annoying as it’s hard to see or move around though. The other functions of the controller’s screen appeared to have been a leader selection and radar mode, you can activate these as a sub screen here pretty easily, though I rarely found myself using them.The combat system and world traversal is pretty simple.  You draw up your weapon and use it on enemies.  There are various upgrades and extra abilities to unlock to help you out.  You can consume certain items to recover or boost yourself or even throw things like rockets at enemies.  You pretty much have one attack button and you can dodge, jump, and block.  The combat itself is far too chaotic though.  The camera is non adjustable and most of the time it's hard to see what’s going on.  The HUD is huge, blocking out so much of the screen.  Character voice text bubbles block out a huge part of the screen, ironically as they’re trying to help you, but end up hurting you because you can’t see what’s going on anymore.  It’s easy to lose track of where you are since there’s usually a lot of large enemies on screen and you’re a small mass of tiny humans, with one somewhere in the middle being your actual controllable leader character.  The enemy design and certainly boss battles are unique to battle, assuming you can tell what’s even going on, but overall the game feels very repetitive very quickly and very chaotic.Visually the game looks ok. The character designs have a viewtiful joe aesthetic, but the rest of the game isn’t anything special to look at either technically or stylistically.  The game does support ultrawide resolutions. From direct comparison it seems to be proper support too.  No zooming or stretching both in game and in cutscenes.  The menu UI and HUD are far too big.This game seems like a mashup between Viewtiful Joe’s character style, Okami’s paint brush combat mechanics, and Beyonetta’s large combat setpieces.  In execution it feels messy and clumsy and I can’t help thinking that it being designed around the Wii U’s controller screen was a mistake.  I can’t see how it made the game better and it made this version even clumsier to use.  My love for VIewtiful Joe, Okami, and Beyonetta individually didn’t help me love this game either.  It’s a decent remaster.  As a standalone game though, it’s just not very good.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:1. It's a Platinum Game and carries with it all the Pros associated with a core Platinum Game. If you like Platinum Games then this is really the only pro you need. If you don't then continue on.(If you like platinum games you will like this)2. This is a good port/remaster of the Wonderful 101. There have been a few tweaks, especially in that they are bringing over a 2 screen game to one screen, but for the most part they all work really well. 60 Fps 1080p works like a dream.(If you already liked the original 101 you will like this)3. The story is amazing. It starts with 1 teacher collecting collecting kids on a bus and ends in space doing Gurren Lagann level fights.4. The sound is spectacular. When a game is so well designed you can identify exactly when a button should be pushed based off of a noise off screen, you've got good sound design.5. The graphics are awesome, It is a semi action game semi comic book character design.6. Ran consistently at the max FPS allowed (more on this in the cons)Cons:1. Certain actions in the game are based off of the frames. I unfortunately streamed 16 hours before i realized I had V-sync on. This made dialogue slightly off sync sometimes, and added in an inconsistency to the combat drawing system, which requires rather precise inputs. It was a running gag that i was apparently very bad at doing shapes. Once i finally realized i had V-sync on, dialogue immediately synced up, the game ran noticably smoother, and all of the sudden I was chaining together the exact attacks i wanted to when i wanted to them.DO NOT USE V SYNC and if you have a potato for a computer just know that the game might be more difficult than intended though not impossible.2. Sensitivity, Your controllers sensitivity might work against you, the game's combat system uses shape recognition and drawing with an analog stick. If your controller is so sensitive that releasing the stick causes an entirely new input, you may have problems. This sensitivity combined with the previous frame dependency, might cause you to experience problems while running the game. You can adapt to it, but be prepared to make a ton of whips when you wanted hammers, until you do.3. Not every screen was upscaled. like 98% of the game was remastered and scales decently, but some scenes (notably still pictures) will randomly stick out as low quality. It is more of a testament to how well everything else looks that makes these extremely rare pictures look low res. (Im looking at you end credits picture) Nothing in the gameplay will be affected and they even did up the model viewers correctly as well, but a handful of graphics didn't receive any love.4. Lastly, there have been a few changes to the original game, in terms of what abilties you have and how much they cost. If you played the original 101 be aware of these changes. Most of these were to improve things that players complained about but there might be some differences to what you remember. for instance and maybe I'm remembering wrong from way back when but you have to buy the ability for your team to unite morphs with you, and you have to purchase for each new member. I.E. you purchase 1 extra active unite morph, and then you can purchase the ability to have another simultaneous unite morph individually. Requiring 2 semi expensive purchases to use 3 fists at the same time. (the Team unite morph thing might have always been that way, but not in any of the demos.).

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Pikmin, but if the Pikmin were Super Sentai/Mighty Morphin Power Rangers, and that's kinda what Wonderful 101 is like. The story is fantastic, with plenty of jaw-dropping, awe-inspiring and just plain, fist pumping moments abound. The soundtrack is great and really heightens the game's awesome moments, especially the new vocal tracks they've included in the Remastered Edition. The voice acting is pretty solid in my opinion, and I love the character interactions and how they all get along. The writing for the humor is also pretty solid.The combat is fun and fluid, especially by the second half to the end, and it's deeper than it looks at first glance. It'll take some practice, and at first it might not seem all that great, but by the end of the game you'll be pulling off slick combos and using every Unite Morph in a combo with ease. My only two gripes with this game are drawing the Unite Morphs/how the game interprets them, and how the game handles the Wii U gamepad sections. Drawing the Unite Morphs works for the most part, but since drawing them was meant to be done on the Wii U Gamepad, it feels a bit wonky on a stick, and even when you have the hang of it and can draw them flawlessly, the game can sometimes interpret it as a different Unite Morph, causing you to not get what you wanted, or at least that's how it was for me every now and then. As for the Wii U Gamepad sections, there are these specific parts of some levels where you have to solve a puzzle to continue, and you would look at the Wii U Gamepad for the puzzle. These levels are done with an up close, third-person perspective rather than the zoomed out perspective that most of the game has.  What would normally be displayed on the Wii U Gamepad is instead displayed in a small picture-in-picture in the lower right corner of your screen. The only reason I have a gripe with this is that it can make some of the levels confusing to navigate, especially since the right stick controls both the camera and the Unite Morphs in these levels. However, they are pretty short sections, so if you get stuck, you won't be for long. The game's difficulty is pretty solid, but not so hard that it'd make you wanna quit. As of this review, (which I am writing after having just finished the game) , I have only completed the game on normal, so I can't say anything about the other difficulties.This game is an absolute BANGER and I highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys character action games or anything made by PlatinumGames, who also made this game coincidentally.

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who is a fan of Platinum, this is a must-play for you. Wonderful 101 oozes with creativity, fun and passion. If you like action, it's got it. If you like comedy, it's got it. Unique gameplay, got it. Sentai heroes, unexpected turns, great dialogue, over the top action, got it, got it, got it, and definitely got it!This game very much feels like a spiritual successor to the Viewtiful Joe games, with many throwbacks and small references here and there for the eagle eyed fan. However it still maintains its own sense of identity and style.The combat can take a little time to get used to, however it's one of those things that can be incredibly satisfying when you master it. This game is just fun, and that's definitely something that we need during these times. I backed this game on Kickstarter for the Switch physical version, but was given the steam code due to the covid-19 delays. I look forward to having an excuse to play this again on the switch when I get my copy.

If you like Platinum's other titles then you owe it to yourself to get this, this game is one of their best and a must buy for people who love action games.

_childDocuments_.review: This is without a doubt one of my all time favorite video games, needless to say I was quite excited to be a backer for this Kickstarter project.
