_childDocuments_.review: When the announcement for the PC port of The Wonderful 101 was announced, I was glee with joy. It was a unique Platinum game directed by the big man himself, Hideki Kamiya. I had been foretold of how amazing this game is by peers and online personalities, so much so that I went into this game with high expectations. Though this game is still technically decent, I feel like I’ve been ultimately let down.In The Wonderful 101, you control up to 100 individuals at the same time, morphing into various shapes by drawing them using the right analog stick to take down all sorts of no-gooders. Simple concept, right? Well, for some reason you have an energy gauge that seems to do nothing but detract from your experience. Everything but attacking consumes energy, even parrying and dodging, thus leaving you open to attacks. Speaking of those two, you actually don’t start out with them and have to buy them from the shop, and one of the very first enemies you encounter is one that absolutely requires you to parry against them. When you get hit, your party is separated and everyone within the hit radius is knocked out temporarily, and you have to run around waking everyone up to be at your prime fighting capabilities. Also, you need to have a certain amount of available party members in order to either dodge or parry, so if you get hit or if an attack barely misses you but hits a good chunk of your party, you’ll be left completely defenseless. Also, during certain boss battles that take up the entire chapter, you’ll engage something known as Unlimited Form, which gets a super cool and flashy cutscene every time and makes your team look flashy, and when it comes to gameplay, it does nothing. At all. What is even the point of it?The enemy variety in this game is good, and some require you to utilize specific weapons to take them out. Unfortunately, while that would normally be fun, some enemies are just beyond irritating to deal with. For instance, spikes are dealt with using the whip, and there’s an enemy that has spiked armor all around. You have to wail on him using the whip until he takes enough damage and then you can attack to strip him of one piece of his armor, and it’s excruciatingly slow to do. There’s another enemy that’s shaped like a turtle and the only means to deal damage to it is to use the hammer, arguably the slowest weapon in your arsenal that does just as much damage as the fist weapon you get from the beginning of the game. It takes forever to take down that enemy, and even worse, that enemy almost always spawns as twins.I wish I liked this game more because the setpieces you’re thrown into are absolutely a blast to play. It’s not everyday where you fight a three-headed dragon in the air while it’s carrying the Statue of Liberty in its mouth, and that’s just the first chapter of the game. That said, this game does like to switch genres every now and then to a different playstyle for a brief period, and while normally this was very much welcome in games like Bayonetta, I actually hate them here. There’s a schmup section that’s aimed at a diagonal angle so you can hardly see what’s ahead of you, in addition to your main firing weapon doing a pitiful amount of damage against enemies. There’s multiple sections where you need to steer a ship, but in order to do so, you have to use the fist weapon to grab the steering wheel in order to be able to move the ship around and fire, but if you get hit once, you get knocked back and have to wait for your party to get up again so you can form the fist again to grab the steering wheel again, and on top of that the ship has its own separate health bar and during that brief moment where you’re not in control, you can crash into everything in your way and instantly die. I was doing pretty well on one run and then got hit once and immediately lost all of my health during the brief period where my team was knocked out. Also, during that section, the enemy can throw slimes at you at stop you from reaching the wheel, and at no point does the game explain that you have to use the sword to get rid of the slime (and furthermore, that makes no sense). In another minigame, you had to play a section that was clearly inspired by Punch-Out… without ever explaining how Punch-Out works. I took so long in that section because I had never played Punch-Out before and I didn’t know what I was doing wrong. Did I forget to mention that the boss during that section also has an unfair instant-kill?Something that bothers me greatly about the enemies is that they rarely seem to take any hitstun. Instead of taking control and changing the battlefield to your favor, you have to constantly dance around enemies. I’ve gotten so used to games like Devil May Cry and Bayonetta that this element was incredibly off-putting, and if you thought enemies not taking hitstun was bad, it’s even worse with bosses. Much like with every Kamiya game, there’s a rival character you fight consistently throughout the game, and it’s amazing how this little element has made him incredibly unfun to fight. On top of that, that rival’s hitboxes are stupidly big, so you’ll get hit by attacks that normally shouldn’t have hit you, even if you’re very far away and the boss is off-camera. For some reason, the game likes to give you heals, even to full health, at random intervals while you’re fighting, or increase your health bar for no reason. This is exacerbated even further during the rival fight where drawing a line amongst his soldiers can instantly heal you fully. Yes, I did have the Wonder Liner skill that does damage enemies while you’re drawing, but at no point does it say that it heals you. The worst of all is that you fight this rival character that’s unfun to fight five times in the game. Yes, Devil May Cry 3 let you fight the rival character three times, but every time was different and so the strategy changed for each time. Also, that boss could take hitstun! Here, it’s the same fight over and over again, and every time it takes forever to do because he hardly gives you any openings to damage him. What should have been my favorite aspect of the game ended up being my least favorite. Oh, and for some other boss fights, you can be standing on a platform that has its own health bar which you need to protect, and said platform can easily take hits you can’t do anything about. Even worse, there are sections in the game where you fight alone, where you cannot dodge, cannot block and have access to only one weapon, and those segments are dreadful.So what do I like about this game? Well aside from the awesome setpieces and the overall wonderful superhero flair this game has, it just feels great to play. All the weapons (except for the hammer; it sucks) are such a blast to use. Some of the inputs for special moves are a little weird, but you don’t need to use them all that often and even then you can easily get used to them if you’ve played action games long enough. The game also becomes incredibly fun to play when you unlock the Multi-Unite skill, allowing you to draw multiple weapons at a time to dish out a humongous amount of damage. Watching the health bars of bigger enemies that previously gave me trouble deplete in mere seconds gives me so much joy. While I hated the QTEs in Bayonetta, here Kamiya has learned from his past mistakes and actually figured out how to make them fun. You’re given more than enough time to react and even if you don’t, it never counts as a death. For most of these QTEs, you have to draw the weapon you need to get out of that sticky situation, and it just works. Amazing. The writing is also Kamiya-grade cheeky fun and I am all for it. I just love how silly and goofy this man’s games get.Despite everything, I still do recommend this game, though it’s a very very weak recommendation. Play other better games first, then when you’ve seen everything, and only then do you pick up this game. Such a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: As a "Remaster", it doesn't seem all that great as it seems like all it did was have better loading times and it can run on better hardware now. I've had a few crashes in-game and even during cutscenes; I've even had crashes during boss missions, which don't auto-save until the end, making me have to redo the boss as a result. Even the graphics look like they've just been taken from the Wii U without much polish.Its story is themed around the Japanese transformation super hero stuff, and it can be very entertaining with how over-the-top it gets with its camp and goofiness all the way to the end. You can choose between EN and JP audio and they're both exaggerated, however, the subtitle timings of either are different as well so the text or voices can move too fast or too slow.It's a character-action arcade game overall, except you're controlling one hero who's leading many more, and you combine them to make giant weapons and other utilities to save the day. To make said weapons, you make use of the drawing mechanic in the game, which can be very frustrating to do, especially when it can be interrupted when you least expect it, like when the camera zooms in and something like an environmental hazard or enemy you can't touch is off-screen as you can't make drawings on those.The combat itself can be great when you get it working, but alongside these frustrations comes a big learning curve as well, especially since the game doesn't teach you a whole lot.The camera is almost always at an isometric angle. Thanks to that, it makes inputting directional-based inputs a lot easier. However, that angle also comes with its problems, never mind the weird pseudo-dual-monitor aspect of the game.The depth perception for platforming sections can be confusing. There's supposed to be a big colored ring under you to tell you where you are, but when there's no floor under you or your teammates are covering that ring, you're left to do some guesswork. You're almost always required to make yourself visible to the camera, and the environment doesn't always become transparent to show your character either; this is especially more of a problem against larger enemies as you'll constantly be trying to make sure they don't block your view so you don't accidentally touch a spike or get blindsided by a smaller attack.The biggest problem with the camera is that it tends to zoom in when you just want a better view of the battlefield so you can keep an eye on enemies that are farther away. I'm guessing you're supposed to react to audio cues, but there can be so much noise going on that the sound of incoming attacks can get drowned out. No matter how much you zoom out, the game will always zoom in again at some point for whatever reason, even when there's only one enemy left.When you actually get the combat working, it's very satisfying to do, but there's so much wonkiness to try and keep in mind, namely the camera itself.A single playthrough is fine for its ridiculous story, but for a Platinum game, it's really frustrating to even tolerate replaying; even some of the collectibles are frustrating to acquire, namely the ones that require you to do all the secret missions in each level on three specific difficulties.It takes around a dozen hours to finish the first playthrough as well, which is pretty long for what's essentially an arcade game.

Playing at higher resolution (1440p+) also seems to introduce artifacting on menus. Hopefully will be fixed.- The combat controls can be difficult to a good grasp on. If not, take a look at youtube videos as this is just a pure action game and you have to comfortable with that in order to enjoy it. I love this game and I'm so glad it didn't die on the Wii U.

_childDocuments_.review: This game pretty much exemplifies why using the right stick for camera control in 3D action games is the standard, automatic camera for something like this simply doesnt work well enough. Past the first mission almost every single fight is going to be in arenas too big for even the most zoomed out level of view, which the game won't keep to anyway as it constantly zooms in and out on its own, or full of clutter and giant enemies that obscure your position or even their own attacks from view with their bulk. There's also loads of gimmicky platforming segments where the floor tilts in all sorts of directions and your position and the position of platforms you need to jump to become impossible to accurately determine, or segments where your characters go into an enclosed area and it switches to an awful imitation of regular camera controls anyway. These segments are frequently meant to utilize the dual screen gimmick of the original console the game was on, the WiiU, and though I havent finished the game yet to see every implemenation of this gimmick I can say from the ones I have seen that it's never been worth the headache that it is to try and navigate those segments. The second screen for all of them has basically just been a stationary view of something simple that could have just been put in a little window on the original screen anyway, which is how it's implemented in this version, and that I guess just goes to show how ill-conceived the WiiU was in general.The line drawing gimmick that takes the place of proper camera control is in no way a worthy exchange, past the first two weapons the shapes become far too similar for clear tracing in-combat and the quirk of deciding how big a weapon you get by how big you draw the line is pointless as not only is bigger always better but due to the imprecise nature of drawing with an analog stick you basically can't get the shapes properly differentiated at small sizes anyway.At least the cutscenes are funny I guess

_childDocuments_.review: The Wondeful 101 is a fantastic game whose developers put a lot of heart and soul into...but who unfortunately didn't really put a whole lot of thought into the making of the PC Port.Performance-wise the game runs perfectly fine - with my various much average rig still able to chug along at 60 FPS - but there are currently a few issues on some of the more technical / mechanical things that ruin the experience.The game does not like dual monitors at all - with mine for example no matter if I went for a locked fullscreen it'd default to borderless, with my mouse flying off into my second monitor and every click sending the game into a minimized state.The Wonder-Liner feature also works incredibly awfully with Mouse and Keyboard - the Wonder Liner is controlled entirely by the mouse, which in theory SHOULD work even better than an analog stick, yet it has it's own heaps of problems.Primarily the first issue is that Wonder Liner has a mind of it's own, with the line itself starting or turning however it wants to without  player input.A simple line to Unite Sword for example will almost always start off going into the wrong direction from your character, and in the process somehow form up for something like Unite Gun.In Post - Game is fun but hampered by technical aspects, and until these issues are addressed I cannot really recommend the game to anyone - or at least anyone without a controller.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful this is not. On a presentation and the general idea of the game goes, I absolutely love it! I wish I could recommend this game, but its design philosophy is ass backwards. A game with THIS steep of a learning curve is in desperate need of a tutorial to ease people into it. I shouldnt have to go to youtube or forum posts to figure out essential mechanics. Thats flat out bad game design. I dont understand how people can defend this by saying "Well once you get past it then the game becomes fun" when all the game has to do is just give a 10-15 minute tutorial. This is a great example of another remaster that doesnt fix huge issues with the original game; just being content with doing the bare minimum. Boss fights are annoying and not fun at all. The same can be said about certain enemies (The tanks can fall into the deepest pit in HELL) and the core gameplay loop while it is fun, I can see it getting pretty repetitive pretty quickly. 'The Wonderful 101' has some really amazing qualities with its presentation, writing, and a interesting, original idea. However, it succumbs to its horrid camera, terribly explained mechanics, and bad boss fights. Wonderful 101? More like Frustrating 101BEST ASPECT: ART DESIGN WORST ASPECT: POORLY EXPLAINED MECHANICSFINAL SCORE: 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game, but it's such a frustrating experience to try and play.The wonder-line controls simply do not function with a mouse. They are  close to working, but a portion of the time, starting a wonder-line creates a phantom input that shoots your line out in a random direction. This, obviously, completely destroys whatever shape you were attempting to draw, and you may have to re-start the line several times in a row before you get an input that starts on neutral.This is something you're supposed to be doing quickly and accurately in combat, which is impossible given this bug. I have failed several very easy quicktime events simply because I was unable to draw a straight line in time.This might be alleviated if you are using a controller, but the problems with this port don't stop there.Sometimes, the game will randomly pause. It won't give you a menu or any way to un-pause, it will just stop with the "paused" text on screen. Hearsay says it's a poorly-disguised loading system, but regardless of the reason, on this platform it's equivalent to a crash- since it never unpauses, and there is no way to force it out of the pause. Combined with the stingy use of checkpoints, I've had to re-do several entire missions simply because the game softlocked itself for no reason at the last moment.Additionally, this is a port of a game originally for the Wii U. While most of the time, the two-screen mechanics are irrelevant, there are a few sections of the game where looking at both screens becomes important.I don't envy the game designers who had to make that work on a single screen, but as is, they really don't work very well with the pop-up window system the game has to emulate that. They are technically playable but it's highly disorienting. It's possible that there is no good way to port those sections, but the fact remains that they were ported badly.Finally, the control mapping just... doesn't make sense. There is no ability to rebind keys, and there are several sections of the game where the controls are just bonkers: left and right punch bound to right mouse and  mouse respectively, for example (yes, left punch is bound to  mouse). There must be something tightly coupling inputs under the hood for them to do that, since there is no way those were picked on purpose.It makes me wonder why they even bothered with keyboard controls at all. They were clearly unable to change the input system to work well with a mouse and keyboard, why not save everyone the trouble and just declare "get a controller or go home"?The game itself is fantastic, I suffered through the whole thing on a keyboard just to experience the whole thing. I can't recommend that experience to anyone else though.If you want to play with a controller, the game is good but the port is a technical mess. If you want to play with a keyboard, don't.

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part I love Platinum Games. Nier: Automata, Bayonetta and Okami are regarded as some of the best games ever made and for good reason. I also really liked Vanquished, Astral Chain and a few of their other less successful titles too so I was sure I would at least have a good time with The Wonderful 101. I mean though there would be at least one or two mechanics, story aspects or visual style choices I couldn't get in to in every game they made, over all I would love the majority of the experience.However, I have basically hated every minute of my short time with The Wonderful 101. It really comes across as a collection of all the stuff I found dull or annoy in their other titles. It takes the clunky painting mechanics of Okami, makes them happen in real-time gameplay (also I feel it was a lot more punishing about accuracy than Okami). The characters and story as far as I can see are all 2 dimensional cliches like in Vanquished. The progression system is just a shop between missions like in Bayonetta rather than through exploration and achievement. Though I respect that the game is about 8 years old now -- so can't be expected to look amazing like Nier -- it also doesn't have a timeless art style like Okami so this many years down the line comes off as pretty ugly to me. Finally, I also felt that the game had far more mechanics than it needed considering the player has barely any moves for a Platinum game.I know this game has a cult following. So take this review for what it is. Maybe I just didn't play the game in the right era for it. Maybe it doesn't work anywhere near as well without the old Wii U controls. Maybe I just didn't give it enough time to learn what makes it 'fun' in the first place. I don't want to hate on your good time, but I also can't pretend that I get it...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty much Kamiya in a nutshell, it feels and looks like a mix of Viewtiful Joe, Bayonetta, and Okami (and some elements from Pikmin), problem is, this game was clearly designed with the Wii U pad in mind, and the right analog stick just doesnt work the same.I dont know if they will "fix" this in the future, because I dont know if it can be fixed when the game was designed with an especific system in mind.It is a shame, because the game has a lot of charm, and Viewtiful Joe is a game I love, but the controls, at least for me, just dont work.Game is well optimized, but beware, it was released 7 years ago on a system that pretty much was running on 10 years old hardware, so dont expect anything spectacular.The art style is great, but you can tell is an old game.If you are a Platinum fan, I would suggest to give it a try, you can always ask for a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: YET ANOTHER CRAPPY PC PORT BY PLATINUM GAMES. WHERE THE HELL ARE THE CONTROLLER BUTTON PROMPTS?????LEt me get this clear, I'm still angry for the Nier Automata PC port and how little effort and care was put into it. You can't play it in 1080p resolution, and it has several other graphic issues that make using a THIRD party tool a necessity. They didn't even fix it with time, notr when they re-launched the game as a Something Something Edition. I still don't forget it for that. That's where I come from to this game, plus having seen it ages ago and thinking the concept was fun.Now, this game is probably fun, in its wacky japanese way (which is already a bit hit and miss). But in this PC port, this turns against the game. The unfamiliarity and rushed nature of the action are severely hindered by the LACK OF CONTROLLER BUTTON PROMPTS. So you're given instructions to use KEYS and mouse motions while holding your controller, and you have NO CLUE to what to press in each moment. Granted, with time you'll learn the basic stuff. But the game is about throwing new stuff at you all the time. So for a game launched in 2020 it's unforgiveable to not have button prompts for the defacto standard controller for PC which is XBOX 360/One (Xinput, that is).I mean, they DID have to code the keyboard + mouse prompts, right? those are new to PC. Why not do it for controller too???? It makes me mad.Otherwise the game has potential. The visuals are a bit crappy, but it's an old game. The perspective is confusing and the action is really really hard to follow. But it's okay.To be honest, I'm holding off to decide whether I return it or not to see if they implement the controller prompts. Believe me, knowing what to do with the controls at any given time is a BIG part of the game flow.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR play Bayonetta, Vanquish, MGR or anything else by Platinum instead.Probably the worst Platinum game - well, the worst one with a budget at least. Everything the game tries to differentiate itself from it's vastly superior siblings ends up either failing or being a doomed gimmick. Instead of using a button to swap weapons, you need to draw a shape with your analog and mostly mash one button, which slows combat and feels bad in general; Instead of a simple counter button, like a dodge or block, the game relies a lot on QTEs and encounter/context specific gimmicks for your defensive options.What encounter/context specific gimmicks? Well, whatever the game feels like doing, I guess. In some encounters you need to have a specific hero out and be in a certain position, or attack with a specific hero, or jump at the right time to trigger a QTE, or block having a certain amount of heroes in your party. None of this is explained to you, mainly because it can't be, it's just random nonsense.The game has a serious hard on for not explaining anything and mistakes obscure, poorly explained mechanics for depth - your block only works on certain attacks, and you need energy to use it, and actually it doesn't work on all attacks it should and that can be for different reasons and many bosses are just a gimmick fight with several QTEs where you need to guess what you're supposed to do and Jesus Christ, did Platinum make this? They seem to have completely forgotten that the combat in their game is cool because you, the player, is making those crazy combos and perfect dodges/counters happen, not the developers.The game also has some severe camera problems; for some reason - I'm guessing the Wii u hardware couldn't take it - the camera is REALLY zoomed in a lot of sections (even with the "zoomed out" camera) and the map designers were particularly inspired in this game, creating lots of moving and twisting set pieces... with a zoomed in camera...  when you control a dude with a hundred other dudes nearby... while you're trying to draw stuff on the screen. Ok.A few extra bullet points: the port is pretty bad and looks terrible on high resolutions (in general, to be honest); The Wii-u screen, which you need to use for some parts, is just shoved on the lower-right corner of your screen - by the way, remember the whole "gimmick and QTEs" complaint? Yeah, it's this bad; the game loves on-rails and "different control-scheme" sections where you pilot ships and stuff like that, so I hope you like them too. They're always the best part of every Platinum game, right?; the menu's are an affront to God Himself.I'm certain the game gets better after a first playthrough, since the player will know the crazy gimmicks - at least most of them, certainly (hopefully?) - and possess the obscure knowledge needed to play this like any other of Platinum's games, which they could play right now, with no extra effort or having to deal with non-orthogonal mechanics, instead of... instead of this game. Oh. Ooooh.Still probably worth it if it's on sale and you're also a fan - just don't feel bad for dropping it midway through because it's boring and frustrating.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I can finally see why no one bought it on the WiiU, and now so can you.tl:dr; The game is a visual and unreadable mess during gameplay and the controls are frustrating and limited. Most character designs are fantastic and there's a fair bit of fun to be had if you are prepared to suffer through a very frustrating first playthrough, but only if you're into this aesthetic and unconventional stylish action games. Unfortunately many didn't stick around back when this released on the WiiU, and since nothing has changed or improved, the same fate might await this current gen port.The game suffers terribly from not having an effective and clear visual style, it especially struggles with communicating where you are in relation to special effects or enemies. It is hard to spot where your characters are a lot of the time since the indicator shows up behind your own characters, enemies and stage geometry.Judging when enemies attack is the game's biggest challenge, but not for the right reasons. Huge enemies are mostly fine since they have long wind ups, but the medium sized enemies, especially non-humanoid ones, don't effectively convey their attacks and the worst offenders briefly squash and stretch in place right before any action or attack. The tiny enemies that accompany them are, like your characters, very hard to spot in most situations where the screen is cluttered with action or stage effects, so they end up breaking up your formation and knocking you down. I can imagine the animations work fine in a vacuum but the game insists on showering the screen with an overabundance of visual noise for every action, the challenge ends up being trying to spot what you're supposed to hit or what just hit you in the middle of the flashy fireworks.Since W101 was created and developed by the same people that made Bayonetta and MGR Revengeance, you would hope they'd also implement a similar visual flash and sound cue before an enemy strikes, but that is completely absent here. In such a visually cluttered game like this, it's hard to imagine not one single person at Platinum thought to implement it when every other game they've made includes it. The general gameplay is tedious and frustrating, micromanaging the characters just to be able to press an attack button with a gauge that limits how often you can use it doesn't instill you with the classic Platinum confidence you would expect from them.The waggle mechanic to recover from a knockdown has always been annoying and is still annoying here. The visual cue to wake up also gets covered by everything on screen, visibility and clarity is unfortunately a very big and and a very common problem in this game.The lack of lock-on I think really hurts the game, because the soft lock-on gives small virtually invisible enemies priority over bosses and larger enemies, you end up in situations where you're wasting your meter.The game is also full of abrupt and mostly unexplained gimmick levels and hazards, these are often coupled with instakill QTEs. Many times the game introduces new mechanics or situations but doesn't tell you which hazards kill you or what triggers a quick time event until you get hit by it. Cutscenes in this game tend to drag on for too long and, outside of the amazing character designs, the very limited visual style doesn't work here. There are intents of masking the visual novel style text boxes with small animations by the characters on screen while they talk, but all that does is remind you that the characters don't have anything important to say. There are also some few unskippable cutscenes such as transformation sequences.Unlocking moves takes too long on your first playthrough and you end up being severely limited in your options against enemies so you end up having to play the waiting game until they do something you can counter. This makes your first impression of the game incredibly awkward since you are deliberately cut off from core movement options, the game is afraid to overwhelm you but at the same time is afraid to give you a dodge move or a parry move. You'll have to buy those moves in the shop individually.The drawing function to change weapons is imprecise and cumbersome even with a stick, it could've easily been a radial menu or a togglable weapon button, especially for this port. The touch screen functionality is equally uninteresting and underused, on the PC port it takes up a fair bit of the screen (though you can change the size of it or simply leave it disabled and not miss out on anything). There's also no way to use two screens with the game.The game doesn't have a "retry from last checkpoint" button and instead lets you continue right where you died with full HP and a score penalty. An understandable decision, but there's no reason why it couldn't have both. If you ever want to maintain your rank you have to go back to the main menu and click through more menus to retry the stage. It ends up being a very tedious exercise if you're trying to get platinum rank.The menus in this game are very annoying to get through, there are four tiers of menus and it often leads to having to press the back button a total of 4 times and then confirm you want to exit each submenu if you want to get back to the game after shopping for skills.7 years and a Kickstarter later and unfortunately not a single QOL improvement was made and not a single lesson learned.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot to say about this game, and towards the end, I had so much more negative to say than positive. Long story short, I don't think I can recommend anyone play this game. Watching it, though, is a whole matter else entirely.***INCOMING WALL OF RANT***During its amazing parts (and there are many, many of them), TW101 is an over-the-top, adrenaline-in-your-eyeballs Super Sentai anime come to life. The cinematography, voice acting, art design, humor, and incredible set pieces all make you feel like you're watching a Saturday morning cartoon show on steroids. It's funny in a lot of places, stirs you up into a heroic frenzy in others (especially with the fantastic orchestral soundtrack), and it's also one of the most stylish games I've ever played this side of Persona 5.If you're watching someone play through it and seeing the set pieces and bombastic boss fights and all the hilarious and awesome callbacks to other games and genres, it's easy to get caught up in the action and think that it's equally fun to play, but the truth is, it really isn't.I get that Platinum Games want you to git gud so that you can play their games in the most stylish and optimal ways humanly possible. But TW101 definitely feels like a game stuck in 2013 with its mechanics, UI, and pacing. OK, here I go.I'm not even going to complain about the disco fireworks explosion vomit that the combat is because there are ways around it when you understand the systems, but why in Kamiya's sake does everything grind to a halt when you acquire new members? They couldn't be introduced in the sidebar like all the temps, or at the end of operations since you're forced to watch the score screen anyway with no way out? Or how about un-telegraphed enemy moves, random team scatter, or hell, random moments of getting stuck or stunned without any indication of what's happening?And speaking of sidebars, it really ground my gears to have the UI take over 2/3 (or more) of the screen when events happened, switch between zoom distances arbitrarily, and the ultimate worst, when the endgame narration started happening while in the midst of combat. What the actual F. Let me fight, or give me a cutscene, stop trying to do both TERRIBLY.***INCOMING SPOILERS***As for the endgame, just...wow. This is the first time I wanted to throw my controller at the wall for having finished a game. The repetition is absolutely mind-boggling. HA HA RED IS BEING EXTRA. HA HA BLUE BEING A DUM DUM. HMM WHY DON'T WE PIVOT THE ENTIRE PLOT AROUND AN ANNOYING LITTLE ♥♥♥♥ OF A KID?How about that last boss, eh? Like that fight? How about 15 million final forms? Oh you want final forms for your team, its robot, AND its ship as well? Got you fam. Oh wait, you wanted credits? Nah, you don't, how about grinding even more for a pointless score while it rolls instead of being able to kick back and relax after breaking your pad or keyboard from mashing? Now how about replaying the intro, unskippable, but now YOU'RE the annoying little ♥♥♥♥? Good times! Oh wait, the credits wasn't done, how about 35 billion different endings before you get sent back to the menu to finish (because you bet your ass the huge "THANKS FOR PLAYING" banner was only ending 5 of 509345)?It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ incredible, is what it is. You should see and hear how much I wanted to Wonder Punch my own face playing through the last 30 minutes. I want to recommend this game, I really do, but I just can't. In my overwhelmingly frustrated opinion, the most wonderful move you can do is watch someone else play it.

_childDocuments_.review: How the hell does this game have less than 1,000 reviews?This is probably the most creative game Platinum has ever developed, taking clear influence from their previous works (both at Platinum and Clover Studios), along with some Pikmin influence, yet making something one-of-a-kind out of the elements it combines. The combat is interesting, encouraging the player to chain as many Unite Morph attacks in as little time as possible without getting hit in each encounter. It takes the spectacle fighter formula Platinum has perfected, and makes a gameplay loop that, while proudly wears it's influences on it's sleeve, I cannot directly compare to any other game out there. All of this is thanks to the game's Unite Morph concept and the unique control scheme that compliments the system well.The art direction is beautiful and captivating. It's a really colorful game with playful, toy-like setpieces that are a joy to journey through and do some light exploration in. These setpieces have exhilarating spectacle going on, from giant robots collapsing city streets and skyscrapers, to trekking through crumbling ancient ruins. The game has a wide variety of setpieces to play through, and it keeps things interesting through the game's runtime!The storyline is there. It is not exactly an amazing story, being a really simple good vs. evil story between a group of superheroes and alien invaders. With that being said, it is still entertaining throughout the cutscenes and dialogue, with funny comedy playing throughout that pays homage to the sentai shows that influenced it. The QTE fails in particular are amazing and some of the best QTEs ever made because of that. The story does drop from simply written to lazily written by the third act, but that does not bother me thanks to the comedic writing staying cosistantly strong throughout.It's not a perfect experience. I do feel the controls can be janky at times, with some Unite Morphs being a bit harder to do properly than others. This especially applies to certain Unite Morphs you get if you apply certain cheat codes into the game, where you need to be more precise to avoid the system confusing certain unite morphs with others. There is also keyboard and mouse support, but the game is best played on a controller due to how poor the mouse support is. That is a shame, since I was hoping drawing shapes with the mouse would be a good experience. But at least the right analog stick isn't too bad for what the game wants you to draw.Ultimately, I recommend The Wonderful 101. It is an incredibly unique game that is worth at least one playthrough, even if it is not as good as some of Platinum's other titles, such as Bayonetta or Metal Gear Rising. This game is underrated, and I wish more people into spectacle fighters tried out this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I still own my WiiU copy of TW101, this game is such a gem. I was kind of surprised to see Nintendo let this one go multiplatform but then again, seeing that nobody really cared about the game it makes sense. Everybody keeps complaining about developers only putting out uninspired sequels but then they also ignore unique and fun new IPs like this one.The game has a very fun hack n slash combat in which you draw the weapons you want to use via the right stick, e. g. a circle for a fist, a line for a sword, etc. In order to draw you need to recruit units that can be found throughout the different missions. Them more units you have the bigger the shape so you deal more damage damage. I will say though that the drawing can be a bit finicky, especially later on when you have shapes that can overlap a bit. The drawing system also feels terrible to use in missions that limit your available units so you have to rely on small shapes.The writing is super funny with constant bartering between the party members. The game relies heavily on stereotypes but not in a malicious way, it's just fun. The visuals have also aged really well with its colourful artstyle.I will say though that revisiting the game has made me more aware of its frustrating aspects:- The camera often doesn't play nice, it's way too zoomed in during fights and you can very often get hit from attacks/projectiles that you can't even see because the camera doesn't allow for it.- Blocking and dodging have to be purchased from the shop after the prologue but the game doesn't tell you so. If you don't buy it (which I didn't) you will have an absolute terrible experience in the first mission. When you look at the achievement completion rate you will see that only 80 % of the players finished the prologue. But then there is also a massive drop off for chapters 1 to 3 which only 20 % of the players finished. I wouldn't be surprised if a lot of players ended up quitting during chapter 1 because they didn't buy the block in the shop- Another reason people probably quit is how difficult the game is. The game really punishes the players. If you get hit, not only do you lose a lot of health but your units get knocked out and cannot be used until they recover after like 10 seconds or before you touch them. So getting hit means that you lose HP, cannot attack yourself and cannot block/dodge because that also requires units.- The game is also a bit too long for this genre with its roughly 15 hours. There are a couple of missions that suck, mostly the ones that switch genre like Shmup and PunchOut. If they were cut it would have made for a better and more replayable experience.Overall though despite all the frustrating things the game is pretty awesome and there is really nothing quite like it on the market.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been a big fan of Platinum Games’ work ranging from MGR: Revengence to Nier Automata/Replicant, but it turns out I was first exposed to them through The Wonderful 101 when it first came out on the Wii U. Back then, I was a preteen and I couldn’t make it through the game’s demo, but instead of being frustrated, I was sad because I thought what the game showed me so far was really cool. Fast forward a decade and I finally gave it another go. This time, I had an absolute blast. In my eyes, it has the most satisfying gameplay I’ve seen from them, but it takes a lot of work to get there. The game’s story and presentation are superb and most of the characters are easy to get attached to. Of course, it has a lot of small flaws that persist throughout the entire game, but that doesn’t keep me from recommending it to just about anyone. Give The Wonderful 101 a try! I promise you won’t be good at it right away, which is the best thing possible for a unique action game.GAMEPLAYWhen I first started playing, I struggled to get high scores and I often sucked at figuring out what I was supposed to do against particular enemies. The game isn’t clear about its grading system, both in level and at the final tally at the end of each level. Even when I felt like I was getting a hang of the core gameplay and figuring out all of the things that were not explained to me, I would still be thrown for a loop at nearly every level because of the insane amount of variety this game has. There are certain parts of each level where you’ll be forced to play in a different genre for a short time, like a side-scrolling shooter, a Punch-Out minigame, a blocky mining minigame, or a fast-paced Star Fox shooter. We are given little time to master the new mechanics in these sections and we’ll often be killed because of our inexperience. These sections are great in a vacuum, but they are frustrating for first-time players since they have pretty much nothing to do with the core gameplay. At this point, you may be wondering why I recommend this game when I have all of these criticisms, and that’s because the most satisfying part of this game is “getting it”. The common consensus for TW101 is that you aren’t truly playing the game until it’s your second playthrough, where everything has become clear. Finally being able to handle everything the game throws at you is the best feeling ever, which leads me to everything I love about this game, once again starting with the gameplay. First of all, the game’s core combat is one of a kind. You look at the enemies in front of you and make a split-second decision about which weapon would be best to use. It took a while for me to get the hang of drawing stuff like the hammer or the claws, but most of the weapons were simple enough to draw and understand their strengths and weaknesses. The most satisfying part of the core gameplay is gradually increasing the amount of people in your group, so your weapons can either get bigger, or you can choose to use multiple weapons at once. It always feels nice to wrap the Wonder Liner around people and it's awe-inspiring to see how big your weapons can get by the end of the game. This game is amazing at slowly increasing the scale of every battle. At the beginning of the game, your weapons make you look ant-sized compared to the city-destroying mechs you encounter, but by the end, those mechs are adopted into your party, so your weapons become larger than cities or even states. While this game has a cartoony art style meant for a dated console, the weapons looked beautiful in their respective colors, especially the fist and the sword. Overall, the core combat is among the best I’ve seen in a video game, but that’s only half of what makes this game iconic. The other half is made up of spectacular quick-time events. A multitude of these can be found in every level and they all bring a sense of humor and awe to the gameplay. They can fulfill a character arc, like when Red shoots an arrow up at Laambo, piercing him, and from above, he grabs Laambo’s blade to cut him in two. At the time, we don’t realize this is the person who killed Red’s father, but now that we know, it’s extra satisfying to see Red give him a taste of his own medicine. The same can be said for Blue’s big moment when he relied on his teammates for the first time to take down his big brother’s betrayer, Vijounne. They can also be pretty hilarious, like when Red tickles a giant mech’s armpit to get it to let go of the Virgin Victory. My favorite quick-time event, which combines humor, spectacle, character growth, and a bit of meta-commentary, is the final one where Red is giving his final attack a ridiculously long name as Jerginga’s laser is barreling toward Earth. Blue gets more and more restless until he jumps at Red to fire the cannon, which he does, and then the most meta thing I’ve seen from Platinum Games turns its head. Throughout the game, I’ve been mashing the button with one finger during quick-time events, and in this final quick-time event, they show the main cast of the Wonderful 100 doing the same thing. I also have to point out that there are a ton of creative fail-state animations for every quick-time event that go unnoticed, but I appreciate them nonetheless. While the soundtrack in this game doesn’t have a lot of variety, it carries the game to the end and it sends the big spectacle moments into overdrive whenever the cheesy vocal theme pops up. It just feels like a necessary part of the game’s DNA.STORYAll that’s left to talk about are the story and characters. The game’s story is basically Gurren Lagann the video game, so it’s predictable, unpredictable, and fist-pumping awesome the whole way through. I had a great time getting to know most of the characters by seeing their personalities unfold as the story progresses, Red and Blue especially. Blue is just Sonic the Hedgehog (voice included) with a “learning the power of teamwork” arc and Red already reached a level of maturity that Blue will eventually learn from. I love all of the ridiculous names he has for special moves and the overly detailed title cards he blurts out for every main character in the game. Both of their personalities shine through right when Red is assigned as the leader. He doesn’t think himself worthy since he couldn’t save his dad but he embraces the role regardless. At the same time, we see Blue frustrated with the new chain of command so when we first enter a level, Red tells the team to “Unite Up!” and everyone enthusiastically yells “Roger!” except for Blue who says it like he just got put in time out. In retrospect, Red had a crazy amount of reserve for not going berserk against his father’s murderer, which is an example Blue eventually learns from. Later, Blue goes on his revenge arc and Red chases after him and they beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of each other because Red wanted to knock some sense into Blue (another Gurren Lagann trope) because he wants to help him with whatever he’s going through. Afterward, when Red is put in mortal peril, Blue unconsciously chooses Red over his thirst for revenge so he kinda learns his lesson until he makes another big mistake and is lore dumped about Red’s sad backstory making them “not so different after all”. Blue embraces the power of teamwork and the rest of the story is just the coolest and dumbest ♥♥♥♥ ever. I gotta say the voice acting in this game is incredible, especially Red’s. Everyone including Blue is pretty one-note but it feels like Red’s voice actor knew how to confront every emotion necessary. The other characters are serviceable, but I wanted to point out Black just because of how hilariously racist his intro is. He’s got dreads, he breakdances, he refuses to socialize, he’s always playing video games, and he throws BOMBS. I was laughing my ass off at how on the nose he was. So yeah, the story is great fun and it’s cool seeing events unfold in a second playthrough because of our new perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: As with several of the games I have now on Steam, I first played this game on a different system, in this case the Wii U back in the mid 2010s when this game dipped to $30. As such, while my review will show the 16 hours I've put into the game on PC so far, my actual playtime is closer to 100 hours across platforms. I went in completely blind not knowing what I was getting into, buying it with some birthday money because why not, and when it was over I almost regretted not having bought it for $60 months earlier.What is the Wonderful 101? The description I give to people is always "It's power rangers on crack."In reality, it's a very niche game with an undeniable appeal and a very interesting blend of gameplay that is easy to get into but has a very high skill ceiling. At first glance many people think this is going to be just like Pikmin, but in reality it's like Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, Okami, Gurren Lagann, and Super Sentai had a very wild night together. This game is what resulted nine months later. Incidentally, Bayonetta is in the game too (as are not-Viewtiful Joe and his girlfriend Sylvia). The basic premise is having control of several dozen heroes (at the start) and slowly expanding your reservoir as the game goes on in order to grow into a mighty force. There is a "light" attack that throws these heroes forward and can stun enemies after a time allowing you to hit harder with other moves, but this move is individuals going together in a group to attack. The "heavy" attack is where the real meat and potatoes of the game lies: UNITE MORPH! The Unite Morph is an ability granted to our heroes, The Wonderful Ones, which allows them to use their Centinel Suits in order to construct different objects out of thin air. This lets them turn into a rail that tosses a wayward bus away from a collision course with a school full of children, an elevator on a tall building, a massive plug in the glass wall of an underwater facility, and more. These however are not the morphs you'll be utilizing throughout the game, no no, the ones you use are the kind used to hit things, *really* hard. Unite Hand, Sword, Gun, Whip, and others are the tools of the trade, and while the light attack lets the heroes attack in a group, Unite Morphs let them attack as one, and this is a massive difference. Imagine if you will a group of one hundred people forming a giant fist with their bodies. You get what our red-clad leader, Wonder-Red, has jutting out of his left fist on the game page's title illustration but a whole lot bigger. Unite Morphs are performed by drawing a symbol representing the weapon and then executing the attack which will transform the heroes into that weapon which is then wielded by a single Wonderful One to fight. You can choose the size of the morph, allowing you to keep some of the heroes on the ground to continue pummeling the enemy as a group while using the rest in your morph, adding wild variety as you unlock upgrades, and as you level up your individual Wonderful Ones by assigning them as the leader of that Unite Morph type (lead Unite Hand type unit, Unite Sword type unit, etc) you'll earn new moves for each individual Unite Morph. It doesn't stay as simple as "press button to attack" for very long at all so long as you remember to cycle your members. You'll have enough moves in your arsenal by the end to make Dante blush, so do not take the first hour or two as all there is to this combat system because you'll be depriving yourself of one of the most in-depth combat systems you can find in a game by the end.All that said, this game can be extremely difficult at times. Enemies are fast and make sudden movements requiring you to have quick reflexes and the ability to take their tells and anticipate what they'll do. This being a PlatinumGames game, you're scored at the end of every combat section, letting you know how you performed overall. In this game specifically, sometimes this system feels very janky. Speaking of janky mechanics, the part of Okami that played into this frankenstein baby is the drawing. Utilizing one of the sticks if you're a civilized person, you'll draw different symbols that will let you access the different Unite Morphs. Sometimes this isn't as accurate as you'd like, and you'll end up with the wrong thing if you're not careful. The line will change color to the one of the morph you'll be getting, so you have that heads up, as well as time slowing down while you're drawing it, so in that aspect the game is very fair.The world is under invasion from the Geathjerk, returned after a twenty year absence upon their previous attempt to invade and conquer Earth. One Hundred nameless heroes must come together in order to repel the alien invaders and save humanity from complete extinction. They'll face a myriad of different enemies across the entire planet in their crusade all the while overcoming the difficulties of working as a team and getting into boxing matches using giant robots, a shmup stage or two, and even exterminating a virus inside of an alien's body. There is also a giant sexy blue alien woman and a sexy three eyed pink alien woman. Do with this information what you will. I cannot go any further into this without spoiling things, and that would be criminal, so go forward with confidence knowing that you're going for a wild ride.This game can easily appeal to a broad range of tastes and ages. I'd as easily play this in front of a 4 year old as I would an 80 year old. There are five difficulty levels for those looking to simply experience the story, and higher ones for people salivating for a true challenge. I can highly recommend this to people who love to go for the high score and try to get perfect rankings. You'll definitely get your money's worth whether you get it on sale or not.I recommend not buying the DLC until you have beaten the game at least once, as well as not utilizing the free codes to unlock even more characters. The natural progression of the battle system works for the base game, and getting all this stuff beforehand would make the game far too easy on a first go-around, cheapening the experience. Now go forth; TEAM, UNITE UP!

The Story is a little campy at first, but it gets legit good if you stick with it, and some of the emotional moments are simply Wonderful!The Gameplay however is BEYOND Wonderful if you stick with it. it is pretty tough to get used to at first, since you have to use the right stick on a controller to draw shapes and make your weapons, and pretty frequently too. However, once you get used to it, the combat is SO SO fun, and alot of enemies actually have simple ways to beat them, it's all about discovery and figuring things out, and that's one of the best parts of this game!The only word of warning I have, is keep in mind that this is a Platinum Game, and if you play on Normal, expect a tough but fair challenge throughout most of the game, as their games DO NOT hold your hand, or pull their punches! If you feel you are confident in your action game abilities and want an actually challenging game, GIVE THIS GAME A SHOT! It even has a demo too, so you can see if this game is worth your money to get it. I do highly HIGHLY recommend it, as this game is Truly WONDERFUL!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best action games I've ever played. The premise of controlling a Pikmin-esque group of superheroes and drawing shapes to form giant constructs is executed flawlessly, with each construct being easy to learn and the combat satisfying enough for anyone, even hardcore action fans. Because, there's a lot of depth to the game in the form of combo-stringing with the various weapons you can draw, and each enemy has patterns, strengths, and weaknesses, to learn and master. Without a doubt this is one of the most unique action games you can buy, and just for that alone I think it's worth buying. On the face of it, the game is a just superhero/Power Rangers spoof, but the light-hearted aesthetic of the game is just serious enough at times to elevate the game from simple parody to an earnest, heart-felt tale about saving the day.Buy it on sale or at full price, this game is worth it either way.

_childDocuments_.review: Hoo boy.This game's really good! It's also really hard! And really frustr8ing! The game goes to absurd lengths to try to tell you what to do sometimes, and it's still just not enough. Platinum games are notorious about their garbage tutorials and steep learning curve, but this is the game they finally hit a boiling point with it. The curve has steepened so much, it is now a wall. There's parts of this game where you'll be yelling at your screen about how you have no idea what the ♥♥♥♥ to do, because the tutorial for the mechanic was two levels ago, and even then it was just a single pop-up that came and went in 20 seconds with no actual teaching done to the player.The game has humor, depth, and charm oozing out of every pore. If you like the Saturday Morning Cartoon vibe, you're gonna jam with this so hard. If you're here for the polished Platinum gameplay, well... Tough news, it's not so polished anymore. The Unite Morph is a super experimental mechanic, and while most of the inputs aren't so difficult without the gamepad, not having the option really hurts, especially for some of the more puzzley-aspects of the mechanic. No, the mouse controls don't make up for this. It's jank, and there's no way around that. If you want to enjoy this game, you're going to have to spend a lot of time fiddling with its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. My personal advice is to watch a guide or let's play about the game before you buy. ChipCheezum did a really good LP of this game on YouTube where he does in-depth tutorials and explanations on mechanics the game only takes maybe 15 seconds (if that) to teach you. It's a really good thing that somebody out there is doing tutorials for Platinum Games, because for some reason it isn't Platinum. If you're willing to put up with some jank, and a lot of frustration while you learn how to play, there's a really fun and exciting character action game here. If you're already intimid8ed by the difficulty curve and high speed of games like Bayonetta, this one with all its gimmicks might be a bit much for you.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: The game itself is fantastic. It has a couple of foibles and hiccups in specific moments, exactly the same as the original version did, but there's nothing quite like it in the genre. If you're persistent, the combat is very rewarding and the pacing of the game's story is, in a word, Wonderful.To start with, I'll give my thoughts on this game as a remaster. I believe it recreates what the original release had very well, which is both good and bad. There are moments in which it is hard to tell what exactly the game wants from you. And there will be times in which you are trying to make a jump, and because of the perspective you will fall. That hasn't changed at all. So every once in a while the game can be frustrating because of little moments that break the momentum. The other issue is the second screen fix. This game originally came out on the Wii U, which had a second screen on the controller. This game in particular made very clever use of that second screen. In the original version you could also use the select button to show a small picture-in-picture display of what would be on that screen if you wanted. The fix in this remaster for that is to more aggressively make use of the picture-in-picture feature. It will show up infrequently when the game makes mandatory use of the "second screen." It's not a very elegant fix, but these sequences are part of what set this game apart 7 years ago.I don't know much about the technical side of this, and therefore I won't try to make any claims about the game's performance. My setup can't run the game at the highest resolution anyway, so my personal experience doesn't matter much to the people who care.On a separate note, I should mention the way this game came to be released. The original sold terribly. The developers, Platinum Games are notorious for making these games that appeal very well to the niche audience that already like them, but can't really draw a new audience. The Wonderful 101 was the worst selling out of all their games, in part because it was exclusive to the Wii U, which already had sold poorly. So a niche sell on a niche platform resulted in disastrously low sales numbers. Members of Platinum Games have mentioned in the years since then that they still love the game and wanted a chance to bring it to a new, more popular platform. But they couldn't even receive conventional funding for the re-release. They had to run a Kickstarter campaign, and ask the fans for donations to make it happen. The Kickstarter was very successful, and with the stretch goals they were able to get a couple of extra features, such as the rerecording of a couple key songs in the soundtrack with a live orchestra. I myself contributed to this Kickstarter campaign, and as a result was given a copy of the game for free. As a result of the Coronavirus lockdown, the physical copy I and many other contributors were sent were delayed before they could be shipped. As an apology to the people affected by this delay, Platinum Games also sent anyone who had requested physical copies codes for the steam version. That is the copy I'm reviewing. While it was very slightly limited as they only offered codes for the steam version in the apology, I still believe Platinum Games went above and beyond in this circumstance.The fact that this game now exists on platforms like PS4 and PC is a bit of a miracle. I won't spoil anything, but this game has a number of overt references to older video games. Some of these references are to games and other products owned by Nintendo, and their inclusion had always convinced me that a PC port of the game couldn't happen. But here we are, and I wouldn't change it at all.As a game on it's own, The Wonderful 101 exists as a blending of Pikmin and Bayonetta, with the aesthetic of Power Rangers. The zoomed out perspective and camera angle make for a very unique game among the genre. It plays incredibly well, with a lot of focus both in the gameplay and story on scale. The combat revolves around using giant fists and swords and guns and other things to fight monster sized enemies.The game is significantly longer than most games by the same developer, with multiple decently long missions in each of the 9 environments the games story unfolds over.Overall I believe this game deserves to be remembered for it's excellent pacing and artstyle. The gameplay stands out beside other games in the genre, and can be very rewarding and smooth if given time to get used to it. (On a tangent note, to anyone who was waiting for a Gurren Lagann game. This is the best you're going to get.)

_childDocuments_.review: What makes the Wonderful 101 remarkable compared to other action games is that it's fun in some very simple and traditional ways. In all likelihood your appreciation for its more unique aspects will only come with time. What will happen first is you'll make a huge sword and split a tank in two. This is how it all begins and the insane level of spectacle just escalates from there. This game is many things but it's not subtle. It's childish and cliched but its pure unfiltered enthusiasm and lack of cynicism is infectious. It's wonderful. Wonderful Wonderful Wonderful!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. It is an action game with unique mechanics. There are six different unite morphs (weapons) you can use: a fist, sword, gun, whip, hammer, and a time bomb. You will be required to use each of these to defeat certain enemies or to get through obstacles in a level. What makes the mechanics so unique in this game is that your weapons are made up of people. So basically you are wielding giant weapons made from the civilians you rescue throughout the level. It really makes you FEEL like a super hero. The game feels great. You can pull of insane combos by using certain abilities and switching between unite morphs. The further you along you get the more you'll be able to do. The story isn't the strongest part of the game, but it's fine. It is a sci-fi action adventure story that I don't think is supposed to be taken too seriously. There are parts of the story which change up the gameplay quite a bit. They range from ok to annoying. I would give this game an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is easily one of my favorite games ever, but be warned: it's very divisive. It is a truly special game and it has a lot to give. It's pure over-the-top hype from the beginning all the way to the very end. The combat system is very complex but once you get it, it flows so incredibly well.If that sounds interesting and you have money, then give it a chance. I'd heavily recommend to give a brief watch to some tutorial videos in Youtube (for example Saurian has some really great ones).

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of platinum's most unique games they've made and an homage to superhero shows like Power Rangers, Wonderful 101 is an overall great game from platinum with a different take on action games that unfortunately sometimes get in it's own way. If you enjoyed Bayonetta then check this game out as it's the same director and overall feel (the story even has a similar flow in it's climax) and just like that game this is meant for multiple playthroughs as you will struggle to get Platinum ranking without most of the powers. The combat revolves around drawing out which weapon you’ll want to use and switching between multiple on the fly. I recommend using a beginning level to get the hang of this as it can take time to get used to. But unlike other Platinum games the requirements to get certain moves can feel tedious to unlock at times. Moves such as the block and dodge have to be bought and while cheap enough to get on the first mission, ultimately should have been a part of the core moveset given how essential they are. Then moves like multi unite, were you summon another wonderful one to attack on their own while you attack(think assist from Marvel vs. Capcom), are really fun to use and offer so much more combo variety it feels like it also should have been in the base moveset and the upgraded version be unlockable. Also if you’ve played Bayo then prepare for way too many on rail shooting levels that can completely ruin your ranking.Overall despite these complaints wonderful 101 is still one of my favorite Platinum games, it just has too many weird design choses that keep it from being 9 or 10/10. Go check it out if you’ve already played Bayonetta or Devil May Cry to see if you like the genre and want something else or if you simply want to try an action that feels completely unique.

_childDocuments_.review: If you missed out on this game on the Wii U (and I don't blame you) then you owe it to yourself to play Platinum's masterpiece. This game is bursting at the seams with charm, attention to detail, depth, secrets, replayability, and immensely satisfying gameplay. You'll be stumbling through at first, but eventually you start to sink into the rhythm of the game, recognizing cues before they show up, knowing reflexively how to counter and parry incoming attacks until you're styling your way through fights while feeling amazing the whole time.My only complaints come from a couple particular levels that were frustrating in the original version. Otherwise, the remaster plays, loads, and runs fantastically. It was never advertised as an HD remake, so there are some textures and assets that don't look as nice as they could, but it never subtracts from the overall experience. That said, the game did crash on me a few times and at one point even required a full reinstallation to get things working. Hopefully a future patch will solve these problems.

_childDocuments_.review: Its simultaneously one of Platinum's best works, and also a game I would have a hard time recommending to most people. Its very unabashedly a Hideki Kamiya game and comes with all the baggage that brings (poor and sometimes non-existent tutorials, constant genre shifts that have varying degrees of success, etc.). But, if you can go in with an open mind to learning it and improving, you'll be rewarded with one of the genre's most satisfying combat systems, and a campaign that only gets better and better the more time you put in.

_childDocuments_.review: Backed a physical copy of the kickstarter, received steam code due to coronavirus delays. The Wonderful 101 is a game I enjoy more every time I go through it. Theres a line about the game's creator saying the first playthrough is the tutorial, and that's pretty accurate. My first playthrough on normal way back on Wii U was a bit of a struggle and while I enjoyed the game overall, I was wondering if I'd even be able to make it through the higher difficulties. Having beaten it on 101% difficulty on Wii U and starting it now on the Steam version, I can say that once the game clicks, it clicks pretty hard.While the story won't be winning any awards, it's pretty well done for a genre that isn't too well known for them. Essentially a story about a 100 man and woman member superhero sentai squad trying to stop an alien invasion, the game feels like a love letter to classic saturday morning cartoons and starts with the dial set to 11 and manages to exponentially go up from there. The gameplay will probably trip some people up the first time they play. While it's a similar game to Platinums other action titles like Bayonetta and Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance, it also has a very unique feel that's all it's own. For starters, you control 100 members at once with the leader character taking damage while the others can be temporarily knocked out. You will need these members to form your moves and attacks in the game. Instead of pressing a button/trigger/d-pad to switch weapons like in other games, you use the right stick to draw a symbol for the weapon (a circle for punch, a straight line for a sword, etc.). This might seem awkward and maybe even unnecessary at first, but before the end of the game I believe it justifies itself. You'll get 7 main weapons in the game (each of which have their use in and out of combat), 4 temporary which you can unlock after getting certain bottle caps (this games version of achievements), all of which have about 3-4 different sizes as well as a few bonus draw abilities. On top of that, the act of drawing can have benefits itself. Any item or ko'ed team member touched by a drawn line will be picked up and drawing into an enemy can recover battery power which you'll need to manage to use your moves and an upgrade can make it so drawing into an enemy does a bit of damage. Whew, that's a lot to take in. Then theres the enemies, all of which seem to have a lot of thought and care put into their design, and the bosses that are some of the most epic I've seen in the genre. While other more proficient players are able to articulate the intricacies of combat better than me, I will say that theres a ton of neat little details in the combat where it feels like that make me feel like theres something new to try out which also makes going for higher rankings for each stage that much more satisfying.The game isn't perfect however. While combat areas are fine tuned, some of the non-combat areas can be hit or miss. The camera might get obscured by building or large enemies, and the screen can get a little busy making it hard to seem some attacks coming. And theres a kid character named Luka who is kind of a PoS for most of the game. The second screen gimmick also feels a bit awkward, and the resolution feels a bit low quality at points. I had the game crash at one point (although might have been my computer).Despite that, the great soundtrack, pitch perfect story, great nods to Platinum's previous games and gaming in general, deep and inventive combat has kept me coming back again and again to this title.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played the game, and are just wondering if it is a good port it is, ran perfetly on my machine 950gtx + amd 6300X + 8gb of ram at high settings 1080p. i never noticed a graphical glitch or frame drop load times are extremelly short, i haven't tried playing it with kb and mouse (doesn't sound like a good idea) so if you don't have a controller you may want to wait till you have one.Side note, i played the game with a nintendo switch pro controller using the steam controller thing to remap a bunch of the face buttons so they matched the place on the xbox 360 controller, i didn't run with any issues using this configuration.The review will be spoiler free untill i warning you about it, it will also contain a couple gameplay tips you may want to find out by yourself, but id say they barely spoil the experience. (THE FIRST TIME YOU CAN GO TO THE WONDER MART, BUY UNITE GUTS AND SPRING, i don't get why they aren't part of your initial moveset since they are basically free and are esential to defense)anywaysThe defining feature of TW101 is the wonder liner which lets you change weapons, it may seem like it was intended for the wii u game pad, trust me the analog stick is way better than that, people on the wii u were using the right stick too, the morph shapes you have to draw are pretty forgiving, what i mean is that you don't really need to draw them perfectly, it will be a little bit hard to get used to drawing them but after a while you will be drawing multiple of them in no time to string combos, id say the key to it is thinking of them as fighting game inputs, Hand is a C motion, gun is an L motion whip is an S motion etc.There are a whole lot of enemy's, id say around 14 each one with plenty attacks and ways to defeat them, a lot of them seem like they can only be defeated by using a specific weapon, however besides ONE i can always think of other strategy's to circumvent the "intended" one, and this is one of the best things the game has, because im not even sure myself if the enemy im thinking of has an alternate strategy to it, because of all of the options the game has i may be missing something, there is always something new to learn on the game, don't get me wrong the game explains all of the mechanics you need to beat it with quick and easy to understand tutorials.Each one of the bosses is extremely diferent from the others, some changing the game to a shootemup or a punch out clone, there are plenty of these gameplay variations each one is executed but personaly i feel like a lot of the shootemup segments could be shorter, because they lack a lot of the depth the real game has, even when you are fighting the bosses normally a lot of them can have pretty specific ways of fighting them so on your first time going through the game they will probably beat you up a whole lot, but after you understand all there attacks and they ways you can beat them they are really satisfying to beat and add a lot of variety to the game which will make repeated playthroughs way more enjoyable as a result.If you've played bayoneta you will know that a whole lot of the QTE's on it were pretty unfair, with barely any time to react, here they are really fair, with plenty of time to do them and even if you don't manage to do them they won't instakill you (afaik i failed almost none on the whole game) coupled with a funny and unique fail state animation for all of them.Also small thing don't be intimidated by being 100 characters, basically the only one that can take damage is the leader (you) if the others get hit they will get put in  a dizzy state which will run out after a bit or if you touch them like pikmin.All of this is wraped with stelar graphics highlighting important stuff, like incoming enemy attacks, and giving all of the actions the player will perform a whole lot of impact and flare, a exelent soundtrack elevating a lot of moments in the game to unforgettable heights and writing and VA that will make you genuinely laugh with the game.Minor negative points, and i remark these are minor.I found a couple of bugs on the time ive played, one related to a bridge on operation 1A, and another that makes it so frozen enemy's can still damage you if they started an attack even when they are frozen. Both hopefully will be patched.When there is no ground on platforming sections my depth perception goes to hell.Minorest one, the very first time you boot up the game it may use keyboard prompts even if you are using the gamepad, if that happens go to options and change it.SPOILERY STUFF BELLOWEDIT 55 hours in"This just keeps getting better and better"EDIT 124 hours inThe best action game.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to people complaining about the drawing mechanics. _childDocuments_.review: 101% Platinum goodness. Probably Platinums's most unique game they've put out after becoming a more well known studio with the runner-up being Astral Chain. There's a lot that's familiar, and a lot more that's differnt. The game oozes with charm and has plenty of depth, hidden secrets and unlockables to keep you playing over and over. While not topping Bayonetta, Won101 stands tall in its own right, and deserves all the praise I can heap on it. It takes a little bit to get used to, but once it clicks, you'll not want to put it down, So just play it. Especially if you've played other titles from Platinum and the games they made when they were Clover Studios. The amount of references to those earlier titles, whether big or small, put a big smile on my face when I encountered them.
