_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest, and most certainly one of the most unique action games ever produced. And the port is okay.It's a relentless romp that takes you around the world to fend off an alien invasion. Calling it a roller coaster doesn't capture the enormity of the game, it's an entire amusement park with glued on wheels careening down a 100 meter drop with constant set pieces and genre switches, equal parts frustrating and delightful. But at its core is a deep, well-designed action combat system that challenges you and taps into the drive to do better and get better. It's just that sometimes you're going to be under the clock getting scored on shooting free throws and skee ball when you'd rather get back to the combat. So take your consolation prizes  with good humor.The remastered version is a mostly straight port with very little in the way of QoL features for platforms lacking a second screen. There are many little idiosyncrasies that result from this, and ideally, the game would support ultrawide monitors or multi-monitor setups to bring the second screen experience back to parity. On the other hand, the controls are probably more comprehensible without the distracting touch screen, and the benefits the remastered version does bring such as being able to see what's happening and cutting load times to almost nothing are very welcome. In my playthrough of the game, I experienced one soft-lock bug and some minor graphical issues (notably abundant z-fighting and a peculiar 59 FPS lock).So despite niggling technical issues, a disappointing lack of polish for the port, and the fact that I can now very clearly see that all of the placeholder text is Lorem Ipsum, this is still one of the best action games ever made and this is the best way to experience it.

_childDocuments_.review: I like it overall. I can see why some people might not enjoy it. The combat is mostly forming a weapon and then mashing the attack button at first. But you gain more variety in attacks and weapons as you progress which makes it more interesting. There are certain segments where it can be annoying or frustrating but they don't last too long. It can also be a little too gimmicky at times but most of them don't overstay their welcome and some of them are pretty fun like the Punch Out boss fight. The visuals are really cinematic and the characters are excitable. Admittedly I think the graphics could be better considering this is a remaster but I really don't care about that.I don't think everyone would enjoy this and don't expect it to be like Bayonetta or Nier. Of PlatimumGames' works it is most like Okami in terms of gameplay and the story and setting are kind of like Viewtiful Joe. If that is interesting then you'll probablly enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Wonderful 101 is Platinum Games unfiltered.It is an odd game, and one you definitely won't be able to understand for the first several hours of the game. But do not worry, this is normal.You play as the Wonderful 100, a team of 100 superheroes who can unite into various weapons, such as fists, swords, guns, whips, and so on. In classic Platinum spectacle action style, you then fight your way through the menacing GEATHJERK foes, comboing, dodging, and blocking as you go. By drawing shapes with the right analog, you change weapon mid-battle, and mastering this is the key to mastering the entire game. What weapon to turn into when is a choice you'll make over and over.The game also has a habit of changing gameplay on you. Hijacking an enemy spaceship gives you a shooter, all bosses have some weird trick to them, like a Star Fox-like battle, and some stages are flat out copying gameplay from classic games. If this is something you like or not is up to you. I liked it.Speaking of bosses, they are spectacular, every single one. You go through the first operation, fighting a few unique enemies you think could be bosses... and then the real boss shows up and is an entire level to itself. All bosses are. And it's amazing.The Wonderful 101 also has a spectacular presentation. While the graphics are definitely from 2013, and from Wii U, no less, the style and music is timeless. Add to that a story that keeps escalating to a silly degree and you have a memorable game like few others.The difficulty is of note, too. This game is hard. If you're not a Platinum Games veteran or have trouble adjusting to drawing shapes to change weapons, you will get your shiny head handed to you on Normal. However, the only thing hurt by using a Continue is your end of level ranking, you revive where you fell and the enemies are still hurt. It is hard, but forgiving.All in all, The Wonderful 101 is an odd game. It's very unique for a character action game, and it being a Platinum Games game is very readily apparent throughout the entire game.The Wonderful 101 is an acquired taste, no doubt, but if you like it, there really is nothing that compares to it.

_childDocuments_.review: An important note: I backed this game via Kickstarter because I wanted PlatinumGames to succeed in self-publishing such an underrated classic that wasn’t given enough attention it deserves on the Wii U. Despite never playing the game. I feel it is prudent for my readers to know when reading this review of the Wonderful 101 in order to grasp my thoughts and experiences. Basic premise/StoryFrom developer studio, Platinum Games. And originally directed by Hideki Kamiya with Takanori Sato directing the remastered port. Is an action-adventure and hack and slash game. Where you play as a group of secret superheroes called the Wonderful 100. They work for the CENTINELS, a group created by the United Nations. Whose purpose is to save civilians and repel the invading alien terrorist organization called GEATHJERK. All while keeping their secret identity concealed from public eyes. As Wonderful-Red it’s up to you to lead your ragtag group of superheroes against Earth’s deadliest enemy. Will Wonderful-Red break? Before he makes it!?Unique Gameplay Essentially, you go across the world completing operations which are essentially main missions: containing several sub-missions within. Since Geathjerk are invading Earth; the Wonderful 100 missions are varied in stopping their numerous efforts in attacking key points on Earth. So all of these missions will have you go across some unique settings around the world from cities, jungles, ice caverns, volcanoes and more. Defeating the many enemies Geathjerk produces intermittently from time to time. Fighting enemies along the way or when the game locks you in place to defeat all enemies in a zone before moving forward with the next mission objective. Each sub mission allows you to traverse through a generally decently sized area of the main setting of the operation. Usually these submissions last for less than 30 minutes depending on how thoroughly you explore the surrounding for secrets or hidden objects tucked away. Typically, I found myself completing each operation in a little under an hour or over. The game has a lot of environmental puzzles you can solve like pulling a knob to set the right coordinates to unlock a gate, using your wonder powers to pull cargo containers to get over an obstacle, or using your wonder-powers to unlock specific large containers only accessible with the right colored power to gain the contents within. Usually using your wonder powers to overcome an obstacle blocking your next objective destination. I was surprised seeing some Platinum formula reach through when the game would mix the genre from an action-adventure hack and slash. Into other genres. I won’t say it, to not spoil the surprise. But it’s definitely a nice change of pace the game delves into time and time again. The main gimmick of the Wonderful 101 is the ability to gather citizens around in these missions to help you morph your powers. Using citizens, from kids, teenagers, and well secret wonder operatives hidden throughout the world. You can create a variety of weapons from using a hand to punch enemies, a sword, whip, gun and more. Drawing the weapon’s image using the right analog stick on my xbox controller. The overall amount is over ten unite morph abilities. With more custom abilities you can unlock by buying in the shop. It’s nice to go through the game using various powers to overcome an obstacle using a key morph ability of defeating enemies with a certain morph. The GraphicsGraphically, I found the visual style to be a mix between superhero tv shows in a city and oddly enough power rangers… As odd as that comparison might be. There’s a lot of destructible environments in the game from cars, flora, and infrastructure that can be destroyed for money. The environments were decent, as a remastered port I expected more effort from Platinum games, to the point I didn’t have to mod the exe from a steam guide I found to reach 60fps or else there would be frame pacing issues. As someone who backed this game on Kickstarter, I feel a bit betrayed to say the least with the amount of money Platinum made, they can’t make a noticeable effort to fix the game’s frame pacing and latency issues hitting up to only 59 fps. It’s a minor gripe. But I feel it should be said nonetheless. The Usage of Sound And Music. For starter’s I found the overall soundtrack in Wonderful 101 to be a mix between heroism, gung-ho, and sublime all rolled into one. I felt like playing a souped up tokusatsu filled with power rangers and secret identities all to boot. There’s more references I’d place here in this review however, that would spoil the fun of the source material. Regardless, most of the music tracks were filled with such spirit of and awe, taking inspiration from tracks to fill you with hope, dread, city life, and anxiety mixed in. I did enjoy the soundtrack for the most part. It was decently done. For voice acting. I felt it was a mixed bag. There are some good lines here marred by repetitive character tropes too grating to hear. Like their tagline or motto repeating time and time again. I admit for the type of game Wonderful 101 envisions itself as, it may be on point to repeat. But, It would be nice to tone down the repetitive lines that I know are unique for each member of the Wonderful 101. Despite these remarks I still found the voice acting especially that of Wonder-Red, to be pleasant enough to hear.Final thoughts/RuminationsThere are some problems in the game. Here is a condensed paragraph of these issues. Jarring introduction with a not so cool transition in letting players learn the mechanics. The lack of a enemy log or codex from the start instead of finding enemy intel. This correlates to the game's quickness in killing off the enemy combat log without any menu option to recall upon. No tutorial page. To help explain some game mechanics like the parry or shield ability. To help explain what can and cannot be blocked/parried. Dialogue isn't synced sometimes when you try to skip dialogues from characters. The game will recycle old minibosses constantly. Making it seem a lot like padding to extend the game's length. Bug within the game when enemy attacks you and you will be stuck in place for a second or two. Total Times Beaten: 1(normal)Score: 7.5/10 (Score is based off how much I enjoyed the game)Date Finished: 5-20-20Date Reviewed: 5-21-20Date Posted: N/A Date Edited: Major paragraph cutsHours Played: over 10 hours in game, steam says 19...

_childDocuments_.review: Of all the action games I've played, this is the first one that's made me want to 100% it and replay it multiple times on the hardest difficulties. The action oriented parts are a blast. The minigames are fun on a first playthrough, but most of them are effectively autoscrollers so you can't do them faster on subsequent playthroughs. _childDocuments_.review: Runs at perfect 60fps, set to high, at 900p. On my i5-2500K and HD7850.This Wii-U original has been ported "emulator-style". No functions or sequences requiring the gamepad screen have been removed. Instead, you are given an OSD of the gamepad screen that you can toggle with SELECT button, which is necessary for certain functions and sequences in the game.Just like the original release, I really feel that Chapters 1 and 2 (operations 001 and 002) are very clumsy in both writing and overall design. I beg of you to be forgiving for janky sequences that get you stuck and lots of long and awkward cut scenes in these chapters. Not to mention, you can't even block OP-002 bosses punches till you gather enough fighters, which you are without for the first half of the fight (without NG+ atleast).The game gets more exciting and has better flow from Operation 003 and onwards. The main campaign is my absolute favorite campaign of all Director Kamiya's games. I recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my personal favorite Platinum GameDon't get me wrong, the first time I played this game on my Wii U I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ got my ass kicked throughout the entire game. I still loved it regardless of my own performance because I think this game has some extremely funny writing and just great corny tokusatsu/sentai stuff that plays really well in contrast to the times where the game takes itself EXTREMELY seriously.But after that first play through I went back and paid a lot more attention to the environments, enemy patterns, colors, etc. and learned what this game wanted me to learn when it wanted me to learn it. Suddenly  this game kinda opened itself to me and made the combat worthwhile and fun instead of a slog. Playing it now, like 7 years after it came out, this game (not the port itself) has some really bad moments for its camera control, its not entirely bad but sometimes you are just at the mercy of the game for a bit while you flail around, usually during boss fights.The port is fine, I haven't encountered anything really egregiously bad about it. I don't know what I'd want added to it other than some better res menus and fonts.Its amazing this came out the same year as MGR, if you like Platinum Games going for it, like really weird mashups of genre, and enjoy laughing I highly recommend The Wonderful 101

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly fun game with fast, fluid gameplay, style for days, and a story that escalates to truly ridiculous scenarios.  If you have any interest in spectacle brawlers you owe it to yourself to buy this game and master its systems. It is very rewarding to learn. Quick note: this game was always meant to be played using the right stick to draw shapes, do not attempt to use the mouse. Do not assume the game is unplayable without a touchscreen. Think of the shapes as fighting game inputs: full circle for fist, hold forward for sword, etc. It will quickly become second nature.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wonderful.I was one of perhaps 7 people in the world that owned The Wonderful 101 on WiiU. This remaster changes very little, because it doesn't really NEED to change too much. The game is high execution and a serious challenge, and like any spectacle brawler, it WILL wreck you given half a chance, but this is quite possibly Platinum's best game. It starts over the top and just screams upward from there. If you like these kind of games, you owe it to yourself to get this delightful ball of craziness.

_childDocuments_.review: A very great game, twas a shame it was stuck on the Wii U during its initial release. It's very well rounded, combining combat and puzzles making a fun experience. Not exactly the easiest game to get into as it throws many things at you and is fast paced, especially during boss battles. Luckily there's several difficulty settings to curate your preferences and items/upgrades that make fights a ton easier. The story itself is also a joy with all the humor and references, as well as the plot keeping itself interesting. Everything feels over-the-top in the best way possible. Overall I'm shocked this flew over my head and I'm glad to have it.

With that said this game is an absolute gem and wholly original experience even to those well versed in stylish hack and slashes while still packing more trademark platinum spectacle than even the more well known titles like Bayonetta. _childDocuments_.review: Received a Steam key for backing the game on Kickstarter. Some minor bugs, mostly relegated to cutscenes (your team will be standing sideways on air instead of on the ground), the first boss fight (the camera is stuck on a corner instead of being properly placed in the middle of the screen, cutting part of the fight off), and a late level (Unite Sword Multi-Unite does not do anything for this one segment in the mission). Wonderful 101 is a true masterpiece of a niche title -- if you like it, you'll fall in love, but if you dislike it, you'll hate it with a passion. For anyone that's played long enough for the gameplay to click, this seems to be the case -- they understand the combat, but it still feels difficult and annoying, or they understand and it clicked hard. Be a bit wary of that, but if it clicks for you and you like it, you really will fall in love. You control a team of heroes a la Tokusatsu (Power Rangers) and can use the right stick to form weapons to attack enemies -- the Unite Morph. The combat system looks completely different from other Action Games, but at its core lies the same basic formula of Platinum Games action games. Takes some time to get used to the controls of directing dozens of heroes to attack and combine, but once it clicks you start to play one of Platinum's greatest games. The combat is great if it clicks for you, but the Saturday Morning Cartoon dialogue, story and music are even greater -- this game starts with the ball rolling and simply doesn't stop. The story will absolutely remind you of the kind of crap you used to watch as a kid, which is absolutely awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Wonderful 101: Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: I am a Kickstarter backer, and I played through this game before the official retail launch. It was also my first complete run because I was just impatient with the Wii U version. This game is about as good as it gets on PC, despite any bugs it might have at launch. Loading times are almost nothing and runs great at 1440p on my mid-tier rig. Combat is tight with lots of depth, room to learn and grow, with tons of replay value through secrets to find and collectibles. Story is about as bonkers as Platinum games get too so if you know what you're in for, you won't be disappointed. Be sure to use your controller of choice. Coming to this game with a casual mindset might leave you a little frustrated with the way the game ranks you, but keep in mind it's designed for multiple playthroughs. You won't get platinum ranks your first time playing, period. There's easy modes for beginners - but if you've played a Platinum or Kamiya title before, like Bayonetta or Devil May Cry, you might feel at home starting with the Normal mode. Just don't be too prideful when playing this game and you'll have a good time.My only complaints are related to the non-combat focused missions and some quality of life things. The shmup missions feel out of place in a character focused action game, and unskippable cutscenes in addition to an inconsistent checkpoint system makes retrying missions tedious. Overall though the highlights of the Wonderful 101 make it worthwhile despite its dark spots. Enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Good port, no bugs encountered yet. Recognized my xinput controller (Xbox Elite V2) from start up and never had controller trouble. PC version seems to be the best bet to avoid any bugs or performance issues (as usual). Running at 60fps/1440p with little trouble. Some stuttering here or there, but no specific instance of it that I felt impacted my gameplay. The 75% of the Vorkken battles I've done so far ran flawlessly at 60fps, which was one of the more infamous sections of the original game that was compromised due to poor performance.Gamepad sections are done by placing a small screen in the bottom right corner that gives you the view of what would be normally on the gamepad screen. So far, it's only as cumbersome as the actual gamepad sections were in the original Wii U release, so it passes in my book.Only complaint is that I can't customize the music to play the original version of the Wonderful 101 theme during gameplay (it's still in-game via the music player). tl:dr good port, fixes framerate problems from the original game and runs at 60fps/1440p and a controller with no issues. Needs music customization.
_childDocuments_.name: The Wonderful 101: Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: The Wonderful 101 Remastered can be overwhelming, and the initial impression may be that it simply bombards the senses too much, confusing both the eyes and the thumbs. The key is to play at the right difficulty level, work with its peculiar logic and remain open to its mechanics. In return, it offers an exceptional experience where no scenario is too outrageous and no enemy is too exaggerated. It's not perfect, but there's simply no other game on the market that focuses so much on ridiculous fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Wonderful 101: Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: Lead an army of 100 Wonderful Ones from around the world in this Unite Action spectacular! A team of heroes from around the world must UNITE to protect the earth from vicious alien invaders! This band of 100 Wonderful Ones works together using their fantastic abilities to create a variety of forms. Whether it be a giant fist or a sharp blade, they’ll use their wits and power to overcome the enemy’s pitfalls and perils! And the final member of this team of courageous heroes—is you. From PlatinumGames, creators of the Bayonetta series, ASTRAL CHAIN, NieR:Automata, and Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance, comes The Wonderful 101: Remastered! This game will be PlatinumGames' first self-published title, and is a powered-up version of The Wonderful 101, originally released by Nintendo on September 15th, 2013 as a Wii U exclusive. The Wonderful 101: Remastered offers the unprecedented ability to control 100 heroes at once, with the flowing controls and dynamic action that are the PlatinumGames hallmark. It’s all brought together by a pulse pounding tale of heroic bravery and friendship standing tall against evil, and is PlatinumGames’ most ambitious offering to date. Hideki Kamiya, director of The Wonderful 101, has supervised this remaster and added numerous improvements to ensure that this game can be more easily and thoroughly enjoyed by all and on various platforms, and with improved visuals, framerate, and loading time for an enhanced experience on all fronts.

name: House Flipper 2
detailed_description: It doesn't matter if you're a makeover veteran or if you're only starting out - you'll feel at home in no time! House Flipper 2 introduces new mechanics and revamps the ones from the original game. The good old hammer, the trusty paint roller, and the sturdy mop, all await your return! The new visuals make our fixer-uppers look crisp as never before! Why renovate a house when you can just build one? Unleash your creativity in the Sandbox Mode! Use it to recreate real-life buildings or design projects that exist in your imagination. Remember: building from scratch is no easy task! But let's face it, it's definitely worth putting in extra effort to design the house of your dreams. Between the mountain tops and the endless sea, there lies the town of Pinnacove. A place where time slows down, and the friendly residents are ready to entrust you with their homes. Can you discover some of the stories within these walls? Your old pal Tom, who seems to know everybody in the neighborhood, will gladly share some local knowledge with you. In House Flipper 2, you are the foreman! You get to decide what 'relaxing gameplay' means! Do you enjoy building? Choose the Sandbox Mode which allows you to construct houses from scratch. Or maybe you prefer cleaning and decorating? In the Story Mode, you will delve into long and engaging renovation projects, as well as deal with some quick jobs. Sit back and relax, here comes the new age of House Flipper!

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the story, but have not bought and renovated many houses yet. This title is a big next step and improvement to the gameplay of the OG title. You can expect the designing to take longer, because you have so much more control over the end results. We also received some huge quality of life improvements, like copy pasting a colour palette between furniture, or duplicating and pasting assets.The base game story is somewhat short - please note my 22 hrs include at least 5 hrs AFK - but  I know I will get a lot more hours in when buying houses. You can also replay story missions at any time.I found the game to be satisfying in its current state, but I will say there's a bit of a lack of rug diversity as well as curtains. I know it'll come later, though. Demolition can get laggy, but not too major.Tip:  use WASD for painting. This, to me, fixed all issues with controls.Additional feedback from a 3D artist POV: I don't see why the UV maps have seemingly random orientation and scale for a lot of the furniture. For such a texture oriented game I'd have expected UV maps to share orientation and density, or for density to be reviewed more carefully.I hope you can find time to review this and fix it at least on beds and couches, as the issue makes many of your textures incompatible with some furniture.  It's the only major issue I had the whole game. Congratulations to the team - you did great with this one - and I can't wait to see what more you do with it!
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: House Flipper 2's engine and tech is definitively an upgrade to House Flipper 1. The new building and painting options are great(especially being able to paint parts of walls to make patterns). The glaring issue at hand is that furniture options are incredibly limited right now and without workshop support at the moment the lack of decoration variety really holds the game back. As the game is while I love the upgrades they made in HF2 and I have faith in the team to turn the potential into a great game, House Flipper 1 is still the better game to realize the houses I want to create. That being said HF2 is still very much an enjoyable game in its own right and certainly not one I regret buying.(Also IMO the furniture assembly minigame was kind of a miss but it's so seperated from the main game you can ignore it)
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: Not nearly as much content/ choices of different looking furniture as basegame HF1 :c I adored the first game, and this feels like a shell of the former, with more bugs... I want to like this, but in its current state, I would reccomend the first game to players instead of paying for something not as good. It could get better in the future, but currently it is just not worth $40.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: Overall good experience, enjoying it! No carpets though :(Weird issue with my left handed mouse where in game the buttons are flipped even though they are set to left and right like any normal mouse and not swapped like left handed ones are default to. Works normally when in the Menu, but swaps in game?
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: Five years after the release of House Flipper 1 with constant free content updates and several DLCs, all catering extremely well to player suggestions, the devs have taken the step to build the game from the ground up again, avoiding everything that limited HF1 - a fresh start to take this game even further. So of course, HF2 is very similar to HF1. BUT it gives the much needed room for so much more to come!I played now for about 18 hours - and I'm just getting started! Story mode alone (which is more like an advanced version of a tutorial) took me about 15 hours. But the real purpose of this game is letting your imagination run wild! Building houses from scratch, totally redoing houses and selling them, playing around with all the possibilities the game's mechanics offer - well, there's a reason I had 500 hours in HF1 and I'm sure HF2 will someday have stolen even more of my time :). This game is just the perfect game for everyone who played The Sims mainly because of building and decorating houses, to live out their dreams house-wise, for people who always think at every Ikea visit that they'd need 3 or 4 homes to realize all the ideas they have :D. It's just the platinum game in the genre of flipping games. And all that with a team of devs behind it who are in it with all their hearts who care A LOT about their players! So yes, if you are in any way into this kind of games, GET HOUSE FLIPPER 2!!!
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: To say that I am addicted to the House Flipper saga would be a gross understatement. There are not enough words in the English vernacular that could accurately depict my love affair with these games. I have never been bored. There is always something to do and my ability to be creative is almost limitless. The developers listen, they take onboard new ideas from within the community and work tirelessly to make the game the best that it can possibly be.I can't fault it. Obviously the game has it's flaws, but all games do. The game is new, and for a game that is relatively new, the amount of improvement that's already been implemented is hard to fault. I genuinely cannot wait to see what the future holds for not only this game, but all of Frozen Districts future endeavours, because these are the types of developers who deserve all the praise and support in the world. I can't speak highly enough of HF2 and it's entire team.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: HF1 was my all time favourite of all house building simulation games. HF2 does not disappoint you. A big upgrade on tools and visuals. Addition of the tool sense which I've seen in for the first time on House Builder, not bad at all, very useful. Had lots of fun of course but it looked a bit short in my opinion. I have over 100+hours on HF1 but that includes all the DLC' s. The only thing I did not like was the auctions, instead of keeping the old format they downgraded a lot with the customers. Maybe that is food for thought for a later update.Definitely recommend to people who love these genres.ps. I am trying to get all the Bessies, keep replaying the 9 houses but the achievement does not popup.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: The first game had me hooked, waited years for this release, time was worth the wait. Its the same charm and idea of the first game with some of the building mechanisms tweaked, in a good and sometimes more challenging way (although it makes more sense for painting to be like this for example). _childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: Chill game. Satisfying animations and progressive gameplay with entertaining quests and small story line.There could be a better system set up to help with side features like assembling items and building a house from ground up as an example to show all the tools you can use to build a house on your own instead of flipping it.Comparing the house flipper to house flipper 2: House flipper 2 has the ability to use wasd buttons to clean windows and paint which adds to the pace of the cleaning: you feel faster and move eficient. Although figuring out this was a "self help" thing since there was no mention about that anywhere and you have to find that out on your own. A lot of the learning process in house flipper 2 is "figure it out as you play" instead of reading a little tip or feature description, which is a tiny minus.Minimap missing is not as noticible since a big point of house flipper 2 is learning to use "flipper sense", so being mad at that doesn't make much sense. Flipper sense needs work, but it just released and I like that feature nonetheless.Painting is altogether more satisfying in house flipper 2 than the original. It's more "tedious", but the actions is more satisfying. Cleaning has better animations and changing trash bags makes sense and adds a finishing action to your cleaning making you feel more accomplished. I did not play house flipper with it's release or in the history, but buying house flipper 2 with it's release and being able to compare does not make me sad or upset with spending the money and I'd buy house flipper 2 again. It has beatiful animations, feels very smooth and satisfying and I don't regret buying it one bit. I'm looking forward to getting house flipper 2 DLCs!!!
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: house flipper 1 is very near and dear to my heart so i was worried that 2 wouldnt live up to the hype. luckily i was wrong, the game is super fun! i love the new artstyle, its so soft and cozy. the characters are super charming AND no more shower assembly... i could practically hear the angels sing when i plopped down a fully made shower straight from the store. perfection. this game has a lot of improvements especially in optimization. i had nearly every dlc for house flipper 1 and my game could not even start itself up without crashing or freezing at least 3 times. meanwhile in house flipper 2 i have not had a single crash yet. things load quite quickly too!It is a bit hard moving from having all the furniture options of majorly dlced house flipper 1 (like in-ground and indoor pools, a variety of decorations, that i dearly miss) to just basically having the base game again, but the presence of outdoor gardening items helps to soften that blow a bit.I do also hope that the 'upload your own photos to hang on your wall feature' makes a glorious return in 2. i was pretty sad when i didnt see an option to hang up my own pictures anywhere.however, what i believe i miss the most from house flipper 1 (other than the pools and custom photos LOL) is actually the workshop support!I know its a bit dumb to say but I can hardly live without my community-made clutter items! i would love love love to see this game get workshop support, then my life would truly be complete. all in all i'm having lots of fun! if you liked house flipper 1 you will like house flipper 2 ^w^now, i'm off to clean more windows....

_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's just not the same. It feels like Unpacking by Witch Beam in 3D. It feels like it lost its root in being a house flipping game. Granted I haven't put a lot time in it but with many hours in HF1 and buying nearly every DLC because they were all amazing, this game just feels like a miss. (where did the amazing soundtrack go?)
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's finally out and looking good! The absolute first thing that stands out to me is the improved optimisation in comparison to HF1; finally, my gaming laptop can handle having a HF game open and discord on in the background! With the option to turn off day/night cycles removed, I was really concerned that this would prove to be an issue, as the night cycle in HF1 definitely impacts the performance, but everything has been smooth as butter.I really love the new graphics. Everything feels a lot more vibrant and personally tailored to the game itself. It might mean missing out on a few giggles as I stop finding housing assets from HF in games like Phasmophobia, but I think the saturation is absolutely worth it.With only a few hours under my belt, I haven't played around nearly enough with all the options for changing around furniture, but I'm also absolutely digging it. The copy style, duplication and edit style tools just make the whole thing tie together into a much more engaging and faster experience when composing a room. Painting is so much faster, though I do agree that not having a way to toggle it could raise an accessibility issue. Not having to spend two minutes to install a shower almost made me cry.Probably the biggest things I'm missing from HF1, however, is the map and the before and after shots at the end of a job. Particularly with the jobs, I feel like I can kind of just slap down furniture in the first style its shown in and not really care about the cohesion, because there's no real measure of success or lasting impact from just making a space look like a clown exploded all over it. The highlight method when cleaning is great, but doesn't stop me from having to spend five minutes looking for the one bit of mould I missed on the corner of a skylight when I'm looking at it from all the wrong angles.There's a few other odds and ends which I feel is more geared towards adjusting to HF2 from HF1, but I'll update my review if they prove to be more persistent than a few dozen hours more of gameplay. The lack of before and after shots is a huge detriment on the satisfaction levels, but all in all I am really happy with what I've played so far!
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: if you've played house flipper extensively and you're looking for more of that, i think this is worth buying, but i'm not blown away.  it's enjoyable, and i like some of the new things, like npc's giving you a call while you're doing a job, updated graphics are nice, the music is fun. but i do feel like house flipper 1 'plays' better. the paint tool in this one, even now that i've unlocked all it's 'tiers', is just unpleasant to use. same thing for tiling and wallpaper. i miss the before/after slideshow after jobs and flips as it was a nice way to wrap up a project vs a screen with 3 stars that just lets you take your money and move on. i sometimes can't find trash. some objects have to be placed a very specific way but it's just trial and error until you get it. it's frustrating.and this has nothing to do with the game but since i am airing my grievances i wish they had added some sort of feedback feature on jobs. it would motivate me to set up kitchens instead of placing all the cabinets and appliances all over the floor at random and moving on because i'll get the points regardless.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game, following in the foodsteps of HF1 with some nice improvements and new features, but also has it flaws:Pro:* New painting system, takes maybe some time to get used to, but it's a nice upgrade compared to HF1* No longer assembling 100.000 radiators!* Performance wise the game runs smoothly* House buildingCons:* No before and after pictures. You can't even compare how it was after your work like in HF1* Assembling against time for discount feels like you are forced to do something as fast as possible, while the whole point of the game is relaxing* Available content feels quite low atm, hopefully the dev will add more stuff in the near future, it sometimes really feel like a base game* No feedback from potential buyers when flipping houses?In HF1 the assembly of radiators got annoying, because you had to do it so many times, but now there is 0% of the old mechanics to be found, sinks, toilets, place it where you want, no tubing required. Handy, but remind me not to flush in your house :)I do recommend this game, also for this price, but I just find it weird they didn't take some of HF1 beloved features over to number 2
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I literally LOVE House Flipper 1 so much and I was so excited that there was a second one coming out. I'm so in love with this game as well. I think the tools and abilities that you have in this game are great and easy to understand. I can't wait to see what else gets added to the game and where the developers go! I'm so excited to keep playing even just flipping houses with no missions and I have like over 20 hours in the game and it's been only 2 weeks that it's been out. I really appreciate that this game has been created. Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game is alright, has much potential but I don't think it should've been released yet.There really isn't that much content to make it worth the full price, the first part has much more content and is cheaper. I know there will probably be more stuff added but as it stands now, it's not worth it. There are also a few consistent bugs going through almost every level. I really had fun playing the game, but it's too short for the price, I finished it in less than 20 hours and all I have to do is freeplay for the last 3 achievements. And I'm just hoping they don't go the EA way and make every bit of new content paid, though that's probably what's gonna happen.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the original House Flipper, you'll like this one. More abilities, including moving and deleting windows, new ways to customize materials (including building materials), more flexibility for using materials, building staircases and steps, a lot of good new upgrades that make it more interesting. However, there are also some issues for me with user friendliness. Had to figure out selling a house via players' videos and trial and error, after deleting columns the columns I could purchase weren't tall enough, and in the new assembly challenges I've found one that simply won't work for me at the last step. I do wish they allowed you to delete/sell decorative materials; one small slip and you have a piece of wood where the wallpaper should be. Hopefully these things will be sorted out in a patch or two. For now I'm enjoying completing jobs and working on my own houses. Worth the money for me.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to start by saying that I love the original game, despite it's flaws. I put in 60 hours and had a great time. As for the sequel, I adore the upgraded textures, the new furniture, and getting to know SOME of the clients (I would have breakfast with the grandma whose attic you renovate). The first thing that bothered me was the new painting mechanic. It's not fun and was an unnecessary change. I've seen other users point out that it also makes the game less accessible for them, which is unacceptable and I hope is patched as soon as possible. My other big issue is how little there is to the main storyline and that's the reason I cannot recommend this game. It just doesn't feel right to pay more for less content.UPDATE 1/2/24:The accessibility issue with painting seems to be fixed, which is great. However, it'd be better if the wasd keys followed the wall and not the camera.I've finished all of the jobs included in the game and I still stand by my opinion that the price does not reflect the value, especially if you prefer having a list of tasks as opposed to free-playing in sandbox mode. Since my initial review, I've also bought a house to flip and I think there's a lot of room for improvement. For starters, it'd be helpful to know whether I've removed all of the trash and cleaned the whole house. Also, having an idea of what potential buyers want is something that I miss from the original game. It gave me a better idea of what to make to maximize my profits.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: i just... can't recommend this game. i really, really wanted to, as i was a huge fan of HF1, but I can't. first of all, the price. i went back and forth for about a week trying to decide to buy it now or wait until it went on a better sale, before finally taking the plunge and buying it full price anyway. as someone who makes $15/h, it's a big purchase. i fully believe that game devs should be paid for their work, but this game is not worth $40.this game has some improvements from the first one, but it's really struggling. the graphics are nice, and it has polished some mechanics, i especially like the free painting ability, but the lack of item variety, especially decorations, is oppressing. especially the lack of things like curtains! or bath towels, stacks of books. the list goes on. but at least there's 8 different bottles of perfume. there types of items they decided to focus on is really weird. it also feels like there's only a handful of interior styles to chose from and after flipping a house or two, it all starts to blur together and look the same. which is boring. i also miss installing the physical objects and putting together machines, that was a really unique feature that HF1 had. and for what it's worth, the assembly feature in this game is absolutely miserable. the controls are weird and clunky, the camera controls suck, and it's just irritating to have to do. i love putting together furniture but the assembly feature is just a miserable slog to work through.my biggest problem though, is the saving. i don't mean that the save corrupted; twice now i've lost HOURS of work because the game just didn't save. the first time, i sold a flipped house for about $800k, bought a bunch of the cheaper houses, and had about $400k remaining. i saved the game, waited for the save icon to finish, and closed it down. when i launched next, the house i had flipped was sold! but none of the houses that i had bought were owned by me, and i didn't have the $400k left over in my wallet, i had the ~$70k i had Before i sold the expensive house. but it was sold so i couldn't get it back unless i wanted to buy it and do it all over again. second time i spent several hours straight on fixing up a house, going through and replacing all the siding, cleaning, decorating the front. i saved the game several times throughout, and then once again before closing it down. when i launched it just now... i was dumped back in front of the house for the first time and it was in the condition i had originally purchased it in, garbage and peeling paint and all. to say that it's frustrating is an understatement. there was no indication that my saves had any issue. So.. no. i don't recommend this game, and especially not at full price. and i feel bad about that! but unless they do a big patch and double their item catalog, i just don't think it's worth $40
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: Was very excited to play this game, however, I was greeted by disappointment. There are a lot of things that are missing in the game that should have been transferred or improved from the first House Flipper. There weren't a lot of missions to do. It felt like I just did 5 houses and that was it. They also removed the option to assemble fixtures or repair broken outlets that existed in the first game. Overall, this game is just an unfinished jigsaw puzzle, missing pieces everywhere and have a few underwhelming parts to the game. Wouldn't recommend people to play the game as is right now, wait until there are updates to the game to make it worth buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok not the best, prefer the HF1 layout, you can't search for anything on the store via the tablet on the steam deck. Which means I can't access the deluxe items I purchased via DLC. It's disappointing. Recommending this game is a hard one, absolutely loved HF1 but this not so much so it may say yes but for me it's definitely a maybe.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun and relaxing. A lot of key things from the first game have been expanded or fixed. To list a couple, you have more freedom with customizing furniture with material texture and color options along with patterns, the painting system is more fleshed out with instead of generic you can only paint a panel of wall you can now paint whatever and however you want, the jobs now feel like there is a person behind it as they call you and give you context on the state of the house (I just think that's a neat feature and reminds you that yes this is a job and your talking to your client as opposed to just an email), etc. There are a lot of very small but much needed improvements compared to HF1 but the biggest one for sure is customizing now feels more free. Overall its a fantastic experience for a more cozy and relaxing couple of hours as seeing a house that was trashed now be clean and fixed is rewarding.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so I thought long and hard about this and I'll be honest my thoughts draw more towards not recommending as it does towards the positive and I'll try and explain why.Okay so first off, the game looks great, the style is nice and clean and the aesthetic really works for the game. It has differing mechanics from the first one and in some regards this is both good and bad.Pros: Now for the downsides, which sadly outweigh what I found positive.Cons:Basically I think before I can recommend this it would need some updating, FREE updating I would add. I have the dreadful feeling that stuff like gardening and installations might just get sold back to us as DLC at a later date. Some recommendations that I think the game could use.Gardening and installations brought back.More items because the stuff you can buy is kind of barebones.Some sort of endless mode. When you finish the story all you can do is buy and renovate houses, which isn't a new issue. It could do with some sort of randomly generated job mode so you can still do "missions" because I find it to be a fun addition to just flipping your own houses.If you liked the original I do think you might enjoy this enough to be a worthwhile purchase, but I think they also removed enough features from the original to make me hesitant to recommend it for that reason.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I have 400+ hours in HF, and I'm really happy with HF2 so far. It's improved a good chunk of the jank from the previous game, and it's really fun to play. I love being able to have a lot more freedom with how to paint/tile walls, and the flipper tool is a godsend with the ability to duplicate, edit, and copy and paste item settings onto another item.I've completed all the available jobs and I think they were a good intro to the mechanics of the game, but it did feel a bit more like a cleaning simulator until the later jobs where you actually get to design more. The item catalog is pretty lacking overall, but for now I think the trade-off is the vast amount of customization you can do for each item. I do wish they had ported over some of the more recent items from HF, some of the posters made it in but none of the previous furniture. This will probably be alleviated with future updates, dlcs, and (hopefully) the addition of steam workshop items. My biggest complaint: please let use turn off the day/night cycle. It's an option in the first game and I'm not sure why they didn't add it here. :(
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I love the updated mechanics and the easier ability to customise. There’s some massive improvements from HF1.However, as others have stated, it doesn’t feel like a complete game. That being said, with the developers already implementing changes, I’m looking forward to seeing what they do. There’s a definite replay value to playing now and then replaying once more things have been added.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's an overall decent sequel to the original but I have some comments.This game does most things better then the original HOWEVER it does feel like the game is lacking in content at the moment, I am aware at the time of this writing that game hasn't even been out a year yet but it may be worth waiting some still for more content updates and DLC to come out if that is an issue for you.The story mode is a bit short (especially if you do the bare minimum to finish a job) and it's not terribly in depth, which it really doesn't have to be for something as simple of a concept as this is, but it felt like the base game for the original had a more expansive list of side jobs available to take.Mod support through mod.io integration isn't terrible but I wish it was done through the workshop on here, as a side note right now only jobs and properties are available to download but unfortunately, they don't show up in the "campaign" mode as far as I can tell right now. Other downer about mods is the lack of ability to mod in items right now from the looks of things which I feel is a step back for this game,The UI is okay, it definitely feels cleaner and is much smoother then OG House Flipper's but it also feels more confusing to navigate through at times.Honestly a good buy if your in to relaxing job sim games, relatively bug free as far as they go but you also may want to give this game some time to cook a bit more if you want more content.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I adored the first house flipper game, and upon my first few hours playing i was not a fan of the second. But as i became more aware of how the game works i started to grow very found of the game. 10/10 imo. I just don't do well with new things and changes, am i autistic?  That doesn't matter, you're not my doctor or my therapist just by the game and thank me later  <3
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is everything I was hoping it would be and it's everything a sequel should be.I was worried about performance but you know what? works just fine on my GTX 1080 just fine on high graphics settings, the sandbox mode is increadible, morphing the base land and building structures from single cubes and streaching it to wide spanning planes, there's a actual campaign with characters, more engaging perk progression  and easier placement of objects, a lot of good stuff to gush about so here's the "bad".It being a fresh game at launch, it's going to have severely less content as opposed to it's predecessor which received multiple free updates of stuff along with DLC to go along with it, another is you can't build walls diagonally unless you do it MInecraft style by placing blocks adjacent to eachother AND I think it takes a bit too long before you are let loose to embrace your true nature of a being able to Flip Houses but those just feel like nitpics that can be dismissed and besides there this game's going to recieve a lot of community input and support from the devs.It's a definite BUY.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: HF1 is better than HF2. HF1 has more choices such as full glass wall and carpets for the floor. With the pricing being more expensive than HF1, it lacks the 'WOW' factor that HF1 has and more customization with regards to  the different items that we can chose. Just get House Flipper 1. Don't bother with House Flipper 2.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a few hour into this game now and I've been getting really bad motion sickness. I've look at advice online and turned off the motion blur and turned up the FOV but still having it. I played the first game for hundreds of hours without any issues (aside from mowing the lawn used to make me feel sick). It's such a shame as well because they've completely changed the way you paint - there was nothing wrong with the previous way of doing this and it seems like a change for the sake of it and also one of the main things making me feel sick. They also left out the before and after sequence you'd get when completing as job which was something I really enjoyed in the last game.The graphics are good and there's a nice story line in  story mode - they've given the flipper a family and friends. I recommend this game if you don't suffer from motion sickness or are happy to wait to see if the developers fix this.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first House Flipper--I bought every expansion pack and played for hours on end. In fact, I'm still not completely done with the game. It made me feel a bit queasy at times, but I was able to power through and eventually it didn't bother me much at all unless I was having an off day. Not so this new game. I can hardly play before I get sick and I set all the developer's recommended settings to avoid it. So I can only play for maybe an hour at a time. Notwithstanding the motion sickness problem, I find I'm not having fun with this one. I'm not sure exactly what the problem is. I feel like there's not enough cleaning, which I loved from the first game. Also, and I'm sure I'm in a distinct minority here, but I really don't like all the endless options for design. To me, it's kind of overwhelming. I'm sure I would appreciate it when renovating my own home in the game, but for jobs, it just makes me tired. There's just something about this one that isn't grabbing me, and I've played for 8 hours so far. If it wasn't making me sick to my stomach, I would give it a longer go, but as it stands, unless they can fix that problem, I likely won't play much, if at all, and I definitely won't be buying any expansions. I'm really disappointed because I looked forward to this release. If anyone has any suggestions for the motion sickness beyond the standards that I already use (lighting, seabands, play on a small screen, developer recommended settings, etc), please let me know.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hot mess. So many bugs. They built it up that it 2as supposed to be really great and it's a very big let down. It's very cartoon like as others have stated and even after adjusting blur and other motion settings gave me motion sickness within 5 minutes. There are not many furniture options like HF1. I miss the old tools immensely. Who wants to walk around filling up trash bags then having to take them all the way outside to the bin? _childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the original House Flipper, you will almost certainly love this sequel. I put a lot of hours into the first one and I liked it a lot but there were always things that bugged me in the first one.  I'd be having a good play session then be reminded that there was not easy way to copy styles of something or to duplicate an item, etc. The selling tool had such potential for other functions involving objects and it just wasn't there. It felt like being emotionally nickeled and dimed the whole time, being reminded of these glaringly obvious features that just weren't there.House Flipper 2 addresses every one of those frustrations and more. Through the story mode, the different renovation tools will be unlocked. At some point, the extra features of the Flipping tool thing become available and it's! So! Good! You select the tool, then you can bring up a radial wheel for itself to switch between Sell, Copy Style, Duplicate, and Edit. That alone would be reason enough to want the sequel. It makes adjusting things so easy. You can copy the style of a door and paste it onto a cabinet or a storage unit, etc. Let's say you made a need chair, went and did something else, then came back and decided you wanted another chair. You don't have to try to dredge up the memories of what it was you put together. You can just COPY THE THING and buy another one! This review could be only on those tool additions and I wouldn't feel bad about writing it, but there are a lot of other great things in here. - The item customization is ridiculously good. The patterns available for use at launch are great and they can be further augmented via textures, pattern size, and color adjustments, etc. And you can apply them to so many things. Pillows? Wallpapers? Wooden things? Sure! Go nuts! - The surface textures (paint, wallpapers, tiles, etc) are also real good. There's some overlap here with the above statement since the patterns can be used as wallpapers but I'm mostly directing this one at the other types of surfaces: wood textures, brick, tile, marble, etc. They're all so good and such an improvement over the original at its launch. - The available color palettes for paints and textures. The previous game had a lot of desaturated tones to choose from and then a lot of incredibly intense tones but it missed a lot of mid-tones and that was always frustrating to me. But now, there are four intensities of the color palettes available for use in various applications. - The soundtrack! The music was pretty lacking in the first game. The main theme was good but there just wasn't enough music and it got very repetitive. The sequel has many more songs available and they real nice to listen to. There also seems to be some neighborhood-specific songs, so you're not always hearing all the same ones all the time, which is a refreshing change.- The art direction. I've seen some people complaining about the art style in this game and how it's not as realistic as the first game and I honestly don't understand the gripe. The first game was at least partially shackled to the assets they originally used, which is limiting. The devs even talked about this in an article recently. House Flipper 2's art direction allows them more freedom to be expressive and when you're working with a cohesive vision from the start, everything looks like it belongs, even if the types of furniture, textures, materials, etc represented are of different styles/eras. You're not beholden to the artistic vision of an asset artist from outside your studio, too. It's an overwhelming net-gain for this series.There are a lot of other positives here but I'd be typing all day. So, it's time for some drawbacks before wrapping this upI have hopes that there will be a free content update at some point in the next few months before the inevitable first DLC is announced. I'm not rabidly upset about the amount of items available at launch. There are a respectable amount. Given the systems they had to develop to make such deep customization in everything, as well as the new features, I'm not surprised at the amount of items in game. For those who haven't picked it up yet, it's not a small amount. I don't want you to think that there's only a few things to play with. That's not the case. But coming from House Flipper with most of the DLCs, it will feel like there's not much available. I don't remember now the amount of things the original House Flipper launched with, so I can't say if it's close to 1 to 1 or if one had more than the other. House Flipper 2 being so much better in almost every way makes me more than okay with the available items at launch. Would I have liked it if there were a few more types of furniture or lighting or such available at launch? Of course. Though, the biggest bit of frustration in regards to items at launch comes from the fact that there are currently no blinds, shades, or drapes/curtains at launch. THAT is a bit more frustrating. But again, given everything they had to develop for this game, I'm guessing the tech for that was tricky. And, the original House Flipper didn't have those things for awhile, either. I'm sure it will be added in the future. And I hope it doesn't come exclusive to a DLC. I don't think they would do that (I hope they wouldn't do that) but if they do, then I'm gonna be Big Annoyed about it. So far, those are my only real complaints. There could be more items at launch but it's not the end of the world and I don't feel like what's available is paltry. And yeah, interior window coverings should be there. Other than that, though, if you liked the original, you will almost certainly fall in love with the sequel immediately. I got sucked in the day in launched and played for like 7 hours. And it didn't feel like that long at all. It was so good.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the first House Flipper and have almost 200 hours in the original. It was the best house decorating game ever created, in my opinion, so I was so excited when I found out a new one was coming out. And I can say that I am quite pleased with the result. I do not agree with anyone not recommending this game in its current state as it seems to have a decent amount of content for the money and I've put many hours into it already and only just finished the final community center.(I did accidentally leave my game on overnight so it took me about 12 hours total I think to get there and I did NOT finish every single job and have not bought even one house yet.) I do take my time, thoroughly enjoy the decorating process, and always get my three stars for each project so how fast you finish will be very dependent on who is playing.   My only critiques of this game so far are that I can honestly say I just prefer the original way of painting. While I appreciate the attempt at making a more realistic looking painting process it is just a little bit wonky and even when you get used to it its just not that enjoyable. Another minor thing that I would honestly not even care much for them to change is I kind of preferred being able to fill the whole floor with paneling/tiling just because it saved a little bit of time. It's not that big of a deal though. With that being said the other changes have been great. Making walls, the color/pattern creation, the changes to the flipper tool for duplication and style copy, cleaning(especially with windows), and other aspects of the game are noticeable improvements. My biggest GLARING issue with this game currently is the one everyone else is pointing out....not having before and after photos after each flip is a serious oversight that I cannot comprehend why they made that decision. I feel the entire point of this game is the enjoyment you get afterwards seeing the improvements you have made. Whenever they do their first update I really hope they add that back into the game because I am so sad without it. Overall though, I think the game is great and I think it is still absolutely worth buying. Edit: Before and After photos have been added and i'm sailin happy!

_childDocuments_.review: With 10 hours in, I highly recommend House Flipper 2 for both fans of HF1 and new builders. House Flipper 2 is beautiful, with more comfortable, intuitive controls than HF1 and far more build options. Sandbox mode is fantastic. With some experience with the controls, which largely carry over from HF1, you are able to create a house quickly but with very fine control over details. House Flipper 2 feels like a massive upgrade from House Flipper 1.PROS:     - Gorgeous     - More build options     - New style designer & ability to copy materials     - Intuitive controls     - Less motion sickness--camera is a bit more stable and certain tasks require less movement than in HF1     - Sandbox mode is what I've wanted in HF1 for yearsCONS:     - Missing some important items like window treatments     - I'd like to see some of the sandbox features implemented in the normal gameplay mode, such as columns     - No Steam Workshop support. Instead the game uses something called mod.io      - Few bugs that I expect will be patched quickly, nothing game breaking (sandbox mode bugs & small changes to your house not being saved after assembly)     - I'd like to see more accessibility options.Overall House Flipper 2 is more than a worthy successor to House Flipper 1 and I'm excited to see what Frozen District has in store for the future of HF2.

_childDocuments_.review: I love house flipper the first one and I'm enjoying this second one, as an actual interior designer it brings me joy to actually get to design houses. That being said there are a few things I am not a fan of, first being I feel like there are not enough interior and exterior door options, you have very limited to choose from. Secondly some of the mechanics are a little wonky, specifically when you're trying to make stairs, I was flipping my first house and even working on the starter house it was hard to make stairs. Third of all assembling furniture, some of the mechanics don't work, like I tried for several times trying to get a handle onto the nightstand and it would not go on, the same thing happens when building the desk and some of the cabinets. It doesn't always click right away and takes some time and it's very frustrating. It can take you several moments to do it and by the time you do you've gone over the time limit. Which brings me to my next point, DO NOT HAVE TIME LIMIT CONSTRAINTS when assembling furniture, it made me stress out and mess up a lot because I was trying to do it in the set time limit to get three stars. I have to keep going back and doing it over and over to get three stars. Oh one more thing, have more options for pictures, I know you can upload your own but there is very little art to choose from, I'm hoping for more in the future because this game has a lot of potential. Would I still recommend this game of course. There just needs to be more options overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so I played a few more hours than I intended to try and change this review but it didn't unfortunately. I put so many hours into the first game that I really wanted this one and I had imagined what it would be - HF1 but with better graphics and hopefully everything being a little faster, more cool stuff etc etc and that is NOT what we've got. What we've got, is robbed. I'll start with some positives though just to be thorough:Graphics are better, no doubt. Really nice. Building, panelling and tiling are better and faster, thankfully.I like the fact you can create your own styles with each item - very Sims 3-ish. There's a Sandbox mode! _childDocuments_.review: Not recommended yet, will need to give it time for patches before I really get into it. It's by no means a bad game but I'm mostly disappointed after looking forward to this for months (and avoiding spoilers).There are many improvements over the first game, such as the dramatically increased freedom to change objects. Some quality of life features are things I really missed in the first game, like the duplicate feature or the ability to change object styles. Visually, it's absolutely lovely and I enjoy the story bits very much.As for the negatives: A lot of UI things where I'm unsure if I haven't found the option or if it's missing/requires specific actions to unlock, such as...- seeing all open quests for a house- selling a house (after buying your first house to flip), this is probably explained but if so I don't know what I need to do to trigger this explanation. I shouldn't have to look up videos or guides for a cozy casual game, though.- getting out of a sub menu for color changes for things like beds (probably exists, but couldn't find it). Seems to be a bit inconsistent, didn't really have a problem for surface coverings. The paint menu for example is great.As for tools:In general: - You have to move furniture around to change the walls and floor. QoL downgrade imo- No more assembly required, apparently. Feels like playing the Sims. I suppose this could be seen as an improvement, but I found this part of HF1 very satisfying, which is the main point of playing a game like this for a long time for me.Painting: Feels very clunky. Being able to limit the painted area is great, but I cannot figure out a way to not have to select an area and just get started. Also, the large brush is nice but can only be used on a 3x3+ square area so it's a bit of a minor improvement. Also, since your camera is locked to the selection area, moving it around is tedious and slow.Tiles/Panels: So much clicking. At least it's fast from the start.Cleaning: Already tired of walking to a bin all the time. A lot less satisfying than it used to be in the first game. _childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write reviews, but wanted to chime in and give my two cents as someone who was a huge fan of the first game.HF2 takes EVERYTHING from the first game, gives it a brand new coat of paint, and improves on it in almost every way.Gone are the stock unity assets that the first game came to be known by, and in it's place are a whole multitude of original assets that can not only be customized in color, but also finish, and even structure in some cases.The painting system has been completely revamped and gone from probably the most tedious part of the first game, to a fun, and significantly less daunting activity in the sequel.The vacuum system, as minute as it sounds, has been given a brand new polish, and not only are there multiple things that can be sucked up using the tool, but you'll never run into errant cockroaches or shards of glass that can't be located without wildly waving the mouse around until the task is complete.If you played the original game's HGTV and Luxury DLC, you'll remember how they introduced "quests" through context sensitive bubbles that would appear in rooms. This has been carried over from those experiences, and are a great way to segment out a house and make it simpler and more intuitive to keep track of tasks in each room.The purchasing system has also gotten a HUGE upgrade, as the new "flipper tool", is used for a lot more than just selling items, as it was in the first game. When you purchase items, you have a lot more granular control over the materials, colors, and construction of said items, with a load of presets if you don't want to fuss about with color schemes of basic items to match your interiors. The second, and biggest QOL improvement that comes with the new tool, is the ability to copy themes from one item, to another, and change themes of items that have already been bought. This may not sound like much, but being able to purchase an item in one color, see it in your space, and then tweak it's theme without having to buy it again is more appreciated than you may think.The last thing that majorly stands out to me with this game, is the extreme polish that it seems to have launched with. In the era of buggy "early-access-but-not-early-access" PC ports of console games, and studios that never have any intention of releasing a "finished" game, i've yet to encounter any bugs with the game, and performance is extremely respectable (Running on a Ryzen 7 5800x3d & 3070). This game easily churns out native 1440p at 80-150fps average, and even has support for DLSS and FSR for that added frame boost on older and less capable hardware. On top of there not being any major bugs that stand out so far. The item placement system that uses large grid stepping, or smalled "precise" grid stepping, is a huge welcome addition that makes symmetrical item placement easy, and adds to that overall feeling of polish and work that Frozen District put in.I almost never buy games on launch anymore, but given the post-launch support of the first game, and the joy it brings me as my go-to relaxation game, I decided to give it a shot, and woke up at 5am to play it on launch day. I'm glad I did, and have already been sending out recommendations to friends.Well done FD!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Game's not for me, It's a great game, but I personally don't like it. Get the game if you love the dev's work and want to try house flipper, but with more advanced/detailed mechanics to the first game. I do and I don't recommend this game, but I will be thumbs upping it in support of the dev team.I don't know how to mark text as spoilers as I don't do reviews often, but SPOILERS FOR THE GAME BEYOND THIS POINT!!!!!!!!!Alright after playing it for under 2 hours I did have to refund the product. House Flipper 2 is not as good as the first one, not that's not to say the game is bad. It just isn't for me. I'll do my personal likes and dislikes. I won't do a pros and cons, but I will put some technical things that did turn me away from this game and lead me to refunding it.Likes:Graphics - The graphics are nice, I personally like them. They look good regardless of your resolution. Soundtrack - The soundtrack is simple and really adds to that "this is a chill game" vibe.Starter Home - The way the game starts and the starter home feel like welcoming, the home itself definitely needs improvement and you'll have to renovate the home to your liking, which again, fits the games narrative and vibe. Love it.Placement Grid - Holy hell do I love this feature, it makes placing objects superior to the first house flipper.Dislikes: The missions - The further you go into the game the more repetitive the missions are, and yes I get it, the last house flipper game suffered from the same thing, at least it felt some what unique with each mission and passing DLC. It's just clean, unpack, sell, and repeat. Some missions have you buying items which is normal, but I don't know it just felt more enjoyable to do in the first one compared to this one. I could just be biased.The Perks - Alright look, the perks for this one are more clean looking, but they suck. An example, you need a perk to move quickly while holding objects... no thank you. Another bad perk in my opinion is the flipper radar to see dirt and trash... you don't need to extend the time items stay high lighted as they're lit for a decent amount of time as is. The Painting - This is what made me uninstall. After finishing the first mission in the second area I found myself annoyed at how the painting works. It works EXACTLY like cleaning a window, but in a grid like format. Not a fan of that, I prefer HF1's way of painting. I don't want my camera to have to scroll up and down for me to get spots I missed. While I get this might be a little petty, if there is any mechanic in a game that is a core mechanic and I'm not very comfortable with how it works, then I just won't play the game.Now do I recommend this game? Yes and no.Yes if you like the series and want to support the dev team. I 100% would recommend it, if you like change and if you just generally enjoy home renovating GET THIS GAME. No if you're like me and prefer the nostalgic aspect of the dev's work from HF1. I like this game, I do believe it's a great game in the making. It's just not for me and that's okay. Now for the bug section:The biggest game breaking bug I've found, and that I've tested a few times is that when you change your graphic settings from ultra high to high and you're in a mission, the game black screens. this only happens when switching from Ultra High to High. Easy fix? configure the graphics at the home screen until they patch, not that big of a deal though.
