_childDocuments_.review: When I recommend this game, know that it is a very weak recommendation. If you have never played House Flipper, you will love this game. If you were an avid player of House Flipper, this game will infuriate you. While it is a bit prettier than the first game, that's about all it has going for it. The main story is laughably short (10ish hours? for $40??), and the new mechanics introduced (like laying surface tiles/panels, painting, the new quest system, etc.) are super annoying. I honestly wouldn't be surprised if the new method of laying tiles/panels and painting were introduced just to make the game take longer to complete. Painting is also a pain because it constantly freezes if you're too close to the wall, though in some jobs you have to be right on top of the wall to even reach where you need to paint. Additionally, you can't place furniture if you are standing on something other than the floor anymore; it's really frustrating. I greatly wish they would bring back the full to-do list for the entire property, not just the room you're in. I also dislike the fact you get 3 stars when the entire property isn't finished. Please bring back the old mechanic for painting and laying tiles or panels, or at least make it an option in the menu.tldrNot a bad game, but I only recommend it to players that didn't play House Flipper. For House Flipper fans, prepare to be disappointed

_childDocuments_.review: I loved house flipper. It wasn't perfect as nothing ever is but I loved it because it was unique, casual and that it could be calming. Nothing like turning off the sound, playing Spotify in the background and just doing some easy, repetitive tasks to meditate in a way . So i got really excited when House Flipper 2 was announced. I wish I could give numerical ratings instead of a yes or no recommendation. The game isn't bad, it has the same basic elements and there are definitely improvements that are really awesome, but I just feel meh about the game. It will take some getting used to since it is different but I don't think I will ever like it as much as I liked the original, but only time will tell. There are a few things that I dislike: I dislike the painting mechanics in this game (originally I had hate here but the longer I played and the more used to it I got, I stopped hating it is as much. Still prefer the old HF1 painting mechanic). There is no more assembly required for plumbing fixtures or outlets or heating or cooling systems so things can just go where ever. There is an assembly menu but it it not the same. You access the assembly menu from your tablet and you assemble furniture(although you do get to assemble a bathtub. There may be other plumbing fixtures but I havemn) and get future discounts on assembled items from then on. You do not have to assemble them more than once unless you want to. I will say I like that there are different levels of difficulty when it comes to assembly. I had the option enabled in HF1 but there really wasn't a difference in the difficulties. I don't know if discount is determined by grade (max 3 stars), difficulty (easy, medium), or a combination of both. You can re-assemble as much as you want so you can keep trying for 3 stars Again there is a new feature, wiring, but it is very limited and just assigning lights (maybe other electronics too, I haven't tried) to work with a specific switch. I do like the extra assembly since it is a real thing you have to do (and I am apparently the family furniture assembler so I have done it a lot) and its pretty realistic assembling too, but I miss setting up pipes for plumbing fixtures and the simple wiring of outlets or AC units, outside of an assembly menu and as part of the renovation game play. The game is less renovation simulation now and more decoration simulation, which isn't bad but part of the unique fun of HF1 was the home renovation actions required when preparing houses. I also do not like the lack of a mini map, but I do like the new flipper sense or whatever that kind of takes the place of the mini map when it comes to locating trash or dirty areas. I don't like the new star system for job completion instead of percentage (they mean the same thing for the most part but you don't only get 3 starts at 100% completion so you may not be 100% done when you have 3 stars  and I am a completionist so it was nice to know when I was completely done with everything) .  I also do not like the new job task menu in the tablet. At first it was confusing but as I got used to it, it became easier to understand, but instead of being able to see the tasks all at once and by room, you only see the tasks of the current room you are in and I find the perks are a bit lame  (I just feel like they are a bit lackluster in upgraded capabilities compared the the first game).  I am not too happy with the whole actually having trash bags to throw away feature but its not the worst thing ever and this game is not the only way to have a feature like that, but that doesn't change the fact I wish there was an option to turn the limited trash bag capacity on or off. There are a couple of achievements that require throwing away the trash bags so people should be reminded of that if the option is available (Like: Warning You are about to enable unlimited trash bag capacity. Please be aware there are 2 achievements that require the limited bag feature, but that the feature can be toggled at any time. People can be a bit dumb sometimes so even if it feels unnecessary, explicitly stating some  things is a must in games -.-).I do not like the fact curtains and blinds are not in the game. This is a little thing but curtains just feel like one of those basic items that should be available at the beginning. I have said a lot of things I dislike about the game but there are also things that I like. The new flipper tool features (that's the thing you use to sell stuff), which are things I so wanted to be implemented in the first game. Of course a better game engine means nicer and smoother game play and graphics, making it somewhat difficult to go back to HF1. The furniture customization options have expanded. At first I thought it was like sims 3 in that you can customize everything however you want, but there are limits so that was a bit disappointing, but there are generally more options for objects. Will say though, when choosing colors of things, you have 4 options (drab, faded, rich and another one i can't think of) but when it comes to paint colors, you only get to choose between rich and faded. Little disappointing when I was trying to color match wallpaper and paint. Speaking of wallpaper, placing wallpaper, tiles and paneling is much nicer in this game. When it comes to walls, instead of being 1 tall column, the wall is broken down into smaller squares so you can panel half the wall and then paint, wallpaper or tile the other half with whatever combination you want or go crazy and tile, panel, paint and wallpaper all at the same time! I don't notice a lot of difference when it comes to flooring or the ceiling (besides being able to also paint the floors now). However, you don't get to see your character holding the tiles or panels in their hands or make hand motions when placing surfaces. Not a big deal, just a tad disappointing again. Overall, I think if you enjoyed playing HF1 that you will enjoy playing HF2, but I wouldn't say it was worth buying full price. I want to support the developers but I wasn't super excited and blown away when I started the game, which made it hard to think my money was well spent. I am excited to see future DLCs and content and features, hoping some HF1 DLCs make a comeback of some type, and I would like there to be an option for classic mode or something. Like how in HF1 you could choose to show cockroaches or broken glass, but this time it would be for choosing between HF2 style tablet, trash picking up or the HF1 one style . I want to include painting but with the ability to to customize a bunch of little squares instead of the entire wall column, I do not know how the original painting mechanic could be implemented again. I would also like to see a return of old assembly of things (and more wiring options), and I hope there would be a way to do it so people who liked the assembly from HF1 can do it, but players who don't miss the features aren't forced to do it. So Devs, if you read this: maybe the first DLC can be like HF Classic Style or something. It would be nice to have all the HF1 features that are missed being implemented for free, but I understand that it would be a lot of work to do and so would be willing to support the team by paying for the options as a DLC and I hope that many other players will agree.EDIT: Some windows do have shutters as options but thats not the same as curtains but felt like it was worth mentioning. I also just realized there is no carpeting. There are rugs you can buy as floor decorations but you can't carpet the floors.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy playing this game. The graphics are pretty much the same as in House Flipper 1, IMO, but the custimizations are better, and I really like the duplicate/clone tool as well as the ability to "fly". I can imagine that I've got many, many hours of gameplay left. And if I should run out of jobs to do or houses to flip, there's always the community content.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow I can't shake the feeling that the developers didn't understand why people liked HF1 so much.After a few hours in HF2 I no longer have any motivation to continue playing. Everything is casualized, everything feels very inconsequential and slick.A lot of interesting things have been removed from the game. Even a trained monkey can do what's left. What a shame, I was really looking forward to the second part.Oh, the new method of painting the walls is one of the worst things that has been done, it's just not fun at all.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: It is a lot more to take on than the previous House Flipper game. But I do kind of find it annoying it took me close to 7 hours of playing before I could buy a house and build walls. I still wish I could cut the grass. I also feel the game is lacking paint colors, carpet floor coverings so I do not need to use area rugs, differ floor tiles.Painting is kind of a pain in the butt too because some times the roller just wont move with my mouse even when I have a fresh roller of paint.Other than that the graphics are great and the game runs smooth. _childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed reviews about this game. I really love House Flipper the original game. With House Flipper 2, I was excited at first but disappointed after playing it. I loved the original mechanics for painting, destroying walls and  building, but House Flipper 2 has a really annoying painting mechanic and the building is strange to me as well. If you never played House Flipper 1, then House flipper 2 will be ok for you. It is just a disappointment for me to switch to 2
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great iteration on the first game with many, many quality of life improvements, better performance, and much more control over your designs and houses.A little light on content at the moment, but a great foundation for the inevitable DLC, and plenty to do in the mean time.Only real complaint I have is that painting is a little awkward compared to first, but still very usable.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: The good: I love the customizability of all the items and what not in game. also the ability to duplicate items, or copy item styles or change them afterwards is really nice and much appreciated.The bad: I very much miss the old painting mechanic, I get the draw for a more realistic way of doing it, but I wish there was at least an option to go back to HF1's painting mechanic. also I can't believe I'm saying this but I also miss the plumbing assembly mechanic from HF1. I wish there was an option to turn that on, and not just as a mini-game. overall HF2 doesn't seem to be keeping my attention the same way HF1 did, and I find myself quitting halfway through a flip because the motivation and enjoyment just isn't there. And for some reason playing this game makes me want to go back to playing the first one. The game isn't bad by any means, it just feels like some things are missing.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I really hope they will add additional story later on, because I feel like HF 1 had so much more "work" even in the base game. I was shocked to see it already ending.I'm only 2 hours into the game, but I can already tell you it's worth every penny! The game changed so much, but still has the the same "house flipper vibes" and I'm so happy about it. It's nice to see that there's a storyline this time and the voice acting is great. _childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: By now I've played for about 125 hours. At first I was quite happy with the game, but the further along we get in development, the less fun it's becoming. I don't have the best pc, but considered I was able to run it on very high graphic mode at the start, it's a mystery to me as to why my game keeps crashing over the graphics now even on medium. The loading screens are miserably long and the music which consists of multiple layers, keep lagging so the different layers don't play at the right time and become unbearable to listen to. With the so called big summer update we got 1 new job to play. 1. This feels like a joke at this point. I don't think I'll be playing this very soon again. Maybe I'll check it out in a few months to see if things are more to my liking.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game so long now and I love it! Even more then the first House Flipper which I've put ALOT of time in. It's a bit of a learning curve but sooo fun. I love all the new additions and so far all the things I thought was missing or was right out tedious in the first House Flipper is changed for the better in this one. _childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: There is no longer assembly required for showers and appliances. There isnt much furniture or picture frames to choose from, not alot of content. Im still trying to figure out where the siding is for the outside of the home, and I cant find any. There is no carpet in the game, just all hard flooring. Plaster is no longer required to paint rough walls in run down homes. I was hoping the second game would be more realistic especially in the construction area, like actually being able to frame up a home, and screw in dry wall. The graphics are better than the first game, but the game is so incomplete and it should have not been released.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this game, it has a lot of positives, though the negatives are felt for those that are fans of the first game. Pros:Looks greatRuns SmoothFeels more polished and up to dateBeing able to do things by each square allows you to paint and build in a much more customized way. The story line is cute and sillyCopy and paste for item and style is top notchNot having to install plumbing is really nice and less tediousCleaning is more satisfyingPlacement feels betterSense mode to find items you missed it helpfulCons:No before and after is a punch to the gut, because that really makes the remodel feel less finalizedVery small catalogue of items considering how much was in the first game (I understand they will add more, but why are we having to wait when that could have been in the full game).Feels like there are things missing, just to be able to make DLCs to come. Overall it is a great addition the the franchise, though in some ways it feels like the content is a lateral move from the first one, while it does looks better and have updated mechanics. It is almost like a well made remake of House Flipper 1 and that isn't bad, just not what I was hoping it would be. I am hoping and expecting these things to all be fixed and added as patches and content are put out for the game. Edit (5/25/24):I am changing this to a downvote, because the work in progress mechanics and additions are really being thrown aside for garbage updates, and so many of them are what I am waiting for in order to play this game. Stick with the first one and just forget about this one until they actually add a game here.Edit (6/26/24):While I do appreciate the updates from the first game. I would suggest you wait until there are many more updates and DLC releases. The overall flip ability is smooth, however there is still a smaller catalogue as compared to the first one. The before and after has finally been added, however it is much worse than the first game with it zooming in on one wall you worked on in about 70% of the rooms you just worked on. They tried to make it have style and in the end made it worse. Just put the camera in the top corner of the room, or allow players to place the before and after cameras. I still do not understand how they made a game that has so little compared to the original, and before people complain that most of that came in the DLC, this is a sequel. When you make a sequel you implement the good things from the first game, not follow the same timeline as number 1. You improve...not just do the same thing with updates. It feels more like a remaster, rather than a follow up.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I know they will release DLCs to add more items to the game, but the base game is EXTREMELY bare bones. There are hardly any choices for decor at all. They seemed to have removed the ability to see what items you used recently, which, if you customize something, makes it very difficult to re-do that customization again. Also, when you copy a used item (Like Paint or Panels), you don't get the full amount. Perhaps there should be an option for that? TLDR: The game is OK. But not for base price. I'd wait until it goes on sale for 50% off or more.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: With a ton of improvements and additions comes the taking away of a lot of essential features from the first game. Play if you loved 1 and wanted more, but expect disappointment.This game is unexpectedly.. empty? In the furniture department?? I would ASSUME they want you to get your variety out of the endless customization (which btw i really like but even with the right perks matching all of your furniture is a chore.) Outdoor customization is rather limited which is EXTREMELY WORRYING.. I have a sinking feeling a lot of stuff will be added at a later date, but as 15 dollar DLC, AGAIN.... Which would be extremely disappointing. Let's hope they plan to add workshop support. The sandbox mode I can only describe as *really irritating.* I would rather you give me empty houses and unlimited money, not expect me to go make my own levels for players.I still like this game, and I find myself coming back to it again and again, but I hold out hope that they're going to give us something more than this.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game so far. They've made so many great changes. In sandbox mode we can build our own house and even make them dirty so you can upload and other people can play the house. That makes option endless really. _childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first time I've been drawn to leave a review on any game. Summary: Great update to the first, updated mechanics for some tools and lovely graphics, but lack of _any_ buyer feedback (or buyer personalities like in HF1) makes it not fun for me to actually flip houses.I cannot recommend this game for most people until this is added. You might enjoy it if you like more abstract sandbox style play? If you have played HF1 you will probably be frustrated by this. If you have not, then go and play HF1 instead of buying this.Was very excited for this, bought it day 1! I played HF1 a lot, with all the DLCs, and enjoyed it tremendously, although it was not a perfect game. So even if this was basically HF1 with an updated graphical engine and new houses/jobs I would have been extremely happy. However, I am very much not. Unfortunately you have to play through a few job levels to start buying houses, and I was not in a rush and did a few so by the time I realised the lack of the buyer feedback mechanic I already had too many hours logged to request a refund. This review will remain as a not recommend for me unless this changes :`( PROS: - It's beautiful! Graphically very pretty, lots of cute details- Updated mechanics for many tasks, cleaning, painting, surface finishing (formerly tiling), that I prefer overall. - Cute easter eggs, story, details in the houses- Vastly expanded aesthetic choices- Changed the assembly mechanic entirely (a very tedious part of HF1 in my opinion), big improvement.- Really adorable art style for loading screens and other supplementary things.- Probably a lot more, and I look forward to (hopefully) being able to edit my review to recommend so I can find more things I like about it!- Nice relaxing music (although could use more variety)CON: (There is only one I found but as mentioned before, for me it is fun-breaking).There is no buyer feedback (like in HF1 when you put the house up for sale, you would get comments from buyers like "+house is clean", "-damaged walls" etc. to give you an idea of how you can get a better house price in general.Beyond the general buyer feedback, if the buyers in HF2 have individual preferences there is no indication of that. In HF1 the buyers had personalities and related individual preferences. There were different family configurations from single people to large families, who wanted different amounts of bedrooms. They liked modern or rustic furniture etc. etc. etc. It was not perfect in HF1, the range of personalities got a little limited and repetitive after a while, but it provided more structure and interest than just cleaning everything and repainting damaged things. This just doesn't seem to exist in HF2. It really undermines what otherwise seems like a well made update to a game I sunk too many hours into.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game I wanted the original House Flipper to be. It's great to see the devs grow and remake the game into something absolutely wonderful. The controls are so much more fluid and pleasing to use. The art-style is beautiful and all of the items are very cohesive, making this feel like an actual game, and not just a proof of concept. I love the story line and best of all, the game has been greatly optimized over the first, so it runs really smooth and doesn't crash (which was a huge issue for me with the original game) I can't wait to see what the devs add to this addicting and fun game! I haven't found anything I dislike about this, and there was tons I disliked about the original. If you love cleaning, designing and decorating, this is the game for you!
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: had a longer review, but here's what you need to know:--game is full of bugs--bugs are only being addressed piecemeal monthly--updates sometimes make it worse--game shipped incomplete--obviously going to add stuff through DLC (think EA The Sims money hog)--didn't even include carpeting or window blinds--something like 3 feasible lamps to actually use (translation: most of the existing objects are too weird to use, or they don't stack properly to make any kind of tableau--they don't seem to want to use Steam Workshop at all to allow players to add objects--most game features that make this title different are in Sandbox and not Story mode, so it's not houseflipping anymore but housebuilding--although Sandbox can be used to make amazing things, it seems that incorporating it and player mods breaks the game repeatedly in crazy waysso: buy on sale, if at all
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, I love the original house flipper, and in most respects, I love the sequel. However there are several issues with the current game that I am desperately hoping the developers are planning to change through updates and dlc.To begin, the things that I like about this game:1. The door mechanics. I personally hated how the first game would allow the door to swing both ways regardless of how it was positioned. The doors in this game will only open one way, and can be obstructed by objects, which makes the game more realistic and personally, makes the builds slightly more personalized. 2. The color palette has been significantly improved. I love how the colors are sectioned into four categories to help with choosing the specific color palette you want for your home. 3. Tiling walls is no longer a chore. It's actually quite enjoyable to place tiles and wallpaper on walls, especially compared to the original game.4. The option for paint finishes. I love how you have the option to choose between the current two finishes, and I hope that over time there will be more finishes added to the paint selection.5. Cleaning windows is much easier and more enjoyable in this game. I will say that I personally had to lower the movement speed in order to make it usable, and if you move too quickly there will be spots that you have missed cleaning along the glass, but personally cleaning the windows no longer feels like a chore in this game. 6. You are finally able to place items inside of other objects. Specifically, drawers. This is a massive feature that was missing from the original game, and it made furnishing the kitchens a nightmare. But you can finally fill the kitchen with items in every nook and cranny. 7. The plant pots and the garden section of the store had been improved. I love how you can choose a pot and plant by the size, it makes it so much easier to go through the store and choose which option you are specifically looking for. 8. You can finally plant LARGE trees. I've had some issues trying to plant the largest trees currently available, but the medium sizes and small sizes are a delightful inclusion for various home designs.9. Flipper sense is a true blessing. You no longer need to stare at a mini map and blindly scrub for the last piece of dirt. You can clearly see where the dirt or other things that you need to handle are. 10. The copy tool makes flipping items so incredibly easy. You can finally go through the entire house and change all or the windows to match with a single click. You don't need to sell each individual window and look them up and change them individually. 11. The in-game artwork is beautiful. 12. You do not need to walk to the laptop in order to choose a job, buy a house, or check the email. It saves time and makes the process easier and more accessible. However, it does also make the laptop essentially pointless. 13. You can place towels on the handle of the oven. 14. You can place items inside of the fridge.15. Flower vases. I love the shapes and customization of the vases currently available in game. There are also a few options for plants that can be placed in the vases. Now, the things I don't like about the game:1. Currently, the color selection for paint outside of the sandbox mode is horrible. There is a small and curated selection of colors available for selection instead of the promised wide variety. This may be personal error with my confusion over using the in-game store, however it is annoying to try and find a specific color for your walls, only for it to not be available. 2. There are currently no blinds or curtain options available in game. 3. Like many other people have mentioned, the current selection for items in game is limited. I'm hoping that the developers will have some time to include different pieces, or that the workshop will be included into the game at some point, as there is a limited amount of items to choose from. The main items that I have noticed the lack of options in are: the rugs/carpets, clothing accessories, trash can options, and gym equipment.4. There is no longer the option to place a group of books at one time. In the original game there was the option for individual books or stacks of books, however in this game there is only the option to place individual books. 5. Currently the story mode is incredibly short. I finished the entire story mode in one day. I am hoping that the story will be expanded, or there will be more locations available over time, but currently there isn't much to go through. 6. The options for plants is currently very limited. The plants available are very detailed and beautiful, but there aren't a variety available for players to choose from. 7. There is currently no option for carpeted floors. 8. I have not been able to figure out how to import my own photo's into the game for custom photo's yet. There appears to be the option to import photo's into the game, however it isn't very straight-forward, and I would also be cautious about the security of personal photo's. If you don't want the photo's you use in-game to potentially be viewable to other players, then do not import them into the game.9. You are unable to place Polaroid photos on table tops. It appears that they are only able to be placed on walls. 10. Hanging clothing is only possible on specific hooks at this point in the game development. I've seen some houses in-game that have clothes hanging in wardrobes, but I have been unable to do the same in my own builds. 11. There are very few options for towels at the moment. There appears to only be the small, hand sized, towel option. 12. I have been unable to place more than one apple inside of a bowl. I have seen houses in-game that have multiple fruits in one bowl, however it has yet to be achieved in my own builds.

_childDocuments_.review: Just to get it out of the way, this does NOT have all the features and content as House Flipper 1 with all DLC has.What this DOES have is a ton of improvements to the foundational gameplay, which will likely be added on to over time through free updates and, yes, probably paid DLC.The big improvements over the base game include: -Better optimization-A more cohesive art style-Greater color customization for furniture and surface covers-Surface covers are now universal and can be placed on floors, walls, and ceilings-More freeform painting and building. Building is essentially voxel-based now, with each voxel being 20cmx20cmx20cm, allowing you to make variable height walls, raise or lower ceilings, build whole new additions to houses, destroy entire sections of houses, add or remove stories to houses, place windows just about anywhere, et cetera. Painting works by coloring the faces of the voxels that make up the house, allowing you to split up colors horizontally and vertically any way you like within the resolution allowed by the voxels.-A sandbox mode that is apparently very robust and allows even more customization than the normal tools available in regular gameplay, though I haven't tried it myself yet.Features HF1 fans might miss: -No before/after pictures (devs have all but confirmed these will be added, however)-No pets-Gardening and exterior decorating is there but not as in-depth as the Garden Flipper DLC-Furniture assembly has been relegated to its own minigame in the story mode separate from decorating so if you enjoyed putting together showers, sinks, and other appliances that's not really a part of the gameplay anymoreFeatures that are conspicuously missing: -No curtains-No carpeting-No master checklist of objectives when doing regular jobs-No seller feedback when actually auctioning a house-No minimap and by extension no way to look over the floor plan of a house-No way to tag rooms by functionOverall I do recommend this for offering a lot more freedom and customization over the first House Flipper, but I can't call it a strict upgrade from the first game just yet. Once the content updates get rolling I think this has the potential to surpass HF1 someday.

_childDocuments_.review: This version is even better than the original! Small but VERY important quality of life changes have been made - such as the eye dropper to match colors and patterns on all your furniture, the duplicate tool, the laser-thingy that shows you the patch of dirt you missed, etc - and it's absolutely awesome. The design is clean and beautiful, the paintings on the loading screen add a nice modern vibe to the game, the clients can phone you and tell you a bit more about their life which I find refreshing, and the choice in furniture, materials and colors is a thousand times better. Not sure about the new way of painting walls but it's doable enough with the keyboard so I'm sure I'll get used to it. Anyway, this is a very good follow-up to HF1 and I can't wait to dive more into it. Well done!EDIT: some things that may or may not get fixed by an update or DLC:- No more book stacks, which is sad. You have to put the books one by one and even though you can change the covers, it's really not ideal.- After my first house flip I noticed that there are much less choices of furniture than in HF1 but it'll probably get better with updates.- A lot less accessories and the ones we currently have are kind of empty, they don't make the houses feel like someone is living in it. Maybe modders will make cool things like in HF1 but I wish the base game would have done the work first.- Plants are difficult to center in pots and you have to put them one after the other. Centering things has always been a huge problem in HF but once again, I wish this problem had been addressed by the devs before the release. It's in progress though because now we have a grid that appears on screen and it helps center things a bit better than before.- While flipping houses for sale I also noticed that we have no indications regarding potential buyers. We don't know what they like or who they are so we have to flip houses blindly and hope it'll get bought. And once a buyer wins the auction, we don't know what they liked in the house, we can just accept or cancel the sale. No infos on the NPCs whatsoever. Too bad, it was fun to tailor house flips to one of the NPCs, it added some challenge.I'll edit further as I go along :)

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much a re-render of the first with a few mechanical changes. Overall, I agree with several prior reviews that this should've just been an update for the first game and not a whole new game in of itself. Couple of my biggest gripes:-Options. Decorations and furniture are extremely limited. Some things like the column supports are not in store, but can be duplicated....aka don't sell them if you plan to use them! -Completely missed aesthetics. Where are the curtains / blinds? There are none! I have yet to see a house IRL that doesn't have one or the other. -You cannot sell/delete any of the original roofs on a house, meaning you are stuck simply ADDING on instead of completely remodeling / rebuilding. Also means properties with detached carports are stuck being divorced carports or converted to a divorced garage.My biggest gripe out of all of them is simply the lack of money in ACTUALLY FLIPPING HOUSES!!! For the time invested my payout should be FAR GREATER than just 30-70k. Spend almost 2 hours or more completely redoing a property nets me less money per hour than just replaying certain jobs, which can net 31k in 15 minutes if you do everything (3 Stars). It's almost as if there is some unwritten rule that a property can only sell for a max of 20-30% more than the player's investment in the property and it's absolutely hocus-pocus.

I dont get why devs nowadays don't get the essence about their own game and why it got successful. The reason ppl loved the first game was to a great extend the workshop. It builds a community, it keeps you hooked to the game. What a shame. And probably money-driven, considering they want you to buy their own assets.- the game is still empty and not finished. After a while your houses  will all have the same looking rooms, because assets are so limited. - decisions dont matter at all in this game. It doesnt matter what you make a room, because there are no room types anymore. _childDocuments_.review: I have over 100 hours in the first game and have played this one to the point of unlocking all the tools. Long story short...House Flipper 2 gets a thumbs up from me, but just barely. TLDR summary = There's a few great improvements from the first, and a few major downgrades and over-simplifications. Overall, the game is overpriced for what it has available now. To new players, I'd say wait for a sale or the first round of DLC.Positives- Flipper tool changes are a big win! Before you only used it to sell items. Now you can also use it to modify items, duplicate items, or copy/paste styles from one item to another. An awesome feature to help make a consistent look and feel across a house or room.- The grid based item placement is a huge upgrade from the last game!- I love the changes to house plants. In HF1, you bought the pot and plant together as one item. Here, you buy them separately. You can buy the pot, and then buy one or more plants to place into them...you're free to create your own arrangements- Building walls has improved in this game. Click once for starting point, again for ending point, again for height. Big improvement...because building partial walls was cumbersome in the first game.- Cleaning windows no longer makes that awful squeaky noiseNegatives- Selling houses was my favorite part of HF1. The different buyers had different wants, you got active feedback for how your changes were affecting the opinions of perspective buyers, and there was a strategy to it. You could add an elaborate office space to appeal to one buyer, or add children's rooms to appeal to a buyer with a family. Now in HF2, you buy a house, you upgrade blindly, and you're given an offer from a random NPC...that's it. All of the heart this game mechanic used to have has been sucked out. This is my biggest criticism of HF2.- Assembly. In HF1, when you bought a sink or toilet or shower or various other items, you had to manually assemble them. Maybe even purchase plumbing hookups for them to work. It was something satisfying to do. But this has been removed in HF2. Everything you buy is simply drag-and-drop. Assembling things has been removed from the main game and relegated to a completely separate mini-game. You complete the "one and done" assembly mini-games for various items to receive a permanent 2% discount from buying these items in the future (which is a pretty trivial reward honestly). But you don't get the satisfaction of building them on site.- The environments around the houses are boring. HF1 houses felt more unique. In HF2...if, for example, you are working on a house in Crayfish Cove, that same house is surrounded by the same generic beach background every other Crayfish Cove house has with invisible walls to keep you from wandering too far. You never feel like you're building something in a new or exciting location.- The game's all around look and feel is more cartoonish than its predecessor

_childDocuments_.review: So I've played for almost 30 hours, and I'll say this. It's not terrible, has lots of cool houses to renovate and I love the different environments. However, so many elements of the first game are glaringly missing. You no longer assemble fixtures or outlets, you just plop them down. And I really enjoyed the assembling of things like showers, sinks, toilets, etc. You also don't have the before and after photos. And when you buy a house and renovate it for auction, you no longer have the list of buyers and what they prefer in a house. When you put it up for auction, you only get ONE buyer at first. To see a new price, you have to cancel the whole auction. Later you can get a perk to see at least three buyers and their prices, but it annoys me...that's not how auctions work. Another nice thing that's missing from the first game is the mission progress and task list for rooms. In the second game, you can finish the mission with one to three stars, but even when you have three stars there could be more things to finish and you won't know unless you run around and look for the yellow floating icon. Honestly, overall, I say the first is better. Maybe wait for this one to be on sale. Or until they add to it.

_childDocuments_.review: 4/13/2024 update:i figured this game would be better with time and thankfully it is :) every single issue i listed above has since been resolved, although i do wish there were more wallpaper options. personally i find a lot of them to be incredibly tacky, so i find myself having to settle for the least offensive ones. additionally, i think an undo button is in order because i deleted the roof at the peacy's house and now i can neither sell it nor fix it!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! LOL i'm looking forward to this game receiving more updates and continuing on this upward trajectory, although i can't say i'm not disappointed about another dev studio releasing a half-baked product for full price. anyways, as this game is right now i'd say its worth your money. i just think the original review is somewhat worth archiving (for my own peace of mind). TL;DR: game bad at launch but game pretty good now- original review below:i don't particularly appreciate how this game restrains what you can sell in the confines of your own home/office vs the original house flipper game. it frustrates me how i'm held hostage with specific items that the game deems unsellable/untrashable just based off how the developers programmed the game. i don't want the banana & envelope from the mailbox that you're given in the default office, yet i'm forced to keep it because the devs couldn't be bothered to program in selling or trashing it. there's no option to sandbox the base game, which is EXACTLY what i'd fear the devs would do after adding a full mode developed to sandboxing. these modes don't need to be mutually exclusive. you should be able to remove every single item from your office without any restraint. one of the best aspects of house flipper 1 was EXACTLY this feature. being able to fully customize my office was absolutely my favorite part of the game. i find it counterintuitive to the concept of house flipper to be unable to fully customize the base office to my liking. if i want to sell every single cabinet and drawer, so be it. it's ridiculous to be held back by the game's coding in this regard. LET ME SELL THE DAMN BANANA. LET ME SELL THE CABINETS I DON'T WANT. If I can't even do this in the base office, when i was able to fully flip and customize the original office, who is to say that this logic won't apply to any future homes i buy in game? in house flipper 1, i used my profit to buy a nice home. i sold every single piece of furniture within it to start from scratch. this option is not available to me in the sequel, despite this being a second rendition of a pre-existing game. if you're going to make a sequel, at the very least, basic controls and functions should carry over. i should not feel punished for buying the second game. everything else about this game is definitely a draw, but i am severely unimpressed by the lack of customization abilities within the confines of MY OWN OFFICE. Ultimately i cannot recommend this game, because although it is VERY FUN, you cannot do any customization in the base office beyond the tools they give you.ADDITIONALLY, i have to add that the window cleaning function is VERY BUGGED. Upon first installing and playing house flipper 2, i found that no matter how clean i got the windows, it would not mark it as clean. if i moved away/clicked away from the window upon realizing i was stuck in an infinite window cleaning glitch, the game would reset my progress and make me clean it from scratch again. considering window cleaning was such a cathartic process in the original game, i was profoundly disappointed to find that it is a glitchy mess in house flipper 2. upon reading other reviews as well, i noticed others pointing out that carpet and blinds/curtains were fully removed from this rendition. if that winds up being DLC, i will be SEVERELY disappointed. this game being $35 and then potentially asking me to spend extra money on something included in the original house flipper is just ridiculous. i'm jumping to conclusions here but i just can't find the reasoning behind the lack of carry over in this regard. that's all. thank you :)

_childDocuments_.review: Runs great on PC at launch, have experienced only a few minor bugs that were quickly fixed with a restart. Would not be surprised if they're hotfixed out very quickly. Given how glitchy some of the HF1 DLCs have been at launch, this was a very pleasant surprise.Improves a lot on the mechanics of HF1. I love how you can use WASD for painting so you don't have to move your wrist around a lot, and I like that with cleaning and vacuuming you don't have to "scrub", you can hover your mouse and it does most of the job.Pros over HF1: Customization is amazing. The tools are greatly improved, especially wall building and painting. I love how you can use the flipper tool to copy styles or change objects that are already placed - no more going back and forth trying to color match and having to sell furniture over and over. The graphics are really beautiful and the game runs great.Cons over HF1: I miss the before and afters a LOT. Especially spending extra time on quest houses to clean up and organize. There are also far fewer items than in HF1. Naturally, there's no DLC yet, but I wish there was more variety. There are also small frustrations like being unable to replace columns you sell. This seems like a big oversight.I miss the gardening DLC a lot, and I hope that they add it quickly into HF1. I like that you have a lot of landscaping options out of the box, but I miss paving stones and lawns.Overall the game runs great and is a very high-quality successor to HF1. I can't wait to see how they expand on this one with new DLCs.

_childDocuments_.review: Around the game's release, I posted a detailed review, but I wanted to make an entirely new one with my updated thoughts after months with the game.First of all, it's shocking to me how much this game has been review bombed. I think it has received the most unfair judgement of any recent releases. And I loved HF1, but for me, this game takes the cake for many reasons.One of the biggest changes is the mechanics. Painting, cleaning, and many of the other chores you're required to do throughout the campaign are made far more satisfying and less tedious in my opinion. Painting also allows you to be a lot more creative, as it's based on individual "squares" of wall, rather than top-to-bottom strips.And speaking of creativity, being able to make your own color and material variations on most pieces of furniture is a game changer. Even though this game is still fairly young and more furniture is being added, allowing the player to mess around with the individual parts of each piece of furniture makes the selection seem far bigger.There's also the graphics and performance. Like with House Flipper 1, the performance in this game isn't perfect, and that's probably one of the only cons I have with it, but it still runs fairly well on ultra with my card. The graphics are nice, a lot of people complained about it being too cartoon-y, but I think it strikes the perfect balance between realism and stylized. The lighting is way better than in HF1 which makes all the difference.Finally, my biggest pro for this game is the sandbox mode. It adds so much content, not only because you can build your own creations from scratch (with just as much detail as the houses in the campaign), but you can also build your own campaign levels and publish them for others to play. This feature alone adds infinitely more gameplay, because even if you don't like building your own structures, you can expand your playtime by downloading quests that other players have made.Overall, I'd highly recommend House Flipper 2. It's still so surprising to me that the game only has a mostly positive, I think it deserves at least 85-90% positive reviews. Many of the nitpicks that were mentioned in the earlier negative reviews, such as the lack of the before and after feature, and the game not having curtains, have been fixed. If you enjoy the creative process behind building your own house, or just the simple fun in transforming a dump into a palace, you'll really enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: House Flipper 2 is the sequel to one of my all time favorite comfort games ever, House Flipper. It brings much needed QoL adjustments, more in depth story, more decorative expression and building freedom as the player, and even an entire new sandbox mode. Yet, it also manages to miss a few things from the first game, things like the Steam Workshop (replaced by Mod.io, but full integration hasn’t yet happened) certain furniture items, some game settings, and oddly enough, even some sound effects. I believe the developers do know, and are working to fix these things, though. While the game is still a bit buggy even after the post-launch patches, it’s still a delightful game to play if you like interior design and the relaxing atmosphere that comes along with menial tasks like cleaning and unpacking. I will say, the game is a bit short for my liking, but I may be biased considering I just came from House Flipper original with several DLC packs added on, making the game quite long and obviously much longer than it would have been at launch. I’m excited to see what updates bring us, and how the game evolves from the state it’s in soon after launch. I’m hopeful that this will quickly surpass its predecessor as my favorite comfort game, but we will have to wait and see!

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of great improvements from the first version. The visuals are more cartoon-like this time around, but I can't complain about that much. It's a fun mini-game, though the controls are very touchy and not intuitive.The biggest complaint is that the game is very short. I hope that the devs will add more story-line content in a future patch for free. If not, then the game is not worth $39.99. You're better off saving your money and hoping that it becomes available through Xbox Game Pass sometime in the future. For this reason alone, I cannot recommend this game. If, however, you really don't mind burning $39.99, then do it!P.S. There are no blinds for the windows :(

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best building simulator I've seen so far (and I've seen pretty much all of them), by a very large margin.What can I say? It just works. It is way more flexible than anything else I’ve ever seen. Colour options, while not unlimited, are well chosen and useful; the object catalogue is rock solid; graphics look good and consistent. There are currently some annoyances when it comes to recolouring (e.g. some objects can only use certain materials; fabric patterns are mostly large or extremely large) but I don’t expect those to last and everything else … just works.Technically, it’s been super stable on my machine – I’ve had three or four crashes in 100+ hours of playtime and the built-in recovery worked flawlessly every time.There is one big caveat: sandbox mode, the actual building simulation, relies entirely and exclusively on the first-person game mechanics from Story Mode (and House Flipper 1, I assume). I can see that they wanted to cater to their existing user base, but still, for building it is mind-boggingly useless. You can’t just drop a thing and then move and resize it -- you need to select a different „tool“ for every little step along the way. Open the catalogue, drop your object. Open the tool selection, select the move tool. Open the tool options, change from Move to Resize. Yes, with the mouse(!). Open the tool options again and again whenever you need to turn the grid on or off (or even just check whether it is on or off, since there is no visual indicator for that), selecting the same two options with your mouse from a menu … over and over again.I very much hope this will change, but for now, be prepared for a lot of mind-numbing menu-clicking if you want to build anything more than a box with a door.For me, it’s totally worth the hassle though – I just love building stuff, and I really enjoy not having to find workarounds for every little thing like it used to be in other games.Can’t comment on the story mode side of things, since I haven’t used that and probably never will, but for those who like to build, you should definitely check this out.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure when I saw the sequel launch, I liked house flipper 1 so much and I was worried that the launch would be rough.I'm happy I was wrong.The sequel improves on every single system introduced in the original. Also, the graphics are absolutely gorgeous, a massive upgrade compared to the previous game. There's so much heart and love poured into the game and it really shines through as you advance in the game.It runs well, there are only few minor bugs I've experienced. A total surprise, a functioning, feature-rich game that's playable and fantastic right on launch. I've had some minor performance blips and FPS drops, but I'm sure those are gonna be addressed in future patches and hotfixes. Absolutely recommend this to everyone, not just fans of the original.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game so far!  Despite the negative criticism regarding there not being enough decorations, I'd say that the developers probably have some DLC or updates for that.  They'd always add new content to House Flipper 1 periodically.  Pros:- Item Favorites (Something I always wished was a thing)- Items stay in box or stays on shelf when moving, the entirety and contents all move- Different ways to search items- You start in a large house with 'potential'- Being able to use a phone and make response choices (you'd have to do that IRL too..)Cons:- 'Enough' to start with, but lacking in variety of items/surfaces- Story mode little slow to start, no tiles or wallpaper til the second area- Painting with the roller is WEIRD, somewhat helpful not to paint in unwanted areas, but the roller is hard to controlI'd say the game is worth buying and trying!  Guarantee they'll add more items, houses, content the older the game gets.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's like the first House Flipper but better! Sandbox mode is what I've always wanted and story mode is fun too. The ability to build from scratch opens up so many dream home opportunities. But the best part in my opinion is coordinating styles throughout the house build and interior design. Picking and choosing colors as well as textures/finishes gives you seemingly endless looks with a small amount of items. Sharing builds and even creating jobs gives me satisfaction and makes the time put into a big build worth it. There are some things that can be improved and added but I'm confident the developers will follow through.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun and relaxing game, but it's a P.O.S. regarding quality.I have to manually shut the game down after EVERY mission because it either locks-up on loading, or starts falling through the floor into an infinite void.Now I've played for 9 hours, so they got their money and it's too late to get a refund.I hope they fix the issues to make it playable in the future, but for now I would not recommend it.EDIT, Sept 4, 2024:  I got a response to the review from the Dev's saying there have been improvements.  (Likely a "canned" response to all negative reviews.)  I tried the game again, starting from the beginning.  Finished the first mission, then the game froze trying to load the next level.  It's still not ready yet.  (PS, my system is an I9-12-core fast system with RTX4090 and all E.2 drives.  It's super-fast and stable.)
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I would still recommend this game, especially if you liked the first one. But I now have some notes that really impacted the game. 1. You can't delete the existing stairs and roofs, which is kind of fine but it heavily impacts customization. For most of the houses it doesn't really matter, but you're stuck with the house you start in so not having that ability kind of sucks. Also the top of the chimneys are roofs so it also means you can't move the chimney. 2. I do kind of miss some of the mechanics from the first one. While I think the first one was too technical, I do feel this one lacks just a little.3. I imagine some things will come with DLC but I do wish you could alter the terrain/grass pattern. If you delete something, there is like a big dirt patch where it was so it looks pretty bad. But this is not a huge deal.4. There isn't any negotiating so what your offered for a house is basically all you get. And adding bedrooms and bathrooms doesn't seem to have an impact (but I could be wrong).Some more positive: There are a lot of color options, the patterns are really fun, and overall I think the customization is wonderful. It is a super fun game and I've spent a lot of hours in it. It truly is a beautiful game and it is much more fun than the first one to me.Highly recommend! It is more fun than the first one for sure. _childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this game if you are a fan of the first House Flipper game. However there are some bugs that are to be expected with a new game launch. _childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: Houses are much smaller than the first game and it took me a while to get used to feeling so cramped. It definitely made me claustrophobic at first, maybe it's just me but it wasn't pleasant.The quest screen is too confusing. I have to walk around the house several times trying to figure out if I haven't left any rooms unfinished and the star system seems too counter-intuitive... Having percentages was more satisfying and the hud of the first game made everything much clearer.I really miss the mini map.I expected a hud more similar to the first game and in general more content than what there is. Likewise, I recommend this game for people who like to make constructions like in Minecraft and play with moods. I guess I'm not the target audience.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: Loved number one, but the more I played, the more restricted I felt with my design choices. This is so much like the original, but SO MUCH BETTER. Really fun story line, fantastic and well-planned features. Highly recommend. Such a therapeutic game - can't wait to see what the devs have in store for us.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I can't begin to explain how excited I was for this game. I adored house flipper and all of the DLC. The game came out a day before my birthday so of course, early birthday present!! I planned to spend all day playing. But honestly I am shocked. All that waiting... For this?? Okay. So after sinking over 500 hours into HF1, I was expecting to be able to do the same. Not the case. The story is short. Like wayyyyyy short. Not many jobs to do after you've finished the story either. The houses you can buy, frankly I don't care for. And as for the characters, I feel nothing for them. I can't even remember their names. Very forgettable. I'll admit, I love some of the new aspects, the new flipper tool is amazing!! Change design, copy, duplicate, love it!! I also love the new trash collecting system and cleaning and painting system. However. The surfaces. They're all over the place!! No more are wall and floor categories. When you have OCD like me, it doesn't make it fun. The paint names are gone!! And decor is EXTREMELY limited. If you don't like a nautical/ocean kind of theme... Well. Enjoy the even more limited decor. There is hardly any paintings, pictures, rugs etc. The amount of decor available is sad. Compared to HF1 it is a downright joke. No carpets either. And I hate assemble mode!! What is up with that? A time limit to get 3 stars?? So what about us that have panic attacks under time limit situations? Sounds pathetic I know, but unfortunately it is a thing and yes, I hate it. What happened to being able to install your own things in a house?? Radiators, bathtubs, showers, sockets, fusebox fixing, lightbulb changing, sinks etc. Gone. All gone. No grass mowing, no planting anymore. No curtains. No fire in the fireplaces or candles!! (I am aware that is a planned update.) But I don't know... The entire thing just feels so rushed and lazy. It's like you've given us a few great new tools but at the expense of losing House flipper. That charm that made the game just so relaxing and perfect. Gone. I have gone back to HF1 and I think that's where I'll stay. Sad times. :(
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: So I was super excited for this- having more than 1000 hours on HouseFlipper 1. But, having played it now to the point where I can buy the first house- I'm mostly disappointed.  I was hoping the graphics would be a little better than they are and there is no zoom/UI option for visually impaired people like myself. I do appreciate the FOV option but again- no zoom in. Also- the controls feel very clunky- especially the painting. Note- I LOVE the fact that now we can paint/tile etc a single square so that we have the option to design walls/flooring better. That's great! But it is super clunky and even with the wasd option- still clunky.The store is really really scarce. Like on the initial parent house you are given - I wanted to paint the posts by the front door- but was unable to- so I sold them- but the bottom sections couldn't be sold. Then I tried to buy a new post and discovered- that's not even an option. It's also hard to see what the items you are buying will look like with the different colors, etc.  I liked the HF1 version of being able to choose the different styles/colors and seeing right then and there what they would look like.  That store UI was awesome- the HF2 store- way lacking and very limited.I love that fridges, etc open up and you can put stuff in them and also move something with things on it- that's a nice feature. I really miss the mini-map that helps you to find the dirt you've somehow missed.This feels- well- not quite done yet to be honest.  I'm really hoping they fix things so it has at least the same functionality as HF1 and a much better store options including previewing the styles/colors and more options.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals look great and the new grid system is very handy. _childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: House Flipper 2 is a major improvement on an already fun game concept. The new mechanics are interesting, and the old mechanics have been made so much better. If you loved the first game and want more, this is perfect and worth the money!
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually not the person to give reviews this early, but I'm just extremely happy that HF2 came out as a full game. I've had one tiny bug where I moved a potted plant and somehow the plant part detached from the pot, meaning I had to place it inside again, but that's far from being gamebreaking or a nuisance even (if it doesn't occur on the regular which so far it doesn't seem to do). Otherwise it runs nice and smoothly and feels much more dynamic, interactive and.. lively somehow than HF1.New features I noticed and (mostly) appreciated so far:1) Placing items got improved by multiple things:- we have a grid now to place items on- the ability to put things in drawers- the ability to put items into cupboards/shelves/etc. above your head (no more awkward climbing around nearby furniture, yay)- when moving pieces of furniture with items inside/on top, they get moved along (I appreciate this A LOT)2) Cleaning feels a lot more satisfying3) Some places have unpackable boxes with the client's household items, decorations, etc. which you can pick up from there and place, feels better and more immersive than having to buy everything from the store 4) Trash gets collected into bags which you have to throw away, adding to immersion (might feel like an extra chore to some players though, the trash bags do have an impressive capacity though and trash cans aren't usually too far away)5) I have legs :O6) You get to interact with some clients more via phone calls which even offer different dialogue options. I'm not sure if there'll be some kind of bigger story but I'm curious to find out. Either way it adds to the game feeling more lively and personal. Job offers via e-mail also contain photos now, giving you an idea of just how much work there's gonna be.7) You don't start the game in a random replaceable garden hut but a house that - grant you - does look like it needs some love but feels like a personal space.8) Flipper Sense - Highlights every quest-relevant item. No more "help, what tiny piece of dirt am I missing?"So far I feel like a lot of attention to detail went into the game. Discovering things like console games named Steampunk 1677 just make me happy and I'm excited to find out what else HF2 has to offer. Thanks for not disappointing me. :)

_childDocuments_.review: is a game I have been waiting for since the announcement. I played the demo, I gave my feedback and I have played the first one extensively. Here are my thoughts after completing the story campaign. Creative mode reviews will be added later when I get a chance to deep dive into it.I am not going to delve into the specifics of the new mechanics too much in House Flipper 2. It is a huge improvement in many areas over the original House Flipper. The flipper tool now allows you to duplicate & match any color or finish on the fly (no more saving those paint cans or tiles so you can remember what you used in a past design), or copy finishes already in the design if you like it (no more searching through the store endlessly).The store's layout is so much nicer,  you can browse by filters and there are so many more colors and finishes. Finally some good looking wood and brick finishes!Once you get the perks unlocked, painting is fluid, fun and much more creative. Demolishing and building after opening the perks up is also much more efficient and quick. I love being able to adjust the height of the walls, finally half walls! I hope in the future we can build circular walls and diagonal walls but as of now they are not in the game. The campaign itself is a bit short (I finished story mode in about 12 hours and that repeated some jobs). However I have yet to delve into the creative mode or buy and flip houses in the game to sell so lots more stuff to still do. This review is more of an overview of the new skills and the story.I have over 500 hours (measly compared to some friends) in the original House Flipper. I really like what they did with House Flipper 2 in so many ways but I do have one main gripe.The lack of community workshop support is missing for this game and is not planned, at this time, to be implemented. The devs have stated they moved over to mod.io (never used it so I have no opinions on that site). However I have used the community workshop  for the original game. It really gave longevity and spice to the original game. You could design so many new things from what is in the workshop beyond houses. In this one, so far, not so much. So the decision to leave the community workshop behind (especially when waiting for future content) to me is a misstep.I know why they did it. You can now share designs (maps) with other players. They can download your designs to decorate or alter. Or you can create jobs (like you would find in the story mode) for others to play through like cleaning up and doing quest objectives. A cool idea for sure but I am not sure it will have the same effect the workshop had (and Steam does not support the sharing of full designs like mod.io). Time will tell but truthfully I love what the mods have created for the original game. Their efforts gave many, like me, the ability to make some very awesome designs that the base game could not. So some great new features and some gripes too. I really enjoyed the story campaign and unlocking the new perks. It was short so I hope we see lots of future dlc for this game, like the original had and not too much of a wait in between. I will say the price point of this game is much steeper than I would have liked. I own the original House Flipper and all the dlc’s so my price, for me, was okay. But the full price I find is steep. I recommend the game but hopefully with my review you can decide if this is for you now or to wait for a sale. Future edits to my review will be updated on the creative (sandbox mode). 🛠️

_childDocuments_.review: THIS is how you do a sequel! I loved the first House Flipper game and was interested by what approach they would take with a sequel. They actually listened to what their players had to say! You can tell this isn't a group of people out of touch with their product. One of my favorite additions is the new ability to change the materials of objects! No more realizing i bought the wrong thing and having to sell and repurchase a kitchen counter all over again! This truly is the same game, but better! I loved that they heard that we were tired of having to assemble toilets and showers over and over again in the first game. I loved how immersive it was at first, but it just became tedious and distracting from the game itself in the end. But NOW you have the assembly tab in the sequel! You can still do the fun assembly went you want, but not have it distract from your designing! And they added a smart realistic bonus to how fast your record is with assembly! Giving the tab a good purpose but also not necessarily needed for those who don't like it. It's genius! I could go on and on! I cant wait to see where this game goes from here! The company even sent out a timely update with fixes and changes based on what players said not long after release! I'm so happy to have such a healthy outlet for my creativity during times i'm unable to afford even a dollar store run for a craft.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: 7.5 hours played in a single day, so yes, this is a good game that I do recommend to most players, especially veterans of House Flipper 1. Overall I'm very excited to continue digging into it, and can't wait to find all the silly easter eggs.There are a few rough edges, but I think it's important to keep in mind that this is a fairly small scale studio. So here's a few points:Pros:- the houses feel more realistic, with a more true-to-life scale for rooms, with a lot more clutter available and more diverse stains, damage, styles etc.- you can customize a lot more of the building, to an extent that I have not fully explored yet. I get the distinct feeling that I could make some amazing things if I set my mind to it, but I have yet to master the skills I'll need- for everyone that played The Sims 3 and complained when they abandoned the swatch mechanic, it's here. Copy styles, favourite them, mix and match textures and gloss levels and colours to your heart's content- because of the flexibility of the customization systems, this game feels like it would have more replayability than the previous one, which is always lovely- there's a lot of whimsy and affection put behind all the little stories, phone calls, environmental storytelling etc. It feels more like you're a person, rather than a disembodied pair of arms.- I no longer need to mount every damn shower cabin! THANK YOU- no more cockroaches - again, THANK YOU - the sound from HF1 will forever haunt meCons:- I miss jumping- the camera can fight you sometimes, which isn't usually an issue but it absolutely is in Assembly mode, which is thankfully a minigame off to the side- currently missing some polish - the Assembly system is broken in several places (I cannot complete the Clock assembly, it always bugs out for me). The perk they give for 3 stars is quite nice though. I also got the same phonecall multiple times until I began a new job, all because I was doing Assemblies in the meantime.- you can reach impossible distances with your paint roller or tile placement - while it's nice to not have to move all the time, I think the devs overcompensated. I can paint a wall from so far away that it gets tiring. Moving around while painting would also ensure our hands don't cramp holding down the paint button, and it breaks down the monotony.- as another review mentioned, the lack of accessibility controls can be painful during long gameplay sessions, even for able-bodied gamers. I can get wrist pain sometimes, so I pay attention to these details, and right now  I feel my fingers and right wrist hurting (no, I did not play 7.5 hrs in one sitting) because I have to keep controller buttons pressed down for extended periods of time.Misc:- while playing on a controller, I keep finding myself pushing the wrong buttons when navigating my tablet. I can't quite put my finger on why that is, but I feel like after 7.5 hours I shouldn't be fumbling around. Maybe that's just me. This is certainly not bound to be an issue with keyboard+mouse gameplay though.- you can tell that the voice acting is done on a bit of a budget, but these people aren't phoning it in. They are doing their best to embody the little characters they have and this attention to detail, even from perhaps less experienced VAs, is appreciated. They miss the mark sometimes, but gosh darn they try 💜Overall, I love what I've seen so far. I know these devs work hard and if the development process for House Flipper 1 is anything to go by, this release is just the beginning for HF2 in terms of quality of life and content updates.

_childDocuments_.review: I am writing to share my formal assessment of the recently released game.In my view, the game was launched prematurely, evident in the presence of several bugs. However, my primary reason for not recommending the game stems from its lack of substantial gameplay, notably falling short in comparison to its predecessor, House Flipper 1. The limited variety of furniture options and the absence of detailed progressions, such as setting up a toilet as in House Flipper 1, are significant drawbacks.Given these concerns, I believe it is essential to express dissatisfaction and, if possible, request a refund for my purchase. Constructive feedback is crucial for the improvement of any product, and I hope this input contributes to enhancing the overall gaming experience.
