_childDocuments_.review: House Flipper 2 is a game that tries to build and improve on its predecessor, without understanding what players really wanted to see in a sequel. I wish there was a neutral review option for a game, because honestly that is how I feel about this game. I loved the first House Flipper and ordered this game right away. However, there are many issues in this game that hold it back from being a good successor to the original.One of the things I hated the most in a job in the original House Flipper was the way wallpaper worked. From a realism perspective it wasn't bad, just a bit too tedious since the strips of wallpaper were so small and the animation for putting it on was so long. This was a change I was glad to see in House Flipper 2 had changed, so it now works more like laying down tiles, even though it does remove the realism aspect. I do think this could have just been changed to just holding more wallpaper at once and the strips of wallpaper being bigger in order to keep more of the realism approach. House Flipper 2 in general just lacks the realism that was present in the original game. I don't mind this change to more of a cartoonish style, though if you are looking for more of the realistic appeal the first game had you will be disappointed here. As an addition I really did enjoy, this game has more of a story aspect to it. I loved the implementation of receiving extra tasks and requests from your employer while on the job.With all of that said, there are a few glaring issues with this game that make it hard to recommend.     - Motion sickness. I have never had an issue with it in other games, but this was a huge issue when I started this game. It was a bit better after toggling with settings (turning off motion blur and changing FOV to 75), but definitely not something I could play for extended periods of time.    - The removal of before and after images at the end of a job. This is more of a satisfaction thing. It feels rewarding to see all the changes and improvements you did when you finish    - The lack of outdoors panels. There are so few options for customizing the exterior of a house. Even the amount of interior options felt a bit lacking, but outside there were about 3 options to use    - Searching for furniture. This is an absolute pain in this game opposed to the previous entry. I really do get where the devs where coming from, but most often I ended up trying to search for items because I can't find what I am looking for in the listed categories     - Camera movement in assembly mode. This has to be by far the most frustrating implementation of camera movement I have ever seen. ctrl + left click and drag the mouse, then you let go when you finally get the camera centered where you want it and it moves over slightly again anyways to cut out the area you were just focusing on. What was wrong with using wasd to move the camera like in the first game?     - Sandbox mode isn't implemented into the main game. You can build many different houses in sandbox mode to share screenshots with friends, which is definitely cool. But this is very much just an additional feature where you get the bare minimum. It feels very similar to building in the original House Flipper as a part of the farm DLC. There is nothing extra about it. No job will ask you to build something for them in this game. Create the house, screenshot it, and then forget about it entirely. I just help but wish there was a bit more to this gamemode than there is.I really did like House Flipper 2, I just can't help but feel a bit disappointed with it and I'd have a hard time honestly recommending this game to anyone over the first game. It is possible some of these things will change with the addition of future DLC content and updates to the game, and if that happens I will gladly change my review, but as of right now I would have to recommend waiting on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: One step forward, five steps backwards. Don't bother with this game. Base House Flipper one has more features, runs better and is cheaper. The devs proved that they are more a asset store than game devs with the first game and this game proves it even more. Frame rate is all over the place often dipping into the teens and the controls are clunky. They seem to be pushing their assembly feature pretty hard which basically changes the game into a furniture/Ikea making simulator. This could be ok but they added a arbitrary timer to rate you and the controls for making the furniture are unresponsive/inaccurate and overall frustrating. Their roadmap is lackluster and seems to indicate they are going to resell the features from House Flipper one as dlc. Don't support this kind of dev. If you really want to play this just play House Flipper one you're not missing out on anything.

_childDocuments_.review: honestly kind of disappointing, I was a big fan of the first game and the DLC. I will give it something, the painting/cleaning animations are really satisfying and the build workshops were really fun. And although it is very appealing in that sense I still have some major complaints.I still feel like it is heavily lacking content. Even in sandbox mode.- There are no before/after transitions like in the first game,I originally thought that there were transitions like that because of the trailer, and I know they said that it was something they were working on, so I hope that gets added soon-There is not a lot of diversity with furniture or even furnishings, which is what I also thought was lacking in the first game, lots of similar games have lots of diversity in architecture and styles, and this game seems to only know 2 of them, Modern and 'rustic' if you even want to call it that -Fast Paced. I finished the main story in less than 46 hours, I had a similar complaint with the original game, I want more diverse jobs-There is almost no creative freedom when doing flip jobs (at least in my opinion). I tried to use the base wall panels to match the other furnished half of the bedroom and it got marked incomplete because I didn't use the exact tile it was asking for) maybe that was the whole point of it but I HATE that it looks off color and mismatched.- NO ASSEMBLY FEATURES. Now I understand, yes they have 'workshop/assembly' Mode but the whole reason I liked the first game so much is because you had to assemble appliances. I think that DEFINITELY should have stayed in this game.-You cannot fill holes or mess with the lawn, I feel like the only reason this isn't a base game feature is because they're going to make it a DLCI did overall enjoy playing it, however based on the things I listed I don't think I can recommend it to others. All in all, I don't think it was worth the price, and if you DO wish to buy it, wait until it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, usually don't write reviews so I'll keep this short and sweet. As for both House Flipper 1 and 2, I've found that they are both great games to just relax and design things the way I want lol. With the new game, I have found that I like the changes made to your abilities (such as the wall painting or picking up trash) and it feels like a much more immersive first person experience. I have had some difficulty with small mechanics, but I really haven't had any issues or bugs which influenced my game-play. The only thing that I would really complain about is the short story-line, as I had finished it within the first 16-18 hours, and that is with taking my time and doing EVERYTHING. I think there are like 25 houses to do which isn't bad, but I do wish that it was longer or more stuff to do in the story houses. I do really like a lot of the mechanical, visual, and just overall design changes. Plus I think that this game runs SO MUCH BETTER than House Flipper 1 with DLC. My CPU (i5) got kinda messed up by the first game, but I have had no issues so far with the second one.Overall, I personally would give this game a 9/10. I feel as though this game should be 30 dollars instead of 40, but if you think that you will go more in depth with your own house flipping and renovations, then I think it's worth the money, especially if you are in need of a good singleplayer game :)

_childDocuments_.review: First off I want to say that my negative rating for this game is because I am directly comparing it to House Flipper 1, as I am an avid House Flipper 1 enjoyer with hundreds of hours sunk into the first game. Therefore, I compared all of the systems with the first game, and have concluded while I don't necessarily mind playing the 2nd game, it just isn't as good as the first game, nor do I feel that it is worth even the sale price I got it for (it should go for less imo). I'm going to list some pros and cons about this game from my opinion:OCTOBER UPDATE:- Having more furniture and decor options is starting to really improve this game! Would still like to see more options continuing to be added however.- Walls panels and molding are a HUGE quality of life upgrade!- We seem to have gotten more decoration options with this update, really a great thing but would still love to see more yet.- Getting info on buyers is a step in the right direction for value information!- Additionally, the sold panel seems to now show the highest price you made off each property- not sure if this was actually in the update or not, but it is good information.- Really a lot of good things added in this, in another few updates if they maintain the same update quality, I will change my overall review to positive.PROS- If you haven't played any House Flipper game before, this game may actually be great for you! Coming in without comparisons will give this game its best chance to leave a positive impression on you.- Seeing and flipping new houses.- Updated graphics: everything really is lighter and brighter than HF1, and has more detail. - The ability to demo and create half-walls to use in spaces such as kitchen bars etc.- The addition of architectural elements to add to rooms such as arched doorways, porch pieces, etc.- Currency being in one basic unit vs dollar/pound to make tracking financial achievements easier.- The ability to create more intricate wall designs with the surface tool.- The ability to create specialized flowerpot arrangements.CONS- Lack of mini map for tracking dirt: personally, I strongly dislike the "flipper tool" with the highlighted dirt-while it shows stains great, it is way too light when it comes to showing trash as well as weeds. - Lack of vertical setting for wallpapers and paneling unlike the first game: it's way too easy to mess up an intricate wall border, as well as it takes extra time to get any surface tool work done even with the expanded tool. I'd like to see more, larger options for the surface tool, in addition to a surface borders similar to the paint borders.- Lack of regular stepladder: there are only either the tiny 2-step or the huge scaffolding and no inbetween. I'd like to see a regular ladder option.- Inability to walk on the sidewalks in front of properties in order to landscape front flower beds bordering it: there's an invisible wall blocking you from ever getting directly in front of the property, and some landscaping is too close to it. Very frustrating.- Past the immediate nearby homes, the background of each location is actually the same within areas (i.e. Old Pinnacove Suburbs, the Coast).- Lack of reset button for changing colors/designs on any item in the store: even logging out doesn't auto-reset any changes you made- good luck figuring out what items looked like originally if that is something you wanted to go back to! I'd like to see a reset option, as well as a save color preset option.- Lack of recent items bought screen in the store unlike the first game: sometimes I wanna know what I just bought 5 min ago so I can buy it again!- Lack of pet decor- I really enjoyed in the first game getting to put cat towers/dog toys etc. especially when it comes to the house I am using as my office.- Lack of summary when selling homes showing what buyers liked about it/what made them offer that price; I liked the green/red arrows when making changes that show what affected the house value in HF1. I'd like more concrete information on what raises the values here to get maximum profits.- Inefficient cleaning tool: no, I don't enjoy the extra step of spraying the dirt before cleaning it, especially as I still have to spend more than a minute on some stains even with that. Please just give us the swiffer back from 1, OR the option to change between the rag and a mop.- "Trash" not picking up correctly outside story mode: the trash bag can also collect items that aren't actually trash, as well as it won't pick up scrap construction materials such as pallet pieces, broken wood planks, etc unlike the first game.- Lots of glitches- just the other day I had a door glitch into a bathroom sink and refuse to get unstuck."MEH":- Having to micromanage colors/designs on everything: this is honestly exhausting. I understand it gives more creative freedom, but I prefer the first game where everything is separate and easily accessible.- Lack of lawnmower: I don't think that the grass in yards in 2 is that low- personally, I would never allow my yard to be that high in real life, so I don't want it that tall in game either.- Limited wall decor options: there's also a HUGE lack of wall decor- pictures, photos, paintings, etc. They just don't seem to exist in 2, which is a disappointment as it means less personalization options.- Building mode requiring you to do each separate wall as well as ceilings and floors: in 1, you can just make a regular box room and then knock out a wall to connect it. Here, you have to do a lot of extra work when creating additions, and honestly it feels like a pain.- Assembly being moved to a mini-game only vs being a normal part of installing appliances.- The wiring tool is honestly too micromanaging and excessive- just let switches placed in a room turn those lights on please.- Once you buy and sell a house, it doesn't seem to show back up in buyable houses, unlike HF1 where once you complete story mode you can buy and sell houses as often as you like even the same ones over and over again. *Update: the houses still don't show as buyable even after selling all except the office, but you can re-buy from within the sold tab....very confusing though, they should show on the buy tab just like in 1 personally.Basically, I wish they would've kept all the same systems from 1 along with DLC systems and then expanded on making them better in the new graphics, vs just initiating new systems that aren't as good or efficient. I really feel that instead of releasing a whole new "game," the devs should have just released more paid DLC for HF1.

_childDocuments_.review: Having completed the game, I'll now leave my thoughts. I was a keen player of House Flipper 1 and I bought all the DLC that was released. I was really looking forward to House Flipper 2 and in terms of game play I enjoyed it. What I didn't like however (and I'm sorry if I'm proved to be wrong) is that in buying House Flipper 2 it feels like you are buying a base game that will be fleshed out through many DLC packs which has left me feeling deflated about the game. So many things are obviously missing for example curtains and blinds are non-existent, furniture, paint and wallpaper options are incredibly limited. Sorting the garden is restricted to selling weeds (so I expect a Garden DLC to launch at some point - Even though the basics for this exist in Sandbox mode). No before and after pictures. You basically get a prettier version of House Flipper 1 but with less content. Don't get me wrong I want to support the developer but if this goes the way I think it will we will just end up buying the same DLC as before along with various DLC for addition paints, wallpaper etc and I am not a fan of this practice. As such at this point in time i probably would not recommend. Instead buy House Flipper 1 for the time being.

_childDocuments_.review: I hesitated to buy it after reading some comments, but I eventually caved in and it proved to be an excellent decision.The game is good, funnier and prettier than the first one. I really enjoy the missions and the gameplay has improved in many ways. Congratulations for the improvement in color customization : now for each object, you can chose the material and the colors of it, which allows for so much more personalization than the first one!Several improved points I noted : - windows cleaning, aka what I considered the most annoying part of the first game, has become a very fun part of the game!- two differents placements methods (grid and precise) which allows for placing the objects as you wish- new painting gameplay (there are two according to the trailer)- better color customization for every object, including materials you can choose the colors of and a much larger catalogue of materials- there are no difference between floor and wall tiling anymore, and you can choose their colors + place them as you want, unlike the first where one band of wall = one pattern- variants for many assets; for examples, there are different types of faucets for showers and baths- a story and voice acting for many characters- so much more plants!- The houses in missions feel so much more natural- when a mission asks you to place kitchen furniture, the required objects perfectly fit the room, unlike many missions of the first game!- sandbox modeMuch more to say, but no doubt that this game dethrones its predecessor in many ways!Just several things that would make the game even better : - a color palette dropper would make interior design even easier, as well as the game having a list of "recently used colors/materials"- I don't see an option to import your own assets as in the first game. this would help a LOT for making the house of your dream- more varieties for windows and doors, they are heavily lacking in the current state of the game- curtains

_childDocuments_.review: From a positive standpoint, the game play is a very smooth and feels quite nice in comparison to the original House Flipper, especially the painting. The messes feel better scaled as well.However my biggest gripe is the story length. I was able to complete the entire story and all sub missions that came up in under 10 hours. The map only uses three areas and there's an entire half of the map that's not even touched - which makes me feel the game was rushed out. The voice acting, though present, is also .... well it seems very forced and not fluid. It certainly could have been done better and feels more like it was voiced by AI. The last gripe I have is lack of content when it comes to the number of houses. This plays back into the really short story too. I would have liked to see a larger variety of homes, and definitely larger ones.I do still recommend the game but don't expect an epic adventure, and it may be best to wait for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, to me, is very much not the rehash/downgrade people say it is. HF1 has been out coming up on six years, of course it has had plenty of time bake and become the great game it is today with so much content. This one on the other hand, is very young. The devs haven't had the same amount of time to add content and receive feedback like on the first game and it's unfair to review it as such. The graphics are a major upgrade even with the few errors they have. The colours pop so much more vibrant!  And the houses (although a smaller bunch), have noticeably more love and variety into them. I'm certain more great homes are to come. My only complaint with the houses themselves is that I don't find the same story behind the messes they start in like the first game did so greatly. There are a few details in the presentation here and there, but nothing comes close to the narrative a couple plots had in the first. I hope they add more of that to the sequel! Also me personally, I don't miss the assemblies for every radiator and washing machine I place down. I felt it took me out of my groove time to time, so I'm glad they are treated as side content now.Over all, I say the game is very worth the price now that they have added some of the lacking bits they forgot on launch--Such as ceiling fans and window blinds/curtains. If you already own HF1, it's worth the change of pace to perhaps breed some new creativity in you! If you don't, well, I suggest both games! They are both amazing titles with a lot of love. Personally I think I prefer this one.

_childDocuments_.review: So before I talk about my problems with HF2 let me start with a few things and changes I love.-I love the customization options and building decisions this game gives you which is something the first one was missing. I'm talking about being able to choose how big a wall is to create half walls or painting only part of one to make more intricate walls and item designs. Its not all just one strip of paint or tile or panel or the set color scheme for items and counters.-It also added copy and pasting of not just items but taking the color scheme of one item and pasting it on another making designing faster. -You can also now eye-drop materials to easily find them in the shop if you ran out and had left that page for a different Item. -And finally Sandbox mode. I can't explain fully how much I looked forward to this game just because they announced a sand-box mode. Most of my playtime is in sandbox mode but I do have some critics on how to make it better.For sandbox mode the only thing I wish it had is being able to move the house you make itself, like if you accidentally placed it too far back or need to center it you can just move the entire building like you can in The SIMs.Now the main reason I don't recommend this game is despite all the choice you have for color and designing, there is not a huge choice on the actual items you can buy. There is just not enough stuff for decorating to justify buying it at full price. Nor is it worth if they put all of the decorations, that should have been in the base game, behind paywalls when they do eventually add more. Like I was expecting a good chunk of the furniture and decorations from the first game just revamped a little to match the game and its customization.Also I wish you could buy some of the items that are only available in sandbox mode in story mode, because you can still sell some important items in story mode that you cant buy. (like ramps and the column in the starter house) But overall the main thing is the lack of items/decorations/furniture.The game has also crashed twice and lags heavily for me, despite being on a new gen computer, lowering the graphics and turning v-sync off, making the overall game-play experience not ideal. But I am going to mess with settings some more till I figure out whats causing these problems.I loved the first one and was so excited when this came out but until there is more stuff in the game for decorating I can't recommend it at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:Buy the game on sale. Don't pay full price.The Negatives:Reviews should have a "meh" option. It's not terrible but given this isn't an early access title and therefore a full release, it has some issues.The in-game tutorials don't contain all the information you really need. For that you have to follow their link to their Youtube videos. Those videos include demonstrations of activities you can't even do in game as yet, like moving an entire structure that you've created in sandbox mode. I spent about an hour wasting my time trying to do something that they apparently haven't implemented. A game should contain all the necessary information needed to play within itself, without having to visit outside websites, and it should be accurate, not cut features that the devs can't get working properly as yet. Tutorials aren't meant to be a wishlist of what you hope you can get working, but how actual game content works.The game also feels like it's missing some content, such as in-ground pools and ornamental ponds that were in HF1 but not HF2. This is especially odd given you can dig holes using the terrain manipulation tool. Either they couldn't get water, ponds and pools working (in which case terrain manipulation is a half baked feature) or it's being held over for a paid DLC.The Positives:The sandbox mode is mostly pretty good. Being able to build your own structures allows for a degree of freedom that HF1 didn't have.Terrain manipulation really lets you bring dimension to your landscaping which is great if you enjoy the gardening side of things.The ability to resurface, retexture and duplicate items on the fly is an excellent addition.Summary:It's ok but feels like it should be in early access. There are areas that lack polish and there are noticeably fewer exterior plants and other landscaping options

_childDocuments_.review: I have like a million hours in House Flipper 1 and even though this has just released a few days ago, I am going to offer my two cents on it and shed some light on some of the complaints I've been seeing on the reviews."This game is seriously lacking content in the base game as compared to House Flipper(1)'s base game."    While I agree, we must remember for House Flipper(1)'s initial release, the game did not have as much content as we remember. The game was updated with content throughout its reign. I still, however, do agree that House Flipper 2's content is seriously lacking in what I expected (like why are there no curtains in a interior decorating game??)."Constant crashes and FPS drops."   This was something I was deeply worried about before install. All in all, I think this really depends on your PC specs especially your amount of space on your PC. However, I play the game on max graphics with little to no issues, and I don't have a terrible PC but it's not beefy either. My game runs smoothly and has never crashed so I cannot really weigh in on this issue as I have not experienced it.Now, I'm going to talk about the positives (or at least in my opinion).   This game has a severe quality of life update that I desperately craved after the first game. I love the uses of the flipper tool with the ability to duplicate styles/items and being able to change color of items without having to return to the store and buy a different item when you want to change your mind on a style (which was one of my biggest gripes with the original House Flipper). I love the ability to change roofs and change the wood paneling that is on the front of the roofs (for the life of me I cannot remember what these are called aha). I love the art style of the game, it's more cartoon-y (but still realistic) than the last game and is comparable in art style close to the Sims 4. I like that this game has some lore with the town and the character you are playing, it gives your job some backstory. So, do I think you should buy this game now or wait?   To be honest, it's really what your expectations are for this game that answers that question. If you're looking for a content-full game, I would wait for some future updates or DLC.. I think that we shouldn't expect such a well endowed game upon the release- even with the previous House Flipper, Frozen District never lets us down and always proves to update and add content. Whether that content be DLC or just in updates, they always provide. I enjoy the game, but I can understand why it may become "boring" or over-played so soon because of the lack of content.   Buttttttttttt... If you just want a nice cozy game to scratch your exterior/interior design itch, I would definitely buy this game now while it is 10% off. All in all, it's a very good game so far and I am excited for the future updates and possible DLC. Just remember, the devs are people too. Do not bash them for your critiques of the game. They should be proud of the game they produced. We can ask for specific things to be changed/added to the game in the future without hating on the developers. Happy Flipping and Merry Christmas. <3

_childDocuments_.review: I've played it all day, especially so I could compare it compare it to the other game that I've played for thousands of hours, and as a result became a real-estate multimillionaire. Sigh, if only it were real-world money!There are things I like, and things I don't. Experience with the other game has given me the ability to make the comparison. First off, I'm not crazy about the painting. It's not intuitive and while I understand that modern technology has advanced well beyond my 1990s experience and learning, and using HTML and CSS for a few years online, I understand that things progress and eventually, as we age, it moves beyond our experience of decades ago. Still while I realise that the painting format will allow me to tile half walls, and to paint without having to cover a whole wall, it doesn't mean I have to enjoy using the method in this game. It will take a while for me to master the skill of creating a "box"for the paint. I'll push on, get it right eventually.What else don't I like? Hmm I think that the small houses are going to take some getting used to. I'm a romantic lover of history and opulence. My "wealth"in the other game allows me to design elegant, formal homes I could only dream of owning in the real world. Of course I'm aware this is only the beginning but that ugly wallpaper in the "office" house has to go, so I'll keep on battling through with the painting if only to remove the ugly wallpaper. (I'm not a fan of wallpaper at the best of times, so I'm biased, I accept that).Now, what I like.The more realistic way of getting rid of trash. I figured that out fairly quickly, but I'm not a sportswoman, so even on a computer screen, I'm not able to throw objects further than my feet. So my character won't need the gym after running around with full trash bags. That's very cute. I enjoy that.I struggled a bit with the empty boxes, didn't know what to do with them, until I closed one. Excellent idea, well done to the person who came up with that.I enjoy the way items "snap"into place. It's much nicer than in the other game that can become tedious when furnishing dressing rooms with walls of cupboards. This snapping together is a great idea, avoiding the frustration of trying to make things line up neatly. I like that. After trying and finally succeeding with the first paint job, I went back to the "office"to practice painting. I'll focus on that tomorrow, I'm determined to not fail at that.Otherwise, the vacuum cleaner as part of the tool set, I like that rather than having to input keystrokes to get it. Also a good idea. All in all, my compliments to the team who designed this game. I have ADD and I'm bed-bound with old age heart issues so I expect that I'll log thousands of hours with this game before I give up my PC and the joy of my interior designing skills learnt while being entertained. Thank you and well done!  I hope the game will be successful - you've all worked hard to get it to us before Christmas, so you deserve it being a great success.

_childDocuments_.review: I know, most of the things that I´m going to say have already been said - but still I feel like having to write this review.I really - REALLY loved HF1! I spent hours in cleaning and renovating houses to finally sell them and (best part of the game) see the before-after pictures. But this whole experience was really disappointing in HF2:- The whole store is very limited on items - starting with wall and floor designs which we already knew from various DLCs of the first part - but also the selection of furniture and (above all) decoration is so limited, it is almost impossible to create cozy, realistic homes. This was really the most satisfying part of HF1 - you had LOTS of opportunitied to make even the smallest houses unbelievable cozy with all the decorations, lights and accessories for every single room (especially kitchen, bath and living room). Also, gardening and outdoort stuff ios very limited too. On the other side, you can buy lots of construction site stuff - but I don´t really see the sense of that...- The mechanic of before & after pictures is unfortunately missing completely - so you get no reward for the hard work invested. I really hope, this will be added soon!- The workshop for HF1 always guaranteed never ending fun, as steadily new objects and styled were added and could easily be used within the game. So far, this mechanic is missing also - and will hopefully be introduced asap.- Within the TAB selection, you have the chance to do isntallation courses (e.g. for bath tub, shower, heater aso.) - still, when buying these stuff within a house, no installation is needed - which was always a fun part of HF1.Of course, some things have been improved compared to the first part, e.g.- building of walls- collecting trash in a trash bag - the flipper tool, for later adjustments of furniture- unpacking boxed in jobsBut all in all, I really expected more of House Flipper 2 - especially for the price called. I really, really hope, that cost-free updates will fix at least some of the issues that have been named various times in reviews to give some fun & satisfaction back to the HF-community :)
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game has given me so much joy! I'm a huge fan of the first game, and House Flipper 2 ticks all the right boxes! _childDocuments_.review: It is a good improvement over the previous game, but do not come into this expecting to get everything you had from House Flipper---especially if you purchased all of the DLCs. Sandbox mode is offers a lot options for those who want to get really creative, but design options are limited. As an example, you have maybe 6 options for doors (both interior and exterior). May not be a huge issue, but as stated earlier, if you are coming from the original and expecting the same amount, you will not find it. Hopefully we will start to see some over the previous DLCs get added to the game (and not have to pay to mow our yard again, hint... hint) and once mods start flowing in we will get additional design features. Overall, it's a good game if you just want to let your mind go blank and throw some paint on wall.

_childDocuments_.review: Was looking forward to this game once I found out it was releasing. However, after day 2 of playing, I lost all of my progress. Tried following other people advice about the save file, but it's day 7 now and still having issues with the save data. I got over 30 hours through three attempts with nothing to show. I'm still going to visit the forums until there's a fix for the save files (which seems to be a big complaint about this game).This game is also missing things from the base game that felt like a missed move. They added in living aids, which is a good sign, but I feel like it's missing decorations that gave the living room and bedroom more life. I feel like the bathroom  has decent about of add-ons, but you have three types and you can't even place the toothbrush in the toothbrush cup. Lots of kitchen items such as pans to food items, that enrich your experience, I just have a lack of interest in dealing with the kitchen as it's normally the smallest room in my house. I'm not much of a fan of how things are organized through the menus. There's decorations and there's accessories. Accessories have like two or three tabs of just kitchen items, a tab for bathroom, a small tab for office supplies, and the others tab for three cloithing and shoe options. Feels like I'm lacking bedroom and living room items. It's not even a progress bar of oh you leveled up here's more items or collections. I will give it props for change style/copy style, as it takes me so long to judge if this is the same wood type that I used on the bench. Feels like I can customized anything inside of the house. One thing is I find these wedges pieces it Over the Garage, but I cannot figure out the correct name of the item, so I can only duplicate it on that house build. Wished I knew the item names. Otherwise it's me realizing an hour later, oh the bathroom shelf is located here in the menus. Maybe I would've liked it better if it was based off room types. I'm not quite sure. I just don't like having to go through all of the menus to furnished one bathroom as the shelf I want is from this area, the sink I want is from this area, but there's no toilet to match it exactly as it's not from the bathroom fixture tab but cabinet tab instead. 4So until the Devs figure out the fix or someone can find the cure all solution to the save file issue, I'm not going to spend any more time worrying about this game. I rather go back to HF1 until this gets sorted out in a few months.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice step from the first game, not a big one though. I love the feature that you can "scan" for the missed dirt spots, trash e.g. now. No more give up, because you can't find the invisible dirt.My only con is the object placement. You can choose to place by grid or free, but both options make it difficult to place something on spot. If you want e.g. to install a window, you have to look on the floor to fit it in. It is hard to estimate sizes of doors and windows, so they rarely fit properly. I don't have the wall tool yet, which I guess will solve this. The customization of everything is amazing. You can put any pattern and color on almost everything. How about a black plastic breadbox with wood foundation and pink leopard pattern? Just do it! You can assign lamps to specific light switches now, so you decide which switch triggers what. There is lots of stuff...The only thing that is really bad in this game, is my creativity.

_childDocuments_.review: After 80+ hours and 100% achievements I felt the need to edit my review to focus more on mechanics, that are unlikely to change, instead of considering story content and items that are guaranteed to come in time as they did for HF1.What I likeMost mechanics are a massive improvement over HF1, tiling/paneling is fantastic, painting too once you learn to use WASD movement, duplicate items, copying styles and/or changing it in place are a godsend, also removing assembly from bathroom fixtures makes it soo much better to position them exactly as you want them.Items are not duplicated anymore to allow for different materials like in HF1, but each item has its own style customization option that lets you choose from a plethora of different materials and colors, I love this because it makes the game much less "bloated".Sandbox mode is ABSOLUTELY AMAZING, you can go crazy building whatever comes to your mind, everything is instant and you can fly, you can also disable collision between items to "invent" new items, it has become my favorite (and only) way of playing the game.What I don't likeFlipping houses is not as relaxing and enjoyable as it is in HF1, while furnishing in general has better mechanics, cleaning up is annoying as hell (while it's oddly satisfying in HF1) mostly because you have to keep spamming the new flipper sense (that replaced the minimap) and that's obnoxious.HF2 also lacks the same sense of progression HF1 has. In HF1 you start in a small shack in very bad conditions, you have to progressively work your way up until you can flip bigger and bigger houses and it's done so well that it ends up being pretty satisfying.In HF2 you start in big houses already and while there is some variety in size and locations, there's no tangible sense of progress. On top of that, it feels unrewarding because the profit doesn't feel adequate to the amount of time and effort you need to put into renovating those houses, unlike HF1 (tho this point can be very easily fixed if devs are willing to make profit more predictable, as it is in HF1).BugsThere are a few glitches but I honestly haven't encountered anything major, not so far at least, and the game runs smoothly for me, tho I do play on a high-end gaming desktop, it probably matters.TL;DR get HF1 (+ DLCs) if you like progression and flipping houses, get HF2 if you prefer going creative building your own stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on HF2.  I put many, many hours into HF1, so I was incredibly excited for HF2.  I thought the price point was a bit high for a sequel, but the reviews looked decent enough.Unfortunately....HF2 is lacking, and lacking severely.  While they DID introduce a lot of improvements from HF1 - they also took some of the fun out of the elements out.Some of the things I wished the developers did better:- Longer, much longer, story line.  There's a million scenarios you could've drummed up.  I don't always want to be creative, I want structured tasks that I can complete with my brain turned off.- Assembly, while fun in mini-game mode, was short-lived and pointless in HF2.  I really do like the way they added assembly as a mini-game...but it's incredibly elementary and lacking grit.- I liked the theme of the mini-three housing areas...but branch out a little.  Do a strip mall, a classroom, maybe a pole barn...there's so many things you could've added. Most importantly, the story mode, while fun, is incredibly short.  You can "complete" this game in about 6-8 hours...and that's going slow.  This was the most frustrating part for me, and certainly felt like I did not get my money's worth.  It feels like the developers rushed this sequel, spit out a version that was baseline and operational - without really capitalizing on the value to the consumer.This will be the last HF I purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick update: I just opened the game and all my progress of this afternoon is lost. Omg I'm so pissed, at least 2 hours of game are lost. Nice game, right? Another thing to add to the negative list. I played HF 1 for almost 136 hours, and it was an amazing game, but for me, it has its problems; it's not perfect.The problem with HF 2 is that it lacks the positive aspects of the first game. It's attempting to be a good game, but it falls short.What I don't like:- The graphics are not entirely good. For example, when you see water near the coast, it looks awful, even when playing it with the highest graphics configuration.- The assembly mini-games are VERY flawed, not because they are boring or anything like that, but due to the horrible camera controls. You have to accomplish a lot of tasks in a certain time, and it's impossible because of the buggy and bad camera controls. If developers fix this issue, the mini-games could be a nice addition to the game.- The worst part for me is that you can't see the "before-after" work, as you can in HF 1. This, for me, is a significant drawback.- The store is not good; it's difficult to find things, and the order is weird.- Painting is HORRIBLE, even when you have the painting perk leveled.- If you have a small item like a cup or glass in your hands, you can't run as if you have a bed or something bigger. It is not realistic at all in a game that is trying to be realistic in many other aspects.- In the demolition tool, if you break the top, sides, and bottom, the middle pieces float.- If you choose to change or edit a piece of furniture, and you regret what you did without saving, you can't choose the original wood or material; you have to exit the furniture and do it all over again.What I like:- You can move objects with items on them.- Copy style and duplicate items are amazing.- You can edit every item in the game.- Grid for aligning objects.- It's fantastic that you can choose a style for every item with a lot of detail.- Realism in some things like doors, items, shadows, etc.I haven't explored the 'buy and sell' feature in the game yet, but in HF1, I found it lacking. I'm optimistic that developers will enhance this aspect. Update: I played it and it worst than in HF1. :(I truly hope the developers persist in refining this version of the game without resorting to DLCs or similar additions. It has the potential to be a good and enjoyable game, but it needs a considerable amount of attention and improvement.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really really want to love this game. I really do. And I hope I get to change my review later. I want to have hope that the devs are listening to the complaints....But honestly for now, please just go play House Flipper 1. Yes, mechanically this is a better game (in a *technical* sense). You can tell they've updated how their engine handles stuff and I like the way the tools are organized better in HF2. I feel like this is a good skeleton for a good game. HOWEVER -- there's so much *less* in HF2. Seriously. It doesn't show you what kind of room the game considers you've decorated (is this counting as a bedroom? A kitchen? a living room? will that even matter in the auction??). It doesn't let you tailor the house to a seller type so you're totally blind when you go to sell (and for me quite frequently disappointed with the amount at auction). You get so much more money by replaying the jobs that it's almost not worth it to actually flip the houses you have access to. And legit - HF1's ability to even just mow your grass is impossible to play without. I wouldn't think they would have even considered releasing without being able to tidy up your yard, but here we are. Devs, please prove me wrong and bring this game up to HF1 standards. Meanwhile -- gamers just play HF1. It's amazing, you will love it to pieces. I've got hundreds of hours over there and planning on many more.

I'd rather have the old way back. getting the border to work right was sometimes painful and then once it was upgraded it would paint over areas I didn't want so I had to go back to making the borders again. It just wasn't a great time with that aspect.  The game was also missing simple things like curtains, and a variety of doors, the electrical system was a bit strange, and choices just seemed limited. _childDocuments_.review: I would genuinely love to give this game a positive review. But in its current state, I can't. It doesn't make sense to not have any prompts before deleting anything so if you're doing something like cleaning up your property photos and then delete your entire project. that's all she wrote.  Manually saving does nothing for...reasons. This entire project is unfinished and would have done better as an add-on to the first game, which is fantastic. Losing all my work five days before I have to turn it in for a project is enough for me to request a refund.Edit:I was contacted swiftly by the Support Team who were SUPER kind. I had already discovered a solution and communicated as such with the team in the hopes that  should anyone else encounter this issue, they'll be able to remedy it quickly. That being said, I do still stand by the sentiment that the game feels particularly unfinished. And while I'm a touch annoyed given the price tag, I have never had a bad encounter with this dev team and have high hopes that the updates will fix the issues that we're currently running into.  While I wish the game had been finished from the start or simply left in Early Access, I also understand that sometimes this happens. Die-hard House Flipper fans will enjoy themselves but notice the vast difference between the first entry and House Flipper 2. So I can recommend this game with an asterisk - expect many bugs but also expect a fantastic team who will work very hard to ensure the game runs smoothly.

_childDocuments_.review: Current Review: I was asked by devs to re-review the game after updates. I understand this is probably a boiler plate thing that's done semi-automatically, so no hate to whoever has the job of doing this. Instead, I'd like to direct my annoyance to the team making the game. First off, I still have had performance issues with the game despite updates. I have indeed played the game recently, though I started to give up when I ran into several "ruin the game" situations. First, the issue of the game randomly crashing wasn't fixed when I played last. I just instinctively save now. No, instead, my issue is the still-to-my-knowledge unfixed bug that will, without rhyme or reason, remove all of the textures of whatever house you have as your home office. I dedicated three or four days of play sessions to completely redoing the OG starter home cause I loved it so much. I did custom furniture, designed a floor plan, and made a home that I really liked. Then, one day when I launched to play, every single wallpaper, floor tile, and ceiling tile had reverted to the default brick texture. To say I was deflated undersells it; i was distraught that all of my progress was gone. As if to mock me, while I stared at all of my lost work, the game autosaved. I haven't had any desire to play since. I see in the patch notes that this has been fixed, but I just don't want to lose my progress to similar situations in the future. The game is early access, and I get it, but I'll play the game once it's been properly launched at this point. I'm tired of losing my progress seemingly at random. There's only a few hours at most of "story" content, but I wasn't getting this game for the story. I wanted a better version of HF1, and in some regards this is that still. The texture on furnitures is much more consistent, and I like the fact you can more heavily modify a home now. I just don't think it's worth it to me that you can lose so much really important progress still. Original Review: In its current state, probably wouldn't recommend this game. While I am enjoying playing I lost about an hour or so of progress after a crash because the auto-save is so infrequent and the game fluctuates between running well and borderline crashing. My PC isn't amazing, but it isn't so poor that it shouldn't be able to run this game. The new painting style is also really annoying; I felt slightly motion sick after a few times due to having to move the camera around so much. I would like to like this game but I feel really jaded by the progress loss still seeing as I was having a lot of fun up until the crash.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely recommend this game. If you have as many hours in the first game as I do, you know this game is something special. Unfortunately, yes, this game is currently lacking quite a lot (carpet, curtains, holiday decor, smaller lights, pictures/paintings, being able to change the size of things like rugs, and just an overall lack of content) in comparison to the first game. However, the first game had many DLC and many years of development. I have high confidence this game will reach the same level of quality content as the first one, and even better still because of the shiny new graphics, object customization, and overall improvement to the ability to customize a house from the ground up. Other few notes are the lack of settings like turning off the day and night cycle, and other UI things like when completing a job it no longer says "All Tasks Completed". It would also be nice to have more accessibility settings, the painting is a little clunky, and surfaces are way too easy to misplace without having an undo button. Besides all that, the game is beautiful on it's own, and a wonderful upgrade to the first. It just needs more time to develop and again, I have high confidence in the developers to do so!

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of House Flipper and was a little worried that HF2 wouldn't live up to the love I had for the original. If you loved the first one, you will love the second one! I'm borderline obsessed. Better graphics, a cute story line, and customization features we didn't have in the first one. They took away the assembly for furniture and showers and such, which I am personally a big fan of. But they elaborated on other things, such as building walls and offering an 'assembly mode' for discounts.  I also read a comment on here the other day talking about how painting was painful. If you set your border for painting and then hold down the mouse button, you can actually use your "wasd" keys to move the roller. The click and drag isn't necessary and it speeds up your painting time. I've played HF2 now for 21 hours. I love it. It is 35$ well spent. I am hopeful we will see DLC's down the road like we did for the original HF. The only thing I haven't figured out is the stairs. Your beams can be destroyed with the demo tool, then rebuilt from the architecture beams or you can build them with bricks and cover them with a wood surface. If you unselect the 'cut' then it appears almost like it is a full beam. However, I cannot figure out how to edit or replace the stairs on the front and back porches. The steps specifically.For 21 hours of play, that is my only thing. Hands down recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have 235 hours in the first House Flipper and it's one of my all-time favorite games. When I initially played the demo for this game, I was really disappointed. I hated the changes to the tools. I had planned to pass on purchasing as a result of my extreme distaste for the demo, but I got sucked in by friends who were playing. Surprise, surprise: I'm a fool for buying the game with full knowledge of this, but the tools remain clunky and just plain bad. One friend could not rotate items with the mouse wheel at all, needing to resort to the square bracket keys instead. Additionally, several maps are buggy. I am not the only person I know who failed to find all the trash in certain areas of certain maps because those pieces seemingly only exist in the minus realm. The trash highlighting is abysmal and it hardly helps unless you happen to be right on top of the piece(s) you're looking for, and maybe not even then.After 25 hours, I've finished the campaign, I've yet to sell a house, I don't have all the achievements, and...I just don't care to do any more. The game lacks the soul of its predecessor. I enjoyed the feeling of working my way up from the tiny office shack to bigger and bigger houses; imagine my surprise when .House Flipper 2 is cartoonish and forgettable, and that breaks my heart to say as such a huge fan of the first game. With the original, I bought all the DLC on the day they were released, so I've spent a decent amount of money on it and I don't regret it for a second; with this one, I bought it for $30 thanks to bundle pricing, and I still feel like I paid too much. When I've been asked by others which one is better, which one they should play, without hesitation I recommend the original game. I can't imagine this game improving enough to where I'll ever say otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is.... fine. not a significant upgrade from House Flipper. Some of the in game mechanics (painting, cleaning, etc.) feel smoother, but that's about it. Likes: Some improvements to game mechanicsDislikes:  -They've removed the mechanics of installing certain fixtures (from the first game, eg the "steps" to install a shower, sink, etc) that makes the game much more boring. -The in-game store for items for renovations is very poorly designed and the selection of items is really sparse. I assume the plan is to introduce DLCs with "new" content later, but honestly - really boring gameplay/limited creativity-They've added an interactive mobile phone element that forces you to interact with clients, which feels unnecessary. It interrupts tasks at the start of each gig, and honestly - did not come to this game for some mid storytelling (that actually adds nothing to the game), came for a cozy, creative experience.-They've also added a gig element where you have to unpack for people - feels like a rip off of the game "Unpacking" and feels like busy workI think I've used the word "boring" 3x now. _childDocuments_.review: Firstly I want to say I think this game has great potential like the first one, it just isn't there yet. If you didn't play House Flipper 1, I think you'll be pretty happy with this, however if you did then I feel like this is a step backwards from the original game. The only pros that really stand out to me are that the store UI from the first one is much smoother - swatches, wood grains, colors etc. are in the same place for every item now (in the first one, sometimes Texture A would be first in the list, sometimes it would be third, IFYKYK) and you can point your flipper tool at something and look it up in the store to duplicate/edit. For me, compared to the first game, this just seems like the focus is more on decoration than actually flipping and renovating houses. - I enjoy the WASD for window cleaning and painting but you can paint an entire wall without moving with the WASD which takes away from it. - Demolishing walls, there's no animation like in the first one if you remove supporting bricks and ones above fall away. - Outside, you no longer need to buy scaffolding to reach higher areas to clean/paint like in the first one - You can put doors and windows literally anywhere, you no longer need to knock out space for them- You don't have to construct anything anymore; I loved that in the first one if you wanted a shower you had to put the fixtures in first and then plumb the shower in but there's none of that here. I know it's just a game so don't come at me for complaining about the lack of realism but the entire game just seems like a husk compared to the first one. I'd love if all of the above issues I have with it were addressed and there was also more impact on how you decorate people's homes in their quests - I don't see the point in them calling you to tell you what they want when everything's automated for you.

It's great. I've encountered a couple of minor bugs, but nothing session-ruining so far.

_childDocuments_.review: House Flipper 2 introduces some changes that significantly alter the gameplay experience from its predecessor, and not necessarily for the better. As a fan of the original House Flipper, I was disappointed to find that many beloved features have been removed or simplified. For instance, the absence of turf rolls and the ability to install radiators myself takes away some of the hands-on, detailed renovation aspects that made the first game so immersive and enjoyable.It feels like House Flipper 2 was rushed to release, as evidenced by the lack of depth in its features compared to its predecessor. While the graphics have received a noticeable upgrade, which is commendable, the gameplay features have taken a noticeable hit. The game seems to have been streamlined to appeal to a broader audience, but in doing so, it has lost some of the charm that made the original game a favorite among simulation enthusiasts.One of the most disappointing aspects is that House Flipper 2 no longer feels like the same game. It's been downgraded to a point where it lacks the unique identity and depth that defined the first House Flipper. As someone who genuinely enjoyed the original game's detailed renovation mechanics, this departure from its roots is particularly disheartening.Despite my criticisms, I do appreciate the effort put into improving the game's visual presentation. However, I hope the developers will take feedback into consideration for future updates and perhaps reintroduce some of the beloved features through DLC, similar to how the original game expanded over time. There's potential for House Flipper 2 to evolve into something great, but for now, it falls short of capturing the magic that made its predecessor so beloved.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I have completed the base game story campaign I feel confident I can review this game. I come from a position where I had played the original House Flipper since version 1.0 and its remarkable how much better the day 1 version of House Flipper 2 is. To keep it short this sequel is a fantastic continuation of the series with graphical and systematic improvements over its predecessor. If you loved the first one you are sure to love this one as well.Now onto the meat and potatoes if your interested... So This game in comparison to House Flipper 1 is much more modular and customizable in its design and allows for much much more unique houses. It had progressed and improved over the years in House Flipper 1 but was still limited due to its framework. Being able to destroy any walls, floors, stairs, roofs and create custom plant/pot designs and truly create your own house is something that a lot of us had always wished for with these games. Let me talk about some of the systems in the game and give me overall impressions of them.Cleaning: Its servicable and overall is more fluid and less frustrating than the first game with more clear outlines for where to clean with the new scanner function with is highly appreciate (although I do wish the map was still there)Trash: Its more realistic now in that your trash actually fills into a trash bag as opposed to just disappearing into the void. You can also lob trash bags across an entire house to a trash can which was pretty fun.Painting: The new system of painting where you manually paint each portion of the wall is more interactive and aside from the sometimes nauseating camera angles that you get I enjoy the new method of painting.Assembly: Assembly is much, much more in depth in this game compared to House Flipper 1 but this has positives and negatives. The positives: Feels more realistic, feels more rewarding; The negatives: Much slower compared to previous assembly system, some might find the system to be too complex for no real reason.Flipper Tool: Oh man I love the changes to the Flipper Tool. Selling is the same as always but they added perk point upgrades that allow you to duplicate items to avoid redundant menu traversal. A really nice addition was the copy function which allows you to copy any item style or surface finish and copy it to another item which makes matching sets easy. The final and arguable best addition was the designer function which allows you to change any items style of any furniture truly a godsend and makes it so that you can keep the same furniture without having to change to another one because you dislike the color.Demolition/Building: The system is much quicker than in House Flipper 1 and despite being less satisfying in my opinion provides a much more friendly system considering how much more demolition you do in House Flipper 2 and is a good change overall. Building is a depressing and makes filling in uneven gaps that are anything other than a rectangle kinda awful but it could be worse.Surface finishing: Its quicker and easier to customize compared to House Flipper 1 with a grid style placing system instead which is much more natural from my playing.Scanning tool: I really like the scanning tool and it makes it much more clear to my eyes where objects I have missed are.Overall: This game is the best the House Flipping genre has ever been (not saying much) and if this at all interests you then maybe this was of help to you have fun flipping!

_childDocuments_.review: I originally wrote a rather scathing review of House Flipper 2, with the sky-high hopes I had for it, knowing how much I enjoy(ed) the original game. I won't lie: there are a few things I still like better about the first game, and I still feel there is at least  room for improvement for House Flipper 2...With that said, though, since posting my original review, I've played a lot more of it (not that I hadn't played much at the time, mind you), I feel like Frozen District has been doing their part in listening to the fans and making tiny-yet-substantial adjustments to make the overall experience much better. We finally got a stepladder (though, I  wish it was just a tad taller; I feel like the ladder from the first game was an ideal height boost), we can sleep in beds to change the time of day (very much appreciated!), and I feel that the game runs and even looks better in parts...I still wish the vegetation looked more lively, and that we could do something about the grass/terrain outside of Sandbox Mode, but my bigger, more important concerns have otherwise been addressed! I've also seen footage just one or two months ago, and it looked...for lack of a better term, less polished back then - it looked more like a Sims 4 attempt, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but I'm both one of the few people who likes the overall aesthetic of Sims 3 over Sims 4, and that I feel like, because House Flipper is about flipping, decorating, and staging houses for buyers, the emphasis is on the general aesthetic. Yes, I always spout my usual "Gameplay > Graphics" rhetoric, and I stand by that, but House Flipper is a homely, sandbox-y, artsy game - the kind of game that, I feel, graphics matter more than, say, an RPG, because half the fun is seeing a nicely renovated and decorated house in its splendor.Like I said, I still feel there is room for improvement for House Flipper 2, but if Frozen District continues to deliver in both content and tweaks moving forward, I can certainly see it surpassing the first game - especially if they don't become greedy  like EA. House Flipper 1 had meaty, diverse DLCs with lots of new items, new tools, and new mechanics coinciding with free updates for every player; and said DLCs were reasonably priced if you ask me! If they treat House Flipper 2 with the same love and respect for the fanbase that they did the first game, my opinion will go from a soft "Yes" to an unconditional "Yes."

_childDocuments_.review: House Flipper 2: A Renovator's Dream Come True! 🏡✨If you loved the original House Flipper, then get ready to be blown away by House Flipper 2! This game takes everything we adored about its predecessor and cranks it up to eleven. From the moment I picked up my virtual sledgehammer 🛠️, I was hooked.First off, the graphics are stunning 🎨. The level of detail in each house is incredible, and the new colour palette options make decorating feel more personal and vibrant. I found myself lost in the game for hours ⏳, meticulously picking out the perfect wallpaper and flooring combinations.The new features are a game-changer 🚀. The ability to completely customise layouts and build new walls opens up endless possibilities. Ever dreamed of turning a cramped little shack into a sprawling modern masterpiece? Now you can! Plus, the added landscaping tools mean you can make the outside of your house as gorgeous as the inside 🌳🌺.One of the best parts is the expanded catalogue of furniture and decor 🛋️. The variety is fantastic, and there's something to suit every taste, whether you're into sleek contemporary styles or cosy, rustic vibes. _childDocuments_.review: The negative reviews on this almost put me off, but I'm glad I bought House Flipper 2.  I've been playing it a lot since buying it, and have played HF1 since it was released (for 100+ hours), so I have a lot of thoughts!The devs are obviously going the EA/Sims route by releasing the next iteration of the game and not including aspects from previous DLC- which means, HF2 is, of course, missing a lot of things that HF1 + 6 years of development + 7 DLC has.  I have mixed feelings on this: in one sense, you always hope the sequel has some of the cool stuff the first game added, but I also understand this is the way games are made and released now.  It's a bit unreasonable to expect that the base game would come with everything that HF1 has currently, and if you miss those things- HF1 is still there (and apparently still going to get content).That being said, if we're comparing base game to base game, I think HF2 is a big improvement!  The graphic style put me off when I saw videos before the game came out, but it looks lovely in-game.  The level of customisation is great- putting individual plants in pots, changing designs on bedding and furniture (looking forward to them adding new patterns too!)- is all fantastic.  The new flipping tools are really useful (particularly the copy/paste style functions and duplicating items).  Laying tiles, wallpaper, and breaking walls is a lot better now (though painting and building walls in Story Mode is slightly more tedious). I enjoyed the story, even if it was a tad short, and am really liking the new houses and environments.  The furniture is also really nice compared to HF1's base game furniture, which was pretty terrible.  Mod.io support and being able to download player's houses/custom jobs is really cool.  The game isn't perfect: there's some weird glitches (items trying to clip into the ground, receiving level up points when you've already maxed out a skill), the auctioning with buyers seems pointless as they have no feedback (and I hated the buyers in HF1, but I miss having SOME sort of feedback on the house), before/after pictures are missing, cleaning is more tedious (but I actually like cleaning, so don't mind it), lack of rugs/no curtains, and I miss just being able to do custom canvas pictures instead of everything in frames.  I do wish we could at least mow the lawns in the base game, but I know there'll be a garden DLC just like there was for HF1.  The mini-game to assemble furniture is annoying to play and pointless (I stopped doing them halfway through)- I guess the devs put that in to replace the assembly mechanic for plumbing, etc. in HF1, and while I didn't actually like doing that either, I would've preferred that back, instead.  Building a house in Sandbox mode seems really finicky, but that might be a "me" problem, as I've seen people make incredible houses.And obviously we need Workshop support so we can add in modded furniture and decor!However, the devs are really responsive and seem to be working on all these things.In the end, though, I'm having a blast with House Flipper 2.  It's a really solid base game with some big improvements from House Flipper 1's base game.  The game will naturally get more content as patches and DLC are released, but even with the base game content, I've already gotten my money's worth and then some.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game so far has been great! Let's go over some points on what this game has been able to achieve.• Graphics    The graphical fidelity in this game is a stark improvement over the first game, art direction and the very well used displacement, normal, specular and more are very appreciated, the sun casts a warm glow and the global illumination looks great, with objects properly interacting with light and leaving shadows as well, the game is much more stylized than HF1, some may find it unappealing, but the game exudes style and consistency, even in the smallest of objects, the consistent modelling and texturing work shines and brings each scene of the game together.• Gameplay    The Gameplay, just like the graphics is not a complete departure from the first game, but a reworking and polished version of what the first game tried to do, all the usual house flipping gameplay is back, changing walls and floors, buying objects, vacumming, and yes, window cleaning among others have found their way into this game but every single tool has been tweaked and tuned to be much more malleable and consistent, the flipper tool now being able to not just sell items, but to duplicate, change style and copy style as well, styles also being a huge part of the furniture and objects in House Flipper 2, you can make anything be made of, well, anything, a toilet is just a vessel, make it ceramic, plastic, metal or god forbid fabric, any color you want, the possibilities are actually endless and that terrifies me.• Assembly     Assembling radiators is not a thing anymore in House Flipper 2's jobs, instead assembly is now a separate mode in which you can enjoy building a lot of furniture items from the ground up! It is as close as building an ikea shelf  as it gets, literally every single step is present, and I gotta say, the camera angles aren't the best, which I expect to be patched, but the gameplay itself is very fun, assembling items will then give you a permanent discount on the specific item you assembled in the store, so there's nothing to lose, if not your patience after having to perfectly time screwing in 30 screws while trying to get the impossible 3rd star by finishing the goshdarn side table in 8 minutes and 30 seconds or less.• Sandbox     Sandbox mode is creative mode on crack, you can fly around, build walls instantly, not worry about money, and do basically anything, and if you're feeling ambitious, the Sandbox mode allows you to create your own jobs! the tools are super in-depth and allow you to do literally anything and I can't stress that enough, it's almost overwhelming how much stuff there is to it. and talking about making jobs, why make them if you can't share them with the world? well, that's the thing, you can! HF2 releases with mod.io, which allows any player to upload any job or house to their mod.io platform, and other players can then search for, download and play on your own lot! The devs just literally gave us the power to make a whole game's worth of content as if the almost unquantifiable amount of hours of gameplay and replayability this game has wasn't already enough, props.Overall, this game is like giving redbull to a kid and then telling it to go jump on a trampoline until they tire out, which will be never, and if they do it's just temporary cuz they'll go right back to it later, anyways House Flipper addiction is a real addiction with real victims and I am one of them, go buy the game or whatever if you want, also jerma played it so it already has the thumbs up

Very limited amount of decor or furniture (no carpets?). A very very short campaign. im happy with the systems they have added though, except for walking out to a bin all the time, but its early access and its hard to deny that and should be marketed as such.
_childDocuments_.name: House Flipper 2

_childDocuments_.review: I do enjoy the game so far, but it has been a bit of a frustrating experience. I have been grinding through the story missions and 3 starring every job. I finally made enough money to buy my first "real" flip. I spent a little over an hour cleaning/prepping the house for the new ideas I had. I sold everything in the house and had like $110,000+ after all of the sales. I saved the game twice to make sure it saved, went to bed and logged back in the next day and am back to the initial budget I had after buying the house! Now the entire house is empty and my budget was basically cut in half.I guess it's not the worst thing, but personally I think the original house flipper is better to play at the moment. I have most of the DLC for that, there's ALOT more options for building and I get to see the before/after when I finish the project. HF2 has a ton of potential but feels like it wasn't ready to be fully released yet. I don't like that I can't use some of the other DLC  from before for lawn maintenance etc. For now, I'd say save your money and keep an eye on it! I'll be playing the original for now.

A few things to consider / that we can hope for as the game continues to develop:* Really miss the before / after slideshow and saving these* Hope we get the full H&G or at least ability to fix up the yards and landscaping more* More variety of appliances, custom walls and floors etcOverall it's a "win" for players and the Frozen District team. _childDocuments_.review: This game is not fun. I love the original House Flipper. HF2 is not nearly as good. Either the game was released six months too soon or it just isn't any good. They took one of HF's best mechanics/activities--painting--and replaced it with a buggy, awful, hard on the hands and arm painting system that is not at all fun. There's no minimap showing you where the dirt is, so you can search for hours for that last bit of dirt before giving up. The only reason I haven't asked for a refund is I'm hoping that they fix it sometime in the next few months. For now, I've uninstalled it. I'll just play original HF and come back in a few months and see if they've fixed HF2. For now, don't waste your money.

_childDocuments_.review: This promises to be quite good if the developers continue to add to it. It is limited compared to HF 1 because it has just been newly released. The game is missing some big design elements, like curtains. The options you have for each type of furniture are limited to maybe 20. There will be a lot that you can't quite do in this game, but the building and colour options are pretty great. A lot of the tweaks on the tools are super neat. It has lost a bit of the interactivity of the first game. I honestly think a lot of people will find that to be a relief/good thing. For me it was kind of disappointing. You don't install things in each house. Instead you have a system of learning to install things in a minigame. Your success gives you discounts on items as you're designing. The designing is then just click and place. The paint tool has some really cool tweaks, and you can build half walls, etc now. You can even put chair moulding on the bottom half of a wall and paint above it in any colour that you like. You can apply ACTUAL back splashes in kitchens and bathrooms. There are way more colour options, and if the Devs continue to add items and DLC it's gonna be a really great game.
