_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing.I was so excited for this game to come out! It was sitting in my wishlist since it was announced. I loved every second of playing the story and doing the hired jobs while casually working on flipping houses, but where it become disappointing for me was the story itself. It was built up like you would really need to work long and hard to get to the end game project and that it would be a massive project when you did get there. I was excited for this, I wanted to work for it and feel that satisfaction of finally getting there, but then I got there in like... 13hrs of playing the game. It didn't feel rewarding at all.  Plus, the end project was nothing like it had been built up to be. It was made to sound like it was a massive project, but I feel like I had more time consuming hired jobs where I did way more work. The story felt so short that when it ended and the credits rolled, I sat there like... what just happened?? With a $40 price tag, I expected at least 40hrs of game play. And yes you can argue that the independent house flipping portion would add game play time, but so much emphasis was put on the story portion, that it just felt lacking.Pros:- The game was very pretty and I liked the furniture and patterns.- You can customize any of the "finishes" (wallpapers and flooring) which I thought was pretty cool (but could be annoying and time consuming as well at times.)- The cleaning aspect, which is my favorite part of the House Flipper games, was very satisfying. I also liked the trash collecting.- Mom and dad were very cute.Cons:- Short and unsatisfying story mode- The manual painting drove me absolutely insane and I hated every second I had to paint something.- There's no undoing painting or finishing, so if you accidentally cover something you didn't mean to, you have to buy whatever you covered to touch up a little tiny spot and the controls can be slippery sometimes and matching it was impossible.- They put the satisfying assembly from HF1 into a side, timed game that was stressful, confusion, and annoying.Overall, I don't think I'd recommend the game to someone else. It definitely doesn't feel like it's worth the $40 price tag. Maybe if you got it during a decent sale? But if you do, don't expect too much.

_childDocuments_.review: I would ABSOLUTELY recommend this, but... Devs, please read this and listen! I would really appreciate it!There's lots of things that need polish, or need to be added. _childDocuments_.review: Good:This is a fantastic upgrade to HF1. The graphics are just beautiful, especially the plants. The plants look so much nicer, and they are easier to place. The neighborhoods look great, with one suburban, one beachfront, and one forest neighborhood. There are a nice variety of houses with interesting and detailed exteriors. I love that we have a color wheel that allows us to customize colors and materials for most items. Overall the interface is great and the tools are easy to use. Fences are click and drag, which is so much better than HF1. However, a lot more items could benefit from click-and-drag treatment: ceiling beams, shelving, patios etc. I hope they add that in the future. I love the feedback site they created where you can request items and features. Mixed:Assembly is now a separate mini-game, which I am happy to ignore. HF1 did not have a compelling system for actually selling the houses, HF2 has almost no system at all? I sold my first house, got one offer, the end. You can't view buyer's preferences and there is no feedback about the house. There are also no before/after pictures :(. This is a weak point, but not a huge deal. I'm pretty sure they will add before/after pictures back into the game, since it's a popular feature. After buying a lot of DLC for HF1, HF2's catalog of items feels limited. The color wheel helps you not get bored using a small catalog of items, but I am itching for more content to come out. Overall this game is definitely worth it, even without DLC. It feels like an upgrade, and will only get better from here.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about House Flipper 2 but I'd say most of it is positive...The things that bother me most is the lack of curtains/blinds for the windows as of this review, story mode is short, and there's a complete lack of assembling the furniture (you can only do so in a dedicated "practice area" for a single piece of furniture so you get a discount when buying said furniture in story mode). That said, I do love the fact that furniture is now fully interactable with as opposed to the first game where the base stuff was a static mesh. I also really like that you can place objects inside the fridge and counters, effectively making things feel more "lived" than before. Surface finishing is much more simplified in this game but it's probably for the better as putting down tiles in the first game was daunting, and the painting system has been completely revamped making things faster and possibly easier this time around, given you are able to define the paint area before hand so no more painting outside the area you wanted to paint.Finally demolishing walls has been overly simplified and there are no physics for it. I miss smashing down a wall and watching the rest of it crumble. None of that here.Overall I'd say it's a bit of a mixed bag. I really enjoy what's there, but I also really miss what is not.

_childDocuments_.review: A frustrating split decision between yes and no. Ultimately I decided with no because of just how much content is missing from the base game. I do not mean some of the additional furniture / decorating options from the DLC in HF1. There is just a staggering low amount of base stuff in HF2's current state. To me this is my biggest gripe, however there is more to this than just missing content. These are what I consider minor negative points. Things like, lighting issues. Sometimes lights fail to realize their potential and just stop glowing. Other times they shine so bright that I'm surprised the house doesn't catch on fire from 3.828×10^26 luminescence burning all those who cast their thoughts upon it.Another minor thing is how some mission/stories (What ever you wish to call them) feel abandoned half way. Some houses generally ask you to build something for them -- only to leave it unpainted or unfinished. Did they run out of money? If so thats pretty realistic then but since this is about house improvement I'm going with no. The devs simply forgot to ask for it to be finished. The perk system just feels half hearted and empty. Some categories only have just a few options (If I recall HF1 was also like this). What is the point in earning 8 points to pick 3 total perks? Either redo the system completely so you earn 1 point and choose out of all categories, or add more meaningful perks. So here is what I'm hoping for to turn this from a no, to a overwhelming yes. Triple the base content. That is a lot to ask for, I am aware. Modelers, animators, texture artists aren't free. But releasing a second version of a game with even less content than the first is a slap in the face at this pointGo through and give some missions a second glace.Typical bug fixing which is bound to happen but figured I might as well list it.Adjust or out right redo the perk systemThen and only then, open the flood gates of DLC and just go nuts on actual additional content. HF2 does so much right over HF2. The new tools are honestly the best part. Being able to actually copy styles and paste them is just, mmmffh, chefs kiss right there. Being able to build from the ground up and demolish entire parts. Beautiful. So much going for it just needs a helping step. Only then can it take EA's face and ram into the ground. Knocking the Sim's series of building off a peg or two.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very difficult review for me to write, and I hate that I for now can't give it a positive one, because I absolutely love HF1 and had such high hopes for this one. I really, REALLY wanted to love it, but so far it's not enough and not worth the rather expensive price.Now it's not all bad, it has quite a few nice features that I'm really enjoying, but almost every nice feature comes with its own complaint attached to it, so in the end it doesn't end up looking too good. But let's dig into it anyway.First off, I love the clutter, but it's not enough. I don't know how many times we begged for more clutter to be added to HF1, and the fact that they didn't take that with them to HF2 is already a huge let down. The clutter itself, however, is really nice. I love the different foods added and that we can have groceries in our fridge and all that, but already here things are just... not quite there yet. There's fruit but you can't stack them in a bowl, putting things on plates is kinda awkward, and things like toothbrushes can't be put in the toothbrush holder. They've added a few clothing items, but you can't hang them on the furniture that have hooks, and the kitchen towels can only be used directly on the wall rather than the hooks you put up. There are no big towels for the bathroom, nothing to put on the shelves, and almost no rugs, and while the clutter itself is improved from the first game, it's just not nearly enough. (I do love that you can hang the toilet rolls on the holder, though. That's a really nice little detail.)Then we have the flowers. There's not a lot to pick between, but I love that you can now put any flower you want in whichever pot you prefer. However, it also comes with a downside. You can't put the flower in the center of most pots. Most of them will have to be more to one side than the other, and that's frustrating as hell. It shouldn't be, but it is.There are no curtains or blinds. I know the devs have said this is something they have noted and will add in later, but I just have to point out how stupid it is to not have it in the game from the start. A whole game about furnishing houses and there are no curtains to hang in the windows? Who made that stupid call? Come on, do better. I don't know if there is an undo button somewhere, but if there is it's not easy to find or use. We need an easy ctrl+z. Like really. In a game like this, it's essential.Another thing that bothers me is how difficult it is to paint or put down tiles/floors where there's already furniture. Now I know, in real life you can't exactly paint the wall while the sofa is standing against it, but this is a game. I don't want to have to move everything around just so I can change the colors in my living room for the 27th time. Do you know how hard it is to find the perfect wallpaper? And how many times I will change my mind about what floor matches the coffee table the best? Please let me place floor underneath it without this struggle, I am begging you.I know we've been promised before and after pictures in the future, but this is something that needs to happen sooner rather than later. It feels so empty without it, and almost pointless to even make the place nice because I won't be able to enjoy my hard work of turning this house into the perfect home. It doesn't scratch that itch we have when playing these kinds of games, so I really hope this is something that will added SOON. I don't understand how they even released the game without it tbh. The copy style function is something I've wanted badly for ages, so I'm SO HAPPY it was added to HF2, HOWEVER, it doesn't work as well as it should. It doesn't always copy the style you actually want, instead it takes that tiny little detail of your furniture that happens to be in another color and paints your whole next furniture in that one color you didn't even know you had added to your first piece. It's annoying but I'm not sure how it could actually be fixed. I also wish you could edit the already placed furniture and maybe change that small detail and try again, rather than having to find it in the shop again and make all the changes to it once again. It's a really nice feature, but it's a bit wonky and can sometimes be rather frustrating. I feel like all I do is complain in this review, but sadly the game feels unfinished. It should have been an early access or beta or whatever. As it is right now it's not worth how expensive it is. It also annoys me that the developers refer to their voting page when it comes to suggestions. Like no, we shouldn't have to vote on things that should already have been in the game to begin with. Take the criticism, and once again, do better.To say something positive before I finish this review; the artwork is wonderful and I like the whole collecting trash and having to toss out the bags thing (though I wish we could carry more than one trash bag with us. Who on earth can only carry one?). I like the phone calls and the slightly different answers we can give, and though the story quest was way too short, it was enjoyable. The new way of painting is nice and I'm happy I'll no longer accidentally paint a wall I wasn't planning on painting and I do so enjoy that you can have both wallpaper and pain on the same walls if you want to. The fact that any furniture can go in the same color and pattern is also very nice. I do see a lot of potential in this one, and I will keep playing it, but as it is right now, I won't recommend it. I will change my review if the game turns out better. Because I really do still hope it will be everything we thought it would be when they first started teasing us about it.

_childDocuments_.review: House Flipper 2 – Because My Virtual Life is Cleaner Than My Real OneIf you thought smashing walls and flipping houses was fun in the first game, House Flipper 2 takes it to a whole new level. This time around, it’s not just flipping houses; it’s flipping your entire digital existence into a zen-like state of organization while your real-life bedroom looks like it was hit by a hurricane of laundry.The graphics are shinier, the houses are bigger, and yes, you can now obsess over even more detailed interior design choices that will definitely make you question why your own home doesn’t have an open-concept kitchen with a minimalist Scandinavian vibe. Spoiler: It’s because decorating in real life is hard and expensive. But in House Flipper 2? No worries, just sell that ugly lamp and replace it with a high-end designer one in a few clicks. Easy-peasy!Of course, my favorite feature remains the cleaning – not because I enjoy scrubbing floors, but because I get to do it virtually while pretending my real home doesn’t have dust bunnies the size of small dogs. It’s incredible how much motivation I can muster to clean someone’s digital bathroom while actively avoiding the dishes piling up in my own sink.And the renovations? Pure art. One minute I’m a humble painter, and the next, I’m a certified interior design genius, knocking down walls like a pro and creating Pinterest-worthy spaces that leave me wondering why I’m still sitting on the same creaky chair IRL. And don't even get me started on the garden expansions – I've landscaped more in this game than I've ever done to the weeds taking over my actual backyard.In House Flipper 2, I can finally live the fantasy of being someone who "has their life together," one perfectly aligned virtual sofa at a time. Sure, my actual home might be a disaster, but my House Flipper empire is spotless.11/10 – I may never clean my real house again, but I will absolutely keep power-washing virtual walls until they sparkle!

_childDocuments_.review: I have 260 hours on the original house flipper, and after playing 17.5 hours in two days on this one, I thought I would give my feedback on what I like/dislike to provide insight to others buying the game. First off, Positives:The graphics are much more realistic from the original house flipper. Every thing seems more vibrant (color, item, house wise), and the interaction with my agent friend/ other people seems much more personal. This version of HF feels like things are more 3D! I'm loving the customization for the different furniture, and some of the new tools!! Being able to see more environments/styles of houses right of the get-go is nice as well! Varies things up quite a bitNegatives:That being said the higher graphics make it hard to run on my computer, and even with lowest graphics settings on everything, the game has a major lag. Some problems that have arisen due to this is that the game is not automatically saving my progress (I had to do a job 3 times), and even when I click the manual save button, things such as the money I've made from selling stuff doesn't save, which means that even though the things that I have sold are gone, the money is not in my account. Another problem with the low graphics, is the fact that when trying to see the patterns/colors in the store, the resolution is so low that it doesn't let me see the patterns of the text.   The game itself, also takes some getting used to if you are transitioning from the original to this one. If you are like me, and feel more comfortable with less "wavy/moving" settings while walking, placing etc. you can adjust it in settings, but it still isn't completely the same. The drag on the trackpad is real. Cleaning windows, painitng, and selling items with a trackpad seems unnecessarily hard, like I have to dig into my pad in order to move everything around.Some smaller complaints that I have are just thatThe furniture  (basically all store items) in the game, while unique, is very limited, and also very expensive if you are just starting out. I miss not being able to interact/see what the customers are saying about the house you're flipping, and also the ability to see what they are looking for in the house that you are designing. The minimap being gone is also a MAJOR downside; that and the progress bar being gone for specific roomsThings such as trash disposal are a major pain. I get the point is to make it realistc, but when does realistic become completely inconvenient.  Look, while I think that this game is heading in the right direction, and am completely excited for what comes next; I'm not sure it's at it's finest yet. It's still really buggy, small, and while I'm positive I'd recommend it in the future, I'm not sure if it's worth the money I paid for it now. I think that after a few months, and a few more things are added/fixed, I think  this is going to shape up to the level of the original house flipper, or even surpass it!Hi, back again. After playing the game an additional 76, I have to say; this game has surpassed all of my expectations. It took a LOT of getting used to, but I'm loving the more realistic features, items; everything! Great job!!

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished story mode. I did so in 15.5 hours, taking my time and being a bit lazy in the process. I thoroughly enjoyed it. I am looking forward to the new expansions should they choose to add them, but my wallet is not really happy about those, however (the base game being expensive already). I highly recommend it to anyone who:-is artistic-is creative-enjoys renovating houses irl-loves to build or deconstruct-enjoys cleaning-enjoys esthetics and pleasing house related furnitureSo with this said, if you enjoy flipping houses that are dilapidated, this game is for you.In today's economy, especially, considering flipping houses irl does require a fair bit of coinage to execute.Happy House Flipping!

_childDocuments_.review: I never thought I'd be leaving a negative review for the sequel to a game whose original game I loved and enjoyed dearly. House Flipper 2 is a shell of the former game, and for me that's a problem. So much of the content and DLCs that made up the first game are gone. There is content to be found in House Flipper 2, but its lacking considerably to its predecessor. While I feel like the paint colors have a lot more depth this time around, there's a serious lack of other content. Blinds/curtains for windows are gone, wallpapers have very little variety. The wallpapers that are available all have a very ugly 80s aesthetic. House Flipper 2 at this time doesn't support the steam workshop, so user created content is non-existent.All the content from the original game's DLC is gone. This is something I expect from games made from mainstream publishers like Electronic Arts/Activision, as their whole shtick is recycling and reselling content. House Flipper 2 being an indie title, I expected a lot more of the content from the original game to transfer over when in fact, a lot less of the original game transferred over.Even the ability to put together toilets, showers, sinks, etc. is no longer a mainstream part of the game, its a simple mini-game that's been tacked on outside of jobs. This in my opinion should have been an accessibility option. It should have been something included in jobs, but something that could be disabled if someone so choosed to do so...All-in-all, House Flipper 2 at the moment is large step in the wrong direction. So much of what was built up to make House Flipper 1 the great game that it is now has either been removed or changed (and not for the better) and whats here is an empty shell... The campaign is very short, the items are lacking, the customization is sub-optimal, and the original games DLC and community made creations are just gone.Save your money. Play the original. House Flipper 2 feels like an Early Access game that was sold as a full game for $40, which in my opinion is overpriced at the present time.EDIT (7/18/2024): I saw the new roadmap and I'm even happier that I jumped ship from this game. They truly are drip-feeding content into this sequel and putting full content DLCs into the original game is a huge yikes. House Flipper is an indie game, House Flipper 2 feels like a game owned by Electronic Arts.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great, I can sink so many hours of relaxing house flipping/cleaning/decorating.  However, HF2 has the good, the bad, and the ugly......The good: Has the same relaxing vibe.  The sound and feel of cleaning and placing objects and textiles feels good.  I like the optional snap to grid feature.  In HF1 I found it challenging to place wall hooks and ceiling light fixtures because I could never seem to line them up properly, I don't have this issue in HF2.  The voice acting is good and I enjoy the campy story.  Placing tiles and wall panels is much easier than it was in HF1.  Painting walls has a different mechanic than HF1 and takes getting used to, but after spending time with it I find the painting mechanic in HF2 more suitable to my liking.  The build wall mode is also more enjoyable and satisfying.The Bad: The store feature is still not organized in a way that always makes sense to me so things can still be challenging to find.  The store feels very limited in the way of decorations, furniture... the lot.  I feel very limited.  I hope that the devs add more in a patch or the game will feel stale quickly for me.  I will be disappointed if more decor is rolled into a paid DLC as the current price point for the game should come with more decor options as that is the whole premise of the game.  So far there are no curtains. I have only played for 20 hours, so either I haven't unlocked them or they don't exist.  A problem I have with both HF1 and 2 is that the yards come looking like **** with over grown grass.  I'm fine with a DLC to focus and expand upon the yard, however at LEAST let me mow!!The ugly:  I've noticed a few small bugs.  One example is my avatar will rubber band as I am rounding a corner, going up and down stairs, etc.  The game isn't some immersive RPG but it still takes me out of the vibe when I see myself rubber banding.  Finally... HOW DARE YOU NOT GIVE ME BEFORE AND AFTER SHOTS??!?!?!  It's an absolute travesty!!!  I already felt like HF1 should have had more angles and shots, now we have nothing.  Finally, assembling items is bad.. so SO very bad.  If this feature disappeared from the game forever  I would celebrate it.P.S.  I miss the Easter eggs!  There are some in HF2  (post-it notes), but not nearly as much and as fun as HF1.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★☆☆TLDR: A big step up from the previous game in a lot of ways but missing some content and features that would make the game a lot better. For me, this game edges on a recommendation. With a bit more content and QoL features this game could be a 5 star!Gameplay★★★★☆A huge improvement from the previous instalment in most ways. For instance, being able to copy styles to another object, or find the exact colour of the painted walls in the store, etc. However, some things fall a little short. Such as the lack of decorative items, carpets, ability to light fireplaces, the list goes on. A lot of items only seem to have the same wooden presets, but I do like the ability to fine tune object customisation.Graphics★★★★☆A large step up from HF1 (which you would expect), not too badly optimised, but quite demanding at times. I have a mid-end PC and my PC runs quite hot on mid settings.Audio★★★☆☆The background music manages to still be as relaxing as the previous game, but does get quite repetitive and a little bit more annoying. Some sound effects, such as using the cloth to clean the floor, is a little annoying because it sounds like sandpaper. Other than that, I have no further beefs with the sound.Difficulty★★☆☆☆Giving this 2 starts because some of the new mechanics are a little more complicated than the last game. The painting takes some getting used to and the assembling for objects has a little more to it. However, it is by no means a difficult game.Price★★★☆☆Maybe a little on the pricey side for what you get content-wise. A good solid game though so maybe wait for at least a little bit of a price drop or more content to be added.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a step forward in some areas and 3-4 steps back in others and I gave the game its best shot at it. Its not horrible but not good compared to HF1. The good: 1. Looks good and does steam line some stuff like paint and the grid or free moving of items. 2. Dialogue is based on your choice, and while it does cause some unique back and forth, it has no real impact. 3. Less pain of trying to match some stuff with some upgrades. 4. Slightly better options for painting as you can paint in different directions and build walls for more room in a house. The bad: 1. The story is boring and lazy; trying to fix the ugly house feels empty, as there is no cut scene for it, just people talking about it. You hear about bad contractors but never see anything or have moments in the story showing off their shady deals. It's like an evil ghost doing bad stuff, and while emails do say some stuff and some missions reflect it, the lack of cutscenes kills it. 2. Lack of quality of life features that HF1 has, no map, no clear way to know if the job is 100% done, no sound bits, music is not good, and stale, the scan feels bugged when looking for stuff, clunky tablet, and buying stuff is annoying as it bugs out for me. I spent several minutes running around the house, not knowing if it was 100% complete because the game never tells you. You can do 90%, but the 3-star system makes it look like you did 100%. 3. There are no clear borders for rooms/outdoor areas. I have put stuff down, and it was in a different area, but I couldn't tell it was.4. Buggy missions: While HF1 had bugs, completing tasks is a chore sometimes in HF2, such as doors taking away floor tiles, but not really; the scan sometimes didn't highlight stuff like stains or selling stuff that was not clearly shown. 5. UI: I hate the HF2 coins. They feel childish or like mobile game currency. The standard money system feels so much better, as you get a better sense of the value of items. 6. Padding is annoying with some changes, like floor tiles, putting up wallpaper, or painting. While you can upgrade to free paint, you are almost forced to use the WASD keys to paint, and it's annoying since you need to stand in a good spot to make it work. also, you can't switch paint roller size mid-paint, forcing you to back off and change it to start again. 7. Annoying emails: This might be just me, but all the emojis and kid-like emails annoy me. No one would send an email like this to you for professional help. The one for the YouTuber makes sense, but it feels like 70% of emails have these dumb emojis for no reason. 8. Assembly is lifeless, with no music, and it is annoying to find the right part since it either doesn't work or flies past what you need. I struggle with some since finding the right stuff is next to impossible due to how it works.9. Lack of cutscenes. While this is mostly the HF1 DLC stuff that had them, the cutscenes showing off the part of the house you need to fix helps you know where to go and what to do. 10. No before and after, I want to see the work I do, and with a big house, you want to see the changes. In HF1 you wanted to skip, you could. It was nice. 11. Phone calls: I was working on a house when I randomly received a phone call from the client. I thought it was because I entered the house to do it, but sometimes it just happens, and I don't know why or if it is tied to a certain area. It's not the worst, but you can end it quickly, which I have done several times.Conclusion: While the game has plenty of negative aspects, most can be fixed, which is good. There could be a toggle option for some things, and I am sure more DLC is coming. I won't say it is a cash grab but an under-baked sequel that could have used more playtesting before being pushed out.

About the Game A secret Sengoku Era drama begins now. 'Touken Ranbu Warriors' is an action game that is a collaboration between the 'spirits of blades' simulation game 'Touken Ranbu ONLINE' presented by DMM GAMES and NITRO PLUS, and the thrilling '1 vs. 1,000' WARRIORS series of KOEI TECMO GAMES. ●'Touken Ranbu' is in 3D at last. Witness the most beautiful graphics in the history of the WARRIORS series. The Touken Danshi characters, which will be familiar to fans of the source material, rush about the battlefield in 3D. In addition to the thrilling action you expect from the WARRIORS series, you can enjoy battles with a plentiful variety of animations, such as battling together with a partner and dueling. Experience battles with the Touken Danshi that are both fierce and beautiful. ●Fifteen blades incarnate from a drifting honmaru base set out on a historical drama in the Sengoku Era. Experience an original epic story that can only be found in this game. Story overview: The Touken Danshi, 15 blades incarnate who had been drifting aimlessly without a Saniwa master, are suddenly attacked by the History Retrograde Army. After the battle, they are assigned by the Government of the Time to undertake 'onslaught investigations.' The masterless blades have no choice but to depart for the chaotic world of the Sengoku Era, whose history had already begun to be altered. ●The honmaru serves as the base of the Touken Danshi. Enjoy tons of special events and elements that can only be found in this title. The Touken Danshi can be placed freely within the 3D-depicted honmaru, the characters' base where they live. Players can also see how the Touken Danshi are doing at the honmaru, as well as view original events unique to this title in which they interact with one another. Between battles, players can take a break and enjoy mini-games such as 'Pose Matching' and 'Tag.' Photo Mode, in which players can take pictures of the Touken Danshi , is also included. ●Easy Mode has been included, so even players who are less proficient at action games can control the game easily. Two types of controls are included: 'Regular Mode,' which features the control scheme traditionally used for the WARRIORS series, and 'Easy Mode,' which uses controls for players less proficient at action games. The latter only requires simple button inputs, so players will be able to enjoy the beautiful actions.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface this review by saying that im playing this game as a big fan of the Musou genre, its my favourite overall genre along with JRPGs. I am not however a Touken Ranbu fan, and have actually never seen or heard anything about it before this game.As many have already said, this is a very cut down musou game. Basically every single aspect of a typical musou game has been simplified in Touken Ranbu Warriors which is certainly disappointing to see, and is absolutely something I hope wont be seen in any future musou games. Besides this however the core aspects of a musou game are here in some aspect, so fans of the genre will feel mostly at home, with the most major and obvious loss being the wide open maps and long missions that have been replaced with mostly linear maps on missions that quite literally last 4 - 8 minutes.Besides the fact that I absolutely consider this a 'diet' musou game, I am admittedly still having a good time with it and will continue to play it. The combat and core gameplay is still fun, if a bit strange and off feeling compared to an average musou game, and the game visually looks great.Overall I will recommend this game, but if you're not a hardcore fan of either musou games or Touken Ranbu, I would absolutely wait for a sale before picking this up.Tl:dr: A strange direction for a musou game, and a direction that I hope wont continue in the genre. However as a stand alone one off 'experiment' at a simpler musou style im still having a pretty decent time playing through this title. Definitely one for Touken Ranbu fans primarily, and for die hard musou fans that want to experience every musou game. For everyone else, definitely wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I personally enjoy this game but I understand why some people may not like it.Hear me out for a sec.Lets break down the story... It's about a group of blades that are turned into warriors called Touken Danshi, and are tasked to protecting the Japanese history from these ugly lookin' monsters called History Retrograde Army. You time travel around the history of Japan to make sure history follows the correct course. This game is very much targeted for my girllies~ As the characters are ALL male.I'd say this game is pretty easy for those who are first time playing button mashing, combo learning and such. Story wise in my opinion in the game is understandable but because I've watched the animes and played the first game I know how the story goes really. If you don't quite understand any of the story line or any of the terms, I'd suggest watching Touken Ranbu: Hanamaru to get at least the basics down. For the ones that dont like it, I can totally understand why, as it dosen't really feel like a true warrior -slashing game. It's prob because it was made for new people trying something different.As someone who is still new to controllers and plays mainly on the keyboard and mouse - it was really a great why to introduce me to the controllers better into the fighting style type.Now the Story Mode/Easy Mode. I PRAISE on how they make it EXACTLY what the mode says! Some games make the Story Mode wayy too hard when it hits like what.. Chapter 3?This game REALLY says, "Here I give you help so you can move into the game quicker and enjoy the story fr." And I appreciate it a lot! Hence why I personally enjoy the game. c:

_childDocuments_.review: New to these characters/story but not new to Musou Games, the most recent game I could compare this one to is Samurai Warriors 5. So I'll just make some comparisons and observations between those two games. The story is well written, probably good for someone unfamiliar with this franchise. You can skip past most of it, but if you don't, you'll have around 5 minutes of downtime between levels.Characters are split up into 5 teams, each chapter you'll use a different team and the final chapter you'll be able to choose from the entire roster.  While a stage in Samurai warriors 5 will typically take 15-20 minutes to complete with some optional bonus objectives, stages in Touken Ranbu warriors will last 3-4 minutes on average, with a few objectives that are mandatory. Some are unknown and you'll have to search for clues on some levels. Considering your mission and the story, it kinda makes sense to have shorter stages. Although the stages are shorter compared to the other musou games, there are about 99 of them including the prologue.  So the game doesn't feel any shorter unless you're skipping past all of the story.  The stages have decent variety, some are strictly combat, some are "stealth" oriented, some you have to destroy certain items, some stages have puzzles  elements to complete. They tried to do a lot of different things with the stages and it shows. Combat has been tweaked. Specials don't have a cool down and are spam-able, which works to make combat more flashy and flamboyant, like the characters in this game. It does make the game easier as a side effect but maybe that was intended. I suspect that this game is casual friendly. You can also dodge at any time, even in the middle of a special move. Speaking of difficulty, I finished the game on normal and was only in danger of dying once. You can complete boss fights untouched if you don't stand in the "fire" (the red warning areas on the ground). Graphics are about the same.Music is great, was a nice surprise. Each track is motivating. Right now their doesn't seem to be much replayability, due to the fact that you can't freely use characters until the last chapter. Also, there isn't an alternative character storyline. I'm not really sure what DLC will add to the game. I wouldn't buy this at full price either, I only bought it because I had a wallet credit and nothing else to use it on. If i think of anything else I'll add it later.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great for those wanting to begin playing Musou games, a lot of people complain that this game is not a proper one but keep in mind this game is based upon the Saniwa/Touken Ranbu games that are made for a female audience and most likely hadn't played a game like this that's why it's a more simple Warriors game. The story is about the Touken Danshi who are famous historical Japanese swords that were brought to life as Men fighting to preserve history. The gameplay is very easy however the games levels are very short unfortunately but still pretty fun, you play as 16 characters that as said before have to fight to preserve history, although its not like other warriors games such as Dynasty Warriors or Berserk and the Band of the Hawk that have somewhat less simple combat its still the perfect game for those who want to get into the genre, I highly recommend this game to anyone who wants to start playing a Musou and have mindless fun in combat. However with every pro theres a con. Theres not many outfits for the characters, the Standard which is their uniforms and the Uchiban which is their casual clothes and sadly unlike most Musou games there’s no co-op online or split screen. But overall this game gets a huge recommendation from me and i hope that more content comes at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me, you're probably interested in this game cause there's some husbandos up in here and you're gay.I've played through the first team's part of the story and at first the gameplay was meh, I was worried it wouldn't get any better but you start to unlock more abilities as you level up the characters. I don't really care for the smaller characters but, one thing that scared me was that they have the smae running animation so my first thought was "oh my god, not clones!" but to my surprise each character has their own unique cool looking moveset.Now it's not as deep as samurai warriors combat but it's flashy and pretty.My only gripe with the game is the maps are small, but I think at the end of every chapter you're gonna get to fight a big boss monster which seems cool. I play on the hardest difficulty and I still fly through these maps with some ease so, take that as either "wow this game is nice and accessible for anyone including Touken Ranbu Fans!" or you can take it as maybe it isn't for you if it's a bit easy. But warriors games aren't all that hard to begin with anymore to be honest.The best factor about this game though is when the units receive enough damage their clothes break so.... I'm just sayin'.I do recommend this game for fans and for players interested for a charming, fun time you can pick up from time to time to enjoy.Anyway, Tsurumaru Kuninaga is best boy.

_childDocuments_.review: Touken Ranbu Warriors is more of a puzzle game than a warriors game.There are 2 types of missions which are usually "Follow the set path we set you" and "Explore the map" to find the secret to actually complete the mission. Without doing these side events on [?] missions where you have to investigate you instantly fail the mission immediately.If you happen to succeed a mission you are immediately forced back to the main hub forcing you to watch a 5-6 second animation of a number going to the 2205 time zone over and over.The actual gameplay isn't as engaging as a dynasty warriors game as there isn't as many enemies to hack and slash. There is around 100 or so enemies on a given map in total and they only interact with enemies if you are in a 10-15 step radius around the player character.If you want a mindless dynasty warriors game. This isn't for you.If you want to be a Detective that fixes events in history (the plot of Touken Ranbu) then this is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, not recommending this game is due to the price point and the unfaithful rendition of the Warriors genre. If you're a touken ranbu fan looking for a game to enjoy and this is on sale, I would encourage you to try it out.Playing this game with my boyfriend watching was a good experience overall as we're both touken ranbu fans, however I have complaints for this game as both a Warriors fan and a TouRabu fanCons for Warriors fans-Extremely scaled down, watered down version of the genre. Each battle lasts for less than 10 minutes and the amount of troops you get to kill barely hit the hundreds in most missions. It's like playing a lite version of the genre.-Weird missions that are the opposite of the hack and slash, feel good of massacring enemy units. Without much spoilers, there are 'battles' that are entirely composed of stealth and a 1v1 fight against bosses with mechanics to dodge and what not. These aren't a bad thing for a game but it just doesn't fit a warriors game-You can't control your partner in missions. Not a huge detail but most of the missions consist of you controlling 1 main touken danshi and a partner. In most warriors games nowadays you are able to switch control between them but the game restricts you to only using 1 in each battle while your partner follows you around for combo attacks and other mechanics in game, slightly disappointingAs a TouRabu fan, I only really have 1 issueThe abysmal cast. 16 swords, 1 of which is an original character is extremely disappointing. Understandable with their focus being on the Sengoku era and swords that were used in that time period for a more emotional connection between danshi and their former masters, but sacrificing the cast number for that is a travesty.Overall the game being advertised as a part of the Warriors series leaves a bad taste in the mouth. With the watered down combat missions, including stealth and weird boss fights, the game would have thrived as an RPG without relying on the Warriors name. As stated before, I'd recommend you get the game on a discount if you are a fan of the TouRabu franchise without any high expectations of a fleshed out warriors game.

_childDocuments_.review: I gave it a thumbs up, but I wish I could put it somewhere in the middle so that's what this review is for. I wouldn't recommend this game unless you are a fan of warriors games and touken ranbu cause if you're going in as one or the other I won't promise that you'll like it.Story :idk anything about touken ranbu so idk if the story was original, related, or what but the story was fine for a musou. These guys are trying to change the timeline and it is your job to stop them and make sure the timeline doesn't change so you get split into 5 groups and you go about picking your main character and someone to join you to complete this task.Gameplay:The game uses a charge combo system for those familiar with other Warriors games its basically you do an attack with your square/x button than finish off the combo with triangle/y.  Something introduced in Pirate warriors 4 and Samurai warriors 5 is having skill attacks using the trigger + face buttons. I'd say I have mixed feelings on this aspect because of the way it is utilized in this game being that normally combo strings are unique with skills being random attacks, but in this one some skills are attached to certain charge attacks.Take for example your s+t is a skill, or ss + t is also another skill, so on and so forth. It just feels a bit lazy to me, but the farther in the game you go the better it is because you'll technically be able to use every skill you unlock by having them as charge attacks, and sticking the rest on your face button menu.Something I'm not too fond of is that some enemies basically have hyper armor and some characters attacks will literally slide them across the map and more than likely out of the battlefield where you can't actually hit them so watch out for that.Going along with the story mode, all of the characters are cut up into 5 groups, why this matters storywise idk, I'd rather be able to choose whoever I want whenever I want, but it is what it is. The game gives you a side area for mini games that you can stick up to 9 people in as you complete missions, the benefit of this area is that they get xp as you finish missions so this way even when you switch groups later in the story your other characters won't be far behind in level.There are postives and negatives such as the game feeling like a gimped down warriors games, but at least everyone has a unique moveset.Stages:Let's just say the maps are tiny which is unfortunate because I prefer the regular sized maps in other warrior games, but it fits thematically with the story. What do I mean by this? basically the characters are tasked to go to a certain point in a battle to make sure history is on the right course, so it makes sense that they aren't partaking in the full battle, but small skirmishes here and there.But thats all I have to say, if you are a fan of both go for it, if not than skip.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good introduction to musuo if a gamer is interested. Definitely 100% geared toward Touken Ranbu fans and doesn't compare to other titles in its niche genre. I don't fully agree with the AAA price, but I don't regret the purchase either although it lacks content as well as varying play-styles per character. The story kept me engaged but it does seem monotonous with its missions ( which are very short and not difficult to accomplish even on 'Hard Mode' ). It's been a fun, casual, experience so far. Try to grab it on sale if you're interested.

_childDocuments_.review: HEADS UP. If you're here for Warriors type of gameplay, this won't be the game for you. I'm saying that now as a Tourabu fan and Warriors fan.It's a good game. I enjoy the story and the investigation aspect of it, especially as a long-time Saniwa. But while the gameplay is enjoyable, it is not something that will tickle the brain of a Warriors player. Proof of this is that I had to set up the game to its highest difficulty and still find the game too easy. I enjoy the stylish combos and the idea of pairing up the swords and them getting combos together the more they gain trust. I do wish there's still the smithing and sword break system just to raise the stakes, or other little things from the OG game like the tantos being better at night combat but weaker on broad daylight against heavily armored enemies on the battlefield, but that'd be too complicated I guess.Overall, I'd still recommend this game, especially for fans of Touken Ranbu or are interested in Touken Ranbu. If you're here thinking of getting a Samurai or Dynasty Warriors type of gameplay this might not satisfy you.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good warriors game.Pros:1. Great battle flow, dodge can be used at any time, enemy attacks are telegraphed very well2. Very detailed design of playable characters3. Good performance, no lags or invisible enemies that didn't have time to render yetCons:1. Small maps2. All battles are linear instead of having a choice of several objectives that you can complete3. All enemies are plain4. For some reason there are 4 different resources which drop at the same place and used to upgrade skills, could have used just one5. No post game (after story completion there is only grind for some achievements left, no extra challenges or modes and there aren't even stats that track which levels you completed on which difficulty so no reason to replay most missions the second time)6. No info about characters (for someone who knows nothing about Touken Ranbu universe it was frustrating to find out that I can't read any info about playable characters in game encyclopedia because it simply doesn't exist)Basically to implement enjoyable battles some things like larger scale and higher variety of enemies (there are no detailed enemy characters, only bugs and plain samurai) had to be sacrificed. I am fine with this sacrifice and enjoyed playing the game. Story was completed in about 20 hours, 10 more hours to complete all tasks (first warriors game that I 100%), 10 more for idling. _childDocuments_.review: I’ve played a lot of Musou games - some good, some bad, most mediocre, but this one might just be the worst yet.Touken Ranbu Warriors is another one of those spin-off Musou games like Persona 5 Strikers, Hyrule Warriors, etc. This time though, it’s based on the Touken Ranbu series, a free to play browser game VERY popular with the female demographic. I have never played the original game, but I have seen both anime adaptations, so I was already familiar going into this one. What I was met is the worst Musou experience I have had yet and I had originally planned to give this game a full review, but honestly, it was a struggle to even play as far as I did, so I gave up on that idea.It’s not even like the combat was that bad. I mean, Musou games aren’t known for their revolutionary combat, but the combat here is at least par for the course. It’s more so the egregious level design, mission structure, and repetition that brought this one down.For example, the first handful of missions - you’re just fighting skeletons. An hour later? More skeletons. A few hours later? Skeletons, but with some humanoid ones too. What makes this worse is that each level is the most small and linear thing ever. Gone are the usual large, open, or interconnected environments of most Musou games and here we get maybe a few open areas connected by short paths. You can walk across most levels in seconds and this extends into the actual playtime of those missions as well.The vast majority of the missions have you go to an area, take down a strong enemy, go to the next area, take down the same enemy, and repeat until it is over. It takes maybe a few minutes max to do this, but sometimes the game purposefully blocks you from completing the missions that fast and forces you to use your animal sidekick to “analyze” the environment. This usually requires you to wait around for that to complete or to plow through another ten or so waves of identical enemy types before the analysis reaches 100% and you can finally finish the mission.The entire thing just lacks substance, more so than the usual for this series and it’s not helped here by the fact that you spend more time looking at menus and loading animations than actual gameplay. In-between missions you get the boring, lengthy dialogue scenes too, not helped by how “samey” a lot of the Touken Ranbu characters come off as here.So I can’t say I had a good time with this one. Granted, maybe it improves later on, but I am hours into it and it’s hardly done anything at all to hold my interest enough to finish it for a full review. Maybe if you’re a diehard Touken Ranbu fan, but even then, this is a tough one to recommend at all.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: Key obtained via Keymailer for streaming purposes.Touken Ranbu Warriors tries to be dynasty warriors without the grand battles.making the combat rather simplistic and dull in doing so.in short, it acts like a dynasty warriors game but thus far i have only been given linear maps that last 5 to 10minutes each. haven't been able to select what characters i want to play with outside of the tutorial.the characters for that matter are dull. only 3 or 4 of them are relatively interesting in design. all others are fashion boys that would not know a thing about battle. but alas this is what we get to choose from.the combat wants to be dynasty warriors, but you don't get the button combination skills. if anything i always feel like the "strong" skill is random or something.instead of a musou you now have a special,a partner combo and a partner execution.all pretty obsolete as you pretty much steam roll though the early part of the game.like i mentioned the missions are short, almost uninspired as i never felt the enemies were able to do their objectives and on top of that. you're in the menu longer than the combat lasts.the game tries to be dynasty warriors with you beating lots of enemies. but non of that matters as the only thing u got to fight are the captains. there's no benefit in beating small fries. there is no upgrade systems for weapons, the only thing u do is strenghten your character that you use. the resources required are only obtained in the dojo or whatever u call it.the relationship between the characters and "bonds" you make with them all feel lackluster.in all honesty. it's an ok hack n slash but don't expect much.i would rather play the old dynasty warriors games. it would definitely be more enjoyable for my viewers to watch. i'll tell ya that.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very pretty game with very pretty characters, and it plays really well for a rather dumbed-down Musou/Warriors experience. Its presentation is generally nice, and it has a lot of options that are very pleasing visually, and I'm sure nice sounds, if you care at all about the series or the game it came from.That said, Touken Ranbu is just a stupid series that's badly-written, and it makes it really hard to tolerate the frankly too-short levels. It's not worth replaying them, because they're so short and limited. And the writing is so bad that the premise becomes one you don't want to believe in...which is made even worse by the characters hamfistedly bringing up abhorrent things they're doing that will probably cause all kinds of deaths and suffering of innocent people. So...why bring it up and make the audience think about how unsympathetic and monstrous these characters they're being forced to play are? And oh yes, there are required loadouts, meaning you aren't going to be playing the characters you want, most of the time.There's also the always-annoying and very East Asian writing tactic of "there must be order"/"things must be returned to how they were, and we're not even going to entertain that changing them might be correct" -- lazy writing, and unpleasantly authoritarian in the most grandiose of ways. It's boring to be that jackass, and furthermore, it's usually vile and shows a tremendous lack of...sentience, really, or any sense of what's right or wrong.The DLC is obscenely overpriced, and it doesn't add all that much unless you're a super Touken Ranbu otaku. This doesn't even have most of the more interesting characters in it. Maybe a handful of the characters in this are interesting enough to look at for countless tiny stages, but they're sure not worth the asking price for the game, much less the DLC.I can't even really recommend this on sale. It's just vile, and it's Warriors For Dummies. They should have just made basically a hamster cage for these stupid characters, so fans could just have them to play with and didn't have to go through the clearly superfluous part of playing an action game to interact with them. This was a Warriors game made for people who don't play Warriors games and will never play any other Warriors game. It might work in Japan, for super-fans, but it doesn't work anywhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: For most people, you're better off looking up porn of a tomboy and a twink. Just look up 2B x 9S from Nier Automata or Armin x Annie from that trash Japanese cartoon. I got this game because I am a fan of the Warrior series, and I thought it was hilarious that the cast was mostly comprised of twinks. We thought we were going to have a good time, expecting a typical Warriors game that was even more over the top. That was a mistake. Saying that it is for casuals and that criticisms should be disregarded because of that is a bad mindset. Animal Crossing, Stardew Valley, and even The Sims are for casuals, and they are way better than Touken Ranbu Warriors.The best thing about this game was the story. _childDocuments_.review: I find a lot of talk about Touken Ranbu Musou is phrased as "This game is a bad Musou but it's not for Musou fans, it's for TR fans," as if those two things are mutually exclusive and that TR fans just deserve bad games. This notion is gibberish and is blatant infantilization. As if TR players are incapable of engaging in art that respects their time, money, and ability to understand basic functions of the medium they're acting in. I'm not certain if this PC port is just awful or if there's a problem w/ the game's compatibility w/ my machine. The game runs like complete hog. My solution was to turn the game's graphical setting to high (There's no other forme of graphical adjustments) and that solved the problem half the time. The game was still dipping frames often and otherwise running badly. I understand that TRM is originally a Switch game (I finished the Switch version last year; the game ran fine); I find it quite hard to believe this port could be in such rudimentary states. If anything, it's biting commentary on how infantile the rest of the game is. TRM thinks its audience is too stupid to follow basic game mechanics thus must stop you every single time a boss is vulnerable, attacking, and really just existing (This includes every single repeat fight). Almost every single mission is riddled w/ cutscenes pointing the way to the next objective despite the map design being circles and corridors leading to either new circles or new squares, of which there is never any sort of deviation in areas to "explore." There're investigation missions, most of which just involve running to a spot and killing an enemy. Which is already 97% of the game, so what's being investigated here must be the air if anything. There's the obligatory modern action game stealth missions that are bad thanks to being banal and pathetically easy. There's no sense of danger or intrigue, partially because Konnosuke won't shut up and stop telling the player where to go and mostly because there's literally no way you can get lost or not find what you're supposed to do instantly. For a Musou, it sure is pathetic that this game doesn't have a block. Another crime From Software will have to pay for. This is particularly egregious given that TR and Sengoku Musou could easily be married together w/ nary a forethought. The human enemies sure love to poke and prod their way out of combos in a game w/ no way to counter their nonsense. Luckily, the game is badly designed and the launch skill (Recycled regular special for every character btw) is so absurdly broken that you can trap most enemies in a juggled state till they fall down. Luckily again, the launch skill is a pick-up so you can just keep spamming launch. There are only four combos for every character, all of which are reused for skills. There are only four unique skills that are not tied to combos, although this does mean that the default combo tree ends at 4 regular attacks and 1 special input. How anyone thought this was a good idea is beyond me. I've never really felt that Musou is repetitive, simply due to the fact the games are usually trying to be engaging, although this game's lack of content and lack of basic combat systems present since the beginning of the franchise makes me understand the accusations of vapidity.  How OF has gotten away w/ publishing the most cynical and lazy products this side of Namco Bandai I'm not certain, though given that they think a few recycled costumes from the browser game and some backgrounds for the honmaru are worth 110 USD, I'm sure no one thought to begin w/. Of course, the base price of 60 USD is a buffoon's gambit to keep the sales low. There's very little content in this game. The pacing is breakneck until the game thinks you're too stupid to understand what red means. Missions take upwards of 5 minutes max, there's barely more than 100 enemies in a map total, and there's no side content outside of tedious, worthless mini-games. No side content in a game that asks 110 USD for some ugly tracksuits and a night theme for a building the characters don't do anything in. My gamer qualifications, in case any obnoxious pedant reads this, for this rant are that I play TR and I play a lot of Musou. More than most people (This is a cry for help, aye). Bad game but I would do anything for Yamanbagiri Kunihiro, so really who's the biggest fool here?

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally leave bad reviews, because all games have their good points. And this game isn't half-bad in some areas. If you're looking for a casual Warrior's game, this is a great one to try out. Especially for new people to the series (like me) and don't like getting invested in long battles. BUT, specifically because of how expensive this game is--DO NOT BUY. This is a gross attempt at getting fans to pay full price for a game that isn't even a full game. The DLC is laughable. You get 6 new backgrounds, a few BGM tracks, and one new outfit for the 15 characters in the game. For $30 dollars. It's pretty blatantly trying to get money from fans, and I can't recommend a game that does this kind of marketing tactic. I do love this game, as I'm am a huge fan of TouRan, and love that we finally have a TouRan game with 3D models that have their own unique attacks. But it's just not a very deep game to justify a $70 price point. Only buy this when it's on sale. NEVER buy the DLC. I hope Mikazuki Munechika never drops in the actual TouRan game for you, if you are foolish enough to actually buy the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Touken Ranbu Warriors was an interesting game in that I have little confidence these days in warriors/musou style games, they seem to be a dying art that misses the point, playing legendary warriors who take out many opponents and fighting other legendary warriors in combat, Touken Ranbu is kind kind of that yet more in a style of warriors game that I'm more than happy I bought, in fact it's a game I hope turns into a game series one day, with unique mechanics to the style of game, the balancing, the detail to characters and bonds all make for a fun, if you're a warriors fan it's just enough to be right up your ally and yet adds that bit more to be itself dood.Okay onto the meat of the game, TRW is a game based in 2205! What? That doesn't sound right? Did I put the wrong number in? Nope 2205! And you play as a group of legendary swords of past owned by generals and warriors of Japan but given human form, to what end you ask? To go back to the past and fix anomalies, now how's that for a crazy plot point dood?The game plays much like warriors games, you kill little units who are fodder as we all want in these games, generals who are tougher but here's the thing, they are part of a group known as the HRA (History Retrograde Army) the main antagonists of the game, these creatures are pretty much just straight up demons and vary in size, species and battle capabilities making for some interesting combat at times dood.As for how the player fights? We have our usual Square/X button mashing as is the usual for these games but Y/Triangle? Rather than a heavy attack it turns into a special, here's the thing though, if you use Y then it's tied to what hit in a combo you use, Y alone will be a straight attack, X then Y will be a ranged attack and then as you level up your characters with materials you will get even more still among other perks, then of course you have the warriors staple special attack, for the longest while these have always felt too weak but in these kinds of games, at most taking out a basic general in one if you're lucky, here it does some nice damage, over a wide range at that so you can hit multiple generals and it works for a game like this where it's not your typical warriors game dood.Of course there's a bit more combat wise as you have a teammate but they don't fight with you...and yet they do! It's a funny mechanic really, press the R2 button and you call your partner to use a special attack with you, then for a while they also fight with you too, makes up at least a little for no co-op although that said with how the game works I feel that's a good thing, I will get to that in the next paragraph though, for now finally you also have L2 which puts you into an invulnerable, faster state, you can end it and save meter if you want or you can press B/Circle as you would for the special to perform a big combo special, that said that will drain your meter, it also activates automatically if the meter runs out dood.So as for the game flow, now as usual of course you kill generals but there are also kind of investigation elements to the game, they are mostly simple, kill a certain enemy first, go to this area that's hidden or out of the way and fill up the % meter to 100% get this person here safely ect ect, there are even stealth sections to the game which you'd think is off putting but as a master of being found like myself even I could do it so no worries there, of course there are also just straight up beat the enemy missions but the point is it's nice to vary up the gameplay in this way and fits the whole feel and aim of the story and what the protags do dood.The games not really all that difficult, in fact I would suggest playing on hard if you feel confident, I think once in the game I went down to half health and even then it was because I was being risky, I barely saw the clothes breaking mechanics even which is a nice detail, it's great to see a game that does it with males for once XD especially if you're into that kind of thing :p although mostly it's actually just cool looking rather than anything perverse, some scarring, torn clothes and a more muddied look as though you just took a beating, it's an awesome detail I saw maybe 6-7 times at most dood.The music and the visuals are both super nice, especially the character designs, it's rare for me to find a game with multiple characters where I like pretty much every character, only one didn't really vibe with me visually or as a person but that's just a preference thing, the maps are smaller than your standard warriors game affair but not to it's detriment seeing as just imagine trying to investigate and failing it only to start over on a huge map, it uhhh would be grating to say the least haha but they do a great job of using what space they do have with blocked path's secret paths and enemies appearing in other places and such to still make it feel like a fun time dood.Things they could improve? Let's see some side missions to pad out how much there is would be a nice start, sure it says 37 hours but to note I have a bunch of stuff more I need to do but there's no benefit to replaying older levels again and despite doing my best to max out certain things using the base as best I could everyone still needs their bonds maxed out, if I wanted to max characters levels and skill trees out it will take me a long while longer too and I'm happy to do it granted but it's gonna feel stale to do, that and well most warriors games go on longer anyway, there's a lot of history to draw from and okay sure this is it's own condensed story so to speak but for the style of game more would have been nice dood.Another thing they could fix is the fact that you play as teams per chapter which means they limit who you play as, on random occasion they let you choose peeps outside of the team and replaying missions let's you use anyone but to progress typically you will play as 2-4 people who are with you, this could have been mitigated with a much larger final chapter though but it's about as long as the rest of them sadly or barely a bit more maybe for reasons I can't say dood.Oh before I forget, each character has their own playstyle and attacks to them and there are I suppose three? Kinds of weapon, you have your typical Katana/samurai sword, you have the smaller variety you usually see people commit Sepaku with or that ninja's are usually shown having and then you have Naginata/polearms, it's not the most varied but even so the variety of how they fight makes up for that dood.That's all I got to say I guess, honestly it was a pleasant surprise to enjoy this so much, the fixes could easily be implemented in a second game, you even get mini-games that reward you to play at home base I forgot to mention, they have a lot for a warriors game honestly in some ways despite being shorter than a normal one, if you're a fan of these style of games I suggest it but if you're looking for something a bit different then I suggest it even more, I hope this review helps you decide and thank you for reading dood ^-^

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Touken Ranbu fan in me is immensely happy, but this game leaves a lot to be desired.Pros- Controls are decent, not the most intuitive, but good enough.- Characterizations and writing were handled quite well. I enjoy the combinations of sword interactions that aren't possible in the browser game.- Photo mode lets me get up close and personal.- Bond system gives me instant serotonin- Minigames. that's itCons- Gameplay feels very simplistic. I get it's an entry level warriors game since it adapts a joseimuke autobattler, but did hard mode need to be this easy? I appreciate the inclusion of easy mode, but hard mode wasn't hard at all. Something for the hack-and-slash crowd and warriors enjoyers would have been nice. I came from a different hack-and-slash series and this was my first Warriors game, and I know enough to tell this isn't probably the best entry point.- What's the deal with the camera, why does it keep wanting to correct itself (I have auto-locking turned off)- Mouse mode and controller mode are simultaneous instead of toggled between one or the other- SO THE ENEMY CAN PARRY BUT WE CAN'T?A good buy if you're a fan of tkrb like me, can't say much about it otherwise. I'm still giving it a recommendation, since it does the source material enough justice to be a good introduction to Touken Ranbu. Get it for the sword boys, if anything.

name: Spidersaurs
detailed_description: Alert! Alert! The nightmarish dinosaur-spider hybrids known as Spidersaurs have run amok and only you (and a friend in co-op mode) can stop them! Created by InGest Corp to provide the meat and muscle that humanity needs to end world hunger, the Spidersaurs are now on the loose, leaving it to two former taste-testers – officer-in-training Adrian and punk-rocker Victoria – to use their awesome firepower to overcome six stages of ferocious run-'n'-gun action. Blast through a sweltering jungle, an infested laboratory, the heart of a live volcano, and more! The tangy food source with a bite is biting back, but by grabbing power-ups, gaining new abilities, and obliterating everything in sight, you can send these mutant monstrosities back to the stone age. Key Features: • Intense, Saturday-morning-cartoon-style action for one or two players — complete with theme song and epic intro from Powerhouse Animation! • Two distinct playable characters: punk rocker Victoria and officer-in-training Adrian! • Unleash awesome firepower — everything from spread guns and lasers to detonating footballs and bass-heavy electronica! Twelve weapons in all! • Explosive environments including volcanoes, jungles, laboratories, and more! • A menagerie of unique and terrifying Spidersaurs to battle! • Unlock new abilities as you advance through the InGest Corp facility! • Three difficulty settings: Well Done, Medium, and Rare! • Unlockable arcade mode and speedrun mode!

_childDocuments_.review: Whaaat the heck has happened with WayForward?The Shantae games are my favorite from WayForward games and Shantae: Half-Genie Hero was what I consider peak WayForward. It was fun with great graphics, gameplay and story. When I think of WayForward, I think of Shantae. So it's obvious that they've spent a lot of time, money and effort into making Half-Genie Hero. But... ever since that highly successful game, it seems like they are like a lost puppy that can't find its home. In other words, they can't find the right way to move forward.So they started milking Half-Genie Hero with DLCs (ok that was expected), but then continued to produce smaller scale games that are like OK-ish and prioritize apple store (of all the possible places!) as their prime platform of choice. What a let down.And then we're at that point where we have Spidersaurs. OK, it's meh at most. Probably my biggest issues is with controls. It's not that they're bad. It's that they could've been much better. Like using the right stick for pointing and shooting with RT for example. Instead, you need to press a button to stop moving, aim with a stick and then shoot with another button! What the hell are they thinking?!? It's so uncomfortable. On top of that, they introduce more mechanics later in the game. Then there's the spread gun. You know how it's the best one in Contra? Well, they made sure it's the worst one here. Also, some of the other weapons are also bad. Then, there's the story. It's.... there. It wasn't able to grab me at all. You see, the game is more of an arcade-style game, where you constantly move forward. But they decided to carry the dialogue system of Shantae, which was a completely different game than this. So it doesn't work here. Then, there are these characters. Unlike Shantae, these doesn't resonate with the player. Then there are the graphics. You can kinda feel some of the Shantae touches here and there, but overall they're not even close to Half-Genie Hero. The music also not that inspiring. I dunno.I tried to find more things I like in this one, but overall, it's such a let down. I hope the downhill stops here and they begin making great games again.
_childDocuments_.name: Spidersaurs

_childDocuments_.review: A new run 'n gun from the makers of Contra 4? This has gotta be awesome, right? Not quite. First off, there are no resolution options.  For me, at least, the game launches at 720p and stays there. It's also locked at 60 fps. There are actually no graphics options whatsoever that I could see. It's pretty jarring to see this nowadays. As far as the game goes, it's not a good run 'n gun.The weapons are really meh and not fun to use, the enemies and levels are generic, and there just isn't much to like here. It's also not hard. Instead, it's cheap. It's very frequently impossible to not take damage depending on your positioning. There are times where you'll fall and respawn in a position where you can't not get hit. Levels require memorization due to how certain enemies will almost definitely hit you if you don't already know where they are. And the only checkpoints are at the midpoint, meaning you have to play the second part of the levels over and over to memorize them and take less damage. It's super doable, but it's also super boring. Shooting the spider-dinosaurs just isn't entertaining.  I'm very disappointed in this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Spidersaurs

_childDocuments_.review: If you want Contra mixed with saturday morning cartoons then look no further! Spidersaurs is going to scratch that itch. Even if you are looking for an incredible run 'n gun game, Spidersaurs is a great addition. Contra 4 was released on the Nintendo DS in 2007. The foundation that game set is seen here and a lot of the mechanics seen there are transferred and build upon in Spidersaurs. The added content makes Spidersaurs more "full" than it's Apple Arcade release. The new ending, stages, and enemies are a welcomed addition. There are also two new modes added. Arcade mode and speedrun mode. Arcade mode is all thriller no filler. The cut scenes are removed and abilities are unlocked in order. Speedrun mode is self-explanatory except all abilities are unlocked out of the gate. I completed story mode with both characters, Victoria and Adrian, Victoria is more adept and controlling the screen and can make ease of enemies while never stopping. Her arsenal helps cover wide areas of the screen. Adrian is a powerhouse with his arsenal. While he does have some screen covering weapons, they are nowhere near as helpful as Vicotrias. The flamethrower (upgraded) is probably the best weapon for stages while his exploding football makes a lot of the bosses trivial. If you are looking something to play with a friend or continue your love for 80's/90's vibes then this is perfect. There are three adjustable difficulties so don't feel intimated or deflated when  individuals compare this to Contra. This game is much more welcoming!
_childDocuments_.name: Spidersaurs

_childDocuments_.review: A charming blend of Contra and Saturday-morning-cartoon tropes made by the developer of the amazing Contra 4 (NDS, 2007). It's not as good as this or the classic Contra games, but a well-made and fun substitute. It offers a story mode with a save function and three difficulty settings as well as two unlockable modes (arcade and speedrun) that you have to beat in one sitting. Please more short and dense arcade-style action platformers like this!
