_childDocuments_.review: Contra-lite?Spidersaurs is a run & gun in the vein of Contra. The similarities are so apparent that you could say it's Wayforward's own Contra game but without the Contra license. Originally released for Apple Arcade, Wayforward have decided to bring Spidersaurs to PC and consoles.There are multiple abilities that you have in Spidersaurs that are carried over from Contra but you cannot go prone here. Instead you are able to crouch and shoot. Some of your abilities will be unlocked as you beat levels. Controls feel very similar to Hard Corps Uprising so those that have played that game will feel right at home. Like the grappling hook in Contra 4, here there is a web-line move that allows you to zip upwards. It does have some original ideas like the stomp move that allows you to stomp the ground or thrust downwards with an attack in mid-air. There are two playable characters (Victoria and Adrian) but here, although the same weapon pickups are available, your weapon will differ depending on which character you are playing. For example if you pick up the spread weapon with Victoria it will function similar to the Contra series but with Adrian he will fire a single projectile that will split apart on impact and bounce off surfaces in multiple directions. Victoria will will be the most familiar to Contra veterans. Adrian, whilst he has short-range attacks, will pack a wallop when he hits so the differences between the selectable characters are welcome. Weapon pods will fly on to the screen for you to shoot and release the weapon pickups. Weapons can be upgraded if you collect multiple pickups of the same weapon.  You are able to carry two weapons in total and switch between them freely.  Each character has 3 hit points. If you are hit whilst you have an upgraded weapon equipped then it will be automatically downgraded. If you die then you will lose your equipped weapon and it will revert to the starting weapon.In addition to the weapon pods there are the Fire, Rain and Flash pods that you can shoot which will basically clear the screen of enemies somewhat.  You choose which of these 3 pods you want to appear in the level before you start.Enemies attack from all angles and weapon choice will make the game easier or harder. Level designs feature a mostly left-to-right approach but some have some verticality and there are some auto-scroll sections thrown in for good measure plus a short "vehicle" section. The game offers a little challenge especially for those not familiar with the genre but nowhere near Contra-hard and most genre veterans will likely find the game to be relatively easy. It actually might be a good first-time run and gun game for new players. Boss battles are quite fun to play, as are learning their attack patterns. Co-op will increase enjoyment somewhat as well.Once you complete the game then there are both an Arcade Mode and Speedrun Mode that are unlocked for those that just want to get straight into gameplay and don't care about story. In Arcade Mode you unlock abilities at the same pace that you do in Story Mode. In Speedrun Mode all your abilities are unlocked from the start. However, in these modes you have to complete the game in one sitting (although you still have infinite continues in Arcade Mode and none in Speedrun Mode). Speedrun Mode has another advantage and that's that you will have all your abilities unlocked from the beginning of the game which increases enjoyment somewhat. It will make the game slightly easier but at the same time you have no continues to fall back on which offsets this. All modes feature 3 difficulty settings.Music is adequate but unfortunately also quite forgettable. It's not particularly bad but I can't remember a single track from the game (other than perhaps the mission select music for some reason) unless I've just played it which isn't a good sign.  There is a fully voice-acted story too but it does feel very weak. Story dialogue will differ depending on who you play as. Weapon sound effects don't really have enough pop and just make them feel a bit insubstantial.The game has an anime-inspired art-style and is extremely colourful which may sometimes make it hard to spot different hazards or projectiles. Some of the art on display here would not look out of place in a cartoon. Admittedly the colourful, detailed backgrounds look great on the different stages. However, with the HD sprites some of the simple animations don't look right and could use some added frames. Also quite a few animations looked tweened instead of frame-by-frame which is a little off-putting as it makes some movements look a little stiff. This is mostly apparent on bosses. I did play the Cuphead DLC not that long before playing this game so it's possible that may have skewed my opinion but I was never expecting Cuphead levels of animation here anyway. I know Wayforward are capable of much better in this department so not sure why this approach was taken. Perhaps due to budgetary constraints but the animation woes become a little more understandable knowing that it was originally a mobile title.The game is very short even for the genre. This could be due to the game's mobile origins. There are only 6 levels but that includes a very short tutorial stage and the final level which is little-more than a boss battle. In fact even if you combined the tutorial level and the final stage, the resulting stage would still feel short.A couple of other gripes I have is that firstly I had to edit an .ini file in order to adjust the resolution and secondly you have to move the mouse cursor off-screen in order to hide it. Both things that really should have been available in-game by default.Tip: For resolution options go to \AppData\Roaming\Wayforward\Spidersaurs and open and edit  wfEngine.ini.Lastly (another nitpick) the controls assume you are using a PlayStation controller no matter what you are using.I had a more annoying issue on the jungle level at the start of the run & gun section, where there is a thin, black horizontal line that will appear somewhere on the the screen. At first I thought it was just visible texture seams but honestly I'm not so sure. I tested this when playing at a few different resolutions and it happened in every playthrough. I've noticed these lines appear in a couple of other stages too.The last thing I should mention is that there seems to be a weird bug where the game seems to hover at 59 fps as opposed to a solid 60 fps. I have reached out to Wayforward support about both these issues but have yet to get any response. Realistically I'm not expecting any of these issues to be addressed as Wayforward's River City Girls which was far more successful is still laden with bugs years after release so keep that in mind.  Overall it's an OK (but not great) game in the genre. It borrows so heavily from Contra but for some reason still doesn't manage to hit the same highs. This could be partially due to it's Apple Arcade origins. It is however a fun little distraction if you enjoy these types of games. It's definitely far less successful as a modern run & gun than Blazing Chrome, Cuphead or Super Cyborg (easier and shorter than them too) but still worth adding to your library if you enjoy the genre or if you are starting out in the genre. Hopefully Wayforward can give it another try and make improvements in a potential sequel (preferably one with a bigger budget and not targeted at mobile gamers). Mildly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Was highly anticipating this one to come to other platforms when it was revealed, happy to have it finally. Still pretty early on in play time but it maintains the good ol Wayforward charm and humor in the writing and character designs (shoutouts to Victoria and Sorez). as far as the genre goes, my experience has only been with the 2 Gunstar Heroes games really, and even then very recently, but I have as much fun with this one. _childDocuments_.review: Great idea, great style, excellent opening tune... Absolutely atrocious game play. So incredibly clunky, aiming is too rigid and enemies are always in "dead zones". _childDocuments_.review: First they put snakes on a plane, then they put sharks in a tornado,and now with advances in 90's cartoon technology they've put spiders into dinosaurs or is it the other way around?I think Spidersaurs is a good yet flawed game. I don't think it's the next great Run N gun game, orthat it elevates the genre but It does have a nice presentation and solid gameplay with a lot of reply value for such a short game.I once rented out a saxophone during high school band.The Sax had many issues with the keys, and some pads that didn't seal properly.I just got used to it and was able to find workarounds, yet, when I had the instrument inspected by a private instructor,she questioned why I didn't get the pads and keys fixed... My special fixes, didn't impress her. She said that despite the fact that I had found a way to workaround the problem, didn't change the fact that the Saxophone still had core issues.Just like in this game. I have found ways to workaround most of the issues I'm going to mention about the game, buteven though I have taken troubleshooting steps and got gud, the game still has core problems.There are some really strange decisions in this game.You design a piercing shot that upgrades to a wave, but then you design small,turret like dinos that are hard to hit cause the shot waves over them.You have tanky enemies where you have to position your character and shoot them for a while, butif you stand still too long you have an enemy that sneaks up behind you and has almost no telegraph andit's random. This is a PC port and there are no graphic settings and no controller vibration,or in depth resolution settings. The tutorial stage is underwhelming and has to be played every time you start a game,this is a step back, it shows that you don't know your audience...or underestimate them...Also the stage is boring, add more enemies, some explosions, something to make the player excited about what they're about to play. One of my biggest issues with the game is the weapon caches that fly into the screen. There's no way of knowing what weapon it is until you shoot it and it falls to the ground. They fall in awkward places. A good run N gun gives you powerups before bosses, or in between areas. giving you enough space andtime to get the powerups you want. It is so annoying in games where the items designed to make your character stronger, becomes another obstacle for you to avoid. it's really bad on some of the auto scrollers and some areas where I just have to guess what weapon it is or memorize which drops I pick up.       All you have to do to fix 90% of this issue, is to show what weapon is going to drop in advance so I know which ones I want to shoot.If you like Run N Gun games, play this, it's great and has all the right moves. It gets better as you get better. but as much as I respect Wayforward, and the great retro-style games they attempt to make. I Don't love all of them. In fact there is always something in every Wayforward game that just falls short. Shante is really cool premise and great game concept, but it has some issues that make the game scenarnio hard to navigate.       The ducktales game was almost perfect but had that one ending section that was a bit overdesigned. Spidersaurs is a also a great concept that is so close to being great but is hindered by a bunch of issues. I look forward, way-forward, to the time when this talented company will make it's masterpiece. It will be a glorious day for all gamers and indie devs everywhere.I'm sure that such a day will come soon. We just have to wait a little bit longer. For now, I smell my moms bacon and pancakes on Saturday morning, time for breakfast.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good Contra style run'n gun. The controls are spot on, it has good bosses, the music rocks, and it has really nice graphics, even if the Cartoon Network style isn't for me. It's a lot like Contra 3, Contra 4, and Hard Corps Uprising, if you've ever played those. I thought some of the guns were a bit slow, but they all have their uses. There's also strategy to keeping the guns you like on you, just like in every Contra game. There's a good challenge on Normal and Hard difficulties, too, which throw more enemies and faster bosses at you. I've already beat it on Easy and Normal, and I'm working on hard now.The game does give you abilities as you beat the bosses, and I don't really like that, but once you've beaten all the levels in Story, you can go back and replay any levels with all the abilities. That also adds some more replay value. I think the game is a lot more fun with all the abilities.

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels like a cross between Pirate's Curse and Half-Genie Hero. And that's a VERY good thing.Rather than innovation for its own sake, Seven Sirens feels like a natural evolution of the series. Tight controls, good graphics, great voice acting, and that classic sense of humor. It's all here for Shantae fans and fans of metroidvania games.Very much recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played a Shantae game, it's basically Castlevania with half naked women and it's awesome. You can start with this entry, the story is self-contained.Now, about the game itself, I've got to say it's a lot better than , almost as good as . They basically fixed most of the usually cited issues with Half-Genie Hero, namely:- It's now a proper Metroidvania, the world is a single interconnected map, yet there are still boss dungeons and small challenge caves, just like in other Shantae games.- The animal transformations no longer halt the gameplay, you transform instantly based on context, e.g. if you dash in mid air you'll automatically turn into the animal that does this and you'll stay in that form until you hit the ground. You can still dance, but it's used for other things.- While the game recycles a good amount of assets from Half-Genie Hero the graphics are quite a bit better. Seven Sirens has gorgeous 2D backgrounds instead of the ugly low poly 3D ones like in Half-Genie Hero and the character portraits (in dialog scenes) are beautiful.- There are high quality anime scenes done by Studio Trigger (Kill la Kill, Little Witch Academia etc) sprinkled throughout the game.It's not all sunshine and roses though:- They changed the composer (supposedly, Jake Kaufman wasn't available this time), and the music while not bad is nothing to write home about. Some tracks can be catchy, others are more bland and generic.- The difficulty is very casual, you get showered in healing items and gems everywhere you go, the enemies barely do any damage. I maxed out the hair upgrades (both speed and damage) after only one boss.All in all, still highly recommended, for both Shantae fans as well as newcomers. As far as Shantae games go, Seven Sirens is definitely one of the better ones.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the Seven Sirens is the best Shantae game since Pirate's Curse. Almost everything wrong that was in Half-Genie Hero is fixed in this game, and it feels like the proper HD Shantae game that Half-Genie Hero should have been.One of the best things about it is the new fusion transformation system. These transformations work similarly to the pirate gear from Pirate's Curse. Instead of having to stop and dance to transform, they automatically activate with a press of a button. This is by far the best transformation system the series has ever had and I hope they stick with it for the next game. Now that doesn't mean the old dance menu system from Half-Genie Hero has gone away. It's still here in this game but instead of having go through 3 menus of animal transformations that play similar to each other, you now have a single menu that contains 4 transformations that can affect the environment around you. These range from revealing hidden enemies and items in an area to causing earthquakes that can damage enemies nearby and move heavy obstacles out of your way. While the game uses the same engine as Half-Genie Hero, the controls feel a lot tighter this time around. My only issue is that they removed the ability to get down to another platform by pressing down on the d-pad, which was a handy feature in the other games. The level-based structure from the last game is now gone and the interconnected world from the early games is back and it's probably the best one in the series. The dungeons are back too and they're good for the most part. The last two are a bit weak though but still, it's nice to see them back. There are even multiple towns again which the series hasn't had since the original GBC game. The map feature is also back thankfully and man, you're definitely gonna need it for this one. My only issue with it is that it doesn't mark the items you have discovered so trying to get 100% will take a lot of time if you don't have a guide with you. Difficulty-wise though, I think they give you way too many healing items. I never ran out of them due to the game almost constantly dropping them and the fact that you have like 6 or 7 different healing items which get filled up pretty quickly. It's also really easy to get a lot of gems. Hell, I fully upgraded my hair whip by the time I beat the first siren. Pirate's Curse had the best balance in my opinion. Seven Sirens introduces the card system which are basically upgrades that you can equip at any time. Enemies have a chance to drop them when they get killed but there are a few special ones that can be only bought by NPCs in the towns. The maximum amount you can equip at once is 3 which sounds fair but honestly it can be a bit annoying just to go to the card menu screen to equip another card just for one specific situation and then having to go back to the menu to use the one you had before. I think there should have been a card that increases drop chance which would make grinding for them to be less tedious.  Now the music on the other hand, isn't quite as good as the previous games. This is due to Jake Kaufman not being available to work on the soundtrack this time so WayForward had to get someone else to do it. The soundtrack was composed by Kentaro Sakamoto, Mark Sparling, Madeline Lim and Gavin Allen. Some of the new tracks are nice and catchy, but there are others that are pretty bland and unmemorable. The story itself is alright and a lot more focused than Half-Genie Hero's. It does enough to keep you engaged and the dialogue is still really funny and charming. There are also new fully animated cutscenes which look great but the voice acting isn't quite the best. The new characters are great too but I wish they expanded upon them further. Risky didn't really change that much in terms of character development but at least she appears a lot more often. I just hope they develop the characters more in the next game and explain what happened to Shantae's mother and the other genies.Visually, the game looks as good as Half-Genie Hero, if not better. The character sprites are reused but the 3D polygonal models in the environments have been replaced by high resolution 2D art backgrounds and they're quite beautiful. The art-style of the character portraits have been changed again and they look fantastic this time. I had no crashes during gameplay but for some reason the game would always crash every time I exited the game. Not that big of a deal though since I didn't lose any progress. The game runs fine but the loading times can be a bit long however so I hope that gets fixed in a future update. Overall, Seven Sirens is a return to form for the series and I would highly recommend it. It does have a few issues but they don't bring down the game that much.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually write reviews after I've played games for good amounts of time, but I just feel like I need to write a review for this now, to clear up misconceptions and help you decide whether to buy this game or not. I noticed a handful of people either saying that this is their favorite game, or that this is the worst Shantae game. Why such polar opposites? Let's find out.Shantae is on another adventure this time. And with some actual story. True, Shantae games are not story focused, but having some substance there is good. This game goes back to its roots, the exploration a la metroid, unlike half genie hero, which was more of a platformer and less of a metroidvania. The gameplay revolves around you using your brain and fingers to press buttons, and Shantae destroying stuff with magic, or hair, or cute animal transformations.- Vast, colorful world full of life- Responsive controls- The instant transformations are cool, mostly fun to use and are actually useful in combat- A variety of ways to play thanks to Monster Cards.- Music is nice, considering that Jake Kaufman wasn't here this time. If Jake was a 10/10, the new people who made this OST are about a 8/10 IMO.- There is Squid Baron (certified 4th wall breaker)- There is Squidsmith- Tons of beautiful girls, and monstergirls. Self-explanatory.- Long loading times- There are A LOT of collectibles, but the map doesn't show them, and some are very difficult to find unless you're Sherlock Holmes, or a game designer. At least a counter to show what can be collected in each area would be nice.- The difficulty is non-existent, thanks to overabundance of food/healing. (you can also not use food if you want a challenge, but I still think of this as a con of sorts).I could end the review here, but I would like to address the most common complaints and see if they are legit complaints, or just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ statements coming from angry, mentally challenged attention seekers.This is a matter of personal preference. I can understand why someone wouldn't like it. But I think it is quite good actually. Truth be told, a track or two do feel like they have too much chiptune going on, but it's not bad. Now, if you are someone who listens to ♥♥♥♥♥♥ nightcore remixes on youtube, and you claim this OST is objectively bad, please shut the ♥♥♥♥ up.Hollow knight doesn't have it either, the characters say some gibberish in a language we can't understand, for 1 second, while you need 10 seconds to just skip through dialogue. And that didn't bother me in the slightest. Hell, Pirate's Curse had this too! Not every cake has to have walnuts if you like walnuts. It's not a bad cake without them, nor is it a better one with them. Classic example of nitpicking. Or... nutpicking. i know i am very funny yesThis is true. You will have enough food to feed an entire continent, and this nice difficulty curve the game had was ruined by overabundance of healing. There are some tough and highly damaging enemies, and even with magic cost reduction, your magic bar depletes rather quickly when using a fully upgraded spell. All that good stuff, rendered pointless because what's the point if you can just heal it all up? At least I think it's not too hard to fix. Now, Shantae games have always been on the easy (easier) side to be fair, and the only way to raise difficulty in them is to limit your item usage options, or upgrades. Which is good, but as stated earlier, I still think of it as a con of sorts.Yes. Please fix those WayForward. If this was fixed, the game would be MUCH more enjoyable to play, even a patient man like me doesn't like these loading times.I am managing to find most stuff without too much issue, but I agree that there are way too many of them, and a map would certainly help, because some collectibles are just hidden in the stupidest of places. Completely valid point. Hell, I may need a map myself!While this game does contain a lot of cleavage, is it really a bad thing? I will quote myself on this one:So, in the end, a good amount of criticism that people have is valid, and I think that, if these issues I addressed earlier in the review were fixed, the game would be an absolute joy to play through. Do I recommend this game? I do, but be prepared for a bit of annoyance in the form of loading times and searching for all the collectibles without much indication of their location. This game feels rushed, which is a shame, so a message for WayForward from me: "Next time, instead of promoting Apple Arcade, promote yourself.", but if they decide to fix some of these problems, it could easily be an 8.5/10 game. Thanks for reading, and hopefully this review helped you.

_childDocuments_.review: The followup to 2016's Half-Genie Hero is finally here and with no crowdfunding necessary. I backed and enjoyed HGH pretty thoroughly, so when I heard this game was going back to Shantae's metroidvania roots with a new interconnected world to explore, needless to say I was pretty hyped. So, how does Shantae's tropical vacation gone wrong live up to expectations?  Shantae and the usual suspects are back and better to look at than ever. While the overworld sprites for both the old and new characters maintain the same style that they had with Half-Genie Hero, the character illustrations for the dialogue are the best they've ever been. Inti Creates has once again flexed as hard as possible to make the characters incredibly cute, fun, and appealing to look at with every moment of dialogue, and that goes double for the new half-genies and bosses. There's also animated cutscenes in this game which is a new for Shantae. The opening animation by Trigger is very fun, and even the fully voiced in-game cutscenes produced by Top Peg and Studio Yotta are charming despite the lack of real lip sync and occasional choppiness. Shantae's brief foray into a level based experience with HGH was shortlived as Seven Sirens brings us back to an open world metroidvania experience that's as tight as ever. The world is a lot of fun to explore and the platforming is smooth and intuitive. The game also has an intuitive warp system which makes traversing the map progressively simpler over time. Despite most of the game taking place below the island's surface in the Sunken City, each area of the game is very distinct in style and maintains a refreshing look as you progress through the game's world and dungeons. With the return of classic dungeons and exploration, Shantae has also reverted to a fully 2D experience. If you were a fan of the 2.5D approach that Half-Genie Hero was experimenting with that had more dynamic backgrounds, you may be disappointed. Shantae and fetch quests are pretty inseparable for better or worse. Thankfully, Seven Sirens saves you a lot of the headache by making the quests a natural progression. When you need to find items to progress the story, they're always in areas you weren't able to reach before because you didn't have the proper upgrades. The game also places NPCs in critical locations that are pretty hard to miss that practically point you in the right direction. Sometime they even give you quest markers on the map! Another short-lived design philosophy from Half-Genie Hero was having your transformation powers be locked to dancing. Seven Sirens has made quick work of that by making your powers and dances two very distinct things. All of your transformation upgrades that provide you with new movement options have very simple keybinds that make the platforming and general movement throughout the world smooth and satisfying. Dances now have their own very specific uses throughout the game that are used to uncover secrets and new locations which makes the upgrades in this game feel double layered, which is nice.  If you were looking for the trademark quirkiness and humor that you expect form every Shantae release, then you won't be disappointed. The writing is still as clever and fun as ever, and the introduction of more colorful characters to the cast rounds this experience out and makes for a lot of fun character dialogue moments from start to finish. There's even a few touching character moments that got a verified "awww" from me. If you liked Giga Mermaid because she was a giant monster girl, you're in luck. This game is very much for you.  Longtime composer Jake Kaufman did not return for the newest Shantae release, reportedly because he was too busy with another project to split his time. Instead, WayForward opted in for Japanese chiptune musician Professor Sakamoto who brought a retro chiptune feel to Shantae's soundtrack. A lot of the tracks are remixes or play on previous Kaufman compositions so there is a bit of callback to the original style, but the fact of the matter is that if you're looking for a classic Shantae soundtrack, you're not going to find it here. I think the soundtrack is good for what it was going for and there were a few tracks that definitely stuck in my mind but it's definitely going to stick out like a sore thumb for you if you're hoping for business as usual. For the audiophiles, prepare yourself as they opted in for 128kpbs lossy audio tracks and that may drive you insane. Here's hoping Kaufman returns for Shantae 6.  If you're looking for a challenge, you're not going to get it playing the game normally. Seven Sirens cannot resist dropping you food items from every other enemy, and the more powerful healing items seem to drop more. You also get money so quickly that buying upgrades takes no time at all. While the bosses are often creative and fun to fight, they are equally easy to defeat and you're probably not going to find much challenge in that department. Any difficulty will have to be self-imposed if you want a challenging experience.  and recycled it into what is known as the Monster Card system in this game. Your mileage may vary on how much you enjoy the addition of this system into the game. Monster Cards can give you nice perks and bonuses to your existing powers but are not essential for getting through the game. Get ready for 100% collection to be a bit of a headache as some enemies only appear in one or two locations throughout the game, and there are even weirder cases like the Jellyfish card which is a pre-requisite for even getting the Pincher card since you can't kill them without it. Thankfully, cards do not actually contribute to the game percentage. If you want to 100% this game, you need to collect all the heart squids and nuggets. There's a handful of both collectibles that are completely hidden and must be revealed with liberal use of the  which is a pain because you have to use it randomly in EVERY room if you want to find all the secrets. It's a bit of a frustrating experience going at it blind, so don't feel bad if you use a guide. I hope they don't rely so much on invisible secrets for the next game. This is a well documented complaint with the game and WayForward is aware of it, but the loading times are bad. I have this game installed on an NVME M.2 and the loading times exceeded 10+ seconds at points. Also, make sure the turn down the priority level of the game process in Task Manager because it will max out your CPU on EVERY level load if you don't. I hope they patch this soon as this is my only big complaint with the game.Shantae and the Seven Sirens is a gratifying metroidvania experience and a must play for longtime fans of the series. While not perfect, it's a worthy entry to the series and I look forward to more of Shantae's adventures in the near future. Even with 100%, you can still complete this game in around 10 hours, so feel free to judge whether that is worth a full price purchase. If not, definitely consider getting it when it goes on sale. Hopefully by then the loading issues will be fixed. Very Yes

_childDocuments_.review: I had very low hopes for this game after I watched gameplay footage of the much rougher Apple Arcade version, but  ended up being my favorite game out of the entire series.Seven Sirens' gameplay is a strange-yet-effective marriage of  and , taking the best elements from both and expanding upon them while throwing away what missed the mark.Like Pirate's Curse, Seven Sirens has action abilities which activate at the tap of a button, meaning no lengthy dancing sequences to use your basic transformations. Like Risky's Revenge, the game world is a large single map of interconnected areas (though the style of the map's design is more evocative of Castlevania, and not Risky's Revenge's awful, super-horizontal layered map).Compared to Half-Genie Hero's laundry list of abilities with limited utility, Seven Sirens trims a lot of fat. You receive only a few passive abilities throughout the game, but they're all immensely helpful in aiding your mobility, offense, and ability to traverse the map. You'll be using all of them frequently for those reasons, but also because they're just satisfying to use; air dashing through enemies as a Newt or bowling through them as a Turtle feels liberating compared to playing as the Monkey or Elephant.Seven Sirens is easily the largest and longest Shantae game yet. My first playthrough clocked in at 9 hours with 66% completion, which is super long compared to its predecessors. If Pirate's Curse or HGH's shorter length and linear formula put you off, Seven Sirens offers slightly more meat in both categories.The production value on Seven Sirens blows every past game out of the water, including Half-Genie Hero. While there is liberal sprite recycling, the character portraits, voice acting, fully-animated cutscenes, and overall scale of Seven Sirens are of a higher quality than any Shantae game before it.If you were a fan of Pirate's Curse, this game will feel like home to you. If you felt burned by Half-Genie Hero, then consider this game a return to form.

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the Seven Sirens is the 5th game in the series and I think it plays about as strong as Pirate's Curse did. It fixed a lot of issues I personally had with Half-Genie Hero and I'm glad they were able to touch on that and not make it feel like they barely made any changes. I had high expectations for this game since Half-Genie Hero felt a little on the weaker side, and they met my expectations with this game and beyond actually. This is one of the things I loved about Half-Genie Hero is the art style fits this game so well. Seven Sirens returns with the same art style, but is an overall upgrade. It's the same idea of art, but there is a very clear difference in colour contrast and overall vibrancy from Half-Genie Hero. There is also more fluid art/animations in terms of enemies and NPCs from the previous game, which is always a plus. The biggest thing graphically wise is fully animated cutscenes that really give it an anime type style and it works out perfectly. I loved the style they did for the teaser/trailer that was shown and was a really not getting my hopes up that we would see anything past that, maybe the ending scene but nope, every boss encounter and every important story element had cutscenes that were fully animated. It's very obvious that a good amount of the budget for the game went into the animated cutscenes and I can't express how much I appreciate that choice because they nailed the style to reflect for this game. Background for the zones is fantastic, sunken city, wrecked ship, underwater laboratory, lush jungles/overgrowth, underwater volcano, they nailed it and that's just something Shantae games have always nailed I feel, which goes even further this art style they've used for the past two games. Soundtrack I enjoyed most of the music but I feel the other Shantae games nailed the music better. Don't get me wrong, there is nothing wrong with the music in this game, just previous titles I had a way wider amount of soundtracks within the game that I did enjoy. What I did love, is the remixes in here and how some of them actually seem to take cues from other songs and somewhat mimic them. One of the towns you come across later on sounds like a "Burning Town" remix that fits this game's overall sound design (I could be wrong if it's actually a remix or not, but since there is no official Burning Town soundtrack in this game that I can think of, this sounds the closest to it.) Another one that is strong and I think a lot of people would easily pick up on it once they hear it is Sunken Shipyard. Within the first 10 seconds I thought I had YouTube opened with an EDM version of Rasputin. This soundtrack sounds like it took cues from Rasputin, Moskau and Kirby, threw it together, added their own remix and came out with such a great sounding masterpiece. I hope that was intentional because it was instantaneously that I thought of those 3 when I heard it.  Here we go, right what I was waiting for. So as I mentioned, Seven Sirens improved a lot on where I feel Half-Genie Hero fell short on. Half-Genie Hero felt too linear, like a platformer game with no real exploration outside of just to collect items but the maps just felt like you could only go on a one straight path and that was it. Shantae, Risky's Revenge and Pirate's Curse all had some sort of exploration to them where you had some freedom of where you wanted to go, Half Genie just felt like go to this area on this set path and be done with it unless you were going for 100%. Seven Sirens fixed this and returned back to the roots of Shantae. The whole world is connected together through multiple passageways/tunnels and each dedicated area is either a town or it's own labyrinth for a boss fight. I felt I got what I paid for in terms of story and exploration because it didn't feel like it was just a one way linear path that you run through. No, the game isn't like Super Metroid where you can take whatever path you want by sequence breaking (really hoping that comes in future titles) but it felt like there was an actual emphasis on exploration this time around. Another gameplay aspect I love that they added in was the Monster Cards. They are tedious trying to get them all, RNG based, some have a 1% drop, but they actually change your gameplay through faster crawl speed, more damage on a skill, eating food giving more health and so on. I seriously hope this is something they continue to use going forward as it lets you try out new things for speed runners and adds a nice little collecting feature on top of going for a 100% game. Shantae games have always been good at making bosses that have their own little quirks and requirements on how to beat them, which they once again nailed in here. The only "boss" you're able to really just button spam are the sub/mini bosses of Risky battles as you can just use your skill and spam attack with them, other bosses, you really can't do that as you need to moving around to engage the setups needed to start attacking. Transformations return once again with new transformations that share either the same function or very similar functions. We get a newt instead of a monkey for example that can be used to scale walls and dash between surfaces. I did like two of the new transformations over the originals but other than that, I love the original transformations more than what they were replaced with in here (rip Harpy transformation.) They also added in Fusion Dances which give you a special ability that is used for uncovering paths/items needed in the overworld, healing yourself or attacking enemies. There are warp zones in the game, which I'm glad is in because there is a lot of traveling between zones and the map is a pretty good size.Nothing really wrong with the game at all, was overall a serious improvement over the last one. Only thing I can say is:- If you're going for a 100% game, be prepared to be grinding some areas for Monster Card drops as they are RNG based and as I mentioned, some of them are a 1% drop, on top of some Monsters needing multiple cards to collect a set. - Gorgeous visuals and a fantastic animation job for the cutscenes. You can tell a good amount of the budget went into the animation and art style of the whole game and it's a very appreciated job.- Returning back to their roots of emphasis on exploration without the feel of dragging on for the sake of dragging on.- Controls that are very fluid and responsive, this is something I've always loved with WayForward games.- If you're a fan of Cristina Vee's voice acting, she got to voice Shantae a lot more than in previous games. Not fully voiced, but enough to really let her talent shine. Personal favourite voice actress of mine from her roll as Velvet Crowe in Tales of Berseria, so it's nice to see her nail another part and be able to shine with it. If you are a little weary due to how Half-Genie Hero played out, this game really does return Shantae back to it's roots in terms of how map and gameplay design should work. This is a huge improvement over the previous game and I would highly recommend giving the series another try. If this is your first Shantae game, I think this would a perfect place to start. You don't need to play the other games to follow the story at all, the stories don't really connect, they may make references to previous games but nothing is a direct sequel that will make you feel off. The fluid controls, vibrant art all around and the emphasis on exploration in this game would make for a perfect first time entry into this series or even into the MetroidVania genre. This game was an easy 10/10 for me, simply because I already had high expectations for the game and they crushed and surpassed each one, really turned around with how I felt where the series was going from their previous game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't a massive fan of Half-genie hero, but this game seems much more up my alley! It's more of a metroidvania, and transforming via dancing seems like less of a focus (I always found constantly having to transform was tedious). There's also a neat card collecting mechanic where you get trading cards for killing enemies, you can then equip the cards to get different effects based on what enemy it is. It reminds me of the shard system from Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night. The music, and art are fantastic as you would expect from the Shantae series. Overall I see it as an improvement to Half-Genie Hero so far. Was well worth the wait!

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to edit this review slightly with some more serious points after going through the game a second time.Pros:-A bunch of cute new half genies-Boss designs-Animated cutscenes-More voice acting than previous entries-Gameplay being a fun mix of both Pirate's Curse and Half genie Hero-Multiple towns-HD Squidsmith-Multiple Risky boss fightsCons:-Food and gems drop way too much-Bosses are too easy-The art design of the levels can feel very samey and boring-Uninteresting transformation designs-No Squidbaron boss fight-Pike Ball/Scimitar still feels OP-The story of the sirens did not feel fleshed out enough-Monster card systemTo elaborate on the monster card system: Too many of the cards felt extremely useless and there only ever a select few that actually felt useful. The effects to the gameplay never really felt substantial enough to really justify their existence and it really came off as if the cards were tacked on to the game at a later point in development. The initial idea could have been very interesting and actually add some more replay value to the game but the execution didn't feel fleshed out enough.I still really enjoyed this game and I do feel it is a very worthy entry to the series but I also feel the experiences from the previous two entries (Pirate's Curse and Half Genie Hero) were way better. Especially in regards to the art design of the levels and the general difficulty of the bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: So as some one who has enjoyed previous Shantae titles, seven sirens certainly will scratch that super metroid itch...  but it's not perfect. - not just me, other users have experienced it. - abilities and items make sure that you basically have somewhat of an infinite life pool unless your really trying to ignore your life.- this actually feels like the strongest con- besides some of the new character art- everything feels very copy-paste, even down to the mini boss fights with risky boots which are the most uninspired boss fights I've seen from a Shantae game.  Listen, if you've played the other Shantae games, it's very unlikely you're  going to play this one. Shantae is a small series, and for what it's worth, 30 bucks for 7-10 hours of gameplay, it's not a rip off.The humor is  there, Shantae is there, and there is decent level design. _childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the Seven Sires certainly seems to taken direction back to what Pirate's Curse was and forgotten the ways of Half-Genie Hero, well besides of the art style which is nice to look at and mostly similar here to what it was in previous title, though at first game seemed blurry, but after fiddling a bit the effect vanished. Shamefully though they didn't take the good part which were boss battles, as those are pretty bad in this one. Invulnerable phases, waiting, guessing games and so on. Boss design in this title was really bad, besides ye olde trusty slap fest with Risky that is familiar from the first title.Gameplay, music, art, transforms, map, story, variety, cutscenes and so on are done very well in the latest title. Transformations aren't the familiar monkey/elephant/mermaid and so on, instead you get fusion power from other Half-Genies that give instant transformations, so basically this fluids gameplay a ton, which is great idea. No just with push of a button can do most of the things that were in previous games. Sadly though they did counter intuitive choice with dances, you need to spam them several times everywhere to find hidden items from the map and the dance effect area is only screen, so you need to really spam them hundreds of times through the large map this title has. Also did get all of the upgrades insanely fast, like hadn't even done half of the game completion to get all items and upgrades from the three town stores.Overall great Shantae title and almost would have been the best without bad boss fights and counter intuitive dances.

_childDocuments_.review: The Shantae series is like a soap opera that has been running for 18 years. You know what to expect when you tune in, you know it's bad but it's sort of a guilty pleasure. Instead of improving, well, anything, they spend half their budget on inviting a popular guest star. They rarely try anything new, and when they do, you bet it'll make you roll your eyes.Bozon, the overlord of Shantae, is the original creator of the show and has been in charge since its inception. And he has also proven time and time again that modern game design is beyond him. The man is stuck in 2005 or is unfortunate enough to work with too many stubborn people. This is the fifth Shantae game, and so the sheer amount of experience should be apparent here, right? I wish. Shantae 5 feels like a HD remaster of the decade old handheld prequels.How can I review it with so little playtime? I beat all the other Shantaes, and, as I said, nothing really changed here.Mobs are as basic as in a SNES game; their AI comes down to walking left and right, and they usually have just one attack. The large Metroid-like map takes its Super Metroid roots too seriously and is divided into unnecessarily tiny rooms. Mobs respawn on exiting and re-entering the room, unconditionally. The rooms really didn't have to be so tiny because it's not a resource-starved handheld game anymore, but I'll get to that later. The SNES had 128KB RAM by the way, and the DSi had 16MB.Enemies drop tons of food, and you can use it any time in the pause menu. This single-handedly turns the game into a cakewalking simulator. You cannot die at any given point in time ever, and if you still manage to do so, guess what–auto-potions still exist and respawn you after death with full health. And you can buy them in chunks!Level design. It's not great. Like in Risky's Revenge, if you branch out, you're almost sure to just hit a progression roadblock. There is one path you should go at a given point in time, and everywhere else, well... don't go there. You don't have the X transformation yet. It's literally just a tiny cave with a heartsquid, after a skill gate. It doesn't have a map that seamlessly expands as you gain new abilities; the old rooms/portions of the map can be thrown away after you clear them unless you're looking for unlockables.And then there's Mr. Save Point Guy. Mr. Save Point Guy is the nostalgic green dwarf that has been saving the game since Shantae GBC. That's right, folks, GBC. Why did old games have manual saves in fixed locations? Because you can't afford background auto-saves on an 8-bit handheld. You probably don't want it on a DS either. HGH was a stage-based sidescroller and saving was really fast, so it worked just fine. Here, however, you have a separate room where you have to press several buttons and wait several seconds for the game to be saved, every few minutes. Let me rephrase, this is a 2020 game with modern hardware in mind, or so it should be. You didn't need to do this. It's tedious. It breaks the flow. It forces me to go to the nearest save point guy if I want to quit. You can't argue it's a retro game with retro design because at the same time you added HD graphics. Speaking of hardware, oh boy, you better whip out that NVMe SSD and be ready to goggle your eyes at those loading times. I saw other reviews addressing it so it's not just me. It takes 10-15 seconds to load a chunk of the map. This is not okay in a professional game drawn in 2D cartoon style. Better yet, there is no level caching whatsoever, even though the game idles at measly ~1.4GB RAM. If you for example exit the first town (triggering a loading screen), but then change your mind and go back, you'll have to watch the loading screen again. The game is several months old at this point (it had an exlusivity deal with Apple, the source of that sweet money for Studio Trigger) so the game isn't exactly out-of-the-box, and honestly I wonder how it works on consoles with HDD drives. Or is something else the bottleneck? Honestly WayForward, just how did you manage to make it so slow?And speaking of WayForward, I haven't looked at their bank account but their money management looks atrocious. Those weebs hired the big name anime studio Trigger to make cutscenes (or just the intro cutscene? but there are more of them either way). It's just like last time when they they prioritized a shiny 2.5D enviroment (which maybe would have looked cool in mid 2000s) over gameplay. Don't get me wrong; I liked the cutscenes, even though they were slideshow-y at times, but this kind of stuff is a . Budget your game so that you for sure get the important chunks done. Voices, for example. I've been playing Divinity:OS2 recently and I was amazed at how good voice acting and, more importantly, having all lines voiced could help me immerse me into the story. In Seven Sirens, like in the two previous Shantae games, they hired voice actors, but their work is partial. I feel like some of them spent more time commuting than being in the studio; just what's the point? Sometimes they say half the line, sometimes they grunt, sometimes they say something else, but most of the time they say nothing. If they skipped the shiny but ultimately useless animated shorts, they'd for sure afford full voice acting this time around. And the inconsistency is annoying (and Cristina Vee, I love you but please stop shouting every other time I use dash) so I'd rather mute voice altogether, BUTthere is only one volume slider. Forget a voice slider; there is no separation of SFX and music. While an FOV slider isn't necessary, the settings menu overall makes TotalBiscuit roll over his grave. It's also unsurprisingly locked at 60Hz. I overlooked such issues in older Shantaes (aside from HGH) because they were made with handhelds in mind, with a PC port as an afterthought. Seven Sirens does not just have a lazy port; WayForward cares so deeply about non-Japanese platforms such as PC and Xbox that they only released the Collector's Edition on PS4 and Switch. They literally don't want my money. The game appears to have had zero marketing on Steam. WayForward is based in the US, by the way.The final point, graphics. People claim this is the best-looking Shantae game ever, and I see where it comes from,  a lot of assets were copied from HGH, which was a 2.5D game. Animations are unfinished to the point of Shantae climbing the air in some places. Master-tier 16-bit pixel art was replaced with very average cartoon style. The quirky, almost parodic, though genuine retroness of the series is lost, even though it's how Pirate's Curse drew me into the franchise in the first place. However, as much as this series tries to modernize its graphics, it doesn't do so in the game design department, and that leaves it in the state of severe identity crisis where you don't know whether you should treat Seven Sirens as a modern or a nostalgic game, an engaging "metroidvania" or a kids game. It  they went with a chiptune soundtrack, which by the way is forgettable and undeniably the worst in the series. It's the first one not to be composed by Virt. His music was all over the place; it was the star of the show, the ultimate mood catalyst, and it got replaced with something that's clearly an imitation that achieves the opposite result.I liked they gave me an early dash (ignoring the annoying voices). I liked how they'd realized how bad lock and key design was in HGH and made transformations akin to Pirate's Curse but with genie magic, and I thought it was all I ever wanted from a Shantae game. I love the series for its silliness, retroness and character design. The transition to high-definition graphics took away a bit of everything. As it is right now, it's not worth $29.99–the price of Ori and the Will of the Wisps, a sequel done right.(I'm out of space so more in the comments)

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of Shantae for a while now, and I have to say that this game is really weak in comparison to previous iterations for a number of reasonsThis game is very easy, almost insultingly so. Shantae has never been an extremely difficult series, but this game showers you with healing items that make the most effective way to play to just damage boost through everything. I had 5 full health + magic refill items before the miniboss of the first dungeon. The only halfway challenging boss was the very final boss, but by that point I had healing items for days.The visuals of the game are flat, the world is a sort of Atlantis type fallen city, and every part of the map just feels like that, oh here's Atlantis but it's blue, here's red Atlantis, and green Atlantis. There's little variety between the different sections of the map beyond color. One of the big strengths of the Shantae series has always been its characters, which is why it's such a shame that all the new characters are so utterly boring. The other half-genies have interesting designs, but have little personality between them and feel like they don't contribute much to the story, and the titular 7 sirens are even worse. There's 0 dialogue for 5 of the 7, they all have no personality whatsoever. The game has really long loading screens as you transition from one section of the map to the other, and it really kills the pacing of the game. Not to mention that after every boss fight my computer seizes up something fierce to the point where there were multiple times where I thought the game had just crashed, and I'm not the only one experiencing this issue.This one is relatively minor, but the music is really bland. This is the first game in the series to not have it's soundtrack composed by Jake Kaufman (Shovel Knight, Contra 4) and it really shows. I won't say the music is bad, but it's just bland. Nothing really sticks out.Ultimately I get the impression that this game was rushed in order to get on Apple's gaming thing, it just feels like too much of a step back from Half-Genie Hero to be anything else. Bland characters, bland visuals, bland music... if you like the Shantae series you're probably going to get this one eventually, but I'd wait until a price drop because as it is currently it's not worth the $30 price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a while to sit down and properly play this game but when I did, I loved every second of it. Unlike Pirate's Curse and Half-Genie Hero, the game has a whole world map with tons of areas to explore similar to games like Super Metroid and Hollow Knight. Seven Sirens is a metroidvania just like those games where you have to get upgrades to be able to access new areas and uncover secrets. The game takes place on Paradise Island rather than starting in Scuttle Town like usual, which allows the game to introduce a ton of new characters and enemies. You use transformations by pressing a button rather than dancing and then transforming, which speeds up the gameplay tremendously like the pirate weapons in Pirate's Curse and the Risky DLC in Half-Genie Hero. The game also has collectibles known as Monster Cards which you can get randomly from enemies and other people on the island, you can use them to make Shantae better at certain things, which allows you to play in tons of different playstyles. The game also has a bunch of other modes and achievements to go for, and I'll definitely be playing through all of it. Shantae and the Seven Sirens may be the best Shantae game ever made as well as being a fun as hell metroidvania. I'd recommend it to Shantae fans, metroidvania fans and heck even just platformer fans in general, it's a ton of fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've played four of the Shantae games, Pirate's Curse feels even more like a one hit wonder. Half Genie hero was pretty fun overall, but not a good follow up to PC and just didn't fit in with the rest with the linear play style. But at least it had some heart- Seven Sirens feels like the series just giving up and fizzling out.This game starts out fairly strong with a fully connected overworld to explore, and decently enjoyable labyrinths with more of a Zelda feel than previous games had. But it feels like the devs quickly ran out of steam and the final third of the game is full of simple and uninspired dungeons, a timed enemy rush harkening back to Risky's Revenge and the awful Battle Tower, and a final dungeon that has absolutely nothing to it. The final boss feels easy, bland and pointless. We get neither the exciting gear from Pirate's Curse nor the varied animal transformations from Half Genie Hero. Instead there are a few powerup dances and a few transformations that are more like special moves for destroying obstacles or navigating specific hazards- you can't actually control the animals in the way you'd expect.Difficulty on this "definitive" update is all over the place, with attacks from the final boss taking off a heart or so while random enemies earlier in the game can take off three or four entire hearts of damage with one hit. The game is never difficult because you can dance to heal, on top of all your healing items and food, but the inconsistency is distracting and confusing. The story takes itself a little more seriously but has very little of the hilarious one liners and charm that the last couple of games did. The story is not particularly interesting on its own and some of the side characters I was looking forward to don't even make an appearance here so we can get a bunch of extraordinarily bland Half Genie friends. When you look at the game outside it's role in the Shantae series, it's not the worst thing you could play- controls are relatively solid still, and I can't say I had no fun at all. But I think even a half off sale is pushing it a little bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this the only Shantae game I have played previously has been Pirate's Curse, so I'll be referring to that as reference when needed.Complaints:Difficulty - The difficulty of the game (or rather lack there of), is what most of the complaints center around in the other reviews. Without healing items, the game would be pretty hard. Enemies respawn after leaving the room, and the distance of the hair whip is pretty short. One specific example are the fights with Risky. She doesn't telegraph when she's going to move, so she often runs into you, doing damage. And some rooms are just filled with enemies that make it bullet hell. All of the difficulty is negated because of the over abundance of healing items and the gems to buy them.Load Times - I'm not a game programmer (yet) so I can't really say how difficult it is to reduce load times, but I can say I've seen much bigger games load faster.Menu Bug (Maybe) - I don't know if it's just my controller or the game, but I've had difficulty navigating the menus. It's not that it won't input my direction, but the cursor moves sporadically and moves further than instructed.Card System - I like the card system. It's like it's straight out of Dawn of Sorrow. However, I feel like it's extremely underused. Some of the cards do the same thing as others, making them pointless. The system itself isn't bad, I just feel that you kinda forget it's there. It's not mentioned much and the abilities (aside from a few) are pretty underwhelming.Over Abundance of Gems / Lack of Upgrades - Multiple times during my play through I reached 999 and had nothing to spend it on. They couldn't necessarily have you upgrade your dances or transformations because then the card system would be redundant. Exploration -My biggest complaint is the size of the map. I find it lacking, and I wish it was bigger. My favorite part of Metroidvanias is the exploring, but here the map is small and some rooms are bland.Positives:Mostly Unique Transformations - I say "mostly" because the drill and the frog are basically the same thing, just in different substances. Charming Humor - There's a lot fun jokes and quips that make interactions interesting. Such as fourth wall breaks of restoring undead enemies. I'd say most of the humorous moments come from Squid Baron, who talks about video games and breaks the fourth wall often.Conclusion:I know that the stated negatives are in bigger number than the positives, but the rest of the positives are basic stuff. Like controls feel good, the animated cutscenes, voice acting, and new game +. I'd recommend this game to those who are looking for a good Metroidvania or a quick 2-3 day adventure, but I can understand why some fans were disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Update - Post-Game Thoughts: Meh, I've spent more on worseAs evidenced below, Seven Sirens made a good first impression by bringing all the best aspects of the previous games together into one. Unfortunately, the rest of the game seems kind of...uninspired, is the word I guess I'd use.  There's nothing wrong here, I think I'd just say that everything from the combat to the dialog is just...not as good. Which sucks, because the last message I want to send to Way Forward is "just do another Pirate's Curse!" I liked PC, don't get me wrong, but I want something like Seven Sirens could have been: continuous world map, one-button upgrade use, great tunage, but tied together with the same creativity and passion that was put into older games like PC and Risky's Revenge. All that said, 3 great games and 2 pretty okay games isn't a death warrant. I'm excited to see WayForward try and bring this back around. --------Original Review---------First Impressions from a returning fan: Sad because Shantae did away with their single-open-world-maps after Risky's Revenge? Hurt because Shantae figured out how to make upgrades fun and fluid in Pirates Curse and then seemingly forgot? Not a fan of the bland and overproduced soundtrack in 1/2 Genie Hero? Seven Sirens has you covered with a big ol' map, dedicated action buttons, and glorious chiptunes.

_childDocuments_.review: :Shantae returns once again in an adventure to save the day.:Shantae and 5 other never before seen Half-Genies get invited to Paradise Island, a tropical island. Along her she brings her friends and Uncle. The Mayor of Arena Town, the island's prominent town, has arranged for a stage performance where the half-genies will all get to show off their powers and entertain a crowd. However, during the performance the other 5 genies mysteriously vanish, leaving only Shantae. The following day, Shantae decides to investigate further and try to rescue her newly found friends. Little does she know she's about to uncover a dark secret of the island... and does Risky Boots have something to do with it?:After Half-Genie Hero's focus on 2D sidescrolling, Seven Sirens is a return to Shantae's origins, the Metroidvania genre. The island consists of multiple sections tied together and it hides many secrets to discover, including dungeons hiding bosses. As someone who found HGH too simplified, Seven Sirens fulfilled my wish in that department. The world is suprisingly larger than it first appears to be, so be ready to spent a couple of hours searching every nook and corner.Replacing Shantae's normal dance transformations are fusion coins and dances. The former let you transform into an animal with specific powers at the push of a button or when entering certain areas. This works more like the Pirate Items from Pirate's Curse, being more pace-keeping. The latter allow you to do many things such as  or  for instance.Seven Sirens also introduces a new mechanic called Monster Cards. When killing enemies there's a chance they drop a card that you can equip to boost one of Shantae's abilities. It's entirely optional to use and some of the cards are honestly pretty pointless by the time you can get them. Mostly a gimmick but one that is not intrusive and lets you experiment at the very least.There is however one area where 7S fails massively compared to PC and HGH. Outside of dungeons, the game does not let you keep track of collectibles, which for me late-game made 100%ing the game way more tedious than needed. Something to keep in mind.Overall though, the gameplay is solid but would've been even better had it not been for the issue i mentioned.:Graphic wise, 7S reuses many assets from Half-Genie Hero, mostly sprites from old characters, essentially doing what Pirate's Curse did with Risky's Revenge's. This is IMO a fine move as Half-Genie Hero's sprite quality was amazing and re-using them saved development time that could be spent on other aspects. This does not apply to the character portraits which are all newly drawn in a less chibi-like style.New for the Shantae series are animated cutscenes. This includes both the attract movie and campaign cutscenes. They're gorgeously colored and bring a new element of storytelling to the series.Soundtrack wise, long-time fans may be disappointed to hear that Jake Kaufman, the composer of the previous 4 games, didn't return to score the music for Seven Sirens. While understandable reactions, the composers WayForward hired for the game does a respectable job at imitating his style, even if they don't manage to make it sound as catchy and relies a LOT on chiptunes in the tracks. Personally, i find it to be more atmospheric than earwormy.:Seven Sirens controls just as well as Half-Genie Hero and Pirate's Curse. Shantae is tight on either the ground or in the air and doesn't suffer from floaty momentum when you stop moving. However, she can no longer jump down from platforms which can make traversing certain sections a little less convenient. Why this was taken out, i don't know.The PC port also remedies one big issue i had with PC's PC port. The controls can be fully reconfigured regardless if you're using a keyboard or controller.:Seven Sirens is a grand return for the Half-Genie to her origins, taking inspiration from Shantae 1, Risky's Revenge and Pirate's Curse while keeping Half-Genie Hero's amazing graphical quality. The world will get you immersed and make you want more as you unearth it's mystery.Personally though, i still hold Pirate's Curse in slightly higher regard as it's pacing is just a little more consistent and is less tedious to beat 100%. Another point of contention is the price. At 25€ (30$ in the US) it's a bit difficult to recommend the game fully unless you're an already existing fan or are craving another Metroidvania game, even with the increased production qualities.None the less, Shantae and the Seven Sirens is a solid game to play through at least once and if you like interconnected worlds, consider it. As such, it gets a final score of:8.5/10..

_childDocuments_.review: Better than Half-Genie Hero, but still doesnt beat Pirate's Curse (no game in the series beats Pirates Curse).Also, this is the only true "metroidvania in the series" if you consider that Pirates Curse & Half-Genie Hero have a level system, while this has an interconnected map with optional teleportation. _childDocuments_.review: For a sequel that so unabashedly reuses  assets, it's not really a better or worse game than it's predecessor. The art is not much different, what with the reuse, but they did change a few things, like the character art, which I think HGH's was better. The short cartoon video animations were a nice little addition though, when they don't (rarely) bug out like a corrupted youtube video. The gameplay is built around a single overarching "level" with areas with different biomes connected to each other that you mostly just walk(or teleport) into, working more like the older games. It makes for a more cohesive experience, but the lack of more fun "set-piece" sections makes it a bit...well, less fun.The thing that did chaff me were the bosses. They generally felt underwhelming and progressively annoying, to the point one of the latter bosses just being a really annoying memorization test. Exception for the very last boss, though, that one was p.good.There's also a "card" system, where you can equip 3 cards from mobs that drop them randomly. I was almost tempted to not mention it at all, because, frankly, most cards you'll find are just a +1 one of your abilities. Easily the most useless addition to this sequel. So, with all that said: It's more Shantae. It's alright, neither better or worse than HGH on it's aggregate. A rec if you want more of that, and/or is on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a longtime Shantae fan or fan of metroidvanias in general, I believe you'll like this game overall.Here are my pros and cons.Pros:Back to the full metroidvania map format. This is something that I sorely missed and it's great to see this mapstyle return.The new powers/forms are fun, although I do miss some of the forms from previous entries such as the spider and harpy.Hoping to see DLC with further additions.Cards are an interesting way to buff Shantae and allows for some nifty small gameplay changes.The scenery is beautiful.Overall movement is much more streamlined with quick activation for the new transformations.The fully-animated cutscenes are a nice touch.Okay:The Music:For the first time in Shantae's history, Jake Kaufman had no part in the OST and it shows.The OST has few standout tracks, but I'm not going to say it's bad. His absence is a weird one and I hope he returns if there are any further entries.Clashing art styles:While all of the art assets look great, it sometimes seems like they don't match with each other. Feels somewhat inconsistent but okay overall. Very noticeable during dialogue.Cons:No method of marking items on the map:There were many instances in which I found a hidden item I couldn't access at the time and completely forgot where they were on the map because there's no way to mark an item's location. Using Metroid as an example, if an item were hidden and discovered, it would be marked on the map for later acquisition. Such a feature being absent made item collection a drag overall and I hope Wayforward considers adding it.Little to no indication of damage stage during boss fights.Inability to jump down from platforms once you're on them:Now this is a weird and downright annoying gameplay change that was present in previous titles but missing here.Major Con: BUG WITH THE LOADSCREENSThere are many, many loadscreens when moving between biomes, which you will do frequently.Under normal circumstances this would be okay, but there is currently a bug that slowed my PC to a COMPLETE halt during EVERY loadscreen for about 20-30 seconds. I had the game on my SSD and have not experienced anything like this with any other game thus far. My computer isn't bad by any means so I'm not sure what's going on.

_childDocuments_.review: I already own and played the previous Shantae games and sadly... The Seven Sirens is only upgrade in visuals and animations. Loading times are long, and many screen transitions are annoying. Especially when you had to jump up, and if you dont keep the jump pressed with a direction you WILL fall back and forced to watch the loading again. The level design seems to be half done. We get power ups but barely used. I mostly felt this with the Frog form where the spikes locations are... positioned in a way that you can only hit them if you want to commit suicide. And the worst part of the game... the bossfights. INSULTINGLY easy. So easy I started to look up maybe I accidently put the game to faceroll easy mode. We have magics but no need to use them. The only spell I used was the SCIMITAR because it helped to defeat those easy bosses quicker, since the only "challange" of the bosses are that ridiculous amount of health they had. And whats up with the ATTRACT powerup when at the start of the game the kid explains if you dance, you collect every items in the area. On the other hand, the dances only gives effect on the screen that you are in and without a good indication if you plan to get 100% you move side, and do all your dances and hope the best... Quality of life update needed:  dances should be timed buff or stances. Example: while you have the oracle dance, you see hidden things. And if we mentioned Dances: previous Shantae games had actual dance animations. This one have one looped animation with a picture effect. In the end Shantae is a "weeb guilty pleasure" but this one is gameplay downgrade to the old games. A patch with difficulty settings is needed.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is fine. Not the best Shantae game but it's passable and a decent metroidvania (yeah, this one is actually a metroidvania as opposed to ½-Genie Hero). I'd probably wait for a sale though.However, WayForward insta-abandoned the game despite some ridiculous issues with load times. The game is using 4K assets regardless of the resolution it's running at, something that could probably be fixed with a free lower-res assets DLC, but that doesn't appear to be happening. As a result it will spike CPU load when loading assets and make e.g. recording/streaming stutter unless you manually set the CPU-priority for the process. On top of that it's consuming a lot more VRAM than necessary because it loads assets for a way higher resolution than necessary. I obviously don't know the whole reasoning behind it, but it seems like an extremely sluggish and unprofessional way to go about it.They keep saying patches are forthcoming (July 29 2020:  and September 14:  but they refuse to say whether or not they include a fix for the load times. But it may not matter, though, because as of now no patches have come out anyway and I'll be very surprised if they ever do.Ultimately I would skip this game and spend my money on developers that actually care about their game and its player-base: Shovel Knight (Yacht Club Games), Guacamelee (DrinkBox Studios), The Messenger (Sabotage), Explodemon (Curve Studios), and Axiom Verge (Thomas Happ Games) are all great examples of that.I used to love WayForward and have bought a  lot of their games, but I'll be a bit more wary of that in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a Shantae fan for a super long time, even backed the 1/2 genie hero back on Kickstarter (got my art in the gallery!) and all I have to say is that the game is already solid, and I think I favour it more than 1/2 genie.Wonderful work on Studio Trigger (Kill la Kill, Little Witch Academia, BNA) for making the opening and the wonderful Christina Vee for singing the theme song. While the game's graphics are similar and maybe not as impressively different from 1/2 genie, the metroidvania gameplay remains similarly the same (which is key in this series) and adds a few extra things (such as collectible monster cards that you can equip for passive buffs). I won't spoil the story, but it's pretty interesting and good from what I have played thus far, adds a lot of new characters who have a lot of personality to em'.Props to whatever studio made the ingame cutscenes, I was blown away to see *actual* animated cutscenes in a Shantae game. Despite being an Apple Arcade exclusive for some time, it's good to see the game on Steam finally so we can dip into the wonderful metroid-vania world of Shantae once more. Do yourself a favour and play this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Not much to say about the game, if you have played the previous titles, it is basically the same deal  with better visuals. Just casual 8ish hour game that you can stroll through, not very difficult or innovative, but fun for what it is. Edit: There has been a patch that addressed the issues I mentioned in the paragraph below, which was my only real gripe with the PC version of the game. Updated to a recommend, assuming the fix does work for everyone.That being said, I cannot actually recommend this title on PC due to very noticeable loading times when you traverse between sections of the map (section being about 2-4 screens long)that inexplicably put a significant amount of stress on your CPU, resulting in 20 second loading times, and your entire PC stuttering. It wouldn't be an issue if it didn't happen very frequently, but I found myself having to sit at these long loads every few minutes when I wasn't doing a dungeon. Considering the game has been out for months at this point, with no mention of a fix/patch for the issue, I can only assume that developers have no intentions of addressing the issue any time soon, if at all. Definitely cannot recommend this game until they address the loading issues.

_childDocuments_.review: The Shantae serie is one of the best metroidvania serie ever. This game is no expection to the serie. The first part is really good despite being quite classical, really much inspired by Wonder Boy The Dragon's Trap and the Castlevania's Sorrow games. The devs, as always with Wayforward, are clearly huge fans of the classic NES/SNES/GBA games, because they added SO many references here and there to older games, like Batman, TMNT , Super Mario 2 and 3, Megaman, Castlevania 1 and 2 (NES) to name a few. The most memorable is probably the reference to Dragon Ball.The humor is also excellent, defintiely inspired by the Paper Mario serie.Unfortunately the game seem to lose itself during the second part, with tons of unnecessary backtracking and annoying/frustrating plateform parts. The world map is also quite a letdown. The wonderful artstyle is probably the most memorable part.The soundtrack is more than decent tho not as good as in the previous games (it's hard to replace Jake Kaufman).Overrall this is a more than decent metrovania game. Not as great as The Pirate's Curse but still much better than The Half Genie Hero
