_childDocuments_.review: This is a review written from the perspective of Shantae fan.A competent platformer but only a below-average addition to the Shantae series. It forgoes the series's traditional transformation mechanics for more context-sensitive traversal transformations used only in specific places. While the game itself is ok and I would recommend playing it, it doesn't leave a lasting impression and doesn't fully satisfy after finishing it. Steam showed about 10 hours while my save file says 7 hours and 30 minutes for the first playthrough assuming you are checking for some secrets and dying sometimes. The price being about half that of a AAA game I believe this entry in the series is still a worthy purchase.If you enjoyed other games in Shantae series, then this one should be fun as well, even if a bit weaker than the others.Shantae and the Seven Sirens is a metroidvania type platformer where you play as the titular Shantae - a half-genie who can transform into several different creatures and use magic through belly dance. The game's structure will have you explore various environments to complete objectives and unlock new skills and magic to allow access to other areas of the game. It's not a hard game, but if you die, you go back to the last save you made. Mind you that this shouldn't be mistaken for a kid's game. While it has no nudity it's still a bit sexual in a lot of aspects, from the very design of the characters to some animations and dialogue.About difficulty.Shantae series (aside from the very first game) is very easy. This game is no different. I don't put it under pros or cons, because it's a personal thing whether you need the game to be challenging in order to enjoy it. I love Hollow Knight for it's challange. I also love Shantae for many different reasons. It's up to you to decide what's important for you.More about pros and cons below.The controls are snappy with full power given to the player. Jumps and dashes can be short or full depending on how long you press the button. You can fully control the direction in mid-air. There's no mommentum buildup - you spring into full speed the moment you start moving and you stop immediately. Attacking is responsive and, when upgraded, you can attack in a very rapid fashion as long as you can press the button quick enough.Style reminds me of flash animations. Smooth animations are the highlight. Some of the more expressive enemies like mermaids or slime girls have a lot of frames for all their actions.Each area of the game has a theme to it. While for the most part it's still generic theming like "fire level" or "water level" or "undead level", it works well in this game.After you beat the last boss, save the day and watch credits your save file will still be accessible and game still grants you access to everything you've already unlocked. You can use this to finish up any side content, find all the treasure and fully explore the game's world.Shantae returns in her skimpy belly-dancer outfit and still makes the bum-jiggle when crawling. Some other characters and enemies also got some lewdness to them with a disappearing, chain-whipping bat-girl that slaps her own butt at you and has her clothes dissolve when defeated being the most of what you can expect. No nudity of course, she disappears before you can see anything explicit. Still, the theme of sexual allure is very much present in this game, as it was in other titles in the series. Naughty things will probably go over a 7 year old's head, so I don't think it's going to do any damage if you buy this game for your kid. Still, a pegi 7 rating is a bit... interesting.Dancing doesn't transform you anymore. Instead, dances provide screen-wide effects for unlocking paths, dealing damage or uncovering treasure. Transformations are more context sensitive than in other games. Forget about changing to another form and walking around in it. Now if you change to your wall-climbing form, you will instantly turn back to your half-genie self the moment you touch the floor. Same goes for other forms like the one that lets you swim turning you back after you resurface from water etc. It takes away a lot of the series's charm in my opinion. This series should encourage you to transform more, not less. I want to see Shantae with many different traversal and combat transformations, not just gimmicks that let you cross through previously blocked off areas.The main rewards for exploring are heart squids, which are used to forge more heart containers, and gold nuggets, which can be traded for cards giving you special passive abilities like increased damage. Hunting down secrets ain't all that rewarding.Something's wrong when this game can take about 10 seconds to load a level when you already spend so much time walking through all the connections between them. I mean I thought the purpose of long corridors in between areas is to hide load screens, but here the game will still spend a lot of time loading. And don't get me started on the load times after you die, because having another 10 seconds to reload the area you are already in is inexcusable.A personal pet peeve of mine. This game does not autosave at all. Not on entering new area, not on teleporting, not on discovering a key item, nothing! The only times the game will actively ask you if you want to save is when you defeat one of the main bosses. You can potentially lose hours of progress exploring if you don't go out of your way to visit save rooms on a regular basis. I personally find it to be just a bad design in general and autosaving wouldn't even break the game in any way. It's already easy, if you die, it's probably because you didn't pay attention to your heart meter while trying to quickly complete exploration of an area. Put autosaves in your games, please...Shantae Half Genie Hero had a lot of the same enemies. Bat girls, mermaids and a lot of basic monsters as well are all borrowed from the previous game. Most spells are likewise returning. All in all there's far less new stuff that I would like.There are several types of lategame grunts that you will fight in the last dungeon. It's clear they were added at the end and didn't have as much love as many other sprites. For the most part they are just running from side to side or standing still and shooting projectiles with not much going on with the animations.Shantae and the Seven Sirens is a very average game overall. I'd give it aBut I still recommend it based on how much fun I had. At it's core it's a very competent metroidvania platformer with solid controls and decent content. The price for me is just right for this type of game, but waiting for sale may be a safer option if you're not fully convinced. Shantae Half Genie Hero was a better game and it's pretty cheap nowadays, so you can start there if you haven't played it yet and wait for Seven Sirens price to drop.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game before not on Steam, so this time I went in playing rule breaker mode. I went back and forth between if I like this game or not, or, well rather I started by giving it a benefit of the doubt, but then as I played and played I kept coming back to my initial review and going back on all the things I thought were positives, as I realised that for each there happened to be some sort of catch or intense mediocrity.-The art style is well drawn but lacks an earnest personality distinct to Shantae.-The music style appears good and polished, but you soon start to realise it's starting to sound a bit meh, and while good I guess is not very fitting to the game, especially in contrast to some of Shantae's older soundtracks. Gets a bit lacklustre, appearance of being energetic without the oomph.-The card mechanic felt a bit uncharacteristically grindy towards the end, and their effects did not leave me any sense of fulfilment in their (lack of) creativity and variety.-The characters felt very skin deep and I couldn't manage to ever feel close or care about any of them, even a teensy bit, I mean not necessarily about emotional depth (obviously, it's Shantae), but even feel excited or just anything about them for more than mere moments.-The voice acting seems good at first, but then listening closer and paying attention to how I actually felt about how it related to the characters made me realise that the particular voices (often times) didn't really fit with the characters, and lines felt like they were read to simply sound fancy rather than if the character were actually saying it. Like you'd hear Risky say some quip but it would sound uncannily weird in the context of the scene. Perhaps if the game were fully voice acted instead of snippets then it could feel more grounded, but right now it's like they just arbitrarily make brisk utterances that only give crumbs of personality (in the bad way) while avoiding the characters' actual personalities.-The design would appear to be fine, but the more you play, these 'little' annoyances gradually become apparent like how certain features of the design seem very redundant, or how enemy placements often feel a bit uncomfortably misplaced in a way that the game isn't properly balanced to handle. In general enemies were moreso (sometimes a little tanky) nuisances than any real challenge. Magic wasn't something I felt encouraged to use since it was a bit too easy to get rid of and too sparse to regain, I would have liked it if it regenerated inchingly naturally (instead of needing a card) so that you could regain some during the empty parts of exploration. Then there were the metroidvania elements that just felt more like empty filler rather than actually meaningful and engaging as in more competent (yeah I said it) metroidvania games. It felt like I had to trek from one place, then all across the map back to another and another, and it never really had any feeling of cohesion or deep sense and personal connection with the map as would usually be the case. Maybe it's hard to explain what I mean, but that's just how it felt to me (and I've played tons of assorted metroidvania games). I know Shantae tends to be a bit different in its structure, but whatever they did it didn't seem to work very well.I know all this sounds very harsh from me, and I'm sure if it were just one or two things not quite up to fluff or odd then it would be fine. However, it seems like the whole game is like this. Nothing seems to  together, so the game feels uncomfortable, empty (despite there being plenty of enemies), and overall gives a pit in my stomach where I'm not even sure why I'm playing except to see it through to the end as of my commitment to the series. Sorry, I just don't think the game was really worth playing. No real fun, no real thought, just flashy tropical void.

_childDocuments_.review: Save for a RNG-heavy dungeon before the last, a rather long, awkward section in the dungeon before that and a few points of awkwardness here and there, beat for beat they surpassed Half Genie Hero (but definitely not Pirate's Curse)  and Risky's Revenge (which it has a map at least ten times larger than easily) pretty much definitively in a lot of departments. It controls better, it has a more in-depth story, it isn't the same five levels, and quite frankly, it's overall a breath of a fresh air from the Shantae franchise. This is the true metroidvania that Shantae: Risky's Revenge could have been had the DSi allowed any space for apps, It houses some of the most precise controls I've used in a platformer (though definitely not always the kindest hitbox detection with it, Shantae very much feels like a precision instrument in this one more than any other of the games). Would I recommend you get it? Absolutely. It has a mostly smooth progression until the last third and it really shines as WayForward's finest work. Also the anime scenes were done by Studio Trigger (clearly on a shoestring budget, but knowing how that industry works that's nothing even remotely unusual and they're still lots of fun to watch).

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I've been expecting much worse from this game, and it pleasantly surprised me. I wouldn't say it's an outstanding game, but it's an enjoyable experience. Graphics are fine, music is, obviously, not as good as Jake Kaufman works, but is not bad either. Cutscenes are great, monster girls are adorable as always, and gameplay is surprising refinement of a transformation system that used to annoy me so much. I can understand why it worked that way in the original game, given how few buttons GBC had, but going through dances to, say, turn into a mermaid every time you wanted to swim was really annoying and unnecessary in sequels. Well, now traversal abilities are finally divorced from dances - if you unlocked a transformation, you automatically transform into a digging or swimming form when you go into dirt or water, respectively.Level design is a bit of a double-edged sword - now it's a big Metroidvania map again rather than several separate levels. Diversity of locales suffer a bit even compared to the earlier games, as it is all different flavors of aquatic ruins - but, to be fair, Castlevania games are mostly different flavors of castles and Metroid is different flavors of alien caves, and no one complains about them (though they do manage to pull off more variety in their respective themes).And now we get to my biggest gripe about the game that tainted my first walkthrough.  Everyone seems to be angry about Seer Dance, but no, the one aspect of this game I hated the most was the card system. You see, the monsters drop cards that give you bonuses, and that's fine, but you can only equip three cards at once in the Definitive mode. In theory it means that you have to choose wisely what cards do you need the most, but the problem is that most of this cards give small situational bonuses, usually to a certain ability, and they also have to compete with cards that give big and powerful abilities like mana regeneration. My "favorite" example is Wetman card - it gives extra health from food, and you can only eat food in pause menu, so there is no reason why it shouldn't be always on, you just have to go through extra step every time you want to use food. Having to constantly switch between cards is just an annoying busywork, so you just pick the three strongest cards and ignore the rest. The smart way to design cards would've been a system similar to Paper Mario badges, where every card has some kind of Power Rating and you can equip as many cards as you want as long as you don't exceed certain Power Total that you can upgrade - so you can pick between having few strong cards or many utility ones (and certain cards, like Wetman, should have rating of zero). But for the game as short and easy as Seven Sirens, the Rule Breaker mode where you can just equip every card works just fine  - I don't think it breaks the game in any way. It shouldn't even exist in first place, it should be a part of default Definitive mode, with current system relegated to Classic mode.So, I understand this whole grievance is kinda self-afflicted, but they did worded Rule Breaker mode like it's some kind of cheat mode for repeat walkthroughs. So, as a good boy, I did not picked it for the first walkthrough, and even though I had second thoughts at 15% mark, I did not fully realized my error until it was too late to restart the game. So do not repeat my mistakes, , and if you want to experience the busywork, just do it when you are achivement-hunting.

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae's back at it again, but this time, she has the help of other guardians; however, they've vanished and must be found.  Rating grades are 1-5.Graphics: 4.75 - Beautifully animated and the cut-scenes all look nice and the entire presentation is wonderful.  Only issue: I'm not a huge fan of the opening animation and design.  Still, it's Shantae and the game looks beautiful nonetheless.  Eventually, the models grew on me and the final siren is adorable.Sound: 4.5 - I highly enjoyed the voice acting, but the intro song wasn't as memorable as Half-Genie Hero.  It's still a good intro song, but just lacks the impact the one from Half-Genie Hero had.  Still, as stated, voice acting isn't irritating and very well recorded.  Sound effects do their jobs and we do hear screams from some enemies when defeated, which is a nice little touch. Control: 5 - NOTHING has changed with the controls and that's a good thing.  If you've played previous entries before, you won't expect nothing but the tightness of the controls.  Transformations are dedicated to either a simple button press, a charge up using the attack button, double-jumping with the jump button, or directional control in certain areas.  Gameplay: 4 - I have to dock gameplay on this one as the game is simply too easy.  Granted, this was started as an iOS game, but it's fairly easy.  As easy as it may be, however, secrets and hidden areas are still well placed and rewarding to a degree.  There's sadly no transformation to critters and no special attacks for said critters you can transform to, but some will run over enemies and cause damage either way. Other than that, the gameplay itself is relatively easy to get into and there is enjoyment to be had.Final Score: 4.5 - I had a great time with this game and I've gone back to try to complete the achievements.  Fans of the series will enjoy this game and anyone who enjoys puzzle/platform games will find quite a bit of enjoyment from the series as a whole, including this game, despite its easy difficulty.I've been a fan since the 2nd game (semi-remastered (Risky's Revenge: Director's Cut )) and I've even gotten into the original GBC original (emulated by Limited Run Games and sold on the Nintendo Switch).  Every game has been satisfying my itch for platform/puzzles, and I HIGHLY recommend them all (even the GBC one).

_childDocuments_.review: ConsIncredibily short and alot of... 'half assed' feels. Like one of the bosses is like puzzle simon says. The first squid isn't it. The 2nd squid is, then you hit the 1st squid and its wrong so you hit the 2nd again, then the 3rd, then the 4th, and the 4th is wrong so start over hitting the 2nd. It reeks of the devs not putting in proper effort to do alot of things.And they ruined the underwater/swimming mechanic. There is no mermaid shantae, you're a frog darting forward in a mechanic very similar to how you 'dig'. It's not exploring the depths in areas that you've come across many many times before, it's just darting from one water surface to the next.Which is how alot of this game feels. Half-assed in alot of regards.===============ProsIt's got that shantae feel. The asehtics is perfect and it feels cool to work with the other half-genies. The story isn't anything as developing or cool as Pirate's Curse, but it's there and decent enough. Feels good to have multiple towns to go through. _childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the Seven Sirens has a lot of weaknesses, and ultimately, I'm not sure I enjoyed it as much as I hoped I would.Way too often it felt like a chore and the tedium sometimes was unbearable.My thoughts after 100%ing the Game and getting every Achievement are as follows.First of all, one of the most important things in a Metroidvania, the exploration and collecting:What I would have wished for was an ability/item which allowed me to instantly teleport back into the city/main hub, as backtracking was necessary very often and it felt like a chore most of the time to run back to the closest warp point.When it comes to quality of life features the game is pretty barren as it is, like a map for the Heart Squids/Nuggets/Secrets, items that show whether a collectible is near, these things don't exist.The map doesn't even show caves that contain treasure or important locations like windmills or withered flowers. It's just a basic map consisting of many rectangles, the only things shown are: Towns, Boss dungeons and Teleport rooms. Aside from that, the map shows nothing.So when you come by a cave somewhere and don't yet have the ability to reach the Treasure, you better note that down, cause your map won't list the caves location, doesn't matter whether you got the treasure inside or you didn't. An easy solution would've been to sell a map at the end of the Game, even if it costs 999 Rupees, that shows all of the collectibles. Money is an abundance near the end anyways.Ultimately, searching for those collectibles is annoying and feels like working through chores, not like exploring.When collecting you'll run into either of the following problems:1. You don't have the ability yet to reach the collectible.2. There is no indicator whether there even is a collectible, so you have to use all of your abilities to detects those, which consist of 2 dances, which take 10 seconds to perform both. Doesn't sound too bad, until you realize you have to use these on (almost, since some are water and you can't dance there) every single square in the Game. I don't think anyone would do this and think it's fun. Any sane person would just look up a 100% map and work that through.3. You'll have to farm enemies, and that can take minutes per enemy, dependent on your luck with the drop of their monster-card.None of these obstacles feel good to play around. There are just way too many things to collect, so unless you are ignoring collecting until you have every ability and then run through a 100% map and setting a route, you'll run into a problem when you are missing 5 or so collectibles because, as said, neither the uncollected nor collected items are shown on your map.In the game there are 32 Heart Squids and 50 Gold Nuggets as well as 50 Monster Cards, of which 43 need to be dropped (some multiple times).Now find all that in a huge map that shows you not a single collectible related thing, while many of these collectibles are also hidden and need to be uncovered randomly with dances.That doesn't even cover the "Statues". Yea, random statues that need to "discovered" by randomly doing the last dance you unlock in random locations on the map. There are 10 of those scattered around, one even containing a Heart Squid.The collecting aspect is simply tedious, annoying and unfun.What I liked though, was the animation sequences, enemy and character designs as well as the overall aesthetic of the game. The music was amazing and I definitely will regularly listen to some of the songs in the future.I would have wished that Shantae could actually transform into the forms in her dances, instead of only a slightly animated picture appearing with every dance.Felt disappointing that in these dances she looks so amazing, basically an altered version of her human form. But the only "playable" forms she has, are things like a Newt or an ugly frog.Why couldn't she actually transform into the different forms of her dances? Shooting leaves with the Up-Dance, using her Hammer with the Down-Dance and so on. No, barely animated PNG.However, these couple positive features, just couldn't bring me to recommend this game... It's a Metroidvania after all, with achievements bound to collecting a lot of stuff, you will either have to spend dozens of hours searching through every nook and cranny or look up a guide.I can only imagine how much I would have hated the Game by the point that I would've found every single thing, if I didn't use a guide to find it all.

_childDocuments_.review: + Excellent game world+ Fun gameplay mechanics+ Cool new upgrade system+ Cheesy, but fun story and dialogue- Graphical and musical downgrade- Mobile game designThe Shantae series is great, so of course I was excited when they announced a new one. However, my expectations were immediately lowered upon hearing that the game would be developed for Apple's new Apple Arcade service, effectively changing the target platform to mobile devices. Now, nearly half a year later, the game is fully out on all platforms, so it's time to see how it measures up.Seven Sirens is another great addition to the Shantae series. It takes what prior games did right and expands on them, introducing new abilities, a cool new card mechanic, and fleshing out the game world at the same time. Of course, this is on top of the cheesy, yet fun storytelling and dialogue that WayForward has become known for. Sure, it may not be as good as its predecessor Half-Genie Hero considering that it was designed for mobile platforms first, but it's a solid action platformer all things considered and one I would recommend, even to those that have not touched the series before.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: Although the Metroidvania genre to me has felt a bit oversaturated these past couple of years, Shantae and the Seven Sirens manages to stand out thanks to its joyful and upbeat atmosphere, whereas a lot of games in this genre tend to be a bit more on the dreary side.It also features a surprising number of fully animated and voiced cutscenes, which did a lot for my overall enjoyment of the game, and for keeping me invested in the story. The game is a bit on the easy side, and because of that may not be a great fit for someone who's looking for a big challenge. However, I believe that it would be perfect for someone who's either new to the genre, and/or someone who's a bit younger.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit unsure on how to feel about this game. Don't get me wrong, it's good. I guess I'm just trying to compare it to Half-Genie Hero.Let's note down those differences then and put my thoughts on those where they apply.First off, the animation is great as was in HGH but my biggest note here is that the characters are much less chibi in appearance which I call a plus.Where HGH was level/area-based here it's an open world like the games before HGH. This has it's pros and cons as it can lead to a lot of running around trying to figure things out but that's just be me being dumb.The amount of transformations has been streamlined down to 5. And they are pretty damn cute to look at.Yes, less usually sounds like worse but in this case I'd say not since the mobility forms have been made a lot more easier to use instead of having to cycle through dances to select them.In a way this game does feel smaller to me, like a Shantae 4.75 though but I just finished AC:Odyssey before this so that may just be me. And I haven't gone for 100% (yet).If anything I hope to see more of the new Half-Genies in future games and hope WayForward keeps up the good work with Shantae 6.Beyond that I can't really think of anything to add that would be worth mentioning and/or not be a spoiler.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game throughout (with only like 1 or 2 hiccups) and I definitely see this as my 2nd fav Shantae game (Pirates curse still taking that top spot)Lets start with positives:- The transformations are even better than ever as now they work like the pirate gear from pirates curse, where all ya gotta do is press a button and you will instantly transform to the ability needed. While the dances are more for the much more powerful moves that are used mainly for messing with the environment but also have uses with dealing with enemies- The level design was great and apart from like 1 or 2 sections, I knew exactly where to go and the ways I can take to get there. Helps that the map system is very helpful for letting you know where each path can lead to, but it wont show how the path exactly works unless you already explored there or you get one of the maps in the dungeons.- The animated cutscenes are amazing. I'm a huge fan of studio trigger and Kay Yu, so it was definitely gonna be awesome to see.- I heard people saying that the music was not as good as other Shantae games, but to me personally, I loved most of the tracks on this game (I'm a sucker for retro styled music like this)- Shantae does not get fired from her job this time, hooray.Now for a few downsides that I had:- Bosses were a bit too easy for my liking, apart from the first siren you fight, since I was being very reckless, I didn't really die to any of the bosses. Hell some of them I was able to basically avoid all their attacks and just whale on them.- That squid heart behind the minigame is a bit annoying to get since you need to get a perfect, not that easy to do when Shantae cant even stay at one speed.- Im kinda conflicted on the choice to make the backgrounds 2d instead of doing the 3d stuff like with half genie hero. On the one hand its very nice art, but on the other, I kinda wish they kept the 3d backgrounds because they were nice in that game.Overall this is a high recommendation, even if your new to the Shantae series, as the story has its own story line split from the other games. Go and get it if you have the money to spare, show the developers the support

But this game is exactly what I like about the shante games- metroidvania with fun abilities, a great soundtrack and platforming. It's all here, and it's awesome!! I just wish Way forward would alter a few things...like please for the love of God just autosave in the save rooms. Instead, you have to open 3 dialog boxes every time to save, and this would be just me mashing the A button to hurry through them. Also, the game can be text heavy at times, and while you're free to skip them, many times it'll include important information on where/what to do next. I'm a semi text skipper so putting a small hint in the item menu on what to do next would be great. Definitely a fun game though and a must play if you like metroidvanias.

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the Seven Sirens is a cute, accessible, and relaxing platformer in the Metroidvania style. It has been some time since I enjoyed myself as much as I enjoyed playing Shantae. There are a couple of flaws though. First, there is a ridiculously long loading time between areas. This only occurs between chunks of the map and not between every screen or anything, but if you find yourself wanting to collect absolutely everything, it would get a little grating. Second, if you are looking for a serious challenge, this game might not be for you. _childDocuments_.review: Shantae is one of those weird series where despite being rather popular with four previous entries, only Pirates Curse was truly excellent. Half Genie hero was one of my biggest gaming disappointments – it wasn’t just underwhelming, it was actually on reflection a pretty poor and blatantly unfinished game despite spending the best part of four years in development. The overpriced and rushed DLC just hammered the nails in, and after such a shabby treatment of both the kickstarter backers and poor Shantae herself I honestly didn’t expect to see another game in the series.So when Seven Sirens sneaked onto the Steam front page with basically no fanfare after being trapped on IOS for a year, it’s fair to say I went in with rather more muted expectations. I’ll just come out and say it – this is a massive improvement over Half Genie Hero, and is probably the second best in the series overall despite some pretty critical design flaws. Production values are even more lavish than usual for Wayforward, with animated cutscenes by anime studio Shaft, gorgeous art and animation and a memorable soundtrack. There’s some reused art from Half Genie hero, but it didn’t really bother me – we could also level that accusation at Pirates Curse, and there’s plenty of new enemies and art to round out the bestiary.And if you thought the cheesecake was a little on the nose in Pirates Curse, this might be the most blatant it’s ever been. Make no mistake, this is Waifubait fetish fuel of the highest calibre, made by dedicated practitioners of the art. If you’re into monstergirls you owe it to yourself to at least check out the art for the game, as if there was even the slightest scope to stick tits on it you can be assured that Wayforward took the opportunity.In terms of design, we’re back as well to the traditional metroidvania + dungeons design of the previous games. If I’m being honest there’s nothing here in terms of both power ups and map design that you won’t have seen a dozen times before. It lacks Pirates Curse’s willingness to try out different genres and styles to keep things fresh – here everything progresses pretty much exactly as you would expect. It’s more testament to the timelessness of the original template set out by Super Metroid 26 years ago that the core gameplay loop is still really fun and engaging. One thing I could do without is the need to use the ability to spot invisible items if you don’t want to miss power-ups – this isn’t essential to progress, but if you’re going for 100% you can expect a slow slog spamming the ability on literally every screen as there is no indication if an item might be hidden.However, by far the biggest issue with Seven Sirens is that the game is insultingly easy. You can collect cards from monsters that grant abilities (like faster swim speed, better missiles etc). Some of these are absolutely game breaking, like the one that grants you magic regeneration. In addition to this, you have a magic ability that regenerates your health, so you can see why this might become a problem. Even if you don’t make use of this obvious combo, you can carry about 100 healing items meaning that there is basically no chance of you dying without self-imposed restrictions. The bosses all go down like beautifully animated sacks of ♥♥♥♥, with even the final boss being long rather than in any way difficult.Overall though, I’d say it’s worth a play in spite of the issues, though probably not for full price. It’s very much in that middle ground that steam sadly doesn’t let you give – great art and animation, middling design. Top tier waifus. Let your heart guide you as to whether this is your thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: The transformations are easy and intuitive (e.g. double jumps and dashing at the push of a button), the music is overall pretty good even though Jake Kaufman was unavailable, and the art design is about as good as Half-Genie Hero.There are just two major issues that stop this from being a full step up from the previous games.1. It's laughably easy.The earlier games had a tendency to start out relatively easy with the platforming challenges and then ramping them up until at the end you would die many times trying to get through a single screen. It was hard, but it was equally rewarding when you got through section using a combination of pixel-perfect timing and understanding the enemy movements and your own abilities. In Seven Sirens, all this goes out the window. Platforming challenges are heavily watered down to the point that you could barely call them "challenges" at all. They are basically just locks to be opened by the appropriate ability with no actually skill involved. In the entire game, there was exactly 1 decent  platforming challenge (it involved gaining speed with one transformation and then switching to another in midair).  Even if you are so uncoordinated that you still struggle with them, there are cards you can equip that completely negate fall and spike damage, so there is no risk. Even if you haven't found those cards, the game loads you up with so much food and gems that healing and upgrading from the shop is trivial. You can easily max out on gems and healing items halfway through the game.All the healing items (not even counting the healing spell and regenerating magic card) means that bosses are basically just normal enemies with more health. You can beat every boss by just dealing all the damage you want while mostly ignoring their own attacks because healing is so easy. The final boss was just as easy as the first. Heck, some of the normal enemies were harder than the bosses. At least some of them can BLOCK. Even then, every normal enemy becomes trivial near the end of the game due to your high-damage screen-clearing abilities and regenerating magic.2. The mechanics for finding hidden items is tedious and unfulfilling.There is a "seer" ability that is used to reveal invisible objects. This would be fine, except that there is no indication of where you should look and the ability doesn't even cover the entire room. After I already beat the game, I went back to literally every single room and used the seer ability multiple times in each room to check for secrets. There was absolutely no skill involved- just mindless scanning. I think Half-Genie Hero did a much better job on this. In that game, most collectables were usually in plain sight but were blocked behind platforming challenges. Here, the overwhelming majority of secrets are either "invisible" or are trivial to pick up once you get the right ability. You smash a rock and an item is behind it- that's it. Combine this with the fact that there is no indication of where you have already checked or what items remain in an area and you end up with a pretty tedious experience.Overall, while I would recommend this game, it is only because of the artwork, fluid movement, and entertaining dialogue. If you want an actual challenge, I would wait until they release some harder modes. I'd give it a 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A definite upgrade over the previous entry in the series(Half-Genie Hero), and a welcome return to the metroidvania genre, but incredibly easy and pretty short. If you already like Shantae, you'll probably have a good time. If you're not familiar with Shantae, you should play Risky's Revenge and Pirate's Curse first - not because you need them to make sense of this story, but because they're cheaper and just as good as this game, if not better.PROS- New transformations and dance magic! In place of Shantae's traditional transformation dances, she gains tropical animal forms that she instantly switches to when performing their associated action(you dash to become a newt, unlike other Shantae games where you would become a newt to gain a dash). In place of her transformation dances, Shantae gains other abilities from her new half-genie friends that reveal secrets, damage enemies, and create new paths. I like both of these features, but the instant transformations are the real star improvement this game has over others in the series.- Great visuals, including animated cutscenes! Each area has a distinct look, character designs are nice and clean, etc.  Checks all the boxes for being a nice game to look at. The music is also good, and there's plenty of the jokes and fanservice expected of a Shantae game.- While the game is pretty easy to clear, there are plenty of secrets to look for and things to do. If you want a little more out of it, you have a NG+ option and speedrun challenges!CONS- While I love the instant transformations, it's a notable annoyance that the digging and swimming forms work pretty much the same way, except you can't even fight enemies while swimming. Considering the amount of time you'll spend backtracking in these forms, it'd be nice to have more variety in gameplay.- The genie powers you unlock are cool, but they also kill most of the opportunities for puzzles - the answer is always "find a thing and do a dance at it." The same process applies to secrets. The last dance you unlock in particular has a long animation and is associated with a specific set of secrets that have very few hints as to their locations - unless you're also constantly checking everything with another dance. (assuming you don't get frustrated and look up a guide)- The shooting gallery minigame took me longer than any other single thing in this game. Don't expect a challenge unless you make it for yourself(i.e. speedrunning).

_childDocuments_.review: I'm forever grateful to the close friend of mine who bought me this game; they're a great person and I respect them immensely. Shantae and the Seven Sirens, however, does not get the same kind of compliment from me. I knew I'd miss Jake Kaufman's music in this game, and that feeling only grew after hearing the intro theme, which sounds like something right out of a bad anime fandub. The retro tunes also don't feel very catchy or fun and are merely serviceable at best. My big problem with the game, however, is that it's not friendly to people with OCD, which I have.The map has no markers for collectibles unless they're plot-related, so I can only imagine how painful a 100% run would be, but even beyond that, the "reveal invisible objects" magic completely drained me of my will to keep playing. The idea that something potentially important is invisible with no obvious tell that it even exists is already less than pleasant to me, but there's one element that boosts this problem to the point of rendering the game unplayable for someone like me, is that the update to this game gives you an icon at the top of the screen to show when a room has something invisible in it.This is not the fix you'd think it is because THERE IS AN ICON FOR INVISIBLE CONTENT IN NEARLY EVERY ROOM IN THE GAME AND NOTHING SHOWS YOU ON THE MAP WHERE YOU'VE ALREADY FOUND SOMETHING. Making that realization exhausted me more than words can describe.On top of that, reveal costs MP to use, and that means constantly hiking back to the bathhouse or guzzling potions to regain your MP. It's so much work, so much anxiety, and man, I can't will myself to stick with the game as a result. I'm glad the new update allows for this game to have more quality of life updates and new ways to play (especially since one new mode gives you all the cards you'd otherwise have to deal with an agonizing grind for), giving fans more to do and get out of this game. Me, though? I'm just going to stick with Pirate's Curse and Half-Genie Hero.

_childDocuments_.review: I played SS after HGH back-to-back, and I have to say SS is way superior. Mapping, level design, puzzles, length, missions, powers, upgrades, etc. are improved in every way. The card system is an interesting mechanic, although only a handful significantly make life easier. As before, SS puts you in a bright, quirky, and charming world that gives you a light-hearted romp. It can be challenging, and it will take you a bit to figure out some boss fights--but it's not soul-crushingly difficult. There's also been a change to availability of magic pick ups, so there is a bit of resource management you'll need to pay attention to. The only thing I'll have to gig SS for is is the cutscene issues some players seem to have--I updated various codec packages, and was still getting artifacts and frozen screens. (Not horrible since you can find the cutscenes online.) All in all, a fun game--to consider how big an improvement SS is to HGH, I would rate SS with an A- whereas its predecessor HGH would get a B-.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this franchise and how they joke about themselves, it's very meta.The game is cheeky and fun, truly the best adaptation of Megaman platforming genre, with lovable characters, a decent balance in its abilities and dances, and great level design. The one thing I have to say about this game is that it's riding a fine line between that teen rating and mature. It's a fan service franchise for sure, but it's almost as if the devs are pretending it's not. Maybe they're trying to convince the ESRB? I dunno.I do have a bit of a gripe with this entry into the franchise though, and that's the use of fairly low budget animated cutscenes. I love that they took the time to have them done, I love that they're voice acted, and I do love that they really do add to the flavor of the experience as a whole. With that said, the lip syncing is bad, the animation is choppy, and the illustrative quality goes down the toilet in parts. But, I am picky because I am an artist and dislike that the game art content itself is at a much higher quality than the cut scenes. This will of course not affect my rating of the game.Overall: 8/10Art: 9/10Music: 9/10 (very relaxing stuff)SFX: 8/10Control: 8/10Is Shantae best girl?: 10/10Cutscenes: 5/10Would play with people watching me?: 2/10I recommend you dive into this franchise and fall in love with Shantae. But, not in that way. She's a friend you love, not an actual love. She's a virtual girl, of course you know that. I know that. We don't judge.

_childDocuments_.review: WayForward is really good at catching what made retro games so enjoyable. Shantae and the Seven Sirens is Metroidvania fun. If Samus were to use her hair as a whip and be scantily clad while belly dancing a bunch, you'd have Shantae. I'd say it this is a more forgiving entry than most into the vast library of Metroidvania's out there. If you purchase a key for this for sub $5, which is readily available online, then this is a heck of a fun bargain.

_childDocuments_.review: Ret-2 Go!After the seemingly out of nowhere announcement back in March of 2019, Shantae and the Seven Sirens is finally out and available on all major platforms. It's a game I was definitely excited to see more of, and the real lack of gameplay footage they had for a while was a bit odd at first, and the screenshots seemed to indicate something more 2D than the 2.5D foray with Half Genie Hero. Then the revelation that the game was already available on Apple Arcade in 2 parts... I started to get worried this wouldn't be the game I was hoping for.I was wrong.Seven Sirens is a return to form of sorts, ditching the MegaManX style exploration and level-by-level approach from Half Genie Hero, and going for the classic Metroidvania/Zelda approach that has been a part of every other Shantae game. On top of that, a few new mechanics have been added and others tweaked to make this a new style that takes the best of both styles. The Fusion Dances you get turns Shantae's usually dancing into a sort of tool rather than straight up transformations. You still do, but it's brief, and it's more towards exploration and uncovering secrets (sometimes, quite literally), but some do have utility with combat. The Fusion Transformations effectively serve as Shantae's new mobility, and function more contextually than having to transform via button press then using the new form to navigate. Instead, you transform based on what is needed, revert as soon as the action is done. This, in effect, converts the movement mechanics from Pirate's Curse into transformations, and I think it's a perfect complement to the overworld functionality of the dances.New to this game, are the Cards you can acquire from Monsters. This now allows some special buffs or changes to further customize Shantae to suite one's playstyle. Ranging from reduces magic consumption, more damage, more speed, conversions, etc... getting the cards active allows for some particularly interesting that give a wide range of varying playstyles.The humour of the series remains intact, and perhaps a bit more on-the-nose than usual, but for the most part, you wind up with the usual antics from the usual suspects, but it's all in good fun.If you enjoyed previous entries, you'll more than likely find yourself enjoying this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae games have been hit or miss in the past, but this game is easily the best in the series next to Pirates Curse. It isn't without its flaws, but for the most part, it's a fun time.If you're unfamiliar with the series, it's essentially a Metroidvania, except with cute girls and boobs plastered all over the map. But don't let that cutsie fanservice fool you. This game can be pretty challenging if you don't know what you're doing. (assuming you play on definitive mode) You play as Shantae, a belly-dancing half-genie who can harness magical abilities via dancing. She and her friends are on a vacation that is quickly interrupted when a handful of other genies vanish out of nowhere. Shantae must find and rescue these girls.Upon rescuing each girl, they share their own abilities with Shantae, granting her new powers that open new paths. The game is essentially a giant labyrinth. You have to explore and complete tasks in order to progress, until you reach a dungeon, which is basically a smaller, more puzzle oriented labyrinth.combat is fairly simple. Shantae's main attack is whipping enemies with her hair, but she can also utilize a multitude of purchasable items. For example, a ball that spins around Shantae, or a shield that protects from projectiles. all of these things can be upgraded as well, including the strength and speed of her hair whip.Music is a great mix of different genres, including old-school sounding chiptunes, and upbeat electronic music. (The boss battle theme is probably one of my favorites)The game looks beautiful. easily one of the best looking platformers I've played. Animations are smooth, everything is bright and colorful. and the character portraits are gorgeous.Speaking of animation, this game actually has a small amount of animated cutscenes, (The intro is actually made by Studio Trigger). You can definitely tell the other cutscenes weren't though... They do come off looking a bit "awkward" at times. but it's nothing insulting, and I respect the attempt at something so ambitious, seeing as their last game was literally crowdfunded.Most of the plot however, is delivered via text, with limited voice acting. Voice acting is serviceable, but it can be a bit distracting when random lines are voice acted. An option to turn them off would have been nice.The story and writing is again, serviceable. There's nothing mind-blowing here, and some of the writing can feel a bit corny, but it's mostly harmless silly fun. There are also some pretty funny 4th wall breaking occasions, and the ending was actually very well done imoWhen it comes to critiques, the main one is probably the fact that the game starts to feel a bit too much like filler towards the 2nd half. there were a couple times where I would do something and think to myself "Yeah they probably could have cut that part out and not have lost anything of importance.". For example. You rescue one of the girls, she tells you to go to some other place and bring her back a thing, except when you return, she's not there, but at a different part of the map for basically no reason, in which you have to go find her there instead.Also a lot of enemy placements can feel "cheap". But I chalk that up to not knowing how to utilize your arsenal because I struggled with this less as the game progressed. If you do it right, your character is essentially broken.Overall, I'd give this game an 8 out of 10. Definitely worth a play if you like Metroidvanias

_childDocuments_.review: Want to go on a new exciting vacation with Shantae and her friends? If so, then I'd say that Seven Sirens will be right up your alley.Despite the difficulty level feeling like its been lowered compared to Half-Genie Hero (which in itself was already fairly easy if you don't count the DLC), this new installment will keep you going for a long time as the series goes back to its Metroidvania roots with a very big map, plenty of eye-catching areas to explore, and of course, a wide variety of magic and dances you can use to come back for collectables and quest items you might have missed or couldn't get to the first time around.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my all time favorite games of all time for sure. I could be honeymooning, but I really enjoyed this game. It is a tad "short" with my profile saying I played the game for 8 hours at the time of writing this review (even though in game I beat it in 4?), but that's to be expected since none of the other Shantae games were ever too long and it's a Metroidvania is the same vein as Symphony of the Night or Aria of Sorrow. Speaking of which this game is a LOT LIKE Aria of Sorrow in many ways. There's a Monster Card system where randomly, an enemy will drop a card and depending on how many duplicates of that card you need (ranging from 1-10 in some cases) you can use the card's effect which range from Dash Speed increases, or Damage Reduction, or Magic Reduction, etc. It's lot like the Soul System in Aria of Sorrow or the Shards in Bloodstained. One major difference between this game and a game like Bloodstained or Aria of Sorrow is that Shante has "Zelda" Dungeons and they function a lot like "Zelda" Dungeons. Each Dungeon has a Map, 3 heart containers, Keys, Puzzles, and a Key Powerup that allows Shantae to complete the dungeon and open up the overworld map more. Bosses however don't work like "Zelda" Bosses where you need to use the Item to "beat them" Instead they work kinda like how Castlevania or Bloodstained Bosses work where you can use whatever magic you have or just whip with Shantae's Hair. And when the boss is defeated Shantae Warps out like Megaman does. And speaking of Megaman when Shantae falls in a pit or steps on a spike or you lose all your hearts she Explodes in a magic burst much like how Megaman explodes.Overall the gameplay is a mishmash of Metroidvania, Megaman, and Zelda. If you like any of those games especially a game like Bloodstained or Hollow Knight, I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I didn't entirely care for the game. The long loading screens between zones combined with it being overly too easy dulled the game experience, but as the game progressed it became more enjoyable. The game was still too easy though as monsters drop healing items far too often. Before the third boss I had almost all the upgrades already, maxed healing items, and I sat at the max of 999 coins for more than half the game due to not having a need to buy anything. It got to the point where I no longer cared if I got hit since an auto revive potion would save me if I didn't heal. Aside from that, the level design was fun. I got lost several times exploring the underground and had to resort to the map many times to know where I was. I really enjoyed the music. It has a retro feel to it that occasionally made me stop just to listen to them. Puzzles were nice but not complicated. However, there was one spot where you had to complete a portion of the map in a time limit that had me at the edge of my seat. Shantae also has 5 new transformations in this game (no returning transformations). Although I am all for new transformations, I was a little disappointed to realize that they were all pretty much reskins of older transformations since they pretty much did the exact same thing. Shantae also has 4 fusion dances which is completely new to the series. These were fine, but I would have preferred other transformations since that is what Shantae is all about.At some point I hope that the game gets trading cards and a badge progression. I think this is the only Shantae game that does not have it. If you are a long time Shantae fan, you will enjoy the game. If you are looking for more of a challenge, I would recommend Shantae and the Pirate's Curse as it is largely considered the best game in the series still.

_childDocuments_.review: I've not played any other Shantae game so no comparisons here. Overall this is a okay game, artstyle is cute though maybe the animations are a bit too bouncy. Game does not respect your audio settings on the splash screen and intro cutscene. Personally i almost quit due to the first bosses poor design but once you get past it they get better. Kept playing because writing is very funny, and was surprised when one of the spa attendants mentioning selling bathwater. _childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: To make it short:Did i have fun? Yes.But taking into account that this game is supposedly a celebration of 30 Years of Shantae, it certainly is quite bothersome that its weighed down by looking like a port of a mobile game. and i mean thats what it started out as and it still doesnt look bad, the opposite in fact, and the fully voiced cutscenes are awesome. It jsut bothers me that optically it seems to be a step down from Half Genie Hero.Apart from that there really is nothing to complain. The gameplay is the usual Shantae Gameplay, Whip everything in sight with your Hair and you should be good. But on top of that theres also the new Transformations which now fluidly combine into each other, enabling you to string multiple transformations together in midair, cancelling them and combining them for a movement that i havent seen so far in Shantae. And some of them are really fun for combat too!Speaking of combat, the bosses seem better than in Half Genie hero but that could just be me.The soundtrack is still banging as allways and all in all it seems to be the logical next step.A few things to complain before closing:Completing the game at 100% is pretty tedious, since there is no way of telling which areas you already found everything in so completing it basically just boils down to trying every power everywhere once you got them all.Also the Loadingscreens seem to have been programmed weirdly so they use the whole cpu, seemingly slowing down loading times and most importantly lagging out the whole pc, which gets especially annoying when streaming the game.But all in all its still a very fun Game, mostly not what i expected, but i mean this in a good way (well apart from the graphics sadly).Is it better then Half Genie Hero tho? I dont know about that right now, but i'd say after some more bug fixing patches and maybe fixing some translation errors it could very well be at least on par with it tho.Also HGH still has al the DLC which means it has more content rn and im not sure if Seven Sirens is ever gonna have DLC but i for one would enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the Seven Sirens is the fifth game in the Shantae series. Back is the large open areas from Pirates Curse and before. This game builds upon what Half Genie Hero did by bringing over the beautiful art and combining it with the more classic Shantae gameplay with updates of course. They added a card system which acts as a perk system that allows you to move faster while crouching or turn green gems into magic.I'm only an hour and a half in the game and it's damn good fun. I love the addition of anime cutscenes and even having the opening animated by Studio Trigger (Little Witch Academia, Kill La Kill) is amazing. As before Christina Vee is back to voice Shantae as well as to sing the opening theme to the game. I've waited several years for this game to come out and it certainly did not dissapoint although loading times need some fixing but outside of that the game is everything a Shantae fan wants.

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the Seven Sirens takes a step back from the platforming style of the past two series entries and returns to the pure metroidvania formula that we last saw in 2010’s Shantae: Risky’s Revenge. The game feels more immersive thanks to having one big interconnected world; it actually gave me some Super Metroid vibes in the deeper parts of the island, which was really cool. Shantae herself has a bunch of cool new abilities like being able to transform immediately without having to dance first, while dance moves are reserved for area-effect abilities like Seer Enhance, which reveals all the secrets on the screen. Seven Sirens is a much more focused game than its Kickstarter predecessor, Half-Genie Hero. No random bonus rooms or backer content – just a really good game that has everything it needs and trims off all the excess. There are short but beautiful animated cutscenes, tons of fun writing with the same silly sense of humor that we’ve come to expect from the Shantae games, and of course, lots of fan service. :) As for criticism, I’d say it’s too easy on first playthrough, and the random card drops (equipping the cards give Shantae small perks) are kind of annoying if you want to try and collect them all. The story – while good – doesn’t reach the same level of depth and intensity as Shantae and the Pirate’s Curse and left me feeling like they could have done more with it. Regardless, Seven Sirens is a really good game and I love the return to metroidvania style. I’d actually say this is my second favorite Shantae game behind Pirate’s Curse. (Rating: 8/10 “Very Good”)
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is the best Shantae game since Pirate's Curse. It doesn't quite reach the same highs as Pirate's Curse, but the game is way better than Half Genie Hero. This incarnation of the franchise leans even harder on the Metroidvania style of gameplay. I think I still prefer having multiple unique worlds instead of a single giant Metroid-style map. There's still a lot of fan-service, which has always been in this series, so take that for what you will. But behind that with this game, and especially Pirate's Curse, are very fun action platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably the most metroidvania-like in the series, though the difficulty isn't very high due to resources granted to the player, but most games in the series do that anyways.  It's certainly fun and some self-imposed challenges could be implemented to make it harder.  The game is also short enough to keep you begging for more.As far as technical issues, there was the 1-2 second hiccup after each dungeon, but it's very minor and I use an i5 with a budget graphics card.My main gripe with this game is that I'd like there to be better item tracking, something to let you know that you've collected something already and/or the ability to put notes on the map for pickups you can't reach yet.Overall, while this game is not the best in the series, it's still good.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game that axes a lot of complaints I had for the previous game, Half Genie Hero and with a recent update even more problems have been axed. I'll cover that in it's own thing. This is Shantae in it's most Metroid-like state possible, there's one large map that you explore but also dive into dungeons inside said map. You can explore more of the map as you unlock more transformations and powers. So what's improved over Half Genie Hero? Transformations are INSTANT and are all useful in their own ways. First Transformation, hit RT and you dash through the air as a newt+hit a wall and you are now climbing. I won't spoil later transformations but it's a similar idea. You still have a dance mechanic but that's for magic which helps you in other ways that aren't mobility. So things are much faster with no waiting around for things like the old dance mechanics. The art is even better in this game, going to all 2D visuals vs the stylized 3D BGs of HGH. Some things were 3D and drawn over but it's not something you'll notice unless you're an artist. Everything Gels together much better I feel visually, it's for the better!.This is probably the most I've seen crammed into Shantae's game, there's tons of bosses, more enemies and ..animated cutscenes?! Is this the early 2000s? We got an anime intro by Studio Trigger and cutscenes throughout the game by another studio. Which, others have complained about too and the animations are good, they're not studio trigger but if there wasn't that high a bar as an opening cutscene.... I think there'd have been less complaints. Comically the animation was likely made before the game's ideas were started because it has NOTHING to do with Seven Sirens. Not the setting, Shantae's friends aren't playable, nada. I've seen some complaints about the soundtrack. I have no idea what these people are on, there's plenty of good tracks and for once it's not remixes of tracks we've heard before. I'm not dissing Jake Kaufman, he's made great tunes and I frequently listen to them- but there's some nice tunes here and if you don't believe me? Look up "Coral Mine" on youtube. It's good stuff. Okay, so they've updated the game very recently and it makes load times much faster and they're some quality of life changes.I'm playing through it again and noticed that they've made hints for one of the quests (so far) meaning there's less hunting cluelessly and more traveling to said place. You can ignore it as it's only on your map in the menu. They also made the Dance Parlor challenge easier, before you had to hit every object without missing- now I think you just need to get over 100 gems?? IDK I did it on my first try vs not knowing what I needed to do. Complains then. Well the game is too easy and there is no hard mode (unless this was added in the patch, I've seen no notes to say there is one added) you have the usual Magic mode though.Why is it too easy? There's so, many, ways, to heal. Enemies drop hearts and/or food. Hearts instantly heal, food can be used at any time. You can also buy potions, auto-potions (heal upon death) and you can hold quite a few. There's even a spell that heals you on top of this. Then there's armor you can get later to boost defense & it's not hard to raise your max health a bunch with Heart Squids. There's also a card skill that lets you increase the health gained by food. Enemies drop food frequently so there's 0 need to buy any potions. Is this a deal breaker? No. It's still a fun game with a lot of charm. If the game is too easy? Try not to claim your heart squids or avoid the armor. Play with only the 3 hearts & food items. Should be enough to make the game harder.Other than that? I like the game a lot. I feel like they listened & instead of giving us too many transformations like in HGH they just went with simple ideas that are fun. (Did anyone like the Mouse transformation in HGH? No. And there's nothing like that here) So do I recommend it?Yes. I think it's more fun than HGH, they listened to the community & improved the gameplay in substantial ways that make it more fun. But if you're a stickler for "it's gotta be super hard to the point I bleed from my eyes with RAGE or it's not a good game" well maybe not.

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Genie Hero used more of a mission-based approach to the game, departing from the feel of exploration that Risky's Revenge and Pirate's Curse provided. Thankfully, Shantae and the Seven Sirens returns to what made those games such a fun and engaging time. There are large areas to explore and backtrack to, returning to a true Metroidvania feel that I loved about the older games. Seven Sirens provides plenty of help in returning to previous areas with the use of fast travels and quick, engaging movement abilities that make it fun to explore. This game also introduces Monster Cards that provide benefits to Shantae; there are plenty to collect and you can tinker your kit to your playstyle, making it more engaging. I haven't fully completed the game, but I already know this one comes with a high recommendation!

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the Seven Sirens is a wonderful return to form for the series. Instead of the level based format of Half-Genie Hero, it returns to the singular map structure similar to Shantae GBC and Risky's Revenge. Transformations are more fluid than ever. Forms are changed by a simple button press allowing for more movement freedom and less pauses in the action. This change makes Shantae's moveset seem much more agile and complete similar to her movement capabilities in Pirate's Curse. This game foregoes the 2.5d aesthetic used in Half-Genie Hero in favor of a 2d style. Although I am a fan of the former, the new direction looks great. The game's length is a pleasant surprise since it is longer than the other games in the series for a standard playthrough. Overall I am very happy with the direction they decided with this game, and I hope future entries in the series follow the same path.

_childDocuments_.review: If you just want to enjoy a Metroivania with cute girls, the game is basically for you.But if you want something new about the Shantae series, I don't recommend it. Beyond adding animation for cutscenes and some new power-up, the game feels less complete and polished than the previous game, Half-Genie Hero.Visually, it's always looking good.The power-ups are basically the same just with some extra.The story was never interesting and often dulls, as all Shantae games.I was really surprised with the direction WayForward took with hidden item and such, there's rarely a clue that lets you know you have to smash the ground, dig or "scan" the area and so, you end up spamming these abilities at random hoping to find something new.Something that also suprised me is how lazy the map was. There is no indication there is a hidden item like you can see on a Metroid's map. Not even a mark, anything that traces all the items you found.I remember in previous Shantae game having to be selective when shopping upgrades but in this game, it's a joke. After the first dungeon I was nearly sitting at 800 rupies without farming and constantly hitting the 999 limits. The game simply overflows with money, in a game where money has limited uses. You'll drop enough consummable to skip potions you can find in shops and will focus on diverse Spells and upgrade. That overflowing money feels like all the upgrade are handed to you and makes the money very uninteresting.Overrall, the game is good but feels like a "Lazy Shantae" with less transformation than before, the exact same magic with one or two new spells and just basically the same actions. Climb on walls, smash rocks... With of course some new abilities.I really wish that WayForward would innovate with the Shantae license, rather than exploiting the same recipe.But overrall a good game, if you expect the same gameplay as the previous one.

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the Seven Sirens is a major improvement over the previous title. Let's explore the ups and downs of the game (+, +/-, -, ?):+ The art style is beautiful. I think this might be the best-looking Shantae so far, even though I adore The Pirate's Curse.+ That opening animation kicks so much ass. The same goes for all the 2D animated stuff in the game.+ I love these new characters. Harmony is probably my favorite. I mean, anyone who can switch a bra holder's side in a flash is top tier, right?  is so damn cute! Love her!  have some "step-on-me-queen" energy, in a positive way.+ Thank god, the transformations are all good here. No flappy bird style horror! The platforming feels awesome, and I'm so happy this game scrolls so smoothly.+ The OST is as great as it's always been.+ The story is given enough time to be meaningful. I liked the story*, even though the plot twist wasn't much of a twist at all.+ This is the longest Shantae title. Oh hell yes! This is a blessing for us non-speedrunners.+/- Some gauntlet rooms are painful. Dodging all the attacks, when there are 5 to 10 enemies on screen, is kinda hard you know.+/- Enemies might respawn instantly when you move forward in a stage. Also, there are some endless spawning points in the game. Not sure if these are intentional, but it makes farming for stuff easy. Especially at the final dungeon of the game. Golden crabs everywhere.+/- The weapons are pretty good, but, as always, I only used some of them.-*The story is great, yes, but Risky's  plot is so meaningless. It barely plays any part in the story, and is probably here only because it justifies Risky being in the game. Yes, it is the , but still...- There are some enemies early on that use a homing attack. When you barely have any hearts, this can be really annoying. Also, the enemy attacks are way too powerful towards the end of the game. It's weird when mobs are way more dangerous than bosses.- I don't really like the monster card system. Some of them are really useful, but, I ended up using maybe 5 of them. I also somehow managed to miss about half of the cards.? The NPCs are moving like they're on double speed. It's a bit odd.Shantae and the Seven Sirens is a great Shantae title. It's a satisfying journey, even though there are some minor faults here and there. This is a great platformer for all you cool peeps out there. Dance, whip your hair and beat ass! 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:+ Beautifully animated graphics+ Anime cutscenes+ Fun and addictive gameplay+ A welcome return to Metroidvania+ Large map+ Banging soundtrackCONS:X Notably easy, with almost no balance.X No difficulty settings or challenge modes.X Little to find and collect within the labyrinth.Phil's capsule review: The fifth game in the Shantae series, Seven Sirens drops the hub world select screen of the previous two titles for an interconnected Metroidvania map. The change is good, and the adventure itself is a hair whipping, gem collecting, bikini armor wearing blast. Issues emerge, however, in the realm of balance. About halfway through the game, I was so overpowered and rich with money and health items I was almost invincible. Enjoyment of Seven Sirens may depend on how willing you are to NOT die, and there are no higher difficulty settings or challenge modes. Another problem has to do with what lies within the labyrinth, or rather, what doesn't. Once Shantae is able to fully explore the map, there isn't much worth discovering within it. Still, if you enjoy the Shantae games and have made it up to here, there's no reason not to pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: I have quite mixed feelings about this game on the whole. Out of the four I've played, I'd put this ahead of Risky's Revenge but behind Half-Genie Hero and Pirate's Curse. Ultimately, I gave it a thumbs up because I  did enjoy it, albeit with caveats. What did I like? The main plot resolves in a convoluted but pretty interesting way. Risky Boots has this setup where it's like, heads she wins, tails you lose. Risky knows that Shantae has that irrational reformist belief in her and definitely abuses it in what she likes to present as being benignly Machiavellian by the end of the story.I actually do think the game is more fun after you get the healing dance, balance concerns aside. In the early game, enemies are often grazing you due to their generous hitboxes and the slight trickiness of positioning Shantae when hair-whipping. You're squishy then and healing isn't plentiful, so the ability to self-heal acts as a solid quality-of-life enhancement. I also quite like the other half-Genies and their personalities, even if they're a bit simple. I'm not really sure why the traditional monkey got traded out for a newt transformation, but it is fun to expand your transformation set and more fully explore the world. By and large the pacing of doing fetch quests and then dungeons is solid.What am I less into? In general, I think the bosses while aesthetically solid aren't tuned well - they're a little static and if anything seem to get easier as the game progresses. I was expecting a little more from the last boss in particular - it's very easy to outheal the simple mechanics. I think the droppable food mechanic basically was a waste of time. Only a few of the monster cards are really worth using and I think it naturally would be difficult to design a balanced set of so many in this genre - maybe just keep them as token collectables. I found scouring for every nugget annoying given one of them ended up being in a room where the dance icon didn't appear - I also felt that just spamming a bunch of dances when icons appear on the screen was unengaging. This was my least favourite aspect of 100%-ing the game. The music lacks an overall identity I feel. It's technically fine with a couple of bangers - hello Armor Town theme! - but there are some really derivative and interchangeable themes obviously based on popular franchises like Pokemon and Mario. That, to be fair to the composer, is partly an issue with how a lot of the areas in the game lack distinctness and individuation in their visual design and mechanics. Super Metroid was able to make several underground biomes quite distinct in character, for example. The only dungeon that I thought had an overly interesting meta-design was the third one, the Sea Vent Lab. The first one is fine but very simple, the second one isn't too bad but the sand-digging mechanic just isn't very interesting. The fourth is ok but unusually short and the fifth is centered around a monster rush time-trial which I could personally have lived without. The last dungeon is really linear, it's often best to just skip past enemies and rush through quickly. I'm a little critical here in that this is an experienced developer, I think some of these issues shouldn't necessarily exist in this way if you're several games down the line. It wouldn't have taken a lot to bring things a couple of notches up across the board.But, it is a working, functioning game. It is decently fun. It's fine, but it's not excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: An overall decent entry into the Shantae series, that tries something new by taking the main cast outside of Scuttle Town. Unfortunately however I feel like this game is lacking some of the series' usual charm. Some usual side characters are completely missing due to the change of locale, the ones who are present get very little screentime (except for Bolo), and the music isn't quite as great or memorable as that of The Pirate's Curse or Half-Genie Hero.In regards to artstyle, gameplay and waifus however, this game definitely has the usual WayForward quality. I have read of players complaining about the lack of difficulty, so I started my first blind playthrough on the Definitive mode for some extra challenge. The Definitive mode was definitely more difficult than the past games, and wasn't until one of the last bosses that I truly caught up in terms of power.All in all I can definitely recommend this game, but I would not place it above The Pirate's Curse or Half-Genie Hero. Let's see what WayForward can cook up next.
