_childDocuments_.review: Looks good with cute character designs, nice animations and new cinematics. Controls are responsive. Transformation abilities are now tied to button presses or certain types of environments instead of being a form you remain in giving you some easily accessible abilities to keep you mobile or out of an enemy's reach. You gain a form for dashing for speed or to get past enemies, swimming, digging, crushing blocks, and double and triple jumping. Transformations work well and some can come together for well made areas but take away from having well made other forms to remain in. The swimming and digging is never fun and never leads to any interesting stage design, and the other abilities really only come out at there best in the final area where they seemed to finally try to put the slightest bit of challenge in the game.It is absolutely terrible as a metroidvania style game. They clearly didn't have much actual game and used the genre as a lot of developers do to make dull, small, repetitive, simplistic areas, to force needless backtracking, and give you things hidden all over to find to pad the length. The issue with the hidden objects being that there is nothing of value to find, you can dig up statues and shock machines but most will just drop a few gems to buy potions or the magic abilities that there is never any real reason to use. You can find hidden heart squids to increase your maximum life but I decided to just get the achievement for finding them all and never using them to add to my life because this is one of the easiest games I've played. You can already heal with magic that you can get to constantly regenerate, heal by finding hearts, and heal from eating all the food items that drop from enemies. Enemies can drop cards and you can trade gold nuggets for others that will give you passive abilities like getting more gems, doing more damage with certain moves, crawling faster, etc nothing that makes any interesting changes or that is really needed and further slows the game down if you are trying to get a specific type of card.The game introduces other half genie characters that have almost no character and that you spend next to no time with. If there was some better ideas and initiative here you might be able to play as them, learn more about the game's world from them, make them more interesting characters to appear in future games, have access to different kinds of magic through meeting them. Instead, all they do is get you a new dance that is said to have something to do with their powers. You get an ability to see hidden platforms, walls you can walk through, or items in the environment, the platforms are just something that you have to do when you get to certain areas, the items are just things that often would give you know idea that they are there unless you just run around constantly using that dance and are never useful. You can use one to heal yourself and purify water, one to shock enemies and machines, and one to cause an earthquake (with no real visual effect other than shaking) to damage enemies or open paths in the environment. The only time any of these are remotely interesting is that some enemies are weak to them in certain ways, healing can change a type of enemy to an ally or partially give back bodies to zombies and shocking enemies that spin on a metal pole can lead to new animations and an instant kill. The characters were both disappointing mechanically and narratively.The way you unlock and need to possess the abilities they give you also makes the metroidvania essentially completely linear. This was a series that had no real reason to go back to this style compared to the stage selection of the last two, and would just be a much better series if they ditched the exploration entirely, made linear stages, and gave you fun abilities to use in interesting ways (maybe some character switches) kind of like they did in only the very last section of this game. For a game that wants you to backtrack it also has unusually long load times, not that it will make you sit around for minutes at a time, but much longer than you would expect for a title that should barely see any.If you want an easier game that plays well or want to get something for someone new to the genre I would be ok recommending this when it is on sale. The asking price is ridiculously high for something as short and as unambitious as this when you have such a wide variety of other games in the genre (even the past games in this series) available instead. This is serviceable (maybe better if you just play through it and ignore hidden objects) but it really makes it seem like they are either completely out of ideas for the series or that they are ok coasting off of the character of Shantae and maybe they can sell you on some scantily clad other character designs to attract old fans when they skimp on content. As someone who was unintentionally wearing a Shantae T-Shirt while writing this, I was pretty disappointed.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: Story:In this one, it initially follows a vacation, when the half genies are kidnapped. And as Shantae proceeds, while it is a rescue effort. She does learn a bit more about what the genies left behind. It also gets into Risky's plan, and why everything here happened.System:Mostly the same, with the Dance transformations changed to like special moves. And the animal transformations linked more to the movements. This is cool and all, and the concept was nice. Though, pretty sure peeps play to turn into a monkey. That aside, it could have been a better execution if the concept was combined with actual transformations.The map as well is a bit larger overall.Animations:Amazing art style, and amazing mini animated cutscenes.Music:Amazing as usual.Overall:This is a really good game, and it does correct a number of issues the previous entries had. The platforming, as well as the difficulties in them are much better managed here.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best Shantae game since Pirate's Curse.  It combines the signature transformations of Shantae with the free-flowing gameplay of Pirate's Curse.  It's also probably the most Metroidvania of any Shantae game since the original with a large, interconnected map to explore.  Highly recommended for both Shantae fans and newcomers!
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae is back with another sunny adventure, and this one is a lot better than the previous one ! Shantae and the Seven Sirens is basically what Half-Genie Hero should have been with the transformations and the result is a game that's way more engaging and fun to play.If you've played Half-Genie Hero, you probably remember how the main gimmick of the game, the transformations, felt sluggish and pointless. They were handled much better this time : they're instant at the press of a button or activated whenever they're needed. This simple change makes the whole exploration part smoother than ever before, in a game that is now a real Metroidvania.Going back to places you've visited previously whith new abilities is rewarding and that's how you will be collecting heart containers, nuggets and monster cards. Those monster cards are drops from enemies you can equip and provide a small (or substantial) boost to Shantae's abilities, while nuggets are just regular collectibles used to get the rarest monster cards. The art style is great for all the main characters as well as the bosses, and the design of the island as a whole creates a believable world for an adventure you won't want to drop until the end, 8 hours later. That's 8 hours of Shantae dancing, and you may even join her because the soundtrack, different for every zone, is an absolute banger once again.With all these qualities come a few odd design choices, and some issues specific to the Shantae franchise.As usual, the beginning of the adventure is considerably harder than when you have access to healing and more health at the end, and goes from rather hard to too easy. The objectives and their locations are not always obvious and easy to follow, so getting lost can be annoying. Thankfully, this definitive version comes with a higher difficulty mode and a compass, that will greatly help.The bosses are also an improvement over the last episode, even if some of them are more of a health/healing check than they are a skill check. However, the Risky Boots fight is the same as it was last time, and it happens five times ! It's a good fight, but come on... That made me realize that it may be time to stop trusting her Shantae, hmm ? Hmm ?Finally, the dances used around the map for exploration and even story progression consume a lot of magic, so if you're out when you need to use them, you have to backtrack and hope enemies drop some refills... An odd and impractical decision for sure.This doesn't really impact the overall experience, as Shantae and the Seven Sirens is a great game and probably one of the best in the series. It may not offer as much variety in gameplay as Pirate's Curse, but it's a trip you don't want to miss if you're a Shantae fan.A holiday I'd go back on anytime, and a refreshing . The Shantae series is back on the right track !

_childDocuments_.review: The follow up to Half-Genie Hero, no crowdfunding required this time!So, I generally had fun with our dear half-genie's latest jaunt, but I have a few things to bring up here.Why do most of the usual magic spells (Fireball, Pike Ball, etc) feel so underpowered? The only ones at all useful to me were bubble shield and third tier pike ball. Even the dances were underpowered and it was way faster for me to just whip everything, and given how speedy you can get Shantae's one basic attack, everything else becomes moot. The monster cards, while some were useful, just got rendered worthless by the time I even got enough of them to drop (or drop at all), and some just seem to have no use whatsoever because you're never put into a position where they'd be useful (frog speed up comes to mind--I cannot think of a situation outside speedrunning where that'd actually be a benefit). It just seemed like a massive afterthought.Some of the bosses were actually interestingly thought out, if predictable. Most of the time, though, I could just cheese bosses with the third level attack damage/whip speed/bubble shield (completely invincible as long as your mana holds out) and just pop food items to keep it going since the game seems to be over-generous with how frequently they drop. Seriously, the game just . You have to be actively ignoring your health for it to ever really be an issue.On that last point, New Game + will probably be even easier to cheese since you get less defense, but more magic, so just keep up that strategy and literally be nigh unstoppable. We shall see. Depends what I get to keep.Map feels way smaller than past games too. Some of the cutscenes and damage-sponge enemies make it feel longer than it ultimately . WayForward has returned to the series' Metroidvania roots, a change from the level-based progression of Half-Genie Hero, which is nice, but the game still feels very linear and doesn't seem to encourage much exploration. They aren't Sonic '06 levels of bad, but they get annoying very quickly when you're otherwise blasting through an area going for some of the speed-based ending images--thankfully it does not seem like load screens count towards this, but they're still irritating.That all said, the art style from Half-Genie Hero returns, and the cast is as cute as ever. The FMVs are quite pretty, and Cristina Vee giving Shantae a somewhat "bratty" voice actually still works really well for her character. (Or maybe that's just how her voice is, either way, it suits Shantae well.) Writing is about what I'd expect from a Shantae game, though a lot of the cast just feels...there. Underused, really. End of the day, I'd give it a 6/10. It's fun and engaging, but it feels like it could have done far more. Nothing wrong with it functionally, but it just feels...painfully short. I'd wait for this to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best of the Shantae games.This time they changed the formula (slightly) to be full metroidvania. Most of the other games have a sort of metroidvania structure, but the zones are all self-contained levels. This time, the entire world is interconnected, and you peel it apart slowly as you acquire new powers. In general, I think this change is great for the series, and hope they continue this trend going forward.On top of the interconnected over-world, the game features 6 self-contained dungeons that are a nice change of pace to exploring. The boss fights in this game are also the best in the series in my opinion.As always the character design is on point. The story is never anything too special, but personally I play the games for the character interactions and their various (mis)adventures, and this game delivers those. If you have enjoyed any of the previous Shantae games, you will likely enjoy this one too.

_childDocuments_.review: I have tried playing most of the Shantae games and I dropped most of them. The only one I've completed was Half-Gene hero, and that was mostly because I kickstarted it and forced myself to finish it.I'm very glad to report, this is the most fun I've had with a Shantae game ever. It's very approachable. They made transformations into small forms instant, which lets the player move in a very fluid way. There are dances, but now they are just screen-wide effects. More than 50% of players finished the game, based on Steam Achievements, which is pretty huge.There are things I didn't really like. Most powerful upgrade to your damage is speed in which Shantae can hit, which means damage is proportional to your mashing speed. There were some corridors where I had troubles keeping up. I'm probably too old for it, but I'd love different ways to increase "DPS", or maybe multitap button that attacks with full speed. I guess I can do it with steam input.There are cards you can collect. They drop randomly from enemies. You can equip 3 of them, and change as you want. With 50 cards you'd think there would be interesting builds, but in reality you always keep 3 best cards on you. You'll never give up damage up for climbing speed. Especially when there are only few places where you have ropes to climb on, and none of them require you to climb faster. Maybe it would work better if different cards had different cost to equip, or there were card types and you could equip only one of each type. The bigger issue though, is the fact the card drops are completely random, and you have no way to influence the odds. In Castlevanias there's usually luck stat, or passive buffs to drops which you can utilise to get better drops. Here if it is 3% it is 3%. You then can spend 2 hours just trying to get that single card. Moreover, cards with higher drop rate require multiple copies to be usable. It's a pain, and I really ignored the cards most of the time. But some of the best cards are actually only purchasable from NPCs, and you can get nuggets to purchase them while exploring the world.All in all card system isn't very good, but inoffensive.The new dance-spells allow you things like seeing invisible objects, and take quite a lot of your magic meter. With MP reduction item equipped I could use 5 of the cheapest spell before I would run out of MP. The game will tell you when there's a reason to use a spell on current area, so you won't need to blindly use it everywhere. Additionally there are visual prompts on the stage itself which you'll recognise as related to one of the spells. But, the spell for seeing invisible is useable on almost every room, since there are hidden items everywhere. And some rooms are very wide or high, and the spell only works on a current screen, so you might need to use the spell 5+ times just to find the hidden item(s). It's a problem early on, when you might not have many MP potions yet, and magic doesn't recover automatically. Around the half of the game you basically get infinite MP, when it stops being a problem. Too bad this is the first spell you get. All other spells are used MUCH less often.Overall the difficulty of this game is very low. You get tons of food items from killing monsters, which heal your HP(and with proper card also magic). You can purchase very cheap health potions, and auto-health potions, which cure you fully when you would die. You can hold 9 of each, allowing you to ignore all damage and just mash attacks as fast as you can.The health upgrades are rather easy to find. You have a counter of health upgrades in each dungeons, so you know when you found them all. Most of the upgrades are in caves, which you have marked on the map, so it's easy to look them up. Overall finding all health upgrades and gold nuggets is pretty fun.If you want to challenge yourself you can try getting trough the game with no health upgrades, which probably is balanced, as even with all the healing items you'll need to start avoiding stuff. There are also "cheat" modes when you just want to have fun. There's a mode with all cards unlocked that allows you to use all cards at once etc. So no matter if you're a speed-runner, item collector or just a regular player you'll probably find a way to enjoy Shantae. For collectors there's tons of unlockables.It's a minor gripe, but I would like fast-travel rooms to just show me the map and let me choose which other fast-travel room I want to get to. Like most other metroidvanias. This one makes you stand on platforms, that teleport you to certain part of the island, but I always had to first check the map to make sure which platform did I really want. While the game looks glorious in 4k, it also looks fine-ish in 720p on Steam Deck. The scaling makes everything look a little bit blurry, but still pretty. You can limit CPU power to 3W and get 4+ hours of play with 60FPS and no drops. Nice.One small issue are loading times between major zones. If you play at 4k it takes about 7-10 seconds to load from SSD. The same zones load under 1-2 seconds when playing with 1080p, as the game loads smaller assets. So in a funny twist, you might get much faster loading times on Steam Deck than on your beefy PC. That said, there are only about 10 major zones, and each of them is built of many rooms, which load instantly afterwards. It only becomes a bit of an issue late, when you're trying to find all collectibles.All in all, this is nowhere near the top of my metroidvania toplist, it's qute, has catchy music and is very enjoyable to play. It doesn't take that much time to beat, and there is nothing really wrong with it. I hope they keep the quality with their next game, and maybe improve the systems from this game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, out of the three Shantae games that I've played, I would say this is the second best overall. Better than Half-Genie Hero but not quite as good as Pirate's Curse.The animated cutscenes done by Studio Trigger were a real treat. I enjoyed them a lot, especially as a big fan of their other works. The game's presentation overall is fantastic, beautiful sprite work and the music was great too, which is to be expected from this series.Game itself was a lot of fun too, I'm generally a fan of Metroidvanias and this is a good Metroidvania. I did find myself getting lost more easily than in the previous games however, but that could've just been my fault for not paying enough attention.That being said there is one glaring issue that the previous games didn't have, and that is the lengthy loading times. I'm not sure what happened here, but I definitely don't recall them taking this long before. This issue could've been exacerbated by me playing off my HDD instead of the SSD, but I'm not sure just how much that would've changed things, as it seems I'm far from the only person with this problem. Entering a new area by accident was a lot more annoying as a result.But aside from that I do definitely recommend this game, especially if you're a fan of the previous entires. Oh and yes, the girls are all very cute. I know that'll be the most important buying factor for some...

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Shantae games, and this is easily my new favorite. The cutscenes are beautiful and the soundtrack is unique and catchy. What's more, you don't need to play other Shantae games in order to understand this one (although some conversations might not make too much sense, but context clues help)Unlike previous Shantae games, you don't go to a level select screen in order to progress. It keeps the world open, but blocks you out of areas by requiring certain transformations or powers. Basically, if I had to describe this game using other games, I'd describe it as a platformer with the smooth controls and art of Hollow Knight, the difficulty of Super Mario Bros., and the level design and progression of Legend of Zelda.

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to make a return after completing its prequel: Half Genie Hero. Knowing Wayforward, this game would be pretty much a breeze to run through, and while it was, I couldn’t help but notice improvements, as well as recycled mechanics from 1/2 Genie Hero. The first thing that got me hooked with the game was the opening animation, brought to you by the guys who animated the Kill La Kill and Tengen Toppa Gurren Lagann series, that's right... Studio TRIGGER. It's very catchy. I wondered if the game was gonna be as good as the last one, and to an extent it was, here I’ll be covering the pros and cons about this game, and why I think there were some decisions that would've made the game a bit replayable or rather easy to navigate through. I could not finish the game without a guide. This is due to the navigation being so contrived in this game. I managed to beat the game in under 8 hours, as of this review.The story takes after the events of Half Genie Hero as mentioned previously, with you and your allies going into a vacation on a sweet island resort. The game has you blasting through dialogue with sometimes what seems like childish, comedic writing, which at times got a few genuine laughs out of me, since the Shantae series aren't really known for their writing, but rather its plotlines and art style.  The Story keeps you invested in what's going on in a straightforward manner. Upon rescuing them, you learn about the islands true identity and learn about the Sirens. There are also new faces for you to remember in this installment of the franchise. I will not spoil its ending, Play it for yourself. The game doesn't take itself too seriously . The game is short though, and the story a bit forgettable at best, but I liked it.The game is jam-packed with tunes, themes and songs that can instantly put you in a state of excitement, contemplation, or sheer enjoyment. the game acknowledges its retro styled gameplay and each of their themes fit well with their distinctive levels. My favorite track is the Sea Vent dungeon theme, its hardcore for a Retro Volcanic theme. Overall, I enjoyed the music for the most part.So, what makes it different from any other Metroidvania styled game. Well, the Shantae series prides itself for its easy to play-hard to master combat system that has always circled around in the since the beginning, with the exception of Risky's Revenge or the original Shantae game. your main weapon is your hair. you whip it, tremendously fast mind you, and dispatch enemies before they land hits with projectiles or by touching you, not to the level of bullet hell, you use Dances to work your way through levels. There's a new mechanic, Cards. which are essentially perks. Spells are your secondary weapons. Speaking about the dances, These, while helping you advance through the game, can be really overpowered when combined with certain cards to level their cost or their Damage Output. it gets to the point, where I felt invincible, I never truly died. I didn't feel that challenged for the most part. If anyone remembers the dances from the previous games, they would notice that they have been swapped out for Fusions. You turn into different animals, species with distinct abilities, like Half Genie Hero and get through puzzles.I always had and at this point have a love for the game's art direction. and with the integration of TRIGGER, the well-known studio for bringing us the Little Witch Academia, Gurren Lagann and the Kill La Kill series, it truly is fitting for a game like the Shantae series to compliment with their talent the game's cutscenes while short, have a chance to express the atmosphere, or characters beautifully, while keeping it in the formula of a game rather than an anime script would. The game has 1-Upped themselves in terms of polished artwork. it is by far the best good-looking game in the franchise ever since the leap from Pirate's Curse Retro to Half Genie Hero Smooth Art style. The game blends these two perfectly, but its essence still lies within the music. The Character and Enemy Design is by far the bread and butter of the game. Visual effects wise, it is indifferent from the other games, it is what makes and sets the genre for Shantae. The game isn't heavily reliant on graphics, in fact, the game runs at perfect 60fps with little to no effort. I was able to play the game on a GTX 1050 Max-Q with ease, and even if you can't run the game smoothly on its first, there are a few options that let you tweak with the performance in terms of detail. The game is flourished with colorful backdrops and thematic scenery. it looks incredibly detailed despite it being set in a 2D environment.The game is laughable in terms of difficulty, however, one thing about these games that you must keep in mind, its if you choose it to be difficult. you can take the ultimate No Heal/ Heart Upgrade challenge and you will truly suffer perfection,as late game enemies can one shot you, and even with the HP Saver upgrade you get mid game, unlike the previous games, where you can go up to 75% less Damage taken, you can only go up to 25%. You can choose how you approach the game and its boss battles. The game is quite fun even if it’s not as difficult. it’s a relaxing game if you approach it casually, like your normal Metroidvanias, filled with challenges, collectibles, and exploration. It's a fun game in general, and I’m fairly sure their goal was to make it as accessible to everyone, not just for its simple difficulty, but rather its flexibility.I feel like WayForward, after realizing what they did with Risky's Revenge, stopped making these boss fights hard enough to challenge people anymore ever since I noticed their contrast with Half Genie Hero. However, this doesn't go to say it isn't challenging, just not as much given by its flexibility and abused forgiveness. In terms of the actual bosses themselves, I guess it’s fair to describe them as accessible to everyone. Kids can even take this as their first game with bosses and come up on top. The battles can be short and with quite simple mechanics which are followed by the corresponding Dance/Fusion you previously learned. Their attacks are well telegraphed, and again, they aren't as aggressive as previous games.It's a very casual game to pass through in a short amount of days, but while doing so, you can learn to appreciate that even with poor gameplay choices, it’s  your call whether you want the game to be hard or not. And even then, it’s still fun, its great looking, and has some love put into it. the voice acting is formidable since it’s a cheerful game that doesn't take itself too seriously, and even the game pokes fun at that fact in its characters breaking the fourth wall. It's a highly rated game with a short story and I can appreciate the love it was put into it. And with this, I'd say this game is highly recommended if you wanna get started with Metroidvanias, it’s a wholesome experience packed into 7 hours of gameplay. However, there are a few things in mind, and it’s that you can easily get lost in the game from its nonlinear mapping. you go all over the place with this one. and even given that the Warp Room is missing the areas labels; you must memorize the map's layout. With that being said, the game is a genuinely nice cup of tea for those looking forward to exploring the Metroidvania genre in its artistic aspect, you won’t regret it. If it weren’t for its difficulty however, this game would top other games of its genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Having followed Shantae since her humble Game Boy beginnings, it really brought a tear to my soul seeing just how far this series has come with what is easily the best installment to date. Taking place in a big open world packed with as much charm as ever, Seven Sirens is a fine mesh of the best elements from past games in the series along with new mechanics that flow nicely together. Instant transformations feel great and are more than just keys to exploring new areas: the Newt Dash is useful for dodging attacks and picking off weaker enemies as one example.The generous amount of recovery items has not changed, but those looking for a challenge will still find it should they choose not to exchange any Heart Squids and/or try out the New Game + (which is a bit of a misnomer as it's actually Magic Mode from Risky's Revenge: a fresh start in a new outfit that doubles maximum magic and damage taken), not to mention the speedrun challenges.If you have yet to experience what this full-fledged half-genie has to offer, now's the time.

_childDocuments_.review: While Half Genie Hero was a pretty big departure from the metroidvania style of previous Shantae games, Shantae and the Seven Sirens attempts to bring it back to the metroidvania style, again. It does this with a lot of additional bells and whistles that make the game feel more polished. That said, however, there were some areas that I felt it wasn't as good as some previous titles, particularly Shantae and the Pirate's Curse. One way in which it didn't feel as good was in the music. The music was pretty bland compared to previous titles. Part of the reason for this is likely due to Jake Kaufman not having worked on it, despite working on all of the previous Shantae games. The music wasn't bad, but it just didn't have the same life and energy to it as Kaufman's works. One of the things that the previous games did fairly well was the humor with the fourth-wall breaks, silly jokes, and fun dialogue. This one, however, struggled to capture it and there were several points of pretty cringe dialogue. For instance, one of the villains in the game, when you defeat him, he says  There were a few such moments like that in the dialogue with characters that just felt odd for the characters and was sort of cringe instead of humorous. That leads me to another problem I had with the game: the characters didn't really feel like they did before. It's a bit difficult to describe, but it was as if the dialogue and character development was by someone else. I suspect one reason for this was the voice acting which felt like it altered how the characters come across in previous titles. Another reason is parts of the dialogue felt like it was out of character or characters were saying things that I couldn't imagine them saying in previous games. Another reason, of course, as I previously mentioned, were jokes simply falling flat. For example, anyone who has played previous Shantae games knows that Shantae's catchphrase is "Ret-2-Go!" I played through the entire game and never heard her say it once, neither in-game or in dialogue. This is obviously a more minor example, but it just seems odd to me that she wouldn't use her main catchphrase that she uses all the time in previous games. Another problem I had with it was that the boss battles were pretty lackluster. The only boss battle that was decent was the final boss battle, and even that one had problems with it. Some bosses were just too simple and boring, or they were over before they even started. The ones that did last a little time were usually just damage-sponge bosses or ones that required a particular timing that just dragged the battle out longer. None of them were really all that memorable or had memorable or interesting designs. The animations are a nice addition, but looked very low budget, outside of the opening animation by Studio Trigger. The in-game cut-scenes look more like high-quality fan animations. Considering that they had no animations before, it's an obvious improvement, but some scenes looked like they needed extra work because there was a noticeable difference in quality between the opening and the in-game cut-scenes.  That said, it's still a pretty good entry in the series and still worth playing. It's not a bad game by any stretch of the imagination, but it still doesn't manage to live up to the very high bar WayForward set with Shantae and the Pirate's Curse. In many ways, it feels like the sort of metroidvania style Shantae everyone wanted Half Genie Hero to be, but knew it couldn't because of budgeting, so if that's what you're looking for, check it out. There's a lot to explore and secrets to find in it.

Which can make larger/stronger enemies feel a bit lackluster. Bosses are also relatively easy, but they still feel like a boss battle. _childDocuments_.review: I am a gigantic fan of this series and have played everything from Risky's Revenge onward (I never owned a Gameboy Color so I sadly missed out on the original). Like many of the reviews have said, Seven Sirens is essentially a halfway point between Pirate's Curse and Half Genie Hero. But for every step forward there's also a step back or to the side.The animation is as gorgeous as ever, but environments are now pure 2D instead of HGH's 2.5D look. Speaking of environments, the majority of this game takes place underwater in a big submarine, so most of what you'll be looking at is claustrophobic industrial areas (with some details like "this is the mossy area" or "this is the leaking area") interspersed with, admittedly, a few gorgeous views of the ocean floor, and a few areas on land too.This is also the first Shantae game without Jake Kaufman's music, and while a good number of the old themes appear, and the new composers do a solid job with the return to a chiptunesy vibe, it's a step back from the bombastic, orchestrated brilliance of HGH.Gameplay-wise it is everything you'd expect from a Shantae game with some nice new additions. Collectible cards give you passive bonuses to your various abilities and items, dances focus on AOE powers rather than transformations, and transformations are instant shifts for very brief, specific uses, like dashing, swimming, or stomping. Sadly this does mean my personal favorite transformation, the Elephant, is MIA, but is replaced with a tortoise so... that's quite nice. But I do feel like we don't get to "know" the new forms as well as we did the old ones, so I hope our Elephantine friend can make a trumpeting return next time around.In the end, even with its more limited scope compared to HGH, it's impossible to hate on Shantae. There is still so much fun and humor on display here that it's well worth the adventure through the Sunken City, and the backend is likely in a better place for future installments than it was after the previous entry. Pick it up and have a grand ol' time!

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent combination of all the Shantae games in one package. We get a large overworld map to explore, movement options on a single button, and the beloved Shantae-style dungeons make a return.+ Opening animation by Studio Trigger+ Fast and fluid sidescrolling gameplay+ New half-genie waifus, new boss waifus, and Bolo+ Animated cutscenes+ Change your playstyle with card drops+ Great chiptune music- Loading screens when changing zones are a bit longer than I feel they should be (especially on an SSD)- Just 1 crash during an event and lost 15 minutes. Save whenever you can!- Voice acting is pretty minimal- Somewhat inconsistent artstyle- Too many healing items, making the game very easy- Getting 100% is tedious and very unrewarding. I really want to get into why this is an issue:If you want to get 100%, seriously just use a guide unless you have a ton of free time on your hands. Getting all the items requires you to use dances at the right spot. The real problem here is that there is practically no indication as to where you need to do these dances aside from maybe some non-hostile enemies wandering around... that disappear when you are at the end of the game! Having to use your item reveal dance at every corner was a pretty horrible design choice by WayForward. The last two Shantae games did not require anything close to this and was very rewarding once you completed it. After getting 100% in this game, I didn't feel particularly accomplished. I just felt like I wasted some of my time. I think something like this is easily fixable through a patch such as an item indicator by zone like in the previous games.100% completion aside, I'm having a hard time deciding if I believe this is the absolute best Shantae game to date, beating out Pirate's Curse. It is truly a blast to play and was well worth the wait.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: My scores/reviews are almost always based on having bought the game at close to the "lowest historical price" on steam at time of purchase.Quick score: 3/5Notes: Another Shantae game, and another super polished, but extremely casual and low difficulty game. The world is decent and has a good amount of variety visually.Characters and dialogue, while very "fan servicey", are generally good and I never felt the urge to just start skipping all the dialogue.The game looks great and plays great, but the game has basically zero challenge. The combat is completely trivialized by having unlimited health/healing options and is overall incredibly spammy. Bosses are generally spammed down in about 10 seconds. Enemies are very basic and if you don't want to farm currency or cards it very quickly becomes obvious that you should just run past all enemies, if you take damage its not a problem because again, infinite healing.Player movement and mechanics are in general very fluid and fast paced which is the only thing that really makes the game enjoyable from a gameplay perspective IMO, but again there is not a single section of the game that poses any challenge at all. All 3 of the shantae games I have played on steam have their pros and cons. Some are better, some are worse, all in slightly different ways. But all of them are overall very similar and share many of the same fundamental flaws. The primary issue being a lack of any challenge whatsoever.

At around the 50% progression you can already purchase all items in the shop and have effectively almost 1000HP (while the single hardest boss attack takes 5). At this point getting paid in money feels like an insult. And chieftain's card - definitely ends on the top 10 most ridiculous awards in games, considering _when_ you'd get it. The whole game is an examplary collection of bad design practices, cheap regurgitation of assets, and repetitiveness. In fact the single hardest challenge of the game is not to break the X button or your thiumb. The game is all about mashing that button. It feels long, tedious, repetitive. In the timed room you have to perform the same challenge 8 times! Who decided it has to be 8? Why not 4? 16? 35?. The final boss run is boring and too long - I didn't even bother to look for secrets at this stage, I did not care anymore, and that is the worst problem of the game - it is boring. P.S. _childDocuments_.review: In more ways than one, this game is what Half Genie Hero (the previous Shantae game) should have been. That game had a really weak story, the levels were simple and uninspiring (most likely rushed), the difficulty of the game was between child's play and overly casual; and some of the abilities you'd unlock during your playthrough would serve their purpose once or twice and then be left to rot in your ability menu until you finish the game.Thankfully, Shantae and the Seven Sirens rectifies these issues. It makes you actually care about the story since it isn't just "Same bad guy shows up, does the same bad guy thing, bad guy gone, fin". This time there's an entirely different story setting with some new characters, both allies and enemies. Your list of abilities and transformations doesn't contain things that become obsolete after 5 minutes which is appreciated. On the topic of gameplay as a whole, it's still not a "challenging" game, but at least this time there's some trial and error involved; you're actually forced to use your brain which I can't say for the last game. However, some of the boss fights are rather underwhelming, but at least they are continuing the tradition of making us beat up hot monster girls.I've seen some people complain about the fact that Jake Kaufman wasn't the composer for this game's soundtrack. They cite this fact as the reason why the soundtrack is "bad", but don't let them fool you. The soundtrack retains amazing quality, it just doesn't have the same feeling since it's not by the same composer as the last 3 games.Amongst other new features, this game also introduces a card collecting system which I think is by far the best new thing here. Each enemy has a chance of dropping a card with their name on it and these cards can be equipped for various different bonuses. I had a lot of fun customizing my loadouts like this while progressing the game. I also like how they added fully animated cutscenes and gave the voice actors more lines to work with. Before, the voice acting was mostly limited to characters saying names, laughing, grumbling, sighing and similar sounds, but now they actually voice entire sentences.All in all, I enjoyed this game and hope WayForward actually keeps going forward in this direction.6/12/2021 UPDATE: A new update for the game was released a few days ago which added some extra difficulties. Amongst them is "Definitive mode" which increases the difficulty of the game and intensifies every boss battle. This is a great feature as it fixes the issue I described earlier in this review: easy gameplay and underwhelming boss fights. I had a lot of fun playing through this new gamemode.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Seven Sirens brings the series back on track, in my opinion. The map is much bigger and more expansive to explore than in Half-Genie Hero, and dungeons/labyrinths return as well. It's much closer in line to Pirate's Curse which I still feel is the peak of the series, but Seven Sirens is certainly a formidable contender for best in the series.The dances/transformations are much better integrated here compared to past entries as well. Transformations are automatically activated with an applicable area/button input, so transformations are instant with no more standing around to transform. This also allows you to combine transformations one after the other to traverse platforms, defeat enemies or speedrun the game, it's very well made. The dances themselves are used for specific objects/areas to find secrets or screen-wipe enemies, which makes more sense those take time to use since dancing is done in real-time and consume your magic meter.If you love Shantae, you'll love Seven Sirens without a doubt. Even if you're just a platformer/metroidvania fan, this will also be for you. It's a great mix of platforming and exploring.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid Metroidvania with classic Shantae humor and gameplay. I'm on the fence with recommending since there are a few major gripes I have, namely with difficulty of gameplay, story/character depth, and art direction.Gameplay is more fluid than other Shantae titles with contextual transformations. However, the dances halt gameplay the numerous times you need to use them. And difficulty is trivialized since healing powers/items are much too plentiful. Making the game feel like it's holding your hand the whole way through.The shallow character depth and story are serviceable but lacking. Now this isn't to say the game needs a complex narrative, as no Shantae game has needed one. I just hoped the story would've been less predictable and the characters more than just cute sprites to save with barely any personality traits.The art direction of the game is great with cute girls aplenty. The sprites from Half Genie Hero are reintroduced and the new character art is good. But while the Trigger intro animation is gorgeous, all the following cutscenes feel rushed and amateur. The colors are off, the lines look half-hearted, and the scenes in general don't add as much as some meaningful dialogue would.

_childDocuments_.review: A massive upgrade, mechanics wise, from Half-genie Hero. Although I enjoyed that title, it felt like a downgrade from what Pirate's Curse had to offer. But this one, oh boy, it got me hyped since the 1st trailer dropped. A return to the basics/roots of the series, now in HD.If you are either a fan of Pirate's Curse, Half-genie Hero or both - go for it and play the Seven Sirens. It's the near-perfect mix of both.Now why did I say "near-perfect"? Let's see below some Pros and Cons.:- as a veteran of the series, you're getting around 8-9 hours of gameplay, maybe 12 with item collection; as a new player, you're in for a fun adventure that will keep you hooked up for many more hours- controls, as always, feel responsive and tight. You're in control at any time- graphics are more or less from Half-genie hero, but they are improved to feel more natural if it makes sense- great enemy variety- puzzles are fun, but not overly complex- big map to explore and enjoy- fun characters- interesting story that leaves a cliffhanger at the end- more voice acting across the board for multiple characters- ANIMATED CINEMATICS!:- load times between main areas are longer than they should be, which I suspect that a patch will fix this- music is only fine; a step down from Pirate's Curse and Half-genie hero (I know the reason why, but still, had to be said)- although the map is big, it doesn't offer much environmental diversity- the last stage is too easy; compared to Pirate's Curse and Half-genie, this felt like a walk in the park- small typos (I counted three in the entire game during dialogs, maybe there are more)Conclusion? The game gets a solid 8/10 from me. If the music, map diversity and the last stage were given more attention, this would've been a 9.5/10. Alas, Pirate's Curse remains on 1st place for me, while the Seven Sirens took 2nd place from Half-genie, which now is 3rd.As an ending note, Seven Sirens is to Half-genie Hero what Pirate's Curse was to Risky's Revenge.Edit: my opinion is unchanged thus far, but I'm disappointed due to the lack of updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't buy this if game length per value is a huge point of contention for you. Or even a small point, I'm fine with any game so long as I feel like I get like... what, an hour per $2? A little under if it seems like I just went through it cuz I was better than average. But I beat this game in under seven hours. Seven hours for $30 is absurd. It does have New Game Plus but it's just the generic "you take more damage" variant.I didn't get 100% completion, so that could have extended the play time, but the map has no way of indicating what exactly you're missing and where it might be. There's no indication when walking by one of the optional challenge caves if it's something you've already completed before, you have to duck in and see if its familiar before popping out. I got all of the store items, I got most of the squids, nuggets, and achievements... but unless I get a walkthrough to tell me where exactly everything is, there's no point in trying to get all of it.Honestly I wish I liked this game because the presentation is 5 out of 5, but in terms of gameplay I'm closer to give it a 2 out of 5. Granted, it'd be at least a 3 if you haven't played Half-Genie Hero yet. A lot of my problems stem from how this game recycles Half-Genie Hero's engine and for the most part recycles its upgrades. There's very little in this game I'd call NEW, just... improved. But considering Half-Genie Hero actually _did_ make it easy to keep track of where collectibles were and weren't, I think it breaks even in terms of how fun it is to play.I'm not gonna try and refund it, since I did beat the game and i did kinda enjoy parts of it, but I wouldnt recommend buying it unless you don't care about cost to content ratio or you can get it at least 30% off.

_childDocuments_.review: Is Shantae as adorable as ever?  Sure.Are there some cool mechanics and fun power ups?  Yes.But the level design and boss fights...they're pretty bad.I'm not even talking about the egregious loading times (that practically freeze up my computer) or the fact that you can often fall back down into the level loading zone.  I mean just from a perspective of being fun to explore and intuitive to solve, it's a hot mess.  Plenty of times your only reward is just a couple gems when it's stupidly easy to get really large amounts.  Finding key items is either painfully easily or miserably difficult and specific.  It's really a game that boils down to the lowest form of metroid-vania challenge: did you go literally everywhere yet?  No?  Then you've missed something essential and can't progress the story.  There's no consistency to glean off what is bonus or not or what the next thing you might need to do is.I spent most of the game confused though still slowly completing everything.  Fast travel is so spaced out that it's miserable to double check everything.  Honestly just a map pin system might've solved a lot of that even though the levels themselves would still be mostly unfun.Hopefully the next iteration of this series will take level design more seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I strongly admired its superbly punctual controls and overall fast pace, this series still hasn't really done enough for me to keep me interested; especially 5 games this far in. I honestly don't know how to explain this properly, but the game just feels a little too self aware of what it is and wants to be in the fact that it is indeed a video game and continues to naively misunderstand any additional design supplements like its Metroidvania-esque levels that it so desperately wants to be categorized as.+ Punchy controls, action commands, and overall speedy pacing+ Pleasing presentation featuring charming cutscenes, colorful visuals, and fluid animation- Particularly rigid level design that feels more like isolated levels stiched together rather than one large world- Fetch quest game progression STILL present for the 5th game in a row in conjunction with the bad level design

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like another miss and not great on Steam Deck. The game sprites I believe are designed targeting 1080p, similar to Half Genie Hero. This makes the downscaling to 720p for the Steam Deck look very blurry. This game is also locked to 60 fps so to get the best experience, remember to change your frame cap to 60, down from the default 90 for the OLED. Also locked to a 16:9 aspect ratio, which either gets gray bars on the LCD model (since it's not pure black) or promotes uneven burn in on the OLED model (the pixels outside the 16:9 aspect ratio won't degrade at all so there will be two noticeable horizontal lines if you keep playing games in that aspect ratio. Not sure how long it'll take but is definitely something that I've started to keep in mind). The sprite work is definitely the most problematic, the other two less so.This is my opinion from playing the game a bit more after obtaining your first genie dance power. The biggest problem for me would be the enemies in the game. The enemy placement is awful and will lead you to walking into them without any way to stop it. The enemy attacks aren't the most telegraphed so I took more damage than I felt like I deserved to. The infinitely respawning enemies in some rooms or just respawned enemies upon revisiting a room makes getting around the map an absolute chore.The amount of damage that I took on a normal basis would lead to three paths:- I farm the easy to kill enemies for them to drop hearts, gems, or monster cards. This seems like the path the developers want you to take with gems and the new monster cards dropping, with some requiring 10 monster cards while some of the tougher enemies requiring only 1 to unlock the ability that comes with it. Not a fan of grinding- I spend way more gems than I want to on healing items. Doesn't feel great, I want to use the gems to buy upgrades anyways and I need to farm enemies to get gems in the first place. - I die and lose a bunch of progress. There's a good amount of save points but no auto save which is annoying. I have to talk to the old man to save and click through the dialogue everytime I run past him, else I lose all my progress. The chances of dying and losing all my progress goes up as the amount of time I want to spend grinding enemies for hearts and gems to spend on potions goes down, which made this game annoying to play.My patience is wearing real thin upon getting the first dance spell as this seems like a thing that will bring further annoyance. First, dance spells cost mana. I lost a good amount of progress from trying to farm enemies to get mana drops so I could use the dance spell. Second, with how often the developers want you to use the first dance, they sure did make activating it unnecessarily time consuming. You have to hold the dance button for a second or two before you're able to activate the specific dance spell you want which just gets annoying. The first dance spell you get also promotes you to revisit all of the areas you just went to to see if there are any secrets you can uncover with it. It's annoying to activate the dance spell repeatedly, it's annoying to repeatedly kill easy enemies for mana drops to use the dance spell, and (partly on me, partly on the devs) I just revisted all the areas looking for the fifth nugget prior to completing the fetch quest for the dance spell so I would have to do it again.

_childDocuments_.review: The only Shantae game so far I haven't felt like finishing. It feels like they've learned nothing and invested their effort in the wrong places. The voice acting's... not good. The animated cutscenes are 00's Newgrounds-tier. The new characters are... surprisingly uninspiring since writing a punchy, entertaining character in a few sentences has always been a strength of the Shantae series, instead mostly I just find myself wishing the new characters would go away and let the old favourites come to the fore.Level screens are oddly small after, hell, all the previous games. The ones in HGH were huge, heck, even Pirate's Curse had bigger level screens, I'm convinced. Speaking of HGH, expect a lot of of stuff, like half the enemy roster, to be recycled from that game. Not fundamentally bad but another example of the low-effort nature of the game.Soundtrack is okay but... lacking Kaufman's touch feels like it makes it miss something.As much as I'm glad to see the return of the open world, compared to Pirate's Curse and HGH, each area feels void of any sort of interesting gimmick or design trait, at least as far as I played before just getting... bored. Also what the hell is with the level design of enemies that pop out of the floor immediately after you land from a jump, with no indicator at all of where they're gonna burst out, so it's just random chance whether you land on the wrong tile and take unavoidable damage? That's bad platforming, that is.Really also impressed that they managed to make a REVEAL THE INVISIBLE-ability so boring and formulaic to use. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.I hope we get more Shantae games but I also hope that Wayforward learns something before making them.

The music, as being composed not by Jake "Audio Guy" Kaufman, was also very forgivable, sadly. The other nitpick I have is the art style, which feels like it's all over the place. Yet another style change 5th time in a row for dialogue art. It looks good, but initially felt clashed with the 1/2 Hero sprites. The cutscenes were also fine, although felt unnecessary.Anyway, the game is okay and I would suggest Shantae fans check it out. Maybe you will enjoy it more than I did, I dunno.

_childDocuments_.review: 2 Crashes in as many days. Every game gets 2, IMO, I'm willing to accept 1 fluke. Both times I've been using the Seer dance, so that's probably related. On top of that, the game's load times are unacceptable. How are there area load times of 8-10 seconds on an SSD? Super Metroid didn't have load times like this and it was on SNES! Underneath the tech issues is a fun and cute Shantae game like you've come to expect. Not as good as Pirate's Curse so far - it has its moments where it rivals that best Shantae game, but there's just as many terrible boss battles and boring abilities as good ones. With apologies to the new music team, Jake Kaufman's presence is sorely missed. New music isn't bad, some of it's quite catchy, but the heavy use of 8 bit doesn't live up to Kaufman's catchy tunes.Despite dips in gameplay quality, the game mostly plays to the series strengths of fun writing and pretty girls - and those were both consistently good throughout. Assuming this game eventually works properly, I'd probably recommend it, at least on sale. As it is now though, the technical state it's in is really kinda embarrassing.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just going to get the positives out of the way first. The fluidity of just meshing the transformations into your core platforming this time around is great, you get dash early on. BUT, stuff like tortoise feels useless after getting it to just get certain items, you notice you never really use it again. Like you use the tortoise against the boss, but after that there's no enemy that you really need to use it against. The last movement unlock of triple jump is at the very end which you only really use for maybe about 1 more hour, which kind of sucks because you wish you could have gotten it as your 3rd unlock to play around more.The monster cards are interesting and do very little augments to your core abilities, and it can be fun/convenient.Storywise it's alright but I find it to be lacking in introducing the Sirens and giving them any purpose. You see these animations before a fight, but they don't say anything and you just go into a fight. Makes it feel meaningless as there's no tension.Now for the main downsides, as a Metroidvania it feels shallow compared to existing games like Hollow Knight.  I see that they were trying to go for an easy game, but playing this game just reminds me that Kirby games does everything this is trying to do, but better. Even as a Metroidvania, Amazing Mirror comes to mind as a much better and more fun game. If we are to compare, both are simplistic platformers that aren't hard but suppose to be fun and challenging in small ways. Shantae I feel takes it up on being too simplistic in its boss battles, some finishing in less than 10 seconds, while others are just easy but annoyingly long to fight because of the waiting. You will never die because healing items are infinite, enemies just keep dropping consumables. Shantae also has the poor game design thought process of doing invisible secrets instead of any challenging puzzles, meaning you're going to spam Seer Dance in each new zone to see if there's a secret you missed. It wouldn't be much of a problem if you'd at least know which area on the map is incomplete. Again, Amazing Mirror an old GBA game did this better and will show a zone is incomplete by not glowing on the map, while a zone that is glowing means you got everything there. This makes this game tedious if you want to go for 100% by collecting all the cards/heart containers. Some of the collectible items are in caves and are also just backtrack and use ability once you get it instead of using said ability in a fun way to get a secret item, so again not much real thought process going on. If you like Shantae you'll probably get this anyways, if you're new to the series and suck at platforming then this game is fine to get. If you like challenging platformers/metroidvanias this game will probably already be too easy for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Another well done entry in the Shantae series. Personally, I rate this a bit lower than both Half-Genie Hero and The Pirate's Curse, but better than Risky's Revenge. I did not much care for the monster card system as some of them just had abyssal drop rates and I didn't want to grind when the super rare cards you trade for gold chunks are better anyway. It felt really weird that you couldn't dropt through platforms like in previous titles and I do not understand why Shantae couldn't transform into anything and had to get new forms that basically do exactly the same as her old one's (although it was fun enough).The level design was good for the most part. I did not care much about the screens where you had to dig through sand with only 1 type of enemy throughout the entire game. Just made little sense to me. Also, not being able to teleport back to town all the time was a weird choice to pad game time.Still, overall this was a lot of fun with a cool soundtrack and responsive gameplay. I played the definitive difficulty and it wasn't really all that hard, so I can guess the lack of difficulty the game originally had really hurt it.

_childDocuments_.review: ok. i consider myself a shantae fan. i loved Pirates Curse and Half Genie Hero, and was excited with this one. but when i saw the Studio Trigger intro... i didn't like it... like at all. it was too glossy, very in-your-face, and the song, topped with the visuals made it very annoying. now for gameplay, its actually not that bad. i like that its going back to its metroidvania roots and the characters are still the same as we like them. but the writing just isnt as charming as before. and the music, while some is still good, felt really underwhelming. but the worst part is the challenge, or lack there of. this game gives you too many gems and healing items, by the first hour, i was already maxed out on golden crabs and roast steaks! this nullifys any challenge and replayability. the humor in this game is very underwhelming too. some were just meh... and others like when Shantae and Sky were mocking the generic female rpg "armor" is just cringe worthy. yeah, mocking the fact that it shows more skin than it does protect it couldve been funny... if you wern't doing this to begin with like with Zapple, Shantae's Quake form, and some of the Sirens themselves. but we all know its just for eye candy. and the cutscenes animation is just, pathetic. ive seen some beautiful animation from Shantae Half Genie Hero, i was hyped to see how theyll handle cutscenes... but the movement is very stiff and the Lip syncing makes the Donkey Kong Country Cartoon look professional. i wanted to like this game, and in some aspects like some of the gameplay and characters, i did... but its just fails in presentation, writing, and challenge. if your a Shantae fan, or if your new to metroidvanias, wait for a price drop... or just get Pirates Curse or Half Genie Hero, or Even Risky's Revenge instead. i know Wayforward can be better than this.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is actually alright. While not exactly amazing, this is probably the best Shantae game so far. The gameplay was given more polish. Some fundamental like having an actual map to consult are introduced. The levels are designed fairly well. The difficulty curve is reasonable (the game is not a walk in the park with a crawl through barbed wire and broken glass in the final dungeon). Developers didn't entirely cheap out on voiceover. There's even nice animated cutscenes.There are still some problem inherent with the series, but they can generally be overlooked. You still have very little clue where to go next a lot of the time. The story needs to progress in a very specific order. You can collect a ton of food and auto-potions to carry with you, so being careful with combat is not really necessary.If you wanted to check the series out, I would strongly recommend to go for this game and skip any of the earlier titles.

_childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical of this game at first, mainly because the conflicting art styles, obviously reused assets, and cheap animation positively scream low-budget. I guess they needed to dial it down after the Herculean task that was making Half-Genie Hero. What you're getting here is definitely not the most polished Shantae game in terms of production value. That being said, I think there's still all the same heart and charm in the story and the dialogue as there ever was. It's also still fun to play. I really liked the new dances and transformations. I like that you can use animal transformations automatically and use the dances for exploration instead of just for transforming. I think that's a really fresh take on the series' magic system. I hope this game is a sign that Way Forward hasn't completely given up on this franchise and is instead taking a step back and trying new things. If they do make a new game, here's what I would add/change if I could:1) The monster card feature is the only part of this game that felt weak to me. Drops are rare, so grinding for all the cards takes forever. I also learned far too late that they only drop if you use your hair whip to defeat enemies, which means I wasted way too much time trying to use magic to harvest cards. Even after learning this, it still felt like a chore to get them all. If they're ever brought back, I think either the drop rate should be higher or else there should be a power or item that makes them easier to get. Maybe some could also be purchased?2) The difficulty is absurdly unbalanced. The first boss took me an hour to defeat because each attack does massive damage and they're all almost impossible to dodge. The final boss was a joke because I had collected so many items that I could just cheese the whole thing. There are also enemies that do massive damage but take almost no effort to beat. I think there could be more strategy overall.3) Stop teasing information about Shantae's mother and then leaving us with nothing, good gRaVY.  I get that they have to keep people interested in these games, but after five games of doing the equivalent of the "will-they-won't-they" game, it just feels like I'm being led along with no payoff. You guys have so many great characters and so much interesting lore here, just take that to the next level instead of giving us a plot that's on the level of a Saturday morning cartoon. At least we have more half-genies now, so maybe that's a sign that the writers are trying to tap more into that aspect of the world.Also can we maybe get more clothes on the women? I'm not saying we need to erase all their curves or even that we need to eliminate all the little innuendos (I get that the whole thing is harmless and tongue-in-cheek in this franchise), but it's getting disturbing watching the characters become visually younger with each entry and yet still barely have anything covered. Maybe it made sense to make the characters eye candy back in 2002 when this series was new and female protagonists didn't sell as well without some cleavage showing, but it's 2023 and there are so many games with female protagonists that have found sizable and loyal fanbases without the weird pedo vibes. I think the series would have an easier time finding an audience if the devs would either commit to making the visuals as child-friendly as the story or else commit to making a more mature adult experience. I imagine I'll be pilloried for this, but that's just my opinion.I'm not sure where I'd rank this game. It's definitely below Pirate's Curse and Half Genie Hero, but it doesn't feel right putting it at the bottom. I think this is a good Shantae game, but not a great one.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid entry in the Shantae series. Seems like it incorporates at least a little bit from all of the previous titles while making a fresh adventure. The core gameplay and movement are very satisfying and very much in step with what I've come to expect from the series. The music is great and fits well, even though it's done by a new composer. The new fusion coin abilities and equipable monster cards are both phenomenal features that serve to enhance Shantae's potential.For me, this game still doesn't quite supplant Pirate's Curse as my favorite (though the attempt to be more like that game is transparently obvious,) but it's definitely a step in a direction that I'd like to see more of from this series. Seven Sirens is an ambitious title and I definitely applaud it for aiming high. I enjoy this game and I'd essentially like to see the series going forward do this, but even better.Better is important though. This game tries to do a lot, and while I appreciate it, there's room for improvement. There are two key things that felt especially cumbersome while playing and made it difficult for me to enjoy this one as much as I've enjoyed other Shantae titles.The idea of the interconnected metroidvania map sounds great on paper, but it's held back in this game by one particular issue. Your mileage may vary on how much this bothers you, but it was a real sticking point for me: loading screens.You start the game, walk two small screens to the right, and run straight into a load screen. You're in the town, a cutscene plays, and then you get a load screen to just be in the same town area again. You're exploring the blue area, what's to the left here, woops, load screen, now you're in the orange area. Wanna go back one screen to blue? Watch that load screen a second time. There's a load screen between every dungeon and its boss. The final dungeon has a load time for the final boss, another load time for the second phase, and then a third load time for the characters standing on one screen and talking to each other at the end. And the towns are the worst offenders. Two of them are only one screen, but they require a load screen to enter and another to exit. Need to go back to the pink area and get something you missed? Warp to Tree Town (load screen) and then leave the town's one screen by heading down (second load screen.) And they couldn't load the dance mini-game as part of Tree Town; that loads separately and then you have to load back into Tree Town afterward.Shantae and the Pirate's Curse, even though it had segmented areas, didn't make the player sit through load screens for them and certainly didn't interrupt the final boss fight to load each of its forms.Half-Genie Hero had its fair share of load screens, but it handled them well. In that game you can tell when a segment is ending and generally feel confident that you've done all you can in that segment for now. The load screens there are very much in pace with the way that game is designed to be played. They never feel like they're interrupting you while you're in the middle of something. Seven Sirens, on the other hand, is designed like a big open metroidvania, but ultimately still divided into segments that just happen to be next to each other. There's no situation that lends itself to wandering freely between these areas. It feels more practical to just explore one area at a time, at which point it might as well be Half-Genie Hero.I'm sure this issue is less bothersome to some people, but I just couldn't stop feeling the annoyance each time a load screen came up. And the biggest reason for that annoyance is that I've played other metroidvania games (and other Shantae games) that don't have this problem. One game on my mind is Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night, which is doing more in terms of graphics than Seven Sirens, is fully voiced, has a huge interconnected map to explore, is comparably priced, and does it all without making the player watch load screens all the time. WayForward should talk with some of the other teams that worked on that game about how they handled/masked loading times while giving the player freedom to explore and warp all over the map. A 2D sidescroller at this level of graphical detail should be achievable without all of the waiting around. Seven Sirens with no load screens would be an absolute dream for me to play, even with its other issue.The second strongest drawback in this game: the dances. Of the four Shantae games to feature the transformation dances as a game mechanic, this one has the least interesting version of it. You dance, wait a second for your four options to come up, choose one, a near-static png image of a transformed Shantae pops up, and then the ability does whatever it was going to do to the portion of the room that happens to be visible to you at that time. If you're the type who likes to explore every area and find all of the collectibles, you'll be doing these dances a lot. This, combined with the load screens, slows down the pace of this otherwise fast-paced game and makes exploring that big open metroidvania map to find all the goodies feel tedious. I might feel differently as I get more familiar with where the collectibles are, but definitely in that first playthrough, searching for all the things, using that Seer Dance multiple times in some rooms, really started to wear out its welcome.The transformation system in the other Shantae games has had its shortcomings, but I don't think giving the transformations an even narrower set of mechanics was the right way to fix those shortcomings. If the game is going to have the transformation dances, I'd rather see them become more robust and fully featured, not less. I'd like to see each transformation have (or at least be able to learn) its own full move set. Something on the attack button, something on the magic item button, something on each bumper and trigger. That way you're not just transforming, doing the one thing your transformation can do, and then transforming back. You might choose to stay transformed for a bit if you have ways of dealing with enemies and traversing the terrain that are comparable to regular Shantae. This applies not just to previous game styles, but Seven Sirens as well. Becoming the humanoid creatures from those near-static pngs and playing as them? Actually swinging that giant hammer? An electric hair whip attack? And then putting those special screen flash abilities on a dedicated button press? That would be epic.I could go into more minor concerns, like why each of the fusion coin abilities don't quite measure all the way up to their Pirate's Curse counterparts, or some walls and one way pass-through platforms dividing the metroidvania map that i wish I could destroy with the earthquake, but I'm not sure if I want to get that particular. The abilities are fun in their own right. And, in spite of the preceding paragraphs of complaints, I don't want to seem too down on this game. I went into this game wanting to love it at least almost as much as Pirate's Curse, so I experienced some disappointment, but "not quite Pirate's Curse" is still a mighty fine game. It's an entertaining and satisfying product that is definitely worth its price. The limitations took some getting used to, but it's still very fun, warts and all.I really do want to see future Shantae games follow this path, refine this style, and optimize this type of gameplay experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a return to form for the Shantae series!After the major disappointment that was Half Genie Hero, this game is a Metroidvania again and not just some platformer.I am also extremely happy that they decided to stop using 3D assets with 2D sprites because it looked terrible.If you liked Pirate's Curse (which imo is the best title in the series), you're going to enjoy playing this one. It's not as good, but still very enjoyable.The soundtrack is also top-notch despite Virt (a.k.a. Jake Kaufman) not working on the music this time around, and the animated cutscenes are a pleasant surprise, to say the least, too.The way transformations are handled is also more intuitive, they function very similar to special abilities in Pirate's Curse, and I'm a fan of that.I have some complaints, however: This game is plagued by long loading times when changing areas, which you will be doing often. The devs recently released a 1GB update that completely fixed this for me, but I've seen others say that they are still having this issue, so you might want to keep this in mind.Second of all, it's about the writing of a specific character, namely Sky. I feel like Sky is a complete b*tch in this game, and that this is sort of out of character for her. She's always been more... aggressive and tomboy-ish than other characters, for sure, but never outright rude. In this game, she does a complete 180 degree turn and just becomes plain rude and annoying. In the past games, she would always try to help Shantae, and in this game she outright refuses to help because "muh vacation".Last, but not least, the actual "dances" in this game are a bit underwhelming, and they just use a 2D image as a visual effect. I wish they would have more of a visual "oomph" to them, but it's not a big problem, I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: It's really cute! Honestly, I'd probably wait for a sale since $30 seems a bit steep considering the main story is about 8 hours and you can pick up Hollow Knight for $15.Don't go into this looking for a whole lot of depth or extreme difficulty, but Shantae is adorable and always fun. There are hints and map waypoints enabled by default. If you're a more seasoned Metroidvania player you may want to turn them off, but the accessibility they add makes this a great stepping-in point for players new to the genre.I recommend it if you're a fan of Metroidvanias and you're looking for a fix after playing most of the "Big Names" in the genre or are just looking for something light and silly in tone.

_childDocuments_.review: The game as a whole flows much better than Half Genie Hero in almost every aspect. The transformations are easy to flow in and out of while giving her dance button more utilitarian purposes that have neat effects. The monster cards add a decent layer of customizing how you want to play. A much more natural game world to explore than segmented levels.On the flip side, some of the dungeon layouts feel a bit rushed and it would have been nice to get more mini games like the dance parlor to break up the gameplay loop. While the story, humor, and ending in particular are better than Half Genie Hero, Pirate's Curse still feels more ambitious with it's concepts, but in general, I wish Shantae games would change the status quo of it's world, even if slightly. Characters never change or change roles except if it's directly moving the plot and it ends with everything being mostly the same.Still, it was a better ending than I was actually expecting after Half Genie Hero and if you like Shantae, you should buy this one too, crossing my fingers for any chance of future content.And if you don't know if you do like Shantae or not, this game is a pretty good jumping on point to trying the others on Steam!
