_childDocuments_.review: Soooo, Shantae & The Seven Sirens... (beat the game on Switch first & then bought it for PC a few days ago)I had my doubts at first, after hearing this was originally a mobile game I was scared it would just be a watered down clone of Half Genie Hero, well it kind of is but it stands on it's own thanks to it's new gameplay tweaks, new locations & the return of the open world style from previous games.  I like the plot, it's pretty simple & straightforward while having quirky characters to talk to. Gameplay, generally it's a refined version of Half Genie Hero (it even uses the same game engine & sprites) I liked the new monster cards & instant transformations, I would want to see these elements return in Shantae 6, that's how well they work. The Music is the best in the series, yep I said it, I looove Jake Kaufman's Score in HFG & Pirate's Curse don't get me wrong but I feel like Seven Sirens has more upbeat, catchy & memorable songs that don't get annoying after listening to them on repeat while being in a certain zone. However here are my gripes, some objectives are really cryptic, like if you have to talk to a certain npc in order to progress without giving you any hints, so you end up walking & backtracking talking to everyone until you get a clue on how to proceed.  HFG had the same issue but since the game was mostly linear you didn't have to spend too much time searching for knickknacks. Another issue I have is the voices as certain lines are voiced in text boxes and some aren't so you end up accidentally skipping over voiced text boxes, Would it have killed them to have every line voiced? They definitely can because another Wayforward game: Spidersaurs had full voice acting.. so they didn't really have an excuse here. The bosses are extremely easy & not at all memorable, you do the same Risky Boots boss like 5 times and it gets repetitive, The Seven Sirens also don't add anything, they just show up randomly, cause chaos & Shantae defeats them, boring... also the final boss (I won't say who it is for spoilers) but it's incredibly underwhelming & doesn't feel as climatic as the ending of half genie hero. On the topic of difficulty I found the game way too easy, sure maybe they reduced the difficulty to attract more new fans (this was an IPhone game first after all) It's still underwhelming, They shower you with food items 24/7, I was talking about the monster cards earlier, they are great yes, I feel like some of them make the game too easy, like the one where you get more magic (coral siren card I think), or one where you get more hp (forgot this one), they're like cheats they make the game too easy. Another gripe is the price, 30$.. Sure it's a new release the game is only 2 years old (it came out in 2019) & all, but the main campain is only about 6 hours long if you know what you're doing, & the magic mode you unlock after beating the game only changes Shantae's Outfit & Gives her less HP, kind of a wasted opportunity... If the extra mode was like Sonic Mania's Encore Mode adding new playable characters & changing the zone layouts than I would have been glad you know? For 30$ you can buy other games which offer more bang for your buck (like Half Genie Hero which has more content, including more costumes, new game modes, & more playable characters for the exact same price as seven sirens) honestly just wait for a price drop if you're a new fan, but if you're a long time fan of Shantae, you won't be too dissapointed.

_childDocuments_.review: The classic humour and amazing characters, both old and new, were spot on as usualIt's good it returned to the less linear world after 1/2 Genie Hero, and the bosses were creative, especially the end game boss.The animations were a pleasant addition as well, and making transformations instant and using dance for secondary abilities made the game a lot more fluid.However the boss fights themselves could have done with some improvement. The first boss was the hardest (after the last one ofc) and as I progressed they got easier and easier and their mechanics became more easy to grasp at the first glance, which should go the other way around. Also the recurring Risky Boots fight in every dungeon was pointless, and she got weaker too, firing 8 bullets  instead of 2 in the same direction just gives me more time to deal massive damage to her back.Overall an absolutely amazing game as all in this series, improved in many ways and made quite a few new mistakes as well.

_childDocuments_.review: "Half-genie down! Someone get a medic in here!"So, before I get into why that thumb-icon there is pointing firmly downwards, let me say some nice things about Shantae and the Seven Sirens.WayForward games nail the sound and colourful nature of a Shantae game once again. The music is a nice, swinging mix of beats and chip-sounds I couldn't help but jam to every now and then, and the colourful backgrounds, cute characters and bouncy animations are all peak Shantae! And good heavens the intro animation looks like something an 8-year-old me would have LOVED on Saturday mornings!Sadly, beyond that sounds and visuals, Shantae stumbles and falls this time around. Gone is the level design and enemy placement that brought on challenge in the previous games, and gone are the bosses that could knock you down if you were careless. In their place is a loosely designed map with hardly any distinct features, where compromises and cracks seem abundant as the developers struggle to push the game into a more genuine metroidvania experience than the hub-based worlds of previous entries in the series.In place of challenge, Shantae 5 seems to instead dive right into ultra-casual gameplay, where the game showers the player with gems, healing items and little rewards for virtually no effort. The entire latter half of the game was trivialised for me, by the over-abundance of healing items to the point where several bosses, including the very final boss, could be just tanked. No need to evade enemy attacks if you can just scarf down a few burgers or sea-critters for full health in the pause menu, and even if you forget to heal in time, the cheap auto-potions will bring you back up to NINE times! Sure, you can choose not to buy the auto-potions, but I ran out of things to spend money on around the halfway point of the game, so...The game also seems to lose a lot of the charming details of the older games. For a game with a dancing genie-girl as the protagonist, we seem to have forgotten to actually add any dancing animations in to the game this time around. Previous entries had those, but instead of unique animations we now get seemingly unrelated pin-up pictures of characters/creatures I'm still not entirely sure were relevant to what was going on in the game. Why do I get a screen-sized picture of a glistening fish-girl whenever I cast the vastly overpowered thunder spell that utterly breaks the time-restricted portions of the game?As for the story, there seems to be very little of it. We get a loose premise, then basically nothing until the very last half-hour of the game, and then it's all over. Familiar characters make appearances, bust out a few jokes and disappear again. The eponymous Sirens seem to pose little to no threat at all, and the old lady waving a little flag and dreaming of a suit of armour of her own was, by far, the most entertaining character of the game.As a long-time fan of the series, I really hope Shantae can get back on form in some future entry, but I feel fans and especially newcomers to the Shantae series will do much better going for the older entries in the series than this.(Oh, and I deducted a point from Audio for no Rottytops theme! FOR SHAME!)Playtime: 8+ hours (A single playthrough)Ratings (1-10)Visual: 8Audio: 9Story: 3Gameplay: 4Overall: 4

_childDocuments_.review: Well... the controls are fluid and the game doesn't stress you I suppose...? Guess that already suffices for an overwhelmly positive reception.This is a new low point in the series to me, after half genie hero which was already a deeply flawed game, this one is absolutely nihilistic about its gameplay and balance.I can assure everyone, no matter how bad you are at plattformers, you will be able to play through the game. Why? Because I never encountered such an lenient healing system. Enemies will drop frequently consumables which heal 1 to 6 or 7 hearts. Enemies will never do more damage than 1,5 hearts. At the same times hearts for healing "to go" still spawn frequently. But of course this is just the beginning. Pretty early on the game gives you an healing dance, where you can heal yourself for 2 hearts, only for a tiny fraction of your magic bar, chances are high that you already earned a perk which automatically refills said magic bar. This is totally ridiciolus if everything breaks, there is still the item shop with an plethora of healing items that even heal you after death so you don't even have to open your pause menu. WayForward must think of you as a drooling brainless baboon, they don't entrust you even the easiest challenges.I've played through the game with only 3 hearts, the whole damn time and still it wasn't challenging the slightest except for the final boss which just takes forever.Any other boss in the game is a joke too, you already can kill them after two cycles of hair whipping. They have ultra simple patterns you have to dodge and usually a phase where they are vulnerable sometimes they didn't even survived a minute before they exploded it was every single time just anti climatic.The game goes back to its root as a Metroidvania, but for what price? Exploring doesn't feel rewarding at all, you are literally a genie god, shortly after starting the game. There are cards to collect from defeating enemies like in these Castlevania games, but all they do are some passive enhancements like "fire ball consumes less magic" or Quake Spell consumes less magic" or "you crawl faster" how exciting...!!!Most rooms you already will visit through the main campaign, the rest are very minor things, small caves with squids, gold nuggets by using spells to expose hidden treasures *yawn* the content of the findings are either gold nuggets you can trade for more boring cards or health upgrades, since I played with only 3 hearts I didn't need either of them. I also spent most of the currency in the game in the first few hours. It's very normal to walk through this game with the cap of 999 currency all the time. It didn't take long to buy every single upgrade the game has to offer, except an item which gives you more armor I ignored that on purpose (again this and 3 hearts and the game was still easy, i'm not a pro I do not brag trust me it's really that forgiveable)Just after the first boss I did have the highest damage and attack frequency upgrade, this can't be right, but it is.So because you are op there is no incentive to explore the enviorment, but even if you do it, it gets downright tedious since the game loads between biomes and there are a lot of biomes in the small world of the game. Loading times are an insolence for a game that looks like that, it must be pretty bad programmed, it becomes worse when you have to travel between the 3 villages there are times where you just move from on loading screen to another. The quest design doesn't help. The game follows a simple structure: Quest -> Dungeon -> Quest -> Dungeon and so on. The quest part demands a lot of backtracking from you, if you explore areas beforehand you most likely have wasted your time since the main campaign already leads you there for the next event. There is always something you need to collect with a new ability you learned along the way. These are times where I wished that the game wasn't an Metroidvania and that loading times were shorter, the game simply feels stretched out artificially since the quests offer you nothing special, no surprises. The level design is nothing special either WayForward games were never really innovative but their design was at least solid, here you can ocassionally skip plattforming section with abilitys you already unlocked at that point. The graphics of the biomes look like the same just different colors for their walls. Their are some dungeons but you do not encounter any remarkable puzzles or gimmicks there.I don't wanna hate everything since the game is still quite charming and Squid Baron is still the best character, but this can't redeem for what an utter failure the game is - gameplay and balancing wise. To me it seems like WayForward has lost their touch, it doesn't look like they value the gameplay in their games anymore. The decisions they made look like are only there to please a larger demographic, overcompensation just in case if a player begins to complain about that the game is too hard for them. I hope I'm not right. Game designers should stick to their game vision and they should invent a decent difficulty curve for it. Shantae and the seven Sirens doesn't have any curve at all at times it looks like just a fetish monster girl game.It sacrifices its integrity as an exploration plattformer for the sake of cute graphics. The majority of positive reviews will like the game nontheless because:- controls are fluid- it doesn't stress you out.- It's still Shantae they want to love the gameSo you will never feel rage about this game, but that diminishes relieve too. You will feel just nothing. The perfect game to turn your brain off and just play. If you have no standards and are fine with that, more power to you. But I don't think it's worth to pay the 25 bucks for it.

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone who has played Shantae from its roots on the Game Boy Color, this will be a refreshing experience. Returning to the single interconnected world layout (with a map this time, thank God!) was just what the series needed. Everything is bright and colorful and the music has some hot new tracks as well as remixed classic ones.Matt Bozen and WayForward never cease to impress. I've been awaiting this game with baited breath ever since the first announcement dropped. I just have one request: DLC is welcome, but please do not make a separate release of this game like the Half-Genie Hero Ultimate Edition.RET-2-GO GAMERS!!!

_childDocuments_.review: The only software I've ever used that forces 100% CPU load every time it transitions to a new room, freezing my entire PC. Made a forum post with almost 100 comments now and no word from the devs. I could look past that since while it's not loading, the game runs as you'd expect, but this is Shantae by the numbers at this point. Half Genie Hero, which was barely tolerable, might at least trick you into having fun with the excellent Jake Kaufman OST, but he isn't around for Seven Sirens and it shows. This game's music is just awful. The Trigger OP is great, and most of the art and animation is great too. But it can't absolve the technical problems nor the milquetoast gameplay. Pirate's Curse must have been a fluke as it's the only game in the series I can recommend without stipulation. This felt awful to write and I hope for much better from Wayforward and this series in the future.4 March 2021 edit:They just pushed a patch today that improves, but does not fix, the 100% CPU utilization problem. Transitions still freeze everything, but for a much shorter, and more manageable amount of time. As of right now I've still received no feedback, nor are there any patch notes.

_childDocuments_.review: Another excellent Shantae game.What's good about this game:What could be improved:Shantae Seven Sirens is the sequel to Half-Genie Hero. According to the developer It had the shortest development cycle of all Shantae games. I'd say that's probably because it borrows sprites and engine experience from the previous game. To compensate it looks like they put a lot more effort into mechanics, level design, bosses, and other improvements.Here are some of the differences with Half-Genie Hero:This game is more of a Metroidvania styled than Half-Genie Hero. Overall it feel is a mix of Pirate's Curse with Half-Genie Hero. It's an harder game than the other games as well, so you do need skill, but it's not hard enough to be frustrating. For beginners there are lower difficulty options. This is a game that should appeal everyone so difficulty options are welcome. The bosses have clear distinct personalities and patterns. With some experience it's possible to never get hit.The recurrent and new characters are likable. It's a simple story like all other Shantae games, but they always put bits of plot along the way and jokes that you'll only get if you are a man of culture to keep you interested. It's a proven formula that works like a charm. Once you're almost done with the game you can easily travel through the entire map to get all powers, cards, items, and secrets. I usually don't complete the whole thing because I see no point in just collecting, just if that's your thing it shouldn't be too hard.In conclusion, this is more a traditional 2D skill game than Half-Genie Hero, and to me both games are solid and recommended despite the different styles. All Shantae games have been good so far and this one is no exception. There are some technical improvements that can be done, and perhaps the sprites will need to be updated next time, but WayForward has a very good record, and here's hoping the next game will be just as good or better.There are a couple of technical problems:WayForward uses its own in-house engine and while they improved 4K rendering they need to tune the engine a little bit for the PC gamers with high refresh rate. Despite optimizing for 4K it seems like many sprites are actually optimized for 1080p, so you will notice a bit of pixelization in 1440p and 4K.

_childDocuments_.review: This is pretty fun, with a few annoyances.  Mostly it's fairly inventive platforming / metroid with some very interesting and different powers than usual for the series, and though some of them are obviously given away by the rooms you enter (water, sand) others are a bit of a surprise.  The map is compact enough that once you have your powers you can get around pretty fast.  There are plenty of secrets and tons of extras.  And sometimes it's very funny (Squid Baron/Armor Baron).  The map is quite helpful!My complaints:- In 2024 that heavily MLP influenced Opening Song is like drills in the ear.- The biggest complaint is the card drop system - there are about 50 monster cards that will give you some upgrades, which is nice, but then sometimes there is only a single enemy of that sort in the entire game, you have to traverse out of the room and back to fight it again, and the drop rates are abysmally low.  So you run out and back of this room 100 times beating that mob and hoping it drops its card when you could be doing something fun.  And then it's quite a mess locating it on the card assignment screen because they only show you its face and a lot of them look quite a bit alike.  Anyhow, this is the worst thing.- There are some enemies that are just freaking annoying, like the eagle bombers.  I do not feel my experienced was enhanced in any way by having to run through their constant infinite respawn bombardment while trying to jump across gaps.- Starting to dance takes JUST long enough that it gets kind of tedious revealing invisible stuff, though at least it tells you when and only seems bugged sometimes.So some annoyances, but I stuck it through and beat it, so obviously was not that bad!

_childDocuments_.review: 6.5 / 10 - Recommended. This is my favourite entry in the franchise.  As the score suggests I'm not blown away by Shantae games but they are just pure enjoyable fun.  This game was no different.  Great presentation.  Surprisingly funny.  A better story than expected.  A really solid little metroidvania that actually gets better into the second half as you unlock more powers and start to really breeze through combat.   I also really like the game types you can choose from at the start.  The negatives are an inability to disable screen shake (this game challenged my motion sickness but was still bearable).  I think having the ability to warp to town from anywhere would fix a lot of problems with backtracking moments that weren't engaging.  Metroidvania's have backtracking...but you can minimize how much of it feels like busy work.  The combat in this series has always been mediocre at best.  This is not a series to recommend metroidvania fans due to its combat or traversal.  Its good at everything...not great.

_childDocuments_.review: To the point=======================Fun and colorful metroidvania that goes back to the series rootsPlayed on Base difficulty ( the menu mentioned this was like a remix of the original release IDK)Good Stuff======================- Solid controls and platforming, especially when you can toss the transformation traversal moves into the mix later on- Sufficient difficulty, the game can have some rough parts early on, never oppressive but it may take you a few attempts- Well interconnected world map that doesn't make it too inconvenient to explore/ backtrack- Fantastic OST, I feel like this is inline with most of the games and this one is no differentBad Stuff========================- The magic dances take up a lot of magic and you're encouraged to use them often which means you'll run out of magic very quickly even in mid/end game. There are items/cards to help this but it's annoying- There are very sparse magic and health drops in normal play. This is addressed by cards and items to buy but I once had to exit a dungeon after farming for 10 minutes when no enemy would drop something to refill my magic.-Enemy hitboxes can be very weird I feel like sometimes I got hit for a respectable distance away by touch damage
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Half genie hero makes for a tough act to follow and Sirens reels things back in by returning to a more traditional action platformer / metroidvania experience.The art style from the previous game is back but this time we've gone full anime with animated and voice acted cut scenes. I don't think it adds much but at this point they've really mastered the art so there's not many other directions to take things to add more polish. The new music is fine, but lacks the insanely catchy score from previous games - though it's nice that they didn't just try a 2nd round of remixing. There's a host of new characters and enemies but sadly both the other genies and the sirens are pretty forgettable characters and feel very much like filler to pad the story and enable the adventure.The gameplay feels like a return to Risky's Revenge as the levels are more linear and less challenging. There's a ton more backtracking than the previous two games and the animals forms and magic here are either remixes of what we've seen before or go back to acting as progress gates which is a little disappointing given how the ones in 1/2 Genie Hero expanded the game world.It's unfortunate that Sirens ends up feeling like one of the weakest entries in the series so far if only because the bar was set so high by previous entries. It's an okay platformer with an okay story, but only really worth getting if you want more Shantae.

Deluxe Mode has very absurd damage scaling. There are early enemies dealing a WHOLE HEART WORTH of damage easily, and late enemies deals little damage from contact while their projectiles can deal two hearts worth of damage EASILY. A major offender is the red spider, specially because it's just "spider with triple shot".2. Magic usage feels rather discouraging until later on, as it costs a lot, repleshiments are rarer, and they don't help much. Even with full arsenal, all maxed, with all cards, I still didn't use most magics sans Bubble's and its variants, and the Genie Dances when needed.3. The card grind is really really bad. I swear I spent an hour grinding the same cards over and over, and more often than not it was from an enemy with awful drop rate or one that required multiple of the same card.4. The FMVs kept glitching for some reason. It wasn't consistent, but I suspect it had to do with the loading. _childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the Seven Sirens is the 5th game in the Shantae series, and this time it is a fully fledged metroidvania, even more than the Pirate’s Curse, the 3rd game.That game was great, and I think this one manages to surpass it, although not by a lot. The map regions are nicely interconnected, with a few contained zones, similar to dungeons. The platforming and combat are smooth and satisfying. It has beautiful art and animations in high resolution. It even has some nice animated cutscenes. The music is also decent, with a few great songs, especially the dungeon ones. It has a nice story, with new and returning characters. While the 5th game in the series, it can easily be played as the first entry in the series.A major addition is the card system, allowing you to equip 3 cards that can drop from monsters. There’re 50 to collect, allowing for some different builds. However, it can be annoying to farm them if you’re looking for 100% completion. Speaking of 100%, one of the powers must be used in a lot of places, which is annoying if you want to clear everything. But it doesn’t affect regular gameplay. There’re also map markers, so you’ll always know where to go next.A free update added some new modes, including a new standard Definitive mode, which is harder than the original Legacy mode, still available as well. Even then, it’s not a hard game, especially after you obtain the heal magic, and if you restock potions regularly, which are cheap. But these modes definitely add some replay value to an already juicy game.This is another easy recommendation, since it’s another very enjoyable Shantae game, although it’s probably better getting it on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The Shantae franchise is a rare example of a series that, despite having a decent number of games released across several decades, there really isn't a bad game in it. The newer titles are obviously more polished and content-rich than, say, the original Game Boy Color game, but that only demonstrates the series' continuous improvement with each entry, a pedigree that Shantae and the Seven Sirens fully lives up to.Seven Sirens, like Half-Genie Hero before it, has a colorful, cute, and expressive hand-drawn art style for all the characters, enemies, items, etc. that is really a treat to look at, a fantastic soundtrack with tunes that range from chill and relaxing to intense and rocking, all of which had me jamming along as I played, a lighthearted story with WayForward's trademark off-kilter humor that, while not breaking the fourth wall, definitely puts some cracks in it, and of course tight platforming controls with unlockable transformations and abilities that expand your moveset.Seven Sirens brings plenty of new ideas to the series as well, such as a fully interconnected world map in true Metroidvania style, a collectible card mechanic that will give you small bonuses or minor enhancements to abilities, and a streamlined dance/transformation system, with transformations now mapped to a button or automatically triggering when usable, and gorgeous fully animated cutscenes throughout the game done by Studio Trigger.There are really no major flaws I can see in this game, any issues I encountered on my playthrough were due to my personal lack of skill with Metroidvania style games and were easily remedied by finding a walkthrough or guide online. WayForward has once again knocked it out of the park, and I look forward to Shantae's next adventure!

I've played it earlier this year, and it's a lot different than the idealized image people seem to have of it. It's hard, and it's honestly cryptic in some places. Honestly, I consider this game to be a mechanical improvement, and it dips more into the metroidvania genre than before, which I consider a positive. It is slightly more fluid but it doesn't compromise on difficulty.Is it perfect? No, no game is. But is it still a VERY good game? Absolutely.Do I consider the overall changes to be positive compared to Pirate's Curse? Yes.Also yes this game is absolutely better than Half-Genie Hero, there isn't even a competition. _childDocuments_.review: Compared to its predecessor, this game feels a lot cleaner in terms of play and ease of transformations. It's still the same goofy, lighthearted series about a belly dancing half-genie who whips foes with her hair and dances to "TRANSFORM!" but greatly simplifies the unnecessarily complex transformations of its predecessor. You still dance to activate particular magic but now you can easily change forms on the fly with simple controls based on what you're doing in the environment.The monster card system unlocks new abilities that can be of great use...if you can collect enough cards. Some drop regularly and can be traded for gems; others require grinding (the Naga Monster and Muckman Monster cards are horrible). The rarest cards require backtracking to find Nuggets to trade for them, though their value is typically worth it.Finding said nuggets is where things get irritating. Most are hidden in flowers that need the Refresh Dance to bloom, hidden by illusions the Seer Dance will reveal, locked in electric boxes the Shock Dance will energize, or buried alongside statues the Quake Dance will uncover. Just finding where to perform each dance requires careful observation of the environment for clues about which dance to use and frequent backtracking.I'm also not a huge fan of the existing character's dialogue images this time around. It's clearly by a different artist from the previous titles and there's a real lack of emotion to most of them. Also the voice actress for Shantae (the same one from each entry with voices) made Shantae's voice higher than before so she sounds younger as well as looks younger than in . It's not game-breaking but it is disconcerting.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like the Shantae series? Play this game.Do you like metroidvania games? Play this game.Do you like having fun? Play this game.Do you like -- you know what? Just play this game.I had a blast playing through it. Actually I had so much of a blast I immediately played through it again but faster and 100%, and I had a blast again. WayForward knows how to make a fun game and believe me, they did just that here.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Not the best Shantae game there is, but OK.PROS:Pretty visualsGood controlsSome grind if you wantQuest markers for easy navigatingDancingCONS:Super easy bossesOnly one slide to adjust volume, no separate music and SFX. I would've wanted to listen more background music.Backtracking for 100% of items.10-15sec loading time between major areas! I mean, seriously? Emperor's year of 2022, and 2D game loads this long?So if you are a fan of Shantae (Fantae?), I can recommend this title. If you look for a Good Shantae game, I'll point you to Pirate's Curse.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best recent Shantae games. The rebalancing helps a lot. I personally recommend playing with the option that lets you use all of the cards though. Most are simply just small passive upgrades that are nice to have always on, like increased speed for walking,swimming,climbing etc. Nothing really game breaking, and most just keep things relevant. Still not super hard, but it was an enjoyable playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: The update is great. The game became WAY better for me with the new 3 modes added. Definitive mode is a much needed re-balance to the main game. Rule Breaker mode allows you to be overpowered the more you grind for cards. And Full Deck mode allows you to skip the card grinding entirely and focus on card building.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the Seven Sirens is an excellent Metroid-style adventure/platformer game. It is a bit too easy and could use some more challenge, in my opinion, but that's a pretty minor issue considering how great the rest of the game is. The action and exploration are great, the story and characters are great, the graphics and music are great, the voice acting is great, pretty much everything is great.Just keep in mind that this is the fifth game in the Shantae series. Knowledge of the rest of the series is not required to play and enjoy this game, but it can deepen your appreciation of this game's story and characters. Your mileage may vary on that point, so if you haven't ever played a Shantae game before, don't let that stop you from playing this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: While it isn't as good as Pirates curse, I feel its slightly above Half Genie hero. All Shantae games are great, but this one had alot of shoes to fill. And with the latest balancing update, I feel like it just does. Alot left to be desired for sure, but you can't go wrong with Shantae. Super fun stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: It's an ok-ish Shantae game. Unfortunately it follows on the same design and gameplay choices of HGH so, again, it's a downgraded experience in comparison to the classic Shantae games. This one doesn't even have transformations (which are basically the trademark of the franchise) but an instant gimmick, it's even worse than HGH. The level design (even if backgrounds are really good) is extremely simple, there are very few secrets and they don't even need this much of an effort to be found. Again the bossfights are a one-way gimmick, monster variation is very skinny and the game overall is extremely easy. Ok, Shantae was never a Castlevania-tier challenge game but the new ones are really on the opposite side of the trench. Adding insult to injury they added the recycled material from the anime (which thankfully never aired) from trigger studios and by God this is a very low effort, The cinematics and opening are awful, really, and they can do better (see L.W.A.).The game is still ok, if you are ok with HGH its basically the same with more. If you are a fan of the series from the first game and hoped HGH was just a mistake you will be disappointed, again.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only Shantae game I've ever played, and I thought it was a fun experience overall.I am a bit of a completionist when it comes to these kinds of games though (don't really care about speedrunning though) and I will say that it can become a bit tedious to have to check every single piece of the map with seer and/or quake to gather all the items. I also didn't really find myself needing to use the different spells that much as the dances and standard hair attack seemed to cover everything combat-wise.Aside from those small nit-picky comments, I found the game itself to be charming and lighthearted.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Another adventure with Shantae! Overall a fun experience and good platformer! New powers are spaced far enough apart that you get aquainted with your most recent, but not so far apart that you spend time wondering when youre going to get the next. Only one part had me going in circles, which for a game like this, isnt bad!
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played 1/2 Genie Hero already its probably fun, otherwise it feels like a step backwards in pretty much all regards. Disappointing, but still worth a go if you need some new Shantae in your life. If you have never played the series, ans would like to try one 1/2 Genie Hero again is far better.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: The graphic and story line are good. There are many improvements in transform system, I lke it how Shantae now can transform without dancing quite similar to the Pirate cirse so the game pace is not interupted. The map design and the warp system is very good, it is very Shantae series’ signature. The down side of this 5th game in the series is the boss machanic of this installation is quit boring. It may not bad but the third and forth games’ boss fights are too good. And because the forth game have a very cute ending theme song, so I hope to have another good ending theme song here, but it was not here in the fifth game. Over all I still love this game and will definitely buy the sixth game if it were released.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game lightly, if you already have played previous shantae games and you wanna play this 1, by all means go ahead. As someone who has played all previous entries i have to say that I feel like this one is the weakest entry in the series. And it's kind of hard to explain why honestly, if i compare it to half-genie hero (my favorite one) this game feels much less interesting honestly. The transformations in 1/2 genie hero felt more fun to use, the music and the levels were more vibrant and the game just felt more energetic, The bosses were absurdly easy and I'd just sit there tanking hits with scimitar up + mashing attack and eat food whenever my hp/mana got low. this game felt much more like going through the motions and didn't really have that same sense of fun and adventure. And for being the most recent entry it feels unfair to compare it to the much older entries. If this was a earlier entry I'd be more lenient, but the newest title being this hollow feeling to me is pretty disappointing, at least i got it on sale. Overall and okay game, can't say I had many instances of "fun" playing it though.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Not quite as good as Half-Genie Hero imo, but still a solid entry and a super fun game. This one is more a pure Metroidvania than Half-Genie, so if that's the only one you've played it might be a bit different than you're used to. I did find the bosses a bit underwhelming, and getting 100% is super frustrating, but aside from those pretty minor gripes it's fab.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun metroidvania that took me about 8 hours to beat. The story isn't anything special but it is a fun and upbeat one. The monsters are fun and varied, the boss fights are enjoyable, the transformations are neat and overall I enjoyed my time with the game but felt like it was a bit too easy. I would recommend getting this game during a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I would say this game is great casual game. Which probably is the case of it being released on iOS first.While a bit too easy in general I really liked this game. It did not have frustrating dungeons or difficult sections like Pirates Curse had. Art and graphics are probably the best to date. And the story is light and charming.Biggest negative with this game would be its map. It does not show points of interest. It either should have been in style of Resident Evil 2 Remake or there should have been a purchasable compass or a map of interests.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I like the light-hearted story that doesn't really take itself seriously. The map was (mostly) fun to explore, the controls were tight, the movement felt nice, the character designs are...... nice. The music is pretty good as well. However, there are some parts where the level design is not very good and makes you go out of your way sometimes and it makes navigation feel horrible. I wish I didn't have to press start to see the map like in Hollow knight because that just disrupts gameplay. This game is very easy so I think it is more for beginners than long time fans. As someone who has never played a Shantae game until now, I would recommend it for newbies to platformers or people who just want to relax.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the Seven Sirens feels like one of the better entries of its series. Making the transformations into button presses lends the game a greater sense of flow than waiting for the dances to play out, and the dances still get to return via new non-traversal abilities. The world design also returns to a more conventional, interconnected Metroidvania structure rather than the more disjointed level structure of Pirate's Curse and Half-Genie Hero. It's still Shantae at its core, but it feels like it's evolving in small ways.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Quick reviewGameplay 10/10Difficulty 6.5/10Art 10/10Plot 8/10Mechanics 9/10Power ups 10/10Bosses 8/10My main gripes were the quick drop off in difficulty once you got a certain dance that allowed you to heal, and the balance between available currency and power ups as you progressed. It's not a huge complaint, but i'd love for that to be looked at in the next game. This one brought back the metroidvania style that a lot of people wanted, while adding some interesting mechanics, and as usual being super accessible for all kinds of players. Overall, I'd recommend it to anyone that was interested in platformers, metroidvanias, and games with a fun art style and atmosphere. Had a pretty great time with this title.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: From the top, this game isnt as good as Half Genie Hero. Dont expect that, because it wont happen.The soundtrack is still pretty good, but the game is very bad about giving you an inkling of what to do next. 40% of the games runtime is backtracking through every single room in the game trying to figure out what wall you havent broken since you got the turtle ability, so on and so forth. It's so ridiculous that it makes finding where you're at in a walkthrough a pain in the ass.If you've played Half Genie, go for it. Just know that this is a lower point in the series. I honestly prefered the level based approach.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: This is my third Shantae game I've played the first being Half Genie Hero and the 2nd being Pirate's Curse. I love this series a huge shout out to the YouTuber Fuchsia Butter who made a video about Shantae. Honestly while I had fun with this game I found this Shantae game to be a step back from the other Shantae games. I still recommend this game but I would highly advise you go to the others first if your new to the series. I found this game to be really easy with very little challenge at all. You earn gems WAY to fast I ended up walking out of one dungeon with around 500 gems allowing me to make Shantae very strong very early. There were places where the tactic was SPAM ATTACK UNTIL YOUR THUMB BREAKS, The new transformations like the newt for example takes the same role that the monkey form did in half genie hero, the frog takes up the crab and mermaid and the tortoise takes the role of the elephant. Thanks to the gems you can get healing items and magic abilities which you can get thanks to how fast you earn gems you get fast. The bosses designs are great but they were easy. I had to nerf myself to make the final boss a bit tougher. Maybe I got use to the Shantae games idk. But this game is not bad. The world is awesome, Shantae is still the same adorable half genie we all know and love, the humor is still there, Squid Barron is still the funniest (to me at least), Music is good and a new to Shantae is cutscenes and they are fantastic. It introduces new half genies which is so amazing seeing other half genies besides Shantae and on top of that one of them kind of gives Shantae something that can set up for a sequel. Theres a new card collection system where these cards if assigned can give you buffs. There's different towns and their stores contain different items, After rescuing the half genies and combining powers you get new forms that are new to Shantae. There are invisible enemies that require the first form to find them also theres puzzle hints that require it, the lightning power is to power things like rope machines and wind mills also it does damage against enemies, the plant form to revive dead plants which drop items and gems, and the earthquake form which in certain places can open areas and cause mega damage against enemies. The mystery of the island is interesting and gets you wanting to investigate more. Even though this one is flawed I still enjoyed my time playing this game. If you haven't played Half Genie Hero and the other Shantae games then go straight for this one. However if you're new to the franchise I'd recommend you play the others first.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: The Shantae games may not have the namesake of the genre like Metroid and Castlevania, or the perfected gameplay of Hollow Knight, but this series just oozes charm and I am always overjoyed to rediscover the weirdly 4th-wall breaking meta comedy. I adore this series and every Shantae game is an absolute joy to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Really liked Shantae and the Pirate's Curse so I was looking forward to another Metroidvania-style Shantae game. This game however was a disapointment. The bosses are boring and the game gives you these anoying powerups that just deals damage to everything on screen. The game is boring but I finished the whole story hoping that something interesting would happen, but it never did. Don't bother, play Pirate's Curse instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a pretty fun and easy-going game. I do miss a few things like more depth to the story-the bad guys and the supporting characters feel too shallow, the former are nothing but bosses and the latter could've been so much more interesting, really hoping they bring the other Half-Genies back in future adventures. Some more difficulty wouldn't hurt either and for the love of god some kinda tool to keep track of which collectibles you gathered.Still, I liked tis Shantae better than HGH, an interconnected map feels much better to explore than isolated stages and makes way more sense for a Metroidvania. If future installments of the franchise are like this I'll be more than happy to play them.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the Shantae franchise, I played 4 out of 5 games (I just didn't play the gameboy).It is a very old school metroidvania and enjoyable to play, but what draws the most attention is the art / theme. It has a good story and good characters, it would not be the same success without all this charisma.That said, the franchise is not perfect, but I will refrain from highlighting the cons that are repeated in all games (after all, I understand that the purpose of the game is to be simple and fast, you cannot charge for a triptype A)These are the comparisons with the previous games in the franchise:Difficulty: Gained a drastic reduction compared to other games. Even the "B-side" unlocked when the game is over is still pretty easy. While Pirate's Curse has puzzles that you spend 20 minutes trying and failing, and Half-Genie Hero has Hardcore mode and DLC campaigns that are very challenging, this one you finish in the most casual way possible.Playing time: Unlike the difficulty, there was a nice increase in the duration of the game. Even focusing only on finishing fast, it takes about 6h to 8h to finish the game in the first game, dropping to 3h to 4h the second time you play, but the highlight is to close 100%. The amount of extra stuff you have to focus on looking for on the map, and things well hidden, increases to up to 15h. If you try to get all the achievements, this time increases even more, having to start another save until, and it does not get boring, it is a lot of fun to be collecting 100%.Innovation: Although the game's proposal is to be retro, it added some new mechanics. The former command to transform now invokes the magic of the other half-genius, and some enemies need specific spells to be defeated, I thought it was pretty cool. While the transformations you now use with normal commands. In part, it became faster to transform, on the other hand, it took away much of the potential of the transformations. They make the movement and disappear, there is not much to do with them. It also limited aquatic exploitation a lot.The card system was something unprecedented in the franchise, but it seems that it did it to be more similar to the current games. Partly it is legal to collect the cards (apart from those you have to collect 10 to use), but using only 3 of them at a time is a pain. Either you are limited to using a spell just to focus on the effect of the cards, or you have to press start all the time and change them whenever you do something different. If the idea was to open up a range of strategies, it failed, it makes you use less variety, and in the end you will stay the same as always. It would be much better if as soon as you take the card, the effect is permanently active.Soundtrack: Here, unfortunately, I can't defend. He sinned ugly. The quality dropped a lot. I have songs from Pirate's Curse and Half-Genie in my playlist, but in this game there is no single song to save. It seems that they were all made in a program to create generic music for games. Some can defend saying that it is nostalgic for being simple, but if compared to the soundtrack of other games I cry blood.Final conclusions: Apart from the soundtrack, the game is fantastic. I recommend that you play and replay several times.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first run of this game and I have to say, hats off to WayForward for another great installment in the Shantae series. I definitely recommend this game SPOILERS AHEAD, YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED!!!The Good: Things that this game did great with- The setting: Having the game take place on a tropical island instead of the traditional setting that we are used to is a great change of pace. It's not something that I would particularly want to see repeated but for this game its fun and refreshing.- The Animation: I loved the animated bits of the game. It looked great and it was always nice to watch, if anything I would have liked to see more animated cut scenes sprinkled throughout the game.- The gameplay: The gameplay ran smooth and the mechanics were solid. The initial buttons to play were a little weird but they let you customize them.(Note, try to use a controller if possible. The controls can get a little jenky if you use keyboard and try to customize the buttons)- The humor: I love the semi self-aware, 4th wall breaking humor of the game from turning Shantae and Sky into action figures to Squid Baron pitching a new game idea to Shantae, its all a lot of fun and it works great with the tone of the game.The Bad: While this was a great game and well worth the price to play it wasn't perfect. - The other half-genies, while all likable, felt somewhat one dimensional and while I understand that there are limits to characterization in a platformer I just felt that they were lacking, their dialogue didn't really let the player get to know who they are beyond their one dimensional personality which are the mature older sister, the intense one, the shy one, and the slightly hyper young one. - The dialogue of the main cast felt lacking. Sky is the only one that you really get to speak with regularly and her dialogue is usually some variation of go away I'm relaxing right now. You hardly get to see Bolo, or Uncle Mimic to the point were mimic is almost only present during cutscenes and bolo's presence isn't much better.The Meh: Things that were ok but could have been better.- The transformations are good but not great. WayForward decided to forgo Shantae's traditional animal forms in favor of using special animals native to the island. On paper this sounds great but in practice you kinda miss some of her OG transformations. I would have kept the monkey transformation for the wall climbing and dashing since that is her most iconic one, ditch the frog (it looked kinda dumb), use the newt for the swimming portion and the other two transformations can stay the same.- The difficulty: The game felt rather easy, I don't know if I was just taking my time and that was what was making it so easy. I never had any health problems, the monsters dropped so much food that it was never an issue. I didn't actually buy any potions until the right before the final boss and that was only because I had such a surplus of gems to spend. Also, I got gems pretty easily, it wouldn't be uncommon to finish an area with 500 gems to go buy the items (one time I walked out with max gems, wasn't even trying to farm them). I would recommend adding a difficulty setting to the game with the higher difficulty having enemies hit harder or have more health as well as dropping less stuff.TLDR; I loved the game, pick it up for yourself if you've played the other Shantae games, like platformers with fun mechanics, or you just think it's interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: My only real complaint about the game is that it's incredibly easy. Aside from that, I really really like it and recommend it to anyone who enjoys the series. The setting and music in this game are my favorites in the whole series, and I also really enjoy what they did with the transformations. I do wish the dances got utilized a bit more, but I still like them in concept.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun Metroidvania style game. Not frustratingly difficult and has a lot of light-hearted humor. Seems to be average length for these style of games. I enjoyed it a lot and there is no shortage of waifus to love. If you enjoyed Shantae 1/2 Genie Hero, this is more of a good thing for you.The only con I can provide is that sometimes the game is a little vague on where to go. It also 'felt' short, but mostly because I was enjoying it so much. Count me in the for next game!
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: While I have not yet beaten the game, I have very much prepared the 11 or so hours I've put into it so far. I was one of the people who actually really liked 1/2 Genie Hero's attempt to shake up the typical Shantae formula with stages instead of the more traditional metroidvania dungeons and regions, but this game returns to something a little more typical for Shantae's method of interacting with the world. It does reuse a lot of 1/2 Genie Hero assets which, honestly, I'm fine with, I don't need a new image of what a Crab looks like every new game. My one complaint, though, is that I want it to be just a pinch harder. I've faced down against three dungeon bosses so far without running into any real problems, and I have nearly every upgrade in the game's shops. Maybe I'm on the cusp of meeting some truly taxing bosses, and maybe there's more upgrades coming around the corner, but so far I feel like I'm running out of core mechanics to explore and am hitting that old adventure-game standby of going to every room in sequence and trying out every item and power to see if I can find new interactions (here's to the Metroidvania and Adventure Game formats!) All in all, though, the game's funny, the mystery's mysterious, and while all of the cutscenes keep breaking into crazy artifacts I'm still having a good time anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 50/50 on this one, been a fan since Risky's Revenge and granted I'm not the biggest fan for Metroidvanias.Visuals are fantastic and the cast of colourful characters and dialogues all there thankfully, but I feel like this is 1 step forward 2 steps back from Half-Genie Hero. Now granted the level based structure HGH and The Pirate's Curse also felt a bit shallow, but here as a Metroidvania it feels kinda basic. In HGH the levels felt so cool and fresh to explore with the detailed 2.5D backgrounds but here it's kinda just samey looking tile based rooms with different paint jobs.Likewise the gameplay loop feels a bit overly simplistic, there's not really any fun and challenging platforming or interesting "battles" and the bosses are incredibly basic. Granted it does mean the game feels very nice and relaxing if you're looking for a metroidvania-lite with pleasing visuals while you dig into a podcast or something on the other monitor.It is an enjoyable title but one that I'm struggling to finish now that it's felt the same for the past few dungeons.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Besides the BGM from the menu screen being reused in a couple of places/moments I love this game, a very worthy addition to the series. Puzzles are great, platforming is fun, story is goofy and colourful as always, the addition of animated segments is welcoming. It would be nice if they voiced all dialouges as opposed to only a few sentences (like they did in 1/2 Genie Hero) but since this is an indie game I can't complain, especially for the price, here is hoping for DLC or better yet a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: With gorgeous graphics, excellent music, and a true metroidvania experience this could have been one of the best games of 2020, a magnum opus for WayForward..... Unfourtunately, it has one huge problem: The existence of consumable health items. The consumable health items exist because after 20 years WarForward still hasn't figured out that the green save guy is supposed to heal you to full health when you save. Because the health items exist, you can heal anytime, any place, and you'll never run out of healing items and this makes the game a complete and utter joke if played normally, it is simply impossible to die. Therefore, In order to enjoy this game and make it fun you will have to manually implement the proper healing system in this game. You do this by setting a strict rule for yourself to only use your consumable healing items right before you save. You MUST adhere to this rule no matter how frustrated you may get at some point, otherwise you will pretty much ruin this game for yourself. Oh, also, don't buy this game if you don't have a SSD drive that you can install it on. The load times will be huge if you install this game on a HDD.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I've always been a huge fan of Metroidvania style games and will almost always love them without question and this game was no exception.  While I don't feel like this game brings anything new to the table, I also don't see that as a bad thing.  I came to this game seeking a familiar, fun and just enjoyable game and that's exactly what I got.  The music is the same,  It's nothing new for the series, but that's why I love it!  Gameplay?  Just as slick and enjoyable as I remember.  Characters?  Same ones with a few new additions that I've come to love.  Art?  A beautiful and colourful hand drawn experience that to a younger me would have felt like he was playing a cartoon.  I just can't gush enough about this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Can't say there's too much I really dislike about the game so far, loading times are a teeny bit too long, but it's not a deal breaker. The controls are good, music is awesome, and characters/art is great. I think Seven Sirens holds up pretty well with the rest of the franchise and is worth a try if you're a fan of the series. Maybe not the best starting point for a beginner, but still fun as your intro to the franchise too.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the Seven Sirens is a very accessible game. There has been a lot of criticism about how easy the game is, and it definitely is easier than previous Shantae games, but it feels to me as if they're trying to pull in new fans and make the series more accessible to newcomers rather than rely on pandering to old fans.Onto the game itself, I think the most amazing new addition is the addition of fully animated cutscenes which, while typically short, are awesome and make me really want a Shantae animated project in the future. Most of the music in the game is nothing special, but there are particular songs in the labyrinths that are really good and get stuck in my head. The transformations are fluidly enabled and I had no issues coming back to the game after a short break and still remembering how to do things, which is more than I can say for previous games.The biggest gripe I have with the game is the bosses. In particular, the final boss (no spoilers as to who/what it is) has so much health and it just hurts mashing the attack button for 5 minutes non-stop. The attacks aren't even particularly difficult to dodge, it's just a bullet sponge that takes forever to defeat. I can forgive doing it the first time, but after the fourth time defeating the boss, it was incredibly draining.There's also no on-screen indicator of where collectibles you're missing could be, so if you're missing a squid heart or a nugget and you aren't sure where it could be and you don't want to refer to an online map, you're kind of screwed, especially since some collectibles can be not-so-obviously hidden and require use of an ability to see it. 100%ing a single game of Seven Sirens was harder than 100%ing a single run of the previous games that are on Steam.Overall, yes, this is an easier Shantae game. It has less content than Half-Genie Hero and it isn't as fun as Pirate's Curse, but this is still a quality Shantae game that would appeal to you more if you're new to the series than if you're a returning fan. I definitely recommend getting it, I still smiled and laughed at many points and the maneuverability when you're trying to 100% things is really smooth.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: The most fun I've had playing any of the Shantae titles. It might not be the most challenging thing in the world, but its just so delightfully charming and fun that I got totally absorbed by it. The return to a more traditional metroidvania structure after Half-Genie Hero was a welcome change, and the small QoL changes made to transformations make it an even more snug fit for the game. The card collecting is a nice addition, new powers are a blast... everything in this game appears to be tuned to make it the comfiest possible experience to play.As to be expected from Shantae, the writing is tongue-in-cheek, quick-witted, and super charming. Seven Sirens features some of the most fun character moments in the series since Pirate's Curse. Throughout every interaction, from the start of the game up until the final boss, I was smiling.Some personal gripes:- overly long load times for area transitions, not a dealbreaker but made the 100% cleanup run more of a drag than it should have been.- some slightly underwhelming animated cutscenes (though admittedly, the opening movie by TRIGGER is a hard act to follow)- the dancing minigame is a super hard miss in a really strong game, and quite disappointing in concept, considering Shantae's whole gimmick.Those downsides in mind, I still can't say I've enjoyed any other Shantae as much as this one. Sure, Pirate's Curse might have had more interesting story stuff going on, but this one is the whole package. Would recommend to longtime fans and anyone remotely interested in checking it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: While I recommend this game, I must say it's absolutely the weakest in the series. It doesn't feel like it was made with love.In fact, the whole thing feels rushed and you can see where the corners were cut very obviously. Gone are the detailed story, character interactions, and villain introductions. There are some great animations by Studio Bones, but it feels like that's where the entire budget went. Most of the character animations and models are recycled from Half-Genie Hero, which would be fine if they at least made them look as good as they did in that game, but they don't. Each of the bosses clearly has a defined design, but you never get to understand what they're about because any story involving them was cut out, so they just show up at the end of stages without explanation. They're also boring and way too easy. In fact, boring and way too easy defines most of this game.So while it's a fine game in a vacuum, when compared to other Shantae games, it's a real disappointment.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: It's a funny, cute metroidvania with just enough of a challenge to keep the gameplay interesting without going into "tough as nails" territory. I found it easier than Half-Genie Hero but also a lot more enjoyable, especially since there's less emphasis on the platforming than on mastering new abilities to access new parts of the map. I finished the game in about 15 hours, though there's a new game plus mode and special win screens to unlock by beating it under more difficult conditions if you're looking for an excuse to play through it again.

_childDocuments_.review: The latest entry in the Shantae series is fantastic, as always. Vibrant blend of 3D and 2D artwork combined with tight controls and the series' signature (mildly) lewd character designs make an excellent platformer that doubles as an antidepressant. Shantae games have consistently great music, and Seven Sirens is best in series. (IMO)

_childDocuments_.review: Solid entry to the Shantae series but not the best.  The return to a metroidvania style is a welcome change but the load times between areas are quite high.  Dances have been changed to screen wide abilities with a magic cost. Transformations were merged into Shantae's move-set streamlining map traversal so it has a bit of a different feel from previous games.   Fans of the series should pick this up but if you are new to the series then "Shantae and the Pirate's Curse" is arguably better.

_childDocuments_.review: This may be one of the weakest Shantae entries, but that's still more than enough to get a "worth playing" for me. A fast and gratifying platform game moveset with all of Wayforward's superb animation, lots of collectables to scour the map for, and a lovely story of intrigue that advances the Shantae franchise's overarching plot kept me engaged happily. It might have a few mediocre moments -- it's far too easy, and the environment design just doesn't feel quite right -- but they weren't enough to kill the game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Seven Sirens is a very welcome installment in Shantae's story, bringing back the series' Metroidvania roots after they were neglected in Half-Genie Hero. The new Fusion Coin upgrades are a nice compromise between Shantae's traditional transformations and the more fluid on-the-go actions of Pirate's Curse, while Shantae's new dances offer all-new ways to interact with the game's environment. The series' tongue-in-cheek sense of humor is as strong as ever, including the return of fan-favorite side characters like Squid Baron and the Squidsmith.The game's biggest flaw is probably its poorly optimized loading screens -- moving between zones causes a huge spike in the game's resource usage, and it often takes several seconds to finish the transition. While it's not a problem inside the various dungeons, it quickly becomes grating when quests (or unexpected zone borders) require you to make several transitions in a short period of time.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Long time fan of the Shantae series and this new entry does not disappoint. The animated cutscenes add additional charm that makes me wish that wayforward would just bite the bullet and make a cartoon out of some of their series like this. As positive about this game as I'm about to be, I should start with some things that weren't so good right off the bat. -The music in game lacked...something. It's hard to place a finger on it, but the soundtrack just feels kind of generic and lack luster this time around. The music isn't overly atmospheric and the intro theme song feels more like the opening to a cartoon than related to the game you get to play. -The frog transformation: This was just...a complete disappointment. In past games you got to explore slowly in the water, dealing with enemies, puzzles and had skills to back up that exploration. here...you use a frog that you can barely see, where everything that touches you is an instakill, and you're navigating hallways of spikes, or getting locked in rooms to collect money. If the water sections were taken out, the game would lose nothing for it and that's disappointing as the water sections in other games were always some of my favorites. -Voice over in standard dialogue. I loved the voice acting in the cutscenes, and the periodic full line being voiced was great, but that's where the problem lies. Aside from very few full lines, the characters often shout out names, or part of a line or even...things that aren't in the dialogue at all and instead of being engaging, it winds up being more distracting and stilted. I'd love having just cutscenes voiced or even the first sentence in a paragraph, but not scattershot like this. -The fusion transformations. I loved the artwork for the fusion dance transformations, but they felt...incomplete somehow. I would have loved it if Shantae transformed and instead of a screen effect, she had new platforming abilities or ways to attack or solve puzzles, making the magic feel less a gimmick that wound up being clunky to use and more an integrated part of exploration. The same ideas could be kept where the refresh magic blooms flowers or the electric magic turns on lights and such, but make it something the player manually gets to participate in.-The Seer dance...entirely. There are rarely hints that you may want to use this dance, and because accessing it takes so long it's exhausting seer dancing in every room that might have something...and even then, some of the reveals are in places that you are never going to realize you could, should or might need to do the dance. Some hint, a minor particle effect or a shared layout, a shadow where it shouldn't be...something would have been more enjoyable. It felt like bombing walls in zelda 1. Rewarding...but tedious.  Those gripes aside, this game was an absolute blast. The return to the interconnected world like the original game or even pirate's curse was a welcome return to form as the jilted fully separated zones that didn't feel connected or deep aside from selecting them on the map screen never sat well with me. A few more fast travel options would be nice and a bigger map would have been appreciated, but this isn't hollow knight, it's Shantae and the game felt just fine without those niceties. The new snappy transformations are a blast, though felt a bit puzzle solving only, I'd like to maybe see a new game where you have the snappy, quick puzzle solving transformations, but also transformations that can change up combat or give new skills that can be more long term. The cutscenes and animation were outstanding. While it can be exhausting that wayforward changes Shantae up with each iteration, it really feels like they hit the nail on the head here and I hope that this new style keeps going forward. The sprites are similar enough in the past few games that she doesn't feel much different to play, and I hope we get more voice acting and cutscenes in a future game. The game controls how you would expect from any wayforward game I've played all the way back to the first Shantae. The jumps, movement and weight to the character feel appropriate and the transformation (newt and octo) don't ever feel out of control or frustrating to use. Shantae controls as well as you could ever ask for in a metroidvania titleIf you like the shantae series, or are a fan of metroidvania games in general, this title comes highly recommended.
