_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Overall, it seems to take all the best elements from its predecessors, especially HGH and Pirate's Curse, and it adds lots of new improvements. A must-play for Shantae fans. It's my favorite game in the series by a long shot.- Feels mechanically solid like HGH. Generally responsive and feels nice to play, especially the platforming. You jump and move around a lot quicker.- They've got some great new ideas for transformations. (One of them is so fun that it's become an all-time favorite of mine.) Transforming into creatures has been moved to fusions (quick actions), and your actual dance menu is for special abilities. I think it's a lot more fluid this way, especially compared to the three-layer dance menu of HGH.- The length seems about average for the series, maybe longer. The pacing is very enjoyable for a normal playthrough, but as always, it can be tedious if you're going for all achievements.- Difficulty-wise, this might be the easiest game in the series, except maybe HGH if you don't count its DLC. The combat difficulty is fine, but you get practically infinite recovery items so you can always just pause and heal up. Though there is a mode where you take double damage, so it might be better there.- I love the addition of a "bestiary" in the form of collectible cards, each with its own equippable perk. It's a really fun addition that I hope they keep in future games. Unlocking them is satisfying progress-wise, and lets you focus on your preferred playstyle. It can be really tedious to farm for some of the enemies, but thankfully it's not counted for 100% if that's what you care about. (None of the really good perks are easily missed.)- Level design is back to open world, with the overall layout feeling more like Risky's Revenge than anything. HGH was more of a side-scroller, but this goes back to the classic Metroidvania style that rewards thorough exploration and revisiting areas. The layout and visual design of the levels is some of the best in the franchise, easily putting HGH's levels to shame. (The blending of 2D and 3D art is a lot smoother this time.)- Expands from HGH's art style, with lots of new Trigger-esque art. The new dialogue sprites are particularly engaging. The new UI is also very pleasing, giving it a more modern/streamlined take on HGH's UI. The new map is especially nice.- The new tropical/aquatic setting is refreshing. It doesn't stray too far from the series' style, but it still gives this game a strong identity of its own. (Which was something sorely missing from HGH, good as it was.)- Animated cutscenes add a layer of depth to the narrative that you couldn't really get before. I didn't get the impression that cutscenes were necessary in previous games, but you can really appreciate them here. In general the quality isn't nearly on-par with the Trigger animated intro, but they're decent on their own and still enjoyable.- Lots of voice acting. Cristina Vee does great as always, but with far more lines than before. Voices from HGH like Cherami Leigh's are also here, as well as new talent that really fits the characters. (Especially Mimic, who didn't get voiced in HGH.)- The story & writing overall goes a bit deeper (like Pirate's Curse) but at a larger scale, while still carrying forward the simple charm and tongue-in-cheek humor that the series is known for. It also does an excellent job of expanding on character relationships from previous games, surprising you with some moments of real nuance. Personally I like this game's story the most out of any so far.- Part of the fun of any Shantae game is spotting little references and elements from earlier games, and there is plenty of that here. Classic enemy designs have gotten reworks, NPC dialogue is a treat as always, there's music and dialogue throwbacks going back to even the original on the Gameboy, etc.- Lots of new characters with fun designs and personalities. They fit right in and expand on the lore of the genies.- Music is great as always. Old themes are remixed and there are enjoyable new aquatic/tropical tracks. Despite not having Jake Kaufman around, they did a great job. Some of the new music really complements the setting. Hope they can get Virt back next time though.I'm really glad to see the franchise where it's at now. The folks at Wayforward are full of ideas and are willing to take risks, and clearly understand everything that makes the games so entertaining. It's apparent how much care, attention, and passion go into these games, and that really comes through to make an enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I received Shantae and the Seven Sirens as a gift from a friend and was glad I did. It has all of the color, charm and musicality I've come to expect from the series, with the welcome return of the open-world exploration not seen since Risky's Revenge. It features animated cutscenes beyond just the intro, a series first, which you no doubt have heard were animated by Studio Trigger. There's also some character art by Inti Creates. It is unfortunate that Jake Kaufman was not involved with this game's soundtrack, but I hear he was busy and there's always next time. The game has a few design and technical issues that are oft vented about in the steam forums, though with an undue amount of vitriol. The game is a far cry from the disappointing DLCs for the previous title, further marking them as anomalies in a otherwise consistently fun and chill series.This entry sees our half-genie heroine and friends on a much needed island vacation to meet other half-genies, that quickly goes awry thanks to the unfailing appearance and malfeasance of pirate queen Risky Boots, and a new, mystical threat dwelling beneath the island. You'd think Risky would stop being such a pain in the ass after having HER ass repeatedly saved by Shantae, but hey, at least she's consistent.As mentioned above, this fifth iteration marks the return of the Metroid-style map layout last seen in the second game, with a number of interconnected regions and three different hub towns, each with multiple exits and warp rooms. The game is still fairly linear otherwise and compared to its inspirations, with core ability progression taking you from one region to the next in sequence, but with room to backtrack and search for collectibles at pretty much any point up to and including standing outside the final boss's door. However, outside of the dungeons there is no way to track your collected items, and no way of even knowing your overall completion percentage without quitting back to the file select screen. This is a rather glaring omission from any metroidvania, and certainly from a fifth title in a series. Thanks to the map guide here on steam I was able to find everything, but I had to revisit several areas more then I would have liked. Regardless, it was far from impossible to achieve 100% completion.Dance magic returns, but is handled differently then before- traversal abilities are now regulated to dedicated quick button inputs a la Pirate's Curse, with the actual dances now resulting in screen-filling spell effects that can do damage, heal Shantae (and certain other characters and objects) and reveal secrets. Coupled with the series mainstay attack spells such as the orbiting spikeballs, that run of a Zelda-style magic meter, Shantae has more means of attack and healing then ever before, and that's saying something. Shantae 5 is still far to the easy side of metroidvanias and platformers, and though this is a frequent point of complaint against the series, I would kindly ask those people to ♥♥♥♥ off and leave me to my enjoyment. Go play Hollow Knight if you want to be punished while collecting things so badly. That's a great game mind you, but I maintain that games being "too easy" is an entitlement problem as compared to games being too hard being an accessibility problem. Any time Wayforward has listened to these types of complaints, the resulting changes have been to the game's detriment.The game runs well for the most part and controls fine on keyboard, in contrast to a lot of platformers. The default control mapping, as in 1/2 Genie Hero, is very similar to the control mapping I used in the typical SNES emulator, a surprising bonus. Unlike the fourth game however, this game is subject to a weird loading issue where it places a strain on my processor and takes just a few seconds longer then it seemingly ought to. It doesn't go above the level of low-grade irritation but it never got any better in that regard. The game also crashes on exit, for what that's worth, and crashed seconds into a new game as well until I verified the steam files. The series' penchant for amusing dialogue, appealing character designs for protagonists, NPCs, enemies and bosses alike, somewhat interesting but not frustrating dungeon mechanics and presentation in boss fights are present and accounted for, and Seven Sirens exceeds 1/2 Genie Hero in overall quality, especially when I take things like Friends to the End and the Costume Pack into account. I feel that Pirate's Curse was still the strongest entry in the series, but Seven Sirens has a level of glam, glitter and visual polish which belies the series' humble Game Boy Color origins, and it was enough fun that I didn't put it down until the credits rolled. Technical and design shortcomings aside, Seven Sirens is every bit the charming cartoon adventure the genre deserves and a sign of even better genie goodness in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is somewhat conditionally positive and I would implore you to seek out all the other games in this series long before turning to this particular entry, as it is by far the weakest and overall just an OK game that won't set your passions ablaze. The past games are really great, and this one just comes as a disappointment, as one can very much enjoy it, but it feels like a massive letdown compared to previous games.The interactions between characters and dialogue as always is a highlight of the series, making fun of tropes and gameplay elements, but on further reflection nothing much really happens and only slightly adds to the lore introduced in the reboot Half-Genie Hero. The story itself just amounts to you being the only one capable of doing anything at first so everything from then on falls to you.The art style is a return to form for the series after Half Genie Hero's experiment with 3D environments with 2D sprites and is more or less functional. I don't find it more or less than adequate and it's hard to express more than "it works and the character's look good".The music and sound is equally serviceable. It more or less uses music from the previous entries, with some new additions, but does not have anything that jumps out.And finally gameplay... The part that more or less caused me to become unenthused with this outing.  This is a metroidvania game, where you get new abilities to get around as you go. This happens in two ways: upgrading your  movement, and gaining the power to summon abilities of other half-genies. The first part is fine and normal for this genre, but the summons drag down the flow and is more or less pointless except to act as keys to unlock segments of the map as opposed to being an active part of your arsenal. It would have been better as either an active ability you could wield, or  switching to that other character that you gained the ability from to keep you actively involved in the game and not halting the action.The game will not challenge you, giving you plenty of healing items and health, whether you seek it out or not. It took me around 10-15 hours to beat the game with 100% items, and on my second run, I easily managed to get to the end of the game 100% under 4 hours without even upgrading my health. The hardest boss fight in the game is hard not because of the skill required, but because of the randomness of the arrangement of platforms  to attack the weakpoints. And that doesn't make it hard, just frustrating.The power-ups provided in shops have more or less lost all purpose compared to the previous entries except for the rotating spikes, and even then it more or less can be passed by as it only offers slightly more damage output or being useful in one boss fight. I don't mean to come off as harsh as I do, as the game is fine and enjoyable on it's own merits, but I don't think this game is worth $30 especially compared to the past games that were leagues better designed. Play any of the others on steam. Play the Gameboy Color original (it's on the 3DS eshop). Unless you have an overwhelming desire to play this one for some reason or have played the others and can't get enough bellydancing should you consider this anemic sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game with great gameplay mechanics, visuals and memorable/catchy music. the return to the metroidvania style is a big highlight but also feels small (especially the overworld) in terms of map size.The game is moderately challenging with the bosses actually being quite tough at times, but thanks to the wide range of abilities, power ups and customizable nature of the monster cards, the bosses are only as difficult as your ability to take them on.Like i said with the overworld being too small, the game's story is very short and doesn't feel like its been taken to its full potential. Unlike the past games where the story revolved around the characters and the lore of the world, this game has a pretty generic and predictable storyline with no surprises that is also easily completable in 5 to 8 hours if you are just doing the story, or in my case, 11 hours because i went back to collect all the items for the 100%.in general i really loved the game despite the lack of exploration and lackluster/short story. What was there however was really fun and enjoyable, and is part of the reason why i feel like there needs to be more.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: The fifth Shantae game and it is as cute as ever!Shantae and the Seven Sirens offers:- a full open world map and boss dungeons to explore, a great step up compared to Half Genie Hero:- instant animal transformations, you can dash, wall climb, stomp, swim and double jump with a press of a button; great to keep the pace of platforming;- dances are now used for wide screen magic to find hidden secrets, open new paths to continue the story and damage the enemies;- monster cards to collect from dead enemies to add up to three passive bonuses to customize your gameplay;- fully animated cutscenes during key moments of the story and before a boss encounter!So, overall it looks like a great improvement over Half Genie Hero and almost as good as Pirate's Curse but there are few glaring issues i have with the game:- Loading times..... Even on a SSD, the game takes quite few seconds to load between an area to the other and eats away CPU too. This is quite annoying especially in the first few minutes of gameplay where you have to move in an out of the first town multiple times. Wayfoward aknowledged this but we don't have an ETA to a possible fix.- Trying to 100% this game is painful, some items are hidden in such way you need to use the Seer dance in every screen, even multiple times to find some obscure hint where a Squid or a Nugget (items needed to 100%) are hidden. Sure, treasure hunting is a core of Shantae games but in Seven Sirens became annoying without a collectible counter like in Pirate's Curse and Half Genie Hero. I suggest to try to find everything without the use of a guide once or twice, but don't feel ashamed if you resort to read where your missing collectables are.- The difficulty is really low. This time healing items and gems are dropped too often so i've found myself with most of the spells and upgrade at the end of the second dungeon and a bunch of healing items to tank most of the damage from enemies while rushing to get all treasures and bosses. Be prepared to not find too big of a challenge in this game.In conclusion, even with the glaring issues this game has, i really enjoyed it, because i still found the charm of a Shantae title i look for: cute characters, funny moments and the reward of exploration i love in a metroidvania.If you can move past the problems this game has, you will still enjoy Seven Sirens for a nice casual experience! Maybe wait for a sale instead of being a Shantae fanboy like me that paid full price ;)

_childDocuments_.review: This is game for the casual player. If you're looking for an andrenaline fueled twitch fest - look elsewhere. There's no real threat at any point and basically everyone should get through it with minimal difficulties.  It's not the best in the series and the writing is sub par compared to the ridiculously crazy stories in e.g. the Pirate's Curse. But all in all it feels like an OK addition to the franchise and it doesn't have the crazy difficulty spike at the end that some others have.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: This is a super solid game! It takes a lot of the gameplay from 1/2 Genie Hero and refines it. Movement is smooth and fairly seamless, and gets much moreso as you gain transformations - the direct opposite of what happens with the transformations in earlier games. That's a massive improvement. The character controls very well now, and there's a fair amount to do and explore in the game with a pretty good variety of enemies, too. One thing I have to criticize is the difficulty. Normal Mode is waaaaaay too easy - you never even have to bother with the shop, and I died *once* through my whole initial playthrough. Playing it through again on Magic Mode just made me think 'why isn't this the default difficulty?' Magic mode brings the game up to a comfortable level of challenge and makes shop items much more worth it. If I were someone looking to play the game, I'd probably ask around for a cleared game save so I could play through on magic mode right from the start.Regardless, still a 5/5 for me. Solid Metroidvania with good platforming and a great lighthearted style.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game, jumping in to the Shantae series playing this was a blast. I thought the story was amazing and found playing this game quite addictive. The achievement grind was extremely fun and rewarding. overall the boss fights are extremely straightforward but each of the individual transformations are unique and fun to experiment with. I would highly recommend this game even if you have never played a Shantae game, you wont be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Seven Sirens has all the elements that made the previous games so great.The card system and new cutscenes are great additions.The only two bad things I can say about the game:1. The game is very easy.2. Music is definitely not up to par with previous games.Despite these minor flaws, it's easily one of the best games in the series.Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: good game, despite what people are saying the soundtrack is pretty good (not as good as the others though, but just by an inch) only thing I hate is the fact that there are no markers/pin-points on the map on where nuggets & heart squids are already found. I found myself going in circles around the map trying to 100% the game. This really tests your temptation to look it up, and even though I didn’t, I’m sure most people did. _childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Game's pretty fun, feels like another round of half genie hero, overall music is great, gameplay is fun and the whole game is very well designed, has the same issues as any other platformer, lots of backtracking and exploration, but if you don't mind that, it's a great experience, and well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I start with my biggest concern, and that is the games moving away from transformation dances. I am aware that they kinda bring the game play to a halt, so I'm not strictly against instant transformations. I just wished they still incorporated dance moves in some way.Which is an overall critique of this game. It barely representing the dancer side of Shantae or her energetic character. There is a dancing mini game, but it kinda proves my point, since there barely is dancing involved.I still enjoyed the game. The writing wasn't at it's best, but it got better over time. The character i think they did best was Rottytops, even though she wasn't present during most of the game. (She's always a joy.) And though i don't want to spoil it i really liked the conclusion.There's still some choices I don't understand. Most of the transformations where functionally the same as those that already existed. (Maybe they had too much artwork they didn't know what to do with?) Same for the location, which didn't differentiate itself from sequin land all that much. Also it now feels kind of weird that in previous games there could be pretend half genies. (Which was kind of a fun running gag.) But non of that are deal breakers. This was not the perfect game featuring my favorite belly dancing half genie. That's still somewhere out there. But i still had a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: A solid entry that brings Shantae back to it's Metroid-vania roots with great visuals and a fun world to explore. A few issues I had were:-The bosses being either tedious or very easy. The final boss was easily the best. -In order to 100% the game you to collect all enemy cards which can drop randomly upon defeating them and as far as I could tell there's no way to increase those odds making it annoying constantly kill the same enemy until it drops enough cards to complete the set. That alone discouraged me from collecting everything.-The game started off a bit difficult but manageable and quickly became very easy thanks to the consumable items that can restore your health in the menu and eventual enemy cards that further assist you. A fix for this is having less restoration items overall and instead of them being menu items they should make you use them in real time and have a delay of using it so it's not spammable.-Surprisingly long load times for transitioning between zones or warping. While not on SSD generally games like this load within 3 to 5 seconds but this usually took about 8-10 seconds which surprised me and made bactracking for secrets just a bit more annoying.What I liked/loved:-The music which I saw some didn't like but I found many tracks to be great to listen to and really distinct from one another.-The animations/visuals, while outside of the opening the normal animation is okay. The in-game animations are fantastic and expressive-The dialogue is great with just the right amount of charm and jokes that had me chuckle at the scenarios and references.-The character design is as fantastic as it's ever been with many of the new NPCs and enemies really caught my eye-The progression system is simple and a classic but still feels great every time you get an upgrade to your abilities and healthOverall a great game with a few issues that felt minor thanks to the great dialogue, controls, amazing art and the classic sense of progression that you get from games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I had a fun time with this game, despite how extremely easy it is. The story and characters are fun and endearing, the action is always fast and fluid, and the movement is precise if somewhat overly forgiving. My first play through took about 9 hours, which makes this an exceptionally good game to play if you're on a sick day or something. Ultimately, this game is geared towards younger or less experienced players and it does some hand holding throughout, but not in a way that is detrimental to exploration. Due to the forgiving and responsive controls, even novice Metroidvania players will be able to perform impressive acrobatics by the end. Certainly not as engaging or as good as Shantae and the Pirates Curse, but the art and music are excellent throughout and it brings the same charm and charisma through the fantastic characters. I definitely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. The main narrative is very engaging, with a great cast of characters new and old. The combat is simple, yet fun as always. It is very inspired by both Pirate's Curse and Half-Genie hero. The new transformations were changed so that you didn't have to dance in order to transform, instead you could do it right on the fly, just like how Pirate's Curse attacks were. But they still had dance transformations, which served more as a tool to unlock secrets and passageways throughout the levels.One of my only complaints (which is a small complaint) is that a lot of the zones aren't very unique. The East and West surface zones are their own things, but all the other underground zones pretty much have the exact same designs, just different colors. Just to clarify, the separate rooms/puzzles were NOT the same, each one had a different and unique approach, it's just that the art design is essentially the same.The other complaint I had, which I feel a little more strongly about, is that some of the bosses were just too easy. I won't go into too much detail as to avoid spoiling the game, but there were bosses in this game where I purposefully avoided using certain magic spells, or attacked a little more slowly just so I wouldn't defeat them as fast. Some bosses were fun and challenging, however, so it's not entirely a lost. The final boss fight was really fun, and definitely something to look forward to. I haven't played the 'New Game+' mode yet, which I'm hoping will make the bosses a little more challenging on my next play through.All in all, if you're looking for a nice casual single player to just have fun with, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just an average MedroidVania. The Magic is too overpowered the analog controlls are clunky as hell. I recommend the D-Pad. If you change the biome you get a loading screen every time. I mean this game is just 4GB big and can load it im my RAM why the hell do they use loading screens. I wasted 42 minutes witjust loading the next area.If you want to play a good MetriodVania go for Messenger, Ori or Hollow Knight.The only good thing about this game is the artstyle.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the Seven Sirens is a enjoyable game, but I believe it isn't worth its price to new or less avid fans of the series.The quick and easy use of the transformations, the funny dialogue, story and new Animal and Fusion transformations make this a great game.The lack of the character development for the Bosses and especially the new Half Genies is underwhelming and the game felt a little too easy with a lack of challenge.The soundtrack doesn't appeal to me as much as Jake Kaufman's tracks but it is still good and worthy of the series/Overall, Shantae and the Seven Sirens provided a great 10 hour romp through a new setting, new characters and the Metroid-vania styled gameplay last seen in The Pirate's Curse, scratching that itch for a new Shantae game. If you're not a fan, I'd suggest starting with either Risky's Revenge or The Pirate's Curse, working your way to this game, whenever it gets a price drop.

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae and the seven sirens is a very good game. It's a good 9 out of 10 and in my opinion a step up from half-genie hero. The game itself is easy but can give you a problem if you aren't paying attention and if you want something harder play new game+ or do a no squid run with no magic. the story is subpar sadly they don't explore the sirens or the new genies as much as they should have but it still has the humour that the Shantae series is know for and sets up the next game in the series. overall i would recommend this game but if you don't want to pay $30 wait for a sale they happen after 3 mouths or so

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been the biggest divide i've felt of a shantae game. On one hand, it plays really well, its had several years to get the shantae gamefeel down right. However, there are severe issues with things outside gameplay. Both story and level design are extremely formulaic, to the point where you can start guessing exactly what a character will say just based on how copy/paste it is from the last character. I like the idea of shantae being taught new ways to use her dances, but dancing in this game just feels like a chore, and not her main ability. The coins you get for new mobility options is fun, but the fun stops at the newt dash (the first one). All other coins from then on are extremely situational, and not very useful. There is a coin that functions nearly identical to the sword from Pirate's curse, but whereas that game has well designed levels that implement the sword's use, this game does not accomodate the skill very well, and in fact hinders it at some points for no reason. If it is a convience item meant to make you dash fast, then make it a fun skill mini game to be able to dash from one side of the map to the other, without breaking turtle. But instead its just another mediocre ability.If you max out every item (which is incredibly easy to do), you will end up with 72 different healing items, not including the fact you get a dance that heals you for the cost of mana. This is WAY TOO MANY! I prefer to go for the no heart upgrades challenge/achivement, and even still i think i have way too much health at times. Bosses are absolutely pathetic, and also formulatic. Risky boots is reduced to a boss that shows up EVERY SINGLE TIME exactly at the same place, with the same boss fight, and the same dialogue afterwards, only changing slightly as the game goes on. I really like the boss visuals though, but i'm a weeb who likes cute girls ¯\_(ツ)_/¯The card system is really fun and enjoyable, but easily exploited for uber gains. I was able to demolish a boss in a single cycle due to having good cards and max upgrades.Did I mention the fact you get WAY TOO MANY COINS in this game? Literally the first dungeon i got out of i ended up with 600 something coins, WTF! Very quickly i realized i had upgraded everything i usually go for, and could vaporize any boss within a cycle or two.The boss fights themselves are also extremely lackluster, though they are cute, i can't for the life of me remember their names, or what they were supposed to be (they're all fish >.<) there was one boss after you unlock the tortoise that you could literally not even allow her to attack you once you figure out that you need to ground pound to get her out of the ground. Bosses in this game are pathetic, and need to be redesigned to not be overly cluster ♥♥♥♥♥, but also not be complete cakewalks (and please for the love of god not a 3 stage nightmare of a boss).I was intending to go for a 100% run, but after seeing how much of a nightmare it was from other people in the forums, i think i will pass, and instead go back to 100% Pirate's Curse.TL;DR Shantae and the Seven Sirens is a good game held back by bad design :(

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the low hour count fool you, it's from my second playthough, I played through the first time offline and it didn't record my time.Anyway, I quite enjoyed this game. I've played all of the Shantae games except the very first one, and I think this is a great addition to the series. It's much more of a Metroidvania than any of the others, even Risky's Revenge if you ask me, in that it has a large map with all sorts of things and paths to backtrack to once you have new abilities. The artwork is great, if slightly more subdued than in Half Genie Hero. The instant transformations are great for gameplay flow.As for the game being too easy, I would say that's both true and not true at the same time. It's easy to become OP pretty quickly, but if you're sort of a casual Metroidvania player like I am, there are still plenty of challenges during exploration and platforming to deal with (and the new Monster Card system can really help out with the infamous Shantae insta-death spikes if you play it right!) If I had to pick a hard negative about the game, it would be that you will notice the load screens. They can really add up on a playthrough, but they're not a deal breaker for me. If you're on the fence about this one, maybe wait for a sale. But I would also encourage you to go ahead and give it a go if for no other reason than to support the team that continues to make their own unique thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: the game is great. And so is the music.I've been a big fan of the Shantae franchise since "Risky's Revenge" (I could not get myself to play the original GBC one). To me, every single installment has been a paragon of game, graphics and sound design (at least as far as platformers go), and as much as I hate story in games, Shantae's tongue-in-cheek narrative has always managed to find that golden balance between being informative and entertaining.Luckily Shantae and the Seven Sirens is no exception to the rule. People at Wayforward somehow still manage to come up with fresh ideas and hit the nail on the head when it comes to pure fun. Everything about this game is just as good as the previous ones, including music (which, as rumours have it, was not composed by Jake Kaufman). The only thing borrowed from the prequels is the formula and certain characters; everything else is fresh stuff, and top tier at that.There are some differences, however, the main one being difficulty level - SATSS is noticably easier. I'm an average joe when it comes to platformers, yet still I haven't managed to die even once. Also, this game not as grindy as before - I wasted a full hour farming for gems in the beginning, only to find out that the game actually showers you with crystals later on. Finally, SATSS makes a return to a more traditional metroidvania formula - you don't have separate worlds connected by a hub, like in the previous two games; instead, you have an extensive singular map with different sections (much like in Risky's Revenge).If I have any gripes with this one, it's the loading times. They are similar to Doom Eternal's. And that's not necessairly a bad thing - DE did exceptionally well in this departent; still, one's a 2D platformer, and the other is the peak of 3D graphics. Also, I would love to run this game in 144 hz, though I guess 60hz in a platform game is still plenty good. Finally, I could not find any in-game stats keeping track of all the heart squids / artifacts etc. that I've collected. Not a big deal for me personally - I am by no means a completionists - but I know some people may scowl at the idea.To sum up - SATSS is every bit as good as any of its prequels. Took me just over 12 hours to complete and each of these hours was pure, honest fun. Deffo recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game in the series is a little bit more like "Pirate's Curse".The Transformations are immediate, resulting in a more fluid gameplay. There are still dances with various effects which take a few seconds though. I thought the game as a whole was more on the easy side to get though but some of the collectibles to get 100% are really tough to find.Overall I can really recommend this game for everyone who likes a little more relaxed matroidvania with a purpose fullfilling story and a little bit of fan service.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I bough this game as a fan of the franchise and I was a bit disappointed. Even if the game still does have the charming art style and the quirky writing that made me fall in love with the Shantae games, the gameplay was the big turn-off for me.1. The game was too easy. Infinite healing and easy to get upgrades makes the game feel more like a chore than a challenge. The special moves that you unlock later in the game deals a lot of damage while consuming a very small amount of magic, making the best combat option into spamming these moves.2. Level design was very bland. All rooms look very similar, even rooms in completely different areas all have similar layouts and the whole game is basically just navigating through a big maze. In Half-Genie hero, the previous Shantae game, the levels felt a lot more alive and unique due to the beautiful backgrounds and the more linear approach to their levels.3. Backtracking and fetch quests. Backtracking is very prominent in the game, this being the case for a lot of metroidvania games. The backtracking never really felt intuitive and often left me confused as to where I was supposed to go. The game also forces you multiple times during the game to go fetch mandatory collectibles that are so easy to get that they just feel like filler content made to make the game longer.Overall, pretty disappointed. Buy Half-Genie Hero instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a good addition to the Shantae franchise.  The raw game mechanics are great.  All moves have a good purpose and it gives your good reasons to use all the dances and the spells.  Movement thought the game is crisp and responsive in all the ways I want it to be.   The game controls are easily my favorite from the Shantae series.  Animation and voice acting was also really well done.  Level design is diverse and looks great.  Level design also keeps enemy placement and obstacles relevant  thought the game, but also lets you feel powered up once you get all the powers.  Overarching story is a good idea, though aside from the beginning of the game where they introduce all the characters, it's clear they they did not put much thought into it.  Extremely little discoverable lore to be found by going around and talking to NPCs.  With the exception of 3 or 4 characters, not including Shantae and Risky, most characters had no personality and were there for the single purpose of being there to complete a task.  There were some very very slight hints of personalities for some characters, which is a shame because I really liked the hints of those personalities.  They were just not brought out in this game, and that's what i think hurt it the most.  They had a great cast of characters and if they added more TLC to make those characters more fun and engaging, this game would have easily been a 10/10 for me.  Otherwise, Its a solid game for anyone looking for a casual metroidvania.  I give it a 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: Well done game!  As usual I enjoy the humor and light heartedness of this series.  Tight gameplay with a casual level of difficulty.  I noticed no bugs at all in the game. They seemed to have tested this well.  Loved the switch transforming between the various beasts and the speed at which you can do it.  The card system was interesting although some of the cards seemed way too hard to get without grinding.  The Dances were all useful too.  Fun game!I only have a couple complaints. 1) Wish the load times were shorter between sections. 2) Maybe if the font was a little more different (minor) 3) Wish you could skip the full Dance image.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: It is a step up and a step down from the other shantae games. The cards were a good chance. Having more ability to customize your gameplay is always good. The magic was pretty recycled from the other games. The map layouts felt a lot worse than the big changes in scenery we had in Pirates Curse and Half genie hero. Most of which just felt like sewers or recolored sewers. The movement was a lot better though but you were almost required to constantly dash as the maps felt so bloated. Most of your powers of movement not requiring dancing was a big plus and helped keep moving around a lot smoother.Normally I 100% the game without guides before fighting the last boss but this game had more hidden objects than usual and going through every screen to scan or sometimes multiple times on the same screen in these massive maps was mind numbing. I got 91% completion when I ended the game. I might replay it at some point but my time played for money spent wasn't great. In the future I wish all of the areas had counters for the amount of hidden squids, nuggets, etc in an area so you don't have to create tedious gameplay to 100% it or feel bad for looking something up. Inflated hours played just searching for 1-2 last pieces isn't very fun nor is having to give up to use a guide but that depends on the person.Shantae is always fun to control and the humor is great. Shes a cutie half genie but I feel like the negatives this time out ranked the positives. Still it was enjoyable overall but i'd wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: On a scale of F to S, Shantae and the Seven Sirens gets a B-It's a cheery and colorful metroidvania, and overall I enjoyed my time with it, but unfortunately the game doesn't excel at anything.  The combat toolset is snappy but it's too small to feel expressive.  The movement kit is uninspiring but adequate.  Enemy variety is good, but the encounter design gets bland.  The map is complex and satisfying to navigate, but the different areas have little aesthetic variety.  The writing and characters were fun, but there wasn't much of either to go around.If you're just coming off of Hollow Knight or Ori and you're looking for the next masterpiece of the genre, then this isn't it.  If you're looking for a cheerful, low-stress metroidvania to explore and beat over a weekend, then this'll do nicely.  Shantae and the Seven Sirens would have been a very good metroidvania six or seven years ago; today it's just good.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: When I played Shantae and the Pirate's Curse, I thought that was the direction that the series would take with the magic system, and then 1/2 Genie Hero came out and I was let down because it seemed so awkward with level based gameplay and slower transformations. This game was all I ever wanted as the sequel to Pirate's Curse, with transformations that add to your moveset instead of stopping everything to turn into an elephant for 2 seconds, then turning back just to check for a secret. The fusion dances are fun at first, but get tedious over time. I still love this game and I can't wait for the next Wayforward project!

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game! Best one since Pirate's Curse with an amazing metroidvania layout and tons of collectibles that will keep you busy. Takes the HD graphics from Half=Genie Hero and implements the gameplay of Pirate's Curse with some new ideas like the Card System which modify the game to your playstyle. It can be on the easy side with some of the card combos which can absolutely break the games combat. Plenty of throwbacks from the series such as Squid Baron making his return to tease his video game. The only real complaints is some of the cards are harder to get then other since some enemies appear very few times in the game and in one instance you need to have a card unlocked that lets you damage Pincher enemies just to get the Pincher card and secondly, late game if your going for 100% game completion back tracking through every corner to find one or two collectibles you missed can be kind of annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: THANK YOU THANK YOU THANK YOU WayForward for going back to a full on Metroidvania. Don't get me wrong; I enjoyed Half-Genie Hero as much as everyone else did, but the reason I think that game suffered was that it looked like Shantae, played like Shantae, but ultimately wasn't the traditional Shantae experience that we all came to love. Throw in the fact that WayForward added all those difficult side modes, and what we got in Half-Genie Hero was, in my opinion, an over ambitious video game that couldn't decide what it wanted to be. But, more on that with my Half-Genie Hero review.All that being said, I feel like this game has the opposite issue. Yes, this game is easy, (but the fact that Shantae games have always been easy has never been an issue for me), but I have never played a Metroidvania to this point that's constantly handing you healing items, or giving you a lot of money at one time. There have been harder modes added to the game via the update it received, thankfully, to balance things out. Course you can always play the game as it originally was released. The fact that the transformations has been streamlined is nice though, and the story is full of the flavorful writing that comes with all Shantae games. Add in the fact that Christina Vee nails her performances of both Shantae and Risky Boots, as this is easily by far the best performance of voice acting by far. The dungeons are also the best part of this game, hands down. However, the main issue that really makes me have mixed feelings about this game is the world itself. Simply put, it's too big. There's several areas to explore, and the different areas are color coded on the map. Thing is, most of the time, when not doing plot related quests, you're either going to be rewarded for your exploration with the returning heart squids from Pirate's Curse, or Nuggets, which you can use to get rare collectible cards. This wouldn't be an issue except that, 1) the map gives no indication that an item is in the room you're at, and 2) I don't care for the card system. I don't really use the cards except for a couple of the Siren cards you can get via the nuggets.To add further insult to injury, the game will sometimes mark your map as to where plot related items are located. WayForward did a better job with the map system in Pirate's Curse. What I find myself doing every time I get a new transformation or new dance is just backtracking through the entire world in hopes I'll be able to find SOMETHING... Trying to achieve 100% is simply tedious. It IS possible, but unless you're using a fan generated completion map or something, don't expect to 100% on your first play through. Thankfully this has been fixed in the updated version.Then there's the issue of the dungeons. The actual process of going through the dungeons is still functionally the same since Pirate's Curse, with the major difference being the fusion coins you get which allow you to transform instead of just getting a piece of Pirate Equipment in a chest. That's not my issue. My issue is that in the room before you find said fusion coins, you have to fight Risky Boots as a mini-boss. EVERY. SINGLE. TIME. Why did Risky get demoted to mini-boss goon? I mean, yes her fights get harder with each dungeon, but still.... Risky's the main antagonist of this franchise. She should AT LEAST have a more threatening role in this game than just mini-boss goon of the game. What makes it even more annoying is that the fights play out exactly the same as her fight in Half Genie Hero, which is lazy in my opinion. She's not even part of the final boss, which is rather unusual, (if we ignore the fact that she wasn't tied to Pirate's Curse final boss either for a second).Then there's the sirens themselves. Simply put, they're no where near as menacing as any of the bosses Shantae faced off against in previous games, which is honestly a shame. I mean, sure the final boss is hard, and can take you a while to figure out how to beat the final form, but it's the final boss; IT SHOULD be the hardest fight in the game. Even then, the final boss just drags on too long for my liking. As far as the soundtrack is concerned, I'm willing to go a bit easier on it. Yes, it doesn't hold a candle it Jake Kaufman's work. However, I feel like this soundtrack does a decent job of immersing the player into the game's massive world. It does it's job. My favorite's being the different dungeon themes, the boss theme, and Arena Town.This game was also notorious for having long loading times as well as stuttering issues, but this has been fixed in the update as well. The problem is that WayForward shouldn’t of had to release that update to begin with. They should’ve delayed the development process to make sure what we got at launch was of the same quality that came with previous Shantae games. The fact that they did the update way too late and reuse assets and bosses just goes to show how lazy they have been with this series as of late. Plus they dropped so much lore in Pirates Curse, but then never explored it further. I would love a prequel to the original Shantae where you play as Risky Boots back when she was working for the Pirate Master and how the war between the Pirates and Genies began and progressed.Overall, this is still an enjoyable game, just not worth going for everything. It's easily better than the original Shantae, and Risky's Revenge to some extent, but in my opinion, Pirate's Curse is still Queen.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: this game feels like the real sequel to risky's revenge and pirate's curse.when 1/2 genie hero was released its return to the clunky dance system that pirate's curse had seemingly done away with on top of incredibly linear, short levels and an overall far less "metroidvania"-ish gameplay style felt oddly out of place to me.but seven sirens, with the addition of "fusion magic" keeping the shantae series staple of transformations while making ability usage tied to an instant input (like the abilities in pirate's curse) AND still keeping the dance mechanic (another series staple) for the more "big use" abilities is just such a perfect solution that I can't not compliment it.this on top of the return to a COMPLETELY interconnected world map, which we haven't even seen since risky's revenge, the game adopting a very much more cohesive world map design, and dungeons making a return as well, all put together a very fun return to shantae's more traditional metroid-ish game design.I can't recommend this enough, especially for those who preferred the older shantae games, but even for those who prefer 1/2 genie hero there's a lot to love here too.

My little problem with those sprite is that, Rottytop have red eyes on both portrait and sprite, while Shantae and Sky have black on sprite, and blue and purple on portrait, why???!!! Sorry to be so nitpicky but I gotta say it somewhere you know!RiskyBoots have yellow eyeballs on sprite, and white eyeball on portrait, why too?!!! The animations are super smooth(except the english lip sync in cutscene doesn't seem perfect yet) and great but the personality of characters could have been more fleshed out, but that's where we see the "pokemon G1"'s influence on this game that Matt Bozon mentionned. I wish they could add directional aiming for the hair whip, I believe the ponytail isn't what take the most of time to draw but I could be wrong, hollow knight had a nice nail he could swing up down and side, I wish Shantae could do the same, if I was very demanding I would even wish a 3 hit combo that could slow down the fall in middle of the air, a bit like byleth in super smash bros ultimate with his whip sword. _childDocuments_.review: As others have said, Seven Sirens is a great combination of the Metroidvania exploration of previous installments with the visual style of Half-Genie Hero. Pretty much a solid delivery of all things Shantae, which has always been a pretty good in my book. Kinda like how I've never really picked up a Kirby game I didn't like, Shantae remains consistently enjoyable and Seven Siren keeps that trend going.It does feel a bit easier than HGH and Pirate's Curse (despite lacking HGH's one notable game breaker), but then again Shantae has never been a particularly difficult series. Though since HGH did have a harder difficulty mode available, it is odd that said mode is absent this time around. One notable area of change is the meaner style platforming designs from the last installment seems to be dialed back a bit. Since that can be more annoying than challenging, I don't mind. With so many other games these days being vexing and frustrating for one reason or another, it's nice to find something that's just plain fun with no pretentiousness about it.If you like light-hearted platforming adventure, this is a good pick.

_childDocuments_.review: After Half-Genie Hero, it was clear that the game felt way more at home in the classic metroidvania format. It's not only fun, but it doubles down on the collection elements that make a game like this rewarding to complete and fun to come back to.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've enjoyed other Shantae games in the past then you'll also enjoy this solid new addition to the series. While some of the harder platforming from 1/2 Genie hero is gone, the same energy and spirit of the franchise shines as bright as ever, and they've changed the transformation system to no longer be tied to dances which makes movement much more fluid in general. I also enjoyed how they've gone back to one large interconnected map as opposed to individual levels which felt more disjointed in the past. If you're looking for a challenge, this isn't the game for you (at least not on your first playthrough) I'd recommend Hollow Knight instead. But if you're just looking for a solid 8-10 hours of fun then I'd give our cute purple dancing half genie a try.

_childDocuments_.review: The Shantae series has been a favorite of mine for a long while. I have played and beaten all the previous titles before this one. Even 100% Pirates Curse and Half Genie Hero. This game feels like it calls back to all the best parts in the series while still having its own standing. Shantae 1's fullly explorable map, Risky's revenges Barons, Pirate's Curses's Heart Squids and Squidsmith, and Half Genie Hero's  art style. All wrapped up in good writing, with great characters, and new and unique transformations. The challenge is fair without being too unfair, with one exception, Without spoilers there is a room in a dungeon that is long and required, its full of poisonous water that drains your health like mad, maybe I got through it the wrong way, but it was not fun going through it.Something new to the series is animated cutscenes, they're great and well timed. But with my version I had animation errors, the 3rd to last and 2nd to last cutscenes glitched out, where the video would go gray and static for a few seconds, missing out on animations. Then again this is only version 1.0 before any patches have been applied yet.  The game is fantastic and I highly recommend this in these times of tragedy.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love the visual style of this series, wayforward knocks it out of the park with their presentation. However I have to say once again, the game just falls slightly short as far as actual game design.  While I'm personally very happy they went back to an search/explore style opposed to levels system like they had in half genie hero. There are unfortunately a few certain major aspects of the game cause it to suffer. My three main criticisms are:1. Too easy. the game literally hands you healing items like they were going out of style. I think between all the food and potions I could stock up to about 80 healing items and probably heal myself back to full health 45 times over. No boss in the game really was hard enough that I needed to use more than 1 to 2 healing items, bringing me to my 2nd point2. The bosses are just too easy. Normal enemies are actually pretty well designed and the exploration of the stages feel great, but the boss fights are pretty disappointing. They have some interesting idea, but overall they felt too easy and were not much of a challenge. I made it a point to try and not use any healing items to challenge myself a lil bit but even then, the only one I really ended up using more than a single healing item on was the final boss. 3. The load times between the zones are fairly long and cause my entire system to hiccup. I have a pretty high end system and while a 8 -10 second load time isn't that bad, it quickly becomes and annoyance when you quickly go between zones every 30 seconds especially while trying to find collectables and power ups. I still think over all the quality of the game is still pretty high and I still love the Shantae series, although maybe get it on sale, it's a tad short, 9 hours for me to 100% and I spent about an hour searching for that last 1%.I don't think there's much chance of them fixing the boss designs but if they could adjust the difficulties by limiting the number of healing items you can carry, or just separate difficulty levels, and hopefully fixing the load times, it would have been a much more enjoyable experience for me. I think the series top game was pirates curse personally, but there is still a chance this can still be updated and be a solid contender for silver medal
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of the series for quite some time, not since the beginning, but ever since the second game was only a couple years old and the first one was about to be rereleased for the first time, I played them both around the same time and I've loved the series ever since, Shantae and the Pirate's Curse came out in 2014 and it has since become one of my favorite games of all time, naturally after loving the first 2 games and with how good Pirate's Curse was I was extremely excited for the next game in the series, Half-Genie Hero......Half-Genie Hero came out in late 2016 and was a disappointment. Don't get me wrong, it's a very good game in its own right, hell I bought it twice as well and played through it multiple times as well as all the DLC, but it stripped away so much of what made those first 3 games so good, Pirate's Curse did away with the singular connected map, but it was still at its core a Metroidvania, HGH took it a step further and turned it into a linear platformer, all Metroidvania elements were gone and so were the dungeons that had been there since the first game. I enjoyed HGH in spite of the formula changes, not because of them, and I was concerned this was going to be the formula going forward, it was still a good game but it let me down to see the series that got me into Metroidvanias drop the Metroidvania formula entirely. Thankfully that wasn't the case, this is much more in line with the first 3 games, we're back to a singular connected map like the first 2, and the dungeons that were there in the first 3 games are back, this feels like the sequel to Pirate's Curse I've been wanting for years now and what I was expecting to get with Half-Genie Hero, and it's amazing. Oddly enough though, the music was the one thing I was sure I wouldn't be disappointed by, and it was the one thing I was a little disappointed by, what's here is good don't get me wrong but it's a very different direction than the previous games, it grew on me as I played more of it but in comparison to Half-Genie Hero's soundtrack and especially Pirate's Curse's soundtrack it's a bit of a downgrade if you ask me, everything else is great though, really no complaints that I can think of. If you've never played a Shantae game before this isn't a bad one to start with, though I would recommend starting with Risky's Revenge and playing the rest of the series from there if you like it, as for fans of the series this is definitely not one you want to miss out on, would highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Shantae is a long-running game series, the first releasing in 2002. Transform into creatures, Whip with your hair, and dance through the danger to save the day. _childDocuments_.review: I have amassed a large library on Steam. I will constantly buy games on sale, thinking that one day I will play them. Sadly, many games end up in a graveyard never to be touched. Sometimes, I buy games at full price and they too end up in the back log graveyard. The Shantae series is different for me. I started with Risky's Revenge when it first came out. I bought it, installed it, and beat it within a day or two. I have done that with Pirate's Curse, Half Genie Hero and now Seven Sirens. I have fun with it, and I like that they change the mechanics every game that still remains familiar yet new. The Shantae series is not a difficult metroidvania, which is fine, I don't always want to play a hard game. It is a fun series that has a mild story and will entertain you. This one brings a new monster card mechanic system, it lets you tweak things and improve your abilities slightly which is fun. There's a couple new magic spells, and they changed the dances to puzzle skills, and your animal transformations are more streamlined. In addition, while they don't have full voice acting, there is more than there was for Half Genie Hero. I also liked that they added anime styled cutscenes (Shantae could seriously be turned into an Anime by now).  Wayforward does a great job with pacing in the Shantae games, at no point do you feel like you're being rushed, you don't need to grind, and there's no tedious parts. They added a warp room system, so you won't be doing a lot of heavy back tracking. It's a good addition to the series, and I hope they keep up on delivering quality like this every time.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a solid B+ game in a my book.  It was nice to return to a more Metroidvania style version of Shantae granted I had no issues with what Half-Genie Hero did. Most of how this game plays off of what Half-Genie Hero introduced in its new style. Platforming feels solid as ever.  The changes with how the new transformation work really streamlined movement. Combat is still smooth and feels good granted the hit boxes of some enemies feel a bit too generous.  The utility items magic don't vary much as well and most of the time you will just stick with just using scimitar or bubble shield the main choices.  All of combat aspects can be upgraded but I feel the game is way too generous with healing items and  the currency.  You are able to upgrade a lot of abilities even after the first boss which ends up trivializing the game fairly quickly.  I know this isn't meant to be a super hard game but sometimes it just feels like your hand is getting held constantly.The card collecting system is a great addition, being able to have some extra bonus passives to customize your play style was a nice touch.Story-wise, the game falls inline with what the Shantae series has always delivered, simple, nothing too complicated but still enjoyable with great banter between all the characters. Small gripe I had was just the lack of backstory in general of the sirens,  The player basically knows nothing of them until after defeating the first boss and you come to find out, oh there  be sirens here in this town.  My biggest complaint is the music,  the composers for this game cannot even hold a candle to what Jake Kaufman did in Half-Genie Hero.  There are a few decent tunes but so much of this soundtrack is mixed chip tunes which in comparison to the past is a huge downgrade for this game.  Very little of the music in this game sticks in my mind whereas I could basically recall almost every tune in Half-Genie Hero.  This was the largest impact of the game for me and why it really affected my review, music especially for this series has always been a high point till now.Again the game is a solid B+, doesn't innovate too much but the few additions work well however some story points and the extremely lackluster music just hurts the game enough to where I cannot give it an A.  Well hopefully if WayForward makes another in the near future.  They can give it the TLC it truly deserves.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game for the first time. While there was no challenge in terms of difficulty, I had lots of fun while playing. For me it was well worth the money, and overall I consider Seven Sirens to be a step forward after 1/2 Genie Hero.Despite the game being really easy, it had everything I expect out of a Shantae game:- A nice and colorful world to explore- entertaining dialogue- a simple story that takes itself just seriously enough to keep me hooked and curious about what will happen next.Loading times between zones take a bit longer than I expected. However I eventually got used to it.The soundtrack is nice to listen to. Nothing special, but it's there, and i liked the "gameboy"-like touches it sometimes has.People looking for a challenge should be aware, that this game is really far from being even remotely difficult.It took me around 18 hours to beat, and I consider myself a slower player.I can easily recommend this to people who don't mind super low difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good (and easy) metroidvania, it took me about ~6 hours to finish the first playthrough, with ~70% completion rate.This game took something from every other Shantae game and put it in this game and added a little more, so if you found any of the other Shantae games fun and you like the metroidvania style, you will like this. Its a good continuation to the series, but if you are new, I would recommend Shantae Risky Revenge over this one, but if you already played it, this might be the next best entry in the series.Now you have 3 passive slots to choose what abilities improve. You can get those passive abilities by killing enemies, and they will drop a card, so if you are a completionist you will find yourself finding every enemy of the game and trying to get their cards.The metroidvania formula is back! An interconnected world with hidden items to find, upgrades to find/buy, and a light hearthed humor.The gameplay is as good as any other Shantae, responsive controls to the point you will never feel cheated, or that you took a hit that you shouldn't.This game is really easy, probably the easiest so far, so if you want a relaxed game, this game is perfect for that.Personally, I don't really like how this game uses the transformations. You no longer dance to transform, now you do it instantly and it only last until you no longer needed. For example, you transform automatically in water, and you get back to normal once you get out of the water. But I can see why they did this and its only a minor complain (and probably most people will like this change).The only bad thing I can say about this game are the loading screens between zones and towns, it can take up to 20 seconds to load a new zone, and while this doesn't sound too bad, it gets tiresome once you start to backtrack searching for all the hidden stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: I know I don't have a lot of hours on the pc version yet as I only beat the first dungeon on this version. the game is amazing and I am loving it so far however there seems to be a stuttering glitch during the loading screens for the pc version. it stutters for around 5 seconds and fps drops a lot then it goes back to normal and loads in about 10 seconds. gameplay is super smooth and fun everywhere else.the Switch version does not have this issue during the loading screens and it takes around 10 seconds instead wasting 15 to 20 seconds the pc version has cause of the stuttering glitch. for this reason if you own a Switch I recommend you buy that version instead until this issue is fixed. to be clear I love all the Shantae games and this game itself is wonderful and amazing, I bought it for the pc and Switch cause I love the hard work and effort WayForward puts into the Shantae games. this is just a minor issue they will hopefully iron out soon. I still recommend this game or any other Shantae games to anyone looking for a game with amazing story and solid content. keep up the awesome work WayForward and thanks for releasing this wonderful new game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a new shantae game. If you enjoyed the others, you'll enjoy this. the cons/critiques list being longer than the pros is because I want to give feedback, not because they overshadow the fun of the game.Pros:an actual interconnected world map (+submap dungeons), not the islands or levels of the previous two gamesnew transformations aren't just monkey/elephant/bird/etc. how you use them is much better than previous gamesMonster card system is neatMovement's really funall but one enemy type (the big crabs that block) is fun to fight, and all but one boss (the second one) is fun to fightcons/critiques:map doesn't show stuff you've seen but not collected or other points of interest, making 100% really tedious without a guideknowing where to use Scan is similarly annoying, there's almost never an indication for hidden stuff (unless that's a card I didn't get)this game is a resource hog, every time you move to a different area it chugs the whole computer for 5-10 seconds (ex. youtube on other monitor freezes)Pike Ball/Scimitar are still busted, though bosses seem to have more health to compensateStory/progression is very formulaic for most of the gameI don't know what monsters drop new cards, or what cards are worth collecting, until after I've got one of them, also got the store discount after I bought all the upgrades

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to remake my review now that I've gotten to play the revised main mode difficulty. But TLDR game is still one of my all time fav platformers and I couldn't recommend it moreFor those who are unfamiliar with the case originally the game was much too easy due to the extreme overabundance of healing you were offered and enemies not posing that much of a threat to begin with. With the new revamp the healing is drastically decreased and some bosses are noticeably more difficult, while I feel it didn't quite do enough and the game is still too easy that may be because I've now beaten it like 4-5 times so take it for what you will. If you'd prefer to play the game in the old mode it's still available as Legacy Mode, alongside other more for fun modesNow then, moving onto the good stuff.  If you've looked through the other reviews you've probably seen a lot of split opinions on the new mechanics, how the game plays, and so on, and I think that's one of the wonderful things about the shantae series as a whole. Each game gives the player a ton of cool new stuff to do and they're all done in quite different ways, no two shantae games are the same. Sometimes they're amazing, sometimes they're janky, but I'm always glad that the devs are ambitious and have fun with the gameAs for the rest I feel there's nothing more I could add that's not already obvious. Music, art? Outstanding! Story? Pretty enjoyable quirky adventure with a couple neat highlights. Waifus? If you're here for those why do you even need me to sell you on SEVEN SIRENS
_childDocuments_.name: Shantae and the Seven Sirens

_childDocuments_.review: A great entry in the Shantae series. Seven Sirens takes the series back to its Metroidvania roots and does a good job at it but it has it's flaws. The exploring is fun and it feels good to find things as all good Metroidvanias should aim for. However the problem I have comes from the invisible collectables. Oh boy, there are 20 invisible statues you have to find and god only knows how many golden nuggets which for the most part aren't invisible but some unfortunately are. Also the monster cards (Which give passives ala Aria of Sorrow/Bloodstained) are a cool edition but the drop rates on some tankier monsters are insanely low especially since that RNG fest counts towards 100% and yes the 100% speedrun challenge is still in the game AND YES the invisible items DO count AS WELL AS the monster cards. As somebody who loves to complete games he enjoys this is going to stop me from even doing a 100% casual run since I really don't have the patience to grind this out. Maybe I'll come back later down the road when I can have guides up on another monitor but as of now none exist. With all that being said this game is good and if your looking for a casual playthrough of a Metroidvania game give this game a go! Movement is fluid, music is good, and like I said obtaining upgrades is satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review:
New locations, abilities, and friends await in Shantae's biggest adventure yet!

Shantae and the Seven Sirens sends the belly-dancing, hair-whipping, half-genie hero to a tropical island where Shantae and her friends encounter other Half-Genie allies, but they soon learn there's trouble in paradise. As Shantae gets caught up in the island's sinister secrets, she'll use all-new dance abilities and instant-transformation Fusion Magic to explore the nonlinear, interconnected world where she'll visit multiple towns, overcome treacherous labyrinths, and battle dastardly bosses. name: Say No! More
detailed_description: A brand new experience from Studio Fizbin! In a world where everyone sticks to the status quo of saying “YES!”, create your custom character and take on the role of an intern on a mission to change the world with the positive power of saying “NO!“. With this new power, nothing will get in your way as you shout “NO!” at any absurd requests fired your way. Say No! More is the world’s first NPG (NO!-Playing Game). Using simple controls designed for anyone to pick up and play, start your working life through a set path in a quirky office environment. As well as shouting 'NO!' in your chosen language, use your 'NO!' in different emotional states to send them reeling. Confuse people with different actions to let their guard down, then charge up your 'NO!' for an even greater effect on unsuspecting colleagues! Touching on timeless and modern issues such as social etiquette, friendship, and workplace standards, this hilarious adventure also has tender depth. It’s all wrapped up in a fun late 90s video game style, complete with chunky, colorful visuals, comical animations, and jazzy music that you’ll struggle to say “NO!” to. Choose how to say 'NO!' : Heated No! Cold No! Lazy No! Wacky No! Charge your 'NO!' for bigger effect! Irritate your colleagues! Laugh at them! Clap at them! Hmmm at them! Make them feel you listen to them, but sarcastically! Say 'NO!' in many different languages! Customize your character! Fight mean colleagues , supervisors and bosses! Make friends in your lunch break! Laugh out loud because this game is very funny! Listen to rad mixtape music And learn to say 'NO!' from the pros (like this guy👇)

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where you think at first "oh, it's just one joke without much to say."To that, I say this:  Shut up and buy this game.1. _childDocuments_.review: 8.8h (100% achievement, finished the game) Yes (~2 achievements that require you to idle ~6.7h). Yes (14 achievements). No. is a short, joke game that tells the ironic truth of the workplace world: how it's hard to say no and how you need to learn to say that sacred word. It's a story-focused game with minimalistic gameplay where you just need to spam a button to progress.- Nice moral message- Chapter select- Relatable jokes- Unable to skip or fast-forward dialogues for the second playthroughIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 uses a combination of pixelated visuals and simplistic 3D models. The models are less blocky than voxels, although the textures, particularly on facial expressions and clothing, are using pixelated art. However, it looks blurry and sometimes it's hard to see the expression behind the face, especially when characters are opening their eyes; you hardly can differentiate when they are shocked or angry.The story looks relatable if you have entered the workplace. You are an intern in a company and you need to do whatever your supervisor says. It also tries to exaggerate it by giving a bunch of nonsense orders, giving you more excuses to say no (but you can't). The story might seem foolish at first due to all of the exaggeration, but it ended up giving a nice moral message. I didn't like how it suddenly got sentimental at the end though, but I still liked the ending.The gameplay is divided into two parts. You'll have to watch the story in the first part and say no to everyone in the second part. The story part is straightforward; you just need to wait for the dialogue to unfold and watch it like a movie. I don't like how you can't fast-forward the dialogues, though. It can take a while to get to the scene that you wanted that way if you replay the game for the missable achievements.The majority of the fun comes from the second part. People will come to you (because you're an intern who has free time and all) and ask you to do a lot of nonsensical stuff. You are given the option to say no by pressing the Space button or wait until the timer runs out (if there's any) to accept their request. Most requests are just selfish, others are not. The ones who are not are usually given a different color to differentiate and this will lead to a different, short scene if you accept their request.What's fun about the saying no part is how exaggerated it was. A simple no can just make them fall to the ground while charging it will blast people to the wall. There are also different variations that you can do, from laughing to even nodding before saying no to give more impact. I find the variation to be useless, but at least it makes the gameplay not too repetitive.I found the switch between the story and the saying no portion to be perfect. I never got bored playing it since the story is ridiculous and funny, and it's just fun mashing the button to say no. Moreover, the game doesn't overstay its welcome either. There is only so much that you can do to prolong this, and the dev knows that. The game ends right just at the perfect time, giving a nice moral message before it closes its absurdness.I finished the game in 2.1h. I then left the game open to idle for 2 achievements, which took me ~6.7h to get. The game isn't hard at all since you just need to mash the Space button to say no, and although there are some missable achievements, the game has a chapter selection for you to go back to.I know there are a lot of books that tell you how to say no, but I'm quite surprised that the game manage to convey such a message in a ridiculous way. It's not about saying "say no more" (aka yes I understand), but about getting used to saying no to people. It's relatable, and the way the game exaggerates it provides nice entertainment to me. I can recommend it if you relate to these experiences about being a yes man, but due to its short length, make sure to buy it on a sale.

More really pushes the message that you DON’T need to say yes to everything in the job environment to move up. You DON’T need to give up parts of yourself or be stepped on to make it.
