_childDocuments_.review: Would recommend with the asterisk of wait for a sale first. I scored this for £2 and would've paid about £4-5 at most, but not the full £13.49/$15 price.Very cute game with a silly and fun story about standing up for yourself and worker's rights (with an ending that's sweet but maybe a little too idealistic, as the game itself acknowledges). Cute way to spend an hour or two, it's essentially a visual novel with a unique artstyle, banger soundtrack and a fun gimmick mechanic tying everything together. Only real gripe I have is that the extra mechanics that feel like they're going to add depth don't really have any purpose than comedy. The only time you're required to use specific types of no's are the tutorials they get introduced in. Might have been fun to have the type and length matter a little more mechanically to make it more meaningful. Still a fun time overall, glad I picked it up!
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: As an intern who has grown tired of the soul-sucking nature of the office environment, you're armed with a powerful tool - the word "NO!" This simple yet liberating word becomes your weapon to navigate through office politics, annoying colleagues, and mind-numbing tasks. It's a quick and light-hearted experience that guarantees one or two laughter-filled gaming sessions. Smashing a single button, you repeatedly say "NO!" to progress through absurd and humorous situations. The developers tried to spice it up, adding a few possible styles of saying NO!, and few other reactions (laughing, clapping hands and some more), but these elements were poorly developed, and have no real impact on the game-play. You don't control movements. Instead, you'll navigate through a scripted experience , just like in old arcade games.  Any replay value,? NO! Now, I know what you're thinking: "Is smashing a button even a game?" There is only one legit answer: NO! It's more a silly animated graphic novel than a game.If you're in the mood for some easy laughs, this is definitely worth checking out. But if you are looking for a real game, well follow the game's mantra and say NO! more.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game, sadly.I'll admit that I bought the game after seeing the prologue chapter being played. I loved the humor of it, and even though I knew there was very little 'gameplay', I thought the jokes would carry the game. Then I played the prologue myself, and was enjoying it as much as when I saw it in the video. Immediately after, however, it switches to this corporate setting and from there on the jokes did not really land anymore. There was an occasional funny moment, but every chapter is a repetition of the one before that. Had they not done this 'tongue-in-cheek' concept of 'don't let people boss you around', but instead gone with the artsy fairytale aesthetic, I am fairly certain I would have enjoyed this so much, but now I just ended up waiting until every chapter was over. Add an immense grind of an achievement on top of that, and the game is just kinda ruined for me.This game is one of those 'Catchy title first, gameplay second' kind of games. You know they were in their office like 'Haha, "say no more" is a funny saying we can twist!' but then forgot to make an actual game. Well, they obviously tried with the beginning, but then just prayed this one funny concept of 'press a button to say no' would carry the entire game, and that is only possible if the story around the game is actually good or funny and that's just not the case here with multiple of the same jokes such as doing nothing for a 'staring contest'.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely get this game for a sale price (Especially currently, as of this review!)It's got a lovely art style, absurd humor and a warm message. I can describe the sense of humor as Jazzpunk mixed with Japanese comedy. It's underlying message of workplace hierarchy, abuse cycles and self-confidence was a welcome surprise, too! You can tell the voice actors were having a lot of fun recording this, which shows with every bit of dialogue, and the ability to even say 'no' in multiple different languages was a nice bonus. The length of the game with regards to the full price, like other reviews pointed out, I'm divisive about. If the experience is good, then the length doesn't matter too much. Though the gameplay itself does lack the depth I'd expect from that price. It's fun! But it doesn't have much replayability, nor do any of the taunts go much deeper besides regaining energy. There's no strengths/weaknesses, there's no real reason to use different types of 'no', as far as I could tell.If the gameplay had these depths, or the game itself had some sort of silly 'endless mode' or something that might give a reward for replays, the full price would be more justified. All in all, a great time if you get this game for a good price!
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: Now, before I get to the review, and possibly my first (of memory anyway), let me get my one negative I can think of out of the way. Despite all that I love about this game, I don't necessarily think that Say No! More is worth the $15 price tag. Maybe $7-9 dollars? Not too sure, there isn't much else that it provides that changes up the gameplay, and the short playtime provides too little variety to shake things up aside from visuals. Either way, I'd recommend you only get this on sale, unless you'd like to support the developers in full, which I highly recommend any way you can. Conflicting statement, I know, but beside that.Now, to get to the good part, if you're still reading. Do I think the game is perfect? NO....But I love it. The visuals are absolutely charming, the voice acting reeks of a bunch of people from different places, full of love for the creation they made, and the story is such a lovely ride that it made the friends who watched me play it tear up. Especially with its wackiness with the Staring Contest Club, the Robot overtaking, and even the heartwarming ending wrapping the story up in a nice little bow. For a 2 hour romp, its not much, but for such colorful visuals and an entertaining time all around, this game can't help but put a smile on my face. Sure, it doesn't have much in terms of branching off, but I do hope that someday, we get a follow up or something from this title again. But at the same time, maybe one time is all it needs to make a mark on my heart that I can't help but cherish with every beat it takes. I know that the game is a bit too short for such a cost it asks from you, but if you're looking for a fun game to try out, and you ain't too badly off yourself, I'd recommend giving the game a try. Do I think you'll regret it?NO.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: Thanks to this game I've learned to say No! to my boss at work.  No Susan, you don't need that task done by 2 PM.  The client is on vacation and won't be back till next week, anyway!Jokes aside, it is a fun game that doesn't take long to finish in one run.  In fact, I recommend playing in short bursts (ex. one level per session).  Of course play whatever way you want, but doing one level at a time seems better to absorb all the jokes the game has.  Graphics are simple so it won't be punishing to your pc if it's not the strongest.  To prove my point, I decided to play on an outdated Macbook Air, and had no issues running it [beyond a loud fan].If you are adjusting to a 9-5 shift in an office environment, I would check this game out.  It will not cure the dread of going to work, but maybe you can find the lighter aspects of working in a cubicle (or utility closet).

_childDocuments_.review: The game actually was pretty fun. Good story and good visual art style that I liked, but two achievements for this game wasn't fun at all.I try to 100% games that I find great and fun. That's why I thought I'd 100% this game. Level specific achievements were a good choice. It gives you another opportunity to see what you missed by just saying no. I finished the game around 2h and I did the level specific achievements, but two achievements added 6 extra hours. I get the point of this game is to say no, but I think it was a bad choice to add achievements that have you say no 9,999 and 99,999. I think saying no 999 is good enough, but it could've been a bit less and saying no to 99,999 times was a bad choice. . in my first run I was close to 999 no's said. Your basically asking to use a auto clicker to press space bar 99,999 times or play the story hundredths of time to get two achievements. I'd still recommend this game for anyone. It's fun and has a fun concept, but achievement grind is so hard.I'd give it a 8/10 for a fun story and a 6/10 for level achievements being fun, but it brings it down to being a 6/10 because of that grind to say no 99,999 times.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an incredibly simple concept, yet the comedy is enough to keep you going. It's wholesome, heartfelt, it's insanely basic and, if you check my play time you'll see, it's incredibly short on a whole, but it's a great game everyone should play at least once.Plus, you can say NO! in basically every language and gender, ontop of the customisation the game has (which isn't a lot but you'll find, even if they don't mimic you, you'll enjoy how they look regardless). Honestly, if you don't expect a 40 hour epic, you'll have a good chuckle here and maybe learn the importance of knowing when to say yes and when to put your foot down and scream, buttocks clenched, NO!!
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: Say No! More is a great game that I bought off a whim. I enjoyed the overall theme of the game that emphasizes the power of learning to say "No".It is fairly short with me being able to speed through the game in just under 2 hours but I will say that those 2 hours resounded with me. $15 may be a big chunk of change for a game of this length but looking back at the purchase I can not say that I was disappointed. I recommend this game as a gift or as a purchase (maybe even a steam sale purchase if you're still on the fence) 8.2/10

_childDocuments_.review: A great game with a great message, something a lot of us struggle with. Nobody wants to be a jerk, but nobody wants to get taken advantage of either, or to be forced to do things we don't want. It's at that point that saying No to things becomes important, and in terms of the message the game gets it across beautifully.There isn't much in terms of a 'game' in the traditional sense however, though if a game is meant to entertain then this will definitely entertain you for a couple of hours with its wackiness and zany happenings. How many games can you just revive by just straight up saying 'NO' to Death (who is apparently the pun loving crocodile you met a few chapters back)? Yeah, it gets that goofy. Bonus points for saying it in Irish Gaelic.I do wish, though, that there was more to the different 'NO's you can say. Perhaps a fail state, even, but the game sadly says 'NO' to fail states too, so you can just press spacebar and blast through the game. What about all the times where you should (optionally) say yes? Maybe there are times when you shouldn't just press space bar blindly at the people in front of you, you have to listen to what they have to say. What about having different enemies affected differently by different NOs? What about the Lazy No charging all the other NOs when used, but isn't that effective? What about making it a proper 'game' in the traditional sense, is all I'm saying.All in all, it's fun, but I do wish there was more to it. Recommended for the wacky zaniness, and here's hoping that their next game is as goofy as this one...but with more of a game aspect to it than just spamming a button to advance.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed. It's cute and fun but short and basically one long cutscense with some button presses. No real fail-state, no reason to replay unless you are going for 100%. _childDocuments_.review: "Say No More" is an absolute delight, delivering a fresh and hilarious take on the world of office culture. From the moment you pick up the game, you're greeted with vibrant visuals and an infectious energy that keeps you hooked from start to finish. The game's central mechanic of saying "no" with gusto adds a unique twist to the gameplay, encouraging players to embrace their inner assertiveness and reject absurd requests with flair.One of the standout features of "Say No More" is its impeccable humor. The writing is sharp and witty, delivering laugh-out-loud moments at every turn. The absurd scenarios you encounter in the office are both relatable and surreal, making for an entertaining experience that never fails to put a smile on your face.In addition to its humor, "Say No More" also boasts intuitive controls and smooth gameplay mechanics. Whether you're delivering epic rejections or navigating through office obstacles, the game feels responsive and polished throughout.Overall, "Say No More" is a gem of a game that offers a unique and memorable experience. With its humor, charm, and engaging gameplay, it's sure to leave players grinning from ear to ear.

_childDocuments_.review: This action-walking simulator has some really funny dialogue and narrative moments in it, as you brazenly saunter through an office environment yelling/derping/yelping random "no"s at demanding coworkers who come up to ask for favors or demands. It's satisfying (especially considering the short experience), but gets boring quickly, and the only reason you hang around is because of the mayhem of being the Dovahkiin of negativity. In order to make the gameplay seem more interesting (or more likely, a narrative-branching device that got scrapped), they added in adjustable moods that don't really add anything to the design. Either "lazy," or "angry," they hit your shaky-headed opponents the same, which makes me wonder why they didn't just randomize them in order to provide variety to the "No" deliveries without making me actively choose one until I get tired of the voice. Either way, the gameplay shouldn't be why you're playing it; it's really a timed, spacebar push game, and one I don't think you can lose. There is a fun narrative experience here though, and feeling like YOU'RE the one saying "NO" adds an impact that I feel would be lost watching it on YouTube. Good voice acting, overall build quality, and there's some fun little surprises sprinkled throughout. Worth the price of a movie for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the $15 price tag seems a bit high at first glance considering that the game can be played in less than 2 hours, but after playing through this game, all I can say to that is "NO!"The graphics are clean, the characters are funny, and the story is great. Yeah, the game is a bit short, and yeah the game mechanics are reeeeally easy (like it's actually impossible to lose in this game), but that's alright! This game is truly something special, and I would highly recommend it for anyone simply looking for a fun gaming experience with a creative story.

_childDocuments_.review: A stylish, fun, CATHARTIC game! It touches on some deep themes, like the mental and emotional damage caused by a lack of boundaries, but doesn't overstay or beat the themes to death. The game wants to be fun and provoke those thoughts, rather than lecture. It does get a little didactic at times, and those moments do stick out, but it doesn't kill the vibe. The overall aesthetic is lovely, very katamari-esque! I also enjoy the sheer quantity of languages you can say "NO" in.Lastly, it's a very quick playthrough......unless you decide to get all the achievements. _childDocuments_.review: Since I am new to gaming I haven’t experienced a lot of the games that others have. Due to this I have friends who would always recommend things for me to play and I would ultimately say sure, I’ll add it to the list. Until my list eventually began to become rather overwhelming. By overwhelming I mean I currently have over 100 games that are either in my steam library or have been recommended by others. When I started streaming a friend of mine brought up Say No! More to me as a joke. He said that I should learn to Say No! More and eventually redeemed it as a channel point reward on my stream. Overall I was looking forward to the playthrough though, even if the title was lesser known with under 1k reviews on steam and it being rather out there in terms of content. The reviews still average out as Very Positive plus I was looking forward to a short playthrough of something rather comical. Would I recommend this game to people though? Well, to be honest, with Say No! More it really depends. This game was purely for jokes and the humor, graphics, and style of the game are all rather niche. While I enjoyed the playthrough on stream, a personal friend of mine picked it up soon after and didn’t enjoy the game at all. The game may not be as entertaining to some and personally I’d never play alone. Meaning I’d recommend this for someone to play through with their friends or on stream with others if they don’t mind the dumb humor. The game overall has a very silly story with not much in terms of control or gameplay, it's simply something that you go through for the laughs and probably won’t play through again. Overall, I wouldn’t pick it up for its normal price of 15$ USD on steam. Picking the game up on sale and spending a few hours enjoying it with friends is worth a shot though. You may enjoy it for the 2-3 hours you play it, or you may dislike it and return it pretty quickly. Video of this Review:

_childDocuments_.review: This game is listed as a comedy, but honestly I didn't find it to be very funny. There's very few actual jokes and it seems over-reliant on the wacky performances of the cast to carry it. That's okay, though, because it's still satisfying to say NO! to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for its two hour length. There's also a really nice message at the end about understanding the mentality of those above you and standing up for yourself and valuing yourself even if the person who is asking something unreasonable of you is sympathetic. Plus, it's just nice to see a game use the Megaman Legends artstyle. It's aged incredibly well for the PSX era and it was always a shame that more games didn't use it even back then, so it's nice to see it return between this and Delta Gal. $15 is probably five dollars too many for a short comedy adventure, but you can always wait for a sale if you like. It's not something you're going to get a ton of mileage out of, but I think it's worth a couple playthroughs if you want to play a game about refusing the unfair request ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: A short but funny game about saying no (and standing up for yourself). Simple, but it's a one-note gimmick that could put some people off within minutes. And there's some flaws:- The different kinds of No's you can say are superficial. There are no unique interactions from using a certain type at specific moments, they're just for flavor.- Same goes for the non-No actions you can perform. Although they're used to build up a charged No, I noticed they were less relied upon as the game progressed.- The 99,999 No's achievement is too much. Just 9,999 of them is enough. An actual sincere "No" is in order here.Steam Deck users should check that their input is correct. I was under the mistaken impression the game actually had no controller support when it did. I played the whole game with a community binding but the Gamepad with Joystick Trackpad template is all you need. Maybe try applying it before first boot.Save this one for a rainy day or something short to play between games.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel that this game is very important in our current world and I recommend that everyone play it.  There's a lot here about standing together and standing up to worker abuse and greed, with handy examples of how those things manifest.  ("We're a family", "You should be grateful", etc.) On a surface level, I love the chaotic energy of the animations and effects. It's all delightfully over-the-top.The only negative is the price point vs. play time. This game can be completed in 2 hours while experiencing all of its content.  It's tough to justify buying it at full price especially now when money is becoming tight for people.  If you see this on sale, I fully recommend getting it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm saying Yes! What a fun, well-stylized little game! You can tell that the creators put their heart into this and had a lot of fun! The unique art style is what originally drew me to this game, but the message and the whimsy made it worth it. I was also pleasantly surprised by the voice acting. Every character was fun to listen to! Oh and the music is fantastic. I think good music is important, especially for an indie game such as this, and they really hit the mark.For those of you wondering about gameplay: keep in mind it's more about the journey than anything else! You can make some choices that will lead to different little interactions BUT it doesn't affect the overall story. Think of it like a visual novel of sorts.I will admit it's on the shorter side, so maybe wait for a sale if $15 for 2hrs doesn't sound like a good deal to you.HOWEVER, this game is anything but boring! If you're looking for a fun, quirky time: give "Say No! More" a shot!

I haven't finished it yet, but I can tell how much I have left based on the achievements.Gameplay is basically on-rails ride where you can pick how to reject or accept NPC encounters, some requiring a certain way to get passed in order to continue.Regardless, this game is high quality in many aspects, a decent price, and a GREAT way to relieve stress and anxiety from your work! _childDocuments_.review: Say No! More (1.5 stars out of 5)Brief synopsis of story: You are an intern who learns how to say no. You then proceed to say no to your co-workers (if you want) and then sometimes you have to say no in order to progress the story. This game felt like an on-rails shooter except it was more of an on-rails space bar hitter. Pros: it was funny at times.Cons: All you have to do is hit the space bar until the credits roll. The on-rails style does not work in my opinion, if the levels let you walk around I think this game would have been better. The achievements to say NO 99,999 times is awful. I beat the game while excessively spamming the no button and I was at 6,000 of 99,999. The game is pretty short and having an achievement that would require you to grind for 4x the amount of game play hours is ridiculous.  Achievement total: 22Total hours played: 14.6 (about 12 hours was me idling)Tips for any achievements:To get the achievement to say no 99,999 times download an autohot key program. Program it to hit the space bar and go to chapter 5. You can let the game idle there until you get the achievement.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: Really on the fence with this one. It's cute and I like where the developers are going, so if you have some spare $ throw it at em! Otherwise, just watch Yes Man.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: It has good style and some funny gags, but it felt like a really one note fable. This could work for some people, presumably those who really *really* need to be affirmed that setting boundaries is good, but for me it overstayed its welcome by the third chapter, which isn't great considering its short total run time of less than two hours.That said, Studio Fizbin is definitely a group to keep an eye on because I just really love the look and sound of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: Say No! More took me by surprise. I had received the game through the support Ukraine Bundle, I was not expecting much of it the first time that I had launched it. I was caught pleasantly surprised to find a meaningful premise hidden under it's wacky and quite frankly enjoyable story. As someone who has personally struggled with the ideas of saying no, the ending to this game almost brought a tear to my eye. Although this game is not very long, it has a heartfelt message that can be felt through many of the games cut scenes all in the midst of a perpetually chaotic story. I don't think this game is meant to be replayed but it's message will stick with me for a long time. Try to get this on sale or in a bundle. If you do, you will not regret taking the two hours it takes to run through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely adorable from beginning to end. A short, but very sweet experience that has obviously had a lot of care put into it. _childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say this game was in a bunch of games I got as a bundle and today I went though them, I thought this was going to be a game I would open and close pretty fast but the silly art style the game ideas and the random game play just to get the message across to  say no more in a world that wants to hear yes was a pretty neat way to get the point across.Well done on the game, I completed it and now I want to find the last 9 hidden achievements and the 9,999 and the 99,999 ones also.It can give you a little bit of a headache but it was worth every min.

_childDocuments_.review: A short animated interactive movie about self respect and healthy work/life boundaries... and the tendency for survivors to perpetuate unhealthy environments. The visual style is lifted from Megaman Legends - and what a good choice! Visually flexible, efficient and very expressive - Studio Fizbin have done a fantastic job with these graphics.My only complaints are that you're looking at around 2 hours max playtime / viewtime with this experience (which, honestly, if you think of it as being similar to a cinema ticket, isn't too bad) and that the game play seems... VERY slight. On the other hand, it's probably intended to be as accessible as possible - if so, mission accomplished.Looking forward to Fizbin's next project...!
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: A wholesome, cathartic, and very anticapitalist game about self-advocacy in a strangely familiar dystopian world where the practice of accepting self-destructive work has been normalized as a part of the path to becoming “happy”.Sure the game’s unnervingly real message is great, but I do wish that the whole thing were a little bit more interactive and mechanically complex. I mean, there's already a color/gesture system in place. The potential here for stronger allegorical gameplay is massive and the absence of situational "No"s or gestures feels like a missed opportunity. After all, wouldn’t it have benefited the story more if the gameplay itself actively encouraged skillful use of aptly-timed "No"s instead of inorganically accepting any "No" that the player says at any point? Don’t just tell the player to get out there and stick up for themself, give them the chance to digitally apply the pointers that you gave them about the delicate yet powerful tool of self-respect.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: In the spirit of this game, I will be saying what it isn't.Is this a fun game? No. It is a delightful experience that everyone should playIs it silly? No, while it does have many wacky elements, the message that Mach-no Man Randy Savage was trying to tell us was deep, thought provoking, and powerful.Is this hard? No, the controls are simple, the only key you would need to hit is spacebar, and maybe occasionally the arrow keys, everything else is just flavor, which is amazing.Do I recommend it? No. I absolutely commend it and push anyone reading this to play it. I so desperately want to click the "No" button on if I recommend the game, but I have to press yes because it is that good that I have to break the cardinal rule of the game.Overall, the story is both mature and deep, and while a lot of the wackier elements do blindside you from time to time, there are various clues throughout the story about what is going on in the subtext, everywhere.In short,  "No" this: If you get this game, you will be in for a delightful and humorous time.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely funny. The game is extremely fleshed out, with plenty of background gags or jokes you can miss out on entirely if you happen to say no to the wrong person. The game feels less like a game and more like an interactive cutscene, because there really isn't much other than pressing space. You could just watch a playthrough of the game, but i absolutely recommend you buy the game and play it instead.Say No! So you get a job at some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ business, who's model is  "Say Yes!" This, like any boss takes as an excuse to manipulate, steal, and undercut as many employees as possible. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a tough nut to decide whether to recommend a lot. Its a satirical game about corporate capitalism and workaholic culture. It can be pretty funny at times. It leans a lot into its set pieces. Its very short - you can finish the main story within the return window. There also isn't a lot of replayability here.  If you're an achievement hunter: in the 2 hours I played I finished the main story and said "No" 332 times. There's an achievement for saying "No" 99,999 times, so be prepared to use a macro, unless you want to replay this game 300 times over (lol). Even then you'll probably have to run the macro for quite a while. Overall, while I admit I enjoyed the game, I can't really imagine recommending it to anyone. But if you really do want to play $7.50 (games cheapest sale price on Steam as of this writing) for this 2 hour experience, you're probably the target audience, so don't let me stop you.

_childDocuments_.review: A silly, interactive, cathartic exercise for anyone experiencing the woes of being an unpaid intern or an assistant who's constantly being taken advantage of and overlooked. _childDocuments_.review: I got this game as part of the support Ukraine bundle, and I'm really glad I did! _childDocuments_.review: A short absurdist comedy about shaking up status quo in an office filled with abuses bosses with your ability to say no and a desire to regain your stolen lunch box.Make a character, choose what language you want to say no in and follow a mostly linear path where interacting with each person in your way allows you to say no to them or listen to what they have to say in some cases. You can charge up to release a more powerful no and over time learn to say four different types of nos and four different way of mocking the person in front of you before telling them no. Destroy the environment, launch people through the air, and shatters their disillusions with your power to tell them no.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: A very short game with a very wise message at the end. It shows how saying YES can slave and be destructable for us if we don't feel like it. Most of the game i felt like this game is only about saying no to everything just for fun, but then the final suddenly turned 180 and surprised me in a very positive way. Now I think Say No! More is worth playing just for the final chapter. I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: Want to mention up top that I got this as part of a Humble Bundle, but all things considered, I would have likely been happy to pay full price. The game is a fun, lighthearted look at corporate culture in our world, through the lens of an intern learning to say "No!" more. The art style is charming, there's a surprising amount of character customization available, and the story and characters are well-written, if a bit simplistic. The voice acting is great and gives you the option to say no in a huge variety of languages, too! If I had one major complaint it's that I wish there was a bit more to the actual mechanics of the game, even though they definitely take a back-seat to the story and characters. Easily a solid 8/10, gave me a good 1.5-2 hours of fun and hilarious gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't exactly a game, it's more a combination of a motivational tape, an assertivity guide, and a political stance. Despite it all, even though I don't agree with what this game is trying to convey, the style and humor is good enough to keep the viewer entertained. Just... don't expect any challenge. You literally have to press space whenever someone talks, that's it.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the humor and tone of this game, I had a lot of fun with this game's story and enjoyed its sense of humor. Plus I dug the art style of the game and the message of the game is a pretty good one as well.However I do have to say that this game is a bit lacking mechanically. It introduces four ways to say no (Heated, Cold, Lazy, and Wacky) as well as four actions to take before saying no (Laughing, slow clapping, nodding in agreement, and going hmmm...), but none of those things really felt like they did anything special in terms of gameplay, I didn't feel the need to change up my no's all that much and mostly ignored the other actions as well. It didn't really feel like there was a benefit to doing one no or the other at any given time.Plus this game is admittedly short, I was able to complete the game under 2 hours, which makes it hard to recommend at the sticker price of $15, but if you can get it on sale then this was a nice humorous experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute and fun game, I thoroughly enjoyed it, and the message is relevant and powerful (although it gets weirdly sympathetic to the villain at the end...) That being said, I got it on Humble Bundle, and checked the store page because I was curious, and £13 is way too much for its playtime. Definitely get it if it's on sale, otherwise just watch it on YouTube.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hilarious. At first I was really annoyed with it since you just walk around saying "no" to everything. The way the characters walk cracks me up though. The story actually started to draw me in which was a surprise. It's somewhat relatable if you have worked a corporate job, and at least at one point I thought it would be a nice message for a CEO to see. Definitely unique. Linear game with no choices, practically a short, animated visual novel. Lastly, if you start the game and can't finish in one sitting, the save points are automatic at the start of each chapter. If you need to come back to it, just let the chapter start and then exit the game. Pretty cute game with a positive message. I'll also note it did crash on me once when the game was near the end. Not sure why, I was playing around with the arrow keys during a speech so maybe I triggered it to crash. Had to restart the chapter and second play-through was fine, thankfully. Can't skip the text when your character is in observation mode and not able to say no. I think the price is a bit high. I got it in the Ukraine bundle but would never pay full price even though I do recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: Short, sweet, easy controls. What else could you want? If you like basic graphics or don't have enough RAM to run the fun graphics on other games, then this is for you. This can give you a bit of self-confidence if you didn't already have some. The idea that saying no sometimes is a great message to have. This is one game I can't say "No!" to.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a short but very sweet game. It teaches the importance of standing up for yourself and for knowing when to say yes or no to things. It even had me just saying no outloud and sure enough I kind of felt better. The game has a wonderful sense of humor and a light tone which perfectly conveys the message it is trying to put out there. I would highly recommend picking this up if you need a pick me up!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: A great little gem game that will be worth the time you put in to it. But is it right for you? Here's what I think.Yes it's short, I clocked up just over 90 minutes to completion (I don't worry about achievements). Those minutes were well paced and contained no filler time wasters activities. The plot flows with a good increase in stakes and has a nice conclusion. Though the team wouldn't have had english as their first language the writing was darn good. (Along with a few pop culture nods and a message that we should all remember.) Yes, the graphics are intentionally low poly with 'first gen' textures and animation that puts me in mind of puppets. It’s an art style that is fun and bright, completely fitting the theme. A nice change from the over realistic or over designed art styles a lot of  ‘AAA’ games.  The music matched the theme and the voice acting was great. The game play might be 'one button' (though really 9 to use by the end) but I didn't feel like I wasn't in control or didn't have any options during my play time. Treat this game as a palette cleanser. Something light and fun between the more grindy or dour ‘AAA’ games. Thumbs up, full recommend Say No More.
_childDocuments_.name: Say No! More

_childDocuments_.review: This is a GOD TIER GAME. Definitely worth the grab. It is about like 2-3 hours of playtime (Going to play it again).I've actually looked at this game to get for like a year now. I did wait for a sale for this game, which was lovely. Got it in a bundle.This is like a great small part of assertiveness training, not allowing yourself to be pushed away and bullied.To learn to say, yep, "NO!". Though the game kept its very comedic and funny elements to the game, it was able to include such a touching and heartwarming story towards it, that kept me playing, despite the only thing that you did in the game, was to say "No!". At first I thought it was an open world game where you can cause havoc any where, but now playing it, I'm glad it was not. It was like watching a high quality movie at the rhythm of your choosing. I loved every single part of it. I recommend it to anyone who is considering to buying this game. Absolutely a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: A very silly, but surprisingly emotional tale about the importance of work/life balance and the power of workers banding together to make a difference. _childDocuments_.review: This is a cute, but shallow, game.If you go into it with those expectations, it's an enjoyable experience, but I could easily see how someone could be disappointed by this if they didn't anticipate what it would be like.The actual moment-to-moment gameplay is practically nonexistant: the game is more of a sequence of cutscenes with QTEs, than something that can actually be "played". This isn't really a problem with the game, since the focus is on the presentation and humor, not on action. You can think of it more like a Visual Novel than any other genre, really.Given those constraints though, the game leans more heavily on its storytelling to hold it up, and this is where I think it falters a bit.The writing is not particularly strong- it's minimal, and functional, but it follows a saturday-morning-cartoon kind of logic that might leave some wanting more from this already somewhat sparse experience. Particularly given the game's themes- if the game is going to talk about capitalism, wealth inequality, and name-drop unionization: I kind of expected it to have something of substance to say about these things, but instead the story solves the major plot conflict with what amounts to anime magic and the power of friendship. You can't have characters explicitly point out systemic economic issues, suggest forming a union, and then not have collective bargaining actually happen in the game's story.There's nothing wrong with having politics in your game, but Studio Fizbin seems to have been unable to commit to it, opting for a moustache-twirling villain at the helm of it all, rather than the systemic mechanisms of oppression the game is otherwise eager to throw sound-bytes at the player about.While I would have liked a more in-depth story though, it doesn't kill the game, since I already mentioned that this is best experienced with an expectation for something shallow and cute. The presentation and delivery are top-notch: every interaction is uniquely voice-acted, and the visual aesthetic, although crude, is clearly well thought-out and adhered to throughout.This is accompanied by a fantastic OST, which may in fact be my favorite part of the game. Its upbeat and lighthearted style serves the critical role of setting the atmosphere for the game, since taking it too seriously will lead to disappointment.Small things come in small packages. If you can pick this up for an equally small price, and it sounds like the kind of thing that's fun for a small amount of time, you might just have a small amount of fun with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, what an indie-hit!"Say No! More" is an indie title that focuses on story and gameplay solely based around social interaction using a variety of ways to say one word: NO!On behalf of the story, it's just a short and simple adventure with its own charms. The characters that you encounter throughout the game, really make the story entertaining and the writing, no matter where you look, is mostly humorous. Only about at the end of the game, the story turns a little more serious and tries to convey a message. The gameplay is an on-rails interactive visual novel, basically. Your character moves by themselves. All you can do is press "Space" to say "NO!" and some other minor features I don't want to spoil. But basically, this is it. Of course, there are also times, where you don't have to say "NO!", which I'll leave to you to discover. But there's plenty of them. A couple of them even make you find secret events you would otherwise skip. Say "NO!" with conscience!The visuals are pretty crisp and nice pixel-art coupled with 3D-rendered environments and wacky physics for comedic effect. Nothing really looks out of place and the developers really made the world look consistent. Environments and character designs are pretty unique throughout the game, making it a fresh experience all the way. The music also works well with the designs, but isn't really worth talking about; not bad, not outstanding either.The achievements you can get in this game are mostly you completing each chapter or finding all the secrets. Except one. One achievement wants you to say "NO!" 99999 times. Yes, that many. And it's an absolute time waste. I personally ended up watching YouTube videos in Picture-in-Picture mode while pressing "Space" in the Character Language Select to just rack up all those damn NOs. It took about 6 - 8 hours of just mashing one button without any gameplay whatsoever. A dreadful achievement for such an otherwise great game.All in all, a great experience. What seems to be a comedy-show at first glance, just about turns into a poetic work of art over the course of the game. This game guarantees a fun time, if you are willing to give the gameplay a chance. What are you waiting for?

_childDocuments_.review: a truly fun and funny game that wears its heart on its sleeve. the aesthetic and animation that borrows heavily from katamari really boosts the charm, and it's probably gonna be pretty hard to stop smiling. there's some real comedy gold here, but its message is pretty clear from the title and through the narrative. it wants you to build this skill in the real world too--the game views its advice as crucial to building a better world to live in. saying "no" is an inherently challenging act, and doing it enough will get you to wake up to the cruel and absurd reality that surrounds usit's the length of a film for the price of a movie ticket. don't get so hung up about the price of games and their length, and instead buy this game at full price to support an indie dev.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to talk about Say No! More like how we talk about most games - boxed, consumer products with features listed in neat bullet points (although the devs took a good stab at it!). Is it, effectively, a game where you just repeat variations of the same action over and over throughout its runtime? Well, yes...but also No?Say No! More is a cathartic playground, a Standing-Up-For-Yourself simulator that equips you with a toolbox of ways to say no, with non-verbal responses and different tones of voice, to let the player express themselves in a consequence-free environment. It invites you to think of every ludicrous or unreasonable request you've faced in interpersonal relationships, office jobs or when faced with authority, and let out how you really felt.The fact that it's so freeform and uncomplicated is precisely the point. The developers could have made the different tones of voice into 'elements' that only work against certain enemy types like a rudimentary puzzle game or RPG, and I'm glad they resisted that temptation. It means so much more to be faced with a situation and decide for yourself the ideal No. I laugh when someone tells me to pay their parking ticket because I feel it's a laughable demand and deliver a cold, biting hard 'No' when someone else would pump the aggression to the maximum. It's a short and linear story, but those tiny meaningful variations are yours and nobody can take them from you.This toolbox is a gift in a story about personal boundaries, office politics, people-pleasing, Bull[-you-know-what] Jobs, collective power and creating a more equitable workplace. If you're into short, experimental, expressive experiences, say 'yes' just one more time and buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SO much fun, and quite a silly and unique concept! The writing and voice acting is hilarious, the art style is incredible, and the music is SO GOOD.There are tons of options for skin tons, hair styles (including facial hair) and body types when you create your character, and instead of choosing a gender you can pick what voice you want. There are tons of voice language options (so you can have the game be in English but shout No in Portuguese) and you can also pick the pitch of the voice (high or low). Within the game itself, the other characters appearances are varied. I like the inclusion of the background characters having diverse appearances, like a few had facial hair and feminine outfits, for example.I loved the message of the game, and the humor and diversity within the character creator and cast really sold it for me. I highly recommend picking this one up!

_childDocuments_.review: First, and most importantly. This game is ridiculously overpriced. Got it at what I think is launch sale, $13.50, down from $15.00, both way too high. I took 1.8 hours to beat it, rushed through some things and skipped a lot more (unintentionally). I don't recommend buying this at its full price, or a low discount. If I could've picked, I would not have paid more than $7 for it, and even that would feel steep.That being said, overall I recommend it because it is a cute game and a fun story.The basic controls are one button to say "No!" which you can charge up - but charged "No!" uses energy, four buttons to flavor your "No!" such as sarcastic or direct, and four buttons to perform various actions to build up energy for charged "No!". The game proceeds on rails, almost like an Indigo Prophecy or a movie with small interactive moments.The art is simplistic but totally works. It's vibrant and nice to look at. The animations are a little weak but also definitely exaggerated for comedic effect. The only real complain I have on the animations are that the characters just float off the ground - you can tell they're pivoting on a point near their waist instead of resting on the ground. The music is nice and sorta catchy but not exactly a stand out. Good enough to fit the mood and tone of the game, and to be fun while playing, but I don't think anyone's craving that OST. The UI is snappy and clean, actually really well done. Character customization is a nice touch, though you won't really end up creating a character that truly stands out from the NPCs. The ability to change the language you shout "No!" in is a great touch, though completely superficial and doesn't seem to have any impact on gameplay at all. Big shout out for the use of "they" in the voice acting. Great way to be inclusive without pandering.The story is simple, but layered, and that's where things get a little complicated. I want to avoid spoilers here, so pardon the generalizations. On one level, it's a story about understanding your own boundaries, sticking up for yourself, having confidence, and valuing yourself. On that level, it is beautiful. It works. It's great, it's relatable, and well done. At least one other level of the game's story, though, is a look at workplace hierarchy and similar power structures. On this level, the game's story is incredibly shallow and childish. The "upper management" characters are complete caricatures, straw people that we often like to pretend these types in real life are in order to dehumanize them and thereby rationalize their poor treatment of others. It's not the main focus of the game, so I don't think it hurts it *too* much, but it definitely takes anyone that has experience with the real world out of the game a little bit.Overall, a  cute,  fun little experience and worth it at half price at most. I give it the recommendation for the day it ultimately drops in price, but really, it's not worth checking out at full or only 10% off.

Hi-jinks ensue.GOOD:Humorous storySomewhat catharticArt style is very reminiscent of old PS1 games, which I personally loveHas some good lessonsCustomizationBAD:ShortReplayability may not be a thing, unless you want to see how a character reacts if you don't say no? Is that a thing?MEH:Gameplay is kinda simplistic. You either say no in one of 4 ways, do an action like laugh or clap, or you do... Nothing.It's on-rails. I think it works for this game, but that might be a turn off for someVERDICT:I liked it, though I feel the price may be just a tad steep after playing. If you're into quirky experiences, go ahead a check it out.Honestly wouldn't mind seeing what this studio has in store in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: A truly eyerolling 10 dollar experience. Its mindless, harmless fun, with catchy music, stylistically pleasing visuals, and a call to action that will have everyone agreeing at least on the broad strokes. They could have made it more game centric, which would make the long tutorials of the different "no's" have a point; they could have made it a more comedy or theme driven, getting rid of the needless tutorials altogether and making the experience streamlined, almost like a movie. Buy it on sale if you want to have an evening of simple good vibes.
